summary: XYZprinting is presenting the MfgPro220 xPF, an ultrafast stereolithography 3D printer powered by Nexa3D, at booth #2142 at the Fort Worth Convention Center, April 24-28, 2018. Priced at $19,950—a fifth the cost of equivalent printers—it offers a 16-liter build volume, twice that of competitors, and is suited for functional prototyping, production tooling, and end-use parts. It uses cognitive software, integrated sensors, and deep machine learning algorithms, with on-board and cloud controls. XYZprinting also announced a three-way partnership with BEGO and Nexa3D targeting digital dentistry, and a strategic investment in Nexa3D. The printer's LSPc technology and structured light matrix reach speeds of 1Z cm per minute, reducing print cycles from hours to minutes.

Collagen is a protein making up about 30% of the body's protein, providing structural support to skin, tendons, and bones. Natural production decreases with age, prompting interest in supplements. Of around 28 collagen types, I, II, III, IV, and V are most common. The three main supplement forms are hydrolysed collagen (considered most effective due to easy digestion and absorption), undenatured collagen, and gelatin. Most supplements are animal-sourced: marine, bovine, porcine, and chicken, containing mainly types I, II, and III. Reported benefits include improved skin, reduced wrinkles, stronger nails, better bone density, reduced joint pain, and muscle support, with limited research suggesting thicker hair growth. Studies indicate daily doses of 2.5g to 15g may benefit joints, skin, bones, and muscles. Research is ongoing; manufacturers recommend at least 12 weeks of use. A balanced diet also supports natural collagen production.

Sensient Technologies Corporation (NYSE:SXT) reported quarterly EPS of $0.80, beating the Zacks consensus estimate of $0.78 by $0.02. The company announced a quarterly dividend of $0.30 per share, payable March 1st, with an ex-dividend date of February 3rd. KeyCorp raised its price objective to $84.00 with an "overweight" rating, while Zacks upgraded the stock from "sell" to "hold."

This is the first lecture of MIT's course on Discrete Stochastic Processes. The professor explains that the course, created about 25 years ago to unify the fragmented field of queuing theory for students interested in networks, will cover probability in the real world versus probability as mathematics, the definition of discrete stochastic processes, the field's usefulness, the axioms of probability, and a review of independent events, experiments, and random variables.

He emphasizes that the hard problem in probability is not solving well-posed problems but finding appropriate models for real-world situations. Using coin flipping as an example, he notes that many "random" phenomena are deterministic when examined closely, and that models—such as treating data as random in compression, or financial risk models—can be mathematically sound yet fail if poorly chosen. He cites Whitehead's advice to "seek simplicity and distrust it" and stresses that Kolmogorov's 1933 axioms keep probability models free of paradoxes.

A discrete stochastic process is a probability model whose sample points represent sequences of random variables in time. The course will study counting (Poisson) processes, Markov chains, renewal processes, and random walks and martingales, with applications in communication systems, networks, computer systems, queuing, risk and catastrophe management, and many other fields.

The lecture reviews the axioms: a sample space, events closed under countable unions, and a probability measure satisfying P(Ω)=1, nonnegativity, and countable additivity for disjoint events, with consequences including P(∅)=0, the complement rule, and the union bound. Independent events satisfy P(A1∩A2)=P(A1)P(A2), and combining experiments via Cartesian products preserves the axioms. Finally, a random variable is defined as a function from sample points to finite real values such that {X≤x} is an event, which guarantees that every random variable has a distribution function, whether discrete, continuous, or mixed.

A new Weather Channel Android app for developing countries uses IBM's mesh networking to send messages directly between phones via Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, letting information spread even when mobile networks fail during emergencies. It works over 200 to 500 feet without extra battery burden or reconfiguration. Each download adds a mesh node, and the network could support other applications like messaging. IBM uses digital signatures to verify trusted devices. The 3.2MB app launches in Asia, Latin America and Africa and works on slow 2G networks.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2016. Total revenues were $1.15 billion, up from $939.9 million in Q1 2015, driven primarily by Model S deliveries worldwide and Model X deliveries. Gross margin declined to 22.0% from 27.7%. Net loss was $282.3 million ($2.13 per share) versus $154.2 million ($1.22 per share) a year earlier. Total assets were $9.19 billion, with cash and cash equivalents of $1.44 billion and stockholders' equity of $970.4 million.

The company produced 15,510 vehicles in Q1 2016, including about 2,650 Model X vehicles, and has delivered over 122,000 vehicles cumulatively. Model 3, unveiled in Q1 2016, received more than 325,000 reservations within one week, with volume production targeted for late 2017. Tesla advanced its 500,000-unit build plan by two years to 2018 and expects 80,000–90,000 Model S and Model X deliveries in 2016. Capital expenditures are expected to be approximately 50% higher than the previously estimated $1.5 billion for 2016, and operating expenses are expected to grow 20–25%.

As of March 31, 2016, $565.0 million was outstanding under a $1.0 billion asset-based credit facility; $350.0 million was repaid in April 2016. The 2018 convertible notes ($617.1 million carrying value) were classified as current liabilities because conversion conditions were met. Gigafactory construction costs totaled $354.6 million, with cell production expected to begin in Q4 2016 and Panasonic partnering on battery cell production. A November 2013 securities class action was dismissed with prejudice in September 2014; the plaintiffs' appeal remains pending.

The message returns to the House of Representatives, with objections, a bill donating public lands to States and Territories that provide colleges for the benefit of agriculture and the mechanic arts. The bill grants each State 20,000 acres for each Senator and Representative, plus 20,000 acres for each additional Representative under the 1860 census—totaling 6,060,000 acres, valued at $7,575,000. States must establish at least one college within five years or forfeit the grant and repay proceeds from lands already sold; States lacking suitable public lands receive land scrip instead. The writer deems the bill both inexpedient and unconstitutional, citing six objections: (1) it would deprive the Treasury of land-sale revenue, estimated at $5,000,000 for the next fiscal year, because States' sale of scrip would glut the market and depress prices below even the 85 cents per acre already fetched by bounty-land warrants; (2) it would blur the distinct spheres of the Federal and State governments and squander lands needed as security for wartime loans; (3) it would injure new States by enabling speculators to buy scrip cheaply and claim the best public lands, forcing cultivators to pay higher prices; (4) the Federal Government has no power to enforce the States' faithful execution of the trust; (5) it would harm existing colleges by creating federally endowed rivals, while local struggles over dividing the fund would frustrate the bill's purpose; and (6) Congress lacks constitutional authority to give public lands to States for education, since "dispose of" in the Constitution does not mean "give away," and lands purchased with tax money, such as those from the Louisiana and Florida purchases, cannot be devoted to purposes beyond those of the money itself. Earlier land grants to new States for schools were permissible as prudent management to promote settlement and enhance land value, but a donation to all States for colleges does not fall within that principle.

Bell Academy physical education teacher Joyce Aycock received a Mississippi Alliance for Health, Physical Education, Recreation and Dance grant from Blue Cross Blue Shield of Mississippi in November 2016, funding a new P.E. building built behind the school by parent volunteers and community members. Students report being able to do more activities without the noise disruptions of the previously used open areas and outdoor concrete space. A horizontal rock-climbing wall will be added before the ribbon cutting at 9:30 a.m. Friday.

Bethesda announced Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus will release on Nintendo Switch on June 29, available digitally and physically, though the physical version requires a download. The shooter originally launched on PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and PC in October. Bethesda previously ported Doom and Skyrim to the Switch.

The Drive concept is a pass game combination featuring a 10-12 yard basic route and a 3-4 yard shallow crossing route from the same side of the formation. It creates a triangle read for the quarterback and stresses linebacker-level defenders. It performs well against man coverage, where moving receivers are difficult to cover, and against Cover 4, where the basic-post combination can create big-play opportunities. It struggles against Cover 2 and Cover 3, which feature four or five low defenders outnumbering the underneath routes. Route responsibilities differ slightly by coverage: against man, receivers stay on the move; against zone, the slot and tight end sit in open voids. The quarterback's post-snap progression is go route, shallow cross, basic route, then check-down, with the post route peeked pre-snap. Variations include pairing the drive with a bunch formation to create natural picks against man coverage, and attaching it to the backside of other schemes as a quick outlet against blitz.

The Department of Higher Education and Training is working to integrate NSFAS into college and university systems ahead of the free higher education roll-out, after delayed payments sparked student protests. Minister Naledi Pandor acknowledged some continuing students' funding remains unfinalised and instructed urgent resolution, citing system integration challenges affecting registration data submission. R7.2bn was allocated in 2018 for bursaries, with NSFAS's baseline allocation rising from R9.9bn to R35.3bn by 2020-21, plus R105m for administrative capacity. The DA criticised the minister's vague responses and will request an urgent meeting with NSFAS.

Council traffic bosses say they are doing all they can to tackle congestion around Southway and Tamerton Foliot. The council coordinates planned roadworks with utility companies, avoids scheduling non-emergency work alongside the Derriford Transport Scheme, and requests night or off-peak working where possible. Examples include restricting South West Water's temporary signals on Tamerton Foliot Road to 9.30am–2.30pm and working with Wales and West on Lulworth Drive and Southway Lane. The council monitors traffic around the Derriford scheme, suspended bus lane restrictions on Tavistock Road, altered signal timings at George Junction, and is reviewing Budshead Roundabout arrangements, with proposed lane marking changes under safety audit. Planned roadworks are publicised online, via media, and on roadside signs.

ADT is described as undervalued relative to newly listed peer Verisure, supported by strong revenue growth, improving profitability, and a high share of recurring revenue. Partnerships with Google and State Farm, ongoing debt reduction, and aggressive share buybacks boost shareholder yield to 11%. Customer churn and static subscriber numbers remain challenges, though investments in AI, remote assistance, and smart home solutions aim to improve retention. Applying a 12-14x P/E implies 33%+ upside from current levels. The author discloses a long position in ADT shares.

This is a Week 10 fantasy football newsletter from Joe Bryant of cheatsheets.net, dated November 2, 2000. It announces a new "On Target" feature analyzing how often wide receivers were targeted with passes during the first half of the 2000 season. The main content consists of passing game and rushing game matchups, organized into categories based on favorability: Locks (heavily favoring the offense), Prime Matchups, Even Matchups, Downside Matchups, and Defensive Slam Dunks (heavily favoring the defense). Notable items include Jeff George replacing the injured Brad Johnson as Washington's starting quarterback, Terrell Davis's return for Denver, and favorable matchups such as New Orleans' passing game and Ricky Williams against San Francisco, along with difficult matchups like Tennessee's passing game against Pittsburgh and Charlie Garner against New Orleans. Player injuries, depth chart changes, and start/sit considerations are discussed throughout, with statistics provided by Mike Hall's FLM software and ESPN.com.

This document describes the Versioned Chip Endorsement Key (VCEK) certificate and the AMD Key Distribution System (KDS) interface used to retrieve certificate information for AMD SEV-SNP technology. It is intended for software developers supporting virtualized host environments using SEV-SNP. VCEK certificates are X.509v3 certificates generated at request time and not stored in the KDS. They are rooted in a chain consisting of the product-specific AMD Root Key (ARK) and the intermediate AMD SEV Key (ASK), both valid for 25 years. VCEK certificates are valid for seven years, backdated one day to avoid clock synchronization issues. Product names are determined via CPUID FMS information. The KDS provides an HTTP interface (TLS 1.2) at kdsintf.amd.com for retrieving VCEK certificates, certificate chains, and certificate revocation lists, with rate limiting (Error 429) and Error 404 for unsupported URLs or nonexistent device IDs. Certificate extensions describe TCB_VERSION elements, with hwID lengths of 64 bytes for Family 19h processors and 8 bytes for Family 1Ah (Turin and later). The service permits pre-fetching and caching certificates with SPL values above currently released firmware, enabling seamless future firmware upgrades.

USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino named a 26-player roster for two October friendlies, headlined by Christian Pulisic and Weston McKennie. Matches are scheduled for Oct. 10 in Austin, Texas, and four days later in Commerce City, Colorado, with all three countries involved already qualified for the 2026 World Cup. Training camp begins in Austin on Oct. 4. Antonee Robinson received his first 2025 call-up after recovering from knee surgery, while McKennie returns for the first time since March's Concacaf Nations League. Tanner Tessmann and Aidan Morris were rewarded for strong club form, with Tessmann scoring twice for Lyon and Morris earning multiple Man of the Match awards with Middlesbrough. Pulisic is the roster's most in-form player, with six goals and two assists for AC Milan this season. Injuries kept several players out, and a Norwich City forward was excluded despite a strong league start, having not scored an international goal since 2019. Ecuador recently clinched its fifth World Cup appearance, and Australia secured its sixth consecutive berth.

UPMSP will declare the UP Board Class 10 and Class 12 Results 2018 on April 29 at 12:30 pm on upresults.nic.in and upmspresults.up.nic.in. Class 10 exams were held February 6–22 and Class 12 exams February 6 to March 12, 2018. Results can also be checked via other websites and SMS. In 2016-17, 34,04,571 students appeared for Class 10 and 26,24,681 for Class 12, both with 81.6% pass rates.

The player describes a tight checking game, noting Hasek's frequent puck handling complicates forechecking. He cites frustration over scoring and defensive lapses, emphasizing the need to refocus and play tighter from the defensive zone. Detroit's adjustments added frustration, though Arturs played well, and the team will correct breakdowns while trusting coaching decisions.

Mr. Allen reported that Kim Ok-kiun, who led the 1884 revolution and was a refugee in Japan, was assassinated in Shanghai by Hong Chong-oo, whom the King wanted sent to Korea for trial. The American consul-general declined to interfere, and Hong was turned over to the Chinese authorities. In Tokyo, Ye, claiming a written order bearing the King's seal authorizing him to kill rebel refugee Pak Yung-ho, was arrested by Japanese police and implicated a conspirator named Hong, who took refuge in the Korean legation. When the Korean chargé d'affaires refused to surrender him, Japanese police forcibly entered the legation and imprisoned him. Kim's body and Hong were later delivered to Korean authorities at Chemulpo; the body was mutilated in Seoul, and foreign representatives chose not to interfere beyond unofficial explanation. Mr. Sill reported uprisings against oppressive officials in three southern provinces, prompting the King to request an American ship at Chemulpo and the recall of missionaries to treaty ports; he advocated more frequent naval visits.

The passage describes a patent application for a vehicle sensing system that uses radar sensors with two-dimensional antenna arrays. The system employs multiple transmitting and receiving antennas arranged in rows and columns, with a control applying two-dimensional multiple input multiple output (MIMO) processing to the antenna outputs to detect objects exterior to the vehicle. An illustrated embodiment uses 12 transmitting antennas arranged in three rows and 16 receiving antennas arranged in four columns, yielding 192 virtual receivers and an enhanced two-dimensional virtual aperture that provides improved horizontal and vertical angular accuracy and resolution, unlike conventional one-dimensional MIMO approaches. Other antenna arrangements are also possible. The system may support driver assistance functions such as autonomous or semi-autonomous driving, automated parking, blind spot detection, cross traffic alert, lane change and merge aid, automatic emergency braking, pedestrian detection, turn assist, and intersection collision mitigation. It may optionally fuse camera image data with radar data, generate alerts, overlay alerts on display screens, or control vehicle systems such as steering or braking.

Jennifer Thompson was raped at knifepoint at age 22 and identified Ronald Cotton as her attacker, leading to his conviction. Eleven years later, DNA testing proved Cotton innocent; the actual rapist was Bobby Poole, who assaulted six more women while Cotton was imprisoned. Jennifer learned how memory can fail in traumatic situations. After she apologized, Cotton forgave her, and they became best friends. She now works with Healing Justice, which brings harmed parties together.

Russia's central bank cut its key rate to 9.25 percent from 9.75 percent, its second cut this year and deeper than analysts predicted. It forecasts inflation will fall to 4 percent by end-2017 but remains concerned about inflation and market volatility. The rouble briefly weakened to 57.19 against the dollar.

The Oct. 15 pay date for 1.3 million active-duty military members may pressure the White House and Congress to end the government shutdown, since missing a pay period could provoke public anger. Goldman Sachs economists expect the shutdown to end by mid-October, though prediction markets give a 71% probability it lasts past Oct. 14. Other potential catalysts include TSA operations, expiring WIC benefits on Oct. 13, Obamacare open enrollment on Nov. 1, and Congress's Nov. 21 Thanksgiving break. Pimco analysts say the shutdown, the first full one since 2013, seems intractable, and Raymond James does not rule out a shutdown extending into November.

This work presents the fabrication and characterization of hybrid superconducting microwave circuits consisting of NbN coplanar waveguide (CPW) resonators on n-doped Si/Si₀.₇Ge₀.₃ quantum well wafers. A 100 nm NbN film was reactively DC sputtered onto the wafer, patterned by e-beam lithography, and dry etched, with an additional deep etch into the CPW gap regions intended to reduce intrinsic loss by shifting substrate-vacuum interfaces away from high electric field regions. TEM/STEM imaging confirmed epitaxial layer growth, though oxygenation was observed in the Si cap layer. Two samples were measured over four cooldowns spanning two years, with resonance frequencies near 5.04–5.60 GHz and internal quality factors (Qᵢ) of roughly 500–1064. Power spectroscopy showed TLS-related frequency shifts and Qᵢ saturation at low photon numbers, with no measurable degradation over time. Loss modeling indicated that while TLS losses contribute to dissipation, scattering centers and impurities dominate. Temperature-dependent measurements revealed a blue shift up to 900 mK followed by a redshift attributed to quasiparticle losses. The authors estimate a maximum gatemon relaxation time of ~14 ns and conclude that the platform offers a CMOS-compatible, stable route toward integrating superconducting and semiconductor qubits, with further wafer optimization needed.

Monday opened the seven-day 2025 World Grand Prix of Darts with an eight-game slate featuring Luke Humphries, James Wade, Nathan Aspinall and Stephen Bunting. Rob Cross won the opener in a last-leg decider. Ratajski eliminated the first seed 2-0 with a 95.94 average, Menzies knocked out the #8 seed, and Cullen rallied from 2-0 down in set two to beat Wade 2-0 in sets.

Gold mining companies in Ghana, including Newmont, Gold Fields and AngloGold Ashanti, welcome new government tests to certify export values, the industry association said. The tests, part of President Akufo-Addo's efforts to tighten control of the sector and tax it appropriately, will be conducted by the Precious Minerals Marketing Company alongside existing checks. Ghana, Africa's second-largest gold producer, earned $5.78 billion from gold exports last year, while about $5 billion in revenues from exports to the UAE remain unaccounted for.

A Minnesota school district, Edina School District, introduces kindergarten students to the concept of "white privilege." At Highlands Elementary School, K-2 students participate in the Melanin Project, tracing and coloring hand cut-outs to reflect their skin tones for a poster. Separately, Michigan State University professor Shreena Gandhi co-authored an article claiming white yoga practitioners contribute to "white supremacy," linking yoga's popularity in the United States to colonialism and cultural appropriation.

A diverse workforce is essential in a global marketplace, but subconscious biases about gender, race, and ethnicity can influence hiring decisions. Studies demonstrate this bias: men were twice as likely to be hired for math positions despite equal performance, white-sounding names received 50% more callbacks, and non-English last names resulted in fewer interview callbacks. To reduce bias, employers should review job posting language by listing desired behaviors rather than personality types, remove names from resumes before review, require skill-based challenges before collecting other applicant information, and analyze gut feelings during interviews to ensure prejudice is not the source of unease.

In his farewell address, the outgoing President announces he will soon leave office and return to the title of citizen, thanking Vice President Mondale, his Cabinet, his staff, and above all the American people for the opportunity to serve. He describes the presidency as the world's most powerful office yet constrained by law and custom, dependent on the support of the people and Congress, and stresses the importance of public involvement and scrutiny in democracy. He notes that a government designed for a few hundred thousand people now serves nearly 230 million, and warns that single-issue and special interest groups can distort the national interest, making a strong presidency essential. Pledging support to the President-elect, he addresses three global issues: the growing threat of nuclear war, requiring both American strength and arms control; environmental protection, including threats to air, water, land, and resources; and human rights, which America must uphold at home and abroad, noting that "human rights invented America." He calls the present an uneasy era of transition, urges adherence to founding principles, commits to a smooth transition, and says he will continue praying for the American hostages in Iran, closing with gratitude and farewell.

Teach For America's Ignite Fellowship, which over five years has reached more than 40 communities and trained over 5,500 virtual tutors, shows high-dosage tutoring delivers benefits beyond pandemic recovery. Middle school math students' test scores grew up to 2.5 times the expected rate, and elementary readers grew up to three times faster than average. The program's lessons: structured training and ongoing coaching are essential, with students reporting greater confidence; technology should expand rather than replace human relationships, as shown by Los Angeles eighth graders three grade levels behind in math who saw a 77-point jump in state assessment scores; and tutoring serves as a teacher pipeline—new research finds tutoring nearly triples the likelihood of applying to TFA's teacher program, with the largest effects among men, people of color, and non-education majors. The author argues tutoring should be treated as a long-term strategy for student growth and educator recruitment.

Amazon.com, founded by Jeff Bezos, launched its website on July 16, 1995, as an online bookstore and went public on May 15, 1997, raising $54 million at $18 per share. Over two decades, it grew into the fourth largest U.S. public company, behind Apple, Alphabet, and Microsoft, while deliberately sacrificing short-term profit through investments in expansion and research and development. The company expanded into new product categories, acquired Audible, Zappos, and Quidsi, launched the Prime membership program and Prime Day, developed in-house devices such as the Kindle, Fire tablets, and Echo, and created Amazon Web Services, which helped originate the cloud infrastructure industry. Despite failures like the Fire Phone, Bezos fostered a culture tolerant of failure. By the IPO's 20th anniversary, Amazon's market capitalization reached $458 billion, shareholders had earned nearly a 64,000% return, and cumulative net income from 1997 to 2016 totaled only $4.9 billion, with some observers predicting earnings could reach $20 billion annually within five years.

China's foreign exchange regulator said pressure from capital outflows eased in 2016 and the yuan's exchange rate will become more flexible in 2017. Authorities have taken steps to curb capital flight and attract inflows. Final 2016 data showed a $196.4 billion current account surplus and a $26.3 billion capital and financial account surplus. The yuan weakened 6.5 percent against the dollar in 2016.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2020 describes the company as a technology firm founded in 1975, headquartered in Redmond, Washington, with a mission to empower every person and organization to achieve more. As of July 27, 2020, 7,567,652,935 shares of common stock were outstanding, and as of December 31, 2019, the aggregate market value of common stock held by non-affiliates was $1.2 trillion. The company operates three segments: Productivity and Business Processes (Office, LinkedIn, Dynamics), Intelligent Cloud (Azure, server products, GitHub, Enterprise Services), and More Personal Computing (Windows, Devices, Gaming, Search). The report discusses COVID-19 pandemic impacts, a $1 billion sustainability investment with goals to be carbon negative by 2030, actions to address racial injustice, and a digital skills initiative including $20 million in non-profit partnerships. Products are developed internally through engineering groups, protected by over 63,000 issued patents, and distributed through OEMs, direct sales, and distributors and resellers; in June 2020, Microsoft announced closing its physical Microsoft Store locations. Executive officers include CEO Satya Nadella and CFO Amy E. Hood. As of June 30, 2020, Microsoft employed approximately 163,000 people full-time. Risk factors include intense competition, cloud execution risks, acquisition integration challenges (including the $7.5 billion GitHub acquisition completed in October 2018), potential goodwill impairment, cyberattacks, and disclosure or misuse of personal data.

The paper studies the "free option problem" created by Ethereum's proposed enshrined Proposer-Builder Separation (ePBS, EIP-7732), scheduled for the Glamsterdam upgrade. While ePBS removes reliance on trusted MEV-Boost relays by staking builders and debiting winning bids directly, its dual-deadline design—separate deadlines for execution payloads and blobs, intended to improve scalability—grants builders a roughly 8-second window in which they can withhold blobs or payloads to prevent a committed block from becoming canonical. This lets builders revert unfavorable trades (e.g., CEX-DEX arbitrages affected by adverse price movements) without protocol penalty, leaving slots empty and degrading liveness.

Theoretically, the authors show option value and exercise probability increase with volatility, option window length, liquidity, and the CEX-DEX MEV share of block value, and decrease with atomic MEV and penalties. Empirically, using historical blocks from January 2024 to March 2025, the option is profitable in 0.82% of blocks on average (34.6% of missed blocks), but rises to 5.5% of daily blocks during high-volatility periods (80% of missed blocks). Builders more dependent on CEX-DEX flow exercise more frequently, and trailing MEV reduces consecutive exercise.

Two mitigations are evaluated: shortening the option window (reducing exercise probability by over 77% at 2 seconds, but sacrificing scalability) and imposing penalties (a 0.075 ETH penalty cuts exercise probability by roughly 75%, but raises entry barriers for builders). A dynamic penalty mechanism based on online gradient descent achieves a 0.096% exercise rate with an average penalty of 0.104 ETH. Both approaches involve trade-offs among scalability, builder competition, and protocol complexity, and the problem may extend beyond trading to applications such as prediction markets.

On October 24–25, 2001, Enron Corp. replaced its chief financial officer, Andrew Fastow, with Jeff McMahon, head of the company's industrial markets group, after announcing an SEC inquiry into partnerships Fastow had run (LJM Cayman and LJM2). CEO Kenneth Lay stated that restoring investor confidence required replacing Fastow, who was placed on a leave of absence. The partnerships, which conducted transactions with Enron, led to a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity and a $35 million loss. Enron's stock fell 17% to $16.41, roughly half its value since October 16, dragging down other energy-trading stocks such as Dynegy. McMahon had previously raised conflict-of-interest concerns about Fastow's partnerships while serving as treasurer. Analysts, including Prudential's Carol Coale, downgraded the stock, citing lack of transparency and potential undisclosed liabilities. Multiple shareholder lawsuits were filed against Enron, and Moody's placed the company's debt on watch for possible downgrade.

Geary County deputies investigated a road rage incident near Fort Riley in which a passenger waved a gun from a white Dodge Ram truck. Isaac Torgerson was later arrested at Estes Gate on suspicion of Aggravated Assault.

The Yankees made a surprise lineup change for ALDS Game 4 against the Blue Jays, starting Paul Goldschmidt at first base and batting him sixth while Ben Rice moves to the bench. Toronto is starting opener Louis Varland with a bullpen game behind him. Goldschmidt had started only one postseason game, while Rice went 2-for-11 in the ALDS. Benching Rice provides lineup flexibility, as he can catch or pinch-hit.

The author ordered from Temu after the platform resumed direct shipping from China following a summer pause, and received the order with no extra tariff fees. Earlier, President Trump imposed tariffs on Chinese goods and moved to close the de minimis exemption, which had allowed packages under $800 to ship duty-free from overseas and underpinned the low prices of Temu and Shein. In response, both platforms changed their apps so US customers saw only products shipped from local US warehouses. Some shoppers using other international shippers received large duty bills, such as a $600 FedEx fee on two dresses. The author's toy order arrived in a week or two with mixed quality, and a month later no fees had been charged. A research report noted Shein prices rose about 30% on average.

The 2025 Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine was awarded to Mary Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell, and Shimon Sakaguchi for discovering regulatory T cells (T-regs), which calm the immune system after infection or wound healing and prevent it from attacking the body. Sakaguchi identified T-regs in 1995. Brunkow and Ramsdell tracked down a mutation causing a fatal autoimmune disease in male mice in the 1990s, and in 2001 they revealed mutations in people. Scientists are learning to harness T-regs to treat cancer and other conditions involving an overactive or misdirected immune system.

Donnell Gibson, known as "Mr. D," is a behavior intervention specialist and junior varsity basketball coach at Como Park Senior High in St. Paul, and this week's Excellent Educator. Having experienced homelessness as a child, he now helps students navigate life. In April 2015, he ran into a burning house three times to save a family of 10, earning the Fire Department's highest honor. He then started the Gibson Foundation, mentoring young African-American inner city men through motivational speakers, college tours, and basketball.

An October 23, 2001 email compiles news coverage of Enron, including:

- A class action lawsuit filed by Cauley Geller Bowman & Coates, LLP on behalf of investors who purchased Enron stock between January 18, 2000 and October 17, 2001, alleging securities law violations through material misrepresentations—failing to disclose declining Broadband Services demand, overstated operating results from unwritten-down investments in partnerships managed by Enron's CFO, and untimely impairment write-downs. Enron had announced $1.01 billion in third-quarter charges, and insiders sold over $73 million in stock during the class period.
- The SEC's informal inquiry into Enron's 1999–2000 transactions with limited partnerships run by a senior officer, which sent shares down over 20% to $20.65; Enron said it would cooperate fully.
- Analysts largely maintaining high ratings while investors fled, cutting the stock's value 42% in a week; a few downgrades occurred amid concerns about management credibility following the partnership disclosures and Jeffrey Skilling's August resignation.
- Enron's request that Citigroup arrange a $750 million loan amid credit concerns; Moody's placed $13 billion of long-term debt on downgrade watch; Enron bought back 62 million shares to unwind partnership positions, reducing shareholder equity by $1.2 billion.
- A Texas Monthly feature tracing Enron's transformation from pipeline company to trading colossus, Jeff Skilling's role and aggressive culture, Rebecca Mark's failed Azurix venture, California energy crisis criticism, telecom troubles, and Skilling's resignation.
- A conference call where CEO Ken Lay disputed an investor's valuation of Marlin II water assets, while keeping earnings guidance at $1.80 for 2001 and $2.15 for 2002.
- AES Corp.'s complaint to India's prime minister about alleged interference by the Orissa state government, following Enron's threatened legal claims of up to $5 billion over the Dabhol power project.

This passage discusses microtubule (MT) dynamics in prostate cancer (PC), focusing on metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). Approximately one-third of mCRPC tumors are primarily refractory to systemic therapy, and resistance to tubulin inhibitors is universal. The androgen receptor (AR) and its splice variants (ARv567, ARv7) differentially associate with MT polymers; ARv7 is correlated with taxane resistance while ARv567 is sensitive to docetaxel. The authors present a computational approach using automated tracking of fluorescently tagged EB1/EB3 comets to quantify MT polymerization dynamics in living cells. In M12 isogenic PC cell lines, ARv7 expression increased EB1 speeds by over 40% compared to AR-wild-type cells, indicating differential MT regulation between taxane-sensitive and resistant cells. Patient-derived organoids from 16 PC patients were established to match individual tumors to tubulin inhibitors based on MT dynamics signatures. The passage describes that androgen-independent circulating tumor cells (CTCs) are smaller than normal epithelial cells and can be identified via PSMA expression. GSK3β-mediated phosphorylation of pVHL at Ser-68 inactivates pVHL's MT stabilization functions, and both faster and slower than normal MT turnover rates are hallmarks of drug resistance. BRCA1 knockdown in A549 cells reduced paclitaxel sensitivity, demonstrating a distinct resistance mechanism. The authors propose methods to anticipate drug resistance ex vivo, sensitize resistant tumors by targeting the tubulin transcriptome, and use MT dynamics as a functional assay to screen compounds that correct aberrant MT homeostasis. They suggest that targeting GSK3 isoforms, which are differentially elevated in early (GSK3α) and advanced (GSK3β) disease, may offer therapeutic strategies for PC at different stages.

A team representative described an upbeat meeting about adjustments to the game plan. Physicality isn't seen as a major issue, but the team needs to improve its speed and skating. This email, forwarded by Steven J. Kean at Enron on February 28, 2001, compiles news articles dated February 23, 2001, concerning California's energy crisis. Topics include: La Cresta residents opposing Enron North America's proposed $450 million hydroelectric plant and power lines near the Cleveland National Forest; California Republicans' difficulty politicizing the crisis against Governor Gray Davis while lacking their own energy plan; Davis's announced "agreement in principle" to buy Southern California Edison's transmission lines for an estimated $2.7 billion, with negotiations continuing with PG&E and Sempra; the state's power-buying costs potentially exceeding $3 billion by mid-March; the first day without power alerts since January 13; disputes over how utilities will reimburse the state for power purchases; Assemblyman Lowenthal returning campaign contributions from energy firms; a proposed bill giving residents near power plants a 20 percent electricity discount; criticism of Davis's missed deadlines; potential Republican challengers (Bill Jones, Bill Simon Jr., and Arnold Schwarzenegger) in the 2002 gubernatorial race; a PUC ruling that could leave taxpayers responsible for power costs; and small generators agreeing to roughly halve their prices under legislation expected to save the state billions.

Donchian Channels, invented by Richard Donchian, consist of an upper band based on the high of the last N bars and a lower band based on the low of the last N bars. They work well as a trend-following indicator for commodities and currencies, but not for stocks. Backtests by Curtis Faith on currencies, commodities, and Treasuries (1996–2007) produced CAGRs of 29.4% and 57.2%. A trend-following test on the S&P 500 (1960–2021) yielded a 4.57% CAGR, below buy and hold's 7.15%, though with lower drawdowns. When reversed into a mean reversion strategy for stocks, a 5-day lookback on SPY produced a 9.16% CAGR with small drawdowns and a high win rate. Donchian Channels resemble Bollinger Bands but may yield different backtest results. Overall, they function as trend-following tools for commodities and currencies and as mean reversion indicators for stocks.

This article examines special and general education in Hungary, considering how demographics, government, and economy shape schooling. Hungary has about 9.7 million residents, most of whom are Hungarian, and faces a declining population. Its multiparty parliamentary democracy and evolving economy—including the centrally planned economy introduced in 1948 and later reforms under Prime Minister Viktor Orbán—influence education laws and opportunities.

General education dates to the eighteenth century, with the Education Act of 1868 establishing compulsory schooling (now ages six to sixteen). In 2020, about 82% of three- to twenty-two-year-olds attended formal education. School admission is competitive, with private schools selecting students based on desirable traits, and secondary education requires entrance examinations, 50 hours of community service, and a school-leaving examination. Teacher preparation includes bachelor's-level training for preschool and primary teachers; since 2013, undivided teacher education requires five years for primary and six for secondary teachers, culminating in mentored teaching practice.

Hungary pioneered special education in Europe, opening its first school for deaf students in 1802 and founding its first special education teacher college in 1906. Disability diagnoses are made by a committee of professionals, with parents making final placement decisions. In 2019, over 88,000 students had special education needs, 60% of whom were educated in inclusive environments. Special education teachers complete a four-year specialized program, choose one or two of eight specialties, and undergo a two-year traineeship with an evaluation exam and portfolio, followed by ongoing in-service training. Key legislation includes Act III of 1993, providing family allowances, and the Hungarian Act on Public Education of 2011, guaranteeing free education and earlier compulsory schooling.

Current issues include a difficult diagnosis process (only about 8% of Hungarians with autism have official diagnoses), inaccessible older school buildings, limited inclusion, reliance on frontal teaching methods, lack of special education training for general education teachers, low teacher pay (the worst in the OECD), and teacher attrition, though church-run schools show higher retention. The authors recommend improving teacher training, accessibility, diagnosis procedures, and teacher compensation.

President Trump suggested that some federal workers furloughed during the government shutdown, now in its seventh day, may not receive back pay, saying "it depends on who we're talking about." This position conflicts with the administration's own recent Office of Personnel Management guidance and a 2019 law stating furloughed workers shall be paid for the lapse in appropriations. The administration has also warned of permanent layoffs, with Trump saying details would come "in four or five days." Democrats, who want an extension of Affordable Care Act premium tax credits included in any resolution, have dismissed the threats. President Reagan, speaking at the University of Virginia, reflects on Thomas Jefferson's enduring influence on the university, American higher education, and the idea of self-government, drawing parallels between the partisan conflicts of Jefferson's era and a new Jeffersonian populism that rejects excessive regulation, taxation, judicial activism, and insular foreign policy.

He describes a global democratic revolution, citing Freedom House figures showing more people living in freedom than ever before, alongside a worldwide shift toward free-market economics. He reviews diplomatic achievements with the Soviet Union: the INF treaty eliminating an entire class of nuclear missiles, START negotiations for 50-percent reductions in strategic weapons, progress on regional conflicts in Afghanistan, Cambodia, and Angola, human rights improvements, and expanded exchanges.

Reagan offers three reflections: first, Soviet-American progress remains in doubt and requires skepticism—"trust but verify"—military strength, and public candor about fundamental differences; second, Soviet changes were not inevitable but resulted from Western strength and resolve, though Gorbachev's steps deserve credit; third, foreign policy succeeds when the President and Congress cooperate but falters when they act as adversaries, as over Central America, and congressional restrictions hamper presidential flexibility. He closes with the lesson of Jefferson and Adams' late-life reconciliation, urging tolerance and affirming the enduring question of whether self-government is possible.

In a question-and-answer session, Reagan states that most-favored-nation status for the Soviet Union depends on deeds matching words; the PLO's acceptance of stated conditions marks a step toward Middle East peace, which must be negotiated by the principals; his policy of complete resistance to terrorism will continue under the incoming administration; he advises young people to vote and supports a balanced budget amendment and line-item veto; he cites restored military strength, economic recovery through tax cuts and deregulation, and nearly 19 million new jobs as accomplishments; and he plans post-presidency speaking, possibly a book, while Nancy Reagan continues her antidrug campaign.

Scientists at Newcastle University have produced the first 3D printed human corneas, a technique that could eventually provide an unlimited supply for transplant. Stem cells from a healthy donor cornea were mixed with alginate and collagen to create a bio-ink, which was extruded in concentric circles using a simple, low-cost 3D bio-printer in under 10 minutes; the stem cells then grew. The gel kept cells alive while remaining firm enough to hold its shape. By scanning a patient's eye, the team printed corneas matching individual size and shape. Led by Professor Che Connon, the research is published in Experimental Eye Research, though further testing means transplants are likely several years away.

This study developed a rapid, reproducible method for selecting AI-detected chest X-ray (CXR) abnormalities to prioritise urgent reporting and support faster lung cancer diagnosis. Conducted across seven acute trusts in Greater Manchester, it used two cohorts: a retrospective cohort of 1,282 patients with confirmed lung cancer and abnormal CXR (June 2020–June 2022) to calculate sensitivity, and a prospective cohort of 13,802 GP-referred CXRs (June–July 2024), with the Annalise Container CXR system (detecting up to 124 findings) run in shadow mode to estimate specificity, assuming 1% detectable cancer prevalence. Findings were classified as CRITICAL, HIGH, or STANDARD, and three prioritisation strategies were evaluated. Strategy 1 (19 findings with prevalence ratio >5) achieved 92.82% sensitivity and 87.21% specificity; Strategy 2 (41 HIGH findings) achieved 97.27% sensitivity but 62.68% specificity; Strategy 3 (32 findings incorporating clinical judgement) achieved 95.87% sensitivity, 79.11% specificity, and 99.95% negative predictive value. The authors conclude this data-driven approach balances sensitivity and NPV, though limitations include single-region data, an assumed reference standard, and count-level analysis; external validation and multicentre studies are planned.

The NFP (Non-Farm Payrolls) report, released monthly by the US Department of Labor on the first Friday at 8:30 am Eastern time, shows the number of new jobs created in US non-agricultural businesses during the previous month. It is a key indicator of US economic health and influences Federal Reserve interest rate decisions, as the FOMC may interpret high job numbers as inflationary pressure warranting a rate hike, or low numbers as weakness warranting a cut. The report causes significant market volatility and affects all financial markets, with the bond market being most impacted—higher NFP figures tend to depress bond prices due to the prospect of rate hikes and inflation, while lower figures are positive for bonds. In equities, positive NFP data boosts investor sentiment, while in forex, figures beating consensus are bullish for the USD and lower figures are bearish. The report also affects gold, oil, gas, and energy. Backtests on SPY since 1993 showed an average gain of 0.09% from open to close on NFP days, while TLT averaged -0.02%; over the following 1-5 days, both stocks and bonds performed poorly. The article concludes that it is difficult to trade NFP numbers, as they are hard to predict, and no edge has been found in trading on macro numbers.

The lecture examines the relationship between eigenvalues and pseudorandomness in graphs, focusing on n, d, λ graphs: d-regular graphs on n vertices whose eigenvalues, other than the top one (equal to d), are bounded by λ in absolute value. By the expander mixing lemma, smaller λ corresponds to stronger pseudorandomness.

Cayley graphs, built from a group Γ and a symmetric subset S (vertices are group elements; edges come from multiplication by S), are an important source of examples. The Paley graph—on the cyclic group mod p (p prime, 1 mod 4) with S the nonzero quadratic residues—is shown to be pseudorandom by explicitly computing eigenvectors (built from roots of unity) and eigenvalues, which reduce to Gauss sums; all non-trivial eigenvalues are small relative to the degree (p−1)/2. For Abelian groups, Cayley graph eigenvalues correspond to Fourier coefficients; for non-Abelian groups, representation theory plays the analogous role.

A theorem of Conlon and Zhao states that for all Cayley graphs, including non-Abelian ones, the discrepancy property (DISC) is equivalent to the eigenvalue property (EIG) up to constant factors: EIG(ε) implies DISC(ε), and DISC(ε) implies EIG(8ε). This equivalence fails for general graphs—a large random d-regular graph with a disjoint copy of K_{d+1} satisfies DISC but has second eigenvalue d—while the reverse implication follows from the expander mixing lemma. The proof of the hard direction uses Grothendieck's inequality, which states that a semidefinite (vector-valued) relaxation of a certain bilinear maximization over ±1 values exceeds the original by at most a constant factor k (best known k ≈ 1.78; the optimal Grothendieck constant is unknown but exceeds 1), combined with a symmetrization trick exploiting group rotations to bound the spectral radius by 8εd.

Finally, the lecture addresses how small λ can be. The Alon-Boppana bound says that for fixed d, the second largest eigenvalue is at least 2√(d−1) − o(1). Two proofs are given: one via the Courant-Fischer characterization, constructing weighted vectors around vertices at distance at least 2r and combining them to be orthogonal to the all-1's vector; the other via the trace (moment) method, counting closed walks of length 2k and lower-bounding them using Catalan numbers in the infinite d-regular tree. The constant 2√(d−1) is the spectral radius of the infinite d-regular tree, the universal cover of d-regular graphs. Future lectures will cover graphs achieving this bound and then begin graph limits.

The Bridgeton National Bank sued Hepner to recover $1,400 on a promissory note made to the Kil-Tone Company and endorsed to the bank. Hepner defended that the original note was given for stock purchased through the company's fraudulent representations and a promise the note would not be negotiated unless the stock was resold at a profit, and that the bank had notice. He sought to prove this by showing the bank's cashier, who also served as the Kil-Tone Company's treasurer, knew of and participated in the fraud. The trial court excluded this testimony, holding the cashier's knowledge could not be attributed to the bank, and directed a verdict for the plaintiff. Applying precedent that an agent's knowledge binds a principal only when the principal would have received notice, the court declined to presume the company would have disclosed the facts to the bank's directors and discharged the rule to show cause.

The article discusses the Real Estate Select Sector SPDR Fund ETF (XLRE) and argues that lower interest rates in the US and globally signal a potential rebound for the housing sector and related cyclical stocks over the next one to four years. Recent tariffs on lumber and wooden goods favor domestic manufacturers over importers, though trade deals could shift this dynamic. While a subprime-like crisis risk exists due to loose lending, current leverage appears lower than in 2007, supporting a diversified, high-upside approach to housing-related stocks. The author is a Brazil-based regulated investment analyst with five years of experience and an MBA in Macroeconomics and Portfolio Management, and discloses no positions in the mentioned companies.

On appeal from a 1916 Kings County conviction of grand larceny in the first degree (sentence to Sing Sing, maximum ten years, minimum five), the Appellate Division, Second Department, reversed the judgment as to defendant Solomon Montlake and granted a new trial. The court held that a trial judge may discharge a jury during trial, before submission, when a substantial reason arises, with the defendant's remedy being a plea of former jeopardy at the new trial rather than habeas corpus; after submission, discharge is limited to instances specified in section 428 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The prior dismissal of the jury—following the assistant district attorney's repeated accusations against defense counsel in the jury's presence—was a proper exercise of discretion, and the record indicated the discharge occurred with the defendant's consent, given his counsel's earlier motion to withdraw a juror. Permitting cross-examination of an alibi witness about unpaid rent was an unwise exercise of discretion but not reversible error, as it did not tend to show moral turpitude. However, the charge on alibi—requiring the jury to find the defendants "could not have been at the place" of the crime before acquitting—was reversible error, as it demanded exclusion of a bare possibility of presence. The burden of proof as to alibi is not on the defendant, and the specific charge was not cured by general statements placing the burden on the People.

This passage documents AMD AGESA™ software interfaces, initialization procedures, call-outs, and configuration controls. It describes AmdReadEventLog, which reads the oldest entry from a circular event log buffer (returning zero in EventInfo if empty), and AmdReleaseStruct, which frees storage allocated by AmdCreateStruct. Boot-time entry procedures are detailed: AmdInitReset performs minimal processor initialization after reset and allocates up to three execution cache regions subject to alignment and boundary rules; AmdInitEarly performs full processor initialization and accepts platform configuration parameters (C-State settings, Core Performance Boost, DMI/PState/CRAT/CDIT/WHEA table generation, power and frequency limits, VRM properties, and PCIe/GNB settings); AmdInitPost initializes system memory with options for bank/node/channel interleaving, ECC, memory training modes, and UMA allocation; AmdInitEnv transfers HOB/artifact data from pre-memory storage to permanent host-controlled buffers; AmdInitMid configures graphics display hardware; AmdInitLate generates ACPI and DMI information tables for the operating system; and AmdInitRtb performs final Ready-To-Boot configuration and saves registers for system suspend. Resume-path procedures (AmdInitResume, AmdInitS3LateRestore, AmdS3FinalRestore) restore saved processor and silicon context using NvStorage and VolatileStorage data. The document also specifies required host-environment call-outs (AgesaAllocateBuffer, AgesaDeallocateBuffer, AgesaDoReset, AgesaLocateBuffer, AgesaReadSpd, AgesaRunFcnOnAllAps) and optional call-outs for IDS data reading, heap rebase, memory timing hooks, external Vref control, and FCH customization. Finally, it lists build options (BLDOPT_REMOVE_*) for removing code such as DIMM, ECC, socket, and S3 support from the build, and build configuration elements (BLDCFG_*) for platform-specific settings including VRM limits, frequencies, PCI MMIO, IO APIC counts, and ACPI table customization.

This passage is from the SD Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 and describes SD memory card commands, functions, and performance specifications.

**Application-Specific Commands (CMD55/ACMD):** APP_CMD (CMD55) causes the card to interpret the following command as an application-specific command (ACMD). The APP_CMD bit in responses signals ACMD expectation. Undefined ACMDs are treated as regular commands; illegal ones are handled as illegal commands. Certain ACMD numbers are reserved. ACMD41 responses do not include APP_CMD status.

**Switch Function Command (CMD6):** CMD6 switches or expands card functions across four function groups: Access Mode, Command System, Driver Strength, and Power Limit. It is mandatory for Version 1.10+ cards, valid in Transfer State, and returns an R1 response plus 512 bits of status data. Functions return to default after power cycle, CMD6 (Mode 1, Function 0), or CMD0. Mode 0 queries supported functions and maximum current/power consumption; Mode 1 sets functions. The default Power Limit is 0.72W. In UHS-II mode, Function Group 4 support is mandatory.

**Other Commands and Modes:** High-Speed mode provides 25 MB/sec at 50 MHz via CMD6 and is optional. CMD8 verifies card operation at the host supply voltage and returns R7. SDHC/SDXC cards use block addressing with fixed 512-byte blocks, while SDSC uses byte addressing with CMD16-set block lengths. The host may lower or stop the clock with restrictions, including providing 8 clocks after transactions.

**Error Handling and Timing:** CRC7 protects commands and responses; CRC16 protects data blocks. Read timeout is 100 ms; write busy is up to 250 ms (500 ms for SDXC in certain cases). Commands are 48 bits, organized into Card Command Classes, with response types R1–R7 and three status fields (Card Status, SD Status, Task Status).

**Speed Class Specifications:** Three methods classify card performance: Speed Class (2, 4, 6, 10), UHS Speed Grade (1, 3), and Video Speed Class (6–90). These use Allocation Units (AU), Recording Units (RU), and performance parameters (Pw, Pm, Pr), with FAT/CI update timing rules and the CMD20 Speed Class Control command for SDXC recording optimization.

This study proposes excess deaths and years of potential life lost (YPLL) as metrics for tracking racial health inequities in the United States, building on the 1985 Heckler Report, which documented nearly 60,000 excess deaths annually among Black people relative to White people. Using CDC WONDER death certificate data for non-Hispanic Black and White people under age 85 from 1999 to 2020, the researchers calculated age-adjusted excess mortality and YPLL rates by sex, cause of death, and age.

Over the 22-year period, there were an estimated 658,356 excess deaths among Black females and 1,154,108 among Black males, along with approximately 35 million and 47 million excess YPLL, respectively. Excess mortality declined from 1999 to 2011 among males (404 to 211 per 100,000) and to 2015 among females (224 to 87), then plateaued through 2019. In 2020, rates rose sharply to 395 (males) and 192 (females) per 100,000, returning to levels similar to those one to two decades earlier, coinciding with the COVID-19 pandemic. COVID-19 itself accounted for excess mortality of 47 per 100,000 among females and 80 among males in 2020.

Heart disease was the leading cause of excess mortality for both sexes. Excess deaths were highest among infants (654 per 100,000 females; 776 among males) and increased with age, peaking at 75–79 years, while excess YPLL was greatest among the youngest age groups. The authors conclude that despite earlier progress, gains were erased by 2020, current efforts to eliminate mortality disparities are failing, and publicly reported race-based YPLL metrics could support national accountability and motivate new strategies.

Japan's government raised its business sentiment assessment in April, the first upgrade in four months, after the Bank of Japan's tankan survey showed improved corporate mood. The overall economic assessment remained unchanged for a fifth month, citing gradual recovery with pockets of weakness, supported by recovering exports and factory output.

One officer and two gunmen, including a Barrio 18 leader suspected in more than a dozen murders, were killed and eight officers wounded when the gang attacked police searching for illegal weapons in a poor San Salvador neighborhood. The officers suffered superficial wounds; four have been released. El Salvador recorded 60 homicides per 100,000 inhabitants in 2017.

The passage explains the Simple Moving Average (SMA), a technical analysis tool that averages a security's closing prices over a specified period to identify trend direction and potential support/resistance levels. It is calculated by summing closing prices over "n" periods and dividing by n, updating continuously as new prices arrive. Shorter SMA periods react quickly to price changes and suit short-term trading, while longer periods smooth volatility and suit long-term analysis. The SMA is a lagging indicator built on past prices; shortening the period reduces lag but increases false signals.

Backtests of four moving average crossover systems showed stocks exhibit short-term mean reversion: buying when the close crosses below a short-term moving average is more profitable (the 5-day MA returned 8.34% CAGR versus 9% for buy-and-hold). For longer averages, trend-following works better—buying when the close crosses above is more profitable, with the 200-day MA returning 7.89% CAGR and roughly half the maximum drawdown of buy-and-hold (28% vs 56%). The best result came from buying when the close crossed above the 200-day MA and holding for 200 days, averaging 10.93% per trade.

Compared to the EMA, which weights recent prices more heavily and reacts faster, the SMA treats all prices equally and has more lag, making it preferable for smoother long-term strategies. The authors prefer the SMA and believe most traders use it, though they consider the two not very different.

The SMA can be misleading with seasonal or cyclical stocks, generates false signals in range-bound markets, and its starting point can skew values in volatile markets. It can also be applied to non-price data such as volume or economic indicators. There is no universally best SMA period—backtesting per asset is required—and the SMA works best as one parameter among several, such as a trend filter.

U.S. colleges are preparing for disruption around Oct. 7 anniversary demonstrations. Columbia requires advance protest plans for Oct. 6–8 and restricted guest passes citing safety. The University of Maryland limited campus access; its Students for Justice in Palestine plans Gaza solidarity events. Thirty-seven lawyers, including 10 partners with expertise in collateralized loan obligations and asset-backed lending, have left Cadwalader, Wickersham & Taft for Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe, joining offices in Charlotte, London, Washington, D.C., and New York. Bloomberg Law counted 33 partner departures from Cadwalader this year; Law360 reported at least 23 excluding retirements. Cadwalader's revenue ranking fell from No. 39 in 2007 to No. 85 by the end of 2024, though profits per equity partner averaged $3.7 million in 2024. The firm is pursuing a "shake-up path," adding second managing partner Wesley Misson alongside Patrick Quinn, but has still lost nearly a fifth of its partnership this year.

Yahoo is in advanced talks to sell AOL to Milan-based tech firm Bending Spoons for about $1.4 billion, though no deal is signed. Bending Spoons, with over 300 million monthly app users, recently agreed to take Vimeo private. Music labels could reach licensing agreements with AI companies—including Google, Spotify, and startups like Suno and Udio—within weeks, seeking micropayments for AI-generated tracks. This patent application, a continuation of earlier filings dating to 2017–2020, concerns enabling operation of carrier aggregation and scheduling in multicarrier communication systems. It describes OFDM subcarrier arrangements, guard bands, and carrier timing structures supporting FDD and TDD, with 10 ms radio frames divided into subframes and slots, and scalable numerologies from 15 kHz to 480 kHz subcarrier spacing. Radio resources are organized into resource elements, resource blocks, and resource block groups. Uplink and downlink physical channel processing (scrambling, modulation, layer mapping, precoding, resource mapping, and OFDM/DFTS-OFDM signal generation) is outlined, along with base station and wireless device architectures comprising communication interfaces, processors, and stored program code.

The disclosure covers 5G network architecture in which base stations interconnect via Xn interfaces and connect to an NGC via NG-C and NG-U interfaces. Cells are categorized as primary (PCell) or secondary (SCell) with associated component carriers. Multi-connectivity is described, where a UE connects to a master gNB and one or more secondary gNBs using MCG, SCG, or split bearers, with separate MAC entities and cell groups. Serving cells may be grouped into timing advance groups (a pTAG containing the PCell and one or more sTAGs, up to four per cell group), with random access procedures and initial timing alignment for secondary TAGs. PUCCH offloading to SCells, PUCCH groups, and per-TAG time alignment timers are addressed. Tight interworking architectures between 5G RAN (gNB) and LTE RAN (eNB/eLTE eNB) are presented, including master/secondary base station roles and bearer structures. gNB deployment may be centralized (CU/DU) or non-centralized, with eight functional split options configurable per CU, DU, UE, bearer, or slice. Network slicing support via slice IDs/NSSAI for routing NAS signaling is described.

Further embodiments address LAA operation in unlicensed spectrum using listen-before-talk (LBT) procedures (Categories 2–4), energy detection thresholds, discontinuous transmission, and channel reservation. Logical channel configuration covers identifiers, groups, mapping to TTIs/numerologies and cells, per-numerology priorities, and logical channel prioritization for MAC PDU formation. Bandwidth part (BWP) configuration, activation/deactivation, default BWP behavior, BWP switching timers, common and group-common search space monitoring, and CORESET configuration based on BWPs are also described.

On April 3, 2015, Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC under Items 2.02 (Results of Operations and Financial Condition) and 7.01 (Regulation FD Disclosure), stating that it had published a press release dated April 3, 2015, attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by Deepak Ahuja, Chief Financial Officer. The content of the press release itself is not included in the filing.

The speaker thanks his predecessor and marks the inauguration as a new beginning, urging renewed faith in the nation's founding dream of spirituality and human liberty. He calls for a new national spirit of unity and trust, acknowledging the country's limits while committing to competent and compassionate government, human rights, equality of opportunity, fair laws, and preservation of natural beauty. He argues that strength at home underpins strength abroad and that America should demonstrate its democratic system as worthy of emulation, help shape a just and peaceful world, and favor societies respecting individual human rights. He pledges strength sufficient that it need not be proven in combat, perseverance in limiting armaments and eliminating nuclear weapons, and hopes to build a lasting peace based on the nation's values rather than weapons.

The DAWN-Plasma trial was a randomized, multicenter, open-label phase II proof-of-concept study evaluating the efficacy and safety of convalescent plasma added to standard of care versus standard of care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Between May 2020 and January 2021, 489 patients were randomized 2:1 to convalescent plasma (n=326; 320 in the full analysis set) or control (n=163). The intervention consisted of 4 units (800–1000 mL) of high-titer convalescent plasma (80.7% of units from donors with NT50 ≥1/320), with the first dose given within 12 hours of randomization and the second 24–36 hours later. The primary endpoint—proportion of patients alive and free of mechanical ventilation at Day 15—did not differ between groups (83.7% vs 84.1%; OR 0.99, p=0.976), and no secondary endpoints showed significant differences. Adverse events, serious adverse events, and fatal events were similar between groups; transfusion-related side effects occurred in 19/320 plasma-group patients (5.9%), with no TRALI cases reported. Neutralizing antibody titers increased from baseline to Day 6 but were unaffected by the intervention, although higher titers at Day 0 and Day 6 correlated with better outcomes. The study concluded that early transfusion of high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma did not significantly improve clinical status in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.

This prospective, hospital-based study assessed surgical diagnoses and post-operative outcomes of adult intestinal obstruction at three public regional referral hospitals in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania (December 2021–July 2022). Among 228 patients (75.4% male; median age 34 years), adhesions were the commonest surgical diagnosis (n=98; OR 5.7), followed by hernia (48), volvulus (37), and abdominal tumors (20). Median hospital stay was 4 days. Outcomes included discharge in 76%, superficial surgical site infection in 9%, 8 referrals, 12 deaths (crude mortality 5.3%), and 12 unknown outcomes. No significant differences in outcomes were found among the hospitals. The authors note that the predominance of adhesions—typically reported in developed settings—may reflect a changing epidemiology or referral bias, since hernias may be managed at lower-level facilities. Male preponderance is consistent with prior literature. The observed mortality falls within the wide range (0–42.2%) reported elsewhere, with advanced age a common predictor of death. Study strengths include its prospective design and enrollment of all eligible patients; a noted limitation was the use of odds ratios rather than absolute risks.

Averaging down is a trading strategy in which an investor buys more shares of a stock after its price falls, lowering the average purchase price and reducing the increase needed to break even. For example, buying 100 shares at $45 and another 100 at $30 lowers the breakeven point to $37.50. However, averaging down does not automatically produce breakeven—the stock must still rise, and prices can continue falling. Whether it is a good strategy depends on circumstances: it can work as part of a planned scale-in entry strategy, particularly for long-term investors familiar with the company, but is risky for short-term traders who cannot distinguish temporary declines from serious drops. A backtest on SPY using RSI-based buy signals, with equity split into two 50% positions, showed that averaging down improved trading metrics, produced a smoother equity curve, reduced drawdowns, and used capital more efficiently. The authors conclude that stocks are the best asset class for averaging down because they are prone to mean reversion, while other markets carry higher risk of failure.

The Personalized Medicine Conference, held in South San Francisco since 2008 in partnership with San Francisco State University's Department of Biology, SF State Alumni, and the City of South San Francisco, will host Personalized Medicine 10.0 on June 2, 2017. Titled "Has It Changed Your Life?", the event will review past topics, assess prior predictions, and look to the future of personalized medicine, covering themes such as bioinformatics, oncology, epigenetics, rare disease genomics, sequencing technologies, the microbiome, gene therapy, and genome editing. Opening keynote speaker Amylynne Santiago Volker, whose son was the first person saved by genetic sequencing, will address challenges in provider adoption and insurance coverage. Founded by Michael Goldman and three SF State alumni, the conference features speakers from academia and industry, and registration is open to all.

This work investigates how structural information can be incorporated into Bayesian optimization for therapeutic antibody development. While antibodies require both target binding and developability properties (thermostability, low hydrophobicity, expression), existing Bayesian optimization approaches have not used structural information, and it is unclear whether it benefits developability or binding properties—particularly when the antibody-antigen binding pose is unknown. The authors examine when structural information aids optimization, whether antibody-specific structural models outperform general protein models, and whether structure is necessary, comparing against sequence-only approaches in low-data regimes. They also propose a protein language model "soft constraint" for incorporating sequence-only prior information.

The Fund is the consolidated entity formed by the reorganizations of seven Aberdeen funds into Aberdeen Chile Fund, Inc., renamed effective April 30, 2018 and trading on the NYSE American Exchange under ticker "AEF." It pursues a multi-cap emerging markets equity income strategy, may use leverage (currently unused), and invests at least 80% of net assets in emerging market equity securities, seeking current income and long-term capital appreciation. As of May 25, 2018, its largest holding was Tencent Holdings (6.45%), with cash and equivalents at 5.81%. A tender offer and special distribution aggregating approximately 41% of assets as of April 27, 2018 could further change portfolio composition. Figures are unaudited, holdings are subject to change, and there is no assurance the Fund will achieve its objectives.

This study compared a chest radiograph-based biological aging model (CXR-Age) with epigenetic clocks (Horvath Age and DNAm PhenoAge) in 2,097 participants from the Project Baseline Health Study. CXR-Age, a deep learning model estimating biological age from chest X-rays, correlated moderately with chronological age (r=0.50), whereas epigenetic clocks correlated strongly (r≈0.93–0.95), and CXR-Age acceleration showed no significant association with epigenetic clock acceleration.

CXR-Age acceleration was associated with higher coronary artery calcium, higher 10-year ASCVD risk, lower pulmonary function (particularly DLCO), reduced physical performance (grip strength, walking tests, balance), and greater disability. DNAm PhenoAge showed similar associations, while Horvath Age did not. CXR-Age associations with functional measures were significant in adults as young as 45, unlike DNAm PhenoAge.

Plasma proteomic analysis linked CXR-Age acceleration to CDH13 and ApoD, and DNAm PhenoAge to thirteen proteins including CDH13; no proteins were associated with Horvath Age. Chest X-rays with the highest acceleration more often showed lung abnormalities.

The authors conclude CXR-Age captures aging-related cardiopulmonary decline and frailty, potentially enabling opportunistic biological age screening from routinely obtained radiographs, though longitudinal and generalizability limitations remain.

Steve Stephens, 37, is suspected of killing Robert Godwin Sr., 74, in Cleveland and broadcasting it on Facebook Live. He cited his ex-girlfriend Joy Lane and his mother as reasons. Lane texted CBS News expressing condolences, calling Stephens kind and generous, and asking for privacy. Police are investigating and searching for Stephens.

This preprint presents PhenoID, a two-module natural language processing pipeline that extracts dysmorphic findings from free-text dysmorphology physical exam observations in the electronic health record and normalizes them to Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) terms. The pipeline uses Bio-ClinicalBERT transformers: an extractor performing sequence labeling (BIO schema) to identify spans of abnormal findings, and a normalizer classifying each extracted span into one of 11,988 HPO term IDs. Two heuristics (Noisy-BIO and Recast-BIO) were used to handle disjoint and overlapping mentions, and the system was trained to ignore normal findings.

The authors built a standardized EHR documentation system at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia and annotated 3,826 organ system observations (3,136 unique) from 1,655 individuals with 935 HPO terms, using four physician annotators (inter-annotator F1 of 0.844). PhenoID achieved a 0.717 F1 score for normalization, outperforming six competing systems (txt2hpo, Doc2HPO, NeuralCR, PhenoBERT, PhenoTagger). With gold-standard spans, the normalizer reached 0.82 F1, near human agreement. Error analysis identified ontology imperfections, descriptive phrasing, misplaced attention, and hyperonym predictions as leading error causes. The authors note limited author diversity as a limitation and suggest large language models may improve extraction and semantic understanding.
