New research demonstrates that limiting a resource needed by pathogens can harness competition between drug-sensitive and drug-resistant strains, preventing resistance from emerging and extending the usefulness of existing drugs. Published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, the study addresses the growing problem of drug resistance in HIV, tuberculosis, and malaria, which collectively kill nearly 3 million people annually. Researchers manipulated a nutrient in the drinking water of mice infected with malaria parasites alongside traditional drug treatment. When the nutrient was provided, treatment failed in 40% of mice due to resistant strains, but when the nutrient was limited, infection did not rebound in any mouse. The team confirmed this was due to competition among parasites, as resistant parasites survived when alone but were eliminated when sensitive parasites were also present. The researchers suggest this ecological approach could be integrated into drug development pipelines, potentially extending drug lifetimes at relatively low cost. Future work must identify which resources resistant strains require more than sensitive ones and determine optimal intervention strategies.

A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket is scheduled to launch Monday carrying Hewlett Packard Enterprise's "Spaceborne Computer," a supercomputer that could be the most powerful commercial, off-the-shelf computer to operate in space. It can perform one trillion calculations per second, roughly 30 to 100 times more powerful than an average desktop. Onboard processing could reduce the volume of data sent to Earth from high-definition satellite imagery, which requires 200 to 300 times more data. Unlike typical space hardware that undergoes "hardening," this computer uses special software to detect hazards such as high radiation and make adjustments. HPE's Mark Fernandez expects confirmation of boot-up on September 4, followed by about 2.5 hours of tests and a full year of operation. Success could pave the way for more powerful computers in space and aid future Mars missions, where communication lags make onboard data processing valuable.

This patent application describes methods, apparatus, systems, and computer-readable media for automatically classifying objects represented by 3D point clouds, particularly for objects at long range, in real time or near real time. The application is a continuation of prior filings and was developed with government support under a Department of Navy contract.

The background describes LIDAR (light detection and ranging) techniques, including direct ranging based on pulse travel time, chirped detection based on frequency differences between transmitted and returned signals (using heterodyne or homodyne detection), and phase-encoded detection. Chirped LIDAR uses long optical pulses with low peak power, with range accuracy determined by chirp bandwidth.

The core invention is a classification method that: obtains a 3D point cloud of an object's external surface; extracts surface normals to define translational and rotational invariant coordinate systems; extracts feature variable values; computes first and second classification statistics (e.g., spin images and covariance matrices) and matches them against statistics for N classes using two classifiers; and, if the classifiers disagree, computes a third statistic (e.g., iterative closest point) comparing the point cloud only to model point clouds of the two candidate classes. The object is assigned to a class, and a device is operated accordingly.

Hardware embodiments include heterodyne and homodyne chirped LIDAR systems comprising laser sources, modulators, splitters, telescopes, balanced photodetectors, and processors. Supporting sections cover k-d trees for nearest-neighbor searches, point cloud generation and surface reconstruction, and feature variables (α, β, θ, ρ, ψ) used to build spin images and covariance matrices trained via linear discriminant analysis and clustering.

Experimental results using a commercial LIDAR system tested objects including cones, boxes, pipes, and toy guns at ranges of 400–2000 meters, achieving high classification accuracy even among similar-shaped objects.

Apple Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended April 1, 2017 reports net sales of $52.9 billion, up 5% from $50.6 billion in the year-ago quarter, driven by growth in Services, Mac, and Other Products, partially offset by foreign currency weakness. Net income was $11.0 billion ($2.10 diluted EPS) versus $10.5 billion ($1.90) a year earlier; six-month net sales were $131.2 billion, up 4%. By product, iPhone sales rose 1%, iPad fell 12%, Mac rose 14%, Services rose 18%, and Other Products rose 31%. All geographic segments grew except Greater China, which declined 14%. Gross margin was 38.9% versus 39.4%, and total assets were $334.5 billion. During the quarter, Apple issued $11.0 billion of U.S. dollar-denominated debt, repurchased $7.0 billion of stock, and paid $3.0 billion in dividends. Term debt totaled $88.9 billion and commercial paper $10.0 billion. Gross unrecognized tax benefits were $8.8 billion. The filing discusses the European Commission's State Aid Decision ordering Ireland to recover up to €13 billion plus interest from Apple, which the Company and Ireland have appealed, and ongoing Samsung patent litigation involving $548 million in previously paid damages. The Company anticipates third-quarter gross margin of 37.5% to 38.5%.

The passage describes the NVIDIA Blackwell GPU architecture and GeForce RTX 50 Series. Blackwell's fifth-generation Tensor Cores support the FP4 data format, which reduces generative AI model memory requirements to less than half of FP16 while delivering over 2x performance versus the previous generation; for example, the FLUX.dev model requires under 10GB of VRAM at FP4 versus over 23GB at FP16.

The fourth-generation RT Core doubles ray-triangle intersection throughput and introduces Mega Geometry, which enables ray tracing of highly detailed geometry through Cluster-level Acceleration Structures (CLAS) and a Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structure (PTLAS), supporting level-of-detail systems like Nanite and real-time subdivision surfaces. Blackwell also adds hardware-accelerated Linear Swept Spheres for strand-like geometry such as hair, roughly 2x faster with about 5x less VRAM than triangle-strip methods. Shader Execution Reordering (SER) 2.0 features twice as efficient reorder logic, and a new AI Management Processor (AMP), a RISC-V-based scheduler, offloads GPU context scheduling from the CPU.

Blackwell adds hardware 4:2:2 encode/decode, a ninth-generation NVENC with improved AV1/HEVC quality and a new AV1 UHQ mode, a sixth-generation NVDEC with 2x faster H.264 decoding, and DisplayPort 2.1b support up to 80 Gbps. Max-Q improvements include advanced power gating, separate GPU and memory voltage rails, frequency switching 1000x faster than prior architectures, and sleep-state entry 10x faster than Ada, with up to 50% power savings shown in small language model inference.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, producing up to three AI-generated frames per rendered frame with a model that is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM, and replaces CNN-based models with transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA. Blackwell also introduces neural shaders via the Cooperative Vectors API, enabling RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces.

The document provides specifications for GB202 (RTX 5090), GB203 (RTX 5080/5070 Ti), and GB205 (RTX 5070), and concludes with NVIDIA legal and trademark disclaimers.

The London-St. Thomas unemployment rate rose to 5.5 per cent in September from 5.4 per cent in August, while the labour force fell by 3,000, down 9,300 year-over-year. Only about 75 per cent of residents aged 25-54 are working, last among 15 major Ontario cities. A King's University College study found only half of working adults have full-time permanent jobs with benefits; precarious work, more common among young people and minorities, was linked to stress, poor health, depression and family strain. Men aged 25-54 had a historic-low participation rate of 76.9 per cent. Canada's unemployment held at 6.2 per cent; Ontario's fell to 5.6 per cent, the lowest since 2000.

Children's cell phone ownership varies by country. In Germany, about 51% of children ages 6 to 13 own a mobile phone, and one American family found phones uncommon among third-graders in Berlin, while in California their daughter became the only student in her fourth-grade class without a smartphone; her parents plan to give her a flip phone next year and a smartphone in high school. A 2015 European study found about 46% of children 9 to 16 owned smartphones, with school restrictions and cost concerns varying by country. In the US, a Nielsen report found about 45% of children 10 to 12 had smartphones with service plans, and Common Sense Media reported 42% of children 8 and younger own tablets. In South Korea, 72% of children owned smartphones by ages 11 to 12, spending up to 5.4 hours daily. Among Taiwanese children, use rose from 45% of 11-year-olds to 71% of 15-year-olds. Turkish parents disagreed on the appropriate age, with most saying 12 to 17. In South Africa, 81% of secondary school students own or have access to a phone, while ownership in Ghana and Malawi is lower but rose between 2007 and 2014. In Australia, 31% of fourth-year primary students owned or used phones, rising to 43% a year later, with a median first-ownership age of 8. The American Academy of Pediatrics states there is no "right" age but recommends avoiding regular digital media for children under 18 to 24 months, limiting screen time to one hour daily for ages 2 to 5, and monitoring content.

The Renewable Energy Alaska Project (REAP), in partnership with Southeast tribes, is training residents from Kake, Angoon, Hoonah, Yakutat, and Metlakatla as energy assessors to conduct affordable home energy assessments in diesel-powered villages, where electric bills can reach several hundred dollars a month. Unlike private audits costing thousands of dollars, these assessments cost $25 and identify simple upgrades—such as LED bulbs or insulated coffee pots—that could reduce household electric bills by nearly 10 percent. Trainees practiced on a Juneau home and plan to offer assessments in their own communities. The Home Energy Leader Program runs through July 31.

This work presents the development of a classical EAM potential for the ternary tungsten-hydrogen-helium (W-H-He) system for radiation damage simulations relevant to fusion reactors. Tungsten is a candidate plasma-facing material, but irradiation and implantation of helium and hydrogen isotopes cause microstructural changes such as gas bubble formation, hardening, embrittlement, and increased tritium retention. Existing W-H-He potentials have limitations: the Bonny potential was not fitted to gaseous properties, while the Li and Yang potentials overestimate relaxation volumes and describe voids inaccurately due to errors in tungsten surface energies. The new potential builds on the Mason W-H potential, extended to include helium, and emphasizes two properties: binding energies of light gases to vacancy-type defects and defect relaxation volumes, which govern gas retention and irradiation-induced swelling.

The potential uses a generalized Finnis-Sinclair formulation permitting negative electron densities, with pair potentials constrained to the ZBL stopping model at short range. Fitting employed a loss function balancing defect formation energies, relaxation volumes, binding energies, and gaseous properties, optimized through a parallelizable importance-sampling algorithm followed by the Simplex method. DFT data were primarily sourced from literature, supplemented by new VASP calculations of hydrogen-helium cluster relaxation volumes. Specific functional forms were developed for W-He (weak, meV-scale interaction), the helium embedding function (repulsive response to electron density), He-He interactions (balancing high-pressure hcp DFT data with second virial coefficients), and H-He interactions (fitted to dimer binding energies). Charge density analysis showed non-negligible electronic interactions for helium within the tungsten lattice.

Republic Services of Southern Nevada has been charging commercial property owners trash fees that were never approved by local lawmakers in Las Vegas, North Las Vegas, Henderson, and Clark County. The Las Vegas City Council is set to introduce an ordinance Wednesday to codify these fees, which include container delivery, removal, exchange, and industrial dry run charges. Elected officials said they were unaware of the fees, with some unable to recall approving them. Republic said it provides municipalities an annual list of supplemental services containing the fees. A Henderson official said the fees possibly violate the ordinance.

This Mendelian randomization study investigated causal relationships among gut microbiota, plasma metabolites, and fibromyalgia (FM) using GWAS summary data from European populations. Six gut microbiota taxa showed causal effects on FM: family Enterobacteriaceae, genus Butyricicoccus, genus Coprococcus1, and order Enterobacteriales appeared protective, while genus Eggerthella and genus Ruminococcaceae UCG005 were risk factors. Eighty-two plasma metabolites were associated with FM, with enrichment in caffeine metabolism, alpha-linolenic acid metabolism, and GLP-1/incretin pathways. Mediation analysis identified 2,3-dihydroxypyridine and palmitoylcholine as mediators linking Enterobacteriaceae and Enterobacteriales to FM, with mediation proportions of 14.91% and 12.34%. The authors propose dietary interventions—limiting caffeine, increasing omega-3 intake, adopting a low glycemic index diet, and reducing oxalate consumption—to regulate metabolic pathways and alleviate symptoms. Limitations include the absence of demographic data for subgroup analyses, restriction to European ancestry populations, and the need for experimental and clinical validation of the MR findings.

Guinness has partnered with footballer Thierry Henry for the first time as part of its Made of Black campaign. Henry, known for his Arsenal career, will work with Guinness in Nigeria and across Africa to highlight people demonstrating the Made of Black spirit. The campaign launched in August 2014 on MTV Base. This season, Guinness will celebrate football fans through Fanzone activations and continue sponsoring EPL broadcasts via DStv.

NAB executive Andrew Hagger called advisers' false witnessing of superannuation documents "sloppy and unprofessional." The royal commission exposed wrongdoing in banks' and AMP's financial planning arms, prompting backflips despite years of reporting and inquiries. A CBA planner wiped out much of Joe Hockey's mother-in-law's savings.

This patent application, a continuation of several prior applications concerning magnet management MRI compatibility, describes an implantable medical device—exemplified by a cochlear implant but applicable to other hearing prostheses, pacemakers, and other implanted devices containing magnets. The background section reviews types of hearing loss (conductive and sensorineural), conventional hearing aids, bone conduction devices, and cochlear implants, as well as the concept of fitting medical devices to individual recipients.

The invention comprises a magnet housed within a body, typically made of an elastomeric material such as silicone, with structural components (plates) that sandwich the magnet. When the device is subjected to an externally generated magnetic field, such as from an MRI machine (e.g., 3 T), the field imparts a torque on the magnet, causing initial rotation. This rotation pushes the plates apart, stretching or displacing the elastomeric material, which generates an increasing restoring force that counteracts the torque and limits further rotation of the magnet.

Alternative embodiments include resilient components such as springs or pillars between plates, rigid housings with rails, long plates extending from a stimulator unit, curved or canted plate surfaces for nonlinear force responses, and bumpers or tracks to guide magnet movement. The magnet apparatus may be enclosed in a container permitting the magnet to revolve about its longitudinal axis while rotation relative to the plates is resisted. Plates may include holes or features for interlocking with the elastomeric material and can be made of materials such as PEEK or PTFE. A slit in the elastomeric housing enables insertion or removal of the magnet apparatus.
TCI Fund Management lowered its valuation of Zodiac Aerospace shares to 7-10 euros after the firm posted a first-half loss, while campaigning to pressure Safran to drop its takeover bid.

Stock futures were little changed after the S&P 500 snapped a seven-day winning streak. Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell said demand for AI computing power is "tremendous," and while "at some point there'll be too many" AI data centers, the company sees no signs of that yet. Dell shares rose over 3% after the company raised its long-term annual revenue growth target to 7%–9% from 3%–4% and its diluted EPS growth target to 15% from 8%. Its server networking business grew 58% last year and 69% last quarter, and Dell plans to ship $20 billion of AI servers in fiscal 2026, double last year's sales. The article presents three bullish candlestick patterns that backtested successfully: the Bearish Engulfing Pattern, Three Outside Down, and Bullish Harami. Although candlestick patterns generally have a poor reputation among quantitative traders due to a lack of rigorous testing, these three produced decent results. Tests were run on the S&P 500 via the SPY ETF from 1993 to October 2021, using an exit rule of selling at the close when the day's close exceeded the previous day's high. The Bearish Engulfing Pattern yielded a 5% CAGR over 296 trades with a 71% win ratio; Three Outside Down produced a 2.3% CAGR over 112 trades with a 78% win ratio; and Bullish Harami achieved a 3.1% CAGR over 306 trades with a 76% win ratio. Ironically, the Bearish Engulfing Pattern works as a bullish signal, contrary to textbook definitions.

Articles 2–9 of a 1942 agreement among Belgium, the United Kingdom, and the United States concern Congo products. Scheduled quantities are minima, with further purchases not precluded; prices require Belgian–UK or Belgian–US agreement; payment follows usual practice. The UK will ensure Congo products are not disadvantaged by customs duties relative to British colonial products, and the UK and US will deliver industrial supplies to the Congo within war-effort limits. Belgium will enforce Congo measures prohibiting transactions aiding enemy powers and an export licensing system coordinated with British-administered African territories. A State Department airgram to Ambassador Biddle comments on the draft tripartite agreement: it accepts a revision clause before December 31, 1943, requests agreed price lists, questions payment for unshipped goods (preferring warehouse receipts), rejects a shipping guarantee, and suggests options on total output and a Congo development article, citing pyrethrum production figures.

Turkish authorities issued detention warrants for 133 public servants, including 101 from the Finance Ministry and 32 from the Ministry of Labor and Social Security, over alleged Gülen movement links based on use of the ByLock messaging app; only four were on active duty. Related detentions included 14 women in a Uşak-based probe, at least 18 dismissed teachers in Aksaray and Ankara, 19 military personnel across nine provinces and Northern Cyprus, nine people in Kozan, and seven in a Bitlis-based investigation. Since the July 15, 2016 failed coup, which killed 249 people, the government has blamed the Gülen movement, arrested 50,510 people, and dismissed over 150,000 public servants.

This passage is from QuantifiedStrategies.com and lists articles on market timing strategies and indicators. Gregory Vinarsky et al.'s appeal from 2008 New York County Supreme Court orders was withdrawn pursuant to the parties' January 11, 2010 stipulation.

On September 20, 2016, Microsoft's Board of Directors amended Section 1.14 of its Bylaws (the proxy access bylaw) to clarify when groups of funds count as a single shareholder for the 3% ownership threshold, count loaned shares recallable within five business days (up from three) toward that threshold while eliminating the requirement they be recalled at the time of notice, clarify certain indemnification provisions, and reduce the voting support needed to re-nominate a proxy access candidate in one of the following two years from 25% to 15%. NVIDIA's Titan V has outperformed the Titan Xp and GTX 1080 Ti in leaked benchmarks, scoring 32,774 in Fire Strike despite lower clockspeeds. The card uses Volta architecture and HBM2 memory with 652.8 GB/s bandwidth, and performs well in games at 1440p. Priced around $3,000, it targets prosumers and developers with AI capabilities, though gamers may also want it. More affordable Volta-based cards are expected in 2018.

Sunderland manager David Moyes urged his relegation-threatened players to create more chances for Jermain Defoe, who has scored 14 of the club's 24 league goals. Bottom of the table, seven points from safety with 10 games left, Sunderland face Watford, Leicester City and Manchester United in eight days.

The passage discusses three technical indicators—RSI, ADX, and IBS—collectively called the "Big Three" for short-term trading. RSI, developed by Welles Wilder in 1978, is a momentum indicator oscillating between 0 and 100, with readings above 70 suggesting overbought conditions and below 30 oversold; backtests show two- and three-day periods work best for stocks. ADX, part of Wilder's 1978 Directional Movement System, measures trend strength without indicating direction; a 5–10 day period and a 30–40 threshold performed best. IBS measures the closing price relative to the high and low, oscillating between 0 and 1, with low values bullish and high values bearish. Backtests showed: IBS on QQQ yielded a 12.1% CAGR with a ~32% risk-adjusted return; RSI on SPY produced a 7.5% CAGR with ~18% risk-adjusted return; ADX on SPY yielded 6.5% CAGR. Combining two indicators on SPY produced a 56% risk-adjusted return, with 2018 the only losing year, and on QQQ a 1.3% average gain per trade with no losing years since 2000. While no "Holy Grail" strategy exists, these indicators complement each other for mean-reversion and trend-following strategies.

The former Glenwood School in Erie, closed years ago as a cost-saving measure, has reopened as Erie Federal Credit Union's corporate headquarters and ninth branch after an 18-month renovation. The 42,000-square-foot building offers full banking services and a community room preserving the school's history. Officials say the project returns the property to the tax rolls and allows room for future growth.

Beluga whales Qila and Aurora died at the Vancouver Aquarium in November 2016 from an unidentified toxin, not bacteria or viruses. Their DNA enabled researchers to sequence the complete beluga genome, providing a baseline and tools to study the species and support conservation efforts.

After the unexpected outcomes of Brexit and the U.S. election, the author argues that Marine Le Pen's victory in the French presidential election cannot be ruled out. Her main rival, François Fillon, has been weakened by a scandal over employing his wife as a parliamentary aide. Meanwhile, riots in Paris suburbs—sparked by the alleged police rape of a young black man—have led to nearly 250 arrests, with a leaked report citing over 50 violent incidents in one night. Citadel Securities hired Anthony Cronin from Societe Generale to head Treasuries trading in Europe, extending its market-making across the European day, part of Asia hours, and the Middle East. The firm also hired Michele How for fixed-income sales in London and Daniel Gottlander to lead U.S. interest-rate swaps trading. It has about 100 Treasuries clients in 17 countries, which it expects to double this year. Treasuries traded totaled $6 trillion in 2017, up from $5 trillion. After adding products like TIPS and strips, it likely seeks to become a Fed primary dealer.

The Chaikin Oscillator, developed by Marc Chaikin in the 1980s, measures accumulation and distribution as well as the momentum of stock moves, oscillating around zero. It is calculated in four steps: determining the money flow multiplier, calculating money flow volume, updating the Accumulation/Distribution Line (ADL), and subtracting the longer EMA of the ADL from the shorter one. The indicator generates signals through bullish or bearish divergences and crosses above or below the zero line. The authors tested ten Chaikin trading strategies and found no significant profitable results. A zero-cross strategy on the S&P 500 produced a CAGR of only 2.4% over twenty years, while a reversed strategy yielded 287 trades with a profit factor of 1.76 and a 37% max drawdown. Strategies combining the oscillator with RSI produced 216 trades each, with 0.3% average gains, profit factors of 1.6, and drawdowns of 17–18%. The authors concluded the indicator showed little value in their tests but might work with other criteria.

Zach Parise and Andy Greene discussed playoff frustrations after losing home games, saying the team has rebounded by refocusing. Parise noted the team created chances but failed to score, including a crossbar shot, and stressed that scoring is their responsibility. Video review showed strong offensive zone play despite being shut out twice in three games, which caused frustration. Greene said bus trips in earlier series kept the team fresh, and traveling again means fewer distractions; Parise added that extra rest and no time changes could help as the series progresses. Parise said turnovers cost them chances in overtime, and the opponent's penalty kill pressures well and holds the blue line, forcing more dump-ins. Greene said the opponent resembles Philadelphia, forechecks hard, and success depends on executing plays. Both felt the post-flight practice went well.

University of Kansas sociologist Brock Ternes surveyed 864 Kansans—48 percent private well owners, 52 percent municipal users—and found well ownership significantly correlates with increased watering during droughts, with conservation varying by well type. He attributes this to well owners' awareness of water supplies and crop irrigation, since precipitation reduces groundwater reliance in non-drought years. The over-pumped High Plains Aquifer may no longer support irrigation wells in southwestern Kansas within 25 years unless pumping is curtailed. Ternes will present his findings at the American Sociological Association's 2017 meeting in Montreal.
Dwyane Wade, Gabrielle Union and Zion Wade visited the Frost Museum of Science in Miami, enjoying a planetarium show, stingrays and tacos. Wade also responded on Twitter to a critic.

Investor Leon Cooperman, chair and CEO of Omega Family Office, says the market is in the late innings of a bull market—the stage Warren Buffett warned about in 1999, when crowds buy stocks simply because it seems a mistake to be out of them. He cites "ridiculously high" valuations for artificial intelligence companies, the S&P 500's nearly 40% rally since April lows led by mega-cap tech, and the Buffett Indicator at 217%, above Dotcom Bubble and 2021 peaks. Despite these risks, Cooperman considers stocks less risky than government bonds, which he dislikes due to elevated inflation eroding their real returns.

This patent application, a continuation of several related applications, describes an autonomous vehicle management system (AVMS), also called a controller system, that uses artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques to control autonomous vehicle operations safely. The background notes that while AI-based autonomous driving technologies have grown significantly, current solutions are not well equipped to ensure functional safety.

The AVMS receives sensor data (from onboard or remote sensors such as LIDAR, radar, cameras, GPS, IMU, and V2X sensors), generates and maintains an internal map representing the vehicle's state and environment, and generates a plan of action based on the map, goals, and safety considerations. It then controls vehicle systems (e.g., braking, steering, propulsion) to execute the plan. AI techniques used include convolutional neural networks for object detection and classification, and reinforcement learning (RL) for action selection.

Several safety techniques are described: (1) simulating "what-if" scenarios by modifying internal map parameters to project behavioral predictions and determine safe action sequences; (2) dynamically controlling sensor behavior—changing what data is captured or communicated, when, and how—to update the internal map on demand; (3) generating model confidence scores measuring how statistically similar an inferring data point is to the training dataset, with low-confidence predictions potentially overridden; (4) outputting information to users about planned future actions and the reasons for them, increasing trust and enabling manual override; and (5) an infrastructure for safe RL use, including a Safety Sanity Index (SSI) indicating safety performance and interruptible commands to override unsafe RL-selected actions.

The AVMS may comprise subsystems including a sensors interface, localization (vehicle positioning, map matching, visual odometry, dead reckoning), perception (building the internal map using multilayered graph data structures; object detection, classification, and tracking), planning (generating plans, what-if analysis, sensor control), controls (executing plans, monitoring dynamics, fail-safe actions), and an information subsystem for rendering feedback to users. Example processes and figures illustrating these components and methods are also described.

Several major school districts approved teachers union contracts with raises but lacked the funds to pay for them. Philadelphia, after agreeing to 3% annual raises, sought to borrow up to $1.5 billion, partly because a state budget impasse delayed funding and added about $15 million in interest costs. Chicago Public Schools approved raises in a four-year contract while facing a $734 million deficit; it considered delaying raises until the union threatened legal action, then adopted a $10.25 billion budget using refinancing to close the gap. Baltimore County rescinded a scheduled 5% raise, later settling on 3.05% after an impasse. Fairfax County received less than half the funding it requested from its board of supervisors and delayed raises. U.S. public school debt grew from $415 billion in 2013 to over $586 billion in 2023.

This patent application, a continuation of prior filings from 2018–2019, describes methods and apparatus for providing ACK/NACK feedback in wireless networks with multiple transmission reception points (TRPs), particularly in 5G NR systems. A base station may send a UE information indicating PDCCH monitoring occasions for each of multiple TRPs, whether ACK/NACK feedback across the TRPs is allowed, rules for performing ACK/NACK feedback bundling, and a DAI definition indicating whether DAIs transmitted by the TRPs are independent. The UE may transmit joint ACK/NACK feedback in a PUCCH based on the rules, or transmit multiple ACK/NACK feedback individually to first and second TRPs. In multi-TRP downlink transmission, either a single DCI grants a single transport block with layers from different TRPs, or multiple DCIs each grant one TB from a TRP. Bundling is useful when TRPs transmit the same payload for diversity, allowing a bundled ACK if at least one TB decodes successfully. For dynamic codebook determination, DAI may be defined jointly across TRPs (requiring tight coordination) or independently per TRP (suitable for non-ideal backhaul), with the base station indicating which definition applies. The UE determines the ACK/NACK codebook size based on the number of PDCCH monitoring occasions and DAIs in received DCIs. Multiple PUCCHs may be transmitted at different times, on different resources, or concurrently from multiple UL TRPs.

C-BerryTrans is a C++ code, licensed under GNU General Public License 3.0, that computes Berry curvature (Ω), anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC), and anomalous Nernst conductivity (ANC) within an ab initio framework. It extracts eigenvalues and momentum-matrix elements directly from WIEN2k (FP-LAPW) calculations and evaluates Ω using the Kubo-like formula. AHC is obtained by integrating Ω over the Brillouin zone weighted by the Fermi–Dirac distribution, while ANC applies entropy function weighting. Unlike Wannier-interpolation-based approaches (e.g., Wannier90, WannierTools), this direct method avoids interpolation errors and dependence on Wannier function quality. Band-resolved Ω is stored in binary files, enabling fast post-processing of AHC/ANC over user-defined ranges of temperature and chemical potential in a single run. Calculations are parallelized over k-points using OpenMP, with batched k-point processing to manage RAM usage. The code includes a klist_gen_div module for generating full-BZ k-lists, an energy-window feature to limit computed bands, and a visualization module (berryTrans_plot.py). Spin-orbit coupling must be included, as the transverse responses vanish without it. The code was validated on Fe (AHC) and Pd, Fe3Al, and Co2FeAl (ANC), with results compared to literature values. It is currently interfaced with WIEN2k but can be linked to other DFT packages such as ELK and Quantum Espresso.

Last week's market events—earnings, economic data, and policy news—were clouded by controversy, contradiction, or doubt, raising the probability of a new market tone. GDP beat expectations (3% vs. 2.5%) but remained distorted by tariff policies, while the jobs report disappointed with 73,000 additions versus 100,000 expected, accompanied by the largest two-month downward revisions on record since 1979 (excluding the pandemic). The FOMC meeting featured two dissenting votes, the first since the 1990s, and Powell maintained a patient, data-dependent stance. President Trump fired the BLS commissioner, announced nuclear submarine deployments toward Russia, announced tariff deals, and gained a Fed vacancy following Governor Kugler's resignation. Despite strong earnings—82% of S&P 500 companies beating EPS estimates and upward revisions at multi-month highs—the market ended with a bearish engulfing pattern, declining 2.2% to 4.2%, with all sectors down except Utilities. Featured cards include: a Discover card with 0% Intro APR for 15 months, 5% quarterly cash back, and a first-year Unlimited Cashback Match; a Bank of America card offering 6% cash back in a choice category for the first year plus a $200 online bonus; a Bank of America travel card with 25,000 bonus points and 1.5 points per dollar on purchases; a Citi card with 0% APR for 18 months on balance transfers and 2% cash back; Capital One Quicksilver with unlimited 1.5% cash back and $300 in welcome bonuses; Capital One VentureOne with 1.25 miles per dollar; and additional Citi cards offering bonus points and ThankYou Points rewards. World stocks rose on Monday, recovering from their biggest weekly losses of 2017, which had been driven by fears of a U.S.-North Korea nuclear standoff. European shares bounced after falling nearly 3 percent last week, and U.S. futures pointed to a higher open. Last week's losses were sparked by a war of words between Washington and Pyongyang, including North Korea's threat to fire missiles at Guam. Tokyo shares slipped 1 percent to three-month lows despite robust Japanese growth data, due to worries over the yen's surge. The dollar rose 0.5 percent to 109.70 yen after hitting four-month lows. This paper proposes a hybrid method-of-moments (MoM) and generalized scattering matrix (GSM) framework for multiscale electromagnetic problems involving antennas interacting with electrically large structures, such as radomes, reflectors, and implantation media. Unlike the existing MoM–T-matrix approach, whose efficiency is limited to O(N² log N) for large irregular structures, the proposed method inverts the roles: the large environment is discretized and solved by MoM, while the antenna is represented by a compact GSM, reducing unknowns and enabling modular reuse of precomputed antenna data. The framework can be extended into specialized variants, including a fully coupled GSM-PO hybrid for large reflectors that captures higher-order interactions, and a GSM+T-matrix hybrid for structures admitting spherical-wave expansions. The paper then derives the formulation: total fields are decomposed into incident, structure-scattered, and antenna components; PMCHWT integral equations are solved via MoM using RWG basis functions; antenna fields are expanded in vector spherical waves; and the antenna's GSM relates excitation and response vectors through port S-parameters, receiving, transmitting, and scattering matrices.

The Single/Double Offense uses double and down screens to free up a team's best shooter, requiring defenders to disrupt both screening actions. The basic NBA defensive approach is "Show and Recover" rather than switching, since "Bigs" screen for "Smalls" and switching would allow screeners to post up smaller defenders. This method involves dictating the shooter's preferred side, showing (stepping out) to force shooters wide, chasing under screens, and recovering to deny post passes while weakside defenders pack in. An alternative, the All Out SOS Disruption, uses aggressive trapping of the shooter on the wing, sequential and contact switches with Snuggle denial positions, and Triangle "I" rotations to force the offense into freelancing. Half court traps and inverting defenders to keep "Bigs" inside are also recommended tactics.

UBS has reaffirmed it will proceed with dividend increases and its share buyback programme despite Swiss regulators calling for higher capital buffers. CEO Sergio Ermotti said the shareholder return strategy remains on track, noting authorities have allowed flexibility to build capital without limiting payouts. Following heightened scrutiny after the Credit Suisse takeover, integration is progressing, with Swiss systems consolidation expected by early 2026 and most transfers outside Switzerland finalised. UBS outlined a USD 2 billion share repurchase programme running from mid-2025 to 2027. Analysts view the stance as a signal of financial strength, though some caution that balancing regulatory compliance with investor expectations may prove challenging if market conditions worsen.

The Russian ministry of marine deemed Captain Scullen's claim of $45,000 for five whales allegedly lost exaggerated, considering $2,500 sufficient compensation for losses from the temporary detention of the bark Cape Horn Pigeon. It also stated, based on Navy testimony, that Scullen himself declined lodgings and food offered at Vladivostok, contradicting his allegation that his crew was left without either. A telegram reported the vessel was seized by a Russian naval officer on September 10 while whaling in the closed Okhotsk Sea and taken to Vladivostok, where the crew was allegedly put ashore without food or shelter. Wurts requested an investigation and aid for the crew, while Chichkine later reported the bark's liberation and that the inquiry was proceeding.

Iceland's capital Reykjavik has endured an unusually gray, wet summer, with the worst May and June since 1914, while a heat wave continues in Britain and Scandinavia. High pressure over western Europe alters the jet stream, pushing rain toward Iceland. June brought only 70 hours of sunshine and a high of 13.2 degrees Celsius, two degrees below average; May saw rain every day. Residents are fixated on forecasts and often disappointed. Tanning salons are thriving while ice cream vendors, house painters, and pools struggle. A Reykjavik campsite reports slightly fewer guests, though some campers prefer the cool weather. A similar pattern occurred in June 1914, and locals remain hopeful.

Apple Inc.'s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 28, 2019, reports that the company designs, manufactures and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories, and sells related services. In 2019, it introduced iPhone 11, iPhone 11 Pro and iPhone 11 Pro Max, new versions of MacBook Air and Mac mini, iPadOS, two new iPad Pro models, iPad Air, an updated iPad mini, a 10.2-inch iPad, AirPods Pro and Apple Watch Series 5. Services include the App Store, Apple Music, Apple TV+ (expected November 2019), AppleCare, iCloud, licensing, Apple Arcade, Apple Card, Apple News+ and Apple Pay. In 2019, 31% of net sales came through direct channels and 69% through indirect channels; no single customer exceeded 10% of net sales. The company had approximately 137,000 full-time equivalent employees as of September 28, 2019. Risk factors cited include global economic conditions, intense competition, reliance on single or limited-source components and outsourcing partners primarily in Asia, legal proceedings, changing laws and regulations, data security, and foreign currency fluctuations. Total net sales were $260,174 million in 2019, down 2% from $265,595 million in 2018, driven by lower iPhone sales (down 14% to $142,381 million), partially offset by higher Wearables, Home and Accessories (up 41% to $24,482 million) and Services (up 16% to $46,291 million). Net income was $55,256 million versus $59,531 million in 2018. By segment, Americas net sales rose 4% to $116,914 million, Europe fell 3% to $60,288 million, Greater China fell 16% to $43,678 million, Japan fell 1% to $21,506 million, and Rest of Asia Pacific rose 2% to $17,788 million. Total gross margin was $98,392 million (37.8%), with Products at 32.2% and Services at 63.7%. In April 2019, the share repurchase authorization was increased from $100 billion to $175 billion; the company repurchased $67.1 billion of stock and paid $14.1 billion in dividends during 2019, and raised its quarterly dividend from $0.73 to $0.77 per share.

In a speech to the United Nations General Assembly, President Trump argued that the future belongs to sovereign, independent nations rather than globalists, and urged world leaders to put their own people first and defend their national foundations. He cited U.S. economic gains, including unemployment at its lowest level in over half a century, job growth, rising wages, and American leadership in oil and natural gas production, along with military rebuilding funded by over $2.5 trillion. He called on allies to pay their fair share of defense costs.

On trade, he highlighted the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement replacing NAFTA, a pending deal with Japan, and a planned agreement with the UK. He criticized China for trade abuses, intellectual property theft, and currency manipulation, noting tariffs placed on over $500 billion of Chinese goods, and said the WTO needs drastic change. He also urged China to honor its treaty commitments regarding Hong Kong.

Trump called Iran the world's leading state sponsor of terrorism, defended his withdrawal from the Iran nuclear deal, and described new sanctions following Iran's attack on Saudi oil facilities. He mentioned diplomacy with North Korea's Kim Jong Un and continued efforts in Afghanistan.

On immigration, he criticized illegal migration and open-border activists, thanked Mexico for deploying 27,000 troops to the border, and warned migrants they would be returned home. He condemned Venezuela's Maduro government as a Cuban puppet, noted a 55-country coalition recognizing Venezuela's legitimate government, and warned against socialism, stating America would never be a socialist country.

He also raised concerns about social media companies' power over speech, affirmed support for LGBTQ people and women's economic empowerment through the W-GDP initiative, defended religious freedom, opposed internationally funded abortion, and rejected the UN Arms Trade Treaty. He closed by urging leaders to strengthen their nations, saying the path to peace begins at home.
I am unable to summarize this passage.

Louisville officials advise residents against neighborhood fireworks on Independence Day, as smoke is particle pollution that can worsen air quality, aggravate asthma, and exceed federal limits. Airborne fireworks are illegal in city limits; the last exceedance was in 2015.

A student group at Ohio's Kenyon College, the Whiteness Group, founded by student Juniper Cruz, works to educate students on whiteness and work toward anti-racist actions. Run through the school's multicultural center, its first meeting drew about 50 students. Ground rules include barring white members from asking questions of people of color, encouraging unpopular opinions to be voiced, and prohibiting spreading rumors about meeting discussions. Cruz said the group aims to create sustainable activism, motivated by frustration with white students whose activism was limited to social media posts.

The Supreme Court appeared largely sympathetic to Colorado counselor Kaley Chiles, who is challenging the state's 2019 ban on conversion therapy for minors. A majority seemed to agree the ban discriminates based on the views she expresses, though some justices suggested sending the case back to lower courts to assess its constitutionality. The law bars mental health professionals from providing conversion therapy to clients under 18, with an exception for religious ministry. A federal trial judge denied Chiles' request to block enforcement, and the 10th Circuit affirmed, reasoning the ban regulates conduct and is subject to rational basis review. Chiles' lawyer argued the ban unconstitutionally restricts speech, a position shared by the Trump administration. Colorado's solicitor general countered that the ban regulates a harmful medical treatment, not speech, and noted similar bipartisan laws in 25 states. Justices debated standing, whether the ban regulates conduct or speech, and whether strict scrutiny should apply.

Excerpts from Texas Instruments documentation (2012–2014) present terminal functions for DDR2/DDR3 Memory Controllers 0 and 1 (Tables 4-5 and 4-6). Data strobe signals (DQS) for each byte of the 32-bit data bus synchronize transfers, serving as outputs when writing to DDR memory and inputs when reading; DQS[3] handles the upper byte (D[31:24]) and DQS[0] the lower byte (D[7:0]). On-die termination pins for chip selects 0 and 1 have internal pulldowns (IPD) enabled during reset and disabled (DIS) when reset is released. Controller 1 pins use internal pullups (IPU) during reset, some switching to IPD afterward. DQM signals and pin-type abbreviations (I, O, Z, S, GND, A, MM, DSIS) are also defined.

In Ry. Mfg. Co. v. Roden, the Curtis & Cook patent for an improvement in portable elevated railroads was considered. Uncontradicted testimony by Joseph H. Haynes that a similar single-track overhead railway was used at Camden Iron Works by 1866 led to claims 1, 2, and 3 being held void for anticipation. Claim 4, covering a main elevated track combined with branch tracks, a switch, and a traveler, was held valid and infringed, as Haynes admitted the defendant's track contained these elements. The presumption of patentability was not rebutted, and a decree was granted for the plaintiff on claim 4.

This study developed a cost-effective, culture-independent citizen science approach to survey the microbiome of household drinking water in China. Fifty tap water samples were collected by college student volunteers from 19 provinces between December 2020 and August 2021, including opportunistic samples following the 2021 Henan Floods and Typhoon In-Fa Landfall. Using a protocol optimized for low-biomass samples, 22 of 50 samples tested positive for microbial DNA. 16S rRNA gene metabarcoding on pooled samples identified 7,635 Amplicon Sequence Variants, revealing a diverse tap water microbiome. Pathogenic bacteria including Mycobacterium spp., Acinetobacter spp., and Legionella spp. were detected in all PCR-positive samples. Post-weather samples from Zhengzhou and Changzhou contained pathogenic species such as Salmonella enterica and toxin-producing cyanobacteria such as Microcystis spp. The study demonstrates the utility of citizen science for enhancing microbial monitoring of drinking water and informing public health strategies. Methods included volunteer recruitment from the Duke Kunshan University community, a standardized sampling kit with syringe filters, video tutorials, DNA extraction with bead-beating, PCR amplification of the 16S rRNA V4 region, and Illumina MiSeq sequencing processed through the DADA2 pipeline with Silva reference taxonomy assignment.

Dr. Pasvolsky stated that respect for international obligations, including treaties, was inherent in the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals, though enumerating it specifically might be discussed later. The Ambassador of Honduras recalled that Pasvolsky had agreed to include this phrase, while the Ambassador of Chile agreed with him but maintained the principle was not clearly part of international law. After a correction requested by the Ambassador of Venezuela, the previous minutes were approved. Discussion then turned to Chapter VI, where Pasvolsky explained that the Security Council must be both effective and representative; the five permanent members reflected the preponderance of military and industrial power, and nonpermanent members must outnumber permanent ones to prevent decisions by permanent members alone. The Ambassador of Brazil urged permanent Latin American representation on the Council.

A hockey player describes the disappointment of losing in the finals, though he was happy his brother won. He values time with his brother's family and the trust within their line, which Randy kept intact all year. He credits both goaltenders for their success.

Quarters coverage is a 4-deep, 3-underneath scheme widely used because safeties can support both the pass defense and the run game, allowing coordinators to adapt it against various offensive threats. Cornerbacks relate to the #1 receiver, safeties key the #2 receiver, outside linebackers cover the flats, and the middle linebacker serves as the middle hook defender. The two best ways to beat it are throwing to the flats and attacking the deep middle of the field. Flats are exploited by reading outside linebackers' post-snap movement, while aggressive safeties are vulnerable to play-action passes. The middle of the field can be opened by running safeties off, and overload concepts can create 1-on-1 matchups. The passage concludes with five example quarters-beater plays drawn from the BYU, Red Zone, Ohio State, Georgia, and Wake Forest playbooks.

Sixteen years ago, a Mexican boy badly injured in a pickup crash in California woke in a vegetative state in a San Diego hospital; nurses called him Pancho. A Texas woman saw his photo online, wondering if he was Gilberto.

North Carolina is expanding child care academies—short, low-cost training programs lasting two to six weeks with 20 to 64 hours of class time—operating in at least 11 counties to address early childhood educator shortages, which affect 60% of licensed providers. Two models exist: a classroom-ready model qualifying graduates to work in licensed facilities (but not as lead teachers), and a teaching credential model that includes EDU 119 coursework, qualifying graduates as lead teachers. A $1.476 million pilot passed the House but was excluded from the final budget signed by Gov. Stein, though the DCDEE offers grants up to $50,000 for up to 10 institutions. Programs in Wayne, Johnston, Stanly, McDowell, and Durham counties have graduated dozens of students, many entering child care jobs or higher education, funded by sources including the Camber Foundation, Dogwood Health Trust, and Duke Community Affairs.

Caffeine content varies among coffee chains: McDonald's contains 9 mg per ounce, Dunkin' Donuts 12.7 mg, Peet's 16.7 mg, Starbucks 20.6 mg, and Deathwish 54.2 mg—the world's strongest coffee. Research indicates people can drink more coffee than previously thought and may even live longer.

The Trump reflation stock market rally faces two inter-related problems: the Trump administration and high valuations. The failure of the healthcare bill underlines the risk of similar failures on tax cuts, infrastructure spending and deregulation. With the S&P 500's price-to-sales ratio at an all-time high and price/earnings ratios at levels last seen during the dotcom bubble, there is little room for error. Sentiment indicators have surged while hard data lags, with the Atlanta Fed forecasting 1.2 percent first-quarter growth. Some Fed officials cite rich asset prices as a reason to tighten policy faster. High valuations have historically predicted poor future returns. The author expects tax reform to be piecemeal, with repatriated cash funding buybacks, and considers a reflation unlikely.

This patent application, a continuation of earlier U.S. filings, relates to automated sortation systems, particularly robotic systems for sorting objects such as parcels. It describes drawbacks of conventional approaches: human-labor-based sorting with throughput and divert limits, tilt-tray or bomb-bay conveyors with high cost per divert, and manual sortation cells that do not overcome limits on the total number of collection bins.

The invention provides methods and systems for processing objects using programmable motion devices (e.g., robotic arms). An object is acquired from a mixed input stream, identifying indicia are perceived, and an intermediate station (collection bin) is dynamically assigned based on the object's destination, rather than using fixed bin-to-destination mappings. The mapping between intermediate containers and destinations changes dynamically during operation, and bins are emptied and reassigned when full or when further objects for that destination are unlikely.

Embodiments include sorting stations fed by input conveyors (including circulating loops and multiple conveyors), each with robotic systems, perception units, stacks of spare bins, and a central controller managing assignments. Unsorted objects may be returned to the input stream or routed to a manual sorting area. Dynamic allocation may draw on historical usage trends, current system state, object physical characteristics, facility layout, and other factors.

Further embodiments describe shuttle wing sortation stations, where a drop camera unit images objects that fall into carriages traveling between sortation stages and ejecting objects into bins arranged in wings (e.g., 16 bins per wing), achieving divert costs in the hundreds rather than thousands of dollars. Systems scale by adding robots and wings, with the number of robots typically not exceeding half the number of wings, and can optimize bin placement to reduce shuttle cycle times and network-wide costs.

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture on smart contracts and DApps, co-taught by the professor and Harvard law professor Larry Lessig, covers technical, market, and legal perspectives.

The professor defines smart contracts using Nick Szabo's 1996 definition: a set of promises specified in digital form, including protocols and algorithms. He cautions that smart contracts may not be "smart" (functioning more as dumb contracts) and may not be legal contracts. Comparing Ethereum to Bitcoin across cryptography, decentralization/consensus, and transaction format, he explains that Ethereum uses state transitions and account-based balance ledgers rather than Bitcoin's transaction ledger. Ethereum, designed by Vitalik Buterin, is Turing complete, supports multiple programming languages (mainly Solidity), produces 14-second blocks, and has changed its monetary policy twice (from 5 to 3 to 2 ETH per block), unlike Bitcoin's fixed policy. Ethereum launched with a presale/ICO raising $18 million. Other platforms discussed include EOS ($4.2 billion raised), NEO (China-based), and Ethereum Classic. Current DApps show limited adoption—the most active gambling site has only 1,500 daily users. Initial coin offerings have raised roughly $20–28 billion, with studies suggesting 59% fail within nine months and estimates ranging from 25% to 80% being scams.

Lessig presents four points on contract law: (1) contracts contain express and implied terms, illustrated by vending machines; (2) the state is always an implicit third party that determines enforceability; (3) contract law's objective is risk allocation, and blockchain infrastructure can substitute for underdeveloped legal systems and lower transaction costs, enabling new markets such as automatic flight delay insurance; (4) ambiguity in contracts is often valuable, but smart contracts require specifying all outcomes, potentially increasing transaction costs for complex agreements. In Q&A, he argues government involvement is inevitable, code-based contracts raise questions about judicial interpretation, and lawyers must become technically literate to handle code as they do legal language.

The passage documents the GHCB (Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block) protocol for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests. It describes MSR protocol functions by which guests request AP reset hold, a preferred GHCB GPA, GHCB GPA registration/unregistration, page state changes, Run VMPL, and hypervisor feature support, with corresponding hypervisor responses. GHCB GPA registration is required for SEV-SNP guests before first VMGEXIT use; registering a new GPA automatically unregisters any prior one, and a hypervisor must terminate a guest supplying a GPA that does not match the registered one. Guests may also request termination with a reason code.

Negotiation examples show the hypervisor setting VMCB offset 0x00a0 with protocol version and SEV page table encryption bit information before launching the vCPU. Guests use #VC exception handlers, CPUID, and MSR protocol requests to determine the encryption bit, establish long mode, allocate a shared GHCB page, and register its GPA before issuing VMGEXIT.

For non-automatic exit (NAE) events, hardware throws a #VC exception whose error code equals the VMEXIT code. Guests copy required state into the GHCB, set the corresponding VALID_BITMAP bits, and invoke VMGEXIT; hypervisors return results and can signal errors or request exception injection via SW_EXITINFO1/SW_EXITINFO2. Specific events covered include IOIO_PROT and MSR_PROT (requiring instruction decode or para-virtualization), VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO reads and writes using the GHCB shared buffer, Page State Change (private/shared, PSMASH/UNSMASH hints, with cur_entry/end_entry tracking allowing resumable processing), and SNP Guest Request (requiring shared request/response pages, RMPUPDATE and page reclaim handling, sequence number validation, and recommended rate limiting to prevent denial-of-service against the SNP firmware).

The passage also defines the Secrets Page Guest Reserved Area for communicating guest message sequence numbers and AP Jump Table addresses between operating environments, and an EFI configuration table for conveying the secrets and CPUID pages to the OS.

The lower highs and lower lows pattern signals a downtrend but functions primarily as a short-term reversal pattern. Backtests on the S&P 500 (SPY), gold (GLD), and long-term Treasuries (TLT) showed that longer holding periods produced better returns due to long-term upward drift. A two-day version of the pattern slightly improved results in stocks but not in gold or Treasuries. A three-day pattern in stocks increased both average gain and profit factor, with a low maximum drawdown of 9.9% for a one-day hold. Overall, the pattern works well as a short-term reversal in stocks, though other patterns may offer better rewards. Trading rules involve pattern identification, entry points, backtesting, confirmation signals, and risk management.

Pompey expect contact from the Football Association after Charlton fans released smoke bombs in the Milton End at Fratton Park. If the FA is unsatisfied with the club's handling, a fine could be issued. Chief executive Mark Catlin said the club follows correct procedures and that entry leniency is sometimes abused.

The U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia denied the plaintiffs' motion to enforce a settlement agreement. Three former D.C. Department of Corrections employees sued the District of Columbia, alleging they were wrongfully terminated without prior notice or opportunity to challenge their dismissals, in retaliation for speaking to the media about the city's halfway-house system. Five days before the October 2001 trial, the parties reached a tentative agreement under which the plaintiffs would dismiss their First Amendment claims in exchange for $625,000. The plaintiffs later claimed the settlement also included their re-enrollment into the retirement system, while the defendants contended the agreement was exclusively financial. The court found that although the parties assented to the monetary portion, they never reached a meeting of the minds on re-enrollment, citing the defendants' uncertainty, failure to initiate the re-enrollment process, and the absence of any written or oral agreement on that term. The court also declined to enforce the settlement as to Ms. Thomas alone, agreeing that the settlement was a joint and indivisible decision among the three plaintiffs. The court gave the plaintiffs until September 9, 2002 to either accept the $625,000 offer without retirement benefits or reject the settlement, in which case the case would be set for trial.

In Morris v. Scott, the plaintiff sued for malicious prosecution after the defendant, without probable cause, complained to a magistrate accusing him of aiding the fraudulent removal of another's property, leading to his arrest and acquittal. The trial court nonsuited him because the declaration did not allege that the magistrate or special sessions court had jurisdiction. On writ of error, the court held that lack of jurisdiction in the original proceedings does not bar an action on the case for malicious prosecution, provided malice and falsehood are the gravamen and the arrest is alleged merely as a consequence. The judgment was reversed and a new trial ordered.

Niantic will add 80 second-generation Pokémon from the Gold and Silver games to Pokémon Go this week, bringing the total to 88. The update includes two new Berries—Nanab, which slows Pokémon, and Pinap, which doubles Candy—plus new avatar customization items. Twelve second-generation Pokémon remain absent, including six legendaries: Raikou, Entei, Suicune, Lugia, Ho-Oh and Celebi. First-generation legendaries also remain unavailable.

Collagen, a protein making up about 30% of the body's natural protein, provides structural support, strength, and elasticity to skin, tendons, and bones. Its production declines with age, prompting interest in supplements. Of around 28 collagen types, types I–V are most common, with types I, II, and III featured in oral supplements. Supplements come as hydrolysed collagen, undenatured collagen, or gelatin, and are sourced mainly from marine, bovine, porcine, or chicken materials. Hydrolysed collagen, which is easily digested and absorbed, may be the most effective form. Reported benefits include improved skin firmness, reduced wrinkles, stronger nails, better bone density, reduced joint pain, and muscle support, though research is ongoing. Suggested daily doses range from 2.5 to 15 grams depending on the goal. Experts recommend third-party tested products taken for at least 12 weeks, and note that a balanced diet rich in protein, vitamin C, zinc, and copper supports natural collagen production.

A player discusses the team's two-day break to regroup, emphasizing the need to create traffic in front of goaltender Roberto to score. He notes the first game was about finding opponents' tendencies and calls the next game crucial for earning a split at home.

The Midline Option is an option play where the Quarterback reads an interior Defensive Lineman to decide whether to hand off to the Fullback (A-gap) or keep the ball (B-gap). Though traditional option offenses are fading, programs like Oregon and Coastal Carolina use modernized variations. Its primary strength is that the offense doesn't have to block one defender—"If you can't block them, read them"—and unlike other option runs, it reads an interior lineman rather than an edge defender. It also complements veer offenses, with Wingback motion serving as "eye candy" while the ball runs up the gut. Its biggest weakness is exposing the Quarterback to heavy hits, requiring a rugged QB. The passage details assignments against 3-4 Odd and 4-3 Even fronts. Variations include Flexbone Midline, which replaces the Tight End with a Z to spread the defense, and Midline "Follow," used by Army, Navy, and Air Force in short-yardage, where a Wingback acts as an extra lead blocker.

Backtests of the Santa Claus Rally (end-of-year effect) in German stocks and the Euro Stoxx 50 show significantly better performance during the Christmas season than random periods. Using the EWG ETF for German stocks, the average gain per trade was 2.1%, with an 81% win ratio and profit factor of 13; using the FEZ ETF for Euro Stoxx 50, the average gain was 1.5%, with an 81% win ratio and profit factor of 9. Returns in recent years fell below prior averages. The backtest ran from 2001 with no leverage, and positions were held on average 6-10 days. The rally exists but its continuation is not guaranteed.

This study examined var gene expression and immune responses during a Controlled Human Malaria Infection (CHMI) in 19 semi-immune adults in The Gambia infected with the NF54/3D7 P. falciparum strain. Volunteers were classified as sero-high or sero-low based on pre-existing antibody levels. Sero-low individuals developed higher parasitaemia and more symptoms, while two sero-high "controllers" exhibited longer latency and lower parasite growth rates. Transcriptome analysis revealed var genes as the primary source of expression heterogeneity between individuals. Controllers showed restricted var expression (low entropy), while non-controllers expressed a diverse var repertoire. In vivo var gene turnover rates were very high, with transition probabilities exceeding 86% per cycle for groups A, C, and E. In vitro cultures of sero-low isolates converged to a similar high-entropy steady state within 20 days, whereas sero-high isolates retained distinct expression profiles longer, suggesting lasting effects of host immune selection. Pre-existing PfEMP1 antibody breadth was moderately negatively associated with var gene expression diversity. Sero-low individuals showed a significant post-infection increase in antibody breadth against PfEMP1 domains, while sero-high individuals did not. No direct correlation was found between var expression intensity during infection and subsequent antibody acquisition, suggesting some PfEMP1 domains are poorly immunogenic.

Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced the Model 3 had over half a million advance reservations as he delivered the first 30 vehicles to employee buyers at the company's Fremont, California factory. The $35,000 base model has a 220-mile range, while a $44,000 version drives 310 miles per charge. Musk warned of "at least six months of manufacturing hell" during early production, and new buyers likely would not receive cars until the end of 2018. Tesla aims to produce 500,000 vehicles next year, nearly six times its 2016 output, having already spent over $2 billion in cash this year. The Model 3 launch is central to Tesla's transition from niche luxury producer to mass-market electric car maker.

Trend Micro researchers discovered 89 malicious Chrome extensions on the official Chrome Web Store that affected over 423,000 users and formed a botnet called "Droidclub." Installed through malvertising and fake error messages, the extensions display low-quality ads and inject the Yandex Metrica Javascript library to enable session replay, allowing theft of form data such as names, credit card numbers, CVV numbers, email addresses, and phone numbers, though not passwords. An earlier version injected Coinhive code to secretly mine Monero. The extensions were made difficult to uninstall through redirects to fake pages. Trend Micro contacted Google and Cloudflare, and the extensions and command-and-control servers were subsequently removed.

Dr. Edward Kwapong, newly elected President of Ghana's IHRMP, urged HR practitioners to embrace professional certification over raw academic qualifications at the Institute's ninth graduation ceremony in Accra. Executive Director Ebenezer Agbetor reported 136 Associate and nine certified graduates, a 32 percent increase. Guest speaker Irene Asare said artificial intelligence and robotics are already transforming workplaces.

Soccer formations are strategic player placements used for effective defense and attack. Key factors in choosing a formation include the number of players per age-specific rules, player skills, and the coach's comfort with the tactics. Over the past 100 years, influenced by the Offside Law, the game has trended toward fewer forwards, more equal spacing, greater all-around skills, higher fitness, and more short passes. In 11-a-side games, formations are designated by the numbers of defenders, midfielders, and forwards among the 10 field players, such as 4-3-3 or 4-4-2; recent variations include 4-3-2-1 and 4-6. U.S. Soccer recommends specific formations by age group, while younger, smaller-sided games leave positioning to the coach's discretion. Coaches must understand position names, initial placement, and tactics, then diagram and present the chosen formation to the team.

NASA/ESA's Hubble Space Telescope captured an image of NGC 6000, a spiral galaxy located 102 million light-years away in the constellation Scorpius. The galaxy has a glowing yellow center of older, cooler stars and blue outskirts hosting young, massive stars. Hubble gathered the data while surveying recent supernovae; NGC 6000 hosted SN 2007ch in 2007 and SN 2010as in 2010, whose faint glows help researchers constrain progenitor star masses. An asteroid also crossed the field of view, leaving four colored streaks from separate filtered exposures.

Billy Caldwell, a 12-year-old Northern Ireland boy with a rare form of epilepsy, has had his return home from London delayed. The Home Office granted him a short-term licence for cannabis oil, which his mother says helps control his seizures. She claims the Department of Health in Northern Ireland must ratify the decision and is not responding. The department says it is actively working toward a resolution.

On May 12, 2021, Amazon.com, Inc. closed the sale of notes in eight series: $1 billion of 0.250% notes due 2023 (the "Sustainability Notes"), $2.5 billion of 0.450% notes due 2024, $2.75 billion of 1.000% notes due 2026, $2.25 billion of 1.650% notes due 2028, $3 billion of 2.100% notes due 2031, $2 billion of 2.875% notes due 2041, $3.25 billion of 3.100% notes due 2051, and $1.75 billion of 3.250% notes due 2061. The sale was made under an underwriting agreement dated May 10, 2021 with J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, Citigroup Global Markets Inc., Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, and Wells Fargo Securities, LLC. The aggregate public offering price was $18.437 billion, with estimated net proceeds of approximately $18.395 billion after underwriting discounts and before offering expenses. The notes were issued under an indenture dated November 29, 2012 with Wells Fargo Bank, National Association as trustee, and were registered under a Form S-3 filed June 1, 2020. Amazon intends to allocate an amount equal to the net proceeds from the Sustainability Notes to finance or refinance green or social Eligible Projects.

This passage, from a book on container-based distributed system design patterns, first argues for the value of patterns: they let developers learn from others' experience, provide a shared vocabulary that speeds communication, and enable reusable shared components. It then explains why single-machine applications should be split into multiple containers—for resource isolation, team scaling, and separation of concerns—and introduces three single-node patterns built on tightly coupled container groups (pods in Kubernetes).

The sidecar pattern pairs an application container with a sidecar that augments it, often without the application's knowledge. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy HTTP service via an nginx sidecar, synchronizing configuration from an API to the filesystem, providing standardized introspection (topz), and building a simple Git-based PaaS. Successful sidecars require parameterization (e.g., via environment variables), a stable API, and documentation using Dockerfile directives such as EXPOSE, ENV, and LABEL.

The ambassador pattern uses a container to broker communication between the application and external services. Applications connect to localhost while the ambassador handles routing—examples include proxying to sharded Redis via twemproxy, service brokering for portable service discovery (e.g., MySQL), and request splitting for experiments (nginx sending 10% of traffic to an experimental service).

The adapter pattern standardizes interfaces: an adapter container transforms an application's heterogeneous output (monitoring metrics, logs, health checks) into a consistent format. Examples include a Prometheus exporter for Redis, fluentd for normalizing logs from Redis and Storm, and a Go-based health-check adapter for MySQL.

The passage then turns to multi-node patterns, contrasting microservices (small, independently scalable services with formal APIs) with monoliths, noting benefits in agility and scaling but drawbacks in debugging and design complexity.

The replicated load-balanced service pattern serves stateless applications: at least two replicas behind a load balancer provide high availability, with readiness probes signaling when replicas can serve traffic. Session tracking (via IP hashing or cookies) keeps a user on the same replica. A caching layer (e.g., Varnish) is best deployed as a few large replicas above the web tier rather than as sidecars, and can also provide rate limiting and denial-of-service defense. An nginx layer handles SSL termination. A complete example deploys a dictionary service in Kubernetes with Varnish cache and nginx SSL layers.

Finally, sharded services split data across replicas, each serving a subset of requests, and are generally used for stateful data too large for one machine. A sharded cache example shows how sharding maximizes memory utilization (50% versus 5% of the dataset in the example). Cache hit rate affects system capacity and latency, so shard failures or rollouts have performance implications; replicated sharded caches address this by making each shard a replicated service. Hands-on examples deploy sharded memcached with a twemproxy ambassador or a shared shard-router service. Traffic is routed to shards via a sharding function, commonly a hashing function combined with the modulo operator.

In his inaugural address, the newly sworn President outlines the principles that will guide his administration. He asserts that the Constitution rests on the people, whose sovereignty is limited to powers expressly granted, leaving individuals with unalienable rights such as freedom of faith, speech, and due process. While acknowledging disputes over constitutional interpretation, he identifies the chief danger to the government as the accumulation of power within a single department, particularly the executive, and pledges to counteract this tendency. He announces that he will not serve a second term, arguing that prolonged tenure of high office fosters a corrupting love of power. He describes the veto as a conservative power meant to protect the Constitution, prevent hasty legislation, and defend minority rights. He further pledges to limit executive influence over elections, the press, the Treasury, and the drafting of revenue legislation, and criticizes an exclusively metallic currency as harmful. He maintains that citizens of the District of Columbia are free citizens, not subjects, and urges states to refrain from interfering in one another's domestic institutions, emphasizing preservation of the Union as the foremost interest. He commits to encouraging States to fulfill their financial obligations, to pursuing peaceful and just foreign relations, and to mitigating party violence, while expressing reverence for the Christian religion and confidence in the people's support.

IDC identifies global cooperation as a key future aspect of HPCaaS. Rising hybrid work and digitalization challenge manufacturers, requiring integrated, data-based development, a single source of truth, and efficient workstations, though upgrades are costly.
William Riley's petition for certiorari to review the Court of Appeals' judgment was abated by his death and dismissed.

Thirteen-year-old Time for Kids reporter Benje Choucroun asked White House press secretary Sarah Huckabee Sanders what the administration has done and will do to prevent school shootings, citing students' mental health worries. Sanders appeared taken aback, then said the administration takes it seriously and the president's school safety commission is meeting this week. Time's editor-in-chief praised the question.

HRO Today will host a webinar on October 18, 2017, at 12:00 PM ET, featuring Elliot Clark, Katy Theroux, and Cory Kruse, covering HR strategy tied to business outcomes, recruitment metrics, and the candidate experience's impact on hires and retention.
The team held their own after the opponents tied the game, avoiding a collapse, but couldn't score a second goal. Sergei's timely goal proved decisive in an otherwise balanced game between two teams.

Eric Thames homered in his fifth straight game, tying a Brewers club record, as Milwaukee beat the Chicago Cubs 6-3 Monday night for their sixth win in seven games. Thames' opposite-field homer broke a 3-3 tie in the third inning, while Ryan Braun and Jeff Bandy also homered off Cubs starter John Lackey (1-2). Brewers starter Chase Anderson (2-0) earned the win, allowing three runs on seven hits over five innings, and Neftali Felix recorded his fifth save. The Cubs lost their fourth straight game and have dropped four consecutive at Wrigley Field for the first time since May 2014. Milwaukee added insurance runs in the eighth on Braun's RBI double and catcher Willson Contreras' throwing error.

Six teachers from Haoreibi Makha Leikai LP Madrasa and Thoudam Wangmata Primary School were suspended for negligence of duty after Education Minister Th Radheshyam's surprise visits. Three ran an unauthorized school without classes; three were absent without informing authorities.

The United States District Court for the Western District of Virginia, Harrisonburg Division, granted summary judgment for plaintiff Riverton Investment Corporation (RIC) in this tax refund case against the United States, decided March 6, 2001.
