RIC, formed in 1980 as a holding company to purchase Riverton Corporation's stock, issued stock to Riverton managers under a December 26, 1980 Management Stockholder's Agreement (MSA). In the 1990s, upon the managers' termination of employment, RIC bought back the stock at 60% of book value and deducted the payments as compensation. The IRS disallowed the deductions as non-deductible stock redemptions; RIC paid the tax and sued for a refund. The Magistrate Judge had recommended judgment for the United States, but RIC objected. The central issue was whether the stock was "transferred" to the managers in the 1980s under Treasury Regulation 1.83-3, which depended on whether the MSA's restrictions were permanent "non-lapse" restrictions or "lapse" restrictions. The dispute centered on MSA Paragraph 9, concerning liquidation, merger, acquisition, or reorganization. The court found Paragraph 9 ambiguous, admitted parol evidence, and denied the United States's motion to strike. The uncontroverted parol evidence showed the parties intended only the timing restriction to lapse, while permanent restrictions on the sale price and permissible buyer remained. Because these non-lapse restrictions prevented a "transfer," the 1990s payments were not redemptions and were deductible. The court sustained RIC's objections, rejected the Magistrate Judge's recommendation, and entered judgment for RIC.

LeBron James said his expiring contract "doesn't bother me at all" and will have no impact on his performance as he enters his 23rd NBA season—a league record, breaking a tie with Vince Carter—and his first with the Lakers on an expiring deal after exercising his $52.6 million player option. Coming off a Grade 2 MCL sprain in his left knee, James is focused on getting his body ready for an 82-game season and may be limited in training camp. He said his eventual retirement decision will not hinge on his son Bryce making the NBA, but on whether he still loves the process of preparing each year.

Facebook announced on Tuesday it has acquired the team behind Bloomsbury AI, a London-based startup specializing in natural language processing, in an "acquihire" rather than a full acquisition. TechCrunch reported the deal could be worth up to $30 million, with Facebook interested in the software to combat fake news. Bloomsbury AI's future operations remain unclear.

The passage traces the history of patterns in software development: as program complexity grew, procedural programming and algorithms proved insufficient, leading to object-oriented programming and an explosion of pattern books in the 1990s, most famously the "gang of four" book *Design Patterns*. The rise of open source software in the late 1990s and 2000s reinforced that software development, particularly distributed systems, is a community endeavor; all container technology underlying the book's patterns is open source.

Patterns for distributed systems are general blueprints for organizing systems without mandating specific technologies. They offer three values: learning from others' mistakes, providing a shared vocabulary that speeds communication, and enabling reusable components built once and shared.

The book focuses on container-based patterns. Single-node patterns involve tightly coupled containers co-located on one machine (called pods in Kubernetes). Motivations for splitting single-machine applications into multiple containers include resource isolation, team scaling with reusable modules, and separation of concerns leading to more reliable deployments.

The sidecar pattern pairs an application container with a sidecar container that augments it, often without the application's knowledge. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy service via an nginx proxy, synchronizing configuration from an API, process introspection via topz, and building a simple Git-based PaaS. Successful sidecars require parameterization, a stable API surface, and documentation.

The ambassador pattern brokers interactions between an application container and the outside world. Uses include client-side sharding (e.g., sharded Redis with twemproxy), service brokering for portability across environments, and request splitting for experiments (e.g., 10% traffic to a new version using nginx).

The adapter pattern transforms an application container's interface to conform to a standardized interface. Examples include adapting Redis for Prometheus monitoring, normalizing logs with Fluentd, and adding rich health checks to MySQL without modifying the original image.

Multi-node patterns are loosely coupled, communicating via network calls with loose synchronization. Microservices architectures break applications into small services with formal APIs, enabling small teams, decoupled releases, and independent scaling, but making debugging and design more difficult—motivating distributed patterns.

The replicated load-balanced service pattern uses identical servers behind a load balancer, suited to stateless services; at least two replicas are needed for high availability. Readiness probes inform load balancers when applications can serve traffic. Session tracking routes a user's requests to the same replica, often via consistent hashing. Additional layers include caching (Varnish), rate limiting for denial-of-service defense, and SSL termination (nginx).

Sharded services split data across replicas, each serving a subset of requests, and suit stateful services whose data exceeds one machine's capacity. Sharded caches improve memory utilization over replicated caches; cache hit rate affects system capacity and latency. Replicated sharded caches combine both patterns, providing resilience to failures and independent scaling of hot shards.

Ida C. Scott sought to enjoin enforcement of a judgment against her real estate. John R. House had obtained a justice court judgment against her for $61.50 for goods sold and delivered, and an execution was levied on 80 acres of her land. Under Comp. St. 1911, ch. 53, sec. 1, a married woman's property is not liable for debts contracted for necessaries furnished the family until execution against the husband has been issued and returned unsatisfied. The stipulated facts showed no judgment had first been obtained against her husband. The court held this condition precedent to liability had not been established and that the wife may raise this defense at any time before sale of her property, rejecting defendants' argument that she was concluded by the prior judgment. The district court's injunction was affirmed.

This study applies the spherical fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (SFAHP) to evaluate and rank the impact of digitalization on online higher education quality in Vietnam. Five criteria—accessibility of digital resources, adaptability and innovation, pedagogical integration, student engagement, and technological infrastructure—were assessed through pairwise comparisons by nine education experts. Results ranked pedagogical integration first (23.6%), followed by student engagement (21.2%), accessibility of digital resources (20.3%), adaptability and innovation (18.4%), and technological infrastructure (16.5%). The findings challenge the traditional emphasis on infrastructure, indicating that integrating teaching methodologies with technology is central to improving online education quality. The authors note the study's reliance on expert evaluations as a limitation and suggest future research include broader stakeholder perspectives.

Patrick Cullen, 33, was sentenced at Limerick Circuit Court after pleading guilty to robbing a 21-year-old woman of her handbag at Wolfe Tone Street on July 11. The victim was pushed from behind and fell, cutting her finger. Cullen made immediate admissions after arrest, with his barrister citing desperation to fund his drug habit. Judge Tom O'Donnell imposed a four-year sentence, suspending the final 12 months, backdated to July 12.

A Reuters table presents Asian currency rates against the US dollar at 0134 GMT on Feb 2, showing daily and 2018 year-to-date changes. Most currencies strengthened in 2018, led by the ringgit (+4.12%) and baht (+4.09%), while the peso weakened (-3.39%).

The Ottawa Senators defeated the Philadelphia Flyers 4-3 in a shootout Saturday at Wells Fargo Center. Mike Hoffman scored the deciding goal in Round 6 using the Peter Forsberg move, which he previously used in last spring's series-clinching Game 6 in Boston. Coach Guy Boucher described Hoffman as a high-risk, high-reward player. Rookie Colin White recorded his first NHL point with an assist on Matt Duchene's goal. Defenceman Johnny Oduya earned a $250,000 bonus by appearing in his 41st game of the season. Boucher also praised Flyers centre Sean Couturier, whom he coached in junior with Drummondville. Calgary Flames scout Don Maloney attended the game, with the Flames reportedly interested in Ottawa's Zack Smith and Jean-Gabriel Pageau ahead of the Feb. 26 trade deadline.

Mets GM David Stearns criticized pitcher Kodai Senga for two inconsistent, challenging seasons. After pitching well in 2023, Senga made only one start last year due to injuries, struggled this season, and was demoted to Triple-A. Stearns said the team will work to unlock his potential but called guaranteeing 30 starts next year "foolish."

SCDNR biologists satellite-tagged a pregnant female tiger shark named Harry-Etta, measuring 12 feet 2 inches and weighing 820 pounds, in St. Helena Sound. The SPOT tag will transmit real-time movement data for a year, helping researchers study the species' lifespan, reproduction, and migration. This is the third encounter with Harry-Etta, previously tagged in 2013 and 2015, and she is the fifteenth tiger shark tagged by the team and the first known to be pregnant. The tag was sponsored by the Harry Hampton Wildlife Fund, which also funded a previous tag. Her movements can be tracked on the OCEARCH Global Shark Tracker.

The offensive line (OL) is described as the most selfless position in sports, with players protecting teammates and enabling touchdowns without receiving statistical recognition or public praise. The unit is responsible for run blocking—creating creases through coordinated communication despite complex defensive blitzes and stunts—and pass protection, giving quarterbacks time to throw as defenses evolve. The name derives from the five players lining up on the line of scrimmage. Common nicknames include Hogs, Bruisers, Bulldozers, Big Uglies, and Monsters. Required skills include run-blocking, pass-blocking, athleticism, strength, awareness, and technique; typical body types range from 6'2" to 6'8" and 300-340 pounds. Notable players cited include center Jim Otto, guard John Hannah, and tackle Anthony Munoz. Though often blamed when offenses struggle, the passage states steady offensive line play is the #1 factor in an offense's season-long success, enabling stars like Patrick Mahomes and Derrick Henry to perform.

Research by Sarah Sajedi, a Concordia University PhD candidate and co-founder of ERA Environmental Management Solutions, found that individuals ingest 39,000 to 52,000 microplastic particles annually, with bottled water drinkers consuming 90,000 more particles than tap water drinkers. Her review of over 140 scientific articles, inspired by plastic waste she observed on Thailand's Phi Phi islands, notes that particles ranging from one micron to five millimeters shed from low-quality plastic bottles during production, storage, transport, and breakdown. These particles can enter the bloodstream and reach vital organs, potentially causing inflammation, hormonal disruption, neurological damage, and cancer, though long-term effects remain understudied due to limited testing and costly detection tools. Sajedi emphasizes education, noting bottled water is acceptable in emergencies but not for daily use, as the risk is chronic rather than acute toxicity.

A University of Pennsylvania study published in the Journal of Neuroscience found that transcranial direct-current stimulation of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex reduced intentions to commit aggression. In the trial, 81 healthy adults with an average age of 20 were randomly assigned to receive either about 20 minutes of stimulation or a brief sham treatment. The next day, stimulated participants reported a 47 percent lower likelihood of committing physical assault and a 70 percent lower likelihood of sexual assault, and judged the acts as more morally wrong. Skeptics noted that stated intentions may not reflect actual behavior, and lead author Olivia Choy pointed out that participants received only one session.

A fossil found by elk hunter David Bradt in Montana in 2010 led to the discovery of a new elasmosaur species, a marine reptile that lived about 70 million years ago in an inland sea east of the Rocky Mountains. Unlike most elasmosaurs with necks up to 18 feet long, this species had a shorter neck of about 7.5 feet with roughly 40 vertebrae. The finding, published in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology, contradicts the belief that elasmosaurs did not evolve longer necks over millions of years. The well-preserved, nearly complete fossil was excavated from the Charles M. Russell National Wildlife Refuge.

President Martin Van Buren's January 5, 1838 proclamation addresses unlawful US citizen interference in the civil war in Canada. Despite proclamations by the governors of New York and Vermont and the presence of civil officers, excitement has increased; insurgents have procured arms and organized a military force at Navy Island under a US citizen. Van Buren exhorts citizens to return home and warns neutrality violators face arrest, punishment, and no government aid.

In this lecture, the professor continues Chapter 7 on algebra, aiming to reach finite fields as preparation for discussing Reed-Solomon codes; Ralf Koetter will substitute as lecturer the following week. The lecture reviews integers and mod-n arithmetic (Zn), then covers groups, noting that all finite cyclic groups are isomorphic to Zn. Subgroups are defined as subsets that form groups under the same operation, with examples such as {0,5} and the even elements in Z10, and the even integers in Z. Cosets, or translates of a subgroup, are shown to form a disjoint partition of the group, yielding Lagrange's theorem: the size of any subgroup divides the size of a finite group. Coset addition produces quotient groups, with Z mod nZ isomorphic to Zn, offering a view of Zn as residue classes. Fields are then defined by axioms: an abelian group under addition, the non-zero elements forming an abelian group under multiplication, and the distributive law. The real, complex, and binary fields are verified as examples. Prime fields Fp are constructed using mod-p addition and multiplication, which form a field only when p is prime. It is argued that every finite field with p elements is isomorphic to Fp, and every finite field contains a prime subfield whose size is the field's characteristic; adding any element to itself p times gives 0, and in characteristic 2, addition equals subtraction. Finally, polynomials over a field are introduced, covering degree conventions (with the zero polynomial defined as degree minus infinity), component-wise addition, multiplication via convolution, and the conclusion that the only invertible polynomials (units) are the non-zero degree-0 polynomials.

The author attended a webinar hosted by the presidents of Middle States, SACSCOC, and WASC on credit transfer and AI, finding it vague, with no concrete changes identified. MSCHE president Heather Perfetti said accreditors are urging a shift in the burden of proof for credit transfer from yes to no, but the author notes urging is not requiring. Colleges reject transfer credits out of economic self-interest, and change occurs only when mandated from above. Accreditors' leverage from regional monopolies tied to federal financial aid ended when the first Trump administration opened the door to alternative accreditors. The new preference is to "default to yes" on transfer, though disqualifying evidence remains undefined. AI could speed transfer decisions, helping students make informed choices. The author views the direction positively but hopes it moves from intention to plan.

A security aide to Ebonyi State Governor David Umahi allegedly slapped a Federal Road Safety Corps officer, Soji, at a checkpoint set up to restrict access to the PDP convention venue at Eagle Square. The officer was restrained by colleagues and left the scene. The FRSC spokesman said no official report had been made. Security personnel at the venue were also observed extorting money from individuals without accreditation.

Coach Sutter said his team played well recently but must finish opportunities and not give up more than one goal. He praised the first period aside from a marginal call, said pressure is on the Devils as home team, noted the first goal has been decisive in the series, and described a screened goal allowed when a tired winger stayed on.

CBS's drama Doubt premieres February 15th at 10/9c, airing Wednesdays. It follows attorneys at New York's top defense firm, Isaiah Roth And Associates, led by Isaiah "The Legal Lion" Roth (Elliot Gould), known for risky hires including transgender lawyer Cameron Wirth (Laverne Cox), Nick Brady (Kobi Libii), and Sadie Ellis (Katherine Heigl). Sadie's biggest case defends Billy Brennan (Steven Pasquale), a pediatric surgeon accused of a 24-year-old murder, forcing her to balance personal feelings with professional duty.

The 7th annual Julia's Hope Cup and Carnival takes place at Chippawa Park in Welland on Feb. 17. Founded by Paul Turner in memory of his daughter Julia, who died of cancer in 2011, it raises money for The Hope Centre, which combats homelessness. Now resembling a winter carnival with food, games, and a silent auction, the event includes a mini-tournament for kids six to 12. The 2017 event raised $20,000 and drew about 1,000 people.

Tesla, Inc.'s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2021. Tesla, a Delaware corporation headquartered in Austin, Texas, with common stock listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol TSLA, reported 1,033,507,611 shares outstanding as of January 31, 2022, and an aggregate market value of voting stock held by non-affiliates of $541.28 billion as of June 30, 2021.

The company designs, develops, manufactures, sells and leases fully electric vehicles and energy generation and storage systems, operating in two reportable segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. Automotive products include Model 3, Model Y, Model S and Model X, with Cybertruck, the new Roadster and Tesla Semi announced. Energy products include Powerwall and Megapack storage, retrofit solar systems and Solar Roof. Vehicles are manufactured at the Fremont Factory, Gigafactory Nevada, Gigafactory New York and Gigafactory Shanghai, with Gigafactory Berlin and Gigafactory Texas expected to begin production in 2022. Tesla sells directly through its website and company-owned stores, operates a Supercharger network, and offers financing, insurance and service/warranty programs. As of December 31, 2021, the company had 99,290 full-time employees.

The report also discusses government incentives and regulations, competition from established and new automakers and energy companies, and intellectual property policies. Risk factors described include impacts from the COVID-19 pandemic and supply chain constraints (including semiconductor shortages), potential delays in launching and ramping production, dependence on battery cell suppliers such as Panasonic and CATL, reliance on single-source suppliers, challenges in constructing and ramping new factories, competition, risks of international operations, product defects and liability, the need to maintain public credibility, and risks related to vehicle financing programs including residual value and resale value guarantees.

Houston Dash star Carli Lloyd suffered an ankle injury in the 28th minute of Sunday's game against FC Kansas City after falling while heading a ball. Her X-rays were negative, and the team has not said how many games she could miss.

The speaker acknowledged Jersey's strong defense after taking the lead limited his team's offense. He declined to discuss Peter, who won't play, noted the powerplay's success, and emphasized the importance of the upcoming road game.

Two teenagers, ages 14 and 17, staying at the Smoky Mountain Children's Home stole a van and led police on a high-speed chase across East Tennessee, ending near Chickamauga Dam after hitting another vehicle and a barrier wall. No serious injuries occurred.

Cirque du Soleil will donate US$1 million to Las Vegas shooting victims and first-responders: US$500,000 to victims' families and US$500,000 in 5,000 tickets to police, firefighters and paramedics. None of its 1,500 local employees were hurt in the attack.

HID AMDI0095 lets the OS bind a driver to the TMPM device in ACPI. The driver must enable PAGEMIGRATION_EN in all IOMMUs. TMPM's mailbox register interface supports parallel command execution via a ring buffer. Firmware controls the Read pointer; the driver the Write pointer. Command order is not guaranteed; completion is signaled when the Read pointer passes the command or the PM_Status TOGGLE bit changes.

President Ram Nath Kovind addressed the nation on the eve of Independence Day, his first speech since taking office on July 25. Congratulating India on 70 years of Independence, he honored freedom fighters and urged citizens to participate in initiatives like Swachh Bharat and Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao. He called for a national resolution to build a "New India" by 2022, emphasizing GST adoption, pride in paying taxes, and demonetisation's role in building an honest society. He appealed to citizens to educate underprivileged children. Kovind, fielded by the BJP-led NDA, defeated Meira Kumar in the July 17 presidential election.

WIRED's Zoë Schiffer and senior politics editor Leah Feiger discuss five stories. Rutgers professor Mark Bray, who wrote a 2017 book about antifa and donated half its profits to an antifascist defense fund, is fleeing the US for Europe after death threats from a far-right online campaign; his family's United Airlines reservation was mysteriously canceled at the airport. This follows Trump's September 22 executive order designating those involved with antifa as domestic terrorists. ICE plans to hire roughly 30 analysts for a 24/7 social media surveillance program across platforms like Facebook, TikTok, and Instagram to support deportation raids, seeking private vendors for centers in Vermont and Southern California, including AI integration. A Harvard Business School study found that five AI companion apps (Replika, Character.AI, Chai, Talkie, Polybuzz) used emotional manipulation in 37 percent of goodbye interactions. After the FDA approved leucovorin calcium tablets for cerebral folate deficiency as a purported autism treatment, tens of thousands of parents joined a Facebook group filled with misinformation, conspiracies, and supplement sellers. Finally, an OpenAI blog post about internal tools caused software stocks to fall, including DocuSign dropping 12 percent, prompting discussion of whether AI—with $500 billion in projected infrastructure spending versus roughly $12 billion in consumer spending—constitutes a bubble.

GoDaddy gave The Daily Stormer 24 hours to move its domain to another provider for violating its terms of service, after the neo-Nazi website posted an article denigrating Heather Heyer, who was killed at a white nationalist rally in Charlottesville, Virginia.

Lexus announced UK pricing for its 2017 LC flagship coupe, with the V8-powered LC500 and hybrid LC500h both starting at £76,595. Over a third of UK units are already pre-ordered. Optional Sport and Sport+ packages add performance and styling upgrades.

Former Southport MP John Pugh fears Homebase's closure could be followed by further job losses. Sefton Council approved a 60,000 sq ft Sainsbury's megastore at Meols Cop retail park, on the Homebase site, creating 400 jobs. Pugh warns the store will compete with town centre shops and could cause an exodus of big stores from Lord Street.

New research on more than 24,000 obese Slimming World members found that dieters who set ambitious targets lost almost twice as much weight as those who set realistic goals. Over a 12-month period, those aiming to lose less than 10 percent of their body weight shed an average of 11 percent, while those with the toughest targets lost an average of 19 percent. The findings, reported in the Journal of Human Nutrition and Dietetics, have prompted obesity experts, including Professor Amanda Avery of Nottingham University, to call for changes to NHS and NICE guidance recommending a 'realistic' 5-10 percent loss. They argue slimmers should aim for their 'dream weight' with regular support, noting those who set their own personal targets were 10 times more likely to succeed.

WIRED tested and reviewed a range of carry-on bags and luggage for air travel, including roller suitcases, duffels, backpacks, weekenders, and kids' luggage. Featured bags include the Peak Design Roller Pro with a "drawbridge" opening, the lightweight and affordable Travelpro Maxlite 5, the durable anodized aluminum Rimowa, Antler's roller bag with quiet wheels and a front pocket, Briggs & Riley with a lifetime warranty, the Yeti Crossroads 35L, and the Beis weekender with a removable bottom compartment. Also covered are the Tom Bihn Aeronaut 45, travel backpacks from Six Moon Designs and Aer, kid-friendly State bags, and budget options like the Amazon Basics carry-on. The guide offers advice on checking airline size requirements, choosing between softshell and hardshell luggage, and following the TSA 3-1-1 liquids rule. Each bag was tested on at least two flights, with evaluation of materials, weight, size, wheels, handles, straps, and zippers.

A Colorado board has become the first in the nation to set a payment limit for Amgen's arthritis drug Enbrel, applying to government agencies and commercial health plans for state residents. The Colorado Prescription Drug Affordability Board set the limit at $600 per unit—matching Medicare's maximum fair price effective in January—or roughly $30,350 per person annually, compared with about $53,000 that average state insurance plans paid per person in 2023.

The long snapper is a specialized football position responsible for accurate snaps on extra points, field goals (about 7 yards), and punts (about 15 yards). Despite being essential to special teams, their work rarely appears on stat sheets, and successful snaps typically go unnoticed. NFL teams reserve one roster spot for this position despite the 53-man limit, demanding pinpoint accuracy since holders have limited mobility to catch wayward snaps. The best snappers deliver consistent spin for easy catches. On punts, they must also cover downfield and occasionally tackle, requiring both toughness and athleticism. The position is also called LS, deep-snapper (punts), or short-snapper (kicks). Ideal skills include accuracy, consistency, balance, athleticism, and physicality, with a typical build of 6'1"–6'3" and 230–250 pounds, comparable to a linebacker. Notable long snappers include Zak DeOssie (Giants, two Super Bowls) and Don Mulbach (Lions). Errors are unacceptable, as blocked punts result in wins about 90% of the time.

Forwarded by Eric Bass on October 5, 2000, this email contains the Dallas Morning News newsletter "Inside UT Football," a Q&A column by writer Chip Brown. It opens with quotes from Oklahoma coach Bob Stoops, whose 4-0 team has lost three straight to Texas and blew a 17-0 lead in last year's 38-28 loss. Reader questions cover a possible Royal-Memorial Stadium expansion, Adam Doiron possibly redshirting, the halo rule penalty, the offensive line's improved gap-blocking against Oklahoma State, Sean Rogers' ankle injury, and OU's passing attack versus Texas' secondary. Brown predicts a 24-20 Texas win, says Major Applewhite will start ahead of Chris Simms at quarterback, discusses punt-team problems, Texas' 231-game scoring streak, criticism of coach Mack Brown, and notes the October 14 Colorado game will not be televised.

Shuckers attendance in Biloxi is up 21 percent this season, including a record 4,066 fans at Jackie Robinson Day. ESPN named center fielder Johnny Davis's catch SportsCenter's top play. The team returns home April 22 for a jersey auction benefiting March of Dimes.

This email forwards a PAKK Yahoo Groups digest (Number 529) containing 24 messages from members discussing adoption from Kazakhstan. Topics include HIV testing requirements for Russian and Kazakh visas, with members reporting inconsistent enforcement; accommodations in Kazakhstan, with members sharing experiences of hotels, rented apartments, and host families; a new Delta Airlines adoption airfare contract through Travel-On offering discounted fares to Russia and Kazakhstan; travel experiences adopting from Taraz, including train travel details; and a discussion on whether to change adopted children's birth dates or hold them back a grade in school, with parents describing differing approaches and children's growth outcomes. The digest also includes new member introductions and instructions for removing mistaken posts from the group's message archive.

The Trump administration announced it will continue much of the Obama administration's nuclear weapons policy while taking a more aggressive stance toward Russia, warning that Moscow would face "unacceptably dire costs" for even a limited nuclear attack in Europe. The Pentagon-led review, ordered by Trump a year ago, calls for no net increase in strategic nuclear weapons and labels North Korea a "clear and grave threat," while casting China as a potential nuclear adversary. It endorses modernizing the arsenal with new bombers, submarines and land-based missiles, and adhering to arms control agreements like New START. However, it breaks with Obama by ending efforts to reduce nuclear weapons' role, citing Russia's "escalate to de-escalate" doctrine. The plan proposes modifying some Trident submarine missiles with smaller-yield warheads and, longer term, developing a nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile retired in 2011. Arms control groups criticized the policy as reckless.

This preprint describes the development and validation of the Language Phenotype Assessment (LPA), a 15-item, 10-minute clinician-administered test designed to evaluate language comprehension phenotypes in children aged 2 to 5 years. Building on prior research identifying three language comprehension phenotypes in autistic individuals—Command (simple commands), Modifier (color, size, and number modifiers), and Syntactic (spatial prepositions, verb tenses, flexible syntax, and complex explanations)—the authors hypothesized that typically developing children progress through the same stages. Existing assessments (PPVT-4, EVT-2, PLS-5, Token Test, CELF-5, TROG) were deemed unsuitable for ages 2–4 due to vocabulary-only focus, overly complex items, inappropriate age norms, or reliance on pictures rather than manipulatives.

The LPA uses toy-animal and object manipulatives with brief verbal instructions, comprising three command items, five modifier items, and seven syntactic items, each scored 0 or 1 based on completing at least three of four tasks. A parallel parent-reported tool, the Language Phenotype Evaluation Checklist (LPEC), shares the same structure. The LPA was administered to 116 neurotypical children (ages 1.5–7) and 79 children with ASD (ages 2–8).

Results showed near-linear increases in LPA and LPEC scores from ages 1.5 to 5, followed by a ceiling plateau. By clinician-administered LPA, 50% of children attained the Command Phenotype by 1.6 years, the Modifier Phenotype by 3.0 years, and the Syntactic Phenotype by 3.7 years; parent-reported LPEC median ages were 1.6, 2.7, and 3.0 years, respectively. Psychometric properties were strong: Cronbach's alpha of 0.92 (LPA) and 0.91 (LPEC), 4-month test-retest correlations of 0.96 and 0.85, inter-observer Kappa of 0.97, and an LPA-LPEC correlation of r = 0.78. Among children with ASD aged 5 and older, only 39% attained the Syntactic Phenotype per LPA (45% per LPEC), compared with essentially all neurotypical peers.

The authors argue the LPA can support early identification of language deficits, enable a two-dimensional classification of communication (verbal ability plus comprehension level), shift language therapy focus from vocabulary toward syntactic training, and help tailor therapy to a child's current phenotype level. Findings on noncanonical word order suggest autistic individuals may rely on routinized responses, while the Modifier Phenotype appears uniquely human. Limitations include the logistical burden of manipulatives, mitigated because manipulatives reduce attentional demands compared with picture-based tests.

Ministers negotiating with the DUP to form an administration say abolishing line dancing may be necessary, as the DUP objects to it because Ian Paisley declared it sinful. Brexit minister David Davis said other concessions, including ending Sunday trading and restricting same-sex relationships, were rejected. A Leave voter expressed support for the decision.

A new EducationNext poll shows a 12-point drop in support for charter schools, from 51 percent to 39 percent, while support for vouchers (45 percent) and tax-credit scholarships (55 percent) rose slightly. The charter decline occurred among both parties and all racial and ethnic groups, with no clear explanation, though the question's wording about new charter formation and community conflicts over charter expansion may be factors. The poll revealed a partisan divide, with Democrats and Republicans switching positions on vouchers, and a "Trump effect" whereby Republicans are more likely to support issues Trump backs while Democrats are the opposite, though Trump's net influence is nearly nil. The results reflect a breakdown of bipartisan education consensus, though both parties similarly approve of local public schools.

This patent application describes robotic systems with multi-gripper assemblies configured to selectively grip and hold objects. The technology addresses limitations of conventional robots, which often have difficulty selectively gripping objects from groups with immediately neighboring objects or irregularly shaped/sized objects. The disclosed systems include transport robots with multi-gripper assemblies containing addressable vacuum regions or banks that independently draw in air, allowing only selected target objects to be held via vacuum grip. Target objects are identified based on captured image data, and pick-up regions are selected accordingly. The system can pick up, transport, and release single or multiple objects simultaneously or sequentially, repeating the process to move objects between locations.

The system can operate in warehouse or distribution environments with unloading, transfer, transport, and loading units. Components include processors, storage devices (storing master data such as object dimensions, shapes, and weights), communication devices, sensors (including imaging devices, contact sensors, and force detectors), and controllers. The end effector includes a vision sensor device positioned below the horizontal plane of the gripping interface to detect objects without obstruction, and a force detector assembly (e.g., a six-axis force-torque sensor) that measures grip forces, weights, and center-of-mass information. Vacuum levels and airflow rates can be dynamically adjusted based on object weight and contact area. The gripper assembly includes a housing, bracket assembly, manifold assembly controlling airflow to individual grippers, and suction elements with compressible sealing members.

Operationally, the system receives image data of a pickup environment, identifies target objects, selects appropriate vacuum regions, generates commands to grip objects, verifies grip strength against thresholds, and executes transport plans. If grip measurements fall below thresholds, the system performs regripping actions; after exceeding an iteration threshold, it stops and may solicit operator input.

On February 16, 2017, the Fraser Institute will release a study examining whether B.C.'s carbon tax revenues are offset by tax reductions, as promised when the tax was introduced in 2008, amid federal carbon pricing requirements and policymaker interest in the model.

The lecture reviews pointwise and uniform convergence of sequences of functions, noting that uniform convergence—requiring f_n to be close to f across the entire set—is strictly stronger than pointwise convergence.

An example, f_n(x) = x^n on [0,1], converges pointwise to f (0 on [0,1), 1 at x=1) and uniformly on [0,b] for any b < 1, but not uniformly on [0,1]. The non-uniform convergence is proven by negating the definition using ε = 1/4. A second example, a "tent" function peaking at height 2n at x = 1/(2n), converges pointwise to 0 but not uniformly.

The lecture discusses the interchange of limits, showing via an example that limits cannot always be swapped. Three questions are posed: whether limits of continuous functions are continuous, whether limits of differentiable functions are differentiable with derivative of the limit equal to the limit of derivatives, and whether the limit of integrals equals the integral of the limit. Counterexamples show all three fail under pointwise convergence alone: x^n converges pointwise to a discontinuous function; x^n/n converges pointwise to 0 with derivatives converging to a function g that differs from f′; and the tent functions have integrals equal to 1 for all n while the integral of the limit is 0.

Three theorems are then proven for uniform convergence: (1) the uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous, via an ε/3 argument; (2) the integral of the uniform limit equals the limit of the integrals; and (3) the uniform limit of continuously differentiable functions is continuously differentiable, with the derivative of the limit equal to the limit of the derivatives, proven using the fundamental theorem of calculus.

Finally, the Weierstrass M-test is presented: if |f_j(x)| ≤ M_j for all x, and the series of M_j converges, then the series of f_j converges absolutely for each x, and its partial sums converge uniformly. As an application, the function given by the sum of sin(2^j x)/2^j is continuous, since it is a uniform limit of continuous partial sums.

The De'Longhi Rivelia automatic latte maker is $200 off, now priced at $1,300. Using a built-in touchscreen, it makes milk-based drinks like lattes and flat whites from start to finish. Its swappable hopper holds two bean types, and a "bean adapt" function fine-tunes settings per bean, including brewing a test cup. While it can't match a classic portafilter machine's quality, it's easier and more consistent. Its milk frother produces silky micro-foam, though not as hot as a traditional steam wand.

Imran Mohammad, a Rohingya man from Myanmar recognized as a refugee by the UNHCR, arrived in Papua New Guinea on October 29, 2013, at age 19 and has spent four birthdays in detention on Manus. He describes overcrowded compounds with shipping-container rooms, long queues for food, toilets, showers, and washing facilities, and severe shortages of basic items. In Mike compound, over 400 men shared a TV room fitting only 50, and rooms lacked air conditioning. He experienced suicidal thoughts but coped by avoiding crowds, eating late, and focusing on education, adopting the motto "the pen is mightier than the sword." He recounts hunger, restricted phone access, and ongoing hardships, stating that asylum seekers who sought safety from Australia received pain, anguish, and sometimes death.

The Triangle (1-3-1) offense is an effective way to attack the Diamond & One defense by placing the "Star" player in the middle for 1-on-1 isolation. Since the Star's defender (Chaser) focuses primarily on pass denial, they are typically unprepared for high post defense. The offense produces open looks, easy layups, and putbacks. Key actions include high post entry initiating triangle action, drive options with drop passes to teammates, kick out passes for open shots or penetration, post flashes by O4, and lob passes when defenders overplay. Success depends on execution, coordination, defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience. Game strategies include scouting opponents, deploying varied alignments, and attacking the weakest defenders.

Throughout history, total solar eclipses have often caused fear: ancient Greeks saw them as signs of angry gods, Vikings as apocalypse, and ancient Chinese as a dragon devouring the sun. In his book "American Eclipse," David Baron describes the 1878 eclipse, when some Americans believed it was Judgment Day; one father killed his young son and himself. Although astronomers dismiss an eclipse at the crucifixion, some Christians fear the Aug. 21 eclipse signals the end of days. Sister Mary Elizabeth, a cloistered nun in Ellisville, Missouri, reassures anxious callers that it is not a bad omen, and the nuns plan to watch it. In Islamic tradition, Muhammad taught that an eclipse was a sign of God, not of his son's death. Even non-religious viewers find eclipses profound; Baron says they tap into the same part of the brain as religion.

A funnel-web spider, the world's most venomous spider, was spotted on a wall of a house in Springwood, NSW, in the Blue Mountains. Its venom can kill a human within 15 minutes by shutting down the nervous system, and the Australian Museum has recorded 13 deaths. Funnel-webs are common but rarely seen along Australia's east coast, and bite victims are urged to go to hospital immediately. They favor cool, damp places such as pools and bathrooms, and males roam in search of females during mating season. Despite their reputation, they are defensive rather than aggressive, and no fatalities have occurred since antivenom was invented in 1981. Experts advise leaving them alone, as they help control cockroaches, flies, and mosquitoes.

KGI analyst Ming-Chi Kuo predicts the 2H17 Apple Watch will keep the same form factor as previous generations, contrary to earlier reports, which would mark three generations with the same design. He expects LTE and non-LTE versions in 38mm and 42mm sizes. The only design change since the 2014 original was a slight increase in thickness. It is speculated the LTE model may keep the current design and battery life, while a non-LTE version could offer better battery life or a thinner body.

A recent college graduate with a music education degree lives at home with no savings and is starting a three-month, minimum-wage job paying about $1,600 monthly. He owes $1,700 in tuition, needs about $600 for certification exams, and must save for a car and apartment, while his mother demands $480 monthly for rent and phone. He says she imposed rent after becoming angry when his hearing problems prevented him from hearing her, and previously kept $3,000 from his $5,000 school refund check. He asks how to handle the situation without damaging their relationship. The columnist advises: budgeting the roughly $500–$1,000 remaining each month toward debts or savings; taking a second job to earn extra income; using this period to experiment with other work, such as waiting tables; and being honest—noting the mother's behavior seems abnormal and she may need professional help, while urging the writer to take responsibility if he has omitted his own role in the conflicts.

The speaker, upon taking the presidential oath, pledges to preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution, which defines the Executive's duties and the purposes of government. He reviews the nation's progress in the thirty-six years since the Constitution's adoption: laws and departments established, population grown from four to twelve million, territory extended from sea to sea, new states admitted, treaties concluded, and commerce expanded, all at comparatively low cost. He acknowledges evils endured, including disease, wrongs and wars from other nations, and internal dissensions that at times threatened the Union. He concludes that the experiment in human rights has succeeded, that both major political parties contributed talents and integrity to the government, and that party strife, once inflamed by Europe's revolutionary wars, has since subsided. He lists shared political principles, including popular elections, limited and divided sovereignties, economy in expenditures, civilian control of the military, and freedom of press and religion. He urges former partisans to discard rancor and notes that divisions based on geography and interests are more permanent and dangerous than those based on opinion, while the federal and national character of the government protects both State and national rights. He praises his predecessor's eight years of peace, citing debt reduction, repeal of internal taxes, acquisition of the Floridas, extension of the boundary to the Pacific, recognition of southern American independence, military reforms, and internal improvements. He expresses hope that constitutional objections to internal improvements will be resolved through deliberation. Acknowledging the unusual circumstances of his election and his lesser initial support, he pledges upright intentions and commits his fate and the country's destiny to Providence.

A tough, frustrating playoff loss: the team showed tenacity but gave up too many chances and two-goal leads in the third period. Detroit was credited for battling hard. The up-and-down team needs to rebound in the playoffs.

In a proclamation dated September 1, 1814, President James Madison states that British forces briefly occupied the nation's capital, defended by fewer troops and militia, destroying public buildings unrelated to war, including artistic monuments and repositories of archives. A naval force, exploiting the loss of a fort guarding Alexandria, plundered private property there under threat of conflagration. He cites the British commander's declared intent to destroy assailable coastal towns, with the alleged pretext of retaliation for destruction in Upper Canada, which Madison calls false, and characterizes these acts as disregard of civilized warfare during peace negotiations. He exhorts citizens and officers to defend threatened places, authorizing militia call-ups.

A hockey player recounts a tight game in which the opponent scored after a series of bounces and blocked shots, with the puck eventually striking his goalie's leg. He says his line created scoring chances that didn't convert and admits hitting an opposing player on the foot after the game in response to his continued talking. He describes a puck resting on the opposing goalie's back and being unsure of the applicable rule. He defends a change that gave forwards a breather, notes missed opportunities to clear the puck, and says both teams made mistakes but his team remains confident heading into the next game.

This email from Ann M. Schmidt, dated May 9, 2001 and titled "Enron Mentions," compiles news articles about Enron and related topics. Questia Media, an online college library firm backed by investors including Enron Chairman Ken Lay, laid off half its workforce (139 jobs) to reduce costs after struggling to attract subscribers, though paying subscribers recently rose above 5,000 and the company projects positive cash flow in about 18 months. U.S. stock indexes finished mixed, with Enron shares falling $1.93 to $56.11. In Japan, Enron officials said the newly deregulated power market lacks competition and contains barriers deterring newcomers, calling for an independent regulator; a Brattle Group report commissioned by Enron was to be released May 15. U.S. energy company Williams announced entry into Europe's deregulating gas and power markets via a London trading operation. In India, Enron reportedly relocated expatriate executives' families from Mumbai to Singapore and tightened security amid uncertainty over the $2.9 billion Dabhol Power Company project, which the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB) considers too costly; MSEB defaulted on payments, and DPC's board authorized termination of the power purchase agreement. MSEB denied underutilizing its own capacity, said its Uran plant expansion was uneconomical, denied federal government pressure over the deal, and appointed former High Court judge ML Pendse as arbitrator for London proceedings. The Swadeshi Jagran Manch demanded a judicial probe into the Enron deal. Dabhol lenders indicated willingness to support PPA termination, with a deadline of May 15. Prize Petroleum moved to acquire Enron's 30% stake in the Panna, Mukta, and Tapti fields, valued at around Rs 600 crore.

This study applied the optimization phase of the Multiphase Optimization Strategy (MOST) framework to identify combinations of intervention components in a mobile health platform for increasing weeknight sleep duration in children aged 9–12 years with insufficient sleep. Ninety-seven participants from southeastern PA and southern NJ were randomized in a 2⁵ factorial design testing five components—sleep goal (guideline-based or personalized), child-directed and caregiver-directed loss-framed financial incentives, screen time reduction messaging, and daily routine messaging—alongside a core intervention of sleep tracking and weekly performance feedback, using Fitbit trackers and the Way to Health platform over a 7-week intervention and 2-week follow-up. Overall, sleep duration increased by 24 minutes during intervention and 21 minutes at follow-up; no single component met the ≥30-minute optimization criterion. Two combinations achieved the criterion: the top-ranked (caregiver-directed incentive, screen time reduction messaging, and routine messaging) increased sleep by 39.6 minutes during intervention and 33.2 minutes at follow-up, and the second (caregiver-directed incentive and routine messaging) by 32.0 and 26.6 minutes. The caregiver-directed incentive outperformed the child-directed incentive, which was redundant. Limitations included a single, predominantly non-Hispanic White site, short follow-up, and a single-sensor tracker. The optimized package will next be tested in a randomized controlled trial.

At least 30 children died at Gorakhpur BRD Hospital, which a central team found had accommodated patients 10 times its admission capacity, with infant warmers shared by multiple babies. SNCUs in nearby districts are non-existent or non-functional. Union Health Minister J P Nadda and other officials announced a Rs 85 crore regional medical centre in Gorakhpur for research on children's diseases.

This paper addresses the challenge of weak permission in deontic argumentation, where an action is weakly permitted when the obligation to the contrary cannot be derived. The authors show that grounded and stable argumentation semantics fail to justify weak permissions when normative conflicts exist, such as when both an action and its negation are obligatory. They define Deontic Argumentation Theories, including "imaginary arguments" representing weak permissions, and prove that under grounded and stable semantics, weak permissions are not justified conclusions in conflictual theories. To address this limitation, they propose a new wp-semantics, based on the argumentation semantics for Defeasible Logic, which distinguishes natural and imaginary arguments and constructs extensions through a fixed-point process of acceptable and rejected arguments. They prove the wp-extension is unique, conflict-free, and that no argument is both justified and rejected; additionally, weak permissions are justified even under unresolved conflicts, and every argument justified under grounded semantics remains justified under the wp-semantics. The paper discusses the legal significance of conflicting obligations, arguing that when no conflict-resolution mechanism exists, neither obligation should be justified, thereby yielding weak permissions for both. Related work largely neglects weak permission; the closest approach, Defeasible Deontic Logic, lacks an argumentation semantics, which the proposed wp-semantics is expected to characterize.

The global aluminum foil packaging market is expected to grow at approximately 4.5% CAGR during the forecast period, driven by packaging innovation, changing consumer lifestyles, and rising spending power. Aluminum packaging provides corrosion-resistant, hygienic, non-toxic protection for food, beverages, pharmaceuticals, and cosmetics, with growth influenced by the pharmaceutical and cosmetic industries. However, lack of proper recycling processes in some countries may hamper growth. The market is segmented into North America, Europe, Asia Pacific, and RoW, with Asia Pacific expected to grow fastest due to rising per capita income and purchasing power.

MyWorld is a new gaming platform in which players create their own games, controlling objects, genres, scenes, rules, and play modes such as single-player, PvP, or Co-Op. Games are built in design mode and constructor mode, and can be stored locally or shared with the community. Players level up to unlock pre-built materials and can customize avatars. The team has launched a Kickstarter crowdfunding campaign, offering early backers exclusive materials.

Naïve traders mistakenly believe super talent is required to trade Forex, but successful Australian traders prove otherwise. Traders should wait for profitable setups, make independent decisions, and develop strong mental stability to handle losses. Mastering technical, fundamental, and sentiment analysis is essential for profitability. Rather than copying others, traders should rely on themselves, build their own trading style, and enhance judgmental skills, as active traders outperform passive ones. While experts' advice can provide knowledge, novices should start small and think carefully before following it, since differing opinions and lack of experience make blind adherence unwise.

At Tesla's 2021 Annual Meeting of Stockholders held on October 7, 2021, stockholders voted on nine proposals. James Murdoch and Kimbal Musk were elected as Class II directors for three-year terms. Management proposals to reduce director terms to two years and to eliminate supermajority voting requirements were not approved, as neither received at least 66 2/3% of outstanding shares. Stockholders approved ratifying PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as the independent registered public accounting firm for fiscal year 2021. Of the non-binding advisory stockholder proposals, two were approved: reducing director terms to one year and additional reporting on diversity and inclusion efforts. Proposals regarding employee arbitration reporting, assigning human capital management oversight to an independent board-level committee, and additional human rights reporting were not approved. The report was signed by CFO Zachary J. Kirkhorn on October 13, 2021.

The National Technology Security Coalition (NTSC) and Cloud Security Alliance (CSA) have partnered to promote cybersecurity best practices and standardize cloud security vendor reviews through the CSA's Security, Trust & Assurance Registry (STAR) program. The organizations aim to streamline the vendor security review process, reduce time and effort, and offer benefits to vendors following best practices. They will collaborate on a STAR-based questionnaire mapping to commonly used compliance frameworks and produce a joint whitepaper explaining how CISOs and vendors can incorporate the program. The two groups will also participate in each other's events, discuss industry issues in working groups, and collaborate on cloud security research.

On February 5, 2019, Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K announcing that Angela Ahrendts, Senior Vice President, Retail, would depart the company effective April 15, 2019. Deirdre O'Brien succeeded her as Senior Vice President, Retail + People, effective February 5, 2019. The report was signed by Katherine Adams on February 6, 2019.

Daniella Teutsch and Sara Wolf founded athletic clothing company HydroChic in 2007 to offer modest women more attractive swimwear. They found an underserved market among women with mastectomies, bariatric surgery, skin cancer, or psoriasis, and now design swim tops with built-in mastectomy bras, compression workout gear, and skin-protecting suits. Former educators who met at a women's hat business, they were inspired by their own discomfort with revealing bathing suits as religious Jewish women.

As the Supreme Court begins its new term, legal experts expect higher education to feature prominently, though only two college-related cases—West Virginia v. B.P.J. and Little v. Hecox, both concerning transgender athletes—are on the main docket. The increasingly used "shadow docket" allows rapid interim rulings without briefings, arguments, or opinions, creating uncertainty; it has already been used to overturn lower-court rulings on issues including Department of Education staffing cuts. Hecox has asked the Court to dismiss her case, citing illness, her father's death, and public scrutiny, though some suspect she seeks to avoid an unfavorable ruling. Even if dismissed, B.P.J. will likely produce a ruling on Title IX, with implications possibly extending beyond sports to areas like bathrooms and locker rooms. Experts also anticipate cases on visa policies, First Amendment rights, academic freedom, and federal funding, and are watching Trump v. Orr on gender-marker passports. The Court has blocked every lower-court injunction against Trump's higher education policies on the shadow docket, and experts warn resulting harms may be irreversible.

Consumer Electricals Ltd submitted a bid on September 20, 2017, as an expression of interest for the business and brand of debt-laden Kenstar, a Videocon group subsidiary. The bid price was not disclosed and results are pending. Videocon, with debt over Rs 40,000 crore, has been considering asset sales to reduce debt.

Riley Oil Company in Paoli, Indiana, is one of the last full-service gas stations in the area, offering free gas pumping, windshield washing, and oil checks without charging customers extra. Founded in 1971 by Glendon Riley, the business remains family-owned, with six family members, including owners Jo Ann and Jeff Riley, working there. Employees and customers value the personal interaction, and the family expects the business to remain in the family for generations, as great-grandchildren are already being born.

Employees of an Oklahoma City Taco Bell called police Tuesday to report 52-year-old Zette Madden chasing them with a weapon, threatening them and demanding money. Madden destroyed cash registers, doors, and windows, causing thousands of dollars in damages. She was tased after ignoring officers' commands and remains jailed on multiple charges.

This study presents molecular dynamics simulations of nanoindentation in single-crystalline α-titanium for the [0001], [10̅10], and [2̅110] orientations at 10, 300, and 600 K, performed with LAMMPS using an EAM potential and coupled, for the first time, with orientation-resolved Schmid factor mapping. Load–displacement curves show an initial Hertzian elastic response followed by pop-in events marking plasticity onset, most pronounced for the [0001] orientation and more subdued for the prismatic orientations. A stress-driven, martensitic HCP→BCC transformation occurs beneath the indenter, with propensity highest at low temperatures. Plasticity is dominated by basal a-type dislocations (1/3⟨1̅210⟩), while pyramidal ⟨c+a⟩ slip becomes increasingly active with temperature. Schmid factor maps spatially coincide with the plastic zone, linking resolved shear stress to slip system activation. Surface morphologies differ by orientation: circular/quasi-hexagonal pile-up for [0001], a dual-lobe pile-up associated with a lasso mechanism forming prismatic loops for [10̅10], and asymmetric pile-up for [2̅110]. Elevated temperatures produce more diffuse deformation and enhanced recovery. Dislocation density is highest in [0001] at all temperatures and increases with temperature there, whereas prismatic orientations show lower densities that decrease with temperature due to annihilation. The results agree with AFM experiments and provide a mechanistic framework for temperature-dependent deformation in hcp titanium.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on June 2, 2022, reporting that it updated its guidance for the quarter ending June 30, 2022 due to unfavorable foreign exchange rate movements through May. A slide deck with the revised guidance was furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The filing includes standard forward-looking statement disclaimers and states the information is not deemed "filed" under Section 18 of the Exchange Act. The report was signed by Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer. Microsoft's registered securities include common stock, 3.125% Notes due 2028, and 2.625% Notes due 2033, all trading on NASDAQ under the symbol MSFT.

Falkland Islands Senior Fisheries Scientist Alexander Arkhipkin is contributing to international efforts to address unregulated high seas fishing, which limits data on vessels and catches and constrains stock assessments of straddling stocks, increasing overfishing risk. In the Southwest Atlantic, over 250 jiggers and trawlers annually take hundreds of thousands of tons of squid, hake and rock cod. In September 2017, Peru's IMARPE held a workshop on jumbo squid stock assessment, where Arkhipkin gave a keynote speech, producing recommendations on surveys and assessment techniques.

Nintendo confirmed its Labo line will include the Toy Con Garage, a kit for building custom cardboard creations using basic inputs, actions, and if-then statements. Demonstrations included a cardboard electric guitar and electronic tennis, though whether a Labo set purchase is required remains unclear.

This patent application, a continuation of related applications, concerns physical layer preambles and signaling for wireless communication in WLANs conforming to the IEEE 802.11 family of standards. It describes methods, apparatus, computer-readable media, and systems for receiving a packet whose preamble includes a universal signal field (U-SIG) followed by version-specific signal fields, such as an EHT-SIG, on one or more subchannels. The U-SIG carries a version identifier, frequency occupation information (bandwidth and punctured channel information), and a format information field, from which a receiving device determines the packet format and the subchannels containing the version-specific signal field. The disclosure covers preamble designs for channels up to 320 MHz that minimize preamble length, accommodate different signal field types, and support parallelized signaling across content channels, subchannels, and subbands. It describes U-SIG formats for trigger-based, single-user, multi-user, and unified SU/MU PPDUs; EHT-SIG structures with common and user fields carrying RU allocation, spatial stream configuration, and per-user information; options for indicating punctured channels; encoding and painting schemes for EHT-SIG code blocks; and RU allocation tables supporting OFDMA and MU-MIMO with up to 16 spatial streams. A stated advantage is a universal signal field that supports future wireless communication protocols with new features and greater bandwidth.

Darren Till won a close, controversial unanimous decision over Stephen Thompson in the main event of UFC Fight Night 130 at Echo Arena in Liverpool on May 27, 2018. Some argued the outcome was influenced by the location, prompting Till to offer an immediate rematch in America, predicting the same result.

The Justice Department has directed Education Secretary Linda McMahon to investigate the University of Nevada at Reno's UndocuPack program, which supports undocumented students, citing reports that the university assists undocumented immigrants with resources, aid, and career support and questioning whether taxpayer funds subsidize illegal immigration. UNR president Brian Sandoval, a former Republican governor, responded that the program serves all students regardless of citizenship status, uses no federal funds, and that the university complies with federal and state law; the university plans to respond through legal channels. Advocates view the move as part of an escalating Trump administration campaign against higher education benefits for undocumented students, following lawsuits against five states over in-state tuition and investigations of universities offering related scholarships. They fear colleges may preemptively scale back or close such programs, of which at least 59 exist nationwide.

This patent application, a continuation of prior filings, describes systems and methods for processing mobile payments when disconnected from payment servers ("offline payments"). A user device with an e-wallet can make purchases by communicating with a merchant payment system via a local network (e.g., NFC, Bluetooth, LAN, or QR code scanning) when external network connectivity is unavailable, such as during natural disasters or network congestion. The user device and merchant payment system synchronize transaction details and store records of offline transactions. When either device reconnects to the payment server, it transmits the offline transaction information, and the server processes the payment only once per transaction ID to prevent duplicate processing.

A payment server maintains an offline mode status repository ensuring offline mode is enabled for only one user device per e-wallet at a time, preventing account overdrawing. Users can reserve amounts for offline transactions through pre-authorization charges. The offline mode can be transferred between user devices via local communications, involving handover data, confirmation messages, and status messages even when both devices are offline. The payment server includes components for e-wallet configuration, offline mode status updates, and payment processing. The invention may be implemented as a method, system, or computer program product, including in cloud computing environments.

The High Post Split Offense is a simple yet devastating basketball offense used from youth to professional levels, featuring high post splits, down screens, and back cuts. Its 2-3 high alignment frees the baseline for quick cuts, creates scoring opportunities for all five players, eliminates weakside defensive help, and provides strong offensive rebounding. The offense progresses through four phases: high post splits with reads and counters (handoffs, fake splits, back cuts, same-side cuts), down screens with counters (curls, fades, back cuts, screen-and-rolls, slips), high post isolation with counters to overplay (lob passes, wing feeds, exchanges), and strong post ups. Entry variations include the Flop/Back Cut, Wing Pass, Wing Double Away, and Post Single/Double. Success depends on spacing, execution, coordination, non-verbal communication, timing, and defensive recognition, along with individual skill development.

The disclosure relates to a tonneau cover for pickup truck beds, comprising a fixed base panel and pivotally attached panel sections that fold up for stowed storage. Each panel section includes a latching assembly with pinch latch assemblies on opposing side walls, connected by a longitudinally extending connector, enabling both latches to release by actuating a single pinch handle. Features include spring-loaded pinch handles that return to the latched position, integrated lights near the latch assemblies, a vertical gusset assembly supporting folded panels upright, a buckle securement system, hinge assemblies with resilient seals and seal rods, and adjustable side rails with clips for securing panels to the truck bed.

A Bank of England regulator said British banks should not expect further major capital or liquidity rule changes now that Basel III reforms are implemented; future focus will be on new risks and unintended regulatory consequences.

Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge suffered an elbow injury in late July, missing 10 days. After returning, his arm strength remained diminished, though his hitting was unaffected. Judge said he will "do some work" on the elbow this offseason but does not know if surgery is needed.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-K annual report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2021, filed with the SEC (Commission File Number 001-37845), describes the company as a technology company founded in 1975, headquartered in Redmond, Washington, with a mission to empower every person and organization to achieve more. As of December 31, 2020, the aggregate market value of common stock held by non-affiliates was $1.7 trillion, and 7,514,891,248 shares were outstanding as of July 26, 2021.

The company operates through three segments: Productivity and Business Processes (Office, LinkedIn, Dynamics), Intelligent Cloud (Azure, server products, Enterprise Services), and More Personal Computing (Windows, Devices, Gaming, Search advertising). Key developments include a March 2021 acquisition of ZeniMax Media Inc., an April 2021 definitive agreement to acquire Nuance Communications, and the June 2021 announcement of Windows 11.

As of June 30, 2021, Microsoft employed approximately 181,000 people full-time (103,000 in the U.S., 78,000 internationally). Corporate social responsibility commitments include being carbon negative by 2030, water positive by 2030, and zero waste by 2030, with a $1 billion climate investment pledge; the company reported reducing its carbon emissions by 586,683 metric tons in fiscal year 2020. Initiatives addressing racial injustice and digital skills are described, with over 42 million people accessing free training through the skills initiative.

The report details competition across its markets (including Apple, Google, Amazon, Oracle, Salesforce, SAP, and others), research and development activities (with over 65,000 patents issued and over 21,000 pending), distribution channels (OEMs, direct, distributors and resellers), and volume licensing programs. Executive officers as of July 29, 2021 include Satya Nadella (Chairman and CEO), Amy Hood (CFO), and Bradford Smith (President and Chief Legal Officer), among others.

Risk factors highlighted include intense competition across all markets, competition among platform-based ecosystems, varying business models of competitors, and execution and competitive risks associated with the company's increasing focus on cloud-based services, including the need to build and maintain cloud infrastructure that reduces operating margins.

This patent application describes methods and structures for forming multi-die integrated fan-out (InFO) packages and multi-chip modules (MCMs). Interconnect structures containing through-substrate vias (TSVs), dielectric and metallization layers, redistribution layers, and external connectors are fabricated, tested as known-good, singulated, and bonded to a carrier substrate using an adhesive film. The structures are then encapsulated in a first encapsulant and thinned to form a reconstructed wafer with exposed external connectors. Tested packaged semiconductor devices, such as processor dies (e.g., CPU, GPU) and memory cubes (e.g., hybrid memory cubes), are arranged on the reconstructed wafer and bonded to the interconnect structures using either low-temperature direct copper-to-copper bonding or solder bonding, followed by underfill (capillary underfill or moldable underfill), encapsulation, thinning, de-bonding of the carrier substrate, and formation of external contacts. In an alternative embodiment, a single universal interconnect structure shared by multiple semiconductor dies is embedded in the encapsulant, with a series of universal redistribution layers (URDLs) formed over it, to which discrete semiconductor components are flip-chip bonded. The disclosed approach enables super large package sizes (e.g., greater than 70 mm by 70 mm) for high-performance computing applications, improves component and board level reliability through known-good testing, reduces coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) mismatch stress by matching the package CTE to that of printed circuit boards, and simplifies manufacturing through wafer-level integration.

On November 26, 2001, Enron's stock fell to an all-time low, closing at $4.01 after dropping as much as 20% intraday, amid mounting doubts that Dynegy's proposed acquisition would be completed on its original terms. Enron traded at less than one-third of its reported book value of $12.90 per share, reflecting investor distrust of the company's financial figures following repeated restatements and disclosures. Dynegy's board declined to comment on the deal's status while the company continued due diligence; the deal included a "material adverse change" clause that could allow Dynegy to back out. Enron formalized a three-week extension on a $690 million loan to December 14 and sought $500 million to $1 billion in additional financing. Citigroup had reduced its Enron exposure by $2.38 billion through credit default swap transactions. A third employee class-action lawsuit was filed over 401(k) losses, seeking $850 million and alleging Enron stock was sold without a required prospectus. Enron bonds traded at distressed levels of 48 cents on the dollar, while Dynegy's bonds also slipped on concerns the acquisition could harm its credit rating. Separately, Petrobras and its pension fund Petros were close to acquiring Enron's stakes in Brazilian gas distributors CEG and CEG Rio, and India's AV Birla group denied reports it would bid for Enron's stake in the Dabhol Power Company.

Martin Colin Hodder, 45, of Macclesfield, was jailed for 18 weeks at Stockport magistrates' court after admitting two assault charges for a January knife attack on his ex-partner and her daughter. After drinking one and a half bottles of vodka, he held a knife to his own throat, then cut his ex-partner's arms and slashed the daughter's wrist as she tried to disarm him. The sentence, which includes a one-year restraining order, was criticized by the older victim.

Coach Julien said an injured player is being evaluated, with no update available, and that he may play the next game. He explained he gave a skilled but inexperienced player a chance to move into Bergy's spot and was not disappointed with his performance. He acknowledged his team played better in the third period after sitting back too much in the first two. He noted Kane scored three goals in the last two games by finding quiet areas near the net and said his team needs more awareness around its own goal. With the series at do-or-die, he said the goal is to win the next game at home, expressing no panic and confidence that the committed group will bounce back. He said depth scoring from players like Shaw and Paille is not surprising, defended Zdeno as one of the league's best defensemen, and said he is deciding between Daugavins and Soderberg due to Gregory Campbell's injury. He also discussed momentum swings, coaching adjustments between the two teams, the need for every player to contribute without passengers, and overtime bench management focused on scoring the next goal.

The Enerfax Daily newsletter (No. 937, February 20, 2002) lists physical natural gas prices across Gulf/Eastern, Western, and Canadian/Rockies regions, with Henry Hub at $2.32, along with physical power prices for multiple hubs. Natural gas futures rallied on fund buying, with March settling up $0.191 at $2.397/MMBtu and April up $0.17 at $2.427, triggered by a bullish below-normal weather forecast; the AGA storage report was expected to show a withdrawal of 110–120 Bcf. SG Resources Mississippi is conducting an open season through March 4, 2002 for firm storage services at its Southern Pines Energy Center on the Mississippi-Alabama border.

In company news, JP Morgan Chase was sued by shareholders alleging it failed to fully disclose its Enron exposure, initially listed at $900 million and later raised to $2.6 billion; the bank called the suit without merit. El Paso Corp plans to sell 10,677 miles of Texas pipelines and gathering systems plus a New Mexico plant share to El Paso Energy Partners for $750 million to boost its balance sheet after a Moody's warning. AES, whose stock fell over 50% in two sessions, will sell $1–1.5 billion in assets and cut capital spending by $490 million; Fitch downgraded its debt. A Dynegy executive stated Enron's accounting problems stemmed from poor financial disclosure rather than mark-to-market accounting. The National Energy Marketers Association criticized Senator Feinstein's derivatives oversight bill as an overreaction to Enron's collapse. A Platts study found feared data center power demands never materialized. MISO, PJM, and SPP announced a Single Market Design Forum meeting for March 13. Power futures tables, NYMEX volumes, option volatility data, technical analysis of price gaps, and a financial summary showing declines in major indices are also included, along with advertisements for energy industry software and services.

The passage describes subsystems and features of TI's MSPM0G3519/G3518/G1519/G1518 microcontrollers. The Low-Frequency Sub System (LFSS_B) combines peripherals clocked by a 32kHz LFCLK, including the RTC_B real-time clock (with calendar counters, alarm interrupts, crystal offset and temperature drift calibration up to ±240ppm, and clock output for calibration) and an independent watchdog timer (IWDT) that generates a POR reset if not serviced within its programmed time, with eight selectable periods from 2ms to 2hr. A windowed watchdog timer (WWDT) can generate resets or interrupts and supports an interval timer mode. Two timer types are provided: TIMGx general-purpose timers (16-/32-bit counters, prescaler, QEI and Hall sensor support in some instances) and TIMAx advanced timers (complementary PWM with programmable dead band, fault handling with fast PWM responses, and additional capture/compare channels). The IOMUX manages peripheral function selection on digital IOs. A two-wire serial wire debug (SWD) interface provides debug access, and a bootstrap loader (BSL) enables device configuration and memory programming via UART or I2C, protected by a 256-bit user-defined password and invocable via pin state, blank device boot, or software command. A memory-mapped FACTORY region provides read-only device identification and trim data. Application guidance recommends decoupling capacitors on VDD/VSS, a 47kΩ pullup with 10nF capacitor on NRST, an external 100kΩ resistor for the SYSOSC frequency correction loop, and a 0.47µF tank capacitor on VCORE. The document also covers development tools (Code Composer Studio, IAR, Keil, TI Arm-Clang, GNU Arm), device nomenclature (X for experimental, MSP for production devices), revision history changes from November 2024 to April 2025, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

A hockey coach reflects on his team's important overtime win, saying they skated better and generated quality chances but must improve in the second period, where the opponent has dominated the series.
