He credits a player for scoring by doing things right, defends his team against the perception that they only play defense, and attributes earlier losses to not skating after a long break. He stresses resiliency, ignoring media criticism, and focusing on the dressing room, while noting the opponent succeeds through team play rather than individual stars. He praises Carney's poise as leadership, emphasizes managing the puck and staying composed, and expresses confidence that the best team will win the Stanley Cup.

University of Michigan researchers led by Anish Tuteja have developed an "omniphobic" coating that repels nearly every known liquid. Inspired by Tuteja's goal of making cleanup after his child easier, the clear, durable coating can be applied to any surface to prevent grime buildup on tables, floors, walls, and phone screens. It combines fluorinated polyurethane and F-POSS. The team is now testing whether it is toxic.

The United States District Court for the Middle District of Alabama granted summary judgment for defendant Waste Away Group, Inc. in a Title VII gender discrimination action brought by plaintiff Paula Norrell, who alleged the company failed to promote her because of her sex and maintained practices with a disparate impact on women.

Norrell, hired in 1996, was promoted to customer service manager in 1997 and to Opelika district sales manager in 1998. When Waste Away combined the Montgomery and Opelika districts in 2001, Norrell, Greg Folmar, and Terry White interviewed for the single combined district sales manager position. Decisionmakers Johnson and Mitchell selected White, citing his prior experience in the combined role, outside sales experience, and organizational and leadership skills. Norrell was instead offered a lower-paying Temporary Construction Representative position, which she declined after maternity leave and left the company.

The court found Norrell established a prima facie case of disparate treatment, but concluded Waste Away articulated a legitimate, nondiscriminatory reason for promoting White. Norrell's pretext evidence—an alleged request that she train White, allegedly discriminatory remarks by supervisor Malphrus, and a crude comment by Johnson—was deemed insufficient, as the remarks were stray, isolated, or unrelated to the promotion decision, and the qualification disparity was not "so apparent" as to establish pretext. Norrell also abandoned her disparate impact claim. Final judgment was entered for the defendant, with costs taxed against the plaintiff.

Plug Power Inc (NASDAQ:PLUG) shares fell 1.54% in the most recent session, closing at $1.92. Analysts project a 52-week mean price target of $3.22, with a high of $5 and a low of $1.30, based on 7 opinions. The stock's average brokerage recommendation is 1.86; of 7 analysts, 1 rates it Buy, 4 Outperform, 1 Hold, and 1 Underperform. Its ATR-14 is 0.08, with weekly volatility of 3.54% and monthly volatility of 4.50%. The RSI stands at 51.76. The company has a market capitalization of $445.8 million and 232.19 million outstanding shares, with 2.29 million shares traded recently versus an average of 3.79 million.

Ben Bishop says he feels better after a few days of rest, which made playing easier. He credits GMs Doug Armstrong and Bryan Murray for his path from Ottawa to Tampa Bay, saying he wasn't ready after two years and that years in the minors taught him to be a pro. He prepares the same way for every game regardless of stakes, credits the team's consistency for its playoff success, and says losses won't change how they bounce back. He calls the experience enjoyable with a great locker room.

The Triangle Post Offense, created and refined by Tex Winter, is the offense that has won the most NBA championships. Rather than relying on set plays, it is a system of defensive recognition based on sound principles, precise court spacing, and execution of fundamentals. It consists of three components: an entry, a sideline triangle, and a weakside two-person game. Players are spaced 15 to 20 feet apart at all times, which spreads the defense, discourages help or double-teaming, and enables accurate passing. Any pass or dribble can initiate the offense, making it difficult to disrupt, with the defense's deployment dictating which entry is used. The sideline triangle features strong post-ups, post split actions, and post solo cuts, while the weakside two game offers pass and dribble series with reads and counters based on defender behavior. Because the offense is based on defensive reads, defensive overplays such as fronting the post, double-teaming, or denying passes trigger automatic counters that often produce easy baskets. Success requires players to be well-schooled in fundamentals and footwork, taught through a whole-part-whole method using progressive breakdown drills from two-on-two to five-on-five. Game strategies include scouting opponents, anticipating reads, and varying entries so defenders cannot focus on one option. Even teams not using the offense should learn to defend against it, as it is among the most used in the game.

Bollinger Bands, developed by financial analyst John Bollinger in the 1980s, are a technical indicator used to analyze asset volatility and potential trend changes. They consist of a central moving average with standard deviations plotted above and below it. While robust and easy to use, they have disadvantages: false signals, reduced effectiveness in range-bound markets, signal delays, and sensitivity to time periods and settings. Default settings use a 20-period moving average, which can be adjusted in TradingView. A breakout strategy based on band breaches can be implemented in TradingView using Pine Script functions such as ta.sma() and ta.stdev(). Testing on the H4 time frame with modified parameters produced considerable returns using 100% of capital per trade, though drawdowns may be uncomfortable. TradingView enables quick prototyping of such strategies.

Queen Elizabeth visited young victims of the Manchester bombing at the Royal Manchester Children's Hospital on Thursday, meeting patients, doctors, nurses, and emergency responders. The attack killed 22 and injured over 100; she called it "wicked."

The speaker, taking the oath of office, accepts the trust placed in him by the people and expresses a solemn sense of responsibility to all citizens. He affirms the strength of democratic self-government and urges that partisan bitterness and sectional prejudice give way to patriotism and unity. He pledges devotion to the Constitution and promises to be guided by a just construction of it, observing the distinction between Federal and State powers. He notes that every citizen shares in upholding the government and owes vigilance over public servants. He advocates economical public spending, a foreign policy of peace, independence, and neutrality, sound finances with relief from unnecessary taxation, protection of the public domain, fair treatment of the Indians, repression of polygamy in the Territories, exclusion of servile immigrant labor, civil-service reform based on merit, and equal justice and rights for the freedmen. He closes by invoking God's blessing on the nation's labors.

FTB Advisors Inc. raised its Vanguard Total International Stock ETF (VXUS) stake by 3.6% in Q2 to 13,149 shares worth $706,000. Jane Goodall, who died October 1 at age 91, assembled a unique collection of chimpanzee skeletons from Gombe National Park, where she had studied chimps for nearly 30 years. Her team retrieved bodies within days of death, placed them in a tin drum for insects to clean, and preserved bones from individuals with known sex, age, weight, and life histories, enabling research on how development shaped skeletal features. In a 1990 phone interview, Goodall responded with humility about implications for understanding ancient hominids, saying "We just don't know." She explained she began collecting skeletons early in her research because "you shouldn't waste anything." The skeleton of Flo, a dominant matriarch who died in 1972, was larger than most at Gombe yet weighed less than a stockier male, showed bone loss patterns unlike human osteoporosis, and reflected a birth within a few years of her death at nearly age 50.

The TPS7H500x-SP series is a family of radiation-hardness-assured PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, optimized for silicon and GaN power semiconductor applications. Each controller features a 0.613-V reference with +0.7%/-1% accuracy and a configurable switching frequency of 100 kHz to 2 MHz with external clock synchronization. The series comprises the full-featured dual-output TPS7H5001-SP, the single-output TPS7H5002-SP and TPS7H5003-SP, and the dual-output TPS7H5004-SP for non-synchronous push-pull and full-bridge topologies. The devices operate from a 4-V to 14-V input, use fixed-frequency peak current mode control, and support topologies including buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge. Functionality includes programmable dead time and leading edge blank time, configurable duty cycle limits, soft start, three oscillator modes (internal, external synchronization, primary-secondary), hiccup mode overcurrent protection, external fault protection, slope compensation, and thermal shutdown at 175°C. The document also provides a synchronous push-pull converter design example and PCB layout guidelines.

The author describes the second week of motherhood as the most difficult period, harder than the first week when endorphins, visitors, and pain medication still provided support. By week two, sleep deprivation turned her into an emotional mess, breastfeeding became painful with raw nipples after her prescription pain medication ran out, and her babies struggled to gain weight due to low milk supply or protein allergies. She felt lonely after her mother left and visitors stopped, couldn't soothe her crying baby during an unrecognized growth spurt, fought with her husband over small things, and her baby wouldn't sleep at night. These challenges affected her mental health, confidence, and marriage, though things eventually improved and she came to love the fourth trimester.

On June 15, 2017, Amazon.com, Inc. entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger with Whole Foods Market, Inc. and Walnut Merger Sub, Inc., an indirect wholly-owned Amazon subsidiary. Under the agreement, Merger Sub will merge into Whole Foods Market, which will survive, and each outstanding Whole Foods Market share will be converted into the right to receive $42.00 per share in cash. Closing is conditioned on Whole Foods Market shareholder approval, expiration of the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period, and Competition Act (Canada) clearance; the transaction is not conditioned on financing. Either party may terminate if the merger is not consummated by February 15, 2018, extendable once by 90 days. Whole Foods Market must pay a $400 million termination fee in specified circumstances, including a board recommendation change or entry into an alternative acquisition agreement. Amazon expects to finance the merger with debt financing and cash on hand, supported by a commitment letter for a 364-day senior unsecured bridge facility of up to $13.7 billion from Goldman Sachs Bank USA, Goldman Sachs Lending Partners LLC, Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith Incorporated, and Bank of America, N.A. A joint press release announcing the agreement was issued on June 16, 2017.

A follow-through day is a market-timing concept developed by William J. O'Neil, creator of the CANSLIM method, designed to identify when a market correction or downtrend has ended and a new uptrend has begun. It occurs on Day 4 or later of a rally attempt, when a major index (such as the S&P 500, Nasdaq, or Dow) closes significantly higher than the previous day on greater volume. A rally attempt begins with Rally Day 1 (an up day, or a "pink" day closing slightly down but in the top half of its range), and Days 2 and 3 must not fall below Rally Day 1's low, or the attempt fails. Early signs of failure include weak closes and closes below the prior follow-through day's low; a new low below the rally attempt's starting point means complete failure and serves as a sell signal. Since the early 1900s, no bull market has started without a follow-through day. However, a backtest on the S&P 500 (using SPY) showed poor short-term results due to the market's mean-reverting nature, though results improved slightly with a filter such as a 25-day RSI below 55.

The double top chart pattern is a bearish reversal price action formation consisting of two swing highs at approximately the same level with a swing low between them. It appears at the end of an uptrend or prolonged pullback in a downtrend, signaling a likely downward reversal. The swing highs form a resistance level, while the neckline—connecting the swing lows—acts as support. A break below the neckline suggests the uptrend may be ending, prompting traders to close long positions or open shorts. Profit targets are estimated by projecting the pattern's height downward from the neckline; stop losses can be placed in the middle of or above the pattern. Trading rules include confirming an existing uptrend, ensuring swing highs are within 3% of each other, and waiting for a significant volume break below the neckline. Thomas Bulkowski's research found only 39% of double top formations reach their target, versus 68% for double bottoms. The authors conclude shorting is generally difficult due to the market's upward tailwind, making this pattern tough to trade.

Retired Metro Police homicide detective Phil Ramos reviewed the newly released 1 October body camera videos, noting officers' tension outside Stephen Paddock's hotel room. He did not fault the first officer for not activating his camera and found an accidental gunshot unsurprising given expectations of a firefight. He was surprised the footage lacked a time stamp and said conclusions cannot yet be drawn.

This passage is a compilation of news articles dated October 29, 2001, concerning Enron Corp.'s deepening financial crisis. Moody's Investors Service downgraded Enron's senior unsecured debt to Baa2 from Baa1—two notches above junk status—and placed its commercial paper rating on review for downgrade, citing deteriorating financial flexibility after write-downs and charges from previously undisclosed partnership investments. Enron's shares fell to near seven-year lows (around $13.81–$14.02), having lost more than half their value in two weeks, after the company reported its first quarterly loss in over four years (roughly $618–638 million) and wrote down $1.2 billion in shareholder equity tied to partnerships run by former CFO Andrew Fastow, who was ousted; the SEC is examining those transactions.

Enron drew down about $3 billion in bank credit lines to repay roughly $2 billion in commercial paper and is negotiating with banks, including Citigroup and J.P. Morgan Chase, for $1–2 billion in additional credit to restore investor confidence. Analysts called the drawdown an act of desperation and predicted lenders would demand harsher terms, such as collateral. Enron's bonds fell to about 80–83 cents on the dollar, near distressed levels, with yields rising to 12.1 percent.

Major U.S. energy traders—including Mirant, El Paso, American Electric Power, and Duke Energy—said dealings with Enron continued at normal levels while they monitored its credit; several large European energy groups froze dealings pending new credit arrangements. GimmeCredit said Enron was unlikely to fall to junk status and its bonds might be undervalued if off-balance-sheet obligations were limited to about $3 billion. A newsletter reported Royal Dutch/Shell may be a potential takeover suitor.

Other articles noted broad corporate credit deterioration, with roughly $100 billion of debt expected to default in 2001 amid recession; insider buying at independent power producers (excluding Enron, which lacked positive insider signals); a commentary warning Enron's debacle could undermine overall market confidence; and a Houston Chronicle opinion piece praising Enron's contributions to Houston.

A heat wave in the northeastern United States is expected to move west after the Fourth of July, reaching southern California, the National Weather Service said. New York City's heat index reached 106°F, and at least one heat-related death was reported. An air quality alert was issued for New York, while a storm front is expected to cool the eastern seaboard this weekend.

This March 2024 paper argues that meaningful cross-partisan education policy is achievable despite heightened political polarization, which has been intensified by the pandemic, post-2020 racial reckoning, and eroded trust in schools. The paper prefers the term "cross-partisan" over "bipartisan," reflecting how compromise is now often viewed as capitulation. Focusing on state-level policy, where education is primarily governed, the authors identify five factors common to successful cross-partisan initiatives: (1) problems and solutions that are easy to communicate for broad appeal, illustrated by the science of reading movement and teacher shortage responses; (2) policies responsive to local context, such as the Interstate Teacher Mobility Compact and career and technical education programs in Idaho and North Carolina; (3) political cover for policymakers, exemplified by Virginia's history standards revision; (4) outcomes allowing both sides to claim victory, seen in teacher pay raises and civics education legislation; and (5) strategic use of media as an accelerant, notably the "Sold a Story" podcast. Additional considerations include understanding the political landscape, establishing a shared definition of the problem, gauging urgency, avoiding threats to frontline school staff, framing policies as expanding rather than narrowing options, maintaining mission focus, prioritizing objectives, and understanding opponents' values. The paper concludes that substantive, cross-partisan education reform is occurring in states and remains both real and achievable.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2021 reports total revenue of $45.3 billion, up 22% from $37.2 billion in the prior-year quarter, with net income of $20.5 billion (up 48%) and diluted EPS of $2.71. The effective tax rate was 0% versus 14%, primarily due to a $3.3 billion net income tax benefit from transferring intangible properties from its Puerto Rico subsidiary to the U.S. Segment revenue: Productivity and Business Processes $15.0 billion (+22%), Intelligent Cloud $16.9 billion (+31%), and More Personal Computing $13.3 billion (+12%). Microsoft Cloud revenue grew 36% to $20.7 billion; Azure and other cloud services grew 50%. Operating income rose 27% to $20.2 billion, and total assets were $335.4 billion. The company completed its $8.1 billion acquisition of ZeniMax Media in March 2021 and has a definitive agreement to acquire Nuance Communications for $19.7 billion, expected to close by early in the third quarter of fiscal 2022. A new $60 billion share repurchase program was approved on September 14, 2021, with $2.5 billion remaining under the prior $40 billion program. A quarterly dividend of $0.62 per share was declared. Unrecognized tax benefits were $15.9 billion, and IRS audits remain open for tax years 2004–2017, primarily concerning transfer pricing. Accrued legal liabilities were $333 million, with reasonably possible additional losses of approximately $500 million. Net cash from operations was $24.5 billion.

This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the seroprevalence of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) in Ethiopia, where the disease was first documented in June 2016 in the Dollo Ado district. Following PRISMA guidelines and registration in PROSPERO, researchers searched multiple electronic databases for observational studies published between 2016 and November 2023. Of 40 articles identified, five studies (four cross-sectional, one case-control) involving approximately 335,821 subjects from five regional states and Dire Dawa city administration were included. Diagnosis relied on ELISA (four studies) or RT-qPCR (one study). The pooled seroprevalence of Chikungunya in Ethiopia was 12.35%. The highest regional prevalence was in SNNPR (43.6%) and the lowest in Dire Dawa (~12%); at district level, Debub Ari had the highest (51.58%) and Lare the lowest (6.25%). Prevalence varied by occupation (highest among farmers at 49.7%), education (higher among the formally educated), and age (higher in adults), while findings by sex were inconsistent across studies. Random effects meta-analysis yielded an overall negative effect size of -1.25 (95% CI: -1.87, -0.63) with significant heterogeneity (I²=97.72%). ELISA-based studies showed significant variability, whereas RT-qPCR studies did not. Begg's and Egger's tests indicated no publication bias. Limitations included the small number of studies and predominance of cross-sectional designs. The authors conclude Chikungunya remains a public health concern in Ethiopia and recommend proactive preparedness, collaboration, and public awareness campaigns.

Days before the 2018 NFL Draft, the Colts hold nine picks, including No. 6 overall, as general manager Chris Ballard implements his rebuild. Top prospects include edge rusher Bradley Chubb, ideal if available given the team's poor 2017 pass rush; interior lineman Quenton Nelson, considered by some the safest prospect who could protect Andrew Luck; and running back Saquon Barkley, possibly the class's most talented player, though he may not be available.

This passage is from *Designing Distributed Systems* by Brendan Burns (O'Reilly, 2018). It begins with front matter covering supplemental material on GitHub, permissions for reusing code examples, O'Reilly Safari, contact information, and acknowledgments.

The introduction explains that modern applications require the reliability and scalability of distributed systems, and that containers and container orchestrators have simplified building them, much as object-oriented programming once transformed software development. A brief history traces computing from purpose-built machines through time-sharing, client-server architectures, and the rise of distributed systems in the 2000s driven by the internet and large-scale datacenters. The history of patterns covers Knuth's *The Art of Computer Programming* (1962), object-oriented design patterns such as the "gang of four" book, and the growth of open source. Patterns are defined as general blueprints for organizing distributed systems without mandating specific technologies; their value lies in learning from others' experience, providing a shared vocabulary, and enabling reusable components.

The book then presents single-node patterns, where co-located containers form atomic building blocks (called pods in Kubernetes). Motivations for splitting single-machine applications into multiple containers include resource isolation, team scaling, and separation of concerns.

The sidecar pattern pairs an application container with a sidecar that augments it. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy service via an nginx sidecar, synchronizing configuration from an API to the filesystem, a topz container for resource introspection, and a simple PaaS built with a Git synchronization sidecar. Reusable sidecars require parameterizing containers (e.g., via environment variables), defining a stable API, and documenting containers using Dockerfile directives such as EXPOSE, ENV, and LABEL.

The ambassador pattern brokers interactions between an application container and the outside world; the application connects to localhost while the ambassador routes traffic. Examples include client-side sharding (twemproxy with sharded Redis on Kubernetes), service brokering for portability across environments, and request splitting for experiments (nginx directing 10% of traffic to an experimental service using IP hashing).

The adapter pattern transforms an application container's interface to conform to a standardized one. Examples include Prometheus monitoring via a Redis exporter, log normalization with fluentd (for Redis slow queries and Apache Storm), and rich health checks for MySQL implemented in a separate adapter container.

The passage then introduces multi-node patterns, contrasting microservices with monolithic architectures. Microservices enable small teams, decoupling through formal APIs, and independent scaling, but make debugging and design more difficult.

The replicated load-balanced service pattern consists of identical stateless servers behind a load balancer; at least two replicas are needed for high availability. Readiness probes inform load balancers when applications can serve requests. Session tracking routes a user's requests to the same replica using IP hashing internally and cookies externally, with consistent hashing minimizing remapping during scaling. A caching layer (Varnish) is best deployed as a separate tier with fewer, larger replicas, and can also provide rate limiting and denial-of-service defense. SSL termination is handled by an additional nginx layer using certificates stored as Kubernetes secrets.

Finally, sharded services are introduced: unlike replicated services, each shard serves only a subset of requests, with a root distributing them. Sharding is generally used for stateful services whose data is too large for a single machine, and the passage concludes by beginning a discussion of sharded caching.

The Piotroski F-Score strategy, developed by Stanford finance professor Joseph Piotroski, is a stock selection method that uses financial analysis to identify undervalued stocks with strong fundamentals. It scores stocks on 9 criteria covering profitability, liquidity, and efficiency; scores of 8–9 indicate strong financials, while 0–4 indicate weak ones. Though mainly used for value stocks, it can also aid growth stock selection, but it is not a guarantee of success and should be combined with other research. Backtests support the strategy: Alpha Architect's version returned 13.3% annually on NYSE stocks (1974–2014) versus 12.6% for the original score and 11.2% for the S&P 500, with similar standard deviations; on the 20% cheapest stocks scoring above 6, returns were 15.9%, 15.2%, and 11.2%, respectively. ValueSignals tested it on European stocks (1999–2011), and Alexander Eriksen studied it on Norwegian and Swedish stocks (1997–2011). Implementation involves setting goals, calculating scores, diversifying, and regular monitoring and rebalancing.

Patrick McCaffery, son of Iowa head coach Fran McCaffery and brother of Hawkeyes player Connor McCaffery, committed to Iowa basketball Thursday night. The 6-foot-8 wing/forward is a consensus four-star prospect and potential McDonald's All-American, ranked as high as 30th nationally by Rivals, making him Iowa's highest-rated recruit since 2003. He is the program's first 2019 recruit, with two open slots remaining. McCaffery cited the chance to play for his father, alongside his brother, and in front of family as key reasons for committing. As a sophomore, he averaged 13.8 points on 60.6 percent shooting while helping Iowa City West win a Class 4A state title. He has since followed a nutrition and weight-lifting regimen, gaining roughly 10 pounds to address concerns about his strength.

During oral argument, several Supreme Court justices appeared open to allowing trial judges to restrict attorney-client discussions during overnight recesses while a testifying defendant remains on the stand. The case involves David Villarreal, convicted of murdering his boyfriend after the trial judge barred overnight discussion of his testimony; Texas courts upheld the restriction. Villarreal's lawyer, Stuart Banner, argued the distinction between "trial strategy" and "testimony" is unworkable and would chill constitutionally guaranteed advice. Justices Jackson, Kagan, and Gorsuch suggested a line could be drawn, with Gorsuch distinguishing impermissible "coaching" from suborning perjury. Prosecutor Andrew Warthen said even advice like "stop mumbling" would constitute impermissible coaching, surprising Chief Justice Roberts, but he accepted Justice Barrett's proposal permitting discussion of strategic consequences while barring testimony content and delivery. The court must choose between Texas's rule barring "management" of testimony and the United States's bright-line rule prohibiting any discussion of testimony, under which plea bargain advice would still be allowed.

The passage explains motivations for splitting applications into multiple containers even on a single machine: resource isolation (e.g., separating a user-facing service from a lower-priority background loader), team scaling around small, focused ownership of reusable modules, and separation of concerns that simplifies testing, updating, and deployment. It then introduces single-node container patterns, which assume containers are coscheduled on one machine and share resources such as filesystems, network namespaces, and memory—a grouping called a pod in Kubernetes.

The sidecar pattern pairs an application container with a sidecar that augments it, often without the application's knowledge. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy HTTP service via an nginx sidecar, synchronizing configuration from an API into a shared filesystem, providing process introspection through a topz container sharing the PID namespace, and building a simple PaaS where a sidecar syncs a Git repository while a Node.js server reloads updated code. Successful sidecars require parameterization (e.g., via environment variables), a stable API surface (where even subtle changes, such as altering parameter units, can be breaking), and documentation using Dockerfile directives like EXPOSE, ENV, and LABEL.

The ambassador pattern uses a container to broker interactions between the application container and the outside world. Applications include client-side sharding (e.g., twemproxy proxying to sharded Redis or memcached deployed via StatefulSets), service brokering for portability across environments, and request splitting for experiments (e.g., nginx directing 10% of traffic to an experimental service using IP hashing).

The adapter pattern modifies an application container's interface to conform to a standardized interface. Examples include exporting Prometheus-compatible metrics from Redis, normalizing logs with fluentd (e.g., Redis slow queries, Storm logs), and adding rich health checks to MySQL via a separate script container, avoiding modification of third-party images while enabling reuse and sharing.

The passage then turns to multi-node patterns and microservices, noting benefits (small teams, decoupling via formal APIs, independent scaling) and drawbacks (harder debugging and design). The replicated load-balanced service pattern serves stateless applications; at least two replicas are needed for high availability, and readiness probes inform load balancers when replicas can serve traffic. Session tracking (via IP hashing or application-level cookies) keeps a user's requests on one replica. A caching layer (e.g., Varnish) can be added as a separate tier and also supports rate limiting and denial-of-service defense, while nginx handles SSL termination as an additional layer.

Finally, sharded services split data across replicas, each serving a subset of requests, and are generally used for stateful services. Sharded caches improve memory utilization over replicated caches but make failures and rollouts more impactful; replicated sharded caches address this. Sharding functions map requests to shards using hash functions with determinism and uniformity, and choosing an appropriate key (e.g., request path, possibly country) is important. Consistent hashing limits key remapping when the number of shards changes.

The report and appendix cover events up to the Hawaiian revolution of January 17, 1893, with the narrative continued in the report accompanying the President's February 15, 1893 message, which transmitted to the Senate a treaty signed February 14, 1893, by the U.S. Secretary of State and representatives of the Provisional Government of the Hawaiian Islands. A chronologically arranged list of papers and a subject index follow. The passage includes a bibliography of works on the Hawaiian Islands and various congressional documents, along with dated correspondence and documents from 1826 to 1853, including the Treaty of Friendship, Commerce, and Navigation between the United States and the Sandwich Islands, signed at Honolulu on December 23, 1826, by Thomas ap Catesby Jones and King Kauikeaouli, as well as correspondence concerning protection of seamen, American claims, and commercial interests.

Middlesbrough striker Rudy Gestede says the team must believe they can end their slump to avoid relegation ahead of Monday's Premier League match against Arsenal. Middlesbrough, 19th and six points from safety, have not won a league game since mid-December.

This MIT lecture concludes the coverage of the predecessor problem by proving a lower bound nearly matching the known upper bound of min(log w, log_w n) achieved by Van Emde Boas and fusion tries. The bound holds even for static, randomized data structures with polynomial space, and is larger by a log log w factor; that factor is not real for near-linear space, but removing it is harder and not covered.

The lecture surveys prior lower bounds: Ajtai (1988) proved Omega(sqrt(log w)) for some problem size; Miltersen proved a complementary Omega(cube root of log n) bound and introduced the communication complexity perspective; Miltersen and others introduced round elimination; Beame and Fich (1999) proved Omega(log w / log log w) (for all w, some n) and Omega(sqrt(log n / log log n)) (for all n, some w), plus a static upper bound achieving the min of the two; an earlier PhD thesis (Xiao) independently proved the same bounds; Sen (2003) gave the clean round elimination proof covered here; and Patrascu and Thorup (2006–2007) gave a tight n–w–space trade-off, implying Van Emde Boas is optimal for small w and fusion tries for large w.

The proof targets the easier colored predecessor problem (each element is red or blue; a query reports only the predecessor's color), so its lower bound applies to standard predecessor, including randomized structures succeeding with probability above one half. In the communication complexity view, Alice (the query algorithm) knows the query x and sends messages of at most a = log s bits (s = space in words); Bob (the memory/data structure) knows y and replies with b = w bits; each round corresponds to one word read.

The round elimination lemma states that a protocol for f^k—where Alice holds x1…xk, Bob holds y and an index i (knowing x1…x_{i−1}), and the goal is f(x_i, y)—with Alice speaking first can be converted into a protocol for f with Bob speaking first, one fewer message, and error increased by O(sqrt(a/k)). Intuitively, Alice's first message can devote only about a/k bits to the relevant x_i, which Bob can guess.

Applying the lemma: eliminating Alice-to-Bob messages splits Alice's w′-bit input into k = Theta(a t²) chunks, with all elements differing only in one unknown chunk, reducing w′ by a factor of a t² (analogous to Van Emde Boas). Eliminating Bob-to-Alice messages splits Bob's n′ integers into k = Theta(b t²) groups via a tree, reducing n′ by a factor of b t² (analogous to fusion trees). Each elimination adds O(1/t) error, so after 2t eliminations the total error is below 1/3, contradicting the fact that a zero-message protocol errs with probability at least 1/2. This yields t = Omega(min(log_{a t²} w, log_{b t²} n)) = Omega(min(log_a w, log_b n)). For polynomial space (a = O(log n)), this gives Omega(min(log_w n, log w / log log n)) and implies the Beame–Fich bounds.

This study examined immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccines in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients treated with methotrexate (MTX), abatacept, or rituximab compared to healthy controls. The cohort included 40 individuals (13 healthy controls, 27 RA patients). Rituximab-treated patients showed near-total loss of anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibodies. Abatacept-treated patients had significantly reduced S-specific and neutralizing antibodies, reduced B cell class switching to IgG, altered memory B cell differentiation, and diminished production of IL-2, IFNγ, and IL-21 by S-specific CD4+ T cells. MTX-treated subjects showed reduced S-specific CD4+ T cell frequency but no significant differences in antibody levels, B cell numbers, phenotype, or class switching compared to controls. RBD-specific B cell numbers were similar across control, abatacept, and MTX groups. The findings indicate that abatacept impairs vaccine efficacy by disrupting T cell help to B cells for production of high-titer, class-switched neutralizing antibodies. The authors suggest temporary cessation of abatacept treatment before vaccination when clinically manageable to improve vaccine-induced immune protection.

The whitepaper describes the NVIDIA Ampere GA102 and GA104 GPUs, part of the GA10x class building on the Turing architecture. Compared to Turing, GA10x GPUs are up to 1.7x faster in raster graphics and up to 2x faster in ray tracing. GA102 powers the GeForce RTX 3090, RTX 3080, RTX A6000, and NVIDIA A40; GA104 powers the GeForce RTX 3070. Fabricated on Samsung's 8nm 8N custom process, GA102 contains 28.3 billion transistors on a 628.4 mm2 die, with 10752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor Cores. The RTX 3090 targets 8K HDR gaming with 24GB of GDDR6X; the RTX 3080 delivers up to 2x the performance of the RTX 2080; the RTX 3070 rivals the RTX 2080 Ti. The RTX A6000 and A40 use 48GB of GDDR6, scalable to 96GB via NVLink.

Key architectural features include doubled FP32 processing (both SM datapaths execute FP32, delivering over 35 FP32 TFLOPS in the RTX 3090); second-generation RT Cores offering up to 2x ray tracing performance with concurrent RT, graphics, and compute execution; third-generation Tensor Cores whose sparsity feature doubles throughput and whose TF32 precision provides up to 5x training throughput; GDDR6X memory at up to 19.5 Gbps; third-generation NVLink with 112.5 GB/sec total bandwidth; and PCIe Gen 4. The full GA102 contains seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, 84 SMs, and 112 ROPs, now located in the GPC. Ampere GPUs are up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing.

Indonesia's sovereign wealth fund Danantara will launch at least eight waste-to-power projects by the end of October, beginning in Jakarta before expanding across Java and Bali to cover 33 municipalities. Each plant will process 1,000 tonnes of waste daily and generate an estimated 15 megawatts of electricity, with capital costs of 2–3 trillion rupiah (around $180 million) per facility. Danantara will finance and oversee the projects, with state utility PLN purchasing the electricity for the national grid. The government has removed tipping fees for municipalities, and local governments will provide up to five hectares of land per site. The initiative supports Indonesia's 2025–2034 electricity plan targeting 453 MW of waste-to-energy capacity and could reduce landfill reliance, cut emissions, and advance renewable energy goals.

MTN and four banks—Access Bank, Agricultural Development Bank, Republic Bank, and Societe Generale—are seeking to raise a combined GH¢4.67 billion on the Ghana Stock Exchange within six months, the highest amount in the bourse's nearly three-decade history. MTN aims to raise GH¢3.48 billion by offloading 35 percent of the firm, while the banks seek GH¢1.19 billion through rights issues to meet the Bank of Ghana's new capital requirement of GH¢400 million by December 2018. Experts, including former GSE Council Chairman Dr Sam Mensah, expressed concerns about market capacity and timing risks, noting the MTN IPO could exhaust available funds. Pension assets exceeding GH¢21 billion may provide a cushion, but success would require strong foreign participation, which could affect the cedi if profits are later repatriated.

This study developed and validated an Arabic version of the Orthognathic Quality of Life Questionnaire (OQLQ), the only instrument for measuring quality of life in patients with dentofacial deformities undergoing orthognathic surgery. Using a translation and back-translation process, the questionnaire was tested in 74 adult patients recruited between January 2021 and December 2022 in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. Internal consistency was excellent (Cronbach's α = 0.92), and test-retest reliability in 15 patients was excellent overall and for three of four domains, with only the awareness of dentofacial deformity domain rated as good. Construct validity was supported by correlations between OQLQ scores and surgical satisfaction and perceived appearance change. Responsiveness testing showed overall OQLQ scores were significantly lower after surgery, with facial esthetics improving significantly in a paired subgroup (n=12). Limitations included small validation cohorts and sampling from a single private practice. The authors conclude the Arabic OQLQ is reliable, valid, and responsive, filling a gap for Arabic-speaking populations.

The Supreme Court will consider whether the Constitution's ex post facto clause applies to the 1996 Mandatory Victims Restitution Act (MVRA) in the case of Holsey Ellingburg, who robbed a bank. If the clause applies, Ellingburg owes only the restitution required when he committed his crime; if not, more onerous revisions increase his obligations. Ellingburg argues restitution is criminal because it is imposed as part of the criminal sentence, uses criminal procedures, limits victims' involvement, and imposes incarceration for noncompliance. The government concedes restitution under the MVRA is criminal, so a court-appointed amicus defends the lower court's decision. The author predicts the justices will side with Ellingburg.
The appeal in United States v. Frank Walker was docketed and dismissed without costs, on the appellant's motion and the appellee's consent.
Delta announced plans to acquire up to an additional 32 percent of Grupo Aeroméxico's shares at MXP$43.59 per share, pending regulatory approvals in Mexico and the United States.

Tradeshift, a supply chain payments and marketplaces startup that recently added blockchain, raised $250 million in a Series E round led by Goldman Sachs and PSP Investments, bringing total funding to over $400 million and valuing the company above $1.1 billion.

A hockey team representative says the team is more comfortable in the Stanley Cup Finals after not bringing their game in the first two games, noting that games three and four showed they can succeed when they play their own style. He cites the team's strong road record, the owner's increased financial commitment after past fan criticism, and roster depth with four lines, six defensemen, and good goaltending, aided by trade deadline additions. He praises a teammate who overcame injuries as one of the team's best players and says the focus is on the next game in Anaheim.

Stephen Pearse, a former CEO, entrepreneur, and angel investor with a background in telecommunications, IT, and health science, discusses startups and fundraising. He states that roughly one in ten startups succeeds, with investors seeking 10x returns, three of ten yielding moderate returns, and six failing. Startups must plan to exit by going public or being acquired so investors can recover their money. Startups can build products faster than large companies because employees work for stock, making them attractive acquisition targets.

Pearse emphasizes crafting a powerful elevator pitch to cut through noise: keep it simple enough for a third grader, open with a hook, induce greed in investors, know the audience, pitch to the lowest common denominator, limit pitches to 20 minutes, use pictures, avoid technical jargon, focus on customer benefits expressed in dollars, and firmly deflect tangential questions. He criticizes a 2004 pitch that led with financial projections and jargon, and praises a Boulder smart-home company, Revolve, for a clear, direct demonstration.

On fundraising, he advises raising money before it is needed, assuming six months to close, pitching to multiple VCs in parallel to create competition, and preferring top-tier firms over slightly better terms. He stresses cash flow management, willingness to pivot (citing Revolve's shift from irrigation systems to home automation), speed over patents, a clear mission, a resilient team, maintaining focus, and leveraging investors' networks rather than expecting direct help. He concludes that leadership—shown through passion, confidence, and engagement—determines success.

In 1977, Leeds hosted the UK's first Reclaim the Night march, prompted in part by the Yorkshire Ripper murders and advice that women should not walk alone after dark. The Leeds Revolutionary Feminist Group organised two marches in the city and encouraged feminist groups nationwide to march on the same night, with women gathering in 12 towns and cities on November 12. The marches continued for over a decade before fading in the early 1990s and were revived in 2004. Forty years on, the event inspires The Darkest Corners, a new work by Leeds theatre company RashDash, to be performed in a Holbeck car park as part of the Transform 17 festival, addressing issues that persist today.

This systematic review, conducted using Cochrane Collaboration methodology and PRISMA guidelines, examined evidence on how student personality traits influence satisfaction and success in online learning in higher education. Noting the growth of online and hybrid education, including in occupational therapy programs, the authors identified the absence of any prior review consolidating this literature. Searches of seven databases (January 2000–June 2024) yielded 848 articles after duplicate removal, of which 23 met inclusion criteria: peer-reviewed, English-language studies of higher education students in online settings using recognized Big Five or Myers-Briggs assessments with satisfaction or success outcomes. All included studies were level 4 evidence, resulting in low strength of evidence across all themes. Studies spanned multiple countries (most in the United States) and disciplines, but none examined occupational therapy.

Findings were organized into three themes: personality's interaction with online education (GPA, satisfaction, assignment preferences, engagement), comparisons across class formats, and personality's influence on choice of class format. Conscientiousness was consistently positively associated with grades, engagement, and satisfaction, while neuroticism was generally negatively related; openness and agreeableness also showed positive associations. Extraverts often preferred face-to-face formats but sometimes performed better online, and introverts frequently preferred online courses. Satisfaction measures varied widely and lacked standardization.

Limitations included the exclusively descriptive, low-level evidence, restricted search dates, possible omitted articles, and geographic and language differences. The authors recommend future intervention research, support for self-regulated learning, use of Universal Design for Learning, and study of occupational therapy education specifically.

Adjuncts at Southwestern College held a poorly attended rally seeking better wages and equal protections with full-time instructors. Adjuncts teach nearly 75 percent of classes but lack full-time benefits, often traveling between multiple colleges to earn enough to survive. Speakers described job insecurity, inadequate medical benefits, and financial strain. President Dr. Kindred Murillo and Trustee Roberto Alcantar voiced support for adjuncts. Organizers asked students and faculty to get involved in helping adjuncts secure paid office hours and disability leave.

Pika, an AI video company founded by 26-year-old Demi Guo and Chenlin Meng after they left Stanford's PhD program, has raised about $135 million at a $470 million valuation and reports 16.4 million users. Its new TikTok-like app includes a Predictive Video feature that generates complete videos—script, music, background, effects—from simple prompts or selfies, targeting Gen Z and Gen Alpha self-expression rather than cinematic output like OpenAI's Sora or Meta's Vibes. In San Francisco, AI-driven growth has lifted rents 6% in the past year, with Mission Bay up 13%, intensifying competition for apartments. TSMC's profit rose 39.1% on AI chip demand, beating estimates; it raised its 2025 revenue growth forecast to the mid-30% range and plans at least $40 billion in capacity investments. Spotify is partnering with Sony, Universal, Warner, Merlin, and Believe to develop "responsible" AI music products, including a generative AI lab. A survey shows low trust in AI mental health tools: 11% of Americans would consider using one, 8% trust them, and 4% have tried one.

The passage describes the NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture and its key features. Turing GPUs include hardware support for USB Type-C and VirtualLink, an open industry standard led by NVIDIA, Oculus, Valve, Microsoft, and AMD that delivers power, display, and data to VR headsets through a single USB-C connector, reducing cable clutter and enabling VR on small form factor devices. For SLI, Turing TU102 and TU104 GPUs use second-generation NVLink instead of the MIO and PCIe interfaces; each link provides 25 GB/sec per direction, with TU102 offering two links (100 GB/sec bidirectional). Two-way SLI is supported, while 3-way and 4-way configurations are not.

Turing introduces dedicated RT Cores in TU102, TU104, and TU106 GPUs that accelerate bounding volume hierarchy (BVH) traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, enabling real-time ray tracing roughly 10 times faster than Pascal (10+ Giga Rays/Sec versus ~1.1). A hybrid rendering model combines rasterization and ray tracing, aided by denoising techniques. The architecture also includes NGX, a deep learning technology stack using Tensor Cores (not functional on pre-Turing GPUs), featuring DLSS—trained on 64x supersampled reference images—DLSS 2X, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.

New rendering capabilities include Mesh Shading (Task and Mesh Shaders using a cooperative thread model to eliminate CPU draw call bottlenecks), Variable Rate Shading (adjustable shading rates per 16x16 pixel region, enabling content adaptive shading, motion adaptive shading, and foveated rendering), Texture Space Shading (decoupling shading from screen-space pixels with texel reuse), and Multi-View Rendering (up to four views per pass, expanding Pascal's Simultaneous Multi-Projection).

Chip specifications are provided: TU104 contains 13.6 billion transistors, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores, used in GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000; TU106 (GeForce RTX 2070) contains 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, without NVLink or SLI support. An RTX-OPS workload-based metric weights peak operations by usage, yielding 78 for RTX 2080 Ti. The document concludes with a ray tracing overview covering ray casting, BVH structures, denoising, and ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, followed by legal disclaimers and trademark notices.

This study examined Colombian undergraduate students' perceptions and preferences regarding online learning (OL) versus emergency remote education (ERE), a temporary teaching modality adopted during the COVID-19 pandemic. Eighty-eight students from a medium-sized private university in Colombia's Caribbean region completed a survey rating 14 components (e.g., content quality, interaction, assessment, feedback, resources) on a 1-10 scale for both modalities, plus open-ended questions. Analysis used descriptive statistics, the add-on preferential groups (APG) model with permutation tests, and content analysis. Results showed students generally preferred OL over ERE, with 10 items showing statistically significant differences favoring OL, particularly in assessment strategies, independent/asynchronous activities, content quality, and resource accessibility. Student-student interaction was the only area where preferences were nearly equal, with a slight lean toward ERE. Content analysis revealed ERE's advantages included pandemic adaptation, comfort, and instructor contact, while its drawbacks involved poor organization and instructor preparation. OL was valued for flexibility, structure, and learning effectiveness, but criticized for limited instructor interaction and repetitive activities. The authors conclude that both modalities were positively perceived, but recommend ongoing instructor training, improved assessment design, and greater support for peer interaction in post-COVID-19 learning environments.

Mark Cuban said President Trump's TrumpRx.gov—a federal website launching in early 2026 to sell prescription drugs directly to consumers at discounted rates—could succeed if it forces pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) to change. Cuban, who founded a similar DTC platform, Cost Plus Drugs, in 2022, graded the initiative a "B," saying it would have earned an "A" had PBM stocks not risen after the announcement. Pfizer will sell drugs at DTC cost with average savings of 50% and receives a three-year reprieve from Trump's pharmaceutical tariffs. Cuban said the system remains "rigged" to benefit PBMs, which a 2024 report found steered patients toward pricier drugs. Experts like KFF's Drew Altman are skeptical, noting the platform currently applies only to Pfizer and, as a cash-only option, would mainly help the uninsured.

The Russell 2000 Index tracks approximately 2,000 US small-cap stocks and rebalances annually on the fourth Friday of June to maintain accurate representation of the small-cap universe, adding and removing companies and adjusting weights based on changed market capitalizations. This process can create buying and selling imbalances. The article presents a trading strategy that buys the Russell 2000 at the close of the first trading day after June 23rd and sells at the close of the first trading day of July. Backtesting from 1988 using the ^RUT index shows an average gain of 1.34% over about six trading days, compared to 0.85% for the S&P 500 over the same period. A hedged version (50% long Russell 2000, 50% short S&P 500) averaged only 0.23% and performed flattishly in recent years.

Motley Fool Money reviews the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card, which offers unlimited 2% cash rewards with no categories or limits, a $200 bonus after spending $500 in the first 3 months, 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers (then 18.99%, 23.99%, or 28.99% variable APR), a $0 annual fee, and up to $600 cell phone protection subject to a $25 deductible. Approval is most likely for applicants with good credit (670+). The page also lists the Capital One Quicksilver card (unlimited 1.5% cash back, 5% on Capital One Travel bookings, $300 in welcome bonuses, 15-month 0% intro APR) and a Citi card (2% cash back, $200 bonus after $1,500 spend in 6 months, 18-month 0% intro APR on balance transfers). The site discloses receiving partner compensation, which does not influence its product ratings.

Digital leaders use transparent, data-driven objectives aligned with company strategy to unite teams around a shared "North Star" vision, developed through combined top-down and bottom-up processes rather than simply mandating OKRs. Even so, they can struggle when high data-analysis requirements slow simple decisions. Digital laggards, by contrast, set high-level goals with weak strategic connections, leading employees to deprioritize poorly understood objectives—a problem worsened by a "culture of genius." Data culture aligns organizations vertically (leadership to front-line workers) and horizontally (across teams). Digital leaders treat data culture as central, ensuring employee behaviors reflect stated values, while laggards show gaps between espoused values and actions, hindered by entrenched habits and skill gaps. Changing mindsets is transformation's hardest part, but laggards can still transform. Organizations typically fit one of four patterns: data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, or data reliant.

The President returns to the House of Representatives a bill appropriating $1,378,450 for more than forty harbor and river improvements, withholding his approval. He argues the Constitution grants the Federal Government no power to construct internal improvements or appropriate money for them, and that the claimed power is neither expressed nor a necessary incident to any granted power, citing Madison's rule of construction. While accepting long-established appropriations for lighthouses, beacons, buoys, and piers connected with foreign commerce and navigation, he objects that many items in the bill are local in character, lack foreign commerce, and were never ports of entry or delivery. He warns the bill would consolidate power in the Federal Government, foster sectional rivalry, produce wasteful expenditures, and unjustly burden states that oppose or doubt the power. He further objects to spending $1,000,000–$2,000,000 on non-urgent objects during a foreign war, which would risk increased debt or taxation, and expresses regret at withholding approval.

Coach DeBoer acknowledged his team made mistakes the opponent capitalized on but made no apologies for playing to win. He felt the team started tentatively, as expected in a Stanley Cup Final, but improved as the game went on, and noted they overcame similar deficits against Philadelphia and New York. He said the group self-analyzes well and will be better Saturday, admitting they did not deserve to win. He expressed excitement about the series and the community's enthusiasm. Drawing on the Lundqvist series, he stressed traffic, bodies, and shots without frustration. He does not expect the opponent's layoff to cause rust and plans no changes to routine, calling his team workmanlike. He noted the Kings' forwards' speed and size, and credited his organization's wealth of experience from top to bottom.

A hockey coach addresses a loss to Boston, crediting the opponent's strong play, goaltending, and defensive effort while expressing disappointment but refusing to blame injuries. He notes both teams competed hard, with each performing well at home, and acknowledges Boston was the better team in this game. Looking ahead to Game 7 of the Stanley Cup Finals, he says Jeff will get an opportunity to play, expects both teams to be nervous, and emphasizes focusing on the process. He describes Daniel as a leader who believes in the team. The coach reflects on his career, including six years away from NHL coaching and his fifth year in Vancouver, expressing excitement about the chance to play for the Cup.

This document is the statistical analysis plan (SAP) for Zealand Pharma protocol ZP4207-17086, a phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled, parallel-arm trial evaluating dasiglucagon 0.6 mg versus placebo and versus GlucaGen® for treating hypoglycemia in children with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM). The primary objective is to demonstrate dasiglucagon's superiority over placebo; secondary objectives include comparison with GlucaGen® and assessment of safety and pharmacokinetic (PK) profiles.

The trial will be conducted at approximately 5 centers in Europe and the USA, comprising a screening period (Day -30 to -3), a treatment period (Day 0 to 1), and a follow-up visit at Day 28. Sample size calculations, based on phase 2 results (median time to recovery of ~10 minutes for dasiglucagon versus >50 minutes for placebo), specify 20 patients for dasiglucagon, 10 for placebo, and 10 for GlucaGen®, providing 90% power at a 5% significance level using a 2-sided log-rank test.

The primary endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery (a ≥20 mg/dL increase from baseline within 45 minutes without rescue IV glucose), analyzed on the full analysis set (FAS) using a stratified log-rank test and Kaplan-Meier plots, with supportive Cox proportional hazards modeling and sensitivity analyses. Secondary endpoints include plasma glucose recovery within 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes (Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test) and plasma glucose changes from baseline at those time points (ANOVA). A hierarchical testing procedure controls multiplicity. Three analysis sets are defined: safety analysis set, FAS, and per-protocol set (PPS). No interim analyses are planned, and no imputation will be applied to missing data.

PK parameters will be derived by non-compartmental analysis using Phoenix WinNonlin Version 6.4 or higher; the pharmacodynamic endpoint is the plasma glucose area under the effect curve above baseline from 0 to 30 minutes. Safety analyses, based on the safety analysis set, cover treatment-emergent adverse events (coded with MedDRA), local tolerability, laboratory parameters, vital signs, ECG, and immunogenicity (anti-drug antibodies). All analyses will be performed using SAS Version 9.4 or higher; analyses conducted after unblinding will be labeled post hoc and exploratory. Appendices specify programming and presentation standards, SAS programming quality control requirements, and a list of planned tables, figures, and listings.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC dated May 1, 2018, reporting under Item 2.02 that it issued a press release and related data sheet regarding its financial results for the second fiscal quarter ended March 31, 2018. The press release and data sheet are attached as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2. The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The passage describes NVIDIA's GA10x Ampere architecture GPUs and associated technologies. Developed with Micron Technology, GDDR6X is the first consumer GPU memory to exceed 900 GB/sec bandwidth, using PAM4 four-level signaling to transfer two bits per clock edge—doubling the data rate of GDDR6's NRZ signaling. A new MTA encoding scheme addresses signal-to-noise challenges. Supporting data rates up to 19.5 Gbps, GDDR6X delivers up to 936 GB/sec on GA10x GPUs, over 52% more than the TU102 in the RTX 2080 Ti.

NVIDIA RTX IO enables GPU-based loading and lossless decompression of game assets, working with Microsoft's DirectStorage API to accelerate I/O up to 100x versus hard drives and offload work from potentially dozens of CPU cores.

The NVIDIA A40, based on GA10x, is described as the most powerful data center GPU for visual computing, delivering up to 2X FP32 and ray-tracing throughput versus the Quadro RTX 6000, up to 5X AI training throughput (10X with sparsity), 48GB memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink, and vGPU support.

Ampere GPUs support DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1, enabling 8K60 and 4K120 output with DSC 1.2a. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds industry-first hardware AV1 decode, and seventh-generation NVENC achieves encoding quality on par with x264 Medium.

The GeForce RTX 3090 (GA102, 24GB GDDR6X, 82 SMs) is 1.5x faster than TITAN RTX; the RTX 3070 (GA104) outperforms the RTX 2080 Ti. A new Error Detection and Replay (EDR) feature retries erroneous memory transmissions, causing performance to plateau so overclockers can identify memory limits without crashing. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU features 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 48GB GDDR6, expandable to 96GB via NVLink.

Queen Elizabeth, 91, reportedly plans to step aside at 95 and pass the throne to Prince Charles, according to a Royal Household source. Clarence House has not commented on 'Plan Regency', under which the Regency Act would grant Charles full power to reign while the Queen lives. Royal commentator Robert Jobson says transition preparations are moving ahead. Elizabeth became monarch in 1952 after George VI's death and is Britain's longest-reigning monarch. If she abdicates, Charles would be the oldest-ever UK monarch crowned; if he abdicates, Prince William would succeed, with Prince George third in line.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC dated April 12, 2021. Under Item 7.01, Microsoft announced it had entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Nuance Communications, Inc. for $56.00 per share in an all-cash transaction valued at $19.7 billion, inclusive of Nuance's net debt. The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1, and an investor presentation is attached as Exhibit 99.2. Representatives of Microsoft and Nuance will present information about the transaction to investors on and after April 12, 2021. The report was signed by Keith R. Dolliver, Assistant Secretary.

The Office of Management and Budget has identified between 4,132 and 4,232 federal workers for layoffs as the government shutdown continues, with OMB Director Russell Vought announcing "The RIFs have begun." The layoffs follow a pre-shutdown memo directing agencies to consider terminating employees in programs not consistent with the President's priorities. Affected departments include Commerce (315), Health and Human Services (1,100–1,200), Housing and Urban Development (442), Homeland Security (176), and Treasury (1,446). Labor unions have filed suit, calling the cuts unlawful, and requested a temporary restraining order. About 658,000 furloughed workers began receiving partial back pay on October 10, though a memo suggests back pay may require congressional authorization. Workers report financial stress and expect further cuts.

Punith Kumar, a 19-year-old from Choolai, secured first place in India and third internationally in the ACCA final P2 exam. He completed the course in two years and three months while interning at IRIS Techsolve, crediting his mentor and rigorous study schedule. He scored 83% in corporate reporting and plans to start his own company.

The passage cites numerous cases and describes the application of a damages rule—measuring loss of a detained vessel's use by its probable catch—before international tribunals. In the Hope On case, detained by Chile in 1883, an arbitration commission (one commissioner dissenting) awarded damages based on loss of probable catch. In the Col. Lloyd Aspinwall case, the umpire allowed damages for 114 days' interrupted trade. The Bering Sea Commission, which adjusted Canadian sealers' claims against the United States, adopted this rule as contended by the English Government; awards in cases including the Favorite, Alfred Adams, and Triumph included amounts for estimated catch earnings. The Triumph case, where the sole claim was loss of catch, demonstrated the rule, which the Commission applied universally. The passage concludes that a government agent may not rightfully board a friendly nation's ship on mere suspicion and forcibly enroll its citizens, citing Hall and Bluntchli that aliens may not be enrolled without their consent.

The passage examines why the SPY tends to rise after down days and fall after up days in the short term, attributing this to mean reversion—the tendency of asset prices to revert to their long-term average. While momentum works over longer timeframes, the SPY exhibits short-term mean-reverting behavior. The authors backtested a simple strategy of buying after a red day and selling after a green day using SPY data adjusted for dividends and splits. Results showed the red day strategy outperformed, with higher CAGR, better risk-adjusted returns, less time in the market, and less than half the maximum drawdown compared to a buy-and-hold approach. The conclusion is that the S&P 500 is highly mean-reverting in the short term, while trend following remains effective over longer timeframes.

Ofcom has proposed that landline and broadband providers pay automatic compensation—cash or bill credit—to customers when services aren't repaired promptly, new services aren't activated on the promised day, or engineers miss scheduled appointments. The scheme would apply to fixed broadband and landline services only, with payments set by Ofcom. An estimated 2.6 million additional customers could receive up to £185m in compensation annually. A consultation runs until 5 June, with a decision expected around the end of the year.

An email forwarded on January 23, 1999 by Enron's Mark Taylor to colleagues contains the Option Investor Newsletter dated Thursday, January 21, 1999. The market wrap reports the Dow fell 71.83 points to 9,264.08 and the Nasdaq dropped 70.77 points—its sixth-largest point loss ever—amid an Internet stock selloff, profit taking, Brazil currency worries, and a denied rumor of a Chinese devaluation. IBM, Lucent, and Sun Microsystems beat earnings estimates, but the stocks fell afterward, prompting a warning against holding positions through earnings; Sun announced a 2:1 split. The market posture turned Neutral on technology and Bearish on insurance and oil & gas. Pinnacle Capital Advisors' sentiment analysis flagged bearish short-term indicators, citing the Dow's 9,400 level and a VIX above 30% as key benchmarks. Call picks included Nokia, Dell, Cisco, AOL, MCIWorldCom, AT&T, Microsoft, Tellabs, Maytag, Sun, Lexmark, Xircom, Coast Savings (COF), and Ethan Allen, with several noted as split candidates. Put picks covered stocks such as Avnet, BankAmerica, Becton Dickinson, Eastman Kodak, and Merck. New call plays featured Vodafone (following its AirTouch/ATI merger) and Qwest Communications. New spread plays included Citrix Systems, Read-Rite, Level 3 Communications, and Sepracor. Dropped picks were Qualcomm, Disney, Yahoo, Check Point, Lucent, and ATI. Updates covered United Technologies, Clear Channel, Ford, FedEx (FTL), EMC, Micron, and Jabil. Subscription information ($39.95 monthly, $99.95 quarterly) was included.

The 2017 Sonora High School Athletic Hall of Fame class includes a dozen former Wildcats who graduated between 1950 and 2008, spanning nearly 70 years of Wildcat sports. Inductees are Howard "Socky" Keefe (1950), a multi-sport athlete drafted by the Baltimore Orioles; Dennis Jackson (1959), a football, wrestling and track standout; Don Moore (1961), who lettered in tennis, football and basketball; Cam Fray (1967), a football and baseball player who later coached at Sonora High; Jon Wagner (1978), a football player and wrestler invited to the 1978 USA Olympic Training Camp; Mark McCollough (1979), the state's leading rusher; Becky Fray Aguilar (1984) and Jodi Gardella Richey (1986), both three-sport athletes; coach honoree Lloyd Gaspar, a tennis coach and former Athletic Director; Jessica Peterson McCornack (2003), a three-sport athlete who earned a volleyball scholarship to Fresno State; coach Gary Smith, whose teams won multiple VOL and section titles in football and girls' basketball; and Lexi Kopf Scoles (2008), a soccer record-holder who received a Division 1 scholarship to UC Irvine. The banquet will be held at the Sonora Elks Lodge on Saturday, Nov. 4, costing $40 per person and $20 for children 12 and under.

A federal judge ruled that FACEA, the 1994 law barring harassment of women seeking abortions, also protects Falun Gong practitioners. U.S. District Judge Jack Weinstein rejected a constitutional challenge from the Chinese Anti-Cult World Alliance, accused by Zhang Jingrong and a dozen other practitioners of harassment. The alliance argued FACEA conflicted with the commerce clause, but Weinstein found religion is deeply rooted in interstate commerce. He also ruled that "a place of religious worship" must be construed broadly, noting Falun Gong operates from tables in Flushing, Queens. Weinstein certified the opinion for appeal ahead of the two-month trial, which will require interpreters and 500 jury decisions.

Banned Books Week (Oct. 5–11) occurs amid rising censorship threats; a PEN America report documented 22,810 instances of book banning in U.S. public schools from 2021 to 2025. Although higher education once largely ignored book banning, the passage states censorship now extends to colleges, including book removals at the U.S. Naval Academy, a West Point professor's resignation over removed authors, a professor's dismissal at Texas A&M, and state proposals requiring public syllabi. The Trump administration asked nine universities to sign a "Compact for Academic Excellence in Higher Education," which the author characterizes as a threat to academic freedom. The passage concludes that most Americans oppose book banning and calls for educators to form a united front against censorship.

The Carter administration used MONs to introduce higher-risk, higher-cost, or geographically specific operations under previously approved Perspectives objectives, requiring CIA–State Department coordination and broader interagency coordination through the SAWG or SCC. MONs later covered significant changes to any finding, while entirely new covert actions still required new presidential findings. Under the Hughes-Ryan amendment's "timely fashion" standard, the CIA typically notified Congress of new covert initiatives within 48 hours. The Intelligence Oversight Act of 1980 scaled back Hughes-Ryan by limiting required briefings to the two intelligence committees, clarifying that notification did not constitute a requirement for congressional approval, and allowing the President to restrict prior notice to the "Gang of Eight" during extraordinary circumstances, with timely follow-up notification and explanation required. The passage also documents January 1983 materials on US-Soviet relations, including Shultz's memorandum to Reagan presenting a four-part agenda—human rights, arms control, regional issues, and bilateral relations—along with related memoranda, including Dobriansky's critique of Shultz's paper and a record of Shultz's meeting with Dobrynin.

In *St. Louis & San Francisco Railroad Co. v. Conarty* (1913), the Arkansas court affirmed a $10,000 judgment for the widow of a switchman killed when an engine on whose footboard he was riding collided at night with a disabled coal car lacking a draw-bar and coupler. The court held: (1) the Employers' Liability Act's prohibition against removal to federal court on diversity grounds is valid; (2) under the 1910 amendment, only one action and one recovery is allowed, but it may include both pecuniary loss to the widow and next of kin and the deceased's pain and suffering, which survives to his personal representative; (3) the car, though taken to Fort Smith for heavy repairs, remained in use in interstate commerce under the Safety Appliance Act, imposing absolute liability for defective equipment; (4) the railroad was liable because the missing coupler was the proximate cause, even though the deceased was not attempting to couple the car; and (5) the widow's testimony about the deceased's contributions to her was admissible as collateral to the issue of liability.

The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe (RBZ) stated that the official US dollar to bond note exchange rate remains 1:1 and urged the public to use licensed financial agencies for currency transactions. Governor Dr John Mangudya said 45 financial institutions have been licensed, with exchanges involving other currencies subject to a fee spread of not more than 10 percent. Following a new law criminalising illegal forex trading, money changers have been arrested. The RBZ will also act against retailers refusing non-cash payments, after inflated cross rates caused panic buying and artificial shortages.

The dollar started the week at three-week highs after a Fed official reinforced commitment to rate hikes, with the dollar index up 0.1 percent at 101.260. New York Fed President Dudley said rate hikes might pause only briefly while the Fed shrinks its bond portfolio. The dollar rose 0.3 percent to 111.43 yen. Markets monitored geopolitical risks in Syria and North Korea. The euro fell 0.1 percent to $1.0580 amid French election uncertainty. U.S. March jobs data missed forecasts, but unemployment fell to 4.5 percent.

An optical interferometer encodes an external signal in the phase of an optical field, with estimation precision bounded by the quantum Cramer-Rao bound. For unentangled inputs, Heisenberg scaling is achievable with a pair of squeezed states. This work addresses whether such scaling holds for continuous-wave operation and time-dependent signals. Modeling squeezing over a finite bandwidth, the authors derive a spectral QCRB showing precision scales as 1/n for large photon flux n, improving with narrower bandwidth. The bound is attained by a nonlinear maximum-likelihood estimator acting on filtered homodyne detector records.

This study evaluates the prognostic value of PNI, NLR, and PLR in chronic hepatitis C-associated cirrhosis complicated by type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). HCV infection is a significant risk factor for T2DM, and CHC, cirrhosis, and decompensated cirrhosis progressively increase T2DM risk. Although PNI, NLR, and PLR have been verified as prognostic biomarkers in various cancers, their relationship with clinical prognosis in CHC-associated cirrhosis with T2DM remains unclear. The study included 56 CHC-associated cirrhosis patients with T2DM (group A), 85 CHC-associated cirrhosis patients (group B), and 85 T2DM patients (group C) from Fu yang Second People's Hospital between January 2018 and December 2021. Based on 6-month treatment prognosis, patients were divided into poor prognosis (23 cases) and good prognosis (33 cases) groups. Blood parameters were measured using automated analyzers, and NLR, PNI, and PLR were calculated from neutrophil, lymphocyte, platelet counts, and albumin.

The Rubber Band trading strategy is a contrarian, mean-reversion approach for trading stocks that identifies overbought or oversold points where price is likely to snap back toward the mean. It reflects Warren Buffett's principle of buying when others are fearful and selling when others are greedy. Traders commonly use Keltner Channels (typically 20 periods with a 10-period ATR), Bollinger Bands, or momentum oscillators. A buy setup occurs when price opens and closes below the lower Keltner Channel band, ideally confirmed by a bullish reversal candlestick such as a hammer or inside bar; a sell setup occurs above the upper band, confirmed by bearish patterns like a shooting star. Profit targets are the middle band or just before the opposite band. A backtested XLP strategy (published April 2013) produced 328 trades with a 0.45% average gain, 6.1% CAGR, profit factor of 2, and 16% max drawdown. The strategy works mainly on stocks; assets like gold and commodities are harder to trade with it.

UK university staff striking over pension scheme changes enter a fourth week, with talks failing and the UCU announcing 14 additional strike days likely during the April-June exam period. Separately, the University of Edinburgh has been criticised for asking law lecturers to provide recordings of past lectures to compensate for missed teaching.

This study developed a two-stage machine learning framework using ADNI data to predict the rate of cognitive decline in non-demented individuals by integrating plasma biomarkers (Aβ42/40, p-tau 181, NfL) with MRI data, demographics, APOE4, and baseline composite cognitive scores. Ridge linear regression was applied to MRI data to derive an MRI score, which was then combined with other predictors using random forest regression.
