The platform serves learners through a gamified dashboard, categorized challenges, a Simulation Lab, and a speech-based Viva Mode, while administrators can create or upload challenges, view performance analytics, and export data. The modular architecture combines a Question Generation Pipeline, adaptive delivery engine, React/Vite frontend, Node.js/Express backend, MySQL storage, Docker sandboxes, vector databases, and Whisper-based ASR.

Evaluation showed high annotation quality (97% Bloom taxonomy utilization, low concentration indices), weak correlations between Bloom levels and other dimensions, and question-answer semantic similarity clustering at 0.6–0.8. Fine-tuning Mistral-7B with 4-bit quantization and LoRA yielded stable convergence, a final perplexity of 2.04, and BERTScore F1 of 0.427 (precision 0.289, recall 0.818). Explainability analysis indicated the model attends to semantically relevant tokens, supporting interpretable, pedagogically aligned outputs.

This patent application describes Polkadot, a heterogeneous multi-chain framework designed to address the isolation of existing blockchain networks by enabling shared security, interoperability, and scalability among heterogeneous blockchains. The system comprises a central relay-chain hosting multiple parallelized chains (parachains), with a decentralized network of nodes assigned four basic roles: validators, nominators, collators, and fishermen. Validators, secured by staked bonds, validate candidate blocks produced by collators (parties who collate transactions into blocks for specific parachains) and reach consensus through a Byzantine fault-tolerant process with Nominated Proof-of-Stake selection. Nominators contribute stake to validators, while fishermen act as independent bounty hunters reporting misbehavior. Misbehaving participants face bond reduction or total confiscation. The framework decouples consensus from state-transition execution to overcome the scalability bottlenecks of conventional blockchains, where transaction execution is intrinsically tied to consensus. Interchain communication occurs through ingress/egress queues administered on the relay-chain, with transactions routed asynchronously between parachains. The document contrasts Polkadot with prior proposals including Factom, Tangle, side-chains, Cosmos, and Casper/Ethereum 2.0, noting Polkadot's distinguishing features of pooled security and trust-free interchain transactability. Interoperability with Ethereum is achieved through break-in and break-out contracts, while Bitcoin interoperability faces challenges due to its limited multi-signature support, with threshold signatures proposed as a possible solution. The relay-chain protocol includes a staking contract, parachain registry, mechanisms for sealing relay blocks, bond confiscation, and hyper-cube routing to scale beyond direct routing limits.

This randomized, controlled superiority trial tested whether radial extracorporeal shock wave therapy (rESWT) combined with a specific rehabilitation program (RP) is effective and safe for acute hamstring muscle complex (HMC) injury type 3b in athletes. Forty semi-professional athletes from a sports club in Buenos Aires, Argentina, were randomized between May 2018 and December 2020 to rESWT + RP or sham rESWT + RP. Four patients were retrospectively excluded because their lesions measured less than 5 mm (type 3a), yielding a modified intention-to-treat population of 36 (18 per group). The primary outcome was time to return to sport; secondary outcomes were patient satisfaction at six months and re-injury within six months. The rESWT + RP group returned to sport in a median of 25.5 days (mean 25.4 ± 3.5) versus 27.5 days (mean 28.3 ± 4.5) in the sham group, a statistically significant difference (p = 0.037). Patient satisfaction (9.0 vs 8.4) and re-injury rates (one re-injury per group) showed no significant differences. The authors conclude that adding rESWT to the rehabilitation program shortened return to sport without increased re-injury risk, and that the rehabilitation program alone produced shorter return times than programs reported in the literature. Limitations included the small sample size, use of ultrasonography rather than MRI, and retrospective exclusion of 10% of enrolled patients.

U.S. stocks sold off Tuesday after Caterpillar said it did not expect to exceed its first-quarter profit for the rest of 2018, raising fears that rising oil prices and other costs would slow company profit growth. The Dow Jones industrial average, which fell as much as 619 points during the day, closed down 424.56 points, or 1.7 percent, at 24,024.13. The S&P 500 lost 1.3 percent and the Nasdaq composite dropped 1.7 percent, while small-company stocks held up better. Industrial, technology, and basic materials companies took sharp losses; Caterpillar fell 6.2 percent and 3M, which cited rising material costs, dropped 6.8 percent. The 10-year Treasury yield reached 3 percent for the first time since January 2014. Alphabet, Facebook, Microsoft, and Amazon also declined. Analysts noted investors remain uncertain whether tax cuts will produce stronger economic growth.

In *Jane Richmond v. Walter M. Richmond*, the court granted the complainant a divorce from the defendant on the ground of adultery (October 13, 1837) and placed the couple's three children in her care. A master valued the defendant's estate at $19,060 and recommended annual allowances of $390 for the wife's alimony and $482 for the children's support. The defendant filed exceptions claiming the allowances were excessive. The Chancellor held that no fixed general rule governs alimony; each case depends on its own circumstances. Allowances should not be based solely on the estate's actual rents and profits, nor on the complainant's actual wants, and the defendant's property must be valued at the time of the master's report rather than when the bill was filed. Children must be maintained in a manner corresponding with the father's condition in life, with no pecuniary burden imposed on the mother. New evidence showing reduced property values and larger debts than the master had supposed justified reducing his figures. The court awarded the complainant $250 annually for her own maintenance and $130 annually per child, totaling $640 per year, payable half-yearly. The decree required the defendant to provide security for payment, constituted a lien on his New Jersey property, ordered him to pay the complainant's costs, and permitted either party to apply for modification of the allowances upon a change of circumstances.

Veterans warn that a concrete dome containing radioactive waste from 42 nuclear explosions at Enewetak Atoll is leaking into the Pacific Ocean. The US tested 30 megatons of weapons there in the 1950s, and more than 8,000 workers later moved 110,000 cubic yards of contaminated soil into a crater on Runit Island, which was sealed under a concrete dome. Veterans who took part in the cleanup say the dome was never fit for purpose, that porous and fractured coral allowed seawater to flow through with the tides, and that a typhoon could breach the structure. They report having received inadequate protection during the cleanup and attribute various illnesses to radiation exposure, with their survivor group losing six to eight members annually to cancer and related illnesses. Experts note the hazard depends on how much radiation escapes and is ingested, with the main health risk being an increased lifetime cancer risk that cannot be attributed to specific individuals.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on October 26, 2015 to recast previously reported financial information from its 2015 Form 10-K to reflect segment reporting changes resulting from an organizational realignment announced in June 2015. Beginning in fiscal year 2016, the company reports performance under new segments—Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing—using operating income as the measure of segment profitability. The recast covers consolidated financial statements for the three years ended June 30, 2015 and is presented in Exhibits 99.1, 99.2, and 99.3. The filing is informational only and does not amend or restate previously issued audited financial statements.

The lecture covers the theorem of irrelevance: when a signal occupies J degrees of freedom, noise and other signals outside those degrees of freedom are independent and can be ignored. For white Gaussian noise channels, all modulation systems are equivalent regarding noise analysis; differences arise only in secondary issues such as carrier recovery, synchronization, and filtering.

For a sequence of J independent inputs, maximum likelihood detection performed signal-by-signal yields the same decisions as joint detection over the whole sequence. When inputs are dependent, such as after error-correction encoding, joint detection using the full observation achieves lower error probability, which motivates the field's shift from algebraic to probabilistic decoding techniques.

The lecture then examines orthogonal, simplex, and biorthogonal codes. Removing the mean from an orthogonal code yields a simplex code with the same error probability but less energy (a factor of 1−1/m); adding negated codewords yields a biorthogonal code with the same energy but roughly double the error probability. For m greater than 2, exact error probability calculation becomes harder because decision regions are not orthogonal.

Analyzing error probability for large orthogonal signal sets by conditioning on W1 and applying bounds, the lecture shows error probability decreases exponentially with the number of bits b when Eb/N0 exceeds ln 2—the channel capacity for unlimited bandwidth—constituting the essence of Shannon's capacity theorem for this case.

Finally, the lecture introduces wireless communication: cellular networks as appendages of the wireline network (mobiles, base stations, and the MTSO switching office), forward/broadcast and reverse/multiaccess channels, the difference between delay-intolerant voice and delay-tolerant data, time-varying channels, and the need for physical electromagnetic modeling, including Doppler shift and carrier frequency effects.

Hundreds of nursery schools in England could be forced to close due to funding cuts, headteachers have warned. Since a new funding system was introduced in 2017, the Department for Education has provided £60m in supplementary funding until 2019-20, but there is no guarantee it will continue after 2020. Headteachers, including Shelagh Morpeth of Millfield Community Nursery in Sunderland, say budget cuts have forced staff reductions and increased costs. Only 400 council-funded nursery schools remain, providing around 30,000 places, mostly in deprived areas. Children and Families Minister Nadhim Zahawi said funding continues until 2020, while Conservative MPs urged certainty over future funding.

The article argues Exxon Mobil (XOM), trading near its summer 2015 lows, is a "screaming buy" for contrarian dividend investors, citing its 4.1% dividend yield (versus the 2.2% U.S. market average), 20% year-over-year cash flow growth, and half-decade lows on price-to-cash flow. The stock has traded between 56.50 and 103.80 since 2007, with both extremes occurring in summer months. The author contends macro fundamentals have mattered little, with WTI crude instead influenced by the U.S. dollar and stock benchmarks, but believes the bear market in crude that began in July 2014 has ended, with oil and gas prices stabilizing. XOM trades below 16x forward earnings, and the company's goal of doubling earnings by 2025 would require roughly 10% annual profit growth. Chart analysis identifies critical support near 71.60, and the author, who is long XOM, expects bull rallies in the first half of the year.

Stefon Diggs had 10 catches for 146 yards in the Patriots' Sunday Night Football win over his former team, the Bills. He matched Julian Edelman by recording consecutive 100-yard games in a season and posted 61 yards after catch, his most since 2022. Traded by Buffalo in 2024, Diggs joined New England via free agency.

TopoSPAM provides a unified simulation framework across biological scales, offering intracellular tools for polar fluids, gels, and nematic liquid crystals, and tissue-scale vertex and coarse-grained 3D models for morphogenesis.

This patent disclosure relates to a display apparatus including a flexible vibration module and a method of manufacturing the module. The flexible vibration module is disposed on a rear surface of a display panel and vibrates the panel to generate sound with good sound pressure characteristics and sound localization, addressing limitations of conventional speakers (space requirements, thickness) and fragile piezoelectric elements. The module includes a piezoelectric composite layer with alternating first portions (inorganic, piezoelectric material such as perovskite ceramic, e.g., PZT-based) and second portions (organic, flexible material such as polymer), plus first and second electrode layers and protection films. The organic portions absorb impacts on the fragile inorganic portions, enhancing durability while providing flexibility, enabling application to curved, rollable, bendable, and flexible display apparatuses. The module size may correspond to the display area to improve sound localization and low-pitched sound characteristics. Multiple embodiments describe different patterns for the portions (line/stripe, circular, triangular), with sizes adjustable based on desired piezoelectric characteristics, flexibility, or sound band performance. A bimorph embodiment uses two piezoelectric composite layers separated by an insulation layer to enhance sound pressure. Another embodiment provides first and second vibration modules on left and right regions of the display panel, separated by partition members forming air gaps, to output two-channel stereo sound. The manufacturing method includes forming the piezoelectric composite from inorganic and organic materials, applying electrode layers, polarizing the material under voltage and temperature, and forming protection films.

Oklahoma has received approval to become the first state allowed to seek rebates from drug-makers whose medicines don't work as claimed. Participation is voluntary; talks have begun with 20 companies, 10 engaged.

Kalidou Koulibaly's stoppage-time header gave Napoli a win at Juventus, cutting the Serie A gap to one point with four games left. Juventus, previously four points clear and chasing a seventh straight title, face a tougher run-in, including matches against Inter and Roma, while Napoli, seeking a first Scudetto since 1989-90, visit Fiorentina next. In the match, Giorgio Chiellini went off injured early, Miralem Pjanic hit the post, Lorenzo Insigne had a goal ruled offside, and Koulibaly headed the winner from Jose Callejon's corner.

Some Prince Edward Island parents are frustrated by the cost of school supply lists. Jerica Devos of Cornwall has spent about $70 on supplies for her six-year-old son, a Grade 1 student at Westwood Primary School, which requires specific brands and colours. She believes costs should be consistent across schools, noting some schools instead charge a flat fee of up to $40. The Public Schools Branch has provincial guidelines, but schools may adjust lists by removing items or adding amounts, colours, and brands—though they cannot add items. Parents at fee-based schools can opt out, but those at schools without fees cannot choose to pay a flat fee. Director Parker Grimmer welcomes feedback, and Devos plans to raise her concerns.

The passage explains the bullish engulfing pattern, a two-candlestick pattern that forms after a downward price swing, in which a small bearish candlestick is completely engulfed by a larger bullish candlestick, signaling a potential reversal to an upward swing. The pattern tends to form around support levels and is considered more reliable after a significant pullback, such as a 61.8% Fibonacci retracement, in an uptrend. Traders are advised to seek confirmation, such as a follow-through day or an additional bullish candlestick pattern, and to consider broader market conditions, support and resistance levels, and volume changes. The passage covers building a profitable trading plan, identifying entry and exit points (exits may occur at profit targets, stop losses, or the appearance of an opposite signal), applying risk management techniques, and using advanced trading techniques. It also discusses backtesting, which involves using historical price data to simulate trades and evaluate performance. Benefits of trading the pattern include a reversal signal, confirmation of trend change, high probability of success, identifying key levels, and effective risk management. Common mistakes should be avoided, and sticking to a solid trading plan can increase the chances of success with bullish engulfing trades.

Most Scottish councils are unprepared for a new law protecting disabled taxi passengers, with only eight of 32 expected to meet the government-recommended October deadline. An April change to the Equality Act means drivers face fines of up to £1,000 for refusing wheelchair users or charging them extra, but it applies only to drivers on councils' Section 167 lists of wheelchair accessible taxis. Perth and Kinross is the only Scottish council to have completed a list; 18 have no plans or are undecided. Doug Paulley's Freedom of Information research across England, Scotland and Wales found 11 per cent of councils have created lists and 59 per cent have no firm plans. He and Muscular Dystrophy UK are urging the government to ensure all councils set deadlines for creating lists.

On March 21, 2018, Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that its stockholders approved the CEO Performance Award, a performance-based stock option granted to CEO Elon Musk on January 21, 2018, at a special meeting of stockholders. Approval required meeting three standards: the NASDAQ Standard (approximately 81% of votes cast in favor), the Bylaws Standard (approximately 80% of votes present and entitled to vote in favor), and the Disinterested Standard, which excluded shares owned by Elon and Kimbal Musk (approximately 73% in favor). Vote counts were 96,795,092 for and 23,407,632 against under the NASDAQ and Bylaws Standards, and 63,014,339 for and 23,407,632 against under the Disinterested Standard. The award's material terms were previously summarized in Tesla's Proxy Statement filed February 8, 2018, incorporated as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by General Counsel Todd A. Maron.

Point-of-care lung ultrasound (LUS) offers portability, rapid results, low cost, and no radiation exposure, and has been proposed for evaluating COVID-19 pneumonia. The traditional LUS score requires summing all 12 lung zones, which can be difficult in unstable patients. This prospective study at Johns Hopkins Hospital enrolled 264 adults with SARS-CoV-2 infection between April 2020 and September 2021 to determine whether baseline LUS findings predict subsequent oxygen support needs or death, using a mean LUS score (mLUSS, range 0–3) that permits fewer than 12 zones. Standardized scans were performed by trained research personnel, with an inter-reader correlation of 0.77. Each point increase in mLUSS was associated with progression to ICU-level care (aHR 3.61) and 28-day mortality (aHR 3.10), though not the composite outcome of ventilation or death. Among individual findings, B lines were associated with 28-day mortality, A lines with decreased risk of progression and death, and pleural line abnormalities with mechanical ventilation plus death. Results were unchanged in sensitivity analyses adjusting for available lung zones, excluding asymptomatic patients, or accounting for symptom duration. The authors conclude that individual LUS findings and the mLUSS are associated with ultimate oxygen requirements or death among hospitalized COVID-19 patients, supporting LUS use for triage, including by non-clinician operators. Limitations include hospital-based enrollment, variable enrollment timing, and wide confidence intervals from limited sample sizes.

Subdivision surfaces, common in film rendering, are usually ray traced via tessellation, causing expensive per-frame BVH builds for animations. Mega Geometry enables mapping tessellation to clusters, allowing rapid BVH construction from CLASes and real-time performance.

An email dated December 14, 2000, from Todd Kimberlain (Enron) to V. Charles Weldon forwards a message from Jack Beven of the National Hurricane Center, who in turn passes along data from Jim Gross of the NHC. Gross reports finding a file of watch/warning areas covering 1963 to 1998, constructed by Mark Demaria and assumed complete for the continental US. The file's key defines the record format (month, day, year, hour, storm name, number of warnings, storm ID) and warning codes: 6 = hurricane warning, 5 = hurricane watch, 4 = storm warning, 3 = gale warning, 2 = tropical storm warning, 1 = tropical storm watch, with the from/to locations being arbitrary. The remainder of the passage consists of the data itself: chronological records listing dates, times, storm names (e.g., Cindy 1963, Betsy 1965, Camille 1969, Andrew 1992, Georges and Mitch 1998), warning counts, storm IDs, and the geographic areas covered by each watch or warning.

An international study led by Senckenberg and the University of Vienna, involving UCL researchers, found that alien species numbers have risen continuously worldwide over the past 200 years, with no sign of saturation. Using over 45,000 first records of more than 16,000 alien species, researchers found 37% of introductions occurred between 1970 and 2014, peaking in 1996 with 585 new species. Trends vary by taxonomic group due to human activities such as colonial expansion and trade globalisation. The increase threatens native ecosystems, and current prevention laws have proven insufficient.

This study reports the first instance where precision therapies (targeted and immunotherapy) have overtaken traditional cytotoxic treatments in routine community-based care of advanced cancer patients, resulting in improved overall survival. Researchers at Providence implemented a pathologist-directed comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) protocol using a single 523-gene DNA/RNA assay, initiated at time of diagnosis at no cost to patients, between September 2019 and November 2021. Among 3,216 tested patients, 49% had at least one guideline-based actionable biomarker, with TMB-High being the most common (22%), followed by BRAF (11%) and EGFR (4%). Compared to an in silico 50-gene panel, CGP identified significantly more actionable mutations (67% vs. 33%) and clinical trial matches (53% vs. 26%). Among 1,482 patients with documented follow-up, 54% of those with an appropriate immunotherapy biomarker received immunotherapy with or without chemotherapy, exceeding the 32% who received chemotherapy alone. Patients treated with targeted therapy showed significantly better overall survival compared to chemotherapy alone (median 25 vs. 17 months; HR 0.66, p<0.001), and NSCLC patients showed similar benefit (26 vs. 16 months; HR 0.55, p=0.032). The authors note remaining gaps including non-actionable genomic findings in a subset of tumors, acquired resistance, physician hesitancy, and access barriers, and anticipate that current CGP panels will be supplanted by more extensive sequencing approaches as costs decrease.

A researcher stated losing 5% of body weight requires 10% fewer calories to maintain, possibly explaining weight regain. This week's Disasters Averted covers keeping weight off. dMeetings educates diabetes patients at their own pace.

The Lenovo Legion Go S with SteamOS, $120 off, is a capable gaming handheld suited for travelers and couch gamers. The SteamOS version is preferred over the Windows model, with quick setup and smoother gameplay. The device is bulky but comfortable, with built-in grips, a bright 120-Hz IPS screen, 1 TB of storage, 32 GB of memory, and a MicroSD slot. It is more powerful than the older Steam Deck, though some games may need settings tweaks. The upcoming Legion 2 is larger, pricier, and runs Windows.

President George Washington declares that, despite initial efforts at conciliation—including offers of forgiveness conditioned only on submission to law—combinations against the Constitution and laws in certain western Pennsylvania counties persist, leaving government set at defiance. Invoking his constitutional duty to ensure faithful execution of the laws, he announces that militia from New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Maryland, and Virginia have responded patriotically, and an adequate force is moving toward the disaffected area. He promises protection to loyal citizens and liberal treatment to those who submit, exhorts all persons to oppose measures leading to such crimes and to uphold the Constitution and laws, and warns against aiding the insurgents, requiring that offenders be brought to justice.

Mercedes-Benz has launched a "Grand Edition" version of its GLS flagship SUV amid competition from Range Rover, Volvo, and BMW's upcoming X7. The limited edition features 20-inch alloy wheels, "Grand Edition" badges, nappa leather, exclusive wood trim, and porcelain and espresso brown quilted seats. Available as an €8,250 upgrade on non-AMG GLS variants, deliveries begin March 2018.

Czech central bank board member Toms Nidetzky said one more rate hike is likely this year after three increases since last August, though none is needed yet. The repo rate is 0.75 percent, with another increase forecast around end-2018 or early 2019.

FoLix is the first FDA-cleared fractional laser treatment for hair loss, offering a nonsurgical alternative to hair transplants. Administered in-office, it creates microscopic channels in the scalp to trigger a healing response, boost circulation, and stimulate existing follicles. Sessions last 20 to 30 minutes, require no anesthesia, and involve little to no downtime. Patients need three to six sessions in the first year, then maintenance up to twice yearly, at a cost of $750 to $1,250 per session. Dermatologists say it works best for early to moderate hair loss in people with intact but underperforming follicles, and may appeal to those avoiding daily medications like finasteride or minoxidil. Unlike PRP, it requires no blood draw. Side effects are mild and temporary, including redness, sensitivity, and shedding. Doctors recommend consulting a physician first, since hair loss can have various causes.

An infant sustained Erb's palsy during delivery; the jury found the hospital and a staff member negligent. The court upheld the reduced damages award as reasonable, finding the original future pain and suffering award excessive.

Protesters in several U.S. cities gathered Sunday to counter a deadly white supremacist rally in Virginia. Seattle police arrested three men; New York demonstrators demanded Trump denounce white nationalist groups.

Players expressed confidence in both goaltenders who have responded in tough situations. An opposing player was described as smart and intelligent. Despite good looks, they didn't score and emphasized persistence. The team ignores media coverage and remains confident against the favored opponent, needing better execution. Pulling the goaltender signaled a need to support a player who has battled for them. They felt they played within the rules but were tentative; most penalties were stick infractions.

This study examined the views of visually impaired students receiving professional music education in Turkey regarding the distance education process implemented during COVID-19. Using a qualitative case study design, semi-structured interviews were conducted by telephone with seven visually impaired undergraduate and graduate music students—representing 80% of such students in Turkey—recruited through a communication network of the Association for the Visually Impaired in Education, and data were analyzed via content analysis.

Findings showed that, except for one participant, courses were delivered synchronously. Participants used computers, cellphones, or tablets independently. Course materials were often inaccessible or insufficient, and all participants stated their special needs were not considered in the prepared materials. Some individual assessment arrangements existed, such as video exams or homework formats, but theoretical written exams posed difficulties. Perceived strengths included time and place flexibility and greater social acceptance, while weaknesses involved technical deficiencies (e.g., poor sound synchronization and quality in online platforms), teachers' technological incompetence, and low productivity. Students suggested longer lessons, software converting written text and notation into audio, accessible systems and interfaces, Braille notation archives, faster technical support, and more understanding teachers.

The study concludes that distance education was very difficult for visually impaired professional music education students, who often depended on others for access, and recommends assistive technologies—screen readers, speech recognition software, Braille printers, and audio materials—along with customized educational planning and cooperation with families and professionals to improve accessibility.

Round 2 of the Florida Winter Tour ROK Edition at Palm Beach drew 191 drivers, with Birel ART supported teams showing strong performance. Ryan Norberg won the ROK Senior final, regaining the championship lead despite a heat 2 DNF. Scott Davidson earned his first ROK Shifter Master win of the season, with Igor Pushkin finishing P5. Ryan MacDermid placed P10 in ROK Junior and Justin Aresneu P12 in Mini ROK. The team next competes in the Rotax edition starting February 16.

The United States sued Hale County, Alabama, under the Voting Rights Act of 1965 to challenge the county's change from district-based to at-large elections of County Commissioners without the preclearance required by Section 5. A three-judge federal district court found that Alabama was a covered state under Section 4(b) and that the 1965, 1971, and 1973 state enactments establishing at-large elections were never precleared and were therefore invalid and legally unenforceable. The court allowed the November 2, 1976 election to proceed but ordered the elected commissioners to serve only provisionally, directed defendants to submit the enactments to the Attorney General within fifteen days for expedited review, and required reversion to district elections under the 1959 act absent successful preclearance or a favorable D.C. district court judgment. In a supplemental opinion, the court rejected defendants' argument that Hale County was not individually designated, holding that designation of a state subjects all of its political subdivisions to the Act, relying on legislative history and precedent including Allen v. State Board of Elections, Perkins v. Mathews, and Beer v. United States.

The speaker acknowledges missed scoring chances, including an empty-net shot that went wide, and stresses staying positive and preparing for the third game. They note the opponent capitalizes on turnovers, emphasize avoiding lapses, and express confidence despite nobody expecting them to come this far.

The passage describes the NVIDIA Ampere GA10x GPU architecture and its key features:

- **2x FP32 Processing**: GA10x SMs support FP32 on both datapaths, doubling peak FP32 processing rate versus Turing. The GeForce RTX 3090 delivers over 35 FP32 TFLOPS.
- **Second-Generation RT Core**: Delivers up to 2x ray tracing performance over Turing, doubles ray/triangle intersection testing rate, adds hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur via a new Interpolate Triangle Position unit, and supports concurrent RT Core with graphics or compute workloads.
- **Third-Generation Tensor Cores**: Add TF32 and BF16 data types; a Sparsity feature (2:4 structured pattern) doubles throughput, with up to 5x TF32 training throughput over the previous generation.
- **GDDR6X Memory**: Uses PAM4 signaling, supporting up to 19.5 Gbps and up to 936 GB/sec bandwidth (over 52% more than TU102).
- **Third-Generation NVLink**: Provides 112.5 GB/sec total bandwidth between two GPUs, scaling memory from 48GB to 96GB.
- **PCIe Gen 4**: Doubles PCIe 3.0 bandwidth, up to 64 GB/sec peak.
- **GA102 Structure**: Seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, 84 SMs, and 112 ROPs (ROPs now located in the GPC); each SM has 128 CUDA Cores and 128 KB of L1/shared memory, 33% larger than Turing.
- **RTX IO**: GPU-based loading and decompression working with Microsoft's DirectStorage API, accelerating I/O up to 100x versus hard drives.
- **NVIDIA A40**: Data center GPU delivering up to 2x FP32, 2x ray tracing, and 5x (10x with Sparsity) AI training throughput versus Quadro RTX 6000.
- **Media features**: Fifth-generation NVDEC includes first AV1 hardware decode; seventh-generation NVENC handles encoding; support for HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a enabling 8K60 and 4K120.
- **Product specifics**: RTX 3090 (GA102, 82 SMs, 24GB GDDR6X), RTX 3070 (GA104, GDDR6, no NVLink), RTX A6000 (GA102, 10,752 CUDA Cores, 48GB GDDR6). Ampere GPUs are up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing.

Anna Gasser of Austria won gold in the Olympic debut of women's Big Air snowboarding at Pyeongchang, edging two-time gold medalist Jamie Anderson. Gasser's final jump, a double cork 1080, scored 96—the highest of the day—giving her a total of 185.00. Anderson led entering the final round but fell on her last jump. Zoi Sadowski Synnott took bronze, New Zealand's first Winter Olympic medal in 26 years. Finals were moved up a day due to wind concerns.

Russian journalist Arkady Babchenko appeared at a Kiev news conference a day after being reported killed. Ukraine's security services said the death was faked to foil a plot against him. Investigators said a Ukrainian citizen paid $40,000 by Russia's security service hired a gunman. Babchenko, a Kremlin critic who fled Russia in 2017 after death threats, apologized to friends and family unaware of the plan.

This patent application describes flex cable technology for connecting electrical circuitry in quantum computing systems. The flex cables contain multiple parallel signal lines (implemented as striplines, micro-strips, or coplanar waveguides) and connect to rigid boards at one or both ends, often with a fanout configuration for improved mechanical integrity. The technology addresses challenges posed by growing I/O counts in quantum computers, including thermal load in cryogenic systems, assembly time, and connector density limitations.

The flex cables may include metallic grounding planes, shielding vias, and can be constructed with various materials—superconducting metals (Nb, TiNb, Al) for low-loss applications or normal metals (stainless steel, cupronickel, brass) where electrical loss is tolerable. Composite materials with conducting particulates (e.g., copper particles) can provide high-frequency absorption in the 10 GHz to 1 THz range.

In cryogenic systems, flex cables route signals through isothermal plates of a dilution refrigerator to a quantum processing unit, carrying both excitation and readout signals. Cables can bypass intermediate isothermal plates without thermally shorting them. Electronic components such as filters, attenuators, and amplifiers can be integrated onto rigid boards or directly into flex cables. Connections between flex cables and rigid boards may use solder bumps (e.g., indium), while compliant joints with spring contacts enable non-permanent electrical connections to quantum processing units. Stiffeners can be laminated to flex cable ends for mechanical support, and signal conditioning modules can interface with flex cables via compliant joints or push-on connectors.

Former New York Judge Louis L. Nock joined Anderson Kill, citing family considerations and an approaching mandatory retirement at age 70. The same day, the New York State Commission on Judicial Conduct agreed to drop ethics charges in exchange for his resignation and agreement never to accept judicial office again. Complaints alleged he acted rudely toward court staff and threatened complaints against commission staff and witnesses unless charges were dismissed. Nock denied the allegations. Anderson Kill said he disclosed the allegations before being hired and no wrongdoing was found; his lawyer said Nock had already planned to leave the bench.

A Teagasc survey of 314 male farmers in south-east Ireland found 20% had never consulted a doctor, and Irish farmers show higher mortality from cardiovascular disease and cancers than other occupational groups. 57% visited a doctor in the past year, below the national average. 39% reported ill health, mainly back pain, arthritis, or anxiety. Farmers under 45 were more likely to smoke and drink weekly; those over 45 more often reported arthritis.

This analysis of the phase 3 LIVE-AIR trial (520 randomized hospitalized COVID-19 pneumonia participants) examined baseline CRP as a biomarker for guiding treatment with lenzilumab, a GM-CSF neutralizing monoclonal antibody. Lenzilumab improved survival without invasive mechanical ventilation (SWOV) versus placebo (HR 1.54; 95% CI 1.02–2.32; p=0.0403). In multivariate analysis, elevated baseline CRP was the strongest predictor of progression to IMV or death (OR 0.15; 95% CI 0.07–0.29; p<0.001). Participants with baseline CRP<150 mg/L (78% of those with evaluable CRP) showed the greatest lenzilumab benefit: SWOV HR 2.54 (95% CI 1.46–4.41; p=0.0009), reduced incidence of IMV/ECMO/death (OR 0.38), more ventilator-free days, shorter ICU stay, and faster recovery; no benefit was seen with CRP≥150 mg/L. Treatment effect showed a sigmoidal relationship with baseline CRP, declining above 150 mg/L. Participants progressing to IMV or death had sustained CRP>100 mg/L, and 72% of SWOV failures had CRP>150 mg/L at some point. Lenzilumab lowered CRP faster than placebo and was well tolerated, with no attributable serious adverse events. Findings support CRP-guided lenzilumab treatment, though most analyses were post hoc and not prospectively powered; further evaluation is planned in the ACTIV-5/BET-B trial.

An athlete calls the finals the biggest game possible, saying the team is calm but nervous and ready, and that an injured teammate's playing would mean a lot. Fans and the city have been supportive; Ryan Kesler, Alexandre Burrows, and Alexander Edler are named.

The White House confirmed plans to withdraw the nomination of Kathleen Hartnett White, a climate change skeptic with fossil fuel industry ties, to chair the Council on Environmental Quality. Nominated in October, her confirmation stalled in the Senate and was resubmitted in January. She faced criticism for statements dismissing mainstream climate science, downplaying particulate pollution, and praising fossil fuels. The Washington Post first reported the withdrawal, later confirmed by an anonymous White House official. Senator Tom Carper called the withdrawal the right thing to do.

The author expected institutional investing to be highly professional but found boards and investment committees imperfect, often lacking investment expertise. This prompted a five-year PhD research project at Marquette University examining asset owner governance. Since governance data was unavailable, the author and colleagues generated their own. Studying 35 public pension plans (about 14.5% of the industry by assets) from 2008-2012, they found wide performance variability: the best plan annualized at 15%, the worst at -4.2%, versus 1.4% for the S&P 500 and about 4.5% for a balanced index. Performance gaps proved to be behavioral gaps driven by governance. Key factors included institutional knowledge and turnover, professionalism (monthly meetings outperformed quarterly), board composition (retirees performed better), engagement, staff involvement, and diligence. Investment expenses and required contribution rates were not statistically significant. The central finding: governance influences investment performance. Plans in the top Fiduciary Effectiveness Quotient (FEQ) quintile outperformed the bottom fifth nearly 2 to 1, and each FEQ improvement unit yielded a 0.36% performance increase, a relationship that persisted under a one-year lag. Good governance drives results and can now be measured.

Ray tracing realistically simulates scene lighting; Turing GPUs render physically correct reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect lighting in real-time. Previously, single GPUs could not perform real-time ray tracing, so games relied on rasterization. Real-time ray tracing required nearly 10 years of NVIDIA collaboration and new hardware-based RT Cores.

This cross-sectional study assessed the levels and predictors of knowledge, attitude, and practice (KAP) of contraception among 217 female students (average age 22 years) at NTA TV College, Jos, Nigeria. Good knowledge, attitude, and practice were found in 55.3%, 47.5%, and 50.7% of participants respectively, while 73.7% had ever had sexual intercourse. Friends and the internet were the main sources of contraceptive information, and condoms and oral contraceptive pills were the most commonly used methods. Fear of side effects or health risks was the commonest reason for non-use. Multivariable logistic regression showed that being a young adult predicted good knowledge; being a diploma student, living off-campus, and having good knowledge predicted good attitude; and being from the state's indigenous population and ever engaging in sex predicted good contraceptive practice. The authors concluded that KAP levels were relatively low and highlighted an urgent need for improved advocacy, policies, and youth-friendly sexual and reproductive health services among young people in Nigeria.

Donna Adelson, 75, was sentenced Monday to life in prison plus 30 years for conspiracy and solicitation to commit murder in the 2014 killing of Florida State University law professor Dan Markel, her former son-in-law. She maintained her innocence, citing a lack of evidence, and Judge Stephen Everett warned he could consider her "utter lack of remorse." Adelson was convicted after three hours of jury deliberation and accused of plotting with her son Charlie Adelson, who used a woman he was dating as a go-between to hire two hit men; a second hit man pleaded guilty to second-degree murder. Prosecutors alleged the motive was the family's desire to move Wendi Adelson, Markel's ex-wife, to South Florida. Her husband, Harvey Adelson, also asserted her innocence.

Hui Ying Financial Holdings Corporation reported fiscal year 2017 results, with revenues increasing 88.4% to $46.50 million from $24.68 million in 2016, driven by increased loan volume and its newly launched entrusted loan business. Net income rose 343.9% to $15.27 million, with diluted EPS of $0.21 versus $0.05. Total loans facilitated through its platform grew 59.9% to $1,308.7 million, involving 8,047 borrowers, 69,232 investors, and 23,263 loans. Operating income increased 301.6% to $17.95 million, while operating expenses rose 41.2% to $28.55 million. Outstanding loan balances reached $436.3 million at year-end 2017, up from $246.1 million, and cash and cash equivalents were $12.68 million. The company, formerly known as Sino Fortune Holding Corporation, operates an online financial platform (www.hyjf.com) matching investors with under-served SME and individual borrowers in China, and set aside risk reserve funds to limit investor losses from defaults.

Model and author Chrissy Teigen, 32, who is due to give birth to her second child, a son, in June, has discussed her stretch marks and prevention routine. She says she has had stretch marks for years, particularly on her inner thighs, and has previously shared photos of them online. Believing prevention is key, she spends 10-15 minutes each night applying products to her belly, with help from husband John Legend and daughter Luna. Her routine includes Aquaphor on her elbows, coconut oil on her body, and Lumière de Vie concentrate on her belly, which she receives for free through her work with the brand. She notes her belly is her only stretch mark-free area and that every model she has worked with has stretch marks.

Research from the University of Essex and University College London, based on a survey of 9,859 UK adolescents aged 10 to 15, found girls who used social media for an hour or more by age 10 showed lower well-being by 15. Girls used social media more than boys, and while well-being declined for both genders during adolescence, the drop was larger for girls. Researchers advised monitoring early social media use, particularly among girls, and warned the link may be underestimated.

This email, sent by Ann Schmidt on January 26, 2001, compiles news articles mentioning Enron from various publications. The Times of India describes California's power crisis and rolling blackouts, drawing parallels to India's Maharashtra State Electricity Board dispute with Enron. A Pittsburgh Post-Gazette market report notes Enron stock rose $2.25 to $82 after the company indicated 2001 profits would likely surpass analyst predictions. A Boston Globe column criticizes Enron for profiting from California's energy shortfall and notes Enron executives were major contributors to President Bush's campaigns. The Business Standard reports that US Ambassador Richard Celeste offered to mediate between Enron and Maharashtra's chief minister, who has indicated the state cannot honor its contract. The San Francisco Chronicle covers a Democratic club meeting where a member criticized Bush's ties to Enron's Argentine pipeline deal. The Wall Street Journal reports on the resurgence of wind farms as a response to the energy crisis, noting Enron has deployed windmills in Southern California, West Texas, Minnesota, and Iowa. A World Watch brief states Maharashtra's electricity board was expected to miss a $34.3 million payment to Enron's Dabhol Power unit. Finally, the Houston Chronicle describes employee anger over Enron's new "rank and yank" performance-review system that ranks workers against each other in five categories.

A hockey coach discusses his team's adjustments after Chris Pronger's one-game suspension, saying the group must absorb the redistributed minutes, with Joe Dipenta entering the lineup and Jackman, Beauchemin, Niedermayer, O'Donnell, and Huskins taking on larger roles. Chris Kunitz is a game-time decision. The coach addresses discipline, distinguishing acceptable penalties that prevent scoring chances from undisciplined ones like careless stick use. Recalling the previous game, he says early emotions and penalties hurt the team, but penalty killing, goaltending, and individual efforts enabled a turnaround. He praises Huskins' puck retrieval and Teemu Selanne's leadership, skill plays, and career revitalization, including a setup for Dustin Penner's goal. He stresses never risking a player's health, matching the opponent's intensity and skill, and notes the next game will be the toughest to win, with preparation beginning immediately.

The President returns House bill No. 6242, a rivers and harbors appropriations bill, without signature. He acknowledges many appropriations serve the general welfare, including measures he had recommended for Potomac reclamation, harbor lines, and Mississippi River improvement, but objects that the bill funds purely local improvements that do not serve the common defense, general welfare, or interstate commerce, which he deems beyond Congress's constitutional powers. Such local appropriations, he notes, grow as states seek similar benefits, rising from $3,975,900 in 1870 to $18,743,875 in this act. He also believes the sum exceeds the country's needs for the fiscal year and cannot be spent economically, and warns that extravagant spending demoralizes officials. He suggests appropriating half the amount for expenditure as determined by the Secretary of War under the President's direction, noting Congress reconvenes in four months.

A free domestic violence support group for women survivors meets Tuesdays at noon. AARP Tax Aide offers free tax preparation and e-filing at Hood River and The Dalles sites, with Spanish-speaking assistance available. Registration is open for the Feb. 24 Chess for Success Tournament for K-12 students in Hood River, Wasco, Sherman and Gilliam counties. Hood River Valley High School's Girl Up is collecting cleaned used bras throughout February for local women and homeless shelters.

Pakistan Volleyball Federation Chairman Chaudhry Mohammad Yaqoob urged the federal government to build a well-facilitated sports complex in Abbottabad, where summer weather is moderate, so national camps could be held there from May to September. He noted Liaquat Gymnasium at the Pakistan Sports Complex Islamabad lacks air conditioning, weakening players in heat, and criticized the Rs1200 million spent on the distant, underused Narowal Sports Complex. He also suggested adding a hostel in Islamabad. For the Asian Games, he sought an early PSB camp, saying four months were needed; camps have not begun after PSB halted them over financial issues. Youth and junior camps have shifted to Peshawar, where Iranian coach Hamid Movahedi arrives Thursday to oversee all three camps.

The passage, from the TPS7H500x-SP datasheet, explains that slope compensation prevents subharmonic oscillation in peak current mode converters when duty cycle exceeds 50%. For these controllers, slope compensation is a voltage ramp subtracted from the divided error amplifier output, set via a resistor from the RSC pin to AVSS; the recommended value equals the inductor falling current slope (1 × m). Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation can be used with the transconductance error amplifier, with Type 2A adding a capacitor for high-frequency noise attenuation. Thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C (typical) and restarts below 160°C (typical). The devices use fixed-frequency, peak current mode control.

The application section describes the TPS7H500x-SP as radiation-hardness-assured PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting switching frequencies up to 2 MHz and topologies including buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge. A design example demonstrates a 500-kHz, 5-V synchronous push-pull converter using GaN FETs, detailing component selection for switching frequency, feedback divider, dead time, leading edge blank time, soft start, transformer, FETs, RCD clamp, output inductor and capacitance (including single-event transient mitigation), current sensing, hiccup, frequency compensation, and slope compensation.

Power supply recommendations specify a 4–14 V input with at least 0.1 µF ceramic bypass capacitance. Layout guidelines address noise reduction, ground separation, trace routing, and bypass capacitor placement. The document concludes with revision history, mechanical and packaging information, and TI legal disclaimers.

The former Johnson Publishing Company headquarters in Chicago, longtime home of Ebony and Jet magazines, has been granted landmark status and sold for $10 million to 3L Real Estate. The developer plans a $20 million conversion of the 46-year-old building into a luxury residential complex with 150 apartments, with rents ranging from $1,200 to $2,700. Construction is slated to begin in 2018, with features like the Ebony and Jet signs preserved.

The Federal Government has unveiled plans for developmental projects in the South-East, beginning with the foundation laying of the Assumpta Science Centre in Owerri, Imo State. Science and Technology Minister Ogbonnaya Onu said the centre, under a Memorandum of Understanding between the ministry and the Pontifical Council for Culture of the Vatican City, reflects the administration's commitment to using science, technology and innovation to diversify the economy. He thanked the Ofekata community for donating land and urged stakeholders to sustain the project. Governor Rochas Okorocha pledged support for its speedy completion.

CJ Affiliate (Commission Junction) is an online advertising company offering affiliate programs for retailers, operating since 1998 and consistently ranked among the top 10 affiliate networks. It acts as a middleman between advertisers and publishers, tracking sales or leads and paying commissions while handling payments and technical issues. Joining is free; applicants need a website or social media profile with relevant content and an audience from the US or Canada. After approval, users complete their network profile, add payment and tax information, and apply to advertiser programs to earn commissions by sharing affiliate links. CJ offers promotional tools like banners and product feeds, along with granular reporting tools. The platform is considered legitimate and user-friendly, though it has a learning curve and a strict approval process. CJ takes a 5-10% commission on sales and pays via direct deposit, check, or Payoneer, with a $50 minimum payout ($100 outside America). Alternatives are available for those seeking other options.

This is the first lecture of MIT 2.830J Control of Manufacturing Processes, team-taught by Duane Boning (lead lecturer this term) and David Hardt (nominally on sabbatical), with teaching assistant Hayden Taylor, and video-linked between Cambridge and Singapore. Boning covers logistics: lectures are videotaped, all materials are distributed through the Stellar website, and slides are posted a day before class. Prerequisites are experience with a manufacturing process (e.g., 2.810 or 6.152J) and basic probability and statistics. Two required textbooks are May and Spanos on semiconductor process control and Montgomery's Introduction to Statistical Quality Control. Grading comprises roughly eight weekly problem sets (40%), two quizzes (40%), and a three-student team project with a presentation and report; there is no final exam. Problem sets require individual write-ups that articulate reasoning, while the project is collaborative.

The course's central theme is quality and manufacturing variation. Early lectures cover process physics, including semiconductor fabrication and forging examples, followed by statistical modeling, design of experiments, process optimization, and feedback control. Example control problems include shrinking semiconductor feature sizes (90 and 65 nanometers), microfluidic channels for DNA diagnostic chips, assembly fit, and high-density electrical connectors. A generic process model describes a workpiece transformed by equipment and a process environment via operator settings, with sensors providing feedback. A simple variation equation shows output deviations arise from disturbances and control inputs, framing the course's three parts: statistical process control, process optimization, and active feedback control.

This passage is from the Texas Instruments TMS320DM814x/DM8127 DaVinci Digital Media Processor datasheet (2012–2014). It specifies terminal functions for analog TV video output pins (composite/S-Video luminance and chrominance amplifier outputs and feedback), including external resistor requirements for Normal and TVOUT Bypass modes, and supply voltage pins—several 1.8-V supplies must remain connected even when their peripherals (PCIe, CSI2, HDMI, USB, VDAC) are unused. Boot configuration is latched from BTMODE[15:0] pins at reset, determining GPMC bus width, boot mode order, Ethernet PHY mode, XIP muxing, and PCIe addressing; ROM-configured pin lists are provided for NAND, I2C, MMC/SD, SPI, EMAC, PCIe, and UART boot modes. Pin multiplexing is controlled by MUXMODE bits in PINCNTL1–270 registers. Guidance covers internal/external pullup/pulldown resistors, with typical 1-kΩ and 20-kΩ recommendations. The system interconnect comprises L3/L4 interconnects and a switched central resource. The document provides absolute maximum ratings, recommended operating conditions, and electrical characteristics. The PRCM module manages power, reset, and clocks: four core logic voltage domains, four memory voltage domains with LDOs, six power domains, SRAM shutdown, and SmartReflex-based DVFS (AVS not supported). Four supply-sequencing groups with defined power-up/down order are required. Reset types (POR, warm, emulation, watchdog, software, test, local) are described with priority ordering and reset isolation for PCIe and the EMAC Switch. Clocking derives from DEV/AUX inputs (crystal or 1.8-V LVCMOS), 12 top-level and 4 embedded PLLs with frequency limits, and SYSCLK/module clock maximums. Interrupts are handled by the ARM Cortex-A8 AINTC (up to 128 sources) and the C674x DSP controller. Peripheral sections cover DCAN, EDMA (64 channels), Advanced Event Triggering, Trace, JTAG (ID register value 0x0B8F 202F), and the 3-port gigabit EMAC switch supporting MII/GMII/RMII/RGMII with 3.3-V I/O.

The Eagles practiced Monday ahead of Thursday's preseason game against the Bills. Matthews was traded to Buffalo on Friday, with a third-round pick, for cornerback Ronald Darby, who took first-team snaps Sunday. Defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz said Darby isn't yet up to speed; questions remain about Alshon Jeffery's debut and how long Carson Wentz and starters will play.

This study translated and cross-culturally adapted the Waterloo Footedness Questionnaire-Revised (WFQ-R) into Arabic (WFQ-Ar) and evaluated its measurement properties. Footedness is a behavioral predictor of cerebral functional laterality and is clinically relevant, as leg preference influences postural control and relates to stroke impairment severity. Following Beaton's five-stage guidelines, the questionnaire underwent forward translation, synthesis, back translation, expert committee review, and pilot testing with 30 participants. Modifications included rewording one item and replacing abbreviations in the answer grid with full words. Subsequently, 290 Arabic-speaking adults from Saudi Arabia completed the WFQ-Ar twice, one week apart, along with a single foot-dominancy question. Face and content validity were supported by participant interviews, expert consensus, and absence of floor/ceiling effects. Exploratory factor analysis confirmed a single-factor structure explaining 55.79% of variance after extraction, with all items loading above 0.5. Internal consistency was excellent (Cronbach's α = 0.93), as was test-retest reliability (ICC = 0.94; SEM = 4.5 points). The WFQ-Ar correlated significantly with the dominancy question (r = 0.48, p < 0.001). The authors conclude that the WFQ-Ar is a valid and reliable measure of footedness for clinical and research use, while noting that further testing is needed in other Arabic-speaking countries and other populations.

CoreWeave shares rose as much as 8% Wednesday after the cloud provider announced new tools to help programmers develop AI agents. The new serverless reinforcement learning service automatically adjusts computing power, and tests showed developers can train models faster with 40% lower costs compared to running Nvidia H100 GPUs locally, with no impact on model quality. The launch comes five months after CoreWeave paid $1 billion to acquire Weights and Biases, complementing its existing business of renting Nvidia GPUs to clients such as OpenAI. Separately, some Core Scientific shareholders are recommending a vote down of CoreWeave's $9 billion acquisition offer, though CEO Mike Intrator said the bid will not be readdressed.

Seasonal trading exploits regular price patterns at specific times of the year, and commodities like silver are particularly seasonal. Since 2001, silver's price has typically risen rapidly early in the year, with January and July being the best months (positive 69.5% and 63.6% of the time) and June and September the worst (31.8% and 54.4%). This seasonality is attributed to industrial users placing annual orders at the start of the year. A backtested strategy holds silver only from December to February and July to August. Since 2001, it has outperformed buy and hold by roughly 4% annually, achieving a risk-adjusted return of 26.93% versus 7.33%, while reducing maximum drawdown from -71.65% to -23.34%. The article concludes that silver's seasonal pattern is solid, making such a strategy potentially sensible.

Lasting peace must rest on equality of rights among nations, regardless of size or power, rather than equality of territory or resources. It must also accept that governments derive their just powers from the consent of the governed, and that peoples cannot be transferred between sovereignties as property; the speaker cites a united, independent, and autonomous Poland as an example. Any peace rejecting this principle will inevitably be upset, since stability requires a sense of justice, freedom, and right. Great peoples should be assured direct access to the sea, whether through territorial cession or neutralized rights of way. Freedom of the seas is described as essential to peace, equality, and cooperation, possibly requiring reconsideration of established international practices. This connects to limiting naval armaments and, more broadly, armies and military programs, which must be addressed candidly and with accommodation, as peace requires concession and sacrifice and cannot coexist with preponderating armaments. The speaker, addressing these matters as head of a great government, believes he speaks for the American people, liberals everywhere, and the silent mass of mankind.

On March 30, 2001, Miyung Buster of Enron forwarded a compilation of news articles on California's energy crisis to numerous recipients. The articles report: Gov. Davis requested an additional $500 million for power purchases on behalf of Southern California Edison and PG&E, bringing state spending to $4.7 billion since January; both utilities began repaying the state under a PUC order, with Edison paying $43.5 million and PG&E $61.8–65.2 million; Republican lawmakers sued Davis seeking details of long-term power contracts; utilities revised projections so that more customers than initially estimated will face rate increases of up to 46%, giving California the highest electricity rates in the continental U.S.; President Bush declared energy a paramount concern, defended rolling back Clinton-era environmental measures, and rejected the Kyoto treaty; California fast-tracked power plant approvals by easing environmental reviews to add capacity before summer; the Legislature considered over 190 bills, including roughly $1 billion in conservation measures; radio ads backed Davis's handling of the crisis; a commentary criticized Davis for distancing himself from the PUC rate hike; the PUC ordered PG&E and Edison to share detailed blackout information with San Francisco and Huntington Beach; police reported difficulty enforcing the order requiring businesses to cut outdoor lighting; Canada offered to expand oil and gas exports to the U.S.; the PUC weighed reinstating fines for businesses failing to curtail power in the interruptible program; the state controller projected a $7.4 billion shortfall over 18 months; and EPRIsolutions offered consulting services on California power problems.

President Akufo-Addo is expected to deliver his State of the Nation Address in Parliament on Thursday, February 8, 2018. The House will adjourn early on Wednesday, February 7, for chamber preparations. Members were urged to arrive by 9:15am and not bring guests.

The passage is from the datasheet of the ADS868xW family (ADS8681W, ADS8685W, ADS8689W), 16-bit SAR ADC data acquisition devices with an integrated analog front-end and reference buffer.

The device uses an internal 4.096V reference by default or an external reference, selected via the INTREF_DIS bit of the RANGE_SEL_REG register. The internal reference is factory-trimmed, temperature-compensated from –40°C to +125°C, and can shift due to soldering-induced thermal stress; a minimum 4.7µF capacitor is required on REFIO. In external reference mode, an internal buffer drives the ADC reference, requiring 10µF and 1µF capacitors on REFCAP; buffer drift is typically 0.5ppm/°C (maximum 2ppm/°C).

The ADC supports single-ended and differential inputs in bipolar and unipolar ranges with straight-binary output, where LSB = FSR/2¹⁶. Alarm features include a user-programmable input alarm with hysteresis and a fixed-threshold AVDD alarm (4.7V/5.3V), with active and tripped flags accessible via the ALARM pin, ALARM_REG register, or appended to output data.

The multiSPI interface supports standard SPI protocols for read/write, single or dual SDO operation, source-synchronous (SRC) protocols, and daisy-chain topology for multiple devices (optimal frame: 32 × N SCLK cycles). The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states controlled by the RST and CONVST/CS pins. Nine configuration registers manage device ID, reset/power control, SPI modes, output data flags, ranges, and alarm thresholds.

An application example describes an eight-channel industrial analog input module combining the ADS8681W with the MUX36D08 multiplexer for PLC, DCS, and DAS systems, settling to 1% accuracy in under 5µs. Power recommendations cover supply decoupling and low-power NAP and power-down modes, followed by PCB layout guidance.

The disclosure relates to video encoding and decoding methods enabling a single bitstream to serve both standard dynamic range (SDR) and high dynamic range (HDR) systems, avoiding the need for separate bitstreams that increase storage, processing, or bandwidth demands. In one embodiment, an encoder receives an HDR master, a reference SDR master, and target SDR display properties, finds a color volume transform that converts HDR values into SDR values which, when processed by the target display's operations, substantially match the reference SDR values, and encodes the SDR values into a bitstream with metadata identifying the transform. SDR decoders display the decoded SDR values directly, while HDR decoders use the metadata to apply an inverse color volume transform and reconstruct HDR values. In an alternate embodiment, the encoder encodes HDR values into the bitstream and provides metadata enabling SDR decoders to convert decoded HDR values into SDR values. The transform and its inverse may be represented as parameters of a parametric tone mapping function, a scaling factor, a 3D lookup table, or three 1D lookup tables. The encoder may also perform color conversion, quantization, and chroma subsampling operations, and can select the transform by minimizing the distance between candidate display values and reference values.

India, after beating England in the Test series, will pick squads this week for three ODIs and three T20Is against England—their only limited-overs matches before the ICC Champions Trophy in June. With several players injured or rested ahead of Tests against Bangladesh and Australia, the T20I squad is expected to differ from the one that played 21 T20Is in 2016. Rohit Sharma is not fully fit, so KL Rahul may open alongside Shikhar Dhawan, with Mandeep Singh and Rishabh Pant competing for a third opening spot. Virat Kohli and MS Dhoni are certainties, while Manish Pandey, Karun Nair, Suresh Raina, and Deepak Hooda are likely candidates. Amit Mishra is the only front-line spinner available, and Jasprit Bumrah, Ashish Nehra, and Bhuvneshwar Kumar are set to complete the 15-man squad.

A federal judge, Susan Illston, issued a temporary restraining order halting the Trump administration's layoffs of federal workers during the government shutdown. A lawsuit filed by AFSCME and AFGE in a Northern California District Court alleges the administration unlawfully used the shutdown as the basis for staff cuts. An OMB filing indicated 4,132 to 4,232 workers were marked for layoffs across departments including Commerce, Education, Energy, HHS, HUD, Homeland Security, and Treasury; OMB head Russell Vought said layoffs will total about 10,000. Around 700 CDC employees received erroneous RIF notices that were rescinded. Hundreds of thousands of workers remain furloughed, and some organizations are offering bridge loans. The administration may appeal the ruling.

Ella Ravenscroft, a 20-year-old model from Salford, Manchester, who used sunbeds once or twice a week for two years, had four moles removed from her stomach after they changed in size, leaving scars. She now warns others about the dangers of sunbeds, shared before-and-after photos on Facebook, and says she will use fake tan instead. Studies show sunbed use increases melanoma risk by 16 to 20 percent; nearly 500 people in Greater Manchester are diagnosed with melanoma each year, and around a fifth die. Most moles are benign, but changes in colour, shape, size, or texture—such as darkening, ragged edges, bleeding, or inflammation—can be early signs of melanoma and should be checked by a doctor. Cancer awareness nurse Jessica Turner advises people to know their skin and report unusual changes promptly, as early treatment can make a significant difference.

Sprint and its Sprint Foundation will provide free devices and wireless service to 180,000 low-income high school students this school year as part of the 1Million Project, a five-year initiative aiming to connect 1 million students lacking home internet. Starting Aug. 15, students in over 1,300 schools across 32 states will receive a smartphone, tablet, or hotspot with 3GB of monthly LTE data for up to four years. Sprint is donating roughly $2.16 billion in services and support, with devices contributed by vendors including Alcatel, LG, Motorola, and ZTE.

Gulf stock markets mostly fell on Wednesday, led by Qatar's 2.3 percent drop as blue-chips including QNB and Qatar Islamic Bank declined on profit-taking after surging since MSCI announced weighting increases in mid-May. Dubai's index slipped 0.5 percent, falling below its level before the UAE's long-term visas announcement, though DXB Entertainments rose 4.1 percent. Abu Dhabi fell 0.4 percent. Saudi Arabia's index edged up 0.1 percent as Al Tayyar rose after early repayment of a 307 million riyal loan. Egypt's index dropped 1.4 percent.

Hexane is a hydrocarbon solvent derived from crude oil, present in plants such as guava and orange, and a significant constituent of gasoline. Two types exist: pure hexane, used only in laboratories, and solvent-based hexane, used to extract vegetable oils from crops such as soybeans, cottonseed, and rapeseed, and as a cleaning agent in textile, printing, furniture, and leather industries. Excess inhalation can cause weakness, numbness, blurred vision, headache, and fatigue; OSHA has set a permissible exposure limit of 500 ppm. Hexane's ability to remove unwanted taste and odor is expected to drive demand in the edible oil industry. Asia Pacific, led by China, dominates global production and consumption, with European and North American manufacturers shifting facilities there.

On Friday, Oct 13, Josie Goodenow, Bee Chairman for California Garden Clubs Inc., will present "All About Bees" to the Laguna Beach Garden Club. Her program covers differences between native bees, specifically the Blue Orchard Mason Bee, and European honeybees, and how to increase bee populations and improve yard health. The public is welcome; first visits are free.

Nicole Sciortino and Vincent Licciardello, both 30, were charged with endangering the welfare of their two children, ages 10 and 11, after leaving them home alone for three days while the mother vacationed in Florida. Police responding to a March 7 report found the children alone in a Dunmore, Pennsylvania home in deplorable condition with the thermostat at 58 degrees. Licciardello had dropped the children off on March 5 and occasionally stopped by with food. One child missed 16 days of school this year, the other 26. Both parents received $10,000 unsecured bail, and the children are staying with family friends.

This study evaluated cerebrospinal fluid tumor-derived DNA (CSF-tDNA) analysis using CAPP-Seq for diagnosing and monitoring leptomeningeal disease (LMD) in advanced lung cancer. Researchers analyzed 81 CSF, blood, and tissue samples from 24 patients with suspected LMD, including a subset of 12 patients from a prospective osimertinib trial. CSF-tDNA variant allele fractions (VAFs) were significantly higher than plasma ctDNA VAFs (median 32.7% vs. 1.8%). For LMD diagnosis, CSF-tDNA showed 91.7% sensitivity, exceeding cytology (81.8%) and MRI (80.0%). CSF-tDNA detection was strongly associated with poor overall survival (HR = 7.1). Resistance mutations to EGFR-targeted therapy, such as EGFR T790M and MET amplification, were common in plasma but rare in time-matched CSF, indicating spatial heterogeneity in resistance mechanisms between CNS and peripheral compartments. In the osimertinib cohort, patients with CNS progression had increased CSF-tDNA VAFs during treatment, and post-treatment CSF-tDNA VAF was strongly prognostic for CNS progression (HR = 6.2). The authors conclude that CSF-tDNA detection is feasible and may improve LMD diagnosis sensitivity, prognostication, and therapeutic strategies accounting for compartment-specific resistance.

Hospital admissions for eating disorders in the Devon, Cornwall and Isles of Scilly NHS area reached 719 in 2016-17, including two children under 10, according to NHS Digital figures described as worrying by charities. Anorexia accounted for 45 per cent of cases and bulimia 24 per cent, with women and girls making up 94 per cent. Admissions are at a record high, more than double the 298 in 2010-11, though experts caution this may reflect greater awareness or bed availability rather than rising prevalence.

Poor medication adherence is common among hemodialysis patients, who often take 10–20 tablets daily, with non-adherence rates exceeding 50% and reaching 98.6% in some estimates. Non-adherence is linked to inadequate management of CKD complications and increased mortality. Person-centered care (PCC)—integrating evidence-based approaches with individual patient preferences and shared decision-making—has been advocated to improve adherence, but empirical evidence remains limited. Trust in physicians is theorized to mediate the relationship between PCC and medication adherence. This multicenter cross-sectional study, conducted at six Japanese outpatient hemodialysis facilities from April 2022 to February 2023, aimed to (1) explore interrelationships among PCC, trust in physicians, and medication adherence, and (2) examine trust's mediating role via mediation analysis. Adults on hemodialysis with regular prescriptions were included; adherence was assessed using the Japanese ASK-12 scale.

Archive360 announced on April 18, 2017, that it was named a finalist in two categories of the 2017 DBTA Readers' Choice Awards. Its Archive2Azure managed compliance storage solution for Microsoft Azure is a finalist for Best Cloud Storage Solution, and FastCollect for PSTs, an automated PST discovery, migration and storage solution, is a finalist for Best Data Storage Solution. Victor Tony Jones, sentenced to death in 1993 for killing Matilda and Jacob Nestor, is scheduled for execution Tuesday and has asked the Supreme Court to block it. The court has not granted any stay this year despite receiving more than 30 emergency applications; if the pattern continues, Jones will be the 34th person executed this year. This passage is a compilation of news articles about Enron from July 2001. Key items include: Enron ranked No. 16 on the Fortune Global 500 list; Enron's 196% revenue gain masked otherwise flat sales in BusinessWeek's second-quarter profit survey; falling western U.S. electricity prices, attributed by some to federal price caps, led Enron's Portland General Electric unit to halt a 45-megawatt turbine project; Enron canceled plans for a Miami-Dade County power plant in favor of a Deerfield Beach site, though that project was stalled by a Broward County construction moratorium; Enron was cited as a potential entrant into Japan's newly deregulated wholesale power market; White House adviser Karl Rove, who held Enron stock, met with Enron CEO Kenneth Lay before divesting his holdings in June; Enron executives Lay and Jeff Skilling sold large amounts of stock while publicly calling shares undervalued; and Enron's broadband business recorded a $109 million loss, with the company scaling back the venture after earlier promoting it as worth billions.

Coach Sutter described a player as coming from a winning background with back-to-back Pittsburgh finals appearances, calling him an old-school professional who comes to work every day.
