Tesla unveiled its $35,000 Model 3 in March 2016, securing 115,000 pre-orders that grew to 500,000 by 2018. By mid-2018, however, the company was in "production hell," with CEO Elon Musk working up to 120 hours a week, a second-quarter net loss of $743 million, and a need to produce 5,000 units weekly to reach profitability. Musk admitted that excessive automation at the Fremont factory was a mistake. Investors were divided on whether Tesla would disrupt the auto industry or face bankruptcy.

The U.S. new car market was worth about $270 billion in 2016, with sales expected to remain flat until 2021. GM, Ford, and Chrysler held nearly 46% market share; Tesla held 0.2%. Automakers earned low returns, faced high exit barriers, and customers showed little brand loyalty. Entry barriers were high, with a new car requiring up to $6 billion and six years to develop. The fragmented $2.2 trillion global supply business was more profitable than automakers, and Tier 1 suppliers were investing in EV technologies since electric vehicles require roughly one-third the parts of combustion cars.

Consumers were shifting behavior: Millennials bought pragmatically, 75% of buyers would consider purchasing online, and dealerships were losing appeal.

The industry was being reshaped by electrification (EV sales rose 25% in 2017; battery prices fell 80% between 2010 and 2017; GM, Ford, Toyota, and BMW expanded EV plans), autonomous driving (Tesla, Uber, Waymo, Apple, and GM testing vehicles despite crashes), connectivity (connected car revenue projected to grow from $53 billion in 2017 to $156 billion by 2022), and mobility-as-a-service alternatives such as ride-hailing and scooter startups Bird and Lime, with one study predicting an 80% drop in U.S. private car ownership by 2030.

Founded in 2003, Tesla went public in 2010 and by August 2018 had a market capitalization exceeding GM's despite only two profitable quarters. Following Musk's Master Plan to enter at the high end and move down market, Tesla launched the Roadster, Model S, and Model X before attempting mass production with the Model 3. Tesla made up to 80% of Model 3 components in-house, produced batteries at its $5 billion Nevada Gigafactory with Panasonic, and skipped beta production, contributing to quality problems and an estimated 40% of parts requiring rework. Tesla sold directly through company-owned stores, operated over 1,300 charging stations with nearly 11,000 Superchargers, and delivered over-the-air software updates. Musk's Master Plan, Part Deux envisioned a Level 5 self-driving vehicle and a shared autonomy ride-sharing platform, possibly by end of 2019. While many credited Tesla with spurring industry innovation, its long-term survival remained uncertain.
I am unable to summarize this passage.

DLSS 4 introduces a transformer-based neural network architecture, replacing the CNN-based approach used since DLSS 2, for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA. Transformers use self-attention to identify longer-range patterns across larger pixel windows, scale more effectively with 2x more parameters, and deliver improved temporal stability, less ghosting, enhanced lighting detail, and better anti-aliasing.

NVIDIA's Blackwell architecture introduces neural shaders, the next step in shader evolution from fixed-function pipelines through vertex, pixel, geometry, compute, mesh shaders, and RTX ray tracing. The new Cooperative Vectors API, developed with Microsoft for DX12 and Vulkan, allows Tensor Cores to be accessed through any shader type, enabling neural texture compression (up to 7:1 VRAM compression), RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces.

Key neural technologies include: RTX Neural Materials, which uses neural approximations to render film-quality assets at game-ready frame rates; Neural Texture Compression, which reduced a demo's memory use from 1110 MB to 333 MB; Neural Radiance Cache, which infers multi-bounce lighting from path-traced rays after one bounce; RTX Skin, the first ray-traced subsurface scattering in games; and RTX Neural Faces, which uses a real-time generative AI model to infer natural-looking faces from rasterized input and 3D pose data.

The Blackwell GPU family includes GB202 (92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA cores; RTX 5090), GB203 (45.6 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA cores; RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti), and GB205 (31 billion transistors, 6,400 CUDA cores; RTX 5070).

The North Carolina Court of Appeals affirmed the trial court's dismissal with prejudice of Lewis Williamson's appeal challenging the Town of Surf City's closure of a 20-foot portion of North Shore Drive under N.C.G.S. § 160A-299. The Town, which owned adjacent property and had received a state grant and CAMA permit to construct beach-access facilities requiring use of the street right-of-way, complied with the statute's procedures: a resolution of intent, notice by registered mail, posted notices, four consecutive weeks of publication, a public hearing, and a majority-vote street closing order. Williamson conceded procedural compliance and proper vesting but argued the Town's intent to build public facilities on the vested portion was an improper purpose, citing Wooten v. Town of Topsail Beach, and that the statute permits closing only an entire street. The court held Wooten was inapplicable because the Town obtained a vested interest through the closing, found nothing in the statute limiting a town's authority based on its intent, and, citing Wofford v. Highway Commission, concluded a town may close all or part of a street.

This patent application, a continuation of PCT/CN2019/130905 claiming priority to a Chinese application, relates to a rotating shaft mechanism and a mobile terminal for foldable devices. It addresses the problem that bent parts of prior-art hinges are thicker than the structural design, degrading the folded terminal's effect. The rotating shaft mechanism comprises a main shaft assembly, swing arm assemblies, and a support assembly. Each connecting rod group includes two connecting rods rotatably connected to the main shaft assembly on two sides, while each swing arm group includes swing arms fixedly connected to the two housings and rotatably connected to the main shaft assembly around axes different from, but parallel to, those of the connecting rods. Swing arms are slidably connected to connecting rods via sliding slots and protrusions, and connect to the main shaft assembly through first arc-shaped sliding slots and arms, which may be staggered for stability. Support plates are either rotatably connected to swing arms and slidably connected to connecting rods, or rotatably connected to the main shaft assembly and slidably connected to swing arms. When folded, the swing arms and connecting rods drive the support plates to rotate, enclosing space that accommodates the flexible display, while the folded mechanism's thickness is approximately equal to two stacked housings. Engaging gears on the connecting rods ensure synchronized folding, and a cam-based limiting mechanism with an elastic part, such as a compression spring, maintains folded or unfolded states. A flexible blocking layer, such as an elastic steel or plastic plate, covers notches on the main shaft to improve appearance. The mobile terminal includes the mechanism, two housings, and a flexible display attached by adhesive, with non-adhesive areas forming droplet-shaped or semi-arc bends when folded.

This passage introduces a study on forecasting COVID-19 confirmed and death cases for the five most intensely affected countries: USA, India, Brazil, Russia, and UK. The outbreak began in Wuhan, China in December 2019, and WHO declared COVID-19 a global pandemic on March 11, 2020. As of November 28, 2020, more than 6,171,5119 confirmed infections and 1,44,4235 confirmed deaths were reported worldwide. Since COVID-19 datasets exhibit both linear and nonlinear patterns, single models such as ARIMA, ARNN, or SVM are insufficient for accurate prediction. The study therefore proposes hybrid models—ARNNS (ARNN-SVM) and SVMAR (SVM-ARNN)—which showed excellent performance for short-term and long-term out-of-sample forecasting of both confirmed and death cases, offering easy interpretability, dynamic and robust predictability, and adaptability to seasonality. Data were collected from the Global Change Data Lab, with a terminal date of January 15, 2021. The study aims to provide health workers, policymakers, economists, and researchers with realistic estimates for pandemic policy-making.

The railway line from Lincoln to Grimsby, used by fans travelling to Blundell Park, was opened in 1848 by the Manchester, Sheffield and Lincolnshire Railway to transport goods to and from the port of Grimsby and distribute fish inland. The route included a bridge over the River Witham at Stamp End, which Network Rail has just replaced in a £7m project. Designed by MS&LR chief engineer John Fowler, the bridge used box-shaped iron girders, then state-of-the-art technology, and is described in a report for Network Rail as possibly the oldest surviving wrought iron box girder railway bridge in Britain, maybe the world, and certainly the oldest in Britain still carrying trains. After the 1847 Dee Bridge collapse, which killed five people, Fowler adopted William Fairbairn's tubular girder design. The bridge carried a double track on three spans, including a 74ft central span and timber side spans. It was reinforced in 1903 and 1948 due to heavier trains; the timber spans were replaced with steel plate girders around 1901–3, sleepers caught fire in 1937, and a new steel deck was added to the central span in 1968.

This multicenter cross-sectional study assessed SARS-CoV-2 humoral immunity in 1,411 patients treated at emergency departments of five university hospitals in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, between August and September 2022. Researchers measured Spike (S)-IgG and Nucleocapsid (NC)-IgG levels and serum neutralization against Wu01, BA.4/5, and BQ.1.1 variants, combining these with medical history and immune status data.

S-IgG was detected in 95.6% of participants. S-IgG levels were lower in participants with drug immunosuppression and increased with the number of S-antigen contacts from vaccination or infection. NC-IgG was detected in 24.0% of participants. Multivariable analysis identified NC-IgG detection as the strongest predictor of S-IgG levels, followed by number of vaccinations, time since infection, time since last vaccination, drug immunosuppression, and number of infections.

Neutralizing activity was detectable against Wu01 in 94.4% and BA.4/5 in 84.9% of participants, with a 5.92-fold reduction against BA.4/5. S-IgG levels were the strongest predictor of neutralization against both variants. In a representative subsample of 423 participants, only 73.8% showed neutralizing activity against BQ.1.1, with geometric mean ID50s of 1,302 (Wu01), 231 (BA.4/5), and 55 (BQ.1.1), representing 23.6-fold and 4.2-fold reductions compared to Wu01 and BA.4/5, respectively. Among participants with S-IgG below 1,000 BAU/ml, 59.6% showed no detectable neutralization against BQ.1.1.

The authors conclude that despite high S-IgG seroprevalence, serum neutralization against BQ.1.1 was substantially impaired, and improved vaccine uptake is critical for reducing COVID-19 risk in upcoming BQ.1.1 infection waves.

The passage defines intraday trading as buying and selling financial instruments—stocks, futures, or forex—within the same trading day, either through scalping (profiting from small price fluctuations) or day trading (capturing major moves while closing positions before the market closes). In the US, FINRA's pattern day trader rules apply to those executing four or more day trades within five business days, requiring $25,000 minimum margin account equity and limiting leverage to four times. The authors list rules for success: learning the market, setting realistic goals, avoiding herd mentality, choosing a reputable regulated broker, trading liquid stocks, studying company fundamentals, using quantified systems, and periodically reviewing results. Common indicators include moving averages, MACD, Bollinger Bands, and RSI, though the authors consider them unlikely to work intraday. An example strategy based on consecutive lower lows and lower highs, backtested on WTI crude oil futures, performed poorly historically but improved after July 2021. The passage concludes that most intraday traders lose money, since intraday trading is a zero-sum game, and recommends backtesting any strategy.

Scientists have developed parachutes inspired by kirigami, the Japanese art of paper cutting. Thin Mylar disks perforated with concentric slits unfurl into a latticework vase shape as cargo falls, producing drag that slows descent. Unlike traditional parachutes, they fall straight down regardless of orientation and landed closer to intended targets in laboratory tests. They are also simpler to construct and deploy, though they produce less drag. In a test, a 1-kilogram bottle dropped from a 60-meter-high drone fell at about 14 meters per second. Potential uses include humanitarian aid drops and drone package deliveries; researchers are also exploring biodegradable materials and designs for space missions.

The Buck Sweep, credited to Tubby Raymond and the University of Delaware, is the signature play of the Wing-T offense. It is a misdirection off-tackle run with two pullers as lead blockers, designed to exploit indecision, get blockers in space, and hit a vertical crease rather than simply run to the perimeter. Its strengths include confusing defenses about ball location through the Buck Series' layered fakes and using angles that allow undersized linemen to displace defenders horizontally. Its weaknesses are dependence on timing, spacing, and pulling blockers, plus the practice time needed to master its intricate footwork. The passage details blocking assignments against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts. Variations include the Shotgun Wing-T version, popularized by Gus Malzahn at Auburn with Cam Newton, which allows a QB keeper read, and the I-Wing version, which adds a counter step by the Tailback but keeps the same blocking scheme.

Speculation that Google's Inbox email app is being phased out has grown due to an upcoming Gmail redesign adopting Inbox features, slowed Inbox development, and Google's recent move of Allo to "life support." This passage covers container design patterns for distributed systems. It begins with documentation practices for containers, recommending Dockerfile directives such as EXPOSE (with comments explaining ports), ENV (for parameter defaults and documentation), and LABEL (for metadata following the Label Schema project's shared taxonomy).

It then reviews the sidecar pattern, where a container augments an application container, and introduces the ambassador pattern, in which an ambassador container brokers communication between an application container and the outside world. Ambassador use cases include client-side sharding (demonstrated with twemproxy proxying to sharded Redis and memcached deployed via Kubernetes StatefulSets), service brokering for portable service discovery, and request splitting for experimentation (demonstrated with nginx using IP hashing to send 10% of traffic to an experiment).

The adapter pattern is described next: an adapter container transforms a heterogeneous application's interface—for monitoring, logging, or health checks—into a consistent, standardized interface. Examples include a Prometheus exporter for Redis, fluentd adapters for normalizing logs from Redis and Storm, and a Go-based health-check adapter for MySQL. The text argues that adapters enable reuse and sharing rather than modifying third-party images.

The passage then shifts to multi-node patterns, introducing microservices—systems of small, independently scalable services communicating over formal APIs—which improve team agility and scaling but complicate debugging and design.

The replicated load-balanced service pattern is presented for stateless services, requiring at least two replicas for high availability, a load balancer, and readiness probes, with a Kubernetes dictionary-server example. Session tracking (via IP hashing or cookies) keeps a user's requests on the same replica. Additional tiers include a Varnish caching layer (which can also provide rate limiting and denial-of-service defense) and an nginx layer for SSL termination.

Sharded services are covered next: each shard serves a subset of requests, enabling scaling for large state, as illustrated with sharded caching. Sharding functions map requests to shards using hashing and the modulo operator; choosing the right key (e.g., request path, or country plus path) is critical. Consistent hashing minimizes key remapping when the number of shards changes. Replicating each shard adds resilience and enables hot-shard scaling.

The scatter/gather pattern farms requests to all leaf nodes in parallel and merges partial results at the root, useful for parallelizable work such as document search. However, per-node overhead and the straggler problem limit gains from parallelism and affect latency and availability; replicating each shard addresses reliability and scale.

Finally, the passage introduces function-as-a-service (FaaS)/event-driven computing, noting benefits such as simplified deployment, automatic scaling and recovery, and modularity, alongside challenges from forced decoupling, statelessness, and network-only communication.

Freelance writer Oobah Butler created a fake TripAdvisor listing for "The Shed at Dulwich," which was actually his shed home in South London. Using fake reviews from friends and family, a burner phone, a website with an emotion-based menu, and photos of dishes made from household products, the nonexistent restaurant rose from last place (18,149th) to the No. 1 ranking among London restaurants by early November. It drew reservation inquiries from around the world and reportedly received 89,000 views in a single day. TripAdvisor said it had already applied a penalty and removed reviews before Butler exposed the ruse in an article on Vice. The hoax highlighted vulnerabilities in online review platforms and drew comparisons to disinformation on other sites. Butler later opened the shed for one night, serving instant food to actors and real diners, one of whom asked to book again.

Stroke disrupts the relationship between the motor cortex, spinal cord, and muscles, causing upper extremity weakness and impaired coordination that hinder daily activities. Heterogeneity of motor deficits among stroke survivors creates a need for more sensitive measures of motor function. Surface EMG can quantify changes in muscle activation, such as excessive antagonist co-contraction, which impairs coordination and correlates with spasticity. Muscle synergy analysis also reveals altered coordination after stroke, including changes in synergy number, composition, and merging. Traditional low-density EMG cannot measure smaller hand muscles, while existing high-density EMG (HD-EMG) systems are cumbersome and limited to expert researchers.

This study characterized movement coordination of extrinsic hand muscles in chronic stroke and able-bodied groups using an easy-to-use HD-EMG wearable sleeve (NeuroLife) spanning the forearm. Seven stroke participants (60±5 years) and seven able-bodied participants (27±1 years) performed 12 hand, wrist, and forearm movements; able-bodied participants additionally performed 25 dexterous movements. Stroke participants underwent clinical assessments (UEFM, Box and Blocks, Modified Ashworth Scale) and were split into mild and severe groups for some analyses.

EMG signals were recorded at 3,000 Hz, notch- and bandpass-filtered, and corrected for artifacts using blind source separation (AJDC with QNDIAG), with RMS features extracted from 150 ms bins. A standardized sleeve mapping procedure converted all sleeve sizes to a common 70-channel medium-sleeve format, and a validated HD-EMG-to-muscle-group mapping reduced channel data to six forearm muscle groups. Analyses included co-contraction index, muscle correlation, and muscle synergy decomposition via non-negative matrix factorization. The work aims to demonstrate the information obtainable from an HD-EMG sleeve and to identify motor-related biomarkers for stroke rehabilitation, movement disorders research, and clinical care.

Using cryogenic four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) with a liquid helium-cooled stage down to ~20 K, the authors visualize polar textures in quantum paraelectric SrTiO3. Polarization is extracted from intensity asymmetries between inversion-related Kikuchi bands (Friedel pairs) in diffraction patterns, an approach validated by dynamical scattering multislice simulations. Below the antiferrodistortive transition (TAFD ≈ 105 K), SrTiO3 is locally polar, hosting spatially fluctuating polar nanodomains with a correlation length of ~20 nm that exhibit periodic spatial ordering at λ ≈ 25 nm, reflecting correlations between nanodomains rather than a true incommensurate structural modulation. Below Tq ≈ 40 K, the quantum paraelectric regime is characterized by fragmentation: domains shrink (~14 nm), become more disordered and randomly oriented, and the periodic ordering is suppressed. Temperature tracking shows nanodomains nucleate near TAFD, grow and self-organize down to ~69 K, then fragment upon further cooling. Quantum paraelectricity thus involves re-entrant disordering of preexisting polar nanodomains rather than a complete absence of polarization, with quantum fluctuations entwined with increased spatial fluctuations. These textures likely underlie anomalous thermal conductivity, glass-like dynamics, and polar-acoustic anomalies, and may inform how external stimuli induce ferroelectric order and the link between the fluctuating polar state and unconventional superconductivity in doped SrTiO3. Methods include focused ion beam sample preparation, liquid helium cryogenic STEM, 4D-STEM acquisition with an EMPAD detector, multislice simulations, center-of-mass analysis of Kikuchi bands, and autocorrelation analysis.

Following tax reform, Apple now has greater access to foreign cash reserves that were previously held offshore to avoid repatriation taxes. On its earnings call, CFO Luca Maestri announced that Apple is targeting to become approximately net cash neutral over time, with a current net cash position of $163 billion. CEO Tim Cook clarified this means having equal amounts of cash and debt that balance to zero. To achieve this goal, Apple could reduce gross cash, increase debt, or both, potentially through a special one-time dividend, a larger share repurchase authorization, or more aggressive annual dividend increases. Regarding existing debt, Apple could call its bonds, roll them over with new issuances, or pay them off at maturity; its debt extends as far as 2047. Specific capital allocation plans will be provided with second fiscal quarter results.

The S&P 500 ended a six-day run of record highs on Friday as U.S. nonfarm payrolls fell 33,000 in September—the first monthly decline in seven years—due to hurricanes Harvey and Irma, though average wages rose more than expected. Walgreens and CVS fell 4.9 percent each after a report that Amazon was close to selling prescription drugs; Amazon rose 0.9 percent. The Nasdaq set a sixth straight record close. For the week, the S&P 500 rose 1.2 percent, the Dow 1.6 percent, and the Nasdaq 1.5 percent.

The war is waged by many nations against an international menace, but Allied leaders retain nationalist aims, producing divergent purposes and uncoordinated strategy. Nationalist control of the Western Allies has caused conflict with partners: misunderstanding with Russia, and Italy's disaster after supplies were withheld and her front overextended, as with Rumania. Unity requires pooling purposes and shifting power toward middle parties and the moderate left; governing groups resist this, weakening their own peoples while aiding enemy cohesion. Since decision must come by exhausting Germany's reserves on the Western Front, success demands broad popular consent and diplomacy exposing Germany's deceptive liberalism. Germany will likely attempt a winter peace offensive; the Allies will resist, then force a German retirement behind the Meuse and Scheldt and invade through Lorraine. The decision will involve destroying submarine bases, recapturing northern France, and potentially invading Germany; the deeper decision lies in manpower reserves, as Germany faces Lorraine's reconquest while the American reserve materializes.

The dollar rose to two-month highs against the yen and seven-week highs against the euro after September's jobs report showed wages rising 0.5 percent, despite payrolls falling 33,000 due to hurricanes. Traders now price a 93 percent likelihood of a December Fed rate hike, up from 84 percent.

Fior Markets has published a market research report, "Cooking Oil Market 2017 Global Analysis and Forecast to 2022," covering industry trends, segmentation, growth, market share, revenue, leading players, regions, types, and applications. Based on primary and secondary research with expert inputs, it includes forecasts, market size estimates, and player profiles. It covers product, application, and regional segments across USA, Europe, Japan, China, India, and South East Asia for 2017 to 2022.

PIMS employees, protesting for a fifth day under the All Employees' Movement for Restoration of PIMS, forced SZABMU Vice Chancellor Dr. Javed Akram out of his office and sealed it, demanding PIMS' separation from the university. The VC offered to resign and cautioned against suspending services for up to 20,000 daily patients. After a meeting between CADD Minister Dr. Tariq Fazal Chaudhry, movement representatives, and Law Minister Zahid Hamid, the PIMS amendment bill was to be sent to the Prime Minister, who has in principle agreed to the separation. Protestors resolved to continue the strike; JI leader Mian Muhammad Aslam and CDA's Chaudhry Muhammad Yasin expressed solidarity.

Dinbych followed three high-scoring wins by defeating a well-drilled Wrexham, who matched them try-for-try and took a losing bonus point. Despite more territory and possession, Dinbych were frustrated by Wrexham's defence. Wrexham led 12-10 at half-time through tries from James Price and James Weston, while Tom Seddon scored for Dinbych. Second-half tries from Aidyn Jones and Owain Davies put Dinbych ahead before Jack Ratcliff replied for Wrexham. Dinbych 2nds lost 16-10 at Flint in Division Three (North).

Singapore Airlines will resume non-stop flights between Singapore and Newark on Oct. 12, a route it discontinued in 2013 after deeming it unprofitable with its four-engine Airbus A340 aircraft. The route, covering approximately 9,000 nautical miles (9,537 statute miles), will become the world's longest flight by distance, displacing Qatar Airways' Doha-Auckland route. Scheduled flight times are 18 hours, 45 minutes Singapore-bound and 18 hours, 25 minutes on the return. The route will be flown using the new ultra-long-range Airbus A350-900ULR, with Singapore Airlines as the launch customer. The aircraft will be configured with 161 seats—67 business class and 94 premium economy—with no standard coach seats. Service will initially run three times weekly, moving to daily after an additional aircraft enters service. Newark will become Singapore Airlines' fifth U.S. airport served.

A hockey player discusses his team's comfort with media attention and loud arenas, noting they have started every playoff series on the road. He credits the team's success in "hanging around" and persevering through many one-goal games, but admits the last game was disappointing, as they failed to make things difficult for the Devils' defense or generate shots on Brodeur. He describes the team as patient and level-headed when facing adversity and says they will stick with their plan. He acknowledges they were too passive and did not skate or work hard, but believes the fix is simple: show up and play harder in the next game.

Peruvian police are considering expelling a U.S. citizen and a Canadian citizen who allegedly incited rural communities to protest against Hudbay Minerals' Constancia copper mine after entering Peru as tourists. Hudbay suspended mine operations in November amid protests demanding promised development projects.

This manuscript presents a mapping review of United States occupational therapy fieldwork education literature from 1989 to 2020, conducted by the Research Promotion ad hoc committee of the AOTA Academic Fieldwork Coordinators Academic Leadership Council (AFWC–ALC). The committee searched four databases and the Journal of Occupational Therapy Education, screening 1,619 articles and including 67 that met eligibility criteria. Articles were mapped along three axes: the AOTA Occupational Therapy Education Research Agenda – Revised (2018) categories, level of education (OT or OTA), and level of fieldwork (Level I or II).

Results showed the literature disproportionately focused on Level II occupational therapy fieldwork (36 of 67 papers; 53%) and on two agenda categories: Instructional Methods (n=23) and Learner characteristics and competencies (n=31). No articles mapped to Theory building, Signature pedagogies, or Promotion of diversity, inclusion, and equity. OTA programs and Level I fieldwork were dramatically underrepresented.

Limitations included difficulty mapping articles to agenda categories, inconsistent description of fieldwork levels in the literature, exclusion of gray literature and non-U.S. research, and COVID-19-related delays. The authors recommend collaborative, team science approaches involving stakeholders and propose that fieldwork be formally included in future revisions of the AOTA Education Research Agenda to address identified gaps.

This final lecture examines ramifications of the collective Thomson scattering spectrum. The spectral density function contains electron and ion components, both representing scattering from electrons—either electrons repelling other electrons or electrons accompanying ions. For Maxwellian distributions, susceptibilities depend on the collective scattering parameter alpha (1/kλ_Debye, using the electron Debye length) and the function w(x), where x is the ratio of phase velocity to thermal velocity.

When alpha² approaches 0 (scattering wavelength smaller than the Debye length), the plasma response vanishes, yielding incoherent scattering that recovers the electron distribution function. For arbitrary alpha at high frequencies (ξ_i >> 1), there is no ion response; resonances where the real permittivity vanishes recover the electron plasma wave (Langmuir) dispersion relation, with peak positions depending on density and temperature, and peak broadening related to electron temperature through Landau damping.

At low frequencies, if zTe/Ti < 3, ion acoustic resonances are damped and do not appear; if zTe/Ti >> 1, ion acoustic wave resonances occur at a derived frequency. Using the Salpeter approximation (equal temperatures), the total cross-section shows that alpha determines whether electron or ion features dominate the spectrum.

Electron-ion drift breaks the symmetry between positive and negative frequency ion acoustic peaks; fitting the full spectrum yields drift velocity and thus local current. The ion acoustic spectrum provides electron temperature, ion temperature, ion flow velocity, and drift, though not electron density. Collisions damp coherent features and modify spectra. Finite collection volumes with temperature or velocity gradients, and finite collection angles, broaden and distort measurements. Current research addresses non-Maxwellian distributions and multi-angle observations.

Archaeologists in Egypt have discovered a 4,400-year-old tomb near Cairo's pyramids, the Antiquities Ministry announced Saturday. It likely belonged to Hetpet, a high-ranking 5th Dynasty official, and features wall paintings of hunting and fishing scenes, including monkeys reaping fruit and dancing before an orchestra. Excavation is underway for another tomb believed to be Hetpet's in Giza's western necropolis.

Turkey's education administration is unitary and centralized, with policies determined and decisions taken by top authorities of the Ministry of National Education and applied downward; directors are often appointed based on political views rather than competence, and fundamental components such as accountability, transparency, democracy, participation, efficiency, and flexibility are generally not considered. Turkey falls well below OECD averages in 2018 PISA results and GDP per capita. The study aims to develop a local education boards model for Turkey based on the education administration models of OECD countries and the views of teachers and administrators.

Using a mixed method with an exploratory sequential design, the researchers analyzed the education administration structures of 16 OECD countries whose PISA averages and GDP exceed OECD averages, and surveyed teachers and administrators in Seyhan district, Adana (421 participants). Findings show these countries manage education through various boards and commissions composed of stakeholders, and that countries with localized administration surpass OECD averages in PISA and GDP. In the survey, 61.5% preferred local administration over central; 41% wanted provincial education boards/commissions to undertake decentralization; 61% preferred management by elected boards; majorities favored participatory boards including teachers, principals, parents, students, unions, and local representatives; and most supported transferring 22 of 27 listed duties from the central government to local units.

The study concludes that Turkey's centralized, directorate-based system should be replaced by a Local Education Boards model, in which the Ministry retains only policy-setting, monitoring, evaluation, and audit functions while implementation duties transfer to local boards (provincial/district boards, vocational education boards, and school boards), with a central organization comprising a National Education Supreme Council, the Ministry's central organization, and a Higher Education Council. Recommendations include pilot schemes, further research, and consideration of the model by policymakers. Limitations include sampling restricted to Seyhan district in 2016–2017 and coverage of only 16 of 36 OECD countries.

A federal judge declined the government's request to delay an order allowing transgender individuals to enlist in the military starting January 1, 2018. The Pentagon is preparing to accept transgender recruits, while the Justice Department reviews legal options.

A new Texas law will replace the STAAR standardized test with three shorter exams administered at the beginning, middle, and end of the school year, launching in 2027-28. The law also bans benchmark practice tests for grades 3-8 and requires scores to be released about two days after each exam. Supporters, including the lawmakers behind the overhaul, say it will reduce overall testing time and relieve student stress.

However, some parents, teachers, and administrators worry the changes do not go far enough and that three tests could triple pressure rather than reduce it. The law directs the Texas Education Agency to study reducing the weight of testing in school accountability ratings, but the report is not due until 2029-30 and the agency is not required to implement its findings, leading critics to fear the end-of-year test will continue to dominate ratings. Schools may choose TEA-approved national assessments for the first two exams, and some educators hope to use MAP tests, which they say create less pressure than STAAR. Educators also want greater input on designing the new end-of-year exam and fewer lockdown-style testing protocols. Critics cite Florida's similar 2022 switch as a cautionary example.

NVIDIA RTX IO integrates with Microsoft's DirectStorage API to enable GPU-based lossless decompression, offloading work from potentially dozens of CPU cores and improving I/O performance by a factor of two, with claims of 100X throughput and 20X lower CPU utilization. The NVIDIA A40, based on the GA10x Ampere architecture, is positioned as the most powerful data center GPU for visual computing, delivering up to 2X FP32 throughput, 2X ray-tracing throughput, and 5X AI training throughput (10X with sparsity) versus the Quadro RTX 6000, with 48GB memory expandable to 96GB via NVLink. Ampere GPUs support 4K at 120Hz and 8K at 60Hz through DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1, the latter being a first for discrete GPUs. The fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware decoding for codecs including AV1—a first among GPUs—while the seventh-generation NVENC handles encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC. GA10x offers up to 2X performance in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI, featuring second-generation RT Cores and third-generation Tensor Cores, and is the first GPU architecture to support GDDR6X memory, achieving 936 GB/sec in the RTX 3090. The RTX 3090 (GA102) is 1.5x faster than TITAN RTX with 24GB memory; the RTX 3070 (GA104) outperforms the RTX 2080 Ti. A new Error Detection and Replay (EDR) feature helps overclockers identify memory limits before crashes. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU includes 10,752 CUDA cores and 48GB GDDR6, expandable to 96GB via NVLink.

England have qualified for the 2018 World Cup in Russia but were unimpressive in a 1-0 win over Slovenia. The passage criticizes manager Gareth Southgate's cautious 4-2-3-1 formation, arguing it limits attacking players like Harry Kane, Marcus Rashford, and Raheem Sterling. Dele Alli is described as England's only viable No. 10, while Sterling is better suited as a winger. With friendlies against Brazil and Germany upcoming, the author urges Southgate to adopt a bolder approach using three centre backs and attacking wing-backs, warning that without change England risks another early tournament exit.

A bug in Atlassian software, including Jira and Confluence, exposes private server keys through a vulnerable proxy that enables XSS and SSRF attacks, potentially allowing attackers to steal AWS access keys and take over instances. NIST rated the bug 6.1 out of 10, and fixes have been released. Security researcher Robert Wiggins found over a dozen major companies running outdated, exposed deployments. Several affected organizations, including EE, Insider, Easy Metrics, a US government agency, IEEE, Ronin, and A&E Networks, fixed or shut down their servers after being contacted. Three companies did not respond and remain vulnerable. Updating Atlassian software is recommended.

Spotify, Comcast, and Oracle have recently announced co-CEO arrangements, a once-unusual leadership model. Co-CEOs lead roughly 1.2% of Russell 3000 companies, a figure unchanged over five years, though experts say more boards may adopt the structure as AI accelerates the pace of change. A Harvard Business Review study found dual-CEO companies posted 9.5% average annual shareholder returns from 1996 to 2020, versus 6.9% for single-leader firms. However, the model carries risks, including unclear responsibilities and power struggles. Other companies with dual chiefs have included Netflix, Salesforce, Sony Interactive Entertainment, and Chipotle, which returned to a single CEO in 2016. Experts say success depends on clear roles, alignment, and collaboration. At Comcast, Mike Cavanagh will work in partnership with Brian Roberts without divided duties, which some analysts say could pose challenges. At Oracle, two chiefs replace Safra Catz while cofounder Larry Ellison remains chairman.

This ebook, released by the U.S. Department of State's Office of the Historian in May 2018, is an edition of Foreign Relations of the United States, 1902, concerning whaling and sealing claims against Russia arising from the arrest and seizure of the American vessels Cape Horn Pigeon, James Hamilton Lewis, C. H. White, and Kate and Anna. The volume contains a translation of a memorandum presented by Herbert H. D. Peirce, counsel for the United States, to arbitrator T. M. C. Asser of the Netherlands, in an arbitration established by an exchange of notes dated September 3, 1900, between the United States and Russia. The memorandum supports claims by the owners, officers, and crews of the vessels for indemnity. The passage also describes the ebook initiative, including citation guidance and contact information, and includes correspondence between Secretary of State John Hay and Peirce regarding the transmission of the memorandum to Senator H. C. Lodge for printing as a public document.

NVIDIA Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended October 25, 2015 (Q3 fiscal 2016) reports revenue of $1,305 million, up 7% from $1,225 million in the prior-year quarter, and net income of $246 million ($0.44 diluted per share) compared with $173 million ($0.31) a year earlier. Nine-month revenue was $3,609 million (up 5%), with net income of $406 million ($0.72 diluted) versus $437 million ($0.77). Gross margin was 56.3% for the quarter.

The GPU segment generated Q3 revenue of $1,110 million (up 12%), driven primarily by high-end GeForce gaming GPUs (up 40%), while Tegra Processor revenue fell 23% to $129 million due to declining OEM smartphone and tablet sales, partially offset by growth in automotive. The "All Other" category contributed $66 million from the Intel patent cross-licensing arrangement.

In May 2015, NVIDIA began winding down its Icera modem operations after failing to find a buyer, recording restructuring charges of $8 million in Q3 and $97 million for the nine months, with an additional $25–35 million expected in Q4, affecting approximately 5% of the global workforce. A $21 million charge was recorded for the voluntary recall of SHIELD 8-inch tablets due to overheating batteries.

Patent litigation with Qualcomm and Samsung continues before the ITC and in multiple district courts; in October 2015, an ITC administrative law judge issued an initial determination that importation of Samsung's accused products did not violate U.S. law, with a final decision targeted for February 10, 2016.

The company completed a $400 million accelerated share repurchase (18 million shares at an average of $21.63) in October 2015, paid $53 million in Q3 dividends, and announced an 18% dividend increase to $0.115 per share. As of October 25, 2015, total assets were $7,174 million, shareholders' equity was $4,465 million, and cash plus marketable securities totaled approximately $4.7 billion. Nine-month operating cash flow was $664 million. NVIDIA is constructing a new Santa Clara headquarters under an off-balance-sheet lease arrangement with bank funding of up to $380 million.

In this Court of Claims action, Ralph Hartwell Brubaker (substituted as claimant for Berenice M. Brubaker, individually and as administrator with the will annexed of her estate) sought damages for the State's appropriation of portions of an approximately 365-acre property near Massena for the St. Lawrence River project. Four appropriations occurred: approximately 183 acres north of Middle Road (May 19, 1955); a .15-acre permanent flooding easement (June 12, 1956); 25.34 acres in fee (April 1, 1957); and a 55.38-acre easement for an electrical transmission line (May 1, 1957). The claimant asserted damages of $309,000; the State asserted $28,000 to $40,000.

Applying United States v. Miller, the court held that increases in value attributable to the Seaway project itself could not be charged to the sovereign where the land was probably within the project's scope. For the first taking, the record lacked probative evidence that the property probably would be condemned, so project-related enhancement was excluded. The later appropriations involved adjacent land outside the original project scope, so market value as enhanced by proximity was payable.

The court awarded $32,000 for the first appropriation, $100 for the flooding easement, $39,750 for the fee taking ($12,675 direct and $27,075 consequential damages), and $27,700 for the transmission easement, each with interest.

This patent application, a continuation of several prior applications tracing back to a Korean application filed April 16, 2015, relates to a display device such as a liquid crystal display, organic light emitting diode display, or electrophoretic display. The described display device includes a substrate, a pixel electrode and an opposing electrode, an encapsulation portion with at least one organic layer and at least one inorganic layer alternately deposited, and a planarization layer on the encapsulation portion. The planarization layer covers the edge portion of the encapsulation portion, where the encapsulation's upper surface height gradually decreases, and the angle between the planarization layer's edge side surface and the substrate surface (about 70 degrees or more, nearly 90 degrees) is larger than the corresponding angle of the encapsulation portion (less than 45 degrees, possibly less than about 20 degrees). The planarization layer may include organic material and provide an entirely flat upper surface on which patterns such as touch sensors—touch electrodes and touch wiring—may be formed in an on-cell configuration. This arrangement maximizes the flattened area available for patterns, reduces dead space and bezel size, and reduces parasitic capacitance between the opposing electrode and the touch patterns, improving touch sensitivity. The encapsulation portion's organic layer is covered by the inorganic layer to block moisture penetration. Touch electrodes may use transparent conductive materials such as ITO, IZO, silver nanowire, metal mesh, or carbon nanotubes, and may operate through mutual or self-capacitance sensing. Other embodiments include a planarization layer with a flat, cut edge surface or one formed only partially over the encapsulation portion, mainly in the peripheral area.

The passage presents two defensive strategies against the UCLA offense, which produces easy baskets against teams unprepared to defend high post rubs and down screens. The Basic NBA Show & Recover approach avoids switching on high post rubs, since a "Big" screening a "Little" would allow the screener to post up a smaller defender. Instead, the cutter is forced behind the screen, the screener's defender shows and bumps, and defenders recover into pass denial positions while weakside defenders pack in, ending in final matchups. The All Out SOS Disruption strategy traps the wing on the first pass, exploiting the point guard's low post cut, which makes ball reversal difficult. When the ball is passed out of the trap, all defenders rotate according to the near player concept, concluding with standard SOS defensive principles and final matchups.

This study uses a microscale four-point probe setup inside a scanning electron microscope to decouple the electrical resistivity of Al-Mg-Si alloys into contributions from the Al solid solution grain interior and secondary-phase precipitates (Si and Mg2Si). Three compositions (99.5, 94.5, and 90.5 at. % Al) were synthesized, heat treated under three conditions (24 h at 300°C, 72 h and 120 h at 350°C), and characterized by XRD, EDS, and EBSD, revealing micron/sub-micron Si and Mg2Si precipitates and hundred-micron-sized grains. Grain interior resistivity was found to depend on heat treatment rather than composition, while Si and Mg2Si precipitates contributed equally to resistivity regardless of shape. Bulk resistivity increased linearly with total solute (Mg + Si) content, with coefficients dependent on annealing condition, since precipitate volume fraction—not precipitate identity—controls resistivity. Contributions from vacancies, dislocations, and grain boundaries were negligible. The approach enables resolving bulk resistivity down to micron length scales.

A substantial majority of the Supreme Court, possibly seven justices, appears willing to reverse lower court rulings that Rep. Michael Bost lacked standing to challenge an Illinois law counting mail-in ballots postmarked by Election Day but arriving up to 14 days later. The unresolved question is what standing test applies in election-law cases. Paul Clement, arguing for Bost, proposed broad "candidate standing," which Justice Kagan resisted, though she suggested candidates need only allege a likely electoral disadvantage under the new rule, not that they would lose. Justices Sotomayor and Jackson doubted Bost's standing, noting he admitted the rule could not cost him his safe seat. Illinois's solicitor general accepted Kagan's test but argued Bost could not meet it, drawing pushback from Kavanaugh and Jackson. Kavanaugh also questioned what remedies would exist if such challenges were forced into the post-election period.

Y-Cross is a drop-back passing concept common in the Air Raid offense and used widely across football. It is a weak-side flood concept featuring a post route, crossing route, and running back stretching the flat, with taggable backside routes. The crossing route is typically run by the tight end but can be assigned to a slot receiver. The concept performs well against man coverage and Cover 4, but is less effective against Cover 3, where a post safety occupies the middle of the field. The quarterback's progression is post, deep crosser, then running back check-down or dig. Variations include a post-wheel read and a curl-flat tag, the latter useful against 1-high defenses and requiring a strong-armed quarterback.

DWI arrests in Wichita Falls have declined, with only 5 arrests over St. Patrick's Day weekend and 25 this year, compared to 39 in 2016 and 38 in 2017. Sgt. Harold McClure attributes the drop to people recognizing the importance of sober driving. Ridesharing services Uber and Lyft, which arrived last summer, may also contribute; an Uber study found 90% of riders believe it reduces drunk driving.

The passage is a guide to EUR/USD forex trading, covering strategy development, backtesting, and market analysis. EUR/USD, representing the Euro against the US Dollar, is the world's most traded and liquid currency pair, influenced by economic data, interest rate differentials, inflation, and central bank policies. The authors present a backtested strategy of 713 trades with a 53% gain and emphasize backtesting as the best approach to trading. Effective strategies combine fundamental analysis (interest rates, GDP, employment data), technical analysis (moving averages, Fibonacci retracements, support/resistance levels), and market sentiment, though sentiment is mainly useful for short-term trading. Optimal trading times occur during the European-US session overlap (12:00–4:00 pm GMT in summer; 1:00–5:00 pm GMT in winter). Trading styles discussed include position trading, swing trading, day trading, and scalping—the latter two being difficult, with about 90% of traders failing. Risk management involves stop-loss orders, position sizing (typically risking no more than 1% of capital), and diversification across uncorrelated pairs. Instruments include spot forex, futures, options, ETFs, and CFDs, though most CFD traders lose money. The article also covers broker selection, demo account practice, and common mistakes such as excessive leverage and lacking a backtested plan. The authors conclude that forex is a difficult zero-sum game and state they do not trade EUR/USD themselves.

This study presents a bibliometric analysis of artificial intelligence (AI) in STEM education research from 2020 to 2024, using citation analysis of 35 articles retrieved from the Dimensions database with the keywords "artificial intelligence" AND "stem education," analyzed via Microsoft Excel and VOSviewer. Results show that 2024 saw 15 publications receiving 234 citations (averaging 15.62 per publication), while 2020 had 100 publications with no citations. The United States led in documents (9) and citations (103), followed by China (5 documents, 0 citations). The most-cited authors were Nesra Yannier, Kenneth R. Koedinger, and Scott E. Hudson, each with one article cited 55 times. The International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education was the most-cited journal (55 citations), and the most-cited article was "Active Learning is About More Than Hands-On: A Mixed-Reality AI System to Support STEM Education" (55 citations). Carnegie Mellon University was the most-cited institution. The study highlights AI's benefits in STEM education, including personalized learning, advanced analytics, and instructional automation, while noting challenges such as ethical concerns, the need for AI literacy, and potential student engagement issues. The findings aim to guide researchers, educators, and policymakers in integrating AI with STEM education.

Bitcoin rose to a six-week high on Tuesday, up 4.4 percent at $9,340.88, after a 50 percent first-quarter loss. Positive headlines about major financial institutions entering the cryptocurrency space lifted sentiment. Bitcoin's gains pushed total market capitalization to $427 billion, the largest since early March. Goldman Sachs hired Justin Schmidt as head of digital asset markets, and Barclays gauged client interest in a cryptocurrency trading desk. A Thomson Reuters survey found one in five financial institutions considering cryptocurrency trading within 12 months. Regulatory challenges remain.

The Trump administration's $100,000 fee for new H-1B visas could threaten thousands of college jobs. As of June 30, U.S. colleges employed over 16,000 H-1B workers, about 5 percent of fiscal year 2025's total. The administration argues the program is abused to avoid hiring American workers, while employers say it is necessary to attract skilled talent. At least 930 colleges had at least one H-1B employee, with nearly half of all college visas concentrated at just 50 institutions. The fee, effective Sept. 21, does not apply to current visa holders, and universities are exempt from the annual 85,000-visa cap. Experts doubt most colleges can afford the fee, and the National Postdoc Association warns it would create barriers to attracting international talent.

Benjamin Franklin's advice that prevention outweighs cure applies to natural disasters. Hurricanes Maria, Harvey and Irma exposed serious health hazards: Puerto Rico's near-total power loss, Houston floodwaters contaminated with E. coli, lead and arsenic, toxic chemical releases, mold, mosquito-borne disease risks, and elderly deaths. Health risks linger long after storms, and better planning could have reduced damage. The author urges improved preparedness, public education, hardened infrastructure, secured industrial sites, stronger seawalls, and storm-resistant grids, noting that despite Florida's upgrades, Irma still cut power to half the state for ten days.

At the 2018 California Democrats State Convention in San Diego, Dave Min won the party's endorsement in the race against Rep. Mimi Walters after a floor fight, and Hans Keirstead was endorsed against Rep. Dana Rohrabacher despite opponents' efforts to block both endorsements. No candidate for governor or U.S. Senate reached the 60-percent threshold for endorsement. In three other targeted GOP districts, candidates fell short: Mike Levin and Bryan Caforio each received 53 percent, and Jay Chen received 47 percent. Delegates favored Kevin de Leon over Sen. Dianne Feinstein, 54 to 37 percent, and in the governor's race, Gavin Newsom led with 37 percent while Antonio Villaraigosa finished fourth at 9 percent.

Markets face seasonal weakness and institutional rebalancing, with diminished liquidity, thin volume, tax loss selling, and fading earnings momentum in August. TLT rallied to the July 6-month calendar range high before selling off, showing a mean reversion sell signal but also a bullish divergence. A dollar break below 98 would suggest further declines, which is bullish for commodities. Weakening dollar, lower yields, and rising gold are generally risk-off, while the growth-value divergence continues to widen.

Coccolithophores, microscopic algae smaller than dust, regulate Earth's climate by capturing carbon dioxide, producing oxygen, and forming calcium carbonate plates that sink to the ocean floor, creating chalk and limestone layers that record climate history. Five European institutions—the Ruđer Bošković Institute, the Lyell Centre at Heriot-Watt University, NORCE Norwegian Research Centre, MARE at the University of Lisbon, and the International Nannoplankton Association—announced October 10 as International Coccolithophore Day to raise awareness of these organisms. They generate over 1.5 billion tonnes of calcium carbonate annually, storing carbon in deep-sea sediments, but climate change threatens their survival. Research at these institutions examines their role in carbon cycling, interactions with viruses and bacteria, aerosol-driven distribution across the Atlantic, and their fossil record for reconstructing ancient oceans. The campaign aims to inspire ocean literacy, policy focus, and public engagement.

A Tennessee mother's video of her son Keaton describing bullying at middle school drew support from athletes and entertainers. Keaton said classmates mocked his appearance, said he had no friends, and poured milk on him. The video surpassed 18 million views, a fundraiser raised over $29,000, and figures including Delanie Walker, Tyler Byrd, Kelsea Ballerini, Dale Earnhardt Jr., and Snoop Dogg offered support.

On June 28, 2021, NVIDIA Corporation completed a Domestication, simplifying its corporate structure by repatriating the economic rights of certain non-U.S. intellectual property to the United States through domestication of a foreign subsidiary. The Company updated its second quarter fiscal 2022 tax rate outlook: GAAP and non-GAAP tax rates are both expected to be 13 percent, plus or minus 1 percent, excluding discrete items, up from the prior outlook of 10 percent, plus or minus 1 percent. The discrete tax impact from the Domestication is expected to be a benefit of approximately $250 million to $300 million. The Domestication aligns the Company's corporate structure with its operating structure in accordance with the OECD's Base Erosion and Profit Sharing conclusions and changes to U.S. and European tax laws.

Gunmen kidnapped 52 farmers, mostly from the Uzbek minority, from three villages in Jowzjan province's Darz Ab district while they worked on their land. Police blamed the Taliban, which controls most of the district. Elders and the police chief are negotiating for the farmers' release, with an operation planned if talks fail. A Taliban spokesman could not confirm the report.

This study performed cross-disorder analyses of prodromal symptoms and drug prescriptions preceding Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), using the UK THIN primary care database with replication in the UK Biobank. The THIN cohort included 20,214 AD patients, 28,222 PD patients, 4,682 DLB patients, and 20,214 controls.

All 12 investigated health conditions were more frequent in all three diseases than in controls during the 5 years before diagnosis. Disease-specific patterns emerged: memory problems were more frequent before AD, tremor before PD, and memory troubles, confusion, hallucinations, constipation, falls, and depression before DLB. Autonomic dysfunction (constipation, urinary disorders, hypotension) was more strongly associated with PD and DLB than AD, with some symptoms observable up to 15 years before diagnosis.

Lower prescriptions of antihypertensive and antidiabetic medications preceded all three diseases, while benzodiazepines and serotonin reuptake inhibitors were more frequently prescribed. Statin prescriptions were lower before PD than before dementia-related disorders, a finding replicated in the UK Biobank. Among PD patients, prescriptions of drugs against hypercholesterolemia, constipation, depression, and psychosis were associated with developing dementia within five years of PD diagnosis.

The authors conclude that neurodegenerative diseases have a long prodromal phase observable in primary care, which could enable prevention measures, and that lipid-lowering therapies may play a differential role across these diseases.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2015. The company designs, manufactures, and sells fully electric vehicles, powertrain components, and Tesla Energy products.

For the three months ended June 30, 2015, total revenues were $955.0 million, up from $769.3 million in the prior-year quarter, driven primarily by increased Model S deliveries. Net loss was $184.2 million ($1.45 per share) compared with $61.9 million ($0.50 per share) a year earlier. Gross margin declined to 22.3% from 27.7%, attributed to product and regional mix, manufacturing costs related to the dual motor drive unit ramp, obsolete inventory, and lower ZEV credit revenue. Research and development expenses rose to $181.7 million from $107.7 million, and SG&A expenses rose to $201.8 million from $134.0 million.

As of June 30, 2015, total assets were $6.47 billion and cash and cash equivalents were $1.15 billion. Operating cash flow for the first six months of 2015 was negative $291.3 million, investing activities used $855.2 million (including $831.2 million of capital expenditures), and financing activities provided $404.5 million. The company expects approximately $1.5 billion in capital expenditures for 2015.

Tesla had delivered over 78,000 Model S vehicles through June 30, 2015, and expects to deliver 50,000–55,000 Model S and Model X vehicles in 2015. Model X deliveries are planned for late in the third quarter of 2015, with the mass-market Model 3 targeted for late 2017. The Gigafactory under construction near Reno, Nevada had incurred $206.6 million in construction costs, with Panasonic partnered to supply battery cells and first products expected in the first quarter of 2016. Tesla also announced Powerwall and Powerpack energy storage products.

The company's debt includes convertible senior notes due 2018, 2019, and 2021; the 2018 Notes became convertible in the third quarter of 2015 and were classified as current liabilities. Tesla borrowed $114.3 million under its Warehouse Facility and $50.0 million under a new $500 million asset-based Credit Agreement. A November 2013 securities class action was dismissed with prejudice in September 2014, though an appeal is pending.

Gold is one of the world's most widely traded raw materials and the most popular precious metal. Gold trading means speculating on gold prices for profit via futures, options, spot markets, stocks, CFDs, and ETFs, with most trades cash settled and no physical gold handled. Prices fluctuate due to supply, demand, and political, social, and economic unrest, and gold is considered a "safe haven" asset that can negatively correlate with stocks and bonds. Historically, Egyptians used gold by 3400 BCE, it became an official medium of exchange around 1500 BC, and the 1946 Bretton Woods agreement set gold at $35 per ounce before the gold standard ended; the first gold futures contract traded on COMEX in 1974. The article backtests a weekend swing trading strategy on the GLD ETF from late 2004 to September 2021, finding that nearly all of gold's gains come from overnight ownership. Buying at Thursday's close and selling at Monday's open produced 0.19% per trade with a 1.3 profit factor, improving when one additional parameter was added.

The article analyzes gold, mining stocks, and the US Dollar Index. Gold rallied strongly on Friday as the USD Index declined, but gold remains below a rising resistance line and continues to mirror its 2011–2013 price pattern. Mining stocks, including the VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF (GDXJ), failed to rally alongside gold, closing below the April high for a third consecutive day. The author views this divergence as bearish, since gold stocks typically outperform gold early in rallies, suggesting the early stage of a larger decline. The USD Index is described as forming an inverse head-and-shoulders pattern, verified by a move back to the neck level, with a projected rally to at least 101.3. Stocks, having fallen below a rising support line after failing to exceed previous highs, show bearish signals despite a current pause. The author compares the overall setup to 2008 and references the Peak Chaos theory.

This study reviewed the latest Voluntary National Reviews (VNRs) from 18 Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR) countries submitted between 2016 and 2021 to assess reporting on health-related SDG targets and indicators. All 18 VNRs established mechanisms to monitor SDG progress; 11 reported on all 17 SDGs, with comprehensiveness associated with country income level. Only 8 VNRs explicitly mentioned country targets for 2030. Nine VNRs reported data availability; Morocco and Qatar were the only countries reporting over 50% data availability for the 244 SDG indicators, and SDG3 data availability ranged from 48% to 93% among the five countries reporting this figure. Fourteen VNRs cited limited data availability as a challenge, including human resource capacity, low data quality, lack of statistical tools, and lack of disaggregation. Reporting on health indicators varied by indicator type and income level; the most commonly reported were maternal mortality ratio (100%), neonatal mortality (83%), and under-5 mortality (78%). Trend reporting was less common, and Qatar was the only country reporting trends across all SDG3 indicators. Indicators derived from disease surveillance and civil registration and vital statistics systems were reported more frequently than those from routine health information systems or national surveys. The authors conclude that while VNRs demonstrate commitment to the SDGs, weak national health information systems, limited data availability, and analytical capacity remain challenges; strengthening regulatory frameworks, CRVS systems, and population-based surveys are key steps to improving access to quality data and achieving the health-related SDGs.

Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones was fined $250,000 by the NFL for an "inadvertent" obscene gesture toward fans at MetLife Stadium during Dallas' 37-22 victory. Videos showed Jones flashing his middle finger late in the game after a touchdown increased the lead to 37-14. Jones called the gesture "unfortunate" and said it was accidental, claiming he intended a "thumbs up" toward excited Cowboys fans. The Cowboys are likely to appeal but have until Friday to decide. The article notes the NFL has previously fined owners for interactions with fans: Panthers' Tepper was fined $300,000 for throwing a drink toward fans, and Titans owner Bud Adams was fined $250,000 for making an obscene gesture while celebrating a win.
The speaker says tomorrow's game is important but the series is long. They controlled the first two periods but let up in the third, allowing the opponent back, and the power play must score more.

A rare white moose filmed in Sweden has drawn worldwide attention. The BBC reports only about 100 exist there, with white fur from a genetic mutation, not albinism. It is unknown whether the twin white calves are albino or piebald.

Princeton scientists and international collaborators have developed Diag2Diag, an AI tool that generates synthetic, highly detailed data for fusion diagnostics that cannot capture certain plasma measurements, particularly at the plasma edge (pedestal), where stability determines performance. Published in Nature Communications, the research used sensor data from the DIII-D National Fusion Facility. The synthetic data aligns with real-world measurements and is more detailed than actual sensors can provide, potentially making future fusion reactors more compact, affordable, and reliable by reducing reliance on bulky hardware. The tool could also support 24/7 commercial fusion operation and has potential applications in spacecraft and robotic surgery. Diag2Diag additionally provided new evidence supporting the magnetic island theory of edge-localized mode (ELM) suppression, showing simultaneous flattening of temperature and density in the pedestal when resonant magnetic perturbations are applied. Researchers plan to expand the AI's use to other diagnostics and fields where data is missing or limited.

This passage is from the datasheet of the ADS8681W, ADS8685W, and ADS8689W, 16-bit SAR ADC data acquisition devices from Texas Instruments. The devices integrate a high-bandwidth, low-noise ADC driver buffer and operate with either an internal 4.096V reference (factory-trimmed, temperature-compensated from –40°C to +125°C, but subject to output shifts from soldering thermal stress) or an external reference, selected via the INTREF_DIS bit of the RANGE_SEL_REG register. The ADC supports single-ended and differential inputs in bipolar and unipolar ranges with straight-binary output. Alarm features include a user-programmable input alarm with hysteresis and a fixed-threshold AVDD alarm (4.7V low, 5.3V high), with active and tripped flags readable via the ALARM pin, internal registers, or appended to output data. The multiSPI digital interface supports four legacy SPI protocols, dual-SDO mode, source-synchronous (SRC) protocols, and daisy-chain topology for multiple devices. The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states and is programmed through nine configuration registers using 32-bit data transfer frames. Application information describes an eight-channel industrial analog input module using the MUX36D08 multiplexer and NTC thermistor-based temperature sensing with alarm hysteresis. Power recommendations cover supply decoupling and two low-power modes (NAP and power-down), and PCB layout guidelines are provided.

The passage reviews the top 10 AI content generator and writer tools for 2022, describing each tool's features and pricing.
