The Supreme Court declined to hear Ghislaine Maxwell's appeal of her 20-year sentence for sex trafficking of a minor. Maxwell sought review of a 2nd Circuit ruling that a 2007 non-prosecution agreement between Jeffrey Epstein and the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida did not bar charges against her in New York. She argued the agreement's co-conspirators clause, referencing "the United States," bound all districts, and that the ruling deepened a circuit split. Solicitor General D. John Sauer called the clause "highly unusual" and opposed review. The denial was among over 30 pages of denied petitions from the justices' Sept. 29 conference.

The 5-Day Low of The Range Strategy goes long at the close when IBS is below 0.25 and the close is below the lowest low of the previous 5 days, exiting after 5 days. From January 1993 to today, it produced 517 trades with 309 winners and a 0.46% average return per trade, versus 0.11% for any 5-day period. With a 60% win ratio, profitability peaks at 3-7 days, yielding a 10.76% annualized return while in the market 510 days versus 2826 for buy and hold. Performance has weakened lately. Adapted for shorting using 0.75 (or 0.9 for similar fills), it returned almost 10%, though shorts are harder and less profitable.

This study evaluated the MicroGEM Sal6830™ SARS-CoV-2 Saliva Test, the first saliva-based RT-PCR point-of-care (POC) device with emergency use authorization. The test allows patients to self-deposit saliva directly into a sealed cartridge, eliminating operator exposure to biohazards and reducing sample mix-ups. Six non-laboratory trained healthcare workers at two US clinics performed blinded sample testing and a prospective clinical study comparing Sal6830™ to the Cepheid Xpert Xpress CoV-2/Flu/RSV platform. All blinded sample results were concordant with expected results (one positive returned invalid). Clinical performance showed 87.2% positive percent agreement, 97.2% negative percent agreement, and 93.3% overall percent agreement. Usability questionnaires confirmed that healthcare workers found the system easy to use, felt confident operating it, and did not require technical support. The study concluded that Sal6830™ can be used accurately and easily by non-laboratory trained healthcare workers in POC settings.

Origin PC announced a new version of its Eon15-S gaming laptop starting at $999 in the US. It uses Nvidia's GeForce 1050Ti graphics card for good gaming performance at low cost. The base model pairs this GPU with an Intel Core i3 processor and 120GB SSD. Though $100-200 more than Dell's Inspiron 15 7000, it offers an IPS display and 24/7 US-based lifetime support.

NRC is a neural shader that caches and approximates radiance for real-time global illumination and dynamic lighting. It takes path-traced rays after one bounce and infers lighting for many bounces, training on live game data. This reduces GPU load and improves performance and indirect light quality.

This patent application describes a voice-directed inspection system that supports multiple inspectors working simultaneously on the inspection of business assets. The system comprises inspection assistance devices (each including a headset and a portable computer device), a site computer, and a host computer. The site computer receives an inspection plan from the host computer (or creates one locally), and when multiple inspection assistance devices request assignments for the same asset, it determines whether the plan has multiple unfinished sections. If so, it distributes different sections to the requesting devices, which provide audible commands to their inspectors and receive spoken updates as inspection items are completed. Updates are relayed to the site computer and then to the host computer. Sections may be divided by physical parts of the asset, by component systems, or so that inspectors do not overlap or interfere, and may be prioritized or assigned based on request order, inspector qualifications, or prior work on the asset. The application further describes the hardware of computing devices and inspection assistance devices, and an inspection plan editor that lets operators create or modify plans using text-to-speech, speech recognition with adaptive voice templates, transcription of free-form speech, and configurable parameters such as prompts, limits, confirmations, and conditional actions. Flow diagrams illustrate the assignment, inspection, and update process, which enables parallel work on large inspection plans to improve efficiency, training, and allocation of specialized inspectors.

The Supreme Court's *Bruen* decision established a two-step test for Second Amendment challenges: courts first ask whether the Amendment's plain text covers the challenged conduct; if so, the government must show the regulation is consistent with the Nation's historical tradition of firearm regulation. Critics, including Justice Breyer and Judge Carlton Reeves, contend this test burdens judges who lack historians' expertise. The author argues this is the wrong question because judges are lawyers, not historians, and their role differs from historians'. Originalists maintain that legal evidence is durable and that judges must decide cases despite uncertainty. Step one is relatively easy, as precedent has settled the meaning of key terms like "people," "keep," "bear," and "arms." Step two requires historical work, but genuine traditions would be reflected in multiple durable sources, and efforts to compile historical evidence have emerged. When history is uncertain, legal tools such as burdens of proof allow judges to decide cases. The author rejects supplementing history with means-ends scrutiny as involving a legislator's role, and argues the "past is a foreign country" critique of originalism is inapt because the law has a past that must be understood.
Washington's appeal of Nelson's judgment resulted in reversal and remand.

The speaker celebrates winning the Stanley Cup, praising Buffalo as a strong young team. After missing the playoffs last year, he reflects on winning the cup ten years earlier and describes this year's grueling run through adversity and injuries, including Hull playing with a wrist injury. He expresses pride in the veteran team's experience and perseverance.

The lecture introduces a "decision mentality" for analyzing poker: evaluate decisions by expected results rather than actual outcomes, illustrated through a credit card roulette story and the law of large numbers. Three levels of reasoning are presented: (1) my hand versus your hand (soul reads), (2) my hand versus your range of hands (exploitative play), and (3) my range versus your range (optimal play, analogous to Nash equilibrium). Exploitative play builds models of opponents' tendencies but can be counter-exploited; optimal play makes opponents indifferent to their choices and slowly profits from their inconsistencies, as shown through a rock-paper-scissors analogy. A "Who's Taller" game demonstrates why blinds are necessary for poker to function as a game. Key concepts covered include stack size versus effective stack size, position (later positions can attack blinds with weaker hands), and equity—the probability of winning the pot—calculated by counting outs or using tools like PokerStove. Practical advice includes raising rather than calling when first to act, raising to roughly 2.25 big blinds with antes, and going all-in when effective stacks are 12 big blinds or fewer (10 without antes). Conservative opening ranges by position are recommended, from about 6% of hands under the gun to roughly 55% on the button. The lecture concludes with bluffing versus value betting and a live demonstration of an all-in hand using equity calculations.

In the UK, nearly half of women with ovarian cancer are diagnosed only after reaching emergency care, and just one in three cases is identified at the earliest stages. Jo Stanford of Ovarian Cancer Action attributes late diagnosis to difficulties getting timely appointments and symptoms being dismissed by healthcare providers. With no screening test available, awareness is vital: 90% of women don't know the four main symptoms—persistent bloating, difficulty eating or feeling full quickly, needing to urinate more frequently or urgently, and persistent tummy or pelvic pain. Other signs include lower back aches, digestive discomfort, post-menopausal bleeding, and fatigue. Early detection offers a 95% survival rate, compared with 16% at stage four. The charity offers a free online symptom checker and a downloadable symptoms diary. Stanford notes the 'silent killer' label is misleading, since most women diagnosed early experienced symptoms, and stresses that everyone, not just women, should know the signs.

DryShips Inc (NASDAQ:DRYS) filed a 6-K on April 17th detailing common stock issuances under a continuous offering plan. The company raised $14.5 million by issuing 7,912,449 shares at an average price of $1.79, falling short of the $30 million requested from Kalani Investors, the offering agent. This marked the third consecutive failure to fulfill a Fixed Amount Request, with only 48% of requested amounts issued. Equity issuance equaled 8.86% of volume traded for the April 11th–17th period, the weakest showing to date. Shares issued from April 10th through 17th caused 16.8% dilution, leaving 54.92 million shares outstanding. $173.4 million remains to be issued against an equity market capitalization of $106 million at the April 17th close. At the recent pace of roughly $3.2 million per day, completing the offering would take about 54 trading days and require an additional 105.7 million shares. The author expects DRYS to pursue a debt capital raise, after which remaining equity issuance would likely continue.

Hurricane Maria struck Puerto Rico on September 20, 2017, with 155 mph sustained winds, gusts up to 190 mph, and torrential rains causing island-wide floods. It destroyed the electricity grid, leaving 3.4 million inhabitants without power, damaged infrastructure, and caused damages exceeding US $82 billion, including $780 million in agricultural losses. Prior studies of excess deaths from Hurricane Maria had limitations, including restricted time periods, limited causes analyzed, and failure to account for population displacement. This research proposes a semiparametric Poisson regression model to estimate deaths caused by a state of emergency, incorporating intra-annual variability, population displacement, and causes of death including non-communicable diseases. The model uses indicators for pre- and post-emergency periods and causes of death, with interaction terms and a smooth function capturing within-year variation. Coefficients are estimated by penalized likelihood maximization, with smoothing parameters determined by restricted maximum likelihood. Excess deaths by cause during post-emergency periods are estimated through differences between model predictions while accounting for population displacement.

Dylan Drysdale, Tim Loughran, and Garry Cullum won series class titles at the final round of the 2017 Molecule ProKart Series at KartSport Hamilton's Agrisea Raceway. Cullum took the KZ2 Restricted class title for a record fourth time, winning all heats, the Pre-Final, and Final. Drysdale secured the Wifiplus KZ2 title by four points over Aaron Wilson after Mat Kinsman, who won the heats and Pre-Final, crashed in the Final. Loughran won the KZ2 Masters title after points leader Enrico van der Griend crashed in the third heat. Time penalties for kerb hopping affected several drivers, including Madeline Stewart.

NASA's HAMMER spacecraft could deploy a nuclear device to destroy asteroid Bennu, a "potentially hazardous" object with a 1 in 2,700 chance of hitting Earth on September 21, 2135. NASA has monitored Bennu since its 1999 discovery.

Hendrik Bessembinder's 2017 study examined whether stocks outperform Treasury Bills using data from 26,000 shares listed on American stock exchanges between 1926 and 2015. The findings show that most stocks fail to beat one-month Treasury Bills: only 43% of equities produced returns higher than Treasury Bills, and just 86 of 26,000 stocks accounted for half the returns. While the market average has been strong (historically around 10% annual returns), the median stock performed poorly, meaning investors randomly picking individual stocks are likely to select underperformers. An example of an equal-weighted market illustrates this: the average return was 5.11%, but only 5 of 17 stocks contributed positively, giving a 70.6% probability of randomly selecting a negative-return stock. The Valueline geometric index, representing the median stock, has drastically underperformed the S&P 500 since 1990. Thirty stocks, including Exxon, Apple, General Electric, and Microsoft, generated 30% of all returns from 1926 to 2015. A similar study of the Oslo Stock Exchange (1985–2017) found that only 18 large companies—2.7% of IPOs—explained the entire value creation of 2,000 billion NOK, with most shares performing worse than risk-free rates. The conclusion is that only a small proportion of stocks create value; the recommended solutions are buying passive funds or, for individual stock investors, maintaining diversification.

When a player is injured but the referee allows play to continue—due to the advantage rule or not seeing the injury—players may show sportsmanship by kicking the ball out of bounds to stop play. After treatment, the referee restarts with a throw-in to the opposing team, which returns the ball to the team that kicked it out. Neither team may exploit this courtesy; the ball should be passed backward and not challenged until play resumes. A similar courtesy applies to dropped balls after referee-stopped injuries.

The passage discusses intelligent maintenance systems and their integration with e-Business. Predictive maintenance (e-Maintenance) enables near-zero downtime through real-time smart monitoring, shifting focus from fault detection to degradation prediction, and connects via web-enabled agents to e-business tools such as CRM, ERP, and e-commerce systems. E-Maintenance is described as a major pillar supporting e-Manufacturing and e-business integration, with research needs including predictive intelligence, data mining tools, secure informatics platforms, distributed computing, and workforce training.

A reconfigurable maintenance concept is proposed to align production quality with customer requirements, supporting intercompany maintenance cooperation through shared diagnostic knowledge, which improves reconfiguration efficiency and provides data for system reliability and sustainability.

Modular reconfigurable maintenance systems use distributed architectures, remote maintenance via telecommunications networks, and sensor-based monitoring. Maintenance policies should vary with system changes, and expert systems using historical data and knowledge bases are needed to detect abnormalities, identify faults, and enable corrective reconfiguration.

The conclusion states that mass customization and competitive pressures require companies to respond rapidly at minimal cost, making integrated reconfigurable maintenance systems necessary to handle adverse conditions and ensure production reliability.

Teachers' Union of Ireland general secretary John MacGabhann warned teachers that becoming Facebook friends with students is ill advised, as it narrows the necessary professional distance and can lead to professional damage. He also cautioned members about hasty social media comments, noting some had endangered their employment or faced legal issues, and advised pausing before posting and avoiding online feuds. He criticised employers for excessive use of technology and social media that effectively places staff on a 24/7 roster, advising members not to respond to unreasonable contact.

The author admits having given up on the equity market prematurely and questions whether equities could melt up instead. While low VIX levels are typically attributed to complacency and met with caution, the author presents 21 charts suggesting those predicting doom for US equities should reconsider, as market breadth now shows underlying strength. The author discloses long positions in US equities and VIX.

Pledging to execute the laws within the limits of Executive power, he commits to preserving peace and friendship with foreign nations, respecting the powers reserved to the states, and practicing strict economy in managing public revenue to extinguish the national debt and counteract profligacy. He favors equal treatment of agriculture, commerce, and manufactures in impost selection, supports internal improvement and the diffusion of knowledge, and considers standing armies dangerous in peacetime, relying instead on the militia while gradually strengthening the Navy.
