This study examines how the discourses of TRNC Presidents have shaped education policies in Northern Cyprus, framing education as a tool for strengthening social belonging and preserving Turkish Cypriot identity. It traces the historical development of the Turkish Cypriot education system from the Ottoman period, through British colonial rule and the 1960 Republic of Cyprus, to the post-1974 restructuring aligned with Turkey. Education Council decisions are highlighted as key drivers of structural reforms, curriculum regulation, teacher training, and quality improvement. History textbooks have long presented a Turkish identity-centered narrative emphasizing Turkish-Greek conflict and Turkish Cypriot victimization, though reforms since the early 2000s—particularly after the 2004 Annan Plan and EU harmonization—sought more pluralistic, reconciliatory narratives despite political setbacks. Presidential discourses varied by era: Denktaş emphasized national identity and integration with Turkey; Talat focused on EU harmonization; Eroğlu and Tatar stressed cooperation with Turkey; Akıncı promoted multiculturalism and peace. Other policy themes include maintaining Turkish as the medium of instruction, educational cooperation with Turkey, internationalization of higher education, and balancing secularism with religious education. The study concludes that education policies should adopt multi-perspective, scientifically grounded approaches within a long-term strategic framework independent of political leaders' ideologies.

Michael Ben'Ary, an assistant U.S. attorney in the Eastern District of Virginia, was abruptly fired while prosecuting the 2021 Afghanistan airport bombing that killed 13 U.S. service members and 160 Afghan civilians. A letter taped to his door, bearing his typed signature, said a false social media post—by commentator Julie Kelly, who claimed he was an ally of former Deputy Attorney General Lisa Monaco—apparently led to his termination. The letter said DOJ leadership is "more concerned with punishing the president's perceived enemies" than protecting national security, and noted that Ben'Ary's interim boss, Halligan, replaced a U.S. attorney after Trump pressured him to indict James Comey for an alleged false statement to Congress.

The team must prepare for an opponent playing to extend the series, with focus on getting off to a strong start tomorrow. The opponent has been successful at home throughout the playoffs, and failing to start well could result in a rough night.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said India's SCO accession has increased the grouping's political profile and capacity to stabilise Central and South Asia and help resolve the Afghanistan crisis. He called India's independent foreign policy important for global and regional security, said bilateral trade was unsatisfactory with a target of $30 billion by 2025, and noted deepening defence cooperation would increase technology transfer. Lavrov said the US force-based strategy in Afghanistan would not work, denied Russian support to the Taliban, and regretted the US declining the Moscow Process for the Six Plus One group, adding a smaller group including Central Asian countries was needed to resolve Afghanistan's political situation.

Yandex announced it will report its financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2018, on Thursday, July 26, 2018, with a conference call and webcast at 8:00 a.m. U.S. Eastern Time. Dial-in numbers, replay details (available until August 2, 2018), and a webcast link were provided. Yandex is a technology company listed on NASDAQ since 2011.

New England Patriots wide receiver Malcolm Mitchell, who caught six passes for 70 yards in the team's 34-28 Super Bowl comeback win over the Atlanta Falcons, will receive the Promise Hero Award from America's Promise Alliance at its 20th Anniversary Summit and Gala in New York. Mitchell, 23, struggled with reading until college at the University of Georgia, where he taught himself to read starting with children's books. He founded Read with Malcolm, a youth literacy initiative promoting books to students in underserved communities, with goals of introducing book ownership and improving below-average reading skills. He graduated in December 2015 with a communications degree, was drafted by the Patriots, and wrote the book The Magician's Hat. In an interview, he credited his mother, Pratina Woods, advised kids to never give up, and said the award motivates him to expand his literacy advocacy.

This paper presents the design, implementation, and evaluation of a one-day digital accessibility workshop in India, targeting software professionals and computer science educators—a group with limited access to such training. Motivated by low global WCAG compliance, economic losses from inaccessible products, and a lack of accessibility education in the Global South, the authors delivered five instructional modules (basics, design, development, reporting, and teaching accessibility) alongside hands-on activities, tool demonstrations, and thematic booths. Of the 73 participants, feedback was highly positive: 100% would recommend the workshop, 90% found it effective and engaging, and 52% reported a significant shift in their perception of accessibility. Thematic analysis of open-ended responses identified interest in advanced design practices, AI applications, inclusive design for diverse users, organizational strategies, and practice-based learning. The authors recommend distributing pre-workshop materials, customizing content by role, incorporating case studies, encouraging peer learning, and providing continued engagement. They conclude that experiential, informal accessibility education is effective in building capacity and call for sustained efforts to embed accessibility in India's computing education and professional ecosystem.

DA Leader Mmusi Maimane delivered a speech in Parliament during the debate on the State of the Nation Address, arguing that President Zuma's talk of Radical Economic Transformation is a cover for elite self-enrichment. He cited the deaths of 94 Esidimeni mental health patients, the Marikana shootings, and the heavy security presence and violence at the SONA as evidence that the ANC has become "the enemy of the people." He accused the President of 783 counts of corruption and claimed land reform, BEE, the nuclear build, and the MPRDA Bill would benefit ANC cronies. Highlighting youth unemployment, he presented the DA's "Rescue Plan," including education reforms, apprenticeships and internships, labour market reforms, support for small businesses, halting the nuclear deal, partial privatisation of state-owned enterprises, title deeds and land redistribution, 50,000 additional police officers, an alternative health plan, and measures to reduce corruption and the size of the state.

Alexa can assist with cleaning tasks in several ways. The Cleaning Buddy skill helps create cleaning schedules. Voice purchasing can be enabled to order cleaning supplies from Amazon, confirmed with a four-digit code. Robot vacuums like Neato and Roomba can connect to Alexa and be controlled by voice commands for starting, scheduling, pausing, or stopping cleaning. For laundry, the Laundrapp service (available in about 100 US cities) picks up and delivers clothes, while the Good Housekeeping or Stains Be Gone skills provide stain removal advice.

This study investigates topographic defects introduced by electropolishing (EP) on highly polished bulk niobium samples using atomic force microscopy (AFM) and white light interferometry (WLI). Rather than examining defects eliminated from as-received surfaces, the authors started from mechanically polished Nb (initial roughness below 5 nm) and characterized defects created by EP. Measurements revealed that electropolishing produces sharp intergranular sloped steps at grain boundaries, with step heights up to 70 nm and slope angles reaching approximately 50°. Sequential EP experiments showed that a new step forms at each polishing increment while previous steps are smoothed, and that step geometry is primarily controlled by relative grain orientation rather than EP depth. Exposure to EP electrolyte without applied voltage caused only minor step growth, indicating the EP process itself is the primary cause. Using London theory, the authors calculated magnetic field enhancement and superheating field suppression factors for these defects, finding they can substantially degrade the achievable peak magnetic field in SRF cavities. Diffusion simulations further showed that impurity concentration is locally reduced at the bottom of sloped steps—where vortex nucleation is expected—potentially compromising treatments like low-temperature baking and nitrogen infusion. The results indicate that electropolished Nb, despite appearing "mirror-smooth," hosts defects limiting high-field performance, highlighting the need for smoother surfaces to approach the superheating field of niobium.

MIT researchers have developed a refined prime editing system that significantly reduces errors in gene editing. By identifying Cas9 protein mutations that loosen cutting constraints—destabilizing old DNA strands so they degrade—the team lowered error rates, then combined mutations and added an RNA-binding protein to stabilize the RNA template. The resulting editor, called vPE, reduced errors to 1/60th the original rate, from roughly one in seven edits to one in 101 for the most common editing mode, and from one in 122 to one in 543 for a more precise mode. Tests were conducted in mouse and human cells. Led by Vikash Chauhan, with senior authors Phillip Sharp and Robert Langer, the study suggests gene therapy could become safer for treating many genetic diseases. The team is now working on improving efficiency and tissue-specific delivery.

The article examines whether the Supreme Court will overrule Humphrey's Executor, its 1936 precedent allowing Congress to insulate certain agency heads from full presidential control, in the case of President Trump's firing of FTC commissioner Rebecca Kelly Slaughter. The author predicts the court will uphold the firing without overturning the precedent. The 1936 decision arose after President Franklin Roosevelt fired Commissioner William Humphrey without cause, despite a statute permitting removal only for inefficiency, neglect of duty, or malfeasance; the court held the FTC's duties were neither political nor executive. Recent precedent shows the court assesses an agency's actual powers, and it rejected CFPB independence partly because the agency lacked a bipartisan, expert, multi-member structure. The modern FTC, though structurally similar, now acts primarily as an executive law enforcement agency with expanded rulemaking and enforcement powers. The court's order staying rulings that blocked Trump from firing NLRB and MSPB members suggests it views such agencies as exercising considerable executive power. The author expects a "mend it, don't end it" approach that preserves the Federal Reserve's distinct independence, noting the court's rephrased question separates the constitutionality of Slaughter's firing from the precedent's future.

British police declared a major incident after a man and woman in their 40s were found unconscious and hospitalized in critical condition in Amesbury, eight miles from Salisbury, after exposure to an unknown substance. Counterterrorism officers are working with Wiltshire Police. Testing is ongoing to identify the substance, and it is not yet clear whether a crime was committed.

The United States Bankruptcy Court for the Middle District of Florida, Tampa Division, entered judgment in favor of debtor Ambrozy Jerry Fasolak and against plaintiff D.A.N. Joint Venture III, L.P., which had sought denial of the debtor's Chapter 7 discharge. The plaintiff asserted four grounds: fraudulent transfer or concealment of property (§ 727(a)(2)), failure to keep or preserve financial records (§ 727(a)(3)), false oaths (§ 727(a)(4)), and failure to explain a loss of assets (§ 727(a)(5)). The court found that although the debtor had transferred funds to his wife and his schedules contained inaccuracies, the plaintiff failed to prove fraudulent intent, did not identify specific missing records, and did not establish that specific assets were unexplained. The court concluded the inaccuracies resulted from mistake or misunderstanding rather than intent to deceive, and the debtor's discharge was granted.

Horse polo originated in Persia over 20 centuries ago, not Victorian England, and spread through the Middle East, Central Asia, and the Far East. The modern game derives from India, where it was called pulu after the wooden ball. English travelers brought the sport home, and from England it reached the U.S., which now has about 250 clubs in 43 states. The Milwaukee Polo Club, located in Hartland about 26 miles west of Milwaukee, continues polo's local tradition dating to 1923 and has occupied its current site for over 20 years. Thomas Esser, who handles the club's marketing activities, works to counter polo's elitist "Sport of Kings" image, describing the club as "blue collar" with members including nurses, students, bartenders, and retirees. Matches cost $5 (kids free), feature six seven-minute chukkers with a half-time divot stomp, and last about two hours. Games are weather-dependent for safety reasons. Esser emphasizes horse welfare, noting horses are treated as teammates whose work is limited with rest days. The club's summer season opened June 18.

A hockey coach discusses his team's mindset during a playoff series, emphasizing preparation, focus, and execution over momentum. He calls losing devastating because salary cap constraints and injuries make championship opportunities rare. He defends a player's difficult decision to join the team, saying the player performed excellently. He stresses roster depth, crediting farm team development and contributions from players like Helm, Ericsson, Abby, and Leino. The coaching staff will review tapes to find advantageous matchups, noting that starting on time in Pittsburgh improves their chances. He acknowledges early-game breakdowns, turnovers that strengthened the opponent's forecheck, and goaltending that has performed better at home. He reports an injured player is feeling good, praises his goaltender's professional response to adversity, and describes the final as competitive between two strong teams.

A 13-year-old girl is in serious but stable condition after being shot in the thigh while sitting in an open garage in Guildford, Sydney's west, on Tuesday night. Police believe the shooting was not random.

The passage argues that penny stocks are bad investments and should be avoided. Penny stocks, defined by the SEC as any stock below 5 USD, mostly trade over-the-counter (OTC) and on the Pink Sheets rather than formal exchanges like NYSE or Nasdaq, since most companies cannot meet exchange listing requirements. They attract investors dreaming of quick riches, but most traders lose money and become prey for bigger, more informed players and scammers. The main reasons penny stocks are bad include unproven or failing business models, low liquidity resulting in high trading costs (slippage), less regulation and financial disclosure, and exposure to scams such as the "know-it-all" guru scam, pump and dump schemes, and dump and dilute practices. Almost all penny stocks ultimately fail and become worthless. The passage recommends avoiding penny stocks altogether or, at minimum, conducting proper due diligence and understanding the risks before trading them.

Sen. Mark Warner, top Democrat on the Senate Intelligence Committee, says Republicans are engaged in an unprecedented effort to undermine the Mueller investigation and the FBI's integrity. Warner said he and Sen. Richard Burr were blocked from viewing the Nunes memo before its release, and criticized the House Intelligence Committee's party-line vote blocking the Democrats' document as partisan. He stressed the Senate Russia investigation's importance to defending against cyberwarfare threats.

The paper studies many-to-one two-sided matching between participants and teams, focusing on fairness for both sides. While the stability notion of Gale and Shapley, based on justified envy-freeness, ensures fairness among participants, it can leave teams unfairly treated. Igarashi et al. [2024] showed that team-EF1 and participant-justified EF may be incompatible in many-to-one settings. The authors therefore introduce team-justified EF1, a relaxation of team-EF1 that disregards a team's envy toward another team when it arises from participants who strictly prefer the other team.

Under ordinal preferences with ties, two warm-up approaches are presented: a round-robin algorithm restricted to participants who rank the team first (yielding team-justified SD-EF1 and participant-EF, but possibly unbalanced allocations), and an auxiliary one-to-one instance approach (yielding team-justified SD-EF1, participant-justified EF, and balancedness, but not swap stability).

The main algorithm creates team-slots and maintains eligibility sets for participants, iteratively computing matchings that maximize team-slot values in round-robin order, with lexicographic tie-breaking over participant preferences. It runs in polynomial time and returns allocations satisfying team-justified SD-EF1, participant-justified EF, balancedness, and Pareto optimality (and hence swap stability). It generalizes both the round-robin algorithm (when participants are indifferent) and the Gale–Shapley algorithm (under strict preferences).

With augmented tie-breaking, the algorithm is group-strategyproof for participants, proved via blocking paths; it is not strategyproof for teams. The paper further extends the setting to teams with quotas and parties preferring to be unassigned, showing the algorithm yields a mechanism that is simultaneously stable, Pareto optimal, and group-strategyproof for participants, and satisfies extended team-justified SD-EF1.

After ICE detained at least 51 people in the Austin area, Austin ISD lawyers sent a memorandum directing staff not to share unvetted resources with students or discuss political or controversial topics, citing possible scrutiny from state lawmakers. Schools reported student anxiety. Board Vice President Paul Saldana criticized the memo, saying the board was not briefed. Superintendent Paul Cruz posted general resources for immigrant and refugee students, while Education Austin distributed documents about ICE encounters and immigration lawyer names, calling the information informational, not political. The union plans a Wednesday news conference, and the board will discuss the memo.

The passage contrasts the data cultures of digital leaders and digital laggards. Digital laggards prioritize short-term efforts, discourage risk-taking, and exhibit low trust in employees and leadership, while even digital leaders find that instilling a learning mindset requires deliberate, sustained effort rather than a "light switch" change. A pharmaceutical case study shows how a highly regulated company fostered innovation through a localized, controlled experimentation environment, automating compliance checks in a quarter of the previous time.

Digital leaders emphasize transparency, making data widely available across roles, discouraging hoarding, and pairing access with governance controls that build trust. Laggards, by contrast, share data only on a "need-to-know" basis, store it in departmental silos, and favor business judgment and a "culture of genius" over data-driven decisions; 88% of digital leaders have standardized APIs compared with 27% of laggards.

Digital leaders embrace measurement, using data-driven metrics and 360-degree reviews, which provides structure while enabling flexibility, experimentation, and risk-taking; a retail case study illustrates real-time sales reporting enabling faster, data-driven decisions. Laggards set aspirational goals ungrounded in data, leading employees to avoid measurement and focus on process adherence, which stifles innovation.

Digital leaders use transparent, data-driven objectives to align the organization vertically and horizontally around a shared "North Star" vision, developed through combined top-down and bottom-up processes, though they must avoid bogging decisions down in exhaustive analysis. Laggards' goals lack clear strategic connection, causing misalignment.

Overall, digital leaders treat data culture as central, aligning beliefs, values, and daily behaviors, while laggards show misalignment between espoused values and actions. Laggards are not doomed to stall; organizations fit into four patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant—and can take targeted actions to build a strong data culture.

The ATR trailing stop, introduced by J. Welles Wilder, is a technical indicator that helps traders set stop-loss levels based on price volatility measured by the average true range (ATR). It provides a dynamic stop-loss level that adjusts to market conditions, helping traders determine exit points, protect profits, and minimize losses. Calculation involves multiplying the ATR by a multiplier, typically 3.5, and subtracting the result from the previous close for long positions or adding it for short positions. The indicator can be applied to stocks and used for both exit points and entry signals. It signals potential trend reversals when price breaches trailing stop levels, while ATR bands help identify breakouts and gauge volatility. Risks include that it does not account for past performance and price movements, so traders should incorporate other technical and fundamental analyses.

The speaker marks a century of national life, recalling that the weak Articles of Confederation were replaced by a National Union founded on the people's will. Under the Constitution, twenty-five States have been added, territory and population have vastly grown, and the civil war settled the supremacy of the Union and its laws. The elevation of the negro race from slavery to full citizenship is called the most important political change since 1787, bringing moral and industrial gains despite disturbance in Southern communities; the emancipated race is promised full and equal protection. Denying the ballot is condemned as a crime that could destroy the Government, while voter ignorance and rising illiteracy are identified as dangers to be met through universal education, with the whole nation responsible. The speaker urges leaving settled controversies behind and pursuing reconciliation and peace. Prosperity is credited partly to restored public credit and specie payments. He favors a monetary system based on gold and silver, redemption of paper notes in coin, and refunding the debt at lower interest. He calls for attention to agriculture, manufacturers, and transportation, and for American supervision of any interoceanic canal. He condemns polygamy and obstruction of law in the Territories, proposes civil service reform, and pledges economy, law enforcement, and honest service, closing with an appeal for support and divine blessing.

Harvard University's first female president, Drew Faust, announced she will step down on June 30, 2018, after 11 years, coinciding with the conclusion of Harvard's fundraising campaign. Hired in 2007 after serving as dean of the Radcliffe Institute, she succeeded Lawrence Summers and was credited with restoring campus trust, fostering collaboration, expanding financial aid, and raising $8 billion. Her tenure also faced controversies, including backlash over cracking down on all-male social clubs and suspending the men's soccer team. A search committee will be assembled to find her replacement.

Texas A&M has had at least one first-round NFL draft pick every year since 2011, and receiver Christian Kirk, who bypassed his senior season, is the Aggies' best hope of extending that streak. Kirk projects as a fringe first-round pick, ranked by USA Today as the draft's fourth-best receiver. Safety Armani Watts forecasts as a mid-round choice, with receiver Damion Ratley a possible late-round pick. Defensive tackle Zaycoven Henderson's draft stock dropped after a December arrest. Von Miller began the first-round streak in 2011, followed by picks including Ryan Tannehill, Luke Joeckel, Jake Matthews, Mike Evans, Johnny Manziel, and Myles Garrett, the program's only No. 1 overall selection.

Michigan State Superintendent Michael Rice is retiring Friday after serving as the state's top education leader since 2019. Glenn Maleyko, current Dearborn Public Schools superintendent, will succeed him, with Sue Carnell serving as interim until then. Rice's tenure coincided with pandemic-related setbacks, including lower test scores, increased chronic absenteeism, and the state's worst third-grade reading scores in the exam's 11-year history. In a Chalkbeat interview, Rice highlighted four key issues: state law allows schools to count up to seven professional development days and 15 virtual learning days as instructional days, potentially reducing instruction below the required 180 days; Michigan has made progress on some goals, including a record 82% graduation rate and expanded preschool enrollment, though none of its eight strategic goals have been fully achieved; Michigan could learn from Mississippi's fourth-grade reading gains, which followed mandatory science-of-reading teacher training; and teacher shortages are improving, with the number of people preparing for the profession rising from 9,500 in 2017 to 18,000 annually.

Alphabet will pay $24.5 million to settle Donald Trump's lawsuit against YouTube over his suspension following the January 6, 2021 Capitol riot, with $22 million going to Trump and $2.5 million to co-plaintiffs. Trump sued YouTube, Twitter (now X), and Meta in July 2021, alleging free speech violations. YouTube suspended his account six days after the riot and lifted restrictions in March 2023. Trump directed his $22 million to the Trust for the National Mall for White House ballroom construction. Alphabet admitted no liability or fault. Trump has received over $57 million in related settlements.

Peter Lynch was a renowned money manager who led Fidelity's Magellan Fund from 1977 to 1990, achieving 29.2% annual returns—more than double the S&P 500's performance. Born in 1944 in Boston, Lynch gained early exposure to investing while working as a golf caddy at an elite club where he served corporate executives, including Fidelity's George Sullivan. After buying his first stock in 1963 and interning at Fidelity in 1966, he joined the firm as an analyst in 1969 and took over the Magellan Fund in 1977. Under his management, the fund grew from $20 million to $14 billion, increasing more than twentyfold.

Lynch's philosophy centered on "invest in what you know" and finding "ten baggers." He avoided market predictions and short-term price fluctuations, focusing instead on fundamental analysis and undervalued companies overlooked by large investors. He categorized companies into six groups: slow-growing, moderately growing, fast-growing, cyclical, turnarounds (crisis recovery), and those with undervalued assets. His portfolio typically held 30-40% growth stocks, 10-20% moderately growing companies, 10-20% cyclicals, and the remainder in turnarounds, plus 1% spread across 500 minor potential companies. He reviewed holdings quarterly, never held cash, and sold stocks when prices rose without fundamental support or when fundamentals deteriorated. He advocated buying quality stocks after significant price drops, viewing a 25% decline as a buy signal rather than a sell signal.

George Afriyie, Vice President of the Ghana Football Association, has been relieved of his duties following an Executive Committee meeting, weeks after announcing his intention to contest the 2019 GFA polls. His removal follows a long-rumoured rift with GFA boss Kwesi Nyantakyi, which began when Afriyie described Nyantakyi as greedy over financial disagreements. Though Afriyie had denied being at loggerheads with Nyantakyi, the sacking validates those rumours, and he is expected to challenge for power. History is against him: previous vice presidents Fred Pappoe (2011) and Fred Crentsil (2015) were also sidelined. The Executive Committee had grown divided, with some members backing Afriyie and others supporting Nyantakyi. Afriyie was earlier removed as head of the Black Stars Management Committee, a role he held since 2014, and colleagues including Winfred Osei, who replaced him, publicly criticized him. With uncertainty over whether Nyantakyi, in charge since late 2005, will seek re-election in 2019, the sacking has emboldened opinions that he must do so to protect his legacy.

An email from Nikita Varma containing Enron India Newsdesk newsclips from June 8, 2001, covers the Dabhol Power Company (DPC) crisis. Following a three-day lenders' meeting in Singapore, Indian and foreign lenders appointed consultants Stone & Webster to evaluate the cost of suspending the 2,184-MW project's second phase, which is 92% complete with over $1,570 million invested. Enron India managing director K Wade Cline suggested a temporary suspension, and lenders proposed closing the plant for a year to address tariff issues; Phase II's launch was postponed pending resolution of the rescinded power purchase agreement (PPA). DPC indicated willingness to reduce its rate of return from 16% to 11%, and Enron sought assurance that all Phase I power would be purchased. The Godbole renegotiation panel held that DPC's return on equity should not exceed 16% and accused DPC of doublespeak. DPC petitioned the Bombay High Court to stay a MERC order restraining it from reactivating the escrow account and pursuing arbitration, arguing MERC lacks jurisdiction, and also opposed public hearings. Lenders formed a committee led by IDBI to negotiate with MSEB, which defaulted on $48 million in payments and stopped buying power. Private producers welcomed PM Vajpayee's optimism about a resolution, though lenders were disappointed by his statement. The Centre's plan to sell DPC power to other states was considered unworkable, as states cannot afford tariffs above Rs 3 per unit. Medha Patkar demanded a judicial inquiry into the deal.

Scientists recommend listing cheetahs as Endangered on the International Union for Conservation of Nature list, citing low southern Africa population estimates; cheetahs have disappeared from 91 percent of their historic range.

This study models and forecasts Aedes invasive mosquito abundance in the Basque Country, Spain—a non-endemic region with no recorded autochthonous Aedes-borne disease cases—using ovitrap egg counts and climate data. Motivated by rising imported dengue, chikungunya, and Zika cases and increasing Aedes albopictus eggs and Aedes japonicus establishment in the region, the authors analyzed egg counts from ovitraps (2013–2023) across three provinces alongside meteorological data (temperature, humidity, precipitation; 2016–2023) from Euskalmet. Araba was excluded due to sparse egg data, leaving Gipuzkoa and Bizkaia for analysis.

After pre-processing (biweekly aggregation, zero imputation, selection of the 20 highest egg counts per province, and smoothing with a moving average), several models were compared with and without lagged variables: Generalized Linear Model with Gaussian distribution (GLMG), SARIMAX, Random Forest (RF), and Conditional Inference Trees (CT). Exploratory analysis found a strong monotonic correlation between egg counts and temperature (Spearman ≥0.72 in both provinces), highest at a two-week lag; humidity showed a positive intermediate correlation, and precipitation a low negative correlation at a ten-week lag. Including lagged versions of variables improved most models' performance.

RF performed best on training data (R² = 0.98 in both provinces) but showed possible overfitting; GLMG performed best on test data (R² = 0.85 for Gipuzkoa, 0.81 for Bizkaia), followed by SARIMAX, while CT performed worst. Poor Bizkaia test performance was attributed to unusually high 2023 egg counts relative to training data. Using the best-performing models with extended training data, 2024 forecasts suggest mosquito abundance will be lower than the previous year at provincial and municipal levels.

The authors conclude that temperature is the most influential climate factor, egg abundance is a key predictor, and continuous entomological surveillance is essential for accurate forecasting and for informing public health strategies against mosquito-borne diseases in non-endemic regions. Limitations include micro-climatic variation within provinces, and future work should consider finer temporal resolution and improved train-test partitioning.

The author, who graduated college eight years ago, reflects on their experience, recognizing what they did right and wrong. They loved college but regrets not taking advantage of opportunities or realizing how much time they had for adventure. While noting everyone's experience differs, they met exceptional people and enjoyed their classes, but will focus on their mistakes.

HPBOSE declared the HP Board Class 12 Result 2018 on April 24 at 14:07 pm on hpbose.org. Class 12 exams were held March 6–29. Results are also available on examresults.net, indiaresults.com, and via SMS by sending HP12ROLLNUMBER to 56263.

Seven more candidates qualified Feb. 14 to replace U.S. Rep. Tom Price in the 6th Congressional District, bringing the field to 15. Price was nominated as Health and Human Services secretary. The special election is April 18, with a likely runoff June 20.

Liverpool open the 2017/18 Premier League season away at Watford on August 12. Key fixtures include Everton, Manchester United, Swansea on Boxing Day, Chelsea, and a final home match against Brighton.

A UK study published in Thorax found that lung cancer screening via CT scan may increase quit rates among smokers already motivated to stop. Researchers sent questionnaires to nearly 2.5 million British residents aged 50–75, identifying 8,729 people at high risk for lung cancer. Eligible smokers were invited to CT screening or not, with all receiving cessation materials. At follow-up, 10 percent of screened participants had quit at two weeks and 15 percent at two years, versus 5 percent among those not invited. Authors note participants were self-selected and conclude screening offers a "teachable moment" for cessation.

A hockey coach addresses reporters before an upcoming Stanley Cup Final game. He says four games in the series were closely contested and two were one-sided, with momentum swinging between teams, and praises his team's will through a playoff run marked by injuries. Having won before, he feels differently this time, citing Scotty Bowman's approach of treating the final like a regular game, and calls it exciting to now control a lifelong dream. He values Original Six traditions such as Mr. Lindsay attending meetings and visits from Gordie and Steve, notes Pittsburgh's similar bond with Mario, credits Igor Larionov for his team's power play breakout, and says the team borrows "Nickisms" from great players. He describes being far more comfortable at home in the playoffs and recalls his team becoming paralyzed after the opponent scored the last time he was in this situation. He calls the Stanley Cup the greatest prize in hockey, stresses enjoying the current opportunity, and praises the head-to-head battles in the series, including goaltenders Fleury and Ozzie. He notes Rafalski shared thoughts with the team that morning, describes Detroit fans' passion for hockey amid local economic hardship, and says Hossa need only do his part rather than worry about who scores. He also recalls Rafalski telling him, laughing, that his team was once outcoached, while calling Rafalski a really good player on an impressive back end.

The Geminid meteor shower peaks Wednesday night, possibly one of the year's best. Best viewing is midnight to 4 a.m. Thursday, with up to 50 meteors visible. Named for the Gemini constellation, it occurs when Earth passes through asteroid Phaethon's debris.

Northwestern basketball is nearing its first NCAA tournament bid after a 66-59 upset over Wisconsin, but coach Chris Collins and players Bryant McIntosh and Vic Law stress staying focused amid growing media attention. The Wildcats host Maryland next, remaining shorthanded as Scottie Lindsey misses a fourth straight game with mono.

Valmet Oyj's Board of Directors has decided on a new long-term share-based incentive plan for key employees, comprising discretionary periods for 2018, 2019 and 2020. The 2018 reward is based on Comparable EBITA margin and orders received growth of the Services and Automation business lines, and will be paid partly in shares and partly in cash in 2019. The plan covers approximately 120 participants, with total rewards capped at around 586,000 shares. Rewarded shares cannot be transferred during a two-year restriction period, and Executive Team members are recommended to hold shares equal to their gross annual base salary.

An American Airlines Net SAAver Fares promotional email sent to Theresa Staab at Enron on November 19, 2001, advertising weekend getaway fares. Domestic fares are valid for departures November 30 – December 1, 2001, and international fares for November 29–30, with tickets to be purchased by Friday, November 23, 2001. The email lists roundtrip domestic fares ranging from $69 to $312 (e.g., Abilene to Dallas/Ft. Worth at $69; Kona to Los Angeles at $312) and international fares from $59 to $519 (e.g., Fort Lauderdale to Nassau at $59; New York to Sao Paulo at $519), with some routes partly served by American Eagle. It also promotes a Thanksgiving sale requiring purchase by November 21, AAdvantage Net SAAver Awards starting at 4,000 miles plus cash amounts, and vacation offers from AA Vacations, Fairmont Hotels, Starwood Hotels, and Hertz. Fares exclude certain taxes and fees, are nonrefundable, and seats are limited. Booking is available at www.aa.com/netsaaver, and the email includes unsubscribe instructions.

A U.S. study of 202 daycare staff in Illinois found sun safety ranked low among health teaching priorities, with nutrition, exercise, and teeth brushing ranked highest. Fewer than one in five respondents listed sun protection as a top priority. About half of programs provided sunscreen, but 77% didn't allow children to apply it themselves, possibly influenced by state regulations for older students. Many programs used spray sunscreen to avoid touching children, though some sprayed it directly on faces. Researchers note the study's limitation to Illinois and emphasize the need for greater sun safety education among teachers and parents.

A federal jury in Denver found Monday that radio host David Mueller assaulted and battered Taylor Swift by groping her during a 2013 preconcert photo session. Mueller had sued Swift in 2015, claiming her accusation was false and led to his firing from radio station KYGO; Swift countersued with the assault and battery claim. The jury awarded Swift the $1 in compensation she had demanded, which her lawyer described as symbolically significant. Swift also announced she would donate to organizations helping sexual assault victims. The jury additionally found that Swift's mother and a member of her management team had not interfered with Mueller's contract to get him fired. Swift had been dropped from Mueller's suit after a judge ruled there was insufficient evidence she fabricated the encounter. Mueller had sought about $260,000 in lost wages.

Lawyer Angela B. Ryan recounts that during three pregnancies over less than four years—27 months total practicing law while pregnant—her body became subject to public commentary and unwanted touching in court, including opposing counsel stroking her belly in front of a judge. She argues such acts, often euphemized as "the Rub," constitute assault and harassment, noting that the Pregnancy Discrimination Act of 1978 and EEOC guidance address pregnancy-based harassment, though the practice is rarely confronted. She calls for explicit policies, training, and cultural change in the legal profession requiring consent before touching pregnant individuals.

Caltech and six other institutions received $4.9 million from the USGS to develop the ShakeAlert earthquake-warning system, giving West Coast residents seconds of advance warning. Nearly defunded this year, it received $10.2 million after legislators' outcry; completion requires an estimated $38.3 million plus $16.1 million annually.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth summoned hundreds of generals and admirals from across the globe, arguing for shaking up a military he said had gone soft and "woke."

The team has played better recently, managing the puck well and keeping it away from Brodeur. Having won two straight, they are confident but not cocky and are focused only on Thursday's game as the most important one. They hold the best road record in the playoffs and see no home-road issue. A six-hour flight is tough but affects both teams equally. The team is in good spirits after holding serve at home. The goaltender has been fantastic all playoffs, winning games single-handedly. A ten-day layoff hurt timing but not conditioning. Both teams are comfortable with their matchups, feel confident in overtime, are strong defensively, and have shown they can come back after conceding first.

The passage, from the SD Memory Card Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00, covers card write, erase, protection, and command functions. ACMD23 (pre-erase) lets the host specify the number of write blocks before a Multiple Block Write to speed up the operation; the count resets to 1 afterward and should be sent just before the write command. Erase operations use ERASE_WR_BLK_START (CMD32), ERASE_WR_BLK_END (CMD33), and ERASE (CMD38); out-of-sequence commands set ERASE_SEQ_ERROR or ERASE_RESET status bits, and write-protected sectors are skipped with WP_ERASE_SKIP set. DISCARD (CMD38 argument 00000001h) de-allocates blocks whose contents become "don't care," while FULE (CMD38 argument 00000002h) logically erases the entire user area; both are supported only on SDHC/SDXC cards, not via SPI, with busy timeouts of 250ms and 1 second respectively.

Three write protection methods exist: a mechanical switch (host responsibility), card internal write protection, and password lock. Password protection uses non-volatile 128-bit PWD and 8-bit PWD_LEN registers; locked cards respond only to basic command class commands, ACMD41, CMD16, and lock commands. CMD42 handles lock/unlock operations (SET_PWD, CLR_PWD, LOCK, UNLOCK, Force Erase). Card Ownership Protection (COP) adds FEP (Force Erase Password) registers; when FEP is set, COP cards require CMD42[1Fh] (COP Unlock) after power-on, Force Erase and Clear PWD are disabled, and FEP Force Erase requires the FEP password.

Application-specific commands are invoked via CMD55 (APP_CMD); undefined ACMDs are treated as regular commands. CMD6 (Switch Function) supports six function groups (Access Mode, Command System, Driver Strength, Power Limit, and others) with Mode 0 (check) and Mode 1 (set) operations, returning a 512-bit status block. High-Speed mode (25 MB/sec at 50 MHz) is enabled via CMD6. CMD8 verifies supply voltage compatibility for Version 2.00+ cards. SDSC cards use byte addressing while SDHC/SDXC use fixed 512-byte block addressing.

The host may stop the clock but must provide 8 clock cycles after transactions. CRC7 protects commands and responses; CRC16 protects data blocks. Read timeout is 100ms; write busy is up to 250ms (up to 500ms for SDXC in certain cases). Commands are 48 bits, consisting of a start bit, direction bit, command index, 32-bit argument, CRC7, and end bit. Commands are grouped into classes recorded in the CSD's CCC field; classes 0, 2, 4, 5, and 8 are mandatory. Response types include R1 (48-bit), R1b, R2 (136-bit CID/CSD), R3, and R6.

On Christmas Eve 2012, Commander Chris Hadfield floated through the International Space Station, playing Santa by hiding cards from crew families for the other five astronauts to find. Because crumbs can clog ventilation filters in microgravity, his crew ate a dense, non-crumbly fruitcake made by Trappist Monks in the Ozarks, along with ready-to-eat turkey, a two-foot artificial tree velcroed to a wall, and personalized stockings. Hadfield's American and Russian crewmates celebrated holidays from their respective cultures, and he considered maintaining traditions vital to psychological health. Now home, Hadfield is bringing this cross-cultural perspective to his science-based variety show, Generator, premiering in Toronto in January.

A100 provides 1.5x the L1 cache and shared memory per SM versus V100, 40 GB HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache with 2.3x read bandwidth, L2 residency controls, and Compute Data Compression.

In this negligence action, the plaintiff was injured when a splinter from the worn, uneven "sliding floor" of the defendant's bowling alley entered his finger as he delivered a bowl with his hand close to the floor. The jury returned a verdict for the plaintiff for $750. The court held the evidence warranted a finding that the proprietor was negligent in failing to keep the premises reasonably safe, including failing to plane the worn approach as was customary. There was no evidence that the plaintiff's manner of delivery was unusual or that he observed the splinter beforehand, so contributory negligence could not be ruled as a matter of law. The refusal of the defendant's requested instructions was proper, as they addressed factual questions for the jury. Judgment was entered for the plaintiff.

Polling began Wednesday for 69 of Uttarakhand's 70 assembly seats amid tight security, with Karnaprayag polling rescheduled to March 9 after BSP candidate Kuldeep Singh Kanwasi's road accident death. Over 74 lakh voters will decide among 628 candidates.

Samsung announced three new water- and dust-resistant Galaxy A smartphones—the A3, A5, and A7—its first product unveiling since the Galaxy Note 7. Launching in Russia later this month, the devices feature a 16-megapixel camera and differ by screen size, but have less processing power than Galaxy S phones. Pricing has not been announced.

Only the Secretary of State may issue passports in the United States; applicants abroad apply to diplomatic representatives, consuls-general, or consuls, and those in insular possessions apply to the chief executive. Passports are denied to persons not owing allegiance to the United States, including declarants of intention. Applications must be written affidavits to the Secretary of State, attested by an officer authorized to administer oaths, stating birth date and place, occupation, residence, intent to return, and an oath of allegiance, accompanied by a physical description and a credible witness's certificate. Native citizens need only this information. Persons born abroad to native-citizen fathers must show the father's citizenship. Naturalized citizens must submit their naturalization certificates and details of emigration, naturalization, and residence. Unmarried women must state they have never married; wives or widows of naturalized citizens must provide the husband's certificate and related facts. Children of naturalized citizens must submit the parent's certificate. Residents of insular possessions must affirm sole allegiance to the United States, supported by two witnesses.

Parents of Camp Mystic campers who died in the July 4 Kerr County floods along the Guadalupe River — which killed 25 campers, two counselors, and the camp's director, with one camper still missing — advocated for camp safety legislation. Led by families including Matthew and Wendie Childress, whose 18-year-old daughter Chloe was a counselor who died, and Blake Bonner, whose 9-year-old daughter Lila died, the parents worked with lobbyists, testified before legislators, and met with Gov. Greg Abbott, House Speaker Dustin Burrows, and Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick. The resulting bills, House Bill 1 and Senate Bill 1, require camps to move overnight cabins out of floodplains, monitor weather warnings with radios, install alert systems, and train staff on emergency plans. Abbott signed the bills on Sept. 5. The parents believe these measures could have saved their children, though they continue to grieve.
China launched a talent visa program Wednesday to attract young professionals and science and technology graduates, coinciding with the US's $100,000 H-1B fee. The move drew xenophobic backlash.

The passage addresses two questions: how AI will transform social science research, and how AI governance should evolve. Social science has historically sought empirically falsifiable laws of human behavior, an approach criticized by interpretivists for oversimplifying human interaction. Computational social science emerged with large-scale behavioral data, and LLMs—described as a "blurry JPEG of the web"—offer new opportunities. LLMs can synthesize research data by simulating demographic groups through role-playing, though concerns remain about accuracy, biases such as underrepresenting minority opinions, and oversimplified stereotypes; incorporating in-depth interviews may improve authenticity. LLMs also show zero-shot capabilities in tasks like stance detection and sentiment analysis, but raise ethical challenges such as misinformation generation; model alignment and watermarking may help, though responsible use requires multidisciplinary expertise and societal engagement. LLMs may also contribute to generating novel social theories, but concerns about originality and validity point to the need for human-AI collaboration.

On governance, generative AI poses challenges including misinformation, deepfakes, and bias amplification. The EU, US, and China have introduced regulations, and companies have published AI principles. Remaining challenges include industry-government communication gaps, lack of international consensus, and risks like jailbreaking discovered only in practice. The authors call for top-down partnerships among industry, academia, and policymakers, forward-looking regulation, and bottom-up mechanisms for transparently reporting and addressing issues. The remainder of the passage consists of references and acknowledgments for this whitepaper by Microsoft Research Asia's Societal AI team and collaborators.

This TMS320DM814x DaVinci Digital Media Processors documentation references System MMU details in the Technical Reference Manual (SPRUGZ8) and notes that the L4 Fast and L4 Slow Peripheral Domain memory maps appear in Tables 3-5 and 3-6; regions decoded internally by the Cortex-A8 Subsystem are not physically part of the L4 Slow and are reserved for other masters. The TILER provides an additional 4-GB addressing range, enabled by a 33rd address bit, for accessing frame buffers in rotated and mirrored views; this range is accessible only to the HDVPSS and ISS subsystems, while other masters can access single views through the 512-MB TILER region. Figures 4-1 through 4-8 show bottom-view package pin assignments. Terminal functions tables identify signal names, pin multiplexing, ball numbers, package designators, pin types, internal pullup/pulldown settings, supply voltage, and pin functions, including PINCNTLx registers, de-selected input states, and Multi-Muxed options. Boot configuration pins (e.g., GPMC signals) are multiplexed with ARM Cortex-A8 boot mode functions, with BTMODE bits sampled at reset.

This study analysed cross-sectional data from the COVID-PCD cohort study (747 participants with primary ciliary dyskinesia from 49 countries) to examine which diagnostic tests were used worldwide, how well patients recalled them, and factors associated with testing. Most participants (92%) reported diagnostic testing: biopsy in 75%, genetic testing in 58%, and nasal nitric oxide measurement in 49% of those aged five or older. Test use varied widely between countries; biopsy was most common overall, except in North America and France where genetic testing dominated. Recall of tests also varied between countries and was poorest in Switzerland; only one-third of participants over age five reported having all three tests. In multivariable regression, diagnosis after 2010 was associated with more reported testing, while situs abnormalities were associated with fewer tests; age at diagnosis showed no association. The authors conclude that PCD diagnostics differ markedly worldwide, many people have incomplete diagnostic work-up, and those diagnosed long ago or with situs abnormalities may benefit from supplementary testing, particularly as personalized treatments are developed.

The Third Circuit vacated a district court order denying Prava Chatterjee's petition to set aside the settlement and release of her deceased son's maritime wrongful death claim, arising from the January 31, 1975 collision of the S.S. Edgar M. Queeny and S.S. Corinthos in the Delaware River, and remanded for further proceedings. Chatterjee, a resident of Bangladesh, alleged that her son-in-law, Anil Ranjan Ghosal, forged a special power of attorney and fraudulently settled her claim for $87,000 without her authorization or knowledge. The court held that Indian law governs the validity of the power of attorney, while federal maritime law governs the validity of the release. Applying Garrett v. Moore-McCormack, it held that shipowners bear the burden of proving that a release executed by a seaman's surviving family members was made freely, without deception or coercion, and with full understanding of rights. Although the exclusion of prior Calcutta Commission testimony was not an abuse of discretion, the denial of a new commission in India constituted a gross abuse of discretion depriving Chatterjee of due process. The district court was directed to invoke a commission to take testimony in India.

Halliburton reported first-quarter net income of $46 million, or 5 cents per share, after a year-earlier loss. Adjusted earnings of 41 cents per share met analyst expectations, while revenue of $5.74 billion missed forecasts.

August entry data shows 19 percent fewer international students arrived in the U.S. than in August 2024, according to the National Travel and Tourism Office, aligning with enrollment decline predictions but contradicting SEVIS data showing a 0.8 percent increase. Experts note the arrivals figure excludes continuing students and September entrants, and the State Department has not released visa-issuance data. NAFSA criticized the SEVIS data as likely inaccurate, while Boston College professor Chris Glass suggested the sector may have overestimated the impact of Trump administration policies. Declines were steepest among students from Africa, Asia, and the Middle East, with Iran, Syria, Haiti, Ghana, Nigeria, and India showing the largest drops. Experts warn total declines could exceed 20 percent, with larger losses possible in 2026; more definitive data is expected in November from the Institute of International Education.

NAFTA has driven Canada's economic growth and transformed its manufacturing sector, and securing a modernized agreement should be the federal government's top priority. However, ongoing renegotiations highlight that Canada does not export enough outside North America. Despite having 14 free-trade agreements, including CETA and the CPTPP, exports to most of these markets have not expanded since signing. The author proposes a five-part plan: reform Canada's tax and regulatory environment to improve competitiveness; ensure FTAs address non-tariff barriers such as subsidies and currency manipulation; prioritize trade partners with natural business ties rather than political expedience; leverage existing integrated supply chains, since roughly 85 percent of value-added exports are production parts; and support small and medium enterprises' global expansion by consolidating export-support programs. Structural changes are needed now, given the uncertainty surrounding NAFTA renegotiations.

A federal judge, Reed O'Connor, rejected an effort to overturn the Biden-era gainful-employment rule, siding with the Education Department on every point. The rule requires for-profit and nondegree programs to prove graduates can afford loan payments and earn more than high school graduates; those failing two consecutive years could lose federal aid. Trump officials urged the judge to keep the rules. Industry representative Jason Altmire looks forward to revisiting the rule during rule-making; Dan Zibel of Student Defense applauded the ruling.

In this address to Congress, the speaker reports on his return from the Crimea (Yalta) Conference, stating that lasting results depend on Congressional and public support for the conference's conclusions. The conference had two purposes: defeating Germany quickly with minimal Allied losses, and building foundations for lasting international peace. Concrete outcomes included agreements to hold meetings of the three powers' foreign ministers every three to four months; plans for the occupation and control of Germany; resolution of remaining differences from the Dumbarton Oaks Conference regarding Security Council voting procedures; and settlements concerning liberated areas, Poland, and Yugoslavia. Unanimous agreement was reached on all points. Military arrangements provided for daily coordination between Allied forces on the western and eastern fronts. Unconditional surrender for Germany was defined as occupation by four zones under a Control Council in Berlin, the end of Nazism, disarmament, and reparations in kind rather than money. The speaker describes the destruction he witnessed at Yalta and Sevastopol. A conference of the United Nations at San Francisco on April 25, 1945, is expected to produce a charter for an international security organization, requiring Senate approval, with a bipartisan American delegation attending. The three powers agreed on joint responsibility for liberated areas, including reorganizing Poland's government on a broader democratic basis with free elections and a boundary compromise along the Curzon Line. France was invited to occupy a zone in Germany and serve as a permanent member of the Security Council. The speaker notes that the war against Japan will require a long struggle and Japan's unconditional surrender, describes meetings with King Farouk, Emperor Haile Selassie, and King Ibn Saud, and concludes that the conference presents a choice between world collaboration and another world conflict.

The speaker says a player probably won't play and won't reveal his status for tomorrow, noting replays were deemed inconclusive. He sees no fatigue factor, says venue hasn't greatly impacted the team though distractions affected top players, and remains confident. The last two games went to overtime.

Pokémon GO's fire and ice-themed Solstice Event offers triple XP for catches, accurate throws, curveballs, and first throws; combined with discounted Lucky Eggs, this yields six times the XP for catch-related actions. The author appreciates that the event rewards throwing skill rather than evolution, which receives no bonus. While hardcore players past level 30 won't benefit, the bonuses help casual and midcore players prepare for upcoming gym system changes.

Theresa May faces pressure from Conservative Brexiteers ahead of a Friday cabinet meeting at Chequers. MP Andrea Jenkyns, who resigned as a ministerial aide, warned failing to deliver Brexit would be "catastrophic" for the Tories, while Jacob Rees-Mogg said Leave-supporting MPs could revolt if May compromises on leaving the single market and customs union. Brexiteers fear a "soft Brexit" would keep Britain aligned to EU rules, while Remain-supporting MPs argue pragmatism is needed to avoid business disruption and border problems. Environment Secretary Michael Gove expressed confidence May would not compromise and the cabinet would unite, playing down suggestions of pro-Brexit resignations.

A Delhi court deferred to July 6 the hearing on the ED chargesheet against Karti Chidambaram and two companies in the Aircel-Maxis money laundering case. The June 13 chargesheet under PMLA, 2002 named Karti, ASCPL and CMSPL, alleging Maxis invested Rs 3,565.91 crore as FDI, exceeding the Finance Minister's Rs 600 crore approval limit. Karti has interim protection from arrest till July 10. A special court dropped charges against Dayanidhi Maran and others for lack of evidence. Karti is also accused in the INX Media case.

The S&P 500 has nearly quadrupled from its post-crisis lows, but market conditions have shifted in recent months. The index has gone more than 60 trading days without a new all-time high, its longest such streak since 2015-2016. Unlike past periods of volatility, the Federal Reserve is no longer offering reassurance, having raised rates once in 2018 with further increases expected, while global central bank policies are becoming increasingly disconnected. Despite strong projected earnings growth from corporate tax cuts, investors have grown unsettled. Volatility has risen: after trading below 10 for much of 2017, the VIX spiked in early February and has remained elevated above 15, a pattern last seen in 2006-2007 before the financial crisis. In 2017, only 8 of 251 trading days saw moves exceeding 1%, but in 2018, 31 of 79 days have, placing the year among the most volatile since World War II. The author suggests this may foreshadow a bull market top, expects volatility to persist or increase through 2018 and 2019, and advises investors to identify risks that the broader market is not yet seeing.

The passage describes the Bogleheads 3 and 4 Fund Portfolios, low-cost, diversified investment strategies based on Jack Bogle's philosophy of buying and holding index funds. The 3 Fund Portfolio consists of a U.S. Total Stock Market Index Fund, an International Stock Market Index Fund, and a U.S. Total Bond Market Index Fund; the 4 Fund Portfolio adds a Total International Bond Market Index Fund. The article's sample allocations are 50% U.S. stocks, 30% international stocks, and 20% bonds for the 3 Fund version, and 50/30/10/10 for the 4 Fund version, using funds such as VTI, VEU, BND, and IXUS. Backtests showed annual returns of 7.6% (max drawdown 28%) for the 3 Fund Portfolio and 7.8% (max drawdown 31%) for the 4 Fund Portfolio. The 4 Fund Portfolio may better suit global investors due to its international bond exposure, though market conditions and interest rate changes affect both portfolios' performance.

This broadcast announces the mobilization of a national organization, led by Walter Gifford, to coordinate relief for citizens facing unemployment and privation during the coming winter, a crisis deepened by events abroad. Over a thousand towns and cities have organized relief committees, and a nationwide movement begins to raise funds for them, providing both work and direct assistance, along with health and character-building measures. The Federal Government is aiding through expanded public works supporting nearly 700,000 families, halted immigration, credit measures, and work-sharing by employers, while states, counties, and municipalities expand their efforts; voluntary contributions must cover the remaining need. The speaker emphasizes that voluntary giving and individual responsibility to neighbors are vital to democracy and cannot be replaced by government action, and appeals to Americans to ensure no one suffers hunger or cold by Thanksgiving, November 26.

The conference will attract over 250 delegates and 40 exhibitors, review the regional waste management action plan, and include development partners IDB, UN Environment, CDB, and PAHO.

Drug repurposing—identifying new therapeutic uses for existing drugs—accounts for roughly one-third of drug approvals and is especially valuable for rare diseases, which have limited treatments and small patient populations. Knowledge graphs integrating biomedical associations, combined with machine learning embeddings, have become a popular method for predicting new drug-disease connections.

This study uses Elsevier's Biology Knowledge Graph (EBKG), built via proprietary AI NLP technology from both open access (OA) and controlled access (CA) literature, to compare the two corpora's contributions to drug repurposing knowledge. The EBKG contains 17 relation types across 15 biomedical concept types, extracted from PubMed abstracts, full-text articles, and clinical trials.

Key findings:
- OA and CA contribute roughly equally at the relation level, though NLP asserted 1.5 times more statements from CA text.
- OA contribution grew significantly after 2006; over 50% of rare disease relations are now OA.
- Well-studied rare diseases (over 100 relations) tend to have majority-OA relations; no such bias exists for drug-target relations.
- Most relations in both corpora are supported by a single reference; nearly all relations with four or more references are OA.
- CA-only facts still increase yearly, but more slowly than OA facts.
- Citation rates and time to first citation show no difference between OA and CA, indicating no accessibility barrier.
- Single-reference (uncited) relations accumulate exponentially in both OA and CA, attributed mainly to lack of follow-up by the scientific community rather than fraud or accessibility issues.
- 85% of uncited relations were extracted from peer-reviewed literature; most originate from original research articles.
- CA journals show a higher retraction rate (68.3% of retracted PubMed articles were CA).

The authors conclude that additional confidence measures are needed beyond reference counts, suggesting epistemic discourse analysis, citation indices, statistical alignment with the knowledge graph, and distinguishing self-citations. They propose credibility tiers for published knowledge and recommend training large language models on different literature subsets to improve confidence assessment and potentially support automated peer review.

The LG V35 ThinQ is LG's new premium smartphone, succeeding the V30S ThinQ. It features a Snapdragon 845 processor, 6GB RAM, a 6-inch OLED display, Gorilla Glass 5, IP68 rating, and MIL-STD 810G testing. Managed by Q ("Q"), founded by Dan Teran and Saman Rahmanian, launched in New York in April 2014 as an on-demand office cleaning and maintenance company. Unlike most on-demand startups that used independent contractors, Q hired its workers as employees, paying above-industry wages, offering benefits, training, and advancement opportunities. The company differentiated itself through technology, giving customers iPads with dashboards for transparent task monitoring, maintenance requests, and supply ordering. By July 2015, Q had raised $17.4 million total, including a $15 million Series A, and operated in New York, Chicago, and San Francisco with over 90% customer retention. It grew about 33% monthly, with roughly 70% of typical customer spending coming from cleaning. Q emphasized a culture of transparency, community, and quality, calling all employees "operators." Facing copycats and investor interest, CEO Teran weighed growth options: entering new markets such as Boston, Atlanta, and Washington, DC, or deepening existing markets by adding services and expanding its third-party vendor platform. He was determined not to pursue growth at the expense of the business model and culture that had made Q successful.

In this MIT lecture on control of manufacturing processes, the instructor reviews the relationship between hypothesis testing and control charts. Alpha (false alarm probability) sets the control limits, while beta (missed alarm probability) is reduced by increasing sample size, which tightens the sampling distribution while maintaining alpha. Average run length is defined as 1/alpha for false alarms (ARL0) and 1/(1-beta) for detecting shifts (ARL1). The lecture distinguishes control limits, set statistically from false alarm rates, from spec limits based on design requirements—confusing the two is an error. Process capability indices are introduced: Cp compares the six-sigma process spread to the distance between spec limits, while Cpk additionally penalizes mean offset from target. A Cpk of 1 corresponds to roughly 3 nonconforming parts per 1,000; a Cpk of 2 corresponds to about one part per billion and provides robustness against small mean shifts. Quality loss functions, typically quadratic, drive both mean centering and variance reduction. When an alarm occurs, the chart alone cannot distinguish false from true alarms, so investigation is required—starting with measurement verification, reviewing historical data for trends, and consulting operators. With many independent control charts, aggregate false alarm rates must be considered. The lecture previews alternative charts for sample size one: moving average, exponentially weighted moving average, and cumulative sum charts, which improve detection of small shifts, along with autocorrelation considerations in sampling.

President Trump will deliver his first State of the Union address Tuesday, with lawmakers using the event to make statements. Many female Democratic lawmakers will wear black in solidarity with the #MeToo movement against sexual harassment, and some are inviting guests affected by assault. Dozens of young immigrants protected under DACA were invited by Democrats to highlight the immigration debate, while Rep. Kevin Cramer invited the president of a company contracted to build a border wall prototype. At least eight Democratic lawmakers are boycotting the speech. Iraq has begun bombing Islamic State-held Tal Afar, west of Mosul, its next target after Mosul's recapture; a ground offensive will follow the air campaign, an Iraqi Defence Ministry spokesman said.

The Sarahah app, though newly trending on social media, is actually a few months old and was already a hit in Egypt and Saudi Arabia. Users create profiles that anyone can visit to leave anonymous messages; receivers can flag, delete, reply, or favourite them. The app is polarising, with nearly equal 5-star and 1-star reviews on Google Play, as anonymity enables hurtful behaviour. Privacy features let users remove their profiles from search results, restrict access to logged-in users, and block senders. Unlike earlier anonymous apps such as Yik Yak, Secret, and Whisper, Sarahah focuses on messaging rather than social media, but its anonymous, non-replyable comments raise bullying concerns. It is free on Android and iOS.
