The PGA848 is a monolithic, high-voltage, high-bandwidth, precision programmable gain instrumentation amplifier with a single-ended output, combining a current-feedback input stage, an internally matched gain resistor network, and a four-resistor differential amplifier output stage. It provides eight binary-gain settings from 0.5V/V to 100V/V via three digital pins (A0, A1, A2) and targets applications such as factory automation, analog input modules, data acquisition, and test and measurement. Its linear input range extends within 3V (maximum) of either supply, with the common-mode range depending on input common-mode voltage, differential voltage, gain, and reference voltage.

A typical application drives a 16-bit, 1MSPS SAR ADC (ADS8860) using ±15V input-stage supplies and a 5.3V output-stage supply shared with the ADC. A REF6250 5V reference, divided to 2.5V and buffered by an OPA192, sets the PGA REF pin at ADC midscale. Three filters—an input EMI/RFI filter, a feedback capacitor filter (CFB = 75pF, 318kHz cutoff), and an ADC charge-kickback filter—yield a nominal 318kHz bandwidth with –0.1dB flatness to 41kHz.

Nominal performance is specified with ±15V supplies and mid-supply VICM and VREF; supplies above 40V (±20V) permanently damage the device. Layout guidelines recommend symmetrical input paths, local 0.1µF bypass capacitors, trace separation, minimized leakage and parasitic capacitance, and distance from thermal sources. PSpice for TI and free TINA-TI software support simulation; documentation resources, E2E support forums, trademarks, ESD handling, revision history, and packaging information are also addressed.

This study experimentally characterises the oxidation of pure tungsten (99.95%) in dry air between 400 and 1050°C and the sublimation of WO₃ powder between 750 and 1100°C, using simultaneous thermal analysis (TGA-DSC), XRD, Raman spectroscopy, and SEM/EBSD. Motivated by fusion applications, the work addresses tungsten oxidation during accident (LOCA combined with LOVA), maintenance, waste handling, and detritiation scenarios, where oxide sublimation, dust formation, and spalling may occur.

Oxidation kinetics showed a transition from parabolic to linear regimes, with activation energies of 180.4 ± 3.8 kJ/mol (parabolic) and 117.5 ± 3.3 kJ/mol (linear). Oxidation was preferential at specimen edges, with rates increasing linearly with perimeter-to-area ratio, and the edge oxide spalled readily during handling. WO₃ sublimation followed zero-order kinetics with an activation energy of 335.8 ± 17 kJ/mol.

Raman and XRD analysis identified a three-layer oxide scale: an inner WO₂ layer (~30–50 nm), a dense intermediate WO₂.₇₂ layer (10–20 µm), and an outer layer of WO₂.₉/WO₃ phases. The parabolic-to-linear transition was attributed to growth limitation by the dense WO₂.₇₂ layer rather than cracking, since voids were already present at the end of the parabolic regime. Above 600°C, voids and cracks formed, attributed to high Pilling-Bedworth ratios (about 2 to 3.4), thermal expansion mismatch between W and WO₃, and grain-orientation-dependent oxidation rates ({100} planes oxidising fastest, near {111} slowest).

The confirmed presence of WO₂, predicted to act as a tritium permeation barrier, may explain the low detritiation efficiency reported for JET tungsten tiles.

Joseph Nicholson of Barrie, sentenced to life in prison for the 2007 stabbing death of 16-year-old Joey Tanner of Hamilton and the attempted murder of Jeremy Rodgers, may become eligible for parole earlier after the Ontario Court of Appeal overturned his first-degree murder conviction, citing inadequate jury instructions, and ordered sentencing for second-degree murder. The Crown is seeking parole eligibility at 16 years. Court heard Nicholson has a violent criminal record and misbehaved in prison. Nicholson apologized in court; the victim's parents expressed ongoing grief. Justice Guy Di Tomaso will impose the sentence on Aug. 11.

A Missouri detective inhaled heroin mixed with fentanyl while giving rescue breaths to an overdose victim, causing headache and lightheadedness. Both are okay; police say the increasingly common combination is dangerous to first responders.

Katie Albert, a Waterloo High School graduate and psychology student at Southern Illinois University Edwardsville, continues her six-part series on studying abroad in Florence, Italy. Her Italian classes have progressed, allowing her to order food in local restaurants. In painting and drawing classes, she completed five paintings, including a pointillism Tuscan landscape and a surreal Venus piece, along with drawings of local gardens, sculptures, and Michelangelo's Aurora. University activities included a cooking class and day trips to Siena, Pisa, and Lucca. During spring break, she visited seven countries in 10 days: Denmark, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, France, Germany, and Switzerland. A highlight was visiting Becherbach, Germany, the birthplace of her fourth-great-grandfather, Abraham Maurer. She also went tandem paragliding near Geneva. After returning to Florence amid the start of tourist season, she traveled to Split, Croatia, for white water rafting, cliff diving, and beach time, reaching a milestone of 20 countries visited by age 20. With three weeks remaining, she faces final exams and bittersweet feelings about leaving Florence.

From July 2, Australia's Turnbull Government will replace the Child Care Rebate and Child Care Benefit with a single means- and activity-tested childcare subsidy. Of the roughly 1.2 million eligible families, about 489,000 risk missing out unless they update their Centrelink details via myGov, providing estimated 2018-19 income and work hours. Both parents must undertake at least eight hours of approved activity per fortnight. Subsidies range from 85 per cent of fees for families earning up to $66,958, tapering down to 20 per cent, with no subsidy for those earning above $351,248. Households earning under $186,958 face no annual cap, while the cap for higher earners rises from $7500 to just over $10,000 per child. Education Minister Simon Birmingham urged families to update their details, while Labor claims one in four families will be worse off. Children must also be immunised, and hourly rate caps vary by care type.

Jeffing is a fitness method created in the 1970s by Olympian Jeff Galloway, also known as the run-walk-run method. It alternates running with planned walking breaks instead of running continuously to exhaustion. According to Dr John Gallucci Jr, CEO of JAG Physical Therapy, benefits include improved aerobic endurance with reduced fatigue, built-in muscle recovery, and lower injury risk for those unused to jogging. Beginners should start by running 1–2 minutes, then walking 1–2 minutes, adjusting the ratio to their comfort level, with slow, steady progression. Experienced runners can use it during long runs and recovery weeks. Jeffing may be less suitable for athletes requiring sustained high-intensity effort, and improper progression can still cause injuries such as knee pain, shin splints, or plantar fasciitis.

The last trading day of the month is a weak day in the stock market, exhibiting negative seasonality. Backtesting from 1993 to July 2021 showed that $100,000 invested in SPY only on this day produced an average loss of 0.06% per trade and a negative annual CAGR of 0.8%, compared to an average daily gain of 0.04%. However, buying at the close of the second-to-last trading day and selling at the next open yielded an average gain of 0.04%, matching the overall average. The poor performance comes from the open-to-close period, which averaged a negative 0.11% with a low win ratio of 42%. Profit-taking is speculated as a possible cause, and the weakness appears structural rather than driven by outliers.

Sharon Haliwell, 48, wife of a Wigan businessman, died by suicide in April after struggling with sleeping pill addiction and abuse from her husband. A coroner raised concerns about communication failures between teams at North West Boroughs NHS Foundation Trust after Mrs Haliwell discussed suicidal tendencies with two services within a fortnight. The trust has implemented staff training and plans to amend procedures by March 2018, though the coroner issued a prevention of death notice.

This survey studies algebraic, algebro-geometric, and combinatorial invariants of matroids and their connections to hyperplane arrangements, examining whether these invariants depend on the matroid itself or its realization. The invariants discussed include the Orlik–Solomon algebra, holonomy Lie algebra, holonomy Chen Lie algebra, resonance varieties, Koszul modules, and multinets.

For realizable matroids, the Orlik–Solomon algebra is isomorphic to the cohomology ring of the arrangement complement, and the holonomy Lie algebra's graded ranks correspond to lower central series ranks of the fundamental group, though torsion may arise in positive characteristic. Chen ranks are conjecturally expressed in terms of k-multinets on sub-matroids. Degree-1 resonance varieties decompose into linear subspaces corresponding to k-multinets, and Koszul module supports coincide with resonance varieties in degree 1. Open questions include linearity of higher-degree resonance varieties for non-realizable matroids and whether torsion can distinguish realizable from non-realizable matroids.

The paper reviews matroid fundamentals: matroids as pairs (E, I) satisfying an exchange axiom, rank functions, flats forming a geometric lattice, the Möbius function, localization and direct sum operations, and realizability by hyperplane arrangements, with examples including uniform and graphic matroids.

Multinets partition a matroid's ground set into k ≥ 3 parts with a multiplicity function satisfying constant-sum conditions and a base locus of rank-2 flats; weak multinets can be refined to multinets. Reduced multinets include (k,d)-nets, where each base locus flat contains one element per class. For realizable matroids with base locus size greater than 1, k must be 3 or 4, and non-reduced multinets require k = 3.

A (3,d)-net determines a Latin square, and k-nets correspond to tuples of orthogonal Latin squares. Several finite groups, including cyclic, dihedral, and quaternion groups, are realizable by 3-nets in CP2. A 3-net is algebraic if its dual points lie on a cubic curve; Yuzvinsky asked whether all 3-nets in CP2 are algebraic.

The passage concludes by defining the Orlik–Solomon algebra as a quotient of an exterior algebra by circuit relations, with Betti numbers computed via the Möbius function, and noting that the OS-ideal admits a quadratic Gröbner basis precisely when the matroid is supersolvable.

Anna Ryder Richardson, 53, is leaving Manor House Wildlife Park in Pembrokeshire and divorcing her husband Colin MacDougall after 16 years, blaming the stress and expense of running the zoo for the marriage's collapse. The former Changing Rooms presenter bought the park near Tenby for £1 million in 2008 against Colin's better judgment, and the family's renovation was filmed for Channel 4's Chaos At The Zoo. The couple spent four years living in a cabin while investing in animal facilities, and constant work, financial pressure, and loss of privacy strained their relationship. In 2010, a falling tree injured a three-year-old visitor and his mother, leading to over £100,000 in fines and costs; Colin took the blame and pleaded guilty, and the case against Anna was dismissed. Though the zoo recovered, the marriage did not, and the couple, who remain friends, realised they were no longer in love. Anna is moving to a dilapidated property near Bordeaux with her daughters Bibi and Dixie, while Colin will continue managing the zoo. She is returning to television co-presenting 60 Minute Makeover with Peter Andre on Quest Red.

The speaker says fatigue is irrelevant in the Stanley Cup finals because adrenaline takes over. Though his team has not won a game yet, it has rebounded with strong performances and has experienced players like Thornton, Manson, Carbonneau, Hatcher, and Modano. He notes the opposing Sykora-Elias-Arnott line plays well together, and that he and Hatcher must be physical to shut them down. He defends Joe, who is playing well despite not scoring, contrary to expectations after winning the Conn Smythe.

Hackers released more unaired HBO episodes, including "Curb Your Enthusiasm," "Insecure," "Ballers," and "The Deuce," but not "Game of Thrones." HBO acknowledged the hack and a multi-million-dollar ransom demand, which comes as Time Warner awaits regulatory approval for its $85.4 billion sale to AT&T.
I am unable to summarize this passage.

The American Heart Association's Go Red For Women campaign encourages women to take heart health seriously. Tiffany Gholston, 41, born with a heart murmur, received her first pacemaker at 20. She stays healthy through activity, diet, and meditation, and raises research funds through the Circle of Red.

This Motley Fool Money article reviews the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card, highlighting its unlimited 2% cash rewards on purchases, a $200 cash rewards bonus after spending $500 in the first 3 months, 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers (then an 18.99%–28.99% variable APR), a $0 annual fee, and up to $600 cell phone protection with a $25 deductible. Approval is most likely for applicants with good credit (670 or higher). The page also briefly features the Capital One Quicksilver card (1.5% cash back, 15-month 0% intro APR, $300 in welcome bonuses) and a Citi card (2% cash back, 18-month 0% balance transfer APR). Disclosures note that Motley Fool receives partner compensation, which may affect offer placement but not product ratings.

Researchers at Albert Einstein College of Medicine, led by Young-Hwan Jo, found that exercise-induced appetite reduction involves temperature-sensitive neurons in the hypothalamus's arcuate nucleus (ARC). In mouse studies, about two-thirds of appetite-suppressing POMC neurons in the ARC had TRPV1-like receptors that respond to heat and capsaicin. Infusing capsaicin into the ARC reduced mice's food intake for 12 hours, an effect prevented by blocking or silencing these receptors. Forty minutes of treadmill exercise raised mice's body and ARC temperatures and cut their food intake by about 50 percent, but did not affect mice lacking TRPV1 receptors in POMC neurons. The findings suggest body temperature regulates feeding behavior and could lead to new appetite-suppression or weight-loss approaches.

Researchers from the Harvard-Smithsonian Centre for Astrophysics and Tel Aviv University propose using a global network of mobile phones and low-cost radio receivers to detect fast radio bursts (FRBs) from within the Milky Way. FRBs are millisecond-long signals from unknown sources; only one, FRB 121102, has been found to repeat. Participating phones would record candidate FRBs and upload data to a central website for correlation, with GPS triangulation providing sky position. FRBs occur at frequencies matching mobile phones and Wi-Fi. Researchers estimate a Galactic FRB might occur once every 30 to 1,500 years, or weekly if repeating.

McLaren says reliability issues from pre-season testing in Barcelona—including a wheel nut failure, battery problems, a loose exhaust and overheating bodywork—have been addressed at its Woking factory ahead of the Australian season opener. Racing director Eric Boullier expressed confidence, while Fernando Alonso said the Renault-powered MCL33 showed potential. Boullier added that the tight midfield makes it hard to judge McLaren's position and the team is not expecting miracles.

This patent application describes systems and methods for adapting and updating radiotherapy treatment plans based on biological, physiological, and/or anatomical data extracted from imaging data acquired in real-time during treatment sessions. The systems comprise an imaging system (e.g., PET detectors, X-ray, MRI), a radiation treatment system (including a therapeutic radiation source, dynamic multi-leaf collimator, and motion system), a controller, and a communication interface. Biological activity data may include tracer uptake values (SUV), PET tracer kinetics, tissue metabolism, oxygenation, genetic expression (e.g., HER2), blood flow, and lymphatic activity data. Treatment plan updates may involve modifying dosimetric objectives, target region geometry, number of treatment sessions, session duration, and fractionation patterns. Methods for evaluating treatment plans include calculating plan quality index (PQI) values and dose-volume histograms (DVH) based on real-time imaging data, comparing them with pre-determined ranges, and generating tiered notifications (e.g., PASS/GO, FAIL/NO GO) to indicate whether to proceed with treatment. Various PET tracers targeting different biological markers (e.g., FDG for metabolism, FMISO for hypoxia) are described with corresponding plan adaptations. Adaptive radiotherapy may be performed online (at the start of a session), in real-time (throughout a session), or offline (between sessions).

A hockey player reflects on winning the Stanley Cup after eight years in the league, calling it an unforgettable moment and praising his teammates, including Larry Murphy. He describes his difficult adjustment to the NHL, few people believing in him, and thanks Scotty, his teammates, and his family, including his six-year-old daughter Dasha, for their support. Feeling healthy and motivated, he plans to play another year. He also hopes to bring the Cup to Moscow with Commissioner Gary Bettman's approval to generate interest and investment in Russian hockey.

National Weather Service forecasts make Monday's partial solar eclipse visibility in Philadelphia uncertain, as unsettled weather to the south could move north. Philadelphia is outside the path of totality; the total eclipse occurs in Charleston at 2:48 p.m. ET, the first visible in the U.S. since 1979.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC dated October 26, 2017. Under Item 2.02, the company reported issuing a press release that day announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2017, furnished as Exhibit 99.1. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration, and Chief Accounting Officer.
Huddersfield Giants, following a 12-0 pre-season win at Warrington and a 28-16 Super League XXII triumph at Widnes, face Salford Red Devils at home. Coach Rick Stone demands continued improvement.

The Texas Supreme Court denied the writ of error in a Health Spa Act suit where the Department prevailed against Anna Black's letter-of-credit surety. Black challenged admission of documentary evidence not timely identified in response to an interrogatory. The Court did not approve the appellate witness/document distinction; good cause must be shown under Rule 215.5.

This compilation lists English-language reports on the 1945 San Francisco Conference from the United States, Britain, the USSR, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand. It serves as a bridge between the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals and the UN Charter, focusing on the United States' role in establishing the UN's legal framework and presenting the American Delegation's positions, with emphasis on informal agreements among the major Powers rather than formal Conference meetings. US policy recommendations are traced chronologically, and documentation covers four phases: policy development, negotiation, debates, and drafting. Records include minutes of seventy-nine US Delegation meetings, twelve "Big Four" and twenty-nine "Big Five" meetings, and informal meetings with other American Republics, drawn from State Department files and other archives.

On March 22, 2016, NVIDIA Corporation entered into an accelerated share repurchase agreement with Barclays Bank PLC as part of its previously announced intention to return $1 billion to shareholders through quarterly cash dividends and share repurchases in the current fiscal year. NVIDIA will pay $500 million to Barclays and receive 12,108,715 shares of NVIDIA common stock. At settlement, Barclays may be required to deliver additional shares, or NVIDIA may deliver shares or make a cash payment, based on the average daily volume-weighted average price of NVIDIA common stock during the agreement's term.

A hockey coach discusses team strategy and player management. The team shortens players' ice time in the third period so they come to the bench with energy. Lineup decisions among Hrkac, Plante, and Hogue remain undecided, with Sydor potentially providing a physical presence. Hull is doubtful due to injury, as playing him risks further damage. The coach's shutdown pair has focused on Buffalo's Brown, with flexibility to match against Peca. He declines to disclose specific injury details to protect players but commits to stating game-time availability, as was done with Modano and Hull. Keane was given rest options after heavy minutes. Regarding Hull, the coach describes a compromise: Hull has freedom with the puck but must play the team's physical style without it, comparing this to his earlier difficult relationship with Rob Brown. Hogue is progressing from injury and may be evaluated after the pregame warmup. The team, feeling it lacked sacrifice in its overtime loss in Colorado, emphasizes greater mental and physical commitment. Finally, the coach stresses preventing Buffalo's Peca from controlling the tempo and keeping him away from the net.

Intel is in early talks with AMD to manufacture chips for its foundry business, according to a Semafor report. Intel shares rose 7% on Wednesday, while AMD shares gained over 1%. A deal would be a significant win for Intel's foundry business, which is seeking big customers, and would signal AMD's confidence in manufacturing with its biggest competitor. The extent of any AMD manufacturing with Intel is unclear. Intel shares are up nearly 77% in 2025. Intel declined to comment; AMD said it does not comment on rumor or speculation.

On May 18, 2001, Saudi Arabia announced its selection of international oil companies for three major natural gas projects requiring a combined investment of approximately $25 billion, reopening its energy sector to foreign investment for the first time since nationalization in the 1970s. ExxonMobil, Royal Dutch/Shell, BP, and Phillips Petroleum were selected for Core Venture 1 (South Ghawar, estimated at $15 billion); ExxonMobil will lead Core Venture 2 (Red Sea), with Enron and Occidental Petroleum awarded stakes; and Shell, TotalFinaElf, and Conoco won Core Venture 3 (Shaybah). Leaders for Ventures 1 and 3 will be announced by June 5, when memoranda of understanding will also be signed. The U.S. Energy Department welcomed the selection of American firms, saying it aligned with the Bush administration's energy plan. Chevron, ENI, and Marathon were dropped from the participants list. Separately, a Dow Jones column reported that California's $43 billion in long-term power contracts had declined in value by roughly $6.5 billion as forward power prices fell, though the state took advantage of lower prices to purchase summer power. In options trading, Enron's June options were active, with an institutional investor executing a bullish spread.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated July 18, 2019, reporting that it issued a press release announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2019. The press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and, per General Instruction B.2 of Form 8-K, is not deemed "filed" under the Exchange Act. The report was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration, and Chief Accounting Officer.

A March 7, 2001 email from Steven Kean to James Hughes discusses Enron's limited role in defending the Export-Import Bank (Ex-Im) against proposed budget cuts. Kean notes Enron cut headcount and expenditures from its 2001 budget and that John joined Linda Robertson's DC office, though considerable project finance work remains. John Hardy states Enron will not lead the battle with OMB but is negotiating with EXIM and OPIC on Electrobolt and needs their support on problem projects; Rebecca McDonald sits on EXIM's advisory committee.

Attached articles report that major exporters including Boeing, Caterpillar, Enron, and Halliburton are lobbying Congress to protect the Ex-Im Bank from a proposed 25% cut to its $865 million operating budget, which the White House labels corporate welfare; Enron received $135 million in Ex-Im financing in fiscal 2000. Other articles cover downtown Houston office development (including a tower built for Enron), emerging competition in Dutch gas trading involving Enron Europe, Southern California Edison's $2.7 billion line sale to the state that could take until 2002 (with Enron Wind among suppliers suing Edison), Sierra Pacific's CEO doubting SEC approval of its $3.1 billion acquisition of Enron's Portland General Electric, unfinished California power contracts (Enron agreed on terms except credit details), and falling U.S. natural gas prices.

The Stack Offense compacts players into two stack alignments outside the free throw line rather than spreading the floor, allowing ballhandlers to maneuver sideline to sideline. Turnovers are reduced by limiting possession to three ballhandlers, while two post players act as stationary screeners. On dribble penetration to a wing, the ballhandler on that side pops out off the post screen. When defenders overplay or show, players back cut or roll to the basket for easy shots. Ballhandlers may drive when the basket is unprotected, and posts seek drop passes when their defenders sag. Continuity resets as players re-establish stack alignment.

STIs remain a major public health challenge in the US, with over 2.4 million reported cases of chlamydia, gonorrhea, and syphilis in 2023, disproportionately affecting marginalized populations. Expedited Partner Therapy (EPT), a CDC-endorsed strategy allowing treatment of sexual partners without prior clinical evaluation, remains inconsistently implemented, partly due to limited pharmacist awareness.

This study used a cross-sectional "secret shopper" design to assess the accessibility of electronically prescribed, nameless EPT at 335 randomly selected New York City pharmacies and to examine whether accessibility varied by neighborhood socioeconomic vulnerability, measured by the socioeconomic subcomponent of the CDC Social Vulnerability Index (SVI). Trained pseudopatients called pharmacies with a standardized script describing a hypothetical EPT prescription for the partner of a chlamydia-positive patient.

Results showed 40% of pharmacists were aware of EPT, and awareness was associated with willingness to dispense nameless prescriptions (48% vs. 18%). Overall willingness to dispense was low (30%); 31% refused, most commonly citing unfamiliarity with EPT or belief that a patient name was legally required. Only 46% of fillable prescriptions adhered to New York State guidelines. Contrary to the hypothesis, higher socioeconomic vulnerability was associated with greater pharmacist awareness but not with willingness to dispense. National chain pharmacies reported higher awareness than non-chain pharmacies, and neighborhood chlamydia incidence showed no significant association with awareness or dispensing.

The authors conclude that pharmacy-level barriers—limited awareness, low dispensing willingness, and poor guideline adherence—hinder EPT implementation, and recommend targeted education, policy interventions, and improved electronic prescribing systems. Limitations include the hypothetical nature of the calls, potential interaction variability, and limited generalizability from a single metropolitan area.

Keaton Jones, a sixth-grader at Horace Maynard Middle School, described in a viral video posted by his mother that classmates poured milk on him and put ham in his clothes at lunch. The video drew attention from celebrities and the public under #StandWithKeaton. Principal Greg Clay said Monday he was unaware of repeated bullying, that the incident had been resolved weeks earlier, and that action was taken with the children involved. The school planned an assembly on bullying and a January anti-bullying talk. Other parents said bullying occurs occasionally but is no worse there than elsewhere.

This disclosure describes techniques for hardware-aware AI/ML model searching, centered on a machine learning model swapping (MLMS) system that selects and interchanges ML models (e.g., subnets derived from a supernet) in an energy and communication efficient manner while adapting to real-time changes in system and hardware constraints. The MLMS system includes an MLMS engine (with an interface and subnet selector) and a performance auditor that monitors model performance and context information—such as mode of operation, system state, physical environment, and networking environment—to detect status changes that trigger a new subnet search. Energy efficiency is achieved through a similarity-based selection process in which the replacement subnet with the greatest overlap in pre-trained parameters with the currently deployed model is chosen, minimizing memory write operations and data transfer costs. Subnets are encoded as vectors of elastic parameters (kernel size, expansion ratio/width, and depth), and a two-stage search-and-swap algorithm first identifies candidate subnets meeting performance and constraint criteria, then selects the candidate with minimal transfer cost. The system supports model-based and platform-based performance metrics, can employ various NAS/evolutionary search algorithms, and applies to use cases such as autonomous vehicles, IoT devices, drones, remote sensor arrays, and federated learning on edge nodes. The document also covers background ML concepts, example neural network structures, and example hardware/software configurations including accelerator architectures and compute node components.

This passage discusses integrating globalization education into English as a Foreign Language (EFL) curricula, focusing on Taiwanese university students. It argues that globalization connects world citizens into a single social order, making English essential as a tool of international communication. The paper reviews globalization's effects on educational policies in countries such as Switzerland, Japan, and China, and proposes that global issues—such as HIV/AIDS, global warming, and war—can serve as teaching materials tailored to students' majors. The researchers conducted an 18-week study with 372 non-English-major university students at three Taiwanese universities (Taichung, Yunlin, and Changhwa), using surveys, group discussions, and a Facebook page to explore topics including festivals, food, art, technology, sports, animals, the Middle East, folk stories, energy, therapies, buildings, and environmental protection. Results showed strong student support: 95% agreed globalization education is important, 96% said it stimulated English learning motivation, and 87% found it interesting. Students identified global warming, global energy, and environmental protection as the most significant topics, and suggested pedagogical methods such as travelling (22%), disaster films (20%), and news reading. The study concludes that global issues should be incorporated into English curricula to prepare students as interdependent global citizens, which is particularly significant for Taiwan given its political isolation, limited natural resources, and need for economic and technological competitiveness.

A single case study examined the effects of anti-seizure medication (ASM) changes and seizures on smartphone touchscreen interactions in a man in his late twenties with refractory right temporal lobe epilepsy. Over 185 days, an app recorded over 718,000 touchscreen interactions and seizure diary entries. During a five-day epilepsy monitoring unit admission, his medications (lamotrigine and perampanel) were tapered and withdrawn, and video-EEG documented multiple seizures including a focal to bilateral tonic-clonic convulsion. Analysis of joint-interval distributions using cluster-based permutation testing showed increased probability of fast next-interval dynamics during ASM tapering, which reversed upon medication restart, and increased probability of slow next-interval dynamics on the day of the convulsion. The authors propose that smartphones can unobtrusively track medication and seizure-related behavioural changes in epilepsy, and that increased behavioural ageing in epilepsy is partly explained by ASM exposure and seizure occurrence. Cohort studies are needed to establish generalisability.

Skinimalism is a skincare trend focused on streamlining routines to a few essential, high-quality products rather than complex multi-step regimens. GP Dr Hazel Parkinson explains it involves choosing targeted, multitasking products that respect the skin barrier, embracing natural texture and long-term support rather than instant results. Benefits include protecting the skin's natural barrier, reducing irritation and sensitivity, and improving wellbeing by removing pressure from social media-driven ideals of a 'perfect' routine. It is also more sustainable and budget-friendly, producing less waste and packaging. However, skinimalism is not suitable for everyone. People with acne or pigmentation may still need specific ingredients such as retinoids or azelaic acid, though not necessarily alongside many additional steps. Parkinson advises that for acne, a gentle cleanser, non-comedogenic moisturiser and one targeted active can be more effective and better tolerated than a 10-step routine. Skin with a compromised barrier benefits from barrier repair, fragrance-free emollients and ceramide-rich moisturisers, with actives introduced cautiously. Rosacea-prone skin requires a minimal routine with a soothing cleanser, anti-inflammatory moisturiser, SPF and a single calming active. For hyperpigmentation, consistent use of one well-chosen active plus daily SPF achieves more than layering multiple products. Menopausal skin may need richer moisturisers and targeted ingredients such as vitamin C, peptides or retinoids. For those with healthy skin, routines should reflect individual needs, age and lifestyle. When transitioning from a multi-step routine, she recommends eliminating one or two products at a time and allowing 2-4 weeks for the skin to adapt.

This case examines the 2014 leadership crisis at Market Basket (DeMoulas Super Markets, Inc.), a New England supermarket chain founded by Greek immigrant Athanasios Demoulas and later run by his sons Mike and George. A decades-long family feud over ownership led to a 1996 court ruling granting George's family (led by Arthur S. Demoulas) a 50.5% stake. Mike's son, Arthur T. Demoulas, became CEO in 2008 and led a company that by 2014 had 25,000 non-unionized employees, 71 stores, and $4.6 billion in revenue, built on low prices driven by high volume, no debt, lean management, long-tenured employees, a profit-sharing plan, internal promotion, strong customer service, and close supplier relationships.

After Arthur S.'s side gained board control in 2013, the board curtailed Arthur T.'s authority, approved a $300 million shareholder dividend, and fired him on June 23, 2014, naming Felicia Thornton and James Gooch interim co-CEOs. On July 18, 2014, headquarters, warehouse, and trucking employees walked out demanding his reinstatement. Store employees picketed, customers boycotted, and some vendors halted deliveries; sales fell more than 90%, part-time employees were let go, and local suppliers and neighboring businesses suffered while competitors benefited.

On August 27, 2014, an agreement was reached for Arthur T. and his family to purchase the 50.5% stake from Arthur S.'s side for $1.6 billion. Arthur T. was reinstated with full operational authority, and the deal closed in December 2014, financed largely with debt. Employees returned and sales rebounded, but observers questioned whether the company could sustain low prices, high wages, and growth while carrying the new debt.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2018 reports total revenue of $29.1 billion, up 19% from $24.5 billion in the prior-year quarter, with net income of $8.8 billion ($1.14 diluted EPS) versus $6.6 billion ($0.84). Operating income rose 29% to $10.0 billion. Revenue grew across all three segments: Productivity and Business Processes ($9.8 billion), Intelligent Cloud ($8.6 billion), and More Personal Computing ($10.7 billion). Commercial cloud revenue increased 47% to $8.5 billion, with Azure revenue growth of 76%. Total assets were $257.6 billion and stockholders' equity $86.0 billion as of September 30, 2018; net cash from operations was $13.7 billion. The effective tax rate fell to 14% from 18%, primarily due to the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, for which Microsoft recorded a provisional $13.7 billion net charge in fiscal 2018. Microsoft entered a definitive agreement in June 2018 to acquire GitHub for $7.5 billion in stock, expected to close by the end of October 2018. The company had $25.6 billion remaining under a $40 billion share repurchase program and declared a $0.46 per share dividend. Legal matters include 39 pending patent cases, Canadian antitrust class actions, a Chinese regulatory investigation, and a gender discrimination class action; accrued legal liabilities were $334 million, with reasonably possible adverse outcomes up to approximately $1.0 billion beyond recorded amounts.

The 2022 NFL draft featured a record six wide receivers selected in the first 20 picks, reflecting the position's growing value as offenses shift toward passing. Wide receivers complete the passing game by running crisp routes, getting open, and securing catches, while also contributing through run blocking. The position name comes from lining up "wide" near the sideline and "receiving" passes; it is also called WR, wideout, split-end, or flanker. Key skills include route-running, speed, strong hands, and agility, with typical builds ranging from 5'10" to 6'4" and 180-220 pounds. Notable receivers include Jerry Rice, Randy Moss, and Steve Largent. Elite receivers disrupt defenses by forcing difficult alignment decisions and creating matchup problems.

This paper presents PerovSegNet, a lightweight deep learning segmentation framework built on YOLOv8x-seg for analyzing SEM images of perovskite and lead iodide films in perovskite solar cells. The model incorporates two novel modules: ASDCB, which enhances multi-scale feature fusion through dilated convolutions and channel attention, and SAD, which captures both fine-scale textures and large-scale structures via dual-path downsampling. To address the scarcity of annotated data, the authors constructed the PerovData dataset of 10,994 augmented SEM images from 40 manually labeled samples, with UMAP analysis confirming class separability. On this dataset, PerovSegNet achieved an mAP@0.5 of 87.3%, outperforming baselines including Mask R-CNN, Cascade Mask R-CNN, and Cascade InternImage-XL while using fewer parameters (79M) and lower computational cost (265 GFLOPs). Ablation studies showed both modules improved accuracy, with defect segmentation rising from 33% to 64%. The framework operates across magnifications from 200 nm to 2 µm and enables automated quantification of grain area and count. Correlation analysis of approximately 25 published studies found perovskite area strongly positively associated with power conversion efficiency (r = 0.78), while defect metrics correlated negatively. The authors note limitations including the observational nature of the correlations and the need for larger, more diverse datasets.

A University of Connecticut study found that vaping nicotine-based liquid can cause DNA damage approximately equivalent to smoking unfiltered tobacco cigarettes. Researchers used a low-cost 3D-printed electro-optical screening device, acting as a fake lung with human metabolic enzymes and DNA, to detect damage. Potential DNA damage increased with the number of puffs taken. The findings were published in ACS Sensors, and researchers are continuing to develop similar platforms for toxicity screening and cancer diagnostics.

The passage explains how to backtest a momentum trading strategy in Python. Momentum is an investing factor that aims to benefit from the ongoing trend of a stock or asset, with rising stocks having positive momentum and declining stocks negative momentum. The backtest uses Select Sector SPDR ETFs, with historical data downloaded via the yfinance library using adjusted close prices. Momentum is defined as the rolling past 9-month performance, and the portfolio is rebalanced monthly by buying the top 3 ETFs in an equally-weighted portfolio. Returns are calculated and plotted against SPY. The strategy compounded at a 9.89% CAGR versus SPY's 9.46% CAGR, showing nearly identical performance and little alpha.

The Evening Star is a bearish reversal pattern in technical analysis consisting of three candles: a tall bullish candle, a small candle that gaps above the first, and a bearish candle closing below the midpoint of the first candle. Traders use this pattern to identify potential bearish price reversals and profit from them, often confirming the pattern with tools such as trendlines, resistance levels, and momentum oscillators before placing short positions. The pattern is more reliable when the gap between the first two candles is significant and the third candle is longer than the first. Success depends on proper pattern identification, confirmation, and a solid risk management plan, as the pattern is not a guarantee of market movement. Risks include false signals, market volatility, over-reliance on technical analysis, and losses without proper risk management. The strategy can be adjusted for different market conditions and timeframes depending on trading style and risk tolerance, and indicators such as RSI, the stochastic oscillator, and Bollinger Bands can provide additional confirmation. Backtesting with specific rules and settings is recommended.

Anna Mae Blessing, 92, was charged with first degree murder, aggravated assault and kidnapping after allegedly shooting her 72-year-old son at their Fountain Hills, Arizona home. Authorities said the shooting stemmed from a dispute over his plan to place her in an assisted living facility. Her son's girlfriend disarmed her, and Blessing was arrested.

American public education has long borrowed business practices, from Horace Mann's framing of schooling as a means to supply skilled factory workers to the bureaucratic structures of large schools. The 1983 report *A Nation at Risk* and the subsequent *A Nation Prepared* led to teacher professionalization and national certification, but did not improve teachers' financial security and produced virtually no gains in student reading and math scores. The No Child Left Behind Act of 2001 introduced competition, accountability, and standardized testing, with sanctions for schools failing to make adequate yearly progress, including conversion to charter schools. Research shows charter schools have produced mixed results, increased segregation and disparities, and no broad test score gains, with some successes attributed to student selectivity.

The passage critiques the medical model of learning, which attributes success to inborn biological traits—a view traced to eugenicist and slave-owner beliefs. Diagnosis can foster fixed mindsets, stigma, and stereotype threat, harming academic outcomes. The author proposes reframing education as problem-solving, involving students in diagnosis as self-discovery and treating conditions as solvable problems.

Problem-solving is presented as the fundamental process of learning, evident across species, computers, and human cognition, and mirrored in children's theory-building behavior (the child scientist theory). Perception itself relies on heuristics and prediction developed through environmental interaction. The author argues education should be restructured around this universal problem-solving process, with metacognitive support from mentors, assessment based on individual progress rather than norms, and recursive application from classroom pedagogy to institutional administration, with self-directed learning as the ultimate goal.

Minister Richard Bruton told the Dáil that 12 Autism Units—five primary and seven post-primary—will be built in Sligo/Leitrim and Donegal during the 2018/19 school term, responding to Deputy Marc MacSharry's questions. Since 2011, Leitrim's ASD classes rose from two to five, SNAs increased by 3,545, resource teachers by 3,660, and special classes by 712. Where applications exceed places, a fair, non-discriminatory selection process may apply.

The passage addresses legal principles for compensating losses from a vessel's unjustified detention. It states that the mate of the Costa Rica Packet should have taken command as a precaution, and that loss of catch may be admitted when estimating damages for a whaling vessel's detention. It cites U.S. Supreme Court cases (The Potomac, per Justice Gray; Williamson v. Barrett, per Justice Nelson) holding that owners of an injured vessel may recover for loss of use during repairs, measured by market price where available or by evidence of lost profits otherwise. The English case of the Gazelle allowed gross freight less expenses as compensation for detention, though this may fall short if repairs take longer. This rule was applied to whaling ships captured by the Confederate cruiser Shenandoah in the Alabama Claims decision.

The passage reports a study of chemical etching (polishing) of Cd1-xZnxTe1-ySey (CZTS) crystals, which are considered promising materials for X-ray and gamma-ray detectors, using a 5% bromine-methanol solution. Cutting and polishing these soft-brittle crystals produce a damaged surface layer (up to ~100 μm) that blocks charge collection and causes leakage currents, so it must be removed chemically. Samples with zinc content x ≈ 0.1 and selenium contents y = 0, 0.02, 0.06, and 0.1 were etched at +19°C, and etching trajectories and average rates were determined. A proposed thermodynamic model predicts that the CZTS etching rate is lower than that of CZT and proportional to the negative excess Gibbs energy of the solid solution. Experimentally, average etching rates were 24, 18, 15, and 13 μm/min for CZT, CZTS2, CZTS6, and CZTS10, respectively; even y ≈ 0.02 reduced the rate by about 20% (24% measured vs. 22% theoretical), providing direct evidence of crystal-lattice hardening by selenium. At higher selenium contents, differences in etching rates level off. Stirring increased the rate 1.5–2 times, etching beyond 3–5 minutes degraded surface quality, and zinc addition, by contrast, increases the etching rate. The results can guide optimal processing of CZTS detector elements.

The author rejects Ambassador Hartman's recommendation to trade the INF deployment option for an arms control agreement, arguing that non-deployment would cast doubt on NATO's ability to implement controversial decisions, embolden pacifist and anti-American forces, and threaten the Alliance's viability. Disputing Hartman's reading of the European mood, the author cites Mitterrand's support and expects the Italians, British, and Germans to honor their commitments, recommending the U.S. hold firm on the zero-zero option and deploy as scheduled unless the Soviets restructure their position, in which case asymmetrical reductions toward theater-nuclear parity might be considered. Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic sections specify summary statistics of plasma concentrations by treatment group and time point, mean and individual concentration-versus-time plots on original and log scales, and the pharmacodynamic endpoint of plasma glucose area under the effect curve above baseline from 0 to 30 minutes (AUE0-30min), calculated using SAS. Plasma glucose is sampled at pre-dose and multiple time points up to 45 minutes (60 minutes if body weight ≥21 kg), with sampling restricted to ±30 seconds until the 20-minute time point and ±1 minute thereafter.

Safety analyses, based on the safety set, cover: extent of exposure (insulin administration, hypoglycemia induction, trial medication, and post-treatment rescue glucose infusion, with descriptive statistics for time to first IV glucose infusion); local tolerability assessed at 30, 120, and 300 minutes post-dose; adverse event summaries restricted to treatment-emergent AEs (TEAEs), coded using MedDRA version 21.0 or higher, with overview and frequency tables by system organ class, preferred term, causality, and severity (missing causality is set to related if queries fail; missing severity is not imputed); laboratory parameters including change from baseline (screening V1 versus follow-up V3); vital signs; physical examination; ECG with categorical QTcF summaries (>450, >480, >500 ms and changes >30 or >60 ms); and descriptive immunogenicity analysis counting treatment-induced and treatment-boosted (≥5-fold titer increase) anti-drug antibody patients.

The document also lists changes made to protocol-specified analyses, cites the ICH E9 guidance, and includes appendices covering data presentation and programming specifications (formatting rules and derived variable formulas such as BMI), SAS programming quality control requirements, and a list of planned tables, figures, and listings prepared according to ICH E3 guidelines.

This chapter reviews the reservoirs of small bodies that source exocomets, combining Solar System observations with formation theory. Small-body populations exist in discrete dynamical reservoirs; in the Solar System these include near-Earth asteroids, the main belt, co-orbitals and Trojans, the Hildas, irregular satellites, Neptune Trojans, trans-Neptunian populations (cold classical and dynamically excited objects, scattered and detached discs), Centaurs, Jupiter-family comets, and the Oort cloud, with outer populations being the most massive and numerous. Trans-Neptunian objects have predominantly icy surfaces containing H₂O, CO₂, CO, CH₄, CH₃OH and organics.

Stars form in dense molecular cores, developing protostellar discs classified as Class 0–III by their spectral energy distribution slope. Discs are the sites of planet formation; Class 0/I discs are more massive than Class II discs, whose dust masses may be insufficient to account for known exoplanets. Most stars form in clusters, where stellar flybys and external photo-evaporation can truncate or destroy discs, with the dominant mechanism depending on cluster type and density.

In protoplanetary discs, dust grows by collisional sticking, but silicate aggregates encounter bouncing and fragmentation barriers, and radial drift limits growth at larger distances. Planetesimals therefore likely form via gravitational collapse of pebble concentrations, aided by particle traps and possibly the streaming instability, which requires high dust-to-gas ratios (super-Solar metallicity) and reaching the Hill density. Resulting size distributions favour large bodies; Solar System evidence suggests asteroids and cold classical KBOs formed at ~100 km ("born big"). Planetesimal composition is set by disc temperature structure and snowlines, which lie farther out around more luminous stars, though chemical processing also produces observed CO depletion and C/O anomalies.

Once gas disperses, remnant solids form debris discs, detected around ~20% of nearby AFGK stars; collisional grinding depletes their dust with age, implying exocomets are preferentially detected around younger stars. Although exocomets are mostly found around A stars, planet formation occurs across stellar masses, and wide-orbit giant planets correlate positively with stellar mass up to ~2 M⊙. Solar System evidence—orbital structures, surface colours, JWST spectroscopy, sample returns, and Rosetta measurements—constrains formation models, though subsequent evolution complicates interpretation. The Oort cloud, source of long-period comets, likely formed from planetesimals ejected from beyond Jupiter's orbit, possibly including captured non-native objects; exo-Oort clouds are theoretically plausible but lack observational proof. The chapter closes with open questions and notes upcoming facilities, including JWST, ALMA, the Rubin Observatory, SPHEREx, the Roman Space Telescope, and extremely large telescopes, that will advance the field.

This passage from the TPS7H500x-SP datasheet details application design components and layout guidance. The leading edge blank time was set to roughly 50 ns using a 49.9-kΩ RLEB resistor, though this may require optimization and is correlated to the device's minimum on-time. A 33-nF soft-start capacitor yields a ~7.5-ms soft-start time. The transformer uses a 2.5 turns ratio with a 35% maximum duty cycle target (versus the 50% controller limit), and a 40-μH primary inductance was used despite a calculated value of 33 μH. Primary-side GaN FETs are rated 170 V for a 36-V maximum input, while an 80-V GaN FET serves as the synchronous rectifier, optionally paralleled with a Schottky diode to reduce losses. An RCD clamp limits switch-node voltage. The output inductor is 0.47 μH with 40% ripple current. At least 1.3 mF of output capacitance is required; 2.3 mF (seven 330-μF polymer tantalum capacitors) was used, partly for single-event transient mitigation in space-grade designs. Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins at ~35 A, using a 1:100 current sense transformer and a 7.5-Ω sense resistor. The hiccup capacitor is the minimum recommended 3.3 nF. Type 2A compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover, with RCOMP = 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP = 15 nF, and CHF = 47 pF. A 102-kΩ slope compensation resistor connects RSC to AVSS.

The controllers operate from a 4-V to 14-V supply with at least 0.1-μF ceramic bypass capacitance. Layout guidelines cover feedback trace routing, switch-node minimization, ground separation, trace widths, bypass capacitor placement, and routing of noise-sensitive signals. The passage also lists related documentation, revision history (Revision F, August 2024, adding QMLP options for TPS7H5002/3/4-SP), and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information with standard TI disclaimers.

Germany is an industrialized Western European nation of about 83.2 million people whose education system has been shaped by its complex history. After unification in 1871, Chancellor Otto von Bismarck introduced universal mandatory education based on the Prussian system. The National Socialists standardized higher secondary education in 1938 to create citizens aligned with Nazi ideology. After World War II, West Germany established a three-tiered secondary system—Hauptschule (vocational preparation), Realschule, and Gymnasium (university preparation via the Abitur)—while East Germany created a free system spanning primary through higher grades. Following reunification in 1990, the three-tier model became the norm nationwide and public education became free. Education today is primarily under federal state jurisdiction, so structures vary; the Hauptschule has acquired a reputation as lower-quality, and some states have combined it with Realschulen.

Special education schools (Hilfsschulen) emerged in the 1920s to educate students with disabilities for low-wage vocational roles. In 1960, the Standing Conference of the Ministers of Education and Culture (KMK) established various special school types and their legal frameworks. Despite pushes for inclusion since the early 1990s, special and general education schools grew further apart, and students in special schools performed worse than peers in inclusive settings. About 577,000 students with disabilities are enrolled in one of seven special school categories; in 2019–2020, roughly 2,800 special schools employed about 68,500 educators. Only 33.6% of children with disabilities are included in elementary schools and 14.9% in secondary schools. About half of included secondary students attend Hauptschule, which offers few job opportunities.

Qualification for special education resembles the U.S. individualized education program process, involving referral, comprehensive evaluation, and collaboration to create individualized plans; Mobile Special Education Services support schools with other funding priorities. About 40% of individuals with disabilities attend public schools—moderate compared to other European countries. Parents support inclusion for physical or sensory disabilities but are more skeptical about behavioral or severe cognitive disabilities.

Teacher preparation follows a two-phase model: university academic training ending in a first state examination, then the Referendariat, a two-year paid in-school induction ending in a final state examination. Teachers are civil servants with strong job security, though professional development pressure and career-switching options are limited. Special education teachers complete similar training but intern in special schools, specialize in two or three academic subjects, and receive heavier emphasis on pedagogy and behavior management; they typically work in elementary or vocational secondary schools rather than Gymnasium.

Key policies include the 2006 General Equal Treatment Act, the 2008 UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, and North Rhine-Westphalia's 2013 9th School Law Amendment Act implementing inclusive education. In 2015, the KMK published recommendations supporting inclusive education.

Current challenges include balancing inclusion with individual needs, unstable funding, teacher attitudes (physical inclusion does not guarantee social inclusion, though positive teacher attitudes improve integration), negative perceptions of MTSS/RTI, and the ability-focused secondary system, particularly the Gymnasium's lack of special services. The system is shifting toward greater inclusion, potentially redefining special educators as interveners in general schools.

This patent application, a continuation of multiple prior applications titled "Metal Gates of Transistors Having Reduced Resistivity," describes methods and structures for forming transistors with low-resistivity metal gates. The background notes that polysilicon gate electrodes suffer from a poly depletion effect, which metal gates address, but tungsten gates require a high-resistivity nucleation layer due to poor adhesion, degrading performance in scaled-down devices.

The disclosure details a FinFET fabrication process: forming a substrate with shallow trench isolation (STI) regions, recessing the STI to create protruding fins, forming a dummy gate stack with gate spacers, etching source/drain recesses, and selectively growing epitaxial source/drain regions (e.g., SiGeB for p-type, SiP or SiCP for n-type). After inter-layer dielectric (ILD) formation and planarization, the dummy gate is removed and replaced with a replacement gate dielectric (an interfacial layer plus a high-k dielectric such as hafnium oxide), work function layers (e.g., TaN, TiN, TiAl depending on device type), a titanium nitride barrier layer, and a metal-containing material.

The metal-containing material may comprise a lower cobalt silicide layer (layer A) and an upper silicon-free cobalt layer (layer B), formed by adjusting wafer temperature during deposition, or alternatively a homogeneous cobalt or metal silicide layer (Ti, Ni, W, Mo, or Ta silicides). Source/drain contact plugs and gate contact plugs similarly use metal nitride barriers with cobalt-containing layers over them.

Advantages cited include cobalt's resistance to acid corrosion during polymer removal, smaller roughness than tungsten, low resistivity (about 5.8 μOhm·cm for cobalt silicide) at small dimensions, and good adhesion to TiN, whereas tungsten's nucleation layer has a resistivity of about 200–250 μOhm·cm.

The passage describes features of the TMS320DM814x DaVinci Digital Media Processor. The Spinlock module provides 128 hardware spinlocks (semaphores) for synchronizing processes across multiple processors, enabling device resource locking with a single read-access. The Mailbox module facilitates communication between the ARM Cortex-A8, C674x DSP, and Media Controller via mailbox registers, using interrupt signaling for message and overflow notification; it supports flexible mailbox-to-processor assignment, four-message FIFO depth per queue, and four interrupts. The device uses a unified memory map across bus masters, including L3, L4 Fast, and L4 Slow peripheral memory maps, with the C674x DSP having limited access to certain peripherals. The TILER provides an additional 4-GB addressing range for rotated and mirrored frame buffer views, accessible only to the HDVPSS and ISS subsystems. Terminal functions tables define pin multiplexing, ball numbers, pin types, internal pullup/pulldown resistors, and supply voltages for peripherals including boot configuration, camera interface, DDR2/DDR3 memory controllers, EMAC, GPIO, GPMC, HDMI, I2C, McASP, PCIe, JTAG, SD/SDIO, SPI, timers, UARTs, USB, and video I/O. Boot configuration is determined by sampling BTMODE[15:0] pins at reset, supporting boot modes including XIP (NOR), NAND Flash, NAND I2C, MMC/SD, SPI, EMAC, PCIe, and UART, executed in order until a successful boot occurs. Pin multiplexing is controlled by MUXMODE bits in PINCNTL1–PINCNTL270 registers, and unused pins may be left unconnected with internal or external pull resistors enabled to prevent floating inputs.

The Boston Zone Offense, developed by Tom Davis and nationally recognized during his time coaching Boston College, requires players to play only one position without interchanging, making them more efficient in their single roles. The offense emphasizes a strong low post attack and uses a dribble entry rather than pass entry, making it effective for up-tempo teams. It combines overloading and spreading principles against zone defenses. The basic alignment includes a point guard (O1), corner/baseline runner (O3), low post (O5), shooting guard (O2), and weakside rebounder (O4). Continuity relies on sharp passing, ball reversal, and corner basket cuts. Post reads depend on defender positioning, while baseline runners create matchup and vision problems. Overplay counters involve skip passes when passes are denied. The offense includes specific strategies against 2-3, 1-2-2, and 1-3-1 zones.

Hawaiʻi is expanding free preschool access through charter schools as part of its goal to provide all 3- and 4-year-olds with preschool by 2032. Waikīkī Community Preschool recently became the first program to transition from private to charter status, making it tuition-free. Charter schools currently operate 33 preschool classrooms statewide. Advocates say the charter model helps address the early educator shortage by offering teachers state employee benefits and salaries equal to K-12 public school educators. However, current funding of $171,000 per classroom falls short of covering costs, forcing schools like Waikīkī (facing a $150,000-$200,000 shortfall) and Parkway Village Preschool to rely on fundraising. Charter schools also require licensed teachers, a difficult requirement amid the statewide educator shortage. The state received only two charter preschool applications this year, and the charter commission plans to add 15 more preschool classrooms by fall 2028.

The article concludes that making money day trading is possible—the author personally traded stocks profitably from 2002 to May 2012 and achieved F.I.R.E.—but emphasizes that most day traders fail. Trading is described as a struggle requiring preparation, strict discipline, and patience; the author spent two years barely profitable before finding profitable edges. The author's statistics show stellar years in 2006 and 2009 with very few losing days, and the best 1% of trading days accounted for 11% of total profits, with 19 of the best 25 days occurring in 2008. A difficult period from mid-2011 to mid-2012 was attributed to changing market conditions, a broker switch from Echo to Nevis Trading, relocation stress, and the rise of algorithmic trading, which reduced volume and increased competition. Court records from the failed prop firm Tuco Trading, seized by the SEC in 2008, revealed poor profitability among its day traders in 2007. The author now trades mean reversion strategies, is adapting to larger drawdowns, and is collaborating with a Latvian programmer to automate trading. Swing trading is recommended before attempting day trading.

The Turnaround Tuesday effect refers to the stock market's tendency to reverse direction from the close of Monday's session through at least Tuesday's close. When Monday is weak, subsequent returns tend to be above average; when Monday is strong, returns are lower. Backtests of SPY from 1993 to September 2021 show that buying at Monday's close is roughly twice as profitable as buying at Tuesday's close, and more profitable than other weekdays. The strategy works only on weak Mondays—buying on strength is not profitable. One variant buys when Monday's close is at least 1% below Friday's close and sells at Tuesday's close; filters like the Intraday Breadth Strength (IBS) can improve performance. The effect has been profitable for about 30 years, though caution is advised amid current geopolitical risks.

The reciprocity treaty between Hawaii and the United States was signed January 30, 1875, and took effect September 9, 1876. Great Britain and Germany initially objected under the parity clause of the 1852 Anglo-Hawaiian treaty; Germany's claim was successfully contested by Mr. Carter, while Britain's claim produced prolonged correspondence, a rejected compromise, a change of ministry, and eventual Hawaiian acknowledgment of exclusive US privileges. An "annexation scare" led Secretary Evarts to instruct Minister Comly to deny any US designs beyond the treaty. Later interpretation and fraud questions were settled diplomatically. A domestic scandal caused ministerial changes and a briefly recalled request for Comly's recall. The US also aided Hawaii in suppressing the liquor traffic in the Ralik Islands and in negotiating a treaty with Japan. In 1881, Comly reported continued British efforts to invoke the parity clause.

This study employs femtosecond noise correlation spectroscopy (FemNoC) to investigate ultrafast magnetization fluctuations in the canted antiferromagnet Sm0.7Er0.3FeO3, focusing on the interplay between quasi-ferromagnetic (qF) magnon fluctuations, the spin reorientation transition (SRT), and the free energy potential landscape. Temperature scans across the SRT, with critical temperatures identified near 299 K and 321 K at low fields, reveal that the qF magnon variance is strongly enhanced and its resonance frequency softens near the lower critical temperature, accompanied by random telegraph noise (RTN) from picosecond stochastic switching. Atomistic spin model and Monte Carlo simulations reproduce these trends, showing that fluctuations increase where the free energy potential softens. Field scans show hysteretic magnetization behavior and demonstrate that an external magnetic field along the c-axis suppresses spin fluctuations and increases the qF magnon frequency, attributed to field-induced stiffening of the potential. The authors conclude that the magnitude of picosecond spin fluctuations is dictated by the free energy landscape, that external fields offer a means of tuning ultrafast magnetization fluctuations, and that FemNoC can serve as a tool for characterizing magnetization potentials in complex magnetic systems.

This patent application, a continuation claiming priority through multiple earlier U.S. applications to four Chinese applications filed August 1, 2016, relates to camera modules and their molded circuit board assemblies, molded photosensitive assemblies, and manufacturing methods. The background explains that conventional integral molding packaging, though theoretically superior to holder-type COB packaging, was unsuitable for mass production because square-shaped through-holes caused friction, deformation, and damage during demoulding, and vertical inner walls reflected stray light onto the photosensitive chip, degrading image quality. The invention provides a molded base integrally formed on a circuit board (and optionally a photosensitive element) with a light window that is not prismatic; its inner and outer side surfaces form acute inclination angles (first, second, third, and fourth inclination angles) within predetermined ranges (e.g., 3°–30° and 3°–45°) to facilitate demoulding, reduce damage and stray light reflection, and provide sufficient top surface area for mounting a lens, lens actuator, or optical filter. A molding mould with a light window forming block having a trapezoidal or multi-step trapezoidal cross-section, with diameters increasing from bottom to top, eases demoulding. The application further covers manufacturing methods involving filling and solidifying molding material in a base forming guide groove, integral arrays of molded assemblies produced by joint board array operations, and electronic devices such as mobile phones incorporating the camera modules.

In this MIT 2.830J lecture, guest lecturer David Hardt revisits manufacturing process definitions from a mechanical engineering perspective. He models a manufacturing process as an interaction between equipment and material through a directed energy exchange—mechanical, electrical, thermal, or chemical—that changes geometry or properties. He identifies four geometry change modes: removal, addition, deformation, and formation. A taxonomy distinguishes serial processes (small interaction area moved over time, e.g., laser cutting, CNC machining) from parallel processes (energy distributed over the whole area via shaped tools, e.g., molding, stamping), noting some processes, like rolling, are mixed. This classification affects control: serial processes are governed by tool trajectory, while parallel ones depend on the shape of the energy distributor. Energy mode influences rate, quality (through diffusivity, repeatability, and side effects), and flexibility; serial removal processes tend to be most flexible, while deformation is highly sensitive to material property variation. Finally, Hardt divides process parameters into equipment states, equipment properties, material states, and material properties. States are transient energy quantities, while properties are inherent constitutive characteristics. Equipment states are the most controllable, aided by modern CNC and servo controls, whereas material properties and states—along with the uncertain energy exchange interface—are the largest sources of variation. Control efforts typically manipulate equipment states.

The lecture examines forces between neutral atoms. Classically, neutral atoms have no dipole moments or dipole fluctuations, so no attraction is predicted. In quantum mechanics, zero point fluctuations of atomic dipole moments exist by necessity, and when correlated between two atoms, produce a non-vanishing force. Perturbation theory yields a 1/R³ potential (first order) for a ground- and excited-state atom pair, and the van der Waals 1/R⁶ potential (second order) for two ground-state atoms. An LC circuit analogy shows the 1/R⁶ potential arises from the zero point energy of two coupled oscillators. Alternatively, a fluctuating dipole in one atom induces an aligned dipole in the other via polarizability, again giving 1/R⁶. Including vacuum fluctuations of the electromagnetic field, which induce correlated dipole moments in both atoms, yields a 1/R⁷ potential, with dominant contributions from modes with wavelengths near the atomic separation. The short-range 1/R⁶ (van der Waals) potential assumes instantaneous interaction, while the long-range 1/R⁷ (Casimir-Polder) potential includes propagation effects; the transition occurs at distances comparable to the wavelength of the atomic transition. A QED diagrammatic treatment shows the interaction arises in fourth-order perturbation theory through exchange of virtual photons. At short range, photons are exchanged sequentially; at long range, two photons are emitted nearly simultaneously, adding an extra power of 1/R and yielding a retarded potential.

A hockey player reflects on going back-to-back with a group that included many returning players. He describes the joy of overcoming how difficult it is to repeat and sharing the feeling with longtime teammates, family, and friends. He notes his competitive nature and the team's willingness to do whatever it takes. He praises defensemen and other players who handled the pressure of losing a high-minute teammate, along with veteran additions that paid off. He highlights goaltenders who stole games during the playoffs, including one who kept the team in the Washington series, and a young player's scoring. Finally, he describes passing it off to a longtime teammate who could appreciate it.

This study assessed the potentiality and apprehensions of AI in education from the perspectives of academic staff and administrators at Kuwait University's Faculty of Education, addressing a gap in research on AI in education within the Arab region. Prior studies reported mixed perceptions: teachers viewed AI as a source of scaffolding but feared role replacement, while medical students saw AI as a tool to enhance learning rather than replace doctors.

Using a cross-sectional design, 63 participants were recruited through random sampling and completed an online questionnaire comprising the Attitudes for Artificial Intelligence (ATAI) scale, the Teachers' Perspectives on Artificial Intelligence Questionnaire, and the Scenarios of AI Education and AI-related Applications Questionnaire. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS version 26 with descriptive statistics, t-tests, and ANOVA.

Results showed medium acceptance of AI among faculty (overall mean 3.37), with the highest consensus that AI will benefit humanity (mean 4.03) and low fear of AI. Most participants (58.7%) had no prior teaching experience with AI. The most important educational aspects linked to AI were data analysis, machine learning, and natural language processing (overall mean 4.21). Key student empowerment requirements included identifying AI use cases, assessing the intelligence of AI systems, and recognizing their technical limitations (mean 4.36). Challenges in using AI were rated high (mean 4.83), mainly the lack of suitable teaching materials, insufficient expertise, and subject complexity. Preferred educational scenarios (mean 4.82) included personalized intelligent teaching, smart schools, and online and mobile remote education. No statistically significant differences were found by gender, academic degree, or academic department, except for challenges and difficulties of using AI between males and females.

The study concluded that both apprehensions and potentiality regarding AI integration in education are high, and reforms are needed to prepare AI for education. A limitation was the exclusion of student perspectives; future research should use larger samples from different universities.

The lecture introduces risk preferences from the expected utility perspective, the standard economic model for choices involving risk. Nearly all life choices involve risk—education, housing, farming, investments, health—along with risk-mitigation strategies like insurance. Risk aversion is typically modeled as diminishing marginal utility of wealth (a concave utility function), though other factors like anxiety, regret, and disappointment relative to expectations also play roles.

Three stylized facts are presented: (1) people buy insurance even when it pays less than fair value; (2) people accept risk when returns are high enough (stocks, entrepreneurship); (3) some people seek risk with negative expected value (casinos, lotteries), which is inconsistent with risk aversion.

The expected utility model values gambles by weighting utilities of final outcomes by their probabilities. Key assumptions: only final outcomes matter, and probabilities enter linearly. Risk-averse people (concave utility) reject all fair gambles. Risk aversion is measured via the coefficients of absolute or relative risk aversion (gamma), estimated through certainty equivalents, choices among gambles, or insurance choices.

Large-scale choices (e.g., a 50-50 bet between $50,000 and $100,000) suggest gamma is between 0 and 2. However, rejecting a small 50-50 bet of winning $11/losing $10 implies gamma exceeds 18. Rabin (2000) proves that an expected utility maximizer with weakly concave utility who rejects small gambles must have marginal utility declining so rapidly that absurd implications follow—such as rejecting a bet of losing $100 to gain an infinite amount. The single-parameter expected utility model cannot reconcile small-scale and large-scale risk attitudes, motivating alternatives like Kahneman-Tversky's loss aversion, to be discussed later.

Finally, the lecture introduces Justin Sydnor's study using real-world home insurance deductible choices (from 50,000 policies with four deductible options) to estimate risk aversion, to be covered in more detail next time.

CSUSB veteran students describe tuition benefits for active duty members and veterans. Active duty members receive tuition assistance up to $4,500 annually, though military obligations can interrupt studies. The Post-9/11 GI Bill offers up to four years of education benefits to those who served at least 90 days on active duty, covering tuition, fees, and books, and pays full tuition at public schools. The Montgomery GI Bill offers similar benefits but requires students to pay those costs, with payments based on credit load. After service, members have 10-15 years to use their GI Bill.

Sears borrowed $100 million from CEO Eddie Lampert's hedge fund, with up to $100 million more available. Lampert's fund has loaned Sears nearly $2 billion over two years amid store closures and falling sales.

R. L. Wells was convicted of embezzlement and sentenced to two years in the penitentiary. His appeal bond, though approved by the sheriff, was approved by Judge Oltorf rather than the trial judge, as required by article 904. The bond was therefore insufficient, and the appeal was dismissed.

**Shircliff v. The State (No. 11,670):** An indictment charging a conspiracy to bribe a township trustee, by payment or promise of money, to employ a person as a public school teacher is valid under sections 2139 and 2009, R.S. 1881, without averring that any school was vacant; the motion to quash was correctly overruled. Affidavits supporting a motion for continuance or other motions become part of the record only by bill of exceptions; a bill filed in vacation without granted time is not part of the record, so the contentions regarding the continuance and admission of evidence could not be considered. Objection to the discharge of co-defendant O'Connor under section 1804 to make him a witness for the State was waived, having been raised for the first time in the Supreme Court.
