After the first special judge failed to appear at the April term, the regular judge appointed another special judge, who rendered judgment; it would be presumed the first appointee absented himself or was unable to preside, making the second appointment proper. The judgment was affirmed, with costs.

Congressional Democrats, led by House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, are holding firm on health care demands ahead of a Monday meeting with President Trump and Republican congressional leaders aimed at avoiding a government shutdown set for 12:01 a.m. Wednesday. Jeffries rejected the GOP-backed spending bill and criticized Republicans on health care. Democrats insist any deal must extend enhanced Obamacare tax credits expiring at the end of 2025, while Republicans want those negotiations to occur after a funding resolution passes the Senate. At least seven Senate Democrats would need to vote with Republicans to pass a shutdown-averting bill.

Memoranda for President Roosevelt and the American delegation for the Malta and Yalta Conferences (January 30–February 11, 1945) were completed on January 16, 1945, and compiled into the "Yalta Briefing Book." A memorandum of conversation by Leo Pasvolsky records a second meeting with the Soviet Ambassador on the Dumbarton Oaks proposals, lasting over two and a half hours. The Ambassador, soon departing for Moscow, sought to clarify several points, including Chapter VIII, Section C, paragraph 1, concerning whether the Council should encourage regional agencies to settle local disputes peacefully. The voting formula was discussed again without new points. He considered the Court matter settled in substance, with details under study in Moscow. The dependent areas discussion was lengthy; the Soviet Government, though lacking colonies, was favorably impressed by Secretary Hull's memorandum. Pasvolsky outlined approaches to trust and colonial areas, noting only international trusteeship belonged on the United Nations Conference agenda, while colonial questions might be addressed at a special conference or by the future international organization.

H&M's March local currency sales rose 6 percent, one percentage point below a preliminary estimate, adding to concerns the retailer may miss its full-year growth target of 10-15 percent. The company has repeatedly missed forecasts amid competition from budget rivals and online players, and February saw its first sales decline in four years. Analysts with "sell" recommendations cited the tough market and suggested slowing store expansion. H&M had 4,426 stores at end of March, up 11 percent year-on-year, and its shares have fallen around 26 percent over the past year.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2022 (Commission File Number 001-37845) reports the company is incorporated in Washington and headquartered in Redmond, with common stock, 3.125% Notes due 2028, and 2.625% Notes due 2033 listed on Nasdaq. As of December 31, 2021, the aggregate market value of common stock held by non-affiliates was $2.5 trillion; as of July 25, 2022, 7,457,891,872 shares were outstanding.

Founded in 1975, Microsoft develops software, services, devices, and solutions, with a mission to empower every person and organization to achieve more. Its three ambitions are reinventing productivity and business processes, building the intelligent cloud and intelligent edge platform, and creating more personal computing. In March 2022, Microsoft completed its acquisition of Nuance Communications; in January 2022, it announced plans to acquire Activision Blizzard.

Sustainability commitments include being carbon negative by 2030, water positive and zero waste by 2030, and a $1 billion climate investment. The Racial Equity Initiative includes a $150 million investment to strengthen inclusion. As of June 30, 2022, Microsoft employed approximately 221,000 full-time people (122,000 in the U.S. and 99,000 internationally).

The company reports three segments: Productivity and Business Processes (Office, LinkedIn, Dynamics), Intelligent Cloud (Azure, server products, Enterprise Services), and More Personal Computing (Windows, Devices, Gaming, Search and news advertising). LinkedIn has over 850 million members, and Microsoft holds over 69,000 issued patents. Executive officers include Satya Nadella (Chairman and CEO) and Amy Hood (CFO). Products are distributed through OEMs, direct sales, and distributors and resellers. Risk factors include intense competition, competing platform ecosystems, alternative business models, and execution risks from cloud-based services.

In Leslie B. Canion v. United States (decided October 10, 1958), the parties stipulated that the merchandise—glassware, furniture, and smoker's articles from France—presented the same issues as Bert Friedberg & Co. v. United States. The court found foreign value under section 402(c) of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended, to be the proper basis: invoice unit values plus 12.44% plus packing, and for 40 excess boxes of item 21008, 337 French francs each plus 12.44% plus packing, with no higher export value.

The U.S. government has provided over $55,000 to Cambodia to preserve 3,000 to 5,000 personal items belonging to prisoners at the Khmer Rouge's Tuol Sleng prison, where an estimated 17,000 people were tortured and killed. Some items will be displayed at the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum.

Connor McDavid signed a two-year, $25 million contract extension with the Edmonton Oilers, carrying a $12.5 million average annual value. Less than two hours later, the Oilers extended defenseman Jake Walman for seven years and $49 million, starting next season. McDavid, 28, has 1,082 points in 712 career games, five scoring titles, and three Hart Trophies, and was set to become an unrestricted free agent after this season. He took time evaluating the Oilers' contention window, with a three-year term discussed before the sides settled on two years. Walman, 29, posted a career-high 40 points last season, giving Edmonton long-term deals for three of its top-six defensemen.

Amazon.com, Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2016 reports net sales of $29.1 billion, up 28% year-over-year, with net income of $513 million compared to a net loss of $57 million in Q1 2015. Operating income rose to $1.1 billion from $255 million, and diluted EPS was $1.07 versus $(0.12). By segment, North America net sales grew 27% to $17.0 billion with $588 million in operating income; International sales grew 24% to $9.6 billion with a $121 million operating loss; and AWS sales grew 64% to $2.6 billion with $604 million in operating income. Operating cash flow was $(2.2) billion for the quarter, while trailing-twelve-month free cash flow was $6.4 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $15.9 billion at quarter end, and total assets were $61.1 billion. Long-term debt included $8.3 billion face value of unsecured senior notes. In February 2016, the Board authorized a $5 billion stock repurchase program, replacing the prior $2 billion authorization; no shares were repurchased in Q1 2016. Legal proceedings include European blank digital media tariff disputes (Austro-Mechana, ZPU, AUVIBEL), a patent suit by Hand Held Products (Honeywell) dismissed in March 2016 and appealed in April 2016, and wage-and-hour lawsuits, including the Vance case dismissed with prejudice in March 2016 and appealed. Tax matters include an IRS transfer pricing dispute seeking approximately $1.5 billion in additional federal tax for 2005–2006, a French tax assessment of €196 million, and a European Commission state aid investigation regarding Luxembourg taxation. The company adopted new income tax classification guidance in Q1 2016 and expects new lease and stock-based compensation accounting standards to have material impacts.

NVIDIA Corporation's Form 10-Q for the first quarter of fiscal year 2019 (quarter ended April 29, 2018) reports revenue of $3,207 million, up 66% year over year and 10% sequentially. Net income was $1,244 million ($1.98 diluted EPS), up 145% from $507 million ($0.79) in the prior year. Gross margin rose to 64.5% from 59.4%. GPU segment revenue was $2,765 million (up 77%), driven by gaming ($1,723 million) and datacenter ($701 million); Tegra Processor revenue was $442 million (up 33%). OEM sales included $289 million related to GPUs for cryptocurrency mining. Operating expenses were $773 million, up 30%. Income tax expense was $67 million, with a 5.1% effective rate, reflecting the U.S. statutory rate reduction from 35% to 21%. The company adopted a new revenue recognition standard on January 29, 2018, with no significant impact. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $7.30 billion. NVIDIA repurchased 3 million shares for $655 million and paid $91 million in dividends, intending to return $1.25 billion to shareholders in fiscal 2019. Debt included $1.00 billion each of 2.20% Notes Due 2021 and 3.20% Notes Due 2026, plus $14 million of Convertible Notes outstanding. Pending litigation includes patent suits by Polaris Innovations and ZiiLabs, for which no accruals were recorded. Management concluded disclosure controls were effective.

The passage describes U.S. objectives for dependent areas: promoting their advancement through international collaboration, encouraging self-government and higher economic and social standards, safeguarding security interests, and applying non-discriminatory treatment. A March 9, 1943 Draft Declaration distinguished mandated or detached territories, proposed for international trusteeship, from colonial territories, for which regional commissions and progressive self-government leading to full independence on a fixed schedule were suggested. The draft was discussed with the British at Quebec and with the British and Russians at Moscow, where British objections were noted, as also during the Stettinius Mission talks in London. The proposals were refined before the Dumbarton Oaks Conversations, but the trusteeship chapter was deleted at the Joint Chiefs of Staff's request to avoid difficult territorial questions; dependent territories were therefore not discussed there, though the British, Soviet, and Chinese expressed interest. A January 1945 Pasvolsky letter acknowledged British acceptance of the President's Security Council voting proposal. Stimson's memorandum urged the great powers to settle fundamental problems first and to avoid territorial discussions during the war, warning these would provoke controversies.

The passage describes the NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture, which enables real-time ray tracing through dedicated RT Cores that accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, offloading this work from the SMs. Combined with denoising algorithms, RT Cores allow Turing to perform ray tracing roughly 10 times faster than Pascal GPUs. The architecture also introduces NGX, a deep learning technology stack using Tensor Cores for AI features including DLSS (which achieves image quality similar to TAA with roughly half the shading work, enabling RTX 2080 Ti to reach 2x the performance of GTX 1080 Ti), InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. Additional rendering advancements include Mesh Shading (Task and Mesh Shaders that eliminate CPU draw call bottlenecks), Variable Rate Shading (allowing shading rate control per 16x16-pixel region for techniques such as Content Adaptive Shading, Motion Adaptive Shading, and Foveated Rendering), Texture Space Shading (decoupling shading from screen-space pixels), and Multi-View Rendering (up to four views per pass). Turing also supports USB Type-C and VirtualLink for VR connectivity. The document details the TU104 GPU (used in GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000) and the TU106 GPU (GeForce RTX 2070), including transistor counts, core counts, and memory specifications. It introduces RTX-OPS, a workload-based metric combining Tensor, FP32, RT Core, and INT32 operations. The passage further explains ray tracing fundamentals—ray casting, BVH structures, and denoising—and illustrates ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections in games such as Battlefield V and Shadow of the Tomb Raider. It concludes with legal, trademark, and copyright notices.

The passage covers container design patterns for distributed systems. Single-node patterns include the ambassador pattern, in which a container brokers interactions between an application container and the outside world; examples include client-side sharding (using twemproxy with sharded Redis), service brokering for portable service discovery, and request splitting for experimentation (using nginx to direct 10% of traffic to an experimental service). The adapter pattern uses a container to transform an application's interface into a standardized one, applied to monitoring (a Prometheus exporter for Redis), log normalization (Fluentd for Redis slow queries and Apache Storm), and rich health checks (a Go-based MySQL health-check adapter). This modularity enables reuse and sharing without modifying third-party images.

Multi-node patterns address loosely coupled distributed systems. Microservices offer reliability, agility, team decoupling, and independent scaling, but make debugging and design more difficult. The replicated load-balanced service pattern deploys identical stateless replicas behind a load balancer; at least two replicas are needed for high availability, and readiness probes signal when replicas can serve requests. Session tracking (via IP hashing or cookies) routes a user's requests to the same replica. A caching layer (Varnish) can be added for performance, along with rate limiting for denial-of-service defense and nginx for SSL termination.

Sharded services split data across machines when state exceeds a single machine's capacity, with each shard serving only a subset of requests. Sharding functions map requests to shards using hashing and the modulo operator; key selection (e.g., request path or country) is critical, and consistent hashing minimizes remapping when the number of shards changes. Shards can themselves be replicated for reliability and to handle "hot" shards receiving disproportionate traffic.

The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes request processing across leaf nodes whose partial results a root node combines, as in document search; however, per-node overhead and the straggler problem limit gains, so replicating each shard improves reliability and enables upgrades under load. Finally, function-as-a-service (FaaS) provides event-driven computing with simplified deployment and automatic scaling, but poses challenges for debugging, monitoring, background processing, and applications that need to hold data in memory.

The President reports to Congress that the agent of the United States with the Creek Indians has invoked federal protection of rights and territory secured by the treaty ratified April 22, after Georgia surveyors were found surveying within the Indian Territory, with some reportedly arrested by the Indians. Under the act of March 30, 1802, such surveying is punishable by fine and imprisonment, enforceable either by military arrest in Indian country or by civil process within a State. The Executive has chosen civil process, directing prosecutions against the surveyors and assurances to the Indians, and has abstained from military force because the surveyors acted under color of Georgia authority, and a conflict between federal and state forces must be averted. The President states that Georgia's actions violate the treaty, warns that military force will be employed if encroachment persists, and submits to Congress whether further legislation is necessary.

Apple Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended December 26, 2015 reports net sales of $75.9 billion, up 2% year-over-year, and net income of $18.4 billion, with diluted earnings per share of $3.28. Gross margin was 40.1%. Growth was driven primarily by Services (up 26%, including $548 million received from Samsung related to a patent lawsuit settlement) and Other Products (up 62%), partially offset by declines in iPad (down 21%) and Mac (down 3%); iPhone net sales rose 1%. By segment, Greater China grew 14%, Europe and Rest of Asia Pacific each grew 4%, while Americas fell 4% and Japan fell 12%, with foreign currency weakness negatively impacting results. Total assets were $293.3 billion and shareholders' equity was $128.3 billion. The company held $215.7 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, with $7.3 billion in commercial paper and $55.5 billion in term debt outstanding. Operating cash flow was $27.5 billion. Under its capital return program, $110 billion of a $140 billion share repurchase authorization had been utilized, and quarterly dividends of $0.52 per share were declared. The effective tax rate was 25.3%, and gross unrecognized tax benefits totaled $7.4 billion. The European Commission is conducting an investigation concerning alleged state aid to the Company in Ireland, the potential impact of which could not be estimated. The Company operated 469 retail stores and anticipated approximately $15 billion in capital expenditures for fiscal 2016.

AT&T announced it will launch LTE-M, a cellular technology designed for Internet of Things devices, nationwide by the end of June. Tuned for everyday objects rather than phones, LTE-M uses little energy—devices can last up to 10 years on a single charge—penetrates walls thicker than standard cellular signals can, and transmits small amounts of data sufficient for IoT uses. Companies at AT&T's event demonstrated applications including Pepsi's internet-connected soda fountains that track flavor preferences by location, RM2's smart pallets with built-in radios for tracking goods, and Capstone Metering's smart water meters that can detect leaks or malfunctioning toilets. AT&T said these devices' minimal data use won't strain its network. Pricing hasn't been announced, but the company is considering per-bit or per-device charges.

Tesla debuted more affordable versions of its Model Y SUV and Model 3 sedan on Tuesday, with the Model Y standard priced just under $40,000 and the Model 3 standard starting around $37,000. The Model Y standard lacks a panoramic glass roof, leather seats, and light bars, costs about $5,000 less than the previous entry-level version, and has an estimated range of 321 miles versus 357 miles for the Long Range version. The lower prices may help attract buyers after the loss of $7,500 federal EV tax credits, amid global competition from EV makers. Tesla's shares climbed 5% Monday on announcement buzz but dipped about 3% Tuesday. The company's auto sales have been in a multi-quarter slump due partly to consumer backlash against Musk, an aging lineup, and competition. Tesla's stock jumped 40% in the third quarter and is up 12% for the year, aided by Musk's purchase of about $1 billion of Tesla stock.

The Rock Springs City Council will hold a public hearing on May 1 regarding ordinance amendments allowing downtown restaurants to operate outdoor "Dining Decks." The Planning & Zoning Commission approved the petition on April 11. Regulations include seasonal operation (May 1–October 31), six-foot sidewalk clearance, and maintenance responsibilities for restaurants.

The speaker discusses the Detroit Red Wings, a club with weaknesses that will prepare better despite playoff struggles. Power play is a key scoring opportunity since opponents take few penalties. A great player will bring offense and defense to his club. Having played with him in Magnitogorsk during the lockout, the speaker notes the player's increased confidence and maturity in his third NHL year. The speaker describes recovering from his first long-term injury, calling the absence his worst feeling as a player, and credits post-injury changes for improving playoff chances. Facing the team that beat them last year makes this a highly competitive series.

Tigers manager A.J. Hinch confirmed that ace Tarik Skubal will not pitch in Game 4 of the ALDS against the Mariners, despite Detroit facing elimination. Skubal, who threw seven innings of two-run ball with nine strikeouts in Game 2, is being saved on normal rest for a potential Game 5 in Seattle. High-leverage relievers will be available for Game 4.

Lego DC Super Villains has been officially announced with a full trailer. Players can create their own super villain and work alongside DC's classic bad guys in a parallel universe where the DC Super Heroes are absent. The game releases on October 16, 2018, for PC, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and Nintendo Switch, with special editions featuring bonus characters available.

A hockey coach discusses several players and team matters. He describes Jarome as one of the league's best players and a historically slow starter who improved this year by assuming genuine team leadership rather than merely being the face of the franchise, which had created unfair pressure. He notes versatile players like Jordan and Andrew who can play both sides, praises an underrated veteran defenseman who faces opponents' top players without taking penalties, and explains that Rhett was brought in as an experienced young defenseman. The coach acknowledges a poor first period that improved in the second, says the team focuses on its own improvement rather than opponents like Detroit or San Jose, and dismisses fatigue and ice conditions as factors. He also praises a veteran official, Scamp, as a respected throwback, and says a young player continues to develop in his role.

Pakistan has halted work on three CPEC road projects after China stopped funding them on November 20. Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal confirmed this to the Parliamentary Committee on CPEC, which stated the projects were not abandoned and would resume upon Chinese approval. The halt followed Pakistan's refusal of Chinese funding for the Diamer-Bhasha Dam and rejection of yuan trade at Gwadar Port. Experts view this as debt-trap diplomacy, while EFSAS suggests China aims to shift CPEC control to the Pakistan Army.

This retrospective cohort study analyzed 290 patients (244 male, 46 female; aged 41–80) who underwent coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery at Mordovian Republic Hospital between 2017 and 2021, examining whether the number of shunts and internal thoracic arteries (ITAs) used influenced postoperative complications. Most patients (95.86%) underwent on-pump surgery. Reported complications included arrhythmia, psychosis, stroke, myocardial infarction, hydrothorax, re-sternotomy, dyspnea, and sternal wound infection, with postoperative hydrothorax being the most frequent. Five patients died. Findings showed elderly patients faced higher risks of psychosis, arrhythmia, stroke, and prolonged ICU and total hospitalization. Hydrothorax was associated with low BMI, prolonged aortic cross-clamp time, and longer cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) time. Diabetes and its complications were linked to longer hospitalization. The number of complications correlated with age, CPB time, aortic cross-clamp time, and hospitalization duration, and was increased by preoperative progressive angina and post-myocardial infarction myocardial sclerosis. However, no statistically significant association was found between the number of complications and the number of shunts or ITAs used. The study concludes that advanced age, prolonged operative times, progressive angina, and PMIMS are key factors in post-CABG complication development.

The author urges national legislators to enact a graduated inheritance tax, with rates increasing with the amount inherited and possibly with the beneficiary's remoteness of kin, while keeping the tax small on moderate estates to encourage thrift and the desire to provide for one's children; the prime aim is to place a growing burden on swollen fortunes. Progress should be gradual. Inheritance taxes were previously imposed by acts of 1797, 1862, and 1898, and the Supreme Court upheld the constitutionality of the Civil War succession tax and the 1898 inheritance tax. An income tax differs, concerning the adjustment of burdens to benefits rather than the perpetuation of large fortunes; the 1894 income tax law was held unconstitutional by a one-vote majority, though the Court's hesitation may suggest a constitutional income tax is possible. Constitutional amendment should be a last resort if legislation fails.

Coach Sutter discusses centermen matchups, noting Tanner and Tyler played together in the American League, and praises Selke nominee Kopy as a top two-way player with exceptional playoff playmaking who logs the most minutes in crucial situations. He describes his players as tenacious rather than physical, says success comes from the complete package rather than star power, and credits preparation and leadership for the young, playoff-proven team's maturity. He notes one player provides strong leadership and consistency, calls Slava a good player adjusting to his first Stanley Cup Final game, says both teams are fast, declines elimination-game questions, and says his top goalie will probably play tomorrow.

Lewis Roberts v. David B. Prosser and Charles R. King (General Term, Third Department, September 1871) affirmed a $100 judgment for the plaintiff in an action for false imprisonment. After a $2,245.71 judgment was obtained against the plaintiff and Myers, assignees of an insolvent debtor, in a creditor's suit to compel an accounting and distribution of assigned funds, the defendants—the judgment creditor's attorneys—issued execution against the assignees' persons, and the plaintiff was arrested and jailed. The issue was whether that prior suit was "an action for money received in a fiduciary capacity" under section 179 of the Code, permitting arrest. Parker, J. held it was not: the suit sought a judicial determination of amounts the assignees received and ought to have received, and the statute covers only actions primarily and simply for recovery of money, addressing direct fiduciary relations such as factor, agent, or broker, not trustees accountable to multiple creditors. The execution was therefore unauthorized, and the judgment was affirmed with costs; Miller, J. concurred, and James, J. expressed no opinion.

America Saves Week, held annually since 2007 and coordinated by America Saves and the American Savings Education Council, promotes good savings behavior. The 2017 event runs February 27 to March 4, featuring daily focuses, engagement activities, and resources for registered participants.

After his cousin Jonathan Jeffrey died of a drug overdose, St. Olaf student Erik Brust honored their shared idea for a fruity, creamy frozen treat by founding JonnyPops. With classmate Connor Wray, he developed a recipe of fruit, real cream, cane sugar, and salt, launching at Twin Cities farmers markets in 2012. The company expanded into professional distribution, entered grocery retail in 2014 with about 50 Minnesota stores, and now has 10,000 distribution points nationwide. Brust and Wray, named to Forbes' 30 Under 30, work full-time as CEO and CFO. A new Delights line launches in March, and the company's "Better Pop for a Better World" mission includes uplifting stick messages and fundraising for addiction treatment organizations.

Addressing his reelection, the speaker expresses gratitude and considers himself the instrument rather than the cause of the union shown in the election. He recalls the recently concluded war with a powerful nation, which drove commerce from the sea, invaded the frontiers, and added $120,000,000 to the public debt, and describes the defensive measures adopted afterward—coastal fortifications and an augmented navy under laws of 1815 and 1816—as economical, peace-preserving steps rather than acts of hostility. In foreign affairs, he affirms continued strict neutrality between Spain and its South American colonies, describes actions against buccaneering in neighboring seas, and reports the ratified treaty with Spain, which settled the disputed western boundary, provided for citizens' claims, and ceded Florida, an acquisition he deems highly important. A treaty with Britain revived the commercial convention for ten years and adjusted fishing differences; negotiations with France continue; relations with the Barbary Powers are maintained, and naval forces protect commerce while suppressing the slave trade and piracy. Nearly $67,000,000 of the public debt has been paid without direct taxes or excise, though depressed prices have diminished revenue, requiring loans and possibly internal taxes if the deficiency persists. He proposes securing individual land rights and educational funds for Indian tribes, notes Europe's unsettled condition while pledging neutrality and defense of maritime rights, and celebrates the nation's growth, territorial expansion, and elective, single-order system of government.

Players credit their Stanley Cup win to handling playoff adversity, confidence from playing at home, and an early-season emphasis on being tough in their own building, which Pat prioritized upon being hired. John became the defensive go-to player after Holik's departure, and others stepped up when Joe was injured. Injuries and coast-to-coast travel during a seven-game postseason took a toll. Despite losing leaders like Bobby Holik and adding new players through trades, the team grew together. One player says the Mighty Ducks' standout deserved the Conn Smythe, but winning the Cup matters more. Another recalls a past missed opportunity and blown series lead, saying it looked like the same thing was happening this year before the team pulled it off. A final speaker says it is too early to call the team a dynasty but hopes to build on the win with young players.

Nvidia will continue sponsoring H-1B visa employees despite Trump's new $100,000 fee, which could cost the company an estimated $147.3 million based on visas approved in 2025. The fee applies only to new applicants, not renewals or current visa-holders. In an internal memo, CEO Jensen Huang wrote that legal immigration remains essential to U.S. leadership in technology and ideas. Though initially positive about the changes, Huang later said the fee "probably sets the bar a little too high" while noting it eliminates abuse of the visa system.

On Friday, October 6th, analysts issued numerous price target changes. BNP Paribas set targets for several German firms: Covestro (€64, sell), BASF (€96, buy), Evonik (€29, neutral), Linde (€175, neutral), Lanxess (€65, neutral), and Wacker Chemie (€110, neutral). Targets were raised for AdvanSix, Deckers, New Oriental, Netflix, Plug Power, Constellation Brands (by Stifel and Royal Bank of Canada), 2U, and Yum China. Ascena and Rite Aid saw lowered targets. New targets included Costco ($185, buy), Inovio ($13, buy), Eli Lilly ($86, hold), and Mallinckrodt ($70, buy).

This protocol describes a systematic review assessing the relationship between viral burden measures (such as serial rt-PCR Ct values) and the presence and duration of infectious SARS-CoV-2 in viral culture among solid organ and hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients. The review will search LitCovid, medRxiv, Google Scholar, and the WHO Covid-19 database from November 2019 to December 31, 2021, with no language restrictions. Studies reporting respiratory sample viral burden data alongside viral culture results will be included; studies using only post-mortem or non-respiratory samples, or lacking viral cultures, will be excluded. Screening and data extraction will be performed by independent reviewers with arbitration by a third reviewer. Quality will be assessed using five criteria covering diagnosis, reporting, study duration, and rt-PCR and culture methods. Data will be reported per PRISMA standards and reviewed narratively rather than pooled, due to differences in laboratory practices. Funding is provided by the NIHR Evidence Synthesis Working Group and the University of Calgary.

The President has been murdered—the fourth such death in the Republic's history—and his constitutional successor assumes the Executive chair, demonstrating the strength of popular government. The speaker pledges to honor his predecessor's aspirations and continue his measures to correct abuses, enforce economy, and advance prosperity. With the country prosperous, fiscal policy settled, and no foreign threats or need for a special congressional session, he assumes office relying on divine guidance and the American people.

A fossil unearthed in southwestern China reveals a pregnant Dinocephalosaurus, a long-necked fish-eating marine reptile from the Triassic Period (about 245 million years ago), with a developing embryo, indicating it gave birth to live young rather than laying eggs. It is the first archosauromorph known to be viviparous. The creature was fully marine, roughly 13 feet long, and determined its offspring's sex genetically, like mammals and birds.

The Nebraska Supreme Court affirmed a judgment in favor of Farmers State Bank of Craig on a $3,000 promissory note against Samuel J. Lydick. Lydick alleged the note was given as partial payment on a prior $5,000 note lacking consideration, and that bank officer Everett J. Martin fraudulently induced him to purchase Missouri Valley Cattle Loan Company stock. The trial court withdrew issues lacking evidentiary support, and the jury found the bank was a holder in due course—having purchased the note for value, before maturity, in good faith, and without notice of any defect—and returned a verdict for the bank; the jury also found for Martin on the fraud claim. The court held that a payee receiving a negotiable instrument in good faith, for value, before maturity, and without notice of infirmity, from a holder to whom it was negotiated as a completed instrument, is a holder in due course, precluding defenses of fraud and failure of consideration between the maker and the prior holder. The jury's finding that Martin was not a party to the fraud was held sufficient to sustain the verdict, and the court's instructions were found free from error.

Lincolnshire County Council has approved a care leavers strategy. Corporate parenting manager Andrew Morris said the council supports care leavers beyond 18, as research shows they struggle to pay bills. Measures include council tax discounts up to 100% for ages 18-21 and extended government support to age 25. The council helps with university costs and driving licences. The leaving care budget is £1.2 million, covering 300 young people, with over 600 in care.

Amazon Prime Day 2 officially runs October 7–8, 2025, but early deals on WIRED-approved, hand-tested gear have already begun. The WIRED Reviews team plans to cover the sale with multiple stories and a liveblog. As of the September 30, 2025 update, ten new deals were added, including the Apple iPad (2025, A16) for $299 ($149 off), Apple MacBook Air (M4, 2025) for $799 ($200 off), Arlo Pro 5S Security Camera for $100 ($80 off), Amazon Kindle Scribe (2024) for $300 ($100 off), and Anker MagGo Power Bank (10K) for $70 ($20 off). Other discounted items include earbuds, chargers, power banks, keyboards, and fitness trackers. Ultrahuman rings will no longer be sold in the US after October 21 due to an FTC ruling.

China has modernised its military for about 20 years to gain hard power matching its soft power, defend regional interests such as South China Sea claims and sea lanes, support initiatives like AIIB and OBOR, and mitigate rising American military presence in the Indo-Pacific. Since the late 1990s, the PLA has become a modern, nearly unrecognisable force, and China more assertive; the final outcome remains open.

North Korea's defaulted debt, once seen as a bet on a future economic opening, may move further out of reach after new UN sanctions imposed following Pyongyang's missile tests. The country has about $1 billion in syndicated loans in default since the 1980s, with total debt including interest estimated at roughly $3 billion. The debt was repackaged in 1997 into transferable securities through NK Debt Corporation. Trading, active since around 2000, froze in early 2013 after UN sanctions, with no trades seen in the past three to four years. The Franklin Emerging Markets Debt Opportunities Fund holds $15.5 million principal of these bonds. Experts say resolution is distant, with interest arrears estimated at four to five times the principal, likening North Korea to "Cuba in spades."

Latin American stocks rebounded on Monday from last week's selloff as tensions between the United States and North Korea eased, boosting appetite for risky assets. Mexico's stock index rose 1.1 percent after its biggest weekly decline in eight months, while Brazil's Bovespa touched its highest level since May, led by gains in Cia Paranaense de Energia shares. Currency moves were subdued, with the Mexican peso firming 0.3 percent ahead of NAFTA negotiations and the Brazilian real fluctuating ahead of an expected fiscal goal revision.

Materials characterization of compositionally complex materials often requires complementary techniques: X-ray diffraction (XRD), which probes long-range periodic structure, and X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) spectroscopy, which measures short-range, element-specific local structure. These measurements are typically performed at synchrotron facilities, but beamtime is limited, and conventional homogeneous mapping strategies (fixed-step raster scans or geometric grids) are mismatched to spatially inhomogeneous samples, potentially missing scientifically valuable features.

To address this, the authors developed a modular, open-source framework for AI-driven, multi-modal synchrotron experiments at NSLS-II, built on the Bluesky software suite, queue servers, Tiled data access, and JupyterHub. An ensemble of AI agents performs data processing, analysis, and interpretation, while human-controlled adjudicators moderate measurement requests, ensuring researchers retain oversight and that agents cannot interact with safety interlocks. Agents are plug-and-play, configurable, and deployed on virtual machines.

Autonomous operation follows a Bayesian optimization loop: K-means clustering reduces data dimensionality, a Gaussian process regressor trained on a scientific value function serves as a surrogate model, and an acquisition function (upper confidence bound) selects subsequent measurements.

The framework was demonstrated by synchronously orchestrating XRD at the PDF beamline and XAFS at the BMM beamline on identical Al-Ni-Pt thin-film combinatorial libraries. EXAFS analysis yielded composition ranges of Al (18.2–44.3%), Ni (21.8–50.9%), and Pt (21.8–53.6%), while diffraction revealed face-centered cubic and face-centered tetragonal phases, though data complexities limited further structural conclusions.

A digital twin using a simulated Al-Li-Fe oxide combinatorial library enabled benchmarking of measurement strategies. In silico campaigns showed AI-driven mapping achieved 98.9% model accuracy after 5% of possible measurements, surpassing geometric grid (95.9%) and random sampling (96.6%) approaches, and better resolved phase boundaries and localized minor phases.

The paper further discusses supporting infrastructure (network upgrades, Tiled, Bluesky Adaptive), operating modes ranging from manual to fully autonomous, automation levels 0–3, and the choice between raw data and physics-based scientific products as agent inputs. The authors conclude that the framework enables real-time, synchronous, multi-beamline AI-driven experiments with human-in-the-loop oversight and provides a foundation for routine collaborative human-AI experimentation at user facilities.

Let's Grow Kids, a Vermont child care advocacy organization founded in 2015 by Rick Davis and led by Aly Richards, was designed from the start to sunset after ten years. Over the decade, it raised more than $70 million in private philanthropy, grew to 40 staffers, and supported Act 76, the 2023 law creating Vermont's near-universal child care program. Since implementation, more than 100 new child care programs have opened, creating over 1,000 spaces, 230 early childhood educator jobs, and tuition assistance for an additional 4,000 children. The organization officially ended operations on Oct. 3. Leaders credit the time-limited structure with sharpening focus, accelerating fundraising, attracting talent, and encouraging staff to move into roles at permanent organizations now handling child care financing, workforce, data, and advocacy. Remaining staff transitioned to the Let's Grow Kids Action Network, a 501(c)(4) tasked with protecting Act 76's funding provisions. Vermont's program is not fully universal, as 80 to 90 percent of families with children in care are subsidy-eligible, and officials from several other states have contacted Richards about the state's approach.

Four people have been arrested in the shooting death of 39-year-old Jennifer Bartell in Portsmouth, Virginia. Court documents say Joshua Bowen allegedly shot Bartell on March 14 after a Facebook argument involving Bowen's girlfriend, Albany Pierce, and Bartell's daughter escalated. Pierce, her mother Shaunicka Cooley, and Shyrayno Jackson face accessory charges.

A federal judge ruled that Nirvana's 1991 album cover depicting a naked baby underwater is not child pornography. Spencer Elden, photographed as a 4-month-old, had filed a 2021 lawsuit under a federal law providing civil remedies for victims of certain crimes committed as minors. Judge Fernando Olguin found that, aside from Elden's nudity, no factor suggested the image was lascivious, comparing it to a family photo of a nude child bathing.

PenFed Credit Union President and CEO James Schenck was named Large Business Philanthropist of the Year by Volunteer Alexandria at the 20th annual Business Philanthropy Summit. PenFed supports the Washington metro area through the credit union and the PenFed Foundation. Recent donations include $300,000 to Serve Our Willing Warriors, $125,000 to the Kennedy Center, $100,000 to DC Habitat for Humanity, $75,000 to the Military Officers Association of America, and $15,000 to Bunker Labs, plus Gary Sinise Foundation donations and the recently launched Veteran Entrepreneur Investment Program. The PenFed Foundation has provided more than $30 million to the military community since 2001. Schenck, a West Point and Harvard Business School graduate who flew Blackhawk helicopters in Korea, volunteers as the Foundation's unpaid CEO and was elected 2017 National Credit Union Hero of the Year. PenFed, established in 1935, is America's second-largest federal credit union with over 1.6 million members and $23 billion in assets.

A Florida Museum of Natural History study by Bret Boyd and David Reed found that lice parasitizing primates and humans have hosted their bacterial symbionts continuously for at least 20 to 25 million years, contradicting earlier suggestions of multiple symbiont replacements. The researchers sequenced endosymbiont genomes from human, chimpanzee, gorilla, and red colobus monkey lice, finding them remarkably small (530,000-570,000 base pairs). The study revealed extensive genome remodeling over 25 million years, with genes critical to symbiosis clustered together, and much of the genome devoted to B-vitamin synthesis. The findings offer insights into bacterial genome evolution and primate evolutionary history.

This study examined whether resting-state functional connectivity (FC) of the nucleus accumbens (NAc) could predict the course of ADHD symptoms in 54 adults newly diagnosed with ADHD. Participants underwent fMRI and clinical assessment (Wender-Reimherr-Interview) at diagnosis and follow-up approximately three years later; 34 continued stimulant treatment while 20 had discontinued medication. Higher baseline symptom severity correlated with lower FC between the NAc and right paracingulate gyrus (default mode network). Symptom improvement over time was associated with reduced FC between the NAc and right anterior insula (salience network). Regarding medication status, higher NAc–posterior insula FC predicted improvement in treated patients but worsening in non-responders. The authors conclude that FC between the reward system, default mode, and salience networks may serve as a biomarker for ADHD prognosis and stimulant response, while noting limitations including small sample size and the need for replication.

A new study led by Dr. Valentin Bickel of the University of Bern, using deep learning on over 50,000 satellite images from ESA's CaSSIS and HRSC cameras, found that Martian winds and dust devils reach speeds of up to 44 m/s (about 160 km/h)—much faster than previously measured. The team analyzed stereo images of about 300 dust devils to track their movement. These stronger winds likely lift far more dust into the Martian atmosphere than previously assumed, significantly influencing the planet's weather and climate. The findings, produced with collaborators including the Open University and the German Aerospace Center, will help model the Martian atmosphere, assess risks, and improve planning for future landed missions. Researchers plan continued coordinated observations using CaSSIS and HRSC.

The Aedes aegypti mosquito, known today for spreading Zika, caused Philadelphia's 1793 yellow fever epidemic. A hot, dry summer created mosquito breeding grounds, and Caribbean refugees brought the disease. Symptoms included pain, fever, bleeding, vomiting, and yellowed skin, often ending in death. Benjamin Rush advised residents to flee; about 5,000 people—over 10 percent of the population—died by November. Rush and other doctors tried bloodletting, purifying the air with smoke, and quarantine without success; the mosquito's role as a disease vector was discovered more than a century later, leading to sanitation and drainage improvements. The last North American outbreak occurred in New Orleans in 1905. Brazil now faces its worst yellow fever outbreak in decades, with 326 confirmed cases and 220 deaths since December 2016. An effective vaccine exists, and Penn researchers are developing DNA and mRNA Zika vaccines.

Rachael Caplan, 29, suffers from Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS), a rare disease causing constant, severe nerve-injury-type pain that has left her bedridden on the top floor of her parents' Thornhill home, unable to go downstairs or leave the house since August 2016. Formerly athletic with a law degree, she first developed symptoms seven years ago during law school at Queen's University, when a hip injury worsened after acupuncture treatment in 2012. Diagnosis took a year and a half, coming from pain specialist Dr. David Shulman in June 2013. CRPS affects just over 9,000 Canadians annually, with more than half in Ontario, and typically begins in a hand or foot before spreading. Early diagnosis is crucial, with an 80 to 90 per cent treatment success rate in the first three months, but after six months reversal is unlikely. Caplan's case is severe; standard treatments, including physiotherapy and opioids, worsened her pain, leading her to about 60 healthcare providers and trips to the U.S. Recently, green light therapy improved her sleep. Her friends launched a social media campaign, including an ice water challenge with the hashtag #AceThisFire, to raise awareness, with videos gaining over 20,000 views. Caplan hopes her story leads to faster diagnoses, better treatments, or a cure, and ultimately remission.

Gulf Island Fabrication (GIFI), which builds offshore platforms, support vessels, and complex steel structures through its Fabrication, Shipyards, and Services divisions, has been hurt by an oversupplied offshore support vessel market and operational problems, including a $23.9 million loss on two multi-purpose support vessels built for Hornbeck Offshore, producing a fourth-quarter loss of $24.3 million on revenue of $37.3 million. Positives include essentially no debt and a backlog concentrated in the shipyards segment, along with selection as prime contractor for SeaOne Caribbean's fuels supply project and a memorandum of understanding with EEW for an offshore wind project. The core thesis is valuation: with a market capitalization of roughly $120 million, GIFI is selling Texas facilities carried at about $100 million, with the South Yard under a $55 million purchase option agreement with Buckeye Pipe Line Co. If these sales close near book value, the remainder of the company would be priced at about $30 million. Shares have fallen 40% from recent highs; the author views them as attractive on valuation, with technical support at $7.

A state audit found Utah's alcohol department overcharged customers $1,161 after prices were entered wrong during a markup increase, losing $186 on other sales. It plans refunds and added a program to flag errors. Auditors found a failed $4.6 million transfer to school lunch and public safety programs, later corrected.

European statesmen will prioritize obtaining means of recuperation, as demobilization risks either insurrectionary discontent or economic crisis. Control over raw materials, transportation, markets, and credit will be the strongest instrument of negotiation. The disputed belt from the Baltic to the Persian Gulf will likely remain within German lines, and German supremacy in the Near East represents her victory thus far. Since Mittel-Europa cannot be a closed economic system, Germany must regain foreign markets to pay for essential supplies from the outer world. Two schools of German imperialism exist: the Fatherland Party, which seeks access through military and naval power, and the Kühlmann group, which favors accommodation with the western nations. Both agree on dominating eastern Europe and needing outer-world supplies, differing only on method. Belgium is the pivot of German policy, as its control would prevent England from landing armies in France. Bethmann considered an "administrative division of Belgium."

QoCGM (Quantification of Continuous Glucose Monitoring) is an open-source MATLAB tool for comprehensive CGM data analysis, developed to address gaps in existing tools such as cgmquantify, iglu, GLU, rGV, and CGManalyzer, particularly regarding newer metrics, night/day analyses, and day-to-day variation. It processes CSV files containing timestamps and glucose values in two stages: preprocessing (duplicate removal, identification of missing periods, and gap filling via PCHIP interpolation or period removal) and metric derivation. Metrics span six domains: basic descriptive statistics, time-in-range metrics, glycemic risk indicators (GRI, LBGI/HBGI, GRADE), glycemic variability metrics (CONGA, MAGE, Mobility, DTpM, day-to-day SD), glycemic control indicators (fasting glucose proxy, GMI, hypoglycemia events), and multiscale entropy. Selected metrics are computed separately for daytime and nighttime and include day-to-day standard deviations. In an example application using the first seven days of CGM data from 324 participants with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes in the DiaMonT trial, an R² analysis showed substantial overlap among many metrics, while a few—including day-to-day SD of TIR and mean glucose, MCI, Mobility, and DTpM—showed low R² values (<0.5) with all other metrics, suggesting they capture unique information. Diurnal and nocturnal TIR metrics also differed significantly. The authors conclude that QoCGM may help identify clinically relevant CGM metrics, though further research on clinical implications is needed.

The District Court of Appeal of Florida, Second District, denied Sarasota County's petition for writ of certiorari seeking review of a declaratory statement issued by the Department of Administration. The County had petitioned the Department under Section 120.565, Florida Statutes, asking whether a crude oil splitter facility proposed by Manatee Energy Company, a subsidiary of Belcher Oil Company, in Manatee County should be considered a development of regional impact (DRI) under Chapter 380, the Florida Environmental Land and Water Management Act of 1972. In December 1976, the Department issued a declaratory statement concluding that the DRI definition in Section 380.06(1) was limited to projects described in Fla.Admin.Code Rule 22F-2, and no hearing was held before its issuance. The Manatee Chapter of the Isaac Walton League of America appeared as amicus curiae, taking a position identical to the County's.

The court held that Sarasota County lacked standing. It reasoned that the mere issuance of an unfavorable declaratory statement does not confer standing, and that the County did not fall within the categories of entities—regional planning agencies, appropriate local governments, the state planning agency, or developers—authorized to initiate the DRI process under Chapter 380. The court suggested the County petition those statutorily designated entities instead.

Chief Judge Boardman concurred specially, noting two alternatives: proceeding through the regional planning agency under Section 380.06(3), or initiating proceedings under the Florida Environmental Protection Act of 1971, Section 403.412. Judge Scheb dissented, arguing the declaratory statement constituted final agency action subject to judicial review and was incorrect as a matter of law, because the state land planning agency retains authority to determine whether unlisted developments are DRIs; he would have remanded to the Department.

Dunkin' Donuts will launch its fall lineup on Aug. 28, bringing back pumpkin spice and adding maple, pecan, and bacon flavors, including pumpkin cream cheese, maple pecan coffees and lattes, and a maple sugar bacon breakfast sandwich. Rivals McDonald's and Starbucks have not yet announced this year's releases. Dunkin' has reported seven straight quarters of better-than-expected earnings, boosted by new and limited-time products.

ICICI Bank's mortgage loan portfolio crossed Rs 1.5 trillion, making it the largest private player in the segment, with a target of Rs 2 trillion by FY20 at 15% annual growth. The mortgage book is half of its Rs 3 trillion retail portfolio. Growth, driven by tier II and III towns, is supported by digitisation—2,000 housing projects approved online—and a planned 50% expansion of its 1,050 loan processing centres.

The passage presents a modelling study estimating COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness over time. Building on Khoury et al.'s approach using neutralizing antibody titres as a correlate of protection, the authors fit a mechanistic model of biphasic immune waning and boosting to vaccine effectiveness data from England for three vaccines (AZD1222, BNT162b2, and mRNA-1273) against mild disease, hospitalisation, and death, covering the Delta and Omicron BA.1/BA.2 variants. The model estimates a 6.5-fold reduction in vaccine-induced immunity against Omicron relative to Delta, an initial immune half-life of 33 days, and a longer-term half-life of 580 days. mRNA-1273 generated the highest immune levels, followed by BNT162b2 and AZD1222. Effectiveness against hospitalisation 180 days after boosting was estimated at 49.5% (AZD1222), 69.8% (mRNA-1273), and 63.7% (BNT162b2). Applying a 1.61-fold NAT increase from the Moderna bivalent vaccine, the model predicts similar short-term protection to the original vaccine but better sustained protection at one year (77.9% versus 60.0% against hospitalisation). The authors note limitations, including the inability to separate infection- and vaccine-induced immunity, the lack of immunological measurements, and difficulty distinguishing COVID-19-related hospitalisations from those with other causes.

A coach said a player was fine and just given a day off. He noted second periods were a problem in two Boston games and the team must make every shift count. He believes two players are playing better than their point totals indicate, crediting the opposing goaltender and defensemen. The team maintains a one-game-at-a-time mentality, and while agreeing the trophy is hardest to win, he says the group has been ready since day one.

A survey of 2,000 British adults by Tweak Mattress found the average Brit wakes three times a night, with one in ten waking 7-10 times. Causes include toilet trips (47%), snoring (41%), being edged out of bed (25%), aches and pains (19%), nightmares (11%), tossing and turning (10.5%), partner talking or phone light (10% each), TV or reading (4.6%), and anxiety (6%). Psychologist Robert Stewart said sleep quality depends on sleep hygiene and sleep cycles, with REM the lightest stage, and advised creating a good environment, such as earplugs or a comfortable mattress.

This article backtests Larry Connors' R3 strategy (RSI 2) from his 2009 book "High Probability ETF Trading" to see if it still performs 12 years later. The mean-reversion strategy requires the close to be above the 200-day moving average, a three-day consecutive drop in the 2-day RSI (with the first day's drop from a reading below 60), entry when the 2-day RSI is below 10, and exit when it is above 70. Tested with Amibroker on ETFs until December 2020, the authors could not fully replicate Connors' original results. As a portfolio of 25 ETFs (2000–2020), it produced 992 trades, a 75% win ratio, 0.68% average gain per trade, a 2.08 profit factor, a -16% maximum drawdown in August 2011, and a 6.47% CAGR. On QQQ/SPY, the profit factor was 3.37 with a 2.69% CAGR. The authors conclude the strategy still works, performs best on equity markets, and could be improved with small changes.

Treasury bills worth N62.4 billion (91-day and 182-day maturities) and an OMO maturity of N168.1 billion were expected in the market this week. System liquidity stayed negative last week due to primary market issuances and the CBN's Retail SMIS forex auction; the CBN mopped up N28.6 billion via OMO sales, pushing OBB and overnight rates to 105.0% and 107.8% midweek before they closed at 55.8% and 59.3% on Friday. The treasury bills market closed bearish, with average yield rising 61 basis points to 18.5 per cent. In the forex market, the CBN continued interventions and auctioned $100 million in SMIS; the naira held flat at N305.55/$1 officially, appreciated to N365.91/$1 on NAFEX, and remained at N367/$1 on the parallel market. The bond market was bearish, with average yield flat at 16.8 per cent. The Federal Executive Council approved dollar-backed treasury bills with tenors extended to two and three years to reduce borrowing costs, alongside the 2018-2020 MTEF pegging oil at $45. The I&E window attracted $4 billion from foreign investors since April, and the Bankers' Committee said the economy was on the verge of exiting recession.

After conservative Texas politicians targeted faculty teaching about gender identity, six Texas public university systems ordered reviews of curricula, syllabi, and course descriptions. Texas A&M demoted two administrators and pushed out its president after criticism of a gender identity lesson not listed in a course catalog description; its Board of Regents ordered an audit of every course. The University of North Texas, University of Texas, University of Houston, and Texas Woman's University systems also launched reviews, some citing a gubernatorial order asserting only two sexes exist—though no current federal or state law prohibits teaching about transgender identity. It is unclear how systems will respond after the reviews conclude. Conservative politicians have found professors through syllabi posted online, often via Simple Syllabus, a platform used by over 500 institutions; some universities restrict access, but Texas House Bill 2504 requires public syllabi. A University of Houston lecturer was targeted by a conservative news site using information from the platform. A Simple Syllabus spokesperson said the company has received no targeting reports and offers privacy features. Professors are now advised to limit public syllabus details, though some are encouraged to include everything to avoid complaints.

This study investigated the effects of COVID-19 mRNA vaccine (BNT162b2) boosters on insulin resistance and glucose control. In a longitudinal clinical trial of 155 adults (healthy controls, pre-diabetic, and diabetic subjects), immune responses to the vaccine were similar across all groups. However, booster shots significantly elevated HbA1c, HOMA-IR, triglycerides, and TyG index in pre-diabetic and diabetic patients, indicating worsened glucose intolerance and insulin resistance, while fasting blood glucose and insulin levels remained unchanged. Approximately 61.1% of diabetic subjects showed impaired insulin sensitivity, and 66.7% had increased cardiovascular complication risks. HOMA-IR was positively correlated with immune response markers. In mouse experiments, repeated COVID-19 vaccination impaired glucose tolerance and insulin signaling through reduced insulin-induced Akt phosphorylation, without affecting insulin secretion. Metformin at a clinically relevant dosage alleviated vaccine-induced insulin resistance in mice without compromising the vaccine's protective immune responses. The authors suggest that subjects with impaired glucose tolerance should monitor blood glucose homeostasis after COVID-19 vaccination, and propose metformin as a potential adjunctive treatment for maintaining glucose control post-vaccination. Potential mechanisms involve SARS-CoV-2 spike protein binding TLR4 and estrogen receptors, affecting insulin signaling pathways.

Love in the Time of Chasmosaurs is a dinosaur website featuring factual reports from scientists and paleontologists, paleoart in varied styles, and humorous reviews of children's books, toys, films, TV shows, and museum exhibits. Active since 2009, it posts nearly weekly plus a monthly dinosaur news round-up. Its name plays on Gabriel Garcia-Marquez's "Love in the Time of Cholera"; a Chasmosaur is a dinosaur formerly called Triceratops. The reviewer recommends it to fans of dinosaurs, science, or humor.

Olivia Munn, despite clear mammograms, an ultrasound, and negative genetic testing, was diagnosed with stage 1 breast cancer at 43 after a two-minute online lifetime risk assessment showed she had a 37% risk, prompting her to get an MRI. Her mother, Kim Munn, took the same assessment and was diagnosed with and treated for stage 1 breast cancer in July 2025. Munn says the assessment should be standard care; those scoring 20% or higher are encouraged to speak with their doctors and get screened sooner.

Hugh Jackman, 48, is undergoing another treatment for basal cell carcinoma, the most common and rarely fatal form of skin cancer. Previously treated at least four times, first in November 2013, he has upcoming films Logan and The Greatest Showman on Earth.
The Eighth Circuit denied the petitions for en banc and panel rehearing; Judge Bye would have granted rehearing; Judge Benton did not participate.

Newly elected Progressive Conservative leader Doug Ford launched his election campaign at the Toronto Congress Centre before an enthusiastic crowd. The event aimed to unify the party after its leadership contest, with defeated rival Christine Elliott embracing Ford on stage and other rivals Caroline Mulroney and Tanya Granic Allen also attending. Kory Teneycke is expected to serve as campaign manager and Jeff Silverstein as communications manager. Ford targeted Premier Kathleen Wynne and the Liberals over debt and spending, and promised "a day of prosperity" for all Ontarians. Party candidates expressed confidence, though supporters acknowledged the campaign ahead will be difficult despite favourable polls.

Valeant Pharmaceuticals, J. Michael Pearson, Pershing Square Capital Management, and William Ackman entered into a litigation management agreement concerning a putative class action in California. The agreement covers Allergan litigation cost-sharing, terminates November 1, 2017 absent a settlement, and includes a mutual release of claims.

Stan Lee, 95, was rushed to Cedar-Sinai hospital due to shortness of breath and an irregular heartbeat. His condition remained stable, and the hospitalization was precautionary. Now discharged, Lee will return periodically for monitoring and told ABC News he "feels great." He last appeared at the "Black Panther" premiere on Jan. 30, posing with Chadwick Boseman. The film, co-created with Jack Kirby in 1966, opens Feb. 16.

A hockey player and captain reflects on his team's Stanley Cup final victory. He says experience from big games and good habits developed over the season pay off in high-stakes games, and the team maintained its routine of optional morning skates. He states he did not put extra pressure on himself during the playoffs, crediting the team's collective play rather than individual effort. He describes mixed emotions of excitement while trying to keep things routine, and recalls playing minor hockey in his hometown, including the Joe Lamontagne tournament. He calls the championship a dream come true, noting he would have preferred winning in four games, and credits shot-blocking, goaltending, and contributions from many players, as well as the sacrifices of his parents, coaches, and others who influenced him. He describes a knee injury from a collision with Franzen, when his knee was jammed against the boards; despite numbing treatment and pain pills, he could not stop or turn and chose to watch rather than risk mistakes against Datsyuk and Zetterberg. He notes teammate Gonchar's long wait for a title and that both teams returned to the final after the previous year. He dismisses thoughts about fans reacting to his injury and praises Pittsburgh fans' loyalty, noting the team won its fourth road series, sold out home games for three straight years, and finished the victory after the previous year's devastating loss.

Severe storms with tornadoes moved across the Southeast Monday night, damaging homes and downing trees, with forecasters warning that more than 29 million people could be threatened. At least three tornadoes were confirmed in northern Alabama, where power outages and roof damage were reported, including significant damage at Jacksonville State University. No injuries were reported. Forecasters warned of possible intense tornadoes, hail up to 3 inches in diameter, and wind gusts to 70 mph. Alabama raised its emergency threat level, schools dismissed early, and Gov. Kay Ivey urged residents to prepare safety plans.

This prospective study compared inflammatory and oxidative stress markers between 101 cardiomyopathy patients (43 with dilated cardiomyopathy and 58 with other cardiomyopathies) and 101 healthy controls. Blood samples were analyzed for CRP, TNF-α, IL-6, NT-proBNP, MDA, and glutathione peroxidase (GPX) activity using ELISA and biochemical assays. CRP and TNF-α concentrations were significantly higher in cardiomyopathy patients than in controls. TNF-α showed positive correlations with GPX and MDA, and NT-proBNP was associated with both MDA and GPX. GPX activity was positively related to NT-proBNP across all cardiomyopathy patients. The authors conclude that inflammatory and oxidative stress markers are correlated in cardiomyopathy patients but not in normal cases, suggesting cross-talk between these two cellular processes in late-stage cardiomyopathy.

Premier Li Keqiang said China will further open its economy, allowing foreign and domestic firms to compete on equal terms, increasing access to services and manufacturing sectors, and lowering import tariffs. He stated there will be no forced technology transfers and China will better protect intellectual property rights. These pledges come amid trade war concerns following US President Trump's announced steel and aluminium tariffs, with new tariffs on Chinese goods expected.

Amadeus FiRe AG issued a correction on 15.02.2017 of a voting rights notification originally published on 10.02.2017, under Article 26, Section 1 of the German Securities Trading Act (WpHG). The notification concerns BNP Paribas Investment Partners (Paris, France), with BNP Paribas Investment Partners Belgium S.A. holding the shares directly. The threshold was crossed on 09 Feb 2017 due to acquisition/disposal of shares with voting rights. Cardiac surgery patients frequently require blood transfusions, but a 2006 study linked transfusions after AVR or CABG to significantly reduced survival. While the U.S. national transfusion rate for these procedures averaged 48.9%, Huntington University Hospital's (HUH) rate was around 71% between 2011 and 2013. Dr. Frank Young, who joined HUH's Center for Cardiac Medicine in 2011, initiated a blood conservation project aiming to reduce blood product use by two-thirds within one year, bringing transfusion rates to the national average, saving $2.5 million annually, and saving an estimated 125 lives per year over 10 years. Young faced challenges including physician autonomy, his status as a newcomer, and HUH's complex organizational structure, in which surgical team members reported through separate chains of command and no one reported to surgeons; nurses could even order transfusions without notifying the surgeon. A hospital committee found that 51% of cardiac patients had bleeding-related complications, costing nearly $8 million in 2013. Young planned to apply techniques such as autologous blood harvest and retrograde autologous priming. While some staff supported the project, veteran surgeons were skeptical of changing established routines.

Ajman's Ruler issued a decree reducing the tourism tax on hotels and tourism companies from 10 to 7 percent, effective immediately until December 31, to promote tourism and support Ajman Vision 2021's 700,000-visitor goal.

This passage is a Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) for clinical trial ZEA-DNK-02170 evaluating dasiglucagon.

**Sample Size:** The primary comparison is dasiglucagon 0.6 mg versus placebo. Based on phase 2 results (median time to a 20 mg/dL glucose increase of ~10 minutes for dasiglucagon; >50 minutes assumed for placebo), a 2-sided log-rank test with 45-minute follow-up achieves 90% power at 5% significance with 20 patients on dasiglucagon and 10 on placebo. Ten patients receiving GlucaGen® serve as a reference comparator.

**General Analysis Considerations:** Analyses will be reported via tables, listings, and figures using ICH numbering. Testing is 2-sided at the 0.05 significance level. Continuous variables will be summarized with descriptive statistics; categorical variables with counts and percentages. SAS Version 9.4+ and Phoenix WinNonlin Version 6.4+ will be used. Analyses defined before unblinding are a priori; those after are post hoc and exploratory.

**Analysis Sets:** Three datasets are defined: the safety analysis set (randomized patients receiving ≥1 dose, based on treatment received), the full analysis set (FAS, based on randomized treatment), and the per protocol set (PPS, FAS patients without relevant protocol deviations). The primary endpoint analysis uses the FAS, a secondary analysis uses the PPS, and safety analyses use the safety set.

**Efficacy Analyses:** The primary endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery (≥20 mg/dL increase from baseline within 45 minutes without rescue IV glucose), analyzed with a stratified log-rank test (stratified by age group and injection site) and Kaplan-Meier plots. Secondary endpoints include recovery within 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes (Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test) and plasma glucose changes from baseline at those time points (ANOVA). A hierarchical testing procedure controls multiplicity. No interim analyses are planned, and no imputation will be applied for missing data. Sensitivity analyses and a supportive Cox proportional hazards model are specified.

**PK/PD Analyses:** Plasma dasiglucagon and glucagon concentrations will be analyzed by non-compartmental methods. The pharmacodynamic endpoint is plasma glucose area under the effect curve above baseline from 0 to 30 minutes (AUE0-30min).

**Safety Analyses:** Based on the safety set, covering extent of exposure, local tolerability, treatment-emergent adverse events (coded via MedDRA), laboratory parameters, vital signs, ECG (including QTcF categorical summaries), and descriptively analyzed immunogenicity (ADA occurrence).

**Protocol Changes:** The primary efficacy analysis wording was revised with added sensitivity/supportive analyses, and secondary endpoint terminology changed from "within" to "at" specified minutes.

**Appendices:** Include data presentation and programming specifications, SAS programming QC requirements, and an ICH E3-conformant list of tables, figures, and listings.

Meb Faber's Three-Way Momentum/Trend-Following Model Strategy, published in 2015 and based on research from Ned Davis Research, invests equally in stocks, bonds, and gold when the monthly 3-bar moving average is above the 10-bar moving average. The strategy returned 13% annually from 1971 to 2015. The authors backtested it using GLD, SPY, and TLT ETFs starting in 2006, turning 100,000 into 422,000, with an 8.9% CAGR, 57% win rate, 1.6 profit factor, and an 18% maximum drawdown. Performance since 2015 was weaker at 5.3% annually, below the stock market, but the strategy's main strength is its low drawdown, including only a small loss in 2022. With 1.5 leverage, annual returns were 13.1% with a 26% maximum drawdown. Optimization of nearby settings produced similar results, indicating the strategy is not curve fitted. The authors conclude the strategy remains effective, simple, and defensive during major recessions.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on January 31, 2017, announcing its financial results for the first fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2016.
