Mark E. Haedicke emailed the State Bar of Michigan e-Journal list on October 25, 2000, requesting to be deleted from the mailing list. His message included the full e-Journal for that date, which contained summaries of Michigan Court of Appeals and Sixth Circuit opinions in constitutional, criminal, family, litigation, malpractice, and worker's compensation law, along with fields of practice listings, classified advertisements, professional news, and upcoming bar events.

Soccer passing directions terminology refers to the line or path a ball is expected to take when struck by a passer to a potential receiver. Although the terms are generally defined for a player in possession facing the attacking goal, they apply regardless of the player's orientation—for example, a midfielder facing the defensive goal who passes to a defender behind him still makes a "back" pass. Passes may be on the ground or in the air. Directions are organized clockwise around the player: Forward, Angled Right, Right, Back and Right, Back, Back and Left, Left, and Angled Left. Each direction includes multiple synonymous terms, such as "deep," "long," "short," "square," "diagonal," and "wide." Additional terms cover concepts like passing angle, near and far post, outlet passes, possession passes, and switching fields.

The passage describes NVIDIA's GA10x Ampere GPU architecture and its improvements over the prior Turing generation. ROPs are now part of the GPC rather than tied to the memory controller, increasing the full GA102 GPU to 112 ROPs from 96. The GA10x SM doubles FP32 throughput by enabling FP32 processing on both datapaths, supports 128 FP32 operations per clock across four partitions, and features a 33% larger combined L1 data cache/shared memory (128 KB per SM) with double the shared memory bandwidth of Turing.

GA10x introduces second-generation RT Cores that double ray/triangle intersection testing rates over Turing and add a new Interpolate Triangle Position unit for hardware-accelerated ray-traced motion blur, enabling up to 8x faster motion blur rendering. Third-generation Tensor Cores (one per partition, four per SM) are twice as powerful as Turing's, add TF32 and BF16 data types, and support Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity for up to 2x throughput on sparse matrices. GA10x also enables concurrent RT Core, graphics, and compute workloads within each SM.

The memory subsystem uses GDDR6X with PAM4 signaling, delivering up to 936 GB/sec bandwidth (over 52% more than TU102). NVIDIA RTX IO, working with Microsoft's DirectStorage API, enables GPU-based lossless decompression, accelerating I/O up to 100x compared to hard drives and traditional APIs. The architecture supports HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC, AV1 hardware decode (first GPU to do so), and seventh-generation NVENC encoding.

The NVIDIA A40 data center GPU delivers up to 2x FP32 and ray-tracing throughput versus the Quadro RTX 6000, with 48GB memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink. The GeForce RTX 3090 (GA102) ships with 24GB GDDR6X and is 1.5x faster than TITAN RTX; the RTX 3070 (GA104) outperforms the RTX 2080 Ti. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU includes 10,752 CUDA Cores and 48GB GDDR6. A new Error Detection and Replay (EDR) feature helps users find safe memory overclock limits. Ampere GPUs are up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing at the same performance level.

Samsung Galaxy J5 Prime, launched in India at Rs 14,900, has started receiving the Android 7.0 Nougat OTA update in UAE, according to SamMobile. Imported Indian models may get it, though an official rollout could take time. The over-1GB update brings improved multi-window usability, dual messenger, stricter app permissions, new emoji, and battery optimisation. Users can check manually via Settings > About Device > Software Update, using Wi-Fi with at least 50% battery.

U.S. stocks fell sharply Friday, with the Dow dropping more than 650 points (2.5 percent) below 26,000, capping its worst week in two years; the S&P 500 fell 2.2 percent and the Nasdaq 2 percent. Investors sold off on fears that a stronger-than-expected jobs report—200,000 jobs added in January with wage growth of 2.9 percent—would prompt the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates more than anticipated, possibly three to four more hikes. Analysts attributed the decline to economic fundamentals rather than the House GOP memo. President Trump, who had previously touted the market rally on Twitter, was silent on the downturn Friday.

Peloton launched five new AI-powered fitness products—including refreshed bikes and treadmills and a new rowing machine—in an effort to revive its struggling post-pandemic business. Higher-end models feature Peloton IQ, an AI coaching system providing real-time form feedback, rep counting, and personalized training plans. Prices rose across the lineup, with the Tread+ increasing $700 to $6,695, and monthly membership fees increased $5 to $49.99. This is the first major product change under Stern, a former Apple and Ford executive who took over in January and announced a 6% workforce layoff in August. The company's stock, down over 90% since its January 2021 peak, fell 3.67% on launch day.

The 48-inch LG C4 OLED TV is at its lowest-ever Amazon price of $800 for Prime Day, while the 65-inch model is priced at $1,300. The C4 offers strong picture quality with natural colors and good shadow detail, though it lacks the brightness of flagships like the LG G4. It features VRR up to 144-Hz across four HDMI inputs, LG's webOS interface, and a magic remote with voice search and point-and-click functionality. The article recommends the 65-inch for living rooms and the 48-inch for bedrooms or gaming use.

RaySearch and Eckert & Ziegler BEBIG have signed a partnership agreement to integrate the RayStation treatment planning system and RayCare oncology information system with BEBIG's brachytherapy systems, enabling a complete brachytherapy solution. Brachytherapy uses radioactive implants placed in or near tumors, most commonly for prostate cancer.

The passage presents a simulation study of phlogopite (KMg3(AlSi3O10)(OH)2), a layered dark mica, irradiated with a 92 eV, 10 fs laser pulse using the XTANT-3 code, which combines tight-binding molecular dynamics, transport Monte Carlo, and Boltzmann collision integrals to model nonequilibrium, nonthermal, and nonadiabatic effects. The calculated band gap (7.5 eV ideal, ~6.5 eV at room temperature) agrees with prior studies. Simulations identify dose-dependent damage thresholds: ~0.17 eV/atom (Te~11,000 K) causes hydrogen migration, consistent with the experimental value of ~0.2 eV/atom (1000 kGy); ~0.4 eV/atom produces Mg diffusion and a superionic-superionic transition; ~0.5 eV/atom disorders the entire lattice, with sublattices disordering at different rates; ~0.9 eV/atom collapses the bandgap, forming a metallic liquid; and ~2 eV/atom drives femtosecond nonthermal acceleration, selectively affecting oxygen and potassium due to the electronic density of states. Electron-phonon coupling raises the damage threshold relative to Born-Oppenheimer simulations by cooling electrons and suppressing nonthermal damage. Comparisons with β/γ-irradiation and swift heavy ion etching experiments qualitatively support the results. Damage threshold fluences are estimated to guide future X-ray experiments, and the study suggests dose-tunable transient states—superionic, semi-metallic, or metallic—in irradiated phlogopite.

This lecture covers two case studies. In the Winthrop Center case, the 2019 market showed no green premium (100 Summer Street transacted at a 4 cap), and anchor tenant State Street chose 1 Congress Street due to floor plate usability, the building's condo-dominated design, and Winthrop's unwillingness to give up its rent premium. The building had 0% pre-leasing. When COVID hit in January 2020, HSBC withdrew financing and construction paused for about three months, before a Kuwait-based fund provided a $700 million loan. The Cornell Tech project—the largest Passive House at the time, de-risked by Cornell's equity stake—was instrumental to Winthrop's decision. A 2020 study found Passive House cost premiums of 1% to 8%, with Winthrop achieving 1% through experienced execution. Winners included tenants and the city of Boston, whose regulations (BERDO 2.0, the envelope backstop, and MEPA learnings) incorporated Passive House elements; by 2021 Boston hosted three of the largest US Passive House projects. Sustainability adoption typically progresses from innovation to pilots in corporate/MUSH sectors, then followers, then regulation-driven scale-up.

In the 425 Park Avenue case (2012), L&L Holding bet $1 billion on building "the healthiest building in New York." Constraints included a cash-draining ground lease, Lehman's insolvency, and zoning requiring retention of 25% of the existing structure (an 8% cost premium). Healthy-building options (MERV 15 filtration, WELL certification) carried combined 2–6% cost premiums against a projected 5% rent premium, which students questioned as optimistic. Using the law of diffusion of innovation and "Crossing the Chasm," L&L targeted finance tenants like Citadel, which signed a record lease, though the project's equity was wiped out after construction delays. A later flight-to-quality trend favored ultra-high-quality offices over Class B stock.

A hockey coach acknowledges his team played poorly in a recent game, lacking offense, physicality, quickness, defense, and special teams play, identifying it and a game in Montreal as the two playoff performances he was unhappy with. He declines to discuss lineups or opposing goaltenders but expresses confidence in his goaltender Michael, whose playoff numbers are the best. He notes the team has played better at home, where its playoff record is excellent, while road games have featured costly bad chances against. He describes Chicago's strong start and three late first-period goals in the previous game and expects his team to bring its best effort tomorrow. He recalls a painful past near-championship loss, says the team is capable of fighting, and expects big games from Mike Richards and Jeff Carter, the latter returning after nearly two months lost to two injuries. He cites past situations, including Carolina, as motivation in pursuing a special championship.

This lecture covers utility from beliefs and biases in learning. The instructor reviews anticipatory utility, explaining how people may avoid negative information (e.g., about Huntington's disease) to maintain positive beliefs. In a model where beliefs must be correct conditional on information received, people are information-averse if the utility-from-beliefs function is concave and information-loving if convex. If people could freely manipulate beliefs, they would choose maximal optimism unless beliefs affect future outcomes (e.g., treatment decisions, savings, family planning) or create disappointment via elevated reference points. Optimal expectations thus trade off current happiness against distorted decisions and future disappointment.

Evidence of overoptimism includes Weinstein's study, where students judged positive events more likely and negative events less likely for themselves than for average peers; similar overconfidence appears among couples, small business owners, smokers, drivers, and professors. MIT students, however, show under-confidence (only 31% rate themselves academically above average), possibly due to frequent feedback, biased perceptions of the average, or self-motivation; female students are particularly under-confident. Ego utility (feeling good now) is distinguished from anticipatory utility, though they are hard to separate empirically. A literature on positive illusions argues overconfidence promotes mental health ("depressive realism").

Biases are greater for personally important traits, with ambiguous feedback, and under perceived control, and smaller with objective feedback. Lab experiments (Eil and Rao; Mobius et al.) show asymmetric updating: people process good news roughly Bayesianly but discount bad news, and pay for information expected to be positive. Zimmermann's motivated memory work shows people remember positive signals more. Real-world evidence includes overconfident traders losing money (Barber and Odean) and overconfident managers conducting value-destroying mergers (Malmendier and Tate).

The lecture then discusses why Bayesian learning is cognitively hard: people get the direction of updating right but not the magnitude. Three systematic deviations are presented: the gambler's fallacy (believing an outcome is due after independent draws, illustrated by a coin-flip experiment), the hot-hand fallacy (believing performance streaks continue), and base-rate neglect (the HIV test example, where the correct answer is 50% but many say 99%). The first two stem from the belief in the law of small numbers—producing the gambler's fallacy when the distribution is known and the hot-hand fallacy when it is unknown. Real-world implications include judges' parole decisions and interpretation of COVID antibody tests.

Finally, heuristics—informal algorithms yielding quick approximate answers—are introduced. The representativeness heuristic (the Linda problem, violating the conjunction rule) and the availability heuristic (judging frequency by ease of recall) are highlighted. The lecture concludes that the reason people are misinformed matters for policy: salience and information help with attention failures or wrong theories, respecting motivated beliefs may be preferable when correction reduces happiness, and correcting systematic learning biases is less controversial.

A hockey player praises teammate Oskar's intelligence, timing, and work ethic, and notes his line's good chemistry. He says the team has improved each series and aims to win the next game in a best-of-three. He credits better structure, composure, and key goalie saves, while stressing continued improvement through video review.

Topological insulator lasers combine topological states with laser design to address common laser problems: sensitivity to defects and the emergence of unwanted colors and unstable output at high power. In a crystalline insulator, electrons occupy two energy bands separated by a gap; while the interior does not conduct, surface states can, and in some materials these surface states tie an electron's spin to its direction of travel. Because reversing direction requires a spin flip, which is energetically difficult, surface electrons flow with minimal scattering from defects. Researchers applied this principle to light using rings of optical waveguides that leak light to neighbors through intermediary rings that shift phase. Exciting only the outer rings confines light to the edge, where it is protected from scattering and amplified, producing a stable, single-color laser. Experiments comparing protected and unprotected edge states showed the protected laser remained functional even with rings removed, was more efficient, and did not develop new colors at high power. Such lasers may benefit applications like 5G networks and space-based interferometers.

Law enforcement has spent two years planning security for Super Bowl LII at Minneapolis's US Bank Stadium. The Minneapolis Police Department is the lead agency, assisted by dozens of federal, state and local agencies. Measures include a heightened police presence, bomb-sniffing dogs, helicopters and fencing, with brutal cold—forecast around 3 degrees Fahrenheit—adding a planning challenge. Attendees will be prescreened at indoor locations such as the Mall of America, a first for the NFL, with stadium screening beginning more than four hours before the game. The FBI leads counterterrorism efforts, analyzing past mass-event attacks and conducting background checks on over 30,000 credentialed individuals. Regional concerns include a mall stabbing, a mosque bombing and Al-Shabaab's influence. Homeland Security Investigations will monitor counterfeit goods, and more than 400 Minnesota National Guardsmen have been called up.

The passage discusses Alaska's development, noting it has yielded eleven million dollars in government revenue and nearly three hundred million dollars in gold, furs, and fish since purchase, and endorses the Alaska Yukon Pacific Exposition in Seattle. It highlights the potential of Pacific commerce, worth over three billion dollars annually, to benefit American industries if pursued fairly. On international morality, it argues that nations, like individuals, can act from ethical motives rather than mere self-interest, and that ethical standards in national action should be raised. It insists that lawful immigrants be treated with justice and good will regardless of religion or origin, with only their conduct subject to question. The passage condemns hostility toward Japanese immigrants, particularly their exclusion from San Francisco schools, as discreditable and potentially consequential. It praises Japan's astounding development since Commodore Perry's expedition over half a century ago, citing achievements in military, industrial, artistic, and scientific fields, including the Japanese Red Cross's donation of over $100,000 to San Francisco sufferers. The Japanese have earned the right to treatment on a basis of full and frank equality, and Americans, who are well treated in Japan, must reciprocate that courtesy.

Waterstone Financial (NASDAQ:WSBF) received positive press coverage on Friday, earning a media sentiment score of 0.26 from Accern, with an impact score suggesting recent news is somewhat unlikely to affect the share price. BidaskClub downgraded the stock from "buy" to "hold," while Sandler O'Neill upgraded it to "buy" and lowered its price objective to $20.00. Shares traded down 0.26% to $19.45. The company declared a quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share, representing a 2.46% yield.

Researchers recorded medical problems among participants receiving BNT162b1 or BNT162b2, noting causes could be unrelated to the study, due to the vaccine, other medicines, or unknown.

In Phase 1, a few participants had a temporary lymphocyte drop 1 to 3 days after Dose 1, returning to normal by 6 to 8 days; none had low lymphocytes after Dose 2. Injection site reactions and systemic events within 7 days were well tolerated and mostly mild or moderate, with pain, tiredness, and headache most common. All Phase 1 doses were well tolerated except BNT162b1 at 100 µg, which was stopped after Dose 1; BNT162b2 at 30 µg was selected for Phase 2/3. No participants left Phase 1 due to medical problems.

In Phase 2/3, few participants left due to medical problems (32 of 21,926 on BNT162b2; 36 of 21,921 on placebo). Serious medical problems were rare; researchers did not believe most were vaccine-related, though a few in participants 16 and older may have been related. No one died in Phase 1; Phase 2/3 deaths occurred from various causes and were not believed caused by BNT162b2.

This lecture covers neutral particle diagnostics for measuring the ion distribution function in the core of magnetically confined plasmas. Because core ions are well confined, existing techniques—electron cyclotron emission (measures electron temperature), laser-induced fluorescence (fails since core particles are fully ionized), and Thomson scattering (measures the electron distribution)—cannot measure the ion distribution directly. The proposed approach relies on core ions becoming neutrals via charge exchange, allowing them to escape and be detected externally.

Two issues are addressed: neutral production and neutral transport. Production occurs through charge exchange with edge neutrals or with neutral beam injection. Transport concerns whether neutrals escape before being re-ionized by electron impact ionization, ion impact ionization, or further charge exchange; charge exchange is resonant and dominates attenuation. Escape probability follows an exponential attenuation law analogous to radiation transport. For 10 keV neutrals in a plasma of density 10²⁰ per cubic meter, the mean free path is about 10 centimeters, so a low line-integrated density (below roughly 10¹⁹ per square meter) is required for neutrals to escape.

Regarding production, edge fueling yields a detectable flux of core neutrals, while radiative recombination is negligible (neutral-to-ion ratio around 10⁻⁸ at 1 keV). In the passive diagnostic, escaping neutrals pass through a stripping cell, are re-ionized, and are separated by a magnetic field into an energy-sensitive detector, yielding the ion distribution function, including fast-ion tails. This measurement is line-integrated, and cold edge neutrals can contaminate the signal.

Active techniques using neutral beams provide localization. Charge exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS) uses charge exchange with fully stripped impurity ions (e.g., oxygen, carbon, boron), which then emit characteristic photons upon decay. It measures impurity density from intensity, ion temperature from Doppler broadening, and flow velocity from Doppler shift. Bremsstrahlung background can be separated by modulating the beam. Beam emission spectroscopy (BES) measures density fluctuations from fluctuations in beam emission line intensity, though beam attenuation and additional atomic processes must be modeled. Finally, the motional Stark effect (MSE) arises because the beam velocity crossed with the magnetic field produces an electric field in the particle's frame, splitting energy levels. Measuring this splitting determines the magnetic field strength, and analyzing the polarizations of emitted lines yields the field angle, enabling inference of the poloidal field and current profile for magnetic reconstruction.

This passage discusses verification, validation, and uncertainty quantification (VVUQ) for physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models in radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT). Radiotheranostics enables personalized cancer treatment, exemplified by FDA approval of [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 for prostate cancer, but current RPT regimens remain standardized despite interindividual variability in pharmacokinetics, tumor burden, and radiobiological sensitivity. Computational nuclear oncology addresses this through theranostic digital twins (TDTs), with PBPK models offering advantages over conventional approaches by incorporating patient physiology and drug characteristics.

PBPK models comprise computational, anatomical-physiological, and radiopharmaceutical frameworks, and can be developed using bottom-up, top-down, or middle-out approaches. The proposed VVUQ workflow includes: verification (confirming correct model structure and implementation), internal validation (goodness-of-fit assessment, model selection via AIC/BIC/F-test, and local or global sensitivity analysis), external validation (prediction evaluation through data splitting and resampling), and uncertainty quantification (assigning statistical distributions, propagating parameter uncertainty, and characterizing output precision and accuracy).

Extending PBPK models to dynamic TDTs introduces additional VVUQ challenges, as continuous integration of patient data requires iterative, data-responsive verification and validation. The passage concludes that PBPK models for RPTs lack regulatory standards comparable to those in the pharmaceutical industry, and establishing fit-for-purpose VVUQ frameworks, along with engagement from organizations such as SNMMI, EANM, and IAEA, is critical for translating PBPK models from research to clinical practice.

This case describes a crisis in Toyota's relationship with supplier ChassisCo over rear suspension cradles for the Suprima crossover. In late 2004, fourteen months after the September 2003 launch, ChassisCo's Athens, Georgia plant was producing at roughly 60% of target rate, with nonconforming parts, high scrap and downtime, and weak defect tracking. Toyota had previously succeeded with ChassisCo on the 1997 Suprima and 1999 Responsa launches, when Toyota controlled part design, tuning, and sourcing. For the 2003 Suprima, Toyota gave ChassisCo responsibility for sourcing 85 second-tier parts and project management, while the new cradle was more complex and highly automated (102 robots). ChassisCo lacked project management, parts-tracking, and supplier-audit capabilities; its 2000 decentralization and many concurrent launches stretched resources thin. Aggressive target prices led to low-bid, unqualified suppliers and underestimated logistics costs, and ChassisCo did not tell Toyota the price was unrealistic. Problems at second-tier suppliers, including the Tulsa stamping plant, surfaced too late, and the plant failed Toyota's high-volume production trial three times before launch. The Toyota Production System, based on jidoka and Just-in-Time with principles of continuous improvement and respect for people, depends on supplier problem-solving skills ChassisCo lacked. By late 2004, both companies' resources were strained, raising questions about how to resolve the crisis.

McGill University researchers developed DOLPHIN, an AI tool that detects previously invisible disease markers within single cells by analyzing how genes are spliced from smaller pieces called exons, rather than using conventional gene-level counts. In a test on pancreatic cancer patients' single-cell data, it identified over 800 disease markers missed by conventional tools and distinguished high-risk, aggressive cancers from less severe cases, potentially helping doctors match patients to suitable therapies and reduce trial-and-error treatment. The tool also enables virtual simulations of cell behavior and drug responses, laying groundwork for digital models of human cells. Researchers next plan to expand the tool from a few datasets to millions of cells.

A hockey player discusses the finals, saying both teams are good and similar, which is why they are there. He notes the opponent rebounds well and his team must respond with consistent effort, keeping the game simple and playing a patient team game. He does not consider the opponent a one-line team, citing Nieuwendyk as a dangerous shooter and noting the third and fourth lines check well and contribute. He praises head coach Larry for speaking well and motivating the team. With the series at two games to one, he expects the opponent to play harder and stresses sticking to the game plan.

The S&P 500 rose 2.2% in July (+7.8% YTD), its third month above the 10-month moving average, though it slipped 1.6% on the first day of August. July was a risk-on month with stocks up and bonds down; Frontier Markets led monthly returns while US large caps placed third. Volatility and credit spreads are seeing a seasonal upturn, investors are increasingly skewing portfolios toward tech stocks, and US electricity demand has reached a new all-time high. August began poorly, with Friday erasing a chunk of July's gains. Short-term technicals appear tenuous—50-day breadth is rolling over from overbought levels with bearish divergence—but medium- and longer-term trend indicators remain healthy as focus shifts from rebound to risk amid seasonal headwinds.

The author downgrades Alibaba Group Holding Limited from "Buy" to "Hold" as shares approach fair value following a significant rally. This paper proposes a theory-driven framework for measuring and improving the persuasive capabilities of large language models (LLMs), grounded in Bayesian persuasion. Motivated by longstanding debate over persuasion's consequences and by the difficulty of evaluating LLM persuasiveness—given heterogeneous effects, inconsistent metrics, and subjective, resource-intensive human evaluation—the authors conceptualize persuasion as a Sender's strategic information revelation that shifts a Receiver's beliefs toward the Sender's objectives. They repurpose existing human persuasion datasets to construct environments where both Sender and Receiver are implemented as LLMs, validated through a human study with 45 participants. Using persuasion gains and signals (measured via conditional mutual information) as instruments, experiments show that stronger frontier models such as DeepSeek-R1 achieve significantly higher persuasion gains and exhibit more sophisticated behaviors, such as adaptive information revelation. The authors further train LLMs with reinforcement learning, demonstrating that even small models (Llama3.2-3B-Instruct) can achieve strategic persuasion capabilities comparable to larger LLMs, with improvements transferring to different Receiver architectures. Key contributions are: (1) a principled measurement framework inspired by Bayesian persuasion; (2) concrete environments for evaluating and training LLMs in strategic persuasion built from existing datasets; and (3) empirical evidence that frontier models exhibit strong persuasive capabilities that can be improved at scale via reinforcement learning.

The "Clock" is a simple, powerful zone offense combining a 1-3-1 freelance passing attack with basic rotation rules, named for the clockwise and counterclockwise rotations of outside players. It is easy to teach and execute, works against both person-to-person and zone defenses, and relies on sharp ball movement to create open outside shots, basket cuts, and post rolls. Its options include the corner pass (wing cuts to the basket), ball reversal (attacking the weakside), and dribble clear (corner back cuts, exchanging roles with the wing). The offense exploits the 1-3-1 zone's weakness along the baseline and the 1-2-2 zone's vulnerability in the middle and corners. Against double teams, the "Cat" counter shifts into a 2-1-2 alignment, and the trap rule requires passing out of traps. Additional rules: the post rolls on corner passes, and baseline corners back cut on middle entries. Crunch time specials include "Vegas" (double screen away for a shot) and "Back" (weakside lob).

The passage describes the NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture, focusing on the TU102, the line's highest-performing GPU, with TU104 and TU106 as scaled-down variants. The TU102 contains six Graphics Processing Clusters, 36 Texture Processing Clusters, and 72 Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs), each with 64 CUDA Cores, eight Tensor Cores, an RT Core for ray tracing acceleration, and 96 KB of configurable L1/shared memory. The full chip includes 12 GDDR6 memory controllers, 96 ROP units, and 6 MB of L2 cache.

The Turing SM supports concurrent FP32 and INT32 execution, yielding roughly 36% additional floating-point throughput, and its unified L1/shared memory design delivers a 50% performance improvement per CUDA core over Pascal. Second-generation NVLink provides 100 GB/s aggregate bidirectional bandwidth on TU102 for multi-GPU connectivity and two-way SLI.

Enhanced Tensor Cores add INT8 and INT4 precision modes for inference. The Tesla T4, based on TU104, delivers up to 130 TOPS of INT8 performance and 40X higher inference performance with over 50X better energy efficiency than CPU-based servers.

Turing is the first GPU architecture to use GDDR6 memory (14 Gbps, 20% more power efficient than GDDR5X), and combined with improved compression achieves 50% higher effective bandwidth than Pascal. The new display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K at 60 Hz, HDR with tone mapping, and VirtualLink over USB-C for VR headsets. NVENC adds 8K HEVC encoding.

Dedicated RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, enabling real-time ray tracing roughly 10 times faster than Pascal through a hybrid rendering model combining rasterization and ray tracing with denoising. NVIDIA NGX provides AI features including DLSS, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.

New graphics features include Mesh Shading (Task and Mesh Shaders), Variable Rate Shading with per-16x16-pixel control, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering supporting four views per pass. TU104 contains 3,072 CUDA Cores and 48 RT Cores; TU106 contains 2,304 CUDA Cores and 36 RT Cores but lacks NVLink/SLI support.

The passage describes NVIDIA's Blackwell architecture and DLSS 4 technologies. DLSS Multi Frame Generation generates up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame using fifth-generation Tensor Cores; the new AI frame generation model is 40% faster, uses 30% less VRAM, and replaces hardware optical flow with an AI model. Blackwell's enhanced Flip Metering shifts frame pacing logic to the display engine for smoother output. DLSS 4 also transitions from CNN-based to transformer-based AI models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving temporal stability, detail in motion, and anti-aliasing.

Blackwell introduces neural shaders, enabled by the Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan developed with Microsoft, giving shaders access to Tensor Cores. Applications include RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression (over 3x memory savings in a demo, with up to seven-to-one compression), Neural Radiance Cache (which infers multi-bounce lighting from path-traced rays in real time), RTX Skin (the first ray-traced subsurface scattering in games), and RTX Neural Faces (a real-time generative AI model that infers natural faces from rasterized input and 3D pose data).

The passage also provides GPU specifications: GB202 (92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA cores) powers the GeForce RTX 5090; GB203 (45.6 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA cores) powers the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti; and GB205 (31 billion transistors, 6,400 CUDA cores) powers the RTX 5070. The document concludes with standard NVIDIA disclaimers and trademark information.

This passage discusses the concept of equality and equality of opportunity in education. Equality is defined as a moral and social ideal in which people hold the same position and value, and the education system plays an important role in implementing equality of opportunity and means. Equality of opportunity, a key argument of the democratic tradition, is interpreted differently across countries—as educational, cultural, economic, or gender equality. Education is defined variously as a system maintaining social order, an uninterrupted lifelong process, and a means of intentional behavioral change and human development.

Equality of opportunity in education emerged with state-supported compulsory education in 18th-century Prussia and was advanced by James S. Coleman's 1968 report. It is generally defined as all individuals benefiting equally from educational services without discrimination, based on their abilities.

Factors affecting equality of opportunity in education are economic, geographical, political, individual, and social. In Turkey, the Ministry of National Education shapes education policy, and reasons for the issue's prominence include inadequate schools, economic difficulties, unequipped learning environments, and lack of student motivation due to cultural and social factors.

The conclusion notes disagreement over what equal opportunity in education requires, though the ideal itself is widely accepted. Recommendations include measuring children's abilities early and independently of family background, increasing education quality and access, improving teacher quality through reforms in education faculties, and expanding preschool education and schooling rates.

This patent application describes systems, methods, and non-transitory computer-readable media for a variable multiplexer for vehicle communication bus compatibility. Vehicles use communication buses (e.g., CAN bus) with data link connectors, but while manufacturers use standardized hardware interfaces, pinout configurations vary among manufacturers, requiring different cables for compatibility. The disclosed external device includes a programmatically configurable variable multiplexer that can be electronically configured to match a vehicle's pinout configuration, enabling compatibility with various vehicles using a single standardized cable. The device determines the proper pinout configuration through several techniques: transmitting a vehicle identifier (e.g., VIN) to a remote computing system that maintains a vehicle data index; gathering data transmitted across the communication bus during a listening mode and comparing it to known pinout configurations; and using checksum values to verify data against multiple known pinout configurations. The device includes components such as a connection detection component, a pinout configuration determination component, and a pinout configuration modification component.

This passage discusses design patterns for building distributed systems with containers, emphasizing that patterns enable reusable shared components that improve quality through widespread use.

The text first covers three single-node patterns, where containers are tightly coupled and coscheduled on one machine (grouped as pods in Kubernetes):

1. **Sidecar pattern**: A sidecar container augments an application container, often without the application's knowledge. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy service via an nginx proxy, synchronizing configuration from an API to the filesystem, providing process introspection (topz), and building a simple Git-based PaaS. Effective sidecars require parameterization (preferably via environment variables), a stable API, and documentation using Dockerfile directives such as EXPOSE, ENV, and LABEL.

2. **Ambassador pattern**: An ambassador container brokers interactions between the application container and the outside world. Uses include client-side sharding (e.g., twemproxy proxying to sharded Redis), service brokering for portability across environments, and request splitting for experimentation (e.g., nginx directing 10% of traffic to an experimental service).

3. **Adapter pattern**: An adapter container transforms an application's interface to conform to a standardized interface. Examples include adapting Redis metrics for Prometheus, normalizing logs with Fluentd, and adding rich health checks to MySQL without modifying the original container.

The passage then turns to multi-node patterns and microservices, noting benefits (small focused teams, API-based decoupling, independent scaling) and drawbacks (harder debugging and design). It details the replicated load-balanced service pattern for stateless services, including readiness probes, session tracking via consistent hashing, caching layers (Varnish), rate limiting, and SSL termination (nginx). Finally, it describes sharded services for stateful data, where sharded caches improve memory utilization over replicated caches, and replicated sharded caches add resilience. Sharding functions typically use hashing with the modulo operator, and selecting an appropriate shard key—balancing generality and specificity—is critical to proper system design.

The passage describes NVIDIA's RTX Blackwell GPU architecture. Blackwell doubles integer throughput for many INT instructions by unifying INT32 and FP32 cores, though unified cores operate as either type per clock cycle. Texture units increase from 512 (RTX 4090) to 680 (RTX 5090), raising texel rates to 1636.76 Gigatexels/sec, with doubled point-sampled texture filtering versus Ada.

Blackwell introduces GDDR7 memory using PAM3 signaling developed with JEDEC, delivering improved signal-to-noise ratio, doubled channels, and better energy efficiency. The RTX 5090 ships with 28 Gbps GDDR7 (1.792 TB/sec) and the RTX 5080 with 30 Gbps (960 GB/sec). ECC is built into the DRAM die and always enabled.

Fifth-generation Tensor Cores add FP4 and FP6 support alongside a second-generation FP8 Transformer Engine; FP4 requires less than half the memory of FP16 with over 2x performance. The fourth-generation RT Core doubles ray-triangle intersection throughput and introduces Mega Geometry (cluster-based acceleration structures and Partitioned TLAS for high-detail ray tracing), plus hardware-accelerated Linear Swept Spheres for strand rendering. SER 2.0 doubles reordering efficiency, and a new RISC-V based AI Management Processor offloads GPU context scheduling from the CPU.

Blackwell adds 4:2:2 hardware encode/decode, a ninth-generation NVENC with 5% quality gains and an AV1 UHQ mode, a sixth-generation NVDEC with 2x faster H.264 decoding, and DisplayPort 2.1b (80 Gbps). Max-Q improvements include advanced power gating, 1000x faster frequency switching, and 10x faster entry into the deepest sleep state.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation (up to three AI-generated frames per rendered frame) and transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA. Neural shaders are enabled via the Cooperative Vectors API, supporting Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. The product lineup includes GB202 (RTX 5090), GB203 (RTX 5080/5070 Ti), and GB205 (RTX 5070).

NVIDIA evolved the GPU into the world's leading parallel processing engine for gaming, content creation, HPC, and AI. Turing, its biggest architectural leap in over a decade, advances efficiency and performance for PC gaming, professional graphics, and deep learning inferencing through Hybrid Rendering, a new SM architecture, GDDR6 memory support, and Tensor Cores powering Neural Services.

The SEC opened an informal inquiry into transactions involving partnerships (LJM Cayman and LJM2 Co-Investment) formerly run by CFO Andrew Fastow. The Reverse Action Offense, introduced by Hall of Fame Coach Pete Newell in the late 1950s, features a simple guard around continuity that is difficult to defend due to its precise execution and footwork. Its most recognizable option is the weakside wing's rub cut off a post screen to the basket, but it also provides a strong post-up game, two-player guard around isolation, and numerous quick-hitting counters against defensive overplay.

The basic continuity involves entry passes, guard around cuts, rub cuts off post screens, and reversal passes. Successful execution requires patience and coordinated off-ball screening among the passer, screener, and receiver, emphasizing footwork, timing, and non-verbal communication.

The offense does not rely on a single entry pass; any pass or dribble can initiate the continuity, with weakside, strongside, dribble clear, and back door entries available. Each action includes reads and counters based on defensive reactions, such as drives, pull-up jumpers, rolls, and slips against various screen defenses.

The guard around action creates a sideline triangle enabling post isolation options similar to the Triangle Post Offense, including lob passes, post splits, and high post splits. Tex Winter's "line of deployment" concept assists in reading and countering defensive post deployment, with counters for defenders playing high side, baseline side, behind, fronting, or double-teaming the post.

The offense's spacing makes it ideal for back cuts against overplays, and it offers crunch-time specials such as weakside screen and rolls, double screens, and back screen lobs.

A defensive "wall" in soccer consists of defenders standing shoulder-to-shoulder to block the goal during a nearby free kick, typically positioned 10 yards from the ball. The wall blocks approximately half of the goal, giving the goalkeeper more reaction time to cover the other half. The goalkeeper is the sole decision-maker for building a wall, based on ball location and personal experience. Wall size depends on the ball's distance and angle: two players near the end-lines, up to five or more when the ball is directly in front of the goal.

In traditional wall building, the "Anchor" (usually the tallest available midfielder or striker) moves to a spot on an imaginary line from the near post to the ball, 10 yards away. The goalkeeper directs the Anchor's exact positioning using verbal commands and hand signals, then the remaining wall players fill in shoulder-to-shoulder, often ordered by height. Players must avoid gaps, may protect certain body parts without moving hands toward the ball (which is a handling violation), and may jump so long as a ball cannot pass beneath them.

An alternative approach uses a "Wall Setter" positioned beyond the ball to direct the Anchor, freeing the goalkeeper to watch the ball and defend against quick kicks. On rare occasions when an indirect free kick is awarded less than 10 yards from goal, defenders form a wall on the goal line between the posts. Referees are not obligated to allow time for wall construction; attackers may take quick kicks, and defenders delaying the restart receive a yellow card. Attackers must remain at least one yard from walls of three or more defenders.

The reverse play is a high-risk, high-reward football trick play designed to deceive the defense by initially running the ball in one direction before giving it to another player moving the opposite way. A 2018 Carolina Panthers example shows Cam Newton tossing to DJ Moore, who then tosses to Curtis Samuel for a big gain and eventual touchdown, aided by offensive linemen forming a "seal" to block pursuing defenders. Variations include the fake reverse, used by the 2020 Arizona Cardinals, where Kyler Murray fakes handoffs before running himself after safeties bite on a receiver's motion. The reverse screen, shown by 2021 Purdue, involves the ball being tossed back to the quarterback, who throws to the original ball carrier behind a wall of blockers for a touchdown. The reverse pass, considered the best variation, adds a final twist where the quarterback becomes a passing option and catches a touchdown pass.

This IDC white paper examines technology trends in industrial development and manufacturing, based on a December 2021 survey of 200 decision makers from enterprises with over 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

Key technologies discussed include engineering workstations "as a Service" using cloud and AR/VR technologies for collaborative development, and digital twins, which IDC believes will enable new business models such as "Product as a Service" and "Outcome-based Services."

The paper focuses on high-performance computing (HPC) as a game changer for product and process innovation, cited by 81% of decision makers (96% among those who have implemented HPC). Demand for high-performance calculations is expected to grow significantly, with nearly half of respondents anticipating high demand within two years, compared to 8% currently. HPC enables complex simulations, faster iterations, new usage scenarios, and greater innovation and agility.

Challenges include security concerns (72% of respondents), high energy consumption (58%), lack of expertise (42%), and high investment and licensing costs. Most enterprises prefer external HPC infrastructure (87%) or colocation datacenters (74%), while only 6% operate on-premises HPC.

IDC anticipates public cloud and HPCaaS will become dominant architectures, offering scalability, cost flexibility, and access to cutting-edge technology; 81% of current HPC users intend to implement HPC-based business models.

Recommendations include establishing virtual product development, creating a holistic data strategy with a single source of truth, evaluating suitable HPC operating models, prioritizing scalability, security, and energy efficiency, and leveraging external expertise.

Charles W. Parker, administrator of Melvin Douglas's estate, appealed a district court ruling that Farmway Credit Union could exhaust its security interest in Douglas's personal property without filing a probate claim or a foreclosure action. Douglas had defaulted on $111,290.17 owed to Farmway, secured by farm machinery, crops, livestock, and real estate. Before his death, Douglas and his wife orally agreed with Farmway to sell the collateral at public sale; after his death, the heirs carried out this agreement, and the sale occurred on May 26, 1984, with ten days' written notice to heirs and creditors. The administrator, who took no steps to halt the sales, later sought a declaratory judgment claiming sole right to the property. The district court granted Farmway summary judgment. On appeal, the court held that the administrator's right to possession is not absolute and that, given the uncontroverted security agreement and prior oral agreement, Farmway had the contractual right to repossess and sell the collateral, while expressly not deciding whether self-help repossession is permitted absent such an agreement. The court also rejected the argument that summary judgment was premature, as no material facts remained to be discovered. Affirmed.

Packers coach Mike McCarthy singled out cornerback Damarious Randall as the standout of offseason workouts, praising his play at the nickel or "star" position. The Virgin America brand will disappear overnight on Wednesday, two years after Alaska Airlines acquired it for $2.6 billion. The final Virgin-branded revenue flights—Flight 1182 departing San Francisco and Flight 1948 to Los Angeles—will fly Tuesday night. At 29 airports where both airlines operate, all Virgin America check-in counters, kiosks, signs, and gate areas will be rebranded as Alaska Airlines. Frequent fliers have planned celebratory events and surprises for the final flights. Overnight, Virgin America employees will switch to Alaska's computer systems, website, mobile app, and call center, creating a single flight network. Updating the Airbus livery and retrofitting cabins will continue until the end of 2019.

Counter is a football run play that gives the illusion of a Power play in one direction while blocking for the runner to go the opposite direction, with the backside Guard pulling to kick out an edge defender and the Fullback inserting onto an Inside Linebacker. Its main strength is exploiting quick, aggressive defenses that over-pursue the Power action, giving the offense more blockers than defenders at the point of attack. Its main weakness is slower development, making it vulnerable to penetration—especially in the open B gap—and to defenses spilling the play to force the ball carrier laterally into pursuing defenders. The passage outlines assignments for Counter Trey against 3-4 Odd and 4-3 Even fronts, covering pulling guards, combination blocks, counter steps by the Fullback and Tailback, and the Quarterback's fake. Variations include Singleback GT Counter, where the backside Tackle replaces the Fullback as the insert player, and Gun Split GT Counter Triple Option, which adds triple option reads for athletic Quarterbacks.

Texas quarterback Arch Manning has been inconsistent in his first four games as the Longhorns' full-time starter in 2025. He performed well against Sam Houston State and San Jose State, totaling seven passing touchdowns, an interception, and 295-plus passing yards in each, but struggled against Ohio State and UTEP, throwing one touchdown and one interception in each with long throws of 32 and 23 yards. The paper develops a mathematical framework for investigating cubic-to-tetragonal (CT) phase coexistence in perovskite ferroelectrics using high-resolution X-ray diffraction 3D reciprocal space mapping. Building on the adaptive state (AS) concept and Wechsler–Lieberman–Read (WLR) crystallographic theory, the framework models CT coexistence through periodic assemblages of tetragonal domains that are macroscopically averaged into a pseudo-uniform phase, enabling mismatch-free connection to the cubic phase via a habit plane (HP), without requiring domain miniaturization.

Three tetragonal domain variants (Ta, Tb, Tc) pair along six permissible domain walls. The macroscopic averaging introduces a volume ratio parameter ω, with mismatch-free ASC connections existing when ω = ω₁ ≈ xc/xT or ω = ω₂ ≈ x̄a/xT. The authors derive analytical expressions for orientation relationships between C, AS, and T basis vectors and predict Bragg peak splitting for all 24 ASC variants.

The framework is validated through synchrotron-based high-resolution reciprocal space mapping of PMN-35PT single crystals at the CT transition (~435 K). Experimental results show strong agreement between predicted and observed Bragg peak separations. The condition xc = −2xa is satisfied, yielding M = 1 and habit planes along {110} planes with domain volume ratios of 2/3 and 1/3. Domain sizes estimated from peak widths are several hundred nanometers, confirming that tetragonal domains diffract independently while maintaining ASC orientation relationships, supporting AS-like coexistence without domain miniaturization.

IDC research finds that industrial simulation, modeling, and analysis depend on complex computing operations, forcing enterprises into trade-offs between calculation time and quality when hardware is limited; 42% of respondents report their simulations are already outdated or inaccurate. Demand for high-performance calculations is expected to rise sharply—from 8% currently identifying high demand to almost half within two years—and half of respondents already say iterations and calculations take too long.

Four out of five surveyed decision makers view high-performance computing (HPC) as a game changer for product and process innovation, rising to 96% among enterprises that have implemented it. HPC enables complex calculations, faster and higher-quality simulations, new usage scenarios, and greater innovation and agility. More than a quarter of surveyed enterprises already use professional HPC infrastructures, with another 39% planning or piloting deployment.

Key challenges include security concerns (72% of respondents), high investment, licensing and operating costs, energy consumption and sustainability (58%), inadequate computing performance, availability problems, and lack of expertise (42%). Most enterprises prefer external infrastructure: 87% use or plan cloud-based HPC, 74% use or plan colocation, while only 6% operate on-premises HPC.

IDC anticipates the public cloud will become the most important HPC architecture, followed by hybrid cloud. HPC-as-a-Service (HPCaaS) offers cost flexibility through OPEX instead of CAPEX, scalability, resilience, and access to cutting-edge technology; 81% of enterprises that have implemented HPC intend to build HPC-based business models. Engineering workstations "as a Service" and digital twins further support collaboration, efficiency, and new data-based products and services.

BA.2.86 (Pirola), a SARS-CoV-2 lineage first detected in Denmark in late July 2023, carries 33 spike mutations relative to BA.2 and shows significant antigenic shift from XBB sub-lineages. Its descendant JN.1 is on track to become globally dominant. Using a reverse mutational scanning approach with 33 single-reversion mutants on the BA.2.86 background, researchers identified mutations contributing to immune escape from vaccine-induced antibodies. Testing against sera from 30 healthcare workers before and after BNT162b2 XBB.1.5-adapted vaccination showed that BA.2.86 and JN.1 pseudoviruses were neutralized 40-fold and 80-fold less efficiently than wild-type, respectively, by pre-booster sera. The mutations ins16MPLF, K356T, N460K, V483Δ, A484K, F486P, and S621P, distributed across NTD, RBD, and S1/S2 domains, contributed to BA.2.86 immune escape. XBB.1.5-adapted booster vaccination substantially increased neutralization titers against both BA.2.86 and JN.1 to comparable levels, eliminating JN.1's greater pre-booster escape advantage. Reversions insMPLF16Δ, ins144Y, K554E, S621P, and K484A restored neutralization to BA.2 levels post-booster. This represents the first reported use of reverse mutational scanning to identify escape epitopes in polyclonal antibody responses.

The Washington Supreme Court affirmed a judgment confirming a local improvement assessment roll of the city of South Bend. The city's 1911 ordinance for filling low lands and tide lands estimated the cost at $9,500, anticipating fill material at nominal cost from a contemplated federal dredging of the Willapa river. When the government deposited material only within a 1,500-foot limit, the city contracted with a private dredging company to fill the remaining area, raising the actual cost to $89,199.92. The court held that the preliminary cost estimate required by Rem. & Bal. Code § 7974 serves only to guide the council's decision on whether to initiate the improvement, and an assessment exceeding the estimate is not invalidated if it does not exceed the actual bona fide cost, with § 7983 permitting additional amounts after notice and hearing. The ordinance was not void for indefiniteness, as it complied with statutory requirements, and the evidence preponderated in favor of the assessed benefits.

This study investigated elementary school mathematics teachers' (grades 1-5) perceptions, obstacles, and future preferences regarding distance education (DE) in the UAE following the pandemic-driven transition from face-to-face classes to online teaching. A quantitative approach was used, employing a 37-item Likert-scale questionnaire distributed via Google Forms to 90 teachers (75 female, 15 male) from private and governmental schools in Al Ain City, selected through convenience sampling. The instrument was validated by a panel of five reviewers, pilot-tested with 30 teachers, and showed an overall Cronbach's alpha of 0.79.

Results showed generally positive perceptions of teaching mathematics online (average mean 4.00). The highest-ranked item concerned teachers' ability to use different digital technologies (mean 4.43), while the lowest-ranked item stated that online teaching is more suitable than face-to-face for elementary students (mean 2.89). Obstacles were moderate overall (average mean 3.69), with school resource availability ranked highest and difficulties using online resources ranked lowest. Regarding future preferences, 87.8% reported receiving administrative support, 76.7% preferred teaching face-to-face if given the choice, and 64.4% enjoyed teaching online. Statistical tests found no significant differences in perceptions by educational level, gender, or years of experience; however, obstacles differed significantly by educational level, favoring graduates.

The study concluded that teachers were confident using digital tools but faced increased workload, stress, and concerns about student achievement, and it recommended professional development, robust support systems, hybrid teaching models, and improved assessment methods. Limitations included the modest sample size, participants' access to support and resources, and the obligatory pandemic context of online teaching.

The passage is from a specification for the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) used with AMD's SEV-ES (Secure Encrypted Virtualization - Encrypted State) and SEV-SNP (Secure Nested Paging) features, which protect guest register state from the hypervisor by encrypting it during world switches. VMEXITs are classified as Automatic Exits (AEs), which do not expose guest register state, or Non-Automatic Exits (NAEs), for which the guest controls what register state to share through the GHCB. The document's purpose is to standardize the GHCB memory area so a guest OS can interoperate with any hypervisor supporting SEV-ES or SEV-SNP, to standardize the required NAEs and the minimum guest state exposed, and to standardize actions requiring unique support (e.g., NMI handling, SMP booting). The GHCB must be mapped decrypted and is defined as 4,096 bytes to fit in a single decrypted page. Its format mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save state area through offset 0x3ff, allowing hypervisors to map the VMCB save state area to the GHCB with limited changes; however, only fields required to handle a VMGEXIT are provided, limiting guest state exposure. Version 2 adds SEV-SNP support and hypervisor feature advertisement, with a minimum set of required features. The passage also documents revision changes: 2.01 adds 64-bit guest request message sequence numbers and a new error code for malformed input; 2.02 adds the VLEK certificate GUID definition and expanded SW_EXITINFO2 error reporting; 2.03 adds APIC ID list retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, and page state change notification support.

This lecture covers Langmuir probes, which are simple metal conductors inserted into plasma to measure potential, with references to Hutchinson's textbook and Lieberman and Lichtenberg for sheath theory.

When inserted into plasma, the probe collects electrons faster than ions because electrons move faster, charging negatively until current reaches zero at the floating potential, which differs from the plasma potential. Biasing the probe produces an IV curve with electron and ion saturation currents and three regimes depending on probe potential relative to plasma and floating potentials.

Sheath theory uses the Debye length (roughly 20 micrometers for a cold plasma with 1 eV temperature and 10^17 per cubic meter density), permitting a quasi-planar assumption since the Debye length is much smaller than the probe. Assuming cold ions, a sheath forms only when the probe is biased below -Te/2e. Using continuity and energy conservation, ion density at the sheath edge is n-infinity times exp(-1/2), and ion velocity is the square root of Te/mi, yielding Hutchinson's equation for total current.

For a single probe, electron temperature is obtained by fitting ln(I minus ion saturation current) versus probe voltage near the floating potential, and density from the ion saturation current. Limitations include risk of drawing excessive current and melting the probe, plus sweep-time constraints on temporal resolution.

A double probe uses two probes biased against each other; Kirchhoff's law limits current to the ion saturation current (I = I_si times tanh of eVB/2Te). A triple probe adds a floating probe, allowing density and temperature measurement without sweeping and with fast time resolution, though it assumes the IV curve model is correct. Probes must be spaced so presheaths, which extend hundreds of Debye lengths, do not overlap. Additional complications include magnetic fields altering particle orbits and collisions modifying particle flux through diffusion.

Apple Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended March 26, 2022. Total net sales were $97.3 billion, up 9% from $89.6 billion in the year-ago quarter, driven primarily by growth in Services, iPhone and Mac. This study developed and evaluated a Patient Report Template (PRT), a structured clinical decision support tool combining established handoff methods (SBAR and I PASS the BATON) to streamline nursing handoffs and reduce EHR documentation burdens. The PRT comprises nine sections: Patient Profile, Review of Systems, Situation, Safety, Background, Actions, Timing, Ownership, and Next.

A survey of 106 nurses at University of Iowa Health Care assessed the perceived usefulness of each PRT component and nurses' sentiment toward AI (comfort, trust, expected utility) on 5-point Likert scales.

Most PRT components were rated as useful. The highest-rated items included Patient Name (4.42), Chief Complaint (4.40), Code Status (4.38), Allergies (4.36), and Current Medications (4.29). The lowest-rated were Level of Uncertainty (3.25), Family History (3.36), Coordination (3.72), and Rationale (3.71).

Nurses reported low comfort (2.38) and trust (2.5) with AI in their workflows, with moderate expected utility (3.0). Respondents were demographically diverse: Pediatrics was the largest department (18%), 27% worked in "other" units, 54% had 0–10 years of experience, and ages were nearly evenly split between Young Adults (44%) and Adults (46%).

Limitations include selection and response bias and reliance on perceived rather than hands-on usefulness. The authors conclude the PRT shows potential for improving handoff efficiency and patient safety, and recommend future clinical testing, usability evaluation, and validation of AI-generated reports.

A new Gallup-Walton Family Foundation survey finds that more than 1 in 4 U.S. public school teachers lack the basic materials or staffing support needed to do their jobs, significantly affecting workplace satisfaction. Two-thirds report shortages of teaching assistants, aides or paraprofessionals, and 62% report insufficient mental health resources or special educators. Among teachers with adequate resources, 77% report job satisfaction, compared with 44% of those without. While 72% say they have the equipment needed to teach effectively, 24% lack classroom furniture, 25% lack laptops and 35% lack printing supplies; teachers in low-income schools report greater technology shortages. About half say professional development is not grounded in students' needs, and only 1 in 3 get the opportunity to observe other teachers, which 43% consider the most worthwhile activity.

The passage discusses the turn of the month trading strategy, an extension of the end-of-month effect (also called the Ultimo Effect) that includes the first three days of the following month. The strategy involves going long at the close on the fifth last trading day of the month and exiting at the close of the third trading day of the next month, resulting in roughly 33% exposure time. Backtests show the strategy has performed well in the S&P 500 for over 60 years, achieving a 7.1% CAGR with smaller and shorter drawdowns than buy and hold. The effect was also tested across numerous markets and sectors, including emerging markets, healthcare, gold mining, high yield funds, real estate, gold, Treasuries, consumer staples, Brazil, Japan, Bitcoin, commodities, utilities, technology, energy, and India's Nifty index, with mostly positive results, though tech stocks and gold showed weaker or erratic effects. Possible causes include structural forces such as capital inflows and fund rebalancing. The article also notes that the last calendar day of the month averages a 0.1% gain versus 0.04% on random days, and provides Python and Amibroker code for backtesting.

The speaker praises a physically strong, smart hockey player who played another solid game. The team's first and third periods were better than the second; they must stay aggressive and create scoring chances. Systems log data heterogeneously, with varying levels, output destinations, and formats across libraries. Containerized applications are expected to log to stdout. The adapter pattern addresses this: an adapter container can redirect file logs to stdout and transform different formats into a single structured representation for log aggregators. While modifying your own application container can work, adapting third-party containers is expensive to maintain; adapter containers are cheaper and enable sharing and reuse.

The passage analyzes quarterly financial and operating results of eight oil majors: Exxon Mobil, Chevron, Royal Dutch Shell, BP, Statoil, Total, ENI, and ConocoPhillips. Oil prices, which bottomed in 2016, have risen, driving higher revenues, margins, and return on sales. Aggregate revenues bottomed in 2016 and are rising on higher prices and production. Aggregate oil production grew 5.3% from 2Q15 to 2Q17 (10.7 to 11.3 M b/d), while aggregate natural gas production grew 9.7%, with seven of the eight majors reporting gas growth. Lower upstream capital spending and higher cash flows lifted net operating cash flows, with all eight majors reporting positive NOCF in 2Q17. The supply-demand balance is tightening, and oil inventories are being drawn down. The majors can sustain profitable margins at roughly $50/bbl, and positive trends are expected to continue into 2018.
A hockey player describes scoring by shooting pucks at the net, emphasizing staying positive and confident through tough stretches, and credits his father's support.
The patent includes color drawings available for a fee. Figures show an animated graphical user interface; broken lines and transitions form no part of the claimed design.

The Imperial and Royal Government, through the United States, Spain, and Switzerland, received the adversaries' rejection of the December 12 peace proposal, which was deemed insincere and meaningless. Addressing neutral governments, the Central Powers attribute the war to Britain's encircling policy, France's revengeful policy, Russia's ambitions, Serbian provocation, the Sarajevo assassination, and Russian mobilization, claiming they fought in defense of their freedom and existence. They protest the characterization of their proposal as a war maneuver, asserting their sincerity and readiness to disclose peace terms once negotiations opened. They criticize the enemies' demands for reparation and acknowledgment of nationalities, citing the adversaries' own conduct regarding Ireland, South Africa, North Africa, and Greece, and accuse them of violating international law through maritime measures, starvation tactics, pressure on neutrals, use of colored troops, mistreatment of prisoners, and deportations of civilians.

A hockey coach previews a series against Dallas, predicting a close, exciting matchup between similarly built, disciplined, physical teams with strong goaltending, likely decided by special teams, while noting the first game may not indicate how the series unfolds.
