Fifteen Sacred Heart Academy students, accompanied by five chaperones, spent their spring break (March 30–April 7) on a mission trip to Alajuelita, a poor neighborhood of San Jose, Costa Rica. Organized by Spanish teacher April Dice, the trip required students to be enrolled in or have completed Spanish Two; a similar 2016 trip to Nicaragua was cancelled due to concerns over bombings in Belgium. The students' main goal was building relationships with residents, playing with children, bringing meals, and visiting a local senior center. They worked alongside American mission leaders who had served the area for nearly a decade, hiked to La Cruz de Alajuelita, and reported improved Spanish skills and personal growth. Dice found the experience rewarding and looks forward to future trips.

The Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly passed the Rs 95,666.97 crore budget for 2018-19, a 20 per cent increase over the previous year, with the appropriation bill moved by Finance Minister Haseeb Drabu passed by voice-vote. For the first time, the bill was linked to expenditure reforms, including release of budgets to departments within two weeks, mandatory classification of plan allocations, payments only through the BEAMS system from April 1, a 60-day cap on procurement plans, first charge on lapsing funds for centrally sponsored schemes, and a ban on fresh engagement of casual and need-based workers. Drabu said reforms over the past three years aim to stabilize the state's economy and reduce volatility.

The passage introduces PATCH, a network growth model extending the Barabási-Albert model that combines preferential attachment, triadic closure, and homophily to study inequality in networks containing minority and majority groups. Simulations show that homophily drives segregation and inequity, preferential attachment drives degree inequality, and triadic closure moderates segregation and inequity only when the selection among friends-of-friends is unbiased; biased triadic closure does not amplify segregation under homophily. Whenever one group accumulates more links, it also exhibits higher internal degree inequality, meaning only a few of its members benefit from the advantage. Applying likelihood-free inference (Approximate Bayesian Computation) to five decades of APS collaboration, APS citation, and DBLP data, the model variant in which both global and triadic closure links are biased by preferential attachment and moderate gender homophily best reproduces the observed gender inequalities. The authors conclude that reducing network inequalities requires simultaneously addressing all link formation mechanisms, since isolated interventions can produce unintended consequences, while noting limitations such as fixed symmetric homophily, fixed preferential attachment strength, and the exclusion of tie dissolution.

Researchers in the U.S. and Australia discovered that dandelion seeds attach via an off-center strand surrounded by horseshoe-shaped shielding. This structure steadies seeds against downward or lateral forces, but when wind tilts a seed toward the horseshoe's open side, the tether releases, allowing easy detachment. Experiments confirmed that pulling seeds upward requires an order of magnitude less force than pulling them downward. This directional release mechanism helps seeds catch upward gusts and reduces the chance of doomed downward flights.

This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the prevalence of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Fatty Liver Disease (MAFLD) and its association with glycemic control (HbA1c) among adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D) in Africa. MAFLD, formerly NAFLD, has a global prevalence of 32.4% and is the commonest liver disease; among people with T2D worldwide, prevalence is 55.5%. T2D confers a two-fold risk of advanced liver disease in MAFLD, elevated cardiovascular risk, nearly a three-fold risk of chronic kidney disease, and higher liver-related mortality. African evidence is limited, with a prior estimated MAFLD prevalence of 30.4% in T2D based on only four studies. Following PRISMA guidelines, researchers searched major and African-specific databases up to December 6, 2023, including observational studies of adults with T2D in African countries with calculable MAFLD prevalence. Study quality was assessed with the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist; prevalence was pooled using a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model, with correlation coefficients pooled for the HbA1c association. Of 659 identified references, 10 studies (nine cross-sectional, one case-control) from six African countries were included, comprising 1,667 T2D participants (61.1% female, mean age above 50 years, mostly overweight/obese with poor glycemic control); MAFLD was diagnosed mostly by ultrasonography.

This passage from the SD Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 describes the Switch Function command (CMD6), introduced in Version 1.10 and mandatory for cards of that version and higher. Hosts must verify support via the SD_SPEC field in SCR or CCC bit 10 in CSD. CMD6 is valid in Transfer State, supports six function groups with sixteen functions each (Function 0 being the default), and responds with R1 plus a 512-bit status block containing support bits, function selection results, busy status, and current/power consumption. Mode 0 queries supported functions and maximum current/power; Mode 1 switches functionality. Selected functions persist until a power cycle, CMD0, or CMD6 Mode 1 with Function 0. Function Group 1 covers Access Mode/Bus Speed Mode, Group 2 the Command System, Group 3 driver strength, and Group 4 Power Limit (default 0.72W; up to 1.80W for removable cards).

High-Speed mode (25 MB/sec at 50 MHz) is optional and enabled via CMD6, with only one card driven. CMD34-37, CMD50 and CMD57 are reserved for the optional Command System. CMD8 verifies voltage compatibility for Version 2.00+ cards and returns R7. SDHC/SDXC cards use block addressing with a fixed 512-byte block length, while SDSC uses byte addressing; SDHC/SDXC disable partial, misaligned, and write-protect group access.

The host may lower or stop the bus clock under restrictions, including providing eight clocks after transactions. CRC7 protects commands, responses, CID and CSD; CRC16 protects data blocks. Read timeout is 100 ms; write busy is generally 250 ms, up to 500 ms for SDXC in defined cases and up to 1 second after a Data Burst in UHS-II.

Commands are 48 bits, organized into Card Command Classes, with responses R1, R1b, R2, R3, R6 and R7. The card provides Card Status, SD Status, and Task Status. Performance is defined through Speed Class (2, 4, 6, 10), Video Speed Class (6, 10, 30, 60, 90), and UHS Speed Grade (1, 3), based on Allocation Units (AU), Recording Units (RU), and the parameters Pw, Pm, and Pr. For SDXC, CMD20 provides Start Recording, Update DIR, and Update CI functions; CMD20 support is mandatory for SDXC and optional for SDHC.

The Supreme Court announced that recommendations on judicial appointments, transfers, and elevations, along with their rationale, will be disclosed publicly online. The Collegium decision, led by CJI Dipak Misra, follows criticism over lack of transparency from senior lawyers, the Supreme Court Bar Association, the Gujarat High Court, and Justice Chelameswar. Reasons for recommendations and rejections will be posted on the court's website under "Collegium Resolutions"; details for the October 2017 Madras and Kerala High Court appointments are already online. Some judicial community members have criticized the decision.

Drug addiction, particularly opioid addiction, poses a significant public health challenge with over 100,000 overdose deaths in 2022 and high treatment dropout rates averaging 30% (up to 91% in opioid addiction). The iRISA model attributes addiction persistence to excessive value placed on drug cues over nondrug cues. Current clinical assessments rely heavily on self-report measures, which are susceptible to recall bias, social desirability, and compromised self-awareness, while urine toxicology is limited as a binary measure unable to capture dynamic drug use patterns. Although literature on objective cognitive-behavioral measures for predicting treatment outcomes is scarce, measures of impulsivity, working memory, decision-making, and drug-biased attention have shown predictive value. This study tested whether cognitive-behavioral markers of drug bias—picture-viewing choice tasks and a verbal fluency task targeting drug-related words—could outperform demographics and traditional measures in predicting 4-month treatment adherence in inpatient individuals with opioid use disorder (iOUD). Fifty-nine iOUD inpatients and 29 age- and sex-matched healthy controls participated. Researchers hypothesized that iOUD would show higher drug-biased behavior than controls and that objective drug-bias measures would better predict treatment completion than subjective measures.

Data transmission is synchronous to the clock; blocks consist of start bits, a payload data stream (with optional ECC), and end bits, protected by CRC. Block reads use a maximum 512-byte block size, settable via CMD16. CMD17 reads a single block; CMD18 reads consecutive blocks until stopped by CMD12. Read commands are rejected on BLOCK_LEN_ERROR or ADDRESS_ERROR, and data is not destroyed by sudden power-off except during write or erase operations.

The Rotary Club of Greenwich presented a $5,000 check to Greenwich United Way CEO David Rabin to fund its Reading Champions program, covering tutor supplies, books, and year-end awards for participating children.

The TLV321x and TLV322x are families of 5V single, dual, and quad channel high-speed comparators from Texas Instruments with a 40ns propagation delay and rail-to-rail inputs that extend 200mV beyond the supply rails. They operate over a supply range of 1.8V to 5V with a quiescent current of 40μA per channel. The TLV321x features a push-pull output stage capable of sinking and sourcing current, while the TLV322x has an open-drain output that can be pulled up to voltages up to 5.5V independent of the supply. The family includes a Power-on Reset (POR) feature that holds the output low until the minimum supply voltage is reached, 1.8mV of internal hysteresis, and is specified for operation from –40°C to 125°C. Applications include current sensing, zero-cross detection, logic level translation, and other speed-critical uses.

National Journal's CongressDailyAM (June 8, 2001) reports:

- **Appropriations**: House Appropriations subcommittee allocations for FY02 largely follow President Bush's requests but differ in some cases—$3 billion more for Labor-HHS, $1.1 billion more for VA-HUD, and $1.2 billion more for Energy and Water. Chairman Young and Defense Subcommittee Chairman Lewis intend to stick to the president's nearly $7 billion FY01 supplemental request despite defense hawks like Weldon calling it inadequate ($10-15 billion needed). Blunt warned the president would likely veto a larger supplemental, and a Senate aide predicted the Senate would also stick with the president's number.

- **House Leadership**: House Republican leaders say the Democratic Senate takeover will have little impact on House partisanship. Blunt said Republicans feel liberated and expect to pass an energy bill, prescription drug benefit, campaign finance reform, and possibly permanent tax cuts before the August recess. Hastert listed similar priorities plus a patients' bill of rights and trade negotiating authority. Gephardt accused Republicans of stiff-arming Democrats, and Blue Dog Democrats complained of a lack of consultation.

- **House Races**: Rep. Steve Largent will resign his Tulsa-area seat November 29 to run for Oklahoma governor and wants an earlier special election. GOP candidates include Sullivan, Pruitt, and Cathy Keating; Dodd is the likely Democratic nominee. NRCC Chairman Davis called the seat "strongly Republican."

- **Judiciary**: Rep. Hutchinson's expected confirmation to head the DEA leaves business groups without a House champion for liability-limiting legislation, a setback worsened by the Democratic Senate shift.

- **Labor**: Boehner and Norwood praised Labor Secretary Chao's three July ergonomics forums and September deadline for action; Democrats urging a new rule were more cautious.

- **Health**: FDA officials testified that roughly two million mailed parcels of FDA-regulated products annually overwhelm inspection capacity and may be contaminated or counterfeit, as Congress considers relaxing the 1988 reimportation ban. Separately, the House Energy and Commerce Committee is "open-minded" on adding generic drug patent reform to a Medicare prescription drug bill, despite skepticism from Waxman and brand-name makers.

- **Trade**: EU officials said Bush's steel import investigation could dampen the upcoming EU-U.S. summit; Lamy voiced concern about U.S. unilateralism, and Kyoto Protocol talks remain the hardest issue.

- **Senate Leadership**: Senate GOP negotiators agreed on assurances for quick consideration of Bush's nominees and are nearing a final organizing resolution with Daschle.

- **Politics**: Bush intends to nominate Jo Anne Barnhart as Social Security commissioner. Republican Census Monitoring Board members released a report questioning statistical sampling. Hansen and others filed the National Monument Fairness Act, requiring public input and congressional approval for monuments over 50,000 acres. Mica scheduled a June 20 hearing on airline customer service commitments.

Using 7 tesla magnetic resonance spectroscopy, this study compared brain metabolite concentrations among people with psychotic psychopathology (PwPP, n = 64), first-degree biological relatives (n = 42), and healthy controls (n = 43) in occipital cortex and dorsomedial prefrontal cortex volumes of interest. Methods included an ultra-short echo time (8 ms), explicit macromolecule modeling, a rigid baseline, and no soft constraints to address prior quantification concerns. Among six metabolites examined a priori, NAA was lower in occipital cortex in both PwPP and relatives versus controls, and NAAG was lower in prefrontal cortex in PwPP, though this difference was not significant after accounting for age, sex, and BMI. Post hoc analyses revealed higher glucose in PwPP in prefrontal cortex, with a similar non-significant trend in occipital cortex. Repeat scans in a subset showed fair-to-excellent longitudinal reliability (ICC 0.44–0.96). Hierarchical clustering indicated that glucose levels in both regions clustered with psychiatric symptom measures and visual task performance. The authors conclude that the findings suggest metabolic dysfunction in PwPP and, to a lesser extent, relatives, and note that demographic factors, tissue composition, and antipsychotic medication did not fully explain the observed group differences.

Several boxers have transitioned to mixed martial arts with varying success. James Toney, a multi-division boxing champion, lost his lone MMA fight to Randy Couture at UFC 118 by first-round submission. Holly Holm, a boxing and kickboxing titlist, became UFC bantamweight champion by knocking out Ronda Rousey, though she has since lost three of her last four fights. Ray Mercer, the former WBO heavyweight champion, won his only MMA bout by knocking out Tim Sylvia. Heather Hardy remains undefeated in both sports. Eric "Butterbean" Esch had modest MMA success after a lengthy boxing career. Art Jimmerson, likely the first boxer to try MMA, lost at UFC 1 to Royce Gracie. Mia St. John won her single MMA fight, while Ricardo Mayorga went 0-3. Ana Julaton posted a 2-2 record, and Marcus Davis and Chris Lytle had longer MMA careers with respectable records.

In this lecture, the Z-transform is introduced as a generalization of the discrete-time Fourier transform—and the discrete-time counterpart of the Laplace transform—to address the problem that the Fourier transform does not converge for all sequences. The Fourier transform converges when a sequence is absolutely summable, a condition linked to system stability. The Z-transform is defined as X(z) equal to the sum of x(n)z^(-n), where z = r·e^(jω), corresponding to the Fourier transform of the sequence multiplied by r^(-n). The Fourier transform equals the Z-transform evaluated on the unit circle (|z| = 1). Examples show that x(n) = (1/2)^n u(n) converges while x(n) = 2^n u(n) does not.

The region of convergence (ROC) specifies the values of z for which the Z-transform converges. Z-transforms of exponential sequences are ratios of polynomials, representable by poles and zeros in the z-plane, but the same rational expression can correspond to different sequences distinguished only by their ROCs. ROC properties include: no poles within it, bounded by poles (or zero or infinity), outside the outermost pole for right-sided sequences, inside the innermost pole for left-sided sequences, and between adjacent poles for two-sided sequences. Finite-length sequences converge over the entire z-plane, possibly excepting z = 0 or infinity. If the Fourier transform exists, the ROC includes the unit circle.

The Z-transform maps convolution into multiplication, and the transform of the unit sample response is called the system function. Stability implies the ROC includes the unit circle; causality implies the ROC lies outside the outermost pole. Using the difference equation y(n) − ½y(n−1) = x(n), choosing the ROC outside the pole yields a stable, causal system with h(n) = (1/2)^n u(n), while choosing it inside the pole yields an unstable, anti-causal system with h(n) = −(1/2)^n u(−n−1). The inverse Z-transform will be developed in the next lecture.

The passage begins with a Microsoft notice stating that the device contains WM-DRM software used by content providers to protect Secure Content; if the software's security is compromised, Microsoft may revoke its right to acquire new licenses, though playback of unprotected content is unaffected, and revocation lists are delivered to the device when licenses are downloaded. It then presents the SanDisk End User License Agreement, under which SanDisk grants a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use the Software in executable form for personal use on a single computer. Users may not modify, reverse engineer, decompile, rent, or lease the Software, and SanDisk and its Licensors retain all rights not expressly licensed. The Software is provided "as is" without warranties; SanDisk's total liability is limited to the amount paid; and the Software is not designed for high-risk activities. The Agreement may be terminated upon violation, is governed by California and U.S. federal law, and is subject to U.S. export restrictions. Finally, disposal instructions state that the device should not be discarded with unsorted household waste and that users should consult local waste authorities for return and collection systems.

Five U.S. Atlantic coast ports—Norfolk, Savannah, Port Everglades, Jacksonville, and Miami—handle nearly half of U.S. poultry exports and could be impacted by Hurricane Irma, a powerful storm expected to hit Florida Sunday after killing 21 people in the Caribbean. Top exports include poultry, grocery items, soybeans, cotton, citrus, and beverages.

Source Energy Services Inc., Canada's largest fracking sand distributor backed by TriWest Capital Partners, is seeking to raise about C$250 million in an IPO at a valuation of about C$1 billion, planning to use proceeds for a facility acquisition, debt repayment, and capital expenditures.

The Tenth Circuit affirmed the INS's reinstatement of a 1996 exclusion and deportation order against Alejandro Mendez Suarez, a Mexican citizen removed after attempting to enter the United States with counterfeit documents at El Paso, Texas. After illegally reentering the country in October 1999, he was arrested in Colorado in 2002 on a domestic-violence charge, released on bond, and then taken into INS custody, whereupon the INS reinstated the prior order under INA § 241(a)(5). The court held that the district court properly transferred his habeas petition to the court of appeals because he was actually challenging the reinstatement decision. The court rejected his argument that reinstatement caused him to violate bond and jeopardized his state criminal defense, finding the INS was not required to consider such effects when reinstating an order. It also rejected his claim that § 1231(a)(5) was improperly applied retroactively, since his unlawful reentry occurred after IIRIRA's April 1, 1997 effective date, and the record showed he was deported rather than having voluntarily departed. The court found him ineligible for adjustment of status under the LIFE Act because his prior misrepresentation rendered him inadmissible. Finally, it declined to reach the merits of his due process challenge to the reinstatement procedure because he could not show prejudice, as he did not contest the factual requirements for reinstatement.

Ashby Fields Primary School in Daventry has proposed closing at 1:15pm on Fridays to help teachers maintain a healthy work-life balance, citing national recruitment and retention problems caused by teachers working an average of 60 hours a week. A public consultation is underway, with results to be published in May. Parent Kelly Holmes criticized the plan, arguing it does not consider working parents and that the on-site childcare, Orchards Wrap Around Care, has limited spaces and costs money. The proposal would cut two hours from the current 27.5-hour weekly timetable. Parents can voice opinions at an April 25 meeting, and governors will review feedback before considering a formal proposal.

This passage is from the Texas Instruments datasheet (SLASFJ6A, revised September 2025) for the MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 microcontrollers, covering peripherals, support, and packaging. The SRAM provides zero wait state access, retention in RUN/SLEEP/STOP/STANDBY modes, and 1KB-resolution write protection. GPIO supports up to 45 pins with wake functionality from low-power modes. The IOMUX handles pad configuration and pin muxing. The 12-bit ADC achieves up to 1.6-Msps with 10.6-bit ENOB using an external reference. A factory-calibrated temperature sensor connects to an ADC channel. The LFSS combines an RTC and independent watchdog timer on a 32kHz clock. VREF offers 1.4V/2.5V references; the comparator supports six blanking sources and an 8-bit reference DAC. Security features include firewalls and CRC-16. Communication peripherals include UART (with LIN support), I2C (up to 1Mbps), and SPI (up to 16Mbits/s). Timers include general-purpose (TIMGx) and advanced (TIMAx) types with PWM and fault handling. Debugging uses a two-wire SWD interface with a DEBUGSS subsystem featuring a mailbox and security options. Factory constants store device identification. Application guidance recommends decoupling capacitors and pullup resistors. The document also covers device nomenclature, development tools, revision history (including removal of the DGS32 package), and mechanical packaging details.

Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common, highly inherited endocrine-metabolic disorder affecting 5–15% of reproductive-aged women and is associated with metabolic, reproductive, and mental health (MH) complications. This study assessed the direct healthcare-related economic burden of PCOS-related MH disorders through a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies comparing women with and without PCOS, following PRISMA guidelines and using the DerSimonian-Laird random effects model to estimate prevalence ratios (PRs). Of 2,018 identified studies, 25 were included. Women with PCOS had higher prevalence of anxiety (PR 1.42), depression (PR 1.65), and eating disorders (PR 1.48); the association with postpartum depression (PR 1.20) was not statistically significant and was excluded from cost calculations. Estimated excess annual direct healthcare costs in 2021 USD were $1.939 billion for anxiety, $1.678 billion for depression, and $0.644 billion for eating disorders, totaling approximately $4.26 billion. Combined with prior estimates, the total annual direct economic burden of PCOS exceeds $15 billion in 2021 USD, with MH disorders accounting for roughly 28%. The authors note limitations including the number of eligible studies and use of U.S. cost estimates applied to international studies, and conclude that improved detection and treatment of PCOS is cost-effective.

The passage describes credit card offers highlighted by CompareCards, noting that issuers are providing generous deals, including 0% Intro APR periods ranging from 12 to 21 months, which benefit consumers who pay balances in full and on time. Listed cards include a Discover card with 15 months of 0% Intro APR, 5% quarterly category cash back, and a first-year Unlimited Cashback Match; a Bank of America card offering 6% first-year cash back in a choice category and a $200 bonus; a Bank of America travel card with 25,000 bonus points and 1.5 points per dollar; Citi cards with 0% balance transfer APR for 18 months and cash back bonuses; and Capital One VentureOne and Quicksilver cards offering 1.25 miles or 1.5% cash back per dollar with 15-month 0% intro APRs. The passage also explains the difference between fixed and variable APRs and states that the site's editors evaluate over 100 cards from more than 50 issuers, with compensation not influencing ratings.

This email, sent by Enron employee Courtney Votaw on October 23, 2001, compiles news articles about Enron. A class action lawsuit was filed against Enron on behalf of investors who purchased stock between January 18, 2000 and October 17, 2001, alleging the company issued material misrepresentations that inflated its stock price, including failures to disclose declining demand in its Broadband Services Division, overstated operating results from investments in limited partnerships managed by its chief financial officer, and untimely write-downs of impaired assets; insiders sold over $73 million of stock during the period. The SEC requested information about Enron's transactions with limited partnerships managed by a senior officer, causing shares to fall $5.40 to close at $20.65. Enron asked Citigroup to arrange a $750 million loan as Moody's placed its $13 billion in long-term debt on watch for possible downgrade. Despite a 42 percent weekly drop in share value following disclosure of a $1.2 billion equity reduction from unwinding CFO-run partnerships, most analysts maintained high ratings on the stock. A Texas Monthly feature examined Enron's transformation, culture, and Jeff Skilling's resignation as CEO. A conference call failed to reassure investors about off-balance-sheet deals involving the LJM2 partnership and the Marlin II and Whitewing trusts. Separately, AES Corp. complained to India's prime minister about harassment by the Orissa state government, following Enron's similar dispute over the Dabhol power project.

Apple Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended December 30, 2023 (Q1 FY2024, 13 weeks vs. 14 weeks in the prior-year quarter). Total net sales rose 2% to $119.6 billion, driven by higher iPhone (up 6%) and Services (up 11%) sales, partially offset by declines in iPad (down 25%) and Wearables, Home and Accessories (down 11%). Net income was $33.9 billion ($2.18 diluted EPS) versus $30.0 billion ($1.88) a year earlier, with total gross margin of 45.9%. By segment, Americas rose 2%, Europe 10%, Japan 15%, and Rest of Asia Pacific 7%, while Greater China fell 13%. The company repurchased 118 million shares for $20.5 billion and paid $3.8 billion in dividends ($0.24 per share). Term debt outstanding was $106.0 billion and commercial paper $2.0 billion. In legal matters, the Supreme Court denied petitions in the Epic Games case, confirming the District Court's ruling in Apple's favor on antitrust claims, and the CBP determined Apple's redesigned Apple Watch models fall outside the ITC exclusion order in the Masimo dispute. Apple also disclosed changes to comply with the EU Digital Markets Act and noted Rule 10b5-1 trading plans adopted by executives Luca Maestri and Katherine Adams.

Michael Coren, an author and journalist in Toronto, wrote a satirical tweet supporting sex education that received 220,000 likes and 81,000 retweets. He notes organized opposition to new curricula in Ontario and Alberta from conservative Roman Catholics, evangelicals, and some Muslims and Sikhs, with demonstrations showing anger, homophobic comments, and misunderstanding. He argues sex education is not indoctrination but teaches children not to feel shame, including about same-sex attraction, and empowers them to recognize and report abuse. He attributes opposition to fear and culture rather than faith, and expects the controversy to fade.

A maths problem posed to Chinese schoolchildren aged 11 went viral after leaving adults defeated. The question—"If a ship had 26 sheep and 10 goats onboard, how old is the ship's captain?"—was unsolvable. Pupils and adults attempted various answers, but the Shunqing Education Department confirmed there was no answer, stating the impossibility was the point and that questions allowing different answers are good questions.

This passage is a compilation of news articles dated May 16, 2001, forwarded in an email titled "Enron Mentions." Key contents include:

- Criticism of the secrecy surrounding Vice President Cheney's energy task force, whose 170-page report encouraged oil, gas, coal, and nuclear production. Industry executives—including Enron's Kenneth Lay, Conoco's Archie Dunham, and Exxon Mobil's Lee Raymond—met directly with Cheney, while environmental groups, consumer organizations, and California Governor Gray Davis were denied comparable access.
- Texaco's consideration of an offshore facility in shallow Louisiana waters to regassify liquefied natural gas, with a feasibility study expected within six months.
- Enron's agreement to drop lawsuits against NGX Canada and Canadian Enerdata after NGX agreed to include EnronOnline trades in its Alberta gas price indexes by August.
- Enron Japan's publication of a reform proposal urging further deregulation of Japan's electricity market, citing prices 46 percent higher than OECD averages.
- Saudi gas project memoranda of understanding expected to be signed June 6, involving eleven companies including Enron.
- The Dabhol Power Company dispute in India, where lenders were voting on whether to issue a contract termination notice to Maharashtra; three members of the Godbole renegotiation committee resigned; and former deputy chief minister Gopinath Munde urged an amicable settlement.
- Additional articles covered Houston's strong office market driven by energy firms, hydroelectric dependence risks in Brazil and Chile, and the commissioning of two 60 MW units at Karnataka's Sharavathi Tailrace Project.

President Theodore Roosevelt proclaimed September 19, 1901, the day of President McKinley's burial, a national day of mourning and prayer following McKinley's assassination, urging citizens to gather in places of worship to honor his memory. The proclamation was issued September 14, 1901, signed by Roosevelt and Secretary of State John Hay.

This study examines the 1976 separation of the Druze school system from Arab education in Israel and its impact on Druze students' matriculation results and higher education achievements. Using semi-structured interviews with nine Druze principals, supervisors, and trainee principals, analyzed through thematic analysis, the study identified eight themes. Interviewees expressed satisfaction with rising matriculation eligibility rates (about 89% in 2022), a desire to continue excelling, and noted the program's uniqueness in Druze heritage alongside largely shared academic content. They credited quality teaching staff, liberal-modern social trends (particularly women's increased education), and identity-related motivations as key factors behind high achievements. Views on the separation itself were divided: some saw it as accelerating the sector's development, while others attributed success to sociocultural change rather than separation, with some describing it as a government tool for "reeducating" the Druze population. Principals agreed schools should serve as academic advocates but noted insufficient investment in preparing students for higher education. The study concludes that Druze achievements stem mainly from investment by educational leaders and staff, and recommends intervention programs to improve students' academic preparedness. Limitations include convenience sampling and the subjective nature of qualitative data.

Resource Generation (RG), a 20-year-old nonprofit, works with about 500 Americans aged 18 to 35 who are in the top 10 percent by wealth, through 17 chapters across the U.S. It encourages members to share their "money stories" and move their wealth to grassroots movements fighting social, economic and racial injustice. Members such as Emily Bookstein and Adam Roberts significantly increased their giving after joining. Executive director Iimay Ho says RG teaches social justice philanthropy principles rather than pooling funds, stressing that those most affected by injustice should decide how money is spent. RG operates amid sharp U.S. inequality: between 1963 and 2016, the top 1 percent's wealth grew sevenfold, and an estimated 34 to 45 percent of U.S. wealth is inherited. The organization also addresses race, linking wealth inequality to institutionalized racism, and members like Hanna Mahon and Elizabeth Baldwin have redirected giving to social justice organizations led by people of color.

Alex Caruso, the Lakers' inaugural two-way player, has spent 42 of his allowed 45 days with the team as of Wednesday's game against the Magic, after which he must join the South Bay Lakers until their season ends. He has appeared in 25 games, averaging 2.6 points and 1.9 assists, with a season-best nine points and eight assists against the Knicks on Jan. 21. Coach Luke Walton praised the system for providing continuity. Caruso's deal extends through next season and pays nearly $300,000, compared to the G-League maximum of $26,000. With the second-place South Bay Lakers (26-17), he averages 19 points and 7.4 assists in 25 games.

Williams Jones & Associates LLC reduced its Star Bulk Carriers Corp. (SBLK) stake by 52.6% in Q2, holding 31,600 shares worth $311,000. Other institutional investors adjusted positions: GLG Partners LP and Capital Fund Management S.A. bought new stakes, while Goldman Sachs, Citadel Advisors, and Impala Asset Management increased their holdings. Institutional investors own 75.03% of the stock. SBLK opened at $10.28, with a market cap of $651.91 million and a 52-week range of $4.04–$13.40. Analysts issued mixed ratings; three hold and six buy ratings yield a consensus "Buy" with a $12.80 target price. Star Bulk Carriers is an international shipping company operating 73 dry bulk vessels as of December 31, 2016.

Participants must remain employed through the payment date to earn awards. This study evaluated the expected performance of COVID-19 testing and isolation strategies adopted in France, Belgium, and Italy for the winter 2022/2023 season. Using a multi-country Influenzanet survey of 4,594 participants on prospective booster vaccination, testing, and isolation behavior, combined with a branching process model parameterized to Omicron subvariants (R=1.6), the authors predicted that the French and Belgian protocols would reduce community transmission by 17–18%, while the Italian protocol would achieve a 24% reduction but require longer isolation (about 11 days versus about 6 days). None of the protocols alone would reduce the effective reproductive number below 1. Introducing a test cost of up to 20 Euros would more than halve testing adherence in France and Belgium, reducing protocol effectiveness by approximately 60%. The fall 2022 booster campaign was estimated to substantially raise vaccine-induced protection, though willingness to receive boosters varied by country. The authors conclude that simpler isolation guidelines, similar to the Belgian protocol, could maintain effectiveness while reducing testing costs, and that high booster coverage remains essential for controlling the winter wave.

The Philippine government is responding to a bird flu outbreak in San Luis, Pampanga. Agriculture Secretary Manny Piñol announced restrictions within a 7-kilometer radius, banning movement of poultry and poultry products, with culling planned to isolate infected birds. The H5 strain found is not transmissible to humans, though samples were sent to an Australian laboratory to test for H5N6, with results expected within 12 days. Fowl shipments from Luzon are banned as a precaution, and local officials were directed to institute quarantine measures. Health officials state the virus mainly affects birds, human transmission is remote, and properly cooked chicken is safe. Epidemiologists are monitoring farm workers for symptoms.

Alcoa reported a fourth-quarter loss, but its stock has gained 68% since the October Arconic spinoff and is up 36% in 2017. Contributor Rich Duprey argues the stock is a buy, citing expected bauxite production growth to 47.5–48.5 million bone dry metric tons, nearly $600 million in new supply contracts, new Chinese customers, and potential doubling of EBITDA to $2.2 million, though he notes risk if higher prices do not persist. Contributor Jason Hall is more cautious: shares trade at a 12% discount to asset value of $42.13 per share, but book value fell due to facility closures and impairments, more write-downs are possible, Trump-related trade policy could harm a company reliant on foreign raw materials, and aluminum prices remain near multi-year lows. Hall is staying on the sidelines until profitability becomes clearer.

Vienna has topped Mercer's annual quality of living survey for the ninth consecutive year, while Baghdad remains last. The survey of 231 cities, which considers factors such as political stability, healthcare, and transport, helps companies set compensation for international staff. Zurich ranked second, followed by Auckland and Munich in joint third. London fell one place to 41st, while eastern European cities like Sarajevo and Bratislava showed the greatest living standard improvements over 20 years.

A March 19, 2001 email from Enron's Miyung Buster distributes news articles on California's energy crisis:

- FERC ordered six power suppliers to justify February prices or refund $55 million, following a $69 million January order; critics called the amounts too small, while Dynegy ($23 million) and Williams Energy ($22 million) face the largest potential refunds.
- Creditors, including Coram Energy Group, moved to force Southern California Edison into involuntary bankruptcy; PG&E and Edison stocks fell sharply, and PG&E retained bankruptcy lawyers while negotiating to sell its transmission lines to the state.
- San Diego County's air board voted to allow the Cabrillo power plant to emit more nitrogen oxides, with ozone increases expected if scarce natural gas forces a switch to fuel oil.
- OPEC's 4% production cut prompted Energy Secretary Abraham to call for increased U.S. domestic output; Sen. Schumer proposed tapping the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.
- Auto makers, manufacturers, and Westlands Water District cited the energy crisis to challenge regulations, with mixed results.
- The state Department of Water Resources, purchasing power for near-bankrupt utilities at roughly $350 million weekly, is described as inexperienced and outmatched by traders, with about $40 billion in contracts kept confidential.
- PG&E reclassified its blackout-exempt "Block 50," removing 810,000 customers and adding 690,000.
- A commentary describes a restaurant owner wrongly cut off over PG&E billing software errors; an opinion piece argues against blaming "out-of-state" generators, since wealth transfers flow from power consumers to producers regardless of location.

This email compiles news articles from November 11, 2001, focused on Enron and related business news. Enron agreed to be acquired by its smaller Houston rival Dynegy for approximately $9 billion, a fraction of its value the prior year, after an S.E.C. probe, a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity, and an admission that it had overstated profits by about $600 million. The S.E.C. was investigating off-balance-sheet partnerships (LJM1 and LJM2) formed by former CFO Andrew Fastow, in which Fastow and five other employees invested; two employees were terminated, and shareholders filed lawsuits against the company, the partnerships, and its law firm. An editorial attributed Enron's collapse to opaque financial arrangements, noting the company restated finances back to 1997, subtracting $586 million from net income and adding $2.5 billion to debt. Other articles discussed the blow to Houston's image from Enron's demise, alongside troubles at Compaq and Continental Airlines, while noting Dynegy's Houston presence softens the impact. Separately, the Dow Jones industrial average closed above its pre-September 11 level, aided by the Federal Reserve's tenth rate cut of the year, to 2 percent. Energy deregulation was reported as continuing despite California's crisis and Enron's fall. Wall Street was increasingly scrutinizing pro forma earnings, with Standard & Poor's revising its treatment of certain charges. Finally, a Senate stimulus bill of roughly $70 billion was criticized by Republicans as a grab bag of special-interest provisions.

This MIT lecture covers sustainability strategy, centering on a Porter article about corporate social responsibility (CSR). The professor explains Porter's argument that common CSR justifications—moral arguments, license to operate, sustainability, and reputation—are incomplete: moral choices lack measurement and vary by context, license to operate ignores company capabilities, reputation's business value is unproven, and sustainability is too vague for trade-offs. Porter instead proposes prioritizing social issues across generic social impacts, value chain social impacts, and social dimensions of competitive context, advocating strategic CSR integrated into a company's DNA. Examples include Whole Foods, Siemens, GE, Toyota, Nestle, and UPS, which tie sustainability to competitive advantage. The class discusses how deep companies should go into supply chains: Ford focuses on tier-one suppliers, while Starbucks (with its CAFE Practices), Unilever, and Nestle go deeper because agricultural commodities are central to their businesses. The professor emphasizes adopting a life cycle view, noting most impacts occur outside a company's own boundaries. On implementation, he stresses setting goals tied to reliable operational metrics and incentives, and gradually integrating sustainability into supplier selection over multiple years, citing Natura as an example. Administrative notes include an upcoming EMC guest speaker and guidance for the team project, which requires comparing two companies' sustainability performance and assessing whether their CDP rankings are deserved.

This passage is a transcript of the first lecture of an MIT course on geometric folding algorithms, taught by Erik Demaine. The class studies the mathematics and algorithms behind folding and unfolding geometric objects—linkages (rigid bars connected by hinges), paper (which cannot stretch or be cut), and polyhedra (3D surfaces that can be unfolded from or folded into flat material). Applications discussed include robotics and programmable matter, computer graphics, mechanical linkages, manufacturing, optics, medical devices such as stents and drug delivery, aerospace deployment, protein folding, origami sculpture, and reconfigurable architecture. Although some problems in the field date back four or five centuries, most activity has occurred in the last twelve years, and the course aims to cover and extend the frontier, aided by an optional open problem session.

The instructor distinguishes two types of questions—foldability (whether and how a given structure folds) and design (finding a folding that achieves a desired shape)—and three types of results: universality (everything foldable, with an algorithm), decision results (efficiently determining foldability), and hardness (computationally intractable problems). The class requires attendance, a few problem sets, and a project with presentation for credit; the textbook is *Geometric Folding Algorithms* by Demaine and O'Rourke.

Sample content covered includes: historical linkages converting linear motion to circular motion (Watt, Peaucellier), universality of linkages tracing polynomial curves, open problems on non-crossing linkages, rigidity testing being easy in 2D but open in 3D, reconfiguration complexity and locked trees and chains in 3D, NP-hardness of flat foldability of crease patterns, computational origami design (Origamizer and the tree method), the fold-and-cut theorem, curved creases, self-folding sheets and universal hinge patterns, paper thickness limitations, edge and general unfolding of polyhedra (dating to Dürer), and a recent theorem that any equal-area polygons can be connected in a hinged chain to fold into all of them, with applications to transformers and sculpture.

This passage is from a paper on coupling cell-centered finite volume (CCFV) and discontinuous Galerkin (DG) methods for steady, convection-dominated convection-diffusion problems. The authors introduce a bound-preserving technique targeting spurious overshoots and undershoots in high-order DG regions: if a DG cell average violates prescribed bounds (up to a tolerance), the approximation is reverted to CCFV in a small neighborhood of that cell, in a procedure similar to p-adaptivity, rather than through postprocessing. Once satisfactory cell averages are obtained, standard conservative slope limiters can be applied to make the full solution bound-preserving. The approach does not modify the CCFV or DG schemes and can be incorporated into hp-adaptivity routines.

The paper surveys related work, including nonintrusive DG postprocessing, FV-DG limiter approaches, artificial viscosity, flux-corrected transport, and nonlinear bound-preserving modifications, noting trade-offs among these methods regarding cost, bound preservation, conservation, and error analysis.

The model problem is a steady convection-diffusion equation with diffusion coefficient K, convection field β, reaction coefficient c, and source term f on a bounded polygonal domain with Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions. The domain is partitioned into an FV region and a DG region with a matching interface. The FV region requires a TPFA-admissible mesh (e.g., Voronoi), for which orthogonality and shape-regularity assumptions are stated. The passage defines mesh and facet notations, jump operators across interface types, and the coupled approximation space Xh, which uses degree-k polynomials in the DG region and piecewise constants in the FV region. The text ends mid-definition of the DG average operator.

A Yale-led research team compiled a dataset of historical urban populations going back to 3700 BC by digitizing and standardizing past research, extending beyond UN data limited to 1950. This passage is a transcript of the first lecture of MIT's 6.858 computer security course. The professor introduces course logistics: co-lecturer James Mickens (a visiting professor from Microsoft Research), four TAs, a lecture format based on discussing assigned research papers with questions submitted beforehand, and lab assignments in varying languages (C/Assembly, Python, JavaScript), with lab one requiring students to exploit buffer overflows in a web server. Students are also warned about MIT rules governing security research on its network.

The lecture defines security as achieving a goal despite an adversary, structured around three components: policy (goals such as confidentiality, integrity, and availability), threat model (assumptions about the adversary), and mechanism (the software or hardware enforcing the policy). Security is difficult because it is a "negative goal"—ensuring no unauthorized access—and is inherently iterative, with every system having a breaking point.

The professor gives examples of failures in each category:
- **Policy failures**: Yahoo's account recovery questions weakened security, exemplified by Sarah Palin's email compromise using information from Wikipedia; the Mat Honan case, where Gmail, Apple, and Amazon password-reset systems interacted to enable account takeover.
- **Threat model failures**: overestimating human behavior (strong passwords, avoiding phishing); outdated assumptions, such as Kerberos's 56-bit DES keys, which 6.858 students later broke; NSA hardware backdoors; SSL/TLS's assumption that hundreds of certificate authorities are all trustworthy; and a DARPA red team compromising a "secure" OS through its unsecured source code server.
- **Mechanism failures**: iCloud's find-my-iPhone interface lacking a password-guessing limit; Citibank's website allowing account access by changing a URL's ID number; Android Bitcoin wallets compromised by an unseeded SecureRandom() PRNG; and SSL certificates' length-based encoding conflicting with C's null-terminated strings, enabling certificate spoofing.

The professor then demonstrates a buffer overflow live: a C program using gets() overflows a stack buffer, overwriting the return address and letting an attacker redirect execution. He shows jumping to existing code, discusses injecting "shell code" into the buffer, and explains defenses like non-executable stacks and return-to-libc attacks that bypass them.

The lecture concludes that systems should minimize their trusted computing base—enforcing security policy through a small number of components—so that bugs elsewhere cannot violate security. Two quizzes are scheduled, with no final exam during final week.

The passage criticizes Keith E. Whittington's argument that, after the Kirk assassination, professors must self-censor to preserve academic freedom. This study uses molecular dynamics simulations with first-principles parameterized effective Hamiltonians to investigate topological textures in Zr-substituted barium titanate, Ba(ZrxTi1−x)O3 (BZT). In a 12.5% ordered superlattice, where Zr substitution doubles the unit cell along [111], induced nanodomains exhibit an alternating pattern: one half hosts the known −2 antiskyrmion composed of six −1/3 topological quarks, while the other hosts a +4 skyrmion with six +2/3 quarks. The integer offset of +1 per vortex arises from the reversed chemical motif between the two halves, which modifies the local anisotropy; an alternative field-theoretic interpretation based on an Ising-like color background is also presented. In randomly substituted BZT (0–12.5% Zr), nanodomains remain stable at 1 K, but increasing disorder pins and distorts vortices, producing a "skyrmion-glass"-like state with heterogeneous fractional charge redistribution. Thermal ramping shows that critical temperatures decrease with initial Zr substitution, reaching a minimum near 6–8% before partially recovering toward 12.5%; pure BT remains stable up to ~65–110 K depending on diameter. The 12.5% superlattice retains its rhombohedral phase above 300 K (rhombohedral–orthorhombic transition at ~320 K cooling, ~345 K heating). At 293 K, nanodomains cannot be retained without bias, but a local electric field of 350 kV/cm along [111] writes and stabilizes volatile Q=+4 textures in the superlattice, whereas the random composition fragments into multidomain states under the same field. The authors conclude that BZT provides a versatile platform for ferroelectric topology, from fractionalized quarks at low temperature to field-stabilized textures near room temperature, and identify strain, electrostatic engineering, and compositional patterning as routes toward nonvolatile room-temperature operation. The microscopic mechanism of topological charge transport between planes remains open for future investigation.

This study employs the quasiparticle self-consistent GW method augmented with excitonic ladder diagrams (QSGŴ) to investigate excitonic and magnetic proximity effects in WSe2/CrI3 van der Waals heterostructures, covering bilayer and FM/AFM trilayer configurations. Structures were optimized using DFT (PBE functional, DFT-D3 van der Waals corrections) with the C1 stacking and a 3.53 Å interlayer distance. LDA predicts a type II band alignment with a 0.77 eV gap, whereas QSGW and QSGŴ predict type I alignment with gaps of 2.33 and 2.21 eV, respectively, with both band edges on WSe2 (W-d character) at the K point. Because the predicted band gaps of CrI3 (~2.6 eV) and WSe2 (~2.3 eV) are similar, and CrI3's experimentally reported gap varies between 1 and 2.6 eV, the alignment is sensitive to deviations from pristine conditions. The proximity field produces ~1 meV (~10 tesla) splitting at the K point. Calculations reproduce WSe2's A and B excitons (binding energies 0.79 and 0.37 eV) and CrI3's Frenkel-like dd excitons at 1.45, 1.85, and 2.1 eV. Novel bright interlayer excitons appear between the A and B excitons (~1.84 eV, binding energy ~400 meV), with oscillator strength roughly twenty times that of intralayer CrI3 excitons, and are robust across all configurations. Magnetic splittings range from tens of GHz to 100 GHz in bilayer and AFM trilayer configurations, and reach ~1000 GHz for the B exciton in the FM trilayer; splittings are highly sensitive to band alignments, and finite splittings occur even in the AFM trilayer despite net zero magnetization. The authors conclude these heterostructures are promising platforms for tunable, bright, magnetic interlayer excitons relevant to photonic and spintronic applications, and suggest CrBr3-based structures would yield brighter interlayer excitons but smaller magnetic splittings.

Michael Liersch, head of goals-based advice and strategy at JPMorgan, says most investors can succeed by having a plan, managing their perspective, and staying the course. His five tips: (1) Make a plan—create a budget to see where your money goes and decide how much to invest or save; (2) Reframe decisions—view situations from a different perspective, such as seeing market declines as opportunities to buy low rather than reasons to panic; (3) Stay the course—investing is a long game, so be patient and don't try to time the market; (4) Don't go it alone—get a second opinion from someone with a different mindset, like a spouse or adviser; (5) Take small steps first—start with modest actions like paying down a credit card or contributing to an IRA, and consider automating savings.

This passage is a compilation of Indian newspaper articles from May 23–24, 2001, circulated by the Enron India Newsdesk, covering the Dabhol Power Company (DPC) dispute. The Centre is considering roping in the Power Trading Corporation to dispose of surplus Dabhol power in power-deficit states. Following the Dabhol debacle, Karnataka decided to review 11 private power projects. This paper compares the reproduction number (R), a standard measure of viral spread, with an alternative "acceleration index" (ε) introduced by the authors. The reproduction number's major shortcoming is that it does not account for the quantity of tests performed, even though observed cases depend on testing. The acceleration index is an elasticity measuring the percentage change of cases relative to the percentage change of tests, interpretable as the ratio of current to average viral speed. Theoretically, the authors show the reproduction number is a special case of the acceleration index: the ratio between the two equals the ratio of infectivity intensity to test intensity. When test intensity exceeds infectivity intensity, R overestimates viral acceleration; when infectivity intensity is greater, R underestimates it. Empirically, using French data from May 13, 2020, to October 26, 2022, the reproduction number largely underestimates viral spread compared to the acceleration index, particularly during the Omicron wave in autumn 2022. During the second French lockdown (starting October 30, 2020), R fell below 1 while the acceleration index still indicated ongoing acceleration. Similar analyses for five other countries confirm the bias is not specific to France. The authors conclude that public health authorities should track either the acceleration index alone or R combined with test and infectivity intensities, arguing the former is more parsimonious. Limitations include unaccounted cases when testing is not compulsory, asymptomatic cases, and the index's dependence on testing volume and its associated costs.

This study examined the intentions of Ethiopian national education policy documents and the conceptualizations of secondary school principals and teachers regarding curriculum differentiation (CD). Two principals and 17 subject teachers from one regular and one special day secondary school in Addis Ababa were selected through purposive and convenience sampling. Data were collected through document analysis of the Education and Training Policy (2023), the General Education Curriculum Framework (2020), and the Guidelines for CD and IEP (2012), and through interviews. The ETP and GECF conceptualize CD in terms of multiple pathways, including fields of study, streams, and school types, whereas the Guidelines emphasize differentiation of curriculum components—contents, instructional processes, assessment strategies, and learning environments—and highlight inclusive classrooms. Principals' and teachers' conceptualizations varied across three levels: lack of awareness, divergent views, and alignment with policy intentions, falling under five themes: CD as gifted programs, as student placement into subjects, streams, and schools, as special curriculum for groups of students, as identification and accommodation of gifts and talents, and as curricular planning and teaching strategy. The absence of coherent policy guidance and the limited engagement of principals and teachers with reform ideas contributed to these variations. Additionally, school-type-based differentiation practices appear to inadequately address policy intentions, as they do not correspond to variations in subject types and levels of difficulty. The study concludes that policy coherence on CD and flexible, diverse secondary school curriculum structures are needed to meet students' varied needs, abilities, and career aspirations.

The commissioner had long faith in Las Vegas as an NHL market, despite hurdles including securing a building, a committed ownership group, and an economic problem. Former FBI Deputy Director Andrew McCabe was fired on March 16, two days before his planned early retirement at age 50, following an OIG investigation into his approval of unauthorized media disclosures about the Hillary Clinton email probe. Under the Federal Employees Retirement System, he was set to receive an estimated $60,000 annual pension, but his firing puts that at risk until age 57 and eight months, along with loss of family health insurance coverage. The passage explains that pensions are defined benefit plans in which employers guarantee post-retirement payouts, unlike 401(k) defined contribution plans. Some lawmakers offered McCabe temporary Capitol Hill work to secure his pension, but a former official said this would only work if the role were a primary law enforcement position, or he would need to work another 10 years. McCabe can file an appeal.

The June 4, 2001 ISDA Press Report compiles news on risk management, credit derivatives, energy, Latin America, and structured products. On Basle II, revised capital adequacy rules are expected to be agreed by year-end 2001 for implementation in 2004, though disagreements persist. Australia's regulator APRA argued proposed residential mortgage risk weightings create competitive inequalities, as large banks using internal ratings-based methods could apply 5–10 percent weightings versus the standard 50 percent. Asian central bankers said infrastructure and capacity limitations may prevent full implementation by 2004. The banking community's reaction was largely negative: big banks called the plan too conservative, smaller banks warned of higher capital costs and a deepening divide between rich and poor nations, and the Institute of International Finance estimated costs of $2.25 trillion over five years for 30,000 banks. Derivatives industry officials are optimistic some criticisms will be adopted, but the fate of the 15 percent "W" factor charge on credit derivatives remains unclear; ISDA criticized rigid capital floors, operational risk and "W" charges, and internal ratings calibration.

In credit derivatives, an ISDA working group is nearing completion of standardized documentation for swaps based on convertible bonds, while a new subcommittee is prioritizing how contracts are treated in demergers, spurred by AT&T's planned restructuring and unresolved National Power swaps. Deutsche Bank and ABN-Amro withdrew from managing Argentina's roughly $20 billion debt exchange over concerns research may have breached US securities regulations, risking shares of $110 million in fees. In energy, California's Independent System Operator is headed toward a showdown with FERC over board independence amid state government influence. Finally, structured products built with options are popular in developed markets and are expected to do well in India.

Using data from the China Education Panel Survey (13,981 students after handling missing values), this study applies descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression to examine the relationship between parental education level and child cognitive ability, controlling for child, family, and school characteristics and testing mediating effects of educational expectations and parent-child interaction. Findings show a significant positive correlation: a one-year increase in the maximum parental education raises child cognitive ability by 0.019 points. Effects are partially mediated by expectations and investment, are stronger for girls and urban families than for boys and rural families, and are greater among children with lower cognitive ability.

In this lecture, Siqi Zheng discusses portfolio-level financing of sustainable real estate, focusing on REITs and green bonds. REITs are publicly traded companies investing primarily in income-generating commercial real estate. They enjoy tax benefits (no corporate-level income tax) if 75% of assets are in real estate and 90% of annual income is distributed. Compared to direct property ownership, REITs offer geographic diversification, liquidity, lower capital requirements, and tax advantages, but less investor control. International examples were discussed, including Colombia, Mexico, Thailand, and China, where infrastructure-focused REITs were launched by quasi-governmental entities after cities lost land-sale revenue during the pandemic recession.

Research on green REITs shows over 60% of large US REITs have net-zero carbon targets, largely driven by institutional investors—especially European and Canadian pension funds—who condition capital on sustainability performance; Middle Eastern investors care least. A 2012 study found REITs with higher shares of LEED-certified and Energy Star properties had higher returns on assets and equity and lower beta, though reverse causality is a possible concern. Ongoing research distinguishes REITs' "green talking" from actual "green doing."

Green bonds are fixed-income instruments issued by governments or companies, with proceeds earmarked for green investments; they enable lower cost of capital. Fannie Mae issues green bonds backed by pools of green mortgages. Non-profit Green Bond Principles require issuers to meet standards to prevent greenwashing.

Finally, the lecture covered data and benchmarking tools—EPA Portfolio Manager, measurabl, DNV carbon audits, CRREM, and GRESB, a portfolio-level ESG rating system founded by Nils Kok. Studies link higher GRESB scores to better returns and lower borrowing costs. However, MIT's ESG Confusion project notes that ESG ratings across providers are inconsistent, noisy, and weakly correlated.

The passage documents AMD AGESA procedures. AMD_ENABLE_STACK is a stackless assembler routine using a register passing model that initializes the processor and cache to establish a pre-memory stack region before main memory is available. The stack is divided among processor cores, mapped to global address space, and MTRRs are set; it must run on all cores. It handles protected and real mode stack setup and creates a UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF instance. Status codes include success, warning (stack reentry), and fatal (unknown processor family). AARCH64 APUs with PSP do not use the stack; the PSP initializes DRAM. AMD_DISABLE_STACK removes the pre-memory stack once main memory is available, disables CAR mode without modifying MCRR settings, flushes cache lines, must run on all cores, and should only be invoked by the BSP; it preserves EBX. AmdCreateStruct creates and pre-initializes storage for AGESA parameter structures using PreMemHeap, PostMemDram, or ByHost allocation methods.

The passage is a whitepaper describing the NVIDIA Ampere GA10x GPU architecture, focusing on the GA102 GPU and features common to GA10x GPUs. GA102 powers the GeForce RTX 3090, GeForce RTX 3080, NVIDIA RTX A6000, and NVIDIA A40, while GA104 powers the GeForce RTX 3070. Compared to Turing, the Ampere architecture is up to 1.7x faster in raster graphics and up to 2x faster in ray tracing.

Key architectural features include:
- **2x FP32 processing**: GA10x SMs execute FP32 on both datapaths, doubling FP32 throughput (over 35 FP32 TFLOPS in RTX 3090).
- **Second-generation RT Cores**: double the ray/triangle intersection testing rate of Turing and add an Interpolate Triangle Position unit enabling hardware-accelerated ray-traced motion blur (up to 8x faster than Turing). GA10x also supports concurrent RT Core, graphics, and compute workloads.
- **Third-generation Tensor Cores**: support new data types (TF32, BF16) and Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity, doubling throughput for sparse matrices (RTX 3080 delivers 238 sparse Tensor TFLOPS).
- **GDDR6X memory**: developed with Micron using PAM4 signaling, supporting up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec bandwidth in the RTX 3090.
- **Other features**: third-generation NVLink (112.5 GB/sec total between two GPUs), PCIe Gen 4, 112 ROPs on full GA102, larger L1 cache (128 KB per SM), and DLSS 8K support enabling 8K60 gaming on the RTX 3090.

The whitepaper also covers NVIDIA RTX IO, which enables GPU-based loading and lossless decompression of game assets via Microsoft's DirectStorage API, delivering up to 100x I/O throughput and lower CPU utilization. The NVIDIA A40 data center GPU provides up to 2X FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to 5X (10X with sparsity) AI training throughput versus the Quadro RTX 6000. Display features include DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 (8K60), fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode (the first GPU to offer it), and seventh-generation NVENC. Appendices cover GeForce RTX 3090/3070 specifications, a new Error Detection and Replay (EDR) feature for GDDR6X memory overclocking, and RTX A6000 professional performance data.

The American whaling bark Cape Horn Pigeon was in the Okhotsk Sea on September 10, 1892, engaged in whaling. Her captain had twice called at Vladivostok and requested Russian permission to fish in certain bays, because Russia had issued an 1875 notice forbidding whaling within 3 miles of its coast or in bays within that limit. Permission was not granted, but Russia gave no indication it claimed jurisdiction over the entire Okhotsk Sea. Nevertheless, the bark was seized on the open sea by an officer of the Imperial Russian navy commanding an armed vessel and taken by force to Vladivostok, despite the captain's protests; the crew was compelled to navigate the vessel. The bark was detained until October 1, 1892. The arresting officer claimed the Okhotsk Sea was a closed sea, a claim unsupported by Russia's June 1893 note. After the captain telegraphed the US legation at St. Petersburg and the US Chargé d'Affaires protested, Russia replied that the bark had been released.

In this introductory lecture, Professor Scott Hughes outlines the materials and structure for a one-semester general relativity course. The main textbook is Sean Carroll's text (semi-required), supplemented by Schutz's *A First Course in General Relativity* (second edition recommended, as the first contains errors), Misner, Thorne and Wheeler's *Gravitation* (a useful reference but not recommended for beginners), and Wald's mathematically rigorous *General Relativity*. Grades are based entirely on 11 problem sets—ten worth 9% each and one worth 10%—with no final exam. The first half of the course covers the mathematical foundations of general relativity, culminating in the Einstein field equations before spring break; the second half covers applications such as Newton's law, classic tests of relativity, cosmology, black holes, gravitational waves, and neutron stars.

The course begins with special relativity presented in geometric language to introduce the mathematical tools. Spacetime is defined as a manifold of events endowed with a metric: a manifold is a collection of points with connectedness properties, an event specifies when and where something happens, and the metric provides a notion of distance between events. An inertial reference frame is visualized as a lattice of clocks and measuring rods that moves freely (no forces, no rotation), with orthogonal, uniformly spaced rods, uniformly ticking clocks, and synchronization via Einstein's procedure, which exploits the invariance of the speed of light. Units are chosen so that the speed of light equals 1. The lecture then introduces the displacement vector between events as a geometric object existing independently of coordinate representation, with different observers' components related by Lorentz transformations. Notation covered includes four-vector arrows, Greek spacetime indices, Einstein's summation convention, and the distinction between dummy and free indices. Finally, a spacetime vector is defined as a quartet of numbers that transforms between inertial reference frames like the displacement vector and obeys vector space linearity rules, with scalars required to be Lorentz invariant.

Ultra-processed food (UPF), which contributes up to 60% of calories consumed in developed nations, is increasingly linked to adverse health outcomes, but existing food processing classification systems are subjective, inconsistent, and poorly reproducible. To address this, the authors developed FoodProX, a machine-learning algorithm that translates nutrient concentrations from nutrition facts into a continuous Food Processing Score (FPro) ranging from 0 (unprocessed) to 1 (ultra-processed), trained on NOVA classification labels. Applying this to over 50,000 products from the online stores of Walmart, Target, and WholeFoods, they created GroceryDB, an open-source database publicly available at http://TrueFood.Tech/. Analysis showed most grocery offerings are ultra-processed, with WholeFoods offering more minimally-processed items than Target or Walmart. Higher processing is generally associated with cheaper price per calorie, though this varies by category (e.g., a 10% FPro increase corresponds to a 24.3% price-per-calorie decrease in soups & stews, but an increasing trend for milk & milk-substitutes). The authors also introduced IgFPro, an Ingredient Processing Score ranking individual ingredients' contribution to ultra-processing, finding that complex ingredient trees, certain additives, and oils such as palm, vegetable, and soybean oil signal ultra-processing. GroceryDB aims to support consumer decision-making, public health initiatives, and policymaking. Limitations include reliance on nutrition facts alone, which may miss processing-induced matrix changes; future work aims to incorporate chemical composition data on additives and processing byproducts.

This study examines the reliability of deep learning-based mammographic density predictions on low dose (approximately 10% of standard dose) mammograms compared to standard dose images, motivated by the potential to assess breast cancer risk in younger women who are not routinely screened. Two datasets were used: ALDRAM, containing paired standard and low dose images from 147 women aged 31–45 previously diagnosed with unilateral breast cancer, and PROCAS, comprising 15,290 standard dose mammograms with density labels averaged from pairs of radiologist readers, used for training. ResNet-18 models were trained separately on standard dose PROCAS images and on simulated low dose images generated from them.

All models showed high correlation with radiologist labels. Predictions on standard and low dose ALDRAM images were highly similar, particularly when averaging across CC and MLO views and across multiple trained models, which significantly improved agreement. No effect of age or dose ratio was found. However, prediction differences increased at higher densities and smaller breast areas, with low dose predictions generally lower than standard dose ones. The apparent effect of image size was attributed to its relationship with breast area. Larger differences between CC and MLO predictions, or between separately trained models, were associated with larger standard–low dose differences. No significant outliers were identified. The authors conclude that low dose mammography can support density estimation comparable to standard dose, especially when averaging views and models, though systematic differences and confounding factors warrant further investigation and possible corrections.

Tecomaria capensis (Cape Honeysuckle), a scrambling shrub or small tree up to 6 m in the Bignoniaceae family, bears orange-red trumpet-shaped flowers and is a popular garden and hedging plant. Listed as Least Concern by SANBI, it occurs in thicket and on forest margins across southern, eastern and tropical Africa, including several South African provinces. Browsed by game and stock and visited by sunbirds, butterflies and honey-bees, it is used in traditional medicine for fever, pain, sleeplessness, chest ailments, dysentery and to encourage milk flow. Nursing mothers wear carved wooden necklets (isixhoxho) made from its wood as protective amulets. It grows best in well-drained soil with compost, mulching and regular pruning.
Various views of a headphone design; broken lines depict unclaimed environmental subject matter.

The passage describes NVIDIA's Turing GPU architecture. VirtualLink enables VR headsets to connect via a single USB-C connector, bringing VR to small form factor devices. Turing's TU102 and TU104 GPUs replace MIO/PCIe-based SLI with NVLink (25 GB/sec per direction per link), supporting only two-way SLI. Turing introduces RT Cores in TU102, TU104, and TU106 GPUs that accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection, enabling real-time ray tracing at 10+ Giga Rays/sec versus Pascal's 1.1—roughly 10x faster. Hybrid Rendering combines rasterization and ray tracing, aided by denoising to reduce rays per pixel. NGX, a deep learning stack using Tensor Cores, includes DLSS (trained on 64x supersampled reference images, with a standard mode and DLSS 2X), InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. Mesh Shading adds Task and Mesh Shaders, eliminating CPU draw call bottlenecks. Variable Rate Shading permits per-16x16-pixel shading rate control, enabling Content Adaptive Shading, Motion Adaptive Shading, and Foveated Rendering. Texture Space Shading decouples shading from screen space, and Multi-View Rendering supports up to four views per pass. The TU104 (3072 CUDA cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores) powers the GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000; the TU106 (2304 CUDA cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores) powers the GeForce RTX 2070 without NVLink. RTX-OPS is introduced as a workload-based performance metric. The document concludes with legal disclaimers and trademark information.

This passage describes a bundle of three short-selling trading strategies, backtested only on SPY, XLP, and SMH ETFs. Entries and exits occur at the close or next open, with no commissions or slippage included. The bundle provides trading rules in plain English plus code for Amibroker, TradeStation/EasyLanguage, and TradingView/Pine Script (no guarantees for the latter). The connections bypass the public internet, reduce latency, and provide greater routing control, though data is not encrypted by default.
