The newsletter also lists headlines covering topics including the government shutdown's expected furlough of more than 32,000 HHS employees, the Trump administration backing off 100% pharma tariffs, a Trump-Pfizer drug pricing deal, Tylenol and autism debates, women's health, and company news involving Amgen, Lilly, MoonLake, and Uniqure.

Nanyang Polytechnic scientists led by Dr Henry Leung have developed a sustainable way to turn coffee waste into biodegradable plastic. Water and bacteria are added to the waste; after seven to 10 days, the bacteria produce a biopolymer, PHA, used to make biodegradable plastic. The team used Cupriavidus necator bacteria, which works at room temperature. Switching to eco-friendly acetone and an alkaline solvent and genetically modifying the bacteria raised purity above 50 per cent, yielding 1g to 3g of PHA per 100g of waste. PHA decomposes faster and releases fewer toxic compounds than PVC. With laboratory experiments completed, the team seeks industrial partners and aims to commercialise the process in three to five years.

The Supreme Court of Iowa reversed and remanded a district court decision that had allowed Gary G. Kehde to recover unemployment benefits after the Iowa Department of Job Service disqualified him for misconduct under section 96.5(2). Kehde was discharged by Dubuque Packing Company after a supervisor found him holding a lit marijuana cigarette on company premises during a work break. The claims deputy, hearing officer, and appeal board all found he had violated a known company rule, constituting misconduct. After an arbitration decision in Kehde's union grievance, Dubuque Pack attempted to withdraw its protest to Kehde's benefits claim, but the appeal board refused, stating a protest could not be withdrawn after a hearing and decision. Kehde petitioned for judicial review without first applying for a rehearing, and the district court ruled the Department's refusal to honor the withdrawal was arbitrary and an abuse of discretion.

On appeal, the Supreme Court held that the district court had jurisdiction, because an application for rehearing under section 96.6(8) is not a prerequisite to judicial review, consistent with Ellis v. Iowa Department of Job Service. However, the court found the district court erred in reversing the Department, since withdrawal of a protest does not alter eligibility, which is determined by the facts of the case; any error in refusing the withdrawal was harmless. The court also held that substantial evidence supported the misconduct finding: possession of marijuana, a serious misdemeanor, on company premises constituted a deliberate violation of standards the employer had a right to expect, even though there was insufficient evidence that Kehde knew of the company rule. The case was reversed and remanded to the district court.

Industry-sponsored clinical trials have become increasingly complex, lengthening Phase II and III trials and increasing burdens on participants and staff. ICH guideline E19 encourages reducing irrelevant data collection, but little progress has been made, and "copy-and-paste" protocol design allows complexity to accumulate. Because no prior study measured how protocol design inefficiencies affect trial costs, participant hours, and staff time, Merck initiated a "Lean Design" project. Using Faro Health's Smart Design Tool, which estimates burden, hours, costs, and complexity in real time, workshops applied Lean Design principles to six protocols across therapeutic areas. The method rebuilds schedules of assessment (SoAs) from a minimal "Ground Zero" starting point, adding assessments only when biologically plausible, with timing, frequency, and sample sizes justified; routine clinical care items are excluded, and only relevant laboratory panel elements are captured. Recommendations would have reduced participant hours by 4 to 47 per participant per trial; in a 12,600-participant cardiovascular trial, recommended savings of $9,000 per participant totaled nearly $120 million, while few changes were recommended for the oncology trial. Teams adopted some but not all changes, limited by late protocol stages and caution, yet partial adoption still yielded substantial savings (e.g., about $58 million in the cardiovascular trial). Merck has launched a company-wide implementation of Lean Design principles, though generalizability to other companies requires testing.

The IMF described Ghana's 'Ghana beyond Aid' vision and first-year economic performance under President Akufo-Addo as an inspiration to Africa. Finance Minister Ken Ofori-Atta, speaking at the IMF/World Bank Spring Meetings, outlined revenue measures to boost domestic resource mobilisation and fund job-creating growth initiatives.

A regulation American football field measures 120 yards (360 feet) long and 53.3 yards (160 feet) wide, covering about 1.32 acres, with 100 yards of open field between 10-yard-deep end zones. Ball carriers must break the plane of the end zone or goal line to score, and pass catchers must show control with one foot in bounds (two in the NFL). Goal lines sit 100 yards apart and span sideline to sideline. Yard lines are marked every yard, with solid lines every five yards and numbers every ten. Hash marks aid ball placement and vary by level: 18 feet 6 inches apart in the NFL, 40 feet in college, and 53 feet 4 inches in high school. Field numbers are placed 12 yards from the sideline in the NFL, 9 yards in college, and 6 yards in high school. Sidelines are 6 feet wide, and coaches are commonly restricted between the 25-yard lines to keep the sideline orderly and end zones clear for officials.

Since 2015, WebRTC bugs have leaked users' real IPs despite VPN use, though most providers can now hide IPs. On March 27, 2018, Stagno tested 124 VPN and proxy providers: 20 (16.13%) leaked IPs via WebRTC, while 101 kept IPs hidden. A Google Docs list includes logging policies. Users can test for leaks online and disable WebRTC or install add-ons if leaks occur; most browsers enable WebRTC by default except Tor Browser, Edge, and Internet Explorer. Ranked non-leaking VPNs are listed, with ExpressVPN rated best.

MoviePass, which offers subscribers a movie per day for $6.95 per month, has signed a marketing and performance-based revenue agreement with an unnamed independent movie distribution company, meaning it will promote specific films and earn revenue from incremental ticket sales. The service reported that its ticket purchases accounted for 13.21% of the opening weekend domestic box office for Roman J. Israel, Esq. and 10.00% for Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri, with its share increasing from the first to second weeks for films like Justice League, Coco, and The Snowman. MoviePass's parent company, Helios and Matheson Analytics, plans to use subscriber viewing data to target advertisements, similar to Facebook or Google.

The passage describes a patent application for an improved non-occluding intravascular blood pump designed to reduce hemolysis and blood clotting caused by shear stress hotspots. The pump comprises a cylindrical shroud with an inlet and outlet, an impeller sharing a central axis with the shroud, a centrally disposed motor that rotates the impeller, and pillars coupling the motor to the shroud. Hemolysis-reducing design features include a trumpeted shroud with a larger inlet than outlet, a sufficient inlet length (e.g., at least 1.5 times the shroud inner diameter, approximately 9 mm in the prototype) to prevent turbulent flow detachment, an elongated bare hub (0.2–0.3 times the shroud inner diameter), raked-back impeller blade leading edges (e.g., 75–85 degrees), a wrap angle of approximately 100 degrees, shroud-to-blade clearance of 200–300 microns, matched impeller and stator flare angles, and pillar angles matched to the outlet blade angle. The device, suited as a minimally invasive axial pump (~6 mm) for NYHA Class III–IVa patients and placed in the descending aorta, was optimized through three phases of design and testing. Transient CFD simulations identified hotspots at the impeller, inflow shroud, and pillars, and hemolysis was estimated using Lagrangian particle tracking with Heuser constants. The final prototype (P_31) with 30-degree pillars and an extended shroud reduced maximum impeller shear stress by 150–200 Pa, lowered mean shear below 400 Pa up to 30,000 rpm, showed a 78% NIH improvement at 20,000 rpm, and maintained or slightly improved hydraulic output and efficiency.

MRC Vaudreuil-Soulanges council members reassured residents that collected recyclables are valued, responding to a global recycling crisis. China, formerly the buyer of two-thirds of North America's recyclables, issued stringent standards deeming contaminated plastics and paper of little value, concerning Canadian municipalities. Since 2017, the MRC has belonged to Tricentris, a non-profit managing nearly 33 percent of Quebec's recyclables. Officials visiting the Lachute sorting centre stated Tricentris is doing well and urged citizens to continue recycling.

Asteroid 2025 TF, measuring 1 to 3 meters in diameter, passed within 428 ± 7 km of Earth's surface over Antarctica at 00:47:26 UTC on October 1—roughly the altitude of the International Space Station. The Catalina Sky Survey detected it a few hours after the flyby, and astronomers from ESA's Planetary Defence Office later observed it with the Las Cumbres Observatory telescope at Siding Spring, Australia, determining its distance and timing of closest approach with high precision. Objects of this size pose no real threat, typically producing fireballs and small meteorites. Larger asteroids pose greater risks, prompting international planetary defense monitoring efforts.

This appeal for reappraisement concerned the dutiable value of Christmas tree ornaments exported from Germany and imported at Boston. Based on a stipulation, the court found the merchandise similar to that in F. W. Woolworth Co. v. United States and incorporated that case's record. It held the proper dutiable foreign and export values to be the per se unit invoice prices plus 3% social assessments, plus packing and container costs when not included. The appeal was dismissed as to all other merchandise.

This study employs molecular dynamics simulations to investigate radiation damage in pure niobium at primary knock-on atom (PKA) energies of 1–75 keV at 300 K, comparing four interatomic potentials: EAM, FS-1, FS-2, and the machine-learning-based SNAP potential. Surviving Frenkel pair production follows a power-law relation with PKA energy, exhibiting two regimes with a transition near 20 keV where subcascade formation begins. At low energies, defect production and clustering follow trends governed by the stiffness-to-range ratio (|S/R|), threshold displacement energy, and defect formation energies, with FS-1 as an exception; at higher energies, subcascade formation makes these parameters insufficient to explain cascade behavior. Vacancy clustering exceeds interstitial clustering across all potentials and energies, resembling vanadium rather than tungsten. Defect morphology is highly potential-dependent: EAM produces a balanced mix of C15-like rings and 1/2⟨111⟩ loops with rare ⟨100⟩ clusters; FS-2 favors extended 1/2⟨111⟩ dumbbells, crowdions, and dislocation loops; FS-1 and SNAP generate more compact or disordered clusters, with SNAP producing a high fraction of C15-like rings that may evolve into 1/2⟨111⟩ and ⟨100⟩ dislocation loops. Older potentials produced more defects and predicted incorrect self-interstitial atom ground-state configurations compared to newer potentials.

Winning gives confidence and forces the opponent to adjust. The days off allowed the team to enjoy their San Jose win. A day-to-day player key to faceoffs and penalty kills remains uncertain. The upcoming opponent is big, strong, and skilled, making a tough matchup; the key is playing to their potential.

Horsell Lodge near Woking, Surrey, provides specialised residential and dementia care, from short-term respite to long-term, with bespoke support; service descriptions come from the care home without accuracy guarantees.

A WIRED review compares the Google Pixel Watch 4 ($399 for the 45-mm model, $349 for the 41-mm) with the Apple Watch Ultra 3 ($1,300–$2,000) as an outdoor adventure watch option under $500. In testing during camping, running, and hiking trips, the Watch Ultra 3 was the overall winner but costs twice as much. Both watches lasted a full weekend of use; the Watch Ultra 3 offers up to 42 hours of battery life and the Pixel Watch 4 offers 30–40 hours with fast charging. Both have satellite communications requiring an active carrier plan, though the Pixel Watch 4 supports only 911 emergency calls in the contiguous US, while the Watch Ultra 3 allows regular texting internationally. The Watch Ultra 3 is more durable (10ATM vs. 5ATM) and functions as a dive computer. However, the Pixel Watch 4 offers better sleep tracking through Fitbit, an integrated bike computer, dual-band GPS, and convenient Google Maps offline syncing. The reviewer concludes that the Pixel Watch 4 is the strongest adventure watch option under $500, noting that not even Garmin offers satellite communications at that price.

Machine learning (ML)-assisted GWAS, which imputes missing phenotypes to increase statistical power, is increasingly common but its validity has not been carefully evaluated. The authors show through theoretical analysis, simulations, and benchmarking that conventional ML-assisted GWAS can produce pervasive false positives: a GWAS on imputed type 2 diabetes in UK Biobank had an 81% replication failure rate against a ground-truth GWAS, partly because HbA1c used in imputation is influenced by non-glycemic (erythrocytic) pathways irrelevant to diabetes risk. Existing methods treat imputed phenotypes as observed and yield biased estimands unless strong, unrealistic conditions hold. To address this, the authors introduce POP-GWAS, a framework that combines three sets of GWAS summary statistics (observed phenotype in labeled samples, imputed phenotype in labeled samples, and imputed phenotype in unlabeled samples) to debias estimates on a SNP-by-SNP basis. POP-GWAS provides unbiased estimates and valid p-values regardless of imputation algorithm, variables, or quality; is always at least as powerful as GWAS on observed phenotypes; and requires only summary statistics. The authors also derive a closed-form effective sample size formula showing an upper bound given fixed imputation quality. Applied to DXA-derived bone mineral density across 14 skeletal sites in UKB, POP-GWAS identified 188 loci (39% more than conventional GWAS) and, with meta-analysis, 89 novel loci, revealing site-specific genetic architecture including a head-specific association at LGR5. Software and a power calculator are publicly available.

Live Nation is offering $20 all-in tickets to thousands of summer concerts from April 30 through May 8 for National Concert Week, with over 1.5 million tickets across multiple genres, featuring artists including Alan Jackson, Bon Jovi, and Shakira.

A Federal High Court in Katsina ordered former Governor Ibrahim Shema remanded in EFCC custody until April 27 over alleged misappropriation of about N5.7 billion SURE-P funds. Shema pleaded not guilty to 26 fraud charges. His bail application was opposed by prosecution as premature; the court will hear it on April 27.

The paper extends the study of semiring semantics to existential second-order logic, proving analogues of Fagin's and Cook's theorems over commutative, positive, non-trivial semirings K. After reviewing semirings' applications in computer science (weighted automata, BSS machines, database provenance) and existing semiring semantics for logics, the authors define propositional logic PL=K, first-order logic FO=K, and existential second-order logic ESO=K with formula (in)equality atoms and constants from K, where satisfaction corresponds to non-zero semiring values, and introduce the satisfiability problem SAT=K. Existential second-order quantifiers range over K-relations in the Boolean sense (values restricted to 0 or 1); the problem 4-FEAS≥0 of degree-4 polynomials over non-negative reals is shown definable in ESO=R≥0. The BSS machine model is adapted to semirings (BSSK machines), with non-determinism realized by guessing additional K-values appended to the input, yielding the class NPK of languages decidable in polynomial time by non-deterministic BSSK machines, along with polynomial-time many-one reductions and NPK-completeness. The main result is a version of Fagin's theorem, ESO=K = NPK: the inclusion ESO=K ⊆ NPK follows from polynomial-time evaluation of FO=K formulas, while the converse encodes machine computations via existentially quantified K-relations for tape contents and node states over ordered K-interpretations. The work also generalizes the connection between the Boolean part of NPR and the existential theory of the reals to positive commutative semirings, introducing a novel non-arithmetic reduction.

Jason Day will face Louis Oosthuizen, Jason Dufner, and James Hahn in the WGC-Match Play group stage, a rematch of his 2016 final win. Marc Leishman is grouped with Branden Grace, Bubba Watson, and Julian Suri, while Cameron Smith faces Hideki Matsuyama, Patrick Cantlay, and Yusaku Miyazato. Smith needs a strong finish to secure a Masters invitation.

This paper presents a framework for designing dilute viscoelastic fluids (Boger fluids) with prescribed rheological properties. Using polyisobutylene (PIB) dissolved in a polybutene–light mineral oil solvent mixture, the authors extract the shear modulus G0, relaxation time τ, and polymer-solvent interaction parameter χ from small-amplitude oscillatory shear measurements fitted to the Zimm model, and measure the first normal stress difference coefficient ψ1 via rotational shear tests. They experimentally determine power-law scaling relationships between these rheological properties and the design parameters—polymer concentration c, molecular weight M, and solvent viscosity ηs—noting deviations from theory, such as a weak dependence of τ on c and a correction factor δχ showing that the Zimm approximation overestimates ψ1. Because the measured scaling matrix has full rank, it can be inverted to compute the fluid composition needed to achieve target values of G0, τ, and ψ1. The authors validate the approach by fabricating fluids with independently controlled G0 and τ, and fluids with nearly constant ψ1 despite viscosity varying by roughly a factor of nine. The method enables decoupling viscous and elastic effects in flow experiments, estimating properties of fluids below rheometer torque resolution, and testing viscoelastic flow theories based on Oldroyd-B or FENE-P models.

The Supreme Court returns this week for its annual "long conference," the unofficial end of the summer recess, where justices will review the 1,000 to 2,000 cert petitions accumulated since June and are expected to grant five to 15 cases; the 2025-26 term begins Monday, Oct. 6. Justice Clarence Thomas criticized treating stare decisis as "talismanic," while former Justice Anthony Kennedy, promoting a new book, expressed concern about rising partisanship and antagonistic discourse in the court's opinions. Other pieces profiled Louisiana solicitor general J. Benjamin Aguiñaga's work on Voting Rights Act and Ten Commandments cases, Joel Klein's reflections on clerking for Justice Lewis Powell, and George F. Will's praise of Justice Amy Coney Barrett's originalism. On Friday, the court allowed the Trump administration to withhold nearly $4 billion in foreign-aid funding over a dissent, and the administration asked the court to review the legality of Trump's birthright citizenship executive order. A response brief on ending protected status for Venezuelans is due today. Analysis also found emergency docket speed in 2024 correlated with outcomes: conservative-result cases averaged 23 days versus 41 for liberal ones.

In Week 6 of Idaho high school football, the top 15 rankings remained largely intact as top teams won, with Bishop Kelly and Eagle surviving scares to stay undefeated. Two new teams entered the rankings: Minico (4-1) and Ririe (6-0), while Middleton and Capital dropped out. Notable results included Bishop Kelly's 22-20 escape against Columbia, Rocky Mountain's 41-7 win over Centennial, Eagle's 21-14 victory over Mountain View, Timberline's 50-19 rout of Capital, and Coeur d'Alene's 50-9 homecoming win over previously unbeaten Sandpoint, which fell from No. 15. Owyhee improved to 5-0 for the first time in program history, Lakeland started 6-0 for the first time in over 20 years, and the Panthers extended the state's longest winning streak to 15 games.

This email forwards a November 2001 Texas Monthly article by Mimi Swartz, "How Enron Blew It," examining the company's decline. The article describes Enron's transformation from a stodgy pipeline company in 1985 into a trading colossus, with its stock rising 1,700 percent over sixteen years and revenues growing from $40 billion to $100 billion. Jeff Skilling, hired as a consultant by then-CEO Ken Lay, drove this change through the "Gas Bank" concept, in which Enron bought and sold gas itself and profited on transactions like an investment bank. Skilling built a culture recruiting aggressive graduates from top schools with uncapped, merit-based bonuses, and the company expanded into electricity, broadband, EnronOnline, and other commodities, using mark-to-market accounting on an unprecedented scale. The internal culture grew harsh, marked by a forced-ranking Performance Review Committee ("rank and yank"), high turnover, and paranoia. Skilling sidelined rival Rebecca Mark by placing her in charge of Azurix, a water venture that failed, and became CEO in February 2001. Trouble followed quickly: criticism over California's energy crisis, a costly Indian power plant, the collapse of the telecom and Blockbuster ventures, and analyst questions about accounting practices. Executives sold large amounts of stock, and the share price fell from a high of $80 in January to below $40 by late August. Skilling resigned abruptly after six months, citing family time; Lay returned as CEO, promising a kinder, gentler company innovating "much closer to our core." Skilling maintains his interests were aligned with shareholders, noting 90 percent of his net worth was in Enron stock, and says he plans to remain involved in commodity trading in Houston.

The NBA released its full 2017-18 season schedule on Monday, four days after announcing the Christmas Day schedule and the first week's national TV lineup. The passage lists the complete national TV schedule from October through April, with all times Eastern, airing on TNT, ESPN, ABC, and NBA TV. Opening night on Oct. 17 features Boston at Cleveland and Houston at Golden State on TNT. Christmas Day games include Philadelphia at New York (ESPN), Cleveland at Golden State, Washington at Boston, and Houston at Oklahoma City (all ABC), and Minnesota at L.A. Lakers (TNT).

Euro zone stocks opened 2017 at their highest in more than a year after data showed manufacturing activity grew at its fastest pace in over five years, lifting the Euro STOXX 50 by 0.5 percent. The euro slipped 0.4 percent below $1.05 as the dollar strengthened on expectations of U.S. rate hikes and Trump administration fiscal expansion. Italy's FTSE MIB rose 1.5 percent to lead European indexes, while lower-rated euro zone bond yields fell to multi-week lows. Islamic State attacks in Istanbul (39 killed) and Baghdad (24 killed) had little market impact, though the Turkish lira slipped. China's manufacturing expanded for a fifth month, the yuan posted its biggest annual loss in over 20 years, and bitcoin rose above $1,000 for the first time since late 2013.

Apple Inc.'s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 26, 2015 describes the Company as a California corporation established in 1977 and headquartered in Cupertino, California, that designs, manufactures and markets mobile communication and media devices, personal computers and portable digital music players, along with related software, services, accessories and third-party digital content. Products include iPhone, iPad, Mac, iPod, Apple Watch and Apple TV, supported by the iOS, OS X, watchOS and tvOS operating systems and services such as the iTunes Store, App Store, Apple Music, iCloud, AppleCare and Apple Pay. In September 2015, the Company announced iPhone 6s and 6s Plus, iPad Pro, iOS 9, OS X El Capitan, watchOS 2 and a new Apple TV.

The Company manages its business primarily on a geographic basis with reportable segments of Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan and Rest of Asia Pacific. In 2015, direct distribution channels accounted for 26% of net sales and indirect channels 74%, while domestic and international sales represented 35% and 65%, respectively. Substantially all hardware products are manufactured by outsourcing partners located primarily in Asia. The Company had approximately 110,000 full-time equivalent employees, and R&D expense was $8.1 billion in 2015.

Risk factors cited include global economic conditions, intense competition, reliance on single or limited-source components and outsourcing partners, dependence on resellers, legal proceedings, international operations, IT system failures, data security, key personnel and stock price volatility. The report also describes the Apple eBooks antitrust litigation, in which the District Court found the Company conspired to restrain trade in violation of the Sherman Act; the Company appealed. The Company paid $11.4 billion in dividends in 2015 and repurchased approximately 131.8 million shares in the three months ended September 26, 2015.

The retail apparel sector has declined about 20% over the past 52 weeks due to e-commerce threats, store overexpansion, and trade policy uncertainty (TPP withdrawal, NAFTA renegotiation, Brexit). The author argues Francesca's Holdings Corp. (FRAN) is positioned to survive and strengthen. FRAN, with $488 million in sales and a $320 million market cap, holds $48 million in cash, carries no debt, and generates ~$57.6 million in free cash flow. It operates 670+ stores in 48 states, targeting women aged 18-35, and plans to reach 900 stores. Q1 FY17 sales rose 1% to $107.7 million, though comparable sales fell 5% and net income declined to $4.3 million from $7.1 million. FY18 guidance projects sales of $518-537 million and EPS of $1.07-1.17. The company shows strong liquidity ratios, a low P/E of 8.4, solid profitability, and share buybacks. The author projects share prices of $14.50-$17.00 within 1-3 years and $27.00-$29.00 within 3-5 years, while disclosing no positions in the stock.

This passage describes a Bengali transliteration system mapping Bengali numerals and symbols to English equivalents. A tilde (~) removes the previously typed Bengali character before typing a symbol; special symbols are typed with a trailing ~. English punctuation translates to itself. ZWJ (^) produces half-formed consonants and separates vowel pairs, while ZWNJ (^^) produces dead consonants.

U.S. stocks made modest moves near record highs Thursday as oil prices fell after Israel and Hamas agreed to a rare truce, pausing fighting in Gaza so remaining hostages can be freed in exchange for Palestinian prisoners. The S&P 500 rose 0.1%, while gold held near its record at $4,054.50 per ounce. U.S. benchmark crude dipped to $62.34 per barrel and Brent crude to $66.07. PepsiCo shares edged up after adjusted earnings beat forecasts despite an 11% drop in net income. Delta Air Lines topped profit expectations, lifting other airline stocks. Novo Nordisk announced a $4.7 billion acquisition of Akero Therapeutics. European shares were mixed, while most Asian stocks rose, with Japan's Nikkei 225 up 1.8%.

Callinex Mines Inc. has filed an independent technical report for a Preliminary Economic Assessment (PEA) on SEDAR for its 100% owned Nash Creek and Superjack Projects in New Brunswick's Bathurst Mining District. The 2018 PEA outlines a 10-year, 3,900 tpd open-pit operation with a Dense Media Separation plant and 1,950 tpd flotation facility at Nash Creek, generating a pre-tax IRR of 34.1% (25.2% post-tax) and pre-tax NPV8% of C$230 million (C$128 million post-tax), based on C$168 million in pre-production capital costs and a zinc price of US$1.25/lb. The deposit is located near Highway 11, a 230 Kv transmission line, and 25 km from Glencore's Brunswick Smelter at the Port of Belledune. A drill program will begin within 10 days to identify potential satellite deposits. The PEA is preliminary, includes Inferred Mineral Resources, and carries no certainty of realization.

This study conducted a multi-ancestry transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) using the METRO method to identify genes associated with general cognitive function, white matter hyperintensity (WMH), and Alzheimer's disease (AD). Using genotype and gene expression data from 1,032 African American (AA) and 801 European American (EA) participants from the Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA), combined with GWAS summary statistics, the researchers identified 602 genes associated with general cognitive function, 45 with WMH, 231 with AD (EA GWAS), and 9 with AD (AA GWAS). After FOCUS fine-mapping, 266, 23, 69, and 2 genes remained in the 90%-credible sets, respectively. ICA1L was the only gene overlapping between WMH and AD after fine-mapping, suggesting it may contribute to overlapping AD and vascular dementia neuropathology. TOMM40 overlapped between AD TWAS from EA and AA GWAS. Identified genes were enriched for pathways involving innate immunity, vascular dysfunction, neuroinflammation, amyloid-beta clearance, and protein binding. Many identified genes were not previously reported in the original SNP-based GWAS. The study noted limitations including the use of B-lymphocyte gene expression rather than brain tissue and insufficient power in the AA AD GWAS. This is the first TWAS using expression mapping studies in multiple ancestries to identify genes associated with cognitive function and neurocognitive disorders, potentially identifying targets for pharmaceutical or preventative treatment for dementia.

Private college presidents' pay rose in 2015, with 58 earning over $1 million, up from 39 in 2014, and average compensation up 9% to $570,000, per a Chronicle of Higher Education survey. Average American worker pay rose 3-4% annually. Ohio's highest-paid was Daniel Curran ($2.4 million, No. 8); Barbara Snyder, Grant Cornwell, and Marvin Krislov ranked in the top 100.

Not all offsites need breakthroughs; many focus on aligning, communicating, coordinating, or celebrating. For breakthroughs, create a disruptive environment that fosters connections, center on a meaningful shared purpose, organize people and programs accordingly, drive deeper connections, and ensure practical actions with follow-through and measurement. Yarrow Kraner's HATCH experiences apply these principles through five BRAVE questions: Environment (disruptive settings like the Panamanian jungle), Values (a shared purpose to better the world), and Attitude (curating diverse people and creativity-sparking programs).

Tesla, Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2022 reports total revenues of $18.76 billion, up from $10.39 billion in the prior-year quarter, and net income attributable to common stockholders of $3.32 billion versus $438 million. Total assets were $66.04 billion as of March 31, 2022. The company operates two reportable segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. Management cites ongoing COVID-19 impacts, supply chain constraints, semiconductor shortages, and inflation affecting costs and product pricing. The 2.375% Convertible Senior Notes due 2022 were fully settled in the first quarter, and $380 million of Solar Asset and Loan-backed Notes were early repaid. Digital assets had a carrying value of $1.26 billion and a fair market value of $1.96 billion. Under the 2018 CEO Performance Award, three operational milestones were achieved in the quarter, with $48 million of related stock-based compensation expense recognized. Legal matters include the SolarCity acquisition litigation (decision expected mid-2022), litigation over the 2018 CEO Performance Award (trial set for October 2022), a going-private securities class action (trial set for January 2023), a JP Morgan lawsuit over stock warrant adjustments, and race discrimination matters, including Diaz v. Tesla, where damages were reduced to $15 million. Tesla also consolidates certain solar financing funds as variable interest entities for which it is the primary beneficiary.

This passage is an email dated June 7, 2001, from Ann M. Schmidt (ann.schmidt@enron.com) with the subject "Enron Mentions," containing a compilation of news articles about Enron Corp.

Key items include:

- **Chicago power deal**: Enron and Exelon's Commonwealth Edison signed an agreement to supply power to Chicago and 47 suburban communities, the largest such deal since Illinois deregulated its electricity industry in 1997. Enron will provide 60% of the 400 megawatts contracted annually; terms were not disclosed.
- **Dabhol dispute (India)**: Lenders to Enron's Indian unit, Dabhol Power Co., met in Singapore for three days over the future of the $2.9–3 billion project, which is in dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB) over unpaid bills (about $48 million). The meeting ended "positively," though earlier talks deadlocked and IDBI Executive Director R.S. Agarwal left early without explanation. DPC proposed suspending construction of Phase Two (1,444 MW, over 90% complete) for about a year; lenders asked Stone & Webster to assess the proposal. Completing Phase Two would require roughly $500 million, with $30–40 million owed to contractors. Indian Prime Minister Vajpayee expressed confidence the dispute would be resolved soon. Dabhol also plans to challenge in court a regulator's order barring it from seeking international arbitration until June 14, and DPC claims its power purchase agreement with MSEB remains in force.
- **Other Enron news**: Enron Broadband participated in a $30 million venture investment in Massachusetts tech firm AP Engines; Enron Power Operations pre-let additional office space at 21 Grosvenor Place, London; Chicago Mayor Daley proposed purchasing 60% of electricity for city buildings from Enron, saving about $3 million on the city's $50 million annual bill; and California regulators were considering suspending direct access to alternative power suppliers, a component Enron has been lobbying for.
- **Peripheral mentions**: Enron is cited as a member of a coalition opposing Bush's steel import investigation, as a windmill owner Pacific Hydro aspires to rival, in a commentary referencing California's attorney general's remark about Enron chairman Kenneth Lay, and in an article on India's foreign investment climate describing its $3 billion Maharashtra plant as the largest foreign investment in India.

This study examines how the interval between SARS-CoV-2 vaccination and natural infection affects hybrid immunity. Using two cohorts—10 previously infected individuals plus 20 infection-naive vaccinated controls (longitudinal), and 23 with prior infection, 23 with breakthrough infections, and 20 vaccine-only controls (cross-sectional)—researchers measured antibody levels via ELISA and neutralizing titers via live-virus assays against WA1 and variants Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, and Omicron BA.1/BA.2.

Hybrid immunity produced significantly higher antibody levels (3.1–3.7 fold) and neutralizing titers (8.4–22.7 fold) than vaccination alone, with the largest gains against vaccine-resistant variants (Beta, Omicron). Cross-neutralization was greater for all variants except Delta, and the neutralizing potency index improved 2.7–7.2 fold.

Exposure intervals ranged from 35 to 404 days. Longer intervals correlated strongly with higher neutralizing titers and antibody levels, with titers against Omicron BA.1 increasing 17.6-fold by day 400. Cross-neutralization also improved with longer intervals, while potency index did not. These trends held for both infection-before-vaccination and breakthrough infection groups.

The authors conclude that the primary immune response continues developing for over a year between exposures, and that longer intervals yield stronger, broader hybrid immunity. They emphasize that these findings support increased vaccine access rather than intentional infection, and suggest delayed vaccination still provides substantial benefit.

Chiefs defensive tackle Chris Jones addressed his lack of pursuit on Trevor Lawrence's game-winning touchdown run in the Chiefs' loss to the Jaguars, calling it a teaching point and saying he thought the play was over when Lawrence stumbled and got up to score. Jones said the incident won't happen again. He also clarified that his X and Instagram accounts were deactivated before the game, not in response to criticism. The Chiefs next face the Lions on Sunday night, and Jones said he is focused on helping slow the NFL's top-scoring offense.

DPI (UK), a Castle Donington-based maker of aluminium frames and lightboxes, has received a £12,200 grant from Collaborate, an ERDF-funded scheme overseen by Leicester City Council. The money will fund a new automated saw, enabling the firm to produce larger structures in-house, cut contract times, and create new jobs. Founded three years ago, the company grew 37 per cent last year. Collaborate offers grants of £5,000 to £25,000, covering a third of capital project costs, from a £1.2 million pot.

This is the opening lecture of MIT Sloan's 15.401 Finance Theory course, taught by Andrew W. Lo for first-year MBA students. Lo argues that finance—defined as mathematics plus money—is central to all business decisions, illustrating with three successful figures: hedge fund manager James Simons, investor Warren Buffett, and former GE CEO Jack Welch, who share an innate understanding of finance despite different backgrounds. The course focuses on four components of the financial system: households, financial intermediaries, non-financial corporations, and capital markets. The two fundamental challenges of financial analysis are valuing assets and managing them, with time and risk being the factors that distinguish finance from other disciplines. Lo demonstrates price discovery through a live auction of a mystery box, which sold for $45 and contained an iPod Nano worth $149. The analytical framework begins with accounting—balance sheets measuring stocks of wealth and income statements measuring flows. He presents six principles of finance, including that there is no systematic free lunch, individuals prefer more money, money now, and less risk, and agents act in self-interest. Course requirements include readings from Brealey, Myers, and Allen; a case study (10%), participation (10%), midterm (25%), and cumulative final (55%), with most exam questions drawn from a provided problem package. Lo encourages students to apply concepts personally and attend a "Practice of Finance" pro-seminar.

President Trump's description of the House-passed health care bill as "mean" frustrated conservatives like Rep. Dave Brat, whom Trump had pressured to support it, despite Trump previously calling the bill "a great plan." Meanwhile, Senate Republican efforts to draft their own version have been slowed by disagreements between conservatives and moderates over Medicaid expansion, coverage requirements, and subsidies. Trump wants the Senate bill to be "more generous," and Sen. John Cornyn said passage could come by the end of July.

ARDD issued a report commending Jordan's legal response to the Syrian refugee crisis, presented at the third International Conference for Refugees in the Middle East at Yarmouk University. It praised governmental agencies partnering with UNHCR for rapid support and noted that internationally recognised legal sections at camps offer specialised services such as juvenile courts and family protection. Challenges remain, including access to the formal labour market, pressure on services, and lack of financial resources. A recent registration campaign has yielded 25,000 newly registered refugees.

Despite risks, the government may still meet its 3.3 percent fiscal deficit target for the year ending March 2019, according to Moody's, which said capital spending cuts could offset potential slippage. A Moody's-ICRA poll in Singapore and Mumbai found most respondents expected fiscal slippage, viewed rising crude oil prices as a major economic risk, and considered the PSB recapitalisation package insufficient.

This patent application describes a system for responding to database queries by executing differentially private versions of those queries on private databases. A hardware database privacy device, communicatively coupled to a private database system, receives a query request from a client device, identifies a level of differential privacy corresponding to the request (including a privacy parameter indicating the degree of information released), identifies the relevant set of data and operations, modifies the operations based on the identified privacy level, performs the modified operations to produce a differentially private result set, and provides that result set to the client for display.

The background notes that sensitive information such as health data, financial records, telecom data, and confidential business intelligence is underutilized because existing privacy methods—access controls, data masking, hashing, anonymization, aggregation, and tokenization—are invasive, resource intensive, compromise analytical utility, or fail to ensure privacy.

The differentially private security system comprises a user interface, a library, an account management system (which validates query commands and manages client privacy budgets), a query handling engine, a database integrator, and a privacy system. Clients specify privacy parameters (ε, δ) with each query, and the system balances information release against the privacy protection required by the entities managing the databases.

The privacy system includes engines for differentially private count, median, mean, variance, and interquartile range queries; batch and stochastic gradient descent for general linear models; random forest classification (perturbing leaf-node proportions); histograms (via count perturbation or private wavelet decomposition); model testing (generating perturbed confusion matrices across cutoff thresholds); synthetic database generation (projecting data while preserving spatial relationships); and validation of whether queries satisfy (ε, δ)-differential privacy. Differential privacy is defined so that query outputs cannot distinguish between neighboring data objects differing by at most one entry.

High-tech sensors revealed that greater noctule bats snatch songbirds out of the sky.

TyreWatch, a predictive tyre management system, was launched on 16th May at the Harwell Innovation and Science Campus in Oxfordshire. Developed by the Pathway to Autonomous Commercial Vehicles consortium with £1.2 million of Innovate UK funding, it uses wheel-rim sensors to monitor tyre pressure and temperature, transmitting data via cellular and satellite communications to a central server. The server analyses data against vehicle-specific baselines, issuing maintenance or critical alerts with AI-recommended corrective actions. Under testing, it prevented 95% of tyre-related breakdowns, reducing fuel consumption, tyre wear, downtime and improving road safety. Built on open architecture, it is offered as software-as-a-service or a complete retrofit solution.

The "Horns" or double mid screen alignment is an effective way to isolate a star ballhandler against a Box & One defense, allowing the star to go right or left past the screens and drive to create an outnumbered situation. If driving is unavailable, the star can feed the rolling screener or kick out to corner shooters. Against ballside post help, a drop pass to a cutter produces an easy layup. In screen-and-pop variations, one screener pops while the other rolls. If no shot develops, Single/Double screen action can be initiated with a reversal pass. Success depends on execution, coordination, non-verbal communication, timing, and scouting opponents to attack their weakest defenders.

Japanese government bonds firmed on Friday after a two-year auction drew strong demand, with a bid-to-cover ratio of 5.51 times versus the previous 3.82. The 10-year yield held steady at 0.015 percent while other yields declined. Investors awaited the Bank of Japan's May bond-purchase details. BOJ officials attach less importance to purchase guidance, though some worry removing it could signal tapering. Governor Kuroda said the main policy target is interest rates. The BOJ kept policy unchanged and offered its most optimistic economic assessment in nine years. Core consumer prices rose slower than expected in March but increased for a third straight month.

J&K Deputy CM Nirmal Singh said the government is considering introducing skill development courses in educational institutions. Interacting with students of two women's colleges, he appreciated their vocational projects and said colleges should upgrade technical skills to foster entrepreneurship.

A former Washington Walmart employee, fired for allegedly trying to steal a safe, returned days later to retrieve it. Loss prevention staff found heroin and Xanax inside. The 24-year-old admitted the drugs were his and was booked into Pierce County Jail for unlawful possession of a controlled substance.

In this address to Congress, the President gives thanks for national blessings, including abundant harvests, peace, and civil and religious liberty. He reviews foreign relations: a war between Russia and the Ottoman Empire, unchanged but mutually beneficial relations with France (with indemnity claims still unadjusted), submission of the northeastern boundary dispute with Great Britain to the King of the Netherlands as umpire, altered commercial relations with Britain due to its revived colonial exclusion system, a treaty prepared with Austria, and progress in settling indemnity claims against Denmark. The Treasury's condition is favorable, with receipts of about $24 million and over $12 million applied to the public debt, leaving $58,362,135.78 due on 1829-01-01. European harvest failures have opened grain markets to American exports, and revenue for 1829 is expected to equal or exceed 1828's, permitting $10 million more debt extinguishment. He defends the tariff as protection for native industry against restrictive British legislation, while urging revision of provisions that burden one section of the union to relieve another.

He warns against state resistance to federal laws and recommends the Secretary of War's proposals regarding relations with Indian tribes. He reports progress on fortifications, surveys, canals, and the West Point Academy; naval improvements, suppression of piracy, and a nearly ready Pacific exploring expedition; Post Office growth to nearly 8,000 offices; completion of a penitentiary; awards of over $1.19 million under the Treaty of Ghent claims; land revenue of nearly $2 million; and the need for early legislation for the fifth census, with suggested improvements to its conduct.

This study examined adrenal vessels in 30 adrenalectomy specimens (2018–September 2022) with and without neoplasms. Normal adult adrenal central veins showed asymmetrical longitudinal smooth muscle bundles morphologically indistinguishable from fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) of renal or carotid arteries; these features were confined to adrenal tissue and absent in 9 fetal adrenals (15–37 gestational weeks). Adrenal cortical adenomas displayed hyalinized arterial walls with CD68-positive macrophages, intimal fibroplasia, and myxoid/fibrinoid medial degeneration consistent with segmental arterial mediolysis (SAM), resembling acute atherosis of preeclampsia. Pheochromocytomas showed thin-walled arteries, blood lakes, and degenerative changes, with normal muscular arteries infrequent in both tumor types. Hemorrhage and vascular thrombosis were the most common complications, and no FMD-like lesions occurred in arteries outside the adrenal gland. The findings support unifying FMD and SAM as a single spectrum and suggest shared pathogenic mechanisms involving adrenal hormones or hormone receptor abnormalities, potentially linking adrenal vein morphology, FMD, SAM, atherosis, and Moyamoya disease.

Donna Adelson, 75, was sentenced Monday to life in prison plus 30 years for conspiracy and solicitation for her role in the 2014 murder of Florida State University law professor Dan Markel, her former son-in-law. She told the judge she was innocent and that no evidence tied her to the crime. Judge Stephen Everett warned he could consider her "utter lack of remorse." Prosecutors said she plotted with her son Charlie Adelson, who used Katherine Magbanua to hire two hit men, allegedly so Wendi Adelson could move to South Florida with her children.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC dated October 26, 2021. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer.

Two pieces of ammunition found in a Litchfield High School bathroom Wednesday prompted a lockdown of the high school and middle school, with students dismissed to parents around 10:00 a.m. as police responded.

HPC architectures have evolved to include traditional custom systems, prebuilt standard systems, and cloud products. IDC expects the public cloud to become the most important HPC architecture for manufacturing enterprises using or planning HPC, followed by hybrid cloud architectures. IDC recommends a "make or buy" decision between in-house infrastructure and purchased HPC services, noting OPEX-based public cloud HPC may offer technical and financial advantages over CAPEX-based in-house infrastructure.

In-house HPC has limitations: increasing performance requires hardware renewal or cluster expansion with higher costs; custom environments have limited expansion options; and on-premises infrastructure offers restricted flexibility for new usage scenarios, hampering agility in development. Over half of HPC users consider optimization important for developing new solutions and products.

Improving security and resilience is important to over 80% of industrial HPC users. Where sensitive data requires on-premises infrastructure, IDC suggests hybrid architectures that analyze sensitive data in-house while addressing load peaks via public cloud.

Factors favoring HPCaaS include cost optimization (a major advantage for two-thirds of decision makers), support for global collaboration through scalable cloud-based workstations, and scalability as a basis for new business models—81% of HPC users intend to implement HPC-based business models. Additionally, 49% view HPCaaS as complete infrastructure outsourcing, 42% as HPC use without own infrastructure, and 52% consider fast access to cutting-edge methods and hardware a core innovation aspect. Cloud HPC still requires trained IT personnel.

The findings are based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 decision makers from industrial enterprises with over 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. IDC recommends establishing virtual development, creating a holistic data strategy, evaluating suitable HPC operating models, considering scalability, security, and energy efficiency, and leveraging external expertise.

The passage discusses baseball's trend, including the Yankees, of de-emphasizing starting pitching in favor of relievers and closers, exemplified by Aroldis Chapman's five-year closer contract. The Yankees have historically built strong bullpens, from the Torre era's Wetteland, Nelson, and Rivera tandem to the 2017 Betances-Chapman combination. The author questions whether starting pitchers earning $20-25 million justify their salaries when removed after roughly five innings, noting starters averaged only 87 pitches per start in 2015. John Smoltz argues pitchers should throw more, comparing muscles to exercise. Overuse of bullpens lengthens games, prompting the Commissioner to consider limits on reliever use.

A new study, led by Vicki Stover Hertzberg of Emory University and funded by Boeing, suggests passengers wanting to avoid colds or flu should sit in a window seat and not leave it. Researchers tested surfaces and air on 10 US flights but found no cold or flu viruses. Mathematical modeling estimated only about one passenger per 150-person flight would be infected by a hypothetical sick passenger in an aisle seat. The study found 38 percent of passengers never left their seats, with aisle passengers moving most often and window passengers least. The 11 people seated nearest a sick person face the highest risk. Outside experts said the small study limits general conclusions but called it novel research on a previously understudied topic.

The Supertrend Indicator is a trend-following tool created by trader Oliver Seban that signals trend direction, continuation, or reversals. It appears as a line on price charts—green when price is above it and red when price is below it—and reverses when the closing price crosses the previous period's indicator value. Its formula is based on the median price and the Average True Range (ATR), with Seban's default settings of 10 periods and a multiplier of 3. A backtest on the S&P 500 over 60 years using weekly bars showed a win rate of about 67%, a maximum drawdown of 24.6% (versus 56.24% for buy-and-hold), and acceptable risk-adjusted returns. The indicator is lagging, works best on instruments that trend and on weekly timeframes, can be combined with tools such as RSI, moving averages, and Bollinger Bands, and adapts dynamically to changing volatility, though it may produce false signals in choppy or ranging markets.

Nathan Calvin, general counsel of Encode—a three-person AI policy nonprofit—publicly accused OpenAI on X of using intimidation tactics, alleging the company used its lawsuit against Elon Musk as a pretext to target critics by implying they were secretly Musk-funded. Calvin and Encode were subpoenaed in August, with OpenAI requesting his private communications related to California's SB 53, an AI safety law signed at the end of September requiring frontier AI developers to publish safety frameworks, transparency reports, report safety incidents, and share catastrophic risk assessments. Tyler Johnston of The Midas Project said he received a similar subpoena. OpenAI chief strategy officer Jason Kwon said Encode's support of Musk and its not "fully disclosed" funding raised legitimate questions, calling subpoenas standard in litigation. Calvin alleged OpenAI sought to weaken SB 53 by urging California to treat companies as compliant if they had signed federal safety agreements. Encode refused to turn over documents, stating it is not Musk-funded. OpenAI's Justin Achaim and former board member Helen Toner expressed concern over the alleged tactics.

This State of the Union message reports that the country is at peace, national defense is effective, industrial conflict is low, and public health is at its highest recorded level, with mortality and infant mortality rates declining from 1928 to 1932. Private agencies, local authorities, and states have mobilized to provide winter relief, supplemented by Reconstruction Finance Corporation loans to states that exhausted their resources.

Despite the continuing worldwide depression, emergency measures and policies are credited with saving the country from economic disaster, and credit expansion through the Federal Reserve System and the Reconstruction Finance Corporation is described as invaluable. The President identifies three priorities for recovery: reducing government expenditures and balancing the Federal budget, reorganizing the banking system, and cooperating economically with other nations.

The proposed budget reduces appropriations by over $830 million, limits federal public works to existing commitments, continues the furlough system, and recommends a temporary 11 percent salary reduction for officials earning over $1,000. Abusive veterans' payments should be eliminated, and manufacturers' excise taxes should be extended to nearly all manufactures at a uniform rate. Executive orders will consolidate over fifty government agencies.

On banking, 4,665 banks have suspended since January 1930 with $3.3 billion in deposits, and reform is called a national necessity, excluding inflation or governmental conduct of banking. Internationally, the United States participates in the World Disarmament Conference and a proposed World Economic Conference, but does not approve suspension of December 15 war debt payments. The address concludes that government should act as a regulator, not a participant, in economic life, preserving the American system of individualism.

New research from Case Western Reserve University, published in The Journal of Family Violence, estimates the federal government spends about $55 billion annually on the effects of childhood exposure to domestic violence. The study links such exposure to higher health-care costs, higher crime rates, and lower productivity, totaling nearly $50,000 per person by age 64—including $11,042 in medical costs, $13,922 in crime-related costs, and $25,531 in productivity losses. An estimated 15.5 million U.S. children are exposed to intimate partner violence yearly. Researchers say the findings can help policymakers push for preventive and therapeutic interventions.

Plaintiffs, targets or subjects of an Eastern District of New York grand jury investigation concerning the issuance and trading of Pallet Management Systems, Inc. stock, sought an injunction barring NASD Regulation, Inc. from compelling them to testify under Rule 8210, punishing them for invoking their privileges against self-incrimination, and misusing grand jury materials, on the theory that Regulation was acting as an agent of federal prosecutors.

The court found that Regulation's Division of Enforcement (DOE) conducted an independent private investigation of Cromwell, while its Criminal Assistance Prosecution Unit (CPAG) assisted federal prosecutors, including in the Hanover Securities indictment (United States v. Cataggio) and a search of Cromwell's offices. Despite a policy of complete separation, the physical and administrative arrangements between CPAG and DOE provided no assurance of confidentiality. Nevertheless, all relevant Regulation personnel denied that the Rule 8210 demands resulted from government urging, and the court credited Regulation's evidence, finding the demands were the product of entirely independent DOE action.

Because Regulation is a private entity—except as to CPAG attorney Bettigole's conduct as a special assistant U.S. Attorney—the Fifth Amendment claim failed absent state action, which plaintiffs did not establish. The court also rejected plaintiffs' analogy to the substantial relationship test used in attorney disqualification cases.

On the Rule 6(e) claim, the court found no credible proof that grand jury materials were disclosed to or used by unauthorized Regulation personnel; documents shown to an employee during testimony were likely seized pursuant to a search warrant and were not "matters occurring before the grand jury."

Judgment was entered for the defendant, though the court noted that Regulation should give careful attention to the physical and administrative relationships between CPAG and DOE, since the existing arrangements left doubt sufficient to require a trial.

We Energies, a regulated monopoly, has been criticized for high rates and executive pay. Its rates are set by the Public Service Commission (PSC), which allows a return on assets exceeding 10%. Three decades ago, under CEO Charlie McNeer, the area had the Midwest's lowest electric rates. After his retirement, PSC appointments under Gov. Tommy Thompson created a compliant regulator that approved most utility requests, and rates rose to the Midwest's highest over 15 years due to power plant overbuilding and shareholder returns. The Citizens Utility Board and large businesses have pushed back, and a new group, the Initiative for Competitive Energy, advocates lower prices. We Energies proposed a rate freeze through 2019, but ICE and CUB argue a rate rollback is needed.

Canadian Blood Services is opening Canada's largest blood donation clinic at Eau Claire Market on July 10th, with 20 donation beds, replacing the current 18-bed clinic. The organization aims for 150,000 donations by July 1st for Canada's 150th birthday but needs 50,000 more, with O negative blood supplies critically low. A new operations facility off Barlow Trail opens in 2020; the current clinic closes July 7th.

Reigning champion F2 Logistics faces Generika-Ayala at 7 p.m. at The Arena in San Juan City, seeking a fourth straight win and the No. 2 seed in the 2018 Chooks to Go-PSL Grand Prix. Generika-Ayala, coming off its first win after four losses, is led by imports Darlene Ramdin and Symone Hayden. Earlier, Sta. Lucia (2-3) plays winless Smart.

Prince's music became available on Spotify after his death, despite his lifetime opposition. Other artists refusing Spotify include Taylor Swift, who pulled her 2014 album; Garth Brooks, absent from Spotify and iTunes; Thom Yorke, a critic despite Radiohead's presence on the service; Beyoncé, whose Lemonade is exclusive to Jay Z's Tidal; and Joanna Newsom, who called Spotify a "villainous cabal of major labels."

Market Research Future has published a report on the global Blowout Preventer market, forecast to grow significantly by 2021. The market is segmented by type (Annular BOP and RAM), well type (land and offshore), and region. Growth is driven by rising oil and gas demand, increased offshore exploration, and higher safety standards. The Middle East is expected to dominate due to onshore drilling, while Asia-Pacific shows high growth due to hydrocarbon potential. Key players include Aker Solutions, Weatherford International, FMC Technologies, Cameron International, National Oil Well Verco, Proserve, and Uztel Ltd. This document is the SD Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00. It states that implementations incorporating SD Specifications versions 1.0 or 1.01 require appropriate licenses from SD-3C, LLC, such as the SD Host Ancillary License Agreement or the SD Memory Card License Agreement. The Simplified Specification is a subset of the complete SD Specification owned by the SD Card Association, provided on a non-confidential, "AS-IS" basis without warranties, and implementation may require a license.

The SD Memory Card is designed for audio and video consumer electronic devices, featuring a content protection mechanism compliant with SDMI security standards, using mutual authentication and a cipher algorithm. The SDIO Card, defined in a separate specification, provides I/O functionality and is compatible with the SD Memory Card.

Communication uses a 9-pin interface operating at up to 208 MHz. Cards are classified by capacity: SDSC (up to 2 GB), SDHC (over 2 GB up to 32 GB), and SDXC (over 32 GB up to 2 TB). Bus speed modes range from Default Speed (up to 12.5 MB/sec) and High Speed (25 MB/sec) to UHS-I modes (up to 104 MB/sec) and UHS-II modes (up to 624 MB/s in FD624 mode). Five Speed Classes define minimum card performance.

The specification covers system concepts, SD and SPI bus protocols, card registers, ROM cards, UHS-I/UHS-II operation, card initialization and identification, data transfer modes, commands, responses, speed class specifications, and features such as Cache, Self Maintenance, and Command Queue. All communication is host-controlled via broadcast and addressed commands, with two operation modes: card identification mode and data transfer mode.

Lake Lugano, a glacial lake in Switzerland's Italian-speaking canton of Ticino, lies about 40 kilometers west of Lake Como and remains a quieter, lesser-known alternative to its crowded neighbor. Straddling the Swiss-Italian border, the region offers a mild, sunny climate, palm-lined promenades, cobbled streets, and a relaxed pace. Visitors can explore villages such as Gandria, Morcote, and Bré, take a funicular up Monte San Salvatore, hike Monte Generoso, visit parks and art museums, sample Ticino merlot, and dine at lakeside restaurants. Experts recommend using local ferries and slowing down to enjoy small moments, as the area still draws far fewer tourists than Lake Como.

Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and Public Safety Minister Ralph Goodale expressed sorrow, but not panic, after a deadly van attack in Toronto. Trudeau said there is no apparent link to terrorism or national security element, offered condolences to victims, and praised first responders. Goodale, in Toronto for a G7 meeting, described a large homicide investigation led by city police and thanked other countries, especially the United States, for condolences and offers of help. Police arrested 25-year-old Alek Minassian, who is due in court Tuesday.

European stock markets rose slightly on Tuesday, with the energy sector lifted by rising oil prices ahead of central bank rate decisions. Brent crude hit a more than two-year high after the Forties pipeline was shut down over a leak. Focus is on Fed, Bank of England and ECB meetings.

Outgoing Federal Reserve chair Janet Yellen said Wall Street's recent gains do not constitute a "bubble" but advised investors to stay cautious and diversify. She described the US economy as strong, citing rising wages and low unemployment. Yellen, the first woman to lead the Fed, admitted disappointment at not being renewed for a second term; Jerome Powell replaces her Monday.

In Hogg's Estate (December 4, 1936), the majority (Bok, J.) upheld the auditing judge's ruling that the word "grandchildren" in the testator's 1855 will includes all grandchildren, including those of afterborn children. The court held that positive language controls over rules of construction and probability arguments, citing Robison's Estate, Luce v. Harris, and Ludwick's Estate, and found that "per stirpes" determines shares without discriminating among ancestors. The exceptions were dismissed and the account confirmed absolutely. In dissent, Steakne, J. (joined by Sinkler, J.) argued that the testator intended only the issue of his four named children to take, that the will was revoked pro tanto as to three afterborn children who received full shares by operation of law, and that the majority's result produces an unjust distribution; he would sustain the exceptions.

The passage consists mainly of a list of financial news headlines, accompanied by one full article profiling Dunas Capital Asset Management. Supervised by the CNMV and the DGSFP, it manages portfolios for financial institutions and third parties through traditional and alternative investments across financial and real estate markets. Its philosophy centers on capital preservation via an absolute return, value-investing approach, with flexibility across asset classes and no restrictions by sector, country, rating, or asset type. Risk is managed through volatility-based "risk budgets," and options and futures are used to mitigate tail risk.
