Its alternative investments cover infrastructure, renewable energies, transportation assets, and agriculture from a sustainability perspective. The firm operates on six founding principles—independence, transparency, flexibility, innovation, experience, and sustainability—with all capital held by independent partners and a team of more than 80 professionals. The passage concludes with a brief description of Pan Finance, a global financial intelligence publication with over 200,000 readers across 150 countries.

The tax department is likely to use the net asset value method to calculate the fair market value of unlisted shares for computing capital gains tax on transfers, instead of the subjective DCF method, to target undervalued property sales through company structures. This budget proposal was seen as a dampener for unlisted companies, especially start-ups.

The Dogs of the Dow (DOD) is a stock-picking strategy that invests equal dollar amounts in the 10 highest dividend-yielding stocks among the 30 DJIA components, rebalanced annually. Popularized by Michael B. O'Higgins' 1991 book "Beating the Dow," the concept traces back to a 1951 article by H.G. Schneider. Investors can implement it through individual stocks, ETFs, or mutual funds. While the strategy outperformed before being revealed, backtests show it has underperformed the S&P 500 over the last couple of decades: a $10,000 investment grew to $32,000 for DOD versus $60,000 for the S&P 500 (CAGR of 5% versus 7.7%). A second backtest of related ETFs (SDOG, IDOG, EDOG) also showed underperformance against the broad market. The article concludes that despite its simplicity, the strategy should only be a small part of one's assets due to poor diversification.

This passage contains AMD's SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) Specification, comprising copyright notices, a legal specification agreement, and technical documentation.

The specification agreement permits use of the Specification only as a reference for designing products to interface with AMD products and for providing feedback to AMD. It disclaims all warranties and liability, grants no intellectual property rights, requires compliance with U.S. and European export laws, and is governed by California law with disputes litigated in Santa Clara County.

Technically, SEV-ES and SEV-SNP protect guest register state from the hypervisor by encrypting it during world switches. VMEXITs are classified as Automatic Exits (AEs) or Non-Automatic Exits (NAEs); NAEs trigger a #VC exception, and the guest selectively shares register state with the hypervisor through the GHCB, a 4KB decrypted page whose format mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save state area. The document's purpose is to standardize the GHCB memory area, required NAE events, and minimum guest state so a guest OS can interoperate with any supporting hypervisor.

Version 2 introduces hypervisor feature advertisement via a 52-bit FEATURES bitmap delivered through the GHCB MSR protocol (MSR 0xc001_0130), which also handles protocol negotiation, CPUID requests, AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration (required for SEV-SNP), page state changes, and termination requests. Revisions 2.01 through 2.04 add 64-bit guest request sequence numbers, a VLEK certificate GUID, APIC ID list retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, Page State Change support for SEV-ES, the SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob EFI Protocol, SEV-TIO trusted IO, and Secure AVIC backing page support.

Defined NAE events include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO access, Page State Change, SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request (certificate return), SNP AP Creation, #HV doorbell, IPI, and timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Request, Secure AVIC, and Termination Request. The document also covers SNP Restricted Injection, SMP booting via AP Reset Hold or SNP AP Creation (which enables vCPU hotplug), AP Jump Table handling, NMI handling via #DB interception and "NMI Complete" messages, debug register virtualization, and states that SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

Former Katsina State Governor Ibrahim Shehu Shema was remanded in EFCC custody by Justice Babagana Ashigar of the Federal High Court, Katsina, over alleged money laundering of N5.7bn SURE-P funds. He pleaded not guilty to 26 counts. His written bail application will be heard on April 27, 2018.

This passage is an email (subject: "IEP News 6/26/2001") from Jean Munoz distributing news articles from June 26, 2001, covering California's energy crisis.

Key points from the articles:

- **Refund settlement talks**: A federally ordered settlement conference began in Washington, D.C., led by FERC Chief Judge Curtis Wagner, with about 150 participants in up to 15 days of confidential talks. California demands $8.9 billion in refunds for alleged generator overcharges since May 2000, while generators dispute the figure and claim utilities owe them billions. Wagner indicated he doubted refunds would exceed roughly $2–2.5 billion. If no deal is reached by July 10, Wagner will recommend a solution to FERC's five commissioners. Other Western states may seek up to $6 billion in refunds.

- **FERC commissioners visit Sacramento**: New FERC commissioners Pat Wood and Nora Brownell met with Gov. Gray Davis to discuss natural gas prices, refunds, and allegations against Duke Energy. Davis softened his rhetoric toward federal regulators.

- **Duke Energy allegations**: Three former employees of Duke's Chula Vista plant testified that Duke discarded spare parts and reduced output during shortages to influence prices. Davis praised them as "heroes"; Duke called the accusations "baseless," saying its actions followed ISO directives.

- **Direct access program**: State officials moved to suspend customer choice of electricity providers, fearing customer flight would jeopardize repayment of nearly $50 billion in power purchases and a planned $13.4 billion bond sale. The PUC was poised to vote on suspension by July 1.

- **Solar housing**: A San Diego County subdivision by Shea Homes is among California's first solar developments, aided by falling panel costs, subsidies, and high electricity prices.

- **New power plants**: 42 plants are pending before the California Energy Commission, but uncertainty remains over whether all will be built and what prices they will charge; some developers have paused projects citing the state's political climate.

The passage describes COVIDFast, an RNA extraction-free RT-qPCR assay for rapid, high-throughput SARS-CoV-2 detection, comprising SwabFAST (anterior nares swab) and SalivaFAST (saliva). Conventional PCR methods require an initial RNA extraction step that is laborious, expensive, and prone to contamination and human error. COVIDFast addresses this using optimized buffers—a viral transport buffer (VTB) for swabs and a TCEP-based buffer for saliva—enabling direct-to-PCR testing. The assay uses standardized 2 mL barcoded cryovials with screw caps for both sample types, facilitating automation and high-throughput processing. Analytical validation showed extraction-free results comparable to extraction-based methods, with a limit of detection of 4 copies/µL for both specimen types. Clinical validation against extraction-based testing showed 100% positive and negative percent agreement for swab samples and 98.8%/99.4% for saliva samples. Compared to SalivaDirect, SwabFAST showed 83.3% PPV and 99.4% NPV, while SalivaFAST showed 95% PPV and 100% NPV. Since launch, 409,883 tests were performed by December 23, 2021, with an overall positive rate of 8.10%. The authors report 24-hour turnaround times at volumes exceeding 5,000 tests/day and suggest the platform could be extended to other pathogens.

The S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller U.S. National Home Price NSA Index reported a 6.3% annual gain in February, up from 6.1% the prior month, while the 10-City and 20-City Composites rose 6.5% and 6.8% year-over-year, respectively. Seattle led the 20 cities with a 12.7% annual increase, followed by Las Vegas (11.6%) and San Francisco (10.1%). Thirteen of 20 cities reported greater annual gains than in the year ending January 2018. Month-over-month, the National Index rose 0.4% before and 0.5% after seasonal adjustment, with all 20 cities posting increases. David M. Blitzer noted national prices have risen for 70 consecutive months since May 2012, averaging 6% annually, and that rising employment is expected to support continued price growth.

FULE logically erases the entire user area, identified via CMD32 (argument 0) and CMD33, then CMD38 (argument 00000002h). Hosts must verify FULE_SUPPORT (b312); unsupported cards execute ERASE. Out-of-sequence commands set error bits and reset the sequence. FULE is limited to SDHC/SDXC, not SPI, with progress shown by DAT0 held low.

Coach Quenneville discusses his team's experience in big games and the excitement of some players being at home for the first time, emphasizing focus and preparation while aiming to improve on the previous game. He describes the long process of returning after a game-seven overtime loss in a conference final, the battle through a tough division, and the challenging Anaheim series, calling the team resilient. He praises Hossa as a consistent, complete player whose contributions may be overshadowed by other top players. He credits Stan for revamping the team, notes deadline acquisitions, and highlights the core group's leadership. He stresses keeping the same approach, not getting ahead of himself, and focusing on the task at hand. He discusses growing with experience while maintaining a team-first approach, praises Kimmo's dependability, addresses handling healthy scratches and the team's depth, notes the need for quicker play against strong forechecking, and points to depth players like Steeger and Vermy stepping up in key moments.

In Betteys v. Ætna Life Insurance Co. (Mich. 1923), the beneficiary of an accident policy sued for the death benefit and weekly disability indemnity after Dr. William H. Betteys died, allegedly from an infection following a hand injury caused by a slipping wrench. The insurer initially sent proof-of-death blanks, then recalled them and denied liability for the death benefit on the ground that death resulted from disease, while offering to consider a claim for weekly disability indemnity if proof was made. The court held that letters from the insurer and its agents were admissible on the question of waiver of proof of death, and that the denial of liability excused the plaintiff from making such proof. However, the insurer was not estopped from invoking the policy's contractual time limit for bringing suit on the death benefit, since waiver of the proof requirement did not waive the limitation period. Because suit was not brought within the stipulated time, the judgment for the plaintiff was reversed as to the death benefit, and a new trial was granted on the weekly indemnity claim.

The preliminary inquiry into the murder of Phyllis Caesar and Constance Fraser, found bound and gagged in their South Road home, continued before Magistrate Judy Latchman. Three police ranks and a former corporal on remand for murder testified. Imran Khan, Steven Andrews, and Phillip Suffrien are charged with killing the women during a 2017 robbery. The PI continues Monday.

Austria's Financial Market Authority raised its forecast for proceeds from winding down bad bank Heta Asset Resolution to 8.6 billion euros, up 2.6 billion, citing better-than-expected asset sales. The revision benefits Austria, which loaned Carinthia money for a Heta bond buyback. An initial 4 billion euro payment to creditors is expected soon.

This paper proposes a hybrid deep learning framework, DNN-Transformer-AE, for corporate tax risk supervision and risk-level assessment, addressing limitations of traditional manual and rule-based approaches that struggle with large-scale data and concealed risk patterns. The framework combines three modules: a Deep Neural Network (DNN) for static enterprise attributes, a Transformer for temporal financial data, and an Autoencoder (AE) for anomaly detection via reconstruction error. Outputs are fused and mapped to a risk score, categorized as high, medium, or low risk.

The model was evaluated on a dataset of approximately 12,000 enterprises from real tax declarations, covering static features, time-series features, and expert-assigned risk labels. The DNN-Transformer-AE outperformed baselines including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and DNN-LSTM, achieving 0.91 accuracy, 0.86 recall, and 0.88 F1-score. Training and validation loss curves converged at approximately 40 epochs, indicating stable generalization.

The authors note limitations, including the exclusion of macroeconomic conditions and inter-firm relationships, and computational complexity; future work may focus on incorporating broader data and developing interpretable, lightweight models.

This passage, from the SD Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00, describes SD memory card operational features. A tuning block (CMD19) tunes sampling points for hosts, mandatory for HOST-SDR-VD and optional for HOST-SDR-FD; the card completes up to 40 CMD19 executions within 150ms. In Data Transfer Mode, the host operates at fPP frequency, uses CMD9 to obtain the CSD, CMD4 (SET_DSR) to configure driver stages, and CMD7 to select one card into the Transfer State. All data read and write commands can be aborted by CMD12; block write buffering is supported, while write CSD, write protection, and erase operations have no buffering. Block reads (CMD17/CMD18) and writes (CMD24/CMD25) are CRC-protected; ACMD23 enables pre-erase for faster multiple block writes, and ACMD22 reports the number of well-written blocks. Erase uses CMD32/CMD33/CMD38, with Discard (250ms busy timeout) and FULE (1 second busy timeout) variants supported only for SDHC/SDXC cards and not via SPI.

Write protection methods include a mechanical switch, card-internal protection, and password-based lock/unlock via CMD42 using 128-bit PWD and 8-bit PWD_LEN registers. The optional Card Ownership Protection (COP) feature adds Force Erase Password (FEP) registers and COP Unlock (CMD42[1Fh]); if FEP is set, the card locks after power-on until COP Unlock is performed. Locked cards accept only limited commands and reject ACMD6. Application-specific commands are invoked via CMD55 (APP_CMD). The switch function command (CMD6) supports multiple function groups—access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit—with mode 0 (check) and mode 1 (set) operations returning 512 bits of status; the default Power Limit is 0.72W. High-Speed mode (25 MB/sec at 50 MHz) is enabled via CMD6. CMD8 checks host supply voltage for Version 2.00+ cards. SDHC/SDXC cards use block addressing with a fixed 512-byte block length, whereas SDSC uses byte addressing with CMD16-set lengths. The host may change or stop the bus clock, providing 8 clocks after each transaction. CRC7 protects commands, responses (except R3), CSD, and CID; CRC16 protects data blocks, applied per line in wide bus mode. Read timeout is 100 ms for High/Extended Capacity cards, and maximum write busy is 250 ms.

This letter presents a theoretical investigation of the orbital degree of freedom (ODF) in magnon–phonon coupled systems (magnon-polarons). The authors show that the ODF of bosonic quasiparticles such as magnons and phonons originates from two mechanisms: global rotation of the system and the quantum geometry of the wavefunctions, formulated via the quasi–quantum geometric tensor. Using a 2D antiferromagnetic honeycomb lattice with Néel order (parameterized for MnPS3) as a model, they demonstrate that magnetoelastic coupling breaks parity-time symmetry, enabling transfer of intra-band orbital angular moment (OAM) between magnons and phonons, while also inducing inter-band transitions that generate inter-band OAM. Through hybridization with magnons, phonons can acquire a finite OAM despite their intrinsic linear polarization.

The authors propose an experimental probe: a temperature or strain gradient excites magnon-polarons whose magnetic moments generate electric polarization, producing a measurable transverse voltage composed of spin Berry curvature and OAM contributions. In MnPS3 at low magnetic fields, the OAM contribution dominates, and the net electric polarization is enhanced by 5–6 orders of magnitude compared to a case with only Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. The voltage increases with temperature and coupling strength, vanishes without magnon-phonon interaction, but remains finite at zero temperature.

The authors conclude that magnon-phonon coupling enables electrical control over magnetization and phononic transport, and that their quantum-geometric framework for ODF extends universally to fermionic and bosonic quasiparticles, laying foundations for phonon orbitronics.

The Value Area trading strategy uses the volume profile (market profile) to identify the range of prices where the majority of trading activity occurred during a given time period. The Value Area is defined as the price range where 70% of total trading volume occurred, a figure that roughly approximates one standard deviation on either side of the mean. Traders view these areas as potential support and resistance levels and areas for buying and selling. The strategy is commonly used in futures markets but can also be applied to stock and forex markets.

Trading signals are generated by identifying key support and resistance levels within the value area and looking for price action suggesting breakouts or reversals. Breakouts above the value area high or below the value area low may indicate a trending market, while rejection of the value area may indicate consolidation or reversal. Rejection can be identified through reversal candlestick patterns such as hammer/shooting star, engulfing, and dojis, or through divergences with momentum oscillators like stochastic, RSI, and MACD.

The strategy is commonly used on intraday and daily timeframes, though it can also be applied to weekly or monthly charts depending on trader preference. Risks include false signals, changing value areas that may contain outdated information, and the insufficiency of the value area alone for trading decisions. Risk management involves stop-loss orders, position sizing, portfolio diversification, and discipline. The passage notes that the strategy is not easy to backtest, and the authors did not conduct a backtest.

The IMF advised Saudi Arabia not to rush reforms and price hikes, praising its reform programme but warning that rapid fiscal consolidation would harm growth. Saudi Arabia has posted $200 billion in budget deficits over three years, with a $53 billion shortfall forecast this year. The IMF expects the deficit to fall to nine percent of GDP, down from 17.2 percent in 2016. Riyadh's Vision 2030 aims for budget balance by 2019, though the IMF recommended 2022. Austerity measures include higher taxes and prices, plus a planned five-percent VAT next year.

Scientists are preparing to study the upcoming total solar eclipse—the best in the U.S. in nearly a century—using ground telescopes, the International Space Station, 11 satellites, three planes, and over 70 high-altitude balloons. The federal government is spending about $7.7 million on the eclipse, whose shadow will sweep from Oregon to South Carolina. Citizen scientists will participate through projects like Citizen CATE, the iNaturalist app, and Eclipse Megamovie 2017. Researchers will focus on the sun's corona, which is more than 1 million degrees hotter than the sun's surface. Past eclipses led to major discoveries, including helium in 1868 and confirmation of Einstein's theory of relativity in 1919.

This study computes finite-temperature equilibrium vacancy concentrations in a nine-component refractory multi-principal element alloy composed of group 4, 5, and 6 elements on a body-centered cubic lattice. An embedded cluster expansion (eCE) model, parameterized with density functional theory calculations on roughly 9,400 configurations, reproduces formation energies to within about 8 meV/site and is combined with a coarse-graining statistical mechanics framework, extended to the canonical ensemble, to compute vacancy concentrations via Monte Carlo simulations.

Alloys containing only group 5 and 6 elements (e.g., VNbTaCrMoW) exhibit very low vacancy concentrations (approximately 10⁻⁷ at 2000 K), while adding group 4 elements (Ti, Zr, Hf) raises concentrations by one to two orders of magnitude, reaching about 10⁻⁴ near 1700 K in the Senkov alloy HfNbTaTiZr. Vacancy concentrations depend strongly on short-range order and bonding: phase-separating Cr-W shows higher-than-ideal vacancy concentrations, ordering Nb-W shows lower-than-ideal values, and ideal-mixing Mo-W matches ideal predictions. Substituting Ta for Mo in HfMoNbTiZr unexpectedly increases vacancy concentrations because Mo forms stronger bonds with group 4 elements. Vacancies are surrounded by enriched Zr and Hf in the first neighbor shell and Mo in the second. Vacancy formation free energies decrease with increasing group 4 content, with roughly 50–60% group 4 concentration needed to achieve vacancy concentrations of 10⁻⁴–10⁻⁵ at 1500°C. Simulations also indicate a miscibility gap in the equiatomic nonary alloy.

Compared with special quasi-random structure (SQS)-based approaches, which underestimate vacancy concentrations by factors of 3–7 in tested alloys due to short-range order and finite-size errors in chemical potentials, the method agrees with semi-grand canonical simulations while requiring far fewer samples. Limitations include neglect of vibrational contributions and the dilute-vacancy assumption.

The superintendent of Iowa's largest school district, described as a well-known figure in the state, was arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The remainder of the passage consists of headlines and links from the education news outlet The 74, covering topics such as school integration, COVID-19 academic recovery, the Every Student Succeeds Act, STEM opportunities for girls, and various student and teacher stories, along with donation and newsletter subscription prompts.

A Danish study found that children born to mothers with rheumatoid arthritis were almost three times more likely to develop the disease themselves, and also had increased risks of thyroid disease and epilepsy. Researchers said the findings should be used to increase awareness among doctors.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-Q reports results for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2020. Third quarter fiscal 2020 revenue was $35.0 billion, up from $30.6 billion a year earlier, with net income of $10.8 billion versus $8.8 billion. Nine-month revenue totaled $105.0 billion with net income of $33.1 billion. Total assets were $285.4 billion and stockholders' equity was $114.5 billion as of March 31, 2020. Revenue is reported across three segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. Commercial cloud revenue increased 39% to $13.3 billion, and server products and cloud services revenue grew 30%, driven by Azure growth of 59%. The effective tax rate was 16%. Long-term debt was $62.9 billion and cash and short-term investments totaled $137.6 billion. A $40 billion share repurchase program approved in September 2019 commenced in February 2020, with $36.8 billion remaining. The report notes COVID-19 had minimal net impact on quarterly revenue, as increased cloud usage offset slowdowns in transactional licensing and advertising spend. Accrued legal liabilities were $304 million, with reasonably possible adverse outcomes of approximately $800 million beyond recorded amounts. Deloitte & Touche LLP reviewed the interim financial statements and reported no material modifications were needed.

In an action of trespass quare clausum for removing a barn and blacksmith's shop from the plaintiff's land, the court held that a conveyance by extent of execution is subject to the same rules of construction as a conveyance by deed, and passes all buildings standing on the land, whether their foundations are sunk below the surface or not. The land had been set off to Brooks under an execution against Jack, and the appraisers' and sheriff's returns contained no exception or reservation of the buildings. The defendants' offered parol evidence—that the buildings were excluded by the creditor's direction and left for the debtor—was rejected as inadmissible to vary written testimony. Judgment was entered on the verdict for the plaintiff.

Aspects of the disclosure provide methods and apparatuses for video encoding and decoding. The present application is a continuation of prior U.S. patent applications related to video coding using a directional mode and a non-separable transform.

For a block coded with a directional mode, processing circuitry determines the directional mode based on a nominal mode and an angular offset indicated by coding information, determines a non-separable transform for the block based on the nominal mode, and reconstructs the block based on the directional mode and the non-separable transform. A transform set mode associated with the nominal mode indicates a set of one or more non-separable transforms, and a signaled non-separable transform index identifies the specific transform within the set. The non-separable transform can be a non-separable secondary transform, such as a low-frequency non-separable transform (LFNST), which in some examples does not apply to PAETH or recursive filtering modes.

For blocks coded with non-directional modes (including DC, PAETH, SMOOTH, SMOOTH_V, SMOOTH_H, recursive filtering, and chroma from luma modes), a set of non-separable transforms is associated with the mode, and a transform within the set is determined based on a signaled index.

The passage provides background on video compression (including lossless and lossy techniques), intra prediction, intra prediction directions in standards such as H.264, H.265, and JEM/VVC/BMS, and describes video encoder and decoder architectures, communication systems, and streaming environments. It details AV1's directional modes (56 modes based on eight nominal modes with angular offsets), non-directional smooth predictors, recursive-filtering-based prediction, chroma from luma prediction, and multi-line intra prediction. Reduced non-separable secondary transforms (RST) are described as applied between primary transform and quantization to reduce memory and computation, with applicability conditions such as requiring coefficients outside a first subgroup to be non-significant. Transform set selection tables map intra prediction modes to transform sets, and line graph transforms (LGT) derived from generalized graph Laplacian matrices are also described.

A University of Maryland study of 1,099 young adults found energy drink consumption between ages 21 and 24, even occasionally, was linked to greater risk of later cocaine or non-medical prescription stimulant use; those who stopped were less likely to develop substance-abuse issues.

The Business Insider Scottish Accountancy & Finance Awards annually recognise accountants' work in private and public sector organisations. Presented by Sarah Heaney with entertainment from Britain's Got Talent act DNA, the event includes categories such as firm of the year and finance director of the year. Tickets cost £132 (single) to £1,440 (table of 12), plus VAT.

This study examines the characteristics, employment patterns, and earnings of Hungarian higher education lecturers, using data from the Hungarian Educational Authority, Central Statistical Office, National Employment Service, and international databases (World Bank, Eurostat, OECD, UNESCO).

Following the 1990 regime change, Hungarian higher education expanded from a low-capacity system, with the 1993 Higher Education Act setting the goal of raising participation to the level of developed democracies. Pluralism in institution establishment created non-state (church and foundation) institutions, which employed almost a third of lecturers by 2020. Student numbers were shaped by demographic decline, the 2005 Bologna two-cycle reform, and admission policies, including tuition reimbursement in the late 1990s and, from 2010, reduced state funding and tighter requirements under the illiberal government, which increased inequality in access and left the share of young graduates below the EU 2020 strategy's 40% target.

The number of lecturers correlated strongly with student numbers between 1990 and 2004 (+0.9752) but weakly negatively between 2005 and 2022 (−0.3135). The student-teacher ratio rose from 5.9 (1990) to 17.9 (2006), then fell to 10.4 (2022). The teaching load roughly tripled by 2006 and remained about double the 1990 level in 2022. Staff are older than the average in developed countries but mid-range among OECD countries; the female lecturer share (41.5% in 2020) ranks Hungary 80th among 144 countries.

Employment regulation evolved from the centralized Soviet-era scientific qualification system (1951), through the 1993 Act restoring universities' doctoral and habilitation rights, to the 2011 Act, which reduced institutional autonomy, introduced a chancellor system, and set minimum weekly teaching hours. In 2020, 22 state institutions were reorganized into public foundations, abolishing civil service status and replacing it with performance-linked employment and substantial pay rises.

University and college professors fell by two-thirds between 2005 and 2020, attributed to demographic retirement, funding cuts, stricter legal requirements, and low salaries—the professor salary base stagnated at 554,400 HUF/month despite significant inflation.

Doctoral graduates' earnings are lowest before age 37 and reach business-sector levels only in their early-to-mid fifties; their lifetime earnings fall below those of average university graduates, making academic careers unattractive. Hungary ranks worse than 40th internationally in doctoral student numbers, which correlate with scientific publication output (+0.7257), raising concern for future research capacity. The study concludes that policymakers should address factors hindering educators and young researchers, such as low incomes, emigration, and rigid institutions.

Azerbaijan aims to increase honey exports, Agriculture Minister Heydar Asadov said. World honey production stands at 1.5 million tonnes, with demand projected to reach 2-2.5 million tonnes in 2020-2022. Azerbaijani honey is organic; 6 tonnes were sold last year at 8-8.5 thousand USD/tonne. Proposals will be submitted to increase state support for beekeeping.

The Texas Education Agency is investigating hundreds of teachers' social media posts about the killing of conservative activist Charlie Kirk. Education Commissioner Mike Morath called the remarks "reprehensible and inappropriate" and pledged to recommend license suspensions, while Gov. Greg Abbott endorsed the effort, accusing teachers of inciting violence. Legal experts and education advocates say the investigations amount to a "witch hunt" that violates teachers' free speech rights, noting that public employees retain First Amendment protections when speaking in a personal capacity. Experts say the state must prove comments caused significant workplace disruption to justify discipline, and warn that political pressure could chill educators' speech.

Marc Ó Sé believes an injury-free James O'Donoghue could be a 'huge' boost for Kerry this summer. The 2014 Footballer of the Year scored nine points in Sunday's win over Clare, and Ó Sé expects him to improve with every game if he stays injury-free.

The player recalls Detroit fondly as his first team, which reached the semifinals two straight years. He was excited to be traded to Washington, but the trade initially didn't work out. He believes in the team's players, is excited to return to Detroit, and says his first trade was a shock.

Enron Corp. is in advanced talks to sell its Portland General Electric utility to Northwest Natural Gas Co. for about $1.8 billion in cash and stock (roughly $2.8 billion including about $1 billion in assumed debt), with a deal possibly announced within days. The transaction would give Enron a minority stake in Northwest Natural, whose previous sale of the utility to Sierra Pacific Resources collapsed in April amid the California energy crisis. Separately, Enron plans to cut 500 jobs in Europe, about 10 percent of its workforce there. In India, BG Group's $388 million purchase of Enron's 30 percent stake in the Panna/Mukta and Tapti offshore fields is in jeopardy over a dispute about operatorship rights with partners ONGC and Reliance. Tata Power expects to finalize a bid within three weeks for Enron's 65 percent stake in the $2.9 billion Dabhol Power project, while BSES has declined to buy the stake. Northwest Natural also raised its quarterly dividend to 31.5 cents per share.

Bond trading strategies offer diversification and potentially uncorrelated returns, making them complementary to stock strategies. The article focuses on Treasury bonds rather than corporate bonds and presents backtested strategies using the TLT ETF, which tracks 20-year Treasury bonds. A bond involves an issuer borrowing from investors, who receive scheduled interest payments and principal repayment at maturity. Bond trading strategies are systematic approaches aiming at capital preservation, income generation, or appreciation, and include yield curve, duration, credit spread, and tactical asset allocation strategies. They vary by time horizon, risk tolerance, and market conditions. Common mistakes include poor understanding of market dynamics, overreliance on historical data, weak risk management, chasing yield, misjudging interest rates, insufficient diversification, inflexibility, and emotional biases. Interest rate risk is illustrated by an example where a one-million investment in Treasuries fell to 800,000 after rates rose. Bonds show little correlation with stocks, as demonstrated by SPY-TLT correlation near zero. Four backtested TLT strategies are presented, including a seasonal strategy that returned more than twice buy and hold while invested only 61.8% of the time, with a 16.2% risk-adjusted return. Combining bond strategies with an S&P 500 strategy bundle raised annual returns from 11.5% to 18.6% while reducing drawdowns. Interest rates inversely affect bond prices, shaping approaches such as riding the yield curve. Day trading bonds is more challenging than trading stocks due to lower volatility, with traders focusing on liquid government bonds. Bond strategies can be automated, though human oversight remains important. Beginners may consider dollar-cost averaging.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated July 1, 2020, announcing that Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration and Chief Accounting Officer, is retiring. Brod will step down as Chief Accounting Officer on July 31, 2020, but will remain with the Company through September 30, 2020 to assist with the transition. Alice L. Jolla, age 54, will become Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer effective July 31, 2020. Jolla has served as Corporate Controller since 2014, previously held senior director roles in financial planning and corporate accounting, and was a FASB Industry Fellow from 2005 to 2007. In connection with her appointment, Jolla will receive a $1.5 million stock award under the Microsoft 2017 Stock Plan, vesting 6.25% quarterly, contingent on continuous employment.

President Trump criticized ABC after the Roseanne reboot was canceled over Roseanne Barr's racist tweet about former Obama adviser Valerie Jarrett, tweeting that ABC CEO Bob Iger apologized to Jarrett but never apologized to him for "HORRIBLE statements" made about him on ABC. Iger, Disney's CEO, had previously clashed with Trump, leaving his business advisory council and calling the end of DACA "cruel and misguided." Democratic lawmakers criticized Trump's comments, and Jarrett said Iger told her the show was being canceled, adding that tone "starts at the top" but every individual also bears responsibility.

Bitcoin fell below US$8,000 for the first time since November before recovering most losses, having wiped out more than half its value since a December 18 record high of US$19,511. Setbacks include regulatory threats from several countries, a US$500 million heist at Japanese exchange Coincheck, and Facebook's ban on cryptocurrency ads. Rival coins fell at least 18 per cent.

Microsoft is developing Polaris, a version of Windows 10 built on the modular Windows Core OS, designed for desktops, laptops, and 2-in-1 devices. Unlike Windows 10 S, which used full Windows 10 code, Polaris will run only UWP apps from the Microsoft Store and feature CShell, a new graphical interface replacing the shell used since Windows 95. This should make it lighter, faster, more secure, and less resource intensive, though legacy applications won't run natively; Microsoft is exploring 'remote virtualization' to support them. Windows Central suggests Polaris may arrive in 2019.

Best Hope Services will launch Nigeria's first online trade exhibition in May to promote local innovations. CEO Olu Adenodi said the e-fair lets exhibitors showcase products worldwide without hiring grounds, while visitors participate remotely. Originator Prof. Joseph Mba said it would positively impact national development, covering e-fair expo, connect, trade and events. Nigerians are urged to register before May 1.

The United States and China share an interest in peace, have approximately $3.5 billion in annual two-way trade, and both are concerned about the Soviet military buildup, though they disagree on Taiwan. A Reagan-Bush Administration would observe five principles for the Far East: treating U.S.-Chinese relations as a global, strategic partnership while expanding trade, scientific, and cultural ties; working with Japan, the People's Republic of China, the Republic of Korea, and Taiwan for Western Pacific peace and economic growth; cooperating with regional countries against aggression or hegemony; and conducting relations with Taiwan in accordance with the Taiwan Relations Act. The author criticizes Jimmy Carter's normalization concessions to China, arguing a liaison office on Taiwan should have been retained. The Act, revised by Congress, safeguards Taiwan's security, provides defensive weapons, administers relations through the American Institute in Taiwan, and includes Congressional funding, auditing, and oversight.

Researchers at the Institute of Synthetic Polymer Materials of the Russian Academy of Sciences, MIPT, and elsewhere determined how the regularity (isotacticity) of polypropylene molecules and thermal treatment affect its mechanical properties, enabling synthesis of materials with predetermined properties such as elasticity or hardness; the findings were published in Polymer. Polypropylene is second only to polyethylene in production volume. Randomly arranged, amorphous chains yield soft materials, while crosslinks between chains form crystallites that make materials harder. Isotactic segments, with methyl groups on one side of the carbon backbone, form crosslinks effectively, so higher isotacticity yields stronger materials. Using pentads—five-unit isotactic segments—to measure isotacticity, the team tested polypropylenes of 25 to over 95 percent isotacticity as films made by ice-water quenching or slow cooling, then stretched them on a testing machine. Stress-strain curves showed behavior depended on isotacticity and thermal prehistory, with elastic modulus rising with crystallinity, and crystallite forms differing between quenched and slowly cooled samples. The team is now doing similar work with polyethylene.

The JACL Kakehashi Program will select up to 200 participants for nine-day trips to Japan to strengthen U.S.-Japan relations. Eligible applicants are students or young professionals aged 18-25 of Japanese or Asian American heritage; Japanese nationals are restricted. Trip 1 runs Dec. 13-20 (apply by Oct. 9); Trip 2 runs March 12-20, 2018 (apply by Jan. 2, 2018).

Wal-Mart's bid for Bonobos is part of its effort to recover ground against Amazon in online fashion and reach millennial customers, analysts said. It would be the fourth acquisition of a small online clothing-and-accessories brand since early 2017, following ShoeBuy, Moosejaw and ModCloth. The strategy is led by Marc Lore, who took over Wal-Mart's e-commerce business after the $3.3 billion Jet.com acquisition. Intel has released Coffee Lake-based 14nm desktop processors and Z370 chipsets, with motherboard vendors selling Z370 motherboards worldwide. Intel plans more Coffee Lake processors, chipsets, and notebook processors through 2018, plus Gemini Lake processors in November 2017. Its 10nm Cannon Lake processors are expected mid-2018, with Ice Lake in 2019.

The passage introduces molecular augmented dynamics (MAD), an O(N) modified molecular dynamics method designed to find low-energy, ab-initio accurate atomistic structures of disordered materials that match experimental data. Standard Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics sampling do not guarantee experimental agreement, while reverse and hybrid reverse Monte Carlo methods can yield unphysical structures and are computationally inefficient, having been restricted to a few thousand atoms. Two earlier MD-based approaches suffered from poor scaling, inaccurate gradients, and neglected thermal effects. MAD employs a Hamiltonian combining kinetic energy, interatomic potential, and an experimental potential, performing multi-objective optimization of experimental agreement and system energy. The paper derives analytic, linearly scaling forces for XRD, ND, PDF, and XPS observables that account for thermal broadening, and shows that any observable depending on local, position-differentiable descriptors is amenable; simulation parameters and CPU/GPU scaling in the TurboGAP code are also provided.

Tips of the Week features making tips, including: Kent Barnes adding rare earth magnets to tester wires for easier hookups; John Park converting a motor into a rotating turntable for filming his Clockwork Goggles project; Phillip Stokes' tip to attach a hobby knife to a compass as a cutter; Andy Birkey's advice to mark untrue material edges with squiggly lines; a drill press drum sander Instructable; and Ben Krasnow's recommendation of a ten dollar Ikea flexi-neck LED lamp for workbench lighting.

The "Drive & Kick" offense is a three-player weave from a 3-2 spread alignment, initiated with dribble penetration for a layup. If penetration is denied, the handler passes back outside and replaces the receiver, continuing the weave among O1, O2, and O3. Handlers have a "Green Light" to drive but must avoid charges. The offense runs time off the clock and includes corner kick-outs and back cuts when defenders sag off.

The passage describes the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, the eighth-generation data center GPU built on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture (GA100), fabricated on TSMC's 7nm process with 54.2 billion transistors and a die size of 826 mm². The A100 delivers significant performance improvements over the Tesla V100 for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads.

Key features include:

- **Third-Generation Tensor Cores** supporting FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and Binary formats. TF32 operations run 10x faster than V100 FP32 FMA operations (20x with sparsity); FP16/FP32 mixed-precision delivers 2.5x V100 performance (5x with sparsity); and new IEEE-compliant FP64 operations deliver 2.5x V100 FP64 performance.
- **Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity** using a 2:4 non-zero pattern that doubles Tensor Core throughput by skipping zero values, with minimal accuracy loss for inference.
- **Multi-Instance GPU (MIG)**, which partitions the A100 into up to seven GPU Instances with isolated memory paths, providing quality of service and fault isolation, particularly beneficial for Cloud Service Providers.
- **Memory enhancements**: 40 GB HBM2 with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth (73% more than V100), a 40 MB L2 cache (nearly 7x larger than V100) with 2.3x read bandwidth, L2 cache residency controls, and Compute Data Compression.
- **Third-Generation NVLink** with 600 GB/sec total bandwidth (double V100), plus PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV support.
- **New SM features**: 192 KB combined L1 cache/shared memory, asynchronous copy instructions, asynchronous barriers, and simultaneous FP32/INT32 execution.
- **CUDA 11 advances** including Task Graph acceleration, L2 residency controls, and Cooperative Groups improvements.
- **Additional hardware**: NVJPG decode engine, Optical Flow Accelerator, improved atomic operations (11x FP16, 2.7x FP32 over V100), and five NVDEC units.

The A100 contains 108 SMs, 6,912 FP32 CUDA cores, and 432 Tensor Cores. The passage also covers the TCAIRS mixed-precision solver (TF32 achieved a 2.0x geomean speedup over the FP64 baseline) and the NVIDIA DGX A100 system, which includes eight A100 GPUs delivering 5 PFLOPS of performance, interconnected via NVSwitch, and supporting up to 56 discrete accelerators through MIG.

The Housing Authority of the City of Santa Barbara received a Gold Nugget Award for Best Affordable Project at the Pacific Coast Builders Conference for Bradley Studios, a 54-unit development built in 2012. Developed by the Housing Authority, designed by Peikert Group Architects LLP, and built by McGillivray Construction, the infill project houses low and extremely low-income residents with special needs and offers on-site amenities including community rooms and social service offices.

This study used spatial transcriptomics (10x Visium and Nanostring CosMx) and immunohistochemistry to characterize the cellular and molecular microenvironments expressing IDO1 and PD-L1 (CD274) in cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) lesions from Sri Lankan, Brazilian, and Indian patients. IDO1 and CD274 expression localized to myeloid cell-rich niches in the papillary dermis, with mature dendritic cells (DC3) and CCL18+ macrophages identified as the primary expressing cell types. Neighbourhood analysis revealed that CD8+ memory T cells and regulatory T cells (Tregs) were the most common neighbours of IDO1+/CD274+ myeloid cells and were the major source of IL-32. A core gene signature (IL32, LYZ, GBP1, IFI30, FTH1) was identified as common correlates of IDO1 and CD274 across all three disease forms studied. In Sri Lankan CL patients treated with sodium stibogluconate, high abundance of IL-32+ CD8+ T cells was associated with slower cure rates (hazard ratio 2.78), identifying IL-32 as a prognostic biomarker for treatment response. The authors propose a model in which CCL18+ macrophages recruit IL-32+ T cells into the niche, which paracrine signalling induces IDO1 and PD-L1 expression in myeloid cells, thereby promoting loss of effector T cell function through tryptophan starvation and PD-1 signalling.

Acting CDC director Jim O'Neill called on vaccine manufacturers to replace the combined measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine with three separate monovalent shots, linking to a similar call by President Trump. The change is not supported by medical research: monovalent vaccines are no longer available in the U.S., a 2017 study found 69% of children receiving the combination vaccine completed the recommended series versus 50% for single-antigen vaccines, and no safety or effectiveness advantage from separating the shots has been shown. The idea originated with Andrew Wakefield, whose paper claiming an MMR-autism link was retracted. Producing monovalent vaccines would likely take years, and experts warn the rhetoric could deter parents and lower vaccination rates.

The passage describes the MSPM0C1105/6 microcontrollers from Texas Instruments, part of the ultra-low-power 32-bit MSPM0 MCU family based on the Arm Cortex-M0+ core operating at up to 32MHz. These cost-optimized MCUs support temperatures from -40°C to 125°C and supply voltages from 1.62V to 3.6V, with up to 64KB flash and 8KB SRAM, plus a high-speed on-chip oscillator eliminating the need for an external crystal. Key peripherals include a 3-channel DMA, CRC-16 accelerator, a 12-bit 1.6Msps ADC, a comparator with 8-bit reference DAC, an on-chip temperature sensor, one 16-bit advanced timer with deadband, four 16-bit general purpose timers, a windowed watchdog, and three UART, one SPI, and two I2C peripherals supporting protocols such as LIN, IrDA, SMBus, and PMBus. The devices offer five power modes (RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, SHUTDOWN) across two power domains (PD1 and PD0). The document details the CPU subsystem, power management unit, clock module, DMA, GPIO (up to 45 pins), IOMUX, ADC, temperature sensor, LFSS, VREF, comparator, security features, communication interfaces, watchdog timers, RTC_B, timers, debug subsystem (SWD/DEBUGSS), and factory constants. It also provides application guidance (decoupling capacitors, NRST pullup resistor), device nomenclature, development tools, a revision history noting removal of the DGS32 package, and mechanical packaging information.

This study examined the empathy levels of 206 teachers in the faculties of Education at University G, Spain, using the Spanish adaptation of the Interpersonal Reactivity Index (IRI), which measures four dimensions: Perspective Taking, Fantasy, Empathic Concern, and Personal Distress. Results showed overall empathy above the theoretical midpoint, with high scores in Empathic Concern, Perspective Taking, and Fantasy, and moderate scores in Personal Distress. Female participants scored significantly higher across all dimensions. No significant differences were found by degree programme, campus, contractual status, or teaching experience. The authors concluded teachers exhibit high empathy, though limited sample size and potential social desirability bias caution against generalisation.

The Department opposes dividing the General Assembly into four regional sections, viewing decentralization as premature and potentially harmful to establishing a strong, effective international organization; such discussion should be postponed until the organization is firmly established. The Dumbarton Oaks proposals provide for an International Court of Justice as the Organization's principal judicial organ, with its statute annexed to the Charter. UNC Chapel Hill placed associate professor Dwayne Dixon on leave Monday while investigating his "alleged advocacy of politically motivated violence." Dixon, formerly of the Silver Valley Redneck Revolt chapter of the antifascist group Redneck Revolt, previously faced blowback for activism—including a 2018 arrest for bringing a rifle to a KKK counterprotest, later dismissed as unconstitutional—but remained employed. Three Illinois gang members were shot to death at point-blank range during a drag racing event at Great Lakes Dragaway near Union Grove, Wis., on Aug. 13, 2017. The Bearish Engulfing candlestick pattern is a technical analysis tool used to identify potential trend reversals from an uptrend to a downtrend. It consists of a bullish candlestick followed by a bearish candlestick whose body completely engulfs the previous bullish body, signaling that sellers have taken control. It differs from the Bullish Engulfing pattern, which indicates a reversal from a downtrend to an uptrend.

According to backtesting on the S&P 500 since 1993, the pattern's success rate is between 55% and 65%, with 311 occurrences, making it the third most frequent of 75 candlestick patterns. Despite its name, it often acts as a continuation pattern in the stock market.

Traders may close long positions, enter short positions, place stop-loss orders above the high of the white candlestick, and target profits at support levels. The pattern does not guarantee reversals and is more reliable when confirmed by other indicators, such as RSI or MACD, and by changes in market momentum; adding an RSI filter in one backtest increased the average gain per trade from 0.73% to 0.88%.

Risks include false signals, varying market conditions, volatility, and leverage. Risk management approaches include stop-loss orders, risk/reward ratios, position sizing, diversification, and hedging. Similar patterns—dark cloud cover, evening star, and bearish harami—indicate weaker bearish sentiment, as their black candlesticks only partially cover the preceding white candlestick.

The 50 EMA strategy is a technical analysis trading strategy that uses the 50-day Exponential Moving Average to identify trend direction and generate buy and sell signals, typically for capturing medium-term trends. An up-sloping line with price above it indicates an uptrend; a down-sloping line with price below it indicates a downtrend. Traders enter long positions when price is above the 50 EMA and short positions when below, often confirming signals with indicators like RSI or MACD. It is typically used on medium-term timeframes, such as 4-hour or daily charts.

Backtesting showed a simple moving average crossover system performed poorly on multiple assets, with 6.8% annual returns on the S&P 500 versus 7.3% for buy and hold, though with a lower maximum drawdown. Using the 50 EMA as a filter with a second indicator improved results: 11.5% annual returns on QQQ versus 9.8% for buy and hold, a 73% win rate, and 22% maximum drawdown while invested only 27% of the time. SPY produced 8.9% annual returns with a 16% maximum drawdown, and bonds performed decently but with small average gains per trade. The authors note that, based on their backtesting, stop-losses rarely improve strategies.

The AMD Secure RNG Library provides an easy-to-use API for accessing hardware-generated random numbers through the RDRAND and RDSEED x86 instructions, which return 16-bit, 32-bit, or 64-bit random and conditioned random values. The library abstracts low-level programming, handles possible outcomes from register outputs, manages hardware failure checks with user-specified retry attempts, and supports both single values and streams of random numbers. It exposes APIs for fetching single values, arrays of 32-bit/64-bit values, and random byte arrays using either RDRAND or RDSEED. The is_RDRAND_supported and is_RDSEED_supported APIs use the CPUID instruction to verify hardware support, and applications should invoke these first. Random numbers are widely used in cryptography, HPC applications such as Monte Carlo simulations, communication protocols, gaming, and seeding software-based PRNGs. AMD Zen processors include a dedicated cryptographic co-processor within the AMD Secure Processor, and each RDRAND or RDSEED invocation reads from this block via memory-mapped I/O (MMIO), which is relatively slow compared to software-based PRNGs. For latency-sensitive applications, a hybrid approach—seeding a PRNG with a hardware-generated value—can improve both security and performance. Hardware-based generators provide more secure and robust random values than software implementations, and applications such as cryptographic key generation can benefit from the library.

The First Circuit Court of Appeals granted a stay, allowing the Education Department to fire half of the 550 Office for Civil Rights employees. The March reduction-in-force plan cutting 276 OCR staff prompted lawsuits including New York v. McMahon and Victim Rights Law Center v. Department of Education. U.S. manufacturing faces a shortage of qualified workers for jobs requiring education and specialized skills amid increasing automation, with nearly 390,000 positions open. Displaced workers like Herbie Mays lack the training for these new jobs, while workers with in-demand skills benefit.

The 1-2-2 Zone is a strong defense against outside shooting teams, facilitates fast breaks since defenders are already in fast break positions, and can protect a late-game lead when opponents must attempt three-point shots. The point positions at the top of the circle, wings at the elbows, and baseline players above the blocks, with defenders shifting while the ball is in the air. Specific shifts are defined for ball positions in the corners, wings, and middle. Baseline players work in unison, wings work opposite and are responsible for weakside rebounding, and the point guards the ball out front and defends the high post otherwise. Adjustments include wing corner shift options (pass denial or dropping to help the post), a corner trap, switching to a 2-1-2 zone on the first pass, and extending into half or full court presses.

This study examined the effect of enforcing the Kenya Health Sector Referral Guidelines 2014 on facility referrals to Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH). Tertiary hospitals in resource-limited settings face congestion from patients bypassing lower-level facilities, as documented in studies from Zambia, South Africa, Nigeria, India, and Taiwan. Kenya's health system comprises six tiers, including four Tier 6 national teaching and referral hospitals, among them KNH. KNH's orthopaedic wards recorded high bed occupancy (142.2%, 138.2%, 116.5% in 2018–2020) and a nurse-patient ratio of 1:10. On 1 July 2021, KNH began enforcing the guidelines, requiring written referral letters and prior concurrence with its referral office. Using a pre-posttest design covering five months before and five months after enforcement, 468 orthopaedic and trauma facility referrals (220 before, 248 after) were abstracted from three admission points and analyzed using chi-squared tests and logistic regression. Nairobi County and neighboring counties accounted for over four-fifths of referrals; about three-fifths were from government facilities, and about half were from Tiers 2–4. Overall changes in referral numbers after enforcement were not statistically significant, but referrals from Tiers II and III declined significantly while referrals from Tiers IV–VI increased (p=0.002). Forty-three facilities, mostly private and lower-tier, stopped referring directly to KNH. Major referral factors were human resource capacity and availability, infrastructure, equipment availability, patient preference, and financial considerations, with cost influencing patient preference for KNH. The authors conclude that enforcement reduced referrals from lower-tier facilities and that guideline implementation is feasible, offering recommendations for policymakers, KNH, and health facilities. Limitations included the COVID-19 pandemic and the retrospective quasi-experimental design.

New research from Emory University suggests that the probiotic Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) may help protect the liver from drug-induced damage, such as from acetaminophen overuse, which can cause liver damage or death by increasing free radicals and oxidative stress. In a study on mice, those fed an LGG-rich diet showed an improved antioxidant response in the liver, protecting it from oxidative damage. The study found that the protein Nrf2, which regulates genes that fight free radicals, plays a pivotal role in this protection. Lead author Bejan Saeedi noted that probiotics' effects extend beyond the gastrointestinal tract, but further studies are needed to determine whether the results can be replicated in humans.

This email compiles news articles from March 2001 concerning Enron and energy industry developments. Enron CEO Jeff Skilling attributed the company's stock decline (dropping below $60 for the first time since January 2000, after losing 8 percent over March 21–22) to market-wide selling of high price-to-earnings stocks, though an analyst noted Enron-specific factors including reduced broadband valuation, payment problems with India's Maharashtra State Electricity Board over the Dabhol plant, and the terminated 20-year Blockbuster video deal. In Closson v. Billman (Ind. 1904), lumber supplier Edgar D. Closson sued to foreclose a material man's lien against Marie E. Billman's lot for lumber used in a dwelling constructed under a contract between Charles D. Billman, acting as his wife's agent, and contractor Levi A. Worley. The contract required Worley to furnish all materials and to provide a $1,500 bond conditioned on building and completing the residence according to the contract; Closson signed the bond with Worley. Worley purchased $863.35 of lumber from Closson but failed to pay for it, and liens were filed. The court held that Closson was a guarantor rather than a surety, since his undertaking was that his principal would perform a collateral contract. Because Worley's failure to pay for materials breached the contract, the guarantor became liable for the liens. The court further held that pleading such facts was a sufficient defense to the foreclosure suit to avoid circuity of action; that no notice of acceptance of the guaranty was required, as it was executed contemporaneously with and as part of the consideration for the transaction; and that the burden was on the guarantor to plead and prove an omission to give notice of default and resulting damage. Judgment was affirmed.

Despite seventy years of unprecedented education expansion, education worldwide remained deficient by 2020, and the COVID-19 Pandemic aggravated existing problems. The paper reflects on what the pandemic means for the repositioning and reinvigoration of Comparative and International Education (CIE) in 2023. The United Nations' 2015 Sustainable Development Goals and the Incheon Declaration, drafted by over 1600 participants from 160 countries, articulate humanity's vision for education by 2030, with education seen as both a goal in itself and a precondition for realizing the other goals. However, by 2020 education showed massive shortfalls in quantitative participation (258 million children of school-going age not attending school), quality (across input, process, output, and product dimensions), and equality (inequalities along socio-economic, gender, and racial/ethnic lines). The pandemic led to school closures affecting about 91% of the global student population and a shift to distance education, which risked ending education opportunities for many, lowering quality, and disproportionately harming already disadvantaged learners, as illustrated by a South African survey. Simultaneously, the pandemic forced the traditionally conservative education sector to embrace technology. The paper argues that CIE should investigate the pandemic's education ravages and the use of technology across diverse system and societal contexts, generating recommendations for pursuing the 2030 goals, while also addressing the field's deficiencies, including unresponsiveness, the "black box syndrome," lack of autochthonous theory, inadequate university presence, Northern Hegemony, and limited impact. CIE is presented as pivotal in recovering education beyond its pre-pandemic state and building new, better education systems.

The passage is a Motley Fool Money review of the Wells Fargo Active Cash Card, which offers unlimited 2% cash rewards on purchases with no annual fee, a $200 cash rewards bonus after spending $500 in the first 3 months, and 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers (then 18.99%, 23.99%, or 28.99% variable APR). Texas Tech University's provost office posted a FAQ on Sunday providing the first written clarification of new policies prohibiting faculty from speaking or teaching about transgender identity, but removed it three days later without explanation. The passage describes a patent application (a continuation of International Application No. PCT/CN2020/070820, claiming priority to a Chinese application filed January 14, 2019) concerning systems and methods for route planning based on maps, particularly topological maps, for vehicles such as automatic guided vehicles (AGVs). The background notes that motion information of other vehicles can affect node information (e.g., passability), impacting the accuracy and efficiency of route planning.

The disclosed method includes obtaining a topological map corresponding to a scheduling system; preprocessing the map by modifying node information based on motion status information of AGVs and the nodes they occupy; determining start and destination nodes for a current AGV; determining total costs for nodes between the start and destination; and performing route planning based on these costs. The disclosure covers multiple aspects, including methods, devices with processors and storage, computer-readable media, and systems with modules for obtaining locations, maps, motion status information, and determining routes. The route planning system may include a server, network, vehicles, terminal devices, and storage devices, with applications such as AGV freight transport, sightseeing, and automatic food delivery.

Preprocessing may include first preprocessing (modifying node information around static AGVs, such as assigning high weight values, marking nodes as incapable of turn, or designating them as impassable barriers) and second preprocessing (additionally modifying nodes on planned routes of moving AGVs that have not yet been passed). If a first planned route would collide with moving AGVs, second preprocessing and re-planning are performed.

Total cost is calculated as f(n) = g(n) + h(n), where g(n) is the cost from the current node (including the node's weight value, parent node cost, distance cost, and turn cost) and h(n) is the cost to the destination (e.g., Manhattan distance). Route planning may use algorithms such as A-star, Dijkstra, Floyd-Warshall, Bellman-Ford, or RRT, employing open and closed sets with a binary heap structure to select nodes with minimum cost. Tasks may be allocated to idle AGVs, and the map may be updated at defined intervals or upon request.

This document outlines the U.S. approach to Soviet relations in 1983. On arms control, it urges maintaining high standards—real reductions, equality, verifiability, and stability—while holding firm in INF and START negotiations. On regional issues, it proposes testing Soviet intentions on Afghanistan through bilateral talks, strengthening the US-PRC dialogue on Kampuchea, pressing for Cuban troop withdrawal in Namibia/Angola, warning against unacceptable Soviet Third World behavior, and avoiding dialogue that would help Moscow reenter the Middle East peace process. Human rights efforts should use private diplomacy to secure prisoner releases, resolution of divided-family cases, and increased Jewish emigration. Economic steps must not aid Soviet military power or subsidize its economy, with a Joint Commercial Commission possibly managing trade pressures. Bilateral steps should be mutual, reciprocal, and broaden access to Soviet society. Dialogue should proceed through four levels—summitry, ministerial contacts, ambassadors, and departmental specialists—building toward a possible summit without premature commitment. The document concludes that if the Soviets fail to meet U.S. criteria, responsibility for continued tensions will rest with Moscow.

W. T. Hay, adjudged a voluntary bankrupt in November 1915, had previously conveyed real estate to his brother, who in turn conveyed an interest in it to Hay's wife, Matilda M. Hay. Deposit National Bank, holding a judgment entered against Hay before the bankruptcy, received a dividend in the bankruptcy distribution, and Hay was discharged from his debts in June 1916. In July 1917, the bank issued execution on the judgment and levied on the real estate held by the wife, alleging the conveyance had been made to defraud creditors. The lower court stayed the writ except as to that property, and Hay appealed. The Supreme Court affirmed, holding Hay had no standing to complain, as he neither owned nor claimed the property, the execution was stayed against him personally, and the sale could not affect his rights. Questions about the bank's right to proceed and the validity of a sheriff's sale could not be raised by the bankrupt. Appeal dismissed at appellant's costs.

In September, Scott donated $70 million to UNCF to bolster pooled endowments across 37 HBCUs, aiming to narrow historical funding gaps. The case examines the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) under commissioner Lisa Baird, who began the role on March 10, 2020, just as COVID-19 halted sports. After two failed women's leagues (WUSA, 2001–2003; WPS, 2009–2012), the NWSL launched in 2013 as a single-entity league supported by U.S. Soccer, which paid salaries for allocated national team players and managed the league's front office. The USWNT's international success—including four World Cup titles—drew attention to the league but also prompted a 2019 equal pay lawsuit against U.S. Soccer by 28 players.

Facing the pandemic, Baird secured a Paycheck Protection Program loan to pay non-allocated players and organized workstreams covering medical protocols, finance, competition format, host city selection, player relations, childcare, and social justice. The result was the Challenge Cup (June 27–July 26, 2020), a 23-game tournament in a Utah bubble that made the NWSL the first U.S. professional league to return to play. Over 2,000 tests produced zero positive cases, and the tournament cost $1.8 million. The opening game drew a record 572,000 CBS viewers and the final over 650,000; the Houston Dash won. Players were permitted to kneel and wear Black Lives Matter shirts. A Fall Series followed (September 5–October 17, 2020), scheduled after Baird secured CBS broadcast slots opened by postponed college football.

By 2021, the league had formally separated from U.S. Soccer (December 2020), added expansion teams including Angel City FC with numerous high-profile women investors, increased allocation money, and saw USWNT players Lindsey Horan and Crystal Dunn sign directly with the Portland Thorns. Baird's second year brought challenges in fan engagement, media exposure (2020 viewership rose 493%), a planned 2022 rebrand, social justice leadership, expansion, and negotiating a collective bargaining agreement with the NWSLPA, announced April 7, 2021.

Cu-doped NiO thin films were synthesized on ITO-coated glass substrates via ultra-fast spray pyrolysis (1.5-minute deposition at 450°C) using 7 wt% copper chloride dihydrate, and compared with undoped NiO films. XRD confirmed the cubic NiO (111) phase; Cu doping shifted the peak from 37.2° to 37.0°, increased the lattice parameter from 4.18 to 4.20 Å, and reduced crystallite size from 21 to 20 nm, attributed to the larger ionic radius of Cu²⁺ relative to Ni²⁺. SEM showed well-dispersed cuboidal/polyhedral grains with homogeneous coverage. UV-Vis analysis revealed enhanced visible-light absorption and a bandgap reduction from 3.70 to 3.65 eV after doping. Raman spectra showed disappearance of the TO mode and red shifts of the LO and second-order modes, indicating lattice distortion and successful Cu incorporation. PL spectra exhibited emission bands at 564, 700, 749, 808, and 881 nm, with reduced intensity after doping, suggesting non-radiative recombination centers and increased defect density. In I-V measurements under ~1 vol% LPG, current increased for both films; at 5 V, NiO rose from 249 to 327 mA and NiO:Cu from 265 to 480 mA, yielding sensitivities of 1.3 and 1.8, respectively. The results indicate that Cu doping enhances charge transport, surface reactivity, and LPG sensitivity, making NiO:Cu a promising low-cost material for gas sensing applications.

This passage documents the AMD AGESA™ software interfaces and build process. It describes PPIs published after AmdInitEarly and AmdInitPost, a memory information HOB, PEIMs that initialize memory and coordinate reset requests among AMD PEIMs, and DXE drivers that perform late initialization, generate data tables (published via AgesaDxeProtocol), and control VGA resource decoding. It covers reference files in the \Addendum directory, UEFI build control files, required environment variables (AGESA_ROOT, AGESA_OptsDir), and integration steps including Cache-As-Ram setup. Two build methods are described: binary modules (indirect) and source integration. Stack procedures, provided as native assembly macros, establish and remove the pre-memory Cache-As-RAM stack, with defined register usage, dependencies, and status codes. Entry procedures are listed in time point order: AmdInitReset (minimal post-reset initialization with execution cache allocation rules), AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost (system memory initialization), AmdInitEnv, AmdInitMid, AmdInitLate (generates ACPI and DMI tables), AmdInitRtb, AmdS3Save, and the resume procedures AmdInitResume, AmdLateRestore, and AmdInitRecovery. Service procedures include AmdCreateStruct/AmdReleaseStruct for parameter block storage, plus routines returning data eye results, APIC and PCI addresses, execution cache size, current core identification, memory FRU location, MMIO mapping, and event log entries. Required host environment call-outs include AgesaAllocateBuffer, AgesaDeallocateBuffer, AgesaDoReset, AgesaLocateBuffer, AgesaReadSpd, and AP task execution functions.

The improvement of farmers' conditions requires broad education that produces good citizens rather than merely scholars, training executive powers and instilling dignity of labor. Scientists at Oregon Health & Science University have been working for four years to create functional human eggs in the lab. In 2022, the team led by Mitalipov reported the birth of three healthy mouse pups from lab-created eggs using DNA from adult mice skin cells. However, a new paper published in Nature Communications revealed that applying this technique to human cells has been mostly unsuccessful so far. The team did make some progress, including developing a chromosome-reduction process called "mitomeiosis," which is necessary to prevent embryos from having double the normal chromosome count. Mitalipov acknowledged the technology requires refinement before clinical testing but remains optimistic, stating "We will figure it out. We know it can be done." If successful, the research could help treat infertility, prevent heritable diseases, and enable same-sex couples to have genetically related children.

A new study suggests the brain chemical dopamine plays a role in developing a healthy mother-child bond, potentially motivating mothers to provide better care. Researchers studied 19 mothers and their babies, video-recording interactions and performing brain scans while mothers watched videos of their own or other babies. Mothers secreted more dopamine when watching their own babies, and those who secreted more dopamine were more likely to provide optimal care and be sensitive to their infants' needs. Less responsive mothers secreted less dopamine. The researchers suggest responsive caregiving supports infant brain development, and that dopamine's role may continue throughout the lifespan and in other close relationships. Published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, the study is small, and it cannot determine whether some mothers are primed for better bonding before their child is born.
