Trauma, defined by SAMHSA as experiences perceived as harmful or threatening with lasting negative effects on mental, physical, social, emotional, or spiritual well-being, influences academic achievement in post-secondary students. An estimated 50% to 70% of students have experienced at least one adverse childhood experience (ACE), and trauma may manifest as attendance challenges, poorer academic performance, lower self-efficacy, isolation, and dropout risk. Healthcare providers and students are at risk of secondary traumatic stress and vicarious trauma through indirect exposure to others' trauma.

Studies of occupational therapy (OT) students found that trauma affected daily routines, including rest, social participation, and education, though many students avoided disclosing trauma due to fear of stigma.

This paper used a literature review of peer-reviewed sources (2015–present) to describe the trauma-informed care (TIC) framework in health professions education (HPE), provide an overview of TIC models and practices, and discuss strategies for OT educators. SAMHSA's TIC framework comprises six core principles and ten implementation domains, including governance, training, physical environment, screening, and policy. Implementation in higher education requires engagement of institutional leadership, faculty, staff, and students. Research indicates health educators may have limited awareness of trauma-informed strategies, and validated tools such as the ARTIC-35 Scale can assess faculty attitudes.

TIC models include the PATH simulation-based training, which increased knowledge and self-efficacy among physical therapy and OT students, and health and wellness coaching. Validated TIC competencies exist for medical education, but OT curricula lag behind; only 12 of 82 surveyed OT programs reported trauma education. Recommended strategies include trauma-informed professional development, advance notice of potentially triggering content, self-care modules, peer support networks, transparent communication, and culturally responsive practices.

The paper concludes that trauma-informed practices in OT education may mitigate trauma's effects on learning, with potential short-term outcomes including student support and engagement, and long-term outcomes including increased retention and graduation rates.

Robert Stuart has spent nearly two years investigating alleged fabrications in the BBC Panorama documentary "Saving Syria's Children," which was based on footage following a claimed incendiary bomb attack on the Urm al-Kubra school near Aleppo on August 29, 2013, as the UK Parliament prepared to vote on military action. On June 11, Stuart released a PDF presentation highlighting concerns: medical professionals questioning the injuries shown in BBC footage, inconsistent victim counts (Dr Ahsan citing 25 then 40, Ian Pannell 30, and the Hand in Hand For Syria website 50), and timeline discrepancies placing the attack up to six hours apart. The passage also examines Dr Saleyah Ahsan's British Army background and Dr Rola Hallam's charity ties, including her father's disputed connection to the Syrian National Council. It concludes that evidence of fakery is "undeniable" and questions how such narratives might relate to possible future events.

This study models the global risk posed by pfhrp2/3 gene deletions in *P. falciparum*, which cause false-negative results on HRP2-based malaria rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs). Deletions have been reported in 40 of 47 surveyed countries, with false-negative rates reaching 80% in the worst-affected settings. Using an individual-based mathematical transmission model parameterized with data on malaria prevalence, diagnostic practices, treatment-seeking, RDT usage, HRP3 cross-reactivity, and fitness costs, the authors estimate that malaria prevalence is the most important driver of selection for pfhrp2 deletions, with faster selection at low prevalence. Analysis of WHO Malaria Threat Maps data found 63.5% of pfhrp2-deleted samples also had pfhrp3 deletions, indicating positive linkage between the deletions. Model fitting estimated relative fitness of 96.4% for pfhrp2-deleted parasites and a 29.0% probability of positive HRP2-RDT results via HRP3 cross-reactivity. Two risk maps were produced: an Innate Risk Score (susceptibility once deletions are established) and a Prospective Risk Score (projected spread from current prevalence). Most malaria-endemic areas—particularly low-transmission regions, the Horn of Africa, East Africa, and parts of West Africa including Senegal and Mali—are predicted to be at high risk. The maps are intended to guide surveillance and RDT switching decisions.

Researchers replaced the nucleus of a human egg cell with the nucleus of a skin cell (fibroblast) via somatic cell nuclear transfer, then fertilized the egg and added the molecule roscovitine to coax it into expelling half its chromosomes. Some fertilized eggs formed early human embryos, but none had the correct chromosome sets, likely because chromosomes paired randomly instead of with their proper counterparts during division. No embryos were viable or allowed to develop beyond the blastocyst stage. The technique is a proof of concept that could one day help women without eggs or same-sex male couples have genetically related children, but it remains too inefficient and risky for clinical use. Clinical trials are estimated to be at least a decade away and would likely not occur in the United States, which prohibits genetic modification of human embryos. The method also requires donor egg cells.

This lecture discusses protein folding using a mechanical model where protein backbones are treated as fixed-angle chains (fixed edge lengths and angles, with only rotational freedom around edges). Four main problems are explored: (1) Span—finding maximum/minimum distances between endpoints, which is NP-hard for flat configurations but solvable in linear time for orthogonal chains in 3D; (2) Flattening—determining whether a chain has a non-self-intersecting planar configuration, which is NP-hard; (3) Flat state connectivity—whether all flat states belong to one connected component in configuration space, with orthogonal and obtuse chains proven connected but the general case open; and (4) Locked chains—where locked examples exist easily with fixed angles, and it remains open whether equilateral, equiangular, obtuse chains can lock. The lecture concludes with a theorem on producible protein chains: chains generated from a ribosome modeled as a cone have all producible configurations in one connected component, and all flat states are producible and mutually reachable. This provides an algorithm for folding such chains and serves as a candidate model for how nature folds proteins mechanically.

Gas colic, while the least serious form of colic in horses, is very common and can lead to complications such as displacement or twisting of the large colon. Gas is produced normally through fermentation in the hindgut by the microbial population, but colic occurs when gas builds up instead of passing through the large colon. Causes include inadequate forage consumption, stall confinement, stress, ulcers, intestinal inflammation, inadequate exercise, dehydration, and abrupt feed changes. Two widespread practices contribute to gas colic: limiting forage, which disrupts digestion and causes horses to gorge when feed arrives, and confinement, which reduces hindgut motility. Stress increases inflammation, raising colic risk. Feed changes should be gradual—approximately one week for hay and 2 to 3 weeks for new feeds—with prebiotics possibly aiding the transition. Bran mashes, if fed, must be given consistently, not weekly. Helpful supplements include B vitamins, yeast, and colostrum. Reducing inflammatory ingredients like sugar and soy products is recommended. Slow feeders can simulate grazing and help horses self-regulate their intake. The most significant change is making hay available 24 hours a day, as colic is rare among horses grazing on large pastures.

The Michigan Supreme Court decided People v Helzer, in which Richard L. Helzer was convicted of two counts of gross indecency and of being a sexually delinquent person at the time of the offenses. The Court held that sexual delinquency constitutes an alternate sentencing provision rather than a penalty enhancement, tied to a broader statutory rehabilitation scheme and unrelated to proof of the principal charge. Because of the jury's broad function and discretion in the sexual delinquency hearing, the potential for automatic conviction, and the possible life sentence, the Court required a separately empaneled jury to decide the sexual delinquency charge unless the defendant waives a jury trial. A defendant is entitled to 20 peremptory challenges for the second jury, but only the number appropriate to the principal charge's possible sentence for the initial jury. The sexual delinquency charge must be included in the original indictment before trial begins, and no reference to it may be made to the jury deciding the principal charge; discovery of such exposure is grounds for mistrial or reversal. Applying these rulings, the Court found no error in Helzer's trial on the gross indecency charges but remanded for a hearing before a separate jury if the prosecutor pursues the sexual delinquency charge, with the defendant accorded 20 peremptory challenges. The Court declined to consider the defendant's constitutional claims raised on cross-appeal. Chief Justice Kavanagh dissented, reasoning that the sexual delinquency statute is unconstitutionally void for vagueness.

The passage describes the NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture and its key advancements:

**Memory Subsystem:** Turing is the first GPU architecture to use GDDR6 memory, delivering 14 Gbps signaling rates and 20% better power efficiency than GDDR5X. The TU102 includes 6 MB of L2 cache (double the prior generation's 3 MB). Combined with improved lossless memory compression, Turing achieves approximately 50% higher effective bandwidth than Pascal.

**Video and Display:** A new display engine supports 8K at 60 Hz via DisplayPort 1.4a with VESA Display Stream Compression 1.2, native HDR processing, and ITU-R BT.2100 tone mapping. The enhanced NVENC encoder adds H.265 8K encoding at 30 fps with up to 25% bitrate savings for HEVC and 15% for H.264; NVDEC supports HEVC 4:4:4 and VP9 10/12-bit HDR.

**VR Connectivity:** Turing provides hardware support for USB Type-C and VirtualLink, delivering power, display, and data to VR headsets through a single USB-C connector.

**NVLink/SLI:** TU102 and TU104 use NVLink for SLI data transfers instead of MIO/PCIe. TU102 provides two x8 links (100 GB/sec bidirectional); TU104 provides one x8 link (50 GB/sec). Only two-way SLI is supported.

**Ray Tracing:** Dedicated RT Cores within each SM accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, achieving 10+ Giga Rays/Sec versus Pascal's ~1.1 (10x faster). Combined with denoising algorithms, this enables real-time ray tracing through a hybrid rendering model that combines rasterization and ray tracing.

**NGX and AI:** NGX is a deep learning technology stack using Turing Tensor Cores (not functional on earlier architectures). Features include DLSS (Deep Learning Super-Sampling), trained on 64x supersampled reference images, which delivers TAA-comparable quality with roughly half the shading work, plus a DLSS 2X mode, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.

**Shading Innovations:** Mesh Shading introduces Task and Mesh Shader stages with cooperative thread models, eliminating CPU draw call bottlenecks. Variable Rate Shading (VRS) allows per-16x16-pixel shading rate control, enabling Content Adaptive Shading, Motion Adaptive Shading, and Foveated Rendering. Texture Space Shading (TSS) decouples shading from screen-space pixels. Multi-View Rendering (MVR) supports up to four views per pass (32 at API level).

**GPU Variants:** TU104 contains 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and 13.6 billion transistors (used in GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000). TU106 contains 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores, and 10.8 billion transistors, without NVLink/SLI support (used in GeForce RTX 2070). Tesla T4 targets data center inferencing with 2560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores.

**RTX-OPS:** A workload-based metric combining Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations weighted by usage percentages; the RTX 2080 Ti totals 78 RTX-OPS.

The document concludes with an appendix covering ray tracing fundamentals (ray casting, BVH acceleration structures, denoising) and ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, including game examples from Battlefield V and Shadow of the Tomb Raider, followed by standard NVIDIA disclaimers and trademark notices.

Higher wind supply and easing demand curbed prompt European power prices, with German and French day-ahead contracts down 16 and 20 percent respectively. Forwards tracked lower coal prices, and traders cited a bearish outlook, while gas and oil markets saw price gains.

The American Cancer Society has updated its guideline, published in CA: A Cancer Journal for Clinicians, to recommend colorectal cancer screening begin at age 45 for average-risk adults, citing rising incidence in younger populations and modeling showing a favorable benefit-to-burden balance. Adults 45 and older should undergo regular screening with a high-sensitivity stool-based test or a structural (visual) exam; the new starting age is a "qualified recommendation" due to limited direct evidence for ages 45-49, while screening at 50 and older is a "strong recommendation." Positive non-colonoscopy tests require timely follow-up colonoscopy. Screening should continue through age 75 for healthy adults, be individualized for ages 76-85, and discouraged after 85. Recommended options include annual FIT or HSgFOBT, stool DNA testing every three years, colonoscopy every ten years, and CT colonography or flexible sigmoidoscopy every five years, with no prioritization among tests. Incidence has declined in adults 55 and older but rose 51% among those under 50 since 1994, with death rates also rising. Adults born around 1990 have twice the colon cancer risk and four times the rectal cancer risk of those born around 1950. The earlier starting age is expected to benefit blacks, Alaska Natives, and American Indians as well as average-risk individuals.

This passage introduces tensor network methods for modelling quantum spin dynamics in radical pair systems, which consist of two unpaired electrons interacting with surrounding nuclear spins under external magnetic fields of arbitrary orientation and strength. Such systems are relevant to quantum computing, spintronics, organic semiconductors, molecular qubits, and the magnetic compass of migratory birds. Three main computational challenges are identified: (i) nuclear spins begin in randomly oriented mixed states requiring ensemble averaging, (ii) Hilbert and Liouville space dimensionality grows exponentially with the number of hyperfine-coupled nuclei, and (iii) relaxation processes occur on 1 ns to 1 µs timescales, demanding stable long-time propagation. Existing approaches include Monte Carlo sampling, stochastic Schrödinger equations, classical vector treatments of nuclear spins, and Markovian methods such as the Haberkorn model and Bloch-Redfield-Wangsness theory. The stated purpose of the work is threefold: to introduce tensor-network methods to spin chemistry, to present the radical-pair problem to the physics community, and to showcase avian magnetoreception. The radical pair Hamiltonian comprises Zeeman, hyperfine, exchange, dipolar, and Haberkorn relaxation terms. Three tensor network methods are presented: stochastic matrix product states (MPS) employing spin-coherent state sampling, and matrix product density operator (MPDO) formalism in two realisations—directly vectorised MPDO (vMPDO) and locally purified MPS (LPMPS)—which permit deterministic evaluation without stochastic sampling. MPS reduces wavefunction elements from O(d^N) to O(Ndm²), while MPDO reduces density operator elements to O(Nd²χ²).

Terry Rozier scored a career-high 31 points with seven rebounds in his second career start, and Jayson Tatum added a career-high 27 as the short-handed Boston Celtics beat the Atlanta Hawks 119-110. Rozier started in place of Kyrie Irving, who sat with a right quad contusion and is day-to-day. Jaylen Brown scored 19 and Al Horford had 17 points with seven assists as Boston won for the fourth time in five games. Taurean Prince had a career-high 31 points and Dennis Schroder added 25 for Atlanta, which has lost five of six. Trailing at halftime, Boston outscored the Hawks 41-20 in the third quarter to take a 19-point lead into the fourth. Only 10 Celtics players suited up due to injuries.

President-elect Trump tweeted on January 2, 2017 that CNN's book "Unprecedented: The Election That Changed Everything" used "the worst cover photo" of him, though he hoped the book would do well. The photo shows Trump pointing, and a different cover appears on CNN's 2017 commemorative edition. The tweet drew responses including awkward photos of Trump and comments calling him vain or saying he should focus on more important matters. The tweet added to recent Twitter buzz surrounding Trump, including the brief appearance of the "Emergency Kittens" account among those he followed on January 1, and a tweet claiming he knew he would win more than the required 270 electoral votes (306) when Clinton's camp canceled its fireworks celebration. Trump also retweeted a photo montage from Ivanka Trump expressing appreciation for the events of 2016.

Sources say the Bank of Japan will not rush to exit its ultra-loose monetary policy despite solid economic growth, citing the risk of a sharp yen appreciation and stubbornly low inflation. The weak yen is viewed as a key accomplishment of its stimulus, and policymakers fear that signaling normalization could trigger a yen spike that would hurt the export-reliant economy and draw political pressure. Any rise in yield targets, possibly next year, would likely be a modest, one-off move rather than the start of a rate-hike cycle, since inflation at 0.8 percent is expected to slow unless firms raise wages. An April leadership change, with candidates including easing advocate Etsuro Honda, further complicates the outlook. Analysts say adjusting policy could preserve tools against shocks; otherwise the BOJ may need to deepen negative rates or bankroll government debt.

A cave rescuer with over 30 years of experience calls the Thai rescue of 12 boys and their soccer coach—found alive after nine days in the flooded Tham Luang Nang Non cave—one of the toughest he has seen. The basic tenet of flood rescue is to wait: if the trapped are alive and safe, taking risks endangers rescuers unnecessarily; if they have perished, there is no reason to take risks. Surface efforts include monitoring water and weather, diverting or pumping water, and searching for other entrances. This case is unusual: the group was found 1.2 miles inside, monsoon rains may keep the water up for months, and the cave's mid-70s temperature likely spared them hypothermia. After nine days without food, they are weak and must be fed gradually. Three exit options exist: diving them out (the most dangerous, requiring skills that take hundreds of hours to learn), drilling an entrance (equipment-intensive and imprecise), or finding a new entrance (unsuccessful after 10 days). If their location is safe from flooding and divers can supply food and care, they can stay indefinitely; otherwise, diving out may be the only option. Rescuers face pressure and potential blame if all are not safely out.

The Arizona Supreme Court held that A.R.S. § 13-4033(B) bars a defendant from directly appealing a contested post-judgment restitution order entered pursuant to a plea agreement that contemplated payment of restitution up to a capped amount; appellate review must instead be obtained through Rule 32 post-conviction relief proceedings. Frank Hoffman pleaded no contest to DUI and agreed to pay restitution up to $53,653.45; after a contested hearing, the court ordered him to pay $40,933.45, and his direct appeal was dismissed. The court reasoned that such a restitution order is part of the defendant's "sentence" because this construction furthers the legislature's goal of eliminating direct appeals involving plea agreements, avoids a burdensome dual-track system of appellate review, and reflects that restitution is mandatory and typically imposed at sentencing. The court disapproved State v. Foy and State v. Unkefer to the extent they conflicted, rejected Hoffman's remaining arguments, and affirmed the superior court's dismissal of his appeal.

This preprint describes a blood-based, non-invasive test for detecting glial malignancies (GLI-M) by identifying circulating glial cells (CGCs) in peripheral blood. The method uses a CTC enrichment medium that selectively induces apoptosis in non-malignant cells, followed by immunocytochemistry profiling for co-expression of GFAP and OLIG2. Analytical validation demonstrated sample stability for up to 48 hours at 2°C-8°C, a limit of detection of 1 cell/5 mL, and analytical sensitivity of 92.5% (GFAP) and 95.0% (OLIG2). Clinical validation across two case-control studies and two prospective studies showed sensitivity ranging from 92.9% to 100% and specificity of 100% for detecting GLI-M and differentiating it from benign brain tumors, epithelial malignancies with brain metastases, non-glial CNS malignancies, and healthy individuals. Fluorescence in situ hybridization of EGFR amplification showed 100% concordance between CGCs and matched tumor tissue. The test, performed on 5 mL venous blood, detects subtypes accounting for approximately 97% of GLI-M, but does not detect rarer subtypes such as CNS lymphoma and gliosarcoma, and does not differentiate subtype or grade. The study was funded by Datar Cancer Genetics Private Limited, which employs several authors.

U.S. stock futures rose modestly ahead of the Federal Reserve's rate decision, with economists expecting a hike to 1–1.25% and focus on Fed Chair Janet Yellen's commentary. Dow futures gained 0.12%, Nasdaq-100 0.16%, and S&P 500 0.06%. Tuesday's options volume was average: 13.8 million calls and 12.2 million puts. Apple CEO Tim Cook confirmed autonomous car plans; AAPL gained nearly 1% with over 1.1 million options contracts traded. Tesla options rose on positive reports, and Micron rebounded after a bullish Macquarie note.

Apple Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended December 25, 2021 reports total net sales of $123.9 billion, an 11% increase from $111.4 billion in the prior-year quarter, driven primarily by iPhone, Services and Mac. Net income was $34.6 billion ($2.10 diluted EPS) versus $28.8 billion ($1.68) a year earlier. By category, iPhone sales rose 9% to $71.6 billion, Mac rose 25% to $10.9 billion, iPad fell 14% to $7.2 billion, Wearables, Home and Accessories rose 13% to $14.7 billion, and Services rose 24% to $19.5 billion. All geographic segments grew except Japan, which declined 14%. Total gross margin was 43.8% versus 39.8%. The Company repurchased $20.4 billion of common stock (124 million shares) and paid $3.7 billion in dividends; $40.5 billion remained under its $315 billion repurchase authorization. Operating cash flow was $47.0 billion, and total assets were $381.2 billion. New products included 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro models, third-generation AirPods, and Apple Watch Series 7. The Company noted ongoing COVID-19 effects, including remote work and supply shortages. In the Epic Games litigation, the district court ruled in Apple's favor on nine of ten counts; both parties appealed. Management concluded disclosure controls were effective, with no material changes to risk factors or internal controls.

Carleton University in Ottawa is hiring a professor to establish a research and teaching program in the "conjuring arts," named after Allan Slaight, with Carleton matching a $2 million grant from The Slaight Family Foundation. Interim president Alastair Summerlee said the timing is opportune given widespread deception, such as fake news, and the role will explore why people are good at deceiving and being deceived. About 80 applicants have applied, with an announcement expected this summer. The position is a five-year renewable term with possible tenure. A University of London study of 120 people found that 87% solved a card trick when no fake swipe was performed, versus 60% when an empty hand was shown, suggesting people become stuck on initial solutions.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC dated July 31, 2018, reporting that it issued a press release and related data sheet regarding its financial results for the third fiscal quarter ended June 30, 2018. The press release and data sheet are attached as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2. The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Devils players Adam Henrique and Travis Zajac discussed their game against the Kings, noting they knew coming in that the Kings were a big, physical, deep team with puck-moving defensemen and strong goaltending. They admitted being nervous and tentative in the first period, throwing pucks away and failing to execute, but remained encouraged that they stayed competitive despite not playing their best. They expect the physical play to continue throughout the series and emphasized the need to improve execution, get pucks behind the defense, and generate offense through cycles and net-front traffic.

U.S. stocks rallied after President Trump's Nov. 8 election on hopes for tax cuts, infrastructure spending and deregulation, but enacting these proposals has proved difficult and some early winners have faded. Hospital stocks fell 7.1 percent from the election to the inauguration on fears of an Obamacare repeal, then gained 4.1 percent as passing healthcare legislation proved complicated. Infrastructure stocks rose 13 percent and then 2.4 percent, though gains leveled off as no package has materialized. Bank stocks rose 20.8 percent and then 3.1 percent, with concerns emerging about slowing loan growth and doubts about deregulation. Small-cap stocks, a tax-cut barometer, rose 12.6 percent and then 5.3 percent; tax-cut optimism persists, but Trump's legislative struggles and international distractions have raised doubts.

Former U.S. senator and Anchorage mayor Mark Begich's entry into Alaska's governor's race has raised concerns among some Democrats and independents that he and independent Gov. Bill Walker could split the vote, handing the election to Republicans. The race is shaping up as a three-way contest between Begich, Walker, and the eventual Republican nominee, with former state Sen. Mike Dunleavy seen as an early GOP favorite ahead of the Aug. 21 primary. In 2014, Walker and Democrat Byron Mallott formed a unity ticket that won; after Begich's entry became apparent, Walker and Mallott chose to skip the primaries and gather signatures to go directly to the general election. The Democratic party is backing Begich, and its executive director dismissed concerns that his candidacy hurts their chances. Begich criticizes Walker's budget leadership, while Dunleavy has attacked Walker over halving the oil-wealth fund dividend in 2016. Begich supports placing a dividend formula in the state constitution. A Libertarian candidate, William "Billy" Toien, is also running.

A hockey player credits his father Patrick Kane's years of support and Buffalo's growing hockey scene. Comfortable as both a disher and finisher, he is flexible about position and cites coaches Don Harkins, John Hines, Dale Hunter, and Dave Gagner. He chose the OHL over college and hopes to bring Buffalo a cup.

Dr. Howard W. Ellzey, a Memphis physician, was convicted of conspiracy and eleven substantive counts for illegally distributing controlled substances, receiving concurrent three-year terms and $18,000 in fines. About half his patients were "diet patients" paying $15 cash for brief visits yielding B-12 injections and amphetamine prescriptions, usually Preludin. He ran two offices with separate records, letting patients obtain two prescriptions in one day. A DEA survey found 29,000 of 39,000 schedule II prescriptions at six Memphis drugstores were his, nearly all for amphetamines. The court found substantial evidence supported the convictions and no error in evidentiary rulings, the indictment, instructions, or voir dire. Affirmed.

This article presents a weekly roundup of discounted iOS and Android games. Listed titles include A Good Snowman is Hard to Build (£2.99/$2.99), Ace Attorney (free, iOS), Assassin's Creed Identity (99p/99c), Kensho (£1.99/$1.99, iOS), Royal Trouble (£1.99/$1.99 or cheaper), Runic Rampage (£2.19/$2.49, Android), Spite & Malice HD (free, iOS), and Warhammer 40,000 (£4.99/$4.99, iOS). Each game receives a brief description, and the article notes the deal list may change throughout the week.

This is the November 23, 2001 daily edition of Energy Central Direct, an energy industry e-mail newsletter sent to Enron employee Paul D. Thomas. It compiles electric power and gas industry news headlines with brief summaries. Top stories include Los Angeles retaining its partnership in a Nevada power plant, E.ON planning U.S. acquisitions, federal regulators ruling that Southern Co. can no longer charge unregulated rates for some wholesale electricity sales, and FERC planning a workshop to expedite hydro relicensing. Coverage spans California's power crisis (including FERC orders on grid data sharing and PG&E bankruptcy developments), deregulation debates, and mergers and acquisitions—notably Dynegy seeking to speed up its Enron acquisition, Enron's continued financial decline and stock losses, and WestLB's talks to buy Wessex Water from Enron. Other sections cover rate changes, new power projects, nuclear and environmental issues, and international news such as Electricite de France becoming Britain's biggest electricity distributor. The newsletter also includes sponsor advertisements, a CAL ISO load forecast, Restructuring Today headlines, and subscription information for the free service.

Ebberston, Mulgrave and Ganton won their respective finals at the first triple-header T20 Cayley Cup Finals Day at North Marine Road. In the Division Two final, Ganton beat Kirkbymoorside by nine wickets, chasing 97-8 with Ian Cousins scoring 40 not out. Mulgrave defeated Sherburn by 28 runs in the Division One final after posting 165-5, with Chris Knight hitting 43, before bowling Sherburn out for 137. In the Premier Division final, Ebberston restricted Filey to 86 all out, with Eddie Swiers taking 4-19, and won by six wickets with Ben Lealman unbeaten on 25. Cups were presented after each match, and thanks were given to umpires, scorers, Scarborough CC and league secretary Simon Dobson.

The author, diagnosed with panic disorder (PD) after a first panic attack at age 19, shares expert-backed techniques for managing panic attacks. Panic attacks differ from "anxiety attacks"—a term not recognized in the DSM-5—and attacks linked to panic disorder occur without an obvious trigger, though anyone can experience one with a clear cause. Recognizing symptoms such as heart palpitations, sweating, shortness of breath, and fear of dying is helpful, though a physical exam is advised to rule out other conditions. Recommended coping strategies include writing down reassuring facts and positive mantras (panic attacks are not life-threatening), visualizing panic as a passing wave that typically peaks within 10 minutes, using smartphone games or relaxation apps as distractions, and practicing slow, deep breathing daily so it can be used during an attack to slow the heart rate and calm down.

The passage describes the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere architecture. The A100 includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory delivering 1555 GB/sec bandwidth (1.7x higher than Tesla V100), protected by SECDED ECC, and a 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x larger than V100) divided into two partitions, providing 2.3x the L2 bandwidth of V100. Compute Data Compression offers up to 4x improvement in DRAM read/write bandwidth, up to 4x in L2 read bandwidth, and up to 2x in L2 capacity.

The A100's third-generation Tensor Cores, across 108 SMs (versus 80 in V100), deliver 16x peak mixed-precision performance compared to standard FP32 FMA operations. Improvements include data sharing across all 32 warp threads, a new asynchronous copy instruction that bypasses the register file, and increased shared memory allocation, enabling strong scaling for deep learning workloads.

The Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) feature partitions the A100 into up to seven GPU Instances with dedicated and isolated compute and memory resources, providing quality of service and fault isolation for multi-tenant environments. GPU Instances are constructed from GPU slices and can be subdivided into Compute Instances; vGPU migration between instances is supported.

Third-generation NVLink provides twelve links with 600 GB/sec total bandwidth (versus 300 GB/sec for V100). The A100 also supports PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, improved error detection, isolation, and containment, hardware JPEG decoding (NVJPG), an Optical Flow Accelerator, improved atomic operation throughput, and five NVDEC units.

CUDA 11 advances include task graph acceleration, asynchronous copy operations, asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls, and enhanced Cooperative Groups. The DGX A100 system combines eight A100 GPUs connected via NVSwitch, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS, with MIG providing up to 56 isolated accelerators. An appendix explains fine-grained structured sparsity (2:4), which prunes neural networks to increase throughput, reduce memory bandwidth usage, and lower latency with virtually no accuracy loss.

This study used the 2019 National Survey of Early Care and Education (NSECE) Household Survey to identify child care and early education (CCEE) search types. Using latent class analysis (LCA) on data from 1,190 households that searched for care for a focal child under age 6 within the past 24 months and considered more than one provider, the analysis examined five potential information sources: friends and family with children, known providers, social media, internet search tools, and CCR&R agencies or local organizations. Families reported up to two sources; about half used one source and half used two.

Five search types emerged: Type 1 (CCR&R or friends/family, N=101), Type 2 (internet search or social media, N=323), Type 3 (known providers or friends/family, N=104), Type 4 (social media or friends/family, N=243), and Type 5 (friends/family or internet search, N=419). Friends and family was the most commonly used source, followed by internet search.

Multinomial logistic regression analyses found search types varied in three ways: (1) whether families sought information about type of care, (2) whether the child had a condition affecting care provision—Types 1 and 3 were more likely to involve such children (19% each versus 5–10% in other types), and (3) geographic region—Type 5 was more likely in the Northeast and Type 3 more likely in the West. No relationships were found between search type and other child or family characteristics.

Limitations include the recording of only the first two sources mentioned and an analytic sample that was higher-income, more likely two-parent with both parents working, and more likely English-speaking than the overall household population. The authors conclude that search types were more similar than different across family and child characteristics, suggesting the sources families use may matter more than search content or family traits, and recommend future research on interactions between sources.

This MIT web security lecture demonstrates the Shellshock bug, in which attacker-controlled HTTP headers are set as Bash environment variables, allowing arbitrary command execution, and cross-site scripting (XSS), where untrusted input printed directly into HTML executes as JavaScript, sometimes bypassing browser filters through malformed markup. XSS defenses discussed include browser filters (incomplete heuristics), HTTP-only cookies (still vulnerable to CSRF), privilege separation using separate domains for untrusted content, content sanitization (e.g., Django's HTML entity encoding, which can fail due to complex HTML/CSS/JavaScript grammars), less expressive languages like Markdown, and Content Security Policy, which restricts content sources and blocks inline JavaScript and eval. The X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header prevents content-type sniffing. SQL injection occurs when untrusted input enters database queries; the remedy is rigorous escaping, which frameworks like Django provide. Untrusted path names can enable directory traversal. For session management, cookies containing session IDs are sensitive and should not be shared across untrusted subdomains; alternatives include stateless cookies authenticated with Message Authentication Codes (as used by AWS), DOM storage, and client-side certificates, each with limitations such as key storage, revocation, and usability issues. Protocol vulnerabilities include inconsistent URL parsing between components (e.g., Flash versus browsers) and the GIFAR attack, which embeds a JAR file inside a GIF so an applet runs with a victim site's authority when combined with XSS. Finally, covert channel attacks exploit timing to infer browsing history: link-color sniffing (mitigated by browsers lying to JavaScript), cache timing, DNS timing, and rendering-based attacks.

Eagles wide receiver A.J. Brown has exceeded 30 receiving yards only once this season—a 109-yard, one-touchdown performance in a victory—and is frustrated by his limited targets. Speaking Wednesday, he said he wants the ball to spark the offense and in clutch moments, not for personal stats. DeVonta Smith also hasn't topped 60 yards in a game. Despite a 4-0 record, coordinator Kevin Patullo must find ways to involve both receivers.

UK scientists found bumblebee queens exposed to the neonicotinoid pesticide thiamethoxam were 26 percent less likely to lay eggs. Researchers at Royal Holloway University of London say this could cause wild bumblebee populations to decline and die out, though other threats like limited nutrition and parasites may also matter. The findings may strengthen calls for restrictions; the EU's 2013 moratorium may become permanent, which pesticide companies and some farmers oppose, citing lower canola yields and increased spraying.

Students at Swarthmore often take themselves too seriously, stressing over grades, internships, and appearing flawless. The author argues that while high expectations are appropriate, making mistakes is acceptable and laughing at oneself can help students cope, since campus mishaps are not life or death and people often learn more from mistakes than successes. The passage also urges students to give others a break, assume good intent when peers misspeak, and forgive mistakes. Though laughter won't solve everything, it serves as a useful defense mechanism that makes people feel better.

A Spring Valley woman is San Diego County's first confirmed West Nile Virus case this year. California has reported 231 illnesses and 12 deaths this year. County officials urge residents to use insect repellent, wear protective clothing, and remove standing water to prevent mosquito breeding.

The lecture opens with notes on problem set 8: problem 8.2 lacks sufficient background to attempt, and 8.3 (a BCJR decoding exercise) is deferred since the BCJR algorithm was not covered.

The main topic completes Chapter 11 with Hadamard transform realizations of Reed-Muller codes. The Hadamard transform over F2 uses the universal matrix Um, an m-fold tensor product of the 2x2 matrix u1; Um is self-inverse, so the inverse transform is the transform itself. Reed-Muller codes are generated by rows of Um, and row weights relate to the Hamming weights of the binary expansions of row indices. A graphical realization is built recursively from simple 2x2 blocks (controlled NOT gates), resembling fast Fourier transform butterflies. For the 8,4,4 code, reductions produce a "reduced Hadamard transform" realization using only binary variables and simple constraints (3,2,2 and 3,1,1 types), but it contains cycles. Agglomeration yields a cycle-free realization equivalent to a two-section trellis, which is more complex (higher state and branch complexity) but permits exact decoding. The trade-off is that cyclic representations are simpler but decoding is slightly suboptimal, while cycle-free ones meet the cut-set bound. A four-section agglomerated realization is described as the simplest known cycle-free realization of Reed-Muller codes, closely related to the Golay code realization. The appendix discusses alternative graphical model styles: factor graphs, Markov graphs, and Bayesian networks.

The lecture then introduces Chapter 12's sum-product algorithm for a posteriori probability (APP) decoding. APP decoding computes the probability of each variable given the received sequence and minimizes bit error probability, unlike sequence decoding, which minimizes word error probability; soft outputs are useful for decoding composite codes such as turbo codes. The APP computation reduces to a sum of products, decomposable into intrinsic and extrinsic information. On cycle-free graphs, the algorithm uses a past/future decomposition and the Cartesian product lemma, giving exact APP decoding in finite time (the BCJR algorithm on trellises). On graphs with cycles, it becomes iterative and approximate, requiring stopping criteria; designing graphs with large girth mitigates degradation from short cycles.

Asian equities turned cautious after the US Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points for the second time this year and detailed plans to unwind its balance sheet. The Nikkei fell 0.6 percent, the Kospi declined 0.75 percent, and Australia's S&P/ASX 200 dropped 1.13 percent, while mainland Chinese markets edged higher. Markets viewed the hike as dovish, with analysts skeptical of the Fed's forecast of three rate hikes this year. Toshiba shares fell 2.68 percent amid legal action by Western Digital subsidiaries. Oil prices hit a seven-month low, and the dollar index traded below 97. Australian jobs data beat expectations, while New Zealand's GDP missed forecasts. Wall Street closed mixed, with the Dow gaining 0.22 percent.

This study developed a deep learning model to predict disease duration (DD) from structural brain MRI in people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS), using data from 4,392 patients across 15 European centres. The resulting "brain-predicted DD gap"—the error in predicting DD—was proposed as a measure of MS-specific brain damage, complementing the brain-age gap (BAG), which captures deviation from healthy brain ageing. MS patients showed older-appearing brains (mean BAG: 7.81 years). The DD gap was largely independent of BAG (r = 0.06) and explained more variance in DD than total lesion or thalamic volumes. Both BAG and DD gap were positively associated with disability (EDSS), and the DD gap added significant explanatory value over BAG alone. In a longitudinal early-MS cohort (252 patients, mean follow-up 4.5 years), annualised DD gap changes correlated with EDSS worsening and added to BAG change in explaining disability progression. An alternative "MS-age" model was accurate but correlated with BAG and did not significantly improve model fit. The authors conclude the DD gap is a clinically meaningful, disease-specific biomarker of MS brain damage and progression, while noting limitations including the noisy nature of DD estimates, potential confounding by disease-modifying treatment, and DD-dependence bias in gap values.

The paper uses the Situation Calculus—a logical language for specifying and reasoning about dynamical systems in AI—to model a taxonomy of obligations via non-Markovian theories. Reiter's successor state axioms solve the frame problem for actions affecting the external world, but rely on the Markov property, whereby action preconditions and effects depend only on the current situation. Gabaldon extended this to non-Markovian settings where past situations may matter, appropriate for domains such as database transactions, dynamic integrity constraints, and smart contracts. Scherl and Levesque extended Reiter's solution to knowledge-producing actions, and subsequent work extended it to obligations. The paper applies the obligation account of [37] to formalize the obligation taxonomy of [31].

The sequential temporal Situation Calculus is a many-sorted second-order logic with sorts for actions, situations, time, and objects. Situations are finite action sequences; fluents change across situations. Domain axiomatizations comprise action precondition axioms, successor state axioms, unique name axioms for actions, and initial situation axioms, together with foundational axioms. Non-Markovian basic action theories permit preconditions and effects to refer to past situations through bounded formulas, and regression has been generalized accordingly.

A running example of a door-opening domain illustrates actions (unlock, lock, pressButton, moveTo, notify), fluents (open, locked, notifiedManager, at), and corresponding precondition and successor state axioms.

Regarding obligations, Demolombe and Herzig first formulated deontic logic in the Situation Calculus using a fluent O(s′, s) for deontic accessibility. Building on this, [37] combines deontic modalities with time, accounts for actions that produce obligations, and extends regression. Obligations are expressed as Oblg(φ, s) ≡ (∀s′).O(s′, s) ⊃ φ[s′], based on the Kripke semantics condition (C.O+). The paper outlines subsequent sections covering formalization of obligation types, their properties, violation and compensation, related work, and conclusions.

Five years after archaeologists confirmed that a skeleton found beneath a Leicester car park was that of Richard III, the discovery changed the lives of several people. Dominic Smee, who has the same type of scoliosis as the king, underwent combat and riding training for a Channel 4 documentary and gained lasting confidence from the experience. Michael Ibsen, a cabinet-maker descended from Richard's sister Anne, provided a DNA sample that helped confirm the remains and was later asked to make the king's coffin. Mike Mistry, the car park attendant who had worked above the grave for over 15 years and painted the "R" marking the spot, met visitors from around the world but was made redundant in 2016. Musician Ian Churchward's band, The Legendary Ten Seconds, went on to produce multiple Richard III folk-rock albums after the discovery inspired him.

The TPS7H500x-SP series are radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge, with switching frequencies up to 2 MHz for GaN-based designs.

Duty cycle is configurable via the DCL pin: 100% (DCL to VLDO), 75% (floating), or 50% (DCL to AVSS, supported only on TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP); the TPS7H5004-SP supports only 50%. The CS_ILIM pin senses primary-side current for PWM generation and overcurrent protection, with a 1.05-V threshold triggering hiccup mode. The CHICC capacitor sets cycle-by-cycle delay and hiccup restart timing (minimum 3.3 nF recommended). The FAULT pin enables external protections; exceeding 0.6 V for 0.4–1.4 µs causes shutdown, with soft-start restarting after a delay of approximately 15 switching cycles. Slope compensation, set via the RSC pin, mitigates subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle; the minimum is 0.5× the inductor falling current slope, with 1× recommended. Type 2A or 2B frequency compensation can be used with the transconductance error amplifier. Thermal shutdown occurs at 175°C junction temperature, with restart below 160°C.

A design example demonstrates a 500-kHz synchronous push-pull converter using GaN FETs, covering component selection: feedback divider (10 kΩ/1.4 kΩ), 25-ns dead time, leading edge blank time, soft-start capacitor (33 nF, ~7.5 ms), transformer (2.5:1 turns ratio, 40-µH primary inductance), FET voltage ratings, RCD clamp, 0.47-µH output inductor, ~2.3-mF output capacitance including single-event transient mitigation, 7.5-Ω current sense resistor, hiccup capacitor, and compensation components.

The controllers operate from a 4–14 V input supply with required bypassing. Layout guidelines address feedback trace routing, switch-node minimization, ground separation, trace widths, bypass capacitor placement, and routing of noise-sensitive signals. The document also lists related documentation, revision history, and mechanical/packaging information.

The number of registered independents in California has surpassed registered Republicans, which the author argues reflects declining partisan affiliation rather than a cure for partisanship. California's top-two primary system, adopted in 2012, was intended to reduce extremism, but the author contends primaries reveal rather than cause polarization, and predicts unaffiliated voters may soon outnumber Democrats, producing a more fragmented, factional politics. A Quinnipiac poll shows Sen. Ted Cruz leading Rep. Beto O'Rourke 50-39 percent in the Texas Senate race, up from a closer April survey. House Republicans are airing immigration-focused ads while Democrats emphasize health care. Trump plans to appear at a $100,000-a-head fundraiser for the America First Action super PAC. Phoenix Mayor Greg Stanton resigned to run for Congress. Trump continues spy claims despite Rep. Gowdy's assessment that the FBI acted appropriately, and reportedly pressed Sessions to reverse his recusal from the Russia investigation, which Mueller is examining.

Junior County, a top-five shooting guard in the 2026 class, has committed to UConn after taking his final visit there last weekend. The 6-foot-4 combo guard from Wasatch Academy (Utah) is ranked No. 43 overall in the SC Next 100 and No. 4 among shooting guards. He averaged 13.6 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 3.4 assists for the Utah Prospects on the Nike EYBL circuit. County cited his relationship with coach Dan Hurley and the program's intensity as factors in his decision. He is Hurley's first commitment in the 2026 class, following three straight top-10 recruiting classes for the Huskies, who won back-to-back national championships in between.

VentureWire's November 14, 2000 newsletter from Technologic Partners reports private company business news. Top stories include Apax Partners merging its European and Israeli units with a pledge to invest $600 million in Israeli companies over three years; DSL provider New Edge Networks laying off 135 employees; consulting firm KSolutions receiving a $50 million first round from Great Hill Equity Partners; and Cisco acquiring wireless chip firm Radiata for $295 million in stock. The issue lists numerous funding rounds across sectors, including PhotonEx's $80 million second round and StorageApps' $50 million second round. Bad news items cover executive departures at Buzz MSP, the closure of eSociety, and layoffs at iExplore. The newsletter also reports company name changes, acquisitions (including iKnowMed's purchase of CancerSource.com), board appointments, CEO changes, venture capital fund and personnel news, and corrections to prior stories.

Researchers from the Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology and collaborators traced fungal origins to roughly 1.4–0.9 billion years ago, hundreds of millions of years before land plants emerged. Because fungi rarely fossilize well, the team used a novel approach combining the molecular clock with 17 identified horizontal gene transfers between fungal lineages to constrain the timeline. The findings suggest ancient fungi partnered with algae, recycled nutrients, broke down rock, and created primitive soils, acting as ecosystem engineers that prepared Earth's surface for land-based life. This reframes plant colonization of land as occurring in a world already shaped by fungi rather than a barren wasteland.

The passage argues that peace is best served by strength, citing the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis, when American strategic superiority of roughly 8 to 1 led Khrushchev to withdraw Soviet missiles from Cuba. Despite this, US policymakers ignored Soviet declarations of a military buildup, and in 1965 Secretary of Defense McNamara claimed the Soviets accepted strategic inferiority—a self-delusion, since the Soviets now lead in nearly all strategic military categories. The Carter Administration's responses to Soviet actions—a combat brigade in Cuba, the invasion of Afghanistan, and promises to defend the Middle East—are described as weak, inconsistent, and damaging to American credibility, leaving allies confused and adversaries unrespectful. The passage contends that weakness, not firmness, provokes aggression, and calls for restoring the margin of safety through stronger conventional and strategic forces, combating terrorism, consulting allies, and refusing to compromise American principles, with world peace as the reward.

This email compiles news articles from October 19–20, 2001, largely concerning Enron. The Wall Street Journal and Bloomberg reported that Enron CFO Andrew Fastow's partnership, LJM2 Co-Investment LP, realized millions in profits from transactions with Enron, including $7 million in management fees and $4 million in capital increases on a roughly $3 million investment, raising conflict-of-interest concerns. Enron announced a $618 million third-quarter loss, including a $1.01 billion write-off, and its stock fell 9.9% to $29. A shareholder lawsuit alleged the board cost the company at least $35 million by allowing Fastow to manage partnerships that bought Enron assets. TheStreet.com criticized Enron's accounting, noting a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity tied to repurchasing 55 million shares from LJM2-related deals. The New Power Company revised its netting agreement with Enron subsidiaries, reducing required cash collateral through January 4, 2002. A National Journal article ranked Washington lobbying firms by fee income, noting Enron paid Quinn Gillespie $525,000 for lobbying on energy deregulation. The Houston Chronicle reported four Houston business leaders were inducted into the Texas Business Hall of Fame. Dow Jones reported that recession fears, budget cuts, and travel concerns would subdue London Metal Exchange Week, with several firms exiting the metals business, including staff cuts at Enron Metals. The Times of India reported the Bombay High Court would hear Dhabol Power Company's petition challenging the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission's jurisdiction in its dispute with the state electricity board.

United Airlines took subtle jabs at rivals Delta and American while positioning itself as a premium carrier. On its Thursday earnings call, United promised uncrowded airport lounges—a swipe at Delta, whose Sky Clubs have faced long lines and customer complaints. Delta raised lounge pass prices by $150 in 2023, increased guest fees, restricted basic economy access, and is launching a more exclusive club tier at four locations in 2025. United also touted seatback entertainment on over 146,000 seats across 765 airplanes, a jab at American, which installs tablet holders instead of screens on most domestic aircraft to save weight and fuel. United's premium cabin revenue rose about 6% year-over-year in Q3, less than Delta's 9%. United's stock fell more than 7% after earnings beat expectations but revenue missed estimates, though it remains up 34% over the past year.

China's top official in Hong Kong, Zhang Xiaoming, warned that no one would be permitted to use the city to harm national sovereignty, challenge central government authority, or subvert the mainland, amid concerns over an emerging independence movement following the ousting of two pro-independence lawmakers. Many fear Beijing is eroding freedoms guaranteed under the 1997 handover deal. Meanwhile, leader Leung Chun-ying will not seek re-election, and hardliner Regina Ip plans to run.

MusConv is an online software available at MusConv.com that enables users to transfer playlists from Spotify to Amazon Music by selecting a source, playlist, and destination. It offers three subscriptions—Basic, Professional, and Ultimate—differing in features such as CSV export, batch importing, Apple Music support, and free update durations.

A hockey goalie describes his pre-game routine of wearing a hoody and headphones to focus and block out distractions. He credits the team's penalty kills, shot blocking, and prevention of second chances for the win, in which teammate Max scored a key goal. He emphasizes learning from past experiences, including a tough Chicago series, and values the win over individual saves. He plays for himself, teammates, family, and friends, motivated by winning the Stanley Cup, and the team now looks ahead to Monday night's game.

Beijing ordered 15 online real estate portals to remove misleading information, false advertising, and feng shui content by Wednesday to cool the housing market. They may not promise rising returns, help with residence permits or school enrolment, or offer financing advice. Earlier measures raised down payments and banned third-property purchases.

On July 23, 2015, Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC announcing its second quarter 2015 financial results. The filing includes a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures as Exhibit 99.2. The report was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Caring Health Center in Springfield marks National Health Center Week with 50+ Massachusetts health centers and 1,200 nationally. Serving over 20,000 residents, it held Elected Officials Day Monday. The week ends August 19.

Education regulators are reviewing a whistleblower's claim that Ohio's largest online charter school, the Electronic Classroom of Tomorrow (ECOT), intentionally inflated attendance figures tied to state funding using software purchased after earlier attendance-inflation allegations. A former technology employee told the Ohio Department of Education that officials ordered staff to manipulate student data with ActivTrak software, obtained after the state demanded $60 million in overpayments be returned for the 2015-2016 school year. He also shared his claims with Ohio Auditor Dave Yost, whose office included them in an upcoming financial audit. The state previously assessed a $60 million penalty for 2015-2016 and $19 million for 2016-2017. ECOT's lobbyist dismissed the allegations, while two Democratic officials called for a criminal investigation. The Franklin County prosecutor has received no criminal referral.

The Competition and Markets Authority warned that unscrupulous fees charged by care homes to elderly residents may be illegal. Controversial practices include billing residents who died months earlier, charging before admission, threatening eviction, and failing to advertise prices. Self-funding residents, often forced to sell homes to cover bills exceeding £600 weekly, are targeted to offset lower council fees. The CMA may seek new legislation and is bringing a test case to court.

This paper examines blockchain education at 533 AACSB-accredited US business schools. In a March 2024 search, 151 universities (approximately 28%) were found to offer at least one blockchain course, totaling 361 courses.

The paper first outlines that blockchain integration spans enterprise functions including management, finance, supply chain, IT, law, procurement, and sales, and requires technical, social, methodological, and personal competences beyond technical expertise.

Findings show Computer Science (70 courses) and Information Systems (67) departments offer the most courses, though courses also appear in departments such as Biology, Literature, and Political Science. Most courses (72%) are undergraduate-level, 23% graduate-level, and 5% offered at both levels. Private universities offer courses at a higher rate (36%) than public universities (24%), and larger undergraduate populations correlate with course offerings. The Business field accounts for the most courses (216), followed by Computer Science (85) and Law (31). By topic, the largest category is Fundamentals & Overview (140), followed by Digital Assets & Cryptocurrencies (71), Technical Development (66), Business Implications (33), Law and Compliance (29), Supply Chain and Governance (12), and Interplay with Other Technologies (6). AI & Machine Learning is the most referenced emerging technology (30 courses), followed by IoT (18) and NFTs (15).

The authors conclude that blockchain education increasingly intersects with emerging technologies and addresses competences beyond technical skills. Future research should evaluate course topics against industry needs and replicate the study in five years.

In his final Oval Office address, President Clinton thanks Americans for twice electing him and credits them for the nation's progress over eight years, including 22 million new jobs, the lowest unemployment in 30 years, reduced crime and poverty, expanded health coverage for children, better schools, and a cleaner environment. He offers three thoughts for the future: first, maintaining fiscal responsibility, having turned deficits into surpluses and paid down $600 billion of the national debt; second, continuing to lead in an increasingly connected world, where integration brings both opportunity and threats such as terrorism, crime, disease, and global poverty; and third, uniting as "one America" by overcoming differences and treating all people with fairness and dignity. He wishes success to incoming President George W. Bush and his administration. Clinton states he leaves office more idealistic and hopeful than when he arrived, and that while his presidency is ending, he hopes his days of service are not, noting no title will make him prouder than that of citizen.

After his grandfather died of heart disease, seven-year-old Joseph Nyberg created "Heart Cents," collecting pennies and dollars in buckets in Savannah and Richmond Hill for a month. He raised over $200 for St. Joseph's heart patients, which a heart patient's family matched, bringing the total to $422. The money covers costs like transportation and co-pays. Joseph plans to keep fundraising year-round to honor his grandfather, and an anonymous family later donated $250, bringing his total to $672 and 14 cents.

The disclosure relates to noninvasive devices and methods for monitoring a patient's physiological information using multiple data sources. Conventional patient monitors, such as pulse oximeters, typically measure physiological parameters at a single site, and existing stereo pulse oximeters process data from multiple sites independently. The disclosed embodiments combine raw or minimally processed sensor data from optical sensors at multiple measurement sites in a single signal processor to generate a single measurement of a physiological parameter, such as oxygen saturation, pulse rate, perfusion index, methemoglobin, carboxyhemoglobin, total hemoglobin, or glucose. Measurement sites may include cephalic sites (e.g., the nose or earlobe) and peripheral sites (e.g., the finger), which can comprise different types of body tissue. Sensors may include multiple light emitters and multiple photodetectors arranged in a three-dimensional configuration conforming to the contour of the measurement site. This spatial configuration can provide topology information to confirm correct sensor placement and offers a diversity of light path lengths, improving measurement robustness. Combining data from multiple sites can reduce errors and noise associated with a particular sensor and may be more informative of patient well-being than single-site measurements. The signal processor can also independently generate measurements for each site and compare them with the combined measurement.

This patent application, a continuation of several prior applications tracing to a 2015 UK filing, concerns torque sensing in a surgical robotic wrist. The background notes that surgical robots must balance mechanical flexibility, precise and compact positioning, and force measurement. Conventional roll-pitch-roll wrists require very fast joint operation when nearly straight, and can only sense forces perpendicular to the instrument axis via a torque sensor on the pitch joint; sensing forces from other directions requires additional sensors such as strain gauges, increasing weight and power requirements.

The invention provides a surgical robotic component with an articulated terminal portion comprising distal, intermediate, and basal segments. A first articulation connects the distal and intermediate segments, a second connects the intermediate and basal segments, and a third articulation (e.g., a universal or spherical joint) permits relative rotation about third and fourth axes. Torque sensors sense torque about the third and fourth axes, and optionally about the first and second axes. In at least one configuration, the first and second axes are parallel and transverse to the third and fourth axes.

In one embodiment, a robot arm comprises four revolute joints alternating roll and pitch (RPRP) with three shaft sections, terminating in a wrist formed by a base block, an intermediate member, and a head block constituting a universal joint, plus a terminal revolute joint. A surgical instrument with an end effector attaches to the terminal unit; alternatively, the wrist is located within the instrument itself. Torque sensors associated with the wrist joints output to a processor that resolves externally applied torques, enabling force feedback (e.g., haptic) to the surgeon. An alternative arm design uses lateral offsets between joint axes to increase mobility without enlarging the swept volume near the instrument tip.

Stated advantages include a slim, lightweight arm with high mobility, human-like wrist motion facilitating translation of conventional surgical techniques, reduced kinematic singularities, the ability for multiple arms to work closely at a surgical site, and flexibility in positioning robot bases.
In 2023, biochemist Katalin Karikó became one of the few women to win a Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine.

The device requires a minimum of 32 SCLKs for valid write operations. Data read protocols fall into three categories: legacy SPI-compatible protocols with single SDO-x, legacy SPI-compatible protocols with dual SDO-x, and ADC controller clock or source-synchronous (SRC) protocols. Four SPI-compatible protocols exist (SPI-00-S, SPI-01-S, SPI-10-S, SPI-11-S); SPI-00-S is the default after power-up or asynchronous reset. Alternative protocols are selected via SDI_MODE[1:0] in SDI_CTL_REG and SDO_MODE[1:0] = 00b in SDO_CTL_REG. The RVS output remains low during SPI data transfer frames. Short data transfer frames read only required MSB bits from the 32-bit output word; long frames with SDO_CNTL_REG[7:0] = 00h enable daisy-chain operation. Dual SDO mode, enabled by SDO1_CONFIG[1:0] = 11b, launches two bits per SCLK edge, requiring half as many SCLK cycles as single SDO mode.

This passage introduces a book on distributed system patterns, aiming to regularize distributed system design the way common patterns improved object-oriented programming. Although distributed systems span many machines, the book's first section covers single-node patterns because groups of containers co-located on one machine form the atomic elements of distributed system patterns. The passage outlines motivations for splitting single-machine applications into multiple containers: resource isolation (e.g., prioritizing a user-facing service over a best-effort background loader), team scaling through small focused teams owning reusable modules (e.g., a Git sync tool), and separation of concerns, which enables easier testing, updating, and deployment with fewer dependencies and more reliable rollouts. The single-node patterns assume tight dependencies: containers are reliably coscheduled on one machine and may share volumes, filesystems, network namespaces, and shared memory—a grouping called a pod in Kubernetes.

According to the CoreLogic Home Price Index, house prices rose 8.3 percent in Los Angeles County, 8.2 percent in Riverside and San Bernardino counties, and 6.2 percent in Orange County in the 12 months ending in May. Nationally, prices rose 7.1 percent; California's rose 8.9 percent. CoreLogic attributes rising prices to a lean housing supply, noting many homeowners are keeping low-rate mortgages rather than selling.

Kesha tweeted support for Taylor Swift after a judge threw out former DJ David Mueller's lawsuit accusing Swift of fabricating a 2014 groping claim; Swift's $1 countersuit remains. In 2016, Swift donated $250,000 to Kesha during her legal battle with Dr. Luke, whom she accused of abuse; he denied the allegations. Kesha's new album Rainbow topped the iTunes chart. Other stars, including Lena Dunham and Nelly Furtado, have also voiced support for Swift.

Mikel Obi has assured the Super Eagles will give their best in the friendly against England at Wembley Stadium on June 2, 2018, two weeks before their World Cup opener against Croatia on June 16. Nigeria will also face Iceland and Argentina in Group D, while England plays Tunisia, Panama, and Belgium in Group G.

The passage documents the AMD AGESA™ software interface, covering stack management procedures, entry point procedures, and host environment call-outs. AMD_ENABLE_STACK is a stackless native assembler routine using a register passing model that initializes the processor and cache system to establish a pre-memory stack region before main memory is available, dividing it among processor cores, mapping it to global address space, and setting MTRRs. AMD_DISABLE_STACK removes the pre-memory stack once main memory is available, disabling Cache-As-RAM mode and flushing cache lines; it preserves the EBX register. Both must run on all processor cores (the disable procedure by the BSP only) and return status codes such as AGESA_SUCCESS, AGESA_WARNING (stack reentry), and AGESA_FATAL (unknown processor family). AArch64 APUs with the Platform Security Processor (PSP) do not use the stack or early macros, as the PSP initializes DRAM.

AmdCreateStruct and AmdReleaseStruct create and release storage for parameter blocks, with allocation methods PreMemHeap, PostMemDram, and ByHost. Auxiliary procedures obtain DIMM data eye results, APIC addresses, execution cache sizes, base PCI addresses, processor core identification, DIMM location for a memory address, MMIO range mapping, and event log entries.

Entry procedures, listed in time point order, include AmdInitReset (minimal initialization after reset, with execution cache allocation rules), AmdInitEarly (boot environment establishment and platform configuration parameters), AmdInitPost (system memory initialization and transition to post-memory phase), AmdInitEnv (pre-memory closure and HOB transfer), AmdInitMid (graphics display configuration), AmdInitLate (generation of ACPI, DMI, and related information tables), AmdInitRtb (suspend preparation), and the resume procedures AmdInitResume, AmdS3LateRestore, and AmdS3FinalRestore.

Required host environment call-outs include AgesaAllocateBuffer, AgesaDeallocateBuffer, AgesaDoReset, AgesaLocateBuffer, AgesaReadSpd (SPD data over SMBus), and AgesaRunFcnOnAllAps. Optional call-outs cover IDS data reading, heap rebase, memory timing and voltage hooks, video BIOS repost, FCH customization, and platform-specific device controls. Most procedures require a stack established via host environment service functions, and several apply only to x86-64 architecture APUs. Customization is available through build configuration settings and user-defined register tables.

"Combo" defense combines person-to-person and zone defense against the North Carolina Four Corner and spread offenses relying on dribble penetration. Three outside players deny passes; two inside players zone for backside support. On penetration, X5 traps or takes a charge with X1. On a picked-up dribble, X4 and X5 close out in pass denial, forcing difficult passes. If O4 and O5 are skilled handlers and shooters, switch to a quarter court 1-3-1 trap.

The Supreme Court of Louisiana affirmed a judgment dismissing United Distributors' suit against Willis. Willis signed a personal guarantee of Aireo Appliance & Hardware's debts while contemplating acquisition of 50% of the corporation's stock, but two days later decided not to join the venture; the plaintiff was informed, and its salesman returned the signed papers—except the guarantee, which remained unknowingly in plaintiff's files. The note sued upon, in the amount of $3,107.82, was given by the corporation a year later for air conditioning units purchased under Burke's continued operation of the business. The court found that the sole motive for Willis's execution of the guarantee was his intention to become a half-interest stockholder and associate in the undertaking; when that failed and the plaintiff was apprised, the motive failed and the contract became ineffective under Revised Civil Code Articles 1825, 1826 and 1827. Liability of Burke and the corporation was not at issue.

Johnson & Johnson reported a mixed first-quarter trading update, with sales slightly below consensus estimates but adjusted earnings per share meeting expectations. Shares trade around $125, implying a forward P/E of 19x and an enterprise value to Ebitda ratio of 11.9x, levels the author views as neither a bargain nor prohibitively expensive. The company raised its full-year 2017 guidance to sales of $75.4–$76.1 billion and adjusted EPS of $7.00–$7.15, incorporating the Actelion transaction. Remicade sales fell 6% year-on-year to $1.67 billion, and baby care, oral care, and wound care units declined. Excluding stock buybacks, EPS would have been $1.57 instead of $1.61. Regulatory risks include Trump's calls for domestic drug manufacturing and lower prices, while Treasury Secretary Mnuchin said summer tax reform is "not realistic." Falling interest rates have boosted JNJ debt values, though rates are expected to rise. The author concluded to seek value elsewhere.

The passage lists peace conference tasks—estimating doubtful states, arranging economic agreements, and safeguarding minorities—across regions including Russia, the Balkans, Turkey, Africa, and Latin America. It explains how the Inquiry can assist through data collection, maps, reports, and trained personnel, and identifies tasks it cannot handle, such as prisoner repatriation, armament limitation, and commercial treaties, which are assigned to other departments. It then includes correspondence between Dr. S. E. Mezes and Secretary of State Robert Lansing: Mezes requested the text of a contemplated agreement between the United States and other American republics for mutual guarantee of sovereignty and territorial integrity, to be studied as a possible model for general international cooperation. Lansing sent the confidential draft, calling it a "Pan American Treaty," whose preamble commits signatory governments to maintaining territorial integrity, political independence under republican government, defining boundaries, and settling disputes peacefully.

ConocoPhillips has agreed to sell its San Juan Basin assets to an affiliate of Hilcorp Energy Company for $2.7 billion in cash, plus up to $300 million in contingent payments over six years if Henry Hub natural gas averages at or above $3.20 per MMBTU ($7 million per qualifying month). This follows an earlier $13.3 billion sale of Canadian assets to Cenovus. The San Juan assets contain 0.6 billion boe of proved reserves—78% natural gas, 20% natural gas liquids, and 2% oil—reflecting management's shift away from natural gas. Downsides include a production cut of about 115 thousand barrels per day (combined with the Canadian sale, output falls 25.4% versus 2017 forecasts), a $0.3 billion drop in operating cash flow, and a likely non-cash impairment of roughly $2.9 billion, since the assets are carried at $5.9 billion on the books. The impairment may be usable for tax purposes. Management said proceeds will fund "general corporate purposes"; the author expects share buybacks and would favor accretive acquisitions. The author concludes the deal, at about $5 per boe, is reasonable and can create value if the cash is allocated well.

VIX futures, introduced in 2004 and traded on the Cboe Futures Exchange, are contracts based on the VIX Index, which measures implied volatility in the U.S. equity market and serves as a barometer of market sentiment. A VIX futures strategy involves using technical or fundamental indicators to determine entry and exit points, along with risk management and position sizing, and can be used for hedging, portfolio diversification, or speculation. However, VIX futures do not precisely track spot VIX, and rolling costs make long-term hedging expensive. The authors' backtests found VIX futures strategies not valuable to trade; instead, a spot VIX strategy—buying stocks when the VIX is high—produced a 0.64% average gain per trade, a 44.06% risk-adjusted return, and a 23% maximum drawdown, less than half of buy-and-hold's 55%. VIX seasonally performs better in summer and fall. Prices are influenced by the stock market cycle phase and contango/backwardation effects. The full contract equals the index value multiplied by $1,000 (the mini is one-tenth), with a $50 tick size, 0.05 minimum price fluctuation, financial settlement, and monthly contracts. VIX futures traded at 22.450 as of December 19, 2022, with an all-time high of 80.850 in March 2020. The biggest risk is adverse price movement amplified by leverage.
The figures depict a graphical user interface design for a display screen in four embodiments, with broken lines excluded from the claimed design.

The Cleveland Guardians beat the Detroit Tigers in Game 2 of the AL Wild Card Series, forcing a decisive Game 3. A five-run eighth inning was sparked by Brayan Rocchio's go-ahead solo home run off Tigers reliever Troy Melton, breaking a 1-1 tie. Rocchio hit a 99.9 mph four-seam fastball over the right-field wall despite wind blowing in from that direction; per ESPN Research, only Oscar Mercado in 2020 had homered on a pitch that fast for Cleveland over the past decade. The Tigers stranded a team playoff-record 15 baserunners, while Cleveland had just two hits and five baserunners through seven innings. Rocchio struggled early this season, spending six weeks at Triple-A despite contributing to the Guardians' 2024 AL Central title and being a Gold Glove finalist at shortstop. When he returned, Cleveland was 15½ games behind Detroit in the AL Central. Both teams face elimination in Thursday's Game 3.
