The David Swensen Portfolio (Yale Model) is a diversified investment strategy developed by David Swensen, President and Chief Investment Officer of Yale University's endowment from the mid-1980s until his death in May 2021, along with Dean Takahashi. Swensen transformed the endowment from a small, poorly performing 60/40 stock-bond portfolio into one of the world's largest and most successful endowments. The strategy diversifies across asset classes with a focus on alternative investments such as private equity, real estate, hedge funds, and natural resources, and emphasizes low-cost index funds, passive investment strategies, and risk management. From 1985 to 2020, the Yale Model generated a 12.5% annualized return, outperforming the S&P 500's 9.7%. However, a recent ETF-based backtest produced 6.23% annual returns and underperformed the S&P 500, attributed to a large bond allocation and weak emerging markets performance, though drawdowns were lower. The allocation is not fixed and can be adjusted based on investor goals and risk tolerance.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere architecture, contains 108 SMs with 432 third-generation Tensor Cores delivering up to 312 TFLOPS of dense mixed-precision FP16/FP32 performance—2.5x that of Tesla V100 and 20x V100's FP32 throughput. Beyond FP16, INT8, INT4, and binary formats from prior architectures, A100 adds TF32, BF16, and FP64 support. TF32 enables tensor core acceleration for AI training by default without code changes, providing FP32 range with FP16 precision. For HPC, A100 delivers 19.5 TFLOPS peak FP64 throughput (2.5x V100) via a new Double Precision Matrix Multiply Add instruction. The TCAIRS solver in cuSOLVER demonstrated TF32's effectiveness for iterative refinement, achieving a 2.0X geomean speedup over FP64 solvers.

A100 introduces Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity using a 2:4 pattern (two non-zero values per four-entry vector), which doubles compute throughput and halves memory footprint with virtually no accuracy loss across tested networks. Sparse MMA instructions skip zero-value computations for 2x speedup.

Memory improvements include 40 GB HBM2 with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth (1.7x V100) with SECDED ECC, a 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x V100) with 2.3x bandwidth increase, and Compute Data Compression. The combined L1 data cache/shared memory is 192 KB/SM versus 128 KB/SM in V100. Separate FP32 and INT32 cores allow simultaneous execution at full throughput.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitions a single A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated memory paths, enabling quality of service and fault isolation for multi-tenant environments. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth across twelve links (versus 300 GB/sec over six links in V100). A100 also supports PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, a five-core hardware NVJPG decode engine, an Optical Flow Accelerator, improved atomic operations (11x FP16, 2.7x FP32 over V100), and five NVDEC units.

CUDA 11 adds task graph acceleration, asynchronous copy operations, asynchronous barriers, and L2 cache residency controls. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs delivering 5 PFLOPS, with MIG enabling up to 56 discrete accelerators per system.

This prospective study evaluated bioimpedance spectroscopy (BIS) for assessing fluid status and predicting outcomes in 157 patients hospitalized for acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) at a single center in Taiwan. BIS measured overhydration (OH) and the OH-to-extracellular water ratio (OH/ECW) at admission and discharge, with patients stratified by chronic kidney disease (CKD; 45.9%) and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF; 70.7%). Outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; 32.5%) and heart failure hospitalization (HHF; 28.7%) over a mean follow-up of 10.7 ± 7.1 months.

CKD patients had higher admission OH and OH/ECW values, but these were not significantly associated with MACE or HHF. HFrEF patients showed significantly greater OH/ECW reductions than non-HFrEF patients (P = 0.036), suggesting better response to diuresis, though this did not translate into improved outcomes. Across all subgroups, Cox models adjusted for age, sex, NT-proBNP, and ejection fraction showed that OH, OH/ECW, and changes in these parameters were not significant predictors of MACE or HHF. Kaplan-Meier analyses similarly found no significant differences based on OH/ECW reductions in CKD, non-CKD, HFrEF, or non-HFrEF groups.

The authors conclude that BIS effectively monitors fluid status in ADHF, particularly in HFrEF, but its prognostic utility for predicting outcomes in CKD and HFpEF subgroups is limited. Study limitations include the single-center design, small sample size, lack of a control group, and follow-up duration. Further research with larger cohorts is needed to validate BIS prognostic value and explore its integration with other markers.

The lecture examines wireless communication, where, unlike wire-line systems, fading complicates the channel. A sinusoidal transmitting antenna in free space produces a far-field electric field decreasing as 1/r with propagation delay r/c, and antenna patterns account for directional and frequency-dependent behavior. Since Maxwell's equations are linear, a system function describes the response to sinusoidal inputs; with fixed antennas in free space, the channel reduces to the earlier white Gaussian noise case, as with microwave towers.

When the receiving antenna moves, a Doppler shift occurs, with relative frequency change equal to velocity divided by the speed of light; although small, multiplying by gigahertz carrier frequencies makes effects occur within milliseconds. A single Doppler shift is not a problem because frequency recovery can track it. With a reflecting wall creating two paths of changing relative lengths, positive and negative Doppler shifts produce a beat pattern causing periodic fading—called multipath or fast fading. The real problem is multiple Doppler shifts that differ across paths. A road-reflection example shows path length differences decreasing as 1/r, causing field decay of 1/r² and power decay of 1/r⁴; real environments involve attenuations from 1/r² to 1/r⁶, sometimes exponential through walls, so solving the electromagnetic field at a receiver is impractical.

A ray tracing model represents J paths with attenuations β_j(t) and delays τ_j(t). The resulting channel system function is linear but time-varying, so frequency-domain multiplication no longer applies, though time-varying convolution still works; the impulse response consists of impulses at path delays, each yielding a delayed, attenuated copy of the input. Narrowband inputs keep this model valid over the used frequency band.

At baseband, demodulation uses the carrier frequency plus the average Doppler shift, replacing each path's Doppler shift by its deviation from that average. The Doppler spread—the difference between largest and smallest Doppler shifts—determines how long the channel appears time-invariant; channel measurements must be updated roughly every 1/(2 × Doppler spread), making Doppler spread a key parameter in wireless system design.

NVIDIA Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended July 30, 2017 (Q2 fiscal 2018) reports revenue of $2,230 million, up 56% year over year, and net income of $583 million ($0.92 diluted per share), up 123% from the prior year. First-half revenue was $4,167 million with net income of $1,091 million. Growth was driven by GPUs for gaming, datacenter, and professional visualization, and by Tegra processors. GPU segment revenue was $1,897 million (up 59%), including datacenter revenue of $416 million (up 175%); Tegra revenue was $333 million (up 101%), including automotive revenue of $142 million. BrainWorking Recursive Therapy (BWRT), created by Terence Watts in 2011, has arrived in Dunstable to help Bedfordshire residents with anxiety, depression, stress, and related conditions. The neuroscience-based treatment replaces negative reactions with preferred feelings before conscious awareness. Keith Tunstall offers free, confidential consultations, including via Skype or FaceTime.

Chester Gibson, a Mohawk man, once hunted deer outside the Six Nations Reserve stealthily to avoid prosecution. After the government's 2013 recognition of an 18th-century treaty affirming Haudenosaunee hunting rights in southwestern Ontario, he and others now hunt openly during a six-day annual deer harvest in Short Hills Provincial Park, with ministry biologists assisting. Protesters, including members of the Animal Alliance of Canada, gather at the park entrance with signs, record license plates, and delay drivers; nails were found on the trail, and police are investigating a crime during the hunt. Some animal-rights groups support the hunters, noting that hunts by mostly white hunters are not protested. The community calls the event a harvest rather than a hunt, viewing deer as part of the ecosystem, and considers it a step toward reconciliation that has revived traditions among a new generation and shifted diets from beef to venison. The hunt is limited to six days a year, sunrise to sunset, with bows only and no deer limit. The deer population, about 400 in 2016, exceeds the park's carrying capacity of 50 and has damaged plant species. Meat is shared among six longhouses, elders, and hunters, and research links traditional lean meats to better health outcomes in Indigenous communities facing high obesity and diabetes rates.

Sterling Bank Plc improved its profits for the year ended December 31, 2017, and increased loans and advances by 27 per cent to N598.1 billion, unlike most banks that reduced lending due to rising payment defaults. Gross earnings rose 19.8 per cent to N133.5 billion, driven by growth in interest and non-interest income. Profit before tax grew from N6 billion to N8.606 billion, while profit after tax rose from N5.163 billion to N8.521 billion. Customers' deposits increased 17.1 per cent to N684.8 billion, and shareholders' funds grew 20.2 per cent to N102.9 billion. The non-performing loan ratio fell to 6.2 per cent from 9.9 per cent, and total assets reached N1.1 trillion, a 28.7 per cent increase. Managing Director Abubakar Suleiman attributed the performance to disciplined loan growth and a diversified funding base, noting the launch of the "Specta" online lending platform. In 2018, the bank plans to pursue agility, digitisation and specialisation, focusing on health, education, agriculture, renewable energy and transport.

Idea Generator's investment process requires cheap valuation, a predictable thesis, and manageable identifiable risks. The company's Magnequench segment, the global leader in rare earth magnetic powders, represented 46.7% of 2017 revenues and 72.8% of EBITDA, and the stock traded at 6.1x EV/EBITDA. Because this risk affects the core of the bullish thesis and could not be ignored, no position was taken in Neo Performance Materials.

NASA has required employees working on Artemis missions with contractors SpaceX and Blue Origin to continue working through the government shutdown, which began early Wednesday morning. Their work will be unpaid during the furlough, but they should record their time and are expected to receive pay after reopening, according to NASA Chief Human Capital Officer Kelly Elliott. Artemis II is scheduled for early 2026, Artemis III in 2027 will be the first to involve SpaceX directly, and Artemis V is expected to involve Blue Origin. Neither company has finalized its lunar lander design.

The lecture continues the study of folding polygons into convex polyhedra by gluing a polygon's boundary to itself, represented as gluing trees, illustrated with the cube-from-a-cross example of an Alexandroff gluing. The focus is on counting, enumerating, and deciding gluings for general, edge-to-edge, and bounded-sharpness polygons. The number of combinatorially distinct gluings is exponential (2^Θ(n)) in the general and edge-to-edge cases, proven via a spiky star polygon with near-zero convex angles and reflex angles near 360°, using perimeter halving. For bounded sharpness (reflex angles bounded away from 360° by a constant), each leaf has constant curvature, so gluing trees have only a constant number of leaves and polynomially many (n^O(L)) gluings result. Algorithmically, dynamic programming enumerates all edge-to-edge gluings in exponential time (optimal, since outputs can be exponential) and decides existence in polynomial time (n³). The general-case enumeration algorithm handles "zip" and "tug" cases in exponential time, becoming polynomial for bounded sharpness. Whether general-case decision can be made polynomial remains open. Implementations of these algorithms exist. Examples show the Latin cross produces exactly five convex polyhedra via edge-to-edge gluings and 85 total gluings (23 distinct polyhedra), while the equilateral triangle and square admit rolling belts with infinitely many gluings; the square's maximum-volume folding is an octahedron.

U.S. consumer gasoline demand reached a record March high of 9.6 million b/d, according to the EIA, with exports trending high. Declining inventories pushed the national gas price average up two cents to $2.55, 26 cents higher than a year ago. Michigan, Ohio, and Illinois saw the largest monthly increases, while Hawaii and California are the most expensive markets. Gasoline inventories remain above 85 million bbl.

Kashmiri students at Haryana Central University in Mahenderhgarh were assaulted by a group of 15-20 people, according to student Aftab. Haryana Police lodged an FIR, and J&K Chief Minister Mehbooba Mufti urged stringent action against the perpetrators and demanded a probe.

The team's defensive play fell short of their usual playoff standard, and the opponent capitalized on power plays, scoring in the second and third periods. The goalie, returning after three to four months, played well, but the team did not give him their best effort.

The Nigerian Immigration Service told a Federal High Court, Abuja, that suspended Supreme Court Justice Sylvester Ngwuta used two similar standard international passports interchangeably. Witness Tanko Kutana said a new passport was issued after Ngwuta swore an affidavit that his original was lost, but he failed to report finding it. Forensic analysis of six passports found in his possession showed no evidence of forgery. Kutana stated using two similar passports violates immigration law. Justice John Tsoho adjourned the trial until October 20.

The passage describes interrupt shadow handling and #HV doorbell page usage in SEV-ES. Because #HV is delivered without regard to interrupt shadows, guests lose control over HLT and interrupt interaction; instead, guests should execute HLT with interrupts disabled without examining pending interrupt state, and the host should immediately re-enter the guest if interrupts or non-maskable events are pending.

The doorbell page is configured via VMGEXIT SW_EXITCODE 0x8000_0014 using GET, SET, and QUERY actions. The host may execute RMPUPDATE to clear the RMP assignment of a mapped doorbell page, and the guest must access the page with C=0 in the guest PTE.

The host must faithfully emulate APIC behavior, presenting interrupts by writing vector numbers to PendingEvent in the doorbell page when the guest vCPU is not running, and sending #HV notifications when appropriate. It sets NoEoiRequired when only one interrupt is ready and clears it when multiple interrupts are pending. Non-maskable events are signaled by setting PendingEvent bits and NoFurtherSignal.

Guests must use atomic exchanges to retrieve pending event information and must validate vectors, since a non-cooperative host may write random data. EOIs are completed either by atomically clearing NoEoiRequired or by performing an APIC register write via VMGEXIT. Guests must dispatch non-maskable events even when EFLAGS.IF=0, and receipt of #HV while NoFurtherSignal is non-zero is grounds for a system panic.

NES Global Talent is seeking a Performance Specialist for a six-month onshore contract in Aberdeen with a global operator, responsible for PSCM Functional Performance Management and Risk & Assurance. The Texas Rangers' search for Bruce Bochy's replacement as manager is centered on Skip Schumaker, a special adviser with the organization and the 2023 NL Manager of the Year. President of baseball operations Chris Young said a formal interview process has begun, with no external candidates considered yet. Schumaker, hired in November and under contract through the end of October, previously managed the Marlins. Bochy, 70, agreed Monday to end his three-year stint after Texas finished 81-81, and has been offered an advisory role with the Rangers.

The Tri State Psychology Conference, founded at Marshall University in 1993 to give students conference experience, will celebrate its 25th anniversary April 20 at West Liberty University. Started by Psi Chi students and faculty, it grew into a regional event funded by Psi Chi's national office, with no registration fee.

Martin Braithwaite left Middlesbrough for Bordeaux in the January transfer window, reportedly seeking regular playing time to secure his place in Denmark's World Cup squad. The author argues Braithwaite may have taken "the easy way out" rather than staying to fight for his place under Tony Pulis. Viktor Fischer, a former Boro winger who returned to Denmark with FC Copenhagen, is Braithwaite's main rival for a squad spot. Pulis expressed disappointment, noting Braithwaite had signed a four-year deal just six months earlier. The author suggests that had Braithwaite stayed and helped Boro win promotion, he could have earned both a World Cup place and Premier League football. Boro now aim to show him what he's missing, with a possible play-off place and Wembley final on May 26 still achievable.
Russia's foreign ministry said U.S. missile defence systems in Romania and a planned site in Poland violate the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Force Treaty signed by Washington and the Soviet Union.

The passage discusses two main topics. First, it explores whether LLMs can generate novel social science hypotheses and theories, noting that while AI has succeeded in natural sciences, concerns persist about the originality and validity of LLM-proposed theories, and advocating human-AI collaboration. Second, it addresses AI governance: generative AI brings legal and ethical challenges such as misinformation, deepfakes, and amplified societal biases, and may outpace existing legal frameworks. Governments (EU, US, China) and companies like Microsoft have introduced AI regulations and principles, but challenges remain, including communication gaps between industry and government, lack of international consensus, and micro-level risks like jailbreak prompts bypassing content filters. The authors call for top-down partnerships among industry, academia, and policymakers, forward-looking regulations, and bottom-up issue-reporting mechanisms. The passage also includes an extensive reference list and acknowledgments of contributors to the whitepaper by Microsoft Research Asia's Societal AI team and academic collaborators.

This paper introduces ASTROCO, a conformer-style encoder for self-supervised learning of astronomical time series that combines multi-head self-attention with local depthwise convolutions and gating. Unlike prior transformer-based models (Astromer and Astromer 2), which treat all time steps equally and lack mechanisms to regulate noisy or distant measurements, ASTROCO balances long-range dependency modeling with local feature extraction. Each encoder block contains three sublayers—multi-head self-attention, a depthwise convolutional sublayer with Gated Linear Units, and a gated feed-forward network—connected via residuals and layer normalization. Photometric values are concatenated with sinusoidal time embeddings through a learned projection, and features from all layers are mixed via trainable softmax weights followed by masked mean pooling. On the MACHO R-band dataset, ASTROCO-S (5.9M parameters) and ASTROCO-L (15.2M parameters) achieve lower reconstruction error and higher macro-F1 scores than Astromer baselines, with the smaller model outperforming prior work using fewer resources.

A hockey coach discusses his team's poor performance in a Stanley Cup Finals game against Anaheim, citing turnovers, weak puck movement, and a loss of coverage that led to the winning goal. He attributes Anaheim's physical forechecking to good dump-ins and his team's failure to hold up forecheckers, and says his players must adjust since it is not being called by officials. He believes the game was winnable until late and expects better play in the next game. He discusses Jason's need to return to his earlier form and explains his decision to keep his lineup intact rather than panic and break it up. He recounts the draft in which his team selected Getzlaf and later traded for Perry, and mentions signing Kunitz. He also mentions a conversation with Scotty about Zetterberg and Datsyuk being reunited. He expresses frustration with officials, citing extra hacks at Ray Emery and being told to stand behind the bench. He criticizes the team's two-man advantage, noting only one good shot was generated, and says his centers failed to support the puck in their own end. He compares Anaheim to Buffalo, noting Buffalo forechecks and pinches well but does not finish checks as hard.

The Carlsberg UK Northamptonshire Food and Drink Awards 2017/18, in its ninth year, announced winners at a dinner at Northampton's Royal & Derngate on November 15. Special guest Antonio Carluccio OBE had died a week earlier, and a toast was led by his friend William Sitwell. The evening also honoured gold venues in the Eat Out Eat Well scheme from five of seven councils. The Hopping Hare won Booker Food Pub of the Year, with its chef Arturs Dzerins runner-up for Young Chef of the Year. Winners included Triple 'F' Pure Apple Juice, Northamptonshire Blue, Honey, Lemon and Ginger Marmalade, Workbridge Coffee Shop, The Exotic Dining, The Folly (also Great Service Award winner), Richard Walker (Chef of the Year), Victoria Austin (Young Chef), The Dukes Arms (Community Pub), Steve Reid (Local Food Hero), and Tom Warner and Christina Warner-Keogh (F&B Achiever). Alaric Neville received the Chairman's Award.

The speaker said brief breakdowns led to quick goals that couldn't be recovered, though they felt they played a solid game with good chances, important for team confidence. Not worried after losing the first game, they noted the opponent is among the league's best defensive teams, requiring hard work to score.

The passage outlines defensive strategies against the Triangle Offense, which poses unique problems because its options are predicated on defensive deployment. Two approaches are presented: the Basic NBA Show & Recover and SOS Disruption. The NBA approach emphasizes packing the inside, forcing perimeter shots, and showing and recovering against cutters and screens, detailed across four phases: the corner cut show, post feed, corner screen and roll, and weakside two-man game. SOS Disruption aggressively disrupts the offense's initial flow and can be extended full court to lengthen passing lanes. All Out SOS Disruption initiates a first-pass trap on the wing, forcing offensive players into freelance situations, with specified defensive rotations for passes out of the trap and an optional trap on the corner pass.

Girlfriends' shop employee Kenna McNeil says staff are preparing flowers and accessories for Liberal High School's prom on April 22, helping customers select flowers, ribbons, and stones for corsages. The shop has received close to 100 orders, including from other schools like Southwestern Heights, Forgan High School, and Hugoton. Preparation began around March 1, since flowers ordered from Arkansas take time to arrive. Business has been steady, with many students ordering about two weeks before prom; the shop took 20 to 30 tux and corsage orders in recent days. McNeil's favorite part is seeing customers post photos online, and the shop continues working to make each order unique and beautiful.

This paper overviews twelve shared tasks organized by NFDI4DS, a German consortium supporting the research data lifecycle in Data Science and AI with emphasis on FAIR principles, transparency, and reproducibility. The tasks, hosted at venues including NSLP, SDP, CLEF, SemEval, and ISWC, comprise seven completed, one ongoing, and four future tasks. Completed tasks include SOMD 2025 (software mention detection), SciVQA (visual question answering over scientific figures), ClimateCheck (fact-checking climate-related social media claims against scholarly articles), FoRC2025 (field of research classification), LLMs4Subjects (automated subject tagging for the TIBKAT catalog), LLMs4OL-2024 (ontology learning with LLMs), and Scholarly QALD (question answering over scholarly knowledge graphs). The ongoing CheckThat!Lab Task 4 addresses scientific web discourse detection and claim-source retrieval. Tasks under development cover dataset and ML model mention detection using GSAP-NER, GitHub README-to-knowledge-graph extraction (ReadMe2KG), clinical uncertainty quantification for decision support (CURED, planned for 2026), and algorithm generalisability benchmarking (Algorithm2Domain). The paper argues that these community-driven tasks drive methodological progress and contribute to a FAIR research data infrastructure, supporting NFDI's broader mission of sustainable, interoperable research data practices.

Scores of fishermen clashed with police in central Vietnam while attempting to file lawsuits demanding compensation from Taiwanese firm Formosa, whose toxic waste dump killed tonnes of fish in 2016. Formosa paid $500 million to Vietnam's government, but fishermen say they have received no compensation. Witnesses reported beatings and brief detentions. A previous group's lawsuits were dismissed by a court in September.

Las Vegas Valley residents must postmark returns by 10 p.m. April 18, 2017 (extension: October 16). Postal headquarters closes at 10 p.m. and offers a drive-up drop-off. Tips: sufficient postage, clear addresses, sealed envelopes, saved receipts.

Digital leaders use extensive data collection and measurement to set objectives and track progress, with employees evaluated through data-driven metrics and 360-degree reviews. Rather than creating rigidity, this measurement focus provides teams flexibility and autonomy, encouraging innovation, experimentation, and risk-taking in pursuing clearly defined goals.

The potentially record-breaking release of "Avengers: Infinity War" kicks off Hollywood's summer movie season early as the industry seeks to recover from a nearly three percent box office decline and last summer's worst performance in more than a decade. Major franchise films like "Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom" and numerous sequels dominate the slate, but reporter Ben Fritz warns that oversaturation could produce more flops as films compete for the same box office dollars. With 2017 ticket sales at a 25-year low, competition from Netflix, and box office dollars concentrated in a few films, studios are promoting diverse slates including female-led comedies, action films, documentaries, and original movies like "Hotel Artemis," reflecting what filmmakers describe as an audience appetite for less formulaic fare.

On May 17, the Colchester-Milton Rotary Club, with volunteers from Dealer.com and Vermont Gas, planted saplings at Pine Island Farm near the Winooski River in Colchester. Organized by Burlington's Intervale Center, the project enhanced a 2014 planting on the same land. The effort fulfills Rotary International president Ian H.S. Riseley's challenge to plant a tree per member during the Rotary year, covering the local club's 45 members. Earlier in 2018, the club planted five larger trees at Porters Point School, and local president Kevin Endres hopes to bring similar projects to Milton next year.

On July 19, 2016, Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2016, via a press release furnished as Exhibit 99.1. Per General Instruction B.2, this information is not deemed "filed" under Section 18 of the Exchange Act. The report was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration, and Chief Accounting Officer.

Motley Fool Money reviews the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card, which it describes as one of the best no-annual-fee cash back cards. The card offers unlimited 2% cash rewards on purchases with no categories or limits, a $200 cash rewards bonus after spending $500 in the first 3 months, and 0% intro APR for 12 months from account opening on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, followed by a variable APR of 18.99%, 23.99%, or 28.99%. It has a $0 annual fee and provides up to $600 in cell phone protection (subject to a $25 deductible) when the cell phone bill is paid with the card. Approval is most likely for applicants with good credit (670-850). The page also lists the Capital One Quicksilver card (unlimited 1.5% cash back, 5% on Capital One Travel bookings, $300 in welcome bonuses, 0% intro APR for 15 months, no foreign transaction fees) and a Citi card (2% cash back earned as 1% at purchase and 1% at payment, $200 bonus after $1,500 spend in 6 months, 0% intro APR on balance transfers for 18 months). The article discloses that Motley Fool receives compensation from partners, including Citi, JPMorgan Chase, and Wells Fargo, but states that product ratings are not influenced by compensation.

The passage describes the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture and its key innovations:

- **HPC acceleration**: A100 Tensor Cores support FP64 computations, delivering 2.5x the FP64 performance of Tesla V100 (19.5 TFLOPS peak) via a new Double Precision Matrix Multiply Add instruction. The TCAIRS solver in cuSOLVER enables mixed-precision iterative refinement, with TF32 delivering the fastest, most robust results (2.0x geomean speedup over FP64).

- **Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity**: A new 2:4 sparse matrix pattern (two non-zero values per four-entry vector) doubles compute throughput by skipping zero values, with virtually no accuracy loss across vision, NLP, and other networks.

- **Memory improvements**: Combined L1 data cache/shared memory of 192 KB/SM; 40 GB HBM2 DRAM with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth (1.7x V100); 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x larger than V100) with residency controls; Compute Data Compression providing up to 4x bandwidth improvements.

- **Multi-Instance GPU (MIG)**: Partitions a single A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated memory paths, enabling QoS, fault isolation, and multi-tenant use cases for CSPs.

- **Interconnect and I/O**: Third-generation NVLink with twelve links providing 600 GB/sec total bandwidth; PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV support.

- **Additional features**: Hardware NVJPG decode, Optical Flow Accelerator, improved FP16/FP32 atomics, five NVDEC units, and simultaneous FP32/INT32 execution.

- **CUDA 11 advances**: Task graphs for reduced launch overhead, asynchronous copy operations, hardware-accelerated asynchronous barriers, and L2 cache persistence controls.

- **DGX A100**: A system with eight A100 GPUs delivering 5 PFLOPS, interconnected via NVSwitch, targeting unified AI infrastructure with NGC software containers.

Wall Street stocks gave up early gains Thursday as rising bond yields and a tech retreat offset robust earnings, putting the S&P 500 on track for its first weekly decline in five. The Fed held rates steady but flagged inflation concerns, supported by data showing low unemployment claims, near 7-year-high factory prices, and 2.0 percent higher labor costs. The Dow rose 0.14 percent while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq fell. Banks gained; eBay rose 13.8 percent, PayPal fell 8.1 percent, and UPS dropped 6.1 percent. Of 227 companies reporting, 79.7 percent beat estimates.

Free agent wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. has accepted a six-game NFL suspension for violating the league's performance-enhancing drugs policy, delaying his comeback attempt. Beckham said he failed a PED test last season and insisted he did not knowingly take banned substances, saying the league told him his testosterone levels were too high. The suspension appeared on the NFL's transactions wire Tuesday, making him ineligible until Week 12. Beckham, who will be 33 when the suspension ends, wants to return this season and named four franchises he'd be interested in joining. He was released by the Dolphins last December after recording nine catches for 55 yards over nine games.

This study examines the global rankings of the top five higher education institutions (HEIs) in ten Asian countries—Bangladesh, China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Pakistan, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, and the Russian Federation—between 2015 and 2025 using the Times Higher Education World University Rankings (THE WUR). Noting that prior research mostly focused on single or few Asian cases, the study addresses a gap in understanding the overall ranking positions of Asian HEIs over time. Using a qualitative multiple case study design and document analysis of THE WUR datasets, the research analyzed the top five HEIs from the 2024 THE Asia University Rankings (and the 2025 THE WUR for Russia) in the ten most populous Asian countries.

Results show that Chinese and Japanese HEIs were the most successful. All five Chinese HEIs improved consistently, with Tsinghua University (12th) and Peking University (13th) leading in 2025 and four of the five in the top 50. Japanese HEIs appeared in the rankings throughout the period, with the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University in the top 100. Russian HEIs, led by Lomonosov Moscow State University (=107 in 2025), showed stable performance. Indian HEIs, particularly the Indian Institute of Science, displayed a positive trend. In contrast, HEIs in Indonesia, Thailand, Pakistan, and the Philippines showed neutral or declining patterns, while Vietnamese HEIs exhibited a pronounced downward trend. Bangladeshi HEIs were newcomers with neutral rankings.

The study concludes that, except for China, Japan, and Russia, most Asian HEIs lag behind international competitors and lack stable ranking profiles. Two limitations are noted: only the top five HEIs per country were examined, and only the THE WUR was used. The study recommends that Asian governments diversify globalization efforts, strengthen marketing and public relations, expand funding opportunities, and support overseas offices to improve the visibility and rankings of their HEIs.

The passage describes patterns for building distributed systems with containers. It begins by noting the dramatic rise of open source software in the late 1990s and 2000s, which demonstrated that software development—particularly distributed systems—is a community endeavor, and that all container technology underlying the book's patterns was developed as open source. Patterns are defined as general blueprints for organizing distributed systems without mandating specific technologies. Their value lies in letting developers learn from others' mistakes, providing a shared vocabulary, and enabling the construction of reusable components.

The first section covers single-node patterns, where tightly coupled containers are co-scheduled on one machine (a grouping called a pod in Kubernetes). Motivations for splitting applications into multiple containers include resource isolation, team scaling, and separation of concerns. The sidecar pattern pairs an application container with a sidecar that augments it; examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy service via an nginx sidecar, synchronizing configuration from an API, deploying monitoring tools like topz, and building a Git-based PaaS. Successful sidecars require parameterization, a stable API, and documentation. The ambassador pattern brokers interactions between an application container and the outside world; examples include proxying to sharded Redis with twemproxy, service brokering for discovery and portability, and request splitting for experimentation using nginx. The adapter pattern transforms an application's interface to conform to a standardized one; examples include Prometheus monitoring exporters, log normalization with fluentd, and rich health checks for MySQL.

The second section covers multi-node patterns, which are loosely coupled and communicate over networks. Microservices offer reliability, agility, team decoupling, and independent scaling, but make debugging and architecture harder—challenges that distributed patterns address. The replicated load-balanced service pattern handles stateless applications using readiness probes, session tracking, and optional layers for caching (Varnish), rate limiting, and SSL termination (nginx). Sharded services, used when state is too large for a single machine, assign each shard a subset of requests; sharded caches greatly improve memory utilization and hit rate, though shard failures cause cache misses and slower recalculation. Replicated, sharded caches add resilience and per-shard scaling. Hands-on examples throughout demonstrate deployment on Kubernetes using StatefulSets, Services, ConfigMaps, Secrets, and ambassador containers.

This lecture discusses renormalization and logarithm resummation in Soft-Collinear Effective Theory (SCET), using the b to s gamma decay as an example. The Wilson coefficient's counterterm cancels a 1/epsilon squared divergence, and the operator's delta function parameter omega equals the b-quark mass mb due to kinematics. The anomalous dimension contains a regular term and a cusp anomalous dimension multiplying a log of mu/omega; the cusp term generates the leading logarithms. Solving the renormalization group equation with a tree-level boundary condition at the hard scale produces Sudakov double-logarithmic exponentials: with a fixed coupling (as in QED), the result is a Sudakov exponential, while a running QCD coupling yields a solution depending on ratios of alpha_s. Leading logs correspond to alpha_s^k log^(k+1) terms, next-to-leading logs to alpha_s^k log^k, and so on; the cusp anomalous dimension is universal and known to three loops.

The "cusp" arises from a kink in the ultrasoft Wilson line at the operator insertion, and a general renormalization theory for Wilson lines with cusps gives a single-log anomalous dimension at all orders; collinear diagrams ending on quark fields exhibit a similar structure. The omegas are fixed by external kinematics when operators involve only one building block per collinear direction, as in pp to dijets with four directions. When two fields belong to the same collinear direction, renormalization equations involve integrals, reproducing classic evolution equations such as Altarelli-Parisi/DGLAP for parton distribution functions and the Brodsky-Lepage equation.

The lecture then begins an analysis of deep inelastic scattering (DIS) in the Breit frame, focusing on the inclusive region where Px squared is of order Q squared. The cross section splits into leptonic and hadronic tensors, and the effective theory's lowest-dimension operators involve two collinear quark (or gluon) fields. The operator definition of the parton distribution function is shown to coincide with this operator, where the forward matrix element fixes one momentum combination via a delta function while the other remains an unconstrained integration variable.

A study by Giuriato and Lovecchio (2025) examined whether increased physical education (PE) hours with cognitively demanding activities improved attention in middle school students. Seventy-five participants from two classes were assigned to experimental or control groups: Class 6 received four hours of PE weekly, while Class 7 received two. Using the Bells Test administered in October and December, results showed significant improvements in attention speed (30-second test) for both experimental groups, while sustained attention (120-second test) improved only in Class 6. Control groups showed no significant changes. The authors conclude that increased PE hours with cognitively engaging activities can enhance short-term attention, though 120 minutes weekly may be insufficient, and further research is needed on long-term effects and activity-specific impacts.

This patent application describes methods and hardware for configuring Deep Neural Network (DNN) implementations, focusing on activation modules that use programmable lookup tables to approximate activation functions. The method involves providing calibration data to a representation of the hardware, monitoring inputs to an activation module to determine the actual range of input values, generating lookup data representing the activation function over that determined range, and loading the data into the hardware's lookup table. This range calibration improves efficiency by using lookup table entries across the likely input range rather than the full range permitted by the input bit length. Lookup data can be generated as data points or curves, with linear or quadratic interpolation used to compute outputs between stored points, where the most significant bits of an input serve as the lookup address and the least significant bits support interpolation. Inputs outside the determined range may be clamped at the range bounds or handled by extrapolation. The lookup table may comprise two data stores (even and odd entries) enabling simultaneous reads and concurrent loading of data for subsequent activation functions. A ReLU unit may serve as a simple path, allowing the lookup table to be turned off when ReLU is used. Configurable offsets can center input values, and the methods may be implemented in software, hardware, or manufactured via integrated circuit manufacturing systems.

The UK's Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) has designated Google Search with Strategic Market Status (SMS)—a label for companies with "substantial and entrenched market power"—following a 10-month investigation, marking the first use of these powers under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act against a major tech company. Proposed measures include letting users choose rival search engines, "fair ranking principles," increased data portability, and requiring Google to seek permission to use publishers' content in AI Overviews. The CMA says Google handles over 90 percent of UK general search queries, and over 200,000 UK firms spent more than £10 billion on its search advertising in 2024. Google argues the interventions could inhibit UK innovation and harm businesses. The rules affect Google Search's News tab, Top Stories carousel, and Google Discover, but not Google News or Gemini. Apple is also under investigation for potential SMS.

The Rockwood School District in Missouri keeps students in classroom cohorts for whole-class reading instruction regardless of ability, rather than grouping readers across grade levels by reading level. All students, including English multilingual learners, participate in daily grade-level phonics and comprehension lessons, followed by flexible small groups based on real-time data for reteaching or enrichment. Students also engage in independent and partner reading, receive targeted interventions from reading specialists when needed, and use movement-based learning tools. Advanced readers work with complex texts, while emerging readers receive scaffolded support such as visual cues and pre-teaching. The passage cites research indicating ability grouping can have lasting downsides, including a study of nearly 12,000 students finding that those in the lowest kindergarten reading groups rarely caught up to peers. At the end of the 2024–25 school year, Rockwood kindergarteners outperformed national proficiency averages in every skill group, in some cases by more than 17 percentage points, while first and second graders outpaced national averages across nearly every domain. The district attributes these results to strong universal Tier I instruction with strategic support, arguing that removing students during critical learning moments widens rather than closes gaps.

China has announced it will shut down its domestic ivory market by the end of 2017. Despite a 1989 international ban on ivory trade, elephant poaching continued because older ivory remained legal, allowing poachers to pass off new ivory as old. China, the world's largest ivory market, has laid out a plan that includes reassigning ivory carvers and educating the public. Conservationists say the move could be a turning point and may encourage other countries to follow suit.

This passage reviews multiple studies on quality in higher education. Several works examine online and e-learning quality during the COVID-19 pandemic: Ramírez-Hurtado et al. (2021) assess online teaching service quality using the SERVQUAL framework, identifying technological infrastructure and instructor competence as key factors; Elumalai et al. (2021) explore factors affecting e-learning quality from students' perspectives; Shahzad et al. (2021) compare male and female students' e-learning experiences, noting gender-related challenges; and Dagiene et al. (2022) gather higher education leaders' views on pandemic-era opportunities, quality factors, and required changes.

Organizational and leadership themes appear in Karsono et al. (2022), who link leadership spirituality to educational quality in Indonesia, and Anastasiadou and Taraza (2020), who examine resistance to change as an obstacle to quality in higher education institutions. Tight (2020) provides an overview of quality assurance and management research, while Pedro and Kumar (2020) address institutional support for online teaching within quality assurance frameworks.

Multiple works by Kayyali cover university rankings—their benefits, limitations, role in combating diploma mills, use in accreditation, and relationship to academic quality—alongside topics including quality assurance concepts and evolution, virtual universities, AI in education, faculty development, academic freedom, entrepreneurship, career development, and recognition of non-formal learning. Other studies address e-learning interoperability (Naim and Alahmari), service quality and student loyalty (Del Río-Rama et al.), e-learning acceptance (Khodadad Hoseiny et al.), stakeholder quality expectations (Cavallone et al.), Curriculum 4.0 (Lukita et al.), internationalization (De Wit and Altbach), co-creation in teaching (Bovill), and demonstration as a teaching method (Sotivoldievich and Rakhimdjanovich).

The conclusion states that higher education publications are undergoing dynamic shifts driven by innovative models and technologies, requiring stakeholders to engage critically, adapt strategically, and collaborate effectively.

A global study found 75% of honey samples from nearly 200 sites contained neonicotinoid pesticides, with North America highest at 86%. Researchers say bees worldwide are exposed to these pesticides, which may harm pollinators.

Platinum futures are standardized, exchange-traded contracts on the CME Globex platform, settled by physical delivery, representing legally binding agreements to exchange a specified quantity of platinum (50 troy ounces) at a predetermined price on a future date. They can be used for speculation, portfolio diversification, or hedging. A platinum futures strategy involves technical and fundamental analysis, precise entry and exit signals, position sizing, and risk management.

The article presents two backtested strategies. The first trades both long and short: long trades produced 243 trades with a 0.54% average gain, 64% win rate, and 1.7 profit factor; short trades produced 230 trades with a 0.59% average gain, 64% win rate, and 2.9 profit factor; combined, 473 trades with a 0.57% average gain, 64% win ratio, and 1.7 profit factor, uncorrelated to the stock market. The second, a seasonal strategy, had 60 trades, a 75% win rate, 0.66% average gain, and 2.3 profit factor. Platinum futures tend to perform better in winter and spring months.

Platinum prices are affected by supply and demand, political and economic conditions, production costs, and the automotive and jewelry markets. South Africa accounts for about 80% of global supply and 90% of proven reserves. The contract trades under the symbol PL, has a minimum fluctuation of $0.10 per troy ounce (tick size $5.00 per contract), and trading terminates on the third last business day of the contract month. As of December 14, 2022, platinum futures traded at $1036.90; the all-time high was $2308.8 (March 2008) and the all-time low was $267.1 (July 1985). The biggest risk is adverse price movement amplified by leverage. To trade, one must register with a futures broker and deposit initial margin, or alternatively trade platinum CFDs. The article notes commodities are difficult to trade due to the lack of a natural edge, erratic news, and supply from countries where the rule of law can be questioned, and considers gold a better long-term investment than platinum.

The President returns House bill No. 7864, an act to amend the immigration laws, without approval. The bill would exclude aliens over sixteen who cannot read and write English or another language, with exceptions for certain relatives of qualified immigrants. The President argues this is a radical departure from the nation's traditional policy of welcoming all immigrants except those posing moral or physical danger. He rejects claims that recent immigrants are undesirable, that they dangerously swell city populations, or that they deprive citizens of work, attributing unemployment to business depression instead. He contends a literacy test is misleading, since violence and disorder stem from educated agitators rather than illiterate laborers. He finds the family-exception provisions indefinite and inadequate, omitting siblings and raising unclear formalities. He also objects that sections criminalizing the employment of aliens crossing borders are vague, harmful to border communities, and un-American. He concludes the bill is unnecessarily harsh and oppressive.

Teach For America's Ignite Fellowship has spent five years scaling high-dosage virtual tutoring, reaching over 40 communities and training more than 5,500 tutors, with 2,000 fellows delivering nearly 200,000 hours of instruction last year. Middle school math students' test scores grew up to 2.5 times the expected rate, and elementary readers grew up to three times faster than average. The author draws three lessons: training and ongoing support are essential; technology should enable relationships rather than replace them, as shown by a Los Angeles school where students saw a 77-point assessment gain; and tutoring functions as a teacher pipeline, with research showing tutoring nearly triples the likelihood of applying to Teach For America's teaching program, particularly among men, people of color, and non-education majors. The author argues tutoring should be treated as a long-term strategy for both student learning and educator recruitment.

This study introduces GeoSQL-Eval, the first end-to-end automated evaluation framework for assessing large language models (LLMs) on PostGIS GeoSQL query generation, built on Norman L. Webb's Depth of Knowledge framework. Alongside it, the authors construct GeoSQL-Bench, a benchmark of 14,178 tasks across three categories: 2,380 multiple-choice/true-false questions, 3,744 syntax-level SQL generation questions, and 2,155 table schema retrieval questions, spanning four cognitive dimensions, five capability levels, and twenty task types. Using this framework, 24 models across six categories were evaluated. Results show general non-reasoning and reasoning-enhanced models perform best, with GPT-5, o4-mini, and DeepSeek-R1-0528 ranking highest; table schema retrieval remains the primary bottleneck. Errors are dominated by PostGIS function errors and SQL syntax errors (approximately 70% combined), and performance degrades on underspecified prompts. A publicly released leaderboard platform supports continuous model submission. Limitations include incomplete coverage of PostGIS functions (focused on vector processing), restriction to the PostGIS plugin, and insufficient model coverage.

At Dumbarton Oaks on October 7, 1944, United States, British, and Chinese representatives informally discussed dissolving the League of Nations and transitioning to the United Nations Organization; as a non-member, the United States awaited other governments' initiative. In December 1944, the League's Supervisory Committee met in London and appointed a three-member committee (Hambro, Bruce, Castillo Nájera) to select a Conciliation Committee to confer with a designated United Nations group on dissolution and transfer of functions. The Mexican Ambassador raised this matter with Mr. Stettinius twice; no commitments were made. It was recommended the United States take no initiative, leaving the question to the United Nations Conference unless the United Kingdom or China initiated. At a January 31, 1945 Washington meeting with American Republics' representatives, discussion of the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals continued, and the Chilean Ambassador requested a minutes correction regarding "assuring respect for international treaties."

Kyle Busch became the second driver, after Kevin Harvick, to win three consecutive 2018 NASCAR Cup races with his Richmond victory. He hopes he isn't peaking too early, noting short tracks suit him and that running Kyle Busch Motorsports gives him an edge. After crashing at Daytona, his season has been strong, but he expects a fourth straight win at Talladega to be difficult due to the randomness of restrictor-plate racing.

Otis Tucker lives in New Orleans' Lower Ninth Ward, the area most devastated by Hurricane Katrina in 2005, when protective levees failed. Many poor residents have struggled to return due to lack of funds, developers moving in, and gentrification. Katrina killed more than 18,000 people and destroyed over 800,000 homes. Since then, New Orleans has adapted to extreme weather through evacuation centers, raised homes, solar panels, rain gardens, and above-ground planting to cope with contaminated soil. Architects Waggonner and Ball lead the Greater New Orleans Urban Water Plan, which addresses flooding and subsidence; David Waggonner says the city must learn to live with water, citing Amsterdam, with projects including the Mirabeau Water Garden and green infrastructure. According to the U.S. Geological Society, Louisiana loses wetlands at a rate of a football field per hour. The state's Coastal Master Plan, approved in 2017, outlines $50 billion in projects to rebuild barrier islands and wetlands, construct levees and flood gates, raise houses, and buy property. Louisiana is also subsiding partly because oil and gas withdrawal causes land to sink. Professor Alex Kolker says sea level rise is the biggest variable for Louisiana's future, with predicted U.S. increases of about 1 cm annually by 2050, and believes Louisiana's lessons will be invaluable globally.

Biosecurity screening software that monitors DNA manufacturing orders for harmful proteins can be bypassed by AI-designed variants of toxins and viral proteins, according to a study published October 2. Researchers led by Eric Horvitz of Microsoft generated roughly 76,000 digital blueprints for 72 harmful proteins; while screens flagged nearly all original proteins, many AI-adjusted versions evaded detection. New software patches improved screening, even catching genes broken into fragments, though about 3 percent of variants went unflagged. The work was done entirely on computers, and whether the variants retained function is unclear. A Twist Bioscience official noted that attempts to produce malicious proteins are extremely rare.

The cup and handle pattern is a bullish continuation chart pattern resembling a cup with a handle, marking a consolidation period followed by a breakout. The cup forms as a "u"-shaped rounded bottom after a price rally, while the handle is a trading range with a slight downward drift on the right side. The pattern completes when price breaks above the handle, signaling continuation of the prior uptrend. William O'Neil first described the pattern in his 1988 book "How to Make Money in Stocks" as part of his CANSLIM method. Qualifying criteria include occurrence in an existing uptrend, a U-shaped cup with 30-50% depth retracement, handle development, and a breakout above handle resistance. An inverted version forms in downtrends. Examples include Jabil Inc. (1999) and Wynn Resorts (2005-2007). Backtests show mixed results: Ali Akhtari's 2016-2018 test on S&P 500 stocks underperformed the index, while Thomas Bulkowski's research found a 26% failure rate (dropping to 10% when waiting for upside breakout) with a 38% average gain. Volume typically declines during cup formation, decreases in the handle, and spikes at breakout. Stop-losses are commonly placed below the handle's low or cup bottom. Common mistakes include premature entry, ignoring volume, inaccurate targets, and neglecting broader market context. The pattern reflects investor psychology shifting from pessimism to optimism and forms more reliably in low-to-moderate volatility.

The lecture discusses the induced graph removal lemma, a variant of the graph removal lemma in which the hypothesis concerns induced copies of a graph H, and the conclusion is that the graph can be made induced H-free by adding or deleting (editing) fewer than εn² edges. Even for triangles, the regularity method is essentially the only known proof technique. A direct adaptation of the triangle removal proof fails because irregular pairs in the regularity partition cannot simply be discarded, and the half graph example shows that irregular pairs cannot be eliminated entirely.

To address this, the strong regularity lemma is introduced: it produces a pair of vertex partitions P and Q where Q refines P, Q is extremely regular (with regularity parameter depending on the number of parts of P), and the energy difference between P and Q is small. The proof repeatedly applies Szemerédi's regularity lemma until energy increments become negligible; the resulting bounds grow like the "wowzer" function (the tower function iterated). A corollary yields subsets Wᵢ inside partition parts that are regular with each other and with themselves, with edge densities mostly matching the ambient parts and no irregular pairs.

Using this corollary, the induced removal lemma is proved through the usual partition, cleaning, and counting steps. Related generalizations include the colorful removal lemma and the infinite removal lemma, which handles infinitely many forbidden induced patterns and requires regularity parameters depending on the number of parts. Finally, the property testing perspective is presented: a simple randomized sampling algorithm tests triangle-freeness, and the infinite removal lemma implies that every hereditary graph property is testable with one-sided error using an oblivious tester.

Boston has been the undisputed capital of the world's life sciences industry, with the most lab space globally, billions in venture capital funding startups, and federal government research funding driving regional prosperity. However, federal funding cuts and threats to higher education are now undermining the city's recipe for success and challenging its competitive edge.

The lecture examines a higher-order Feynman diagram containing a self-energy correction loop on a propagator. Calculating its amplitude yields an integral behaving as q³/q⁴, which diverges logarithmically when integrated to infinity, producing infinite results—a serious problem that stalled the theory's progress. Introducing a cutoff scale keeps the calculation sensible under Lorentz transformations, though an infinite contribution remains. Through renormalization, physical masses and couplings are redefined as bare values plus corrections; while these corrections diverge at infinite scale, experiments occur at specific scales, so theoretical predictions remain comparable to measurements. The electromagnetic, weak, and strong couplings all run logarithmically with energy and do not converge at the same point at high scales. Introducing new particles changes this running behavior, motivating the idea of unifying all couplings at a specific scale—a possible new physics scenario, though unverified. Observed masses and couplings are evaluated at specific scales and run with energy.

The passage compares two investment timing strategies: dollar-cost averaging, which invests fixed amounts at regular intervals regardless of market conditions, and lump sum investing, which invests a large amount all at once. The article backtests a lump sum buy and hold strategy using a portfolio of five equally weighted asset classes—U.S. stocks, foreign stocks, U.S. bonds, U.S. REITs, and world commodities—via diversified, liquid ETFs with long performance histories. Backtests were conducted for before-crisis, after-crisis, and at-bottom-of-crisis intervals, presenting equity curves, drawdowns, monthly and annual returns, and performance statistics. The conclusion states that lump sum investing over long-term horizons, preferably at least ten years, historically offers a higher probability of success, that earlier investing produces higher total profit, and that financial crises become insignificant over long investment horizons.
Roma are reportedly keen on Manchester United winger Adnan Januzaj, who is expected to be sold to raise funds and could replace Mohamed Salah, whose transfer to Liverpool Roma are negotiating.

NeoWorld is a deep learning framework that constructs an infinitely expandable, interactive virtual world from a single image, progressively unfolding 2D object representations into full 3D models as users explore or issue prompts. It uses a hybrid object-centric scene structure: background regions are rendered as lightweight 2.5D Gaussian layers with instance-aware codebook embeddings, while foreground objects—selected by camera proximity or user requests—are converted to aligned 3D via an image-to-3D module, with a fallback to 2.5D when reconstruction fidelity is low. Natural language commands are interpreted by an LLM to enable object selection, manipulation, and physics-based animation. Experiments show NeoWorld outperforms WonderJourney, WonderWorld, and video diffusion baselines in 3D consistency, scene quality, text alignment, and interactive manipulation, while achieving the second-best rendering speed among 3D methods. As a cascade of pre-trained modules, its robustness is limited by error propagation from alignment failures, LLM misinterpretation, reconstruction errors under occlusion, and segmentation inaccuracies.

The passage is a June 5, 2001 email compiled by Enron employee Ann M Schmidt, containing news articles and media mentions about Enron and related energy matters. Articles from the New York Times, Wall Street Journal, Los Angeles Times, and Houston Chronicle cover California's energy crisis, including elevated natural gas prices, accusations of price manipulation involving El Paso Corporation and Southern California Gas, and FERC's new price mitigation plan. Several articles discuss the PBS "Frontline" documentary "Blackout," which examines the crisis and features interviews with Enron's Kenneth Lay and Jeff Skilling. The California Senate Rules Committee approved subpoenas to eight out-of-state power generators—Enron, Reliant, Dynegy, Williams, Duke, Mirant, NRG, and AES—seeking bidding and pricing documents for an investigation into illegal profiteering. Multiple articles address Enron's Dabhol Power project in India, where Indian and foreign lenders met in Singapore to seek resolution of disputes over the $2.9 billion project following conflicts with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board over unpaid bills and tariffs. USX-Marathon Group took over Enron's 20% stake in a $25 billion Saudi Arabian natural gas venture after Enron withdrew. Other items include Enron North America's proposal with the Connecticut Resources Recovery Authority to use $125 million from the state's conservation fund for a fuel cell power project, which critics opposed; Enron's growing presence in the newsprint market; the Alliance for Retail Energy Markets' response to California's proposed "Fair Plan"; Enron's 50 billion yen note offering; White House advisor Karl Rove's delayed stock sale, which included Enron holdings; and Domtar's $1.65 billion purchase of four Georgia-Pacific mills.

Senator Sherwin Gatchalian urged the Department of Education to address delays in public school teachers' performance-based bonuses, an ongoing issue since school year 2012-2013. Teachers have not received their 2016-2017 bonuses, with DepEd citing failed biddings and delayed clearance processing.

Former president Robert Mugabe has returned to Zimbabwe after receiving medical treatment in Singapore, facing allegations from President Emmerson Mnangagwa's government that his family and their allies, the Generation 40 (G40) faction, were behind the June 24 bomb explosion at White City Stadium in Bulawayo, which killed two and injured over 40 people. Mugabe's nephew, Patrick Zhuwao, warned British PM Theresa May that Mnangagwa could use the blast to target perceived enemies, while Jonathan Moyo said the administration was "seeing ghosts everywhere."

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition (DAQ) system from Texas Instruments featuring an integrated analog front-end. Each analog input channel includes an internal clamp protection circuit allowing inputs to swing up to ±18V, provided input current stays within ±10mA, and a programmable gain amplifier (PGA) supporting single-ended and differential inputs with independently configurable ranges. A wide common-mode voltage rejection circuit supports CM voltages up to ±12V.

The device outputs 20 bits of conversion data in straight-binary or binary two's-complement formats and operates with differential or single-ended clock inputs. A SMPL_SYNC signal synchronizes sampling across multiple devices. The ADS9803 includes a precision internal voltage reference (or an external reference option) and supports 2-lane and 4-lane data interfaces in single-data-rate (SDR) and double-data-rate (DDR) modes, outputting data MSB first in 24-bit packets. Additional features include a data output randomizer using bit-wise XOR to reduce ground bounce interference, simple and moving average modes to improve SNR, and test patterns (fixed, digital ramp, alternating) for debugging the data interface.

A speed-boost mode allows up to 8MSPS sampling for a user-selected analog input channel pair. Configuration occurs via SPI using three register banks, with daisy-chain topology support for multiple devices. The device requires a free-running sampling clock and an initialization sequence of register writes after power-up or reset.

The ADS9803 uses three power supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, IOVDD) with no required power-up sequence. For automatic test equipment (ATE) applications, the device achieves a total unadjusted error (TUE) of 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C post-calibration, with wide-bandwidth mode settling to 99.95% of full-scale in 7.5µs for multiplexed signals.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2017 reports total revenue of $24.5 billion, up from $21.9 billion in the prior-year quarter, with operating income of $7.7 billion and net income of $6.6 billion ($0.84 diluted EPS). Tuberculosis (TB), caused by *Mycobacterium tuberculosis*, remains a major cause of mortality, with an estimated 1.6 million deaths in 2021, and progress against it has been hindered by the COVID-19 pandemic. While pulmonary TB is the most common form, extrapulmonary TB (EPTB)—most frequently lymph node and pleural TB—accounted for about 16% of reported cases in 2019, yet its treatment is understudied. Standard TB therapy uses four first-line drugs: rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol.

The authors developed a whole-body physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model that, for the first time, simulates time-dependent tissue concentrations of all four first-line anti-TB drugs and includes drug distribution to the pleura and lymph nodes, the predominant EPTB sites. The model comprises 17 perfusion-limited tissue compartments described by 18 ordinary differential equations, with parameters taken from literature or estimated by fitting to plasma and lung concentration data. Slow and rapid acetylation of isoniazid were modeled as separate cases. The model was calibrated and validated using independent plasma and lung concentration data.

Simulations compared predicted concentrations at extrapulmonary sites with WHO critical concentrations. Rifampicin and isoniazid exceeded critical concentrations in most compartments, though the model over-predicted rifampicin in pleural fluid. Ethambutol failed to reach critical concentrations in brain, kidney, bone, and skin, and pyrazinamide did not attain its critical concentration in any organ. Limitations include assumptions of drug susceptibility, absence of drug-drug interactions, and a single consolidated lymph node compartment. The model is presented as a starting point for evaluating and optimizing EPTB treatment regimens.

The Federal Reserve raised the federal funds rate by 0.25 points to a 1 to 1.25 percent target range, its second hike within half a year and third under Chair Janet Yellen, following seven years at 0.25 percent after the 2007 crisis.

This study harmonized two national stroke registries—CRCS-K (Korea) and TREAT-AIS (Taiwan)—into a multinational registry of 9,941 EVT-treated patients to examine outcomes of endovascular thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke in East Asia. Taiwanese patients had more vascular risk factors, more severe strokes, and lower functional independence at 90 days compared to Korean patients, while 90-day mortality was higher in Korea. Age was identified as a significant predictor of outcomes, with the strongest effects observed between 75–85 years; patients aged ≥80 years had lower favorable functional outcomes and higher mortality. However, symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage rates did not differ significantly by age. Among elderly patients, approximately 16% achieved favorable outcomes, with pre-stroke functional independence and bridging thrombolysis identified as key predictors of improved outcomes. The findings support careful patient selection based on factors beyond chronological age.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2022. Q2 2022 net sales were $121.2 billion, up 7% from $113.1 billion in Q2 2021, while the company reported a net loss of $2.0 billion versus net income of $7.8 billion in the prior-year quarter. For the six months ended June 30, 2022, net sales were $237.7 billion with a net loss of $5.9 billion. The Q2 net loss included a $3.9 billion valuation loss from Amazon's equity investment in Rivian Automotive, which totaled $11.5 billion for the six-month period. Amazon effected a 20-for-1 stock split on May 27, 2022, and effective January 1, 2022, changed its estimated useful lives of servers from four to five years and networking equipment from five to six years, reducing Q2 2022 depreciation and amortization expense by $928 million.
