Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities were $60.7 billion as of June 30, 2022, down from $96.0 billion as of December 31, 2021.

The lecture defines probabilistically checkable proofs (PCPs) and constructs them from the GKR protocol. A PCP converts an NP witness into a possibly larger proof that a verifier can check by querying only a few random locations instead of reading the entire proof. The class PCP[c, s, r, q] consists of languages with a probabilistic polynomial-time oracle verifier such that for x in the language, some proof is accepted with probability at least c (completeness), while for x not in the language, no proof is accepted with probability above s (soundness); the verifier uses r random bits, makes q nonadaptive queries, and the random query locations are unknown to the prover, preventing cheating. The lecture proves that all of NP has PCPs with completeness 1, soundness 1/2, and polylog n randomness and query complexity (known results achieve as few as 3 queries). The construction focuses on 3SAT, whose verifying circuit has polylog depth and is logspace uniform. The PCP is the GKR protocol unrolled: for each circuit layer and each possible verifier randomness, the prover writes all possible sumcheck transcripts into the proof. Parameters are set with H^m = s and a field F of polylog s size, so F^m is polynomial in s, keeping the proof polynomial-sized. Soundness follows by a union bound over the 2d sumchecks, requiring F to exceed roughly 12dmH, which remains polylog. The verifier runs the GKR verifier treating the oracle as the prover, and one low-degree test is needed on the input layer since the verifier lacks the witness. The lecture concludes by noting the second part will move from information-theoretic soundness to computational soundness (arguments), marking the first use of cryptography in the course.

This study examined the effect of mydriasis (pupil dilation) on image gradability and the performance of an AI model for diabetic retinopathy (DR) screening using the Phelcom Eyer portable retinal camera. Retinal images from 327 patients (mean age 57.03 years; 45.26% male) were captured before and after mydriasis with Tropicamide 0.5%, with two images taken per eye. Images were graded by masked ophthalmologists using the ICDR scale, and a ResNet-200d convolutional neural network trained on the mBRSET dataset was validated on the study dataset. In the mydriatic group, 82.1% of images were gradable, compared with 55.6% in the non-mydriatic group (P < 0.001). Within the non-mydriatic group, systemic hypertension, older age, longer duration of diabetes, male gender, and Indigenous race were significantly associated with lower image gradability. The AI model achieved higher accuracy in the mydriatic group (82.91%) than in the non-mydriatic group (79.23%), with F1 scores of 0.83 versus 0.79 and AUCs of 0.94 versus 0.93. The mydriatic group had fewer false positives (13.9% vs 17.8%) but slightly more false negatives (3.2% vs 3.0%); a Chi-square test showed no statistically significant difference between groups (P = 0.3279). The authors conclude that mydriasis improves image quality and may enhance AI-based DR screening, particularly relevant for resource-limited settings, while noting limitations including a learning curve with portable cameras, selection bias from analyzing only image pairs, and the use of a single dataset and camera model.

Image registration is a non-linear inverse problem that finds a coordinate transform aligning a moving image to a fixed image, and is widely used in biomedical and life sciences. Existing methods work reliably only at macroscopic scales (~50M warp parameters) and exhaust memory at higher resolutions, where problems can require up to 11B parameters. The paper identifies three key memory bottlenecks—deformable interpolation and warp composition, cross-correlation loss, and mutual information loss—and proposes fused CUDA kernels: a composite implicit grid sampler, implicit Parzen windowing for mutual information, and fused local normalized cross-correlation, reducing HBM usage and fitting problems up to 64× larger on a single GPU. It further introduces Flash Fused Distributed Primitives (FFDP), a distributed framework combining Grid Parallel sharding with boundary synchronization, a ring sampler that avoids allgather of the moving image, and distributed loss functions, scaling to an arbitrary number of GPUs. The authors demonstrate registration of a 250µm in-vivo MRI to a 100µm ex-vivo human brain FLASH volume—over 570× larger than standard clinical data, with over 11.8B transform parameters—in about one minute on 8 A6000 GPUs. FFDP accelerates traditional registration pipelines by up to 7.48× with up to 59% memory reduction, and deep learning pipelines by up to 6.14× with up to 24% less memory. On a simulated 250µm ex-vivo brain MRI dataset (faux-OASIS), the method improves accuracy where baselines degrade—increasing Dice by 18.1 points and reducing average HD90 by 62.1%—while being Pareto-efficient in accuracy versus compute cost.

This paper investigates the relationship between Artificial Intelligence (AI), Big Data (BD), and Advanced Analytics (AA) within digital business platforms. It develops a multidimensional data-driven AI innovation taxonomy framework with an AI/BD/AA innovation value chain and related levels of maturity improvement. Using a taxonomy development methodology combining conceptual-to-empirical and empirical-to-conceptual approaches, the author collected qualitative data through literature review and semi-structured interviews with members of the Russian National Technology Initiative. The paper describes seven overlapping technology platforms supporting digital business: information systems, customer experience, data and analytics, IoT, ecosystems, trust, and integration platforms. It proposes an AI/BD/AA micro-level value chain comprising four key activities: Big Data Acquisition, Curation, Storage, and Usage. The study presents a five-level AI maturity framework, ranging from Human Led/Initial Analytics to Machine Controlled/Advanced Analytics IV, mapping analytics maturity levels to value chain stages. The framework is intended to help organizations evaluate AI-based transformation initiatives, identify industry and functional use cases where AI can automate specific tasks, and support strategic innovation planning. The conclusion emphasizes that organizations must transform their people, processes, technology, and data readiness, and that business and IT leaders should embrace AI and participate in discussions of AI ethics to avoid negative unintended consequences for organizations and society.

A Georgia appeals court affirmed Robert Pearl Bryson's convictions for two counts of aggravated sodomy, four counts of aggravated child molestation, one count of child molestation, and two counts of failure to register as a sex offender. The court found the evidence sufficient on all challenged counts: penetration is not required for aggravated sodomy, only contact; the jury could infer intent to arouse from the circumstances of the kiss underlying the child molestation count; and Bryson's departure from the state for over a year without notifying the sheriff supported the failure-to-register conviction. The court also upheld the denial of Bryson's motions to quash the indictment (untimely and meritless, as a sheriff's wife serving on the grand jury was not error), the denial of trial counsel's motion to withdraw on the eve of trial, the denial of his motion to sever the failure-to-register counts, and the admission of his prior no contest plea, which was admissible to show a conviction for registration purposes. Bryson's ineffective assistance claim was deemed waived because he declined to raise it in the trial court.

The Supreme Court of Mississippi affirmed Ulysses S. Gandy's second manslaughter conviction and ten-year sentence stemming from a June 26, 1976, two-car collision on Highway 25 near Starkville, in which Daniel Palmer and his two passengers were killed. Gandy's first conviction had previously been reversed and remanded. On appeal, Gandy raised four assignments of error: that the verdict was contrary to the overwhelming weight of the evidence, that the court wrongly refused Instruction D-13, that State's Exhibits 1, 5, and 7 were improperly admitted, and that the jury was denied a recess for food during deliberations. The court held that conflicting testimony regarding vehicle positions and Gandy's intoxication was for the jury to resolve, and sufficient evidence supported the finding that an intoxicated Gandy drove into the wrong lane, constituting culpable negligence causally connected to the deaths. The refused instruction was properly declined, as other instructions adequately presented the intoxication issue. The sketches were admissible because witnesses used them to illustrate scenes they personally observed rather than to reconstruct the collision. The jury-recess claim was without merit. The judgment was affirmed.

This document is a specification update for the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device (Silicon Revision A3, March 2006), listing errata items 100–116. Key issues include: SSMI events may not be signaled before the triggering I/O completes if an interrupt request occurs simultaneously, making SSMI generation unreliable (use the Geode GX processor instead); UDMA transfers fail if the IDE bus master is enabled before the PIO command packet (use the normal PIO-first procedure); most wake event inputs (GPIO[27:24]) do not function from the ACPI S3 state (use PWRBTN#); RTC CMOS RAM may return incorrect data when a write to the extended port is followed by a legacy port read; LPC I/O cycles can fail during block and demand mode legacy DMA (use single transfer mode); USB controller clock gating causes register read failures when idle (disable clock gating); an ATAPI CD-ROM with specific firmware could reset the bus master engine on early interrupts (firmware since revised); the AuxOutputFull bit is incorrectly cleared on Port 60h reads (use interrupts for PS/2 emulation); tACK bits have no effect, though the fixed 30 ns timing satisfies all UDMA modes; ATAC can hang with WORD-aligned PRDs (use DWORD alignment); the LPC controller may abort transactions with certain LPC-to-ISA bridges (a PLD workaround is available); the SMB NEGACK bit may set late or clear unexpectedly (write twice to SMB_STS); the GLPCI retry counter counts all bus retries, not just its own (adjust or disable the limit); atomic writes to GPIO High Bank Feature Bit Registers clear non-selected bits after suspend (use read-modify-write); the SMBus data hold time falls short of the 300 ns specification; LOWBAT_FLAG is not set after abnormal standby; and SLEEP_X/SLEEP_Y may not deassert if delay counters exceed the PM_SED delay (program smaller values). The document concludes with AMD copyright and disclaimer text.

The authors developed a meta-population model, based on an extended age-structured SIR framework, to quantify the contribution of contacts in different social settings to SARS-CoV-2 transmission using Google Community Mobility Reports (GCMR), which measure daily activity levels relative to a pre-pandemic baseline. The model assumed a linear relationship between GCMR activity and contacts in four settings (Retail and recreation, Grocery and pharmacy, Transit stations, Workplaces), with additive contributions to transmissibility, while temperature (a seasonality proxy) and the Alpha and Delta variants of concern acted multiplicatively on the infection probability per contact. Residential and Park settings were excluded due to implausibility of the linear assumption and minimal outdoor transmission. A region- and week-specific parameter captured infections outside these settings. The model was fitted Bayesianly (Hamiltonian Monte Carlo in Stan) to weekly hospitalization counts for 11 Norwegian and 21 Swedish regions (February 2020–July 2021), accounting for age-prioritized vaccination, and to two German regions (Bavaria and Berlin) for February–December 2020.

The model fit hospitalization data well. A 20°C temperature increase reduced transmissibility by approximately 40%. Delta approximately doubled transmissibility; Alpha showed a ~20% increase in Norway but no clear evidence in Sweden. The model attributed 60.0% of infections in Sweden and 38.7% in Norway to the four GCMR settings, with county-level variation (27.5–73.3%). Transit stations and Workplaces were the most important settings at baseline activity in Norway and Sweden. In the German regions, GCMR settings explained a larger share of infections (64.5% Bavaria, 69.7% Berlin), with Retail & recreation being most important—opposite to the Nordic countries.

The authors conclude that GCMR data show a clear association with SARS-CoV-2 dynamics and are useful for real-time assessment of population activity, but their non-standard definition requires strong assumptions (linearity, temporally constant effects, all-or-nothing vaccination) and complex modeling, potentially limiting causal interpretability. More direct measurements of contact frequencies would be desirable in the future.

The speaker accepts his party's nomination for President at a convention in Dallas, thanking Texas for its hospitality. He frames the election as a choice between two visions of governing—the opposition's, which he characterizes as pessimism, big government, and higher taxes, versus his party's hope, growth, and individual freedom. He criticizes the opposition's economic record, citing double-digit inflation, high interest rates, tax increases, and rising poverty, and credits his administration with economic recovery, including 6.5 million new jobs, low inflation, record business incorporations, and increased family purchasing power. On defense and foreign policy, he cites military rebuilding, repaired alliances, support for Israel and Latin American allies, and the Grenada rescue mission, which he defends against comparisons to Soviet actions. He calls for a balanced budget amendment, line-item veto, tax simplification, anticrime legislation, tuition tax credits, and enterprise zones, and urges the Soviet Union to rejoin nuclear arms reduction negotiations. He describes the election as a choice of "up or down"—toward statism or individual liberty—and states his party rejects intolerance and bigotry. Reflecting on his Democratic origins and his party's record since 1980, he closes with imagery of the Olympic torch relay and the Statue of Liberty's "golden door."

This passage from a Texas Instruments datasheet (covering the ADS8681W, ADS8685W, and ADS8689W) includes an ESD caution stating that integrated circuits can be damaged by electrostatic discharge, with effects ranging from subtle performance degradation to complete device failure, and that precision ICs may be more susceptible. The revision history notes that from Revision * (June 2024) to Revision A (May 2025), the document status of the ADS8685W and ADS8689W changed from Advance Information to Production Data. The document also covers mechanical, packaging, and orderable information, with footnotes explaining status, material type, RoHS values, lead finish/ball material, MSL ratings and peak reflow temperatures, and part markings. A disclaimer states TI provides technical data and resources "as is" without warranties, limits its liability to the annual purchase price of the parts sold, and states users are solely responsible for product selection, design, validation, and meeting applicable standards.

Grief is an emotional reaction to losing someone or something a person cares about, and it is a unique, personal experience shaped by many factors. It can follow bereavement, life changes such as becoming a carer, declining health, retirement, or moving out of a long-term home, and it can cross generations. Grief may also arise before an impending loss, known as anticipatory grief, which allows time to say goodbye. Rather than following sequential stages, grieving is complex and variable, with possible emotions including numbness, denial, acceptance and relief, yearning and searching, restlessness and disturbed sleep, loss of confidence, guilt, anger, and profound sadness or depression. There is no fixed duration for grief, but most people eventually find good days outnumber bad ones. Support from friends, family, GPs, and specialist organisations can help.

An email dated July 10, 2001, from Ann M Schmidt compiles news articles covering Enron and the California energy crisis. Key items: Los Angeles Times reports show California's power crisis involved more diverse suppliers than Gov. Davis claimed, with public entities such as Powerex ($498/megawatt-hour), a Sempra subsidiary, and LA's Department of Water and Power ($292) charging higher average prices than the criticized private firms Dynegy, Duke, and Mirant ($146-$240), while the state spent nearly $8 billion on power in five months. Senator Joe Dunn accused Duke Energy of refusing to release price bidding data from its Chula Vista plant for a price-gouging probe; Duke says it is complying. After 15-day settlement talks failed, FERC judge Curtis Wagner will recommend a refund plan worth hundreds of millions to possibly $1 billion, far below California's $8.9 billion demand; generators offered $716.1 million. Multiple articles cover Enron's Dabhol project in India: CEO Neil McGregor resigned after his contract expired; the $2.9 billion project (Enron holding 65%) is in a payment dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board, with Phase II construction halted at 85% completion; Chairman Kenneth Lay met Indian officials, said Enron has no immediate plans to quit India, and sought CII's help in resolving the dispute. Tropic Networks revealed Enron Broadband Services and Anschutz Investment Co. as key investors in its $60-million financing. A Chicago Tribune analysis notes Enron shares fell 43% this year amid setbacks but rate a "buy" from analysts. Power producers are expected to meet second-quarter earnings targets despite June price declines. A judge ruled California's attorney general may share subpoenaed documents from Reliant, Mirant, and Dynegy with Oregon and Washington.

The New England Patriots had one of their worst offensive performances of the Tom Brady era against the Miami Dolphins on Monday night, but still trailed by only seven in the final minute. Stephen Gostkowski's onside kick attempt appeared bizarre, and the Dolphins recovered it to win the game.

Researchers led by Joshua Caldwell of Vanderbilt University reported in Nature Materials a fundamental improvement in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN), an optical material used in hyperlensing. By creating hBN crystals from isotopically purified boron—natural boron's two isotopes degrade infrared optical properties—they enhanced imaging resolution by about a factor of ten, potentially resolving objects as small as 30 nanometers. Isotopic purity reduced optical losses, tripling the lifetime and travel distance of surface phonon polaritons that allow hBN to surpass the diffraction limit. Unlike electron or atomic-force microscopes, hyperlenses could image living cells in their natural environments using low-energy infrared light, which also provides spectroscopic "fingerprinting" of materials. The researchers suggest another tenfold improvement is theoretically possible. Potential applications include biological and medical science, communications, and nanoscale optical components.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system from Texas Instruments. It offers two data averaging modes to improve SNR: simple averaging (reduces output data rate by a factor of 2) and moving averaging (does not affect output data rate). The device supports test patterns—fixed, digital ramp, and alternating—for debugging and verifying the data interface, configured for channel groups CH[4:1] and CH[8:5]. The device is reset via the RESET pin or a register write and powered down via the PWDN pin or register; an initialization sequence of register writes is required after power-up or reset, with a free-running sampling clock connected beforehand. A speed-boost mode enables up to 8MSPS sampling for one user-selected channel pair while the remaining six channels idle. Configuration uses SPI with 16-bit registers across three banks, and multiple devices can be connected in a daisy-chain topology. In ATE applications, the device achieves a post-calibration total unadjusted error of 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C and settles multiplexed PMU signals to 99.95% full-scale in 7.5µs in wide-bandwidth mode. It uses three power supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, IOVDD) with no required power-up sequence, and layout recommendations include placing bypass capacitors close to power-supply and reference pins.

Ocean acidification from absorbed carbon dioxide damages calcifying organisms like coral and oysters. Researchers exposed periwinkle sea snails to predicted 2100 conditions (pH 7.85) and found they adapted by producing less-dense inner shells and less-soluble shells, suggesting some calcifying organisms could adapt to acidifying oceans.
The court reversed the judgment and acquitted the defendant, deciding the case on the grounds of its decision in case No. 2037, which was nearly identical except for the amount of the loan.

Beating the offside trap is a subset of defeating offside in general. Unlike normal defense, where backs retreat, the trap has defenders move up, placing strikers in offside positions. To beat it, attackers must recognize the trap through scouting or frequent offside calls, adjust their play to avoid offside, and use the space behind defenders. Patience is needed to avoid offside positions, not interfere with play if offside, and execute tactics. Tactics include dribbling through after faking a pass, through passes to onside receivers, horizontal or lateral runs broken at nearly 90 degrees toward goal, checking runs back toward the ball carrier, short passes, deep-lying runs by midfielders, bending runs starting toward the halfway line, back passes, delaying with square passes and possession play, delayed runs, and a designated non-runner who comes back for a short pass, especially on free kicks. Coaching tips note that fakes can reveal the trap, a defender failing to move up can leave attackers onside, a successful striker will face the goalkeeper one-on-one and must be prepared to score, and opponents are less likely to use the trap again.

Netflix shares declined slightly last week, and Jack Hough of Barron's suggested the stock could lose more than half its value, citing Disney's decision to pull content from Netflix starting 2019, Facebook's new video service, competition from Amazon Prime, Netflix's cash-burning, and unconventional accounting. The author counters that competition fears are overblown, noting Netflix's subscriber base more than quadrupled from 23.6 million despite Amazon Prime Video and YouTube. Netflix has also shown pricing flexibility, raising U.S. prices 25% since early 2014 without losing subscribers, and recently increased prices in Australia and Canada. The author argues Netflix's 104 million streaming accounts, growing quarterly, create a moat that allows cost control and attracts content creators, concluding that betting against Netflix is dangerous. The passage ends by promoting Motley Fool's Stock Advisor newsletter, whose 10 recommended stocks do not include Netflix.

A new study published in Pediatrics found that nearly one child dies monthly and about two are injured daily in window blind-related incidents, with nearly 17,000 children under 6 treated in emergency rooms from 1990 to 2015. While most injuries were minor, entanglement—almost always involving window blind cords—accounted for nearly 80% of hospitalizations and over 94% of deaths. Dr. Gary Smith, the study's senior author, calls for mandatory standards requiring blinds with unexposed or inaccessible cords, arguing the current voluntary standard is insufficient. The CPSC approved a petition for mandatory rulemaking in 2014, which remains in its first stage, while the Window Covering Manufacturers Association has proposed updating the voluntary standard to require cordless stock products. Advocates like Linda Kaiser of Parents for Window Blind Safety support mandatory rules.

Ryan Kerr, 26, of Evercreech, admitted a series of attacks, including punching a woman in the face and leaving a man unconscious in a pub toilet. Despite previous convictions and showing no remorse, his defense argued he was a viable prospect for rehabilitation. Judge David Ticehurst remanded him in custody until October 13 while considering sentencing.

China has blacklisted Canadian technology research firm TechInsights and nine subsidiaries, accusing it of endangering national security after it published an analysis of Huawei's advanced AI chips. The Chinese Ministry of Commerce added the firms to its "unreliable entity list," banning them from business with Chinese organisations. The move followed TechInsights' report suggesting Huawei's latest processors contained components from international foundries. Chinese companies and research institutions are now prohibited from collaborating with or supplying data to TechInsights, cutting it off from a significant market. Analysts say the ban reflects China's tightening control over information flows and deepening global tensions in the race for semiconductor dominance.

Chef and cookbook author Shannon Bard announced Wednesday the permanent closure of Zapoteca, the Portland restaurant she owned with her husband Tom, citing changed priorities as their five children enter their last years of high school and college. The Bards opened Zapoteca six years ago and still own Toroso, Salud, a cooking school, and a catering company. Bard published "The Gourmet Mexican Kitchen" in 2015 and appeared on Food Network shows, including "Beat Bobby Flay."

Peterborough City Council has pledged £4 million to provide new homes for homeless families and is working with St Michael's Gate residents. Under its Empty Homes strategy, 179 of 574 long-term empty privately-owned homes were brought back into use last year, with 663 returned over five years, generating over £3 million through the New Homes Bonus scheme. Phase Two budget proposals have been published for consultation amid warnings that core government funding will be halved and phased out by the decade's end; Peterborough's grants have already fallen 80 per cent, from £55 million to £10 million, over eight years. Two Public Space Protection Orders appear successful, with littering fines decreasing and unauthorised cycling dropping sharply. A new service, CHUMS, will support children and young people with mild-moderate mental health issues.

The NAAIM Exposure Index, compiled by the National Association of Active Investment Managers, measures the average exposure to US Equity markets reported by its members, based on weekly surveys of firms' equity exposure as of each Wednesday. The indicator line is a two-week moving average of managers' responses and is used to gauge investor sentiment: high readings suggest bullishness and potential market tops, while low readings suggest bearishness and potential market bottoms, making it a possible contrarian indicator. However, the index is not predictive. The author's backtests, including a strategy investing when the weekly reading is below its 10-week moving average (CAGR of 4.4%), showed poor performance, indicating better contrarian indicators exist, such as VIX-based strategies.

Lubrizol Corp. is investing US$80 million to expand its TPU production capacity in North America, Europe, and Asia due to increased demand. New lines were inaugurated in Songjiang, China, and further expansions in Asia and Europe are planned for 2019.

Jeff Horn will defend his WBO welterweight title against Gary Corcoran in Brisbane, aiming to dispel claims that his win over Manny Pacquiao was a hometown decision. Promoter Bob Arum said a victory could lead to major fights in 2018, potentially against Terence Crawford, with Pacquiao possibly returning to the ring. Horn, unbeaten in 18 bouts, upset Pacquiao in July 2017; the disputed decision was upheld by the WBO, though Pacquiao holds a rematch clause but hasn't committed to a date or venue. Corcoran, 17-1 and ranked 10th by the WBO, is the underdog in his first fight outside Britain and Ireland. The buildup featured accusations of head-butting against Horn and biting threats from Corcoran, with both fighters expecting an aggressive bout.

Sanofi confirmed it is being investigated by the European Commission for potentially anticompetitive activity. President Trump announced that Pfizer agreed to offer lower drug prices to Medicaid and directly to patients, and to launch new medicines at prices at parity with other countries; in return, Pfizer will not have to pay certain tariffs on imported drugs if it continues investing in U.S. manufacturing. Pfizer is the first drugmaker to publicly announce such a deal, though details remain undisclosed, and policy experts say the deal's impact on drug affordability remains unclear.

Manchester City hosts Burnley at the Etihad Stadium on January 2, with kickoff at 10:00 AM ET. City needs wins as Chelsea challenge for the title, while Burnley sit just above the relegation zone. Sergio Aguero returns after missing City's 0-3 victory over Hull City. City will look to Kevin de Bruyne and David Silva to break down Burnley's defense, while Andre Gray and Sam Vokes are Burnley's main goal threats.

This study used EEG to investigate neural noise in Tourette syndrome (TS), operationalized as trial-by-trial variability in EEG responses to single-pulse median nerve electrical stimulation (MNS). Nineteen adults with TS and 19 age- and sex-matched healthy controls participated. Results showed no between-group differences in the amplitude, timing, or spatial topography of early and mid-latency somatosensory evoked potential (SEP) components, with two exceptions: a 1ms delay in the P1 component (considered trivial) and a substantially increased P2 (P100) component in the TS group, which is associated with conscious perception of tactile stimuli and was predicted by tic severity (YGTSS-impairment score). Trial-by-trial variability (SD) was substantially increased in the TS group throughout the epoch, while coefficient of variation decreased comparably in both groups following stimulation. Power spectral density analysis showed increased spectral power in the TS group at high-beta and gamma frequencies, yielding a flatter 1/f slope. Inter-trial phase coherence increased post-stimulation in both groups, with altered coherence dynamics in TS. Regression analyses linked measures to YGTSS, PUTS-R, and WASI scores. The findings suggest trial-by-trial recruitment of sensorimotor neural populations is less stable at rest in TS but may normalize in response to stimulation.

Facebook has publicly released a detailed version of its community standards rule book, previously available only in brief form, to clarify what content is permitted on topics such as drug use, bullying, hate speech and violence. The move follows criticism that Facebook does too little against hate speech and terrorism while also being accused of removing content for repressive regimes with little explanation. New policies allow appeals of individual content removals for the first time and provide specific takedown reasons in more cases. The roughly 8,000-word document is updated frequently through a biweekly "Content Standards Forum" led by Monika Bickert, informed by feedback from over 100 outside organizations and experts. The rules include examples like barring drug-use admissions and cursing at minors, but do not address false information or government removal requests under local law.

On June 20, 2017, Apple Inc. consummated the issuance and sale of $1,000,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 3.000% Notes due 2027 under an underwriting agreement dated June 13, 2017 with Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, and Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith Incorporated as representatives. The Notes were issued pursuant to an April 29, 2013 indenture with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A. as trustee, and an officer's certificate dated June 20, 2017. Interest is payable semi-annually on June 20 and December 20, beginning December 20, 2017, and the Notes mature on June 20, 2027. The Notes are Apple's senior unsecured obligations, ranking equally with its other unsecured and unsubordinated debt. The report, signed by Vice President and Corporate Treasurer Gary Wipfler, lists related exhibits including the underwriting agreement, officer's certificate, note form, and legal opinions.

A federal jury in Little Rock cleared retired police lieutenant David Hudson of accusations that he used excessive force when he punched Jon "Chris" Erwin seven times outside the Ferneau restaurant on Oct. 29, 2011. After two days of testimony, the jury unanimously found the force reasonable from Hudson's perspective. The incident, captured on video and widely shared on social media, fueled national debate over police use of force. Erwin's misdemeanor charges were later dropped for procedural reasons, but the judge barred testimony about them. The city of Little Rock and the restaurant's owner settled Erwin's claims before trial, meaning Hudson would have personally paid any damages. Hudson testified he acted under the police department's use-of-force policy, while Erwin maintained he was a victim of excessive force.

The study was approved by Independent Ethics Committees, followed the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP guidelines, and required informed consent. COVID-19 management is mainly supportive; dexamethasone and tocilizumab have demonstrated mortality benefit, while remdesivir shows little benefit. Convalescent plasma may offer passive immunization; a meta-analysis found no mortality benefit, possibly due to differences in timing, volumes, or antibody titers. Investigators hypothesized that early high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma would reduce the proportion of patients requiring mechanical ventilation. The primary objective was to evaluate efficacy and safety of best supportive care with versus without convalescent plasma in hospitalized COVID-19 patients; the secondary objective assessed efficacy versus standard of care by severity, oxygenation, ventilation, and hospitalization.

An email from Toby Kuehl to eight Enron employees shares a November 2001 Texas Monthly article by Mimi Swartz titled "How Enron Blew It," which examines the company's decline. Enron evolved from Houston Natural Gas, merged with InterNorth in 1985 under Ken Lay, into an energy trading giant largely built by Jeff Skilling. Hired as a McKinsey consultant in 1985, Skilling created the Gas Bank model, guaranteeing gas supply and price while Enron profited from transactions. The company expanded into electricity, coal, paper, steel, weather, EnronOnline ($335 billion in online commodity trades in 2000), and broadband. Its culture recruited graduates from top schools with high salaries, uncapped bonuses, and a harsh Performance Review Committee known as "rank and yank." Enron used mark-to-market accounting on an unprecedented scale, booking multi-year profits up front. Rival Rebecca Mark was moved to head Azurix, a water utility venture that failed, leading to her resignation. Skilling became CEO in February 2001 but abruptly resigned after six months. The company's stock fell from a January high of $80 to around $35 amid criticism over the California energy crisis, a costly India power plant, the collapse of the broadband division, and analysts questioning its accounting. Ken Lay resumed leadership, promising to refocus on core businesses.

Finnish press paid little attention to official U.S. statements about the war. Finland was increasingly irritated by German troops, seen as contributing little, yet remained wholly dependent on Germany for military supplies and food. German influence persisted, notably through Press Attaché Metzger's dictatorial treatment of the Finnish press and suppression of parts of the Pope's Christmas message. War weariness deepened: on January 3, the Central Federation of Finnish Trade Unions petitioned the Prime Minister, warning that continued war would worsen difficulties and requesting relief from conditions like food maldistribution. The schism between Socialists and Conservatives appeared to be widening, and popular impatience grew with the Field Marshal's aims of conquest, as soldiers questioned holding Soviet Karelia. It seemed Finnish resistance might eventually be worn down if Russia kept the front moderately active. Chargé Thurston inquired of Vyshinski about rumored Soviet-Finnish conversations; Vyshinski denied knowledge of them. Separately, Mr. Higgs told Finnish representative Toivola that Finnish censorship of Legation telephone calls and anti-American press attacks—possibly German-inspired—risked harming Finland's standing in the United States; Toivola agreed and promised to urge greater caution from Helsinki.

Amazon.com, Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2018 reports net sales of $51.0 billion, up 43% from $35.7 billion in Q1 2017, with net income of $1.6 billion compared to $724 million. Operating income rose to $1.9 billion from $1.0 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $3.27 versus $1.48. The company operates three segments: North America (net sales $30.7 billion, operating income $1.1 billion), International (net sales $14.9 billion, operating loss of $622 million), and AWS (net sales $5.4 billion, operating income $1.4 billion). Sales growth reflected increased unit sales, third-party seller sales, the Whole Foods Market acquisition, and advertising. Amazon adopted new revenue recognition guidance on January 1, 2018, increasing retained earnings by approximately $650 million. On April 12, 2018, Amazon acquired Ring Inc. for approximately $900 million, net of cash acquired. Long-term debt included $24.3 billion of unsecured senior notes outstanding. Operating cash flow was negative $1.8 billion for the quarter, and cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $25.0 billion at fair value. The 2017 Tax Act resulted in a provisional tax benefit of approximately $789 million. Legal and tax matters include patent infringement lawsuits by Smartflash LLC and SRC Labs LLC, an IRS transfer pricing dispute involving approximately $1.5 billion in proposed adjustments (with a Tax Court ruling in Amazon's favor now on appeal), and a European Commission state aid decision with an initial recovery amount of approximately €250 million deposited into escrow. Total contractual commitments as of March 31, 2018 were $119.2 billion. No common stock was repurchased in Q1 2017 or Q1 2018.

A hockey coach discusses his team's finals series against Detroit, saying that tightened penalty calling has affected both teams equally and prevented either side from establishing its style of play. He attributes his team's problems mainly to insufficient quickness moving the puck and getting into defensive position, and does not expect his struggling power play to improve against what he calls the league's best penalty-killing team, filled with intelligent players like Ron Francis. He explains that unfair offensive expectations placed on Sandis caused inconsistency, and that acquiring Hedican and Kevyn Adams allowed him to restructure and strengthen his defense. He prefers fewer penalties for better hockey, rarely speaks to goaltender Arturs Irbe, and plans two general matchup ideas rather than strict line matching. He praises Eric Cole's improvement, notes difficulty rotating all lines, describes his adaptive coaching philosophy and reliance on assistants, confirms Sami Kapanen will stay on the power play point despite tentative play, and says he enjoys coaching's pressure.

This paper addresses process modeling in Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) through the identification and extraction of Ontology Design Patterns (ODPs) for scientific workflows. Noting that existing MSE process ontologies suffer from interoperability and reuse issues, with limited explicit adoption of ODPs, the authors define three requirements for ontology-based process modeling: process structure, data and resources, and project goals and participant roles. They analyze ontologies including P-PLAN, Metadata4Ing, OPMW, WILD, the General Process Ontology, and PMDcore, manually deriving patterns that were reviewed by nine domain experts from NFDI-MatWerk's Linked Open Data Working Group. A baseline method for automated ODP extraction is proposed, embedding natural-language requirements and ontology metadata (labels, definitions, comments) into a shared vector space using sentence transformer models, applying cosine similarity with a threshold, and extracting modules via the ROBOT framework (STAR method with no intermediate classes). Evaluation showed P-PLAN achieved the highest F1-scores for Process and Resource ODPs, while PMDcore supported all three ODP categories. Limitations include bias from annotation quality, sensitivity to requirement wording, and per-ontology processing. Future work involves extending to additional MSE subdomains, integrating ontology mappings, addressing evaluation biases, and developing a platform for publishing extracted patterns.

Florida State linebacker Ethan Pritchard was released from Tallahassee Memorial Hospital on Thursday, nearly six weeks after being shot in the back of the head on Aug. 31 in what authorities described as a case of mistaken identity while he was driving his aunt home. The school said he is alert, responsive and able to communicate, and is being moved to Brooks Rehabilitation in Jacksonville for the next stage of his recovery. Four people were arrested in connection with the shooting. His father thanked supporters, including coach Mike Norvell, hospital staff, and law enforcement.

Old Forge High School seniors Christian Killino, Iain Kerrigan, and Kole Barbetti held a Math-a-thon for their senior project, with students earning donations for St. Jude's Research Hospital by completing math problems, raising $3,864. Rosemarie Corigliano was installed as president of the Wayne Memorial Hospital Auxiliary on June 4 at Lukan's Farm Resort in Hawley, with new officers serving two-year terms; the auxiliary planned two fundraisers, Attic Treasures and the Best of the Eagles Concert. Hannah Perry Burgess, a fifth-generation beekeeper and owner of the Beekeeper's Daughter, presented a honey bee program at the Scranton City DAR meeting focused on conservationism.

GoDaddy gave The Daily Stormer, a neo-Nazi website, 24 hours to move its domain after publisher Andrew Anglin posted an article mocking Heather Heyer, killed when a car struck demonstrators at a white nationalist rally in Charlottesville. GoDaddy said the article could incite additional violence, violating its terms of service. The site then claimed it had been hacked, which contributor Andrew Auernheimer called a prank, noting an alternate domain exists. GoDaddy is only the domain provider, not the host. The site is known for harassment campaigns; Tanya Gersh sued Anglin in April, and the site raised over $152,000 for his legal expenses. Other internet services, including PayPal, have taken similar action.

In July 2021, Public Health Wales investigated an outbreak of Salmonella Typhimurium gastroenteritis linked to an Eid al-Adha celebration barbecue and associated lunch attended by a Cardiff North African community. A cohort study of 36 attendees and a nested case-control study using Firth logistic regression were undertaken. Twenty-two cases were identified within a social network of 43 (attack rate 51%), with illness severe enough that 12 sought emergency hospital care, six were admitted overnight, and one required intensive care. Consumption of a traditional raw liver dish, 'marrara', was the most likely vehicle of infection (adjusted OR 49.99, 95% CI 1.71–1461.54, p=0.02). Whole genome sequencing showed genetically indistinguishable isolates (0 SNP difference) from human cases, leftover raw lamb, the two local butchers, and the supplying abattoir, suggesting widespread sheep meat contamination and cross-contamination during food preparation. Some cases were co-infected with STEC or Campylobacter. Sequenced cases also belonged to a larger ongoing 5-SNP cluster dating back to 2018, spread across Wales, Scotland, and England. Culturally sensitive community engagement produced food safety messaging and educational sessions. The investigation identified a traditional raw offal dish as a new vehicle of interest, highlighting the need for outbreak questionnaires to consider community-specific dishes and for targeted food hygiene advice.

In a post-game interview, the coach said his team's play improved after Holik's chance in the second period slowed the game's pace, with the second overtime being their best period. He noted his team had been chasing the series since the first game, with faceoffs being one of the few areas where they held an edge, and that hanging onto the puck helped their confidence grow. He described using three centers with four sets of wingers and putting five players together as a transition unit. He said the game became driven by emotion rather than strategy, that players lacked leg and arm strength by the end, and that the experience recalled lessons from the Edmonton series, such as bringing extra fluids. He acknowledged New Jersey still leads the series—needing one win while his team needs two—and said his team must be better in more areas to win the next game. He cited a third period of mistakes in an earlier game as motivation, noted unusual success on faceoffs on an unfamiliar side of the ice, said both goaltenders played exceptionally, and stated that coaches and management must help players manage emotion. He added that New Jersey had forced his team into uncharacteristic mistakes, but his team stood firm.

A federal appeals court ruled April 7 that the government cannot restrict interstate trade of Burmese pythons and other giant constrictors within the continental U.S., upholding a lower court's finding that the Lacey Act doesn't grant the wildlife service such authority. Snake owners are cautioned not to move their reptiles yet, and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service is reviewing the decision. The ruling doesn't affect import bans or state laws like Florida's pet prohibition. The reptile keepers association, which sued in 2013, called the ban government overreach, while a conservation attorney noted the court didn't address the scientific data justifying it.

Dietician Bonnie Taub-Dix states that fad diets, juice cleanses, and carbohydrate elimination are not healthy or sustainable ways to lose weight. She advocates a non-diet approach focused on building a healthy relationship with food and one's body, which promotes lasting healthy habits. Moderation is key, and dietary fat is an important part of the diet.

The passage asserts that worthy family life is the life best worth living and that wilful sterility threatens national and racial death; those who shirk life's primary duties lose self-respect. Addressing Congress, the speaker urges action on two subjects. First, American shipping: a law based on the House report should pass and would primarily benefit seaboard states such as Maine, Louisiana, and Washington while ultimately benefiting all; if a general law is impracticable, fast mail lines to chief South American ports should be provided, since American business people lack direct steamship communication there and are disadvantaged versus Europeans. Second, currency reform: the national bank act has served well, with per capita circulation rising from $21.41 to $33.08, but crop seasons expose defects, call money fluctuated from 2 to 30 percent, and commerce bears abnormal rates. Complicated proposals and any plan impairing the 2 percent bonds should be ruled out; a feasible Treasury-endorsed plan would let national banks issue capital-proportional notes, taxed highly to drive them back when not needed, to meet emergencies rather than yield bank profits.

Veteran Michael Gordon has signed a two-year NRL deal with the Gold Coast Titans after being released from the final year of his Sydney Roosters contract. The 34-year-old fills the fullback void left by Jarryd Hayne's departure to Parramatta and is expected to assume goal-kicking duties. A former NSW representative who grew up in northern NSW, Gordon's Roosters position had become uncertain following James Tedesco's signing.

The Coppock Curve is a long-term momentum indicator devised by economist E.S.C. Coppock around 1965 under a mandate from the Episcopal Church. It is calculated as a 10-month weighted moving average of the sum of the 11-month and 14-month rate of change values, with parameters derived from Coppock's study on how long it takes to recover from mourning a death. Signals trigger a long entry when the curve crosses above the zero line and an exit when it crosses below. Applied to a monthly S&P 500 chart since 1960, the strategy produced only 12 trades over 63 years, all winners. It reduced drawdowns, kept traders in the market about a quarter less time, and delivered risk-adjusted returns exceeding buy & hold, suggesting it remains valid for exploiting the market's bullish bias.

This passage is a transcript of STAT's "First Opinion Podcast," in which editor Torie Bosch interviews Morgan McSweeney, known online as "Dr. Noc," a biotech employee with a Ph.D. in pharmaceutical sciences and immunology who has millions of social media followers. McSweeney describes his science communication as "edutainment," combining education and entertainment through formats such as reaction videos debunking incorrect health claims and explanatory content on topics like the gut microbiome. He explains that his pseudonym originated from a former video game handle. He says he targets people "in the middle" who are confused about public health rather than those who vehemently disagree, since addressing opponents is emotionally exhausting and unproductive, and that adding nuance reduces reach but better informs viewers. He argues audiences want detailed explanations rather than simple dismissals. McSweeney attributes institutions' limited influencer-style communication to resource constraints, red tape, and the difficulty of producing engaging videos. He keeps his biotech job separate from his content, avoids discussing his work on monoclonal antibody therapeutics for respiratory diseases, and handles negative comments by hiding or blocking rather than responding. Sharing personal details, such as mentioning his wife, builds trust through parasocial relationships, and he regularly offers guest seminars on science communication.

Nick Foles, the Philadelphia Eagles' backup turned Super Bowl starter, took over after Carson Wentz's knee injury ended an 11-2 season and is one win from the franchise's first Super Bowl title against the New England Patriots. Despite a potential championship, Wentz remains the Eagles' franchise quarterback, with indications he's on track to return from a torn ACL by Opening Day 2018. Foles' contract allows him to test free agency after 2018, and teams like the Arizona Cardinals could express trade interest, with Howie Roseman's trade history increasing the likelihood of a move. Foles, known for a quiet demeanor and having nearly retired previously, defers to Wentz as the team's quarterback. The Eagles face a difficult decision on whether retaining Foles as a backup is riskier than trading him at peak value, especially with third-stringer Nate Sudfeld's development. Foles' future remains uncertain regardless of the Super Bowl outcome.

In an address to the 100th Congress during the Constitution's 200th anniversary year, President Reagan cited economic progress, including the lowest inflation in a quarter century, a prime interest rate down from 21.5 to 7.5 percent, nearly 13 million new jobs, and record employment. He acknowledged one major regret: a risk taken with action in Iran that did not work, for which he assumed full responsibility, while pledging not to yield to terrorist blackmail. He criticized Soviet military spending and weapons transfers to client states, called for support of Afghan and Nicaraguan freedom fighters, defended the Strategic Defense Initiative, and threatened to veto measures undercutting national security or negotiating leverage. He supported a political solution in Afghanistan requiring Soviet withdrawal and opposed a "Soviet beachhead" in Central America. On trade, he opposed protectionism and sought a Canada-United States free trade arrangement and participation in the Uruguay round. Domestically, he proposed a balanced budget constitutional amendment, a line-item veto, welfare reform through State-sponsored demonstration projects, legislation addressing catastrophic illness among the elderly, and competitiveness measures including research funding and regulatory reform. He called for raising literacy by 2000, drug-free schools, voluntary prayer in classrooms, and Federal commitments to worker retraining. Concluding with the theme "We the people," he recounted Benjamin Franklin's observation that the sun painted behind Washington's chair was rising rather than setting, asserting that America's best days had just begun.

This passage, from the TMS320DM814x DaVinci Digital Media Processors documentation, describes the L4 Fast and L4 Slow Peripheral Domain memory maps, noting that certain regions are decoded internally by the Cortex-A8 Subsystem and are not physically part of the L4 Slow. It explains the DDR DMM TILER Extended Addressing Map, which provides an additional 4 GB of addressing via a 33rd address bit for accessing frame buffers in rotated and mirrored views; this range is accessible only to the HDVPSS and ISS subsystems, while other masters can access a single view through the 512-MB TILER region. The passage also covers package pin assignments and terminal functions tables, which identify signal names, pin multiplexing, pin types, internal pullup/pulldown states, supply voltage, and pin functions. It further details boot configuration pins multiplexed between ARM Cortex-A8 boot mode and GPMC functions, with BTMODE bits sampled at reset to determine boot and peripheral configurations.

A team member addressed insufficient effort during the Stanley Cup Final, saying players must not be outworked and should play for each other; he was shocked the issue arose at this stage. The author wrote this book after years of building distributed systems from scratch, where reusing components was difficult. Containers and orchestrators changed this landscape by enabling reusable components and shared patterns. The book provides practitioners a common language and collection of repeatable patterns to make reliable distributed system development more efficient.

The NDSU Faculty Senate sent a draft resolution to all 11 North Dakota University System campuses declaring a "crisis of confidence" due to budget cuts, misguided consolidation, and lack of support for higher education. It calls on the State Board of Higher Education and Chancellor Mark Hagerott to improve advocacy and proposes a Higher Education Summit with stakeholders, the SBHE, and Gov. Burgum. The lecture covers financing sustainable real estate at the asset level through debt (mortgages) and private equity. Sustainable finance emerged around 2020 when BlackRock CEO Larry Fink declared climate risk a financial risk in his letter to CEOs. Real estate links space and capital markets through a four-quadrant model; investors compare a property's market return to a weighted average cost of capital or evaluate NPV. Portfolio theory shows that adding green buildings as a fourth asset class (alongside bonds, stocks, and brown real estate) shifts the efficient frontier northwest—green buildings offer higher returns and lower risk—and attracts capital. Sustainable finance incorporates externalities into asset pricing: regulations (e.g., Local Law 97) and tenant/investor preferences raise green building values, while brown buildings face penalties, fleeing tenants, and risk premiums. Early "frontrunner" investors earn excess returns before equilibrium returns decline as capital flows in. Climate risk increases mortgage default risk; a wildfire study found defaults rose 1% in affected zones. Government-subsidized mortgages and flood insurance create systemic problems, and accurately pricing climate risk raises social equity and political dilemmas. Green or energy-efficient mortgages permit larger loans because energy efficiency lowers default risk (energy-efficient homes are one-third less likely to default) and reduces monthly energy bills, freeing income for repayment. EU renovation-wave financing lends extra funds upfront for renovations, anticipating post-renovation appreciation. Private equity commingled funds (GP/LP structures) increasingly integrate ESG into investment processes, aligning social value with business value.

The National Weather Service in Lubbock issued updated zone forecasts for the South Plains area of Texas on Sunday, March 18, 2018, covering counties including Lubbock, Childress, Parmer, Castro, Swisher, Briscoe, Hall, Bailey, Lamb, Hale, Floyd, Motley, Cottle, Cochran, Hockley, Crosby, Dickens, King, Yoakum, Terry, Lynn, Garza, Kent, and Stonewall. Treasury market bears recovered some losses after safe-haven buying driven by Italian political instability forced traders to close wrong-way positions. Havant Borough Council in Hampshire has banned bouncy castles and inflatables on its land until an inquiry establishes the cause of an inflatable trampoline explosion that killed a three-year-old girl at Gorleston Beach, Norfolk.

Italian and Spanish Wikipedia blocked all articles on 3 July in protest of the EU Copyright Directive, the first update to European copyright legislation since 2001. The European Committee on Legal Affairs voted in favour of the directive, with the EU parliamentary vote scheduled for 5 July. Goalie Michael Leighton recalled his daughter being born the day before a game he remembers well and credited Jeff Reese with changing his style successfully. A blitz is a defensive play in which five or more defenders rush into the offensive backfield to pressure the quarterback or ball carrier, exceeding the typical four-man pass rush. Because blitzing leaves fewer defenders to cover receivers and can be evaded by mobile quarterbacks, it carries risk, but a well-timed blitz can be highly disruptive. Defensive coordinators call blitzes, which come in several types: zone blitzes, where a linebacker rushes while a lineman drops into coverage; safety, cornerback, and zero blitzes, which involve riskier coverage trade-offs; and run blitzes aimed at stopping running plays. Offenses can beat the blitz through quick passes—often to the running back—mobile quarterback play, or max protection schemes that keep extra players in to block.

The passage defines market sentiment as the aggregate attitude of market participants—bullish, neutral, or bearish—citing Benjamin Graham's "Mr. Market" analogy. The AAII sentiment index, published weekly since the 1980s by the American Association of Individual Investors, surveys members on their six-month outlook for the stock market and is described as the most widely used sentiment indicator, alongside others like Investors Intelligence Bulls & Bears and the VIX. Sentiment indicators work on contrarian logic: extreme bullishness suggests most participants have already bought, limiting further upside, while extreme bearishness means little is needed to trigger a reversal. Backtests of the AAII index show that going long on bearish readings (bull-bear spread below -20) produced an average gain of 1.03% per trade over four weeks, while bullish readings above 20 yielded 0.52%, and readings above 40 produced an average loss of 0.33%. The authors conclude that bullish readings are followed by lower returns than bearish ones, but argue better indicators exist for short-term trading.

Rapid technological and social development means initial LIS education (bachelor, master) in Romania cannot fully prepare graduates for specialised labour market requirements, making lifelong learning indispensable. Romania's library system comprises the National Library, public, academic, school and specialised libraries, administered by the Ministries of Education and Culture and local authorities, with two professional associations. Academic LIS education, ignored during the communist period, began after 1999; of seven initial universities, four remain. Three training paths exist: a Bachelor in LIS (unattractive due to low prestige and salaries); a Bachelor in another field plus a post-graduation LIS programme (preferred by most librarians, though paradoxically supplying only initial education); and a Bachelor plus competences assessed through Occupational Standards (encouraged by public libraries, notably via the BIBLIONET programme, but difficult to certify). Non-formal training includes library visits, conferences, and tutorship/mentorship. Despite legal requirements, few libraries fund staff training. The National Library of Romania developed the Occupational Standard "Librarian (Higher Education)," acknowledged by the National Authority for Qualifications, detailing professional competences and activities. The authors recommend adding competences such as institutional internationalisation, information literacy education, and reading promotion, and note that negative stereotyping of the profession deters youth, requiring new strategies from higher education institutions and methodological libraries.

This paper develops a theoretical framework for information design that integrates framing effects—where the presentation of information influences receiver beliefs—into the classic Bayesian persuasion model. Motivated by behavioral economics findings (e.g., Tversky and Kahneman) that persuasion effectiveness depends on framing beyond quantitative signal correlations, the authors model framing as a mapping from natural language descriptions to receiver beliefs via a "belief oracle," which LLMs can approximate. They study three sender optimization variants: recommendation-only, framing-only, and joint framing-and-recommendation. Theoretically, framing-only optimization is NP-hard even to approximate, and sender utility is discontinuous in the induced belief, making it sensitive to oracle errors. In contrast, joint optimization yields continuous utility and admits a quasi-polynomial-time approximation scheme (QPTAS). Empirically, the authors propose a hill-climbing method combining LLMs (for generating framings and predicting beliefs) with analytical optimization of recommendation schemes, validated through case studies (a realtor pitching to buyers and a clothing brand's advertising campaign) and human subject experiments, where predictions were directionally correct and approximated effect magnitudes, though human responses showed more variance. The work characterizes when LLM-based persuasion design is tractable and offers a scalable procedure for organizations to jointly select framings and recommendations.

The passage describes container-based design patterns for distributed systems. It first covers the adapter pattern, a single-node pattern in which an adapter container modifies an application container's interface to conform to a standardized interface. Examples include adapting Redis for Prometheus monitoring, normalizing logging formats to stdout using Fluentd, and adding rich health checks to a MySQL container via a separate adapter. The pattern provides modularity, reuse, and decoupling of application and adapter containers.

The passage then introduces multi-node distributed patterns and microservices, which decompose applications into small, independently scalable services communicating over defined APIs. Benefits include team decoupling and independent scaling; drawbacks include more difficult debugging and design.

Key patterns described:
- Replicated load-balanced services: stateless services replicated for redundancy and scaling, using readiness probes, session tracking (IP hashing or cookies), caching layers (Varnish), rate limiting, and SSL termination (nginx), with Kubernetes deployment examples.
- Sharded services: each shard serves a subset of requests, suited to stateful services whose data exceeds a single machine's capacity. Topics include sharded caching, sharding functions (hashing plus modulo), shard key selection, consistent hashing to limit remapping during resharding, and handling hot shards through replication.
- Scatter/gather: requests are dispatched in parallel to all leaf nodes, which return partial results that the root merges; useful for parallelizable work such as document search, but constrained by per-node overhead and the straggler problem; replicating each shard improves reliability.
- Functions and event-driven processing (FaaS): functions simplify deployment and scale automatically, but complicate debugging, limit background processing and in-memory data, and can become costly under sustained load. Patterns include decorators for request/response transformation, asynchronous event handlers such as two-factor authentication, and event-based pipelines.

Committee members pushed back over two days, and at the end of Tuesday's session submitted their own definition, to be discussed Wednesday. The committee will meet this week and again in November before voting; without unanimous consensus, the department may propose its own regulations subject to public comment. This MIT lecture covers the second-order wave equation utt = c²uxx and its equivalent first-order system form, whose symmetric matrix has eigenvalues ±c, indicating waves traveling in both directions at speed c. Real problems involve variable coefficients and forcing terms; high frequencies in electromagnetism require very small delta x for accuracy. The leapfrog method is introduced as a new approach. Analysis begins with the continuous equation, where exponentials yield solutions traveling along characteristics at speeds ±c with no dispersion. The semidiscrete method (method of lines) discretizes space only, replacing k² with (2−2cos(kΔx))/Δx², which introduces dispersion and involves the sinc function, explaining second-order accuracy. The fully discrete method yields a quadratic equation for the growth factor g, with stability requiring both roots to have magnitude ≤ 1, which reduces to the Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy condition r ≤ 1. Staggered grids, a premier method in electromagnetism, will be discussed next.

This study demonstrates high-energy (1 MeV) electron beam irradiation as a controllable method for defect engineering in CVD-grown monolayer MoS2, with defect density tuned by varying exposure time (30–120 s) at fixed beam energy and flux. Raman spectroscopy showed peak shifts and the emergence of LO(M) and LA(M) modes consistent with chalcogen vacancy formation and irradiation-induced disorder. XPS revealed the appearance of Mo5+ and increasing Mo6+ states along with Mo–O bonding upon prolonged exposure, indicating oxidation at sulfur vacancies while sulfur remained largely unaffected. KPFM measurements showed the work function increasing from 4.8 eV to 5.24 eV, indicating irradiation-induced p-type doping attributed to oxygen incorporation at vacancy sites. Temperature-dependent PL spectroscopy revealed a defect-related emission (D peak) 200–300 meV below the A exciton that intensified with irradiation, resolving into deeper (D1, ~1.64 eV) and shallower (D2, ~1.73 eV) states, alongside PL quenching and excitonic blueshift. Power-dependent PL confirmed the bound, saturable nature of the defect states. Circular polarization-resolved PL showed valley polarization decreasing from 62% to 38% with irradiation, attributed to defect-mediated intervalley scattering and carrier trapping. First-principles calculations indicated that sulfur vacancies produce donor states near the conduction band, while oxygen bonding or physisorption at vacancies creates acceptor states near the valence band, yielding net p-type doping; transitions from the conduction band to these acceptor levels explain the observed defect peak, and reduced Γ–K separation supports the observed valley depolarization. The authors conclude that high-energy electron beams provide a reliable, tunable defect engineering approach for monolayer MoS2 that may be extended to other TMDs.

The passage consists of interview remarks, with several attributed to George McPhee, about the Vegas team's Stanley Cup finals run. Gold, historically valued for its beauty and rarity, is now used for speculation and as an inflation hedge. Its price is influenced by supply and demand, the US Dollar's value, investor behavior, central bank reserves, and jewelry demand; a stronger dollar lowers gold prices while a weaker dollar raises them. From 1955 to 2022, gold set 80 monthly all-time highs, though it went 14 years without a new high between 1981 and 2005. The authors backtested a trading strategy for gold at all-time highs using World Bank monthly closing prices. The strategy invests only a third of the time, reduces maximum drawdown, and helps identify bull regimes in gold.

Tencent has added Batman to Arena of Valor as an Assassin-class character with batarangs and forearm blades, joining other DC heroes. The update introduces a Death Match mode with five two-player teams and eight-minute matches, a Valor TV feature for viewing matches, and interface refinements.

The Wing-T offense uses misdirection, unusual formations, and a diverse run game to exploit aggressive, undisciplined defenders by making plays look similar so defenses cannot identify where the ball is going. It was developed by Coach Harold "Tubby" Raymond at the University of Delaware during his tenure from 1966 to 2001, which is why it is often called the Delaware Wing-T.

The offense requires at least two running backs who can threaten to carry the ball, a fullback capable of tough inside running and occasional receiving, an athletic quarterback with good footwork, and smaller, quicker offensive linemen skilled at pulling and trapping. Its main strength is slowing down more physically talented defenses through misdirection, play action, and unusual formations, along with decades of coaching answers and its rarity making it hard to prepare for. Its main weakness is the lack of a traditional dropback pass game, though many teams supplement it with shotgun spread formations.

Common formations include the Wing (100/900), Wing-Slot (Red or Doubles 100), and Unbalanced formations. Common run plays are the Buck Sweep, Down Play (Belly G), and Trap. Common pass plays include the Waggle (Buck Sweep Boot), Single Receiver Option Route, and Play Action Vertical Pass.

The traditional Wing-T is largely extinct in major college football but remains common at the high school level. Coaches like Gus Malzahn have incorporated its principles into modern spread offenses at Auburn and UCF.

The passage is from the Texas Instruments datasheet for the ADS8681W/ADS8685W/ADS8689W. In the ACQ state, the device acquires the analog input signal, entering this state on power-up, after an asynchronous reset, or after each conversion; a low-power NAP mode is available. A rising edge of CONVST/CS moves the device to the CONV state, where conversion uses an internal clock and further CONVST/CS transitions are ignored until conversion completes.

The device features nine configuration registers and supports data write and read operations. A data transfer frame begins at the falling edge of CONVST/CS and ends at the subsequent rising edge. Frames with 32 SCLKs are optimal; shorter frames are treated as NOP for writes (though output data remains valid), and longer frames use the last 32 bits as the command. HWORD commands operate on 16 bits and ignore the LSB of the 9-bit address. Output data words depend on the previous frame's command and DATA_VAL[2:0] bits, with optional flags (device address, range, alarm flags, parity) appended.

The multiSPI interface supports four legacy SPI-compatible protocols for writes and, for reads, single SDO, dual SDO, or source-synchronous (SRC) protocols with selectable internal/external clock; dual SDO halves the required clock cycles. Register maps include DEVICE_ID_REG, RST_PWRCTL_REG (write-protected by a 69h key), SDI_CTL_REG, SDO_CTL_REG, DATAOUT_CTL_REG, RANGE_SEL_REG, ALARM_REG, ALARM_H_TH_REG, and ALARM_L_TH_REG.

The application section describes the ADS868xW as a fully integrated 16-bit SAR ADC with integrated AFE and reference, used in an eight-channel industrial analog input module with the MUX36D08 multiplexer for standard voltage/current ranges. The programmable input alarm with hysteresis is illustrated using an NTC thermistor. Power recommendations cover AVDD/DVDD decoupling, and NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption at low throughput rates. PCB layout guidance addresses analog/digital partitioning and decoupling capacitors. Revision A (May 2025) changed ADS8685W and ADS8689W status from Advance Information to Production Data.

The team of over a dozen members focused on generalist tasks, such as improving chatbot writing—work the company said is in less demand amid an industry shift toward expert-driven data labeling. Corning Incorporated, a materials science company founded in 1851, has innovation as its core identity. The company suffered severely during the 2002 telecommunications crash—revenues fell from $6.3 billion to $3.1 billion, the stock dropped from $100 to $1.50, and the company took a $5.4 billion loss while laying off over 12,000 people. By 2008, Corning had recovered, holding global leadership in LCD glass with its stock trading at $23, and roughly 70% of employees who left during the downturn had returned.

Innovation at Corning is centrally managed by the Growth and Strategy Council (GSC), led by a triumvirate of CEO Wendell Weeks, COO Peter Volanakis, and CTO Joe Miller. Begun in 2001, the GSC meets several times monthly to advise the company's four business segments—Display Technologies, Telecommunications, Environmental Technologies, and Life Sciences—on pacing investments, allocating resources, and maintaining a balanced innovation portfolio. It works alongside the Corning Technology Council (CTC), which handles early-stage projects. Corning spends 10% of revenue on RD&E and follows a stage-gate process focused on creating "keystone components." The company embraces "patient money," sustaining long investment periods before profitability, as with display (14 years) and optical fiber (20 years).

The GSC played key roles in major decisions, including adding diesel filter production for Volkswagen in 2005 and supporting Verizon's fiber-to-the-home program in 2003. Going forward, the GSC faces challenges as Corning aims to double its innovation rate, including maintaining its culture of honest dialogue, prioritizing among growing opportunities, and understanding new business models.

The article presents a long-only trading strategy for the Global X Robotics & Artificial Intelligence ETF (BOTZ), founded in 2016, combining short-term Donchian Channels (length 3) with a 200-period Exponential Moving Average filter to reduce false signals. Optimization was used to test robustness rather than find perfect inputs, since results that change sharply with small parameter adjustments suggest curve fitting. Backtesting on daily data from September 2016 showed nearly all Donchian settings were profitable (Profit Factor 1.25 or above), and the EMA filter improved results across almost all length settings. The final strategy beat Buy and Hold with less volatility, though its low trade count (87) makes results statistically limited and raises curve-fitting concerns. The strategy also showed good results on a 2-hour timeframe, but out-of-sample backtesting and an incubation period are recommended before live trading, and the article is not investment advice.
A speaker reflects on a tough loss, saying the team started well but lost momentum, needs to limit turnovers and make smarter plays, and didn't come through in the third period.

A Knox County judge sentenced three defendants in the 2015 death of 15-year-old football player Zaevion Dobson, who shielded friends from gunfire. Christopher Bassett received life plus 35 years after a jury convicted him of first-degree murder, while Richard Williams III was sentenced to 143 years and Kipling Colbert to 109 years for facilitating the murder.

Japanese and Chinese forces are massing in Korea, with over 4,000 Japanese troops present and Chinese soldiers arriving at Chemulpo. Japan holds Seoul while Chinese forces are encamped 15 miles south. Japan will not withdraw until China guarantees non-interference in Korean affairs except under the 1885 Tientsin convention, which required prior written notice before sending troops; China allegedly notified Japan only after its troops had landed. Li Hung Chang reportedly holds plenipotentiary powers by secret imperial edict, though war was said to be regretted during the Empress's birthday year. Japan's army numbers 120,000, while Li alone commands 50,000 foreign-drilled troops plus larger reserves. Foreign representatives proposed simultaneous withdrawal; China refused, stating its troops must remain since Japan would not withdraw. The Empress set aside 60,000,000 taels for the conflict, canceling birthday celebrations. Japanese troops occupy strategic points around Seoul and control the river and roads. The American minister agreed to grant asylum to Korea's royal family if necessary and increased the legation guard to 120 men. Japan's minister presented a demand for radical changes in Korea's government before troop withdrawal.

The passage discusses the S&P Financial Services sector, comprising S&P 500 companies classified under the GICS Financial Services sector, including banks, investment houses, insurance firms, and fintech companies. The sector is tracked by the Vanguard Financials ETF (VFH) and Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLF). Its five largest stocks by market capitalization as of July 21, 2022, are Berkshire Hathaway, JP Morgan Chase, Bank of America, Citigroup, and Goldman Sachs.
