A backtested XLF trading strategy produced 198 trades with a 1.05% average gain, 73% win rate, 21% max drawdown, and 2.25 profit factor. The sector is highly correlated with the overall market but is considered a good trading vehicle due to its high volatility.

This work presents a simple, robust, and scalable fabrication method for visible-wavelength Fabry–Perot microcavities using buckled dielectric membrane mirrors. Starting from double-side polished silicon wafers, repeated wet thermal smoothing reduces surface roughness to ~33–50 pm, followed by ion beam sputtering of 21 pairs of SiO₂/Ta₂O₅ quarter-wave layers with a SiO₂ capping layer. Photolithography and a Bosch etch suspend the coating, which buckles under built-in compressive strain to form concave micromirrors (600 µm diameter), with reliable fabrication of radii of curvature from 0.9 mm to 21 mm and perfect rotational symmetry.

Using a swept ring-down measurement at 780 nm, the cavities achieve a maximum finesse of 0.89 × 10⁶ (linewidth κ = 2π × 233 kHz) and a maximum quality factor of 2.3 × 10⁹ (κ = 2π × 124 kHz) over cavity lengths of 66–3750 µm. Finesse decreases with cavity length due to diffractive loss. Loss analysis bounds scattering plus absorption at ≤ 2.20 ppm, implying surface roughness ≤ 90 pm, and extrapolates to a finesse of 3.5 × 10⁶ at telecom wavelengths.

Glued cavity assemblies with 45 µm and 1 mm cavity lengths show finesses of 0.616 × 10⁶ and 0.263 × 10⁶, linewidth κ = 2π × 5.16 MHz, and a free spectral range of 3.18 THz, demonstrating integrability. Proposed applications include quantum networking, neutral-atom and ion-trap systems, visible lasers, sensing, filtering, and laser stabilization.

Amazon is developing a top-secret domestic robot, codenamed "Vesta," overseen by Gregg Zehr of its Lab126 hardware division. The project began a few years ago, and hiring has ramped up this year. Amazon reportedly aims to seed robots in employees' homes by year's end and with consumers possibly by 2019, though the timeline could change. The company declined to comment. The robot's tasks are unclear, but it may function as a mobile Alexa; prototypes feature advanced cameras and computer vision software. The project differs from Amazon Robotics' warehouse robots. Earlier home robots like the Topo sold poorly; iRobot's Roomba is the field's standout. Advances in computer vision, artificial intelligence, and voice activation could make Amazon's robot feasible, in a market projected to reach $15 billion by 2023.

The disclosure relates to digital twin simulations. A digital twin is a virtual representation of a physical asset that tracks changes over its lifespan using real-time data from sensors and IoT devices, allowing users to monitor performance, predict future behavior, and diagnose or optimize the asset. Embodiments describe a computer-implemented method, system, and computer program product for executing digital twin simulations that bypass one or more input parameters. A processor captures a real-time data feed from a data collection device connected to a physical asset to create a digital twin model, creates multiple versions of the model reflecting changes to components and performance over time, configures simulation input by selecting a version and one or more components to bypass, and outputs simulation results. Users may simulate the current model, a previous version, or a hybrid model combining components from multiple versions, which can be built via a graphical interface or augmented reality. Simulations may substitute alternative components for bypassed ones, isolate selected portions, and use user-provided overriding values as inputs for non-simulated components. Intermediate simulation results can be verified and fed into downstream components. A host system hosts a digital twin module comprising a creation engine, data collection engine, version management, simulation engine, and reporting engine; an alternative embodiment containerizes the module. New model versions are created from self-reported changes or deviations detected in collected performance data, timestamped, and stored in a repository along a timeline. The reporting engine displays and archives results, and users may revise parameters or re-run simulations.

Nigeria is experiencing a consumer revolution, with shopping malls opening across the country, particularly in Lagos, creating jobs and boosting tax revenue. Factors driving this growth include one-stop shopping convenience, brand consciousness, and demand for after-work shopping. Over five upscale malls have opened, with retailers like Shoprite and Spar expanding their outlets. Ibukun Efuntayo & Co executives say the malls reflect investor confidence, suit changing lifestyles, and provide direct employment to thousands of Nigerians.

The offering is needed to meet the 15% minimum public ownership rule after merging with Ginebra San Miguel and San Miguel Brewery to form San Miguel Food and Beverage, Inc.

Exeter City manager Paul Tisdale said his side could be proud despite a 1-0 defeat to Luton Town, decided by Harry Cornick's deflected strike. The device's post-boot state is determined by sampling BTMODE[15:0] pins at reset de-assertion, with values latched into the CONTROL_STATUS register. BTMODE[15:11] configures GPMC CS0 settings, BTMODE[4:0] sets boot mode order with fallback modes, BTMODE[7:5] are reserved, BTMODE[9:8] selects Ethernet PHY mode, and BTMODE[10] selects GPMC muxing for XIP boot.

This patent application, a continuation of several prior applications titled "Security Appliance," describes a network security appliance incorporating a local touch screen or similar input/output interface for command and control, eliminating the need for network-based administration. During denial of service attacks, commands from the local interface receive priority access to processing resources and memory, enabling mitigating actions such as shutting down ports, blacklisting packet sources, or modifying filter rules without requiring a manual reboot or network disconnection.

The application also describes geoprocessing-based packet processing, in which filter parameters (such as IP address ranges) are mapped to minimum bounding rectangles and searched using R-tree indexes, reducing search times significantly compared to B-tree searches (e.g., 0.05 seconds versus 1.5 seconds). Multidimensional regions can incorporate multiple filter parameters simultaneously.

Rules are divided into mandatory rules addressing known or active threats, distributed to all appliances, and potential rules addressing inactive threats, distributed to a subset of appliances according to likelihood scores or weights. A management server maintains the rules database and generates per-device rule sets, reducing memory, bandwidth, and CPU usage while providing early attack warnings; detected attacks increase a rule's distribution to 100%, while undetected rules may have their likelihood reduced.

The security device may include processors, network interfaces, a packet processing engine, multi-touch displays, indicator lights, and memory. Methods are described for detecting attack packets, authenticating administration requests, reserving resources for the local user interface during attacks, and quarantining packets from unrecognized new devices until authorized via physical interaction with the local interface.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting results of its Annual Meeting of Shareholders held on March 10, 2015. Shareholders elected seven directors: Tim Cook, Al Gore, Bob Iger, Andrea Jung, Art Levinson, Ron Sugar, and Sue Wagner. Approved proposals included ratification of Ernst & Young LLP as the Company's independent registered public accounting firm for 2015, an advisory resolution to approve executive compensation, and an amendment to the Employee Stock Purchase Plan increasing authorized shares by 50,000,000. Two shareholder proposals, "Risk Report" and "Proxy Access for Shareholders," were not approved. The amended and restated Employee Stock Purchase Plan was filed as Exhibit 10.1. The report was signed by D. Bruce Sewell, Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary, on March 13, 2015.

Chat apps are evolving into ecosystems of products and services, as WeChat already offers meal ordering, cab booking, and gaming. WhatsApp, with 94% reach in India, is adding voice/video calls and payments. Content drives user engagement, boosted by cheap data from Reliance Jio. Hike, backed by Airtel, launched payments before WhatsApp and could bundle Airtel TV and Wynk content. Gaming, like the Gamepind JV between AGTech Holdings and Paytm, is another engagement tool. India's internet is becoming an oligopoly backed by global conglomerates, and winning chat could define the next decade.

Research shows that high-stakes standardized testing shapes curriculum and instruction, with teachers narrowing lessons to match tests. Some states extend this burden to private schools through choice programs, such as Wisconsin's requirement that participants take the state's Forward Exam and a nearly passed 2023 Texas bill tying private schools to state assessments. College entrance exams are also used to evaluate high schoolers: Oklahoma ties scholarships solely to ACT scores, Wisconsin and North Carolina require the ACT for choice program students, and several states mandate the SAT or ACT for graduation. The passage argues these tests are increasingly degraded, citing shortened SAT passages aligned with Common Core, a 240 percent spike in top AP Literature grades amid declining reading scores, and a 71-point drop in SAT math rigor from 2008 to 2023. Rather than banning testing—which universities reversed after trying test-optional admissions—the author advocates testing choice, pointing to the Classic Learning Test as a validated alternative with a 0.89 score correlation to the SAT. The passage recommends that states offer menus of assessments for school choice programs and accept multiple tests for public college admissions and scholarships, citing Arkansas and Florida as examples.

The Supreme Court will hear oral arguments on Oct. 7 in a challenge to Colorado's 2019 ban on providing conversion therapy to minors. Kaley Chiles, a licensed counselor in Colorado Springs, argues the ban violates her free speech rights because her counseling uses only speech, making the law content- and viewpoint-based discrimination subject to strict scrutiny. She contends Colorado lacks a compelling interest, since no study shows the counseling causes harm, and that the ban is both over- and underinclusive. The federal government, supporting Chiles, argues the law regulates speech as speech and the case should be remanded for strict scrutiny review. The lower courts upheld the ban under rational basis review, reasoning it regulates conduct—treatment by licensed professionals—that incidentally involves speech; one 10th Circuit judge dissented, saying the majority treated speech as conduct. Colorado argues the ban regulates a treatment found unsafe and ineffective, warrants rational basis review, and would survive strict scrutiny because protecting minors is a compelling interest and the law is narrowly tailored.

A new analysis by the Canadian Society of Palliative Care Physicians (CSPCP) concludes that providing palliative care services across Canada would deliver better care at lower cost. Based on published economic studies, the report notes Canada's aging population and that roughly a quarter of health care costs are spent in the last year of life. Hospital-based palliative care saves approximately $7,000–$8,000 per patient compared to usual acute care, with greater savings when consultation occurs within two days of admission. Outpatient palliative care yields about 30% cost savings while improving patient satisfaction, symptom control, and quality of life. Expanding home-based palliative care in Ontario could avoid $191–$385 million in health care costs annually, and shifting patients to residential hospices saves an estimated $600 per day. The CSPCP has developed recommendations for federal, provincial, and territorial governments to improve palliative care quality and access.

AMP's new chairman David Murray criticized ASX corporate governance principles for deteriorating financial sector governance standards by inhibiting better models, creating a "trust deficit." He argued broad principles evolved into prescriptive "one-size-fits-all" regulations that everyone conforms to despite opt-out options.

Gardaí in Louth have made a fresh appeal for information about the murder of 18-year-old student Cameron Reilly, found dead with neck injuries at Rivervale, Dunleer. Officers are seeking his iPhone, believed to contain messages from his would-be attackers. Separately, gardaí seized a shotgun and around €1m of heroin and cocaine in west Dublin, arresting a man and a woman.

The seventh annual Johnston Press South Business Awards were held at Brighton's Grand Hotel, presented by TV personality Nick Wallis. Chichester's Guardian Angel Carers won both Overall Business of the Year and Large Business of the Year. Olive and Vine received the Place to Eat or Drink Award, with owner Dean Brown-fuller planning to grow its outdoor catering arm. Brandon Relph of Go Creative in Eastbourne won the Young Achiever award, while Southsea Bathing Hut in Portsmouth took Retailer of the Year. Talks at Six, a Chichester charity forum that has raised over £7,500 in 15 months, won Outstanding Contribution to the Community. Other winners included Gardiner and Scardifield, Ricardo Plc, Bunn Leisure, and Martin Putman, who received the Lifetime Achievement award.

Environmental Defence criticized Canada's finding that none of over a dozen phthalates posed human health risks, noting the EU found at least four harmful. The group says Canada should require manufacturers to prove safety, as Europe does. Environment Minister McKenna said recommendations to modernize the law are being considered, with a plan by June 2018.
The Central Bank of Nigeria introduced FORM X, requiring only basic documentation, to ease forex access for SMEs and retail businesses with needs of $10,000 or less.

This patent application, a continuation of earlier filings, discloses techniques for providing enhanced trick-play modes (faster-than-real-time playback such as fast-forwarding and rewinding) for video content streamed from a server to a client. Conventional streaming trick-play provides poor feedback, such as low-resolution thumbnails, and typically requires rebuffering after repositioning. The disclosed media guidance application maintains a normal buffer window of continuous video content for normal playback, and additionally maintains a trick-play window in the buffer that stores only a subset of selected frames (e.g., key frames spaced at approximately equal time intervals) from portions outside the normal buffer window, without buffering the intervening ranges of frames. During trick-play operations, the video player plays only from this buffered subset, adjusting display timing to emulate the requested playback rate. Frame selection, stream selection among multiple bitrate streams, and buffer sizing are based on factors such as streaming performance metrics, playback rate, and anticipated trick-play duration. The described system may include a video repository with frame, trick-play, audio, and jump-point indexes; an HLS-compatible streaming server; an optional proxy server that generates indexes, metadata, and proxy streams for conventional servers lacking such support; a streaming client that adaptively assembles buffered content from different streams; a performance monitor; and a trick-play optimizer that instructs the streaming client which individual frames to request. After trick-play, the normal buffer window can be expanded by requesting intervening frames without re-requesting already-buffered frames.

In *National Sheet Metal Company v. A A A Highway Express Incorporated* (decided March 4, 1937), the court affirmed a verdict for the defendants in a suit for damages to the plaintiff's automobile allegedly caused by the defendants' negligent driving at a street crossing. The court held: the trial court's charge adequately covered the allegation that the defendants failed to sound a horn approaching the intersection; absent special requests, no error occurred in failing to charge on right-of-way or speed-reduction rules where those matters were not alleged in the petition; charging that both parties were lawfully entitled to use the highways was not error; a specific charge regarding violation of a state law and city ordinance did not preclude the jury from considering other negligence allegations; charging the law of comparative negligence was proper where the evidence authorized a finding that both parties were negligent; any error in the charge on the measure of damages was harmless given the verdict for the defendants; and the conflicting evidence authorized the verdict.

Breast cancer is the most common cancer in the UK, with around 56,000 new cases annually. Breast lumps vary in feel—some are pea-sized while others are larger, hard, and irregular—and can occur in the breast or armpit. Self-examination involves visual checks for changes in shape, skin, and nipples, plus physical examination while lying down and sitting up. Checking every two weeks to monthly, ideally around a week after a period, helps identify what is normal. Warning signs such as nipple changes and skin puckering should be checked by a doctor. Risk factors include weight, alcohol, HRT use, family history, BRCA mutations, and reproductive history. Breastfeeding and an active lifestyle may reduce risk. Men can also develop breast cancer, typically between ages 60 and 70. Early detection improves survival, which has almost doubled in the last 40 years.

Travis Haydon, aged 20, was jailed for 18 months in a young offender institution after stabbing Liam Brown in the stomach with a flick knife during a row over a spilt drink at the Newmarket Tavern in Plymouth. Haydon pleaded guilty to assault causing actual bodily harm, possessing a knife in public, and cannabis possession, and was in breach of a suspended sentence for affray. The victim suffered a two centimetre puncture wound and was kept overnight at Derriford Hospital for observation, though lasting damage was not expected. Recorder Paul Grumbar noted Haydon's "appalling record" for violence and said the facts of the case suggested a malicious wounding.

NVIDIA Corporation filed an 8-K reporting that on June 16, 2019, its Board appointed Donald F. Robertson Jr. as Vice President, Chief Accounting Officer and Principal Accounting Officer, effective June 17, 2019, reporting to CFO Colette Kress. Robertson, age 50, previously served as VP Finance and Chief Accounting Officer at Western Digital in 2019 and VP Accounting from 2016 to 2019, and earlier as VP and Chief Accounting Officer at SanDisk (2011–2016) and its Corporate Controller (2006–2011). He is a CPA with degrees from UC San Diego and San Jose State University. He assumes the role from Michael Byron, who moves to a new position as VP, Finance, Merger & Acquisition Integration and Financial Systems. Robertson's at-will offer includes a $650,000 annual base salary, a $600,000 sign-on bonus repayable if he departs before his first employment anniversary, and a grant of 15,000 RSUs vesting over four years (25% on September 16, 2020, then 6.25% quarterly). He is also eligible for NVIDIA's Employee Stock Purchase Plan and benefits programs, and signed NVIDIA's standard indemnity agreement. The offer letter, dated May 21, 2019, is filed as Exhibit 10.1.

A 167-million-year-old fossil lizard discovered on Scotland's Isle of Skye, named Breugnathair elgolensis ("false snake of Elgol"), combines snake-like jaws and hook-like teeth with a lizard's short body and limbs. It belongs to a newly defined group of extinct predatory squamates called Parviraptoridae and shows both snake-like and gecko-like features in a single animal, contradicting earlier beliefs that such bones came from two different creatures. Discovered in 2016, the specimen was studied for nearly a decade using CT imaging and x-rays. Researchers could not conclusively determine whether it was a lizard-like ancestor of snakes or a stem-squamate that independently evolved snake-like features.

The A100 GPU includes 40 MB of L2 cache, 6.7x larger than V100's, improving HPC and AI workload performance. The cache is divided into two partitions, each containing 40 slices, delivering 2.3x bandwidth increase over V100. The architecture adds cache residency controls and Compute Data Compression, offering up to 4x bandwidth improvements.

SPYR, Inc. (OTCQB: SPYR) announced a dividend of shares in a new spin-off company to all shareholders of record as of May 19, 2017, issued on a one-for-one basis. The spin-off is being created to divest SPYR from its restaurant division. After the spin-off is concluded, the new company will file a registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission to qualify as a separate publicly traded entity with its own trading symbol. The spin-off company will focus on licensing or possibly franchising the Eat at Joe's® name and concept, and will include the manufacture and distribution of branded foods, in part by acquiring companies with new food concepts. Like SPYR, the new company will be a low float stock. The article notes that before becoming SPYR, the company traded as Eat at Joes (JOES) at $.20–.50 per share. The publisher, Stock Market Media Group, discloses it is an exclusive publisher of SPYR news and, under a one-year contract begun February 1, 2015, is compensated by SPYR with a $5,000 monthly fee plus 250,000 shares of restricted common stock, subject to resale restrictions.

This passage is from the SLASFA2A datasheet (November 2024, revised April 2025) for Texas Instruments MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 microcontrollers. It describes several peripherals: the RTC_B real-time clock, which operates from a 32kHz source and provides calendar counters, customizable and interval alarm interrupts, crystal offset and temperature drift calibration (up to ±240ppm), and a clock output pin; the IWDT_B independent watchdog timer, which has its own clock source, eight selectable periods (2ms to 2hr), and generates a POR reset if not serviced; the WWDT windowed watchdog timer, with eight selectable periods, automatic stopping in sleep mode, and an interval timer mode; and two timer types, TIMGx (general-purpose) and TIMAx (advanced), the latter supporting complementary PWM with programmable dead band, fast fault response, and additional capture/compare channels.

The document also covers device analog connections, IOMUX input/output diagrams, the two-wire serial wire debug (SWD) interface, and the boot strap loader (BSL), which supports UART or I2C programming, is protected by a 256-bit user-defined password, and can be invoked by pin state, on blank devices, or by software command. A memory-mapped FACTORY region provides read-only device identification and trim data.

Application guidance recommends decoupling capacitors on VDD/VSS, a pullup on NRST, an external 100kΩ resistor for the SYSOSC frequency correction loop, and a 0.47µF tank capacitor on VCORE. Additional sections describe device nomenclature (X prototypes versus MSP production devices), development tools (including Code Composer Studio, IAR, Keil, and the MSPM0 SDK), documentation and support resources, ESD handling precautions, revision history changes from November 2024 to April 2025, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information, concluding with legal disclaimers.

Chicago faces a significant security challenge as it hosts three major sports events: the Chicago Marathon with up to 1.7 million spectators and more than 40,000 runners, a Cubs playoff game at Wrigley Field, and a Bears game at Soldier Field. The Las Vegas massacre, along with reports that gunman Stephen Paddock had booked hotel rooms overlooking Lollapalooza, has raised concerns about a lone-wolf gunman firing from a skyscraper. Officials say security has been reviewed and strengthened: police will deploy 1,000 additional officers and more undercover personnel, conduct random bag checks, and coordinate with downtown high-rise security staff. Mayor Rahm Emanuel expressed confidence the events are secure. Experts note copycat attacks are rare and layered security is effective. Some runners expressed concern but do not plan to withdraw.

Saudi Aramco plans to change the formula for pricing its long-term crude sales to Asia from October, the first benchmark change for its official selling prices since the mid-1980s, according to trade sources. The new formula will use average monthly DME Oman futures prices and Platts-assessed Dubai cash prices instead of Platts' Oman-Dubai average. The decision, discussed internally for years, could boost liquidity in DME Oman futures trading. Aramco's OSPs set the trend for Iranian, Kuwaiti and Iraqi prices, affecting over 12 million bpd to Asia; it is unclear if other producers will follow.

DoorDash has unveiled Dot, a new autonomous delivery robot created by DoorDash Labs, its automation and robotics wing, as part of a "hybrid" delivery model combining humans, drones, and autonomous vehicles. Dot is nearly five feet tall, bright red, equipped with nine cameras and seven other sensors, and is intended to operate on sidewalks, roads, and bike lanes. DoorDash also partners with Coco Robotics, whose smaller sidewalk robots operate in Los Angeles and remain partly remote-controlled by teleoperators. Industry enthusiasm for delivery robots peaked around the pandemic, then cooled as Amazon and FedEx abandoned their projects, though Starship Technologies continues operating on college campuses. The discussion covers regulatory complications around bike lane use and labor implications: robots may displace rather than eliminate human work, and hybrid models, such as those used in Chinese hotels, still rely on human delivery workers.
AI models Evo 1 and Evo 2 generated bacteriophage genomes from scratch; some outperformed a well-studied strain.

The speaker welcomes leaders of a nation visiting the seat of government for the first time, affirming friendship and urging lasting peace between peoples born in the same land. He describes his seventeen growing states as just, willing to buy land only when its owners wish to sell, and promises that agreed boundaries will be protected, with a law provided to punish encroachers. Responding to a request signed by Puckshanublee and other chiefs to sell lands to pay debts, he favors lands on the Mississippi for boat resting places and provisions en route to New Orleans, and says agents will later negotiate the boundary on-site. Regarding lands formerly sold to the English, he argues custom, elapsed time, and living witnesses indicate payment was made; any unpaid debt would be the English's, not his nation's. He encourages the visitors to adopt farming, stock-raising, and weaving over hunting, promising assistance. Last year's clothes were gifts, and the store was sent at their request, with the land remaining theirs. The Secretary at War will address remaining matters. Carriages will convey the visitors, who will return home by land; the speaker regrets the error that sent them to Savannah instead of Augusta and thanks the Great Spirit for their safe arrival.

The District Court of Appeal of Florida, Second District, reversed the Unemployment Appeals Commission's order denying Genel Altimeaux unemployment benefits, finding the appeals referee's determination that he voluntarily quit was not based on competent, substantial evidence. Altimeaux, born in Haiti with limited English, worked at Ocean Construction. After a September 26, 1997 pay dispute in which coworker Vidieu Tanis stated the Haitian workers would no longer work for the company, Altimeaux was advised the following Monday that he was no longer employed. At the first hearing, held without Altimeaux because he had not received notice, supervisor Bruce Milliken testified Altimeaux said he quit. On remand, a second hearing was held; Milliken did not appear, and supervisor William Tranowski admitted on cross-examination that he never personally heard Altimeaux quit. Because the referee resolved factual conflicts by relying on Milliken's earlier testimony, which was not subject to cross-examination and was therefore incompetent, the court reversed with directions to reinstate the unemployment award.

Pin and Pull is a football run play that creates down block angles while getting blockers into space as lead blockers for outside runs. Its main strength is delivering extra blockers to the point of attack on perimeter runs; it is also versatile, allowing any lineman to down block or pull, and lets the Tailback take the ball from the C-gap to the sideline based on the Guards' blocks. Its biggest weakness is that it requires specific personnel, particularly at least two Guards who can pull and run, and it works best with speed Tailbacks who can get vertical within one cut rather than power backs. Unlike the traditional Buck Sweep, which requires a simultaneous inside run threat such as a Fullback dive, Pin and Pull is a true perimeter run. The passage details blocking assignments for the play against a 3-4 odd front and a 4-3 even front, covering each position's responsibilities. Two variations are described: the Pin and Pull Toss, where a receiver motions in and the under-center Quarterback tosses to the Tailback for faster perimeter delivery, and the TE-Wing Pin and Pull Toss, which adds a Tight End and Wing to create a four-man blocking surface with advantageous angles.

Researchers equipped greater noctule bats, Europe's largest bat species, with biologgers containing accelerometers, magnetometers, altimeters, and microphones to track their hunting. The study, published October 9 in Science, provides evidence that these bats capture, dismember, and consume migrating songbirds in flight. The bats ascend above the altitude of migrating songbirds—over 1,200 meters—then dive vertically for several minutes, emitting high-frequency feeding buzzes that birds cannot hear. Of 611 recorded hunting events, two involved birds: one escaped near the ground, while the other was consumed during a 23-minute in-flight meal. Wing removal appears part of the process, and DNA analysis of wounds on recovered wings confirmed greater noctule bites. Researchers note much remains unknown about the species.

The article reports that gold rallied strongly on Friday while the USD Index declined, though gold remains below a rising resistance line and follows its 2011–2013 price pattern, with the recent upswing resembling the November 2012 rally. Silver, platinum, and mining stocks did not rise notably; the VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF closed below its April high for a third consecutive day, which the author says confirms bearish implications, since gold stocks normally outperform gold early in precious metals rallies. The USD Index is described as forming a bullish inverse head-and-shoulders pattern, likely to rally to at least 101.3, with breakouts verified by a return to the neck level. Stocks, after failing to exceed previous highs and falling below a rising support line, show bearish signals and may decline significantly. The author compares the current setup to 2008 and states the Peak Chaos theory remains intact.

Verizon and AST SpaceMobile announced a commercial agreement for space-based cellular broadband across the continental US. On October 8, ASTS shares rose over 9% while VZ shares were roughly flat. The author rates VZ a "strong buy," citing the partnership's marginal boost to long-term growth and competitive positioning, plus a strong outlook with expected revenue and earnings growth, low trading multiples, and favorable analyst sentiment. ASTS is rated a "sell" due to heavy dilution, minimal revenue, and high valuation.

Parents are questioning Township High School District 113's process for hiring a new Highland Park High School principal, citing limited parent representation on the stakeholder committee and transparency concerns. Superintendent Christopher Dignam is using search firm Ray and Associates to replace Tom Koulentes, who leaves June 30 for Libertyville High School. Administrators will narrow candidates to two or three finalists for an 18-member stakeholder committee to interview April 25, using the same process as last year's Deerfield High School search.

Former Nepali prime minister K.P. Oli appeared set to return to power after winning his parliamentary seat, with his Communist UML party and Maoist allies on course for a majority. Oli, 65, vowed to form a full five-year-term government and pledged infrastructure projects, including extending China's railway into Nepal. Final results are expected within a week.

Brock University research led by Evangelina Tsiani found rosemary extract stopped the survival, spread, and multiplication of aggressive lung cancer cells by blocking the Akt signalling pathway, enhancing apoptosis, and preventing protein activation. Published in Biomedicine & Pharmacotherapy, the study suggests rosemary may have anti-tumour and chemoprevention properties. Tsiani cautioned it is too soon to recommend eating more rosemary; next steps involve identifying the responsible chemicals, possibly the polyphenols carnosic acid and rosmarinic acid.

Plans for England's longest "smart motorway" will go on show before work starts on the M4 in September. The 32-mile stretch between London and Theale will be widened to four lanes, costing up to £862.4m, with completion expected by March 2022.

This paper introduces COTUTOR, a generative AI model for personalized programming education that integrates knowledge tracing, convex optimization, and signal processing. The model processes real-time student learning signals—submission and grading data, participation logs, and queries and feedback—through an iterative flywheel mechanism that continuously updates estimates of student knowledge states and generates optimized learning strategies. A key innovation is formulating knowledge tracing and feedback adaptation as a convex optimization problem, which provides interpretability, globally optimal state tracking, and lower computational requirements than autoregressive LLMs. Unlike systems such as Khanmigo and GitHub Copilot in the Classroom, COTUTOR maintains an explicit, interpretable model of student learning trajectories. Knowledge states are estimated using a Bayesian Knowledge Tracing framework applied to Online Judge submission data, with learning, slip, and guess rates updated in real time. COTUTOR is implemented as an interactive AI chatbot copilot on the My Code Weapon and Nemobot platforms, offering proactive reminders, question handling, and resource recommendations, with standardized replies and logging to mitigate hallucinations. A case study formulates educational resource allocation across thirty sessions with two resource types as a convex optimization problem that maximizes student sentiment under resource and priority constraints, tested under linear and other influence models. A two-part evaluation—dataset benchmarking and a controlled classroom study—indicates COTUTOR outperforms baselines including traditional methods, BKT, DKT, and code-DKT in knowledge state estimation and student learning outcomes.

The passage describes NVIDIA's GA10x Ampere architecture GPUs and associated technologies. GDDR6X memory supports data rates up to 19.5 Gbps, delivering 936 GB/sec of peak bandwidth—a 52% improvement over the RTX 2080 Ti's TU102 GPU and the largest generational bandwidth leap in ten years. As game sizes exceed 200GB and PCIe Gen4 SSDs reach 7 GB/sec, traditional storage APIs have become bottlenecks, with decompression capable of consuming all 24 CPU cores on a Threadripper. NVIDIA RTX IO addresses this through GPU-based loading and lossless decompression via Microsoft's DirectStorage API, accelerating I/O up to 100x versus hard drives and traditional APIs while offloading dozens of CPU cores' worth of work.

The NVIDIA A40, built on GA10x, is described as the most powerful data center GPU for visual computing, delivering up to 2X FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and 5X AI training throughput (10X with sparsity) compared to the Quadro RTX 6000, with 48GB of memory expandable to 96GB via NVLink. GA10x GPUs support 4K at 120Hz and 8K at 60Hz displays, including HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC. Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware decoding for codecs including AV1—a first for GPUs—while seventh-generation NVENC enables encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

The architecture provides up to 2x performance in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI, featuring second-generation RT Cores with doubled ray/triangle intersection performance and motion blur acceleration, plus third-generation Tensor Cores with structural sparsity. The GeForce RTX 3090 (GA102) ships with 24GB GDDR6X and is 1.5x faster than TITAN RTX; the RTX 3070 (GA104) outperforms the RTX 2080 Ti. A new Error Detection and Replay (EDR) feature helps overclockers identify memory limits by retrying failed transmissions. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU includes 10,752 CUDA cores and 48GB GDDR6, expandable to 96GB via NVLink. The passage concludes with NVIDIA's standard legal disclaimers.

JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon said AI is a genuine, transformative technology but that some asset prices are "in some form of bubble territory," comparing current AI exuberance to the early internet era, which ultimately paid off. He warned that AI will eliminate jobs and urged society, government, and business to address job loss through retraining, new forms of income, or early retirement. Dimon distinguished between AI applied to specific tasks—such as risk, fraud, and marketing at JPMorgan, which has invested billions since 2012 with over 2,000 AI staff—and generative AI, whose efficiency gains he called largely anecdotal. Responding to an MIT study finding 95% of generative AI pilots failed to yield returns, he said getting data into proper format matters more than measuring costs. Days earlier, he cited a 30% chance of a market correction and called for regulation, safety nets, and planning.

Seeking Alpha published a slideshow page for BioNTech SE's (BNTX) special call with InstaDeep Ltd, noting BioNTech released the slide deck. The page describes its transcripts team, lists related articles, and shows a chart spanning 2025-09-26 to 2025-10-01 with values from 96.98 to 102.72.

Jane Goodall, who died October 1 at age 91, studied chimpanzees in Tanzania's Gombe National Park for nearly 30 years. Beyond observing living chimps, she assembled a unique collection of chimp skeletons. Her team retrieved bodies within days of death, and each skeleton came from an individual with known sex, age, body weight and life experiences, allowing researchers to study how individual development influenced skeletal features. Interviewed by phone in 1990, Goodall expressed uncertainty about the collection's implications for understanding ancient hominids, saying "We just don't know," and explained she collected skeletons because "you shouldn't waste anything" in the field. One notable specimen, Flo—a dominant matriarch who died in 1972—demonstrated that body weight cannot be reliably estimated from bone size and showed a bone loss pattern unlike human osteoporosis. Flo gave birth within a few years of dying at nearly age 50. The collection continues to pay scientific dividends.

Gold prices are forecast to reach a four-year high of $1,400 an ounce by year-end, driven by U.S.-North Korea tensions and strong demand from China and India, according to VTB Capital's Evgeny Ananiev, who sees bullion at $1,360 within three months and supported above $1,200. Gold, trading at $1,281.86, has climbed 12 percent this year amid nuclear conflict worries and subdued U.S. inflation. Analyst Chirag Sheth expects $1,400 in six to nine months. Indian imports may jump 30 percent to 800 tons, while Chinese consumption rose almost 10 percent to 545.2 tons.

A Business Insider reporter stayed one night in the Aurora Suite at the Villa Casa Casuarina, the former Versace Mansion turned hotel in Miami's South Beach, paying about $860 for the cheapest available room in October 2021. The Spanish-style mansion, built in the 1930s, was transformed by Gianni Versace in 1992 into 12 suites for family and friends including Princess Diana and Elton John, and later became a hotel. The reporter received a golden key instead of a key card and found the suite featured a four-poster king-size bed, a luxurious shower with multiple showerheads, Italian soaps and lotions, and detailed ceiling artwork. Highlights included the Thousand Mosaic Pool made of thousands of 24k gold tiles, a rooftop deck with ocean views, an observatory with a copper dome added by Versace, and a complimentary breakfast. Attentive staff made the reporter feel like the hotel's only guest.

This patent application, a continuation claiming priority to earlier filings, describes multi-camera imaging systems and methods for imaging faint objects (e.g., in space or other low-light environments) using arrays of economical or low-performance cameras that, individually, cannot image such objects. Three array configurations are disclosed: (1) a common field array, in which cameras share a common field of view region and a computing system co-registers and combines their images, yielding a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) improvement of at least √N, where N is the number of combined images; (2) a hybrid field array, in which multiple common-field camera arrays with partially overlapping fields of view produce combined images that are stitched into a wider-field composite image; and (3) an adaptive field array, in which cameras initially cover a wide composite field of view and automatically reconfigure into a common field arrangement upon detecting a target. Stated benefits over prior systems—such as expensive high-SNR telescopes exemplified by the DARPA Space Surveillance Telescope—include lower construction, operational, and maintenance costs; increased effective bit depth (approaching Log2(N) enhancement) enabling advanced deconvolution; reduced cosmic ray artifacts; and scalability and flexibility, including partitioning into independently steerable sub-arrays. Applications include astrophotography, deep space searching, satellite detection and tracking, tactical sensing, and night vision. The application further describes camera calibration processes (dark, flat, bias, barrel distortion, and field calibration), data collection via star matching and image combining, and data reduction involving streak detection (e.g., Hough transform), streak characterization, initial orbit determination, and catalog search to identify uncorrelated targets.

Asian shares were mostly lower Wednesday after a late U.S. sell-off ended a three-day winning streak. Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 0.3 percent, the Shanghai Composite dropped 0.8 percent, Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 1.2 percent, and South Korea's Kospi lost 0.2 percent, while Southeast Asian and Taiwanese shares rose. Researchers from the University of Washington and several small companies conducted the first large-scale field trial using poplar trees fortified with a probiotic microbe to clean groundwater contaminated with trichloroethylene (TCE), a common industrial pollutant and known human carcinogen. The microbe was selected from poplars already growing in TCE-contaminated soil, and one strain eliminated nearly all TCE in laboratory tests. At the Middlefield-Ellis-Whisman Superfund site at NASA's Ames Research Center in California, inoculated trees grew larger and healthier than untreated trees, and trunk samples showed greatly reduced TCE levels. Groundwater downstream of the test site had lower toxin levels, and chloride, a harmless byproduct of TCE degradation, was found in soil around the roots. The method could offer a lower-cost alternative to traditional cleanup approaches, and organizations and landowners have expressed interest in using it.

New reports citing anonymous U.S. officials say Russian intelligence officials repeatedly contacted members of President Trump's campaign staff. The communications were intercepted during routine intelligence collection targeting Russian officials while agencies investigated Russian election tampering. Officials have seen no proof of collusion but are concerned by the contacts' frequency and timing, and are still determining their purpose. Trump dismissed the reports as "conspiracy theories," and the Kremlin criticized the media's use of anonymous sources. The FBI is investigating, and the Senate Intelligence Committee is probing Russian election meddling, though some Republicans, like Rep. Mike Johnson, oppose an independent investigation and question leaks of classified information. Three Trump associates—Michael Flynn, Paul Manafort, and Carter Page—have exited over Russia-related allegations; Manafort called the officials' account "absurd."

The passage describes deploying a sharded Redis cache on Kubernetes using a StatefulSet, which creates three Redis containers with unique DNS names, and a Service that provides DNS entries for the replicas. twemproxy, a lightweight proxy developed by Twitter, is configured to point to these replicas and deployed via a ConfigMap.

Iraqi Shi'ite cleric Moqtada al-Sadr set conditions for followers to hand over weapons used against Islamic State, demanding jobs or integration into official forces and care for martyrs' families. Prime Minister al-Abadi declared final victory over the group, saying the state should hold a monopoly on arms.

The Delaware-incorporated company, headquartered in Palo Alto, California, designs, manufactures and sells electric vehicles and solar energy generation and energy storage products through two segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. In May 2020, a subsidiary entered into an unsecured revolving facility of up to RMB 4.00 billion in China for Gigafactory Shanghai expenditures.

Natural zircon single crystals from the Mud Tank deposit (Australia) were shock-loaded to 13.6 and 51.3 GPa in laboratory recovery experiments to study trace element behavior during the zircon–reidite transition. At 13.6 GPa, the zircon structure was retained, though the sample was strongly fractured and showed reddish cathodoluminescence patches near fractures, attributed to structural defects. At 51.3 GPa, the material transformed to textured, mosaic reidite with minor residual zircon, consistent with the orientation relation (112)R||(200)Zrn. Cathodoluminescence intensity decreased about six-fold, the emission maximum shifted to shorter wavelengths (~430 nm), and changes in REE3+ lines indicated at least two Dy3+ positions with different local symmetries. Numerous bright yellow speckles (2–10 μm), related mainly to the 577 nm Dy3+ band, were confined to crystallographic planes and interpreted as segregation of REE3+ ions on planar defects and dislocations formed during the transformation. This segregation occurred within tens of seconds without prolonged annealing, implying rapid transport via vacancies, grain boundaries, or dislocations, possibly linked to local charge imbalance during the reconstructive transition. The authors conclude that the zircon-to-reidite transformation can cause trace cation segregation on planar defects, and that fracturing may promote sudden trace element release during subsequent interaction with fluids or melts, while isotopic characteristics may remain largely unchanged.

This patent application, a continuation of multiple related applications on ladar transmitters, addresses limitations of conventional ladar systems for computer vision, such as high cost, size, weight, power requirements, and bandwidth use. The inventors disclose three main innovations: (1) an optical field splitter/inverter positioned downstream from the scanning mirrors that splits and inverts the scan area so the fast portion of a resonant scan occurs at the edges and the slower portion in the middle, increasing gaze time on desired regions such as the center; it can be implemented as W-shaped reflectors or a triangular prism, with adjustable overlap via hinges; (2) an induced periodic phase drift in Lissajous scan patterns, in which one or both resonant mirrors are driven slightly off resonance using a total least squares optimization, reducing scan gaps and blindspots in selected gaze regions without slowing revisit time; and (3) a compact beam scanner assembly using an ellipsoidal conjugate reflector (ECR) reimaging mirror placed between two scannable mirrors located at the ellipsoid's foci, with an upstream focusing lens, enabling equally sized, closely spaced mirrors and increased scan speed and field of view, while a coplanar angle (CPA) design formula eliminates scan field distortions.

A week after Assistant Professor Jharna Dalei hanged herself at Padmanava College of Engineering, security guard Ram Chandra Gouda died on duty; his asthmatic death is unrelated. A faculty member faces abetment charges and is absconding.

An email sent June 5, 2001, by Miyung Buster of Enron to numerous recipients, compiles news articles on California's energy crisis. Topics include: Rep. Doug Ose's wholesale electricity price bill, which Democrats oppose as encouraging market manipulation; an editorial citing economists who argue price controls are warranted given the market's lack of competition; stereotyping in the Davis-Bush energy dispute; power plants returning from maintenance shutdowns, though blackouts remain expected despite an 11 percent drop in electricity use; Chevron's threat to cut refinery output unless exempted from blackouts; PG&E creditors approving $17.5 million in executive bonuses tied to timely filing of a reorganization plan; a poll showing 56 percent support for electricity price limits; PG&E's lawsuit challenging the state's reimbursement calculation; criticism of San Jose's agreement with Calpine over the Metcalf power plant; a PBS "Frontline" documentary on the crisis mentioning Enron; editorials on conservation and FERC's weak market oversight; Edison's shareholder lobbying campaign for its $2.7 billion bailout plan; SDG&E's proposed rate hike to repay $915 million to the state; GWF Energy's 10-year, 430-megawatt contract with the California Department of Water Resources; concerns over high natural gas prices and possible market manipulation; and a state Senate committee's approval of subpoenas to eight out-of-state power generators.

The White House blocked congressionally approved funds for the Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency, effectively shuttering it Tuesday. Two senators demanded the money's release, and top Senate Republicans condemned the decision.

Trading recommendations: Nifty at 10,094 with stops at 10,050/10,200; Bank Nifty at 24,245, trend negative but short-covering possible Monday; go short Tata Steel (target Rs 567), short Ambuja Cements (Rs 226), and long PowerGrid (Rs 196), with specified stops.

This passage is an email compilation of news articles dated December 31, 2001, primarily covering Enron's collapse and related financial news. Key items include: a New York Times article reporting that the broadband bandwidth trading market collapsed after Enron's fall; a Wall Street Journal opinion arguing that companies like Enron and Nortel were damaged by chasing unrealistic Wall Street growth expectations; a WSJ article contending that large write-offs (e.g., Bethlehem Steel, At Home, Lucent, Providian) often signal company distress; a WSJ piece on how SEC Chairman Harvey Pitt's handling of the Enron investigation will test his leadership, noting his required recusal due to a former client, Arthur Andersen; a WSJ guide to early-warning signs of corporate bankruptcy, including credit-default swaps and bond prices; an LA Times survey finding 401(k) investors hold overly optimistic long-term return expectations; an LA Times article on anger over retention bonuses for Polaroid executives during its bankruptcy; an LA Times report that power producers are cutting expansion plans after Enron's collapse, raising possible shortage concerns; a commentary criticizing University of California fund managers for losing $145 million on Enron stock; brief items on American Electric Power's $175 million purchase of Enron Wind's Indian Mesa wind project, CSFB's resignation from Enron's creditors committee, California utility regulator Loretta Lynch's comments on the power crisis, and Bloomberg's year-end "Stocky" awards highlighting Enron's 99 percent stock decline and Providian's 94 percent drop.

NASA scientists have developed a theoretical plan called HAMMER (Hypervelocity Asteroid Mitigation Mission for Emergency Response) to deflect asteroid Bennu, which has roughly a 1 in 2700 chance of hitting Earth on September 22, 2135. The plan involves either sending a nine-tonne "bulk impactor" or using a nuclear device to nudge the asteroid off its path. NASA engineer Brent Barbee said the study is meant to prepare for potential threats, noting that space objects frequently strike Earth, including the 1908 Tunguska event and a 2013 Russian meteor that injured 1100 people. NASA's Planetary Defense Coordination Office detects about 1000 new near-Earth objects annually, with possibly 10,000 unaccounted for. Bennu serves as a useful test target for calculations, and NASA's OSIRIS-REx spacecraft is en route to map the asteroid and return a 2.1-ounce sample to Earth.

The Citi Simplicity® Card, featured by Motley Fool Money (Sept. 30, 2025), offers a 0% intro APR for 21 months on balance transfers—one of the longest interest-free periods available—and 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases. After the intro periods, the variable APR is 17.99%–28.74% based on creditworthiness. Balance transfers must be completed within 4 months of account opening, with a 3% transfer fee (minimum $5) during that period, rising to 5% afterward. Party-list Rep. Lito Atienza of Buhay filed House Bill 4758, seeking to replace the MMDA with a Metropolitan Manila government headed by an elected governor. He argued the current appointed chairman lacks accountability and that megacities like New York and Tokyo managed similar problems through elected governors. Citing persistent traffic, flooding, and garbage issues, he proposed a government composed of an elected governor, vice governor, and Metro Manila Council members elected from Metro Manila's congressional districts.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC dated April 27, 2021, announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended March 31, 2021 via a press release furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The report, signed by Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer Alice L. Jolla, states the information is furnished rather than filed under the Exchange Act. Microsoft's registered securities include common stock and 2.125%, 3.125%, and 2.625% notes due 2021, 2028, and 2033, respectively, traded on NASDAQ.

Ten-man Manchester City beat Burnley to move up to third, closing to within two points of second-place Liverpool. Fernandinho was sent off in the first half for a two-footed challenge, triggering a four-match ban—his third red card in six games. Gael Clichy and substitute Sergio Aguero scored for City, with Aguero's tight-angle finish proving the winner after Ben Mee had replied for Burnley.

Eric Fung, 37, CEO of Colega AI, left California—citing high living costs and a dimmed Bay Area atmosphere—and moved to Tokyo to start an AI company. Born in Brooklyn to a family originally from Hong Kong, he studied advertising and public relations at Penn State, worked in advertising and at a startup in New York, then moved to San Francisco at 24 to build companies. He co-founded a company in 2019 that exited, partly due to the pandemic, and later opened several restaurants in California. His US-registered startup, with seven remote-first employees mostly based in Tokyo, targets Japan's many small businesses. He partnered with a local to navigate cultural and language barriers and is adjusting to Japan's hierarchical work culture. He and his wife Shana rent a studio near Shibuya for about $1,350, roughly half the cost of a comparable place in San Francisco.

The Consumer Mortgage Coalition is urging the Treasury Department to let lenders use the National Directory of New Hires database as an alternative to the IRS's problematic Income Verification Express System, which could delay mortgage closings. In a Jan. 31 letter, the coalition said the database would enable rapid income verification with consumer consent and expand credit access. It also asked Treasury to seek funding to upgrade the IVES system.

CompareCards reports that credit card issuers are offering generous deals, with banks providing long 0% intro APR periods ranging from 12 to 21 months, which benefit consumers who pay balances in full and on time. Featured offers include: a Discover card with 15 months of 0% intro APR, 5% quarterly cash back, and an unlimited first-year Cashback Match; a Bank of America card with 0% APR for 15 billing cycles, a $200 online bonus, and 6% first-year cash back in a choice category; a Bank of America travel card with 25,000 bonus points and 1.5 points per dollar; a Citi card with 18 months of 0% APR on balance transfers and 2% cash back; Capital One VentureOne with 1.25 miles per dollar and 15 months of 0% intro APR; Capital One Quicksilver with unlimited 1.5% cash back; and a Citi card offering 30,000 bonus points. The passage explains that low-rate cards come in variable and fixed APR types, with intro offers typically lasting 6 to 21 months at 0% to 3.99% interest, and that the interest rate is considered the most important card component. Editors evaluated over 100 cards from more than 50 issuers using an objective rating system.

Sirius XM (SIRI) is presented as a low-growth, cash-generative business with ~4.3% fixed-rate debt. Satellite spending cuts should boost free cash flow ~20% by 2026, and share buybacks lift per-share value. At ~7.6× EV/EBITDA versus a historical 15×, with 11-12% ROIC against a 6% WACC, the author sees 2-3× upside via unlevered DCF and discloses a long position. Charted prices ranged from ~22.43 to ~24.00 during October 2-7, 2025.
MLB parks debut creative 2025 foods topped by Cubs' Korean corn dog; Savannah Bananas selection show airs Oct. 9 on ESPN2; Stephen A. Smith celebrates Yankees' Game 3 win.

A new study found that during the 2014-2016 West African Ebola epidemic, just 3 percent of patients caused about 61 percent of infections, highlighting the role of "superspreaders." The epidemic, which infected over 28,000 people and killed at least 11,000 across Guinea, Sierra Leone, and Liberia, was partly driven by traditional funeral practices, as bodily fluids from dying patients and dead bodies remain infectious. Researchers, including Benjamin Dalziel of Oregon State University, used computer models and found each patient infected an average of 2.39 others, though transmission was uneven. Little transmission occurred in hospitals; spread was driven by people staying home, often not suspecting Ebola. Age was a key predictor, as the very young and old attract caregivers. Superspreaders also drove SARS and MERS outbreaks. Ebola was stopped through safe burial and quick hospitalization.

The passage describes NVIDIA's GA10x Ampere GPU architecture and its key features:

**Second-Generation RT Core**: Delivers up to 2x ray tracing performance over Turing, supports concurrent RT Core and graphics/compute workloads, and adds hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur via a new Interpolate Triangle Position unit (up to 8x faster motion blur rendering than Turing).

**Third-Generation Tensor Cores**: Support new data types (TF32, BF16) and a Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity feature that doubles throughput for sparse matrices. TF32 provides up to 5x AI training throughput without code changes. Enables DLSS with 8K gaming support.

**Memory**: GDDR6X with PAM4 signaling achieves up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec bandwidth on the RTX 3090. RTX A6000 and A40 use 48GB GDDR6, scalable to 96GB via NVLink.

**Third-Generation NVLink**: Provides 112.5 GB/sec total bandwidth between two GPUs.

**PCIe Gen 4**: Doubles PCIe 3.0 bandwidth, up to 64 GB/sec with x16 slots.

**GA10x SM Architecture**: Doubles FP32 processing (both datapaths execute FP32), features 128 KB L1/shared memory per SM (33% larger than Turing), and doubled shared memory bandwidth. Each SM contains 128 CUDA Cores, four Tensor Cores, and one RT Core.

**ROP Optimizations**: ROPs moved to GPCs, increasing total ROPs from 96 to 112 on GA102.

**NVIDIA RTX IO**: GPU-based decompression working with Microsoft's DirectStorage API, accelerating I/O up to 100x versus hard drives while offloading CPU work.

**NVIDIA A40**: Data center GPU delivering up to 2x FP32 and ray-tracing throughput, and up to 5x (10x with Sparsity) AI training throughput versus Quadro RTX 6000.

**Display/Media**: HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a support (8K60, 4K120); fifth-generation NVDEC adds AV1 hardware decode (first GPU to do so); seventh-generation NVENC for encoding.

**Products**: GeForce RTX 3090 (GA102, 24GB GDDR6X, 82 SMs), RTX 3080, RTX 3070 (GA104), and RTX A6000 workstation GPU (10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT Cores, 48GB GDDR6).

**Other**: Ampere GPUs are up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing; a new Error Detection and Replay (EDR) feature helps overclockers identify memory limits without crashes.

Bayhorse Silver Inc. is increasing its non-brokered private placement from 1,500,000 to 3,000,000 units at $0.10 per unit, for gross proceeds of $300,000, subject to TSX-V approval. Each unit comprises one common share and half a warrant, exercisable at $0.15 for 24 months. Proceeds will fund equipment acquisition, working capital for the Bayhorse Silver Mine, and general administrative costs.

The global automated fare collection (AFC) system market was valued at $4.81 billion in 2016 and is projected to reach $12.81 billion by 2024, growing at a CAGR of 13.3% from 2017 to 2024. AFC systems automate public transportation ticketing, improving efficiency, transaction rates, security, and accuracy while reducing queues and manual errors. Growth is driven by technology adoption, new AFC technologies, and government investments, while lack of awareness and limited smart card use act as restraints. The market is segmented by component (hardware, software), application (bus, toll, train, car rentals), technology platform (smart card, NFC, OCR, others), and geography (North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, LAMEA). Key players include Advanced Card Systems, Atos SE, Cubic Transportation Systems, LG CNS, NXP Semiconductors, Omron, Samsung SDS, Scheidt & Bachmann, Thales Group, and LECIP Group.

This patent application describes methods, systems, and devices for small data transmission using Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) in new radio (NR) wireless communications. The background notes that in LTE, small data transmission requires RRC connection establishment, which is inefficient, and summarizes existing Control Plane and User Plane solutions. It further notes that no uplink NOMA was discussed in LTE Rel-14 and that current NOMA approaches may reduce spectral efficiency or degrade channel estimation performance.

The disclosed solutions mitigate or eliminate sequence collision by exploiting the randomness of user-specific reference bits and data bits. In one aspect, a network apparatus (e.g., a gNB) configures contention-based radio resources for a physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) as a configured grant PUSCH and broadcasts information, such as via a remaining system information block, including NOMA parameters (e.g., DM-RS port indications, multiple access signatures, interleavers). A UE can then transmit small data via the configured grant PUSCH while remaining in RRC-IDLE or RRC-INACTIVE state. In another aspect, an apparatus generates reference bits based on a UE-specific identity and a multiple access identity, jointly encodes them with information bits (e.g., via systematic LDPC), and uses the encoded reference bits to generate a preamble or demodulation reference signal.

The detailed description covers NOMA scheme categories (codebook-based, sequence-based, and interleaver-based) and their benefits for mMTC, URLLC, and eMBB scenarios; procedures for small data transmission in the idle state (with brief transition to connected state using NAS security) and the inactive state (without requiring state transition); configured grant resource configurations, including time/frequency allocation, DM-RS configuration, and MA-signature mapping; extended cyclic prefixes and guard bands to support asynchronous transmission; random access procedures with NOMA-enabled PUSCH to reduce collision probability and latency; an OFDM-IM-based NOMA scheme using sparse subcarrier activation patterns; and an example communications system comprising WTRUs, radio access networks, and core networks in the context of 3GPP NR standards.

The Massachusetts House and Senate passed a supplemental budget bill providing $15 million for school districts educating students who arrived from Puerto Rico after Hurricane Maria. More than 2,300 students have arrived since September. Funding will be distributed through the existing education aid formula, with Springfield accepting the most students. Minor differences between the bills will be negotiated.

The Tax Court sustained the IRS Appeals officer's determination permitting collection by levy of petitioner's unpaid 1994 and 1996 income taxes. Petitioner, a songwriter, filed returns reporting $2,084 (1994) and $66,874 (1996) but paid nothing, believing the amounts incorrect due to a royalty dispute with record companies. At his collection due process hearing, he asked the IRS to subpoena record company information; the Appeals officer declined, concluded the underlying liabilities were not properly at issue under section 6330(c)(2)(B), and sustained the proposed levy. On review, the court rejected respondent's argument that self-reported liabilities cannot be challenged under section 6330(c)(2)(B), citing Montgomery v. Commissioner. Nevertheless, it granted summary judgment for respondent because petitioner failed to allege specific facts—such as erroneous income, deduction, or credit items—showing error in the assessments, and his claims of procedural errors and improper levies lacked factual support, particularly since no levies had yet been made.

Acting CDC director Jim O'Neill approved recommendations allowing anyone over 6 months to receive an updated Covid-19 shot after discussing risks and benefits with their provider, maintaining insurance coverage though it doesn't specify whether some individuals will need a prescription. He also approved giving children under 4 the measles, mumps, rubella vaccine and chickenpox shot separately rather than combined. The approval, which came more than two weeks after advisers issued the recommendations, allows states to order updated Covid vaccines for low-income children through the Vaccines for Children program; the delay had left roughly 50% of U.S. children relying on the program unable to access the shots. A new routine childhood vaccine schedule is expected Tuesday.

After passing an online "Jeopardy!" contestant test despite not being a trivia expert, the author reflects on how people recall things not thought of in years. Memory, once called the "search for the engram," remains unsolved in neuroscience, with no conceptual consensus; Todd Sacktor has called it "the last of the great 20th century problems in biology," and solving its biological basis could merit a Nobel Prize. Where memories are stored remains unresolved: Karl Lashley's rat experiments suggested memories are distributed throughout the brain, like a hologram, while Wilder Penfield found specific memories could be triggered by stimulating localized brain areas. Recent UCLA research suggests RNA may transfer memory in snails, echoing James McConnell's 1960s planarian experiments, which the author tried unsuccessfully to replicate. He jokes about demanding an RNA drug test if he loses on "Jeopardy!" The author, John Kizer, is a former National Science Foundation Fellow in cell biology.

Agents Mutual, owner of OnTheMarket.com, plans to float on London's Alternative Investment Market and raise £50 million to challenge rivals Rightmove and Zoopla. Britain's third biggest property portal, it will use the funds to boost marketing, sales, customer relations and technology, including a national TV, digital and print campaign. Having abandoned its mutual status, it has signed long-term listing agreements with several estate agencies. Chief executive Ian Springett said the firm is well placed to challenge the leading portals, though analyst George Salmon noted toppling Rightmove remains a significant challenge.

A father was allegedly assaulted by two men at Coed Bach Park in Pontarddulais, Swansea, on 29 June, after confronting a man riding a moped erratically near children. He was spat at, punched to the floor, and kicked by the motorbike rider while his children watched. Police are appealing for witnesses and have described the two attackers and a woman accompanying them.

The plaintiff insured sued on burglary insurance policies containing an exclusion clause barring recovery unless the insured kept records from which the insurer could accurately determine the amount of the loss. The sole issue was whether the trial court erred in failing to direct a verdict for the defendants on the ground that the plaintiff, as a matter of law, failed to comply with this record-keeping clause. The plaintiff maintained a cash fund of approximately $3,000 for cashing patrons' payroll checks, kept the cash and checks locked in the insured safe overnight, and recorded only their combined total on a scratch-pad, without separate totals for cash and checks. Following a burglary discovered on February 10, 1954, the jury found a loss of $2,740, after crediting $182 the plaintiff recouped by recalling details of two stolen checks and obtaining duplicate payment from their drawers. The court held that compliance as to cashed payroll checks required records listing each check's amount plus data, such as the drawer's name and the payee or check number, enabling claims upon the drawers. Because the plaintiff's records were insufficient to allow the insurers to accurately determine the loss, this breach of condition barred recovery. Judgment reversed, and cause remanded with directions to dismiss the complaint.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed a Tax Court judgment holding Pacific Basin Manufacturing & Trade Company liable for income tax deficiencies for 1975 and 1976. The taxpayer, a Delaware corporation manufacturing jewelry in American Samoa, excluded revenue from sales to its Hawaii-based parent from gross income under 26 U.S.C. § 931(a), which exempts income of domestic corporations doing business in U.S. possessions. The IRS agreed the taxpayer qualified under § 931(a) but assessed deficiencies under § 931(b), which taxes amounts "received within the United States." Because the parent deposited payment checks into the taxpayer's Honolulu bank account, the court held the amounts were received in the United States. The court rejected the taxpayer's argument that receipt should depend on the corporation's primary physical location, as this would render § 931(b) redundant.

Language enrollment in the United States is declining, with some programs cut or reduced and languages such as German and French in especially precarious positions. This article argues that the purpose of language education lies in connection, echoing ACTFL's tagline "language connects," and proposes fostering students' imagined communities—connections formed through imagination with target-language speakers and cultures—as a way to operationalize this idea. The approach was implemented in a yearlong study in two suburban eighth-grade German classrooms in the Northeastern United States, where German had the lowest enrollment, in order to boost interest and retention. Because no prepackaged curriculum exists, instructors must design plausible, authentic scenarios, best delivered through task-based instruction, in which students imagine themselves using the target language in real-world situations, such as finding and furnishing an apartment, navigating transit, or, at the postsecondary level, applying for jobs or planning study abroad. Scaffolding and just-in-time instruction support task completion. Reported outcomes include deeper cultural learning, increased feelings of connection and membership in target-language communities, and, anecdotally, more students continuing language study beyond required years. The approach requires planning time and ongoing adjustment but can be applied at all levels and with all languages.

This work examines the application of steady-state global variance reduction techniques (VRTs) to time-dependent Monte Carlo neutron transport simulations and their interactions with population control techniques (PCTs). VRTs discussed include implicit capture (IC), weight windows, CADIS, FW-CADIS, and Cooper-Larsen (CL) weight windows; PCTs include uniform combing (UC) and weight-based combing (WC). Simulations used Shift with its time-dependent branch and DENOVO for adjoint flux generation, and the fully time-dependent code MC/DC, run on LLNL's Lassen supercomputer. Performance was assessed using a figure of merit (FOM) normalized to analog cases. In a pulsed slab problem in Shift, FW-CADIS performed best, though gains were modest, partly because weight windows lacked time dependence and WC was always active. In the supercritical AZURV1 benchmark in MC/DC, CL weight windows with UC greatly improved FOM, with time-dependent weight windows outperforming static ones; CL with WC exhausted memory because WC's weight resetting caused excessive splitting at the pulse edge. IC showed unexpectedly poor synergy with UC in both supercritical and subcritical versions. In a 1D SCRAM problem with a moving surface, PCTs proved necessary for managing particle populations, and CL with UC again performed best while CL with WC failed. The authors conclude that inappropriate VRT-PCT combinations—weight windows with WC and IC with UC—reduce efficiency, whereas CL weight windows with UC substantially improve time-dependent simulations, and time-dependent adaptations of steady-state VRTs are promising.

The National Endowment for the Humanities and First Nations Development Institute will each contribute about $2 million to fund Native language education in tribal communities. Roughly 150 Native languages are spoken nationwide, including 20 in Alaska, and these languages are endangered. Funding will be highly competitive, favoring working immersion programs and language retention efforts. Tribes will submit proposals, and about 15 programs will be funded annually.

The passage is a patent application disclosure describing methods, polypeptides, nucleic acids, and genetically modified host cells for producing cannabinoids, cannabinoid derivatives, cannabinoid precursors, or cannabinoid precursor derivatives. It identifies novel geranyl pyrophosphate:olivetolic acid geranyltransferase (GOT) polypeptides (e.g., CsPT4) that catalyze production of cannabigerolic acid (CBGA) from geranyl pyrophosphate (GPP) and olivetolic acid at levels at least ten times higher than previously discovered Cannabis polypeptides (e.g., CsPT1/SEQ ID NO:82). The disclosure covers genetically modified host cells (eukaryotic, prokaryotic, yeast, plant) comprising heterologous nucleic acids encoding GOT polypeptides, along with other pathway enzymes including tetraketide synthase (TKS), olivetolic acid cyclase (OAC), acyl-activating enzymes, geranyl pyrophosphate synthetase, acetyl-CoA carboxylase, and mevalonate pathway enzymes. Methods for producing cannabinoids include culturing genetically modified host cells in suitable media and recovering produced cannabinoids. The disclosure also describes isolated nucleic acids, vectors, and methods for making genetically modified host cells. The cannabinoid biosynthetic pathway proceeds from GPP and hexanoyl-CoA through TKS and OAC to produce olivetolic acid, which is then prenylated by GOT to produce CBGA, which is converted by synthases to cannabinoids like THCA and CBDA. The broad substrate specificity of these polypeptides enables production of non-naturally occurring cannabinoid derivatives.

Louisiana Congressman Steve Scalise and three others were shot by 66-year-old James T. Hodgkinson, a former Bernie Sanders campaign volunteer, at a congressional baseball practice. Dozens of federal judges responding to a New York Times survey expressed concern about the Supreme Court's emergency docket decisions in cases involving President Trump since his second term. Of 65 respondents, only 12 said the Court made appropriate use of the emergency docket, and only 12 said lower-court judges receive sufficient guidance on applying emergency orders. Of 54 judges asked about public perception, 42 said the docket caused harm, 10 said no effect, and two said improvement. Anonymous judges called the orders "mystical," "overly blunt" and "demoralizing," while a Trump appointee said they were "flushing out anti-democratic rulings." The survey was sent to more than 400 judges, with 28 Republican and 37 Democratic nominees responding. The Volokh Conspiracy critiqued the survey, suggesting possible oversampling of judges likely to disagree with the rulings.
