Following an FBI raid on the home and office of President Trump's personal attorney Michael Cohen, Trump pardoned former Bush administration aide Scooter Libby, who had been convicted in 2007 of perjury and obstruction of justice. Critics, including Rep. Adam Schiff, said the pardon signaled protection to those implicated in the Russia investigation; the White House denied this but declined to rule out a future pardon for Cohen. The Constitution grants the president exclusive pardon authority, but the full scope of that power has never been tested. Legal scholars debate whether pardons issued for corrupt purposes are valid and whether a president can pardon himself, noting historical precedents such as Bush's Iran-Contra pardons, Nixon's considered self-pardon, and Clinton's pardon of Marc Rich. Schiff introduced legislation requiring public disclosure of evidence against pardon recipients connected to investigations involving the president or his family, while New York's attorney general seeks to close a "double jeopardy loophole" that could enable state prosecution of federally pardoned individuals. Legal experts note that a pardoned person loses Fifth Amendment protections and must testify truthfully, meaning a pardon could potentially advance rather than hinder an investigation.

JPMorgan downgraded Valero Energy (NYSE: VLO) from Overweight to Neutral while raising its price target from $75 to $78. Analysts believe the stock has already gained some multiple uplift from stable returns and improved capital discipline under CEO Joe Gorder, but further uplift may take time given the industry's cyclical nature. JPMorgan views 2016 as below mid-cycle but not a trough for refining.

This study investigates whether LLM-driven agents spontaneously exhibit egoistic or altruistic behavior in social dilemmas where individual and collective interests conflict. The authors propose a Schelling-variant urban migration model in which 225 LLM agents reside across nine blocks and must trade off individual utility against system utility, with a public message board introduced to foster pro-social norms and three GSD prompt levels controlling reasoning depth. Six LLMs were evaluated using quantitative metrics (Price of Anarchy, Residential Gini Index, and micro-level action classification) alongside a qualitative LLM-as-judge analysis inspired by Grounded Theory. Results reveal two behavioral archetypes: "Adaptive Egoists" (o1-mini, o3-mini, Qwen2.5-7B) default to self-interest and settle into sub-optimal equilibria, but show significantly increased altruism when exposed to the message board; "Altruistic Optimizers" (Gemini-2.5-pro, Deepseek-R1, Deepseek-V3.1) consistently converge to the system-optimal state with high altruistic actions regardless of social interaction. The authors conclude that selecting an LLM for social simulation constitutes a choice of the simulation's underlying theoretical foundation, and argue that evaluation should shift from task performance to the social theories of behavior that LLMs embody. Noted limitations include the model's simplification of real-world migration complexities and the homogeneity of agents.

This retrospective study examined the association between resting heart rate (RHR) and all-cause mortality (ACM) in ICU patients with intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) using the MIMIC-IV database. A cohort of 1,918 adult patients (mean age 67.6 years; 970 male) admitted to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center between 2011 and 2019 was divided into four RHR quartiles. Overall ACM rates were 17.2% in the ICU, 28.9% at 30 days, 32.0% at 90 days, and 37.0% at 1 year. Multivariate Cox regression showed no significant RHR-ACM association when RHR was ≤78.5 bpm, but RHR above 78.5 bpm was significantly associated with ACM, with Q3–Q4 showing approximately 50–100% higher mortality per quartile increase compared with Q1. Restricted cubic splines identified a nonlinear (J-shaped) relationship with a threshold of 90.3 bpm: RHR below 90.3 bpm may be an independent protective factor, while RHR above this threshold is independently associated with increased ACM risk and showed predictive value (AUC >0.5). Subgroup analyses revealed an interaction between RHR and age, with a negative mediating effect of age, and the RHR-ACM association was not significant in the IVH subgroup at 30 days. The authors conclude that RHR stratification may support heart rate management strategies, noting blood pressure exclusion and the need for randomized trials as limitations.

The court affirmed the Unemployment Insurance Appeal Board's decision denying Michael Moss unemployment benefits, finding substantial evidence supported the ruling that his resignation in lieu of discharge—after pulling a box cutter on his supervisor—constituted disqualifying misconduct.

In this lecture, Siqi Zheng explains how to quantitatively measure the benefits of green buildings and cities using the hedonic pricing model. She distinguishes between stated preference (surveys, which are unreliable) and revealed preference (observing real estate transactions) for estimating willingness to pay. The hedonic model decomposes a house's price into components—physical attributes, location, amenities—plus an unobservable residual ("trash can"), estimated through regression on large transaction datasets. Log-transformed coefficients are interpreted as percentage changes; empirical studies find roughly 6% rent premiums and 7.6% price premiums for green buildings.

Zheng then addresses causal inference challenges: researchers cannot observe the counterfactual, leading to bias and endogeneity, which arises from omitted variables, reverse causality, and selection bias. Comparing green and non-green buildings is often an "apples-to-oranges" comparison. Solutions include randomized controlled trials (the gold standard, though difficult), geographic matching, propensity score matching, instrumental variables, regression discontinuity, and difference-in-differences.

Applications discussed include the Winthrop Center case, where hedonic analysis could justify design choices, and her own research estimating an 8% school district premium in China. Case studies of Bryant Park's private-public restoration and the High Line Park illustrate how amenities raise nearby property values, with the High Line also demonstrating environmental gentrification, where wealthier households displace original residents. Zheng emphasizes that understanding these methods enables future decision-makers to critically evaluate quantitative analyses.

Purdue University ended its GEAR UP program, which served over 13,000 low-income Indiana students, after the Education Department canceled its $34.9 million federal grant, citing violations of its merit, fairness, and excellence policy and civil rights law. Purdue did not appeal.

Edinburgh has experienced increased haar this spring due to reduced temperature contrasts across the Atlantic, which weakened the jet stream. The Turtle Trading Strategy is a trend-following approach developed by Richard Dennis and William Eckhardt in the 1980s, named after Dennis's 1983 experiment designed to determine whether trading could be learned. Dennis recruited 14 novice traders through a Wall Street Journal advertisement, trained them for two weeks, and funded their accounts with $500,000 to $2,000,000. The experiment succeeded, supporting Dennis's view that trading can be taught; Eckhardt later acknowledged he was wrong.

The original rules included three key elements: volatility-based position sizing using the average true range (ATR) to maintain equivalent risk per dollar; pyramiding, or adding to winning trades while keeping a low risk-to-reward ratio; and predetermined stop-loss orders and exit criteria. The Turtles traded over two dozen instruments, including US bonds, commodities, currencies, and S&P 500 futures.

The strategy's logic assumes that established trends persist, so traders enter on breakouts (such as a 20-day high), add positions on subsequent breakouts, and exit when an opposite trend emerges. Turtles who followed the rules profited substantially, while some who struggled with exits were dismissed. Jerry Parker still manages Chesapeake Capital, while Curtis Faith's money management firm failed. Dennis lost more than half his assets between 1987 and 1988 and stopped trading; Eckhardt founded a CTA in 1991 that produced a 17.35% compound annual return over 20 years.

The strategy still works today, though likely less profitably than in the 1980s, as indicated by the Barclay CTA Index and hedge funds such as Sweden's Lynx, which show low or negative correlation to stocks. Turtle systems performed well in bitcoin and crypto until 2022, though trends have weakened as that market matures. Backtests from 2007 onward of momentum, dual moving average, ATR channel breakout, and Bollinger Band breakout strategies showed lower performance than earlier periods. Trend-following involves many whipsaws, a low win rate, and long drawdowns, making real-money trading harder than backtests suggest.

The Microbus-inspired ID Buzz hasn't been cleared for production but may succeed through shared ID underpinnings, possibly arriving by 2025. The regular ID targets Golf buyers; the Crozz may suit Americans with all-wheel drive.

The ADS868xW family (ADS8681W, ADS8685W, ADS8689W) from Texas Instruments comprises 16-bit successive-approximation-register (SAR) analog-to-digital converters with an integrated analog front end (AFE), ADC driver, and voltage reference. A second-order antialiasing low-pass filter at the PGA output typically has a –3dB cutoff of 500kHz. The device operates with an internal 4.096V reference (default after reset) or an external reference, selected via the INTREF_DIS bit of the RANGE_SEL_REG register. The internal reference is factory-trimmed, may shift due to soldering and thermal stress, and is temperature compensated over –40°C to +125°C. In external mode, a 4.096V reference is applied at REFIO, and the internal buffer drives the REFCAP pin with typical drift of 0.5ppm/°C (maximum 2ppm/°C). Output data is in straight-binary format, with LSB size equal to FSR/2^16.

Alarm features include an active-high ALARM output with an input alarm (user-programmable thresholds and hysteresis) and an AVDD alarm with fixed thresholds of 4.7V (low) and 5.3V (high); active and tripped alarm flags are stored in the ALARM_REG register. The multiSPI digital interface supports four legacy SPI-compatible write protocols, read protocols using a single SDO, dual SDO, or source-synchronous modes, and a daisy-chain topology for multiple devices; the host perceives the device as a 32-bit input-output shift register. The device has three functional states (RESET, ACQ, CONV), programmable NAP and power-down low-power modes, and nine configuration registers.

An application example describes an eight-channel industrial analog input module combining the ADS8681W with a MUX36D08 differential multiplexer, handling standard voltage and current inputs up to ±10V with settling to 1% accuracy in under 5µs. Power-supply decoupling, layout recommendations, register map descriptions, and related documentation are also provided.

According to preliminary BC Coroners Service data, 1,422 suspected illicit drug overdose deaths occurred in British Columbia in 2017, a 43% increase from 993 deaths in 2016. Deaths declined in the final four months of 2017, averaging 96.5 per month versus 129.5 per month in the first eight months. Fentanyl was detected in approximately 81% of deaths, often combined with other illicit drugs, and carfentanil was found in 64 deaths between June and December 2017. Most deaths occurred indoors, particularly in private residences; four out of five victims were male, and more than half were aged 30 to 49. Vancouver recorded the highest number of deaths (358). No deaths occurred at supervised consumption or overdose prevention sites. Officials stated 2018 strategies will include naloxone distribution, drug-checking services, and outreach teams.

This study investigates dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) using natural dyes extracted from mangosteen peel (MP), rich in anthocyanins, and grass jelly leaves (GJL), rich in chlorophyll, combined at volume ratios of 3:1, 2:1, 1:1, 1:2, and 1:3. DSSCs were fabricated with TiO2-coated ITO substrates, a KI/I2 redox electrolyte, and graphite counter electrodes. UV-Vis analysis showed complementary absorption between the two dyes, broadening light harvesting across the visible spectrum. Morphological analysis revealed MP-rich films suffered cracking, while balanced and GJL-rich mixtures formed more uniform films. The 1:3 MP:GJL ratio achieved the highest power conversion efficiency (3.50 ± 0.19%), outperforming pure MP (2.75%) and pure GJL (2.12%), attributed to synergistic effects enhancing photon absorption and charge collection. GJL-rich mixtures also retained performance better over ten test cycles, while the 1:1 ratio degraded rapidly. The findings indicate optimized natural dye blends can serve as low-cost, eco-friendly sensitizers, though long-term stability requires further improvement.

Depoe Bay, Oregon, a town of 1,500 residents, is preparing for the August 21 total solar eclipse—the first to cross the continental United States in a century and the first visible from any of the lower 48 states since 1979—as if it were a natural disaster, since the town is near where totality will first appear on land. Fearing crowds estimated in the thousands to hundreds of thousands, the city has rented portable restrooms, added garbage cans, and ordered protective glasses, while advising residents to stock up on supplies. With Highway 101 the only access route, firefighters will staff three stations for four days, and the Coast Guard will monitor harbor traffic.

NVIDIA RTX IO is a suite of technologies enabling GPU-based loading and decompression of game assets, accelerating I/O performance by up to 100x compared to hard drives and traditional storage APIs. Working with Microsoft's DirectStorage API, it offloads decompression work from CPU cores to the RTX GPU, improving frame rates, enabling near-instantaneous loading, and reducing install sizes. It also benefits artists and designers working with large datasets and production rendering.

Forecasts indicate the Oroville Dam's spillways may face less severe testing than feared, with 7.5 inches of rain expected over 10 days—far less than the 13.6 inches that damaged the spillways in February. The lecture reviews obtaining scattering amplitudes from momentum-space correlation functions via the LSZ theorem: one takes the on-shell limit, distinguishing initial momenta (negative energy root) from final momenta (positive energy root), and sums truncated, connected Feynman diagrams with external propagators stripped. Diagrams that only correct external legs are captured by a factor Z, which is the same for different processes but different for different particle types; Z is set to 1 at leading order and physically represents a particle interacting with its own virtual particles. Concluding scalar interacting theories, the lecture turns to fermions. Historically, the Klein-Gordon equation lacked positive-definite probability and contained negative-energy states, so Dirac sought a first-order, Lorentz-covariant equation. By promoting the coefficients to matrices and requiring that squaring the equation yields the Klein-Gordon equation, one obtains anticommutation conditions minimally satisfied by 4×4 matrices, making psi a four-component object called a spinor. Rewriting with gamma matrices gives the Dirac equation and the Clifford algebra. Infinitely many representations exist, all related by similarity transformations and thus physically equivalent, though different forms are convenient in nonrelativistic or ultrarelativistic regimes. For massless particles, 2×2 (Pauli) matrices suffice, so massless fermions have fewer degrees of freedom. The Dirac equation also admits a positive-definite classical current. Scalar Lorentz covariance was recalled; demonstrating Dirac covariance is deferred to the next lecture.

Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt will fund, through Schmidt Sciences—the organization he created with his wife Wendy—a project sending uncrewed surface vessels (USVs) into the rough ocean around Antarctica to collect data on the Southern Ocean, one of the world's most important carbon sinks, which scientists understand poorly. Schmidt Sciences will spend $45 million over five years on carbon cycle research projects, including this one. Extreme conditions, such as the Drake Passage and cloud cover hindering satellites, have limited data collection, and most ocean carbon data comes from commercial ships restricted to shipping routes. Four USVs will operate continuously for five years, including winter, taking sophisticated CO2 partial pressure measurements, with machine learning guiding their routes; the data will be made public. Funding is structured as a public-private partnership involving NOAA. Scientists note private funding is becoming more crucial as federal science budgets face proposed cuts.

The passage documents AMD AGESA procedures. AMD_ENABLE_STACK is a stackless, native assembler routine using a register-passing model that initializes the processor and cache system to establish a pre-memory stack region divided among processor cores, maps it to global address space, and sets MTRRs (x86-64 only). It must run on all cores, sets up SS/ESP differently for protected or real mode, creates a UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF instance, and returns AGESA_SUCCESS, WARNING (stack re-entry), or FATAL (unknown processor family). PSP-enhanced AARCH64 APUs do not use the stack; the PSP initializes DRAM. AMD_DISABLE_STACK removes the pre-memory stack, returning the processor and cache to a non-stack-enabled state; it is run once when main memory becomes available, disables CAR mode, flushes cache lines, preserves EBX, and should only be invoked by the BSP.

AmdCreateStruct creates storage for an AGESA parameter block and pre-initializes it with default values, supporting PreMemHeap, PostMemDram, and host-pre-allocated methods; it requires a stack and must be paired with AmdReleaseStruct.

Additional service procedures include: obtaining DIMM data eye results as a 31-element, 32-bit bitmap normalized to the 1D trained center; determining a core's APIC address (x86-64 only); returning available pre-memory execution cache size; determining a processor die's base PCI address; identifying the current core by socket, die, and core; and mapping a memory address to its FRU DIMM location (socket, channel, DIMM, chip select, bank, row, column) to aid memory failure diagnosis. These procedures require operational HyperTransport links and an established stack.

Lab experiments show that jostling microbubbles of air and methane in water can generate tiny microlightning zaps, possibly explaining what ignites methane to create will-o'-the-wisps—the bluish lights reported above swamps and cemeteries for centuries. Chemists led by Richard Zare and Yu Xia used a 3-D-printed nozzle to make bubbles, detecting flashes with a photon counter and high-speed camera. Smaller bubbles carry negative charge while larger ones are positively charged, causing electrons to leap between them. Skeptics like Antonio Pavão and Luigi Garlaschelli note that the experiments occurred underwater while wisps are flames hovering in air, so the mystery remains unsolved. Researchers suggest such microlightning could serve as an environmentally friendly trigger for chemical reactions and help break down pollutant gases.

All devices share the host's CONVST/CS and SCLK pins; each device's SDO-0 connects to the next device's SDI, with the last device's SDO-0 returning to the host. The host programs identical register values (SDO_CTL_REG bits 7-0 = 00h). Devices sample inputs on CONVST/CS's rising edge, shifting data MSB-first so the host receives device N's data first. Optimal frames use 32 × N SCLK capture edges; shorter frames cause erroneous configuration.

In this message to Congress, the President addresses the conservation of national resources. The public domain has declined from 1,055,911,288 acres in 1860 to 731,354,081 acres, with an additional 368,035,975 acres in Alaska. Early lax land laws allowed fraudulent acquisition of millions of acres, now unrecoverable due to statutes of limitations. The administration has continued prosecuting land frauds and withdrawing coal lands and power sites, with temporary withdrawals covering 102 streams. Congress is urged to validate these withdrawals and authorize the Secretary of the Interior to make temporary withdrawals pending new legislation. Lands should be classified by the Interior Department through the Geological Survey; mineral rights should be separated from surface titles, with coal, oil, and phosphate leased on royalty terms, and water-power sites disposed of under conditions such as fifty-year limits and graduated rentals to prevent monopoly. Soil conservation is called the foremost concern, aided by Department of Agriculture work and state action, while the enlarged homestead of 320 acres has advanced dry farming. Reclamation projects, though generally well executed, exceed available funds, leaving settlers distressed; the President recommends issuing up to $30,000,000 in bonds repaid from the reclamation fund with the credit of the United States pledged. The timber acts of June 3, 1878, should be repealed. Forest reserves of about 190,000,000 acres are under the Department of Agriculture, but only 3 percent of privately owned forests are scientifically managed, and control of private forests rests with the states. Reforestation at the sources of navigable streams is proposed. Finally, inland waterway improvements, including Ohio River dams with a remaining cost of $63,000,000, and Mississippi and Missouri River projects, are recommended, and pending investigations of the Interior Department and Forest Service should not delay this legislation.

The passage describes NVIDIA RTX IO, which works with Microsoft's DirectStorage API to enable GPU-based lossless decompression, moving compressed data directly from NVMe SSDs to the GPU. This reduces CPU load, improves I/O performance, and delivers up to 100X throughput with 20X lower CPU utilization, benefiting professionals working with large datasets and enabling faster game loading.

The NVIDIA A40, based on the GA10x Ampere architecture, is a data center GPU for visual computing offering up to 2X FP32 throughput, 2X ray-tracing throughput, and up to 5X (10X with sparsity) AI training throughput compared to the Quadro RTX 6000. It features 48GB of memory (scalable to 96GB via NVLink), PCIe Gen4, and vGPU support.

Ampere GPUs support 4K at 120Hz and 8K at 60Hz displays via DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 with DSC 1.2a. The fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware decoding for codecs including AV1—a first for GPUs—while the seventh-generation NVENC handles encoding at quality exceeding x264 Fast and matching x264 Medium presets.

GA10x delivers up to 2X performance improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI, featuring second-generation RT Cores and third-generation Tensor Cores. It is the first GPU architecture to support GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling, achieving up to 936 GB/sec bandwidth in the RTX 3090. The GeForce RTX 3090 (GA102, 24GB GDDR6X) is 1.5X faster than TITAN RTX, while the RTX 3070 (GA104) outperforms the RTX 2080 Ti. A new Error Detection and Replay (EDR) feature helps overclockers identify memory limits before crashes occur. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU includes 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 48GB GDDR6, expandable to 96GB via NVLink.

This document specifies the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) for AMD's SEV-ES and SEV-SNP technologies, which protect guest register state from the hypervisor by encrypting it during world switches. VMEXITs are classified as Automatic Exits (AEs), which expose no guest state, or Non-Automatic Exits (NAEs), which trigger a #VC exception and allow the guest to selectively share register state with the hypervisor through the GHCB.

The document's purpose is to standardize the GHCB memory area so a guest OS can interoperate with any SEV-ES/SEV-SNP-capable hypervisor, define required NAE events and minimum guest state, and standardize actions such as NMI handling and SMP booting. The GHCB is a 4KB decrypted page whose format mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save state area through offset 0x3ff.

Version 2 adds initial SEV-SNP support and hypervisor feature advertisement via a 52-bit FEATURES bitmap returned through the GHCB MSR protocol. Later revisions added 64-bit guest request message sequence numbers, a VLEK certificate GUID, APIC ID list retrieval, multiple VMPL support, page state change support for SEV-ES guests, SEV-TIO trusted IO, and Secure AVIC.

The GHCB MSR protocol defines request/response functions for hypervisor feature support, CPUID queries, SEV information, AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration (required for SEV-SNP guests), page state changes, Run VMPL, GHCB unregistration, and termination requests.

The document details NAE event handling, including IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, MMIO access, Page State Change (private/shared/PSMASH/UNSMASH operations), SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request (certificate return), SNP AP Creation, #HV doorbell page management, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Request, Secure AVIC backing pages, and termination requests, with errors communicated via SW_EXITINFO1/SW_EXITINFO2.

Additional sections cover SMP booting (AP Jump Table, AP Reset Hold), NMI handling via #DB interception and "NMI Complete" messages, debug register virtualization, and note that SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported. The #HV doorbell page defines PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields for host-guest interrupt communication.

The article examines the relationship between consumer confidence and stock market returns using US consumer confidence data from the OECD starting in 1993. Consumer confidence, measured by indices such as The Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index (CCI) and the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index, gauges consumers' optimism or pessimism about the economy. The CCI is based on a monthly survey of 5,000 US households; changes below 5% are considered insignificant, while shifts above 5% indicate a change in the economy's momentum. In the first backtest, a strategy investing in the S&P 500 only when consumer confidence was above its 12-month moving average turned $10,000 into $99,000 over 28 years (CAGR 8.4%, max drawdown 23%, invested 55% of the time), compared with buy and hold's $159,000 (CAGR 10.4%, drawdown 55%). The opposite strategy—investing when confidence was below the average—turned $10,000 into only $15,000 (1.58% annually). The backtests conclude that stocks perform much better when consumer confidence is above its 12-month moving average and poorly when below it.

Natalie Grabow, 80, of Mountain Lakes, New Jersey, set the world record as the oldest woman to finish the Kona Ironman World Championship, completing the full-distance race in 16 hours, 45 minutes, and 26 seconds, under the 17-hour cutoff. She learned to swim at 59, having been unable to afford lessons as a child, and began competing in triathlons at 60. After running 5Ks and 10Ks in her 50s, she qualified for Kona at 61, completing her first ocean swim and marathon there. She trains about two hours daily for months before races and eats healthy food without restrictions, favoring sweets. After the 2025 race, where she tripped near the finish line, she was greeted by previous record holder Cherie Gruenfeld and received a winner's bowl. She plans to compete for as long as she can.

Lenovo officially unveiled the ThinkPad 25, a limited edition retro laptop based on the T470, at Yamato Labs in Yokohama, Japan. Inspired by the 1992 ThinkPad 700C, it combines retro elements like a red TrackPoint and seven-row keyboard with modern hardware. Limited quantities are available in select countries starting at $1,899.

COPD, a leading cause of death in the United States, is caused almost exclusively by smoking and presents with chronic coughing and shortness of breath. Diagnosis involves a smoking history and pulmonary function testing. While incurable, treatments include inhalers, oxygen, and pulmonary rehabilitation; quitting smoking is the key prevention.

Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations employ two principal methods for calculating thermal properties: the Green-Kubo (GK) method, based on heat flux autocorrelation in equilibrium systems, and Non-Equilibrium MD (NEMD), which applies a temperature gradient between thermal reservoirs. Heat flux is central to both methods and to computing Interfacial Thermal Conductance and the Spectral Decomposition of the Heat Current (SDHC). LAMMPS, a widely used MD code, originally used a heat flux formula valid only for pair potentials, which can yield incorrect thermal conductivity results for many-body potentials. Although Torii et al. derived exact formulas for arbitrary many-body potentials, prior implementations were limited to specific systems or pairwise interactions. This work extends and implements the Torii et al. formulas in LAMMPS for calculating heat flux in both control volumes and control surfaces, including spectral decomposition, for arbitrary many-body potentials. The paper presents comparative tests using Tersoff and Stillinger-Weber potentials on 2D and 3D solids, and SDHC results for graphene and MoS2. The Methods section introduces the Hardy formula for instantaneous heat flux and discusses partitioning of many-body potential energy among atoms.

This paper presents first-principles calculations of the tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) effect in Mn3Sn(01̄10)/MgO(110)/Mn3Sn magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs), where Mn3Sn is a kagome noncollinear antiferromagnet with an inverse triangular magnetic structure that breaks time-reversal symmetry at room temperature. While conventional antiferromagnets lack net spin polarization and thus show no TMR in Julliere's picture, antiferromagnets breaking time-reversal symmetry exhibit momentum-space spin splitting that enables spin-polarized currents and finite TMR. The chosen Mn3Sn(01̄10) orientation is suitable because electrical switching via spin-orbit torque has been experimentally realized in this geometry. Using density functional theory with the Landauer–Büttiker formalism and sufficiently thick MgO barriers that ensure tunneling transport, the authors find the TMR ratio reaches ≳1000% at 12 MgO layers, with resistance-area products reasonable for practical devices. Analysis of Mn3Sn's Fermi-surface spin polarization and MgO's complex band structure shows the TMR effect arises from the momentum-dependent spin splitting of Mn3Sn—mainly the x-component along the cluster octupole easy axis—combined with electron filtering by MgO, whose lowest decay rate is smallest near k∥ = 0 where the transmission difference between parallel and antiparallel configurations is largest. Unlike previous Mn3Sn studies lacking realistic barriers, this work provides a practical reference for Mn3Sn-based antiferromagnetic spintronic devices, which offer advantages such as reduced stray fields and faster switching.

Jeff Bezos has proposed that future data infrastructure could be built in space, arguing that orbital data centres could ease constraints on land, energy, and cooling while providing resilience against terrestrial disruptions. The idea responds to growing demand for cloud services and AI computing power, which is straining existing infrastructure that already consumes large amounts of electricity and water. Orbital facilities could tap solar energy, but face unresolved challenges including radiation shielding, power storage, cooling in a vacuum, reliable low-latency communication links, and high launch and maintenance costs. Other aerospace and technology companies are exploring orbital and lunar-based infrastructure, encouraged by falling launch costs and miniaturised hardware. Proponents argue early investment could become commercially viable as data demand continues to rise.

This study qualitatively evaluated distance education applications in sports higher education institutions in Turkey during the COVID-19 pandemic. Fourteen lecturers were selected through criterion sampling and interviewed using a semi-structured form, with data analyzed via descriptive analysis in MAXQDA 20 (82% reliability). Four themes emerged: positive aspects, including independence from time and space, access to resources, use of information technologies, and socioeconomic benefits; negative aspects, including motivation and communication problems, access and participation issues, inequality of opportunity, and ineffective applied lessons; challenges, primarily infrastructure and connection issues and difficulties in assessment and evaluation; and management concerns, with participants stating the process was poorly managed and lecturers insufficiently trained. Findings indicated distance education provides flexibility and resource access, but applied sports courses could not be conducted adequately, and data security requires attention. The study concluded that further research is needed to determine distance education's efficacy, advantages, and disadvantages across departments.

A study in the Journal of Neuroscience found that barn owls, despite simpler brains than humans and primates, group together elements moving in the same direction to distinguish objects from backgrounds—a visual processing task previously studied only in primates. Researchers led by Yoram Gutfreund showed owls moving dots and measured head turns toward a target. Owls performed better when contrasting dot directions were uniform, and the ocular tectum brain area appeared responsible for this task.
US job gains of 200,000 and 2.9 percent wage growth fueled Fed rate-hike expectations, lifting the dollar and bond yields while stocks fell; 10-year Treasurys hit a four-year high.

Clark County Schools Superintendent Pat Skorkowsky retired on the last day of school, after five years as superintendent and 30 years in the district. He cited the graduation rate rising from 60 to 83 percent and expanded magnet schools as his proudest achievements. Facing a $60 million budget shortfall, he urged incoming superintendent Dr. Jesus Jara and the school board to prepare for the pivotal 2019 legislative session, including reconsidering marijuana tax distribution.

Suicide remains a taboo subject in Fiji, says Lifeline Fiji's program director Jeremiah Merekula. NSAAC statistics record 124 suicides and 107 attempted suicides in 2015; 102 and 104 respectively in 2016; and 627 suicides with 694 attempts from 2011 to March this year, including 56 in children. Fiji reportedly has one of the highest global rates; Lifeline Fiji promotes help-seeking behaviour among students and parents.

At RSA Conference 2017, Intel Security's Chris Young warned of "data landmines"—corrupted data used to influence decisions, citing the 2016 presidential election and risks to businesses whose big-data analysis depends on altered small data. He also identified insecure home networks containing internet of things devices as attack surfaces that can threaten corporate networks as more employees work from home, and stressed that security professionals must cooperate. Microsoft President Brad Smith called on the tech community to act as "a digital Switzerland," adopting Red Cross-style principles: defense only, no offensive activities, collaboration on responses, protecting all customers, and refusing to attack civilians. He proposed a "digital Geneva Convention" barring attacks on the private sector and civil infrastructure, an end to government stockpiling of software vulnerabilities, and an international agency to monitor and attribute nation-state attacks, citing industry cooperation and the U.S.-China cyber espionage agreement endorsed by the G20.

The passage is a patent application (a continuation of earlier filings) describing systems and methods for location sharing within social networking applications. It discloses a geographically-based graphical user interface, termed a "map GUI," that displays approximate positions of a user and the user's friends in a social network using avatars.

The core invention is a method for predicting a user's destination. A social network system receives location information from the user's client device via wireless communication, determines the user's current trajectory, accesses the user's historical location information from a database, and correlates the trajectory with the historical data to determine a presumed destination. The system then displays, on client devices of the user's friends, a map depicting an icon at the location of the presumed destination, and may provide an estimated time of arrival.

The system architecture includes client devices running location sharing client applications, an API server providing programmatic interfaces, an application server hosting a location sharing server application, a messaging system, and a social network system, and a database server storing message data, entity data (including an entity graph of relationships), and location information (geographic coordinates with timestamps). A processing environment includes a processor with a location component, a historical location component, a prediction component, and a map GUI component.

Users may authorize or restrict use of their location information and select audiences (e.g., "Best Friends," "Friends," "Custom") with whom location is shared. Users can view friends' avatars on the map, select friends to center the map on them, and initiate chats without leaving the map.

Destination prediction may involve computing, for candidate destinations (habitual places such as home, work, or school inferred from historical data), probabilities based on distance trends, likelihood of arrival within a preset time, conditional probability of staying, and behavioral match scores; a candidate exceeding a threshold becomes the presumed destination. Alternatively, the system computes a correlation score between the current trajectory and candidate trajectory patterns, selecting a pattern's arrival point when the score exceeds a threshold.

Trajectory patterns (recurring routes) are extracted by clustering historical trajectories using distance functions (e.g., Euclidean, Hausdorff, DTW, LCSS) and clustering methods, then aligning and averaging trajectories within each cluster. Patterns may include average duration, schedule, and mode of transport inferred from infrastructure mapping.

The system updates probabilities as new location data arrives and interrupts display if the probability falls below a second threshold. If communication with a client device is lost, the user's location may be extrapolated by projecting onto the identified trajectory pattern. Transport mode may be used to access schedule and delay information (e.g., trains) to refine arrival predictions. Estimated time of arrival is computed from the pattern's average duration, adjusted for factors such as weather, traffic, and public transport schedules, and updated based on the user's average speed.

The map GUI displays the user's avatar, a destination icon (e.g., a house for home), trajectory pattern illustrations, estimated arrival time, instantaneous speed, and selectable elements for notifications, messaging, and media sharing.

The passage concludes with descriptions of a layered software architecture (operating system, libraries, frameworks, applications), machine hardware (processors, memory, I/O components), and standard patent definitions of terms such as signal medium, communication network, processor, machine-storage medium, component, hardware component, carrier signal, computer-readable medium, and client device.

Gold edged lower as the dollar rose 0.2 percent against the euro ahead of U.S. nonfarm payrolls data, expected to show 180,000 January jobs. Stronger figures could reinforce Federal Reserve rate-hike expectations, weighing on bullion. Spot gold fell 0.3 percent to $1,345.22 an ounce, set to end the week little changed after hitting a 17-month high of $1,366.07. World stocks headed for their biggest weekly drop since late 2016. Silver fell 0.7 percent, platinum 1.4 percent, and palladium was on track for its biggest weekly drop since September, down 4.8 percent.

Vale of Glamorgan Brewery has applied to open a micropub, the Radyr Tap, in Station Road, Radyr—a Cardiff suburb without a pub since the Radyr Arms closed in 2003. The plans follow a Twitter campaign started by resident Jamie Grundy. The pub would occupy a unit previously used by a dry cleaners, serving the brewery's own beers, local cask ales, craft beers, wines, and spirits, along with artisan meats, cheeses, and snacks but no cooked food. A consultation runs until June 19 before Cardiff council makes a decision.

The passage is from the Texas Instruments datasheet SLASFA2A (November 2024, revised April 2025) covering the MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 microcontrollers. It describes the CPU subsystem with an ARM Cortex-M0+ core (32kHz–80MHz), pre-fetch/cache, SysTick timer, MPU, and NVIC. Five operating modes (RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, SHUTDOWN) and two power domains (PD1, PD0) balance performance and power consumption. The PMU generates core supplies and supervises VDD with brown-out reset monitoring. The clock module provides LFOSC, SYSOSC, LFXT, HFXT, and SYSPLL oscillators, distributing clocks such as MCLK, CPUCLK, ULPCLK, MFCLK, and LFCLK. Additional subsystems include a 12-channel DMA, an event manager, flash memory (up to 512kB) with ECC and bank address swap for OTA updates, up to 128KB of SRAM in two banks, up to 93 GPIO pins, IOMUX, two 12-bit ADCs at 4Msps, a temperature sensor, VREF, comparators, and a 12-bit DAC. Security features include an AES-128/256 accelerator, keystore for up to four keys, CRC-16/32, TRNG, and a math accelerator (MATHACL). Communication peripherals include UART (with LIN support), I2C (up to 1Mbit/s), SPI (up to 32Mbits/s), and CAN-FD (up to 5Mbit/s). The LFSS contains RTC_B and an independent watchdog, plus a windowed watchdog and TIMGx/TIMAx timers. Debug uses a two-wire SWD interface, and a BSL enables UART/I2C programming protected by a 256-bit password. The document also covers recommended application circuitry (decoupling capacitors, NRST pullup, ROSC resistor, VCORE capacitor), development tools and documentation support, device nomenclature, the revision history between November 2024 and April 2025, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information with standard TI disclaimers.

MIT has become the first of nine universities invited to publicly reject the Trump administration's "Compact for Academic Excellence in Higher Education," which would require sweeping institutional changes in exchange for preferential federal funding. President Sally Kornbluth, in a letter to Education Secretary Linda McMahon, stated that while MIT's practices meet many compact standards, the document would restrict free expression and institutional independence, with a premise inconsistent with merit-based funding. Other invited universities offered mixed responses, with most reviewing the compact and Texas officials expressing enthusiasm. Some state officials, including California Governor Gavin Newsom, threatened funding consequences for signatories. MIT's rejection drew celebration from academic leaders and Democratic lawmakers, while former Trump administration official Kenneth Marcus hinted at pending legal accountability for MIT's "noncompliance."

Komar Uddin, 68, denies raping a 19-year-old woman at her Leicester home during a candlelit ritual intended to drive out an evil spirit, while her family remained downstairs. The court heard he was invited by her father, who was concerned the woman feared being followed by an evil spirit after a relative's death. The alleged victim said Uddin rubbed holy oil on her stomach, stroked her back, sexually touched her, and raped her twice. He allegedly told her she was pregnant and offered to make it 'go away' for £200. After his arrest, he was released on bail but left the country and was extradited from Germany last November. DNA matching Uddin was found on an internal swab. The defence claims the woman lied and instigated the activity. The trial continues.

Prosecutors released three cellphone videos in which Nikolas Cruz, suspect in the Feb. 14 massacre at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida, announced his intent to become "the next school shooter," kill at least 20 people with an AR-15, and said, "You're all going to die." The undated videos, found on his phone after the attack killed 17 and injured 17, described logistics that surveillance footage showed he almost exactly followed. Cruz, 19, is charged with 17 counts of murder and 17 of attempted murder; his lawyers say he would plead guilty in exchange for life without parole, but prosecutors refuse to waive the death penalty. The videos became public under Florida's discovery law.

Amazon.com, Inc.'s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2020. Amazon, incorporated in Delaware and headquartered in Seattle, Washington, trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol "AMZN." The company operates three segments—North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS)—serving consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators. As of December 31, 2020, it employed approximately 1,298,000 full- and part-time employees, with 503,564,743 shares outstanding as of January 20, 2021.

For 2020, net sales were $386.1 billion (compared with $280.5 billion in 2019), operating income was $22.9 billion, and net income was $21.3 billion, with diluted earnings per share of $41.83. Total assets were $321.2 billion, and cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $84.4 billion at year-end. Operating cash flow was $66.1 billion, and cash capital expenditures were $35.0 billion. The company incurred more than $11.5 billion in COVID-19 related costs during 2020 and hired over 400,000 employees since February 2020 to expand fulfillment capacity.

The filing identifies risks including intense competition, international operations (including regulatory restrictions in China and India), inventory and fulfillment challenges, data security breaches, payments-related risks, evolving government regulation, litigation, and tax liabilities. As of December 31, 2020, the company operated facilities totaling approximately 454.4 million leased and 20.1 million owned square feet.

The author argues that, beyond simply disrupting the existing liberal world order, President Trump is attempting to build a new one divided between fossil-fuel-producing "carbonite" states and post-carbon green-energy powers. Trump's strategy involves forming a trilateral alliance of the world's top oil and gas producers—the United States, Russia, and Saudi Arabia—while isolating renewable-energy leaders like Germany and China. Three steps illustrate this design: revitalizing the U.S.-Saudi partnership (including a $110 billion arms deal), weakening NATO and the EU while seeking closer ties with Russia, and withdrawing from the Paris climate accord to boost domestic fossil fuel production. The author notes that this prospective alliance, together with allied producers, would control roughly 57% of world oil output and 59% of natural gas production. Obstacles remain, including Russian sanctions linked to election-meddling allegations and disagreements between Russia and Saudi Arabia over Syria and Iran, though recent Russo-Saudi energy cooperation suggests these barriers may be surmountable.

Researchers led by Omri Yosef and Prof. Michael Berger of the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, in collaboration with Philipps University of Marburg and the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, found that blocking the protein Ant2 reprograms T cells' energy metabolism, making them more resilient, faster to replicate, and more effective at attacking tumors. The mouse study focused on mitochondria as the cells' metabolic hub. The rewiring can be triggered with drugs as well as genetic modification, suggesting potential clinical applications, though further studies and trials are needed.

The passage first addresses naval staffing: a thousand additional officers are needed to man ships provided for and under construction; Annapolis classes should be enlarged, retirements of impaired senior officers facilitated, and promotion fostered. The officer shortage has imposed unusual labor on lieutenants and junior grades, whose steadfast conduct merits thanks. No foreign trouble is anticipated, but maintaining an efficient navy is necessary, as failure to do so would invite trouble and disaster. Second, Post-Office receipts for the fiscal year ending June 30 reached $121,848,047.26, an increase of $10,216,853.87—the largest in postal history. Rural free-delivery, now a fixed policy, had 11,650 routes operating by November 1, 1902, covering about one-third of available territory, with 10,748 additional routes requested; it benefits rural populations and warrants liberal Congressional appropriations. Finally, nationally-aided irrigation in the far West has begun, and legislation is needed to protect forests and game on forest reserves.

This study assessed Belgian medical students' knowledge, attitudes, and exposure to global surgery through an anonymous online survey, receiving 304 responses from four universities. Although 95% of students agreed that global surgery is a relevant topic and 75.3% wanted more exposure, only 24.7% had prior exposure, most commonly through social media. Knowledge was poor: 23.9% correctly identified that five billion people lack access to safe, affordable surgical care, 21.7% knew that approximately 150 million additional procedures are needed annually, and 12.8% knew the three Bellwether procedures. Only 28.6% had heard of InciSioN. Master's students were less likely than bachelor's students to want additional exposure, compulsory global surgery teaching, or a surgical career. About half of students (53.3%) were interested in a surgical career, 35.9% in global surgery, and 37.5% in global health. The most commonly perceived obstacles to a global surgery career were personal or family responsibilities, language barriers, lack of established career paths, financial constraints, and lack of role models and mentorship. The authors conclude that knowledge and exposure are lacking despite profound interest, and advocate for pre-clinical global surgery seminars and equitable, bidirectional international clinical internships in formal medical education. Limitations include possible selection bias, absence of a validated questionnaire, and limited generalizability outside Europe.

Fifty years after Paul Ehrlich's 1968 book The Population Bomb suggested over-breeding poor countries were killing the planet, demographer Jack Caldwell noted similar crowds could be seen during rush hours in London, Paris, or New York, raising the question of racism in concerns about developing-world megacities. Half of humanity lives in urban areas, a figure predicted to reach 66 percent by 2050, with most growth in developing countries' megacities. Cities are described as the solution to population growth rather than its cause: urban women have fewer children than rural women, and migrants swiftly adopt small families. Yet cities also create a consumption bomb, housing half the population while consuming three-quarters of the planet's materials and depending heavily on hinterlands.

Since 2015, the WebRTC VPN bug has leaked users' real IPs even when using VPN services. On March 27, 2018, Stagno tested 124 VPN and proxy providers, finding 20 (16.13%) leaked IPs via WebRTC while 101 kept IPs hidden. Leaking providers include Astrill, BlackVPN, Hola!VPN, and others; users can test their VPNs via provided web pages and disable WebRTC manually or via add-ons if leaks occur. Most browsers enable WebRTC by default except Tor Browser, Edge, and Internet Explorer. A ranked list of privacy-protecting VPNs is provided, with ExpressVPN rated best.

Facebook took over two hours to remove Steve Stephens's videos of the fatal shooting of 74-year-old Robert Godwin, as it relies on user flagging. Hugo Castro went missing in Mexico after pleading for help on Facebook Live. In Georgia, Democrats hope Jon Ossoff, who raised $8.3 million, can flip a Republican House seat.

Section 11 of a Texas Instruments datasheet provides mechanical, packaging, and orderable information for the ADS8681W, ADS8685W, and ADS8689W products, noting the data is subject to change without notice. Footnotes define status, material types for preproduction parts (prototypes sold without warranties), RoHS values, lead finish options, moisture sensitivity level ratings, and part marking conventions. TI disclaims warranty of accuracy for information based on third-party data and limits liability to the annual purchase price of parts sold. Tape and reel dimensions are described as representations; actual packages may vary. TI provides technical and reliability data "as is" with all faults, disclaiming all warranties, including merchantability and fitness for purpose. Resources are intended for skilled developers, who are solely responsible for product selection, application design, validation, and meeting applicable standards. Usage is restricted to development with TI products, no other intellectual property licenses are granted, and users must indemnify TI against claims. Products are subject to TI's Terms of Sale.

Global equity markets declined Monday as U.S. bond yields approached 3 percent, with the 10-year yield hitting 2.998 percent, its highest in over four years. Investors worried about growing government debt supply and accelerating inflation. Commodities fell after the U.S. hinted it might relieve sanctions on Russia's Rusal, with aluminum down 8.7 percent and Alcoa shares down 13.51 percent. The stronger dollar pressured the euro and yen. Oil settled higher after volatility. U.S. stocks were little changed ahead of earnings, with over 180 S&P 500 companies reporting this week.

Caterpillar's board voted to keep its quarterly dividend flat at $0.77 per share, marking the seventh straight quarter without an increase despite the company's 23-year record of dividend growth. The stock, yielding 3.25%, has gained about 20% in nine months, outperforming the Dow and S&P 500. Goldman Sachs added the stock to its 'conviction buy' list with a $120 price target, citing increased mining capital spending. Potential positives include Trump's proposed $1 trillion infrastructure spending, pro-energy policies, an improving US economy, higher oil prices, and dissipating China concerns. However, the stock trades near its 52-week high despite a federal tax investigation and is expensive at 29-times this year's earnings. Risks include the uncertain fate of the infrastructure plan. Caterpillar's 2016 revenues fell 18% to $38.5 billion and EBITDA fell 39% to $4.27 billion, the fourth consecutive annual decline, while excess cash flows dropped to $881 million. The company guides for further 2017 declines, and the author recommends investor caution.

ECGs are widely used for cardiac assessment due to accessibility and cost-effectiveness, and estimating echocardiogram (ECHO) variables from ECGs could enhance early disease detection and healthcare access in resource-limited settings. Two challenges hinder this: the complexity of ECG signals and the scarcity of ECG data labeled with ECHO outcomes. The authors propose EchoingECG, a probabilistic student-teacher framework integrating PCME++ and ECHO-CLIP. Unlike traditional deterministic contrastive learning with one-to-one mappings, PCME++ models the mean and variance of latent representations, enabling many-to-many mappings that capture uncertainty across ECG windows, ECHO frames, and texts. To reduce dependence on large-scale annotated datasets, ECHO-CLIP, trained on ECHO-text pairs, acts as a teacher to distill echo-based cardiac information into ECG representations through ECHO-ECG pairs. Contributions include a probabilistic multimodal ECG model capturing ECHO-derived structural and functional insights, a knowledge distillation approach, and experimental evidence of uncertainty-aware evaluation of downstream tasks.

Henry L. Stimson concluded that the United States should not raise territorial adjustments, including "trusteeships," for discussion until the war progressed further and Russian participation in the Pacific war was accomplished, arguing that raising the subject would provoke distrust and discrimination. The Cairo Declaration of December 1, 1943, stated the Three Great Allies coveted no territorial gain and intended that Japan be stripped of Pacific islands seized or occupied since 1914. At an informal meeting in Washington on January 26, 1945, with diplomatic representatives of certain American Republics, Mr. Grew announced plans for a conference at Mexico City, emphasized strengthening the Inter-American System for the postwar world, noted that ten American republics had commented on the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals, and stated that preserving peace required preparedness to use all means, including force, likening the needed measures to drastic cancer treatment.

On April 20, 2022, Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the Securities and Exchange Commission reporting that it released its financial results for the quarter ended March 31, 2022. The results were made public by posting the First Quarter 2022 Update on Tesla's website, with the full text attached as Exhibit 99.1 and furnished under Item 2.02, "Results of Operations and Financial Condition." The filing identifies Tesla as a Delaware corporation headquartered in Austin, Texas, with common stock trading under the symbol TSLA on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. The report was signed by Zachary J. Kirkhorn, Chief Financial Officer, on behalf of the company.

Chris King, 57, who lost both hands in a work accident and received a double hand transplant at Leeds General Infirmary, visited Headingley Carnegie Stadium for the first time to watch the Rhinos beat Widnes Vikings 42-22. The UK's first double hand transplant patient was applauded after drawing the winning golden gamble ticket at half-time.

The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office rejected Crocs Inc.'s design patent, finding competitor USA Dawgs filed a similar patent a year earlier. Crocs plans to appeal amid store closures and declining revenue.

This study presents a bibliometric analysis of research on Digital Accessibility in Education, using data from the Web of Science, Scopus, and ERIC databases for 2013–2024. Two search queries—"Digital Accessibility" and "Digital Accessibility" AND Education—retrieved 1,544 and 924 records respectively, with VOSviewer 1.6.20 used for analysis and visualization.

Publications on digital accessibility rose from 12 in 2013 to 502 in 2024, with rapid growth after 2020 following the COVID-19 pandemic. Scopus contained the most publications (1,199), followed by WoS (308) and ERIC (37). Journal articles were the most common publication type (468), and the leading research areas were Digital Accessibility and Inclusion (438), Education, Higher Education and Social Sciences (385), and Computer Science and Engineering Sciences (340). English was the dominant publication language (873), and Higher Education was the most represented educational level (469). The USA (236), UK (104), and Spain (74) produced the most publications.

Citation analysis identified Gorriz (2023) as the most cited document (74 citations) and Chen Weiqin as the most cited author (58 citations). The USA (156) and England (155) were the most cited countries, and Norway had the highest link strength. The study concludes that digital accessibility is an increasingly significant research area, while noting limited international collaboration and a need for stronger legal frameworks and future research on computer literacy and motivation for students with disabilities.

This study evaluated a streamlined analysis workflow for Optical Genome Mapping (OGM) data using Variant Intelligence Applications (VIA) software in hematologic malignancies, focusing on myeloid neoplasms. Ten retrospective cases (nine AML, one MDS) were independently analyzed 5–6 times each by blinded technologist-director teams. Datasets were processed through Bionano Solve, then analyzed in VIA using custom views, filters, and classification schemes for variant curation and reporting. Results showed complete concordance between OGM and standard of care (SOC) testing, with all SOC-reported variants identified by OGM. OGM additionally revealed variants absent from SOC reports in five of six positive cases, including small deletions undetectable by karyotype and complex rearrangements. Tier 1A variants were unanimously identified and classified across all reviews. Technologist review times averaged 25.2 minutes for negative cases, 28.5 minutes for simple cases, and 47.3 minutes for complex cases. VIA reduced analysis time by approximately 50% compared to Bionano Access alone. The study concludes that OGM with VIA offers an efficient approach to cytogenomic variant interpretation and reporting in hematological disorders, with potential to standardize analysis across laboratories.

A community has backed Mark Ryan, headteacher of St. Patrick's Catholic Primary School in Thornaby, after a newspaper report inaccurately claimed he took a two-week term-time holiday to attend a wedding abroad and told a parent she would face a fine for taking her child out of school. In fact, Mr Ryan took a three-day leave of absence (June 7-9), sanctioned by school governors as an exceptional circumstance under school policy, to attend a close family friend's wedding. He never directly spoke to the parent who made the complaint. In his 22 years at the school, he has never been absent through illness and made only one other absence request. Governors, staff, parents, and the local community, including chair of governors Gary Wilson and Father Michael Keogh, have voiced their support.

The Shippers Group celebrated the grand opening of a new 540,000-square-foot distribution facility in Austell with a DC Chamber Ribbon Cutting on September 15th. The multi-client facility provides warehousing, transportation, packaging, and e-commerce fulfillment services, bringing the company's total Georgia warehouse space to 1.5 million square feet.

The Mets are overhauling their coaching staff after missing the playoffs with baseball's most expensive opening-day roster. Manager Carlos Mendoza will return, but pitching coach Jeremy Hefner, hitting coaches Jeremy Barnes and Eric Chavez, and third base coach Mike Sarbaugh will not; bench coach John Gibbons resigned and catching coach Glenn Sherlock is retiring. Assistant pitching coach Desi Druschel and bullpen coach José Rosado have permission to speak with other teams, while first base coach Antoan Richardson, strategy coach Danny Barnes, and coaching assistant Rafael Fernandez were invited back. The team went 38-55 over its final 93 games after a 45-24 start, with pitching and defense the biggest problems. A $765 million, 15-year offseason signing pushed roster costs to $429 million in payroll and projected luxury tax. President of baseball operations David Stearns said the rest of the staff would be evaluated.

Apple, the world's most valuable company, is nearing a $1 trillion market cap, but Amazon is closing in. The gap, 50 percent in early 2018, is now about $85 billion after Amazon's shares gained $260 billion this year.

World stocks dipped on Tuesday after the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield crossed 3 percent for the first time since January 2014, dampening equities despite strong earnings from companies like Verizon and Caterpillar. European and U.S. stocks declined, with Alphabet falling 4.93 percent due to surging costs. The Dow fell 0.19 percent, the S&P 500 lost 0.24 percent, and the Nasdaq dropped 0.73 percent. Chipmaker AMS slumped after warning of weaker orders from a major customer. Meanwhile, U.S. earnings showed a strong start with a 21.1 percent expected growth rate, and Brent crude rose above $75 per barrel, its highest level since November 2014, supported by OPEC-led production cuts and strong demand.

The Best 6 Months Timing Model strategy, created by Yale Hirsch, is an active and simple market timing strategy applicable to any asset class and portfolio. Unlike passive strategies that remain invested 100% of the time, it enters the market on an entry signal and exits on an exit signal, reducing risk exposure. Yale Hirsch founded the Hirsch Organization and created the Stock Trader's Almanac, first published in 1968, which brought market phenomena such as the Presidential Election Year Cycle, January Barometer, Santa Claus Rally, and Best Six Consecutive Months to the public. The article backtests the strategy over the past 16 years using a portfolio of five asset classes with equal weights—stocks, bonds, REITs, and commodities—implemented through diversified, liquid ETFs with long performance histories. The backtest showed the timing strategy produced a drawdown of -27.27%, compared to -47.77% for a buy-and-hold approach with the same portfolio.

The speaker responds to the Secretary of State's criticism of calls for restoring American military strength, defining "superiority" as being strong enough that no other nation would dare violate the peace. He contends an arms race already exists, with the Soviets outspending the United States militarily and advancing through Cuban proxies in Africa, and through Soviet, Cuban, and East German presences in Ethiopia, South Yemen, Afghanistan, and Central America—movements he links to threats against essential minerals and oil supplies. He maintains peace must be the top priority but not at any price, citing Czechoslovakia, Vietnam, Laos, and Cambodia. He characterizes the Vietnam War as a noble cause, attributes the "Vietnam Syndrome" to North Vietnamese propaganda, and calls for gratitude toward veterans. This paper examines the normative assumption underlying studies on educational disparities—gaps in opportunities, resources, and attainment tied to social background such as socioeconomic status, gender, region of origin, ethnicity, or disability. It applies luck egalitarianism, a theory of distributive justice holding that inequalities arising from brute luck (factors beyond individual control) are unfair and should be eliminated, while inequalities from option luck (individual choices) fall within personal responsibility. The paper argues that fairness justifies correcting educational disparities but identifies problems through Elizabeth Anderson's critiques: the harshness objection, where individuals face severe consequences for past choices (illustrated by a musician unable to escape poverty), and the humiliation objection, where compensatory policies stigmatize the disadvantaged (illustrated by classroom embarrassment). In response, it proposes three values to supplement fairness: fresh start (permitting new beginnings despite past choices, per Fleurbaey and Tomlin's dynamic luck egalitarianism), sufficiency (guaranteeing resources above a threshold, per sufficientarianism), and respect (avoiding shame and stigma, per Wolff). The paper suggests a pluralistic approach combining sufficiency and luck egalitarianism to address both problems. It concludes that empirical research on educational disparities should examine not only fairness but also fresh start, sufficiency, and respect—for example, through longitudinal data on second chances, achievement thresholds, classroom humiliation, and relational capacities—and that collaboration between normative philosophy and social science can generate new research questions on educational disparities.

The Los Angeles Dodgers defeated the Arizona Diamondbacks 9-5 in Game 1 of the NL Division Series on Friday night in Los Angeles. Justin Turner homered and drove in five runs, tying a Dodgers postseason record for RBIs in a game shared with Pedro Guerrero and Davey Lopes. Home Capital Group is in talks with a syndicate of banks, including Royal Bank of Canada, Bank of Montreal and Toronto-Dominion Bank, for a roughly $2 billion loan to replace an emergency credit line. Depositors have withdrawn 95 per cent of funds from its high-interest savings accounts since March 27, though withdrawals have slowed since mid-May.

Facebook's new algorithm limits feed visibility, making social influencers valuable for maintaining reach. A social influencer is a credible social media user with a large following; their posts about a business are highly valuable. Rather than paying for influencers, pizzerias can seek local ones, such as food bloggers, food enthusiasts, community leaders, and local celebrities.

In *Hardin v. White*, the plaintiff sought to enjoin an execution sale of real estate in Keokuk, claiming the property was not subject to the execution sale, and obtained a decree; the defendant appealed. The court held, first, that although an injunction bond restraining collection of a judgment must be double the judgment's amount, this requirement does not apply where the injunction only restrains the sale of specific property under a general execution; the motion to increase the bond was therefore properly overruled. Second, where a judgment creditor sells real estate under an execution for only part of his judgment, he exhausts his remedy as to that property and cannot later sell the debtor's statutory right of redemption under a second execution for the remainder, even if issued under a decree in a different action, since the debt in both actions is the same and only one satisfaction is allowed. The case was distinguished from *Barnes v. Cavanagh*, and on rehearing the court treated the two decrees covering the same indebtedness as identical. The judgment was affirmed.

The United States Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Tennessee denied defendants East Tennessee Equity, Ltd. and Theodore A. Erck's motion to dismiss an adversary proceeding brought by Thomas E. DuVoisin, Liquidating Trustee under Southern Industrial Banking Corporation's (SIBC) confirmed Modified Plan of Reorganization, to recover alleged fraudulent conveyances under 11 U.S.C.A. § 548(a). Defendants contended the trustee lacked standing under § 548 and that any recovery would not result in equality of distribution among creditors. SIBC filed a chapter 11 petition on March 10, 1983; its Modified Plan, confirmed effective January 20, 1984, provided for a merger into a federally insured successor-in-interest and conveyed certain assets—including preference and fraudulent conveyance claims—to a Creditors' Liquidation Trust that the trustee was empowered to enforce. Impaired general unsecured creditors received, among other things, certificates of deposit and shares of, or warrants to purchase, stock in the successor-in-interest. Following Centennial Industries v. NCR Corporation, the court held that recovery would benefit these creditors by increasing the successor-in-interest's assets and, proportionally, the value of the stock rights included in their distributions, rejecting the equality-of-distribution argument. The court also held the trustee had standing under 11 U.S.C.A. § 1123(b), which permits a plan to provide for retention and enforcement of claims by the debtor, a trustee, or an estate representative, and found defendants' cited authorities—Texas Consumer Financial Corporation, Sapolin Paints, and Whiteford Plastics—distinguishable. Concluding that denying the action would give defendants a windfall while providing no benefit to impaired unsecured creditors, the court denied the motion. A footnote notes that defendants' original jurisdictional challenge under § 109 had been resolved by the district court, which held SIBC eligible to be a chapter 11 debtor.

The IMF released a report on China's financial system, saying regulators should prioritise financial stability over growth, as regional growth targets and efforts to prevent job losses have driven a debt surge, particularly at local government level. It recommended forming a financial stability sub-committee comprising the central bank and three financial regulators, and increasing staff at the banking watchdog. The IMF warned that rapidly developing new financial products, including wealth management products, could pose systemic risks. Stress tests covering 33 banks showed widespread under-capitalisation among joint-stock and city commercial banks under a severely adverse scenario, with a capital shortfall equal to 2.5 percent of GDP. The PBOC said the report was objective but that the stress tests did not reflect the whole picture.

Chrissy Teigen discussed her anxiety and postpartum depression (PPD) in a Marie Claire interview. She was diagnosed with both conditions shortly after her daughter Luna's birth in 2016 and experienced PPD for four months, from September to December 2016. Teigen now takes an antidepressant and, despite still having bad days, wants to expand her family. The article notes her openness shows women experiencing anxiety and depression that they aren't alone.

Islamic finance has thrived despite 2016's economic shocks, with Islamic banks expanding at 19.7% annually and holding $3trn in capital, expected to reach $4trn by the early 2020s. Over 300 Islamic banks operate globally, gaining popularity in non-Muslim majority countries; the UK, Luxembourg, Hong Kong and South Africa have issued sukuks, and the US has 25 Islamic banks. More than half of Islamic banks are investing $5m–$20m in digital banking. The World Finance Islamic Finance Awards honour leading institutions.

An email dated March 19, 2001, from Miyung Buster at Enron to numerous recipients forwards several news articles about California's energy crisis. The articles cover: a San Diego County board's 4-1 vote allowing the former Encina (now Cabrillo) power plant in Carlsbad to emit more nitrogen oxides, with officials warning of increased ozone if the plant must burn fuel oil due to expected natural gas shortages; FERC's identification of $55 million in possible February overcharges by six power suppliers, which must justify prices above $430 per megawatt-hour during Stage 3 alerts or issue refunds, a threshold state leaders criticized as too generous to generators; Energy Secretary Spencer Abraham's call to boost U.S. domestic oil production following OPEC's 4% output cut, while Sen. Schumer suggested possibly tapping the Strategic Petroleum Reserve; groups including automakers, manufacturers, and the Westlands Water District seeking to use the crisis to advance their agendas, though the Air Resources Board unanimously reaffirmed its electric car mandate; the state Department of Water Resources' purchase of power on behalf of near-bankrupt utilities at roughly $350 million per week, with officials acknowledging they are outmatched by professional energy traders; creditors, including Coram Energy Group, moving to force Southern California Edison into involuntary bankruptcy, sending PG&E and Edison stocks sharply lower; PG&E's revision of its "Block 50" rolling blackout exemption lists, removing about 810,000 customers and adding about 690,000; a commentary describing a San Francisco restaurant owner's billing problems caused by a PG&E software error; and an opinion piece arguing that blaming "out-of-state generators" for the crisis could lead to bad policy decisions.

The author returned to school part-time for journalism six years ago, without a clear career goal but staying open to possibilities as the field shifted toward online and digital storytelling. Learning new technology alongside younger peers, they rediscovered a love of being a student that had been lost after severe junior high bullying, and viewed the return as healing that old wound. Despite the challenges of financing school in their 40s, they passed a statistics class, joined the Lambda Pi Eta Honors Society, and participated in campus activities including the paper, magazine, blog, radio station, and events such as a talk by James Foley. After a joyful graduation, they are now beginning a digital storytelling graduate program and serving as a research assistant to professors they admire.

Coach Quenneville addressed various topics regarding the playoff series against Boston. He expressed hope that Toews, dealing with an upper body injury, would be ready for the next game. Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a genetic group of disorders that affect red blood cells, causing the body to produce abnormal hemoglobin. The resulting sickle- or crescent-shaped cells do not last as long as normal cells and can block blood vessels, affecting nearly any area of the body. According to the CDC, people of sub-Saharan African descent are most likely to carry the gene, and the condition affects approximately 100,000 people in the United States. A key symptom is the sickle cell crisis, a sudden episode of severe pain. Other symptoms include anemia, jaundice, acute chest syndrome, infections, and strokes. Acute chest syndrome accounts for the largest number of hospitalizations and deaths, and smoking increases the risk of pain episodes and this syndrome. Diagnosis requires a simple blood test, usually performed at birth through newborn screening; prenatal tests also exist. Management combines medical care—regular screenings, vaccinations, daily antibiotics for children until age 5, pain medication, blood transfusions, and, in severe cases, hematopoietic stem cell transplantation—with lifestyle choices such as quitting smoking, eating a balanced diet, limiting alcohol, resting, and exercising.

The coach credits the players for their will to win, inspired play, preparation, and determination in a game he calls the team's best of the series. He expresses trust in the leadership group's businesslike approach and ability to respond in important games. He praises Sid as the most driven athlete he has known, noting his disciplined habits, care for the organization, and tone-setting power-play goal, and describes Jake as a poised, competitive player with strong hockey sense and quiet confidence.
