AppLovin shares fell sharply after Bloomberg reported the SEC is investigating the mobile advertising company's data-collection practices, responding to a whistleblower complaint and short-seller reports. The agency is examining whether AppLovin violated agreements on targeted ads. The stock rose about 80% this year after surging more than 700% in 2024 on AI-driven ad targeting, and joined the S&P 500 despite short-seller opposition, including Muddy Waters Research's claim that its ad tactics violate app stores' terms of service.

Thousands of "Budget $aver Cherry Pineapple Monster Pops" and "Sugar Free Twin Pops" ice pops are recalled over possible Listeria contamination and distributed in 16 states. Listeria can cause serious or fatal infections.

Research from the University of Exeter suggests that the traditional, "inefficient" fishing methods used in the Fal oyster fishery in Cornwall—including sail-driven boats and hand-hauled dredges—are crucial to preventing overfishing and ensuring the fishery's long-term survival. Motorising the fleet could increase fishing by a conservative estimate of nine-fold. The fishery, one of only three remaining in England, faces its greatest threats from disease and motorised fishing. Using GPS tracking and on-board observers, researchers demonstrated that dredging under sail is less efficient than mechanically powered methods.

A Gallup poll found 44 percent of Americans believe Donald Trump can prevent major scandals, compared with 74 percent for Obama in 2009 and 77 percent for Bush in 2001. Trump inspired less confidence than prior incoming presidents across all categories, with deficits of 15 to 32 percentage points.

The passage discusses building a "Get Rich Portfolio" aimed at generating the highest returns with the lowest risk. Citing Jeremy Siegel's research covering 1801 to 2021, it reports that stocks vastly outperformed other asset classes—a $1 investment in stocks grew to $2,334,920, while bonds reached only $2,163, with bills and gold performing worse—concluding that becoming rich requires investing mostly in stocks, alongside decades of investing and saving. It notes that stock ETFs carry high maximum drawdowns, but draws a distinction between drawdowns and permanent capital loss, advising patience. The authors select liquid, diversified ETFs ranked by Return/MaxDD ratio, assemble a moderately aggressive portfolio with weighted stock categories, and backtest it, presenting equity curves, drawdown data, and performance statistics.

Apple Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended December 30, 2017 reports net sales of $88.3 billion, a 13% increase from $78.4 billion in the prior-year quarter, with growth across all geographic segments. Net income was $20.1 billion ($3.89 diluted earnings per share) compared to $17.9 billion ($3.36). Gross margin was $33.9 billion (38.4%). iPhone net sales rose 13% to $61.6 billion due to a mix of higher-priced iPhones; Services rose 18% to $8.5 billion; iPad rose 6%; Other Products rose 36%; and Mac declined 5%. The company began shipping iPhone X in November 2017 and iMac Pro in December 2017. Total assets were $406.8 billion, and cash generated by operating activities was $28.3 billion. The company repurchased $10.1 billion of common stock, paid $3.3 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents, and issued $7.0 billion of term debt; total term debt outstanding was $111.0 billion, plus $12.0 billion in commercial paper. The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, enacted December 22, 2017, lowered the U.S. federal statutory tax rate from 35% to 21% and imposed a deemed repatriation tax; the company recorded a $7.0 billion tax provision, including a $2.6 billion provisional estimate, with an effective tax rate of 25.8%. FOX 17 News, a Tribune station in the 40th market in West Michigan, seeks a Weather/Multimedia Journalist with at least two years of weather forecasting/reporting experience in a commercial TV newsroom; medium market experience is preferred. Candidates must have strong digital/social media, editing, and shooting skills and be able to deliver forecasts, produce weather graphics, cover breaking news, and create content across all platforms. Applications, including a demo reel link, should be submitted at www.tribunemedia.com. Tribune Media operates 42 local TV stations, WGN America, Tribune Studios, digital properties, WGN-AM, multicast networks, and real estate holdings.

Heikin Ashi is a Japanese candlestick charting technique meaning "average bar," imported to the West in the late 1990s and popularized by Dan Valcu's 2004 article. It smooths price movements using averaged, artificial values to highlight trends and consolidation phases while reducing noise, but it does not show real prices, making direct trading on it impossible. The article explains its calculation, noting that haOpen is an exponential moving average of the previous haClose (three periods), and offers simplified formulas and Amibroker code. The authors backtest a simple Heikin Ashi strategy on the S&P 500—buying when haClose crosses above haOpen and selling on the opposite—finding profitable trend-following results with a 49.4% win ratio and a favorable asymmetric profit/loss distribution. A second strategy using an ADX filter produced a 5.27% CAGR with only 5% exposure on the S&P 500, performing better on consumer staples. The authors conclude Heikin Ashi works mostly on long timeframes and, being a lagging indicator, reflects past rather than future price movements.

After a tough game, the speaker cited missed opportunities, opposing saves, and the opponent's last bounce. Their best play came late, and they called it a painful learning experience that brought the team closer together.

On October 22, 2001, Enron Corp. shares fell about 21% to $20.65, their lowest level since 1998 and down 75% for the year, after the company announced that the Securities and Exchange Commission had requested information regarding certain related-party transactions, including dealings with limited partnerships (LJM Cayman LP and LJM2 Co-Investment LP) organized and formerly run by CFO Andrew Fastow. Enron pledged full cooperation, and Chairman and CEO Kenneth Lay said the company welcomed the request. Enron stated that its internal and external auditors and attorneys had reviewed the arrangements, that the board was fully informed and approved them, and that they were disclosed in SEC filings. Enron had taken a $35 million charge related to the partnerships and repurchased 55 million shares, reducing shareholder equity by $1.2 billion; it also reported a $618 million third-quarter loss after $1.01 billion in charges. A shareholder filed a derivative suit in Texas alleging the board breached fiduciary duties by allowing Fastow to run the partnerships, and the law firm Shapiro Haber & Urmy filed a class action alleging securities fraud on behalf of purchasers of Enron stock from July 13 through October 16, 2001. AG Edwards downgraded the stock to "hold," and a Salomon Smith Barney analyst estimated dismantling Enron's affiliated companies could cost up to $3 billion. Separately, broader stock markets rallied on earnings news, and UniPrime Capital signed a letter of intent for partial interest in a wind park ground lease owned by Enron Wind Development Corp.

Fabinho has reaffirmed his intention to leave Monaco, following the departures of Bernardo Silva, Benjamin Mendy and Tiemoue Bakayoko. The 23-year-old, a reported Manchester United target, said the club knows his wishes, though vice-president Vadim Vasilyev stated Fabinho and Lemar will not be sold.

Trinidad and Tobago won the men's 4x400 metres relay at the World Athletics Championships in London, denying the United States a seventh successive world title. Lalonde Gordon overhauled Fred Kerley on the final straight after the U.S. had led for most of the race. It was Trinidad's first world title in this event and their only gold of the championships. Britain took bronze, while Jamaica, Bahamas and Botswana failed to reach the final. Trinidad's winning time of 2:58.12 was the fastest this year.

Gold rallied strongly on Friday as the USD Index declined, but gold remains below its rising resistance line and mirrors its 2011–2013 price pattern, resembling the November 2012 rally. Silver, platinum, and mining stocks did not move visibly higher; the VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF closed below its April high for a third consecutive day, confirming bearish implications. The author notes gold stocks typically outperform gold early in precious metals rallies, so the opposite occurring suggests the early stage of a larger decline. The USD Index shows an inverse head-and-shoulders pattern, expected to rally to at least 101.3, with the breakout verified by a return to the neck level. Stocks declined below their rising support line after failing to exceed previous highs, signaling potential significant declines. The author likens the setup to 2008, stating the Peak Chaos theory remains intact. A reader comment criticized the technical analysis presented.

FHA loans, a popular government-insured loan type, treat married couples jointly, requiring lenders to pull credit on both spouses even if one is not on the mortgage. The non-borrowing spouse's debts count toward the debt-to-income ratio, potentially reducing borrowing power for purchases or refinances. This requirement applies only to legally married couples, not single or engaged individuals. Married applicants whose spouse has problematic credit may consider switching to conventional loans, which lack this requirement and require only slightly more down payment.

A resurfaced 2013 YouTube video shows actress Allison Mack, arrested for reportedly recruiting women as sex slaves in NXIVM, praising the organization and its affiliated women's group JNess. Mack was charged with sex trafficking and forced labor on April 20, less than a month after NXIVM founder Keith Raniere faced sex trafficking charges. The video also shows her citing Lena Dunham and Miranda July as personal heroes.

The Side Screen is a motion offense built on continuous "On Ball" side screens that pressures defenses with quick hitting options, full-court ball reversal, and constant player movement that hampers boxing out. Entries include a high post rub, dribble clear, or pass and clear, and the action can start on either side. Basic actions feature the wing driving off the screen, the screener rolling, ball reversal with back cuts, and dribble hand-offs. Against defensive adjustments, counters include the post slipping the screen, exploiting outside or post mismatches on switches, and stringing out double teams to create a 2-1-2 alignment with corner and high post cuts.

A 16-year-old girl from Waterloo, Iowa, suffering from severe depression, had been unable to brush her hair for a prolonged period, leaving it matted. Ahead of her school portrait, she visited a salon asking for her hair to be shaved off, but her assigned stylist, 20-year-old student hairdresser Kayley Olson, refused. Instead, Kayley spent 13 hours over two days untangling the hair and restyling it to shoulder length. She described the experience in a Facebook post that was shared over 75,000 times and emphasized that mental health should be taken seriously. The client, kept anonymous, said she would smile for her school pictures and felt like herself again. Facebook users praised Kayley's act and shared similar experiences.

Kieran Trippier described England's penalty shootout win over Colombia as "the best feeling of my career" after the team was held 1-1 over 120 minutes in Moscow. Trippier converted England's fourth penalty between two Colombian misses, and Eric Dier scored the winning kick. England had won only one of their previous seven penalty shootouts, and would have avoided the shootout had Yerry Mina not scored an injury-time equaliser after Harry Kane's penalty. Dele Alli, who has a thigh injury but said he was "all good", praised Jordan Pickford's penalty save from Carlos Bacca, calling him a "phenomenal" and "top-class" keeper.

A three-year study of 195 health facilities in Uganda found that smaller, rural and for-profit facilities struggle to sustain HIV treatment services, while large hospitals attract multiple donor grants. Key barriers include shortages of ART-proficient staff, funder reporting requirements, and irregular ARV supply. For-profit providers' goals often misalign with mass treatment access, and patients bypass smaller facilities for larger hospitals offering more services and shorter waits. Proposed solutions include mentoring between large and small facilities, service purchase agreements, salary support, and increased government funding, as reliance on external donors is unsustainable.

This MIT OpenCourseWare transcript records a lecture on nuclear arms control and nonproliferation, focusing on India and Pakistan. The introductory professor describes South Asia as a potential nuclear flash point, notes the catastrophic human and climate effects of nuclear exchange, and encourages students to pursue research and careers in arms control. The main speaker, MIT political science professor Vipin Narang, presents an overview of proliferation in South Asia. He explains basic deterrence theory—deterrence by punishment versus denial, and the requirements of capability, credibility, and communication—along with nuclear delivery systems and arsenal management choices.

Narang traces India's program from its 1962 defeat by China and the 1974 "peaceful nuclear explosion" (motivated partly by domestic politics) through dormancy, reactivation in response to Pakistan's program, and the 1998 tests. Pakistan's program, triggered by the 1971 war that created Bangladesh, relied on AQ Khan's stolen URENCO centrifuge designs and Chinese assistance while the US overlooked it during the Soviet-Afghan war. After 1998, India adopted an assured retaliation posture with no first use and civilian control, while Pakistan developed a first-use, asymmetric escalation doctrine with battlefield nuclear weapons under military control to offset Indian conventional superiority. Unlike the Cold War, South Asia features two-minute flight times and Pakistan-linked militant groups such as Lashkar-e-Taiba. Narang reviews three crises—the 1999 Kargil War, the 2001–02 Parliament attack mobilization, and the 2008 Bombay attacks—showing how Pakistan's nuclear signaling restrained Indian conventional retaliation and created policy paralysis. He concludes that stability depends on Indian restraint, and another mass-casualty attack could risk nuclear escalation. A question-and-answer session addresses escalation dominance, the AQ Khan proliferation network, US influence over Pakistan, and stalled peace negotiations.

Corn futures are contracts with corn as the underlying asset, representing agreements to receive or deliver a specified quantity of corn at a pre-agreed price on a future date. They trade on the CME Globex platform and are settled through physical delivery. A corn futures strategy involves technical and fundamental analysis, entry/exit signals, position sizing, and risk management. Corn prices are influenced by weather in major growing regions, USDA reports (including WASDE), and demand from China. Corn futures show seasonality, performing better in January, February, April, May, October, November, and December than in summer months. The full contract size is 5,000 bushels; the mini contract is 1,000 bushels. Minimum price fluctuation is $12.50 for the full contract and $1.25 for the mini. According to 62-year MacroTrends data, the all-time high was 831'25 cents in 2012 and the all-time low was 100'7 cents in 1960. As of November 24, 2022, corn traded at 663'2 cents. Major risks include adverse price movements amplified by leverage. The Teucrium Corn Fund (CORN) ETF offers exposure to corn, and CFDs are an alternative to futures. Two seasonal backtested strategies are discussed, one with a 70% maximum drawdown and another averaging 1.13% per trade over 175 trades.

A Supreme Court case scheduled for argument on Oct. 6 addresses whether state statutes limiting medical malpractice litigation apply in federal court. The case involves Delaware's "affidavit of merit" statute, which requires malpractice plaintiffs to either allege obvious negligence—such as leaving a foreign object in a patient—or file an affidavit from a medical professional attesting to negligence. The case stems from Harold Berk's claim against doctor Wilson Choy and Beebe Medical Center over treatment of an ankle and foot injury; because Berk is a Florida resident, federal law allows him to sue in federal court rather than Delaware state court, where his case would have been dismissed for lacking an affidavit. Lower courts dismissed the case, treating the statute as "substantive" under a doctrine derived from a 1938 Supreme Court case. Berk argues federal rules govern pleading requirements, while Choy and Beebe contend the statute does not conflict with federal rules, citing Rule 11's exception for statutes that "specifically state otherwise," and argue the affidavit requirement serves substantive purposes by limiting litigation costs. A filing from civil procedure professors argues implementing such statutes in federal court would be chaotic, since states altered procedural rather than substantive rules.

The passage specifies mechanical and electrical socket requirements. The cover's latch and support tabs secure the actuation lever; actuation force must be less than 3.6 kgf, pin displacement during actuation less than 1.0 mm, and the socket must maintain integrity after 50 actuation cycles. Visual inspection requires intact solder balls, gold-plated contacts, and an undamaged cover, base, tabs, and latch with no gaps. Electrically, contacts are rated 1.5 A with less than 30°C temperature rise; LLCR must not exceed 25 mΩ; partial self-inductance must be under 4 nH; capacitance under 1 pF; differential impedance 100 Ω ±10%; propagation delay skew under 10 ps; dielectric withstanding voltage at least 650 Vac; and insulation resistance at least 1000 MΩ.

AIRSS generates random sensible structures from MINSEP (atom separation) and TARGVOL (target volume) parameters via two-stage optimisation: separating overlapping atoms, then optimising lattice and ionic degrees of freedom.

The speaker praised an opposing player's puck handling and power-play effectiveness, noting the goalie may have been screened on the winning goal. He said his team controlled play at times, particularly late in the second period, but the opponent's power play, which scored multiple goals, was the difference. He expressed surprise at a late-game call, said officiating was stricter than in previous games, and emphasized needing to regroup for Thursday's game and handling matchups well on the road.

The President reports to Congress that South Carolina's opposition to the revenue laws has created an emergency threatening the Union. A convention at Columbia passed an ordinance declaring the tariff acts of 1828 and 1832 null and void within the state, effective February 1, despite the President's December 10 proclamation and efforts by the Administration and Congress to modify the laws. The South Carolina legislature has since passed acts to enforce the ordinance—including provisions for replevin of seized goods, fines and imprisonment for those executing federal revenue laws, mandatory oaths for state officers and jurors, and authorization for the governor to accept volunteers and call out the militia—and the state is openly preparing for military resistance, with a rendezvous opened in Charleston. The President has instructed customs officers, moved the custom-house from Charleston to Castle Pinckney, and transmitted the relevant documents to Congress. He characterizes both nullification and threatened secession as revolutionary, arguing that no single state may annul federal laws or dissolve its obligations under the federal compact, and that South Carolina has bypassed constitutional remedies such as the courts and amendment. He contends that no oppression justifies the state's actions, noting its own documented prosperity. He recommends that Congress authorize the President to alter ports of entry and relocate custom-houses to secure places, protect customs officers and vessels with land and naval forces when necessary, allow removal of state-court suits against federal officers to federal courts, provide for the safekeeping of federal prisoners, and modify the act of 1795 so the President may employ the militia when law enforcement is obstructed by force. He expresses confidence that Congress will cooperate to maintain the supremacy of the laws and preserve the Union.

Claude Julien addressed reporters after a game in which his team tied the score and forced overtime but lost. He said the team did not play its best game, citing poor decision-making, weak puck movement, defensive breakdowns, and being outplayed for the first half, and described the overall performance as average while crediting players for battling back. He noted frustration with calls and non-calls had pulled the team away from its game before they refocused. He praised Patrice Bergeron's two-way reliability, said defenseman Johnny, who scored the tying goal and has six playoff goals, has played well, and stated Jagr's vision and chemistry with linemates have created power-play options. He said it is too late in the playoffs to criticize players, the series is tight, and the team must focus on the next game. He also discussed a player filling Gregory Campbell's faceoff and penalty-killing role.

Plasma microbial cell-free DNA (mcfDNA) sequencing enables unbiased, noninvasive pathogen detection with rapid turnaround for infectious disease diagnosis. The Karius Test, an analytically and clinically validated commercial mcfDNA sequencing test, identifies and quantifies mcfDNA from more than 1,500 bacteria, DNA viruses, fungi, and parasites. This study reviewed results from 19,739 samples from 16,172 hospital patients across 39 states and the District of Columbia collected from April 2018 through September 2021. The median time from sample receipt to result was 26 hours, and 96% of samples yielded valid results; most ordering clinicians were infectious disease (64%) and hematology/oncology (14%) providers. Of valid results, 42% were negative, while 58% identified at least one microbe, comprising 701 unique taxa (526 bacteria, 103 fungi, 47 viruses, 24 parasites) and 22,792 total detections. The top 50 taxa—36 bacteria, 9 viruses, and 5 fungi—accounted for 69% of detections. Detections included diagnostically challenging organisms such as Legionella (80), Nocardia (76), Mycobacterium (156), zoonotic and vector-borne bacteria (247, with Bartonella henselae predominating), fungi including Candida, Aspergillus, Mucorales, and systemic dimorphic fungi, and eukaryotic parasites. Performance metrics were not significantly different from those of the initial validation study, demonstrating the test is robust and can be performed at scale in a clinically relevant timeframe. The 58% positivity rate was lower than the 70–85% reported for well-defined clinical uses, supporting the need for diagnostic stewardship. Limitations included lack of orthogonal testing data and clinical context available for only 29% of patients. The authors conclude that plasma mcfDNA sequencing may enhance diagnosis of challenging infections and public health surveillance, but requires careful clinical application, expert interpretation, and outcomes studies to optimize its utility.

A pilot study trained a convolutional neural network (CNN) to classify thyroid nodules as benign or malignant from ultrasound images. The study used the Thyroid Digital Image Database (TDID), a public dataset published in 2015 by the Universidad Nacional de Colombia, in which images were labeled via the Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (TI-RADS), with TR2 and TR3 classified as benign and TR4 and TR5 as malignant. Because the dataset was small and skewed toward malignant cases (roughly four times more), image augmentation, early stopping, and class weights favoring benign images were applied. The model combined two pre-trained architectures, VGG16 and InceptionV3, implemented in Python with TensorFlow, and used binary cross-entropy with a sigmoid activation. Training ran for 10 epochs with a batch size of 8 on a desktop computer. The hybrid model achieved 87.5% accuracy and an AUROC of 0.929. The authors concluded that a CNN can accurately determine malignant or benign thyroid nodules from ultrasounds in place of, or to support, a radiologist, and noted that a larger dataset would further refine the model.

NVIDIA Corporation filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended April 28, 2019 (Q1 fiscal year 2020). Revenue was $2,220 million, down 31% year-over-year and up 1% sequentially, with net income of $394 million ($0.64 diluted per share), down 68% from the prior year. Gross margin was 58.4%, down 610 basis points year-over-year, and operating expenses rose 21% to $938 million. GPU segment revenue declined 27% to $2,022 million, and Tegra Processor revenue declined 55% to $198 million, reflecting declines in gaming and data center revenue and the absence of $289 million in cryptocurrency mining processor sales. Revenue outside the United States was 93% of total. On March 10, 2019, NVIDIA entered a merger agreement to acquire Mellanox Technologies for $125 per share in cash, an enterprise value of approximately $6.9 billion, subject to approvals, with a potential $350 million termination fee. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $7.80 billion. NVIDIA adopted the new lease accounting standard on January 28, 2019, recognizing $470 million of operating lease assets and $500 million of lease liabilities. The company paid $97 million in dividends, made no share repurchases, and retained authorization for up to $7.24 billion in repurchases through December 2022. Consolidated securities class action and derivative lawsuits concerning channel inventory and cryptocurrency-related statements are pending; patent litigation with Polaris and ZiiLabs was settled with immaterial financial impact. Total assets were $14,021 million and total shareholders' equity $9,704 million as of April 28, 2019.

Rahul Gandhi, great-grandson of India's founding prime minister Jawaharlal Nehru, was elected unopposed as president of the opposition Congress party, succeeding his mother Sonia, party president since 1998. The move aims to challenge Prime Minister Narendra Modi ahead of 2019 national elections. Gandhi has struggled to convince voters of his leadership since Congress's heavy 2014 defeat, while Modi remains popular, with a Pew survey showing his favourable rating 30 points higher.

The Hiscox DNA of Entrepreneur report (Q4 2016) surveyed over 4,000 small and medium-sized businesses (up to 50 employees) across the US, UK, France, Spain, Germany, and the Netherlands. Key motivators for US entrepreneurs were flexible working hours (68 percent), greater control (61 percent), and working remotely (57 percent), while only 37 percent cited making more money; 22 percent take no vacation. Seventy percent reported revenue growth, 68 percent profit growth, and 73 percent gained new customers, led by financial services, hospitality, and technology/media/telecom sectors. US businesses showed the highest optimism among surveyed countries, with 23 percent planning to increase headcount. Sixty-one percent lack a succession plan. Funding remains challenging: 17 percent found bank funding harder to obtain, leading many to use personal credit cards, venture capital, or peer-to-peer lending; Oregon's Business Oregon offers loan programs including OBDF, CAP, CEF, IDB, and EDLF. Only 34 percent believe government policies support entrepreneurs, and 31 percent say political instability negatively impacts their business. Forbes ranked Bend, Oregon No. 1 among small places for business, with 6.6 percent job growth. Overall, US entrepreneurship reflects cautious optimism, with Oregon's economy approaching full employment and growth expected through 2017.

The passage examines the commonly held belief that interest rates and stocks have an inverse relationship. Rate changes take at least 12 months to broadly affect the economy, but the stock market reacts more quickly and anticipates future changes. Backtests using the S&P 500 (not dividend-adjusted) showed that a simple strategy trading on whether the SMA is above or below the 10-year yield produced poor returns when buying during rising rates. The inverse strategy—investing when rates are falling—dramatically improved CAGR with similar drawdowns, though it performed better before the 1990s than during the quantitative easing era of the 2000s and 2010s. Since the 2000s, the correlation has become more positive, but holding stocks during falling rates remains far more profitable than buying when rates rise.

The LTE-enabled Apple Watch Series 3, launched in September 2017, has expanded slowly to limited markets, facing carrier reluctance and a ban in China. Pre-orders open May 4 in Denmark, Sweden, and India via Three, Reliance Jio, and Airtel; pricing remains unannounced.

President Obama announced he will deliver a farewell address on Jan. 10 in Chicago to reflect on his time in office and thank supporters, citing George Washington's 1796 precedent. Trump, taking office Jan. 20, pledged to undo Obama's policies including his health-care law. Obama has sought a smooth transition despite policy differences and leaves his party without a clear figurehead.

IFC Films promoted Mark Boxer to executive vice president of sales and distribution and Lauren Schwartz to senior vice president of publicity and promotions. Both longtime executives have contributed to the company's releases, including "Boyhood," "45 Years," and "Finding Vivian Maier."

The MMA Manifesto's middleweight rankings, updated Mondays and Fridays by a voting panel of Jeff Fox, Ryan MacDonald, Ricky Leone, and Daniel Vreeland, exclude suspended fighters or those inactive for 12+ months without upcoming fights. UFC Middleweight Champion Michael Bisping ranks first with 39 of 40 points (record 30-7), followed by Luke Rockhold and Yoel Romero. Chris Weidman and Ronaldo 'Jacare' Souza are tied at fourth, with Gegard Mousasi, Robert Whittaker, Anderson Silva, and Vitor Belfort occupying positions six through nine. Kelvin Gastelum debuts at tenth and faces Belfort at UFC Fight Night on March 11th. Derek Brunson dropped off the rankings, while Brunson, David Branch, Mamed Khalidov, and Krzysztof Jotko are listed as bubbling under.

Marquez Charter Elementary has opened a temporary campus nearly nine months after the January Palisades fire, which spared only three classrooms at the site. Its roughly 130 students are the first public school students to return to a campus destroyed by the Palisades and Eaton fires. The temporary campus houses 19 classrooms, a kitchen, a library, and play areas; the temporary campus and full rebuild will cost the district about $202.6 million, with completion slated for 2028, while rebuilding all three damaged campuses is estimated near $600 million. Enrollment has declined roughly 58%, from about 310 to 130, and LAUSD estimates three-quarters of enrolled students no longer live in the Palisades. The reopening followed a parent survey; Palisades Charter Elementary families opted to wait for permanent buildings. The Eaton fire affected five Pasadena Unified schools and three of its charters, which have installed portables but have no rebuild timeline.

This study conducted a bibliometric analysis of open education research using co-citation and co-word analyses on 402 articles retrieved from the Web of Science database in September 2023. The co-citation analysis identified five clusters: evolving open education, OER's role in education, adoption of open education, educational paradigms of MOOCs, and implementation of OEP. The co-word analysis identified five future-oriented clusters: blended learning, openness in the COVID-19 era, challenges of OER adoption, inclusive digital pedagogy, and collaborative online academia. Results showed publications grew steadily after 2015, peaking in 2020 with 82 publications. The findings indicate open education is a dynamic, evolving field, with OER offering cost savings, accessibility, and personalized learning benefits. However, faculty resistance and insufficient institutional support remain barriers to adoption. Limitations include reliance on a single database, subjective cluster interpretation, and threshold value selection. Future research should combine bibliometric methods with qualitative approaches and examine regional and institutional variations.

The OHL trading strategy is an intraday stock trading strategy that uses the configuration of open, high, and low price levels in the first few minutes of a session to determine trade entries. A buy signal occurs when the open price equals the day's low, suggesting bullish sentiment, while a sell signal occurs when the open equals the day's high, suggesting bearish sentiment. Some traders combine it with CPR levels calculated from the previous day's high, low, and close, going long only above CPR levels and short only below them. The strategy is best used on lower timeframes, such as 1- or 5-minute charts. Backtests on S&P 500 and ES futures produced 1,401 trades with an average gain of 0.04% per trade, improving to 0.06% when the open was above the previous close. WTI crude oil showed a 0.12% average gain under certain rules, while flipped rules yielded 0.00% for both SPY and WTI. The backtests indicate the direction of the first minutes of the trading day sets the tone for the rest of the day.

This paper introduces a neural solver combining physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) with isogeometric analysis (IGA) to enable the application of PINNs to complex, multi-patch computer-aided design (CAD) geometries. While PINNs offer a mesh-free alternative to traditional numerical methods for solving partial differential equations, they face three main challenges on such domains: enforcing solution continuity across patch interfaces, strongly imposing Dirichlet boundary conditions, and handling geometry parts with significant variations in size and shape. The proposed solver, rooted in the finite element tearing and interconnecting method and mortaring methods, develops NN-based ansatz functions that operate on the IGA reference domain, with solutions mapped to the physical domain via the NURBS-based pushforward map. A modified output layer strongly imposes Dirichlet boundary conditions, while separate interface ansatz functions connect neighboring patches and ensure solution conformity. Training uses the variational PINN framework, minimizing the discretized energy functional derived from the weak PDE form. Operating on the reference domain also normalizes NN inputs naturally. Unlike most prior works, which address only single-patch geometries, this method handles multi-patch domains. The approach is demonstrated on two real-world applications: a 2D magnetostatics model of a quadrupole magnet and a 3D nonlinear solid mechanics model of a mechanical holder using a hyperelastic material with contact boundary conditions.

Owen Sound Foodland is one of 87 new stores selected through an LCBO bidding process to sell beer and cider beginning in April, bringing Ontario's total to 370 authorized stores. Located in Georgian Bluffs, it is the first grocery store in the immediate Owen Sound area to sell these products. Its new 34,000-square-foot location, tentatively opening March 22, will expand offerings and staffing to about 160 employees.

This passage introduces ADAPT (Accelerated Deep Atomic Potential Transformer), a coordinate-based Transformer for predicting atomic forces and energies in defect computations. Machine learning force fields (MLFFs) offer computationally efficient alternatives to costly first-principles methods like Density Functional Theory (DFT), with state-of-the-art MLFFs typically using graph neural networks (GNNs). However, GNNs face challenges with point defects, including oversmoothing, the computational demands of large supercells, potentially prohibitive data requirements, and an inherent focus on local interactions, whereas defects depend on non-local interactions. ADAPT instead computes attention over all possible atom interactions, trained on a DFT database of defects in silicon, primarily complex defects. Each atom is represented as a token containing a 12-dimensional vector of coordinates and atomic properties (e.g., electronegativity, covalent radius, valence electrons), embedded into a higher-dimensional space via an MLP. ADAPT employs distinct networks for forces and energies, avoiding graphs and inductive biases. It achieves state-of-the-art performance in energy and forces, outperforming MACE, MatterSim, and MACE retrained on the same dataset, with a training cost two orders of magnitude lower than message-passing architectures.

Nearly 88 per cent of Ireland's publicly-quoted companies met or beat market earnings expectations despite post-Brexit referendum fears, according to a Merrion Capital review of 33 companies, with average earnings per share growth of 8 per cent. Aryzta, Ryanair, Tullow Oil and IFG Group missed expectations. The Iseq reached a 15-month high but underperformed other European markets due to Brexit concerns. Irish Continental Group is the top performer this year, while Aryzta fared worst, with shares down 27.2 per cent.

This study examined the experiences, opinions, criticisms, and suggestions of parents in Turkey regarding the compulsory distance education implemented during the COVID-19 pandemic, using a descriptive survey model. Data were collected through a 16-question questionnaire from 2,371 parents selected via quota sampling based on Turkey's NUTS first-level regions, and analyzed with SPSS 24 and NVIVO 10.

Of the participants, 57.7% expressed positive views of distance education, citing continuity of education, health protection, and independence of time and place, while 42.3% viewed it as inefficient, difficult, and inadequate. Most parents (86.4%) did not arrange private lessons for their children during the process. WhatsApp (91.1%) was the most used channel for parent-teacher communication. The highest agreement (90%) was that internet connection fees should not be charged for EBA use; 74.9% found it difficult for students to adapt, 73.4% stated exams could not measure actual success, and 86.5% disagreed that distance education should completely replace face-to-face education. Criticisms focused on inadequacy (41%), difficulty (17.8%), temporal problems (17.4%), dissimilarity to face-to-face education (15.2%), and technical problems (8.6%). Positive opinions concerned process management (47.4%), opportunity for repetition (42.2%), and health (10.4%). Suggestions included testing (30.5%), continuation of distance education as support (26.7%), content and material support (23.3%), and increased lesson time (19.5%).

The study concluded that parents considered distance education positive but not a replacement for face-to-face education, that inequality of opportunity and the digital divide deepened during the pandemic, and that EBA content was inadequate. Recommendations included solving technological infrastructure problems, providing free or affordable internet access, strengthening the openness philosophy and content, and developing digital literacy policies.

The Detroit Tigers, who used a closer by committee this season, need a true closer. Writer TJ Morin suggests two-time All-Star closer Suarez, expected to opt out this offseason, would be an ideal fit. Suarez posted a 2.97 ERA, 75 strikeouts, a 0.904 WHIP, and 40 saves over 70 appearances. Pairing him with Tarik Skubal could secure wins, and the Tigers should pursue him in free agency.

This is the November 2, 2000 weekly job announcement email for Haas School of Business alumni, listing 17 job openings at various companies. Positions include multiple marketing and management roles at Plumtree Software (San Francisco), program management openings at Sanrise, Inc. (Dublin, CA), a Vice President of Marketing in Chicago, a Product Manager at ViroLogic, a Finance Editor at CJOL.COM in Shenzhen, China, a Controller at Atomz.com, a Business Analyst at Kaiser Permanente, Director of Business Development at Copper Mountain Networks, various technical roles at Loudcloud, Controller/Operations Manager at Terrace Consulting, Product Manager roles at Rhapsody Networks, Senior BPI Analyst and Consultant positions at Pacific Gas and Electric, Financial Analysts at McKinsey & Company, a Marketing Director at Amerix, finance and e-commerce positions at The Nature Conservancy and PBS, business development and marketing roles at Zhanra Infostructure, and a Research Associate at Morgan Stanley Dean Witter. Expanded job descriptions with qualifications, contact information, and application instructions are provided for most positions.

The email also announces the UC Berkeley Business Plan Competition launching November 8, a Big Game BBQ on November 18, and a Women in Leadership Conference on November 11. It includes instructions for submitting job openings, contacting the Haas Alumni Career Advisor, and subscribing or unsubscribing from the list, and notes that companies and search firms listed have not been researched by the Haas School.

The Mongolian and Tibetan Affairs Commission is to be merged with the Ministry of Culture and the Mainland Affairs Council by the end of this year, ending nearly a century of operations. Six of its 49 employees will transfer to the council, with remaining staff handling Mongolian and Tibetan affairs under the ministry. Founded in 1928, the commission has faced abolition calls since Taiwan's democratization. The Executive Yuan will propose scrapping its authorizing act in the next legislative session. Legislators offered mixed reactions, with some opposing the merger plan and others urging faster abolition.

The team knows the difference between winning and losing and takes pride in playing tough within the system, with everyone contributing and feeling responsible to each other. Despite growth and a missed scoring chance, they narrowly lost.

Renewable energy output fluctuates due to natural resource variability, requiring backup power plants and prompting operators to sometimes pay consumers to use excess electricity to prevent grid collapse. Prof. Mahesh Bandi of the Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology used turbulence theory and experimental wind plant data to explain the statistical nature of wind power fluctuations. While wind power spectra were previously assumed to match wind speed spectra because power equals wind speed cubed, Bandi showed the match arises from differing measurement types: wind speed is measured across distributed points in space at the same time, while power is measured at a fixed location over time. Turbines within the same time-scale eddies fluctuate as a unit, and geographically dispersed plants only partially decouple. Geographic smoothing averages fluctuations at high frequencies but not low frequencies, imposing a natural limit confirmed using data from 20 Texas plants and 224 Irish wind farms. These findings enable better estimates of required energy reserves and inform environmental policy decisions.

Marouane Fellaini has turned down a new Manchester United contract, with manager Jose Mourinho urging him to sign quickly. Substituted during the Tottenham defeat, Fellaini faces a knee injury that could sideline him for up to two months, ruling him out against Huddersfield and possibly the Champions League ties with Sevilla. He has missed 20 games through injury this season.

Merger arbitrage is a market-neutral trading strategy that exploits the spread between a target company's stock price and the acquisition offer price after a merger announcement. Success requires assessing deal completion likelihood, regulatory risks, deal terms, and stock liquidity. Backtests showed modest returns with low volatility: the IQ Merger Arbitrage ETF achieved a 2.73% CAGR versus 18.52% for the S&P 500 (volatility 7.83 vs. 17.27), and The Merger Fund achieved 4.46% versus 17.37% (volatility 3.81 vs. 17.29). A Verdad Research study of 835 deals from 2000–2020 found an 89% deal closure rate, with successful deals averaging 2.0% returns and canceled deals losing 2.8%, for a blended average return of 1.5%. The strategy offers uncorrelated returns but requires deep understanding of each deal.

On January 26, 2022, Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC announcing the release of its financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended December 31, 2021. The results, titled the "Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2021 Update," were posted on Tesla's website and attached as Exhibit 99.1, furnished under Item 2.02. The report was signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn.

Oxygen-containing rare-earth hydrides (REHO) exhibit a color-neutral photochromic effect under ambient conditions, losing nearly 50% transmittance without a pronounced absorption band, making them promising for smart windows. Their phase composition remains incompletely understood; although a single-phase oxyhydride model was proposed, films have been shown to consist of O-rich and H-rich regions, with hydrogen migration suggested as the photochromic mechanism. EELS measurements of photochromic and opaque YHO films showed a 1.5 eV difference in plasmon peak positions, indicating a higher concentration of free or mobile hydrogen in photochromic films. Photodarkening kinetics could not be described by zero-, first-, or second-order reaction models, but a two-phase exponential decay function provided a drastically improved fit. This revealed a fast decay (k1=0.016 s−1) within the first 2–3 minutes of illumination and a slow decay (k2=0.001 s−1) thereafter. The fast process is probably associated with local structural changes, while the slow decay is attributed to hydrogen migration/diffusion within the film and associated lattice contraction. The model describes the data well and enables straightforward comparison of photochromic film performance for developing and optimizing devices for energy-efficient applications.

Chicago wheat prices rose on Tuesday, recovering from their biggest three-day decline since 2013, after a winter storm brought beneficial rain and snow to drought-affected U.S. winter wheat in the southern Plains. The most-active wheat contract rose 0.9 percent to $4.54-3/4 a bushel, having fallen 7.8 percent over three sessions. Corn edged up 0.1 percent to $3.75-1/2 a bushel, ending a four-session losing streak, while soybeans gained 0.2 percent to $10.25 after Monday's losses. The USDA rated 11 percent of Kansas winter wheat in good-to-excellent condition, down from 12 percent a week earlier.

Congress failed to avert a government shutdown, with federal operations ceasing at midnight Wednesday after temporary funding expired. Most schools face minimal short-term disruption: Title I and special education funds will be available as expected, and the Agriculture Department can reimburse school meals for September and October. SNAP benefits should continue if the shutdown lasts no more than a week. However, districts relying on impact aid—nearly 1,100 districts serving about eight million students—could face cash flow problems, and a prolonged shutdown could affect Head Start and WIC nutrition assistance.

Lawmakers could not reach a deal; Democrats seek Medicaid offsets and Affordable Care Act premium tax cut extensions. The Trump administration, which blames Democrats, may use the shutdown to downsize government: the Office of Management and Budget has directed agencies to consider mass layoffs, prompting a federal employee union lawsuit. At the Education Department, civil rights investigations, regulations, and guidance work will be halted, and schools planning to open with recently awarded $500 million in Charter School Program funds may face delays. The last shutdown, in 2018-19, lasted 35 days.

U.S. billionaire investor Paul Kazarian, owner of Japonica Partners and one of Greece's largest bondholders since 2013, has opened his first European office in Lisbon, saying Portugal's corporate sector is ripe for investment. He credits the Socialist governments of Greece and Portugal with strong recovery policies after the euro zone debt crisis. Japonica is exploring investments in Portuguese real estate and technology, and aims to help local companies become globally competitive. The Lisbon office will also examine opportunities across Europe.

William Asa Hutchinson III, son of Arkansas Gov. Asa Hutchinson, was arrested on DWI, speeding and implied consent charges and released on $1,626 bond. He faces court Wednesday. A prior DWI conviction was dismissed, and he received pretrial diversion in a 2016 MDMA possession case.

This study examines degradation in commercial NMC/graphite lithium-ion coin cells (3032, 200 mAh) cycled at 1C, 2C, and 3C rates between 2.7 and 4.3 V at room temperature. Over 278 cycles, capacity declined to approximately 42 mAh, with 3C cycling causing ~60.19% capacity loss and internal resistance rising to 0.34 Ω. Coulombic efficiency remained stable (99.88% at 1C, slightly lower at higher rates). XRD revealed c-lattice parameter contraction in the cycled NMC cathode and expansion in the graphite anode. SEM and EDS showed surface decomposition products, micro-cavities, cracking, and density changes in both electrodes. Li-NRA depth profiling quantified lithium redistribution: the cathode lost 1.86 × 10²² atoms/cm³ while the anode gained 1.38 × 10²² atoms/cm³, with the degraded anode showing a 115.96% lithium increase attributed to plating and trapping. The findings identify lithium plating and loss of cyclable lithium as primary aging mechanisms and demonstrate non-destructive Li-NRA as an effective technique for lithium depth profiling in battery degradation studies.

The T-bills market traded slightly bullish, with demand skewed to shorter maturities amid buoyant liquidity from N300bn bond maturity inflows. The CBN's N49.60bn PMA was moderately over-subscribed at N103.40bn, while OBB and OVN rates fell to 1.75% and 2.50%. The I&E FX window rate depreciated to N362.02/$, and sovereign bonds lost ground, with the 2047s down c.1.30pt to 99.70.

The Panthers signed Kawann Short to a five-year, $80 million contract extension, ending a year-long negotiation and eliminating the franchise tag. The deal reflects general manager Dave Gettleman's win-now philosophy, echoed by his comments that the goal is to win every year. The extension strengthens Carolina's defensive line, where Short has recorded 17 sacks over the past two seasons. Other off-season moves include a one-year contract with Julius Peppers, the addition of safety Mike Adams, and the return of cornerback Captain Munnerlyn, making the projected base defense average 29.45 years old. Offensively, questions remain around quarterback Cam Newton, who had shoulder surgery and has a recent injury history, prompting plans for the offense to evolve. The Panthers replaced receivers Ted Ginn Jr. and Philly Brown, signed tackle Matt Kalil to a deal worth up to $55 million, and hope Michael Oher returns to form at right tackle. The team's final major off-season move is expected to be drafting an offensive playmaker with the No. 8 pick, with Leonard Fournette, Christian McCaffrey, and O.J. Howard as top candidates.

The annual Battle of Alberta chess tournament will be held at the University of Calgary from Feb. 18–19, hosted by the U of C Chess Club. Between 30 and 40 players will compete under World Chess Federation rules. Registration is $10 for students and $15 for non-students.

This patent application, a continuation of U.S. application Ser. No. 17/809,484, describes methods and systems utilizing a cache coherent switch on chip communicatively coupled to components such as accelerators, processors, memories, storage, and network interface cards via the Compute Express Link (CXL) protocol. The switch provides cache coherency between components, low-latency memory access paths, and sharing of cached and transient data without CPU involvement, preventing the processor from becoming a bottleneck in component-to-component traffic. It supports multi-host access, resource pooling and disaggregation, composable virtual servers, and memory expansion using memories such as DDR4/DDR5, DRAM, persistent memory, and NVMe. The switch includes upstream and downstream ports supporting PCI and/or CXL protocols, switched fabric circuitry, a processing core, virtual hierarchies, and bridges (including SR2MR and SLD2MLD) for legacy device support. A fabric manager allocates and deallocates resources, manages hot-plug insertion and device inventory, and connects to higher-level management software. Multiple switches may be coupled via expansion ports, fabric switches, or networks, including Ethernet, to pool memories, accelerators, and other resources across servers, racks, and data centers. The switch may include AI/ML-based memory prefetchers, a compression and security module, and an erasure code accelerator that provides data redundancy and offloads erasure coding from processors. Cache coherent traffic may be bridged over Ethernet by tunneling CXL commands in Ethernet frames, with defined packet and frame formats including CXL 3.0 flits, modified L2 layers with configurable interframe gaps, and CXL-over-MPLS formats. The disclosure further covers computational storage services, chiplet coupling, resource clusters across networked server racks, and embodiments implemented in hardware, software, firmware, and computer-readable media.

Sugar is a sweet-tasting carbohydrate extracted from sugarcane and sugar beet, used to sweeten food. Sugar futures are tradable, legally binding derivative contracts to receive or deliver a specified quantity of sugar at a pre-agreed price on a future date, traded on both ICE and CME. On ICE, Sugar No. 11 futures (symbol SB) are settled by physical delivery, while CME Globex contracts (YO) are financially settled; most brokers close retail positions before expiry to avoid delivery. Each contract covers 112,000 pounds, with a minimum price fluctuation of 0.0001 per pound and a tick size of $11.20, in a March, May, July, and October cycle. A sugar futures strategy combines technical and fundamental analysis with position sizing and risk management, and can be used for speculation, portfolio diversification, or hedging. The authors consider sugar particularly hard to trade and do not trade it themselves. They backtested an ATR channel breakout strategy based on the turtle trading systems; it showed a low win ratio with many small winners offset by a few big winners. Sugar futures historically perform better in February, June, July, November, and December. Key price drivers include government subsidies and tariffs in top producing and consuming nations, ethanol demand (linked to oil prices), Brazil's currency, weather, and sugar inventories and crops. As of December 14, 2022, sugar traded at 19.69 US cents per pound on ICE; its all-time high was 66.00 cents (November 1974) and all-time low 2.63 cents (June 1985). The biggest risk is adverse price movement amplified by leverage. Sugar can also be traded via CFDs or ETFs, and its price is partly controlled, as some exporters may occasionally limit exports.

The Education Department announced it will rewrite two Obama-era rules—Borrower Defense to Repayment and Gainful Employment—governing student loan forgiveness in cases of fraud and misconduct by universities. Betsy DeVos called the rules overly burdensome and confusing, noting colleges complained the definition of misrepresentation was too broad and lacked due process. Hearings are set for July, and nearly 16,000 pending claims will be fulfilled. Eight states and D.C. filed a motion to retain the rules; consumer advocates criticized the revision, while the for-profit college industry supported it. The rules followed crackdowns on for-profit colleges like Corinthian Colleges and ITT Technical Institute.

Prime Day offers at least $200 off all current MacBooks on Amazon. The 13-inch M4 MacBook Air at $800 (16 GB RAM, 256 GB storage) is called the best deal and the laptop most people should buy. Buyers needn't worry about rumored M5 MacBook Air upgrades, since Airs aren't performance-driven and improvements may not be worth $200 more. The M1 MacBook Air, still sold at $600, remains a solid budget option, though a new entry-level MacBook—reportedly using an iPhone chip and possibly a 12.9-inch display—may eventually replace it. MacBook Pro discounts are smaller (10-13%), and rumored M5 MacBook Pros, in production with unclear timing, make waiting potentially worthwhile, though M4 models remain excellent. A thinner, possibly touchscreen redesign is expected for the M6 generation.

The Supreme Court appeared likely to side with police in William Case's challenge to a 2021 incident in which Montana officers, responding to reports that he had threatened suicide and to harm police, entered his home without a warrant and shot him. The case asks how certain officers must be of an emergency before making a warrantless home entry. Case argued for a probable cause requirement, but justices across the bench questioned applying that criminal-context standard to emergency situations. Several justices favored an "objectively reasonable basis" standard for believing someone needs emergency help, while debating whether to apply it directly to the case's facts or send it back to the Montana Supreme Court. A decision is expected by the end of June or early July.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2019 reports total revenue of $33.1 billion, up 14% from $29.1 billion a year earlier, with operating income of $12.7 billion (up 27%) and net income of $10.7 billion (up 21%). Diluted earnings per share were $1.38 versus $1.14. Segment revenue was: Productivity and Business Processes $11.1 billion, Intelligent Cloud $10.8 billion, and More Personal Computing $11.1 billion. Commercial cloud revenue increased 36% to $11.6 billion, and Azure revenue grew 59%. The effective tax rate was 16%, compared with 14% in the prior-year quarter. Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $136.6 billion; total assets were $279.0 billion and stockholders' equity was $106.1 billion. Long-term debt stood at $66.5 billion. During the quarter, the company repurchased 29 million shares for $4.0 billion under its 2016 $40 billion repurchase program, which had $7.4 billion remaining, and a new $40 billion program was approved in September 2019. Unrecognized tax benefits were $15.7 billion, and Microsoft remains under IRS audit for tax years 2004 to 2013. Accrued legal liabilities were $346 million. Shares outstanding were 7,628,805,618 as of October 18, 2019.

A presidential proclamation by Thomas Jefferson, dated November 27, 1806, warns that persons within the United States are conspiring to mount a military expedition against Spain's dominions, fitting out armed vessels in the western waters and recruiting citizens under false pretenses. It commands all participants to cease immediately, directs civil and military officers to apprehend offenders and seize vessels, arms, and military stores, and calls on citizens to assist in preventing the enterprise and reporting offenders to authorities.

Kano Pillars drew 1-1 with Niger Tornadoes in a rescheduled week 12 Nigeria Professional Football League match in Kano. Andrew Ikefe scored for Tornadoes in the 19th minute; Junior Lokosa equalized with an 81st-minute penalty, raising his season tally to 11 goals.

A market structure trading strategy involves analyzing price movements through swing highs and lows, support and resistance levels, and trendlines. The three primary market structures are trending, ranging, and consolidating markets, each suited to different trading approaches. Key analytical components include candlestick patterns (such as doji and engulfing patterns), volume analysis, and Fibonacci retracements (38.2%, 50%, 61.8%) to identify potential reversal or continuation points. Entry strategies include breakout trading, which capitalizes on price breaking support or resistance levels, and pullback trading, which enters during retracements within established trends. Risk management involves stop-loss orders and adjusting position sizes based on the strength of the identified market structure. Additional techniques include multiple time frame analysis and harmonic patterns such as Gartley and Butterfly. The article emphasizes backtesting to validate or falsify trading methods.

The President transmits to Congress dispatches from Mr. Wise, minister to Brazil, revealing schemes used to evade American laws against the slave trade. American vessels are nominally chartered but effectively sold to slave dealers in Brazil, aided by English brokers and capitalists. These vessels clear from the United States to British ports, load "coast goods," and are delivered on the African coast, where merchandise is exchanged for slaves and the vessels' names and papers destroyed. Legal penalties fall mainly on crews, who may be ignorant of the venture, while the organizers escape punishment. Both British subjects and American citizens are implicated. The President argues that Britain's policy of transferring captured Africans to West Indies apprenticeships, with bounties paid to capturing crews, perpetuates rather than suppresses the trade, and hopes Britain will adopt more efficient measures consonant with restoring captured Africans to their homes.

DS, PSA Peugeot-Citroen's premium brand, is launching the PureTech 225 petrol engine for its DS7 Crossback SUV in the UK. The 225hp engine reduces fuel consumption by 6% and pairs with the EAT8 eight-speed gearbox. At launch, the SUV offers four Euro 6.2-compliant engines, including two diesels. The PureTech 225 starts at £34,990 on Ultra Prestige, Prestige, and PERFORMANCE Line models.

A majority of Hawaii's aborigines, Creoles, and naturalized foreigners favor annexation to the United States, which may be pursued if the childless sovereign dies, though only with US government sanction. Hawaiians, educated by American missionaries for fifty years, hold Puritan and democratic ideas, and the Fifteenth Amendment has increased annexation's popularity. The native population, now about 45,000, is declining, while 5,000–6,000 foreigners, two-thirds American, own most foreign capital and hold key government offices. Strategic and commercial reasons favor US acquisition: the islands' central position in the North Pacific, their value as a naval depot and coaling station, protection of growing Pacific commerce, tropical products, and the risk of seizure by a hostile European power. The king, 41 years old and obese at 300 pounds with breathing difficulties, is the sole surviving Kamehameha, unmarried and heirless, and reportedly will not name a successor.

This address to Congress describes a nation enjoying prosperity, domestic tranquility, and foreign peace, attributed to the character of the American people and the cooperation of the Federal Government. Constructive economy has replaced wastefulness through four revisions of the internal revenue system, payment of one-third of the national debt (reduced by about $906 million last year), and a national income increased nearly 50 percent to over $90 billion. With a surplus margin of only $37 million, the Treasury cannot undertake expenditure increases, and new appropriations require new revenue to avoid an unbalanced budget.

In foreign affairs, the Sixth International Conference of American States met at Habana; 11 new arbitration treaties were signed, with 22 more under negotiation. Marines were sent to Nicaragua at its government's request, and an agreement secured by Col. Stimson led to a successful national election. Relations with Mexico have improved, Chile and Peru have resumed diplomatic relations, and China's Nationalist Government has been recognized with a tariff-autonomy treaty. Settlement of the Greek and Austrian debts is recommended. A treaty signed at Paris by 15 nations, with 44 more intending to adhere, renounces war as national policy. The Navy requires cruiser replacements, but no increase in Army or Navy personnel is sought; defense spending is at its limit.

Veterans' relief expenditures approximate $765 million annually. Agriculture has improved but faces a surplus problem; creation of a Federal farm board with a revolving loan fund is proposed, while government entry into business, subsidies, and price fixing should be avoided. International trade reaches about $9 billion annually. River and harbor appropriations exceed $91 million, and a Colorado River dam at the Black Canyon site is recommended, with electrical development left to private enterprise. Wages have risen 12.9 percent since 1922, Federal civil service salaries over 63 percent in seven years, and Prohibition under the eighteenth amendment is binding, requiring state cooperation in enforcement. The address concludes that peace and prosperity require unremitting effort, governmental actions commanding public confidence, and generosity toward other nations.

A mom is warning parents to keep sick children home after her 3-year-old daughter Chloe, who has asthma, was hospitalized with RSV following a Christmas dinner where she played with a cousin who had a lung infection. Chloe, who is fully vaccinated, is on antibiotics and a breathing machine.

Developer Ed Russo commemorated the groundbreaking of the Annin Loft apartment complex at the former Annin Flag manufacturing building in Verona on Flag Day, June 14, 2017. The building, which produced flags from 1919 until ceasing operations in 2013, will be converted into 112 rental units—52 loft-style apartments in the main building and 60 in a new second building, offering studio, one-bedroom, and two-bedroom options. A penthouse floor will be added to the existing four-story structure. Architect Kurt Vierheilig anticipates completion within 12 to 14 months. Former plant manager Joe Vallone recalled the facility's history, including its response to the Sept. 11, 2001 attacks, while Mayor Kevin Ryan noted the site serves as a gateway to the community.

A goalie described a key Stanley Cup Final save: Modano took a hard slapper that was difficult to control, and the rebound went to a charging Brett Hull, whom the goalie stopped with his glove. The save came before the team scored two quick goals and took over. Speakers praised Kenny for scoring an emotional goal, calling him the heart and soul of New Jersey for years. They respected their opponent but noted lucky bounces helped them.

Apple Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended March 26, 2016 reports second-quarter net sales of $50.6 billion, down 13% from $58.0 billion a year earlier, and net income of $10.5 billion versus $13.6 billion, with diluted earnings per share of $1.90 compared with $2.33. Six-month net sales were $126.4 billion and net income $28.9 billion. The sales decline was driven primarily by lower iPhone sales (net sales down 18%) and weakness in foreign currencies relative to the U.S. dollar, while Services grew 20% and Other Products grew 30%. Gross margin fell to 39.4% from 40.8%. By segment, Greater China declined 26% and the Americas 10%, while Japan rose 24%. The Company introduced iPhone SE and a 9.7-inch iPad Pro during the quarter, available beginning in the third quarter of 2016.

Total assets were $305.3 billion as of March 26, 2016, and cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $232.9 billion, of which $208.9 billion was held by foreign subsidiaries. During the quarter, Apple issued $15.5 billion of U.S. dollar-denominated term debt (total term debt principal of $71.3 billion), utilized $7.0 billion for share repurchases, and paid $2.9 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents at $0.52 per share. The $140 billion repurchase authorization had $117 billion utilized. Gross unrecognized tax benefits were $7.5 billion. The European Commission is conducting a formal investigation regarding state aid involving two Irish subsidiaries, which could require recovery of past taxes. In the Samsung patent litigation, Samsung paid $548 million in December 2015, and in March 2016 the U.S. Supreme Court agreed to hear Samsung's appeal.

The Chargé in the United Kingdom received a memorandum on negotiations to renew the Anglo-Belgian purchase agreement for the Belgian Congo, which had expired August 31. The importance of West African raw materials to the Allied war effort had increased, prompting Britain to press Belgium to raise production of wolfram, tin, copper, palm oil, and rubber. Belgium faced difficulty because of higher competitive offers from Allied buyers, including US prices for palm oil and rubber exceeding UK prices; the matter was raised urgently with the US Government. Another obstacle was the lack of coordination on the Belgian side in assessing requirements for machinery and steel; Britain hoped Belgium would submit a comprehensive twelve-month program. Separately, the British Ministry of Supply proposed that the UK and US jointly approach the Belgian Minister of Colonies on a broad over-all arrangement with the Congo; Washington meetings produced unanimous agreement that this would simplify and coordinate trade.

Sienna Senior Living Inc. announced a February 2017 dividend of $0.075 per common share ($0.90 annualized), payable March 15, 2017 to shareholders of record as of February 28, 2017. The company offers an optional Dividend Reinvestment Plan issuing shares at a 3% discount. Sienna operates 55 seniors living residences across Canada.

Following protests and resignations over Project Maven, a controversial Pentagon project, Google says it will develop an ethics policy to guide its military involvement, which according to The New York Times will explicitly ban the use of AI in weaponry. A Google spokesperson said employee feedback would inform the drafting of principles, with details expected in coming weeks. Internal emails show executives, including Fei-Fei Li, expressed concern about media backlash. Employee opposition included Jeff Dean signing a letter against autonomous weapons, and a roundtable hosted by Diane Greene on April 11 did little to allay employee concerns.

Eleven Ursuline High students and six adults will travel to Nicaragua April 2-8 during spring break to help locals with food, housing, home visits, and building houses, while learning empathy and embracing other cultures.

Nigeria and foreign countries, including the United Kingdom, have commenced the Automatic Exchange of Tax Information (AETI) on overseas assets held by Nigerians, which Nigeria joined in January 2018. Finance Minister Kemi Adeosun said data received on bank accounts, property and trusts supports the Voluntary Assets and Income Declaration Scheme (VAIDS) and 'nudge' letters to potential tax defaulters. She advised offshore structure users to regularise taxes before the amnesty expires. The National Tax Policy Implementation Committee presented a progress report on tax laws reform, having considered three policy documents and identified seven major tax areas, including Company Income Tax, VAT and Personal Income Tax. Proposed changes aim to increase and diversify revenue, simplify tax payment, promote small businesses, protect vulnerable persons and remove obsolete provisions, yielding two executive orders and five amendment bills.

Pharmacist Dr. Chukwuma Agubata of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, stated that Irvingia Fat from Ogbono nuts can improve the efficacy of the anti-malaria drug Artemether. Because the drug's low water solubility limits its dissolution and absorption into the bloodstream, his research formulated Ogbono fat as microparticles that entrap the drug and act as a carrier to the bloodstream, improving delivery and efficacy. He called for government and private sector support to mass produce the locally sourced material and help reduce malaria's burden.

A Nationwide Home Insurance survey found pet owners spend almost £3,500 in the first year of ownership, with cats costing £2,455 annually and dogs £4,791. ABI figures show a record £706 million in pet insurance claims in 2016, and Nationwide's Rob Angus advised owners to plan ahead and budget for pet costs.

This study investigates the (re)construction of professional identities of teachers in initial formation, motivated by the author's approximately eighteen years of experience with bachelor's degrees and six years teaching English in elementary public school, where recurring guidance such as "You have to frame in the system or the system swallows you" prompted reflection. Drawing on Alsup (2006), the study employs the concept of Borderland Discourse—discourse in which personal and professional selves are integrated or negotiated—while emphasizing sociolinguistic and emotional rather than linguistic aspects. Identity is understood as multiple, transitory, and conflictual, negotiated through discourse, distinguishing claimed and assigned identities. The cited literature notes that the first year of teaching remains extremely difficult for most preservice teachers and that 50% of novice teachers do not last more than five years.

Data consist of narratives from internship reports produced over four semesters (2010–2011) by two participants, Laura and Richard, in a supervised internship discipline, alongside interactions on the Moodle platform. Laura perceived a "breach" between university theory and school practice but, through borderland discourse, developed a flexible professional identity that prioritized students' interests and assumed the identity of a foreign language teacher rather than an intern. Richard experienced tension moving from student/researcher to teacher, criticized his university training as disconnected from the chaotic reality of public schools, yet developed a confident professional identity; he ultimately refused to become a foreign language teacher, identifying as a mother language teacher instead.

The study concludes that: the analyzed contexts were arenas for negotiating new professional identities; identities are transient and interact in a non-chronological, pendulum-like movement; the Supervised Internship discipline was relevant to identity reconstruction; and the Moodle platform served as an environment for sharing emotions and experiences, functioning as emotional scaffolds, with narratives in virtual and in-person contexts constituting privileged sites for understanding language's role in identity construction.

The Palmerston North Rescue Helicopter made three callouts on 9 December 2017, transporting a man with a suspected spinal injury to Christchurch Hospital, a motorcyclist with a fractured leg to Palmerston North Hospital, and a boy with a trampoline injury to Whanganui Hospital.

Ariel Miranda pitched seven shutout innings, allowing four hits with five strikeouts and no walks, to earn his first win as the Mariners defeated the Marlins 6-1 at Safeco Field. Miranda, who always believed he was a starter, moved into the rotation after Drew Smyly was injured late in spring training. He relied heavily on his fastball, throwing it 63 times out of 97 pitches, and attacked hitters aggressively early in counts. It was the sixth time this season a Seattle starter threw seven shutout innings. Robinson Cano, who had been hitting .212, broke out with a 441-foot home run off starter Tom Koehler in the first inning, and Nelson Cruz followed with a 410-foot homer. Manager Scott Servais praised Miranda's approach and said the middle of the lineup drives the team's success.

The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau finalized rules this week that could force many payday lenders out of business, though Republicans in Congress oppose the changes. The rules would require payday and auto title lenders to verify borrowers can repay in full within 30 days and would limit account debits. A 2014 CFPB study found more than 80 percent of payday loans are rolled over or followed by another loan within two weeks. The industry's trade group says the rule would devastate an industry serving 30 million to 40 million customers a year. The CFPB estimates loan volume could be halved and many of 16,000 stores in 35 states could close. The rule takes effect in 2019 and could still be rolled back by Congress.

The passage consists largely of repeated financial news headlines on topics including the Bank of England's AI bubble warning, Fifth Third's $10.9 billion acquisition of Comerica, gold surging above $4,000 on Fed easing expectations, and OpenAI's $500 billion valuation. The main article reports that oil prices fell Thursday as easing Middle East tensions reduced the geopolitical risk premium. Brent crude dropped about 1.4 percent to $65.07 per barrel and WTI to $61.55, also pressured by rising U.S. crude inventories and slowing demand in transport and manufacturing. Reports of progress toward a Gaza ceasefire lifted confidence that broader regional disruption could be avoided. Expectations of possible Federal Reserve rate cuts next year sent mixed signals, supporting risk assets but tempering oil demand forecasts. With tensions subsiding, analysts said focus has returned to fundamentals—rising U.S. and Brazilian output and subdued demand in Europe and parts of Asia—expected to keep prices under pressure, with relative stability forecast unless tensions reignite. The passage also describes Pan Finance, a financial intelligence publication with over 200,000 readers across 150 countries and offices in London, Lagos, Barcelona, Miami, and Sharjah.

This MIT lecture continues a discussion of quantum states of light, building on coherent states—eigenstates of the annihilation operator whose complex eigenvalue alpha represents the electric field phasor. The professor describes quasi-probability distributions (Q, P, and Wigner functions), which arise from different operator orderings and each have advantages and disadvantages: Q is always positive, P yields a delta function for coherent states, and the Wigner function's projections give actual position and momentum distributions, though it can take negative values.

The lecture demonstrates that coherent states are minimum uncertainty states, satisfying the Heisenberg limit. It then introduces the second-order temporal coherence function g2(tau), which classically cannot fall below 1 but can be smaller for quantum states, serving as a litmus test for non-classical light. For a single mode, g2 relates to photon number fluctuations and the Fano factor: coherent states are Poissonian with g2 = 1; thermal states are super-Poissonian with g2 = 2; and photon number (Fock) states are sub-Poissonian with g2 = (n-1)/n.

The lecture emphasizes that attenuating a coherent state does not produce a true single-photon state, since it remains Poissonian. Single photons can be created using single atoms coupled to high-finesse cavities, or through heralded schemes using many atoms.
