Finally, the Hanbury Brown Twiss experiment, which uses a beam splitter and two detectors to measure intensity correlations, is described as the landmark experiment marking the beginning of quantum optics.

New research led by MBARI shows that marine heatwaves in the Gulf of Alaska reshaped plankton communities and disrupted the ocean's biological carbon pump, slowing the transport of carbon to the deep sea. Analyzing data from robotic BGC-Argo floats and ship-based plankton surveys during two heatwaves (2013–2015 and 2019–2020), researchers found carbon accumulating near the surface or lingering in the twilight zone instead of sinking, attributed to shifts in phytoplankton and an increase in small grazers that produce slow-sinking waste. The study found that not all marine heatwaves have identical effects and underscores the need for sustained, collaborative ocean monitoring.

The northern mountainous province of Yen Bai aims to develop raw material resources and hi-tech processing facilities to boost its agro-forestry-fishery sector, focusing on the processing industry, trademarks, and market expansion. With 430,000 hectares of forests, it has 104 wood processing facilities and seeks investment in high-quality furniture for export, targeting wood processing revenue of 850 billion VND by 2020 and double that by 2025. The province also grows tea, cinnamon, and cassava, supported by 99 tea-processing facilities, four cassava factories, and 13 cinnamon oil extracting factories. It seeks investment in camellia fruit and bamboo shoot processing and plans cattle meat processing facilities.

In State of Oklahoma ex rel. Vassar v. Missouri-Kansas-Texas R. Co. (W.D. Okla., Oct. 11, 1939), the defendants moved to dismiss, arguing that plaintiff Bill Vassar ceased to be Lincoln County Attorney in January 1939 and his successor, Frank McVey, was never substituted within the six-month period required by Rule 25(d) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, so the action abated. The court held that the rule, whose effect is substantially the same as 28 U.S.C.A. § 780, is clear and mandatory. Although the plaintiff contended Vassar was only a nominal party and that the State of Oklahoma was the real party in interest, the court found the rule applicable and dismissed the action without prejudice. Similar orders were entered in the related cases Nos. 1996, 1997, 1999, 2000, 2001, 6362, and 6363.

Celebrity chef Mario Batali has surrendered oversight of daily operations at his restaurant empire following reports of sexual misconduct involving at least four women over at least 20 years, according to Eater New York. Batali acknowledged the complaints matched his past behavior and apologized. A company spokesperson said an employee's October complaint was the first formal one, and Batali was reprimanded and required to attend training. He is taking leave from ABC's "The Chew," and Food Network has placed plans to relaunch "Molto Mario" on hold.

Austria-Hungary's Foreign Ministry issued a note stating that the enemy governments had rejected the allied powers' December 12 peace proposal as lacking sincerity, and that the reply's form prevented a direct answer, so its views were addressed to neutral powers. It declined to re-discuss the war's origins, citing Serbia's growing hostility and the Sarajevo assassination, and dismissed debate over the military situation as idle. It asserted the alliance sought only defensive ends, while the enemy states sought the annihilation of Austria-Hungary, conquest of Alsace-Lorraine, partition of Turkey, and curtailment of Bulgaria. Claiming it had acted in good faith and that the adversaries offered no counter-proposal, it cited the treatment of the Irish, Finnish, and Boer peoples, North Africa, and Greece. It disclaimed responsibility for the war's continuance and pledged to continue fighting until securing an honorable peace.

This study developed the Grocery Basket Score (GBS), a model that rates entire shopping baskets for their health properties based on their link with mortality, aiming to complement product-level rating systems like the Nutri-Score and translate nutritional guidelines (such as the AHEI) into actionable supermarket insights.

Using NHANES data (2001–2018) linked with 2019 mortality data from 35,462 participants, the researchers constructed two types of dietary signals: "density signals" (proportions of nutrients relative to total calories) and "deficiency signals" (whether nutrient-per-calorie density falls below recommended levels). These signals were evaluated in Cox proportional hazard models adjusted for age, sex, BMI, and poverty-income ratio.

The final GBS combines separate food and beverage models as a calorie-weighted average. The food model uses seven signals—punishing saturated fats, sugar, sodium, and deficiencies in protein, vitamin C, and iron, while rewarding fiber. The beverage model penalizes calorie density. Vitamin C and iron deficiency and beverage calories were the largest risk drivers.

Validation showed a Pearson correlation of 0.60 between the GBS and Nutri-Score across 913,298 Open Food Facts items (ranging 0.25–0.75 across 15 food clusters), with disagreements driven mainly by dairy and sweet snacks. Correlation with the AHEI among 4,382 NHANES 2017–18 participants was -0.62 (without alcohol's protective effect) and -0.60 (with it), compared to -0.48/-0.47 for calorie-weighted Nutri-Scores.

Limitations include development on a U.S. population, self-reported dietary data, exclusion of items with missing nutritional information, use of Nutri-Score 2017 for AHEI validation, and no modeling of alcohol's negative health effects beyond calorie density. Strengths include requiring no manual food annotation, enabling automated deployment via retailer loyalty or digital basket programs, and not requiring knowledge of household size or absolute quantities.

Cam Newton apologized in a video posted the night of Thursday, October 5, for sexist comments made to Carolina beat writer Jourdan Rodrigue, whom he told he found it "funny" that a female was asking about routes. After backlash, including losing his Oikos Greek Yogurt sponsorship, Newton called his words degrading and disrespectful to women and apologized to women worldwide.

The Fifth Circuit addressed whether a Chapter 7 debtor with above-median income may claim the vehicle ownership deduction under the means test in 11 U.S.C. § 707(b) when the debtor has no loan or lease payments on the vehicles. The Tates filed Chapter 7 bankruptcy on January 10, 2007, and because their household income exceeded the state median, they were subject to the means test under BAPCPA, under which Chapter 7 cases are presumptively abusive if disposable income can pay unsecured creditors at least $166.67 monthly. The Tates claimed IRS Local Standard ownership deductions of $471 and $332 for two unencumbered vehicles plus $343 in operating expenses, yielding monthly disposable income of $137.66. The U.S. Trustee moved to dismiss the case for abuse; the bankruptcy court granted the motion and the district court affirmed, holding that the ownership deduction requires a monthly note or lease payment. Reviewing de novo, the Fifth Circuit noted a split between the "plain language approach," which allows the deduction regardless of debt, and the "IRM approach," which requires a debt or lease payment. Adopting the Seventh Circuit's reasoning in Ross-Tousey, the court held that "applicable" refers to the debtor's geographic region and number of vehicles rather than actual expenses; that the statute's exclusion of debt payments contradicts the IRM approach; that Congress did not incorporate the IRM into the statute, as confirmed by legislative history; and that uniform, bright-line application of the means test, the existence of ownership costs without payments, and arbitrary results from disallowance further support the plain language approach. The court reversed the district court's judgment and remanded for further proceedings.

This document describes optional extensions to the Secure Encrypted Virtualization API (SEV) and SEV Secure Nested Paging Firmware ABI Specification (SNP) that enable page migration operations, facilitated by AMD's Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine. TMPM support is determined via the ENGINE_READY bit in the PM_Status register, and IOMMU enablement is required. TMPM offloads page migration and addresses two challenges: it can pause DMA traffic to a page during copying and table updates, and it acts as a trusted agent capable of migrating guest pages protected by SEV/SNP.

The PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO command migrates pages that are concurrent DMA targets and requires software to supply the relevant IOMMU host Page Table Entry location. The PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST command migrates SNP guest pages, with destination pages in a newly defined Pre-Migration state (RMP containing PS_ASID_VAL, not PVALIDATable by guests), convertible back to Hypervisor state via RMPUpdate.

Multi-page commands may migrate up to 128 pages via a Page Migration List with per-page status entries. PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS requires checking individual entries; PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE permits retry. Performance is best with 128-page commands, a ring buffer kept ahead of the engine, and paced interrupts. IOMMU data structures, vIOMMU buffers, and the ring buffer itself do not support migration, and software must avoid concurrent hPTE modifications during TMPM operations.

Firmware reload requires pausing operations, tearing down the ring buffer, using the BIOS-to-PSP mailbox protocol, and providing firmware of the same or greater version. EPYC family is identified via the FW_VER_Major field returned by PM_GET_CAPABILITIES (Family 19h corresponds to a value of 71 decimal), which determines the reload execution path.

Starbucks stock has been flat since late 2015 due to weak U.S. comparable-store sales. Mobile Order & Pay, over 20% of orders in some locations, caused congestion, though comps are rebounding with new solutions. The Unicorn drink drove sales via social media buzz, and Frappuccino Happy Hour should support sales; last year's Q3 miss stemmed from loyalty program changes and altered traffic recording, now resolved. Starbucks' dividend, initiated in April 2010 at 5 cents per share, rose to 25 cents in November 2016, with growth exceeding 26% annually. In China, Starbucks is opening 500 stores yearly, a pace management expects to continue for decades, with 7% comp-store sales last quarter.
Liberty Island was evacuated on July 4 after a person climbed the Statue of Liberty's base, shortly after six people were arrested for hanging an "Abolish I.C.E." banner from the pedestal.

This paper presents FoodSEM, a fine-tuned open-source large language model (based on the instruction-tuned Llama 3 8B model) specialized in food named-entity linking (NEL). FoodSEM links food entity mentions in text to entities from three ontologies—FoodOn, SNOMED-CT, and the Hansard taxonomy—using an instruction-response (IR) scenario in which entity recognition precedes linking. The fine-tuning dataset was created by converting the CafeteriaFCD and CafeteriaSA corpora from BioC format into IR pairs and supplementing them with artificially generated NEL instances to balance entity coverage, totaling 21,027 instances. The model was fine-tuned with Low-Rank Adaptation in 4-bit precision for one epoch and evaluated using five-fold cross-validation, with general instruction data from Dolly-HHRLHF added to prevent catastrophic forgetting. FoodSEM achieved macro-weighted F1 scores of 0.942–0.974 on artificial NEL instances, 0.827–0.863 on CafeteriaFCD, and 0.654–0.730 on CafeteriaSA, outperforming 0-shot, 1-shot, and 5-shot prompting baselines of the non-fine-tuned model, whose best F1 was around 0.40; 0-shot results were 0.0 across all settings. Lower recall on scientific abstracts was attributed to NER errors propagating to the NEL task. The stated contributions are publishing food-annotated corpora in IR format suitable for LLM fine-tuning, releasing the model, and providing a benchmark baseline. Code, datasets, and the model are publicly available on GitHub and Hugging Face.

Checkr, a background check technology company founded in 2014 by Daniel Yanisse and Jonathan Perichon, served mainly gig economy customers with fast, automated checks using artificial intelligence. The founders observed that candidates with conviction records—a high percentage being Black and Hispanic—were rejected at alarming rates, prompting the company to embrace fair chance hiring, the practice of offering fair and equal job opportunities to individuals with records. By early 2024, Checkr, valued at $5 billion with $678 million raised, was a leading voice in the movement and a fair chance employer itself.

Roughly 80 million Americans had arrest or conviction records, over one-third of the workforce, and faced barriers including 44,000 collateral consequences, unemployment exceeding 27%, and high recidivism. Meanwhile, the U.S. had 9.5 million job openings. Proponents argued that fair chance hiring enlarged talent pools, lowered turnover (Checkr's fair chance attrition was 5% versus 22% company-wide), did not lower hiring standards, and benefited society, with employment barriers costing the U.S. economy $78–87 billion in GDP annually.

Checkr offered fair chance tools including Candidate Stories (context for flagged candidates, with nearly 45,000 approved since 2020), Assess (filtering convictions, affecting over 2 million individuals since 2019), a fair chance dashboard tracking EEOC compliance, and an expungement tool. In 2021, it signed Pledge 1%, created a CSR division led by Ken Oliver and the Checkr.org foundation, formed nonprofit hiring partnerships, and launched a 12-month apprenticeship program in July 2023.

After noticing post-pandemic mission-business misalignment, Checkr clarified that mission impact would be driven through its customers, emphasizing that the mission's success depended on business success. With fair chance talent showing 30% higher loyalty and engagement, Yanisse sought to expand the movement amid speculation about a potential IPO.

In the DAWn-plasma trial, which investigated convalescent plasma plus standard of care (SOC) versus SOC alone in hospitalized COVID-19 patients (320 patients in the plasma+SOC group, 163 in the SOC group), no statistically significant differences were found for any secondary endpoints; estimated treatment effects were close to identity values, and results were similar for the Per Protocol Set.

Safety outcomes were similar between groups: 139 patients (28.78%) experienced adverse events (90 in plasma+SOC [28.13%], 49 in SOC [30.06%]); fatal AEs occurred in 49 patients (33 plasma+SOC [10.31%], 16 SOC [9.82%]); and SAEs occurred in 100 subjects (66 plasma+SOC [20.62%], 34 SOC [20.68%]). Five AEs led to discontinuation of study treatment (all in plasma+SOC), and two led to discontinuation of the study. Fourteen AEs in 12 patients (3.75%) and seven SAEs in 7 patients (2.19%) were considered treatment-related. Transfusion-related side effects occurred in 19/320 intervention patients (6.0%), with no TRALI cases reported.

Mean evolution of laboratory parameters (D-Dimer, CRP, ferritin) and body temperature showed no significant differences between groups. Neutralizing antibody titers (NT50) increased between baseline and day 6, but this increase was not influenced by the intervention (p = 0.766). Higher titers at Day 0 and Day 6 correlated with better outcome, but the magnitude of increase did not.

Overall, the intervention had no impact on the primary endpoint (alive and free of mechanical ventilation on day 15), mortality, or other secondary endpoints, and transfusion of four units of high-titer convalescent plasma could not change the natural course of the disease in these patients.

The passage is a section of a Texas Instruments datasheet for the TLV321x comparator devices (TLV3211, TLV3212, TLV3214, TLV3221, TLV3222). The inputs and outputs include internal ESD protection circuits to (V+) and (V–), limiting input voltages to 0.2V beyond the rails; TI recommends a series current-limiting resistor (10mA or less) when connecting inputs to low-impedance sources. An internal Power-On Reset circuit holds the output low for up to 32μs after the supply crosses VPOR of 1.65V, after which the output reflects the differential input.

Basic comparator operation is described: the output is logic low when VIN is less than VREF and logic high when VIN exceeds VREF, with logic invertible by swapping input pins. Propagation delay (tpLH, tpHL) is measured from the input midpoint to the output response, and smaller overdrive voltages—particularly below 100mV—increase propagation delay.

Because the devices have only 1.8mV of internal hysteresis, external hysteresis via a positive feedback loop can prevent output chatter. Inverting configurations use a three-resistor network referenced to VCC, while non-inverting configurations use a two-resistor network with VREF; equations define trip voltages and total hysteresis.

A typical application is low-side current sensing, where a comparator signals an over-current condition (logic high alert) when an amplified shunt voltage exceeds 1.1V. Layout guidance includes 0.1μF low-ESR bypass capacitors at supply pins, minimizing output-to-input coupling, and using controlled impedance traces for long runs. Remaining sections cover documentation update notifications, TI E2E support forums, trademarks, ESD handling cautions, revision history, packaging information, and TI's legal disclaimers.

In an address, the President said that three days earlier Iraqis had voted in large numbers to choose their leaders, calling it a landmark day and noting that ballots would be counted and a new government formed. He acknowledged that much of the prewar intelligence on weapons of mass destruction proved wrong, but maintained it was right to remove Saddam Hussein and took responsibility for the decision to go to war. He outlined a three-part strategy—remaining on the offensive, building Iraqi democracy, and pursuing reconstruction—and said troop decisions would be based on conditions on the ground rather than artificial timetables. Michael Daniels, 40, a former head of sales at BMW Berry in Chiswick, was jailed for five years and three months for conspiracy to steal motor vehicles. He gave accomplice Alex Tingle, 28, spare keys to newly sold cars and passed on customer addresses from the dealership database. Tingle and Vincent Murphy used the keys to steal nine cars worth £210,000 over six weeks between December 2015 and February 2016; the vehicles were given fake plates and handed to a figure known as "Ali" in Alperton. Murphy received 16 months for aggravated vehicle taking. Tingle admitted conspiracy, was jailed for two years plus two months concurrent for drug possession, but will be released immediately having served 13 months. Made for $34 million, the film exceeded expectations following its June 28 release. Kevin Spacey, Lily James, Jamie Foxx, Jon Bernthal, and Jon Hamm also star.

Exchange-traded funds (ETFs) are baskets of securities traded as single instruments on stock exchanges, behaving like stocks with ticker symbols and intraday pricing. This article covers 18 ETF trading strategies, including trend following, mean reversion, momentum, sector rotation, arbitrage, high-frequency trading, quantitative trading, options trading, volatility trading, statistical arbitrage, pair trading, market-neutral strategies, global macro trading, equal weight strategies, smart beta strategies, currency hedging, fixed income, and commodities trading. The first ETF, SPY, launched in 1993, tracks the S&P 500. ETFs offer benefits such as diversification, liquidity, low expense ratios, tax efficiency, and the ability to trade throughout the day, but carry risks including market volatility, liquidity concerns, tracking errors, and elevated volatility in leveraged or specialized funds. Unlike mutual funds, ETFs can be bought and sold continuously during trading hours rather than only at end-of-day prices. ETFs can be day traded, swing traded, or scalped, though the authors note day trading and scalping are difficult and favor swing trading. Popular ETFs discussed include SPY, VTI, and IEFA. The article recommends backtesting strategies and incubating them before live trading, and emphasizes diversification across multiple strategies, time frames, and market directions rather than seeking a single best strategy.

Jury selection is underway in Isaiah Hagan's murder trial; Hagan, accused of killing Halee Rathgeber, faces four counts. After a mistrial, 10 of 14 jurors have been chosen; opening statements begin Monday.

This document describes optional extensions to AMD's Secure Encrypted Virtualization (SEV) and Secure Nested Paging (SNP) specifications, implemented through the Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine, which copies page content between system physical addresses while preserving guest physical addresses. TMPM availability is checked via the ENGINE_READY bit in the PM_Status register, and IOMMU enablement is required. The engine offloads page migration, can pause DMA traffic during copies, and can migrate SNP-protected guest pages inaccessible to the hypervisor/OS.

Two primary commands are described: PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, which migrates pages that may be concurrent DMA targets using IOMMU host page table entries, and PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST, which migrates SNP guest pages using a new Pre-Migration RMP state. Multi-page commands can process up to 128 pages via a Page Migration List with per-page status; PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS requires checking individual entries, and PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE may be retried. Performance is best with 128-page commands, with interrupts requested at the end of command sequences. Certain IOMMU and ring buffer structures cannot be migrated. All migrated system physical addresses must be 4KB aligned (host page table entry addresses may be 8-byte aligned).

Firmware can be reloaded via the BIOS-to-PSP mailbox protocol when no operations are in flight; PM_GET_CAPABILITIES reports FW_VER_Major, with 71 denoting EPYC Family 19h. The driver initializes through mailbox registers and a ring buffer of 1–255 pages, supports pause/resume, and manages six interrupt sources. Errors are reported via command status and sub-status fields, the PM_Status register, or the Machine Check Architecture.

A Bihar girl diagnosed with TB in 2012 developed drug-resistant TB after normal medicines failed. Hungarian Minister President Count Tisza told Ambassador Penfield that the enemy peace terms would mutilate Germany and dismember Austria-Hungary and Turkey, amounting to a war of destruction contradicting President Wilson's views, and that the dual monarchy best suits southeastern Europe's mixed populations; he asked that these points reach American statesmen and the public. The passage describes NVIDIA's GA10x Ampere GPU architecture and related products. Key features include:

**Memory**: GA10x GPUs introduce GDDR6X memory (developed with Micron), using PAM4 signaling to reach speeds up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec bandwidth in the GeForce RTX 3090. The RTX 3080 delivers 1.5x more memory bandwidth than the RTX 2080 Super.

**Interconnect and I/O**: Third-generation NVLink connects two GPUs (e.g., two A40s or RTX A6000s) to scale memory from 48GB to 96GB, providing 112.5 GB/sec total bandwidth. PCIe Gen 4 doubles bandwidth versus PCIe 3.0, up to 64 GB/sec.

**GPU structure**: The full GA102 GPU contains seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, 84 SMs, and 112 ROPs. ROPs are now part of the GPC rather than the memory controller, improving raster operation performance.

**SM architecture**: Each GA10x SM contains 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, and a second-generation RT Core. FP32 processing is doubled by enabling FP32 on both datapaths. The L1 data cache/shared memory is 128 KB per SM, 33% larger than Turing, with double the shared memory bandwidth.

**Ray tracing**: Second-generation RT Cores double the ray/triangle intersection testing rate over Turing and add a new Interpolate Triangle Position unit for hardware-accelerated ray-traced motion blur, enabling up to 8x faster motion blur rendering. GA10x also supports concurrent RT Core, graphics, and compute workloads.

**Tensor Cores and AI**: Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32 and BF16 data types and support Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity (2:4 pattern), doubling throughput for sparse matrices. With Sparsity, the RTX 3080 delivers 238 peak FP16 Tensor TFLOPS. DLSS is enhanced with a 9x Super Resolution scaling factor, enabling 8K 60 fps gaming on the RTX 3090.

**RTX IO**: A suite of technologies enabling GPU-based loading and lossless decompression of game assets via Microsoft's DirectStorage API, accelerating I/O up to 100x versus hard drives and traditional APIs while offloading work from CPU cores.

**Data center and workstation products**: The NVIDIA A40 is positioned as the most powerful data center GPU for visual computing, offering up to 2x FP32 and ray-tracing throughput versus Quadro RTX 6000, and up to 5x (10x with Sparsity) AI training throughput. The RTX A6000 is the flagship workstation GPU with 10,752 CUDA Cores and 48GB GDDR6.

**Display and video**: Ampere GPUs support HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC, enabling 8K60 and 4K120 output. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware AV1 decode (a first among GPUs), and seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

**Overclocking**: A new Error Detection and Replay (EDR) feature on the GDDR6X memory interface detects and retries data transmission errors, helping overclockers identify memory limits without crashing.

Overall, the GA10x Ampere architecture delivers up to 2x performance improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI, and up to 1.9x better power efficiency than Turing.

After the death of President William Henry Harrison, the speaker, formerly Vice President, has assumed the Presidency under the Constitution—the first such occurrence in the nation's history—and outlines the principles that will guide his administration. In foreign affairs he pledges justice to all nations while yielding to injustice from none, cultivating peace and maintaining efficient Army and Navy defenses. He warns against concentrating power in the President, particularly the dangers of the removal power and growing patronage, and will seek Congressional measures to separate the "sword and the purse," removing officials only for partisanship or misuse of office. He advocates rigid economy, avoidance of peacetime debt, abolition of sinecures, and strict accountability for public agents. Though existing financial laws will be enforced until repealed, he considers them unwise and will support constitutional measures restoring a sound circulating medium. Finally, he commits to preserving the constitutional balance between federal and state authority and to protecting the nation's free institutions.

Detente—relaxing tensions with well-armed potential enemies—is meaningful only if both sides take positive actions; one-sided negotiations during the Soviet Union's massive military buildup do not advance peace. Continued negotiation with the Soviets is supported, provided goals of peace and freedom are preserved and agreements are not sought merely for their own sake. Honest, verifiable nuclear reductions are endorsed, but treaties like SALT II that legitimize one-sided buildups are rejected, with the Austrian State Treaty cited as a successful negotiation example. The passage warns of Soviet objectives: dividing NATO, expanding influence in the Arabian Gulf and South Asia, encircling China, and sponsoring subversion in the Caribbean, including Cuba-trained guerrillas targeting Jamaica, Honduras, El Salvador, and Guatemala, plus leftist regimes in Nicaragua and Grenada. Quoting Paul Nitze's remark that Kremlin leaders "want the world," it argues the Soviets seek military superiority that would force submission or conflict. Restoring American strength would secure real peace and might persuade the Kremlin to accept true arms limitation. American arms serve defense only, and Lenin-Marxist philosophy is described as primitive, comparable to feudalism.

Merck halted the late-stage trial of its Alzheimer's drug verubecestat after an independent study found it had "virtually no chance" of working, following Eli Lilly's termination of its solanezumab trial three months earlier. Merck will continue studying verubecestat in less advanced cases, but experts called the failure a substantial setback. Approximately 47 million people worldwide live with dementia, with Alzheimer's accounting for 60–80% of cases, a figure expected to reach 131 million by 2050. No new Alzheimer's drug has been made available in over a decade, and no treatment has been proven to slow the disease. Verubecestat is a BACE inhibitor targeting amyloid plaques, and its failure raises doubts about the beta amyloid theory. Other companies, including Biogen with its drug aducanumab, continue trials. Merck's early-stage trial results are expected in February 2019, and its shares fell nearly 2% after the announcement.

Vermont City Electric (VCE) is a municipal utility formed in 1905 to lower electricity costs in Vermont City, serving roughly 16,000 residential, 2,845 small commercial, and 784 large commercial customers across about 16 square miles. VCE has invested in demand-side management (DSM) since 2000 to reduce energy use and peak demand, but the 2008 economic downturn led its internal Finance Committee to cap 2009 DSM spending at $800,000, below the $1,035,027 cost of running all nine DSM programs. The case explains power versus energy, peak demand, and load duration curves, which divide annual demand into five load blocks. VCE supplies power through its wood-fired McNeil plant, the oil-fired VCE GT used for peak loads, medium-term hydro-based contracts, and the ISO-NE wholesale market, with wind capacity planned for 2012; costs, carbon emissions, and discount factors through 2014 are provided. Daniela Shazar, an MBA graduate serving on VCE's Citizen's Oversight Board, is tasked with building a mixed-integer optimization model to determine which DSM programs to retain or eliminate within the budget and to assess the total carbon impact, following detailed modeling and analysis assignments.

This passage describes components of the TMS320DM814x DaVinci Digital Media Processor. The system MMU remaps C674x accesses through its MDMA port to physical system addresses, protecting ARM Cortex-A8 memory regions from accidental corruption, and EDMA TC0/TC1 accesses may optionally be routed through it via the MMU_CFG register. The Media Controller manages the HDVPSS and ISS modules. The HDVICP2 is a video encoder/decoder hardware accelerator supporting MPEG1/2/4 ASP/SP, H.264, VC-1, RV9/10, AVS-1.0, and ON2 VP6.2/VP7 codecs. The Face Detection module performs face detection and tracking with QVGA (320x240) 8-bit gray-scale input, supporting minimum face sizes of 20, 25, 32, or 40 pixels, and uses 51.25KB of DDR working memory. The Spinlock module implements 128 hardware semaphores enabling lock operations via a single read-access. The Mailbox module facilitates communication between the ARM Cortex-A8 and C674x DSP, featuring four-message FIFO queues and four interrupts. The device uses a unified memory map with L3 and L4 peripheral domains, and the TILER provides an additional 4-GB addressing range accessible only to HDVPSS and ISS subsystems. Terminal function tables describe pin assignments, multiplexing, internal pullup/pulldown states, and supply voltages for peripherals including GPMC, DDR2/DDR3 controllers, EMAC, GPIO, HDMI, I2C, McASP, PCIe, JTAG, SD, SPI, timers, UARTs, USB, and video I/O. Boot configuration is determined by BTMODE[15:0] pins sampled at reset and latched into the CONTROL_STATUS register, supporting XIP (NOR), NAND, NAND I2C, MMC/SD, SPI, EMAC, PCIe, and UART boot modes. Pin multiplexing is controlled on a pin-by-pin basis by MUXMODE bits in the PINCNTL1–PINCNTL270 registers, with multimuxed functions labeled "MM" in the terminal function tables.

The Supreme Court of Oklahoma addressed whether a district court could reduce a six-month license revocation imposed after Edward C. Turner was arrested for driving under the influence and refused a chemical breath or blood test. The Commissioner of Public Safety revoked Turner's license for six months; an administrative hearing sustained the order, but the district court modified it to three months based on Turner's driving record. The majority reversed the modification, holding under State ex rel. Department of Public Safety v. Kopczynski (1972) that the district court lacked authority to shorten the mandatory six-month suspension, and that the 1975 amendment to § 755, permitting modification only for extreme and unusual hardship, confirmed this interpretation. The revocation was affirmed. In dissent, Justice Simms, joined by two other justices, argued that Kopczynski was distinguishable, that § 6-211(e) allows courts to modify excessive suspensions, and that the 1975 amendment was cumulative rather than exclusive; the dissent would have affirmed the trial court's judgment.

This is the first lecture of an MIT course on effective field theory (EFT). The course lists quantum field theory 2 as a prerequisite, with QFT 3 lecture notes posted as background reading. Grading consists of five biweekly problem sets and an end-of-term presentation on an EFT topic; there are no exams. No single textbook covers more than a fraction of the material.

EFT allows one to focus on interesting physics at a particular scale, in contrast to the usual bottom-up way physics is taught. More general theories are harder to compute with (e.g., hydrogen's spectrum is easier in quantum mechanics than in QFT; planetary orbits easier in Newtonian gravity than in general relativity), so EFT seeks the simplest framework capturing the essential physics while remaining correctable to arbitrary precision order by order.

Developing an EFT involves identifying the relevant degrees of freedom, identifying symmetries (which may even emerge upon expansion), and determining the expansion parameter (power counting) and leading-order Lagrangian. Power counting is as fundamental as gauge symmetry. The key principle, attributed to Wilson, is insensitivity to physics at higher scales, though expansions need not be strictly in mass ratios—for example, non-relativistic QED expands in velocity.

Hydrogen illustrates multiple expansions: bottom quark effects are suppressed by (me/mb)², the proton is treated as a static charge, and the theory is non-relativistic. A subtlety is that integrating out particles can change the coupling definition (running of alpha). Ultraviolet divergences do not invalidate these ideas.

EFTs are used in two ways. Top-down: the high-energy theory is known, heavy particles are integrated out, and the low-energy theory is obtained by matching; the two theories agree on infrared observables but may differ in the ultraviolet (examples: heavy quark effective theory, NRQED/NRQCD, soft-collinear effective theory). Bottom-up: the high-energy theory is unknown or matching is too difficult, so the theory is constructed from symmetries, degrees of freedom, and power counting, with couplings fit to experiment (examples: chiral perturbation theory, the standard model itself, quantum gravity). Logarithms can be understood and summed via renormalization of the low-energy theory.

The standard model can be treated bottom-up as an EFT, expanding in standard model mass scales divided by higher scales (e.g., the Planck mass), with corrections described by higher-dimension operators built from standard model fields. Finally, renormalizability is redefined in EFT: a theory is renormalizable order by order in its expansion parameter, allowing infinitely many parameters in principle but only finitely many at any fixed order. The standard model's leading Lagrangian is traditionally renormalizable, meaning the higher scale is invisible at leading order, unlike chiral perturbation theory, where higher-dimension operators are required even at lowest order.

DTE Maharashtra has released the MHT CET 2018 syllabus and exam pattern circular. The May 2018 exam is for admission to Engineering, Technology, Pharmacy, and Pharma-D courses. It carries 20% Class XI and 80% Class XII weightage, has no negative marking, and difficulty at par with JEE.

This patent application, a continuation of several related applications, describes methods, apparatuses, and systems for multi-user (MU) transmission in wireless local area networks (WLANs). The background states that the IEEE 802.11ac group ID mechanism supports only downlink MU-MIMO with limited numbers of groups and users, cannot support large numbers of clusters, combinations of OFDMA clusters and OFDM MU-MIMO groups, or flexible per-transmission clustering and scheduling, and that current MU control frames add overhead and reduce MAC efficiency.

The disclosed embodiments provide new MU clustering and scheduling mechanisms supporting multiple MU transmission schemes, OFDMA/MU-MIMO combinations, and per-transmission scheduling. A wireless transmit/receive unit (WTRU) may receive a frame, determine whether it is a null data packet (NDP) multi-user MAC PPDU based on an NDP condition, process an NDP SIG field containing MU control information, and generate and transmit a response.

Several MU clustering mechanisms are described, including clustering management frames containing membership and position bit-fields, cluster ID assignment via NDP MAC frames, signaling cluster membership within MU data transmissions or in control frames preceding them, and per-transmission position updates. Two high-efficiency (HE) NDP MAC PPDU designs are presented: one with a single HE-NDP-SIG field and one with HE-NDP-SIG-A and HE-NDP-SIG-B fields. Example NDP MU control frame bodies include MU-RTS, MU-CTS, and MU-Poll frames, along with procedures in which STAs detect NDP frames, determine whether they are intended receivers, prepare responses, and set network allocation vectors (NAVs).

Best-selling author James Patterson has increased his annual classroom library donations from $1.75 million to $2 million. Through the "Patterson Pledge," launched in 2015 and run with Scholastic Book Clubs, he is distributing 4,000 gifts of $500 each to teachers across the country. The Draw play is a run play disguised as a pass play, where the offense briefly mimics a pass before handing the ball to the running back late. It exploits a defense's commitment to the pass, causing defenders to spread out before the ball is run up the middle. The play is most effective in pass-heavy offenses and obvious passing situations, but its main weakness is vulnerability to blitzes—particularly interior pressure, which can trap the Tailback in the backfield since all five offensive linemen are locked in 1-on-1 blocks. For this reason, many offenses tag an RPO to the Draw. The passage outlines player assignments against 3-4 Odd and 4-3 Even fronts, and describes two variations: QB Draw, which uses an athletic quarterback's running ability, and Lead Draw from 12-personnel Strong-I, which adds a Tight End and Fullback into the blocking scheme.

The author, on a 10-day family road trip visiting Badlands, Glacier, Yellowstone, and Devil's Tower National Parks, shares several weather- and climate-related "confessions." Old Faithful's eruption estimate given with a margin of error prompted him to suggest weather forecasts better convey uncertainty, citing Capital Weather Gang's "Boom or Bust" probability graphics and Dan Satterfield's blog on the topic. After witnessing a man approach a bison despite warning signs, he reflected on people ignoring warnings and risks, such as driving through flooded roadways, citing Hank Paulson's view of climate change as the biggest economic risk the planet faces, Castle Williams on challenges in weather risk messaging, and Karen Cerulo's "optimism bias." Standing at Jackson Glacier, he felt despair, noting the park's glaciers declined from over 100 in 1910 to 26 active glaciers in 2015. He felt frustration when a woman dismissed climate change based on one cold night camping, and learned Devil's Tower appeared in Close Encounters of the Third Kind.

This study by Lamtara and Bouziane (Hassan II University of Casablanca) examines teachers' perspectives on the role of education leaders in implementing and sustaining ICT in Moroccan primary and secondary education after the COVID-19 pandemic. A questionnaire administered in October 2023 initially drew 297 respondents, of whom 43.8% (n=130) reported abandoning technology after face-to-face classes resumed; these teachers became the study's focus.

Findings show that, despite institutional initiatives during the pandemic (broadcast lessons, platforms such as TelmidTice, Collab, and e-Takwine, and distribution of devices), significant barriers persist: limited access to devices, fast internet, and digital resources; lack of training (only 22.3% of the 130 teachers had received ICT training); and insufficient institutional support. Chi-square analyses showed few significant demographic differences, indicating barriers stem from leadership factors rather than teacher variables such as age, gender, or location.

Discussing the results against ISTE standards for education leaders, the authors find these standards unmet, citing the GENIE program's lack of shared vision, unstructured training, absent national platforms, and underused teacher-training resources. Recommendations include unifying distance-learning platforms, strengthening stakeholder coordination, expanding teacher training via e-Takwine, evaluating and accrediting digital content, providing devices and connectivity, and integrating digital literacy from primary level. The study concludes that education leadership must play a stronger role in sustaining ICT integration.

This work uses first-principles density functional theory to investigate how stacking geometry controls magnetism in chromium diiodide (CrI2) bilayers. The monolayer adopts a stripe antiferromagnetic (AFx) ground state with a band gap of 1.12 eV. Among bilayer stackings, the indirect BA′ registry with intralayer AFx order and antiparallel interlayer alignment is the global energy minimum; direct (AA, AB, BA) and high-symmetry stackings lie 25–50 meV/f.u. higher. Bilayer band gaps (0.99–1.07 eV) are reduced relative to the monolayer by interlayer orbital hybridization, and broken inversion symmetry in indirect stackings produces spin splittings sensitive to the interlayer magnetic alignment. Sliding between registries involves moderate energy barriers (~25–50 meV/f.u.), enabling mechanical switching. Exchange analysis shows that intralayer coupling sets the primary energy scale, strengthening by ~6–10% in bilayers, while symmetric anisotropy (ΔJxy ~1.48 meV for A-B bonds and ~1.03 meV for A-A/B-B bonds) is nearly registry-independent. Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions emerge only in non-centrosymmetric stackings, and interlayer exchange is an order of magnitude weaker, with its sign depending on registry and spin texture. Spin-selective superexchange, in which only majority-spin Cr-d states hybridize effectively with I-p states, explains the antiferromagnetic ordering. Indirect stackings also enable in-plane polarization (a few µC/cm²), reduced by spin-orbit coupling, suggesting magnetoelectric control for reconfigurable 2D spintronic devices.

Ian Murray, 74, was fined after pleading guilty at Chesterfield magistrates' court to driving without due care and attention over a collision on May 14 in Hathersage, which injured a cyclist as he turned into the Spar garage. The cyclist feared he had broken his neck and suffered bruises, grazes, a facial laceration and pins and needles, but is expected to recover. Murray, of previous good character, was fined £185, ordered to pay £85 costs and a £30 victim surcharge, and received six penalty points.

Westman reported recent Allied reverses had strengthened Finnish confidence in German success against the Russians, though Finland feared German exhaustion the following fall; Mannerheim found it hard to decide, and further Finnish offensives remained an open question. Westman said Finland had miscalculated in expecting a short, victorious war ignored by Britain. Assistant Secretary Berle told the Finnish Minister that Germany was the enemy of the United States and Finland's alignment placed it with Germany; the Minister denied misleading his government and reported Welles had warned continued policy would likely mean a breach of relations. Schoenfeld reported the Finnish press had not mentioned Stalin's declaration that recovery of the Baltic States and Karelia was a Soviet war aim, and that Finland was suppressing or distorting Roosevelt's statements while reporting Churchill's in detail. Jubilation over a bread ration increase was short-lived; icebound food ships forced Finland to requisition seed grain, underscoring its dependence on Germany for food.

The passage outlines defensive strategies against a star player: denying them the ball through aggressive pass denial and help defense, influencing ball handlers to the opposite side of the court, attacking offensively to force the star to expend energy on defense, and employing combination defenses.

A Hylian Shield edition of the New Nintendo 2DS XL, pre-loaded with "The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds," launches exclusively at GameStop on July 2 for $159.99. The streamlined handheld lacks 3D display but plays 3DS and DS games. The 3DS family has sold 72 million units; the Switch, nearly 18 million.

Marsha Jackson, newly promoted Head of Internal Audit at RiseEngineer Corporation, a NYSE-listed green design and construction firm, is responsible for internal financial controls and Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA) compliance, including oversight of its Elysium subsidiary in a country with a high incidence of societal corruption. An anonymous whistleblower alleged that the company's $1.2 billion Elysium government contract win involved misconduct. The compliance team's fact-gathering found dinners and gift exchanges with Elysium officials, a Boston facilities tour for four officials and their families, monthly $100 million government wires with $90 million transferred to Boston headquarters, a $3 million payment to offshore consultant TGH Consulting, $5 million in cash withdrawals with only $1 million documented, and an internal email expressing discomfort with the deal. The subsidiary was its auditor's only client, and two employees suggested a disgruntled former employee may have made the whistleblower claim under false pretenses. A controls report found subsidiary head Sarah Smith prioritized profitability, gave five salespeople uncapped commissions and substantial autonomy, and deferred to sales in conflicts. The finance manager handled all accounting entries and most banking transactions, permitted undocumented withdrawals and transfers without separate approval, and assigned transactions to accounts by best estimate. Exhibits outline the COSO internal control framework and the FCPA, which is enforced by the SEC and DOJ.

Soccer players specialize in positions within a formation, and coaches must select position names and use them consistently. Young players should be given the opportunity to play all positions rather than being type-cast. Positions are generally described from the goal outward: the goalkeeper (G, GK, K), the only position named in the IFAB Laws of the Game, has the handling privilege within the Penalty Area; defenders (D, B) stop opponent attacks; midfielders (M, MF) link defense and attack and require all-around skills and fitness; and forwards (F) are the main attacking force, also called strikers. More specific position names vary by formation and include center backs, stoppers, sweepers, liberos, attacking and holding midfielders, wing backs, and various striker designations. Coaches must choose a formation suited to their players' talents and apply position names consistently.

Monitoring a distributed system requires integrating diverse applications with different monitoring interfaces (e.g., syslog, etw, JMX) into a single system. The adapter pattern addresses this: an adapter container transforms the application container's monitoring interface into the format expected by the general-purpose monitoring system. This decoupling improves maintainability, allows independent rollouts and container reuse, and gives each container dedicated CPU and memory resources.

The article demonstrates how to backtest a Bollinger Band trading strategy in Python. Bollinger Bands, developed by John Bollinger, are plotted two standard deviations away from a simple moving average; this backtest uses 2 standard deviations from a 20-day SMA. Historical data for Microsoft since 1986 is downloaded using the yfinance library, and pandas functions calculate the SMA, standard deviation, and upper and lower bands. The strategy assigns a buy position when the adjusted close falls below the lower band and a sell position when it rises above the upper band, using numpy's np.where() function. Daily and cumulative returns are computed and plotted as an equity curve. The strategy compounded at 2.65% annually while invested only 10.6% of the time, and is presented for informational purposes.

Skoltech researchers developed a mathematical model of memory based on "engrams" (neural units representing concepts through features). Their analysis found that memory capacity is maximized when concepts are described in a seven-dimensional conceptual space, suggesting seven senses may be optimal rather than five. This result appears robust regardless of model details. The findings could improve robotics, AI, and understanding of human memory, though the application to human senses remains speculative.

The Williams Vix Fix is a synthetic VIX indicator created by Larry Williams in 2007 to provide VIX-like readings for instruments beyond the S&P 500, Nasdaq, and Dow Jones 30. Calculated as (Highest(Close,22) – Low) / Highest(Close,22) × 100, it measures price volatility over the last 22 trading days, representing a typical month. The indicator closely resembles the real VIX in levels, swings, magnitude, and timing. Testing showed trading strategies based on it work: one S&P 500 strategy produced 322 trades since 1993 with a 0.5% average per trade and a profit factor of 2, while an improved QQQ strategy achieved 352 trades since 1999, nearly 1% per trade, a 75% win rate, and outperformed buy-and-hold (12.7% versus 9.2%). The indicator is mean revertive and seems to work reasonably well on stock indices, including on the short side.

The passage consists largely of repeated financial news headlines, with one substantive article about Opera launching Neon, an AI-powered browser designed for proactive, task-oriented browsing. Marketed as a subscription product for power users, Neon enters the "agentic browsing" race alongside competitors such as Perplexity's Comet and The Browser Company's Dia. Challenges include ensuring reliability, compliance, safety, transparency, and regulatory oversight. Melania Trump is hosting executives from major online and social media companies, including Amazon, Snap, Facebook, Google and Twitter, to discuss cyberbullying and internet safety — her first public event on the topic, more than a year after naming it a priority. Tech companies have strict anti-harassment policies but rely mainly on users to report abuse, and efforts have fallen short despite measures like Twitter's crackdown on hateful tweets. Warby Parker (WRBY) is presented as an attractive entry point, supported by retail expansion, customer base growth, rising average selling prices, new product lines, and high gross margins despite tariff headwinds. This patent application describes a sole structure for articles of footwear featuring an outsole with an arrangement of traction elements. The outsole includes an annular cleat set comprising traction elements arranged in series about a central axis, typically disposed on the medial side in the ball portion of the forefoot, and one or more radial cleat sets aligned along radial axes intersecting the central axis, with at least one peripheral cleat formed on the outsole's peripheral surface. The annular cleat set consists of taller major cleats in an outer ring and shorter minor cleats in an inner concentric ring. Lateral radial cleat sets each include a major cleat, progressively smaller minor cleats, and a peripheral cleat extending at an oblique angle; an anterior radial cleat set and a heel cleat set are also provided. The outsole comprises a forefoot plate and a heel plate, each formed as a modular structure with an outer shell, an inner skeleton, and cleat inserts. The midsole is a composite of a casing and a core, with a shank and cradle disposed between the plates. This configuration provides traction in lateral and longitudinal directions while allowing rotation about the central axis, with peripheral cleats improving traction when the medial side lifts from the ground.

Researchers have generated muons using compact, laser-driven particle accelerators rather than massive facilities. A laser blasts plasma, creating a charge wave that accelerates electrons; when these electrons strike dense material like lead, they produce muon beams. At Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, electrons accelerated over a distance shorter than a bowling pin reached energies up to 10 billion electron volts, yielding muons of several billion electron volts—a traditional accelerator would need to be a thousand times longer. Similar experiments were reported at Romania's ELI-NP facility and the Shanghai Superintense Ultrafast Laser Facility. Muons, heavier than electrons, penetrate dense materials deeply, but naturally occurring muons are scarce—one per minute per square centimeter of Earth's surface—making imaging slow. Artificial beams could enable portable scanners to detect contraband such as plutonium and uranium in shipping containers. At Colorado State University, researchers demonstrated a proof-of-principle by making a lead object inside a truck visible on a muon detector. Laser accelerators are not yet portable, but future advances could make portable muon sources a reality.

The paper develops pseudospin (Ising) models for two organic crystals of the 5-Phenyl-1H-tetrazole family that exhibit long-range order: APHTZ, a canted ferroelectric with FE ordering along the a axis coexisting with AFE ordering along the b axis, and MPHTZ, a uniaxial antiferroelectric. In both crystals, tetrazole groups form hydrogen-bonded quasi-one-dimensional chains, and dipole switching arises from proton tautomerism—protons moving in double-well potentials flip switchable π-bonds and the associated dipoles.

For APHTZ, a two-sublattice mean-field model reproduces the FE-I ground state (FE along a, AFE along b) and predicts that a transverse field Eb switches one sublattice, inducing a transition to the FE-II phase—a 90° rotation of net polarization—producing double hysteresis loops for Eb, in contrast to the observed single FE loops for Ea. A tricritical point occurs at T* = 409 K, below which switching is first order. For MPHTZ, a four-sublattice model reduces to a two-sublattice AFE Ising model with checkerboard AFE-I ground state; a longitudinal field induces classical AFE-to-FE switching with double loops and a tricritical point at 413 K.

Both models yield second-order phase transitions, Curie-Weiss permittivity behavior, and switching fields proportional to the spontaneous order parameter. Fitting is constrained by scarce experimental data, making APHTZ predictions largely qualitative; the authors call for additional measurements of polarization, permittivity, and transition temperatures to validate the models, and suggest future study of the electrocaloric effect in MPHTZ and the AFE/AFE phase mixture in parent PHTZ.

President Trump met with Jared Isaacman to discuss another nomination to lead NASA, months after withdrawing his initial nomination. Trump had pulled the nomination following a dispute with Elon Musk, citing Isaacman's Democratic ties and close friendship with Musk. Isaacman, who led two private SpaceX flights and founded Shift4, declined to comment. Tensions between Trump and Musk have since cooled.

This study investigated whether genetic variations in vitamin B12 metabolism contribute to Parkinson's disease (PD) risk, age-at-onset, and progression. Although epidemiological evidence shows lower B12 levels in PD patients, no genetic studies had causally linked B12 to PD. The researchers analyzed common variants using PD GWAS data, constructed pathway-specific polygenic risk scores based on B12 metabolism genes, performed rare variant analysis using whole-exome and whole-genome sequencing from 4,929 PD cases and 68,029 controls, and applied Mendelian randomization to test causal relationships. Results showed no significant association between common or rare variants in B12 metabolism genes and PD risk after multiple testing correction. Mendelian randomization and genetic correlation analyses found no causal or genetic link between B12 levels and PD risk, age-at-onset, or progression. The authors suggest that non-genetic factors, such as gastrointestinal dysfunction and gut microbiota alterations, may explain lower B12 levels in PD patients, and recommend further studies in diverse populations with larger datasets.

Niantic announced that over 80 Generation II (Johto) Pokémon will be added to Pokémon GO "later this week," roughly seven months after the game's launch. All new Pokémon will be discoverable in the wild once the update goes live, unlike December's egg-only additions. The update also introduces evolution items obtained from PokéStops, two new berries (Nanab, which slows Pokémon, and Pinap, which doubles candy from catches), new avatar items, and unspecified new "encounter gameplay." Notably absent are improved tracking, trading, and player-versus-player battling. This is the largest addition since launch, following Ditto, a holiday Pikachu, and baby Pokémon. Of the original 100 Gen II Pokémon, 8 babies are already in the game, roughly 12 may require evolution items, and 6 are presumably Legendaries being withheld. Screenshots suggest Pokémon genders, an evolve button previewing evolutions, and purchasable berries.

This MIT lecture by Lorna Gibson completes the topic of energy absorption in foams. Energy absorption diagrams are constructed from compressive stress-strain curves by plotting energy absorbed versus peak stress, both normalized by the solid modulus, on log-log scales. The "shoulder point" represents the most efficient use of the material, where maximum energy is absorbed at the plateau stress before densification. Diagrams can be generated from experiments or from models. For elastomeric foams, normalization by the solid modulus means one diagram represents all such foams; for foams with a yield point, diagrams are valid only for foams with the same ratio of solid yield strength to solid modulus. Equations are derived for the linear elastic region, stress plateau, densification, and the line connecting shoulder points.

Three design examples illustrate foam selection for impact protection: (1) an iterative method determines foam thickness (~0.15 m) and relative density (~0.01) for packaging a 0.5 kg object; (2) given a fixed thickness, the required solid modulus (28 MPa) and density (0.1) are found; (3) for bicycle helmets, expanded polystyrene at 5% density is selected, corresponding to a maximum impact speed of about 22 mph.

The lecture ends with a talk on woodpeckers: 1970s high-speed video showed impacts up to 1,500g. A scaling argument explains this through small brain size (factor of 8 in radius), brain orientation (factor of 2), and short impact duration (factor of 4). Woodpeckers also have stiff tail feathers and zygodactyl feet that aid pecking.

A December 15, 1917 progress report of the Inquiry briefly notes German peace plans and the President's determination to check them, then describes the Inquiry's organization. An Executive Committee of four oversees Division Chiefs, each with voluntary and paid assistants. Material is deposited with Dr. Mezes, edited by Mezes and Mr. Lippmann, and filed by librarian Andrew Keogh and cataloguer Miss Wilson using the Belgian Institute of Bibliography system. Collaborators are drawn from numerous universities and institutions, with operations housed at the American Geographical Society. Research aims to provide reliable material by February 15 on urgent problems: the region from the Baltic Sea to the Persian Gulf, Central Africa, the Central Powers' economic needs, and freedom of the seas. A compilation of official government declarations is complete; an examination of western press and periodical literature is underway, due around January 5.

Nutritional High International Inc. announced an extension of its US$800,000 secured note on its Pueblo, Colorado property with Veterans Capital Fund, LLC. The extension adds twelve months through April 18, 2018, maintains monthly interest payments at 13% per annum, includes a 1% renewal fee and 1% extension fee, extends 3,333,334 existing warrants (exercisable at CAD $0.06) to October 18, 2018, and issues 1,000,000 new warrants at CAD $0.15 expiring October 18, 2018. The Company also entered a term sheet for an Oregon Loan against its La Pine, Oregon property, with the principal set at the lesser of 85% of the appraised value or US$400,000, secured by a first charge over the property, bearing 13% annual interest over 18 months, and including up to 1,125,515 warrants at an exercise price of $0.165, subject to lender due diligence expected to be completed in May 2017. Nutritional High develops and distributes hemp and marijuana-infused products through licensed facilities; Veterans Capital is a Florida-based specialty finance company.

This email, forwarded by Eric Bass on October 5, 2000, contains the "Inside UT Football" newsletter from The Dallas Morning News, in which writer Chip Brown answers reader questions about Texas football. A hockey coach discusses a physical player who won't play tonight but remains useful, particularly on the power play, and notes Laddy skated lightly. Charleston is expected to revisit carriage horse heat rules; a proposal would let tours resume below 95 or heat index below 110 after 30 minutes. One company added body cameras.

The speaker said the team was frustrated after the loss but regrouped with a good practice. During the government shutdown, the federal judiciary will use funds not tied to a new congressional appropriation, such as court fee balances, to continue paid operations, with staff expected to be paid through Oct. 17. Federal judges' salaries are constitutionally protected. Most proceedings will continue, though hearings and filing dates may be rescheduled when executive-branch attorneys aren't working. The Supreme Court plans to rely on similar funds. At least 10 district courts have issued standing orders delaying some civil cases involving the federal government. When funds run out, courts will operate under the Antideficiency Act, with some staff possibly working without pay and others furloughed.

In this MIT lecture, Andrew Lo examines Lehman Brothers' 2007 financials—$19 billion in revenues, $4 billion net income, $145 billion in long-term capital, $282 billion in assets under management, and 28,500 employees—and its collapse nine months later, attributing it partly to a 16-to-1 net leverage ratio. Using mortgage examples, he explains how leverage magnifies losses when asset values fall, and discusses subprime mortgages, teaser rates, non-recourse loans, and the Fed's refusal to backstop Lehman, which led Barclays and Bank of America to decline a purchase and Lehman to file for Chapter 11. He notes Wall Street hiring will be disrupted for a few months but sees opportunities for students entering finance. The lecture then covers inflation, distinguishing nominal from real returns (real return approximately equals nominal return minus inflation), and introduces fixed income securities—treasury, federal agency, corporate, municipal, mortgage-backed, and complex instruments—whose markets dwarf equities. He describes market participants (issuers, intermediaries, investors), notes bonds trade less frequently than stocks, and recounts the 1987 market crash's effect on leveraged market makers. Finally, he explains bond valuation: coupon bonds pay fixed coupons plus principal at maturity and are priced via present value; pure discount bonds pay only face value at maturity and are priced by discounting; and STRIPS separate coupon and principal payments into individually traded discount bonds.

The U.S. Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to withhold $4 billion in foreign aid funds while Congress considers a rescission request under the Impoundment Control Act. The court found the government sufficiently showed the plaintiffs, including the ABA, weren't entitled to sue under the law or to mandamus relief, and that harms to foreign affairs outweighed plaintiffs' potential harms, though the decision is not a final determination on the merits. The case, decided on the emergency docket in two consolidated lawsuits, arose from a district court order requiring the government to spend $10.5 billion in foreign aid. Justices Kagan, Sotomayor, and Jackson dissented, with Kagan citing "uncharted territory" and high stakes.

More than 200 schools across North Wales are closed today after snow and ice caused disruption over the weekend. Councils closed schools over health and safety concerns after temperatures fell to -8C overnight, with snow-covered roads and black ice preventing staff and pupils from reaching schools. A yellow weather warning for ice across the region remains in place until 11am, with the Met Office warning of injuries from slips and falls on icy surfaces and potentially hazardous journeys due to lying snow. Boston University Summer Term offers over 700 undergraduate and graduate courses in 75+ subjects via open enrollment, with day, evening, and online six-week sessions, plus Pre-College Programs for high school students. Sessions run May 23–June 30 and July 3–August 11.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2015. Total revenues were $939.9 million, up from $620.5 million in the prior-year quarter, driven primarily by increased Model S deliveries. Gross margin improved to 27.7% from 25.0%. The company reported a net loss of $154.2 million ($1.22 per share), compared to $49.8 million ($0.40 per share) a year earlier, reflecting higher research and development expenses ($167.2 million) and selling, general and administrative expenses ($195.4 million). Cash and cash equivalents were $1.51 billion at quarter-end. Operating activities used $131.8 million in cash, investing activities used $432.3 million (including $426.1 million of capital expenditures), and financing activities provided $186.2 million. Tesla had delivered over 66,000 Model S vehicles cumulatively through March 31, 2015, and plans to begin Model X deliveries late in the third quarter of 2015 and introduce the Model 3 in 2017. The company expects approximately 55,000 Model S and X deliveries in 2015 and about $1.5 billion in capital expenditures for the year. The Gigafactory in Nevada had $146.2 million in construction costs incurred as of quarter-end. Tesla had $2.96 billion in convertible senior notes outstanding; the 2018 Notes became convertible in the second quarter of 2015, while the 2019 and 2021 Notes were not convertible. A securities class action dismissed in September 2014 is on appeal. Management concluded that disclosure controls and procedures were effective.

This email from Enron's internal communications manager compiles news coverage of Enron dated January 25, 2002. Key stories include: a New York Times report that Enron executives offered wealthy investors in the LJM2 partnership confidential inside information about the company's off-balance-sheet dealings; the search for a new CEO after Ken Lay's resignation, with Stephen Cooper of Zolfo Cooper reportedly meeting with Enron managers; mixed reactions from former employees to Lay's departure; allegations from ex-staffers that the Enron Energy Services division inflated profits by hundreds of millions of dollars; Jesse Jackson's planned rally in support of laid-off Enron workers; congressional interest in 401(k) rules prompted by employees' retirement losses; a chronology of the Enron-Andersen scandal, including Andersen's October 2001 document destruction and congressional hearings at which former auditor David Duncan invoked the Fifth Amendment; a federal judge's order barring Andersen from further shredding; a recommendation that Enron Australia be placed in liquidation, with creditors initially forecast to receive about 37 cents on the dollar; several book deals related to the collapse; and charities, including the United Way and Houston Ballet, adjusting to the loss of Enron's philanthropic giving, with a businessman donating $1 million to keep the Enron Boys & Girls Club open. Reader editorials criticized corporate greed and questioned whether other companies could hide similar problems.

The passage is from the Texas Instruments ADS9803 datasheet, an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition (DAQ) system. The device is initialized through a sequence of register writes after power-up or reset, requiring a free-running sampling clock. A speed-boost mode enables up to 8MSPS sampling for a user-selected analog input channel pair while the remaining six channels remain idle. Configuration uses an SPI interface with 16-bit registers organized in three banks addressed by 8-bit addresses; bank selection occurs via register 0x03, and register reads are enabled by setting the SPI_RD_EN and SPI_MODE bits. Multiple devices can be connected in a daisy-chain topology sharing CS and SCLK signals, with the chain length set by the DAISY_CHAIN_LEN register; register writes require N × 24 SCLKs. Register descriptions cover data format, averaging, XOR/PRBS operations, digital test patterns, gain error correction codes, analog input bandwidth, common-mode range, output lanes, and speed-boost configuration. For ATE applications, the ADS9803 achieves a post-calibration total unadjusted error (TUE) of 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C and offers low-noise (up to 22.7kHz) and wide-bandwidth (up to 700kHz) modes, with the latter settling to 99.95% full-scale in 7.5µs. The device uses three power supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, IOVDD) with no required power-up sequence. Layout guidance recommends placing bypass capacitors close to supply pins and keeping analog signals away from noise sources. The document concludes with support resources, ESD precautions, revision history, packaging information, and legal disclaimers.

Researchers created the OpenChart-SE citizen science project to address the lack of publicly available Swedish EHR text corpora for clinical NLP research. Swedish physicians and medical students wrote artificial EHRs for imagined emergency department patients using a Swedish mock EHR form modeled on systems used in the Scania region, hosted on GitHub. During the pilot phase (November 2021–December 2022), 50 artificial EHRs were collected, all of which passed quality control by an experienced emergency care physician and were released as OpenChart-SE corpus version 1 on Zenodo. The corpus covers varied scenarios: text lengths of 954–2738 characters, 12% priority one patients, 58% female and 21 male patients, ages 18–94 (mean 52), and no pediatric patients. The most frequent main diagnoses were abdominal pain (R10.4), ureteral calculus (N20.1), and dyspnea (R06.0). While the artificial data cannot yield clinical insights, it resembles real Swedish EHRs and serves as training and validation data for clinical NLP. The project's main phase opened in January 2023, with further quality-controlled data to be released periodically.

Particle has released an LTE-enabled module for product developers whose devices relied on retiring 2G and 3G networks, featuring built-in cloud and SIM support. The company says LTE hardware is cheaper, offers better battery life, and suits industrial devices, particularly dispersed sensor networks. The module is part of Particle's suite including a device cloud, operating system, and developer toolkit. The lineup includes two LTE CAT-M1 models powered by Qualcomm's MDM9206 modem and u-blox's Sara-R410-02B module. The evaluation kit costs $89; individual modules $69.

Light-field imaging captures complete 3D scenes in single snapshots by recording both the spatial and angular distribution of light rays, eliminating the scanning required by conventional 3D microscopy, which faces an inherent trade-off between imaging speed and signal-to-noise ratio. Its theoretical foundations trace back over a century to Lippmann's integral photography, Ives' multi-view recording methods, and Gershun's definition of the light field.

The plenoptic function, originally a 7D description of visual information, is typically reduced to a 4D light field, often expressed in a two-plane parameterization. Practical implementations use microlens or pinhole arrays in unfocused, focused, defocused, wavefront-coded, or Fourier configurations. While geometric optics provides a practical framework, wave-optics modeling is required for accurate reconstruction in high-numerical-aperture systems. Key rendering capabilities include computational refocusing, synthetic aperture imaging, multi-view outputs, and volumetric reconstruction.

In biomedicine, light-field microscopy (LFM) captures 4D datasets in single exposures, enabling high-speed volumetric imaging with reduced phototoxicity, with applications in functional brain imaging across model organisms and in single-cell imaging. Fourier light-field microscopy (FLFM/XLFM) samples spatial frequencies to overcome non-uniform sampling artifacts of conventional microlens-based methods. Light-field mesoscopy bridges microscopic and macroscopic scales, with systems such as MesoLF for mouse cortex imaging and miniature mesoscopes (CM2) for freely moving animals. Light-field endoscopy integrates light-field modules downstream of conventional endoscopes or replaces entrance optics with microlens, liquid crystal, electrowetting, or GRIN lens arrays, enabling 3D imaging in otoscopes, laryngoscopes, and micro-endoscopes; flexible fiber-bundle implementations face challenges in transmitting angular information.

Key challenges include the large data volume of 4D acquisition, addressed through compressive sensing, event-based cameras, and squeezed light-field microscopy (SLIM); inherent trade-offs among field of view, depth of field, and resolution, since light-field imaging redistributes rather than increases the space-bandwidth product; and reconstruction quality. Emerging directions include meta-optics, where metasurfaces enable resolution enhancement, extended depth of field, and compact integrated cameras, and deep learning-based reconstruction, spanning fully learned and hybrid physics-informed approaches that improve speed and reduce artifacts, though generalization and interpretability remain open challenges.

Carolina Panthers kicker Graham Gano, who missed three of four field goals in a loss to Tampa Bay, complained the Buccaneers' video board showed live footage of his kicks while displaying a solid red background for their kicker. A league official confirmed using a video board to distract an opposing kicker violates rules. Officials stopped play due to loud PA feedback before Gano missed a 45-yard attempt. Coach Ron Rivera criticized the board for twice showing a slow-motion replay of Thomas Davis hitting Russell Shepard.

A hockey player describes moving to a forward role, which allows more creativity and offense, while making room for linemates Mike and Jere and keeping his game simple. He calls the next game key for both clubs, expecting the opponent's best effort. He credits the team's shot-blocking culture and organizational depth, with reserve players ready to step in when injuries occur. Though leading the series, the team plans to take the remaining six periods one at a time.

This paper examines the need to optimize teacher education for 21st-century classrooms, focusing on technology integration, inclusive pedagogies, critical thinking, lifelong learning, and global challenges. It applies two theoretical frameworks: TPACK, which addresses the intersection of technology, pedagogy, and content knowledge, and constructivism, which emphasizes active, inquiry-based learning. The paper highlights preparing teachers for diverse learners through differentiated instruction and cultural competence, fostering collaboration through professional learning communities, and equipping educators to address global issues such as climate change and social justice. It concludes that teacher education is a continuous process requiring ongoing professional development and responsiveness to emerging research and trends.

On March 11, 2015, NVIDIA Corporation appointed Michael McCaffery and Persis Drell to its Board of Directors, with Mr. McCaffery also appointed to the Audit Committee. Under the 2007 Amended and Restated Equity Incentive Plan, each received an initial grant of 10,656 restricted stock units vesting semi-annually over three years beginning March 11, 2015, a pro-rated grant of 2,361 restricted stock units vesting in full on May 20, 2015, and a pro-rated annual cash retainer of $15,625 payable March 11, 2015.
