NVIDIA Tensor Cores, introduced in Volta, deliver an 8x peak mixed-precision speedup for deep learning matrix multiplication versus FP32. The Ampere-based A100 has more SMs (108 vs 80) and third-generation Tensor Cores with 16x higher peak mixed-precision performance, plus optimizations enhancing utilization and programmability while reducing complexity, bandwidth use, and latency. Ampere targets strong scaling, keeping GEMM tile sizes per SM unchanged despite 2.5x faster data consumption.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated March 15, 2021, reporting that effective that date, the titles of Elon Musk and Zach Kirkhorn changed to Technoking of Tesla and Master of Coin, respectively. Both will continue to serve as Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, respectively.

After 24-year-old Sana Bhat died of leukemia in February, her family's viral Facebook appeal—which raised $40,000 in a month—inspired a group of Srinagar businessmen to launch the #TwentyRupeesMiracle crowdfunding campaign. The campaign collects monthly donations of 20 rupees (about $0.30) for the Lalla Ded Charity, named after a 14th-century Kashmiri female poet. More than 50,000 donors worldwide signed up within days, and founders aim to reach 100,000 donors, yielding about $30,000 monthly. Cancer cases are rising in Kashmir, and 95% of patients in Jammu and Kashmir seek treatment at the government-run SKIMS, where costs range from $600 to $6,000—high against the region's $970 per capita income and India's underfunded public healthcare. The charity sends collected funds to credible groups such as Help Poor Voluntary Service and the Cancer Society of Kashmir, which helped 18-year-old patient Towseef Ahmad Bhat, whose health has since improved. Sana's sister views the charity as a tribute to her sister's battle.

Tom Lee, chairman of digital asset treasury company BitMine, says the bubble in digital asset treasuries (DATs)—firms that hoard cryptocurrency and offer publicly traded shares providing exposure to it—may have already burst. Lee, formerly JPMorgan's chief strategist and founder of Fundstrat, became BitMine's chair in June as the Bitcoin mining company rebranded to become the largest institutional holder of Ethereum, following the model Michael Saylor pioneered with MicroStrategy and Bitcoin. BitMine, with a market capitalization above $15 billion, holds over 3 million Ethereum tokens, about 2.5% of total supply, with a goal of 5%. Lee argues Ethereum remains the "blockchain of Wall Street" and that BitMine offers advantages such as staking rewards and stock index inclusion, but notes many DATs now trade below their net asset value.

The Italian stock market has stagnated, with the IT 40 index—comprising the 40 largest companies on Borsa Italiana, including Monclear, Pirelli, Tenaris, Ferrari, and Campari—trading at the same level as in 1998. Using the dividend-adjusted ETF EWI, the article backtests seasonal strategies. Italian stocks perform best on Tuesdays and Wednesdays, with Thursdays slightly positive, Fridays flat, and Mondays performing poorly. An end-of-the-month strategy achieved a 6.17% CAGR versus 4.71% for buy-and-hold while investing only one-third of the time. March and June are the best months, while May is the worst. The article concludes that the Italian stock market shows strong seasonality.

This passage from the MSPM0G3519/G3518/G1519/G1518 datasheet describes several peripheral features: a Keystore for secure AES key storage (up to 4 keys, 128- or 256-bit), a CRC module supporting CRC16-CCITT and CRC32-ISO3309, and a MATHACL hardware math accelerator. Communication peripherals include UART, I2C (supporting Standard, Fast, and Fast-mode Plus up to 1 Mbit/s, plus SMBus 3.0), SPI (up to 32 Mbit/s), and CAN-FD compliant with ISO 11898-1:2015 up to 5 Mbit/s. The Low-Frequency Sub System (LFSS_B) contains an RTC_B real-time clock with alarms, calibration, and compensation features, plus an independent watchdog timer (IWDT); a windowed watchdog (WWDT) is also provided. Timer peripherals include general-purpose (TIMGx) and advanced (TIMAx) types with PWM, dead-band insertion, and fault handling. The device also provides an IOMUX for pin configuration, a serial wire debug interface, and a bootstrap loader (BSL) protected by a 256-bit user-defined password for programming via UART or I2C. A memory-mapped FACTORY region stores read-only device identification and trim data. Application guidance recommends decoupling capacitors, an NRST pullup circuit, and an external resistor for SYSOSC frequency correction. The document further covers TI development tools (Code Composer Studio, Keil, IAR, SysConfig), device nomenclature distinguishing experimental (X) from production (MSP) devices, documentation and support resources, ESD handling precautions, a revision history detailing changes from November 2024 to April 2025, and mechanical packaging information.

Fiat is celebrating the 60th anniversary of the Fiat 500 and of the 500 Jolly "Spiaggina", its first special series from 1958, with the new Fiat 500 "Spiaggina '58", a limited edition of 1,958 convertible cars. The model features exclusive Volare Blue livery with ivory soft-top, vintage Fiat logos, 16-inch alloy wheels, a two-tone interior, and standard connectivity including a Uconnect 7-inch HD LIVE touchscreen with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto compatibility. The passage contains 1902 State Department documents. Officers preferring charges against other officers must communicate them confidentially to the Department of State, which will dispose of the case at its discretion. On May 20, 1902, Secretary Hay informed Mr. Lord that US military occupation of Cuba had ceased and an independent republican government under President Tomás Estrada Palma had been inaugurated. On May 24, Hay instructed Lord to ask Argentina to permit US consular officers to represent Cuban interests until Cuban consuls were appointed. An October 22, 1902 circular, following the act of June 14, 1902, authorized diplomatic and consular officers to issue passports to loyal residents of US insular possessions—Porto Rico, the Philippine Islands, and Guam—who declared allegiance to the United States and provided affidavits from two witnesses, with the same fee charged as for citizens.

The GST Council fixed a 0.1 per cent tax rate on goods procured for export, with refunds available to merchant exporters. It extended AA/EPCG/EOU schemes to foreign and domestic sourcing, exempted IGST and cess on imports, treated domestic supplies to scheme holders as deemed exports, and allowed specified banks and PSUs to import gold without IGST. A goaltender praised his team's defensive play and net-front battling, admitted rebounds made things difficult for himself, and admired another goaltender's ability to elevate his game in the playoffs.

The City of Bisbee petitioned for a writ of mandamus to compel Cochise County, its treasurer, and its board of supervisors to pay $2,730.86 in penalties and fees collected on delinquent city taxes between 1918 and 1928, which the treasurer had deposited into the county general fund instead of remitting to the city. The trial court sustained demurrers and dismissed the action, and the city appealed. The Supreme Court held that mandamus was a proper remedy against the treasurer, who holds such funds in trust for the city, but not against the county or the supervisors, since the money was never legally county property and no claim or board order was required. The court also held it immaterial that the current treasurer had not held office during the entire period, as retiring treasurers are presumed to have turned over funds to their successors. Construing the 1913 and 1917 statutes together, the court concluded that fees, costs, interest, and penalties collected on delinquent city taxes belonged to the city and had to be paid over to it. The one-year statute of limitations did not bar the claim, because such funds are held in trust and limitations run only from a clear repudiation; the suit was brought within a year of the treasurer's 1931 refusal to pay. However, a 1931 statute directed that interest, penalties, charges, and fees on delinquent taxes be credited to the county general fund, so the city was entitled only to amounts collected through June 13, 1931. The judgment was reversed and remanded, with instructions to overrule the demurrer as to the treasurer.

This manual for the SanDisk Sansa Fuze player covers basic operation, including the Hold Switch that locks all buttons, the non-replaceable rechargeable battery and its charging methods (USB, AC adapter, or car adapter), power on/off/reset functions, and thumbwheel navigation. It explains connecting the player to a computer, updating firmware, and formatting the device. Music, photos, and videos can be transferred via drag-and-drop, Windows Media Player, or Sansa Media Converter. The manual details playing music, audiobooks, videos, and photos; using the FM radio with up to 30 presets; voice recording; deleting content; and customizing settings such as wallpaper, backlight, language, and USB mode. A troubleshooting section addresses common issues, followed by SanDisk's one-year limited warranty and the End User License Agreement terms.

World stocks neared record highs and the dollar rose for an 11th straight day after Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen signaled a possible U.S. interest rate hike in March. MSCI's global equity index rose 0.25 percent to its highest level since May 2015. European stocks gained, led by banks, with Credit Agricole up over 3 percent after better-than-expected earnings, while Goldman Sachs hit a record high. Asia-Pacific shares and Japan's Nikkei also rose. The dollar index reached 101.220, while sterling slid 0.5 percent on weak UK wage growth data. In 2018, over 5,000 Maharashtra HSC students scored above 90 per cent. Among differently-abled students at NGO Niwant Andh Mukta Vidyasalaya, Kshirsagar Kedar Kailas topped the school with 80.15 per cent and aims to take the IAS exam, while Vanshika Joshi scored 70.77 per cent despite a leg deformity. Akash Dhindle topped with 79.23 per cent despite a 10-hour job, and 30-year-old delivery agent Vitthal Ishwarkatti scored 75 per cent after an 11-year break.

AggregateIQ executives Zack Massingham and Jeff Silvester told a Canadian House of Commons committee that the firm is not a subsidiary or department of Cambridge Analytica, disputing Christopher Wylie's claim that it functioned "like a franchise" of the company and that he helped set it up. They said AggregateIQ never had access to Facebook data allegedly improperly obtained by Cambridge Analytica, does not harvest data, and refused to distribute a violent video during Nigeria's 2015 election. Silvester said the firm worked with four pro-Brexit groups—Vote Leave, BeLeave, Veterans for Britain and the DUP—and was paid by Vote Leave for work done for BeLeave (over £625,000) and Veterans for Britain (£100,000). He said there was no evidence of coordination between the campaigns and that the unusual payment arrangement was investigated and deemed legal.

The passage outlines defensive strategies against the Side Screen Offense, in which a "Big" screens for a "Small," creating risks of dribble penetration and post-up mismatches. The Basic NBA Show & Recover is the preferred NBA tactic, since switching would allow the screener to post up against a smaller defender; it involves the screener's defender stepping out hard to force the ballhandler wide, then recovering to the post once the on-ball defender re-establishes position. Some teams instead slide through the screen or "Jam" the screener. SOS Disruption provides three scenarios: above the free throw line, an aggressive contact switch, snuggle pass denial, and smother are used; below the free throw line, a baseline trap with "Triangle I" coverage is employed; and All-Out Disruption traps the point guard before the screen is set, forcing the offense into freelance play. A secondary trap covers passes to the screener on the base roll, with all rotations occurring as the ball leaves the passer's hands.

The Software carries restricted rights for Government use under FAR and DFARS. SanDisk may terminate the Agreement for violations, requiring deletion of all Software copies. The Software is not fault-tolerant and is not intended for high risk activities; SanDisk disclaims liability for such use. The Agreement is governed by California and U.S. federal law, with exclusive jurisdiction in Santa Clara County courts. Exports must comply with U.S. regulations. The device should not be disposed of with unsorted household waste; consult local waste authorities.

Hubble has released a new image of NGC 2775, a galaxy 67 million light-years away in the constellation Cancer that is difficult to classify. It has a smooth, gas-free center resembling an elliptical galaxy and a dusty ring of star clusters like a spiral galaxy, leading researchers to classify it as either a spiral or lenticular galaxy. A hydrogen gas tail stretching nearly 100,000 light-years suggests past galactic mergers may explain its unusual appearance. The new image adds observations of red light emitted by hydrogen gas around massive young stars.

A line formed Saturday before the 9 a.m. opening of the Crossroads of the West Gun Show at the Del Mar Fairgrounds, while about 80 protesters gathered nearby in orange T-shirts carrying signs against gun violence and bearing the names of the 17 people killed in the Parkland, Fla., school shooting. Protest organizer Rose Ann Sharp said students are now telling adults they have not done enough. Show owner Bob Templeton expected 8,000 to 10,000 attendees at $16 per ticket, slightly more than previous years, which he attributed to the gun debate. California gun show purchases require a background check and 10-day waiting period. The show ends Sunday at 5 p.m.

Skinimalism is a skincare trend focused on streamlining routines to a few high-quality, essential products rather than complex multi-step regimens. According to Dr Hazel Parkinson, it involves choosing targeted, multitasking products that respect the skin barrier instead of layering multiple actives that may clash or cause irritation. Benefits include protecting the skin's natural barrier, reducing irritation and sensitivity, relieving pressure from marketing-driven ideals of a "perfect" routine, and offering a more sustainable, budget-friendly approach. However, skinimalism is not suitable for everyone: people with acne or pigmentation may still need specific ingredients such as retinoids or azelaic acid, though not necessarily alongside many other steps. For conditions like rosacea or a compromised skin barrier, simplified routines using gentle cleansers, barrier-supporting moisturisers, and minimal actives are recommended. Those transitioning from longer routines should eliminate one or two products at a time, allowing 2–4 weeks for the skin to adapt, and tailor routines to their age, lifestyle, and skin needs.

This study presents a field-deployable metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) protocol for detecting SARS-CoV-2 in clinical swab samples using Oxford Nanopore Technology. The protocol combines sample pretreatment (DNase I treatment followed by 0.22 µM filtration), nucleic acid extraction, random amplification, and untargeted sequencing. Testing on 16 pooled SARS-CoV-2-positive oropharyngeal swab samples showed that combined DNase-filtration pretreatment increased SARS-CoV-2 BLAST hits from 31.8% (no treatment) to 99.9%, achieving over 50% reference genome coverage within 10 minutes of sequencing. For 14 individual positive samples (Delta variant), all samples with CT-values ≤30 achieved high reference coverage (85.8–100%), while samples with CT ≥33 reached only 40–60.5%. All samples were typed as clade 21J (Delta), with Pangolin sub-lineages identified for samples with CT <33. The protocol was designed to avoid specialized equipment such as centrifuges and thermal cyclers, making it suitable for mobile or field laboratories. Limitations include testing on only one virus type and reduced sensitivity compared to RT-qPCR, likely because the method detects only extracellular viral RNA. The authors conclude this approach may enable rapid virus identification at the point of incidence in animal and human swab samples.

A ranch manager discovered a new elasmosaur species—a carnivorous marine reptile—in northeastern Montana's Charles M. Russell National Wildlife Refuge in November 2010 while hunting elk. The well-preserved, nearly complete fossil took three days to excavate. The smaller creature suggests elasmosaurs evolved longer necks over millions of years. An inland sea once teemed with marine reptiles, but few fossils have been excavated due to research bias favoring land dinosaurs.

Oral communication among soccer players during games is critical to success. Because of the game's fast pace, short words or phrases ("calls") are used, and these must be immediately recognizable and understood by every player, along with the actions to take. Players without the ball speak most often, since they have better views of the action—especially those behind the ball, who are best positioned to direct play. Calls are presented at age-appropriate intervals and range from introductory to advanced, covering receiving, dribbling, defense, and offensive tactics. Some calls share the same meaning; coaches may choose which to use, but all players should know all terms. Categories apply to all field players, with additional calls specific to the Defensive Organizer and goalkeepers. Coaches are advised to develop age-appropriate team vocabulary, consider non-verbal communication for crowd noise, and use decoy calling.

The Centre told the Supreme Court it would grant revised pension benefits to all Major Generals and equivalent ranks, including pre-2006 retirees. The court directed compliance within three months and disposed of a contempt plea seeking One Rank One Pension implementation.

A Consumer Reports investigation published Oct. 14 found that more than two-thirds of 23 popular protein powders and shakes tested in the U.S. contained more lead per serving than CR's food safety experts consider safe for a full day. Naked Nutrition's Vegan Mass Gainer contained 7.7 micrograms of lead—1,572% of CR's level of concern—and Huel Black Edition contained 6.3 micrograms, or 1,288%. Plant-based powders were the most contaminated category, averaging about nine times the lead found in dairy proteins like whey, because plants absorb heavy metals from soil; processing can further intensify contamination. Lead levels were higher than in CR's previous testing in 2010. As dietary supplements, protein powders face limited oversight: there is no federal lead limit, the FDA does not approve supplements before sale, and it inspected only 600 of 12,000 registered manufacturers last year. CR's Paris Martineau said most people do not need protein powder, noting the recommended 0.8 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight daily is easily obtained from whole foods, and most Americans already exceed protein needs.

Bank employees have alleged unethical tactics to meet sales targets, and advisors face production pressure, including layoffs for missing revenue thresholds. The author proposes three reforms: tie advisor incentives to client satisfaction rather than sales (as Sun Life is doing by linking 25% of bonuses to client satisfaction), compensate advisors for recommending against purchases, such as through base salaries, and require minimum education standards like a degree. These changes would support client-first advice and improve the industry's reputation.

A hockey coach addresses reporters after a playoff loss to Calgary, saying he has not yet met with his team. Regarding an incident involving Danny, he states no one was hurt and insurance will cover the damage. He acknowledges Calgary deserved the win and played as the best team in the western conference, while his team was nonchalant and lacked the needed tenaciousness. He praises Marty's performance, noting an early missed chance that could have changed the game, and expects him to score consistently soon. He rejects the "must win" label, saying every game should be approached the same way. He emphasizes the needed fix is mindset rather than tactical adjustments—respecting the opponent and responding instead of dwelling on losses. He credits team leadership and maturing young players for maintaining an even keel, and expresses confidence that Nikolai Khabibulin will be their best player and lead the response in the next game.

This passage is an email dated July 18, 2001, from Jean Munoz containing a compilation of news articles about California's energy crisis:

- **NPR report**: California is expediting power plant permitting under Governor Davis's emergency directive, permitting 450 megawatts in 21 days, but will fall short of the goal of 5,000 new megawatts by July 1, with only 2,500 megawatts expected online. Blackouts are described as a near certainty this summer.

- **AP/LA Times**: PG&E sued California seeking reimbursement for energy contracts seized by Governor Davis in January; the state valued them at $150-160 million, while the Power Exchange priced them at $347 million.

- **Contra Costa Times**: PG&E's 20/20 rebate program has produced $7.6 million in savings, with 29% of customers processed so far qualifying for the 20% discount by reducing energy use.

- **LA Times**: Duke Energy reported a 27% increase in second-quarter profit, driven by trading and wholesale power businesses.

- **Orange County Register**: Governor Davis is leveraging the energy crisis for national political advantage, aided by consultants Mark Fabiani and Chris Lehane.

- **San Francisco Chronicle**: Lawmakers are debating competing bailout plans for Southern California Edison to avoid bankruptcy before an August 15 deadline.

- **Chicago Tribune editorial**: Criticizes the Bush administration's energy policy, noting market forces eased predicted price spikes and California's intervention may carry long-term economic costs.

Intermediate attacking runs in soccer build on individual runs by creating opportunities for both the runner and teammates, while retaining basic concepts like recognizing opportunities, timing, and communication. Individual runs include the back-door run (looping behind the defense), drifting, doubling back, holding the run, recycled runs, and setting up a defender. Runs can also draw opponents away from teammates, such as decoy runs, drawing or dragging opponents, dropping the ball, and dummy runs. Offensive switches with teammates involve exchanging positions, either "called" (using oral communication) or "natural" (occurring during normal play). These include the basic horizontal switch (diagonal runs forming an X pattern), vertical switches (back-to-front or front-to-back exchanges), and cross-over exchanges where a dribbler passes to a stationary teammate and sprints into open space. Coaching tips emphasize being prepared to receive passes, anticipating the next move, and going to the ball.

U.S. workers' wages and benefits grew 2.6 percent last year, the fastest 12-month pace since spring 2015 and up from 2.2 percent the prior year. President Trump cited the wage growth as an economic accomplishment, but private economists contend wages should be rising faster given unemployment at a 17-year low of 4.1 percent.

The passage reviews ten AI tools designed to automate tasks, improve workflow, and increase productivity. ChatGPT generates human-like text for tasks like translation and question answering, though it may produce biased or inaccurate content. DALL-E generates images from text prompts using GPT-3 architecture. Lumen5 helps create videos and social media content, while Grammarly checks grammar and improves writing clarity. OpenAI Codex creates code from natural language descriptions, and Tabnine suggests code snippets to improve coding efficiency. Jasper AI assists with content writing, and Surfer SEO helps optimize websites through audits, keyword research, and backlink analysis. Zapier automates repetitive tasks by connecting web applications, and Compose AI generates text from structured data. The passage concludes that these tools should be used with care, reviewed before use, and treated as aids rather than replacements for human knowledge.

The FDA approved another generic version of the mifepristone abortion pill, allowing three U.S. companies to produce it and drawing pushback from anti-abortion groups and politicians aligned with the Trump administration. The approval is unlikely to affect access; the pill, typically taken with misoprostol, accounts for roughly two-thirds of U.S. abortions. Amgen reported its cholesterol-lowering shot Repatha prevented heart disease death, heart attack, and the most common type of stroke in a 12,000-patient trial, which could help the drug reach a broader market. The Trump administration also delayed closing a loophole that exempts some drugs from Medicare price negotiation.

Players praised a teammate's timely goals and composure, saying he belongs and is key to their success. They emphasized maintaining speed in the third period, aided by Pekka's saves and an empty-net goal. One called the win his best birthday gift. Success was credited to depth players like Freddy, Sissons, Jarnkrok, and Fiddler, with focus on improving as the series continues.

US manufacturing and services firms expect a stronger economy and rising revenue into 2018, according to an Institute of Supply Management survey. Manufacturing revenues are projected to rise 7.8 per cent, with services expecting a six per cent increase. Over 60 per cent of firms report difficulty finding workers, leading many to raise wages. Employment, capital expenditures, and labor costs are expected to increase, while material costs rise only slightly.

Apple Inc.'s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2017 reports that the California corporation (established 1977, headquartered in Cupertino) designs, manufactures and markets mobile communication and media devices, personal computers, and related software, services, and accessories, including iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, iOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, iCloud, and Apple Pay. In 2017, the company introduced iPhone 8 and 8 Plus, announced iPhone X, and released iOS 11, macOS High Sierra, watchOS 4, Apple TV 4K, and Apple Watch Series 3. The company manages its business on a geographic basis across five reportable segments: Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan, and Rest of Asia Pacific. In 2017, direct channels accounted for 28% and indirect channels 72% of net sales; domestic sales were 37% and international sales 63%. No single customer exceeded 10% of net sales in 2015–2017. R&D expense was $11.6 billion in 2017. Substantially all hardware is manufactured by outsourcing partners primarily in Asia. As of September 30, 2017, the company had approximately 123,000 full-time equivalent employees. Risk factors include global economic conditions, intense competition, reliance on single or limited-source suppliers, dependence on outsourcing partners, legal proceedings, data security, and tax matters. The company paid $12.6 billion in dividends in 2017, and its share repurchase authorization was increased to $210 billion, with $44 billion remaining as of September 30, 2017.

The author criticizes Jerry Coyne's post claiming new evidence for the multiverse, based mainly on a YouTube video citing NASA and ESA satellite data. Coyne seeks a multiverse with varied physical laws to counter the theological fine-tuning argument, but the author argues the inflation models cited do not lead to such a multiverse. The author also notes David Gross's Nobel Week Dialogue talk on truth and the scientific method, asserting science will survive Trump.

Gatwick Airport recorded its busiest July ever, with 4.7 million passengers, up 2.4%, marking 53 consecutive months of growth. Long-haul traffic rose 10.7% and cargo 20.4%. New routes to California and China are growing, with additional destinations including Denver, Seattle, Taipei, and Singapore launching soon.

James Walker Morales, 35, escaped Saturday from the Wyatt Detention Center in Central Falls, R.I., by climbing a basketball hoop, cutting through fencing, and descending from the roof. His absence was discovered three and a half hours later; two correctional officers were placed on administrative leave. Morales, a former Army reservist held for allegedly stealing firearms from a Worcester armory, is believed to have fled to Attleboro, stolen a car, and been injured by razor wire.

A study by Ombudsman Services found one in five rail passengers in Britain is resigned to poor service, with rail complaints rising 31% to two million last year. The most common complaints were punctuality, customer service and overcrowding. MP Tim Loughton has proposed a rail ombudsman, while the Department for Transport said £40 billion is being invested in railways. The Rail Delivery Group acknowledged service issues but noted long-term complaints are falling. Overall consumer complaints reached 55 million, with transport accounting for 7%.

Rockefeller scientists led by Shai Shaham discovered an unusual cell-death process in the tail-spike cell of C. elegans, a microscopic worm. Postdoctoral fellow Piya Ghose observed that the cell's core is severed from its extension and disintegrates, while the extension vanishes in two steps: the proximal part breaks into bead-shaped bits, and the distal part retracts into a ball that is removed by a neighboring cell. The same process was observed in a worm neuron, suggesting similar death events may occur in many animals and possibly human disease. The team also found that the protein EFF-1 helps phagocytes seal around dead cell remnants. The findings were published in Nature Cell Biology.

U.S. hedge funds were active in FAANG stocks in the second quarter, regulatory filings showed. Daniel Loeb's Third Point increased its stakes in Alphabet and Facebook, while Leon Cooperman's Omega Advisors cut stakes in Facebook, Netflix, and Amazon but kept its Alphabet holding unchanged, which Cooperman called his biggest position. Separately, Jana Partners raised its Whole Foods stake and profited by selling after Amazon agreed to acquire the grocer for $13.7 billion.

The U.S. government was on track to shut down after midnight Tuesday as Republicans and Democrats remained deadlocked over a funding deal. The Congressional Budget Office estimated a shutdown would furlough about 750,000 federal employees, with daily compensation costs of roughly $400 million. House Speaker Mike Johnson blamed Democrats, who are demanding an extension of enhanced Affordable Care Act tax credits set to expire at the end of 2025, while Republicans push for a "clean" funding bill. Johnson accused Democrats of seeking federal health benefits for undocumented immigrants, which House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries denied as an "outright lie," noting federal law prohibits taxpayer-funded coverage for undocumented individuals. Jeffries said Republicans would bear responsibility for a shutdown.

A hockey coach says the league did not rule a play as a kick, though he felt there was a kicking motion, and accepts the officials' decision. He acknowledges the Ottawa Senators outworked his team, says discipline was an issue and frustration showed in the third period with penalties, and notes his team played far below its capabilities yet still had a chance to win. He credits Ottawa's lesser-known players for stepping up and expects his team to regroup and refocus. All players are available, but the coaching staff must decide whether Chris Kunitz, cleared by doctors after a lower body injury unrelated to a previous one, will play. Conditioning is a concern given the demanding Stanley Cup Final environment, though Kunitz worked hard off the ice. Kunitz is described as a physical, hardworking top-line winger with an excellent shot, though its quality after a hand injury is uncertain. The coach praises under-the-radar defensemen like O'Donnell and checking center Samuel Pahlsson, along with Moen and Niedermayer, for elevating their play, and calls the next game the most important yet.

This patent application, a continuation of prior applications by inventor Tony M. Brewer, concerns configurable computing circuitry, specifically a heterogeneous computing system with configurable computing circuitry, an embedded interconnection network, dynamic reconfiguration, and dynamic control over energy or power consumption. It addresses limits of existing computing systems in computation speed, energy consumption, and heat dissipation, and the need for high-performance, energy-efficient architectures for compute-intensive kernels such as FFTs and FIR filters used in applications including synthetic aperture radar, 5G base stations, graph analytics, machine learning, and stencil codes.

The disclosed embodiments provide a multi-threaded, coarse-grained configurable computing architecture capable of self-scheduling, dynamic self-configuration and self-reconfiguration, conditional branching, backpressure control for asynchronous signaling, ordered and loop thread execution with data dependencies, automatic thread start upon completion of dependencies, loop access to private variables, and use of thread identifiers for nested loops. Representative circuits comprise a configurable computation circuit, synchronous network inputs and outputs, and a configuration memory including a first instruction memory storing data path configuration instructions and a second instruction and instruction index ("spoke") memory storing spoke instructions and indices for selecting master synchronous inputs and current or next data path instructions. Further embodiments include control circuits with memory control, thread control, and control registers storing loop tables, completion tables, thread identifier pools, and thread identifier stacks; conditional logic circuits for branching; flow control circuits generating stop signals; and continuation, reenter, priority, and run queues for ordering thread execution.

System embodiments include arrays of configurable circuits ("tiles") coupled to synchronous and asynchronous packet networks, and hybrid computing systems comprising a RISC-V-based, multi-threaded hybrid threading processor, hybrid threading fabric (HTF) circuits and clusters, memory interfaces, dispatch interfaces, and optional network interfaces. HTF clusters contain tiles interconnected by a synchronous mesh communication network forming synchronous domains and an asynchronous packet network carrying control messages such as completion and continuation messages. Tiles include multiply and shift and arithmetic, logical and bit operation circuits, instruction and spoke RAMs, tile memories, and control circuitry. The synchronous network carries data, instruction RAM addresses, thread identifiers (TIDs), and transfer identifiers (XIDs).

The passage covers several sections of the MSPM0G3519/G3518/G1519/G1518 datasheet. The IOMUX manages peripheral function selection on digital IOs, along with output drivers, input paths, and wake-up logic from SHUTDOWN mode. A serial wire debug (SWD) two-wire interface via an ARM-compatible SW-DP enables debug functions. The bootstrap loader (BSL) supports device configuration and memory programming through UART or I2C, protected by a 256-bit user-defined password, and can be disabled; it is invoked during boot via the BSL_invoke pin, automatically on blank devices, or at runtime via software command. A memory-mapped FACTORY region provides read-only device capability and trim data, including DEVICEID and USERID registers. Application guidance recommends decoupling capacitors on VDD/VSS, an NRST pullup resistor and capacitor, a 100kΩ FCL reference resistor, a 0.47µF VCORE tank capacitor, and pullup resistors for 5V-tolerant open-drain IOs. The document also describes development tools (CCS, IAR, Keil, TI Arm-Clang, GNU Arm), device nomenclature (X for experimental, MSP for production devices), documentation and support resources, ESD handling precautions, revision history changes from November 2024 to April 2025, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

A Lewisville mother works as a paid mystery shopper. Contrave, combining bupropion and naltrexone, is FDA-approved for obese or overweight people with a BMI of 27 or higher. Consumer Reports found only modest weight loss—five to nine pounds versus placebo—and risks including anxiety, insomnia, headaches, liver damage, seizures, and heart problems. Experts advise diet, exercise, and behavioral programs.

Penn State and USC meet for the 10th time—their third Rose Bowl and fourth bowl meeting—with USC leading 5-4. The Pac-12 is 49-43-3 all-time in the Rose Bowl; the Big Ten is 31-37-0. The 1923 Penn State-USC game was the first played at the current Rose Bowl Stadium and the first officially called the Rose Bowl Game. Hugo Bezdek, Penn State's 1923 coach, is the only coach to lead three teams to the Rose Bowl. Penn State has allowed the two greatest passing performances in Rose Bowl history: Danny O'Neil's 456 yards in 1995 and Mark Sanchez's 413 in 2009. Since 1952, 20 players have rushed for 150 yards, but only seven play-by-play broadcasters have called the game. USC has appeared in the Rose Bowl during every presidency since 1929. Penn State will tie Pittsburgh's four Rose Bowl appearances.

Facebook has publicly released its Community Guidelines, which describe what content the company will remove when alerted by users. The document, grounded in principles of safety, voice, and equity, is a manual of adjudication for deciding on individual posts. Content moderator Rochelle LaPlante praised its transparency and detail. The guidelines mix broad rules with oddly specific provisions—such as extensive crisis-actor language and a "too young to stand" clause—apparently shaped by reactions to news events and decisions made in regular internal meetings.

Point72 Europe London LLP purchased a new position in Hershey Company (NYSE:HSY) in the second quarter, buying 10,000 shares valued at approximately $1,074,000. Other funds also adjusted stakes: Sun Life Financial increased its position by 12,637.5%, QCI Asset Management by 10.8%, and Independent Portfolio Consultants by 139.5%, while Fiduciary Trust and Invictus RG opened new positions. Institutional investors own 51.39% of the stock. Analysts issued mixed ratings; Sanford C. Bernstein upgraded the stock to "outperform" with a $127 price target, while Morgan Stanley set an "equal weight" rating with a $108 target. The stock carries a consensus "Hold" rating and $111.55 consensus target price. Insiders Michele Buck and D Michael Wege recently sold shares, and insiders own 0.92% of the company. The stock traded down 0.08% to $108.83, with a market cap of $23.12 billion and a P/E ratio of 34.77. Hershey reported quarterly EPS of $1.09, beating estimates, on revenue of $1.66 billion, and declared a $0.656 quarterly dividend yielding 2.41%.

The paper reports low-temperature properties of YbCu1.14Se2, an exchange-disordered triangular-lattice magnet related to the AYbSe2 quantum spin liquid (QSL) candidate series. Motivated by Anderson's 1973 QSL prediction and the controversial role of disorder in candidate materials such as YbMgGaO4, the authors synthesized single crystals via the self-flux technique, obtaining consistently off-stoichiometric YbCu1.14Se2. Single-crystal x-ray diffraction shows Yb ions form a well-ordered triangular lattice separated from disordered, partially occupied Cu sites (56.6±0.7% occupancy versus an expected 50%), with no ordered Cu vacancies. Magnetic susceptibility confirms well-defined Yb3+ moments with antiferromagnetic exchange. Specific heat shows no magnetic ordering transition and sub-linear behavior (C ∝ T^0.95 up to 1 K), inconsistent with magnon or Fermi-surface descriptions; the data are modeled by a distribution of singlet-triplet gaps from disordered quantum singlets. Ultra-low-temperature AC susceptibility reveals a frequency-dependent peak near Tf ≈ 0.1 K, characteristic of spin-glass freezing, and no 1/3 magnetization plateau, indicating a significant departure from the ideal 2D triangular Heisenberg model. The behavior closely resembles YbMgGaO4 and matches theoretical simulations of disordered triangular magnets, suggesting possible universal behavior of disordered QSL materials.

A 92-year-old woman, Anna Mae Blessing, was arrested on suspicion of murdering her 72-year-old son, allegedly over his plan to place her in an assisted living facility. She was taken into custody at their suburban Phoenix home and held on US$500,000 bail. Blessing told detectives she hid two handguns in her robe and shot her son multiple times.

Mark Messier and a Bridgestone representative announced the winner of the fourth annual Bridgestone Youth Leadership Award: Robert "Knobby" Knudsen, who overcame difficult early circumstances to become an advocate for children, founding the Kids Skate for Kids program with the Windsor minor hockey association. His son Robert Knudsen Jr. and grandson Matt Knudsen accepted the award, with his son sharing a quote his father lived by about being important in the life of a child.

The three finalists for the Mark Messier Leadership Award were also announced: Dustin Brown of the Los Angeles Kings, Shane Doan of the Phoenix Coyotes, and Ryan Callahan of the New York Rangers, with winners to be named at the awards show in Las Vegas.

In a question-and-answer session, Messier praised Dustin Brown's charity work and maturity as a young captain, recalled how difficult every Stanley Cup playoff run was regardless of record, reflected on an epic conference final series against the Devils and Martin Brodeur, credited rule changes with restoring speed and skill to the game, noted the emergence of young talent, and discussed the Rangers' season, saying deep playoff experience was a valuable lesson, the team needs to add depth going forward, and Marian Gaborik has continued to improve since joining the Rangers.

Christian Bushman survived a May 2014 cardiac arrest after her sister-in-law, CPR instructor Cathy Carson, performed CPR on her. Seventy percent of out-of-hospital cardiac arrests occur in homes. A recent study found women are less likely than men to receive bystander CPR. Bushman has since learned and taught CPR herself.

In his inaugural address, the speaker accepts the nation's first executive office with humility, acknowledging the task exceeds his talents and relying on the wisdom of fellow constitutional authorities. He calls for unity after the contested election, declaring "We are all Republicans, we are all Federalists," and affirms that majority rule must be reasonable while minorities possess equal rights under the law. He warns against political intolerance, comparing it to religious persecution, and defends republican government as the strongest on earth. He advocates a wise and frugal government that restrains people from injuring one another while leaving them otherwise free. He lists essential principles: equal justice, peace and honest friendship with all nations without entangling alliances, support of state governments, the right of election, a well-disciplined militia, civil supremacy over military authority, economy in public expense, honest payment of debts, encouragement of agriculture and commerce, freedom of religion, press, and person, and trial by jury. He asks for the people's confidence and indulgence, pledging faithful service and readiness to retire when a better choice is available.

This paper proposes a class of bivariate zero-inflated Poisson (BZIP) models for multivariate count data exhibiting excess zeros, motivated by applications such as insurance claim counts. The model generates correlated zero-inflated Poisson variables through a common Bernoulli inflation factor applied to a latent pair of counts, which follows either a comonotonic or counter-monotonic shock bivariate Poisson model, permitting both positive and negative dependence. The dependence structure is governed by two parameters: the inflation rate ϕ and the dependence parameter θ. The proposed models satisfy the PQD ordering, and the positive-dependence model attains the upper Fréchet-Hoeffding bound when θ = 1. Estimation is addressed through the method of moments, maximum likelihood (one-step and two-step implementations), and an EM algorithm. Simulations across 72 scenarios show that likelihood-based methods outperform moment estimation in terms of RMSE, with estimation becoming more variable as the inflation rate increases. A real data application to Australian catastrophic events (flood-storm and flood-bushfire monthly counts) indicates significant zero-inflation and dependence under both positive and negative dependence settings. Extensions to higher dimensions, particularly for positive dependence using multivariate comonotonic shock models, are also discussed.

Torsten Sløk, chief economist, argues the U.S. economy is accelerating rather than slowing, and that forecasts of an imminent slowdown have been wrong since January—nine months running. He says the economics profession should confront its record of misjudgments, as repeated predictions of weakness have undermined its credibility. Growth has remained strong, with the Atlanta Fed's GDPNow model forecasting 3.9% third-quarter gains, while consumer spending, business investment in AI, energy, and reshoring, and housing have proven resilient. Sløk attributes slowing job growth to reduced immigration, not economic weakness. Morgan Stanley's Mike Wilson maintains the economy has been in a "rolling recession" since 2022 and is now transitioning to a "rolling recovery," though ADP data showed September job losses and a negative August revision. Sløk warns that strong growth combined with continued Fed rate cuts could rekindle inflation, calling the consensus 50,000 payrolls forecast "too pessimistic."

National Literacy Month, observed each September, is framed as a call to action to address persistent literacy inequities, especially for Black children in south Los Angeles. The authors highlight Partnership for Growth LA's Read Lead Freedom Schools, which pair literacy instruction with culturally relevant books, small classes, and civic empowerment projects. A 2023–24 pilot showed a 14.5-point gain in English Language Arts proficiency, chronic absenteeism falling from 47% to 5%, and 88% of families reporting gains in confidence and motivation. Research cited notes third-graders below grade level are four times more likely to drop out of high school. Funding cuts have forced schools to reduce tutors and programs, and federal support remains uncertain, though California recently approved funding for evidence-based literacy instruction. Alumna Anastacia Nwosu—once "Kid Mayor," now a field deputy to a California Assemblymember—illustrates the authors' message that literacy is leadership.

The President reports that, following Congress's adjournment in Philadelphia, the public offices, records, and property have been moved to the permanent seat of government, where Congress now assembles, though accommodations remain incomplete. He urges Congress to consider exercising its constitutional powers over the District of Columbia. The temporary army has been discharged, and improvements to the federal judiciary system are again recommended. A treaty of amity and commerce with the King of Prussia has been concluded and ratified, while difficulties over the sixth article of the treaty with Great Britain persist and negotiations with France remain unfinished. The President stresses the need for self-protection, advocating a defensive navy, completion of harbor fortifications, and domestic arms manufacturing. Revenue for the year exceeds any prior equal period. He closes by urging Congress to guard public institutions and pledges his zealous cooperation.

A bearish view is given on the US$INR January futures contract, recommending selling at 68.20-68.30 with targets of 67.95/67.75 and stop loss at 68.40. Government bond yields saw their biggest annual fall in eight years, the rupee posted a sixth straight yearly loss against the dollar, and the NSE January contract ended at 68.09.

The ADS7828 operates with an internal 2.5V or external reference. A +5V supply requires an external +5V reference for full dynamic range; a +2.7V supply works with the internal reference. Lower reference voltages reduce LSB size, increasing apparent offset, gain, and noise errors.

Zimbabwe's Ministry of Health and Child Care estimates 44,586 sex workers aged 15-49 nationwide, with about 7,000 in Bulawayo. HIV prevalence among sex workers averages 55 percent versus the 13 percent national average. The HIV and Aids Estimates Report, launched by Dr Owen Mugurungi, aims to help planners understand how funding levels affect HIV programmes. About 25,900 people died of Aids-related causes in 2016, down from 278 daily deaths in 2005. Dr Ruth Labode warned that ignoring key populations may reverse gains in combating HIV and Aids.

Gas prices hit a 2017 high, with Montgomery's average rising to $2.18 and the national average reaching $2.40, the highest since 2015. Analysts attributed the increase to declining oil inventories and geopolitical tensions. GasBuddy predicted prices may soon peak, while AAA forecast increases through September due to summer demand.

GoSun has introduced The Fusion, a solar-electric oven that enables users to steam, bake, or roast without fuel, indoors or outdoors, day or night. The Fusion combines solar energy with a 150-watt electric heating element powered by a compact lithium-ion battery, cooking at 350°F and feeding up to five people. Weighing 10 lbs, it is vacuum insulated, weather-tolerant, and cool to touch. Founder and CEO Patrick Sherwin described it as the culmination of six years of work. A Kickstarter campaign has been launched to promote the product.

Beatrice Fihn, this year's Nobel Peace Prize winner and executive director of the International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons (Ican), warned that a moment of panic or carelessness could lead to nuclear destruction of cities and millions of deaths. Her remarks addressed escalating war rhetoric and insults between Donald Trump and Kim Jong Un, including Trump's September 19 UN threat to obliterate 25.4 million North Koreans. Ican, a coalition of hundreds of NGOs, has worked toward a treaty banning nuclear weapons.

In this MIT 6.832 Underactuated Robotics lecture, Russ Tedrake reviews temporal difference (TD) learning for policy evaluation and extends it beyond discrete Markov chains using function approximation. After a crash course on least squares function approximation, he contrasts neural networks—historically popular but difficult to optimize—with linear function approximators, which are linear in their parameters and allow exact analytical least squares solutions rather than gradient descent. Various basis functions are demonstrated, including radial basis functions, barycentric interpolators (tent functions), Fourier bases, and polynomials. He notes this approach underlies kernel methods in machine learning and offers convergence guarantees in reinforcement learning, where nonlinear approximators can fail to converge. He then applies linear least squares to system identification, showing that robot manipulator dynamics are linear in their parameters, demonstrated with a pendulum simulation estimating inertia, damping, and mass parameters from noisy data. TD learning is adapted to function approximators by replacing state-based eligibility traces with traces on the parameters, where each parameter's credit is the gradient of the estimate (phi of x for linear approximators). Tsitsiklis and Van Roy proved convergence to the true value estimate for linear approximators across lambda values. Finally, he introduces LSTD (least squares temporal difference learning), a batch method that accumulates data into matrices and solves directly for the steady state, offering greater data efficiency, no learning rate tuning, and independence from initial conditions. Upcoming topics include policy approximation and actor-critic methods.

The United States District Court for the District of Nevada granted Plaintiff AAA Nevada Insurance Company's motion for summary judgment in a declaratory relief action regarding an insurance policy. Defendant Vinh Chau, insured by AAA with bodily injury liability limits of $100,000 per person and $300,000 per accident, was involved in a car accident resulting in Benjamin Buenaventura's death. Counsel for the Buenaventuras made a policy limits demand requiring payment within two weeks and proof that those were the only available policy limits, but did not identify all heirs or lienholders or provide a release. AAA's attempts to follow up went unanswered, and the demand expired. In April 2007, counsel stated the client would no longer settle for policy limits, and a wrongful death action seeking $999,997 was later filed. Family members of the decedent intervened in AAA's June 2008 declaratory relief action.

The court held that AAA's contractual liability was limited to $100,000 and that its failure to settle within the two-week deadline did not constitute bad faith under Nevada law, as AAA had a reasonable basis for noncompliance because counsel refused to respond to inquiries identifying all potential claimants. The court found the demand letter unreasonable and noted the same counsel used similar letters in at least three other cases. Interveners' request for further discovery under Rule 56(f) and jurisdictional objections were denied.

The passage discusses essay writing services and guidance for students writing academic essays. It states that essay writing is difficult for many students, who may face complications, time constraints, or lack of interest in assigned topics. It claims custom essays are completed by subject specialists and will not be published online as samples. Advice includes choosing an interesting topic, brainstorming, editing after writing, avoiding restating the thesis or adding new information in conclusions, and evaluating the reliability of online sources. Benefits of hiring professional writers include high-quality, error-free coursework and better grades. Tools mentioned include the Hemingway app for readability and FreeMind and XMind for mind-mapping.

The passage contains a treaty in which the High Contracting Parties mutually guarantee territorial integrity and political independence under republican governments. They covenant to settle pending boundary disputes by agreement or arbitration, to submit unresolved disputes to a permanent international commission for one-year investigation before any hostilities, and then to arbitration unless the dispute affects honor, independence, vital interests, or third parties. They also agree to prevent hostile military expeditions and arms exports to insurrectionists against established governments. Ratifications are to be deposited at the Pan American Union in Washington; the treaty takes effect sixty days later, continues indefinitely, and may be denounced by written notice to the United States, effective one year after notification. It was concluded in Washington in Spanish, English, French, and Portuguese. Two letters follow: Mezes offers to draft general principles from confidential material, and Secretary of War Baker tells Lippmann that postwar Germany must be made livable.

The Trap play is a quick-hitting, downhill run scheme that kicks out an interior Defensive Lineman and is especially effective against aggressive pass rushers. Its strengths include its speed, which limits defenders' time to identify the ball carrier, and its use of angle blocks, making it forgiving for smaller Offensive Linemen and useful against unblockable Defensive Tackles. Its main weakness is difficulty against defenses that squeeze interior gaps, such as a Bear front or an even front with Defensive Linemen in both A- and B-gaps. The passage details assignments for each position against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts. Two variations are described: the Gun Trey Same-Side Trap RPO, run from Shotgun with a Quarterback option to throw, and the Wing-T Trap, a sister play to the Buck Sweep that shares identical backfield action.

Most Southeast Asian stock markets edged lower on Monday ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's two-day policy meeting, with a 25 basis point rate hike expected. Thai shares fell the most on weak energy stocks, while Singapore declined for a fourth straight session on financial losses. Indonesian shares slipped, and Philippine shares recovered from early falls to close marginally lower. Malaysian shares closed slightly higher, and Vietnam rose for a sixth straight session, posting its highest close since March 2007.

Hillview Middle School will host an outdoor family movie night on April 27 at 7:30 pm, featuring the PG-rated film Sing. Proceeds benefit the Leukemia and Lymphoma Society and Juvenile Diabetes Research Foundation.

In this address to Congress, the President reviews U.S. foreign policy amid the Indochina crisis. He states that North Vietnam violated the 1973 Paris accords by infiltrating over 350,000 troops, while American legal restrictions and reduced aid prevented enforcement, contributing to South Vietnam's failed withdrawal. Citing General Weyand's assessment, he requests $722 million in emergency military aid and $250 million in economic and humanitarian assistance for South Vietnam, asks Congress to clarify restrictions on using U.S. forces to evacuate Americans and endangered Vietnamese, and sets April 19 as a deadline for action. He also describes Cambodia's dire situation and appeals for aid, quoting a letter from acting President Saukham Khoy.

The President urges national unity and refuses to assign blame. He reaffirms alliances with Japan, Korea, and Europe, urges lifting the arms embargo on Turkey regarding Cyprus, and seeks authority to waive a trade-act provision excluding OPEC members such as Ecuador and Venezuela. On the Middle East, he pledges continued peacemaking after two disengagement agreements, despite suspended Israel-Egypt talks. Regarding the Soviet Union, he hopes to finalize the Vladivostok arms agreement during Brezhnev's visit and criticizes trade sanctions tied to emigration, which he says cost American business opportunities and set back emigration progress. He reaffirms China policy under the Shanghai communique and plans a visit. He also addresses global challenges—food, energy, oceans, and the environment—defends the CIA against sensationalized investigation, and argues against reducing the defense budget, closing with a call for one unified foreign policy.

Criminologist Gary Kleck and Marc Gertz concluded from 1993 surveys that more than 2.2 million defensive gun uses occur annually in the United States; the results were published in 1995 and repeatedly attacked by the anti-gun movement. Newly recovered Centers for Disease Control and Prevention surveys, conducted shortly afterward during the Clinton administration, reached a similar conclusion—about 2.5 million defensive gun uses per year—but were never published. Kleck states the CDC data confirm his estimate and that guns are used defensively about 3.6 times as often as offensively; he does not accuse anyone of malfeasance but notes someone at the CDC decided against publication. The author argues the buried findings undermine an anti-gun talking point, show that government agencies require verification, and support arguments for private gun ownership, stressing that public education on gun issues is essential.

This passage is a porting guide for interfacing the AGESA™ software binary module with a host BIOS. All reported errors other than SUCCESS and BOUNDS_CHK are logged in an event log buffer retaining the 16 most recent events, retrievable via AmdReadEventLog. Support for 16-bit Real Mode is deprecated; the binary module executes in 32-bit protected mode with flat addressing.

The interface model consists of a Bridge (host-side code calling the AGESA Dispatcher), a Dispatcher (entry point taking a function number), a Call-Out port, and a Router (host-side re-entry point for call-outs). The host environment must establish a valid stack, fill the standard header (AMD_CONFIG_PARAMS), implement a call-out router, and load its address into the standard header.

For UEFI environments, four execution stages (SEC, PEI, DXE, RTP) span three execution modes. AGESA core files are organized into libraries, plus four UEFI libraries, producing four build targets. Specific assemblers and compilers are listed for 16-bit, 32-bit, and 64-bit development. PEI-phase PEIMs handle processor initialization, memory initialization, and reset coordination, publishing PPIs and a memory information HOB. The DXE driver performs late initialization and generates data tables (ACPI, DMI) published via AgesaDxeProtocol; AmdGpuVgaControlDxe controls VGA resource decoding.

Build methods include Binary Modules (indirect) and Source Integration, with defaults customizable via <plat>Options.c. Environment variables AGESA_ROOT and AGESA_OptsDir must be set. Cache-As-Ram must be enabled before AmdInitReset using the ByHost allocation method; the host must not modify SS/ESP or cache controls (MTRRs) during the CAR period.

Stack procedures include AMD_RESET_ENABLEMENT (very early silicon controls), AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK (establishes the pre-memory stack across processor cores), and AMD_DISABLE_STACK (removes it once main memory is available). Service procedures include AmdCreateStruct/AmdReleaseStruct, AmdGetDimmDataEye, AmdGetApicAddress, AmdGetPciAddress, AmdGetExecModuleId, AmdLocateMemory, AmdAddMmioRange, and AmdReadEventLog. Entry procedures, in time-point order, are AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost, AmdInitEnv, AmdInitMid, AmdInitLate, AmdInitRtb, and the resume-path procedures AmdInitResume, AmdInitS3EarlyRestore, and AmdInitS3LateRestore.

On Tuesday, Kinder Morgan rose after Canada agreed to buy its pipeline project for $3.4 billion; Bank of America fell as interest rates dropped; Petrobras declined amid Brazil's diesel price subsidy; ZTO Express rose on Alibaba's $1.38 billion stake purchase.

Questions are being raised about the environmental value of biodegradable plastics. A University of Edinburgh study led by Jesse Harrison, cited by Andrew Masterson in Cosmos, found research on biodegradable plastic bags inconsistent and poorly defined, offering little use for informing policy or regulation.

Mitsui & Co raised its full-year net profit forecast to a record 440 billion yen after April-December profits jumped 64 percent to 376.8 billion yen, boosted by higher iron ore and coking coal prices. Rival Itochu reported a 19-percent profit increase but kept its forecast unchanged, while Sojitz raised its forecast 12 percent.

This patent application describes systems and methods for dynamically providing video overlays in video stream processing. A client device (e.g., a smart TV) identifies a set-top box presenting overlaid information on a video stream, selects a corresponding template, and presents a replacement video stream mimicking the original presentation. Video content is identified through fingerprinting: query fingerprints generated from video frames are matched against reference fingerprints in a database. Based on the identified content, replacement video is selected (e.g., a local commercial replacing a national one). The replacement video may be presented at specific positions, sizes, portions, or playback speeds, or alpha-blended with overlaid information, according to the template. Templates can be generated manually or programmatically by analyzing video regions. The system comprises fingerprint generators, a video identification system with index, match, and identification modules, and a replacement content server providing video and templates.

Peter DeBoer says each win brings the team closer to its goal and a Saturday night win could turn the series. He credits returning veterans for their energy and praises a rookie's composure, calling it the best rookie performance he has seen. He notes the team finally gained momentum after three games without a first goal or overtime winner. He says the players still have fire, praises a veteran star's composure, hopes a goal builds confidence, credits the opponent's goaltender and penalty kill, and says the team must end its losing streak or its season ends.

A writer describes waiting more than six hours at Norfolk General Hospital's emergency ward on April 9, arguing doctors and nurses should not be blamed and that doctors should have authority to call in additional doctors when waits exceed two hours, blaming bureaucrats instead. A second letter says seniors in long-term care should not pay medication fees and questions why long-term care bed funding was announced a month and a half before the June 7 provincial election.

KDKA-TV and WPXI-TV in Pittsburgh reported on June 22 that video showed Antwon Rose II firing a gun before he was fatally shot by East Pittsburgh police, and that gunshot residue was found on his hands, citing unnamed police sources. Allegheny County Police Superintendent Coleman McDonough stated the video did not show Rose firing a gun and the residue claim was false, cautioning media against unverified information. WPXI defended its report while KDKA backed off. On June 27, DA spokesman Mike Manko criticized local media, saying stations "failed" by reporting wrong information. KDKA retracted and apologized that day; WPXI initially did not apologize but issued a written apology on June 28. The New Pittsburgh Courier questioned the sources' motives and agreed the stations failed.

Coffee sales in Britain are booming, with Costa—now the world's second largest coffee chain behind Starbucks—a major driver. Sales rose 37 per cent over five years to £3.4billion in 2016 and are forecast to rise a further 29 per cent by 2022. Costa has more than 2,000 UK shops, though Britain ranks only 44th in per capita coffee consumption, with Finland topping the charts.

Costa opened a new roastery in Basildon, Essex, chosen from 20 candidate sites for its proximity to Tilbury Docks and road links to London. The facility quadrupled roasting capacity from 11,000 to 45,000 tonnes annually—producing 2.1billion cups a year—and can receive and store 24 tonnes of beans per hour. Beans arrive green and rock hard, are cleaned, roasted, and tested by infrared for colour and measured for moisture to keep flavour consistent. Robots measure, pack, label, and shrink-wrap the coffee, processes predicted to improve productivity by 25 per cent.

The roastery achieved a BREEAM 'outstanding' design stage assessment and is targeting the same at final stage, using solar panels, rainwater harvesting, and LED lighting; all Costa coffee is Rainforest Alliance Certified. Vietnam is the world's second biggest coffee producer after Brazil, supplying bitter robusta beans that form part of Costa's blend alongside arabica.

Master of Coffee Gennaro Pellicia, whose tongue is insured for £10million, oversees quality; lab staff sample every bag of beans, with around eight per cent typically rejected annually. The roastery can train 3,000 baristas a year. Costa, which had 41 shops when Whitbread took it over in 1995, built the site with at least a 30-year lifespan and could open another 6,000 shops worldwide in that period.

This passage is a transcript of an MIT class session on multi-stakeholder engagement in sustainable supply chains, led by Alexis Bateman, centered on a palm oil case study involving Golden Agri-Resources (GAR). Students, acting as consultants for GAR, presented differing strategies: cooperating with Greenpeace, treating Greenpeace as an irrelevant outsider to preserve self-regulation through the RSPO, and a market-driven approach offering a premium product above existing standards. The class mapped stakeholders, including GAR, farmers, mills, major corporations (Nestle, Unilever), consumers, the Indonesian government, certifying bodies, NGOs, investors, and local and international communities affected by slash-and-burn practices.

Discussion covered Greenpeace's campaign against Nestle, noting that targeting consumer-facing brands is more effective than targeting deep-tier suppliers. Challenges identified included supply chain opacity, limited price premiums (only about 10% of palm oil is certified), certification costs for small farmers, and uncertainty around costs and benefits. The class compared the voluntary RSPO standard with the mandatory Indonesian ISPO standard and debated whether GAR should pursue higher or lower sustainability standards.

The instructor then reviewed models of company-NGO engagement: one-on-one partnerships (Chiquita with the Rainforest Alliance, Dell with Goodwill on e-waste, Walmart with the Environmental Defense Fund), multiple partners (Starbucks), and industry collaborations (RSPO, the Sustainability Consortium, the Electronic Industry Citizenship Coalition, and the Sustainable Apparel Coalition). Communication strategies, risk mitigation, and the proliferation of certification labels—roughly 440 across 30 industries with little regulation—were also discussed. The session concluded with logistics: the Environmental Defense Fund would visit the following week, and a project deliverable was due.

The Kiss of Death is a sell signal in the S&P 500 that triggers when the index drops from an all-time high, falls below its monthly 21 exponential moving average (EMA), bounces back above the 21-EMA, and then drops below its recent low. Since 1960, it has triggered in 1969, 1973, 1978, 2001, and 2008, each time preceding major bear markets, though it also produced a false signal in September 2022 when the market rose instead. The trading rules involve selling when the signal triggers and buying back when the S&P 500 closes above its 10-month EMA. A backtest starting in 1967 using unadjusted S&P 500 data showed the strategy improved buy-and-hold performance, with a higher CAGR and maximum drawdown reduced to almost half, making it potentially worthwhile for conservative investors.

Fair Isaac, creator of the FICO score, unveiled a new pricing model allowing mortgage lenders to bypass credit bureaus by licensing FICO scores directly to mortgage resellers, who can then distribute scores to borrowers. Its shares rose more than 20% on Thursday, their largest increase since Nov. 22, though they remain down about 9% this year. Shares of Experian, TransUnion, and Equifax fell between 4% and 10% as investors saw the move as reducing the role of credit reporting agencies. Fair Isaac will offer both mortgage score pricing models to the three bureaus on the same terms. CEO Will Lansing said the change eliminates unnecessary markups and gives pricing choice to users. Raymond James analyst Patrick O'Shaughnessy said the scheme could improve FICO's economics and disintermediate credit bureaus from their roughly 100% markup. FHFA Director Bill Pulte called it an effort to generate creative solutions for American consumers and encouraged credit bureaus to take similar actions.

The MSPM0C1105/6 are cost-optimized, ultra-low-power 32-bit MCUs based on the Arm Cortex-M0+ core, operating up to 32MHz. They provide up to 64KB flash, 8KB SRAM, an on-chip oscillator, analog peripherals including a 12-bit ADC and comparator, timers, DMA, a CRC-16 accelerator, and UART, SPI, and I2C communication peripherals.

YouTube's Original Content team, led by Susan Daniels, is adding four new YouTube Red series for family audiences, debuting in the spring: Hyperlinked, DanTDM Creates A Big Scene, The Kings of Atlantis, and Fruit Ninja: Frenzy Force. This marks YouTube Red's first investment in family-oriented original programming. The YouTube Kids app will also soon be available on LG and Samsung Smart TVs.

Tesla Motors filed a Form 8-K on March 11, 2016, disclosing an immaterial error in its 2015 Form 10-K that overstated the cost and net book value of the Supercharger network. The net book value as of December 31, 2015 should have been stated as $166.6 million. The error was limited to the Management's Discussion and Analysis section and did not impact the consolidated financial statements or notes. Management determined the error to be immaterial. The report was signed by CFO Jason Wheeler.

Finnish official Pekkala reported that most Finns sympathized with the democracies and increasingly favored a separate peace with the Soviet Union, views shared by Mannerheim, the Social Democrats, and smaller parties, though not the Agrarian Party. Foreign Minister Witting, however, told Minister Schoenfeld that Finland, dependent on Germany for 93% of its imports and "like a mouse in a trap," showed little willingness to resist German control, fearing starvation if imports were interrupted. Minister Johnson reported from Sweden that Finland's military situation was rapidly deteriorating; a Russian offensive ending in Finland's collapse could provoke demands in Sweden for assistance to Finland, strengthening pro-German elements and endangering the coalition government. Soviet Minister Kollontay, concerned about effects on Sweden, believed peace required a simple cessation of fighting and had conveyed this view to her government.

Researchers have developed a molecular sensor that releases a thyme-like flavor (thymol) when it encounters the influenza virus, potentially enabling flu detection through chewing gum or lozenges. The sensor uses a neuraminidase substrate with attached thymol molecules, which viruses cleave in infected individuals. In lab tests, the sensor released free thymol within 30 minutes in saliva from flu patients and did not affect cell functioning. Human clinical trials are planned in approximately two years. The technology aims to provide a rapid, accessible screening tool that could detect pre-symptomatic infections, addressing limitations of current slow, expensive PCR tests and lateral flow tests that miss early infections.

Four leading candidates for Baltimore County executive—Vicki Almond, Jim Brochin, Johnny Olszewski Jr., and Al Redmer Jr.—spoke before more than 100 real estate professionals, promising smart growth and an improved development approval process. None supported impact fees, each citing different reasons. All agreed the approval process is cumbersome, citing examples of lengthy permit waits. On rezoning, candidates called for more predictable decisions based on the county's master plan. Only Brochin criticized "pay-to-play politics," while others emphasized development's importance to the economy. The forum was the first of several that week. Primaries are June 26, with candidates vying to succeed Kevin Kamenetz, who is running for governor.

The 12th Harrogate Advertiser Business Awards will be held at the Royal Hall for the first time on Thursday, April 27, as a black-tie event with dinner and entertainment. The entry deadline is noon on Monday, March 13. The Royal Hall, restored at a cost of £10.7m and reopened by Prince Charles in 2008, is considered one of the finest Edwardian theatres in the North. There are 10 award categories, and businesses may enter as many as they like. The main sponsor is Verity Frearson. Past winner Zara Jackson said winning boosted her business's credibility.

The article examines the first trading day of the month effect in the S&P 500, tested using SPY since 1993. The average gain from the close of the last trading day of the month to the close of the first trading day is 0.24%, six times higher than the average daily gain of 0.04%. However, this simple approach is too unstable and unreliable to trade, with most gains occurring before the 2008/09 GFC. Adding a simple filter reduces trades by one third and increases the average gain per trade to 0.35%, producing a 3% CAGR while invested only 1.7% of the time, with a 67% win ratio and 5% max drawdown. Another variant, buying at the close of the first trading day under one criterion, produced 61 trades with an average gain of 1.1%. The most likely explanation is monthly capital inflows from savers, pension funds, and automatic 401(k) contributions. The best-performing first days occur in February and July.

Robert Oscar Lopez, formerly a tenured professor at California State University, Northridge, resigned after eight years, citing a desire to be true to God, following criticism for opposing adoption by same-sex couples. He now argues that academic freedom is neither a virtue nor a reality, linking it to a tenure system that protects few faculty while adjuncts lack protection, and claims students were coached to file Title IX charges against him. The author contends academic freedom is impossible because everyone draws limits on acceptable views, and cites perceived double standards: conservative professors like Lopez and John McAdams faced consequences, while Drexel professor George Ciccariello-Maher, who tweeted about "white genocide," received support. Echoing Lopez, the author calls for cutting funding to colleges, promoting trade schools and apprenticeships, and notes the labor market creates fewer degree-requiring jobs than there are graduates. The author concludes that truth, not academic freedom, should govern curricula, and calls for a purging of academia.

This paper studies profit maximization in repeated bilateral trade through online learning, where a broker aims to maximize profit (buyer payment minus seller payment) under dominant-strategy incentive compatibility and individual rationality, unlike prior work focused on efficiency metrics like gains-from-trade. In the stochastic i.i.d. setting with possibly correlated valuations, the authors present a polynomial-time algorithm achieving ˜O(√T) regret against the best mechanism in hindsight, matching an Ω(√T) lower bound up to poly-logarithmic factors and settling the offline sample complexity (approximately 1/ε² samples suffice and are necessary for ε-optimality). In the adversarial setting, they construct hard instances showing no algorithm can achieve sublinear regret even against a 2/3 + ε fraction of the optimal profit, revealing a separation between stochastic and adversarial models. They also reduce the joint ads problem's regret from O(T^3/4) to ˜O(√T), resolving an open problem, via a correspondence with non-excludable mechanism design. Key challenges include the non-parametric action space and non-regular profit functions, which prevent standard discretization approaches.
The passage describes figures of a cooling fan design shown from multiple views, with broken lines indicating unclaimed portions.

Mediation analysis is important in psychological intervention research, as mediators explain how and why treatments work, can guide intervention refinement, and may serve as early indicators of treatment success. Structural equation modeling (SEM) is the standard approach for latent mediation analysis but relies on sequential ignorability (no unmeasured confounding), an assumption rarely achievable in practice; omitting relevant confounders can severely bias mediation estimates.
