Rank-preserving models (RPMs) based on g-estimation offer an alternative, relying on a no-effect-modifier assumption that permits omitted covariates provided they do not interact with the treatment or mediator, but they have not been extended to latent variable models. The authors introduce RAPSEM (Rank-Preserving Structural Equation Model), which integrates RPM with factor score regression and interaction corrections to enable robust mediation analysis with latent constructs even under measurement error and omitted mediator-outcome confounding. The paper defines the controlled direct effect and controlled mediation effect within a potential outcomes framework and outlines the model's measurement and structural components.

A hockey player discusses his team's playoff performance, saying they felt comfortable throughout the game, played better than in previous games, and capitalized on their chances. He expresses happiness for the goalie who played well after a trying year for both goaltenders, noting the team needs him to stay hot for three more games. He says the team has grown up together and praises teammates, including the "face of the organization," a highly skilled player who scores big goals and plays hurt, and Ryan Smyth, who competes hard despite a weak shot. He notes opponents are keying on Pronger and pressuring their power play, but the team is confident the power play will score and make the difference. He credits coaching, game plans, and adjustments—including better shorthanded structure—for their success, says the team can handle adversity like the frustrating goal situation, believes they haven't yet played their best, and values the franchise's tradition with former players involved.

Speakers credit having fun during hard practices for their current position, praise a fearless teammate who gets in front of shots and attends every practice, note building hype around upcoming games with media present, and agree that a smooth, unflashy defenseman nominated for top defenseman has had a great career.

This study investigated the sero-prevalence, knowledge, attitudes, practices (KAP), and sand fly vectors of visceral leishmaniasis (VL) in Denan district, Somali Region, southeastern Ethiopia, from April to August 2021. A cross-sectional study of 187 participants found an overall VL sero-prevalence of 9.63% by Direct Agglutination Test. Significant risk factors included age group 19-36, damp floors, outdoor sleeping, and sleeping near animal shelters. Only 53.48% of participants had heard of VL, and 42% knew sand flies transmit the disease, indicating poor community awareness. Entomological investigations collected 823 sand flies comprising 12 species, with Phlebotomus orientalis being the dominant Phlebotomus species, suggesting its potential role in VL transmission in this new focus. The study concluded that VL sero-prevalence is relatively high among the pastoralist community, and improved awareness and further studies on vector bionomics are needed.

This paper investigates whether transformers can learn to infer transitive relations—equivalent to graph connectivity in directed graphs—when connectivity information between node pairs is provided as individual training examples rather than in-context prompts. The authors hypothesize that transformers learn connectivity more easily on graphs whose nodes can be embedded in a low-dimensional subspace, and define grid graphs for this purpose, contrasting them with disconnected chain graphs, which lack such embeddings. In experiments where transformers are trained on node pairs with path-existence labels, they achieve near-perfect accuracy on grid graphs but struggle to generalize on disconnected chain graphs. Scaling model size improves performance on grid graphs but not on disconnected chain graphs. Scaling graph size keeps performance consistent across grid graphs and improves performance for larger disconnected chain graphs with a fixed number of chains. Transformers perform better on lower-dimensional grid graphs, and increasing the number of nodes helps more than increasing model size for higher-dimensional grids. Similarly, performance on chain graphs degrades as the number of chains increases, and scaling graph size benefits more than model scaling for chain graphs with many chains. Overall, data scaling helps transformers more than model scaling on higher-dimensional grid graphs and chain graphs with many chains. The authors note that future work should assess connectivity learning on real-world graphs, such as knowledge graphs and causal graphs.

Cincinnati handed No. 14 Iowa State its first loss, using a 17-point first quarter and a 111-yard, two-touchdown rushing performance. The Bearcats (4-1, 2-0 Big 12) beat a ranked opponent at home for the first time since defeating No. 16 Houston on Dec. 4, 2021. Iowa State (5-1, 2-1) trailed 31-7 late in the first half but rallied to within eight before Cincinnati recovered an onside kick. Cyclones quarterback Rocco Becht passed for 314 yards and two touchdowns and ran for two more scores. Iowa State, typically among the least penalized teams, had five first-half penalties, including an offside that extended Cincinnati's opening drive, which ended in Pryor's 30-yard touchdown run. The Cyclones played without 16 injured players and their top two kickers.

In State v. Roy Allen Whisnant (N.C. 1967), the defendant, charged with assault with intent to kill, withdrew a guilty plea after being informed it waived his right to challenge his arrest. He requested continuances to obtain witnesses from West Virginia and Florida, but both requests were denied and he was tried the next day, resulting in conviction of misdemeanor assault with a deadly weapon and a two-year prison sentence. The court held it was error to force trial so soon, since the withdrawn guilty plea likely prejudiced the jurors and counsel lacked reasonable time to prepare. A new trial was ordered.

Plymouth gift and gadget shop Hawkin's Bazaar will close its New George Street store on Sunday, February 4. A closing down sale offers at least 50 per cent off, with some items reduced by up to 75 per cent.

MADSEN Cycles offers a uniquely designed bucket bike that can carry up to four kids plus cargo, along with a wide range of accessories for comfort, security, style, and functionality. The bucket includes two removable bench seats and four seat belts. Accessories include custom rain covers, frame-mounted front racks, and a middle bucket seat for transporting pets, diaper changes, or drinks.

The Supreme Court will hear oral arguments on Oct. 7 in a case addressing whether Section 924(j) of the federal firearm statute creates a separate crime carrying separate punishment from Section 924(c). Barrett was convicted in 2013 under both provisions for his role in armed robberies in which a victim was shot to death by a coconspirator. Section 924(c) prohibits using a firearm to advance a federal crime of violence or drug-trafficking offense, while Section 924(j) applies when a Section 924(c) violation also causes death through the use of a firearm. Under double jeopardy principles, courts presume Congress did not intend multiple punishments when one offense's elements are a subset of another's, unless Congress clearly intended otherwise. Because the government and Barrett agree separate sentences are not permitted for the same conduct, the Court appointed an amicus to defend the 2nd Circuit's judgment allowing separate convictions. Barrett argues neither statute provides for cumulative punishment; the amicus counters that Section 924(c)'s consecutive-sentence mandate is sufficient.

Formative assessment in vocational education and training (VET) is a socially oriented process requiring active participation from both teachers and students, immediate feedback, and dedicated lesson-plan time, though some teachable moments arise spontaneously and teachers unprepared for the added workload may not use it fully. Formative assessment identifies student difficulties and misunderstandings, and includes strategies such as communicating expectations, descriptive feedback, multiple attempts, peer reviews, and self-assessments; students typically show greater motivation toward formative than summative assessment.

Vocational teachers face tension between vocational-based formative and academic-based summative assessment, as academic tools like written tests often do not suit VET and may prioritize documentation over measuring learning. Competence-based education (CBE) offers an alternative by connecting classroom theory to workplace skills, defining competence as achieving industry-standard performance in a workplace context, and has been shown to improve student motivation and engagement.

Balancing authenticity and reliability is essential: overly standardized assessments become disconnected from workplace realities, while contextualized assessments can compromise reliability. Authentic assessment develops deeper understanding and relevant technical skills, and tools such as rubrics and professional development can improve consistency. Including supervisor feedback during practicums enhances authenticity and may strengthen industry relationships.

A comprehensive assessment program should combine written testing, technical skills assessments, workplace evaluations, and both summative and formative methods, evaluating students across the four levels of competence-based knowledge: knows, knows how, shows how, and does. Overall, VET assessment must account for both theoretical knowledge and technical skills, using authentic, competence-based approaches to foster deeper learning.

The Second Circuit affirmed the district court's grant of summary judgment to Reisdorf Brothers on the Georges' federal claims. On the Clean Water Act claim, the court held the plaintiffs failed to raise a triable issue of fact as to any continuous or intermittent discharge of pollutants, as their evidence concerned a single discrete March 2009 spill or was too speculative, including regarding the alleged molasses discharge. The RCRA claim failed because the plaintiffs neither alleged nor provided evidence of violations of the relevant federal regulations defining an "open dump." The court found no abuse of discretion in the district court's refusal to exercise supplemental jurisdiction over the state adverse possession claim, which was dismissed without prejudice. Finally, the court upheld the denial of the defendant's request for attorney fees under 42 U.S.C. § 6972(e), finding the plaintiffs' claims, though unsuccessful, were not frivolous and were litigated in good faith.

This study used data from the PREVEND prospective cohort in Groningen, Netherlands, to fit a multi-state model estimating age- and sex-specific transition rates between KDIGO risk stages (defined by eGFR and UAE) and their association with new-onset heart failure (HF). Among 8,569 participants followed a median of 12.6 years, 373 developed HF and 710 died before developing HF. Forward transition rates between risk stages increased exponentially with age and were higher in men, while backward transitions were more likely in younger subjects and women. KDIGO stage progression was rapid, with movement to intermediate risk mostly occurring between ages 60 and 70, and to high/very high risk after age 70. Intermediate and high/very high risk stages were associated with increased HF risk compared to low risk; relative rate ratios were stronger in younger subjects, whereas absolute rate differences were larger in older subjects and men. Misclassification of risk stages was accounted for and was lower using cystatin C-based eGFR. Model fit was excellent. The authors conclude that kidney disease progresses quickly in middle-aged populations and that slowing KDIGO risk stage progression may importantly reduce new-onset HF, though generalizability is limited by the UAE-enriched, predominantly Caucasian cohort and the Markov assumption.

Phil Kessel scored twice with an assist and Evgeni Malkin added two goals and two assists as the Pittsburgh Penguins defeated the Washington Capitals 7-4, winning their fourth straight game and seventh consecutive home game to pull within four points of first-place Washington. Sidney Crosby recorded two assists to extend his scoring streak to 11 games. Alex Ovechkin scored twice for Washington, reaching an NHL-best 32 goals. Pittsburgh went 3 for 4 on the power play while Washington went 0 for 3.

Australian financial markets can be accessed through ETFs, American Depository Receipts, international brokers such as Interactive Brokers, or stock CFDs. Backtesting using the US-traded EWA ETF shows profitable strategies exist, though mean reversion strategies perform less consistently in commodity-heavy markets like Australia than in the US, and classical strategies like the 200-day moving average and Golden Cross failed. Seasonal strategies work well, particularly the Santa Claus effect: since 1996 it has had only two negative years (2002 and 2020), a 92% win rate, and a 2.4% average gain per trade. Australian equity ETFs trade on US exchanges, while FXA is the only currency ETF offering AUD/USD exposure. The primary exchange is the Sydney-based Australian Securities Exchange, which merged with the Sydney Futures Exchange in 2006; the Sydney Stock Exchange is a wholly-owned subsidiary of AIMS Financial Group, licensed in 2013. The market trades weekdays excluding national holidays, from 10:00 am to 4:00 pm AEDT (11:00 pm to 5:00 am GMT), and the Australian dollar can be traded against major currencies.

This study developed a scale to measure prospective teachers' attitudes towards values education through distance education. Noting that few studies and no existing scales address values education via distance education—despite its widespread use during the Covid-19 pandemic—the researchers conducted a descriptive survey study with 341 prospective teachers at Gazi University, most of whom were female. Following established scale development steps, an initial pool of 43 items was reduced to 40 after expert review, and a pilot study with 30 participants resulted in a 40-item, five-point Likert scale. Data from 341 participants were analyzed using SPSS 22 through exploratory factor analysis, reliability testing, and item analysis. A KMO value of .971 and a significant Bartlett's test confirmed the data's suitability. After four items were removed for failing specified criteria, the final 36-item scale (21 positive, 15 negative) showed a two-factor structure: "Necessity and Usefulness" (21 items, 35.029% variance) and "Feasibility" (15 items, 28.257% variance), together explaining 63.286% of total variance. Cronbach Alpha coefficients were .969 and .961 for the two factors, with split-half reliabilities of .934 and .930, indicating reliable measurements. Item-total correlations (.656–.841) and significant t-tests showed all items were distinctive, and the two factors correlated moderately (.632). Tukey's test revealed the scale lacks additivity, so subfactors should be evaluated separately rather than producing a total score. The study concluded that the scale provides valid and reliable measurements. Limitations include gender imbalance among participants, restriction to a single university, and the absence of an external scale for comparison. Future research is recommended to conduct confirmatory factor analysis with participants from different universities, examine various forms of validity, and apply alternative reliability methods such as test-retest.

Jerome "Jay" Powell, a Republican former investment banker appointed by President Donald Trump, becomes Federal Reserve chair Monday, succeeding Janet Yellen, the first and only woman to hold the post and the first in nearly 40 years not reappointed. Powell takes over amid a quiet economy—unemployment at a 17-year low of 4.1 percent, subdued inflation, and nearly four years of uninterrupted growth—but faces difficult decisions on interest rates amid fiscal stimulus and a synchronized global upswing. The Fed, which raised rates five times during Yellen's tenure, signaled three hikes for 2018, with the first expected in March; faster hikes could unsettle markets.

On April 27, 2001, Indian press reported that the board of the Enron-promoted Dabhol Power Company (DPC), meeting in London, authorized its management (DPC President Neil McGregor and Enron India MD K Wade Cline) to issue a termination notice for its power purchase agreement with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB). The decision passed six votes to one, with IDBI opposing and MSEB representatives barred from voting as an interested party. The dispute stemmed from MSEB's missed payments since December 2000 and its Rs 401-crore penalty on DPC for power supply failures; DPC had invoked government guarantees and a political force majeure clause. MSEB made a "protest payment" of Rs 134 crore toward its March bill of Rs 146.64 crore. International lenders supported Enron's exit and held further Phase II disbursements in abeyance, while domestic lenders led by IDBI opposed termination and favored renegotiation. If terminated, the Centre's liability was estimated at one year's electricity bill plus a $300 million termination fee (estimates ranged from Rs 1,800 crore to Rs 2,840 crore). Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh called the decision unfortunate, said the state wanted renegotiation, and announced a committee to renegotiate the contract. Enron called the renegotiation offer "too late" but did not rule out talks. Enron holds 65 percent of DPC, GE and Bechtel 10 percent each, and MSEB 15 percent.

Las Vegas gunman Stephen Paddock purchased 1,000 tracer rounds—capable of improving nighttime accuracy—from a private buyer at a Phoenix gun show, though it is unclear whether he used them in the attack that killed 58 and injured nearly 500. His preparations included an upper-floor room, 23 guns (12 modified for continuous fire), and cameras. He had booked rooms overlooking other festivals, and authorities are investigating possible additional attacks, including a car bombing. His girlfriend said she noticed no warning signs.

Defending a talented post player requires total team effort and special adjustments. Individual techniques include playing defense before the post receives the ball, pushing the post off the block, fronting to deny passing lanes, and influencing the ball to the post's weak side. Post traps, full court presses, 2-3 zones, and Diamond & One defenses can further disrupt post players.

Amazon.com, Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2017 reports Q2 net sales of $37.96 billion, up 25% from $30.40 billion in Q2 2016, with net income of $197 million, down from $857 million. Operating income declined to $628 million from $1,285 million. The company operates three segments: North America (Q2 sales of $22.4 billion, operating income of $436 million), International (sales of $11.5 billion, operating loss of $724 million), and AWS (sales of $4.1 billion, operating income of $916 million). In May 2017, Amazon acquired Souq Group for approximately $586 million, net of cash acquired. In June 2017, it agreed to acquire Whole Foods Market for approximately $13.7 billion, to be funded with debt financing and cash on hand, supported by a committed $13.7 billion bridge facility. Q2 2017 included a $600 million charge to record a valuation allowance against Luxembourg deferred tax assets. The U.S. Tax Court ruled in Amazon's favor in March 2017 on IRS transfer pricing disputes for 2005–2006, though the decision is subject to appeal. Pending litigation includes patent suits by Eolas Technologies, which alleged potential damages of $130–250 million, and the University of Tennessee Research Foundation regarding AWS services. Total assets were $87.8 billion and stockholders' equity $23.2 billion as of June 30, 2017.

Sporting News No. 22 Aledo Bearcats lead the Ryan Raiders 2-0 in a Friday night game in Denton, Texas, after a safety from an intentional grounding penalty in Ryan's end zone. Aledo is ranked No. 16 in the Massey Ratings; Ryan has not cracked any Top 25.

Justice Babatunde Quadri of the Federal High Court, Abuja, admitted EFCC documents against Chinese national Li Ya Ping, charged with concealing $300,000 (N108 million) while attempting to board a flight to Dubai, contravening the Money Laundering (Prohibition) Act, 2011. A witness testified the defendant, arrested by the Nigerian Customs Service, was handed over to the EFCC on March 16, 2018.

Children born to obese women have double the chance of being obese by age two, and childhood obesity is also linked to paternal obesity. Egg and sperm cells carry molecules, including non-coding RNAs, that respond to parental nutrition and can influence a child's obesity risk. Maternal BMI at conception is most closely associated with childhood obesity, and egg mitochondria defects in obese females can alter offspring metabolism. However, embryos are "plastic" and respond to positive signals as well. Research in mice shows that diet, exercise, and anti-diabetes drugs can improve egg and sperm quality and stop obesity transmission to offspring. Similar effects are expected in humans, and pre-conception health improvements for both parents may reduce community obesity rates.

The passage has two parts. First, a sources note for Foreign Relations, 1981–1988, Volume IV, Soviet Union (January 1983–March 1985), identifies key documentation in the White House Staff and Office Files at the Reagan Library—including NSC and NSPG meeting files, National Security Decision Directives, and files of NSC staff members—and in Department of State Lot Files, including those of Lawrence Eagleburger and Kenneth Dam, plus the Central Foreign Policy File and Internet resources. Second, a Note on U.S. Covert Actions states that editors identified key covert action documents to comply with the Foreign Relations statute and describes evolving procedures from the Truman through Carter presidencies. Under Truman, NSC 4–A (December 1947) authorized peacetime covert operations under the CIA, partly because of its unvouchered funds; dissatisfaction at State and Defense led to NSC 10/2 (June 1948), which broadened the mandate to "covert" operations allowing plausible U.S. disclaimers of responsibility.

VentureWire's October 19, 2000 issue reports private company business news. Top stories: St. Paul Venture Capital closed its sixth fund with $1.3 billion; incubator Idealab! postponed its IPO citing market volatility; Constellation Ventures closed a new $350 million fund; and New Edge Networks raised $139.9 million in a third round led by Goldman Sachs' GS Capital Partners III. The issue lists numerous venture funding rounds, including Alopa Networks ($15.1 million), MMS ($19.2 million), Egenera ($20 million), Widevine ($11 million), Propel ($38.3 million), EZchip ($22 million), Revit ($30 million), and LockStream ($15 million), among others. Cornerbacks are crucial in football's offense-first era, as their primary job is covering the opposing team's wide receivers in man or zone coverage. In man coverage, they must mirror receivers one-on-one despite starting at a disadvantage, since receivers know their routes while cornerbacks must react. The position's name comes from protecting the outside thirds of the field. Teams typically field two cornerbacks, sometimes a third in a nickel package. They are also called "DBs," with elite players known as "lockdown corners." Cornerbacks must be fast and agile, backpedaling before sprinting, and also assist in run defense. Notable cornerbacks include Deion Sanders, considered the greatest, Charles Woodson, and Darrell Revis, nicknamed "Revis Island." Eighteen cornerbacks are in the Hall of Fame.

CeeDee Lamb, who has missed the past two games with a high ankle sprain suffered in Week 3, was seen doing rehab work outside on a side field at Wednesday practice for the first time since his injury. Stephen Jones said Tuesday he expected Lamb back within the next two weeks. Lamb has not been placed on injured reserve, and the Cowboys' first injury report of the week was expected later that day.

Defending soccer goal kicks requires strategic positioning and pressing to win possession, either immediately in a dangerous area or by denying the opponent an easy build-up from the back. A goal kick is awarded when the ball crosses the end line last touched by an attacker and is taken from the Goal Area; under Law 16, the ball is in play once kicked and visibly moves. The three main defensive tactics are positioning defenders in a combination of man-to-man and zone coverage, aggressively moving to win the ball first, and either transitioning to attack if the ball is won or pressing high if it is not. For young players, build-out lines force defenders to retreat, enabling simplified goal-kick plays. Older youth add multiple target receivers, while adults use all options, often with the goalkeeper taking the kick. Coaches should scout opponents, drill all scenarios, and account for field conditions such as wind.

Zameer Ghumra, a 38-year-old Leicester pharmacist, was jailed for six years at Nottingham Crown Court for disseminating terrorist propaganda after showing children a beheading video and attempting to radicalise them into supporting Islamic State, causing one child PTSD.

David Jones has confirmed it will not renew Jesinta Franklin's contract after two years, saying it is "taking another direction" with Victoria's Secret model Victoria Lee as its new ambassador. Fashion insiders are reportedly shocked, and the future of fellow ambassador Jessica Gomes is unclear.

NewMarket Corp. (NYSE:NEU), primarily through its Afton Chemical business, is a leading producer of additives for fuels and lubricants, with strong EBITDA margins, cash flow, and returns on capital. However, growth has been weak—sales fell about 12% between 2014 and 2016—due to longer oil-change intervals, improved fuel efficiency, and the company's limited strength in the faster-growing diesel additives market. The company is expanding in emerging markets via a new Singapore plant and the ~$183 million acquisition of Aditivos Mexicanos, which should support modestly improved long-term revenue growth (the author expects around 3%). Despite healthy margins, expected free cash flow improvement, and ongoing R&D spending, the author concludes the shares are not undervalued, as the current price already reflects high-single-digit FCF growth and trades above 12x estimated 2017 EBITDA.

This article backtests Larry Connors' 3-day high/low method/strategy from his 2009 book "High Probability ETF Trading." The strategy, which involves buying an ETF after three consecutive days of lower highs and lower lows, performed well in Connors' original tests (conducted through the end of 2008 on the 20 most popular ETFs) and still works reasonably well 12 years later. Connors emphasized quantification, high win-ratios (at least 65%), and trading only ETFs, since ETFs are unlikely to go to zero, though correlations among ETFs can cause many signals on the same dates. The article's backtest found 13 of 20 ETFs performed worse since the original test. When tested as a portfolio of 25 ETFs with a maximum of five positions at 20% equity each, the worst drawdown occurred in late July 2011 during the EU debt crisis. The authors conclude the strategy has deteriorated somewhat but still shows promise.

This passage contains articles 5 through 10 of a whaling vessel contract. Expenses from misdemeanors, desertion, or mutinous conduct are charged to the responsible individuals. The master may displace incompetent officers or seamen, with corresponding adjustments to their shares. If sickness or death prevents voyage completion, legal representatives receive a proportional share. Officers and seamen are accountable for vessel property entrusted to them and must perform assigned cargo-handling duties. Those who faithfully complete the voyage are paid in San Francisco: whale oil at 20 cents per gallon, sperm oil at 40 cents per gallon, and whalebone at $1.25 per pound, or $1.50 if the fleet's total catch does not exceed 200 whales. Signatories agree to board as ordered and not to carry distilled spirits except for medical use; violation forfeits their share. The document includes certifications from the San Francisco Collector's Office (1893) and the Department of State (1900).
EON Resources Inc. published a slide deck for an event. Seeking Alpha's transcripts team publishes thousands of quarterly earnings calls per quarter.

The Bifrost subsea cable, a $760 million, 20,000-kilometre system connecting Singapore to the U.S. West Coast, is set to begin commercial operations. Developed by a consortium led by Keppel with Meta and Telin Indonesia, and built by Alcatel Submarine Networks, it links Singapore to Guam and Grover Beach, California, with branches to Jakarta, Manado, Davao, and Winema, Oregon. It will deliver over 260 terabits per second with roughly 165 ms latency, about 10 ms faster than existing trans-Pacific systems. Keppel holds five of the twelve fibre pairs through a 40:60 joint venture and invested around $350 million. The project faced delays from weather and Indonesian regulatory issues, with the Jakarta landing station completed in mid-2024. Its activation boosts regional bandwidth for cloud, AI, and content delivery, strengthens Singapore's role as a digital hub, and adds redundancy to one of the world's busiest subsea networks.

This study examines how engineering and technical management students at a Hungarian university evaluate their education within the Education 4.0 framework and which skills they consider important for employability. Drawing on Industry 4.0's impact on the labor market and the World Economic Forum's top 10 job skills (grouped into problem-solving, self-management, working with people, and technology use and development), the authors surveyed 147 second-year students (65.3% engineering, 34.7% technical management) via questionnaire in 2019 and 2021, partly during COVID-19 lockdowns. Data were analyzed using SPSS with CHI2 tests and CHAID decision tree analysis.

Problem solving was the top-priority skill for both faculties (66.7%), but significant differences emerged: engineering students prioritized knowledge related to specialization and technical/mathematical knowledge, while business students favored decision-making techniques and analytical thinking, supporting hypothesis 1. Regarding international experiences (Erasmus and Stipendium Hungaricum), 84.6% of students valued improved language skills, with a significant faculty difference in the perceived value of a new approach to structuring and interpreting learning material. For career success factors, no significant faculty differences were found (hypothesis 2 rejected); students ranked individual talents and skills (53.1%), professional devotion (51%), and an excellent network (49.7%) highest. Regarding higher education's contribution to knowledge and self-awareness, significant differences appeared in four areas—knowledge related to future workplace, analyzing quantitative problems, teamwork, and understanding oneself—so hypothesis 3 was partly accepted. The decision tree model was 77.6% accurate, with knowledge related to future workplace as the primary splitting variable.

The authors conclude that Education 4.0 combines technological and soft skills, and universities must adapt curricula to develop both. Limitations include non-probabilistic sampling, a small sample size, and the absence of prior research at the surveyed faculties for comparison.

Irrfan Khan, diagnosed with a Neuro-Endocrine tumor, is receiving treatment in London. He shared an inspiring poem by Rainer Maria Rilke on Instagram, offering insight into his thoughts. Nippon Express said an employee at its Hiroshima office falsified inspection stamps on government-stockpiled rice, affecting 251 bags. Mitsubishi, which entrusted the storage, received a farm ministry business improvement order in May and reported preventive steps Monday. Fifteen bags were shipped for livestock feed with no reported health damage; the rest will be incinerated, none shipped for human consumption. It follows similar falsifications at major Japanese manufacturers.

Plymouth Argyle beat relegation rivals Gillingham 2-1 through goals from Joel Grant and a 90th-minute Toumani Diagouraga strike, moving level on points with the Kent club and out of the bottom four only on goal difference. Positives included Ryan Taylor's return from a broken ankle—he assisted the opening goal—after no lone striker had established himself in his absence; the DJM takeover with Bidfood, which brought around 2,700 young players and coaches to Home Park for the third and most popular such event; and climbing off the foot of the table, with four wins and a draw from the last seven games. Negatives were a goalkeeping crisis, with loanee Kelle Roos becoming the seventh keeper used this season after Luke McCormick's injury, and the poor recent form of Graham Carey, despite his run and cross leading to the winning goal.

Thirty-seven lawyers, including 10 incoming partners, have left Cadwalader, Wickersham & Taft to join Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe, specializing in collateralized loan obligations and asset-backed lending. They will join offices in Charlotte, London, Washington, D.C., and New York. Bloomberg Law counted 33 partner departures from Cadwalader this year; Law360 reported at least 23, excluding retirements. Cadwalader's revenue ranking fell from No. 39 in 2007 to No. 85 by 2024, though profits per equity partner averaged $3.7 million in 2024. The passage highlights racial disparities in income and, more starkly, wealth: in 2015, white families' median wealth was $171,000 versus $17,600 for black families, a 10-to-1 gap. Homeownership differences (73% of whites versus 45% of blacks) contribute, since home equity builds wealth. Drawing on research indicating people prefer owning even modest homes over renting, the author criticizes Durham's affordable housing policies—new Housing Authority units, developer set-asides, and Community Land Trusts—for producing expensive units with little or no equity for residents. This conceptual survey examines the relationship between slavery and pedagogy through Michel Foucault's theory of panopticism, arguing that the two are entwined by surveillance as a form of extraction, a capitalist imperative, and a technology of power. The author notes that scholars frequently omit slavery when defining pedagogy, despite pedagogues in Ancient Greece typically being enslaved people. Drawing on Foucault, Browne, Zuboff, Givens, and others, the passage traces how surveillance, examination, and record-keeping turned human experiences into texts for control in prisons, plantations, and schools. It describes how racial chattel slavery in the United States relied on monitoring, violence, and data extraction practices resembling later scientific management and contemporary surveillance capitalism, in which digital platforms extract and monetize personal data. Building on Givens's concept of fugitive pedagogy, the author introduces "surveillance pedagogy" to describe observation and monitoring in teaching and learning, sustained by extraction, inscription and textualization, and the differentiation of personal data in the digital age. The study concludes that the legacy of slavery persists in digital surveillance, that pedagogy and slavery are inseparable, and that surveillance pedagogy offers a framework for future research on the intersection of surveillance, texts, and education.
The order appealed from was reversed with ten dollars costs to the appellant.

This cross-sectional study assessed the magnitude of lung function decline and its associated factors among heroin users on methadone therapy attending the Medication Assisted Therapy (MAT) clinic at Muhimbili National Hospital in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, between May 2022 and July 2023. A total of 310 participants were enrolled through systematic sampling, of whom 302 completed spirometry and questionnaires. Most participants were male (95.7%) with a mean age of 42.78 years. Lung function decline (FEV1 <70%) was present in 28.5% of participants. Restrictive lung disease was the most common pattern (13.2%), followed by obstructive lung disease (11%) and mixed abnormality (4.3%). The mean age at onset of lung function decline was 44 years. Being underweight (aOR 4.73), living with HIV infection (aOR 2.61), and having a history of pulmonary tuberculosis (aOR 2.48) were independent risk factors for lung function decline. The study concludes that over a quarter of MAT clients had lung function decline and recommends routine lung function screening to address undiagnosed and underdiagnosed lung diseases in this population.

The Superior Court of Pennsylvania affirmed Clay Williams's judgment of sentence, dismissed his ineffectiveness claims without prejudice, and denied his petition for remand. Williams was convicted of first-degree murder, robbery, and firearms offenses for the March 10, 2005 shooting death of Mizael Velez during an attempted cell phone robbery at a Philadelphia Chinese store, and was sentenced to life imprisonment without parole plus concurrent terms. Witness Dante Moore saw Williams attempt to steal Velez's phone and flee after hearing gunshots; the shotgun was recovered from a book bag Williams had given a friend, and Williams admitted his gun went off during the theft attempt. On appeal, Williams raised six issues. The court found his suppression claim waived because his Rule 1925(b) statement failed to specify when, where, or to whom the challenged statements were made, and his sufficiency-of-evidence claim waived because he did not identify which elements the evidence failed to prove, citing Commonwealth v. Flores. His claim regarding the detective's second reading of Moore's statement was waived for failure to develop the argument or cite supporting authority. Under Commonwealth v. Grant, his ineffective-assistance claims were dismissed without prejudice to collateral review under the PCRA, as no evidentiary record had been developed on them. His petition for remand concerning a juror's disclosure was denied because the record was adequately developed and the issue had been expressly waived at trial when both counsel stated they had no objection.

The paper analyzes intimate performances in "personal attention" ASMR YouTube videos using Olivia Kissper as case studies, exploring how media infrastructures produce sexuality through mediated intimacy, and redefines sexuality as affect-centered, framing ASMR consumption as a sexual practice.

The passage introduces BALLAST (Bayesian Active Learning with Lookahead Amendment for Sea-drifter Trajectories), a methodology for placing Lagrangian observers—free-floating drifters that measure ocean currents. Existing placement strategies rely on space-filling designs, expert opinion, or hand-crafted criteria; no active learning approach has previously been presented. BALLAST accounts for Lagrangian data by simulating hypothetical trajectories using vector fields, employing a spatio-temporal vector-output Gaussian process surrogate with a temporal Helmholtz kernel and an information-theoretic utility function based on expected information gain. Placement locations are selected at predetermined times to maximize information gain about the time-dependent vector field. The authors' contributions are: introducing active learning to Lagrangian observer placement, proposing BALLAST, and developing a new GP posterior sampling method combining standard GP regression with the SPDE approach for efficient computation. Numerical results demonstrate benefits on both synthetic and high-fidelity ocean current models.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on May 25, 2022, shareholders approved an amendment to the Company's Restated Certificate of Incorporation effecting a 20-for-1 stock split and a proportionate increase in authorized shares. The amendment became effective upon filing with the Delaware Secretary of State on May 27, 2022. Shareholders of record at the close of business on May 27, 2022 will receive 19 additional shares per share held, reflected in accounts on or about June 3, 2022, with split-adjusted trading expected to begin June 6, 2022. At the Annual Meeting of Shareholders, eleven directors were elected, Ernst & Young LLP was ratified as independent auditor for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2022, executive compensation was approved in an advisory vote, and the stock split amendment was approved. All shareholder proposals presented were not approved. The report was signed by Senior Vice President David A. Zapolsky on May 27, 2022.

A report for the Elementary Teachers' Federation of Ontario finds that fundraising in affluent Ontario schools brings in $548 million—averaging $280 per student—far exceeding the $179-per-student learning opportunities grant for needy schools, reversing the grant's intended equity effect. Boards receiving the least grant money raise the most. The 1997 Conservative funding formula removed over $1 billion and boards' taxing powers. The Liberal government now spends $23 billion ($12,107 per student, inflation-adjusted), ranking fifth in Canada, but much went to class size reductions and full-day kindergarten, while special education, ESL, and maintenance have been underfunded for two decades. ETFO president Sam Hammond says boards still struggle with special education funding despite a recent $219 million announcement. The union recommends five-year funding reviews, increased special education and mental health funding, and more counselors, psychologists, social workers, and speech therapists.

The Citi Simplicity® Card offers 0% intro APR for 21 months on balance transfers—one of the longest interest-free periods available—and 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases. After the intro period, the variable APR is 17.99%–28.74% based on creditworthiness. The card charges no annual fee, no late fees, and no penalty rate, and allows flexible payment dates. It targets consumers with Good/Excellent credit scores (670–850). According to Motley Fool Money, the card is well-suited for paying off debt while avoiding interest.

Joe Ezeokeke appealed his 138-month sentence for possession of cocaine with intent to distribute, arguing the district court erred in applying an obstruction-of-justice adjustment for perjury and that his sentence was substantively unreasonable. The Fifth Circuit found the record supported the adjustment, as his false testimony was material, and held his within-guideline sentence was entitled to a presumption of correctness. The sentence was affirmed.

This study examined the relationship between long-term visit-to-visit blood pressure (BP) variability and cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD) using 1284 participants from the Kailuan cohort. Systolic BP (SBP), diastolic BP (DBP), and pulse pressure (PP) variability were categorized as low, middle, or high, and magnetic resonance imaging was used to identify white matter hyperintensities, lacunae, cerebral microbleeds, and visible perivascular spaces. High SBP variability was associated with moderate cSVD burden and perivascular spaces; high DBP variability was associated with lacunae; and high PP variability showed risk effects on moderate and severe cSVD burden, lacunae, and perivascular spaces. These associations were modified by age and hypertension status. Among participants under 60 years old, only high PP variability was significantly associated with severe cSVD burden, lacunae, and perivascular spaces. The risk effects of SBP and PP variability on cSVD burden were significant only in participants with hypertension. The study concluded that high long-term BP variability, particularly in combination with hypertension, is a risk factor for total cSVD burden, lacunae, and perivascular spaces, and that PP variability warrants attention in young adults.

In this MIT lecture, Gary Gensler marks the 10th anniversary of Bitcoin, citing statistics including its ~$6,300 price, $110 billion market cap, 17.3 million coins mined, roughly 500,000 unique addresses, and about $28 billion raised through ICOs. The class discusses pain points in traditional payment systems—multiple intermediaries with parallel ledgers, high costs, delayed settlement, charge backs, fraud, privacy concerns, and financial inclusion—and debates whether blockchain can address them. Students raise blockchain's own challenges: scalability, slow transactions, high costs, interoperability, error resolution, governance, and regulation. A guest from MasterCard argues existing systems can achieve blockchain's promises without it, while others note blockchain's potential in developing countries lacking reliable infrastructure. India's UPI system is cited as a non-blockchain leapfrog success. The class reviews blockchain payment companies such as BitPay, Ripple, Quorum, and Bakkt, noting few retail successes and that incumbents are filing many patents. Cross-border payments via a "bridge currency" (fiat-to-crypto-to-fiat) are examined, with concerns about volatility, liquidity, and added costs, though potential exists for remittances where fees reach 8–10%. The next class will cover central bank digital currencies.

This passage is from a Texas Instruments datasheet (SLASFA2A, revised April 2025) covering the MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 devices. The document also includes mechanical, packaging, and orderable information with package drawing notes on dimensions, soldering, and stencil design, plus notes on automotive-qualified versions (MSPM0G3518-Q1, MSPM0G3519-Q1). Sheree Coffman, Student Assistance Counselor at Northmont High School, spoke to the Northmont Rotary about the Student Assistance Program, which identifies and helps students facing difficulties such as family crises, depression, and substance abuse. She cited statistics on youth mental illness and emphasized early intervention. Northmont's prevention approach is universal, targeted, and indicated, with programs including U.N.I.T.Y. Day, the Alternative to Expulsion Program, Peer Facilitation, SADD, and support groups. U.N.I.T.Y. Day, themed "Be the Change," has involved over 400 students annually for the past three years.

This article tests whether ChatGPT can create a profitable Bollinger Bands trading strategy. Bollinger Bands, developed by John Bollinger in the early 1980s, consist of a middle band (simple moving average) and upper and lower bands set by a number of standard deviations, incorporating volatility. ChatGPT proposed two strategies: a mean reversion strategy and a squeeze strategy. The authors backtested the squeeze strategy, which identifies a squeeze when the Bollinger Bands move inside the Keltner Channels, which use average true range (ATR) instead of standard deviation. The backtest used SPY data from 1993, unadjusted for dividends and splits. Results showed low compounded returns, erratic performance, and potentially excessive drawdowns. The authors concluded the strategy was not very profitable, though ChatGPT performed the backtest well. The article also promotes the blog's compilation of backtestable trading rules available for purchase.

Business Insider ranks Taylor Swift's 20 best breakup songs in ascending order. The article states that Swift is known for writing exceptional breakup songs exploring the full range of heartbreak, from regret and anger to despair and relief, and cites "Dear John," "Champagne Problems," and "All Too Well" among the best examples in her catalog. Three songs from "The Tortured Poets Department" are the newest additions to the ranking.

The list spans Swift's career, from her 2008 debut singles "Should've Said No" and "Picture to Burn" to "The Tortured Poets Department" tracks "How Did It End?," "Loml," and "The Black Dog." Other entries include "Better Man," which Swift wrote during the original "Red" era and offered to Little Big Town before recording her own version for "Red (Taylor's Version)"; "You're Losing Me," released as a vault track from "Midnights" in 2023; "Death by a Thousand Cuts," inspired by the Netflix film "Someone Great"; and "Champagne Problems" from "Evermore." The ranking concludes with "All Too Well (10 Minute Version)" from "Red (Taylor's Version)," which the article describes as a 10-minute masterpiece that became widely known following a promotional campaign that included a Saturday Night Live performance.

Passwords are stored in non-volatile PWD and PWD_LEN registers; if set, the card locks automatically at power-on. Locked cards respond to basic commands, ACMD41, CMD16, and lock commands, but not data access. The lock/unlock command, usable only in transfer state, uses a single block write structure.

Geologists from the Department of Natural Resources and Mines and the University of Queensland have found evidence of platinum, gold and rare earth elements in rare geological pipe structures in western Queensland, south-west of Mount Isa. The discovery, called the Diamantina Minerals Province, could open a new frontier for Queensland. The pipes, previously found only in South Africa, Brazil, Russia and Finland, may be up to six kilometres wide and contain minerals used in technologies such as fuel cells, mobile phones and hybrid vehicle batteries, worth trillions of dollars.

The Hubble Space Telescope captured images of NGC 4536, a galaxy in the Virgo constellation 50 million light-years from Earth, forming stars faster than it can replenish its gas, possibly acquired during a galactic collision.

Ocwen reached a settlement with Connecticut, bringing its total to 28 of 31 jurisdictions that took regulatory action over alleged escrow and servicing issues. Like prior settlements, it bans new residential mortgage servicing rights until April 30, 2018, but adds unique terms: additional borrower communications, review and reporting obligations, and a $500,000 fine for noncompliance. Newlywed Sarah Illig was bitten on the arm by a nurse shark while swimming with sharks as part of a resort attraction during her Caribbean honeymoon. Her husband, Evan Carroll, captured the attack on a GoPro, and Illig later shared the footage on social media, saying she was lucky to keep her arm. She suffered flesh wounds but did not need stitches and is healing well. Shark attacks at Caribbean resorts are considered extremely rare unless provoked, and nurse sharks are not known to be predatory toward humans.

NVIDIA Corporation's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 26, 2020. NVIDIA, headquartered in Santa Clara, California and traded as NVDA on the Nasdaq Global Select Market, pioneered accelerated computing and the GPU, investing over $20 billion in research and development since its inception. The company operates two reportable segments—GPU and Tegra Processor—serving four markets: Gaming, Professional Visualization, Data Center, and Automotive, under brands including GeForce, Quadro, Tesla, DGX, GRID, and DRIVE. It uses a fabless manufacturing model relying on suppliers such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and Samsung. As of February 14, 2020, 612 million shares were outstanding, and non-affiliate voting stock was valued at approximately $102.15 billion as of July 26, 2019. Fiscal 2020 details include cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities increasing 47% to $10.90 billion; Dell accounting for 11% of revenue; 92% of revenue from outside the United States; and China, including Hong Kong, representing 25% of revenue. The company had 13,775 employees and announced an agreement in March 2019 to acquire Mellanox for approximately $6.9 billion. Executive officers include Jen-Hsun Huang (President and CEO) and Colette Kress (EVP and CFO). Risk factors include intense competition from companies such as AMD, Intel, and Xilinx; cybersecurity threats; dependence on third-party manufacturers; demand forecasting errors; customer concentration; international operations; intellectual property protection; privacy regulations such as GDPR; tax liabilities; and the expected negative financial impact of the coronavirus outbreak identified in China in January 2020.

Kent McFarland of the Vermont Center for Ecostudies will speak on mercury along elevational gradients at Lyndon State College on February 15 at 4:00 p.m. in Room S-102 of the Thaddeus Fairbanks Science Wing. The free, public Wednesday seminar series runs through May 3; the schedule may change.

Mr. Grew argued that no plan for the world organization would satisfy all nations, citing the American Constitution as an initially imperfect but ultimately successful document, and urged that the organization be given a chance to succeed, warning that another war might destroy whole peoples and civilizations. He reiterated support for strengthening the inter-American system and asked Mr. Rockefeller to preside in his absence. At Chile's request, discussion began on paragraph 5 of Chapter II. Ambassador Mora proposed that states not be obligated to participate in military operations for regional disputes not endangering world peace. Dr. Pasvolsky noted armed forces would be subject to special agreements and that the Security Council would decide a dispute's scope. Mexico's ambassador objected to leaving such decisions to regions, citing the Saar plebiscite, while Honduras favored extending inter-American solidarity. The matter was left open for future discussion, and Mexico's ambassador then led review of Chapter III.

The passage contains certifications by Deputy Collector M. Webber (December 7, 1891) verifying a copy of the crew list of the bark Cape Horn Pigeon of New Bedford, mastered by Thomas Scullan, and by Secretary of State John Hay (September 1, 1900) certifying annexed documents as true copies from Department of State files. The main document is a whalemen's shipping paper for the bark's whaling, walrusing, and trading voyage from San Francisco to the North Pacific and Arctic oceans, with service not to exceed twelve months. Officers and crew must pay freight on catches shipped by other vessels, remain aboard eight days after arrival at the final port, pay fifteen percent interest on advances, and not participate in trade. Seamen must obey officers, seek a cargo of oil, and not leave the vessel without leave. The log keeper must record drunkenness, unauthorized absence, women brought aboard, and disabilities. Forfeitures include twenty days' pay for officers failing to expel unauthorized women, five days' pay for abetting or criminal intercourse, and two days' pay for drunkenness, payable to the owners.

The Czech crown firmed, reversing an early slide to 18-month lows against the euro, as the central bank's commitment to capping its value below 27 per euro expired on Friday. The Czech National Bank omitted from its statement a line saying it would end its "weak crown regime" around mid-year, meaning the cap could be removed any time after Friday, creating uncertainty and expectations of increased volatility. The crown rebounded to 27.024 after hitting a low of 27.252, and forward rates also recovered from multi-month lows. The CNB has spent tens of billions of euros defending the cap. Czech bonds were mixed, while other central European bond markets were bullish; the forint firmed 0.1 percent and the zloty eased 0.4 percent. A dealer suggested investors closing crown positions might reinvest elsewhere in Central Europe.

The Superior Court of New Jersey considered whether an employee's sick time and wages received for personal days and family illness days constitute collateral sources subject to deduction from a lost wages award under N.J.S.A. 2A:15-97. Plaintiff, injured as a passenger in an automobile accident, sought lost wages from the defendant tortfeasor, who argued such benefits should be disclosed and deducted under the collateral source statute. Relying on the Minnesota case Bruwelheide v. Garvey and reasoning from American Jurisprudence, the court found that the plaintiff earned these benefits as part of her compensation and surrendered them by using them, diminishing their availability for future illness or retirement cash-out. Because she gave something up in exchange for compensation during her absence from work, the court held that sick pay and payments for personal and family illness days are not benefits within the statute and cannot be set off against her lost wages claim.

This paper argues that Ontario's K-12 education system, through its special education model, excludes rather than includes disabled and marginalized students. Drawing on Carella (2024), it contends that students are invited into classrooms without being made to feel they belong or having their needs met. Educators face challenges including limited resources, policy constraints, and little to no training on disability in Ontario teacher education programs (McCrimmon, 2015), while students are excluded from decisions about their educational placement and lose self-esteem.

After outlining terminology (people-first language, disability as identity, lowercase "d" versus capital "D" usage) and defining inclusive education per UNESCO (1994), the paper traces the history of special education in Ontario from 1860s residential institutions through the establishment of special classes (1906–1920s), the rationalization of segregation, and the integration movement beginning in the 1960s. It also reviews the history of racialized students, noting that multiculturalism policies failed to reverse discriminatory attitudes, anti-racist policies were repealed in 1995, and racialized students are overrepresented in certain disability categories while less likely to be diagnosed as gifted.

The paper critiques the "empty vessel" view of learning, arguing that knowledge emerges through interaction rather than transmission (Rodriguez, 2012). It describes the IEP process, school-based disability identification, and five placement types ranging from regular class with indirect support to full special education class. It argues that lack of planning frames diverse learners as "unexpected," that the Policy on Accessible Education for Students with Disabilities (2018) makes claims without accountability, and that educators receive no guidance on enacting policy in practice. Citing Slee (2018), it concludes that the current system sorts students by identity and perpetuates hierarchies, making education exclusionary.

Recommendations include policies supporting educators with disabilities, disability education in teacher preparation, intersectional approaches, involving disabled students and teachers in policy development, and adopting a non-ableist universal design for learning. The paper concludes that the system was designed to exclude and devalues disabled students as learners.

The FDA approved another generic version of the mifepristone abortion pill, allowing three American companies to produce it and drawing pushback from anti-abortion groups and Trump-aligned politicians. The approval is unlikely to affect access to the pill, which, combined with misoprostol, accounts for roughly two-thirds of U.S. abortions. Separately, Amgen reported that its cholesterol-lowering shot Repatha prevented a composite of heart disease death, heart attack, and the most common type of stroke in a 12,000-patient trial, results that could help the drug reach a broader market. Repatha generated $2.2 billion in global sales in 2024, up 36% from the prior year. Amgen did not provide full results of the VESALIUS-CV study, saying only that it met its two primary goals. The Trump administration also delayed closing a loophole that exempts some drugs from Medicare price negotiation.

This paper proposes SafeBehavior, a hierarchical jailbreak defense mechanism for Large Language Models (LLMs) inspired by human multi-stage cognitive reasoning. While LLMs are powerful across NLP tasks, they remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks—adversarial techniques that bypass built-in safety mechanisms to produce harmful content. Existing input-only defenses (e.g., Self-Examination, Intention Analysis, Self-Reminder) show limited effectiveness against sophisticated attacks such as IFSJ, Papillon, and PPPI, while output-based analysis introduces additional inference latency.

SafeBehavior simulates human adaptive reasoning through three stages: (1) intention inference, which performs coarse-grained screening of input queries to quickly identify obvious risks and terminate unsafe generation early; (2) self-introspection, which evaluates the model's own response through structured introspection and produces a confidence score guiding acceptance, refusal, or revision; and (3) self-revision, which rewrites uncertain responses to preserve user intent while mitigating risks. The authors claim to be the first to systematically incorporate human-like multistage reasoning into the LLM inference pipeline for safety alignment.

The method is evaluated against five jailbreak attack types (including GCG, DeepInception, Papillon, PPPI, and IFSJ) and compared against seven state-of-the-art defenses: Paraphrase, PPL Calculator, Intention Analysis, Retokenization, SafeDecoding, Self-Examination, and Self-Reminder.

The related work section categorizes jailbreak attacks into white-box (gradient-based, logits-based, fine-tuning-based) and black-box (template completion, prompt rewriting, LLM-based generation) attacks, and defenses into prompt-level (detection, perturbation, system prompt safeguards) and model-level (SFT, RLHF, DPO, gradient/logit analysis, refinement, proxy defenses) approaches.

The threat model assumes a powerful adversary capable of crafting arbitrary prompts across optimization-based, contextual manipulation, and prompt-based attack categories. Defense objectives include robust output integrity, effective threat mitigation, and efficient execution with minimal computational overhead.

This study developed and validated a learning module to introduce Critical Multicultural Education (CME) to pre-service English language teachers in Türkiye. Using a qualitative research design, the module was created through a four-stage process: researcher brainstorming sessions, feedback from a critical friend, implementation with a small group of 15 pre-service teachers, and implementation with a larger group of 86 participants at Çanakkale Onsekiz Mart University, followed by interviews with 10 participants. The two-week, six-hour module covered transformative learning, CME, critical consciousness, and critical language teaching. Findings identified personal benefits, including positive attitudes toward diversity and perspective on social issues, and professional benefits, such as awareness of educational goals, ideologies behind education, the political position of teaching, and pedagogical insights for implementing CME. Reported challenges included limited time, dense content, teacher-centeredness, and insufficient information on taking critical action. The study concluded that the module achieved its goals of raising awareness and initiating attitude change toward CME, demonstrating the significant impact of CME courses on pre-service teachers' development, while noting the need for longer timeframes and further research in the Turkish context.

This passage examines equity in access to higher education (HE) in Pakistan through a distributive social justice perspective. Higher education was largely neglected after Pakistan's establishment in 1947, with only 2% of university-age students enrolled by 2000. The Higher Education Commission (HEC), created in 2002, initiated reforms including new campuses, scholarships, and technology use, raising enrollment from 2% to 12.6% between 2003 and 2021. However, the authors argue this growth has been uneven and potentially inequitable.

Universities are concentrated in major cities (Karachi 21%, Lahore 17%, Islamabad 11%), and 65 of Pakistan's 120 districts lack college campuses. Private universities, charging $1,000–$2,000 per semester versus $200 at public institutions, primarily serve urban, affluent populations. Government commitments to equitable access appear in the National Education Policies (2009, 2017), Pakistan Vision 2025 (targeting 25% enrollment), and UN SDG 4.3.

Using secondary data from HEC statistics, AEPAM, Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PSLM), and PPAF, the study analyzes enrollment by region, gender, poverty zone, and sector. Enrollment grew approximately 500% from 2001-02 to 2020-21, and the gender gap narrowed, with female enrollment rising from 27% to 46% between 2001-02 and 2014-15. Nevertheless, disparities persist: extreme poverty zones (5.6% of the population) have one public university and 0.2% enrollment, while low-poverty zones (40% of the population) host over 70% of universities. Female enrollment in extreme poverty zones is 0.02% versus 0.18% for males. Islamabad accounts for 14% of enrollment with only 0.97% of the population, while Baluchistan and rural Sindh lag severely.

The study concludes that HE expansion has not been inclusive and reforms have failed to address structural inequalities. Recommendations include opening public universities in rural and high-poverty areas, regulating private institutions, targeting scholarships, and establishing skill-based community colleges. The study's limitation is its macro-level focus, and further research on micro-level barriers and vocational education is recommended.

Digital leaders foster cultures that encourage risk-taking, experimentation, and long-term employee development, viewing failed experiments as sources of learning and prioritizing critical thinking skills in training. They emphasize transparent data access across teams, discourage data hoarding, and implement governance controls that build trust and increase data sharing. They also embrace measurement, using data-driven metrics and goals to give teams flexibility and to align the organization around a shared vision developed through combined top-down and bottom-up processes. In contrast, digital laggards prioritize short-term efforts, discourage risk, restrict data access to a need-to-know basis, favor business judgment over data-driven decisions, and set aspirational goals poorly grounded in data, leading to process adherence rather than innovation. Case studies illustrate a pharmaceutical company creating a localized experimentation environment within a regulated industry and a retail company implementing real-time sales reporting. Data culture aligns organizations both vertically and horizontally, and digital leaders treat it as central to their business, though even they face challenges balancing risk with failure and analysis with intuition. Laggards are not doomed to stall, and organizations typically fit one of four patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, or data reliant—each able to build on strengths toward a strong data culture.

The passage first presents a statement criticizing the Carter Administration's treatment of Taiwan. The speaker pledges to enforce the Taiwan Relations Act as the official basis for relations with Taiwan, to end practices such as barring meetings with Taiwanese officials in their offices, and to reject foreign interference in protecting American interests, with implementation awaiting the November election. The second part is an address by George Bush, Reagan's running mate, to the Commonwealth Club of San Francisco. He recounts an anecdote about Franklin Roosevelt and speechwriter Sam Rosenman regarding an unkept 1932 budget-balancing promise, then argues that Vice President Mondale's recent speech reflected the Carter administration's campaign perspective rather than its record since 1977. Blake Geoffrion, winner of the 2010 Hobey Baker Award, represents the fourth generation of a hockey family: great-grandfather Howie Morenz, grandfather Bernie "Boom-Boom" Geoffrion, and father Dan all played in the NHL.

Howie Morenz, born in Mitchell, Ontario in 1902, moved to Stratford in 1917 and played five seasons with the Stratford Midgets, losing the 1921 Memorial Cup finals. Dubbed "The Stratford Streak," he worked as a Canadian National Railway apprentice. After scoring nine goals in a 1922 CNR tournament game, referee Ernest Sauve informed Montreal Canadiens managing partner Leo Dandurand, who sent negotiator Cecil Hart to sign him. The July 7, 1923 signing—Dandurand's birthday—led Morenz to wear number 7.

Joining the Canadiens in December 1923, Morenz quickly impressed with his speed and scoring. Alongside linemates Aurel Joliat and Billy Boucher, he won the Stanley Cup in his first season, scoring a hat trick in the finals opener. Over eleven seasons (1923-1934), he became the Canadiens' brightest star, setting a 51-point record in 1927-28, winning three Hart Trophies, two Art Ross Trophies, and three Stanley Cups.

The Great Depression hurt attendance, the team was sold, and Hart resigned. As Morenz's play declined, he was traded to Chicago in October 1934, then to the New York Rangers, with poor results. The struggling Canadiens rehired Hart, who conditioned his return on re-acquiring Morenz.

During a January 28 game against the Black Hawks, Morenz fell feet-first into the boards, his skate blade caught in a crack, and was hit by Earl Seibert, breaking his leg in four places. Hospitalized, he became convinced he would never play again, suffered a nervous breakdown, and died of a heart attack on March 8. His funeral was held March 10 at the Montreal Forum, and he was buried at Cote-des-Neiges Cemetery. Aurel Joliat remarked, "I think Howie died of a broken heart."

Amazon.com, Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2022 reports net sales of $116.4 billion, up 7% year-over-year, comprising North America ($69.2 billion), International ($28.8 billion), and AWS ($18.4 billion). The company reported a net loss of $3.8 billion, compared to net income of $8.1 billion in Q1 2021, primarily due to a $7.6 billion valuation loss on its equity investment in Rivian Automotive. Operating income declined to $3.7 billion from $8.9 billion. North America and International segments posted operating losses of $1.6 billion and $1.3 billion, respectively, attributed to increased shipping and fulfillment costs, higher wage rates, and supply chain constraints, while AWS operating income rose to $6.5 billion. Effective January 1, 2022, Amazon extended the useful lives of its servers and networking equipment, reducing depreciation expense by $973 million. In March 2022, the company acquired MGM Holdings for approximately $6.1 billion and authorized a $10 billion stock repurchase program, repurchasing $2.7 billion of stock during the quarter. As of March 31, 2022, Amazon held $66.4 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, had $49.7 billion of unsecured senior notes outstanding, and reported trailing twelve-month free cash flow of negative $18.6 billion.

The Dengvaxia scandal has remained unresolved for over half a year despite investigations. The World Health Organization announced in Geneva that the vaccine should be used exclusively on people previously infected with dengue, requiring a testing system not yet available but expected in coming years. WHO defended its earlier recommendation for children aged 9 and older in previously exposed areas, having asked Sanofi to study the vaccine's effects on those never exposed; that study led Sanofi to announce the vaccine could increase severe dengue risk in such recipients. Sanofi defended the vaccine's safety. Some senators, led by Senate Minority Leader Franklin Drilon, defend former President Aquino, citing lack of malice and of conclusive proof that Dengvaxia caused the 65 deaths—assertions the passage contrasts with WHO's caution and with senators' duty to serve the public interest.

LimeWire, formerly a 2000s file-sharing tool, has re-emerged as an AI content publishing platform. It enables users to create AI-generated images using models such as Stable Diffusion 2.1, Stable Diffusion XL, and DALL-E 2, with design styles including cinematic, digital art, pixel art, anime, and analog film. Published content is automatically minted as an NFT on the Polygon or Algorand blockchain and can be shared publicly or exclusively with premium subscribers. Creators earn a 2.5% royalty each time their content is traded and 70% of ad revenue, paid monthly in LMWR tokens, which can be traded on exchanges like Kraken, ByBit, and UniSwap. The platform currently focuses on AI image generation, with plans to add music and video tools. A free tier offers 10 credits and 20 images daily with 50% ad revenue share. Premium plans range from $9.99 to $99 per month, offering up to 11,250 credits, 22,500 image generations, early access to new models, and up to 70% ad revenue share, plus a Pro badge, full creation history, faster generation, and no ads.
