The passage describes the power, reset, clocking, interrupt, and peripheral features of the TMS320DM814x DaVinci Digital Media Processors.

**Power management:** SRAM blocks can switch between ACTIVE and SHUTDOWN modes; SHUTDOWN removes supply voltage and loses data. SRAM in switchable power domains enters SHUTDOWN when its domain is OFF and returns to ACTIVE when the domain is ON; certain ALWAYS_ON SRAMs can be independently shut down via x_MEM_PWRDN registers. SERDES_CLKP/CLKN buffers are powered by an internal LDO programmed through the REFCLK_LJCBLDO_CTRL register. Dual-voltage I/Os are grouped into DVDD, DVDD_GPMC, DVDD_C, and DVDD_SD, each independently powered at 1.8 V or 3.3 V; DDR interface I/O voltages are independently selectable between 1.5 V and 1.8 V. PHYs must be placed in power-down mode before their power domain is turned OFF. Low-Power Standby Mode is defined as all switchable power domains OFF, the ARM Cortex-A8 executing an IDLE loop at its lowest frequency, and unneeded blocks clock gated. Power supplies are organized into four sequencing groups with required power-up and power-down sequences; during power-down, 3.3 V supplies must never be more than 2 V above the 1.8 V supplies. PLL and analog supplies benefit from ferrite beads and capacitors (a Pi filter is recommended); 0.1 uF decoupling capacitors no larger than 0402 are recommended at one per two power pins, with a bulk 10 uF capacitor per roughly 10 power pins.

**Resets:** Reset types include Power-on Reset (resets the entire chip, including Test/Emulation logic and EMAC Switch), External Warm Reset, Emulation Warm Reset, Watchdog Reset, Software Global Cold and Warm Resets (via PRM_RSTCTRL), Test Reset (TRST), and Local Resets. When multiple resets occur simultaneously, only the highest-priority request is processed. Reset isolation is supported for the PCI Express subsystem and the EMAC Switch (via the ISO_CONTROL bit in the RESET_ISO register). The RSTOUT_WD_OUT pin reflects reset status and is always asserted on Watchdog Reset; its behavior depends on the latched BTMODE[11] value. Each power domain has dedicated Warm and Cold Resets triggered by domain state changes. During any reset other than Test Reset, I/O pins enter Hi-Z except emulation pins, some EMAC Switch pins under isolation, and RSTOUT_WD_OUT. After reset, the ARM Cortex-A8 begins executing from the Boot ROM.

**Clocking:** Device clocks are generated from reference clocks fed to on-chip PLLs and dividers. DEV and AUX clocks can use external crystals with internal oscillators or 1.8-V LVCMOS clock inputs; the DEV clock is typically 20 MHz (optionally 20–30 MHz under certain conditions), and the AUX clock is optional at 20–30 MHz. A low-jitter differential clock, AC coupled, is required at SERDES_CLKN/P for the PCIE PHY. Optional external inputs include AUD_CLKIN0/1/2 (maximum 50 MHz) and a 32768-Hz CLKIN32. Two general-purpose clock outputs (CLKOUT0/1) are selected via the CLKOUT_MUX register. The device has 12 top-level PLLs and 4 embedded PLLs, which come up in Bypass mode after reset; PLL supply pins require external filtering, and multiplier/divider settings must conform to specified frequency limits.

**Interrupts:** The ARM Cortex-A8 Interrupt Controller (AINTC) handles up to 128 requests with programmable priorities, generating IRQs or FIQs (FIQs are not supported on general-purpose devices). The C674x DSP interrupt controller combines up to 128 events into 12 prioritized interrupts, with events 15–95 alternately sourced from 24 multiplexed events via DSP_INTMUX_x registers.

**Peripherals:** The device provides two DCAN (CAN 2.0) interfaces; an EDMA controller supporting up to 64 channels with mapping to 512 parameter entries; Advanced Event Triggering, Trace, and IEEE 1149.1 JTAG (JTAG ID register value 0x0B8F 202F at address 0x4814 0600); a 3-port gigabit EMAC Switch supporting 10/100/1000 Mbps in MII, GMII, RMII, and RGMII modes with a shared MDIO interface; GPIO with four 32-channel modules (up to 128 pins); a GPMC memory controller for NOR/NAND Flash and SRAM with an Error Location Module (ELM) for BCH error location; an HDMI 1.3a-compliant transmitter with TMDS, DDC, and CEC interfaces and PCB layout guidelines; and a High-Definition Video Processing Subsystem (HDVPSS) with two display processing pipelines, HD/SD encoders, video capture support, and three independently generated graphics layers.

Forecasters predict UK temperatures could reach the mid-20s C by the weekend if a ridge of high pressure takes charge, though Tropical Storm Gert in the Atlantic may affect this. Forecast confidence is low due to the storm, but a low pressure system is expected to absorb the worst of it, potentially allowing high pressure to build from the middle of next week. President Arthur returns Senate bill No. 71, "An act to execute certain treaty stipulations relating to Chinese," to the Senate with his objections. He maintains that a nation should repudiate treaty obligations only when they conflict with paramount interests, and only after exhausting reasonable means of modification. The Burlingame treaty granted Chinese subjects voluntary emigration rights with most-favored-nation privileges; when unrestricted Chinese labor immigration threatened American interests, a new treaty was concluded permitting the United States to regulate, limit, or suspend—but not prohibit—the coming or residence of Chinese laborers, a unilateral concession from China. The act before him suspends Chinese laborer immigration for twenty years, which he regards as a breach of national faith, since neither party to the treaty contemplated so long a prohibition. He further objects that the act's personal registration and passport requirements, imposed only on Chinese, are undemocratic, hostile to the spirit of American institutions, and easily evaded, and he questions their consistency with treaty obligations. He notes the bill makes no provision for Chinese subjects transiting the United States from foreign countries. On policy grounds, he observes that Chinese labor was instrumental in constructing the Pacific railways and that harsh exclusion may drive Oriental trade from American ports, particularly San Francisco. He recommends a shorter suspension as an experimental period and transmits related treaty papers and a memorandum from the Chinese minister.

A group fishing for tuna about 120 kilometres off Tofino, including former NHLer Willie Mitchell, spotted a large shark fin and initially believed it was a great white. Using a GoPro, Mitchell identified it as an eight to nine-foot salmon shark, which resembles a great white but preys mainly on Pacific salmon and generally avoids mammals. A Vancouver Aquarium biologist noted salmon sharks are common in B.C. waters but rarely seen, and that sighting one signals a healthy ecosystem. Experts say climate change could push sharks, including great whites, further north.

Sean Combs was sentenced to 50 months in prison on Friday, closing his criminal case, but he still faces dozens of civil suits. Combs, who has denied all accusations of sexual assault, was once worth nearly $1 billion through businesses in music, fashion, alcohol, and media, but his empire has crumbled: Diageo terminated his Cîroc vodka partnership and bought out his DeLeón tequila stake, Sean John was pulled from Macy's, he stepped down as chairman of Revolt, and his music catalog has declined in value. Cassie Ventura's civil suit helped bring his behavior into the spotlight, and attorney Tony Buzbee said more lawsuits will be filed. MIT's CSAIL, led by professor Mohammad Alizadeh, developed an AI called Pensieve that selects the best algorithms for smooth, high-quality video streaming based on network conditions. Using a neural network trained through a reward system, it reduced rebuffing by 10 to 30 percent and improved quality by 10 to 25 percent. The system is user-tweakable, will be open-sourced at SIGCOMM, and will be tested on VR video.

In *Causey v. Wolfe, Administrator* (opinion delivered June 24, 1918, on appeal from the Desha Chancery Court), the decree was affirmed. The court held that Eugene A. Causey acquired a fee simple title to certain lands in section 16 by virtue of a prior chancery decree (*Causey v. Alice and Laura Williams*), which was based on a gift from his uncle Isaac Adair, Causey's actual possession, and the making of valuable improvements; a promise to give land and make a deed conveys the grantor's whole estate, not merely a life estate, and "title" in real estate means the fee. That decree was binding on Causey's children (the appellants), although they were not in esse when it was rendered, and Causey was neither estopped nor barred by limitations. However, Causey held only a life estate, with remainder in fee to his children, in the west half of the west half of section 15 under Adair's will, and T. F. Tillar acquired that life estate by Causey's deed. As to waste, the Tillar estate, as life tenant, was liable to the remaindermen for removing timber from the 160-acre woodland in section 15; because good husbandry required leaving one-fourth of the standing timber, damages were limited to one-fourth of the timber's actual value of $619.38, amounting to $154.84.

Two years after being traded from the Toronto Maple Leafs to the Pittsburgh Penguins, Phil Kessel, now a two-time Stanley Cup champion, spent his day with the trophy golfing and filling it with hot dogs, captioning an Instagram post referencing a Toronto Sun fat-shaming column.

Rumors about Nikki Haley's sex life resurfaced after Michael Wolff suggested she had an affair with President Trump, prompting defenses from figures like Mika Brzezinski and renewed media debate over why female sex scandals are rare. The passage contrasts this with Nashville Mayor Megan Barry's admitted affair with her security detail subordinate, police Sgt. Robert Forrest Jr.; she had traveled with him and doubled his overtime pay, and he subsequently retired. Barry's response—acknowledging the affair, emphasizing it was consensual, avoiding details, expressing shame, and citing God's forgiveness—is described as an emerging playbook for female politicians in scandals. Some defenders argue she should not resign, noting men in power have affairs without consequences. The PGA Tour says player and fan safety is its top priority, with security advisers collaborating with law enforcement, ahead of the Dell Technologies Match Play tournament in Austin, where police are investigating a serial bomber who has killed two people and injured four.

This study reports the first observation of water-permeable structural defects at the merging regions of single-orientation graphene flakes grown on single-crystal Cu(111)/sapphire, challenging the prevailing expectation that such stitched graphene films are uniformly impermeable barriers. Using SEM, AFM, Raman spectroscopy, and STM, the researchers found that merging regions either appear seamless or show merging lines with distinct contrast. STM measurements revealed that some merging lines are overlapped junctions, where one graphene flake edge lies atop another rather than forming a continuous stitch, with copper steps (~2.2 Å) appearing to play a role in their formation. Wet oxidation experiments, in which graphene flakes on Cu(111)/sapphire were immersed in 90°C water, showed that approximately 45% of merging regions allowed water permeability—indicated by interfacial oxidation of copper to Cu2O—while around 55% were likely seamless stitches. The authors classify merging behaviors into three types: seamless stitching, defective stitching (e.g., Stone-Wales or point defects), and overlapped junctions. These findings advance the understanding of single-orientation stitched graphene and suggest potential applications in nanofiltration, water desalination, and molecular sieving.

This ebook, generated on May 26, 2018, presents Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, 1902, released by the Office of the Historian at the U.S. Department of State as part of a program to publish the FRUS series (established in 1861) in ebook form. The edition offers full volume content, full-text search, bookmarking, and offline access, and recommends citing document numbers rather than page numbers. The volume includes the President's message to Congress, which describes a period of unbounded prosperity, states that the nation's place among nations must be great, attributes material well-being to economic forces, laws, and citizenship, acknowledges that evils have grown alongside prosperity, and advocates progressive regulation of industrial development while preserving its benefits.

Singer Meghan Linsey, 31, was bitten by a poisonous brown recluse spider while sleeping at her Nashville home on February 12, waking with a stinging face and a dead spider in her hand. She went to urgent care with the spider, experiencing symptoms including severe nerve pain, muscle spasms, rash, and swelling. Brown recluse bites are rare and rarely fatal, with only about 10 percent requiring medical attention. There is no antidote—only treatment for symptoms and the wound. The venom causes necrosis, killing tissue, which left Linsey with a wound she describes as a "hole in her face." She underwent hyperbaric oxygen therapy, and after three sessions, dead tissue began coming off and new skin developed. More than two months later, her wound is healing well with a nearly unnoticeable scar. She shared her story publicly to raise awareness about brown recluse spiders.

The passage introduces AutoPrune, a training-free complexity-adaptive token pruning framework for Vision-Language Models (VLMs). Noting that existing training-free pruning methods rely on fixed schedules or handcrafted layer-wise heuristics that cannot adapt to sample- and task-specific demands or guarantee adherence to a computational budget, the authors draw on neuroscientific evidence about human visuolinguistic reasoning to propose measuring mutual information between early-layer visual and textual tokens to quantify input complexity. This score linearly modulates the slope and inflection point of logistic retention curves, which are analytically rescaled so the area under the curve equals a user-specified token or FLOPs budget. AutoPrune integrates into models including LLaVA-1.5, LLaVA-NeXT, and Senna, and on LLaVA-1.5-7B prunes 89% of visual tokens, reduces inference FLOPs by 76.8%, retains 96.7% of original accuracy, and achieves a 9.1% improvement over PDrop.

The 1-4 "Slice" zone offense uses a high player alignment that creates matchup problems for all zone defenses, allowing entry passes to any of four receivers, with a strong inside post attack and spot-up outside shooters. Quick ball reversals force zones to constantly shift, and the offense is easy to teach but tough to defend. Basic actions include the Slice cut, where the opposite post cuts hard to the basket when O1 enters to a post popping out; post-up isolations with High/Low feeds; low post feeds; weakside skip passes; and "Give & Go" rotations. Counters to post and wing overplays use pump fakes and back cuts. Continuity is maintained through skip passes and ball reversal when no good shot is available.

This passage is from a technical reference document for the TMS320DM814x/DM8127 DaVinci Digital Media Processors covering peripheral information and timings. The device's interrupts are serviced by the ARM Cortex-A8 Interrupt Controller (AINTC), which handles up to 128 requests with programmable priorities, and the C674x DSP interrupt controller, which combines 128 device events into 12 prioritized interrupts with multiplexing options controlled via DSP_INTMUX_x registers.

Timing parameters do not include board routing delays; IBIS models are recommended for timing analysis (not required for DDR2). The device provides two DCAN interfaces supporting CAN protocol version 2.0, and an EDMA controller with up to 64 channels mapped to 512 parameter table entries. Debug capabilities include Advanced Event Triggering (breakpoints, watchpoints, counters, state sequencing), Trace, and IEEE 1149.1 JTAG with a JTAG ID register value of 0x0B8F 202F.

The EMAC SW contains a 3-port gigabit switch supporting 10/100/1000 Mbps across MII, GMII, RMII, and RGMII modes, conforming to IEEE 802.3-2002, with an MDIO interface for PHY control. The device includes four GPIO modules of 32 channels each (up to 128 pins), a GPMC memory controller for NOR/NAND Flash and SRAM with an Error Location Module using BCH algorithms, and an HDMI 1.3a-compliant transmitter with TMDS routing specifications requiring 100 Ω differential impedance.

The HDVPSS provides video input/output processing with two display pipelines, the video DACs operate in Normal or TVOUT Bypass modes, four I2C modules support Philips specification 2.1, and the Imaging Subsystem captures pixel data through CAM and CSI2 interfaces processed by the ISP. In this MIT OpenCourseWare lecture (11.350, March 16, 2023), instructor Siqi Zheng explains how policy acts as a "game changer" for sustainable real estate. She recaps the three bottom lines (planet, people, profit) and two prior market failures—information asymmetry (addressed by certifications like LEED) and split incentives (addressed by green leases)—before introducing the third: externalities.

**Positive externalities:** Green buildings generate societal benefits (e.g., reduced carbon emissions) that developers cannot monetize, causing undersupply. Policymakers respond with "carrots" (subsidies, tax rebates) to internalize these benefits. Examples include the EU's €672 billion "renovation wave" for building renovations (with private financial matching), Massachusetts' Mass Save program (heat pump subsidies around $10,000, free efficiency upgrades for owners and renters), and density bonuses such as Arlington, Virginia's FAR increases for LEED Silver, Gold, and Platinum (0.25, 0.35, and 0.50 respectively). She notes that sizing carrots is difficult, requiring balance between social benefits and costs like embodied carbon, traffic, and infrastructure strain, and that subsidies can flip a project's NPV from negative to positive. She also describes her research with the Massachusetts Association of Homebuilders on the state's HERS energy index mandate (from 55 to 45/42), which found energy bill savings would be small relative to price increases passed to buyers, pushing some multifamily income groups above the 30% housing affordability threshold.

**Negative externalities:** Dirty buildings impose social costs builders don't bear, addressed with "sticks" (taxes, penalties). Examples include NYC's mandatory A–D energy grade postings, Boston's BERDO and Cambridge's BEUDO disclosure ordinances, the UK's minimum efficiency standard (buildings below E rating cannot be leased), and NYC's Local Law 97. Government tends to use sticks for large commercial players and carrots for households. Cambridge's BEUDO uses relative 2018–2019 baselines requiring net zero by 2035—more aggressive than Boston's 2050 target. MIT is subject to BEUDO: Building 9, renovated before the baseline, faces continued reductions, while Hayden Library, renovated after, is "lucky." MIT's 2026 Net Zero Committee plans to buy credible carbon offsets in the near term despite a "messy" offset market, targeting real net zero by 2050. Energy codes also grow stricter over time, though developers may relocate to states with laxer codes.

**Climate resiliency:** Despite climate risks, Americans keep moving to high-risk coastal areas, and developers favor "climate denier" neighborhoods. Zheng contrasts Miami—a rich city investing in resiliency, creating a positive feedback loop of investment, growth, and tax revenue—with Fair Bluff, North Carolina, a poor town hit by 19 hurricanes (1954–2016) caught in a negative feedback loop toward becoming a "ghost city." Biden's 2021 Bipartisan Infrastructure Act allocated $47 billion for climate resiliency, raising moral hazard concerns (analogous to the Silicon Valley Bank bailout) and inequality concerns, since sophisticated proposals and matching requirements favor wealthy cities. She leaves open the controversial question of managed retreat versus continued investment.

This patent application describes electronic devices, such as smartphones and tablets, with enclosures formed substantially or entirely of glass. The glass enclosure may define multiple sides—potentially all six sides of a rectangular prism—through which an underlying display's graphical output is visible. Touch- and force-sensing systems may make any or all surfaces interactive input surfaces. Physical distinctions between sides may indicate functional distinctions among display regions (e.g., a main graphical user interface on a major side, auxiliary content or device-control affordances on peripheral and back sides), while graphical outputs, background images, or user interfaces may also span multiple sides to create a visually seamless, unified display. Because both major sides may be active, the primary interface surface may be dynamically determined based on device orientation, biometric or touch sensing, active applications, a time-based schedule, or user selection, and hardware such as speakers, microphones, and cameras may be arranged symmetrically so the device functions regardless of orientation. Enclosures may be monolithic or formed from multiple glass members joined such that seams are positioned away from display viewing areas or hidden at corners, using techniques including glass frit bonding, adhesives, fusion bonding, ultrasonic welding, and mechanical interlocks. Some embodiments use openings or slots to insert internal components, closed with caps or plugs, and openings may accommodate speakers and microphones, with the device selecting between them based on orientation. Alternative enclosure shapes include cylinders, elliptic cylinders, and octagonal prisms.

The article examines candidates to succeed LeBron James (40) and Stephen Curry (37) as the face of the NBA, noting the league remains defined by them a decade after their Finals clashes; they rank first and second in jersey sales, social media views, and Instagram followers, while Luka Doncic had the top-selling jersey in 2025, ending an 11-year run. No clear successor exists, but several paths are outlined: Victor Wembanyama follows the LeBron trajectory as the best prospect since James, with 16 of 20 surveyed coaches, scouts, and executives predicting he will be the NBA's best player in 2030, though no big man has been the face since the 1960s and he would be the first international face; Anthony Edwards fits the Jordan/Kobe athletic shooting guard mold after leading the NBA in made 3-pointers and receiving 11 of 20 votes as the best American player in 2030; Jalen Williams mirrors Kobe's early-career path, becoming the youngest player since Magic Johnson to score 40 points in a Finals win; Doncic, 26, represents the Lakers route; Zion Williamson matches Curry's unlikely-rise path as an injury-plagued former Duke star entering his age-25 season; and LaMelo Ball offers a social-media-driven candidacy as the youngest of 13 active players with 10 million Instagram followers. Giannis Antetokounmpo, the leading All-Star vote-getter the past two seasons, is closest among foreign-born stars but is already 30. Rivalries involving Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Doncic, Edwards, Wembanyama, and rookie Cooper Flagg—second to Edwards with five votes as the best American player in 2030—could also produce the next face of the league.

Nearly 700 pilot whales stranded in two pods at Farewell Spit, on the northern tip of New Zealand's South Island, in one of the country's largest mass strandings. The beach was closed as authorities removed over 300 carcasses, punctured to prevent them exploding from gas buildup during decomposition. About three-quarters of the first pod of 416 died, while survivors and the second pod of about 250 were re-floated. Farewell Spit has seen at least nine strandings in the past decade.

The paper addresses the paradox of moral education in philosophy of education, arguing that it stems from an unexamined libertarian assumption about free will—namely, that freedom requires alternative possibilities and that a person is the initiator of their own actions. This assumption conflicts with the causal-deterministic scientific picture of the world. The dilemma of determinism shows that moral responsibility is undermined whether determinism is true or false, since indeterminism yields random, uncontrolled choices. Drawing on Harry Frankfurt's thought experiment, the paper argues that alternative possibilities are not necessary for moral responsibility. Frankfurt's hierarchical theory of the will locates responsibility in the person's psychological structure: second-order desires (aspirations) and reflexive self-assessment enable a subject to identify with first-order desires, providing volitional control sufficient for responsibility regardless of whether determinism or indeterminism holds, and even under manipulation. Metaphysical conditions of the world thus become irrelevant when assessing responsibility and autonomy. The paper concludes that the hierarchical interpretation resolves the paradox of moral education, which it characterizes as specific to the libertarian position, and suggests that those involved in moral education should help young people understand the role of the will and take responsibility for their actions even when they cannot act differently.

In Hill v. Levine (1925), the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court reviewed a bill in equity seeking specific performance of a written agreement to sell two parcels of land in Boston. The plaintiff's 1898 deed imposed restrictions for twenty years from August 20, 1896, and separately stated that the grantee could re-divide the land into lots with no frontage of less than fifty feet. The dispute centered on whether the fifty-foot frontage restriction expired in twenty years or thirty years, and whether this doubt excused the defendant from purchasing. The Superior Court dismissed the bill, finding the restriction's duration open to reasonable doubt. On appeal, the court held the frontage provision was a personal agreement between the original grantor and grantee, not intended to benefit other lot owners, and did not create an equitable easement appurtenant to remaining lots. The mere possibility of future claims by others did not justify denying specific performance. The decree was reversed and specific performance ordered.

Maldives President Yameen Abdul Gayoom said Saturday he is willing to hold an early presidential election, following a Supreme Court order to release opposition political prisoners—including exiled former President Mohamed Nasheed—and reinstate 12 lawmakers whose return would cost his party its parliamentary majority. Nasheed said he would mount a fresh challenge for the presidency this year.

Marine heatwaves—prolonged periods of unusually warm water at a given location—can occur at any time of year but had received little research attention until a 2015 working group developed a definition for the phenomenon. Analysis of over 100 years of sea surface temperature data shows marine heatwaves have become longer and more frequent, with heatwave days increasing 54% from 1925 to 2016. These trends are attributed to rising ocean temperatures. Recent heatwaves have caused significant ecological and economic damage, including kelp forest loss off western Australia in 2011, Shark Bay seagrass decline, disruption of the Gulf of Maine lobster fishery in 2012, and the North Pacific "Blob" (2014-2016), which caused fishery closures and harmful algal blooms. Anthropogenic climate change has made some events substantially more likely, such as the 2016 tropical Australia heatwave that bleached the Great Barrier Reef. Scientists aim to develop forecasts to help manage risks, while emphasizing the need to curb greenhouse gas emissions.

Scientists used stored sperm from Sudan, the last male northern white rhino who died in March, to fertilize eggs from southern white rhinos, creating two frozen hybrid embryos—the first lab-grown rhino embryos viable for implantation, though the transfer procedure remains undeveloped. Researchers await permission to collect eggs from the two remaining females, Fatu and Najin, aiming for a calf within three years. Alternatives include breeding to dilute southern genes, embryonic stem cell lines, and inducing sperm and eggs from blood or skin cells. Some conservationists view the technology as speculative.

This passage is a lecture transcript discussing Kerberos, a cryptographically secure protocol for authenticating computers and applications to one another over a network. Developed at MIT roughly 25-30 years ago as part of Project Athena, it was designed to authenticate users on workstations to distributed servers (such as file, mail, and print servers) without trusting the network. It remains in use at MIT and forms the basis of Microsoft's Active Directory.

The trust model requires all parties to trust the Kerberos server (Key Distribution Center, or KDC) and users to trust their workstations. The KDC stores a shared key for every entity in its realm, mapping cryptographic keys to string names called principals. Client keys are derived from user passwords. Kerberos provides only authentication; individual services handle authorization through mechanisms such as access control lists. Reusing principal names is risky because services' stored permissions are not versioned.

The protocol uses two interfaces to the same server: the Kerberos interface for initial login and the Ticket Granting Service (TGS) for subsequent tickets. This design lets clients discard their password-derived key shortly after login, limiting exposure to a bounded ticket lifetime. A ticket contains the server and client names, client IP address, timestamp, expiration time, and a session key, encrypted with the service's key. An authenticator (client name, IP address, timestamp) accompanies requests to prevent replay attacks.

The lecture identifies several flaws in Kerberos 4: it assumed encryption also provided message authentication; it allowed offline password-guessing since clients verify passwords by decrypting server responses; it was fixed to 56-bit DES, now brute-forceable; it used one key for both communication directions, enabling reflection attacks; authenticators were not bound to message contents; and the password-change protocol allowed anyone learning an old password to decrypt subsequent password changes. Kerberos 5 addresses these with explicit message authentication, multiple ciphers including AES, separate keys per direction, message-bound authenticators, and Diffie-Hellman key exchange for password changes.

Additional topics include KDC replication through read-only replicas, the catastrophic consequences of compromising the KDC or a service's secret key (which requires out-of-band key recovery), two-step login verification for dial-up machines because they hold secret keys while workstations do not, and the requirement that password changes use tickets obtained directly from the Kerberos interface rather than TGS, so stolen tickets cannot be used to change passwords.

This patent application, a continuation of several prior applications, describes methods and systems for detecting, processing, and responding to speech signals from multiple endpoints simultaneously. In one embodiment, data modules in a networked group detect an activation command ("Hot Word") and compute scores based on factors such as signal power, output of a Hot Word detector (which may use a neural network), the user's location relative to the module, and additional audio processing. Modules with scores above a threshold send recorded audio data to a group leader (Player), which may combine the audio and send a request to an external server. The server returns a requested action, which is distributed to the modules, optionally with an audible confirmation. Processing can be centralized (via the group leader) or decentralized (modules broadcast scores and confidence levels to one another). The system also supports partial processing, capturing parts of a spoken sentence from the best-positioned loudspeaker, with synchronized clocks enabling comparison of signal-to-noise ratios between segments. Data modules operate as Players, Followers, and Renderers, with roles dynamically configurable; leader selection is based on CPU capabilities, codec availability, and bandwidth/latency. A control client may send control messages to the Player and act as a data source. Implementations may involve processors, memory, and various storage or transmission media.

The United Nations Conference on International Organization met in San Francisco from April 25 to June 26, 1945, for the purpose of drafting a charter for a world security organization. Delegates from fifty governments unanimously approved the Charter of the United Nations, the Statute of the International Court of Justice, and Interim Arrangements for the Preparatory Commission on June 25; the Charter was signed the following day by 153 delegates, with space left for Poland. The United States Senate consented to ratification on July 28; President Truman ratified the Charter on August 8 and signed the United Nations Participation Act of 1945 on December 20. The Charter entered into force on October 24, 1945, after ratification by the five major powers and twenty-four other states. The Dumbarton Oaks Proposals constituted the Conference agenda, whose structure included four commissions, twelve technical committees, and four general committees; its principal documents were published in a 22-volume series.

This passage is from the SD Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 and describes card locking, application-specific commands, switch functions, speed classes, commands, responses, and status information.

Force erase does not erase the secure area. During erase execution the card remains locked and retains Temporary and Group Write Protection; after all user area is erased, it becomes unlocked and Write Protection is cleared. On an erase error, the card can continue force erase if the error is "don't care." ACMD6 is rejected while the card is locked; bus width can be changed only when unlocked. A locked card accepts only listed commands and treats all others, including security commands, as illegal; CMD11 and CMD40 are newly accepted in the locked state. Three lock/unlock card types exist: Type 1 (earlier versions), Type 2 (Version 1.10 and higher), and Type 3 COP Card (Version 5.10 and higher). Hosts should not issue force erase when Permanent Write Protect is set (making a Type 1 card unusable), should not set FEP on a COP card locked with an unknown password, and should clear Temporary Write Protect after force erase if it is not cleared.

APP_CMD (CMD55) causes the card to interpret the following command as an application-specific command (ACMD); undefined ACMDs are treated as regular commands. Certain ACMD numbers (ACMD6, 13, 17-26, 38-49, 51) are reserved. ACMD41's response does not contain APP_CMD status.

CMD6 (Switch Function) switches or expands card functions among function groups: Access Mode, Command System, Driver Strength, and Power Limit. It is valid in Transfer State, mandatory for Version 1.10 and higher cards, and functions revert to defaults after a power cycle, CMD0, or CMD6 Mode 1 with Function 0. Mode 0 queries supported functions and maximum current/power; Mode 1 switches functions. The card responds with R1 plus 512 bits of status data. Power Limit defaults to 0.72W. In UHS-II mode, Function Group 4 support is mandatory.

High-Speed mode (25 MB/sec at 50 MHz) is achieved via CMD6, is optional, and requires one card per host. CMD34-37, CMD50, and CMD57 are reserved for command system expansion. CMD8 checks whether the card can operate on the host supply voltage, is valid in Idle state, and shall be issued before ACMD41 for Version 2.00 and later cards.

SDHC/SDXC (CCS=1) use block addressing with a fixed 512-byte block length, disable partial and misaligned access, and do not support write-protected groups (CMD28-30); SDSC (CCS=0) uses byte addressing and CMD16-defined block lengths. The host may lower or stop the bus clock, must provide 8 clocks after the last bus transaction, and may shut down the clock of a busy card. Commands and responses use CRC7 (except R3); data blocks use CRC16. CRC failure sets COM_CRC_ERROR; illegal commands set ILLEGAL_COMMAND. Read timeout is 100 ms; write busy is up to 250 ms, extendable to 500 ms for SDXC in defined scenarios. Commands are 48 bits with a 6-bit index and 32-bit argument. Command Classes 0, 2, 4, 5, and 8 are mandatory; Class 7 except CMD40 is mandatory for SDHC/SDXC. Responses R1-R7 are defined. Three status fields exist: Card Status (32-bit via R1), SD Status (512 bits via ACMD13), and Task Status (CQ mode). UHS-II modifies definitions of certain commands (e.g., CMD3, CMD12, CMD13, CMD55).

Three speed class methods are defined, all optional in this version: Speed Class (2, 4, 6, 10), UHS Speed Grade (1, 3), and Video Speed Class (6, 10, 30, 60, 90). Performance is based on Allocation Units (AU) and 16KB Recording Units (RU), with parameters Pw (write), Pm (move), Pr (read), and FAT/Directory read time TFR(4KB). Classes 2-6 are measured at 20 MHz in Default Speed Mode; Class 10 at 40 MHz in High Speed Mode. SDXC Speed Class uses AU sizes up to 64 MB measured in 4 MB sub-units, requires sequential writes to entirely free AUs, does not support move operations (Pm=0), uses an exFAT-based FAT update sequence, and defines CI (Continuous Information) updates via CMD20. Cards must comply with the File System Specification Version 3.00.

One year after Loper Bright overruled Chevron v. Natural Resources Defense Council—ending a 40-year regime of judicial deference to agency interpretations of ambiguous statutes—three doctrinal shifts are worth watching in the 2025-26 term. First, courts must now use independent judgment to find the "single best" reading of statutes, shifting justification for agency action toward textualism—dictionaries, ordinary meaning, grammar rules, and structural cues—rather than statutory goals and practical considerations. Second, the future of Skidmore deference, under which courts give respect to persuasive agency interpretations, is uncertain. The Supreme Court cited Skidmore in Loper Bright, suggesting it would survive, but citations have declined. Lower courts have applied a "Shadow Skidmore," treating consistency between agency and judicial interpretations as evidence of correctness (Kavanaugh used "buttresses"); this may be a legitimating tool for judges facing technical questions, or the doctrine may become one of many interpretive resources. Third, the major questions doctrine (MQD) was effectively baked into Loper Bright's ordinary-meaning analysis. Kavanaugh's concurrence in the FCC universal-service case carved out a potential MQD exception for foreign policy and national security, possibly laying groundwork for the upcoming case challenging tariff authority under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.

Scale-in trading is the practice of gradually building a position size as the market creates entry opportunities, as part of a planned trading strategy rather than a reaction to losing trades. Retail investors use it to buy additional shares as prices drop (such as dollar-cost averaging), lowering their average purchase price on the assumption that declines are temporary. Day traders scale in by testing the market with small trades and adding to winning positions, using floating profits to cover the risk of new trades. Institutional traders use scale-in to fill large orders gradually without attracting attention or being front-run. The strategy differs from double-down and Martingale strategies, which add to losing trades hoping to break even, whereas scale-in is a deliberate entry approach. Scale-out, the opposite technique, involves exiting a position in portions to lock in profit while leaving room for further gains. Benefits include better average entry prices, reduced slippage, and lower initial risk; drawbacks include the possibility of not filling the full position before the market turns, or losses if the market reverses after positions are added. The article's backtest showed scaling in lowered CAGR but improved risk-adjusted returns and capital efficiency.

This retrospective single-center cohort study at Rennes University Hospital (2020–2022) included 226 adult patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) to evaluate previously established predictive factors for rebleeding. Rebleeding occurred in 33 patients (15%). Among the traditional risk factors reported in the literature, only time-to-event was significantly associated with rebleeding risk in univariate analysis, with odds increasing by 0.7% per hour since first symptom onset (OR=1.007, p=0.026). In multivariate analysis, time-to-event remained significant (p=0.008), and WFNS score was independently associated with rebleeding (OR=2.444, p=0.039). Other factors—including systolic blood pressure, Fisher grade, aneurysm location and size—showed no significant differences between rebleeding and non-rebleeding groups. Two-thirds of rebleeding events occurred more than 24 hours after symptom onset. Patients without rebleeding had shorter times to hospital admission and securing. The 1- and 6-month prognoses were not statistically different between groups, though a trend toward higher GOS 5 scores at 6 months was observed in non-rebleeding patients (p=0.03). The study concludes that time elapsed since onset of headache is a significant risk factor for rebleeding, supporting the need for early aneurysm securing.

This study evaluated the German short-form Speech, Spatial and Qualities of Hearing Scale (SSQ17) as a tool for assessing hearing loss-related quality of life in unilateral Menière's Disease (MD). Data from 97 patients of a multicenter prospective registry (SEMM) were analyzed alongside pure-tone and speech audiometry. Affected ears showed worse pure-tone thresholds (mean 4PTA 51.9 dB HL) and speech recognition (33.9%) than unaffected ears. The mean SSQ17 total score was 6.0 ± 2.1. Cronbach's alpha demonstrated excellent internal consistency (0.960 total; 0.904–0.956 subscales). SSQ17 scores correlated negatively with pure-tone thresholds and positively with speech recognition scores of the affected ear. Compared to age-matched normal-hearing adults, MD patients scored below the 0.1 quantile, and scores fell within the pathologic range per WHO disability criteria. The authors conclude the SSQ17 is a viable addition to clinical diagnostic tools for assessing hearing-related burden in MD.

The article examines calendar effects in long-term Treasuries using the TLT ETF, which tracks 20-year Treasury bonds, backtested from 2004 to August 2021. Calendar effects are recurring patterns in asset performance. TLT has an inverse relationship with interest rates: when TLT's price rises, rates fall, and vice versa. Backtests identified two strong effects: the first seven trading days of each month produce strongly negative returns, while the rest of the month delivers returns double those of buy and hold. Combining a long end-of-month strategy with a short start-of-month strategy yields a 10.2% annual return versus 3.8% for buy and hold, with a maximum drawdown of 24% versus 48%. An improved short strategy shows a 0.6% average gain per trade, 5.5% CAGR, and a profit factor of 2. All TLT gains occur after the close of the seventh trading day of the month.

This scoping review examines the role of inflammation in randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of depression and evaluates anti-inflammatory treatment strategies. Evidence indicates that inflammatory processes are associated with depression, with patients showing elevated cytokines and chemokines, and inflammation affecting neurotransmitter metabolism, neuroplasticity, and dopamine production. Anti-inflammatory agents including NSAIDs, Omega-3 fatty acids, and steroids have shown antidepressant effects. The literature review of 31 animal studies identified NLRP3, NF-κB, and P2X7R as key neuroinflammatory signaling pathways targeted by pharmacological interventions (e.g., Empagliflozin, calcitriol, natural extracts) and non-pharmacological interventions (acupuncture, exercise, light therapy), though most studies were short-term and small-scale. The review followed a standard scoping review framework and searched PubMed for RCTs. Of 1057 articles screened, 11 RCTs involving 907 patients were included, published between 2008 and 2024, predominantly in the United Kingdom and China. Treatments included fluoxetine, infliximab, ketamine, minocycline, vortioxetine plus celecoxib, SSRIs, and lacquer tree, with treatment cycles of two to eighteen weeks. Detectable inflammatory markers included CRP, hs-CRP, sTNFR1, sTNFR2, IL-2, IL-6, and TNF-α. Findings suggest anti-inflammatory strategies may improve depressive symptoms, particularly in patients with high baseline inflammation, but challenges include inter-patient variability, drug safety, unclear mechanisms, and higher costs. The authors conclude that anti-inflammatory pharmacological strategies currently have limited research value and feasibility, recommending a shift toward non-pharmacological anti-inflammatory approaches and proposing AI-assisted monitoring, including micro-robot technology.

A Seattle Public Utilities study found that extreme rainstorms have become more common and more intense in Seattle over the last 15 years, though the city's typical drizzle and short showers have not changed. Using data from 17 rain gauges maintained since 1977, SPU determined that storms once considered once-in-a-century events—such as 4 inches of rain over 24 hours—can now be expected every 25 years, with the new century-storm standard exceeding 5 inches. SPU meteorologist James Rufo-Hill said the findings confirm anecdotal reports and may preview climate change effects. The data will guide drainage and sewage projects aimed at preventing flooding and keeping polluted stormwater out of waterways, as Seattle's infrastructure was "built for a drip, not a downpour." Mayor Jenny Durkan cited the study in advocating climate action, and the National Weather Service said it underscores the need for flood preparation across Western Washington.

The RTX Blackwell Neural Rendering Architecture introduces Mega Geometry, a BVH construction technology using Cluster-level Acceleration Structures (CLAS) built from batches of up to 256 triangles, reducing BVH build processing by two orders of magnitude. It also adds Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structures (PTLAS), which update only changed partitions to handle high object counts, and enables real-time ray tracing of animated displaced subdivision surfaces. Mega Geometry is supported in DirectX 12 (via NVAPI), Vulkan, and OptiX 9.0, on all RTX GPUs starting with Turing. Blackwell's 4th-generation RT Cores include hardware cluster engines with new compression schemes, delivering up to 2x the ray-triangle intersection rate of the previous generation and reducing VRAM footprint.

Blackwell also adds hardware ray-intersection support for Linear Swept Spheres (LSS) for hair and strand-like objects, roughly 2x faster than DOTS with about 5x less VRAM. Shader Execution Reordering (SER) 2.0 has twice as efficient reorder logic and accelerates neural shading on Tensor Cores. The AI Management Processor (AMP), a dedicated RISC-V processor, offloads GPU context scheduling from the CPU to reduce latency and improve multitasking.

Video features include hardware 4:2:2 chroma encode/decode, a ninth-generation NVENC with 5% BD-BR PSNR improvement for AV1 and HEVC plus a new AV1 Ultra High Quality mode, a sixth-generation NVDEC with 2x faster H.264 decoding, and DisplayPort 2.1b supporting up to 80 Gbps. Max-Q power improvements include advanced power gating, separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory, frequency switching 1000x faster than prior architectures, and deepest sleep states entered 10x faster than Ada.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, producing up to three AI-generated frames per traditionally rendered frame with a model 40% faster using 30% less VRAM, and replaces CNN-based models with transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA.

Blackwell enables neural shaders through the Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan, supporting techniques such as RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression (up to 7:1 compression), Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin (subsurface scattering), and RTX Neural Faces.

The flagship GB202 GPU contains 92.2 billion transistors and 24,576 CUDA cores, powering the GeForce RTX 5090. GB203 (45.6 billion transistors) powers the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti, while GB205 (31 billion transistors) powers the RTX 5070.

Digital laggards struggle with goal-setting: company priorities reflect high-level outcomes with tenuous ties to strategy, causing misalignment that a "culture of genius" exacerbates. A data-driven culture aligns organizations vertically, using metrics and objectives to connect individuals and groups with company goals, and horizontally, through common data models and transparent access that enable collaboration. Digital leaders emphasize data culture as a centerpiece, adopting learning mindsets, transparent data access, and clear metrics; their employees' behaviors reflect company values driven by leadership beliefs. Digital laggards show misalignment between espoused values and behavior, hindered by entrenched habits, lack of skills, and insufficient top-down focus. Changing engrained mindsets is the most challenging part of transformation, requiring compelling, well-understood reasons. Laggards are not doomed to stall, and even digital leaders identify areas for cultural improvement. Technologically mature firms enjoy better business outcomes and build strong data cultures on learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement. Organizations typically fit one of four patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, or data reliant—and can target focus areas accordingly. The passage concludes by describing Keystone Strategy, a strategy and economics consulting firm.

The present invention is a driving assistance system for a vehicle that utilizes one or more sensors, such as imaging sensors or cameras (preferably CMOS), radar, lidar, or ultrasonic sensors, to capture data representative of objects and scenes exterior of the vehicle. The system detects vehicles approaching from behind at higher speeds and controls the equipped (ego) vehicle to accelerate to match the approaching vehicle's speed and/or to change lanes, in order to mitigate or avoid rear-end collisions. Such maneuvers may be triggered by the driver or performed autonomously, depending on whether the vehicle operates in a driver assistance mode (SAE Level 2) or an autonomous or semi-autonomous mode (SAE Level 3 and higher). Decision logic may account for parameters including distances and speeds of other vehicles, free space ahead, lane openings, speed limits, estimated maneuver discomfort or time loss, and the presence of emergency vehicles. The system includes an image processor for detecting objects, may display images or alerts to the driver, and may communicate via vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) or vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2X) systems.

Mapbox, which provides geographic data for other companies' apps rather than making its own mapping app, announced partnerships with Microsoft, Intel's Mobileye unit, and ARM to expand into maps for self-driving cars. The partnerships involve sending camera data to Microsoft's Azure cloud to improve self-driving algorithms, optimizing Mapbox's vision software for ARM's chips, and delivering Mobileye's cloud-based road data to cars covering about 200 meters ahead.

Delvin Payton and five other former arrestees filed a putative class action against 19 Illinois counties challenging the practice of charging bail fees (ranging from $1 to $45) above the bail amount as a condition of release, a practice authorized by Illinois Public Act 91-0094. The named plaintiffs had personally paid fees only to Kane County ($11) and DuPage County ($15). The district court dismissed the entire action, finding the named plaintiffs lacked standing, and denied class certification as moot. The Seventh Circuit reversed and remanded. The court held that the individual plaintiffs clearly had standing to sue Kane and DuPage Counties, having suffered monetary injuries traceable to the counties' policies, and that the proper remedy for any class representation deficiency was denial of certification rather than dismissal of the whole action. The court also reversed the dismissal of the putative class actions against those two counties. Regarding the other 17 counties, the court discussed the "juridical link" doctrine, noting that because the fees were imposed under a uniform state statute, the named plaintiffs could potentially represent a class suing all 19 counties if they satisfy Rule 23 requirements—an analysis the district court never performed. The court emphasized that once a class is properly certified, standing is assessed with reference to the class as a whole, and that the named plaintiffs were personally injured by the same statute affecting the proposed class, rather than improperly relying on others' injuries.

The passage presents the 1942 volume arrangement of the Foreign Relations series, edited by E. R. Perkins (February 5, 1962), consisting of six numbered volumes plus an unnumbered volume on China. This paper demonstrates near-infrared-to-visible photon upconversion (UC) in a solid-state system combining a donor–acceptor bulk-heterojunction (BHJ) sensitizer with an annihilator layer. A solution-processed BHJ of DIB-SQ (squaraine donor) and PCBM (fullerene acceptor) was optimized at a 1:3 weight ratio to maximize triplet charge transfer state (3CT) population and rubrene triplet generation; the annihilator layer was pristine rubrene or rubrene doped with 0.5 vol.% DBP, deposited by vacuum evaporation. While 3CT states in fullerene-based acceptors are classically treated as terminal loss channels in photovoltaics, this work exploits them as intermediates for triplet energy transfer to rubrene. Under 690 nm excitation, the devices showed anti-Stokes emission visible to the naked eye, whereas devices with neat DIB-SQ or PCBM sensitizers exhibited no or weak UC. The DIB-SQ:PCBM(1:3)/rubrene:DBP device achieved a saturated UC quantum yield of 1.36% and a threshold intensity of 60.5 mW/cm², among the lowest reported for solid-state UC. Transient absorption spectroscopy showed that non-geminate charge recombination forms 1CT and 3CT states in a 1:3 spin-statistical ratio; rubrene triplets (rise ~5.2 ns, lifetime ~1.4 μs) are populated either directly from 3CT states or indirectly via PCBM molecular triplets, followed by triplet-triplet annihilation (TTA) generating upconverted emission. A ~10% decrease in upconverted photoluminescence under a 300 mT magnetic field confirmed the TTA mechanism. The authors conclude this approach repurposes back electron transfer into beneficial triplet sensitization, promising for optoelectronic devices.

The Marin Nail Trail 6 is a £1100 29in trail hardtail available from Marin Bikes UK, reviewed by Andrew Dodd on February 14th, 2017. It features a 6061 Hydroformed Aluminium double diamond frame with a 68-degree head angle, a 120mm Rockshox Recon fork, a SRAM GX 1×11 drivetrain with a Sunrace 11-42 cassette, Shimano Deore hydraulic brakes, and Schwalbe Nobby Nic and Racing Ralph tyres. It also has internal dropper post routing and twin bottle cage mounts. The reviewer found the bike comfortable yet snappy, with an excellent riding position and predictable handling, and it became his daily bike over the winter. He concluded it offers a fun ride with smart, durable components and serves well as a platform for future upgrades.

In Valentine Vredenburg et al. vs. W. J. Behan et al., the plaintiff moved to dismiss a devolutive appeal on five grounds: incomplete transcripts and clerk's certificate, failure to make all parties to the judgment parties to the appeal, failure to join the heirs of a deceased defendant (M. Buck Miller), failure to request citations upon all parties, and acquiescence in the judgment by several appellants. The Supreme Court denied the motion. It held that three transcripts filed under the same docket number, together containing all proceedings, evidence, and documents, constituted substantial compliance with the law. Appellants were not required to name appellees in their petition for appeal, as it was the clerk's duty to issue citations to those shown by the record. Acquiescence by some appellants did not justify dismissal as to those who had not acquiesced, and any omission regarding Miller's heirs did not prejudice appellants absent evidence they knew of his death. The motion was denied with costs.

The San Diego Unified School District rescinded its resolution inviting U.S. Education Secretary Betsy DeVos to visit after objections from the San Diego Education Association teachers' union. In September, he completed four 2.5-hour workouts with Hall of Famer Hakeem Olajuwon, whom he met at the NCAA championship game in April, at Olajuwon's ranch near Houston, developing his own variation of the "Dream Shake," spin moves, and a jump hook under the "big guards" concept. He also held fan supporter tryouts inspired by Paris Saint-Germain's ultras, pledging to cover season tickets for the five most memorable fans, and visited a Texas high school affected by July floods that killed at least 136 people. Spurs coach Mitch Johnson praised Wembanyama's curiosity and intentional approach to improvement, and teammates noted he appears stronger and more controlled. The Woodland Trust's Nature's Calendar project has recorded 42 spring indicators at over a thousand UK locations in 2017, though fewer than last year due to colder January temperatures. The survey helps monitor climate change's impact on UK plants and wildlife.

Tesla, Inc.'s Form 10-K for fiscal year 2017 describes the company's design, manufacture, and sale of fully electric vehicles—the Model S, Model X, and Model 3 (deliveries began July 2017)—along with energy storage products (Powerwall 2 and Powerpack 2) and solar energy systems, including Solar Roof. Risk factors include Model 3 production ramp challenges (targeting 5,000 vehicles per week by the end of Q2 2018), dependence on single-source suppliers, reliance on consumer adoption of electric vehicles, Gigafactory 1 ramping difficulties, product defects, lithium-ion battery fire risks, material cost and supply fluctuations, and product liability exposure.

This passage is a technical reference section for the DM8127/DM814x device covering power, reset, clocking, interrupts, and peripheral timing.

Each Core Logic Voltage Domain supports multiple Operating Performance Points (OPPs) defined by maximum module frequencies and voltage ranges, changeable in real time via Dynamic Voltage Frequency Scaling (DVFS), though not all OPP combinations are supported. Adaptive Voltage Scaling is not supported. SRAM blocks can enter SHUTDOWN mode, losing stored data, and SRAM in switchable power domains automatically shuts down when the domain turns OFF. I/Os are grouped into independently powered supplies (1.8 V or 3.3 V), with DDR interface I/O selectable between 1.5 V and 1.8 V. A Low-Power Standby Mode is defined, and power supplies are organized into four sequencing groups with required power-up and power-down sequences.

The device supports multiple reset types—Power-on Reset, External/Emulation Warm Reset, Watchdog Reset, Software Global Cold/Warm Reset, Test Reset, and Local Reset—with priority handling and reset isolation for PCIe and the EMAC Switch. Pin behaviors, reset timing requirements, and the RSTOUT_WD_OUT pin are described.

Clocking uses DEV and AUX inputs (crystal oscillator or 1.8-V LVCMOS), 12 top-level and 4 embedded PLLs with frequency limits, and defined SYSCLK/Module clock maximums. The ARM Cortex-A8 AINTC handles up to 128 interrupt requests; the C674x DSP controller combines 128 events into 12 prioritized interrupts.

Peripheral sections provide timing data and features for DCAN, EDMA, Advanced Event Triggering, Trace, JTAG (JTAG ID register 0x0B8F 202F), EMAC Switch (3-port gigabit, MII/GMII/RMII/RGMII), MDIO, GPIO (up to 128 pins), GPMC/ELM (NOR/NAND/SRAM interfaces), and an HDMI 1.3a transmitter, including PCB layout guidelines for HDMI TMDS routing requiring 100 Ω (±10%) differential impedance.

Ángel Bracero sued S. Ramírez & Co., Inc. for injuries sustained when about thirty bags of rice fell on him from a pile in a shop in Ponce. The defendant argued it did not own or control the shop and that Bracero, allegedly a workman, should claim under the Workmen's Compensation Act; the court found Bracero was an independent contractor, and the evidence sufficed to show the defendant had a Ponce branch. The majority reversed the judgment for the plaintiff, holding that res ipsa loquitur did not apply because the plaintiff and other workmen had intervened by removing sacks from the pile, so the instrumentality was not under the defendant's exclusive control, and the record showed no negligence attributable to the defendant at the time of the accident. Chief Justice Del Toro, joined by Justice Hutchison, dissented, contending that the evidence—including a timely warning that the defectively erected pile was leaning and the defendant's failure to rebuild it properly—supported the trial court's findings of negligence and warranted affirmance.

Akamai, a Cambridge, Massachusetts-based content delivery network (CDN) founded in 1998, was in 2011 the world's largest CDN, with over 100,000 servers in 1,976 networks across 78 countries, 60% market share, and customers including Apple, Amazon, Netflix, Microsoft, Samsung, and the U.S. Department of Defense. In late 2011, VP Charley Dublin was charged by the CEO with solving "Akamai's localization challenge": the company's market share declined with distance from the U.S., local competitors in non-U.S. markets were eroding its position, and major multinational customers engaged in "arbitrage."

Akamai used a decentralized "edge" approach, co-locating servers at ISPs. Competition included standalone CDNs (Limelight, CDNetworks), a telecom federation (OCX), customers building in-house capabilities (Amazon via AWS from 2006; Microsoft from 2009), and dozens of cheaper local CDNs. Global expansion began in 2000; by 2011, 29% of revenue came from outside the U.S. A 2011 reorganization created three business units and three geographic theaters to address unclear customer ownership and a mutual lack of market awareness between headquarters and local markets. Specific problems included misaligned products and sales targets (e.g., Germany's 37.5-hour work week; France's consolidated ISP market), the redundant $12 million Velocitude acquisition, globally set prices limiting local competitiveness (in South Korea, CDNetworks held ~70% share with prices one-tenth of Akamai's), and low brand recognition abroad. Dublin had to determine where, how quickly, and to what extent Akamai should localize while keeping certain processes global.

This study introduces an evolutionary hypergame framework in which players are restricted to heterogeneous subsets of a three-strategy prisoner's dilemma with voluntary participation—Cooperation (C), Defection (D), and Loner (L). Strategy selection within each set follows introspection dynamics governed by an introspection strength w (a proxy for rationality), while the composition of strategy sets evolves on a slower timescale via replicator dynamics in well-mixed populations and payoff-based imitation on a two-dimensional lattice. Tournament analyses and Markov-chain-based theoretical results show that under weak introspection, sets containing defection or the loner strategy (e.g., {D, L} or {L}) prevail, whereas {C, L} becomes dominant as w and the benefit-to-cost ratio b/c increase, owing to self-reciprocity that sustains mutual cooperation and improved resistance to exploitation; thresholds on w for {C, L} to outperform {D} and {D, L} are derived. Evolutionary simulations confirm these transitions in both well-mixed and structured populations, with intermediate coexistence of sets or dominance of {C} occurring at moderate w in the seven-strategy-set case. The authors conclude that greater introspection strength promotes cooperation and that allowing strategies and strategy sets to co-evolve extends classical evolutionary game theory to settings with heterogeneous access to strategies.

This study assessed ex vivo antimalarial drug susceptibilities and genotypes of P. falciparum isolates collected from patients with uncomplicated malaria in eastern and northern Uganda between July 2019 and June 2024. A total of 1,113 isolates were successfully evaluated for susceptibility to nine antimalarial drugs, and 1,070 were genotyped using sequencing of 80 candidate resistance genes.

Most parasites remained sensitive to commonly used antimalarials at low nanomolar concentrations. However, susceptibility to dihydroartemisinin (DHA) and lumefantrine—components of Uganda's first-line artemether-lumefantrine therapy—decreased over time, though the changes were modest. Chloroquine susceptibility increased. PfK13 C469Y and A675V mutations were associated with decreased susceptibility to both DHA and lumefantrine. The PfMDR1 N86Y wild-type allele was associated with decreased susceptibility to lumefantrine and mefloquine. Additional polymorphisms, including PfCARL D611N and PfMDR1 Y500N, were strongly associated with altered susceptibilities to lumefantrine and DHA respectively. Elevated ring-stage survival assay results were observed in many isolates but were not significantly correlated with PfK13 mutations. PfDHFR mutations confirmed poor pyrimethamine susceptibility, suggesting limited protective efficacy of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine. The authors conclude that continued parasitological and genomic surveillance and policy measures to limit resistance selection remain high priorities.

The passage introduces InVirtuoGen, a continuous-time discrete flow model for molecular generation that operates directly on fragmented SMILES. Unlike autoregressive models and masked diffusion models, it refines all token positions simultaneously at each denoising step, decoupling sampling steps from sequence length. The model uses a diffusion transformer with bidirectional self-attention and a fragment-based notation extending SAFE, in which molecules are decomposed via the BRICS algorithm with fragments randomly shuffled. It was pretrained on ZINC and UniChem (roughly one billion molecules) and evaluated on four tasks: de novo generation, fragment-constrained generation, target property optimization on the PMO benchmark, and lead optimization. In de novo generation, InVirtuoGen achieves a superior quality-diversity pareto frontier over GenMol and SAFE-GPT, with performance improving at finer time granularities. On fragment-constrained tasks, it yields competitive results using a single fixed parameter setting. For optimization, the authors propose a hybrid framework combining PPO-based reinforcement learning adapted to discrete flows with a genetic algorithm, achieving state-of-the-art PMO results and improved lead optimization over prior baselines.

The passage describes NVIDIA's Blackwell GPU architecture. Its Fourth-Generation RT Core doubles ray-triangle intersection testing throughput, includes a Triangle Cluster Intersection Engine, and adds hardware support for Linear Swept Spheres (LSS), which render strand-like geometry such as hair roughly 2x faster than triangle-based methods using about 5x less VRAM. A new Mega Geometry technology enables ray tracing of highly detailed geometry at full fidelity, supporting LOD systems like Nanite and displaced subdivision surfaces. It introduces Cluster-level Acceleration Structures (CLAS) of up to 256 triangles—reducing BVH build processing by two orders of magnitude—and a Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structure (PTLAS) that exploits static scene objects to reduce per-frame rebuild costs. Mega Geometry APIs are fully GPU-batched and supported in DX12 (via NVAPI), Vulkan, and OptiX 9.0 across RTX GPUs from Turing onward.

Blackwell also features SER 2.0, with reorder logic twice as efficient and accelerated neural shading via Tensor Cores, and the AI Management Processor (AMP), a dedicated RISC-V scheduler that offloads GPU context scheduling from the CPU per Microsoft's HAGS model, reducing latency and stuttering.

For video, Blackwell adds hardware 4:2:2 encode/decode for H.264 and HEVC. The ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1/HEVC quality by 5% BD-BR PSNR, with a new AV1 UHQ mode adding 5% more; the sixth-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decode speed. This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture reviews and applies Wald's equality to renewal processes and queueing theory.

The lecture begins with a review of stopping trials: J is a stopping trial for a sequence of random variables if the decision to stop at time n depends only on X₁ through Xₙ. Wald's equality additionally requires the Xₙ to be IID with mean X̄; if E[J] is finite, then E[S_J] = X̄·E[J].

The elementary renewal theorem states that the limit of E[N(t)]/t as t approaches infinity equals 1/X̄. Although N(t)/t approaches 1/X̄ with probability 1, this theorem addresses the expected value at finite times. Applying Wald's equality requires defining the stopping trial as J = N(t)+1, the first arrival after time t, since N(t) itself is not a stopping trial—one cannot know an arrival is the last before t without observing the next arrival. This yields a lower bound of t/X̄ − 1 on E[N(t)]. The full proof, done in the notes, uses truncation arguments: the inter-renewal distribution is truncated at a value B, the theorem is proven for the truncated variable, and B is then let to approach infinity.

The lecture then generalizes stopping trials to sequences of pairs of random variables (Xᵢ, Vᵢ), where the stopping decision can depend on both sets. This applies to the G/G/1 queue, which has IID arrivals and IID service times. The first arrival to an empty system is a generalized stopping trial, and all arrivals and service times after it are independent of those before. Thus, intervals between busy periods form a renewal process embedded within the arrival renewal process. Renewals can only be defined at arrivals to empty systems, not at departures, because inter-arrival times are not memoryless. This analysis extends to broader queueing classes, including G/G/m.

Little's theorem follows from viewing the number in the system, L(t) = A(t) − D(t), as a renewal reward function. The integral of L(t) over a renewal period equals the sum of customer waiting times Wᵢ. Taking limits shows the time-average number in the system equals the arrival rate λ times the expected delay per customer (L = λW). The lecturer characterizes this as an accounting identity that is trivial to use but requires justification for the limits to exist.

Finally, the lecture presents the Pollaczek-Khinchin formula for M/G/1 queues (Poisson arrivals, IID service times with first moment V̄ and second moment V̄²): the expected waiting time in queue is λE[V²]/(2(1−ρ)), where ρ = λV̄ is the duty factor. If ρ exceeds 1 the system never empties; even with ρ < 1, an infinite second moment of service time yields infinite expected waiting time. Examples show deterministic service times produce half the wait of exponential ones, and a heavy-tailed binary service distribution produces expected wait of ρ/(ε(1−ρ)). The formula is derived by computing the expected residual life of the customer in service (yielding λE[V²]/2) and adding the wait caused by customers already in queue, then applying Little's theorem to solve for W_q.

This study used the Delphi method to develop the first evidence-based, localised school-based suicide prevention gatekeeper training program in China. Suicide is a leading cause of death among young people aged 10–24 globally, and although China's overall suicide rate has declined, adolescent suicide risk remains concerning, with lifetime prevalence of suicidal thoughts ranging from 17.6% to 23.5% among students aged 12–18. Existing gatekeeper programs (e.g., QPR and ASIST) reduce stigma and increase knowledge and self-efficacy, but evidence for their effectiveness in reducing suicide behaviour and increasing gatekeeper behaviour is inconclusive. No gatekeeper training studies have been conducted among secondary or high school teachers or parents in China, and Western-developed programs may not be directly applicable due to sociocultural factors, such as left-behind children and a shortage of qualified school counsellors. Initial program content was derived from literature review and expert consultation and organized into eight sections, including teacher- and parent-specific modules and a module addressing barriers to helping, aligned with the theory of planned behaviour. In two rounds conducted between September and November 2022, expert panellists rated statements on importance, feasibility, and appropriateness using a five-point Likert scale. The study was approved by Tsinghua University's institutional review board.

This passage reports a method for generating and detecting magnetic monopoles on the surface of 3D topological insulators (TIs) using scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS). Building on Dirac's monopole theory and the topological magnetoelectric (TME) effect, the authors show that a radially distributed electric field from an STM tip induces circulating Hall currents at the θ domain walls of a vacuum–TI–substrate heterojunction, generating a pair of inverse magnetic monopoles at the two interfaces. Monopoles arise only in 3D TIs beyond the 2D limit. Electrons emitted from the tip form electron-dyon exciton-like quasiparticles, and the monopole-induced broken symmetry reduces the Rydberg degeneracy of image potential states (IPS), producing Zeeman-like energy splitting.

Experiments on Bi films grown on Si(111)—√3-Bi (topologically trivial), Bi(110) (2D TI), and Bi(111) (3D high-order TI)—revealed that only Bi(111) exhibits IPS splitting (e.g., the n = 2 level splits by ~400 meV, consistent in order of magnitude with the theoretical estimate of ~204 meV), while √3-Bi and Bi(110) show unsplit Gaussian IPS peaks. Alternative explanations—symmetric/antisymmetric IPS series, quantum well states, and quantum dot confinement—were ruled out experimentally. The splitting energy varies with tip electric field as predicted by the Fowler–Nordheim relation, supporting its origin in electric-field-induced magnetic polarization via the TME effect. The authors conclude that the results strongly suggest successful detection of magnetic monopole fields, offering a platform beyond accelerator-based methods with potential applications in quantum computing and electronic devices.

The passage describes NVIDIA's RTX Blackwell GPU architecture and its key features. The ninth-generation NVENC encoder improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% BD-BR PSNR, introduces an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode for an additional 5% improvement, and the sixth-generation NVDEC decoder delivers 2x faster H.264 decoding. Blackwell's Max-Q power efficiency improvements include advanced power gating with reduced state transition latencies, new clock gating that can shut off entire clock trees, separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory, and accelerated frequency switching that adjusts clocks to dynamic workloads 1000x faster than previous architectures. Blackwell enters its deepest sleep state 10x faster than Ada, with power savings of up to 50% observed in a real-life small language model inference example.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, which generates up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame using fifth-generation Tensor Cores. The new frame generation AI model is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM than the prior method, and enhanced Flip Metering shifts frame pacing to the display engine. DLSS 4 also transitions from CNN-based to transformer-based AI models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing, ingesting 2x more parameters and delivering improved temporal stability, less ghosting, and more detail in motion.

Applications include RTX Neural Materials, RTX Neural Texture Compression (up to seven-to-one VRAM compression over block compressed formats), Neural Radiance Cache (which infers multi-bounce lighting from path-traced rays after one bounce), RTX Skin (ray-traced subsurface scattering), and RTX Neural Faces (a real-time generative AI model that infers natural-looking faces).

The Blackwell family includes GB202, the flagship chip with 92.2 billion transistors and 24,576 CUDA Cores, powering the GeForce RTX 5090; GB203, the high-end chip with 45.6 billion transistors and 10,752 CUDA Cores, powering the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti; and GB205, the performance-segment chip with 31 billion transistors and 6,400 CUDA Cores, powering the RTX 5070. This patent application, a continuation of earlier U.S., PCT, and Korean applications, relates to image encoding/decoding methods and apparatuses using motion vector refinement to improve compression efficiency and reduce computational complexity, along with recording media storing generated bitstreams. The decoding method derives an initial motion vector (L0 and L1) for a current block, derives a refined motion vector using either a merge mode-based or prediction block-based refinement method, and generates a prediction block using the refined vector, while entropy-decoding related information such as magnitude, direction, and magnitude unit (integer or sub-pixel). Depending on POC differences between reference pictures and the decoding target picture, refined vectors are derived by adding, mirroring, or scaling differences between initial and moved motion vectors. Prediction block-based refinement applies only under conditions such as bi-directional prediction merge mode, equal L0/L1 POC differences, block size constraints (vertical size of 8 or more, area of 64 or more), and a search area ranging from −2 to 2 pixel positions, using distortion measures such as SAD, SATD, SSE, or MSE; blocks larger than 16 are divided into 16×16 sub-blocks. The encoding method derives initial and refined motion vectors and entropy-encodes motion compensation information. The document further describes encoder and decoder configurations, block partitioning structures (quad-tree, binary-tree, ternary-tree), inter-prediction modes (AMVP, merge, skip, current picture reference), and derivation of spatial and temporal merge candidates.
