The passage contains two memoranda on U.S.-Soviet relations. The first argues the double decision aimed to strengthen U.S. credibility and alliance cohesion, warning that prolonged adherence to zero-zero threatens alliance unity, since the Soviets will not dismantle their SS-20 force and allies may not permit deployment without negotiating flexibility. Heating oil is a low-viscosity liquid refined from crude oil, used mainly for heating buildings, and its demand rises in winter, making it a highly seasonal commodity. Heating oil futures are contracts to buy or sell a specified quantity at a pre-agreed price on a future date, traded on ICE Futures Europe (symbol UHO, cash-settled) and CME Globex (symbol HO, settled by physical delivery). Each contract represents 42,000 gallons (1,000 barrels), with a minimum price fluctuation of $0.0001 per gallon, or $4.20 per contract. At the time of writing, heating oil futures traded at $3.388 on ICE and $3.4135 on CME. A backtest of one strategy produced 168 trades with an average profit of $370 per trade, a profit factor of 2.02, and a 59% win rate. Heating oil tends to perform better between February and August than in winter. The all-time high was $5.2215 per gallon (April 2022), and the all-time low was $0.2920 (February 1999). Prices are influenced by weather, crude oil prices, refinery capacity, and alternative fuel costs. The WisdomTree HEAT ETF tracks the market, and the biggest trading risk is adverse price movement amplified by leverage.

An inside day is a two-bar pattern where the latest bar's entire price action falls within the previous day's high and low; the opposite is an outside day. Inside days occur frequently—about 10% of the time in SPY since 1993 (779 occurrences)—and are more common in markets sensitive to macro news like oil and gold, and on daily bars due to overnight gaps. According to the article's backtests, inside days alone are a poor trading signal. Buying all inside days in the S&P 500 produced only a modest average gain, and adding a five-day RSI filter raised the average gain to 0.1%, still not tradeable. A swing trading variant on the S&P 500 yielded 89 trades since 1993 with a 0.45% average gain and a profit factor of 2.1, but worked only in equities and reversed in gold. Two consecutive inside days produced too few trades (22) to evaluate. The conclusion is that inside days require additional variables to form a potentially profitable strategy.

GMR Infrastructure reported a consolidated net loss of Rs565.94 crore for the quarter ended 31 December 2017, versus a net profit of Rs643.44 crore a year earlier. Total income from operations declined to Rs2,295.83 crore from Rs2,587.26 crore, while total expenses fell to Rs2,487.90 crore from Rs2,623.74 crore.

The passage addresses damages for the unlawful seizure and detention of the whaling ship Cape Horn Pigeon at Vladivostok during the height of the whaling season. Unlike trading vessels, whose detention losses are measured by earning capacity during a mere interruption, whaling ships depend on a brief season, and missing it can deprive owners of a year's return and crew of all remuneration. Crew members, paid by lay, are compensated through their lay in the damages awarded rather than by separate claims. The average catch is considered the best evidence of the vessel's use value and the applicable measure of damages. The passage also cites the Costa Rica Packet case, in which Captain Carpenter's detention caused him to miss the best part of the whaling season.

Google has introduced its first Chrome UI changes in two years, available in the Canary build for Windows behind an experimental setting. Tabs are now rectangles with slightly-rounded upper corners instead of trapezoids, and the active tab has been brightened to white. The address bar has also been rounded. Additional changes, such as moving the new-tab button to the left of the address bar, were found in internal Google documents within the Chromium bug tracker, which were later locked to unauthorized users. It is unclear when these changes will appear in the stable build.

The passage is a hockey coach's remarks following a Stanley Cup Finals game. He considers line matchups overrated when both teams skate and execute well, and emphasizes early-game discipline, since referees set a tone against retaliation and stick fouls. Special teams are vital; both teams' strong power plays and penalty killing make offense difficult, and success depends on confidence and execution. He cites his team's defensive depth, strong neutral-zone pressure that limited passes, and contributions from all four lines with traffic in front of the net. Nieminen and Hinote's net drives pressured Brodeur and the defense. After a near turning point in the second period, the team scored the winning goal early in the third, following Sakic's faceoff win and Bourque's top-corner shot. He credits leadership, tenacity, experience, and the team's response to adversity.

Strength training, which includes weight, resistance, and muscle training, offers benefits such as building muscle mass, strength, and endurance, and supports fitness and independence later in life. However, incorrect techniques and lack of proper warm-up or cool-down can cause injuries. Common injuries include rotator cuff injuries from repetitive overhead motions, hamstring injuries from sudden powerful movements, herniated discs from extreme or poor weightlifting movements, tendonitis from micro tears due to repetitive motions, and tennis elbow or golfer's elbow from repetitive wrist and arm movements. Treatment varies by severity and may include rest, painkillers, physiotherapy, or surgery.

Warming up increases heart rate and blood flow, delivering oxygen to muscles and helping prevent injury; a study in rabbits supported warming up's protective effect on muscles. Cooling down helps regulate blood flow after workouts. Dynamic movements are recommended before exercise, while static stretches are more beneficial afterwards.

Prevention tips include maintaining good posture, stretching regularly, adjusting exercises that cause discomfort, not pushing beyond comfort, stopping when pain occurs, and increasing workout intensity gradually. Fitness coach Ollie Kerr recommends lifting weights appropriate to your ability, eating well, staying hydrated, and using ice, compression, and elevation for initial treatment of most sport-related injuries. Consulting a doctor or qualified fitness instructor before starting a new strength-training routine can help ensure proper form and an achievable programme.

The passage is a press conference transcript featuring players Patrick Kane, Jonathan Toews, and Teuvo Teravainen discussing the Stanley Cup Final. Kane and Toews emphasized that offensive production is a shared responsibility regardless of who scores. Toews noted both teams initially tested each other, with scoring picking up in the second period, and expects the series to improve as it progresses. He expressed comfort with potential line combinations involving Hossa and Saader, emphasizing two-way hockey. Kane praised "Dunks" as a workhorse who logs significant minutes in all situations, offensively and defensively. Toews highlighted Teravainen's steady improvement and skill despite limited opportunities behind established forwards. The players expressed excitement about returning home to play in front of their own fans, viewing crowd support as an advantage. Teravainen said he does not care which opposing goalie plays, noting he has faced Vasilevskiy internationally and scored on him before. Toews described the opponent as defensively stingy despite expectations of a run-and-gun series, and credited goaltender Corey for bouncing back after losses. Kane dismissed concern over his low shot totals, saying he prioritizes making the right play over forcing shots, and recalled sitting in front of Snoop Dog at a Ducks game.

This passage is an NVIDIA whitepaper describing the Ampere GA102 GPU architecture and the broader GA10x GPU family. GA102, fabricated on Samsung's 8nm process with 28.3 billion transistors, powers the GeForce RTX 3090, RTX 3080, NVIDIA RTX A6000, and NVIDIA A40, while GA104 powers the GeForce RTX 3070. A full GA102 contains 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor Cores, making it NVIDIA's most powerful consumer GPU for graphics. Compared to Turing, Ampere is up to 1.7x faster in raster graphics and up to 2x faster in ray tracing.

Key architectural features include doubled FP32 processing per Streaming Multiprocessor, second-generation RT Cores that double ray/triangle intersection testing rates and add hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur via a new Interpolate Triangle Position unit, and third-generation Tensor Cores supporting new data types (TF32, BF16) and Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity for up to 2x AI throughput. GA10x introduces GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling, achieving up to 19.5 Gbps data rates and 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth in the RTX 3090, plus third-generation NVLink and PCIe Gen 4 support.

The document also covers NVIDIA RTX IO, which enables GPU-based decompression of game assets alongside Microsoft's DirectStorage API; display support including HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a with 8K output; fifth-generation NVDEC featuring the first AV1 hardware decode in GPUs; seventh-generation NVENC encoding; the A40 data center GPU for visual computing; and a new Error Detection and Replay (EDR) feature for GDDR6X memory that helps identify safe overclocking limits. DLSS 8K enables 60 fps gaming at 8K resolution on the RTX 3090.

The appellant pled guilty to theft by receiving and financial transaction card theft and was sentenced to ten years' probation conditioned on restitution. The court found no abuse of discretion in the trial court's continuance of the restitution hearing. However, the trial court erred in ordering restitution for all items taken in burglaries, as the appellant was charged only with receiving certain items, not the burglaries themselves. Judgment was reversed and the case remanded for resentencing; the remaining enumeration was moot.

This passage describes an ab initio approach for simulating the spin diffusion length (ls) and spin lifetime in solids, based on a linearized density-matrix master equation with quantum treatment of electron scattering. The method has been applied to materials including 2D and 3D semiconductors, graphene-h-BN, Pt, and RuO2, yielding results in agreement with experiments. The authors extend the approach to treat electric fields along periodic directions using a covariant derivative formalism, enabling simulation of the spin-drift effect relevant to spintronic device modeling. The conventional drift-diffusion model may cause significant errors in systems such as graphene-h-BN and wurtzite GaN, where spatial spin precession substantially affects spin diffusion. The methods section derives the linearized steady-state quantum master equation under finite electric field, comprising diffusion, coherent, drift, and electron-phonon scattering terms, with scattering rates computed from first principles. The drift term is calculated using a Wannier-representation finite-difference technique to handle non-smooth Bloch basis functions and band degeneracies. The paper will compare ab initio results with model formulas for monolayer WSe2, bulk GaAs, bulk GaN, and graphene-h-BN.

On June 4, 2018, Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC announcing it entered into a definitive agreement to acquire GitHub for $7.5 billion. The press release announcing the agreement is attached as Exhibit 99.1. On and after June 4, 2018, representatives of Microsoft and GitHub will present information about the transaction to investors, with slides included as Exhibit 99.2. The report was signed by Carolyn Frantz, Secretary of Microsoft Corporation.

A Middlebury Public Safety officer falsely identified Addis Fouche-Channer '17 as having been at the March protest that disrupted Charles Murray's lecture, claiming he pulled her off Bill Burger's car, the escape vehicle for Murray and Allison Stanger. The officer's name is withheld pending an investigation into whether he racially profiled Fouche-Channer, who is black. After she declined interviews with Middlebury police and private investigators, a judicial dean charged her in May with violating the college's Demonstrations and Protests policy. She contested the charge, providing IT Wi-Fi logs, witness statements, emails, and other evidence; on May 13, the dean found no reason to proceed with a hearing. After graduating, Fouche-Channer sought an apology from the officer, prompting a formal internal investigation into whether he violated the college's anti-discrimination policy. She criticized the process, saying she was treated as guilty before proven innocent. As of press time, no decision has been made on whether racial profiling occurred, and officials involved, including college spokesman Bill Burger, declined to comment.

This paper investigates the feasibility of Vehicular Cloud Computing (VCC) in 5G-enabled urban environments, addressing performance, sustainability, and stakeholder incentives. The authors propose a centralized 5G-based architecture comprising end-users, a gNodeB, a Network Operator-owned Controller, compute-capable vehicles, and a cloud backup node. Contributions include an integrated simulation framework combining urban vehicular mobility traces, 5G communication, task characteristics, and energy models, with a utility-driven, lightweight allocation strategy respecting deadlines and energy constraints. A stochastic coalitional game models revenue sharing under uncertainty, with a proven non-empty robust core guaranteeing stable, fair allocations that incentivize participation. The system model formalizes delay, energy, and cost for the Network Operator and executor nodes, with tasks allocated via utility maximization under deadline and capacity constraints. Vehicles transmit ETSI CAM beacons at 10 Hz and become unavailable if no beacon is received within 500 ms. Compared to prior work, the framework incorporates network volatility, energy limitations, economic incentives, and CO2-aware utility modeling.

Chamomile comprises several plant species used as herbal remedies since ancient times; Matricaria recutita (German chamomile) and Chamaemelum nobile (Roman chamomile) are widely grown. Matricaria recutita has been used in teas for fevers, flu, digestive disorders, and skin ailments. Chamomile oil (blue oil), extracted from flowers via steam distillation, contains coumarins, sesquiterpenes, polyacetylenes, and flavonoids, with typical yields of only 0.2–0.4% of flower weight. The extract, included in many countries' pharmacopoeias, has anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and spasmolytic properties. Used orally or topically, it eases insomnia, anxiety, aching joints and muscles, digestive problems, and conjunctivitis, and is employed in pharmaceuticals and commercial products including soaps, perfumes, cosmetics, and foods.

America's science education faces a crisis: only 29% of eighth graders are proficient in science, down from 33% in 2019, and the share of students who enjoy science has declined, even as STEM jobs are projected to grow more than 10% by 2033 with median pay exceeding $100,000. Although 49 states have adopted science standards emphasizing inquiry, many middle and high school courses still prioritize memorization. The author calls for a "science of science education" strategy, modeled on the science of reading movement, built on districtwide use of high-quality instructional materials—such as freely available open educational resources—paired with curriculum-based professional learning. Teachers who experience materials as students shift from delivering content to guiding inquiry and productive struggle, and students engage in substantive discussion, with all students contributing. District and school leaders should adopt quality materials, invest in sustained professional learning from certified providers, allow teachers time to adjust, and signal that science education matters.

On May 25, 2016, Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K announcing plans to streamline its smartphone hardware business. This will result in the reduction of up to 1,850 positions, including 1,350 at Microsoft Mobile Oy in Finland. In the quarter ending June 30, 2016, Microsoft will record an impairment and restructuring charge of approximately $950 million, of which approximately $200 million relates to severance payments. The actions are expected to be substantially complete by the end of the calendar year and fully completed by July 2017. Microsoft's press release is included as Exhibit 99.1. The report contains standard forward-looking statements disclaimers and was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration, and Chief Accounting Officer.

This protocol describes the Canadian Social Determinants Urban Laboratory (CSDUL), a multilevel, longitudinal virtual data environment designed to examine how social, economic, and political determinants shape income-related health inequalities in urban Canada across individual, neighbourhood, city, provincial, and national levels. Operated through a hub-and-node model, with a central Hub at the Urban Public Health Network Research Group at the University of Saskatchewan and five project nodes, CSDUL will combine the Canadian Population Health Survey (linking CCHS, administrative, and registry data) with area-based indicators, initially covering 2011–2017 and restricted to cities and towns. The nodes will develop indicators for political and economic context, environmental context, socioeconomic context, material circumstances, and health systems. Using a twofold Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition, the project will replicate WHO/Europe's analysis of income-related inequalities in self-reported health for urban Canada and estimate the relative contributions of social determinants, including interaction analyses by gender and racial identity.

Exxon Mobil reported December quarter earnings of 88 cents per share, missing analyst expectations of $1.04, causing shares to fall 3% pre-market. Annual 2017 earnings totaled $19.7 billion on revenues of $244.36 billion. The company plans to invest $50 billion in the U.S. over five years to benefit from tax cuts, and kept its dividend unchanged at 77 cents. Exxon aims to triple Permian Basin production to 600,000 barrels per day. While rising U.S. shale production could pressure oil prices, Goldman Sachs forecasts oil could exceed $82 per barrel by summer. The author suggests Exxon could be a break-out stock of 2018.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K current report with the SEC dated November 7, 2018. Under Item 8.01, the company reported that on November 7, 2018, it published a blog post on its website, which is attached as Exhibit 99.1 and incorporated by reference. Item 9.01 lists the exhibit as a blog post dated November 7, 2018. The report was signed by Todd A. Maron, General Counsel.

In January 1917 diplomatic correspondence, Ambassador Page in Italy reported objecting to an anti-American press campaign and government-fixed coal prices; the Italian Foreign Minister defended the fixed prices as necessary to continue the war, citing England's conditions for supplying coal, wheat, and steel, and expressed hope the President would request Germany to define her aims. Page also relayed Vatican criticism of the Balfour note, alleging the Allies' true motives for expelling Turks were territorial, including a 1913 French promise of Constantinople to Russia and planned Russian gains that critics claimed would impose Russian hegemony on Europe and likely lead to a future war against Russia. Minister Droppers in Greece reported the British Minister considered the settlement proceeding satisfactorily, with the blockade possibly raised within a week. Minister Van Dyke in the Netherlands enclosed a Dutch parliamentary exchange regarding President Wilson's December 18 peace note. In a January 22 Senate address, President Wilson stated the Central powers replied they were ready to meet in conference, while the Entente powers gave a more definite reply of settlement conditions, bringing the nations nearer to peace discussions and a postwar international concert of power.

A meta-analysis of 333,247 adults published in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology found that moderate drinkers—men consuming up to 14 alcohol servings weekly, women up to seven—were less likely to die of any cause than abstainers or heavy drinkers. Over roughly eight-year follow-ups, moderate drinkers were no less likely than abstainers to die of cancer but about 25% less likely to die of heart disease or stroke. Heavy drinkers' cancer-death odds were about 45% higher than moderate drinkers', and binge drinking weekly or more raised death odds by roughly 16%. Effects varied by gender, ethnicity and age: heavy drinking increased mortality in men but not women; moderate consumption benefited non-Latino whites but not non-Latino blacks; and protective effects were stronger in adults 60 and older but absent among those 18 to 39.

IWM is the ticker symbol for the iShares Russell 2000 ETF, which tracks the Russell 2000 index, measuring the performance of the 2,000 smallest companies in the Russell 3000 index—about 10% of its total market capitalization. Launched in 1984 by the Frank Russell Company and managed by FTSE Russell, the index is a benchmark for small-cap U.S. stocks and is considered a bellwether of the U.S. economy. The index is rebalanced annually in June, so its components may change. A Russell 2000 Rebalancing Trading Strategy showed solid performance, and IWM, which trends slightly differently from the S&P 500, can aid diversification or be paired against the S&P 500 as a hedge.

Apple has reportedly shelved plans for a lighter, cheaper version of its $3,500 Vision Pro headset, which went on sale in February 2024 but has not taken off, and will instead focus on lightweight AI smart glasses similar to those Meta already sells. A new Vision Pro with a better chip is still planned, though concerns remain that the device is expensive, bulky, and lacks a clear use case. Meta and Google are pursuing similar glasses, but as of October 2025 there is little sign of broad consumer demand for face-worn computers, with potential enterprise uses noted.

Good Sam Club CEO Marcus Lemonis, who also heads Camping World, purchased bankrupt Gander Mountain (now Gander Outdoors) and is reopening 69 stores. He has called club members "marketing tools," cancelled national rallies, and repurposed the Good Sam Man mascot as "Gander Man."

Cory Stillman says Doug Weight has battled hard in the playoffs and other centermen can fill in if he cannot play. He notes the opposing goalie has made big saves and must be pressured with more net traffic. After a tough loss, the resilient team is focused on Saturday's game, hoping to close out the series, rest, play physically, and acknowledges winning the Stanley Cup takes a full team effort.

Taylor Swift is credited as the sole writer—composing both lyrics and melodies—on 67 songs across her career, including fan favorites such as "Our Song," "Love Story," "Dear John," "Red," and "The Black Dog." She began playing guitar at age 10 and, at 15, became the youngest songwriter to ever sign. Although she frequently collaborates, co-writing and co-producing her latest album entirely with Max Martin and Shellback, she is credited as lead writer on every song she has released. In her 2020 Netflix documentary, Swift said her storytelling is what sets her apart and that she would not be where she is without writing her own songs. The article lists these songs in loose chronological order, from her debut album through "The Tortured Poets Department: The Anthology" (2024), noting album placements and lyric excerpts.

Joe Hadzima introduces the first session of MIT's six-evening course "Nuts and Bolts of New Ventures and Business Plans," now in its 25th year. He explains the course focuses on planning and executing new ventures rather than producing a fixed business plan document, and applies to businesses, nonprofits, and social or governmental ventures. He recounts the course's origin—students requested a practical entrepreneurship class he organized in two weeks—and draws entrepreneurial lessons: having customers, hiring good people, and communicating tasks. He emphasizes two core concepts: creating value and capturing it sustainably, along with the need for people, resources, skills, and luck. He introduces the formula Happiness = Reality divided by Expectations, describes the diverse student audience, and presents the Virtual Ink case study. Covering business plan basics, he cites Eisenhower's view that planning is everything, explains the hierarchy from mission statement to elevator pitch, executive summary, and full plan, stresses that the team must own and defend the plan, and describes executive summaries using the "why this, why now, why this team" framework. He discusses plan content—opportunity, market, development, and action plans—as well as the plan as a financing document, reasons plans fail, and the iterative nature of venture planning, before introducing speaker Steve Pearse on pitching.

Officials at several Texas public universities have instructed faculty to review syllabi and course content and remove anything that may not comply with federal and state laws and executive orders, though what counts as noncompliant remains unclear. Texas Tech system chancellor Tedd Mitchell directed the system's universities to comply with laws recognizing only two sexes, and employees were told not to teach about, discuss, or acknowledge transgender identity. Texas A&M's Board of Regents ordered a compliance review after the university demoted two administrators and fired a professor over a gender identity lecture video. No federal or state law prohibits teaching about transgender identity, and a FIRE senior attorney called the directives a voluntary censorship effort unsupported by law and contrary to the First Amendment. The Texas AAUP is encouraging faculty to report censorship instances to FIRE, which has received anonymous, unconfirmed reports of similar efforts at other universities.

The speaker calls winning the Stanley Cup the biggest accomplishment of his career but notes players must continuously prove themselves. He was happy playing in Finland, but his decision to return paid off. After a game-winning goal, he tried to stay emotionally level, knowing much work remained. In a home finals game, a puck sent into the air off the opening faceoff caused him to panic, and Vancouver's pressure made him nervous for the first time in the finals; he admits he was scared and faked his confidence all the way to the Stanley Cup. He describes the Conn Smythe as an honor, noting goalies Patrick, Ron Hextall, and Ken Dryden on it.

Charles Robert Jenkins, a U.S. Army sergeant who deserted to North Korea in 1965 while on patrol near the Korean demilitarized zone, has died in Japan aged 77. He said he deserted to avoid hazardous duty in South Korea and combat in Vietnam. In North Korea, he taught English and married Hitomi Soga, a Japanese abduction victim. Soga returned to Japan in 2002; Jenkins followed with their two daughters in 2004, served a 30-day sentence, and later settled in Sado.

This MIT lecture reviews Markov processes, defined by an embedded Markov chain with exponential state-leaving rates νᵢ. Steady state fractions of time in each state, pⱼ, are proportional to πⱼ/νⱼ normalized by their sum. If the sum of πₖ/νₖ is infinite, the transition rate goes to zero and the process has no meaningful steady state, as illustrated by an M/M/1-like queue with a "rattled server" and "discouraged arrival." Conversely, if the sum of pⱼνⱼ is infinite, all embedded chain steady state probabilities equal zero. A "hyperactive" birth/death chain example, where transition rates increase with the state, yields seemingly sensible pⱼ values, but truncation analysis shows the transition rate grows exponentially with truncation size, making steady state meaningless; the lecture cautions students to check the embedded chain.

The lecture then covers reversibility: a positive recurrent Markov process with finite transition rate is reversible if and only if its embedded chain is reversible. A "guessing theorem" states that finding probabilities satisfying the reversibility equations, along with the finite-rate condition, simultaneously establishes positivity, sample-path time fractions, reversibility, and embedded chain positive recurrence. Birth/death processes and tree-structured Markov graphs satisfying detailed balance are reversible. This yields Burke's theorem for an M/M/1 queue in steady state with λ < μ: departures form a Poisson process of rate λ (not μ, since the server is sometimes idle), the state at time t is independent of departures before t, and for first-come-first-served service, a customer's arrival time is independent of prior departures. Burke's theorem implies that in tandem M/M/1 queues, arrivals to the second queue are Poisson and the two queues' states are independent.

The lecture next introduces random walks—sums of IID random variables viewed as a process—with key questions being whether a threshold is ever crossed, when, and with what overshoot. Such threshold problems arise in queue overflow, hypothesis testing, and ruin problems. Simple random walks (±1 steps) give the trivial result that the probability of ever crossing threshold k is (p/(1−p))ᵏ. Integer random walks and renewal processes (random walks with non-negative increments) are also discussed, with a note that random walk and renewal process diagrams use reversed axes. For G/G/1 queues, the waiting time satisfies wₙ = max(wₙ₋₁ + yₙ₋₁ − xₙ, 0), which behaves like a random walk that resets to zero whenever it goes negative, making it both a random walk-like and renewal-like process.

Finally, the lecture introduces binary hypothesis testing: with a binary hypothesis h and IID observations conditional on each hypothesis value, Bayes' law yields posterior hypothesis probabilities whose ratio forms the basis for decisions. This framework, relevant to detection, decision-making, and scientific hypothesis testing, will connect back to random walks in the next lecture.

Sanitary napkin use in India rose from 50.7% to 54% between 2014 and 2015, driven by a government scheme launched in 2011 by the health ministry for girls aged 10–19 in rural areas of 107 districts across 17 states, merged into the RKSK in 2014. However, an IndiaSpend analysis found problems with napkin quality and supply, low awareness, and unsafe disposal. Napkins, made by rural self-help groups, were of poor quality in Odisha, Rajasthan and Kerala, ran out of stock in some states, and supply delays reached three months. ASHAs sell packs of six napkins for Rs 6. A Rutgers study found 89% of women used cloth, and 14% of girls reported menstrual infections; 70% of mothers considered menstruation a "dirty" subject. NFHS-4 found 48% of rural women aged 15–24 practised menstrual hygiene. Fund utilisation was 7.36% in 2014-15, 29.8% in 2015-16 and 19.72% in 2016-17. ASHA awareness meetings were often not held due to lack of training. Plastic makes napkins non-biodegradable, and funds for safe-disposal choolas were underused.

In macOS High Sierra, screenshot drop shadows can be disabled by entering "defaults write com.apple.screencapture disable-shadow true" in Terminal, then "killall SystemUIServer". Restart if needed. To restore shadows, replace "true" with "false" and kill SystemUIServer again.

This passage consists of archival source descriptions for documents on US-Soviet relations dated February 4 through March 16, 1983, drawn from the Reagan Library, Department of State, and Washington National Records Center. Most items are classified Secret; Sensitive, with some Top Secret or Eyes Only. Reagan initialed several memoranda, indicating he saw them. On February 15, Shultz brought Soviet Ambassador Dobrynin to the White House Residence, where Reagan spoke with him for roughly two hours and stated he wanted Shultz to serve as a direct channel to Andropov; Reagan's diary records Shultz reporting that Dobrynin called the meeting "an historic moment." Clark expressed skepticism that the Soviets intended to permit the Pentecostalists to leave. The notes include drafting, clearance, and forwarding details for memoranda prepared by staff including Simons, Napper, Garthoff, Morton, Burt, and Lenczowski.

The passage argues that minds, like bodies, require regular exercise and daily attention, and that managing one's mind is a skill. It emphasizes that emotions are transient and that happiness should not be equated with external achievements like jobs or possessions; instead, accepting one's current state is key. Jamie presents a seven-step brain training process: (1) check in internally and label your emotion, which research shows begins emotional processing; (2) practice slow, five-count belly breathing for at least 30 seconds; (3) write down your feelings, then rip up the paper to release them; (4) reframe with gratitude by writing a gratitude list; (5) play a mindful mini game, such as drawing, puzzles, or listening to music; (6) complete a compassion challenge, such as forgiving someone or giving yourself a compliment, which triggers dopamine and boosts self-esteem; and (7) do something kind for someone else, as studies show those who think of others most are happier.

The passage, from the SD Memory Card Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00, describes interface selection, initialization, and command operations for SD cards. UHS-II hosts must support both the legacy SD Bus interface and UHS-II interface; after power-up, the host provides RCLK and waits for STB.L detection on the D1 lane within a 200-microsecond timeout to select UHS-II mode, otherwise initializing the card in SD Bus mode. UHS-II initialization consists of five steps: PHY initialization, Device Initialization, Enumeration, Configuration, and SD-TRAN Initialization. UHS-III (FD624, up to 624 MB/s) is newly introduced in Version 6.00. The specification also addresses bus speed modes, power limits, Application Performance Class, Cache, Self Maintenance, Command Queue, and Low Voltage Interface features.

All communication is host-controlled via broadcast and addressed commands, with two operation modes: card identification and data transfer. In identification mode, CMD0 resets cards, CMD8 verifies interface operating conditions, and ACMD41 identifies and rejects cards not matching the host's VDD range; HCS and CCS bits distinguish SDHC/SDXC from SDSC cards. Cards publish their CID (CMD2) and RCA (CMD3). Voltage switching to 1.8V signaling (CMD11) and sampling-point tuning (CMD19) support UHS-I operation.

In data transfer mode, CMD7 selects cards; block reads and writes use up to 512-byte blocks with CRC protection, and CMD12 aborts transfers. Erase functions include ERASE, DISCARD, and FULE, with defined command sequences. Write protection is provided mechanically, internally, and through password lock/unlock (CMD42), including Card Ownership Protection (COP) with Force Erase Password (FEP). APP_CMD (CMD55) enables application-specific commands, and the switch function command (CMD6) changes card functions—bus speed mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit—via check (mode 0) and set (mode 1) operations.

There are accusations that the Government edited or doctored the electoral reform Bill. A Bill is a draft law, drawn up by government departments under ministers and requiring Cabinet approval before submission to Parliament. Under Section 135 of the Constitution, the Law Commission reviews laws and makes recommendations, which pass through the Executive rather than going directly to Parliament. The Cabinet combines these recommendations with its policies to form the Bill. The author concludes the accusations stem from misinformation, since the Executive was entitled to frame the Bill.

This paper develops a theoretical framework explaining why spatial averaging induces macroscopic linearity in populations of nonlinear dynamical systems. Motivated by empirical evidence that linear models are surprisingly effective at capturing macroscopic dynamics of large-scale brain networks and artificial neural networks—despite well-established nonlinearity of individual microscopic elements—the work extends the authors' prior simulation-based and preliminary theoretical results (which assumed i.i.d. subsystems) to heterogeneous, interconnected systems with spatially correlated dynamics.

The contributions are fourfold: (1) extensions to the theory of mixing stochastic processes, including a multivariate central limit theorem for ρ-mixing sequences, the definition and characterization of residual factors, and extensions to spatially-embedded sequences; (2) a mathematical proof that spatially-averaged state dynamics become asymptotically linear—generally linear time-varying (LTV)—as population size grows, under mild restrictions on microscopic nonlinearity, noise distributions, and network connectivity; (3) an extension showing the limit dynamics are linear time-invariant (LTI) under additional stationarity assumptions; and (4) finite-sample convergence rate analysis showing convergence at the parametric rate O(1/√N) for independent subsystems, slowing as inter-subsystem correlations strengthen, with no convergence when subsystems are perfectly correlated.

The paper also reviews preliminaries on ρ-mixing sequences, formulates the problem for heterogeneous populations of discrete-time nonlinear subsystems, proves the existence of residual factors, and derives relationships between correlation decay rates and the growth of residual factors.

During a Business Insider virtual event sponsored by Fidelity Investments, experts from Hinge Health, Fidelity, AuditBoard, and Mel Strategies shared advice on IPO preparation. Panelists noted companies face shifting investor expectations, new regulatory demands, and the challenge of keeping culture intact when going public. Staying private longer gives companies a longer runway to prepare. Experts recommended bringing in outside experts to lead the IPO process, which takes 18 to 24 months, having the right people, tools, and compensation packages, and surrounding leaders with the right investors. Companies should also work with knowledgeable brokers to unlock liquidity and help employees with financial planning, as IPOs are often wealth creation opportunities.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on July 30, 2020, announcing its second quarter 2020 financial results. The filing includes a press release with the financial results (Exhibit 99.1) and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures (Exhibit 99.2). The report was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. Amazon is incorporated in Delaware, headquartered in Seattle, Washington, and its common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol AMZN.

A Netflix documentary, "Unknown Number: The High School Catfish," follows students in the small community of Beal City, Michigan, as they investigate who is sending harassing, vulgar, and threatening text messages to junior high student Lauryn Licari. The messages, eventually reaching 30 to 40 per day, suggested the sender knew Lauryn and her boyfriend, Owen McKenny, personally. After 18 months without resolution, the sheriff sent 720 pages of messages to the FBI, which requested a forensic examination of Owen's phone. The author criticizes the documentary for not exploring cellphone forensics in depth, noting that phones retain transmitted and received data and that cellular provider records can track a person's movements. The perpetrator's identity is not revealed in the column. The author, an Oklahoma criminal defense attorney, connects the case to his state's "bell to bell" law for the 2025-2026 school year, which prohibits cellphones and other internet-connected devices in schools on a one-year trial basis. While some parents and students oppose the law, the author supports it, citing criminal cases involving teenagers that began with cellphone use.

The passage outlines the basic concepts and defensive "Do's" of the SOS Disruptive Pressure basketball defense. Defenders pressure ball handlers toward sideline, corner, or baseline checkpoints using SET, ON, and SMOTHER techniques, keeping the ball out of the middle "Red Zone." Checkpoints include the corners, free throw line extended, baseline, and half court. When the ball is on the wing, defenders push it toward the corner or baseline; middle drives are cut off ("Wing Turn") or handled via a cross switch between X2 and X3. Weakside defenders assume Helpside I, Double I, or Triple I alignments depending on offensive positioning, ready to trap, rotate, or deny weakside cuts into the paint. When traps are set, the three non-trapping defenders form a Triangle I alignment, and on passes out of traps, all players rotate and close out using the Near Player rule. Off-ball screens are switched with contact, and traps are used against screens, dribble penetration, mismatches, and corner situations. All shot attempts require box-outs with all five defenders rebounding, as rebounding is identified as a weakness of the system.

In this lecture, Hong Liu derives perturbation theory from the path integral. Starting from the master formula expressing time-ordered correlation functions as path-integral ratios, the action is split into a free part S0 and a small interaction Si; expanding e^(iSi) writes interacting-theory correlation functions as ratios of free-theory correlation functions, reproducing equation 4.31 of Peskin and Schroeder. Expanding in powers of Si yields a perturbation series whose terms are evaluated using Wick's theorem, so all results reduce to sums of products of free two-point functions.

For λφ⁴ theory, the two-point function is computed explicitly; at first order, two identical terms with opposite signs cancel. Because direct contraction counting is tedious, a diagrammatic method is introduced, where each interaction factor corresponds to a four-leg vertex; drawing all possible diagrams and converting them to analytic expressions defines the Feynman rules. A simplification shows that the n! from expanding the exponential cancels against permutations of vertices, and each 1/4! cancels against permutations of the four φ's at a vertex, modulo symmetries, with remaining overcounting handled by dividing by symmetry factors.

The Feynman rules are stated: in coordinate space, a factor for each external point, a free propagator for each line, a vertex factor with spacetime integration, and division by symmetry factors. In momentum space, Fourier-transformed n-point functions contain an overall momentum-conserving delta function (extracted by convention), propagators take the form −i/(k² + m² − iε), momentum is conserved at each vertex, undetermined momenta are integrated over, and symmetry factors are unchanged. A second-order example diagram is evaluated in momentum space.

On June 22, 2016, Apple Inc. consummated the issuance and sale of $1,377,000,000 aggregate principal amount of its 4.15% Notes due 2046, pursuant to a subscription agreement dated June 7, 2016 with Deutsche Bank AG, Taipei Branch and KGI Securities Co. Ltd. as managers. The Notes were issued under an indenture dated April 29, 2013 between Apple and The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A., as trustee. Interest is payable semi-annually on June 22 and December 22, beginning December 22, 2016, with maturity on June 22, 2046. The Notes are Apple's senior unsecured obligations and rank equally with its other unsecured, unsubordinated debt.

The speaker notes Mike Peca's Selke Trophy win and nominations reflect consistent, deserving performance. Over nine years in various roles with the North Stars and Dallas Stars, the goal has been winning the Stanley Cup, and the team is now participating in the finals. Unrestricted free agency, used alongside the draft and trades, has added players who turned out well for both the club and themselves.

This paper examines whether large language models (LLMs) can generate valid molecules using SMILES or SELFIES representations. Experiments on the ChEBI-20 dataset for text-based molecule generation and molecule captioning show that although SELFIES guarantees 100% validity, LLMs perform worse with SELFIES than with SMILES, attributed to SMILES' greater presence in pretraining data and inherent representation differences. The proposed Invalid SELFIES Editing ensures validity by removing non-alphabet symbols but degrades other metrics. Using LLMs as iterative post-hoc correctors with an external verification tool improves validity but significantly reduces other metrics, with correction rates varying across models and error types; parentheses errors are the most common, followed by valence errors. The paper then introduces SmiSelf, a cross-chemical language framework that converts invalid SMILES into syntactically valid molecular graphs, transforms them into SELFIES, and translates them back into valid SMILES, eliminating both syntactic and semantic errors. Experiments demonstrate that SmiSelf guarantees 100% validity while preserving molecular characteristics and maintaining or enhancing other metrics, with smaller performance trade-offs than constrained decoding or trained correctors like TGM-DLM. In class-specific molecule generation, SmiSelf improved all metrics, including validity and membership. The work aims to expand practical applications of LLMs in biomedicine, though SmiSelf introduces some distortion in text-based generation.

Fitch Ratings has affirmed Marsh & McLennan Companies' (MMC) Long-Term Issuer Default Rating and senior unsecured debt ratings at 'A-' and short-term ratings at 'F2', and revised the Rating Outlook to Positive from Stable. The actions reflect MMC's multi-year trend of improved operating performance and stronger credit metrics, a strong balance sheet, financial flexibility, and its top-tier competitive position as one of the world's largest diversified services firms, with major insurance brokerage and consulting operations. Offset factors include contingent risks related to reputation, litigation, and regulatory actions, which Fitch considers manageable. MMC held $1 billion in cash and equivalents at Dec. 31, 2016, and a $1.5 billion revolving credit facility expiring November 2020. At year-end 2016, EBITDA-to-interest coverage exceeded 16x and debt-to-EBITDA was 1.5x, rising to approximately 1.8x pro forma for the January 2017 debt issuance. The 2016 consolidated operating EBIT margin was 20%, up from 19% in 2015, with both the Risk & Insurance Services and Consulting segments reporting organic revenue growth and margin expansion. Share repurchases totaled $800 million in 2016 versus $1.4 billion in 2015. Potential upgrade triggers include consolidated EBIT operating margins of 18% or better, debt-to-EBITDA near 1.5x, and EBITDA-to-interest expense above 14x. A return to a Stable Outlook could result from failure to reduce leverage, interest coverage below 10x, material litigation or regulatory charges, or material goodwill impairment. Fitch affirmed ratings on MMC's commercial paper and various senior debt issues and notes, all at 'A-'.

Field-free superconducting diode effect (SDE) was observed in strained NbSe2 devices. SDE, where critical currents differ for opposite current directions, requires broken inversion symmetry and time-reversal symmetry (TRS). Bulk NbSe2 is centrosymmetric, while few odd-layer NbSe2 is non-centrosymmetric. Stress was introduced by transferring h-BN and NbSe2 flakes onto curved aluminum nanoridge substrates. Transport measurements showed significant SDE in stressed regions, while non-stressed areas of the same device showed no effect. In Device 1# (Tc = 6.4 K), ΔIc and efficiency η were symmetric about zero magnetic field (B-even), reaching maxima of 286 μA and 6.76% at zero field, decreasing to zero above 1000 Oe and vanishing by 5.8 K. Other devices showed antisymmetric (B-odd) behavior with polarity reversal under field, and one device exhibited a mixed B-even/B-odd response with an offset, allowing zero-field SDE. A theoretical explanation proposes two independent, spatially orthogonal non-reciprocal mechanisms: a stress-activated real-space polarization mechanism producing B-even SDE along the armchair direction, and a magnetic-field-activated valley-polarization/finite-momentum mechanism, driven by the Zeeman effect, producing B-odd SDE along the zigzag direction. The anisotropic SDE is attributed to selective activation of these channels depending on the current direction relative to the polarization axes. The work provides a method for generating field-free SDE and a platform for studying stress effects on superconductors and developing superconducting quantum devices. Devices were fabricated by heating aluminum nanoridges to 680°C to form curved droplets, transferring h-BN spacers and mechanically exfoliated NbSe2, patterning 60 nm gold electrodes via electron-beam lithography, and measuring with a PPMS equipped with a lock-in amplifier and sourcemeter.

The Beerepoot family, owners of Tasmania's Melita Honey Farm, will have their Mole Creek home, known as Blue Wren Hideaway, auctioned by the Meander Valley council on September 1 after failing to pay rates since 2010, believing the land belongs to God. Councillors resolved in March to sell three properties when $9332 in rates was outstanding; two other Beerepoot properties had rates paid in June. Previous legal action saw Tasmania Police seize and sell an old motor vehicle. Auction proceeds, minus unpaid rates, will go to the family.

OpenAI and Stripe have launched an Instant Checkout feature in ChatGPT, built on their open-source Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP), which sits atop Anthropic's MCP standard and focuses specifically on commerce and payments. The feature launches first with U.S.-based Etsy sellers and will extend to more than a million Shopify merchants, including Glossier, Skims, Spanx, and Vuori. Because the protocol is open source, other AI assistants—such as Claude, Gemini, TikTok's AI, and xAI—could adopt it, potentially shifting the foundations of online shopping away from Google and Amazon for the first time in two decades. OpenAI framed the open approach as merchant-friendly, citing strong merchant demand and the need to scale. Adoption challenges include brands ceding some control over customer relationships and Stripe's transaction fees, which may deter thin-margin sellers. Merchants must supply detailed, structured product data to be recommended, giving rise to "AIO" (AI optimization) as a successor to SEO. ChatGPT's recommendations are entirely AI-driven with no fixed formula, though questions remain about how products will be chosen and whether paid placement may emerge.

Scientists observing brown recluse spiders discovered that the spiders use their spinnerets to sew silk into micro-loops, a motion compared to rolling up an extension cord. These loops significantly enhance the silk's toughness. The brown recluse's silk is the only known spider silk that is thin and flat rather than round, resembling Scotch tape 2000 times thinner. This silk and looping technique evolved to catch ground-dwelling prey, creating a sticky, flexible web that resists collapsing. While previous attempts to strengthen synthetic filaments with loops failed due to fiber breakage, the spider's thin, flat ribbon-shaped fibers offer a solution. Researchers have developed mathematical models and filed a patent application, though no synthetic version exists yet. Potential applications include protective webs for space structures against micro-meteorites, lightweight bungee cords, parachute cords, and other high-performance materials, produced without petroleum, toxins, or high energy use.

Researchers documented rock engravings at three rock outcrops in the Nefud desert in Arabia—Jebel Misma, Jebel Arnaan, and Jebel Mleiha—dating to between 12,800 and 11,400 years ago. The engravings include life-size camels and about 150 other petroglyphs, likely made by early nomadic people who entered the region after an arid period ended about 19,000 years ago. The engravings were created in four phases: early stylized depictions of women, larger stylized human figures, naturalistic animal engravings up to 3 meters long, and later "cartoonish" stylized animals. The engravings may have marked territory or indicated nearby water sources. Excavations nearby uncovered stone tools suggesting links to prehistoric peoples in the Eastern Mediterranean. The findings indicate the region was once lush, with the last lush era ending about 6,000 years ago.

New research by University of Washington astronomer Rory Barnes suggests many exoplanets found by upcoming high-powered telescopes will likely be tidally locked, with one side permanently facing their host star. Barnes challenged the assumption that only planets orbiting small, dim stars could become tidally locked, instead modeling varied initial rotation periods, planet sizes, and eccentric orbits. His paper, accepted for publication in Celestial Mechanics and Dynamical Astronomy, indicates that potentially habitable planets—including even an Earth "twin"—may be tidally locked, though atmospheres with winds could moderate climates. The research was funded by NASA through the Virtual Planetary Laboratory.

Japanese Finance Minister Taro Aso said the yen is vulnerable to extreme instability from rising tensions over North Korea's nuclear and missile programs, despite its safe-haven status, and declined to comment on exchange rates. On trade, he said Japan and 10 other nations should proceed with the TPP excluding the U.S., expressed caution on bilateral negotiations, and predicted Washington would eventually benefit from rejoining the deal.

The Hero ISL 2016 finale on December 18 drew 54,000 spectators in Kochi and 41 million TV viewers per BARC, and was Kerala's most-viewed televised sporting event of the year. The third season recorded 216 million total viewership, a 41% increase over 2015, including 101 million from rural India and over 50% growth in Mumbai and Chennai. Viewer engagement rose over 25%, watchtime grew 2.3 times over the previous year on the Jio platform, and average stadium occupancy exceeded 84%.

Industrial products and value creation processes are complex systems facing rising quality, cost, and competitive pressures. According to an IDC survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers at industrial enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, IT-based simulation, modeling, and data analytics are key enablers of innovation, quality improvement, cost reduction, and faster time to market. Around half of surveyed enterprises already use these tools in product development, production, and process planning, with deployment expected to reach 90% within two years. Data silos remain a barrier, and IDC recommends a holistic data strategy creating a "single source of truth."

Key technologies include digital twins, virtual prototyping, IoT-based feedback loops, and digital verification, which can shorten development time and enable new business models such as "Product as a Service."

High-performance computing (HPC) is viewed by 81% of respondents as a game changer for product and process innovation, rising to 96% among enterprises that have implemented it. Challenges include security concerns (cited by 72%), investment and licensing costs, energy consumption and sustainability (58%), inadequate computing power, and lack of expertise (42%). Most HPC users prefer external infrastructures: 87% use or plan cloud-based solutions, 74% use or plan colocation, and only 6% operate on-premises HPC. The public cloud is expected to become the dominant HPC architecture, with HPCaaS offering scalability, cost flexibility, access to modern technologies, and a basis for new data-driven business models.

IDC recommends enterprises establish virtual development, create unified data strategies, evaluate suitable HPC operating models, prioritize scalability, security, and energy efficiency, and leverage external expertise and ecosystem partners.

Oil prices rose around 1.5% after OPEC+ agreed to a smaller-than-expected production increase of 137,000 barrels per day starting in November, following October's similarly modest hike. Brent crude climbed to about $65.44 per barrel and U.S. West Texas Intermediate traded near $61.77. The decision followed internal debate, with the group prioritising price stability over expansion amid subdued demand and rising inventories. Analysts warned gains may be short-lived due to uneven demand, seasonal refinery maintenance, and slower consumption. Traders now await OPEC+'s next meeting for clues on whether the cautious stance will continue into 2026.

This MIT lecture reviews how requiring regularity of the Euclidean black hole (and Rindler) metric at the horizon forces a periodic identification of Euclidean time, implying that any quantum field theory placed in that spacetime is at a finite temperature, with kappa the surface gravity; the temperature depends on the choice of time/observer (e.g., beta = 2pi with respect to Rindler time eta for a local observer).

The professor explains that in curved spacetime the choice of vacuum is not unique and is observer-dependent: periodically identifying Euclidean time gives the Hartle-Hawking vacuum, while not identifying it—corresponding to straightforward canonical quantization—gives the Schwarzschild (Boulware) vacuum for black holes and the Rindler vacuum for Rindler space. The Schwarzschild vacuum's Euclidean manifold has a conical singularity at the horizon, and observables such as a free scalar's stress tensor blow up there (not so for the Hartle-Hawking vacuum, which is regular by construction). Since general relativity says the horizon is smooth, the Hartle-Hawking vacuum is considered more physical, though the two vacua are inequivalent states related by a transformation, each appearing highly excited from the other's perspective.

To derive the temperature's origin, the lecture reviews two preparations: (1) a thermal density matrix can be viewed as an entangled pure state of two non-interacting copies of a system (Umezawa), so tracing out the unknown second system yields thermal behavior; this state is a squeezed state, with new operators b1, b2 annihilating it via a Bogoliubov transformation; and (2) the Schrödinger representation of QFT, where vacuum wave functionals are obtained from Euclidean path integrals.

For Rindler space, Euclidean continuation with theta periodic in 2pi makes the Rindler and Minkowski Euclidean manifolds identical, so Rindler correlators equal standard Minkowski vacuum correlators restricted to the Rindler patch. Since the Minkowski Hilbert space factorizes into left and right Rindler factors, and re-foliating the vacuum wave functional's path integral in Rindler time gives an entangled form, sum over n of e^(−pi En) chi_n(phi_R) chi_n~(phi_L), tracing out the inaccessible left wedge yields a thermal density matrix rho = (1/Z) e^(−2pi H_R) with beta = 2pi. Thus the Minkowski vacuum, which is zero temperature for inertial observers, appears as a thermal state to accelerated Rindler observers because of entanglement with the unseen left patch; the black hole case is analogous and will be discussed further next lecture.

This phase-3, prospective, multicenter, placebo-controlled, double-blind, randomized study evaluated the safety and immunogenicity of a single heterologous booster dose of CORBEVAX™, a recombinant protein sub-unit vaccine developed by Biological E Limited, in Indian adults aged 18-80 years who had received two doses of either COVAXIN or COVISHIELD™ as primary vaccination at least six months earlier. The study addressed waning immunity and reduced vaccine effectiveness against variants such as Omicron, as well as limited booster data in India, where over 90% of adults received COVAXIN or Covishield as primary vaccination. A total of 416 subjects were enrolled (208 per group), randomized 3:1 to receive CORBEVAX™ (n=156) or placebo (n=52).

The primary endpoint was virus neutralizing antibodies (VNA) at 28 days post-booster compared to placebo; secondary endpoints included safety, tolerability, reactogenicity, and immunogenic superiority. All reported adverse events were mild to moderate and resolved without sequelae, with no serious adverse events, grade-3 events, deaths, or adverse events of special interest; the vaccine was found safe and well tolerated.

CORBEVAX™ demonstrated statistically superior immunogenicity versus placebo in both groups. Neutralizing antibody titers rose at least 2-fold in 71% of COVISHIELD™-primed and 68% of COVAXIN-primed subjects by day 28. Against the Omicron variant, responder rates increased from 43% to 91% (COVISHIELD™ group) and 33% to 75% (COVAXIN group). Cellular responses showed enhanced IFN-gamma (Th1) secretion, while IL-4 (Th2) levels remained comparable to baseline. A major limitation was that immune responses were reported only at day 28; subjects are being followed for six months to assess long-term safety and immunogenicity.

According to the Office for National Statistics, UK median disposable household income reached £27,300 in the financial year ending 2017, up 2.3% (£600) on the previous year after inflation and £1,600 above its pre-2008 downturn level. Median household income had fallen 4.5% between 2010 and 2013 following the banking crisis, and the recovery is largely attributed to increased income from employment, reflecting rises in both wages and employment levels. Incomes grew across society, but the poorest fifth gained most, rising £1,800 in real terms, while the richest fifth rose only £200. Inequality has fallen slightly, though a large gap remains: average disposable income is £65,542 for the richest fifth versus £12,748 for the poorest. Retired households' median income (£22,300) trails non-retired households' (£29,900), with the gap widening again, as non-retired incomes rose 3.5% versus 1.2% for retirees in the year to 2017.

This study examines how Russia's full-scale war against Ukraine affected foreign co-funding, authorship patterns, and citation impact of articles funded by three Ukrainian agencies: the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MESU), the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine (NASU), and the National Research Foundation of Ukraine (NRFU). The analysis covers Scopus-indexed articles published between 2020 and 2023, spanning two years before and two years during the invasion.

The passage provides context on Ukraine's Soviet-inherited science system, its underfunded and inefficient research funding allocation, and the war's severe impact: the number of scholars decreased by 22% between 2021 and 2022, 1,518 scholars joined the army, and GDP declined 29.1% in 2022. R&D spending fell from 0.75% of GDP in 2010 to 0.33% in 2023, and NASU experienced a 48% budget reduction between 2021 and 2023.

Using data on 61,698 articles with at least one Ukrainian-affiliated author, of which 15,179 (25%) were identified as funded, the study analyzed funding patterns, authorship patterns (foreign co-affiliation, foreign co-authorship, Ukrainian affiliation), and field-normalized citation impact (FNCI).

Key findings include: the percentage of Ukrainian articles acknowledging funding increased from 21.7% to 28.5% between 2020 and 2023, and the share funded by MESU, NASU, and NRFU rose from 8.6% to 11.9%. Foreign co-funding was most common in NASU-funded articles (40.4%), attributed to the prominence of physics. Poland led foreign co-affiliation for MESU- and NRFU-funded articles, while the Netherlands led for NASU-funded articles. Russia disappeared from top-ten lists of co-affiliation, co-authorship, and co-funding in 2022–2023, while regional contributors such as Slovakia, Lithuania, and Kazakhstan emerged.

Regarding citation impact, foreign-funded articles had the highest FNCI (1.70 declining to 1.49), while Ukrainian-only funding generally yielded lower impact, with NASU-funded articles performing lowest (0.36 to 0.35). MESU-funded articles doubled their citation impact (0.58 to 1.14), largely due to highly cited outliers among articles authored by scholars with foreign co-affiliations. Articles co-authored with foreign scholars or authored by scholars with foreign co-affiliations consistently outperformed those written solely by Ukrainian-affiliated authors. Regression analysis showed a statistically significant positive relationship between foreign co-funding and citation impact, particularly for NASU-funded articles, though explanatory power was limited. Notably, in 2022–2023, NASU-funded articles without foreign co-funding had citation impacts statistically indistinguishable from unfunded articles.

The study concludes that international collaboration is critical to Ukrainian research impact, that foreign co-funding should become a strategic priority, that Ukraine's funding allocation mechanisms require reform, and that a centralized national funding database is needed to improve tracking and evaluation of research funding.

The IRS sets an annual tax deadline (April 17), with extensions available to avoid penalties. Taxpayers have three years to claim refunds before they become U.S. Treasury property; as of March 8, the IRS reported $1.1 billion in unclaimed 2014 refunds for about 1 million non-filers. Even those not required to file may qualify for refunds or credits like the Earned Income Tax Credit. If the IRS files a substitute return, it omits credits and deductions. Unpaid taxes trigger notices, late fees, collection efforts, possible installment agreements, and eventually asset or property seizure. Making an effort to comply and communicating with the IRS can avoid serious legal trouble.

The passage describes a patent for a laser diode proximity sensor in a single integrated package, used in devices such as cell phones, tablets, and personal computers to detect nearby objects, measure distance, and sense ambient light. Prior art sensors use plastic housings, glued glass lenses, and a central barrier, but suffer from difficulties assembling very small parts, lens misalignment, glue voids and overflow, and optical cross-talk. The disclosed invention replaces these with drops of optical resin dispensed over the light-emitting diode and light sensor(s), which cure to form lenses, followed by encapsulation in an opaque molding compound that blocks cross-talk and eliminates the cap, central barrier, and glue. The assembly is polished to expose the lenses and diced into individual packages, offering lower cost, greater ruggedness, simplified manufacturing, and higher yields. Alternative embodiments include an added glass lens with black glue to block cross-talk, a protective baffle or grounded metal cap, an LED mounted on a separate conductive lead with data and reference light sensors for calibration to improve accuracy and avoid false results, and a removable "sensor stick" containing environmental, light, proximity, motion, and wireless connectivity sensors that plugs into computing devices, allowing users to add sensing capabilities to lower-cost phones or computers without batteries, drawing power from the host device.

Bot Store, Automation Anywhere's online marketplace for off-the-shelf plug-n-play bots, has grown 100 percent in bot numbers within two months of launch. The most popular category is artificial intelligence with 24 bots, and the speech-to-text bot leads downloads. Finance and accounting is the most common business process, with "allocate payments against outstanding invoices" the most visited bot, and SAP is the most prevalent application with 31 bots. With the addition of Automation Anywhere IQ Bot, developers and partners can now offer native computer vision, natural language processing, and machine learning capabilities, and several have contributed pre-trained cognitive bots to automate document-centric processes such as utility bills, bank statements, 1040 forms and W4 forms. The bots run on the Automation Anywhere Enterprise platform and can be combined to automate complex business processes.

Colorado Governor John Hickenlooper will testify on February 14 before California's State Governance and Finance Committee about Colorado's experience implementing a recreational cannabis system, including taxes and regulatory timelines. California, which legalized recreational cannabis last November, has until January 1, 2018 under Proposition 64 to establish its regulatory structure. State Senator Mike McGuire, chairing the hearing, stated that the timeframe is unrealistic and that the Track and Trace program will not be in place by January 1. The hearing aims to help California officials understand tax compliance, retailer challenges, and implementation timelines.

Arsenal face Tottenham in the 50th North London derby of Arsene Wenger's reign, having won 18, drawn 21 and lost 10 of the previous 49. Arsenal aim to hinder Tottenham's title pursuit of leaders Chelsea. A Tottenham fan predicts a tight 2-1 home win, sees midfield as decisive, and calls it the biggest British derby after the Auld Firm. An Arsenal supporter says the FA Cup win has boosted confidence, with the focus on securing a top-four finish and preventing a Spurs title, though most fans still believe Wenger should leave, potentially after a Wembley victory.

Research commissioned by the Association of British Insurers after the Grenfell Tower fire, which killed at least 71 people, found fire safety tests on building materials inadequate. Test fires use only wood, while actual fires contain 20 percent plastic and burn 100 degrees Celsius hotter. Cladding is tested sealed under manufacturer conditions, unlike real installations. The ABI called for testing reform and mandatory sprinklers.

A new life sciences venture capital firm led by a former Flagship associate and backed by private equity billionaire Tony James launched today, the firm told STAT exclusively. The remainder of the passage consists of biotech and pharma news headlines—covering topics such as Pfizer's White House praise, Sarepta's Medicaid coverage setback, Amgen's cholesterol shot results, pharma tariffs, and digital health M&A—without additional detail.

Three researchers—Jacques Dubochet, Joachim Frank, and Richard Henderson—won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing cryo-electron microscopy, a technique that allows scientists to visualize biomolecules in detail by freezing them mid-movement. Dubochet vitrified water in samples, Frank developed mathematical models to sharpen images, and Henderson produced a 3-D protein image at atomic resolution in 1990. The technology enables study of molecular interactions down to individual atoms and is significant for understanding life's chemistry and pharmaceutical development. The $1.1 million prize was announced alongside the medicine prize for circadian rhythm research and the physics prize for gravitational wave detection.

A developmental scientist who studies children's trust argues that parents need not fear children's belief in Santa or its eventual demise. Most children believe in Santa, even in households that do not endorse the myth, and most abandon the belief by age eight as cognitive development leads them to notice Santa's impossible, magical qualities. Parents can extend the belief with plausible explanations, redirect questions back to children, or provide disconfirming evidence, but the belief inevitably becomes unsustainable. Research indicates children generally react positively to discovering the truth—often more so than their parents—and a single well-intentioned lie is unlikely to damage trust, especially as children learn some lies are told with good intentions. Fantastical beliefs are associated with positive developmental outcomes, and the author recommends modest gifts from Santa, with larger ones from parents, so every child feels loved by Santa.

Hawking submitted his final paper, co-authored with Thomas Hertog, 10 days before his death at 76. The paper proposes an alternate multiverse theory model, suggesting infinite parallel universes and that our universe will eventually die out. It is under consideration by a leading journal. Hawking never won a Nobel Prize, which isn't given posthumously.

This document specifies the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for AMD SEV-ES (Secure Encrypted Virtualization - Encrypted State) and SEV-SNP (Secure Nested Paging) guests. SEV-ES and SEV-SNP encrypt guest register state during world switches, preventing hypervisor access or modification. VMEXITs are classified as Automatic Exits (AE) or Non-Automatic Exits (NAE); NAE events trigger a #VC exception, allowing the guest to selectively share register state with the hypervisor through the GHCB. The document standardizes the GHCB memory area (a 4KB decrypted page), required NAE events, minimum guest state exposure, and actions such as NMI handling and SMP booting.

Version 2 introduces hypervisor feature advertisement via a 52-bit FEATURES bitmap returned through the GHCB MSR protocol, along with initial SEV-SNP support. Revision history records changes including 64-bit guest request message sequence numbers in the Secrets Page, a VLEK certificate GUID, new error codes, Page State Change support for SEV-ES guests, APIC ID list retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, SEV-TIO trusted IO, and Secure AVIC support.

The GHCB MSR protocol (via MSR 0xc001_0130, which the hypervisor must not intercept) handles protocol negotiation, SEV information and CPUID requests, AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration (required for SEV-SNP guests before first use, with preferred-GPA request and unregistration options), page state changes, Run VMPL requests, and termination requests.

Defined NAE events include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO access, Page State Change (private/shared requests and PSMASH/UNSMASH hints), SNP Guest Request and Extended Guest Request (certificate data identified by GUIDs), SNP AP Creation (creating, updating, or destroying AP vCPU state via VMSA pages, enabling vCPU hotplug), #HV doorbell page, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Request, Secure AVIC backing page registration, and Termination Request.

Additional sections cover SMP booting (AP reset hold and AP jump table mechanisms), NMI handling (the hypervisor must not intercept IRET and must intercept #DB, with the guest sending an "NMI Complete" message), debug register virtualization or DR7 caching, and note that SMM and nested virtualization are not supported. The #HV doorbell page, used with Restricted Injection, contains PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields for host-to-guest notification, with defined host and guest behaviors for interrupt presentation, acknowledgment, and end-of-interrupt handling.

This patent application, a continuation of prior applications entitled "Pin Trap Mechanism for Surgical Linear Cutter," describes linear surgical staplers (linear cutters) used to clamp tissue, cut through it, and simultaneously drive staples to seal the severed layers, such as in gastrointestinal anastomosis. The stapler comprises a cartridge half supporting a staple cartridge and an anvil half supporting an anvil plate with staple-forming pockets, which are clamped together by a clamp lever and fired via a firing assembly containing actuators, beams, cam ramps, and a knife member. The document details the stapler's components, its staple cartridge including a tissue gap post, and its exemplary use. The main subject is a series of pin trap mechanism variations for releasably coupling the proximal ends of the stapler halves, including: a translatable slide with an aperture capturing a proximal anvil pin; a proximally-biased retention pin engaging camming surfaces; distally- and proximally-biased locking members with hook portions and release buttons; C-clips with pivotable ejector levers or slidable ejector slides; locking members with camming release and separation surfaces; opposing biased slide pairs; and a rotatable locking member with a torque arm decoupling feature. These mechanisms allow the halves to remain releasably coupled in an open state while permitting intentional separation, protecting against inadvertent decoupling during single-handed manipulation. The application also presents twenty illustrative examples of feature combinations and references to related patents.

The passage is a webpage from QuantifiedStrategies.com listing recent articles on trading strategies for commodities including gold, crude oil, copper, corn, sugar, lumber, heating oil, cocoa, palladium, platinum, cotton, coffee, and orange juice, as well as articles on technical indicators such as the True Strength Index, Relative Vigor Index, and Polarized Fractal Efficiency. It describes commodity trading approaches—trend following, mean reversion, spread trading, fundamental analysis, arbitrage, and options trading—and states that successful traders often combine these strategies. Specific strategies mentioned include a 12-month (250-day) gold moving average trend-following system, a Gold Gap Strategy based on GLD, a Copper/Gold ratio strategy, and a crude oil Friday seasonality strategy. The site is managed by Hakan Samuelsson and Oddmund Groette, independent full-time traders with over 20 years of trading experience.

The speaker feels increasingly at ease as the playoffs progress, attributing the team's relaxation to three seasons of playoff experience, including past disappointments such as losing to Colorado the previous year. He does not consider his team small, noting most players are of solid size and that the team plays physical but cannot simply overpower players like Lindros and Leclair. He sees no distinct speed advantage between the teams, calling both skilled skating clubs. Reflecting on prior finals experience against the Devils, he notes the real thrill is winning, and beating Colorado was a great triumph.

Sebastian Vettel won the 2018 Bahrain Grand Prix, his 200th race, holding off Mercedes's Valtteri Bottas by 0.699 seconds after Ferrari switched him to a one-stop strategy, requiring him to preserve his worn tyres against Bottas's fresher rubber. Both Red Bull drivers retired early—Daniel Ricciardo with an electrical issue and Max Verstappen after a first-lap puncture and subsequent damage. Ferrari's Kimi Raikkonen was forced to retire after being released from his pit box prematurely, hitting a mechanic. Lewis Hamilton finished third after starting ninth, citing radio issues during his race. Pierre Gasly took fourth for Toro Rosso-Honda, marking Honda's best result since returning to the sport in 2015. Kevin Magnussen finished fifth for Haas, Marcus Ericsson scored Sauber's first points since the previous year's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, and Esteban Ocon rounded out the top 10 with Force India's first point of the season.
