On domestic matters, he cites the Washington, D.C. crime crackdown, planned interventions in cities including Chicago and Portland, strikes on drug boats near Venezuela, and an executive order creating quick reaction forces. He also notes NATO's commitment to 5% of GDP defense spending, tariff revenue, merit-based policies, and criticism of the Biden administration and the media.

Childs Farm Baby Moisturiser, a £3.99 cream sold at retailers including Boots and Asda and made by a small business using natural ingredients, has been credited online with relieving eczema and psoriasis. Laura Gray reported on Facebook that the cream cleared her psoriasis within 24 hours, after previously relying on hydrocortisone. Paige Sweeney said the moisturiser improved her daughter Evie-Rae's eczema when dermatologist appointments and medications had failed; her Facebook post was shared more than 40,000 times. Joanne reported that after four weeks of use, her daughter Kelisha's severe eczema cleared completely. The company's dermatologist, Dr Jennifer Crawley, said regular moisturising is crucial for managing eczema and noted the improvement following regular use of the product.

On April 28, 2021, Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC reporting that it issued a press release regarding its financial results for its second fiscal quarter ended March 27, 2021. The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. Apple's common stock and various notes are registered on The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC.

This study compared the 2009 and 2021 CKD-EPI creatinine equations for estimating glomerular filtration rate (GFR) to determine whether removing the race coefficient from the 2021 equation reduced disparities in chronic kidney disease (CKD) diagnosis timing and staging between Black and non-Black patients. The 2009 equation included a race multiplier based on the assumption that Black patients have higher muscle mass; this was removed in 2021 following recommendations by the NKF-ASN Task Force.

Using a subset of Truveta electronic health record data (patients aged 18 or older with at least three serum creatinine values spanning more than 90 days, between January 1, 2016 and September 30, 2023), the study included 8,080,889 patients, of whom 15.5% were Black. CKD was defined as GFR < 60 sustained for 60 or more days. Outcomes were discordance in CKD staging (stages 3a–5) between equations and the odds of earlier CKD identification with the 2021 equation. Covariates included demographics, comorbidities (Elixhauser index, hyperkalemia), and social determinants of health.

Results showed significant staging discordance, concentrated in earlier stages and among Black patients. Nearly 50% of Black patients classified as stage 3a by the 2021 equation did not meet CKD criteria under the 2009 equation, and approximately 40% of Black stage 4 cases were discordant, versus 99% concordance for non-Black stage 4 patients. The 2021 equation identified CKD earlier for 24% of Black patients compared with 0.7% of non-Black patients. In multivariate logistic regression, Black patients were 126 times more likely to have an increased CKD stage with the 2021 equation (CI 120–133), and earlier identification with the 2009 equation was associated with higher staging under the 2021 equation (OR 5.23). No included social determinants of health factors were significantly associated with increased staging.

The authors note limitations including EHR data constraints and the unvalidated use of the Elixhauser comorbidity index in this population, and conclude the results underscore the need to continue examining the positive impacts of removing race from GFR estimation in the US.

Legal experts Shane Kilcommins and Eimear Spain of the University of Limerick have criticised the Communications (Retention of Data) Bill 2017, drafted in response to the Murray Report. They highlighted two absent Murray recommendations: protection of journalists' sources requiring High Court authorisation, and an independent monitoring body to oversee service providers. Ms Spain also criticised retrospective High Court reviews as insufficiently thorough, citing the Irish Human Rights and Equality Commission's view that the framework is "not human rights compliant", though she noted the bill expands prior judicial authorisation.
Oral GLP-1 drugs like orforglipron show weight loss in trials.

A team representative addresses the upcoming decisive final game, saying home ice advantage is not a major factor and that the team has bounced back all year. He dismisses the earlier Ottawa series as over, notes the opponents earned their playoff spot, and is unsure whether prior experience or scoring first offers an advantage. He describes the situation as a mentally draining psychological roller coaster and says the team needs rest. Surprised by his team's uncharacteristic penalties, he attributes them to frustration and on-ice provocation. A player's availability will likely be known after a night's rest and morning skate. He says the hatred growing between teams over a long series is normal and makes for good competition.

Rory McKelvie, a 19-year-old from Biggar, Lanarkshire, was found dead; his death is not being treated as suspicious. His mother said he passed away in his sleep. Weeks earlier, Rory had shared his mental health struggles on social media, saying his doctor told him he was not "bad enough yet" and to return when closer to "breaking point." He also said someone had stopped him from committing suicide in November and urged others to talk to friends and family. Tributes, including from his girlfriend, have been paid.

Donald Trump faced criticism for a tweet defending his writing abilities that itself contained misspellings and grammatical errors, including "poured" instead of "pored." Tony Schwartz, ghostwriter of Trump's book The Art of the Deal, responded that Trump is incapable of reading a book, much less writing one. J.K. Rowling also mocked the errors. Trump additionally faced criticism from Annapolis's mayor for initially denying a request to lower flags after a deadly newsroom shooting, though he later ordered flags lowered.

Clinton County was named among Site Selection magazine's "Top 100 Micropolitans" in the U.S., with the Wilmington–Clinton County micropolitan tying for 64th. In 2017, Ohio produced 16 Top 100 micropolitans, more than any other state. The Clinton County Port Authority submitted four projects totaling $70 million in new investment, 150 new jobs, and 400 retained jobs, which were vetted by JobsOhio and Site Selection staff. The Bright Farms facility is under construction on Davids Drive in Wilmington.

This passage is a compilation of news articles dated November 30, 2001, concerning Enron Corp.'s impending collapse. Key developments include:

- Enron Australia was barred from trading power futures by Australian regulators because its funding wasn't assured following credit downgrades.
- An Enron-affiliated partnership, JEDI, invested $50 million in Costilla Energy, which went bankrupt; the loss was written off and not separately disclosed in SEC filings.
- Royal Bank of Scotland and other bidders may purchase Enron's Wessex Water unit.
- Nord Pool cleared all Enron trades without losses; Enron was suspended from Nord Pool, the UK Power Exchange, and the European Energy Exchange, though it could still trade on the Amsterdam Power Exchange.
- Enron's withdrawal from Europe disrupted energy markets it helped create; it held a fifth of Europe's $100 billion annual electricity-trading market and employed 6,800 people in Europe.
- Federal prosecutors in Texas and New York want to monitor the SEC's investigation into Enron's accounting as a possible precursor to a criminal case.
- Enron's overseas assets, including stakes in Brazil's Elektro and India's Dabhol venture, remain in doubt.
- Dynegy faces pressure after abandoning its $9 billion buyout of Enron; it plans to take over Enron's Northern Natural Gas pipeline on December 12, stating the pipeline cannot file bankruptcy without Dynegy's consent as preferred stockholder. Enron contests this claim.
- Insurers may face over $3 billion in losses from Enron's bankruptcy.
- Enron failed to deliver natural gas to German utilities, according to Ruhrgas.
- Enron traders described a workplace in limbo, making no new deals but honoring existing commitments.
- Enron's Japan unit will decide on power plant projects by year-end.
- US Senate and House committees plan hearings on Enron's collapse; SEC Chairman Harvey Pitt promised a swift investigation.
- Enron's derivatives could test bankruptcy court safe harbor provisions.
- Enron Nordic Energy seeks a buyer; PPL will increase credit reserves for Enron exposure.
- Enron's Teesside power station continues operating normally; Innogy may buy Enron's UK assets at the right price.
- Enron Europe delayed a job cut meeting expected to announce hundreds of losses among its 5,400 employees.
- Fitch kept Dynegy's ratings on Rating Watch Negative following the terminated merger.

A spinal cord stimulator implant is providing relief for chronic back pain. Deanna Conley, 77, endured nearly 40 years of x-rays, scans, and five spinal fusion surgeries. After other treatments failed, Dr. Michael Bottros of the Washington University Pain Management Center suggested the implant, in which electrodes in wire leads placed in the epidural space pulse to stimulate nerves and block pain signals to the brain. A one-week trial precedes a permanent implant with a battery under the skin. Conley no longer uses a walker or wheelchair; maintenance requires 15 to 20 minutes of charging. Dr. Bottros has implanted 40 to 50 patients in the past year, nearly all with remarkable results.

Arsene Wenger has signed Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang for a record £56million, along with Henrikh Mkhitaryan, and re-signed Mesut Ozil on a £350,000-a-week contract, joining Alexandre Lacazette. Wenger says it is his DNA to field all his attacking players, though Arsenal must improve defensively. He argued re-signing Ozil was cheaper than buying a replacement of similar calibre. Wenger feared the Aubameyang deal could collapse because Borussia Dortmund wanted a replacement first. He will not reassure Lacazette about his place, saying players must compete. Aubameyang is not guaranteed to start against Everton after a fever, and submitted a medical certificate to a German court after missing a hearing over the Dortmund bus terror attack to avoid a £900 fine.

Edmonton blogger Barry Kent Winters, 62, was charged June 1 with wilfully promoting hatred against an identifiable group, a rarely used Criminal Code provision with only three charges laid in Alberta in the past six years. His blogs, the Baconfat Chronicles and Baconfat News, contained racist and derogatory content targeting numerous groups and public figures, along with violent fantasies. After complaints and a 13-month investigation, police laid the charge with the written consent of Alberta's deputy attorney general, and the courts ordered the blogs removed as a condition of pre-trial release. The columnist questions whether criminal prosecution is the appropriate response, citing free speech concerns and the Jim Keegstra case, in which prosecution gave the accused a public platform. The author worries the charge may generate notoriety rather than reduce hate.

The Strategic National Stockpile, a $7 billion government repository of drugs and supplies for bioterrorism, nuclear attacks, infectious disease outbreaks, and other public health emergencies, has been managed by the CDC for nearly two decades. Under a Trump administration plan, oversight of the $575 million program will shift to the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Preparedness and Response (ASPR) within the Department of Health and Human Services. Proponents, including ASPR head Robert Kadlec, say the move will streamline decision-making and create efficiencies. Critics, including some public health officials and bipartisan members of Congress, worry it could disrupt distribution relationships with state and local agencies, politicize purchasing decisions, and favor expensive specialized drugs. Lawmakers have urged HHS Secretary Alex Azar to maintain a strong CDC role in the program.

The Missouri Court of Appeals, Western District, reviewed Paula and John Larison's appeal of a trial court's summary judgment in favor of Public Water Supply District #1 of Andrew County on their personal injury and loss of consortium claims. Mrs. Larison was injured on September 27, 1997, when a water meter lid slid off its well as she stepped on it while mowing, nine days after a Water District operator read the meter. The Larisons argued their claims fell within the "dangerous condition" exception to sovereign immunity under Section 537.600 and that genuine issues of material fact existed regarding operator negligence, the District's knowledge of the condition, and res ipsa loquitur.

The court held sovereign immunity was waived as to the dangerous condition allegations and that a genuine issue of material fact existed as to whether the operator negligently failed to secure the lid, since the credibility of the operator's testimony about his meter-reading routine was for the jury to determine. Summary judgment was therefore reversed on the negligence claims. However, the court affirmed summary judgment on the claim that the District knew or should have known of the dangerous condition, finding it supported only by speculation, and on the res ipsa loquitur claim, finding the District lacked exclusive control over the meter lid, which was accessible to tampering between monthly readings. The case was reversed and remanded solely on the operator negligence theory.

This study examined whether COVID-19 vaccination is associated with audiovestibular conditions (hearing loss, vertigo, tinnitus) using two Australian data sources from January 2021 to March 2023: spontaneous reports to Victoria's SAEFVIC surveillance system and a self-controlled case series (SCCS) analysis of general practice data from the POLAR platform.

Among 678 spontaneous reports in adults aged 18–64 with symptom onset within 42 days of vaccination, vertigo was the most frequently reported condition, followed by tinnitus and hearing loss. Reporting rates were higher following adenovirus vector vaccines than mRNA vaccines overall, and higher after dose 1 than dose 2 for adenovirus vector vaccines, with no dose difference observed for mRNA vaccines.

SCCS analysis found an increased relative incidence of audiovestibular conditions following both vaccine types. Specifically, vertigo risk increased following mRNA vaccines, tinnitus risk increased following both adenovirus vector and mRNA vaccines, but no increased risk of hearing loss was found for either vaccine type. SAEFVIC reports showed higher rates in females, while GP data showed no difference between sexes.

The authors note COVID-19 infection as a potential confounder and conclude that healthcare providers should be aware of these potential adverse events when counselling patients.

The Higgs boson was discovered experimentally at the LHC in 2012, though the mechanism was proposed theoretically in the mid-1960s by Peter Higgs and others to give masses to the W and Z bosons, and potentially to fermions. Adding explicit mass terms for spin-1 gauge fields breaks local gauge invariance, so masses are instead generated through spontaneous symmetry breaking. In a toy model with a complex scalar field and a potential where mu squared is less than 0, the vacuum expectation value v breaks the symmetry, yielding a gauge boson mass equal to the coupling strength times v, a massive scalar field, and a massless Goldstone boson. Using unitary gauge, the Goldstone boson is removed and absorbed as the longitudinal polarization of the massive gauge boson, equivalent to acquiring mass. For the Standard Model's SU(2)×U(1) gauge groups, a complex scalar doublet with four components is introduced, with the vacuum expectation value in its lower component. Coupling the Higgs field to the gauge bosons gives the W mass proportional to the SU(2) coupling times v/2 and the Z mass involving both couplings times v/2, while the photon remains massless; the weak mixing angle relates the W and Z masses. The three Goldstone bosons are absorbed into the W+, W-, and Z bosons, and one additional massive scalar Higgs boson remains, which was finally observed in 2012.

During a BCom (Hons) third semester Corporate Law exam on Monday, students at Indore centres were mistakenly given Corporate Accounts question papers. Devi Ahilya Vishwavidyalaya replaced the papers after being informed, delaying the exam by about 30 minutes. As the Corporate Accounts exam is scheduled for December 18, the error was technically a leak, but university officials denied this, saying the bundles were opened mistakenly but not distributed. The vice-chancellor said the paper set would be changed if complaints arise. DAVV also rejected colleges' demand to shift BCom (Hons) to the semester system, retaining the annual system.

Gold steadied below $1,250 an ounce on Monday after its biggest weekly drop since May, ahead of an expected U.S. Federal Reserve rate hike this week. Spot gold was at $1,247.48 an ounce. Money managers sharply cut net long positions in COMEX gold and silver, with silver net positions falling by a record 34,915 contracts. Silver fell 0.4 percent to $15.77 an ounce, platinum to $886.40, and palladium to $1,004.10.

Fire departments are holding education sessions in October for Fire Prevention month, themed "Every Second counts – know two ways out." Officials warn against blocking doors in cold weather, teach children how to respond when alarms go off, and encourage parents to discuss fire dangers and rehearse home fire drills.

Disparities in basic education quality across China, including the "siphon effect" that draws students and teachers from economically depressed areas to resource-rich cities like Beijing and Tianjin, have led to the formation of education groups—collaborative arrangements between affluent and impoverished schools aimed at balanced educational development. These groups are typically organized around prestigious "core schools" with "ordinary schools" as branch campuses, where core schools send administrators and anchor teachers to provide guidance and training.

Education groups have produced several positive outcomes: they enhance member schools' overall quality through resource sharing and coordinated teaching research; improve teachers' job satisfaction and professional competence (with over 90% of surveyed teachers in Shanghai's Jing'an District reporting improved abilities); facilitate students' comprehensive development through innovative teaching and inter-school activities; and alleviate public anxiety over "school picking" by making prestigious schools more accessible.

However, education groups face problems: core schools' cultural imposition may erase non-core schools' individual characteristics; ordinary schools struggle to apply prestigious schools' educational philosophies due to disparities in teacher and student abilities; and core school management may lack motivation due to resource strain from expansion and evaluation burdens.

Suggested improvements include establishing equal, democratic relationships among member schools through a standing committee; strengthening team building via teacher rotation incentives and online resource sharing platforms; and securing government policy and financial support, including covering operational costs and rewarding contributing teachers.

The passage concludes that education groups represent a novel "deep cooperation" experiment in school administration, though balancing cooperation with preserving individual school characteristics requires further study.

This passage documents the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) specification. It begins with GHCB negotiation examples for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests: the hypervisor sets VMCB offset 0x00a0 before launching a vCPU, the guest negotiates the protocol version and determines the page table encryption bit (via CPUID handling of #VC exceptions or SEV Information requests), allocates a shared GHCB page, and writes its GPA to MSR 0xc001_0130 before issuing VMGEXIT.

The document then covers Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) events, which trigger #VC exceptions whose error code equals the VMEXIT code. The guest copies required register state into the GHCB, sets corresponding VALID_BITMAP bits, and invokes VMGEXIT; the hypervisor processes the event and signals errors through SW_EXITINFO1/SW_EXITINFO2. Specific NAE events described include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO access (using the GHCB shared buffer at offset 0x800), Page State Change (private/shared transitions, PSMASH/UNSMASH hints, with resumable progress tracking), SNP Guest Request and SNP Extended Guest Request (returning certificates identified by GUIDs), AP Creation using RMPADJUST-marked VMSA pages, #HV doorbell page management, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Request for trusted device binding, Secure AVIC backing page registration, and Termination Request.

Additional topics include guest identification of SEV-ES support via CPUID properties; SMP booting constraints (measured registers cannot be updated, requiring AP Reset Hold and AP jump table mechanisms, while SNP AP Creation enables vCPU hotplug); NMI handling (the hypervisor intercepts #DB rather than IRET, with the guest issuing an "NMI Complete" message); debug register virtualization; and statements that SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

Finally, the passage details the #HV doorbell page used under Restricted Injection: a host-owned shared page containing PendingEvent (vector number, NMI/#MC bits, NoFurtherSignal) and NoEoiRequired fields. The host presents interrupts and non-maskable events by writing this page and delivering #HV; the guest must use atomic exchanges to acknowledge events, follow special HLT/interrupt-shadow conventions, and validate vectors against a potentially non-cooperative host.
The court denied John Whitfield's application for a writ of error coram nobis, finding he failed to establish ineffective assistance of appellate counsel.

Adidas partnered with Refinery 29 to create the "Boost the Nation" collection, featuring one custom UltraBOOST X running shoe per state, each designed by a female artist and auctioned to benefit the charity Women Win. Georgia's shoe, designed by Lizzie Darden, features a peach theme with a plastic leaf on the laces. At publication, the Georgia pair's bid was $350, while Ohio's led at $1,000. Bidding closes tomorrow.

The court unanimously affirmed the defendant's conviction after a jury trial of three counts of first-degree robbery. His claim that the prosecutor unlawfully discriminated through a peremptory challenge against a prospective juror was not preserved for review, and the court declined to review it in the interest of justice. The court also held that the defendant's hospital detention was lawful and that reasonable suspicion justified his continued detention for a showup identification and questioning.

Britain's FTSE 100 closed up 0.4 percent after a choppy session following the formal triggering of Brexit, with sterling's retreat boosting the export-heavy index, which is up over 16 percent from pre-Brexit levels. 3i Group rose 5.7 percent after a Morgan Stanley upgrade, LSE gained 2.7 percent after EU regulators blocked its Deutsche Boerse merger, and miners gained, while AA and Acacia Mining fell.

A returned mail notification from Enron's mail delivery system indicates an email sent by Jeff Dasovich to multiple recipients, including hgovenar@mail.acom2.com, failed to deliver because that address was unknown. The original email, titled "Ken Lay's email to Sen. Brulte," discusses Enron's proposed legislative package to address California's electricity crisis. It outlines plans to deliver proposed legislation to Senator Brulte and simultaneously release it publicly, the need to build a supporting coalition, and PR strategy activation. The email details credit risk concerns regarding DWR's authority under AB1X to purchase electricity, identifying ambiguities in ratemaking authority and contract prudence provisions. Two resolution options are proposed: amending AB1X (preferred) or obtaining a PUC order clarifying cost recovery. The email also presents California's supply-demand outlook, forecasting a 5,000 MW shortfall for summer 2001 with likely rolling blackouts. A four-part legislative solution is proposed: increasing supply through siting reform (SB28X), decreasing demand through conservation and price signals (AB31X), establishing a competitive retail market by restoring Direct Access and removing utilities from procurement (SB27X), and returning investor-owned utilities to solvency through staged rate increases (AB18X). Attached documents include CPUC talking points and proposed AB1X amendments.

Amazon's October Prime Day event, Prime Big Deal Days, features deals across nearly all of Kindle's lineup and is the last big deal event before the holiday shopping season. New Kindles are coming out later this fall, but current models remain good deals. The Kindle Colorsoft, normally expensive, is worth buying on sale, particularly for comics and graphic novels; the Signature edition adds wireless charging, an auto-adjusting front light, and twice the storage for $10 more. The second-generation Kindle Scribe combines an e-reader and digital notebook with three-month battery life. The Kindle Paperwhite (2024) is the overall favorite, with the Signature version adding an ad-free lock screen for $25 more. The base Kindle is a budget option with dark mode and a front light that is not warm. Colorsoft Kids includes a cover and a year of Kids+ content, while Paperwhite Kids adds a cover and six months of Kids+ content for $10 more than the standard Paperwhite.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K reporting that on June 16, 2016, David M. Shannon, 60, Executive Vice President, Chief Administrative Officer and Secretary, announced he will retire at the end of the calendar year. Shannon, who joined NVIDIA in August 2002, oversees the company's legal and human resources functions. Upon his retirement, Senior Vice President and General Counsel Brian E. Cabrera, 51, will lead the legal team, and NVIDIA will recruit a leader for the human resources function.

This study investigated enlarged perivascular spaces (PVS) burden in epilepsy using MRI. The glymphatic system, considered the brain's primary waste clearance system, includes PVS—channels formed by astroglial cells surrounding blood vessels, observable on T1-weighted MRI. Researchers recruited 467 people with epilepsy from Hospital das Clínicas, Unicamp, Brazil: 267 with temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis (TLE-HS), 71 with TLE without MRI-visible lesions (TLE-NEG), 65 with extratemporal focal epilepsy (ETLE), and 64 with idiopathic generalized epilepsy (IGE), matched with 473 healthy controls. Participants underwent 3T T1-weighted MRI, and a deep-learning algorithm (PINGU) segmented PVS. PVS volume fractions (PVS-VF) in white matter (WM) and basal ganglia (BG) were analyzed using general linear models with age and sex as covariates. All epilepsy subtypes showed significantly higher PVS-VF in the BG compared to controls (101–140% increase, effect sizes 0.95–1.37), while no differences were found in the WM. The TLE-HS group exhibited PVS asymmetry, larger on the contralateral side, not observed in controls or other subtypes. No association was found between PVS-VF and duration of illness. The authors conclude that PVS volume in the BG is enlarged across epilepsy types, and that longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether seizures impair the glymphatic system or whether impaired glymphatics contribute to epilepsy development.

This paper presents the formal modelling, verification, and correct-by-construction synthesis of a voter unit that selects a reliable measurement from N synchronous, redundant input units for an avionics control system. In each cycle, the voter selects a prime unit, discards measurements with transient errors, isolates permanently faulty units, and outputs the selected value with a validity status (valid, un_id, or not_valid) and an output age. The fault model covers self-identified health status and deviation faults beyond a noise threshold δ, distinguishes transient from permanent faults via a persistence limit, and assumes a bounded number of simultaneous faults. Sixteen functional requirements (R1–R16) are formulated for fault identification, isolation, and output generation; the theoretical limits of achievable soundness and completeness of fault identification are analyzed, and the proposed algorithm matches these limits. The voter is designed as a five-state transition system with user-configurable parameters. The implementation uses the Rocq theorem prover, embedding proof terms of invariants within definitions so the generated code is correct by construction; verification takes about 23 seconds, and the extracted OCaml code (362 lines) executes a cycle in roughly 3 milliseconds. Future work includes extending the approach to hierarchical and asynchronous fault-tolerant systems.

Dr. Thomas Wilson Ikubese, a 2019 presidential aspirant and convener of the YesWeFit Revolutionary Movement, joined the Alliance for New Nigeria (ANN) on May 29, 2018, after the party was adopted by the Nigerian Intervention Movement (NIM). He had left the National Conscience Party on May 14, accusing its leadership of over-taxation. Ikubese described ANN as the third force, urged supporters to join, and is reaching out to other young presidential aspirants.

This 2023 AMD document is an operations guide for Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM), an engine created to aid page migration—the copying of page content and updating of virtual-to-physical mappings. It describes optional extensions to the Secure Encrypted Virtualization API (SEV) and the SEV Secure Nested Paging (SNP) Firmware ABI Specification.

Tiered memory systems consist of multiple memory classes with different performance characteristics; software optimizes performance by moving frequently accessed data to faster tiers. TMPM offloads this migration and addresses two challenges: it can pause DMA traffic while page content is copied and IOMMU page table entries are updated, and it acts as a trusted agent capable of migrating pages owned by guests using SEV or SNP.

Key commands include PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, which migrates pages that may be concurrent DMA targets (requiring software to provide the relevant IOMMU host page table entry location), and PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST, which migrates SNP guest pages (source pages in Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid state; destinations in Pre-Migration state). A new Pre-Migration RMP state uses a Platform Specific ASID value never associated with a guest. Multi-page commands can migrate up to 128 pages via a Page Migration List with per-page status entries; a PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS result requires checking individual entries, while PM_SUCCESS means all pages migrated.

Performance guidance favors commands of 16 or more pages (maximum bandwidth at 128 pages), keeping the command ring buffer ahead of the engine, and pacing interrupts rather than requesting them per command. Certain structures cannot be migrated, including IOMMU data structures, vIOMMU pinned backing storage, and the ring buffer and its argument pages. TMPM requires IOMMU enablement, and system physical addresses must be 4KB aligned (host page table entries may be 8-byte aligned).

The document details driver initialization, shutdown, and pause/resume procedures, ring buffer operation, and six interrupt sources sharing a single x86 interrupt signal. Firmware can be reloaded via the BIOS-to-PSP mailbox protocol when no operations are in flight; reload firmware must be the same or greater version, and software should verify the ENGINE_READY bit before communicating with the firmware. SPA encoding supports 46- or 52-bit addresses depending on whether system encryption is enabled, with a C-bit indicating encrypted memory.

Errors are reported through command status and sub-status fields; ring buffer errors appear in the PM_STATUS register; hardware errors may be reported via the Machine Check Architecture. Hardware errors during batch processing can render all pages in a command unrecoverable, and memory state may become unfixable, allowing software only to save data and system state before an eventual reboot.

This study examines how online informal education contributes to personalized learning in design education. It reviews education classifications (formal, non-formal, informal, random), the shift from conventional to online education, and the impact of digitalization, which enabled virtual environments, online archives, and synchronous/asynchronous distance learning. Using literature review and case studies, the research analyzes two examples of informal online education: the five-day synchronous workshop "Introduction to Computational Design" by Driven by Volumes and the 21-day course "Sustainability through Computational Design" by Rethinking the Future, both teaching computational and parametric design using Rhino and Grasshopper software. Findings indicate these programs offer short-term, applied, multidisciplinary training with discussion environments and virtual accessibility, fostering personalized learning, collaboration, and professional skill development. Limitations include unequal access due to economic disparities, competitive environments, individual material requirements, and certificates that are excluded from formal transcripts. The study concludes that digitalization has transformed education and enabled personalization, and that informal online education is progressively integrating into conventional education models, though structural differences between the systems currently hinder full incorporation.

Doctors have urged greater awareness of eye cancer, as most cases in India are detected late, complicating treatment. Though rare, eye cancer can cause blindness or death. Specialised facilities and trained ocular oncologists are scarce, with only about 10-11 oncologists nationwide. Retinoblastoma, the most common eye cancer in children under five, affects one in 20,000 kids; early detection can save both the child and eyesight.

A seven-judge Supreme Court Constitution Bench headed by CJI T.S. Thakur held that re-promulgation of ordinances is a fraud on the Constitution and that the President's and Governor's satisfaction under Articles 123 and 213 is not immune from judicial review. The majority judgment by Justice DY Chandrachud held that laying ordinances before the legislature is mandatory, though Justice Lokur disagreed and the CJI left the question open. The case arose from Bihar's ordinances appointing school teachers; salaries already paid need not be recovered.

This study develops and evaluates a model for integrating environmental education into teaching and learning at expanded opportunity schools in Nakhon Pathom Primary Educational Service Area 2, Thailand, based on the theory of multiple intelligences. The research was conducted in three phases: assessing the environmental education situation, performing a SWOT analysis, and developing and evaluating the integration model using action and development research.

The sample included 364 junior high school students, 44 teachers, and three school directors from 22 expanded opportunity schools, selected through Yamane's formula and random sampling. Data were collected via questionnaires, structured interviews, and non-participant observation, with triangulation used to ensure reliability.

Results showed the community faced pollution problems primarily from agriculture, particularly rice farming using chemicals, causing soil contamination (48.60%), water pollution (32.70%), and air pollution (35.20%), along with indiscriminate garbage disposal (49.50%) and cultural issues linked to technological advancement. Students showed the lowest environmental awareness (X̄ = 3.79), while teachers demonstrated excellent environmental learning levels (X̄ = 4.48).

The SWOT analysis identified strengths such as community cooperation and semi-agricultural surroundings, weaknesses including pollution from industrial factories and lack of educational continuity, opportunities from SDG alignment and IT use, and threats from urbanization and climate effects.

The developed integration model, incorporating nine intelligence types, achieved efficiency of E1/E2 = 81.51/82.11, exceeding the 80/80 criterion, with high content validity (X̄ = 4.60) and construct validity (X̄ = 3.97). Post-learning achievement scores (X̄ = 24.63) were significantly higher than pre-learning scores (X̄ = 5.90) at the 0.05 level, and student satisfaction was high (X̄ = 3.83). The study concludes the model is practical and effective, recommending future research develop standards for environmental management education for sustainable development in schools.

A University of Surrey study finds solar energy is now the cheapest source of power worldwide, costing as little as £0.02 per unit in the sunniest countries—cheaper than coal, gas, or wind. Global installed solar capacity exceeded 1.5 terawatts in 2024, double the 2020 level. Lithium-ion battery prices have fallen 89% since 2010, making solar-plus-storage systems cost-competitive with gas power plants. However, grid congestion and integration remain challenges, as seen in California and China. Researchers say smart grids, AI forecasting, material innovations such as perovskite solar cells, and sustained policy support are essential to accelerate the clean energy transition.

The passage contains an 1893 notice by Mr. Kung-i of Pai-ling Shan denouncing foreign religions as rebellion against heaven and delusive mockery, accusing Christians of hypocrisy, greed, and improper conduct, and ordering them to depart or face attack by patriots on the seventh of the third moon. It praises the Eastern doctrine of propriety and urges followers to burn the foreign books. A second document, a dispatch from Mr. Heard to Mr. Gresham, reports that on April 4 followers of Confucius in Seoul petitioned the King, claiming the Tong Hâk spread false doctrines corrupting the people and asking that they be compelled to return to the right path or be exterminated. The King replied that the Government would handle the matter and admonished the petitioners to devote themselves to their own principles.

On January 26, 2015, Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2014, via a press release furnished as Exhibit 99.1. Per General Instruction B.2, the information is not deemed "filed" under Section 18 of the Exchange Act. The report was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration, and Chief Accounting Officer.

A non-inverting comparator with hysteresis uses a two-resistor network and VREF. The output switches high when VIN rises above VIN1 and low when VIN drops below VIN2; hysteresis equals their difference.

A delegation of 11 visitors from Ibigawa, Japan, St. George's sister city of nearly three decades, arrived to participate in the 41st annual St. George Marathon. The group, including four runners, was welcomed by Mayor Jon Pike and local officials at a reception, recognized at a City Council meeting, and honored at an international luncheon. Runners include elite entrants Kenji Miyazaki and Mitsue Tomita, along with Nobuchika and Mina Tsuboi of Ibigawa. The delegates are staying with host families and touring local sites. St. George will send a delegation to Japan next month for the 30th annual Ibigawa Marathon.

The passage describes a bull market signal: 18 consecutive closes above the 200-day simple moving average during a bear market, which historically predicts the end of bear markets. The trading rules sell the S&P 500 when it drops 20% from its all-time high and buy after the signal. Backtested on the S&P 500 from 1927, the strategy generated 12 signals—one per bear market—with a 7.24% CAGR, 0.24 Sharpe ratio, 60% maximum drawdown (about 25% excluding the 1929 crash), and 87.38% time in the market. After the signal, the S&P 500 rose an average of 9.54% in six months and 21.84% in one year, being up 100% of the time after 12 months. Compared to the golden cross strategy, it produced fewer signals (12 vs. 49) and performed better, though not on a risk-adjusted basis. The signal last triggered on February 15, 2023. The passage also promotes the blog's compilation of backtested trading rules.

Rain Bird's 9v WPX battery-operated irrigation controller suits locations without mains power. Fully waterproof and submersible, it offers 1-6 zone models, LCD programming, Contractor Rapid Programming™, zone-stacking, and operates one to two years on batteries.
A hockey player describes scoring on an open net after Teemu fed him a pass while coming off the bench, and says the team stayed disciplined in the third period to finish the game.

A study led by Jonathan Rolland of the University of British Columbia found that birds and mammals adapt to temperature changes two to three times faster than reptiles and amphibians. Using about 300,000 million data points from nearly 11,500 species, the team reconstructed habitats over 270 million years. Traits like self-regulated body temperature and warming of developing offspring likely helped endotherms adapt and spread into colder regions. However, Rolland notes modern climate change is too rapid for such adaptations, and pressures like pollution, hunting, habitat loss, and invasive species are driving an extinction crisis, with species disappearing up to 10,000 times faster than normal. He hopes the work will connect macroevolution and microevolution to better predict adaptation to climate change.

The passage describes several SEV-ES/SEV-SNP guest-hypervisor communication features. The SNP Run VMPL NAE event lets a guest request that its vCPU run at a different VMPL level, with each VMPL optionally having a unique VMSA and GHCB; the hypervisor must return an error if a requested VMPL lacks a VMSA.

The SEV-TIO extension enables guests to bind to and use trusted devices in their private address space, with support discovered via the TEE-IO PCIe capabilities register. The SNP TIO Guest Request NAE event resembles the SNP Guest Request but requires unencrypted data (Guest PCI ID, MMIO range, TDISP status). Data pages, which must be guest-contiguous and shared with the hypervisor, may carry a 32-byte measurements nonce and return measurements, certificates, and TDISP attestation reports. The hypervisor validates page sufficiency, returning the required count in RBX if inadequate.

Secure AVIC manages guest-owned APIC state via per-vCPU backing pages that must remain present in the guest NPT; guests use REGISTER_BACKING_PAGE and UNREGISTER_BACKING_PAGE actions, with support implied by the SEV_FEATURES setting rather than a feature bit.

The Termination Request NAE event lets a guest request termination, conveying a reason code in SW_EXITINFO1 and 64 bits of information in SW_EXITINFO2. For unsupported NAEs, the #VC handler uses the "Unsupported Event" exit code. The hypervisor must provide CPUID properties so guests can identify SEV-ES support.

SMP booting is complicated because vCPU registers cannot be changed after measurement and encryption; solutions include modified reset vectors, predetermined CS/IP locations, and AP jump tables (4K, encrypted, page-aligned, communicated via NAE events or the SEV-SNP Secrets Page). The SEV-SNP AP Creation NAE event (SW_EXITCODE 0x8000_0013) uses RMPADJUST-marked VMSA pages and enables vCPU hotplug, which is otherwise unsupported.

For NMIs, the hypervisor must intercept #DB rather than IRET and use the guest's "NMI Complete" message before injecting another NMI. Debug registers are fully virtualized when DebugVirtualization is set; otherwise DR7 accesses are intercepted and cached. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

With Restricted Injection, the host signals guests via #HV using a shared, host-owned doorbell page containing PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields, configured via VMGEXIT SW_EXITCODE 0x8000_0014 (GET/SET/QUERY actions). The host writes interrupt vectors and non-maskable event bits; guests acknowledge via atomic exchange and complete EOIs either by clearing NoEoiRequired or via VMGEXIT. Guests must execute HLT with interrupts disabled and validate host-provided vectors.

Ola and Uber drivers in Delhi-NCR have threatened a one-day strike on Tuesday over low fares. The Delhi High Court has permanently restrained two taxi-driver unions from disrupting the aggregators' services. The Sarvodaya Drivers' Association, representing 1.25 lakh app-based taxis, demands fares be raised from Rs 6 to Rs 20 per km and the 25% commission abolished. It plans a protest march to the CM's residence and threatens an indefinite strike if ignored, though some unions will not participate.

Kuwait's oil minister said the country will finish cleaning up a crude oil spill in its southern Gulf waters this week, with no new oil patches found. The spill's cause and magnitude were not disclosed. The Khafji Joint Operations said its facilities were safe and clear of the spill.

The passage describes a patent application for a tracking system used in an augmented reality system for image-guided surgery. A healthcare professional wears a head-mounted device with displays that project computer-generated images aligned with a patient's anatomy, where misalignment may typically not exceed about 2-3 mm. The head-mounted device includes a tracking device, typically a single camera (possibly high-speed, acquiring more than 50 frames per second), that images a patient marker and/or a tool marker. The patient marker may include an array of elements with an appearance unique to each location and orientation of the head-mounted device, allowing position and orientation to be determined without triangulation techniques. When the first tracking device loses line of sight with the patient and/or tool markers, tracking data from at least one additional tracking device—such as one disposed on a second healthcare professional's head-mounted device or a stationary device in the operating room—is incorporated to generate the augmented reality image. Alternative approaches include displaying the second healthcare professional's view, tracking an already-identified marker using a tracking algorithm (e.g., a Kalman filter), or using an inertial-measurement unit in combination with the last known marker location.

Investors who had long shrugged off geopolitical and economic risks, focusing instead on strong corporate profits and tax cuts, suddenly grew nervous as stocks fell more than 2 percent, marking the worst week in two years. A jobs report showing rising wages raised inflation concerns, and investors worried the cheap central bank money that fueled the nine-year stock boom might disappear sooner than expected.

Market corrections—defined as drops of at least 10% but no more than 20%—are routine occurrences, with fewer than one in five escalating into bear markets (drops exceeding 20%). On average, a correction has occurred every year since 1900, with the average correction being a 13.5% decline lasting 54 days. Historically, the S&P 500 has dropped an average of 33% during bear markets, with more than a third exceeding 40% declines; the 14 U.S. bear markets over the last 70 years lasted from 45 days to 694 days, averaging about a year. From 1980 through 2015, the S&P 500 experienced an average intra-year decline of 14.2%, yet achieved positive returns in 27 of those 36 years, despite events such as two Gulf wars, 9/11, and the financial crisis. The author, citing Warren Buffett, urges investors to understand market behavior, avoid panic selling, and take responsibility for their financial decisions rather than blame the market.

The passage is from the datasheet of the TPS7H500x-SP series (TPS7H5001-SP, TPS7H5002-SP, TPS7H5003-SP, TPS7H5004-SP), radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak-current-mode PWM controllers from Texas Instruments for space-grade DC-DC converters. The controllers support topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge, with switching frequencies up to 2 MHz, and require external gate drivers.

Key functional details include:
- Primary switching outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) have roughly 150-mA peak current capability. OUTB and SRB are active only when the duty cycle limit is set to 50% (DCL pin to AVSS); SRB exists only on the TPS7H5001-SP. SRA/SRB begin switching when the SS pin exceeds 1 V.
- Dead times are programmable via PS and SP resistors (10 kΩ–300 kΩ), except the TPS7H5003-SP, which has a fixed 50-ns dead time; minimum dead time is 8 ns if pins float. Leading edge blank time is programmable via LEB (fixed 50 ns on TPS7H5003-SP). Pulse skipping occurs when COMP is below 0.3 V at the clock rising edge and the previous duty cycle was below 25%.
- Duty cycle limits are configurable via DCL: 100% (VLDO), 75% (floating), or 50% (AVSS); the TPS7H5004-SP supports only 50%.
- The CS_ILIM pin senses primary-side current against COMP/2 (with a 150-mV offset); a 1.05-V threshold triggers hiccup mode with cycle-by-cycle limiting timed by the CHICC capacitor (minimum 3.3 nF recommended).
- The FAULT pin enables external protections with a 0.6-V rising threshold, 0.4–1.4 µs minimum pulse width, and 0.5-V falling threshold, followed by a delay before soft-start restarts.
- Slope compensation, set via the RSC pin, mitigates subharmonic oscillation; the recommended value is equal to the inductor falling current slope. Frequency compensation uses Type 2A or 2B schemes with a transconductance error amplifier.
- Thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C (typical) and restarts below 160°C. Input supply range is 4 V to 14 V.

An application example designs a 500-kHz, 5-V output synchronous push-pull converter using GaN devices with the TPS7H5001-SP, covering selection of resistors, dead time (~25 ns), transformer turns ratio (2.5), FETs, output inductor (0.47 µH), output capacitance (2.3 mF including single-event transient mitigation), current sense resistor (7.5 Ω), hiccup capacitor (3.3 nF), compensation components, and slope compensation resistor (102 kΩ).

The passage concludes with layout guidelines (routing noise-sensitive traces away from switching nodes, separating analog and power grounds, minimizing high-current loop areas), related documentation references, revision history, and mechanical/packaging information.

Apple Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended March 31, 2018 reports net sales of $61,137 million for the three-month period, up 16% from $52,896 million a year earlier, and net income of $13,822 million ($2.75 basic EPS) versus $11,029 million ($2.11). Six-month net sales were $149,430 million with net income of $33,887 million. Total assets were $367,502 million and shareholders' equity was $126,878 million as of March 31, 2018; cash and cash equivalents totaled $45,059 million, and six-month operating cash flow was $43,423 million.

The quarterly sales increase was driven primarily by higher iPhone, Services and Other Products sales, with year-over-year growth in all five geographic segments: Americas ($24,841M), Europe ($13,846M), Greater China ($13,024M), Japan ($5,468M) and Rest of Asia Pacific ($3,958M). iPhone net sales rose 14% due to a mix of iPhones with higher average selling prices; Services grew 31% due primarily to licensing, App Store and AppleCare. Apple began shipping HomePod in February 2018 and introduced a new 9.7-inch iPad with Apple Pencil compatibility in March 2018. Gross margin percentage was 38.3% for the quarter (versus 38.9%), and the Company anticipates 38.0%–38.5% for Q3 2018. The effective tax rate fell to 14.5% from 24.9%.

Following the December 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, which lowered the U.S. federal rate from 35% to 21%, Apple recognized $9.3 billion of income tax expense in the first six months of fiscal 2018, including a $2.6 billion provisional estimate. The Company replaced a $36.1 billion deferred tax liability with a provisional deemed repatriation tax payable of $38.0 billion, and had gross unrecognized tax benefits of $9.5 billion. Related to the European Commission State Aid Decision, Apple expects to begin funding the €13 billion recovery amount plus €1 billion interest into escrow during the third quarter of 2018 pending appeals.

Apple had $12.0 billion of commercial paper outstanding (weighted-average rate 1.68%) and $111.1 billion aggregate principal of term debt. Of its $210 billion authorized repurchase program, $199.6 billion had been utilized; the Company spent $23.5 billion on buybacks and paid $3.2 billion in dividends during the quarter, and on May 1, 2018 the Board authorized a new $100 billion repurchase program. In litigation, a jury awarded VirnetX $503 million in VirnetX II in April 2018 (VirnetX I damages of $440 million are on appeal); the PTO has declared the relevant patents invalid, with appeals pending. Other items include accrued warranty costs of $4,030 million, future minimum lease payments of $9.8 billion, and unconditional purchase obligations of $8.3 billion.
Two teens were arrested and a third remains at large after a police pursuit of a black Subaru with stolen numberplates in Frankston. The car was dumped in Bayswater.

This passage is an email containing several news articles dated May 18, 2001. One article discusses California's long-term power contracts, noting that forward power prices have fallen since the state's $43 billion in purchases announced in March, reducing their estimated value by about $6.5 billion, though sellers such as Calpine stated they do not intend to back out of agreements. An options market report describes investors selling options amid expectations of a flat market, including activity in Enron's June options. Multiple articles report that Saudi Arabia selected international oil companies—ExxonMobil, Royal Dutch/Shell, BP, Phillips Petroleum, Occidental Petroleum, Enron, TotalFinaElf, and Conoco—for three major natural gas projects requiring roughly $25 billion in combined investment. ExxonMobil will lead Core Venture 2 on the Red Sea coast, with Enron and Occidental holding stakes; leaders for Core Venture 1 (South Ghawar) and Core Venture 3 (Shaybah) are to be announced by June 5. The U.S. Energy Department welcomed the selection of American firms, and Chevron, Eni, and Marathon were not included in the awards.

The passage advocates pursuing reform through moderate, common-sense legislation, rejecting both reactionaries and extremists, including government ownership of railroads. Government should not run business but should supervise it to ensure it serves the national interest, aiming at equality of opportunity and burden. Because combination of capital and labor is inevitable and sometimes beneficial, laws should not prohibit all combinations but should provide rigorous control and supervision, distinguishing harmful combinations from beneficial ones. Railroads should be permitted to make agreements if sanctioned and published by the Interstate Commerce Commission. Laws incapable of full enforcement force decent railroad men to violate them and reward willful wrongdoers; the author recommends amending the law if the Commission's assessment is justified. On taxation, some taxes belong to local or state governments, but the National Government, which relies on tariffs and excise taxes, should adopt a graduated inheritance tax and, if possible, a graduated income tax. The wealthy owe a peculiar obligation to the State and should bear their full share, though such taxation requires justice and moderation, with the aim of distributing burdens equitably and treating rich and poor with absolute equality.

FTX, a cryptocurrency exchange founded in 2019 by Sam Bankman-Fried (SBF) and Gary Wang, grew to become the world's second-largest crypto exchange, valued at $32 billion by February 2022. Its sister trading firm, Alameda Research, was co-founded by SBF and Tara Mac Aulay in 2017. Nishad Singh, a friend of SBF's brother, joined Alameda and later led engineering at both firms.

In November 2022, CoinDesk leaked Alameda's balance sheet, revealing that 40% of its $14.6 billion in assets consisted of FTT, FTX's own token, which FTX and Alameda largely controlled. Binance CEO Changpeng Zhao announced he would sell his FTT holdings, causing the token's price to drop 80% and triggering $6 billion in customer withdrawals. FTX paused withdrawals, a proposed rescue by Binance fell through, and FTX, Alameda, and related entities filed for bankruptcy on November 11, 2022.

SBF was arrested in December 2022 and charged with eight counts including fraud, money laundering, and campaign finance offenses; he pled not guilty. Wang and Alameda CEO Caroline Ellison pled guilty. In February 2023, Singh pled guilty to six counts, admitting he wrote code enabling SBF to divert FTX customer funds to Alameda, made illegal political contributions, and inflated FTX's 2021 revenues by about $50 million at SBF's request.

SEC complaints detailed undisclosed diversion of customer funds to Alameda, special privileges including a $65 billion line of credit funded by customer assets, an "allow negative" feature in the code, and use of customer funds for venture investments, real estate, and political donations. Bankruptcy CEO John Ray cited a complete failure of corporate controls, noting FTX lacked an independent board, an accounting department, and a CFO. Questions arose about the roles of investors, auditors, regulators, customers, and celebrity endorsers in the collapse, as well as why Singh, though aware of the misuse of funds, neither reported it nor resigned.

Penn State will no longer allow the Penn State Outing Club, Nittany Grotto Caving Club, and Nittany Divers SCUBA Club to organize student-led outdoor trips starting next semester, citing risks from remote locations with poor cell service and distance from emergency services. The decision followed a two-month review that did not consult student leaders. The university says the assessment was proactive, not based on prior injuries, and plans a university-run trip program.

Google released Android 8.0 Oreo in August, featuring under-the-hood refinements and features such as Picture-in-Picture (PiP) Mode, Notification Dots, Smart Text Selection, Notification Snoozing, and Autofill Framework. PiP Mode advances multitasking beyond Nougat's split-screen by playing videos in a floating window at the OS level. Not all apps support PiP, as developers must enable it; supported apps include Google Chrome, Google Duo, Google Play Movies & TV, Google Play Services, Google Maps, WhatsApp, YouTube, and VLC. YouTube's PiP requires a YouTube Red subscription, unavailable in some countries like India. The article demonstrates using PiP via YouTube in Chrome: play a video in full-screen, tap the home button, and the video shrinks to a movable floating window. PiP can be enabled per app through Settings.

Thomas Henderson sued Alexander Beaton and others in trespass to try title and for partition of an undivided half interest in a league of land in Navarro County, claiming through a chain of title running from a government grant to Mastin Latham, through an 1839 instrument from Latham to William F. Henderson, and ultimately to Henderson via a sheriff's sale. The central issue was whether the Latham-Henderson instrument was an absolute deed or an executory contract. The court held it was an absolute, unconditional conveyance, reasoning that the consideration clause referred to past services (locating, surveying, and paying government dues on Latham's headright), as corroborated by the instrument's language, surrounding circumstances, and unimpeached testimony of William F. Henderson. The partition proviso was construed as a provision for partition rather than a condition; even if treated as a condition subsequent, no forfeiture was enforced by the proper party through entry or equivalent act. The defense of stale demand was inapplicable because the right rested on an executed deed, not an executory contract. The limitation defenses also failed: the ten-year period was incomplete due to constitutional exclusions; the five-year plea lacked evidence of tax payment; and the three-year plea failed because the tenants held possession as tenants of Latham, whose possession was adverse to, not under, the title chain claimed by Beaton, and the deed from Wood's heirs was defective for lack of proven agency and a married grantor's acknowledgment. The judgment for defendants was reversed and the cause remanded.
A fundraising appeal for an Annual Fund supporting rule of law, independent courts, and equal access to justice; donors receive a sticker and magnet set.

Ukraine has partnered with blockchain company Bitfury Group to place all of its government's electronic data on a blockchain platform, described by CEO Valery Vavilov as the largest government blockchain deal ever. The project will begin with a pilot covering state registers, public services, social security, public health, and energy, expected to launch late this year, then expand to all areas including cybersecurity. Countries including Sweden, Estonia, and Georgia have smaller blockchain programs. This is Bitfury's second government blockchain project, following Georgia's land-titling registry pilot.

Reuters outlines five themes for investors in the coming week: (1) The Bank of England's "Super Thursday," featuring a rate decision, meeting minutes, and its Inflation Report, with no rate change expected but attention on sterling's rise to $1.43 and UK bond yields at 1.59 percent. (2) Australian and New Zealand central bank meetings amid cooling housing markets and below-expectation inflation, plus China's monthly data release including trade figures. (3) A widening U.S. trade deficit, expected at $51.7 billion for December, alongside retail sales data and a possible government shutdown. (4) A gap in earnings growth expectations between European and U.S. equities, with major European companies reporting results. (5) A busy week for emerging market central banks, with possible rate cuts in Russia, hikes expected in Mexico and possibly Romania, and India's Reserve Bank expected to hold rates.

The President reports that belligerent nations continue to disregard neutral rights despite efforts to obtain repeal of their edicts. Ministers at London and Paris were instructed regarding suspension of the embargo laws, but France gave no answer and Britain rejected the proposed arrangement, so the embargo remains in force. The President credits the embargo with saving mariners and mercantile property and enabling defensive preparations, leaves further decisions to Congress, and submits the relevant documents. The Chesapeake affair remains unredressed, Britain still adhering to an inadmissible preliminary. Relations with other European powers are unchanged; negotiations with Spain are paused amid its internal crisis. Harmony with the Barbary powers continues except for the dey of Algiers's proceeding against the U.S. consul. Peace is maintained with Indian tribes, several of which have surrendered offenders, and one division of the Cherokee nation is considering U.S. citizenship. Defensive works at seaports are largely being finished except at New York and New Orleans; 103 gunboats were built. No general militia detachments were called, though small detachments enforced embargo laws on the northern frontier; recruiting under the additional military force act is believed satisfactory. Congress is urged to ensure uniform militia preparation, and arms production has shifted to domestic factories. Internal manufactures, spurred by the suspension of foreign commerce, are expanding and likely permanent. Receipts neared eighteen million dollars; 2.3 million of funded debt was paid, leaving about fourteen million in the treasury, and Congress is asked to consider applying future surpluses to roads, canals, and education. Concluding his final address, the President expresses gratitude and confidence in the republic's permanence.

Joseph McGreal, a former Orland Park police officer fired on June 28, 2010, sued the Village of Orland Park and three police officials, alleging his termination violated his First Amendment rights as retaliation for speech at a November 2, 2009 village board meeting, and asserting an intentional-infliction-of-emotional-distress claim. The district court granted the defendants summary judgment, and the Seventh Circuit affirmed. The court held McGreal offered no admissible evidence that the defendants knew of his speech or that it motivated his firing, and no admissible evidence that the defendants' alternative explanations—lying under oath, insubordination, and reckless conduct—were pretextual; suspicious timing alone was insufficient. On the emotional distress claim, McGreal admitted his distress was "garden variety," which fails the "extreme and outrageous" and severe distress requirements under Illinois law.

Kyle Freeland pitched effectively into the sixth inning and doubled during a three-run fourth, leading the Colorado Rockies to an 11-4 win over the San Francisco Giants. Freeland (5-5) allowed three runs on eight hits in 5 1/3 innings, and every Rockies starter had at least one hit. David Dahl hit his first career pinch-hit homer, while Trevor Story and several others contributed RBIs. The Giants lost two pitchers to injury: starter Jeff Samardzija left after one inning with shoulder tightness, and rookie Dereck Rodriguez, who made his major league debut, was struck in the shin by a line drive. Evan Longoria hit two home runs and Buster Posey one for the Giants. Colorado has won 12 of its last 13 games against the Giants at Coors Field.

Maddie Sabourin, an 18-year-old high school senior in Georgia, spent years seeking a kidney match for her grandfather, Sam Senseney, 63, who has been on dialysis and the transplant list for six years. While competing in the Miss Georgia Outstanding Teen Pageant, she raised awareness for organ donation and $7,500 for the American Kidney Fund. After turning 18, she tested as a match but was initially deemed too young to donate; she convinced doctors to allow it. She and her grandfather will meet doctors to set a surgery date, hoped to be within a month.

HoopTactics presents proven baseline, sideline, and full court out of bounds plays that create high percentage shots with two to three options, flowing into predetermined continuity if no shot develops. Full court situations requiring a score in under four seconds are difficult but winnable for prepared teams. Inbounding against pressure creates a 5-on-4 disadvantage; when leading, getting the ball inbounds may be the best option. Teams should keep plays simple, use their best inbounder and shooters, and scout the defense. Late in games, advancing the ball and taking a timeout is preferable, or a baseline play can safely inbound.

This patent application, a continuation of earlier filings, describes embodiments for enhanced features in 5G systems, particularly AMF selection for isolated network slices. It outlines a 5G architecture comprising access networks and a 5G core network with network functions including AMF, SMF, UPF, PCF, NEF, NRF, UDM, NSSF, AUSF, and N3IWF, along with their functionalities. The disclosure covers registration management and connection management state models, PDU connectivity services, a QoS flow-based framework, and network slicing concepts such as S-NSSAI, requested/allowed NSSAI, and slice selection procedures. It notes that existing technologies do not specify how to implement isolated network slices or select a proper AMF for them. The embodiments define three kinds/levels of isolation: fully isolated slices (sharing neither RAN nor core network functions), partly isolated slices with shared RAN, and partly isolated slices with shared RAN and AMF. Example call flows show a UE including network slice isolation information (e.g., a network slice isolation type indicating fully or partly isolated, logically or physically isolated) in registration requests. Depending on the isolation level, an NRF, NSSF, or UDM may select an AMF based on requested/subscribed NSSAI, isolation information, UE identifiers, DNN, operator policies, and subscription data. Flow diagrams describe the RAN communicating with the NRF and NSSF, which return AMF IP addresses or FQDNs to complete registration.

Astronomers from Trinity College Dublin used the James Webb Space Telescope to observe the rogue planet SIMP-0136, detecting strong auroral activity similar to Earth's Northern Lights and Jupiter's auroras, which heat the planet's upper atmosphere. The team recorded temperature changes smaller than 5°C on the planet, which exceeds 1,500°C, and linked these to chemical composition changes suggestive of rotating storms like Jupiter's Great Red Spot. Contrary to expectations, cloud coverage remained constant across the surface; these clouds are composed of silicate grains similar to sand. The findings, from the Exo-Aimsir group led by Prof. Johanna Vos, represent some of the most precise atmospheric measurements of any extrasolar object to date, with future telescopes expected to extend such studies to exoplanets.

Tropical Storm Nate, the 15th Atlantic system this season, has killed 22 people in Latin America and is heading toward Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula and the U.S. Gulf Coast, likely as a hurricane this weekend. Louisiana declared a state of emergency, ordered coastal evacuations, and mobilized 1,300 National Guard troops. Nate is forecast to make landfall in southeast Louisiana as a Category 1 hurricane. September was the most active month on record for Accumulated Cyclone Energy. In Nicaragua, 15 people died; Costa Rica reported seven deaths and 15 missing, with 5,000 residents in emergency shelters.

The article backtests a pair trading strategy in SPY (S&P 500) and TLT (long-term Treasuries), prompted by large opposite-direction moves in both ETFs on June 18, 2021, which reversed the following Monday. The strategy goes long SPY when the S&P 500 falls more than 1.25 times its 50-day average high-minus-low range, and shorts TLT when it rises more than 1.25 times its average on the same day, with positions closed after a set number of days. Backtested from 2003 to June 2021 without commissions or slippage, the strategy produced an erratic equity curve with a 1.93% CAGR, 60% win ratio, and 0.18% average gain per round trip. Testing alternative holding periods and movement thresholds did not significantly improve results, with exits beyond five days performing worse. The authors conclude it is not a tradeable strategy.

The First Appellate District affirmed a judgment in favor of Louis and Louise Helbing against E. F. Joy, assignee of W. W. Montague & Co., who sought to set aside two deeds of gift by which Helbing conveyed San Francisco real property to his wife in May 1893. The deeds, executed while Helbing was solvent, were not recorded until December 11, 1895, after he had obtained approximately $1,000 in credit for plumbing goods from W. W. Montague & Co. by representing himself as the owner of the property. The trial court found the deed was not made to hinder, delay, or defraud creditors, was not made during insolvency, and that the credit was extended because of Helbing's apparent ownership arising from non-recordation, not from any act of Mrs. Helbing, who was not shown to have known of her husband's representations or acts of ownership.

The court held that the grantor's intent was a question for the trial court on all the facts and circumstances; that the two-year delay in recording was a circumstance casting suspicion on the transaction but insufficient by itself to establish fraudulent intent; and that the burden rested on the plaintiff to prove such intent, in the absence of which the court was bound to find none existed. The opinion distinguished Bush & Mallett Co. v. Helbing, where exclusion of testimony regarding the husband's control of the property was held erroneous, noting such testimony was admitted in the present case. The court also upheld the exclusion of evidence concerning goods concealed under the house and Mrs. Helbing's sworn ownership claim to the sheriff, events occurring nearly four years after the deed and involving personal property unconnected to its execution, ruling that even if erroneous, the ruling could not justify reversal. The judgment and order denying a new trial were affirmed.

This retrospective cross-sectional study analysed factors causing delayed discharge from a 23-bed subacute Complex Discharge Unit (CDU) at St James's Hospital, Dublin, during the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic (March 2020–February 2021). Data from electronic patient records for 390 adult patients with length of stay (LOS) exceeding 15 days were analysed using Kaplan-Meier and stratified Cox regression. Of these patients, 83.6% were over 65 years (median age 79), 59.7% were female, and 48.2% had more than four comorbidities. Five potential delaying factors were examined: complications from primary diagnoses or multimorbidity, healthcare-associated infections, frailty or falls requiring integrated rehabilitation, patient-centred needs, and community services. Complications arising from primary diagnoses and patient-centred needs were statistically significant contributors to prolonged LOS across genders and multimorbidity groups, while healthcare-associated infections, frailty or falls, and community services were not. Patients aged 65–75 and females were more likely to experience prolonged LOS, and the five factors were not responsible for delayed LOS in patients over 85 years. The study concluded that complexities from primary diagnoses and patient-centred needs, such as cognition, psychosocial and carer needs, were the most common factors delaying discharge, findings that may inform future contingency planning. Limitations included the single-centre design, focus solely on CDU admissions, and sample size constraints.
OpenAI is preparing to launch a TikTok-like stand-alone app for AI-generated videos, powered by Sora 2, featuring a vertical feed, recommendation algorithm, and like, comment, and remix options.

Bank of England research suggests a central bank digital currency (CBDC) could make monetary policy changes more effective. A CBDC closely substituting bank deposits would strengthen policy transmission, forcing commercial banks to adjust rates more quickly in line with the central bank rate. It would also improve quantitative easing by allowing the central bank to pay non-banks directly, bypassing the banking sector. The Bank is not currently planning to issue a digital currency, unlike Sweden's Riksbank.

In *People v Schaub*, the Michigan Court of Appeals reversed a circuit court order that had reinstated a child abandonment charge against Lawrence B. Schaub. The charge stemmed from allegations that Schaub agreed to sell his ten-month-old daughter to an undercover police officer for $60,000 and relinquish all parental rights. The district court dismissed the charge, finding the child was never left without care; the circuit court reversed and reinstated the charge. The Court of Appeals held that although sufficient evidence established the intent to wholly abandon the child, the element of exposure was not established, because the defendant handed the child to a person who would care for her, creating no risk of personal injury from abandonment. The court reversed and remanded, noting its ruling was without prejudice to filing common-law felony charges. O'Connell, P.J., dissented, reasoning that whether delivering a child to a total stranger constituted exposure was a question of fact for a jury. The opinion also noted that, in response to the case, the Legislature enacted MCL 750.136c, prohibiting the sale or purchase of people.

The Warren Buffett ETF Portfolio (90/10) is a passive investment strategy derived from Warren Buffett's 2013 letter to Berkshire Hathaway investors, in which he instructed the trustee of his wife's inheritance to allocate 90% of the money to a low-fee stock index fund and 10% to short-term government bonds. The strategy invests 90% of funds in low-cost, passively managed S&P 500 index ETFs and 10% in government bonds, aiming for long-term growth with reduced risk and lower fees than actively managed portfolios. The S&P 500 component provides diversified exposure to 500 large U.S. companies, while the bond allocation cushions against market volatility. Investors can build the portfolio through a one-time lump-sum investment or dollar-cost averaging, selecting ETFs based on expense ratios, historical performance, and liquidity. Performance has generally been positive, closely tracking the S&P 500 with slightly less drawdown, though results can be affected by market conditions, economic changes, and geopolitical events. Capital gains and dividends from ETFs carry tax implications depending on tax bracket, account type, and holding period. Three backtests pairing SPY with short-term (SHY), intermediate-term (IEI), and long-term (TLT) Treasury ETFs showed that longer bond maturities compensated for added risk, with the SPY/TLT portfolio performing best and nearly matching SPY alone; underperformance was attributed to the weak bond market in 2022.

American citizens in Cuba, especially in rural central and eastern districts, are destitute and without support. Consul-General Lee estimates 600 to 800 Americans need relief. The President recommends Congress appropriate at least $50,000 under the Secretary of State's direction, partly for repatriation.

Walmart senior vice president Greg Cathey said Tuesday at the UP.Summit in Bentonville, Arkansas, that drone delivery will expand to "most areas that we operate in," marking a shift beyond small-scale tests, though no timeline was given. Drone delivery is currently available at only a handful of Walmart's more than 4,600 U.S. locations through partnerships including Alphabet's Wing and Zipline. In June, Walmart expanded its Wing partnership to 100 stores in Atlanta, Charlotte, Houston, Orlando, and Tampa, and now plans to add Northwest Arkansas, with operations in Bentonville and Rogers. Walmart has surpassed 300,000 drone deliveries, double the figure announced in June. Widespread adoption remains years away due to technical, regulatory, and financial hurdles, including an FAA rule on beyond-visual-line-of-sight flights expected to take effect next year.

This passage comprises the acknowledgements and a description of sources for Foreign Relations, 1981–1988, Volume I, Foundations of Foreign Policy. The editor, Kristin L.
