Ahlberg, thanks staff of the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library and Library of Congress, the CIA, the Estates of Secretaries Haig and Jeane Kirkpatrick, and numerous Office of the Historian staff; research, selection, and annotation were conducted under Historian Adam M. Howard, with review, declassification, and editing by Kathleen B. Rasmussen, Chris Tudda, Carl Ashley, Kerry Hite, and Mandy A. Chalou. Shultz, State Department Policy Planning Staff lot files, and the Central Foreign Policy File, which NARA will eventually hold as Record Group 59.

The Golden Cross Trading Strategy uses two moving averages—a short-term (50-day) and a long-term (200-day). A buy signal occurs when the 50-day average crosses above the 200-day average, while a sell signal occurs when it crosses below. Backtested on the S&P 500 since 1960 using daily bars, the strategy produced 33 trades averaging about 350 days each, with 79% winners and an average gain of 15.8% per trade. The annual return was 6.8%, slightly below buy-and-hold's 7.2%, but the strategy was invested only 70% of the time, yielding a risk-adjusted return of 9.6%. Drawdowns were substantially lower at 33% versus buy-and-hold's 56%. Starting with 100,000, the account grew to 7.2 million, excluding reinvested dividends. The strategy works by exploiting the market's long-term uptrend while reducing losses in bear markets.

The United States District Court for the Northern District of Indiana granted summary judgment for defendants Jack R. Duckworth and Barry Nothstine against pro se plaintiff Richard A. Milan, an inmate who filed a 42 U.S.C. § 1983 complaint concerning the denial of his July 10, 1988 attempted visit with Judy Ballard at the Indiana State Prison in Michigan City. Milan claimed violations of the Fourteenth Amendment's Due Process Clause and the Eighth Amendment. The court reviewed summary judgment standards under Celotex and Anderson, then applied Hewitt v. Helms and Kentucky Department of Corrections v. Thompson, which hold that inmates generally lack a liberty interest in visitation unless state regulations use explicitly mandatory language with specific substantive predicates. Administrative Procedure 02-00-104, Section 11 permitted denial of visitation without specific criteria, so Milan could not establish a protectable liberty interest. Although Nothstine's affidavit admitted the denial was not given in writing as the procedure required, the court found this procedural failure too fragile to support a substantive constitutional claim. Milan did not dispute the defendants' discretionary authority to deny visitation following his escape attempt. The court denied Milan's own summary judgment motion and granted judgment for the defendants for failure to establish a violation of a substantive constitutional right.

This cross-sectional, quantitative study assessed the prevalence of and factors associated with non-adherence to antiretroviral therapy (ART) among HIV patients in the catchment area of Kibungo Referral Hospital, Rwanda. Using stratified random sampling across 14 health facilities, 424 patients participated; data were collected via a structured questionnaire between March 25 and April 30, 2024, and analyzed with SPSS using Fisher exact tests and logistic regression. The overall non-adherence rate was 13% (55 patients), while 87% (369 patients) were adherent. Bivariate analysis identified significant associations with age, education, household size, having multiple sexual partners, travel and waiting times, smoking, and disclosure of HIV status to friends. Multivariate analysis showed that patients younger than 31 years (AoR 15.462), without tertiary education (AoR 8.232), experiencing stigma (AoR 2.148), perceiving ART as ineffective (AoR 9.333), and not integrating ART into daily activities (AoR 11.180) were significantly more likely to be non-adherent; setting an alarm reminder was not significant. Compared with rates reported in Ethiopia, Nigeria, Uganda, South Africa, and other Rwandan settings, Kibungo's non-adherence rate was relatively low. Limitations include the cross-sectional design, reliance on self-reported data, and limited generalizability beyond the study site.

This study estimates the Burden of Disease (BoD) of COVID-19 in the Republic of Ireland from March 1, 2020 to February 28, 2021 using Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALYs), a metric combining morbidity and mortality into a single measure. Data were sourced from publicly available national sources via DATA.GOV.IE. Years of Life Lost (YLL) were calculated from mortality data using GBD 2019 standard life tables. Years Lived with Disability (YLD) were estimated across five health states—asymptomatic, moderate, severe, critical, and post-acute consequences (PAC)—using disability weights from the GBD 2019 study and the European Disability Weight study. Asymptomatic cases were assumed at a 3:1 ratio, and PAC was assumed to affect 13.3% of symptomatic cases for 28 days. DALYs were computed as the sum of YLL and YLD. Ethical approval was obtained from University College Cork.

This paper examines governance for e-learning ecosystems within digital business ecosystems. E-learning is vital for organisational competitiveness, and governance—providing strategic direction, ensuring objectives are achieved, managing risks, and allocating resources—is required for success. The paper reviews e-learning systems, which face cost and integration challenges, and e-learning ecosystems comprising learning communities and enterprises united by a learning management system, with components including content providers, consultants, and infrastructure. The authors propose an e-learning governance framework of structures, processes, and communications and relational mechanisms, adapted from IT governance, and add a fourth element, pedagogies and instructional designs. Darking's characteristics and dimensions of digital ecosystem governance are adopted to strengthen this framework. Information security governance is highlighted as critical, involving security policies, counter-measures, and monitoring. Trust and a knowledge base of regulatory issues are identified as essential to e-learning ecosystems. The paper concludes that further research is needed to understand the business benefits of improved e-learning governance practices.

This patent application, a continuation of prior filings, describes systems for reducing eviction of stable data in a cloud-integrated storage appliance that caches snapshots before archiving them to cloud storage. The appliance receives forever incremental snapshots from data sources and arranges snapshot metadata (inode records, directory records, and data map records) into key-value stores per defined data collection, while writing snapshot data into snapshot data files. The application describes operations for updating the appliance with snapshots, restoring snapshots or individual files by merging valid records back to the baseline snapshot, and reclaiming deleted snapshots by implicitly transferring valid records and data ranges to a succeeding snapshot. With typical eviction policies such as least recently used, stable data blocks (unchanged across multiple snapshots) of older snapshots may be evicted to cloud storage, causing slow restores that risk violating recovery time objectives. To address this, the appliance snapshot manager creates synthetic baseline snapshots and refreshes eviction state data. In one embodiment, ownership of still-valid metadata records from preceding snapshots is expanded to the most recent snapshot by copying records with new key prefixes, and the fingerprint database and eviction state data (e.g., time indicators or use counters) are updated so stable cached blocks appear recent. In another embodiment, a reverse incremental synthetic baseline is maintained: invalidated metadata and data are transferred to a pre-baseline snapshot while new or changed data is incorporated into the synthetic baseline, which is continually refreshed with each received snapshot.

Explainable AI is an important research topic for understanding pre-trained language models, improving resource efficiency, and addressing safety risks such as adversarial attacks and ethical breaches. Interpretability research aims to enhance transparency and trust in AI decision-making. Key challenges include the lack of a unified evaluation framework, methods that scale linearly with model size, and difficulties applying interpretability in real-world deployment. The passage proposes a framework for editing concept activation vectors: activation vectors from LLM layers train a logistic regression classifier to produce CAVs, which, applied during inference, enhance or suppress target concepts such as reducing toxicity while maintaining text fluency and supporting multiple simultaneous concepts.

The court granted in part and denied in part Defendant's motion for summary judgment and denied Plaintiff's motion in this action to enforce a Form I-864 affidavit of support. Plaintiff, an Ethiopian citizen sponsored by Defendant, married him in 1999; they separated the same year and divorced in 2005 with a $49,000 property settlement made without prejudice to her immigration claims. The court held that a sponsored immigrant may sue to enforce the Form I-864, that income must be assessed year by year rather than in aggregate, and that the divorce settlement and student loans do not count as income, while student grants and housing subsidies do. Defendant's evidence failed to show Plaintiff's income exceeded 125% of the poverty threshold in 2003, 2006, and 2007, so summary judgment was granted only for 2000, 2001, 2002, 2004, and 2005. Plaintiff's motion was denied because she did not meet her evidentiary burden.

Molina Healthcare is a pure-play government-sponsored health insurer focused on Medicaid and dual-eligible populations, with strong contract wins and retention. The stock trades at a significant discount (~8–9× earnings, ~0.2× EV/sales). Risks include policy changes, acquisition execution, medical cost inflation, and cash flow volatility, though state-level dynamics and contract discipline mitigate concerns. The author views MOH as a structurally profitable compounder offering value for defensive investors and holds a long position in the stock.

This paper examines how time-delayed feedback affects multi-agent learning in normal-form games. While optimistic algorithms such as OFTRL achieve O(1) total regret and converge to Nash equilibrium in poly-matrix zero-sum games without delay, the authors show that any small time delay (m ≥ 1) degrades performance: in Matching Pennies under an unconstrained setting with the Euclidean regularizer, OFTRL suffers Ω(√T) regret (Thm. 6) and its strategies diverge from equilibrium (Thm. 7). To address this, they propose Weighted OFTRL (WOFTRL), which multiplies the optimistic prediction by a weight n. A Taylor expansion shows the time delay m and optimistic weight n cancel each other out. When n = m + 1, WOFTRL achieves O(1) total regret (Cor. 11), though the regret and required inverse learning rate scale with λ = (m+1)(m+2)/2, and it attains best-iterate convergence to Nash equilibrium in poly-matrix zero-sum games (Cor. 13). Experiments on Matching Pennies, Sato's game, and Rock-Paper-Scissors confirm O(1)-regret when n > m and O(√T)-regret when n ≤ m, with an exceptional O(√T)-regret region when m is large relative to a finite learning rate. The results partially extend to Mirror Descent. Future work includes proving last-iterate convergence and handling stochastic or adversarial delays.

President Carter, speaking at a Notre Dame commencement ceremony, thanks Father Hesburgh and honors three religious leaders—Bishop Donal Lamont, Paul Cardinal Arns, and Stephen Cardinal Kim—for their fights for human freedoms in Rhodesia, Brazil, and South Korea. He then outlines his vision for an American foreign policy grounded in democratic values and human rights. Expressing confidence in democracy, he argues the United States is free of its former "inordinate fear of communism" and should abandon adopting adversaries' flawed tactics, citing Vietnam as an example of failure. He describes how the world has changed since 1945—the decline of colonialism, the emergence of new nations, and rising aspirations—requiring a new foreign policy based on decency and optimism. He details five principles: (1) reaffirming human rights as a fundamental tenet of foreign policy; (2) reinforcing bonds among democracies, noting that all NATO members are now democracies; (3) engaging the Soviet Union to halt the strategic arms race through detente, seeking weapons reductions and a nuclear testing ban; (4) promoting Middle East peace through negotiations involving Israel, Syria, Jordan, and Egypt, based on UN Resolutions 242 and 338, including discussion of a Palestinian homeland; and (5) reducing nuclear proliferation and restricting conventional arms sales. He adds commitments to cooperate with developing nations, normalize relations with the People's Republic of China, and support a peaceful transition to majority rule in southern Africa. He concludes that American policy is rooted in unchanging moral values and designed to serve mankind.

This VentureWire newsletter from Technologic Partners, dated September 28, 2000, reports private company business news. The issue also covers new board members and executives at various companies, including CEO appointments at GlobalNetXchange, ViAir, Expanse Networks, and zGraffiti. Children of obese mothers were nearly 70 per cent more likely to fail fine motor skill tests by age 3, while children of obese fathers were 75 per cent more likely to fail social competence measures. Those born to extremely obese couples were nearly three times more likely to fail problem-solving tests. The Pediatrics study examined over 5,000 US women.

Drew Doughty discusses his playoff performance, saying he struggled early in the season but gained confidence by mid-year and carried that into the playoffs. He admits he felt pressure from signing the team's biggest contract and missing camp, but overcame it by playing carefree and having fun. He describes the team as clicking with consistent lines and defensive pairings, and expects a tough series against an equally strong defensive opponent with two of the league's best goalies. He notes both teams had subpar regular seasons but are now on a roll. He credits the team for overcoming adversity, having beaten the Western Conference's top three teams while losing only two games. He praises the goalie for making key saves, working hard, taking blame, and staying humble while avoiding media attention, adding that the goalie is funny and fun to be around off the ice. Doughty expresses excitement for the first game of the series and visualizes lifting the cup. He notes the Kings are now being recognized around Los Angeles, with fans chanting their names at restaurants, and says the team is putting LA on the map as a hockey city, attracting many first-time fans.

The passage describes the NVIDIA GA10x Ampere GPU architecture and its key features. The GA10x SM includes third-generation Tensor Cores supporting new data types (TF32, BF16), a Sparsity feature that doubles throughput for deep learning, and up to 5X AI training throughput over Turing. The architecture uses GDDR6X memory with PAM4 signaling, reaching 19.5 Gbps and up to 936 GB/sec bandwidth on the GeForce RTX 3090. Third-generation NVLink provides 112.5 GB/sec total bandwidth between two GPUs, enabling memory scaling from 48GB to 96GB. PCIe Gen 4 support doubles bandwidth over PCIe 3.0, up to 64 GB/sec.

The full GA102 GPU contains seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, 84 SMs, and 112 ROPs, with ROPs now located in the GPC rather than the memory controller, improving raster operation performance. Each GA10x SM contains 128 CUDA Cores, four Tensor Cores, and 128 KB of L1/Shared Memory. The SM features FP32 processing on both datapaths, doubling FP32 throughput compared to Turing.

GA10x GPUs include second-generation RT Cores that double ray/triangle intersection testing rates over Turing and add a new Interpolate Triangle Position unit for hardware-accelerated ray-traced motion blur, enabling up to 8x faster motion blur rendering. The architecture also supports concurrent RT Core, graphics, and compute workloads.

NVIDIA RTX IO enables GPU-based loading and decompression of game assets via Microsoft's DirectStorage API, accelerating I/O performance up to 100x compared to hard drives and traditional storage APIs while offloading work from CPU cores.

The NVIDIA A40 data center GPU delivers up to 2X FP32 throughput, 2X ray-tracing throughput, and 5X AI training throughput compared to the Quadro RTX 6000, with 48GB of GDDR6 memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU includes 10,752 CUDA Cores and 48GB of GDDR6.

GA10x GPUs are the first discrete GPUs to support HDMI 2.1 (8K60, 4K120) and the first to provide AV1 hardware decode through fifth-generation NVDEC. Seventh-generation NVENC handles hardware video encoding. A new Error Detection and Replay (EDR) feature helps users identify safe GDDR6X memory overclocking limits. The GeForce RTX 3090 ships with 24GB GDDR6X and is 1.5x faster than TITAN RTX, while the RTX 3070 uses the GA104 GPU and outperforms the previous RTX 2080 Ti. Overall, the Ampere architecture provides up to 2x performance improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI, with GPUs up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing.

This passage is from a Texas Instruments datasheet (SLASFA2A, November 2024, revised April 2025) for the MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 devices. It includes documentation support instructions (registering on ti.com for update notifications), references to the TI E2E support forums, trademark listings, and an electrostatic discharge (ESD) handling caution. The revision history documents changes from November 2024 to April 2025, including a note on PSA-L1 certification targeting, corrections to low-power operation specifications for timers, UARTs, and SPI, addition of new package variants (100_nFBGA_ZAW and 42_DSBGA_YCJ) as Preview, and numerous updates to electrical specifications such as absolute maximum ratings, thermal information, supply current characteristics, POR/BOR thresholds, flash memory endurance, ADC specifications (offset error changed to ±3.5mV, gain error to ±4LSB), VREF, comparator, and temperature sensor values. Functional sections were also updated, including DMA features, SRAM, security features, keystore support for up to 4 keys, UART instances, SPI clocking, LFSS variants, and a cross trigger map for timers. The document concludes with mechanical, packaging, and orderable information, including package drawing notes, soldering guidelines, part status and marking explanations, availability of automotive-qualified versions (MSPM0G3518-Q1, MSPM0G3519-Q1), and TI's legal disclaimers regarding resources provided "as is" without warranties.

With only two aging wolves remaining at Isle Royale National Park, the moose population has surged to an estimated 1,600, threatening balsam fir trees and risking mass starvation similar to 1996, when two-thirds of roughly 2,500 moose died. Michigan Technological University researchers say more wolves are needed to restore predator-prey balance. The National Park Service is weighing four options, preferring to relocate 20 to 30 wolves over three to five years, with a decision expected this fall.

A hockey coach describes his team's ability to win games in different ways, including quick-strike and opportunistic play, while acknowledging the team would like to generate more shots. The staff reviews film after each game, makes adjustments, and emphasizes learning from experiences, having a short memory, and moving forward. Though pleased with the recent win, the coach believes the team can play better and trusts its leadership group to respond to adversity. He praises "Kuny" as a versatile, team-first competitor with multiple Stanley Cup rings, and notes that "Tanger," though not in the lineup, remains involved by attending some coaches' meetings, offering insights, and announcing the starting lineup. The coach says game planning and subtle adjustments are enjoyable parts of a seven-game series, but execution and taking what the game presents are most important, with a hybrid approach between possession and puck pursuit. He states motivation is not an issue with a potential championship within reach. He also highlights "Nick" as an underrated, important player who contributes defensively, on the penalty kill, at faceoffs, and as a calming presence at center. Finally, he calls the last game a bizarre one with long stretches lacking scoring chances, saying the team defended hard, can improve territory control and shot generation, but found a way to win.

The Eagle Creek fire, which has burned more than 48,000 acres since Sept. 2, severely damaged the Oneonta Gorge, raising geologists' concerns about rock falls and debris flows, particularly near Oneonta Gorge and Multnomah Falls Lodge. About 15 percent of the burned area suffered severe burns and 30 percent was moderately burned. Winter rains could dislodge rocks now that moss holding them in place is gone. Fences will be built near the lodge, at-risk trees removed, and Oneonta Gorge trails closed, possibly until September 2018.

A hockey coach discusses his team's playoff performance. He praises Mike for working hard and creating chances, noting that points typically follow, and credits the defensemen, including Pronger and Matt Carle, for strong defensive play. He says Craig Berube does an excellent job running the penalty kill, which requires no changes, only execution. The coach emphasizes that the players' confidence and belief in each other are important, and that the players deserve credit for the team's fast, hard-hitting play against an equally confident Chicago team. He notes Chicago's excellent back pressure limits scoring chances, requiring quick shots when opportunities arise. He acknowledges he was angry at times and should keep it in check. He takes responsibility for not initially having Ville in the lineup, citing a healthy forward group, but praises Ville's attitude, conditioning, and offensive contributions alongside Danny Briere and Giroux. With the season's end in sight, focus is sharp and comes from the players. He has not compared his team to Chicago, noting they took different paths, and does not believe fatigue is a factor for either team, as the hockey has been too good.

Peter Blackmore's August 2000 report to Compaq's Worldwide Sales & Services team cites solid momentum and good morale across all regions despite supply challenges causing a non-linear quarter. Latin America saw success in direct and partner initiatives, with Argentina at 55% direct and Brazil at 60% direct business, plus new e-business alliances with Diveo, Artikos, Terra, and Patagon.com. In Canada, Q2 profits rose 88% over the prior year, with 85% direct business expected by year-end. The U.S. Department of Energy's NNSA selected Compaq to build the world's fastest supercomputer, a 30+ TeraOPS system code-named "Q," valued at over $200M for Los Alamos National Laboratory. Other major wins included Alcatel ($60M), EDF ($50M), the U.K. Cabinet Office ($32M), and the National Science Foundation ($45M). IDC data showed Compaq leading the worldwide PC server market with 30.2% share. The Storage Product Group posted $179M in Q2 profitability, up 45% year-over-year. The Zero Latency Enterprise program will launch in October. CPCG returned to profitability a quarter ahead of expectations with $63M in operating profit, and iPAQ Pocket PC demand reached ten times the initial forecast. The report concludes with extensive lists of customer services, professional services, and regional sales wins worldwide.

The Honor Choir at NRH International Leadership of Texas in North Richland Hills writes its own music, producing a thousand songs between January and June. Their songs are used by teachers in states including North Carolina and Colorado. The choir was invited to the International Children's Choir Festival in New York in June, joining Indianapolis and the Russian Children's Choir.

This passage is a user manual for the SanDisk Sansa c200 media player. It explains how to install and use the Sansa Media Converter to transfer photos (supporting JPEG, TIFF, PNG, BMP, and GIF formats), and describes file transfer methods in MTP mode (WMA/MP3 files to the Media folder, other files to the Data folder) and MSC mode (dragging or copying files). It covers safely removing the device from a computer, basic operations such as powering on/off and using navigation buttons, and music playback features including repeat, shuffle, equalizer settings (Normal, Rock, Jazz, Classic, Pop, and Custom), and GoList playlist management. Photo viewing and slideshow options, FM radio with presets and broadcast recording, and voice recording via a built-in microphone are also described. Settings include display backlight, contrast, auto power off/sleep, and USB mode selection (AutoDetect defaults to MTP mode, which supports Windows Media Player 10 only). A FAQ section addresses supported file formats (MP3, WAV, WMA, secure WMA), copying CDs, podcast compatibility (MP3 at 32–320 kbps), missing ID3 tags, and purchasing playback rights for certain songs. Technical support is available by phone at 1-866-SanDisk or online. The manual details a non-transferable one-year limited warranty for the original end user, excluding third-party software, misuse, and unauthorized repair, with SanDisk's remedy limited to repair, replacement, or refund. It includes a Microsoft WM-DRM notice regarding secure content and potential revocation, an End User License Agreement governing the bundled software (covering license terms, restrictions, warranty disclaimers, liability limits, termination, and exclusion from high-risk activities, governed by California law), and disposal instructions advising against discarding the device with unsorted household waste.

Microsoft Research Asia's Societal AI team has published a white paper, "Societal AI: Research Challenges and Opportunities," arguing that AI's societal impact requires a multidisciplinary approach bridging technical AI research with the social sciences, humanities, policy studies, and ethics. Building on the team's responsible AI work begun roughly seven years earlier with recommendation systems and accelerated by workshops organized after ChatGPT and GPT-4 emerged in late 2022, the paper presents ten key research questions covering fairness and inclusiveness across cultures, safety and controllability, human-AI collaboration, evaluation of AI capabilities, interpretability, value alignment, AI's impact on human cognition and creativity, changes to work and business models, transformation of social science research methodologies, and evolving regulatory frameworks. The team proposes that AI integration into society should be harmonious, synergistic, and resilient. Research highlights include: a value alignment approach combining top-down normative guidelines with bottom-up value learning, alongside evaluation tools (DeNEVIL, CLAVE) for assessing LLM value orientations; CulturePark, a multi-agent debate framework that augments low-resource language data to improve cross-cultural understanding; jailbreak defenses using prompt-based self-reminder techniques; DyVal, a framework that dynamically generates evaluation samples using directed acyclic graphs; and concept activation vectors enabling interpretable control of LLM behavior. The paper also discusses risks such as over-reliance on AI, deskilling, gig economy labor exploitation, and regulatory gaps between industry and governments, calling for both top-down and bottom-up governance involving researchers, policymakers, industry, and users, and invites the broader community to help build the Societal AI research area.

The passage distinguishes between investing and speculation using Benjamin Graham's definition: a security purchase qualifies as investing only if it protects the capital investment and promises an adequate return; purchases failing this standard constitute speculation. The author illustrates this with an example of buying Ask Jeeves stock based on a strategy of purchasing stocks left behind when peer stocks rise in price. Despite earning roughly 25%, the author does not consider it an investment because safety of principal was never considered.

To protect capital, the author recommends buying stocks only at large discounts to intrinsic value, since larger discounts provide greater buffers against business deterioration and allow more room for valuation errors. Investors should also seek financially solid companies—those with clean balance sheets, low long-term debt relative to equity, and strong ratios of current assets to current liabilities, ideally improving over time.

The passage argues that protecting the downside is sufficient for good returns, since businesses tend to experience average results over time and nobody can accurately predict the future. Companies with negative sentiment trade at discounts, creating margins of safety; when pessimism proves unwarranted or temporary problems resolve, prices rise back toward intrinsic value. Net net stocks—trading well below reasonable value with conservative balance sheets—are presented as particularly promising.

Ultimately, whether a person is an investor or a gambler depends on the selection process used, not the assets purchased. Focusing on stocks that protect the downside while offering decent profit potential produces good long-term returns.

In a playoff interview, the speaker describes a tightly contested series where both teams' strong defense and goaltending make the first goal crucial. The team's improved home record may result from relying on home ice throughout the playoffs, creating pressure to retain it. Despite losing two recent games in overtime, the team played well, created chances, and received strong goaltending that gave it opportunities to win. The opponent has become more aggressive, but chances remain available. Although playoff losses hurt more than regular-season ones, the speaker stays positive, noting the team has beaten this opponent twice and will focus on winning the next home game.

Location trackers in devices like smartphones and laptops raise privacy concerns. Kurt Peterson, owner of Experimac in Pueblo, says tracking can be prevented by turning off location services in device settings on iPhones, Androids, Fitbits, Apple watches, and MacBooks. He notes apps pose a greater risk than hacking and advises caution about who is invited into apps. He adds that visiting the App Store re-enables Location Services, and turning devices off is the only way to truly go off the grid.

The Stack Zone Offense is a prolific zone offense based on the overload principle, with Mike Frink instrumental in introducing this continuity. It creates immediate matchup and adjustment problems for any zone, is simple to teach, and assigns players specific roles so they can play within their strengths. Key strengths include precise spacing, flexibility through multiple entries, and offensive rebounding, with missed shots often becoming put-back opportunities. The offense defines five positions—point guard, shooting guard, small forward, power forward, and post—each with distinct offensive and defensive responsibilities. It progresses through phases: basic overload reads, pass and cut action, high post roll, and ball reversal, with continuity repeating the action. Optional entries include the Flop and Exchange entries. The Triple Stack alignment, contributed by Tom Newell, creates additional matchup problems. Crunch Time specials—Vegas (double away double screen), Back (weakside lob), and Cat (a 2-1-2 alignment used against traps and double teams)—can be deployed as the shot or game clock runs down.

Offensive set pieces off free kicks re-start play after fouls and are limited only by the imagination of coaches and players, though all must follow the rules (Law 13) and account for the distance and angle to the goal. Free kicks are either direct (a goal may be scored directly) or indirect (the ball must touch another player before a goal counts). While defensive-half kicks typically serve only to retain possession, kicks in the offensive third become set pieces—planned plays designed to defeat the defensive wall and produce a shot on goal. Designs depend on proximity to the goal (five near and three far starting locations, each facing walls of varying size), whether the kick is direct or indirect, and player skill. Possible features include direct shots, simple touches, crosses, stepovers, misdirection, screening, single or double passes, chips, decoys, ghosting, crashing, and rebound follow-up. Execution requires capable, responsible players, possibly including dead-ball specialists, with only one player in charge. Free kicks may be ceremonial (delayed) or quick (immediate, exploiting defensive lapses). Practice progresses from running plays without defenders to live-defender scrimmages, and coaches are advised to prepare contingencies, scout opponents, and keep designs simple.

This passage is a bibliographic list of U.S. government documents and statements from 1945. Items concern: renewal of trade agreements, with testimony by Stettinius, Clayton, Rockefeller, and Taft before congressional committees, and statements by Acting Secretary Grew on the trade-agreements bill; Clayton's remarks on private barriers to international trade; relaxation of export controls; Wilcox's address on international economic relations; letters exchanged between Ickes and Byrnes on foreign oil policies; presidential messages and reports on foreign war relief, the repatriation program, displaced persons (including the Harrison report), UNRRA participation, and Jewish refugees, along with a directive on admitting displaced persons to the United States; Justice Jackson's report on Axis war criminals; a compiled status of countries in relation to the war; and a list of papers for the United Nations Conference on International Organization, San Francisco, April 25–June 26, 1945.

In September 1917, Walter Lippmann wrote to Secretary of War Baker urging a technical study of armament reduction before the peace conference, citing the economic burden of armaments and the difficulty of preventing cheating through subtle mobilization. Baker agreed and proposed that General Bliss lead the study, possibly assisted by General Crowder, which Lippmann endorsed. Separately, Secretary of State Lansing sought a meeting with Dr. Mezes in Washington to discuss how the Department could assist his work. Mezes planned a visit, staying with Mr. Baruch, and sent Lansing a draft outlining the most urgent subjects for The Inquiry. Mezes also sent Lippmann a memorandum outlining the Inquiry's subjects, reflecting points of agreement from their conferences.

This document provides a user-level description of the procedures and abilities of the AGESA™ software, directed at host environment wrapper implementers. It defines procedure call interfaces, specifies a recommended wrapper implementation, and describes optional features, assuming some knowledge of BIOS programming practices.

The document lists related AMD BKDGs and revision guides for Family 14h, 15h, and 16h processors, along with standards including the DDR3 SDRAM Standard, ACPI 5.0, SMBIOS, the Intel MP Specification, and the UEFI C Coding Standards. It defines terminology such as Link, Node, Socket, Processor, Die, Core, Wrapper, BSP, and AP.

The software uses a three-level version numbering scheme (X.Y.Z), while the specification uses two levels (X.Y). Release packages contain binary compilations, build control files, example wrapper files, and specialized build tools. Source files follow the UEFI C Coding Standards with descriptive names and comment headers. Call-in entry points use the "Amd" prefix; call-out procedures use the "Agesa" prefix. Internal documentation is generated using Doxygen and Dot.

The interface is designed to remain constant across processor generations, with call entry points based on boot timeline points rather than specific technical functions. The software automatically determines configuration parameters where possible, but the host environment must supply certain required parameters. Calls use an "initializer" function that allocates and pre-fills interface data structures with defaults. Errors are reported through return codes (ranging from AGESA_SUCCESS to AGESA_FATAL) and an event log retaining the 16 most recent events.

Build options are centralized in a single "<Plat>Options.c" file. Two build methods are supported: binary modules (indirect, using a dispatcher) and source integration. Binary images carry a "$AMD" signature header and "$MOD" module headers, and execution requires 32-bit protected flat addressing mode.

For UEFI environments, the software supports SEC, PEI, and DXE phases with corresponding libraries and build tools. PEI functionality is divided into PEIM modules handling processor initialization, memory initialization, and reset coordination, which publish various PPIs and HOBs. The DXE driver performs late initialization and generates data tables.

The document also describes stack procedures using Cache-As-Ram (such as AMD_ENABLE_STACK and AMD_DISABLE_STACK), service procedures including AmdCreateStruct and AmdReleaseStruct, and boot-time entry procedures including AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost, and AmdInitLate, which perform processor, memory, and platform initialization at defined points in the boot sequence.

Following the Las Vegas shooting, which killed at least 58 and injured nearly 500, WUWF examined local preparedness for mass casualty incidents (MCIs). The largest recent local MCI was the April 30, 2014 explosion in the flooded basement of the Escambia County Jail, which killed two and led to 184 victims being treated and transported among five hospitals in two counties. Public Safety Director Mike Weaver described coordinated triage using color codes, communication between dispatch centers and hospitals, and hospitals canceling elective surgeries. The closest Level I trauma center is USA Medical Center in Mobile; Sacred Heart and Baptist hospitals have Level II centers. Unlike Las Vegas, where victims self-transported and overwhelmed hospitals, responders knew the jail's population. Florida classified both events as Level 4. Regular training continues, and Weaver believes the community could handle an MCI.

In Hunter v. Bales, Bales, as assignee of Thompson, sought specific performance of a real estate sale contract against the Hunters. Moore verbally agreed to sell land to Thompson through his agent, then executed a title bond to Thompson, but subsequently deeded the land to Matthew Hunter, who knew of the prior bond; Hunter later conveyed to Moses Hunter. The court held that where conflicting theories are supported by evidence, the appellate court adopts the theory sustaining the lower court's finding, and affirmed that Thompson held the prior equity entitling him to specific performance. In equity, a land sale contract makes the vendee the owner, with the vendor holding in trust subject to a lien for purchase money, provided the contract supports specific performance. A vendor who makes a valid sale despite a prior parol contract elects to treat it as void, shielding the intermediate purchaser under the statute of frauds. A plaintiff need only offer by complaint to bring purchase money into court, and after tender, is not chargeable with interest unless he used the money, which the vendor must prove. Judgment affirmed with costs.

In a speech at the 64th Annual Worcester County Lincoln Day Dinner, Ronald Reagan criticized the Carter Administration's foreign and national security policies. He argued that Carter's failure to respond decisively to the Iran hostage crisis, in which 50 Americans were held, encouraged the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan and increased the risk of nuclear confrontation. Reagan stated that America must be strong, reliable, and predictable to maintain peace, accusing the Administration of sending timid, contradictory signals to the Soviet Union while enemies surpass the U.S. in military power. He called for a coherent grand strategy for the 1980s centered on preserving peace and freedom, with priorities including rebuilding military strength by exploiting technological advantages, strengthening nuclear deterrent forces, achieving naval superiority over the Soviet build-up, and restoring the capacity to project military power to vital regions such as the Persian Gulf.

The S&P 500 fell 3.33% (214.3 points) over two days from a record high of 6,427.02 to 6,212.69, closing Friday 1.60% lower at its lowest level since early July, after a weekly loss of 2.36%. Another index fell 1.96% Friday on Apple declines, with potential support near 22,300, while the VIX rose to 21.90, its highest since June 23. S&P 500 futures are set to open about 0.5% higher near 6,300, with resistance at 6,330 and support at 6,280. The AAII survey showed 40.3% of investors bullish versus 33.0% bearish. Crude oil dropped 2.79% Friday and another 2.1% after OPEC+ agreed to a sixth straight monthly output increase of 547,000 bpd, fully reversing major supply cuts; U.S. threats of 100% secondary tariffs on Russian-crude buyers put about 1.7 million bpd at risk, and Goldman Sachs forecasts oil at $64 in Q4 2025. The expected rebound is seen as either a short-term bounce within a broader consolidation or a temporary advance in a potential downtrend, with Palantir and AMD earnings ahead and defensive positioning possibly becoming increasingly important.

Cars.com's 2018 American-Made Index ranks vehicles based on U.S. manufacturing, American-made parts, and support of American factory jobs, including parts percentage, engine and transmission origins, and assembly location. The Jeep Cherokee tops the list, though its parent company, Fiat Chrysler, is based in Europe. Honda has four vehicles in the top 10, and Ford has three. With tariffs threatening higher costs for imported vehicles, determining what qualifies as American-made is complicated by globally sourced automotive parts.

This study compared a hybridization capture-based metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) workflow (Illumina Respiratory Pathogen ID/AMR enrichment panel) with a commercial PCR panel (FTD Respiratory Pathogens 33) on 29 nasopharyngeal samples from individuals suspected of acute upper respiratory infection. PCR detected 15 microorganisms (4 bacteria, 11 viruses) in 28 positive samples, while mNGS identified 44 microorganisms (27 bacteria, 2 fungi, 15 viruses). The methods showed high concordance (98.33% positive percent agreement, 100% negative percent agreement) for the 33 shared targets, with mNGS detecting 29 additional microorganisms beyond the PCR panel. Microorganisms were phenotypically classified into three groups by pathogenic potential using the IDbyDNA Explify Platform. mNGS exclusively identified Coxsackievirus A, SARS-CoV-2 (confirmed by separate specific PCR), and human rhinovirus C, all classified as pathogenic (group 3). The authors conclude that hybridization capture-based mNGS may offer advantages in deciphering etiological agents of respiratory (co)infections and assessing trafficking potential to the lower respiratory tract, though further investigations are required to establish clinical relevance of the phenotypic classifications.

The Florida Department of Transportation presented two plans at a public meeting to connect the Sawgrass Expressway and I-95 via Southwest 10th Street in Deerfield Beach, a project previously blocked by neighbors in the 1980s. The connector, at least three years from construction, would include depressed roadways to ease rush-hour congestion. Local residents expressed opposition, citing property value and quality-of-life concerns.

Nigeria is experiencing a mass exodus of doctors to the UK and US, with 88 percent planning to migrate. The physician-patient ratio has worsened to 1:5,000 against WHO's recommended 1:600. Nigeria needs 303,000 doctors but has only about 35,000 practicing, due to high taxes, low satisfaction, and poor salaries.

This paper introduces an architecture for digitally structured information exchange between industrial enterprises, focusing on the lifecycle domain and technical information. Current exchange practices are manual, labor-intensive, and error-prone (e.g., spreadsheets and email), and existing standards such as EDI do not address technical information. The proposed architecture consists of an open consortium that agrees on common business practices and information formats, and a network of mediators that deliver information between enterprises. Each business party connects to a mediator via a single adapter that maps its heterogeneous back-end systems to the common formats. Mediators implement multi-sided platforms and may also provide matchmaking services. A functional prototype was implemented, and experiments involving two equipment suppliers and two plant operators successfully delivered equipment information (valves and pumps) for maintenance and renewal project cases. Because no consortium or API specifications exist yet, the prototype used import/export applications communicating via spreadsheets instead of actual adapters. The main challenge for realizing the concept is organizing the ecosystem, as the required ICT technologies already exist. Future work includes forming an open consortium, extending the prototype into a mediator network, and expanding the scope to financing, logistics, manufacturing, and marine industry.

This case study investigated the experiences of first-year Physical Education Teacher Education (PETE) students in a 14-week movement education course at a university in Türkiye, where peer mentoring and storytelling were used to develop 21st-century skills. Participants included 3 peer mentors, 25 first-year peer learners, and a course lecturer. Peer mentors created lesson content using narratives from well-known series, cartoons, and digital games, communicated with learners via Instagram and Discord, and provided support in and out of class. In the final four weeks, peer learners applied their own storytelling-based teaching designs. Three themes emerged: peer learners excluded non-contributing members from group work while peer mentors divided responsibilities to complete tasks; peer mentors developed accountability and responsibility through content creation and interaction with a wider audience; and storytelling connected learning to daily life, making knowledge more permanent. The study concluded that peer mentoring provided real field experience, served as a bridge between students and teaching staff, and that storytelling ensured permanent learning. It recommends integrating peer mentoring and storytelling into undergraduate programs and conducting long-term studies.

In Asa B. Meech and others v. The City of Buffalo, property owners sought to restrain collection of a second assessment for constructing a sewer in Mariner street. The common council had determined the amount to be assessed at $1,058.63, assessed that sum upon the benefited real estate, and contracted with Robert J. Randolph to build the sewer, with security for performance. During construction, Randolph encountered an extensive body of quicksand, previously unknown to both parties, which made completion impossible for even twice the contract price. He stopped work and, joined by several plaintiffs, petitioned the common council; the council allowed an additional $588.13 and directed a further assessment on the benefited property. The judge at special term held the second assessment illegal and restrained its collection, but the general term of the supreme court reversed and ordered a new trial, from which the plaintiffs appealed with a stipulation that judgment absolute be entered against them if affirmed. The court held that the supplementary assessment was authorized by the charter as a "further assessment" within the meaning of the provision permitting further assessment when the original proves insufficient. Wright, J., reasoned that a municipal corporation empowered to make a public improvement and contract for the work may increase the contract price where circumstances equitably justify it, unless prohibited by its charter, and that if a first assessment proves insufficient, the corporation has not only the power but the duty to order a further assessment. All judges concurring, the judgment of the general term was affirmed and judgment absolute was rendered against the plaintiffs.

The Korean diet (K-diet) is based on traditional Korean eating habits, emphasizing whole, unprocessed foods including fresh vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, and fermented foods such as kimchi. It is low in sugars and unhealthy fats, with smaller portions than Western diets. Recommended foods include rice, barley, vegetables, fermented products, and seasonings like sesame oil and soy sauce. Foods to avoid include processed foods, sugary drinks, unhealthy fats, and dairy. Benefits include high fibre, low calories, gut health from fermented foods, and antioxidants. Drawbacks include high sodium content, which is unsuitable for people with high blood pressure, low calcium due to the lack of dairy, spicy ingredients that may irritate digestive issues, and high carbohydrates requiring portion control. The diet can be adapted for vegan, low-carb, and gluten-free needs.

Motley Fool Money promotes the Citi Simplicity® Card, which offers 0% intro APR for 21 months on balance transfers and 12 months on purchases, with a variable APR of 17.99%–28.74% afterward. The card has no annual fee, late fees, or penalty rate. A 3% balance transfer fee (minimum $5) applies within the first four months of account opening, increasing to 5% afterward. Balance transfers must be completed within four months. The recommended credit score is Good/Excellent (670–850). The passage estimates someone with $5,000 in debt at 24% APR could save over $2,428. Motley Fool Money discloses receiving partner compensation, including from Citi.

Google is launching three new "appsperimentals" for Android and iOS, following the success of Motion Stills. The apps use experimental technologies like object recognition, person segmentation, stylization, and image encoding/decoding. Storyboard (Android) converts videos into single-page comic layouts with six visual styles. Selfissimo! (iOS, Android) automatically captures black and white selfies when users stop moving. Scrubbies (iOS) lets users manipulate video playback speed and direction to create loops. The technologies are under active research, and Google hopes public feedback will guide future development.

The passage consists of ESPN college football headlines followed by a Week 6 Power Rankings analysis focused on Top 25 offenses as the season's halfway point approaches. Preseason No. 1 Texas and No. 2 Penn State both fell out of the Top 25; Texas lost 29-21 to unranked Florida, with quarterback Manning throwing two interceptions (five this season) and being sacked six times, while Penn State lost at UCLA. Team notes include: Ohio State's rushing attack ranking ninth in the Big Ten; 5-0 Miami, behind Carson Beck's four touchdowns against Florida State, experiencing second-half lulls; Oregon's Dante Moore throwing 14 touchdowns against one interception, with freshman running backs leading the ground game; Indiana's offense averaging 47.8 points per game but converting only 2 of 8 fourth downs; Oklahoma's run game ranking 105th nationally while quarterback Mateer recovers from hand surgery; Alabama's Ty Simpson rushing for 136 yards and a score in a 30-14 win over Vanderbilt but taking four sacks; Georgia's offensive line injury issues; LSU ranking 73rd on offense with a struggling run game; Memphis improving to 6-0 behind Brendon Lewis's 266 yards and three touchdowns; Cincinnati's balanced attack in a 38-30 win over Iowa State; and Vanderbilt's turnovers and penalties in its loss to Alabama. Headlines also cover Oregon State firing its special teams coordinator, Stoops saying there is "zero chance" he leaves Kentucky, Deion Sanders seeing a doctor about possible leg clots, betting lines, recruiting, and NFL draft notes. The passage ends with ESPN BET and website privacy/cookie notices.

This passage documents version 2 of the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) specification. Version 2 introduces hypervisor feature advertisement via a FEATURES bitmap, limited to 52 bits so it can be returned through the GHCB MSR protocol before a GHCB is established; full specification support is mandatory unless a feature is marked optional. The GHCB's guest physical address is guest-specified, must be 4K-aligned, is saved/restored in the VMCB (offset 0xa0), and is accessed through MSR 0xc001_0130, whose lower 12 bits carry the MSR protocol. Protocol functions include hypervisor feature support request/response, SEV information, CPUID requests, AP reset hold, preferred GHCB GPA, GHCB GPA registration/unregistration (required for SEV-SNP guests), page state change, Run VMPL, and termination requests. Negotiation examples are provided for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests, covering protocol version negotiation and obtaining the page table encryption bit.

Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) events generate #VC exceptions; the guest copies required state into the GHCB and invokes VMGEXIT. Supported NAE events include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, MMIO access, Page State Change, SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request (certificate return), AP Creation, #HV doorbell page, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SEV-TIO (trusted device I/O), Secure AVIC backing page management, and termination requests. Errors are communicated through SW_EXITINFO1/SW_EXITINFO2.

Further topics include CPUID-based guest identification of SEV-ES; SMP booting constraints (measured registers cannot be changed, requiring AP Reset Hold or SNP AP Creation, plus an AP jump table for environment transitions); NMI handling (intercept #DB, not IRET; guest issues "NMI Complete"); debug register virtualization; and explicit statements that SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

Finally, the #HV doorbell page used with SNP Restricted Injection is described: it contains a PendingEvent field (vector number, NMI/#MC flags, NoFurtherSignal) and a NoEoiRequired EOI-assist byte. The host presents interrupts by writing vector numbers, the guest acknowledges via atomic exchange, and specific host/guest behaviors and HLT interrupt-shadow conventions are defined.

Pumpkin, a fruit in the Cucurbitaceae family, is a nutritious food that can be used in many dishes beyond pie, such as salads, soups, and baked goods. One cup of cooked pumpkin contains about 52 calories, 3 grams of fibre, iron, potassium (more than a large banana), vitamin E, and carotenoids including beta-carotene, alpha-carotene, and lutein. Carotenoids are described as anti-cancer and anti-inflammatory, with lutein helping reduce the risk of age-related macular degeneration. The passage lists five health benefits of pumpkin: reduced cardiovascular disease risk, immune support, eye health, protection for the brain against dementia and cognitive decline, and lower blood pressure through a higher potassium-to-sodium ratio. The article is written by registered dietitian Doug Cook.

The Russian cruiser's forcible removal of the Cape Horn Pigeon's American crew to serve aboard a Russian vessel violated their natural rights, exposing Russia to damages exceeding the mere value of their labor. The seamen's agreement at Vladivostok, made without counsel, to accept only the value of their labor should not prejudice their claims for indemnity for injury to national pride and violation of personal liberty. Landed at Vladivostok without food or shelter, they took refuge in squalid quarters; the jail lodging allegedly offered by Russia would not have been adequate for innocent citizens of a friendly nation. Full indemnity for both wrongs is expected, and allowing interest on awards is a universally admitted principle, supported by precedents including the 1794 US-British commission, the Chinese indemnity arbitration (12 percent), the 1871 claims commission, the Alabama claims (6 percent), arbitrations against Mexico and Brazil, the Costa Rica Packet (5 percent), and the 1897 Bering Sea arbitration. Regarding damages, Captain Scullun's average catch estimate of 8 whales is reasonable, bone averaged about 1,250 pounds per whale, and oil averaged 100 barrels per whale. As the seizure occurred September 10, claimants are entitled to the August bone price of $5 per pound; oil is established at $13 per barrel.

This paper presents a PRISMA-compliant systematic review of the social science of large language models (LLMs), combining unsupervised machine learning with expert classification. From 64,717 records screened across seven databases (final refresh September 19, 2025), 270 studies were included. Study 1 embedded documents using Sentence-BERT and applied K-means clustering, yielding a stable three-cluster taxonomy: LLM as Social Minds (n=111), concerning mind-like capacities, moral and social reasoning, bias, self-regulation, and deception; LLM Societies (n=99), covering multi-agent simulations, cooperation and games, collective epistemics, institutional design, and group decision-making; and LLM–Human Interactions (n=60), addressing perception and trust, affect and communication, collaboration, education, productivity and inequality, and interactional risks. Latent Dirichlet Allocation provided two interpretable topics per cluster. Study 2 compared the machine taxonomy with an expert-coded classification, finding strong alignment (Macro-F1 = 0.954 ± 0.018, NMI = 0.811, ARI = 0.867). Consensus stability analyses (median ARI ≈ 0.985, AMI ≈ 0.989 across resamples) supported replicability. The authors treat the three clusters as levels of analysis rather than rival schools, arguing the taxonomy enables cumulative, testable research on AI's social dimensions. Limitations include English-language-only coverage, a September 2025 search cutoff, and reliance on narrative synthesis rather than pooled effect sizes. The paper concludes that understanding AI's sociality requires focusing on institutional design and auditing rather than anthropomorphic questions about whether LLMs resemble persons.

Wiseguyreports.com has added a report titled "Smart Service Robots Market – Market Demand, Growth, Opportunities, Analysis of Top Key Players and Forecast to 2022" to its research database. The report provides an in-depth study of the market using SWOT analysis and profiles key players including SoftBank, Kawada, Honda, and Hajime Research Institute (Japan); PROTRYLY VISION GROUP, Ubtech Robotics, Suzhou Pangolin Robot, SIASUN Robot, and QIHAN Technology/Sanbot (China); ROBOTIS, Hanson Robotics, and Dongbu Robot (Korea); Engineered Arts (UK); and Willow Garage (US). It covers production, price, revenue, and market share by manufacturer, segmented by region (North America, Europe, China, Japan, Southeast Asia, India) for 2012–2022. Products are categorized as Personal and Professional Service Robots, with applications in Commercial and Home Use. Manufacturer profiles include company information, products, capacity, production, revenue, price, and gross margin.

This document describes AMD's Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine, an optional extension to System Encryption, the Secure Encrypted Virtualization API (SEV), and the SEV Secure Nested Paging Firmware ABI Specification (SNP) that facilitates page migration—the copying of page content and updating of virtual-to-physical mappings. TMPM requires IOMMU enablement and support can be checked via the ENGINE_READY bit in the PM_Status register. TMPM can pause DMA traffic during migration, enabling safe migration of pages under active DMA use, and acts as a trusted agent capable of migrating SNP-protected guest pages. The PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO command migrates pages that are concurrent DMA targets, while PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages. A new Pre-Migration state supports SNP guest page migration. Multi-page commands can migrate up to 128 pages via a Page Migration List, with per-page status entries; performance is best with 128-page commands. Certain IOMMU data structures and the ring buffer cannot be migrated. TMPM firmware can be reloaded when no operations are in flight, with reload procedures varying by EPYC family (Family 19h is represented by a FW_VER_Major value of 71 decimal). All system physical addresses must be 4KB aligned.

Amazon.com, Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2016 reports net sales of $32.7 billion for Q3 2016, up 29% from $25.4 billion in Q3 2015, and $92.2 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2016. Operating income was $575 million in Q3 2016 versus $406 million in Q3 2015, and net income was $252 million versus $79 million, with diluted EPS of $0.52 versus $0.17. The company operates three segments: North America (Q3 net sales $18.9 billion, operating income $255 million), International (net sales $10.6 billion, operating loss $541 million), and AWS (net sales $3.2 billion, operating income $861 million). Cash provided by operating activities was $4.5 billion in Q3 2016. Total assets were $70.9 billion as of September 30, 2016, including cash and cash equivalents of $13.7 billion. Long-term debt had a face value of $8.3 billion. In February 2016, the Board authorized a $5.0 billion stock repurchase program, with no repurchases in Q3 2016. Legal and tax matters include a September 2016 patent infringement complaint filed by Broadcom and Avago Technologies, an IRS transfer pricing dispute seeking approximately $1.5 billion in additional federal tax for 2005–2006, a French tax assessment of €196 million for 2006–2010, and a European Commission state aid investigation regarding Luxembourg tax rulings. Tax contingencies were $1.7 billion as of September 30, 2016.

The San Francisco 49ers ruled out quarterback Brock Purdy and receivers Ricky Pearsall and Jauan Jennings for their Thursday night game against the Rams, leaving the offense short-handed. Mac Jones is set to start at quarterback—his third start in the first five games—after leading wins in Weeks 2 and 3. Jones is back to full strength after battling a sprained knee. Purdy had expressed optimism about playing despite toe soreness but noted the short turnaround to Thursday made recovery difficult. Pearsall and Jennings both aggravated injuries against Jacksonville, with Pearsall landing hard on his right knee and Jennings taking a hit to the ribs. Jones will likely work with receivers Robinson and Bourne against a Rams defense he called the best in the NFL, which ranks ninth in yards allowed per game, fifth in defensive expected points added, and tied for second in sacks. The 49ers also ruled out a defensive end and will face Tampa Bay in Week 6 after extra rest.

Lincoln County won the first two sets against Laughlin in last Thursday's Homecoming game before the Cougars came back. Coach Chantel Holt noted the team struggled mentally when close to finishing in four sets. Lincoln won the final set to 15, holding Laughlin under 10 points. Holt said her substitutions built camaraderie and gave everyone a chance to play. The Lady Lynx play Calvary at home today at 3 and 4 p.m.

King Salman held talks with Turkish President Erdogan at Al-Yamama Palace in Riyadh, reviewing bilateral relations, cooperation, and regional and international developments. Crown Prince Muhammad Bin Naif later held separate talks with Erdogan on regional peace, security, and combating terrorism.

This passage describes a year-long knowledge exchange project (October 2023–June 2024) between University College London's Institute of Education Citizenship PGCE program and Diversity Role Models, an LGBTQ+ anti-bullying charity, which supported student teachers in England in educating for trans inclusion amid rising hostility toward transgender communities. The project included three workshops on embedding trans-inclusive practices in the citizenship curriculum, with student teachers applying this learning during school placements and presenting their experiences at the project's end.

The political context includes intense media debate on transgender youth, which has coincided with increased transphobic hate crimes and scrutiny of schools. In December 2023, England's Department for Education released draft non-statutory guidance on supporting "gender questioning children," which was widely criticized by education and human rights organizations for potentially leading to students being forcibly outed. A May 2024 draft Relationship, Sex and Health Education guidance proposed banning discussion of gender identity in schools, though the Equality Act 2010 still protects transgender people under "gender reassignment," and schools must teach about this protected characteristic.

Student teachers' presentations showed that "actualizing" LGBTQ+ identities—making subjects concrete in real-life contexts—was their most-cited approach, but this related almost exclusively to sexual orientation rather than transgender identities. They attributed this gap to fear stemming from media debates and proposed government guidance, noting a lack of confidence in discussing gender identity.

Key pedagogical approaches included sharing personal stories and "counter-stories" from LGBTQ+ role models to build empathy, and grounding lessons in the Equality Act 2010 to frame all students as rights holders and foster allyship. International frameworks—the UNCRC, Yogyakarta Principles+10, the Incheon Declaration, and UNESCO/Plan International guidance—were highlighted as supporting comprehensive sexuality education and teacher training for trans inclusion.

Participants also emphasized whole-school approaches beyond discrete lessons: consistent behavior and anti-bullying policies, restorative approaches, visibility through displays and Pride clubs, and bystander-to-upstander training. The authors conclude that Citizenship education, combined with personal stories and rights-based frameworks, can promote trans equality, but that teachers need effective training and support, and that partnerships with specialist civil society organizations are important for inclusive education.

The President calls on Congress, before adjournment, to provide a substantial reduction in tariff duties on Cuban imports, citing reasons of morality and national interest. Cuba's Constitution affirms that she will maintain closer relations with the United States than with any other power, and the message quotes President McKinley's 1898 and 1899 messages supporting friendly, reciprocal commercial ties with Cuba. The President reports receiving an appeal from President Palma urging legislative relief to prevent Cuba's financial ruin. He argues that reciprocity with Cuba stands alone, outweighs reciprocity with any other nation, and is consistent with the protective tariff system, which already allowed reductions of up to 20 percent for a particular country. Objections that benefits would go to American sugar refiners rather than producers can, in his judgment, be addressed. Fears of harm to American industries, like earlier fears regarding Hawaii, are baseless. Following the war with Spain and the prospective Isthmian Canal, the United States will take greater interest in the West Indies and Central America. Since Cuba has assumed special political obligations at American request, the President asks for special economic concessions in return, noting Cuba is a weak republic that owes her existence to American aid and sacrifice.

The passage describes medical problems reported after booster doses of BNT162b2 (5 or 10 µg in Phase 3; 30 µg in Phase 2/3), referencing Tables 6–8 whose contents are not shown. A serious medical problem is defined as life-threatening, requiring hospital care, or causing lasting problems. In Phase 1, two participants had serious medical problems within 1 to 6 months after Dose 2: one of 24 participants (4%) in the BNT162b2 20-µg group had an inflamed appendix, and one of 24 participants (4%) in the 30-µg group had inflamed nerves.

Taiwanese health authorities warn against raw or undercooked eggs amid rising avian flu risk, urging thorough cooking to at least 70°C, handwashing after handling eggshells, and masks with doctor visits for fevers.

Malaysia's central bank will allow all resident entities to short-sell Malaysian government securities from May 2 to boost bond market liquidity. Non-bank entities will gain expanded hedging allowances, and residents may hedge up to 6 million ringgit per bank in sterling, euro, and yen without documentation. BNM is also considering short selling of shariah-compliant MGII bonds and will replace its 1994 financial markets code of conduct.

In an action against the executor of James McKechnie, plaintiff Charles Jones sought to enforce an alleged agreement by which McKechnie promised to protect and save him harmless from liability on notes he endorsed for Sherman Kingsbury, the plaintiff's son-in-law, at the banking firm of McKechnie & Company. Jones claimed that after Kingsbury failed to pay the notes, mortgages he had given as collateral were foreclosed and his real estate was lost. A jury verdict awarded him $16,369.69 against the defendant. The alleged agreements were claimed to have been made in the presence of only Jones, Kingsbury, McKechnie, and Denbow; both McKechnie and Denbow died before the action was brought, leaving Kingsbury, an interested witness, as the principal witness, whose testimony was subject to suspicion. The court found error in the admission of evidence concerning hop speculation by Kingsbury, McKechnie, and Denbow, including testimony that McKechnie refused an offer of forty cents a pound for hops which, if accepted, would have paid Kingsbury's debts. This evidence was held foreign to the issues, calculated to excite sympathy for the plaintiff and prejudice against McKechnie, and damaging to the defendant's case. The judgment and order appealed from were reversed and a new trial granted, costs to abide the event.

Magda Enriquez chose the Revolution over her marriage when her husband discovered her secret work for the Sandinistas in Somoza's Nicaragua. Six years later she sits on Nicaragua's Council of State representing the women's association AMNLAE. Educated at an American university, she founded Nicaragua's first school for mentally retarded children in 1970, but discovering that malnutrition caused most children's conditions drew her into Managua's slums. A Roman Catholic influenced by liberation theology, she joined the Sandinistas secretly in 1976. A 1978 land sit-in, where police jailed men, tractors threatened women, and poison dropped from a plane left ten children dead before treatment, prompted her to request military training. Her 14-year-old son serves in the militia. She credits the Revolution with creating opportunities to solve women's problems and prepare elections, and views her life as rebutting claims that women cannot reconcile public and private roles.

Harry Kane led England to a 4-3 penalty shootout victory over Colombia in the World Cup Round of 16, scoring the opener and converting his penalty, with Eric Dier netting the winning shot. England face Sweden in the quarter-final on Saturday. Kane leads the tournament scoring with six goals. Kieran Trippier praised the team's spirit, while Radamel Falcao accused the referee of bias toward England, and Diego Maradona called the result a monumental theft.

Between 24 and 48 weeks, adverse events occurred in 33.8–40.8% of subjects across the three study groups, with serious AEs in 11.8–14.0% and two fatal bleeding events. Twenty-four deaths were reported overall, and no pregnancies occurred. The AEGEAN study demonstrated high adherence and persistence with apixaban up to 48 weeks; the educational program provided no additional benefit.

Hinsdale South High School seniors were named Illinois State Scholars, a program recognizing outstanding academic achievement. Selection is based on ACT and SAT scores, unweighted GPA, and class size at the end of junior year, with the top 10 percent of the state's graduating seniors qualifying.

The article examines how likely retirees and FIRE (Financial Independence Retire Early) individuals are to go broke, noting that low interest rates push them toward risky stocks and that bear markets can last a decade or longer. An example couple retiring in January 2000 with $1 million, withdrawing $50,000 annually from US large-cap funds, went broke by 2017 due to poor diversification, a high withdrawal rate, and an unlucky sequence of returns including the dot-com crash and the 2008 financial crisis. Sequence risk—the order of returns—matters greatly because of compounding; a Monte Carlo simulation by Mark Spitznagel reshuffling 120 years of S&P 500 returns showed a 10% chance of a CAGR below about 3%. William Bengen's 4% rule, established in 1994, suggests withdrawing 4% annually, though even this rate only delayed the couple's ruin, while a 3% rate allowed recovery. Diversification can offset higher withdrawal rates but has limitations, as correlations change over time. Edward Thorp recommends limiting inflation-adjusted spending to 2% of an endowment's original value. The article concludes that avoiding ruin requires a large margin of safety, a conservative withdrawal rate, diversification, and frugal spending.

Appleton couple Andrea and Luke Benrud gained national attention after Luke used CPR, learned in a Red Cross class, to save Andrea when she collapsed from a rare, undetected heart defect. The now-recovered, CPR-trained family shares their story to encourage others to learn CPR.

Body camera footage shows former Grand Rapids Officer Kevin Penn pressing the muzzle of his AR-15 rifle against a suspect's head during an August 19 arrest that appeared to be a case of mistaken identity. The drunk, noncompliant suspect was subdued with a taser by Sgt. Neil Gomez before Penn pressed the rifle to his head, which he told investigators was to control the individual. Officer James Smith pushed the rifle away. The suspect was arrested on resisting arrest charges and later released. Kent County Prosecutor Chris Becker said Tuesday the behavior was unacceptable but no charges would be filed; Penn resigned after other officers reported him.

Analysts expect the European Central Bank to temper expectations for a quick exit from its stimulus programme at Thursday's meeting, keeping interest rates at historic lows and maintaining a September expiry for its 30-billion-euro monthly bond-buying scheme. Downside risks have re-emerged, including a stronger euro, sluggish inflation (1.3 per cent in March against a target just below 2.0 per cent), and threatened US tariffs on metals imports. Despite growth of 2.3 per cent in 2017 and forecasts of 2.4 per cent for 2018, recent indicators suggest the economy has slowed. Analysts expect any policy normalisation to remain gradual.

Kinlochleven has received three new defibrillators through local fundraising. Lucky 2B Here presented two defibrillators, cabinets and life support training to community first responders, with a third donated by Marcus and Martine Spence. The group has raised £2,900 of its £3,500 target.

Jonathan Erick Miles, 33, was charged with manufacture and possession of a controlled substance, possession of drug paraphernalia, and endangering the welfare of children after police executing an April 9 search warrant found two marijuana plants, controlled substances, and illegal smoking devices in his home. He was released on $20,000 unsecured bail. Manheim Township police also reported charges against three other men for indecent assault, corruption of minors, and offenses from a domestic dispute.

Companies participate in exhibitions and events to enhance brand image and gather customer feedback, requiring experienced hosts and trade show models. While recruitment agencies are expensive with limited databases, Professionate, an online event staffing agency, connects companies with temporary job aspirants. Companies can access thousands of candidate profiles with images, ratings, and reviews worldwide. Recruitment agencies and candidates can also benefit from the portal. Professionate offers professional hosting services in Dubai.

The UN warns that two years of war may deprive Yemeni children of education, putting them at risk of early marriage or military recruitment. Unpaid salaries affecting 73 percent of teachers mean up to 4.5 million children may not finish the school year. The crisis began when the government moved the central bank out of Houthi-controlled Sanaa.

This study examined sex differences in the correlation between self-reported PCL-5 and clinician-administered CAPS-5 scores for PTSD symptom severity in 100 adults (56 males, 44 females). While CAPS-5 scores did not differ by sex or trauma type, females showed a stronger PCL-5/CAPS-5 correlation (Rho = 0.907) than males (Rho = 0.655), and a higher odds ratio for PCL-5 predicting CAPS-5 (144.6 vs. 11.8). Only males deviated significantly from the ideal regression line (mean difference of 12.5), and 26.8% of males were misclassified by PCL-5 compared with 11.4% of females. Civilian trauma was associated with a stronger correlation (Rho = 0.885) than military trauma (Rho = 0.523), a pattern consistent within each sex. The authors suggest PCL-5 may be less reliable for males and recommend caution when relying on self-report alone, considering sex and trauma type. Limitations include the small sample and regional recruitment.

A new Channel 4 documentary, *The Super Orgasm*, follows five women who report experiencing "super orgasms"—up to 100 orgasms in one sexual encounter. The women underwent three experiments exploring psychological, neurological, and endocrinological factors. Results indicated the women were easily aroused, showed specific alpha wave patterns during multiple orgasms, and had increased blood flow in more than 30 brain areas, unlike women who have a single orgasm. Experts note the research was not scientific, given the small sample size and absence of control participants. Cynthia Graham and Nan Wise question the term "super orgasm," saying it differs little from multiple orgasms, which are not unusual for women. They also criticize the documentary's suggestion that all women could achieve super orgasms, describing the participants as outliers and noting that most women are content with one or a few orgasms.

The lecture continues a discussion of continuity, defined as x being sufficiently close to c implying f(x) is close to f(c).
