A three-part theorem is presented and proved: if c is not a cluster point of s, every function is continuous at c (a degenerate case); if c is a cluster point, f is continuous at c if and only if the limit of f(x) as x approaches c equals f(c); and f is continuous at c if and only if for every sequence xₙ in s converging to c, f(xₙ) converges to f(c). The last part is proved by contradiction using a sequence constructed with deltas 1, 1/2, 1/3, and the squeeze theorem.

As examples, sine is shown continuous directly via the epsilon-delta definition using trigonometric identities, and cosine is shown continuous using cos(x) = sin(x + π/2) together with the sequential characterization. A function equaling 1 at irrationals and 0 at rationals is shown to be discontinuous at every real number, using the density of rationals and irrationals.

Further theorems establish that sums, products, quotients (with nonzero denominator), and compositions of continuous functions are continuous. Consequences include that xⁿ and polynomials are continuous, illustrated also by 1/(3 + sin⁴x). The next lecture will cover the min and max theorems and the intermediate value theorem.

Cover 3 is a common zone defense featuring four underneath players and three deep players, used extensively by coaches such as Nick Saban and Pete Carroll. The three deep defenders—two cornerbacks and a free safety—divide the deep field into thirds, while four underneath defenders cover the Hook, Curl, and Flat zones on both sides of the formation. Compared to Cover 2, it adds a third deep defender and allows an extra safety near the line of scrimmage to help stop the run. Its strengths include balanced coverage against deep and intermediate threats and effectiveness against balanced run-pass offenses, making it popular at the high school and college levels. Weaknesses include vulnerability in the flats, seam routes against four verticals concepts, perimeter run defense, and challenging personnel matchups. Variations include flipping the safeties, the Fire Zone blitz, Cover 3 Buzz, and pattern reading coverage such as Rip/Liz.

FDA approved a second generic version of the abortion pill mifepristone. Amgen reported that its cholesterol-lowering injection Repatha cut the risk of heart disease death, heart attacks, and strokes in a 12,000-patient trial, bolstering hopes for wider use of PCSK9 inhibitors. The newsletter also mentions a new NIH office intended to reduce reliance on animal testing.

The court addressed whether John Jacob Beechwood, named in an involuntary bankruptcy petition filed by American Surety Company of New York, was immune from bankruptcy as a farmer under the Bankruptcy Act. A jury found him insolvent and guilty of acts of bankruptcy, including a September 20, 1940 conveyance of his Burlington County, New Jersey farm to his wife with intent to hinder, delay, or defraud creditors. Beechwood, a lawyer employed for 15 years by Fidelity and Casualty Company at a $7,200 salary, confessed on September 23, 1940 to authorizing fraudulent drafts exceeding $100,000, with his resignation retroactively effective September 16, 1940. The farm was operated by an employed farmer, and Beechwood worked it only in his leisure time, netting up to $2,500 annually. The court held that on the dates of the acts of bankruptcy, the principal part of his income came from his employment, not farming, and that the 1938 amendment narrowed the statutory definition. His cited cases were found inapplicable, his defense failed, and an order adjudicating him bankrupt was to be entered.

The President, replying to House resolutions, transmits the Secretary of State's report and all documents and correspondence concerning the treaty of peace concluded with Mexico at Guadalupe Hidalgo on February 2, 1848, and the Senate's amendments. Though he had earlier declined to publish the commissioners' instructions, deeming publicity potentially prejudicial to the public interest, he now transmits them because they are indispensable to understanding the other requested documents. The instructions of March 18, 1848, confined the commissioners to procuring Mexican ratification of the treaty as amended by the Senate, without authority to modify it, and directed them to explain the amendments through personal conferences rather than diplomatic notes. The Secretary of State's letter of March 18, 1848, was the only explanation before the Mexican Congress, which approved the amended treaty on May 25, 1848, without alteration—before the commissioners had been officially received. Ratifications were exchanged on May 30, and the ratified treaty was received in Washington on July 4, 1848, proclaimed, and communicated to Congress on July 6. The President states that the protocol recording the commissioners' conversations with Mexican officials, held after ratification, was regarded by neither government as modifying the treaty and would have been a nullity had it done so. The protocol's three explanations—that substituting the Louisiana treaty's third article preserved the inhabitants' civil, political, and religious rights; that suppressing the tenth article did not invalidate legitimate land grants; and that suppressing part of the twelfth article did not deprive Mexico of the ability to transfer the $12,000,000 payments—were, in his view, consistent with the treaty, requiring no action on his part.

S. E. Mezes reported good progress at a Thursday meeting on The Inquiry and sent memorandum copies to attendees. The memorandum covers the technique of peace conferences, data on war-breeding areas, national aspirations, governmental arrangements for international areas such as Dantzig, Trieste, Saloniki, and Constantinople, world organization, laws of war, reparation for damage, internationalized trade routes, and business and diplomacy. Document No. 893, "A Preliminary Survey," lists tasks the Inquiry can help the Conference with, including establishing boundaries, setting up governments, estimating doubtful states, economic arrangements, safeguarding minorities, equality of economic opportunity, rewriting international law, and noting diplomatic history. Regions addressed include Russia, Poland, Slesvig, Belgium, Luxemburg, Alsace-Lorraine, Trentino, Triest, Austria-Hungary, the Balkans, Turkey, Africa, the Far East, Pacific Islands, Latin America, Persia, Afghanistan, and Spitsbergen. Boundaries must be established for Poland, Alsace-Lorraine, Trentino, Triest, Austria-Hungary, the Balkans, and Turkey; governments for Poland and Austria-Hungary.

Amazon is preparing to cut up to 15% of its human resources staff, known internally as PXT, with additional layoffs likely in other divisions including its core consumer business, according to sources. The total number of affected employees and exact timing are unknown. The cuts come as Amazon invests aggressively in AI while lowering employee costs, with plans to spend over $100 billion in capital expenditures this year. CEO Andy Jassy previously oversaw the largest layoffs in company history—over 27,000 corporate jobs from late 2022 into 2023—and has said AI-driven efficiency gains will reduce the total corporate workforce. Meanwhile, Amazon announced plans to hire 250,000 seasonal warehouse employees for the holidays.

In an inaugural address, the speaker affirms the enduring strength of the Constitution and the nation's founding creed that all people are created equal with unalienable rights to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. The address recounts historical progress—ending the division of slave and free, building infrastructure, and establishing rules for a free market—while stressing that preserving individual freedoms requires collective action. It declares that prosperity must rest on a rising middle class, that citizens deserve security and dignity through commitments like Medicare, Medicaid, and Social Security, and that America must respond to climate change and lead the transition to sustainable energy. The speaker states that lasting peace does not require perpetual war and pledges continued alliances, support for democracy abroad, and hope for the poor and marginalized. The address says the nation's journey is incomplete until women earn equal pay, gay citizens are treated equally under law, voting is accessible, immigrants are welcomed, and all children are safe. It urges action over delay and absolutism, notes that the oath sworn is to God and country rather than party, and closes by calling on citizens to shape the nation's course through their votes and voices.

A study published in the Journal of Hematology & Thromboembolic Diseases by researchers at the University of Brasilia examined the effects of Bt toxin spore-crystals (Cry1Aa, Cry1Ab, Cry1Ac, and Cry2A) engineered into genetically modified food crops. The study found these toxins capable of targeting mammalian cells, particularly the erythroid (red blood cell) lineage, producing changes indicative of anemia. Cry toxins also suppressed bone marrow proliferation and created abnormal lymphocyte patterns consistent with some types of leukemia. The findings contradicted earlier assumptions that Bt toxicity is limited to insects: the toxins exerted adverse effects when suspended in distilled water without requiring alkalinization; a low dose of Cry1Ab (27 mg/kg) induced hypochromic anemia in mice; effects became more pronounced after 72 hours of exposure; and high doses caused blood changes indicative of bone marrow damage. The researchers concluded that further studies are required to clarify the mechanism of hematotoxicity and establish toxicological risks to mammals before deeming these microbiological control agents safe. The passage also references a French study linking GM corn and Roundup to cancer in rats, notes glyphosate has been linked to non-Hodgkins lymphoma and hairy cell leukemia, and states that combined toxicity of Cry toxins and glyphosate residues has not been sufficiently explored.

The Times reported that officials identified Paul Manafort, Trump's campaign chairman, as an adviser picked up on calls; Manafort denied this. U.S. intelligence officials suspect Russia of cyber-attacks on Democratic institutions and believe Putin personally sought to help Trump win; Russia denies involvement. Rep. Elijah Cummings called the report alarming. It came a day after national security adviser Michael Flynn resigned over December calls with Russia's ambassador. Press Secretary Sean Spicer said nothing had changed regarding Trump's denial of campaign contacts with Russians.

H H Martyn & Co, founded by Herbert Henry Martyn in Cheltenham in 1888, closed in 1971. The firm spawned the Gloster Aircraft Company and the Dowty empire, and excelled in diverse craftsmanship including statues, ironwork, stained glass, ship fitting, and aircraft. Moving to a site at Sunningend, it became the area's largest employer by 1910 with over 1,000 staff. Notable commissions included the Marble Arch iron gates, Selfridges' frontage, the House of Commons Speaker's Chair and Dispatch Boxes, and the Cenotaph. It fitted out over 100 ocean liners, including the Titanic and Queen Mary, and made military aeroplanes during the First World War. Bought by Maples of London in the mid-1930s, the firm declined after 1945 due to recession and the demise of British shipbuilding, leading to its closure.

The passage describes a market research report on the Global Meat Starter Culture Market, which analyzes past and current trends to forecast future market values. It covers historical, current, and projected revenues by sector, segment, end-user, and region, and includes key manufacturers such as Chr. Hansen, Danisco, Kerry, SOYUZSNAB, and others. The report examines market drivers, constraints, risks, opportunities, PEST and Porter's Five Forces analyses, and macroeconomic and microeconomic factors. Product segmentation includes Maturation Starters and Surface Starters, while applications cover Meat, Poultry, Seafood, and Others. Geographically, it covers the United States, China, Europe, Japan, Southeast Asia, India, and Rest of World from 2018 to 2025. The report also presents SWOT analysis, investment feasibility, and investment return analysis, with a forecast period of 2018-2023. It is published by Index Markets Research.

In 1826, Capt. Thomas ap Catesby Jones visited Honolulu aboard the U.S.S. Peacock to address deserters and American claims, negotiating a treaty of friendship, commerce, and navigation with the King on December 23, 1826—the first Hawaiian treaty with a foreign power, though never ratified by the United States. In 1829, Capt. Finch delivered presents and a presidential letter of goodwill. U.S. naval vessels continued friendly visits; Commodore Downs interceded for Catholic converts persecuted after the 1831 deportation of priests. In 1839, French commander Laplace secured a treaty protecting Catholics under threat of hostilities. British consul Charlton's complaints led to Lord George Paulet seizing the islands in February 1843 and forcing Kamehameha III's cession. After Commodore Kearney protested, Rear-Admiral Thomas restored the Hawaiian flag on July 31, 1843, disavowing Paulet's seizure.

CarsDirect has identified December deals on fuel-efficient vehicles, with leases as low as $159/month and discounts up to $18,100. Kia offers the Optima Hybrid a $5,000 discount in Western states ($4,000 elsewhere) or 0-percent APR financing for 60 months, though $3,000 in bonus cash is forfeited with financing. The Optima Plug-In leases for $249/month with $12,249 in discounts, plus a $4,919 federal tax credit and California incentives. The Hyundai Sonata Plug-In Hybrid leases for $289/month in California. Chevrolet's 2017 Volt leases for $273/month and qualifies for a $7,500 federal tax credit. The Kia Soul EV offers $18,100 off or a $159/month lease, the cheapest electric-car lease available. The Chevrolet Bolt EV leases for $303/month in select states. The Chevrolet Equinox Diesel gets $4,000 off nationwide, and the Toyota Yaris iA is $2,000 off in Southern California.

This paper proposes a community detection framework for network data based on recursive bipartitioning, consisting of two components: a bipartitioning algorithm and a stopping rule. Unlike most existing methods that require predetermining the number of communities K, the proposed framework uses the Bayes factor as the stopping rule—dividing the network when the data favor a model with community structure over one without—thus avoiding pre-specification of K and revealing hierarchical structure. The framework can, in principle, accommodate any model-based community detection method with a likelihood, and is demonstrated on three model classes: stochastic block models, edge exchangeable models, and latent space models. The authors establish consistency results for recursive bipartitioning under the stochastic block model using the Erdős-Renyi modularity criterion, proving strong consistency when the expected degree of a sub-network grows faster than the log of its size and weak consistency when it grows to infinity. Inference is carried out through Gibbs sampling algorithms derived for each model class. The method is motivated by applications such as stroke patient transfer networks, where detected communities can reveal regional hospital connection patterns and inform investigations of health care access disparities.

On September 9, 2020, Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that its Board of Directors elected General (Ret.) Keith B. Alexander as a director and appointed him to the Audit Committee. Gen. Alexander is Co-CEO, President, and Chairman of IronNet Cybersecurity, Inc., which he founded in 2014. He previously served as Commander of U.S. Cyber Command from May 2010 to March 2014, as Director of the National Security Agency and Chief of the Central Security Service from August 2005 to March 2014, and as a director of CSRA, Inc. from November 2015 to April 2018. In connection with his election, he was granted a restricted stock unit award for 288 shares of common stock under the Company's 1997 Stock Incentive Plan, vesting in three equal annual installments beginning November 15, 2021, assuming continued service as a director. He also entered into an indemnification agreement in the same form as the Company's other directors. The report was signed by Senior Vice President David A. Zapolsky.

A new study suggests the exoplanet WASP-121b, a "hot Jupiter" about 880 light-years from Earth, has a stratosphere, a warm upper atmospheric layer also common in solar system atmospheres. Led by Thomas Evans of the University of Exeter, researchers detected spectral signatures of glowing water molecules using an infrared spectrograph aboard NASA's Hubble Space Telescope during the planet's transits. The signatures indicate temperatures increase with altitude in the upper atmosphere, reaching about 4,500 degrees Fahrenheit (2,500 degrees Celsius), while decreasing in the lower troposphere. Researchers say this is the strongest evidence to date for an exoplanet stratosphere and a technical milestone toward eventually analyzing Earth-like exoplanet atmospheres. The study was published online Aug. 2 in the journal Nature.

Progress Software Corporation held its Q3 2025 earnings conference call on September 29, 2025. The call featured President and CEO Yogesh Gupta, CFO Anthony Folger, and Senior Vice President of Investor Relations Michael Micciche. Micciche delivered a safe harbor statement noting that forward-looking information regarding financial performance, corporate strategies, product plans, cost initiatives, and ShareFile integration is subject to risks and uncertainties. All financial figures referenced on the call are non-GAAP measures unless otherwise indicated.

The NHS Constitution, also called the Patient Charter, sets out patients' legal rights, NHS pledges beyond legal requirements, and patient responsibilities. Rights include free care at the point of use (with exceptions such as prescriptions in England, dentistry and eye care), equal access regardless of personal characteristics, waiting time standards with alternatives if unmet, treatment by qualified staff in safe settings, access to NICE-recommended treatments, consent and privacy rights, choice of GP practice, the duty of candour when things go wrong, and routes for complaints, escalation to the Ombudsman, judicial review, and compensation for negligence. Responsibilities include looking after one's own health, treating staff and patients respectfully, following treatment plans, and participating in vaccination and screening programmes. The Charter is presented as a partnership balancing what patients can expect with what they can give back, particularly amid waiting lists, staff shortages and financial pressures.

Winthrop University will receive $1.1 million as part of a $20 million National Science Foundation award for Research Infrastructure and Improvement distributed to 10 South Carolina institutions over five years. The highly competitive grant, announced Sept. 19, will fund 36 summer student research experiences, faculty resources, and $330 thousand in capital equipment. The initiative, MADE in SC, is managed by the state's EPSCoR program, and Winthrop was selected based on the quality of its proposed research. Investigators include project director Maria Gelabert, Drs. Fatima Amir, Clifton Harris, Jason Hurlbert, and Robin Lammi, with Pat Owens serving as budget and reporting director. Research areas include electronic, optical, and biomaterials, with applications such as lasers, water treatment, and regenerative medicine. Winthrop will also hold two-week summer teacher workshops for regional high schools.

The Average True Range (ATR) is a volatility indicator developed by J. Welles Wilder Jr., typically used for placing stop-loss orders, position sizing, and identifying potential breakouts rather than generating trading signals. The article explains how to calculate ATR in Python using the pandas_ta library and backtests a 14-day ATR strategy on SPY, holding the asset when volatility is high and selling when it is low. The strategy performs better when adjusted for risk but has a drawdown similar to buy and hold; while the results are not promising, combining ATR with other indicators might yield better results.

A new University of Bristol study reveals that the chloroplast lineage split from its closest cyanobacterial ancestor over 2.1 billion years ago in low salinity environments. The symbiotic relationship between chloroplast and eukaryotic host developed 200 million years later. Marine algae diversified around 800-750 million years ago. The findings suggest complex organisms like algae first evolved in freshwater before colonising marine environments, with implications for understanding the carbon cycle and early life on Earth.

Coach Sutter attributed his team's fatigue to an emotional seven-game series against Chicago with three overtime periods, followed by late-night travel and an altered schedule. He noted lineup changes since November and that five or six players were in their first Stanley Cup Final. He said teams cannot always chase leads and both remaining teams had to be resilient. He praised Kyle's energy, said Mike Richards accepts his role and is motivated only by winning, and described Jonathan as focused despite fatigue. He said a young player has taken on a larger role and will improve with age. He also described Manhattan Beach's small-town atmosphere, called Madison Square Garden a special venue, noted the defense has changed since last year, and said he adjusted line combinations after noticing early that many players lacked their usual game.

The Daily Stormer, a neo-Nazi website founded in 2013 by Andrew Anglin, was dropped by domain registrar GoDaddy after it published an article mocking Heather Heyer, who was killed when a car drove into counterprotesters at the Charlottesville rally. GoDaddy, which had previously resisted calls to cut ties with the site, said the article could incite violence in violation of its terms of service. The site briefly moved to Google, which then announced it was also canceling the registration for violating its terms; the site remained active at the time of publication. Neither company provided web hosting, which is obscured by Cloudflare, previously reported to have shared complainants' information with Anglin, enabling harassment campaigns. Anonymous claimed to have hacked the site, though Anglin said he regained control. Anglin also faces a Southern Poverty Law Center lawsuit over a harassment campaign against a Jewish real estate agent's family; his whereabouts are unknown, and a successful suit could lead to seizure of his assets and the site's shutdown.

A retrospective cohort study at Mulago National Referral Hospital in Uganda reviewed charts of 267 children admitted with clinical measles during 2018 to estimate treatment costs and describe outcomes. The median patient age was 1 year and the median hospital stay was 4 days. Mortality was 11.3% (30 deaths), and 69.3% of patients developed complications, most commonly severe pneumonia (39.5%) and gastroenteritis (24.0%). The average direct health care cost per patient was 33.13 USD, with overhead costs of 81.37 USD, yielding a total estimated cost of approximately 114.50 USD per case. Higher costs were associated with male gender, comorbidities, hospital stays exceeding 15 days, and death during admission. The study concluded that mortality and complications were high, and treatment costs far exceeded the estimated 0.86 USD cost of immunizing a child, supporting efforts to promote measles vaccination to reduce healthcare expenditures.

A six-hour spacewalk is scheduled for August 17, during which two Russian members of the Expedition 52 crew—Commander Fyodor Yurchikhin and Flight Engineer Sergey Ryazanskiy—will exit the ISS's Pirs airlock at approximately 10:45am EDT. Tasks include deploying five nanosatellites (one with a 3D-printed casing, one commemorating Sputnik 1's 60th anniversary and Tsiolkovsky's 160th birthday), scraping residue samples from the station's exterior, and attaching handrails and struts. This is the only spacewalk planned during Expedition 52, viewable on NASA Live.

This patent application, a continuation of PCT/CN2019/128475 claiming priority to a Chinese application, relates to big data technologies, specifically a recommendation model training method and apparatus. It addresses problems in recommendation systems (e.g., HUAWEI APPGALLERY, which generates tens of billions of data records daily) where training on massive data causes overfitting, high resource consumption, slow training, and data imbalance between positive and negative samples.

The disclosed method adds positive samples from a sample set to a training set, calculates sampling probabilities for negative samples using a preset algorithm, selects negative samples based on these probabilities, and trains a recommendation model. The algorithm applies up to three rules: sampling probability is negatively correlated with the score difference between a positive sample's and a negative sample's estimated scores; negatively correlated with the vector distance between their eigenvectors; and positively correlated with the variation of a ranking indicator produced by exchanging the two samples' rankings. Negative samples with greater impact on training thus receive higher sampling probabilities. Correcting probabilities by dividing by the maximum value speeds sampling without altering the probability distribution.

The trained model can generate estimated scores for subsequent training rounds, enabling iterative convergence. A related recommendation method ranks to-be-recommended objects by estimated score and recommends the top M to a target user. Testing on a HUAWEI APPGALLERY dataset showed improvements over non-sampling, random sampling, DNS, and optimized LR sampling on NDCG@5, NDCG@10, P@5, and P@10 indicators. The application also covers training and recommendation apparatuses, computer-readable storage media, and computer program products.

Anne-Marie D'Amico, an Invesco employee, has been identified as one of the first victims of the Toronto van attack that killed 10 and injured 15 on Yonge Street and Finch Avenue at around 1.30pm ET on Monday. Suspect Alex Minassian, 25, was arrested and is due in court. Police chief Mark Saunders said the attack appeared deliberate; the motive remains unknown.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere architecture and built on TSMC's 7nm process, is designed for AI and HPC workloads. It features 108 SMs, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, and 6912 FP32 CUDA cores. Key features include:

- **Third-generation Tensor Cores** supporting FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and Binary data types, delivering 2.5x mixed-precision performance over V100
- **Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity** using a 2:4 pattern that doubles compute throughput by skipping zero values
- **TF32 operations** accelerating FP32 workloads up to 10x (20x with sparsity) without code changes
- **FP64 Tensor Cores** delivering 19.5 TFLOPS for HPC, 2.5x faster than V100
- **40 GB HBM2 memory** with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth and a 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x larger than V100)
- **Multi-Instance GPU (MIG)** partitioning a single A100 into up to seven GPU Instances with hardware-level isolation and QoS for multi-tenant environments
- **Third-generation NVLink** with twelve links providing 600 GB/sec total bandwidth
- **PCIe Gen 4** with SR-IOV virtualization support
- **Asynchronous copy instructions** and hardware-accelerated barriers for efficient data movement bypassing the register file
- **CUDA Task Graph acceleration** reducing launch overhead and inter-kernel latency
- **L2 cache residency controls** and Compute Data Compression for improved bandwidth efficiency
- **NVJPG hardware decode**, Optical Flow Accelerator, and five NVDEC units for multimedia workloads
- **Improved error detection, isolation, and containment** for reliability in large clusters

The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs delivering 5 PFLOPS of AI performance, interconnected via NVSwitch with Mellanox InfiniBand networking for scalable AI infrastructure.

On February 8, 2022, NVIDIA Corporation, SoftBank Group Capital Limited, and SVF Holdco (UK) Limited mutually terminated the Share Purchase Agreement, dated September 13, 2020, involving Arm Limited, due to significant regulatory challenges preventing the transaction's consummation. Under the agreement's terms, the Sellers will retain the $1.25 billion prepaid by NVIDIA, and NVIDIA will retain its 20-year Arm license. NVIDIA intends to record a $1.36 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal year 2023, inclusive of the $1.25 billion prepayment, due to the termination.

This passage documents the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) specification, which defines communication protocols between SEV-ES/SEV-SNP guests and hypervisors using VMGEXIT instructions and MSR protocol functions.

The MSR protocol supports requests including CPUID register values (one register per invocation; functions requiring non-zero sub-leafs or XCR0 are unsupported), AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration/preference/unregistration, page state changes, Run VMPL, hypervisor feature support queries, and guest termination. GHCB GPA registration is required for SEV-SNP guests before first VMGEXIT use; guests may request a hypervisor-preferred GPA or register their own, and registration automatically replaces any prior registration.

The document provides GHCB negotiation examples for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests, showing how guests obtain the page table encryption bit and protocol versions, establish #VC exception handlers, and allocate the shared GHCB page.

Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) events require guests to copy state to the GHCB, set VALID_BITMAP bits, and invoke VMGEXIT; hypervisors report errors via SW_EXITINFO1/SW_EXITINFO2 with defined reason codes. Supported NAE events include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO access, Page State Change (private/shared/PSMASH/UNSMASH operations with resumable entry-by-entry processing), SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request (returning GUID-identified certificates), AP Creation, #HV doorbell page management, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Request, Secure AVIC backing page registration, and termination requests.

AP booting under SEV-ES/SEV-SNP requires special handling because hypervisors cannot modify measured register values; approaches include reset vector checks, predetermined initial register locations, AP Reset Hold, and AP jump tables for transferring control between environments (e.g., UEFI to OS). vCPU hotplug is unsupported except via the SNP AP Creation feature.

For NMIs, hypervisors must intercept #DB rather than IRET, using guest "NMI Complete" messages before injecting further NMIs. Hardware debug register virtualization is supported where available; otherwise DR7 access is intercepted and cached. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

The #HV doorbell page, used with SNP Restricted Injection, contains PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields for interrupt and non-maskable event notification. The document specifies host behavior for presenting interrupts and handling EOIs, and guest behavior requiring atomic exchanges to acknowledge events, including defined handling for non-cooperative hosts or guests.

The High/Low zone offense combines an outside three-player passing attack with an inside high/low rotation and can be initiated from almost any alignment. Its relatively simple continuity features constant movement by two interior players, creating matchup problems for zones, especially matchup zones. A weakside attack forces zones to defend sideline to sideline, and when the zone collapses, spot-up shooters get open outside shots. Sharp, accurate ball movement is key to its success. The basic continuity involves point-to-wing entry passes, post rolls to the basket, flashes to the middle, and ball reversal. Post roll options include short corner shots, feeds to cutting posts, and skip passes to weakside shooters. Various entries—Dribble Clear, 1-4 Slice, Mid Screen, and Horns—can initiate the continuity, while quick-hitting specials such as Pin Down, Weakside Double, and Vegas provide set plays for late-clock or post-timeout situations.

This paper presents a knowledge graph-based solution for analyzing Instant Messaging App (IMA) data, such as WhatsApp, in criminal investigations. Developed within an Italian national project, the approach combines Neo4j knowledge graphs for organizing chat dumps, Whisper-based speech-to-text transcription of audio messages, a Named Entity Recognition and Linking (NEEL) pipeline (comprising NER, NEL, NIL prediction, and entity clustering), and two interfaces: Neo4j graph exploration and DAVE, a faceted search application supporting annotation editing. The solution was tested on two real investigations (fraud and corruption), processing over 2,500 chats. Whisper achieved the best transcription performance on Italian audio (BERT score 0.908), while NER results were unsatisfactory, indicating a need for in-domain fine-tuning. Investigators provided positive feedback, particularly on graph visualizations, combined text and relational search, and transcription quality. The solution aims to empower rather than replace human decision-makers, with ethical safeguards including local data storage and avoidance of external APIs.

Aqua Terra (AQTWM, Inc.) has filed a preliminary long form prospectus with Canadian securities commissions, except Québec, for an initial public offering of its common shares, co-led by TD Securities Inc., Canaccord Genuity Corp. and RBC Capital Markets Inc. The share count and price are undetermined and completion is not assured. The prospectus is available on SEDAR and not yet final; the securities are not registered in the United States. Aqua Terra provides oilfield water disposal services in Canada and the U.S.

In this MIT OpenCourseWare lecture, Charlie Tillett, a 1991 Sloan graduate and third-place finisher in the inaugural $10K Contest, explains how to build business plan financials for startups. Tillett, who helped launch NetScout Systems (which went public in 1999) and Reveal Imaging (a bomb detection equipment company), and who raised $125 million in over 10 transactions, presents his Excel template, which is available on the course website.

Tillett argues that financials serve as a company's scoreboard and help founders understand key assumptions, drivers, and cash needs, noting that a CEO's primary job is maintaining cash. He recounts Reveal Imaging's fundraising: a $1 million angel round within 90 days, followed by a $5 million venture round in two milestone-based tranches.

He explains the venture capitalist perspective: investors seek 3x to 5x returns over five to seven years and want significant ownership. Equity given equals investment divided by pre-money valuation plus investment (e.g., $5 million invested on a $5 million pre-money yields 50%). He walks through dilution across angel, Series A (with a 10–20% employee option pool), and Series B rounds, showing founders diluted to 18.2% in his example. Investors receive preferred shares with anti-dilution provisions and board representation.

Tillett describes the business model as an income statement in percentage terms, covering revenue, cost of goods sold (materials, labor, facilities, support—not R&D), sales and marketing, R&D, G&A, and operating profit (EBITDA). When evaluating plans, he examines top-line market size, year-four gross margins, sales and marketing spending (which varies widely by industry), and operating profit as a proxy for cash needed. He presents benchmarks: retail and restaurant companies have low gross margins and low revenue per employee ($45,000–$200,000), while technology, software, and internet firms range from $573,000 to $2 million per employee. He suggests R&D at 10–20% of revenue and G&A at 5–15%.

He advises pricing to capture only a fraction of the value delivered to customers (e.g., charging $2,000–$3,000 for a $10,000 value), building sales projections bottom-up rather than claiming a share of a large market, presenting a single best case rather than multiple scenarios, and avoiding business plan software in favor of building the model personally. Rules of thumb include staffing at 50–66% of expenses, an average employee cost of $90,000 plus 15% benefits, and 2% quarterly salary increases.

For cash flow, he recommends using cumulative operating losses plus capital expenses as a proxy. On equity sharing, he urges that everyone vest over three to four years with quarterly vesting, with typical post-dilution ranges of 5–10% for a CEO, 1–2.5% for VPs, 0.25% for senior managers, and 0.10% for senior individual contributors, with founding team members receiving two to three times more. He notes that angel investors negotiate as toughly as venture capitalists, and recommends hiring an experienced CFO by the first venture round to reduce dilution.

Top drugmakers will meet in early December with Donald Trump Jr. and senior Trump administration officials at a summit hosted by BlinkRx, an online prescription drug delivery company that installed Trump Jr. on its board. Some drug-company representatives worried the gathering signaled the White House wants them to work with BlinkRx because of its ties to the president's family. Meanwhile, the Pfizer agreement with the Trump administration to lower drug prices has prompted other companies to scramble to make deals, though whether these deals will lower prices remains unknown. Separately, a New York panel recommended state Medicaid pause coverage of Sarepta's Duchenne drug.

This lecture from a coding theory course addresses coding for bandwidth-limited additive white Gaussian noise channels, where non-binary, multi-level codes using Euclidean rather than Hamming distance are required. Lattice constellations are introduced, with a union-bound estimate that separates coding gain (from the lattice) and shaping gain (from the region), expressed via SNR norm and independent of rate or constellation size. Shaping is presented as a simple problem: the n-sphere is the optimal region, with a maximum shaping gain of πe/6 ≈ 1.53 dB as dimensions go to infinity; techniques such as shell mapping (used in the V.34 modem) and trellis shaping achieve roughly 0.8–1 dB. Dense lattices are reviewed: hexagonal A₂ (0.6 dB), D₄ (1.5 dB), E₈ (3 dB), the Barnes-Wall lattices (up to 4.5–6 dB nominal gain), and the Leech lattice (6 dB, ~195,560 nearest neighbors), though large numbers of nearest neighbors limit effective coding gain to about 4 dB. Barnes-Wall lattices are constructed via the u, u+v construction, analogous to Reed-Muller codes. Trellis codes, introduced by Ungerboeck, use constellation expansion and set partitioning; a four-state code achieves 3 dB, and eight-way partitions plus Wei's four-dimensional designs reach roughly 4.2–6 dB, adopted in the V.32, V.34, and ADSL standards. Combined coding and shaping gains of 6–7.5 dB still leave a 2–3 dB gap to the Shannon limit. Higher-performance schemes mentioned include turbo codes, sequential decoding, multi-level coding with capacity separability, and the pragmatic Bit-Interleaved Coded Modulation used in practice on wireless channels. The professor concludes that coding for the AWGN channel is now a mature subject, with research activity having moved to multi-user and network settings.

In this MIT lecture, the professor presents the course's fourth and final case study, based on his thesis research on manufacturing microfluidic devices from polymers using hot embossing. Polymers are attractive because they are cheap, transparent, and mechanically tough. The hot embossing process involves heating a thermoplastic above its glass transition temperature, applying a load, holding it, cooling below the glass transition, and removing the load. A related process, thermal nano imprint lithography, patterns sub-micron features in thin polymer layers spun onto silicon wafers, with resolution not limited by light wavelength. The research aims to develop computationally efficient modeling tools for process design. A linear elastic model with one fitted parameter (Young's modulus) predicted embossed topography well, running in about 20 seconds in Matlab, and adding a linear dashpot captured viscoelastic flow during longer hold times. Experiments used PMMA, ZEONOR, and TOPAS with carefully designed test patterns. A fractional factorial study on TOPAS found temperature, force, and hold time significant, while loading rate was not clearly significant; TOPAS also showed significant material anisotropy. De-molding challenges from differential thermal contraction were discussed, with de-molding near 110°C producing flat PMMA features. The lecture concluded with questions about student projects.

The gold/silver ratio measures how many silver ounces equal the value of one ounce of gold, calculated by dividing the gold price by the silver price. Traders use it as a mean-reversion signal—buying silver and shorting gold when the ratio is high, and doing the opposite when it is low—through futures, options, or ETFs. Historically fixed by governments (e.g., 12:1 in Rome, 15:1 in the 1792 U.S. Coinage Act), the ratio has floated since the gold standard's end, averaging 47:1 in the 20th century and ranging roughly 50:1–70:1 in the 21st, peaking at 114.77 in 2020 with a low of 35:1 in 2011. Backtests of ratio-based strategies, including a GLD strategy and a GLD/SLV pair trade, showed erratic or flat performance, and the authors failed to find robust, profitable strategies using the ratio.

Dwayne Dixon, a teaching associate professor at UNC Chapel Hill, was reinstated Friday after a university threat assessment found no basis to conclude he posed a threat or violated policy. Dixon, placed on leave Monday, had faced calls for dismissal from a Turning Point USA spokesperson over his affiliations.

Hetzner, South Africa's largest specialist hosting company with over 330,000 hosted websites, now peers directly at NAP Africa in Isando via a 10Gbps circuit, in addition to existing links at NAP Africa Cape Town and JINX. Over 65% of its local traffic is routed via exchange points rather than transit links, with over 4Gbps contributed to these points. Hetzner advocates settlement-free peering to reduce connectivity costs and latency and increase network resilience, and peers with operators including Telkom, MTN, Vodacom, Google, Microsoft, and Cloudflare. Its carrier-neutral Samrand data centre has redundant 10Gbps transit and peering links and access to four international cable systems. NAP Africa is a neutral layer 2 IXP located in Teraco data centres, supporting IPv4/IPv6 and connectivity up to 10 Gigabit Ethernet.

A letter to the Mayor and Council opposes a development permit application for 7592 119A St. and 7551, 7565, 7595 and 7597 120 St., arguing it conflicts with the North Delta Area Plan and the Cougar Creek Integrated Stormwater Management Plan. The Area Plan specifies six storeys, but 35 are proposed, and the project fails on tree preservation, canopy cover, amenities, and rainwater infiltration. The parking garage would occupy the entire lot, preventing infiltration of the site's 7-8 million litres of annual rainfall. The writer argues the project fails the "low environmental impact" requirement for tax exemptions under the Scott Road Revitalization Bylaw and would increase flood and drought vulnerability. She opposes any changes, saying approval would encourage upzoning, speculation, and higher prices, citing Vancouver's 25,000 empty highrise units. She suggests approval only with mitigation including 15% permeable open space, and recommends requiring all multi-family developments to set aside 15% permeable land.

The SFS specification addresses security, attestation, and resiliency for firmware updates. Attestation data should be requested via side-band (SPDM) or in-band (DPE) interfaces; some attestation schemes prevent updates to certain AMD firmware, which AMD will not modify. Update packages must verify proper firmware versions exist before applying updates to avoid inter-firmware dependency issues; if a package cannot fully apply, it should not occur, as forcing a reset is undesirable. Packages are non-persistent across reboots, and customers may apply patches during OS boot, after boot, or during operation.

SFS commands require memory alignment: the TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER must be a 2MB aligned page. A customer-provided SFS Deployment Agent creates the buffer, appends co-signing headers and signatures if used, and sends requests to ASP firmware via the TEE mailbox. The ASP protects the memory region, verifies customer and AMD signatures, loads and executes the patch, updates patch level information, and returns status. Firmware versions can be queried via GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO.

Packages follow the naming format fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg and must match the specific firmware versions running on a system. Updates run in parallel with x86 and DMA traffic with minimal performance impact; SEV/SEV-ES virtual machines must stop and restart for SEV firmware updates, while SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue operating.

This paper presents EqDiff-CT, a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) framework for synthesizing CT images from cone-beam CT (CBCT) in image-guided radiotherapy. CBCT enables convenient volumetric acquisition for daily image guidance but suffers from scatter, artifacts, and inconsistent Hounsfield Unit values, while conventional CT offers better soft-tissue contrast and HU calibration but cannot reflect day-to-day anatomical changes during treatment. Synthetic CT generation from CBCT addresses these limitations by producing HU-consistent, artifact-reduced volumes for improved dose calculation, segmentation, and adaptive radiotherapy.

Existing approaches include deformable image registration and analytical intensity correction (fast but dependent on prior CT anatomy), GAN-based methods such as CycleGAN (prone to training instability and hallucinated structures), CNN-based models, and hybrid architectures. Diffusion models offer improved training stability and sample diversity, though computational cost and generalization remain challenges.

The proposed method employs a time-conditioned, group-equivariant U-Net denoiser (via e2cnn) with discrete rotational equivariance (cyclic C4 symmetry) and self-attention blocks for long-range spatial dependencies. Training uses a non-adversarial objective combining MSE and SSIM on predicted noise, with the CBCT image concatenated at each time-step; inference uses variance-corrected reverse diffusion. Evaluated on the SynthRAD2025 Head & Neck dataset with an 80/20 patient-wise split, the model outperformed a baseline diffusion model without attention and a CycleGAN baseline across SSIM, PSNR, MSE, and MAE, while preserving clinically relevant structures including the mandible, airway, and cervical spine. The paper further details the DDPM formulation, including the forward diffusion process, time-conditional denoising objective, and reverse sampling.

Apple Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2018 reports third-quarter net sales of $53.3 billion, up 17% from $45.4 billion a year earlier, and net income of $11.5 billion versus $8.7 billion. Nine-month net sales were $202.7 billion (up 15%) with net income of $45.4 billion. Growth was driven primarily by higher iPhone, Services, and Other Products sales, aided by favorable foreign currency effects, with net sales increasing in all geographic segments (Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan, and Rest of Asia Pacific). iPhone net sales rose 20% due to higher average selling prices, while iPad and Mac each declined 5%; Services grew 31%, including a $236 million one-time item. Gross margin percentage was 38.3% versus 38.5%. The effective tax rate fell to 13.3% from 22.9%, reflecting reduced provisional estimates under the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, including a deemed repatriation tax payable of $37.0 billion. Regarding the European Commission State Aid Decision ordering Ireland to recover €13 billion plus €1 billion interest, €4.5 billion was funded into escrow as of June 30, 2018, with an additional €4.5 billion funded afterward. The Company repurchased $20.0 billion of stock during the quarter, completed its $210 billion program, and announced a new $100 billion repurchase program; dividends of $3.7 billion were paid. Term debt totaled $104.1 billion and commercial paper was $12.0 billion. Legal matters include VirnetX patent verdicts of $440 million and $503 million and a lawsuit against Qualcomm. Total assets were $349.2 billion as of June 30, 2018.

A CDC report shows illnesses from mosquito, tick, and flea bites have tripled in the U.S. since 2004. Venice is at risk due to still waters in the Venice Canals and Ballona Wetlands, which can breed mosquitoes. West Nile Virus is present in the area, incubating in birds and spread to humans by mosquitoes; 80 percent of those infected show no symptoms, while fewer than one percent develop neuroinvasive disease. The Los Angeles County West Vector Control District manages standing water in Venice and reports record WNV cases in recent years, with 2015 peaking at 300. Residents are advised to use repellent containing 5–30 percent DEET or alternatives, and to eliminate standing water in their yards.

A hockey coach discusses his team's playoff series against Dallas, now tied 1-1. He acknowledges his team made mistakes but believes Dallas can also play better, noting Dallas's strong record after first-game losses, so his team is prepared. Rather than dwelling on the past, the focus is on preparation, including studying how Dallas was slow in its first game against Colorado before becoming more aggressive and physical. To contain Dallas's stars—Modano, Hull, and Nieuwendyk—both defense and forwards must take away their time and space. Winning game two is important because a 2-0 lead puts pressure on the opponent at home. He was surprised his team scored against Dallas's strong defense and treats each game as its own series. A player has regained his early-season form, with improved defensive responsibility. The team is healthy except for Madden, whose injury was less serious than feared. He notes rivalries are built through playoff competition. Brian has played well but tried to do too much, causing turnovers. Dallas forechecked aggressively, and his team's puck decisions were poor—their worst game in four or five—yet they stayed close, which is encouraging. A Dallas goal followed a missed offside, but he says that wasn't why they lost. With no panic, the team must return to its successful game plan in Dallas.

A model was developed to understand potential sources of influenza A H5 RNA in wastewater and interpret H5 RNA detections. The highly pathogenic avian influenza A (H5N1) outbreak in US birds began in February 2022, and cattle outbreaks were identified in March 2024; between March 1 and December 19, 2024, 865 infected dairy cow herds and 61 human cases were reported in 16 states, with no human-to-human transmission reported. Beginning March 2024, H5 RNA was detected in wastewater at multiple US sites. The most likely sources of H5 in wastewater were concluded to be cow's milk (as wasted milk and dairy processing waste enter sewers), poultry feces, wildfowl feces (via combined sewers), and human contributions. The study retrospectively tested wastewater solids from a publicly owned treatment work in California serving 750,000 people, with combined stormwater and sanitary sewer systems, for total IAV (M gene), H1, H3, and H5 RNA from September 2023 to May 2024 (n=110 samples) using droplet digital RT-PCR. A mass balance model was developed to estimate theoretical H5 RNA inputs from humans, cow milk, poultry feces, and wildfowl feces required to produce measured concentrations, using the Freundlich isotherm to estimate liquid-phase concentrations. Objectives were to identify the timing of the first H5 detection in the sewershed and to contextualize findings through the source model.

The SteelSeries Arctis GameBuds, rated 9/10 by WIRED, are currently discounted at Amazon to $128. The reviewer, who has used them for months for gaming and everyday activities, highlights their portability, compatibility with Xbox or PlayStation (depending on version) as well as Switch, PC, and smartphones, a compact USB-C dongle providing low-latency 2.4GHz audio and Bluetooth, roughly 10 hours of battery life (40 with the charging case), a mobile app with game-specific equalizer settings, and a comfortable fit with physical buttons for controls.
Weston will see about 70% coverage of the Aug. 21 solar eclipse, the continental U.S.'s first in nearly 40 years; the Weston Public Library will host related events.

James Harden scored 60 points with 10 rebounds and 11 assists, becoming the first NBA player to record a 60-point triple-double, as the short-handed Houston Rockets beat the Orlando Magic 114-107. He broke Calvin Murphy's Houston single-game scoring record of 57 points set in 1978. Harden made 17 of 18 free throws and 19 of 30 shots. The Rockets played without Chris Paul and Trevor Ariza, and lost Eric Gordon to back stiffness. Hezonja and Speights each scored 17 for Orlando.

This study reports melt-quenched metal inorganic-organic complex (MIOC) glasses synthesized by introducing chloride into two ZIFs, yielding ZnCl2HIm2 (MIOC-4) and ZnCl2HbIm2 (MIOC-7) via slow evaporation. Both supramolecular structures are stabilized by hydrogen bonding, with MIOC-7 additionally featuring π-π interactions. Melting points (440 K and 508 K) and glass-transition temperatures (282 K and 359 K) were determined by DSC. In situ XRD showed that melting begins with slippage and distortion of strong hydrogen-bonded structures, followed by rapid disordering when hydrogen bonds break, while coordination bonds and ligands remain intact; the freed volume from hydrogen-bond sacrifice enables glass formation. A binary mixed-ligand system formed physical mixtures of MIOC-4 and MIOC-7, exhibiting reduced melting points (lowest 415 K for ZnCl2HbIm0.498HIm1.502) and a linearly increasing Tg (282–360 K) with benzimidazole content due to enhanced steric hindrance. FT-IR, Raman, solid-state NMR, and synchrotron XRD revealed that vitrification weakens C-H···Cl bonds, strengthens N-H···Cl bonds, preserves short-range Zn-N, Zn-Cl, and C-C(N) correlations, disrupts π-π stacking and long-range order, and freezes multiple tetrahedral conformations into a short-range disordered network. The ligand-tuning strategy was extended to metal nodes (Co, Cu) and anions (SCN-), confirming that hydrogen-bond strength and network topology, rather than metal identity, govern thermal behavior. MIOC-7 glass displayed enhanced, excitation-dependent photoluminescence with a red shift attributed to the red-edge effect and frozen conformers, with an internal PLQY of 3.4% versus 1.2% for the crystal, suggesting potential anti-counterfeiting applications.

This patent application describes a networked exercise system, primarily a treadmill, configured to provide streaming and on-demand exercise classes to users. The application notes that existing exercise equipment lacks competitive, gamified, and social features, while gym classes are limited by time, location, cost, and capacity. The disclosed system enables users to participate in live or recorded instructor-led classes from any location with network access, with full interactivity between instructors and users through video, audio, and data channels.

The treadmill includes a deck with a continuous track and slats, posts supporting arms, and separate rotary controls on each arm that control different functions (e.g., incline via one motor and belt speed via another motor). The rotary controls may be infinity wheel-type or substantially linear capacitive controls, featuring detents calibrated for incremental changes (e.g., 0.5% incline or 0.1 mph speed per detent) and providing visual, tactile, and audible feedback, including LED illumination proportional to rotation. Sensors measure performance metrics such as speed, incline, heart rate, and calorie burn. The machine also includes an adjustable display mount, an emergency stop mechanism using a magnetic connector and clip, and trays for personal items.

User interfaces allow browsing featured classes, class libraries, live schedules, and "just run" content, while displaying performance metrics, leaderboards, scorecards, and segmented timelines corresponding to class portions.

The Socket 940 cover accommodates the 940-pin ceramic µPGA package, providing mechanical support with a seating plane flatness better than 0.25 mm. The socket base and cover are made from Liquid Crystal Polymer (UL 94 V-0), with a black base and natural or ivory cover. The cover must not exceed 1.17 mm in thickness and carries markings including "SOCKET 940," directional designators, a triangular orientation symbol, the supplier's UL symbol, and a lot traceability number. Contacts use high-strength copper alloy plated with a minimum of 1.27 µm nickel and 0.76 µm gold at mating areas. Solder balls are tin/lead (63/37 ± 5%), 0.76 mm in diameter, with a 0.20 mm co-planarity requirement. A stainless steel actuation lever enables toolless operation; insertion/extraction forces must not exceed 2 kgf with the lever open, and lever actuation force must be less than 3.6 kgf. The socket must maintain integrity after 50 actuation cycles. Electrically, contacts are rated at 1.5 A with less than 30°C temperature rise; LLCR must not exceed 25 mΩ; partial self-inductance must be under 4 nH; capacitance under 1 pF; differential impedance 100 Ω ± 10%; dielectric withstanding voltage minimum 650 Vac; and insulation resistance minimum 1000 MΩ.

The passage outlines how to teach and implement a basketball early offense and press break. Success depends on precise execution, spacing, timing, and footwork, with coaching done before games rather than during. Using the "Whole-Part-Whole" method, coaches demonstrate roles and responsibilities, walk through options, apply progressive breakdown drills (one-on-one through five-player breaks), and then practice live against motivated defense. Coaching objectives include developing poise against presses, quick controlled passing, attacking outnumbered situations and double teams, and flowing into early offense. The passage lists proven drills and game strategies, emphasizing scouting opponents and disruptive defense, which can also disrupt an opponent's early offense.

A Kentucky high school valedictorian used a bullhorn to deliver his graduation speech outside Holy Cross High School's ceremony after the Diocese of Covington barred him from speaking, citing late submission and content that was "political and inconsistent with the teaching of the Catholic Church." Student council president Katherine Frantz also spoke by bullhorn. Christian Bales, who is gay, praised student gun-reform activism at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School and urged young people to speak out. The speech drew widespread media attention, which Bales' mother said amplified his voice.

The Trump administration's push to hire hundreds of new federal prosecutors is off to a slow start. LinkedIn data shows about 42 people joined the Justice Department as assistant US attorneys from January through August, down more than half from the same period in each of the four preceding years. The slowdown stems from budget and political pressures, including hiring freezes, rising pay costs, sagging morale, and potential recruits' concerns about ethically murky casework. Despite the administration's call to hire over 400 additional attorneys, some offices report staffing shortages—one former prosecutor said his office is down to about 22 attorneys from a full staff of 37. Some offices, including Philadelphia's and southern Florida's, are now making hiring pushes. The DOJ does not appear to have lowered standards, as more than a third of new hires attended Top 14 law schools. The department has faced controversies during Trump's second term, including dropped charges against allies and firings of prosecutors. Some former prosecutors still encourage young lawyers to pursue government jobs, while others warn of potential White House meddling.

The speaker describes a goalie who handled his first adversity well, staying calm and mentally strong even after allowing bad goals. He compares Bergeron and Ryan O'Reilly, both excellent faceoff players who work hard, calling it a great matchup. He sees similarities between the teams: both are strong defensively, physical, hard to play against, and emphasize forechecking; his defensemen are bigger, though the opponent has Chara and mobile defensemen. He stresses discipline after the whistle while remaining physical. The team's identity is that the team comes first, and he agrees two goalies are needed given the schedule and travel.

The passage describes the NVIDIA GA10x Ampere architecture GPUs. The GA10x SM enhances async compute by processing RT Core work concurrently with graphics or compute workloads and can run two compute workloads simultaneously. The second-generation RT Core doubles ray/triangle intersection testing rates over Turing and adds an Interpolate Triangle Position unit that accelerates ray-traced motion blur up to eight times faster than Turing. Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32 and BF16 data types and a Sparsity feature that doubles matrix multiplication throughput; the RTX 3080 delivers 238 peak FP16 Tensor TFLOPS with sparsity enabled. DLSS is enhanced with a 9x scaling factor, making 8K 60 fps gaming feasible. GA10x is the first GPU to use GDDR6X memory, which employs PAM4 signaling to reach data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec bandwidth, over 52% higher than TU102. NVIDIA RTX IO, working with Microsoft's DirectStorage API, offloads decompression from the CPU to the GPU, improving I/O performance up to 100x versus hard drives. The A40 data center GPU delivers up to 2x FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to 5x AI training throughput versus the Quadro RTX 6000, with 48GB memory expandable to 96GB via NVLink. GA10x supports DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 (8K60, 4K120), fifth-generation NVDEC including the first AV1 hardware decode, and seventh-generation NVENC. The RTX 3090 (GA102, 24GB) is 1.5x faster than TITAN RTX; the RTX 3070 (GA104) outperforms the RTX 2080 Ti. New Error Detection and Replay (EDR) technology detects and retries GDDR6X memory errors to aid safe overclocking.

The ADX (Average Directional Movement Index) indicator was developed by Welles Wilder and published in his 1978 book, New Concepts In Technical Trading Systems, alongside the RSI, ATR, and parabolic SAR. The ADX measures trend strength rather than direction and consists of three components: the ADX line, DI+, and DI-. It is a lagging indicator ranging from 0 to 100, with high readings indicating trending markets and low readings indicating non-trending markets; Wilder considered readings under 15 non-trending and above 20 trending. Backtests show the ADX is somewhat useful on its own but adds greater value when combined with other indicators. A DI+/DI- crossover strategy on the S&P 500 produced a 5.4% CAGR, while an ADX breakout strategy yielded a 3.03% CAGR versus 9.9% for buy and hold; both performed best on the S&P 500. When used as a filter with another indicator, the ADX improved results, raising the profit factor and reducing time in the market. Overall, the ADX performs reasonably well alone but much better alongside other indicators, and can also serve as a mean-reverting tool rather than only a trend tool.

A study by researchers at Stanford, Harvard and the Census Bureau found that in 99 percent of U.S. neighborhoods, black boys earn less in adulthood than white boys from similar socioeconomic backgrounds, challenging the belief that class is the primary predictor of economic outcomes. Using data from 20 million children and parents, the study found black and Native American children have the lowest rates of upward mobility, while whites and Asians have the highest. Even among the wealthiest families, black children earned 12.4 percent less than comparable white children. The gap is largely gendered: black women earn slightly more than white women when parental income is controlled for, while white men out-earn black men. Neighborhoods still matter, but the black-white gap is larger in affluent areas. A few neighborhoods, like Silver Spring, Md., showed parity, associated with low racial bias and a higher presence of black fathers. Co-author Nathaniel Hendren suggested historical factors may explain the persistent disparities.

On October 7, 2016, NVIDIA Corporation entered into a Credit Agreement with Wells Fargo Bank, National Association (as Administrative Agent), Goldman Sachs Bank USA, Morgan Stanley MUFG Loan Partners, LLC, and other lenders. The agreement permits the Company to borrow, repay, and re-borrow up to $575 million for working capital and general corporate purposes over a five-year period ending October 7, 2021, with the option to obtain up to $425 million in additional revolving loan commitments and/or letters of credit. Loans bear interest at the Adjusted LIBO Rate or Alternate Base Rate plus the Applicable Rate. The obligations are unsecured senior obligations ranking equally with the Company's other unsecured, unsubordinated indebtedness. The report was signed by Executive Vice President and CFO Colette M. Kress on October 13, 2016.

Future Electronics and NXP are hosting a free seminar on the i.MX RT Series Crossover Processor in San Sebastian, Spain on July 4, 2018. The workshop will introduce the industry's first crossover processor, featuring the highest performance Arm Cortex-M core, real-time functionality, and MCU usability at an affordable price, along with hands-on exercises. The i.MX RT 105x processors use the Cortex M7 core and, lacking flash memory, offer implementation flexibility at low cost.

A hockey player describes an overtime play in which he supported a teammate whose shot decided the game. He credits the team's power play and penalty kill preparation, noting momentum gained during a delay penalty. He stresses staying out of the box to limit the opponent's elite power play, which features many threats and must be defended with quickness and attention to detail. He expresses confidence that the roster's depth can cover for lost key players, and is excited to return home to a supportive hockey town.

The speaker addresses Berliners, celebrating the city's unity after the fall of the Berlin Wall and honoring the courage shown during decades of division, from the 1953 uprising to the Leipzig demonstrations. He pledges a new American Embassy in Berlin and calls for a new "civil courage to build" a Europe of independent democracies, free markets, and security based on bridges rather than walls. He urges rejection of divisions based on race, ethnicity, or religion, appealing especially to young people to believe in peace and their own future. Citing progress such as NATO's Partnership for Peace, he affirms America's lasting support. Having walked with Chancellor Kohl through the Brandenburg Gate, he declares it a gateway to a united Europe and proclaims Berlin free.

On January 18, 2017, NVIDIA Corporation's Board of Directors appointed Tim Teter, age 50, as senior vice president, general counsel and secretary, with employment expected to begin January 23, 2017. Teter previously served as a partner at Cooley LLP, focusing on patent and technology litigation, and holds a B.S. in Mechanical Engineering from UC Davis and a J.D. from Stanford Law School. He assumes leadership of the legal department from David M. Shannon, who announced his retirement intention in June 2016 and will continue leading human resources. Teter's offer letter provides an $850,000 annual base salary, a $250,000 annual incentive target beginning fiscal 2018, a $450,000 anniversary bonus, and RSUs with a target value of $5,800,000 vesting over approximately four years.

President Trump announced an agreement with Pfizer to voluntarily lower U.S. drug prices, aligning them with cheaper prices paid abroad. Pfizer will sell existing drugs to Medicaid patients at the lowest prices offered in other developed nations through a website called TrumpRx.gov and will guarantee "most-favored-nation" pricing on new drugs for Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial payers. In exchange, Pfizer received a three-year exemption from pharmaceutical-specific tariffs, contingent on further U.S. investment; the company plans to invest $70 billion in domestic manufacturing and research. Pfizer shares rose more than 4% after the announcement. The company will offer discounts averaging 50% and up to 85% on many drugs, affecting more than 100 million patients. Trump said he is negotiating similar deals with other drugmakers, including Eli Lilly, and threatened tariffs on those that do not comply.

The author reviews their dividend growth retirement portfolio's 2016 performance on Seeking Alpha. The portfolio, composed of Roth IRAs, 403(b)s, and share builder accounts, gained 15% for the year (excluding new contributions), outperforming the S&P 500's 11.66% dividend-inclusive return every month. The author's long-term goal is a 6-8% annual return, with dividends intended to fund retirement in 20-25 years.

The portfolio began 2016 with 27 positions and ended with 35 after adding Visa, Cisco, Pepsi, Cummins, Honeywell, Qualcomm, Disney, and V.F. Corp. The only sale was Baxalta, traded for Visa in January. Top performers included Chevron (+31%), JPMorgan (+30.68%), AT&T (+23.60%), 3M (+18.54%), and Aflac (+16%). The worst performers were Gilead Sciences (-29%), CVS Health (-19%), Starbucks (-7.5%), Coca-Cola (-3.5%), and Target (-0.52%). The author plans to continue buying dividend-paying stocks below fair value.

This passage examines the growth of virtual education in Indiana public school districts during the COVID-19 pandemic, drawing on surveys of public school superintendents (33.1% response rate) and virtual program administrators (47% response rate), along with follow-up interviews.

The literature review identifies benefits of virtual education, including schedule flexibility, individualized learning, credit recovery, accommodations for students with special needs or physical limitations, increased parental engagement, and preparation for post-secondary-style learning. Challenges include internet access difficulties, the need for independent motivation, delayed teacher feedback, isolation, difficulty providing accommodations, and maintaining student motivation.

Survey findings showed COVID-19 concerns were the most important factor for superintendents implementing programs (79.2% rated it "very important") and for directors maintaining them (84.8% agreed or strongly agreed), followed by credit recovery. The most frequently cited benefits were maintaining enrollment during the pandemic (90.1% of superintendents, 88.6% of administrators), credit recovery, and learner convenience and flexibility. The top challenges were student engagement (80.5% of superintendents, 97.1% of administrators), ensuring quality of curriculum and instruction, and staffing virtual classes.

Interviews revealed three themes regarding the pandemic's impact: on school corporations (enrollment and revenue concerns, accelerated technology plans), on teachers (stress from limited professional development, but growth in technology skills), and on students (social-emotional struggles, the importance of parental support, and difficulties with engagement, self-discipline, and time management).

The study concludes that the pandemic spurred virtual education growth in Indiana, though the identified benefits and challenges mirror those historically present in virtual programs. Implications include helping districts design programs that address student and teacher needs, while future research should examine post-pandemic program changes and the characteristics of successful virtual students and educators.

This paper studies the existence of satisficing paths in pure strategy games from a topological perspective, addressing whether decentralized strategy updates in multi-agent reinforcement learning can converge to an equilibrium. Under the "win-stay, lose-shift" principle, agents maintain strategies that are best responses and otherwise switch; resulting paths are called satisficing paths. The paper introduces the grouped satisficing path, a generalization in which the decision unit is a group of players rather than an individual, and analyzes the local minimum property of the ε-best response group count. The main result (Theorem 2) establishes sufficient conditions: if strategy sets are convex and compact, payoff functions are continuous and partially analytic, and any sub-game has an equilibrium, then for any initial joint strategy there exists a finite-length grouped satisficing path ending at an equilibrium. Theorem 1 provides a reduction principle allowing the original game to be reduced to a sub-game. Corollaries extend the result to continuous games with quasi-convex payoffs, N-player games with finite strategy sets, and stationary and k-step finite-state Markov games, guaranteeing satisficing paths from any initial joint mixed strategy to a mixed equilibrium. The results are consistent with prior impossibility findings since no restrictions are imposed on update functions, and they provide theoretical support for stochastic update approaches. Open problems include identifying necessary conditions, extending to ε > 0, and imposing restrictions on non-best-responding players.

E-minis are electronically traded futures contracts worth a fraction of standard futures contracts, first launched by the Chicago Mercantile Exchange in 1997 for the S&P 500 index. They trade primarily on CME's Globex platform and cover indexes, commodities, and currencies. The S&P 500 e-mini contract is valued at $50 times the index, with a minimum maintenance margin of $10,000, though $13,000–$15,000 is recommended to cover potential losses. The article presents a backtested Rubber Band strategy on the @ES contract (in-sample 2000–2021, out-of-sample 2022), producing 163 trades with a 0.89% average gain, 79% win ratio, and profit factor of 2; in 2022, 13 trades averaged 0.18% while the S&P 500 lost 15%. The authors discourage scalping as overly competitive, stress the need for a backtested trading plan, and note trading costs of $0.50–$2.50 per contract plus fees.

The lecture covers two topics: protein folding and interlocked chains. For protein folding, the professor discusses the HP model, which represents proteins as chains of hydrophobic (H) and hydrophilic (P) nodes folded on a square lattice, scored by the number of adjacent H-H bonds. Finding the optimal folding is NP-hard in both 3D (shown by MIT professors Berger and Leighton) and 2D (by Berkeley researchers), suggesting nature likely finds local rather than global optima. The best known approximation algorithm achieves 1/3 of optimal, using an upper bound based on the even/odd parity of H nodes on a checkerboard-colored grid. Unique optimal foldings exist for closed chains of even length and open chains of doubly even length. Open problems include protein design in the HP model and whether uniqueness results extend to other lattices.

For interlocked chains, the lecture examines which combinations of open and closed chains can interlock. Two-chains (hairpins) always separate, as do pairs of 3-chains, but a 3-chain can interlock with a 4-chain, and three 3-chains can interlock. Lubiw's problem asks for the minimum number of vertex cuts needed to unlock a 3D chain of n bars; the answer is between roughly (n-1)/4 and (n-3)/2. Interlocking results are applied in PSPACE-completeness proofs for 3D chain reconfiguration, where interlocked chains build rigid infrastructure. Whether any chain can be unfolded from a straight configuration remains open.

WIRED has rounded up its top Amazon Big Deal Days deals under $100, an event exclusive to Prime members running October 7 and 8. All picks were tested in person by the WIRED team. The discounted items span categories including streaming devices, wireless chargers, smart speakers and displays, Wi-Fi routers, security cameras and video doorbells, smart locks and garage controllers, pet feeders and fountains, fitness trackers and headphones, kitchen appliances such as air fryers and blenders, cleaning tools, dehumidifiers, bedding, white noise machines, condoms, electric toothbrushes and groomers, a gaming controller, and toys and board games. Featured deals include the Roku Streaming Stick 4K for $30, Samsung's Wireless Charger Trio for $55, the Eufy Security Indoor Cam S350 for $80, the Instant Pot Vortex Slim air fryer for $80, and the Philips Sonicare ExpertClean 7500 for $100.

This study employs bibliometric analysis to identify the competencies required for future leaders of digital education transformation, drawing on research published since 2019 during the COVID-19 pandemic. Set within Thailand's 20-year "Digital Thailand 4.0" national strategy, the paper argues that education must shift toward Education 4.0, moving from teacher-centered instruction to innovation- and project-based learning. Digital disruption, accelerated by the pandemic, has made five pillars essential: Digital Literacy, Digital Readiness, Digital Culture, Digital Mindset, and Digital Leadership. Educators must develop digital skills, embrace technologies such as hybrid learning and data-driven systems, build digital teams, and adopt leadership practices including rethinking, repositioning, and reinventing to guide institutions into the digital era. The study concludes that this transformation is irreversible and educators must become digital leaders, but that technology cannot replace good teachers, who remain central to fostering positive change for students and society.

This research examines the relationship between Songyang Academy's educational philosophy and general education. Using documentary research, field studies, interviews, and observations, the authors trace the academy's history from its founding as the Buddhist Songyang Temple in 484 AD, its transformation into the Taiyi School in 955 CE, its flourishing during the Song Dynasty under Neo-Confucian scholars such as Cheng Hao, Cheng Yi, and Sima Guang, its decline through the Jin, Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties, and its eventual collapse after the abolition of the imperial examination system.

The academy's philosophy centers on moral education, personality cultivation through the "way of adulthood," non-discriminatory admission, autonomous learning through questioning and debate with students as the main body, and the unity of knowledge and action. Its management structure was simple and hierarchical, led by a head of the academy who combined academic and administrative roles.
