The study concludes that Songyang Academy's educational philosophy aligns closely with modern general education, which also emphasizes all-round development of morality, intelligence, physical fitness, and aesthetics. Reviving the academy education model combined with modern general education concepts can provide new approaches for cultivating well-rounded talents, provided traditional ideas are innovated and adapted to contemporary educational needs.

This passage is from Texas Instruments datasheet SLASFA2A (November 2024, revised April 2025) for the MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 devices. It directs users to TI E2E support forums for design help, lists relevant trademarks (LaunchPad, Code Composer Studio, TI E2E, Arm, Cortex), and cautions that the integrated circuits can be damaged by electrostatic discharge. The revision history details changes from the November 2024 revision to April 2025, including a note that the device targets PSA-L1 certification, corrected counts of timers, UART, and SPI instances in low-power modes, added Preview package variants (100_nFBGA_ZAW and 42_DSBGA_YCJ), and numerous specification updates covering absolute maximum ratings, thermal data, supply current, POR/BOR thresholds, flash endurance, oscillators, digital IO, ADC, temperature sensor, VREF, comparator, SPI, DMA, SRAM, security, keystore, UART, and timers. The document also provides mechanical, packaging, and orderable information, notes qualified automotive versions (MSPM0G3518-Q1, MSPM0G3519-Q1), and includes TI's disclaimers that resources are provided "as is" without warranties.

Kobe University researchers discovered that orchid seedlings germinate only near decaying logs, where they rely on wood-decaying fungi for carbon, since orchid seeds are too small to contain nutrients. The fungi associated with seedlings closely match those found in adult orchids with coral-shaped rhizomes of the same species. This finding reveals a previously unknown carbon pathway from deadwood to green plants in forest ecosystems and may explain how some orchid species evolved full mycoheterotrophy, abandoning photosynthesis entirely. The researchers note that orchid conservation is inseparable from protecting deadwood and its fungi.

This study examined elementary teachers' attitudes toward the inclusion of learners with special education needs (LSENs) in Liloan District, Cebu Province, Philippines. Using a descriptive correlational design, 30 purposively sampled teachers answered a demographic questionnaire and a Modified STATIC survey, analyzed through descriptive and inferential statistics within an Input-Process-Output model grounded in the Theory of Planned Behavior, Ecological Systems Theory, Social Learning Theory, and relevant education laws. Most respondents were female (93.33%), married (83.33%), aged 34–43, with graduate units but limited inclusion experience (90% had 1–5 years handling LSENs) and introductory training (80% had 1–2 trainings). Teachers showed overall positive attitudes (grand mean 3.71), rating professional issues (4.08) and philosophical issues (4.03) positively, advantages/disadvantages positively (3.50), and logistical concerns neutrally (3.23), citing concerns about resources, class sizes, and supports. Statistical tests found no significant relationship between demographic profiles and attitudes. The study concluded that while philosophical support for inclusion is strong, sustained professional development, smaller class sizes, assistive technologies, staffing, budgets, and multi-level support systems are needed, leading to an evidence-based Teacher Inclusion Support Plan to foster lasting positive attitudes and practices.

Students returned to Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida, on February 28, 2018, for the first time since a shooting killed 17 students and teachers on February 14. About 50 uniformed officers provided heavy security, which some students found disturbing. Grief counselors, therapy animals, and volunteers greeted students; backpacks were banned, the freshman building remained cordoned off, and classes began with fourth period so students could reunite with those they were with during the shooting. Student activists, including David Hogg, continued pushing for gun control ahead of a March 14 national school walkout. Dick's Sporting Goods announced it would stop selling assault-style rifles and not sell guns to anyone under 21. In Florida's legislature, a bill raising the long-gun purchase age to 21 and allowing some armed teachers advanced through committees, though the NRA opposed ownership restrictions, and some victims' families said it did not go far enough.

The speaker calls the recognition a great honor despite disappointment over not being nominated for the rookie trophy. The Flyers asked him to come over a year earlier, but he stayed in Europe to prepare. After a slow first five games, his confidence rose.

The author, who calls his 21-year-old college-senior daughter "The Girl" (TG) to protect her privacy, believes she would make an excellent literature professor but cannot recommend that path because full-time literature jobs are extremely scarce. He cites a young history professor who found only five suitable faculty positions nationwide last year, noting that scarce jobs tend to deteriorate without countervailing pressure. He sees no hiring recovery for liberal arts fields given cost pressures, a demographic cliff, generative AI, and a hostile political climate, while journalism and publishing also struggle. TG is interested in librarianship, which he encourages, and he invites readers to share career advice for talented young people.

A recent paper examined a hypothetical scenario in which the NIH operated with a 40 percent smaller budget, as proposed by President Trump. The study identified NIH grants in the bottom 40 percent of the funding priority queue between 1980 and 2007 and linked them to FDA-approved drugs from 2000 to 2023. It found that more than half of drugs approved in the 21st century were connected to research that would have been at risk of not being funded. Of 557 approved drugs, 40 had patents directly acknowledging NIH funding, 14 cited at-risk grants, and 65 involved "highly linked" research. Drugs tied to at-risk research received FDA priority review more often and had higher average market values, suggesting such budget cuts would have resulted in fewer medical innovations.

This passage is a datasheet section (SLASFA2A, November 2024, revised April 2025) describing the MSPM0G3519/G3518/G1519/G1518 microcontrollers from Texas Instruments:

- **SRAM**: Up to 128KB with zero wait state access, split into two 64KB banks. Bank 0 has ECC/parity protection and is available in run, sleep, stop, and standby modes; Bank 1 lacks ECC/parity, can be disabled via BANKOFF1, and can be powered off in STOP mode via BANKSTOP1. Contents are lost in shutdown. A write-execute mutual exclusion mechanism enables two read-write partitions and one read-execute partition for code protection, performance, and security.
- **GPIO/IOMUX**: Up to 93 pins across Ports A, B, and C, with wake from SHUTDOWN and FastWake from STOP/STANDBY; IOMUX provides pad configuration and pin muxing via the PINCM register.
- **Analog**: Two 12-bit ADCs (4Msps, >11 ENOB, 14-bit effective resolution via averaging, 12 result registers each), a linear temperature sensor with factory single-point calibration, VREF (1.4V/2.5V internal or external reference), comparators, and a 12-bit DAC with self-calibration, FIFO, and DMA.
- **Security**: AES-128/256 accelerator (CBC, CTR, CCM, GCM and other modes), flexible firewalls, keystore for up to four AES keys, CRC-16/32, and a TRNG generating a 32-bit number every 128 clock cycles. MATHACL provides hardware 32-bit math acceleration.
- **Communication**: UART0-UART1 and UART3-UART7 (LIN support, FIFOs, DMA); I2C supporting Standard/Fast/Fast-mode Plus (up to 1Mbit/s) and SMBus 3.0; SPI up to 32Mbit/s (only HSIO pins support >16Mbit/s); CAN-FD compliant with ISO 11898-1:2015 up to 5Mbit/s with up to 32 transmit and 64 receive buffers.
- **Low power/timers**: LFSS_B contains RTC_B (alarms, periodic interrupts, ±240ppm calibration) and an independent watchdog (2ms–2hr periods, POR reset); a separate windowed watchdog is included. Timers comprise TIMGx general-purpose (16/32-bit, QEI/Hall on some instances) and TIMAx advanced (complementary PWM with dead band, fault handling under 40ns).
- **Debug/boot**: Two-wire SWD interface; boot strap loader via UART/I2C protected by a 256-bit password, enabled by default, with multiple invocation methods.
- **Factory constants**: Read-only memory-mapped region with device identification (DEVICEID, USERID) and trim data.
- **Applications**: Recommended 10µF/0.1µF decoupling capacitors, 47kΩ NRST pullup, 100kΩ ROSC resistor for SYSOSC FCL, and 0.47µF VCORE capacitor; pullups required for 5V-tolerant open-drain IO.
- **Support**: Device nomenclature (MSP production vs. X experimental), development tools (CCS, IAR, Keil MDK, SysConfig, LaunchPad), a revision history documenting 2025 specification updates, mechanical/package data, and automotive-qualified variants (MSPM0G3518-Q1, MSPM0G3519-Q1).

The order of the Supreme Court, Bronx County, dismissing Brian O'Loughlin's defamation action against PBA president Phil Caruso and the PBA for failure to state a cause of action was unanimously affirmed. Caruso's letter, published in New York's Finest magazine, called O'Loughlin and eight other officers who sought refunds of a $20 contribution—donated for a memorial to officers killed in the line of duty—"a disgrace" with "no feelings." Applying the Silsdorf standard and the Steinhilber fact-opinion factors, the court held the statements were vague, could not be characterized as true or false, and constituted pure opinion rather than false or actionable mixed opinion.

Vertical farming involves growing crops in controlled environments without soil and water, stacked in layers, using mechanisms such as hydroponics and aeroponics. Growth drivers include better food quality, rising population, reduced water and soil dependency, and new technologies, while high initial investments and energy consumption of artificial lighting hinder growth. The global market is expected to reach USD 6 billion by 2022 with 21% CAGR (2016-2022). North America holds the largest share; Asia-Pacific is expected to grow rapidly.

Rising global population is driving demand for increased cereal production and pesticide use, with grains and cereals being major consumers of pesticides, particularly herbicides. While crop rotation helps maintain soil nutrients and mitigate pests, crop protection chemicals can adversely affect the environment, human health, and soil productivity. By type, the grain and cereal crop protection market comprises insecticides, herbicides, and fungicides, with herbicides dominant due to low cost and ongoing R&D. Geographically, North America leads, followed by Asia Pacific and Europe, with Asia Pacific expected to grow rapidly. The market includes local, regional, and international vendors, with global players leading in quality and innovation.

Kayleigh Gray, whose daughter Emilia was born prematurely at 27 weeks and treated at Royal Preston Hospital's Neo Natal Unit, donated 25 pairs of acrylic turtle doves to the unit with help from her employer, Sign Build. Designed by Kayleigh, one dove stays with each baby while the other is taken home by parents.

Tesla, Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2022. Tesla, incorporated in Delaware in 2003 and headquartered in Austin, Texas, designs, manufactures and sells electric vehicles and solar energy generation and energy storage products through two segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. As of October 18, 2022, 3,157,752,449 shares of common stock were outstanding. In August 2022, Tesla effected a three-for-one stock split, and all share and per-share amounts were retroactively adjusted.

Total assets were $74.4 billion as of September 30, 2022, up from $62.1 billion at December 31, 2021. Total revenues were $21.45 billion for Q3 2022 (versus $13.76 billion in Q3 2021) and $57.14 billion for the nine months (versus $36.10 billion). Net income attributable to common stockholders was $3.29 billion for Q3 2022 and $8.87 billion for the nine months. Cash and cash equivalents totaled $19.5 billion, and nine-month operating cash flow was $11.4 billion.

Tesla converted approximately 75% of its digital asset purchases into fiat currency, with a carrying value of $218 million as of September 30, 2022. Total debt and finance leases were $1.46 billion current and $2.10 billion long-term; the 2022 Convertible Senior Notes were fully settled in March 2022. Gross unrecognized tax benefits were $778 million, and the IRS is examining returns for 2015–2018. The Inflation Reduction Act of 2022, enacted August 16, 2022, may materially affect the financial statements.

Legal proceedings include the SolarCity acquisition litigation, in which judgment was entered in favor of Elon Musk on April 27, 2022, with an appeal pending; a derivative action challenging the 2018 CEO Performance Award, with trial set for November 14–18, 2022; and a derivative action regarding directors' compensation. Tesla also has lease obligations for Gigafactory New York and Gigafactory Shanghai.

Hockey players discuss their mindset before a potential Stanley Cup-winning game. They stress maintaining the same focused mentality held all series, viewing their recent win as one step closer to the title, with the final step coming tomorrow night. They praise a hardworking, unflashy teammate and note Marian's added motivation after losing two previous finals. They expect an opposing star to bounce back and plan to remain just as physical against him and other top players. One player recalls childhood dreams in Canada and watching Pittsburgh's comeback championship last year as inspiration. Players describe managing excitement, staying disciplined with penalties, and contributions from depth players like Kopey, Nick Boynton, and Tomas. Two players reflect on reaching the Cup Final in only their third professional season, calling it a lucky and enjoyable ride.

On August 15, 2019, NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC announcing its financial results for the quarter ended July 28, 2019. The filing includes a press release (Exhibit 99.1) and a CFO Commentary (Exhibit 99.2) prepared by Colette M. Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. The CFO Commentary will be posted to investor.nvidia.com after filing. The press release and CFO Commentary are furnished rather than filed, and thus are not subject to Section 18 liability or incorporation by reference in other SEC filings. The report was signed by Kress.

Only 18% of American workers are very confident their retirement savings are on track, and Americans spend more time planning vacations than retirement. The passage outlines three steps to ensure sufficient retirement savings: (1) Determine projected retirement income based on current savings rates, noting that saving 10% of income is likely insufficient due to healthcare costs, low interest rates, and longer lifespans; use online calculators and add expected Social Security benefits, aiming to replace at least 100% of current income. (2) Monitor investment fees, which can reduce the outcome of a 30-year, $5,500 annual investment by over $211,000 at a 3% fee. (3) Maintain appropriate asset allocation based on age and risk tolerance, such as subtracting one's age from 110 to determine the stock percentage. The passage concludes with a promotion for Social Security maximization strategies.

An analysis by Notre Dame Law School professor Derek Muller found that 92.45% of campaign contributions from attorneys and staff at the nation's 100 top-grossing firms and 50 larger plaintiffs-side firms went to Democrats in 2023 and 2024—a roughly 12-1 ratio, up from 6-1 in 2017-2020. About $52 million went to Democratic-affiliated groups versus $4 million to Republican-affiliated groups. Cleary Gottlieb, Fried Frank, and Mintz Levin had the highest Democratic contribution percentages, while Nelson Mullins, Lewis Brisbois, and Ogletree had the lowest.

A shorthanded goal was the difference in the game. As the lower seed, the team knew they needed to win road games. The goalie made two or three big saves before the opponent scored on a known play that should have been defended better. A late first-period power play was ineffective. Four lines were used after five days off, and a better first period is needed.

E-mini Russell 2000 Index futures are financial derivatives representing contracts to buy or sell a specified amount of the Russell 2000 Index at a pre-agreed price on a future date, traded on the CME Globex platform for speculation or hedging. The Russell 2000 Index, created in 1984 by the Frank Russell Company and now maintained by FTSE Russell, tracks 2,000 of the smallest-cap US companies in the Russell 3000 Index; the futures launched in 1993.

One contract equals $50 multiplied by the index value, quoted in USD and cents per index point. Contracts follow quarterly cycles (March, June, September, December) listed for five consecutive quarters, are cash-settled, and trading terminates at 9:30 a.m. ET on the third Friday of the contract month. Trading occurs Sundays to Fridays from 6:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET with a one-hour break. The tick size is $5.00 for outright Globex trading and $2.50 for BTIC, TACO, and Calendar Spread, with minimum price fluctuations of 0.10 and 0.05 index points respectively. The block minimum is 40 contracts.

As of November 30, 2022, the futures traded at $1841.2. The all-time high is 2460.8 (November 2021), while the underlying index's all-time low was 106.07 (October 1987). Seasonally, the futures perform better in spring than summer, with August and December stronger within their respective seasons.

A Russell 2000 rebalance strategy—buying at the close of the first trading day after June 23 and selling at the close of the first trading day of July—backtested with a 1.34% unleveraged gain per trade and a 76% win rate. Prices are affected by component stock movements, interest rates, economic news, and the US dollar. The biggest risk is adverse price movement amplified by leverage. Traders can access the contract through a futures broker or trade a CFD alternative, which has no fixed expiration dates.

WiseGuyReports has published a market research report forecasting the data center UPS market in the US to grow at a CAGR of 4.01% during 2016-2020. UPS systems automatically power data center infrastructure during outages until generators take over, protecting facilities from power sags and surges. The market is segmented into centralized, zone/floor-level, and rackmount UPS systems. Key vendors include ABB, Eaton, Emerson Network Power, GE Industrial Solutions, Schneider Electric, and Tripp Lite. The market is driven by an increase in data center power outages, challenged by UPS battery failure, and influenced by advances in data center infrastructure management (DCIM).

The state Board of Regents unanimously approved an emergency plan allowing special-education students to earn local diplomas through occupational assessments instead of minimum scores on Regents exams in English and math. Crafted by Education Commissioner MaryEllen Elia, the measure applies to students graduating as early as January. Students must meet CDOS credential requirements, with superintendents or principals determining proficiency or employment readiness. In 2016, more than 15,000 students with disabilities statewide failed to graduate after four years. Parents who lobbied for the change applauded the decision, but some critics warned it might revive separate academic tracks and objected to the rushed approval process.

Turkey has secured a €974 million loan from a consortium of international lenders, including European development institutions and multilateral lenders, to fund a major highway project in central Anatolia. The highway will link key provincial centres, improve trade routes and logistics networks, and reduce travel times, supporting Ankara's broader goals of connectivity and economic integration. The loan includes environmental and social performance standards aligned with international sustainability benchmarks. The project is expected to generate investment, industrial expansion, and construction jobs, and is seen as critical for connecting smaller cities to export corridors toward Europe and the Middle East. However, rugged topography, potential land acquisition disputes, and volatility in borrowing costs and the Turkish lira could delay completion or raise financing costs.

Jawed Zia, former managing director of Novartis India, resigned 15 days after taking charge and may join rival Abbott India, sources said. Novartis has not named a replacement. The company faces regulatory investigation for alleged price collusion over its anti-diabetic drug Galvus.

The District Court of Appeal of Florida, First District, affirmed AHCA's Final Order of Dismissal with Prejudice against Glenwood Nursing Center. After a February 2010 survey, AHCA issued statements of deficiencies and later an administrative complaint seeking revocation of Glenwood's nursing home license, fines, and fees, with a 21-day deadline to request a hearing. Glenwood filed its hearing request one day late, on June 15, 2010, after AHCA's counsel agreed to accept a belated filing through June 18. AHCA dismissed the request as untimely, revoked Glenwood's license, and imposed a $25,000 fine. On appeal, Glenwood argued the deadline was equitably tolled by AHCA counsel's representation and that its June 15 request related back to an April 16 letter sent to CMS. The court rejected both arguments, holding that equitable tolling did not apply under the circumstances in Machules and Watson, and that the letter to CMS was insufficient because Florida law requires hearing requests to be filed with the state agency's agency clerk, which Glenwood never did.

The passage presents 10 free backtested swing trading strategies, some published since 2012, covering instruments such as the S&P 500 (SPY), Nasdaq (QQQ), gold (GLD), bonds (TLT), and consumer staples (XLP). Swing trading is defined as holding positions for a few days to several weeks—longer than day trading but shorter than position trading. The authors argue that backtesting improves a trader's odds, recommend combining swing trading with a buy-and-hold cornerstone portfolio, and advise trading mechanically, starting small, and risking only money one can afford to lose. They note that most swing traders are unsuccessful, that realistic returns range from 5 to 20%, and that the most successful swing traders use quantified, backtested mechanical strategies. Strategy code is available to paying members, primarily in Amibroker format, and the authors state the strategies should be independently verified and can be improved.

This patent disclosure describes wood-type golf club heads (drivers, fairway woods, and hybrid clubs) featuring raised sole portions with increased curvature. The raised sole portions stiffen the sole, reduce its mass, and modify the club head's sound, reducing the need for internal stiffening ribs and freeing discretionary mass. These portions can be bounded by cantilevered ledges extending below their edges. Some embodiments include sole inserts mounted over sole openings and crown inserts over upper openings, made of less dense materials (e.g., composites) for mass savings. Club heads may include front channels and front/rear weight tracks with slidably adjustable weight assemblies to modify center of gravity (CG) and moment of inertia (MOI) characteristics. Configurations include bi-level soles, a single raised portion spanning most of the sole, or separate toe-side and heel-side raised portions with a weight track between them. Frames are typically metal (e.g., titanium alloys), while inserts use lighter composite materials. The disclosed features aim to provide greater distance, accuracy, forgiveness on off-center strikes, improved acoustics, durability, and customizability. The passage also details curvature measurements, head volumes, mass specifications, forgiveness ratios, and manufacturing methods.

In December 2019, Wuhan identified a viral pneumonia outbreak caused by SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19), for which no approved therapeutics exist. The DAWN protocol investigates drug compounds or convalescent plasma, requiring randomized controlled study.

The passage is from the datasheet of the TPS7H500x-SP series (TPS7H5001-SP through TPS7H5004-SP), radiation-hardness-assured peak current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting switching frequencies up to 2 MHz and topologies including buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge.

Functional features described include: hiccup mode, where cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins when CS_ILIM exceeds 1.05 V and the CHICC capacitor (minimum 3.3 nF recommended) sets the delay and restart timing; external fault protection via the FAULT pin with a 0.6 V threshold and 0.4–1.4 µs minimum pulse width; slope compensation via the RSC pin to prevent subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle (recommended value equal to the inductor falling slope); Type 2A/2B frequency compensation options; and thermal shutdown at 175°C with restart below 160°C.

An application example designs a 500 kHz synchronous push-pull converter with GaN FETs and a 5 V output, detailing component selection: 205 kΩ RT, 10 kΩ/1.4 kΩ feedback divider, 25 ns dead time, 49.9 kΩ LEB resistor, 33 nF soft-start capacitor, 2.5 transformer turns ratio with 40 µH primary inductance, 170 V primary and 80 V synchronous rectifier GaN FETs, an RCD clamp, 0.47 µH output inductor, 2.3 mF output capacitance (including single-event transient mitigation), 7.5 Ω current sense resistor, and 102 kΩ slope compensation resistor.

The controllers operate from a 4–14 V supply requiring at least 0.1 µF of input bypass capacitance. Layout guidelines address noise reduction, ground separation, trace sizing, and component placement. The passage also includes application curves, related documentation, revision history, mechanical/packaging data, and TI legal disclaimers.

This tutorial explains how to deploy Mattermost, an open source, self-hosted instant messaging platform written in Golang and React, on a CentOS 7 server with Nginx configured as an SSL reverse proxy. Prerequisites include a domain name pointing to the server, Nginx installed, and an SSL certificate. The steps covered are: creating a MariaDB database and user for Mattermost, creating a dedicated system user, downloading and extracting Mattermost version 4.9.0 to /opt, configuring database settings in config.json, and testing the server. A systemd unit file is then created to run Mattermost as a service enabled at boot. An Nginx server block is configured with SSL, websocket support, and caching. Finally, the first user account (which receives administrator privileges) and team are created via the browser, the site URL and email notification settings are configured in the System Console, and the Mattermost service is restarted.

The SEC fined Altaba, formerly Yahoo, $35 million for failing to disclose a data breach affecting hundreds of millions of accounts. Yahoo disclosed the breach in 2016, two years after learning of it, leaving investors in the dark.

This withdrawn medRxiv preprint evaluates six machine learning models—Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Neural Network, Decision Tree, and SuperLearner—for diagnosing pancreatic cancer using a synthetic dataset containing demographic, clinical, and symptom variables. Data were split 80/20 for training and testing, with no resampling applied. All models achieved similar accuracy (76.05%–76.35%), but sensitivity was very low: Random Forest and Decision Tree identified no true positives, SVM achieved the highest sensitivity (1.90%), and SuperLearner had the highest precision (66.67%) with only 0.42% sensitivity. The authors attribute poor sensitivity to class imbalance and propose remedies including resampling techniques (e.g., SMOTE, ADASYN, Tomek Links), cost-sensitive learning, threshold tuning, feature engineering informed by gene expression, PCA, and correlation analyses, interpretability tools (SHAP, LIME), use of real-world clinical data, and collaboration between data scientists and clinicians. They conclude that further research is needed to improve sensitivity and address class imbalance before clinical adoption.

U.S. Treasury yields rose on Monday, rebounding from six-week lows, as reduced U.S.-North Korea tensions led investors to pare back low-risk government debt. Comments urging a peaceful solution and downplaying military conflict prompted some investors to return to riskier assets. The 10-year yield rose over 3 basis points to 2.222 percent; the two-year yield rose 2 basis points to 1.314 percent after soft July inflation data lowered Fed rate-hike expectations.

A Feb. 9 study by 11Alive found the CDC cut over $700,000 in 2016, mostly from HIV prevention funding, while spending millions on a failed project. Atlanta has ranked among the highest HIV levels for over three years. Georgia State's Jamal Jones and Victoria Novak cite lack of access to expensive prevention medication like PrEP and healthcare in lower-income communities as key problems. Stigma and Georgia law criminalizing certain activities by HIV-positive individuals discourage testing, so many are diagnosed in advanced AIDS stages. Jones launched a Georgia State campaign to increase student testing. Georgia ranks 5th nationally for new HIV diagnoses, and House Bill 65 proposes adding HIV/AIDS to conditions covered by medical marijuana.

RTX Neural Faces is a generative AI approach to improve real-time face rendering. It takes a rasterized face plus 3D pose data as input and uses a real-time generative AI model, trained on thousands of images under varied conditions and TensorRT optimized, to infer a more natural face.

Salesforce will invest over $2.2 billion in its French business over five years, announced during Macron's state visit to Washington. The company cited rapid growth in France and plans to expand headcount, real estate, and data center capacity.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2017 reports total revenue of $22.1 billion for the quarter (up from $20.5 billion in the prior-year quarter) and net income of $4.8 billion (up from $3.8 billion), with diluted EPS of $0.61. Nine-month revenue was $66.6 billion with net income of $14.7 billion. Total assets were $225.0 billion as of March 31, 2017.

On December 8, 2016, Microsoft completed its acquisition of LinkedIn for a preliminary purchase price of $27.0 billion; LinkedIn contributed $975 million in revenue and a $386 million operating loss in the quarter. In November 2016, Microsoft sold its feature phone business for $350 million.

The company operates three segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. Q3 highlights included commercial cloud annualized revenue run rate exceeding $15.2 billion, Azure revenue growth of 93%, Office 365 commercial revenue growth of 45%, and Surface revenue decline of 26%.

Long-term debt totaled $76.8 billion as of March 31, 2017, up from $40.6 billion at June 30, 2016, following debt issuances of $19.8 billion in August 2016 and $17.0 billion in February 2017. The effective tax rate was 19% for the quarter versus 25% in the prior year. A $40 billion share repurchase program approved in September 2016 had $38.4 billion remaining. The company disclosed pending legal matters, including patent litigation and antitrust investigations, with accrued legal liabilities of $443 million and reasonably possible losses of approximately $1.5 billion beyond recorded amounts.

Since the rail line washed out in spring 2017, Churchill's population of 900 has been shrinking, with 30 families leaving since last May due to job losses and rising fuel and food costs. The town's only school has lost about 40 students since last June, which could affect teaching jobs. The school division has cut student trips south due to costs. No timeline exists for repairing the rail line.

Industrial enterprises face challenges including geopolitical uncertainty, rising energy prices, raw material shortages, supply chain disruptions, skilled labor shortfalls, and sustainability demands, while digitalization fundamentally transforms manufacturing value creation. IT-based simulation, modeling, and analysis are key solution approaches, with high-performance computing (HPC), combined with cloud solutions, unlocking additional opportunities for agility and digital transformation. An IDC survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers from manufacturing enterprises with over 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland (December 2021) found that simulation, modeling, and analysis are closely tied to business goals, with innovation deemed most important by three-quarters of respondents, and 57% viewing these tools as important for improving quality. Around half already use them in product development, production, and process planning, with deployment expected to reach 90% within two years; 64% plan relevant investments. Data silos remain a challenge, making a unified information base—a "single source of truth"—necessary. New usage scenarios include virtual prototyping, digital twins, IoT-driven feedback loops, and design optimization; 42% already use high-performance data analytics. However, growing calculation complexity creates trade-offs between speed and accuracy, with 42% reporting outdated or inaccurate simulations. Demand for high-performance calculations is expected to rise sharply, from 8% currently identifying high demand to nearly half within two years. Four out of five decision makers consider HPC a game changer for product and process innovation, as it enables complex calculations, increases quality and intensity of use, unlocks new usage scenarios, and boosts innovation and agility. Over a quarter already use professional HPC infrastructures, another 39% are planning or piloting deployment, and only 15% are not engaging, citing high costs, limited awareness of deployment opportunities, and the topic's newness.

Research by the Cinnamon Network found that more than 3,500 churches and 200,000 volunteers are supporting the overstretched NHS through health and social care initiatives, filling gaps left by funding cuts and limited resources. Its report, The Church's Impact on Health and Care, studied 32 church-led initiatives addressing issues including mental health, obesity and social isolation, and found them cost-effective; 2016 research valued faith groups' community contribution at £3bn a year. One highlighted project is parish nursing, in which churches recruit registered nurses to support local patients. A Cambridgeshire GP praised the parish nurse at his practice. Parish nursing, founded in the US, reached the UK in 2005; over 100 nurses now work with 85 churches, with 100 more expected within 18 months. Parish nurses provide preventative care and support without replacing NHS nurses, and most of their patients are not church members.

The Columbiana Clippers defeated the Lisbon Devils 49-47, scoring twice in the final 23 seconds. With 36 seconds remaining, Lisbon's Izzy Perez hit a free throw for a 47-45 lead, but Columbiana's Alexis Cross tied the game with a baseline drive, and Kayla Muslovski's steal and layup provided the winning points. The Clippers improved to 5-0 overall and 3-0 in the EOAC, while the Devils fell to 3-2 and 2-1. Muslovski and Cross each scored 14 points for Columbiana. Perez led all scorers with 17 points for Lisbon, and Maddie Liberati added 12. Columbiana also won the junior varsity game 33-23.

Reddit has surpassed Facebook to become the third most visited US platform, according to Alexa, after Google and YouTube. Users spend more daily time on Reddit, whose rise coincides with Facebook's Cambridge Analytica scandal.

The ICC Board meetings in Kolkata may revisit a proposal to replace the 2021 Champions Trophy in India with a World T20, an idea floated at the Auckland conclave and rejected by the BCCI. BCCI treasurer Anirudh Chaudhry said scrapping the Champions Trophy would cause a loss of about $30 million to the BCCI and its stakeholders and would likely be unacceptable to the board's General Body. He criticized ICC chairman Shashank Manohar and the ICC's attitude toward India, noting the Champions Trophy was the brainchild of Jagmohan Dalmiya. Under the Auckland agreement, Australia hosts the 2020 World T20, while India hosts the 2021 Champions Trophy and the 2023 World Cup. Separately, with the IPL advanced to March 29–May 19, the ICC agreed to an altered 2019 World Cup itinerary, with India playing South Africa on June 5 and Pakistan on June 16.

Suspected jihadists killed at least 18 people and wounded several in an overnight attack on the Aziz Istanbul restaurant in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso's capital. Security forces shot dead both attackers and freed those trapped inside. Communications Minister Remi Dandjinou called it a terrorist attack, saying the toll was provisional. Burkina Faso has faced sporadic jihadist attacks, including a January 2016 Ouagadougou assault that killed 30, claimed by AQIM.

This paper proposes iMOOE, a physics-guided invariant learning framework for zero-shot out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization in PDE dynamics forecasting. The authors identify a two-level PDE invariance principle: operator invariance, where PDE dynamics are governed by a set of spatial operators that remain invariant across domains, and compositionality invariance, where the composition of these operators with physical parameters and forcing terms is fixed for a given system. To capture this invariance, iMOOE combines a mixture of operator experts (MOOE) architecture—comprising specialized neural operator experts with mask-based derivative selection and a fusion network for parameter conditioning—with a frequency-enriched invariant learning objective consisting of maximal prediction loss, risk equality loss across training environments, and a frequency enrichment loss addressing spectral bias. Experiments on five PDE systems show state-of-the-art zero-shot OOD results, with average improvements of 40.21% on nMSE and 30.78% on fRMSE over baselines, along with gains in time extrapolation. iMOOE is compatible with diverse neural operators in a plug-and-play manner and achieves the lowest mean and variance of metrics on real-world sea surface temperature forecasting. Sensitivity analysis finds three operator experts optimal. The authors note that validation is limited to a restricted diversity of dynamical systems.

Twenty-nine million people in the southeastern United States faced a threat of severe storms Monday that could bring damaging hail, high winds, and tornadoes. Forecasters said strong tornadoes were increasingly likely, especially in northern Alabama, with parts of Tennessee, Mississippi, and Georgia also at risk. Hail fell in northern Mississippi along a 50-mile path from Holly Springs to Booneville. More than a dozen school systems in northern Alabama dismissed students early, and Birmingham city offices closed at noon. Possible hazards included tennis ball-sized hail and 70 mph winds.

Indian stock markets began the week with sharp gains, but a late-week correction erased most of them, with the Nifty ending down 0.3 percent while mid- and small-cap indexes gained about 1.5 percent each. Sentiment was dampened by concerns over U.S. tariffs and trade wars, possible global interest rate hikes, the TDP's exit from the BJP alliance, the RBI's discontinuation of LoUs and LCs, and tensions between the finance ministry and the RBI. The rupee ended at 64.93 per dollar. Stock-specific news included a thumbs-down to TCS's stake sale, an Ambuja Cements-ACC supply agreement, IndiGo grounding A320neo aircraft, and another fraud at Punjab National Bank. Crude sulfate turpentine, a flammable, water-insoluble derivative of turpentine, is obtained as a byproduct of the Kraft process. It contains terpene hydrocarbons and sulfur compounds, primarily alpha-pinene and beta-pinene, with smaller amounts of limonene, camphene, carene, and terpinene. It is mainly used in producing fragrances and flavors, serving cosmetics and food & beverage industries, and also acts as a solvent for paint thinning and a raw material in chemical synthesis. High distillation investment costs and limited black liquor retrieval are expected to restrain market growth.

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture discusses interacting Bose gases and their superfluid properties. The Bogoliubov approximation replaces the condensate operator with a number, diagonalizing the Hamiltonian into non-interacting quasiparticles with linear dispersion at low momenta and quadratic dispersion at high momenta. Sound was observed by suddenly switching on a repulsive, blue-detuned laser beam, and quasiparticle dispersion was measured through stimulated Raman (BEC) spectroscopy using two laser beams. Quantum depletion—the admixture of finite-momentum states—is about 1% in alkali gases, whereas liquid helium has only a 10% condensate fraction. For trapped, inhomogeneous condensates, the Gross-Pitaevskii equation describes the macroscopic wave function; interactions flatten the density, defining the healing length, and the Thomas-Fermi approximation neglects kinetic energy, giving density as an inverted trapping potential. The equation quantitatively explains condensate expansion (cigar-to-disk aspect ratio inversion) and vortices, which are singular points of zero density; doubly charged vortices are unstable, and vortices arrange into hexagonal lattices due to their repulsion. In optical lattices, introduced to reach strongly correlated regimes, the tight-binding limit yields the Bose-Hubbard model with tunneling parameter J and on-site interaction U. A mean-field decoupling approximation describes the superfluid-to-Mott insulator transition, producing a phase diagram with Mott insulator lobes. The transition is observed via time-of-flight interference patterns and quantum gas microscopes that resolve atom occupancy per site.

This passage describes a pragmatic randomized controlled trial protocol, embedded within a Learning Health System (LHS) framework, to evaluate Ambient AI (Abridge AI), a generative AI tool for clinical documentation, integrated into the Epic EHR at UW Health. A Pragmatic Trial Operations (PTOps) playbook with five components—governance, user experience, technical, documentation sustainment, and analytics—aligned research and operational priorities through a multidisciplinary governance committee meeting biweekly. The alpha phase (June 24–October 10, 2024; 20 providers, 8,527 encounters) refined workflows, addressed patient consent gaps, and corrected a decline in ICD-10 coding accuracy (79% to 35%) via a new note template. An LLM-based automated ICD-10 extraction system, validated using GPT-4o on 200 notes (mean Jaccard score 0.54), reduced manual coder workload. A real-time dashboard tracked utilization, documentation efficiency, and consent compliance, while a difference-in-differences analysis with two-week rolling windows monitored performance drifts. The beta phase is a 24-week multisite stepped-wedge randomized trial randomizing 66 providers into three waves at six-week intervals, with provider well-being measured by the Professional Fulfillment Index as the primary outcome, powered at 90% to detect Cohen's d of 0.44. Alpha-phase weighted median utilization was 65.4%; DiD analyses showed a 6.84 percentage-point decrease in utilization, a 0.33-hour increase in work outside of work, and a 0.43-hour increase in time in notes. The authors conclude that this LHS-based playbook enables rigorous, scalable evaluation of rapidly evolving GenAI technologies while maintaining operational efficiency.

The Utah Court of Appeals affirmed the district court's grant of summary judgment against Kari L. Baumann in her suit against The Kroger Company and Dr. Gregory P. Tayler, in which she alleged she suffered hypotension due to overmedication. Baumann, who proceeded pro se after her attorney withdrew, failed to designate expert witnesses by the deadlines in a stipulated discovery schedule. After Defendants moved for summary judgment, arguing she could not establish the applicable standards of care without expert testimony, Baumann filed an expert report applicable only to Kroger on the day of the hearing, without seeking leave of court. The district court found she failed to make expert disclosures under rule 26 of the Utah Rules of Civil Procedure and that no good cause excused the failure, precluding her under rule 26(d)(4) from using undisclosed materials to contest summary judgment. On appeal, Baumann's argument regarding an expert report applicable to Dr. Tayler was unpreserved and therefore not considered. Her contention that rule 16(d), rather than rule 26(d)(4), should have applied under Coroles v. State also failed; relying on Sleepy Holdings LLC v. Mountain West Title, the court held rule 26 governed because the sanction was for failure to disclose an expert witness, not for violating a scheduling order. The court concluded the district court did not abuse its discretion and affirmed.
The team focuses on winning shifts and periods, not outcomes, calls this the year's best period, shares common purpose with Ray, and must seize a cup opportunity that may never return.

A newlywed Northamptonshire couple walked home after PC Dave Lee stopped their wedding car driver for speeding at 46mph in a 30mph zone and driving without insurance. The couple remained in high spirits and took a selfie with the officer.

The President returns to the House of Representatives a bill to facilitate the refunding of the national debt, stating his objections. Owing to the pressure of public duties in the closing week of his term, he does not present a full argument, but affirms the importance of refunding legislation and urges adoption of another measure if this bill fails. Though he deems it unwise to authorize the Secretary of the Treasury to offer 3.5 percent bonds, he would not object to the bill on that ground. His objection is to the fifth section, which after July 1, 1881, would allow only 3 percent bonds to be deposited as security for national-bank circulation and for public money held by banks. He argues this would prevent new banks from organizing and existing banks from enlarging capital, deprive bill holders of the best security, make the system a monopoly of current bankers, and endanger the national banking system, which he describes as safe, beneficial, and long successful. He warns that withdrawal of bank circulation would bring embarrassment and disaster to business and check the country's growing prosperity. Believing refunding need not imperil the banking system, he returns the bill for further consideration under the Constitution.

The NVIDIA Ampere GA10x GPU architecture (GA102 and GA104) builds on the Turing architecture, delivering up to 1.7x faster raster graphics and up to 2x faster ray tracing performance. GA102, fabricated on Samsung's 8nm 8N custom process with 28.3 billion transistors, powers the GeForce RTX 3090, RTX 3080, RTX A6000, and A40; GA104 powers the RTX 3070. A full GA102 contains 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor Cores.

Key features include 2x FP32 processing (both SM datapaths handle FP32), second-generation RT Cores that double ray/triangle intersection testing rates and add hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur via a new Interpolate Triangle Position unit, and third-generation Tensor Cores supporting new data types (TF32, BF16) and Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity, which doubles throughput by skipping zero-valued weights. GA10x SMs feature a 33% larger unified L1 data cache/shared memory (128 KB) and support concurrent RT Core, graphics, and compute workloads.

GA10x introduces GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling, achieving up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec bandwidth. Additional features include third-generation NVLink (112.5 GB/sec total), PCIe Gen 4, ROPs relocated into GPCs (112 total), DLSS 8K support, RTX IO for GPU-based asset decompression (up to 100x I/O throughput), HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a, fifth-generation NVDEC with the industry's first AV1 hardware decode, and seventh-generation NVENC.

The A40 data center GPU delivers up to 2x FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to 5x (10x with sparsity) AI training performance versus the Quadro RTX 6000. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU provides 48 GB of GDDR6, expandable to 96 GB via NVLink. A new Error Detection and Replay (EDR) feature on GDDR6X retries failed memory transmissions, helping overclockers identify memory limits before crashes occur.

This paper presents DSCHECKER, an LLM-based approach for detecting and fixing API misuses in data science libraries (e.g., NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib, scikit-learn, seaborn). Such misuses are difficult to detect because correct API behavior often depends on dynamic data properties, which static analysis and traditional pattern-based tools cannot capture. DSCHECKER prompts an LLM with both API directives from documentation and dynamic information about the data being processed, requesting detection results, patches in unified diff format, and explanations.

The authors built DSMISUSES, a dataset of 38 verified misuses plus corresponding correct usages (76 code snippets), and evaluated three LLMs (gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4o, llama-3.1-405b) across five research questions. In an ablation study (RQ1), combining directives and data information (Pfull) yielded the best results for most models; llama with Pfull achieved the highest detection F1-score (61.18%) and fix rate (51.28%). Few-shot prompting (RQ2) produced mixed results, improving gpt-4o but slightly hurting llama. DSCHECKER generalized to deep learning libraries (RQ3), achieving 48% F1 and a 26.67% fix rate on 15 reproduced DL misuses, detecting one case missed by the prior tool LLMAPIDET. In comparison (RQ4), DSCHECKER outperformed LLMAPIDET on DSMISUSES (46.15% vs. 16.49% recall), while LLMAPIDET fixed none of its detections. An agentic variant, DSCHECKERagent (RQ5), which autonomously retrieves documentation and variable information via function calling, achieved a 48.65% F1-score and 39.47% fix rate with gpt-4o, demonstrating practical potential despite reduced performance.

The authors conclude that supplying API directives and dynamic data context substantially improves LLM-based misuse detection and fixing, and identify future work in agentic behavior and LLM-friendly documentation formats.

A study published in Psychological Medicine found that lonely millennials have twice the risk of developing mental health problems like depression and anxiety compared to those connected to others. Researchers from King's College London analysed 2,066 millennial twins in England and Wales, with data taken at age 18. Results showed 7% of participants often felt lonely; loneliness was associated with double the chance of a mental health problem, a 38% increased risk of unemployment, and risky behaviours like smoking and not exercising. Contrary to popular belief, loneliness is greatest among teenagers and young adults, not older people. While social media is often blamed, its effect depends on how it is used. Loneliness may also be contagious: a 2009 study found people are 52% more likely to be lonely if connected to someone who is lonely. Researchers said the findings underscore the importance of early intervention to prevent lonely young adults from remaining trapped in loneliness as they age.

Rice University and the Houston Museum of Natural Science (HMNS) have collaborated on space science education since 1988. For the Heliophysics "Big Year" (2023–2024), the partnership, led by Dr. Carolyn Sumners (HMNS) and Prof. Patricia Reiff (Rice), focused outreach on the October 2023 annular and April 2024 total solar eclipses. Updated eclipse animations were requested by 186 educators in 33 countries and 33 US states, with over 19,000 YouTube views. The fulldome planetarium show "Totality," produced with ePlanetarium, was distributed to 147 planetariums, with a Texas version sent to 53 additional sites, generating over 180,000 documented views. Teacher programs—four Rice courses plus workshops—reached 5,104 educators. The project's eclipse website offered animations, activities (including a solar cup projector), safety guides, and equipment lists; survey feedback indicated each respondent shared information with over 500 people on average. More than 35,000 eclipse glasses and 30,000 viewing cards were distributed, and a Buc-ee's-funded card program put nearly a million viewers into Texas schools. Reiff served as Southwest Regional Coordinator for Citizen CATE 2024, an NSF- and NASA-funded project in which 35 community volunteer teams used identical equipment to record coronal polarization during totality; over 250 participants took part and over 80% of teams successfully observed. The team's space weather forecasting correctly predicted the May 2024 "Gannon Storm." Total documented reach exceeded 1.5 million people, with 5,405 confirmed teacher users.

Rams Coach Sean McVay said Todd Gurley will receive more preseason carries after Gurley matched his 2016 preseason workload with four carries in a 13-10 victory over the Cowboys. Gurley and other starters will get progressive work through the third preseason game against the Chargers, as McVay wants him ready for the Sept. 10 opener against the Colts. Gurley rushed for two yards and caught a 10-yard pass from Jared Goff. McVay noted the challenge of keeping the hard-working Gurley from overdoing it.

An email from Enron's Steven Kean to Joe Hartsoe (March 2, 2001) forwards a collection of news articles on California's energy crisis, noting that the first article refers to a 1946 Nebraska case Kean had mentioned earlier.

The articles report that foes of Gov. Gray Davis' plan to buy utility transmission lines said the plan should be abandoned after FERC Chairman Curtis Hebert disclosed federal approval would be required, calling the purchase "nationalization." Republican legislators favored acquiring other assets, such as stock warrants, instead. Davis cited the 1946 Nebraska case as a possible way to avoid federal approval and met with Energy Secretary Spencer Abraham, who was "open" to the plan but did not endorse it; Davis also cited general support from Alan Greenspan. Southern California Edison agreed in principle to sell its transmission grid for about $2.8 billion, while PG&E resisted; the utilities carried nearly $13 billion in debt.

Experts disputed Davis' claim that the crisis was on the "back side," with the ISO projecting summer shortfalls of thousands of megawatts. The PUC planned to review residential baseline electricity levels, and PUC President Loretta Lynch defended her handling of the crisis and criticized deregulation. Calpine signed long-term contracts with the state Department of Water Resources worth up to $8.3 billion.

A California ISO report concluded that generators overcharged $562 million in December and January and asked FERC to seek refunds; generators denied gouging. Pressure mounted on generators to forgive utility debts, with Kean quoted saying he saw no reason to forgive any. PG&E defaulted on $1.21 billion of $1.44 billion owed, paying creditors about 15 percent, outraging smaller suppliers, and faced lawsuits seeking nearly $3 billion. Critics argued Davis' plan to create a state-run "energy island" would not work and could raise long-term costs, while a former FERC commissioner urged temporary federal price caps and experts compared the situation to the savings-and-loan bailout.

A study using camera traps in a durian orchard on Tioman Island, Malaysia, found that the island flying fox, a large bat previously thought to damage durian flowers, actually pollinates them without causing harm. Led by Sheema Abdul Aziz and published in Ecology and Evolution, the research showed the bats' feeding positively affects durian reproductive success, though smaller bats were previously the only known pollinators. Flying foxes are threatened by hunting and habitat loss and are endangered in Malaysia. Researchers note bats pollinate many economically important crops and warn that human-caused threats affecting bees may also harm bats, on which food security depends.

University of Eastern Finland research following 2,480 men for an average of 22 years found that those with the highest blood linoleic acid levels, the most common omega-6 fatty acid, had a 43 percent reduced risk of premature death from all causes and a lower risk of cardiovascular death, though not cancer death. A weaker similar association was found for arachidonic acid. Linoleic acid is found mainly in vegetable oils, nuts, and seeds.

A hockey goalie reflects on allowing three stick-side goals in a lost game, saying he could have been crisper and better positioned. He notes the game was moved from the larger-capacity Greensboro arena and predicts a wild, charged crowd tomorrow. He stresses scoring first, noting his team overcame a deficit to win in overtime previously, while the opponent took an early lead last game; the first ten minutes are crucial. He describes arriving home late and sleeping separately to avoid waking his son, noting his family understands playoff demands. He calls the matchup of two European goalies special, saying Dominik is among the league's best, and one will make history by winning the cup; they hold the most career wins among European NHL goalies.

In this final lecture, the professor first revisits weak duality for minimizing ||b − Ax||² and its dual problem, showing the duality gap equals ||b − Ax − w||², with equality (optimality) when b = Ax + w, which bridges the primal and dual problems. He poses an open geometry problem: for any point, the sums of squared distances to opposite corners of a rectangle are equal (a² + c² = b² + d²), and asks students for a proof.

The main topic is inverse and ill-posed problems. Examples include finding velocity from noisy position data, where small high-frequency noise greatly affects the derivative; finding Earth's density from seismic wave travel times or from gravity; medical imaging (CT, MRI, PET); determining an obstacle's shape from scattering data; finding coefficients in differential equations; and recovering a matrix from input-output pairs, where noise in the data is the central difficulty. He notes such problems are often integral equations of the first kind (Volterra or Fredholm), which are ill-posed, while adding α times the identity yields second-kind equations.

Using GPS as an example, he explains that four satellites determine position and time, additional satellites enable least squares, and velocity from position differences is ill-posed because dividing by a small Δt amplifies noise; Doppler shift offers a frequency-domain alternative.

He then presents Tikhonov regularization—minimizing ||Ax − b||² + α||x||²—where the error is of size δ/√α, making α = δ^(2/3) the best choice. Iterative methods like conjugate gradients must be stopped early, and finer discretization makes integral equations more ill-posed. A final example from genomics—estimating gene importance from few samples in high dimension—is likewise ill-posed and requires regularization. Student presentations begin Monday.

Opioid misuse is a worldwide epidemic with high overdose and mortality rates. The mu-opioid receptor (MOR) is targeted by drugs of abuse and by medications for opioid use disorder (OUD); respiratory depression is a major risk, and naloxone is used to reverse opioid effects. [11C]carfentanil ([11C]CFN) PET has been used since 1989 to measure MOR availability, but studies have been largely limited to the brain in humans and non-human primates. MOR availability increases with age in some regions, and sex differences have been reported. Long axial field-of-view (LAFOV) PET instruments, such as the PennPET Explorer, enable dynamic whole-body imaging with greater count sensitivity. This study presents the first human whole-body neuroreceptor PET imaging using [11C]CFN, investigating extra-CNS reference regions (aorta and muscle). Healthy English-speaking adults aged 18–45 without psychiatric or substance use disorders were enrolled. [11C]CFN was cyclotron-produced and injected intravenously; 90-minute dynamic PET scans were acquired on the PennPET Explorer following a low-dose CT. Images were analyzed in PMOD using bilateral volumes of interest (amygdala, caudate, putamen, thalamus, ventral tegmentum). Distribution volume ratios were computed with the Logan reference tissue model using the visual cortex as reference, and percent receptor occupancy for naloxone pretreatment was calculated.

Mitch Larkin is considering adding the individual medley to his Commonwealth Games trials program to maintain his hunger for Olympic redemption. He won the 400m IM at the Queensland titles in 4:20.45. The dual backstroke world champion, who underperformed at the Rio Olympics, has switched coaches, settling with Dean Boxall after stints with Michael Bohl and Simon Cusack. Despite a difficult year, Larkin says he is hungrier than ever to return to the top.

On Aug. 21, a total solar eclipse will cross the U.S. from Oregon to South Carolina—the first coast-to-coast total eclipse in 99 years and the first to touch any part of the Lower 48 in 38 years. The path of totality, 60 to 70 miles wide, spans 14 states and will be visible only in the U.S., with darkness lasting up to 2 minutes 44 seconds in southern Illinois. NASA and scientists will study the event using high-altitude balloons, satellites, ground telescopes, and cameras aboard the International Space Station, while festivals and viewing parties are planned along the route. Temperatures are expected to drop 10 to 15 degrees during the roughly 1.5-hour eclipse. With an estimated 200 million people within a day's drive, large crowds are expected, and eye protection is needed except during totality. A partial eclipse will extend through Canada, Central America, and northern South America. Another total eclipse will cross parts of the U.S. in 2024.

Ventura's police chief will review procedures after a homeless man fatally stabbed a restaurant patron. Officers monitored the suspect via cameras instead of responding in person. Jackson faces murder charges.

The lecture, working in an arbitrary Abelian group, introduces additive energy E(A,B), defined as the number of quadruples (a1, a2, b1, b2) with a1 + b1 = a2 + b2, and r_{A,B}(x), the number of representations of x as a + b, so that E(A,B) equals the sum of squares of r_{A,B}. Additive energy is analogous to 4-cycles in graph theory. Trivial bounds are |A|² ≤ E(A) ≤ |A|³. Small doubling implies large energy: if |A + A| ≤ k|A|, then E(A) ≥ |A|³/k, proved via Cauchy-Schwarz. The converse fails—a union of a structured set with unstructured elements has large energy but large doubling—motivating the Balog-Szemerédi-Gowers (BSG) theorem: large energy guarantees a large subset A′ of A with small doubling, up to polynomial losses. A two-set version (large E(A,B) yields large A′ ⊂ A and B′ ⊂ B with small A′ + B′) implies the one-set version via the Ruzsa triangle inequality. Historically, Balog and Szemerédi proved the theorem with weaker bounds; Gowers's proof achieved polynomial bounds, the approach presented here.

The proof proceeds through a graphical version of BSG: if a bipartite graph G between A and B (each of size at most n) has at least n²/k edges and a small restricted sumset A +_G B, then large subsets A′, B′ exist with small unrestricted sumset. This implies the additive version by building G from popular sums, since unpopular sums contribute little to the energy.

Two graph lemmas drive the proof. The path of length 2 lemma, proved by dependent random choice (choosing U as a random neighborhood), gives a large subset U in which most pairs have many common neighbors. The path of length 3 lemma, proved by trimming low-degree vertices and iterating, produces large A′ and B′ such that every pair across them is joined by many paths of length 3. Finally, each sum a + b can be written as x − y + z with x, y, z in the restricted sumset, bounding |A′ + B′| by roughly the cube of the restricted sumset size, which completes the proof. The guiding principle is that partial ("1%") additive structure can be concentrated into large subsets with complete structure.

This IDC White Paper examines the role of high-performance computing (HPC) in manufacturing, based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers at discrete and process manufacturing enterprises with over 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

Industrial enterprises face pressures including geopolitical uncertainty, energy prices, supply chain disruptions, labor shortfalls, and sustainability demands. IT-based simulation, modeling, and data analysis are identified as key enablers of innovation, product quality (cited by 57% of respondents), faster time to market, and cost reduction. Roughly half of surveyed enterprises already use these tools in product development, production planning, and quality management, with deployment expected to reach 90% within two years; 64% plan related investments.

New usage scenarios include virtual prototyping, digital twins, design optimization, and high-performance data analytics (used by 42%). Demand for high-performance calculations is expected to grow sharply, with respondents identifying high demand rising from 8% to nearly half within two years.

Four out of five respondents (81%) consider HPC a game changer for product and process innovation. Most HPC users (87%) prefer external infrastructures such as cloud, 74% use or plan colocation, and only 6% operate on-premises infrastructure. Key challenges include security (72%), investment and licensing costs, energy consumption and sustainability (58%), inadequate computing power, and lack of expertise (42%). The paper concludes that cloud-based and hybrid HPC architectures offer improved scalability, flexibility, and financial advantages over in-house infrastructure, and recommends a "make or buy" evaluation when selecting HPC architectures.

The Canon EOS M6 is an entry-level mirrorless camera replacing the M3, aimed at users seeking dSLR-like photo quality to supplement their phones. It lacks a built-in viewfinder (optional) and differs from the M5 in flash, dial placement, and touchscreen. Shipping April 2017 at $780 for the body, it faces cheaper Sony competitors with similar specs.

Colorado football coach Deion Sanders was scheduled to undergo a medical procedure Tuesday for what he believes is a recurrence of blood clots, with hopes of returning to practice the next day and being on the sideline Saturday against No. 22 Iowa State. Sanders was in pain during the Buffaloes' 35-21 loss at TCU, alternating between sitting and limping and not wearing a shoe on his left foot in the second half. He has a history of blood clot issues, including the amputation of two toes on his left foot in 2021 and a 2023 procedure to remove a clot from his right leg. Longtime NFL cornerback Adam "Pacman" Jones attended Tuesday's media session in support. Sanders, 58, also spent time away from the team over the summer while being treated for an aggressive form of bladder cancer, which involved doctors reconstructing a section of his intestine to function as a bladder.

Scientists at The Rockefeller University, led by A. James Hudspeth shortly before his death in August 2025, kept a sliver of mammalian cochlea alive and functional outside the body for the first time. Using gerbil cochlea tissue in a custom chamber replicating the organ's living environment, they observed the active process of hearing at subcellular detail, including ion channel activity in hair bundles and outer hair cell electromotility. The study confirmed that a Hopf bifurcation—a mechanical instability enabling sound amplification—governs hearing in mammals, as previously documented in bullfrogs, resolving a debate dating to 1998. The researchers say the ex vivo cochlea could enable targeted pharmacological experiments and help develop therapies for hearing loss, for which no drug has been approved to restore sensorineural loss. The findings were published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

An Arizona man, Douglas Haig, 55, was charged with conspiracy to manufacture and sell armor-piercing ammunition without a license, allegedly sold to Stephen Paddock, who killed 58 people and himself in the October 1 Las Vegas shooting. Haig ran an ammunition business and faces up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine. Forensic examiners found reloaded cartridges bearing Haig's fingerprints and matching tool marks in Paddock's hotel room. Hundreds, including 422 gunshot victims, were wounded.

This patent document describes memory arrays comprising vertically-alternating tiers of insulative material and memory cells fabricated over a base substrate. Each memory cell includes a transistor with first and second source/drain regions, a horizontally-oriented channel region, and a gate operatively proximate the channel, along with a capacitor having first and second electrodes separated by a capacitor insulator. The first capacitor electrode is electrically coupled to the first source/drain region. Elevationally-extending sense-line structures electrically couple second source/drain regions of transistors in different tiers, while capacitor-electrode structures couple second capacitor electrodes across tiers. Alternate embodiments include memory cells with a single gate, two vertically-stacked memory cells within a single tier, and gate pairs that are not directly electrically coupled to one another. A staircase region with conductive vias provides access to vertically-stacked gates. An example manufacturing method using successive deposition and selective etching steps is also described.

NVIDIA Ampere adds BF16, TF32, and FP64 to Tensor Cores. BF16 and FP16 match FP32 training results with 16x more throughput. TF32 enables tensor core AI training by default; AMP enables FP16 mixed precision with minimal code changes.

President Biden delivered remarks at a Carpenters Training Center in Pittsburgh, outlining his American Jobs Plan, a roughly $2 trillion investment spread over eight years. He credited the American Rescue Plan with progress on vaccinations (200 million shots within his first 100 days) and economic recovery, citing predictions of 6 percent growth this year. He argued the economy is unfair, noting the wealthiest 1 percent gained $4 trillion in net worth during the pandemic while millions lost jobs. The plan would modernize transportation infrastructure, repair bridges and highways, build 500,000 electric vehicle charging stations, replace all lead pipes, expand affordable high-speed internet access, upgrade the power grid, extend home and community-based care, and increase federal research and development spending. He proposed paying for it by raising the corporate tax rate from 21 to 28 percent, establishing a 21 percent global minimum tax, eliminating deductions for offshoring, and increasing IRS enforcement, while pledging no tax increases on those earning under $400,000. He urged bipartisan cooperation, framing the investment as essential to competing with China and demonstrating that democracies can deliver for their people.
The XPIC clears the IRR bit one clock after the second interrupt acknowledge pulse, causing two interrupts during AEOI. AEOI (ICW4 bit 1) applies only to the master PIC.

The passage describes a patent for an automated storage, retrieval and processing system for objects. Unlike traditional automated storage and retrieval systems (AS/RS), which bring totes to people for manual picking, the invention uses a processing programmable motion device (such as a robotic articulated arm) with an end effector to grasp objects from storage bins and deposit them into destination bins. Storage bins and destination bins are moved to a processing location by gantry retrieval conveyance systems operated by programmable motion devices. A perception unit provides camera or scanning data of bin contents, and the system identifies good grasp locations—preferring points near an object's center of mass, on flat surfaces, or at barcodes—while avoiding bad grasp locations, which are remembered for future reference. Machine learning algorithms use correlations between image features and grasp outcomes to improve grasping over time. The end effector approaches objects along a direction normal to the perceived surface to improve grasp quality, particularly with vacuum end effectors. Embodiments include separate storage and destination sections, a single common gantry system allowing comingled bins, multiple storage and destination sections feeding a common processing section, and multi-floor configurations. Computer systems continuously track the location and identity of each bin and direct object distribution according to a manifest.

A hockey coach said his team generated net traffic, pucks to the net, and rebound chances but could not find a third goal, crediting the players for staying with it. He felt the team started unsettled but settled in quickly and battled back, and that Matt settled in as the game went on. He liked the team's energy, speed, territorial control, scoring chances, and shot clock, while noting the opponent generates offense below the goal line with big bodies and that Burns regularly joins the rush from the blue line. He expressed trust in the leadership to channel emotion properly and said Sid has been a force every game regardless of matchups, which are easier to manage at home. He called Sergei invaluable to the defense corps, said he is not superstitious and relies on routines, and stressed staying in the moment during high-stakes games. He described Geno as an elite player whose recent goal makes the team harder to play against, and Matt as a composed, experienced extension of the coaching staff.

The President, answering a House resolution, states that the 653 troops in Washington (excluding marines) are not a large force and were ordered there as a posse comitatus, subordinate to civil authority, to preserve peace and order around the President-elect's inauguration. Although a select committee found no proof of a hostile secret organization, the House tabled by a large majority a resolution calling for the troops' removal, which he cites as a sufficient reason not to withdraw them. He defends the precautionary measure as necessary, amid widespread alarm, to protect public property, the Government archives, and the inauguration.

The passage examines bear markets, focusing on the 2000–2003 downturn following the dot-com bubble. A bear market is commonly regarded as a decline of 20% or more, though no official rule exists; it is longer and steeper than a correction. Volatility rises sharply during bear markets, benefiting traders—both long and short strategies tend to perform better when prices fall. Bear markets are shorter than bull markets, with stocks spending roughly 80% of the time in bull markets, but recoveries take far longer: the S&P 500 fell 45% during 2000–2003 and did not set a new high until late 2006, while the Nasdaq dropped over 80% and took 15 years to recover. Investors should welcome bear markets as opportunities to buy at lower prices, and traders benefit from increased volatility. An example RSI-based mean-reversion strategy on QQQ produced positive results during the dot-com recession, the GFC, and Covid-19. Bear markets are a natural part of market cycles that clean out economic excesses.

The Louisiana Supreme Court denied the writ as untimely and held that relator has exhausted state post-conviction relief, since successive applications are permitted only under narrow exceptions; the district court was ordered to record a minute entry.

This study investigates thermal transport in β-Ga₂O₃, an ultra-wide bandgap semiconductor with favorable electronic and mechanical properties but low thermal conductivity (10–27 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹), under uniform strain (ε) and strain gradients (η). Using first-principles-based neuroevolution potentials (NEP) combined with the phonon Boltzmann transport equation, the authors examine bulk material, 10-nm and 100-nm films, and nanowires at 300 K.

The NEP model, trained via active learning on 649 DFT-derived configurations, accurately reproduces energies, forces, and phonon dispersions, with calculated thermal conductivities (ka: 10.4, kb: 20.3, kc: 15.4 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 300 K) agreeing with experimental data.

Under uniform strain, k modulation is anisotropic and substantial: each component is most sensitive to strain along its own axis, with b-axis strains producing the largest effects (e.g., εb alters kb by −26.8%/+22.9% in 10-nm films). Heat capacity and velocity remain largely invariant, and k changes correlate strongly with intrinsic phonon lifetime (CCC = 0.8802), indicating modulation occurs primarily through three-phonon scattering.

Strain gradients suppress k more strongly than equivalent uniform strains in thin films. A uniaxial η of 0.6%/nm reduces ka, kb, and kc by 31.8%, 35.3%, and 36.6% in 10-nm films, exceeding reductions from uniform εb of 3%. Biaxial gradients cause reductions up to 43.3%, approximately 1.5 times stronger than corresponding uniform biaxial strain, surpassing benchmark materials including silicon and BAs. Gradient-induced scattering dominates for phonons below 10 THz, driven by symmetry breaking that broadens phonon spectra, activates previously forbidden scattering channels, and expands the scattering phase space.

Notably, unlike uniform strain, which alters thermal anisotropy ratios by ~25%, strain gradients reduce k while leaving anisotropy nearly unchanged. The authors conclude that strain gradients must be explicitly treated in β-Ga₂O₃ device thermal modeling and may enable targeted thermal isolation in flexible electronics.

Startup founders face a stressful first fundraising round, but understanding what investors seek helps create an attractive offering. Key focus areas include: return on investment—deciding how much equity to offer, as investors may have a minimum stake in mind, seek rights to invest further, or offer mentoring and industry contacts; the founder and team—confidence, articulateness, openness to advice, an experienced team, and demonstrated market traction such as revenue or customer satisfaction; market opportunities—some investors specialise in certain industries or emerging markets, and gaps or disruptive ideas can attract them; and strategy—a detailed business plan with accurate figures, research on competition, and understanding of financial projections and the consequences of missing them.
