Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on July 20, 2017, announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2017. The press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration, and Chief Accounting Officer.

Hong Kong stocks ended slightly higher as property weakness offset gains in shipping firms and Tencent. Tencent rose 0.6 percent after buying a 5 percent Tesla stake. Banking stocks rose on modest profit growth, while real estate dipped amid new property curbs and Moody's warnings.

UCLA researchers Heather Christofk and William Lowry discovered a method to activate hair follicle stem cells to promote hair growth, potentially leading to new drugs for baldness and alopecia. Published in Nature Cell Biology, the study found that hair follicle stem cell metabolism differs from other skin cells. These stem cells process glucose into pyruvate, which either enters mitochondria or converts to lactate. In mice, genetically blocking lactate production prevented stem cell activation, while increasing lactate accelerated hair growth. The team identified two drugs applied to mouse skin: RCGD423, which activates the JAK-Stat signaling pathway to increase lactate, and UK5099, which blocks pyruvate from entering mitochondria, forcing lactate production. Both promoted hair growth in mice. Provisional patents have been filed, but the drugs remain untested in humans and unapproved by the FDA.

Colgate-Palmolive (CL) stock's decline has paused, and Wall Street has turned bullish as profit growth returns. Argus upgraded the stock with a $72 price target, roughly 12% above current levels, and the forward PE now sits below 20, near financial-crisis-era levels. Analysts expect revenue growth over the next two fiscal years and mid-to-high single-digit profit growth for three years. CL is a dividend aristocrat, having raised its dividend annually since 1964, with a yield of about 2.6%. However, the author remains cautious: Colgate's products are commoditized, its shelf-space advantage has eroded due to e-commerce, and smaller niche competitors now threaten growth. Despite stability and loyal customers, the author considers 20 times earnings too high for a no-moat business.

The passage, from the MSPM0C1105/MSPM0C1106 datasheet (SLASFJ6A, revised September 2025), describes the debug subsystem (DEBUGSS), which interfaces the ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) two-wire interface to on-chip debug functions, provides a mailbox (DSSM) for SWD communication with boot ROM and software, and supports security features such as SWD lockout and password-authenticated debugging. A memory-mapped FACTORY region supplies read-only device identification (DEVICEID and USERID registers) and factory trim data. The typical application section recommends 10µF and 0.1µF decoupling capacitors on VDD/VSS, a 47kΩ pullup with 1000pF capacitor on NRST, external crystal bypass capacitors, and pullups for 5V-tolerant open-drain IOs. Device nomenclature distinguishes experimental (X) devices from fully qualified production (MSP) devices. Development tools include LaunchPad, TI Resource Explorer, SysConfig, MSP Academy, GUI Composer, and the TI Arm-Clang compiler. The revision history notes changes including removal of the DGS32 package and addition of the DEBUGSS section. The remainder covers package mechanical drawings, orderable information, ESD handling precautions, and TI's standard legal disclaimers.
Officials raised the AJC Peachtree Road Race alert to Code Red - Dangerous, urging runners to slow down and follow instructions. The 49th annual race forecasts a dry morning in the upper 80s.

European Commission President Jean-Claude Juncker said nobody outside India calls its 5.7% GDP growth a slowdown, noting it far exceeds Europe's 2%. Amid domestic criticism over demonetisation and GST, World Bank chief Jim Yong Kim termed the slowdown a temporary "aberration," while BJP leader Yashwant Sinha called the economy a "mess."

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture reviews digital communication as communication with a binary interface between source coding and channel coding, justified by standardization (which lowers chip development costs), layering (which simplifies conceptualization), and no loss of performance, as Shannon proved. Source coding is layered into sampling or expansion of waveforms into analog sequences, quantization (which converts an uncountable set of values into a finite one, unavoidably introducing distortion), and discrete coding. The lecture assumes an error-free binary channel and focuses on discrete source coding.

The objective of discrete source coding is to map sequences of symbols into binary sequences with unique decodability. Fixed-length codes assign each of m symbols an l-bit string, where l is the ceiling of log2 m; only alphabet size matters, since symbols have no inherent meaning, and synchronization is assumed. ASCII (256 symbols, 8 bits) serves as an example. Generalized fixed-length codes encode blocks of n symbols, achieving approximately log2 m bits per symbol as n grows; for equally likely symbols, nothing can perform better.

Variable-length codes assign shorter codewords to probable symbols, as motivated by Morse code. Codewords are concatenated without separators, buffering handles the resulting rate mismatch, and unique decodability is required, with both encoder and decoder knowing the code. Prefix-free codes, in which no codeword is a prefix of another, can be represented as binary trees; full trees have no empty leaves. Prefix-free codes are uniquely decodable and instantaneously decodable.

The Kraft inequality states that codeword lengths of a prefix-free code must satisfy the sum of 2 to the minus length ≤ 1; this condition is necessary and sufficient for such codes to exist, with equality holding if and only if the code is full. The proof associates codewords with base-2 expansion intervals. Unique decodability is formally defined as distinct source strings mapping to distinct codeword concatenations, and all uniquely decodable codes also satisfy the Kraft inequality, though a proof is deferred.

Finally, discrete memoryless sources are introduced: sources producing independent, identically distributed symbols from a finite alphabet. This simplifying assumption provides a foundation for later study of more complex sources such as English text, and independent letters represent, in some sense, a worst case.

The shallow cross concept pairs a basic route and shallow drag route run from opposite directions, designed to put defenders—particularly linebackers—in conflict and provide answers against both man and zone coverage. It stresses LB-level players over the middle, enables quick throws against blitz, and allows a skilled TE to find voids. It performs well against man coverage, Tampa 2, and Cover 4, but struggles against Cover 3, which has numbers in the flat/hook areas. Route assignments include the TE on a basic route at 10-12 yards, the slot on a shallow drag at 3-4 yards, plus a go route and post route downfield. The QB reads downfield routes first, transitioning quickly to the drag/basic combination against pressure, following a progression of Post, Drag, Basic, and RB checkdown. Variations include Bunch X Shallow Cross and Empty Shallow Cross Post-Wheel.

This MIT lecture, the first of two sessions on the economics of green buildings, focuses on making a business case for green buildings. Recapping the triple bottom line (planet, people, profit), the instructor emphasizes that since over 80% of buildings are supplied by the private sector, developers must be incentivized. A case study of Millennium Partners shows developers are rational actors whose sustainability priorities shift with market context: the San Francisco Millennium Tower (2008) ignored sustainability and suffered structural failures and lawsuits; Boston's Millennium Place (2013) was pitched via job creation to obtain permits; Millennium Tower Boston (2017) emphasized health and wellness; and the ongoing Winthrop Center markets sustainability with passive house and LEED Platinum certifications. The lecture then examines market mechanisms among three stakeholders—tenants, owners, and developers—linked in a chain where tenant willingness to pay drives owner rent revenue and developer sale prices. A pro forma analysis shows green buildings can raise NPV through higher rents, lower vacancy, lower operating costs, and lower discount rates. Empirical studies indicate average rent premiums of about 6% and sales price premiums of about 7.6%, though with wide ranges; construction cost premiums range from 0% to 12.5% for new buildings and are declining over time. Finally, the lecture introduces market failures—information asymmetry, split incentives, and externalities—focusing on information asymmetry: green buildings are experience goods, enabling greenwashing. China's uncertified market illustrated adverse selection, crowding out quality developers; certification systems like LEED help solve this problem.

WIS News 10 will air "Total Eclipse Columbia" at 7:30 p.m., covering safety and science ahead of the Aug. 21 total solar eclipse. Columbia lies in the path of totality, where the moon will fully cover the sun.

The Brea Police Department has added an all-electric Polaris Gem Global Electric Motorcar, costing about $21,000 and funded by Air Quality Management District money, to patrol The Tracks at Brea trail and the downtown entertainment district. In use for about three weeks, it has a 25 mph top speed and 98-mile battery range.

This email compiles news articles from October 4, 2001, concerning Enron. The main story is BG Group's agreement to purchase Enron's offshore Indian oil and gas assets for $388 million, including a 30% stake in the Tapti gas field and Panna/Mukta oil and gas fields, plus a 62.64% interest in the CB-OS/1 exploration license. Analysts considered the price a bargain at roughly $2.30 per barrel of oil equivalent for reserves exceeding 170 million barrels. The deal is conditional on BG obtaining operatorship of the fields, which ONGC, a 40% partner, is contesting. Separately, Enron is attempting to exit the Dabhol Power Project, India's largest private power plant, amid payment disputes with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board, and its Indian unit defaulted on a $24 million interest payment to lenders. Other articles cover a technology stock rally led by Cisco, a settlement allowing Southern California Edison to repay debt through continued high customer rates, and the appointment of former Enron executive Thomas White as the Defense Department's homeland security liaison.

Learning assessment is well established for credit-bearing higher education courses but has received little attention in noncredit continuing education—organized educational activities that do not lead to a degree or credential, such as licensure-related professional education, career-focused skill building, and personal enrichment. Satisfaction surveys remain common in these formats, while direct learning assessments are rare, possibly because courses are short, taught by field experts, serve learners with varied motivations, and institutions invest limited resources in them. The authors argue that assessment can guide curriculum, pedagogy, and improvement, and draw on their experience at a research-based public institution to describe three approaches. First, learning outcome statements should be clear, measurable, realistic in number relative to course length, matched to learners' prior knowledge (e.g., using Bloom's revised taxonomy), and follow SMART criteria, with instructor collaboration and learner feedback where feasible. Second, learning outcome-focused survey questions, though subjective self-reports, can be a first step; retrospective pre-post surveys suit short courses. Third, direct assessment—expert evaluation of learner products or performances—can include quiz-type questions embedded in end-of-course surveys for short courses and observed practice activities or products for medium-duration courses. Recommendations include using simple scoring (e.g., a 2-point scale), consulting measurement experts for validity and reliability, ensuring fairness within time constraints, and designing products that benefit learners beyond the course. The authors conclude that learning outcome assessment in noncredit continuing education is feasible and worthwhile, noting that digital credentials can motivate learners and that assessment results have supported course improvement, personnel decisions, and resource requests.

The lecture concludes the study of Markov chains with a review of eigenvalues and eigenvectors, followed by an introduction to dynamic programming. For a block upper-triangular transition matrix, the determinant factors into the product of the determinants of the transient and recurrent submatrices, so the eigenvalues of P are the union of the eigenvalues of its transient and recurrent parts. Left eigenvectors of the recurrent submatrix extend to eigenvectors of the full matrix by prepending zeros. The lecture then introduces rewards associated with states, deriving expected aggregate rewards over n steps; for ergodic unit chains, the gain per step converges to a steady-state value independent of the starting state. First passage time to a given state is computed by modifying the chain so the target state becomes a trapping state with zero reward, then solving a set of linear equations. Finally, dynamic programming is introduced: a decision maker at each step chooses an alternative that determines both the immediate reward and the transition probabilities to the next state. Bellman's algorithm solves the one-step problem first and works backward, showing that the optimal decision at each step depends only on the current state and the number of steps remaining.

The power play is a favorite run play among offensive line coaches, featuring a gap scheme with a pulling backside guard, a kickout block, and multiple back blocks that create angles at the point of attack. It can be run from nearly any personnel group or formation. Its main strength is outnumbering the defense with double teams, a kickout, and a pulling guard concentrated at the point of attack, allowing smaller lines to succeed through leverage; double teams can be taught as vertical combinations for powerful lines or horizontal ones for undersized lines. Its biggest weakness is backside pursuit and penetration through the gap left by the pulling guard, particularly against odd fronts where the Center's "point call" is critical. The passage details blocking assignments against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts. Variations include the Diamond Fullhouse, where the F arcs to the perimeter, and the Gun Same-Side Power RPO, a 1-back version with a Tight End blocking the end man.

This patent application, a continuation of PCT/CN2020/108808 claiming priority to a Chinese patent application, relates to communication technology, specifically information sending/reception methods, apparatuses, communication nodes, and storage media. In 5G millimeter wave communication, maximum power exposure (MPE) to the human body requires different maximum sending power backoff under different uplink beams, but base stations cannot effectively realize maximum power reduction (MPR) under different beams through scheduling; the user equipment (UE) passively reduces sending power, degrading uplink performance. The application provides that a first communication node sends report information to a second communication node, where the report information includes at least one of first type power parameter information (e.g., maximum power reduction, remaining energy value, accumulated energy value, uplink duty cycle information, alert identification information, power backoff, or power headroom) or uplink channel state information (e.g., reference signal information, antenna group information, uplink path loss value, quasi co-location information, or uplink additional corrected value). The second communication node receives the report and schedules the first communication node, enabling determination of maximum power reduction and reducing MPE to the human body. Report sending may be triggered by thresholds, parameter variations, or timer overflow, and reports may be periodic, semi-persistent, or aperiodic. The MPR may be beam-specific or panel-specific, and virtual power headroom reporting may include a reference signal index or spatial relation index. Embodiments also cover corresponding sending/reception apparatuses, a first communication node (e.g., a UE), a second communication node (e.g., a base station), and a storage medium.

Bill Purswell appealed his conviction for transporting intoxicating liquor, with a one-year penitentiary sentence, from the District Court of Liberty County. Officers Hightower and Anderson, concealed in a field at McElvain's home during a social gathering, observed the appellant carrying a jug found to contain whiskey and arrested him; the jug and its contents were admitted into evidence. The court held that the right to complain of an illegal search is personal to the owner or possessor of the premises searched, which belonged to McElvain, not the appellant. The warrantless arrest was lawful because the felony was committed in the officers' presence, and the search was referable to probable cause. A general objection to the court's charge was insufficient, as exceptions must be specific. Finding no error, the judgment was affirmed. On rehearing, the court held that an unsupported affidavit alleging the jury considered the appellant's failure to testify did not show jury misconduct, and it was presumed the evidence heard justified overruling the motion for new trial. The motion for rehearing was overruled.

The court affirmed an order denying Dairylea Cooperative's application to quash a subpoena duces tecum issued by the New York Attorney-General for corporate records returnable before a Grand Jury. It held that an appeal lay from the order, rejecting the State's cited authorities as no longer controlling. On the merits, it found the subpoena authorized under subdivision 3 of section 63 of the Executive Law, agreeing that a request had been made by the Commissioner of Agriculture and Markets.

The passage is an email chain in which Enron employees forward a November 2001 Texas Monthly article by Mimi Swartz titled "How Enron Blew It." The article recounts Enron's transformation from a pipeline company in 1985 into a trading colossus, driven largely by Jeff Skilling, who joined from McKinsey in 1990 after proposing the "Gas Bank" concept to CEO Ken Lay. Skilling built an aggressive culture that recruited top graduates with high salaries and uncapped bonuses, enforced through a harsh Performance Review Committee ("rank and yank") that replaced 15 percent of the workforce annually. Enron expanded into electricity, broadband, and online trading, using mark-to-market accounting on an unprecedented scale and booking profits up-front. Over time, the culture turned inward, treating employees as commodities. Rebecca Mark's troubled power plant in India and the failed Azurix water venture preceded Skilling's rise to CEO in February 2001. Trouble followed quickly: criticism over California's energy crisis, the collapse of the telecom division, and analysts questioning Enron's accounting drove the stock from a high of $80 to around $35. Skilling resigned abruptly after six months as CEO, and Ken Lay returned, promising a kinder culture. In an interview, Skilling defends his departure, noting that 90 percent of his net worth was in Enron stock.

Firefly Aerospace shares sank nearly 21% after its Alpha Flight 7 rocket exploded during a first-stage test flight at its Briggs, Texas facility on Monday. The company said proper safety protocols were followed and all personnel were safe, and it is assessing the impact to its stage test stand. Firefly debuted on the Nasdaq last month, raising $868 million at a $6.3 billion valuation, but shares have since pulled back more than 50%. The company, which makes rockets, space tugs and lunar landers, competes with SpaceX for NASA deals; its sixth Alpha rocket failed in April.

South Dakota's Board of Regents, without a vote, directed staff and officials from its two largest universities to prepare a closure plan for Pierre's Capital University Center, due at the Oct. 3-5 meeting.

The passage argues that the Arctic must be understood as a complex, interconnected system in which environmental, geopolitical, economic, and sociocultural factors interact and produce cascading effects, as illustrated by the Nome port expansion project. It contends that traditional linear, reductionist educational approaches are insufficient for Arctic security challenges and advocates integrating systems thinking into security education. Key systems thinking principles include seeing the whole rather than individual parts, recognizing patterns and connections, and identifying leverage points where small interventions can produce significant change. The paper proposes a Systems Thinking Education Model with three components: core principles (interdisciplinary learning and interconnected analysis), leverage points (shifting mental models, improving information flows, governance structures, behavioral and operational shifts, and technological advancements), and learning and assessment strategies (scenario-based problem-solving, reflective analysis, and competency-based metrics). Recommended instructional methods include concept mapping, simulations and wargaming, role-playing with stakeholders, and interactive case studies. The framework is presented as well-suited to online graduate education through asynchronous modules, digital simulations, and cross-disciplinary collaboration. The conclusion emphasizes that systems thinking is a practical necessity for preparing security professionals to anticipate unintended consequences, bridge theory and operational reality, and develop sustainable, forward-looking Arctic security strategies.

The passage is a patent disclosure concerning improved transmitting devices and methods for radio resource selection and sensing in wireless communication systems. The background section covers LTE architecture (eNodeB, MME, SGW functions), component carrier structure, carrier aggregation in LTE-Advanced supporting bandwidths up to 100 MHz, protocol layers (MAC, RLC, PDCP, RRC, Physical), L1/L2 control signaling via PDCCH, and semi-persistent scheduling. It further describes LTE Device-to-Device (D2D) Proximity Services (ProSe), including direct discovery and one-to-one communication over the PC5 (sidelink) interface, with two resource allocation modes: Mode 1 (eNB-scheduled) and Mode 2 (UE-autonomous selection from configured resource pools). The passage also discusses V2X services (V2V, V2P, V2I, V2N) for vehicular communication, including periodic Cooperative Awareness Messages (CAMs) and event-triggered DENMs. 3GPP agreed to support sensing mechanisms with semi-persistent transmissions for V2X sidelink, where UEs indicate resource reservations in scheduling assignments so other UEs can avoid reserved resources. The disclosed invention provides an improved UE-autonomous radio resource allocation procedure: a transmitting device continuously performs resource sensing (monitoring scheduling assignments and optionally measuring received signal energy), and when data becomes available, selects resources within a transmission window based on sensing results from a preceding sensing window. The selection distinguishes primary subframes (fully sensed) from secondary subframes (where sensing was missed due to half-duplex operation), preferring primary subframes and ranking candidates by time delay and predicted energy. A preemption procedure is described for cases where no candidates are available. Similar procedures apply to scheduling assignment transmissions, which may indicate reserved resources for future transmissions.

On October 29, 2001, Enron's shares fell to multi-year lows after Moody's Investors Service downgraded its senior unsecured debt from Baa1 to Baa2—two notches above junk status—and warned of possible further downgrades, including its commercial paper rating. The downgrade followed Enron's write-downs and $1.2 billion in equity charges tied to previously undisclosed partnerships run by former CFO Andrew Fastow, which the Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating for possible conflicts of interest. The stock lost more than half its value in two weeks, erasing over $14 billion in market capitalization.

Enron said it was negotiating a new credit line of $1–2 billion with banks to restore investor confidence, after drawing about $3 billion from existing credit lines the prior week to repay commercial paper. Analysts characterized the drawdowns as an act of desperation and predicted lenders would demand harsher terms, including collateral.

European energy firms grew wary of trading with Enron, with several large companies freezing dealings pending new credit arrangements. Separately, Moody's reported that overall U.S. corporate credit quality was expected to worsen. At least five shareholder class-action lawsuits were filed against Enron, naming Chairman Ken Lay, former CEO Jeff Skilling, and Fastow, focusing on hedging transactions with the LJM partnerships. Analysts also questioned Enron's asset-light strategy and its financial disclosure practices.

Anecdotal evidence indicates goals are scored at higher rates during certain five-minute segments of soccer matches: the start of each half, after a goal or a saved/missed penalty kick, after a bad foul or dangerous play, before halftime, at the end of the match, and during extra time. Coaches should prepare players for these periods. The causes are psychological, including excitement, lack of mental readiness, complacency, anger after conceding, and urgency near the end of halves. The most important factor is the let-down after a goal; coaches commonly remind players, "No letdown!"

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture by Lorna Gibson introduces a course on cellular solids—porous materials with less than 30% solid volume. The course covers honeycombs (two-dimensional prismatic cells), foams (three-dimensional polyhedral cells), medical materials such as trabecular bone and tissue engineering scaffolds, and natural cellular materials like wood, cork, and bamboo. Students complete open-ended pair projects; past examples include negative Poisson's ratio honeycombs, elephant skull porosity and sound transmission, and food foams such as bread. The course will develop equations for mechanical properties like stiffness and strength, then apply them to bone, scaffolds, energy absorption, and sandwich panels. Cellular materials are useful for low weight, energy absorption at low stress, thermal insulation, and large surface area for catalyst carriers. The lecture also covers processing methods: honeycombs are made by expansion, corrugation, extrusion (for ceramics), rapid prototyping, casting, and bio-carbon templates, in which wood is pyrolyzed and can be infiltrated with silicon to form silicon carbide replicas. Polymer foams are made via mechanical stirring or physical and chemical blowing agents; syntactic foams bond hollow spheres with resin, and structural foams form dense skins like sandwich panels. Metal foams, mostly aluminum, are produced by gas stirring with silicon carbide powder, titanium hydride decomposition, replicating open-cell polymer foams, vapor deposition, entrapped gas expansion, bonding hollow spheres, and fugitive phase techniques using salt. The lecture concludes with the professor's background in civil engineering, her PhD at Cambridge, and her path to MIT.

Job hunting can be emotionally challenging, especially for newcomers to Canada. RBC's Ivy Chiu recommends building a network before starting a job search. Tips include: starting the search before arriving using job sites, finding free career workshops such as ACCES Employment in Toronto, pursuing internships and volunteer opportunities to gain experience, verifying whether credentials need updating, and improving English or French proficiency through language courses. More advice is available at rbc.com/newcomers.

Treetops, purpose-built in 1992 near Keynsham town centre, provides accommodation for elderly people with dementia across three family-sized units. Each resident has a named carer, families contribute to care planning, and staff organise varied activities.

The Q3 2025 credit commentary states that anticipated challenges have arrived, highlighted by the government shutdown. The Fed lowered short-term interest rates in September, citing slowing job growth and mixed inflation readings. Many municipalities received upgrades for better-funded reserves, which can indicate better budgeting or growth in population or economic activity. Muni credit quality may begin to turn this quarter, though munis remain an extremely safe asset class viewed as a flight-to-quality product. The passage also includes a biography of David Kotok and lists related articles and municipal bond ETFs.

The Supreme Court debated whether Delaware's procedures limiting medical malpractice litigation can apply in federal court. Justice Kagan argued the Delaware requirements conflict with the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure's notice pleading system, effectively forcing plaintiffs to prove their case before it begins. Justice Jackson noted Delaware requires an affidavit to initiate a malpractice suit, while federal law requires only filing a complaint. Justice Sotomayor cited conflicts over deadlines for serving an answer. Frederick Yarger, representing the defendants—a doctor and a hospital—argued federal courts need not ignore an entire state statute if part of it conflicts with a federal rule. Justice Gorsuch questioned this approach, asking what authority federal courts have to rewrite state law. Chief Justice Roberts and Justices Thomas and Alito said little, leaving the outcome unclear, though several justices appear likely to reject Delaware's procedures.

Trump's first meeting with Trudeau signaled a positive view of Canada-US trade, calling problems "much less severe" than Mexico's; USD/CAD fell to 1.3060. The pound outperformed while the euro lagged. A Premium short EURUSD closed with a 130-pip gain. Upcoming events include Yellen's testimony, China's January CPI forecast at 2.4%, and a Kuroda speech amid yield curve control speculation.

CoachingAmericanSoccer.com presents "An American Soccer Player's Creed," a set of principles for players' conduct and tactical philosophy. The creed emphasizes ball awareness, communication with teammates and coaches, avoiding fouls and retaliation, learning from mistakes, playing as part of a team, knowing the Laws of the Game, and demonstrating fair play and sportsmanship on and off the field. It is copyrighted by John C. Harves.

The DAWN-PLASMA study was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 proof-of-concept multicenter trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of convalescent plasma in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Participants were randomized 2:1 to standard of care plus convalescent plasma versus standard of care alone. The primary endpoint was the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Patients received 800–1000 mL of plasma in four doses, with plasma required to have neutralizing antibody titers of at least 1/160. Inclusion criteria included confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and evidence of lower respiratory involvement; exclusion criteria included mechanical ventilation at randomization, prior grade 3 allergic reaction to fresh frozen plasma, and recent anti-CD20 antibody treatment. The study was conducted per the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP guidelines with IEC approval. Six patients were substituted before the intervention; no patients were lost to follow-up. The trial statistician remained blinded until database lock. Data were captured in RedCap at the Clinical Trial Center, UZ Leuven. No quality audits were performed and no QTLs were predefined. The statistical analysis plan was finalized on 27 October 2020.

This study evaluates the usability of e-business websites in Saudi Arabia, an emerging online market where 58% of residents have shopped online and sales are projected to reach $13.9 billion by 2021. Noting a lack of prior research on Saudi business website usability, the authors conducted a cross-sectional study in which two groups of students trained in user interface evaluation (26 and 39 participants) assessed eight popular websites—four retail and four booking sites—after 30 minutes of interaction each, using a Likert-scale questionnaire covering navigation, design, and content. Findings, validated through ANOVA and Cronbach's Alpha (0.66 for group 1, 0.79 for group 2), showed generally positive ratings but revealed weaknesses including disappearing menus, orphan pages, poor sitemap links, weak within-page navigation, inconsistent Arabic-English interfaces, inconsistent font sizes and layouts, unlabeled icons, missing contact information, absent last-update dates, and alphabetical ordering issues. Results from both groups converged despite examining different website types. The authors recommend cognitive evaluation, ethnographic studies, participatory and user-centered design, and involvement of technical writers to improve Saudi e-business portals. A noted limitation is the small sample size of evaluators and websites, which limits generalizability. Improving usability is expected to support customer acquisition, retention, and revenue, though long-term studies are needed to quantitatively measure usability's impact on customer behavior.

A senior Bank of Canada official, senior deputy governor Carolyn Wilkins, told a parliamentary committee she expects Canada's household debt-to-disposable income ratio to gradually stabilize and wind down, as credit growth slows while labour income rises. The ratio stood at 170.4 per cent in late 2017, slightly below its 170.5 per cent peak. Governor Stephen Poloz said high debt loads have made households 50 per cent more sensitive to interest rate movements.

The speaker says his team must battle to reach the net, describes the opposing goalie as big and playing deep, and says the team regrouped after a loss and is ready for tonight, aiming to score first.

In a May 6, 1980 Wall Street Journal interview, Ronald Reagan questioned the President's remarks following a failed mission, asking whether he was washing his hands of it. Asked about Iran potentially moving into the Soviet camp, Reagan noted confusion about Khomeini's stance but acknowledged Soviet influence through border propaganda broadcasts and Iran's Communist Party. He stated that such a shift would be one of the most serious threats to the Middle East and U.S. security. The interview also covered Cuba, defense spending, and U.S. allies. On July 17, 1980, Reagan accepted the Republican presidential nomination at the convention in Detroit, delivering a speech emphasizing peace and security, pledging to protect the American people, and asserting that war comes when the forces of freedom are weak. In another address, Reagan argued that peace is not preserved by weakness and defended military preparedness.

This passage explains strategies for attacking basketball pressure presses. It emphasizes being prepared for pressing situations, analyzing the press type to exploit weaknesses, and advancing the ball quickly through teamwork rather than relying on a single point guard. Key offensive fundamentals include using short, crisp passes, working the ball into the middle, using the dribble sparingly, creating leads as receivers, and attacking outnumbered situations. Attacking with five players is considered more effective than clearing out, and formations like the 2-1-2 alignment are recommended over set plays. After rebounds or made shots, the first outlet look should be long, followed by short and middle options. Guidelines include spreading the floor, employing a slow-to-quick tempo, taking care of the ball, and avoiding one-handed passes, bounce passes, picking up the dribble, and telegraphing passes. Successful execution requires designated player roles and consistently running the press break after made shots to eliminate surprise. Coaches should teach using the Whole-Part-Whole method with progressive breakdown drills, practicing at game speed against strong defense. Coaching objectives focus on developing poise, confidence, passing ability, and the capacity to attack double teams and flow into early offense. Game strategies include playing disruptive defense, scouting opponents, and transitioning smoothly from push to flow to continuity. The passage concludes by noting that immediate defensive pressure can disrupt fast breaks and catch teams off guard, resulting in steals and easy baskets.

Blair school district voters narrowly rejected a $250,000 transportation bond issue, drawing 111 for and 80 against (58.76 percent), below the required 60 percent. It would have bought three 72-passenger buses to replace leased ones. Area municipal and school board elections were also held.

This study demonstrates coherent control of the three nearest-neighbor ¹⁵N nuclear spins adjacent to negatively charged boron vacancy (V_B⁻) centers in isotopically enriched h¹⁰B¹⁵N crystals using electron-nuclear double resonance (ENDOR). While NV centers in diamond dominate quantum sensing, V_B⁻ defects in hBN remain effective near surfaces, making them suitable for integration with target systems. The researchers selectively addressed the four hyperfine states of the three spin-1/2 nitrogen nuclei, enabled by electron-nuclear hyperfine coupling that induces state-dependent mixing and lifts transition degeneracies. This mixing enhanced the nuclear g-factor, increasing the Rabi frequency by a factor of approximately 116 compared to isolated ¹⁵N nuclear spins. Nuclear Rabi coherence times exceeded 10 µs (~12 µs), roughly two orders of magnitude longer than the electron spin T₂. ENDOR linewidths as narrow as 1.2 MHz were observed, and transition energies showed magnetic-field dependence consistent with theory; fitting required a 0.947 isotropic scaling of published theoretical hyperfine tensors. Unexpectedly, optical pumping caused rapid nuclear spin depolarization, with complete thermalization within ~1 µs, tentatively attributed to the triplet excited ³E″ state. The results establish the strongly coupled nuclear spins as a controllable quantum resource with potential for quantum memories and enhanced sensing in hBN-based devices.

The Supreme Court of Pennsylvania affirmed a Commonwealth Court ruling that the Nonpublic Elementary and Secondary Education Act (Act 109) is constitutional and enforceable as applied to nonsectarian nonpublic schools. The case arose after the Department of Education denied the First School's 1974 aid application, contending that Act 109 was invalidated in its entirety by Lemon v. Kurtzman, was not severable, had been impliedly repealed by later legislation, and could not be constitutionally administered. The court rejected each argument. It concluded that Lemon held Act 109 unconstitutional only as applied to sectarian schools, because the excessive entanglement found there stemmed from state involvement with religious institutions, and the injunction in Lemon II covered only sectarian schools. The court held the Act severable, relying on the state's policy favoring severability, the Act's own severability clause, and the Act's purpose of enhancing secular education, distinguishing Sloan v. Lemon and Meek v. Pittenger as severability is a question of state law. Subsequent statutes (Acts 89, 90, and the textbook provisions of Act 195) did not impliedly repeal Act 109, as they were not irreconcilable with it and did not cover its entire subject matter. Finally, determining whether a school is sectarian or nonsectarian would not create excessive entanglement, being comparable to tax-exempt status determinations. Justice Eagen dissented.

With Jake Browning struggling for consistency, speculation has emerged about the Bengals potentially trading for former Cincinnati quarterback Andy Dalton, now with the Panthers. Dalton is familiar with coach Zac Taylor's offense from 2019, though Taylor benched him on his birthday. Signed through 2026, Dalton threw for 319 yards and three touchdowns in a 2024 win over the Raiders. Browning has thrown for 506 yards, three touchdowns, and five interceptions through three games.

Tesla, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2018. The company designs, manufactures and sells electric vehicles and solar energy generation and storage products, operating in two segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. Total revenues were $3.41 billion for Q1 2018, up from $2.70 billion in Q1 2017. Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $709.6 million ($4.19 per share), compared to $330.3 million ($2.04 per share) in the prior-year quarter. Total assets were $27.27 billion and total debt was $10.47 billion as of March 31, 2018, with cash and cash equivalents of $2.67 billion. On January 1, 2018, Tesla adopted the new revenue standard (ASC 606) using the modified retrospective method, changing the timing of revenue recognition for certain vehicle sales with resale value guarantees from operating leases to sales with a right of return, decreasing beginning accumulated deficit by $623.2 million. In February 2018, the company issued $546.1 million of Automotive Asset-backed Notes, Series 2018-A, and repaid $453.6 million under Warehouse Agreements. In March 2018, stockholders approved the 2018 CEO Performance Award granting 20,264,042 stock options to the CEO, vesting based on market capitalization and operational milestones. Customer deposits totaled $984.8 million as of March 31, 2018.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2016. For the second quarter of 2016, Tesla reported total revenues of $1.27 billion, up from $955.0 million in the prior-year quarter, driven primarily by increased vehicle deliveries, including the Model X. Net loss was $293.2 million, compared to $184.2 million a year earlier, and gross margin declined to 21.6% from 22.3%, primarily due to a product mix shift toward Model X. Total assets were $11.87 billion as of June 30, 2016, with cash and cash equivalents of $3.25 billion. In May 2016, Tesla completed a public offering of common stock generating approximately $1.7 billion in net proceeds. On July 31, 2016, Tesla entered into a definitive agreement to acquire SolarCity Corporation. Customer deposits rose to $679.8 million, primarily due to Model 3 deposits. Tesla produced 18,345 vehicles in the second quarter and plans approximately 50,000 deliveries in the second half of 2016, targeting 500,000 vehicles of annual production in 2018. The company expects capital expenditures of approximately $2.25 billion for 2016. Subsequent to quarter end, Tesla received conversion notices for approximately $411 million of its 2018 convertible notes, expected to be paid in the third quarter of 2016.

This is an ebook edition of *Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, 1906, Part I*, released in May 2018 by the Office of the Historian at the U.S. Department of State. The ebook provides the full content of the FRUS series (established 1861) with features such as full-text search, bookmarking, note-taking, and offline access; readers are advised to cite document numbers rather than page numbers. The passage also contains the President's annual message to Congress, in which he notes the nation's unprecedented prosperity, recommends a law prohibiting corporations from making campaign contributions, and urges passage of a bill granting the Government the right of appeal in criminal cases on questions of law, citing conflicting court rulings in rebate conspiracy cases and concerns about obtaining justice for wage workers.

The Socket 940 base and cover are made of LCP (UL 94 V-0), with a black base and natural or ivory cover; cover thickness must not exceed 1.17 mm and flatness must remain below 0.25 mm. A removable tape or plastic overlay covers the pin holes for vacuum pick-and-place and must not outgas or leave residue. Molded markings include "SOCKET 940," a directional designator, a triangular pin A01 orientation symbol, the supplier's UL symbol, and a lot traceability number, all visible after PCB mounting. Contacts are high-strength copper alloy plated with 1.27 µm nickel, with 0.76 µm gold on mating areas; solder balls are 63/37 ± 5% tin-lead, 0.76 mm in diameter, with 0.20 mm co-planarity. A stainless steel actuation lever enables toolless operation; insertion/extraction forces must not exceed 2 kgf with the lever open, extraction requires at least 0.013 kgf per pin when closed, lever actuation force must be under 3.6 kgf, and pin displacement under 1.0 mm. The socket must maintain integrity after 50 actuation cycles, with no damaged solder balls, contacts, cover, base, or lever. Electrically, contacts are rated 1.5 A with under 30°C rise; LLCR must not exceed 25 mΩ; self-inductance under 4 nH; capacitance under 1 pF; differential impedance 100 Ω ± 10%; propagation delay skew under 10 ps; dielectric withstanding voltage at least 650 Vac; and insulation resistance at least 1000 MΩ.

The ADS868xW devices operate from two independent supplies: AVDD for internal circuits and DVDD for the digital interface, each settable within its permissible range. AVDD pins should be decoupled to AGND with 10µF and 1µF capacitors, and DVDD with a minimum 10µF capacitor; decoupling improves power-supply rejection ratio (PSRR). The device offers two programmable low-power modes: NAP mode, entered by setting the NAP_EN bit (after writing 69h to register address 05h) and holding CONVST/CS high, and a deeper power-down (PD) mode, entered by setting the PWRDN bit, in which analog blocks power down while the interface remains active and registers are retained. PCB layout guidance recommends separating analog and digital sections, using 1µF X7R, 0603-size capacitors near AVDD and DVDD, avoiding vias between pins and bypass capacitors, and specific decoupling for the REFCAP and REFIO pins. The document also lists related TI documentation, support resources via TI E2E forums, ESD handling precautions, a revision history note changing ADS8685W and ADS8689W from Advance Information to Production Data, and standard legal disclaimers regarding TI's technical resources.

After a 38–10 loss to Clemson, North Carolina coach Bill Belichick accepted responsibility for penalties and defensive lapses, including 399 passing yards allowed and three illegal-formation penalties. He attributed third-down struggles to earlier downs, declined to evaluate the rebuild, and praised his team's effort while stressing the need to improve.

Russia denies involvement in the poisoning of Sergei Skripal and his daughter Yulia, with Putin calling the accusations nonsense and offering cooperation in investigations. Russia's EU ambassador suggested Britain's Porton Down facility might be responsible. Britain claims evidence Russia has produced and stockpiled Novichok within the last decade. The piece calls for sanctions targeting Russian assets hidden in the West.

Speedy, a hire services company that floated on the stock market in March 1999, has undergone a significant transformation under chief executive Russell Down, who took over in summer 2015 shortly after joining as group finance director amid a profit warning. Down faced challenges including unreliable asset hire data following an IT upgrade, declining revenue from a lost focus on smaller customers, and a centralized testing system that left over 50% of products unavailable in September 2015. He refocused the business on customers, cut costs, improved asset availability, and increased staff engagement through surveys. Results for the six months to September showed profits up 58.8% to £10.8m, reduced net debt, and improved ROCE. Speedy has also acquired Prolift Access Limited and Platform Sales & Hire Limited in the powered access market, expecting revenue and cost synergies, and reports being financially strong for sustainable growth.

The paper proposes a periodically modulated one-dimensional multi-chain system of coupled SSH chains as a platform for non-Abelian quantum interference and entanglement generation via braiding of topological edge states. The non-Abelian characteristics are protected by a time-dependent interchain symmetry, which enables multiple edge-state branches whose temporal braiding induces branch switching and ensures robust adiabatic evolution along a single branch, while a time-independent inversion symmetry protects the evolution of parity-distinct edge states, with an accumulated relative phase determining the partition of particle transfer. In a double-coupled chain, two pairs of edge states exhibit a twisted energy spectrum and swap after one period, enabling transfer of a particle from one end of a chain to the two ends of the other chain at a tunable ratio (0 to 1). Extending to triple-coupled chains, three pairs of edge states undergo non-Abelian braiding whose outcomes depend on the operation sequence, producing sequence-dependent topological transport and non-Abelian Hong-Ou-Mandel interference that generates spatially entangled two-particle NOON states (fidelity ~0.995) on different chains depending on the braiding order. The authors suggest adiabatically modulated photonic waveguide arrays as an experimental platform, and note that time-dependent symmetry protection requires sufficiently long, though not infinite, evolution time.

Clark County schools are individually deciding how to spend their share of new Nevada state funding for English language learners living in poverty. The Legislature's weighted funding formula allocates $1,200 per student who scores in the bottom 25 percent on state tests, is learning English or living in poverty, and attends a school not already receiving Zoom or Victory funding, which target similar students but are used schoolwide. Under the district's reorganization, spending decisions are made at the school level. Garside Junior High School in Las Vegas, with about 1,200 students including 378 benefiting from the funds, is receiving more than $450,000. Principal Scarlett Perryman's team is finalizing spending plans, and teacher Kimberly Ivanick proposes expanding after-school tutoring and adding technology. Statewide, $36 million was allocated this year, with Clark County receiving more than $34 million. Spending will be tracked separately and analyzed for its impact on student achievement.

Mastitis, the most costly disease in the dairy industry, damages cows' mammary gland tissue and is typically treated with antibiotics, which kill bacteria but cannot regenerate damaged tissue. Cornell University researchers published a paper in Scientific Reports detailing, for the first time, the secretions of bovine mammary stem cells. These secreted factors promote new blood vessel formation, cell migration, protection of epithelial cells from bacterial toxins, and antimicrobial activity. The factors proved more effective against gram-negative bacterial toxins, potentially complementing FDA-approved antimicrobials, which work better against gram-positive bacteria. The next step is testing the therapy in cows with mastitis.

Hyundai Motor and Kia Motors have installed a vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication system on a 14-kilometer road in Hwaseong to advance autonomous driving technology. The system enables real-time information exchange between vehicles, roads, signals, and pedestrians. The companies plan to gather data by year's end and make the system operational for highway communication by 2020.

Caitlin Bassett says the build-up to Saturday's Super Netball grand final between her Sunshine Coast Lightning and Greater Western Sydney is unlike anything in her 12-year career. Having never played a national grand final, she has been guided by experienced teammates Geva Mentor and Laura Langman. Mentor prepared by practising against 215cm Junior Levi.

The passage is a glossary and guide to RSI (Relative Strength Index) trading strategies. The RSI, developed by Welles Wilder and introduced in Commodities magazine in June 1978, is an oscillator ranging from 0 to 100 that measures gains and losses over a chosen number of days, calculated as RSI = 100 – (100 / (1+RS)). It is used to identify overbought and oversold conditions and works best on mean-reverting assets, particularly stocks and stock indices, while performing poorly on forex and commodity-related stocks. The authors' backtesting indicates RSI works best when combined with additional filters, indicators, or variables. Shorter time frames (2–6 days) work best on stocks, using extreme thresholds such as 15 for oversold and 85 for overbought; a 2-day RSI strategy on SPY (buy below 15, sell above 85) from 1993 to November 2020 slightly underperformed buy-and-hold but spent only 42% of the time invested with lower drawdown (33% vs. 55%), turning $100,000 into $861,000. A 10-day RSI strategy produced half that result with bigger drawdowns. Combining long- and short-term RSIs is possible but performed worse in one test. Divergences between price and RSI are only identifiable in hindsight and of limited practical use. Daily bars are recommended over intraday data. Variants include Connors RSI and Cutler's RSI, which uses a simple moving average. RSI also works well with the Internal Bar Strength Indicator (IBS), and an RSI 14 setting reacts faster than RSI 21, which offers smoother, more reliable signals for longer trends.

A corner kick is awarded when a defender touches the ball over their own end line. Although goals from corner kicks are relatively rare at college and professional levels, coaches must treat them as significant scoring opportunities. The article outlines a progression for teaching young players: explaining Law 17, demonstrating fundamental skills, showing right-footed and right-side kicks, introducing a play with three designated positions (corner taker, receiver, and cover man), rotating all players through the positions, demonstrating left-footed and left-side kicks, and assigning specific players to positions. Key requirements include placing the ball within the corner arc, defenders staying at least 10 yards away until the kick, and the kicker not touching the ball again until another player does. Passive and then active defenders should be added for realism, with additional passing options and offside discussion introduced as players develop.

The passage discusses Landor v. Louisiana Department of Corrections and Public Safety, a case set for oral argument in the Supreme Court's October Term 2025. Damon Landor, a Rastafarian prisoner who had grown dreadlocks for nearly 20 years as part of his religious practice, was handcuffed and shaved bald by Louisiana prison officials weeks before his release, despite a federal appeals court precedent protecting Rastafarian inmates. Landor sued the officials for money damages under the Religious Land Use and Institutionalized Persons Act (RLUIPA), a 2000 statute prohibiting substantial burdens on prisoners' religious exercise. The lower court ruled RLUIPA does not authorize money damages as "appropriate relief," though several judges dissented, and the Supreme Court agreed to hear the case. The author, who joined a friend-of-the-court brief, argues Landor should and likely will win, citing precedent under the Religious Freedom Restoration Act and noting that without damages, prisoners would effectively have no remedy. The passage critiques the media narrative that religious-freedom cases are polarized, majority-serving, or "culture war" disputes, pointing to numerous unanimous or near-unanimous rulings and claimants from minority faiths. The author concludes the case affirms religious freedom as a foundational right belonging to everyone.

A treaty of annexation, concluded February 14, 1893, between Secretary of State John W. Foster and commissioners of the Hawaiian Islands, is transmitted to the Senate for ratification. The treaty leaves detailed questions arising from annexation to the United States. The monarchy's overthrow was not promoted by the United States but resulted from Queen Liliuokalani's reactionary and revolutionary policy, and her restoration is undesirable, if not impossible. Of two options—a protectorate or full annexation—the Executive favors annexation as best serving Hawaiian and American interests, since no other great power must acquire the islands. No protest has been heard from any government, and foreign representatives at Honolulu acknowledged the provisional Government. Prompt approval is urged, with existing laws maintaining peace and order until Congress provides a permanent government.
San Diego police pursued a wanted shooting suspect in City Heights Sunday. The suspect crashed into fences at Central Elementary School and a fire station, fled armed, and was arrested nearby.

A retrospective study of 671 TBI patients (459 males, 212 females) treated at a republic hospital from July 2017 to December 2018 examined gender-dependent risk factors for traumatic brain injury. Domestic accidents were the most frequent cause of TBI in both men (37.47%) and women (57.54%), followed by alcohol-related injury (20.71% overall) and motor vehicle injury (16.54%). Most patients (99.55%) received conservative therapy, while 198 required surgery. Men were affected at a younger mean age than women (44.41 vs. 49.50 years, p<0.0004), and men had longer hospitalization stays than women. Village residents were at increased risk of TBI compared to city residents (p<0.002), possibly due to lack of primary health care facilities. Hospitalization duration correlated with patient age. The study concluded that gender plays a role in TBI severity and post-TBI outcomes, with domestic accidents, alcohol consumption, and rural residence identified as key risk factors. A limitation was the absence of a control group.

The passage describes NVIDIA's RTX Blackwell architecture. Blackwell features advanced power gating with reduced state transition latencies, new clock gating that can shut off entire clock trees, GDDR7-based memory power management, and separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory, enabling frame-granularity power states beneficial for laptops. Accelerated frequency switching adjusts clocks 1000x faster than prior architectures, and the deepest sleep state is entered 10x faster than Ada, yielding up to 50% power savings in small language model inference workloads.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, producing up to three AI-generated frames per traditionally rendered frame using a 40% faster model that consumes 30% less VRAM, along with enhanced Flip Metering that shifts frame pacing to the display engine. DLSS 4 also transitions from CNN to transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, ingesting 2x more parameters for improved image quality, temporal stability, and detail.

Blackwell introduces neural shaders via the Cooperative Vectors API, developed with Microsoft, allowing shaders to access Tensor Cores. Associated technologies include RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression (over 3x memory savings in a demo), Stochastic Texture Filtering, Neural Radiance Cache for inferred indirect lighting, RTX Skin for ray-traced subsurface scattering, and RTX Neural Faces using real-time generative AI.

The GB202 flagship GPU contains 92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA cores, and a 512-bit memory interface, launching in the GeForce RTX 5090. GB203 (45.6 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA cores) powers the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti, while GB205 (31 billion transistors, 6,400 CUDA cores) powers the RTX 5070. The passage concludes with NVIDIA's standard specification disclaimers and trademark information.

Sodium cumenesulfonate is a hydrotrope compound, available in powder and liquid forms, that increases solubility of less soluble organic matter, lowers cloud points, promotes compatibility of ingredients, and moderates viscosity. It is used as a solubilizer and cloud point depressor in wax cleaners, drilling fluids, laundry washing, detergents, metal processing, oilfield applications, and hydrogen sulfide scavengers. Its cost depends on raw material prices, and price volatility along with declining R&D activities may hamper the market. Heavy exposure can cause eye and respiratory tract irritation. Increasing industrialization and household detergent use in emerging economies are expected to drive demand. The liquid form segment led the market in 2015, as did the household application segment.

U.S. stocks fell about 2 percent on Monday, with the Dow shedding nearly 400 points, as Facebook led a technology selloff after reports that a political consultancy tied to President Trump's campaign gained inappropriate access to data on more than 50 million users. Facebook dropped 7.1 percent, entering correction territory, while the Nasdaq and S&P technology index posted their worst one-day falls since early February. Other FAANG stocks also declined. Data privacy concerns, trade war worries ahead of a G20 meeting, and an upcoming Federal Reserve rate decision contributed to the defensive pullback.

Frost Brown Todd and Gibbons will merge in January, creating a firm called FBT Gibbons with 800 lawyers in 25 offices. The merger gives Frost Brown Todd, which has more than 650 lawyers in 18 offices, new Northeast offices including New York and New Jersey. Leaders say the initial focus will be integration, though further mergers may follow. Robert Sartin will chair the merged firm, with Adam Hall and Peter Torcicollo as co-managing partners. Frost Brown Todd reported $336.5 million in gross revenue; Gibbons had $115 million.

This passage is a bibliographic listing of 1945 documents concerning United States foreign policy. It cites President Truman's December 1945 statement on China policy, his message recommending a Department of National Defense, and his directive on immigration of certain displaced persons and refugees from Europe. It records State Department changes: Edward R. Stettinius, Jr.'s resignation as Secretary of State (June 27, 1945) upon appointment as U.S. Representative to the United Nations; James F. Byrnes's commissioning as Secretary of State (July 2); Joseph C. Grew's resignation as Under Secretary and Dean G. Acheson's appointment (August 16); Patrick J. Hurley's resignation as Ambassador to China and General George C. Marshall's appointment as personal envoy to China (November 27); and Cordell Hull's Nobel Peace Prize (December 10). Executive Order 9608 (August 31, 1945) terminated the Office of War Information and transferred its international information functions, plus those of the Office of Inter-American Affairs, to the State Department. Executive Order 9621 (September 20, 1945) abolished the O.S.S., transferring its Research and Analysis and Presentation Branches to the State Department; Truman directed Byrnes to lead a coordinated foreign intelligence program through an interdepartmental group under the State Department.

An early treaty providing annuities and admission of the Kingdom as a State was objected to by the United States and failed after Kamehameha III died in 1855, his successor being unfavorable to it. A reciprocity treaty concluded in July 1855 by Marcy and Judge Lee also failed ratification. Subsequent correspondence concerned routine matters; in 1863 the diplomatic rank was raised to minister resident under James McBride, and the Civil War deferred reciprocity discussions. In May 1867, McCook and Harris concluded a reciprocity treaty at San Francisco; though approved by the President, it failed Senate ratification. Seward authorized McCook to explore annexation, preferring it over reciprocity. The USS Lackawanna's presence delayed Hawaiian ratification, granted July 30, 1867; the United States Senate rejected the treaty on June 1, 1870.

Stephen Hawking, the best-known theoretical physicist of his time, has died. Diagnosed with ALS at 21, he lived more than 50 years with the normally fatal illness and communicated through an electronic voice synthesizer after a 1985 pneumonia attack. As Lucasian Professor of Mathematics at Cambridge, he sought a "unified theory" reconciling Einstein's General Theory of Relativity and Quantum Mechanics, though he later suggested it might not exist. His book "A Brief History of Time" became an international bestseller, followed by 2001's "The Universe in a Nutshell." Eddie Redmayne portrayed his life in the 2014 film "The Theory of Everything," and his longevity showed severe disabilities need not stop patients from living.

The speaker, upon taking the presidential oath of office, invokes divine guidance and attributes his election to the American people's love for the Constitution and Union. Having determined not to seek reelection, he states his only motive is to serve his country faithfully. He observes that the recent presidential contest ended calmly once the majority's will, expressed through constitutional means, was accepted.

He endorses Congress's application of popular sovereignty to slavery in the Territories, under which Kansas may be admitted with or without slavery as its constitution prescribes. The question of when territorial residents should decide this issue is pending before the Supreme Court, whose decision he pledges to accept. He affirms the government's duty to protect every resident's right to vote, notes that slavery in the States lies beyond federal power, and hopes the more-than-twenty-year agitation over slavery—which he says has produced great evils and endangered the Union—will end. He warns against calculating the Union's mere material value, arguing that free trade binds all sections together and disunion would bring common ruin.

He stresses keeping government free from corruption, noting the unprecedented Treasury surplus encourages extravagant legislation, and recommends applying the surplus to extinguishing the public debt and increasing the Navy. He supports tariff modification to collect only necessary revenue and advocates reserving public lands for actual settlers at moderate prices, praising immigrants as faithful citizens entitled to equality.

He declares strict construction the only true and safe theory of the Constitution, though he argues the war-making power permits Congress to fund a military road necessary to defend the Pacific coast against invasion. In foreign affairs, he advocates peace, commerce, and friendship with all nations, avoidance of entangling alliances, noninterference in other nations' domestic concerns, and acquisition of territory only by fair purchase or voluntary union.

Synaptics announced plans to mass produce an optical in-display fingerprint sensor called "Clear ID," embedded under a phone's screen for bezel-less designs. The company claims it is twice as fast as 3D facial recognition and allows unlocking from any angle. While Apple replaced Touch ID with facial recognition, researchers have hacked such systems, and fingerprint security remains relevant.

On February 16, 2016, Apple Inc. entered into an underwriting agreement with Goldman, Sachs & Co., Deutsche Bank Securities Inc., J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, and Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith Incorporated, as representatives of the underwriters, for the issuance of $500 million Floating Rate Notes due 2019, $500 million Floating Rate Notes due 2021, and Fixed Rate Notes of $500 million at 1.300% due 2018, $1 billion at 1.700% due 2019, $2.25 billion at 2.250% due 2021, $1.5 billion at 2.850% due 2023, $2 billion at 3.250% due 2026, $1.25 billion at 4.500% due 2036, and $2.5 billion at 4.650% due 2046. The notes are issued under an indenture dated April 29, 2013 with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A. as trustee. Floating Rate Notes pay interest quarterly beginning May 23, 2016; Fixed Rate Notes pay interest semi-annually beginning August 23, 2016. The notes are Apple's senior unsecured obligations, ranking equally with its other unsecured and unsubordinated debt.

The Bemidji Lumberjacks (14-6) defeated Thief River Falls (9-12) 77-45 after leading 45-25 at halftime. Caden Rolfes scored 18 points, Linaes Whiting 17, Caleb Carlson 14, and Jeremy Beberg 10. Coach Travis Peterson called the win a big step forward before the section tournament. BHS plays Feb. 18 at Fergus Falls.

Florida State University President John Thrasher has formed a 15-member committee, chaired by Renisha Gibbs, associate vice president for human resources, to review the university's policies on campus names and markers, including statues. The panel, called the President's Advisory Panel on University Namings and Recognitions, was created amid a national movement to remove Confederate designations. The campus chapter of Students for a Democratic Society has sought removal of the Francis Eppes statue, citing his slave ownership and Confederate support. The committee meets next week, with public meetings and a website planned.

This passage covers container design patterns and distributed system architectures.

**Container APIs and documentation:** Containers define APIs through their parameters, calls to other services, and provided HTTP endpoints. Maintaining stable sidecar APIs is essential—even subtle changes, such as altering parameter units, can break users. Containers should be documented using Dockerfile directives (EXPOSE, ENV, LABEL), and the Label Schema project provides a shared taxonomy of metadata labels.

**Single-node patterns:** The sidecar pattern augments an application container with additional functionality. The ambassador pattern brokers interactions between an application container and the outside world, with applications including sharding (e.g., routing to sharded Redis or memcached via twemproxy), service brokering for portability across environments, and experimentation or request splitting (e.g., nginx directing 10% of traffic to an experimental service). The adapter pattern modifies an application container's interface to conform to a standardized interface, applied to monitoring (e.g., a Prometheus exporter for Redis), log normalization (e.g., Fluentd plugins for Redis and Storm), and rich health checks (e.g., a Go-based MySQL health-check adapter), enabling modularity and reuse without modifying existing images.

**Multi-node patterns:** Microservices architectures decompose applications into independently scalable services with formal APIs, improving agility but complicating debugging and design. Replicated load-balanced services deploy identical stateless replicas behind load balancers, requiring readiness probes; session tracking can use IP hashing or cookies. Caching layers (e.g., Varnish) improve performance and can also provide rate limiting, while nginx handles SSL termination. Sharded services assign each replica a subset of data, suited to stateful systems; sharding functions use hashing with modulo operations, careful key selection, and consistent hashing to minimize remapping during resharding. Replicated sharded caches add resilience, and hot shards can be scaled independently. The scatter/gather pattern fans requests out to all leaf nodes in parallel and merges partial results, useful for tasks like document search, but limited by per-node overhead and the straggler problem; replicating each shard improves reliability. The passage concludes by introducing function-as-a-service (FaaS), or serverless computing, for event-driven applications.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere architecture (GA100), is the 8th-generation data center GPU designed to accelerate AI training and inference, HPC, and data analytics workloads. Built on TSMC's 7nm process with 54.2 billion transistors, it contains 108 SMs, 6912 FP32 CUDA cores, and 432 third-generation Tensor Cores. Compared to the Tesla V100, the A100 delivers up to 20x faster INT8 inference with sparsity, 2.5x–5x faster FP16 mixed-precision, 10x–20x faster TF32 operations, and 2.5x faster FP64 performance. It introduces Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity (2:4 pattern) that doubles Tensor Core throughput, and Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology that partitions a single GPU into up to seven isolated GPU Instances for improved utilization, QoS, and fault isolation, particularly benefiting Cloud Service Providers. The A100 includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache with residency controls and Compute Data Compression, third-generation NVLink providing 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, and PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV. Additional features include asynchronous copy operations, asynchronous barriers, task graph acceleration, hardware JPEG decoding, an optical flow accelerator, five NVDEC units, and improved error and fault detection. Supported by CUDA 11, the A100 powers the DGX A100 system, which delivers 5 PFLOPS of AI performance using eight NVLink-interconnected A100 GPUs.

The government shutdown, caused by a stalemate between congressional Republicans and Democrats, has left essential air safety workers—including air traffic controllers, TSA agents, and FAA employees—working without pay. An FAA engineer said the shutdown has made work less efficient and could slow repairs, and the FAA plans to furlough about 11,300 workers. Employees report anxiety over missed paychecks and fear contractors could also be furloughed. Experts warn delays and cancellations will increase as the shutdown continues, especially given long-standing controller staff shortages and a closed training academy. Workers also fear mass firings and threats to their unions; the Trump administration terminated TSA workers' collective bargaining agreement in March before a court preliminarily halted it in June. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy threatened to fire workers who don't show up, while the FAA stated safety-critical positions are exempt from reductions in force and air traffic will be slowed where needed to maintain safety.

This patent application, a continuation of earlier filings, relates to devices, systems, and methods for robotic-assisted and/or navigation-assisted surgical procedures, particularly placement of implants such as screws within a vertebra pedicle. The background identifies challenges in minimally invasive spinal fusion: K-wires may bend or break and accuracy depends on surgeon expertise; current robotic systems do not facilitate robot-assisted advancement of tools within bone; multiple distinct instruments are required and may be incompatible with robotic interfaces; and relative vertebral movement during discectomy and cage placement can cause navigation errors.

The disclosed methods operate a system comprising a manipulator moving an end effector, a screw coupled to the end effector, a coaxial sleeve releasably engaged to the screw, a navigation system tracking the vertebral body with a defined insertion trajectory, and controllers. The controllers position and advance the screw and sleeve along the trajectory through soft tissue, then advance the screw relative to the sleeve to secure it to the vertebra while disengaging it from the sleeve. In one aspect, the sleeve's distal end has a flexible movable feature that remains closed during advancement to prevent tissue ingress and opens when the screw passes through. In another, a tracking device with a ratcheting mechanism rotates markers relative to the screw in one direction.

The detailed description covers a robotic system (e.g., the RIO System by MAKO Surgical Corp.) with a tool assembly including a drive coupler removably coupled to manual, powered, or freehand input devices. The drive coupler interchangeably connects working tools—scalpels, depth probes, burs, tap drills, drills, dilator probes, and tap inserters—via mating and locking features, with haptic feedback constraining movement within virtual boundaries. An elongate sleeve forms a working channel through soft tissue, may include bone-penetrating spikes, and has a movable distal feature (tabs or taper) that opens to permit the working tool to pass. Tracking devices with markers detectable by a localizer removably couple to working tools (e.g., magnetically or via a star-shaped recess) to verify registration or relocalize bony anatomy after movement.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on January 27, 2022, reporting its financial results for the first fiscal quarter ended December 25, 2021, via a press release attached as Exhibit 99.1. The filing lists Apple's registered securities, including common stock (AAPL) and various notes maturing between 2022 and 2042, all traded on the Nasdaq Stock Market LLC. The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Anjuna police registered two unnatural death cases involving tourists from Tamil Nadu and Kerala, without ruling out drug overdose. Pravin Sundaram, 28, collapsed in the Vagator parking area and was declared dead at a hospital; sources said he had attended a rave party. Abdul, reportedly from Kerala, was brought to a hospital by an unknown person and died. Viscera of both bodies will be preserved to determine the cause of death, and police are investigating. The Siolim MLA urged that outdoor music parties be stopped.

The 23rd BMO Okanagan Marathon in Kelowna expects close to 3,000 participants across marathon, half marathon, 10K, 5K, and kids events on a Boston Marathon-qualifying course along Okanagan Lake. New this year are a timed 5 km event and a beverage garden. Saturday features the 5 km and kids activities; Sunday hosts the marathon, half marathon, and 10 km. Team "Special Addition" runs to support double lung transplant recipient Andrew Brownell, and Olympic race walker Mat Bilodeau participates via an honorary category. The event supports The Sunshine Foundation of Canada and is staged from City Park with over 300 volunteers.

A New York panel unanimously recommended the state Medicaid program pause coverage of Sarepta's Duchenne muscular dystrophy drug Elevidys following a safety controversy, pending FDA labeling updates and evaluation of a regimen to mitigate liver failure risk, though some children may still be covered case-by-case.

The St. John's Edge defeated the London Lightning 123-110 in Game 4, tying the NBL Canada Central Division final 2-2, with Game 5 set for Thursday in St. John's and Game 6 in London. The Lightning built an early double-digit lead but played with little intensity, were outscored 50-38 in the paint, and missed 13 free throws. Teammates Royce White and Ryan Anderson tugged at each other near the officials at the end of the third quarter, which Lightning coach Keith Vassell dismissed as competition. Vassell took responsibility for the team's lack of preparation and his short bench rotation. Edge coach Jeff Dunlap started Alex Johnson, while Charles Hinkle and Coron Williams scored 28 points each and Ryan Reid added 22. White led the Lightning with 32 points and Anderson had 21.
