A television clip alleged a Lightning player used a homophobic slur during Game 3; NBL deputy commissioner Audley Stephenson said an investigation produced differing accounts.

The player reflects on a previous loss but focuses on Wednesday's upcoming game, calling it the biggest of their careers and one they will never forget. He notes the team has been strong on the road all season and playoffs, and emphasizes keys like the forecheck, getting pucks deep, and pressuring opponents' defensemen and forwards. He praises goaltender Binner for making big saves and giving the team a chance to win every game. He also mentions an absent teammate whose return is anticipated, plans to relax and prepare during the break, and says getting pucks and players toward the net is a simple strategy.

Mums and their children with Down's syndrome have gained global praise for a Carpool Karaoke-style video watched over 600,000 times, moving James Corden to tears. Made for World Down's Syndrome Day to change perceptions, the idea came from Coventry mum Becky Carless. The video features Christina Perri's "A Thousand Years," who quickly granted permission via Twitter.

Topshop has removed all till barrier display units from its stores nationwide as a safety precaution after 10-year-old Kaden Reddick died from serious head injuries in an incident involving a display at its Reading store in the Oracle shopping centre. The incident occurred at 4.15pm on Monday, and Thames Valley Police and Reading Borough Council are investigating.

This study examined Turkish teachers' experiences with distance education and the technological tools used in Turkish language courses during the COVID-19 pandemic. Using a qualitative case study design, semi-structured interviews with an 8-question open-ended form were conducted with 20 Turkish teachers of grades 5–8 in the Hazro district of Diyarbakır province, and data were analyzed through descriptive analysis.

Findings showed that 45% of participants believed education progressed during the pandemic, 25% believed it progressed but was insufficient, 20% believed it did not progress, and 10% were neutral. Regarding EBA and EBA TV, 10 participants viewed them as advantageous, 3 as insufficient, and 7 did not comment. No participant considered distance education fully efficient: 70% found it insufficiently efficient and 30% found it inefficient. Target behaviors and achievements were considered achieved for students with internet access and devices, but not for those without, with lack of infrastructure and materials identified as the main barrier.

Reported problems included students' lack of equipment (tablets, phones, computers), parents' burden when multiple school-age children were at home, infrastructure deficiencies especially in rural areas, and teachers' time constraints caused by absenteeism and repeated content. For Turkish lessons, 35% of participants said students most needed reading books and dictionaries, 25% technological materials, 20% both, and 20% practice and activity materials for reading, writing, listening, and speaking skills.

The telephone was the most used communication tool (65%), and WhatsApp was the most used application, followed by Zoom, EBA, and BIP. Participants listed teacher qualifications including subject knowledge, planning, communication skills, activity orientation, attention to individual differences, technological competence, and following the national and international agenda.

Suggestions to address deficiencies included reducing textbook volume, establishing drama classes and school libraries, compensation programs, hybrid education models, extended school hours in rural areas, further developing EBA and EBA TV, resolving internet infrastructure problems, and ensuring every child has internet and materials access. For post-pandemic structuring, participants proposed region-specific education systems, distance education as a support to face-to-face teaching, base stations and infrastructure in all villages, strengthened EBA content, technology seminars for teachers and students, teacher-student-parent cooperation, and provincial meetings.

The study concluded that Turkey was unprepared for distance education but managed the process with available means. Most teachers considered themselves sufficient, but irregular student attendance, largely due to lack of materials, prevented target behaviors and achievements from being fully realized and reduced efficiency. Recommendations included resolving infrastructure and material shortages in line with equality of opportunity, continuously updating EBA content, structuring distance education to support face-to-face education, expanding professional development programs, continuing book reading activities, prioritizing student health and safety, and rearranging post-pandemic target behaviors and achievements according to student needs.

In this inaugural address, the speaker describes the moment as a potential turning point in history, noting that the times favor peace and that America has the opportunity to earn the title of peacemaker. He acknowledges national achievements in science, industry, agriculture, and expanding freedom, while identifying a crisis of the spirit—material wealth accompanied by discord, war, and division at home. He argues the answer lies in simple values such as goodness, decency, love, and kindness, and calls for lowered voices and an end to inflated rhetoric. He states that government will listen and assist those left out or behind, but that government alone has reached its limits, requiring citizens to act alongside it. He pledges progress toward full employment, better housing, education, rebuilt cities, and environmental protection, and affirms that black and white Americans must go forward as one nation. In foreign affairs, he declares an era of negotiation after confrontation, seeking an open world, peaceful competition instead of conquest, cooperation on arms reduction and aid to the poor, and strength where necessary. He dedicates his office to peace among nations and closes by invoking the Apollo astronauts' Christmas Eve view of Earth, urging Americans to go forward together in hope.

The FDA announced a crackdown on the sale of Juul e-cigarettes to minors, including a nationwide undercover blitz targeting illegal sales at stores and online. Juul products, which resemble flash drives and contain high nicotine levels—one cartridge equals a pack of cigarettes—hold more than half of the e-cigarette market. Since March, FDA compliance checks uncovered 40 violations, resulting in 40 warning letters. The FDA contacted eBay, which removed Juul listings, and requested documents from Juul's maker to explain the products' appeal to youth, with enforcement possible for noncompliance. The FDA also plans actions against misleading marketing and youth education campaigns.

Ravita Meghwar, a Hindu girl from Pakistan's Sindh province, was allegedly drugged, abducted, and forcibly converted to Islam and married, though she says she eloped willingly. Her case reflects a pattern of Hindu girls converting to Islam in Sindh, home to most of Pakistan's roughly 2 percent Hindu population, causing alarm and prompting some Hindus to reassess their place in the country 70 years after partition. Lower-caste, low-income Hindus are particularly vulnerable, and conversions are often backed by shrines, seminaries, clerics, and local politicians. A 2012 Supreme Court case involving Rinkle Kumari ended with the women choosing to stay with their husbands, disappointing the community. A 2016 Sindh bill banning forcible conversions and conversions under 18 was blocked after opposition from hardline groups like Jamaat-ud-Dawa. Activists now rely on a law prohibiting marriage under 18, though courts often side with the girls. The movement is traced to the past 15 years and General Zia-ul-Haq's Islamization legacy. Hindus are leaving villages for cities, and an estimated 5,000 migrate to India annually.

Diana Beresford-Kroeger lives with her husband Christian on 160 acres near Merrickville, where they built their home and planted rare trees and plants starting in the 1970s. Orphaned at 11 in Ireland, she was raised by families who taught her old Irish teachings about trees and nature. She earned science degrees from University College, Cork, studied in Connecticut, and pursued doctoral and surgical research in Canada. After receiving trees as a wedding gift, she created the arboretum Carrigliath and began "expotitions" to save rare local plants as development spread. Now a full-time author and speaker, her Canadian-made film "Call of the Forest: The Forgotten Wisdom of Trees" examines deforestation and climate change. Her Bioplan proposes planting 50 billion trees to lower atmospheric carbon dioxide from 400 to 300 parts per million. The film has drawn record audiences and award nominations.

A high school senior from Las Vegas recounts being disengaged and at risk of dropping out during his first two years of high school, nearly becoming one of the 42,000 "disconnected" youth (NEETs) in southern Nevada. After landing a job the summer after sophomore year, he worked over 20 hours weekly while maintaining a 4.0 GPA, gaining real-world connections to classroom learning, durable skills, and confidence. Research cited indicates youth employment and internships improve academic performance, reduce delinquent behavior, and build social skills. However, such opportunities remain rare—at most 5% of students access apprenticeships or internships—and youth unemployment stands at 10.5% nationally, over 14% among African American youth. The author argues governments should incentivize businesses to hire young people, noting some states offer tax credits for such programs, and concludes that expanding job opportunities benefits the entire community.

A hockey player describes his former coach as honest, tough, and funny, someone he knew could become a head coach. He calls the opponent's strong defense and depth a challenge requiring hard work. Having waited years for this chance, he is excited that his team shares the same dream of winning. He praises Canadian fans, recalling Edmonton's anthem crowd and expecting Ottawa's arena to be equally loud. He believes goalie equipment is still too big, though goalies are excellent athletes. He credits the team's forward depth, including younger lines and Pahlsson's line, for their success. He feels youthful despite being older and attributes Giguère's lack of recognition to playing in a smaller market rather than Toronto.

On August 1, 2017, Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC reporting its financial results for the third fiscal quarter ended July 1, 2017. The filing includes a press release (Exhibit 99.1) and a related data sheet (Exhibit 99.2), both issued by Apple on the same date. The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The speaker, a hockey coach, attributes a recent loss to self-inflicted critical errors, including puck support mistakes that gave the opponent odd-man rushes, rather than to the opponent's play. He notes similar mistakes occurred in the Colorado series but went unpunished. He considers the errors correctable and states the team's sole focus is winning the next game to bring the series back home. He observes the opponent defends with speed and size, winning the last two games by small margins due to a stronger defensive passion, and that their style has not changed since earlier in the season. When the game's intensity rises, he says his team has shown cracks while the opponent maintained its level. At this stage of the season, he believes emotion and leadership must come from the dressing room, with coaches providing tactical information. He criticizes players, including Modano, for trying to force plays instead of staying with the system, and stresses eliminating odd-man rushes and staying within the team's structure. He praises several opposing players and their goaltender, defends Larry Robinson as a coach who received a raw deal in Los Angeles, and credits Fetisov's influence on the opponent's defense. He also discusses facing elimination, the difficulty of eliminating a team, Carbonneau's need for a defined role, and the cumulative pressure on a defending champion.

Combination defenses are deployed to limit the touches of outstanding offensive players and as surprise tactics, with timing and surprise being critical to their success. The Box & One uses four box zone defenders plus a "Chaser" denying the star player. The Diamond & One takes away the middle but gives up the corners. The Triangle & Two counters two outstanding scorers or catches opponents off guard.

Saturday nights have been the ratings battleground between BBC1 and ITV for over 50 years, and winning this family-viewing slot demonstrates the BBC's commitment to entertainment. New shows rarely succeed there, so established programmes like Casualty, Strictly and The X Factor dominate. Only a handful of entertainment shows have endured, with The Voice UK a rare recent success. Strictly and The X Factor revived Saturday nights after Blind Date declined, but all shows eventually fade, and most new programmes fail, leaving controllers to rely on instinct and hope. The author, Greg Dyke, is a former LWT chief executive and BBC director-general.

A study of 10.3 million patients found that pre-existing psychiatric and behavioural conditions and psychoactive medications are associated with subsequent long-term opioid use. Risk increased 1.5 times for ADHD medications, three times for prior substance use disorders, and nearly nine times for previous opioid use disorders. Researchers recommend thorough mental health assessment alongside long-term opioid therapy.

German Chancellor Angela Merkel has agreed to a deal with her Bavarian coalition allies establishing transit centers along the German-Austrian border, making it harder for migrants to enter Germany. The move followed pressure from Interior Minister Horst Seehofer, whose CSU party faces rising support from the far-right AfD in Bavaria and who threatened to resign over migrant expulsion powers. The SPD disputes the deal, noting transit centers were not part of the coalition agreement. Austria has threatened to return refugees Germany expels, risking collapse of the EU's open-border system. Germany, which took in over 1.4 million refugees in 2015, now accepts roughly 10,000 immigrants monthly.

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture reviews binary detection theory. The professor describes the one-shot detection problem, where a single bit—mapped to plus or minus a—is transmitted through a communication system with added Gaussian noise, and the receiver must guess whether a zero or one was sent based on a single observed value. He recounts an anecdote about Claude Shannon to illustrate the value of reducing problems to simple toy problems first, arguing that the most practical approach is to be theoretical. The detector assumes a known probability model and uses MAP (maximum a posteriori probability) decoding to minimize the probability of error. The a posteriori probability equals the a priori probability times the likelihood divided by the marginal probability, which reduces to a threshold test on the likelihood ratio—a sufficient statistic. For 2PAM antipodal signaling (±a) with Gaussian noise variance n0/2, the log likelihood ratio is 4av/n0, and under maximum likelihood (equal a priori probabilities) the error probability is Q(a/√(n0/2)), or Q(√(2Eb/n0)) in terms of energy per bit. Non-antipodal signaling yields the same error probability, determined by the distance between signal points, but increases energy per bit (a 3 dB loss for a pilot tone of equal magnitude). The analysis extends to antipodal vectors in white Gaussian noise, where the inner product of the observation with the signal vector is the sufficient statistic, implemented via a matched filter, and decision regions are planes perpendicular to the line between the two signal points.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture (GA100), is the eighth-generation data center GPU designed for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads. Fabricated on TSMC's 7nm process with 54.2 billion transistors, the A100 contains 108 SMs, 6912 FP32 CUDA cores, and 432 third-generation Tensor Cores.

Key features include:
- Third-generation Tensor Cores supporting all deep learning data types (FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, Binary), delivering 2.5x V100 performance for FP16/FP32 mixed precision and FP64, and 10x for TF32 versus V100 FP32 operations (20x with sparsity)
- Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity using a 2:4 pattern that doubles Tensor Core throughput with virtually no inference accuracy loss
- 40 GB HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth (a 73% increase over V100) and a 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x larger than V100) with 2.3x read bandwidth
- Compute Data Compression providing up to 4x improvement in DRAM and L2 bandwidth
- Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitioning into up to seven GPU Instances with isolated memory paths, quality of service, and fault isolation, particularly beneficial for Cloud Service Providers
- Third-generation NVLink with 600 GB/sec total bandwidth (double V100)
- PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, improved error and fault detection/isolation/containment, asynchronous copy instructions, asynchronous barriers, and task graph acceleration
- New hardware including a five-core NVJPG decode engine, an optical flow accelerator, and five NVDEC units

CUDA 11 provides support for these features, adding task graphs, asynchronous copy, L2 cache residency controls, and Cooperative Groups enhancements. The TCAIRS mixed-precision solver achieved a 2.0x geomean speedup over the FP64 baseline using TF32.

The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs delivering 5 PFLOPS of performance, interconnected via six NVSwitches with 4.8 TB/s total bidirectional bandwidth. It provides up to 6x the AI training performance of the V100-based DGX-1 and up to 56 fully isolated accelerators through MIG, in a 6U form factor.

The NPD Group has identified five trends shaping Britain's £57 billion foodservice industry in 2018: (1) click & collect via smartphones, which could reduce wait times, boost sales and profits, and require improved restaurant efficiency and staff training; (2) investing in quality staff and training to build customer loyalty, satisfaction and profits; (3) replacing traditional loyalty schemes with tiered, personalized VIP offers targeting the most valuable customers; (4) delivering on brand promises to avoid disappointing consumers, who may complain on social media; and (5) offering recommendations, with staff providing authentic suggestions and technology using customer data to tailor menu choices. Cyril Lavenant, Foodservice Director UK at NPD, noted that success depends on innovation and responding well to these trends.

Plaintiffs, horse dealers, sued to recover the price of a horse sold to the defendant, which died shortly after being returned following two trial periods. The defendant's claims of a thirty-day trial agreement, statute of frauds violation, and warranty breach were rejected; delivery and acceptance were found, and the judgment for the plaintiffs was affirmed with costs.

Three chemists, including Susumu Kitagawa and Richard Robson, won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing metal-organic frameworks—structures combining metal ions and carbon-based molecules that can harvest water or store toxic gases. Over 100,000 have been created since the 1990s.

Amazon.com, Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2020 reports Q3 2020 net sales of $96.1 billion, up 37% year-over-year, and net income of $6.3 billion, up from $2.1 billion in Q3 2019. For the nine months ended September 30, 2020, net sales were $260.5 billion and net income was $14.1 billion. Total assets were $282.2 billion as of September 30, 2020. The company operates three segments: North America, International, and AWS. Q3 2020 operating income was $6.2 billion, with North America contributing $2.3 billion, International $407 million, and AWS $3.5 billion. Effective January 1, 2020, Amazon changed the estimated useful life of its servers from three to four years, reducing Q3 2020 depreciation and amortization expense by $634 million and increasing net income by $479 million. The company incurred more than $2.5 billion in COVID-19 related costs in Q3 2020, totaling more than $7.5 billion for the first three quarters of 2020, and hired over 250,000 full-time and part-time employees since February 2020. As of September 30, 2020, Amazon had $32.2 billion of unsecured senior notes outstanding, including $10.0 billion issued in June 2020, and held $68.4 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities. Operating cash flow was $12.0 billion in Q3 2020. Tax contingencies were approximately $3.0 billion, and the company continues to appeal a 2017 European Commission state aid decision involving an estimated recovery amount of approximately €250 million.

This patent application describes systems and methods for creating arbitrarily-shaped ion energy distribution functions (IEDFs) using shaped-pulse bias in plasma substrate processing. A shaped pulse bias is applied to a power electrode of a process chamber, and the amplitude of the negative voltage jump (V OUT), and hence the sheath voltage, is modulated in a predetermined manner such that the relative number of pulses at a specific amplitude determines the relative ion fraction at the corresponding ion energy. Alternatively, the voltage ramp during the ion current compensation phase can be adjusted to overcompensate or undercompensate for ion current, producing wider IEDFs—a wider, double-peaked profile for overcompensation and a wider, single-peaked profile for undercompensation. The substrate processing system includes a substrate support assembly and a bias supply with memory and a processor for controlling the voltage applied to the power electrode. Applications include hard-mask opening and high aspect ratio etch processes requiring controlled IEDF shapes.
The Fourth Circuit affirmed the district court's denial of Paul Nagy's Fed. R. Civ. P. 60(b) motion, finding no reversible error and dispensing with oral argument.

A Kazakh man died and another was hospitalised after a fire broke out on the Kazakh steppes, triggered by falling debris from a Soyuz 2.1a rocket launched from the Baikonur cosmodrome on Wednesday. The two men were working on debris-clearing for NPO Mashinostroyeniya. Roscosmos attributed the death to difficult meteorological conditions, and the fire was extinguished by around 2100 GMT.

The NVIDIA Ampere GA10x architecture, fabricated on Samsung's 8nm process, introduces the GA102 GPU with 28.3 billion transistors, 10752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor Cores. The architecture delivers up to 2x performance improvements over Turing in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI.

Key features include: 2x FP32 processing through dual datapaths in each SM partition; second-generation RT Cores that double ray/triangle intersection testing rates and add hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur via a new Interpolate Triangle Position unit; and third-generation Tensor Cores supporting new data types (TF32, BF16) and Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity, which doubles throughput by skipping zero-valued weights.

GA10x GPUs are the first to use GDDR6X memory with PAM4 signaling, achieving data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth in the GeForce RTX 3090. Other features include third-generation NVLink (112.5 GB/sec total bandwidth between two GPUs), PCIe Gen 4 support, and a new RTX IO technology that enables GPU-based loading and decompression of game assets in conjunction with Microsoft's DirectStorage API, improving I/O performance up to 100x versus traditional storage.

The architecture supports HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a for up to 8K60 displays, includes fifth-generation NVDEC with first-in-industry AV1 hardware decode, and seventh-generation NVENC encoding. DLSS is enhanced with a 9x scaling factor enabling 8K gaming at 60 fps. A new Error Detection and Replay (EDR) feature helps users identify safe GDDR6X overclocking limits.

The NVIDIA A40 GPU targets data center visual computing workloads, while the RTX A6000 serves desktop workstations, both offering 48 GB of GDDR6 memory scalable to 96 GB via NVLink.

The Princeton Offense is an unstructured, team-oriented style of basketball play, developed and popularized by Pete Carril, that relies on constant motion and defensive reads rather than set plays, with the back door cut as its signature option. All five players are involved at all times, and it requires players who can shoot well from outside, pass and drive with either hand, possess court savvy, and maintain an unselfish attitude, patience, ball control, and superior physical conditioning. Coaches must be fully committed to it, following the "All or None Principle." Benefits include teaching teamwork, never needing to reset the offense or call plays, difficulty of scouting, and making it harder for defenses to block out. The offense is adaptable to any defense, punishing sagging man-to-man or zone defenses with strong outside shooting and patience. Proper spacing of 12 to 15 feet spreads the defense, discourages help and double teaming, and forces defenders to guard the entire court. It typically starts in a 2-3 high post alignment and flows through three phases: entries, exchanges and down screens, and post action leading to back door opportunities. Tempo control involves patience, often 15 to 20 passes per possession, and minimized turnovers. Back cuts serve as pressure releases against defensive overplays, dribbling is used sparingly, and post ups tend to set up kick out passes to outside shooters rather than scoring. The offense also includes quick hitting specials and press break preparation. Psychologically, its reputation as a "giant slayer" and low-possession, ball-control style creates pressure, fatigue, and errors in opponents, while the offense itself remains stable and independent of hot or cold shooting nights.

A hockey team won a road game, boosted by a shorthanded goal, and aims to return to Edmonton where they play well at home. Winning there would force another game. They played four lines against the opponent's three, skated well, and clogged the neutral zone. A player's strong first period set the tone for the victory.

In Secor v. Siver, the Iowa Supreme Court affirmed the district court's dismissal of an action to recover on a New York deficiency judgment against James E. and Elizabeth Siver, who had conveyed town property to their sons; the judgment defendants counterclaimed that John S. Secor's false representations about a mountain farm had induced the original property exchange. The court held that objections to a witness's competency must specifically state the facts creating incompetency; a general objection that a witness is "incompetent and unqualified" is insufficient, and an objection to testimony about personal "transactions" with a deceased person does not necessarily raise the question of personal "communications." Interested witnesses could testify against the administrator regarding the description, quality, and value of the land, their reliance on the representations, and the condition of the property received. On the merits, the trial court was justified in finding for the appellees, who were grossly overreached through material misrepresentations. Costs taxed to the administratrix in her official capacity would not be retaxed to her individually on the claim that she acted officiously. The decree was affirmed on both appeals. Justices Ladd, Salinger, and Stevens dissented, contending the objections were sufficient and the testimony inadmissible.

Volunteers across southern New South Wales and the ACT are conducting a platypus census during late winter, when the animals are most active. Antia Brademann, Cooma region Waterwatch coordinator, said this was the fourth year surveying the Upper Murrumbidgee River. No platypus were sighted on this occasion, though a native water rat was spotted. Four years of data indicate platypus numbers are stable at that site, and the survey is the only formal platypus monitoring occurring in the Upper Murrumbidgee. Platypus numbers have declined across eastern Australia and Tasmania since European settlement due to habitat change, reduced river flows, exotic fish, and discarded waste. People are also encouraged to report sightings at any time of year.

A hockey coach said his team was outmuscled in the second period but responded well late in that period and in the third. He praised a key player who contributes at even strength, on the power play, and on the penalty kill. Noting the team was the best in third-period scoring during the regular season, he said that continued in the playoffs, as the twins' line wore down Boston's defense, tied the game, and won in overtime. He was pleased with Manny's return, citing his faceoffs and increased minutes. Injury updates are game-time decisions because he wants to prevent opponents from exploiting weaknesses and to protect players. He recalled needing three years to distinguish Danny from the more outspoken Henrik. If the returning player plays, he will be eased in and used on faceoffs without breaking up the Torres-Lapierre-Hansen line. The coach also wants fewer penalties and a more effective power play.

The passage presents a guide to ten AI tools for content creation in 2025: ChatGPT for written content, Canva Magic Studio for visual design, RunwayML for video creation, Midjourney V6 for image generation, Synthesia for AI avatar videos, Descript for audio/video editing with transcription, ElevenLabs for voice synthesis, Tribescaler for viral content optimization, Clickable for ad creation, and CopyAI for marketing copy. This MIT lecture reviews Wald's identity for a random walk with two thresholds (α above 0, β below 0), where J is the stopping time at which the walk first crosses either threshold. The identity states E[e^(rS_J − Jγ(r))] = 1 for any r in the range of the moment generating function, and applying the Markov inequality gives P(S_J ≥ α) ≤ e^(−αr*), where r* is the second root of γ(r); r* is identified as the crucial parameter in threshold-crossing problems. The lecture then revisits hypothesis testing, covering the likelihood ratio, sufficient statistics, and the MAP threshold rule, noting that the log-likelihood ratio is a sum of IID random variables (a random walk) and that r* = 1 for all such problems. Sequential testing—continuing observations until a threshold is crossed—is defended as valid because the procedure is fixed in advance, analogous to ARQ in communication systems; error probability is bounded by e^(−α), with a trade-off between the number of trials under one hypothesis and the error probability under the other. Taking derivatives of Wald's identity at r = 0 yields Wald's equality and, for zero-mean walks, E[S_J²] = σ_X² E[J]; for the simple symmetric random walk, E[J] = −βα. Finally, martingales are defined by E[Z_n | Z_{n−1},…,Z_1] = Z_{n−1}, with a lemma extending conditioning to earlier terms, examples (zero-mean random walks, sums of dependent zero-conditional-mean variables, product-form martingales, and the double-or-nothing game showing limits and expectations cannot be interchanged), definitions of submartingales and supermartingales, and Jensen's inequality for convex functions.

The passage specifies requirements for Socket 940, which mates with a 940-pin ceramic µPGA package. Required markings include the socket identifier, directional designator, triangular pin A01 orientation symbol, UL symbol, and lot traceability number, positioned to remain visible after assembly. Contacts use high-strength copper alloy plated with minimum 1.27-µm nickel and 0.76-µm gold on mating areas. Solder balls are tin/lead (63/37 ± 5%), 0.76 mm diameter, with 0.20 mm co-planarity. A stainless steel lever actuates the contacts; insertion/extraction forces must not exceed 2 kgf with the lever open, extraction requires minimum 0.013 kgf per pin when closed, and lever actuation force must be under 3.6 kgf. Pins must displace less than 1.0 mm during actuation. The socket must maintain integrity after 50 actuation cycles. Visual inspections prohibit missing, damaged, or malformed solder balls, contacts, covers, and levers. Electrically, contacts are rated 1.5 A with less than 30°C temperature rise; LLCR must not exceed 25 mΩ; partial self-inductance must be under 4 nH; capacitance between nearest pins under 1 pF; differential impedance 100 Ω ± 10%; propagation delay skew under 10 ps; dielectric withstanding voltage minimum 650 Vac; and insulation resistance minimum 1000 MΩ.

A new study shows that adding four live ants to warmed cow's milk—a traditional method once popular in Bulgaria and Turkey—ferments the milk into yogurt. Bacteria on the ants, formic acid produced by the ants, and milk-digesting enzymes from both ants and bacteria acidify and thicken the milk. Researchers buried the jar in an ant mound overnight, where nest heat acted as an incubator; the resulting milk was tangy and herbaceous. Live ants ferment milk better than frozen or dehydrated ones, but they can carry a parasite that in rare cases causes liver or gastrointestinal disease, so researchers do not recommend making this yogurt at home.

Manufacturers struggle to achieve full-screen smartphones because of the selfie camera and sensors. Xiaomi moved them to the bottom on the Mi Mix 2s, while Apple's iPhone X notch was widely copied by the industry. Vivo's Apex concept used an under-screen fingerprint sensor and a pop-up selfie camera, though its complex mechanism adds cost and bulk. The author proposes transparent OLED panels, which are emissive and need no backlight, hiding the camera behind the screen with per-pixel opacity control. Initially limited to high-end phones, the technology has already been showcased by Samsung, LG, Panasonic, and Sharp.

The Clark County School District's Board of Trustees voted Dr. Jesus Jara as the new superintendent on May 2, 2018. Jara has been deputy superintendent for Orange County Public Schools in Orlando since 2012 and previously served as superintendent of Monroe County Public Schools in Florida. The board was split on his election; Trustee Linda Young and others supported Dr. Mike Barton, who lost a 4-3 vote. After trustees argued for two hours, Vice President Carolyn Edwards called for a vote on Jara, who won. Six finalists were considered: internal candidates Barton, Jesse Welsh, and Eva White, and external candidates Donald Haddad, Shonda Huery Hardman, and Jara. The district received 77 applications, and all candidates were publicly interviewed April 27. Jara is expected to start in June before Pat Skorkowsky retires.

The command moves the contents of one or more pages belonging to an SNP guest within the system physical address space and may serve as a faster replacement for the PAGE_MOVE command. 2M pages must consist of physically contiguous 4K pages and be 2M aligned; DMA to migrating pages is not supported, and CPU access to the pages must be prevented. Source pages must be in Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid state, while destination pages must be in the Pre-Migration state. Firmware validates RMP_ENFORCE, page states, GCTX_PADDR, and exclusive RMP access, then issues TLB invalidation and sync, copies data, and updates both RMPs, returning status codes such as PM_INVALID_PAGE_STATE. Errors are reported in commands, migration list entries, the PM_STATUS register, or via MCA. A batch can cover up to 128 pages, and hardware errors may make the entire batch unrecoverable; the system may eventually cease functioning, allowing software to save state before reboot.

The player expressed surprise and gratitude at the opportunity given by coach Burns, who showed belief in him. He felt calm on game day, crediting the veterans and leadership for keeping the team loose. In his third season with the organization after two and a half years in Albany, he was called up in January and trained hard in case of injuries, never expecting to reach the Stanley Cup finals. He wanted to contribute in any way, not necessarily on the scoresheet. He credited the team's depth, with different players stepping up throughout the playoffs, and noted Jeff's first goal, Marty's performance, and simple plays that wore the opponent down. He said he was not trying to fill the shoes of an absent leader who inspired him, and described the final moments and feeling as unbelievable.

Action on Smoking and Health (ASH) argues that zero tobacco deaths is the only acceptable goal, framing smokers as victims and placing responsibility with the tobacco industry for marketing products engineered to be addictive and deadly. In March, the global health community adopted the Cape Town Declaration on Human Rights and a Tobacco-Free World, endorsed by over 150 organizations. Founded in 1967, ASH is America's oldest anti-tobacco organization, dedicated to a world with zero tobacco deaths.

Eddie Woo, a Sydney maths teacher, has risen from anonymity to celebrity through his YouTube channel "Wootube," which he began in 2012 to film lessons for a seriously ill student. The channel now has over 200,000 subscribers and more than 12 million views. In 2018, Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull named him Australia's Local Hero, and he was one of 10 finalists for the $US1 million Global Teacher Prize awarded by the Varkey Foundation; Andria Zafirakou of the UK won. NSW Premier Gladys Berejiklian announced Woo's new role as a 'master teacher' with the NSW Department of Education, leading innovation in maths teaching and mentoring students and teachers statewide, while retaining his position at Cherrybrook Technology High School. He recently completed a four-day road trip through the NSW Riverina, drawing packed audiences in Griffith and Wagga Wagga. Officials describe him as an exceptional explainer of mathematics, likening him to Julius Sumner Miller. Woo's brother notes fame keeps him away from his job and family, but Woo says he is coping well.

The passage discusses gamification and games in academic education, presenting four projects conducted at the Institute of Pedagogy at the University of Wrocław in 2014 and 2015.

According to European and Polish qualification standards, higher education should provide knowledge, skills, and social competences. Contemporary development of the web society and knowledge economy requires new ways of transferring knowledge, making innovative techniques crucial. Gamification—the conscious use of game design mechanisms to increase dedication and loyalty and modify behaviours—can access gamers' inner motivation. Tkaczyk notes that in 2010, 99% of young Americans played computer games, creating "a system of education parallel to schools." Gamification enables concentrated motivation, requiring clear aims, instructions, certainty of task completion, and immediate feedback. Fun produces positive emotions that facilitate remembering. "Ludology" combines Latin "ludus" (game/play) and Greek "logos" (word). Aarseth defined game elements as gameplay, game structure, and game world; game structure comprises winning conditions, aims, actions, obstacles, and rules.

The four projects:

1. Kulturalny Wrocław: A location-based game combining cultural education and IT courses, run in five editions for MA pedagogy students. Teams located Wrocław places connected with cultural events, solved riddles, and completed a crossword. Participants assessed it highly as an educational and socialising method, noting persistent knowledge gained through experience. The project was inexpensive and logistically simple.

2. Gamification in career management (Lower Silesia): A five-day seminar for higher education students aimed at increasing graduates' labour market competitiveness. It included expert meetings, a science-fiction plot about a space mission, point systems, badges, and prizes, ending with an exam-game. Results were highly positive: broad content covered, top exam results, fast integration, and participant self-diagnosis. However, instructors reported enormous preparation effort, concluding such courses are worthwhile only when conducted repeatedly.

3. Entrepreneurship project: The location-based game "Become an Entrepreneur" involved 25 participants in teams named after famous entrepreneurs, completing quests to earn "money" while avoiding "props" symbolising difficulties, finishing with calculating and paying income tax. Students praised its socialising character, combination of movement and intellectual effort, and potential for developing soft skills. Competition was evaluated ambivalently, as were weather dependence and unfamiliar locations.

4. Learning through games: A LARP game, "Spell of the Black Magic Master," for 12 participants playing adventurers who neutralise a spell within 120 minutes, with character cards defining roles. Students with prior RPG/LARP experience focused on opportunities, while inexperienced students had difficulties and lower satisfaction. Despite integration problems and complex rules, educational goals in negotiations, communication, and group management were achieved. Preparation was time-consuming and required a pilot session.

The conclusion states that location-based games have great potential in academic education. Given students' extensive computer gaming experience, educational projects should draw on this interest. Games must be well-selected considering students' experience, lesson topics, time, and expenses. Simple games with clear rules are well-received, while longer, complex games work best as supplements within subsidised projects, preceded by socialising activities and tutorials.
In Rodes v. Yates (1912), the appeal was dismissed because an order sustaining a demurrer to an amended petition is not final and not appealable.

The IRS announced inflation-adjusted tax brackets and deductions for 2026 under the One Big Beautiful Bill, providing modest relief to offset rising living costs and prevent bracket creep. The standard deduction rises to $32,200 for married couples filing jointly, $16,100 for single filers, and $24,150 for heads of household. The 37 percent top marginal rate applies to incomes above $640,600 for individuals and $768,700 for couples. The estate tax exemption increases to $15 million from $13.99 million, with adjustments to earned income and child tax credit thresholds, and a new $6,000 deduction for taxpayers aged 65 and older begins with the 2025 tax year. Analysts view the changes as a middle-ground approach, though economists caution they may not fully counteract inflationary pressures if price growth accelerates. The passage also lists various financial headlines and describes Pan Finance, a global financial intelligence publication with over 200,000 readers across 150 countries.

The New Jersey Supreme Court affirmed the Chancery Division's denials of defendants' applications for costs and counsel fees under N.J.S. 2A:15-53 of the Anti-Injunction Act in two consolidated appeals. In the strike case, following a 1959 strike and mass picketing at plaintiff's Burlington plant, the company obtained temporary restraints and an interlocutory injunction; the Appellate Division reversed on procedural grounds—delayed findings and overbroad restraint—while concluding the union's conduct afforded a substantive basis for injunctive relief. The court held that costs and counsel fees under section 53 are mandatory only when injunctive relief is denied or reversed on the merits; because the reversal rested solely on procedural violations and the suit was not wrongfully brought, the denial was proper. In the arbitration case, concerning whether a discharged striker's grievance was arbitrable under the new collective bargaining agreement, the court held the action, despite its ancillary request for restraint, was essentially a declaratory judgment suit outside the Anti-Injunction Act's scope, so no fees were allowable; the claim was also raised too late. The court reaffirmed Westinghouse Electric Corp. v. Local No. 449, holding fee allowances mandatory within the Act's scope when relief is denied or reversed on the merits. Judgments were affirmed, costs were awarded to respondent in the arbitration case only, and appellants were granted leave to reapply for statutory trial costs in the strike case.

Central Huron Council heard a presentation from Huron County's Acting CAO, Director of Cultural Services and County Librarian Meighan Wark proposing renovations to the Clinton Library to achieve accreditation and improve services. In 2015, the Huron County Library and 11 of its branches received five-year accreditation under the Ontario Public Library Guidelines, but the Clinton branch did not, due to accessibility issues and insufficient square footage. Wark explained that the county is responsible for staff, materials, furniture, equipment, and services, while the municipality is responsible for the building, maintenance, and utilities. Renovations would need to meet accessibility standards, including lower shelves and wider aisles, as well as minimum square footage based on population served. Wark, along with Clinton Branch Manager Michelle Carter and Deputy County Librarian Sharon Cox, delivered a report outlining a component approach, in which required components are agreed upon with the municipality before an architect prepares draft drawings for council and community review. Mayor Jim Ginn asked about provincial funding; Wark said a shovel-ready project would improve the chances of obtaining a grant. Council will continue discussions, and if the municipality commits, the Huron County Library would invest in the library's interior to match that commitment.

The passage is a user manual for the SanDisk Sansa Fuze MP3 player, a portable digital audio/video player featuring a 1.9" color screen, digital FM tuner (if applicable), built-in microphone, and microSDHC card expansion slot. It supports MP3, WAV, WMA, secure WMA, and audiobook formats, with video compatibility via MPEG4 and additional formats through Sansa Media Converter software. The non-replaceable rechargeable battery lasts up to 24 hours of audio or 5 hours of video playback.

The manual covers basic operations: the power switch turns the player on/off (hold 2 seconds) and resets it (hold 10 seconds); a thumbwheel navigates menus and adjusts volume; and the Hold Switch disables all controls to prevent accidental operation. The battery charges via USB connected to a powered-on computer, or via optional AC or car adapters, though music, videos, and photos cannot be used while connected to a computer. The manual also covers firmware updates and warns that formatting the player deletes all content.

Music transfers via drag-and-drop or Windows Media Player; Audible files require Audible Manager. The Sansa Media Converter converts and transfers photos and videos, offering cropping, rotating, and resizing.

Playback instructions address music (with repeat, shuffle, equalizer, Go List, and delete options), audiobooks (chapter mode and playback speed), videos (bookmarks, ratings, brightness, deletion), and photos/slideshows (shuffle, loop, slide duration, music selection, Go Lists, deletion).

The FM radio supports live listening, up to 30 preset stations, region/mode settings, and recording. The built-in microphone enables voice recording. The product is intended for home and personal use; copying copyrighted material without permission may be prohibited by law.

Charlie Alliston, 18 at the time, is on trial at the Old Bailey for the manslaughter of Kim Briggs, a 44-year-old mother of two, whom he struck while cycling at nearly 20mph on Old Street, east London, on February 12, 2016. He was riding a fixed wheel track bike without a front brake, which is unlawful on roads. Mrs Briggs suffered two skull fractures and bleeding on the brain and died a week later. The court heard Alliston posted online comments blaming the victim, claiming she ignored his warnings. Prosecutors said reconstructions showed he could have stopped in time with a front brake, and that he had previously removed brakes from another bike. He bought the bike for £470 a month before the collision. Alliston denies manslaughter and causing bodily harm by wanton or furious driving.

Elijah Brown scored 27 points, including 17 of New Mexico's final 19, as the Lobos beat Boise State 78-73. New Mexico (16-10, 9-5 Mountain West) took control with an 11-0 run late in the first half, and Brown and Jordan Hunter later sparked a decisive 12-2 run. Obij Ajet and Damien Jefferson each scored 14, with Ajet adding five blocks. Chandler Hutchison had a career-high 31 points for Boise State (16-8, 9-4), which never led. New Mexico made 22 free throws to Boise State's 13. Tim Williams missed his fourth straight game with a foot injury.

The passage describes the NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture. The Turing SM contains 64 FP32 and 64 INT32 cores, supports concurrent FP32/INT32 execution (yielding roughly 36% additional floating-point throughput), and includes eight Tensor Cores and one RT Core per SM. It is partitioned into four processing blocks sharing a 96 KB L1 data cache/shared memory, delivering a 50% performance improvement per CUDA core over Pascal.

Enhanced Tensor Cores add INT8 and INT4 precision modes for inference. The Tesla T4 (TU104-based) includes 320 Tensor Cores, delivering up to 130 TOPS INT8 and 260 TOPS INT4, with up to 40X higher inference performance and 50X better energy efficiency than CPU-based servers.

Turing is the first architecture to use GDDR6 memory (14 Gbps, 20% more power efficient than GDDR5X), doubles L2 cache capacity, and improves compression for approximately 50% higher effective bandwidth than Pascal. A new display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K at 60 Hz, HDR tone mapping, and enhanced NVENC/NVDEC. VirtualLink over USB-C enables single-connector VR, and NVLink replaces SLI bridges on TU102/TU104 (two-way SLI only).

RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, enabling real-time ray tracing at 10+ Giga Rays/sec (about 10x Pascal) through a hybrid rendering model combining rasterization, ray tracing, and denoising.

NVIDIA NGX provides AI features using Tensor Cores: DLSS (trained on 64x supersampled images, achieving TAA-comparable quality with roughly half the shading work), InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.

New graphics features include Mesh Shading (Task and Mesh shaders eliminating CPU draw call bottlenecks), Variable Rate Shading (per-16x16-pixel shading rate control, supporting content adaptive, motion adaptive, and foveated rendering), Texture Space Shading (decoupled shading in texture space), and Multi-View Rendering (up to four views per pass).

Chip details: TU104 contains 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores (used in GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000); TU106 contains 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores without NVLink (GeForce RTX 2070). RTX-OPS is introduced as a workload-based metric combining Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 throughputs (RTX 2080 Ti totals 78).

This retrospective cohort study used the HCUP National Inpatient Sample (2017–2019) to examine whether perinatal mood disorders are associated with peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) and adverse cardiac events. Among over 2.2 million pregnancy-related hospitalizations, 168,729 (7.4%) included a mood disorder diagnosis. Patients with mood disorders had higher rates of PPCM (0.12% vs 0.05%) and composite adverse cardiac events (0.36% vs 0.14%). After adjustment for demographic and clinical confounders, mood disorders remained independently associated with PPCM (aOR 1.36), the composite cardiac outcome (aOR 1.57), and pulmonary edema (aOR 1.62), but not maternal death or other individual cardiac outcomes. The authors conclude that perinatal mood disorders are associated with increased rates of PPCM and other cardiac events, with implications for mental health care and PPCM prevention. Limitations include reliance on ICD-10 codes, restriction to inpatient data, and absence of long-term post-discharge outcomes.

Preempt announced new data and enforcement integrations for its Preempt Behavioral Firewall at RSA 2017. New data integrations include Okta, Azure Active Directory, and VPN gateways, while enforcement integrations include SecureAuth, RSA SecurID, Duo, Google Authenticator, and HP Aruba ClearPass. The Behavioral Firewall combines User and Entity Behavioral Analytics with automated adaptive response to protect organizations from security breaches, malicious insiders, and risky behavior by detecting threats in real-time and applying granular policies to block, notify, or challenge users.

A December 2017 Harvard Institute of Politics poll found 65 percent of millennials favor Democrats over Republicans (33 percent). Only 14 percent believe America is headed in the right direction, Trump's approval among them is 25 percent, and 61 percent support stricter gun laws, up from 49 percent in 2013.

In card identification mode, the host resets cards, validates the operating voltage range, identifies cards, and requests their Relative Card Address (RCA), using only the CMD line. CMD0 (GO_IDLE_STATE) resets cards to Idle State except those in Inactive State; after power-on or CMD0, cards default to RCA=0x0000, 400KHz clock, and default driver strength. In UHS-II Mode, RCA is not cleared by CMD0. CMD8 (SEND_IF_COND) verifies operating voltage via the VHS field; compatible cards echo the voltage and check pattern, while incompatible cards give no response. CMD8 must precede the first ACMD41 for SDHC/SDXC cards.

Washington police will announce charges against 12 Turkish security agents—seven with felonies and five with misdemeanors—related to violence during Turkey's president's visit last month. Two men, Sinan Narin and Eyup Yildirim, were arrested for a violent altercation outside the Turkish ambassador's residence on May 16.

A hockey player reflects on his team's playoff series loss, crediting his teammates for their hard work and acknowledging the opposing team deserved to win. He notes home ice advantage was significant, with all teams winning their home games amid loud crowds. He says preparation leading into the playoffs was key and that every game must be played to win. He was unsurprised by being booed in New Jersey while receiving an individual award, calling it "icing on the cake" compared to the Stanley Cup he wanted. He praises the opposing goalie as possibly the best since Patrick retired. He plans to approach next season one game at a time and expresses sadness at not winning the Cup for his ill mother, but says he will move on.

Apple's iOS 11.4 update introduces AirPlay 2, enabling multi-room support, stereo HomePod pairing, streaming to multiple AirPlay devices, an increased network buffer, and uninterrupted music during calls. Siri on HomePod gains calendar support, though anyone can modify calendars since individual voice recognition remains unavailable. Third-party companies including Bose, Pioneer, Sonos, Bang & Olufsen, and Bowers & Wilkins announced AirPlay 2 support, but AirPlay requires an iOS device as the streaming hub. The update also adds Messages in iCloud, which syncs messages across devices but consumes iCloud storage. Overall, the update brings the HomePod closer to parity with Amazon and Google offerings.

Mary Meeker's Internet Trends report shows time spent on short-form videos in China climbed 360 percent in 2017, yet 76 percent of consumers use only one short-video app. Leading players Douyin and Kuaishou each report about 100 million daily active users and 52 minutes of daily viewing. Long-form video ad budgets overtook network TV in China last year, and short-form viewing is fast approaching long-form levels.

Stocks rebounded Wednesday as banks and energy companies surged and smaller companies made large gains, recovering nearly all losses from the previous day. Investors grew hopeful Italy could avoid new elections after prime minister nominee Carlo Cottarelli said there were "new possibilities" to form a government. The S&P 500 rose 1.3 percent to 2,724.01, the Dow climbed 1.3 percent to 24,667.78, and the Russell 2000 closed at a record high. Bond yields rose, helping bank stocks recover, while U.S. crude oil jumped 2.2 percent to $68.21 per barrel. Trade concerns involving the U.S., China, and the EU persisted.

The court modified Supreme Court's order, holding that summary judgment was improperly granted dismissing Hartford's claims alleging bad faith settlement negotiations by General Accident. Evidence, including testimony that a $1,000,000 settlement would have been accepted before trial, presented triable issues of fact regarding bad faith and damages for jury determination. The court affirmed dismissal of Hartford's fourth cause of action alleging violations of Insurance Law § 2601.

NVIDIA Corporation's Form 8-K reports results of its 2018 Annual Meeting of Stockholders held May 16, 2018. Stockholders approved an amendment and restatement of the 2007 Equity Incentive Plan, increasing its share reserve by 23,000,000 shares, and an amendment and restatement of the 2012 Employee Stock Purchase Plan, increasing its share reserve by 13,500,000 shares; both plans had been previously approved by the Board's Compensation Committee subject to stockholder approval. Eleven directors—Robert K. Burgess, Tench Coxe, Persis S. Drell, James C. Gaither, Jen-Hsun Huang, Dawn Hudson, Harvey C. Jones, Michael G. McCaffery, Mark L. Perry, A. Brooke Seawell, and Mark A. A study by the University of Rochester Medical Centre, published in Scientific Reports, found that low doses of alcohol improved the glymphatic system—the brain's waste-clearance process—in mice. Mice given the equivalent of approximately 2.5 daily drinks showed less brain inflammation and more efficient removal of cerebrospinal fluid waste, including proteins associated with Alzheimer's disease, compared to non-drinking mice, while performing identically in cognitive and motor tests. Intermediate doses (7.9 standard drinks daily) reduced glymphatic function, though it recovered within 24 hours after chronic exposure ended. High doses (21 drinks daily) increased inflammation markers and impaired cognitive and motor abilities. Lead author Dr Maiken Nedergaard stated the findings match the J-shaped model, in which low alcohol doses benefit health while excessive consumption is detrimental.

The TPS7H500x-SP series (TPS7H5001-SP, TPS7H5002-SP, TPS7H5003-SP, TPS7H5004-SP) comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting topologies such as buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge, with switching frequencies up to 2 MHz.

Key operational features include:
- External synchronization mode, where the RT pin is left floating and an external clock (200 kHz–4 MHz, 40–60% duty cycle) at twice the desired switching frequency is applied to the SYNC pin.
- Primary-secondary mode, allowing two controllers to be synchronized via the SYNC pin, with the secondary inverting the clock to produce a 90° or 270° phase shift.
- Primary switching outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) with roughly 150 mA peak current capability; external gate drivers are recommended.
- Programmable dead times (via PS and SP pins) and leading edge blank time (via LEB pin); the TPS7H5003-SP has fixed 50-ns values for both.
- Pulse skipping mode to prevent minimum on-time issues during high-frequency operation and soft-start.
- Configurable maximum duty cycle (50%, 75%, or 100%) via the DCL pin; the TPS7H5004-SP supports only 50%.
- Current sensing via the CS_ILIM pin, with a 1.05-V threshold triggering cycle-by-cycle limiting followed by hiccup mode, whose timing is set by the HICC capacitor.
- FAULT pin for external protection triggering shutdown above 0.6 V.
- Slope compensation via the RSC pin to prevent subharmonic oscillation, and Type 2A or 2B frequency compensation options.
- Thermal shutdown at 175°C (typical), restarting below 160°C.

An application example details the design of a 500-kHz synchronous push-pull converter using GaN devices, covering component selection including the transformer, FETs, output inductor, output capacitance (including single-event transient mitigation), sense resistor, and compensation components. Power supply recommendations specify a 4–14 V input with proper bypassing, and layout guidelines address noise reduction, grounding separation, trace routing, and component placement. The document also includes related documentation, revision history, and packaging information.

The passage explains run fits in football defense, noting that while coverage evolution receives attention due to modern spread offenses, run fits are equally important and vary by team talent and philosophy. Run fits stem from two influences: front spacing (even or odd, determined post-snap by where the open gap or "bubble" is located) and the coverage played behind the fit. Spacing is categorized as 7, 8, or 9 man, based on the number of defenders in the box. In 7-man spacing, the defense is down one defender, uses middle-of-field-open coverage, and employs tools like two-gapping, spill-overlap, and stack-track-fallback. In 8-man spacing ("gapped out"), defenders match offensive numbers, use middle-of-field-closed coverage, one-gap fits, indicator fitting, and lever-spill-lever. In 9-man spacing ("maxed out"), the defense has an extra box defender, uses cover 0, and can play aggressively in each gap. The passage also applies these concepts to 3-4 defense examples across all three spacings.

Sophomore forward Wenyen Gabriel announced he will keep his name in the 2018 NBA draft and begin his professional career rather than return to Kentucky for his junior season. He declared without an agent on April 18 and was the only one of six UK draft entrants not invited to the NBA scouting combine. As a sophomore, he averaged 6.8 points and 5.4 rebounds per game and led Kentucky with 40 blocked shots. Coach John Calipari praised his versatility. Gabriel is likely to begin his career overseas or in the NBA's developmental league, leaving Kentucky's roster without a scholarship junior or senior for now.

In this MIT lecture, Andrew Lo opens with remarks on current market conditions: the stock market is down, three-month T-bill rates have risen, and the Fed is working to maintain liquid markets amid fear surrounding the rescue package. He notes that low borrowing rates suggest banks are waiting on the sidelines rather than facing structural problems. A student describes surviving Argentina's crisis, illustrating that crises create opportunities. Lo discusses psychological biases that paralyze decision-making under fear and proposes an innovation: a website posting transaction prices for complex securities like CDOs and CDSes—an "eBay for CDOs"—to provide transparency and liquidity. He strongly criticizes proposals to suspend mark-to-market accounting, calling it the worst idea of the crisis.

The main lecture covers forward and futures contracts. Lo motivates hedging with examples of currency risk faced by a US machine-tool exporter and Caterpillar's sales fluctuations. He addresses debates over speculators' valuable role, contrasting views of derivatives as efficient risk-management tools versus Warren Buffett's "financial weapons of mass destruction," and presents differing corporate hedging policies: Homestake Mining (no hedging), American Barrick (hedging for earnings stability), and Battle Mountain Gold (hedging up to 25%). A Guay and Kothari study found 57% of 413 large firms used derivatives in 1997.

A forward contract is a binding agreement to buy an asset at a future date at a price fixed today; the buyer is "long," the seller "short," and the forward price is set so the contract's initial value is zero. Forwards are customized, nonstandard, over-the-counter instruments carrying illiquidity and counterparty risk, illustrated by a soybean example involving a tofu manufacturer. Futures contracts address these problems through standardization, daily mark-to-market cash exchanges, and a Futures Clearing Corporation as intermediary. Lo explains margin requirements using a NYMEX crude oil futures example, noting most futures are cash-settled, though currencies remain more commonly traded via forwards.

This MIT lecture discusses light forces, particularly the stimulated (dipole) force, using the dressed atom picture. The professor reviews the dressed atom framework, in which the atom-laser Hamiltonian is diagonalized first and spontaneous emission is added afterward. In the strong Rabi frequency (secular) limit, the Optical Bloch equations decouple into separate rate equations for populations and coherences, naturally explaining the different widths of the Mollow triplet's central feature and sidebands. Two complementary pictures of spontaneous emission are presented: antibunching in the bare basis versus alternating red/blue sideband emission in the dressed basis, which require mutually exclusive temporal or spectral resolution to observe.

The stimulated force is expressed as the population-weighted average of opposite forces on the two dressed levels: red detuning yields attraction, blue detuning repulsion, and on resonance the average force vanishes. A time lag in population adjustment (non-adiabaticity) produces friction, explaining blue molasses cooling in a blue-detuned standing wave. Heating arises from force fluctuations when spontaneous emission switches the atom between dressed levels, dominating photon recoil in strong fields. Sisyphus cooling is described: atoms climb potential hills and emit near the hilltops, dropping to the bottom and losing energy each cycle. In the perturbative limit, the minimum achievable temperature equals the lattice depth, so two-level atoms cannot be laser-cooled into localized optical lattice sites. The lecture concludes with four derivations of the dipole potential, including the macroscopic refraction picture underlying optical tweezers, and outlines remaining classes on magnetic trapping, evaporative cooling, Bose and Fermi gases, and quantum logic with ions.

North Carolina is expanding child care academies—short training programs lasting two to six weeks with 20 to 64 hours of class time—designed to quickly prepare early childhood educators at little to no cost to participants. Operating in at least 11 counties, the academies address staffing shortages affecting 60% of licensed child care providers. Two models exist: a classroom-ready model qualifying graduates to work in licensed facilities, and a teaching credential model that includes EDU 119 coursework, qualifying graduates as lead teachers. A $1.476 million pilot passed the North Carolina House but was excluded from the final budget signed by Gov. Stein; however, the Division of Child Development and Early Education offers grants up to $50,000 for up to 10 institutions. Local programs, funded by sources including the Camber Foundation, Dogwood Health Trust, and Duke Community Affairs, have graduated students who entered child care jobs or pursued further education, and more than a dozen additional community colleges have expressed interest.

In this MIT 6.832 lecture, Russ Tedrake discusses trajectory optimization as a special case of policy search, where open-loop control trajectories are parameterized (e.g., as zero-order hold sequences) and optimized by minimizing a cost function over the parameters. He covers two main approaches: shooting methods and direct collocation methods.

Shooting methods simulate the system forward with given parameters and iteratively adjust them to reach desired final conditions. Gradients of the cost can be computed via the adjoint method (backpropagation through time), which requires forward and backward passes but carries only a vector, or via real-time recurrent learning (RTRL), which requires only forward simulation but carries a matrix of partial derivatives. Each has trade-offs in efficiency and suitability for constraints.

Sequential quadratic programming (SQP) solvers like SNOPT are recommended over simple gradient descent because they eliminate learning rate tuning, converge faster, and handle constraints easily. Demonstrations include pendulum swing-up, cart-pole, and acrobot.

Direct collocation augments the parameter vector with state variables, making dynamics consistency explicit constraints. This allows cost evaluation without simulation, faster gradient computation, and intelligent initialization that can help escape local minima. Its main criticism is fixed-step integration, making it less accurate than shooting methods.

Local minima exist in these methods, as demonstrated in a path-planning example, but are often acceptable in practice. Future lectures will cover trajectory stabilization with LQR and iterative LQR methods.

This retrospective study reports 377 percutaneous tracheostomies performed on intubated, mechanically ventilated COVID-19 patients at Jaber Al Ahmad Al Sabah Hospital, Kuwait, between March 2020 and March 2022—described as the largest single-center series reported. Due to staffing shortages and contamination risks, bedside percutaneous tracheostomy was preferred over the open technique, performed after at least 7 days of intubation under bronchoscopy guidance. Patients (59% male; mean age 56.2 years) most commonly had diabetes (50%) and hypertension (48%). Complications occurred in 23% of cases, with minor bleeding the most frequent (14%); nine tracheo-esophageal fistulae (2%) were reported. Mean time from tracheostomy to weaning from sedation was 7.5 days and from mechanical ventilation was 12.9 days. Mortality was 63%, all attributable to COVID-19 complications; hypertension and age over 65 were significantly associated with increased risk of death. The authors conclude percutaneous tracheostomy can be safely performed in COVID-19 patients, though optimal timing remains debated. Limitations include the absence of an open tracheostomy comparison group, lack of long-term follow-up, and no objective PCR testing of staff.

Florida Panthers coach Bob Boughner said injured goaltenders Roberto Luongo and James Reimer could return to the lineup next week. Luongo has missed 23 consecutive games since suffering a lower-body injury Dec. 4, while Reimer pulled his groin Jan. 23 and was expected to miss two weeks. Boughner hopes both can practice Monday, pending input from goaltending coach Robb Tallas. In their absence, Harri Sateri and Samuel Montembeault have formed the goaltending duo, with Sateri posting a .937 save percentage in three starts, which delayed Montembeault's NHL debut. If Luongo or Reimer returns, Montembeault would likely be sent to AHL Springfield. Forward Jamie McGinn will also return Saturday after missing two games with an upper-body injury, playing left wing on the third line. Florida hosts Vancouver on Tuesday and Los Angeles on Friday.

A Norwalk, Iowa family has been without water for two months after a Department of Transportation highway expansion along I-35 affected their 68-year-old well, their only water source. The Paschells said a 2013 eminent domain contract promised no digging within a certain area of the well. They haul in gallons of water daily and cannot bathe their children or do laundry at home. After a rural water hookup was estimated at 30-60 days, Mark Paschell and a certified contractor dug a 300-yard trench and laid a water line themselves. The DOT is investigating and has offered the family hotel accommodations and reimbursement for cleaning supplies.

Backtests using Yahoo! Finance data from 2014 indicate Bitcoin exhibits an end of month effect, potentially viable as a turn of the month trading strategy. The strategy enters x days before the new month and exits n days after, based on 100 optimization simulations. Max drawdown is high for most simulations and can only be reduced by shortening the holding period. One version, compounding 100,000, produced a 3.3% average gain per trade, 41.8% CAGR, 16% time in market, and 25% max drawdown—lower than HODL but with a much shorter holding period. The strategy is curve-fitted to a degree, though gains exceed random periods (1.33% average). An improved version trades less often, lowering CAGR but smoothing the equity curve. Recent performance was flat amid Bitcoin's crash. The authors conclude Bitcoin has a positive end of month effect but do not reveal the strategy details.
New software patches improve biosecurity screening software's ability to catch AI-designed toxic proteins that evade security filters.

Ghana's Auditor General, Daniel Domelevo, has surcharged 62 organisations—mostly private entities, along with some state institutions and staff of government entities—for receiving state payments without available documentation. The surcharge certificates total GH¢8,886,791.9101742 and cover the period from December 31, 2013 to December 31, 2015. Because efforts to track down the listed companies were fruitless, their names were published. The organisations or individuals were advised to contact the Auditor General's Office in Accra by December 20, 2017, after which they would be deemed duly served. Domelevo, who reported to Parliament his resolve to surcharge anyone receiving undeserved state funds, issued the certificates to recoup the wrongfully paid money. A table lists each surchargee, the surcharge period, principal amount, surcharge amount, and total to be recovered.

The Dow gained 0.6%, S&P 500 1%, Nasdaq 1.3%, and Russell 2000 1.5%; treasuries weakened, the dollar rebounded, gold fell 0.3%, and crude oil dropped 2.5%. Real estate led gains while energy lagged. Bed Bath & Beyond (BBBY) is a major US retailer operating 1,541 stores across all 50 states, DC, Puerto Rico, and Canada, plus eight stores in a Mexican joint venture, under brands including Christmas Tree Shops, Harmon, buybuy BABY, and World Market. The stock peaked near $80 in 2014 and 2015, fell to $39 by November 2016, and lost its NASDAQ-100 listing in December 2016. Risks include stagnating revenue ($11.5–12 billion), declining gross margin (42.8% in 2007 to 38.2%), declining net income ($1,038 million in 2013 to $841 million in 2015), and no structural moat against competitors like Amazon. Debt appears manageable with a D/E of 0.58 and $473 million in cash. The author presents four reasons to invest: (1) investor-friendliness, including a dividend with a ~10% payout ratio and a $2.5 billion buyback program that has repurchased roughly 100 million shares since 2010; (2) online acquisitions of One Kings Lane (~$30 million) and PersonalizationMall.com ($190 million); (3) the Beyond+ loyalty program ($29 annually, 20% discount, free shipping), which exceeded expectations in its invite-only test; and (4) undervaluation, with an intrinsic value of $54.17 and a recommended entry point of $32.50 after a 40% margin of safety. The author is skeptical that Trump's election explains the post-election rally but expects a return to single-digit growth, noting sensitivity to macroeconomic conditions, and would consider investing at $32.50.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system from Texas Instruments with a built-in analog front-end. The device can be powered down via a logic 0 on the RESET or PWDN pins or through register writes, and must be initialized with a sequence of register writes after power-up or reset, requiring a free-running sampling clock. A speed-boost mode enables up to 8MSPS sampling for one user-selected analog input channel pair while the remaining six channels are idle. The 16-bit configuration registers are grouped into three banks addressed by 8-bit addresses, with defined SPI write and read procedures. Multiple devices can be connected in a daisy-chain topology, configured through the DAISY_CHAIN_LEN register, requiring N × 24 SCLKs per frame. Various registers control test patterns, data averaging, gain error correction codes, analog input bandwidth, common-mode range, output lanes, and power-down. For ATE applications, the device achieves a post-calibration total unadjusted error of 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C and offers low-noise (up to 22.7kHz) and wide-bandwidth (up to 700kHz) modes, with the latter settling to 99.95% full-scale in 7.5µs. The device uses three power supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, IOVDD) with no required power-up sequence, and layout recommendations include placing bypass capacitors close to supply pins and keeping analog signals away from noise sources. The document also covers support resources, ESD handling precautions, and standard legal disclaimers.
