Ninety-year-old Muriel Diaz, born and raised in Shrewsbury, taught in Somerset before training as a nurse and midwife. After dreaming of Peru, she went there as a missionary and married Alberto in 1969, living on the Peruvian coast for 32 years. For 18 years she spent six weeks annually as the only nurse at a jungle clinic, delivering babies and treating snake bites, with the nearest hospital 90 miles away. The couple left Peru in 1995 due to escalating terrorism and settled near Cardigan, where Mrs Diaz has volunteered at Barnardo's charity shop for 20 years, repairing donated clothes. She also enjoys landscape painting and learning Welsh.

Yale-New Haven Hospital sued Clifford Mitchell in two actions and Laureen Wilczynski in one to collect payment for medical services. The defendants raised special defenses alleging violations of the Hill-Burton Act and Connecticut's hospital bed funds statute, along with counterclaims under the Connecticut Unfair Trade Practices Act (CUTPA). The hospital moved for summary judgment, arguing that no private right of action existed under either statute and that the defenses and counterclaims were legally invalid. The court denied the motion, holding that the defendants have a private right of action under both statutes and may raise noncompliance as a defense in a collection suit. The court further held that violations of statutes lacking private causes of action can still support CUTPA claims, and that the Hill-Burton Act does not preempt CUTPA. Factual issues in the counterclaims precluded summary judgment.

A hockey goalie focuses on making his own saves rather than worrying about opponents, calling one of the team's five losses among the worst. He credits home ice advantage, aims to learn from playoff experiences, praises captain Alfy as an exceptional leader, and says the team reviewed video and corrections to prepare for Anaheim.

Barcelona manager Hansi Flick admitted mistakes were made during summer talks with goalkeeper Marc-Andre Ter Stegen. Ter Stegen disagreed with his de-registration after back surgery, and Barcelona stripped him of the captaincy. Flick acknowledged miscommunication, saying there was much to improve even on his part. Ter Stegen had threatened to leave and is expected to return in late 2025 or early 2026. Flick said Joan Garcia was signed as Barcelona's future number one.

On June 23, 2017, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Tesla, Inc. entered into an amendment to its Revolving Aggregation Credit Facility, originally established May 4, 2015, with a syndicate of lenders and Bank of America, N.A. as administrative and collateral agent. The facility is secured by certain assets and cash flows of certain SolarCity Corporation subsidiaries and is non-recourse to Tesla. The amendment extended the draw availability period to December 31, 2018, extended the maturity date to December 31, 2019, and, at Tesla's request, decreased total lender commitments to $600 million, aligning with Tesla's shift toward cash- and loan-based solar sales and more frequent securitization of leased solar assets.

The NHS offers cancer screening to detect early signs of cancer in people without symptoms, which has saved around 90,000 lives in the last five years according to Cancer Research UK. The NHS provides three main screening programmes: cervical screening every five years for those aged 25-64, which checks for high-risk HPV strains; breast screening every three years for women aged 50-71 using mammograms; and bowel screening every two years for people aged 50-74, using a home FIT kit to detect blood in stool. Screening detects cancer at earlier stages when treatment is more likely to succeed, and can sometimes identify pre-cancerous changes before cancer develops. Screening is free through the NHS, with invitations sent by post based on age and eligibility. People with symptoms should not wait for screening but consult their doctor. Some screenings, such as prostate screening, fall outside national programmes and can be discussed with a doctor. Women with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) are advised to have yearly mammograms from age 40. Private screening is available for those who don't meet NHS criteria, such as those with a strong family history of cancer or symptoms but below the age threshold.

At the French Open, Grigor Dimitrov beat Jared Donaldson 6-7 (2-7) 6-4 4-6 6-4 10-8, with Donaldson attempting an underarm serve while suffering from cramp. This lecture introduces the computation of the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) and the fast Fourier transform (FFT) algorithm. The FFT, disclosed in a 1965 paper by Cooley and Tukey and reinvented several times over the preceding 20–30 years, is orders of magnitude more efficient than direct DFT computation. Direct computation requires approximately N² complex multiplications and additions, making large transforms impractical. The FFT is most efficient when N is highly composite; for N a power of 2, computation is proportional to N log₂N rather than N².

The decimation-in-time approach decomposes the input sequence into even- and odd-numbered points, computing two N/2-point DFTs, G(k) and H(k), combined as X(k) = G(k) + W_N^k H(k). This reduces computation to N + N²/2, and recursive decomposition down to two-point DFTs yields the N log₂N result. The periodicity of the DFT is the essential key to this efficiency, since only N/2 points of each N/2-point DFT need be explicitly computed.

The computation is structured as butterfly operations, with multiplications by powers of W always applied to branches from the bottom node. Because W_N^(N/2) equals −1, the butterfly can be simplified by extracting the multiplication, reducing the number of multiplications by a factor of 2. The resulting flow graph produces outputs in sequential order but requires inputs in bit-reversed order. Subsequent lectures will cover modifications of this algorithm form.

Joey Chestnut won Nathan's Famous Hot Dog Eating Contest with a record 74 hot dogs, his 11th Mustard Belt. The initial tally of 64 was corrected after a recount; judges missed he ate from two plates. Carmen Cincotti was second with 64.

Szemerédi's graph regularity lemma, developed in the 1970s, is a powerful tool in graph theory stating that every graph's vertex set can be partitioned into a bounded number of parts so that the graph looks random-like between most pairs of parts. A pair of vertex sets is epsilon regular if the edge density between any sufficiently large subsets differs from the overall density by at most epsilon; a partition is epsilon regular if irregular pairs account for only an epsilon fraction of vertex pairs. For every epsilon there exists M, depending only on epsilon and not on graph size, such that every graph has an epsilon regular partition into at most M parts. Sparse graphs satisfy the condition trivially, so the lemma is meaningful mainly for dense graphs. An equitable variant, with part sizes differing by at most 1, can also be guaranteed. The proof uses an energy increment argument: energy, a mean squared edge density, never decreases under refinement and increases by at least epsilon^5 when an irregular partition is refined using witnessing sets, so the iteration stops after at most epsilon^{-5} steps. The resulting bound on the number of parts is a tower of twos, and Gowers' theorem shows such tower-type bounds cannot be substantially improved.

This passage examines how firms can design business models to minimize the negative impact of digital piracy. Since Napster pioneered peer-to-peer file sharing in 1999, digital piracy has thrived by offering fast, convenient, free access to content, causing substantial revenue losses despite technical and legal countermeasures, which have proven largely ineffective. The study addresses its research question through a qualitative analysis of two case studies—Spotify and Netflix—based on 96 archival documents and nine expert interviews, framed by Baden-Fuller and Haefliger's four business model elements: customer identification, customer engagement, monetization, and value chain linkages.

Digital piracy's attractiveness varies across content categories (audio, film, written, and interactive works), exerting the strongest pressure on music and film, where the most effective business model responses have emerged. Spotify and Netflix countered piracy through subscription models with free tiers or trials, real-time streaming, intuitive interfaces, consistent content quality, broad device compatibility, consumer-friendly DRM, personalized recommendations, social media integration, and improved geographical access. Their competitive advantage derives not from price alone but from enriching the consumption experience through community features and personalization, which piracy cannot replicate due to anonymity and user churn. The business model generates virtuous cycles: free tiers feed the userbase, which strengthens bargaining power with content owners, improves recommendation quality, and increases user willingness to pay. Exclusive content plays a limited role against piracy since pirated copies are equally available.

The discussion highlights implications for technological innovation (digital technology serving as both "poison and antidote"), firm diversification, and network competition, noting that digital newcomers like Spotify and Netflix leapfrogged incumbents such as Blockbuster. The authors conclude that digital distribution outperforms piracy primarily by improving the consumption experience, while cautioning that findings require careful generalization to other industries and content categories.

The paper extends Uustalu's combinatorial characterization of monoid structures on non-indexed containers to indexed containers, which describe endofunctors on SetI and are a notational variant of Gambino–Hyland polynomials. The authors define a monoidal structure on the category IC I of indexed containers corresponding to composition of extents, and prove that monoids in this monoidal category correspond precisely to monad structures on the associated container functors. Examples include products of indexed container monads, indexed variants of the state and writer monads, and a free monad that, applied to Fin, yields well-scoped λ-terms. Unlike Gambino and Kock, who studied Cartesian polynomial monads, this work treats general monads on container extents. The development is formalized in Cubical Agda, chosen for its support of functional extensionality. The paper reviews the category IC I, defining indexed containers, their extents, and morphisms, and notes that the extent functor is full and faithful.

C.J. McCollum scored a career-high 43 points, including 16 in a 32-15 third quarter, to lead the short-handed Portland Trail Blazers to a 95-89 comeback victory over the Minnesota Timberwolves on Sunday. Portland, without Damian Lillard for a fourth straight game due to a sprained left ankle, trailed by 12 at halftime and had lost seven of its previous eight games. Mason Plumlee added 18 points and eight rebounds, and Evan Turner scored 11. Andrew Wiggins led Minnesota with 24 points, but Karl-Anthony Towns managed just 11 points on 3-for-15 shooting, and the Wolves fell to 9-11 in games they had led by double digits. Separately, free agent Donatas Motiejunas cancelled a scheduled workout with Minnesota after receiving an offer from New Orleans.

Apple Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended June 27, 2015. Third-quarter net sales were $49.6 billion, up 33% from $37.4 billion a year earlier, with nine-month net sales of $182.2 billion, up 30%. Quarterly net income was $10.7 billion ($1.85 diluted EPS) versus $7.7 billion ($1.28) in the prior year. iPhone net sales rose 59% to $31.4 billion on strong iPhone 6 and 6 Plus demand, while iPad sales declined 23% to $4.5 billion and Mac sales grew 9% to $6.0 billion. Greater China net sales grew 112%. Gross margin was 39.7%, and the effective tax rate was 26.2%. Total assets reached $273.2 billion. The Board increased the share repurchase authorization to $140 billion, with $90 billion utilized; the company repurchased $10 billion of stock and paid $3.1 billion in dividends during the quarter. It issued $8.0 billion in U.S. dollar-denominated and ¥250 billion in yen-denominated debt, bringing total notes outstanding to $50 billion, plus $4.5 billion in commercial paper. Gross unrecognized tax benefits stood at $5.4 billion. The European Commission is investigating Ireland's state aid to Apple, which could require recovery of past taxes. A $533 million Smartflash patent verdict was vacated with a new damages trial ordered, and the Samsung case judgment was reduced to approximately $548 million pending further proceedings. The company operated 456 retail stores and launched Apple Watch and Apple Music during the period.

The Chargers' future hinges on decisions being made at the NFL level. Chairman Dean Spanos has all but concluded he must move the team to Los Angeles but remains anguished and has asked the league for help staying in San Diego; sources say solutions are being discussed at the league and ownership levels. Spanos has until Jan. 15 to exercise an option granted when owners approved the Rams' Inglewood stadium and rejected a Carson bid. San Diego, the county, and San Diego State made a final offer of $375 million—over $100 million less than sought—which the Chargers consider real. The NFL has pledged $300 million total, and the projected $1.025 billion falls up to $175 million short of estimated Mission Valley stadium costs. Talks also covered a downtown venue, which would require a public vote in 2018 or 2020.

Walmart-owned Sam's Club will be open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily starting this weekend, responding to member feedback, with the biggest shift on Sundays, which previously ran 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. The first hour is reserved for Plus members, and curbside pickup starts at 7 a.m. Exceptions include early closure on Christmas Eve and closures on Thanksgiving, Christmas Day, New Year's Day, and Easter. Sam's Club memberships cost less than Costco's, and both chains have posted strong results this year.

A hockey player discusses his team's strategy of getting the puck deep and cycling, crediting young forwards. He praises Ron Francis for leading by example with professionalism, noting Francis succeeds through intelligence rather than exceptional skill, making difficult plays routine. The player describes a seven-year relationship with a coach who has yelled at him, during which both have grown. On the playoffs, he says everyone tries hard and results vary, citing Al Mogilny's point that effort does not always match outcomes. A 1981 paperback by Fred Puhn covering suspension theory, hardware selection and modification, aerodynamic improvements, and brakes for better car handling across all drivetrain layouts.

Mariano Del Cid-Mendez appealed his conviction and sentence for illegal reentry, challenging the constitutionality of 8 U.S.C. § 1326(b)(1), (2) and the district court's application of mandatory Sentencing Guidelines. His constitutional challenge was foreclosed by Almendarez-Torres v. United States and circuit precedent, which he conceded but raised to preserve for further review. Because the Government failed to prove the mandatory Guidelines sentencing error was harmless, the sentence was vacated and the case remanded.

The Qnap TVS-x73 is a business-class NAS series in 4, 6, and 8-bay models, powered by an AMD RX-421BD quad-core APU with up to 64GB DDR4 RAM, delivering up to 1,172 MB/s throughput, with optional 10GbE support, 4K video decoding, and dual HDMI output.

Southern Illinois defeated the University of Evansville men's basketball team 73-61 on Saturday at the Ford Center. Ryan Taylor and Jaylon Brown each scored 19 points for UE (10-9, 1-5 MVC), while Mike Rodriguez led SIU (11-8, 4-2 MVC) with 20 points. Evansville led by as many as nine in the first half, but Southern Illinois took a 33-31 halftime lead and pulled away late. The program honored former head coach Jim Crews before the game.

This study applied a relative risk (RR) statistic based on ICU admissions data to assess the role of different age groups in propagating four Omicron epidemic waves in France between March 1 and December 29, 2022: the Spring wave (March 14–May 15), Summer wave (June 27–August 21), Autumn wave (September 18–November 12), and Autumn-Winter wave (November 22–December 29). The RR statistic measures the change in an age group's proportion among all ICU admissions before versus after the epidemic peak, with higher values suggesting disproportionate depletion of susceptible individuals in that group during the epidemic's ascent. ICU admissions were used because under-detection of SARS-CoV-2 infection is less pronounced in symptomatic ICU admissions than in hospitalizations or community testing.

Children aged 10-19y had the highest RR during the Spring wave (RR=1.92) and Autumn wave (RR=1.64), while children aged 0-9y had the highest RR during the Summer wave (RR=1.61). For the Autumn-Winter wave, the highest RR belonged to persons aged 30-39y (RR=1.47), followed by those aged 40-49y and over 80y. The authors conclude that the leading relative role in propagating Omicron waves in France shifted from children and younger adults to persons aged 30-49y and over 80y, possibly due to immunity built up in younger groups during earlier waves. They suggest that increasing booster vaccination coverage for all adults, and possibly children, should help limit the spread of future Omicron epidemics, and that further efforts are needed to protect the elderly, including in Long-Term Care facilities.

Indian equity markets rose for the fourth consecutive week in the week ended April 21, supported by forecasts of a normal monsoon, strong IT sector earnings, easing WPI inflation, and positive global cues. The BSE Sensex gained 0.65% to close at 34,415.58 points, while the Nifty50 rose 0.80% to 10,564.05 points. However, higher crude oil prices, a weakening rupee—which hit a 13-month low of 66.06 against the dollar—and selling pressure in banking stocks amid expectations of a hawkish RBI stance trimmed gains. Foreign institutional investors sold shares worth Rs 2,821.24 crore, while domestic institutional investors bought Rs 2,124.16 crore. IT, metal, FMCG and realty led sectoral gains, while PSU banks and energy declined. TCS rose 8.11% weekly, touching a record high.

During Larry Nassar's third and final sentencing hearing in Michigan, Randall Margraves, father of three victims, lunged at Nassar after the judge declined his requests for time alone with the former sports doctor. Two of his daughters had just described being abused by Nassar. Deputies restrained Margraves and removed him; after he apologized, Judge Janice Cunningham declined to punish him for contempt but called his actions unacceptable. More than 30 victims have spoken so far. Nassar previously received up to 175 years and 60 years on child pornography charges.

An international team led by Harald Ebeling of the University of Hawaiʻi used the Hubble Space Telescope to discover the distant galaxy eMACSJ1341-QG-1, magnified 30 times by the massive galaxy cluster eMACSJ1341.9-2441 through gravitational lensing. This sets a new record for magnification of a rare quiescent galaxy—one that no longer forms new stars. The magnification enables study of the galaxy's stellar populations and its undistorted shape. Because distant galaxies appear younger and should not yet have exhausted their gas, understanding why this one stopped forming stars may reveal clues about galaxy evolution. Follow-up observations are underway, and the findings are published in the Astrophysical Journal Letters.

Australian PM Malcolm Turnbull said China has an obligation to use its enormous leverage to pull nuclear-armed North Korea back from the brink, calling Pyongyang a reckless threat. His remarks followed a failed missile test and precede US Vice President Mike Pence's Sydney visit. Under US pressure, China has suspended coal imports from North Korea.

Larry Connors' Multiple Days Up (MDU) and Multiple Days Down (MDD) strategy, from Chapter 6 of his 2009 book "High Probability Trading," is a mean reversion strategy, as ETFs consist of many stocks and are unlikely to go to zero. It buys when an ETF is above its 200-day moving average, below its 5-day moving average, and has dropped 4 of the last 5 trading days, selling when it closes above its 5-day moving average, with no stop-loss. Tested on Connors' original 20 ETFs plus five more through December 2020, it had the lowest profit factor of his mean reversion strategies. Trading only SPY and QQQ yielded 287 trades, a 1.82 profit factor, 12% max drawdown, and 2.4% CAGR. The short-only portfolio was not tradeable, but SPY and QQQ shorts showed a 65% win ratio, with much of the gain in 2008. The strategy can likely be improved.

Freeport High School recognized students for academic excellence by naming them to the second quarter honor roll, with students in grades 9 through 12 listed under two categories: High Honors and Honors. Separately, students living in The Forecaster's coverage area who attend North Yarmouth Academy attained honor roll status for the first semester. Those students, in grades 5 through 12, were listed under three categories: Highest Honors, High Honors, and Honors.
A 9-foot boa constrictor escaped a biology classroom enclosure through a broken hinge at a suburban St. Louis school, which sent 400 students home; the snake was found beneath the floor.

Virginia Chestnuts is a family-owned orchard in Nelson County, Virginia, run by David and Kim Bryant, who purchased land in 2003 and planted over 1,600 Dunstan trees, an American-Chinese hybrid resistant to the blight that destroyed most American chestnuts in the early 1900s. After facing harsh winters and cicadas between 2009 and 2014, the orchard produced a bumper crop in 2015 and a 2017 harvest of at least 3,000 pounds. Chestnuts are harvested from mid-September to late October, then graded, washed, sanitized, dried, and stored on-site before delivery or shipping. The Bryants sell raw chestnuts whole or peeled and belong to a five-orchard growers group in Nelson County. Their chestnuts have been used in breads, stuffing, beer, and desserts, and the business has gained attention through events like Fire, Flour & Fork in Richmond and a growing social media following.

Noozhawk's publisher Bill Macfadyen marks the Fourth of July by highlighting the First Amendment's protections, including freedom of the press, which he says is under attack. He describes Noozhawk's mission to provide high-quality, independent reporting for Santa Barbara County, supported by local advertisers and Hawks Club subscribers. With 21,000 daily readers, he asks readers to join the Hawks Club, noting contributions are not tax-deductible since Noozhawk is a for-profit business.

Aston Villa beat Burton Albion 3-2 at Villa Park, with goals from Scott Hogan, Albert Adomah and Jack Grealish, while Burton scored via an Ahmed Elmohamady own goal and Liam Boyce. The win is Villa's sixth consecutive victory, first since 1990, leaving them third, a point behind second-placed Derby.

The discovery of a skull belonging to a new species, Cifelliodon wahkarmoosuch, in eastern Utah suggests the supercontinent Pangea split about 15 million years later than previously believed. The small, catlike creature had hair, suckled its young, and laid eggs. The fossil, found on Bureau of Land Management lands, indicates reptile-like mammals underwent an unexpected burst of evolution across continents and that migration corridors remained intact into the Early Cretaceous. The study was published in the journal Nature.

This datasheet excerpt from Texas Instruments covers support resources, trademarks, ESD precautions, revision history, and packaging information. TI E2E support forums provide verified answers and design help from experts. multiSPI and TI E2E are Texas Instruments trademarks. Revision A (May 2025) changed the document status of ADS8685W and ADS8689W from Advance Information to Production Data. A four-year Michigan State University study led by Jason Rowntree, published in Agricultural Systems, compared adaptive multi-paddock (AMP) grass-fed cattle operations with grain-fed feedlot herds. Conducted at MSU's Lake City research center, the study measured production statistics alongside greenhouse gas emissions from digestion, manure handling, feed production, and energy use, plus carbon losses from soil erosion. AMP systems proved environmentally favorable, potentially offsetting emissions and acting as a net carbon sink, while feedlot emissions were higher due to fertilizer-related nitrogen. However, feedlots were more productive, producing the same beef on half the land. AMP grazing outperformed continuous grazing on a land basis, though carbon sequestration may decline over time. Rowntree stated the researchers were not advocating one approach, noting feedlots could improve through reduced fertilizer use and cover crops.

This passage is from the Texas Instruments datasheet (SLVSF07F, revised August 2024) for the TPS7H5001-SP through TPS7H5004-SP, a family of radiation-hardness-assured peak current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters.

Key functional features described include: an internal 1.23-V bandgap reference divided to 0.613 V for the transconductance error amplifier (1800 µA/V); output voltage programming via a resistor divider to VSENSE; soft-start controlled by an SS-pin capacitor, with synchronous rectifier outputs activating when SS exceeds 1 V; and three switching-frequency modes—internal oscillator (100 kHz–2 MHz set by the RT resistor), external synchronization (clock at twice the switching frequency, 200 kHz–4 MHz), and primary-secondary mode for synchronizing two controllers.

The controllers provide primary outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) with roughly 150-mA peak current, requiring external gate drivers; OUTB/SRB are active only with the 50% duty cycle limit (DCL tied to AVSS) on the TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP. Programmable dead times (PS/SP pins) and leading edge blank time (LEB pin) are supported, though the TPS7H5003-SP uses fixed 50-ns values. Pulse skipping occurs when COMP is below 0.3 V and the prior duty cycle was under 25%. Current sensing via CS_ILIM triggers cycle-by-cycle limiting and hiccup mode at a 1.05-V threshold, with timing set by the HICC capacitor. Additional features include a FAULT pin for external protection, slope compensation via RSC, Type 2A/2B frequency compensation, and thermal shutdown at 175°C with restart below 160°C.

An application example demonstrates a 500-kHz synchronous push-pull converter using GaN FETs with a 5-V output, covering component selection including transformer, FETs, output inductor, output capacitance (with single-event transient mitigation), current sense resistor, compensation network, and slope compensation. Layout guidelines address noise reduction, ground separation, and bypass capacitor placement. The passage concludes with related documentation, revision history, and mechanical/packaging information.

Mumbai Indians are playing with the same squad, while Sunrisers Hyderabad make three changes: Shikhar Dhawan returns after missing two matches, Mohammad Nabi plays his first IPL 2018 match, and Basil Thampi comes in; Billy Stanlake, Ricky Bhui and Deepak Hooda are out. For Sunrisers, Williamson has amassed 230 runs in five games, Saha is below par, and Bhuvneshwar Kumar leads a strong bowling attack with Rashid Khan and Shakib Al Hasan.

Maria Sharapova lost in the first round of Wimbledon to 132nd-ranked qualifier Vitalia Diatchenko 6-7 (3), 7-6 (3), 6-4, despite holding multiple leads, including serving for the match at 5-3 in the second set. Possible explanations cited include unpredictable grass bounces, hot weather, the clay-to-grass transition, and pressure on seeded players. Top seeds Simona Halep, Rafael Nadal, and Novak Djokovic advanced in straight sets on Day 2.

During Leander High School's 2017 prom, senior Keilany Solano, named prom queen, placed her crown and sash on fellow nominee Abby Cano, a classmate with Down syndrome. Solano said the gesture was unplanned and that she felt Cano deserved it more and would be happier. Cano's mother, Sabrina Wycoff, said she was surprised and touched, noting her daughter has been treated kindly throughout school. Cano, known for giving high-fives in hallways, collects women wrestler action figures.

The Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) specification describes AMD's mechanism for applying firmware updates to microprocessors. SFS and co-signing are off by default, requiring customer opt-in and BIOS configuration. In early boot, the customer BIOS passes a signing key to the ASP; packages authenticate against the customer key first, then the AMD SFS key, enabling different co-signing keys for test versus production systems. Customers provide an RSA public key (2048-bit or 4096-bit) via the SET_CUST_SFS_SIGNATURE command during or immediately after SMM setup, signing packages with the RSA-PSS scheme.

Update packages can patch registers, replace firmware images, or update firmware portions, and each checks the existing System Patch Level and firmware versions for applicability. SEV updates are automatically committed and prevent rollback; reverting requires a system reboot. SNP-enabled systems require HV-FIXED pages via the RMPUPDATE command. Attestation data should be requested via side-band (SPDM) or in-band (DPE) interfaces.

Each package verifies dependent firmware versions before updating; if any portion cannot apply, the package does not apply. Updates are non-persistent across reboots and may be applied during OS boot, after boot, or during operation.

Issuing SFS commands requires a 2MB-aligned TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER and a customer-provided deployment agent that assembles the optional co-signing header, AMD package, and signature in DRAM. The ASP protects the DRAM address, verifies customer and AMD signatures, loads and runs the patch, updates patch level information, and returns status. Package names follow the format fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg. Updates run in parallel with x86 and DMA traffic with minimal performance impact; SEV/SEV-ES virtual machines must stop and restart for SEV firmware updates, while SEV/SNP virtual machines continue operating.

Helping Hands Hawaii's Ready to Learn (RTL) program is holding its annual school supply drive from June 1 to July 31, 2017, to provide free school supplies to low-income and homeless students. American Savings Bank branches will serve as collection sites from June 14 to July 14, with donations staying on each island. The Second Circuit affirmed the denial of Rodney Nicholson's habeas petition challenging his New York second-degree murder conviction. Nicholson argued the state courts' exclusion of Darnell Phelps's hearsay confession violated due process under Chambers v. Mississippi by prompting denial of his new trial motion. Even assuming Chambers applies to retrial motions, the court found Nicholson failed to show the state courts mechanistically rejected reliable hearsay. Phelps's confession was deemed unreliable: it contradicted his earlier statement denying knowledge of the murder, could not be tested by cross-examination at retrial, and could have been tailored to publicly known forensic findings. The eyewitness identifying Nicholson was somewhat corroborated and deemed credible by the jury. The confession also did not necessarily exonerate Nicholson, implied a more active role than he admitted, and his failure to disclose Phelps's involvement before trial further cast doubt on it. Accordingly, no due process violation was shown.

A man set off a pipe bomb strapped to him in a subway passageway under 42nd Street near Times Square during Monday morning rush hour, injuring himself and three others with non-life-threatening injuries. Officials labeled it an attempted terror attack. The suspect, 27-year-old Akayed Ullah of Brooklyn, was reportedly inspired by the Islamic State group but had no direct contact with it. The low-tech bomb was attached with Velcro and plastic ties. The blast triggered a large emergency response and disrupted transit near the Port Authority.

The US government faces a shutdown after Tuesday, risking missed paychecks for millions of federal workers. Members of Congress will still be paid because the Constitution requires their compensation and the 27th Amendment delays pay changes until after elections. Since 1981, congressional salaries have been funded through mandatory spending unaffected by shutdowns. Rep. Angie Craig introduced the "No Pay for Disarray" Act to dock lawmakers' pay during shutdowns. The 2019 Government Employee Fair Treatment Act guarantees retroactive pay for furloughed workers. STAT's Morning Rounds newsletter reports that if Congress does not fund the government by the following day, patients receiving hospital-level care at home under the Acute Hospital Care at Home initiative will be returned to hospitals, with CMS guidance stating all inpatients must be discharged or returned by September 30, 2025. Tesla posted a record 497,099 vehicle deliveries in Q3 2025, up 7.4% from a year earlier and above analyst forecasts of roughly 444,000, driven by a U.S. rush to buy before the $7,500 federal EV tax credit expired on 30 September. The UC1825B-SP is a dual-output controller from Texas Instruments with integrated drivers for push-pull topology, usable for half-bridge and full-bridge applications with external high-side drivers, and supporting both voltage and current mode topologies. Its saw-tooth oscillator's rising edge is governed by RT (recommended 1 kΩ to 100 kΩ) and CT; a switching frequency of 215 kHz was chosen using RT of 10 kΩ and CT of 680 pF, and control of DMAX below 70% is not recommended. Design details include a transformer turns ratio of 2.2, an auxiliary winding ratio of 1.5, 6% magnetizing current, 120-µH primary inductance, a 2.2-µH output inductor, an RCD clamp, a 60-V rated output diode, MOSFETs rated approximately 2.5 to 3 times input voltage, around 1145 µF of output capacitance with a 500-nH filter inductor and 0.5-Ω damping resistor, Type IIB compensation with a 5-kHz crossover frequency, and a sense resistor for current limiting and cycle shutdown. The converter operates from a well-regulated 10–30 V input supply, which may require additional bulk capacitance if located far from the device. Layout guidelines recommend low-EMI inductors, feedback traces routed away from noise sources, close placement of input/output capacitors and compensation components to the IC, short thick power traces (minimum 15 mils per ampere), current loops arranged in the same direction, and a ground plane with a designated power ground section for high di/dt currents, including bypassing VCC and VREF with low ESR/ESL ceramic capacitors. The document also addresses documentation updates, TI E2E support resources, trademarks, ESD handling precautions, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

Around 200 people attended a vigil in Nottingham's market square for Mariam Moustafa, an 18-year-old Nottingham College engineering student who died following an attack outside the intu Victoria Centre. Speakers included her sister, a former teacher, and an Egyptian Coptic priest who called for answers into her death and an end to violence. The National Beer Wholesalers Association launched DeliveringLocalJobs.com, a public awareness campaign highlighting the 135,000 beer distribution employees working in all 50 states. Arizona Cardinals quarterback Carson Palmer, a 37-year-old veteran with 175 career games, joined the team in a 2013 trade from Oakland and led them to a 10-6 season, their best since 2009. Palmer says he feels great and is excited about the upcoming season, conducting yearly self-checkups and taking his career one year at a time. He believes the losing 2016 season could benefit the team by allowing it to embrace a lower-pressure underdog role, unlike 2015, when the Cardinals won their first NFC West title since 2009, earned a first-round bye, beat Green Bay in overtime in the divisional round, and lost 49-15 to Carolina in the NFC title game.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2022 reports second quarter revenue of $52.7 billion (up from $51.7 billion a year earlier) and net income of $16.4 billion (down from $18.8 billion). On January 18, 2023, Microsoft announced a workforce reduction of approximately 10,000 jobs and recorded a $1.2 billion charge, including $800 million in severance expenses. The company reports three segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. The Bollinger Band Squeeze strategy involves trading in the direction of a breakout after a period of low volatility, based on the premise that low volatility is often followed by high volatility. Bollinger Bands consist of a center line (the average price over a chosen lookback period) and two outer bands whose width reflects volatility; contracting bands indicate a potential squeeze. The authors backtested the strategy with various rules and assets but found it unprofitable—it underperformed buy and hold (12.5% vs. 14.8% on Pepsi, invested 61% of the time), and multiple variations failed across assets. They caution against relying on anecdotal evidence and state better indicators exist. The strategy's developer, John Bollinger, born in 1950, created Bollinger Bands in the 1980s and published "Bollinger on Bollinger Bands," translated into 11 languages. As a breakout strategy, it has a lower win rate and suffers whipsaws. Common mistakes include lacking positive expectancy and not following the strategy. Assets differ: stocks tend toward mean reversion, while commodities do not, so no strategy works on all assets.

Pedro Russell, after an unconventional academic path and strategy roles at RSM, Cengage, and Juno, earned an MBA at MIT Sloan on a full-tuition Dean's Fellowship. There he met Garrison Jones and Stephen McGarvey, and the three co-founded GPS Partners, a search fund focused on for-profit medical technical schools due to rising demand for healthcare support from the aging U.S. population. Hammerson confirmed it received a preliminary, non-binding proposal from Klépierre SA on 8 March for a possible £4.88bn cash and share offer valuing the company at 615p per share, a 41% premium to its 16 March closing price. Sen. Cory Booker campaigned for Democratic Senate nominee Doug Jones in Alabama the weekend before the election, with an implicit eye toward the 2020 presidential race. In *Pfeiffer v. Commissioner of Internal Revenue* (2d Cir. 1937), the court reviewed a Board of Tax Appeals decision affirming an $89,841.75 income tax deficiency against the petitioner for 1931. Wm. R. Warner & Co. distributed preferred stock as dividends on common stock in 1928 and 1931; the petitioner received 12,582 preferred shares in 1928 and 6,291¾ shares in 1931, valued at $100 per share, and in 1931 the corporation redeemed 2,000 of her 1928 shares at par for $200,000. The Commissioner asserted deficiencies based on both the 1931 dividend's fair market value ($629,125) and the redemption proceeds. The Board upheld the dividend determination, finding the 1931 stock dividend not exempt under section 115(f) of the Revenue Act of 1928, but held the redemption produced no taxable income because the shares had a $100 basis; the Commissioner did not appeal that ruling. The majority reversed, holding that section 115(f)'s unqualified exemption of stock dividends covered the preferred dividend on common stock, relying on the statute's language, its legislative history, and consistent Treasury regulations, and citing *Tillotson*, *Koshland*, and *Gowran*. It also held the redemption proceeds could not be taxed because that issue was neither raised before the Board nor assigned as error, and the Board had not found the redemption essentially equivalent to a taxable dividend. Judge L. Hand dissented, arguing the exemption existed only because Congress believed *Eisner v. Macomber* required it, that preferred-on-common dividends constitute income, and that the Board's view was correct.

Bitcoin rose about 2% to $123,874 on Friday, within 1% of its mid-August record near $124,000, as the U.S. government shutdown entered its third day. Investors are treating it as a hedge against political and economic tensions; Standard Chartered expects a new high soon and $135,000 eventually. Gold and stocks also rose.

Google canceled the website-hosting registration for the neo-Nazi site Daily Stormer, hours after GoDaddy told the site to find a new host, citing violations of policies against inciting violence. The moves followed the site's article ridiculing Heather Heyer, who was killed while protesting a white nationalist rally in Charlottesville. YouTube also terminated the site's channel for hate-speech violations, and Facebook removes links to the site unless captions condemn the content. Google canceled the registration about three hours after the site registered with it, saying the change could take up to 48 hours and that it is not the hosting provider. Tucows denied hosting the site, and Cloudflare said it is not the host while declining to identify who is. The crackdowns followed violent clashes in Virginia, and the online campaign was sparked by Amy Siskind, who urged GoDaddy to drop the site.

The executors of Horace M. Whitmore's estate sued to enjoin trustees from selling land under a deed of trust securing a $1,500 promissory note held by the San Francisco Savings Union, because the creditor had failed to present its claim within the ten-month statutory period after publication of notice to creditors. The trial court overruled the defendants' demurrer, permanently enjoined the sale, and decreed the defendants had no title to the land; the defendants appealed. On appeal, the court held that failure to present a claim within the statutory period does not extinguish the debt, as payment would, but merely takes away the creditor's remedy against the estate. Because the debt remained subsisting and unpaid, a court of equity could not compel the creditor to surrender its security or enjoin the sale without payment of the debt. The judgment was reversed, with directions to sustain the demurrer. Justice Crockett dissented, joined by Justice McKinstry, arguing that failure to present the claim forfeits the lien, that the estate's equitable interest must be administered through the Probate Court, and that compelling release of the legal title is equitable, since allowing non-presenting creditors to retain liens would defeat the statutory administration of the estate and prejudice creditors who duly presented their claims.

This patent application, claiming priority to a 2019 provisional application and a 2020 U.S. application, relates to bonded optical devices for wearable electronics. The background notes that small, high-resolution displays for applications such as AR smart glasses, HUDs, smart watches, and cell phones require very small pixel pitches (e.g., less than 5-6 μm). LCoS technology is inefficient and costly, while microLEDs provide brightness, but forming multi-colored displays from monochromatic LED wafers remains challenging.

The disclosed embodiments involve bonding optical elements—particularly monochromatic LED chips or wafers emitting a single color (red, green, or blue)—directly to one or more carriers, such as silicon or CMOS processor dies with active circuitry controlling the emitters. Direct or hybrid bonding (e.g., DBI/ZiBond dielectric-to-dielectric techniques) is performed without an intervening adhesive, enabling pixel pitches below 5 microns or even below 1 micron. Bonding surfaces are polished, activated by plasma/etch, and may be terminated with nitrogen or exposed to fluorine; after dielectric-to-dielectric bonding and annealing, recessed conductive contact pads (e.g., copper) expand to form metal-to-metal bonds. Bonding may occur die-to-wafer, die-to-die, or wafer-to-wafer, and carriers have a coefficient of thermal expansion below 7 ppm.

Monochromatic images from separate red, green, and blue optical elements are superimposed—via mirrors, beamsplitters, lenses, and waveguides with input and output couplings—to produce a polychromatic image viewable by a user. Optical assemblies may be bonded directly to waveguides or mounted on frames, with applications including projectors, car HUDs, smart watch displays, and cell phone displays. Pixels may be isolated by deep trench isolation structures to limit crosstalk; isolation may separate every pixel or only A×A pixel matrices, the latter improving yield and allowing matrices to function as larger pixels with sub-pixels for brightness control. Superposition also provides redundancy if one image region is damaged.

The claims recite bonded optical devices in which first and second (optionally third) optical elements of different colors—such as red, green, and blue LEDs—are bonded to processor elements without adhesive, with independently controllable emitters having pitches below 50 or 10 microns, wavelength separation of at least 25 nm, and an optical pathway transmitting superimposed light to an output. A corresponding bonding method is also claimed.

Matthew Phelps, 29, called 911 in the early hours of September 1, saying he took Coricidin cough medicine and woke to find his wife Lauren, 29, stabbed to death, claiming the medicine made him kill her. Investigators seized red-stained bedding, an empty box of the same medicine, computers, a knife set, and other items. Lauren died at a hospital. Phelps, who has no criminal record, faces first-degree murder charges and is held without bail. The couple had been married less than a year.

Transport Cabinet Secretary James Macharia attributed the boda boda menace to poor enforcement of existing regulations by bodies like NTSA. Speaking before the National Assembly Transport Committee, he said the ministry is working with county transport committees and the traffic department to speed up implementation. Ruiru MP Simon King'ara proposed a dedicated motorbike safety authority to replace the overwhelmed NTSA and suggested benchmarking with Rwanda rather than banning riders from city centres.

The IRS is furloughing about 34,000 employees—nearly half its workforce—due to the government shutdown, while 39,870 employees (53.6%) remain on the job. An IRS-wide furlough began October 8, 2025, closing most operations; non-exempt employees are in non-pay, non-duty status until further notice.

The passage describes NVIDIA's GA10x Ampere GPU architecture and its improvements over the prior Turing generation. The GA10x SM doubles FP32 throughput (128 FP32 operations per clock across four partitions), features third-generation Tensor Cores that are twice as powerful as Turing's, and includes a 33% larger combined L1 data cache/shared memory (128 KB per SM). Second-generation RT Cores double the ray/triangle intersection testing rate and add a new Interpolate Triangle Position unit enabling hardware-accelerated ray-traced motion blur up to eight times faster than Turing. GA10x also supports concurrent RT Core, graphics, and compute workloads.

Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32 and BF16 data types and Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity, which doubles throughput for sparse matrix operations. DLSS is enhanced with a 9x super resolution factor, enabling 8K 60 fps gaming. GA10x is the first GPU architecture to use GDDR6X memory with PAM4 signaling, delivering up to 19.5 Gbps data rates and 936 GB/sec bandwidth. NVIDIA RTX IO, working with Microsoft's DirectStorage API, provides GPU-based lossless decompression for up to 100x I/O performance improvement.

The A40 data center GPU delivers up to 2x FP32, 2x ray tracing, and 5x (10x with Sparsity) AI throughput versus the Quadro RTX 6000, with 48 GB memory expandable to 96 GB via NVLink. Ampere GPUs support HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC, include fifth-generation NVDEC (first with AV1 hardware decode) and seventh-generation NVENC, and are up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing. The passage also covers the GeForce RTX 3090 and 3070, a new Error Detection and Replay feature for GDDR6X overclocking, and the RTX A6000 workstation GPU with 48 GB GDDR6.

This study analyzes public financing instruments for innovative cleantech start-ups and SMEs in Europe, many under Horizon 2020, which had 80 billion in funding from 2014-2020. Instruments offer loans, equity, grants, and guarantees in fields including energy efficiency, smart cities, ICT, renewable energy, and healthcare. The EIB and EIF are the main managing bodies, alongside EBRD, EUREKA, and the European Commission. The study benchmarks instruments on metrics such as portfolio size, investment size, success rates, TRL, consortium requirements, and monitoring frequency, and notes many also provide non-financial support like coaching and advisory services.

The speaker addresses a relief meeting in Washington held in response to the disaster that struck Johnstown, Pennsylvania, and nearby communities on the Susquehanna River. He notes that such gatherings across the country express sympathy and brotherhood, and reports that Jacksonville, Florida has wired authorization to draw $2,000 for relief. Citing a dispatch from Pennsylvania's governor, he states that communication has been opened with Williamsport, where losses are appalling and thousands are hungry, homeless, and penniless, with urgent need of food. He proposes three committees: one to collect food for dispatch by train that night or early morning, one to gather clothing and bedclothing, and one of business people and bankers to collect money for rebuilding homes. He expresses hope that Washington will respond generously and mentions his own subscription sent to Johnstown's mayor.

The Louisiana Court of Appeal, Fourth Circuit, affirmed William Brock's conviction for molestation of a juvenile under R.S. 14:81.2 and his ten-year sentence at hard labor. Brock, engaged to the three-year-old victim's mother and living with them, was accused after the child complained of pain and her mother found Brock's pubic hair on the child's private area. The child later stated Brock had touched her. Dr. Garza testified that the child's vaginal trauma was caused by manual digital manipulation and was not self-inflicted. Brock denied the abuse but admitted no other man had opportunity to commit the act. The court found the evidence sufficient to establish all elements of the offense, including Brock's identity as perpetrator, sexual intent, and his position of control over the child. The court also found the sentence was not excessive, as the trial court complied with C.Cr.P. Art. 894.1 and imposed a term five years below the statutory maximum. Both assignments of error were found without merit, and the conviction and sentence were affirmed.

The Tennessee National Wildlife Refuge headquarters and Visitor Center will close Monday, August 21 for the solar eclipse. The public is directed to Cross Creeks National Wildlife Refuge in Dover to view the total eclipse, where totality will last approximately 55 seconds. Glasses, t-shirts, and water will be sold as a fundraiser for Friends of Cross Creeks NWR.

Centrica's stock price fell 35% over the past year, giving it an 8.6% dividend yield—nearly three times inflation. The company is transforming its business model amid regulatory uncertainty, trades at a P/E of around 10, and is expected to grow earnings 7% this year, suggesting strong total return potential despite volatility and limited dividend growth prospects. Volution, a ventilation products supplier, reported 11.6% revenue growth and a 6.7% rise in adjusted operating profit to £18.3m, and acquired New Zealand supplier Simx Limited. With earnings forecast to rise 6% this year and 7% next year, and dividends covered 3.3 times by profit, Volution could deliver inflation-beating dividend growth despite its 2.2% yield.

This study examined the attitudes of pre-service teachers at Bayburt University Faculty of Education towards the Research Methods in Education (RME) course, which was renamed from Scientific Research Methods by YÖK in 2018. Using a mixed-methods sequential explanatory design, the quantitative phase surveyed 190 students from Turkish Teaching, English Teaching, and Pre-School Teaching departments via a researcher-developed 21-item attitude scale with three sub-dimensions: contribution to the profession, confidence, and contribution to daily life (Cronbach's alpha = .920). The qualitative phase involved focus group interviews with 10 pre-service teachers, analyzed through content analysis.

Findings showed no significant difference in attitudes by department (p>.05), but a significant difference by grade level (x²=8.62, p<.05), with fourth-grade students showing more positive attitudes than first-graders. The contribution to daily life dimension received the highest mean scores. Qualitatively, 90% of participants found the course necessary, citing gains in scientific research skills, personal development (e.g., using SPSS), and professional knowledge. However, 60% reported insufficient lesson duration, while 20% each cited the lecturer's teaching and inadequacies in tools and materials.

The study concluded that attitudes differed by grade level, possibly because fourth-graders had completed foundational courses. It was recommended that prerequisite courses precede RME, the course be offered to third- or fourth-grade students, made compulsory, extended in credit and duration, or structured as RME 1 and RME 2.

President George W. Bush held his final press conference, thanking the press corps for their professional relationship over eight years. On the remaining $350 billion in bailout funds, he said he would only request it if President-Elect Obama asked him to. On Gaza, he supported a sustainable cease-fire contingent on Hamas stopping rocket attacks, affirmed Israel's right to defend herself, and defended his two-state solution vision. He identified an attack on the homeland as the most urgent threat facing the next President, noting North Korea and Iran remain dangerous. He urged the Republican Party to be more inclusive and compassionate after its defeat. Defending his record, he cited the Iraq surge, 52 months of job growth, and tax cuts, and said he set aside free market principles to prevent a possible depression worse than the Great Depression. He dismissed hostile critics as a small minority and declined to discuss pardons. He acknowledged mistakes, including the "Mission Accomplished" banner and the timing of the Social Security push, and disappointments including Abu Ghraib and the absence of weapons of mass destruction. He rejected claims that America's moral standing had been damaged. He expressed concern about rising protectionism and disappointment over three failed trade bills. On New Orleans, he defended the federal response and cited $121 billion in aid. He said Obama's election demonstrated racial progress, predicted he would not decompress long, and expressed hope for a more respectful tone in Washington under his successor.

This study explored the mentorship needs and experiences of entry-level occupational therapy students, focusing on those from historically underrepresented groups, to inform the development of culturally sensitive mentoring programs. A cross-sectional survey collected responses from 133 students at a large urban private university, 59 of whom identified as being from historically underrepresented groups. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, between-group comparisons, and content analysis of open-ended responses. Results indicated that current mentorship programming was insufficient for students from historically underrepresented groups. Students desired mentors who understood the transition from academia to clinical practice and demonstrated cultural humility, empathy, anti-racism allyship, and support for handling workplace discrimination. BIPOC students rated mentors' awareness of biases and prejudices as significantly more important than white students did, while Hispanic/Latinx students reported lower satisfaction with mentors' effectiveness across cultural backgrounds and with integrating personal life and academic responsibilities. Students valued mentors' personality, expertise, availability, and shared interests, with over a third preferring mentors of similar ethnic or cultural backgrounds. They also sought guidance on networking, certification preparation, job searching, work-life balance, and confidence building, and preferred regular, scheduled communication with mentors. The authors recommend hybrid formal and informal mentorship models, virtual mentoring platforms, culturally sensitive mentor training, increased diverse mentor representation, and institutional support, noting the new 2023 ACOTE standards. Limitations include the single urban institution, cross-sectional design, and focus on race and ethnicity only. The study concludes that culturally sensitive mentorship can enhance equity, inclusion, educational outcomes, and professional resilience for students from historically underrepresented groups.

The Colorado Supreme Court, in an original proceeding in the nature of prohibition, considered whether a district court had jurisdiction over defendants served with summons in California under Rule 4(f)(1) R.C.P. Colo., which permits personal service outside the state upon Colorado residents. Defendants, who sold their Denver home to plaintiffs in April 1951, were first served through a daughter at a Denver address where they had never lived; after they moved to quash that service, plaintiffs personally served an alias summons on them in California. The trial court found the Denver service insufficient but upheld the California service as being upon Colorado residents and ordered defendants to answer, prompting this proceeding.

The court held it could entertain the prohibition action, stating that no question of greater public importance arises than when a court proceeds without jurisdiction of the person or subject matter. On the uncontroverted facts, defendants left Colorado in September 1951 due to a heart condition requiring residence at sea level, stated they had no intention of returning, settled in Ventura, California, where Mr. Kellner obtained employment, purchased lots for a permanent home, secured California automobile tags and operator's licenses, and registered to vote in California before the action commenced. Residence under the statutes and rules is determined by intention, which must be supported by acts; voter registration in California is compelling evidence of intent to change residence. When defendants' affidavits made a prima facie denial of Colorado residence, the burden of proving such residence fell on plaintiffs, who failed to meet it.

The court concluded the trial court erred in denying the motion to quash the California service and was wholly without jurisdiction over the persons of defendants; the rule to show cause was made absolute.

European markets hit record highs, with the STOXX 600 up about 0.5 percent, led by steel and banking stocks. Steelmakers rallied after the European Commission proposed nearly halving tariff-free steel import quotas, while banks gained on stable bond yields and improving credit margins. BMW declined after trimming its 2025 profit forecast. Fed easing expectations lifted sentiment, with gold surpassing $4,000 per ounce, though analysts cautioned valuations could face pressure from sticky inflation or trade tensions.

The Royal Rumble 2017 will take place at the Alamodome, with WWE aiming to sell over 60,000 tickets. Goldberg, Brock Lesnar, and John Cena are confirmed, The Undertaker is expected, and Shawn Michaels is rumoured for a non-wrestling role. The match card includes: AJ Styles defending the WWE Championship against John Cena in their third singles match, with Cena chasing a record-tying 16th World Championship; Kevin Owens defending the Universal Championship against Roman Reigns, with Chris Jericho suspended in a shark cage to prevent interference; and the 30-Man Royal Rumble match, featuring Goldberg as first entrant and Brock Lesnar, with names like Braun Strowman, The Undertaker, and Finn Balor still uncertain.

The Sensex fell 12.31 points to close at 28,339.31, while the Nifty declined 0.14 percent to 8,792. Five stocks hit new 52-week highs: AIA Engineering (Rs 1,441) after reporting 17.6 percent year-on-year net profit growth to Rs 120 crore and declaring an interim dividend of Rs 4 per share; Alkem Laboratories after a 24.9 percent rise in Q3 net profit to Rs 233.4 crore; KEC International (Rs 170); Exide Industries (Rs 218), which received a buy rating with a Rs 230 target; and Kalpataru Power Transmission (Rs 299.85) on unusually high trading volumes.

U.S. rare earth and critical mineral mining stocks surged after China tightened export restrictions, requiring licenses for products containing rare earths worth 0.1% or more of the goods' value and for use of China's extraction, refining, or magnet recycling technology. The restrictions came ahead of an expected meeting between Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump at the APEC summit in Seoul. Investors speculate the Trump administration, which has taken equity stakes in miners including MP Materials, will invest further in building a domestic supply chain, as rare earths are crucial inputs for weapons platforms, robotics, electric vehicles, and electronics.

Bath Rugby fans remain stranded in France three days after their team's 24-20 Champions Cup loss to Toulon, as snow, ice and wind across southern England and northern Europe caused travel chaos. Flight cancellations from Marseille, Nice and Amsterdam, plus disruption at Heathrow and other London airports, forced supporters to take creative routes home via cities including Munich, Brussels, Madrid and Paris. The Bath team flew home on a chartered BMI flight on Sunday. Fans reported missed connections, delayed Eurostar services, cancelled trains and twice-cancelled British Airways flights; one group is unlikely to return in time for the funeral of season-ticket holder Mike Grice. A BA error cancelled the wrong flight at Nice, causing chaos, and a death on the rail line delayed journeys from Toulon. Some flights were diverted to Bournemouth or Cardiff. Several fans, including Steve Watson, Trish Lawrence and James Marchant, remained positive despite the disruption.

Two Boeing 737 MAX 8 crashes—Lion Air Flight 610 in October 2018 (189 deaths) and Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 in March 2019 (157 deaths)—killed 346 people and led to the grounding of all 737 MAX aircraft in March 2019. Investigations focused on the Maneuvering Characteristics Augmentation System (MCAS), software designed to push the nose down, which relied on a single angle-of-attack sensor and could repeatedly force the nose down based on erroneous data. Internal communications showed Boeing engineers knew of MCAS problems before the crashes. The fleet remained grounded 21 months; Boeing lost 1,043 orders, and the FAA permitted return to service in November 2020.

The case traces Boeing's history: its market dominance under leader Thornton Wilson, an engineering- and family-oriented culture, and the 1997 McDonnell Douglas merger, after which critics said the culture shifted toward shareholder value. Competition with Airbus, particularly the A320neo, prompted Boeing to rush the 737 MAX's development on a compressed schedule rather than build a new aircraft. During certification, Boeing presented MCAS as a minor modification, failed to report later design changes to the FAA, and avoided requiring simulator training, relying instead on computer-based training.

Afterward, CEO Dennis Muilenburg was fired and replaced by David Calhoun. Estimated costs exceeded $21 billion directly, with $67 billion in lost sales, and Boeing's stock remained 52% below pre-crash levels by August 2022. The case raises unresolved questions about Boeing's safety culture, FAA independence, and industry self-regulation.

The speaker recounts being out of action for about seven months during contract negotiations, which he describes as deep and honest but prolonged. Russian coaches selected him for the Olympics, and three weeks of workouts with the junior whalers helped him get back on track mentally. An offer came from a team in North Carolina, giving Detroit seven days to match; wanting to stay in Detroit, where he defected from Russia to play, he was relieved when Detroit matched. He returned to play on a Friday night, mentally exhausted from rapid changes and travel from Japan, and focused on reconnecting with teammates and winning back fans while correcting misinformation. He also recalls Vladi appearing at the Stanley Cup game after Scotty Bowman's inspirational speech, describing how he spoke Russian with Vladi, who smiled and posed on the ice.

This paper presents HCAR, a three-phase hybrid Constraint Acquisition (CA) framework designed to address over-fitting of global constraints learned from limited positive examples. Passive CA infers constraints from fixed datasets but over-fits when examples are few; active CA queries an oracle but incurs high query costs; existing hybrid methods lack mechanisms to correct over-fitted global constraints from the passive phase. The proposed framework consists of: (1) a passive learning phase that generates candidate global constraints (AllDifferent, Sum, Count) via structural pattern detection and prunes fixed-arity constraints inconsistent with positive examples; (2) a Query-Driven Interactive Refinement phase, the core contribution, which assigns machine learning-based confidence priors to candidates, poses targeted oracle queries, updates confidence via Bayesian updates, accepts or rejects constraints based on predefined thresholds, and applies a Subset Exploration mechanism that recovers valid sub-constraints from rejected globals by removing variables while preserving parameters; and (3) a final active learning phase using MQuAcq-2 to learn remaining fixed-arity constraints. Adaptive query budget allocation redistributes unused budget among candidates. Empirical validation on diverse benchmarks demonstrated high accuracy and target model coverage from limited examples with manageable query complexity.

This study examined research expectations for US mathematics education faculty. A literature review indicated that expectations vary by institution type (Carnegie classification), department type (education vs. mathematics), and the percentage of time devoted to research, and that scholarship is typically measured by the quantity and sometimes quality of publications.

The researchers surveyed faculty identified through publications in 55 mathematics education journals and related book series from 2015–2017. Of 1,593 surveys sent, 821 responded, yielding 404 target-population respondents. The survey addressed demographics, expected annual publication numbers, and the value of various scholarly activities. Data were analyzed using frequencies and multinomial logistic regressions.

Overall, faculty are expected to publish about 1.64 papers per year, with research journal articles valued most. Expectations vary by institution type: R1 faculty average 2.25 expected papers per year with 40% research time and value non-journal publications less; R2 faculty average 1.5 papers, with 65% devoting at least 40% of time to research and being most likely to have written expectations documents; Other-institution faculty average 1 paper per year with about 20% research time. Higher research commitment correlates with more expected papers (0.184 per 10% increase). Mathematics departments expect 0.309 fewer papers than education departments, value conference proceedings and funding more, and value presentations, professional development, and first authorship less. Surprising findings included variability at R1 and Other institutions, 11% of R1 faculty expecting three or more papers yearly, and written documents being more common at R2 institutions.

The authors conclude that expectations vary systematically and recommend that faculty, programs, and the field engage in transparent dialogue and make expectations explicit in written documents.

Keltner Channels (also called Keltner Bands) are a technical analysis tool developed by Chester W. Keltner, a commodity trader, in the 1960s. They consist of three lines: a middle line (typically an exponential moving average or typical price) and upper and lower bands set at a multiple of the Average True Range (ATR). Unlike Bollinger Bands, which use standard deviation and are more responsive, Keltner Channels use ATR and expand or contract with volatility. A common setting is a 20-period EMA with a 2.0 ATR multiplier. The channels are considered leading indicators and can be applied to mean reversion, momentum, scalping, and swing trading. A backtested mean reversion strategy on SPY produced 288 trades with a 77% win rate and 6.3% CAGR, while a momentum approach using 30-day periods and a 1.3 ATR yielded a 3.6% CAGR. The indicator does not repaint. Traders are advised to avoid over-reliance on it and to combine it with other analysis, adjusting settings for market volatility and customizing them for specific trading styles.

On December 12, 2016, NVIDIA Corporation entered into a Termination Agreement with Goldman, Sachs & Co. to terminate 63,259,180.62 warrants to purchase NVIDIA common stock, originally issued under letter agreements dated November 25 and 26, 2013. As consideration, NVIDIA will deliver shares of common stock to Goldman, with the amount determined daily based on the volume-weighted average price during an observation period from December 13, 2016 to January 31, 2017. The shares are being issued in reliance on the Section 4(a)(2) registration exemption.

This paper investigates the orbital Edelstein effect (OEE) and spin Edelstein effect (SEE) in doped monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) in the 2H structure under a perpendicular gate field. Pristine 2H-TMDs, with nongyrotropic D3h point group symmetry, exhibit no Edelstein effect; breaking the mirror symmetry σh—via a substrate or a gate field—produces the gyrotropic C3v group, enabling a non-zero response. The gate field induces Rashba-type chiral spin and orbital textures, and an applied in-plane electric field shifts the Fermi surface, generating magnetization in both channels.

The authors employ a minimal 5×5 tight-binding Hamiltonian in the metal d orbital subspace, obtained by Löwdin downfolding of chalcogen orbitals and fitted to density functional theory bands for several TMDs (MoS2, MoSe2, MoTe2, WS2, WSe2, WTe2, NbS2, NbSe2). The gate field introduces parameters γ1 and γ2, which mix orbital sectors and scale linearly with the field.

For hole doping, the orbital textures of the two spin-split valence bands share the same chirality, so their OEE contributions add, while opposite spin chiralities cause the SEE contributions to cancel. The Γ valley, governed by the larger parameter γ1, dominates the response once holes occupy it, strongly enhancing both OEE and SEE. Since the valence band maximum normally lies at K/K′, a critical hole concentration is required to populate the Γ pocket; small compressive strain reduces the Γ–K energy separation, making the Γ valley accessible at low doping and enhancing the Edelstein response substantially (about 1% strain for MoS2).

For electron doping, electrons occupy the K/K′ conduction bands. Here the OEE is several times larger than the SEE and grows linearly with electron concentration, while the SEE remains small due to interband cancellation; strain is not needed in this case.

The computed Edelstein susceptibilities reach ~10⁻⁸–10⁻⁷ µB V⁻¹m, one to two orders of magnitude larger than previously reported for other systems. Combined with experimentally achievable doping and large gate fields (up to 0.4 eV/Å), the results identify monolayer TMDs as an ideal platform for studying the orbital Edelstein effect, with potential relevance for spintronics applications.

Government shutdowns have historically had little effect on markets and the economy, but this one could differ. President Trump has threatened to make some furloughs permanent, which analysts say could have longer-lasting impacts on an already precarious employment picture and inject new uncertainty. Past shutdowns cost roughly 0.1 percentage point of GDP per week, with losses typically recouped quickly. A prolonged shutdown could also delay key economic data: the Bureau of Labor Statistics would be shuttered, with possible delays and reduced data quality. A delayed CPI could affect Social Security cost-of-living adjustments, and the Federal Reserve might have to rely on private data for policy decisions. Analysts expect a relatively mild overall impact, though furloughed employees and contractors face immediate financial strain.

The column, written by an Oklahoma criminal defense attorney, discusses the Netflix documentary "Unknown Number: The High School Catfish," which follows students in Beal City, Michigan, as they investigate who is sending harassing, vulgar, and sexually graphic text messages to junior high student Lauryn Licari and her boyfriend, Owen McKenny. The messages escalate to 30-40 per day and eventually include threats against Lauryn's life, with the sender appearing to have personal knowledge of the couple. After local investigations stall for 18 months, the sheriff sends the FBI 720 pages of messages, and the bureau requests a forensic examination of Owen's phone. The author criticizes the documentary for not exploring cellphone forensics in depth, noting the distinction between data on a phone and cellular provider records, which can track a person's movements. The perpetrator's identity is not revealed. The author connects the documentary to Oklahoma's "bell to bell" law for the 2025-2026 school year, which prohibits cellphones, smartwatches, and other internet-connected devices in schools on a one-year trial basis. Despite some backlash from parents and students, the author supports the policy, citing criminal cases against teenagers that began with cellphone use.

The Fabian Timing Model, developed by Richard Fabian in the 1960s, is a quantitative long-term trend-following strategy for the S&P 500 based on its 39-week moving average, with signals confirmed by the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the utilities sector to reduce false signals. Fabian described the strategy in his book *The Mutual Fund Wealth Builder* and advocated adhering to a mechanical system rather than discretionary predictions. A backtest of the original rules showed returns close to buy-and-hold, but with low volatility and low maximum drawdown, which are the strategy's main selling points. The key lesson is that discipline in following the system matters more than the model itself.

The Bank of England allocated £5.085 billion in its six-month indexed long-term repo operation, the highest since March 2020 and more than double the prior week's £2.352 billion, reflecting rising bank demand for central bank liquidity. The facility provides six-month secured funding backed by high-quality collateral, typically without surcharges. The BoE is encouraging repo usage as it unwinds quantitative easing—during which gilt holdings peaked at £875 billion—and shifts toward a framework where banks actively borrow rather than rely on abundant reserves. Demand for six-month repos remains modest compared with short-term facilities, as a record £87.149 billion was allotted through the seven-day repo programme last week. The shift's success depends on sustained longer-term repo demand and balancing liquidity provision with gilt market stability.

A South Carolina House panel advanced a pension bill Tuesday that would raise employee contributions from 8.66% to 9% and employer contributions to 18.56% by 2023, aiming to address the system's $24 billion gap; some local officials object to the increased employer costs. A bill requiring recognition of out-of-state concealed weapons permits advanced to the House floor. The Senate passed a bill creating Coastal Carolina University championship license plates, with profits funding scholarships.

In this lecture, Lorna Gibson continues the discussion of trabecular bone and osteoporosis. She describes obtaining a whale vertebra from the Mass Fish and Wildlife Department for a student project, noting its uniform trabecular structure. Osteoporosis was modeled using Voronoi honeycombs analyzed via finite element methods by graduate student Matt Silva. The modulus of the random Voronoi structure closely matched the analytical equations, but strengths were only 0.6–0.8 times those of periodic hexagonal honeycombs, with a minimum near 5% relative density attributed to interaction between elastic buckling and plastic yielding. Models with removed struts showed much greater loss of modulus and strength than models with only thinned struts, reaching a percolation threshold (~30–35% density reduction in 2D; 50% in 3D). A perturbed square Voronoi model was adapted to match vertebral bone architecture, and a 3D version showed similar trends. The lecture then covers metal foams (titanium, tantalum) as bone substitute coatings and implants, describing manufacturing processes including replica methods, fugitive phase, foaming agents, argon expansion, freeze casting, and selective laser sintering. Finally, Gibson discusses bone evolution: early animals were mineralized with calcium carbonate or silica, while calcium phosphate bone appeared about 450 million years ago with ray-finned fish. She describes a study of the roughly 8-million-year-old fossil Oreopithecus bambolii, whose ilium trabecular architecture resembled humans more than non-human primates, suggesting bipedalism. Next week's topic is tissue engineering scaffolds.

Chelsea will face Barcelona in the Champions League last 16 after finishing second in Group C behind Roma. First legs are scheduled for February 13/14 and 20/21, with second legs on March 6/7 and 13/14. Barcelona won Group D with 14 points.
