This article by Hanne Rinholm, Ida Heiberg Solem, and Inger Ulleberg (Oslo Metropolitan University), published in *Dialogic Pedagogy* (2023), explores dialogic classroom practices through two Norwegian cases: a choir project in pre-service music teacher education and an upper-primary mathematics classroom talk. Motivated by the gap between educational rhetoric—such as UNESCO's call for new forms of education and Norway's Education Act and Core Curriculum emphasizing democracy, participation, and critical thinking—and classroom practice, the study asks which theoretical concepts can help analyze dialogic practices, how participation can be promoted, and how epistemological and ontological dialogue appear and interact.

The interdisciplinary qualitative study used a deductive, narrative, and hermeneutic approach. Its framework draws on dialogism (Bakhtin, Linell), distinguishing epistemological dialogue (development of subject knowledge) from ontological dialogue (engagement with questions central to students' lives and self-understanding), alongside Biesta's dimensions of qualification, socialization, and subjectification, the concept of Bildung (including Mündigkeit/autonomy), musicking (Small), mathematizing (Freudenthal), and the didactic contract (Brousseau).

In the music case, the teacher's decision to share her experience of her brother's AIDS death while rehearsing "Seasons of Love" from *Rent* introduced existential, ontological dimensions alongside epistemological learning. In the mathematics case, students discovered a pattern for finding fractions between two fractions, and the teacher's expressed uncertainty fostered ontological dialogue. Both teachers listened carefully, practiced "uptake," took risks, showed vulnerability, and appeared as whole persons within established didactic contracts.

The discussion addresses Bildung as comprising both ontological and epistemological aspects, teachers' limited control over Bildung processes, and paradoxes—including the risk that pursuing empowerment and democratic goals may produce monologizing practices. The authors conclude that the chosen concepts helped make sense of dialogic classroom practices and that both teachers promoted participation by facilitating ontological and epistemological dialogue.

Tesla, Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2021 reports total revenues of $13,757 million for the third quarter of 2021, up from $8,771 million in the third quarter of 2020, and $36,104 million for the first nine months of 2021 versus $20,792 million in the prior-year period. Net income attributable to common stockholders was $1,618 million for the quarter and $3,198 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2021. Total assets were $57,834 million as of September 30, 2021, compared to $52,148 million as of December 31, 2020.

Tesla operates two reportable segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. During the nine months ended September 30, 2021, the company purchased $1.50 billion in bitcoin; as of September 30, 2021, the carrying value of its digital assets was $1.26 billion, reflecting $101 million of cumulative impairment losses, while fair market value was $1.83 billion, and $128 million of gains were realized in March 2021.

The company also repaid its China loan facilities, Solar Term Loan, Solar Revolving Credit Facility and Automotive Lease-backed Credit Facilities, and issued Automotive Asset-backed Notes in March and September 2021.

The 2018 CEO Performance Award consists of 12 vesting tranches tied to market capitalization and operational milestones; all market capitalization milestones were achieved as of the second quarter of 2021, and related stock-based compensation expense was $190 million and $665 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2021.

The filing cites ongoing COVID-19-related impacts, including port congestion, supplier delays and semiconductor shortages. Tesla is obligated under a lease with the SUNY Foundation for Gigafactory New York to spend or incur $5.00 billion in combined costs in New York State over ten years beginning April 30, 2018. The speaker states that the United States must participate in establishing peace among nations after the current war ends, and outlines the conditions under which it would join a league for peace. While America will have no voice in determining the war's ending terms, it will have a voice in whether they are made lasting through a universal covenant. Any such covenant must include the peoples of the New World and be secured by an organized force greater than any nation or alliance. The speaker argues the war must aim at a just and secure peace rather than a new balance of power, advocating a community of power and an organized common peace. Both sides' assurances that they do not intend to crush their antagonists imply a peace without victory, since victory would impose humiliating terms and leave lasting resentment. Only a peace between equals can endure.

A 19-year-old woman was sexually assaulted on a train to Taunton on April 8. A man from a group of passengers touched her after the train jolted and continued despite her shouting, stopping when the public intervened. Police are appealing for information.

In this lecture, the instructor continues the study of linearized gravity, focusing on the transverse-traceless metric perturbation h^TT_ij, the gauge-invariant radiative degree of freedom. A wave propagating in the z-direction has two independent components, h_xx and h_xy (with h_yy = −h_xx). A naive geodesic calculation suggests freely falling bodies are unaffected by a passing wave, but this reflects a coordinate artifact, since the coordinates follow the bodies. Physical effects appear only when comparing separated bodies: the round-trip travel time of light pulses between two particles depends on h^TT_xx (the basis of LIGO's detection method), and the geodesic deviation equation relates relative acceleration to Riemann curvature components. A ring of test bodies undergoes tidal stretch and squeeze: h_xx produces the "plus" polarization and h_xy the "cross" polarization. LIGO detects these effects by timing laser light bouncing between mirrors using interference. To compute the radiation from a source, one solves the linearized Einstein equation in Lorentz gauge, approximates the far field (observer distance much greater than source size), uses the tensor virial theorem to express the result through the source's quadrupole moment, and projects out the transverse-traceless part with a projection tensor orthogonal to the propagation direction. The result is the quadrupole formula for gravitational waves; factors of c make the effect very small, though the waves carry tremendous energy. The next lecture will address the energy content of gravitational waves.

Winter brings parking congestion around Kensington Park. With no plans to expand parking, Whangarei District Council advises drivers to plan ahead, carpool, leave earlier, or drop players off and walk. Tickets are issued for rule-breaking parking after an initial period of warning fliers.

Researchers identified two receptors on brown adipose tissue (BAT) cells, TRPM8 and TRPP3, as potential therapeutic targets for increasing metabolism-boosting "good" fat, with implications for treating obesity and diabetes. Using human bone marrow stem cells and belly fat cells, they found TRPM8 stimulation promoted brown fat formation while inhibitors blocked it, and eliminating TRPP3 function prevented brown fat development. The receptors may be activated by certain foods or new drugs.

The Jammu and Kashmir Public Service Commission (JKPSC) has kept in abeyance the result of the Combined Competitive (Preliminary) Examination, 2016 and withdrawn the notification for the main examination following detection of discrepancies in question papers and answer keys. All question papers and answer keys of 23 subjects will be referred to independent experts for evaluation. The result, declared on April 23, 2017, was based on earlier expert findings, but the Commission subsequently received representations and RTI applications from KAS aspirants citing further discrepancies. Of the 36,681 candidates who appeared, 6,925 had been declared successful.

Lyminster Primary School in Littlehampton was rated as requiring improvement after a May Ofsted inspection. Inspector Marcia Goodwin acknowledged positive changes by headteacher Steven McGinley, appointed in September 2016, but said they had not had time to make sufficient impact. Weak teaching led to Year 6 pupils under-achieving in SATs. McGinley expressed confidence the school would rapidly bounce back to good, noting it was already good in several categories.

Total net sales were $94.8 billion for the three months, down 3% year-over-year, and $212.0 billion for the six months, down 4%. Net income was $24.2 billion for the quarter and $54.2 billion for the six months, with diluted EPS of $1.52 and $3.41, respectively. By category, iPhone sales rose 2% to $51.3 billion, Services rose 5% to $20.9 billion, while Mac fell 31% to $7.2 billion and iPad fell 13% to $6.7 billion. By segment, Americas declined 8%, Greater China 3%, and Japan 7%, while Europe rose 3% and Rest of Asia Pacific rose 15%. Total assets were $332.2 billion and shareholders' equity $62.2 billion as of April 1, 2023. The Company repurchased $19.1 billion of stock and paid $3.7 billion in dividends during the quarter; on May 4, 2023, the Board authorized an additional $90 billion repurchase program and raised the quarterly dividend to $0.24 per share. Commercial paper outstanding was $2.0 billion and term debt $107.6 billion. The effective tax rate was 14.9%. The European Court of Justice hearing on the State Aid Decision was scheduled for May 23, 2023, and the Ninth Circuit affirmed the district court ruling in the Epic Games case on April 24, 2023. No material changes were reported to risk factors, market risk, critical accounting estimates, or internal controls.

Bluehole launched a new PUBG Xbox One community event, Snipe City, challenging players to collectively make 400,000 kills with M24 and Kar98 sniper rifles. Rewards are available if the community succeeds by July 10.

Zacks Investment Research upgraded State Bank Financial Corporation (NASDAQ:STBZ) from "sell" to "buy" with a $30.00 price target, implying 11.69% upside. Separately, Hovde Group downgraded the stock from "outperform" to "market perform," lowering its target from $25.00 to $24.50. Four analysts rate the stock "hold" and three rate it "buy," for an average "Hold" rating and $25.25 target price. NVIDIA Corporation filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended July 29, 2018 (Q2 fiscal 2019). Revenue was $3,123 million, up 40% year over year and down 3% sequentially, with net income of $1,101 million ($1.76 diluted EPS) and gross margin of 63.3%. For the first half of fiscal 2019, revenue was $6,330 million and net income was $2,345 million. The company reports two segments: GPU revenue was $2,656 million (up 40%), led by gaming ($1,805 million, up 52%), datacenter ($760 million, up 83%), and professional visualization ($281 million, up 20%); Tegra Processor revenue was $467 million (up 40%), including automotive revenue of $161 million. OEM and IP revenue fell 54% to $116 million due to lower demand for cryptocurrency mining GPUs, with cryptocurrency-related revenue of $18 million expected to be negligible going forward. The filing also discusses pending patent litigation with Polaris Innovations and ZiiLabs, adoption of a new revenue accounting standard, $14 million in outstanding Convertible Notes, and effective disclosure controls, with no material changes to risk factors.

In this 1978 Texas divorce appeal, the Court of Civil Appeals affirmed the trial court's decree of divorce and its award of custody of the parties' two minor children to the father, John Geesbreght, but reversed and remanded the property division for a new trial.

On jurisdiction, the court held that Mary Lee waived any complaint by appearing in the Tarrant County court while her Illinois suit was dismissed, and that the children's domicile remained in Texas because John, under Family Code § 12.04, held the parental right to establish their legal domicile; jurisdiction was further supported by Family Code §§ 3.26 and 11.051. Mary Lee's appeal was permitted to proceed after she returned the children she had withheld from John.

On the jury trial, the court found no reversible error in the supplemental charge defining possessory conservatorship and visitation rights, treating the sole objection as waived and the jury's answers as non-binding recommendations.

On property division, the trial court erred in valuing John's stock in Emergency Medicine Consultants, a professional corporation, at its $16,000 book value, failing to consider corporate good will existing apart from John personally—a question distinguishable from Nail v. Nail. This produced a grossly inadequate and clearly erroneous award to Mary Lee. Costs were taxed 50% to each party.

This study externally validated a longitudinal Grade of Membership (L-GoM) model of Alzheimer's disease (AD) progression in the Predictors 3 cohort, a community-based, multiethnic sample of 273 older adults recruited from the Washington Heights Inwood Columbia Aging Project (WHICAP) in Manhattan between 2011 and 2019. Unlike the earlier clinic-based Predictors 1 and 2 cohorts—composed of non-Hispanic white, high socioeconomic status patients with mild AD—Predictors 3 included community-dwelling individuals with MCI or AD dementia from diverse ethnic, linguistic, and SES backgrounds.

The L-GoM model, developed using Predictors 2 data, represents each patient's clinical status as a weighted combination of four disease subtypes based on 11 measurement domains and 73 time-varying signs/symptoms. Validation involved inputting initial-visit data to generate predicted survival and need for full-time care (FTC) over 7.5 years, then comparing these predictions with observed group-level outcomes.

Among the 273 participants, 123 had MCI (83 nonconverters, 40 converters) and 150 had AD dementia (118 nonreverters, 32 reverters). The model accurately predicted mortality and FTC for AD nonreverters and MCI cases, but failed for AD reverters, who were likely misdiagnosed, as most reverted to non-dementia CDR scores within 2–3 years. MCI converters survived longer than predicted, while nonconverters showed lower-than-predicted FTC rates. The study also demonstrated, for the first time, that the model extends to MCI.

The authors concluded that the L-GoM model is valid for community-dwelling older adults of different ethnic, linguistic, and SES backgrounds, while noting limitations including the predominantly Caribbean Hispanic sample, small non-Hispanic nonwhite subgroup, and the need for further research on incorporating biological domains.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2022 reports total revenue of $49.4 billion for the third quarter, up from $41.7 billion in the prior year quarter, with net income of $16.7 billion compared to $15.5 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $2.22 versus $2.03. For the nine months ended March 31, 2022, revenue was $146.4 billion and net income was $56.0 billion.

Fibonacci trading uses tools such as the retracement, expansion, and fan to identify potential support and resistance levels, helping traders plan entries, exits, stops, and targets. Unlike lagging indicators, these tools mark levels before price reaches them. The retracement tool draws horizontal lines at ratios such as 23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, and 61.8% of a prior price swing; the expansion tool projects potential profit targets; the fan creates trendlines that may act as dynamic support and resistance. There is no single best timeframe or level—these depend on trading style and market volatility, and should be determined through backtesting. The authors are skeptical of Fibonacci trading, citing a lack of scientific evidence and successful backtests. A study by Clarissa Gunawan found a passive buy-and-hold strategy outperformed an active Fibonacci retracement strategy on Vanguard ETFs, though retracements may still help mark support, resistance, and profit targets. The authors recommend caution and backtesting before use.
Before the Vegas Golden Knights' debut, the Dallas Stars joined them in honoring victims of the Las Vegas mass shooting that killed 58, plus a deceased staff member and announcer Dave Strader.

A Yale-Brookings study led by economist Martha Gimbel argues that AI's impact on the U.S. labor market amounts to "lightning strikes" in specific sectors rather than broad disruption. Drawing on Bureau of Labor Statistics data, the researchers found occupational shifts remain within historical norms and are driven by a slowing economy, an aging population, and reduced immigration rather than AI. While youth unemployment has climbed to 10.5% and recent graduates struggle to find white-collar roles, the authors attribute this to macroeconomic conditions in a "low hire, low-fire" environment. They distinguish AI exposure from displacement, noting workers like radiologists have thrived despite AI adoption. Co-author Molly Kinder says generative AI is more likely to affect big cities with knowledge and tech jobs, and that real displacement, if it comes, will stem from enterprise workflow redesign, taking years rather than months to materialize.

This article presents an overview of day trading, defined as buying and selling financial instruments within the same trading day to profit from short-term price movements. It lists 21 strategies, including momentum, range, scalping, breakout, pullback, reversal, gap, news, pattern, seasonal, dark pool, statistical arbitrage, pairs, order flow, market making, short squeeze, statistical volatility, market profile, regime switching, volatility targeting, and phase analysis trading. Each carries distinct risks; for example, almost all scalpers lose money, and pairs trading has become more competitive than in the past.

Day trading differs from swing trading in time horizon—same-day versus days to weeks. Key risks include market volatility, leverage (which magnifies both profits and losses), and emotional decision-making. Discipline, technical analysis, and backtesting are emphasized; the authors recommend quantified, backtested trading rules. Strategies can be applied across stocks, forex, futures, and cryptocurrencies with adjustments for each market's characteristics.

FINRA requires $25,000 minimum equity for US pattern day traders. The best trading times are typically the first hour after open and the last hour before close, with most volume occurring in the final 30 minutes. Holidays, seasonal changes, and time of day affect volatility and trading volumes. Astrology is not scientifically proven as a trading method.

An example backtested strategy (Strategy #78) on SPY since 1993 produced 165 trades with a 0.51% average gain per trade, 60% win rate, 9% maximum drawdown, and 2.5% annual returns while invested only 2% of the time. Although day trading can be profitable, only about 10% of day traders make money; earning a consistent 1% daily is unrealistic, though a $10,000 account might earn $200–300 daily at 2–3% returns. The 11am rule holds that a trending security making a new high between 11:15–11:30 am EST has roughly a 75% chance of closing within 1% of its high of day.

Impact VC firms, which invest in for-profit businesses delivering social or environmental benefits while seeking market-beating returns, have raised $13 billion since 2001, with $10 billion raised since 2010. The author distinguishes these funds from broader impact investing, which accepts sub-market or net-zero returns, and proposes "GoodBusiness" as a name for the sector of purpose-driven for-profit companies. The author presents what is described as the first comparison of impact VC funds, including only those with explicit profit-from-purpose strategies and portfolios at least 50 percent invested in GoodBusiness. Notable firms include DBL Partners (founded 2004, with exits including Tesla and SolarCity), Capricorn Investment Group (over $5 billion across 24 funds), and Generation Investment Management. Funds are categorized as broad-focus, traditional VC-style firms ($100–900 million), sub-$100 million funds, and founder/LP funds such as Omidyar Network and the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative. Sub-sectors include environmental protection (the largest), emerging markets ($1.25 billion), Western consumer products, and governance/underrepresented founders. The author predicts strong returns for funds backing alternative energy, underserved markets, and future job sectors, and expects dedicated sector expansion to slow in 10–15 years as traditional VC funds adopt GoodBusiness investment theses.

A Ukrainian startup, Denmark-based Dropla, founded by V'yacheslav Shvaydak, has developed an AI software called Blue Eyes to counter Russian ambush drones. Since spring, Russia has deployed explosive-laden quadcopters that lie in wait behind Ukrainian lines to attack supply vehicles, some solar-powered or fiber-optic and unjammable. Blue Eyes processes real-time video from cheap quadcopters flying over supply roads, analyzing thermal and optical footage at up to 130 frames per second to detect threats, including more than 170 types of explosives and idling drones. Detected threat coordinates are sent to Ukraine's battle management system for commanders to act on. Multiple frontline units have tested the system in combat since early summer, and Dropla plans to scale deployments fivefold. Experts warn that ambush drones combined with remote mining can disrupt entire logistics chains, requiring militaries to constantly adapt their technology.

This policy brief examines Education Savings Accounts (ESAs), positioning the 2023 wave of universal ESA authorizations (Arkansas, Florida, Iowa, Utah) as a turning point comparable to the 1993 wave of charter school authorizations. Arizona introduced targeted ESAs in 2011; Arizona and West Virginia made them universal in 2022, followed by additional states in 2024–2025. The author notes a political contrast: the "class of 1993" charter states were predominantly blue, while ESA states are red. Unlike charters, ESAs carry few regulatory strings.

Both conventional vouchers and ESAs derive from Milton Friedman—conventional vouchers from his 1955 essay and "divisible" ESAs from his lesser-known 1973 essay. Vouchers were designed to cover only a basic education, requiring parents to "top up" for costlier schools. Citing Nancy MacLean, the author argues vouchers aimed at privatization rather than educational improvement. U.S. ESA allocations fall far below per-pupil public spending (e.g., Wyoming 32%, West Virginia 34%, Georgia 44%), unlike European systems; EdChoice's emphasis on taxpayer savings suggests, per the author, that shrinking government is the primary purpose.

Documented problems include: weak spending accountability (Arizona banned purchases of weapons, pets, and pools; Florida approved kayaks and theme park tickets); weak pedagogical accountability (no teacher certification, testing, or curriculum alignment requirements); rising private school tuition (Iowa); and ballooning costs as middle- and upper-income families already in private schools receive subsidies (Arizona grew from $77 million in 2013 to over $1 billion in 2025; Florida to $3.7 billion). Charter school studies suggest public districts cannot cut costs commensurate with enrollment losses. Rural schools are especially vulnerable because ESAs enable homeschooling and pods, threatening schools that anchor civic life. ESAs also facilitate discrimination: few states mandate nondiscrimination in admissions, private schools push out low-achieving students, and LGBTQ+ faculty lack protections after Our Lady of Guadalupe v. Morrissey-Berru. Supreme Court voucher rulings (Zelman, Espinoza, Carson) ignored European systems imposing nondiscrimination and curriculum requirements.

Spread may accelerate through the Trump administration's Educational Choice for Children Act, though low private school teacher pay and limits on homeschooling capacity act as brakes. The author concludes that voters have rejected voucher referenda (Colorado, Kentucky, Nebraska in 2024) and recommends repealing ESAs or, where infeasible, opposing expansion, imposing budget limits, requiring certified teachers, assessments, audits, and civil rights compliance, and strengthening expenditure oversight.

An April 11, 2001 email from Jean Munoz (McNally Temple) distributing "IEP News" to numerous energy industry, government, and legal recipients, compiling news coverage of the California energy crisis. Key stories include: a confidential Cal-ISO study, reported by the Los Angeles Times, alleging that government-owned utilities—the Los Angeles DWP, Bonneville Power Administration, and BC Hydro's Powerex—helped inflate wholesale electricity prices, with Powerex earning $176 million in alleged excess profits; DWP officials denied manipulation. California legislators traveled to Boise to urge FERC to impose wholesale price caps but left without commitments, as Chairman Curt Hebert opposed caps. PUC President Loretta Lynch testified further rate increases may be needed absent federal action against gouging. Southern California Edison agreed to a $2.76 billion state purchase of its transmission grid, while PG&E pursued bankruptcy and sought a restraining order against the PUC. Additional items covered state-mandated business lighting conservation, Cheney's defense of the Bush administration's anti-price-cap stance, Bonneville's threatened 250 percent rate increase due to drought, resident opposition to reactivating Maryland's Cove Point LNG facility, and Spain's new electricity tariffs designed to avoid a "California experience."

The Side Screen Offense is a two-player screen and roll isolation and the most used play in the NBA. Though simple in appearance, it offers numerous quick-hitting options and can be initiated by a post stepping out to set an on-ball screen. It serves as continuity when plays break down or to create shots as the shot clock winds down. The basic option involves a guard driving over the screen, with choices including driving to the basket, pull-up jumpers, return passes to the post, and kick-out passes to shooters. Success depends on recognizing eight basic defensive reads and executing the corresponding counters, requiring the ballhandler and screener to function as one unit through proper footwork, timing, and non-verbal communication. Common entries include the High Post Rub, Power, and Horns sets, while continuity options include Flex, Triangle Game, and Motion. The passage also covers teaching methods, game strategies such as scouting opponents, and the importance of knowing how to defend against this widely used offense.
A player is seizing opportunities rather than waiting for injuries, jokes his beard beats Marshy's, notes teammates' first Stanley Cup Finals experience, and aims for a split.

This patent application, a continuation of multiple prior patents and provisional applications by Thomas et al. and Foster et al., relates to fluid ends used in hydraulic fracturing. The background explains that fracking requires highly pressurized fluid (typically 10,000–15,000 psi, up to 22,500 psi) carrying proppants to be injected into a wellbore to fracture rock formations. Fluid ends, paired one-to-one with power ends, act as hydraulic pumps and endure extreme pressures, vibration, and abrasives. Traditional fluid ends—single housings machined from high-strength alloy steel with intersecting vertical and horizontal bores—are prone to corrosion and fatigue cracks, particularly at corners surrounding internal chambers and at the neck joining the flange and housing, and may need replacement after as few as two fracking jobs.

The disclosed fluid end instead comprises multiple fluid end sections (preferably five) arranged side-by-side, each with a single horizontal bore and no intersecting chamber, reducing stress points, manufacturing cost, and machining time. Each cylindrical housing mounts to a connect plate secured by stay rods and a stud-based fastening system. Upper and lower intake manifolds allow different fluids (e.g., differing proppant concentrations) to be delivered to each section, while a top-mounted discharge bore with an oval cross-section permits wall compression, stress reduction, and natural gas escape.

Each section includes a stuffing box, retainer, plunger packing, and packing nut (using buttress threads for quick installation), through which a plunger reciprocates to pressurize fluid. A fluid routing plug installed in the horizontal bore directs fluid through first passages leading to an axial blind bore and offset, straight second passages. Suction and discharge valves with tapered sealing surfaces seat against the plug's tapered walls, alternately opening and closing as the plunger reciprocates. Bevels on the plug and housing share operational loads, with a gap accommodating plug expansion. Seals sit in grooves formed in the housing (not the plug) and occupy approximately 97% of groove volume to exclude proppants and prevent erosion; the first seal, exposed to pressure fluctuations, is larger and more robust than the statically loaded second seal. Individual worn components, such as the discharge conduit, stuffing box, or fluid routing plug, can be replaced separately.

Aldwick councillor Jacqui Maconachie died at home on Friday after a battle with cancer, Arun District Council confirmed. Tributes were paid, including from MP Nick Gibb. She served on Arun for 22 years, chaired the council from 2001 to 2002, and leaves husband Dougal.
Admiral Harry Harris, originally nominated as US ambassador to Australia, has been switched to the vacant South Korea ambassador post, at a critical time for US-North Korea negotiations.

A new prospective cohort study published in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology found that more than 99% of people who experienced first-time heart attacks, strokes, or heart failure had at least one of four cardiovascular risk factors: suboptimal blood pressure, cholesterol, or blood glucose, or current or former smoking. More than 93% of the 9.3 million people in two national cohorts followed for 20 years had more than one risk factor, including over 95% of women under 60. Researchers attributed earlier reports of risk-factor-free events to differences between "optimal" and "clinical" thresholds, noting doctors often treat only at higher clinical levels. Experts said treating nonoptimal levels could prevent cardiovascular events, though the U.S. system invests more in treatment than prevention.

MIG allows the A100 Tensor Core GPU to be securely partitioned into up to seven GPU Instances, each with isolated memory paths, ensuring predictable performance, QoS, isolation, and increased utilization—beneficial for multi-tenant Cloud Service Providers.

This patent application relates to applying scheduling offsets for power saving in next-generation (5G NR) wireless networks. It addresses problems arising when a user equipment (UE) enters a power saving state, where hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ) timing parameters (K values), radio resource control (RRC) parameters (time, frequency, and spatial domain), and default beam operations may change, potentially causing incorrect HARQ feedback or transmission via a deactivated antenna panel. The disclosure provides methods whereby a UE receives, from a base station, a power saving signal comprising a minimum applicable K0min indicating a minimum scheduling offset restriction between the PDCCH and PDSCH, determines an application delay based on a predefined value, and applies the restriction after the delay. During the application delay, a different scheduling offset (e.g., RRC-configured) may apply. Implementations describe HARQ feedback for power saving signals, including ACK-only feedback transmitted after a time offset specified in the signal, via RRC signaling, or predefined in specification; inclusion of a feedback bit in the HARQ codebook (positioned as LSB or MSB); dedicated PUCCH resources; and multiplexing with PDSCH feedback. Further implementations address default beam selection in the power saving state, where the UE considers only PUCCH resources or CORESETs whose spatial domain/QCL information is associated with active antenna panels, or uses an SRS resource indicator in DCI format 0_0. Example architectures of base stations and UEs are also described.

Manchester United's Marcus Rashford is reportedly a Real Madrid transfer target, with president Florentino Perez viewing him as a strike partner for Cristiano Ronaldo. Rashford's playing time has been limited since Alexis Sanchez's arrival, though he remains happy at United. Mourinho is also considering a £40m move for Fulham's Ryan Sessengon, though Tottenham are interested.

Ryan Walters' tenure as Oklahoma's state schools chief, beginning in 2023, was marked by culture war actions: removing portraits of respected educators, opening board meetings with Christian prayer, mandating Bibles in classrooms, and purchasing 500 Trump-endorsed Bibles for AP Government courses. Observers describe his administration as a "microcosm" of the Trump administration's education overhaul, noting Education Secretary Linda McMahon has similarly embraced a top-down approach targeting teachers. Walters called Oklahoma a "testing ground for Project 2025" and brought in conservative figures to help rewrite social studies standards. After Trump's re-election, he pushed standards requiring students to identify "discrepancies" in 2020 election results, which the Oklahoma Supreme Court blocked after a lawsuit by parents, teachers, and faith leaders. He also welcomed ICE to round up undocumented students at school, a plan the legislature opposed. Supported by Christian nationalist groups like City Elders but criticized by educators, Walters was jeered at a Turning Point USA event and trailed by 27 percentage points in polling for a potential gubernatorial run. He resigned to lead the Teacher Freedom Alliance, a national anti-union group, citing Charlie Kirk's death as inspiration, and mandated a moment of silence for Kirk plus Turning Point USA clubs in all Oklahoma high schools. Observers question whether he has the national following to succeed.

Andrew & Andrew family solicitors explain the legal process for divorce and civil partnership dissolution. Divorce requires a court order (decree absolute) and legally recognised grounds: adultery, unreasonable behaviour, desertion, two years' separation with mutual consent, or five years' separation. The process begins with a petition, plus a Statement of Arrangements when children are involved. Divorce or dissolution typically takes six months or less, and the firm follows the Resolution Code of Practice.

The Triangle and Two defense is effective against teams with two outstanding scorers, as a change of defense, or when holding the ball late in games. Three defenders form a triangle zone; two chasers deny assigned opponents. The triangle provides backside support against back cuts and dribble penetration. Baseline and middle drives draw double teams. A post/outside variation targets strong inside and outside players. Against a two-guard front, the triangle inverts, shifting like a 2-3 zone. Chasers' denial keeps the ball from top scorers and disrupts set plays.

Hunter Greene, a 17-year-old pitcher and shortstop from Notre Dame High School in Sherman Oaks, California, was selected second overall by the Cincinnati Reds in the 2017 amateur draft. He is viewed as potentially the most significant baseball prospect in years and the most marketable since Bryce Harper was drafted first overall in 2010, with comparable talent, charisma, and star power. As an African American player, Greene arrives as MLB's efforts to grow the game among black Americans reach a crossroads, with fewer than eight percent of big leaguers African-American, down from about 20 percent in the 1980s. He attended MLB's Urban Youth Academy in Compton and, at 13, won an essay contest whose prize was meeting Sharon Robinson, Jackie Robinson's daughter. Commissioner Rob Manfred called his selection "huge for our game." Greene is also a rare two-way prospect, with a fastball clocked at 102 mph and elite power as a hitter, though the Reds drafted him primarily as a pitcher and plan to focus on pitching while allowing at-bats. Expected to sign for a bonus in the high seven figures, he will be developed slowly and is likely years from reaching the major leagues.
Canada's S&P/TSX composite index rose 5.73 points to 15,557.79, helped by financial and materials sectors, while U.S. stocks declined. The Canadian dollar, crude, natural gas, gold, and copper rose.
A startup wants to democratize AI by letting anyone run reinforcement learning, amid growing momentum around open source Chinese models.

The passage presents market commentary noting seasonal weakness over the past 35 years, with diminished liquidity, thin volume, tax-loss selling, and institutional rebalancing ahead of quarter-end. Technical analysis of TLT shows a selloff after an auction, with a rally to the July 6-month calendar range high met by a mean reversion sell signal, though a bullish divergence remains as price holds above the 50-DMA. Yields topped as predicted and may fall further; a dollar below 98 would suggest further declines, viewed as bullish for commodities. Gold is seen positively above 3,350, with new all-time highs possible above 3,450. A weakening dollar, lower yields, and rising gold are generally risk-off signals, and the growth-value divergence continues to widen. The passage also includes headlines on the U.S. government shutdown, gold above $4,000/oz, and website risk disclosures.

Arvell Reese, Ohio State's top linebacker, is emerging as a viable first-round pick and candidate to become just the fifth off-ball linebacker taken in the top 10 over the last decade. Used across the front seven by defensive coordinator Matt Patricia, the 6'3", 243-pound defender excels as a run defender with elite burst, speed, and tackling, and is effective as a quarterback spy. His coverage skills show promise but lack a large sample size, with zone defense representing his biggest uncertainty. He must continue producing against Big Ten competition, add ball production (two passes defended, zero interceptions through Week 5), and prove his strength translates against larger NFL linemen. Described as a Pro Bowl-level talent with a high floor, Reese is projected to start as an outside off-ball linebacker.

The longest woolly rhino horn ever found, discovered in Siberian permafrost along a tributary of Russia's Kolyma River, is about 19,600 years old and 30 centimeters longer than the previous record holder. The horn belonged to a likely female, as the skull was proportionally small for an adult. By counting seasonal growth bands in the horn, researchers determined the rhino lived at least 40 years, making it the oldest woolly rhino yet found. The horn, longer than those of any modern rhino species, may have been used to brush away snow while feeding.

This lecture covers fusion trees, a static data structure by Fredman and Willard (1990) that achieves O(log base w of n) predecessor and successor queries in linear space on a word RAM, with polynomial preprocessing. Fusion trees use a B-tree with branching factor w^(1/5), giving height O(log base w of n), and require constant-time branching decisions at each node. Dynamic versions exist, including exponential search trees (with log log n overhead) and a hashing-based version by Raman achieving matching expected update time.

The core technique is sketching: viewing keys as paths in a binary tree, only the bits at branching nodes (at most k−1 for k keys) are needed to distinguish and order the keys. Since k = w^(1/5), these important bits fit in one word. An approximate sketch is computed by masking the important bits, multiplying by a carefully chosen constant m (chosen so bit positions are distinct and appear in order within O(r^4) space), masking again, and shifting.

Because a query q may diverge from the stored keys, a "de-sketchification" step finds the longest common prefix where q falls off the tree, constructs a corrected query e, and searches with e's sketch to find the true predecessor/successor.

Parallel comparison locates a sketch among all key sketches in constant time by subtracting repeated copies and finding the 0-to-1 transition via multiplication. Finally, the most significant set bit is computed in constant time by splitting the word into √w clusters, identifying non-empty clusters through masking, subtraction, and perfect sketching (possible for uniformly spaced bits), then using parallel comparison against powers of two.

Tesla released a teaser video showing the illuminated outline of a car ahead of a 7 October announcement, sparking speculation about whether it will unveil the long-delayed Roadster or a new mass-market electric vehicle. Reports suggest Tesla has developed a simplified Model Y variant cutting production costs by around 20%. The teaser follows record Q3 deliveries driven by the expiry of the $7,500 U.S. federal EV tax credit, and a lower-priced model could offset an expected sales slowdown. Some investors remain cautious given Tesla's history of delayed launches, including the Cybertruck and Roadster. A confirmed mass-market vehicle would advance CEO Elon Musk's ambition of producing an affordable EV for the global market.

The Supreme Court relisted 17 cases for a second consideration at its upcoming conference, as covered in the Relist Watch column. The cases span diverse subjects, including several characterized as "culture war" cases. Among them: parents challenging a school district's practice of keeping information about children's gender identity from parents, after the 10th Circuit found they failed to adequately plead the conduct was attributable to the district; over 1,000 pseudonymous healthcare workers challenging New York's repealed COVID-19 vaccine mandate, which lacked religious exemptions, after the 2nd Circuit found an undue hardship under Title VII; a minor's suit against Grindr dismissed under Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act; Northern California property owners contesting Humboldt County's administrative cannabis enforcement regime, which deprived them of jury trials; New Orleans Sheriff Susan Hutson seeking termination of a jail-conditions order under the Prison Litigation Reform Act; Flower Foods bread distributors claiming exemption from the Federal Arbitration Act as interstate commerce workers; defendants Hunter and Chaney contesting the enforceability of appeal waivers in plea agreements; a father challenging his daughter testifying behind a screen at his abuse trial under the Confrontation Clause; a Jicarilla Apache member raising public trial and tribal sovereignty questions; a Jan. 6 defendant whose case was affected by a presidential pardon; and a capital defendant alleging race-based juror strikes. Notably, two California cases—FDA regulation of stem cell treatments and the state's unclaimed property practices—were relisted despite respondents waiving responses. Other cases involve qualified immunity for Las Vegas officers, withheld exculpatory evidence in Maryland, the Feres doctrine limiting servicemembers' tort claims, and AEDPA deference standards.

On August 14, 2018, Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC under Item 7.01 (Regulation FD Disclosure), reporting that it published a press release dated August 14, 2018, attached as Exhibit 99.1. The information is furnished rather than filed under the Exchange Act. The report was signed by Todd A. Maron, General Counsel.

This MIT lecture covers life cycle assessment (LCA), a method for quantifying the environmental impacts of products. The class discusses a Dyson-commissioned study comparing hand drying systems (Dyson Airblade, Xlerator, and paper towels), highlighting challenges such as limited data access, assumptions about supply chains, drying times, product lifetimes, and extensive sensitivity analyses. LCA, defined by ISO 14040 standards, involves compiling an inventory of inputs and outputs, evaluating potential environmental impacts, and interpreting results against the study's goals. Originally developed by Coca-Cola in 1969 to compare cans and glass bottles, LCA gained attention during the 1970s energy crisis, but biased "hired gun" studies in the 1980s prompted standardization efforts through SETAC and ISO. The methodology comprises four stages: goal and scope definition (including functional unit, system boundary, cut-off rules, and allocation decisions, as well as the distinction between attributional and consequential studies); inventory analysis (mapping processes and matching bills of materials with third-party databases like ecoinvent, using proxy data where needed); impact analysis (classification and characterization of emissions into categories such as global warming potential, water use, cumulative energy demand, and the more complex IMPACT 2002+); and interpretation (sensitivity analysis, Monte Carlo scenario uncertainty analysis, and bill of activities analysis). Despite uncertainties, the study found the Dyson Airblade generally had the lowest environmental impact, though results depended heavily on assumptions such as drying time and electricity sources.

Sevilla midfielder Pablo Sarabia welcomed his side's Champions League last-16 draw against Manchester United, saying only Manchester City and PSG were teams they wanted to avoid. Second behind Liverpool in their group, Sevilla host United on 21st February before the return leg on 13th March.

A Children's Rights Alliance report examines how homelessness and emergency accommodation affect children's education, as the number of homeless children grows to almost 4,000. Based on research with teachers, school principals, and homeless parents in the greater Dublin area, it describes children attending school hungry, in dirty clothes, and tired after long journeys, leading to frequent absences. Homelessness also affects children's behaviour and mental health. The report calls for free school travel, ring-fenced funding for meals and homework clubs, and housing families near schools, with emergency accommodation limited to six months.

The passage describes a market research report on the Global Angelica Seed Oil Market, covering market status, growth rates, trends, and historical, current, and projected revenues by segment and region. Key manufacturers include Albert Vieille, Berje, Elixens, Ernesto Ventos, Fleurchem, and others. The report analyzes market drivers, constraints, risks, opportunities, PEST and Porter's Five Forces, and macro/microeconomic factors. It segments the market by product type (Therapeutic Grade, Others) and application (Medical, Spa & Relaxation, Others), covering the United States, China, Europe, Japan, Southeast Asia, India, and Rest of World for 2018–2025. It also includes SWOT, investment feasibility, and return analyses, and is published by Index Markets Research.

This study examined malnutrition risk factors and the impact of intermittent preventive therapy (IPTsc) for malaria on the nutritional status of school-age children in Muheza district, North-East Tanzania. Researchers analyzed secondary data from a cross-sectional baseline survey and a three-arm randomized controlled open-label trial in which 1,566 children aged 5–15 years were assigned to dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DP), artesunate-amodiaquine (ASAQ), or standard care, and followed for 20 months. At baseline, malaria prevalence was 27%; 23% of children aged ≤10 years were underweight, 21% were stunted, and 28% were thin or severely thin. Malaria infection was associated with 78% higher odds of stunting (AOR=1.78), and low socioeconomic status with higher odds of underweight (AOR=1.50). A history of malaria in the past month was associated with thinness (AOR=1.37). Changes in weight, height, and BMI over time were not significantly different in the DP and ASAQ groups compared to the control group. The authors conclude that the double burden of malaria and malnutrition is substantial in this setting and recommend that public health agencies reinforce nutritional programs, collaborate with local communities to ensure food availability in schools, and provide sustainable nutritional education alongside malaria control efforts.

The passage describes the NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture and its applications. The NVIDIA Tesla T4, based on the Turing TU104 GPU, is presented as an inferencing solution for hyperscale data centers, enterprise solutions, and edge devices, supporting applications such as image classification, video analytics, natural language processing, and speech recognition. It contains 2,560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores, delivering up to 130 TOPs of INT8 and 260 TOPS of INT4 performance—up to 40X higher inference performance and more than 50X higher energy efficiency than CPU-based inferencing, and twice the energy efficiency of the prior Tesla P4. With 16 GB of memory and 320 GB/sec bandwidth, it nearly doubles the memory capacity and bandwidth of its predecessor.

Key Turing features include an enhanced video engine supporting additional decode formats (HEVC 4:4:4, VP9 10/12-bit), Multi-Process Service for improved inference performance at small batch sizes, and GDDR6 memory—the first GPU architecture to use it—delivering 14 Gbps signaling rates and 20% better power efficiency than GDDR5X. Combined with larger L2 caches and improved compression, Turing achieves 50% higher effective bandwidth than Pascal. The display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K at 60 Hz, HDR with tone mapping, and an enhanced NVENC encoder with HEVC 8K encode at 30 fps. VirtualLink over USB-C consolidates VR headset connectivity into a single connector, and NVLink replaces the SLI bridge in TU102/TU104, providing 25 GB/sec per direction per link.

Turing introduces RT Cores for hardware-accelerated ray tracing, performing BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing to run ray tracing roughly 10 times faster than Pascal, enabling real-time ray tracing. Hybrid rendering combines rasterization and ray tracing. NGX provides AI-based features including DLSS (achieving TAA-comparable quality with roughly half the shading work), InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. Additional features include Mesh Shading (Task and Mesh shaders that eliminate CPU draw call bottlenecks), Variable Rate Shading with per-16x16-pixel-region control, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering supporting up to four views per pass.

The TU104 contains 13.6 billion transistors, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores, and is used in the GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. The TU106 (GeForce RTX 2070) contains 10.8 billion transistors, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but lacks NVLink and SLI support. The document also introduces RTX-OPS, a workload-based metric combining tensor, FP32, RT core, and INT32 operations, and includes an appendix covering ray tracing fundamentals, BVH acceleration structures, denoising, and ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections.

On August 26, 2022, the U.S. government imposed a new license requirement, effective immediately, for future exports to China (including Hong Kong) and Russia of NVIDIA's A100 and forthcoming H100 integrated circuits, as well as systems incorporating them (such as DGX and A100X) and any future NVIDIA chips meeting similar performance thresholds. The requirement addresses risks that covered products may be used in or diverted to military end use or end users in China and Russia. NVIDIA does not sell products to customers in Russia. The requirement may impact timely development of H100, support for existing A100 customers, and may require transitioning certain operations out of China. NVIDIA is seeking exemptions from the USG and engaging Chinese customers to offer alternative products, though there is no assurance licenses will be granted. The company's third-quarter outlook included approximately $400 million in potential China sales that may be subject to the requirement.

Tokyo stocks rebounded sharply Wednesday, with the Nikkei average rising 199.00 points, or 1.03 percent, to 19,437.98 and the Topix gaining 0.95 percent to 1,553.69. The rally was driven by the yen's weakening after Fed Chair Janet Yellen's positive remarks on rate hikes and the Dow's record advance. Export-oriented and financial issues gained, while Dentsu and Toyo Tire surged on strong earnings. Toshiba fell 8.75 percent after projecting a large loss in its U.S. nuclear business.

In the 2016–17 school year, colleges are expected to award over a million bachelor's degrees, many to nontraditional students such as working adults and parents. The Department of Education reported that in 2016, students over 24 accounted for nearly two-fifths of postsecondary enrollment. University of Phoenix president Timothy P. Slottow advises working adults returning to school to: establish a support system; research programs, costs, and institutional resources beforehand; seek credit for prior work, educational, or military experience; and set a plan using flexible options like online or night classes. He stresses that institutions must provide flexibility, structure, and career-relevant programs for these students to succeed.

Construction at Elliott Field and Don Beebe Stadium remains on schedule despite recent rain. Steel beams for the Con Marshall Press Box went up in late March, with roofs, insulation, and masonry added in April and May. June will bring bleachers, field grading, drains, and rock for the turf bed, with the scoreboard expected the third week of June. Field lighting, approved by the Nebraska State College System board in April, will return after being removed in the 1970s, in time for the September 1 opener against Black Hills State University. The expanded construction zone has closed traffic between the NPAC and Chicoine Center lots. The track facility's design phase awaits board approval next month.

This study compared immune responses elicited by two COVID-19 vaccines used in India—Covishield (ChAdOx-1, vectored) and Covaxin (inactivated, TLR7/8-adjuvanted)—in 691 participants aged 18–45 enrolled across four sites in Bengaluru and Pune between June 2021 and January 2022. Participants received two doses of either vaccine per government norms; 506 participants formed the per-protocol population, stratified by baseline serostatus.

In seronegative individuals, seroconversion rates after two doses were 74.4% for Covaxin versus 98.3% for Covishield; in seropositive individuals, 66.9% versus 91.7% (p<0.0001). Covishield produced significantly higher anti-spike antibody geometric mean titers than Covaxin in both serostatus groups at all timepoints. Two doses of Covaxin in seronegative individuals remained 2.2-fold below convalescent-level titers, whereas Covishield exceeded them. In a subset, Covishield elicited significant neutralizing antibodies, while Covaxin did not reach statistical significance.

T cell analysis in the earliest cohort showed both vaccines increased spike-specific CD4 T cells in seronegative individuals, but the fold change was significant only for Covishield; spike-specific CD8 T cells were detected only in the Covishield arm. In seropositive individuals, neither vaccine significantly increased CD4 or CD8 T cell frequencies. Non-responsiveness in seropositive participants was associated with higher pre-vaccination antibody titers.

Cohorts vaccinated or sampled during the Omicron wave showed higher Covaxin seroconversion, and rising nucleocapsid antibodies suggested widespread asymptomatic Omicron infection. Neither vaccine elicited Omicron-specific antibodies in seronegative individuals; in seropositive individuals, a single Covishield dose elicited measurable Omicron-specific responses, but a second dose did not increase them. Covaxin increased activity against wild-type and Delta but not Omicron.

Overall, Covishield elicited stronger and broader responses than Covaxin. Limitations include inability to assess durability due to the Omicron wave, lack of non-neutralizing antibody measurements, and absence of a correlate of protection for Covaxin, precluding inference of efficacy. Findings support heterologous boosting and immunological monitoring in vaccination campaigns.

The Yankee concept is a pro-style "shot" play designed to get over the top of safeties for big plays, using a post-dig combination from opposite sides of the formation to create a high-low read on the safety. It is typically run from heavier sets (multiple running backs or tight ends) to encourage 1-high safety looks. It works well against Cover 1 and Cover 3, where the QB can high-low the free safety with the post and dig routes, but is less effective against 2-high shells like Cover 2 and Cover 4, where the QB should quickly move to underneath routes. The core routes include a crossing tight end, flare route from the tailback, arrow route from the fullback, a 15-yard dig from the X receiver, and a deep post from the Z receiver. The QB's progression is post, dig, crosser, then check-down. Variations include a 2x2 formation with shallow crossers and a version using whip routes underneath to clear throwing lanes.

A hockey player discusses his first Stanley Cup Finals, saying he was overexcited and tried to do too much. He expects the opposing team, frustrated after scoring five goals on the road without winning, to become more physical as the series progresses. He considers both goaltenders strong, noting Leighton had no chance on many goals, and stresses creating traffic in front and moving the injured Boucher side to side. He aims to tire out Pronger and the heavily-used defensemen by controlling the puck, and emphasizes his team's puck possession style while acknowledging they must earn more power plays.

A recent study in Science Advances found that a feedback process that could trigger rapid sea-level rise is already underway in Antarctica. In the Amundsen Sea and Sabrina Coast, rapidly melting glaciers are preventing surface waters from cooling and sinking to form Antarctic bottom water, allowing warm water to pool beneath the ice and melt glaciers from below. This process may have driven a 16-foot sea-level rise at the end of the last glacial period. In a worst-case "pulse" scenario, collapsing glaciers could raise sea levels 10 to 30 feet by 2100—far above current predictions for cities like Miami—and could be accompanied by superstorms. Researchers say stopping global temperature rise is essential.

The speaker, overwhelmed by a recent sad event, feels incompetent for the unexpected duties thrust upon him and declines to announce policy, saying it will emerge through the Administration's acts. He cites his past conduct regarding the rebellion and lifelong advocacy of free government as assurance, and asks for the listeners' support.

Apprenticeships have become a bipartisan workforce development focus, with policymakers seeking to expand beyond construction trades into industries like education, technology, and healthcare. However, traditional construction apprenticeships are highly selective, favoring those with pre-existing skills and advanced coursework, locking out motivated students who need extra help. Pre-apprenticeships—short-term programs offering career exposure, skills building, mentorship, and industry credentials—can prepare participants for these pathways, but they lack funding, limiting capacity and outcomes data collection, perpetuating a cycle of underinvestment. The author proposes financing wraparound supports like transportation and childcare through zero-percent loans repaid only if earnings increase, with unions or employers potentially repaying loans for hired participants, and collecting better data to attract grants and philanthropic investment. Success requires partnership among employers, unions, government, and philanthropy.

Zebronics has launched its Buddy Speaker at Rs. 1699. The lightweight (630g), portable wireless speaker features an LED display, RGB LED light, 5 watts RMS output, built-in FM, and a rechargeable battery offering 3 hours of playback, with Bluetooth, USB, MicroSD, and AUX connectivity.

An AI tool called Waldo scanned over 430,000 past Reddit posts about cannabis use and flagged more than 28,000 as potentially describing unexpected or harmful side effects. Researchers verified 250 flagged posts and confirmed 86 percent represented problematic experiences. Waldo was trained on 10,000 previously hand-reviewed Reddit posts and outperformed ChatGPT, which produced 18 times more false positives, though it did not outperform human reviewers. Researchers say such tools could help public health workers identify harmful products, since agencies like the CDC do not monitor social media. However, it remains unclear whether Waldo would work well for other drugs or products, and future use would need to be done ethically with privacy protections in place.

This paper presents Robodoc, a prototype smart medical chatbot built using openAI's Large Language Model APIs. The author created image-based models with Google's Teachable Machine using transfer learning: an X-ray model detecting viral and bacterial pneumonia, and an OCT model detecting Drusen, Choroidal Neovascularization, and Diabetic Macular Edema. A diabetes detection model was built with TensorFlow.js from numerical data. The chatbot uses openAI's function calling to intelligently select the appropriate model based on user messages or uploaded images, then generates human-friendly responses while keeping technical details hidden from the user. Results showed good integration between models and chatbot with slight deviations, such as misclassifying normal lungs as pneumonia and incorrect urgency tagging. A stub function for scheduling medical appointments based on condition severity was also tested. The author concludes that public APIs enable building complex models without complex research infrastructure and at low cost, positioning chatbots as friendly interfaces for bioinformatics.

Enterprises use various HPC options: 87% prefer external infrastructures like cloud providers, 74% operate or plan their own HPC in colocation datacenters, and 43% use innovation partners such as research institutions, though these are limited for time-sensitive commercial use. Only 6% have on-premises HPC infrastructure; 28% plan adoption within two years.

The passage describes the NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture. Turing includes enhanced Tensor Cores (adding INT8 and INT4 precision modes to the Volta-introduced design, with FP16 fully supported) that accelerate deep learning training and inference, enabling real-time AI features via NVIDIA NGX such as DLSS, AI InPainting, AI Super Rez, and AI Slow-Mo. A TU102 GPU contains 576 Tensor Cores, performing 512 FP16 multiply-accumulate operations per clock per SM, with INT8 operating at double that rate. The Tesla T4, the first Turing-based data center inferencing GPU, contains 2,560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores, delivering up to 130 TOPS of INT8 and 260 TOPS of INT4, up to 40X higher inference performance and more than 50X higher energy efficiency than CPU-based inferencing. Turing also provides an enhanced video engine (HEVC 4:4:4 and VP9 10/12-bit decode, 8K HEVC encode), Multi-Process Service, and double the memory capacity and bandwidth of the Tesla P4.

Turing is the first GPU architecture to use GDDR6 memory (14 Gbps signaling, 20% better power efficiency than GDDR5X), doubles L2 cache to 6 MB in TU102, and improves memory compression, yielding roughly 50% higher effective bandwidth than Pascal. Display features include DisplayPort 1.4a with 8K at 60 Hz, DSC 1.2, HDR tone mapping, and USB-C/VirtualLink support for single-connector VR. TU102 and TU104 use second-generation NVLink for two-way SLI.

Dedicated RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, enabling real-time ray tracing about 10 times faster than Pascal within a hybrid rendering model combining rasterization, ray tracing, and denoising. Additional features include Mesh Shading (Task and Mesh Shaders), Variable Rate Shading (per 16x16-pixel regions, enabling content adaptive, motion adaptive, and foveated shading), Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering (up to four views per pass). The TU104 contains 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores; the TU106 (GeForce RTX 2070) contains 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, without NVLink/SLI. A workload-based RTX-OPS metric is introduced for hybrid rendering. The document concludes with a ray tracing overview and NVIDIA legal and trademark notices.

NASA ambassador Theo Wellington told the Wilson County Commission the upcoming total solar eclipse will be the biggest public one-day event in U.S. history; the last total eclipse visible in Tennessee was in 1869. Half the U.S. population lives within a day's drive of the 70-mile-wide total eclipse path, where populations are expected to double. Wilson County lies near the path's center, with the fairground just 2 seconds off the maximum 2 minutes 40 seconds of viewing. The commission also voted to let qualifying retiring officers keep their service weapons and to fund a school resource officer for Springdale Elementary, opening in August.

The article backtests six swing trading indicators—Williams %R, WilliamsVixFix, Bollinger Bands, Stochastics, the Internal Bar Strength (IBS) indicator, and the Relative Strength Index (RSI)—on the S&P 500 (using SPY as a proxy) to determine which performs best. Conclusions were based on risk-adjusted return (annual geometric return divided by exposure) relative to maximum drawdown, rather than raw returns alone. The recommended time frame for swing trading is 1–15 days. Among the results, the tested RSI strategy performed poorly after 2015, Bollinger Bands showed large drawdowns, and WilliamsVixFix produced about 8.5% annual returns with high and frequent drawdowns. Williams %R was ranked the best indicator, showing the most stable results and the lowest average maximum drawdown, though the top three indicators were considered roughly equal. Mean-reversion indicators were noted to work well on stocks but not on commodities such as gold and oil.

This patent application, a continuation of prior U.S. applications claiming priority to five Korean patent applications filed April 29, 2016, relates to methods and apparatuses for encoding and decoding video signals. The background notes that multimedia data demand is growing faster than channel bandwidth, leading to the establishment of HEVC by VCEG and MPEG, and that inter-prediction accuracy degrades when brightness changes such as fade-in/fade-out reduce correlation between videos.

The invention aims to improve intra-/inter-prediction efficiency, use weights in inter-prediction, improve motion vector precision using adjacent reconstructed information, correct intra-prediction results, effectively encode intra-prediction modes, and perform prediction per sub-block after dividing a current block.

For decoding, the apparatus determines whether a current block is merged with a neighbor block, obtains motion information and a weight prediction parameter accordingly, selects a reference block, and generates a prediction block by applying the weight parameter. If merged, the weight parameter matches the neighbor's; otherwise it is decoded from the bitstream. Motion vector precision may be adjusted upward based on adjacent reconstructed pixels. For intra-prediction, the decoder decodes the intra-prediction mode (via candidate modes based on neighbor usage frequency, or a difference value from a previous block), performs prediction, and optionally corrects prediction samples. Corresponding encoding methods are described, including encoding merge flags, weight parameters or difference values, and correction-related information.

The specification describes a video encoding apparatus comprising dividing, prediction, transform, quantization, rearrangement, entropy encoding, dequantization, inverse-transform, filtering (deblocking, offset correction, ALF), and memory units, and a corresponding decoding apparatus. Blocks may be divided by quad tree or binary tree into square or non-square forms. Inter-prediction uses reference video interpolation, motion information generation (merge or AMVP methods), and motion compensation; intra-prediction uses modes including planar, DC, and directional modes, with AIS filtering.

A weight prediction parameter (multiplication and addition parameters) may be derived via regression analysis (Formula 1) using reconstructed pixels adjacent to the current and reference blocks, converted to an integer by multiplying by 2^N. Alternatively, it may be derived from neighbor pixel trends, from upper or left reconstructed pixel areas, or from a weight prediction parameter set generated by applying offsets. The decoder mirrors these methods or decodes transmitted parameters/difference values.

For intra-prediction correction, the encoder compares costs with and without correction, calculates a standard deviation of the reconstructed pixel area adjacent to the current block, identifies a previously decoded block with a similar standard deviation and the same or similar intra-prediction mode, and derives a correction coefficient (multiplication and/or addition) via regression analysis to correct the prediction block (Formula 2). Candidate blocks may be selected by standard deviation, average value, SAD, or SSD, with related information encoded and decoded accordingly.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2015 reports revenue of $20,379 million, down 12% from $23,201 million in the prior year, primarily due to lower More Personal Computing revenue and a net $1.3 billion revenue deferral related to Windows 10, partially offset by Intelligent Cloud growth. Net income was $4,620 million ($0.57 diluted EPS) versus $4,540 million ($0.54) the prior year, and operating income was $5,793 million. Beginning in fiscal year 2016, Microsoft reports under new segments—Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing—with prior periods recast. Windows 10 license revenue is recognized ratably over the estimated device life of two to four years. The company incurred $780 million in restructuring charges under its Phone Hardware Restructuring Plan, which will eliminate up to 7,800 positions in fiscal 2016. The effective tax rate was 16% versus 23% in the prior year. Microsoft repurchased $4 billion of common stock, with $17.9 billion remaining under its $40 billion repurchase program, and declared a $0.36 per share dividend. Total assets were $172,896 million and stockholders' equity was $77,445 million. Legal matters include a September 29, 2015 agreement dismissing all pending Motorola patent litigation; accrued legal liabilities totaled $551 million in current and $17 million in long-term liabilities, with reasonably possible adverse outcomes of approximately $1.5 billion beyond recorded amounts.

The leu was steady ahead of the Romanian central bank's Wednesday decision on whether to deliver its fourth rate hike this year, with the market split over a possible quarter-point rise to 2.75 percent. Some Central European currencies firmed as investors scaled back selling after China's central bank moved to reverse yuan falls. The forint and zloty have shed about 5 percent this year and the Czech crown about 2 percent amid a dollar-driven emerging market sell-off. In Hungary, the forint rebounded, boosted by speculation the NBH may strengthen its price stability pledge, and the bank discussed inflation trends with analysts.

Organized patriotism, which replaces local pride with national feeling, is essential to a nation's success, and an efficient education system comes next in importance. The federal form of government limits national effectiveness, so technical industrial education must be left primarily to the States, though the National Government should set an example through the District of Columbia schools by promoting commercial and industrial training. Training children solely in literary accomplishments unfits them for industrial work and should be combated; technical education, from mechanic trades to engineering, is vital, and the country should fear educated competitors more than pauper labor. Congress can act directly only under the interstate commerce clause, which should be construed broadly, but can set an example through advanced District legislation on child labor and factory laws. Farmers, whose welfare is as vital as that of wageworkers, need practical technical and scientific training as farming becomes a technical profession requiring intensive cultivation and better business organization.

U.S. stocks rose Monday after the Easter holiday, led by technology companies, as China reported its economy grew 6.9 percent in the first quarter, slightly faster than the previous quarter. The S&P 500 climbed 0.5 percent to 2,341, the Dow rose 0.6 percent to 20,566, and the Nasdaq gained 0.6 percent to 5,840. Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon, and Netflix led gains. Alere surged after accepting a reduced $5.3 billion buyout offer from Abbott Laboratories. Eli Lilly and Incyte fell after the FDA declined to approve their rheumatoid arthritis pill Olumiant. Snyder's-Lance dropped on a weak forecast and its CEO's retirement. Arconic rose after CEO Klaus Kleinfeld agreed to step down. Straight Path Communications climbed on a potential competing buyout offer to AT&T's $1.25 billion deal.

Singapore's Straits Times Index rose 0.9 per cent to 3,308.69, tracking most Asian markets, as weak US inflation data fuelled expectations of a dovish Federal Reserve and US-North Korea tensions eased. Hong Kong, South Korea and China gained while Japan's Nikkei fell nearly one per cent. Last week's losses stemmed from US-North Korea tensions, but assurances from US officials have calmed nerves. Analysts expect continued caution, with geopolitical risks capping rallies and upcoming economic data driving sentiment. Locally, gainers narrowly outnumbered losers, led by OCBC and DBS, while property stocks, Olam International and Asian Pay Television Trust also moved on earnings news.

The article demonstrates how to calculate and backtest a MACD trading strategy using Python. Apple's historical data is downloaded from Yahoo Finance via the yfinance library, with pandas used for data manipulation and matplotlib for plotting. The MACD is calculated as the 12-period EMA minus the 26-period EMA, with a 9-period EMA signal line and a histogram equal to the MACD minus the signal line. A long position is taken when the histogram is non-negative, with returns counted from the day after the signal. The strategy compounded at 15.04% annually versus 19.07% for buy and hold, while being invested only 51.13% of the time.

Two TPS7H500x-SP controllers can operate in primary-secondary mode via the SYNC pin: the primary's SYNC outputs a clock at twice the switching frequency, which serves as the clock input for the secondary controller in external synchronization mode (primary RT populated, secondary RT floating). This mode supports two independent synchronized converters or a single interleaved converter with parallel phases (requiring VSENSE, COMP, SS, and HICC connections). The secondary inverts the received clock, producing a 90° or 270° phase shift.

The paper introduces 3DPCNet, a pose-only, estimator-agnostic module that maps camera-centered 3D human poses into a fixed body-centered canonical frame, addressing viewpoint-dependent variability in monocular kinematic analysis. Its architecture uses a hybrid encoder with parallel graph convolutional (GCN) and Transformer branches fused via gated cross-attention, predicting a continuous 6D global rotation converted to a valid SO(3) matrix via Gram-Schmidt orthonormalization, plus an optional residual correction for joint refinement. The model is trained self-supervised on synthetically rotated poses from the MM-Fi dataset using a composite loss combining pose reconstruction, geodesic rotation, cycle consistency, perceptual, and regularization terms. On MM-Fi, 3DPCNet reduces MPJPE from 63–65 mm to 46–49 mm (~27% reduction) and rotation error from 20–22° to 3–4°, with stable performance across cross-subject (S2) and cross-environment (S3) protocols. On TotalCapture, without fine-tuning, canonicalized poses from off-the-shelf estimators produce wrist trajectories and acceleration signals that more closely match IMU ground truth than a rule-based geometric baseline, including under challenging lateral viewpoints. Noted limitations include non-rigid residual deviations, lack of absolute scale recovery, dependence on input pose quality, and training via pose-space augmentation rather than real multi-view imagery. Future work targets temporal modeling, scale and gravity estimation, and end-to-end clinical validation.

New federal tax law changes to payroll withholding tables will give about 90% of workers extra cash in paychecks starting in February 2018, though amounts vary based on income, children, pay frequency, and W-4 allowances. For example, a married couple with one wage earner making $90,000 and two children under 17 would see about $61 extra per semi-monthly paycheck, while a single person making $35,000 would see about $32 more. The child tax credit doubled to $2,000 per qualifying child, and more higher-income families can claim the full credit. Employers must use the new withholding tables by Feb. 15. Experts recommend reviewing W-4 forms, since outdated information could result in owing taxes in 2019. The standard deduction rises to $24,000 for married couples and $12,000 for singles, meaning many will likely stop itemizing. Home equity loan interest is no longer deductible, and a new $10,000 cap applies to combined state and local tax deductions. The bonus withholding rate drops from 25% to 22%.

Christian Brothers defensive lineman Bill Norton, a four-star 2019 prospect, has committed to Georgia. The 6-foot-6, 270-pound Norton, ranked the nation's 11th-best strong-side defensive end by 247Sports, chose the Bulldogs over offers from schools including Alabama, LSU, and Tennessee.

Roughly 1,000 Liberals attended Del Duca's nomination meeting in Vaughan, where former prime minister Jean Chrétien, speaking a day after the Yonge St. van attack that killed 10 and injured 14, said he was heartened by Torontonians' response. Del Duca urged attendees to reflect and donate blood and, despite polls suggesting Doug Ford could defeat Premier Wynne, asked supporters to work hard. Outside, LiUNA Local 183 members protested budget bill labour changes.

Dick Tuck, a Democratic operative who made a career of political pranks targeting Richard Nixon, died Monday at age 94 in Tucson, Arizona, according to longtime friend Lorraine Glicksman.
