A UC Santa Barbara student in 1950, Tuck first pranked Nixon by arranging a poorly attended campaign event. His stunts included planting fortune cookies reading "Knowland for Premier of Formosa" at a 1958 fundraiser, posing as a fire marshal to give low crowd estimates, hiring a woman to tell Nixon "you'll do better next time" after a 1960 debate, and infiltrating a 1962 Chinatown event with a sign referencing a loan to Nixon's brother. He also worked on Robert F. Kennedy's 1968 campaign and ran unsuccessfully for California's Senate in 1966.

This study presents a bibliometric analysis of research on wartime and online education, focusing on African higher education institutions. The introduction notes that ICT has driven online education growth in African universities since the 1990s, though challenges persist, including weak ICT policies, poor infrastructure, limited internet penetration (47%), faculty lacking digital skills, and an urban-rural digital divide. Africa has experienced extensive conflict, with over three-quarters of African nations facing warfare in the past three decades; wars damage educational infrastructure, displace populations, and hinder ICT deployment in education.

Using the Scopus database, the study screened publications from 2000–2024, narrowing 90 documents on "wartime and online education" to 53 for analysis with Microsoft Excel and VOSviewer. Results show the United States (21 publications) and Ukraine (10) led output, with no African countries represented. Publications peaked at 12 in 2023. Most documents were articles (76.9%), and social sciences dominated subject areas (55%). Keyword analysis identified two clusters: one on learning (e-learning, online teaching) and one on warfare (students, teachers, Ukraine, war).

The discussion highlights a significant research gap on wartime and online learning in Africa. The conclusion calls for urgent research on this intersection, acknowledges the limitation of using only Scopus, and proposes future directions including brain drain, psychological impacts of war, and inclusive online learning.

Defenceman Mathieu Henderson of Brantford capped his four-year Ontario Hockey League career with a breakout final season, recording 10 goals and 44 assists in 68 games with the Flint Firebirds, ninth among OHL defencemen in scoring. His career ended in late March when Flint was eliminated 4-1 by the Sault Ste. Marie Greyhounds in the opening round. After rookie and sophomore seasons in Plymouth, he played through a tumultuous 2015-16 season following the team's relocation to Flint and owner Rolf Nilsen's five-year suspension. He improved his plus/minus to minus-seven and scored Flint's first playoff goal. He later played three games for the ECHL's South Carolina Stingrays and is considering pro hockey or school.

The lecture begins with a review of VCG mechanisms for private value social choice problems. The VCG mechanism implements the utilitarian solution in dominant strategies by having players announce their types, choosing the utilitarian action, and charging each player the negative externality they impose on others. VCG is essentially the only way to achieve dominant strategy implementation, but it is not budget balanced and can be infeasible when the set of social alternatives is very large, as in the FCC spectrum auction example.

The lecture then turns to online markets, focusing on Google, which dominates search with over 90% reported worldwide market share, having overtaken local search engines in country after country (with China as the main exception). Google has roughly $100 billion in revenues and high profit margins, which fund other businesses such as Android, Chrome, and Google Cloud. The Department of Justice sued Google in October 2020 for allegedly monopolizing search, partly citing large payments to Apple to be the default search provider.

Google runs an advertising auction for every search. Advertisers submit standing per-click bids, which are multiplied by quality scores; winners pay the lowest bid that would have kept their position (a generalized second-price auction). Quality weights are essential—without them, pay-per-click auctions attract ads like pornography and ringtones that profit when clicked but are rarely relevant. Yahoo's earlier unweighted first-price auction produced unstable cycling bids.

Edelman, Ostrovsky, and Schwarz model this system as a clock auction. Truth-telling is not an equilibrium and bidders shade their bids, but remarkably the equilibrium reproduces VCG payments. This makes the mechanism an ex post equilibrium, efficient, and immune to price undercutting, since charging less than VCG payments means selecting the wrong ads.

Athey-Ellison endogenize slot values with a consumer search model in which advertisers' qualities are private information. Ordered ads create guided search, and reserve prices can improve welfare by signaling ad quality. With uniformly distributed search costs, consumer surplus and social welfare are maximized at the same reserve price, and producer surplus is three times consumer surplus; any departure from the consumer-optimal reserve price hurts advertisers.

The lecture briefly covers two further papers: Anderson-Renault, which endogenizes firm pricing and finds multiple equilibria, and Armstrong-Zhou, which studies platform information design, showing the consumer-optimal outcome is generally unattainable and that information design mostly transfers surplus between consumers and producers rather than changing social welfare.

The civil aviation ministry has sought a two-month deferral of GST implementation, scheduled for July 1, as airlines need more time to revamp their systems for compliance. Airlines have raised concerns over operational costs and taxation of equipment movement, while the finance ministry says GST remains on track.

This passage is from a patent application describing a data intake and query system, exemplified by the SPLUNK® ENTERPRISE platform, for collecting, indexing, and searching machine-generated data from sources such as servers, sensors, routers, mobile devices, and IoT devices. The disclosed embodiments relate to managing indexed data and, more particularly, to optimizing the size of index files based on storage conditions related to the indexed data.

The system stores machine data as timestamped events and applies a late-binding schema, using extraction rules (e.g., regex rules) to define fields at search time. Key components include forwarders that receive and annotate data, indexers that parse, index, and store events in time-based buckets, and search heads that distribute queries to indexers and combine partial results. The system supports data models for report generation, acceleration techniques (parallel searching across indexers, keyword indexes, high performance analytics stores/summarization tables, and accelerated report generation), security monitoring via the SPLUNK® APP FOR ENTERPRISE SECURITY, data center monitoring via the SPLUNK® APP FOR VMWARE®, and cloud-based deployment. The passage also describes the operating environment, including host devices, client devices, client applications with monitoring components, and networked configurations.

The IRS has announced higher federal income tax brackets and standard deductions for 2026 to adjust for inflation, applying to tax year 2026 for returns filed in 2027. The standard deduction will rise to $32,200 for married couples filing jointly, up from $31,500 in 2025, and $16,100 for single filers. The top rate of 37% will apply to individuals with taxable income above $640,600 and married couples filing jointly earning $768,700 or more. The IRS also adjusted figures for long-term capital gains brackets, estate and gift tax exemption, child tax credit eligibility, and earned income tax credit eligibility. The announcement came a day after the agency said it would furlough nearly half its workforce due to the ongoing government shutdown.

Egyptian archaeologists have unveiled the tomb of Hetpet, an Old Kingdom priestess of the fertility goddess Hathor, on the Giza plateau near Cairo. The Fifth Dynasty tomb features well-preserved, rare wall paintings depicting hunting, fishing, music, dancing, and monkeys. Similar monkey scenes were previously found only in the Saqqara tomb of Ka-Iber. The tomb includes a purification basin engraved with Hetpet's name, and excavations will continue.

This passage is a specification for the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB), defining communication protocols between SEV-ES/SEV-SNP encrypted guests and hypervisors.

The GHCB MSR protocol conveys the GHCB's 4K-aligned guest physical address, maximum and minimum supported GHCB protocol versions, and the SEV page table encryption bit. The hypervisor writes these capabilities before the GHCB address is established; the guest selects a supported version or terminates. Because CPUID causes a #VC exception before the GHCB exists, the hypervisor must supply the encryption bit (obtainable from CPUID Fn8000_001F EBX[5:0]), or the guest may use a CPUID request protocol (which does not support non-zero sub-leafs or function 0x0000_000d). Other MSR protocol functions include AP reset hold, preferred/register/unregister GHCB GPA, page state change, Run VMPL, hypervisor feature support request/response, and termination requests with reason codes.

GHCB GPA registration is required for SEV-SNP guests before first VMGEXIT use. Guests may request a hypervisor-preferred GPA or register their own (making the page hypervisor-owned/shared); registration automatically unregisters any prior GPA, and the hypervisor must terminate a guest supplying a non-matching GPA.

Negotiation examples show the hypervisor setting VMCB offset 0x00a0 before vCPU launch, the guest handling #VC exceptions to obtain protocol versions and the encryption bit, configuring page tables, allocating a shared GHCB page, and writing MSR 0xc001_0130 with the GHCB GPA before any VMGEXIT. SEV-SNP guests additionally verify SEV-SNP status via a non-interceptable MSR and perform Register GHCB GPA.

When a Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) occurs, hardware raises #VC with the VMEXIT code as the error code. The guest copies required state to the GHCB, sets corresponding VALID_BITMAP bits, and invokes VMGEXIT; the hypervisor signals errors via SW_EXITINFO1/SW_EXITINFO2. Supported NAE events include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO access (using the shared buffer at offset 0x800), Page State Change (private/shared/PSMASH/UNSMASH operations, up to 253 entries per request), SNP Guest Request (firmware requests via request/response pages with sequence numbers), SNP Extended Guest Request (adds certificate data pages), AP Creation (create/destroy/update VMSA pages at specified VMPL levels), #HV doorbell page management, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer (emulated APIC timer), APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Request (trusted device I/O with measurements, certificates, and TDISP attestation), Secure AVIC backing page register/unregister, and Termination Request.

Guests identify SEV-ES support via hypervisor-provided CPUID properties (hypervisor bit, SEV support bit, encryption bit position). AP booting is complicated because vCPU registers are measured and encrypted before launch; the AP Reset Hold protocol and AP jump tables (4K-aligned, encrypted) enable AP startup and control transfer between environments such as UEFI and OS. The SEV-SNP AP Creation NAE event enables vCPU hotplug.

For NMIs, the hypervisor must not intercept IRET but must intercept #DB, using the guest's "NMI Complete" message to gate further NMI injection. Hardware debug register virtualization is supported when available; otherwise DR7 accesses are intercepted and cached. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

The #HV doorbell page (a shared, host-owned page) contains a PendingEvent field (NoFurtherSignal bit, #MC and NMI bits, and an 8-bit interrupt vector) and a NoEoiRequired byte for EOI optimization. The host presents the highest-priority ready interrupt by writing the vector and may signal #HV; the guest acknowledges interrupts via atomic exchange and performs EOIs either by atomically clearing NoEoiRequired or via VMGEXIT to the X2APIC EOI MSR. Guests must execute HLT with interrupts disabled and validate vectors against a potentially non-cooperative host.

SOS full court pressure forces offenses to react to backcourt pressure, can adjust game tempo, and wears opponents down through fatigue-induced errors. Primary "shadow" presses (Back, Up, Face) feature a second defender shadowing the on-ball defender, differing only in initial alignments. Secondary "Blitz" pressures are the most aggressive, denying first passing lanes with deep backcourt traps. Purposes include creating turnovers, disrupting tempo, and removing the ball from the playmaker. Effectiveness depends on executing SOS fundamentals; pressure is abandoned if the shadow player is out of position or a deep or middle outlet pass occurs.

Appliance maker Amber Enterprises has received Sebi's approval to raise Rs 555 crore through an IPO, comprising a Rs 450 crore fresh issue and a Rs 105 crore share sale by promoters Jasbir Singh and Daljit Singh.

This study examined perineuronal nets (PNNs)—extracellular matrix structures that envelop inhibitory neurons and stabilize synapses—in the hippocampus of subjects with substance use disorder (SUD). Using postmortem human hippocampal samples from subjects with SUD (n=20), SUD with comorbid major depressive disorder (MDD; n=24), MDD alone (n=20), and psychiatrically normal controls (n=20), plus hippocampal samples from rhesus macaques with or without chronic alcohol self-administration, the authors quantified PNN densities using Wisteria floribunda agglutinin (WFA) labeling and measured gene expression via qPCR.

Subjects with SUD showed significantly increased PNN densities in several hippocampal regions (including CA1 stratum oriens, CA2, CA3, and CA4), along with increased parvalbumin (Pvb) and Vamp2 expression and decreased expression of the ECM proteolytic genes Mmp9 and Ctss. Subjects with MDD generally showed opposite findings, including decreased PNN densities in CA1, while subjects with comorbid SUD/MDD displayed mixed or absent differences, indicating that comorbid MDD can mask or amplify SUD-related changes. Increased WFA-labeled glial cells were observed in SUD subjects and in alcohol-exposed monkeys.

Rhesus monkeys with chronic alcohol self-administration also showed increased hippocampal PNN densities, providing causal support for the human findings. The authors conclude this is the first evidence of increased hippocampal PNNs in human SUD, suggesting PNNs may stabilize contextual reward memories and represent potential therapeutic targets for cue-induced relapse.

The UK and Ukraine discussed future trade links after the UK leaves the EU, welcomed efforts to ensure continuity of the EU-Ukraine DCFTA (over £1.7 billion in trade) with no disruption during the Implementation Period, and agreed to strengthen trade.

This patent application describes systems and methods for localizing and classifying abnormalities, such as lesions, bleeding, or fractions, in medical images. In one embodiment, a multi-task network comprising a jointly trained localization network and classification network localizes lesions in an input medical image using a localization map (e.g., a pixelwise heat map) and classifies the lesion (e.g., as malignant or benign) through a multi-phase training procedure. A multi-modality fusion network variant processes multi-parametric MRI (mpMRI) images by generating localization maps from separate localization networks for each modality and combining them. A regression network variant additionally scores lesions, such as PI-RADS scores for prostate lesions, and a patch-based approach using a deep neural network may also be applied for scoring. In another embodiment, an abnormality is detected by deleting portions of an input medical image to generate incomplete images, synthesizing replacement portions using a trained generative adversarial network (GAN), selecting a normal image depicting the healthiest tissue, and detecting the abnormality by comparing the input image with the normal image to produce a localization map. A further embodiment addresses training deep learning models on multi-site datasets in two stages: a training stage, in which a pretrained model is iteratively updated with sub-datasets reordered by similarity to a source dataset, and a deployment stage, in which the model is refined using an annotated deployment dataset reordered by sample uncertainty. The application also describes computer-based implementations of these methods.

The speaker saw little difference from the Anaheim game, saying the team failed to play their game while the opponent executed their plan and capitalized on a power play. A disputed goal was ruled no goal; the team must move on.

Trump tweeted that the Russia investigation had devastated "young and beautiful lives," though most affected were his inner circle and former campaign aides, and most departures stemmed from infighting rather than the probe. His weekend focus on the investigation, which he believes delegitimizes his presidency, showed his continued obsession; chief of staff John Kelly said Trump is "somewhat embarrassed" by the investigations. Lawyer Rudy Giuliani declined to say whether Trump would be interviewed by special counsel Robert Mueller, saying he was comfortable with collusion questions but not obstruction, a matter of interpretation. Trump called Mueller's team "13 Angry Democrats," though Mueller is a Republican, and repeated claims that FBI informants spied on his campaign, which Sen. Marco Rubio disputed. Trump also falsely claimed a New York Times source "doesn't exist"; the source was a real senior official.

A University of Virginia thoracic surgery recovery program reduced morphine equivalent use by 74 percent and 59 percent in two patient groups without compromising pain evaluations, cut thoracotomy patients' median hospital stay by two days, and saved over $1.3 million while freeing beds for an estimated 28 additional patients. The Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) program, launched in early 2016, enrolled 139 patients in its first year and was compared with more than 220 previous non-enrolled patients. Benefits occurred without increased surgical complications or readmissions. Despite limitations, including limited cost detail, researchers deemed the program a success and plan continued monitoring of outcomes and outpatient opioid use. The findings were published in the Annals of Thoracic Surgery.

Two militants of the outlawed Lashkar-e-Jhangvi, Shaikh Muhammad Mumtaz and Muhammad Ahmed Khan alias Muna, escaped from Karachi's Central Jail late Tuesday night. At least a dozen prison officials, including Superintendent Ghulam Murtaza Shaikh, were suspended, and a case was sought against them for negligence. IG Prisons Nusrat Mangan said the escape occurred from the newly formed ATCs complex on the prison's outer perimeter; a committee has been formed to investigate and police teams dispatched to nab the suspects. Separately, a robber was killed and a citizen, Imtiaz, injured in a police encounter in DHA, while police arrested at least 15 outlaws in citywide raids.
The speaker treats the upcoming Stanley Cup game like any other, acknowledging past playoff losses but focusing on preparing to win rather than dwelling on setbacks.

USD/JPY dropped 2.25% on Friday after a weak US jobs report, downward revisions of 258k, and the firing of the BLS chief, with Fed rate-cut odds rising to 88% following board member Adriana Kugler's resignation. A rebound from the 147.13 Fibonacci level and a move above the 147.80 EMAs could revive upside; a break below the 146.45 50-day EMA may extend losses toward 144.00–144.40. GBP/USD awaits Thursday's BoE decision, where markets expect a 25bp cut to 4.0% despite inflation near double the 2% target and unemployment at a three-year high of 4.7%. Recovery requires breaking above 1.3360; a fall below 1.3135 support could target 1.3000. BTC/USD fell with equities, finding support near the 112,000 50-day SMA. A break above 117,260 would signal bullish continuation; failure to hold 110,750 could open downside toward 105,770–107,500.

A Joseph Rowntree Foundation study finds UK families need £40,000 annually for a decent standard of living: each parent in a couple with two children needs £20,000 (up from £13,900 in 2008), and single people need £18,400 (up from £13,400). The author argues redistribution cannot work since only 30% of households earn above £40,000, proposing instead a higher tax-free personal allowance, separate taxation of couples, relaxed childcare and housebuilding regulation, and greater economic growth.

French President Emmanuel Macron's maiden visit to Nigeria dominates the front pages. His first formal meeting with President Buhari covered security, including the G-5 Sahel force against Al-Qaeda in the Maghreb and intelligence sharing to fight Boko Haram, plus a MoU for a reforestation and agricultural project creating about 150,000 jobs in Ogun State. Macron said tackling Fulani herdsmen violence is Nigeria's responsibility. Times Live reports child trafficking in Gabon, where rescued children are housed in a state-run transit center.

Culpeper defeated host Courtland 2-1 in a nondistrict baseball game Monday, with routine defensive plays proving decisive. Courtland committed seven errors, five in the final two innings. Trailing 1-0 in the sixth, Culpeper tied the game after a misplayed popup, then scored the winning run in the seventh on another error. Both pitchers excelled: Courtland's Alex Kobersteen struck out nine in a complete game, allowing two hits and no walks, while Culpeper's Jake Dudley matched those numbers with three walks. Courtland's lone run came when Addie Burrow doubled and later stole home.

The Department of Education will delay two Obama-era rules—one requiring for-profit colleges to prove "gainful employment" and another clarifying loan forgiveness for defrauded borrowers—that were set to take effect July 1, instead creating committees to review them. The department will honor forgiveness for 16,000 borrowers with pending claims. A for-profit college association has sued to block the rules, while Democratic attorneys general and senators support them. Hearings are set for July.

This is the November 30, 2000 issue of the VentureWire newsletter, sent to Jeff Dasovic at Enron. Top stories include 724 Solutions' agreement to acquire Tantau Software for approximately $375 million in stock; El Dorado Ventures' formation of a $250 million fund focused on early-stage IT investments in the western U.S.; children's website MaMaMedia's layoffs leaving it with 15 employees; and iVMG's appointment of former Prodigy CEO Samer Salameh as its first president and CEO. The newsletter lists numerous funding rounds, including Medschool.com ($26 million), E2O Communications ($38.5 million), Tapestria ($25 million from Hunter Douglas for a 20% stake), Whereoware ($21 million), DemandTec ($16 million), Clarendon Photonics ($16 million), Vectiv ($13 million), IDe ($12 million), Parachute ($10 million), Firstdoor ($9 million), RealTimeImage ($9 million), Latinia ($5 million), INEA ($3 million), Spintopia ($2.85 million), and ProcureZone.com ($3 million from Mitsui). It also reports that 20 corporate investors will take a combined 5% stake in the Ariba-Softbank joint venture Nihon Ariba KK. In M&A news, Blackboard agreed to acquire AT&T Campuswide Access Solutions and CEI SpecialTeams from iCollege. VC fund news covers Hyperion Partners closing $73 million of a $100 million fund and Crosspoint Venture Partners delaying its $1 billion ninth fund. The issue also includes new product launches, board appointments, executive hires, VC personnel moves, an amplification for Cerida, and a correction regarding Three Arch Capital Partners.

Etisalat Nigeria has yet to agree with 13 Nigerian banks on restructuring a $1.2 billion loan after missing a payment. Regulators and banks agreed in March to pursue a default deal over receivership, and Etisalat may consider selling its Nigerian stake.

The offensive goal kick in soccer aims to retain possession and create an attack. Under Law 16, a goal kick is taken from the Goal Area when the ball crosses the defenders' end line last touched by an attacker; the ball must be stationary, opponents must be outside the Penalty Area, and the ball is live once kicked and visibly moves. Younger players typically have the strongest kicker take it, while adults usually use the goalkeeper. For players 10 and under, build-out (retreat) lines prevent defenders from challenging until the kicking team's defenders retreat past the line, and local rules often require building up from the back rather than kicking long. Simple approaches include kicking to a nearby dribbler or to a target receiver who advances up the sideline, with a secondary receiver as an option. Key concepts include keeping the ball wide and upfield and never sending it across one's own goal; the kicker must ensure proper positioning, and a player should be placed in front of the goal to defend. For players 11 and above, kicks go to covered or uncovered targets (Target #1, #2, or a midfielder as #3), with coaches adding passive and active defenders and teaching targets to move forcefully to the ball. Adults may use short kicks, deep targets, or kicks to designated spots, with the goalkeeper usually taking the kick. A goal kick is a direct restart, meaning a goal can be scored directly, and wind can produce unusual outcomes.

This prospective, descriptive cross-sectional study examined 165 scorpion sting patients admitted to Tesseney Community Hospital in Eritrea's Gash-Barka region from June 2019 to May 2020. Cases were nearly evenly distributed by sex (48.5% male, 51.5% female), with 61.2% aged over 15 years. Most stings occurred at night (62.4%), indoors (56.4%), and on the foot (64.8%); black scorpions were most commonly identified (38.8%). Incidence peaked in summer (93%), particularly September and October. The most frequent clinical manifestations were localized pain (70.3%), sweating (56.4%), and vomiting (33.9%). Using Abroug's classification, 43.6% of cases were class III, 35.8% class II, and 20.6% class I. Eight patients died, yielding a case fatality rate of 4.8%, largely associated with class III stings. Children under 15 and patients without formal education showed possible predisposition to symptom severity. Treatment included local anesthesia, oral analgesics, diazepam, and, for class II-III cases, nifedipine and/or scorpion antivenom (15.2%), as prazosin was unavailable. The unusually high proportion of class III cases was attributed to delayed care-seeking among adults. The authors recommend preventive education programs, protective measures, equipping facilities with essential drugs, and further studies on scorpion habitats and care-seeking behavior.

The random walk theory holds that stock prices move unpredictably, making historical prices useless for forecasting future movements. Popularized by Burton Malkiel's 1973 book *A Random Walk Down Wall Street* and originally coined by mathematician Louise Bachelier, the theory assumes a 50% probability of prices rising or falling. A random walk trading strategy relies on random entries and exits, with diversification—across multiple stocks or a broad market index fund—as its key rule. The theory relates to the efficient market hypothesis (EMH), which states that asset prices reflect all available information; despite differing assumptions, both conclude that consistently beating the market is nearly impossible and favor passive investing. In a 1988 Wall Street Journal Dartboard Contest, experts beat the DJIA in only 76 of 140 contests. Backtests showed a random strategy on SPY produced positive results (0.37% average gain, 1.7 profit factor, 13% max drawdown), while GLD results were negative.

This report traces the consistent U.S. policy against foreign aggression in Hawaii and repeated contemplation of annexation. In 1850 Lord Palmerston suggested a U.S. protectorate or annexation; in 1851 a contingent deed of cession was signed by the king; in 1854 a treaty draft under Mr. Marcy failed after the king's death. Mr. Seward (1867), Presidents Johnson (1868) and Grant (1871), and Mr. Fish (1873) each favored or encouraged annexation. After the 1875 reciprocity treaty, administrations defended U.S. commercial rights and supported the Hawaiian Government, with Mr. Blaine (1881) affirming benevolent neutrality or an American solution if needed. The report, submitted February 15, 1893, also notes John C. Jones's 1820 appointment as U.S. agent for commerce and seamen at the Sandwich Islands.

Official mpg figures, based on the outdated NEDC test, are unreliable due to loopholes such as no sustained motorway driving, use of eco modes, disabled ancillary loads, speed tolerances, removable parts, inflated tyre pressures, lack of lab oversight, and an arbitrary 4% reduction. Which? research found the annual fuel cost difference between the most and least efficient medium-sized hatchbacks exceeds £800. From September 2017, the tougher WLTP test replaces the NEDC, applying to all new UK cars by September 2018. Which? tests cars using the WLTP cycle in a lab, including cold, hot, and motorway cycles, under realistic conditions without altering results. Hybrids are tested according to battery charge rules. Which? also measures air pollution, uses PEMS road testing to detect cheating, and has reviewed over 700 vehicles, testing around 120 new cars annually.

Anthurium, a South American plant with red, pink, or white flowers, naturally filters ammonia and xylene but may cause allergies. It needs indirect light, dampness, temperatures of 18–21°C, winter misting, and annual repotting.

This study examines how college teaching modalities—in-person, hybrid, and online—affected COVID-19 spread in surrounding communities. Using a quasi-experimental approach that matches similar colleges with different teaching modes, the authors find that reopening, especially in-person instruction, increased COVID-19 cases and deaths over time. Unlike earlier work focused mainly on K-12 schools, the study addresses the endogeneity of modality choice, since colleges often selected formats based on pre-existing local COVID rates. Identification relies on colleges reopening on different dates, cellphone mobility data, and re-weighting methods that account for multidimensional differences among colleges. Outcomes—new county-level cases and deaths—are measured at the county level because students may spread the virus to vulnerable community members. The authors note the findings may inform responses to future crises, such as new COVID-19 variants.

The passage presents a hierarchical Bayesian multinomial modeling approach that pools viral genomic sequence data across countries to estimate variant growth rates, prevalence, and fitness advantages. The authors note that SARS-CoV-2 genomic data are highly concentrated, with 90% of publicly available sequences coming from 10% of countries and the US and UK contributing 54.9% of GISAID sequences as of July 1, 2022, making standard country-specific regression methods unreliable where sequencing is sparse. The model uses two hierarchical levels—country-specific fitness advantages drawn from each variant's global fitness distribution, and variant fitness advantages drawn from a shared normal distribution—causing extreme estimates to shrink toward the mean and enabling robust estimates from sparse data. Applied to SARS-CoV-2, the model estimated that BA.5 had a higher global weekly fitness advantage relative to BA.2 (0.94) than BA.4 (0.67) and BA.2.12.1 (0.45), while BA.1 was less fit than BA.2; country-specific fitness advantages were heterogeneous, generally higher in the US and UK than in India and South Africa. Retrospective validation of BA.5's emergence in Portugal showed the multicountry model produced lower Brier scores and more stable fitness estimates than a single-country model, and could estimate fitness before a variant was observed in a country. The authors state the framework applies to other pathogens and geographic scales, complements sequencing capacity investments, and is particularly relevant for countries with limited sequencing capacity; a live dashboard for real-time variant fitness estimation was also developed.

This paper studies Gorenstein-projective modules over the ring Z[ε] of dual integers, since classifying all modules over this ring is infeasible. The category G-proj Z[ε] is equivalent to several categories, including torsionless Z[ε]-modules, perfect differential structures of abelian groups, and orbits of bounded complexes of free abelian groups, but lacks the Krull-Remak-Schmidt property. The main result establishes equivalences among five categories: the stable category of Gorenstein-projective Z[ε]-modules, the stable category of submodules of free Z[ε]-modules, the orbit category Db(Z)/[1], and two categories of perfect differential structures; this also holds over any principal ideal domain. These categories form a chain linked by dense functors (modulo the shift, projectives, and stalk objects), which compose order-independently, yielding a cube with commutative faces.

This IDC white paper examines the role of IT-based simulation, modeling, and data analysis in industrial development and manufacturing. More than half of surveyed decision makers use simulation, modeling, and virtual prototyping, while 42% use high-performance data analytics. Digital twins are identified as a key trend, enabling problem detection, scenario simulation, and new business models such as "Product as a Service." Demand for high-performance calculations is expected to rise sharply, with 81% of decision makers viewing high-performance computing (HPC) as a game changer for product and process innovation. Most enterprises prefer external HPC infrastructures (87%) or colocation datacenters (74%), while only 6% operate on-premises HPC. Key challenges include security (72%), energy consumption and sustainability (58%), inadequate computing power, infrastructure availability, and lack of expertise (42%). Cloud-based architectures, particularly the public cloud and HPCaaS, are expected to dominate, offering scalability, cost flexibility, access to modern technologies, and support for new HPC-based business models, which 81% of current HPC users intend to implement. IDC recommends establishing virtual development, a holistic data strategy, careful selection of HPC operating models, attention to scalability, security, and energy efficiency, and leveraging external expertise. Findings are based on a December 2021 survey of 200 decision makers at industrial enterprises in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis have won the 2025 Nobel Prize in physics for demonstrating quantum tunneling and energy quantization in an electric circuit in the 1980s. Their experiments involved billions of electrons on a chip small enough to hold, contrary to expectations that quantum effects are limited to individual atoms. Using a Josephson junction—a superconductor sandwiching an insulator—they observed, at very cold temperatures, tunneling between zero-voltage and voltage states, as well as energy-level quantization. Such circuits are now used as qubits in quantum computers. The three share the 11 million Swedish kronor (over $1.1 million) prize.

This email compiles news articles from October 30, 2001, concerning Enron Corp. Enron shares fell as much as 20 percent to their lowest levels since January 1993 after Moody's lowered the company's long-term debt rating to Baa2, two notches above junk status, and placed its commercial paper rating on review for downgrade. Bond default insurance premiums doubled amid credit concerns. Enron confirmed it was seeking new credit lines after tapping its $3.3 billion facilities, having lost roughly $15 billion in market capitalization in two weeks. The Securities and Exchange Commission was investigating dealings with partnerships run by former CFO Andrew Fastow, who was ousted. A Dow Jones interview featured new CFO Jeff McMahon discussing Enron Industrial Markets' forest products trading, with newsprint volumes growing from under 5,000 metric tons in January to 60,000 tons in July and a goal of becoming one of North America's largest newsprint marketers; the unit would continue without capital pullback. Executives from AEP, Exelon, and Northeast Utilities said they continued trading with Enron while monitoring exposure. NYMEX's president discussed Enron's role in natural gas trading and a new over-the-counter clearing service. A commentary by James Cramer argued Enron's bottom depended on when Janus funds finished selling. Separately, Germany's cartel office threatened legal action against four utilities over balancing energy charges, noting new entrants like Enron Capital & Resources were disadvantaged.

This passage from the TPS7H500x-SP datasheet (SLVSF07F, revised August 2024) covers design guidance and supporting information. An 80-V GaN FET was conservatively selected for the synchronous rectifier, with an optional parallel Schottky diode to reduce losses. An RCD clamp limits switch-node voltage. The output inductor is 0.47 μH with a 40% ripple current target. Output capacitance calculations require at least 1.3 mF; approximately 2.3 mF (seven 330-μF polymer tantalum capacitors) was used, with additional capacitance recommended for single-event transient mitigation in space-grade designs. An optional LC output filter can further reduce ripple. Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins at roughly 35 A output, using a 1:100 current sense transformer and a 7.5-Ω sense resistor. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF. Type 2A frequency compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover, with RCOMP, CCOMP, and CHF values of 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF. A 102-kΩ slope compensation resistor is used. The controllers operate from a 4-V to 14-V supply with at least 0.1-µF input bypass capacitance. Layout guidelines address noise reduction, ground separation, trace widths, and component placement, with example layouts for CFP and TSSOP packages. The passage also lists related documentation, revision history, mechanical and packaging information, and legal disclaimers.

The passage enumerates Allied assets. Postwar economic exclusion threatens Austria-Hungary as seriously as Germany. In Bulgaria, the chief asset is satisfying her just claims, now that the threat of Russian occupation of Constantinople is removed. Regarding Turkey, assets include military successes with religio-political effects and Turkey's postwar financial weakness. Outside Europe, German colonies and Germany's exclusion from the Pacific and the Americas offer bargaining material. The Russian revolution endangers German domination through anti-capitalist feeling, religious antagonism to Protestant Germany, and Moderate nationalism, acting as a dissolving force by example. The Vatican, though pro-German in neutrality, requires skilful handling and could aid the Allied cause. American man-power and resources make crushing victory over the Central Powers certain. Intangibles include the longing for peace, distrust of the old diplomacy, hope for a league of nations, and fear of social revolution. German policy's direction has shifted from south through Italy, to southeast, and now eastward, where Germany may accept sacrifices elsewhere to secure Russian opportunities.

The SLASFA2A datasheet (revised April 2025) for TI's MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 microcontrollers describes the devices' peripherals and support information. The clock module supplies internal and external oscillators (LFOSC, SYSOSC, LFXT/HFXT, SYSPLL) and distributes clocks including MCLK, CPUCLK, ULPCLK, and LFCLK. The document also covers the SWD debug interface, bootstrap loader, factory constants, application schematic recommendations (decoupling capacitors, NRST pullup, ROSC resistor, VCORE tank capacitor), development tools, device nomenclature, a revision history of April 2025 specification updates, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

The Open Source Definition (OSD), published twenty years ago, marked the emergence of open source. The Open Source Initiative dates its inception to February 3, 1998, when Christine Peterson proposed the term at a meeting following Netscape's decision to release its source code. "Open source" was chosen over "free software" because the latter required clarification that "free" meant liberty, not price. Bruce Perens, who drafted the Debian Free Software Guidelines that became the OSD, cites February 9, 1998. Open source proved more commercially palatable than the free software movement, and major technology companies, including Microsoft, now depend on it. Red Hat's Tim Burke says open source has shifted from cloning proprietary software to leading innovation.

Storage, particularly batteries, is promoted as a way to integrate more renewable energy into electricity grids and reduce fossil fuel reliance. Storage systems incur capital and running costs, and are only economically sensible if savings exceed these. Different technologies suit different roles: lithium ion batteries work well at small scale but are expensive; pumped hydro is cheap and suited to large-scale grid management; flywheels aid frequency stability; other options include compressed air, liquid air, flow batteries and hydrogen. Lithium ion costs have halved to US$600 per kWh in five years. For a home with rooftop solar and variable tariffs, a 7kWh battery must cost under A$7,000 (about A$1,000/kWh) to break even; current costs of A$1,000–3,000/kWh put batteries on the cusp of cost-effectiveness. However, retail rates exaggerate peak/off-peak differences, and if retailers flatten tariffs, batteries would need to cost around A$300/kWh. Reduced peak demand only saves network costs if demand is growing, but overall demand has declined since 2009. Pumped hydro, at about A$100/kWh with 1,500 MW already installed, is cheaper, though consumer behaviour may still favour distributed batteries.

An Irish Times "Portrait Gallery" photograph shows Ernest Walton, joint winner of the 1951 Nobel Prize for physics, working in a lab at Trinity College Dublin. Described as quiet and shy, Walton declined to leave Ireland despite his achievement of smashing the atom's nucleus at Cambridge's Cavendish Lab in the 1930s. Jack McManus's photograph gives the machine equal visual status with the scientist.

Bernstorff reports that the blockade will be terminated if a conference can be arranged on reasonable terms. Gerard relays that Zimmermann gave him Germany's submarine note, memorandum, and maps, stating Bernstorff was instructed to present Germany's terms to the President confidentially and urge peace, and that Germany hoped the President would remain quiet for two months while submarine war compelled England to seek terms; Zimmermann also hoped Gerard would work for peace. Droppers reports the Entente permitted indispensable victuals into Greece pending the blockade's raising. Reported German peace terms included giving up Belgium while retaining guaranties, a slice of France, partial return of Serbia, and indemnities paid to Germany. Austria-Hungary's Foreign Minister, via Penfield, states it wages a defensive war and seeks peace without victory, but cannot negotiate while the Entente aims at dismembering Austria-Hungary; submarine warfare cannot be modified since deployed submarines cannot be recalled, and Wilson is asked to persuade the Entente to accept this basis.

The Korean diet (K-diet) is based on traditional Korean eating habits, emphasising whole, unprocessed foods such as vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, and fermented foods like kimchi, along with smaller portions and multiple side dishes. It is low in sugars and unhealthy fats. Recommended foods include rice, barley, seasonal vegetables, fermented soy products, and seasonings like sesame oil and soy sauce, often accompanied by broth-based dishes. Processed foods, sugary drinks, unhealthy fats, and dairy should be limited. Benefits include high fibre, low calories and saturated fats, gut health from fermented foods, and antioxidants, potentially aiding weight loss alongside regular physical activity. Drawbacks include high sodium, low calcium due to limited dairy, spicy ingredients that may irritate digestion, and high carbohydrates requiring portion control. Adjustments can accommodate vegan, low-carb, and gluten-free diets.

The ADS9803 supports a speed-boost mode that converts a user-selected analog input channel pair at up to 8MSPS while the remaining six channels are idle; the sampling rate equals the sampling clock frequency and data output interface specifications remain unchanged. Configuration registers are 16-bit, grouped into three banks addressable by an 8-bit address, with bank 0 always accessible. Register writes are enabled with SPI_RD_EN = 0b; reads require SPI_RD_EN = 1b and SPI_MODE = 1b and use two 24-bit SPI frames. Multiple devices can be connected in a daisy-chain topology where CS and SCLK are shared; the DAISY_CHAIN_LEN register sets the number of ADCs excluding the first, and register writes require N × 24 SCLKs. The document also describes register fields for test patterns, gain error correction, averaging, common-mode range, output lanes, and speed-boost configuration. In applications, the ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system with a built-in analog front-end for ATE use, achieving 0.0015% TUE at 25°C ±5°C post-calibration, with low-noise (up to 22.7kHz) and wide-bandwidth (up to 700kHz) modes; wide-bandwidth mode settles to 99.95% FS in 7.5µs. The device uses three power supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, IOVDD) with no required power-up sequence, and layout guidance recommends close decoupling and keeping analog signals away from noise sources.

Nike posted quarterly earnings and revenue that beat Wall Street expectations, with fiscal first-quarter revenue rising 1% to $11.72 billion after the company had previously projected a mid-single digit sales decline. Net income fell 31% to $727 million, or 49 cents per share, while gross margin dropped 3.2 percentage points to 42.2%, reflecting ongoing efforts to clear old inventory through discounting and less profitable channels. Wholesale revenue rose 7% to $6.8 billion and North America sales climbed 4% to $5.02 billion, though Nike direct sales fell 4% and China revenue declined 9%. CEO Elliott Hill, who took over nearly a year ago to lead the turnaround, said progress will not be linear, and the company is restructuring teams by sport, including the recent launch of NikeSKIMS with Kim Kardashian's brand.

This retrospective study of 109 patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) treated at Kaohsiung Veterans General Hospital between January 2013 and October 2021 aimed to develop a predictive model for shunt-dependent hydrocephalus (SDHC). From 118 consecutive patients who underwent aneurysm obliteration, eight in-hospital deaths and one patient with incomplete data were excluded. Multivariate logistic regression identified three independent risk factors for SDHC: age ≥65 years (OR 3.94), surgical clipping versus endovascular coiling (OR 4.36), and Hunt and Hess scale ≥3 (OR 3.59). A nomogram based on these factors showed an area under the curve of 0.753 (95% CI 0.66–0.84) with adequate calibration (Hosmer–Lemeshow p = 0.963). Fisher grade, posterior circulation aneurysm location, and inflammatory markers (NLR, PLR, PNR) were not significant in this cohort, which the authors attributed to universal external ventricular drainage placement and the distribution of treatment modalities. The authors note the limitations of retrospective design and limited case numbers, and state that prospective validation of the nomogram is needed.

An international team of scientists has studied live specimens of Kuphus polythalamia, a giant black mud-dwelling shipworm that consumes hydrogen sulfide rather than rotting wood. Found in a lagoon on an abandoned log farm in the Philippines, the mollusk hosts microbes that convert the swamp gas into carbon. Researchers hope studying microbes in its gill will yield new antimicrobial substances. The findings were published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

The article presents a seasonal trading strategy for the German stock market using the iShares MSCI Germany ETF (EWG), a convenient vehicle for U.S. investors. Historical monthly returns of EWG since 1996 show the best time to be invested is the year's final quarter, while the ETF trades sideways during the rest of the year. The strategy therefore invests only in the fourth quarter of each year. Backtests using dividend- and split-adjusted data show the strategy performed well and better than buy and hold. The DAX 40, Germany's main index of 40 blue-chip companies founded in July 1988, has returned 5.36% per year since inception.

Climate change is warming streams in the northern Rocky Mountains, threatening native cutthroat trout. Rainbow trout, which prefer warmer water, are invading these streams and breeding with cutthroats, producing hybrids that are less fit and survive less well than the native fish. A study in Global Change Biology found hybridization was widespread, especially where rainbow trout had been introduced since the 19th century. Some states are removing rainbow trout to protect the cutthroat species, which ecologist Clint Muhlfeld warns could otherwise disappear.

Dolphins wide receiver Tyreek Hill dislocated his knee during Monday night's win over the Jets and is undergoing further tests while remaining hospitalized overnight. The injury occurred early in the third quarter when Hill caught a 10-yard pass from quarterback Tua Tagovailoa and his left leg twisted under him as he was tackled out of bounds. An air cast was placed on his leg, and he smiled and waved to the crowd while being carted off. Hill was in good spirits and told the team to secure the win, Miami's first of the season. He entered the game leading the Dolphins with 198 receiving yards and had 67 yards on six catches. Since entering the NFL in 2017, Hill leads the league with 11,363 receiving yards, ranks fourth with 819 catches, and is third with 83 touchdown catches. The Dolphins would need others to step into larger roles, with Waller and a running back among the passing-game options.

Former INEC Administrative Secretary Christian Nwosu told a Lagos Federal High Court that EFCC operatives coerced him into admitting he received N30m from former Petroleum Minister Dieziani Alison-Madueke. Testifying before Justice Mohammed Idris, he said operative Usman Zakari threatened to detain him unless he wrote dictated statements, and that he surrendered property worth N30 million and N5 million cash. He alleged prosecutor Rotimi Oyedepo ordered his detention and warned he would be convicted and jailed if he did not cooperate.

State Street Corporation, the firm that commissioned the "Fearless Girl" statue, agreed to pay $5 million to settle U.S. Department of Labor claims that it paid 305 female employees and 15 black vice presidents less than male and white counterparts in the same positions. The company denies the allegations but agreed to pay approximately $4.5 million in back pay and $500,000 in interest into a settlement fund. The statue, installed in March 2017 before International Women's Day facing "Charging Bull," was a publicity stunt promoting State Street Global Advisors and a gender diversity index called SHE. The sculptor of "Charging Bull" complained the statue distorted his work's message of prosperity and strength.

A large nationwide study published in Neurology (October 1, 2025) found an association between long-term outdoor exposure to trichloroethylene (TCE), an industrial solvent used in metal degreasing and dry cleaning, and increased Parkinson's disease risk in older adults. Using Medicare data for 221,789 people with Parkinson's and over 1.1 million without, researchers estimated TCE exposure via EPA air data and ZIP+4 locations. After adjusting for factors like age, smoking, and fine particulate pollution, those with the highest outdoor TCE levels had a 10% higher Parkinson's risk than those with the lowest. Geographic hot spots were identified, particularly in the Rust Belt. The study shows association, not causation, and is limited to Medicare-aged individuals using 2002 outdoor air estimates.

A swimming advisory was issued for Little Beach in Port Stanley on Friday due to high bacteria levels and remained in effect as of Monday. The Elgin St. Thomas Health Unit warns of health risks like gastrointestinal illness, but the beach remains open, with swimming being a personal choice. Some visitors didn't notice the advisory signs.
John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis won the 2025 physics Nobel for demonstrating quantum effects in electric circuits.

The Evening Sun's 2016 top stories included: siblings Evan (10) and Brynn (6) Meek handing out 220 bagged lunches to homeless people in Manhattan on August 6 after being inspired by their mother's concerns; Norwich Police Officer Thomas Miller, an eight-year veteran who worked with K9 Nitro on community events, accepting a position with the Syracuse Police Department; and Tracy A. Price, 31, of Norwich, being arrested August 16 for allegedly torturing, injuring, and neglecting a dog, granted $750 bail.

Researchers at Chalmers University of Technology in Sweden used machine learning and computer simulations to determine the structure of formamidinium lead iodide, a halide perovskite material considered promising for efficient, flexible solar cells. They resolved the previously unexplained low-temperature phase of the material, whose instability has limited its use. The machine learning approach enabled simulations thousands of times longer than before, involving millions of atoms instead of hundreds. Experimental collaborators at the University of Birmingham validated the findings by cooling the material to -200°C. The study was published in the Journal of the American Chemical Society.

A 36-year-old New York man, Reinaldo De Jesus Henao, was arrested at the Coachella festival after concertgoers used "Find my iPhone" to track him following the alleged theft of over 100 cellphones. He faces grand theft and possession of stolen property charges.

Musicians and singers from Sir John Deane's sixth form college performed at the Evening of Jazz and Soul, in its fourth year, at the Macdonald Portal Hotel in Tarporley. The 35-strong collective, directed by Timothy Murphy, played 60s soul and classic swing. The next event features 14 students performing classical music at Arley Hall on February 9.

Cuba marked the 58th anniversary of its revolution with a military parade honoring Fidel Castro, who died Nov 25 at age 90. Tens of thousands marched at Havana's Revolution Square, some carrying "We are Fidel" banners, though soldiers marched without equipment. Cuba faces a difficult 2017: Raul Castro's final full year in power, a shrinking economy, and US rapprochement threatened by President-elect Trump.

Wafa Yahia, the Syrian grandmother at the center of Hawaii's lawsuit against Trump's travel ban, arrived in Honolulu Saturday night from Lebanon. She is the mother-in-law of Ismail Elshikh, a Honolulu imam and plaintiff, and received US visa approval weeks ago. Legal challenges continue, with an appeals court hearing this month and a Supreme Court case in October. Hawaii's attorney general said the approval does not affect the lawsuit.

A study in the Journal of Experimental Psychology found distraction is the best way to recover from a breakup, though it should be used sparingly since it's a form of avoidance. Focusing on an ex's negative traits may also help.

On July 27, 2021, Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2021. The press release containing these results is furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer. Microsoft's registered securities include common stock and three notes series (2.125% due 2021, 3.125% due 2028, and 2.625% due 2033), all traded on NASDAQ under the symbol MSFT.

Vale SA's stock conversion plan received stronger-than-expected backing, with 84.4% of preferred shares joining, exceeding the 54.09% minimum threshold. Executives said the company could list on the São Paulo Stock Exchange's Novo Mercado as early as this year, ahead of the 2020 target. The single-class share structure aims to attract broader investors, though the government will retain a golden share. Vale will also absorb its former controlling entity, Valepar SA.

A pregnant writer describes difficulty sleeping due to pregnancy restrictions: after the fifth month, lying flat on the back can pressure the vena cava, stomach sleeping becomes impossible, and only left-side sleeping is recommended. As a longtime stomach sleeper, she feared losing sleep. Through a Facebook friend's post, she learned about the Leachco pregnancy pillow and was advised to choose the U-shaped version over the J-shaped one, since it allows flipping without moving the entire pillow. She purchased it on Amazon for $65 (later $81) and found it greatly improved her comfort, enabling side sleeping, easy flipping, and congestion relief. She also uses it around her apartment. Downsides include its large size, a scratchy included cover (softer replacements are sold), and disrupted blankets. She plans to continue using it after the baby is born and recommends it to both pregnant and non-pregnant people.

This study examined the participation of primary school students with disabilities in inclusive settings in virtual education during the COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey, based on teachers' perspectives. Using a phenomenological design, researchers conducted semi-structured interviews with 10 general education primary school teachers from two provinces in the Marmara region, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected in 2021 through in-person interviews lasting 28–35 minutes and analyzed via content analysis, yielding six main themes and 15 sub-themes, with inter-coder reliability of 90.17%.

Findings showed that teachers conducted virtual courses via EBA and Zoom, initially informed parents about the process, and tried various applications such as WhatsApp and video sharing. Most students with disabilities participated at high rates, particularly with parental support, though some did not participate due to factors such as illiterate parents, technology or internet problems, or preference for rehabilitation center education. Teachers reported problems including socialization difficulties, homework tracking issues, cameras kept off, and large class sizes limiting individual attention; others reported no problems, attributing this to EBA's tracking features and daily parent communication. Some students struggled with course activities and assignments, citing unengaging content and disadvantaged home environments, while others completed work successfully and earned high grades. Teacher-parent cooperation varied, with problems including families not expressing needs and unused EBA support points. Teachers applied solutions such as hybrid models and flexible scheduling, and suggested device/internet support, keeping schools open, and coordination with rehabilitation centers.

The study concluded that parents play a key role in virtual education and recommended informing stakeholders, improving technological infrastructure, and conducting further research with other populations.

This paper argues for adopting cooperative education (co-op) in Nigeria to address youth unemployment. Using the UN definition of youth (ages 15–24), it notes that Nigeria's youth unemployment rate, historically lower than most regions, was higher than most by 2021 and at least double the total unemployment rate for most of the period studied. Youth also face low employment-to-population ratios, a high NEET rate (28% in 2019), gender and urban-rural disparities, and higher unemployment among the educated. Co-op, a form of work-integrated learning comprising an integrated curriculum, work-based learning, and logistical coordination, originated in industrialized countries and exists in SSA, including South Africa and Namibia. It operates through alternating, parallel, and other models, with documented benefits for students, employers, institutions, and society, though evidence is mainly from developed countries. Nigeria's existing programs—SIWES, SURE-P, and N-SIP/N-Power—target graduates or occur outside the academic calendar, leaving a gap co-op could fill by aligning university training with industry needs. The paper recommends the alternating model, integration within existing government programs to enable pilot testing, government cost support through tax credits or grants, and employer participation. It concludes that co-op should complement broader multipronged interventions and calls for further research on management structures, program models, and applicability beyond tertiary education.

This study analyses the spatiotemporal dissemination of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron BA.1 variant in England from November 2021 to January 2022 using phylodynamic analysis of 48,615 English genomes alongside mobility and epidemiological data. Researchers identified at least 6,455 independent introduction events, with the earliest estimated between 5 and 18 November 2021. Most importations (69.9%) were singletons that did not lead to observable local transmission. Early importations occurring before or during travel restrictions on southern African countries (26 November–15 December 2021) accounted for approximately 6% of total introductions but were responsible for ~80% of Omicron BA.1 infections in England. Travel restrictions were largely ineffective, partly because the source of importations shifted from South Africa to the US. Greater London served as the central hub for spatial expansion, with long-distance viral movements predominantly directed from London to the Midlands and North West England. Phylogeographic GLM analysis found the gravity model and aggregated mobility as key predictors of viral lineage movements. The study also found that human mobility decreased by approximately 12% for every unit increase in weekly COVID-19 cases per 100 people at hub locations, suggesting voluntary behavioural responses to rising case numbers influenced spatial spread. Findings highlight the limited effectiveness of targeted travel restrictions once local transmission is established and the importance of understanding interactions between perceived risk, human behaviour, and transmission dynamics for future epidemic preparedness.

The TLV321/2x comparator family consumes 40µA per channel with 40ns propagation delay. The TLV321x features a push-pull output, while the TLV322x has an open-drain output that can be pulled up to any voltage up to 5.5V independent of the supply. The input voltage range extends from 200mV below V- to 200mV above V+, with input current limited to 10mA. Unused inputs must not be tied together but connected to voltages providing at least 50mV differential. The family includes 1.8mV of internal hysteresis. Push-pull outputs must be left floating if unused and never shorted to supply rails; open-drain outputs support logic OR'ing and level translation, with recommended pull-up current of 100µA to 1mA. Internal ESD protection limits input voltages to 0.2V beyond the rails. TLV321x devices include a Power-On Reset circuit active up to 32µs after VPOR (1.65V) is crossed, holding the output low during POR. Propagation delay increases as overdrive voltage decreases, particularly below 100mV. External hysteresis can be added via positive feedback in inverting (three-resistor) or non-inverting (two-resistor) configurations. A typical application is low-side current sensing, with an alert output when the amplifier output exceeds 1.1V. Proper PCB layout, including 0.1µF bypass capacitors and minimized input-output coupling, is recommended.

An email dated November 22, 2001, from Commissioner.COM (SportsLine) to Paul Lucci at Enron delivers a fantasy football e-report. It opens with promotional offers, including a 10% discount on an Anna Kournikova 2002 calendar, a Tomb Raider collector's edition DVD, free Sporting News issues, a gas savings promotion, a Vegas vacation or $600 cash sweepstakes, a free satellite dish offer, $9.99 fantasy football guides, and an Xbox giveaway through Taco Bell. The main section provides Week 11 NFL player news and fantasy start/sit recommendations for quarterbacks, running backs, wide receivers, and tight ends across most league teams. Notable updates include Jerome Pathon being placed on injured reserve, Terry Glenn unlikely to play against New Orleans, Az-Zahir Hakim listed as questionable with an ankle injury, Kurt Warner coming off a 401-yard, three-touchdown game, and Marshall Faulk described as a must-start. A final section provides player news specific to the recipient's fantasy team, "Luccis Losers," covering players such as Alex Van Pelt, Charlie Garner, Cris Carter, Duce Staley, and David Akers. The report is copyrighted by Commissioner.COM Inc. and SportsLine.com Inc.

The passage describes NVIDIA's GA10x Ampere GPU architecture. Each SM contains 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, a second-generation Ray Tracing Core, and 128 KB of L1/Shared Memory. GA10x doubles FP32 throughput by enabling FP32 processing on both datapaths, allowing 128 FP32 operations per clock per SM. ROPs were moved into GPCs, increasing the full GA102 to 112 ROPs versus 96 in TU102. Ampere GPUs are up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing.

The second-generation RT Core doubles ray/triangle intersection testing rates and adds an Interpolate Triangle Position unit enabling hardware-accelerated motion blur up to 8x faster than Turing. Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32 and BF16 data types and a Sparsity feature that doubles throughput by skipping zero-valued weights. DLSS is enhanced with a 9x Super Resolution factor, enabling 8K 60 fps gaming.

GA10x introduces GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling, supporting up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec bandwidth. NVIDIA RTX IO enables GPU-based lossless decompression with Microsoft's DirectStorage API, improving I/O performance up to 100x while offloading CPU work.

The A40 data center GPU delivers up to 2X FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and 5X (10X with Sparsity) AI training performance versus the Quadro RTX 6000, with 48GB memory expandable to 96GB via NVLink. Display support includes HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a with 8K60. Fifth-generation NVDEC provides the industry's first AV1 hardware decode; seventh-generation NVENC handles encoding. The GeForce RTX 3090 (GA102, 24GB GDDR6X) is 1.5x faster than TITAN RTX, while the RTX 3070 (GA104) outperforms the RTX 2080 Ti. New Error Detection and Replay (EDR) technology detects and replays GDDR6X memory errors during overclocking. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU features 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, and 48GB of GDDR6.

On August 16, 2018, NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC announcing its financial results for the quarter ended July 29, 2018. The filing includes a press release (Exhibit 99.1) and CFO Commentary (Exhibit 99.2) prepared by Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Colette M. Kress. The CFO Commentary will be posted to investor.nvidia.com after filing. The report was signed by Kress.

The United States defeated Serbia 3-0, its first win over Serbia, to advance to a home Davis Cup quarterfinal against Belgium or Hungary; Serbia played without Novak Djokovic. Kazakhstan swept Switzerland 3-0, which has lost in the first round every year since winning the 2014 title. Belgium led Hungary 2-1 after losing a five-set doubles match. Defending champion France led the Netherlands 2-1. Croatia's Marin Cilic and Ivan Dodig won the doubles against Canada after dropping the first two sets. Spain led Britain 2-1, Germany led Australia 2-1, and Italy led Japan following Saturday's doubles results.

The passage discusses Justice Amy Coney Barrett's book, which the author praises and which argues that originalism is the correct method of constitutional interpretation because the Constitution's enacted text is binding law whose words must be read according to the meaning its lawmakers employed. Accepting that premise for the sake of argument, the author considers its implications for a Supreme Court case involving a constitutional challenge to Louisiana's second majority-Black congressional district, created to avoid violating the Voting Rights Act, and which the Court ordered reargued after failing to reach a decision the previous term. The author argues that the "racial predominance" doctrine—under which districts are unconstitutional when race predominates in their drawing and strict scrutiny cannot be satisfied—cannot be justified by the original public meaning of the 14th Amendment, since the equal protection clause was not originally understood to constrain state elections, as shown by the later adoption of the 15th and 19th Amendments and by the 14th Amendment's second section, which contemplated states denying voting rights subject to a loss of congressional representation. The 15th Amendment likewise cannot support the doctrine, the author contends, because the claim involves no vote dilution or infringement of any individual's right to cast a ballot. Nevertheless, the author argues that even a good originalist must adhere to precedent under the doctrine requiring respect for prior decisions. Because the racial predominance test is unworkable and in tension with Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, a good originalist would reconsider and abandon that doctrine, preserving Congress's power to make vote dilution claims actionable, while Congress remains free to legislate against racially motivated districting. The author hopes Barrett will decide the case with the intellectual honesty her book espouses.
