Resources may change without notice and are limited to developing applications using the described TI products; users must indemnify TI against related claims.

The Investors Intelligence Sentiment Index, also known as Advisor Sentiment, is a contrarian indicator created in 1963 by AW Cohen and published by Chartcraft. It weekly polls over a hundred independent market newsletters, producing percentages of bullish, bearish, and correction expectations among investment advisors, and measures stocks above their 10-week and 30-week moving averages. Although originally intended to show the best time to be long when most advisors were bullish, advisors proved almost always wrong at market turning points, so it became a contrarian indicator. Bullish readings above 55% indicate excessive optimism and are potentially negative, while readings below 35% indicate pessimism and are considered positive; weekly figures above 70% suggest an overbought market and below 30% an oversold market. Unlike the AAII Sentiment Survey, which polls individual investors, this index focuses on professional advisors and commentators.

A cellphone video of a Euclid, Ohio officer repeatedly punching a 25-year-old black man during a traffic stop will be reviewed. The officer is on paid leave, and the NAACP seeks a federal investigation.

Macmillan is launching a new season of early years picture books, including a 35th anniversary gift edition of Rod Campbell's lift-the-flap classic Dear Zoo, in which a child writes to the zoo asking for a pet. Catherine Rayner's Solomon and Mortimer follows two bored crocodiles whose plan to surprise a hippo leads to unexpected results. Paul Stickland's Ten Terrible Dinosaurs, a rhyming counting book based on characters from Dinosaur Roar!, has been republished with a Natural History Museum endorsement. Julia Donaldson and Rebecca Cobb's The Everywhere Bear tells of a classroom teddy who falls from a backpack and is washed out to sea before trying to return to Class One. Morag Hood's When Grandad Was a Penguin features a grandad behaving like a penguin, while Lane Smith's A Perfect Day, inspired by a real bear encounter, depicts a bear disrupting the animals' idyllic day in a garden.

A man wearing a homemade pipe bomb attempted to detonate it at the Port Authority near Times Square in New York City on Monday morning around 7:30 a.m. The device either malfunctioned or didn't go off as planned. Four people were hurt, including the suspect, but none of the injuries are life-threatening. The suspect is in custody. The explosion triggered a large emergency response, shut down the surrounding area, and disrupted subway and bus service, with the A, C, and E lines evacuated and NJ Transit buses diverted. President Trump was briefed on the incident.

On the first day of the US government shutdown, Department of Education employees found their automatic out-of-office replies altered without consent to blame Senate Democrats for the shutdown. Some restored neutral language, only to have it changed again. It is unclear who made the changes, which were first reported on Bluesky by journalist Marisa Kabas. While some agencies offered neutral suggested language, the DOE and, according to sources and screenshots, the Department of Labor received language blaming Democrats. Experts say the partisan language could violate the Hatch Act, which limits federal employees' political activity and carries penalties including fines or job loss. The DOE press line returned the same partisan message when contacted by WIRED.

The Rotary Club of Lakewood and Rocky River honored winners of its annual Speech, Music, and Visual Arts Contest at an April 9 ceremony at Beck Center for the Arts. In the speech contest, Lakewood High School students Nicholas Cleary, Taylor Heckel, and Gabby Murray placed first, second, and third. Music winners were Angeliki Cintron (first, flute), Hannah Cogar (second, voice), and Emily Erhardt (third, flute), with honorable mentions to Grace Cooper and Dan Tomazin. Visual arts winners were Elyza Mihalski (first), Mikah Inak (second), and Chloe Becker (third), with honorable mentions to Phoebe Dunn, Riley Geyer, and Andrew Lewis. More than 90 art pieces from five schools were submitted.

Other items: North Olmsted schools are selling $75 engraved bricks for a new Fan Walk, with a May 11 deadline for the first phase. Free community meals will be held April 28 at Clague Road United Church of Christ (hosting with Westlake Church of the Redeemer) and West Park United Church of Christ. Lakewood City Schools received the NAMM Foundation's Best Communities for Music Education award for the second consecutive year. North Olmsted High School will present the musical "We Will Rock You" April 27-29. "Razzle Dazzle XVIII: Wide World of Sports," featuring performers with special needs, will be staged at Beck Center May 4-5. Two blood drives will honor Dr. Steve Meadows, who died in January 2017. The Cuyahoga West Genealogical Society will offer free research assistance May 2. Volunteers are needed May 5 to prepare Kamm's Corners for the Hooley. Upcoming events include Keep Lakewood Beautiful's Earth Day cleanup, an American Legion Auxiliary rummage sale, and the West Park Historical Society's grand opening.

This policy brief argues that the out-of-school children (OOSC) indicator, which measures only formal school enrollment, is inadequate for capturing educational exclusion and advocates replacing it with an out-of-education children (OOEC) indicator that recognizes formal, informal, and non-formal learning pathways. Using Afghanistan as a case study, the brief contends that the OOSC indicator privileges formal schooling, delegitimizes alternative systems such as madrasas and community-based education, and overlooks the geopolitical, cultural, and social realities driving exclusion.

Globally, out-of-school children have risen by 7 million over the past decade to 251 million, with the Taliban's ban on girls' secondary education in Afghanistan a significant contributor. OOSC figures likely underestimate the problem, particularly for marginalized groups, and COVID-19 disrupted schooling for over 1.7 billion students.

The brief traces Afghanistan's educational history, noting that education has been a contested ideological terrain since modern schooling emerged in the late 19th century. Enrollment grew from roughly 500,000 in 2000 to about 10 million in 2021, but the Taliban's 2021 return left 80% of school-aged girls out of school. Four factors keeping children out of school are examined: geographic disparities, nomadic lifestyles, child labor, and disabilities.

The OOEC indicator is presented as offering three advantages: broadening understanding of educational challenges, catalyzing system transformation, and reimagining education as an interconnected ecosystem. Implementing the shift requires new data systems capturing all pathways, evolved credentialing systems, greater collaboration among education actors, and changed resource allocation. The brief concludes that transitioning to OOEC is a crucial first step toward inclusive, equitable education aligned with SDG 4.

The judgment convicting Ronald Haynes of criminal possession of a weapon in the third degree upon his guilty plea was affirmed. Counsel's withdrawal was granted, and the defendant's pro se claims were precluded by his waiver of the right to appeal.

SFS (Seamless Firmware Servicing) is an AMD firmware feature for developing and distributing fixes for selected high-priority system issues, which datacenter operators can apply without rebooting. Fixes are delivered in AMD-signed SFS Update Packages; customers or OEM/ODMs may optionally co-sign packages by providing an RSA public key to the ASP during early boot. Deploying a package can change three version numbers: the SFS Patch Level (SFSPL), which must monotonically increase to prevent rollback; individual firmware component and Security Patch Level (SPL) versions; and the System Patch Level (SYSPL), which monotonically tracks run-once code executed since the last reboot. The ASP verifies signatures before applying updates, extending its role as root of trust for detection, while OEM/ODMs retain root of trust for update via co-signing. SFS packages apply only at runtime, do not persist across reboots, must be reapplied after reboot, and are applied sequentially in multi-update and multi-socket systems; SFS is off by default and requires BIOS opt-in. Packages can patch registers, replace firmware images, or update firmware portions, and each verifies applicable firmware versions before applying, avoiding partial application. Commands require a 2MB-aligned TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER and a customer-provided deployment agent. Updates run in parallel with x86 and DMA traffic with minimal performance impact; SEV/SEV-ES virtual machines must stop and restart for SEV firmware updates, while SEV/SNP VMs can continue operating.

The passage outlines passport application rules. Applicants must take an oath of allegiance, provide a physical description, and include a credible witness's certificate. Native citizens need only the standard application. Those born abroad to native citizen fathers must show their father's U.S. birth and citizenship. Naturalized citizens must submit their naturalization certificate and detail their emigration, residence, and naturalization. Women's applications vary by marital status; wives or widows of naturalized citizens must submit the husband's certificate. Children of naturalized citizens must also submit the parent's certificate. Residents of insular possessions must affirm sole allegiance to the United States with two witness affidavits. Passports expire two years after issuance. One passport may cover an applicant's wife, minor children, and servants. Professional titles are excluded, and officials may reject applications for unlawful purposes. Signed by Theodore Roosevelt, July 19, 1902, with fees of $1.00 for a passport and 50 cents each for duplicate application and oath administration.

Archaeologists led by Guillermo de Anda of the Great Mayan Aquifer Project will excavate a tunnel sealed centuries ago by the Maya, aiming to reach a hidden cenote beneath El Castillo, a pyramid at Chichen Itza. Cenotes—water-filled sinkholes and Yucatan's only fresh water source—were central to Mayan spirituality, viewed as entrances to the underworld where offerings and human sacrifices were made to deities like the rain god Chac. Chichen Itza, built around the 5th and 6th centuries AD, includes El Castillo, a 79-foot temple to Kukulcan with 365 steps. Two years ago, scientist Rene Chavez Segura determined a cenote lies hidden beneath it. After finding passageways from the Ossuary pyramid blocked with stones, the team plans a roughly three-month excavation. De Anda believes the cenote may represent the "axis mundi," or center of the world. Prior analysis showed 80 percent of sacrificial victims at the Sacred Cenote were malnourished children aged 3 to 11; more research is needed.

The EU has announced a €545 million ($636 million) investment package under its Global Gateway plan to support renewable energy and electrification in Africa, where nearly 600 million people lack electricity. Projects include a high-voltage transmission line in Côte d'Ivoire, rural electrification in Cameroon, wind and hydro energy in Lesotho, and mini-grids in Madagascar; the EU estimates the program could create 38 million green jobs by 2030. Global Gateway, a €300 billion initiative through 2027, also aims to counter China's Belt and Road Initiative, which has invested over $1.3 trillion worldwide, including $39 billion in African energy contracts in the first half of 2025. The US has similarly launched the Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment. Africa, rich in critical minerals, has become a battleground between superpowers.
Lab tests show jostling microbubbles of air and methane can create tiny lightning zaps, possibly igniting the methane behind will-o'-the-wisps.
Enix Bussey's judgments of conviction were affirmed without opinion on October 16, 1947.

Patriarch Theophilos III of Jerusalem announced that his Church will appeal an Israeli court ruling upholding the sale of church property to companies representing Israeli settlers in East Jerusalem. The Church has fought the deal for a decade, arguing it was illegally conducted by deposed Patriarch Irenaios. Theophilos called the ruling politically motivated, expressed concern over Israeli efforts to restrict church property rights, and urged world leaders to intervene.

A take a knee chart helps football coaches determine when the offense can kneel—an almost risk-free play used to run time off the clock when ahead at the end of a game. The offense lines up in the victory formation, and the quarterback kneels immediately after the snap, which counts as a run play and keeps the clock moving. The chart shows offensive player positions and movement order. The passage also stresses the importance of clock management, noting that incomplete passes stop the clock, high school and college football lack a two-minute warning, and mistakes in a close game can give the opponent a chance to drive for a winning score.

This study investigated kindergarten teachers' views on distance education in the Region of Epirus, Greece, during the 2020–2021 school year, following its mandatory implementation due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Using a quantitative approach, an anonymous online questionnaire was completed by 82 kindergarten teachers (96.3% women, mostly holding bachelor's degrees) and analyzed with SPSS 21.

Findings showed that over three in four teachers were little or not at all familiar with distance education before the pandemic, and 91.5% had not previously integrated it into their teaching. Synchronous education was preferred (64.6%), with Webex the most used tool (88.9%). Teachers' views on integrating distance education into kindergarten were mostly negative: about 90% stated it limits psychomotor activities and requires adult supervision, 86% considered it less effective than conventional education for developing social skills, and majorities cited inadequate school digital infrastructure, limited internet access, and preschoolers' difficulty using technology independently. Teachers also expressed doubts about its promotion of individualized learning, student interest and participation, and involvement of students with disabilities.

Statistical analysis showed that holders of a Level B ICT certificate reported significantly higher familiarity with distance education before the pandemic than teachers without certificates, while no significant relationship was found between years of service and ICT literacy.

The study concludes that teachers lacked readiness and highlights the need for infrastructure modernization, teacher training, interactive resources, and support for parents. Results are limited to Epirus and cannot be generalized to the entire country.

The passage consists of AP photo captions from the 3rd Round of the Scripps National Spelling Bee held in Oxon Hill, Md., on Wednesday, May 30, 2018. Pronouncer Brian Sietsema is shown speaking during the round. The captions identify spellers aged 9 to 15 from various U.S. states and South Korea, noting the words they attempted and whether they spelled them correctly or incorrectly. Correctly spelled words included "bonspiel," "slickensides," "aspirator," "heliosis," "revivification," "sclerotic," and "deliverable." Incorrectly spelled words included "giddily," "abandonedly," "finial," "frustraneous," "transude," and "athleisure." Some spellers, such as Ranitha Kumarasinghe and Elizabeth Shvarts, celebrated after correct spellings, while others walked offstage or reacted after misspelling. Photos were credited to Carolyn Kaster and Cliff Owen.

S&P downgraded Bridgeview, Illinois' rating four notches to junk-level BB-minus, citing debt pressures from $135 million of 2005 bonds for its Toyota Park stadium. The rating is on watch for further downgrade. The underperforming stadium left the village with an "extremely high" $256 million debt burden and "very weak" liquidity.

The paper introduces ML²B (Multilingual Machine Learning Benchmark), the first benchmark for evaluating LLMs on generating complete ML pipelines from multilingual natural language descriptions. Existing ML code generation benchmarks (MLE-bench, DA-Code, Weco-Kaggle) are English-only, despite reported performance gaps between English and other languages. ML²B comprises 30 Kaggle competitions (24 public, 6 private) translated into 13 languages, yielding 390 evaluation instances across tabular, text, and image modalities in 12 domains. It includes human-reviewed task descriptions, standardized data cards, and six private competitions to prevent benchmark data leakage. The benchmark consists of a main pipeline, Docker runtime, and code grader, and supports two submission formats (MONO_PREDICT and MODULAR_PREDICT), the latter designed to reduce preprocessing leakage. Translations were generated with GPT-4o and validated by native speakers with CS/IT backgrounds. Evaluation uses percentile-based leaderboard rankings. Five LLMs were tested across two frameworks (AIDE and ML-Master), showing 15–45% performance degradation on non-English tasks. English consistently yielded the best results, while low-resource languages (Kazakh, Belarusian, Romanian) showed higher failure rates, particularly in tabular classification and regression; image categorization was comparatively stable. Hybrid models partially mitigated low-resource weaknesses, and no single model was universally optimal. Static leakage analysis flagged 61 of 554 modular submissions (11%), reduced to 33 (5.9%) after excluding likely false positives. Future work includes expanding private-task coverage and pursuing multilingual alignment strategies.

Amazon.com, Inc.'s Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2018 reports that the Delaware-incorporated company, headquartered in Seattle, operates through three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). Amazon serves consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators, and seeks to be Earth's most customer-centric company. Whole Foods Market results are included from its August 28, 2017 acquisition. The company employed approximately 647,500 full- and part-time employees as of December 31, 2018. Net sales grew 31% to $232.9 billion in 2018, with operating income of $12.4 billion and net income of $10.1 billion; segment sales were $141.4 billion (North America), $65.9 billion (International), and $25.7 billion (AWS). Risk factors include intense competition, expansion strains, international regulatory risks (notably in China and India), fulfillment network optimization, seasonality, foreign exchange, security breaches, inventory, intellectual property, government regulation, tax liabilities, supplier relationships, and payments risks. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $41.3 billion at year-end 2018, with cash capital expenditures of $11.3 billion. The company operated 277.2 million square feet of leased and 11.2 million square feet of owned space. Jeffrey P. Bezos serves as President, CEO, and Chairman, and 491,202,890 shares were outstanding as of January 23, 2019.

The passage contains reader comments posted beneath various news headlines. Most comments are spam messages advertising hacking services, including database hacking, credit score boosting, phone and email spying, bank and money transfers, and partner monitoring, each providing contact email addresses or names of hackers. One comment, under a marketplace article, advertises a marble-topped coffee table for sale at $350, negotiable.

The 9 EMA trading strategy uses the 9-period exponential moving average to generate buy and sell signals for identifying short-term market trends. A buy signal occurs when price moves above the 9 EMA, and a sell signal occurs when price moves below it. The strategy can be applied to stocks, forex, commodities, and crypto, and can be combined with other indicators such as RSI, MACD, and Bollinger Bands for signal confirmation. Backtesting shows the strategy works well in trending assets like Bitcoin (284 trades with a 2.65% average gain per trade) but fails in mean-reverting markets like stocks. Adding a 200-day moving average as a trend filter improved Bitcoin results (153 trades, 4% average gain), though the S&P 500 version remained untradable. Risk management techniques include stop-loss orders, position sizing, diversification, and defined exit strategies. The strategy only works in assets that trend or show short-term momentum.

GOLDWOOD is a plywood brand recognized for premium, no-compromise quality, emphasizing mutual trust, transparency, on-time delivery, and sustainable development alongside business goals. GOLDWOOD PLY, based in Yamunanagar, Haryana, is among the top plywood manufacturers, offering products such as Block Board, Flush Door, and Plywood across India.

Enron's Mark Palmer forwarded colleagues a class action complaint filed November 27, 2000, in San Diego County Superior Court by Pamela R. Gordon on behalf of herself and similarly situated electricity customers, against Reliant Energy, Southern Company, NRG Energy, Dynegy, AES Corporation, Williams Energy, and Duke Energy North America. The suit alleges that beginning around May 22, 2000, these generators and traders unlawfully manipulated California's wholesale electricity market by misusing confidential real-time generator and transmission data obtained through the WSCC, withholding capacity from forward markets, parking power with out-of-state affiliates for resale at inflated rates, and scheduling plant outages and transmission flows to create congestion. The complaint cites FERC, CPUC, and CAISO findings that prices were "unjust and unreasonable" and that customers were overcharged approximately $4 billion during summer 2000. The proposed class includes roughly 1.2 million SDG&E customers. Claims are brought under the Cartwright Act, the Unfair Trade Practices Act, the Consumers Legal Remedies Act, and unconscionability, seeking treble damages, disgorgement, restitution, and injunctive relief. Palmer noted a reporter said Enron's suit would look the same.

The law's real effectiveness often depends on little-publicized bills, which attract scant public attention while interested parties work to defeat them. The bill's importance is heightened because the Government has begun using criminal law in trust and interstate commerce cases where success is reasonably likely; though enforcement began with civil proceedings, criminal prosecutions have produced many successes that deterred wrongdoers through fines and imprisonment. Judge Holt of the New York district court exemplified the need for just severity toward such offenders. In a rebate case, he found the evidence clear and the offense flagrant: rebates exceeding one-fifth of the tariff rate could drive competitors out of business. He deemed the crime deliberate, premeditated, and more heinous than crimes of passion, committed by educated men on behalf of a railroad corporation obligated to treat all citizens equally. Because such crimes are secretive and rarely prosecuted, he imposed a penalty commensurate with the offense, principally on the corporation, since the traffic manager acted without personal gain.

The Missouri Student Union held MU's annual Veterans Day wreath laying ceremony Friday to honor veterans, including a National Remembrance Day Roll Call reading the names of killed MU student veterans. Keynote speaker Col. Roderik Cox, an MU alumnus with over 12 years of service, defined a veteran as anyone who swore an oath to defend the nation. Robert Ross, director of the MU Veterans Center, which serves over 400 student veterans, said the event honored the past and looked toward future peace. Speakers, including Navy veteran David Emily, rejected Hollywood stereotypes, describing veterans as ordinary people. The event ended with a reception at Bengal's Lair in Memorial Union.

The Konektadong Pinoy Act, signed into law on August 24, 2025, removes barriers to competition in the Philippine telecom market, potentially allowing Virtual Network Operators to compete with PLDT. This increased competition arrives as PLDT's profitability declines and growth slows. Capital Cycle analysis suggests the law may drive excess investment into a mature, highly penetrated industry, depressing profitability. Despite PLDT's attractive valuation, the author believes the threat of new entrants is reason enough to stay on the sidelines.

The International Nurses Association welcomes Joy Williams, BSN, RN, with an upcoming publication in Worldwide Leaders In Healthcare. A Louisiana nurse with over seven years of experience, she became an LPN in 2009 and an RN in 2016, crediting her daughter Londen for her success.

This passage examines small group differentiation as a pedagogical strategy for improving learning outcomes and fostering inclusivity in elementary and higher education, particularly for diverse student populations. It cites U.S. enrollment and language diversity data, including shifts in racial/ethnic percentages between 2009 and 2018, a decline in English-only households from 89.1% (1980) to 79.7% (2010), and growth in English language learners. The study uses a systematic literature review of papers from 2000–2023 and is guided by Constructivism and Sociocultural Theory. Differentiation involves tailoring content, process, products, and learning environment to student needs, guided by five principles: flexibility, ongoing assessment, respectful and challenging experiences, collaboration, and student autonomy. Elementary settings emphasize foundational skills and teacher guidance, while higher education involves specialized content, changing student groups, and self-directed learning. Small group instruction is associated with engagement, dialogue, and relationship-building, and culturally responsive environments and reflection exercises can improve outcomes. Challenges include required planning time, large class sizes, limited administrative support, and serving students with disabilities under IDEA (7.3 million students, 15% of public school enrollment, in 2021–22). Limitations include insufficient data for comparative analysis and limited empirical evidence linking small group instruction to test scores. The conclusion stresses flexibility, regular assessment, and varied assessment methods. Recommendations call for longitudinal studies tracking differentiation's effects and research based on visual, auditory, kinesthetic, and read/write learning styles.

This paper presents the Atlas of Human-AI Interaction, a framework that uses large language models to systematically map empirical findings in human-AI interaction (HAI) research. Motivated by the difficulty of synthesizing a rapidly growing literature—and by the limits of traditional reviews that organize papers by topic rather than by relationships among findings—the authors collected 1,888 paper abstracts from ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, Springer Nature Link, and ArXiv using the query "human-ai interaction." Using Claude Opus 4.1, they extracted empirical findings from 1,124 papers (59.53%) as 2,037 structured [cause, relationship, effect] triplets, embedded the keys with Qwen3-Embedding-8B, merged synonyms via DBSCAN (62 clusters), and applied k-means clustering by entity type. The resulting knowledge graph contains 1,310 nodes and 3,908 edges, visualized through three views: a 3D Graph View, a Cause-Effect View (Sankey diagram), and a Paper View.

Analysis identified 24 topic clusters and dominant research patterns, including AI in educational contexts (91 relationships involving students), explanation and trust (14 relationships), design relationships (68 findings), decision support (13), and self-referential research (6). Network analysis using the Louvain algorithm identified 126 research communities (modularity 0.669); structural hole analysis highlighted large language models, generative AI, trust, chatbots, and autonomous agents as concepts with the greatest potential for cross-community integration, leading to five proposed research directions.

A study with 20 expert researchers found the Atlas supported landscape visualization, research gap identification, and relationship discovery, with positive ratings for the 3D Graph View (M=4.95) and Cause-Effect View (M=5.45). Participants noted limitations in summary depth, temporal analysis, and applicability to mathematical research, positioning the Atlas as a complementary exploratory tool. The authors frame the work as using AI to synthesize AI research, aligned with Engelbart's vision of augmenting human intellect.

The 4-3 defense, popular at all football levels, was brought to the NFL by Tom Landry, modernized by Jimmy Johnson, and gained renewed prominence with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' "Tampa 2" coverage in the early 2000s. It consists of four defensive linemen, three linebackers, and four defensive backs, with the 3 technique defensive tackle considered the most important position. Its strengths include strong run defense, gap soundness, and coverage flexibility, while its weaknesses are vulnerability to modern spread offenses and specific personnel requirements. Offenses attack it by spreading the field and running to the edge. Common blitzes include the Will Edge Blitz and DE Drop Blitz, with Tampa 2 and Cover 3 as common coverages. Notable practitioners include the 2000s Buccaneers, the 2006 Chicago Bears, and Mike Bukovsky of Montini Catholic High School in Illinois.

Google has launched Gemini Enterprise, an AI platform for business customers offering access to advanced Gemini Ultra models and enterprise-grade tools for data governance, security, and regulatory compliance. Positioned between consumer offerings and research tools, it enables firms to deploy and customise AI applications on Google Cloud, fine-tune models with proprietary data, and maintain oversight through explainability and access controls. The launch strengthens Google's position in the enterprise AI market against Microsoft, Amazon, and OpenAI, with transparency and accountability features—traceable outputs, privacy safeguards, and compliance tools—serving as its competitive edge. Analysts see particular appeal for financial, healthcare, and manufacturing clients, and integration with Google Workspace may broaden adoption. The launch reflects Google's shift from AI model development to full-scale enterprise deployment. Early feedback is positive, but success depends on proving reliability and delivering measurable returns. The remainder of the passage consists of headlines covering finance, markets, and technology topics.

Ray Dalio's All Weather Portfolio, created by Dalio and his team at Bridgewater Associates, is designed to withstand any economic environment—inflation, deflation, or stagflation. The portfolio consists of stocks, bonds, and commodities, with a heavy allocation to bonds and a small allocation to stocks. Its foundation lies in diversification and low correlation between asset classes, aiming to smooth returns and reduce drawdowns. Bob Prince's 2011 paper outlined the risk parity approach, claiming a balanced portfolio achieves equity-like returns with one-third of the risk.

A backtest from July 2007 shows a CAGR of 4.5% (excluding dividends) versus the S&P 500's 6.7%, but with a substantially smaller maximum drawdown of 17%. The portfolio outperformed stocks during the 2008/09 financial crisis, the 2020 Covid-19 crash (roughly 6% drawdown versus stocks' 33%), and the 2022 bear market (about 12% drawdown). Leveraging the portfolio 1.5 times raises the CAGR to 6.5% with a 25% maximum drawdown.

The article suggests building the portfolio with five ETFs and rebalancing at least annually, preferably in a tax-deferred account. While it will likely underperform stocks and 60/40 portfolios over the long run, it suits risk-averse, conservative investors, retirees, and those pursuing FIRE.

Mother appeals a dissolution judgment awarding $31 per month in child support for each of the parties' two children, arguing the amount is too low and that support was improperly abated during father's visitation. The children, ages 11 and six, spend about half their time with father under an agreed visitation arrangement resembling joint custody. While agreeing that father's visitation expenses may be factored into support calculations, the court found the amount insufficient and modified the judgment to require father to pay $65 per month for each child, affirmed as modified, with no costs to either party.

Please, Continue (Hamlet), created by theatre-makers Yan Duyvendak and Roger Bernat, stages Hamlet's trial for Polonius's murder in real courtrooms with real judges and lawyers, and is playing at Melbourne Festival. Since its 2011 Swiss premiere, it has been performed in 12 countries, adapting to each jurisdiction's legal system and staged only in countries with jury systems. A 12-person jury is selected from the audience. The creators were inspired by shock at reading Guantanamo trial transcripts, which they viewed as fake trials. The show integrates a real 2010 case—a young man accused of killing his girlfriend's father—obtained unredacted from a lawyer friend. The creators' opposing views on that defendant's guilt inspired a format allowing audience opinion shifts. Duyvendak reports participants often change their minds during performances, gaining appreciation for the justice system's complexity, with former jury members reporting altered views on sentencing severity.

This study conducts a systematic review and descriptive bibliometric analysis of research on the metaverse in education, using the Scopus database and VOSviewer software. Following PRISMA standards, 270 journal articles published between January 2015 and July 2024 were identified through searches of terms such as "metaverse and education," "metaverse and instruction," "metaverse and learning," and "Edu-metaverse," with inclusion limited to English-language journal articles.

Results show no publications before 2020, followed by four articles each in 2020 and 2021, 36 in 2022, a peak of 131 in 2023, and 91 articles already in 2024. The most productive countries were South Korea (40 publications), China (35), and the United States (31); South Korea also led in citations, followed by the United Kingdom and China. IEEE Transactions on Learning Technologies published the most articles, while Sustainability (Switzerland) was the most cited journal (447 citations). The most cited article was Dwivedi et al. (2022) with 890 citations, followed by Hwang and Chien (2022) and Akour et al. (2022). Co-occurrence analysis of 910 unique author keywords yielded 22 keywords in 6 clusters, with the most frequent being "metaverse" (192), "virtual reality" (54), "education" (28), "augmented reality" (23), and "artificial intelligence" (18).

The discussion attributes the post-2020 growth to the COVID-19 pandemic's shift toward digital education and later increases to advances in AI, machine learning, and 5G. Prominent topics fall into two areas: use of the metaverse—integrating VR, AR, and AI—to create virtual educational environments (e.g., medical training, AR escape games, virtual university settings, and gameful learning worlds), and student and teacher perceptions and attitudes, which are largely positive, with perceived usefulness, personal innovativeness, and perceived enjoyment facilitating adoption under an extended Technology Acceptance Model.

The study concludes that gaps remain, including a lack of longitudinal studies on long-term impacts and a geographic concentration of research in East Asia and the United States. Future research should assess sustained effectiveness, scalability, and adaptability across learning environments, and explore adoption across diverse cultural and institutional contexts.
Order affirmed with $10 costs; Justice Thomas dissented, citing the ex parte entry.

During Severe Weather Awareness Week, Michigan State Police, Emergency Management and Homeland Security are encouraging residents to join a voluntary statewide tornado drill at 1 p.m. Wednesday, with nearly all state facilities participating. Officials urge residents to identify shelter spots, conduct drills, monitor broadcasts, distinguish tornado watches from warnings, recognize warning signs, and prepare 72-hour emergency kits. If severe weather occurs April 19, the drill moves to 1 p.m. Thursday.

This passage outlines principles and techniques for transition defense in basketball. It emphasizes that good transition defense begins with good offense—taking care of the ball, good shot selection, offensive rebounding, and maintaining defensive balance. Key concepts include the "Level of the Ball" rule (defenders staying ahead of the ball), sprinting back on defense while maintaining ball vision, and never running with backs to the ball. The passage details defending outnumbered situations (2-on-1 and 3-on-2), including containing the dribbler, forcing extra passes, tandem defense, and communication. After missed shots, defenders should jam the rebounder, deny outlet passes to the primary ball handler, slow penetration by pushing ball handlers toward sideline pushpoints, and match up with offensive players. Five methods for disrupting outlet passes are described: attacking the pass, complete pass denial, taking a charge, forcing a premature pass, and trapping. The passage also covers recovery after turnovers and blocked shots, where defensive stops can "erase" bad plays. Game strategies include scouting opponents and substituting for players who fail to sprint back. For teaching, the passage recommends the Whole-Part-Whole method and specific drills such as the "Wolf" one-on-one and three-on-two drills, noting that transition defense must be an integral part of every full court scrimmage.

Passports expire two years after issuance; renewals require new applications, and naturalized citizens may use an old passport in lieu of a naturalization certificate if it contains sufficient information. One passport suffices for a wife, minor children, and servant if their ages and the servant's allegiance are stated; others need separate passports. Professional titles are excluded. A one-dollar fee (currency or postal money order payable to the disbursing clerk) is required; drafts and checks are not accepted. The Department of State does not procure visés and furnishes blank forms only to individual applicants. Communications go to the Passport Bureau. The Secretary of State may refuse passports for unlawful purposes or noncompliance. Theodore Roosevelt prescribed these rules for the United States and similar rules for its insular possessions, where applications go to the chief executive or nearest U.S. diplomatic or consular officer. Passports are denied to those not owing U.S. allegiance, including declarants of intent. Applicants must submit sworn affidavits stating birth date and place, occupation, residence, and intent to return.

The Navy's free Pier Pressure mobile app, part of the Keep What You've Earned campaign, helps Sailors make responsible drinking choices during Alcohol Awareness Month and year-round. The app features a calorie counter, Uber and Lyft integration for safe rides, and has been played over 30,000 times since release.

The passage documents the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) specification for Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) events. For each NAE event, the guest must set VALID_BITMAP bits for SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, and SW_EXITINFO2, while the hypervisor sets bits for SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2; both parties should reset VALID_BITMAP before each event. Bit positions are derived from field byte offsets divided by 8.

Standard VMGEXIT processing is described, with errors communicated via SW_EXITINFO1[31:0], where non-zero values indicate hypervisor-reported errors such as unregistered GHCB addresses, invalid scratch fields, or missing valid input bits. Specific NAE events covered include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO access (using a decrypted shared buffer), Page State Change (supporting private/shared page transitions and PSMASH/UNSMASH hints for SEV-SNP, with up to 253 entries per request), SNP Guest Request and Extended Guest Request (firmware communication with certificate data returned via GUID-identified tables), AP Creation, #HV doorbell page registration (GET_PREFERRED, SET, QUERY, CLEAR actions), #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Request (for trusted device binding), Secure AVIC backing page registration, and Termination Request.

Guests identify SEV-ES support through hypervisor-provided CPUID properties. SMP booting is challenging because vCPU registers cannot be changed after measurement; solutions include the AP Reset Hold NAE event and AP jump tables (4K, encrypted, page-aligned), communicated between UEFI and the OS via SET/GET events or the SEV-SNP Secrets Page. The SNP AP Creation feature enables vCPU hotplug and simpler AP booting via RMPADJUST-marked VMSA pages.

For NMIs, the hypervisor must intercept #DB rather than IRET, using the guest's "NMI Complete" message to regulate injection. Hardware debug register virtualization is supported where available; otherwise DR7 accesses are intercepted and cached. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

The #HV doorbell page enables host-to-guest notification under Restricted Injection, containing a 16-bit PendingEvent field (vector number, NMI/#MC bits, NoFurtherSignal flag) and a NoEoiRequired byte. The host presents the highest-priority ready interrupt by writing the vector, manages EOI semantics, and sets NoFurtherSignal for non-maskable events. Guests must atomically exchange doorbell values, validate vectors against a potentially non-cooperative host, and execute HLT with interrupts disabled, relying on the host to re-enter the guest when events are pending.

The Dow fell 424.56 points, or 1.74 percent, to 24,024.13 on Tuesday amid fears of rising interest rates and Caterpillar's suggestion that economic growth may slow. The S&P 500 fell 1.3 percent and the Nasdaq dropped 1.7 percent, while the 10-year Treasury yield topped 3 percent for the first time in four years.

In Hemsell v. Summers, the Texas Court of Civil Appeals reviewed a judgment awarding appellees a total of $30,890 for the death of J.W. Summers, who was killed on October 9, 1937, in a collision between his automobile and one driven by Clennon C. Hemsell, an employee of Columbian Fuel Corporation. The suit was brought by Florence O. Summers (widow), her three minor children, and Laura L. Summers (mother of the deceased).

The court found the trial court's jury charge constituted reversible error. The instruction accompanying special issue No. 54 improperly assumed the deceased would have lived 34½ years and supported his wife in a particular manner, removing the fact question of life expectancy from the jury. The charge under special issue No. 55 similarly erred by assuming the mother's approximately twenty-year life expectancy based solely on the mortality table. The instruction under special issue No. 56 wrongly allowed recovery for loss of love, care, and fatherly advice, since only pecuniary losses are recoverable, not loss of society or companionship. The charge under special issue No. 57 improperly singled out college education expenses without sufficient evidentiary basis. The court also should have instructed the jury to exclude sorrow and grief as elements of recovery.

The court found no error, however, in refusing requested sole proximate cause issues, as there was no evidentiary basis for them, nor in refusing a new and independent cause issue, since the deceased's own acts could not constitute such cause.

Finally, improper jury argument by appellees' counsel, criticizing appellants' counsel for introducing an admissible divorce record, was error, particularly as the trial court declined to instruct the jury to disregard it.

The judgment was reversed and the cause remanded.

A security researcher discovered a keylogger in hundreds of HP laptop and tablet models, linked to Synaptics touchpad drivers. Michael Myng found the keylogger, which is disabled by default, while examining a keyboard driver. HP confirmed the issue and released patches for more than 450 products in a Nov. 7 security update. HP stated neither it nor Synaptics has access to customer data, though a registry change could allow malicious actors to monitor keyboard activity. This is the second keylogger issue affecting HP devices this year, following a May finding in Conexant audio drivers.

Philadelphia remains unbeaten in four MLS matches, with Czech midfielder Borek Dockal contributing two assists and a penalty against Chicago. Dockal averages 2.4 key passes per game.
