Johnny Juzang is making a strong case for a Timberwolves roster spot, potentially replacing the departed Nickeil Alexander-Walker. On a non-guaranteed contract, he scored 20 points in 14 minutes in a preseason game and has made 9-of-15 three-pointers this preseason. The 24-year-old former third-team All-American has shot over 38% from three the past two seasons.

Researchers at Johns Hopkins and the Mayo Clinic have published a guideline in JAMA Internal Medicine to help physicians stop using the CK-MB blood test for suspected heart attacks, citing evidence that it adds no diagnostic value beyond cardiac troponin. Despite 2014 guidelines, a 2013 survey found 77 percent of U.S. labs still use CK-MB, contributing to an estimated $416 million annual cost of heart attack blood tests. The report, the first in a series from the High Value Practice Academic Alliance, outlines four steps to eliminate CK-MB: hospitalwide education, stakeholder collaboration to remove it from order sets, computerized order alerts, and measuring outcomes. Additional guides will target other unnecessary practices.

Chinese police shot dead three knife-wielding assailants who killed five and injured 10 in Pishan County, Xinjiang, home to the Uighur minority. Authorities called the attackers "thugs," said order was restored, and launched an investigation. It cites past attacks, including in Aksu in 2015 and Kunming in 2014.

This paper uses hydrodynamical simulations combined with time-dependent chemistry and radiative transfer to produce synthetic line observations of a collapsing prestellar core, testing whether observational infall diagnostics accurately reflect the true collapse rate. The authors performed SPH simulations of a critical Bonnor-Ebert sphere (5 M⊙) collapsing over 0.87 Myr, post-processed particle histories with a chemical code to obtain molecular abundance profiles, and generated line emission for C18O, N2H+, HCO+, H13CO+, CS, and C34S at two apertures (0.05 and 0.2 pc) and two timesteps (0.81 and 0.87 Myr). Infall velocities were derived from line profiles using the Myers et al. (1996) method.

The results show that all measured infall velocities fall significantly below the true mass-weighted values (0.153 km/s at 0.81 Myr and 0.228 km/s at 0.87 Myr). CS-based estimates come closest, reaching about half the true value, while HCO+ can yield values an order of magnitude smaller, with discrepancies arising purely from chemical and radiative transfer effects despite identical underlying velocity profiles.

The authors attribute this systematic underestimation to the constant-velocity, two-slab models underlying these techniques: in realistic cores, velocity profiles peak in the inner regions, while self-absorption features originate in the outer, slower-moving material. Consequently, mass accretion rates derived from such methods may underestimate true values by up to an order of magnitude. The paper suggests that the non-thermal velocity dispersion measured from optically-thin lines, which remains within a factor of two of the true infall velocity in these simulations, may serve as a better measure, though this may not hold in more turbulent environments.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that, effective March 11, 2021, Jerome Guillen transitioned from President, Automotive to President, Tesla Heavy Trucking. Since September 2018, Guillen oversaw Tesla's vehicle programs, supply chain, and service infrastructure. He will now lead all aspects of the Tesla Semi program, including related charging and servicing networks, as Tesla enters the heavy trucks market. The report was signed by CFO Zachary J. Kirkhorn on March 12, 2021.

Indian-origin surgeon Dr Sachiendra Amaragiri has been struck off the UK medical register after a tribunal found he abused his position by writing a love letter to a patient, who reported it to police. He apologised and intends to appeal.

Sony launched a US instant rebate and trade-in scheme running through September 30, 2017, offering up to $300 off select full-frame cameras, an additional $500 for trading in an interchangeable lens camera, up to $200 off A7 cameras, up to $100 off select lenses and accessories, and free shipping.

Compass Minerals International (CMP) is rated a "Buy" due to attractive valuation and significant operational improvement. Revenue and volumes in salt and plant nutrition are rising, while cost-cutting initiatives are improving cash flow and EBITDA. Despite higher net debt and leverage than peers, CMP trades at lower multiples, offering upside potential. Management projects further top-line growth for 2025, but leverage risk tempers the rating to "Buy" rather than "Strong Buy." Chart data shows prices ranging from 18.29 to 19.98 between October 2 and 7, 2025.

The CANSLIM method, developed by William O'Neill, founder of Investor's Business Daily (IBD), is described in his book *How To Make Money In Stocks*. It uses seven variables to identify "good stocks," based on the best-performing stocks from 1953 to 1993. Although O'Neill called it simple, the authors consider it difficult to implement because some criteria are hard to quantify. IBD publishes the IBD 50, a computer-generated list of 50 stocks meeting the CANSLIM criteria, available fully only to paid subscribers. Backtests show CANSLIM beat the S&P 500 since 2003 (18% CAGR versus 9%), but with higher volatility and larger drawdowns. This outperformance may result from the method's small-cap bias. The strategy performs well in bullish markets but drops significantly in bearish ones, and it has underperformed the S&P 500 in recent years. Backtesting is difficult because it requires both fundamental and technical data. The method is intended for long-term investing, and its risks include market volatility and potential loss of capital.

Peter Crouch made a humorous tweet about the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge's third child, a boy born at the Lindo Wing at St Mary's Hospital, Paddington, on St George's Day, weighing 8lbs 7oz. Crouch's quip was retweeted over 22,000 times, prompting a brutal reply from his wife Abbey Clancy. Crystal Palace's official Twitter account also joked about the birth, pretending the word following "son" in a news tweet was the baby's name.

The passage examines the Golden State Warriors' tendency to fall behind early and rally with dominant second halves, such as overcoming large deficits against Houston in Games 6 and 7 of the Western Conference finals. Analyst Mark Jackson and former coach Jeff Van Gundy say this pattern would concern a coach, noting the team cannot keep relying on comebacks. The Warriors also struggled at times, losing the second half in Games 2, 4, and 5. The article compares this habit to other comeback examples, including racehorse Silky Sullivan, runner Dave Wottle, and the Oakland A's slow starts from 2000-03. Jackson warns that repeatedly digging holes will eventually catch up to a team.

A hockey player discusses his team's playoff run, crediting Rucchin's two goals in a needed win and noting Jiggy played well. He says he wasn't playing his best hockey in the finals but was glad to contribute offensively. He calls the first two games in New Jersey an aberration, noting both teams have held serve at home. He leads by example rather than speaking up in the room. He was surprised by a hit from Scott but will continue making the same plays. After a hard stick hit, he was checked by a doctor and returned to the game. He describes the long series as a big competition with growing animosity, and recalls fond childhood memories of watching the Stanley Cup.

Airbus is developing Project Vahana, an autonomous, helicopter-style flying vehicle designed to carry several riders and help commuters avoid congested roads. The company is using clean technology to avoid urban pollution and says the vehicle could reduce infrastructure costs. Airbus is in the experimentation phase, aiming for a fully functional prototype by 2017 and short-haul trips by 2021. Other efforts include Uber's planned VTOL aircraft network, Urban Aeronautics' Cormorant drone, AeroMobil's land-and-air vehicle, and investments from Skype's co-founder and Larry Page.

Savvy investors are buying closed-end equity mutual fund schemes on stock exchanges at discounts to net asset values (NAVs). Closed-end schemes have three-to-five-year lock-ins, and poor liquidity causes them to trade below NAV. Buyers profit since redemption occurs at NAV at maturity. Examples include Reliance Close Ended Mutual Fund Series A Growth (10% discount) and HDFC Equity Opportunities Fund (6% discount). Discounts depend on time to maturity and tax considerations. Experts recommend schemes with large assets under management, over Rs 250 crore.

Michael Ben'Ary, an assistant U.S. attorney in the Eastern District of Virginia, was abruptly fired while prosecuting the 2021 Afghanistan airport bombing that killed 13 U.S. service members and 160 Afghan civilians. A letter taped to his door said a false social media post apparently led to his termination, after pro-Trump commentator Julie Kelly suggested he was an ally of former Deputy Attorney General Lisa Monaco. The letter claimed DOJ leadership is "more concerned with punishing the president's perceived enemies" than protecting national security.

This patent application, a divisional of related applications, concerns a light emitting diode (LED) device and a method of manufacturing it, directed to a reliable connection structure between a luminous body and an electrode connected to it.

The background explains that LEDs convert electrical signals into light using compound semiconductors and are increasingly applied to display devices, such as backlights or self-luminous micro-sized pixels. Miniaturizing and integrating LEDs requires highly reliable connections between luminous bodies and electrodes or wirings.

The disclosed LED device includes: a thin film transistor (TFT) substrate having light emitting areas; first and second diode electrodes on the substrate; a first passivation pattern between the electrodes; micro LEDs on the first passivation pattern; a first bridge pattern electrically connecting the first diode electrode to the micro LEDs; and a second bridge pattern on the first bridge pattern connecting the second diode electrode. Sidewalls of the micro LEDs and sidewalls of the first passivation pattern form the same plane, reducing steps on the bridge patterns and thereby minimizing their breaking.

Each micro LED is cylindrical, comprising a light emitting material with an inorganic crystal structure—sequentially arranged p-type semiconductor layer, intermediate layer, and n-type semiconductor layer—surrounded by an insulating protective layer. The first sidewall exposes the p-type layer and contacts the first bridge pattern; the second sidewall exposes the n-type layer and contacts the second bridge pattern. The diode electrodes include fine electrode lines alternately arranged in parallel, with the passivation pattern and micro LEDs between them. Barrier ribs may be provided on the substrate under the electrodes.

The manufacturing method includes preparing a TFT substrate, forming the diode electrodes, forming the first passivation pattern, micro LED, and second passivation pattern through a single mask process with two etching processes, then forming the bridge patterns. Micro LEDs are placed on the first passivation material layer and aligned by forming a voltage difference between the electrodes. The first etching is longer and more anisotropic; the second is shorter, more isotropic, uses an oxygen-containing additive gas, and a higher gas flow rate, so that the micro LED sidewalls and passivation pattern sidewalls form the same plane.

A display device embodiment includes a luminescent panel with light emitting units and a panel driving unit (scan driver, data driver, power supply unit, and timing controller) capable of a simultaneous light emission mode. Each light emitting unit includes three switching devices (e.g., NMOS thin film transistors) and a capacitor, with the light emitting diode composed of multiple micro LEDs aligned by an electric field.

Aspen, Colorado, is replacing its annual Fourth of July fireworks with a 15-minute drone show featuring 50 drones, due to wildfire risks in the drought-hit area. The show, organised by the Aspen Chamber Resort Association in Wagner Park, follows strict fire restrictions imposed across western Colorado.

The US national debt surpassed $21 trillion for the first time, growing by $73 billion in a single day, $215 billion in February, and more than $1 trillion over six months—despite no major crisis and a reportedly strong economy. The author notes debt growth is outpacing GDP growth: the debt grew 6% last year versus 4.4% economic growth including inflation. Over the past decade, the economy grew 36% (from $14.5 trillion to $19.7 trillion) while debt grew 123% (from $9.4 trillion to over $21 trillion). The author disputes the argument that the debt doesn't matter because it is owed to institutions like Social Security, the banking system, and the Federal Reserve, contending that defaulting would be catastrophic. He identifies three public responses: ignoring the debt, dismissing its significance, or preparing for possible consequences.

MLB's wild-card round reaches decisive Game 3s on Thursday, featuring three winner-takes-all games—only the second such day in baseball history. The Tigers stranded a franchise postseason-record 15 runners in Game 2 and are 3-for-38 with runners in scoring position over their last three elimination games. The Padres-Cubs game figures as a bullpen battle, with Yu Darvish (2.56 ERA in six postseason starts with San Diego) facing Jameson Taillon (1.57 ERA in six starts since returning from the IL in August). Red Sox manager Alex Cora pulled Brayan Bello after 28 pitches in Game 2, using six relievers; only two bullpen arms went unused. Also noted: the Yankees beat the Red Sox to force a Game 3, Yamamoto put Los Angeles in the NLDS with Ohtani starting Game 1, Rocchio's homer forced a Guardians Game 3, Snitker won't return as Braves manager in 2026, and the Rockies dismissed GM Schmidt after a 119-loss season.

Jio announced new offers under its Jio Galaxy Club on the Samsung Galaxy J2 2018 and Galaxy J7 Duo, launched in April at Rs 8,190 and Rs 16,990. Both come with Rs 2,750 instant cashback via 55 vouchers of Rs 50 each. J2 2018 buyers get 100GB additional data with Rs 198/299 plans, bringing its effective cost to Rs 5,440, while J7 Duo buyers get double data on those plans. Offers are valid until September 30; both phones are available online and offline.

This study investigates predictors of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) response in sarcomas by analyzing transcriptomic profiles of pre-treatment biopsies from 67 patients enrolled in 3 ICI trials, with validation in an independent cohort of 190 TCGA sarcoma samples. Using RNA sequencing and hierarchical clustering of principal components, researchers identified two distinct immune clusters—"immune-hot" and "immune-cold"—based on baseline immune infiltrates. The immune-hot cluster showed significantly higher overall response rates (30% vs. 8.1%) and longer progression-free survival (3.65 vs. 1.7 months) following ICI treatment. Analysis of transposable element (TE) and epigenetic regulator expression revealed that TE expression and the transcription factor IKZF1 were significantly associated with immune type. Six TE subfamilies and IKZF1 were identified as signature features predictive of the immune-hot state. Both TE score and IKZF1 expression correlated with immune and inflammatory pathways including cGAS-STING, type I and II interferon signaling, and antigen-processing machinery. High TE score and IKZF1 expression were associated with prolonged progression-free survival and higher response rates. These findings were validated in the TCGA cohort, where TE and IKZF1 expression also predicted immune type and correlated with overall survival. The study proposes IKZF1 expression and TE score as potential predictive biomarkers for ICI response in sarcomas and suggests that pharmacologic targeting of epigenetic regulators to promote TE de-repression could enhance ICI response.

Meagan Holt, whose 3-year-old daughter Madeline has Zellweger Syndrome, participates in a Seattle Children's writing program offered by the Pediatric Advanced Care Team (PACT) that encourages parents to journal. Holt says writing gives her an outlet for feelings she bottled up; consultant Julie Arguez calls it an empowerment tool bringing calm, relief, and acceptance. The program relies on donations.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on October 27, 2022, announcing its third quarter 2022 financial results. The filing includes a press release (Exhibit 99.1) and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures (Exhibit 99.2). The report was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. Amazon's common stock trades under the symbol AMZN on the Nasdaq Global Select Market.

Happy Home Furnishers is closing its Neath store after 33 years at The Parade, citing anti-social behaviour, lack of free parking, and rising business rates. Director Mike Semmens said street works disrupted trade without compensation, and a bench placed outside a nearby alcohol shop led to drinking, fights, and rowdiness; staff cleaned up vomit, excrement, and needles, and customers stopped visiting. The bench was removed after about a year. Other traders reported mixed experiences: jacket potato seller Marc Smith said troublemakers caused him no problems, while some shop workers avoid public toilets due to found needles, and Brian Warlow of Neath Health Store described severe summer problems with drunk people and those on legal highs. Neath Council said the street works benefited the town, benches were intended for people with mobility issues, and it supports police against anti-social behaviour. On parking, Semmens argued free 20-minute parking is needed to attract busy families, saying supermarkets like Tesco gain business instead; Smith agreed parking is difficult. The council noted a low shop vacancy rate, a new 600-space multi-storey car park with free parking on level three after 3pm daily, and events like the Neath Food and Drink Festival. On business rates, Semmens said rent was reasonable but rates rose substantially; the Welsh Government noted the 2017 revaluation affected some towns and highlighted its high street rates relief scheme supporting nearly 15,000 businesses plus £110 million annual small business relief. The company continues at other locations and may seek another Neath site.

This study explores physics teachers' attitudes towards physics education research, focusing on science scepticism towards science education research (SSSE), defined as scepticism about its practical value. Motivated by the theory-practice gap and the assumed value of evidence-based teaching, the authors conducted a two-step mixed-methods study: interviews with 13 German physics teachers to develop attitude categories, followed by a survey of 174 physics teachers from Germany and Austria.

The interviews yielded seven attitudes, three positive and four sceptical. The most common sceptical attitudes were that research findings play a minor role compared to teachers' own practical experience and that findings cannot be implemented in practice, attributed to lack of time, overly theoretical findings, and poor researcher-practitioner cooperation.

An exploratory factor analysis of the survey data identified four factors: relevance of research for the individual teacher, feasibility of findings for practice, relevance for teaching practice in general, and cooperation between research and school practice. Latent profile analysis identified four teacher types: The Sceptical Ones (14%), who devalue research overall; The Uncertain Ones (27%), with largely neutral responses; The Undersupplied Ones (41%), the largest group, who value research but criticize its feasibility and cooperation; and The Research Advocates (18%), showing the least scepticism.

Multinomial logistic regression showed that only the frequency of reading instructional journals significantly predicted profile membership; teaching experience, teacher education, school type, and doctoral degree did not. All profiles were critical of research-practice cooperation. The authors suggest integrating research more prominently into teacher education and improving researcher-practitioner collaboration, while noting limitations including small and convenience samples, the Hawthorne effect, and measurement constraints regarding journal reading frequency.

The Baltimore Ravens are trading pass rusher Odafe Oweh and a 2026 fifth-round pick to the Los Angeles Chargers for safety Alohi Gilman, according to sources. Oweh, 26, recorded a career-high 10 sacks last season but has no sacks in his first five games this season, and his playing time has dropped to a career-low 45% of defensive snaps. The move frees roughly $8 million in cap space for Baltimore, and Oweh will be an unrestricted free agent after the season. The Ravens, who allow an NFL-worst 35.4 points per game and rank 31st in pass defense, also added safety Gardner-Johnson to the practice squad. Gilman, 28, was a key part of the Chargers' top-ranked defense last season, though his play has fluctuated this year. Oweh ranks 33rd in the NFL in pressure rate (11%) and gives Los Angeles a young edge rusher while Khalil Mack, out since Week 2 with an elbow injury, is eligible to return in Week 7. The Ravens are 1-4, tying the worst start in the franchise's 30-year history.

African countries have been urged to adopt modern technology to address tax non-compliance. Secretary to the Treasury Ben Botolo made this call while opening the 18th Forum for VAT Administrators in Africa (VADA) in Lilongwe, noting electronic fiscal devices are critical for optimizing tax revenue. VADA Chairperson Henry Saka emphasized formalizing regulatory strategies and designing African solutions to tax evasion.

The lecture reviews the propagator's two interpretations: as a heuristic transition amplitude between spacetime points and as a correlation function. The Feynman propagator is the time-ordered correlation function. In momentum space, the propagator has poles at ω = ±ω_k lying on the integration contour; different contour choices yield the retarded, advanced, and Feynman Green's functions. Rather than changing contours, the epsilon prescription shifts the singularities slightly off the real axis while keeping the contour fixed.

In free field theory, vacuum n-point functions factorize into sums of products of two-point functions, so knowing the two-point function determines everything. Composite operators like φ² are generally singular and require renormalization—a generic feature of quantum field theory.

The lecture then introduces interactions via φ⁴ theory, the simplest interacting theory with well-defined energy (φ³ lacks a definite energy sign). Its nonlinear equation of motion cannot be solved exactly, so perturbation theory in the small coupling λ is required. Scattering experiments are the primary experimental method for probing interactions, historically from Rutherford to deep inelastic scattering.

The S-matrix is defined using the idealization that particles are infinitely far apart at t = ±∞, where interactions can be neglected and states described by free theory. It is a matrix element of the evolution operator, is unitary, and respects Hamiltonian symmetries. It is written as S = 1 + iT, with total momentum conservation factored out to define the scattering amplitude M. The LSZ theorem states that M can be obtained from time-ordered vacuum correlation functions of the full interacting theory. The path integral approach will be introduced next.

The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau has finalized rules that could force many payday lenders out of business, despite Republican opposition in Congress. One rule requires payday and auto title lenders to determine whether borrowers can afford to repay in full within 30 days; another limits account debits without reauthorization. A 2014 CFPB study found over 80 percent of payday loans are rolled over or followed by another loan within two weeks. The Financial Services Association of America says the rule would devastate the $39 billion industry serving 30-40 million customers annually. The CFPB estimates loan volume could be halved, closing many of the 16,000 payday stores in 35 states. The rule takes effect in 2019 and could be rolled back by Congress.

A hockey coach discusses his team's preparation for an upcoming finals game against Philadelphia, stressing the need to stay focused despite home-crowd distractions and noting that players like Vernon, Murphy, and Kocur have experienced this situation before. He praises his goaltending tandem of Mike and Chris, describing Mike's confidence and resiliency after facing goalies such as Grant Fuhr and Patrick Roy. The coach emphasizes that teams must win games away from their own building, says the players avoided retaliating against provocations, and describes Marty Lapointe's penalty as situational rather than foolish. He credits defensive pairings of Fetisov with Konstantinov and Murphy with Lidstrom, along with responsible forward coverage. He reflects on a previous finals loss to the Devils, attributing it to their strong defense and goaltending, and explains that Kirk Maltby was moved to left wing due to a surplus of right wingers, which led to trading Ray Sheppard and Dino Ciccarelli. The team also stays overnight away from the arena before games to help with ice conditions.

The President writes to the Senate to clarify that passages in his recent message and protest may have been misunderstood. He affirms he did not intend to deny the legislative department's power to provide by law for the custody, safe-keeping, and disposition of public money and property. He acknowledges the Legislature's constitutional authority over public funds and disclaims any Executive right to possess or dispose of public property except as granted by law. He requests this communication be entered with the original message on the Senate's journals.

This patent application, a continuation of International Application No. PCT/CN2019/119114, relates to sidelink positioning methods and apparatus in the communication field. Existing positioning technologies determine terminal device position based on reference signal measurements between a network device and the terminal device, are controlled by a core network, and exhibit increasing error as the distance between the network device and terminal grows, making them unsuitable for high-accuracy scenarios.

The application provides sidelink positioning methods in which terminal devices determine position using sidelink signals. In a first aspect, a first terminal device receives a sidelink positioning configuration from a network device and sends a first sidelink positioning reference signal to a second terminal device, which measures it to obtain a first measurement value used, together with the second terminal's position, to determine the first terminal's position. In a second aspect, the second terminal device performs the measurement and reports the value to the network device or the first terminal device. In a third aspect, the network device sends configurations to both terminals and determines the first terminal's position. Measurement values may include Rx−Tx time differences and angles of arrival, reported via Uu or PC5 interfaces. Because measurement values need not be transmitted through a core network, positioning latency is reduced, and the solution also applies when the first terminal device does not support sidelink reference signal measurement.

Further aspects cover positioning apparatuses, processors, chips, computer program products, storage media, and communication systems. Detailed embodiments describe applicable systems (LTE, 5G/NR, V2X, and future technologies), network and terminal device types, the existing LTE/NR Rel-16 positioning architecture managed by a location management function, and multiple interaction flows in which the network device hosts positioning, configures reference signals, and the terminals exchange and report measurements.

The passage lists design figures for two embodiments of an analytical instrument, each shown in perspective, front, back, side, top, and bottom views; broken-line features are not part of the claimed design.

Retired Toronto civil litigator Marcel Strigberger describes decluttering his home by discarding his McGill University law schoolbooks, purchased over 50 years earlier. He recalls cases from his contracts text, including an 1890s English smoke ball reward case and an 1860s case where a carriage owner's contract with a prostitute was held unenforceable as contrary to public policy. From his property law text, he remembers fee simple and fee tail, noting he never used these terms with clients in over 42 years of practice. After placing the books in his recycling bin, he discovered a used copy sold online for over $1,000 Canadian. He kept one thick volume to use as a desk reading stand.

In June 2014, The Wall Street Journal reported that Hertz Global Holdings would have to restate and correct results from the past three years due to more widespread accounting problems than previously anticipated; Hertz's stock closed down about 9%. Analyst Abby Devins questioned whether the issues were related to Hertz's large rental fleet and what impact they might have on future vehicle acquisition plans.

The U.S. car rental industry generated approximately $36 billion in revenue in 2013, divided among leisure travelers, business travelers, and leasing. After revenue growth plummeted during the 2008-09 recession, growth resumed with the economic recovery. Three companies—Enterprise Holdings, Avis Budget Group, and Hertz Global Holdings—dominated the market with a combined 71% share.

Founded in 1918, Hertz changed hands several times, was acquired by private equity firms in 2005, and went public in 2006. By the end of 2013, it had nearly 12,000 locations across 145 countries and a fleet exceeding 700,000 cars. The company expanded through the Dollar Thrifty acquisition (2012), the Firefly brand launch and a 20% stake in China Auto Rental (2013), and operated Donlen for fleet leasing along with an equipment rental business. Hertz reported record revenue and EBITDA in 2013, with revenue up roughly 30% and net income more than doubled since 2011. Depreciation averaged about 25% of total expenses, and revenue earning equipment comprised over 50% of total assets.

Depreciation requires estimating an asset's useful life and residual value, typically allocated using the straight-line method. Hertz depreciated its rental fleet on a straight-line basis over estimated holding periods, reviewing depreciation rates quarterly. Its fleet included program cars, purchased under manufacturer repurchase or guaranteed depreciation programs, and non-program cars, which carried residual price risk. Devins compiled Hertz and Avis Budget Group data on revenue earning equipment and depreciation from 2006 to 2013 for comparison.

The passage examines AI's societal impacts across several domains. Regarding human cognition, learning, and creativity, AI shows potential to augment human abilities but poses risks of over-reliance that could undermine critical thinking and learning, and hinder internalization of new skills. Suggested mitigations include delegating only non-essential tasks and fostering critical mindsets, with AI positioned as an enhancer rather than a replacement of human intelligence. AI may also reform the social division of labor by reducing knowledge scarcity and blurring job boundaries, potentially threatening the middle class and social stability. In work and business, AI may drive the rise of a gig economy offering flexibility but lacking labor protections, and shift collaboration toward dynamic, network-based partnerships. For social science research, LLMs can synthesize data, automate analysis, and aid theory development, though challenges include biases, misinformation risks, and questions about originality. On governance, challenges include industry-government communication gaps, inconsistent international regulations, and risks like jailbreaking that emerge only in real-world use. The passage calls for top-down partnerships among industry, academia, and policymakers, combined with bottom-up issue reporting, to ensure human-centered, safe AI development. The document concludes with references and acknowledgments of contributors from Microsoft Research Asia and collaborating institutions.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on October 25, 2018, announcing its third quarter 2018 financial results. The filing includes a press release (Exhibit 99.1) and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures (Exhibit 99.2). The report was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The TLV32xx comparator family documentation provides usage guidelines and application information. Unused channel inputs must not be tied together; instead, they should be connected to a voltage within the input range providing at least 50mV differential. The devices contain 1.8mV of internal hysteresis, with the transfer curve defined by VTH, VOS, and VHYST. The TLV321x features a push-pull output that sources and sinks current, must never be connected to another output, and unused outputs should be left floating. The TLV322x has an open-drain output allowing pull-up to external voltages up to 5.5V, with recommended pull-up currents of 100µA to 1mA; unused open-drain outputs can float or be tied to V-. Inputs and outputs include internal ESD protection, with input voltages limited to 0.2V beyond the rails and current limited to 10mA. A Power-On Reset circuit holds the output low for up to 32µs after V+ crosses 1.65V. Propagation delay increases as overdrive voltage decreases, particularly below 100mV. External hysteresis can be added via positive feedback using resistor networks in inverting or non-inverting configurations. A low-side current sensing application is described, requiring an alert when the amplifier output exceeds 1.1V. Layout recommendations include 0.1µF bypass capacitors at supply pins, minimizing output-input coupling, and treating outputs as high-speed logic. The document also covers support resources, trademarks, ESD handling cautions, and mechanical/packaging information.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC dated March 19, 2020, under Item 7.01 (Regulation FD Disclosure), stating that it published a press release that day, attached as Exhibit 99.1. The information is furnished, not deemed filed, under the Exchange Act. Tesla, a Delaware company headquartered in Palo Alto, California, has common stock trading as TSLA on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. The report was signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn.

Rivers State Governor Nyesom Wike, during a courtesy visit by US Ambassador to Nigeria William Symington, called for a US Visa Office in Port Harcourt to serve the South-South and South-East. He described the NDDC as a fundraising commission for politicians, alleging corruption and that rerun elections in Rivers State were funded by it for the APC. He said the NDDC ignored 2016 project requests and reneged on the Mother and Child Hospital agreement despite the state paying N800 million. He also called for the Ogoni land cleanup and sought US partnerships in agriculture, oil and gas, and industrialization.

In this MIT lecture, a professor discusses possible pathways to nuclear war, comparing the near-certain danger of climate change with nuclear war's low daily but cumulatively higher probability, which would be catastrophic and could cause global consequences such as nuclear winter. He identifies two main pathways to war: an accidental launch between the US and Russia, potentially from Early Warning system malfunction or cyber attack, and escalation from conventional war between India and Pakistan, with North Korea's use of a weapon considered less likely. He argues fear and distrust drove the nuclear buildup, exemplified by Mutual Assured Destruction, and questions whether deterrence alone explains the absence of nuclear war since 1945. He reviews the Non-Proliferation Treaty, noting tension over Article VI's disarmament obligation, the four states outside the treaty (Israel, India, Pakistan, North Korea), and Iran negotiations, which he views as the best feasible solution given Iran's acceptance of rigorous IAEA inspections. He assesses Obama's record as mixed—praising the Prague speech and New START inspections while criticizing hair-trigger alert, weapons modernization, and lack of engagement with North Korea. He highlights Pakistan's aggressive deployment posture and risk of rogue field commanders, and argues nuclear abolition is desirable though unlikely, emphasizing risk minimization rather than elimination. He finds some optimism in the CTBT monitoring system, which detected North Korean tests, and in public opinion and arms control organizations.

Coach Vigneault spoke after a playoff loss. He had not yet personally spoken with Dan, who misplayed a bounce, though assistants had, and said the team must move on. Having watched parts of the game, he stressed his team cannot beat this opponent unless everyone brings their "A game," calling the opponent one of the best he has seen. He felt the first period was competitive but the third was not good enough. He praised Johnny, a consistent defenseman who skates well with the puck, and Rick, who has competed hard, used his size, and posted the team's most positive scoring chances for and against. He described the opponent as experienced, structured, skilled and physical, executing its game plan without deviation and hard to exploit—unlike previous opponents Philadelphia, Pittsburgh and Montreal. He said the goaltender kept the team in a game that was one shot away, and the group can be better; the team will make adjustments and focus on the next game, needing compete level, execution, adherence to the plan, and strengths like speed. He also praised a player's phenomenal stamina as his best defensive-group player.

CPRE Bedfordshire has criticized Central Bedfordshire Council's claim that 44,000–55,000 new homes are needed over 20 years, citing a Freedom of Information request showing 60% would house people moving into the area. A 2017 assessment identified a need of 32,000 dwellings, later increased by 7,400 homes for Luton plus up to 20% contingency. CPRE calls this unsustainable given strained infrastructure. CBC says Government rules require planning based on migration trends, natural change, and affordability.

President Andrew Johnson transmits to the House of Representatives correspondence with General U.S. Grant concerning Grant's relinquishment of the War Office. In a letter dated February 10, 1868, Johnson accuses Grant of misrepresenting their conversations, asserts that Grant accepted the position of Secretary of War ad interim with the secret intent to defeat the President's purpose of keeping Edwin M. Stanton out of office, and criticizes Grant's refusal to obey the President's order regarding War Department communications issued in the President's name. Johnson includes statements from five Cabinet members present at a January 14, 1868 Cabinet meeting, most of whom corroborate his account of the conversation with Grant. Grant replies on February 11, disclaiming any intent to disobey legal orders from the President and explaining that he merely offered an interpretation of an ambiguous order concerning orders issued by Secretary Stanton. Accompanying documents show Stanton continuing to act as Secretary of War and requesting military assistance from Grant on behalf of other departments.

The passage urges creation of a secretary of commerce with a Cabinet seat, supported by leading commercial bodies, and recommends endowing the department with large powers to supervise interstate corporations. It advocates a reciprocity treaty with Cuba, noting the United States vacated Cuban soil on May 20 and that the Platt amendment established closer political relations, making economic benefits appropriate. A convention with Great Britain for reciprocal trade with Newfoundland, similar to one negotiated by former Secretary of State Blaine, is to be submitted to the Senate. The passage notes warfare among civilized powers is diminishing, favors arbitration where possible, and praises The Hague tribunal, which the United States and Mexico were first to use with satisfactory results. Hawaiian fire claims are commended to Congress. Finally, it endorses building an isthmian canal at Panama, with title available from the French canal company and negotiations pending with Colombia, as a continuing policy.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on October 20, 2016, announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2016 via a press release furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration and Chief Accounting Officer.

Woodstock grief specialists Vicki Travnicek and Nicole Bruder of the Surviving Suicide Grief Support Group offer strategies for coping with loss during the holidays, including limiting events, having an exit plan, expressing emotions, practicing self-care, and creating new traditions while keeping old ones. The group, which has supported people for 20 years and met at Smith Leroy since May 2017, is led by trained peer volunteers and meets twice monthly. Additional grief programs are offered in Woodstock and Ingersoll.

This study explored medical students' perceptions of a curriculum-based resilience skills building course at Mohammed Bin Rashid University of Medicine and Health Sciences in Dubai, UAE. Noting that medical students are prone to stress, burnout, and psychological distress—heightened by the COVID-19 pandemic—and that few MENA-region programs proactively address resilience, the researchers implemented a six-hour course during the first clinical year of the MBBS program, designed according to constructivism experiential learning theory to foster self-directed learning. Using a qualitative phenomenological design, the researchers analyzed reflective essays submitted by 37 of 38 enrolled Year 4 students through Braun and Clarke's six-step thematic analysis with NVivo software. Analysis yielded three interlinked themes—the "3As of Building Resilience": Awareness (students' understanding of resilience and its relevance), Application (practical use of techniques such as mindfulness, meditation, and cognitive reframing), and Appraisal (evaluation of resilience building, the course, and its exercises). Students generally valued the course, reporting improved stress management, self-awareness, emotional regulation, sleep, and wellbeing, though some cited challenges including time constraints, required effort, and initial skepticism. The study concludes that integrating resilience skills building into medical curricula, particularly when anchored in constructivist experiential learning theory, is likely to be positively appraised and supports developing similar contextualized learning opportunities for future healthcare workers. Limitations include the single-institution cohort, the qualitative-only design, assessment of efficacy rather than effectiveness, and potential social desirability bias.

North Carolina lost 38-10 to Clemson, falling to 2-3 and 0-3 against Power 4 teams, having been outscored 120-33. Coach Bill Belichick said he will stay the course, blaming self-inflicted mistakes, execution, and coaching while taking his share of responsibility. GM Mike Lombardi's letter to donors described the season as a rebuild; Belichick downplayed that label but told recruits the program is being built. Receiver Shipp rejected the rebuild notion, saying he came to win games. Belichick said the best players will play as UNC prepares for Cal.

This article describes an undergraduate course, "All Means All: Inclusive Teaching for Students with Disabilities," designed to integrate advocacy as a recurring theme rather than a standalone lesson. Noting that advocacy is a professional responsibility of special education teachers and central to the field's origins, the authors present course structures—including advocacy-related learning goals, weekly TED Talk viewings, low-stakes reflection assignments, a jigsaw activity on special education law cases, an in-class debate on full inclusion, and a week focused on disability policy and advocacy history—all scaffolded toward a final TED Talk presentation and paper arguing a position on inclusive education. The authors argue that advocacy skills can be taught and should be embedded in every pre-service special education course, citing benefits such as reducing the burden on novice teachers, preparing them for systemic barriers, and bridging the research-to-practice gap. They also present Fisher and Miller's ten steps for legislative advocacy. A narrative thread follows Madison, a first-year student who completes the course, later becomes a special education teacher, and seeks her former instructor's guidance on sustaining advocacy efforts through professional connections and Council for Exceptional Children resources.

Youth mental health needs are urgent, with 40% of young people reporting persistent feelings of sadness or hopelessness and many young adults unable to access care. The authors argue that community-based organizations and out-of-school-time programs—such as summer camps, mentoring, sports leagues, and after-school clubs—where young people already build trusted relationships, represent an untapped opportunity to expand support. Rather than turning these programs into clinics, the goal is to equip staff to recognize, respond to, and refer youth in need. Research indicates young people are increasingly open about mental health, with over 80% recommending expanded counseling through schools and community organizations. Staff already provide informal support but often lack training and infrastructure, which is unsustainable. The authors call on funders to invest in strategic planning, staff training, partnerships with mental health providers, and frontline worker well-being, positioning community organizations to complement school-based efforts.

Avoyelles Parish is projected to spend $8,123 per student in state and local revenues for 2017-18, second-lowest among Louisiana's 69 districts, with its local share of $2,102 also second-lowest. The state average is $9,015 per student, below 2015's $10,888. The Minimum Foundation Program provides a $3,961 minimum, weighted toward poorer districts, with added funds for special education and other categories. A Senate resolution asks BESE's MFP Task Force to report on education costs by Feb. 1, 2018.

In this lecture, a substitute professor discusses regulating digital platforms. He contrasts "too much cooperation" issues among competitors (patent pools, data pools, collective negotiation, common ownership, algorithmic collusion) with "too little cooperation," focusing on two-sided platforms serving consumers and merchants/apps. Concerns include self-preferencing, behavioral manipulation, contestability, and fair access and compensation. He argues the Chicago School view—that platforms will not discriminate because they profit from a rich ecosystem—fails for three reasons: consumer prices face a zero lower bound (negative prices invite bot arbitrage), foreclosing third-party apps can deter entry by rival platforms (as in the Microsoft–Netscape case), and a second zero lower bound on app prices yields supranormal app profits. Although platforms resemble public utilities, regulation is harder because they are global and fast-changing. The EU's Digital Markets Act designates gatekeeper platforms, imposes obligations, and relies heavily on self-execution, with enforcement location (DG Comp versus DG Connect) still undecided. Contestability tools include multihoming, portability, and interoperability; Baumol–Panzar–Willig contestability theory and entry-for-buyout concerns (Instagram, WhatsApp) are also discussed. After reviewing traditional access pricing and the ECPR, he presents a two-sided model (with Bisceglia) in which apps have negative marginal costs due to ancillary benefits b: access charges below b induce non-price foreclosure, high charges squeeze app profits, and the optimal access charge equals b, which regulators could elicit through a simple mechanism, though designing practical, simple rules remains a challenge.

Super Bowl LII between the Patriots and Eagles takes place Sunday in Minneapolis, MN. The Steelers-fan author plans to eat 50 wings and host a game thread, and poses five questions plus two bonus questions covering playoff predictions, Kirk Cousins' 2018 team, Nick Foles' completions, the coin flip, Rob Gronkowski's receiving yards, a combined scoring prediction, and Alan Faneca's Hall of Fame chances.

Recapping Senior Bowl Week: 14 respondents believe Le'Veon Bell will sign a long-term contract without being tagged; Rashaan Evans received the most votes as the desired Senior Bowl player; 18 would watch the XFL versus 7 who would not; Chris Boswell scored the Steelers' fantasy points; and Ben Roethlisberger's pick-6 was returned 79 yards in the Pro Bowl. Tom Brady's MVP win was revealed via a photo. Alan Tman leads the contest leaderboard with 48.5 points, a position held since Week 8.

Executive Order 11905, issued by President Ford in February 1976 after congressional investigations of CIA activities, replaced the 40 Committee with the Operations Advisory Group (OAG), required formal meetings and periodic reviews of covert operations, and banned political assassinations and domestic intelligence involvement. President Carter replaced the OAG with the NSC's Special Coordination Committee (SCC), formalized in EO 11985 (1977) and reaffirmed in EO 12036 (1978), which made the Attorney General and OMB Director full members rather than observers. The SCC-Intelligence established the Special Activities Working Group (SAWG), chaired by David Aaron, which fell out of use by late 1979, when an interagency working group chaired by Aaron—known by names including the Black Chamber—handled covert action. The Carter administration also used "worldwide" findings for lower-risk operations, with "Perspectives" documents drafted by the CIA and cleared by the State Department; riskier operations required separate findings or MONs.

This is the first lecture of MIT course 18.100A, Real Analysis. The instructor states the course has two purposes: gaining experience reading and writing proofs, and proving statements about real numbers, functions, and limits. The lecture begins with definitions of sets, elements, the empty set, and basic logical notation, followed by examples including the natural numbers, integers, rationals, and reals, noting that a first goal of the course is to rigorously define the real numbers. Set operations—union, intersection, set difference, and complement—are defined, and DeMorgan's Laws are stated, with the first property proved by showing mutual subset inclusion. The instructor explains the general structure of proofs: assuming hypotheses and using logic, definitions, and calculations to derive the conclusion. Induction is then introduced, taking the well-ordering property of the natural numbers as an axiom and proving the induction theorem by contradiction. Two examples demonstrate induction: the geometric sum formula 1 + c + ... + c^n = (1 − c^(n+1))/(1 − c) for c ≠ 1, and the inequality (1 + c)^n ≥ 1 + nc for c ≥ −1.

New computer modeling and a reanalysis of decades of data indicate that Uranus emits about 15% more energy than it receives from the Sun, contradicting the long-held belief—based on a single Voyager 2 measurement from 1986—that the planet has no internal heat. Researchers, including Patrick Irwin of the University of Oxford and NASA's Amy Simon, built a model incorporating observations of Uranus' atmosphere from ground- and space-based telescopes to calculate the planet's energy budget. The findings, published in the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, align with a separate NASA-funded study. Uranus still emits far less heat than Neptune, and the results may inform understanding of the solar system's history and similarly sized exoplanets.

Oclaro Inc (NASDAQ:OCLR) shares fell 0.99% in the most recent session, closing at $9.04. Analysts project a 52-week price target of $9.27 based on 13 opinions, with a high of $11.25 and a low of $6.50. The stock has an average brokerage recommendation of 2.38, with 2 analysts rating Buy, 3 Outperform, 9 Hold, and none rating Underperform or Sell. Its ATR-14 is 0.29, weekly volatility is 2.50%, monthly volatility is 3.07%, and RSI is 55.48.
