This study developed and externally validated machine learning (ML) models—logistic regression, random forest, and boosted tree—to predict restriction from spirometric, demographic, and anthropometric data, addressing limitations of the ERS/ATS-recommended use of the FVC lower limit of normal (LLN) to exclude restriction. Using 42,462 PFTs from one academic health system for development and 24,524 PFTs from another for validation, the random forest model achieved the best performance, with a negative predictive value (NPV) of 88.3% versus 72.7% for the FVC LLN. The ML models also improved equity: among non-Hispanic Black patients, the NPV rose from 49.5% (FVC LLN) to 74.6% (random forest). However, the random forest model excluded the need for static lung volume measurements in fewer tests (56.7% vs 78.4%) and was poorly calibrated. Decision curve analysis favored the random forest model over most thresholds. Limitations include use of academic health system data, potential ascertainment bias, and limited racial diversity in the validation dataset. The authors conclude that ML models improve both the accuracy and equity of PFT interpretation compared with the FVC LLN.

In G. M. Cox v. George W. Burnham, a certiorari proceeding, the court reviewed a district judge's order granting pharmacist P. H. Bell a permit to sell intoxicating liquor in Benton county. Bell filed his application in March 1901; a remonstrance by the plaintiff and others was filed, but the application was not heard at the April 1901 term and was continued to the September term, where a hearing was held and the permit granted. The plaintiff contended the defendant judge lacked jurisdiction because the hearing occurred at a term subsequent to that at which the application was filed. The court held that liquor statutes are construed under general rules, subject to Code section 2431's directive to prevent evasion; that section 2389's timing provisions are not mandatory and do not abridge the court's control over the business of the term; that adjournment of a term does not operate as a dismissal or deprive the court of jurisdiction; and that, absent a showing to the contrary, cause for continuance is presumed. The proceedings were dismissed.

Tesla, Inc.'s Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2018 describes a company that designs, manufactures, and sells fully electric vehicles—the Model S, Model X, and mass-market Model 3—along with energy storage products (Powerwall 2 and Powerpack 2) and solar energy systems, including Solar Roof. Future vehicles planned include Model Y, the Tesla Semi, a pickup truck, and a new Roadster. Vehicles are sold directly through company-owned stores and galleries, supported by the Supercharger charging network, with warranties of four years/50,000 miles for new vehicles and eight-year battery and drive unit warranties. Manufacturing occurs in Fremont and Lathrop, California; Tilburg, Netherlands; and Gigafactory 1 near Reno, Nevada, where Tesla partners with Panasonic on lithium-ion cell production. Solar panels are produced at Gigafactory 2 in Buffalo, New York. Construction of Gigafactory Shanghai began in January 2019, with Model 3 production for China expected by the end of 2019. Tesla operates two reportable segments—automotive and energy generation and storage—and had 48,817 full-time employees as of December 31, 2018. It earns and sells tradable regulatory credits such as ZEV credits and SRECs. Competition includes established automakers, energy storage companies such as AES, Siemens, LG Chem, and Samsung, and solar installers such as Vivint Solar, Sunrun, Trinity Solar, and SunPower. Risk factors highlight past production delays, dependence on Model 3 ramp targets, reliance on single-source suppliers, Gigafactory expansion challenges, potential product defects, and difficulties managing rapid growth and manufacturing costs.

Asian stocks were shaky and the Chinese yuan hovered near 11-month lows on Wednesday as investors worried about a possible Sino-U.S. trade war ahead of a July 6 deadline for U.S. tariffs on $34 billion of Chinese goods, which Beijing has vowed to match. Wall Street fell on Tuesday, with technology shares under pressure; Facebook, Tesla and Micron declined, and the Micron injunction news hit chip-related shares in Japan. The yuan traded at 6.6715 per dollar after China's central bank said it would keep the currency at a stable level. The Mexican peso surged 2.6 percent, while major currencies were little changed. Oil prices were supported by a larger-than-expected fall in U.S. stockpiles, while copper stayed near nine-month lows on trade friction worries.

The author screens David Fish's January 2017 "All CCC" list (684 companies, excluding REITs and MLPs) using the Dugan Stock Scoring System, then applies filters including a minimum 2.25% yield, $5B market cap, 5% most-recent dividend increase, 5% estimated EPS growth for next year and five years, maximum 70% payout ratio, maximum debt/equity of 1, and a minimum Dugan Score of 50. The Dugan Scoring System evaluates stocks across Risk, Value, Past Performance, and Future Performance Expectations, focusing on current conditions and expected future performance rather than past returns, and provides a balanced view of strengths and weaknesses. A bonus or penalty based on three brokers' sector weightings is then applied. The 2017 system and filters produced 21 highest-scoring January 2017 CCC companies. The author discloses long positions in several mentioned stocks.

The East of England Ambulance Service NHS Trust, which serves Bedfordshire, has been rated as Requires Improvement overall by the Care Quality Commission following a March inspection, though it was rated Outstanding for caring. Inspectors found progress in safeguarding, Mental Capacity Act understanding and incident reporting, but the trust did not meet national ambulance response standards, with winter delays causing serious incidents. Staff morale was low, with reports of late shift finishes and disengagement from senior management. The trust must improve response times, apply procedures consistently, review risk registers and support staff. Chief Executive Robert Morton acknowledged room for improvement but welcomed recognition of staff caring, noting £11.5m of additional funding this year.

Coach DeBoer says the team has faced similar playoff deficits before, against the Rangers and Philadelphia, and is capable of winning several games in a row once it gets the first one. He says lineup changes were considered but rejected, as changes are only made if they improve the team and there is no need to panic. He notes the team created quality chances against Los Angeles, including opportunities for Zajac, Kovalchuk, and Elias, but credits the opposing goaltender and team, similar to past frustration with Lundqvist and Florida's power play. He expresses confidence based on that prior experience. On travel, the team adjusted to the Pacific time zone, with input on scheduling decisions. He praises the officiating, questions a momentum-changing call and wanted an explanation, says he is not disappointed in his team's effort, and stresses the need to score more than one goal.

Temple Grandin will present Livestock Handling and Animal Behavior at a Feb. 23 breakfast at the Tehama District Fairground in Red Bluff, sponsored by Shasta College Ag Leadership Club and UC Cooperative Extension. Grandin is a Colorado State University professor and author.

Apple Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended March 30, 2019 reports Q2 net sales of $58.0 billion, down 5% from the prior-year quarter, driven by lower iPhone sales and partially offset by higher Services and Wearables, Home and Accessories sales. Net income was $11.6 billion ($2.46 diluted EPS) versus $13.8 billion a year earlier; six-month net sales were $142.3 billion with net income of $31.5 billion. Total assets were $342.0 billion and shareholders' equity $105.9 billion as of March 30, 2019. During the quarter, Apple adopted new accounting standards, including ASU 2016-16, which added $2.7 billion of net deferred tax assets. The company held $225.4 billion in cash and marketable securities, including $19.3 billion restricted pending the European Commission State Aid Decision appeal (€13.1 billion plus €1.2 billion interest held in escrow). Debt consisted of $11.9 billion in commercial paper and $101.2 billion in term debt. Apple repurchased $24.0 billion of common stock and paid $3.4 billion in dividends during the quarter; on April 30, 2019, the share repurchase authorization was increased from $100 billion to $175 billion. Legal matters include the VirnetX patent verdicts, an April 2019 settlement with Qualcomm, and iOS performance management litigation. The quarter saw releases of updated iPads, iMac, and AirPods, and announcements of Apple News+, Apple Card, Apple Arcade, a new Apple TV app, and Apple TV+.

Israel and Canada signed a modernized Canada-Israel Free Trade Agreement in Montreal, replacing their 1997 agreement. Signed by Canadian Trade Minister Francois-Phillippe Champagne and Israeli Economy Minister Eli Cohen, the revised deal eliminates duties on thousands of additional products, including fresh fruit and canned goods. It adds chapters on labor, environment, trade and gender, and small and medium-sized enterprises, plus provisions on corporate social responsibility. The agreement takes effect after ratification by both parliaments and aims to double trade between the two countries.

NVIDIA's Turing GPU architecture achieves real-time ray tracing via new dedicated RT Cores, combined with RTX software and filtering algorithms, delivering photorealistic rendering with accurate shadows, reflections, and refractions. Paired with Microsoft's DirectML and DirectX Raytracing APIs, it enables rapid deployment of AI and ray tracing in games. Turing also adds advanced shading features, inherits Volta's CUDA enhancements, and its flagship TU102 ships in the GeForce RTX 2080 Ti and Quadro RTX 6000.

Democrats seek an independent Russia investigation after Flynn's exit; the Trump administration questions a two-state solution as Netanyahu visits; Malaysian police arrest a woman in Kim Jong Nam's death; NATO ministers meet in Brussels; cracks were found at the Oroville Dam; a study finds most drivers take risks; a Boeing union vote proceeds; Swedish produce gets laser labels; Kate Upton covers Sports Illustrated again; Rumor wins Westminster.

This study presents a meta-analysis, conducted according to PRISMA guidelines, examining the effectiveness of AI-related technologies in education. Thirteen studies from eight countries (Taiwan, Australia, Turkey, China, Iran, the Netherlands, Spain, and Switzerland), with sample sizes ranging from 20 to 794 participants, were included. Literature was searched in Google Scholar, ERIC, and Scopus for English-language, peer-reviewed empirical studies published between January 2015 and July 2024.

The overall effect size for AI-related technologies in education was 0.86 (95% CI [0.45, 1.27], p < 0.0001), indicating a large, statistically significant positive effect. Chatbots and generative AI showed the highest effect size (1.02, 95% CI [0.45, 1.59], p < 0.0001). Online learning and virtual reality yielded an effect size of 0.79 (95% CI [-0.04, 1.62], p < 0.07), while learning management systems with AI platforms showed 0.62 (95% CI [0.03, 1.21], p < 0.05).

The researchers also applied novel algorithmic approaches, including Naive Bayes-based algorithms (which produced a positive result), TF-IDF-based weighting of effect sizes (0.86), BERT-based search algorithms (0.84), and a weighted hybrid model combining random and fixed effects (0.88, 95% CI [0.48, 1.29], p < 0.0001), all supporting a positive overall effect.

Substantial heterogeneity (I² ranging from 54.03% to 93.23%) and publication bias were observed, suggesting effectiveness varies by implementation context, student characteristics, and application type. The study concludes that AI technologies, particularly chatbots and generative AI, can enhance educational outcomes, while recommending careful context-specific implementation, larger and more diverse future studies, further methodological development, and consideration of these findings by policymakers.

As temperatures fall in the UK, infections like colds and flu spread more easily, but diet can offer protection. Food provides the nutrients and energy needed to fight infection, while poor nutritional choices can slow recovery and worsen symptoms. Fruit and vegetables have the most impact, supplying vitamins and minerals that support immunity; eating a variety of colours ensures a range of nutrients. Registered nutritional therapist Libby Linford explains that fruit and vegetables provide prebiotic fibres for beneficial bacteria and key nutrients such as vitamins A and C, magnesium, and zinc. Protein supports growth, repair, and immunity, and deficiency can weaken defences by disrupting T cells and antibodies. Herbs and spices like ginger and turmeric offer anti-inflammatory and anti-bacterial benefits. Probiotics from fermented foods support gut health and immunity, while nuts and seeds provide minerals, fatty acids, and vitamin E for cell repair after infection.

A Danish study found children of older mothers display fewer behavioural, social and emotional difficulties at ages seven and 11, though the difference disappears by age 15. Older mothers worry less during pregnancy, have more positive attitudes toward their children, and are more tolerant and emotionally stable, scolding and disciplining less—attributed to 'psychological maturity'. The study used 4,741 mothers from the Danish Longitudinal Survey of Children. Professor Dion Sommer noted older mothers face greater health risks, including miscarriage, premature birth, and children with deformities, so both physical and psychosocial factors should be considered.

The speaker, apparently a hockey coach, discusses a game loss. Fredrik underwent X-rays with results expected by day's end; he returned to finish the game after missing a couple of shifts. The team had a poor start and a poor passing game, causing turnovers that stalled the offense. The power play struggled, taking one-timers from poor angles against a team that blocks shots well. The coach stresses the importance of winning the second game to even the series, recalling Montreal's loss to the Rangers during a three-cup run. He declines to blame a single player, noting that heavy power-play and penalty-killing duty gave Yzerman, Fedorov, and Shanahan excessive ice time while others played under ten minutes. He notes Carolina clears the puck quickly, and Detroit must correct its entries, improve its forecheck, and get the puck deeper into the offensive zone.
Scientists created functional human eggs from skin cells, potentially helping infertile people have children.

Niu Technologies, a maker of urban mobility products such as e-bikes and scooters, has posted significant stock gains in 2025, driven by strong growth in recent quarters. However, the author argues this growth must continue to justify the rally and current valuations, which is not assured, and various factors could disrupt the growth expectations priced into the stock. As a result, the author is neutral on NIU stock with a hold rating.

This patent application describes CAR T cell therapies with enhanced efficacy through disruption of methylcytosine dioxygenase genes (Tet1, Tet2, Tet3). The invention provides immune effector cells (T cells or NK cells) engineered to express a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) comprising an antigen-binding domain, transmembrane domain, and intracellular signaling domain, wherein expression and/or function of Tet genes is reduced or eliminated. Disruption of a Tet gene allele decreases 5-hydroxymethylcytosine levels, enhancing CAR T cell proliferation, cytokine production, and degranulation. Tumor antigens targeted include CD19 and numerous others. Tet inhibition methods include gene editing systems (CRISPR/Cas9, TALEN, zinc finger nucleases), siRNA/shRNA, small molecules, and dominant negative proteins. The invention also covers methods for treating hematologic cancers and solid tumors, manufacturing CAR-expressing cells with Tet disruption, and vectors encoding both CAR and Tet inhibitor sequences. Experimental data from a CLL patient treated with CD19 CAR T cells showed the CAR19 gene inserted into the Tet2 gene between exons 9 and 10, disrupting Tet2 function and resulting in favorable clonal expansion of CAR T cells. Additional figures demonstrate that TET2 knockdown reduces 5-hmc levels, expands Tscm T cells, and affects cytokine production and proliferation in CAR T cells.

Russian math, an after-school enrichment trend rooted in Soviet teaching traditions, is rapidly growing in the United States. The Russian School of Mathematics, co-founded by Russian immigrant Inessa Rifkin in Newton in 1997, has 22,000 students across 40 branches, including 15 in Massachusetts. The curriculum emphasizes reasoning and deep understanding over memorization, introducing algebra and geometry early. Parents enroll children for reasons including dissatisfaction with school curricula, a child's love of math, and fear of falling behind peers. Classes cost about $2,000 per year. The trend poses challenges for American schools, including students who have already covered new material, potential overconfidence, and possible widening of achievement gaps between families who can and cannot afford the classes. However, towns with Russian math programs have seen honors class participation increase. American researchers have not extensively studied Russian math teaching methods.

A Mendelian randomization (MR) study using 11 single-nucleotide polymorphisms as instrumental variables, derived from genome-wide association study data, assessed the causal effect of genetically determined pericardial adipose tissue (PAT) on multiple cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). The results showed genetically determined PAT was significantly associated with increased risks of CVD, heart failure, hypertension, coronary heart disease, ischemic heart disease, ischemic stroke, and venous thromboembolism, while no significant association was found with cardiac arrhythmias, atrial fibrillation, aortic aneurysm, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, myocardial infarction, stroke subtypes, or subarachnoid hemorrhage. A two-step mediation analysis indicated hypertension partially mediated the associations between PAT and CVD, heart failure, coronary heart disease, ischemic heart disease, and ischemic stroke, with mediated proportions ranging from approximately 13% to 19%. The authors suggest PAT may serve as a potential therapeutic target and that antihypertensive drugs could be used conjunctly to provide cardiovascular benefits, particularly for people with obesity who have greater PAT accumulation. Limitations include an exclusively European study population, sample overlap between datasets, inability to perform multivariable MR, and small case numbers for some outcomes.

In October 2001, Enron disclosed that the Securities and Exchange Commission had requested information about its dealings with partnerships (LJM Cayman and LJM2 Co-Investment) formerly run by CFO Andrew Fastow. The informal inquiry, originating from the SEC's Fort Worth enforcement office, followed Enron's $1.01 billion third-quarter write-off, a $618 million loss, and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity from unwinding the partnerships. Enron's stock fell more than 20% to $20.65, and Moody's placed its debt on review for possible downgrade. Chairman and CEO Kenneth Lay said the company would cooperate fully and maintained the transactions were proper and properly disclosed. Fastow had resigned from the partnerships amid conflict-of-interest concerns, having reportedly earned millions in fees; Treasurer Jeffrey McMahon had earlier raised internal concerns with then-President Jeffrey Skilling, who did not share them. Skilling resigned as CEO in August. Investors worried about other financing vehicles, including Marlin Water Trust II and Whitewing, which could require share issuance and dilute holdings if Enron's stock fell and its credit rating dropped below investment grade. Multiple lawsuits were filed, including a class action against Enron, Lay, Skilling, and Fastow alleging securities fraud. Analysts criticized Enron's unclear disclosure, noting the equity reduction was omitted from its earnings release. Janus was Enron's largest institutional holder. Separately, U.S. stocks rallied, with the Dow rising 172.92 points to 9,377.03.

Sexual harassment is commonplace in Nigerian universities and workplaces. Professor Richard Akindele was found guilty of soliciting sex from a student and dismissed by OAU's University Council. OAU's swift handling is commended as an example for other institutions, which should implement measures to punish exploitative lecturers and protect students, while female students engaging in such acts should focus on their studies.

Tom Evans, father of terminally ill 23-month-old Alfie Evans, said his son's life support was withdrawn at Alder Hey Children's Hospital, but the toddler has been breathing unassisted for nine hours. After Tom told doctors the situation seemed "unlawful", they re-intervened, providing oxygen and water. Alfie's mother, Kate James, is sleeping beside him. Tom believes Alfie will need some form of life support within the next couple of hours. Kate posted on Facebook that Alfie had been allowed oxygen and water.

This June 4, 2001 email from Ann Schmidt compiles news coverage of Enron. Key items include: White House adviser Karl Rove held $100,000–$250,000 in Enron stock (among other holdings) while awaiting ethics approval to divest; other officials, including Larry Lindsey (who received $50,000 from Enron for consulting), Lewis Libby, Clay Johnson, and Condoleezza Rice, also had energy company financial ties. Saudi Arabia signed agreements with nine oil firms, including Enron, worth at least $25 billion to develop natural gas fields—the first major foreign investment in its energy sector since 1975 nationalization, with Exxon Mobil leading two projects and Royal Dutch/Shell leading a third. Enron's Dabhol Power project in India faced escalating disputes: the Maharashtra State Electricity Board stopped buying power and terminated its contract over $48 million in unpaid bills, and Indian and international lenders met in Singapore to determine the future of the $2.9–3 billion project. Fitch revised India's sovereign ratings outlook to negative, possibly linked to the Enron dispute, though analysts called concerns overstated. Nigeria's President Obasanjo criticized Enron for "poor performance," bad faith, and exorbitant pricing on the Lagos power project. Spectron brokered the UK's first post-NETA spark spread deal between Powergen and Enron. Additional items included a San Francisco Chronicle opinion piece criticizing energy companies, an editorial predicting a future energy glut, Indian Power Minister Prabhu's comments on power reforms and contract sanctity, an analysis of India–Bush administration relations noting Enron chairman Kenneth Lay's friendship with Bush, and Enron Japan CEO Joseph Hirl's remarks that Japan's electricity market lacks genuine competition, with prices about 400 percent higher than the U.S.

A hockey player discusses preparing for a road playoff game, saying the team aims to set its own tone, expects a desperate opponent, and values a rare practice day for rest and adjustments. He stresses being aware of the home crowd's energy while trying to establish their own game. He praises a versatile teammate who embraces any role, competes hard, and is currently being rewarded with goals. He acknowledges needing to win more faceoffs and execute against an opponent that pressures to force mistakes. He notes injuries affect both teams, experience helps avoid looking ahead, and credits a stronger third period last game. He also praises an intense former-player coach who shares valuable details.

The study developed a metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) workflow combining HostEL (human background depletion) and AmpRE (single-tube DNA/RNA library preparation) to detect bacteria, fungi, and DNA/RNA viruses from plasma. Analytical validation using spiked ZymoBIOMICS standards demonstrated detection down to 70,000 cells/mL with 96% sensitivity and 96% specificity using HostEL treatment. Clinical validation on 42 patient plasma samples showed 93% agreement with qPCR results. The workflow was tested on iSeq 100 and MiniSeq platforms, achieving rapid turnaround (potentially 13–27 hours) with low-depth sequencing, reducing cost and processing time compared to conventional mNGS approaches.

Cruzin' for Life, a Santa Maria-based nonprofit, retrofitted a transport van that has served more than 2,600 cancer patients and logged over 34,000 miles in its first year, providing free rides to Mission Hope Cancer Center in Santa Maria and surrounding areas. The idea arose after a board member's relative was diagnosed with cancer. The group raised $69,000, aided by a $36,000 silent donation from Santa Maria Energy, and continues fundraising through its annual crab feed, which brought in $32,000 last year. Patients call directly or are referred by staff, and a second van may be considered if need and funding allow.

Indian troops killed three youth in a Shopian operation, blasting a mosque and four houses. Protests followed, with civilians injured by pellet firing. Two soldiers were killed and three troops injured in attacks. The joint resistance leadership opposed attempts to undermine Jammu and Kashmir's disputed status, and the Hurriyat forum chairman said the BJP and RSS were challenging Article 35A. A civilian injured in an explosion died.

The 2025–26 season marks Jim Montgomery's first full season as Blues head coach, after he led St. Louis to the first round of the playoffs following a mid-season takeover. The Blues open at Enterprise Center on Oct. 9, with seven of their first 11 games at home and rivalry matchups within the first two weeks. The schedule pauses Feb. 5–25, 2026 for the Winter Olympics, making March and April packed with crucial games. With 26 division games, key questions include tightening the defense, young forwards' development, and how quickly Montgomery's system translates into wins against Central Division opponents.

A woman declared dead by paramedics after a car crash near Carletonville, South Africa, on June 24 was found alive in a mortuary refrigerator hours later. The crash killed two of three occupants. The ambulance service said proper checks were done and has launched an investigation.

San Juan mayor Carmen Yulin Cruz called new death toll estimates for Puerto Rico after Hurricane Maria "a day of collective mourning," saying the government had not told the truth. Harvard researchers estimated 4,645 "excess deaths" between Sept. 20 and Dec. 31, compared to the official toll of 64, with a margin of error of plus or minus 3,852 and a likely figure of about 5,000. Cruz, a critic of the Trump administration, said the island is not prepared for the upcoming hurricane season.

A backtest of the NIFTY 50, India's main index of its 50 largest companies, indicates a positive end-of-month effect comparable to the turn-of-the-month effect documented in the US stock market. Using Yahoo!finance data from 2007 onward, the optimal exit was found at the close of the second trading day of the new month, with the best profit factor from entering on the fifth last trading day. A strategy going long at that entry and exiting at that close, compounded from 100,000, achieved a 10.5% CAGR with a 26% maximum drawdown, outperforming buy and hold despite only 30% market exposure. While somewhat curve fitted, results appear reasonably robust.

This study reviews literature on the benefits and potential connections between drama in education and STEAM education, and presents a pilot case study examining whether drama is a useful method in STEAM. Two research questions addressed how higher education students view dramatic activities in science or history classes and what students can achieve through such activities. Using a qualitative approach based on participant observation and detailed field notes, the study involved 19 first-year female university students at ELTE University in Budapest, Hungary, who completed two drama activities: "The Life Cycle of a Butterfly" and "Indian Caste System." Findings revealed four observations: increased creativity, group collaboration, problem-solving and thinking skills, and student motivation and involvement. Students reported enjoying the activities, expressing creativity, and working together, though some concerns arose regarding language barriers and uneven participation. The study concludes that drama can be a valuable tool in STEAM education, making learning enjoyable, boosting confidence and concentration, and supporting competence development, while noting challenges such as limited time, teacher preparedness, and institutional support. The authors acknowledge limitations, including the small sample size and narrow demographic characteristics, which restrict generalizability and call for validation in future studies.

Celtic's 2-1 win over Rangers at Ibrox left them 19 points ahead with a game in hand, set to be the biggest gap between the clubs in 91 years, since 1925-26 when Celtic won the title with 58 points (83 today) while Rangers finished sixth with 44 points (63 today). That record could be surpassed. In 1985-86, Rangers finished 15 points behind Celtic after a late-season collapse.

Ahead of CES, TrackR unveiled new Bluetooth tracking devices: the TrackR pixel, a cheaper, colorful version of the bravo; the TrackR wallet 2.0, the thinnest item-finder on the market; and the TrackR atlas, a smart plug that maps a home and works with Alexa. Priced at $24.99, $29.99, and $39.99, they launch in Spring.

This patent application describes an autonomous vehicle comprising multiple independent control systems that provide redundancy for specific safety situations. The vehicle includes a set of vehicle interfaces, an autonomous control system (AV control sub-system), and one or more auxiliary control units. The AV control sub-system uses multiple sensors and processing resources to operate the vehicle under normal conditions, performing actions such as steering, accelerating, and braking. The auxiliary control units operate independently of the AV control sub-system and of each other, using dedicated sensors, separate communication busses, and independent programming. They can function in a trajectory verification mode, receiving planned trajectory data and communicating vehicle response outputs to the AV control sub-system to verify trajectory safety, or in a failsafe/bypass mode, detecting predefined conditions or events (such as imminent collisions or AV control sub-system malfunction) and implementing predetermined responses directly through vehicle interfaces, overriding the AV control sub-system's commands. Vehicle response outputs may specify actions such as braking, steering, pulling over, or activating lights, with type and magnitude varying based on detected conditions. The auxiliary control units are optimized for reliability and may satisfy the Automotive Safety Integrity Level (ASIL) definition.

Lightning is not attracted to metal; height, pointy shape, and isolation determine where it strikes. Car tires don't provide protection—the metal roof and sides do. Lightning can strike up to 10 miles from a storm's center, even under sunny skies. It can strike the same place repeatedly, especially tall, isolated objects. Sheltering under trees during storms is dangerous. Contrary to popular belief, most leisure-related lightning deaths occur on or near water, not to golfers.

On May 2, 2016, NVIDIA Corporation announced that it and Samsung agreed to settle all pending intellectual property litigation between them. The agreement results in the immediate dismissal of all pending IP litigation in U.S. district courts, the U.S. International Trade Commission, and the U.S. Patent Office. The settlement includes licensing of a small number of patents by each company to the other, but no broad cross-licensing of patents or other compensation.

Thinking Machines Lab, a heavily funded startup cofounded by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati and other OpenAI veterans, has launched its first product, Tinker—a tool that automates the creation of custom frontier AI models through fine-tuning. Tinker lets users fine-tune open source models such as Meta's Llama and Alibaba's Qwen via a few lines of code, using supervised learning or reinforcement learning, and then download and run the resulting models. The company raised $2 billion in seed funding in July at a $12 billion valuation. Beta testers report Tinker is simpler and more capable than existing tools. API access opens Wednesday and is free for now, though charges are expected later. Murati hopes Tinker will make frontier capabilities broadly accessible and counter the trend of increasingly closed commercial AI models.

This study developed and externally validated two deep learning models using pre-treatment prostate MRI to identify extra-prostatic extension (EPE) and seminal vesicle invasion (SVI) in localized prostate cancer patients. Trained on 820 patients from Yale and tested on three held-out datasets (including community hospital and public datasets), the models achieved AUCs of 0.611–0.775 across test sets. Both imaging biomarkers were independently associated with biochemical recurrence (BCR), with adjusted hazard ratios of 1.76 (EPE) and 2.72 (SVI). The combined biomarker demonstrated improved prognostic value over either alone, with a C-index of 0.73. Integrating these biomarkers into NCCN risk groups reclassified 26.4% of patients and improved discriminatory ability (C-index from 0.592 to 0.617). Interpretability analyses (Grad-CAM, hierarchical clustering, dimensionality reduction) confirmed models identified clinically relevant features rather than spurious patterns. The biomarkers retained prognostic utility even among patients without pathologic EPE or SVI. Limitations include lack of overall survival endpoints, no comparison to tissue-based genomic classifiers, and underrepresentation of African American patients.

Amazon.com, Inc.'s Form 10-K annual report for fiscal year ended December 31, 2021 describes a business organized into three segments—North America, International, and Amazon Web Services—serving consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, content creators, and advertisers. As of December 31, 2021, Amazon employed approximately 1,608,000 full- and part-time employees. Risk factors include intense competition, international operations, fulfillment network challenges, data security, government regulation, litigation, and tax obligations. Properties totaled 570,560 thousand leased and 34,866 thousand owned square feet. Cash provided by operating activities was $46.3 billion in 2021, down from $66.1 billion in 2020; investing activities used $58.2 billion; financing activities provided $6.3 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities were $96.0 billion at year-end 2021, and cash capital expenditures were $55.4 billion. Common stock trades on Nasdaq under "AMZN," with 508,844,410 shares outstanding as of January 26, 2022.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-K annual report for fiscal year ended June 30, 2015. Microsoft is a technology company founded in 1975, operating in over 100 countries, with a mission to empower every person and organization to achieve more. Its strategy focuses on building best-in-class platforms and productivity services for a mobile-first, cloud-first world, organized around three ambitions: reinventing productivity and business processes, building the intelligent cloud platform, and creating more personal computing. The company operates in six segments: D&C Licensing, Computing and Gaming Hardware, Phone Hardware, D&C Other, Commercial Licensing, and Commercial Other. Key products include Windows, Office, Azure, Xbox, Surface, and Lumia phones. In April 2014, Microsoft acquired Nokia's Devices and Services Business. Windows 10 launched in July 2015 as a transformative release. Research and development expense was $12.0 billion in fiscal 2015 (13% of revenue), and the company holds over 57,000 patents. As of June 30, 2015, Microsoft employed approximately 118,000 people. In June 2015, management approved a restructuring plan to eliminate up to 7,800 positions, primarily in Phone Hardware. The company recorded a $5.1 billion goodwill impairment and $2.2 billion intangible asset impairment in its Phone Hardware segment in fiscal 2015. Risk factors include intense competition, execution risks in cloud services, cybersecurity threats, intellectual property challenges, regulatory scrutiny, and global operational risks. Satya Nadella serves as CEO, appointed in February 2014. As of July 27, 2015, there were approximately 8 billion shares of common stock outstanding.

Michael Flynn resigned as national security adviser after the Washington Post reported he had discussed U.S. sanctions with the Russian ambassador before Trump's inauguration. Acting Attorney General Sally Yates warned White House Counsel Donald McGahn that Flynn was vulnerable to Russian blackmail. According to CNN, President Trump was officially aware of Flynn's actions weeks before Vice President Pence, who had publicly defended Flynn, learned of them. Trump has not addressed the situation, instead criticizing illegal leaks and media coverage on Twitter. Pundits believe Flynn did not act alone, and a source described him as ill-suited for the role, having received it due to his loyalty to Trump. Flynn reportedly called the ambassador five times in one day despite previously expressing hostility toward Russia. Democrats and some Republicans support an investigation into Russian interference in the 2016 election. If Flynn testified that Trump knew of or directed the conversations, Trump would be considered complicit. McGahn may claim attorney-client privilege but could still disclose the time, place, and subject of his discussion with Trump.

The passage is from the TMS320DM814x DaVinci Digital Media Processors documentation (Texas Instruments, © 2012–2014), covering reset functions, clocking, interrupts, and peripheral information and timings.

**Reset:** The device supports multiple reset sources, including Software Global Warm Reset (initiated via the RST_GLOBAL_WARM_SW bit in the PRM_RSTCTRL register), Test Reset (TRST pin), and per-module Local Resets controlled through the PRCM. When multiple resets occur simultaneously, only the highest-priority request is processed, and the PRM_RSTST register records the last reset. Reset isolation is supported for the PCI Express subsystem and optionally for the EMAC Switch (via the ISO_CONTROL bit in the RESET_ISO register). The RSTOUT_WD_OUT pin reflects reset status, with behavior dependent on the latched BTMODE[11] value. Pin behaviors at reset (Hi-Z states, internal pull resistors, PINCNTL registers) and reset timing requirements are described. Power domains receive Warm Resets on external/emulation/software warm resets or ON-to-OFF transitions, and Cold Resets on power-on/software cold resets or OFF-to-ON transitions.

**Clocking:** Device clocks derive from reference clocks fed to on-chip PLLs and dividers. The DEV clock (typically 20 MHz, optionally 20–30 MHz under certain conditions) and optional AUX clock (20–30 MHz) can be sourced from internal oscillators with external crystals or 1.8-V LVCMOS clock inputs. An AC-coupled differential SERDES_CLKN/P clock is required for the PCIE PHY. The device contains 12 top-level and 4 embedded PLLs, which start in Bypass mode after reset; multiplier, divider, and frequency limits are specified (PLL_USB must be fixed at 960 MHz). Maximum SYSCLK and Module clock frequencies are listed.

**Interrupts:** The ARM Cortex-A8 Interrupt Controller (AINTC) handles up to 128 requests with programmable priority, generating IRQs or FIQs. The C674x DSP interrupt controller combines up to 128 events into 12 prioritized interrupts, with multiplexed event options.

**Peripherals:** Electrical data/timing is provided for two DCAN (CAN 2.0) interfaces; the EDMA controller (up to 64 channels, 512 parameter entries); Advanced Event Triggering and Trace debug features; IEEE 1149.1 JTAG (JTAG ID register value 0x0B8F 202F); the EMAC Switch (3-port gigabit switch supporting MII/GMII/RMII/RGMII, IEEE 802.3-2002 compliant) with MDIO for PHY management; GPIO (four 32-channel modules, up to 128 pins); the GPMC memory controller (NOR/NAND Flash, SRAM) with the ELM for BCH error location; an HDMI 1.3a-compliant transmitter with PCB layout guidelines; the HDVPSS video processing subsystem; video DACs (Normal and TVOUT Bypass modes); four I2C modules (specification 2.1, 10–400 Kbps); the Imaging Subsystem (parallel CAM and CSI2 interfaces with ISP); and the DDR2/DDR3 memory controller (16- or 32-bit data path, two chip selects and interfaces). Timing measurement methodology, including test load circuits and signal transition levels, is also described.

The "Power" set offense, used by nearly every NBA team, is designed to free up outstanding shooters through baseline and down screens while attacking both sides of the defense simultaneously. Its basic action has shooters crossing under the basket and curling off down screens set by O4 and O5, with the point guard passing to shooters or feeding the rolling screener. Players must know counters for defensive reads—chasing, cheating over, switching, or showing—including curls, fades, back cuts, screen-and-rolls, post and wing isolations, and slipping the screen. Automatic counters address anticipated defenses through fake cross, misdirection, back cut, direct post, and dribble drive entries. Offensive rebounding, requiring anticipation and hustle rather than size, is emphasized, with two rebounders always positioned on the weakside. If initial actions fail, continuity options include Motion, Side Screen, Drive & Kick, and Triangle Post, plus a Single/Double variation for teams with a great shooter. Success depends on execution, coordination, timing, and defensive recognition, taught through breakdown drills. Game strategies stress scouting, alertness to defensive adjustments, varied alignments, and attacking weak defenders.

The President reports that Great Britain has declined the United States' proposal to submit its boundary dispute with Venezuela to arbitration. The British reply, conveyed through communications from the prime minister to the British ambassador, argues that the Monroe doctrine represents a new and strange extension, is inapplicable to present conditions, and is not a principle of international law recognized by general consent of nations. The President defends the doctrine as vital to American peace, safety, and institutions, asserting it cannot become obsolete and that a European power's acquisition of territory from a neighboring republic would dangerously extend its system to this continent. He contends the doctrine holds a secure place in international law, since every nation is entitled to enforcement of its just claims. While the British prime minister acknowledged sympathy with Monroe's objectives, he refused to admit the doctrine into the code of international law. Disappointed by Britain's refusal of arbitration, the President recommends that Congress appropriate funds for an executive commission to investigate and determine the true boundary between Venezuela and British Guiana. Once the report is accepted, he states it will be the duty of the United States to resist by every means any British appropriation of territory determined to belong to Venezuela. He acknowledges the gravity of this position but maintains that submission to wrong and injustice would cost the nation its self-respect and honor.

On June 3, 2015, Apple Inc. entered into an underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs International and Mitsubishi UFJ Securities International plc for the issuance and sale of ¥250,000,000,000 aggregate principal amount of Apple's 0.350% Notes due 2020. The Notes will be issued under an indenture dated April 29, 2013 between Apple and The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A., as trustee, and pursuant to Apple's Form S-3 Registration Statement filed April 29, 2013. Interest is payable semi-annually on June 10 and December 10, beginning December 10, 2015. The Notes mature on June 10, 2020, and are Apple's senior unsecured obligations ranking equally with its other unsecured and unsubordinated debt.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2015. Q2 2015 net sales were $23.2 billion, up 20% from $19.3 billion in Q2 2014, with net income of $92 million compared to a net loss of $126 million in the prior year quarter. Diluted earnings per share were $0.19 versus $(0.27). For the six months ended June 30, 2015, net sales were $45.9 billion and net income was $35 million.

Beginning in Q1 2015, Amazon changed its reportable segments to North America, International, and AWS. Q2 2015 segment results: North America net sales of $13.8 billion (up 26%) with operating income of $703 million; International net sales of $7.6 billion (up 3%) with an operating loss of $19 million; and AWS net sales of $1.8 billion (up 81%) with operating income of $391 million.

Cash and cash equivalents were $10.3 billion at June 30, 2015, with total assets of $52.4 billion. Operating cash flow was $2.0 billion in Q2 2015, and free cash flow for the trailing twelve months was $4.4 billion, up from $1.0 billion. Long-term debt was $8.3 billion, and no borrowings were outstanding under the $2.0 billion credit agreement.

During the six months, Amazon acquired companies for $349 million in aggregate. Legal matters include patent infringement lawsuits from Appistry, ContentGuard, Kaavo, and Smartflash, as well as a European Commission proceeding regarding contracts with European publishers. Tax matters include an IRS transfer pricing dispute seeking approximately $1.5 billion in additional federal tax for 2005–2006, a French tax assessment of €196 million, and a European Commission state aid investigation regarding Luxembourg taxation.

Erwin Chemerinsky writes that the Supreme Court's October 2025 term, beginning Oct. 6, is expected to be momentous. Over the summer, the court's emergency "shadow docket" produced mostly 6-3 rulings allowing Trump administration actions, including firings at the Consumer Product Safety Commission and Federal Trade Commission, termination of NIH grants, and ICE agents' racial profiling in Los Angeles, all reversing lower courts over liberal dissents. Major docket cases include whether the International Emergency Economic Powers Act authorizes Trump's tariffs (argued Nov. 5), whether Congress can limit the president's power to fire agency heads—potentially overruling a 1935 precedent—and a pending challenge to Trump's executive order restricting birthright citizenship. The court will rehear a Louisiana case on whether creating a second majority-Black district violates the 14th or 15th Amendments, raising questions about disparate impact liability under the Voting Rights Act and other civil rights laws. Culture-war cases concern Colorado's conversion therapy ban and transgender athlete bans in Idaho and West Virginia. A Fourth Amendment case asks whether the emergency aid exception to warrantless home entries requires probable cause.

Last week's Northeast Mississippi highlights include: Parkway Elementary parent Karmel Davis being named the Tupelo Public School District's 2017 Parent of the Year for her volunteer contributions; Corey Crayton receiving the keys to her new three-bedroom home, built by Northeast Mississippi Habitat for Humanity and funded by HomeStretch Furniture, where she will live with her daughter and grandson; and Belden native Noah Barbieri, a Millsaps College junior, being named one of 62 Truman Scholars nationwide, receiving $30,000 toward graduate school as he pursues a doctorate in economics.

Ruston (La.), 4-0 and ranked No. 2 in the Sporting News Louisiana Top 25, faces 5-0 Stephenville (Texas), ranked No. 25 in the Texas Top 25. Ruston won last year's meeting 63-17. Bearcats running back Dalen Powell has 686 rushing yards and eight touchdowns this season; Yellow Jackets quarterback Trot Jordan has passed for 996 yards and 13 touchdowns, with Zyler McClendon adding 664 rushing yards and nine scores. Early in the game, Powell fumbled, leading to a 19-yard touchdown pass from Jordan to Jhett Banuelos.

The speaker describes losing a close finals game as difficult but says the team must regroup and bounce back, as they have in similar past situations. Both goalies played well, with only one goal scored in six periods, and the team plans to adjust without dwelling on missed opportunities.

The Department of Homeland Security has proposed replacing the duration of status policy—which lets international students stay in the U.S. until completing their studies—with a four-year cap, with extensions available through USCIS, and would bar students from changing majors or transferring institutions. DHS says the rule aims to reduce F and J visa overstays, but NAFSA and others argue DHS overestimates overstay rates and that the existing monitoring system already alerts ICE to overstays. The comment period closed Sept. 29 with over 15,700 comments. Universities, hospitals, and industry leaders opposed the rule, noting many programs—including five-year architecture degrees and Ph.D.s—take longer than four years, that extensions are costly, uncertain, and slow (about 6.5 months of USCIS processing), and that compliance would burden institutions financially. Commenters warned the change could deter international students vital to research, who fill roughly 17,000 J-1 physician residency slots in high-need specialties and support industries conducting multi-year trials. Few comments supported the change; the Council for Christian Colleges and Universities suggested limiting it to colleges with admission rates under 30 percent.

AI is changing the intellectual property landscape for drug patents, raising unresolved questions such as whether AI can be an inventor or hold a patent and what "a person skilled in the art" would reasonably know. Foley Hoag biotech patent lawyer DeAnn Smith expects these issues to be worked out in future litigation. The article also notes the U.S. patent office required physical models of inventions until 1880, when it switched to requiring diagrams.

This study examined the perspectives of bilingual and monolingual early childhood teachers in Ankara, Türkiye, on bilingualism and bilingual education. Using a phenomenological qualitative design, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 16 preschool teachers—8 bilingual teachers from private schools offering foreign-language education and 8 monolingual teachers from state preschools—selected through extreme case sampling. Content analysis identified five themes: benefits of bilingual education, bilingual children attending monolingual schools, bilingual education programs, issues in bilingual education, and the impact of bilingualism on children's development.

All teachers viewed bilingualism as an advantage, citing benefits for career prospects, self-esteem, brain development, communication skills, and global citizenship, and agreed that bilingual schools should be expanded in Türkiye. Most teachers considered it a disadvantage for bilingual children to attend monolingual schools, fearing loss of the second language, though some monolingual teachers saw advantages such as improvement in the native language. Teachers showed limited knowledge of bilingual education program types but agreed that school staff should be proficient in both languages and that school environments should include materials and stimuli in both languages. Identified challenges included teachers' ineffective use of both languages, insufficient financial and human resources, children's language deficiencies, family factors such as lack of familiarity with the second language, and program-related problems. Views on bilingual children's development differed: monolingual teachers emphasized proficiency in the community's dominant language, while bilingual teachers highlighted multicultural exposure and self-confidence.

The study concluded that teachers lack training in bilingual education and emphasized the need for professional development, qualified bilingual personnel, parental support, and improved resources. Limitations include the small sample, restriction to Ankara, and reliance on self-reported perspectives.

This study compared three surveys of physicians' EHR use and interoperability experiences: the 2021 NEHRS (voluntary, weighted), the 2022 ABFM Continuous Certification Questionnaire (CCQ, mandatory for family physician recertification), and the 2022 UCSF Physician Health IT Survey (voluntary). Analyses focused on primary care physicians and used Rao-Scott corrected chi-square tests, with stratified comparisons by age, EHR platform, and practice type.

Response rates differed markedly: 100% for the CCQ (3,991 respondents), 18.2% for NEHRS, and 3.6% for UCSF. Respondent characteristics varied across surveys; CCQ respondents were youngest, NEHRS overrepresented private practice, and UCSF overrepresented academic centers and large practices. Epic was the most common EHR platform in all three surveys.

All surveys found low EHR satisfaction (roughly one-quarter very satisfied), substantial after-hours documentation, and limited interoperability, with only about 20% of physicians often accessing outside clinical information. However, nearly all questions showed statistically significant differences across surveys. CCQ respondents generally reported better interoperability experiences than UCSF respondents, and differences persisted within age, platform, and practice-type subgroups, though some findings were directionally consistent (e.g., Epic users more satisfied; private practice physicians less likely to have external information).

The authors attribute differences partly to respondent composition and response bias, concluding that mandatory certifying board data could reliably supplement NEHRS. Limitations include differences in question wording and the CCQ's restriction to family physicians.

This review examines lung cancer screening methods and biomarkers, noting that lung cancer has been the leading cause of death in men and women since 1987, with high mortality attributed to late detection, absent early symptoms, and inadequate screening. The authors searched PubMed for United States-based clinical studies from the past 10 years on biomarkers for early lung cancer diagnosis and reviewed articles meeting their criteria. Evaluated biomarkers included volatile organic compounds (80% sensitivity and specificity), circulating tumor DNA (80% sensitivity, 96% specificity), four miRNAs (93–96% sensitivity but 23–33% specificity), DNA methylation of six genes measured in sputum or serum with variable results, Ga-Alfatide II scans (86% sensitivity, 85% specificity), combined score analysis (78% sensitivity, 50% specificity), and WT-IDH (63% sensitivity, 93% specificity). Circulating tumor DNA and Ga-Alfatide II PET/CT showed the highest sensitivity and specificity and were identified as promising screening tools for high-risk or suspected patients, though neither confirms diagnosis. The review also covers lung cancer subtypes, associated gene mutations and targeted therapies, current low-dose CT screening for ages 50–80, prevention strategies, and limitations including restricted sample size and potential false positives and negatives. Improved screening, along with immunotherapy and chemotherapy, may help reduce lung cancer mortality.

A multi-centre randomised controlled trial in England evaluated PrAISED, a 12-month, dementia-specific exercise and functional activity rehabilitation programme for people over 65 with mild dementia or mild cognitive impairment. The individually tailored intervention, delivered in participants' homes by physiotherapists, occupational therapists and rehabilitation support workers, included progressive strength, balance and dual-task exercises, functional activities, community inclusion, risk enablement and environmental assessment, with supervision tapered over time; carers were encouraged to participate. The control group received a falls prevention assessment and advice. In total, 365 patient participants were randomised. The primary outcome was carer-rated disability in activities of daily living (DAD) at 12 months.

The intervention was well received by participants and therapists, and adherence and delivery fidelity were reasonable, though the trial was disrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic. However, no differences were found between groups on the primary outcome or on most secondary outcomes, including physical activity, quality of life, falls, cognition, balance or functional mobility. Small differences favouring the control group were seen on the dual-task Timed Up and Go test and self-reported quality of life. Underpowered cognitive analyses suggested possible benefits in some domains. The authors conclude that exercise and functionally oriented rehabilitation are unlikely to change the rate of loss of ability in dementia, and that different ways of defining and supporting wellbeing after diagnosis are needed.

Stenabolic (SR9009) is a synthetic Rev-ErbA ligand, not a SARM, developed by Scripps Research Institute under professor Thomas Burris. Taken orally, it activates the Rev-Erb protein, affecting circadian rhythms, lipid and glucose metabolism, fat-storing cells, and macrophages. It increases mitochondria count in muscles, enhancing endurance and strength; mice ran 50% more in distance and time. Energy expenditure rises 5% even at rest, making the body act as if in continuous exercise. Studies showed reductions in plasma triglycerides (12%), total cholesterol (47%), non-esterified fatty acids (23%), plasma glucose (19%), insulin (35%), and proinflammatory cytokine IL-6 (72%).

The United States District Court for the Western District of New York granted defendant Garlocks Sealing Technologies' motion for summary judgment and dismissed pro se plaintiff Steven C. Gittens, Sr.'s ADA disability discrimination complaint with prejudice. Gittens failed to respond to the summary judgment motion despite two court-ordered deadlines and explicit warnings that noncompliance could result in dismissal. The court dismissed the action on three alternative grounds: failure to prosecute under Rule 41(b), failure to obey court orders under Rule 16(f), and failure to show a genuine issue of material fact under Rule 56. The court found plaintiff's noncompliance willful and in bad faith, noted that pro se status does not excuse compliance with court orders, and deemed defendant's statement of material facts admitted. On the merits, Gittens alleged a lower spine injury resulting in a 25-30 pound lifting restriction. The court held this did not constitute a disability under the ADA, because inability to perform a single job (punch press operation) does not substantially limit the major life activity of working, and plaintiff remained employed by defendant in other positions, including as a welder and in light duty jobs. Even assuming a prima facie case existed, defendant articulated legitimate, non-discriminatory reasons for reassigning plaintiff, and no evidence showed those reasons were pretextual or motivated by discriminatory animus.

Russian cosmonauts Fyodor Yurchikhin and Sergey Ryazanskiy will conduct a spacewalk from the ISS's Pirs airlock on August 17. Ryazanskiy will deploy five nanosatellites for various purposes, including testing 3-D printed materials. The pair will collect residue samples and install handrails and struts. This will be Yurchikhin's ninth and Ryazanskiy's fourth spacewalk, and the 202nd supporting station assembly and maintenance.

The Pocatello-Chubbuck School District plans to finalize controversial high school boundary changes through three new focus groups providing trustee input. Trustees tabled the decision, originally targeted for Jan. 11, citing need for more public feedback. The changes end a two-decade open-enrollment policy prompted by enrollment and socioeconomic disparities.

The United States Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of Indiana ruled on the Chapter 13 Trustee's objections to the amended plan of debtors Jeffery Wayne and Paulette Monee Smith. The Trustee argued the plan unfairly discriminated by paying Chrysler Financial Corporation in full with 8% interest on a loan secured by the debtors' 1997 Dodge Stratus while treating NBD Bank less favorably, that the plan lacked good faith, and that the debtors failed to devote all disposable income to the plan.

The court found the disparate treatment permissible because the debtors purchased the vehicle five months before filing, made no payments to Chrysler beforehand, and paying less than the full amount would create a "windfall." The court also found the debtors acted in good faith, including in deferring Mrs. Smith's ERISA-qualified profit sharing distribution to a 401(k) plan, holding that undisbursed ERISA-qualified benefits are not estate property or disposable income, though any cash distributions received during the plan must be paid to creditors.

The court granted in part and denied in part the objection, confirming the plan with modifications: interest on Chrysler's claim reduced from 8% to the 3.9% contract rate; semiannual submission of pay stubs and earnings records; increased plan payments for overtime income exceeding projections; a $75 monthly payment increase (reducing the debtors' emergency cushion); payment to creditors of net proceeds from any cash profit sharing distribution; and cessation of voluntary retirement or 401(k) contributions during the plan term.

Justice must be both sure and swift, but administered under the law rather than through mob violence such as lynching. Free public education is essential for all citizens regardless of race, as denying schooling to any class harms the entire nation; industrial schools like Hampton and Tuskegee produce graduates who rarely become criminals and improve relations between Black and white neighbors. Inflammatory speeches and writings that excite mobs and justify lynching deepen racial bitterness and, through "suggestion," encourage repetition of the very crimes denounced; only swift, orderly punishment under law can suppress such criminality. Similarly, demagogues who preach class hatred against the wealthy are the worst enemies of genuine reform, provoke violent reactions, and foster corruption. The path forward lies in a resolute but sane advance, rejecting both those who inflame Americans against one another and those who exploit others for profit.

The passage begins with blank template forms for a U.S. passport application, including an oath of allegiance, a physical description section, two supporting affidavits, and the passport text itself. The substantive portion is a May 10, 1902 dispatch from Mr. Lord to Mr. Hay transmitting the message delivered by Argentine President Julio A. Roca at the opening of the Argentine Congress on May 8. The message was described as hopeful and optimistic but containing little new information. The public had anticipated details on international relations and the financial situation, particularly British-mediated negotiations with Chile to limit armaments, but the message treated these matters only generally—possibly because of the death of Foreign Minister Dr. Alcorta. Both Argentina and Chile had incurred heavy military and naval expenses, including competing warship purchases, leaving both indebted, unable to borrow abroad except at high interest rates, and reliant on further taxes despite taxation already at its limit. With dull business, scarce employment, and frequent failures, both nations recognized that their war policy was ruinous and that costly expenditures needed to end.

The author expresses skepticism about Snap (SNAP), citing intense competition: Facebook's Instagram features have attracted over 200 million users versus Snap's 166 million DAUs, and Snapchat app downloads fell 22% year-over-year. Only 7% of marketers used Snapchat in 1Q17 compared to 94% for Facebook. The upcoming lock-up expiration will make an additional 1.2 billion shares available for sale by the end of July, an estimated 84% dilution, which could pressure the stock currently trading at $17.85, near its all-time low of $17.56. Fundamentals were weak, with Q1 revenue of $150 million missing the $158 million consensus and a loss of $2.31 per share versus an estimated $0.20 loss. With 28% of the float shorted and expensive put premiums, the author considers shorting risky and will watch from the sidelines, making no trade recommendation.

Safety endpoints at 24 and 48 weeks were similar between study groups. Before Week 24, adverse event (AE) and bleeding rates were comparable between the Primary SOC and Additional Educational Program groups, with one fatal bleeding event. Between 24 and 48 weeks, AE and bleeding rates remained similar across groups, with two fatal bleeding events. Overall, 24 deaths were reported. No pregnancies occurred, and no hepatic or renal concerns were identified. The AEGEAN study demonstrated high adherence and persistence with apixaban for atrial fibrillation, but the educational program provided no additional benefit.

The Single/Double offense is an effective way to attack the Triangle & Two defense and free up shooters. Because chasers excel at pass denial, shooters need screens to get open looks. Single/Double screens can be run from either side, with communication between shooters determining who initiates the action and who forms the double screen. Options include double screens, single screens, pop outs, base screens, and side screens, along with counters such as sealing off chasers, drop passes, and kick out passes. Success depends on execution, coordination, defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience. Teaching involves breakdown drills and scrimmaging. Game strategies include scouting opponents, educating players on anticipated defensive reads, deploying varied alignments, and attacking the weakest defenders. The Triangle & Two defense uses three players in a triangle zone and two chasers who deny their opponents the ball.

This study investigated Greek primary teachers' views on STEM education using questionnaires from 114 teachers and 27 interviews conducted in Attica, Greece (March–May 2022). Teachers considered developing students' scientific thinking very important, citing everyday problem-solving (38%), inquiry and critical thinking (26%), and social skills (15%) as main reasons. While 58–75% of teachers valued fundamental STEM practices such as problem-solving, group work, and making observations, only 7–19% reported students frequently practicing them in class, revealing a gap between beliefs and implementation. Only 20–30% felt effective teaching science and 30–40% mathematics, with insecurity extending to STEM approaches. Teachers identified advantages including experiential, interdisciplinary learning (46%), connection to everyday life (38%), and scientific methodology (32%). Weaknesses cited were lack of teacher training and materials (58%), insufficient infrastructure and equipment (42%), and lack of time (31%). Most teachers (71%) requested more training, along with infrastructure, materials, and ongoing support. Although teachers viewed STEM positively as innovative and interdisciplinary, its introduction in Greece (2021–2022, via "skills workshops") was perceived as disorganized, lacking materials and funding. Notably, some teachers saw STEM as a tool for reducing educational inequalities by enabling broader participation. The study concludes that successful implementation requires teacher training, infrastructure, equipment, and more timetable time, highlighting teachers' willingness despite inadequate institutional support.

This statistical analysis plan (SAP) for study ZEA-DNK-02170 describes analyses for a multicenter trial (approximately 5 centers) comparing dasiglucagon 0.6 mg with placebo, with GlucaGen comparisons intended to support study validity, in patients aged 6–17 years.

Concomitant medications and current diabetes treatments will be coded using WHODrug Global (March 2018) and ATC classes, and summarized by ATC class (level 2) and preferred name as patient counts and percentages. Medications with ambiguous start/stop dates are classified as concomitant.

The primary efficacy endpoint, time to plasma glucose recovery (first increase of ≥20 mg/dL from baseline within 45 minutes without rescue IV glucose), will be analyzed in the FAS, with supportive sensitivity analyses in the PPS. Secondary endpoints include recovery within 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes and plasma glucose changes from baseline at these times. The primary model adjusts for age group (6–11, 12–17 years) and injection site (abdomen/thigh). No imputation will be applied, and no interim analyses are planned. A hierarchical testing procedure at the 2-sided 0.05 significance level controls multiplicity; GlucaGen comparisons are excluded from this hierarchy.

Primary analyses use Kaplan-Meier estimates and a stratified log-rank test; patients receiving rescue IV glucose or not recovering within 45 minutes are censored at 45 minutes. Sensitivity analyses vary censoring approaches; supportive analyses include a stratified Wilcoxon test, a discrete-time Cox proportional hazards model (with additional homogenicity models for sex, BMI class, ethnicity, race, and US/non-US status), and linear interpolation of recovery times. Secondary recovery rates will be compared using a stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test, and glucose changes by analysis of variance.

Plasma dasiglucagon and glucagon concentrations will be analyzed by non-compartmental analysis using Phoenix WinNonlin Version 6.4; the pharmacodynamic endpoint is glucose area under the effect curve above baseline from 0 to 30 minutes (AUE0-30min).

Safety analyses, based on the safety set, cover exposure, local tolerability, treatment-emergent adverse events (coded with MedDRA version 21.0 or higher), laboratory parameters, vital signs, ECG (including categorical QTcF analyses), and immunogenicity (ADA incidence comprising treatment-induced and treatment-boosted patients). Appendices specify data presentation standards, SAS programming QC requirements, and a list of tables, figures, and listings per ICH E3 guidelines.

The lecture continues the development toward Freiman's theorem. After recalling Ruzsa's modeling lemma—which represents a large (at least 1/8) subset of a small-doubling set as Freiman 8-isomorphic to a subset of a small cyclic group—the focus shifts to extracting additive structure from a dense subset of a group. In F₂ⁿ, a set of density α need not have A+A containing a bounded-codimension subspace, as shown by a Hamming ball construction; however, Bogolyubov's lemma states that 2A−2A contains a subspace of codimension less than 1/α². The proof considers the convolution 1_A∗1_A∗1₋ₐ∗1₋ₐ, whose support is 2A−2A, and shows it is positive on the orthogonal complement of the set of large Fourier coefficients (bounded in size via Parseval), in a manner parallel to the Fourier-analytic proof of Roth's theorem. The underlying principle is that addition, like convolution, is smoothing. The analogous result in Z/nZ replaces subspaces with Bohr sets: 2A−2A contains a Bohr set of dimension below 1/α² and width 1/4, proved with essentially the same Fourier argument. To extract geometric structure, the lecture reviews the geometry of numbers—lattices, determinants, successive minima, and Minkowski's second theorem—and uses them to show that every Bohr set of dimension d and width ε in Z/nZ contains a proper GAP of dimension at most d and size at least (ε/d)^d times the group. The Ruzsa covering lemma will later extend structure from a constant fraction of A to all of A; the completion of Freiman's theorem and the polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture are deferred to the next lecture.
