Before COVID-19, Japanese universities lagged in ICT use due to beliefs that education should occur within walls and structural barriers such as few adult students and credit limits on distance learning. The pandemic forced a rapid shift to online teaching, prompting this study of digitalization (education via LMS/MOOCs) across four areas: MEXT policy, academic staff, students, and lifelong learning.

MEXT had planned digitalization before the pandemic (e.g., a 1999 60-credit remote learning limit; the 2018 "Grand Design" report linking digitalization to Society 5.0). By June 2020, about 90% of universities offered remote classes; MEXT temporarily lifted the credit cap, then promoted a return to face-to-face teaching from September 2020 after student complaints. An April 2021 policy treated courses taught mostly remotely as face-to-face and accepted over 60 remote credits only as emergency exceptions; by fall 2022, 99.8% of universities offered mostly in-person classes. The March 2022 Central Council report retained the credit limit but allowed exceptions for universities with strong quality assurance, leading to revised standards in October 2022. Government projects (Scheem-D, Plus-DX) subsidized digitalization, while Cabinet initiatives promoted educational data sharing and "My Number" use, raising privacy concerns after 2023 system troubles.

Faculty ICT use was limited pre-pandemic (low LMS adoption due to paper-based preferences and technological anxiety) but rose sharply during the pandemic through hybrid and high-flex classes. Challenges included poor communication, ineffective practical training, and faculty computer illiteracy; universities began publishing good practices online. The pandemic altered the assumption of face-to-face teaching, though cultural transformation remains incomplete.

Student study time falls short of credit-system requirements (about five hours weekly outside class) due to heavy course loads, early job-hunting, and traditional views of education. Online classes increased out-of-class study through assignments and LMS-based evaluation, potentially substantiating the credit system, though students reported heavy assignment burdens.

Lifelong learning remains weakly institutionalized. Distance learning serves adult degree seekers (about 80% over age 25) but stayed marginal; traditional Kokaikoza lectures are rarely digitalized (7.6%), while newer vocational certificate programs are more digitalized, accelerated by the pandemic.

The conclusion notes benefits—visualization of education and opportunities for adult learners—alongside challenges: university culture, credit substantiation, lifelong learning's peripheral status, and privacy risks requiring careful stakeholder discussion.

The passage describes the NVIDIA A100 GPU based on the Ampere architecture and its associated technologies.

**Tensor Core and Memory Improvements**: The third-generation Tensor Cores share data across all 32 threads in a warp (versus 8 on Volta), reducing register file bandwidth and redundant data loads; A100 issues 8x fewer instructions and performs 2.9x fewer register file accesses for matrix multiplies than V100. A new asynchronous copy instruction loads data directly from global memory into shared memory, bypassing L1 cache and the register file, while asynchronous barriers enable efficient data fetch pipelines. Maximum SMEM allocation per SM increases 1.7x to 164 KB. A100 features a 5-site HBM2 subsystem with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth (1.7x V100), 2.3x L2 read bandwidth, and a 40 MB L2 cache (nearly 7x V100) with improved residency controls. Compute Data Compression saves up to 4x DRAM and L2 bandwidth.

**Multi-Instance GPU (MIG)**: MIG partitions an A100 into up to seven GPU Instances, each with isolated memory system paths, providing quality of service and fault isolation for multi-tenant use. GPU Instances are built from seven GPU slices, each containing a Sys Pipe, one GPC, and L2 slices. Compute Instances within GPU Instances support Volta-style MPS and enable simultaneous context execution. MIG also supports vGPU migration between instances and GPUs.

**Interconnect and I/O**: Third-generation NVLink doubles the per-signal data rate to 50 Gbit/sec and provides twelve links per GPU for 600 GB/sec total bandwidth (versus 300 GB/sec on V100). A100 supports PCIe Gen 4 (31.5 GB/sec per direction) with SR-IOV. New error detection, isolation, and containment technologies improve uptime, particularly in MIG environments.

**Additional Features**: A100 includes a 5-core NVJPG hardware JPEG decode engine, an Optical Flow Accelerator, improved atomics (11x FP16, 2.7x FP32 over V100), and five NVDEC video decode units (versus one in V100).

**CUDA Advances**: CUDA 11 adds task graphs (with A100 launch and dependency optimizations), asynchronous copy operations, hardware-accelerated asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls (set-aside in 2.5 MB increments), and expanded Cooperative Groups collectives including a reduce API.

**DGX A100**: The DGX A100 delivers 5 PFLOPS using eight A100 GPUs interconnected via six NVSwitches with 4.8 TB/s bidirectional bandwidth, providing up to 6x the AI training performance of DGX-1 and up to 56 discrete accelerators via MIG. Its software stack centers on the NGC Private Registry, CUDA Toolkit, and Container Toolkit.

**Sparsity**: The appendix explains network pruning and distinguishes fine-grained from coarse-grained sparsity. A100's fine-grained structured sparsity (2:4) balances workload distribution and achieves virtually no accuracy loss across tested networks.

This study developed and evaluated an online version of the SInQUE, a validated social inclusion assessment tool, for use in mental health supported accommodation services. The SUSHI study, conducted in one inner London borough, comprised a lab-testing stage (think-aloud testing with six staff) and a five-month field-testing stage supported by a local implementation strategy, including interviews with 12 staff and 12 service users. The tool was also made available in two other areas without implementation support.

The online SInQUE is a 46-item questionnaire (score 0–75) covering nine areas of social inclusion, completed collaboratively by staff and service users to inform care planning. Participants generally found the tool user-friendly, collaborative, and relevant, suggesting it could promote targeted support and improve staff–service user relationships. Some staff expressed concern that certain questions felt intrusive, though service users did not report this. Minor refinements were made to the tool after each testing stage.

Uptake was limited: 17 staff from six providers completed 30 assessments with 28 service users, approximately 10% of the borough's supported accommodation users, mostly in supported housing. No assessments were completed in the areas without an implementation strategy, indicating such support—particularly leadership endorsement—is essential for uptake.

The authors conclude the SInQUE is a potentially useful and acceptable tool, especially in supported housing settings, but recommend further research on uptake, effectiveness over time, and use in other service types. Limitations include the absence of female service user participants, testing in a single borough, and possible selection bias.

This document standardizes the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) so a guest OS can interoperate with any hypervisor supporting SEV-ES or SEV-SNP, defines required Non-Automatic Exits (NAEs), and specifies minimum guest state exposed during VMGEXIT. The GHCB is a 4KB decrypted page whose format mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save state area, limiting guest state exposed to the hypervisor. Version 2 adds initial SEV-SNP support and hypervisor feature advertisement via a 52-bit FEATURES bitmap returned through the GHCB MSR protocol. Later revisions added 64-bit guest request sequence numbers, a VLEK GUID, APIC ID list retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, page state change support for SEV-ES, SEV-TIO trusted IO, and Secure AVIC backing page management. The GHCB MSR protocol supports negotiation, CPUID requests, AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration/unregistration, and termination requests before the GHCB page is established; GHCB GPA registration is required for SEV-SNP guests. The specification defines supported NAE events—including IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, MMIO access, Page State Change, SNP Guest Request, AP Creation, #HV doorbell, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, and termination—with error handling via SW_EXITINFO1/SW_EXITINFO2. SMP booting requires alternative AP startup methods because register values cannot change after measurement, using AP Reset Hold or SNP AP Creation via VMSA pages. NMI handling uses #DB interception with an "NMI Complete" message. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported. The #HV doorbell page defines PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields governing host-guest interrupt delivery under Restricted Injection.

Chairman Kenneth Lay declined a $60.6 million severance package, while executives Skilling, Fastow, and Lay made millions in stock sales before the collapse. Pension funds considered legal action against Enron. Enron's UK water utility, Wessex Water, was reportedly up for sale, with WestLB offering around £1 billion. The Dark Cloud Cover is a bearish reversal candlestick pattern that appears after an uptrend or a rally within a downtrend. It consists of two candles: a long bullish (green) candle followed by a bearish (red) candle that opens above the previous candle's close but closes below its midpoint, indicating that bearish momentum has overpowered bullish momentum. Traders can use the pattern as a signal to short sell or close long positions, and it is more reliable when it forms near resistance levels. Confirmation can come from monitoring subsequent price action or using indicators such as Moving Averages, MACD, or RSI. The pattern is a warning sign rather than a guarantee of reversal, so it should be combined with other technical analysis, market news, and fundamental analysis, along with proper risk management techniques such as stop-loss orders. The strategy can be applied in any asset market—stocks, Forex, commodities, or cryptocurrencies—but is limited to bearish conditions. Timeframe choice depends on the trader's goals: shorter timeframes generate more signals but carry a higher risk of false signals, while longer timeframes suit long-term traders. Backtesting is recommended, though results vary by market, timeframe, and parameters and do not guarantee future performance. Example trades on AAPL charts show profitable short entries placed at the start of the candle following the pattern. Avoiding common mistakes and following the strategy's rules can improve trading performance and discipline.

This paper analyses ~1000 days of Swift monitoring of the Seyfert 1 AGN Fairall 9 to investigate the connection between the UV-emitting disc and the X-ray corona. Time-averaged SEDs, modelled with agnsed, show a significant increase in mass-accretion rate (~40–50%) after a sharp rise in the UV and X-ray light-curves: the optical/UV disc emission brightens while the integrated X-ray power remains roughly constant, the X-ray photon index softens (attributed to increased seed-photon cooling), and the coronal truncation radius decreases. Fourier analysis, using Gaussian Process regression to produce evenly sampled light-curves, yields power spectra, phase-lags and coherences between the UVW2 and hard X-ray bands. Segments excluding the rise show a semi-coherent low-frequency lag with the X-rays leading the UV by ~6–12 days—too long for disc light-travel times and possibly due to EUV reprocessing in the BLR/wind. Including the rise gives a highly coherent UV lead of ~5.5 days, consistent with an inward-propagating increase in mass-accretion rate. In Segment 3 the coherent signal vanishes. An analytic model combining intrinsic disc and coronal variability with seed-photon, reverberation and wind components suggests Segments 2 and 3 are consistent with the same underlying process, with low coherence arising from interference between disc and coronal variability. The authors conclude that the inner accretion structure evolves on observable time-scales and that current variability models do not fully explain the observed phenomenology.

This paper applies Bacchi's "What's the Problem Represented to be?" (WPR) framework to analyze South Australia's "World Class" public education policy, introduced by the Department for Education in 2018. The authors, drawing on their backgrounds in disadvantaged schools, situate the policy within the Global Education Reform Movement (GERM), a neoliberal approach linked to PISA and shaped by McKinsey and Company's consultancy work. McKinsey's "Universal Scale" placed SA's public education at the lower end of "good," prompting the Department's goal to achieve World Class status by 2028, matching Canada, Finland, and Estonia. Using NAPLAN as a proxy measure, the Department ranked schools 1 to 5, imposed centralized control through a "School Improvement Dashboard" designated the "single source of truth," increased Education Directors by 50 percent, and eroded professional trust in educators. The analysis finds the problem was represented as too many competing educator voices, with centralization and purchased expertise offered as the solution. Documented impacts include marginalized democratic purposes of schooling, greater bureaucratic scrutiny of disadvantaged schools, declining PIRLS results, a widening PISA equity gap, and increased student disengagement. The authors propose an alternative "Beyond World Class" framework emphasizing equity, democratic partnerships, professional trust, and socially just schooling aligned with the Alice Springs (Mparntwe) Declaration.

This study investigates domain boundaries in Mn5Al8, a fully metallic distortive polar metal (DPM). Off-stoichiometric Mn51Al49 undergoes a first-order, martensitic centrosymmetry-reducing transition at ~880°C from a cubic γ-brass phase (I¯43m) to a polar rhombohedral phase (R3m); the observed high-temperature structure differs from the accepted Mn-Al phase diagram. Metallic behavior is confirmed by a positive resistivity-temperature correlation and DFT-calculated density of states at the Fermi level. The transformation produces rank-2 laminate twins with a herringbone morphology of four polar variants separated by {100}PC and {110}PC twin boundaries. 4D-STEM differential phase contrast mapping visualized head-to-head (H-H) and tail-to-tail (T-T) "charged" domain boundaries forming an "interlocking Y pattern." Surface probing indicated electron surplus at H-H boundaries and depletion at T-T boundaries: low-voltage SEM contrast, electrostatic force microscopy, preferential copper deposition at H-H boundaries (attributed to lower work function), and variable oxide formation all followed this pattern. A chemical sorting of the ICSD identified ~134 metallic polar metals (5.1% of polar compounds), of which ~20% are DPMs, with notable examples tabulated. The authors propose that geometric polarization discontinuities influence free-carrier density at boundaries, though the mechanism remains unclear, and note that metallic DPMs may challenge the weak-coupling principle while being amenable to conventional metallurgical processing.

Jane Goodall, the pioneering chimpanzee researcher and conservationist, died at 91 while on tour in California; the Jane Goodall Institute announced October 1 that she died in her sleep of natural causes. A British secretary without formal scientific training, she visited Kenya in 1957, where archaeologist Louis Leakey hired her to observe chimps. In 1960, accompanied by her mother, she began research at Gombe, gaining the chimpanzees' acceptance after about five months. She discovered that chimpanzees make and use tools—after seeing a chimp named David Greybeard fish for termites with a stripped twig—as well as engage in warfare and have personalities. She earned a Cambridge PhD in 1965 without a bachelor's degree and faced sexism, including media coverage focused on her appearance. She married photographer Hugo van Lawick in 1964 (divorced 1974), then Derek Bryceson, who died in 1980. She founded the Jane Goodall Institute in 1977, launched Roots & Shoots in 1991, and lobbied the NIH, leading to the 2015 retirement of the last federally owned research chimpanzees. Honors included UN Messenger of Peace (2002), Dame of the British Empire (2004), and the French Legion of Honor (2006).

This randomized controlled trial investigated the safety and preliminary efficacy of Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) combined with group-format psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy (PAP) versus MBSR alone for frontline physicians and nurses experiencing depression and burnout related to COVID-19. Twenty-five participants were enrolled and randomized 1:1. The MBSR+PAP arm showed significantly greater reduction in depressive symptoms (QIDS-SR-16) at the 2-week primary endpoint compared to MBSR-only, as well as greater reductions in depersonalization, emotional exhaustion at 6 months, demoralization, and increased connectedness. No serious adverse events, emergent suicidality, or self-injurious behaviors occurred. The authors conclude that combining MBSR with psilocybin appears safe, feasible, and potentially efficacious, though larger, more diverse studies with placebo controls are needed.

Stock trading strategies are defined rules and methods for buying and selling stocks, encompassing approaches such as day trading, swing trading, momentum trading, scalping, trend following, arbitrage, high-frequency trading, event-driven trading, sector rotation, pair trading, market-neutral trading, statistical arbitrage, technical analysis, seasonality trading, long-short equity, S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 trading, overnight trading, mean reversion, and oscillator trading. Unlike long-term investing, which holds assets for years or decades, trading focuses on short-term price movements. Many day traders and scalpers lose money, and arbitrage and high-frequency trading are described as best left to institutions. The passage emphasizes research, backtesting with historical data, discipline, risk management, diversification, and controlling emotions such as fear and greed. Common indicators include moving averages, RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, and stochastic oscillators. Strategies can be automated with algorithms, enabling faster execution, fewer human errors, and management of many trades. Trading a single stock is presented as risky because any company can fail; research by Hendrik Bessembinder found only 43% of equities beat Treasury bills from 1926 to 2015. Diversification across stocks, sectors, and strategies is recommended for retail traders. Trading requires experience, and those unwilling to invest time and effort may be better served by ETFs and mutual funds.

On July 30, 1889, an insurrection led by Robert W. Wilcox and Robert Boyd was defeated, and the ringleader with about 60 followers was imprisoned. About 70 sailors and marines from the U.S.S. Adams were landed to protect life and property. A constitutional dispute between the King and cabinet was decided by the supreme court against the King. In March 1890, Mr. Blaine invited the King to the International American Conference, but Hawaii's delegate, Mr. Carter, arrived too late to participate. King Kalakaua died in San Francisco on January 20, 1891, and Princess Liliuokalani was proclaimed Queen. Mr. Stevens reported that the Queen was attempting to force ministers to resign, but a new Cabinet was appointed in spring 1891, allaying apprehensions. The prince consort died in August 1891. A project to revise the reciprocity treaty, prompted by the removal of the sugar tariff, led to Mr. Mott Smith's appointment as special envoy in late 1891, and a treaty-favorable legislature was elected in February 1892.

Deanthony Gordley, a Churchill High School senior in San Antonio, earned his diploma after overcoming homelessness. After moving to San Antonio following Hurricane Katrina, he lost his father to a shooting and later his mother to a heart attack, leaving him to sleep outside for about seven months. NEISD connected him to the McKinney Vento Homeless Project, and local families also helped him. He hopes to inspire others and shares his experiences through music sold on iTunes.

Jalen Carey's commitment gives Syracuse's 2018 class two Top 50 recruits (with Darius Bazley) plus Buddy Boeheim, likely its best in seven years. A list ranking SU's recruiting classes by arrival rankings follows.

Stripe, following its $1.1 billion acquisition of stablecoin startup Bridge, has launched Open Issuance, a product that lets businesses create and manage their own stablecoins and capture the yield earned from reserves backing them. The move, supported by legislation signed by President Trump in July establishing a stablecoin regulatory framework, aims to drive stablecoin adoption beyond crypto firms and potentially reshape global payments. Stripe-issued stablecoins will be interoperable, enabling conversions to U.S. dollars and integrations across blockchains. The first announced adopters—Phantom, Hyperliquid, and MetaMask—are all crypto companies. Stripe president William Gaybrick said he does not know when non-crypto firms will adopt stablecoins, but noted merchants will onboard mainstream U.S. consumers.

This email compiles news articles from May 12–13, 2001 that mention Enron. Key items include: University of California and California State University campuses preparing for possible rolling blackouts during final exams amid California's energy crisis, while the two systems are in a legal dispute with Enron Energy Services, which cut short a contract to supply them electricity; Moody's lowering British Telecom's credit rating after a £5.9 billion rights issue; a Houston Chronicle column urging Houston to invest in nanotechnology; the Center for Houston's Future, whose board includes Enron Chairman Ken Lay, developing plans to improve the city's education, economy, and quality of life; the Maharashtra State Electricity Board deciding not to acquire an additional 15 percent stake in Enron's Dabhol Power Company; Enron reportedly planning to withdraw from the Dolphin project to deliver Qatari gas to the UAE; a Houston yacht charter business listing Enron among its corporate clients; India's power sector struggling with reform, with Enron's Dabhol project mired in payment disputes; Indian officials expressing hope for a renegotiated Dabhol agreement as talks began between Enron and the Godbole committee; India offering to permit third-party power sales if DPC and MSEB jointly propose it; and Oregon Congressman Peter DeFazio proposing the state buy Portland General Electric, owned by Enron, to protect ratepayers, an idea that drew limited enthusiasm from legislators.
Kitagawa, Robson and Yaghi won the 2025 chemistry Nobel for metal-organic frameworks that trap gases, water and other chemicals.

The 3-2 zone defense is a variation of the 1-2-2 zone in which the point defender drops back to the free throw line, allowing wing defenders to play wider and deny wing passing lanes, disrupting zone offenses that typically begin with wing entry passes. It also protects against high post passes but allows point guard shots; if the point guard is a strong outside shooter, it can be adjusted to a 1-2-2 or 1-3-1 zone. Interchanging the point with a taller, active wing makes high post passes harder and lets the weakside baseline defender stay for rebounding. The defense is well-suited for fast breaks, and the passage outlines positional shifts for various ball locations.

Last week's market events—earnings, economic data, and political developments—were clouded by controversy, contradiction, or doubt, resulting in a risk-off shift. Earnings were strong, with 82% of S&P 500 companies beating EPS estimates and 79% beating revenue estimates, while earnings revisions reached multi-month highs. Eleventh-seeded Buffalo defeated No. 3 seed Florida State 86-65, with Cierra Dillard scoring 22 points, to reach the Sweet 16 for the first time in school history. Buffalo will face South Carolina on Saturday in Albany. Stephanie Reid added 18 points and Summer Hemphill 17, while Shakayla Thomas led Florida State with 25.

The global organic pigments market is projected to grow at approximately 4.5% during the forecast period to 2022, driven by demand from application industries such as paint & coating, plastics, textiles, and printing inks. Growth factors include cost effectiveness, consistency, unique shades, solvent stability, and non-toxicity. Asia-Pacific is expected to be the largest and fastest-growing market, with China creating opportunities for local and global players, while North America and Europe compete in value and volume. Key players include BASF SE, Dow Chemical Company, Huntsman Corporation, Clariant, Cabot Corporation, and Evonik Degussa. The report analyzes market segments by types, sources, applications, and regions, including competitive developments and strategic profiles of industry participants.

House prices in the West Midlands rose by around £12,000 on average last year to £181,000, according to an ONS report. UK-wide prices grew 7.2% in the year to December, with England strongest at 7.7%. Shetland saw the biggest rise (26.1%) and Aberdeen the largest fall (9.8%) due to the oil industry slump. Within the West Midlands, growth ranged from 10.4% in Wyre Forest and Kidderminster to 3.1% in South Staffordshire. PwC expects house price inflation to slow to 2-6% in 2017.

This patent application describes a storage system in which stacks of storage bins are housed within a framework formed by uprights and two sets of transverse parallel rails creating a grid pattern. Robotic load handling devices travel on the grid above the stacks to lift and retrieve containers. The invention's key feature is that the framework incorporates service means—such as power, data communications, lighting, fluid supply, and sensors—routed through the uprights and grid, enabling interaction, control, and monitoring of the system and individual containers from within the framework. Services may include water or gases (e.g., CO2 or nitrogen) for irrigation, greenhouse use, or fire suppression, which can be directed at individual containers to avoid widespread damage and costly shutdowns. Sensors on the framework allow continuous condition monitoring of the structure (e.g., via lasers, cameras, or electrical techniques) and detection of fire, smoke, heat, or gas while the system remains in use. Containers may have transparent or absent sides to admit light and may receive power through non-contact methods (magnetic or RF induction), contact brushes, or conductive pads and releasable latching connections. Connectors and sensing means (barcodes or cameras) identify containers so their contents can be controlled or monitored, including temperature, moisture, or nutrient levels. The system may also be partitioned into sections (e.g., ambient, chilled, frozen) using temporary, remotely deployable partitions for safety and environmental control.

The ADS9803 is a 20-bit, eight-channel data acquisition (DAQ) system from Texas Instruments featuring eight simultaneous-sampling SAR ADCs with a maximum throughput of 2MSPS per channel. Each channel includes an input clamp protection circuit (tolerating up to ±18V), a programmable gain amplifier supporting single-ended and differential bipolar inputs, and an antialiasing low-pass filter. The device operates from 5V and 1.8V analog supplies, maintains a constant 1MΩ input impedance, and includes a 4.096V internal reference with an external reference option. It features a common-mode rejection circuit supporting up to ±12V, outputs data in straight-binary or two's-complement formats, and supports 2-lane and 4-lane SDR/DDR interfaces. Additional features include a data output randomizer, simple and moving average modes, test patterns for interface debugging, and a speed-boost mode allowing up to 8MSPS for a selected channel pair. Configuration is performed via SPI with register banks and daisy-chain topology support. The device targets ATE applications, achieving 0.0015% total unadjusted error post-calibration, and requires a free-running sampling clock with an initialization sequence after power-up or reset.

Mineral companies owe more than $42 million in delinquent taxes to 12 Wyoming counties, largely because bankrupt companies leave county debts unpaid, as counties are treated as low-priority unsecured lenders, according to a Powder River Basin Resource Council report. Campbell County is owed the most, over $26 million, followed by Sheridan County at about $7.46 million, mostly from Storm Cat Energy and Summit Gas. An 18-month county tax payment schedule contributes to delinquencies, unlike the state's quicker severance tax schedule. About 75 percent of mineral taxes fund school districts and other public services; Sheridan County educational entities are owed roughly $2.95 million combined. The report recommends monthly ad valorem tax collection, perpetual liens, a state funding pool for bankruptcies, and legislation allowing tax debt checks before asset transfers. Similar bills failed in 2016 and 2017, though a new bill is proposed this year.

UNMC College of Dentistry in Lincoln held Children's Dental Day, providing free dental services to 159-200 Nebraska children annually. Running since 2001, the program has delivered over $3 million in dental work while teaching kids oral care.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2021. Net sales increased 44% year-over-year to $108.5 billion, with net income of $8.1 billion and operating income of $8.9 billion, up from $2.5 billion and $4.0 billion respectively in Q1 2020. Diluted earnings per share were $15.79 versus $5.01 in the prior year.

By segment, North America net sales grew 40% to $64.4 billion with operating income of $3.5 billion; International sales grew 60% to $30.6 billion with operating income of $1.3 billion (versus a $398 million loss in the prior year); and AWS sales grew 32% to $13.5 billion with operating income of $4.2 billion.

The company incurred approximately $2.0 billion in COVID-19 related costs in Q1 2021, with increased demand partially offset by fulfillment network capacity and supply chain constraints.

As of March 31, 2021, total assets were $323.1 billion and stockholders' equity was $103.3 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $73.3 billion. Operating cash flow was $4.2 billion for the quarter. Long-term debt included $32.2 billion of unsecured senior notes, $429 million outstanding under a secured Credit Facility, and $725 million of commercial paper; no borrowings were outstanding under the $7.0 billion unsecured revolving Credit Agreement.

The company had $12.4 billion of net unrecognized stock-based compensation cost and made no common stock repurchases during the quarter. Tax contingencies were approximately $3.0 billion, and the company continues to contest a European Commission state aid decision regarding Luxembourg taxes involving an estimated recovery amount of approximately €250 million.

For Q2 2021, Amazon guided net sales of $110.0–$116.0 billion (24–30% growth) and operating income of $4.5–$8.0 billion, assuming approximately $1.5 billion of COVID-19 related costs.

Boxing out on free throws is vital, as offensive rebounds are "Really Big Plays" that can cost championships. Defenders should stand with feet together, step up the lane, keep hands elbow-high, and communicate to box out the shooter, which can also disrupt concentration. Against strong rebounders, players may pinch (double team), and as many defenders as rules allow should occupy the lane line. Teams should also practice an early push off made and missed free throws to create outnumbered scoring chances.

The article backtests the options expiration week (OPEX week) effect in US stocks. US-listed stock options expire on the Friday before the third Saturday of each month, shifting to Thursday when Friday is a public holiday. Backtests using SPY show the S&P 500 earns above-average returns during OPEX week—a 2% CAGR and 0.2% average weekly gain while invested only about 18% of the time—with QQQ averaging 0.25% per trade. The effect appears only from 1990 onward and varies by month, with July and January negative. The article attributes the effect to declining option open interest and "pin risk" near expiration. In contrast, OPEX day itself shows negative average returns, even with a 50-day moving average filter. The week after OPEX week underperforms (1.5% CAGR), with August the best month and September the worst (average loss 0.94%). The day before OPEX shows weak S&P 500 returns but strong bond returns, while the day after is negative for both. Quadruple witching occurs in March, June, September, and December. A backtest of EU futures found no consistent edge. The article concludes the effect exists but needs additional parameters to be tradeable, and provides OPEX calendars for 2025–2026.

This MIT lecture reviews a case study in which students calculated the corporate carbon footprint of WidgetCo, a chair manufacturer with a fully owned Michigan plant, a 50-50 joint venture plant in Shanghai, two US distribution centers, and a private truck fleet. Competitor FerretCo disclosed 55,000 tons of CO2 (1.1 kg per product) and announced carbon neutrality and product-labeling plans.

The lecture explains footprint mechanics: emissions are calculated by multiplying activity data by emissions factors, using fuel consumption where available or ton-mile based methods for shared transportation. A common error is multiplying aggregated shipment weights and distances, which overstates ton-miles. Footprints typically cover the six Kyoto gases, expressed in CO2-equivalence using global warming potentials that are periodically updated by the IPCC.

Emissions are classified as Scope 1 (direct), Scope 2 (purchased electricity), and Scope 3 (all other indirect). Organizational boundaries may be set via equity share or control approaches, making the Shanghai plant's emissions 0%, 50%, or 100% includable. The GHG Protocol requires Scope 1 and 2 but leaves Scope 3 optional; inclusion often depends on data availability and perceived responsibility rather than emissions magnitude, as CDP data shows business travel is widely reported but small, while product use is large but rarely reported.

Data gathering remains largely manual, with challenges including missing values, aggregation issues, unit conversions, and consistent emissions factor selection. Disclosure discussion noted CDP response rates growing to roughly 80% of large companies, driven mainly by investors rather than consumers. Comparing WidgetCo and FerretCo shows how boundary choices (e.g., contract manufacturing) skew comparisons; Apple owns only about 2% of its end-to-end emissions, and manufacturers' Scope 1 and 2 emissions average around 25% of supply chain totals. The GHG Protocol's newer value chain and product standards were introduced, leading into the next topic, life cycle assessment.

This retrospective study analyzed records of 1,383 noma patients managed at the Noma Children's Hospital in Sokoto, Nigeria—the country's only dedicated noma specialist hospital—between 1999 and 2024 to estimate noma incidence and describe clinical presentation in northern Nigeria. Using a WHO-based method, the study estimated 62,067 new cases and an overall incidence of 114.5 cases per 100,000 population (males: 120.7; females: 108.1), with annual average and median incidences of 4.4 and 2.2 cases per 100,000. Annual incidence ranged from 0.2 (2014) to 21.3 (2021) per 100,000, increasing significantly between 2020 and 2024. Sokoto state had the highest incidence (921.9 per 100,000) and Adamawa the lowest (6.3). Incidence was highest among children under ten years (399.9 per 100,000 for those under five). Most patients (67.3%) presented with acute noma, with gangrene (stage 3) being the most common stage (59.7%); the incidence of gangrene (101.5 per 100,000) exceeded that of oedema (12.4) and acute necrotizing ulcerative gingivitis (0.6). The cheeks were the most affected anatomic sites. Sokoto had the highest incidence among those under 18, while Kebbi had the highest incidence among young and middle-aged adults. The findings underscore the need for noma awareness and screening programs to detect early, reversible stages of the disease.

Eliud Kipchoge, fresh from his third London Marathon title, visited Tottenham Hotspur, meeting Victor Wanyama, coach Patrick Sang, and Mauricio Pochettino. Crowned World Marathon Majors Champion, he is expected to attempt Dennis Kimetto's world record at September's Berlin Marathon.

This study investigated barriers to distance education among 13 faculty members teaching university mathematics education courses in Turkey, where online learning was reinstated after the February 2023 earthquake (following the COVID-19 pandemic) because student dormitories were used to house those left homeless. Using Q methodology, participants ranked 50 statements derived from the literature on e-learning barriers, followed by semi-structured interviews with two participants. Principal component analysis with Varimax rotation identified three factors: student-related barriers (Factor 1, six participants), technology-related barriers such as insufficient digital library access (Factor 2, five participants), and pedagogical barriers specific to mathematics, including unreliable online assessment and the inadequacy of graphic tablets compared to blackboards (Factor 4, two participants). Contrary to expectations based on the literature, no teacher-related barrier factor emerged. Overall, curriculum-pedagogy barriers received the highest average Z score, followed by teacher, technology, and student barriers. All participants agreed that distance education alone is unsuitable for mathematics education and favored blended or hybrid models for the future. The study concluded that its findings were consistent with the general literature, identified obstacles unique to mathematics due to its pedagogy and curriculum, and demonstrated that Q methodology is a suitable tool for examining barriers to distance education in emergency contexts.

This patent application, a continuation of multiple prior filings, describes systems for securely sharing encrypted data between multiple users, with emphasis on healthcare applications. The disclosure identifies problems with existing approaches, including burdensome EMR requirements, poor patient portal enrollment, risks of server-side key storage, and cloud storage in which users do not control their own encryption keys. The described techniques use multiple layers of encryption organized in a key hierarchy structure (KHS) containing a data encryption key (DEK), a master encryption key (MEK), a password-based derived key (PDK), and a questions-based derived key (QDK). Derived keys are generated from user credentials—passwords or security question answers—using functions such as PBKDF2 with salt values and initialization vectors. User data is encrypted client-side, and keys are withheld from the server, enabling "zero knowledge" operation in which the server and cloud provider cannot access encrypted data. Sharing between two users employs public key encryption, with recipients' public keys retrieved from a global lookup directory and data decrypted using recipients' private keys. For group sharing, a shared data key hierarchy structure (SD-KHS) stores encrypted shared data encryption keys (ESDEKs) for each authorized user, and edits to shared data require owner approval via encrypted notifications. The application further describes client device architecture, registration and login processes, key replacement procedures, and secure sharing initiated through a printer driver.

Noe Martinez Paredes appealed his guilty-plea conviction and 57-month sentence for conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine and heroin. His counsel filed an Anders brief finding no grounds for relief and moved to withdraw. The Ninth Circuit's independent review found no arguable grounds for relief, granted the withdrawal motion, and affirmed.

Researchers have identified bacterial strains on grape plant leaves that can degrade guaiacol, a key volatile phenol responsible for the ashy aftertaste, known as smoke taint, in wine exposed to wildfire smoke. In lab tests, the bacteria nearly eliminated guaiacol within 96 hours, and scientists identified the gene responsible for this degradation. The finding could offer winemakers a more targeted alternative to current mitigation methods like charcoal filtering, which can also remove desirable wine components. However, the bacteria are selective and do not break down other smoky compounds, so further research is needed to address the full range of volatile phenols that contribute to smoke taint.

Barbeque Nation Hospitality has filed a DRHP with Sebi for an IPO comprising a Rs 200 crore fresh issue and an offer for sale of 61.79 lakh shares, or 14.22% of post-offer capital. Proceeds will fund new restaurants, loan repayment, and general corporate purposes.

Telstra CEO Andy Penn faces pressure to deliver positive news at the upcoming investor day, with his job at stake. The share price has fallen since a disguised earnings downgrade and S&P Global's downgrade. Analysts expect dividend cuts in 2019, though recent analyst commentary has eased.

Indiana State Police say the case remains active, with over 24,000 tips, a July 17 suspect sketch drawing more than 3,000 tips, and near-daily DNA testing. This document is the March 2006 specification update (31534D) for the AMD Geode™ CS5535 Companion Device, Silicon Revision A3. It catalogs numerous hardware errata, each with a description, implications, and where available, a resolution or workaround. Notable issues include: PIT deviations from industry-standard read-back behavior and incorrect count mode 3 value loading; a debug port that hangs the system; XPIC failures with auto-end-of-interrupt; DMA rotating priority not rotating correctly; lack of thermal alarm recovery in Faulted Standby; UART registers inaccessible during block/demand DMA; system hangs on I/O cycles at addresses 10000h or higher; failure to meet the USB over-voltage protection specification; PIC failures when an interrupt remains high after clock gating; UDMA write CRC corruption following device termination; hangs on byte accesses to ACPI PM1_STS/PM1_EN registers; WORD/BYTE writes to PMC registers potentially corrupting other registers; KEL emulation and Snoop mode defects; USB controller clock gating failures; IRDY#/DEVSEL# timing violations (1.5 ns versus the specified 2 ns); unreliable SSMI generation; failed PIO access when the UDMA bus master is enabled first; most wake event inputs not functioning from the ACPI S3 state; RTC CMOS RAM read errors; LPC I/O failures during block/demand DMA; ATAC hangs with non-DWORD-aligned PRD addresses; LPC aborts on certain SYNC patterns; SMB controller NEGACK bit issues; GPIO High Bank Feature Bit register corruption after suspend; insufficient SMBus data hold time; missing LOWBAT_FLAG after abnormal standby; and Sleep_X not deasserting when delays exceed the PM_SED delay. Many issues carry no operational impact or include workarounds such as avoiding specific features, using alternative modes, or adding external circuitry. The document concludes with AMD's copyright notice, disclaimers, and trademark information.

This study compares interdisciplinary research (IDR) in highly impactful medical journals (top 10% of SJR) versus less impactful journals by constructing co-occurrence networks of second-level MeSH disease terms from PubMed articles for 1999, 2010, and 2022. Results show less impactful journals produce more interdisciplinary work, with higher network coherence, density, and lower modularity, while impactful journals are more compartmentalised. Stable inner cores of tightly connected concepts exist across all networks, and cancer-related research (Neoplasms) is identified as a main driver of interdisciplinarity by bridging distant knowledge clusters. Analysis of positive and negative difference networks (I minus NI-June) reveals a weak tendency for strong differences to co-locate, and differences cluster around topic areas that change substantially over time, in contrast to a stable, universal core knowledge structure shared by both journal types. The authors conclude that impactful medical journals publish relatively more disciplinary-based research, potentially due to peer review penalising innovative work and compliance infrastructures (trial registration, CONSORT/PRISMA standards) favouring discipline-anchored studies, and suggest accommodating IDR evaluation within existing compliance infrastructures.

A Legislative Analyst's Office report says Gov. Jerry Brown's administration has a "weak justification" for a tentative contract offering the California Correctional Peace Officers Association a 5 percent raise—the largest since 2006—for its 27,000 members. The analyst found no recruitment or retention problems justifying the increase, citing rising entry-level officer numbers, stable mid-career staffing, limited outside job prospects, and wages that have outpaced inflation since 2001. CCPOA members are voting on the one-year contract, which also requires legislative approval. The administration estimates it will cost $338 million over two years, though the analyst warns costs could be higher due to overtime and pension contributions.

Bodycam footage from Wildwood, New Jersey shows 20-year-old mother Emily Weinman being "slammed" to the ground during Memorial Day weekend after refusing to give officers her last name during an underage drinking check. She passed a breathalyser and the alcohol was unopened. An officer said she tried kicking them, though this isn't visible in footage, and that he hit her and put her in cuffs. Mayor Ernie Troian said Weinman escalated the situation and the footage would vindicate police. A viral video of the arrest sparked online outrage. The officers were reassigned to desk duty pending an investigation, and Weinman was charged with offences including aggravated assault on police and minor in possession of alcohol.

Archaeologists have confirmed that a mass grave beside St. Wystan's church in Repton, Derbyshire, holds remains of over 250 members of the Viking Great Heathen Army, buried in winter 874. A new study in Antiquity, led by Cat Jarmine of the University of Bristol, found earlier carbon dating was skewed by the marine reservoir effect—a seafood-rich diet altering carbon isotopes. Once corrected, dates matched the invasion recorded in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicles. The site shows distinctive burials, including a double grave with a sword and Thor's hammer pendant, a boar's tusk possibly replacing a genital injury, and four apparent child sacrifices. Earlier doubts—female remains and few battle injuries—were also addressed.

Camp America offers students a summer work opportunity at camps across the USA, with no specific qualifications required, though tennis coaching, horse riding or lifeguarding skills are in demand. With over 8,000 places available, early application is recommended, and applications go live to 1,000 American camps. Camp America also holds the UK's largest summer camp recruitment fair in January and February, with over 200 camps hiring on the spot. A former camper described a typical day beginning at 7am, featuring activities like swimming, archery and sailing. The programme costs £599, covering application fees, medical insurance, a 30-day travel period and return flights, plus pocket money of $650-$1200. Applicants must be over 18, and the experience is said to provide useful skills for future careers.

This lecture covers simplified equilibria used in plasma spectroscopy and X-ray imaging techniques. Complete thermodynamic equilibrium, where electrons, ions, and radiation share a single temperature and every process balances its opposite, is rarely realized because it requires an optically thick system. Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) assumes an optically thin plasma in which collisional processes dominate level populations and cross-sections become unimportant due to process balance; this yields the Saha equilibrium, which gives ionization state populations for a given temperature. Coronal (collisional-radiative) equilibrium applies to low-density, optically thin plasmas where excitation is collisional but spontaneous emission de-excites the system before another collision occurs. Non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (nLTE) requires solving all relevant processes for the specific plasma being modeled.

The lecturer described a workflow for spectroscopic modeling: assume a density and temperature, determine the appropriate equilibrium, calculate ionization and excited state populations, compute line strengths, predict the spectrum (accounting for radiation transport, reflections, and detector response when necessary), and compare with experimental data, iterating as needed. The line ratio technique provides a shortcut: measuring the intensities of strong, isolated, identified lines from different ionization states allows inference of ion population ratios, which—combined with an equilibrium model such as Saha—can yield the plasma temperature.

In X-ray spectroscopy, relevant for fusion plasmas, characteristic lines arise from transitions to low energy levels: K-shell transitions (K-alpha from n=2 to n=1, K-beta from n=3 to n=1) are the strongest and highest energy atomic lines and serve as signatures of impurities. Ions with only a few remaining electrons are described as helium-like or lithium-like. X-ray filters exploit absorption edges—sharp increases in absorption when photon energies match inner-shell excitation thresholds—to isolate particular energy ranges; edge positions depend on the filter element.

Since the refractive index is roughly 1 for X-rays, lenses cannot be used. Pinhole imaging provides inverted, magnified (v/u) images but suffers from geometric blur, proportional to (M+1) times the pinhole diameter, and diffraction blur of 1.22λ/d, requiring a trade-off in pinhole size. Bent crystals enable monochromatic imaging, acting as both filter and focusing element, but are expensive.

Detectors discussed include film (high resolution and well characterized but time-integrated and increasingly unavailable), image plates (reusable, storing X-ray excitation in metastable states read out by laser scanning), time-gated cameras (fast but costly and low resolution), and streak cameras, which record intensity versus position and time using swept electron beams; streak cameras are very fast but highly non-linear and prone to breaking.

Researchers at Aarhus University, in cooperation with dairy company Arla, studied how on-farm milk concentration using reverse osmosis affects milk quality. PhD student Ida Sørensen and Associate Professor Lars Wiking examined key quality parameters, including protein breakdown, free fatty acid (FFA) levels, and total bacterial count. Their analyses showed that neither bacterial count, FFA levels, nor protein breakdown were negatively affected by reverse osmosis, and the concentrated milk was suitable for both cheese and milk powder. Milk powder quality and durability matched that made from ordinary milk, though concentrated milk coagulated approximately ten minutes later in cheese experiments. Implementation models include farmer-purchased, dairy-owned, or leased equipment, with herd size and distance to the dairy affecting profitability. Farmers showed significant interest, while dairies appeared more skeptical; Arla is currently calculating profitability.
Agriculture and fertiliser stocks rose up to 13 percent after the government hiked the minimum support price for paddy by a record Rs 200 per quintal; the cabinet approved MSP for 14 kharif crops.

Nested virtualization is unsupported under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP. Safe isolation for SNP-protected guests requires SNP RestrictInjection, limiting the host to doorbell #HV exceptions. A common format is defined for OS-level notifications, while driver-specific information remains flexible for optimization.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig of the Southern District of Florida was fired by email after conservatives published past blog posts attributed to him criticizing President Trump. Commentator Natalie Winters cited alleged posts calling Trump "mentally unfit" and "an institutional terrorist." Rosenzweig, who joined the office in September 2020, worked in the economic crimes section. The DOJ also fired three other Florida prosecutors who had worked with Jack Smith, who prosecuted Trump.

The British Foreign Secretary, in a note forwarded to the United States Government, responds to the President's peace message, agreeing with his desire for lasting peace but arguing that peace's durability depends on its terms. He attributes the war to dominating powers, unenforced international law, and boundaries misaligned with national aspirations, which the Allies' proposed territorial changes in Europe would address. He defends expelling Turkey from Europe, citing its aggression under German control and massacres in Armenia and Syria. However, he argues territorial changes alone cannot prevent future war, as Germany could retain its military system and strike pacific neighbors. He also rejects reliance on treaties and international law alone, noting Germany refused arbitration treaties, glorified war, and overran a country it was pledged to defend, making treaties alone insufficient protection for any state's rights.

The passage presents a selection of credit card offers featuring 0% introductory APR periods, which CompareCards says range from 12 to 21 months and can help consumers carrying balances or planning large purchases save money. Featured cards include Bank of America options with 15 billing cycles of 0% intro APR, cash back rewards (6% in a choice category the first year, a $200 online bonus), and a travel rewards card offering 25,000 bonus points; Capital One's Quicksilver (unlimited 1.5% cash back, $300 welcome bonus) and VentureOne (1.25 miles per dollar) cards with 15-month 0% intro APR; Citi cards with 18-month 0% balance transfer APR, 2% cash back, and ThankYou Points cards with 30,000 bonus points; and Discover cards featuring Unlimited Cashback Match and 5% quarterly category cash back. The passage explains that low-rate cards come in variable APR forms, tied to rates such as the prime rate, and fixed APR forms, which remain relatively stable. Introductory offers typically last 6 to 21 months at 0% to 3.99% before reverting to regular rates, and the interest rate is described as the most important component of a credit card. Editors evaluate over 100 cards from more than 50 issuers using an objective rating system, and compensation from listed companies does not influence ratings or reviews.

Steve Stephens, a 37-year-old job counselor, is accused of fatally shooting 74-year-old Robert Godwin Sr. in Cleveland and posting video of the killing on Facebook, where it remained for about three hours. Police have not determined a motive; Stephens said in a video that he "snapped" and blamed a former girlfriend, who said he had been good to her and her children. Godwin appeared to have been chosen at random while collecting aluminum cans. Authorities offered a $50,000 reward as the manhunt expanded nationwide; Stephens' cellphone was last detected in Erie, Pennsylvania. Nine Philadelphia schools were locked down over possible sightings, but no sign of him was found. Acquaintances described him as kind but noted a gambling problem and a 2015 bankruptcy. Detectives tried unsuccessfully to persuade him to surrender by phone.

The author draws parallels between dating and choosing a content marketing partner, offering five tips: find a provider whose interests and strategy align with yours; interview multiple candidates rather than settling on the first; verify claims by requesting client references, work samples, and measurable results; make a list of your needs to clarify what you want; and begin with a trial period before committing. The right partner should make your work easier and be enjoyable to work with.

Thermal alarm causes Faulted Standby with no PMC self-recovery, since the alarm resides in the Work domain and its timer is blocked during Standby. Power removal cools the system; if the alarm persists, Standby recurs.

Play action is a pass play designed to look like a run in order to deceive the defense. The quarterback fakes a handoff to the running back, bootlegs out, and looks for an open receiver downfield. It is most effective when a team has established a strong run game, as defenses committed to stopping the run will overcommit to the line of scrimmage, leaving space behind the linebackers and safeties. The entire offense must sell the fake, with the offensive line switching from run to pass protection and receivers running routes such as crosses and drags that exploit the vacated space. Play action is best called in run-heavy situations like short yardage, goal line, and red zone plays; the highest-percentage teams run it between 30 and 40% of the time. Common concepts include the Double Post, featuring two receivers on deep post routes, and Bubble Y Over, a spread concept offering at least four passing options. Unlike a Run Pass Option (RPO), which can become either a run or a quick pass depending on the defense's reaction, a play action pass is always a pass, merely disguised as a run.

Gold rallied strongly on Friday as the USD Index declined, but gold remains below its rising resistance line and continues to follow its 2011-2013 price pattern, similar to the November 2012 rally. Notably, mining stocks, including the VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF (GDXJ), failed to rally alongside gold, with GDXJ closing below its April high for a third consecutive day. The author states that gold stocks normally outperform gold early in rallies, and this opposite behavior suggests the early stage of a larger decline. The USD Index has verified an inverse head-and-shoulders pattern by returning to its neck level near its July high, with a projected rally target of at least 101.3. Stocks, after failing to exceed previous highs and falling below a rising support line, show bearish signals and may decline significantly. The author compares the current situation to 2008 and says the "Peak Chaos" theory remains intact. A reader comment criticizes the analysis as non-standard technical analysis.

Resolute Marine Energy (RME), founded by Bill Staby in 2007, developed Wave O™2, a wave-driven desalination system that used ocean wave power to produce fresh water. The company targeted communities lacking affordable fresh water and reliable electricity, selecting South Africa as its launch market due to significant water stress and weak electric grids, with the municipality of Ugu as its pilot site. RME signed an MOU with Ugu and sought $6 million in funding, with potential support from the Development Bank of South Africa and impact investors.

The company faced a strategic decision among three commercialization approaches: (1) producing electricity to power an off-the-shelf desalination plant, which had access to U.S. government grants but lower margins and competitive risks; (2) using hydraulic power to run desalination directly, as depicted in its business plan, offering higher water-based margins and lower production costs but requiring private investment and a desalination partner; and (3) developing an integrated "black box" system producing both water and electricity, which was most ambitious but capital-intensive and complex. Each option involved trade-offs regarding funding, partnerships, pricing, and technical challenges. RME also pursued a potential electricity opportunity in Alaska as a learning platform. The core question was whether RME should define itself as an energy company, a water company, or something more complex.

The Federal Circuit affirmed the Court of Federal Claims' judgment awarding $250,000 in death benefits under the Public Safety Officers' Benefits Act (PSOBA) to the estate of Christine H. Roberts. Roberts, the mother of Sheriff Harold Ray Presley of Lee County, Mississippi, who was fatally shot in the line of duty in July 2001, filed a benefits claim but died in September 2001 before the Bureau of Justice Assistance issued payment. The Bureau denied the estate's claim, reasoning that benefits were payable only to living beneficiaries. The trial court reversed, holding that eligibility is determined at the time of the officer's death.

Writing for the majority, Judge Moore held that the statutory term "surviving" means alive at the time of the public safety officer's death, at which point the beneficiary's rights vest. Because the statute was unambiguous on this issue, the agency's interpretation requiring survival until payment was not entitled to Chevron deference. The court also rejected the government's arguments based on legislative history, statutory purpose, and a 2006 regulation requiring payment to living payees, finding each contrary to the statute's clear language.

Judge Prost dissented, arguing that the precise question was whether estates are eligible recipients of PSOBA benefits, an issue on which the statute is silent or ambiguous. She would defer to the Bureau's permissible interpretation limiting payment to living payees, noting that the majority's reading could divert benefits to estates rather than other living eligible beneficiaries and could allow proceeds to pass to statutorily ineligible adult children.

New York Attorney General Schneiderman announced the arrest of Guilderland Town Judge Richard Sherwood and financial advisor Thomas Lagan for allegedly stealing $4 million from trusts they oversaw as trustees, funded by philanthropists Warren and Pauline Bruggeman. Both face felony charges including grand larceny and scheme to defraud.

Jaroslaw Buczkowski pleaded guilty at Boston Magistrates Court to driving with excess alcohol after being caught speeding at up to 70mph in 40mph zones on New Year's Day, with a breath reading more than twice the legal limit. He was banned for 20 months, fined £350, and ordered to pay £120 in costs.

Apple's stock fell 6% over two days in June 2017 on heavier volume while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq reached new all-time highs, and it now behaves like a "growth cyclical." Fiscal 2017–2019 consensus EPS estimates have risen since May 31, though revenue estimates slipped slightly. Apple previously underwent two major corrections: a 45% decline from late 2012 to April 2013, signaled by falling EPS estimates, and a 37% decline from early 2015 to May 2016, driven more by macro events such as China's currency devaluation. Current estimates project 8% and 16% EPS growth for fiscal 2017 and 2018, with the stock trading at 14x–16x forward earnings. The author, long AAPL, sold a small amount on June 12, citing concerns that high iPhone "supercycle" expectations and a $765 billion market cap may mean the stock is entering early stages of lagging relative performance, with the $133–$134 level from early 2015 identified as a key technical threshold.

The AEGEAN study evaluated apixaban adherence and persistence in subjects with atrial fibrillation. Mean compliance exceeded 95% at Weeks 4, 12, and 24 and was comparable across study groups. At 24 weeks, adherence was 91.64% in the Primary SOC group and 91.88% in the Additional Educational Program group, with no significant difference. Adherence declined over time, being significantly lower between Weeks 12–24 than from first dose to Week 12, and between Weeks 24–48 than from first dose to Week 24. From first dose to Week 48, adherence was 89.52% (Primary SOC) and 90.93% (Additional Educational Program), with no significant differences. Persistence was 91.7% vs 91.3% at 24 weeks and 85.2%–87.8% across groups at 48 weeks, without significant differences. Fully adherent subjects comprised 28.1% vs 26.5% at 24 weeks and approximately 14.5%–14.9% at 48 weeks. Logit models identified predictors of non-adherence, including alcohol consumption, technical occupations, permanent atrial fibrillation, and MMSE score. Safety endpoints were similar between groups, with comparable adverse event, bleeding, and death rates. The study concluded that adherence and persistence were high and sustained through 48 weeks, and the educational program provided no additional benefit.

This paper examines digital business models for digital startups in Industrial Era 4.0, an era in which companies depend on information technology. Digital startups in Indonesia have grown rapidly, but poor management and low business model exploitation have led to losses and bankruptcy. A business model describes how a company serves customers, organizes itself, and generates value, acting as a bridge between technology, ideas, and potential customers.

The study used a descriptive qualitative method applying the Canvas Business Model to digital startups. Data came from semi-structured interviews with 120 respondents (founders, project managers, coworkers, and customers), selected through purposive sampling, with validity ensured through data source triangulation.

The lean canvas business model consists of nine components: customer segments, value propositions (including newness, customization, accessibility, and convenience), channels, customer relationships, revenue streams, key resources, key activities, key partnerships, and cost structure. It is applied through nine steps: determining target customers, formulating and validating problems, finding solutions, establishing a unique value proposition, selecting channels to gather customers, defining income streams, determining cost structure, setting key metrics (KPIs), and identifying unfair advantages.

The model was implemented in a digital startup called "Beautiful Memories," which addresses problems such as limited photo, video, decoration, and souvenir packages, and difficulty quickly finding photographers, video editors, and decoration services. Its solution connects customers with service providers without package restrictions, offering certifications for photographers, video editors, souvenirs, and decoration services. Target customers include couples getting married, families, birthdays, graduations, and official or non-official events, using social media as its channel and earning 10% of each service order.

This study reports the discovery of a symmetry-broken state in CoSn2, a structurally simple, three-dimensional intermetallic compound primarily used for battery storage. Resistivity measurements show a slope change below 25 K, but no anomalies appear in specific heat or magnetic susceptibility, ruling out magnetic or strong structural transitions. Single-crystal x-ray diffraction reveals weak superlattice reflections at commensurate wavevectors q1 = (1/2, 0, 1/2) and q2 = (0, 1/2, 1/2) below 22 K, indicating a superstructure with doubled a and c axes and symmetry lowering from tetragonal I4/mcm to acentric monoclinic C2, accompanied by loss of fourfold rotational symmetry in the Sn layer. Angle-dependent magnetoresistance independently confirms a fourfold-to-twofold symmetry reduction below ~20 K. Phonon calculations show no imaginary frequencies, indicating the parent lattice is dynamically stable, while electronic susceptibility calculations reveal instabilities at the N and X points suggestive of Fermi surface nesting that can break rotational symmetry electronically (nematic order). Polarization-dependent ARPES shows fourfold symmetry under LH polarization but strong intensity asymmetry under LV polarization, suggesting orbital-driven electronic nematicity, though further investigation is needed. ARPES and DFT also identify type-I and type-II Dirac crossings forming a nodal loop near the Fermi level. The authors conclude that CoSn2 is a platform for studying symmetry breaking in an itinerant, nonmagnetic nodal-line semimetal, extending nematicity beyond strongly correlated systems.

This paper presents a causal Bayesian Network (BN) model developed to improve the clinical diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease (AD). AD is a neurodegenerative disease characterised by amyloid beta plaques and tau tangles, with three phases: preclinical AD, mild cognitive impairment due to AD (AD MCI), and AD dementia. Clinical diagnosis has shortcomings, including physician discomfort and estimated misdiagnosis rates of 12–23%, partly because symptoms are not disease-specific.

Unlike black-box machine learning models, BNs are interpretable and support causal reasoning. The proposed model distinguishes between having AD ('Suspected AD') and being formally diagnosed ('Diagnosed AD'), applies medical idioms proposed by Kyrimi et al., and covers both early- and late-onset AD. Existing BN models were criticised for lacking clinically relevant variables and not making this distinction.

The model structure includes conditions, signs/symptoms, medical tests (cognitive and biomarker), risk factors (age, family history, traumatic brain injury, causal mutations), comorbidities (depression), complications, and treatment, based on validated NIA-AA diagnostic criteria. Parameters were specified using the NACC UDS dataset, literature data, and knowledge-based judgement.

Validation demonstrated internal consistency (prior probability of suspected AD of 3.336%, matching estimated prevalence) and external consistency through clinical scenarios showing 'explaining away', backward reasoning, and the effects of biomarker tests and independence level on diagnosis.

The authors conclude the model can serve as a complementary diagnostic tool but note weaknesses: coarse aggregation of non-AD conditions, reliance on data from diagnosed patients, missing causal relationships, and manually set parameters. Future work includes modelling individual dementia conditions separately, using post-mortem data, expanding early-onset AD details, and developing a research-focused BN including preclinical AD.

Const. Ken Lam has been identified as the Toronto police officer who arrested the suspect in Monday's van attack, which killed 10 people and injured 15. In *Vansickle v. Brown*, the Missouri Supreme Court affirmed a judgment for the defendant in a malicious prosecution action. Susan Ann Vansickle, arrested at the instance of Brown, a road overseer, for obstructing a public highway, waived a preliminary examination, entered a recognizance, was indicted, and sued after a nolle prosequi was entered. The court held: (1) evidence of the arresting officer's uncivil conduct was inadmissible absent proof the defendant instigated it; (2) a trespass judgment obtained by plaintiff's husband after the criminal proceedings began was properly excluded, since probable cause is determined by circumstances existing when the prosecution was instituted; (3) later county court road proceedings were properly excluded because they did not vacate the established road; (4) verbal directions from the county court were admissible to show the defendant's good faith and lack of malice, though not to establish the road's legality; (5) a party may testify to his own good faith and intentions. The court defined probable cause as belief in the plaintiff's guilt founded on reasonable grounds, overruling *Hickman v. Griffin* and re-affirming *Hill v. Palm*. Waiver of examination and entry of a recognizance constituted prima facie evidence of probable cause. Malice must be independently shown; want of probable cause alone is insufficient, and malice is not inferred as a matter of law from lack of probable cause. Napton, J., dissented in part, and Henry, J., dissented as to the waiver instruction.

This document describes AMD's Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine, an optional extension to the Secure Encrypted Virtualization (SEV) API and SEV Secure Nested Paging (SNP) firmware ABI that facilitates page migration—the copying of page content and updating of virtual-to-physical mappings. TMPM support is detected via the ENGINE_READY bit in the PM_Status register and requires IOMMU enablement. The engine off-loads page migration and addresses two challenges: it can pause DMA traffic while page content is copied and IOMMU page table entries are updated, and it acts as a trusted agent able to migrate guest pages protected by SEV/SNP that the hypervisor or OS cannot otherwise access.

Key commands include PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, which migrates pages that may be concurrent DMA targets (requiring the location of the relevant IOMMU host Page Table Entry); PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST, which migrates SNP guest pages (source pages in Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid state, destinations in Pre-Migration state); PM_GET_CAPABILITIES; and PM_NOOP. Commands can migrate up to 128 pages via a Page Migration List with no order-dependence between entries. A PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS status requires checking per-page status entries; PM_SUCCESS indicates all pages migrated; other codes indicate none were executed.

Performance guidance recommends commands with 16 or more pages (128 for maximum performance), keeping the ring buffer ahead of the engine, and avoiding interrupts on every command. Non-migratable structures include IOMMU memory data structures, vIOMMU page tables and pinned buffers, and the ring buffer itself. All migrated system physical addresses must be 4KB aligned. TMPM firmware may be reloaded only when no operations are in flight, and the reload firmware version must be the same or greater; EPYC Family 19h is identified by an FW_VER_Major value of 71. Ring buffer errors are reported in the PM_STATUS register, while hardware errors during batch processing can render all pages in that command unrecoverable.

On August 8, 2022, Apple Inc. completed the issuance and sale of $1,000,000,000 of 3.250% Notes due 2029, $1,500,000,000 of 3.350% Notes due 2032, $1,750,000,000 of 3.950% Notes due 2052, and $1,250,000,000 of 4.100% Notes due 2062, pursuant to an underwriting agreement dated August 1, 2022 with Goldman Sachs & Co. Nearly seven months after its Sept. 30 inception with $100,000 in virtual dollars, the model Yield Hog Dividend Growth Portfolio is down about 2 per cent including dividends, but its annualized dividend income has grown about 6.7 per cent, from $4,094 to $4,369, as 17 of 22 holdings raised payouts and dividends were reinvested. The author says the portfolio illustrates dividend-growth investing rather than serving as a template. Despite pipeline stocks facing rising bond yields and environmental and political opposition, he added eight TransCanada shares (88 total), while avoiding Enbridge, the portfolio's worst performer, citing funding and Line 3 uncertainties. TransCanada's yield is about 5 per cent, and analysts remain largely bullish on the stock.

This study examined pedagogical approaches for teaching education for sustainable development (ESD) in the South African Technology curriculum. Based on Kolb's experiential learning theory, a qualitative descriptive case study was conducted with eight Senior Phase (Grades 7–9) Technology teachers in Mpumalanga's Ehlanzeni District, using semi-structured interviews and non-participant classroom observations analyzed through inductive content analysis, with triangulation and member-checking. Findings showed teachers demonstrated comprehensive knowledge of ESD, citing resource preservation, minimizing technology's negative environmental impacts, renewable energy (solar and wind), societal standards, and indigenous practices such as traditional farming. Teachers identified opportunities for integrating ESD into the curriculum, including technology-driven solutions like processing and recycling, the design process, and investigative teaching; however, actual lessons rarely incorporated ESD, with only two teachers touching on recycling and biodegradable materials without explicit ESD links. Collaborative learning was highlighted as a promising approach for knowledge-sharing, group problem-solving, cross-cultural collaboration, environmental stewardship, and creativity, though classroom practice relied mainly on demonstrations and lectures. The study recommends holistic curriculum integration, value transformation, resource utilization, sustainable design topics, and collaborative learning. Limitations include the single-district scope, qualitative-only methods, and exclusive focus on the Senior Phase.
Holmer drew a penalty by battling and shoving the goalie in front of the net on the powerplay. The team broke the Hasek jinx, got two, and feels confident it can build on that.

This protocol describes a randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled phase 4 trial (the CBC2 study) evaluating the efficacy of Thai cannabis oil on quality of life in women with metastatic breast cancer receiving chemotherapy at King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital, Bangkok, with recruitment starting around January 2023. Ninety participants will be randomized 1:1:1 to Ganja Oil, Metta Osot, or placebo oil, taken once daily before bedtime for 90 days, across four visits, with blood, saliva, stool, and skin samples collected at baseline and post-treatment. The study will assess symptoms using the Edmonton Symptom Assessment System, adverse effects, microbiome profiles, cytokines, bacterial metabolites (short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, equol), bacterial translocation markers (LBP, sCD14), pharmacokinetic parameters, and pharmacogenetic profiles. Background evidence includes cannabinoid anti-tumor activity in preclinical models, symptom benefit in a palliative care pilot study, and reported associations between breast cancer and gut, skin, oral, and fungal microbiota. Thai cannabis products are manufactured by the Department of Thai Traditional and Alternative Medicine and are included in the National List of Essential Medicines. Analysis will be intention-to-treat with 30 patients per arm, using diversity indices and PERMANOVA, with significance defined as p < 0.05.

The use of numbers to identify soccer positions has recently returned to popularity, possibly to reduce confusion caused by the proliferation of position names. The first numbering scheme appeared in England in the 1920s, assigning numbers 1–11 from back to front and right to left in a 2-3-5 formation. In the 1950s, the "W-M" formation kept the same numbers but moved the Inside Forwards back—giving rise to "Number 9" (central striker) and "Number 10" (set-back striker) references—and shifted the center halfback into defense. Beginning in the 1960s, experimentation and "Total Football" eroded the original structure, and players chose their own numbers. Since 2012, U.S. Soccer has standardized position names and numbers based on a 4-3-3 formation, with position profiles based on Technical, Tactical, Physical, and Mental attributes. Terms such as "False 9" and "Double-9s" have also emerged.

Jonathan Huberdeau scored with 7.7 seconds left to give the Florida Panthers a 3-2 win over the Detroit Red Wings.
