Punting, though unglamorous, is a critical role in football. The punter flips field position when the offense fails to score, requiring leg strength, accuracy, hang-time, and touch to help the coverage team pin opponents deep. Punters may also execute fake punts by running or throwing, and many serve as the holder on field goals and extra points. The position is named for the punt, which occurs when the offense fails to convert on 3rd down; the punter kicks the ball after receiving the snap. Required skills include accuracy, leg strength, coordination, flexibility, and creativity, with punters typically slim, 5'10–6'2, and 180–210 pounds. Notable punters include Shane Lechler, holder of the NFL record for average yards per punt (47.6), and Ray Guy, a 1973 first-round pick who won three Super Bowls with the Raiders. Punters matter because field position directly affects a team's scoring chances.

Studies show millennials are saving well for retirement—71% are saving, starting at a median age of 24, and 39% are "super savers" saving over 10% of their salary. However, many are wary of stock market investing: 42% invest conservatively, and 66% of those aged 18-29 find investing scary or intimidating. This caution likely stems from the 2008-09 financial crisis, when the S&P 500 lost about 57% of its value. Experts warn this hesitancy could hurt long-term retirement security, noting the S&P 500 averaged 7.92% returns from 2007-2017 while money market accounts haven't exceeded 0.3% annually. Advisors suggest putting risk in perspective and using tools like robo-advisors to begin investing.

This patent application, a continuation of prior applications titled "Microservices Architecture," relates to cloud computing and describes a system and method for a microservices architecture. The disclosure addresses the evolution of data centers from dedicated hardware appliances toward virtualized and specialized resources, including resource pools of FPGAs, ASICs, SoCs, and other accelerators that can be dynamically provisioned. It presents a microservices framework that partitions functionality in a configurable and scalable way, encapsulating functions in wrappers so that system designers need not know at design time which resources will carry out a function. A microservices API exposes standardized calls to host software, while a microservices driver, in conjunction with a service discovery function (SDF), discovers, registers, and dynamically provisions microservice instances such as local software, virtual machines, FPGAs, and hardware accelerators. The SDF maintains an ontological catalog mapping generic API calls to instance-specific invocations, including FPGA gate configurations. The architecture supports service chaining, in which multiple microservice instances are provisioned and connected via message forwarders so that results pass directly between services without returning to the host software, reducing latency and request-response overhead. Additional components described include uniform APIs and addressing, middleware and drivers, message service path configuration, active message flows using path IDs and tokens, and a load-balancing engine that routes requests based on telemetry, service quality objectives, and various load-balancing strategies.

The Micro E-mini S&P 500 Index futures, launched by CME in 2019, are 1/10th the size of E-mini contracts, created to give small retail traders access to the S&P 500 futures market. One contract equals $5 times the index value, trades electronically on CME Globex (Sunday 6 p.m. to Friday 5 p.m. ET), uses the symbol MES, and is financially settled in cash based on special opening quotes on the third Friday of the contract month. The minimum price fluctuation is 0.25 index points ($1.25). Trading requires a futures broker and margin (about $1,060); CFDs are also available. As of December 9, 2022, the contract traded at $3,959.50, with an all-time high of 4,808.25 (January 2022) and a low of 2,174.00 (March 2020). Seasonally, it historically performs better in winter and spring than summer. The biggest risks come from leverage, as losses are calculated on the full contract value. A backtested mean-reversion strategy exists but is behind a paywall, and the backtest was performed on the E-mini contract due to the Micro contract's shorter history.

Vision on the soccer field—the ability to see, comprehend, and respond to on-field action—is essential for pinpoint passing, defending, and goalkeeping. Legendary player Pelé reportedly had peripheral vision 30 percent greater than the average athlete and supplemented his play through geometry and chess. Since at least 75 percent of learning is visual, and more in sports, ball skills alone cannot produce top-level play; players with strong vision are considered "intelligent," making quicker decisions and better passes or shots. Coaches stress four fundamentals: be aware of everyone's positioning, get your head up quickly when controlling the ball, move to better positions while concentrating, and constantly scan the field for offensive options or defensive threats. Players should also communicate what they see, with goalkeepers having the best overall view. Coaching tips include playing the first touch away from the body, receiving passes with the opposite foot, and running scanning drills.

The MOVE Index measures U.S. interest rate volatility through implied volatility of 1-month OTC options and is known as the "VIX of the bond market." Created by Merrill Lynch in 1998 and acquired by ICE in 2019, it recently rose from 120 to 199 in March amid Fed rate hikes and banking concerns, compared to its all-time high of 264 in October 2008 and average near 85 since 2000. Unlike the VIX, high MOVE readings do not signal good entry points for buying bonds. A backtested strategy starting in 2002 held TLT when the MOVE Index was below its historical mean and sold when it exceeded the mean. The strategy was not highly profitable but avoided high-volatility periods, reducing maximum drawdown to roughly half of buy and hold, which helped in 2022 though slightly hurt 2008 returns. The authors conclude the MOVE index is a good volatility indicator but not a good bond trading signal.

The passage argues that XLP, the Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR Fund tracking major consumer staples in the S&P 500, is an underappreciated but effective trading vehicle. Its holdings are large-cap, low-volatility companies such as Procter & Gamble, Coca-Cola, Pepsi, and Walmart. The DAWN-PLASMA study was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 proof-of-concept multicenter trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of convalescent plasma in hospitalized adults with COVID-19, conducted per the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP guidelines with ethics committee approval and informed consent. The primary objective was to compare best supportive care plus convalescent plasma versus best supportive care alone, with the primary endpoint being the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Participants were randomized 2:1 to standard of care plus convalescent plasma or standard of care alone via a computerized system, with the trial statistician blinded until database lock. Convalescent plasma (800–1000 mL in 4 doses, requiring neutralizing antibody titers of at least 1/160) was administered, with the first dose within 12 hours of randomization. Between May 2020 and January 2021, 499 patients were assessed for eligibility and 489 were randomized (326 plasma, 163 control). Six patients withdrew consent or were screen failures before intervention and were replaced; no patients were lost to follow-up after the intervention. The Day 15 visit was completed in 434 patients and the Day 30 visit in 423. Protocol violations leading to exclusion from the Per Protocol Set included 26 plasma-group patients receiving fewer than 4 units and 3 control-group patients receiving convalescent plasma. Two analysis sets were defined: Full Analysis Set (primary) and Per Protocol Set (sensitivity). Baseline characteristics and concomitant therapy were well matched between groups. In the plasma group, median time to first transfusion was 5 hours, median volume was 884 mL, 80.7% of units had titers ≥1/320, and 294 patients (91.9%) received all 4 units.

Diversification reduces portfolio risk by combining investments whose returns do not move in tandem, but effective diversification requires selecting assets based on how they respond to risk factors and how they fit one's goals and horizon. The passage identifies five common mistakes: not counting all investments, such as provident fund balances or stock options, which may lead to wrong decisions; holding too many investments, which dilutes benefits, increases costs, and makes tracking difficult; buying products one does not understand, while noting that investing only in familiar products can create concentration—advisers or mutual funds can help; losing sight of goals by ignoring income and liquidity needs, such as for retirement; and letting allocation drift over time, which requires periodic rebalancing. Diversification within asset classes, such as equity segments or debt credit profiles, can also improve risk and returns.

The Covid-19 pandemic forced higher education institutions worldwide to cease face-to-face training and adopt online learning. Most universities lacked sufficient on-premise infrastructure and leased commercial platforms such as Zoom, Google Classroom, or Microsoft Teams, which were not well matched to higher education needs and raised personal data protection concerns when hosted on public clouds. Further challenges included rapid adaptation by instructors and students, delivering practical courses, exam security, cheating, low motivation, and digital competence deficiencies.

The study aimed to develop and evaluate a learning management system meeting emergency distance education needs that could be easily integrated with existing software and horizontally scaled. A technological model was created and a prototype implemented using the Education as a Service (EaaS) cloud model, called UZEP.

The paper reviews distance education models (synchronous/asynchronous, passive/interactive) and existing platforms, including Moodle—the most widely used open LMS—and MOOC platforms such as Coursera and edX, which offer asynchronous content delivery, discussion support, and assessment tools.

Using a developmental research model, the researchers built UZEP on an Internet-based synchronous distance education model with a special cloud structure at TUBITAK, allowing universities to use the platform as a service without owning infrastructure. UZEP modules include a learning management system, a virtual classroom (integrating open-source BigBlueButton with load balancing), an online exam module supporting up to 10,000 concurrent students with anti-copying measures, plus homework-project, digital material sharing, announcement, survey, and reporting modules.

Twelve universities advised by the Higher Education Council of Türkiye used UZEP from Fall-2020, serving 78,732 users with 13,180 virtual classrooms and 358,657 exam sessions between October 2020 and February 2021. Weekly meetings with university representatives collected feedback for improvements.

The system was evaluated through expert, pilot, and user evaluations. Six experts rated UZEP favorably for ease of use, simple structure, fast deployment, and integration interfaces with university systems. Compared with Moodle, edX, and Google Suite, edX scored lowest; UZEP was considered better suited for higher education distance education than MOOC software, though it lacked social networking and collaboration components relative to G-Suite and Moodle. Experts recommended adding communication/social tools, learning analytics, question search functions, and HTML5 content support.

Administrator surveys (22 participants from 12 universities) showed 22 of 25 items above the midpoint, with highest scores for ease of learning and use, openness to development, and team availability; lower scores related to responding to change, positive user attitudes, and attractive features. Lecturer evaluations (29 acceptable responses) gave means of 3.48 (LMS), 4.24 (virtual classroom), and 3.90 (assessment software). Student evaluations (111 acceptable responses) yielded dimension means of 3.69, 3.12, and 3.72, indicating positive but not high satisfaction, with needs for social tools and improved measurement.

The study concludes that UZEP enables quick transition to emergency distance education without infrastructure requirements, scales better than competitor platforms, and complies with data protection laws. Limitations include self-reported data, comparison with only four LMS platforms, and pandemic-period evaluation. Future work includes applying artificial intelligence to exam security and assessment, and adding social media and communication channels.

The disclosure provides apparatus and methods for measuring the type and degree of tissue damage around burns and other wounds. Electrodes form capacitive sensors that measure tissue capacitance, which is converted to sub-epidermal moisture (SEM) values indicative of tissue viability. Burn wounds comprise three zones: a necrotic inner zone with reduced SEM, a surrounding zone of stasis with elevated SEM due to edema, and an outer zone of hyperaemia where tissue generally heals. Comparing measured capacitance to data arrays of capacitances and burn depths allows determination of burn wound depth. Apparatus include electrode arrays forming virtual sensors on substrates, with visual indicators such as LEDs, perforations for marking skin, or projectors that display boundaries between viable and non-viable tissue based on SEM thresholds. The methods also apply to other injuries such as cuts, ulcers, and gangrene, and can track healing after wound closure and assess the effectiveness of wound-healing therapies.

Wound Care Advantage (WCA), in collaboration with Dr. David G. The passage examines SPY trading strategies based on when daily highs and lows occur. "Boring" buying on weakness and selling on strength works well, entering at the next day's open and exiting at 1130 the same day. Buying on the close yields similar results but larger drawdowns, so overnight holding is not rewarded. Targets and stop-losses showed no improvement.

This patent application discloses systems, methods, and instrumentalities for low latency medium access control (MAC) protocol data unit (PDU) assembly in wireless systems, such as 5G flexible radio access technology (5gFLEX). Latency may be reduced by a wireless transmit/receive unit (WTRU) determining network transmission parameters and signaling prior to receiving a transmission grant. A WTRU may receive a modulation and coding scheme (MCS), resource range, or a minimum guaranteed transport block size (TBS) before a grant, enabling early generation of MAC PDUs and transport blocks. Data blocks of fixed sizes may be incrementally created, segmented, encoded, and multiplexed prior to a grant, allowing MAC and radio link control (RLC) processing in advance. A WTRU may monitor for and decode downlink control information (DCI), determine decoding parameters (e.g., cyclic redundancy check length, aggregation level, robustness level, DCI format), and derive transmission or reception parameters (e.g., QoS level, spectrum operating mode, HARQ feedback parameters, MCS, resources, timing) based on those decoding parameters, with a network-provided mapping between them. The application further describes example communications systems and WTRU architectures, 5G air interface capabilities (e.g., ultra-low latency, ultra-reliable transmission, MTC support), waveform options (CP-OFDM, OFDM-OQAM, UF-OFDM), spectrum operation modes, frame structures, scheduling modes, logical and transport channels, procedures for WTRU-determined PHY layer parameters, data block size signaling, MAC multiplexing criteria (e.g., by TTL, priority, or QoS), and data block-level ACK/NACK feedback, including aggregated data block status reports for low-latency retransmissions.

The Board of Trustees of Plumbers Local Union No. 93 U.A. and related funds sued Waterworks, Inc. under ERISA section 502 to compel an audit. The parties disputed what occurred at a fall 2004 meeting between Waterworks' president Roger Garbacz and Union representative Lynn Earner: Garbacz claimed the Union agreed Waterworks would not be bound by the collective bargaining agreement (CBA) in exchange for enrolling his son in the apprenticeship program and paying union rates for two employees, while Earner denied any such agreement. Waterworks subsequently submitted fifteen Contribution Reports consistent with the CBA but never signed the "Warranty and Acceptance" clauses, and the Union never rejected them. The court found a genuine issue of material fact as to whether a contract was formed or whether Waterworks' conduct manifested intent to be bound by the CBA, and rejected plaintiffs' LMRA-based argument. Both cross-motions for summary judgment were denied.

Sungi Cho, a 2013 West Point graduate and Army Black Hawk helicopter pilot, used his engineering background and 3D printing to address deficiencies in standard-issue military gear. His first product, the Warbelt Hanger ($10.99), improved barracks gear storage and attracted customers among soldiers and law enforcement. His second product, the MOLLE Backer ($10.99 per two-pack), a universal base mount for MOLLE systems, launched to strong demand. Injection molding offered lower material costs ($0.20 vs. $0.50 per unit), a lower scrap rate (3% vs. 18%), and higher production capacity (200 units per hour), but involved a $0.75 per-unit third-party manufacturing fee. Uncertain how to structure the financial data and aware of unconsidered non-financial factors, Cho considered asking his accounting professor for guidance.

NVIDIA Corporation's Form 10-K annual report for fiscal year ended January 30, 2022. NVIDIA, incorporated in Delaware and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under NVDA. Risk factors include evolving market needs, competition, demand forecasting challenges (including cryptocurrency mining effects), reliance on third-party manufacturers, product defects, international operations, climate change, acquisition integration, and cybersecurity. Options trading in EEM allows investors to profit from both rising and falling markets and to use leverage, but carries risks including market losses, time decay, liquidity, and volatility. Profits and losses are determined by the difference between the purchase/sale price and the exercise price, accounting for fees and commissions; the Black-Scholes model and technical analysis tools can be used to analyze pricing. Common strategies include long call, long put, covered call, covered put, straddle, strangle, collar, and butterfly spread. Leverage magnifies both gains and losses and is not recommended for beginners. Costs, minimum deposits (typically $500–$2,000), and margin requirements (10%–50%) vary by broker and contract type. The passage also covers option delta, expiration dates (generally the third Friday of the expiry month), hedging, risk management through stop losses and position sizing, tax reporting as capital gains or losses, selecting contracts, choosing a reputable broker, liquidity and bid-ask spreads, reading the options chain, and best practices such as backtesting and fully understanding option pricing before trading.

More snow is forecast for Maine, New Hampshire, and Vermont, which already have over 2 feet of snow in places. Two systems will phase too late to bring Connecticut more than a dusting but should drop nearly a foot of snow northward.

This passage is from the datasheet of the ADS8681W, ADS8685W, and ADS8689W, 16-bit SAR ADC data acquisition devices with an integrated analog front-end and precision reference. The devices provide input alarms with independently programmable high and low thresholds and a common hysteresis (set via ALARM_H_TH_REG and ALARM_L_TH_REG), plus an AVDD supply alarm with fixed trip points (high at typically 5.3V, low at 4.7V). The multiSPI digital interface supports multiple data transfer protocols, and the host perceives the device as a 32-bit input-output shift register. Connection topologies include single-device operation using all multiSPI options or a standard SPI interface, and a multi-device daisy-chain in which an optimal data frame contains 32 × N SCLK edges and throughput decreases with device count. The device operates in three states—RESET (application reset or power-on reset, selected by the RSTn_APP bit), ACQ (input acquisition, with an optional NAP low-power mode), and CONV (conversion initiated by the CONVST/CS rising edge). Programming sections describe data transfer frames (optimal at 32 SCLKs; short frames invalidate writes but remain valid for reads; long frames use the last 32 bits as the command), byte and half-word commands, and an output data word to which flags such as device address, range, alarm status, and parity can be appended. Read operations support legacy SPI with single or dual SDO and source-synchronous (SRC) protocols with selectable clock source and bus width. Nine configuration registers are mapped, including DEVICE_ID, RST_PWRCTL (unlocked by writing 69h to address 05h), SDI_CTL, SDO_CTL, DATAOUT_CTL, RANGE_SEL, ALARM, and the alarm threshold registers. An application example presents an eight-channel industrial analog input module using the ADS8681W with a MUX36D08 multiplexer for voltage and current ranges up to ±10V, illustrating the alarm function with an NTC thermistor, where hysteresis prevents false triggering. Additional sections cover power-supply decoupling, NAP and power-down modes, PCB layout recommendations, related documentation, support resources, ESD caution, revision history (Revision A, May 2025, changed ADS8685W/ADS8689W status to Production Data), and packaging information.

South Korea has restored 46 public services after a fire at the National Information Resources Service data centre in Daejeon disrupted hundreds of government platforms. The blaze, reportedly triggered by a battery explosion during maintenance work, broke out over the weekend and caused outages across administrative, postal and public-sector websites ahead of the Chuseok holidays. This protocol describes a scoping review of antipsychotic-induced metabolic syndrome (MS) in community-dwelling adults. Antipsychotics effectively treat severe mental illness but cause MS—weight gain, dyslipidaemia, and glucose dysregulation—in approximately 40–80% of users, doubling coronary heart disease risk and increasing type 2 diabetes risk five-fold. Non-modifiable determinants include gender, ethnicity, age, and family history, while modifiable determinants include diet and physical activity. Non-pharmacological interventions have shown limited clinical efficacy, and the preferred healthcare setting for delivery remains unclear.

Guided by Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and the PRISMA-ScR checklist, the review will search multiple electronic databases and grey literature (January–April 2023), including qualitative, quantitative, mixed-methods studies, and evidence syntheses. Two reviewers will independently screen titles and abstracts; full-text screening will be conducted by one reviewer with a 10% sample checked by another. Data will be extracted using a standardised form and synthesised narratively.

The review aims to describe: (1) non-modifiable determinants, (2) modifiable determinants, (3) non-pharmacological interventions to prevent or treat antipsychotic-induced MS, and (4) the preferred context for intervention delivery. Findings will identify knowledge gaps and inform future research, with results disseminated through peer-reviewed publication.

This study evaluated whether diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and its associated apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps can predict telomerase reverse transcriptase promoter (pTERT) mutation status in glioblastoma (GBM), since conventional structural MRI (T1WI, T2WI, CE-T1) has previously failed to do so. A ResNet convolutional neural network was trained on MRI data from 266 GBM patients (147 with DWI) treated at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University between March 2018 and October 2021, comparing conventional structural MRI sequences against DWI modalities across different regions of interest (entire tumor, tumor core, enhanced tumor).

Conventional structural MRI performed poorly (accuracies 50.10–51.53%, AUCs 0.527–0.571). DWI alone achieved 54.58% accuracy (AUC 0.626), ADC map 78.63% (AUC 0.865), and combined DWI+ADC (DWI*) the best performance at 85.20% accuracy (AUC 0.934), with patient-level accuracy of 86.6%. Using the entire tumor as ROI yielded the best results, though enhanced tumor alone also performed acceptably (81.70%, AUC 0.869). Age, necrosis volume, and tumor location were significantly associated with pTERT mutation on univariate analysis, but an SVM model using these clinical characteristics achieved only 70.91% accuracy (AUC 0.735), and adding them to the DWI* ResNet model did not improve performance.

The authors conclude that DWI combined with ADC maps, analyzed with ResNet using the whole tumor volume, provides the greatest value for noninvasive preoperative prediction of pTERT mutation status and suggest incorporating DWI into clinical management. Limitations include the small, retrospective sample restricted to WHO IV GBM.

The Colorado Court of Appeals affirmed a summary judgment for Shelter Mutual Insurance Company, declaring it had no obligation to make uninsured motorist payments to the Breits. Breit, injured in an automobile accident, received $100,000 from the third party's insurer and demanded $100,000 from Shelter based on two policies, each providing $100,000 in underinsured motorist coverage; his damages exceeded $200,000. Shelter contended the policy's anti-stacking provisions limited the aggregate uninsured motorist coverage to $100,000, and the trial court agreed. On appeal, defendants argued the anti-stacking provisions were ambiguous and contrary to the doctrine of reasonable expectations. Relying on Thompson v. Shelter Mutual Insurance Co., the court found the "Limits of Liabilities" and "Other Insurance in the Company" provisions unambiguously prohibited stacking benefits under multiple policies issued by the same insurer. The court rejected defendants' reliance on Compton v. State Farm, distinguishing it because Compton involved policies from three separate carriers and different policy language, and found no conflict between the "Other Insurance" provision and the anti-stacking clause, as they address different concepts. The court also held the doctrine of reasonable expectations inapplicable because the policy language was neither conflicting, ambiguous, nor contrary to legislative policy. The court declined the plaintiff's request for fees, finding the appeal not frivolous.

The ANC Free State's provincial congress, postponed several times this year, has yet to begin. It will elect new leadership, with Ace Magashule expected to run again. This study examined the experiences and acceptability of self-administered intravaginal 5-fluorouracil (5FU) cream among 12 women living with HIV in Kisumu, Kenya, following a Phase I pilot trial in which participants applied two grams of 5FU every other week for eight applications as adjuvant treatment after ablation or excision for cervical precancer (CIN2/3). Using questionnaires and in-depth interviews, researchers assessed acceptability across dimensions of content, complexity, comfort, credibility, and delivery. All participants completed the study; although some initially reported anxiety or fear, all ultimately felt the cream was safe and that they had used it correctly. All participants preferred 5FU over their previous procedures, citing less pain, less fear, greater privacy, and convenience of home use. Challenges included measuring the correct dose, first-time tampon use, limited anatomical knowledge, side effects such as itching and burning, condom requirements, and difficulty finding privacy at home. Education sessions increased confidence. The authors conclude that self-administered 5FU was highly acceptable and could help address cervical precancer treatment gaps in low- and middle-income countries, though the study's small, single-site sample limits generalizability.

The Trump administration has transferred oversight of career and technical education (CTE) from the Education Department to the Labor Department, which has historically focused on short-term job training for unemployed adults. The transfer includes distributing over $1 billion in Perkins funding, conducting compliance monitoring, and providing technical assistance. Administration officials say the change aims to boost labor force participation, reduce administrative burdens on states, and centralize workforce development programs. Supporters, including the U.S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation's Jason Tyszko, say greater alignment and accountability could benefit students, though some short-term disruption is expected. Critics, including CTE advocates and congressional Democrats, view the move as a step toward dismantling the Education Department, argue the transfer of funds was illegal without congressional approval, and worry that insufficient staff and an emphasis on short-term credentials could limit students' paths to advancement. Former Biden administration official Amy Loyd fears an overemphasis on short-term job training could steer students toward low-wage jobs and reinforce stigma around CTE. Alabama Workforce Board executive director Anna Chappelle hopes the federal change will resemble her state's alignment of education and workforce programs. The number of Education Department staff transferring to the Labor Department remains unclear.

This study evaluated six machine learning models—Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Neural Network, Decision Tree, and SuperLearner—for diagnosing pancreatic cancer using a synthetic dataset of demographic, clinical, and symptom variables. All models achieved similar accuracy (76.05%–76.35%), but sensitivity was very low across the board: Random Forest and Decision Tree identified no true positive cases, SVM achieved the highest sensitivity (1.90%), and SuperLearner had the highest precision (66.67%) but only 0.42% sensitivity. The results highlight class imbalance as the main limitation, causing high accuracy that masks poor detection of positive cases. Analyses of gene expression heatmaps, PCA, and correlation plots suggested clustering patterns that could inform feature engineering. The authors propose improvements including resampling techniques (e.g., SMOTE, ADASYN), cost-sensitive learning, threshold tuning, interpretability tools (SHAP, LIME), and use of real-world clinical data. They conclude that balancing sensitivity and precision, real-world validation, and collaboration between data scientists and clinicians are essential for clinical adoption.

The Indiana Supreme Court reversed a trial court's grant of partial summary judgment in a wrongful death suit arising from Laura Shaner's January 2006 death following complications from dialysis treatments administered after hernia repair surgery by Dr. Albert Milford at St. Margaret Mercy Healthcare Center. Her husband, David Shaner, sued Milford, St. Margaret, and TRC-Indiana, seeking both final-expense damages (medical, hospital, funeral, and burial expenses) and survivor damages (loss of consortium, earnings, and related losses). David died intestate in October 2015 with no known heirs, and his estate escheated to the State of Indiana. Co-administrators of Laura's estate—her father and brothers—continued the litigation. The trial court granted the defendants' motion for partial summary judgment on the survivor damages claim, and the Court of Appeals affirmed, reasoning that because David had no heirs, any such damages would pass to the state and be punitive rather than compensatory. The Supreme Court granted transfer and held that neither the wrongful death statute, the survival statute, nor its prior decision in Bemenderfer v. Williams requires an heir for a survivor damages claim to survive a party's death. However, because the Court was not convinced that Laura's estate co-administrators were the proper party to pursue David's claim, it remanded for the trial court to determine whether a proper party exists to continue the action, potentially through reopening David's estate.

The lecture distinguishes tournaments from cash games. In tournaments, players buy in once, are eliminated upon losing their chips, face rising blinds, cannot choose their table, and aim to survive as long as possible for payouts, with most players (about 80%) receiving nothing. Cash games have fixed stakes, allow rebuying and leaving at any time, and involve more metagame, such as targeting weak players. The instructor chose tournaments for the class because they involve less metagame, are more exciting, cover a wider range of situations, and match the MIT Poker Club's January event. Skills largely transfer between formats except at the very top levels.

The lecture then covers preflop play. Key equities: a bigger pair against a smaller pair is roughly 80/20; a pair against no overcards is about 93%; the best matchup is kings against king-deuce offsuit at 94.6%; a pair against one overcard or a dominating hand is about 70/30; two overcards against a pair is near 50/50; and with four distinct cards, the highest card holds roughly 60/40. Suitness matters more when behind than when ahead.

Regarding all-ins, players should not fear going all-in preflop; when effective stacks are under about 12 big blinds with antes, hands should be shoved or folded. Position matters less for all-ins, so small blind shove ranges can be wider than button ranges. An example shows that if the big blind calls only 25% of hands, the small blind can profitably shove any two cards; the Nash equilibrium at 15 big blinds with antes is shoving about 66.8% of hands and calling about 38.5%. Nash strategies cannot be exploited, but exploitative adjustments must go in the correct direction.

Ranges widen with later position and shorter stacks, with position mattering more than stack size. Suited connectors require larger stacks, while big-card hands like ace-four offsuit depend on having fewer players left to act. Calling all-ins is often correct with adequate odds, and with four big blinds in the big blind, nearly any two cards are playable. Re-raises should be about 2.5 times the original raise, or all-in if committing more than a quarter of the stack. Calling a prior raise is acceptable when deep and in position. Against limpers, add one big blind to the raise size per limper. Finally, "sucker bets" give opponents free options, which is bad against competent players but can exploit weaker ones.

MetSoc of CIM announced its 2018 award recipients, honoring achievements in metallurgy and related fields. The device provides an active-high alarm output on the ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin, enabled by setting SDO1_CONFIG[1:0] to 01b. Two alarm types exist: an input alarm comparing ADC input voltage against user-programmable thresholds, and an AVDD alarm monitoring the analog supply against 4.7V and 5.3V thresholds. Both alarms are enabled by default and disabled via IN_AL_DIS and VDD_AL_DIS bits. Each alarm has active and tripped flags in ALARM_REG, readable via the ALARM pin, internal registers, or appended data output.

The S&P 400 Midcap index, formed in 1991, tracks 400 mid-sized US companies with market capitalizations between $3.6 and $13.1 billion. It is market-cap weighted and rebalanced quarterly in March, June, September, and December. The E-mini S&P MidCap 400 futures (ticker EMD) trade on the CME Globex platform, with each contract worth $100 times the index value. Contracts follow quarterly cycles, are financially settled, and trading terminates at 9:30 a.m. ET on the third Friday of the contract month. Trading runs Sunday to Friday from 6:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET, with a one-hour daily break. The minimum price fluctuation is 0.10 index points ($10) for outright trading. ETFs tracking the index include IJH, SPMD, and EWMC. Seasonality analysis suggests the index performs better in winter and spring. Backtested strategies showed poor results for a volatility strategy and decent results for an overnight strategy, though both performed better on SPY and QQQ. The futures' all-time high was 2924.2 in November 2021, and the all-time low was 119.43 in June 1991. Prices are affected by component stock movements, interest rates, economic news, and the US dollar, with leverage posing the biggest trading risk.

Dolphins wide receiver Tyreek Hill returned to the team's facility and spoke at Friday's meeting, three days after undergoing season-ending surgery on a dislocated left knee suffered in Monday night's win. Coach Mike McDaniel said Hill encouraged teammates to stay motivated and play complementary football. Since Miami traded for Hill in 2022, the Dolphins have played only one game without him—a 30-0 win over the Jets in 2023. Jaylen Waddle steps into Hill's role as lead receiver, though Waddle and McDaniel downplayed the "No. 1 receiver" label as a media creation. Miami will also give increased roles to a 2024 sixth-round pick and tight end Waller, who caught two touchdowns in his debut and has earned more snaps against the Panthers. McDaniel said he won't overcompensate for Hill's absence, expressing confidence in the overall group.

On November 9, 2021, Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that its Board of Directors appointed Alex Gorsky to the Board. Gorsky will serve on the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee and, as a non-employee director, will receive a $100,000 annual retainer paid in quarterly installments and participate in the Non-Employee Director Stock Plan, receiving an initial automatic grant of 486 restricted stock units. Apple will enter into its standard indemnification agreement with Gorsky, and no transactions requiring disclosure under Item 404(a) of Regulation S-K exist. The same day, the Board amended Apple's Amended and Restated Bylaws to increase the Board's size from eight to nine members, effective immediately. The amended Bylaws are attached as Exhibit 3.2. The report was signed on November 12, 2021 by Katherine Adams, Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary.

A Russell 2000 Death Cross occurs when the index's 50-day moving average crosses below its 200-day moving average, often viewed as bearish. Rob Hanna's study of 25 Death Crosses since 1988 found the S&P 500 rose 84% of the time the following year, with the biggest gain exceeding 60% in 2020. However, drawdowns were sizable, and the most recent cross in 2022 was followed by S&P 500 declines. The signal may be less reliable for the S&P 500 than for the more volatile Russell 2000.

John Mellencamp knelt in support of Black Lives Matter after performing "Easy Target" on "Late Show With Stephen Colbert." The song addresses racial inequality. Mellencamp said kneeling, started by Colin Kaepernick, began as a protest of racial and social injustice but was politicized by the current administration.

This email compiles news articles dated July 17, 2001. James Fallon, described as a seasoned trader, will lead Enron Broadband Services after Kenneth Rice moves to a corporate role; the unit lost $102 million in the second quarter and is being restructured as a business unit within Enron Wholesale Services, which one analyst said could make it easier to hide losses. Enron is cutting broadband expenses, closing its Portland office, and reassigning or laying off employees, while a liquid bandwidth trading market is predicted to be six to 18 months away. Representative Henry Waxman urged the White House to seek a Justice Department review of Karl Rove's contacts with companies in which he held stock, including Enron, Intel, and General Electric; the White House said Rove followed all ethical guidelines. Mississippi regulators approved Calpine's plans for a $450 million power plant in Lowndes County. EnronOnline CEO Greg Piper said the platform averages $3.5 billion in daily trades and expects continued volume growth alongside rival IntercontinentalExchange. Texans donated nearly $500,000 to the American Red Cross for Tropical Storm Allison relief, with Enron among corporate donors of $100,000 or more. In India, framing terms of reference for a judicial probe into the Dabhol power project may be difficult given Supreme Court comments, and the Maharashtra government faces potential embarrassment over its 1997 affidavit defending Dabhol Phase-II.

Rick Langenberg's article discusses local predictions for Super Bowl 52 between the New England Patriots and Philadelphia Eagles, noting local disappointment that the Denver Broncos were not participating after their early season exit. Various Teller County residents, TMJ staff, and local officials offered their picks. Most predicted a Patriots victory, with scores ranging from close games (27-24) to blowouts (42-14), citing Brady and Belichick's championship experience in their eighth Super Bowl together. This lecture covers the supply side of static competition models, the empirical results of BLP (Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes), Nevo's cereal market study, and the common ownership hypothesis. Using an ownership matrix combined with demand derivatives, firms' first order conditions can be inverted to recover marginal costs; with fully flexible (non-parametric) marginal costs, the model is always rationalized and thus untestable. Imposing a functional form for marginal cost enables joint demand and supply estimation, improves precision, and provides overidentifying restrictions to test conduct assumptions. The BLP automobile results (1971–1990 US data) show random coefficient models capture heterogeneous substitution patterns better than logit, though the model ignores durable goods, dealerships, negotiated prices, and financing. Nevo tests conduct models by comparing model-implied markups to accounting markups in the cereal industry, rejecting collusion and finding consistency with own-profit maximization; accounting for multi-product firms and demographics proves important, as logit estimates would yield different conclusions. Finally, the lecture discusses the common ownership hypothesis—that diversified institutional investors like Vanguard and BlackRock may soften competition among firms they jointly hold. Backus, Conlon, and Sinkinson document rising profit weights from common ownership over time, but their structural test on the cereal market, using a Rivers-Vuong non-nested test, rejects common ownership, perfect competition, and monopoly models in favor of own-profit maximization, though this remains a single case study and the mechanism behind the hypothesis remains elusive.

The Ichimoku trading strategy is a technical analysis indicator developed by Goichi Hosoda, a Tokyo-based newspaper writer, that defines support and resistance levels, shows trend direction, and gauges momentum by plotting multiple averages on a price chart, forming a "cloud." Its components are the Tenkan-Sen, Kijun-Sen, Senkou Span A, Senkou Span B, and Chikou Span. Price above the cloud indicates an uptrend, while price below indicates a downtrend; a thick cloud signals high volatility and a thin cloud signals low volatility. The Tenkan/Kijun crossover, Chikou Span, and Senkou Span can each generate signals or confirmations. Backtests on assets like QQQ and MDY showed the strategy reduces time in the market and drawdowns, but generally underperforms risk-adjusted buy-and-hold returns. The main risk is that signals may not be accurate or reliable, so backtesting is recommended.

The 2007-09 Great Recession reduced consumer spending at U.S. restaurants, with the casual dining sector particularly affected. By summer 2016, some investors revisited casual dining stocks, believing years of consistent economic growth would encourage consumers to dine out and spend more. In 2016, the U.S. restaurant industry was projected at nearly $800 billion in sales, accounting for 4% of GDP and employing nearly 1 in 10 Americans. Casual dining offers more comfort than fast food at lower prices than fine dining; fast casual is a counter-service variant emphasizing speed. Bloomin' Brands opened its first Outback Steakhouse in Tampa, Florida in 1988 and went public in 2012. By June 2016, it owned 1,335 restaurants and franchised 166 across four brands—Outback, Fleming's, Bonefish Grill, and Carrabba's—about 85% in the U.S., with roughly two-thirds under the Outback brand. The case describes 13 publicly traded restaurant comparables and presents their price-earnings multiples, income statement, and balance sheet data alongside Bloomin's.

The 60/40 portfolio allocates 60% of capital to equities and 40% to bonds, relying on the historically low or negative correlation between the two asset classes for diversification. According to Vanguard, it has averaged an 8.8% annual return since 1926. In 2022, however, both stocks and bonds declined simultaneously—the portfolio fell 17.77% year-to-date as of September 17, 2022—because bonds failed as a safe haven amid rising inflation and interest rates. Despite this, the article concludes the 60/40 portfolio is not dead, noting that double-digit declines have occurred nine times since 1980 and were typically followed by rebounds. The portfolio can be built with ETFs such as SPY and TLT or through ready-made funds like BlackRock Target Allocation Funds. Alternatives discussed include the All-Weather Portfolio, trend-following (CTA) strategies, gold, crypto, international equities, tail risk strategies, and the 80/20 portfolio.

The Supreme Court of Rhode Island affirmed the conviction of Andrew A. Bucci for giving legal advice to Robert Oliva while Bucci was suspended from the practice of law, a suspension effective September 22, 1977. Bucci was convicted in District Court and fined $500, an amount exceeding the statutory maximum under § 11-27-14; after a trial de novo in Superior Court, a jury again found him guilty, and he was sentenced to six months' imprisonment. Oliva, facing armed robbery charges and a suspended-sentence violation, had been introduced to Bucci by Edward D'Alo. Unknown to Bucci, Oliva was cooperating with federal and state authorities and recorded his conversations with Bucci; these recordings were admitted at trial. On appeal, Bucci raised three issues. First, he argued a variance existed between the charge of giving legal advice and evidence that he merely obtained another attorney for Oliva. The court found the recorded discussions of grand jury procedure, search and seizure law, and restitution sufficient to prove he furnished legal advice, since the retained attorney, Joseph DeCaporale, was to act under Bucci's direction. Second, Bucci contended the state was required to prove pecuniary benefit, but the court held § 11-27-10 contains no such element. Third, he argued the Superior Court could not impose a harsher sentence after trial de novo; citing Colten v. Kentucky, the court found no constitutional bar and declined to review the sentence absent a Rule 35 motion in the Superior Court. The appeal was denied and dismissed, and the conviction affirmed. Shea, J., did not participate.

University of Liverpool research links brain structure to hallucination proneness and musical aptitude. This study examined whether individual variability in brain functional organization biases estimates of functional connectivity (FC) differences in psychosis. Using data from the Human Connectome Project – Early Psychosis (121 patients, 57 controls), the authors compared FC disruptions identified using a standard group-based parcellation (Schaefer 100-region atlas) versus an individualized parcellation generated with the Group Prior Individualized Parcellation (GPIP) algorithm. The individualized approach reallocated over 40% of cortical vertices and produced more functionally homogeneous regions than the group-based atlas. Although both methods identified widespread FC reductions in patients, the group-based parcellation yielded significantly larger case-control differences, and Network Based Statistic analysis implicated approximately 9% more dysconnected edges compared to the individualized approach. The specific edges and regions identified as most affected (e.g., insula and medial prefrontal regions) varied considerably between methods, though network-level findings were largely consistent across both parcellations. The authors conclude that group-based parcellations, which fail to account for individual differences in brain organization, may inflate estimates of FC differences in psychosis, and that individualized parcellations provide more conservative and refined estimates of brain network disruptions.

Losing a spouse can endanger the surviving partner's health: sudden shock can trigger heart attacks or broken heart syndrome, and studies link higher death risk after losing a longtime spouse, though timing is often coincidence. Grief can cause poor eating, ignored symptoms, stress, and poor rest, setting the stage for life-threatening conditions. Former President George H.W. Bush, hospitalized with sepsis a day after Barbara Bush's funeral, is recovering; doctors note stress weakens immunity, and his age, Parkinson's disease, and possibly ignored infection signs raise risks. The lecture reviews numerical methods covered so far. Linear algebra problems (Ax=b) solved via Matlab's backslash require n³ operations and typically yield machine-accurate solutions, though ill-conditioning can produce multiple x values that solve the equation equally well. Nonlinear systems are solved with Newton-Raphson (iterations × n³), and fsolve converts root-finding into minimization of the norm of f. Implicit ODE solvers require solving nonlinear systems at each time step, with costs scaling as time steps × iterations × n². The lecture introduces functionals—operators that take functions as inputs—citing density functional theory as an important research application.

The lecture then connects numerical integration, interpolation, and basis functions. Integration rules fit approximate functions (sums of basis functions) to sampled points and integrate those approximations. Interpolation (k=n parameters) forces exact fits at data points, appropriate when data is trusted; fewer parameters (k<n) suit noisy data. Monomials are a poor basis choice due to exponentially growing condition numbers. Lagrange polynomials make coefficients equal function values directly, while Newton polynomials allow adding points without changing existing coefficients. Gaussian quadrature selects weights and points to integrate polynomials exactly up to order 2n−1, outperforming Simpson's rule. Finally, multidimensional integration suffers from the curse of dimensionality, with costs growing exponentially with the number of dimensions.

This MIT lecture by Hong Liu begins with questions on the previous lecture's Hawking-Page transition, clarifying the thermal AdS phase, the heuristic confinement/deconfinement analogy, and the behavior of the partition function sum. The main topic is entanglement entropy: defined as the Von Neumann entropy of the reduced density matrix obtained by tracing out one subsystem's degrees of freedom. For pure states S(A) equals S(B); for mixed states, the entropy also contains classical statistical correlations. A two-spin system illustrates the calculation, and properties including subadditivity and strong subadditivity are presented.

For many-body systems with local Hamiltonians, ground states obey an area law: the leading entanglement entropy term equals the boundary area of region A divided by the short-distance cutoff, reflecting dominant short-range entanglement near the boundary. Subleading terms capture long-range entanglement, which characterizes topological order in 2+1 dimensions and, in 1+1 dimensional CFTs, yields S = (C/3)log(L/epsilon), where C is the central charge measuring degrees of freedom.

The Ryu-Takayanagi proposal states that a boundary region's entanglement entropy equals the area of a minimal bulk surface ending on that region's boundary, divided by 4G Newton. This satisfies subadditivity and strong subadditivity via simple geometric proofs, reproduces the CFT formula through an explicit AdS3 calculation, recovers the black hole entropy formula when A is the entire space, and gives the area law in general dimensions. The lecture concludes that the formula indicates geometry is essentially equal to quantum information, unifying quantum information, condensed matter, and gravity research.

This study investigates the software engineering challenges of integrating open-source and commercial LLMs into financial report analysis workflows through an exploratory case study with the finance department at Getinge AB, a Swedish MedTech company. Using Design Science Research, the authors explored the domain with business controllers and identified use cases for automating narrative commentary on order intake and net sales. Two prototypes were developed: a locally hosted multi-agent workflow using open-source models (e.g., LLaMA 3.1, Qwen 2.5) and a cloud-based solution using GPT-4o. The local models exhibited hallucinations, poor instruction following, and high computational demands, while GPT-4o produced more professional summaries but struggled with strict formatting rules and sometimes mixed positive and negative trends. An evaluation by two business controllers found both models useful for drafting but insufficient for formal reporting without manual review. A prompt-chaining refinement improved data analysis but did not fully resolve adherence to conditional instructions. Three key challenges emerged: task-specificity in prompt and system design, variability in data preparation, and constraints from data sensitivity. The comparison showed local models offer data control at the cost of greater engineering effort, whereas GPT-4o provides stronger out-of-the-box performance but raises privacy, compliance, and vendor lock-in concerns. The study concludes that LLMs can partially support financial reporting workflows, though full end-to-end automation remains challenging.

School shootings, once unheard of, now occur frequently, evoking anger and frustration and renewing calls for stricter gun laws, which the author doubts would deter deranged shooters. Families should plan for natural disasters like earthquakes, including reunification plans and authorized pickups, and schools should conduct disaster drills beyond lockdowns, since drills, like fire drills, save lives.

The passage outlines four key challenges in QED of attoscience: (1) generating massively quantum states of light, including large-photon-number entangled states and multimode squeezed states; (2) generating entangled states of light and matter, focusing on ultrafast processes such as ATI, HHG, and rescattering in solids; (3) developing ultrafast quantum-optical methods to verify and quantify entanglement for applications in metrology, nonlinear optics, and quantum information; and (4) simulating strong-field dynamics using quantum platforms such as cold atoms and ions.

Advances needed to meet these challenges include: theoretical progress in fully quantized descriptions of strong-field processes; experimental techniques for characterizing photon statistics and demonstrating non-classical states such as optical Schrödinger cats and squeezed harmonics; structured and quantum light sources; new material platforms including 2D materials, correlated systems, and topological insulators; quantum simulators using shaken traps and Kramers-Henneberger transformations; and advanced measurement tools such as quantum tomography and machine-learning-based inversion methods.

The passage concludes that the union of attosecond physics and quantum optics is being realized, envisioning scalable quantum light sources, quantum simulation platforms, and ultrafast quantum processors.

The DAWN-Plasma trial was a randomized, multicenter, open-label phase 2 proof-of-concept study evaluating convalescent plasma added to standard of care versus standard of care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Between May 2020 and January 2021, 489 patients were randomized 2:1 to convalescent plasma (n=326) or control (n=163). Participants received 800–1000 mL of plasma in four doses, with 80.7% of units having neutralizing antibody titers ≥1/320. The primary endpoint—proportion of patients alive and free of mechanical ventilation at Day 15—showed no difference between groups (83.7% vs 84.1%; OR 0.99; p=0.976). No significant differences were found for any secondary endpoint. Adverse events, fatal events, and serious adverse events were similar between groups; transfusion-related side effects occurred in 6.0% of the plasma group, with no TRALI cases reported. Higher neutralizing antibody titers at baseline and Day 6 correlated with better outcomes, but the intervention did not affect titers. The study concluded that early administration of high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma did not change the natural course of COVID-19 in hospitalized patients.

JPMorgan's air-rights deal for a taller 270 Park Ave. tower stirred controversy; the Salmagundi Club is a filming location; an Upper East Side garage company is buying air rights; a Midtown project is "mining" air rights; L'Occitane leased a Fifth Avenue flagship; CBAM Partners is moving to 51 Astor Place; Knotel received Newmark investment; DDG plans a Williamsburg project; a Staten Island site faces foreclosure over $2,445.

Matt Damon is asking for prayers as his 74-year-old father Kent battles multiple myeloma, a rare blood cancer revealed in 2011. Damon has canceled appearances, including the 2017 Britannia Awards, to be at his father's side in Boston. His film Downsizing opens Dec. 22.

Speakers at a press conference discuss a young player who responded well after taking two penalties, continuing to play hard and physically. STAT's D.C. Diagnosis newsletter covers health politics and policy twice weekly. It notes Virginia's Eastern Shore pony roundup occurred in September this year, unlike 2013 when it was postponed by a government shutdown, and asks which party will win the shutdown. This proof-of-principle study investigated whether NGS-based detection of cancer gene mutations in saliva and plasma (liquid biopsies) could identify Fanconi anemia (FA) patients at high risk of developing oral potentially malignant lesions (OPMLs) or oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) before clinical diagnosis. Sixteen Spanish FA patients were enrolled in a prospective longitudinal study (~2 years), with 50 liquid biopsy collections analyzed using the Oncomine Pan-Cancer Cell-Free Assay. Mutations were found in 15 samples from 9 patients, most frequently in TP53. Among 14 patients with clinical follow-up, 6 of 7 who developed lesions or carcinomas had mutations detected beforehand, with lead times of 23–630 days (median 205 days). No mutations were found in 5 of 7 patients who remained lesion-free. The diagnostic test showed 92% accuracy, 86% sensitivity, and 100% specificity. The results demonstrate that mutation detection in liquid biopsies can stratify FA patients into significantly different risk groups for oral lesions and carcinomas, enabling closer surveillance of high-risk individuals through a noninvasive approach.

JPMorgan restricted crypto purchases due to monitoring difficulties, overspending risks, and identity theft concerns. Capital One and Discover also ban such purchases. Credit card networks now treat crypto purchases as cash advances with higher fees and interest.

Minister Syed Mohammad Altaf Bukhari urged academicians to boost students' confidence, noting J&K students feel deprived of privileges enjoyed elsewhere. Speaking as Chief Guest at a two-day national seminar on "Assessment and Evaluation" at Cluster University Srinagar, he said students are overburdened by school and tuition work and asked academicians to examine why J&K students' marks percentage is lower than other states, limiting outside admissions. He said teachers should widen students' mental horizons. Vice Chancellor Prof. Dr Sheikh Javaid called for education at par with national and international standards.

Yankees shortstop Anthony Volpe played through a partially torn labrum suffered in early May without going on the injured list. After a difficult 2025 season and postseason, he said surgery remains undecided, and he and the Yankees will assess next steps for his rehab.

This article explains various offensive line blocking techniques in football to clarify terminology and highlight linemen's responsibilities. It defines the Trap block (leaving a defender unblocked at the snap, then kicking him out with another blocker), Base block (one-on-one blocks requiring inside leverage), Reach block (establishing outside leverage on perimeter runs), Down block (angle blocks on frontside defenders, common in gap schemes), Log block (sealing a defender inside, either reactively or by design), Pull (a blocker relocating across the formation for a numbers or leverage advantage), Veer block (dropping step and climbing to the second level, used in under-center triple option offenses), Combo block (two players blocking a first-level defender to a second-level defender), Double Team block (the first-level portion of a combo, with post and trail players), Scoop block (a backside combo block similar to a Reach), Drive block (driving a defender off the line in the run game), Cut block (diving at a defender's legs), Crack block (a perimeter player blocking an interior defender), and Kick Out block (canceling an edge defender to widen the C-gap, which becomes a Log block if the defender wrong-arms).

This passage summarizes results of a study of the BNT162b2 COVID-19 vaccine, which ran about 33 months and ended in February 2023, with participants enrolled for up to 26 months. BNT162b2 was 95% effective in preventing COVID-19 from 7 days after Dose 2, regardless of past infection. BNT162b2SA produced immune responses against the Beta variant comparable to BNT162b2's responses against the original strain. Injection site reactions (most commonly pain) and systemic events (most commonly tiredness and headache) were generally mild or moderate and resolved quickly. In Phase 1, some participants had temporary drops in lymphocyte counts that returned to normal. Few participants withdrew due to medical problems (32 of 21,926 in the BNT162b2 group; 36 of 21,921 in the placebo group). Serious medical problems were rare, and researchers believed most were not related to the vaccine, though a few may have been. No participants died in Phase 1 or among BNT162b2SA recipients in Phase 3; deaths in Phase 2/3 were not believed to be caused by BNT162b2.

This passage introduces the ebook edition of *Foreign Relations of the United States* (FRUS) Volume IV, covering the Soviet Union from January 1983 to March 1985, produced by the U.S. Department of State's Office of the Historian. The ebook format provides full content, search and reading features, and offline access; readers are advised to cite document numbers rather than page numbers. The FRUS series, established in 1861, presents the official documentary record of major U.S. foreign policy decisions and diplomatic activity. Editing standards were first codified by Secretary of State Frank B. Kellogg in 1925, and Public Law 102–138 (1991) established statutory requirements, including thoroughness, accuracy, historical objectivity, indication of deletions, omission of no major facts, and publication within 30 years of the events recorded. Most sources for this volume were located at the Department of State and the National Archives and Records Administration.

Mental health experts continue calling for suicide barriers on Lower Mainland bridges, where half of jumping deaths occurred between 1991 and 2007. Research shows barriers are effective, and crisis phones at Burrard Bridge have saved lives.

George Tidmarsh, head of the FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research since July, used his personal LinkedIn page to question the safety of voclosporin, a drug approved in 2021 to treat lupus nephritis, stating it has "significant toxicity" and has not been shown to provide direct clinical benefit. The post prompted discussion among biotech investors about whether Tidmarsh is seeking revenge on a prominent Wall Street investor after a run-in six years ago; he has a personal connection to the drugmaker's largest investor.

Researchers discovered that pollen gathered by honeybees contains endophytic actinobacteria, primarily Streptomyces, which produce antimicrobial compounds that inhibit bee and plant pathogens. A US team collected pollen from 10 native plant species and hive pollen stores, isolating 34 bacterial strains, with 72% belonging to Streptomyces. Competition assays showed nearly all strains inhibited the mold causing stonebrood in honeybees, and some were active against bacterial bee pathogens. The bacteria possess genes confirming they are true endophytes. The findings suggest that introducing beneficial bacteria into hives could help control specific pathogens, and that plant-diverse landscapes benefit bees by providing greater endophyte diversity.

This illustrated atlas bridges research and practice in periodontal plastic surgery and cosmetic dentistry, covering evidence-based decision making, treatment planning, surgical procedures, case studies, systematic reviews, and decision trees for dentists and specialists.

The passage compares value and growth investing strategies. Value investing involves buying undervalued stocks with strong fundamentals, aiming for long-term stability, income, and lower risk, while growth investing targets companies with high growth potential regardless of valuation, offering higher potential returns but greater risk and volatility. Backtests of small-cap ETFs from 2001 showed growth outperforming value (49,040 vs. 42,281 from a 10,000 investment). However, since 1926, value returned 1,344,600% versus growth's 626,600%, and value has underperformed since 2007—the longest drawdown since WW2. The riskiest stocks are volatile small-caps. The authors present a rotation strategy that switches between value and growth based on short-term momentum, which backtested with higher returns and lower volatility and drawdown than either factor alone. The choice between strategies depends on risk tolerance, investment horizon, and objectives.

The passage is a NVIDIA whitepaper describing the Ampere GA10x GPU architecture (GA102 and GA104), which builds on the Turing architecture and delivers up to 1.7x faster raster graphics and 2x faster ray tracing performance. GA102 powers the GeForce RTX 3090, RTX 3080, RTX A6000, and A40, while GA104 powers the RTX 3070. Fabricated on Samsung's 8nm process, GA102 contains 28.3 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor Cores.

Key architectural features include:

- **2x FP32 processing**: Both datapaths in each SM partition can execute FP32 operations, doubling peak FP32 rates compared to Turing.
- **Second-generation RT Cores**: Double the ray/triangle intersection testing rate and add a new Interpolate Triangle Position unit enabling hardware-accelerated ray-traced motion blur up to 8x faster than Turing.
- **Third-generation Tensor Cores**: Support new data types (TF32, BF16) and Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity, which doubles throughput by skipping zero-valued weights.
- **GDDR6X memory**: Developed with Micron using PAM4 signaling, reaching 19.5 Gbps and up to 936 GB/sec bandwidth.
- **Other features**: Third-generation NVLink (112.5 GB/sec total), PCIe Gen 4, ROPs relocated to GPCs (112 vs 96 ROPs), and a 33% larger unified L1 cache/shared memory.

The whitepaper also covers NVIDIA RTX IO, which offloads game asset decompression from CPU to GPU via Microsoft's DirectStorage API, delivering up to 100x I/O throughput improvements. The A40 data center GPU offers up to 2x power efficiency over its predecessor, while the RTX A6000 provides 48GB of GDDR6, scalable to 96GB via NVLink. Display capabilities include HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a with 8K60 support, fifth-generation NVDEC (first to offer AV1 hardware decode), and seventh-generation NVENC encoding. Appendix content covers RTX 3090/3070 specifications and a new Error Detection and Replay (EDR) feature that helps overclockers identify memory limits without crashes.

U.S. Navy-trained dolphins arrived in Mexico to help locate and capture the fewer than 30 remaining vaquita porpoises, which face extinction in the Gulf of California. Beginning Oct. 12, the dolphins will use sonar to find the animals so scientists can move them to a sanctuary for breeding—a risky plan since vaquitas have never been held in captivity. Vaquitas are often caught in illegal nets set for totoaba fish, prompting Mexico's permanent gillnet ban. A conservationist warned the whole habitat must be protected. The United States District Court for the Southern District of New York granted in part CIT Group/Factoring's motion for summary judgment in this action brought by Manuel and Esther Kitrosser (the Kays), who had guaranteed the debts of two corporations owned by Mr. Kay—Top Form Mills and Top Blush—and pledged collateral to CIT, which provided factoring and lending services to the corporations from 1971 until 1988. After the corporations filed for bankruptcy in 1988 and their petitions were dismissed in 1991 without discharge of debts, CIT liquidated the Kays' collateral in 1992. The Kays sued in 1993, alleging CIT wrongfully withheld their collateral, and CIT counterclaimed under the guarantees.

The court resolved three issues. First, it held that postpetition interest continued to accrue on Top Form's debts during bankruptcy, and because the bankruptcy was dismissed without discharge, the Kays remained liable for the debt and accrued interest under their unconditional guarantees; CIT therefore acted within its rights in liquidating the collateral. Second, CIT's $50,000 settlement with the EDA on its 90 percent guarantee of a term loan did not reduce Mr. Kay's liability, since the guarantee expressly permitted settlement with a co-guarantor without affecting the remaining guarantors; the assignment issue was deemed irrelevant dictum. Third, the two new causes of action added in the amended complaint, based on CIT's reduction of Top Blush's advance rate, did not relate back to the original complaint and were time barred; they were dismissed with prejudice. Because the exact account balance could not be determined, the court did not decide the motion in its entirety.

The paper proposes an AI-based computer science laboratory management system to address limited student engagement, cheating, and inadequate evaluation in practical labs. Faculty provide topic keywords and difficulty levels, and a fine-tuned Code Llama model generates unique questions for each student to reduce copying. The system includes faculty and student dashboards, role-based access control, lab scheduling, automated grading via a fine-tuned XGBoost regressor using SBERT embeddings, progress analytics, and an AI viva that uses automatic speech recognition and rubric-based scoring to assess conceptual understanding. Faculty can choose proctored or non-proctored modes and override AI-generated scores. The authors constructed a synthetic dataset of 10,000 ML/AI programming questions with answers, difficulty labels, and both AI and faculty scores. Validation showed question-answer similarity scores mostly between 0.25 and 0.45, indicating diversity, and faculty rated question appropriateness 4.7/5. AI grading aligned strongly with faculty scores (Pearson 0.914, Spearman 0.892, Cohen's κ = 0.69). The evaluator achieved RMSE 3.37 and R² 0.861, with the largest deviations occurring in sequence-heavy labs such as LSTM, Transformer, and reinforcement learning tasks.

The speaker accepts the Democratic presidential nomination and thanks the convention for nominating Senator Barkley of Kentucky as his running mate. He argues the Democratic Party is the people's party while the Republican Party serves special interests, citing increases in farm income, wages and salaries, and total national income between 1932/1933 and 1947. He criticizes the Republican 80th Congress for failing to act on price controls, housing, minimum wage, education, social security, health care, and civil rights, while passing the Taft-Hartley Act and a tax bill he says favors the rich. He calls the Republican platform's promises hypocritical. He announces a special congressional session on July 26, called "Turnip Day" in Missouri, to address these issues, framing the 1948 election as a continuation of the 1932 fight against special privilege.

The paper presents a DFT+DMFT formalism incorporating non-local self-energy corrections from charge and spin fluctuations, applied to the itinerant magnets iron, CrO2, CrTe2, and the altermagnet CrSb. For iron and CrO2, whose d-state fillings are not close to half filling, DMFT spectral densities resemble the non-magnetic DFT band structure, while non-local corrections produce band splitting near van Hove singularities, qualitatively matching the ferromagnetic DFT bands. For CrTe2 and CrSb, which are closer to half filling, large local susceptibility causes strong band splitting already within DMFT; non-local corrections are small for CrTe2 and enhance the splitting for CrSb. The split bands are dispersive, carry only part of the spectral weight of non-magnetic bands, and may affect transport properties while being highly sensitive to weak magnetic fields, suggesting applications in magnetic nano-devices and spintronics. The density-density approximation overestimates magnetic transition temperatures; extension to SU(2)-symmetric Hund interaction is proposed for future work.

The Triangle Game is an inside basketball offense featuring wing shooters, best suited for physically strong players due to its heavy use of inside screening. Inside players need not be dominant since most shots come off screens, but all players must be well-schooled in setting and using screens. Good wing shooters spread the defense, and a smaller player may be deployed inside to create mismatches. The offense is easy to teach and learn.

The offense includes several options: a basic continuity back screen, skip passes between wings, back door cuts against overplay, and back cuts for lob passes. Success depends on precise execution, with screeners setting solid baseline screens and receivers properly setting up screens.

Reads and counters are based on defensive positioning. When the post defender plays low, the post goes over the screen; when high, the post goes under. If defenders switch, mismatches can be exploited inside or outside. Against "show and recover" defense, the screener slips to the basket. When the post is fronted, a lob pass or ball reversal is used.

For post isolation, players must know basic post moves and be aware of the defender's location. Tex Winter coined the phrase "line of deployment" to help players and coaches read defensive post positioning. Counters include: power lay-up against high-side defense, baby hook against baseline-side defense, turn-and-face triple threat when defended from behind, lob against fronting, and pressure releases to the elbow or short corner against double teams.

Crunch time specials include the Stagger Pop, Double Base Cross Screen, Point One-On-One Isolation (typically run for the top scorer), Single Double Screen, and Side Screen options.

The passage presents two defensive strategies against the Zipper offense, which is difficult to stop without preparation for strong side down screens. The Basic NBA Show & Recover avoids switching because a "Big" screens a "Little"; defenders show on down screens, force the point guard to their weakest hand, recover to deny passing lanes, and maintain match-ups, with post defenders pushing posts off the low block. The All Out "SOS" Disruption traps the point guard on the wing using a sideline trap, with all rotations occurring as the ball leaves the passer's hands, concluding in basic SOS defensive principles.

The speaker recalls having previously urged Congress to regulate large interstate corporations, or trusts, and states that the past year has confirmed the need for such steps. He argues that regulating corporate powers is consistent with property rights and individual effort, and that supervision must come from national rather than state action. The goal is not to destroy corporations, which are an inevitable result of modern industrialism, but to eliminate their evils; the line is drawn against misconduct, not wealth. Regulation must not harm legitimate enterprises, workers, or farmers. He asserts that Congress holds absolute constitutional authority over interstate commerce, sufficient to address monopolies, unjust discrimination, and fraudulent overcapitalization, and recommends legislation; if such a law proves inadequate, the Constitution should be amended.

This paper introduces GEM, a framework applying 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) to cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) reconstruction. Traditional Fourier-space methods rely on the Fourier slice theorem and incur information loss, while NeRF-based real-space approaches require cubic memory and computation, making them slow and impractical. GEM represents protein density explicitly as a set of 3D Gaussians, each parameterized by 11 values, instantiated only at nonzero-density regions. Projection is computed in closed form by integrating along the optical axis, enabling parallel rasterization, and gradient computation is restricted to the Gaussians contributing to each pixel. Experiments on four cryo-EM datasets show GEM achieves up to 48× faster training, lower memory usage, and GSFSC resolutions better than 3 Å, outperforming the Fourier-based CryoDRGN and real-space CryoNeRF baselines. The work focuses on homogeneous reconstruction, where all particles share the same underlying 3D structure.
