This paper presents new results on boundedness of Bergman type projections in tubular domains over symmetric cones and in products of such domains, with potential applications in complex function theory of several variables. The author introduces notation and definitions for tube domains TΩ over irreducible symmetric cones, including the mixed-norm weighted Bergman spaces Ap,q_ν(TΩ), which are nontrivial if and only if ν > −1, and the weighted Bergman projection Pν, given by an integral formula involving the Bergman reproducing kernel. The second part formulates a new sharp decomposition theorem for Bergman A1_α spaces in tube domains and poses related open problems for harmonic function spaces in the unit ball and upper half space of Rn. Similar sharp decomposition results may hold in Siegel domains of second type, bounded symmetric domains, and minimal bounded homogeneous domains. Proofs rely on integral representations, uniform estimates, and Forelly-Rudin estimates. Basic preliminaries on symmetric cones, determinant functions, and Euclidean Jordan algebras are also provided.

This computational study investigates the C–C bond formation reaction (2 CH₂ → C₂H₄) on gold (111) surfaces, comparing a monolayer with three layers of gold using DFT calculations in a 2D periodic setting. On both surfaces, the reaction proceeds in two steps: diffusion of the methylene fragments toward each other, followed by bond formation and product relaxation. However, layer thickness strongly affects adsorption energies, reaction energies, and the reaction path. The monolayer binds reactants and products more strongly, shows a larger reaction energy (−432.06 vs −335.50 kJ mol⁻¹), and has a much lower activation energy (4.78 vs 52.10 kJ mol⁻¹). On the monolayer, methylene fragments adsorb with carbon atoms closest to the surface and ethylene lies flat, while on three layers the fragments rotate more, the intermediate association is less stable, and ethylene orients perpendicular to the surface. The authors attribute the stronger monolayer interaction to greater availability of gold valence electrons. Products are loosely bound in both cases and likely desorb easily. The findings highlight the role of surface morphology, relevant to dendritic structures in plasmonic photocatalysis, for carbon upconversion; future work should examine other Miller indices, surface defects, additional layers, and surface curvature.

This AMD operations guide describes the Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) feature. AMD testing shows that commands with 16 or more pages achieve significantly higher bandwidth, with maximum performance at 128 pages per command; the command ring buffer should be kept ahead of the engine, and interrupts should be requested at the end of command sequences (via NOP or Interrupt on Complete) rather than per command. Low-water mark interrupts let software refill the queue before it empties.

Certain structures do not support migration: IOMMU memory data structures accessed via SPA, vIOMMU page tables, vIOMMU pinned backing storage, and the Ring Buffer with its argument pages. For PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, source pages must be DMA-mapped using IOMMU host page tables. The TMPM engine may modify IOMMU host page table entries non-atomically and set Access/Dirty bits, so software must avoid concurrent hPTE modifications.

TMPM firmware can be reloaded only when no operations are in flight; the HV/OS must pause operations, tear down the ring buffer, and issue the reload via the BIOS-to-PSP mailbox protocol, with PAGEMIGRATION_EN bits disabled as best practice. Reload requires the same or greater firmware version, and software should always check ENGINE_READY before communicating. Reload procedures differ by EPYC family, distinguished via the FW_VER_Major field from PM_GET_CAPABILITIES (EPYC Family 19h corresponds to 71 decimal); Family 19h reload uses a firmware image and header placed in system memory, accessed through ASP registers via a PCI driver.

The hardware moves data only between 4k-aligned pages (host page table entry addresses may be 8-byte aligned; 2M pages must be 2M-aligned and smashed into 4k pages). Commands are issued through a page migration ring buffer, separate from the SEV/SNP ring buffer, holding 256 sixteen-byte commands per page; each command's parameter page contains 1–128 Migration Entries. SPAs are 46- or 52-bit depending on whether system encryption is enabled, with encryption information (C-bit) encoded under SMEE/SME-MK.

Device initialization requires verifying ENGINE_READY, setting a 4k-aligned ring buffer of 1–255 contiguous pages, configuring queue behavior, and setting DRIVER_INITIALIZED. The firmware controls the read pointer and software the write pointer; execution order between commands is not guaranteed. The TOGGLE bit in PM_Status signals completion of RB_Ctl changes. Processing can be paused/resumed via PM_RBCtl[PAUSE], and the firmware can forcibly terminate the ring buffer.

Six interrupt sources share one x86 interrupt: RBWritePtr_Err and RBMem_Err (uncontrollable errors that pause the queue), QfreeIntStat (empty queue), QthreshIntStat (low-water mark), IntOnError, and IntOnComplt. Precise halting requires the target command to be last in the queue. Interrupt status is cleared via PM_RBCtl[CLEAR_INTS].

Commands include PM_GET_CAPABILITIES (queries firmware capabilities/version), PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO (moves hypervisor-owned pages, updates IOMMU host PTEs, requires preventing CPU access and, for non-secure ATS devices, setting hPTE.PMS=1 with ATS invalidations beforehand), PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST (moves SNP guest pages; DMA unsupported; sources must be Guest-Valid/Invalid, destinations Pre-Migration), and PM_NOP (marks the end of command strings). Status and sub-status fields report results, with error codes covering invalid addresses, page states, sizes, and RMP exclusivity.

Ring buffer errors are reported in PM_STATUS; hardware errors appear in command status and/or via MCA. A hardware error during a batch of up to 128 pages can make the entire batch unrecoverable; the system may eventually cease to function, but software can attempt to save data and state before reboot.

In his November 13, 1979 announcement of his presidential candidacy, Ronald Reagan said the United States needed a long-range diplomatic strategy and true friends, and proposed a "North American accord" with Canada and Mexico, arguing that stronger neighboring countries could be key to future security. He attributed Americans' lost confidence to government policies, citing deteriorating defense strength, declining industrial productivity, and an unstable currency. He called for leadership that would remove government roadblocks, a spiritual revival, and a government that serves as servant while upholding religion, education, and family. Invoking John Winthrop's "city upon a hill," he urged Americans to keep a "rendezvous with destiny." Reagan repeated the address that evening before donors at the New York Hilton. In a subsequent statement on President Carter's State of the Union address, Reagan criticized Carter's handling of the Iranian and Afghan crises, calling the Persian Gulf threat vague, questioning its credibility given the pledge to observe SALT I and II, and arguing that grain embargoes and Olympic boycott threats were inadequate responses to the Soviet Union.

The recasting does not constitute a restatement and does not affect previously reported net income, earnings per share, total assets, or stockholders' equity. Additional details are provided in Exhibit 99.1.

The On-Balance Volume (OBV) is a volume-based technical indicator that measures buying and selling pressure by adding volume on days when the market closes higher and subtracting volume on days when it closes lower. In uptrends, OBV typically rises with price; in downtrends, it makes lower peaks and troughs, confirming the trend. When price makes new highs or lows but OBV fails to confirm, this signals potential trend weakness or an ending trend. Conversely, when OBV breaks to new highs or lows while price does not (advanced breakout/breakdown), it suggests trend continuation. OBV was first published in 1963 by Joseph Granville, who believed volume was the main force behind major market moves and that the indicator could track institutional ("smart money") activity. The article includes a backtest on S&P 500 (SPY) using RSI applied to the OBV itself; one optimized variant (5-day RSI, buy threshold of 30) produced 337 trades, a 73% win rate, 0.55% average gain per trade, 24% max drawdown, and a 2.09 profit factor. The authors conclude that volume is of limited value overall and that OBV alone is not an optimal trading parameter.

This lecture transitions from linear algebra to solving systems of nonlinear equations and optimization. It begins with a recap of singular value decomposition, noting that a condition number can be defined for any matrix as the square root of the ratio of its largest and smallest singular values.

The professor discusses stopping criteria for iterative methods: the step norm criteria (comparing successive approximations using both absolute and relative tolerances) and the function norm criteria (evaluating the residual by substituting the solution back into the original equations). Both criteria can fail individually, so both should be used. The lecture also emphasizes validating numerical results through experiments, analytical solutions in limiting cases, and solving problems multiple ways with different initial guesses.

Systems of nonlinear equations take the form f(x) = 0, where f maps R^N to R^N. Unlike linear equations, the number of solutions cannot generally be predicted. An example is the Van der Waals equation of state for vapor-liquid coexistence, which requires solving three nonlinear equations (two equations of state and the Maxwell equal area construction), reducible to two dimensions. A solution is locally unique if it can be enclosed by a ball containing no other solutions. The inverse function theorem states that if the determinant of the Jacobian at a solution is nonzero, the solution is locally unique, though a zero determinant does not preclude local uniqueness.

Linearization approximates functions near a point using the Jacobian, with error on the order of delta x squared. Convergence rates are classified as linear (q=1), superlinear (q>1), or quadratic (q=2), where quadratic convergence doubles the number of accurate digits per iteration.

The Newton-Raphson method linearizes the function at the current guess and solves a linear system for the step direction and magnitude. Potential problems include poor global convergence with bad initial guesses and singular Jacobians, which can occur near non-locally unique solutions. The method possesses a local convergence property: starting sufficiently close to a locally unique solution guarantees eventual convergence, and it converges quadratically.

A first-year student deleted all social media apps from their phone three weeks ago to focus on revision, after realizing they spent at least 15% of their day cycling between three apps. The passage cites a Pittsburgh University study linking greater social media use to depression, and research ranking Instagram worst for mental health among 1,479 young people aged 14-24. It argues that curated online personas can harm mental health, particularly for those vulnerable to mental illness. The experiment proved difficult: the author felt isolated, redownloaded Twitter on day five during Eurovision, and began checking Facebook on their phone. Despite missing notifications and feeling lonely, the author views social media as largely wasted time, recommends monitoring apps like Breakfree and Menthal, and is now focusing on creative habits and revision.

In *Bost v. Illinois State Board of Elections*, to be argued Oct. 8, the Supreme Court will consider whether a congressional candidate has standing to challenge Illinois's rule allowing mail ballots postmarked by election day to be counted until 14 days after polls close. Rep. Michael Bost, a Republican, sued claiming the rule is superseded by federal election law; the district court dismissed for lack of standing, and a divided Seventh Circuit panel affirmed. The lower courts rejected his vote-dilution claim as a generalized grievance and his cost claims as self-imposed or speculative. Before the Supreme Court, Bost argues the extra costs of employing observers constitute a "pocketbook injury" and that the rule harms his electoral prospects through diminished fundraising and a reduced margin of victory. He also urges a blanket rule that candidates have standing to challenge election rules, citing simpler standing law and access for minor-party candidates. The solicitor general supports Bost's narrow standing claim but opposes the broader rule.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC dated October 2, 2017, under Items 2.02 (Results of Operations and Financial Condition) and 7.01 (Regulation FD Disclosure). The filing incorporates a press release published by Tesla on October 2, 2017, attached as Exhibit 99.1. This information is furnished rather than filed and is not incorporated by reference into other filings except by specific reference. The report was signed by Deepak Ahuja, Chief Financial Officer. Tesla is a Delaware corporation headquartered in Palo Alto, California.

This study evaluated the Happy Ring, a novel finger-worn sleep-tracking device measuring electrodermal activity, accelerometry, heart rate, and skin temperature, against in-laboratory polysomnography (PSG), an at-home Dreem headband, and other wearables (Actiwatch, Fitbit, Whoop, Oura). Forty healthy adults aged 20–65 completed a three-night protocol (one laboratory night, two home nights); final analyses included 36 adults across 77 nights. Two machine-learning scoring approaches were compared: a generalized algorithm (leave-one-out cross-validation across nights) and a personalized algorithm (trained and tested on the same subjects). Sleep-wake detection accuracy was 0.92 (personalized) and 0.91 (generalized) in both settings, compared with 0.84–0.92 for other devices. The personalized algorithm showed significantly higher accuracy and specificity than all other devices (P<.001), with specificity of 83% versus 70% for the generalized approach and 19–54% for comparison devices; sensitivity (93–94%) was comparable across devices. For sleep staging (light, deep, REM), agreement was moderate and similar to other devices, though the personalized approach again showed the highest sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy. The authors conclude that the Happy Ring performs well for sleep-wake detection and that personalized, adaptive algorithms may improve wearable sleep assessment, particularly specificity in healthy sleepers. Strengths included both laboratory and home PSG and comparison with multiple device types; limitations included a small, healthy sample, use of a commercial device for home PSG, and non-transparent algorithms. Future research should examine larger, more diverse samples and additional peripheral signals.

Oil prices were flat on Monday, falling early on Chinese demand worries before recovering on potential crude supply reductions from Libya. Libya's National Oil Corporation opened an investigation into security violations at Sharara field, and workers at the Zueitina terminal threatened to block a tanker over pay demands. The Winston County Library is hosting three reading programs for children and teens, sponsored by local businesses. Children ages 3-5 attend "Tiny Titans Storytime" on Mondays in June. Children entering grades 1-5 join "Build A Better World!" on Tuesdays, featuring magicians Dorian LaChance and Todd Smith and The Snakeman. Teens in grades 6-12 attend Monday programs including a graphic novel workshop and a talk by Mayor Will Hill. Both programs offer $50 Wal-Mart gift card grand prizes. The author accepts the scientific consensus on climate change, not because he can evaluate the science, but because of social and economic penalties for denial. As a non-scientist, he questions whether causation between CO2 and warming is one-directional, suggesting natural warming cycles could boost economic activity and CO2 output, making causation potentially two-way. He argues that "doing your own research" is unreliable since laypeople cannot know what they don't know. While he believes climate scientists are more likely right, he considers their persuasion weaker than skeptics', who benefit from confirmation bias, whereas scientists rely on facts, prediction models, and demonizing critics—approaches he says erode their credibility. Separately, he mentions California's new law banning handheld phone use while driving, recommends a dashboard mount and his startup's app WhenHub to reduce texting before meetings, and notes that working on projects with life-saving potential motivates him.

Gladstone Investment Corporation (GAIN) is a business development company with an 8.3% annualized dividend yield, paid monthly. It invests in debt and equity of privately-held, early-stage lower-middle-market companies, targeting a 75%-25% debt-to-equity split, and earns money through capital gains plus interest and dividend income. As of March 31, its portfolio included 35 companies across 17 states and 18 industries. In fiscal 2017, net investment income rose 8.2%, total investments grew 2.9% to $501.6 million, and net asset value rose 8% to $9.95. Realized gains totaled $24 million, including profitable sales of Acme Cryogenics and Behrens Manufacturing. Its debt portfolio is 93% variable-rate with floors, helping protect income if rates rise. As a regulated investment company, GAIN generally avoids income taxes by distributing taxable income. It has paid over 140 consecutive monthly dividends, grown dividends 25% over five years, plans two supplemental dividends annually, and maintains leverage below 50% of assets with a 132% distribution coverage ratio.

A woman died after being struck by an Uber self-driving vehicle in Tempe, Arizona—the first such fatality. The car was in autonomous mode with an operator present. Uber suspended its North American tests and is cooperating with authorities.

Suncor will release its fourth quarter financial results on February 7, 2018, followed by a webcast on February 8 featuring CEO Steve Williams and CFO Alister Cowan, hosted by Steve Douglas. The webcast and archive will be available at suncor.com/webcasts. Suncor is Canada's leading integrated energy company.

The passage lists errata for the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3, covering issues such as PIT deviation from industry standard operation, incorrect DMA rotating mode, UART register access failures during DMA cycles, system hangs on I/O cycles at addresses 10000h or higher, PIC failures, UDMA write CRC corruption, ACPI-related problems, USB controller clock gating failures, ATAPI packet command failures, LPC aborts, SMB controller NEGACK errors, GPIO register write failures, and sleep state issues. It then details the PIT issue: a read-back command does not cancel an uncompleted counter latch command as industry standards specify; the PIT supplies the counter value first. The issue occurs only with a questionable programming sequence, making negative effects negligible. The resolution is to not issue a read-back command.

Congress MP Jyotiraditya Scindia will lead a 72-hour satyagrah at Dussehra Maidan, Bhopal, from Wednesday, joined by around 2000 farmers and senior party leaders, to protest farmer killings by the state government.

The Supreme Court heard arguments in a challenge to Colorado's law banning licensed mental health practitioners from attempting to change a minor's sexual or gender identity. A majority of justices appeared poised to rule against the law, with a decision expected by the end of June 2026. Plaintiff Kaley Chiles, a Christian counselor, argues the law violates her free speech rights. Conservative justices and her lawyers questioned the research and medical consensus showing conversion therapy's harms, with Justice Alito citing the 1927 Buck v. Bell case to argue for First Amendment scrutiny of speech regulation. Colorado's solicitor general and major medical groups, including the AMA and APA, defend the law, citing the provider-patient relationship and lack of evidence for conversion therapy's effectiveness. The ruling could affect how states regulate medicine and weigh medical consensus. About half of U.S. states have similar bans, while 18 have none.

Democratic Senator Ron Wyden formally asked the Senate Intelligence Committee to include a review of financial ties between Russia and President Trump and his associates in its investigation of Russian election meddling, citing the opacity of Trump's finances. The letter followed recent disclosures, including a Russian state bank's executives meeting Jared Kushner and Paul Manafort's admitted work for Russian billionaire Oleg Deripaska. Trump has denied improper ties and says he has no business deals in Russia. A Reuters investigation found Russian elites bought at least $98.4 million in property in seven Trump-branded Florida towers.

iCVS (inferring Cardio-Vascular States) is a dynamical mechanistic model of the cardiovascular system developed to estimate hidden physiological states of critically-ill patients in real-time using only routinely available bedside measurements—specifically arterial and venous blood pressure waveforms. The model includes a one-chamber heart pump, arterial and venous compartments, and accounts for autonomic regulation through a baroreflex component and an independent autonomic component, as well as non-autonomic modulation of vascular resistance. It uses fifteen hidden parameters and five observables (mean arterial pressure, mean venous pressure, heart rate, peripheral resistance, and pulse pressure), exploiting both slow and fast timescales of blood pressure waveforms. The model was demonstrated on ten critically-ill children in a pediatric intensive care unit, successfully identifying hypovolemic (bleeding), distributive, and cardiogenic shock states. Results showed agreement between model-identified states and expert clinician assessments. The authors note limitations including the small sample size, simplified physiology, and the need for prospective validation on larger cohorts.

Former BBC weatherman Bill Giles, who led the corporation's weather team for 17 years until retiring in 2000, criticised the BBC's new weather maps as a "severe disappointment". He argued the zoomed-out view makes UK detail hard to see, that the old maps were better, and recommended Channel 5 for clearer graphics. He said accuracy is not in question since the Met Office still provides forecasts, but clarity suffers. The BBC responded that the new design is more realistic.

The European Union is preparing formal action against Italy for its frequent use of "golden power" laws to influence or block banking mergers, arguing the practice undermines the single market, distorts competition, and discourages foreign investment. A draft proposal calls for stricter limits on national security justifications, requiring clearer explanations and proportionality. Italy defends the laws as protecting economic sovereignty, while EU critics view them as protectionism. The dispute highlights tensions between national sovereignty and European integration.

China faces two debt problems. Domestically, its debt has reached an estimated 328% of GDP due to post-financial crisis stimulus, prolonged loose credit, and shadow banking. Contained behind a closed capital account, this debt will burden the economy long-term and require drastic policy intervention. Externally, China has become a major creditor, lending billions to countries such as Venezuela, Argentina, Kenya, Laos, Sri Lanka, and Pakistan, often for projects of questionable value with no clear means of repayment. Such debts eventually become political, fueling resentment and new governments, as seen in Malaysia. The passage draws parallels to the 1980s Latin American debt crisis, where oil windfalls enabled cheap loans that caused capital misallocation. Similarly, China's accumulated dollar reserves are funding loans unlikely to generate sufficient returns, potentially leaving China unable to enforce its claims when debts go unserviced.

In this speech, the speaker defends his long-standing support for tariff revision, recalling that in 1906 he argued the Dingley bill's rates had become excessive due to changed production conditions. He contends that excessive rates invite monopolies, and that revision's purpose was to maintain protection sufficient to shield industries from foreign competition—not to adopt free trade or lower prices through foreign competition.

He describes the Ways and Means Committee's year-long investigation under Mr. Payne, noting the difficulty of obtaining unbiased evidence, as manufacturers exaggerated needed protection while importers were biased in the opposite direction. He presents figures showing that of 2,024 dutiable items under the Dingley law, the Payne law decreased 654, increased 220, and left 1,150 unchanged. Measured by consumption value, decreases applied to roughly $5 billion in articles, mostly necessities, while increases applied to about $879 million, of which $579 million were luxuries such as perfumes, wines and liquors, and silks.

He addresses specific criticisms: cotton rates were adjusted through a Senate compromise reducing lower grades about 10 percent; the crockery schedule was left unchanged based on evidence; print paper was set at $4 a ton pending Canadian removal of wood-export restrictions; and duties on hides, coal, and lumber were reduced. He concedes that the unchanged wool schedule is the bill's one important defect and a noncompliance with the platform, but defends signing the bill to preserve party solidarity, avoid prolonged uncertainty, and secure other provisions: the maximum-minimum clause against foreign discrimination, a 1 percent corporate excise tax, and free trade with the Philippines with limits on sugar and tobacco.

He calls the Payne bill the best tariff bill the Republican party has passed, argues that the high cost of living stems from worldwide conditions rather than the tariff, and announces a tariff board, funded with $75,000, to compile impartial data for future revisions. He opposes another revision during the current Congress, urging the bill be given two or three years to operate, and encourages low-tariff Republicans to work within the party rather than form a new one.

The ADS9803 has three separate power supplies—AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD—with no required power-up sequence; a common 1.8V supply powers VDD_1V8 and IOVDD. Layout guidance recommends 0.1μF ceramic bypass capacitors near power-supply pins, avoiding vias between pins and capacitors, keeping analog and reference signals away from noise sources, and placing reference decoupling close to the REFIO and REFM pins. TI provides development tools, documentation update notifications via ti.com, and E2E support forums. The document also covers trademarks, ESD handling precautions, a glossary, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information, along with disclaimers stating TI resources are provided "as is" without warranties.

This article offers tips from two dietitians for celebrating a healthier Diwali, particularly for those managing diabetes, heart health, or weight. Recommendations include planning ahead with realistic goals, using smaller plates for portion control, and swapping unhealthy ingredients—such as vegetable or olive oil instead of ghee, spices instead of salt, wholegrains instead of white rice, tofu instead of paneer, and baking instead of deep-frying. Sweets (mithai) should be limited or homemade with unsaturated fats and fresh fruit instead of refined sugars. People with diabetes should pair sweets with protein and fibre, monitor blood sugar levels, and watch for signs of high readings. The article also advises limiting sugary drinks and alcohol, staying active with family activities, avoiding skipped meals, and asking loved ones for support. Several healthy Diwali recipes are included.

Ascension Health and Providence St. Joseph Health are in merger talks that would create the largest U.S. hospital chain, with 191 hospitals in 27 states and $44.8 billion in annual revenue, surpassing HCA Healthcare, the Journal reported. No agreement has been reached. The talks come amid industry consolidation, including a proposed $69 billion CVS-Aetna merger.

This passage describes a pragmatic, two-stage adaptive randomized controlled trial evaluating acupuncture for acute musculoskeletal pain in a U.S. academic emergency department. The study compared auricular acupuncture (AA, based on the Battlefield Acupuncture protocol), peripheral acupuncture (PA, using accessible head, neck, and extremity points), and usual care only (UC). Of 911 patients screened, 236 were randomized. Stage 1 assessed feasibility, acceptability, and safety; Stage 2 assessed change in pain score (0–10 numeric rating scale) at one hour post-treatment. At interim analysis, neither acupuncture arm was clearly superior, so all three arms continued with a 2:2:1 allocation. Both AA+UC (mean pain reduction 2.1) and PA+UC (1.6) showed greater pain reduction than UC (0.5), with no significant difference between the two acupuncture styles. Patient satisfaction was high (mean 4.4/5), opioid use was numerically lower in acupuncture groups (not statistically significant), and adverse events were few with no serious events reported. Limitations included a single urban ED, English-only enrollment, treatment delivery by licensed acupuncturists, and lack of patient blinding. The authors conclude that both styles are feasible, acceptable, and effective in the ED and warrant further exploration for broader implementation.

The lecture covers thermal properties of foams, focusing on their use as thermal insulation. Closed cell foams have low thermal conductivity primarily because they contain a high volume fraction of gas, which has lower conductivity than solids; small cell sizes also reduce convection and radiation. Only aerogels have lower conductivity, but they are very weak and brittle.

A foam's thermal conductivity is the sum of four contributions: conduction through the solid, conduction through the gas, convection within cells, and radiation. Gas conduction dominates. Foams are blown with low-conductivity gases, though "aging" occurs as these gases diffuse out and air diffuses in over time, increasing conductivity. Rayleigh number analysis shows convection is negligible for typical cell sizes, becoming important only above roughly 20 millimeters. Radiation is described by Stefan's Law, with attenuation given by Beer's Law; the radiation contribution increases as relative density decreases. A trade-off between solid conduction and radiation produces a minimum in thermal conductivity versus relative density. Conductivity increases with cell size because radiation is reflected less often. Aerogels achieve low conductivity through pore sizes smaller than the mean free path of air (68 nanometers).

The specific heat and thermal expansion coefficient of a foam equal those of its solid constituent. Foams exhibit good thermal shock resistance: the critical temperature change causing cracking in a foam equals that of the solid multiplied by 0.2 and divided by the square root of the relative density, making foams more resistant than solids.

India's mobile subscriber base rose 0.51 percent, a net 6 million, to 1.19 billion in June, according to regulator data. Bharti Airtel led with 280.6 million users. Tele-density was 92.12. Broadband connections totaled 300.84 million, while fixed-line subscribers fell to 24 million, bringing total phone users to 1.21 billion.

Jonathan Toews describes the upcoming series against Boston as the toughest yet, comparing the Bruins to Detroit and Los Angeles as experienced teams that know how to win, and says the outcome will come down to which team wants it more. Regarding his own scoring, Toews says outside criticism hasn't hurt his confidence and he believes his game has only improved. On Boston's goaltender, he says the approach stays the same: make pucks tough to see and pursue rebounds and second chances. He credits the team's consistency to maturity, smart play over fancy plays, and players setting aside personal agendas, and says they won't engage in post-whistle antics. Toews calls facing childhood favorite Jaromir Jagr a special honor while still intending to compete hard against him. He views Boston's four-game sweep of Pittsburgh as a huge feat showing their competitiveness. Recalling Chicago's previous Cup win and the following first-round loss to Vancouver, he says the organization wants to contend every year. As captain, he emphasizes staying positive, being unselfish, and contributing in any way, and admits he was glad Vancouver didn't win the Cup.

This patent application, a continuation of a chain of prior applications dating back to a 2018 provisional filing, describes systems and methods for offering, purchasing, and reselling tokenized securities on a blockchain platform. A tokenized securities offering entity uses server computers in network communication with investor user devices to verify investor accreditation by synchronizing with third-party accreditation agencies in real time, creating an up-to-date whitelist of accredited investors (and a blacklist of blocked parties). Verified investors receive links to tokenized securities contracts deployed on a blockchain (e.g., ETHEREUM), review mandatory documents whose hashes are recorded on the blockchain, accept terms, and transmit cryptocurrency or fiat currency to an escrow account, after which securities tokens are released to the investor's digital wallet. The process comprises registration, verification, review, acceptance, and purchase steps. The tokenized securities, called BITE (Blockchain Instrument for Transferrable Equity) tokens, can represent common stock, preferred stock, options, warrants, convertible notes, and other securities, with features including optional conversion to stock, dividend-equivalent rights, and automatic conversion upon qualified financing or liquidity events. A rest period consistent with SEC rules prohibits resale before secondary-market trading. The offering entity can enforce compliance by reversing transactions, seizing tokens from noncompliant or disaccredited investors, burning unsold tokens, and operating a token transfer marketplace with bid-ask functionality. The platform also supports proxy contracts, which allow one party to offer or trade securities on behalf of another and enable ownership transfer, and escrow contracts, which encrypt contract data so only the owner can view it.

El artículo analiza la expresión de emociones en un corpus de 798 tuits publicados por las cuentas corporativas de Twitter de Acciona e Iberdrola (empresas del Ibex 35) entre el 1 de abril y el 30 de junio de 2016, mediante análisis del discurso y desde la lingüística cognitiva. Los tuits se clasificaron en informativos (neutros) y emocionales, y estos últimos en descriptivos y evocativos, aplicando una taxonomía de 14 emociones adaptada de Storm y Storm (1987) y del grupo Grid. Los resultados muestran que predominan los tuits emocionales (66,5% en Acciona y 73,62% en Iberdrola), especialmente los de valencia positiva: orgullo (la emoción más frecuente en ambas cuentas), alegría-felicidad-optimismo, interés y confianza; las emociones negativas resultan escasas. El análisis metafórico, basado en la teoría conceptual de la metáfora, identifica dominios fuente vinculados a cada empresa: la luz y la energía para conceptualizar la alegría en Iberdrola, el color verde como metonimia de orgullo, y la sostenibilidad en Acciona para la confianza y el orgullo. Se concluye que los mapas conceptuales parten de la misión, visión y valores de las empresas, reforzando la identidad organizacional, y que el corpus puede aplicarse a la enseñanza del español de los negocios.

PDP-Laban secretary-general and House Speaker Pantaleon Alvarez announced that presidential aide Bong Go will be part of the party's 2019 Senate slate, along with Zajid Mangudadatu, Senate President Aquilino Pimentel III, and several other officials. Party president Pimentel said Go "has a slot." The mid-term elections are seen as crucial for the ruling party, which currently dominates Philippine politics.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC reporting that on November 10, 2021, Thomas O. Ryder informed the company of his decision to retire from the Board of Directors effective December 31, 2021. The report, filed under Item 5.02 regarding departure of directors, was signed by Senior Vice President David A. Zapolsky on November 12, 2021. Amazon's common stock trades under the symbol AMZN on the Nasdaq Global Select Market.

The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

A man set off a pipe bomb strapped to his body in a subway passageway near Times Square on Monday, Dec. 11, 2017, during the morning rush hour, injuring himself and three others with non-life-threatening injuries. Mayor Bill de Blasio and Police Commissioner James P. O'Neill labeled it an attempted terror attack. The suspect, 27-year-old Akayed Ullah of Brooklyn, was reportedly inspired by the Islamic State group but had no direct contact with it. The blast disrupted subway and bus service near the Port Authority terminal, and President Trump was briefed.
Airbus Helicopters threatens to close its Ghimbav manufacturing base in Romania unless Bucharest commits to buying at least 16 H215M helicopters. Poland could be a likely production transfer target.

Amid national debate over football safety and concussions, Justin Timberlake said at a pre-Super Bowl news conference that his 3-year-old son will never play football, then clarified he would support him in arts or sports. Timberlake said his family is focused on manners. Sunday's halftime show will be his second, following the 2004 "wardrobe malfunction" with Janet Jackson, over which he has made peace.

The S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.4 per cent to 6183.4, erasing most of the previous session's gains, as financial stocks declined amid rising global trade tensions. NAB, Westpac, Commonwealth Bank, Macquarie and AMP fell, while Morgan Stanley notes dragged down Platinum Asset Management and Magellan Financial shares.

Researchers developed a fully automatic machine learning tool that predicts 1-year overall survival in pediatric diffuse midline glioma (DMG) from multisequence MRI. The tool uses a deep learning model (nnU-Net pretrained on adult glioblastoma data) to segment tumor core and whole tumor, then extracts and selects radiomic features for survival classification with a support vector machine. Trained on an internal cohort from Children's National Hospital (53 patients) and tested on an external cohort from Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (16 patients), the method achieved 77–85% prediction accuracy, with segmentation Dice scores of 0.91 (tumor core) and 0.88 (whole tumor) internally and comparable external results. The analysis found that homogeneous whole tumor intensity on baseline T2 FLAIR and a larger post-radiotherapy tumor core/whole tumor volume ratio indicate worse prognosis. The authors suggest the tool could support risk stratification, treatment monitoring, and multi-institutional clinical trials, though small cohort size is a limitation.

Most discussion of children online is dominated by moral panic, with few UK exceptions. Two US books take a more positive view. In Screenwise, Devorah Heitner offers practical advice to parents and teachers, urging them not to panic; she covers dangers including pornography, privacy, data collection, and plagiarism, notes that children want parental attention, highlights parental oversharing as a problem, and recommends asking children's permission before posting their photos. In Worried About the Wrong Things, Jacqueline Ryan Vickery argues that fixation on "porn, predators, and peers" ignores unequal access, drawing on nine months of fieldwork at a diverse Texas school, and recommends focusing on online opportunities rather than harms.

Wafra Investment Advisory Group Inc. NY held its stake in Marsh & McLennan Companies (NYSE:MMC) during the third quarter, owning 167,141 shares worth $11,240,000. Several other investors modestly increased their positions, and institutional investors own 83.81% of the stock. MMC shares traded down 0.24% to $67.59, with a market capitalization of $34.85 billion, a P/E ratio of 20.79, and a beta of 0.87. The company reported quarterly EPS of $0.69, beating estimates by $0.01, with revenue of $3.14 billion, below the $3.25 billion expectation, and revenue up 0.6% year-over-year. Analysts forecast $3.37 EPS for the current year. Recent analyst actions included upgrades to "buy" by Zacks, Sandler O'Neill, and Vetr, while Jefferies maintained a "hold"; the consensus rating is "Buy" with a $69.44 target price. Chairmen Alexander Moczarski and Peter Zaffino recently sold company shares, and insiders own 1.51% of the stock. Marsh & McLennan is a professional services firm whose subsidiaries include Marsh, Guy Carpenter, Mercer, and Oliver Wyman.

Investors lack a reliable historical model for how stocks react to U.S.-North Korea tensions, as valuations show little consistent link to global conflict—rising during the Korean War, falling during Vietnam, and climbing despite ongoing wars. The 1990s "peace dividend" that lifted P/E ratios appears to be a coincidence, with the internet and falling interest rates more likely drivers. The Dow's 1.1% drop after President Trump's tough talk on North Korea may reflect his unpredictability and a reversal of the "Trump trade" rather than fear of imminent war, with investors focused on his mindset.

Benchmark indices fell, dragged by energy stocks Indian Oil Corp and Bharat Petroleum on reports they may buy stakes in GAIL. Sensex closed at 32,923, down 253 points; Nifty at 10,094, down 101 points. India's current account deficit widened to 2% of GDP. Asian markets dropped ahead of a likely Fed rate hike. Nifty closed below its 200-SMA with support at 9,900-10,000; Nifty Bank faces support at 24,000. Five stock recommendations were listed.

A hockey coach speaks to reporters ahead of a playoff game against Anaheim. He says his team respects the opponent's playoff record and notes his players' experience, having reached the finals three of the last four years. Joe's injury is day-to-day, and anyone practicing could be a lineup option, with decisions to be made in meetings that night. He discusses Jeff's strong second half with Joe Nieuwendyk, Oleg's injury troubles, and the challenge of refocusing after Friday's emotional win. He praises goaltender Marty's composure, wants players like Gomez to finish more chances, expects two confident goaltenders, and stresses being ready early.

The "Pound Cake" offense attacks the Box & One defense by isolating the star player 1-on-1 in the post, exploiting the chaser's weakness in post defense, while the 2-1-2 alignment removes defensive help. If no shot develops, O4 and O5 set base screens for the star, who counters defensive reads with curls, fades, back cuts, or screen-and-roll actions. Additional options include ball reversal with post flash, screener pops, guard basket cuts, 1-on-1 pop-out isolations, and double mid-screens ("Horns"). Success depends on execution, coordination, non-verbal communication, and timing, developed through breakdown drills and scrimmaging. Game strategies include scouting opponents to anticipate defensive reads, staying alert to in-game adjustments, varying alignments, and attacking the weakest defenders. The Box & One defense uses four players in a box zone while a chaser denies their assigned opponent the ball.

Bayshore Petroleum Corp. announced the immediate resignation of director C.F. Cheng, who is leaving to focus on other business interests. The company thanked him for his years of service and anticipates replacing him soon in connection with an anticipated financing.

Foreign investors on South Korea's main stock exchange have been net sellers for six consecutive sessions, totaling 353.6 billion won ($309.85 million). On April 10, foreigners net sold 54.0 billion won while retail investors net bought 6.5 billion won.

The Supreme Court will consider whether a trial court may bar a criminal defense lawyer from discussing the client's ongoing testimony during an overnight recess. The case arises from the murder conviction of David Villarreal, who stabbed his boyfriend, Aaron Estrada, and claimed self-defense. After Villarreal, the only defense witness, testified on direct examination, the trial judge ordered that he and his lawyers not discuss his testimony overnight, though other matters could be discussed. Villarreal was convicted and sentenced to 60 years in prison. The Texas Court of Criminal Appeals sided with the state's position, but Villarreal argues the order violated his Sixth Amendment right to confer with counsel. Two precedents frame the issue: a 1976 ruling that a blanket overnight ban violated that right, and a 1989 ruling that a ban during a 15-minute midday recess did not. State supreme courts and federal appeals courts have read these cases differently. Villarreal contends the rule is unworkable and chills legal advice, while Texas argues it is workable and that overnight recesses require distinguishing testimony from other topics. Both sides cite historical practice, and the United States filed a brief supporting Texas. The case may indicate whether the Court would reconsider its 1976 precedent.

A sharp drop in FAANG technology stocks pushed the Nasdaq Composite lower on Tuesday, with rising 10-year yields and mixed industrial earnings adding pressure. Alphabet fell 3.9%, erasing its yearly gains, while Facebook, Amazon and Netflix also declined. Apple dropped 0.8% for a fifth straight session on iPhone demand fears. The tech sector fell 0.7%, the biggest drag on the S&P and Nasdaq. The 10-year Treasury yield hit 3% for the first time since 2014. Caterpillar, Lockheed Martin and 3M fell after earnings reports. Zacks Investment Research upgraded Liberty Global PLC (NASDAQ:LBTYA) from hold to buy with a $35.00 price objective, citing growth drivers such as DOCSIS 3.1 services, the Vodafone Netherlands joint venture, and acquisitions, while noting European economic pressures, competition, and currency and integration risks. The bark Cape Horn Pigeon was released too late to continue whaling that season, as the Okhotsk Sea season ends between October 1 and 10, and the vessel could not leave Vladivostok before October 1, 1892. The seizure and detention caused the owners, officers, and crew damages, including loss of the season, consumption of provisions and stores, pressing the crew into Russian service, detention as prisoners, and various expenses. The captain estimated damages at $49,500 and presented a claim in two letters dated September 15–27, 1892. In May 1893, the United States minister requested an investigation; Russia replied in June 1893 that a commission found the arrest a misunderstanding, deemed the $45,000 whale-damage item excessive, and considered $2,500 sufficient. In June 1894, the United States minister formally presented the indemnity claim. In October 1895, Russia requested vouchers for $3,400 in claimed expenses.

Rohingya woman F was raped by Myanmar soldiers in June during an attack in which her husband of one month was killed and her home burned; she later learned she was pregnant from the assault. The Associated Press interviewed 29 rape survivors, aged 13 to 35, who fled to Bangladesh, finding the sexual violence by Myanmar's security forces to be sweeping and methodical, supporting the UN's characterization of rape as a "calculated tool of terror" against the Rohingya. Nearly all victims said attackers wore military-style uniforms. Myanmar's military did not respond to AP requests, and an internal investigation concluded no assaults occurred; Rakhine's border affairs minister dismissed the allegations, and the government previously labeled accounts "Fake Rape." Medecins Sans Frontieres has treated 113 sexual violence survivors since August, a third under 18. F was raped again in September when soldiers killed her neighbors. She now lives in a Bangladesh refugee camp, hoping her unborn child is a boy, as it will be her only remaining family.

During the NHL's centennial year, fans voted to select the greatest NHL team of all time, casting over four million votes. The Edmonton Oilers were announced as the winner. In this address, the President responds to Soviet Premier Khrushchev's threats to end American rights in West Berlin and abandon its two million free residents. He argues that West Berlin, located 110 miles inside Soviet-controlled territory, is a separate territory under Allied control based on rights from the victory over Nazi Germany, protected by NATO commitments. Declaring the threat worldwide rather than isolated to Berlin, he announces defense measures: an additional $3.25 billion in military appropriations, expansion of the Army to approximately one million men, increased Navy and Air Force strength, doubled and tripled draft calls, reserve call-ups, retained ships and aircraft, and $1.8 billion for non-nuclear weapons procurement. He also requests $207 million for Civil Defense, including fallout shelters and warning systems, bringing total new defense requests to $3.454 billion. While affirming readiness to resist force with force, he expresses willingness to negotiate peaceful solutions, though West Berlin's freedom is not negotiable. He attributes the crisis to Moscow, stresses Western unity, and concludes that the nation seeks peace but will not surrender, asking citizens for their support and prayers.

COPD causes symptoms like wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath, and is diagnosed through pulmonary function tests. It can affect younger people and be caused by premature birth, uncontrolled asthma, environmental exposures, or genetics—not just smoking. Patients can manage symptoms through breathing exercises that strengthen lungs and prevent the condition from worsening.

Early Offense consists of three phases: an initial push, a flow into an early set, and a continuity style of play. The push attacks before the defense is organized, creating outnumbered situations and mismatches; if no good shot results, play moves without hesitation into the flow phase, then into continuity as the shot clock winds down. Keys to success include taking initiative to counter defensive pressure, playing tenacious defense to force bad shots and turnovers, rebounding with authority, executing effective outlet passes, pushing the ball at all times with wings in wide lanes and the point advancing within 3-5 seconds, flowing into set offense without disruption, and attacking the offensive boards. Transition begins with defense, and quick outlet passes and passing ahead are essential.

Nike unveiled the Nigeria Super Eagles' 2018 World Cup campaign, with the home kit—featuring bright green, white, and black in a chevron print—ranked best of 20 revealed jerseys by Mirror Football. In April 1983, Secretary of State Shultz sent President Reagan a memorandum proposing a strategy to counter increased Soviet activism under Andropov through an intensified dialogue with Moscow. A cover note from McFarlane to Poindexter indicated the memo was being staffed discreetly. Shultz argued the dialogue would test whether improved relations were possible while keeping the diplomatic initiative with the US, noting no realistic scenario existed for a breakthrough given the adversarial relationship rooted in the two societies' differences. He warned the Soviets would be on the offensive in 1983 in Europe and Asia, and recommended preempting this with greater US diplomatic activism. Preconditions included rebuilding American strength, revitalizing alliances, stabilizing relations with China, regional peacekeeping, and competition in ideas. The dialogue would probe Soviet flexibility, control events, and maintain Allied and domestic support, while addressing Soviet military buildup, expansionism, and human rights violations without lowering basic requirements.

The study used a single-group posttest experimental design to implement an eight-week, activity-based lesson plan in amateur guitar education during the Covid-19 pandemic. The group consisted of five volunteer beginners, aged 18–33, with no prior guitar instruction, who received online one-on-one lessons of 50 minutes each, totaling sixteen instructional hours. The chapter covered scales, chords, and arpeggios, with lessons structured into introduction, development, and evaluation stages converted from the 5E model to the 3E model. Three field experts approved the program outline, and performance was assessed using criteria from Albuz's (2001) doctoral thesis converted into 5-point Likert scales. Evaluation combined a 10-question theoretical knowledge test (weighted 40%) and a 10-question performance test (weighted 60%). Students scored 90, 80, 100, 90, and 100 on the theoretical test (mean 92), with chapter averages of 91, 89.2, 95.5, 93.6, and 98.8, producing a class average of 93.6—all rated "very good." The study concluded that activity-based instruction effectively supported theoretical learning, performance, engagement, and achievement, consistent with prior research, and suggested potential application to other instruments and educational contexts.

The court affirmed summary judgment dismissing Dennis Waldron's claims, brought individually and as administrator of his deceased wife's estate, against Ball Corporation and others. His wife died of granulocytic leukemia in January 1992; a coworker with the same rare leukemia filed a workers' compensation claim alleging factory cleaning toxins caused his illness. After Waldron refused to authorize release of his wife's medical records, Ball and its insurance adjuster used a medical expense reimbursement form he had signed to obtain the records from two hospitals, representing it as a general authorization, and used them to defend the claim. Waldron alleged conversion, fraud, intentional infliction of emotional distress, and invasion of privacy. Conversion failed because he had no possessory or property interest in records belonging to the doctor. Fraud failed because the representations were made to the hospitals, not to him, and were not material misrepresentations. The emotional distress claim failed because the conduct was not outrageous. The privacy claim failed because the statutory right covers only use of name, portrait, or picture for advertising or trade, and CPLR 4504 creates no private right of action.

The suspect who fired on Republican lawmakers playing baseball in Alexandria, Virginia, was identified as James T. Hodgkinson, a 66-year-old home inspector from Belleville, Illinois. He died from injuries sustained in a shoot-out with Capitol Hill police. Hodgkinson raged against President Trump on social media, belonged to anti-Republican Facebook groups, and idolized Bernie Sanders, whom he viewed as the only politician who understood the working class. Sanders said Hodgkinson had apparently volunteered on his presidential campaign and condemned the shooting. Hodgkinson's public posts were almost exclusively political, often criticizing Republicans and focusing on income inequality and money in politics. His home inspection business license had expired and was not renewed, and he had prior dismissed battery charges and a 2007 speeding conviction.

This paper focuses on the negotiation process during the formation phase of a Digital Business Ecosystem (DBE), defined as the co-evolution of a Business Ecosystem (an economic community) and a Digital Ecosystem (a self-organizing digital infrastructure for networked organizations). The DBE lifecycle comprises formation, evolution, and dissipation phases, with formation being the most crucial and negotiation its most important activity. The paper reviews approaches for modeling electronic marketplaces, such as Electronic Institutions and Contractual Agent Societies, and describes the Contract Net Protocol (CNP), a lightweight, high-level communication protocol for cooperative task execution introduced by Reid G. Smith, along with extensions including the FIPA Contract Net Interaction Protocol. The authors propose the Contract Net with Quality Protocol (CNQP), an extension of the FIPA CNP that adds quality evaluation steps: participants evaluate the quality of the announcer, and the initiator evaluates the quality of participants. This introduces additional time slices (tq1 and tq2) and relies on a Quality Backbone Engine (QBE). The main trade-off is reduced negotiation efficiency due to added processing time, but the approach is expected to reduce risk and overhead, improve confidence among business alliances, and support selection of suitable entities. Quality is assessed through three aspects: reliability, trust, and reputation. Future work involves using the proposed protocol for negotiation between business entities on service level parameters.

Offensive tackles are crucial yet underappreciated offensive linemen who line up at the outermost positions on both sides of the formation, occupying 2 of the 5 offensive line spots. Their two main jobs are run blocking and pass blocking, requiring athleticism, footwork, coordination, and high football IQ to handle defensive looks and blitzes. The position's name originated from early football, when edge defenders tackled ball carriers on outside runs. Abbreviated as OT or T, the position demands tall, thick players (roughly 6'3"–6'8", 300–340 lbs). Notable tackles include Jonathan Ogden, Anthony Munoz, and Joe Thomas. The left tackle is especially valued for protecting the quarterback's blind side, and tackles are often considered an offense's most talented linemen.

The Justice Department formed a special task force of prosecutors from Houston, New York, San Francisco, and its fraud section to conduct a criminal investigation into Enron's collapse, the largest bankruptcy in U.S. history. A new study found that cannabis use among people with psychosis increased by nearly 10% five years after states legalized recreational marijuana, based on data from 1,856 adults in the FDA-NIH Population Assessment of Tobacco and Health Study. Medical professionals warn the trend, combined with more potent cannabis products, could worsen mental illness, as THC is known to induce and exacerbate psychosis. The Gaia hypothesis, proposed by James Lovelock in the 1970s, holds that Earth is a self-regulating living organism in which living things interact with inorganic processes to keep the planet healthy despite threats such as a brightening sun, volcanoes and meteorite strikes. Researchers from the University of Exeter, with colleagues from the Universities of Lincoln and Southampton, propose that 'sequential selection' explains how it works: situations where life destabilises the environment are short-lived until a stable state emerges and persists, then acquires further stabilising traits. They say this explains how Earth accumulated stabilising mechanisms over 3.5 billion years. The findings, published in Trends in Ecology and Evolution, may also help estimate the probability of complex life elsewhere and understand responses to climate change.

The passage covers container design patterns and distributed system architectures. It begins with the ambassador pattern for request splitting, using IP hashing to send 90% of traffic to a main application and 10% to an experiment. It then describes the adapter pattern, where a secondary container standardizes interfaces for monitoring (e.g., adapting Redis for Prometheus), logging normalization (e.g., Fluentd for Redis slow queries and Apache Storm), and health checks (e.g., a Go-based adapter for MySQL), emphasizing modularity, decoupling, and reuse.

The text introduces microservices, noting benefits such as small team ownership, decoupled APIs, and independent scaling, alongside drawbacks like harder debugging and more complex design. It details the replicated load-balanced service pattern for stateless applications, including readiness probes, session tracking via IP hashing or cookies, a caching layer using Varnish, rate limiting for denial-of-service defense, and SSL termination with nginx.

Sharded services are presented for stateful systems where data exceeds single-machine capacity; sharded caches improve memory utilization compared to replicated caches. Sharding functions rely on deterministic, uniform hashing, with consistent hashing minimizing key remapping during resharding. Hot shards can be scaled or replicated independently.

The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes request processing across leaf nodes, with a root merging partial results; challenges include per-node overhead and the straggler problem, addressed by replicating each shard.

Finally, the passage examines function-as-a-service (FaaS), highlighting developer benefits (simplicity, automatic scaling) and limitations (debugging difficulty, poor fit for background processing, memory-heavy workloads, and unfavorable costs under sustained load). FaaS patterns include the decorator pattern for request transformation (e.g., adding defaults) and event handling, illustrated by asynchronous two-factor authentication.

Verdad Research analyzed nearly 30,000 US stocks from 2005 to 2023, classifying them into deciles of borrowability. Their findings show that hard-to-borrow stocks in the US typically produce negative returns over 3-, 6-, and 12-month horizons, while general collateral stocks yield positive returns; in Japan and Europe, hard-to-borrow stocks do not systematically underperform. Small-cap stocks performed particularly poorly. However, this negative edge may not translate into a profitable short-selling strategy, since short locates may be unavailable. Stocks become hard to borrow due to limited supply, high demand, regulatory restrictions such as Regulation SHO, stock loan fees ranging from 1% to 50%, and locate requirements. Borrowing costs are lower for large, stable, and liquid stocks, and higher for small, volatile, and illiquid ones. GameStop's short-borrow fee, for example, rose from about 1% in January 2019 to 34% in January 2021 during the short squeeze. Short selling is risky because potential losses are unlimited.

The passage argues that daily bars are the best time frame for trading, though traders should remain agnostic and use multiple time frames for diversification. A time frame refers to a trade's time horizon and the bars used in a strategy, ranging from ticks to yearly bars. Different participants use different horizons: investors hold positions for years using fundamental analysis, while traders—such as day traders, swing traders, and trend followers—use shorter frames. Daily bars are recommended for beginners due to simpler backtesting and the potential to find inefficiencies. Trading multiple time frames spreads risk, optimizes capital use, and can offset losses in one area with gains in another, reducing overall drawdowns.

Researchers at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis have identified peroxisomes, cell structures that process fats, as a backup heat-producing system in brown fat that operates alongside mitochondria. This heat generation occurs through a protein called acyl-CoA oxidase 2 (ACOX2). In mouse studies, mice lacking ACOX2 showed reduced cold tolerance, lower body temperatures, poorer insulin sensitivity, and greater weight gain on high-fat diets, while mice with elevated ACOX2 levels showed increased heat production, better cold tolerance, and improved insulin sensitivity and weight control. The fatty acids involved are found in dairy products, human breast milk, and are produced by certain gut microbes, raising the possibility of dietary or drug-based interventions. Prior studies indicate individuals with higher levels of these fatty acids tend to have lower body mass indices, though the researchers note correlation is not causation.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere architecture (GA100), is NVIDIA's 8th-generation data center GPU designed for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads. Fabricated on TSMC's 7nm process with 54.2 billion transistors, it contains 108 SMs, 6912 FP32 CUDA cores, and 432 third-generation Tensor Cores. The A100 delivers significant speedups over V100: TF32 Tensor Core operations run 10x faster than V100 FP32 (20x with sparsity), FP16/FP32 mixed-precision runs 2.5x faster (5x with sparsity), FP64 runs 2.5x faster, and sparse INT8 runs 20x faster. A new Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity feature using a 2:4 non-zero pattern doubles Tensor Core throughput with virtually no loss in inference accuracy. The GPU includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x larger than V100) with 2.3x read bandwidth, and 192 KB combined L1 cache/shared memory per SM. Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitions the A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances, enabling Cloud Service Providers to improve utilization with defined QoS and fault isolation. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth across twelve links, double that of V100. Additional features include PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, asynchronous copy instructions, asynchronous barriers, task graph acceleration, L2 cache residency controls, compute data compression, improved error detection and containment, NVJPG hardware JPEG decode, an optical flow accelerator, and five NVDEC units. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs connected via NVSwitches, delivering 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and up to 56 isolated accelerators through MIG.

The lecture continues the study of optimization methods. The instructor advises students to focus on the numerics rather than the chemical engineering details in their homework, choosing a reasonable definition when needed and explaining it in their write-up.

Reviewing steepest descent, he explains that step size can be estimated by a quadratic Taylor approximation, which gives smooth convergence where fixed step sizes fail. Students practice drawing steepest descent paths on contour plots; such paths run perpendicular to contours and will run off cliffs if no minimum exists. A dowsing rod anecdote illustrates that flat potential energy landscapes make minima hard to locate, both physically and numerically.

Linear systems Ax = b can be cast as minimization of a quadratic functional, valid when A is symmetric positive definite. Steepest descent with fixed step sizes oscillates on such problems, motivating the conjugate gradient method, which chooses directions conjugate under A so that earlier minimization is preserved. It solves n equations in about n steps, requires only matrix-vector products (no explicit storage of A), works only for symmetric positive definite matrices, and, along with related Krylov subspace methods, represents the state of the art.

Newton-Raphson applied to grad f = 0 uses the Hessian as the Jacobian. It converges quadratically—exactly one step for quadratic functions—but seeks any critical point, struggles with singular Hessians, and may step uphill when the Hessian has negative eigenvalues. Steepest descent always heads downhill but converges only linearly.

Trust-region methods combine the two: Newton-Raphson steps are taken when they stay within a trust radius and reduce the objective function; otherwise steepest descent steps are used, with the radius grown or shrunk based on how well the quadratic approximation predicted the step. Matlab's fsolve and minimizers use a heuristic dogleg trust-region strategy of this kind.

Emily Andrea has partnered with monkey monkey for a children's eyewear summer awareness campaign promoting UV protection. The 28-year-old junior doctor highlighted that 80 percent of lifetime UV exposure occurs before age 18. Her children Millie and Theo already wear the brand's sunglasses.

New research from Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health followed 501 couples trying to conceive and found that higher seafood intake was linked to more frequent sex and higher fecundity (fertility). Ninety-two percent of couples who ate fish or shellfish at least twice a week conceived within a year, and those eating seafood eight or more times monthly had 22 percent higher sexual activity. The researchers, who had not set out to study this, were unsure of the cause, noting zinc's link to testosterone but not measuring it, and suggesting shared meals as a possible behavioral explanation. The article also cites other food-sex links: 54 percent of millennials rank food equal to sex, guacamole mentions increased dating replies by 114 percent, apples improved women's sexual function, and men and women think about sex more often than food.

OpenAI announced a deal with AMD to purchase 6 gigawatts' worth of AMD chips over several years, with the first gigawatt of AMD Instinct MI450 GPUs deploying in the second half of 2026. The deal gives OpenAI the right to purchase up to 160 million AMD shares, roughly a 10 percent stake. AMD executive Forrest Norrod said demand for AI infrastructure is far from peaking. A hockey player reflects on reaching the Stanley Cup Finals after years in the minors, noting his team has been the underdog in every playoff series against the defending champion Detroit Red Wings. He dismisses sweep predictions, saying neither team expects to win in four straight, and stresses focusing on playing rather than media coverage. On October 25, 2001, Shelley Corman of Enron emailed a collection of news articles concerning Enron's replacement of its chief financial officer, Andrew Fastow, with Jeff McMahon, head of the company's industrial markets group and a former treasurer. The change followed an SEC inquiry into partnerships (LJM Cayman and LJM2 Co-Investment) that Fastow had run, which did business with Enron. CEO Kenneth Lay stated that restoring investor confidence required replacing Fastow, who was placed on a leave of absence. Enron's stock fell 17% to $16.41, roughly half its value since October 16, when third-quarter earnings included a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity tied to ending the partnerships. The decline also dragged down other energy-trading companies such as Dynegy. Analysts downgraded the stock, including Prudential's Carol Coale to "sell," citing concerns about undisclosed information. McMahon had previously raised conflict-of-interest concerns about Fastow's partnerships while serving as treasurer. Moody's placed Enron's $13 billion in debt on watch for possible downgrade, and shareholder lawsuits were filed alleging the company misled investors. Some included articles covered unrelated topics, such as small-cap stock performance, a planned service to grade corporate directors, and declines in utility stocks.

Williams %R, developed by trader Larry Williams, is an oscillating indicator ranging from 0 to -100 that measures the close relative to the highest high over a lookback period, making it mainly useful as a mean reversion indicator. Backtests on the S&P 500 (SPY) showed the best results with a two-day lookback period, producing an 11.9% CAGR versus 10.3% for buy and hold, with 22% market exposure, a 2.2 profit factor, and strong performance during the 2008, 2020, and 2022 downturns. The indicator did not work for short positions. Compared to the RSI, Williams %R produced a higher CAGR (11.9% vs. 7.3%) and performed slightly better than the WilliamsVixFix and Stochastics in the strategies tested. The article concludes that Williams %R is an underappreciated indicator.

This study investigated the relationship between hypertension, blood pressure, and blood-brain barrier (BBB) leakage in human subjects using a sparsely time-sampled dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI protocol at 7 Tesla. Between July 2019 and July 2021, 23 patients with essential hypertension and 20 age- and sex-matched normotensive controls were recruited; after excluding two outliers, 22 patients (mean age 66, 64% female) and 19 controls (mean age 62, 42% female) were analyzed. BBB leakage rates (Ki) and blood plasma volume fraction (vp) were quantified via the Patlak approach in grey matter (GM) and white matter (WM) regions of interest, and cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD) markers were rated into a global score.

No significant difference in Ki was found between hypertensive patients and controls after adjusting for age and sex, likely reflecting similar blood pressure characteristics between groups (only SBP was significantly higher in patients). However, vp was significantly higher in hypertensive patients across all GM regions. When blood pressure was analyzed as a continuous measure, Ki showed positive associations with SBP, DBP, and MAP in cortical GM, and with DBP and MAP in total GM, but no relations were found in WM or deep GM. Leakage rates were higher in males, with no age association. These associations remained significant after adjusting for cardiovascular risk factors, medication intake, and cSVD score.

Post-hoc subgroup analysis showed that patients with normal blood pressure on antihypertensive medication (NT+) had lower leakage rates in total and cortical GM than the pooled group with current hypertension (HT- and HT+), suggesting a protective effect of effective medication, though subgroup sizes were small.

The authors conclude that current blood pressure, rather than dichotomous hypertension status, is associated with BBB leakage, particularly in well-perfused cortical grey matter. Limitations include low cSVD scores in the sample, use of a 30-minute blood pressure protocol rather than 24-hour ambulatory monitoring, and insufficient power to compare medication types; larger samples or longitudinal designs are recommended for future research.

Information Services Group (ISG) held its 92nd consecutive quarterly ISG Index call covering the third quarter of 2025, hosted by Stanton Jones with Steve Hall, Namratha Dharshan, and Mark Smith.
