Valid write operations require a minimum of 32 SCLKs within a data transfer frame. Data read protocols are classified as legacy SPI-compatible (single or dual SDO-x) or source-synchronous (SRC). Four legacy protocols exist (SPI-00-S, SPI-01-S, SPI-10-S, SPI-11-S), with SPI-00-S as the default after power-up or reset. A different protocol is selected via the SDI_MODE and SDO_MODE bits and applies to both write and read operations.

In this lecture, Andrew Lo reviews portfolio theory, explaining that combining imperfectly correlated securities produces a bullet-shaped efficient frontier, and that rational investors should hold portfolios on its upper branch rather than concentrating in a single stock. Adding more securities can never make an investor worse off and shifts the frontier northwest, improving the risk-return trade-off. Mixing the risk-free asset (T-bills) with any risky portfolio yields a straight line, and one unique tangency portfolio maximizes the Sharpe ratio—the excess return per unit of risk. Because all mean-variance investors prefer combinations of T-bills and this tangency portfolio M, equilibrium (supply equals demand) implies M must be the market portfolio: all equities weighted by market capitalization, proxied by indexes like the S&P 500. The expected return of an efficient portfolio equals the risk-free rate plus a risk-scaled share of the market's excess return. For individual assets, Sharpe's CAPM extends this using beta—the covariance of the asset with the market divided by the market's variance—to determine fair expected returns and appropriate discount rates for capital budgeting. Lo also discusses alpha as a performance benchmark, the difficulty of finding negatively correlated stocks, and assumptions such as stable parameters, mean-variance preferences, and equal borrowing and lending rates.

Belarus, a former Soviet republic that gained independence in 1991, has developed an out-of-school education system combining Soviet and EU influences. The system evolved through three stages: early literacy programs for the poor, Soviet-era system building, and post-Soviet reforms integrating EU educational ideas with a focus on individual development. The 2011 Education Code defines out-of-school education as part of the lifelong learning system, with subsequent decrees regulating the sector. By the end of 2021, Belarus had 318 out-of-school institutions (185 comprehensive, 133 specialized), with regional study tours comprising the largest specialized category at 47%. Approximately one-third of Belarusian children and adolescents participate, with state-run institutions preferred due to lower fees, qualified faculty, and academic competitions that can guarantee university admission without entry exams. Key characteristics include strong legislative guarantees, diverse options emphasizing personality development, and high popularity among parents, though private capital has begun eroding the public market. Cultivation objectives center on four key abilities: mastering IT knowledge, developing social personality, surviving in a multicultural world, and sustaining lifelong study, exemplified by institutions such as the Minsk State Children's Palace, the Belarusian Youth League, and the Firefighters Association. Noted shortcomings include funding shortages, outdated equipment, unequal access for disadvantaged students, and limited small-scale interpersonal training. The article concludes that Belarus's experience offers reference value for improving China's public out-of-school education system.

The President transmits to the Senate a convention between the United States and Great Britain, concluded at Washington on the 19th instant by Secretary of State John M. Clayton and Sir Henry Lytton Bulwer. The treaty seeks a commercial alliance with maritime states to protect a contemplated ship canal through Nicaragua, as well as the Tehuantepec, Panama, and other interoceanic routes, without drawing on the public Treasury or favoring any route. It aims to protect capitalists constructing canals or railways across the Isthmus and, if ratified, to secure Central America from foreign aggression while maintaining the independence and sovereignty of its republics. The President disavows any policy of annexing these territories and cites prior precedents, including the 1835 Senate resolution and President Jackson's policy. He notes the accompanying correspondence, that the treaty may need amendment to conform with the Nicaragua treaty, and that France and Russia stand ready to accede.

The article presents four overnight trading strategies in the S&P 500 that buy at the close and sell at the next day's open, tested from October 2005 to 2012. Their short holding periods produce small drawdowns. Strategy 1 buys on a new n-day low and requires the close to be above the 200-day moving average, without which the equity curve worsens; it returned 8.43% with a 29% win rate. Strategy 2, also based on new n-day lows, returned 12.69% with a 14% win rate and a profit factor of 2.6; its short version is untradeable. Strategy 3 uses three variables and has a profit factor of about 3.8. Strategy 4, a variation of Strategy 3, benefits from oversold bounces; holding until the close raises P/L to 80% but makes the equity curve more erratic. Recently, holding until the next day's close paid off even when SPY opened up, unlike earlier.

Plans have been submitted to extend the use of the former Bartons County Infant School, Bersted, for Chichester Free School for an additional academic year, citing potential delays to highways works. Pupil numbers would rise from 390 to 420.

This study examined dropout tendencies among students at Turkish public universities using Tinto's Theoretical Dropout Model. Against a backdrop of rising higher education enrollment and increasing dropout rates in Türkiye (from 2.7% in 2012–2013 to 17% in 2023–2024), a descriptive correlational survey was administered to 1,061 undergraduate and preparatory students during the 2023–2024 academic year, using the Turkish-adapted School Dropout Scale in Higher Education (32 items, six subdimensions; α = .911). Results showed a moderate overall dropout tendency (M = 2.67). No gender differences were found, but dropout tendency was significantly higher among students in their third year or above, those studying outside metropolitan cities, working students, and those with close friends who had dropped out. Dropout tendency correlated negatively with school attendance, parental education, GPA, and family income, and positively with number of siblings. All scale subdimensions correlated positively with overall dropout tendency. The findings supported Tinto's model in the Turkish context and highlighted the need for retention strategies—academic mentoring, financial support, and mental health services—particularly at non-metropolitan institutions. Limitations included reliance on self-reported data; future longitudinal and mixed-method research was recommended.

The Dodge Challenger SRT Demon, tested at Atco Dragway in New Jersey, is the most powerful American car ever made. Its 6.2-liter supercharged V8 produces 808 hp, or 840 hp and 770 lb-ft of torque when equipped with the Demon Crate's engine control module and 100-octane race gas. The 8-speed automatic features a TransBrake that engages first and second gears simultaneously for launches. The car is 232 pounds lighter than the Hellcat, with the passenger seat, rear bench, trunk carpet, and spare tire removed. In Drag Mode, it covers the quarter mile in 9.96 seconds on premium fuel and 9.65 seconds on race gas; the author achieved 10.2 seconds at 134 mph using launch control. Priced starting at $86,090, only 3,300 units were built for the U.S. and Canada, all of which have been allocated.
The Louisiana Supreme Court denied Curran's application for supervisory and/or remedial writs.

ZnSe-WSe2 and ZnSe-MoSe2 core-shell nanowires were synthesized by sputter-depositing WO3 or MoO3 precursor layers onto CVD-grown ZnSe nanowires, followed by selenization in a three-zone furnace at 700 and 750 °C for WSe2 and 600 and 650 °C for MoSe2, with an optimized reaction time of 20 minutes. TEM showed conformal, layered shells (approximately 2 nm thick) at the lower temperatures, while at higher temperatures the shells became discontinuous, with large protruding TMD crystals (20–50 nm) forming on the nanowire surfaces. XRD, XPS, and Raman spectroscopy confirmed complete conversion of the oxide precursors into WSe2 and MoSe2, with the wurtzite ZnSe core remaining structurally intact. Photoluminescence measurements showed the ZnSe bandgap emission at 460 nm and a broad blue-green band near 480 nm, attributed to the B' transition, in both core-shell structures. The morphological differences are attributed to a temperature-dependent shift from solid-state reaction at lower temperatures to gas-phase deposition following oxide evaporation at higher temperatures. The authors suggest this approach can be extended to other TMD and van der Waals shell materials for optoelectronic and photocatalytic applications.

A Princeton University-led study published Aug. 2 in Nature found that ISWI chromatin remodelers use the "acidic patch," a negatively charged surface on the nucleosome formed by H2A and H2B histone proteins, to remodel chromatin. This is the first time acidic patch recognition has been implicated in chromatin remodeling. Using high throughput screening, researchers also found that remodeling enzymes outside the ISWI family use this feature, suggesting it may be a general requirement for chromatin remodeling. Chemical modifications on histones adjacent to the acidic patch can enhance or inhibit ISWI activity, and each protein tested showed a unique response to these modifications. The study generated extensive data for future research, and since acidic patch mutations occur in certain cancers, the findings may inform cancer therapeutic targets.

On a pre-Super Bowl episode of "Jeopardy!," contestants left the "Football" category until last and failed to answer any of its five questions, drawing sarcastic comments from host Alex Trebek. Separately, officials have called this the "worst flu season in a decade," and the Philadelphia Eagles, preparing for the Super Bowl in Minneapolis, had as many as three players ill, including Ronald Darby, Timmy Jernigan, and Mychal Kendricks.

The passage contains diplomatic correspondence from 1894 concerning Korea. John M. B. Sill states that Japan appears kindly disposed toward Korea, seeking to end Chinese suzerainty and assist Korea in becoming an independent, reformed state. K. Otori, responding to a suggestion of simultaneous withdrawal of Japanese and Chinese troops, states that withdrawal of Japanese soldiers rests with his government, which he will notify, while expressing agreement on preserving peace in the capital. Yuan Shi-Kai, addressing foreign representatives at Seoul, relays his government's position: Chinese troops were sent at Korea's invitation to suppress rebels, but after the rebels dispersed, China wished to withdraw under the 1885 Tien-Tsin agreement requiring simultaneous withdrawal, which Japan refused. A final address, delivered June 26, 1894, explains that Japanese troops arrived to protect the legation and Japanese subjects, notes the recapture of Chun Chu and dispersal of rebels, and emphasizes the historic friendship and mutual dependence between Japan and Korea.

Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon warned at Italian Tech Week in Turin that stock markets are due for a "drawdown" within the next 12 to 24 months after an AI-driven rally pushed indexes to record highs. Drawing parallels to the late-1990s dotcom bubble, he said much of the capital deployed into AI will "turn out to not deliver returns," and that excited investors are overlooking things "you should be skeptical about." He declined to call the market a bubble but said "there will be a reset." Other investors voiced similar concerns: a speaker at the same event called AI an "industrial bubble," Leon Cooperman said the bull market is in its late innings, and Selwood Asset Management's Karim Moussalem warned of "enormous risks." Despite his warning, Solomon said he remains optimistic about AI's long-term potential.

Scientists from the University of Oxford have proven for the first time that Uranus' clouds contain hydrogen sulphide, the gas that gives rotten eggs their smell. The team analysed infrared light from Uranus captured by the Gemini North telescope on Maunakea, Hawaii. Unlike Jupiter and Saturn, which have ammonia in their clouds, this difference could provide insights into how the planets formed.

Cameroon plans to restore 12 million hectares of deforested land by 2030 as part of the Bonn Challenge, aiming to address dwindling forests and climate change. The programme, launched by Environment Minister Hele Pierre and described as the largest of its kind in the Congo Basin, involves 183 bodies including 74 local councils, 36 NGOs and businesses, with councils receiving FCFA 500 million annually and vulnerable chiefdoms FCFA 70 million. Cameroon's forests, Africa's second largest at over 23 million hectares, lost 777,000 hectares between 2001 and 2015, half of it since 2012. Experts say protecting existing forests is more critical than restoration, as indigenous forests store more carbon, harbour greater biodiversity and provide water. The government says it is reinforcing forest management and imposing sanctions against defaulters.

This paper introduces EduVidQA, a question answering dataset built from educational lecture videos, motivated by a survey of 52 STEM students showing that while 67.9% wanted to ask questions while watching online lecture videos, only 17% did so in comment sections. The dataset contains 5,252 QA pairs: 270 real-world pairs curated from YouTube comments on Computer Science and AI course videos and verified by domain experts, and 4,982 synthetic pairs generated with GPT-4o from NPTEL course transcripts, filtered through timestamp checks, adversarial refinement, and Bloom's taxonomy difficulty tagging. A qualitative preference study with 10 students identified Clarity, Encouraging Critical Thinking (ECT), and Use of Pedagogical Techniques (UPT) as key answer qualities, which informed LLM-based Likert-scale evaluation metrics validated against human annotations. The authors benchmark six multimodal large language models—Video LLMs (mPLUG-Owl3 8B, Video LlaVA-7B) and LVLMs (GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5, Qwen2VL-7B, Llava 1.5-13B)—using text-based metrics (BLEU, ROUGE-L, METEOR, Entailment Score, FactQA Precision/Recall) and qualitative metrics. Results show that supervised finetuning on synthetic data improves performance across all metrics, enabling smaller open-source models (7B–13B parameters) to match or exceed larger closed models; finetuned mPLUG-Owl3 8B achieved the highest Clarity scores, while GPT-4o was the best closed-source model. Limitations include restricted participant demographics, the real-world dataset's limited size and Computer Science focus, dependence of qualitative metrics on LLM reasoning, and compute constraints limiting model selection.

In an address to a joint session of Congress, the President cites Franklin D. Roosevelt's first inaugural to argue that Americans want leadership and action against inflation. Based on the recent Conference on Inflation, he concludes that inflation must be defeated immediately through a combined package of measures and outlines proposals for executive and legislative action: increasing food production by lifting acreage limits on rice, peanuts, and cotton and allocating fuel and fertilizer; creating a national energy board to cut foreign oil imports by 1 million barrels per day by the end of 1975 and expand domestic energy; strengthening antitrust enforcement and raising penalties; regulatory reform, including inflation impact statements; restoring capital markets through an investment tax credit and other tax measures; extending unemployment benefits and creating a Community Improvement Corps; legislation to make more home mortgages eligible for federal purchase; attention to thrift institutions; passage of a trade reform bill; and a 5 percent one-year tax surcharge on corporate and upper-level individual incomes, with a $300 billion federal spending target for 1975. He asks citizens to grow more food, waste less, drive and heat less, and share with others, and announces a volunteer mobilization under the slogan "WIN" (Whip Inflation Now), organized with Sylvia Porter's help. He warns that unchecked inflation could destroy the country.

Poison has long been favoured by assassins for its stealth, and the killing of Kim Jong Nam, half-brother of North Korea's leader, at a Malaysian airport has revived interest in poisoners' methods. South Korean intelligence says female North Korean agents administered the lethal dose, reportedly sprayed in his face; an autopsy was underway. Forensic expert Porntip Rojanasunan notes poisons range from ricin and thallium to arsenic, strychnine, cyanide and potassium, each with distinct effects and detection signs. Poisoning also features in mythology and history, from Shakespeare to the Markov, Litvinenko, Tokyo sarin and Munir cases. North Korea may have added a new chapter.

CompositesWorld's 2017 Carbon Fiber conference takes place Nov. 28-30 in Charleston, SC, with registration open. Peter Blackmore's August 2000 Compaq Worldwide Sales & Services report cites solid momentum and good morale across all regions, despite supply challenges causing a non-linear quarter. Latin America saw success in direct and partner initiatives, with Argentina at 55% direct and Brazil at 60% direct business, plus new e-business alliances including Diveo, Artikos, Terra, and Patagon.com. Compaq Canada increased Q2 profits 88% over the prior year and expects to be 85% direct by year-end. The U.S. Department of Energy's NNSA selected Compaq to build the world's fastest supercomputer, a 30+ TeraOPS system code-named "Q," valued at over $200M for Los Alamos National Laboratory. Other major wins included contracts with Alcatel, EDF, Korea Telecom, KPMG, and the National Science Foundation. IDC data showed Compaq leading the worldwide PC server market with 30.2% share. The Storage Product Group posted $179M in Q2 profitability, up 45%, while CPCG returned to profitability a quarter ahead of expectations with $63M in operating profit. The report also covers the Zero Latency Enterprise initiative launching in October, consumer market gains including leadership in U.S. installed base share, and numerous customer wins worldwide across Customer Services, Professional Services, and regional markets.

CME lean hog futures fell about three per cent on Friday, pressured by spreading and abundant supplies weighing on cash markets. October hogs dropped 1.75 cents to 59.175 cents/lb. Live cattle rose to two-week highs on technical and investment fund buying. CFTC data showed speculators added to net long positions in cattle and hog futures.

This paper addresses memory management challenges in long-running Low-Code/No-Code (LCNC) agents: memory inflation and contextual degradation caused by finite LLM context windows. The authors propose a hybrid memory system comprising Working Memory, an Episodic Memory vector store, and a Semantic Memory knowledge base. Its core, an "Intelligent Decay" mechanism, assigns each memory a utility score combining recency (exponential decay), relevance (cosine similarity), and user-assigned utility; low-scoring memories are deleted or consolidated into semantic memory via LLM-generated summaries. A timeline-based visual interface enables non-technical users to act as Human-in-the-Loop evaluators who can pin, strike through, or consolidate memories. Drawing on cognitive science concepts of episodic/semantic memory and active forgetting, the approach contrasts with baselines such as sliding windows, summarization, and RAG. In simulated 500-turn experiments on project-plan generation, the hybrid system achieved a 92.5% task completion rate versus 81.4% (basic RAG) and 65.2% (sliding window), with lower token cost than RAG, a 0.94 consistency score, and a 1.2% contradiction rate; it exhibited "self-evolution" while an All-Add strategy showed "self-degradation." Limitations include hyperparameter tuning and dependence on user feedback quality. Future work includes autonomous parameter calibration, multimodal inputs, and procedural memory.

This passage from the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block specification describes NAE (Non-Automatic Exit) events and features for SEV-SNP guests:

The SNP AP Creation NAE event lets guests create, update, or destroy AP vCPUs at specified VMPL levels using VMSA pages marked via RMPADJUST, providing an alternative AP boot method and enabling vCPU hotplug. The #HV doorbell page NAE event allows guests to register a doorbell page (via GET_PREFERRED, SET, QUERY, and CLEAR actions) for hypervisor-injected exceptions when Restricted Injection is enabled. Related events include #HV Send IPI (using SW_EXITINFO1 formatted like the x2APIC Interrupt Command Register), #HV Timer (emulated APIC timer with SET/GET actions), APIC ID List (lets guests obtain APIC IDs without INIT-SIPI broadcasts), and SNP Run VMPL (runs vCPUs at different VMPL levels with unique VMSAs).

The SEV-TIO extension enables guests to bind trusted devices, requiring a guest PCI ID, MMIO ranges, and TDISP status, with data pages used for measurements, certificates, and attestation reports. Secure AVIC manages guest-owned APIC state through per-vCPU backing pages registered via REGISTER/UNREGISTER actions. A Termination Request event lets guests request termination with reason codes.

Because hypervisors cannot modify vCPU registers after they are measured and encrypted, SMP booting requires alternative methods: modified reset vectors, predetermined initial register locations, or AP jump tables (4K, encrypted, page-aligned) communicated via NAE events or the SEV-SNP Secrets Page. For NMIs, hypervisors must intercept #DB rather than IRET and rely on guest "NMI Complete" messages. Hardware debug register virtualization is supported when available; otherwise DR7 accesses are intercepted and cached. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

The #HV doorbell page contains PendingEvent (vector number, NMI/#MC indicators, NoFurtherSignal) and NoEoiRequired fields. The host presents interrupts by writing vector numbers and delivers #HV notifications; guests acknowledge via atomic exchanges and may complete EOIs by clearing NoEoiRequired. Guests must execute HLT with interrupts disabled and validate vectors to guard against non-cooperative hosts.

The bark Cape Horn Pigeon was managed at the time of seizure by Joseph and William R. Wing of New Bedford, Massachusetts, copartners as J. & W. R. Wing. On September 10, 1892, ownership in sixty-fourths was held by the Wings (20/64 after later conveyances), Edward F. Potter, Thomas M. Hart, John Wing, Michael Baker, George W. Collins, Charles C. Church, and Louisa B. Haskell, who had acquired the Seabury estate's interest. All owners were native American citizens. The crew numbered 30 besides the captain and was shipped under a shipping paper, with compensation set as shares of the voyage's net proceeds; some crew claims were assigned to the owners against advances, and most seamen were in debt to the ship due to the small oil catch. Built in Dartmouth, Massachusetts, in 1854 for whaling, the 201.42-ton bark was purchased by the Wings in 1887 and fitted out at San Francisco in December 1891 for a year's whaling voyage in the Japan and Okhotsk seas, not for sealing.

The passage opens with acknowledgments to the author's family and helpers. Modern applications demand high availability, reliability, and rapid scalability, making nearly all applications distributed systems. Building these is challenging and often bespoke, resembling software development before object-oriented languages. Containers and orchestrators provide reusable building blocks that simplify building reliable distributed systems.

Formula 1 closed its 2019 season with strong performance: 4.2 million race attendance (up 2% over 2018), a cumulative TV audience of 1.9 billion (up 9%), and a social media following exceeding 25 million. Since Liberty Media purchased Formula 1 in 2016 for $4.6 billion—ending Bernie Ecclestone's control dating to the early 1980s—CEO Chase Carey, CCO Sean Bratches, and Motorsport Director Ross Brawn had run the organization like a startup, building marketing, research, sponsorship, and digital functions that previously did not exist. Their goal was to evolve F1 from a motorsport into a global entertainment brand, guided by five strategic pillars including improving on-track competition, upgrading events, engaging fans digitally, expanding the brand, and broadening the global footprint. Revenue was generated through promotion (30% of 2019 revenue), broadcasting (38%), advertising and sponsorship (15%), and other sources such as the Paddock Club and F1TV. A persistent challenge was limited on-track competition, as aerodynamic wake effects hindered overtaking and the three highest-budget teams—Mercedes, Ferrari, and Red Bull—had dominated the Constructors' Championship for four consecutive seasons. The 2021 Concorde Agreement, which achieved consensus by season's end, introduced a $175 million budget cap and redesigned cars to enable closer racing. Lewis Hamilton and Mercedes again won the 2019 titles. Formula 1 also committed to carbon neutrality by 2030 while balancing commercial, sporting, and societal interests.

The judgment of sentence was affirmed on the opinion of President Judge Griffith, and the appellant was directed to appear in the court below and be committed until complying with any unperformed portion of the sentence.

Carroll County's school board is asking commissioners to reconsider moving the school system's Central Office to the former North Carroll High School building, despite the county budget including funds for the move. Superintendent Stephen Guthrie said the board's main concerns are the non-central location and increased operating costs, with rough figures showing about 50 percent more miles driven and 30 percent more time traveling to schools. The board agreed to send a letter to commissioners detailing its concerns and specific additional annual costs. Board member Marsha Herbert recused herself from discussions, having taught at North Carroll for decades. Commissioner President Richard Weaver defended the budget, saying the school system is one piece of the county's larger puzzle.

The passage describes the NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture, which introduces a Hybrid Rendering model combining real-time ray tracing, rasterization, AI, and simulation.

Key features include:

- **Video encoding**: Turing's encoder exceeds the quality of x264 (fast settings) with dramatically lower CPU utilization, making 4K streaming possible.
- **VirtualLink/USB Type-C**: Hardware support delivers power, display, and data to VR headsets through a single USB-C connector, reducing cable clutter and enabling VR on small form factor devices.
- **NVLink**: TU102 (two x8 links) and TU104 (one x8 link) use second-generation NVLink for SLI instead of MIO/PCIe, providing 25 GB/sec per direction per link (50 GB/sec bidirectional per link). Only two-way SLI is supported.
- **RT Cores**: Dedicated hardware in each SM accelerates BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, offloading the SM. Turing achieves 10+ Giga Rays/Sec versus Pascal's ~1.1, roughly 10x faster ray tracing.
- **NGX**: A deep learning technology stack using Tensor Cores, offering DLSS (trained on 64x supersampled reference images, delivering TAA-like quality with roughly half the shading work), InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.
- **Mesh Shading**: New Task and Mesh shader stages with cooperative thread models eliminate CPU draw call bottlenecks, enabling real-time rendering of hundreds of thousands of objects.
- **Variable Rate Shading (VRS)**: Shading rate can vary per 16x16 pixel region, enabling Content Adaptive Shading, Motion Adaptive Shading, and Foveated Rendering.
- **Texture Space Shading (TSS)**: Decouples shading from screen-space pixels, storing results in texture space for reuse and improved temporal stability.
- **Multi-View Rendering (MVR)**: Supports up to four views per pass (32 at the API level), expanding Pascal's Simultaneous Multi-Projection.
- **TU104**: Six GPCs, 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, 13.6 billion transistors; used in GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000.
- **TU106**: Three GPCs, 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores, 10.8 billion transistors; no NVLink or SLI support; used in GeForce RTX 2070.
- **Tesla T4**: A Turing-based inferencing GPU with 2,560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores.
- **RTX-OPS**: A workload-based metric weighting Tensor (20%), FP32 (80%), RT (40%), and INT32 (28%) operation usage.
- **Ray tracing background**: The passage explains BVH acceleration structures, denoising filters, and ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, with examples from Battlefield V and Shadow of the Tomb Raider.

The passage concludes with NVIDIA legal disclaimers, trademark notices, and copyright information.

WIRED presents a roundup of discounts from Amazon's second Prime Day sale of the year, called Prime Big Deal Days, ahead of Black Friday. Featured deals include smartphones such as the Pixel 9a and the $500 OnePlus 13R, an 11-inch iPad Air, a $70 10-inch Amazon tablet, and the color Kindle Colorsoft. Other products on sale include wireless chargers, the GoPro Hero 13, a power bank, a magnetic wallet, an Echo Show, a 65-inch TCL QLED TV reduced from $1,500 to $948, smart locks, the Orbi 770 mesh router, security cameras including the Arlo Pro 5, a smartwatch, power stations like the Anker Solix C1000, laptops including a $799 M4 MacBook and a Snapdragon-based Windows alternative, the Chromebook Duet Gen 9, an OLED monitor, keyboards, mice, a Stream Deck, and an external hard drive.

This study examined structural and policy-related barriers to medical oxygen access in Peru, conducted as a country case study for the Lancet Global Health Commission on Medical Oxygen Security. Using a problem-based political economy analysis based on 13 key informant interviews and reviews of academic literature, grey literature, and policies, the study found that Peru's fragmented, decentralized health system lacked a national oxygen strategy, with each subsystem and region managing procurement independently. A regulation requiring >99% oxygen purity—despite WHO's recommendation of 93% or higher—created a "policy trap" that concentrated the market among a few large suppliers (two business groups supplied 92.6% of government-contracted oxygen from 2008–2020) and excluded smaller providers. During COVID-19, Peru—which had the highest excess mortality rate globally in 2020—faced severe oxygen shortages, particularly in Andean and jungle regions, alongside slow government response, bureaucratic delays in lowering purity standards to 93%, procurement irregularities, and an absence of data on oxygen demand, production, and distribution. Civil society initiatives, notably Respira Perú, donated oxygen plants—496 were installed by the pandemic's end—but the absence of maintenance plans left nearly 200 plants unused, broken, or abandoned, and health establishments are reverting to cylinder purchases. Interviewees concluded that Peru has not effectively learned from the crisis and recommended establishing a National Oxygen System encompassing demand-supply tracking, maintenance funding, trained personnel, and quality control.

Apple Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended March 28, 2020 reports total net sales of $58.3 billion, up 1% year-over-year, driven by higher Services (up 17%) and Wearables, Home and Accessories (up 23%) sales, partially offset by lower iPhone (down 7%), iPad (down 10%) and Mac (down 3%) sales. Net income was $11.2 billion ($2.55 diluted EPS) versus $11.6 billion in the prior-year quarter; six-month net sales were $150.1 billion with net income of $33.5 billion. Total assets were $320.4 billion and shareholders' equity $78.4 billion. During the quarter, the Company repurchased $18.5 billion of common stock and paid $3.4 billion in dividends. Apple adopted new lease (ASU 2016-02) and hedging (ASU 2017-12) accounting standards in the first quarter of 2020. Term debt totaled $98.0 billion and commercial paper $7.5 billion. The COVID-19 pandemic caused manufacturing and supply chain disruptions, iPhone supply shortages, temporary closure of retail stores outside China effective March 13, 2020, and weakened demand. Legal matters include the European Commission State Aid Decision (adjusted recovery amount of €12.9 billion held in escrow), a proposed iOS performance management settlement of up to $500 million, and a €1.1 billion French Competition Authority fine, which Apple plans to appeal.

Cash-In-Transit (CIT) heists have hit an all-time high in South Africa, with more than 159 reported in 2018 and industry losses of R1.1 to R1.4 million in damaged vehicles. On Tuesday, three trucks were attacked hours apart in Mthatha and Bloemfontein. Suspects shot and twice attempted to bomb a Fidelity armed truck but failed to retrieve money. Two G4S trucks were blocked on the N8; explosives failed to detonate and suspects fled. Drivers survived with minor injuries, and police report no investigative progress.

ARS scientists found that cotton farmers facing Palmer amaranth infestations can conventionally till for one year, then return to conservation tillage. Economist Leah M. Duzy found conventional tilling offers a financial advantage in the first year due to weed pressure, but switching back to conservation tillage saves approximately $25.57 per acre annually in the second and third years.

A hockey player reflects on winning a second consecutive championship, calling it gratifying even while playing without one of his two best defensemen. He says the team followed Vladi and Sergei through their recoveries from an accident without using it as motivation, and that the accident brought the close-knit team even closer. He recounts learning of Vladi's arrival and deciding to give him the Stanley Cup, noting that a year earlier Vladi and Sergei were not expected to live. Proud to have the Yzerman name on the trophy, he says he is having the most fun of his career, hopes to play five more years, and is not considering retirement. He describes the season, with the Olympics in the middle, as draining. He calls the four-game sweep deceiving, saying the first two games could have gone to the Caps and the Dallas series was the toughest physically. He credits strong defense, four balanced lines, and a young core for the team's success, and hopes coach Scotty returns.

Press secretary Sean Spicer cited an audit as the reason President Trump's tax returns cannot be made public, though the IRS says audits don't prevent releasing returns. Weekend protests across the U.S. urged Trump to release his returns.

This scoping review examined approaches used to measure socio-economic status (SES) in sub-Saharan African health research. Following the Arksey and O'Malley framework, five databases were searched from January 2012 to June 2024. Of 19,669 publications identified, 65 articles were included in the final analysis, covering 22 countries, with South Africa, Kenya, and Ghana most represented. Most included studies were research articles (93.8%), cross-sectional in design (52%), and focused on SES assessment and maternal and child health (31% each). The review identified 41 SES measures across 11 categories. The asset-based Wealth Index was the most used measure (61.9%), with the Wealth Index itself accounting for 28.6%. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was the predominant calculation method, used independently in 57.7% of asset-based index cases and combined with other methods in 9.6%. The authors note that measurement variability hampers comparability across studies and that choice of SES measure affects detection of health disparities. Limitations include lack of critical appraisal of study quality, methodological heterogeneity, and possible incomplete literature coverage. The review recommends standardizing SES measurement methods in Africa while allowing adjustments for local contexts.

The speaker addresses a Council dedicated to improving the Nation's moral and spiritual life, arguing that the political success of government depends on the religious convictions of the people. He describes modern life as increasingly complex and interdependent, with science and knowledge multiplying opportunities for wrongdoing, while postwar conditions have weakened restraints, fostered lawlessness, and eroded respect for authority and others' property. He contends that government cannot adequately address these problems: its chief function is maintaining order, security, and justice, and law enforcement and education are effective only when supported by public sentiment and moral growth, which he says come from religion. He asserts that government rests on religion, citing clergymen such as Thomas Shepherd, Thomas Hooker, and John Wise as influences on education and founding principles, and claiming that rights to freedom, equality, and self-government derive from the common fatherhood of God. Punishment, he argues, treats only symptoms; true reform requires an enlightened conscience. While noting present dangers, he sees evidence that religious faith has not diminished but increased, and concludes that the country needs more religion, since redemption comes through sacrifice and without faith enlightened civilization cannot endure.

A research team including Binghamton University archaeologist Carl Lipo and the University of Arizona's Terry Hunt confirmed that Rapa Nui's moai statues could be moved upright in a rocking, zig-zag motion using rope and few people. Using 3D modeling, physics, and field experiments, the team identified design features—a forward lean and wide D-shaped bases—that enabled this movement. A 4.35-ton replica moai was transported 100 meters in 40 minutes by 18 people. Concave roads on the island further supported this transport method. The findings honor the Rapa Nui people's engineering achievement with limited resources.

Poway Unified School District is saying farewell to 28 retiring high school teachers, with profiles provided for those who served at least 30 years. Traci Barker-Ball retires after 35 years, all at Poway High as student services coordinator and a former "Teacher of the Year." Don Jones retires after 34 years, most recently teaching health science and coaching track and field at Rancho Bernardo High. Melinda Watson retires after 34 years teaching math at Mt. Carmel High. Patsy Malta retires after 33 years teaching physical education and coaching boys volleyball at Mt. Carmel. Lori Brickley retires after 32 years, most recently teaching AP biology at Rancho Bernardo High, where she was a founding faculty member. Keith Koelzer retires after 32 years, most recently teaching math at Mt. Carmel. Robert Saxton retires after 31 years at Abraxas High, teaching art and sustainable agriculture. Each reflected on their careers, saying the profession met or exceeded their expectations, and noted changes including technology and increased demands on teachers. The remaining retirees, with 10 to 29 years of service, include Mark Dufva, Kenneth Matson, Joan Quesada, Jayne Lutgen, Lynne Olps, John Carolan, Davette McFadden, Christian Michel, Kenneth Faverty, Anne Rego, Jane Wakeham-Lopez, Richard Willard, Jeannine Ugalde, Marie Metzgar, Emilia Gomez, Lisa Schick, Jacquelyn Whitaker, Tamarah Neuhaus, Mai Sciarratta, Katherine Powell, and Randall Wright.

Sudan, the world's last male northern white rhino, was euthanized Monday at Kenya's Ol Pejeta Conservancy at age 45 after a severe leg infection left him unable to stand. Captured in Sudan in 1975, he lived at a Czech zoo before being relocated to Kenya in 2009 with two females, Najin and Fatu. War and poaching had driven the species to extinction in the wild. Sudan never reproduced, but sperm was collected from him and other males. Scientists hope to harvest eggs from the females and implant fertilized embryos in southern white rhinos, though the egg retrieval procedure has never been done and could risk the females' lives.

Castle Gardens is a purpose-built care home in Invergordon offering dementia, nursing, residential and end of life care. It features en suite bedrooms, organised activities, a mature garden, a GP service, and allows small pets.

Changing lifestyles and hectic schedules are shifting consumer preferences toward convenient, easy-to-eat snacks, driving demand for cheese snacks globally. The global cheese snacks market is expected to grow at a CAGR of 5.2% from 2017 to 2025, according to a Persistence Market Research report. Savory snacks such as extruded snacks and salted chips are the most frequently consumed, while frozen and processed cheese are gaining popularity. Rising health consciousness is increasing demand for baked over fried products, and recent research highlighting cheese's nutritional value has boosted consumption. Leading companies include Sargento Foods, PepsiCo, McCain Foods, TINE SA, UTZ Quality Foods, ITC Limited, and General Mills.

This study developed and tested a Maternal Vulnerability Segmentation Tool (MVST) in Oromia, Ethiopia, to identify pregnant women at higher risk of underusing essential maternal services such as antenatal care (ANC) and health facility delivery. Using baseline data from a community-based quasi-experiment (1,189 pregnant women screened; 470 sampled), the researchers created a 20-item questionnaire covering economic, social, and service-access drivers and applied exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis. The final tool comprised four items for urban-rural settings (rural residence, house not made of corrugated iron, lacking a mobile phone, and far distance from a health facility) and six items for rural settings (adding women's and husband's education and household mobile phone ownership), each with an internal reliability coefficient (Cronbach's alpha) of 0.60 and acceptable goodness-of-fit statistics. Higher vulnerability composite scores were associated with declining ANC visits and health facility delivery (p<0.001), with cut-off scores of 3 (for delivery) and 1 (for ANC) distinguishing more vulnerable women. Mediation regression indicated the effect of vulnerability on facility delivery was mediated through ANC visits. The authors describe the MVST as a segmentation rather than tailoring tool, intended to help frontline health workers identify vulnerable women for targeted interventions, and note limitations including context-specific applicability, the dynamic nature of vulnerability, and the need to validate the tool against health outcomes and across other settings.

Soumya Swaminathan, a pediatrician known for her tuberculosis work and currently Director General of ICMR, will take charge as Deputy Director General (programmes) at WHO in late November, becoming the first Indian in this role. Her priorities align with WHO Director General Dr Tedros's goals, including universal health coverage, epidemic management, non-communicable diseases, and access to diagnostics and drugs. She noted India's regional health disparities and emphasized preventive and promotive healthcare through health and wellness centres. Her father, Dr M S Swaminathan, said international exposure brings valuable perspective, and she hopes her WHO stint will be a learning experience to later contribute to India.

The share of 22- to 27-year-olds without college degrees who are working or seeking work has declined, per a Goldman Sachs analysis, with this group's labor force participation falling more steeply than that of degree holders. The share of disconnected youth—Americans aged 18-24 who are not in school, working, or looking for work—has trended upward, reaching roughly 12% as of May data, higher than any year between 1989 and 2009. Experts attribute this to a mix of economic, cultural, and psychological forces. Some young people can find work but choose not to pursue available jobs, which they perceive as miserable or unable to provide family-sustaining earnings—earnings increasingly concentrated among degree holders. A cultural stigma against non-degree jobs, mental health challenges, extended family support allowing young people to live at home longer, and gig work going uncounted in labor statistics may also contribute. Proposed solutions include education models embedding practical work experience, such as internships and apprenticeships, and efforts to reduce stigma around non-degree career paths. Experts express hope for younger generations but view helping those already in their mid-to-late twenties as an uphill battle.

This passage is a Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP, version 1.0, dated 16 August 2019) for study ZEA-DNK-02170, a multicenter trial (approximately 5 centers) comparing dasiglucagon (liquid formulation, 1 mg/mL, 0.6 mL), GlucaGen (1 mg lyophilized powder), and placebo in patients aged 6–17 years.

**General analysis:** Results will be reported in tables, listings, and figures (TLFs) using ICH numbering. Testing is 2-sided at the 0.05 significance level. Continuous variables will be summarized with descriptive statistics; PK parameters (except Tmax) with geometric mean and geometric % CV. Categorical variables will be summarized by counts and percentages. Analyses will use SAS Version 9.4 or higher; PK/PD analyses will use Phoenix WinNonlin Version 6.4 or higher. Analyses defined before unblinding are a priori; subsequent analyses are post hoc and exploratory.

**Analysis sets:** The safety analysis set includes all randomized patients receiving at least 1 dose (assigned by actual treatment). The full analysis set (FAS) comprises the safety analysis set patients (assigned by randomized treatment). The per protocol set (PPS) includes FAS patients without relevant protocol deviations. The primary endpoint analysis uses the FAS, a secondary analysis uses the PPS, and safety analyses use the safety set.

**Efficacy:** The primary endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery, defined as a first increase of ≥20 mg/dL from baseline within 45 minutes without rescue IV glucose. Secondary endpoints are recovery within 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes and plasma glucose changes from baseline at those times. A hierarchical testing procedure controls multiplicity for dasiglucagon versus placebo comparisons; GlucaGen comparisons are excluded from the hierarchy. The primary analysis uses a stratified log-rank test (by age group and injection site) with Kaplan-Meier plots; patients receiving rescue IV glucose or not recovering are censored at 45 minutes. Supportive analyses include a stratified Wilcoxon test, a discrete-time Cox proportional hazards model, and linear interpolation of recovery times. Secondary recovery rates use a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test; glucose changes use ANOVA. No imputation is applied for missing data, and no interim analyses are planned.

**PK/PD:** PK metrics will be derived by non-compartmental analysis. Plasma concentrations are sampled pre-dose through 300 minutes; glucose is sampled pre-dose through 45 minutes (60 minutes if body weight ≥21 kg). The PD endpoint is the area under the effect curve above baseline from 0 to 30 minutes (AUE0-30min).

**Safety:** Analyses use the safety set and focus on treatment-emergent AEs coded with MedDRA. Summaries cover exposure (insulin administration, hypoglycemia induction, trial medication, rescue glucose infusion), local tolerability, AEs (including adverse events of special interest, injection site reactions, SAEs, and deaths), laboratory parameters, vital signs, ECG (including QTcF categorical analyses), and immunogenicity (ADA occurrence, descriptive only).

**Changes from protocol:** The primary efficacy analysis was reworded with additional sensitivity and supportive analyses, and secondary endpoint terminology changed from "within" to "at" specified minutes.

Appendices specify presentation and programming standards, SAS programming QC requirements, and an ICH E3-aligned list of tables, figures, and listings.

The SPREAD Offense is a 3-2 no post motion offense requiring all five players to be skilled passers and ball handlers. Success depends on reading and countering defensive overplays. Basic cuts involve passing, basket cuts, and clearing to corners. Overplayed players should immediately back cut rather than fight pressure. Ball handlers may drive when defenders overplay, kicking out if defenders help. A back door option lets corners break into the middle when wings are overplayed or the shot clock winds down.

Deepa Das Acevedo, a legal anthropologist and associate professor of law at Emory University, argues in her new book that politicians attacking tenure are solving a problem that "didn't need fixing in the first place." The interview follows the termination or leave of at least five tenured professors over social media comments made after Charlie Kirk's killing. Acevedo traces two decades of state legislation and university policies weakening tenure, often justified by claims that tenured faculty are too hard to fire. She maintains that tenure's core justifications—employment security as compensation for lower pay and protection of academic freedom—remain valid, and that empirical data does not support claims that tenure reduces productivity. She also notes tenure does not shield bad actors, since just-cause employment permits termination for serious misconduct. Recent rapid firings show universities can disregard tenure processes they are legally able to follow.

Research from Ben-Gurion University found that smiley emojis in work-related emails decrease perceptions of the sender's competence and do not increase perceived warmth, unlike actual smiles. The study, published in Social Psychological and Personality Science, involved 549 participants from 29 countries. Participants shared more detailed information in responses to emails without smileys, and smileys led readers to assume the sender was female when gender was unknown. Researchers advise avoiding smileys in initial workplace interactions.

This study reports the qualitative component of a quality improvement project examining regional teaching for Stage 1 anaesthetic trainees in a UK deanery, prompted by the 2021 national curriculum change and low GMC survey scores. Semi-structured focus group interviews were conducted with six trainees and eight trainers, and data were analysed thematically. Themes indicated that Stage 1 training is complicated by the new curriculum, heavy demands including the primary FRCA examination, and heterogeneous trainee needs. Inter-hospital variation in teaching provision was perceived as unfair and fostered competition, while differing compensation for trainers and limited resources created tensions. Participants expressed wariness about logistical challenges of a regional programme, including location, group dynamics, rota organisation, funding, and quality control. However, motivators such as improved exam-focused teaching, fairness, easier organisation for smaller hospitals, educator development, and social networking supported implementation. Trainers and trainees were broadly in favour of a regional teaching programme, with trainers willing to adapt to trainee preferences. The authors conclude that teaching is undervalued and undercompensated, that GMC survey data are insufficient for decision-making, and that qualitative methods aided stakeholder engagement and QIP planning. Findings led to a dedicated trainee survey, policy enquiries, and consultant engagement. Limitations include small trainee numbers and potential interviewer bias.

Larry O'Neal, 44, a U.S. Border Patrol agent in Houlton, was indicted Feb. 15 on a felony count of possession of child pornography. Homeland Security agents began investigating in January after tracing a downloaded file to his home IP address. He was arrested Jan. 19; a search found child and adult pornography on his computer and external drive. O'Neal admitted downloading the material. He pleaded not guilty Feb. 22 and was released on bail. If convicted, he faces up to 10 years in prison, a $250,000 fine, and sex offender registration.

This preprint reports the first genome-wide association study (GWAS) of neonatal jaundice, conducted using nearly 30,000 parent-offspring trios from the Norwegian Mother, Father and Child Cohort Study, with 27,384 neonates and 1,826 cases. Two loci reached genome-wide significance: UGT1A* and CHRDL1. A missense variant at UGT1A4 (rs6755571) was associated with a five-fold lower risk of neonatal jaundice (OR = 0.2) and was replicated in a meta-analysis of two Danish cohorts. Colocalization analysis suggested the association acts through regulation of UGT1A1 expression in the colon, but not the liver. A maternal GWAS identified three loci—UGT1A*, chromosome X, and ABO—with the ABO association explained by maternal-fetal ABO blood group incompatibility. A paternal GWAS identified only the UGT1A* locus. Comparison with adult bilirubin levels showed that the lead adult variant at UGT1A* was not associated with neonatal jaundice after conditioning on the missense variant, and SLCO1B1 variants showed little association. A polygenic score of adult bilirubin levels was associated with neonatal jaundice only when chromosome 2 was included. The authors conclude that genetic effects on bilirubin clearance are context-dependent, possibly with intestinal UGT1A1 as the primary determinant in neonates, and note limitations including the narrow Nordic ancestry of the cohort.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on January 26, 2016, announcing the issuance of a press release, data sheet, and supplemental materials regarding its financial results for the first fiscal quarter ended December 26, 2015. These materials are attached as Exhibits 99.1, 99.2, and 99.3. The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The article backtests six pivot point trading strategies on 1-minute futures data from 2010 onward for the S&P 500, Nasdaq, Russell 2000, and USD/CHF. Pivot points are calculated as the average of the previous day's high, low, and close, with support and resistance levels derived from this central point. Although trader Lewis Borsellino reportedly used pivot points daily in the 1980s and 1990s, he did not describe his specific method. The backtests found none of the strategies consistently tradeable, leading the authors to conclude that pivot points are largely hyped and add noise to the market, though a few day trading ideas may merit further research. Pros include being easy to use, objective, and versatile; cons include lagging price and low win rates.

This patent application describes a hard-sided, collapsible shelter or camper that combines rigid shelter protection with high portability. The shelter comprises a roof section, a floor section, and folding wall panels (e.g., bi-fold or multi-fold panels), which may include an insulated inner core and an outer skin of composite material such as fiberglass or carbon fiber. It transitions between an expanded configuration, in which the wall panels extend vertically to form a weather-tight, lockable enclosure suitable for sleeping or living, and a collapsed configuration, in which the panels fold flat and are enclosed within a low-profile, portable case formed by the roof and floor. When collapsed, the shelter can be mounted on a vehicle roof rack, placed in a pickup truck bed, carried on a trailer, or towed by vehicles including motorcycles and bicycles, or moved by one or more people, without requiring permanent vehicle modification. Collapsed height may be less than 50 inches (down to less than 10 inches), while expanded height ranges from 2 to 8 feet. The shelter may include a bed system that raises and lowers to allow standing height below, as well as a kitchenette, bathroom, seating fixtures, plumbing, lighting, electronics, solar panels, batteries, and heating/cooling equipment. Opening and closing can be performed manually or with mechanical assistance, and joints are sealed with weather stripping or gaskets. The shelter is lockable in both configurations and may also be configured as a stationary shelter.

In this lecture, the instructor recaps the number four-vector for dust and its covariant conservation law, then introduces the stress-energy tensor. For identical dust particles, the rest energy density is ρ₀ = mn₀; in a moving frame the energy density scales as γ²ρ₀, showing it is a component of a tensor rather than a scalar or four-vector component. The tensor is T^αβ = ρ₀u^αu^β, interpreted as the flux of momentum component α in the β direction: T^00 is energy density, T^0i energy flux, T^i0 momentum density, and T^ij momentum flux. Energy flux equals momentum density (apparent when c = 1), and the tensor is symmetric, motivated by a torque argument on a shrinking cube that would otherwise produce divergent angular acceleration. A perfect fluid—no energy flow in its rest frame and no viscosity—has T = diag(ρ, p, p, p), with dust as the zero-pressure case; a covariant form uses the projection tensor. Because energy density is not a scalar, relativistic gravity must use the full stress-energy tensor as its source, unlike the Newtonian Poisson equation; the Einstein equation will involve two derivatives of the metric. Conservation is expressed covariantly as ∂_αT^αβ = 0, with integral forms for energy and momentum. Examples include a point particle (Dirac delta function along its worldline) and electromagnetic fields (energy density, Poynting vector, anisotropic stresses, illustrated by parallel-plate capacitors). The lecture concludes by beginning a prelude to curvature: flat spacetime in curvilinear (polar) coordinates, where basis vectors are non-constant and non-normalized, transformation matrices have mixed dimensions, and the metric acquires a non-trivial functional form.

The second panel of Lawton High School's 22-foot Wolverine mural, funded by the class of 2014, was unveiled Thursday by art teacher Kenneth Hobbs. It depicts the school's front and south side and connects to the first mural, which shows the school's three historic buildings and a championship timeline.

A study challenges the assumption that racial, ethnic, and language minority children are overrepresented in U.S. special education—a belief underlying federal legislation requiring local educational agencies to report disproportionality and allocate 15% of Part B funds to early intervening services. Using nationally representative longitudinal data and adjusting for confounding factors such as family socioeconomic status, academic achievement, and behavioral functioning, the study found minority children are significantly less likely than otherwise similar White children to be identified as disabled. Black children were 58–77% less likely to be identified across disability categories; Hispanic children 29–73% less likely; language minorities 28–40% less likely for learning disabilities and speech or language impairments. The study concludes minority children are underrepresented in special education. The author questions policies aimed at reducing minority special education placements when minorities may actually be underserved.

RWE Supply & Trading may double or triple its LNG derivatives trades this year from 1.5 million tonnes in 2017 to manage price risk for physical cargoes, aided by Asia's potential shift from oil-linked prices. Physical LNG trading rose to 6 million tonnes last year from 4.5 million in 2016. Fragmented Asian demand is driving short-term trading; RWE's 7-10 JKM-indexed cargoes this year already match 2017's volume.
The speaker disagrees with Curtis, saying limiting opponents' puck time and keeping it out of their end is key. Brett's status is uncertain, and Mike and Joe Nieuwendyk are tough to stop.

Mental health services are available in more than 80% of Minnesota's public school districts, with most support provided by school staff and outside mental health practitioners. Nonprofit programs also serve students, offering peer support for addiction and culturally specific services for immigrant and refugee communities.

Know the Truth, a secular offshoot of Minnesota Adult and Teen Challenge, began in 2006 as a prevention program bringing young people who had completed addiction treatment into schools to share their experiences. It now provides peer recovery services in partnership with districts including Anoka-Hennepin and District 916. Peer support specialist Tiffany White, four years sober, works in three Twin Cities public schools, meeting students individually and in groups, and offers support outside school hours. Her contract at Hastings High School was eliminated due to federal funding cuts. She uses a harm reduction approach and spent a year building trust with students at Quora, an alternative learning center in Little Canada.

Restoration for All, a St. Paul nonprofit founded by Nigerian immigrant Tolulope Ola, supports the mental health of African immigrant and refugee youth, whose experiences school staff often misinterpret due to a lack of cultural knowledge. The organization holds workshops for school staff on trauma and cultural understanding. In 2023, it received a four-year, $400,000 Minnesota Department of Health grant to expand services including mental health screening groups, individual therapy, suicide monitoring, and African mind-body practices. Another MDH grant funds school-based work in the Twin Cities, St. Cloud, and Rochester focused on substance use disorder and peer support for youth.

South Korea's spy agency suspects two female North Korean agents assassinated Kim Jong Nam, the estranged half-brother of leader Kim Jong Un, who died Monday after falling ill at Kuala Lumpur airport. South Korean intelligence believes he was poisoned, and that Kim Jong Un had issued a "standing order" for the killing, with a failed attempt in 2012. U.S. sources also believe North Korean assassins murdered him. Malaysian police said the cause of death was unknown pending an autopsy, and CCTV showed a woman involved. TV Chosun reported he was poisoned with a needle by two women believed to be North Korean operatives, which Reuters could not confirm. North Korean embassy officials declined to speak to reporters.

A Salvadoran woman who lost her 19-year-old daughter and 15-year-old son to gang violence fled El Salvador with her common-law husband, hoping to reach Houston and her only surviving child. Captured by the Border Patrol an hour after crossing into Texas, she was deported back to El Salvador with about 100 other migrants under the Trump administration's zero-tolerance policy. Although President Trump has linked migrants to gangs like MS-13, only 0.09 percent of the 310,531 people detained in fiscal 2017 belonged to Central American gangs; most are fleeing violence. In 2000, 98 percent of those caught at the southwest border were Mexican, but by 2017 nearly 163,000 were from El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras. In El Salvador, MS-13 and Barrio 18 control neighborhoods, extort residents, kill those who refuse to pay, and force young women into sexual slavery. Police and soldiers, including clandestine "extermination groups," are blamed for an estimated 10 to 15 percent of the violence. With 60,000 gang members versus 50,000 police and soldiers, and a country too small to hide in, those threatened have few options. An estimated 90 percent of deportees try to migrate again within days. The deported woman, fearing for her life, returned to her gang-controlled town, where, she said, no one was waiting for her.

A Thames Centre councillor is urging the Thames Valley District School Board to adopt a defibrillator policy, after a West Nissouri student fundraised for an AED following a local child's death. The board declined to install the device and has not commented.

Senior guard Adrienne Motley passed Octavia Blue's 1,724 points to become No. 7 on Miami's all-time scoring list as the No. 16 Hurricanes defeated Clemson 81-57. Jessica Thomas also reached a milestone, notching her 1,200th career point and leading Miami with 18. Miami (19-6, 8-5 ACC) led for over 36 minutes, took a 48-30 halftime lead, and outscored Clemson 17-4 in the third quarter. The game was Miami's annual Play4Kay event honoring Kay Yow. The Hurricanes next play at No. 14 Duke on Sunday.

This is a forwarded October 12, 2000 email from Eric Bass containing the "Inside UT Football" newsletter by Dallas Morning News writer Chip Brown. The newsletter previews Texas's upcoming game at Colorado, noting the Buffaloes have won six straight against UT dating to 1989 and that Texas hasn't won in Boulder since 1941. Coach Mack Brown named Major Applewhite the sole starting quarterback for the Colorado game, ending the QB rotation with Chris Simms on a "need-to-win" basis, though the rotation could resume afterward. B.J. Johnson and Roy Williams were promoted to starting receiver spots, and running back Kenny Hayter is expected to get more carries after only two against Oklahoma. In a Q&A format, Chip Brown addresses fan questions about the OU loss, the lack of pass rush (with Shaun Rogers expected back), offensive leadership, play-calling creativity (offensive coordinator Greg Davis is re-evaluating his approach), Mack Brown's job security, Simms's struggles, and next season's expectations. Brown writes that a win would put Texas back in the driver's seat for the Big 12 South title, and that Mack Brown isn't going anywhere. The start time for the Missouri game has not been set.
Belcher v. Kitsap County: the Kitsap County Superior Court's judgment was affirmed on appeal.
Stocks rebounded Wednesday as banks and energy companies surged, with investors hoping Italy would avoid new elections. All major indexes gained, led by the Russell 2000's 1.5 percent rise.

Travis Phippen, a Valencia man wounded in the Las Vegas mass shooting that killed his father John Phippen, has filed a lawsuit against gunman Stephen Paddock's estate. Filed Friday in Clark County, Nevada, by attorney Rick Patterson of Owen, Patterson & Owen, the suit seeks control of Paddock's assets, bank accounts, safe deposit boxes, and real property. At least 59 were killed and 527 wounded when Paddock fired from Mandalay Bay's 32nd floor. Three other SCV victims remain hospitalized but are recovering.

Scale AI cofounder and Meta's chief AI officer Alexandr Wang, 28, advises 13-year-olds to spend their time "vibe-coding"—using AI tools to generate and refine software through natural language prompts. He argues that, like Bill Gates and Mark Zuckerberg with early personal computers, those who log around 10,000 hours experimenting with AI tools now will gain a career-defining advantage. He calls this a moment of "discontinuity," noting entry-level jobs are shrinking as companies prioritize automation. Wang became the youngest self-made billionaire at 25 in 2022 after launching Scale AI around age 19, and this June Zuckerberg appointed him Meta's first-ever chief AI officer, leading its new superintelligence team.

A petition opposing the proposed closure of Gresford Health Centre has gathered more than 600 signatures. Alyn Family Doctors plan to shut the Gresford branch and merge patients with its Llay and Rossett surgeries, saying they lack the manpower to run three sites, and have applied to Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board. Patients fear travel difficulties and pressure on appointments, with concerns also raised about proposed housing developments in Llay and Rossett. Three other Wrexham surgeries handed back their contracts in the past two years. BCUHB is inviting patient feedback.

When a penalty kick is awarded during normal play, it is a re-start, meaning the ball is live once kicked. Per Law 14, all players other than the kicker and goalkeeper must be at least 10 yards from the penalty mark, behind the mark, inside the field of play, and outside the Penalty Area. Defenders must take positions immediately to box out attackers seeking rebounds, holding their ground if they arrive first but not jostling if beaten to a spot. Players may only enter the Area or Arc after the kicker touches the ball and it moves forward. If the goalkeeper blocks but does not secure the ball, or a rebound occurs off the goal, defenders must reach the ball first and clear it, as illustrated by the 2023 Women's World Cup USA-Vietnam match. After the ball is secured or cleared, defenders should transition to attack. A defender entering the Area or Arc early results in a retaken kick if no goal is scored. A rare "tap" penalty kick involves the kicker tapping the ball forward for a teammate to shoot. Coaches should practice positioning, rebound clearance, and outlet passes. This article does not cover shoot-outs, which follow different rules with no follow-up allowed.

This patent application, a continuation claiming priority to a Japanese application, describes a gaming machine, control method, and program that synchronize the display timing of in-game events with the beat of background music (BGM). Prior art synchronized only audio reproduction with the beat, leaving event display timing unsynchronized and potentially causing a time lag and player discomfort. The disclosed gaming machine includes a display, speaker, storage device storing tempo data (beat information of the entire BGM) and BGM sound data, and a controller. The controller starts game display while outputting BGM, determines event display timing based on the tempo data, dynamically configures animation data so the event is displayed at that timing, and displays it. In embodiments, timing may be based on player operations or randomly determined event content; event sound data may be output at the determined timing; rhythm pattern data may define sequential display of multiple events; reel spin and stop in a slot game may serve as events; and illumination may be lit at the determined timing. The application details the machine's hardware (upper and lower displays, cabinet, control panel with player tracking, bill/ticket identification, printer, and operation units), its software and data structure (game and system applications, BGM-related data including tempo and rhythm pattern data), and flowcharts of methods synchronizing reel stops and bonus game events with BGM beats. The stated effect is that event display timing can be synchronized with the beat of the sound, providing a rhythmic and comfortable game progression.

Peter D. Baron's law office renewed a 2,510-square-foot Melville office lease. Jersey Mike's Subs, Hand and Stone Massage, and Fortunoff Bedding leased spaces at Plaza 200, Carle Place. The speaker, called to the chief executive office by his fellow citizens, expresses gratitude for their confidence and anxiety over the duties of the trust. Following his predecessors' example, he reviews the causes of the nation's happy condition: nearly forty years since the Revolution and twenty-eight under the Constitution, during which self-government has flourished—commerce regulated, new states admitted, territory enlarged by treaty, states protected and strengthened, and citizens' rights fully enjoyed, with no execution for treason. The government also proved equal to the trial of the late war, which became inevitable after injuries from parties to European conflicts. He credits the people and their faithful representatives for this success, warning that usurpation becomes easy when the people grow ignorant and corrupt, and urges promoting intelligence among them. Dangers from abroad should be anticipated by fortifying coasts and frontiers, keeping moderate but adequate Army and Navy forces, and organizing and training the militia, on which safety chiefly depends. He also favors internal improvements such as roads and canals with constitutional sanction, fostering domestic manufacturers to avoid wartime dependence on foreign supplies, cultivating friendly relations with the Indian tribes, and using abundant revenue and vacant lands to discharge the national debt at an early period. He pledges economy and fidelity in public disbursements, in cooperation with the Legislature as guardian of the public purse. Entering office in peacetime, he desires to preserve peace on just principles, notes the prevailing harmony of the Union, and commits to promoting its best interests. He praises the examples of his predecessors, especially his immediate predecessor, and closes with prayers for continued divine protection.

This qualitative study used an interpretive phenomenological approach to explore stakeholder opinions on the utility of metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) for infectious disease diagnostics (IDD) in clinical settings. Ten UK-based participants from diverse professions were interviewed between July and November 2021, and thematic analysis identified five themes: diagnostic choice, infrastructure, open data sharing, COVID-19, and communication.

Participants viewed mNGS as a valuable addition to the diagnostic toolkit rather than a replacement for existing methods. Cost was a major barrier, with sequencing often dependent on research funding and marked disparities between larger city hospitals and smaller district hospitals. Speed of results was also critical, as clinically actionable timeframes were needed. Infrastructure challenges included centralised laboratory models causing delays, limited bioinformatics training for staff, difficulties accrediting research-use-only reagents, and inadequate data storage systems. Open data sharing raised tensions between patient privacy and the benefits of public health surveillance. COVID-19 served as proof of concept for sequencing's public health value and increased manufacturing capacity for sequencing platforms and reagents. Communication gaps within hospitals, between hospitals, and with academia and the commercial sector were seen as hindering implementation.

The study concluded that cost, speed, and infrastructure must be considered when developing new diagnostics, and that COVID-19 demonstrated metagenomics' utility, supporting its integration into routine clinical microbiology. Limitations included no participant representation from England's Southwest and Northeast regions.

Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson, and Omar Yaghi won the 2025 Nobel Prize in chemistry for developing metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), molecular structures with gaps that can store gases and other chemicals in vast quantities. Applications include harvesting drinkable water from air, capturing carbon dioxide from industrial plants, and extracting "forever chemicals." In the late 1980s, Robson combined copper ions with organic compounds to create a hole-filled crystalline structure. Kitagawa later created MOFs that absorb gases like methane, nitrogen, and oxygen. In 1999, Yaghi built a MOF whose few grams contained as much surface area as a soccer field. The three share the 11 million Swedish kronor prize.

In this MIT lecture, Professor Andrew Lo first discusses a classroom auction in which a wrapped iPod sold for $45 (roughly a 70% discount from retail) and his hedge fund book sold for $60, illustrating how lack of information affects valuation. He then addresses the weekend federal takeover of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, government-sponsored entities created to buy mortgages and expand credit in housing, student loan, and auto loan markets. Having grown too large with insufficient oversight, and pressured by the housing downturn, they could not make good on their obligations, prompting the Treasury to guarantee their debt. Lo argues the government had little choice but to act, noting concerns about inflation from printing money, the taxpayer burden across generations, and shareholders losing nearly all value as the stock fell dramatically.

The lecture then introduces present value relations. An asset is defined as a sequence of current and future cashflows, valued by an operator V_t. Cashflows at different dates are treated like different currencies, requiring exchange rates (discount factors) obtained from markets to convert them into today's dollars, yielding net present value. Under assumptions of certain cashflows, known market exchange rates, and no frictions, any cashflow can be valued using the interest rate r, where $1 today grows to (1+r)^T. Future lectures will cover annuities and perpetuities, and later relax these assumptions.

Top stories include Broadcom's acquisition of chip developer SiByte for up to $2 billion in stock, Alta Partners raising $275–325 million for its third fund, online retailer Furniture.com shutting down and laying off 76 of 88 workers due to difficulty raising capital, and eStellarNet raising $30 million in first-round funding.
