NHS workers have recreated a 1927 photograph found in a broom cupboard to mark the health service's 70th anniversary. The original image of a matron, her assistant and nurses was taken at Sandwell Hospital, then known as Hallam Hospital, in West Bromwich. Fourteen staff from the Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust recreated it in the same spot nearly 90 years later. The images will be shown at a tea party.

At the busy Honduran port of Puerto Cortés, Sergio Romero finds the Avontuur, a 97-year-old, two-masted schooner that sailed from Europe through the Caribbean using wind rather than bunker fuel, its small crew collecting and delivering small cargo along the way.

This CUPA-HR report examines Title IX staffing trends in higher education from academic years 2019-20 to 2023-24. Title IX staff ensure institutional compliance with federal nondiscrimination regulations, which were updated twice since 2020 under the Trump and Biden administrations, with the incoming Trump administration expected to reinstate the 2020 regulations.

Most Title IX staff are located in Human Resources (29%) or Student Affairs (28%), followed by Compliance (11%) and Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (11%). The report analyzes three positions: heads of institutional Title IX compliance, deputy heads, and Title IX investigators.

The percentage of institutions with at least one dedicated full-time Title IX position rose from one-third in 2019-20 to 43% in 2023-24, though 56% still lack such positions, instead integrating Title IX duties into broader roles. Heads of compliance are the most common position (31% of institutions), followed by investigators (16%) and deputy heads (12%). Total Title IX staff grew 38% over five years, from 542 to 746, with investigators increasing 85% and deputy heads 58%, while heads grew only 7%.

Dedicated positions are most prevalent at doctoral institutions (64%), compared to baccalaureate (45%), master's (39%), and associate's colleges (19%). Doctoral institutions are also most likely to have multiple Title IX staff (36%).

Women hold 77% of Title IX positions, with Black women comprising 13%—more than double their representation among professional staff overall. Median salaries are $96,714 for heads, $84,931 for deputy heads, and $75,000 for investigators, all exceeding the overall professional median of $66,000. Unlike broader higher education trends, women and people of color in Title IX roles are paid equitably relative to White men, with Black women earning $1.16 per $1.00 paid to White men.

The report recommends that institutions reassess Title IX officers' responsibilities, increase staffing where needed, and prepare for compliance with either the 2020 or 2024 regulations amid the changing legal landscape.

Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway sold 10.6 million GE shares in the second quarter, a stake worth an estimated $315 million as of June 30. Berkshire received the shares in 2013 after lending GE roughly $3 billion in October 2008 during the financial crisis; the investment, including hundreds of millions in dividends, generated a profit of more than $1 billion. The sale came as GE replaced CEO Jeff Immelt with John Flannery amid pressure from activist investor Trian Fund Management; GE shares have dropped nearly 20% this year. Berkshire also sold most of its long-held Wal-Mart stake late last year. In other 13F filings, Appaloosa Management sold its SPDR S&P 500 ETF stake, George Soros bought a new stake in PowerShares QQQ Trust worth over $1 billion, and Viking Global Investors purchased 12.3 million Wells Fargo shares worth about $680 million.

Gary Allen Darnell, 45, of Cottage Hills, a registered sexual predator from a 2003 or 2004 child assault conviction, was arrested Thursday in Grafton for allegedly offering children fishing poles. Charged with loitering within 500 feet of a park, a Class 4 Felony, he faces prosecutors seeking the maximum sentence.

The speaker says effort was present but the team didn't work as a unit, expressing unhappiness with the last game and stressing action over talk. Injuries won't stop them; others stepped up amid key injuries.

This study explores kindergarten teachers' views on the role of visual arts in early childhood education and the challenges of integrating them into the pre-school curriculum. The literature review indicates that visual arts support children's expression, communication, creativity, socialization, and emotional development, though teachers often lack training, time, and institutional support, and sometimes treat visual arts as a secondary subject.

The research surveyed 65 kindergarten teachers from public and private kindergartens in the Municipality of Piraeus, Greece, using an electronic questionnaire containing 16 closed-ended (5-point Likert scale) and 5 open-ended questions, analyzed with SPSS and thematic analysis.

Most participants were women (81.5%), aged 33–42 (38.5%), held four-year degrees (70.8%), had 1–5 years of experience (53.8%), and had no visual arts training (89.2%). Teachers overwhelmingly viewed visual arts as crucial in early childhood, contributing to creativity (73.8% strongly agreed), emotional expression, social skills, and intellectual development. Most reported that children respond well to art activities and show high interest. The preferred teaching method was the free approach (33.1%), followed by experimentation with various materials and tools (30.7%). The main challenge was managing children (86.1%), with proposed solutions including individual guidance, patience, rewards, games, and varied materials.

The study concluded that demographic factors do not significantly influence teachers' perceptions of visual arts' usefulness, and recommended targeted professional development and improved resources. Limitations include the electronic administration of the questionnaire and the sample being restricted to kindergartens in Piraeus.

His Majesty has made agreements with commanders of foreign war vessels that were never sanctioned by their governments, causing embarrassment and a strong desire for formal recognition of his Kingdom as a sovereign, independent state. Though tacit acknowledgment has occurred through consuls, commercial agents, and naval commanders, he requests the United States consider the changes in his dominions: twenty-three years ago the nation had no written language, Christianity, fixed government, property rights, or courts; now the language is systematized, schools and a library exist, a limited representative monarchy has been organized, laws enacted, and jury trials established, with foreigners showing confidence in the courts. Since his government provides all that sovereign states do, he seeks formal admission into the community of sovereign nations, believing this would also serve commercial nations, as his islands are the center of the whale fishery and a principal Pacific stop for repairs and supplies.

A Spring ISD teacher at Dueitt Middle School is on administrative leave and under investigation for allegedly calling African American students "cotton pickers." Other students confirmed hearing the slur, and the teacher was replaced with a substitute. Parent Roshonda Davis reported the incident and expressed satisfaction with the district's response.

The passage describes SOS defensive strategies for disrupting side screen/roll plays, divided into scenarios above and below the free throw line. Below the free throw line, when O5 sets a side screen for O3, X5 immediately traps O3 with X3 before the screen is set, followed by specific rotations for pass outs, skip passes, and passes to the low post. Above the free throw line, an aggressive contact switch is executed: X4 bumps the screener and hedges into the ballhandler's path while X3 positions inside the screener, followed by snuggle pass denial and smother phases to disrupt passing vision. The All Out SOS Disruption involves the defense trapping the point guard before any screen or pass occurs, forcing the offense into freelance mode. A secondary trap covers passes to O5 on the base roll. All rotations must occur as the ball leaves the passer's hands, and basic SOS defensive principles apply once matchups are established.

The German Ambassador, recently returned from Berlin, reported that Germany was willing to confidentially state peace terms: giving up Belgium while retaining certain Meuse travel rights; keeping Holland, Denmark, and Belgium as neutral buffer states for England; leaving the French coast entirely to France; restoring Russian territory; treating Serbia and Roumania properly; and indemnifying Belgium. He said Germany learned from secret British sources that England hesitated to state her terms because her maximum terms agreed with allies were infeasible while her minimum terms would cause disagreement with allies, and that American pressure might lead England to disclose them. Separately, the Greek Chargé conveyed Greece's reply to the US peace proposal of January 8: Greece appreciated the initiative, described its suffering as a neutral under blockade, occupation, and disarmament, but could not join because it was excluded from communication with one belligerent, while expressing support and readiness to join future peace efforts.

On November 18, 2022, Amazon.com, Inc. entered into a 364-day revolving credit agreement with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., as administrative agent, and other lenders. The unsecured revolving credit facility provides borrowing capacity of up to $10.0 billion and may be extended for an additional 364 days. The initial interest rate is the Secured Overnight Financing Rate plus 0.45%, with a 0.05% commitment fee on the undrawn portion. Borrowings will be used for general corporate purposes, including backstopping notes issued under the Company's commercial paper program. The agreement contains customary representations, warranties, covenants, and events of default, but no financial covenants. The agreement is filed as Exhibit 10.1, and the report was signed by Vice President and Treasurer Antonio Masone.

Whitman Howard raised its price target on Produce Investments Ltd (LON:PIL) from GBX 210 to GBX 240 with a buy rating; Shore Capital and Numis Securities restated buy ratings, Numis setting a GBX 286 target. Task-Force-Southwest Marines practiced the Instant-Eye drone at Camp Lejeune and will deploy to Afghanistan this spring. The 2nd Law Enforcement Battalion completed grenade training. The Marine Corps awarded the Purple Heart to 91-year-old Lee Anderson for Iwa Jima injuries.

Three female University of Dayton students reported a naked man entering their bedrooms early Wednesday morning. The suspect, a white male in his mid-20s, entered through windows or an unsecured door; one student said he tried to restrain her. University police are investigating.

The speaker expresses confidence in the nation's prosperity and in the current session's work. He notes agricultural abundance, progress in agriculture, manufactures, commerce, and navigation, and a revival of public and private confidence attributed to the Constitution and laws. Rapid subscriptions to the Bank of the United States, completed in a single day, are cited as evidence of confidence in the government and of community resources. Regarding the Western Frontiers, treaties were provisionally concluded with friendly tribes, but hostile tribes required offensive operations, conducted humanely and carried out by the Kentucky militia, which receives commendation. Peace overtures continue, and some Indians have placed themselves under United States protection. He recommends impartial justice, regulated land alienation, equitable commerce, civilization efforts, and penalties for rights violations toward Indians. The act laying duties on distilled spirits has been implemented, though compensation rates may require revision; some discontent arose from the tax's novelty and misconceptions but yields to explanation, and variations consistent with the law's design may be made. A ten-mile-square district on both sides of the Potomac, including Alexandria and Georgetown, has been fixed as the permanent seat of government, with a city laid out and funds expected for public buildings. Loan subscriptions substantially fulfilled the debt act's aims, revenues promise adequacy without new burdens, and attention is urged for the militia, magazines and fortifications, post-office and post-roads, a mint, uniform weights and measures, and sale of vacant lands pledged for debt reimbursement.

The coach describes Corey Perry as a young but experienced player who succeeded with the London Knights and benefited from playing two playoff rounds the previous year, calling him an effective, "greasy" player with strong hands. He says a recent practice was not physical, consisting of regroups, shooting drills, and two-on-ones, and explains the team keeps extra players ("black aces") with the main group for team building and education rather than separating them. A player with a hand injury is doubtful to return pending doctor clearance and confirmation he is in game shape. The coach stresses the importance of a good start, notes the high-paced, physical start of the second game, and expects similar intensity tomorrow. He emphasizes staying on an even keel through success and adversity, preparing for the next game immediately after the previous one, and blocking out distractions such as Ottawa's home crowd. He credits the team's commitment, strong leadership, and willingness to sacrifice, noting veterans like Teemu Selanne are in their first Stanley Cup opportunity, and says the team must work hard, stay committed, and play its system.

Hampton and Newport News Police apprehended a 15-year-old possibly involved in a January 31 Tinee Giant robbery. A clerk reported an armed, masked man robbed the store and fled in a Ford SUV. A witness followed the SUV, seeing the suspect toss something and fire shots. Police found the teen with a handgun; he faces firearm and tobacco charges but no robbery charges.

A Sarasota couple, Michael Bennett, 39, and Trisha Steffes, 36, were arrested after accepting a package containing carfentanil, a synthetic opioid the DEA says is 10,000 times more potent than morphine. A search of their home found over 7 grams of fentanyl and other drugs. Both face drug charges; Bennett was released on $15,500 bond and Steffes on $17,000 bond.

This patent application, a continuation of multiple prior U.S. applications tracing priority to a 2017 Korean application, relates to a display device (such as an LCD or OLED display) with improved crack detection. Cracks caused by impacts in a display panel may grow over time, disconnect signal lines, increase resistance, allow moisture penetration, and cause malfunctions. Embodiments aim to protect defect-detecting circuits and electrical elements from static electricity and to optimize defect detection accuracy during testing.

A display device comprises a substrate with a display area containing pixels, a pad area with input pads, and a circuit area between them containing a crack sensing circuit. A crack sensing line extends around the display area, with a first end connected to an input pad and a second end connected to a static electricity discharge element (e.g., a capacitor, transistor, or diode), which may be positioned at the center area of the circuit area where switching elements are absent. Switching elements connect test data lines to data lines, and matching resistors with resistance approximately equal (e.g., about 1.5 times) to the crack sensing lines' wire resistance balance test voltages.

During testing, a test voltage is applied; if cracks damage the sensing lines, increased resistance causes pixels to display white lines, revealing defects. Without the static electricity discharge elements, static electricity could accumulate and cause erroneous defect detection (weak dark lines). Additional embodiments cover bending crack sensing lines within the bending area, alternative capacitor connections via connection wires, and detailed layer structures including insulating layers, conductive layers, pixel electrodes, emission layers, common electrodes, encapsulating portions, and touch sensors.

Alexander Zverev overcame Dusan Lajovic 2-6 7-5 4-6 6-1 6-2 in three hours, 24 minutes at the French Open to reach the third round, though he has yet to reach a grand slam quarterfinal or beat a top-50 player at a major. Lajovic appeared to struggle with cramp in the fifth set. Grigor Dimitrov and Kei Nishikori also overturned 2-1 set deficits, beating Jared Donaldson and Benoit Paire respectively; Donaldson used underhand serves while appearing to suffer a leg cramp. Dominic Thiem led Stefanos Tsitsipas 6-2 2-6 6-4 when darkness halted play. World No. 1 Simona Halep recovered from a slow start to beat Alison Riske 2-6 6-1 6-1. Novak Djokovic defeated Spanish qualifier Jaume Munar 7-6 (7-1) 6-4 6-4, continuing his comeback after elbow surgery. Marco Trungelliti lost to Marco Cecchinato, while Petra Kvitova and Elina Svitolina advanced in straight sets.

To facilitate the transition, a Blackout Period, expected to run from January 2, 2020 to the week of January 12, 2020, will restrict participants from making exchanges or asset allocation changes, taking loans, or requesting withdrawals or distributions. The Foreign Relations series editors have access to Department of State records, including central files, lot files, Executive Secretariat files, and overseas post files. State Department files from 1981–1989 will eventually be transferred to the National Archives and made available after declassification. Research also draws on restricted documents at the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library and other agencies; all printed material is declassified, though some is extracted from still-classified documents. Some records were scanned under the Remote Archive Capture (RAC) project, which sometimes left uncertainty about attachments, noted as "Not found attached." Documents are presented chronologically by Washington, DC time, reproduced as exactly as possible, with corrections in brackets, footnotes giving sources and classification, and omissions noted.

This patent application, a divisional of U.S. application Ser. No. 15/987,220 titled "System and Method for Indicating Wireless Channel Status," relates to digital communications, specifically indicating wireless channel status. Fifth generation (5G) New Radio systems may operate at high frequencies (6 GHz and above, such as mmWave) for greater bandwidth, but face significant pathloss, which beamforming helps overcome. When a user equipment (UE) detects beam failure with an access node, beam failure recovery is needed, and channel status information must be shared between devices.

Example embodiments provide methods in which, after beam failure recovery, a UE receives a frame on a channel associated with a beam identified during the recovery procedure, determines an assumed quasi-co-located (QCL) relationship between the channel and the beam, and decodes the frame using a reference signal and the spatial domain receive filter used for that beam. After receiving an updated QCL relationship, the UE decodes subsequent frames accordingly. Embodiments address decoding on PDCCH and PDSCH, transmission configuration indication (TCI) states and TCI fields in downlink control information, and scenarios where the QCL configuration of a new beam is either used or not used until TCI state updates are received.

These techniques enable a UE, after beam failure recovery, to determine which reference signal to use with data or control channels and reduce signaling overhead associated with updating channel status information, thereby improving communications system performance.

This commentary presents five strategies for parents and caregivers to move beyond brief answers like "fine" and encourage real conversations with children. The author, dean of the College of Education and Human Development at the University of North Dakota, suggests: asking specific, open-ended questions instead of rote ones; engaging with children's questions rather than dismissing them; admitting when you don't know an answer and demonstrating how to find information through tools like glossaries or internet searches; modeling active listening by repeating and clarifying what children say; and avoiding multitasking by putting away phones, making eye contact, and asking follow-up questions. The author argues that nurturing children's natural curiosity, while respecting their fears and limitations, builds their confidence to ask and answer questions.

This cross-sectional study investigated the relationship between self-esteem and physical activity among 10th and 11th grade students at Capa Science High School in Istanbul, Türkiye. Data were collected from 225 of 278 students (80.93%) using a questionnaire comprising sociodemographic questions, the International Physical Activity Questionnaire Short Form (IPAQ-SF), and the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (ROSE), along with self-reported height and weight for BMI calculation.

Most participants were male (71.60%). Males had higher ROSE scores than females (p=0.002) and higher MET scores (p=0.031). Students who reported exercising regularly had higher ROSE scores than those who did not (p=0.034). Positive correlations were found between ROSE and MET scores (p=0.045, r=0.140) and between ROSE scores and height (p=0.029, r=0.146). Higher self-reported school success was associated with higher self-esteem (p=0.001). No differences in ROSE scores were found across BMI groups. According to IPAQ-SF, 23% of participants were inactive, 61.70% minimally active, and 15.30% HEPA active; MET scores were higher among students living in dormitories (p=0.01).

The authors conclude that higher physical activity is correlated with higher self-esteem, and that self-esteem is also associated with sex, regular exercise, school success, and height. Noted limitations include the highly selective study population in Istanbul, low female participation, and reliance on self-reported height, weight, and school success. The authors state that underlying mechanisms and potential causal relationships between physical activity and self-esteem require further investigation.

Critics say colleges lack viewpoint diversity and faculty have skewed left for decades, but the term is defined differently across groups, and the Trump administration's definition remains unclear. The administration offered federal grant advantages to nine universities agreeing to ban race- and sex-based hiring and admissions, freeze tuition, cap international enrollment at 15 percent, require standardized tests, and maintain a "vibrant marketplace of ideas." Education Secretary Linda McMahon said patriotism may factor into discretionary grant decisions. Students are willing to pay over $2,000 extra for colleges with fewer opposing political views, yet funding tied to a political agenda risks colleges teaching the White House's priorities rather than fostering a marketplace of ideas.

The ADS868xW features a user-programmable input alarm with adjustable thresholds and hysteresis, illustrated using an NTC thermistor for temperature sensing; hysteresis prevents false alarm triggering caused by noise or interference. The device uses two separate power supplies—AVDD for internal circuits and DVDD for the digital interface—which can be independently set within the permissible range. Decoupling capacitors (10µF and 1µF on AVDD, 10µF near DVDD) improve power-supply rejection ratio (PSRR). Two programmable low-power modes reduce consumption at lower throughput rates: NAP mode, entered by setting the NAP_EN bit and holding CONVST/CS high, and power-down (PD) mode, entered by setting the PWRDN bit, which powers down analog blocks while keeping the interface active and retaining register contents. PCB layout guidelines recommend partitioning analog and digital sections, using specified ceramic capacitors for AVDD, DVDD, REFCAP, and REFIO decoupling, and avoiding vias between pins and capacitors. Revision A (May 2025) changed the document status of ADS8685W and ADS8689W from Advance Information to Production Data.

Canadian researchers analyzed blood samples from more than 2,800 people in Toronto and found celiac disease occurs in about one per cent of the population, consistent with findings from other countries. However, roughly 90 per cent of cases go undiagnosed. Celiac disease is a genetic autoimmune condition in which gluten triggers an immune reaction that damages the small intestine, causing symptoms such as abdominal pain, diarrhea, anemia and weight loss. Diagnosis is difficult because symptoms overlap with other conditions; blood antibody tests and a duodenal biopsy are used, and testing should occur while consuming gluten to avoid false negatives. Researchers say the findings are important for health care planning, though studies in other provinces are needed.

The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate by a quarter-point to between 1% and 1.25% and said it would begin gradually reducing its $4.5 trillion balance sheet this year, though it offered few details on timing or pace. U.S. stocks reacted mildly: the S&P 500 fell 0.4%, the Dow hit an intraday record before trading slightly lower, and the Nasdaq dropped 0.9%. Disappointing May inflation and retail sales data, along with a 3.7% drop in oil futures to $44.73 a barrel, weighed on markets. Treasury yields and the dollar declined, while gold rose 0.6%. Fed Chairwoman Janet Yellen said she still expects inflation to reach the 2% target next year. Among individual stocks, H&R Block and Alexion Pharmaceuticals rallied, while oil-related shares fell. Stock futures shrugged off a shooting at a congressional baseball practice that injured House Majority Whip Steve Scalise.

Plaintiffs, alien enemies during World War I, sued in 1931 to recover property seized by the Alien Property Custodian under the Trading with the Enemy Act. The District Court dismissed the bill, holding recovery barred by Public Resolution No. 53 (1934), which postponed deliveries of money or property under that Act and the Settlement of War Claims Act while Germany remained in arrears on certain obligations. Relying on Cummings v. Deutsche Bank, in which the Supreme Court held that the grant to alien enemies of a right to recover seized property was a matter of grace subject to congressional withdrawal, the court found appellants' contention that their claim involved illegally seized property indistinguishable from a lawless withholding. Affirmed.

This patent application, claiming priority to U.S. Provisional Application No. 63/055,096 (filed Jul. 22, 2020), describes devices and methods for optimizing basal insulin delivery parameters using records from automated insulin delivery (AID) systems. The background notes that manually determining optimal clinical parameters is difficult and that users' open-loop parameters may become outdated as they rely on AID systems.

The disclosed device includes a processor, memory, wireless communication device, and an artificial pancreas application operable to determine the total insulin delivered over a predetermined time period (the sum of basal and bolus dosages), calculate the proportion delivered as basal insulin, and determine whether that proportion exceeds a threshold. If the threshold is exceeded, an average basal dosage approximately equal to the threshold is determined, and an instruction is generated to deliver a modified basal dosage via a pump mechanism of a wearable drug delivery device. A corresponding non-transitory computer readable medium is also disclosed.

Examples illustrate the process: with 29.85 U of basal insulin and 12 U of bolus insulin delivered, the basal proportion is 71.3%, exceeding a 0.700 threshold, yielding a modified basal dosage of 1.22 U/hr via the equation (0.7*(12+29.85))/24. Thresholds may vary with user activity levels (e.g., approximately 60% for intense activity, 75% for less intense activity), and basal dosages delivered within a post-bolus period may be omitted from calculations. Time-of-day segmentation and clustering algorithms (e.g., K-means) can generate time-dependent basal profiles on an hourly basis. Safety features reduce the maximum recommended basal proportion based on the user's percentage of time in the hypoglycemic range (e.g., reduction = 2 × percentage of time in hypoglycemic range).

The drug delivery system comprises a wearable drug delivery device (insulin pump), a continuous blood glucose sensor, a personal diabetes management device (PDM), and optionally a smart device and cloud-based services, communicating via wireless links such as Bluetooth or Wi-Fi. The artificial pancreas application may execute on any of these devices, and implementations may be in hardware, software, or combinations thereof, including open-loop modalities such as smart pens or syringes.

This Texas Instruments document excerpt describes boot configuration terminal functions for device pins multiplexed between ARM Cortex-A8 boot mode and GPMC peripheral functions. At reset, BTMODE[10] selects GPMC pin muxing options, BTMODE[9:8] determine Ethernet PHY Mode selection, and BTMODE[4:0] determine the ARM boot configuration. After reset, these pins function as GPMC multiplexed data/address pins. The passage defines internal pull states (IPD, IPU, DIS) and signal type abbreviations including Input, Output, High impedance, Supply voltage, Ground, Analog, Multi Muxed, and De-selected Input State.

At OpenAI's Developer Day, CEO Sam Altman unveiled a new way to embed third-party apps directly into ChatGPT, demonstrating apps from Spotify, Canva, and Zillow running inside the chat window. A preview version of a new Apps SDK is available to some developers, though app distribution is currently limited to a handful of major partners. OpenAI plans to introduce monetization methods, including an agentic commerce protocol with instant checkout. The company previously launched the GPT Store in January 2024, when developers had created over 3 million custom GPTs. Nick Turley, OpenAI's head of product for ChatGPT, said the company meant to build a "super assistant" rather than a chatbot. OpenAI also announced AgentKit for building AI agents, made its Codex coding model generally available, and announced plans to acquire 6 gigawatts' worth of AMD chips, potentially taking a 10-percent stake in the chipmaker. The company faces competition from Google, Anthropic, and Amazon, as well as pressure from open source models from Meta and DeepSeek.

Growing technologies such as 5G, IoT devices and autonomous vehicles are driving demand for edge computing, which the telco industry is positioned to define. Schneider Electric's prefabricated Edge Module is a turnkey, self-contained solution with pre-integrated power, cooling, software and IT components for flexible, scalable and autonomous edge deployments. Suited to the cell tower edge, it offers single or three-phase power, N+1 cooling, a 208-volt single-phase design with power up to 48 KW, and configurable rack options. Using the EcoStruxure platform, it can be metered, remotely monitored and controlled for autonomous operation, with security features including key locks, cameras and a card key reader.

Wall Street's three major indexes posted their biggest weekly losses in two years on Friday as worries about a tightening job market, rising inflation, and surging bond yields drove investors out of equities. The Dow fell 665.75 points, or 2.54 percent, its biggest daily point drop since December 2008. A January jobs report showing the largest wage gain in more than 8-1/2 years fueled expectations of more aggressive Federal Reserve rate hikes, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield to 2.8450 percent. All 11 S&P 500 sectors closed lower, with technology weighing heaviest, and the CBOE Volatility Index hit its highest level since November 2016.

This thesis analyzes Web services in event management and presents a mobile application concept allowing attendees to check and book nearby services via sensors and view events through drone cameras. It reviews the development of e-business since 1995, distinguishing e-commerce from the broader e-business and digital business, and notes drawbacks such as market consolidation, income disparity, and security risks, which are addressed through firewalls, antivirus programs, encryption, and digital certificates. Key enabling technologies include cloud computing, Web 2.0, the Internet of Things, and mobile technology. Using a five-part evaluation model, the authors analyzed 200 event management websites (17 Croatian, 183 foreign) against 103 Boolean-graded attributes, with data collected from August 1 to September 15, 2017. Results showed Facebook (90%) and LinkedIn (78%) were the most linked social media, all foreign sites had blogs and photos, and customer support was mainly provided via e-mail (100%) and phone (99%). The conclusion states that Croatian organizations lag behind, with the highest-ranked Croatian site at 40th place and the lowest at 200th, and should improve user experience, social media presence, and mobile applications. The study's limitation is its country-restricted sample; future research should adopt a customer perspective.

Tail risk, or "fat tails," refers to an increased probability of rare, extreme market events compared to what a normal distribution suggests, a concept popularized by Nassim Nicholas Taleb. Left tail risk involves severe losses, while negatively skewed strategies can produce many small gains but occasional devastating losses. The article gives three reasons to hedge tail risk: limiting losses, surviving (especially when using leverage), and avoiding behavioral mistakes such as selling during market meltdowns.

Six hedging alternatives are presented: buying out-of-the-money put options, diversifying into foreign assets, holding cash, investing in Cambria's TAIL ETF, adopting Ray Dalio's All Weather Portfolio, and using trend-following strategies. Meb Faber's research shows that a strategy of 10% in puts and 90% in ten-year bonds performed best during bear markets, but continuous hedging significantly lowers overall returns, which most investors would likely reject, though reduced drawdowns may help investors avoid panic selling.

Cambria's TAIL ETF, which holds out-of-the-money puts and US Treasuries, has had a negative CAGR of -6.92% since its April 2017 inception but performed as intended during the fourth quarter of 2018, the March 2020 pandemic selloff, and the 2022 downturn. Backtests allocating 10% or 25% to TAIL reduced drawdowns at the cost of lower returns. The authors describe their own 2019 attempt at hedging with puts on SPY, which they abandoned in October 2019 because the ongoing cost was too painful to bear, months before the Covid-19 crash would have made the puts profitable. The article concludes that younger investors may simply buy and hold, while those nearing retirement might consider tail risk strategies, with the trade-offs judged individually.

Jordan L. Couch, a partner at Palace Law in University Place, Washington, writes that artificial intelligence has advanced rapidly and is transforming industries, including the legal profession. AI, the simulation of human intelligence in machines, has existed for a long time, but current discussion centers on generative AI, which creates new content such as documents and legal arguments, and agentic AI, which focuses on decision-making and analysis. AI is powerful but not a panacea, so lawyers should consider whether it is the best tool for a given task. Recommended uses include document review, legal research, and client communication. Tools mentioned include Vincent AI for research, Copilot for drafting and workflows, ChatGPT for general writing tasks, built-in AI features in legal software, and custom tools such as Palace Law's chatbot for injured workers. A second part will address integrating AI into practice and future expectations.

Real Madrid will face Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League last 16 as they bid for a third consecutive European title. Other ties include Barcelona-Chelsea, Manchester City-Basel, Bayern Munich-Besiktas, Juventus-Tottenham, Manchester United-Sevilla, Liverpool-Porto, and Shakhtar Donetsk-Roma.

Minnesota Wild star Kirill Kaprizov signed an NHL-record eight-year, $136 million contract extension through the 2033-34 season, the richest deal in league history in both total value and average annual value ($17 million). The contract includes large signing bonuses over its first four years and was reached after Kaprizov turned down an offer of $16 million annually. He will play this season on the final year of his five-year, $45 million deal signed in 2021. The 28-year-old had 25 goals and 31 assists in 41 games last season despite missing 40 games due to a lower-body injury requiring surgery. He ranks fourth in Wild history with 185 goals and fifth with 386 points, and holds franchise single-season records in points, goals, and power play goals. The eight-year term will be among the NHL's last, as the new CBA limits extensions to seven years.

Photographer Mark Bickerdike has completed a multi-year project documenting Ricky's School of Rock in Linthwaite, capturing students in the school's 10-week RockJam courses across more than 50 gigs. The courses end with performances for friends and family. Founder and guitar tutor Ricky Comiskey said pupils gain confidence on stage, with many forming bands, including Mark's son Tom, who plays in Fading Sunlight. The school also offers adult programs, and Mark's photos are available to parents after each gig.

This qualitative study examined the anticipated challenges and training needs of pre-service physical education (PE) teachers regarding student motivation. Four focus groups were conducted with 18 pre-service PE teachers (M age = 25; SD = 3.61) from francophone Quebec universities, with data analyzed according to Boutin's (2007) four steps. Participants identified two overall anticipated challenges: classroom management and students' lack of motivation. Regarding support for student motivation specifically, five challenges emerged: student heterogeneity, proposing learning activities that sustain motivation, student engagement, managing disengaged students, and gender differences (particularly difficulty motivating girls). Participants expressed three needs for their teacher education programs: additional support in planning motivational strategies, concrete guidance on how to implement these strategies, and more opportunities for hands-on practice. The authors conclude that current Quebec teacher education programs do not fully meet pre-service teachers' needs concerning student motivation, and recommend integrating motivational content across courses and providing more practice opportunities, in line with the new professional competency "support students' love for learning."

In this lecture, the speaker develops the operator-field mapping in the AdS/CFT correspondence, showing that the scaling dimension of a boundary operator is directly related to the mass of the dual bulk field—the "mass-dimension relation."

Working in semiclassical gravity, the bulk action consists of Einstein gravity plus matter fields, all multiplied by 2κ² (related to the Newton constant, small at large N). After canonically normalizing fields, nonlinear terms are suppressed by powers of κ, so small fluctuations around AdS are governed, to leading order, by the quadratic (free) action.

For a massive scalar field, Fourier transformation along boundary directions reduces the equation of motion to an ordinary differential equation in z. Near the boundary (z→0), solutions behave as z^(d−Δ) and z^Δ, where Δ = d/2 + ν and ν² = d²/4 + m²R². The exponents are real provided the BF bound on m² is satisfied; violating it produces exponentially growing modes and instability. Unlike Minkowski space, AdS curvature forbids constant modes, so mildly negative mass squared is allowed.

Using the Klein-Gordon inner product, normalizability is analyzed: for ν ≥ 1 only the z^Δ mode is normalizable; for 0 < ν < 1 both modes are mathematically normalizable, and one chooses standard quantization (A = 0) or alternative quantization (B = 0), with boundary conditions ensuring energy conservation. Normalizable modes belong to the Hilbert space and correspond to states of the boundary theory; non-normalizable modes deform the theory, with the coefficient A(x) acting as the source, via φ(x) = lim(z→0) z^(Δ−d)Φ(z,x).

This identifies Δ as the scaling dimension of the dual operator: m=0 gives Δ=d (marginal), m²<0 gives Δ<d (relevant), and m²>0 gives Δ>d (irrelevant), consistent with RG behavior since the UV corresponds to z→0. A Maxwell field maps to a conserved current of dimension d−1, and metric perturbations map to the stress tensor of dimension d.

Finally, the field theory generating functional equals the gravity partition function with corresponding non-normalizable boundary conditions; in the semiclassical (large N) limit, the gravity path integral is evaluated by saddle point approximation.

A Tom Thomson painting given as a gag gift sold for $481,250 at Heffel Fine Art Auction House in Toronto. Owner Glenna Gardiner had doubted its authenticity until experts verified it. The 118-work auction raised $14.1 million, with artist records for Paul-Emile Borduas's "Figures schematiques" ($3.6 million) and Jack Bush's "Strawberry" ($691,250); Lawren Harris's "Morning, Lake Superior" fetched $1.1 million.

The VIX measures implied volatility of S&P 500 index options and typically moves inversely to the stock market. As a mean reversion indicator, a rising VIX may signal a good time to buy stocks, while a falling VIX may suggest selling. Many VIX trading strategies found online are complex. The VIX can be traded through ETFs like VXX, though these cannot fully replicate it. One example strategy involves going long SPY/ES when the VIX breaks the upper Bollinger Band and exiting after two up days, tested from 2005 to July 2012. The article recommends independent backtesting.

UAE Energy Minister Suhail al-Mazroui said OPEC and non-OPEC producers plan to announce an exit strategy from global supply cuts at a June meeting, though the pact will not necessarily end then. He said it was premature to discuss the strategy's form. Kuwait's oil minister said producers would study the possibility before June. Russian Energy Minister Alexander Novak said withdrawal should be gradual and could take three to six months. The deal cuts supply by about 1.8 million barrels per day.

Southwest Airlines apologized after an employee asked UC Berkeley basketball coach Lindsay Gottlieb to prove her 1-year-old biracial son was hers on a Denver-to-Oakland flight. Gottlieb, who is white, lacked the birth certificate but offered his passport, listing a different last name; the employee then asked for a Facebook post. Gottlieb called the experience "demeaning and insensitive," suspecting his skin color caused the questioning. Southwest said its policy requires verifying lap children under two via birth certificate or ID, and domestic travel does not require matching last names, though it did not specify whether last name or race prompted the request. Chrissy Teigen defended the airline, citing child trafficking precautions.

The paper presents an exact algorithm for computing Nash equilibria in multiplayer imperfect-information games, a problem that is PPAD-hard. The approach generalizes the sequence-form game representation to multiple players, formulates equilibrium computation as a nonlinear complementarity problem, and solves it as a quadratically-constrained feasibility program using Gurobi's nonconvex quadratic solver. On reduced three-player Kuhn poker (with dominated actions removed), the algorithm finds an equilibrium in 2.47 seconds with maximum deviation gain of 1.4×10⁻¹⁷, but cannot solve the full game within 24 hours. Among Gambit's algorithms, only logit quantal response equilibrium (QRE) tracing could solve the reduced game, requiring over 40 seconds with regret of 1.667×10⁻⁵; logit QRE also solved the full game in several minutes. The computed solution matches prior analytically derived equilibrium payoffs, differing only at information sets reached with probability zero, indicating additional Nash equilibria exist beyond the previously computed infinite family. On strategic-form games, the NCP approach outperformed a prior mixed-integer bilinear program approach. The authors conclude that their method is best for small games requiring exact equilibria, logit QRE suits moderate-sized games with convergence guarantees, and iterative self-play methods like counterfactual regret minimization remain the only option for very large games, though without convergence guarantees.

Box Inc beat Wall Street expectations, posting an adjusted first-quarter loss of 7 cents per share versus an expected 8-cent loss and revenue of $140.5 million, up 20% year-over-year. The company added 3,000 customers and issued better-than-expected second-quarter guidance, though its stock fell 4.6% after the bell.
Nigeria's inflation fell to 16.25 percent in May from 17.28 percent in April, though month-on-month prices rose 1.88 percent. Food inflation, driven by costlier meat and cereals, was 19.27 percent.

Thomas Scullun contracted with J. and W. R. Wing to serve as master of the bark Cape Horn Pigeon on a whaling voyage departing San Francisco by December 1, 1891, receiving one-twelfth of the net proceeds, with the Wings paying half his round-trip ticket to Boston. The vessel, carrying 44 men, was cleared at the San Francisco custom-house on December 7, 1891, with an accompanying cargo manifest and sworn declaration. In a diplomatic communication, Russia reported that on August 20 (September 10), 1892, Lieutenant von Cube, commanding the English schooner Maria, seized the Cape Horn Pigeon in the Sea of Okhotsk, believing it had visited Aniva and Patience bays where fishing was forbidden to foreign vessels, and took it to Vladivostok. The investigating commission found no cause for confiscation, deemed the arrest a misunderstanding, and the vessel was returned to her owners.

In *Simmonds v. Simmonds* (decided March 9, 1904), the Texas court affirmed a judgment awarding appellee 117% acres of land in Bell County, part of the Willard Chamberlain headright one-third league, along with rents. Appellee's title rested on a duplicate headright certificate, an 1852 patent, a transfer executed by Louis C. Clemons as Chamberlain's agent conveying the certificate to Joseph P. Sneed, and an 1860 deed from Sneed to appellee. The court held the transfer, more than forty years old, from proper custody, and free of suspicious circumstances, was admissible as an ancient instrument without proof of execution, despite a forgery affidavit; the jury found it genuine. The transfer sufficiently identified the certificate, and Clemons's authority as agent was conclusively presumed. A certified Land Office copy of a third party's affidavit claiming ownership of the certificate was inadmissible, as was an augmentation certificate issued to Chamberlain, which did not disprove the certificate's identity. A party whose testimony is merely contradicted may not introduce evidence of his own character for truth. The court's charge and the evidence were found sufficient, and the judgment was affirmed.

Dusty Baker believes former Giants second baseman Jeff Kent deserves Hall of Fame induction. Kent, eligible since 2013, has received only about 15 percent of votes, far below the 75-percent threshold. Despite 377 home runs and the 2002 NL MVP award in a 17-year career, Kent is puzzled by his low totals, possibly due to his strained relationship with the media.

This patent application, a continuation of prior applications titled "Intelligent Automated Assistant for Media Exploration," relates to providing an auditory-based interface of a digital assistant for media exploration, particularly on devices with limited or no display capabilities. It discloses example methods, non-transitory computer-readable media, and electronic devices in which a digital assistant receives natural-language speech inputs containing search parameters, provides corresponding media items, and allows users to refine requests through additional speech input during playback. Other disclosed methods include providing verbal responses accompanied by playback of related media items, suggesting media items while tracking consecutive non-affirmative responses against a threshold (after which user input is requested), and detecting the physical presence of multiple users to merge their preference profiles for identifying media. The application states these techniques reduce user inputs, provide natural and intuitive interactions, enhance device operability, and reduce power usage. The document further describes a client-server digital assistant architecture, portable multifunction devices with components such as touch screens, audio circuitry, and sensors, various software modules, event handling systems, and a brief description of accompanying drawings.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere architecture and built on TSMC's 7nm process, is designed for AI and HPC computing. It features 108 SMs with 6912 FP32 CUDA cores and 432 third-generation Tensor Cores supporting multiple data types (FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, Binary). The A100 delivers 2.5x the mixed-precision Tensor Core performance of V100, with additional 2x speedups through Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity using a 2:4 sparse matrix pattern. Key architectural improvements include 192 KB combined L1 cache/shared memory per SM, a new asynchronous copy instruction, 40 GB HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, and a 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x larger than V100). The Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) feature partitions each A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances for multi-tenant environments. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth across twelve links. The A100 also includes hardware JPEG decode (NVJPG), an Optical Flow Accelerator, five NVDEC units, and improved atomic operations. CUDA 11 supports these features through Task Graphs, asynchronous copy operations, asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls, and enhanced Cooperative Groups. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs delivering 5 PFLOPS of AI performance with NVSwitch interconnects.

QuantifiedStrategies.com offers trading strategies for TradingView, translating selected strategies into Pinescript. Trading full-time since 2001, the company aims to provide simple, effective strategies and includes a trading risk disclaimer.
Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth told hundreds of summoned generals and admirals that the military had gone soft and "woke" and needed shaking up.

Amazon.com, Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2019 reports total net sales of $59.7 billion, up 17% from $51.0 billion in Q1 2018, with net income of $3.6 billion compared to $1.6 billion a year earlier. Operating income rose to $4.4 billion from $1.9 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $7.09 versus $3.27. By segment, North America net sales were $35.8 billion (operating income $2.3 billion), International $16.2 billion (operating loss $90 million), and AWS $7.7 billion (operating income $2.2 billion). Operating cash flow was $1.8 billion in Q1 2019, and trailing twelve-month free cash flow was $23.0 billion. Total assets were $178.1 billion and stockholders' equity $48.4 billion at March 31, 2019. Amazon adopted new lease accounting guidance on January 1, 2019, recognizing approximately $21 billion of operating lease assets and liabilities, and had $24.3 billion of unsecured senior notes outstanding. Disclosed legal matters include patent infringement lawsuits filed by Dynamic Data Technologies, Saint Lawrence Communications, Data Scape, and Vocalife, as well as ongoing tax disputes, including an IRS transfer pricing matter and a European Commission state aid decision for which approximately €250 million was deposited into escrow.

The design requires an alert (logic high output) when the amplifier output exceeds 1.1V. A low ESR 0.1µF ceramic bypass capacitor must be placed directly between the (V+) and GND pins to prevent supply ringing and oscillations from fast output edges. The device operates from split or single supplies, with split-supply outputs swinging low to (V-) rather than GND. Coupling between outputs and inputs should be minimized.

Former Burlington College president Carol Moore blames a 2010 land deal championed by Jane Sanders for the college's closure. The $10 million purchase is under federal scrutiny, and Moore also criticized a related agreement benefiting Jane Sanders' daughter.

Qualcomm accidentally published a blog post about the Asus Zenfone AR, the second consumer-facing Google Tango-enabled smartphone and the first Tango phone to also support Google's Daydream View headset. It uses the Snapdragon 821. Evan Blass posted renders of the device. Pricing and availability are unknown, with details expected at CES. Asus also teased another Zenfone with the Snapdragon 835.

The 20-day exponential moving average (EMA) strategy uses the 20-day EMA to generate buy and sell signals, purchasing when price rises above the EMA and selling when it falls below. Backtested on SPY, the strategy performed poorly, with low CAGR and significant drawdown despite being invested about 70% of the time. Adding an additional indicator improved performance, nearly matching buy-and-hold CAGR on a risk-adjusted basis, though drawdown remained unchanged. The strategy also worked much better on Bitcoin from 2014 onward, likely due to its strong momentum.

IMF mission chief Ron van Rooden said Ukraine's pension system is unsustainable, supporting about 30 percent of the population and operating at a loss. He noted Ukrainian retirement ages—58.5 for men, just over 56 for women—are roughly five years below EU averages, and suggested limiting early retirements and targeting companies evading pension taxes. He did not explicitly require raising the pension age as a condition of the $17.5 billion IMF program. Ukraine hopes to secure another $4.5 billion this year.

Iron sulfate heptahydrate, also known as ferrous sulfate, copperas, or green vitriol, is a water-soluble sulfate compound produced as a co-product during titanium dioxide manufacturing from ilmenite. It contains 18–20% iron and up to 3% free acid. Its crystals tend to stick together, making the product dusty, and its acid content can attack storage containers. Medically, it treats iron deficiency and is listed by the WHO as an essential medicine. Historically used in textiles, leather, and ink, it also treats iron chlorosis in fruit cultivation, purifies water through flocculation and phosphate removal, prevents eutrophication, reduces chromium ions in cement, and serves as an iron supplier in agriculture.

President Bush addresses the West Point Corps of Cadets near the end of his presidency, reflecting on his role as Commander in Chief. He argues that despite the Cold War's end and reduced nuclear threat, dangers remain from dictators, weapons of mass destruction, and terrorism, requiring continued American engagement and leadership rather than isolationism. He rejects both isolationism and acting as the world's policeman, outlining principles for when military force is appropriate—citing the Gulf War, Somalia, Panama, and the Philippines as examples, while explaining his decision against force in the former Yugoslavia. He states that no rigid rules can govern intervention decisions, stresses the need for clear missions, achievable plans, and international support, and notes he is passing a strong military to President-elect Clinton. He praises the All Volunteer Force and its culture of merit, encourages public service, recalls his own 1942 enlistment in the Navy, and grants amnesty to the Corps of Cadets.

The lecture discusses the Asymptotic Equipartition Property (AEP), a concept that both mathematicians and engineers initially struggled to absorb after Shannon introduced it. For a discrete memoryless source, the weak law of large numbers shows that the sample average of log pmf random variables converges to the entropy H(X). Typical sequences—those whose sample average is close to H(X)—fill nearly all the probability space as n grows. The major results are: the number of typical sequences is approximately 2^(nH(X)), each has probability roughly 2^(−nH(X)), and the probability of obtaining a typical sequence approaches 1. In fixed-length-to-fixed-length coding, about H(X) bits per symbol can be achieved with rare failures, while attempting H(X)−ε bits per symbol fails with probability approaching 1.

Because real sources have memory, Markov sources are introduced. Ergodic, aperiodic Markov chains have unique steady-state probabilities that are approached exponentially from any starting state. Coding for Markov sources uses the conditional entropy H(X|S), which is achievable with n-to-variable-length codes.

Finally, the Lempel-Ziv universal algorithm (LZ77 in 1977, simplified as LZ78 in 1978) contains no embedded probabilities. It uses a sliding window, finds the longest match of unencoded symbols within the window, and encodes match length with Elias's unary-binary code and match position with log W bits. Asymptotically it achieves H(X|S) bits per symbol, automatically discovering statistical structure and adapting to changing statistics.

Coach Quenneville discussed several players and team matters. He described Johnny as an ultimate player who excels without the puck, faces top defensive matchups, and brings value beyond his lower offensive numbers. He called Dunks a thoroughbred with exceptional conditioning who relishes heavy minutes. Bolly, once viewed as a third-line player, has taken on more responsibility, offering defensive predictability and offensive skill. Quenneville expressed appreciation for coaching in Chicago, calling it a special organization and passionate sports city. He reflected on the team's adversity, including being down against Detroit, and praised the group's consistency, improved defense, and goaltending that won the Jennings Trophy. He said Corey has the capability to be a top goalie and complements Ray Emery well. He also addressed the team's too-many-men-on-the-ice penalties, noting they were fortunate to avoid consequences, and mentioned receiving a text from Tom Thibodeau.

Damian Lillard scored 32 points, becoming the fastest player in Portland franchise history to reach 10,000 career points, but the Trail Blazers' four-game winning streak ended in a 130-105 loss to the Toronto Raptors. DeMar DeRozan led Toronto with 35 points, including six 3-pointers, as the Raptors won their sixth straight over Portland and improved to an NBA-best 20-4 at home. CJ McCollum added 21 points and Jusuf Nurkic 20 for Portland.

The passage describes NVIDIA's GA10x Ampere architecture GPUs and related technologies. GDDR6X memory, developed with Micron, uses PAM4 signaling with four voltage levels to achieve data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth in the GeForce RTX 3090—a 52% improvement over TU102. A Maximum Transition Avoidance (MTA) encoding scheme addresses signal integrity challenges, and new Error Detection and Replay (EDR) technology helps overclockers identify memory limits without crashes.

NVIDIA RTX IO enables GPU-based loading and decompression of game assets through Microsoft's DirectStorage API, accelerating I/O up to 100x versus hard drives while offloading work from dozens of CPU cores.

The NVIDIA A40 data center GPU delivers up to 2X FP32 throughput, 2X ray-tracing throughput, and 5X AI training performance versus the Quadro RTX 6000, with 48GB memory expandable to 96GB via NVLink. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU features 10,752 CUDA cores and 48GB GDDR6.

GA10x GPUs support DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1, enabling 8K60 and 4K120 displays. Fifth-generation NVDEC provides the industry's first hardware AV1 decode, while seventh-generation NVENC handles encoding up to 8K HEVC. The architecture doubles ray/triangle intersection performance via second-generation RT Cores and doubles Tensor Core throughput through structural sparsity. The GeForce RTX 3090 is 1.5x faster than TITAN RTX, and the RTX 3070 outperforms the RTX 2080 Ti.

Harvey Weinstein has been indicted on rape and criminal sex act charges, Manhattan District Attorney Cyrus Vance Jr announced. Weinstein, charged Friday on two counts of rape and one criminal sexual act involving two women, declined to testify before the grand jury on his lawyers' advice, citing insufficient preparation time.

The passage quotes the first article of the Russo-British treaty guaranteeing both nations' subjects freedom of navigation, fishing, and trade with natives on unoccupied Pacific coasts. In the Paris arbitration between Great Britain and the United States, a majority of arbitrators found that Russia's 1821 ukase claimed Bering Sea jurisdiction to 100 Italian miles, but that in negotiating the treaties of 1824 and 1825 Russia accepted jurisdiction limited to cannon-shot range from shore and never exercised exclusive seal-fishery rights beyond ordinary territorial waters. Because both treaties referred to "the great ocean commonly called the Pacific Ocean," the tribunal reasoned that the Bering Sea, like the Okhotsk Sea, is a branch of that ocean, so including one necessarily includes the other. Claims of exclusive jurisdiction over gulfs as large as the Okhotsk Sea conflict with accepted international law; de Martens's reasoning on the freedom of the Baltic and Kara Seas applies with greater force to the Okhotsk Sea, and Vattel held that only small bays and straits may be occupied, not great areas like Hudson Bay.

The passage is an email chain among Enron employees forwarding a Texas Monthly article, "How Enron Blew It" by Mimi Swartz. The article recounts Enron's rise from a pipeline company—formed when Ken Lay's Houston Natural Gas merged with InterNorth in 1985—into a trading powerhouse. Jeff Skilling, hired by Lay as a McKinsey consultant, devised the "Gas Bank," which guaranteed gas supply and price, and joined Enron in 1990 to head Enron Finance Corporation. He built a culture that recruited top graduates, offered uncapped merit bonuses, and enforced a harsh ranking system ("rank and yank") that replaced 15 percent of the workforce annually. By 1995 Enron was North America's largest natural-gas merchant, and it expanded into electricity, EnronOnline, and broadband, using aggressive tactics and mark-to-market accounting to book profits up front. Skilling sidelined rival Rebecca Mark by placing her in charge of Azurix, a water venture that failed, leading to her resignation. Skilling became CEO in February 2001 but resigned abruptly after six months as troubles mounted: blame for California's energy crisis, the telecom downturn, the failed Blockbuster deal, and analyst questions about accounting drove the stock from a January high of $80 to around $35. Ken Lay resumed the CEO role, promising a kinder, gentler Enron focused closer to its core. Skilling defends his departure, noting 90 percent of his net worth was in Enron stock, and plans new ventures in Houston commodity trading.

The paper studies the sample complexity of estimating nonlinear functions of quantum states, such as tr(ρ^k O), when restricted to k-replica protocols that perform joint measurements on at most k copies at a time. Although tr(ρ^k O) is linear in ρ^⊗k and efficiently estimable with k-replica joint measurements (e.g., via the generalized swap test), such measurements are experimentally challenging. The authors prove that k-replica joint measurements are necessary: estimating tr(ρ^(k+1) O) within constant error requires Ω(√d) samples with k-replica protocols for suitable observables, while (k+1)-replica protocols need only O(k/ε²) samples. This establishes the first fine-grained hierarchy of replica quantum advantage for all k ≥ 2, resolving an open problem, with constant-vs-exponential separation for constant k.

The main tool is an indistinguishability principle: any "Haar-assembled ensemble," built from Haar-random states via tensor products, unitaries, and mixtures, requires Ω(√(d_min/(m·a_max²))) samples for a 1-replica protocol to distinguish it from its average. Applications include spectrum testing—distinguishing spectra agreeing on moments up to degree k requires Ω(√d/(m√ln m)) samples with k-replica protocols—implying lower bounds for rank testing (Ω(√d/(k√ln k))) and for estimating tr(ρ^α) with non-integer α. An upper bound shows ⌈(k+1)/2⌉-replica measurements suffice with sample complexity Õ(max{k√d/ε, k/ε²}), proving the √d dependence optimal.

The lower bounds reduce estimation to distinguishing ensembles built from distributions matching on the first k moments but differing at degree k+1 (constructed via Chebyshev polynomials); the resulting k-fold tensor products are Haar-assembled ensembles with equal averages, hence indistinguishable. The principle is proved via one-sided likelihood ratios and a generalized permutation-operator inequality, with a Gram-Schmidt rounding lemma handling spectrum testing. Future directions include improving error dependence, pinpointing the phase-transition threshold in ε, extending the principle to ensembles {U diag(p) U†}, and identifying tasks hard for protocols with limited working qubits.

Vertex Resource Group Ltd. has acquired a private hydro-vac services company serving the Edmonton, Alberta region for $4.3 million. The acquisition, which closed June 30, 2018, doubles Vertex's hydro-vac fleet with the addition of 11 units serving municipal and utility clients. The deal expands Vertex's hydro-vac services into the Edmonton market and is expected to add approximately $5 million in annual revenue. Vertex, headquartered in Sherwood Park, Alberta, is an environmental services provider with approximately 750 employees, operating primarily in western Canada.

In a speech to the Foreign Service Institute, the Secretary tells future American diplomats that their task is peace. He contrasts Europe's devastation in 1945 with its present strength, attributing the transformation to collective action and institutions such as NATO. He rejects calls to dismantle NATO, arguing that reform must come through consultation among member nations rather than isolation. NATO, he states, is an alliance to keep peace rather than make war; its integrated military power and political unity have deterred war for twenty years. The United States, together with thirteen other allies, is determined to preserve and strengthen NATO's deterrent, and he expresses hope that any withdrawn member will return to the alliance. He concludes that Atlantic unity offers hope for reconciling Western and Eastern Europe and urges the diplomats to work for human solidarity.

The lower 32kB flash address space supports higher erase/program endurance for EEPROM emulation; devices with ≤32kB flash support NWEC(LOWER) cycles throughout. Definitions are provided for cumulative erase operations, word-line write limits, program time, and sector program time.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-K annual report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2019 describes a technology company founded in 1975 and headquartered in Redmond, Washington, whose mission is to empower every person and organization on the planet to achieve more. The company operates through three segments: Productivity and Business Processes (Office, LinkedIn, Dynamics), Intelligent Cloud (server products, Azure, GitHub, Enterprise Services), and More Personal Computing (Windows, Surface devices, Xbox gaming, and Search/Bing). Its strategy centers on three ambitions: reinventing productivity and business processes, building the intelligent cloud and intelligent edge platform, and creating more personal computing. Notable acquisitions include LinkedIn ($27.0 billion, 2016) and GitHub ($7.5 billion, 2018). Competitors include Apple, Google, Amazon, Oracle, SAP, Salesforce, and IBM across its various businesses. Products are distributed through OEMs, direct sales, and distributors/resellers, with volume licensing programs such as Enterprise Agreements. The company holds over 61,000 issued patents and employed approximately 144,000 full-time people as of June 30, 2019. Executive officers include CEO Satya Nadella and CFO Amy Hood. As of December 31, 2018, the aggregate market value of common stock held by non-affiliates was $769.6 billion. Risk factors cited include intense competition, execution risks in cloud-based services, cybersecurity threats, data privacy concerns, IoT and AI-related risks, intellectual property challenges, legal and regulatory scrutiny under competition laws, and anti-corruption compliance—highlighted by a $25.3 million settlement with the DOJ and SEC related to its Hungarian subsidiary.

A penalty-kick tiebreaker, or "shoot-out," is used to decide a winner in tied soccer matches, typically in single-elimination tournaments. The procedure is governed by Law 10 of the IFAB Laws of the Game, with penalty kick mechanics covered in Law 14. Each team selects five players to take alternating kicks from the penalty spot, 12 yards from the goal. If one team scores more goals after five kicks, it wins; if tied, the shoot-out enters a "sudden death" phase where teams alternate single kicks until one scores and the other misses.

Only players on the field at the end of play are eligible, and each must kick once before any player kicks again. The referee conducts coin tosses to determine the goal used and which team kicks first, and keeps the official record. If teams have unequal numbers due to injuries or red cards, the larger team must "reduce to equate." The result is recorded as part of the match score (e.g., 1-1 (4-3)), though shoot-out goals do not count toward individual statistics.

Coaches should prepare teams in advance by reviewing Law 10 and any tournament modifications, identifying and ranking penalty takers, practicing the full process under pressure, studying opposing goalkeepers, and mentally preparing goalkeepers. During the match, coaches should avoid letdowns, ensure designated shooters remain on the field, and confirm the kicking order. Additional notes cover rules on ball contact, goalkeeper substitutions, forfeited kicks for absent players, and that the match is not abandoned if a team drops below seven players during kicks.

The passage is a Motley Fool Money review of the Wells Fargo Reflect® Card by personal finance writer Ryan Wilcox. The card offers 0% intro APR for 21 months from account opening on purchases and qualifying balance transfers (16.99%, 23.49%, or 28.74% variable APR afterward), making it suited for paying down debt or financing large purchases. It charges no annual fee and includes cell phone protection of up to $600 against theft or damage, subject to a $25 deductible and usable twice per year. Drawbacks include a 5% balance transfer fee (minimum $5), a 3% foreign transaction fee, and no ongoing rewards after the intro period. The recommended credit score is Good/Excellent (670-850), though approval is not guaranteed. The card was named Motley Fool Money's Best 0% Intro APR Card of 2025. The site discloses that it receives advertiser compensation but states that product ratings are not influenced by it.

On June 24, 2020, Tesla, Inc. entered into a 90-day Indemnification Agreement with CEO Elon Musk. During this Bridge Term, Tesla is resuming its annual evaluation of directors' and officers' indemnity coverage options, which had been suspended during COVID-19 shelter-in-place requirements, and intends to obtain a binding market quote for a D&O liability insurance policy with a $100 million aggregate coverage limit. Under the agreement, Musk will provide D&O indemnity coverage from personal funds, up to $100 million, if such coverage is not indemnifiable by Tesla. In return, Tesla will pay him a one-time fee of $972,361, plus an additional amount to reconcile the fee to the market-based premium (prorated for 90 days and discounted by 50%), if greater. The agreement is subject to customary terms and conditions. CFO Zachary J. Kirkhorn signed the report on June 30, 2020.

Patrick Sutherland appealed a judgment dismissing his CPLR article 78 proceeding challenging the Board of Parole's denial of his request for parole release. He contended the Board relied on erroneous criminal history information regarding a shooting charge that had been dismissed. The court held he was precluded from challenging the presentence investigation report because he never timely sought its correction. Finding the Board considered the relevant statutory factors, the judgment was affirmed without costs.

AGNC Investment is a leading mortgage REIT with significant agency mortgage-backed securities holdings, one of two premier mortgage REITs alongside Annaly Capital Management. The author maintains a bullish rating, citing Fed rate cuts that should lower financing costs and drive book value gains through higher MBS valuations. AGNC posted its third consecutive quarter of positive net interest income in Q2'25 and trades at a premium to book value, reflecting investor optimism. Its attractive monthly dividend appeals to income-focused investors.

Sony's Xperia XZ Premium will receive an Android Oreo update later this year, confirmed at IFA 2017 alongside the Xperia XZ1 and XZ1 Compact. It gains the 3D Creator app for scanning faces, food and objects, plus camera improvements including smile-detecting predictive capture and an enhanced burst mode tracking moving objects at 10 shots per second.

In this address to a joint session of Congress, the President calls for a break with tradition, arguing that America's programs and institutions need reform as the nation enters the 1970s. He identifies peace as the first priority, noting progress toward ending the Vietnam War and crediting Congress's support for a just peace. He outlines a new foreign policy based on the doctrine announced at Guam, under which other nations assume primary responsibility for their own defense and development while America reduces its involvement abroad. He cites strengthened relations with European allies, Japan, and Latin America, and a shift from confrontation to negotiation with the Soviet Union and Communist China.

Domestically, he notes projected economic growth of $500 billion over the decade but points to the 1960s' crime, inflation, and social unrest as evidence that government must change. He urges three priorities: total welfare reform, a "New Federalism" returning power from Washington to the states and people, and expanded opportunities including equal voting rights and equal employment opportunity. He attributes inflation to federal deficits of $57 billion in the 1960s, reports a balanced budget in 1969 and a 1970 surplus, and recommends a balanced budget for 1971. On crime, he notes that 13 anti-crime bills sent to Congress remain unsigned and announces that 1971 federal spending for local law enforcement will double that of 1970.

He proposes the most comprehensive and costly environmental program in America's history, including a $10 billion nationwide clean waters program, new financing for open space and parklands, stricter automobile emission standards, and regulations treating air and water as scarce resources. He calls for a national growth policy to address decaying central cities and depopulating rural areas. Looking toward the nation's 200th anniversary in 1976, he envisions an America that has abolished hunger, checked inflation, won the fight against crime, curbed pollution, and achieved peace with all nations, stressing that material progress must be accompanied by spiritual and moral leadership.

Andrea Conti's agent says the 23-year-old wing-back, who scored eight goals with four assists in 33 Serie A appearances, only wants to join Milan and that his time with Atalanta is over. He urged Gasperini not to block the transfer, seeking a collaborative solution.

A swimming robot co-developed by Toshiba and the International Research Institute for Nuclear Decommissioning will be sent into Fukushima Dai-Ichi's Unit 3 containment vessel in July to assess damage and locate melted fuel submerged in radioactive water. The loaf-sized "mini manbo" has lights, tail propellers, two cameras, and a dosimeter. Earlier snake and scorpion robots failed due to extreme radiation and malfunctions. Scientists need this information to plan safe fuel removal.

Nassim Nicholas Taleb is a statistician, mathematician, philosopher, trader, and investor focused on randomness, uncertainty, and probabilities. He gained fame with The Black Swan (2007), though the authors consider Fooled By Randomness (2001) his best book. His Incerto series, published between 2001 and 2018, covers probability, luck, uncertainty, biases, fragility versus antifragility, decentralization, decision-making, and tail risk. Taleb grew up in Lebanon, studied in France, and settled in the US, where he worked as a proprietary trader and reportedly became financially independent after the 1987 crash through a specific options strategy. He co-founded Empirica Capital with Mark Spitznagel, which closed in 2005; Spitznagel later founded Universa Investments, where Taleb remains an advisor. Universa employs a tail-risk hedging barbell strategy, with assets growing from $300 million in 2007 to over $11 billion in 2022, reportedly gaining over 4000% in 2020. Taleb's barbell strategy involves allocating assets to two extremes—low-risk and high-risk—with no middle ground, aiming to profit from tail events. He distinguishes Mediocristan (contained risks) from Extremistan (multiplicative risks). His concept of antifragility describes systems that benefit from shocks and disorder. Skin in the Game (2018) argues decision-makers should bear the consequences of their actions. The article concludes with numerous quotes from his books.

Coach Vigneault expressed disappointment after a Stanley Cup Final loss in which all three games went to overtime, praising his team's effort and noting both goaltenders were outstanding. He said he needed a few days to reflect. In other remarks, he referenced a win where the team held a two-goal lead, stressed the need for more puck possession and a north-south style, and expressed confidence that the power play, which has had good looks but not finished, would come through.

In this MIT lecture, Gary Gensler discusses initial coin offerings (ICOs) as a new form of crowdfunding in which startups sell crypto tokens to raise money. JR Willett conceived the idea in 2010, proposing that applications built on top of Bitcoin could be used to raise funds. ICOs grew substantially, with roughly $25 billion raised between June 2017 and June 2018—about 20-30% of global venture capital funding—though activity has since declined.
