Key characteristics include: proceeds raised before networks are functional (95-99% of recent offerings), about 75% marketed on just an idea, largely centralized development (over half not even open source), promoters retaining some tokens, transferability, monetary policies governing scarcity, and purchaser expectations of profit through appreciation. Gensler distinguishes ICOs from Kickstarter by noting investors anticipate profits.

Evaluation criteria include: assessing token use case viability, reading white papers, examining the team, venture capital involvement, community following, monetary policy, and token distribution. ICO proceeds are typically booked as either deferred or current revenue.

Statistics show 84% of ICOs use the Ethereum platform, 57% raised under $100,000, 67% were unsuccessful, and only 1.7% had source code at offering. In Q3 2018, $1.8 billion was raised, down 78% from Q2. Gensler predicts 90-95% of ICOs will eventually fail, though blockchain technology itself will persist. Regulatory discussion, including recent SEC actions, was deferred to the next session.

The Malawi Health Equity Network (MHEN) has urged government to deploy internal auditors to all 28 district councils, citing research in Ntcheu that found their absence was affecting fund management. Executive Director George Jobe said auditors are needed to guide use of financial resources. The research also found councils excluded rural residents from budget preparation and a coordination gap between councils, NGOs, and CSOs. Government analyst Yohanne Nyanja said plans to deploy auditors were at an advanced stage, adding councils should support them rather than view them as "police." The K7 million research was supported by Mamaye.

Despite Trump's claim that Canada-U.S. trade relations will only be "tweaked," the trade imbalance (18% of U.S. foreign trade goes to Canada versus 76% of Canada's going to the U.S.) means small American changes can significantly hurt Canada. Behind the friendly tone of Monday's Trump-Trudeau White House meeting lie U.S. grievances over beef imports, supply management, and softwood lumber, while Rona Ambrose worries Trump's deregulation and low-tax policies could make Canada uncompetitive. Trudeau's diplomatic performance was praised as masterful and dignified. Trump was gracious, and the meeting produced a communique of mutual support and a new women entrepreneurs council.

Coach DeBoer said home ice matters in the playoffs, noting the team improved between games and expects to be better tomorrow. He cited the need for better support across the ice, as Pittsburgh's speed creates positioning problems. A player has a maintenance issue, and lineup decisions will be made on game day. Drawing on his Devils experience of facing a series deficit, he stressed the series isn't over until a team wins four games. He wants more puck possession, more attacking, and to draw penalties. He called Crosby Pittsburgh's best player so far, with Kessel and Malkin creating matchup problems, and expects momentum swings requiring patience.

The Santa Cruz County Board of Supervisors selected Carlos Palacios, 55, to replace retiring County Administrative Officer Susan Mauriello. Palacios, currently assistant county administrative officer and former Watsonville city manager, will be the county's first Latino in the role, earning a $263,057 base salary. He will oversee 2,400 staff and a roughly $720 million budget. Mauriello retires July 7 after 27 years.

The President transmits a preliminary report by James Bronson Reynolds and Commissioner Charles P. Neill on conditions in the Chicago stockyards, which he calls revolting and requiring immediate congressional action. Existing law prevents satisfactory federal inspection of stockyards, packing houses, and meat products entering interstate commerce, and the Department of Agriculture lacks adequate appropriations and authority. Uninspected meats may currently be shipped between states, though not abroad. The President has directed that labels state only that carcasses were inspected at slaughter, and may prohibit inspection labels if legislation fails. He recommends inspection from slaughter to canning, funded by a fee not exceeding 8 cents per animal slaughtered. The investigation remains unfinished, with allegations about chemicals and tainted meat unreported. He urges enactment of the "Beveridge amendment" (Senate amendment No. 29) to the Agriculture appropriations act.

Armed police arrested a 26-year-old man at Shackleton Court in Newton Heath after reports at around 4:30pm on Monday that a man with a firearm had threatened two people. The incident lasted several hours, with witnesses reporting numerous police vans and officers holding rifles surrounding the tower block.

The DAWN-Plasma trial was a randomized, multicenter, open-label phase 2 proof-of-concept study evaluating convalescent plasma added to standard of care versus standard of care alone in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. Between May 2020 and January 2021, 489 patients were randomized 2:1 to convalescent plasma (n=326) or control (n=163). Patients received 800-1000 mL of plasma with high neutralizing antibody titers in 4 doses. The primary endpoint—proportion of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15—showed no difference between groups (83.7% vs 84.1%, p=0.976). No significant differences were found in any secondary endpoints, including mortality. Safety profiles were similar between groups, with transfusion-related side effects in 6% of the intervention group and no TRALI cases. Higher neutralizing antibody titers at baseline and Day 6 correlated with better outcomes, but the intervention did not affect antibody titers. The study concluded that early high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma did not change the natural course of COVID-19 in hospitalized patients.

The paper studies the complexity of ML-definability and ML-separability of modal µ-calculus (µML) formulae, where an ML-separator of φ, φ′ is an ML-formula ψ with φ |= ψ and ψ |= ¬φ′. Separability generalizes definability (the case φ′ = ¬φ). These problems are investigated over several model classes: all models, words (unary trees), binary trees, and d-ary trees with d ≥ 3.

Main results: ML-separability is ExpTime-complete over all models and binary trees, PSpace-complete over words, and 2-ExpTime-complete over d-ary trees with d ≥ 3. The higher complexity for d ≥ 3 is notable, since higher-arity trees can be encoded into binary ones. Effective separator constructions are given, with sizes doubly exponential over all models and binary trees, exponential over words, and triple exponential over d ≥ 3 trees.

The paper also shows that ML lacks the Craig interpolation property over trees of outdegree d ≥ 3 (while retaining it over all models, words, and binary trees); consequently, the interpolant existence problem is coNExpTime-complete over higher-arity trees. As an application, graded modalities are considered: grML-definability and grML-separability are ExpTime-complete, while ML-separability of graded µ-calculus formulae is 2-ExpTime-complete.

Methodologically, the paper uses parity-game semantics for µML, bisimulations, nondeterministic parity tree automata, and model-theoretic characterizations of separability via joint (σ, n)-consistency. Otto's ExpTime definability results are recalled with a corrected proof, separability over all models is solved analogously, and over words both definability and separability are shown PSpace-complete, with exponential-size separator construction.

Ashley Hollis, an A&O Shearman associate, won the reality show "Big Brother" by hiding her attorney identity and posing as a social media marketing manager. She credited her winning speech to lawyer skills and inspiration from the movie character Elle Woods. She plans to give a portion of her $750,000 prize to her parents and is considering buying a home.

This study presents a bibliometric analysis of STEAM education combined with gamification, based on 34 English-language documents retrieved from the Scopus database for the period 2017–2023. Publication output began in 2017, with growth from 4 to 8 documents annually between 2020 and 2023, peaking in 2022. The most cited article, by Wannapiroon and Pimdee (2022), received 30 citations, while Ceur Workshop Proceedings produced the most publications. The most productive authors were Nilsook, Wannapiroon, and Kummanee, each with three publications and 25 citations. Thailand led in publications (6) and citations (68), followed by Bulgaria, Italy, and Malaysia. Computer science accounted for 37.7% of publications and social sciences for 20.5%. Co-occurrence analysis of author keywords identified gamification, STEAM, STEAM education, and computational thinking as the predominant terms. Malaysia achieved the highest total link strength, while Germany, Latvia, Norway, and France were the most engaged in joint research. Factorial analysis identified three clusters covering educational methodologies and tools, student-centered learning environments, and educational technologies with engagement strategies. Overall, 34 documents and 155 citations were gathered over seven years, and the publication trend is expected to continue growing.

Tharisa plc's investor presentation, introduced by Ilja Graulich, features CEO Phoevos Pouroulis discussing the phased transition from 15 years of open cast mining to underground mining as open pit resources deplete, starting with the west mine. He introduces CFO Michael Jones, Managing Director of Tharisa Minerals Vulela Makuni, and Executive of Operations Roy Murley. The company envisions a fully integrated complex, having coproduced Platinum Group Metals and chrome concentrate profitably for 11 years despite volatile markets.

Libyan National Army forces in Benghazi have lost four men and seen 10 wounded in December, five months after Khalifa Haftar declared victory, amid continued resistance and daily clashes in the Khreibish district.

This article describes a dialogic educational activity developed during the COVID-19 pandemic in a "Non-Formal Education" course within a physics teacher education program at a Brazilian Federal University. Authors Arthur Santiago and Cristiano Mattos drew on Freire's critical pedagogy and Cultural Historical Activity Theory (CHAT) to conduct emergency remote teaching with 19 students using the Discord platform. The activity's central theme was the contradiction students experienced regarding the reopening of schools during the pandemic. Through a seven-stage design, students discussed their difficulties, debated school reopening, researched reliable sources on COVID-19, and collaboratively produced an infographic disseminated via WhatsApp. Analysis of recorded meetings showed that Discord facilitated dialogic interaction, student agency, and autonomy: students moved between groups, shared tasks, and self-organized meetings without the teacher's presence. The authors attribute the successful engagement to students' prior familiarity with Discord, the Freirean-inspired thematic organization based on students' lived problems, and the collective construction of products. The activity enhanced students' conscious awareness by linking their immediate personal difficulties to broader socio-political contradictions, demonstrating dialogue as an activity rather than a mere exchange of ideas.

Abercrombie & Fitch CEO Fran Horowitz, who took over in 2017 after the brand crashed due to sexualized marketing and dismissive attitudes toward customers, rebuilt the company by improving clothing quality, giving employees more input, and abandoning trend-chasing in favor of becoming a long-lasting lifestyle brand. Sales nearly doubled to $2.6 billion between 2019 and 2024, with combined A&F and Hollister sales expected to top $5 billion this year. To sustain growth, she pursued partnerships including selling Abercrombie Kids clothing at Macy's and becoming the NFL's first fashion partner, aiming to acquire customers and better serve female fans whom she says have been underserved by "pink and sparkly" merchandise.

This patent application, a continuation of prior applications, describes electronic gaming systems and methods featuring a stop-based bonus game, such as a wheel or reel with multiple stop positions. The bonus game is associated with two classes of awards: first awards (e.g., large jackpot awards) and second awards (e.g., small credit prizes). When a player selects a stop position associated with a second award, that award is granted, and the stop position is then re-associated with a first award for future plays, increasing the likelihood of winning a jackpot in subsequent plays. These associations may persist across gaming sessions and players. A bonus wheel may trigger a secondary jackpot wheel containing stop positions linked to credit prizes and jackpot awards; when a credit prize is won, it is replaced by a jackpot award. After a jackpot is won, stop positions may be reset to default associations. Various constructs may be used, including wheels, reels, dice, and grid-based treasure maps. Jackpot awards may be progressive or valued at least four to forty times higher than the highest non-jackpot award; second awards may include fixed credits, multipliers, wild symbols, free plays, or no-value awards. The system may operate on standalone gaming machines or networked devices connected to servers such as player tracking, progressive, and casino management systems. Example implementations include a bonus wheel with independently spinning inner and outer wheels offering credit prizes, free games, and access to GRAND, MAJOR, MINOR, and MINI jackpot wheels.

Veteran Rodney Orton of Muskogee, Oklahoma, who relied on a mobility scooter for 15 years due to breathing problems, was left without one when it malfunctioned. The VA told him he needed a new evaluation with a six-week wait. After Problem Solver Travis Guillory contacted the VA, Asst. Chief of Prosthetics Diana Kinion found a suitable scooter in local inventory and delivered it to Orton's hospital room the next morning.

This study examines whether having students prompt, validate, and refine AI-generated simulations can support conceptual learning in undergraduate physics. Conducted in spring 2025 at a large R1 public university in the western United States, the study took place in the laboratory component of a second-semester, calculus-free introductory physics for life sciences course (initial enrollment 187 students, primarily life sciences majors). The topic was electric potential and equipotential lines.

Students were assigned to one of three quasi-experimental groups: (1) a traditional physical laboratory using conductive-solution equipment (control), (2) a lab using a pre-built simulation designed by an author with AI tools, or (3) an "AI-engagement" lab in which students generated their own simulation through structured prompting of Claude AI (Sonnet 4, free version), then validated and iteratively refined it. All groups shared three learning objectives concerning the relationship between potential and distance (V = kq/r), properties of equipotential lines, and the relationship between line density and potential differences. Assessment consisted of five conceptual questions and five Likert-scale attitude questions administered immediately after the lab, with midterm and final exam scores collected later to check sample comparability.

Kruskal-Wallis tests showed significant differences in conceptual question scores across groups (p < .001, η² = .359). Post-hoc tests indicated both simulation groups significantly outperformed the physical lab group, with no significant difference between the AI and pre-built simulation groups. No significant differences appeared on midterm or final exam performance. On attitudes, both digital groups reported more positive responses than the physical lab group on all five questions; the pre-built group rated the lab more favorably than the AI group only on the question comparing the lab to prior weeks.

The authors conclude that AI-guided simulation development supported conceptual understanding equivalently to pre-built simulations and better than physical equipment, without compromising learning despite added cognitive demands. They suggest the AI approach may foster modeling and validation skills, since students must treat AI outputs skeptically, unlike users of pre-built simulations. Limitations include differences in abstraction level between conditions, technical constraints of the free AI tier, and the study's focus on a single concept, homogeneous population, and single institution. The paper concludes that generative AI offers a complementary tool alongside physical equipment and pre-built simulations, with the mixture chosen according to learning objectives.

This document is a specification update (31534D, March 2006) for the AMD Geode™ CS5535 Companion Device, Silicon Revision A3. It lists errata, numbered non-sequentially because resolved issues are omitted, each with a description, implications, and a resolution where available. The issues span multiple functional blocks: PIT deviations from industry-standard behavior; a debug port that hangs the system; PIC failures, including missed interrupts when automatic clock gating is enabled and incorrect AEOI behavior; DMA problems such as incorrect rotating priority, failed 8237 software DMA from LPC, and blocked UART/LPC I/O during block or demand mode DMA; system hangs from I/O cycles or LBAR values at 10000h or higher; lack of USB over-voltage protection; clock-gating failures in the USB controllers and UART CEIR mode; ATAC/IDE issues including UDMA write CRC corruption after device termination, SSMI failures during DMA, potential hangs with non-DWORD-aligned PRDs, and PIO failures when the bus master is enabled first; ACPI/PMC problems such as hangs on byte accesses to PM1_STS/PM1_EN and register corruption from WORD/BYTE writes; KEL emulation and Snoop-mode defects; PCI timing (IRDY#/DEVSEL# tVAL) and back-to-back memory read issues; unreliable SSMI generation; nonfunctional wake events from ACPI S3 except PWRBTN#; RTC CMOS RAM read errors; LPC aborts on Long_Sync/Ready_Sync; SMB controller NEGACK behavior; GLPCI retry counting; GPIO High Bank write failures after suspend; short SMBus data hold time; missing LOWBAT_FLAG after abnormal standby; and Sleep_X not deasserting when configured delays exceed the PM_SED delay. The document closes with AMD copyright and disclaimer text.

Stanford University psychology researchers tested whether appetizing vegetable labels influenced college students' food choices. Dishes prepared identically were labeled in four ways: taste-focused, basic, healthy-positive, or healthy-restrictive. Among nearly 28,000 students, taste-focused labels led to 25% more vegetable selections than basic labels, 35% more than healthy-positive labels, and 41% more than healthy-restrictive labels; students also served themselves larger portions. The passage notes only about 10% of American adults and 1% of teens meet daily vegetable recommendations of 2 to 3½ cups. Taste is a major purchase driver—84% per a 2017 IFIC survey versus 63% citing healthfulness—and Campbell's reversed a sodium reduction after poor sales. The author recommends using descriptive names at home and offers recipes including carrot fries, kale chips, corn salad, beet chips, cauliflower fried rice, and green beans with bleu cheese.
Some dogs' irresistible attraction to toys may parallel human behavioral addictions, offering clues to addictive behaviors.

The lecture covers electroweak unification, combining weak and electromagnetic interactions. Two challenges are differing interaction strengths (mitigated by heavy gauge bosons) and differing coupling structures (vector for QED, vector-axial for weak). The 1-γ5 factor is absorbed into spinor definitions as a projection of left-handed components, making the weak current appear vector-like. QED decomposes into left- and right-handed components with no mixed terms, explaining helicity conservation. Using an isospin-like framework, neutrino and electron form a doublet, with charged currents written via tau matrices. The third component yields a neutral current lacking right-handed contributions; a hypercharge current, defined through a Gell-Mann-Nishijima-like relation, includes right-handed particles. Mass eigenstates differ from weak eigenstates, deferred to later discussion. The W1, W2, W3 isospin triplet and hypercharge singlet B are mixed: W± are combinations of W1 and W2, while the photon and Z boson arise from mixing W3 and B via the weak mixing angle θW, with g sin θW = g' cos θW equal to the electromagnetic coupling, yielding a consistent picture with W+, W−, photon, and Z boson.

NASA shared a Hubble image of the spidery Tarantula Nebula and the Honeycomb Nebula, whose bubble-like shape has puzzled astronomers since the early 1990s; 2010 research attributes it to interactions between an older and newer supernova and the viewing angle.

Browns coach Kevin Stefanski said there is no single thing Shedeur Sanders must do to earn the backup quarterback job, emphasizing long-term player development and not placing players in roles before they are ready. Rookie Dillon Gabriel remains the starter, leaving the backup spot open between Sanders and Bailey Zappe. Stefanski's comments imply Sanders is still developing. Jerry Jeudy praised Sanders for being a professional. Sanders will likely remain the emergency third-string quarterback.

Asmodee Digital has released an updated digital version of the classic board game Abalone for iOS and Android. The article offers five tips: don't rush into offense early, plan moves ahead as in chess, control the centre of the board for greater mobility, shift to offense after a defensive start since removing five opponent counters puts a player in a strong position, and split the opponent's counters into smaller groups to push them toward the edge while watching for counter attacks.

This cross-sectional study characterized Alzheimer's disease (AD) plasma biomarkers in 1,067 Amish individuals from Ohio and Indiana. Compared to cognitively unimpaired individuals, those with AD had significantly higher plasma p-tau181 and lower Aβ42/p-tau181 ratio. The association between p-tau181 and AD was significant only among APOE ε4 carriers (OR = 6.02). Elevated Aβ42/Aβ40 was associated with cognitive preservation. Models incorporating all biomarkers or Aβ42/p-tau181 achieved the best discrimination for AD (AUC = 0.83). K-medoids clustering using Aβ42/Aβ40 and p-tau181 identified subgroups with distinct AD risk profiles, with the high-risk cluster containing more APOE ε4 carriers and AD individuals. The study concludes that plasma biomarkers, particularly p-tau181, Aβ42/Aβ40, and Aβ42/p-tau181, are promising non-invasive indicators for distinguishing AD from cognitively unimpaired states in the Amish population.

This address to Congress reports that the nation has grown in strength and peace has become more assured. In foreign relations, the Kellogg-Briand pact, by which fifty-four nations renounced war, has raised a moral standard for peace; the President will sign the protocol adhering to the International Court of Justice and submit it to the Senate. A naval arms limitation conference with Great Britain, France, Italy, and Japan will convene in London. The arms embargo on Mexico was lifted after that government withstood insurrection, and the Tacna-Arica dispute between Chile and Peru was settled. Marines remain in Nicaragua, Haiti, and China, with reductions planned, and the President recommends stronger diplomatic missions to Latin America and larger State Department appropriations.

National defense spending has risen to over $730,000,000 this fiscal year, and the President asks Congress to consider relief from mounting expenditures. Government finances are sound: the public debt stands at $16,931,000,000, and projected surpluses of about $225,000,000 (1930) and $123,000,000 (1931) justify reducing individual income tax rates from 5, 3, and 1½ percent to 4, 2, and ½ percent, and the corporate tax from 12 to 11 percent. Foreign debt settlements are nearly complete, with France's agreement awaiting congressional approval; only Russia and Armenia remain unsettled.

Following the stock market crash, caused by over-optimism and uncontrolled speculation, the President instituted voluntary cooperation with business to maintain wages and employment, reporting that confidence has been reestablished. Agriculture is improving, aided by the newly established Federal Farm Board. The President reaffirms his tariff principles and urges prompt revision with the flexible tariff preserved. Further recommendations include expanded public building programs, increased waterway and flood control funding, postal reforms, railway consolidation legislation, merchant marine development, study of group banking, full-time Federal Power Commission members, a permanent Radio Commission, settlement of Muscle Shoals, and appropriations for Boulder Dam. Conservation concerns include oil permit abuses, overgrazing, and reclamation policy.

Additional recommendations cover continuing the Sheppard-Towner Act, new federal prisons and a Bureau of Prisons, immigration selection based on fitness, consolidating veterans' agencies, extending civil service to third-class postmasters, departmental reorganization, and prohibition enforcement improvements, including transferring detection functions to the Justice Department. A National Commission on Law Observance and Enforcement is studying crime and the judicial system. The address concludes that decisions must be tested by whether they advance the ideals of the American people.

This patent application describes deuterated heterocycle fused gamma-carbolines in free, pharmaceutically acceptable salt, and/or substantially pure form, pharmaceutical compositions thereof, and methods of use in treating diseases involving 5-HT2A receptor, serotonin transporter (SERT), and/or dopamine D/D receptor signaling systems, including anxiety, psychosis, schizophrenia, sleep disorders, depression, and other psychiatric and neurological conditions. The compounds contain a trideuterated N-methyl and/or a di-deuterated methylene adjacent to the N-methyl, which antagonize 5-HT2A receptors, inhibit serotonin re-uptake transporter, and modulate dopaminergic protein phosphorylation similarly to their natural hydrogen analogs but display unexpectedly improved metabolic stability. The invention also provides pharmaceutical compositions including depot formulations using polymeric matrices for sustained or delayed release, and osmotic-controlled release oral delivery systems (OROS). Methods of treatment include administration alone or in combination with other therapeutic agents such as antipsychotics, antidepressants, cholinesterase inhibitors, and NMDA receptor antagonists. Examples demonstrate synthesis of specific deuterated compounds and comparative pharmacokinetic studies in mice, rats, and dogs showing reduced metabolism to amide metabolites compared to non-deuterated congeners.

The passage describes a patent application for an automated cryogenic storage system. The system includes one or more cryogenic storage vaults (maintained at approximately −150°C) connected to a sample handling module (SHM) that enables automated storage, retrieval, and transfer of individual samples between cryogenic environments while keeping samples below a cryogenic temperature threshold (e.g., −134°C, the glass transition temperature of water). Samples are tracked via barcodes, and a controller maintains a database of sample locations and controls transfers, refrigeration, humidity, and disaster recovery.

Each storage vault is a vacuum-insulated Dewar containing storage racks with two interleaved groups of independently rotating shelves driven by external motors. Pie-slice-shaped trays hold up to 260 samples (e.g., 2 ml vials) and are positioned by kinematic pins. A vertical shuttle assembly with a leadscrew lifts trays through a vertical shaft to a vault opening, where a threshold frames the tray to reduce heat and moisture ingress. Refrigeration is provided by liquid nitrogen circulated through primary and secondary coils; a perforated primary coil releases cold, dry gas to control temperature and moisture, with the secondary coil serving as backup.

The SHM contains a sample transfer robot (e.g., a 6-axis robot) with a gripper featuring picking fingers and an extendable insulating sleeve that protects samples during rapid transfers (in some embodiments under 5 seconds) through the SHM's non-cryogenic environment. The gripper also interfaces with the vault cover's locking mechanism. External ports allow docking of portable cryogenic workstations—insulated devices holding samples at −150°C for up to two hours via a liquid nitrogen-filled sponge chamber—which dock at cryodocks through alignment, clamping, seal compression, and movement prevention steps.

The SHM interior is maintained near ambient temperature or below about 5°C, with dew point controlled (e.g., below −50°C) using refrigerant gas flows and a cryo-drying system employing a cryotrap to accelerate dehumidification after maintenance hatch access. The application further describes a four-stage disaster recovery method for jammed trays, a camera module adapted for ultra-low temperature environments, and an alternative star rack design permitting vertical tray removal.

Alex Ovechkin expressed gratitude for receiving an award, thanking his teammates, coaching staff, and family, and described the year as difficult after switching from left wing to right wing mid-season. He credited coach Adam Oates for the position change, saying he trusted him and that the move worked out. He revealed he broke his foot blocking a shot at the World Championship, with an MRI confirming the injury after he returned from Russia, but continued playing because it was the playoffs. He said his foot is now fine and he plans to start playing tennis soon. He stated he never refuses to play if he can skate and hold his stick, crediting Washington's trainers for treating him well throughout the year.

The coach credits the team's puck-pursuit game with wearing down opponents during the playoffs. He praises Sidney Crosby as a complete, hard-working player who wins faceoffs, defends, scores, and inspires the group. He says the team responds well to adversity, with veterans leading, and stresses a message of playing fast and making good puck decisions. Phil Kessel is described as an unemotional, elite scorer whose line's chemistry has produced timely goals. Evgeni Malkin is playing well and generating chances, with a goal expected soon. Conor Sheary was rested because he was wearing down, as quickness is his key advantage, and young players develop through veteran mentorship and learned consistency. Bryan is a game-time decision after skating that morning. The coach highlights the forwards' balance, the Bonino line's two-way play against top opponents, Bryan Rust's speed and confidence, and a defenseman's puck-moving and offensive instincts. He closes by reflecting on patience in player development, gained from his player development coach role.

Former FDA top vaccine regulator Peter Marks has joined Eli Lilly to oversee molecule discovery and infectious diseases, after being forced to resign in March by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. The passage also notes the chemistry Nobel Prize was awarded for metal-organic frameworks, promotes an upcoming STAT event in Boston, and lists other health headlines, including the Texas measles outbreak, a Supreme Court conversion therapy case, and the Trump administration backing off pharma tariffs.

The "Triangle Rotation" offense attacks the triangle zone of the Triangle & Two combination defense, exploiting the weak zone rotations of defenders who are otherwise skilled at pass denial. It uses a three-player clockwise and counter-clockwise rotation, with two shooters used when inside rotations fail to produce a good shot. Basic actions include the Pop Out, Base Cut, Lob Option, and Side Screen. Success depends on execution, coordination, zone-attack fundamentals, and players functioning as one unit. Game strategies include scouting opponents, anticipating defensive reads, varying alignments and entries, and attacking the weakest defenders.

Two U.S. government studies exposed rats and mice to high levels of cellphone radiation and found a small increase in an unusual heart tumor in male rats, but no significant problems in female rats or mice. Regulators and many scientists, including lead author John Bucher, say cellphones remain safe, noting the radiation doses far exceeded typical human use. The FDA stated current safety limits are acceptable. The studies found "equivocal evidence" for DNA damage and brain tumors, though the link to cellphones was unclear. Surprisingly, radiated rats lived longer than unexposed ones. Critics like David Carpenter argue the studies were too small to rule out rare problems. Previous large human studies found little evidence of cancer risk, though a 2011 international working group called cellphones possibly carcinogenic. California has issued guidance on reducing exposure for concerned users.

This study assessed the accuracy and validity of ChatGPT responses in education through a systematic review of 18 empirical, peer-reviewed studies, conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. ChatGPT, developed by OpenAI, evolved from GPT-1 (2018) to GPT-4 (2023) and attracted over a million users within a week of launch. Its use in education has generated both benefits—such as personalized learning, teacher assistance, feedback, and development of critical and creative thinking—and concerns, including plagiarism, cheating, and writing that plagiarism software cannot detect. The reviewed studies, spanning medical education, writing assignments, business, finance, chemistry, academic advising, physics, social science, and coding, showed that ChatGPT produces coherent, well-structured, precise writing and can pass many undergraduate exams, but struggles with complex scientific problems, calculations, and deep understanding. Reported weaknesses include false information delivered confidently, hallucinations, inconsistent answers to identical prompts, and limited higher-order thinking. The author recommends validating ChatGPT responses, using carefully structured text prompts, redesigning assessments, developing institutional guidelines and policies, and training students, and proposes an "ABCD framework" for adoption. The study concludes that ChatGPT demonstrates educational potential but its responses require validation, and suggests cooperation between educational institutions and developers to create education-specific versions.

Michael Johnson has been named president of John Carroll University, the first lay leader in its 131-year history. Johnson, 61, is provost of Babson College; his five-year contract was approved Dec. 6 and begins July 1. He replaces the retiring Rev. Robert Niehoff. Johnson previously spent 24 years at the University of Michigan and 10 years as dean at Cornell. He will also join JCU's faculty and has the endorsement of the Jesuit provincial.

This cross-sectional study assessed the awareness and attitudes of pregnant women toward labor epidural analgesia (LEA) and factors influencing its use at Hemen Medical Center, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia (June–August 2024). Of 267 third-trimester pregnant women sampled, 230 were analyzed. While 78% had heard of LEA, only 6.5% cited healthcare providers as their primary information source, and only 34% received explanations about LEA during antenatal care. Although 47% believed LEA was effective for labor pain relief, only 14.3% were willing to use it, while 47.8% had no plan and 37.8% were undecided. Main concerns included maternal side effects (20%), additional cost (20%), baby's safety (11%), and interference with natural labor (11%). Multivariable logistic regression showed that education level (degree or higher: AOR 1.9), family monthly income above 25,000 ETB, perceived risk of fetal harm (AOR 0.18), and perceived pain-relief effectiveness were significantly associated with the decision to receive LEA. The authors conclude that comprehensive health education and counselling during antenatal care are needed to address misconceptions and promote informed decision-making.

A King's College London study analysing 49 studies with 266,939 participants found that regular physical activity is linked to lower odds of developing depression across all age groups. Researchers plan further studies on activity types and dosages, and hope the evidence leads to policy changes promoting physical activity.

The Four Down offense, also called "Four Low" or "Four Flat," is primarily used for taking the last shot in a period but can also serve as a spread offense for teams with a talented ballhandler. It is signaled visually by the ballhandler pointing four fingers downward. The four non-ballhandlers align along the baseline with the best shooters in the corners, creating open space for one-on-one isolation. Reads include driving or pulling up, drop passes to posts, and kick-outs to shooters. A pressure release adjustment allows corners to pop out for passes and swap roles. Specials include the Mid Screen, Triple Base Screen, and Misdirection Double.

Intercontinental Exchange, parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, is investing $2 billion in cash in prediction market Polymarket at a $9 billion valuation. ICE will distribute Polymarket's data, and the companies will collaborate on tokenization initiatives. Founded in 2020, Polymarket gained prominence during the 2024 U.S. presidential election, with trading volume peaking near $400 million the day after the election before dipping to $40–80 million daily. Competitor Kalshi raised $185 million at a $2 billion valuation.

The 2-3 zone is the most commonly used zone defense, strong at protecting the basket and defending against dribble penetration and poor outside shooting teams, but vulnerable to good outside shooters. It suits teams lacking quickness, athleticism, or skill, though quick, agile players can make it an aggressive trapping defense. The alignment places two guards side by side above the free throw line, a post in front of the basket, and two baseline defenders outside the three-second area, with specific shifts for ball positions in the middle, on the wings, and in the corners. Wing defenders may stay out or drop down on corner passes, and baseline defenders temporarily "show" on reversal passes. A 1-1-3 variation uses a tandem alignment. Trap options include corner, point, and automatic wing traps against star shooters. Against dominant or tall post players ("Footers"), defenders use pass denial positions and triple-team the post whenever it receives the ball.

Zacks Investment Research downgraded Caesars Entertainment Corporation (NASDAQ:CZR) from a buy rating to a hold rating. Other analysts have also recently weighed in: BidaskClub upgraded the stock to buy, ValuEngine upgraded it to hold, and SunTrust Banks, Wolfe Research, and Imperial Capital initiated coverage with buy or outperform ratings and price targets of $14.00, $16.00, and $15.50, respectively. Overall, the stock has one sell rating, three hold ratings, and seven buy ratings, with a consensus price target of $14.39. Shares traded down 0.76% to $13.00, and the company has a market cap of $1.94 billion. The company reported quarterly EPS of ($0.21), missing estimates, with revenue of $1 billion versus an expected $2.11 billion. Several institutional investors recently adjusted their positions, and hedge funds and institutional investors own 76.68% of the stock.

The passage is from the UC1825B-SP datasheet (Texas Instruments, SLUSDD5A, revised December 2020). The sense resistor senses transformer ripple current and shuts down the switching cycle if peak current exceeds the set limit; the CS pin voltage threshold is around 1 V. Test figures show voltage stress across the main switching MOSFETs, output voltage ripple, and full output voltage transient, all tested with 48-V input. The device operates from a 10-V to 30-V input supply, with bulk capacitance (typically a 100-μF tantalum capacitor) recommended if the supply is distant. The controller supports push-pull, forward, half-bridge, and full-bridge topologies. Layout guidance includes using low-EMI ferrite closed-core inductors, routing feedback traces away from noise sources, placing input/output and compensation capacitors close to the IC, keeping power traces short and thick (minimum 15 mils per ampere), arranging switching current loops in the same direction, and using ground planes with a dedicated power ground for high di/dt output-stage currents (each output driver supplies 2-A peak). VCC and VREF require low-ESR/ESL ceramic bypass capacitors. The passage also covers documentation updates, TI E2E support, ESD precautions, mechanical/packaging/orderable information, and TI legal disclaimers.

A forwarded email from Steven Kean to Bernadette Hawkins contains a collection of late-February 2001 news articles on California's energy crisis. A Dow Jones column argues Governor Gray Davis is focusing on utility solvency rather than the state's expected summer electricity shortage, which could exceed 2,000 MW, and urges rate increases to curb demand. An LA Times report says most Western states face similar power shortages and are seeking to renegotiate their power relationships with California, including Utah recalling power from the Intermountain Power Project. Another article reports that construction of small "peaker" plants is stalled because the Department of Water Resources is seeking to revise contracts originally signed by Cal-ISO. A survey found the crisis has damaged small businesses' views of California, with some considering relocating. A news analysis notes Davis has shifted to a more active, campaign-style role after earlier criticism of inactivity. An AP piece counters claims that California hogs electricity, noting its low per-capita consumption and conservation efforts. Reuters reports spot power prices fell as plants returned to service. Finally, lawmakers expressed hesitance over Davis's plan to buy the utilities' transmission lines for about $7.5 billion, questioning its price and prospects for passage.

Community Board 7 of Manhattan brought a CPLR article 78 proceeding against the New York City Department of City Planning under the Freedom of Information Law (FOIL) after being denied access to documents related to the proposed "Trump City" development on the Penn Central railyards, a project subject to the City Charter's Uniform Land Use Review Procedure (ULURP). The Supreme Court granted the petition and the Appellate Division affirmed, finding the board had standing because its request fell within the zone of interest protected by the Charter. The Court of Appeals reversed, holding the board lacked capacity to sue. As a legislatively created entity, a community board has no inherent right to sue; such authority must be express or implied by necessity from its enabling legislation. The Charter contains no express authorization, and the legislative history—including a 1975 study group's recommendation to grant suing power that was not adopted—indicates no intent to confer it. The boards' purely advisory ULURP role, their lack of subpoena power and independent counsel, and the Charter's specific enumeration of documents they may receive further preclude implying such capacity. The Court also held the case was not moot because the issue was likely to recur, typically evades review, and was novel and substantial. The judgment and Appellate Division order were reversed and the petition dismissed.

The passage is from the Texas Instruments ADS9803 datasheet, covering device operation, SPI configuration, registers, and applications. The ADS9803 is powered down via a logic 0 on the PWDN pin or a register write, and must be initialized through a sequence of register writes after power-up or reset, with a free-running sampling clock connected beforehand. A speed-boost mode allows up to 8MSPS sampling of one user-selected analog input channel pair while the remaining channels are idle. The 16-bit configuration registers are grouped into three banks addressed by an 8-bit address, with defined SPI frame procedures for reads and writes; multiple devices can be configured in a daisy-chain topology using the DAISY_CHAIN_LEN register. Various registers control test patterns, averaging, gain error correction, analog input bandwidth, common-mode range, and output data lanes. For ATE applications, the eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS device achieves 0.0015% TUE at 25°C ±5°C after calibration and offers low-noise and wide-bandwidth modes. The device uses three power supplies with no required power-up sequence, and layout guidance recommends decoupling capacitors and keeping analog signals away from noise sources. The document concludes with support resources, ESD caution, revision history, packaging information, and legal disclaimers.

Cboe Global Markets' smooth launch of bitcoin futures, the first on a U.S.-based traditional exchange, could pave the way for other cryptocurrency products such as options and ETFs, according to CEO Ed Tilly. The most-active contract surged 20 percent at one point, triggering a five-minute trading halt, but trading functioned as expected. By early Monday afternoon, nearly 3,700 contracts had traded, with about 20 trading firms participating. Following the launch, three fund managers again sought SEC permission for bitcoin ETFs, which the SEC has so far denied or tabled. Cboe will wait for a couple of futures settlements before introducing new crypto-derivative products. Tilly also expects futures on other cryptocurrencies as demand rises.

This passage is from the datasheet of Texas Instruments' ADS8681W, ADS8685W, and ADS8689W, 16-bit SAR ADC data acquisition devices with an integrated analog front-end and reference.

For external reference operation, setting the INTREF_DIS bit enables an external 4.096V reference applied at the REFIO pin, which is buffered internally to drive the ADC reference. The REFCAP pin requires a minimum 10µF capacitance plus a 1µF high-frequency decoupling capacitor, and the buffer must not drive external loads. Buffer output is stable from –40°C to +125°C, with typical drift of 0.5ppm/°C (maximum 2ppm/°C). The ADC supports single-ended and differential inputs in bipolar and unipolar ranges with straight-binary output; LSB size equals FSR/2¹⁶.

The device provides an active-high ALARM output with two functions: an input alarm using user-programmable high/low thresholds with hysteresis, and an AVDD alarm with fixed thresholds of 4.7V (low) and 5.3V (high). Active and tripped alarm flags reside in ALARM_REG; the active flag clears at the end of each conversion, while the tripped flag clears only upon reading the register. Flags can be read via the ALARM pin, internal registers, or appended to the data output.

The multiSPI digital interface presents the device to the host as a 32-bit input-output shift register. Connection topologies include single-device operation (full multiSPI or standard SPI) and daisy-chain configurations for multiple devices, where optimal frames contain 32×N SCLK edges. The device operates in RESET (application reset or power-on reset via the RST pin), ACQ, and CONV states controlled by the CONVST/CS and RST signals.

Programming uses nine configuration registers. Data transfer frames begin at the falling edge of CONVST/CS; 32-SCLK frames are optimal, short frames are treated as NOP for writes, and long frames use the last 32 bits as the command. Commands include READ, READ_HWORD, WRITE, SET_HWORD, and CLEAR_HWORD. Output words can append device address, range, alarm flags, and parity bits. Read protocols include legacy SPI with single or dual SDO and source-synchronous (SRC) modes with selectable clock source and bus width; dual-SDO operation halves the required clock cycles. Register maps include DEVICE_ID_REG, RST_PWRCTL_REG (write-protected by key 69h), SDI_CTL_REG, SDO_CTL_REG, DATAOUT_CTL_REG, RANGE_SEL_REG, ALARM_REG, ALARM_H_TH_REG, and ALARM_L_TH_REG.

An application example pairs the ADS8681W with the MUX36D08 multiplexer in an eight-channel industrial analog input module supporting standard voltage and current ranges up to ±10V, settling to 1% in under 5µs. The programmable input alarm with hysteresis suits NTC thermistor temperature sensing by preventing false triggering from noise. The device uses AVDD and DVDD supplies with recommended decoupling capacitors, and offers NAP and power-down modes to reduce consumption at low throughput rates. PCB layout guidance covers separating analog and digital sections and proper decoupling of supply and reference pins.

The document concludes with related documentation, support resources, trademark information (multiSPI, TI E2E), ESD handling caution, a revision history noting that Revision A (May 2025) changed ADS8685W and ADS8689W status from Advance Information to Production Data, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information with TI's standard legal disclaimers.

This paper examines digital wellness services for the "young elderly" (ages 60–75) as a proactive approach to Europe's ageing population challenges. The authors argue that existing EU strategies are often visionary but poorly founded in facts and difficult to implement, while technology initiatives tend to remain at the pilot stage. They propose a three-step approach: (1) proactive prevention targeting the young elderly so they remain healthy, active, and independent upon reaching 75+; (2) intervention tools via mobile smartphone applications; and (3) commercially viable ecosystems to sustain ICT-based tools, since research projects alone cannot maintain services.

The young elderly represent 18–23% of the population in most EU countries—approximately 97 million citizens by 2020. Wellness services were chosen because they avoid dependence on strictly regulated health and social care data. Functional impairment is described as multi-dimensional, compensatory, and non-static, and wellness is operationalized in four dimensions—intellectual, physical, social, and emotional—that mirror impairment dimensions and can compensate for one another.

The BeWell research program (Finland, 2014–16), driven by Tieto Group with 10 additional companies and 4 research partners, develops digital wellness services as interventions to build wellness routines. The technical infrastructure combines the Wellmo omnivore platform, which interacts with 100+ devices and applications and tracks steps, sleep, exercise, weight, and habits, with the Tieto cloud services platform for advanced analytics. Standard fitness devices are noted as designed for active users rather than the young elderly. Services should be designed "with the users, not for the users" using multi-disciplinary action design research (ADR).

An empirical survey of 101 young elderly respondents in the Åland Islands (26.6% response rate from 380 invited) found that about 73% use smartphones and that respondents rated mobile apps as useful and easy to adopt. Wellness issues, particularly intellectual challenges, were rated as important. Statistical analyses (ANOVA, Fisher's test, Cronbach's alpha, Mann-Whitney U) revealed significant differences by education, age, gender, income, and employment status; better-educated respondents were more positive toward mobile applications and their physical health prospects.

Addressing four research questions, the paper concludes that the ageing population makes sustaining wellness routines necessary, with digital business providing the tools and environment; young elderly rate wellness as important and have sufficient smartphone proficiency; service design should be co-created with users on omnivore platforms; and commercial ecosystems are required for sustainability. If scaled to millions of users, such services could reduce EU health and social care costs by tens of billions of Euro annually.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on April 26, 2018, announcing its first quarter 2018 financial results. The filing includes a press release (Exhibit 99.1) and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures (Exhibit 99.2). The report was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Chicago Blackhawks players Patrick Kane, Brent Seabrook, and Bryan Bickell discussed their Stanley Cup Final series against Boston in a post-game interview. Seabrook scored the overtime winner that evened the series, which he attributed simply to shooting the puck rather than any special ability. Kane noted every game has been close, with the series now a best-of-three including two games in Chicago. Bickell emphasized his physical role, including hits on a big-bodied Boston defenseman, saying opening ice for linemates and creating second chances in front of goalie Rask were key. The players praised the team's depth, citing contributions from players like Krüger. Seabrook said he had encouraged Jonathan Toews to focus on scoring, and advised Nick Leddy to keep working after a coaching decision. Kane said goalie Crawford was not a concern despite tough breaks, and Seabrook stressed the team must improve defensively, noting they cannot expect to score six goals every night.

This study examined the spatiotemporal evolution of SARS-CoV-2 Alpha and Delta variants in Vietnam during 2021 using whole genome sequencing of 1,303 samples collected at two tertiary referral hospitals. Vietnam had successfully controlled COVID-19 in 2020 through border restrictions, contact tracing, and mass testing, but importations of the Alpha variant followed by the Delta variant in early 2021 led to a large nationwide outbreak with over 1.7 million infections and 32,000 deaths by year's end. Phylogenetic analysis showed multiple introductions of the Alpha variant between January and May 2021, resulting in only sporadic clusters without sustained community transmission, likely due to rigorous containment measures. The Delta variant AY.57 lineage dominated (99.2% of Delta sequences), with a most recent common ancestor estimated at March 14, 2021. Phylogeographic analysis revealed the virus was first introduced into the Northeast region, with the southeastern region later becoming the main source seeding virus to other areas. Despite the nationwide outbreak, viral dispersal between provinces was infrequent, likely influenced by strict lockdowns and travel restrictions. Genetic diversity increased sharply between April and August 2021, coinciding with the outbreak in a largely unvaccinated population. The study highlights the importance of genomic surveillance in informing pandemic responses.

JPMorgan Chase & Co. reduced its stake in DeVry Education Group (NYSE:DV) by 9.6% in the third quarter, holding 499,104 shares worth $11,509,000 after selling 53,234 shares. Other institutional investors adjusted positions, including UBS Asset Management Americas (+10.6%), M&T Bank Corp (new position), PNC Financial Services (+637.7%), Retirement Systems of Alabama (+0.4%), and KBC Group NV (+82.6%). Analysts hold a consensus "Hold" rating with an average price target of $26.11. Major shareholder Value Advisers International sold 3,272 shares in November.

FreeNAS version 11 has been released after version 10 was demoted to tech preview due to bugs. Based on FreeBSD 11-STABLE, it includes the bhyve hypervisor, FreeBSD jails, AWS S3 compatibility, Slack/HipChat integration, and a beta Angular GUI. Docker support is deferred. Testers found little to complain about.

This systematic review, registered on PROSPERO, examined the relationship between marijuana/cannabinoid use and the microbiome. Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane were searched for English-language, peer-reviewed human studies up to July 20, 2022; animal and in vitro studies were excluded. Of 4,022 identified articles, 9 studies (1 case-control, 6 cohorts, 2 clinical trials) with 2,526 participants from the USA, Iran, Israel, and the UK were included. Participants were predominantly female (>85%), with patients averaging 56.5 years of age. Risk of bias was assessed using the NOS and ROBINS-I tools. Findings indicated associations between marijuana use and microbiota changes across conditions: in HIV patients, use correlated with increased Fusobacterium and Anaerotruncus and decreased Dorea; endocannabinoids (AEA, PEA) were linked to increased butyrate and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6); OEA supplementation reduced energy intake and increased A. muciniphila in obesity; and marijuana use was associated with altered oral microbiota, mitochondrial dysfunction, and a lower Prevotella:Bacteroides ratio in cognitive deficits. Reported adverse events included coughing, wheezing, and drowsiness. Meta-analysis could not be conducted due to limited and heterogeneous data, and further research was recommended.

Chinese textile firms are increasingly outsourcing production to North Korean factories to take advantage of cheaper labor, with garments labeled "Made in China" and exported worldwide. UN sanctions punishing North Korea's nuclear and missile programs do not ban textile exports, which totaled $752 million in 2016, making them the country's second-biggest export after coal and minerals. Agents in Dandong, the main border trading city, connect Chinese suppliers with buyers from the United States, Europe, Japan, South Korea, Canada and Russia, sometimes without final buyers knowing the clothes were made in North Korea. Manufacturers can save up to 75 percent by producing there. North Korea has about 15 large state-owned garment exporting enterprises, and traders say workers produce 30 percent more per day than Chinese workers at far lower wages. Chinese exports to North Korea rose nearly 30 percent to $1.67 billion in the first half of the year, largely driven by textile materials. Chinese firms also employ thousands of North Korean workers in China, earning about half of Chinese wages, with most pay remitted to the state, which the UN says helps fund Pyongyang's weapons programs. New UN sanctions ban increasing the number of North Korean laborers working abroad.

Glenner Town Square, a new daycare program in Chula Vista for Alzheimer's and dementia patients, is an 8,500-square-foot, three-dimensional 1950s-style downtown with 13 storefronts offering interactive experiences designed to spark visitors' long-term memories. Opened in April 2018 at 2678 Main St., it features a cinema, diner, library, boutique, auto shop, pet store, and hospital. Glenner also operates adult day-care centers in Hillcrest and Encinitas that will eventually become Town Square projects. The passage additionally lists other licensed adult day programs for the cognitively impaired in San Diego County, including Clairemont Villa, College Avenue Older Adult Center, George G. Glenner centers, Hope, Loving Care, Neighborhood House Association, and St. Paul in Central San Diego, as well as AltaGolden, Americare, Fallbrook, and Glenner's Encinitas center in North County, with details on services, hours, locations, fees, and contact information.

Ostersunds were drawn against Arsenal in the Europa League last 32. Under Graham Potter the Swedish club won three promotions since 2011, qualifying via the domestic cup. Champions League dropouts Borussia Dortmund, Atletico Madrid, Celtic and Napoli face Atalanta, Copenhagen, Zenit and RB Leipzig.

The passage is a State of the Union address reporting that America has improved through bipartisan cooperation, citing economic recovery marked by inflation falling from 12.4 to 3.2 percent, a nearly halved prime rate, across-the-board tax cuts, and four million new jobs in 1983. The speaker proposes four goals: steady economic growth, developing America's next frontier, strengthening traditional values, and building a meaningful peace. Specific proposals include a bipartisan plan to reduce deficits by roughly $100 billion over three years, a constitutional line-item veto and balanced budget amendment, and simplification of the tax code. The speaker directs NASA to develop a permanently manned space station within a decade and supports private sector launch services. Additional measures address environmental protection, education reform, school prayer, crime reduction, and enterprise zones. On foreign policy, the address covers Soviet relations, nuclear arms reduction, Lebanon peacekeeping, and combating terrorism. It concludes by honoring individuals such as Sergeant Stephen Trujillo for heroism in Grenada and expressing confidence in America's future.

A hockey player, in the finals for the third time with three different teams, says he wants to win the trophy this time after past losses. Having signed as a free agent in Chicago, he credits hard work for reaching the finals, notes enthusiastic fan support in the city, and expects a tight series against an experienced Flyers team.

The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate to 1 to 1.25 percent, its third consecutive quarterly increase, citing strong job growth. The Fed acknowledged weakened inflation, lowering this year's inflation forecast to 1.6 percent from 1.9 percent, and some officials predict unemployment could fall below 4 percent.

Ben Rice, who split time between first base, catcher and designated hitter for the Yankees, was born and raised in Cohasset, Massachusetts, and grew up a Yankees fan with Derek Jeter as his favorite player despite his Boston-area roots. He played hockey before focusing on baseball at Noble and Greenough School in Dedham, then attended Dartmouth, where pandemic cancellations limited him to 110 collegiate plate appearances. The Yankees selected him in the 12th round of the 2021 MLB Draft. After an inconsistent 2024 rookie season filling in for Anthony Rizzo, Rice hit 26 home runs over 138 games in 2025 and homered in the Wild Card Series against the Red Sox.

This study developed a mathematical model, based on the SIR framework, to evaluate the effectiveness of a screening-isolation strategy for controlling infectious diseases in semi-isolated communities when vaccines and medications are unavailable. Theoretical analysis showed that successful disease control requires the screening time lag to remain below a constraint dependent on screening efficiency and transmission parameters, while improving screening efficiency contributed only weakly to robustness. Computer simulations demonstrated that daily screening with efficiency η=0.9 controlled infections at R0=3.0 and R0=6.0, but failed at R0=8.0. Screening every 3 days controlled disease spread, weekly screening was substantially less effective, and biweekly screening failed regardless of efficiency. Higher screening efficiency significantly reduced cumulative infections (142.76 versus 267.46 cases per year at 3-day intervals). Infection sizes increased proportionally with external influx, supporting the necessity of strict border control. The study concludes that regular, periodic community-wide screening can control epidemic transmission in semi-isolated communities, with screening frequency, efficiency, and migration rate influencing infection size. PCR-based tests were identified as good candidates for future community-wide screening.

Tom Brady's agent Don Yee says the 40-year-old quarterback intends to return to the Patriots in 2018 and play into his mid-40s, despite missing voluntary offseason workouts amid retirement rumors. Brady has two seasons left on his contract, and owner Robert Kraft said there is no issue with the current deal.

CoreWeave's stock has rebounded on strong AI sentiment and major deal wins, including $22.4B from OpenAI and $14.2B from Meta, diversifying its customer base. However, Microsoft remains a significant revenue concentration risk, and the company's debt-funded growth and high forward revenue multiple raise sustainability concerns. Joppatowne High School held its 45th commencement ceremony Wednesday at the APG Federal Credit Union Arena at Harford Community College, where more than 130 seniors received diplomas. About 95 percent of the 138-member class will attend college, technical school, the military, or law enforcement, according to Principal Pamela Zeigler. Graduate Amya Hill, 17, plans to study nursing at Albany State University in Georgia, while Zachary Wagmun, 17, will enter an electrician's apprenticeship program at Harford Community College. Valedictorian Kacey Lebrun and class president Breea Stevenson addressed the seniors, with Stevenson sharing three life lessons, including focusing on the present in light of recent mass shootings. Other speakers included state Sen. Robert Cassilly, who cited fallen officer Amy Caprio and Sgt. Eddison Hermond as examples of sacrifice.

A hockey coach declines to analyze the previous night's game with the media, saying he will do so with his team. He notes some players stretched after a five-hour flight to improve circulation. He states the pressure is on Calgary, with all of Canada expecting them to win and the cup in the building, while his team's only goal is to extend the series. MultiChoice CEO Calvo Mawela expressed concern over Netflix's "unfair advantage" as DStv Premium subscribers fell by 41,000 to 1.921m despite overall growth to 13.476m, reducing average revenue per customer from R353 to R344 monthly. The company plans a standalone streaming service, having secured rights for all channels in late 2018, and has asked ICASA not to over-regulate, warning of job losses to streaming giants.

A letter taped to the door of fired assistant U.S. attorney Michael Ben'Ary said a false social media post apparently led to his termination while he was prosecuting the 2021 Afghanistan airport bombing that killed 13 U.S. service members. The letter said he was fired after commentator Julie Kelly suggested he was an ally of former Deputy Attorney General Lisa Monaco, and accused DOJ leadership of prioritizing punishment of the president's perceived enemies over national security.

Over-the-counter (OTC) trading involves direct transactions between two parties through decentralized electronic marketplaces, without exchange supervision. OTC markets handle stocks, bonds, derivatives, and commodities, typically for small companies unable to meet exchange listing requirements, though foreign stocks via American Depository Receipts also trade there. OTC markets are less transparent and less strictly regulated than exchanges, carrying counterparty risk, fraud (such as pump-and-dump schemes), and lower liquidity. In the US, over 12,000 securities trade OTC through networks managed by OTC Markets Group and regulated by FINRA. OTC stocks, particularly penny stocks, perform poorly: over 90% fail, with one study showing an average loss of 27% and a median loss of 37%. The article concludes OTC stocks are unsuitable for long-term investment or short-term trading due to slippage and unfavorable odds. Cryptocurrency trading mostly occurs on exchanges, though OTC desks facilitate large off-market deals.

This manuscript uses exact diagonalization of a continuum model to study the half-filled second moiré bands (hole filling νh = 3) of approximately 2°-twisted bilayer MoTe2, incorporating both valleys and screened Coulomb interactions. As the intervalley screening length d is tuned, the system evolves from a ferromagnetic Chern insulator (d < dc,1 ≈ 0.15 aM) to a non-Abelian fractional spin Hall insulator (d > dc,2 ≈ 0.33 aM), with an intermediate phase between the two transition points. The intermediate phase is identified as an intervalley superconductor based on several signatures: a paramagnetic ground state at zero momentum, enhanced intervalley entanglement, negative Cooper-pair binding energy, a dominant eigenvalue in the pair density matrix, and finite superfluid stiffness. The pairing symmetry is time-reversal symmetric, extended nodal s-wave. The superconducting state is continuously connected to the fractional spin Hall insulator at dc,2, resembling the transition from bilayer Pfaffian fractional quantum Hall states to an exciton condensate, and the authors develop a Chern-Simons-based field theory for this transition in which topology and symmetry change simultaneously. Replacing the second moiré bands with first Landau levels weakens the superconductivity, indicating that realistic band geometry and non-uniform quantum geometry stabilize the phase. The authors suggest the superconducting phase may be experimentally reachable by tuning the screening length through gating or substrate engineering.

OptumCare offers "Brainsaver" classes in the Valley as part of a 12-week course focusing on brain-healthy activities such as physical exercise, stress reduction, cognitive exercises, educational material, socialization, and brain-healthy foods, a combination believed to keep Alzheimer's at bay. Students range from their mid-50s to late 80s, and classes are held at three locations: Deer Valley, Goodyear, and Chandler.

A federal government shutdown appeared more likely after President Trump met with top congressional leaders at the White House, less than two days before the September 30 funding deadline. Vice President JD Vance blamed Democrats, saying "we're headed to a shutdown because the Democrats won't do the right thing." Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer cited "very large differences" but said Trump heard Democrats' objections "for the first time." Republicans want a stopgap bill funding the government until late November, while Democrats demand it include an extension of enhanced Obamacare tax credits set to lapse at year's end. Moina Shaiq, a Muslim mother in Fremont, California, launched her "Meet a Muslim" program after placing a newspaper ad inviting questions about Islam; about 100 people attended her first coffee house session. She now gives talks once or twice a week at libraries, restaurants, churches, and other venues, and has traveled to Arizona and Atlanta, aiming to dispel misconceptions and stereotypes about her faith. Similar programs emerged after 9/11 and have resurged amid a rise in anti-Muslim incidents, including arson, harassment, and a fatal attack in Portland. Shaiq has faced threats herself, including one in Atlanta. Supporters view such initiatives as valuable amid heightened xenophobia, while critics argue the focus should instead be on policy change.

Tensor Cores are specialized execution units for deep learning matrix operations. Turing Tensor Cores add INT8/INT4 precision for inferencing, bring AI capabilities to GeForce and Quadro products, and power DLSS for high-quality image rendering.

This patent application, a continuation of several prior U.S. and international applications, relates to wireless communication systems and proposes a method for transmitting/receiving a sounding reference signal (SRS), specifically for setting and/or indicating a guard period for SRS transmission/reception considering SRS and other uplink transmissions such as PUCCH or PUSCH.

In an embodiment, a UE receives from a base station configuration information including one or more SRS resources and information on their usage, and transmits SRS using those resources. A guard period related to the SRS resources is configured; when it overlaps with a specific uplink channel, the priority between the guard period and the channel is identically configured to the priority between the SRS and the channel. The guard period may be configured for antenna switching, may consist of one or two symbols determined by subcarrier spacing, and may be configured per SRS resource set via higher layer signaling, including a starting position index, the number of symbols, and whether it is configured between SRS and an adjacent uplink channel. When no guard period is configured, the UE performs uplink transmissions before and after it using the same transmission beam, indicated by an SRS resource indicator (SRI) and/or transmit precoder matrix indicator (TPMI). Corresponding UE and base station apparatus embodiments are described.

A first embodiment describes configuring guard periods (Y symbols) between PUSCH/PUCCH and SRS via higher layer signaling, MAC-CE, or DCI, with methods for handling collisions with PUCCH (applying priority rules or dropping) and PUSCH (puncturing, rate matching, or symbol shifting). A second embodiment addresses collisions between guard periods and SRS resource sets using priority rules, dropping lower-priority resources or groups, or shifting transmission to a later slot. These methods reduce performance deterioration from antenna switching distortion during uplink transmission.

Zsolt Lakatos, 31, who was sentenced in his absence to 13 years for wounding with intent after shaking his four-month-old son, was arrested after hiding at a Litherland address for eight days. Cover 0 is a man-to-man football coverage with no safeties providing help over the top, allowing defenses to send maximum blitz pressure (typically 6 rushers) while ensuring every eligible receiver is covered. Its strengths include clear, simple assignments, easy adjustment to offensive motion, effectiveness against the run, Run-Pass Options, short routes, and deep routes due to the pressure generated. It can also be disguised as Cover 4 pre-snap. However, it is high-risk: beaten defenders have no help, making it vulnerable to deep passes, draw plays, quarterback scrambles, and pick plays like the mesh concept. The middle of the field is left open—Al Davis famously forbade Raiders coordinators from running it. Typical assignments include corners on the X and Z receivers, safeties on the tight end and slot, and linebackers blitzing through the gaps. Variations include Cover 0 "Rat," where only five rush and one defender patrols the middle against crossing routes and scrambles, and dropping hybrid defensive linemen into coverage.

This study identifies key dimensions of holistic education within the Indian higher education context. Noting that contemporary education emphasizes material achievement, the authors draw on Indian sages-thinkers—Tagore, Osho, Vivekananda, and Sri Aurobindo—who advocated integrating spiritual and material development, aligning with modern initiatives such as India's NEP 2020, UN SDG 4.7, and the ISEE Assessment. Using a comprehensive literature review followed by a PRISMA-guided systematic review of Scopus and Semantic Scholar databases (472 articles screened down to 8), the study examined Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) frameworks. Five globally relevant frameworks were identified, but the identity and perspectives domains remained underrepresented, prompting the culturally grounded Indian LIBRE/EMC2 framework. Thematic analysis validated four LIBRE dimensions—empathy, mindfulness, compassion, and critical inquiry—as recurring elements in holistic education literature, alongside foundational themes emphasizing whole-person development, global competence, institutional clarity, and lifelong learning. These dimensions align with the sages' philosophies and current policy frameworks, and classroom-level assessment can inform institutional practices and policy through iterative feedback. The authors conclude that the findings support the LIBRE model's application in Indian higher education and enable development of culturally grounded assessment tools, while noting limitations including reliance on two databases and exclusion of non-indexed sources.

The asteroid Oumuamua, the first confirmed interstellar object found in our solar system, likely came from a binary star system, according to the University of Toronto's Alan Jackson. Discovered in October by a Hawaiian observatory, the cigar-shaped, red-tinged rock is about 1,300 feet long and moving away at over 16 miles per second. Researchers believe it was ejected as planets formed and is tumbling from a past collision; once thought a comet, it is now considered an asteroid.

Soybean May futures closed higher as supplies diminished while crushing demand stayed intact on encouraging soy meal exports. April arrivals fell to 97,040 tonnes from March's 1,64,286 tonnes. Prices are expected to trade higher on crusher demand.

A University of Maryland study found that young adults who regularly consumed highly caffeinated energy drinks over time were significantly more likely to use cocaine, non-medically use prescription stimulants, and be at risk for alcohol use disorder at age 25. Of 1,099 participants, 51.4% showed persistent consumption. Those who never consumed or stopped consuming energy drinks showed no increased risk. The study was published in Drug and Alcohol Dependence.

President Woodrow Wilson proclaimed on April 6, 1917, that a state of war exists between the United States and the Imperial German Government, following a joint resolution of Congress. Citing Sections 4067–4070 of the Revised Statutes, he directed that German males aged fourteen and older within the United States who are not naturalized are deemed alien enemies. Such aliens must preserve the peace, refrain from criminal acts and from aiding the enemy, and comply with presidential regulations; those who do so will be left undisturbed and treated with friendliness, while violators face restraint, security requirements, or removal. Wilson established twelve regulations prohibiting alien enemies from possessing weapons, explosives, aircraft, wireless devices, or codes; restricting their presence near military and munitions sites; barring attacks or threats against the government; designating prohibited residence areas; requiring permits for departure and entry; mandating registration if necessary; and authorizing summary arrest and detention of violators. The proclamation applies to all land and water within U.S. jurisdiction.

Consumer advocates reported glitches in the final days of Obamacare sign-ups, though the Trump administration largely delivered a smooth enrollment experience. Some Illinois consumers who completed financial assistance applications received an incorrect message saying no plans were available in their area, despite every county having at least one insurer. Hurricane-affected residents can enroll until Dec. 31. An estimated 9-10 million people have marketplace coverage, and many subsidy-eligible consumers may pay lower 2018 premiums. The Washington Nationals signed veteran Jeremy Hellickson to a minor league contract, adding him to the competition for the fifth starter spot alongside A.J. Cole and Erick Fedde. Hellickson would receive a $2 million one-year deal if added to the 40-man roster, plus up to $4 million in performance bonuses. He may remain at spring training to build arm strength, and his contract includes a later-than-usual opt-out clause. Manager Dave Martinez announced Max Scherzer as the opening day starter, followed by Stephen Strasburg, Gio Gonzalez, and Tanner Roark. Cole is expected to make the team regardless.
