The Economist's "Carrie Bradshaw index" ranks US cities by affordability for single renters, based on the salary needed to rent a studio without spending over 30% of gross income. A score above one means most people can afford a studio; 59 cities scored above one, down from 62 last year. New York remains the most unaffordable for the third year, with Boston, Charleston, and Jersey City also among the least affordable. Coastal cities are least affordable, while Sun Belt and Midwestern cities are more livable.

A review of Jaime Smith's new how-to book for prospective college transfer students praises it as clearly written, logically organized, and full of case studies covering students with military backgrounds, financial issues, disabilities, and weak high school records. Aimed at community college students seeking to transfer to four-year institutions, the book offers practical tips: keeping syllabi copies, taking a W rather than an F, prioritizing fit over prestige, researching housing costs, and understanding that admission to a major differs from admission to an institution. The reviewer adds that local transfer advisers can provide nuances websites miss, such as articulation agreements and transfer scholarships, and objects to Smith's vague answer on finishing an associate degree before transferring, noting that completed degrees often protect against credit loss. Overall, the book is judged accessible, useful, and practical.

Martin Brodeur discussed his team's playoff win after playing well in previous games without results. The team chose not to change its approach, believing their playoff strategy was working. Brodeur noted they were fortunate to get bounces, including shots hitting the post and crossbar, and said scoring first was a goal. He praised a young player's growth, skating, puck handling, and ability to score important goals. He stated he focuses only on winning for his team, criticized a penalty call on Clarkson, and highlighted the team's composure and their first zone-entry pass of the series, which led to a goal.

This study examined trends and risk factors for early sex resumption (ESR, resuming sex within 42 days) after voluntary medical male circumcision (VMMC) among men aged 15–49 in Rakai, Uganda, using four rounds of the Rakai Community Cohort Study (2013–2020). ESR prevalence declined from 45.1% in 2013/2015 to 14.9% in 2018/2020. In multivariate analysis, ESR was consistently higher among currently married men, men with multiple sexual partners (significant in 2016/2018), and men with primary education (significant in 2018/2020); occupation and HIV status were not associated with ESR across survey rounds. The decline may reflect strengthened post-VMMC counseling beginning in 2016, though prevalence remained above the WHO-recommended target. The authors suggest involving female partners and targeting counseling toward married men, men with multiple partners, and men with lower education to further reduce ESR. Limitations include reliance on self-reported data and inability to determine HIV status at the time of circumcision.

CVS Health's stock fell 23.4% between late August and early November, which the author attributes to two events: Walgreens' 2016 agreement with Prime Therapeutics and CVS's removal from the Tricare network. This study tested the safety and efficacy of mifepristone, a glucocorticoid receptor antagonist, in individuals with alcohol use disorder (AUD). Building on preclinical findings that mifepristone reduced yohimbine-induced reinstatement of alcohol-seeking in alcohol-dependent rats, the authors conducted a Phase 1/2, outpatient, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, cross-over human laboratory study at Brown University (2014–2021). Thirty-two non-abstinent individuals with AUD not seeking treatment were randomized to 7 days of oral mifepristone (600 mg/day) or placebo, with a 3-week washout before crossover. Laboratory sessions involved yohimbine (32.4 mg) administration paired with a cue-reactivity procedure, a priming alcohol dose, and alcohol self-administration in an open bar.

The primary outcome, safety, showed no serious adverse events when mifepristone was co-administered with yohimbine and alcohol; mifepristone did not alter alcohol pharmacokinetics or subjective alcohol effects. Secondary outcomes showed mifepristone reduced self-reported alcohol craving (ACQ and AUQ) at the first alcohol cue trial and reduced cue-elicited salivary output in both trials. Mifepristone increased cortisol, supporting medication compliance, but mediation analysis showed cortisol did not mediate the craving reductions. Family history density of alcoholism (FHDA) moderated effects: mifepristone reduced craving only in participants with low FHDA, while salivary output decreased and cortisol increased in both FHDA groups. Alcohol consumption did not differ between conditions in the laboratory or outpatient settings.

The authors conclude that mifepristone is safe when combined with alcohol and may reduce stress-induced craving, particularly in individuals with low family history of AUD, consistent with findings in msP rats. Limitations include the absence of a yohimbine placebo control, no mifepristone blood level measurements, and low female enrollment. Higher-dose studies are warranted to identify response biomarkers and potential responders.

Ronald E. Gabler was convicted of aggravated assault for attacking Thomas R. Duff on January 3, 1984, after following his estranged wife to Duff's home. The court reviewed the evidence in the light most favorable to the jury's verdict and found it sufficient to support the conviction. On appeal, Gabler's sole claim was that his trial counsel was ineffective for failing to investigate Duff's injuries by interviewing physicians and gathering medical reports, and for failing to object to testimony that placed his character in issue. Applying the two-prong Strickland test, the court found counsel's decisions regarding the medical evidence constituted trial strategy, and that Gabler failed to show deficient performance or a reasonable probability the outcome would have differed. The court also found no merit in the character-evidence claim, noting Gabler himself placed his character in issue and insisted, against counsel's advice, on calling a character witness who was then cross-examined about counseling Mary Gabler regarding abuse. The denial of Gabler's amended motion for new trial was affirmed.

Apple Inc.'s Form 10-K annual report for the fiscal year ended September 25, 2021, describes the company's design, manufacture and marketing of smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories, along with related services. During fiscal 2021, Apple released the iPhone 13 series, redesigned MacBook Pro models with M1 Pro or M1 Max chips, updated iPads, third-generation AirPods, and Apple Watch Series 7. Risk factors include COVID-19-related supply disruptions and store closures, macroeconomic conditions, U.S.-China tariffs, reliance on single or limited-source components amid global semiconductor shortages, dependence on outsourcing partners primarily in Asia, intense competition, App Store regulatory scrutiny (including the proposed EU Digital Markets Act), data privacy laws, foreign currency exposure, credit risk, and potential tax rate changes.

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture by Professor Hong Liu (8.323, Lecture 26, May 12, 2023) concludes the treatment of tree-level QED diagrams and introduces loop diagrams, which represent quantum fluctuations. Tree-level diagrams involve no momentum integration since all internal momenta are determined by external ones. Three basic one-loop diagrams are presented: correction to the electron propagator (electron emitting and reabsorbing a virtual photon), correction to the photon propagator (virtual electron-positron pair creation and annihilation), and vertex correction.

Loop diagrams require integration over unconstrained internal momenta from minus to plus infinity, producing divergences that cannot be removed by simple subtraction or division. These divergences arise from naively extrapolating QED to arbitrarily high energies (short distances), where its validity is unknown. In the late 1940s, Schwinger, Feynman, and Tomonaga developed renormalization to remove divergences and obtain sensible results; Freeman Dyson later simplified their work and spread Feynman diagram techniques. Ken Wilson's renormalization group (late 1960s/1970s) eventually provided the physical understanding.

Including loops introduces vacuum fluctuations and shows that physical mass, charge, and fields differ from the bare parameters in the Lagrangian. The electron propagator correction shifts the mass and changes the residue (Z); the photon remains massless due to gauge invariance, though its field is renormalized by Z3; the vertex correction renormalizes the charge by the same Z3 factor, preserving the covariant derivative and gauge symmetry, and also generates an anomalous magnetic moment.

The lecture derives that the Dirac equation predicts g = 2 through its nonrelativistic limit (the Pauli equation). Schwinger's 1948 calculation of the vertex correction yielded g = 1 + alpha/(2pi), agreeing well with experiment. Higher-order corrections (involving 7, 72, and 891 diagrams) were computed later; the anomalous magnetic moment is among the most precisely measured quantities in physics (to order 10^-12), confirming QED's accuracy.

TMPM's PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST command migrates up to 128 pages via a Page Migration List. Pages need not be adjacent, multiple guests may be referenced, and no order-dependence exists between entries or commands. Page Migration Status Entries provide per-page results: PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS requires checking individual statuses, PM_SUCCESS means all pages migrated, and other codes mean none executed. PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE permits retry.

This study defined the transcriptomic profile of granulomatous myositis (GM), a form of inflammatory myopathy characterized histologically by non-caseating granulomas in muscle. Using bulk RNA sequencing of 38 GM muscle biopsies collected from multiple international centers, researchers compared gene expression with other inflammatory myopathies (dermatomyositis, antisynthetase syndrome, immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy, and inclusion body myositis), disease controls, and healthy controls.

GM biopsies showed marked upregulation of IFNγ and IFNγ-inducible genes, elevated T-cell, B-cell, plasma cell, and macrophage markers, and increased expression of proinflammatory cytokines including IL1B, TNF, and TGFB1. Analysis identified 1,293 genes specifically upregulated and 256 genes specifically downregulated in GM, predominantly expressed by macrophages within granulomas. CHIT1 was the most significantly overexpressed gene, confirmed at the protein level in granulomas and giant cells. Spatial transcriptomics confirmed key findings localized to granulomas.

The gene set strongly correlated with disease activity markers. A support vector machine model achieved 99.6% AUC and 98.6% accuracy in classifying GM, suggesting minimally invasive needle biopsies may suffice for diagnosis. Identified pathways overlap with those in sarcoidosis, suggesting potential therapeutic strategies. Limitations include exclusion of infectious or genetic granulomatous diseases and RNA-level-only validation for most markers.

Wilson sold shares in two separate transactions during July and August.

This study compared REM sleep microstructure among patients with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD), RBD associated with Parkinson's disease (PD+RBD), and controls using video-polysomnography. Results showed increased phasic REM sleep proportion in iRBD patients, and reduced sawtooth wave (STW) density and duration in PD+RBD patients. Both patient groups exhibited altered STW spectral characteristics with a shift toward higher frequencies. A gradient was observed in NREM/REM sleep transition durations, increasing from controls to iRBD patients and peaking in PD+RBD patients. Additionally, "STW-first" event sequences predominated in patient groups, while "atonia-first" sequences predominated in controls. These findings indicate that REM sleep anomalies in RBD extend beyond atonia loss and dream enactment, encompassing broader microstructural changes that may serve as biomarkers of phenoconversion in α-synucleinopathies.

Elina Svitolina of Ukraine won her fifth title of 2017 at the Rogers Cup in Toronto, defeating Caroline Wozniacki 6-4, 6-0 in the final. The 22-year-old beat four top-ten opponents during the week, including two former world number ones, and dropped only one set across five matches. The victory was her second Premier final win over Wozniacki in 2017, after Dubai, and made her the first woman to win three Premier 5 titles in a single season. Despite fatigue from playing three matches in 30 hours, Svitolina credited her fighting spirit and mental strength. Now ranked number four in the world and 5-0 in finals this year, she is focused on preparing for the US Open, saying she has her own goals and does not concern herself with external expectations.

The N.C. Wildlife Resources Commission is accepting public comments through April 8 on 2018-19 migratory game bird hunting seasons, with dates to be set April 26. Changes include compensatory days for waterfowl and webless species, a dove season closing extension to Jan. 31, discontinuation of the Southern James Bay Population Canada goose zone, and new brant frameworks, with feedback sought on a reduced brant season.

In this MIT 6.832 Underactuated Robotics lecture, Russ Tedrake recaps the previous lecture on the double integrator system (q̈ = u), covering pole placement design and minimum-time optimal control with bounded input, which yielded bang-bang control with a nonlinear switching surface. He reviews Pontryagin's minimum principle, which uses Lagrange multipliers to verify local optimality along a trajectory. The main new material introduces dynamic programming: starting from discrete-time recursive cost formulations and the principle of optimality, he derives the continuous-time Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation and states its sufficiency theorem. Applying the HJB framework to a linear system with quadratic cost yields the Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR): guessing a quadratic value function leads to the Riccati equation with terminal condition S(T) = Qf, whose solution gives the optimal feedback u = −R⁻¹BᵀSx. The infinite-horizon solution is the steady-state of the Riccati equation, as computed by Matlab's lqr function. The method is demonstrated on the double integrator example, producing an elliptical cost-to-go function and closed-loop dynamics with complex eigenvalues that spiral into the origin. Tedrake explains that Pontryagin's principle was used for the minimum-time problem because its value function is non-smooth, violating the HJB theorem's smoothness requirement. He concludes that these analytical tools break down for nonlinear dynamics, and future lectures will present algorithmic methods built on this foundation.

The passage consists mainly of a list of diplomatic correspondence dates and locations from August 1894 to March 1895, involving United States legations in Seoul, Peking, and Tokyo, the Department of State in Washington, and the British Embassy. The only substantive content is the beginning of a letter from Mr. Heard to Mr. Gresham describing about forty men kneeling before the palace gate, waiting for an officer to take their petition to the King. They represent a religious sect founded in 1859 whose founder, Ch'e Cheng-woo, was put to death as a heretic and sorcerer by the governor of Cholla Do in 1864. Despite persecution, the sect flourished and now numbers many thousands of adherents, chiefly in the southern provinces.

Indian markets are expected to open flat Tuesday, with SGX Nifty down 3.5 points at 10,342.50. On Monday, Sensex rose 0.62% to 33,455.79 and Nifty gained 0.55% to 10,322.25, a third successive session of gains. Analysts recommended buying Adani Enterprises, Tata Global, PC Jeweller, and ONGC.

Hedge funds are investment pools contributed by a limited number of private investors and operated by professional managers, aiming to maximize returns and minimize risk. They are intended for accredited investors and institutions, typically requiring minimum investments of $100,000–$500,000. Hedge funds use complex techniques such as short selling, leverage, and derivatives, and differ from mutual funds by being privately offered and employing more aggressive strategies. They generally aim for neutral market direction through hedging. Common strategies include long/short equity, event-driven, global macro, relative value, and fixed income arbitrage, with some funds focusing on niches like real estate, insurance-linked instruments, or cryptocurrency. Strategies may be systematic or discretionary. The article emphasizes that low correlation between strategies is often more important than individual performance for achieving smooth returns. Risks include liquidity, leverage, counterparty, and strategy failure risks. Hedge funds typically report quarterly, and investors should consult tax advisors regarding tax implications.

Femtosecond pulsed-laser irradiation (λ = 343 nm, 238 fs pulses) was used to form laser-induced periodic surface structures (LIPSS) on ~190 nm thick Nb thin films deposited on Si/SiO₂. By varying pulse energy (0.35–1.1 × E_LIPSS, where E_LIPSS = 3.4 µJ), samples were produced ranging from pristine films to fully LIPSS-covered surfaces and microbridges with ripples parallel or perpendicular to the current path. LIPSS (period Λ ≈ 260 nm, aligned perpendicular to the laser polarization) nucleate above ~0.7 E_LIPSS and fully cover the surface at E_LIPSS; ~10% higher energy produces holes. Increasing pulse energy reduces film thickness, shrinks the Nb lattice parameter by ~1.05%, and increases grain size at ripple peaks. Intrinsic superconducting properties degrade modestly and isotropically: T_c drops from 8.93 K to 8.53 K and the H_c2(T) line shifts down (~ΔT_c ≈ 0.3 K, ΔH_c2 ≈ 50 mT), with T_c correlating with lattice compression. In contrast, flux pinning becomes anisotropic: the critical current density is enhanced along the ripples (J_c∥ > J_c⊥), with the anisotropy ratio growing with pulse energy and undulation depth, and collapsing to unity near H_c2. Optimally treated samples show higher J_c than pristine films at low fields (≲100 mT) and 6–8 K, with bumps attributed to flux-matching effects. Magneto-optical imaging confirms anisotropic flux penetration (d-line angle decreasing from 45° to ~19°). Time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau simulations support the interpretation that thickness undulations (~70–100 nm deep) pin vortices in valleys, multiplying J_c∥ by ~2, and explain the non-monotonic field dependence of J_c∥ via a transition from collective to individual vortex motion. The work demonstrates that laser processing enables controlled modification of microstructure and superconducting properties, qualifying it as an enabling technology for superconducting circuit elements such as filters, diodes, and ratchets.

This study introduces PHIVE, a physics-informed variational encoder deep learning framework for rapid spectral fitting in high-resolution whole-brain MRSI with simultaneous uncertainty estimation. Traditional fitting methods like LCModel are computationally demanding, while conventional neural networks lack physical understanding and typically require supervised training with ground truth data. PHIVE combines a convolutional encoder with a physics-based decoder, trained unsupervised via variational inference, and incorporates a conditional baseline approach with adjustable stiffness levels. An ensemble of five independently trained networks quantifies aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties alongside CRLB. Data from 12 healthy subjects acquired at 7T were used (8 for training, 4 for testing). PHIVE completed spectral fitting in 6 milliseconds per whole-brain dataset, six orders of magnitude faster than LCModel (2 hours). Metabolite maps showed strong agreement with LCModel, with R² values ranging from 0.27 to 0.86, and PHIVE demonstrated lower coefficients of variation for most metabolites, particularly Glx and mIns. No statistically significant differences in relative concentrations were found for most metabolites, except mIns, where PHIVE yielded significantly higher values. Uncertainty estimates were higher in low-SNR regions such as the brain periphery and ventricles. Limitations include lack of ground truth, small sample size, absence of frequency correction preprocessing, and lower correlations for tCho and mIns.

Knees are subject to lifelong wear and tear, with many people over 50 requiring knee surgery. Injury risk can be reduced through healthy lifestyle habits: maintaining a healthy weight, exercising regularly, strengthening the muscles around the knees, and improving flexibility. Experts recommend targeting hamstrings, quads, glutes, and hip flexors, stretching (e.g., yogi squats, child's pose), and low-impact cardio like cycling and swimming to maintain circulation, cartilage health, and range of motion. Higher body weight increases stress on joints and the likelihood of conditions such as osteoarthritis. Knee injuries vary by location, severity, and physical background. Physiotherapy with tailored exercises can restore range of motion, aid recovery, and often prevent or delay surgery. Recommended exercises include quad strengthening, bridges, wall squats, and stretches, modified according to injury type; staying active helps prevent joint stiffness. Most knee replacements occur in people aged 50 and above, and osteoarthritis—degeneration of joint cartilage and surrounding bone tissue—is the most common cause of knee surgery; genetics also play a role. When physiotherapy alone is insufficient, knee surgery is one of the most common elective orthopaedic procedures, with around 160,000 total knee and hip replacements annually in England and Wales. Over 4 in 5 total knee replacements and 7 in 10 unicondylar replacements last 25 years. Post-surgery physiotherapy can speed recovery and help protect the new knee.

Hollywood actors Daisy McCrackin and Joseph Capone were kidnapped and held for ransom for almost three days by a meth-fuelled gang. The passage warns that honest citizens must guard against both demagogues who incite mobs to plunder the rich and corruptionists who enable exploitation by the wealthy, as both threaten popular government and often work together. It urges passage of a moderate bill limiting railroad employees' working hours and supports the goal of a general eight-hour day, noting exceptions where reduction is impractical, such as on the Isthmus of Panama. This study examined behavioural changes in frontotemporal dementia (FTD), comparing behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) and semantic dementia (SD) and testing the contributions of the prefrontal cortex and anterior temporal lobes (ATLs) to social behaviour, within the framework of the controlled social-semantic cognition (CS-SC) model. Forty-seven patients with FTD (26 bvFTD, 21 SD) and 18 controls completed informant questionnaires (CBI-R, AMI-CG, CamQUAIT), neuropsychological assessments, and structural MRI.

Both patient groups showed impairments across behavioural domains relative to controls, with bvFTD more severely affected on measures including everyday skills, self-care, abnormal behaviours, eating, sleep, motivation, and apathy. No behaviours were more prevalent in SD, indicating quantitative rather than qualitative differences between subtypes. Principal component analysis identified three behavioural dimensions—apathy, challenging behaviours, and activities of daily living (ADLs)—with bvFTD scoring higher on the first two.

Apathy was associated with poorer executive function (particularly the Brixton Spatial Anticipation Test) and, in voxel-based analyses, with atrophy in the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex, supplementary motor area, and precuneus. ADL impairments were associated with disease severity and medial prefrontal, precentral, and insular atrophy, though not independently of total atrophy. No associations emerged between behavioural change and semantic knowledge or ATL grey matter volume.

For discriminating bvFTD from SD, neuropsychological measures outperformed behavioural ones; semantic memory and executive function combined achieved the highest accuracy (AUC = 95.1%). Self- and informant-ratings of apathy correlated in controls but not in bvFTD, highlighting the importance of informant reports.

No behavioural disturbances were specific to right-greater-than-left ATL atrophy; the authors propose a unitary-yet-graded model of SD and advise against binary L>R versus R>L diagnostic distinctions in research. Limitations include reliance on informant ratings, incomplete behavioural coverage, and the cross-sectional design.

This passage is an email (dated December 31, 2000, from vkaminski@aol.com to vkamins@enron.com, subject "Recommendations") containing the transcript of the 2000 year-end episode of Wall $treet Week With Louis Rukeyser, produced December 29, 2000, with panelists Elizabeth Dater, Louis Holland, Barbara Marcin, and Brian Rogers.

The 4 Verticals concept is a passing play that allows quarterbacks to push the ball downfield while getting it out quickly, with all four receivers releasing vertically to win matchups or find open zones. Its purpose is to stretch the defense vertically and horizontally and create 1-on-1 matchups, and it is typically taught as a full-field read. It performs well against man coverage and Cover 3, where seams and voids can be exploited, but struggles against Cover 4 and soft zone coverages, where open windows are harder to find. The concept includes specific route assignments for the tight end, tailback, slot receiver, and outside receivers against both 2-high and 1-high looks. Quarterbacks must look off safeties and follow a progression: pre-snap identification, finding a matchup or void, and checking down to the running back. Variations from 3x1 and empty formations keep receiver landmarks consistent while isolating key receivers.

Yunnan Lucky Air, a low-cost airline founded in 2004 and based in Kunming, Yunnan province, grew rapidly to US$104.3 million in revenue and 1.2 million passengers in 2007, modeling its strategy on Southwest Airlines. However, China's heavily regulated airline industry and a growing number of low-cost competitors—11 by 2007—prompted Lucky Air to seek additional competitive advantages through e-commerce. Government regulations constrained its major costs (fuel, landing fees, aircraft leasing, and taxes), which comprised about 70% of operating costs, limiting its cost advantage to roughly 5% below the industry average. Approximately 80% of tickets were sold through agents paying 2% commissions, while only 1% of total tickets were purchased directly by consumers on its website, luckyair.net, despite the site's advanced features. China's e-commerce environment remained underdeveloped, with low Internet penetration in Yunnan (6.8%), limited credit card use, and consumer preference for offline payment. The case reviews U.S. and European airline e-commerce practices—including CRM, Web 2.0, customer self-service, online payment via PayPal, and customer targeting—that Lucky Air might adopt. Lucky Air's executives faced the decision of whether to establish itself as an online travel leader, weighing potential benefits against significant technology investment and uncertain market conditions.

The Education Department restarted loan forgiveness for IBR borrowers with 25 years of on-time payments; balances will be forgiven unless borrowers opt out by Oct. 21. The government shutdown may delay processing, risking taxes once the American Rescue Plan's tax exemption expires Dec. 31.

In a televised address, the President announces an increased rate of American troop withdrawals from Vietnam, with 100,000 additional troops to return home between May 1 and December 1, bringing the total withdrawn to 365,000. He reviews the situation when he took office—540,000 troops deployed, 31,000 dead, and no plan to end involvement—and cites reduced casualties, the Cambodian operation, and the South Vietnamese Laotian operation as evidence that Vietnamization has succeeded. He states the goal of total American withdrawal, preferably through negotiations, and calls on Hanoi to negotiate seriously and release all prisoners of war unconditionally. He argues against announcing a fixed withdrawal date, saying it would benefit the enemy, and defends American servicemen against atrocity charges. He closes by affirming his commitment to ending the war in a way that gives South Vietnam a chance to survive as a free people and achieves lasting peace.

Researchers from the University of Washington, Texas A&M University, and the Western Australian Museum discovered a new genus and species of clingfish, named "duckbilled clingfish" (Nettorhamphos radula), from specimens preserved in jars at the museum in Welshpool, Australia. The fish, caught off the coast of Southern Australia in 1977, is distinguished by its broad, flat snout and an estimated 1,800 to 2,300 tiny conical teeth—10 times more than other known clingfish. Because only two specimens exist, the researchers used CT scanning to noninvasively study the fish's skeleton and 3-D printed enlarged parts for analysis of its mouth and jaw structures. The findings were published April 14 in the journal Copeia. Clingfish are of scientific interest for their suction ability, which could inform the design of surgical devices and whale-tracking instruments. The discovery adds to the well-studied clingfish diversity of Southern Australia and highlights the importance of museum collections.

Tesla Motors' Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2015 describes the company's design, development, manufacture, and sale of high-performance fully electric vehicles and energy storage products. Tesla currently produces the Model S sedan and Model X SUV, and plans to unveil the lower-priced Model 3 in March 2016, with production and deliveries expected in late 2017. Over 107,000 Model S vehicles had been delivered worldwide as of December 31, 2015, and Model X customer deliveries began in the third quarter of 2015. Energy storage products, including the 7 kWh and 10 kWh Powerwall and 100 kWh Powerpack, are marketed under the Tesla Energy brand. Tesla sells directly to consumers through company-owned stores and galleries, operating 208 locations globally, and had 584 Supercharger stations open as of December 31, 2015. Vehicle manufacturing occurs at the Tesla Factory in Fremont, California, with facilities in Lathrop, California and Tilburg, Netherlands, while the Gigafactory near Reno, Nevada produces battery packs in partnership with Panasonic; full production capacity is expected in 2020 with total capital expenditures of $4 to $5 billion. Tesla earns and sells tradable regulatory credits (ZEV, GHG, and CAFE) to other manufacturers. The company had 13,058 full-time employees and operates as one reportable segment. Risk factors include potential delays in production ramps of Model X and Model 3, dependence on single-source suppliers, reliance on consumer adoption of electric vehicles, intense competition from established automakers with greater resources, lithium-ion battery safety concerns, currency exchange fluctuations, exposure from resale value guarantees and leasing programs, and dependence on key personnel including CEO Elon Musk and CTO JB Straubel.

Ultraprocessed foods—engineered combinations of salts, fats, and sugars—may have addictive properties similar to alcohol, nicotine, and opioids, according to growing scientific consensus. These foods trigger the brain's reward system and can produce cravings, loss of control, withdrawal, and tolerance, hallmarks of substance use disorder. Over half of American calories now come from ultraprocessed foods. Research, which gained momentum after a 2007 Yale meeting joining addiction and nutrition experts, shows neurochemical changes in reward-related brain regions, and about 14 percent of adults and 12 percent of children meet food addiction criteria on the Yale Food Addiction Scale. Experts increasingly view these products as distinct from natural foods. Regulatory responses are emerging, including federal scrutiny, proposed school bans, and Chile's warning labels and taxes, which appear to have reduced purchases of unhealthy products.

This passage is from a Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) for study ZEA-DNK-02170, Version 1.0 (16AUG2019), covering analysis methods, presentation specifications, and output listings. Section 14.7 specifies that 12-lead ECG investigator assessments (normal/abnormal clinically significant/abnormal not clinically significant) will be tabulated as counts/percentages, ECG parameters will be summarized descriptively by treatment group and visit, and categorical QTcF summaries will present patients with values >450, >480, and >500 ms and postbaseline changes from baseline >30 and >60 ms. Section 14.8 states that ADA occurrence will be analyzed descriptively with no statistical tests planned; the overall ADA incidence combines treatment-induced ADA patients (baseline-negative, post-dose-positive) and treatment-boosted patients (baseline-positive with ≥5-fold titer increase), divided by the number of evaluable patients. Section 15 notes changes from the protocol: rewording of the primary efficacy analysis with added sensitivity and supportive analyses, and changed secondary efficacy terminology from "within 30 (20 or 15 or 10) min" to "at 30 (20 or 15 or 10) min." Appendix A provides formatting rules for tables, figures, and listings (decimal precision, percentage presentation, footnotes, date/time formats) plus formulas for derived variables (unit conversions, BMI, change from baseline) and a conservative approach for missing/incomplete dates. Appendix B details SAS programming QC requirements covering program structure, log review, output review, dataset validation (including Pinnacle 21), data verification via spot-checks of at least 2 patients, and documentation. Appendix C lists planned tables, figures, and listings per ICH E3 guidelines, covering patient disposition, demographics, diabetes history, efficacy (time to plasma glucose recovery and plasma glucose analyses), adverse events, ECG, laboratory results, vital signs, immunogenicity, PK/PD, and supporting data listings.

The Trump administration announced the 2018 Nuclear Posture Review, a policy to modernize its nuclear arsenal by developing new smaller atomic bombs and enhancing deterrence capabilities. President Trump said the strategy is tailored and flexible to address 21st-century threats and reaffirms commitments to arms control, nuclear non-proliferation, and the moratorium on nuclear testing. Defence Secretary Jim Mattis said Russia and China are pursuing entirely new nuclear capabilities challenging traditional US military superiority, with Russia's nuclear escalation strategies and seizure of Crimea marking a return to Great Power competition. North Korea and Iran are also cited as concerns, while Pakistan is not mentioned in the report. The report calls for low-yield nuclear options, modification of a small number of SLBM warheads, and development of a nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile to counter Russia's non-compliance with the INF Treaty. The US pledged not to use nuclear weapons against non-nuclear NPT-compliant states. Ambassador Nikki Haley and Under Secretary Tom Shannon emphasized deterring threats including nuclear terrorism and maintaining extended deterrence commitments to allies in Europe, Asia, and the Pacific.

The federal government has agreed to give provinces and territories 75 per cent of tax revenues from legalized marijuana sales, with Ottawa retaining 25 per cent up to a maximum of $100 million annually. Finance Minister Bill Morneau announced the two-year agreement, noting provinces will share revenue with municipalities to help cover costs like law enforcement. The federal government expects about $400 million in tax revenue over the first two years, and ministers will reconvene in December 2018 to assess how the framework is working. The original 50-50 split proposed by Ottawa was rejected by the provinces. Provinces may also add markups above taxation levels. Other meeting topics included equalization payments, the Canada Pension Plan, the global economy, and measures to improve corporate ownership transparency to combat tax evasion, money laundering and terrorist financing.

Australian National University and Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris researchers completed a study, using experiments and computer modelling, on alumino-silicate glass—commonly used in mobile device screens—that could lead to shatter-proof phone screens. They found that sodium and potassium atoms form clusters or percolation channels rather than distributing randomly, and that elements including calcium and magnesium influence glass flexibility and resistance, affecting how fractures start or stop. ANU plans to work with manufacturing industry partners to supply better phones.

The speaker reflects on the heavy responsibility of the oath just taken and outlines the anticipated policies of the incoming administration. He pledges to maintain and enforce his predecessor's reforms suppressing the abuses of capital combinations in railroads and interstate commerce, while proposing further action: relief of railroads from certain antitrust restrictions, federal supervision of railroad bond and stock issues, and reorganization of the Department of Justice, the Bureau of Corporations, and the Interstate Commerce Commission to improve enforcement. Amendments to the antitrust and interstate commerce laws will be submitted to Congress.

The most pressing matter is tariff revision; Congress will be called into extra session on March 15 to revise the Dingley Act on a protective basis, with possible rate reductions in some schedules. A $100,000,000 deficit, resulting largely from the depression following the 1907 panic, must be addressed, and if import duties prove insufficient, a graduated inheritance tax is recommended. Government spending should be economical but not at the cost of needed functions, whose scope has widened beyond laissez faire principles. Conservation of forests and waterways, the Panama Canal (to be financed by bonds), and adequate fortifications, army, and navy are endorsed. Foreign policy aims to promote peace through arbitration while maintaining military preparedness, protecting citizens abroad from racial or religious discrimination, regulating Asiatic immigration, and remedying a defect in federal jurisdiction over the protection of aliens.

Further proposals include monetary and banking reform to secure currency elasticity, a postal savings bank, encouragement of foreign trade including free trade with the Philippines and steamship mail subsidies, and continued progress on the lock-type Panama Canal under Colonel Goethals. The dependencies of Porto Rico and the Philippines are progressing. The speaker hopes for improved feeling between the South and other sections and addresses the condition of the negro race, affirming the thirteenth, fourteenth, and fifteenth amendments, supporting industrial education, and urging careful discretion in appointments. He supports further labor protection legislation but firmly opposes removing the courts' power to issue injunctions in labor disputes and rejects legalizing the secondary boycott, while favoring statutory regulation of temporary restraining orders. He closes by asking for the citizens' support and divine aid.

Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a growing global health threat, and whole genome sequencing offers a faster alternative to slow culture-based diagnostics, but translating genomic data into resistance predictions remains computationally challenging. Existing machine learning methods like Random Forest and XGBoost treat SNPs as unordered features, ignoring sequence context, while Transformers require large pre-training datasets unavailable for AMR prediction. To address this gap, the authors developed AMR-EnsembleNet, a soft voting ensemble combining a lightweight 1D Convolutional Neural Network that learns local SNP motifs with XGBoost, which captures non-local feature interactions. Using the GieSSen dataset of 809 E. coli isolates with 60,936 SNP features, the models were evaluated on resistance prediction for four antibiotics (Ciprofloxacin, Cefotaxime, Ceftazidime, and Gentamicin) with varying class imbalance. The ensemble achieved the best performance for CTX and the highly imbalanced GEN dataset, matched top performance for CIP, and provided stable, balanced results for CTZ where Random Forest performed best. SHAP-based interpretability confirmed that top predictive SNPs mapped to known AMR-associated genes such as gyrB, parC, rpsL, and fusA, validating the model's biological relevance. The authors conclude that the ensemble offers a robust, computationally feasible tool for genomic AMR prediction and surveillance.

South Africa is expected to retain its only remaining major investment-grade rating when Moody's announces its decision on Friday, the first assessment since Cyril Ramaphosa replaced Jacob Zuma as president; all 15 Bloomberg survey respondents expect no downgrade. Moody's rates the country one step above speculative grade, while S&P and Fitch already rate its debt as junk. Risks include missed budget targets, weak growth, and land expropriation without compensation, which critics say deters investment. A downgrade would exclude South Africa from bond indexes, risking outflows of up to 100 billion rand and higher borrowing costs as it plans to borrow up to $3 billion abroad.

Saskatoon is proposing a $1.2-million, two-year plan to remove and replant about 1,000 black ash trees damaged by cottony ash psyllids, European tree lice first seen in 2006 that reappeared in 2015. Insecticide injections did not slow the trees' decline. First-year funding of $757,000 has been identified, but the $423,000 second-year funding has not. The psyllids devastated urban forests in Calgary and Edmonton.

The dollar rose broadly on Monday as traders unwound bearish bets made amid North Korea tensions and weak inflation data. The absence of new abrasive rhetoric between Trump and Kim Jong Un, plus Xi Jinping's call for a peaceful resolution, helped the currency. The dollar index rose 0.3 percent, also boosted by gains in U.S. and world stocks. Investors await Tuesday's U.S. retail sales report for inflation clues.

This study demonstrates that water- or ethanol-assisted capillary densification, optionally followed by thermal annealing at 110 °C, improves the mechanical performance of electrospun polyacrylonitrile (PAN) nanofiber yarns. Wetting loosely assembled as-spun yarns with liquid and drying them harnesses capillary forces during evaporation to compact and align fibers, enhancing inter-fiber adhesion and load transfer. Tensile testing revealed five stress–strain regimes; treated yarns exhibited higher modulus and strength but reduced failure strain compared with as-spun yarns, with water-treated yarns outperforming ethanol-treated ones, attributed to water's higher surface tension, slower evaporation, and ethanol-induced fiber swelling. Heat treatment further increased strength and stiffness but produced brittle fracture (~15% failure strain) through partial fiber fusion at junctions. Both effective modulus and peak stress increased strongly with decreasing yarn diameter, and yarns below 10 μm approached single-nanofiber mechanical performance. In controlled comparisons of segments cut from the same yarn, water and water+heat treatments raised peak loads by ~70% relative to as-spun yarns (ANOVA p = 0.013). SEM-based image analysis showed that fiber alignment (coherency factor, R² = 0.68) and packing density (R² = 0.75) each correlated with peak load, and a combined regression explained more variance (R² = 0.80), indicating complementary contributions. A stochastic mean-field constitutive model incorporating Weibull-distributed fiber recruitment and failure, elastic–perfectly plastic fiber behavior, orientation averaging, and post-failure load retention reproduced the experimental curves, with the model parameters ψ·φ mapping linearly onto measured packing density × alignment (R² = 0.91).

In this MIT OpenCourseWare lecture, Gary Gensler discusses financial system challenges and opportunities. After reviewing student papers and mentioning upcoming guest speakers (including Jeff Sprecher of Intercontinental Exchange and Kelly Loeffler of Bakkt), he leads a discussion of readings covering income disparity, financial industry consolidation (the Riegle-Neal Act of 1994 and Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act of 1999), economic rents, and former FDIC head Sheila Bair's views on Citigroup and moral hazard.

Gensler describes finance's central role as intermediating money and risk—moving, allocating, and pricing them—using an hourglass metaphor with Wall Street at its neck. He outlines key functions (storing value, credit), sectors (commercial and investment banking, insurance, asset management, exchanges and clearinghouses), and distinguishes primary from secondary markets, noting secondary markets carry higher volume and that US companies rely more on securities than bank loans.

He explains that ledgers—records of economic activity—are embedded throughout finance and central to blockchain applications, while payment systems transfer value by amending ledgers through authorization, clearing, and recording; blockchain's potential lies in faster final settlement. Regulation of finance spans millennia, from the Hammurabi code through debtor prisons to modern frameworks prioritizing financial stability, consumer and investor protection, and, more recently, illicit activity prevention.

Finance has long had a symbiotic relationship with technology, from carrier pigeons and the IBM 360 to today's fintech tools (AI, blockchain, cloud, biometrics, chat bots). Gensler presents US credit statistics—total debt around 350% of GDP, a $40 trillion bond market, $9 trillion in mortgage debt, and $1.5 trillion in student loans. Drawing on his risk management experience, he identifies market, credit, and operational risks, emphasizing that liquidity, funding, settlement, and correlation risks drive crises.

Reviewing the 2008 subprime crisis, he cites weak underwriting, predatory lending, easy credit, derivatives, poor risk management, and asymmetric incentives, noting government intervention prevented systemic collapse. He concludes that blockchain opportunities exist where finance has legacy systems, data intensity, and economic rents, and previews next week's discussion of blockchain economics featuring skeptical readings by Nouriel Roubini and Paul Krugman.

Jose Verastegui appealed his guilty-plea convictions and 120-month concurrent sentences for being a felon in possession of a firearm and unlawful reentry of a deported alien, arguing his sentences were unreasonable because they exceeded the advisory guideline range of 63 to 78 months, relied on improper departure factors, and were greater than necessary. The Fifth Circuit found no abuse of discretion in the district court's upward departure and variance. His constitutional challenges to 18 U.S.C. § 922(g) and 8 U.S.C. § 1326(b) were foreclosed by precedent and raised only for preservation. Affirmed.
OnePlus announced Android Nougat updates for the OnePlus 3 and 3T, now rolling out globally, featuring redesigned notifications, multi-window support, and other improvements on OxygenOS 4.0.

NYU physicists have developed a method to generate and self-organize droplets of immiscible liquids—oil, water, and alcohol—into well-defined layered patterns. Placed in a confined geometry, the liquids de-mix from the edge inward, forming stripes whose length depends on the tunable speed of the de-mixing wave. A theoretical model matches the data and predicts a step-wise release of inner droplets. Published in PNAS, the work could advance water- and oil-soluble medicines.

The nuclear force is the residual strong interaction between quarks located in different nucleons, and because many quarks, protons, and neutrons are involved, it is described using a mean field approach. Understanding of the force is based on nucleon-nucleon scattering experiments, binding energies and precision mass measurements, and nuclear structure data such as energy levels, spins, and moments. The force depends on the distance between nucleons and on spin and angular momentum, having spin-orbit and tensor components. It is charge independent, meaning it does not distinguish between protons and neutrons, consistent with its origin in the strong interaction, which is insensitive to electric charge. The force is short range, vanishing beyond about 2 femtometers, and strongly repulsive below about 0.5 femtometers, consistent with constant binding energy per nucleon and dense nuclear packing. Electromagnetic effects must be accounted for and removed when measuring the force. Mirror nuclei, which interchange proton and neutron numbers for the same mass number, show similar binding and excitation energies and offer a method to study unstable or radioactive nuclei.

This patent application, a continuation of prior applications, describes methods for training and using a machine-learned model that estimates a depth map from a single color input image, trained using monocular video data, stereoscopic image pairs, or both. The background notes limitations of existing approaches: detection and ranging systems (RADAR/LIDAR) are costly and cannot detect certain objects such as reflective ones; stereoscopic training requires two cameras; monocular video training produces artifacts from objects entering or leaving view; and conventional low-resolution inputs cause depth upsampling artifacts.

During training, images are input into a depth model to extract depth maps and into a pose decoder to extract poses. Synthetic frames are generated by projecting images onto other images using depth and relative transformation (and optionally camera intrinsics). A loss value is computed with an input scale occlusion and motion aware loss function comparing synthetic frames to input images, based on per-pixel photometric reconstruction error, and model parameters are adjusted to minimize it. The loss may use the minimum photometric reconstruction error between two synthetic frames projected from temporally adjacent monocular images, mitigating occlusion/disocclusion and border artifacts; may use upsampled depth features scaled to input resolution to avoid texture-copy artifacts; and may apply a mask (e.g., a Kronecker delta function) discounting static features such as objects moving with the camera. The system may use separate depth and pose models or a depth-pose hybrid model sharing parameters (a depth encoder feeding a pose decoder) for computational efficiency. Training components include image synthesis, error calculation, appearance matching loss, scaling, and masking modules.

The disclosure is illustrated through a location-based parallel reality game in which a virtual world parallels real-world geography, so player movement in the real world updates their virtual position via positioning systems. A client-server architecture includes a game server (with universal gaming, commercial game, data collection, and event modules, plus a depth estimation training system) and client devices equipped with camera assemblies (monocular or stereoscopic), depth estimation models, gaming modules, and positioning modules. A trained depth estimation model lets a client device generate a depth map from a captured image and use it to generate and display augmented virtual content, such as a virtual character that respects scene depth and occlusion. The application also describes an example computing device architecture and incorporates by reference an appendix titled "Digging Into Self-Supervised Monocular Depth Estimation."

Kennesaw State won the 2017 ASUN Championship at The Legends at Chateau Elan in Braselton, Ga., finishing at 1-under 863. A new Accenture study finds investors of all ages and wealth levels want both robo and human advisers, not one instead of the other. Surveying 1,300 investors, it found respondents ranked hybrid wealth management firms highest for offering low-cost robo access plus human expertise.

NASA's New Horizons spacecraft, which became the first to flyby Pluto in July 2015, will arrive at Kuiper Belt Object 2014 MU69 by Jan. 1, 2019. Nicknamed "Ultima Thule" through a public campaign, the object orbits about 1.6 billion km beyond Pluto and will be the most primitive object ever observed by a spacecraft, as well as the farthest encounter in space exploration history. Originally thought to be spherical, 2017 occultation observations suggest MU69 may be an "extreme prolate spheroid" or a close/contact binary. The naming campaign, hosted by the SETI Institute, involved 115,000 participants who nominated 34,000 names. "Ultima Thule," meaning "beyond Thule" (a mythical far-northern island), is a temporary nickname; a formal name will be submitted to the International Astronomical Union after the flyby.

Researchers used exome sequencing data from 454,803 UK Biobank (UKB) and 173,585 Geisinger MyCode (GHS) participants to generate the largest callsets to date of clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP), identifying 27,331 CHIP carriers (6%) in UKB and 12,877 (7.4%) in GHS. DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1, PPM1D, and TP53 were the most commonly mutated genes. CHIP prevalence rose with age, reaching ~15% by age 75, and was associated with older age and heavy smoking.

A common variant GWAS in UKB identified 27 loci (24 novel) harboring 57 independently associated variants, with directional replication in GHS. Rare variant and gene burden ExWAS identified 20 rare variants across 3 loci and 5 genes (ATM, CHEK2, CTC1, CLPTM1L, KDELC2), with evidence indicating germline origins. Gene-specific analyses revealed shared, unique, and opposing effects across CHIP subtypes; notably, the TCL1A locus increased DNMT3A-CHIP risk but reduced risk for other subtypes, and protective variants in PARP1 and LY75 were associated with reduced DNMT3A-CHIP risk.

CHIP was distinct from mosaic chromosomal alterations (mCAs), though CHIP carriers were enriched for mCAs. CHIP shared germline risk factors with mLOY and mLOX but not autosomal mCAs. ExWAS of non-CHIP phenotypes identified novel rare variant associations in genes including KNTC1, TIE1, PTPRF, TM2D3, GIGYF1, RC3H1, and PRR14L, as well as telomere length associations in telomere biology genes.

Cross-sectional analyses across ~4,871 UKB traits showed associations mainly with hematologic, cardiovascular, oncologic, renal, infectious, and smoking-related traits, with opposing directions across subtypes for traits such as blood counts and body mass. High VAF CHIP was associated with COVID-19 hospitalization and severe infection.

Longitudinal analyses of high VAF CHIP carriers showed elevated risks of cardiovascular disease (HR 1.10, driven by TET2), any blood cancer (HR 3.88), myeloid cancer (HR 7.10), lung cancer (HR 1.64, independent of smoking), prostate cancer, and all-cause mortality (HR 1.27). DNMT3A-CHIP was not associated with lymphoid cancer. A DNMT3A polygenic risk score predicted myeloid, lung, and prostate cancers and multiple CHIP subtypes but not CVD or mortality. A previously reported protective IL6R effect on CVD among CHIP carriers was not replicated in the full cohort.

The authors conclude that CHIP comprises heterogeneous, somatic mutation-driven subtypes with shared genetic etiology and distinct clinical risk profiles.

Attacking runs in soccer are off-the-ball movements by offensive players other than the ball carrier into open space among or behind defenders to receive passes. They are spontaneous actions, distinct from designed or planned runs. Two keys are understanding open space—recognizing or creating it—and ensuring the ball carrier rewards the run with a proper pass. An effective attacking run has seven components: recognizing open space, choosing an appropriate run, breaking away from a defender, getting open, timing the run, receiving an optimal pass, and communications. Named runs include bending, checking, diagonal, hooking, inside, lateral, onside, outlet, sideline, straight, through, and wide runs, selected based on which best advances the attack and enables a successful pass. Breaking away exploits the attacker's head start and the defender's need to change direction. Proper timing avoids offside. The pass must match the run's direction and speed, and runners should complete runs once started. Communication may be oral, visual, or through eye contact. The passage concludes with a coaching progression using cones and players, plus tips such as rewarding good runs with good passes, setting up defenders, and having passers make supporting runs.

North Wales Police are appealing for witnesses after an attempted kidnapping on Sisson Street, Rhyl, at 8.25am. A man in his 40s, of oriental appearance, tried to get a woman in her 30s into a car; she fled unharmed and he left in a silver vehicle. The incident appears isolated and the motive is unknown. Denbighshire council had warned schools and parents believing a child was involved, but police later confirmed no child was involved.

The passage is a transcript of a media session with six hockey prospects—James vanRiemsdyk, Kyle Turris, Patrick Kane, Sam Gagner, Keaton Ellerby, and Karl Alzner—held ahead of the NHL draft in Columbus. The interviewer asks each player about their backgrounds and careers: vanRiemsdyk's path from New Jersey to the University of New Hampshire, Turris's choice of Wisconsin and his father's lacrosse influence, Kane's Buffalo roots and hockey influences, Gagner's Sabres fandom and coach Dale Hunter, Ellerby's growth spurt and cousin Shane Doan, and Alzner's experiences with Team Canada and former teammate Ryan Getzlaf.

The Clock Offense is an effective way to attack the Diamond & One combination defense by placing the "Star" player in the middle and attacking it like a 1-3-1 zone. It produces open looks, easy lay-ups, and putbacks while isolating the star player one-on-one in the middle, exploiting the chaser's weakness in post defense. The offense includes basic rotations such as corner pass and cut, post looks, ball reversal, and post roll actions, along with dribble clear options. When the Star receives the ball at the high post, inside triangle action isolates them against the chaser, with drive, kick out, and post flash options available. The offense also creates a three-on-two offensive rebounding advantage on outside shots. Successful implementation requires execution, coordination, defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience. Game strategies include scouting opponents, anticipating defensive reads, deploying various alignments, and attacking the weakest defenders.

Education innovations often stall not because the ideas are flawed but because their stories arrive late or not at all, as illustrated by a school board meeting where an AI pilot was tabled after parent objections. The authors argue the education sector spends billions designing programs but almost nothing designing the narratives that help people understand them, leaving the public to rely on default framings such as top-down control, data as danger, and technology replacing people. They propose treating narrative like R&D through a cycle of framing, testing, iterating, and scaling, and offer guidance for leaders: lead with shared values, use tested metaphors, explain mechanisms, center teachers and students, address risks plainly, and avoid divisive framing. Building this narrative infrastructure, they contend, would make new ideas legible, trustworthy, and adoptable.

The Texas Supreme Court has issued a tentative opinion that the American Bar Association should no longer have final say over whether law school graduates are eligible to sit for the Texas bar exam. The court has requested public comments by Dec. 1, with proposed changes potentially enacted in January. The ABA is reviewing the order and plans to submit comments.

The Las Vegas Aces lead the Phoenix Mercury 3-0 in the WNBA Finals and can win their third championship with a victory in Game 4. In Game 3, the Aces won 90-88 after Phoenix rallied from a 17-point deficit to tie the score with a minute remaining; A'ja Wilson scored 34 points with 14 rebounds and made the last-second winning shot. Coach Becky Hammon has used varied defensive schemes, including zone defense, while reserves such as Jewell Loyd and Evans have provided timely scoring. The Aces hovered around .500 early in the season before a 16-game winning streak. Mercury coach Nate Tibbetts called the Aces a "well-oiled machine." Mercury's Sabally is out for Game 4 with a concussion.
Akure-based lawyer Morakinyo Ogele has given the EFCC a seven-day ultimatum to publicly apologize to Sun Newspaper's management for invading its premises and pay N1 billion compensation.

A post-game press conference in which a hockey coach discusses his team's loss to the Penguins, the defending champions. He attributes the game's turning point to a chain of events during penalty kills, including a third goal that deflected off a defenseman's shin guard and a difficult five-on-three goal. Despite disliking the result, he praised his team's effort, defensive gaps, and stick positioning. He expressed confidence in goaltender Pekka as the team's backbone and highlighted a young player, Freddy, who performed well despite limited NHL experience. The coach also discussed trust in his top four defensemen, the contributions of the bottom pairing, the pressure of the Stanley Cup stage, the team's growing experience from prior playoff series, consistency in preparation, the Penguins' speed, and Filip's emergence as a leader and difference maker.

The S&P 500 fell 1.60% on Friday to a local low of 6,212.69, dropping 3.33% (214.3 points) over two days from its record high of 6,427.02, and closed at its lowest level since early July after a 2.36% weekly loss. The U.S. threatened 100% secondary tariffs on countries like India and China buying Russian crude, putting roughly 1.7 million bpd at risk. Goldman Sachs forecasts oil at $64 in Q4 2025. This week's focus is on earnings from Palantir and AMD, with defensive positioning potentially becoming increasingly important.

Two calculations determine the required output capacitance—one for worst-case load transient voltage deviation and one for output ripple—with the larger value chosen. At least 1.3 mF is required, with derating considered for aging, temperature, and DC bias. For space-grade designs, radiation-induced single event transients (SET) require additional capacitance; the design example used approximately 2.3 mF. An optional output filter (an added inductor and ceramic capacitance) can reduce output ripple; its resonant frequency should exceed the crossover frequency but stay below the switching frequency and ESR zero, and a resistor can damp high-frequency peaking. Cycle-by-cycle limiting begins at roughly 35 A, about 45% margin over the 24.25 A peak inductor current, using a 1:100 current sense transformer.

Guilford and Milford police are warning residents to lock their car doors after thieves targeted dozens of vehicles nightly along the shoreline, including Guilford's Mulberry Point and River Street. Juveniles working in groups steal property and sometimes cars with keys left inside, fleeing recklessly when caught. Milford is investigating thefts and seeking two suspects who used stolen credit cards. Residents are urged to call 911 about suspicious activity.

The President notes that, despite contagious sickness in Philadelphia, Congress can safely convene there, and suggests an amendment to the 1794 law allowing postponement of Congress's meeting on such occasions. Though peace has not returned to Europe, he cites gratitude for domestic tranquility, prosperity, and civil and religious liberty. Envoys to the French Republic have proceeded to Paris, and he pledges to pursue negotiation on equitable terms while urging energy, unanimity, and national defense preparations. He believes European turmoil will persist, making protection of American commerce—essential to the nation's welfare—and a suitable posture of defense necessary. The treaty with Spain remains unexecuted, as Spanish garrisons remain and the boundary line has not been run; foreign agents are also inciting Indian hostilities, possibly requiring a punitive law. He reports on commissioners under the British treaty (the St. Croix boundary, British debt claims, and capture claims, with British awards paid), the Spanish claims commission, and the resulting U.S. obligation to compensate British claimants. He requests reimbursement of consuls' expenses for captured vessels and destitute seamen, and revision of the consular act, including authority to inspect ship papers. He recommends funding government and defense chiefly through taxes rather than loans, notes estimates will be submitted, and closes by urging unity amid the critical situation in Europe.

An International Whaling Commission report found 122 of 333 minke whales Japan caught in the Southern Ocean were pregnant and 114 were not adults. After a 2014 court ruling, Japan cut its quota from 900 to 333.

This passage is a compilation of news articles from July 16–17, 2001, largely concerning Enron Corp. and energy industry matters:

- California Secretary of State Bill Jones urged the attorney general to investigate potential conflicts of interest among consultants hired during the state's energy crisis, several of whom owned stock in energy companies such as Edison, Dynegy, and Calpine. The Department of Water Resources is reviewing past purchases, and consultants with disclosed holdings have been recused from related work.

- The London Metal Exchange fined Enron Metals Ltd 190,000 pounds ($264,000) for persistently failing to deliver warrants on time and to input trades into its matching system; Enron admitted the breaches and settled.

- Dutch electricity traders asked the watchdog Dte to force generators to disclose plant outage information amid soaring spot prices; generators resisted disclosure.

- Northwest utilities including Enron's Portland General Electric and Avista Energy face $611 million in overcharge claims from regional electricity providers.

- India rejected Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay's proposal for state-run National Thermal Power Corp. to buy Enron's stake in Dabhol Power Co., which is disputing unpaid bills with its sole customer.

The passage presents defensive strategies against the Power Offense, whose continuous screening can leave shooters open if defenders get hung up on screens. Required fundamentals include defending base screens, attacking down screens, defending the low post, and defensive rebounding. Two strategies are described. The Basic NBA Show & Recover is preferred because teams avoid switching—shooters would fade to corners and screeners would post up smaller defenders. Defenders "show" against baseline crossings and down screens to force shooters wide, then "recover" to their assignments, finishing with matchups, weakside packing, and optional trapping of post mismatches. The All Out SOS Disruption achieves total disruption by trapping the wing shooter, forcing the offense into freelance play. It includes pushing the ballhandler to a sideline pushpoint to prevent mid penetration, inverting Bigs inside when possible, contact switches with Snuggle denial positions on baseline and down screens, a wing double team, and rapid rotations into Triangle "I," post front, and Helpside "I" Strike positions as the ball leaves the passer's hands, with contingency rules for baseline drives or screening actions.

Despite disappointment over losing the Stanley Cup Finals, the team praised its strong playoff run, a standout player's performance, and organizational improvement, expressing confidence they will be back.

Since Florida governor Ron DeSantis's 2023 takeover of New College of Florida, spending has soared while rankings, graduation rates, and retention have declined. New College spends roughly $134,000 per student, compared with about $10,000 on average at other State University System institutions, and the state has provided funding with little pushback. Critics, including former NCF administrator Nathan Allen, say the college is essentially a personal project of DeSantis, who one faculty member argued sought an educational showcase during his presidential run. Money continues to fund new athletics programs and larger recruiting classes to offset retention problems. The college has dropped nearly 60 spots among national liberal arts colleges, and President Richard Corcoran has disputed ranking metrics, attributing poor peer assessments to backlash against DeSantis's conservative higher education agenda. Critics also say changes such as reinstating letter grades are eroding the college's distinctiveness. Some faculty and alumni fear closure within two years, a possibility Corcoran referenced at a Board of Governors meeting. Allen has proposed privatization—reversing the state's 1975 absorption of the college—as an alternative to closure. Reactions are mixed, but the idea is gaining traction among faculty and alumni, some of whom say they would follow the faculty's lead.

Marian Hossa discusses facing his neighbor and longtime friend from Slovakia, a large opposing defenseman, in an upcoming two-week Stanley Cup Final series, noting both teams' finals experience from the past three years. He says the defenseman is difficult to play against unless opponents keep moving their feet, and that he jokes with him at faceoffs. Hossa praises his coach as an easygoing players' coach who trusts players and communicates well. He describes recovering during a lockout, skating on his own before returning to form. He credits the team's strong season, Joel's four-line rotation, and disciplined defensive play, and expresses appreciation for staying healthy and reaching the finals again after signing long-term.

SFS addresses priority runtime concerns in AMD-provided binary firmware within AGESA releases, excluding x86 code. Non-persistent updates serve as interim steps between BIOS releases, tied to specific PI releases with defined base conditions.

The Bulls lost their sixth straight game, 113-103 to the Clippers, shooting 36.1 percent. Despite remaining active in the trade market, any moves would be for the future rather than immediate help, following Nikola Mirotic's trade to the Pelicans. Zach LaVine scored 21 points in a season-high 31 minutes, his second consecutive 20-point game, while Paul Zipser added 16 points with four 3-pointers. Tobias Harris and Danilo Gallinari each scored 24 for the Clippers. The Bulls and Thunder have engaged in trade talks involving Tony Allen's expiring deal, and the Bulls sit three games clear of the league's worst record.

Quantum-correlated pairs, particularly entangled photons, are crucial for quantum information science, underpinning distributed quantum computation, communication, and metrology, with demonstrated entanglement between photons and matter qubits including atoms, spins, phonons, and electrons. Phonons, which coherently interact with various quantum systems, are promising for solid-state quantum devices; advances include ground-state cooling, Fock state manipulation, and mechanical qubits. However, generating nonclassical phonon pairs optically remains challenging due to limited single-photon optomechanical coupling and underdeveloped high-order nonlinearity. This work generates quantum-correlated phonon pairs from an optomechanical crystal nanobeam cavity using effective high-order optomechanical nonlinearity, implementing Stokes and anti-Stokes interactions in one pulse. Analogous to spontaneous parametric down-conversion, the optomechanical spontaneous four-wave mixing process creates degenerate correlated phonon pairs, retrieved by a second red-detuned pulse and verified via the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality.

The TPS7H500x-SP series (TPS7H5001-SP through TPS7H5004-SP) are radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak current mode PWM controllers from Texas Instruments for space-grade DC-DC converters. Each device requires external gate drivers and supports switching frequencies up to 2 MHz, making them suitable for GaN power semiconductor designs across topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge.

A design example demonstrates a synchronous push-pull converter using GaN devices operating at 500 kHz with a 5-V output. Key selections include: a 205-kΩ RT resistor, 10-kΩ/1.4-kΩ feedback divider, ~25-ns dead time, ~50-ns leading edge blank time, 33-nF soft-start capacitor (~7.5-ms soft-start), transformer turns ratio of 2.5 with 40-µH primary inductance, 170-V primary and 80-V secondary GaN FETs, 0.47-µH output inductor, 2.3-mF output capacitance (including margin for single-event transient mitigation), 7.5-Ω current sense resistor, 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor, Type 2A compensation targeting a 10-kHz crossover, and a 102-kΩ slope compensation resistor.

The controllers operate from a 4-V to 14-V input supply requiring proper bypassing (minimum 0.1-µF ceramic capacitor). Layout guidelines address noise reduction, ground separation, trace routing, and component placement. The document also includes application curves, related documentation references, revision history noting newly released QMLP package options, mechanical/packaging data, and standard TI legal disclaimers.

Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) patterns from direct electron detectors (DEDs), such as Timepix-based hybrid pixel detectors, offer high quality but are limited by large pixel pitch and small pixel arrays. This work applies a sub-pixel shift-and-add algorithm—collecting multiple patterns with sub-pixel offsets, registering them, and summing them—to create super-resolution EBSD patterns. Using a TruePix detector (256×256 pixels, 55 µm pitch) at 20 keV with a 19.4 keV energy threshold on a silicon single crystal, the method increased the signal-to-noise ratio from 30 to 70 at an effective exposure of ~1 second, outperforming single patterns of equivalent dose and frame integration. The resulting pattern reproduced features seen in camera-retracted and simulated patterns, including HOLZ rings and fine band structure, and could be up-sampled 10× to a 2560×2560 grid. The approach requires no hardware modification but currently relies on a common crystal orientation across the sampled region.

Red Same, Red Opposite, and Red Rover are SOS mid court disruptive scenarios used in short intervals to change tempo, create easy baskets, disrupt an opponent's half court offense, and take the ball from a good penetrating point guard. They differ only in which defender becomes the initial trapper. In all three, the ballhandler is trapped near the sideline hash mark while non-trapping defenders form a Triangle "I." Rotations occur as the ball leaves the passer's hands, and each disruption ends in either "Base Go Red" or "Base Go I," as predetermined by the coach.

- **Red Same:** X1 pressures and traps O1 with X3; X5 denies O3, X4 denies O4, X2 denies O5.
- **Red Opposite:** X2 rotates from the baseline side to trap O1 with X1; X3, X4, and X5 cover O3, O4, and O5.
- **Red Rover 4 and 5:** A designated defender (X4 or X5) traps O1 with X1, with remaining defenders in Triangle "I" and SNUGGLE positions.

In all scenarios, if O2 penetrates, "Base Go I" or "Base Go Red" rotations are initiated by coaching decision; if O2 feeds low post O4, "Post Front" trap rotations occur.

This report examines newcomer education in California and offers recommendations for improving student outcomes, drawing on a California Department of Education data request, interviews with staff from 12 districts, and a literature review. Newcomers—students recently arrived in U.S. schools—typically have limited English, are largely socioeconomically disadvantaged, and many have experienced trauma, yet they lack the safeguards and dedicated supports available to other vulnerable groups such as foster youth and special education students. Schools struggle to meet their needs due to shortages of expertise, resources, systems, and funding, contributing to high dropout rates and low graduation and college/career readiness.

During 2020–21, California enrolled 151,996 Title III Immigrant Students (2.5 percent of K–12 enrollment), concentrated in five urban counties; 67 percent were socioeconomically disadvantaged, and fewer than half spoke Spanish at home. Roughly nine in ten newcomers are English learners, comprising about one in eight of that population. No statewide data exist for students with interrupted formal education (SIFE). Federal rulings (Lau, Castañeda, Plyler) guarantee appropriate education, but many districts may not meet the Castañeda standard.

California ranks low in education funding; supports include LCFF supplemental and concentration grants, the state-funded CalNEW program, the Opportunities for Youth pilot, and federal Title III and refugee programs, though 77.6 percent of newcomers went unsupported by the Title III immigrant grant in 2022–23.

Effective practices include specialized instruction, integrated language-and-content teaching, translanguaging, extended learning time, welcoming environments, robust intake processes, and social services partnerships. Recommendations include building state leadership capacity, adding newcomers and SIFE to state data systems, adjusting LCFF census-day funding rules, investing in curricula and research, and advocating for federal action.

Astronomers have discovered a massive exoplanet, MOA-2016-BLG-227Lb, using the gravitational microlensing technique. The microlensing event was detected on May 5, 2016 by the MOA group using the 1.8 m MOA-II telescope in New Zealand, followed by observations from telescopes in Hawaii, Chile, and Israel as part of the K2 C9 program. A team led by Naoki Koshimoto of Osaka University published the finding on Apr. 6. The authors call for further investigation using the Hubble Space Telescope, Keck adaptive optics, and future telescopes.
