The passage describes the NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture and its capabilities. NVIDIA GPUs are widely adopted for deep learning training and inferencing; the Tesla T4, the first Turing-based inferencing GPU, delivers up to 40X higher inference performance and more than 50X higher energy efficiency than CPU-based servers, with 2,560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, up to 130 TOPS of INT8 and 260 TOPS of INT4 performance, 16 GB of memory, and 320 GB/s bandwidth. Turing introduces GDDR6 memory (14 Gbps signaling, 20% better power efficiency than GDDR5X), larger L2 caches, and improved memory compression, yielding roughly 50% higher effective bandwidth than Pascal. The architecture includes an enhanced video engine (HEVC 4:4:4 and VP9 decode, 8K HEVC encode), DisplayPort 1.4a supporting 8K at 60 Hz with HDR and tone mapping, and USB Type-C/VirtualLink for single-connector VR. NVLink replaces the SLI bridge on TU102 and TU104, providing 25 GB/sec per direction per link, with two-way SLI only.

Turing adds dedicated RT Cores that accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, enabling real-time ray tracing roughly 10X faster than Pascal within a hybrid rendering model combining rasterization and ray tracing with denoising. NGX provides AI-based features—DLSS (including DLSS 2X), InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez—accelerated by Tensor Cores. New graphics features include Mesh Shading (Task and Mesh Shaders), Variable Rate Shading (content adaptive, motion adaptive, and foveated rendering), Texture Space Shading, Multi-View Rendering (up to four views per pass), and expanded resource binding. The TU104 (used in GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000) contains 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores; the TU106 (GeForce RTX 2070) contains 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores without NVLink support. The document also introduces the RTX-OPS workload-based performance metric and explains ray tracing fundamentals, including BVH structures, denoising, and ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, with examples from Battlefield V and Shadow of the Tomb Raider. It concludes with legal, trademark, and copyright notices.

The lecture continues a discussion of Riemann versus Lebesgue integration. Riemann integration quantizes the horizontal axis into finer intervals, which fails for "wild" functions. Lebesgue instead quantizes the vertical (value) axis, measuring how much of the function lies in each value slice—this gave rise to measure theory. Whenever a Riemann integral exists, the Lebesgue integral gives the same value, and the familiar integration rules still apply. Lebesgue integration is needed to handle "weird" functions that arise when moving between time and frequency domains and when modeling noise and signals as random processes.

Key measure theory concepts introduced: the measure of an interval is its size (b−a); the measure of a countable union of disjoint intervals is the sum of their measures; and any set that can be covered by intervals of arbitrarily small total measure has measure zero. The rationals between 0 and 1 form a countable set of measure zero. A Cantor-like set—numbers whose ternary expansions contain no 1s—is uncountable yet also has measure zero.

A function is measurable if, for every interval of values, the set of times at which the function falls in that interval is measurable. For non-negative measurable functions, the Lebesgue integral always exists, being either finite or infinite. As an example, a function equal to 1 on rationals and 0 on irrationals has no Riemann integral, but its Lebesgue integral is zero because the rationals have measure zero.

L1 functions are measurable functions whose magnitude has a finite integral; L2 functions are those whose squared magnitude has a finite integral. Any L2 function on a finite interval is also L1. For such time-limited functions, all Fourier coefficients exist and are finite, and the Fourier series converges to the function in the mean (mean-square/energy sense), which is more meaningful for engineering than pointwise equality. Conversely, any coefficient sequence with finite energy corresponds to an L2 function.

Finally, arbitrary L2 functions can be segmented into fixed-width intervals, each expanded in its own Fourier series—a conceptual basis for voice compression—and the lecture closes by previewing the Fourier integral/transform for the next session.

Two-time WWE Hall of Famer Ric Flair, 68, underwent surgery Monday after being hospitalized over the weekend for heart-related issues and placed in a medically induced coma. This paper presents a new anti-unification technique for computing least general generalizations of variadic nominal terms, combining variable binding based on nominal techniques with variadic expressions that allow a variable number of arguments. Motivated by limitations of existing anti-unification methods in software science—difficulty handling non-trivial differences such as insertions or deletions, and overemphasis on differences in local variable names—the approach syntactically distinguishes atoms (which can be bound) from variables (subject to substitution), and further separates individual variables from hedge variables, which can be replaced by finite sequences of terms. The rule-based algorithm VNAU computes generalizations while also capturing difference information and mappings for reconstructing the original expressions, and is parametrized by a rigidity function that controls which nodes are retained, allowing generalizations of varying granularity. Applications include code clone detection, program analysis, automated refactoring, and symbolic reasoning. The paper defines the formal framework (terms, substitutions, freshness constraints, an equivalence relation, and generalization notions), illustrates the method with code clone examples classified into types 1–4, and proves the algorithm's termination, soundness, and completeness. However, the algorithm suffers from high nondeterminism and relies on exhaustive brute-force search with little control over similarity selection, motivating a more efficient and flexible refinement introduced in a later section.

This document describes optional extensions to the Secure Encrypted Virtualization (SEV) API and Secure Nested Paging (SNP) firmware ABI to facilitate page migration—the copying of page content and updating of virtual-to-physical mappings. AMD's Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine offloads this work, enabling software to move data between memory tiers with different performance characteristics. TMPM requires IOMMU enablement, and support can be checked via the ENGINE_READY bit in the PM_Status register.

TMPM provides two capabilities unavailable to x86 software or regular IO devices: migration of pages that may be concurrent DMA targets, and migration of SNP-protected guest pages inaccessible to the hypervisor/OS. The PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO command migrates pages during concurrent DMA (requiring the IOMMU host Page Table Entry location) and handles Hypervisor state pages in SNP systems. PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages, with sources in Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid state and destinations in a new Pre-Migration state, which uses a Platform Specific ASID value and cannot be PVALIDATEd by guests.

Multi-page commands can migrate up to 128 non-adjacent pages via a Page Migration List with per-page status entries; PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS requires checking individual statuses, and PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE indicates a retryable conflict. Performance is best with 16 or more pages per command (maximum at 128), paced interrupts, and a ring buffer kept ahead of the engine. IOMMU structures, vIOMMU buffers, and the ring buffer itself are not migratable, and host software must avoid concurrent hPTE modifications since TMPM updates them non-atomically.

Firmware reload requires quiesced operations and a torn-down ring buffer, must use same-or-greater version firmware, and varies by EPYC family (Family 19h indicated by FW_VER_Major value 71 decimal).
The speaker wants to take more shots to create rebounds, says the team needs to skate quicker, and notes they sat back too much in the third period, giving the opponent too much room.

The passage examines artificial intelligence in education, focusing on the Hungarian context. AI tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot are increasingly used for answering questions, translating, generating content, and coding. While AI is expected to become more prevalent in education, critical thinking is required since current tools have limitations and may provide incorrect answers. AI can assist teachers by generating and grading assignments, though AI readiness in education remains low. Potential benefits include bridging demographic gaps, while risks include reduced critical thinking, unequal access, and loss of human connection.

The author conducted interviews with 14 high school teachers and university lecturers and administered a questionnaire to 53 university students to address four research questions. Results showed ChatGPT was the most recognized tool, listed by all subjects. Participants used AI for debugging, information searching, code generation, practice task generation, and summarizing material. Cited advantages included time savings and immediate answers; disadvantages included easier cheating, over-reliance, and impaired learning effectiveness. Overall, 91% of participants held a positive attitude toward AI integration in education.

The author also tested Gemini, ChatGPT, and Microsoft Copilot on programming tasks. For beginner tasks involving programming theorems, ChatGPT achieved 92% accuracy, Copilot 74%, and Gemini 64%. For complex tasks (HTML, JavaScript, PHP, and C), ChatGPT solved all four after additional prompts, while Gemini and Copilot failed to provide a complete solution for the C task, though both offered partial answers and useful advice.

The conclusion states that education participants are familiar with and actively use AI tools and hold positive attitudes toward their integration. ChatGPT provided the most correct responses, but additional requests were often necessary. Users lacking sufficient prior knowledge can be misled by incorrect responses, whereas those with critical thinking skills and minimal prior knowledge can use these tools effectively for both instruction and learning.

The passage describes command, data-transfer, and register features of the ADS8681W/ADS8685W/ADS8689W devices. Data writes are synchronous to the external SCLK clock and support one-byte or two-byte (HWORD) operations; HWORD commands ignore the LSB of the 9-bit address, and all input commands must be 32 bits long, executing at the rising edge of CONVST/CS. Output data for frame F+1 depends on the command issued in frame F and the DATA_VAL[2:0] bits, producing a fixed pattern, 8- or 16-bit register data, or the latest 16-bit conversion result; optional flags (device address, range, AVDD and input alarms, parity) can be appended per DATAOUT_CTL_REG settings.

The device uses a multiSPI interface with four legacy SPI-compatible protocols (SPI-00-S through SPI-11-S) for writes; SPI-00-S is the default after power-up or reset, and SDI_MODE[1:0] bits select alternatives. Read options include single SDO-x, dual SDO-x (requiring half the clock cycles), and source-synchronous (SRC) protocols, in which the RVS pin provides an output clock synchronous with data; clock source and bus width are configurable.

Nine configuration registers are mapped, including DEVICE_ID_REG (00h), RST_PWRCTL_REG (04h, unlocked by writing 69h to address 05h), SDI_CTL_REG, SDO_CTL_REG, DATAOUT_CTL_REG, RANGE_SEL_REG, ALARM_REG, and alarm threshold registers.

Application information presents an eight-channel industrial analog input module using the ADS8681W with a MUX36D08 multiplexer, supporting standard voltage and current ranges up to ±10V with settling to 1% accuracy in under 5µs, and describes the programmable input alarm with hysteresis using an NTC thermistor. Power recommendations cover AVDD/DVDD decoupling and two low-power modes (NAP and power-down). The revision history notes ADS8685W and ADS8689W changed from Advance Information to Production Data.

The passage describes features and applications of the TPS7H500x-SP series of radiation-hardness-assured current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. The FAULT pin enables additional external protections; a fault shutdown occurs when the pin exceeds 0.6 V for longer than a minimum pulse width (0.4–1.4 µs), discharging the SS pin and stopping outputs until the voltage falls below the 0.5 V falling threshold, after which a delay precedes soft-start restart. Slope compensation, set via the RSC pin, mitigates subharmonic oscillation at duty cycles above 50%; the recommended value equals the inductor falling current slope. Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation can be applied, with component selection procedures provided. Thermal shutdown stops switching at a 175°C junction temperature and restarts below 160°C. The controllers use fixed-frequency peak current mode control, support switching frequencies up to 2 MHz, and suit topologies including buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge. A design example demonstrates a 500-kHz synchronous push-pull converter with GaN devices and a 5-V output, covering component selection for switching frequency, output voltage programming, dead time, leading edge blank time, soft-start, transformer, switching and rectifier FETs, RCD clamp, output inductor and capacitance (including single-event transient mitigation), current limiting, hiccup, frequency compensation, and slope compensation. Power supply recommendations specify a 4–14 V input with proper bypassing, and layout guidelines address noise reduction, ground separation, trace routing, and component placement. The document concludes with related documentation, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

This study examines human-AI interactions in conversational information-seeking (CIS) with ChatGPT across three levels: users' prompting strategies, ChatGPT's communication style adaptation, and the effects of AI responses on user perceptions and attitudes. A 3 (issue: health, science, policy) × 2 (issue controversy) between-subject experiment was conducted with a nationally representative sample of 937 U.S. adults recruited via Prolific in November 2024. Participants reported demographics and pre-existing attitudes, were assigned one of six topics, and interacted with GPT-4o for at least five turns to seek issue-specific information for a hypothetical scenario before reporting their perceptions and attitudes. Of 937 responses, 747 valid conversation URLs were collected (averaging 5.56 turns; 96.7% used GPT-4o). Five information-related communication styles (self-revealing, information-seeking, fact-oriented, action-seeking, cognitive complexity) were extracted using the Symanto Psychology API and LIWC 2022, along with citation and structure counts from ChatGPT responses. Eight prompting strategies, grouped into user-supplied information, style-related requests, and content-related requests, were annotated using ChatGPT and validated by human coders (IRR = .814; weighted F1 = 0.903). A manipulation check confirmed controversial topics (e.g., immigration) were perceived as more controversial than non-controversial ones (e.g., highway infrastructure). Main findings: 19.1% of users used at least one prompting strategy, predicted by education level and party affiliation; issue controversy shaped ChatGPT's response communication styles and citation counts while user prompt styles remained consistent; and ChatGPT's cognitive complexity led users to perceive responses as less favorable but produced more positive issue-relevant attitude changes.

The passage opens with a speech proposing that nations adopt the Monroe Doctrine as a world doctrine: no nation should extend its polity over another, every people should freely determine its own development, and nations should avoid entangling alliances. It advocates government by consent of the governed, freedom of the seas, and moderation of armaments, calling these American principles and those of mankind. Subsequent dispatches report reactions: Italy's Foreign Minister found the President's Senate address idealistic and difficult to implement but not unfavorably received, and asked about the proposed peace preservation league; the Swiss Minister praised it highly. Spain's Minister of State said Spain would cooperate with the United States if consulted before further public communications, noting the address made an excellent impression there. Hungary's Prime Minister, Count Tisza, welcomed peace efforts but stated opponents' conditions would mean dismemberment of Austria-Hungary and the Ottoman Empire, creating a lasting difference with the President's standpoint.

This patent application, a continuation of U.S. application Ser. No. 16/826,036, describes methods, systems, and computer-readable media for automating orthodontic treatment planning by creating, maintaining, and applying collections of user (e.g., dentist, orthodontist) or user group preferences. Conventional treatment planning for patient-removable appliances such as aligners involves many manual, time-consuming steps and provides limited choices and control to dental professionals.

The described treatment planning engine accesses a database of user preferences—linking users, key preference text statements, and corresponding clinical behaviors—along with patient-specific information (e.g., digital scans of dentition) and user treatment instructions to automatically generate treatment plans customized to both the patient and the user. Preferences may be identified by text mining historical treatment data using machine learning agents (e.g., bag of words, random forests, word2vec, convolutional neural networks) and/or similarity searches (e.g., Damerau-Levenshtein distance), with identified preferences verified manually or semi-automatically before being added to the database. Machine learning agents classify text instructions as positive or negative matches to reference key preferences, using text filters and conditional probability calculations.

Alternatively or additionally, statistical preference analysis identifies users with statistically consistent clinical behaviors over time, employing clustering methods (e.g., Gaussian Mixture, KMeans) to detect behavior changes and determine the start date of current preferences, including for users who do not provide explicit text instructions.

Monitoring tools serve as quality control, generating reports on automatically applied treatment options (e.g., counts of recognized, accepted, changed, or manually applied options) to detect incorrect detections or changed user behavior and to update the preference database. Implementation of these methods reportedly reduced the percentage of treatment plans requiring user modification from 12.48% to 8.5%.

A three-year-old boy, Liam Radcliffe, left Barassie early years nursery in Ayrshire unnoticed and walked half a mile home along a busy road, passing through two sets of doors and an unlocked gate. His mother, Sarra Reid, found him crying at the doorstep and drove him back to the nursery, where staff had not realised he had been missing for up to 20 minutes. Following the incident, the nursery's main door will be alarmed, the gate padlocked, and an additional staff member added, measures confirmed by South Ayrshire Council.

On October 4, 2001, BG Group PLC agreed to purchase Enron Corp.'s offshore Indian oil and gas assets for $388 million. The assets include a 30% stake in the Tapti gas field and the Panna/Mukta oil and gas fields, plus a 62.64% interest in the CB-OS/1 exploration license, with reserves exceeding 170 million barrels of oil equivalent. Analysts considered the price a bargain at approximately $2.30 per barrel of oil equivalent, noting Enron likely undersold after rejecting a $400 million offer from Oil & Natural Gas Corp. (ONGC) earlier in the year. The deal is conditional on BG obtaining operatorship of the fields, which ONGC, a 40% stakeholder, is also seeking; BG stated it would walk away if denied operatorship.

Separately, Enron is attempting to exit the Dabhol Power Project, India's largest private power plant, in which it holds a 65% stake, following payment disputes with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board. Dabhol Power Co. defaulted on a $24 million interest payment to Indian lenders for the phase II project.

In market news, technology stocks led a broad rally, with Enron shares gaining 9.4% to $33.49. Southern California Edison reached a settlement with the state Public Utilities Commission allowing it to pay off over $3 billion of debt while ratepayers continue paying higher rates, drawing criticism from consumer advocates. Additionally, Army Secretary Thomas White, a former vice chairman of Enron Energy Services, was named the Defense Department's liaison for homeland security.

Judges should not be immune from criticism, as illustrated by Lord Chancellor Parker and Judge W. H. Taft, who stated in 1895 that free public criticism of judicial action benefits the body politic more than judicial immunity. Fair, informed criticism keeps judges careful and just, and for life-tenured judges it is the only practical means by which the public can hold them accountable. Unjust attacks, however, must be answered, and courts should rely on the strength of their opinions and the people's calm judgment for vindication. The author warns that if respectable citizens and the bar oppose all criticism of judges, the public will instead accept intemperate criticism from agitators; just and temperate criticism guards against widespread antagonism toward the judiciary. The passage then turns to crime, particularly lynching and mob violence, noting lynching is especially frequent against black men, often following rape, and that mob vengeance reduces the mob to the criminal's level.

The S&P 500 rose 2.2% in July (+7.8% YTD) but slipped 1.6% on the first day of August. The passage is an archive log email from archiving@enron.com listing the titles, creators, and creation dates of numerous documents stored in an Enron Notes folder. Centana Growth Partners raised $250 million for its first fund to invest $5-30 million each in financial services startups. Founded in 2015 by Eric Byunn, Steven Swain, and Ben Cukier, the New York-based firm has invested in four companies, including One and Jumio.

A vehicle code violation stop in Chino led San Bernardino County sheriff's investigators to more than $200,000 in stolen items dating back to 2006. Mark William Ellis, 36, of Chino was arrested Feb. 4 on suspicion of grand theft and vehicle theft and is being held without bail. Authorities say he stole from vehicles, homes, businesses and schools in multiple cities over at least 12 years, hoarding items in six Montclair storage units. The passage describes the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture. The A100 contains 108 SMs with 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, delivering up to 312 TFLOPS of dense mixed-precision FP16/FP32 performance—2.5x that of Tesla V100. Each A100 SM delivers 1024 FP16 FMA operations per clock.

The A100 Tensor Cores support multiple data types: FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary. TF32 enables AI training on Tensor Cores by default without code changes, providing FP32 range with FP16-level precision. For HPC, FP64 Tensor Cores deliver 19.5 TFLOPS peak (2.5x V100). The TCAIRS solver in cuSOLVER showed TF32 delivered the most robust results for iterative refinement, with a geomean speedup of 2.0x over FP64.

A100 introduces Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity using a 2:4 pattern (two non-zero values per four entries), doubling compute throughput by skipping zeros, with virtually no accuracy loss across tested networks.

Memory improvements include 40 GB HBM2 with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth (1.7x V100), a 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x larger than V100) with 2.3x bandwidth improvement, and a combined 192 KB/SM L1/shared memory. Compute Data Compression provides up to 4x DRAM bandwidth improvement. New features include asynchronous copy instructions, asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls, and data sharing across 32 threads per warp.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitions each A100 into up to seven GPU Instances with isolated memory paths, providing QoS and fault isolation for multi-tenant environments.

Third-generation NVLink doubles per-signal data rate to 50 Gbit/sec, with twelve links providing 600 GB/sec total bandwidth. A100 supports PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV.

Additional features include NVJPG hardware JPEG decode, an Optical Flow Accelerator, 11x improved FP16 atomics, and five NVDEC units. CUDA 11 adds task graphs, async copy API, asynchronous barriers, L2 residency controls, and Cooperative Groups enhancements.

The DGX A100 system includes eight A100 GPUs delivering 5 PFLOPS, interconnected via NVSwitch with 4.8 TB/s bidirectional bandwidth, and runs software from the NGC Private Registry.

Appendix B explains sparse neural network concepts, covering pruning techniques and the benefits of fine-grained structured sparsity for balanced workloads and maintained accuracy.

Obamacare affects nearly all Americans, not just the 20 million covered through exchanges or Medicaid expansion; seniors pay less for Medicare, many receive free preventive services, and small-business employees are protected from high premiums. President-elect Trump and congressional Republicans plan to repeal the law, starting with spending and revenue provisions—subsidies, Medicaid expansion, taxes, and mandates—requiring only a Senate majority, and eventually undoing all of it except coverage for children under 26. Repeal would likely raise premiums, deductibles, and cost-sharing for Medicare's 57 million enrollees, restore the prescription drug "donut hole," and eliminate free preventive benefits, while increasing Medicare spending by $802 billion over ten years, though higher-income enrollees would gain financially. The employer mandate would end, though most large employers already offer coverage; employees at firms with fewer than 50 workers could lose protections for pre-existing conditions and required benefits. The individual market, where 10.4 million have exchange coverage and 6.9 million buy policies outside it, would lose its regulations and subsidies. Medicaid expansion, which added nearly 17 million people in 31 states plus Washington, DC, would be repealed, leaving millions of the poorest Americans uninsured, and the individual mandate penalty—$695 per adult or 2.5% of household income—would be lifted.

This is the opening lecture of an MIT graduate course on holographic duality taught by Hong Liu. The instructor first reviews logistics: there is no textbook or recitation, grades are based on five problem sets (75%) due every two weeks and a final 8–10 page paper (25%), and office hours are held before Monday lectures. The course outline is flexible, touching on gravity, string theory, and quantum field theory, with students encouraged to ask questions and give feedback.

The lecture then discusses hints toward holographic duality. Unlike the electromagnetic, weak, and strong interactions—which are understood as gauge theories in fixed spacetime—gravity lacks a precise quantum formulation, with unresolved questions about spacetime fluctuations, black holes, and the universe's origin. A 1997 proposal states that quantum gravity equals ordinary quantum field theory on a fixed spacetime, meaning the two are different descriptions of the same quantum system, so gravity and dynamical spacetime can emerge from a non-gravitational system. This builds on earlier ideas, including Sakharov's 1967 proposal and 1950s parallels between Einstein's equations and hydrodynamics.

Attempts to obtain gravity from massless spin-2 bound states were blocked by the 1980 Weinberg-Witten theorem: a theory with a Lorentz-covariant conserved current cannot contain massless particles of spin greater than 1/2 carrying nonzero charge, and a theory with a Lorentz-covariant conserved stress tensor cannot contain massless particles of spin greater than 1. The theorem is consistent with QED, Yang-Mills theory, and general relativity, but rests on the hidden assumption that particles live in the same spacetime as the original theory. Holographic duality evades this because gravity lives in a spacetime one or more dimensions higher. The lecture concludes by sketching a proof of the theorem using Lorentz symmetry, helicity eigenstates, and rotation operators to derive a contradiction for higher-spin massless particles.

This passage presents the protocol for BioRecall, a biobank-recall pilot study designed to collect lifestyle and environmental exposure data and combine it with genotypes, biological samples, and clinical outcomes from biobank registries. Motivated by the importance of environmental factors and gene-environment interactions in non-communicable diseases, and biobanks' lack of such data, the study will invite 1,386 previously genotyped Central Finland Biobank donors diagnosed with type 2 diabetes who have consented to recontact. Participants will complete a 30–40 minute electronic questionnaire via the MyBiobank portal (REDCap), covering physical activity (GPAQ plus novel strength and balance questions), diet (Healthy Diet Index), alcohol, anthropometrics, weight loss history, smoking and substance use, medical history, women's health, work characteristics, emotional states, sleep, residential environment, and background characteristics. Postal codes enable linkage to spatial environmental data. An automated feedback function provides participants with comparisons to national lifestyle recommendations. Data collection begins February 2025, with potential expansion to all Central Finland Biobank donors in autumn 2026 and other Finnish biobanks. Strengths include a low-cost, scalable, fully electronic approach and comprehensive exposome data; limitations include the small pilot sample, single-biobank scope, absence of wearable data, and possible low response rates due to questionnaire length. Ethics approvals were obtained from the University of Jyväskylä and the biobank.

This case examines Sony's launch of the PlayStation 3 (PS3) on November 17, 2006, amid intense competition. Microsoft's Xbox 360 had a year-long head start with nearly 4 million units sold, while Nintendo's Wii, priced at $249.99—half the PS3's $599—targeted mainstream audiences. The PS3 also served as Sony's "Trojan horse" for the Blu-Ray format in its standards war against Toshiba's HD-DVD, a battle with high stakes given Sony's past format failures (Betamax, UMD).

The case traces the industry's history: Atari's dominance and 1983 collapse, Nintendo's rise to over 90% U.S. market share by 1990 through quality control and strict licensing terms, and Sony's 1994 entry with the CD-based, 3D-capable PlayStation, which captured 60% of the U.S. market by 1999. The PS2's DVD playback capability drove its success, giving Sony 55% market share by early 2006.

The industry evolved from in-house development to independent developers and third-party publishers, with rising development costs driving consolidation through acquisitions. The new console generation was the first with Internet connectivity central to strategy: Microsoft's unified Xbox Live contrasted with Sony's more open PlayStation Network Platform and Nintendo's Virtual Console. Sony and Microsoft targeted core male gamers, while Nintendo pursued market expansion with intuitive controls like the Wii's motion-sensitive controller.

Sony also faced public backlash over violent games, including lawsuits, criticism of the ESRB rating system, and legislative attempts—though state laws were ruled First Amendment violations. Despite challenges, analysts predicted the PS3 would hold just over 50% of the next-generation console installed base through 2010.

This Relist Watch column examines Supreme Court cert petitions relisted for the upcoming conference. The court denied review in several cases: a death-penalty case on deference to state courts regarding ineffective appellate counsel (with a statement by Justice Sotomayor, joined by Kagan and Jackson); a Seventh Amendment case (Justice Gorsuch wrote an opinion doubting the amendment could escape Fourteenth Amendment incorporation); and a case involving a school district policy allegedly concealing children's transgender identity from parents (Justice Alito, joined by Thomas and Gorsuch, issued a statement). Two "lost causes"—relisted cases where respondents waived responses—were denied without recorded dissent.

Nine newly relisted cases fall into three groups. One group involves 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(3), which bars firearm possession by unlawful users of or those addicted to controlled substances; the 5th and 8th Circuits held it unconstitutional as applied in various respects, and the government has pending petitions, noting the statute produces hundreds of prosecutions yearly; it is the same statute involved in Hunter Biden's case.

Keathley v. Buddy Ayers Construction concerns judicial estoppel: the 5th Circuit, over a dissent, affirmed barring Keathley's personal-injury suit for nondisclosure in bankruptcy under a categorical rule conflicting with intent-based approaches in five other circuits; the author considers it a serious candidate for grant.

Four pro se prisoner petitions (three handwritten) raise procedural-error claims, and the column lists other relisted cases' questions presented.

Anthony Rizzo hit his seventh home run and added a two-run single as the Chicago Cubs defeated the Pittsburgh Pirates 7-0 on Monday. The game was overshadowed by Rizzo's hard slide into catcher Elias Diaz in the eighth inning, which forced a wild throw and allowed two runs to score. The slide was upheld on review, leading to the ejection of Pirates manager Clint Hurdle. Diaz remained in the game, and Rizzo apologized. Spot starter Mike Montgomery retired the first 13 batters and allowed two singles over 5 2/3 innings, striking out five without a walk. Addison Russell added a pinch-hit two-run homer. The Pirates fell to 2-8 in their last 10 games.

A team led by Ralf Jungmann at LMU Munich reports in Nature Communications a super-resolution microscopy mode, DNA-PAINT, that enables visualization of all individual strands within DNA origami nanostructures. The study found that assembly is robust under a wide range of conditions, but the probability of efficient strand incorporation depends on the precise position of its target sequence. DNA-PAINT uses dye-linked imager strands that transiently bind to target sites, producing a blinking signal that allows higher resolution imaging. Results showed that physical parameters like formation speed have little influence on assembly quality, though not all sites were occupied in all structures. The method enables optimization of DNA nanostructure construction and has potential in quantitative structural biology.

This passage from the MSPM0C1105/MSPM0C1106 datasheet (SLASFJ6A, revised September 2025) describes the devices' peripherals and support information. The PMU generates internal core supplies, monitors VDD via a brown-out reset with three programmable thresholds, and supports RUN, SLEEP, STOP, and STANDBY modes. The clock module provides internal oscillators (32kHz LFOSC, 32MHz SYSOSC), external crystal/clock inputs, and distributes clocks including MCLK, CPUCLK, ULPCLK, MFCLK, LFCLK, ADCCLK, HFCLK, and HSCLK. The DMA_B provides two full-feature channels and one basic channel, with triggers from ADC, UART, SPI, or timers, supporting up to 64k transfers. An event manager routes events between peripherals, the CPU, and DMA. Memory includes flash with 1KB sectors (up to 100,000 program/erase cycles on 32 sectors) and SRAM retained in low-power modes with 1KB-resolution write protection. Additional peripherals include up to 45 GPIOs, IOMUX, a 12-bit ADC up to 1.6Msps with 10.6-bit ENOB, a factory-calibrated temperature sensor, LFSS (RTC and IWDT), VREF (1.4V/2.5V), a comparator, security features (firewalls, CRC-16), three UARTs with LIN support, I2C up to 1Mbps with SMBus 3.0, SPI up to 16Mbits/s, independent and windowed watchdogs, RTC_B with ±240ppm calibration, and general-purpose (TIMGx) and advanced (TIMAx) timers. Debugging uses a two-wire SWD interface with a DEBUGSS subsystem offering a mailbox and security features. The document also covers typical application schematic recommendations, development tools, device nomenclature (X for experimental, MSP for production), revision history, and mechanical/packaging information.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on October 29, 2020, announcing its third quarter 2020 financial results. The filing includes a press release (Exhibit 99.1) and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures (Exhibit 99.2). The report was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. Amazon's common stock trades under the symbol AMZN on the Nasdaq Global Select Market.

This paper studies modal extensions of lattice-based semantics, replacing the two-valued Boolean algebra of classical Kripke semantics with alternative lattices (e.g., Łukasiewicz, Belnap, or n-valued Boolean algebras), and examines how modal sentences can impose constraints on the underlying lattices. The work is motivated by interpreting the truth values of one logic within another—relevant to counterlogical statements and to computer systems whose states operate with different algebraic properties—using a shared lattice order to enable communication between logics; the study is restricted to structures where every world operates in a single lattice semantics.

After reviewing lattice semantics background (partial orders, filters, matrices, valuations, consequence relations), the authors define modal extensions of lattice-based logics. A modal extension is regular when necessity means truth in all accessible worlds (NAW). For complete lattices, the normal modal valuation assigns to □ϕ the meet of ϕ's values across accessible worlds; if the lattice is incomplete, such valuations may be partial. Theorem 1 shows this produces a unique regular modal extension if and only if the designated values form a filter containing their meet; for finite lattices, regularity reduces to the designated set being a filter. Infinite counterexamples include the [0,1] lattice with the filter (0.5,1] and Boolean algebras with non-principal ultrafilters.

The paper then characterizes lattice properties via modal validities: validity of (□ϕ ∨ □ψ) → □(ϕ ∨ ψ) on all frames is equivalent to the designated set being implicative. Regarding axiom K, with strictly deductive implication, validity on all frames is equivalent to the lattice being linear outside the filter; with implication defined as −x+y, K holds if and only if the lattice is implicative, given anti-monotonicity, involutivity, and down-distribution. A twist-algebra construction over a Boolean algebra illustrates these results, recovering the paraconsistent semantics of Carnielli and Coniglio. The paper concludes by noting future work on the finite-model property, significant for computational applications.

The passage introduces a method combining Gaussian process (GP) regression with dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) for modeling nonlinear dynamical systems from data. DMD, grounded in Koopman and Perron–Frobenius transfer operators, globally linearizes dynamical systems and, via eigenvalue decomposition of a linear regression model, extends techniques for linear time-invariant ODEs—spectral analysis, multi-step forecasting, simulation, and control—to nonlinear and stochastic systems, while also enabling dimensionality reduction. Kernel methods, which implicitly construct functional bases in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), are non-parametric, flexible, and offer convergence and statistical consistency guarantees. GP regression provides accurate function estimates from noisy training data with fully probabilistic predictions.

The authors' contribution is a Bayesian interpretation of the embedded Perron–Frobenius operator, producing a modification of Extended DMD (EDMD) that builds models from noisy measurements and provides uncertainty estimates for multi-step predictions. To address the O(N³) cost of Gramian inversion and eigendecomposition in kernel Koopman methods, they apply the variational free energy (VFE) method, balancing generalization error against computational complexity. Unlike EDMD, the approach unifies hyperparameter optimization and sparse dictionary learning within one coherent theory. The authors show their algorithm is a special case of EDMD, inheriting some of its limitations, and discuss the frequentist–Bayesian duality. Section 2 develops a Bayesian formulation treating operators as random variables, using an operator-valued kernel and a lifted observation model with Gaussian measurement noise.

South Carolina golfers Katelyn Dambaugh, Ainhoa Olarra and Ana Pelaez earned Golfweek All-America honors—Dambaugh on the First Team, Olarra and Pelaez as Honorable Mentions. Dambaugh received a program-record fifth All-America honor, ranked 12th in Division I with a 71.68 stroke average, and won the 2017 SEC Championship. Olarra posted five top-10 finishes, tying for fifth at the NCAA Columbus Regional and 10th at the NCAA Championship. Pelaez set a freshman-record 73.12 scoring average and earned medalist honors at the NCAA Columbus Regional.

A hockey player credits his team's win to strong games from linemates Ron Francis and Sami Kapanen and good goaltending, describing a simple, grinding system. He recounts setting up Francis and the value of being tied after two periods before scoring in overtime. He expresses happiness for Aaron's strong game against his former organization and excitement over the team's first Stanley Cup Finals win, while anticipating a tough opponent.

Satish Gupta of astrostocktips.in lists the day's planetary positions and says housing finance stocks (DHFL, Indiabulls Housing Finance, Can Fin Home, Repco Home) and liquor stocks (United Spirit, Jagatjit Industries, Radico Khaitan, GM Brewery) will receive astrological support. He claims financial astrology enables correct timing and that astrologically supported sectors outperform in both bull and bear markets. He announces an early release of Samvat 2074 sector predictions and cites Samvat 2073 dyes/chemical gains, including Bhageria Industries (650%) and Thirumalai Chemical (530%). A disclaimer notes the views are the expert's own and advises consulting certified experts.

In an MIT OpenCourseWare lecture, a professor recaps earlier points: planning matters more than the business plan, planning is dynamic, the goals are to create and harvest value, and investors ask why this, why now, and why this team. Serial entrepreneur Bob Jones then speaks on finding customers. He asserts that a business will not prosper until founders know what they are really selling, who wants it, and how to find them, and that having customers is the one non-negotiable requirement for success. He illustrates this with two product launches. His nutrition bar for dialysis patients, Regain, failed because he surveyed clinicians rather than the patients who would buy and consume it; patients did not want it, could not afford it, disliked the taste, and pharmacies demanded expensive slotting fees. He later sold that business after shifting to inside sales and Medicaid reimbursement. His second product, NiteBite, a timed-release glucose bar for diabetics, succeeded because he talked directly with patients and parents, learned their fear of dying in their sleep, gave it a non-medical name, and built demand through Certified Diabetes Educators and free samples. That demand allowed him to avoid slotting fees, enter pharmacies and wholesalers, and eventually sell the company to a billion-dollar pharmaceutical firm. He closes with lessons on market segmentation, selling benefits rather than products, focus, talking directly to customers, and treating selling as detective work.

The American Indian College Fund announced a two-year study, funded by a $600,000 grant from Strada Education Network, to examine the economic and social impact of five tribal colleges and universities (TCUs) in North Dakota: Nueta Hidatsa Sahnish College, Sitting Bull College, United Tribes Technical College, Turtle Mountain Community College, and Cankdeska Cikana Community College. Working with the North Dakota Association of Tribal Colleges, the project will assess graduate employment, conduct a Gallup College Values survey of 5,000 College Fund scholars, and include a pilot study on TCUs' role in preserving Native languages and culture. Results will be published and shared with state and federal policymakers upon completion in September 2019.

Baidu is incorporating NVIDIA Tesla P40 GPUs and deep learning software into Baidu Cloud as part of its NVIDIA partnership to develop a cloud-to-car autonomous driving platform. Its Autonomous Driving Unit targets commercialization by 2018 and mass production by 2020.

The authors develop an Atomic Cluster Expansion (ACE) machine learning potential for YBCO, trained on DFT data including defects of all species, to overcome limitations of the classical Buckingham+Coulomb potential, which fails to capture the high-temperature orthorhombic-to-tetragonal transition. The training dataset comprises 1368 configurations (545,267 atoms) covering defect-free structures over a range of volumes, vacancies, interstitials, oxygen Frenkel pairs (FPs), approximate transition states, and amorphous-like configurations. The potential achieves RMSEs of about 10 meV/atom and 70 meV/Å for energies and forces, and outperforms the classical potential in reproducing the equation of state, lattice parameters far from equilibrium, and oxygen FP migration and formation energies.

NPT simulations (200–1400 K, ~25,000 atoms, up to 75 ns) capture the orthorhombic-to-tetragonal transition at approximately 800 K, reasonably close to the experimental ~1000 K; the discrepancy is attributed to oxygen degassing in experimental samples. The transition is an order-disorder process in which O atoms migrate from the O1 sites (and, to a lesser extent, O4) to O5 positions between the CuO chains, making the a and b directions equivalent. It is entropy-driven, facilitated by the decreasing formation energy of oxygen FPs at expanded lattices due to thermal expansion. The potential enables accurate modeling of mass transport in YBCO and may support applications such as optimizing annealing strategies for restoring superconductivity in radiation-damaged HTS tapes.

This non-empirical study reviews existing literature to examine the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on inclusive education. It describes inclusive education as embracing all students regardless of background or disability, while identifying barriers such as untrained educators, overcrowded classrooms, inadequate resources, and labeling. The paper outlines AI's benefits, including personalized learning, timely feedback, adaptive learning, assistive technology features, and automation of administrative tasks, but notes AI cannot replace human educators. Limitations include biased data, high implementation costs, over-reliance on technology, privacy concerns, and reduced human interaction. The study recommends designing inclusive syllabi using Universal Design for Learning and assistive technologies, and concludes that AI supports and encourages inclusion. Recommendations for educators and policymakers include incorporating AI in teaching, child-centered learning, continuous professional development on inclusion, and promoting awareness of inclusion.

The lecture compares ion traps with neutral atom systems. Neutral atoms are confined by magnetic or optical forces with trap depths of microkelvin to kelvin, whereas ions can be confined by Coulomb forces strong enough to trap room-temperature ions (10,000 kelvin confinement with fields of 100 volts per millimeter). Ions are cooled by Doppler, evaporative, and sideband cooling. Both platforms are used for clocks, precision measurements, quantum information processing, and quantum simulation of many-body systems.

Because the divergence of the electric field is zero, ions cannot be trapped in static electric potentials and require dynamic traps. The Penning trap confines ions axially electrostatically and radially through cyclotron motion in a magnetic field; Dave Pritchard at MIT used such traps for the world's most precise mass measurements (10^-11 level). The Paul (RF) trap, used in most quantum information experiments, alternates at radio frequency between confining and anti-confining potentials. Using an analogy of separated convex and concave lenses, the professor explains that averaging along the particle's trajectory yields a net inward force, even though the force averaged at a fixed position is zero. The micromotion's kinetic energy appears as the potential energy of the slow secular motion; the averaged cosine-squared term provides the net trapping force.

The second half covers quantum computation with ions. Single qubit rotations are Rabi oscillations on the Bloch sphere. The Cirac-Zoller gate implements a controlled phase gate using the center-of-mass motion as a data bus: the control ion's qubit state is swapped into the shared phonon mode via a pi pulse, a controlled phase gate is performed on the target ion conditioned on the motion, and the information is swapped back. A CNOT gate can be constructed from this controlled phase gate plus Hadamard rotations. Disadvantages of the Cirac-Zoller gate are the requirement of cooling the center-of-mass motion to the ground state and gate speeds limited by the slow center-of-mass vibrational period; alternative gates such as geometric and Sørensen gates exist.

Cadillac sold 35,020 units globally in September 2017, extending a 16-month growth streak. Year-to-date sales reached 256,613 units, up 44,336 from 2016. China grew 37.6% year over year, and the XT5 led sales with 103,645 units delivered worldwide in 2017.

On November 29, 2016, NVIDIA Corporation's Board of Directors amended and restated the company's Bylaws to implement proxy access and revise advance notice provisions for stockholder proposals and director nominations. A new Section 5(h) permits a stockholder, or a group of up to 20 stockholders, owning at least 3% of NVIDIA's outstanding voting capital stock continuously for at least three years to include director nominees in annual meeting proxy materials, with such nominees constituting the greater of two directors or 20% of the Board. Beginning with the 2018 annual meeting, stockholders nominating directors outside of proxy access must provide written notice 90 to 120 days prior to the first anniversary of the prior year's annual meeting, replacing the previous 120-to-150-day notice period. Special timing rules apply if the meeting date is advanced or delayed by more than 30 days. The Restated Bylaws are attached as Exhibit 3.1.

After the Starbucks arrests of two Black men in Philadelphia, The Black Star Project organized National Eat at a Black Coffee Shop Day on May 29, 2018, when Starbucks closed over 8,000 U.S. stores for diversity training. Over 400 Black-owned coffee houses, shops, and tea houses are expected to participate, aiming to gain market share. The event is part of a campaign to circulate Black dollars within Black communities.

AMD's stock surged more than 20% in premarket trading after the company announced a multiyear AI chip supply agreement with OpenAI. Under the deal, AMD will supply high-performance AI accelerators, starting with its next-generation MI450 series, to power OpenAI's data infrastructure, while OpenAI will receive warrants to acquire up to 10% of AMD's equity upon meeting production and performance milestones. Analysts say the agreement could generate tens of billions of dollars in revenue and positions AMD as a challenger to Nvidia, which dominates the AI chip market. However, analysts caution that execution risks, technical complexity, and potential supply chain bottlenecks remain concerns, and sustained growth will depend on delivery, margin management, and consistent demand from clients like OpenAI and Microsoft. The announcement coincides with AMD's $6 billion share buyback plan announced earlier in the year.

This study examined racial differences in the relationship between blood pressure (BP) and longitudinal cognitive decline in older adults. Data from 2,284 Black and White participants aged 55 and older were drawn from three cohort studies (MARS, MAP, and Black Clinical Core). Participants were classified into normal, high, or variable BP groups based on mean systolic BP and its standard deviation, yielding six race-by-BP groups. Cognitive performance across five domains (episodic memory, semantic memory, working memory, processing speed, visuospatial ability) plus global cognition was measured with 19 neuropsychological tests and analyzed using linear mixed effects models, covarying age, sex, education, and diagnosis.

Results showed that among individuals with normal BP, rates of cognitive decline did not differ by race. White adults with high BP declined faster than Black adults with normal and high BP in global cognition, processing speed, semantic memory, and working memory, but not episodic memory or visuospatial ability. White adults with variable BP declined faster than all three Black BP groups across global cognition and all five domains. Secondary analyses indicated these findings were not explained by lower baseline cognitive scores among Black participants.

The authors propose that autonomic nervous system dysregulation and cumulative allostatic load, including chronic racism-related stress, may help explain why older Black adults appear less cognitively affected by elevated or fluctuating BP. Limitations include the lack of medication adherence data and incomplete medication histories. Overall, the findings indicate older White adults are more susceptible to cognitive decline from high and variable BP, supporting targeted interventions to address racial disparities in cognitive health.

Addressing Congress a day after President Franklin Delano Roosevelt was laid to rest, the speaker states that no one can fill the void left by the departed leader but that America must carry on. He declares the United States will continue the fight until no resistance remains, will accept nothing less than unconditional surrender, and will pursue war criminals to the ends of the earth. He affirms the existing war strategy under the named military leaders will remain unchanged, and that the San Francisco Conference will proceed. He argues hope alone is insufficient, urging continued cooperation among peace-loving nations, with great states serving rather than dominating, and appeals to all Americans to support a strong United Nations Organization. He pledges continued efforts to improve the lot of common people and to live and trade with other nations, closing with a prayer to be a faithful servant.

Judges are fining attorneys whose briefs contain faulty, likely AI-generated citations. In Puerto Rico, firms including Paul, Weiss and Sidley Austin will share $24,492 after opposing solo practitioners filed motions with at least 55 defective citations; Chief Judge Raúl Arias-Marxuach said the volume of errors suggests AI use, though the lawyers denied it. In California, Amir Mostafavi must pay $10,000 to the court for fake quotes and off-topic AI-generated cases in appellate briefs; opposing counsel received no fees for failing to detect the errors. Mostafavi said lawyers must proceed with caution until AI stops generating bogus information.

Several manufacturers have discontinued manual transmission models in South Africa, including Audi's A4 1,4T FSI, BMW's 120i, M140i, 220i, 230i and M240i, Volkswagen's Polo GTI, Scirocco and Jetta variants, and Volvo's base S60. The move reflects low market demand for manuals, though Porsche and Jaguar SA continue offering manual options.

The Stranger Things cast is reportedly getting raises ahead of season three in three tiers: Winona Ryder and David Harbour at $350,000 per episode, the young core at $250,000, and teen actors at $150,000. Millie Bobby Brown is negotiating separately.

Dr Chris Bradley of the University of Birmingham says drainage was not to blame for the weekend flooding in Birmingham, agreeing with the city council that drains were overwhelmed by the sheer volume of water. The council said drains are checked periodically and flood water drained away soon after rain ended. A yellow weather warning has been issued for Birmingham and the West Midlands, with thunderstorms forecast for Thursday and potential for 30-40mm of rain in an hour.

The article presents a simple ETF rotation strategy among SPY (S&P 500), TLT (20-year Treasury bonds), and EEM (MSCI Emerging Markets) using monthly data. SPY was chosen as the most followed stock index, EEM for its lower correlation with SPY, and TLT as a potential safe haven. The strategy ranks the three ETFs by the previous month's performance, goes long on the best performer, holds for one month, and repeats. Backtested over two decades, it beat buy and hold with lower drawdowns until 2022, a very bad year. Trades occur at the close of each month, excluding commissions and slippage. The CAGR since inception is 11%; before 2022, the maximum drawdown was 22%, but the portfolio fell 41% from its 2022 peak. The strategy is best performed in a tax-deferred account.

Charlie Javice, founder of the student financial aid platform Frank, was sentenced to just over seven years (85 months) in prison for defrauding JPMorgan Chase by overstating her startup's customer numbers before the bank acquired it for $175 million in 2021. A jury found Javice and her chief growth officer Olivier Amar guilty on three counts of fraud and one count of conspiracy. Frank claimed to have served over five million students but had fewer than 300,000 real customers, with the rest being synthetic identities. Javice was also sentenced to three years of supervision, $22.36 million in forfeiture, and $287 million in restitution to JPMorgan. She remains out on bail while appealing the ruling.

The Forties Pipeline System, which carries 450,000 bpd and roughly 40 percent of UK North Sea oil production, was shut down by operator Ineos after a hairline crack appeared to widen, with repairs expected to take weeks. Brent crude prices rose nearly 2 percent to above $64.50 per barrel, a two-year high, and more than 80 oil platforms may need to shut down. If the outage lasts three weeks, up to 10 million barrels could be disrupted, tightening the Atlantic Basin market and widening the Brent-WTI spread to nearly $7 per barrel, potentially boosting U.S. crude exports.

The S&P 500 fell 1.60% to a local low of 6,212.69, down 3.33% over two days from a record high of 6,427.02, closing Friday at its lowest level since early July after a 2.36% weekly loss. The Nasdaq fell 1.96%, dragged down by Apple, with potential support near 22,300. The VIX rose to 21.90, its highest level since June 23. S&P 500 futures traded near 6,300, with resistance at 6,330 and support at 6,280. Crude oil dropped 2.79% Friday and another 2.1% after OPEC+ agreed to a sixth straight monthly output increase of 547,000 bpd. The U.S. threatened 100% secondary tariffs on countries like India and China buying Russian crude, putting ~1.7 million bpd at risk. Goldman Sachs forecasts oil at $64 in Q4 2025. The market may open higher Monday, but defensive positioning may become increasingly important.

Repeat spellers at the Scripps National Spelling Bee dedicate hours of daily study to return to the competition. Erin Howard, 13, of Huntsville, Ala., who tied for seventh last year after misspelling "Klydonograph," now studies three to four hours on weeknights and six to eight on weekends. Cameron Keith, 12, of Boulder, Colo., who tied for 18th in 2016, studies six hours on weekdays and nine on weekends. Naysa Modi, 12, of Dallas, is competing for the fourth time. Returning spellers report feeling calmer under pressure, and families emphasize the effort is driven by love of words rather than winning.

The S&P 500 has reached its average annual return of 9.1%, prompting caution ahead of a seasonally weak August–October period. July's jobs report missed expectations with only 73K jobs added, and prior months were revised down by 258K, signaling economic slowing, though June data was largely positive. Q2 earnings have been strong: 15 of 17 mega-cap companies beat expectations, lifting S&P 500 earnings growth from 7.7% to 11.2% and sales growth to 5.6%. The US dollar rallied to 2024 lows but was rejected after new tariff announcements and weak data. Despite AI-driven earnings strength, valuations of 22x–25x P/E and a negative equity risk premium suggest limits. The author expects near-term market weakness that could create a favorable setup into year-end, noting up years average 17% returns.

The passage contains diplomatic correspondence concerning the Belgian Congo. The contracting parties agreed the Belgian Government would facilitate, without restrictions, development work to increase Congo supplies if desirable. Day reported a commodity list for negotiations on Congo civilian consumption requirements would be forwarded by August 10, with a full survey requiring six more weeks. The Secretary of State directed that reciprocal supply data go simultaneously to the British Foreign Office and the Department of State for the Combined Raw Materials Board and Combined Production and Resources Board, which would allocate supplies. Concerns arose over increased Congo export duties on palm nuts and oil of geranium. London postponed signing of the tripartite Belgian agreement but made it retroactive, an arrangement the Department found satisfactory; negotiations continued through 1942–1943 without agreement and were discontinued by mutual consent. The passage also lists topics on Hungary, Bulgaria, Rumania, Czechoslovakia, and Finland.

In *Wiechmann v Wiechmann*, the Michigan Court of Appeals affirmed a divorce judgment granting Wesley Wiechmann physical custody of the two older children (Stefan and Loren) and Sylvia Wiechmann physical custody of the younger twins (Cameron and Chase), with the parties sharing legal custody. Although custody specialist Jill Hogenson recommended the defendant receive custody of all four children, the trial court, after reviewing the statutory best-interest factors under MCL 722.23, found the parties essentially equal except that factor (d), concerning a stable environment and continuity, slightly favored plaintiff. The Court held that while keeping siblings together is generally in children's best interests, the best interests of each individual child control when keeping siblings together would be contrary to that child's welfare, and found no abuse of discretion in separating the siblings. The Court also declined to dismiss the appeal as moot, despite post-judgment events in which the defendant removed the children to Colorado, was found in contempt, and the plaintiff obtained temporary custody of the twins, because no permanent custody change appeared in the record.

Most Southeast Asian stock markets closed lower on Thursday amid fears of capital outflows after U.S. Federal Reserve minutes showed most policymakers favor trimming its $4.5 trillion balance sheet later this year. Investors were also cautious ahead of the Trump-Xi meeting. MSCI's Asia-Pacific index outside Japan fell about 0.6 percent. Indonesian shares closed at a record high, led by financials, while Philippine shares fell 0.3 percent. Vietnam and Thailand were closed for holidays.

The Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) Specification describes AMD's architecture, assumptions, test methodology, and maintenance for SFS—a secure method for applying non-persistent updates to running firmware and settings without BIOS reflash or system reset. SFS targets "high-benefit/low-risk-to-mitigate" issues, improving system stability and mitigating some security issues without increasing maintenance downtime.

SFS does not patch x86 code (SMM, AGESA, UEFI) or run-once code such as the AGESA boot loader. Its scope is limited to priority runtime concerns affecting AMD-provided binary firmware components in AGESA releases, including ASP firmware, modules, and register settings. Updates are non-persistent, serving as interim steps between BIOS releases, and apply to a specific PI release with a specified base patch and firmware level.

Customers are responsible for testing and validating patches in their environments and for an SFS Deployment Agent (SFSDA) that initiates and tracks updates via the PSP/ASP driver.

Deploying an SFS package can change three version types: the SFS Patch Level (SFSPL), which must monotonically increase to prevent rollback; individual firmware components' firmware and Security Patch Level (SPL) versions; and the System Patch Level (SYSPL), tracking run-once code executed since the last reboot.

AMD cryptographically signs all SFS packages. Customers may optionally co-sign packages by providing a public key to the ASP during early boot, enabling customer approval of deployments. The ASP verifies AMD's signature before applying each package and serves as the root of trust for detection; the OEM/ODM owns the root of trust for update.

SFS is enabled through BIOS compilation options (APCB_TOKEN_UID_PSP_SFS_ENABLE and APCB_TOKEN_UID_PSP_SFS_COSIGN_REQUIRED), both off by default. Co-signing uses 2048-bit or 4096-bit RSA keys with RSA-PSS signature schemes.

Package application must occur at runtime and be reapplied after any reboot. In multi-socket systems, the first socket's ASP receives the patch and applies it to other sockets as needed; multiple updates apply sequentially. Packages can patch registers, replace complete firmware images, or update portions of firmware.

For SEV/SNP, SFS automatically commits SEV updates preventing rollback (reverting requires reboot), and SNP systems require HV-FIXED pages via the RMPUPDATE command. Each package verifies proper firmware versions before updating to prevent out-of-sync firmware; if a package cannot fully apply, application should not occur.

Issuing SFS commands requires specific memory alignment (2MB-aligned pages for the TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER). The ASP process checks DRAM address protection, verifies customer and AMD signatures, loads and runs the patch, updates patch level information, and returns status.

Packages are named fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg and must match the specific firmware combination running on a system. Updates run in parallel with x86 and DMA traffic with minimal performance impact. SEV/SEV-ES virtual machines must stop and restart for SEV firmware updates, while SEV/SNP VMs can continue operating across updates.

This literature review examines artificial intelligence (AI) in the context of distance education, which gained importance when the Covid-19 pandemic, first appearing in Wuhan in December 2019, forced the interruption of formal education worldwide. The paper defines AI, machine learning, deep learning, and artificial neural networks, citing examples such as IBM Watson, AlphaGo, BabyX, and Google Car. It notes that AI performed similarly to humans at lower OECD proficiency levels but not at higher ones, though IBM predicts computers may reach these competencies before the 2030s. Applications in education include personalized teaching, librarianship, student affairs, and Intelligent Education Systems (IES), which operate through domain, pedagogy, and learner models. The authors outline three education types—AI-supported face-to-face education, face-to-face education with AI, and simulation education—and three scenarios (transfer, studio, negotiation), distinguishing supervised learning, where humans control decision-making, from unsupervised deep learning, where AI determines curricula. Simulation education may rely on devices such as virtual reality equipment or, in the future, brain-computer integration like Neuralink. Reported benefits include efficiency, motivation, reduced costs and risks, and scalability; concerns include loss of human control, privacy violations, isolation, educator unemployment, psychological effects, and confusion between real and virtual life. The paper concludes that AI-based education requires serious, in-depth discussion, particularly in philosophy.

Marco Gonzales pitched 6 2/3 scoreless innings, extending his streak without an earned run to 19 1/3, as the Seattle Mariners beat the Texas Rangers 2-1 on Monday for their ninth win in 10 games. Seattle, 7-1 over its past eight despite scoring three or fewer runs in seven of them, moved 13 games above .500 for the first time since late 2014 and leads the majors with 16 one-run wins. Texas' only run came on a passed ball after Rougned Odor's bunt single. Rangers starter Doug Fister (1-5) allowed one hit through five innings before a sixth-inning error led to two Mariners runs. Edwin Diaz recorded his 19th save.

Taxify, which claims to be Europe's fastest-growing ride-sharing app, launches in Sydney on Tuesday, marking its first entry into the Australian market. It will offer half-priced fares for one month and has over 4000 drivers registered. The company charges a 15 per cent commission, nearly half of Uber's rate. Founder Markus Villig said the business model is based on fairness and transparency. NSW Minister Niall Blair welcomed the investment.

FCA data from its 2017 Financial Lives Survey shows most providers fail to ask customers how they will access pensions, with up to 70% of adults planning to access DC pensions in the next two years not asked about their options. Two-thirds (67%) had no advice from their provider's adviser; 40% of those not taking advice felt they could decide alone and 10% cited fees. A third expect the state pension to be their largest retirement income source.

Research indicates that installing air filters and upgrading ventilation in schools can improve test scores and attendance. Early evidence came from a 2015 natural gas leak in Aliso Canyon, California, where economist Michael Gilraine found that schools receiving air purifiers saw math scores rise by roughly three months of learning, with English gains close behind—effects comparable to smaller class sizes in the Tennessee study, but at about $30 per student versus $7,000. Additional studies link air cleaners to reduced absenteeism, fewer illness-related absences, and improved scores and pass rates. Proposed benefits include direct cognitive gains, better health and attendance, and reduced inequality, since low-income schools are more often near pollution sources and in poorly ventilated buildings. The intervention carries minimal administrative burden. The author recommends reconnecting pandemic-era devices, installing purifiers targeting a Clean Air Delivery Rate of at least 30 cubic feet per minute per student, and calls on philanthropies, advocates, and researchers to support and further study air quality programs.

El neuromarketing, surgido en los años noventa, aplica técnicas de neurociencia al marketing para incrementar la efectividad comercial. Empresas mediáticas como Viacom, Cartoon Network o ESPN ya emplean estas técnicas. Un estudio de la asociación Nmsba en 41 países halló que el 18% de las webs analizadas ofrecía servicios de neuromarketing para la industria del entretenimiento, principalmente en Estados Unidos y Reino Unido.

En España se investiga la figura emergente del experto en neuromarketing audiovisual mediante 18 entrevistas en profundidad a consultoras, representantes del sector audiovisual, neurocientíficos y académicos (junio-septiembre de 2015). Los resultados confirman las hipótesis planteadas: las neurociencias pueden aplicarse al estudio del consumidor audiovisual, aunque con limitaciones éticas, de interpretación de datos y de muestra; los equipos deben ser multidisciplinares; la introducción en España es incipiente; el neuromarketing tiene carácter emergente pero débil, concentrado en Atresmedia y Mediaset España; las productoras no invierten en él por falta de recursos económicos; y la proyección futura es positiva.

Las principales barreras son el desconocimiento (80%), la desconfianza (80%) y la falta de actitud innovadora (60%). Mediaset testa ficción en prime time mediante actividad electrodérmica, mientras Atresmedia investiga bloques publicitarios con EEG y otras técnicas. TVE abandonó estas técnicas por motivos económicos.

Las conclusiones señalan que la implantación definitiva dependerá de la demostración de eficacia, el desarrollo tecnológico, la mejora en la interpretación de datos y la reducción de costes. Las consultoras y los grandes grupos mediáticos españoles se encuentran en una fase de aprendizaje mutuo.

State officials, including Gov. David Ige, held a groundbreaking ceremony for the Mauka Concourse at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport. The $220 million project will add gates, environmentally-friendly space, and a walkway to Terminal 1, with completion expected by the end of 2020.

Index Markets Research has published a report on the Global Plastic Granules Market, covering its definition, applications, manufacturing technology, drivers, segmentation, and revenue forecasts. Key players include Dar Al Khaleej Plastics, Nahata Plastics, Vanshika Plastic Industry, Balaji Plastic, Navkar Industries, Shakti Plastic Industries, and Wiwat Plastic. The market is segmented into Commercial, Government, and Personal sectors and analyzed by volume and revenue across regions including North America, China, Europe, Southeast Asia, Japan, and India for 2012–2022. Product types covered are PP, HDPE, PPCP, LLDPE, LDPE, and Others, with applications in plastic products, clothing, and others. The report also examines manufacturing cost structures, production capacity, market shares and strategies, and includes SWOT and investment analyses.

Australian ecosystems beyond the Great Barrier Reef are experiencing sudden, catastrophic shifts due to the combined pressures of gradual climate change ("presses") and extreme weather events ("pulses"). Research published in Nature Climate Change documents six case studies, including kelp forest loss, wildfire destruction of Gondwanan refugia, floodplain forest dieback, alpine forest conversion, arid zone population crashes, and mangrove dieback. Notably, only one case had prior substantial human disturbance, showing that undisturbed ecosystems are not necessarily more resilient. Australia's temperature has risen about 1°C since the 19th century, with increasingly frequent and intense extreme events shortening recovery intervals. Ecosystem collapse carries significant costs to fisheries, tourism, water resources, and carbon storage. While targeted interventions may prevent collapse, they are costly, carry risks of unintended consequences, and their chance of success diminishes as extreme events become more frequent. The authors suggest the risks of inaction may increasingly outweigh those of intervention.

This retrospective cohort study used data from the All of Us Research Program registered tier dataset v7 to develop machine learning models predicting healthy aging among adults aged 50 and older based on social determinants of health (SDOH). Healthy aging was measured by a composite score of comorbidities, cognitive conditions, and mobility function. Three algorithms were trained: logistic regression, multi-layer perceptron, and XGBoost. Among 99,935 participants (mean age 74; 55.3% female; 44.1% classified as healthy aging), XGBoost with random oversampling performed best (AUROC 0.793) and achieved predictive parity across race and sex groups. SHAP-based feature importance analysis ranked health insurance type as the most predictive feature, followed by employment status, substance use, and health insurance coverage. The study concludes that the XGBoost model accurately predicted healthy aging, outperforming the other models, and underscores the significant role of health insurance in contributing to healthy aging.

The Cincinnati Bengals acquired quarterback Joe Flacco from the Cleveland Browns in exchange for a 2026 fifth-round pick and a 2026 sixth-round pick, and coach Zac Taylor named him the starter for Sunday's game against the Packers. Flacco, 40, previously started against Green Bay in Week 3 as a Brown, winning 13-10, and faced the Bengals in Week 1, throwing for 290 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions in a loss. The move came after Jake Browning struggled while Joe Burrow recovers from turf toe surgery; Browning returns to backup duty. Cincinnati (2-3) has lost three straight games and hopes Flacco can help keep the team in playoff contention.
