On October 22, 2001, Enron shares fell about 21% after the company disclosed that the SEC had requested information on certain related-party transactions, including deals with limited partnerships run by CFO Andrew Fastow. Enron pledged full cooperation, stating its auditors, attorneys, and board had reviewed and approved the arrangements, which were disclosed in SEC filings. A shareholder filed a derivative suit in Texas alleging the board breached fiduciary duties by allowing Fastow to run the partnerships, which reportedly cost the company over $35 million; Enron had also repurchased 55 million shares, reducing shareholder equity by $1.2 billion. Separately, Shapiro Haber & Urmy filed a class action alleging securities fraud on behalf of stock purchasers between July 13 and October 16, 2001. AG Edwards downgraded the stock, and Enron reported a $618 million third-quarter loss. Broader markets rallied on earnings news, and UniPrime signed a letter of intent for a wind park project involving an Enron subsidiary's ground lease.

This study simulates the transition from internal combustion engine vehicles to battery electric vehicles (BEVs) using one year of telematics data from UnipolTech covering 10,441 users and over 10 million trips in the Italian province of Asti. Trips were replicated across four BEV models (Fiat 500e, Renault Megane E-Tech, Tesla Model 3, Audi A6 e-tron) and four charging policies, including workplace AC charging, low-state-of-charge AC charging, overnight AC charging, and fast DC charging. Results show workplace-only charging is least feasible (64–88% of trips), while fast DC charging performs best: with the Audi A6 e-tron, 95% of users are suitable and 72% can complete all trips unchanged. At least 35% of users could already adopt BEVs with overnight charging. However, even the best scenario leaves 5% of users unable to fully electrify. Limitations include assumed constant charging power, universal charging availability, and no cost analysis.

IES Holdings, a 28-year-old diversified infrastructure services provider operating in 130+ US locations, has outperformed infrastructure and Russell 2000 stocks, with its share price nearly doubling year-to-date. While its largest residential division faces challenges, data centre projects are boosting the next two largest divisions. Backlog exceeds $2B, growing over 20% year-over-year, with improved cash flow and record cash balances. However, the stock appears overextended, with a sub-par free cash flow yield and higher insider sales.

Institute manager Kevin Deery expressed frustration after his side's third consecutive draw, this time against Larne at Drumahoe. He felt his team deserved to win but attributed recent results to bad luck, noting their last two goals were own goals and chances were missed, with shots hitting the bar and post. He cited poor decision-making in both boxes, particularly in failing to deal with Larne's freak free-kick goal. Institute remain in the top six with 13 games left.

This passage is an email dated February 6, 2002, from Sarah Palmer, Enron's internal communications manager, compiling news coverage of the company. Key points:

- Congressional hearings continued, with former CEO Jeffrey Skilling, former CFO Andrew Fastow, and Michael Kopper scheduled to testify Thursday. Rep. Tauzin said the committee would question Skilling about the internal report and his failure to sign approval sheets for questionable mergers, and said no special prosecutor was needed.
- William Powers, dean of the University of Texas law school and head of Enron's internal investigation, testified that Enron knew in March 2001 that partnerships were causing losses, gave the Raptor partnership an additional $800 million in stock, and inflated earnings by $1 billion over 15 months, with more than 70% of earnings in that period false. He said Kenneth Lay knew of the problems, that Fastow made at least $30 million from the partnerships, and that Kopper turned a minimum investment into a $10 million windfall. He declined to characterize the actions as fraud.
- Investigators found employees were threatened with firing or loss of bonuses; some received retention bonuses while others, such as Deborah Perrotta, testified to losing retirement savings. A roughly three-week lockout barred employees from selling retirement stock as shares fell from $15.40 to $9.98.
- The Senate Commerce and House Financial Services committees subpoenaed Lay after he canceled a voluntary appearance; lawmakers predicted he would invoke the Fifth Amendment.
- Arthur Andersen CEO Joseph Berardino faced criticism from lawmakers and said information was withheld from the auditors.
- Enron's debtor-in-possession financing shrank from a projected $1.5 billion to $250–500 million, with the hearing postponed to March 6.
- Enron Broadband owes about $440,000 in back taxes after failing to list roughly $15 million in equipment.
- The Houston Astros filed a motion to force Enron to decide on the 30-year, $100 million Enron Field naming rights agreement; Enron plans to challenge it.
- Spain's energy regulator plans to investigate Enron's Spanish distribution operations.
- The compilation also includes commentary on "Enronitis" and market "Enronization," a profile of whistleblower Sherron Watkins, and satirical pieces about Enron.

Virginia defeated North Carolina 71-63 to win the ACC Tournament, ending its two-year run at Barclays Center. Coach Tony Bennett quoted Psalm 133 before the final. Top-ranked Virginia, which began the season unranked, shut down UNC. North Carolina earlier beat Duke, whose Marvin Bagley III is projected as the No. 1 NBA draft pick. Clemson returns to the NCAA Tournament for the first time in seven years.

Linebackers require toughness, athleticism, and intelligence, as they face offensive schemes designed to confuse or overpower them. Positioned 3-5 yards behind the defensive line, they serve as the second line of defense, responsible for aligning teammates, relaying coach calls, and defending both the run and pass—earning the title "quarterback of the defense." The name derives from their position behind the defensive line. Individual positions include Sam, Mike, Will, and Jack. Key skills include vision, agility, tackling, and block shedding. Notable linebackers include Ray Lewis, Chuck Bednarik, and Lawrence Taylor. While the value of inside linebackers has declined as offenses shift toward passing, versatile linebackers who can rush, cover, and stop the run remain valuable, with 3-6 typically drafted in the first round each year.

The Maui News confirmed that Mike Victorino, former Maui County Councilmember and 2018 mayoral candidate, struck two teens while driving on West Papa Avenue on April 13. His wife said he was neither speeding nor under the influence, consistent with police. Victorino stopped and waited for emergency personnel, and both teens suffered non-life-threatening injuries. Police said the pedestrians were not in a crosswalk, but the older teen's mother said her son claimed they were.

The Board of Governors heard gameday feedback at their Thursday meeting. ASCSU President Josh Silva noted low student awareness of the tailgating lot, with many students using it only for parking; ASCSU plans rebranding and pre-game programming to address this. Athletics director Joe Parker reported attendance of 37,583 at the first game and 27,038 at the second, with queuing and congestion issues improving by the second game. Two-and-a-half years of planning contributed to successful transportation, including 7,000 transit riders at the first game and only 50 vehicles towed per game weekend.

This study examined whether role-taking and literacy interventions could reduce the influence of demographic and appearance-based cues (age, gender, ethnicity, and attire) on trust and risk-taking decisions in social engineering contexts. Social engineering attacks exploit human psychology, leveraging stereotypes and heuristics rather than technical vulnerabilities, with prior research indicating that older, female, ethnically similar, and formally dressed individuals are often trusted more.

An online experiment was conducted with 139 Arab participants recruited via Prolific, using a 4×2 mixed factorial design with four groups (Persuader role-taking, Persuadee role-taking, Literacy, and Control) across pre-intervention, intervention, and post-intervention phases (the latter conducted one week later). Participants evaluated 16 personas in a mobile hotspot scenario and engaged in role-taking exercises (financial advisor and lettings agent scenarios) or literacy modules addressing stereotypes.

Results showed no significant changes in trust or risk-taking across persona factors or roles from pre- to post-intervention, with Bayes Factors supporting the null hypothesis. Word-of-mouth measures also remained unchanged. However, a significant decrease in Issue of Involvement was observed, suggesting psychological distancing after the intervention. Covariate analyses including self-esteem, self-efficacy, and age yielded one significant interaction (self-esteem moderating trust based on attire).

The authors conclude that deeply ingrained cognitive biases resist short-term interventions, possibly due to heuristics serving functional roles, the gap between intention and behavior, and status quo bias. They also note that increased awareness may paradoxically create overconfidence and greater risk-taking. Qualitative feedback was positive, with participants describing the intervention as engaging and eye-opening. Limitations include hypothetical scenarios, potential demand characteristics, and the brief intervention duration. Future research should explore longer-term, more immersive approaches such as gamified or virtual reality methods.

The Great Southern Storm have named an initial 45-player colts squad under new coach Glynn Verbruggen ahead of the Great Southern Colts Carnival in Kulin next month. Verbruggen replaces Phil Gilbert, a former AFL player who coached the Storm for seven of the past eight years and has moved to Perth. Verbruggen, the 2008 Sean Plaisted Medal winner, has senior coaching experience with Northampton and the Claremont 15s. The squad includes State 16 members Heath Spinks and Jacob Blight, plus eight players with State Country colts experience. North Albany has 12 representatives, Railways eight, and Albany and Royals seven each. The squad trains at Railways on June 4 and 11.

The loonie is caught between markets pushing it higher and the Bank of Canada, which seems to prefer a lower dollar to help exporters. The currency rose to nearly 75.50 U.S. cents Wednesday, up about 2 per cent from last week, after a May 4 low of 72.73 U.S. cents. CIBC economist Andrew Grantham says the loonie seems volatile because it lacks clear direction. Its movements largely reflect oil prices, which fell below US$45, and the widening Canada-U.S. interest rate gap, as the Federal Reserve raised rates while Canada's has held at 0.5 per cent. Strong data, including 3.7 per cent annualized first-quarter growth, has markets expecting a rate hike; CIBC now expects one in the fourth quarter rather than 2018.

Allen Iverson, discussing his new memoir "Misunderstood" on ESPN's "First Take," said the lowest point of his life was his divorce from Tawanna Turner, whom he married in 2001. The divorce was finalized in 2013, coinciding with his retirement that October. Iverson said this prompted deep self-reevaluation, during which he recognized alcohol as a major problem and decided to stop. The couple has since reconciled. Iverson, 50, also noted that young NBA players look up to him for making them comfortable expressing themselves.

District and Sessions Judge Nasir Khan Yousafzai sentenced four murder convicts: Shehzado to death and Rs. 200,000 fine; brothers Ajab and Fateh Khan to 25 years' imprisonment and Rs. 200,000 fines each; Dilbar Khan to 25 years' imprisonment and Rs. 105,000 fine.

Texas lawmakers passed HB 8, replacing the STAAR standardized test with three shorter exams administered at the beginning, middle, and end of the school year, launching in 2027-28. The law bans practice tests and requires scores to be released about two days after each exam. However, parents, teachers, and administrators worry the changes could increase student stress and testing time rather than reduce it, since the end-of-year test will still heavily influence school accountability ratings. A TEA study on reducing testing's weight in ratings isn't due until 2029-30, and implementation isn't required. Critics say the law largely codifies what districts already do, and educators want greater input on the new test and less restrictive testing-day protocols. Some hope the approved assessment menu includes MAP tests, which they view as less stressful for students.

Germany seeks to organize Central Europe ("Middle Europe") under its control, facing four critical problems: the Poles, Czechs, South Slavs, and Bulgaria. If these peoples become accomplices or servants of German policy, Berlin would dominate the continent. The United States should oppose not economic unification itself but the imperialistic control of the region by ruling groups in Berlin, Vienna, and Budapest. The alliance is bound by shared interests: subjection of the Poles, Czechs, and Croats; German control over Austria-Hungary's external affairs and resources; German-Magyar ascendency; Bulgaria's grievance over the treaty of Bucharest; Turkey's dependence on Germany for its integrity; and postwar debts owed to Germany. American assets include the economic weapon—the threat of excluding Germany from raw materials, markets, and trade routes—which pressures all German classes and could win concessions. In Austria-Hungary, assets include nationalist discontent among Czechs and South Slavs and the rulers' desire to preserve their patrimony through no annexations, disarmament, and a league of nations. US policy should stir nationalist discontent while refusing dismemberment, thereby pushing Austria-Hungary toward independence from Berlin.

This passage presents LAPIS, a compiler framework built on MLIR designed to combine performance, portability, and productivity. It addresses two challenges: developing a compiler framework based on lessons from Kokkos, a performance-portable C++ framework, and enabling high-performance coupling between C++ computational science and engineering (CSE) codes and Python-based ML frameworks by compiling Python ML functions into Kokkos-based C++ code.

LAPIS accepts linalg-on-tensors MLIR input via torch-mlir and MPACT frontends and provides an automatic lowering pipeline to portable, parallel Kokkos C++ source code. Its five contributions to MLIR are: a custom Kokkos dialect with parallel loop operations (range_parallel, team_parallel, thread_parallel), synchronization operations (single, team_barrier), and linear algebra operations (gemm, gemv); mapping of Kokkos Kernels linear algebra operations to sparse and dense tensors; lowering passes supporting accelerators; a Kokkos-inspired memory model including DualView; and a Kokkos emitter that generates C++ source code.

The kokkos-loop-mapping pass maps scf.parallel loops to Kokkos loops based on nesting depth, estimates parallelism (e.g., for CSR-like patterns) to compute team size and vector length heuristics, and inserts synchronization operations.

Related work such as TACO, COMET, MPACT, Triton, DaCe, DISTAL, and LegateSparse has limitations in extensibility, architecture support, or performance portability.

LAPIS is demonstrated by lowering sparse and dense linear algebra operations and coupling CSE with AI/ML use cases, matching hand-optimized performance on AMD MI300A and NVIDIA H100 GPUs and Intel Granite Rapids CPUs.

This paper proves that strong pseudorandom unitaries (PRUs) exist in the quantum Haar random oracle model (QHROM), where all parties have oracle access to a Haar-random unitary U and its inverse U†. PRUs are efficiently computable unitaries that no quantum polynomial-time adversary can distinguish from Haar-random unitaries via oracle access.

Prior work: PRUs were first defined by [JLS18]. Constructing PRUs from one-way functions was only recently achieved through a series of works culminating in [MH25]. In the QHROM, [BFV20] proposed pseudorandom state generators without proof; [HY24] proved pseudorandom function-like state generators exist in the QHROM; and [ABGL25c] constructed PRUs in the weaker inverseless QHROM (iQHROM), showing one parallel query is insecure while two sequential queries suffice. Whether PRUs exist in the full QHROM (with inverse access) remained open.

Main result (Theorem 1.1): Strong PRUs exist in the QHROM. The construction G_U(1^λ, k) = X_{k3} · U_λ · X_{k2} · U_λ · X_{k1} makes two queries to the Haar random oracle and requires only O(log^(1+ε)(n)) bits of randomness for security against poly(n)-query adversaries.

Proof approach: The analysis uses Ma-Huang's path-recording framework, in which oracle access to a Haar unitary and its inverse is simulated by partial isometries V and V†. The ideal experiment (two independent Haar unitaries) is replaced by two path-recording isometries V1, V2 with independent databases, while the real experiment uses a single isometry V with a combined database. The main technical contribution is an approximate isometry S that merges the two databases into one while simulating keys (k1, k2, k3). Using query-by-query analysis with a progress measure (the adversary's distinguishing advantage after each query), the authors prove operator norm bounds such as ∥(VS − SV1)Π≤t∥op = negl(n), showing S maps the real experiment's state close to the ideal one.

Simplifications include: exploiting unitary invariance of the Haar measure to transform the oracle pair (U, X_{k3}UX_{k2}UX_{k1}) into (X_{k3}UX_{k1}, UX_{k2}U); working with non-norm-preserving operators instead of isometries; and decoupling the L and R registers by replacing V_L, V_R with F_L, F_R.

The security proof proceeds through hybrids: the real experiment (O1 = U, O2 = X_{k3}UX_{k2}UX_{k1}) → H1 (rebalanced via Haar invariance) → H2 (replace U with V) → H3 (replace V with F) → H4 (introduce S; the core technical step) → H5 (return to V1, V2) → the ideal experiment (two independent Haar unitaries U1, U2).

The paper motivates studying the QHROM by its utility for analyzing random circuits used in quantum benchmarking and black-hole dynamics, and by implications for the plain model, such as [ABGL25c]'s use of iQHROM PRUs to shorten PRU key lengths relative to output length.

Chipotle released its new queso dip on Sept. 12 to boost sales, but customers criticized its price—$3.95 for small chips and queso, $6.25 for large—and some disliked the taste. Spokesman Chris Arnold cited test-market data showing 63% would visit more often and said there are no plans to lower the price.

An email forwarded by Peggy Mahoney to several Enron executives on August 28, 2000, contains the Energy Central Deregulation Public Forum from August 25, 2000. The forum poses a new question—whether policy should change to encourage natural gas exploration and production on federal lands and the continental shelf, given that nearly 95% of planned power plants will be gas-fired and prices are predicted to reach record highs this winter—with responses due September 15, 2000. It also publishes selected responses to the previous question about whether power generators were deliberately manipulating the San Diego Gas & Electric market and whether price caps should be imposed. Respondents offered mixed views: some blamed flawed California deregulation legislation, supply-demand imbalances, or generator collusion; others attributed price spikes to weather, gas costs, and regulatory neglect. Most respondents opposed price caps, arguing they would discourage new generation investment and hide true costs, while a few supported caps or cost-of-service pricing.

Paul Clement is set to be named Swansea manager after Bayern Munich granted permission for talks. The former Carlo Ancelotti assistant was the club's top choice to replace Bob Bradley, dismissed after a 4-1 defeat to West Ham. Clement is expected to sign a deal until 2019 with a £30million transfer budget. Swansea sit 19th in the Premier League, having conceded 44 goals in 19 games, and face relegation.

CEMEX, a Mexico-based cement company, became one of the world's largest building materials suppliers through international acquisitions beginning in 1992, including the 2005 purchase of UK-based RMC and the $15.3 billion takeover of Australia's Rinker Group in 2007. Its success, notable for an emerging-market multinational in an industry with little cross-border product movement, was attributed to its post-merger integration (PMI) approach, known as the "CEMEX Way." This process standardized business processes, technology, and organizational structure globally while granting countries operational flexibility and deliberately learning best practices from acquired firms. Its internationalization occurred in four stages: laying the groundwork (consolidating Mexico through the 1989 Tolteca acquisition and building IT systems like CEMEXNET), stepping out (the 1992 acquisition of two Spanish firms, which provided lower-cost capital and yielded $120 million in annual savings), growing up (acquisitions in Latin America, the Caribbean, and Asia, plus a 1999 NYSE listing), and stepping up (Southdown in 2000, RMC in 2005, and Rinker in 2007). PMI duration fell from 25 months for the Spanish acquisitions to under five months for Southdown, and the RMC deal delivered over $200 million in synergy savings within one year. CEMEX's share price fell precipitously in 2008 amid the global downturn, credit crisis, and leverage from the Rinker acquisition.

A federal judge dismissed Drake's defamation lawsuit against Universal Music Group over Kendrick Lamar's 2024 song "Not Like Us," which called Drake a "certified pedophile." Judge Jeannette A. Vargas ruled the lyrics were "nonactionable opinion" made during a heated rap battle. The suit, which also included harassment and deceptive acts claims, alleged UMG promoted the song and arranged Lamar's 2025 Super Bowl performance. Drake plans to appeal.

The 1953 East Berlin and 1956 Poznań riots were localized, but the 1956 Hungarian revolt was nationwide and its suppression marked a turning point for the Soviet Union and NATO. After Soviet occupation in 1944, Hungarian Communists under Rákosi consolidated power by 1949 and imposed collectivization and rapid industrialization. Discontent in 1956 stemmed from an irresolute leadership encouraged by de-Stalinization and Titoism, a failing economy, repression following Poznań, and Poland's appointment of Gomułka, which suggested national Communism might be tolerated. After a Budapest rally turned violent when the AVH fired on crowds, revolutionary councils demanded nationalism, neutrality, and Soviet withdrawal. Soviet tanks entered Budapest on 24 October; Nagy was reinstated as prime minister, Gero was replaced by Kádár, and troops briefly withdrew. Using the Suez crisis as a diversion, the Soviets surrounded Budapest on 1 November and attacked on 3/4 November, crushing resistance by 30 November; about 25,000 Hungarians and 7,000 Soviet soldiers were killed.

The DAWN-PLASMA study is a randomized, open-label, phase 2 proof-of-concept multicenter trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of convalescent plasma in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Participants were randomized 2:1 to standard of care (SOC) plus convalescent plasma versus SOC alone. The study was conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP guidelines, with IEC approval and informed consent required. The primary endpoint was the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Inclusion required confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and illness with radiographic infiltrates or clinical assessment with SpO2 ≤94%; exclusions included mechanical ventilation at or before randomization, prior grade 3 allergic reaction to fresh frozen plasma, treatment restrictions excluding ventilation, and recent anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody administration. Six patients withdrew consent or were screen failures before the intervention and were replaced, with no patients lost to follow-up afterward. Participants received 800–1000 mL of plasma in four doses, with the first dose within 12 hours of randomization; plasma with neutralizing antibody titers below 1/160 was not permitted.

Springfield, Massachusetts officer Conrad Lariviere faces disciplinary action for commenting "Hahahaha love this" on Facebook about a car striking and killing a counter-protester at a white supremacist rally in Charlottesville, Virginia. He later apologized and denied being racist. Commissioner John Barbieri initiated an internal investigation, and Mayor Domenic Sarno denounced the comments. The victim was 32-year-old Heather Heyer; 19 others were injured.

Williams & Connolly confirmed that hackers accessed a small number of attorney email accounts through a zero-day attack, but found no evidence of further access to its IT system or extraction of confidential client data. The firm believes the hackers are affiliated with a nation-state actor behind recent attacks on law firms and companies, and has taken steps to block the threat. A Mandiant warning said hackers tied to the Chinese government have targeted firms seeking information related to U.S. national security and international trade.

Coppin State University, a historically Black institution in Maryland, more than quadrupled its out-of-state enrollment over two years through its Expand Eagle Nation program, which offers in-state tuition to students from the 41 states and territories without an HBCU, plus the District of Columbia. Out-of-state students grew from 81 to 195 in 2024, then to 416 of the 1,000-student incoming class this fall; overall enrollment rose 26 percent. The university raised its profile through high school visits, bus and billboard advertising, community college transfer partnerships, and outreach to college-search organizations. The growth coincides with rising HBCU popularity following the 2023 affirmative action ban and concerns about the impending demographic cliff. Coppin expanded housing and courses to accommodate students, though some families initially doubted the tuition offer was genuine.

The passage describes video output data pins from a Texas Instruments datasheet. Three signal groups carry the 8 MSBs of G/Y/YC, B/CB/C, and R/CR video data, with functions varying by mode: RGB, YUV444, Y/C, and BT.656. Footnotes define pin notation abbreviations.

The passage is from the datasheet of the TPS7H500x-SP series (TPS7H5001-SP to TPS7H5004-SP), radiation-hardness-assured peak current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. Key points:

- **Enable/UVLO**: The EN pin can be tied to VLDO, driven externally, or configured with a resistor divider to program start-up and shutdown thresholds; UVLO should be approximately 75% or less of input voltage.
- **Reference and error amplifier**: An internal 1.23-V bandgap reference is divided to 0.613 V; a 470-nF REFCAP capacitor is required. The transconductance error amplifier has 1800 µA/V transconductance and ~10,000 V/V DC gain.
- **Soft start**: A capacitor on the SS pin sets soft-start time; synchronous rectifier outputs activate when SS exceeds 1 V.
- **Switching frequency (100 kHz–2 MHz)**: Set via internal oscillator (RT resistor), external synchronization (SYNC clock at twice the switching frequency), or primary-secondary mode for two synchronized controllers.
- **Outputs**: OUTA/OUTB primary and SRA/SRB synchronous rectifier outputs (~150 mA peak; external gate drive recommended).
- **Protection and control**: Programmable dead times (PS/SP), leading edge blank time (LEB), pulse skipping, duty cycle limits via DCL pin (100%, 75%, or 50%), current sensing (CS_ILIM, 1.05-V threshold) with cycle-by-cycle limiting and hiccup mode (HICC), external FAULT pin, slope compensation (RSC), Type 2A/2B frequency compensation, and thermal shutdown at 175°C (restart below 160°C).
- **Application example**: A 500-kHz synchronous push-pull converter with GaN FETs and 5-V output, detailing component selection.
- **Power supply and layout**: 4–14 V input with bypassing recommendations; layout guidelines address noise, grounding, and trace routing.

The Democratic Party has gained full control of the government, holding the House of Representatives, the Senate, and the offices of President and Vice-President. The speaker interprets this as the nation using the party for a larger purpose than mere party success: a shift in the nation's plans and point of view. While national life is great in wealth, industry, moral force, and government, evil has accompanied the good—waste of riches, uncounted human costs of industrial achievement, and a government too often used for private and selfish purposes. The task now is to cleanse, reconsider, and restore, correcting evil without impairing good. Items for reform include the tariff, the banking and currency system, the industrial system, inefficient agriculture, and neglected natural resources. Government must also safeguard health and rights through sanitary, pure food, and labor laws, which are matters of justice rather than pity. The speaker pledges to restore rather than destroy, adopt justice as the motto, and declares this a day of dedication rather than triumph, summoning honest, patriotic, forward-looking men to his side.

This paper proposes LG-CD, a Language-Guided Change Detection model for remote sensing change detection (RSCD) that integrates visual and textual information. The model uses a pre-trained SAM2 encoder as the shared visual feature extractor, fine-tuned with lightweight multi-layer adapters, and CLIP as the text feature extractor. A Text Fusion Attention Module (TFAM) aligns textual prompts with multi-scale visual features via multi-head cross-attention, treating visual features as queries and word embeddings as key-value pairs, while a visual-semantic fusion decoder generates change detection masks through cross-attention. The paper reviews prior approaches—traditional thresholding and morphological methods, CNN-based and Transformer-based deep learning methods, and foundation model approaches—noting limitations such as sensitivity to interference, restricted long-range context modeling, data scarcity, high annotation costs, and reliance on unimodal visual information. Experimental results indicate that combining visual features with textual semantics improves semantic understanding, detection accuracy, and generalization.

The White House said it was not defending Roseanne Barr over the racist tweet that led ABC to cancel her sitcom, but President Trump and press secretary Sarah Sanders said ABC owed them an apology for airing derogatory comments about the administration. Trump tweeted that Disney's Bob Iger never apologized to him, though Iger had called Valerie Jarrett about Barr's remarks. Sanders cited examples of media figures' attacks on Trump, calling it a double standard, and said the President was focused on other matters.

Indianapolis Public Schools will hold its first public meeting Tuesday on a proposal to close three high schools, based on a Facilities Utilization Taskforce report recommending closures by 2018-2019. The report cites enrollment decline from a 1967 peak of 109,000 to about 30,000 students, leaving all seven high schools under capacity. More meetings run through May; the administration will identify recommended closures by June, with a board vote in September.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan spoke to the media before the team's final minicamp practice prior to training camp in late July. He said practice was competitive, with the offense edging out a strong red-zone defense, and noted areas still needing improvement. He said his father, who attends as an observer, will have an office next to his, watch film, and offer ideas, though he is not considered part of the staff. Shanahan said this helps him as a first-time head coach by providing another trusted set of eyes. He plans to vacation with his family in Mexico before camp. He also called play-action very important to his offense, saying it puts defenses in a bind, reduces pressure on the quarterback and line, and creates explosive plays.

California lawmakers are debating competing proposals to keep Southern California Edison from bankruptcy as the utility struggles with over $3.5 billion in debt. Options include the governor's $2.76 billion transmission line purchase, a Keeley-Hertzberg plan to buy the lines for $2.4 billion with additional provisions, a Senate plan with a five-year purchase option at book value, and a "straight bailout" proposal charging consumers a monthly fee. Consumer groups have criticized the rescue plans as excessive.

PG&E filed a lawsuit against the state seeking compensation for long-term power contracts seized by Gov. Davis in January 2001; their value at seizure was estimated between $150 million and $347 million. The state's consumer advocate also criticized the proposed SDG&E rescue plan, including the $1 billion transmission line purchase, as too generous to shareholders.

An editorial argued that lawmakers face difficult choices about who will pay for past utility debts and state power purchases, contending all parties must share the burden.

In economic news, the Consumer Price Index rose 0.2 percent in June as electricity prices surged while gasoline costs retreated. Contra Costa County approved spending up to $1.7 million on energy conservation upgrades for nine county buildings. The state is selling surplus electricity purchased at an average of $138 per megawatt-hour for as little as $1 per megawatt-hour due to cool weather and reduced demand. Duke Energy reported a 27 percent increase in second-quarter profit driven by trading and wholesale power businesses. Separately, San Diego County officials proposed waiving solar installation fees, and the Pechanga tribe sought federal trust status for land in the path of a proposed SDG&E power line.

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture by Will Ma focuses on post-flop poker strategy, using repeated example hands to illustrate key concepts.

The lecture begins with the concept of checking to the preflop aggressor: opponents check because the preflop raiser's range is stronger (potentially containing pocket aces), and they prefer smaller pots. Bet sizing guidance suggests betting roughly half the pot on the flop, increasing to about 60% on the turn and 70% on the river (50–100% of pot overall), since betting too small gives opponents a free option to check-raise.

The "Fundamental Theorem of Poker" states that bets should either be value bets with strong hands (getting worse hands to call) or bluffs with weak hands (getting better hands to fold), while middle-strength hands should check, since betting folds out weaker hands and keeps stronger ones. Players should avoid continuation betting on "scary" coordinated flops (three connected cards of one suit) or into many opponents.

For calling bets, the general rule is to fold most hands to a half-pot bet, since most hands miss most flops. Examples show folding weak aces, gutshots, and small pairs, while calling with overcards on paired boards, bottom pairs, second pair, and top pair with weak kickers. Raising requirements depend on stack size: with 40+ big blinds, two-pair or better (both hole cards pairing) is generally needed; with around 25 big blinds, top pair justifies going all-in.

Leading (betting rather than checking to the preflop raiser) is described as an advanced, optional play used when the flop favors the caller's range, requiring careful balancing to avoid exploitation.

The lecture covers implied odds—calling hands like suited connectors or set-mining with small pairs despite insufficient direct odds, because they can win large pots postflop—and reverse implied odds, which explain folding weak hands like 7-2 offsuit even when equity calculations permit calling, since such hands are difficult to play postflop.

Two "bluffing epiphanies" are presented: (1) when bluffing before the river, the number of outs matters more than current hand strength, so draws are ideal bluffing hands; and (2) bluffs should consider what hands they represent within one's range, and should be abandoned when the board favors the opponent's range. The lecture concludes by encouraging students to apply these concepts in the online tournaments.

Prof. Cyril Dim of the University of Nigeria explains that cervical cancer is a malignant condition of the cervix, caused almost entirely by sexually transmitted human papillomavirus (HPV), particularly types 16 and 18. The disease has a symptomless precancerous stage detectable by pap smear, recommended every three years, and later every five years. Early-stage symptoms include post-coital bleeding and foul-smelling vaginal discharge; late-stage symptoms include weight loss, weakness, anaemia, pelvic pain, and loss of urinary or faecal control. Diagnosis requires tissue biopsy and histology. Early-stage cancer can be cured through radical surgery or radiotherapy, while late-stage cancer is managed with radiotherapy and chemotherapy to prolong life. In Nigeria, an estimated 15,000 new cases and 10,000 deaths occur yearly, making cervical cancer second to breast cancer among female cancers. Pregnancy is possible in the early, symptomless stage. Some people attribute the illness to witchcraft.

A federal judge ruled that Nirvana's 1991 album cover depicting a naked baby floating toward a dollar bill is not child pornography, dismissing Spencer Elden's 2021 lawsuit. Judge Fernando Olguin found only one factor—Elden's nudity—applied, comparing the image to a family photo of a nude child bathing.

The coach states his team is better than it has shown in the first two games and must now prove it, noting there are no guarantees in the game. He discusses line matching, saying the visiting coach can force favorable matchups and that the opponent's discipline makes this difficult. Chris Neil was given the day off because his wife is having a baby. The coach does not believe the opponent dominated his team, but says they outpositioned and outdefended them and capitalized on mistakes. He praises his young goaltender for giving the team a chance to win both games, while noting they have not tested Giguere. He identifies face-offs as a problem, saying his centers must at least get ties and need better support from wingers, and credits Pahlsson's line for winning draws and protecting the puck. He attributes the team's struggles to turnovers, failed stretch passes, and a lack of puck control and speed, saying they must play more patiently as they did against New Jersey. He expects Alfredsson and other forwards to return to earlier form once they get the puck more. He praises Rob Niedermayer, whom he once traded for in Anaheim, as a strong role player. He anticipates an emotional home crowd and plans to use his fourth line more. He says the team must adjust its attack rather than seeking stretch passes against Anaheim's defensive structure.

This position paper examines the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in higher education. The authors note AI's growing presence, accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic, and argue it has transformed higher education across teaching-learning processes, research, institutional management, and relationships with the outside. Based on document analysis from the B-ON and SCILIT databases, the paper identifies differences between AI-oriented and traditional higher education in governance, training models, and research approaches. AI offers advantages such as personalized learning, intelligent tutoring, automated grading, predictive analytics, plagiarism detection, and support for research and administrative tasks. However, its integration faces challenges including equity of access, privacy and ethical concerns, teacher training needs, financial costs, organizational resistance, and AI's inherent limitations, such as inability to account for emotions. The authors emphasize developing AI literacy beyond digital literacy for all stakeholders, reshaping teachers' roles, and participatory implementation. They conclude that higher education institutions cannot remain static in the face of AI and must balance technological adoption with academic freedom while encouraging discussion of AI competencies and future research.

A hockey player describes being surprised when coach Pat put him back in the lineup after two weeks out, feeling nervous but grateful, and crediting his hardworking teammates. He notes the team's three championships in nine years, a difficult season that included losing Holik but adding Madden and Marshall, and praises Pat as a demanding, focused, no-nonsense coach who kept the team from becoming complacent.

An analysis by University of Notre Dame Law School professor Derek Muller found that 92.45% of campaign contributions from lawyers and staff at the nation's 100 top-grossing firms and 50 larger plaintiffs-side firms went to Democrats in 2023 and 2024—a roughly 12-1 Democratic-to-Republican ratio, up from 6-1 in a 2021 analysis covering 2017 through 2020. About $52 million went to Democratic-affiliated groups compared to about $4 million to Republican-affiliated groups. Cleary Gottlieb, Fried Frank, and Mintz Levin had the highest percentages of Democratic contributions, while Nelson Mullins, Lewis Brisbois, and Ogletree had the lowest.
Purity and higher-order moments of m-qubit states underpin quantum information science, statistical mechanics, and many-body physics.

U.S. stock index futures rose Thursday amid a strong start to earnings season and rebounding oil prices, though North Korea tensions and the French election kept investors cautious. Of 57 S&P 500 companies reporting, 75.4% beat expectations, with quarterly profits estimated up 10.8%, the best since 2011. Qualcomm rose on strong results while eBay fell on a weak forecast.

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture by Hong Liu covers discrete symmetries and path integrals for fermions. It begins with a review of discrete symmetries—parity, time reversal, and charge conjugation—in complex scalar theory. At the quantum level, symmetries are implemented by unitary operators, except time reversal, which must be anti-unitary. This is derived by requiring the time-reversed wave function to satisfy the Schrödinger equation with t → −t, forcing the time reversal operator to be anti-linear (it picks up a minus sign when passing through i). The adjoint of anti-linear operators also requires a modified definition.

For the complex scalar field, transformations carry phases η_P, η_T, η_C. Requiring parity squared to return the original field constrains η_P to ±1, defining scalars (+1) and pseudoscalars (−1), such as the pion. The unitary operators flip the momentum of creation and annihilation operators, and charge conjugation exchanges particles and antiparticles.

For the Dirac field, parity requires a matrix D acting on spinor space. Requiring the transformed field to satisfy the Dirac equation in the reflected space forces D to commute with γ⁰ and anticommute with γⁱ, so D is proportional to γ⁰. For charge conjugation, a matrix C relating γ^μ to −γ^{μT} must exist; it always does because both sets satisfy the same Clifford algebra and all representations are equivalent. Time reversal uses a matrix D_T related to C via γ⁵.

Finally, the lecture introduces path integrals for fermions. Because fermionic operators obey anti-commutation relations, Berezin, a former Soviet physicist, proposed in the early 1960s—solving a problem Feynman could not—integrating over anti-commuting Grassmann variables. Since θ² = 0, functions of such variables truncate at finite order. Differentiation depends on direction (left derivatives are the convention). Integration is fixed by linearity and the requirement that total derivatives integrate to zero; for a single variable, integration equals differentiation. Under a change of variables θ′ = aθ, one finds dθ′ = (1/a)dθ, opposite to the ordinary case.

This patent application describes systems, devices, and methods for spatially and temporally synchronizing a rotating LIDAR sensor with one or more cameras for sensor fusion. The LIDAR sensor rotates about an axis, emitting light pulses and detecting reflections to scan an environment and generate point cloud data. The cameras detect external light and together provide an array of adjacent rows of sensing elements aligned parallel to the LIDAR's axis of rotation. A controller operates the cameras in a rolling shutter mode to obtain a sequence of image pixel rows in an order matching the order in which the LIDAR emits light pulses, with each row exposed during a respective exposure time period. This arrangement aligns the cameras' "fast axis" with the LIDAR's fast axis, improving the matching of image pixels with LIDAR data in both time and viewing direction. Example implementations include a camera ring arranged around the LIDAR's rotation axis, with cameras having partially overlapping fields of view to reduce blind spots. Timing configurations for image capture can be based on the LIDAR's pointing direction, rotation rate, and beam emission order. The combined LIDAR and camera data can be used to generate three-dimensional representations of the environment, such as colored point clouds, by associating LIDAR data points with corresponding image pixels.

Quantbot Technologies LP increased its stake in Zoe's Kitchen (NYSE:ZOES) by 114.5% in the 2nd quarter, holding 17,056 shares (0.09%) worth $203,000. Other institutional investors also adjusted positions, including FMR LLC's new $8.98 million stake and CalPERS's 193.3% increase. Director A Alexander Taylor II purchased 3,100 shares at $12.87 in August; insiders own 3% of the stock. Analysts hold mixed views, with a consensus "Hold" rating and $17.55 target price. The stock opened at $12.39, with a market cap of $242.04 million and a 12-month range of $10.77–$27.41. The company reported Q2 EPS of $0.06, beating estimates, on revenue of $74.30 million, up 12.1% year-over-year, though net margin and return on equity were negative. Zoe's Kitchen operates fast-casual Mediterranean-inspired restaurants.

The Supreme Court, Queens County, convicted Bradford Washington of second-degree murder, criminal possession of a weapon, reckless endangerment, and endangering the welfare of a child under indictment No. 999/05 after a jury verdict, and of second-degree murder under indictment No. 1000/05 upon a guilty plea. On appeal, both judgments were affirmed, with his claims regarding detective testimony, the consciousness-of-guilt charge, and the prosecutor's summation found unpreserved or without merit.

Darren Osborne was sentenced to life in prison with a minimum term of 43 years at Woolwich Crown Court for driving a van into worshippers outside Finsbury Park mosque in London last June, killing Makram Ali and injuring nine others. Found guilty of murder and attempted murder, Osborne reportedly shouted "I want to kill all Muslims" and claimed he wanted to kill Sadiq Khan and Jeremy Corbyn. The prosecutor said he was "brainwashed" by a BBC drama. Ali's family welcomed the verdict, and police said Osborne had planned the attack in Wales. A counterterrorism commander said Osborne failed to divide communities.

Facebook is rolling out a "Trending News" section on iOS and Android that aggregates stories from multiple sources, ranked by publication coverage. Accessed via the Explore tab, tapping a story shows headlines, videos, photos, and related Facebook posts.

Several major hedge funds trimmed healthcare stakes in the second quarter as the sector outperformed the broader market amid fading Republican efforts to repeal the Affordable Care Act. Jana Partners sold stakes in nine healthcare companies, while Third Point cut its Humana and Baxter holdings. Healthcare stocks rose 6.7 percent versus the S&P 500's 2.6 percent gain. Hedge funds also sold energy stocks, which fell 7 percent, and gained 1 percent overall.

This patent application describes an electronic smoking device (e-cigarette) featuring a coil-less atomizer that uses one or more woven fiber tubes serving as both heating element and liquid wick. Each tube has a hollow interior and an electrically conductive heating section connected to leads or electrical contacts, with end sections in contact with a liquid supply. Liquid is transported to the heating section via capillary action through the hollow interior and/or the porous fiber wall. The tubes can be U-, C-, or L-shaped and made from materials such as carbon fiber, nickel-chromium, steel, titanium, ceramics, or composites (e.g., carbon fiber woven with Dacron or silicon dioxide). This single-component design replaces the conventional separate heating wire and wick material, enabling more compact e-cigarette designs. Conductive sections have lower electrical resistance than the heating section, with total resistance typically around 3–5Ω. Multiple tubes of the same or varying diameters may be arranged in parallel or in contact to improve liquid flow or provide staged aerosol delivery. Tubes may be coated or sputtered with conductive materials to modify resistance. The document further describes e-cigarette structure (battery, LED, airflow sensor, liquid supply configurations), operating principles, and a manufacturing process involving masking and sputtering of the fiber tubes.

The United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Massachusetts issued a memorandum of decision in the dispute between Access Cardiosystems, Inc. (the Chapter 11 debtor), its investors (Moriarty, Connolly, Radley, and Zimmel), and founder and former officer/director Randall Fincke. The court had previously found Fincke breached fiduciary duties to Access and violated Massachusetts securities law, Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 110A, § 410(a)(2), by falsely stating in an October 2002 Business Plan that Access had been advised by patent counsel that its product did not infringe any patents. Fincke's motion to reconsider the § 410(a)(2) liability finding was denied, the court concluding the statement was false whether the purported advice was formal or informal. On damages, rescission was unavailable because the investors' stock was cancelled under Access's confirmed plan of reorganization; recovery was limited to securities sales made "by means of" the misstatement. Finding the investors' testimony of reliance on the Business Plan not credible, the court determined only Zimmel's October and November 2002 stock purchases, totaling $1,500,000, were made by means of the misstatement; the April 2003 Transaction and later investments were not recoverable. Judgment was entered for Zimmel for $1,500,000 plus six percent interest from May 25, 2007, and, based on Fincke's waiver, for Access for $281,534.62 plus twelve percent interest from July 6, 2004, plus costs, with postjudgment interest at the federal rate.

The BIRDS workshop aims to bridge digital library practitioners and GLAM domain experts, who often lack technical expertise, with computational researchers who may be unaware of real-world library challenges. Its goals include starting a workshop series, identifying common challenges, providing a forum at TPDL for discussing ideas and ongoing work, producing a SIGIR Forum report, and continuing the series at future conferences. Loosely modeled on the ECIR 2024 Collab-a-thon, the full-day, in-person workshop requires no paper submissions and instead features a keynote, scientific speed-dating, a panel discussion, and breakout group discussions on topics such as LLMs, OCR, and interface evaluation. The target audience is practitioners and researchers, especially newcomers, with around 25 participants expected. The organizers are Christin Katharina Kreutz and Hermann Kroll.

On August 17, 2022, Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting two actions. First, Apple's Compensation Committee approved the Apple Inc. Executive Cash Incentive Plan, under which eligible participants—members of Apple's executive team, including named executive officers and other designated employees—may receive cash incentive awards based on achievement of performance goals over performance periods established by the Committee. Awards are forfeited if a participant terminates service before the payout date unless the Committee determines otherwise. Second, Apple's Board approved amended and restated bylaws, effective the same day, which, among other things, permit special Board meetings on less than 48 hours' notice, enhance procedural and disclosure requirements for shareholder nominations and proposals, clarify the Board's authority over shareholder meeting locations and the meeting chair's powers, revise procedures for requesting special meetings and acting by written consent, require soliciting shareholders to use non-white proxy cards, and add emergency provisions. Exhibits include the Amended and Restated Bylaws and the Executive Cash Incentive Plan.

The Ohio Supreme Court upheld the constitutionality of R.C. 3105.03, which requires divorce plaintiffs to have resided in the state for one year before filing, except in actions for alimony alone. The appellant, who had not met this requirement when filing, challenged it under the "compelling governmental interest" test established in Shapiro v. Thompson and Dunn v. Blumstein for durational residency requirements that penalize the right to travel. The court distinguished divorce from welfare and voting, holding that obtaining a divorce is not a basic need and that the residency requirement does not penalize interstate travel. It further found that Ohio has a compelling interest in regulating marriage and divorce for its residents, and that the one-year requirement is the least restrictive means of ensuring its divorce laws are not applied to nonresidents, since a person's intent to establish a permanent domicile is difficult to verify by other means. The requirement has existed since 1853, and the statute exempts alimony-only actions, providing for basic needs. The judgment was affirmed. Schneider, J., concurred based on the particular facts, noting the grounds for divorce arose in New York, and indicated the decision might warrant re-examination in other circumstances.

Released on December 11, 1987, less than two months after Black Monday's 23 percent market collapse, Oliver Stone's *Wall Street* remains, per the passage, the supreme film about finance 30 years later. The author attributes this to its blend of rags-to-riches parable, Hero's Journey, and fairy tale, following broker Bud Fox's rise under Gordon Gekko's influence, and to its immersive depiction of 1980s excess. Michael Douglas, cast after Warren Beatty and Richard Gere declined the role, won the Best Actor Oscar and made Gekko—an amalgam of figures like Ivan Boesky, Michael Milken, and Carl Icahn—an enduring symbol of greed whose lines, such as "Greed is good," remain recognizable touchstones.

Developer B-S-G modified the Google Camera app to bring HDR+ to Android phones with Snapdragon 820, 821, or 835 processors. Amazon offers refunds for faulty solar-eclipse glasses. HBO refuses to pay hackers' ransom as more episodes, including Curb Your Enthusiasm, leak. Waymo patented technology that softens car bodies to protect pedestrians in collisions.

Retired Justice Anthony Kennedy's memoir is released Oct. 14, with a SCOTUSblog review to follow. Kennedy emphasizes judicial humility and integrity, writing that the Court earns respect by deciding difficult cases in proper, thoughtful ways. He rejects both originalism and pragmatism as judicial philosophies, suggesting instead that better answers to constitutional questions emerge over time through improved perspective. He discusses controversial opinions including Citizens United (campaign finance), the same-sex marriage ruling, the case deciding between Gore and Bush, and flag desecration, stressing that he focused on legal issues rather than preferred outcomes. He disliked being called the "swing justice," saying the cases swung, not him. Though personally opposed to abortion, he believed a moral wrong is not necessarily a legal wrong, and he considered but rejected resigning over the issue. He writes that presidents must give deference to Supreme Court rulings. He also recounts a chilling meeting with Putin on capital punishment, the Court's opposition to cameras in the courtroom, his home being ransacked after he declined to lower bail for a Manson family member, Justice Scalia's personal attack and later apology following the same-sex marriage decision, and his view that classic rock was avant-garde.

The Simons Observatory has deployed over 67,000 superconducting transition-edge sensor (TES) detectors across four telescopes on Cerro Toco, Chile, read out via microwave frequency multiplexing using SLAC microresonator radio frequency (SMuRF) electronics and universal focal-plane modules. For the observatory's large-aperture telescope (LAT), SMuRF electronics are mounted directly to the receiver, exposing their room-temperature coaxial cables to diurnal temperature swings that can induce phase drifts potentially mimicking TES detector signals. Using off-resonance "pilot" tones, the authors measured time delays over 22.6 hours of observations and found phase drifts correlated with ambient temperature but only at the level of a few picoseconds per diurnal cycle. An analytical conversion to TES noise-equivalent current shows this effect is a small contribution to on-sky detector noise, lies within the readout noise budget, and is not expected to affect the telescope's mapping speed.

Amazon.com, Inc.'s Form 10-K annual report for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2016. Incorporated in Delaware in 1996 and headquartered in Seattle, Washington, Amazon completed its IPO in May 1997 and trades on NASDAQ under "AMZN." The company operates three segments—North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS)—serving consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators. It sells retail products through its websites, manufactures electronic devices (Kindle, Fire tablets, Fire TV, Echo), offers the Amazon Prime membership program, and provides AWS cloud services.

The report identifies risks including intense competition, strains from rapid expansion, international regulatory challenges (notably in China and India), fulfillment network optimization, seasonality (32–33% of annual revenue recognized in the fourth quarter), data security breaches, system interruptions, inventory management, intellectual property protection, stock price volatility, evolving government regulation, sales and income tax liabilities, supplier dependence, and payments-related risks.

As of December 31, 2016, Amazon employed approximately 341,400 full- and part-time employees. For 2016, net sales were $135,987 million (27% growth), operating income was $4,186 million, and net income was $2,371 million. Segment net sales were North America $79,785 million, International $43,983 million, and AWS $12,219 million. Operating cash flow was $16,443 million, and cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $26.0 billion. The company has never declared or paid dividends. As of January 25, 2017, 477,170,618 shares were outstanding with 2,448 shareholders of record. Jeffrey P. Bezos serves as President, CEO, and Chairman of the Board.

Evelyn Montiel spent years helping her family run an ice cream truck and frozen fruit stand in East Oakland while excelling in high school as an A-student and class president. With help from Students Rising Above (SRA), she transferred to USC after dropping out of an East Coast college following a bout of depression, and thrived there with SRA's internship support. After graduating during the recession and finding no jobs, she returned to the family business until SRA connected her with an investment firm interview that launched her finance career. She now works as a broker at a Silicon Valley startup and credits SRA, hoping to inspire similar students.

Tesla, Inc.'s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022 describes the company's business, operations, and risk factors. Tesla designs, manufactures, sells and leases fully electric vehicles (Model 3, Y, S, and X, with early production and deliveries of the Tesla Semi beginning in December 2022) and energy generation and storage products (Powerwall, Megapack, retrofit solar systems, and Solar Roof), operating through two reportable segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. The company sells directly to customers through its website and company-owned stores, operates a global Supercharger network (opened to non-Tesla vehicles in November 2021), and offers financing, leasing, and an insurance product available in 12 states. Manufacturing facilities are located in Northern California, New York, Texas, Nevada, China (Gigafactory Shanghai), and Germany (Gigafactory Berlin-Brandenburg). As of December 31, 2022, Tesla had 127,855 full-time employees, a 29,000 increase year over year. As of January 25, 2023, 3,164,102,701 shares of common stock were outstanding, and the aggregate market value held by non-affiliates was $580.48 billion as of June 30, 2022. The report discusses the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022, which provides up to $7,500 in federal tax credits for qualifying electric vehicle purchases through 2032, as well as regulatory credits Tesla earns and sells. Risk factors include macroeconomic effects of COVID-19, supply chain constraints including semiconductor shortages, production ramp delays, reliance on battery cell suppliers such as Panasonic and CATL, competition in automotive and energy markets, product defects and liability, dependence on Elon Musk (who also serves as CEO of SpaceX and Twitter), obligations under the SUNY Foundation agreement for Gigafactory New York (including a potential $41 million program payment), and cybersecurity threats to information technology systems.

NVIDIA Corporation's Form 10-K annual report for fiscal year ended January 29, 2017. NVIDIA, a Delaware corporation headquartered in Santa Clara, California, trades on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under the symbol NVDA, with 589 million shares outstanding as of February 24, 2017. The company, which invented the GPU and has extended into artificial intelligence, operates two reportable segments—GPU and Tegra Processor—serving four markets: Gaming, Professional Visualization, Datacenter, and Automotive. Product brands include GeForce for gamers, Quadro for designers, Tesla and DGX for AI researchers, GRID for cloud-based visual computing, and Tegra processors for mobile and automotive platforms.

NVIDIA uses a fabless manufacturing model, relying on foundries such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and Samsung, along with subcontractors for assembly, testing, and packaging. As of January 29, 2017, the company had 10,299 employees, including 7,282 in research and development; R&D expenses were $1.46 billion in fiscal 2017. The passage consists of news reports from November 27, 2001, covering Enron's financial crisis and the renegotiation of its merger with Dynegy. Dynegy confirmed it was in talks to restructure its acquisition of Enron, originally valued at $9 billion in stock (0.2685 Dynegy shares per Enron share), with new terms reportedly cutting the price by more than 40% to about $5 billion (an exchange ratio below 0.15). Negotiations also included additional funding of $500 million to $1 billion and restructuring of Enron's roughly $13 billion in debt. Enron's trading business deteriorated as partners cut back transactions over credit concerns; one broker estimated Enron's over-the-counter trading volume at about 25% of its level a month earlier, though an Enron spokesman disputed this figure. Enron's equity trading unit was being closed, with roughly 60 employees laid off. Enron's stock fell to around $4, down from $78 a year earlier, leaving a market value under $3 billion. Moody's said Enron's Baa3 rating would remain unchanged for the day. Bankers led by J.P. Morgan Chase were unable for two weeks to raise up to $2 billion in private equity, with investors including Prince Alwaleed, the Carlyle Group, and Blackstone declining to invest. Enron faced a $690 million payment due that week, $9 billion in payments due before the end of 2002, and less than $2 billion in cash. Multiple employee lawsuits over 401(k) losses and more than a dozen shareholder suits had been filed. Some hedge funds considered trades based on the lower exchange ratio, while many arbitrageurs remained wary the deal could collapse and push Enron into bankruptcy. The DAWN-Plasma trial was a randomized, multicenter, open-label phase 2 proof-of-concept study evaluating convalescent plasma added to standard of care versus standard of care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Between May 2020 and January 2021, 489 patients were randomized 2:1 to convalescent plasma (n=326) or control (n=163). The intervention consisted of 800–1000 mL of high-titer convalescent plasma given in 4 doses, with the first dose administered within 12 hours of randomization. The primary endpoint, proportion of patients alive and free of mechanical ventilation at Day 15, showed no difference between groups (83.7% vs 84.1%, OR 0.99, p=0.976). No significant differences were found in any secondary endpoints, including mortality. Safety outcomes were similar between groups: adverse events occurred in 28.13% (plasma) versus 30.06% (control), fatal AEs in 10.31% versus 9.82%, and SAEs in approximately 20.6% in both groups. Transfusion-related side effects occurred in 6.0% of the intervention group, with no TRALI cases reported. Higher endogenous neutralizing antibody titers at Day 0 and Day 6 correlated with better outcomes, but the intervention did not increase titers. The study concluded that early administration of high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma did not change the natural course of COVID-19 in hospitalized patients.

This study used pooled NHANES data (2009–2020) from 32,498 US adults to identify empirical dietary patterns and examine their associations with cardiovascular disease (CVD), social determinants of health (SDOH) scores, and SNAP participation. Principal components analysis identified four dietary patterns: American (most common, 33.7%; lowest HEI-2020 score, 42.4), Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy (27.9%; highest HEI score, 62.0), Prudent (22.6%; HEI 58.2), and Legume (15.8%; HEI 55.0). In fully adjusted models, adults with prevalent CVD were more likely to follow the American pattern (37.1% vs. 33.3% without CVD). Higher SDOH scores were associated with greater alignment with the American and Legume patterns and less alignment with the Prudent and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy patterns. SNAP participants and income-eligible non-participants were more likely to follow the American pattern and less likely to follow the Prudent pattern than non-eligible adults. Most associations were similar across race and ethnicity, though some differences were observed, such as no association between SDOH score and the American pattern among Hispanic individuals. The authors conclude that empirical dietary patterns vary by cardiovascular health and especially socioeconomic vulnerability, and that nutrition interventions—including Food is Medicine approaches and SNAP improvements—should consider these naturally occurring patterns. Limitations include the cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data.

The Pauli–Fierz Hamiltonian describes electron–photon interactions in optical cavities, modifying molecular electronic structure and producing polaritonic states. Standard quantum chemistry methods are not directly applicable, and the non-local, long-range coupling demands a basis capturing both smooth and rapidly varying wavefunction features. The sinc basis—orthonormal and systematically improvable—addresses this, though its O(N⁴) two-electron integral cost can be mitigated via sparse or low-rank approximations.

A player's stable personality and composure helped him score key playoff goals, including an overtime winner. The team focused on getting pucks in and punishing the opposing defense. The Wham play is a lesser-known complementary run concept, best described as a Trap play with a Tight End or Fullback pulling to kick out a Defensive Lineman instead of a Guard. Its main strength is creating favorable running angles quickly and unexpectedly, since defenses rarely practice against it if the offense seldom runs Trap. Its main weakness is that it is complicated and time-consuming to install, requiring the offensive line and Fullback to correctly identify fronts and assignments, as well as a bigger, more powerful blocker to execute the kickout. The passage details blocking assignments for the Wham play against a 3-4 Odd front and a 4-3 Even front. Two variations are described: the Gun H-Back Wham RPO, which targets the Nose Tackle and includes pass options, and the Shotgun Influence Wham, which traps a 3-tech after he widens expecting a down block.

This study assessed horizontal transmission of hepatitis C virus (HCV) among household members of HCV-positive patients attending CUSP health center in Huye district, Rwanda. A descriptive cross-sectional design was used, with 148 participants from 30 families tested using HCV Ab rapid tests and ELISA confirmation between January 2 and February 2, 2021. The study found an HCV prevalence of 10.8% (16 of 148 participants), higher than Rwanda's reported general prevalence of 4%. Significant risk factors associated with HCV infection included HBV history (p=0.001), HIV history (p=0.001), and unprotected sex (p=0.016), while blood transfusion showed no significant association (p=0.058). Awareness of HCV transmission was low, with 93.9% of participants answering questions incorrectly, and awareness showed no significant correlation with test results (p=0.079). The study concluded that unprotected sex was the leading contributor to transmission and recommended early screening of family members of positive cases, improved follow-up of HCV-positive patients by the Ministry of Health, and education on transmission. Limitations included the cross-sectional design, which could not determine the origin of infection; phylogenetic and countrywide studies were recommended.

This paper introduces the Construction Defining Functionality (CDF) framework, a formal model for analyzing the layered structure of computational problems. CDF decomposes a function into three structural spaces—syntactic (Ssyn), semantic (Ssem), and logical (Slog)—connected by mappings αf (syntax to semantics), βf (semantics to logic), and γf (syntax to logic). Unlike the set-theoretic intension/extension distinction, CDF treats intensionality as internal generative rules and extensionality as observable outcomes. The framework defines stability (polynomially bounded mappings) and explosiveness, classifying problems as ComCDF (compositionally coherent, where γf = βf ∘ αf with stable αf), ExpCDF (explosive), or Semi-ExpCDF (intermediate). Examples include a linear function and the factorial function, whose recursive structures become unstable under varying input, a behavior the paper links to NP problems. The framework is applied to compare 2SAT and 3SAT: 2SAT clauses convert to binary implications, yielding local, compositional structure and polynomial-time solvability, while 3SAT's ternary clauses create non-local dependencies that cannot be decomposed, causing exponential semantic growth (|Ssem| = O(2^n)). The paper concludes that 3SAT's semantic explosion is a structural consequence of its generative syntax rather than an artifact of inefficient algorithms; stabilizing αf would require transforming the problem (e.g., into 2SAT), destroying its identity, so algorithmic improvements cannot bypass this structural explosion.

Patents grant inventors temporary monopolies; after expiration, anyone may use the invention. A randomised controlled trial in Kampong Speu province, Cambodia, compared the efficacy of 3·5 mg/kg versus 7·0 mg/kg total doses of primaquine (both over 14 days) for preventing Plasmodium vivax recurrences. After a 7-day artesunate regimen, 119 G6PD normal patients were randomised (2:2:1) to low dose primaquine, high dose primaquine, or no primaquine; 37 G6PD deficient patients were assigned to the no-primaquine arm. Patients were relocated for 90 days to a malaria-free area to prevent reinfection. Within 90 days, recurrence occurred in 81·4% of the no-primaquine arm, 24·4% of the low dose arm, and 4·7% of the high dose arm, with a hazard ratio of 0·17 for high versus low dose. Both primaquine regimens were well tolerated, with comparable safety in G6PD normal patients. The authors conclude that the 7·0 mg/kg regimen is superior and should be endorsed in Cambodia and likely other Southeast Asian countries. Limitations include a small sample size, single-centre open-label design, inability to definitively distinguish relapses from recrudescence, and tightly controlled conditions that do not reflect real-life practice.

The Council of Regional Accrediting Commissions (CRAC), representing seven accrediting agencies that oversee 3,000 degree-granting institutions, released a statement backing the use of artificial intelligence to reduce credit loss during transfer, a major barrier to degree completion. The statement is not a mandate but signals that using AI to expand course equivalencies does not conflict with accreditation standards. A 2024 Public Agenda survey found that 58 percent of adults who tried to transfer credits reported some credit loss, with white respondents reporting higher acceptance rates than Black and Latino respondents. Manually evaluating transfer credits is described as inconsistent, time-consuming, and decentralized. Cryotherapy, a wellness trend involving standing in a chamber cooled to as low as 180 degrees below zero, is gaining popularity in West Michigan with the opening of Polar Brrr Cryo. Bollinger Bands are a technical analysis tool created by John Bollinger in the 1980s that measures price volatility. They consist of a middle band (typically a 20-day simple moving average) and upper and lower bands set at a specified number of standard deviations (default 2) above and below it. The bands expand during high volatility and contract during low volatility.

The article describes twelve Bollinger Band trading strategies, including the Squeeze (predicting breakouts after low-volatility consolidation), Breakouts, %B, Walks, Bounce, Double Band Trend-Following, Band Width, RSI Divergence, Pinch Play, Reversal, Volatility Contraction, and Triple Strategy.

Testing conclusions indicate Bollinger Bands are somewhat profitable in the mean-reverting stock market and show promise as a breakout indicator in gold, but no useful strategies were found for stock indices. A simple mean-reversion strategy on the S&P 500 performed reasonably but failed to beat buy-and-hold since 1993 and has been losing since 2018.

The bands should not be used as a standalone tool and work best combined with other indicators such as RSI, MACD, and stochastic oscillators. Limitations include delayed signals, potential false overbought/oversold readings during strong trends, and inability to predict extreme "fat-tail" market events. Settings such as the SMA period, standard deviations, and moving average type can be adjusted; shorter timeframes produce more signals with more false positives, while longer timeframes yield more reliable signals. Risk management involves stop-loss orders, position sizing, and diversification.
