This paper studies popular matchings in three matching markets—house allocation, marriage, and roommates—where agents have ordinal preferences over items or each other. Since popular matchings (matchings that receive a plurality of votes against any alternative in a pairwise election) frequently do not exist, the authors introduce the popular dimension: the minimum size of a set of matchings (a popular winning set) that is at least as popular as any single matching.

The main results are: the popular dimension of the house allocation problem is exactly 2 in all four cases (weighted/unweighted agents, strict preferences/ties), shown via a polynomial-time algorithm based on top-choice (1,2)-matchings that decompose into two matchings. For the marriage problem with unweighted agents and strict preferences, the dimension is 1, since stable matchings are popular. For the roommates problem with unweighted agents and strict preferences, the dimension is exactly 2, proved with a greedy algorithm. For the marriage and roommates problems with weighted agents or ties, the dimension is between 2 and 3; the upper bound of 3 is obtained by reducing the roommates problem to house allocation and 3-edge-coloring the resulting graph.

Because the popular dimension lower-bounds the Condorcet dimension, these results imply the Condorcet dimension conjecture of Lassota et al. holds for these three problems. The gap between the lower bound of 2 and upper bound of 3 remains open for the general marriage and roommates cases; the authors conjecture the marriage problem's popular dimension is exactly 2.

Climate change and natural disasters displace approximately 21 million people annually, with internally displaced persons (IDPs) in lower- and middle-income countries (LMICs) facing heightened vulnerability due to limited resources and weak infrastructure. This study examines how climate change affects the education of K-12 internally displaced learners in LMICs, addressing a research gap in which educational needs have been overlooked in climate dialogues. Using a framework combining the Human Rights-Based Approach with Education in Emergencies research, the study conducted a literature review of 73 selected documents.

Findings show that climate change restricts educational access and quality through physical destruction of schools, economic pressures forcing school withdrawal, and environmental effects on learning capacity. In new destinations, displaced learners face financial barriers, administrative obstacles (such as household registration systems), discrimination, and inadequate distance-learning options. Learners also experience psychological trauma and health impacts. Girls face compounded barriers, including prioritization of boys' education, increased household responsibilities, and early marriage.

The study recommends scalable financial support, streamlined administrative processes, gender-sensitive policies, and improved data systems, while identifying research gaps including limited climate focus in Education in Emergencies, insufficient long-term outcome studies, and reactive policy responses.

The passage presents two all-optical thermometry methods that use machine learning to measure micro/nanoscale temperatures with fluorescent diamonds containing silicon-vacancy (SiV) centers. The methods combine the photoluminescence of SiV centers and the Raman signal of the diamond host as temperature-dependent features, with spectra recorded from 25°C to 85°C in 10°C increments.

Two regression algorithms were developed: a multi-feature regression (MFR) model and a two-stage multi-feature regression (2SMFR) model using partial least squares, Lasso regression, and spline correction. Both were trained on calibration data from a subset of diamonds and tested on previously unseen diamonds, with performance assessed through generalized accuracy, resolution, and sensitivity metrics.

The MFR model, requiring only 3–4 calibration diamonds and temperature set points, achieved an accuracy of 1.7 K and resolution of 1.2 K·Hz⁻¹/², a ~26% improvement over single-feature (SF) models. Its best version used three features: SiV ZPL wavelength, SiV linewidth, and Raman linewidth, identified through an explicit permutation-based feature selection routine.

The 2SMFR model, trained with seven diamonds and seven temperature set points, achieved 0.7 K accuracy and 0.6 K·Hz⁻¹/² resolution—~59% better than MFR and ~70% better than the best SF model. Its sensitivity (0.04 K⁻¹) was roughly sevenfold higher than the best SF model. The 2SMFR uses implicit feature selection via Lasso regularization and requires a minimum of two training diamonds.

Performance improved with larger training sets, though gains diminished beyond certain thresholds. The authors note the linear feature-temperature assumption holds within the studied range, and extrapolation beyond training temperatures should be avoided. The methods offer a flexible, data-efficient, instrument-agnostic framework applicable to any optical sensor with at least two temperature-dependent observables.

On April 27, 2001, Indian press reported that the board of Dabhol Power Company (DPC), meeting in London, authorized its management (Neil McGregor and K Wade Cline) to issue a termination notice for the power purchase agreement with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB). The decision passed six votes to one, with IDBI opposing; MSEB representatives, holding a 15% stake, were barred from voting as an interested party. MSEB made a "protest payment" of Rs 134 crore toward its March bill of Rs 146.64 crore. International lenders supported Enron's exit from the project, while domestic lenders led by IDBI opposed termination, and lender consent is required to serve notice. The dispute stemmed from MSEB's unpaid bills and a Rs 401 crore penalty it imposed on DPC for failure to supply power. If terminated, the Centre's liability would include one year's electricity bills and a $300 million termination fee. Maharashtra's Chief Minister called the decision unfortunate and planned to appoint a committee to renegotiate the contract.

President Muhammadu Buhari said Nigerians were reporting improved power supply, citing 5,222.3 MW delivered as of December 2017. Meanwhile, his hometown Daura, Katsina State, faced a 10-day blackout after a windstorm felled a newly erected 132 kva power tower and 16 KEDCO poles. KEDCO said repairs were ongoing and power would be restored within 48 hours. Parts of Lagos and Ondo states have lacked electricity for months.

In *Mock v. Watson et al.*, the widow of John Mock petitioned to have her interest in her deceased husband's real estate admeasured and set apart to her. The defendant heirs answered that the estate was heavily indebted with no assets besides the lands, contending the widow's share could be assigned only after all debts were satisfied. The trial court struck these allegations and ordered the interest set apart; the defendants appealed.

The sole issue was whether the widow's interest in her deceased husband's lands is subject to the estate's debts. The court held it is not, and may be set apart without reference to debts. Her statutory interest attaches upon the concurrence of the husband's seizin and the wife's coverture, ripens into a vested interest at his death, and is not part of the estate's assets. Unlike the heirs' interest, it is not made subject to the rights of others or to charges against the estate. Sections 2387 and 2391, authorizing sales for debts, refer to the estate's interest in the lands, not the widow's. Section 2441 merely limits her to one-third and does not subordinate her to creditors, and Section 2451 protects a homestead purchased with her award from her own debts, not the husband's. Affirmed.

This passage is a collection of news articles from September 11–12, 2001, covering the energy sector's response to the terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center and Pentagon. Energy companies including Enron, Dynegy, El Paso, and Reliant shut down offices, evacuated employees, and halted trading. The New York Mercantile Exchange, located near the World Trade Center, closed, and power trading across the U.S. largely ceased. Energy prices soared on fears of Middle East involvement and supply disruption, with oil reaching $31 a barrel and gasoline prices spiking nationwide; OPEC indicated readiness to increase production to stabilize markets. Utilities and nuclear operators, including Exelon and Entergy, implemented heightened security. Enron resumed North American gas and power trading on September 12 via EnronOnline and telephone until noon, stating it saw no reason for markets to become unstable. Energy companies in South Asia reviewed security arrangements; Enron India said it had taken precautions around its installations, including the Dabhol project, in which it holds a 65% stake. Separately, Enron's Indian unit, Dabhol Power Co., said a payments dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board limited its ability to repay debt and maintain the idling plant, while Indian politicians criticized proposed tariff hikes and urged buying Enron power. Bandwidth-trading operations also shut down after the attacks.

The quarterback is widely regarded as the most important position in football and sports overall, serving as the face and leader of the team. Along with the center, the quarterback touches the ball every play, calling plays, communicating them to teammates, ensuring proper alignment, and calling audibles when the defense lines up unexpectedly. The position's name comes from early formations where the quarterback lined up a "quarter back" from the running back, with a fullback in between. The quarterback is also called the Signal Caller, Field General, or Gunslinger, and abbreviated as "QB." Body types for the position have shifted from tall, strong players to smaller, more athletic ones. Key skills include football IQ, decision-making, accuracy, leadership, footwork, athleticism, and arm strength. Notable quarterbacks include Otto Graham, Peyton Manning, Dan Marino, Joe Montana, and Tom Brady. The quarterback is important because he touches the ball every play and kickstarts everything the offense does.

A self-driving Uber vehicle struck and killed 49-year-old Elaine Herzberg, who was walking outside a crosswalk in Tempe, Ariz., in the first fatality involving a fully autonomous test vehicle. The Volvo was in self-driving mode with a human operator behind the wheel. Uber suspended all self-driving road testing in the U.S. and Canada and is cooperating with the police investigation.

HDFC Mutual Fund will wind up HDFC FMP 378D March 2014 (1) after unit holder approval. The scheme's net assets fell below Rs 10 crore after its second maturity extension to May 25, 2020, making it unviable to manage.

In this transfer tax appeal, the Surrogate's Court held that Josephine Slosson validly exercised her power of appointment over a trust fund created by her father Peter Naylor's will, making the beneficiaries' interests subject to transfer tax. Her children could not take under their grandfather's will because the contingency for doing so—her failure to validly dispose of the property by will—never occurred. Since the children had not renounced their legacies under their mother's will, the question of disposition or taxation in the event of renunciation was not before the court. The $24,840 paid to the decedent's creditors from the trust fund was taxable. However, $682.04 paid to Alice Slosson, who had advanced money to settle claims against the decedent to whom the decedent was not indebted, was improperly included in her taxable bequest. The order fixing tax was modified by deducting that amount and was otherwise affirmed.

Carol Christ, 73, has become chancellor of UC Berkeley—the first woman and oldest person to hold the position—after serving as president of Smith College and spending decades at Berkeley as an English professor, department chair, vice chancellor, and provost. She replaces Nicholas Dirks, who stepped down amid sexual assault scandals, budget problems, and a fractured campus community. Christ faces several challenges: a national free speech debate centered on the campus, a student housing shortage amid rising costs, a $110 million budget deficit that must be halved this year, and strained relations with state lawmakers after an audit revealed $175 million in undisclosed funds. She plans to declare a "free speech year" with point-counterpoint debates, partner with Berkeley and Oakland on housing, increase private philanthropy, and make administrative cuts. She also prioritizes addressing low black student enrollment and restoring a sense of community.

A penalty kick taker is a player who takes a penalty kick, a restart awarded when a defender commits a foul punishable by a direct free kick inside their own penalty area. The shot is taken from the penalty mark, 12 yards from the goal, defended only by the opposing goalkeeper. Law 14 of the IFAB Laws of the Game governs the procedure, including ball placement, goalkeeper positioning, and the positions of other players. Coaches are responsible for identifying and training kickers in advance, teaching the rules, and instructing the attacking team; the kicker is responsible only for setting up and scoring. Kickers should develop and consistently practice a routine, beginning with experimentation using cones and disks as targets. Mental preparation—staying calm, blocking distractions, and using techniques such as breathing and visualization—is essential. Three kick types are described: inside-of-the-foot, instep drive, and instep-face. Lower corners are generally the preferred targets, though accuracy matters more than power. Feinting is permitted during the run-up but not after it is completed. Advanced techniques include scouting goalkeepers, maintaining at least two kicks, changing kickers, and the rare "tap" penalty kick. Regular practice under simulated game conditions is emphasized.

Thai Prime Minister Prayuth Chan-ocha said no trade takes place between Thailand and North Korea, ahead of a visit by U.S. envoy Joseph Yun to discuss stepping up pressure on North Korea. The U.S. has urged Southeast Asian countries to cut North Korean funding streams. Thailand's foreign ministry said trade with North Korea dropped by up to 94 percent over the previous year.

Options expiry is the time when an options contract becomes void; in the US, the expiration date is the third Saturday of the expiration month, with the last trading day typically the preceding Friday (or Thursday if Friday is a holiday) and an expiration time of 11:59 a.m. EST. Expiry days bring higher trading volumes and volatility, particularly for large-cap stocks, and expiration weeks show higher average returns, known as the Options Expiration Week Effect (OPEX). Quad witching, when stocks, index futures, and index options expire together, occurs four times yearly (March, June, September, December). The article presents four backtested strategies using Amibroker on SPY and XLV: SPY during expiration week (0.3% average weekly gain), an undisclosed XLV strategy (0.7% per trade), an SPY overnight strategy (0.46%), and an SPY short day trading strategy (0.18% average gain over 306 trades). A backtest confirmed expiry days, especially quad days, have slightly higher volatility than normal trading days. Developing options strategies involves researching models, backtesting over at least 15 years across market cycles, and forward-testing the selected model.

The UC1825B-SP is a PWM controller for high-frequency switched mode power supplies, supporting current- or voltage-mode operation, with protection circuitry, latched logic, undervoltage lockout, and totem pole outputs for driving MOSFET gates.

Chenai Mathabire, a 35-year-old Zimbabwean nurse and epidemiologist, received an International AIDS Society prize for demonstrating that a rapid tuberculosis test could be implemented at health centers in Malawi and Mozambique. After choosing nursing over early dreams of modeling, she joined Doctors Without Borders in 2008, working in Zimbabwe and South Sudan before her 2015 research assignment. Her team found the urine-based test delivered results in under an hour, compared with two to four days—or longer—for standard cough tests or X-rays, and staff could be trained within hours. The findings led some health centers to adopt rapid TB testing, potentially enabling faster care for HIV patients, for whom TB is the leading killer. Mathabire continues working for Doctors Without Borders and recently moved to Sweden to marry.

The speaker accepts the Democratic presidential nomination, thanking Governor Stevenson for his introduction and citing the support of running mate Lyndon Johnson and other party figures. He acknowledges that nominating someone of his religious faith is viewed by some as a risk, but asserts that his policy decisions will be his own and that religion is not relevant to his candidacy. He criticizes Richard Nixon and the Republican platform, arguing the nation needs strong Democratic leadership. He describes a changing world—shifting power, new weapons, Communist influence, and domestic revolutions in farming, urbanization, civil rights, medicine, and automation—and calls for a new generation of leadership. He introduces the "New Frontier" as a set of challenges rather than promises, asking Americans for courage, sacrifice, and innovation rather than complacency, and closes by requesting the audience's help, voices, and votes.

A new study published in The American Journal of Psychiatry found that one hour of weekly exercise can help protect against depression. Tracking 33,908 Norwegian adults over 11 years, researchers found that non-exercisers were 44 percent more likely to suffer from depression, and 12 percent of depression cases could have been prevented with small amounts of exercise.

Speakers describe a hard-fought playoff game in which the opponent came out strong, but their team hung on, scored a late goal, and improved its first periods while keeping shots down. One speaker recounts how a single phone call brought him from Toronto to Detroit, crediting Jimmy Devellano and Scotty Bowman, and calls the Stanley Cup win a total team effort, noting the contributions of five Russian players in critical situations. Another says winning four straight was never predicted, but the team was the league's best and outplayed every opponent.

Google's Project Fi added three new phones: the $199 moto G6 (available for preorder), the $740 LG G7 ThinQ, and the $899 LG V35 ThinQ. Launched in April 2015, Fi supports very few phones and lacks Apple's iPhone, which analysts say limits its market. Fi charges $20 monthly for unlimited calls and texts plus $10 per gigabyte up to 6GB, with no charge for unused data. As an MVNO, it uses T-Mobile, Sprint, U.S. Cellular, and Wi-Fi in the U.S., and Three overseas. Google declined to discuss the potential T-Mobile/Sprint merger's impact or user numbers, claiming a "healthy user base." Analyst Roger Entner doubts Fi is growing, calling it "a project, not a product."

BC Liberal leader Andrew Wilkinson criticized NDP Premier John Horgan for rising gas prices, calling it a tax grab and urging the government to lower the gas tax. Horgan countered that the nine-cent overnight price increase reflects gouging and company profits, not taxation, and raised supply and refining issues with the federal government.

Irish soccer player Megan Connolly posted a viral Twitter video of her scary ride in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, featuring laughing FSU teammate Dallas Dorosy. Irish footballer Sophie Perry checked in on her.

On October 27, 2022, Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC reporting its financial results for the fourth fiscal quarter ended September 24, 2022. The filing includes a press release with the results as Exhibit 99.1 and was signed by Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Luca Maestri. Apple's common stock and various notes are registered on The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC.

The Court of Civil Appeals of Texas, Austin, affirmed a judgment denying the Wilson appellants recovery for damages from a May 28, 1955 head-on collision on a three-lane highway, where the northbound Wilson car collided with appellee King's southbound car in the west lane. Each party alleged the other's negligence, including improper lane use, excessive speed, failure to keep a lookout or control, and failure to yield. The jury found King was not in the center lane and maintained control, while Wilson negligently drove into the west lane as the sole proximate cause. On appeal, appellants complained of the charge, failure to submit issues on discovered peril and excessive speed, and improper argument about the $55,000 sought. Because appellants made no trial objections to the charge or argument, such complaints were waived under Rules 272 and 273, and the judgment was affirmed.

This email from the Enron India newsdesk compiles news articles from May 23, 2001, concerning the Enron-Dabhol Power Company (DPC) dispute with Maharashtra.

Madhav Godbole, chairman of the committee appointed by the Maharashtra government to renegotiate the power purchase agreement (PPA) with DPC, resigned after NCP chief Sharad Pawar criticized the negotiating team's "negative approach." Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh refused to accept the resignation, and Pawar stated his comments were not made on behalf of the state government. The renegotiation meeting was cancelled following the resignation.

DPC had served a preliminary termination notice to the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB) over unpaid bills, and Enron indicated it may seek damages of $3.5–5 billion if unresolved. Maharashtra considered issuing its own termination notice to DPC. The Godbole report criticized DPC, Enron, General Electric, and Bechtel for lack of due diligence, and highlighted the tariff dispute—Maharashtra now pays Rs 8.54 per unit versus the Rs 2.20 assumed when the PPA was signed in 1994.

Indian lenders (IDBI, ICICI, SBI), with exposure of roughly Rs 2,835–5,255 crore, faced potential non-performing asset problems, and their stocks fell after the termination notice. Indian lenders might skip a June meeting in Singapore. Indian power firms, including Tata Power and Reliance, expressed no interest in buying DPC's stake due to high tariffs. The state advocate general deemed MSEB's Rs 401 crore rebate claim against DPC justified. The central government adopted a wait-and-watch policy. Separately, Enron appointed consultants to value its Indian businesses and withdrew from a natural gas project in Qatar.

Coach Bylsma brought new confidence to the team during a difficult period, and the change proved effective from day one. A five-game road trip, in which the team won its first three games, followed by trades acquiring Billy and Adams, marked a turning point in the season. The speaker hopes for a championship ring as a memento. Sid's leadership is shown through playing his game and the team's system, particularly defensively. Jordan is regarded as a responsible two-way forward with offensive talent. The organization has been dominant since winning its first cup, despite losing significant pieces after last year's cup run.

North Tyneside Council's cabinet unanimously approved moving ahead with the North of Tyne devolution deal, which will bring £600m over 30 years, an elected mayor, and an expected 10,000 jobs. Mayor Norma Redfearn said councils south of the Tyne could ask the Government to join later, though it is too late at this stage. She criticised Durham County Council for pulling out after a £200,000 referendum. The combined authority is set to be established in summer 2018, with mayoral elections in May 2019. Newcastle leader Nick Forbes rejected claims the authority would be "under-powered", citing higher per-head investment and health, disability support, and housing elements. A vote to split the existing North East Combined Authority was postponed to mid-April.

The passage describes NVIDIA's Blackwell GPU architecture and associated technologies. Blackwell can deliver up to 50% power savings in small language model inference through reduced active periods, power/voltage gating, and faster entry into deep sleep states. DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, producing up to three AI-generated frames per traditionally rendered frame using a model that is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM than prior methods, supported by fifth-generation Tensor Cores, an AI Management Processor, and enhanced Flip Metering for frame pacing. DLSS 4 also transitions from CNN to transformer-based neural networks for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, using self-attention and 2x more parameters to improve stability, detail, and image quality. Blackwell introduces neural shaders, enabled by the Cooperative Vectors API developed with Microsoft for DX12 and Vulkan, allowing shaders to access Tensor Cores. This enables RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression (over 3x memory savings in a demo), Stochastic Texture Filtering, Neural Radiance Cache for inferred multi-bounce lighting, RTX Skin for ray-traced subsurface scattering, and RTX Neural Faces using real-time generative AI. The passage also provides specifications for the GB202 (RTX 5090), GB203 (RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti), and GB205 (RTX 5070) GPUs, followed by NVIDIA's standard disclaimers and trademark notices.

Plymouth Studio School, a sports-focused free school on the Plymouth Marjon University campus, is to close after being deemed financially unviable due to low enrollment, with only 155 students against a built capacity of 300. The £4.2 million school, which opened in September 2015, is expected to cease operating at the end of the summer term 2018, pending Government approval. The decision follows significant difficulties, including a recent Ofsted inspection that rated the school "inadequate." MP Johnny Mercer expressed disappointment at the closure but is committed to ensuring pupils' education is not interrupted. The school will be the 19th studio school to close since the model's inception.

California Assembly Republican Leader Chad Mayes faces intense criticism but expresses no regret for supporting the extension of the state's cap-and-trade program with Democrats, saying only that he wished he had attended the bill-signing ceremony. Supporters saw the vote as a way to show Republicans take climate change seriously, while critics called it a betrayal of party principles. County chairs, donor groups, and state GOP officials have urged Mayes to step down, and the state party board is expected to vote on the issue. Mayes, who can be removed only by his 25-member caucus, faces a leadership challenge from Assemblyman Jay Obernolte but plans to remain in his post. Other Republicans who backed the bill have also faced backlash. The dispute has complicated party fundraising negotiations and may discourage future bipartisan cooperation on climate issues.

An email from Professor David Levine to his Berkeley economics students assigns Mankiw chapter 10 as mandatory reading for November 17–18, with homework on how monetary and fiscal policy shift IS/LM curves, and includes three optional articles.

The first article discusses France's 35-hour workweek law, a campaign promise of Lionel Jospin's coalition aimed at creating jobs. Some businesses, like the Beyer jam factory, benefited—producing 30% more after reorganizing shifts—though experts doubt the law will cure unemployment. The policy is controversial: unions fear wage freezes, businesses protest costs, and public support has declined. Job creation figures are disputed, and only about 16,000 businesses have formally converted. Service industries struggle, some entrepreneurs resist hiring a 20th employee to avoid the mandate, and some workers report increased stress despite shorter hours.

The second article reports a Latin American stock market rally fueled by expectations of fewer U.S. interest rate increases and optimism about regional growth in 2000. Analysts predict 3.2% regional growth versus contraction in 1999. Chile is expected to grow 5.5%, helped by lower rates and copper price recovery, while Brazil's currency stabilized after the IMF granted flexibility to defend it, with 3% growth predicted. Investors remain cautious about foreign rate hikes and Brazilian fiscal reform delays.

The third article examines Japan's economic crisis, attributing it primarily to policy failures after the late-1980s bubble burst, particularly unaddressed bad loans that triggered a credit crunch; asset values fell over ¥1 quadrillion. Government stimulus halted the downturn, but structural factors—completion of catch-up with the West, globalization, rapid population aging, and technological shifts—account for an estimated 20–30% of the decline. The author argues Japan must overcome the "paradox of success" and reform its systems or risk a "lost decade."

The 2017 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to the International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons (ICAN), a coalition of NGOs in 100 countries, for highlighting the humanitarian consequences of nuclear weapons and pursuing a treaty-based prohibition. The award came amid tensions over North Korea's nuclear testing and questions about the Iran nuclear deal. ICAN drove the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, adopted July 7 by 122 nations, banning development, testing, production, and stockpiling of nuclear weapons. The five permanent UN Security Council members did not participate in negotiations. ICAN chief executive Beatrice Fihn called the award "hugely important."

Pragyan '18, a technology fest, began on March 1, 2018 at the Barn Hall with Dr BN Suresh as Chief Guest. The three-day event featured guest lectures, workshops, a human library with 14 books, and exhibits including Hyperloop India, InMoov, KalamSat, ISRO displays, and Ugears models. Daily infotainment shows included shadow art, ventriloquism, cardistry, mentalism by Suhani Shah, and stand-up comedy by Azeem Banatwalla.

This passage from the TPS7H5001-SP/5002-SP/5003-SP/5004-SP datasheet details a push-pull converter design example using GaN FETs. Dead time was set to ~25 ns (RPS/RSP = 20.5 kΩ) to reduce reverse-conduction losses; leading edge blank time was ~50 ns (RLEB = 49.9 kΩ); soft-start capacitance was 33 nF (~7.5 ms). The transformer uses a 2.5 turns ratio with a 35% target duty cycle and 40 μH primary inductance. Primary-side GaN FETs are rated 170 V for a 36 V maximum input; synchronous rectifiers use 80-V GaN FETs, optionally paralleled with a Schottky diode. An RCD clamp limits switch-node voltage. The output inductor is 0.47 μH (40% ripple), and output capacitance is 2.3 mF (7 × 330 μF polymer tantalum), exceeding the calculated 1.3 mF minimum to mitigate radiation-induced single event transients. Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins at ~35 A output (RCS = 7.5 Ω, 1:100 current sense transformer); the hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF. Type 2A compensation targets a 10 kHz crossover (RCOMP = 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP = 15 nF, CHF = 47 pF), with a 102 kΩ slope compensation resistor. The controllers operate from 4–14 V with at least 0.1 μF input bypass capacitance. Layout guidelines address noise reduction, ground separation, and trace routing. Revision F (August 2024) added QMLP options for TPS7H5002/3/4-SP; the document concludes with packaging information and legal disclaimers.

The 2025 Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine was awarded to Mary Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell, and Shimon Sakaguchi for discovering regulatory T cells (T-regs), which calm the immune system after infection or wound healing and prevent it from attacking the body. Sakaguchi of Osaka University discovered T-regs in 1995. In the 1990s, Brunkow and Ramsdell tracked down a mutation causing a fatal autoimmune disease in male mice; it was in a gene Sakaguchi later discovered, and without it there aren't enough T-regs. In 2001, the duo showed mutations in this gene occur in people. Scientists are learning to harness T-regs to treat autoimmune disease and cancer. The prize, worth 11 million Swedish krona, was announced October 6.

The defendant moved to dismiss a bigamy indictment, arguing his second marriage—performed by a Justice of the Peace in 1955 when he was 19—was void under subdivision 5 of section 11 of the Domestic Relations Law, since his first marriage had never been dissolved. The defendant admitted both marriages. The court noted conflicting case law: Caplan v. Caplan and De Martino v. De Martino held the provision mandatory, rendering such marriages void, while Andrews v. Andrews and Graves v. Graves treated it as a prohibition on the officiant only, leaving the marriage valid. Inclining toward the former view, the court granted the motion to dismiss the indictment.

Christmas Day has been a US federal holiday since 1870 and is not a trading day for US markets, though adjacent days may trade depending on weekends; the bond market closes early at 2 PM the day before. Backtests confirm the Santa Claus rally—strong stock performance in late December and early January—is real, not a myth. In the S&P 500 since 1960, three strategy variations produced gains of 0.7%–1.6% per trade, win ratios of 66%–72%, and profit factors of 2–4.5, though recent performance weakened with three losing years. Possible explanations include mutual fund rebalancing, a lack of macro news, the turn-of-the-month effect, and holiday optimism. The rally also appears in Europe: the EWG ETF (German stocks) showed a 2.1% average gain with an 81% win ratio, and the FEZ ETF (Euro Stoxx 50) showed 1.5% with 81%, though returns have declined recently. Emerging markets (FEMKX) averaged 2.7% per trade, and India's NIFTY averaged 1.2%, though with only 14 observations. The rally typically starts on the third Friday of December, and no other US holiday effect outperforms it.

The University of Maine cancelled its AFLOAT floating offshore wind summit, citing changing federal policies, after the government suspended a $12.5 million grant to the program. It has no plans to revive AFLOAT but will hold private meetings with industry, research, and government leaders.

Drew Doughty said the team isn't discouraged despite losses, having expected a long series, and believes the opponent is simply executing their system better, requiring adjustments. He stressed crashing the net for rebounds against goalie Marty, whom he said they're making look better than he is. He admitted distractions from family and the Cup's presence hurt their earlier game, but Darryl ensured better preparation this time. He called the Cup being in the building motivation and praised his strong relationship with Rob.

Darfon America Corp. is showcasing upgraded energy storage products at Intersolar North America 2018: the H200 and H300 hybrid energy storage systems and the H5001 hybrid inverter. Based on customer and installer feedback, the H200 gained new battery options, the H300 is available in a 10kWh configuration, and the H5001 received lockable components. All three models feature upgraded fans, improved in-rush overload handling, and an optional generator start-up kit.

The Federal Reserve raised short-term interest rates by a quarter point on Wednesday, its third hike since December, bringing the key rate to a range of 1% to 1.25%. Citing a strengthening U.S. economy, the Fed upgraded its growth and unemployment forecasts but lowered its inflation projection to 1.6%. Unemployment fell to 4.3% in May, its lowest since 2001. The Fed also plans to start selling off some of its $4.5 trillion in holdings at $10 billion a month, and most officials expect at least one more rate hike this year.

A hockey player expresses excitement about playing in a hostile environment in his hometown, stressing the need to treat the game like any other and finish the job. He feels comfortable and confident at the net, crediting his team's play in front of him. He expects Edmonton to compete hard, noting teams play well at home, and says he is surrounded by great teammates.

This passage from the TMS320DM814x DaVinci Digital Media Processors documentation describes the device's subsystems and pin functions. The ARM Cortex-A8 Subsystem integrates a Harvard-architecture processor with a NEON SIMD engine, VFPv3 floating-point coprocessor, separate L1 caches, an embedded trace buffer (ETB, 32KB), an interrupt controller (AINTC) that prioritizes peripheral requests and generates IRQ/FIQ signals, and a PLL for clock generation. The processor connects through a 128-bit DMM port to DDR memory and a 64-bit L3 interconnect port. The C674x DSP subsystem includes 32KB L1 program cache with error detection, 256KB L2 RAM/cache with ECC, and a CPU with eight functional units and two 32-register files, supporting packed data types, complex and Galois field multiplication, SPLOOP software pipelining, compact 16-bit instructions, exception handling, privilege modes, and a time-stamp counter. A system MMU remaps C674x accesses to protect ARM memory regions. Additional modules include the Media Controller (managing HDVPSS and ISS), the HDVICP2 video codec accelerator (supporting MPEG1/2/4, H.264, VC-1, RV9/10, AVS-1.0, and ON2 VP6.2/VP7), a Face Detection module (QVGA, 8-bit luma input), a Spinlock module with 128 hardware semaphores, and a Mailbox module for inter-processor communication with four-message FIFOs. The document also presents unified L3/L4 memory maps, TILER extended addressing (an additional 4GB accessible only to HDVPSS and ISS), and terminal function tables detailing pin multiplexing, boot configuration via BTMODE pins, internal pullup/pulldown behavior, and functions for peripherals including GPMC, DDR controllers, EMAC, GPIO, I2C, McASP, PCIe, JTAG, SD, SPI, timers, UART, USB, video input/output, and power supplies.

Amazon.com, Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2019 reports Q2 2019 net sales of $63.4 billion (up 20% year-over-year) and net income of $2.6 billion; for the six months ended June 30, 2019, net sales were $123.1 billion (up 18%) and net income was $6.2 billion. The company operates three segments: North America, International, and AWS. Q2 2019 segment net sales were $38.7 billion, $16.4 billion, and $8.4 billion, respectively, with operating income of $1.6 billion for North America, an operating loss of $601 million for International, and $2.1 billion for AWS. Total assets were $191.4 billion as of June 30, 2019, with cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities of $41.5 billion. The company adopted new lease accounting guidance on January 1, 2019, recognizing approximately $21 billion of operating lease assets and liabilities. As of June 30, 2019, it had $24.3 billion of unsecured senior notes outstanding and $509 million borrowed under a secured credit facility. Disclosed contingencies include Neodron patent infringement lawsuits filed in 2019, an IRS transfer pricing dispute, a European Commission state aid decision involving an escrow deposit of approximately €250 million, and tax contingencies of approximately $3.7 billion. No common stock was repurchased during the six months ended June 30, 2019.

Volkswagen's U.S. unit asked a judge to delay trials over excess emissions, fearing "inflammatory" comments by lawyer Michael Melkersen in a Netflix documentary would prejudice the jury. Melkersen, representing over 300 diesel owners, referenced VW-sponsored monkey diesel fume tests and made comments linking VW to Hitler and the Holocaust. VW argued this would prevent a fair trial; Melkersen called the motion "hogwash." The first consumer fraud trial is set for Feb. 26. About 2,000 owners opted out of VW's 2016 settlement, which involved spending over $25 billion.

President Madison returns to the House of Representatives a bill pledging funds for internal improvements—roads, canals, and water navigation—because he finds it irreconcilable with the Constitution. He argues the power is not among Congress's enumerated powers, that the commerce clause cannot be stretched to include it, and that interpreting the "common defense and general welfare" clause broadly would render the enumeration of powers meaningless and give Congress unlimited legislative authority. He adds that state consent cannot confer a power the Constitution does not grant. While acknowledging the value of such improvements, he believes the Constitution's success depends on a definite division of powers between the general and state governments, and therefore withholds his signature, hoping the desired ends may be achieved through the constitutional amendment process.

NATO's 2017 annual report shows upward trend lines, said Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg. In 2017, the alliance deployed four multinational battle groups to the Baltic republics and Poland, led by Canada, Germany, the UK and the US, and increased its forward presence in the Black Sea region. NATO also strengthened cyber defenses, joined the coalition against ISIS, deepened EU cooperation, and welcomed Montenegro as its 29th member. Defense spending in Europe and Canada rose for three consecutive years, adding $46 billion, including $18 billion on major equipment. NATO deployments grew to over 23,000 troops by end of 2017, up from under 18,000 in 2014. Stoltenberg condemned Russia's nerve agent poisoning of Sergei Skripal as a breach of international norms and cited Russia's pattern of aggressive behavior, including nuclear modernization. The Resolute Support mission in Afghanistan will grow from 13,000 to around 16,000 troops, and NATO plans a new training mission in Iraq.

Scalping is a trading style that profits from small price changes over very short time frames, from seconds to a few minutes. The article argues scalping is a waste of time because almost all scalpers lose money. Scalpers compete against better-equipped players such as high-frequency traders, banks, and hedge funds with superior tools, capital, and lower latency. Backtesting scalping strategies rarely reflects reality due to market noise, randomness, and transaction costs. Commissions and slippage—hidden execution costs—erode theoretical profits and put most scalpers out of business. Scalping is also stressful and requires automation, which carries risks such as errors and losses. A real-life example describes a trader who invested heavily in scalping infrastructure but eventually quit after losses. The authors recommend finding edges on longer time frames, where profit potential per trade is greater and backtests more robust, or considering long-term investing instead.

Becton, Dickinson and Company (NYSE:BDX) has paid dividends since 1962, with 12 of the past 13 years showing double-digit dividend growth averaging 16.3% since 2004. The company is projected to pay $2.98 in 2017 calendar year dividends, a 10% increase over 2016. Fiscal 2017 GAAP diluted EPS guidance of $7.90–$8.00 represents up to a 78% increase over 2016, aided by a litigation reserve reversal from a favorable antitrust ruling. The $12.2 billion CareFusion merger has been successful, though merger costs and higher interest expenses reduced profits in fiscal 2015 and 2016. The dividend payout ratio fell from 59% of GAAP diluted EPS in fiscal 2016 to an estimated 37% for 2017. Fiscal 2017 is on pace for the highest profit since 2014 and may exceed the 2010 record of $1.317 billion. Risks include manufacturing issues, higher interest rates, and competing products. The article concludes the dividend is safe and suitable for dividend portfolios.

This study employs density functional theory (DFT) calculations to predict, for the first time, the properties of three novel out-of-plane ordered (o-MAX) phases, Mo₂A₂AlC₃ (A = Zr, Nb, Ta), using the CASTEP code with GGA-PBE and PBEsol functionals. The compounds crystallize in a hexagonal P6₃/mmc structure containing 16 atoms per unit cell. Negative formation energies, the absence of negative phonon frequencies, and elastic constants satisfying Born stability criteria confirm chemical, dynamical, and mechanical stability. Band structure and density of states analyses reveal metallic behavior, while charge density mapping and Mulliken population analyses indicate mixed ionic, covalent, and metallic bonding, with strong Mo–C covalent interactions. Elastic moduli, Pugh's ratio, Poisson's ratio, and Cauchy pressure identify the compounds as brittle and mechanically anisotropic, with Vickers hardness values (6.02–6.28 GPa) within the typical MAX phase range. Thermal analysis yields high Debye temperatures, high melting temperatures (2064–2237 K), low minimum thermal conductivity (0.74–0.90 W/mK), and thermal expansion coefficients comparable to established thermal barrier coating (TBC) materials. Optical calculations confirm metallic character and reflectivity exceeding 44% across infrared to ultraviolet ranges. Overall, the findings suggest these o-MAX phases are promising candidates for thermal barrier coatings and solar heat-shielding applications.

The passage lists numerous trading-related article titles from QuantifiedStrategies.com, covering topics such as risk-adjusted returns, trading psychology, backtesting, candlestick patterns, seasonality, trading indicators, and various trading strategies. The website offers free backtested trading strategies based on numbers, facts, and statistics rather than opinions, daily YouTube videos, over a thousand free articles, and trading courses for beginners. Its content ranges from stock market basics to quantified and algorithmic trading, including articles on strategies, indicators, backtesting, and seasonal trading.

Celtic's victory at Ibrox demonstrated their superiority over Rangers, who played well but were deservedly beaten by Brendan Rodgers's side. The writer criticizes Rangers chairman Dave King for failing to deliver the promised £30million financial backing to manager Mark Warburton, leaving the manager to pay the price for unfulfilled expectations. Warburton's signings, including Joey Barton and Joe Garner, have disappointed, and Rangers' most consistent players, Clint Hill (38) and Kenny Miller (37), are nearing the end of their careers. Celtic, boosted by Champions League money and shrewd signings like Moussa Dembele (£500,000) and Scott Sinclair, should now spend big to strengthen and permanently move beyond Rangers, having failed to do so when Rangers went bust in 2012.

This critical reflection paper examines how generative AI can be incorporated into education in a humanizing and ethical manner. Drawing on Gunther Anders, the authors highlight the "Promethean discrepancy"—the gap between what technology can produce and what humans can imagine or grasp—and warn against confusing technological possibility with moral justification. Using Foucault's concept of "regimes of truth," the paper argues that corporate AI systems produce inconsistent, biased, and hallucinated outputs, making them unreliable arbiters of truth for educators. Freire's philosophy of conscientization and humanizing education suggests technology is not inherently harmful if it promotes humanizing ends. The authors combine Bloom's Revised Taxonomy with Arendt's hierarchy of labor, work, and action, noting that AI performs lower-order cognitive tasks better than higher ones, but arguing education must prioritize Arendtian "action"—meaningful engagement with the world. They propose a framework situating AI use on a spectrum from consumptive labor to humanizing action, applicable across online, blended, and in-person settings. Example lesson plans illustrate the framework's application, and the paper concludes that educators must continuously reassess AI use, with humanizing education and learner agency as enduring goals.

A market research report on the Global Silyl Modified Polymer Market analyzes historical, current, and projected revenues, trends, and growth rates. Key manufacturers covered include Kaneka, Bostik, Henkel, Wacker, Evonik, 3M, Dow Corning Corporation, H.B. Fuller, Hodgson Sealants, and Risun Polymer. The report incorporates segmentation analysis, PEST and Porter's Five Forces surveys, SWOT analysis, investment feasibility and return analysis, and examination of macroeconomic and microeconomic factors. Product types are segmented into Polyurethane, Polyamine Ether, and Other, with applications in Construction, Automotive, General Industry, and Others. Regions covered include the United States, China, Europe, Japan, Southeast Asia, India, and Rest of World, with forecasts spanning 2018 to 2025. The report aims to provide market guidance and strategies for new players, stakeholders, marketing units, administrative authorities, and distributors.

This patent application, a continuation of prior filings, describes methods and apparatus for handling reduced processing time in wireless systems that use configurable transmission time intervals (TTIs) or short TTIs (sTTIs) to reduce latency. The background notes that low-latency applications (e.g., alarm reporting, automotive safety, factory process control, MTC, gaming, VoLTE) may find 1 ms TTI latencies insufficient, and that sTTIs reduce latency but also reduce available processing time.

A wireless transmit/receive unit (WTRU) may determine processing capabilities (PC), send a PC indication to an eNodeB, receive a PC configuration, and determine or limit a maximum timing advance or Rx-Tx time difference for a specific TTI length. The WTRU may also measure a processing value (PV), determine headroom (the difference between PV and PC), and report or act based on conditions, such as proximity thresholds, including suspending or dropping uplink transmissions. Examples cover PCs based on processing criteria (TTI length, number of symbols, TBS, channel type, timeline), handling DCI with uplink grants (transmitting only if available processing time meets a threshold), and determining uplink HARQ-ACK timing after downlink receptions.

The detailed description presents an example communications system with WTRUs, base stations, RANs, and core networks (E-UTRA/LTE and NR configurations), WTRU hardware components, and background on timing advance, TA commands, time alignment timers, HARQ timing, and processing time.

India's trucking industry will undergo major change by 2027, driven by population growth (projected to exceed 1.4 billion, the world's largest), urbanisation, and policy shifts. OEMs must meet the BS VI emissions standard within four years—leapfrogging BS V—a task that took Europe a decade. The GST is expected to open long-distance routes, creating demand for more powerful, faster trucks than India's current low-powered, two-axled fleet. Global manufacturers like BharatBenz, Scania, Volvo, AMW, and possibly Hyundai are challenging domestic players. The government's AMP II aims to make India's automotive industry a global Top 3 by 2026, with exports at 35-40% of production and 65 million jobs. However, unpredictable government policies pose challenges. While 2027 trucks will be bigger, faster, more connected and efficient, electrification and autonomous driving remain decades away.

This patent application describes implementing fundamental computational primitives using a matrix multiplication accelerator (MMA) coupled to a processor in a device. A streaming engine is configured to stream data from memory, the MMA formats the data, and the primitive is executed. The MMA includes two 32×32 multiplicand (B) buffers, two 32×32 result (C) buffers, and a 1×32 multiplier (A) buffer of 16-bit elements, with B buffers used as ping-pong buffers and C buffers as foreground/background buffers. Each cycle, the MMA performs a Load, Store, and Execute (LSE) instruction. Configurable components include format components for input/output data types, a row offset component with thirty-two five-bit offset values, and a ReLU nonlinearity component. The processor is a DSP with L1 and L2 caches and two streaming engines that use multi-level nested loops for multi-dimensional memory addressing; it applies input formatting (zero padding, even/odd vector generation, value copying, known matrix creation, linked operations) and output formatting (seam removal, stride removal, zero padding, transpose). The document details implementations of primitives including batch small and large matrix multiplication, point wise multiplication, matrix addition, vector matrix multiplication, vector summation, affine transformation, 2D convolution for CNNs, matrix permutations, FFTs, DCTs, 1D convolution/filtering, correlation, matrix assignment, and transpose.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC reporting that Jerome Guillen, President of Tesla Heavy Trucking, departed the company as of June 3, 2021. The report was signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn on June 7, 2021.

Apple briefly overtook Samsung in fourth-quarter smartphone sales, selling 77 million iPhones (17.9 percent share) to Samsung's 76.8 million (17.8 percent), according to Gartner. Apple typically leads in the fourth quarter due to holiday sales, while Samsung's 2016 was hurt by the Galaxy Note7 recall, which damaged both sales and brand. With Samsung launching a new flagship in March and Apple expected to unveil new iPhones in September, Samsung may regain the lead. Meanwhile, Chinese makers Huawei, Oppo, and BBK rank third through fifth and are expanding into developed markets.
Chinese conglomerate CEFC China agreed to acquire a 20 percent stake in Cowen Group for $100 million, plus $175 million in debt financing and three board seats, sending Cowen's shares up 19 percent.

An 80-year-old man was treated on the floor at Gujranwala DHQ Hospital due to a bed shortage; his family demanded authorities take notice. Separately, PML-N Gujranwala celebrated Yaum-e-Takbeer, paying tributes to Nawaz Sharif.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU is the eighth-generation data center GPU, based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture and fabricated on TSMC's 7nm N7 process with 54.2 billion transistors and an 826 mm2 die. It delivers significant speedups over the V100 for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads.

Key features include Third-Generation Tensor Cores supporting TF32, IEEE-compliant FP64, and BF16 data types, along with a new Sparsity feature that can double Tensor Core throughput. TF32 operations run 10x faster than V100 FP32 FMA operations (20x with sparsity), and FP16/FP32 mixed-precision delivers 2.5x V100 performance (5x with sparsity).

The Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) feature allows secure partitioning of an A100 into up to seven GPU Instances with fault isolation and quality of service, particularly benefiting Cloud Service Providers.

The A100 includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth (a 73% increase over V100) and a 40 MB L2 cache, nearly 7x larger than V100. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, double that of V100. Additional features include PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, Compute Data Compression, asynchronous copy instructions, asynchronous barriers, task graph acceleration, and improved error and fault detection, isolation, and containment.

The A100 is designed for elastic computing, able to scale up via NVLink, NVSwitch, and InfiniBand, or scale out to support multiple independent users through MIG.

The Treasury Department recommended rolling back key parts of Obama-era Wall Street regulations in the second of four reports ordered by President Trump to review banking rules. The report calls for making it easier for companies to go public, repealing Dodd-Frank provisions including the requirement to disclose the pay gap between CEOs and workers, allowing companies to "test the waters" with potential investors before IPO filings, raising crowdfunding limits from $1 million to $5 million, and "recalibrating" derivatives rules through SEC and CFTC coordination. Marcus Stanley of Americans for Financial Reform called the recommendations "almost uniformly deregulatory," while the SEC's Jay Clayton and CFTC's Brian Quintenz expressed support. The report comes as Senate action on Dodd-Frank rollback has stalled; Republicans and business groups are likely to welcome it, while Democrats and consumer advocates warn it could expose taxpayers to future bailouts.

Unidentified gunmen attacked U.N. peacekeeping facilities in Timbuktu and Douentza, Mali, killing nine people, including a U.N. peacekeeper and Malian personnel. U.N. troops killed eight attackers. Secretary-General Guterres condemned the attacks, saying they may constitute war crimes. The Mali mission is the U.N.'s deadliest peacekeeping operation, with nine peacekeepers killed this year. The U.N. is investigating whether the attacks were connected.

Arizona ammunition dealer Douglas Haig was charged with manufacturing armor-piercing bullets without a license. Unfired armor-piercing bullets found in the Las Vegas shooter's hotel room contained his fingerprints. Haig sold 720 rounds of tracer ammunition to Stephen Paddock weeks before the Oct. 1 attack that killed 58 people, saying he noticed nothing suspicious. His name was mistakenly revealed in court documents, making him a "person of interest." He has since closed his ammunition business and received death threats but doesn't plan legal action.

This paper examines the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) as synthetic agents in social science research, arguing that treating LLM outputs as random draws from a population distribution is misleading. Unlike Bayesian inference engines, LLMs do not maintain or update posterior beliefs; their probabilistic-seeming outputs arise from static pre-trained weights and sampling techniques. The paper reviews work showing LLMs can replicate survey patterns and predict experimental outcomes, but also documents limitations such as violations of the martingale property (order-dependence in predictions), "introspective hallucination," and "hyper-accuracy distortion," in which synthetic responses show unnaturally low variance. LLMs' apparent predictive success stems from pattern matching over massive training data, and fine-tuning constitutes behavioral alignment rather than statistical correction, potentially degrading statistical coherence. The paper argues that no single universal "homo silicus" exists; instead, researchers should develop domain-specific agents. Practical guidelines include treating LLM agents as high-capacity predictors rather than calibrated probabilistic beliefs, measuring calibration and subgroup validity, anchoring agents in individual-level human data, avoiding order sensitivity, stress-testing with out-of-domain evaluations, and ensuring full reproducibility and disclosure. Synthetic data should augment rather than replace human data. The paper concludes that LLMs hold immense promise for social research, particularly for ethically fraught or impractical studies, but their limitations as non-Bayesian black-box systems must be recognized, and they should be used for near-term, scoped prediction rather than universal modeling of human behavior.

The National Institute of Standards and Technology has revised its password guidelines, now recommending simple, long, memorable passwords using phrases, lowercase letters, and typical English words instead of special characters or mixed case. Passwords no longer need to expire. Paul Grassi says longer passwords are cryptographically harder to break, and the security industry has responded positively. Password manager apps are useful but not necessary, and old rules like frequent password changes frustrated users without improving security.

This study assessed the quality of early childhood education (ECE) in 71 Anganwadi Centers (AWCs) across 25 villages of Nuh Block, Mewat district, Haryana, using checklists and interviews with Anganwadi Workers (AWWs). Findings showed widespread infrastructure deficiencies: only 32.39% of centers had safe building structures, 19.72% had leveled floors, and none had seating materials, desks, or learning resources such as books, flashcards, or play equipment. Only three centers had a safe kitchen, clean drinking water, and a functional toilet. Many AWWs lacked adequate qualifications (43.66% had passed only 8th grade, below the matriculation prerequisite), were unfamiliar with the five domains of child development, did not involve parents (67.71%), and predominantly used repetition and memorization methods (63%) rather than activity-based teaching. The study concludes that ECE in rural Mewat suffers from poor infrastructure, scarce learning resources, and undertrained workers, reflecting broader rural challenges including socioeconomic factors, language and cultural barriers, limited parental engagement, and weak monitoring. The paper notes that India's National Education Policy 2020 includes children aged 3–6 under free and compulsory education and emphasizes holistic, play-based learning. It recommends standardized compulsory infrastructure, systematic provision of learning resources, training of AWWs in child development and pedagogy, parent awareness efforts, and collaboration among governments, communities, NGOs, and CSR initiatives to achieve equity in preschool education.

This December 14, 2000 email is the final "Friday Burrito" newsletter of 2000, written by Gary Ackerman for WPTF readers. Ackerman reviews three weeks of turmoil—FERC orders, emergency and rate stabilization filings, data subpoenas, a credit crunch, and price spikes—and argues the industry needs a stronger public relations effort, noting that ordinary Californians mainly worry about how much their electric bills will rise. He proposes holding down consumer bills through new generation, greater customer choice, and a provider of last resort.

In California news, he satirizes Senator Steve Peace's letter to FERC criticizing high prices and Kaiser Aluminum's smelter shutdown, which WPTF's Kent Wheatland called demand response. He discusses SCE CEO John Bryson's call to re-regulate the market, credit problems facing Pacific Northwest sellers paid by the ISO about 100 days after trades, and the market leverage held by SCE and PG&E. The CPUC reinstated PG&E's and Edison's rate stabilization applications after suspending them, and quotes from CPUC President Lynch assert California has ample power.

Federally, Energy Secretary Richardson invoked a rarely used Federal Power Act authority to require out-of-state sales to California and ordered BPA and WAPA shipments; BPA supplied about 1,500 MW and PowerEx 400 MW. WPTF supported the PX's emergency FERC motion to replace the $250/MWh hard cap on Adjustment Bids, which the ISO opposed. The issue closes with reader mail, details of the February 8–9 WPTF meeting in Scottsdale, Arizona, humorous poems on the 2000 election, and a personal story about a conversation with the author's son.

Evaluating AI systems like LLMs on unforeseen tasks is difficult due to potential overfitting and data contamination from pre-training data, and static benchmarks that lag behind evolving models. The authors propose future benchmarking methods should dynamically generate evaluation samples, support varied difficulty levels, and provide multi-faceted analysis of individual capabilities, while adapting psychometric principles to AI. Further challenges include evaluating cultural respect, values, and safety. As an early effort, DyVal dynamically generates evaluation samples on-the-fly using a directed acyclic graph (DAG) structure, where operators and variables enable infinite samples with guaranteed ground truth for tasks such as mathematical and logical reasoning.

This document is a specification update for the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device (Silicon Revision A3), listing errata with descriptions, implications, and resolutions. Key issues include: the PIT does not cancel a pending counter latch command when a read-back command is issued; the GLIU debug port hangs the system; PIT count mode 3 loads a new count value immediately instead of after the current count completes; the XPIC clears the IRR bit late, causing duplicate interrupts when auto-end-of-interrupt is enabled; DMA rotating priority does not always rotate correctly; thermal alarms cannot be detected while in Faulted Standby because the alarm resides in the Work power domain; the Sleep Clock option must remain enabled in the PMC for other sleep options to work; GLIU debug data-pattern detection fails; the GLIU Error MSR "Unexpected Address" flag and exception do not activate; UART registers cannot be accessed during block or demand mode DMA; 8237 software DMA memory writes from LPC fail; I/O cycles at addresses 10000h or higher hang the system; USB pins do not meet the USB 1.1 over-voltage protection specification, requiring external protection circuits; LBARs accept illegal I/O base addresses of 10000h or higher; the PIC can miss interrupts if an edge-configured interrupt source remains high after the Local bus clock gates off, potentially hanging the system; ATAC and ACC PRD prefetching can err when PRD tables are only 4-byte aligned; UDMA writes can suffer CRC corruption following a host termination in a preceding UDMA read; and ATAC SSMI during DMA does not block I/O as intended. Most issues have no or limited operational impact; resolutions generally involve avoiding the affected features or sequences.

Raja Jackson, the 25-year-old son of retired MMA legend Quinton "Rampage" Jackson, faces one count of felony battery causing serious bodily injury and one count of misdemeanor battery for an assault at a KnokX professional wrestling event in Los Angeles in August. Jackson slammed wrestler Stuart Smith (Syko Stu) to the ground and continued striking him after he appeared unconscious, having said beforehand he sought revenge for an earlier altercation in which Smith hit him with a beer can as a promotional stunt. Smith suffered jaw injuries, a serious head injury, a lip laceration, and lost teeth. Jackson was arrested in September and faces up to four years in prison, with prosecutors expected to seek a sentencing enhancement. His father has condemned his actions.

Stack procedures, provided as macros for host integration, lack segment declarations and require a local file with the INCLUDE directive. These native assembly routines establish or destroy stacks in stackless mode.

In Toll v. McKenzie and Toll v. Peck (decided April 27, 1931), the Colorado Supreme Court reviewed two cases: a probate proceeding Toll sought to reopen (No. 12,391) and his suit to enjoin foreclosure of a trust deed on his Denver residence (No. 12,392). McKenzie had purchased the property by an unrecorded deed, financing it with an $8,000 loan from Casey secured by a recorded trust deed. After McKenzie died in 1922, leaving his estate to his wife and two minor daughters, Casey arranged a backdated deed from the original grantor to Mrs. McKenzie, eliminating the minors' undivided one-half interest, and Mrs. McKenzie then sold the property to Toll for $11,000. Upon learning the true ownership, Toll entered contract "A" with Mrs. McKenzie and Casey, under which they agreed to perfect his title through probate and guardianship proceedings at their expense. The court held the transaction constituted only constructive fraud, that the contract's spirit had been observed, and that Toll would receive good title. However, because Casey had not fully performed his obligations under contract "A," the judgments were affirmed as modified: Toll was to pay the debt balance with interest by June 1, 1931, and Casey was to release the trust deed. On rehearing, case No. 12,392 was remanded to the district court to effectuate the judgment.

Micro E-mini Nasdaq 100 futures are electronically traded contracts worth one-tenth of the E-mini Nasdaq 100 futures, based on the Nasdaq 100 Index of the largest 100 non-financial companies on the Nasdaq exchange. They trade on the CME Globex platform from Sunday evening to Friday afternoon (with a daily break), expire quarterly (March, June, September, December), and are cash-settled based on special opening quotes on the third Friday of the contract month. One contract equals the index value multiplied by $2, with a minimum price fluctuation of 0.25 index points ($0.50) for outright trading and 0.05 index points ($0.10) for calendar spreads. The trading symbol is MNQ, and there is no block trade eligibility.

A trading strategy should combine technical and fundamental analysis with risk management and position sizing; the authors reference a backtested strategy (kept behind a paywall) with three buy variables and one sell variable, backtested using the Mini contract due to the micro contract's shorter history. Seasonality data shows better performance in spring and fall. Prices are affected by component stock movements, macroeconomic reports, interest rate policies, economic conditions, and sociopolitical events. As of December 18, 2022, the contract traded at $11,344.75, with an all-time high of 16,676.50 (November 2021) and an all-time low of 6,628.75 (March 2020). The main risk comes from leverage, which magnifies losses relative to deposited margin. Unlike the futures, CFDs on the contract trade continuously without expiry, and several ETFs track the market. To begin trading, one opens an account with a futures broker and funds it above the required margin.

Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) is a common household disinfectant with uses beyond sanitizing cuts. The article lists 13 ways to use it: gargling a weekly diluted solution to kill bad-breath organisms; gradually lightening hair with a peroxide-water spray; treating ear infections with drops; cleaning produce with food-grade peroxide; whitening teeth when mixed with baking soda; disinfecting toilet bowls; removing caked-on food with a baking soda paste; sanitizing cutting boards; wiping kids' toys; soaking feet to soften calluses and reduce fungus; removing stains (after testing, as it may leave its own stain); soaking plant seeds to simulate rainwater's naturally occurring H2O2; and disinfecting reusable shopping bags.

Mashal Khan's father, Muhammad Iqbal Khan, recalls his son, born in 1992, as a gifted student who left for higher studies at Abdul Wali Khan University. Four days before his death, Mashal told a news channel about the absence of a vice chancellor, high fees, and teachers holding multiple posts. On April 13, he learned Mashal had been chased by a crowd and shot. Police have arrested several young men. The father urges justice and political unity so no one fears school, noting growing public awareness of Mashal's innocence.

The 6-quart Instant Pot Ultra, the newest Instant Pot pressure cooker, is on sale for the first time for $120 at Amazon and Sur La Table, down from its typical $150 price. Unlike the DUO models, the Ultra features a 10th cooking option, the "Ultra" setting, allowing users to customize temperature, pressure, and time. It also provides more cooking information and includes a quick release button.

Orthopaedic surgeon Dr Sushrut Babhulkar and MAFSU veterinary doctors plan to implant a prosthetic limb on Sahebrao, an eight-year-old, 200kg tiger whose paw was amputated in 2012 by a poacher's trap outside Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve—a potential world first, as such procedures have only been done on dogs and elephants. The limb, from Germany's AO Foundation, will be fitted after treating the tiger's painful neuroma. Sahebrao, adopted by Dr Babhulkar, lives at Nagpur's Gorewada Rescue Centre.

Leveraged ETF trading strategy is a short-term investment method using exchange-traded funds that employ financial derivatives and debt to amplify an underlying index's returns, aiming for 2:1 or 3:1 ratios, or inverse performance. Unlike traditional ETFs that track indexes one-to-one, leveraged ETFs magnify both gains and losses—a 3:1 ETF loses 3% if the index falls 1%. Management fees and transaction costs diminish returns, making these funds unsuitable for long-term holding due to volatility decay.

The most effective strategy is short-term trading—day trading or swing trading—since the derivatives used are not long-term investments. Day trading is preferred because it avoids daily rebalancing effects. The main risk is magnified losses: if the S&P 500 lost 35% in a bear market, a 3:1 leveraged ETF could wipe out the entire investment. Risk management includes stop-loss orders and diversification across markets, such as trading both directional and inverse ETFs.

Profits are taxed like stock trading profits—short-term gains at ordinary income rates, long-term gains at lower rates (for US citizens and residents). Performance is measured using standard metrics like the Sharpe ratio, Jensen's alpha, and appraisal ratios.

Backtests showed a strategy on QQQ produced 1.25% average gain per trade, 7.6% annual returns, and 18% max drawdown; the same strategy on QLD (2x leveraged) yielded 2.25% average gain and 13.6% annual returns—though not double the unleveraged version, likely due to time decay. During the 2008/09 financial crisis, the QLD strategy lost over 35%. A less robust RSI strategy showed QLD with a max drawdown exceeding 55%. The authors emphasize that max drawdown is an underappreciated metric and that leverage can be lethal, forcing traders to stop at the bottom.

The passage profiles seven young Indian entrepreneurs whose startups are reshaping the country's entrepreneurial landscape. Sachin and Binny Bansal founded Flipkart, now valued at USD 15 billion and acquired by Walmart. Vijay Shekhar Sharma created Paytm, valued at USD 9.4 billion, which gained momentum during demonetization. UnitedHealth Group has hired Michael Pencina, formerly Duke Health's chief data scientist, as its chief AI scientist. Pencina advocated for greater oversight of health care AI tools and co-founded the Coalition for Health AI, which develops testing and oversight standards.

Accern Sentiment Analysis rated media coverage of Celyad SA (NASDAQ:CYAD) as somewhat positive on Friday, assigning a daily sentiment score of 0.19 and an impact score of 45.69 out of 100, indicating coverage is somewhat unlikely to affect the share price. Former Trump aide Sebastian Gorka endorsed John McCann for the Republican congressional nomination in New Jersey's 5th district. McCann faces Steve Lonegan in the primary; the winner faces Democratic Rep. Josh Gottheimer. Lonegan, a 2016 Trump critic and Ted Cruz state chairman, now bills himself as a Trump supporter. Gorka left the White House in August.

This email compiles news articles from June 4, 2001 mentioning Enron. The TLV322x features an open-drain, sinking-only output stage that can be pulled up to an external voltage from 0V to 5.5V, independent of the comparator supply voltage, enabling logic OR'ing and level translation. TI recommends pull-up resistor current between 100µA and 1mA; lower resistor values improve rise-time but increase VOL and power dissipation. Shorting the output to a voltage source can cause thermal runaway, so a series current-limiting resistor is recommended. Unused open-drain outputs may be left floating or tied to V-.

Inputs and outputs include internal ESD protection to V+ and V-, with input voltages limited to 0.2V beyond the rails; a series current-limiting resistor is recommended for low-impedance sources, limiting current to 10mA or less.

The TLV321x devices include an internal Power-On Reset circuit that remains active for up to 32µs after VPOR (1.65V) is crossed; the output is held low during the POR period.

In basic comparator operation, the output is low when VIN is less than VREF and high when VIN is greater; logic can be inverted by swapping input pins. Propagation delay differs between transition types, and smaller overdrive voltages increase delay, particularly below 100mV.

Because the TLV321x has only 1.8mV of internal hysteresis, external hysteresis via positive feedback can prevent output chatter. Inverting configurations use a three-resistor network; non-inverting configurations use a two-resistor network with a voltage reference.

A typical application is low-side current sensing using an amplifier and high-speed comparator. Design guidance includes using low-ESR 0.1µF bypass capacitors at the supply pin, minimizing output-to-input coupling, and treating outputs as high-speed logic. The document also lists related application notes, support resources, ESD handling cautions, and TI legal disclaimers.

This passage presents safety results from a clinical study of the BNT162b1 and BNT162b2 vaccines across Phases 1, 2/3, and 3. Injection site reactions (redness, swelling, or pain) and systemic events (fever, tiredness, headache, chills, vomiting, diarrhea, muscle or joint pain) were common after vaccination but were well tolerated, mostly mild or moderate, and went away after a short time. Pain at the injection site and tiredness/headache were the most common reactions. In Phase 1, all tested doses (10, 20, and 30 µg) of BNT162b1 and BNT162b2 were well tolerated except BNT162b1 at 100 µg, which was stopped after Dose 1; BNT162b2 at 30 µg was selected for Phase 2/3. No participants left Phase 1 because of medical problems. In Phase 2/3, few participants left due to medical problems (32 of 21,926 in the BNT162b2 group and 36 of 21,921 in the placebo group, both less than 1%). Serious medical problems were rare. In Phase 1, two participants had serious problems (inflamed appendix and inflamed nerves), not believed related to the vaccine. In Phase 2/3, a few serious problems occurred, some of which researchers believe may be related to the vaccine. No participant died during Phase 1. In Phase 2/3, deaths occurred among 85 of 23,141 participants who received BNT162b2 initially, 62 of 21,371 who received placebo then BNT162b2, and 23 of 23,141 who received placebo only; researchers do not believe the deaths were caused by BNT162b2. No participant died among Phase 3 participants who received BNT162b2SA without prior BNT162b2.

The Court of Appeals of Ohio, Franklin County, reversed a common pleas judgment awarding plaintiffs Gail Erdy, Tamara Wolford, and Monica Jones $5,225 each against Technology Education Corporation (TEC) for breach of a contract to perform educational services. Plaintiffs had contracted with Paraprofessional Institutes of Ohio (PIO), which sold the school to Educational Leadership Corporation (ELC) before classes began. After plaintiffs graduated and sued, alleging misrepresentation of the course of study and out-placement services, ELC sold the school to TEC. Default judgment was entered against PIO and ELC, and TEC's liability was resolved against it on a motion to dismiss.

The appellate court held that TEC did not expressly assume liability because the asset purchase agreement incorporated into the assignment exempted the buyer from pre-purchase liabilities except those listed in Schedule F, which did not mention student contracts. Liability could not be implied from TEC's knowledge of the pending litigation, and no authority required TEC to be a bona fide purchaser. TEC was also not a mere continuation of ELC, as there was no evidence of common identity of stockholders or directors. Because the case sounded in contract rather than products liability, strict liability did not apply, and plaintiffs failed to sustain their burden of proof. The judgment was reversed and the case remanded.
