The speaker says the time off allowed the team to focus on tomorrow's big game, not wanting to go back to Dallas down, and calls the opponent an excellent shot-blocking team.

The passage describes NVIDIA's GA10x Ampere architecture GPUs and their improvements over the prior Turing generation. The second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection testing rates and add a new Interpolate Triangle Position unit for hardware-accelerated ray-traced motion blur, enabling up to 8x faster motion blur rendering than Turing. Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32 and BF16 data types and Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity, which doubles matrix multiplication throughput by skipping zero-valued weights. These features enhance DLSS, making 8K 60 fps ray-traced gaming feasible for the first time.

The memory subsystem introduces GDDR6X, developed with Micron, using PAM4 signaling to reach data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth. NVIDIA RTX IO, working with Microsoft's DirectStorage API, offloads asset decompression from the CPU to the GPU, improving I/O performance by up to 100x compared to hard drives and traditional storage APIs.

The A40 data center GPU delivers up to 2x FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to 5x (10x with Sparsity) AI training throughput versus the Quadro RTX 6000, with 48GB memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink. Display support includes HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a with 8K60 capability. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware AV1 decoding—a first among GPUs—while seventh-generation NVENC provides encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

The GeForce RTX 3090 (GA102) ships with 24GB GDDR6X and is 1.5x faster than TITAN RTX; the RTX 3070 (GA104) outperforms the RTX 2080 Ti. A new Error Detection and Replay (EDR) feature detects and retries GDDR6X memory transmission errors, helping users identify safe overclocking limits. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU includes 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 48GB GDDR6, expandable to 96GB via NVLink.

This study estimates SARS-CoV-2-attributable mortality in India, where death registration systems do not record causes of death and official COVID death counts (~530,000 through 2021) may understate mortality, with contested excess-death estimates ranging from 4 to 6 million. The authors administered WHO-compliant verbal autopsy (VA) surveys to next-of-kin of a representative sample of decedents drawn from the Consumer Pyramids Household Survey (CPHS, 2018–2021). Physicians coded causes using ICD-10, identifying SARS-CoV-2 deaths via U07/U08 codes, with excess deaths calculated relative to 2018–2019 rates. Adjustments addressed VA non-response (72.8% response rate; final sample of 20,453 decedents) and delayed death reporting to the CPHS.

The all-cause annual death rate in 2020–2021 was 81.19% higher than in 2018–2019. SARS-CoV-2 accounted for 17.93% of all deaths and 33.15% of excess deaths during the pandemic, with death-rate peaks at the lockdown's end (May 2020), around wave 1, and after wave 2 (May 2021). Cardiovascular disease accounted for 23.15% of excess deaths, while respiratory deaths fell. SARS-CoV-2 death rates increased with age, were higher (not significantly) among females, urban residents, and the top income quartile, and varied by state, from 0.07% (Bihar) to 2.13% (Goa). Unlike official reports, the 2020 spike occurred at the lockdown's end rather than during wave 1. Limitations include vaping-related deaths included in U07/U08 codes, imperfect statistical corrections, and an unvalidated VA modification for SARS-CoV-2.

The 3-4 defense, used by coaches Bill Belichick, Nick Saban, and Kirby Smart, has produced 16 major championships since 2005—9 college football national titles and 7 Super Bowls. The defense consists of 3 down linemen, 4 linebackers, and 4 defensive backs, forming a "mirror" defense where one side mirrors the other. It requires bigger defensive linemen who use a "two gap" approach and hybrid outside linebackers who can rush the passer or drop into coverage. Its main strength is bringing pressure from multiple positions, including a 5-man rush from blitzing both outside linebackers, along with a flexible two-safety setup. However, it struggles against modern spread offenses, where a light 5-man box makes it vulnerable to the run, and trips formations can cause confusion. Common blitzes include the Weakside Edge Blitz and Crossfire Blitz, while common coverages are Cover 4 and Cover 2 Man. The defense traces to Bill Parcells and Bill Belichick's New York Giants teams of the late 1980s and early 1990s, which won two Super Bowls with Lawrence Taylor. Their coaching tree includes Matt Patricia, Romeo Crennel, Nick Saban, and Kirby Smart, who won championships at Alabama and Georgia.

The lecture opens with quiz feedback (average around 78–79), noting that many students answered problem 2's third part with lengthy t-tests and F-tests when existing confidence intervals could have been used directly. The main content extends full factorial design of experiments to k factors. Contrasts—formed as differences between averages of high and low factor settings—estimate main effects and interaction effects in 2^k designs, with interaction columns generated by multiplying factor columns. Scaling relates total effects to model coefficients (e.g., beta 1 equals A/2 with coded levels −1 to +1). Regression offers an alternative estimation approach, using the design table as the x matrix with fictitious columns for interaction terms. ANOVA tests whether effects are significant by comparing mean squares against replicate error via F-tests. A brake forming example (punch depth and material type, 10 replicates per corner) demonstrates fitting a linear model with interaction; residuals must be checked for trends and normality, and residuals stem from two sources: replication noise and model error from neglected higher-order terms. Center points, combined with replicates, enable lack-of-fit tests for curvature; an example showed no significant interaction or quadratic term, only main effects. The lecture concludes with a brief introduction to blocking and confounding: nuisance factors like temperature can be handled through randomization or by arranging blocks so the block effect confounds with higher-order interactions rather than main effects, leading into fractional factorial designs to be covered next time.

The Neofoot study was a prospective single-arm diagnostic test accuracy study conducted in three primary care clinics in Madang Province, Papua New Guinea, as a sub-study of the WANTAIM trial. Its objectives were to determine the diagnostic accuracy of newborn foot length for identifying low birth weight (LBW, <2.50 kg) and preterm birth (PTB, <37 completed weeks), and to compare foot length measurements taken by trained volunteers with those of a researcher. Of 426 babies born to enrolled mothers, 342 were assessed within 72 hours of birth. Birth weight was measured with electronic scales and gestational age was calculated from the last menstrual period or first-antenatal ultrasound. Foot length was measured with a plastic ruler fixed to a cardboard box, using the average of two measurements. Overall, 21.1% (72/342) of babies were LBW and 7.3% (25/342) were preterm. The optimal foot length cut-off was <7.7 cm for both outcomes: for LBW, sensitivity was 84.7% and specificity 69.6%; for PTB, sensitivity was 88.0% and specificity 61.8%. Areas under the ROC curve were 87.0% for LBW and 85.8% for PTB. For the 123 babies with paired measurements, the mean difference between researcher and volunteer measurements was 0.07 cm, with 95% limits of agreement of -0.55 to +0.70 cm; 7.3% of pairs fell outside these limits. The authors conclude that newborn foot length is a simple and feasible method for identifying LBW and PTB babies in resource-limited settings, though implementation research is needed.

Iran's parliament gave initial approval to a bill boosting spending on its missile program and the Revolutionary Guards in retaliation for new US sanctions. It allocates over $260 million each to the missile program and the Quds Force, and requires countering US human rights violations. The bill needs a second vote and clerical approval.

The passage is a datasheet excerpt for Texas Instruments MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 microcontrollers. The devices offer five operating modes (RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, SHUTDOWN) for power optimization and two power domains: PD1 (CPU, memories, high-performance peripherals) and PD0 (low-speed, low-power peripherals). The PMU provides core regulation, brown-out reset supervision, and a bandgap reference. The clock module includes LFOSC, SYSOSC, external crystal/clock inputs, and SYSPLL, distributing clocks such as MCLK, CPUCLK, ULPCLK, and MFCLK. The DMA controller provides six full-feature and six basic channels, and an event manager routes events between peripherals, DMA, and the CPU. Memory includes dual-bank flash (up to 512kB with ECC, plus 16kB data flash) and up to 128KB SRAM in two 64kB banks. Peripherals include up to 93 GPIOs, IOMUX, 12-bit 4Msps ADCs, a temperature sensor, VREF, comparators, a 12-bit DAC, UART, I2C, SPI, CAN-FD, general-purpose and advanced timers, RTC_B, watchdog timers, and a low-frequency subsystem. Security features include an AES-128/256 accelerator, firewalls, secure key storage for up to four keys, CRC, a TRNG, and a keystore. Additional sections cover MATHACL, SWD debug, a password-protected boot strap loader, factory constants, application layout recommendations (decoupling capacitors, NRST pullup, ROSC resistor, VCORE tank capacitor), development tools, device nomenclature, revision history, and packaging information.

Blackwell's clock gating shuts off entire clock trees, including the memory clock tree for the first time via GDDR7's fast-wakeup architecture. Separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory enable per-workload optimization and reduced leakage power.

Delta executives expect premium cabin revenue to overtake coach sales for at least a quarter or two next year. Last quarter, premium ticket revenue rose 9% to nearly $5.8 billion, while main-cabin revenue fell 4% to just over $6 billion. CEO Ed Bastian sees no sign of premium demand slowing. Main cabin tickets made up 43% of Delta's 2024 revenue, down from 60% in 2010.

A Berliner Testament is a will in which spouses appoint each other as sole heirs and generally their children as final heirs, giving the surviving spouse financial security. However, it has a strong binding effect: dispositions cannot be unilaterally altered, even after one spouse's death, which can be problematic if living conditions change. Clauses can ease this effect. Tax allowances should also be considered, as several heirs can use them more effectively. Experienced succession lawyers can offer advice.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI), developed by J. Welles Wilder in 1978, is a momentum indicator oscillating between 0 and 100 that helps traders evaluate whether a security is overvalued or undervalued. A Contract for Difference (CFD) is a financial contract allowing traders to speculate on price movements of assets like stocks, commodities, currencies, and indices without owning them; CFD trading is a zero-sum game. RSI readings below 30 typically indicate oversold conditions and potential buying opportunities, while readings above 70 suggest overbought conditions and possible selling points. For day trading, shorter time frames with more extreme thresholds (15 and 85) are often recommended. Mean-reversion strategies use RSI thresholds to profit from prices reverting to their average. Backtesting is essential to validate strategies; examples tested on SPY produced modest per-trade returns but significant drawdowns. Effective CFD trading with RSI involves combining it with other indicators, adapting time frames and thresholds to the asset, watching RSI divergences, and practicing risk management.

This study compares models for forecasting opioid-related fatal overdoses annually at the census tract level to help public health agencies target interventions with limited resources. Using data from Cook County, Illinois (1,328 census tracts, 2015–2022) and Massachusetts (1,620 census tracts, 2001–2021), the researchers evaluated simple baselines (all zeroes, last year, historical average, weighted historical average), statistical models (Poisson GLM, gradient boosted trees, Gaussian Process, Bayesian spatiotemporal, NBSpLag), and a neural network (CASTNet). They also proposed a new intervention-focused metric, Best Possible Reach (%BPR), which measures the proportion of fatal overdoses a model's recommended K intervention tracts would capture compared to perfect hindsight. Results showed that simple historical average baselines performed competitively with complex models in both regions. Additionally, %BPR produced different model rankings than error-based metrics (RMSE, MAE), potentially enabling identification of 15 additional fatal overdoses annually in Illinois and 18 in Massachusetts. The authors recommend including tuned historical average baselines in future forecasting studies and using intervention-aware metrics for evaluation. Limitations include the restriction to two locations, a fixed intervention budget of K=100 tracts, and a limited covariate set based on the Social Vulnerability Index. The study's software and Cook County data are openly available.

Science is building on long-standing efforts to enhance the mind. Caffeine and nicotine, used since at least 600 BC, work by blocking adenosine and mimicking acetylcholine, respectively. Tim Tully, funded by billionaire Ken Dart, is developing a "memorization pill" by studying people with exceptional memory and sequencing their genomes; he has already engineered fruit flies with photographic memories using CREB activators. Researchers are also seeking genes involved in intelligence for potential enhancement, and developing deep brain stimulation devices that monitor brain activity and correct abnormal states such as panic attacks.

Former Langley City mayor and one-term Liberal MLA Peter Fassbender is considering running for Langley City mayor and will decide by early August. He says he would only run if he felt he had something to contribute. Two incumbent Langley City councillors have already declared for the mayoralty.

The speaker expresses profound gratitude and a sense of solemn responsibility at being called to lead the nation, feelings heightened by the difficult circumstances of the period. Although the country had previously enjoyed unrivaled prosperity through republican institutions, peace, and growth in agriculture, commerce, manufacturing, and public revenue, it now faces distress caused not by its own conduct but by the unjust and arbitrary measures of belligerent powers, against which the United States had maintained strict neutrality and justice. The speaker pledges to pursue peace and neutrality, preserve the Union and Constitution, protect religious liberty, personal rights, and the press, practice fiscal economy, maintain a limited military supported by militia, promote agriculture, commerce, science, and benevolent efforts toward Native Americans. Acknowledging personal inadequacy, he places confidence in fellow citizens, other branches of government, and divine guidance, while honoring his predecessor's distinguished service.

The Supreme Court agreed to review Hunter's case concerning his plea-agreement waiver of the right to appeal. Hunter, a Texas man, pleaded guilty in 2024 to aiding and abetting wire fraud. The 5th Circuit dismissed his appeal of a mandatory-medication sentencing condition based on the waiver; Hunter argues this conflicts with other circuits' rulings.

This chapter describes the host environment requirements for implementing the host BIOS interface mechanisms that access the AGESA™ software. The host environment must establish a valid stack before any AGESA call; all calls are made through module dispatchers, and host bridge procedures must locate the binary image entry point and invoke the AMD dispatcher with a pointer to the configuration block (AMD_CONFIG_PARAMS). All AGESA core call-outs are funneled through a single call-out router implemented by the host environment, which translates function numbers into execution addresses.

The UEFI BIOS environment provides four execution stages (SEC, PEI, DXE, RTP) across three execution modes. AGESA core files are arranged into libraries, with four additional UEFI libraries generating four build targets; specified Microsoft assembler and compiler versions are used for the 16-bit, 32-bit, and 64-bit phases. Build selection involves a platform solution (e.g., Danube, Maranello), a build method—Binary Modules (indirect) or Source Integration—and individual features. Configuration options are described in a separate chapter; no additional UEFI-specific user options exist. The \Addendum directory supplies reference and platform customization files, UEFI .inf control files support the build, and environment variables such as AGESA_ROOT and AGESA_OptsDir must be set.

The SEC phase establishes the C programming environment using AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK. The PEI driver comprises two PEIMs—one for processor initialization and one for memory/post-reset initialization—publishing PPIs such as AMD_PEI_INIT_RESET_PPI, AMD_PEI_INIT_EARLY_PPI, AMD_PEI_INIT_POST_PPI, and AMD_MEM_INIT_PPI, plus a PEIM coordinating warm reset requests. The DXE driver performs late initialization, generates data tables, publishes the AgesaDxeProtocol, and includes an AmdGpuVgaControlDxe driver for iGPU VGA decoding.

Stack macros (AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK, AMD_DISABLE_STACK) create and remove the Cache-As-Ram stack; they are stackless, register-passing routines that must run on all cores, and the host must not modify cache controls during the Cache-As-Ram period. AARCH64 APUs with the Platform Security Processor do not use these macros.

Entry procedures are listed in time-point order: AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost, AmdInitEnv, AmdInitMid, AmdInitLate, AmdInitRtb, and resume-path routines including AmdInitResume. Required host call-outs are AgesaAllocateBuffer and AgesaDeallocateBuffer. Service procedures include AmdCreateStruct/AmdReleaseStruct (PreMemHeap, PostMemDram, and ByHost allocation methods), AmdGetExeSizeParams, and AmdReadEventLog, plus procedures for DIMM data eye results, APIC/PCI addresses, core identification, FRU memory location, and MMIO range addition.

In Thuro v. Meredith (1924), the Colorado Supreme Court affirmed a judgment awarding real estate brokers a commission from their principals, the Thuros. The brokers procured Mrs. Tallman as a purchaser, and a contract was signed by Della B. Thuro, who also signed for her absent husband without written authority. The court held that a principal cannot defeat a broker's right to commission by refusing to be bound by or sign a contract with a purchaser the broker produced. Questions of ratification were immaterial because Mrs. Tallman was a purchaser, fulfilling the brokers' duty. Any variance between pleading and proof was not prejudicial, refused instructions on immaterial issues were properly denied, and overruling a motion to strike replication allegations was harmless error.

The Montecito Union School District, a 350-student district in Santa Barbara County, agreed to pay $7.5 million to settle a lawsuit by two brothers, now 65 and 68, who alleged former principal and superintendent Stanford Kerr molested them in the 1970s. The brothers had sought $35 million; a third plaintiff settled earlier for $1 million. Kerr died in 2013 and was never criminally charged. The district admitted no liability and has no insurance covering the period. The settlement, roughly 40% of the district's 2025-26 budget, will be managed through a hiring freeze, attrition-based staff reductions, and redirected capital funds, avoiding layoffs. The case was possible under AB 218, a 2019 law removing the statute of limitations for such claims. Weeks earlier, lawmakers let SB 577, which would have restored a deadline, die; its sponsor plans to reintroduce it. The California School Boards Association gave the district a $50,000 legal grant.

This study compared Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM) with an explainable machine learning approach—a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with SHAP explanations—for detecting outliers in multi-center plantar pressure data. Experts annotated 1,031 samples from 703 subjects (798 valid, 233 outliers) across four outlier categories (General Acquisition Error, Double Foot Capture, Inverted Orientation, Incorrect Side Annotation), and the dataset was augmented with synthetic outliers to 2,798 samples. SPM used affine registration to a reference template and pixel-wise nonparametric cluster-based testing against a normative dataset; the CNN incorporated foot-side metadata. In nested stratified cross-validation, the ML approach outperformed SPM (F1: 0.99 vs. 0.93; MCC: 0.96 vs. 0.78). SPM false positives were predominantly pathological but valid feet, while its false negatives were mostly Incorrect Side Annotation samples. In an exploratory survey, 16 experts rated both approaches' explanations positively across eight semantic differential attributes, with no statistically significant differences; SPM was descriptively rated as simpler. The ML approach was most preferred (43.48%), followed by SPM (34.78%). The authors conclude both approaches are promising for automated outlier detection and that human-centered evaluation of explanations warrants further research.

Conventional market definitions—a bear market as a 20-per-cent decline, a correction as 10 per cent, a crash as 30 per cent or more—have no rational basis or supporting data and do not help investors manage risk or deploy capital, as illustrated by the 2015 and 2011 declines, when the S&P 500 and Russell 2000 fell into different categories. The author proposes definitions based on economic trends and investor psychology: a secular bull market is a 10-to-20-year period of rising revenues and growing investor willingness to pay for earnings, while a secular bear market features increased volatility and declining willingness to pay. Multiple expansion, not earnings growth, drove most of the 1982-2000 bull market's gains, with roughly three-quarters attributable to rising price-to-earnings ratios. Bear markets begin when this psychology shifts.

Yankees rookie Cam Schlittler shut out Boston for eight innings with 12 strikeouts in AL Wild Card Game 3. Scout Matt Hyde, who first saw him at Northeastern, called it "unbelievable." Schlittler became the first MLB pitcher with eight scoreless innings, no walks, and 12 strikeouts.

The High Post Split Offense consists of a high post split followed by down screens, requiring defenders skilled in guarding the high post, countering down screens, and defending the low post. Two defensive strategies are described. The Basic NBA Show & Recover approach has defenders sag off when the ball is passed to the high post, preventing handoffs and drives; against down screens, defenders show and recover rather than switch, since switching would allow the screener to post up a smaller defender. The All Out SOS Disruption strategy pushes the ballhandler to the sideline, denies the high post feed, switches on splits and down screens, and traps passes to the wing or low post. When a wing trap occurs, defenders rotate into Triangle "I" positions, with further rotations when the ball is passed out of the trap or into the post.

Pharma tariffs that President Trump said would take effect Wednesday did not begin. A White House official said the administration would "begin preparing" tariffs on companies that don't build in the U.S. or make a drug pricing agreement, without giving a new timeline. Pharmaceutical executives are receiving near-daily calls from White House staff, including chief of staff Susie Wiles, and senior HHS and Commerce officials, part of an effort to strike deals ahead of the 2026 midterms. The administration has asked Eli Lilly to produce more insulin, Pfizer to make more of certain drugs, and AstraZeneca to consider a U.S. headquarters.

Deutsche Bank is seeking to sell its 8.8 percent stake in Dubai-based Abraaj Holdings, a plan that has grown more urgent as Abraaj faces a dispute with investors, including the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation and the International Finance Corporation, over alleged misuse of funds in a $1 billion healthcare fund. Deutsche, which is restructuring and cutting jobs, considers the stake a non-core asset; a valuation sought two years ago was weaker than hoped, and any sale now would likely be at a big discount. Abraaj, which denies wrongdoing, has cut jobs, suspended new investments, and seen its private equity unit's CFO and COO resign.

The "Flash/Back Door" offense attacks the Box & One defense, which is vulnerable in the middle. Flashing a baseline post player into the middle creates matchup problems. When no good shot is available, High/Low post action and wing back door cuts follow, and the offense can flow into Single/Double Screen continuity. Variations include initiating the post flash with a baseline screen for the star player or via an entry pass to the wing. Success depends on execution, coordination, defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience. Game strategies include scouting opponents, alertness to defensive adjustments, deploying varied alignments, and attacking the weakest defenders. The Box & One defense uses four box-zone players plus a "Chaser" who denies one opponent the ball.

This study surveyed 333 teachers in Türkiye to determine the potential of metaverse integration in education, teachers' knowledge of the metaverse, their perceptions of its advantages and disadvantages, suitable application areas, appropriate timing for implementation, and anticipated obstacles. The metaverse is defined as a bi-located virtual universe accessed through avatars and is classified into four types: augmented reality, life diary (lifelogging), mirror world, and virtual reality metaverses. Data were collected through a 28-question online questionnaire developed with input from three educational technology experts and analyzed using thematic analysis and descriptive statistics.

Findings showed teachers' average knowledge of the metaverse concept was 5.25 on a 9-point scale, and 78.1% reported prior experience, though mostly with virtual reality or three-dimensional virtual worlds rather than the current metaverse concept. Teachers held a positive attitude toward metaverse use in education (6.23) and viewed it as advantageous (6.19), citing benefits such as attracting student interest, enabling practice of knowledge, learning by doing, experiencing new technologies, and eliminating limitations in education. However, they also expressed concerns (5.38), most frequently regarding technical problems, psychological problems such as addiction, inequality of opportunity, data security, and teacher readiness. Teachers reported willingness to use the metaverse in lessons (6.37) and strong interest in related training (8.08). They considered information technologies, physics, biology, chemistry, and mathematics the most suitable subjects for metaverse use. Teachers rated the education system, colleagues, parents, and schools as largely unready, while students were seen as relatively more ready (4.59). Most teachers predicted effective metaverse use in education within three to five years.

The study concludes that the metaverse has transformative potential in education but will not serve as a straightforward replacement for conventional learning environments. Successful implementation requires dependable platforms, quality network connectivity, device accessibility, and teacher training before and during careers. The authors recommend cooperation among educators, developers, policymakers, and researchers, investment in infrastructure and diverse content, gradual small-scale implementations, and attention to student health concerns related to virtual reality use.

Kress.

A speaker describes watching his baby being born and praises his wife. Another says a teammate took an elbow to the head, like Patrick Eaves's hit, and the team won for Dino. The Drury hit may face league review.

H.B. Fuller Company (NYSE:FUL) VP Traci L. Jensen sold 5,397 shares on October 2nd at an average price of $58.40, totaling $315,184.80, per an SEC filing. The stock opened at $56.81 on Friday, with a market cap of $2.87 billion, a PE ratio of 25.96, and a 52-week range of $41.52–$58.74. The company reported EPS of $0.65 on September 27th, missing the $0.67 consensus, while revenue of $562.87 million beat estimates of $553.66 million. Analysts expect $2.59 EPS for the current fiscal year. A quarterly dividend of $0.15 will be paid November 2nd to shareholders of record October 19th, yielding 1.06% annually. Analyst ratings include two sell, five hold, and one buy, with a consensus price target of $57.40. Institutional investors, owning 92.37% of shares, recently adjusted stakes, including BlackRock's 10,635.2% increase and Principal Financial's 141.0% increase. H.B. Fuller formulates, manufactures, and markets adhesives, sealants, and specialty chemical products across several global segments.

The speaker's MCL has healed and feels strong, though another injury will need surgery after the series. Despite the tear, they feel no pain, will use a brace, and recovered quickly. Ready and anxious to play tomorrow, they hope a teammate also returns soon.

This preprint introduces LUKB Disease Trajectory (LUKB DT), a web tool built on R Shiny and integrated into the authors' UK Biobank data preparation platform, designed to identify disease trajectories from electronic medical records (EMR). Noting that no public tool previously existed for this purpose, the authors describe a four-part workflow: input of EMR data with analysis parameters, disease filtering via Cox regression with time-varying exposure, disease pair detection using binomial tests for temporal order and directionality, and pair validation through conditional logistic regression on case-control datasets. Confirmed pairs are concatenated into trajectories.

In a case study using UK Biobank ICD-10 data (183,386 individuals, 8,411 with COVID-19, 274 diseases analyzed), Cox regression identified 90 diseases associated with COVID-19; 527 disease pairs passed directionality testing and were confirmed. Resulting trajectories showed COVID-19 primarily led to SARS-CoV-2-related diseases and other medical care, while immune-related diseases did not appear, possibly due to limitations of the ICD-10 data. The full analysis took 55 minutes on 8 cores. The authors note limitations, including reliance on processed records and trajectories constructed from pairs rather than patient data, and recommend using the tool for investigating risk factors rather than patient clustering.

Children with language vulnerabilities, such as developmental language disorder, autism, or migrant backgrounds, need tailored language support, and speech-language therapists (SLTs) often ask educators to model specific linguistic structures—a task that is difficult to sustain in real time. Robot-Assisted Language Learning (RALL) is a promising alternative, but prior systems have been static, teleoperated, or rule-based, with challenges in speech recognition and turn-taking. The authors developed TalBot, combining the ChatGPT LLM with the Furhat robot to lead the word retrieval game Alias with three preschool children. Tested with 13 children with language vulnerabilities and 7 educators, the system managed turn-taking, provided clues and feedback, interpreted mispronunciations, and redirected off-topic conversation, with data protection measures in place. LLMs improve on traditional RALL by handling varied input without predefined structures and accepting approximate rather than exact responses. The team plans to extend TalBot to morphological learning in three ways: generating linguistic material, providing a consistent linguistic model, and acting as a role model for educators. Development will proceed through laboratory studies, preschool field studies comparing robot and educator performance, and a feasibility study with 5–10 children. Remaining considerations include data protection under the EU AI Act, ethical assessment of long-term effects, and practical barriers such as cost and potential resistance.

The Supreme Court will hear on August 17 Lt Col Prasad Purohit's bail plea in the 2008 Malegaon blast case and a plea challenging co-accused Pragya Singh Thakur's bail. The High Court had granted Pragya bail but rejected Purohit's. The NIA cleared Pragya but said charges against Purohit were serious.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K reporting that on May 7, 2015, it issued a press release announcing financial results for the three months ended April 26, 2015, with a CFO Commentary by Colette M. Kress attached as exhibits. The Company also announced, on May 5, 2015, that its Board of Directors approved on May 4, 2015 a decision to wind down its Icera modem operations in the second quarter of fiscal 2016, while remaining open to a sale of the technology or operations. If unable to sell, NVIDIA estimates restructuring charges of $100 million to $125 million, primarily during fiscal 2016, consisting of severance, tax expense items, and other wind-down costs.

Officials from the Grand Erie District School Board and Brant-Haldimand-Norfolk Catholic District School Board met Jan. 23 to discuss amalgamating high school sports in Brantford, Haldimand and Norfolk into one league, potentially by 2019-20. Currently, teams mostly compete only within their own counties. The proposal aims to create one district association providing equitable opportunities for all students, though nothing is finalized and no timeline is set. Travel costs and time are potential concerns. The NSSAA head declined comment, and the Catholic board could not be reached.

David Ellison, whose Paramount Skydance owns CBS News, expressed respect for the network while saying it needs to build trust. Speaking at Bloomberg Screentime, he avoided detailing what CBS News should improve and dismissed claims of a plot to make it a media arm of Trumpworld. His installation of Bari Weiss, of The Free Press, as editor in chief has raised questions about the network's direction. Ellison wants the operation to appeal to the 70% of Americans identifying as center-left or center-right and to become the most trusted destination in news media.

The passage documents the AGESA™ software's host environment interface and UEFI integration. All AGESA core call-outs are funneled through a single interface portal; the host environment must implement a call-out router that translates function numbers into execution addresses, taking a function identifier, function-specific data, and a ConfigPtr containing the standard header.

The UEFI BIOS environment has four execution stages (SEC, PEI, DXE, RTP) across three execution modes. AGESA core files are arranged into libraries that generate four build targets, built with phase-specific Microsoft tools (MASM 6.15 for 16-bit SEC; 32-bit and 64-bit versions of ml and CL for later phases). Configuration options are selected via <plat>Options.c files; no additional UEFI-specific user options exist. UEFI re-defines the StdHeader's first reserved element to store the PEI_Services handle.

The SEC phase establishes the C environment and stack via AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK. PEIMs support AGESA: one performs processor initialization and publishes PPIs (reset, early-init, and post-init PPIs with defined GUIDs), another initializes memory and publishes the MemInit PPI plus a memory information HOB, and a third coordinates warm reset requests among PEIMs. The DXE driver performs late initialization, generating data tables accessible through the published AgesaDxeProtocol; AmdGpuVgaControlDxe controls iGPU VGA decoding via the PciIo protocol.

Build integration requires copying options files, setting AGESA_ROOT and AGESA_OptsDir environment variables, and enabling Cache-As-Ram before AmdInitReset using the ByHost allocation method, without modifying SS/ESP or cache controls during CAR. Two build methods exist: binary modules (indirect, routed interface) and source integration. Platform solutions (e.g., Danube, Maranello) are identified by code names.

Stack procedures are provided as macros containing native, stackless assembly: AMD_RESET_ENABLEMENT provides very early silicon initialization controls; AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK establishes the Cache-As-RAM stack, divides it among cores, sets MTRRs, and preserves EBX; AMD_DISABLE_STACK tears down the stack, disables CAR, and flushes cache lines (BSP invocation only). AARCH64 APUs with the PSP do not use these macros; the PSP initializes DRAM.

Service procedures include AmdCreateStruct/AmdReleaseStruct for parameter block storage (PreMemHeap, PostMemDram, or ByHost allocation), plus routines returning DIMM data eye results, APIC and PCI addresses, executable cache size, current core identification, memory FRU location for a given address, MMIO range allocation, and event log entries read from a circular buffer.

This passage from the TPS7H500x-SP datasheet describes frequency compensation using Type 2A compensation with a 10 kHz target crossover frequency and a power stage transconductance of 16.2 A/V. Seven 330-µF polymer tantalum capacitors provide the required 2.3 mF output capacitance, with an equivalent ESR of 0.86 mΩ. Selected compensation values were RCOMP = 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP = 15 nF, and CHF = 47 pF. A 102-kΩ slope compensation resistor is connected between RSC and AVSS. Power supply recommendations specify a 4–14 V input with a minimum 0.1-µF ceramic bypass capacitor from VIN to AVSS. Layout guidelines cover routing feedback traces away from noise sources, minimizing switch node area and switching loops, separating analog and power grounds, using traces at least 15 mils per ampere, and placing bypass and compensation components close to the controller. The passage also lists related documentation, revision history noting QMLP option releases for the devices, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information with associated disclaimers.

Scotland is abolishing burial and cremation fees for children, with the Scottish government and Cosla agreeing to remove all local authority charges for those under 18. Most councils already waive fees for under-16s. The government will provide £500,000 in funding, bringing Scotland into line with England. The Church of Scotland welcomed the move.

On March 30, 2019, Stephen C. Neal was appointed to NVIDIA Corporation's Board of Directors. Under the company's 2007 Amended and Restated Equity Incentive Plan, he received an initial grant of 1,419 restricted stock units vesting semi-annually over three years, a pro-rated grant of 139 restricted stock units vesting fully on May 15, 2019, and a pro-rated annual cash retainer of $10,890. NVIDIA also entered into an indemnity agreement with Mr. Neal. The report was signed on April 1, 2019 by Rebecca Peters, Vice President of Corporate Affairs and Assistant Secretary.

Young people in Kildare and nationwide are completing college applications due in February. The writer says it is reasonable not to know at 17 what career to pursue, and that any choice may change, as technological advancements over the next 40 years will transform many industries—petrol and diesel engines will become less dominant with electric cars, and fax machines, once widespread, are now rarely used. Employees should make their work as valuable as possible, illustrated by the pay gap between a burger seller earning just over €10 an hour and a surgeon earning €850 per surgery. Companies will seek maximum output for minimal reward, so workers must ensure their skills are not cheap. Not every workday will be enjoyable; life outside work matters most.

Cover 2 is a zone coverage featuring two deep safeties who divide the field in half and five underneath players (two corners and three linebackers in a 4-3 defense) who cover short routes. Its purpose is to defend underneath routes while protecting against deep throws. Strengths include effectiveness against short routes like hitches and slants, wide receiver screens, and perimeter runs, aided by "hard" corners who do not bail at the snap. Weaknesses include vulnerability to four vertical routes and trips formations, as well as run vulnerabilities: a 2x2 formation leaves only one linebacker in the box, and trips formations can leave the weak side exposed. Zone responsibilities include flat zones for corners, deep halves for safeties, and hook/curl and middle hole zones for linebackers. Variations include Cover 2 "Switch" and Cover 2 from a 1-high shell.

Emirates Airlines reversed its decision to discontinue the 'Hindu meal' option from its in-flight menu after receiving negative feedback from customers, particularly Hindus, and confirmed it will continue offering this option.

This study conducts a co-occurrence analysis of 1,076 articles published in the Information Systems Education Journal (ISEDJ) from 2003 to 2024, using author-supplied keywords to identify topics over time. The authors grouped the years into five eras and created term maps using VOSviewer software. Results show evolving themes: 2003–2007 focused on IS education topics such as curriculum, assessment, and pedagogy; 2008–2012 emphasized pedagogy and student issues including retention, social networking, and outsourcing; 2013–2017 saw the emergence of cybersecurity and big data/analytics clusters; 2018–2022 reflected COVID-19 impacts and a split of analytics into business and data analytics; and 2023–2024 featured artificial intelligence following ChatGPT's 2022 release. For the full network, 115 keywords met the five-occurrence threshold, forming nine clusters. The 2008–2012 era was the richest and most diverse, while diversity appears to have shrunk in 2023–2024. Pedagogy held the highest overall ranking, and analytics rose to first. The study is the first known examination of the full ISEDJ corpus. Limitations include reliance on author-supplied keywords and possible term inflation from special issues. Future research plans include allowing the data itself to define eras and continued analysis of artificial intelligence topics.

US job growth beat expectations in January, with non-farm payrolls rising 200,000, while wages grew at their fastest pace since 2009, strengthening the case for a Federal Reserve rate rise in March. Unemployment held steady at 4.1 per cent. Following the data, Treasury yields rose, and some analysts suggested the Fed may need to tighten more aggressively this year.

FERC issued an order approving an extension of NYISO's Automated Mitigation Procedures (AMP) through April 30, 2002, rather than October 31, 2002 as the ISO had sought. Enron had submitted comments opposing the ISO's request. FERC directed NYISO to file a comprehensive mitigation proposal by March 1, 2002, effective May 1, 2002, addressing FERC's concerns with the AMP and how NYISO's overall mitigation measures work together. FERC acknowledged two problems NYISO has committed to fix: limiting mitigation to specific zones and hours that fail the impact test, and exempting bids of less than 50 MW unless there is a demonstrated market power concern. FERC also directed NYISO to work with market participants to examine whether the AMP may be a barrier to entry for new generation, whether other energy-limited resources beyond hydro should be exempted, and to consider must-run mitigation measures consistent with ISO-NE and PJM. FERC cautioned that it expects one mitigation plan for the Northeast as part of the RTO process and encouraged NYISO to collaborate with PJM and ISO-NE in formulating its March 1 proposal.

Leicester City manager Craig Shakespeare said Sunday's 4-2 defeat at Everton, his first loss since replacing Claudio Ranieri, would not affect his players ahead of Wednesday's Champions League quarter-final first leg at Atletico Madrid. Leicester, who had won all five Premier League games under Shakespeare, led 2-1 before Everton scored twice from set plays. Shakespeare attributed his five changes to squad rotation and confirmed captain Wes Morgan will miss the Madrid tie with a back injury.

The speaker said no significant changes were made and the team will learn from the last game and move forward with confidence. He cited poor execution, nerves, and careless puck turnovers that gave the opponent momentum, though the team still had chances to win. They will review video and must improve their forecheck against a strong defense and goaltender. He added that big hits can energize a home crowd and shift momentum.

Dr. Harris L. Rittenberg's family dental practice has served children and adults for over 50 years. Known for fair, quality care, he pursues continuing education and was recognized by the American Academy of Cosmetic Dentistry for restoring domestic violence victims' smiles. Dr. Brittany Jones recently joined the team.

Jimmie Johnson will lose sponsor Lowe's, which is leaving NASCAR after 18 seasons, and says its replacement has a "golden opportunity" to partner with him until his career ends. The 42-year-old seven-time Cup champion says he has a handful of years left, and his bucket list could include the 24 Hours of Le Mans, the Rolex 24 at Daytona, and the Indianapolis 500 if IndyCar adopts halos.

The 5-day low overnight trading strategy trades the S&P 500 when it opens at a 5-day low but closes higher than its open, entering at the close and exiting at the next day's open. Overnight trading averages a 0.04% return from close to next open, making it attractive for mean reversion. Backtested from 2005 forward, the strategy produced an average profit of 15.93% and 0.26% per trade; excluding the biggest winner of 6% in October 2008, the average profit is 0.17%. It was backtested using the SPY ETF from 1993 to today.

The passage describes a patent application for an image processing method, apparatus, electronic device, and computer-readable storage medium for placing external objects, such as three-dimensional advertisement models, in videos. The method involves obtaining a to-be-processed video containing m frames, placing a target three-dimensional model on a target plane of the first frame so that feature points of the model surface fall on the plane, determining three-dimensional coordinates of the feature points in a world coordinate system and their pixel coordinates on the first frame, calculating the camera pose of the first frame relative to the world coordinate system, and determining poses of camera coordinate systems for subsequent frames by tracking the target plane using homography matrices. The target three-dimensional model is then replaced with a target model, which is projected onto each frame according to the calculated camera poses, and all frames are synthesized into a target video. This approach does not rely on feature point extraction or videos with large parallax, resulting in a small calculation amount, fast speed, convenient operation, and high accuracy. Planes in the first frame can be detected using a neural network model such as Mask R-CNN, and camera intrinsic parameters can be obtained through deep learning if unknown. The technology relates to AI fields including computer vision and machine learning, and relevant data may be stored in a blockchain.

New York's Excelsior Scholarship Program, introduced last year, offers tuition-free attendance at SUNY and CUNY schools to graduates from families with gross incomes under $110,000, a threshold set to rise to $125,000. The last-dollar program covers only the $6,670 annual tuition—not fees, room, board, or books—and is funded at $118 million for an estimated 27,000 students. The initiative has shifted how students weigh public versus private options, with counselors reporting increased interest in SUNY, CUNY, and Monroe Community College. Highly selective private institutions such as Columbia, Cornell, and the University of Rochester are less affected, but smaller private colleges face enrollment and financial pressures. In response, private schools have launched initiatives: Canisius, after a 6 percent enrollment drop, cut tuition by about $8,000 through its Excellence Within Reach Initiative; Roberts Wesleyan introduced a Four-Year Promise guaranteeing graduation in four years plus a minimum $8,000 annual merit award; Le Moyne unveiled Promise NY, offering a $10,000 four-year scholarship, a graduation guarantee, an internship, and an alumni mentor; and St. Bonaventure increased scholarships by up to $4,000 per student annually. Some private college administrators argue a better solution would have been expanding the state Tuition Assistance Program to include private schools, and question whether free tuition is financially sustainable. Private colleges enroll about 52 percent of the state's undergraduates and employ roughly 180,000 people. Despite the free public option, some students still choose private colleges based on cost, fit, programs, and perceived value.

Text messaging has become a fast, widely used form of communication, and apps with alternative features are emerging to replace it. Music Messenger is a free app that lets users send songs to express moods. WhatsApp, originally created for iPhone users as an alternative to Blackberry's free international messaging, is now available on any smartphone and supports video, photos, sound clips, emoticons, and personalized backgrounds. Facebook Messenger offers media sharing, HD video chats, sound bites, group chats, no advertising, and customizable emojis and text colors.
