The Federal Reserve has proposed easing the Volcker Rule, which bars banks from making risky trading bets with depositors' money—a practice that helped trigger the 2008 financial crisis. The proposed changes would apply the rule's strictest provisions only to banks that do the most trading. This comes amid broader government efforts to loosen financial regulations under President Trump, including recently passed legislation rolling back the Dodd-Frank law and Mick Mulvaney's curbing of Consumer Financial Protection Bureau powers. The Volcker Rule, named after former Fed chairman Paul Volcker, banned proprietary trading, which had been a major profit source for banks like Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase. Consumer advocates criticize the weakening, while a banking law attorney notes proprietary trading desks have largely disappeared. New Fed Chairman Jerome Powell believes post-crisis rules could be improved but doesn't fully support aggressive rollbacks.

The offside trap is a soccer defensive maneuver in which all back defenders move upfield in unison just before an opponent passes to a leading striker, placing the striker in an offside position. If the striker receives the ball, officials are expected to call offside under Law 11 and award an indirect free kick to the defense. First introduced in the 1900s and widely adopted by mid-century, the trap has become riskier due to changes in the offside law and offensive tactics favoring short, quick passes. Its most common failure is a defender not moving in unison, leaving attackers onside and the goalkeeper exposed; attackers may also avoid violation by standing still. Coaches must weigh player maturity, opponent tendencies, and formation—flat-back-four alignments are more conducive than stopper-sweeper systems. Only one designated defender, the upfield defensive coordinator, may call the trap using a unique verbal or non-verbal signal. Execution requires defenders to line up, communicate constantly, and sprint forward in unison. The trap demands extensive practice and judicious use, since over-use allows opponents to anticipate and beat it.

In this MIT lecture, Gary Gensler presents the technical foundations of blockchain technology through Bitcoin, its first use case. He identifies key design features: cryptographic hash functions, timestamped append-only logs, block headers and Merkle trees, asymmetric cryptography with digital signatures, and Bitcoin addresses. Hash functions map inputs of any size to fixed-size outputs and are deterministic, efficient, one-way (preimage resistant), and collision resistant; Bitcoin uses SHA-256, and addresses apply two hash functions plus base 58 encoding for added security. Digital signatures rely on public/private key pairs generated from random numbers, using elliptic curve cryptography, with key generation, signing, and verification functions. Block headers contain the version, previous block hash, Merkle root, timestamp, difficulty target, and nonce, compressing thousands of transactions via Merkle trees. Bitcoin has roughly 550,000 blocks added every 10 minutes across about 10,000 nodes in approximately 180 countries. Its native currency incentivizes mining: 12.5 bitcoins per block (about $80,000), with a 21 million cap and roughly 17 million already mined. Mining pools, the largest in China and Russia, require cheap electricity around $0.03 per kilowatt hour. Gensler also notes Stuart Haber's 1990s timestamped hashing work predating Bitcoin, the double-spend problem, and that software updates in decentralized networks require consensus. Upcoming lectures will cover consensus and proof of work, then transactions.

Lotte Chemical Corp plans to list its Malaysian subsidiary, Lotte Chemical Titan Holding, on Bursa Malaysia in the third quarter of 2017, offering up to 740.48 million shares plus an over-allotment option of 55.54 million shares. Sources say the IPO could raise $1-$1.5 billion, potentially one of Malaysia's biggest IPOs in years. Proceeds will fund projects in Indonesia and Malaysia.

This 2007 case examines SunPower, producer of the world's most efficient solar cells, as CEO Tom Werner considered how to convert the company's advantage into an enduring competitive edge amid rapid industry growth and competition from larger firms like Sharp and Q-Cells.

Concerns over climate change—CO2 levels rising from 280 ppmv pre-industrial to 380 ppmv in 2006—and energy independence drove interest in solar power. The Kyoto Protocol created a carbon market, with over $15 billion in emissions traded in the first half of 2006. Despite costing two to three times more than conventional electricity, the PV industry grew about 41% annually between 2003 and 2006, with profits expected to top $7.7 billion in 2007. Japan led global PV shipments, while China surpassed the United States as the third-largest producer in 2006.

The industry's five-stage value chain—silicon, ingots/wafers, cells, modules, and installation—faced a silicon shortage that pushed prices from $32/kg in 2004 toward a predicted $55/kg in 2006. Over 1,000 pro-solar policies existed worldwide, including California's $3.2 billion Million Solar Roofs initiative and renewable portfolio standards in 24 U.S. states.

Founded in 1987 by Stanford professor Richard Swanson, SunPower partnered with Cypress Semiconductor in 2001, began commercial cell production in late 2004, and went public on NASDAQ in November 2005. Revenues rose from $6 million in 2004 to $78.8 million in 2005, with its first profitable quarter in Q2 2006. The company integrated vertically, securing silicon supply through DC Chemical, investing in a Chinese ingot joint venture, and acquiring installer PowerLight for $335 million. Its back-contact cells achieved 20.7% efficiency in 2005, targeting at least 22% by early 2007, though at higher manufacturing costs of roughly $2/watt.

Competitors included market leader Sharp (26% share), Q-Cells, fully integrated REC Group, thin-film maker First Solar, China's SunTech, and business-model newcomer Citizenre. Werner faced strategic choices between focusing on module pricing, process improvements, or a combination of both.

A North Korean missile launched early Sunday from near Sinpo blew up almost immediately; the White House described it only as a medium-range device. Weapons expert John Schilling of 38 North said the failure suggests a test of a new, undeveloped system, possibly a design shown at Saturday's military parade in Pyongyang. Anonymous US officials told Fox News it was a new Scud type, the KN-17, a single-stage liquid-fueled missile that could target ships. Some speculated US hacking caused the failure, but Schilling called such claims overblown. Also Monday, Pentagon chief Jim Mattis ordered a review of America's nuclear deterrent.

A hockey player from Brick, New Jersey, describes a one-time opportunity, an exciting game ending in a shootout, his goal of playing in the NHL, and choosing New Hampshire over Michigan, with his father Frans VanRiemsdyk present.

Andrew Lo's lecture provides an overview of equity securities and introduces equity valuation models. Equity represents ownership in a corporation, generating value through dividends (cash or stock) and capital gains; growth companies typically forgo dividends to reinvest cash. Key features distinguishing common stock from bonds include residual claimant status (unlimited upside after bondholders are paid), limited liability (risk confined to invested capital), voting rights, and access to public markets—features that foster innovation and capital formation. Short sales enable negative information to be incorporated into market prices. Equities trade in primary markets (new issuances, whose activity follows business and credit cycles) and secondary markets, where trading volume has grown substantially due to technologies like the internet and electronic communications networks.

The Dividend Discount Model prices a stock as the present value of expected future dividends, discounted at risk-adjusted rates determined by the market according to each cash flow's riskiness. With constant dividends and discount rate, price equals D/r; price rises with expected dividends and falls when interest rates rise. The Gordon growth model, D/(r−g), applies when dividends grow at rate g, requiring r > g for validity, and helps explain technology bubbles. Rearranged as r = D/P + g, the required return equals dividend yield plus growth. The model assumes steady-state dividends; forecasting future cash flows and discount rates is difficult and often inaccurate. Companies rarely alter dividend policies, since cuts signal distress, though extraordinary dividends may follow windfalls.

The passage is a datasheet excerpt for the ADS8681W, ADS8685W, and ADS8689W, 16-bit SAR ADCs with an integrated analog front-end (AFE).

- Analog inputs present a resistive impedance of ≥1MΩ, independent of sampling or signal frequency, allowing direct connection of signal sources without high-voltage drivers. Source impedance on AIN_P should be matched on AIN_M to maintain dc accuracy.
- An internal overvoltage protection (OVP) circuit withstands up to ±20V when powered (AVDD = 5V) and ±15V when unpowered; external protection is required for surges, ESD, and EFT.
- A programmable gain amplifier (PGA) sets input ranges via the RANGE_SEL[3:0] bits (default ±3V × VREF), followed by a second-order antialiasing low-pass filter with a 500kHz cutoff and an integrated ADC driver.
- The device uses an internal 4.096V factory-trimmed, temperature-compensated reference or an external reference, selected by the INTREF_DIS bit; reference buffer drift is typically 0.5ppm/°C (maximum 2ppm/°C).
- Output data is in straight-binary format, with LSB size equal to FSR/2¹⁶.
- Alarm features include a user-programmable input alarm with hysteresis and a fixed AVDD alarm (4.7V low, 5.3V high thresholds), with active and tripped flags readable via the ALARM pin, ALARM_REG register, or appended to output data.
- The multiSPI digital interface supports legacy SPI protocols with single or dual SDO pins and source-synchronous (SRC) protocols, plus daisy-chain topology for multiple devices. The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states.
- Nine configuration registers control device operation; data transfer frames are optimally 32 bits, with defined handling for short and long frames.
- An application example describes an 8-channel industrial analog input module using the ADS8681W with a MUX36D08 multiplexer for PLC, DCS, and DAS systems supporting voltage and current ranges up to ±10V.
- Power supply guidance covers AVDD/DVDD decoupling, NAP and power-down low-power modes, and PCB layout recommendations.

This protocol describes a systematic review of Rapid Response Team (RRT) implementation and service redesign in hospitals. RRTs, originating from the Medical Emergency Team concept introduced in 1990 at Liverpool Hospital, Australia, are acute hospital services activated for deteriorating patients, with variable nomenclature, team composition, and calling criteria. The review will include prospective and retrospective observational cohort studies reporting implementation of novel RRT services or service redesign, identified through searches of Medline, CINAHL, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar. Data on study characteristics, team characteristics, implementation methods, and outcome measures will be extracted independently and in duplicate, with analysis primarily narrative and supplemented by simple statistics on implementation methods. The primary outcome is to describe implementation methods; secondary outcomes address reasons for change, implementation time frames, and outcome measures. Risk of bias will be assessed using the JBI critical appraisal checklist. The review requires no ethical approval, is registered on medRxiv, and has no external funding. Limitations include heterogeneity of eligible studies and a possible lack of studies on service implementation and change management.

On October 24–25, 2001, Enron Corp. replaced Chief Financial Officer Andrew S. Fastow with Jeff McMahon, head of the company's industrial markets group and a former treasurer, placing Fastow on a leave of absence. CEO Kenneth Lay said restoring investor confidence required the change, made one day after he had publicly expressed confidence in Fastow. The move followed an informal Securities and Exchange Commission inquiry into two partnerships run by Fastow—LJM Cayman and LJM2 Co-Investment—which cost Enron $35 million in third-quarter losses and were linked to a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity. Enron's stock fell 17% to $16.41, roughly half its value since the October 16 third-quarter earnings release and down about 80% for the year; the decline also dragged down other energy-trading stocks such as Dynegy. Analysts, including Prudential's Carol Coale, who issued a "sell" rating, said replacing Fastow alone would not resolve concerns about Enron's complex financial structure and lack of disclosure. Moody's placed $13 billion of Enron's debt on watch for possible downgrade. Shareholder lawsuits were filed alleging Enron misled investors and that executives profited from insider trading. McMahon had reportedly earlier voiced internal concerns about conflicts of interest in Fastow's partnerships. Enron denied wrongdoing.

Containerization is an intermodal transportation process in which goods are not unloaded or reloaded, and is also conducted by air by civil airlines and military forces. Commercial airlines use custom-made containers, placed on the lower deck of passenger aircraft and both decks of cargo aircraft. Rising demand for rapid global goods transport and lightweight IATA-compliant containers drive the air cargo container market, while global economic slowdown and rising aviation fuel prices hinder it. Growth opportunities include increasing commercial airlines and rising defense demand. The market is segmented by container type (refrigerated and non-refrigerated), aircraft type, end user, and geography, with major vendors including Nordisk Aviation Products, Zodiac Aerospace, and VRR Aviation.

The passage argues that under China's one-child policy, children were often spoiled, and parents' focus on grades over character and moral development has caused problems when children enter society. It proposes ways to improve family education: liberating children's individual interests rather than prioritizing knowledge and discipline (supported by an anecdote about Chinese and American teams investigating each other's education systems, and surveys showing 80% of children cannot do housework and 17% of those under 18 have emotional or behavioral problems); teaching children to give rather than only receive; getting closer to nature; prioritizing moral behavior education over scientific knowledge, drawing on traditional Chinese moral education (illustrated by the Yao Jiaxin case); engaging in manual labor, sports, and joint parent-child activities to build trust and close the generation gap; providing religious education, whose core value is love; and attending to parents', especially mothers', role, since children learn from them. The passage concludes that family education is a heated topic, and that morality, parental guidance, and traditional moral education should be applied in modern social life.

A comprehensive geoarchaeological study of Egypt's Karnak Temple complex, based on 61 sediment cores and tens of thousands of ceramic fragments, reveals that the temple originated on an island of high ground formed when Nile river channels cut into their beds to the east and west. Before about 2520 BCE, the site was too flood-prone for permanent occupation, placing earliest occupation in the Old Kingdom (2591–2152 BC). Over subsequent millennia, the channels diverged further, creating space for the temple to expand, with new construction built atop silted-up rivers. Researchers also found evidence that Egyptians shaped the river by dumping desert sands into channels. The island's emergence from surrounding waters parallels the ancient Egyptian creation myth of high ground rising from primeval waters, suggesting the site's location may have been chosen for religious reasons linked to the creator god Ra-Amun. The team plans to study other sites across the Luxor floodplain.

Microsoft's Cortana, a voice assistant similar to Apple's Siri, receives updates alongside Windows 10. Originally launched for Windows Phone 7, it now works on desktops, laptops, and tablets, integrates with the Edge browser, and helps locate files on hard drives and the cloud. Some manufacturers are adding dedicated Cortana buttons. Cortana is now available on Android and iOS, though less efficiently than on Windows. It learns users' vocal ranges, offers humor, and provides location-based reminders.

Asia-Pacific equities extended April gains, boosted by French election results, easing North Korea concerns, and strong first-quarter earnings. MSCI's Asia-Pacific index outside Japan traded near a two-year high; Indian stocks led, China lagged. Samsung, CITIC, and TSMC posted solid quarterly profits.

This passage is a Motley Fool Money review of the Wells Fargo Reflect® Card, written by personal finance writer Ryan Wilcox. The card is designed for people seeking to avoid interest while paying down debt or financing a large purchase. It offers 0% intro APR for 21 months from account opening on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, followed by a variable APR of 16.99%, 23.49%, or 28.74%. It has no annual fee and includes cell phone protection of up to $600 against theft or damage (subject to a $25 deductible, usable up to twice per year) when the monthly phone bill is paid with the card. Drawbacks include a 5% balance transfer fee (minimum $5), a 3% foreign transaction fee, and no ongoing rewards after the intro period. The recommended credit score is Good/Excellent (670-850), though approval is not guaranteed. The card was named Motley Fool Money's Best 0% Intro APR Card of 2025. The page also discloses that Motley Fool receives compensation from some companies, including Wells Fargo as an advertising partner, while stating that product ratings are not influenced by compensation.

A hockey coach discusses his team's playoff game, crediting mental toughness, net-front rebounding and screens, and composure without frustration. A player, filling in after a teammate went down, played both wings and scored, finding "second gear" in overtime. Toni Lydman, dealing with a charley horse, made his own call to play after meeting trainers. A returning skilled player who had missed games got four days of practice, while another remains in protocol. The coach dismisses special teams as an issue, saying the team must play better five-on-five, and declines to revisit earlier remarks, focusing on game day.

Former Ford CEO Mark Fields said US automakers "went full bore" into EV production without adequately considering consumer demand, overestimating how the market would develop. His comments came as GM announced a $1.6 billion charge to realign its EV capacity and manufacturing footprint, citing an expected slowdown in EV adoption after the Trump administration eliminated federal EV incentives—a $7,500 tax credit for new EVs and $4,000 for used EVs that expired September 30. Fields said GM's full EV lineup, once seen as an advantage, has become an "albatross" as market take-up will likely be lower than planned. Ford CEO Jim Farley said the incentive expiry could halve US EV sales, while McNeill argued the market can continue growing without subsidies, citing the continued growth in France and Germany after subsidies were rolled back.

On March 26, 2020, NVIDIA Corporation entered into an underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC to issue $5.0 billion of unsecured notes: $1.5 billion of 2.850% notes due 2030, $1.0 billion of 3.500% notes due 2040, $2.0 billion of 3.500% notes due 2050, and $0.5 billion of 3.700% notes due 2060. Net proceeds were approximately $4.97 billion, intended for general corporate purposes, potentially including repayment of indebtedness. The notes are governed by a September 16, 2016 indenture with Wells Fargo Bank, National Association, as trustee, supplemented by an Officers' Certificate dated March 31, 2020. Interest is payable April 1 and October 1 of each year, beginning October 1, 2020. The notes are unsecured senior obligations, may be redeemed with a make-whole premium (subject to certain date-based exceptions), and must be repurchased at 101% of principal plus accrued interest upon a change of control combined with a downgrade below investment grade by both Moody's and S&P.

This passage is from the datasheet of the TPS7H500x-SP series (TPS7H5001-SP through TPS7H5004-SP), radiation-hardened, fixed-frequency peak current mode PWM controllers from Texas Instruments for space-grade DC-DC converters.

Functional descriptions include: output voltage programming via a resistor divider to the VSENSE pin (0.613 V reference); soft-start controlled by a capacitor on the SS pin, with synchronous rectifier outputs activating when SS reaches 1 V; and three switching frequency modes (100 kHz–2 MHz)—internal oscillator (RT resistor), external synchronization (clock at twice the switching frequency applied to SYNC), and primary-secondary mode for synchronizing two controllers. Primary outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) have roughly 150 mA peak current capability and require external gate drivers; OUTB/SRB are active only with the 50% duty cycle limit on certain devices. Dead times and leading edge blank time are programmable via the PS, SP, and LEB pins (fixed 50 ns on TPS7H5003-SP). Pulse skipping prevents minimum on-time issues at high frequency. Duty cycle limits of 100%, 75%, or 50% are set by the DCL pin. The CS_ILIM pin handles peak current mode PWM generation and overcurrent protection (1.05 V threshold), triggering hiccup mode whose timing is set by the HICC capacitor. The FAULT pin enables additional external protection with a 0.6 V threshold. Slope compensation (RSC pin) mitigates subharmonic oscillation, Type 2A/2B frequency compensation is supported, and thermal shutdown occurs at 175°C with restart below 160°C.

An application example designs a 500-kHz, 5-V synchronous push-pull converter using GaN FETs with the TPS7H5001-SP, detailing component selections including RT, feedback divider, dead time, soft-start capacitor, transformer, FETs, RCD clamp, output inductor and capacitance (including single-event transient mitigation), current sense, hiccup, compensation, and slope compensation components. The controllers operate from a 4–14 V supply. Layout guidelines address noise reduction, ground separation, trace sizing, and bypass capacitor placement. The passage concludes with related documentation, revision history, packaging information, and standard TI disclaimers.

The article backtests three simple strategies on Bitcoin (BTC-USD) using free Yahoo Finance data from 2015 to April 2021, excluding commissions, slippage, and taxes. Two trend following strategies were tested: one using a short exponential moving average (best result with a five-day average, yielding a 145% CAGR) and another using dual moving averages (100-day and 250-day), which produced a 115% CAGR versus 94% for buy and hold, with a maximum drawdown of 65% in 2018. A momentum strategy—buying when the close is higher than the close 25 days earlier and selling otherwise—also beat buy and hold while minimizing drawdowns despite a low win ratio. The article concludes that trend following works in Bitcoin because its wild price swings suit such strategies, though Bitcoin's drawdowns (comparable to Nasdaq's 82% after the dot-com bubble) have historically recovered quickly, with no guarantee this continues. Code for the strategies is available in Amibroker and Tradestation.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K reporting results of its 2022 Annual Shareholders Meeting held December 13, 2022. Of 7,456,502,484 shares entitled to vote, 6,407,164,715 were voted in person or by proxy. Shareholders elected all twelve director nominees, including Satya Nadella (94.81% support) and Reid Hoffman (99.36%). An advisory vote approved named executive officer compensation with 88.84% support, and the appointment of Deloitte & Touche LLP as independent registered public accounting firm for fiscal year 2023 was ratified with 95.37% support. Six shareholder proposals were not approved: a cost/benefit analysis of diversity and inclusion (1.26% support), a report on hiring persons with arrest or incarceration records (10.93%), a report on investment of retirement funds in companies contributing to climate change (11.21%), a report on government use of Microsoft technology (20.43%), a report on development of products for the military (10.52%), and a report on tax transparency (22.97%). The report was signed December 16, 2022, by Assistant Secretary Keith R. Dolliver.

A hockey player reflects on a game in which he generated many scoring chances, including two in the first period, but failed to capitalize; he plans to work hard and convert chances in the next game. He notes playoff hockey sometimes offers few opportunities and that different teammates step up as heroes each night. He felt his team's first period was decent, did not perceive a trap, and describes the opponent as a fast, hard-working team that beat three good teams. He considers the Islanders series his best, says his game has fluctuated during the long playoffs but is improving, praises teammate Dave for adapting to a defensive role while still scoring, and says his team must chip the puck in to wear down defensemen, which they did not do enough, but he believes they will respond.

Engineers at UC San Diego have developed ultrasound-powered nanorobots—gold nanowires coated with hybrid platelet and red blood cell membranes—that can swim through blood and remove harmful bacteria and toxins. The platelet membranes bind pathogens like MRSA, while red blood cell membranes neutralize bacterial toxins. The coating also protects against biofouling. In tests, treated blood samples showed three times less bacteria and toxins after five minutes. The work, published in Science Robotics, is still at an early stage, with future plans including live animal testing and biodegradable materials.

The Minnesota Timberwolves, coming off a win over Golden State powered by Karl-Anthony Towns' 31-point performance, host the NBA-best Houston Rockets on Sunday. Minnesota (40-30) is sixth in the Western Conference, 1.5 games behind Oklahoma City. Towns is averaging 25.5 points over his last six games, and Minnesota is 4-4 since Jimmy Butler's knee surgery. Houston (55-14) holds a 2.5-game lead over Golden State for the top seed and is 28-3 since Jan. 6. The Rockets have won five straight meetings with Minnesota, including three this season, though Towns averages 25 points in those matchups.

A team member expressed excitement after a strong playoff game, noting penalties were killed off but much work remains. Jersey has a strong road record, and the team hasn't won in that building in a long time. Practices now mainly loosen players up. Shutting down opponents' top lines has gone well, aided by fast forwards' back pressure.

In Oxley et al. v. Oldden, the defendant obtained a rule to strike off the reference an hour before the referees' report was delivered. No misconduct was alleged; the rule was discharged as the motion was too late.

Stifel downgraded GrubHub from Buy to Hold, raising its price target from $100 to $110, citing a balanced risk-reward profile after 200-percent one-year returns. The analyst remains positive on the Yum! Brands partnership and Tier 2/3 city expansion, raising 2019 estimates, but views current valuation multiples as elevated. Shares fell 1.6 percent Monday morning.

The Nobel Prizes, established by Swedish chemist Alfred Nobel and first awarded in 1901, honor scientific discoveries but recognize only narrow slices of science. Many fields, such as ecology, ocean studies, and climate science, do not fit the prize categories, and because only three people can share a prize, many contributors go unrecognized. Winners tend to be white men from wealthy countries like the United States and Western Europe; in 2023, Katalin Karikó became one of only 13 women to win the physiology or medicine prize, and only one Black person has ever won a science Nobel. Selecting winners takes nearly a year, and prizes often go to lab heads rather than equally contributing colleagues, as with 2024 winner Victor Ambros, whose wife Rosalind Lee did not share his prize. The Nobel Foundation is bound by Nobel's will and unlikely to change the prizes, but winners and experts still view the award as important for celebrating science.

Brett Veach, who became the Kansas City Chiefs' general manager after John Dorsey was fired last summer, will lead his first draft this week. The Chiefs have no first-round pick but hold one second-rounder and two third-rounders. Veach has balanced the salary cap through trades, including sending Alex Smith to Washington for Kendall Fuller and a third-round pick, and Marcus Peters to the Rams for picks. He is expected to trade aggressively for players he likes. The Chiefs will likely target a pass rusher or cornerback early, though they may also add pass catchers and offensive linemen to help young quarterback Patrick Mahomes II. Local prospects include Kansas DE Dorance Armstrong and Kansas State CB D.J. Reed. Recent drafts produced Pro Bowlers Peters, Tyreek Hill, and Kareem Hunt, with Hunt and Hill considered bargains.

This patent application, a continuation of earlier applications concerning splice site classification and aberrant splicing detection using neural networks, discloses systems, methods, and articles of manufacture for using trained neural networks to detect splice sites and aberrant splicing in genomic sequences. The technology relates to deep learning-based training of deep convolutional neural networks, incorporating components such as atrous (dilated) convolutions, residual blocks, skip connections, batch normalization, ReLU layers, sub-sampling layers, and global average pooling, with modifications to architectures described in incorporated references such as WaveNet. One implementation trains an atrous convolutional neural network (ACNN)—with disclosed variants referred to as SpliceNet80, SpliceNet400, SpliceNet2000, and SpliceNet10000—on training examples of donor splice sites, acceptor splice sites, and non-splicing sites. The ACNN receives a target nucleotide sequence flanked by upstream and downstream context nucleotides and outputs triplet scores for the likelihood that each nucleotide is a donor splice site, an acceptor splice site, or a non-splicing site. In the ACNN, the atrous convolution rate progresses non-exponentially between residual block groups, and the convolution window size varies between groups. Another implementation detects aberrant splicing by processing reference and variant sequences through the trained network, comparing splice site scores position-wise, and classifying a variant as pathogenic when score differences exceed a predetermined threshold. Parallel implementations use a conventional convolutional neural network (CNN) for the same splice site classification and aberrant splicing detection tasks.

NFL kickers, often undrafted and minimally paid, specialize in extra points and field goals, becoming heroes or targets of blame in high-pressure moments. Their duties include extra points (now 33-yard kicks), field goals worth three points from 25-60 yards, kickoffs featuring touchbacks and directional kicks, occasional onside kicks, and serving as backup punters. Kickers are expected to make roughly 80% of field goals and 90% of extra points. The position name derives from their kicking role; "placekicker" refers to kicks set by a holder or tee. Required skills include accuracy, lower body power, consistent technique, and flexibility; typical builds are slim, 5'10-6'2, and 180-210 pounds. Notable kickers include Justin Tucker (most accurate ever at 91%, holder of the 66-yard record), Morten Andersen (565 career field goals, Hall of Famer), and Adam Vinatieri (all-time leading scorer with 2,673 points, renowned for clutch playoff kicks). Kickers influence fourth-down coaching decisions, decide close games, and contribute to special teams success through kickoffs and onside kick opportunities.

This is the May 31, 2001, issue of VentureWire, a venture capital newsletter. Top stories: Insight Capital Partners closed its fourth fund at over $740 million, focused on software investments; Whitney & Co. will spin off its Tokyo, Hong Kong, and London offices; Rho Ventures closed Fund IV at $435 million; and fabless semiconductor firm Quake Technologies raised $30 million in a second round led by Bowman Capital. The new money section lists numerous funding rounds, including OmniSonics Medical Technologies' $21 million Series B, Neurotech's $30 million third round, and Toppan Printing's $5 million strategic investment in E Ink. PaperExchange shut down its European operations. New deals include Softbank and Scientia Health Group forming Scientia Japan, an alliance between Eqvitec Partners and IT Provider, and a collaboration between Incyte and Iconix Pharmaceuticals. M&A items include Bertelsmann's reported $30 million acquisition of MyPlay, TMP Worldwide's acquisition of FlipDog.com, and Metavante's acquisition of CyberBills. The newsletter also covers new product launches, board appointments, executive changes, MMC Capital closing its Technology Fund II at $250 million, and Royal Bank Capital Partners adding two professionals to its Energy Fund team.

This work presents a machine learning framework for accurately predicting ionic dielectric constants (εion) to enable virtual screening of high-κ oxides. Since εion—governed by Born effective charges (BECs) and phonon properties—dominates the dielectric response of high-κ materials but is poorly captured by existing single models, the authors decompose it: an E(3)-equivariant graph neural network (EGNN) predicts BEC tensors (trained on 928 oxides spanning 45 elements; R² = 0.982), while a pretrained machine-learned interatomic potential (SevenNet) predicts force constants. Analytically combining these via the ionic dielectric tensor formula, the "joint model" achieves R² = 0.843 for εion, substantially outperforming a direct model (R² = 0.418). Additional EGNN models were built for electronic dielectric constants. Applying this framework, 8,717 oxides from the Materials Project database were screened through stepwise filters—dynamical stability, a machine-learning figure of merit (εave·Eg ≥ 200), and DFPT/DDH validation (FoM ≥ 350)—yielding 38 previously unknown high-κ oxides, 12 of which exceed the figure of merit of KTaO3, the best training oxide. Ionic contributions exceed 90% of the total dielectric constant in these materials. Ten of the 38 have been experimentally synthesized, and 36 contain d⁰ transition metals associated with large dynamic charges; most possess oxygen octahedral networks related to perovskite structures. Future directions include extending to non-oxides and incorporating finite-temperature effects.

North Carolina regulators are discussing tests to determine whether GenX, a little-studied industrial chemical, has contaminated backyard gardens near The Chemours Co. plant near Fayetteville. The talks follow a Dutch study that found GenX in about 40 percent of food samples within 2.5 miles of a Chemours factory in the Netherlands. No decision has been made on whether or how to test. GenX, used since 2009 to replace PFOA, is toxic to animals but its effects in humans are unknown, and no federal standards exist. The chemical was also detected in drinking water for about 200,000 people in Wilmington.

The higher highs and higher lows pattern signals an uptrend but yields weak short-term gains. Backtests on S&P 500 (SPY), gold (GLD), and long-term Treasuries (TLT) entered at the close after two consecutive days of the pattern and exited after 1-10 bars. SPY showed a one-day gain of 0.01% and a two-week gain of 0.23%, half of random gains. GLD performed similarly poorly, with two-week gains below random. TLT showed negative short-term returns despite falling interest rates. Three or four consecutive days didn't improve results. The pattern is a short-term reversal pattern, ineffective as a short strategy, and not powerful enough as a standalone signal.

Jordan Chiles is the only remaining athlete heading into Dancing with the Stars Episode 3, themed "TikTok night," after Baron Davis was eliminated in Episode 2 with a score of 18 out of 30. Following the season's first double elimination on September 23, which sent home Corey Feldman with Jenna Johnson and Davis with Britt Stewart, 12 contestants remain. Scoring combines judges' scores (up to 30 points from Derek Hough, Carrie Ann Inaba, and Bruno Tonioli) with audience votes, each carrying equal influence. Viewers can cast up to 20 votes per celebrity weekly during the live ET/CT broadcast.

A hockey coach discusses preparations for an upcoming game, stating he has not closely analyzed the opposing team's injured players because his focus is on his own team's readiness. The team had a light practice after a six-hour flight, intended to loosen up rather than work on systems. A player named Marc, whose health varies, was not on the trip but remains part of the team; players honored him by having trainers bring his equipment and hanging his sweater in his stall, and he would play if doctors allowed. The coach emphasizes a relaxed but focused approach, saying enjoying the moment helps performance and that he sets that tone. He praises a veteran leader, an assistant captain alongside Bergeron, who has two Stanley Cup rings and plays for his teammates. The team atmosphere stems from coaches and upper management, and the team has identified what needs improvement, planning to alter its game tomorrow.

The passage describes the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, the 8th-generation data center GPU built on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture and fabricated on TSMC's 7nm process with 54.2 billion transistors. The A100 contains 108 SMs, 6912 FP32 CUDA cores, and 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, delivering significant speedups over the Tesla V100 for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads.

Key features include:

- **Third-generation Tensor Cores** supporting all deep learning data types: FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and Binary. TF32 enables acceleration of FP32 data with no code changes, running 10x faster than V100 FP32 operations (20x with sparsity). FP64 Tensor Cores deliver 2.5x V100 performance for HPC.
- **Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity**, a 2:4 sparse matrix pattern that doubles Tensor Core throughput by skipping zero values, with virtually no loss in inference accuracy.
- **Multi-Instance GPU (MIG)**, which partitions a single A100 into up to seven GPU Instances with isolated memory paths, providing quality of service, fault isolation, and security—particularly beneficial for Cloud Service Providers, delivering up to 7x more GPU Instances at no additional cost.
- **Memory improvements**: 40 GB HBM2 with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth (73% more than V100) and a 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x larger than V100) with 2.3x read bandwidth, plus L2 residency controls and Compute Data Compression.
- **Third-generation NVLink** with twelve links providing 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, double that of V100.
- **Other features**: PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, asynchronous copy instructions, asynchronous barriers, task graph acceleration, improved error/fault detection and containment, hardware NVJPG decode, an Optical Flow Accelerator, and five NVDEC units.

The passage also covers CUDA 11 software advances supporting these features and introduces the NVIDIA DGX A100 system, which contains eight A100 GPUs delivering 5 petaFLOPS of AI performance, scalable via NVSwitch, Mellanox InfiniBand, and Magnum IO for large-scale deployments.

Medora Brown, formerly of the U.S. State Department and a New York communications consultancy, joined Sanergy in Kenya as a communications fellow in January 2015 and became communications manager that April. She was tasked with developing the company's social media plan, which required allocating limited resources to strategically chosen platforms, demonstrating social media's return on investment, and engaging diverse audiences including slum dwellers, farmers, and global investors and donors.

Sanergy, founded in 2011 by three MIT Sloan MBA students—David Auerbach, Lindsay Stradley, and Ani Vallabhaneni—addresses Kenya's sanitation crisis, in which roughly two-thirds of Nairobi's 3.5 million residents lacked proper sanitation and many resorted to "flying toilets." The company's non-profit brand, Fresh Life, franchises pre-fabricated hygienic toilets through commercial, residential, and school models, with costs of $290–$500 payable through micro-financing. By 2015, 615 toilets served about 32,000 people, with goals of 887 by the end of 2016 and 36,000 by 2020. Sanergy collects waste daily and converts it into Evergrow organic fertilizer sold under its for-profit brand Farm Star, which sold 118 tons in 2015 and targeted over 2,000 tons annually by 2018.

Kenya, dubbed "Silicon Savannah," had a growing middle class, expanding internet access (26.1 million users by 2014), and 82% mobile phone penetration, though smartphones remained a small share of devices. M-Pesa dominated mobile payments. Social media reached only about 10% of Kenyans daily; Facebook led with over four million users, followed by Twitter and LinkedIn. Social media's growth stemmed from political blogging after a 2007 news blackout, and businesses such as Airtel used it for customer service. Farmers were increasingly active online, exemplified by the "Facebook Farmer" Joseph Macharia, while slum dwellers used Facebook sparingly for practical purposes, and only about a dozen of Fresh Life's 320 franchisees had profiles.

Fresh Life relied on personal contact, events, and SMS, with Auerbach doubting social media could build the trust needed for franchise sales. Farm Star generated Facebook leads at roughly $2 each ($7 including follow-up) and tested WhatsApp for farmer engagement. Sanergy corporate focused fundraising on foundations and large donors, where Auerbach also questioned social media's effectiveness. Brown faced open questions about whether Kenya's cultural emphasis on trust and personal contact would translate to social media and what role it could play in sales and fundraising.

University of Edinburgh researchers identified 287 genes linked to male pattern baldness by studying DNA from over 52,000 men in the British BioBank study. Many genetic signals came from the X chromosome, which men inherit from their mothers. The team developed a formula to predict hair loss risk, though it is only somewhat predictive. Male pattern baldness affects about 80 percent of men by age 80. The findings could help identify those at risk and potential genetic targets for intervention.

Mercy University's School of Education has been strengthened by several federal, state, and local grants. The GRAD-PRO grant, a five-year, $2.8 million award from the U.S. Department of Education's PPOHA program (2023), expands opportunities for Hispanic and underrepresented graduate students across health sciences, education, and business, and includes a Faculty Mentoring Fellowship. The three-year BRANCH-ED grant (2023) from a nonprofit supporting teacher preparation at Minority Serving Institutions focuses on district partnerships and curriculum enhancement, including collaboration with the Public Schools of the Tarrytowns; the School of Education achieved a 100% success rate in Year 1 outcomes. The NSF-funded MISTI program, running since 2013, prepares math and science teachers for high-need middle and high schools through intensive observations, student teaching, mentoring, and long-term cohort support, with research showing it helps teachers persist in high-need schools. The NSF Master Teaching Fellowship (2019–2024) supported 14 PK-12 teachers from high-needs districts in becoming STEM teacher leaders through graduate coursework and leadership projects, producing new STEM programs, publications, and presentations. Finally, the $687,500 CR-ITI/ESOL grant from NYSED (2023–2028) prepares teachers for ESOL certification to address teacher shortages in New York City. Together, these grants advance the School of Education's mission of preparing educators for diverse PK-12 student populations.

U.S. mortgage application activity fell for a second week, declining 0.8 percent to 403.6 in the week ended March 24, despite borrowing costs dropping sharply. The average 30-year fixed conforming rate fell to 4.33 percent from 4.46 percent, tracking lower Treasury yields amid doubts over tax cuts and healthcare legislation. Refinance applications fell 2.9 percent, while purchase applications rose 1.2 percent.

A CORAF report presents results from the SRI-WAAPP project, described as the largest System of Rice Intensification (SRI) project in the world. The three-year project involved more than 50,000 farmers, over 1,000 sites, and 13 West African countries, coordinated by Mali's National Center of Specialization on Rice and Cornell University. SRI, an adaptable methodology that reduces inputs while increasing yields, showed yield increases of 54–153 percent depending on system, and a 41 percent average income increase in an independent evaluation. The authors estimate full adoption in 2017 would have eliminated rice imports, and SRI produced over 20,000 additional tons of milled rice in 2015–2016, valued at about US$10 million. They advocate further scale-up, noting success depends on adapting SRI principles to local conditions. Concerns about labor burdens on women led the team to adopt a labor-saving weeding technology from India.

Retired Toronto lawyer Marcel Strigberger recounts decluttering his house by discarding his McGill University law school books, purchased over 50 years ago. He recalls a contracts text by British authors Cheshire and Fifoot, covering the 1890s smokeball reward case involving Lily Carlill and an 1860s case holding a carriage-owner/prostitute contract unenforceable as contrary to public policy. He also reviews a property book by Megarry and Wade, recalling fee simple, fee tail, and a rule from a 16th-century English decision on life interests in land, and discards it—later regretting it after seeing a used copy on Amazon for over $1,000 Canadian. He also discards a book about a cargo ship explosion case. The books went into the blue recycle bin, though he kept one thick volume to use as a reading stand. Strigberger practiced civil litigation for over 40 years before closing his office to pursue humor writing.

A hockey goalie credits his teammates' defensive play for the team's success and shutout, noting tight games keep him focused. He describes a key save on a bouncing puck late in the second period and says the team stayed focused to protect its lead and deny the opponent momentum. The team now heads to Anaheim, a place that has never seen the Stanley Cup finals, where the opponent will be eager to get on the board and apply pressure.

Five days after the Las Vegas mass shooting, investigators say they still do not know what motivated Stephen Paddock, a 64-year-old reclusive high-stakes gambler who killed 58 people and wounded hundreds from his 32nd-floor Mandalay Bay hotel suite before killing himself. The FBI plans billboards urging anyone with information to call 800-CALL-FBI. Investigators are examining whether Paddock hired a prostitute before the attack, his cruises abroad—mostly with girlfriend Marilou Danley—and a cryptic note with numbers found in his room. Standard investigative avenues like politics, finances, radicalization, and social behavior have yielded little. Paddock planned meticulously, stockpiling 23 guns (12 modified for continuous fire), setting up cameras, and booking rooms overlooking other festivals. He also bought 1,000 tracer rounds at a Phoenix gun show. His girlfriend said she noticed no changes in his mental state.

Estonia's Education Minister Mailis Reps signed a directive creating state-run upper secondary schools in Viimsi and Rapla, opening next September. A hiring round for school leaders has begun, and construction is in its second phase.

This study is a systematic literature review of research on robotic coding in science education published between 2015 and 2022. Following PRISMA guidelines, the WOS and Scopus databases were searched between June and August 2022, yielding 74 studies, of which 15 empirical, peer-reviewed English-language articles met the inclusion criteria. Data were extracted into a structured form and analyzed through content analysis, with codes verified by a measurement-evaluation specialist and a field expert.

Results showed that studies mainly focused on cognitive skills, including 21st-century skills (communication, problem-solving, scientific creativity, cognitive process skills) and computational thinking skills (computational thinking, algorithmic thinking, mathematical understanding). Studies on applications followed, mainly in science and engineering using Arduino and tablet applications. Affective-variable studies addressed interest, motivation, and opinion. Suggestions mostly concerned applications—especially integrating robotic coding into STEM fields, subjects, educational environments, and teacher training—and future research, particularly large-scale studies and different data collection tools.

The review concludes that coding education supports 21st-century skills and that robotics increases interest and motivation, though some studies found no significant differences. Recommendations include addressing additional 21st-century skills, other STEM areas, alternative programming tools (e.g., Scratch, Alice), further affective and psychomotor characteristics, curriculum development, and in-service teacher training. The study is limited to 15 articles from WOS and Scopus published between 2015 and 2022.

Smarts moved under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 54(b) to revise the court's prior opinion (Smarts I) denying its motion for partial summary judgment against Avesta and Zager, based on newly-discovered evidence. Smarts alleged that Avesta's "Trinity" program infringed its patents, while Defendants contended that Morgan Stanley's "Delphi" program was invalidating prior art. In Smarts I, the court denied partial summary judgment because a triable issue existed as to whether Delphi qualified as prior art, relying in part on the Klener Declaration to corroborate prior demonstrations of Delphi. Smarts' subsequent deposition of Klener revealed that, before signing the declaration, he was invited to invest in a private placement of Avesta stock ahead of an anticipated IPO, his investment later doubled in value, and he was friends with Avesta executives Saifi and Arbeitel. Klener denied any quid pro quo. The court held the motion was timely and procedurally proper under Rule 54(b). On the merits, the court rejected Smarts' argument that an interested corroborating witness's testimony is per se insufficient, reasoning that witness bias is a credibility matter for the jury under the "rule of reason." The court further found that the extent of Klener's alleged bias and the passage of time did not eliminate all genuine issues of material fact, given Klener's denials and competing interpretations of the evidence. The motion was denied.

The author recalls Warren Weaver's 1947 claim that translation is decoding, notes that machine translation, despite its utility, has ignored understanding, and questions whether high-quality translation is possible without it, introducing his experiments.

The United States District Court for the Southern District of New York denied in part and granted in part a motion by 1515 Broadway Associates, L.P. and Equitable Life Assurance Society to dismiss appeals by the New York City Department of Finance and the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance from the order confirming 1515 Broadway's plan of reorganization. The debtor, a Delaware limited partnership formed in 1984 to operate One Astor Plaza, filed under Chapter 11 in 1990 after overly optimistic projections left it owing Manufacturers Hanover Trust approximately $330 million. The 1991 Plan settled related litigation, required Equitable to provide up to $133.5 million in funding, and provided for possible sale or foreclosure of the Building in 1995 or 1996. Applying the mootness standards of In re AOV Industries, the court held that the City's challenge to the reorganization of the general partnership into a limited partnership was moot because it was central to the confirmed plan, but the City's challenge to a possible future foreclosure was not moot because that transaction had not yet occurred. The State's Gains Tax argument was also not moot, since the Second Circuit's decision in In re 995 Fifth Avenue raised issues the bankruptcy court could not have considered.

The Twitter account @YesYoureRacist, a member since 2012, gained 271,000 followers over a weekend by identifying participants in the Charlottesville, Virginia protest, where marchers carried tiki torches and displayed posters supporting hate groups. The anonymous moderator asked followers to submit names and profiles of attendees. As a result, Cole White was fired from the Top Dog hot dog restaurant in Berkeley, California, which issued a statement disavowing his actions. Peter Cvjetanovic, photographed holding a torch, said he attended to support "white European culture" and expressed being upset that his photo was shared. The account was featured on Good Morning America and credited with identifying the man who drove into a crowd of protestors, killing one. It also identified James Allsup, a Washington State University student and College Republicans president, prompting followers to contact the university's president.

This passage covers software engineering and requirements classification. Requirements are divided into functional requirements, which specify what software must do, and non-functional requirements (NFRs), which define qualities such as usability, security, and reliability. Text classification approaches include unsupervised, supervised, and semi-supervised methods, with classifiers such as K-NN, Naive Bayes, decision tree, and SVM. Related work addresses domain NFR generation, NFR prioritization, effort estimation, NFR interplay, and NFR knowledge reutilization. The proposed methodology clusters keywords extracted from functional requirements into semantically coherent groups and applies a decision tree classifier with an NFR traceability matrix to classify null and non-null functions from an IVR dataset. Results show the proposed method achieves higher accuracy and lower execution time than the existing method, which uses only the NFR matrix. The conclusion states that null functions reduce project efficiency, and the proposed model, tested in Python, outperforms the existing technique.

The passage describes the NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture, which introduces a Hybrid Rendering model combining real-time ray tracing, rasterization, AI, and simulation.

Key features include:

- **RT Cores**: Dedicated hardware in each SM that accelerates Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, offloading the SM for other work. Turing achieves 10+ Giga Rays/Sec versus Pascal's ~1.1, making ray tracing roughly 10 times faster.
- **Denoising**: NVIDIA Real-Time Ray Tracing Denoiser modules reduce the number of rays required per pixel while producing high-quality results.
- **NGX**: A deep learning technology stack using Tensor Cores, offering DLSS (which matches TAA image quality with roughly half the shading work, trained on 64x supersampled reference images, plus a DLSS 2X mode), InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. NGX requires Turing or later architectures.
- **Mesh Shading**: New Task and Mesh shader stages using a cooperative thread model, eliminating CPU draw call bottlenecks and enabling an order-of-magnitude increase in renderable objects.
- **Variable Rate Shading (VRS)**: Shading rate adjustable per 16x16 pixel region, enabling Content Adaptive Shading, Motion Adaptive Shading, and Foveated Rendering; it can also increase shading rate with MSAA.
- **Texture Space Shading (TSS)**: Decouples shading from screen-space pixels, storing results in texture space for reuse and improved temporal stability.
- **Multi-View Rendering (MVR)**: Renders up to four views per pass (32 at the API level), expanding Pascal's SMP, with uses in VR and shadow map rendering.
- **VR support**: Hardware support for USB Type-C/VirtualLink, and VRWorks Audio accelerated by RT Cores.

Chip details: TU104 (48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, 13.6 billion transistors, NVLink) powers the GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000; TU106 (36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores, no NVLink/SLI) powers the GeForce RTX 2070. The RTX-OPS metric weights Tensor (20%), FP32 (80%), RT (40%), and INT32 (28%) operation usage, totaling 78 for the RTX 2080 Ti.

An appendix explains ray tracing fundamentals, BVH structures, denoising, and ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, illustrated with examples from Battlefield V and Shadow of the Tomb Raider. The document concludes with NVIDIA legal disclaimers, trademark, and copyright notices.

Smoky River FCSS seeks parents with babies aged 2-4 months in October for the Roots of Empathy Program, offered in 2017-2018 at regional schools. The Canadian program, created in 1996 by Mary Gordon, uses classroom baby visits to teach children empathy, increasing positive social behavior and decreasing aggression. Contact Crystal at 780-837-2220.

This preprint addresses the challenge of estimating sex-specific causal effects in Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses when one sex group has a small sample size, focusing on the Million Veteran Program (MVP) where only 10% of participants are female. The authors performed sex-specific GWASs of sleep phenotypes in the MVP and developed a semi-empirical Bayesian framework that borrows information from the larger male population to improve female-specific variant-exposure effect estimates. The framework yields two estimators: a fixed-effects meta-analysis estimator and an adaptive posterior mean (APM) estimator that accounts for sex differences in effect sizes. Simulation studies showed that shrinkage estimators (APM and adaptive weight) improve causal effect estimation for the smaller female group, with the APM estimator being less sensitive to sex differences than the meta-analysis estimator. Applying a two-sample MR approach using MVP exposure data and All of Us outcome data, the authors identified sex-specific causal associations: insomnia was associated with increased chronic kidney disease risk in females, long sleep with higher hypertension risk in females, and short sleep with increased coronary artery disease risk in males. A statistically significant sex difference was found in the causal effect of obstructive sleep apnea on chronic kidney disease, and long sleep showed distinct sex-differentiated causal patterns on several cardiovascular outcomes. Limitations include reliance on the same dataset for instrumental variable selection, sensitivity of results to IV selection methods, and restriction to European ancestry individuals.

PML-N leader Rana Muhammad Tariq Khan, at a ceremony at Govt Girls High School Liaquatabad, Lodhran, urged civil society to support government schools and announced a water pump and furniture. An education official cited Punjab government's free education and Rs1,000 monthly stipends.

Last week's market-moving events—earnings, economic data, Fed policy, and political developments—were clouded by controversy, contradiction, or doubt, and markets flipped decisively risk-off, with major indexes forming a bearish engulfing pattern at all-time highs and declining between 2.2% and 4.2%. Q2 earnings were strong, with 82% of S&P 500 companies beating EPS estimates and 79% beating revenue estimates, while upward earnings revisions reached multi-month highs. GDP grew 3% versus 2.5% expected, though tariff-related distortions clouded the data, and personal spending showed softness. The jobs report disappointed with 73,000 additions versus 100,000 expected, accompanied by the largest two-month downward revision on record outside the pandemic; unemployment rose 0.1% to 4.2%. The FOMC meeting featured two dissenting votes for the first time since the 1990s, with Powell signaling patience, while markets priced over 75% odds of a September rate cut. President Trump fired the BLS commissioner, announced tariff deals, and gained a Fed vacancy following Governor Kugler's resignation. The commentary suggests a tactical pullback may be underway, noting that healthy corrections often begin this way.

In an address to Congress less than three weeks after his inauguration, the President presents a budget plan with four features: attention to urgent priorities, investment in the future, deficit reduction, and no new taxes. He states economic growth will yield over $80 billion in new revenues, allowing a deficit cut of nearly 40 percent in one year while meeting Gramm-Rudman-Hollings targets. He proposes two-year budgets, a presidential line-item veto, and a balanced budget constitutional amendment. Priorities include increased funding for the National Science Foundation, NASA, and education initiatives such as merit schools and National Science Scholars; nearly $1 billion more for the war on drugs under drug czar Bill Bennett; $1.6 billion for AIDS education and research; a new Clean Air Act; indefinite postponement of three offshore lease sales; full Medicaid funding; a child care tax credit; and aid for the homeless. He also supports a referendum on Puerto Rico's political future, savings and loan reform within 45 days, and a one-year defense budget freeze. On foreign policy, he pledges caution regarding changes in the Soviet Union, pursuit of the Strategic Defense Initiative, a ban on chemical weapons, and support for democracy abroad. He closes by asking Congress to cooperate in cutting the deficit while keeping America growing.

The passage presents a theoretically proposed and experimentally demonstrated dynamically-controllable x-ray interferometer for Mössbauer science. Traditional x-ray interferometers require Angstrom-level alignment stability, while multi-target Mössbauer settings avoid spatially separated pathways but lack straightforward selective path coupling and phase variation, and radiative coupling between targets impedes direct phase measurements. The new interferometer uses two ⁵⁷Fe-enriched α-iron targets in a high-purity polarimetry setup, engineered so that only two co-propagating pathways contribute to the detection signal. All multi-scattering pathways involving radiative coupling cancel, the two pathways are individually addressable via their different polarizations, and the empty interferometer ideally transmits no light (dark-fringe mode). Mechanically displacing the first target, mounted on a piezoelectric transducer, tunes the relative phase between pathways. Demonstrated applications include nanosecond-timescale control of transmitted x-ray intensity and measurement of relative target displacements on x-ray-wavelength and nanosecond timescales by observing mechanical waves induced in the target holder.

The passage introduces HARMONY, an entropy-based metric for assessing benchmark reliability in language model evaluation from a distributional perspective. Motivated by the observation that benchmark auditing has received less attention than algorithmic advances, and that structural issues such as redundancy and uneven data distributions can skew results, the authors propose measuring how uniformly model performance is distributed across a benchmark's subdomains. The HARMONY pipeline partitions a benchmark into semantic clusters, gathers per-cluster model accuracies, and computes harmony as the uniformity of the performance distribution across clusters. High HARMONY indicates that aggregate metrics capture broad competence, while low HARMONY obscures model strengths and weaknesses—for example, a benchmark dominated by one subdomain may make a specialist model appear to outperform a generalist model despite poorer cross-domain generalization. The authors recommend reporting HARMONY alongside accuracy. Their stated contributions are the HARMONY metric itself and a large-scale empirical mapping of 19 multiple-choice QA benchmarks across five model families in the HARMONY mean-variance plane. The passage also presents the formal setup, defining a benchmark as input-output pairs partitioned by a semantic similarity function, with performance measured per subset and differences from the weighted mean converted into proximity scores via a Gaussian kernel.

A University of Copenhagen study found excessive social media use can harm emotional well-being. Surveying over 1,000 mostly female participants, researchers found passive use ("lurking") most damaging, causing envy and mood deterioration from unrealistic social comparisons. A 2015 study linked teens' social media use over two hours daily to higher chances of mental illness, though such networks can provide mental health services. Researchers recommend limiting use and connecting rather than obsessing.

This lecture continues the treatment of the weak Hamiltonian effective field theory for b→cūd, focusing on renormalization group equations (RGE) for Wilson coefficients. Because the Hamiltonian is mu-independent, the mu-dependence of the coefficients cancels that of the operators, allowing the operators' anomalous dimension equations to be converted into equations for the coefficients.

The coefficient RGE is solved by changing integration variables from mu to alpha using the beta function—a trick valid to any perturbative order. With the boundary condition set at mu_w (of order M_w), where C± = 1/2 at lowest order (C1 = 1, C2 = 0), the solution expresses C(mu) as C(mu_w) times a ratio of alpha couplings raised to a power. This sums the infinite series of leading logarithms (LL) of M_w/M_b, since alpha times such large logs is counted as order one.

Physically, the W is integrated out at scale M_w and the Hamiltonian is RG-evolved down to mu ~ M_b where the physics is done. For the application B→Dπ, using the RG-improved Hamiltonian at M_b removes large logarithms from matrix elements, aiding lattice calculations.

Higher orders follow renormalization group improved perturbation theory: NLL requires one-loop matching plus two-loop anomalous dimensions, with the running needed one order higher than the matching. One-loop matching is obtained by subtracting renormalized effective theory results from full theory (Standard Model) results. The full theory has no extra UV divergences (conserved currents), and the IR logarithms of p² agree between the two theories, confirming the effective theory has the correct degrees of freedom; M_w is replaced by the cutoff mu in the effective theory. The matching splits the full theory amplitude into large-momentum pieces (coefficients) and small-momentum pieces (matrix elements). Notably, C2's coefficient, zero at tree level, becomes nonzero (roughly −0.3) at leading log.

Regarding scheme dependence: the one-loop anomalous dimension is scheme-independent within mass-independent schemes. At NLL, the coefficients, matrix elements, and anomalous dimensions are each scheme-dependent, but the product C(mu)O(mu) is scheme-independent as a physical observable; the combination B1 + J is also scheme-independent. Consistent use of one scheme is essential when combining results.

Finally, full higher-order calculations involve subtleties: careful treatment of gamma_5 in dimensional regularization (the theory is chiral), and evanescent operators—Dirac structures that vanish as epsilon goes to zero but are needed for completeness in d dimensions.

U.K. patient advocacy groups have asked the country's antitrust regulator to investigate several large drugmakers and their U.K. lobbying organization for suspected coordinated efforts to drive up medicine prices. The complaint follows a dispute over mandatory NHS rebates, which rose from 10% to 23%, prompting AstraZeneca, Merck, and Eli Lilly to halt or scrap $2.6 billion in expansion plans.

This passage introduces an ebook edition of *Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, 1919, Volume I*, covering the Paris Peace Conference, produced by the U.S. Department of State's Office of the Historian in May 2018. The ebook, part of the FRUS series established in 1861, offers portable, searchable content with features such as bookmarking, note-taking, and offline access; readers are advised to cite document numbers rather than page numbers. The preface, citing the President's January 6, 1942 address to Congress, explains that the Department of State is publishing official American records of the 1919 Paris Peace Conference to help avoid the pitfalls of the post-World War I settlement while planning the coming peace. It also lists existing unofficial literature on the Conference, including memoirs, document collections, and bibliographies.

Early purpose-built machines evolved into general-purpose programmable machines and then networked client-server architectures. In the early 2000s, the internet and large-scale datacenters gave rise to distributed systems composed of multiple applications or replicas across machines. Properly structured, these systems are more reliable and enable scalable engineering teams, but are significantly harder to design, build, and debug. As demand grows, containers, container images, and container orchestrators have become foundational building blocks, enabling patterns and reusable components for building such systems.

Students in Brandon Nicklas's televideo production class at Lansdowne High School produce daily morning announcements from the school's television studio, gaining hands-on video production experience. Studio use in county schools is rising: about 100 of the system's 161 schools have studios, roughly half of them digital, though expansion depends on school-level funding since none is centrally provided. A basic live-stream setup costs about $400, while a full digital studio costs $15,000 to $18,000. This year, broadcast production facilitator was added to a list of union-negotiated extra-duty activities, paying $2,005 or $3,004. Educators say studios build skills such as teamwork, communication, and public speaking, with video production skills increasingly in demand. Hillcrest Elementary recently debuted a studio run by librarian Jacqueline Schoen, and Arbutus Middle School's studio is run by secretary Matthew Moser.

Penn Medicine researchers found that a single dose of psilocybin reduced pain and pain-induced anxiety and depression-like behaviors in mice with chronic nerve injury and inflammatory pain, with benefits lasting nearly two weeks. The compound acts like a "dimmer switch" on serotonin receptors (5-HT2A and 5-HT1A). Injecting psilocin—the active substance the body converts psilocybin into—directly into the anterior cingulate cortex produced the same relief as whole-body dosing, while spinal cord injection did not, suggesting psilocybin works by modulating brain circuits rather than the injury site. Because psilocybin is non-addictive, researchers hope it could lead to non-opioid therapies for chronic pain and depression, and possibly other conditions involving dysregulated brain circuits, such as addiction or PTSD. Further research on dosing, safety, effectiveness, and long-term effects is planned.

This study applied DIA-based urinary proteomics to identify biomarkers for hereditary angioedema (HAE), a rare disease characterized by recurrent swelling attacks with diagnostic delays of 8–13 years. In the discovery phase, 20 HAE patients (15 type 1, 5 type 2) and 29 healthy controls were recruited from Peking Union Medical College Hospital. Different urinary proteomics profiles were identified among type 1 HAE, type 2 HAE, and healthy controls, with enriched pathways including complement and coagulation cascades, cell adhesion molecules, immune response, proteolysis, and bradykinin catabolic process. A urinary biomarker panel (C1-INH, KNG1, and EGF) was identified as a promising noninvasive diagnostic tool for HAE, with validation in an independent cohort using PRM-based targeted proteomics.

A ferromagnetic microparticle (radius 24–30 µm) is levitated in a superconducting lead trap via Meissner repulsion at 4.2 K, with motion detected by a dc SQUID and driven by a synchronous feedback technique that transitions the magnet from librational to free spinning. Spin-down measurements show exponential frequency decay, with the damping rate linearly proportional to gas pressure, in good agreement with theoretical predictions (γ/P = 11.6 ± 0.2 vs. predicted 12 ± 0.2 (s·mbar)⁻¹). The rotor operates as a cryogenic pressure sensor over a range from 10⁻³ to 10⁻⁸ mbar, with a lowest measured damping rate of 4.75 × 10⁻⁷ s⁻¹ (decay time ~24 days) and quality factor Q = 1.33 × 10¹³. A maximum spinning frequency of 2.3 MHz (138 Mrpm) was achieved, limited by SQUID bandwidth near 2 MHz and an estimated material breaking limit around 5.5 MHz. A low-frequency precession peak, attributed to torque from the superconductor's image field, was observed and fitted with fl = fx²/fs. Compared to prior magnetic rotors, this setup uses smaller magnets, passive trapping without feedback stabilization, and synchronous driving with low heating. Proposed applications include gyroscopes, gravimeters, precision torque measurements, an ultrasensitive magnetometer for axion-like dark matter searches (10²–10⁷ Hz), tests of collapse models and gravitational quantumness, and studies of rotational quantum and relativistic effects.

Researchers at Columbia University have created a silicon chip that converts a single powerful multimode laser diode into a frequency comb—a light pattern containing dozens of distinct, non-interfering color channels. Discovered accidentally during LiDAR research, the chip uses a locking mechanism to purify the noisy laser output, then exploits nonlinear optical properties to split it into evenly spaced frequencies. This compact device could replace racks of individual lasers in data centers, cutting costs and improving efficiency, particularly for wavelength-division multiplexing as AI drives demand for faster data transfer. Beyond data centers, the technology could enable portable spectrometers, optical clocks, quantum devices, and advanced LiDAR systems.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on October 22, 2015, announcing its third quarter 2015 financial results. The filing includes a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures as Exhibit 99.2. The report was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Uber board member David Bonderman resigned after saying during a meeting on the company's sexual harassment investigation that more women on the board would lead to "more talking." He called the comment "careless, inappropriate and inexcusable." The resignation followed other departures, including CEO Travis Kalanick's indefinite leave and executive Emil Michael's resignation. The remark came as board member Arianna Huffington discussed adding a second woman to the board.

Paul Tudor Jones said the ingredients are in place for a massive rally before a "blow off" top to the bull market, comparing today's market to the setup before the dot-com bubble burst in late 1999, citing dramatic tech rallies and speculative behavior. He said AI circular deals and vendor financing make him nervous. Unlike 1999, the Fed has begun easing and the U.S. runs a 6% budget deficit versus a then-surplus. The Nasdaq Composite has bounced 55% from its April bottom to record highs, driven by megacap tech AI investments. Jones believes the bull market still has room to run and would own gold, cryptocurrencies, and Nasdaq tech stocks through year-end.

The eighth annual Regional Theatrical Youth Camp runs June 19–30, 2017, with a production of "Bye, Bye Birdie, Jr." plus a July 2 show. Level I (ages 5–8) has fewer training hours; Level II (ages 9–18) includes 50 hours and a guaranteed role. Cindy Brown directs, assisted by Kenny Brown; Oliver Companies sponsors.

Diffusion Pharmaceuticals Inc (NASDAQ:DFFN) shares rose 6.56% in the most recent session, with the latest closing price at $0.65. Analysts project a 52-week price target of $89.3, based on one opinion. The stock's ATR-14 is 0.12, weekly volatility is 8.70%, and monthly volatility is 10.55%. Its RSI is 31.95.
