The passage covers reactions to John Oliver's book portraying Mike Pence's family pet rabbit as gay, which some LGBT liberals celebrated as "pwning" Pence. A Twitter user noted pride flags appeared in photos of Pence at a Savannah St. Patrick's Day parade. Gay conservative Chad Felix Greene responded, arguing Pence appeared happy and unaffected, calling the activists' efforts a waste of time and describing Pence as polite and friendly. A user named Fran disputed Greene, citing Pence's praise of James Dobson and calling religious freedom discrimination. Greene called her misinformed and shared an article; Fran declined to debate. Another user mocked Pence, which Greene dismissed as silly.

Zeenews.india.com's cookie policy explains how cookies and similar tracking technologies are stored on and accessed from users' devices when visiting its sites. Cookies are small text files used to identify users, remember preferences, track site usage, control access to content, protect the sites, and support research. Third-party service providers also use persistent cookies to analyze usage and improve user experience. Cookies are categorized as first-party (set by the site itself) or third-party (set by external services such as embedded content or social media platforms), and as persistent or session cookies. Functional categories include essential, analytical/performance, functionality, and advertising cookies. Users may refuse or delete cookies through browser settings, though this may limit access to certain site features. Collected data is retained only as long as necessary, and questions can be directed to the provided contact email.

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture transcript covers a class discussion on reverse logistics and closed-loop supply chains. The professor and students first debate the viability of ReCellular, a company that collects donated cellphones for resale in secondary markets. Supporters cite evolving technology, price-sensitive "laggard" consumers, and emerging markets; critics point to shrinking margins, rapid product turnover, and consumers' reluctance to donate phones they now pay for. The class contrasts ReCellular's niche model with Genco's diversified, retailer-partnered approach.

The discussion then turns to Whirlpool's options for appliance recycling in Canada under extended producer responsibility: joining an industry-funded organization (IFO), building its own closed-loop system, or opposing regulation. Students estimate IFO costs at roughly $35 million (about $47–$80 per unit), compared to approximately $70 per unit in forward distribution costs. The professor reviews Whirlpool's Canadian network (17 factories, 24 distribution centers, 2,400 retailers), the operational barriers of reverse collection, and notes that Whirlpool ultimately chose a closed-loop approach, though it proved more expensive than anticipated.

Finally, student groups present final projects on companies including Zara, Hewlett Packard/Dell, BMW, and Philip Morris International, with comments on industry environmental practices and life-cycle emissions. The professor announces an upcoming case study assignment due Wednesday.

NVIDIA Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended May 1, 2016 (first quarter of fiscal 2017) reports revenue of $1,305 million, up 13% from $1,151 million a year earlier. Gross margin was 57.5% (up 80 basis points), operating expenses were $506 million (up 6%), income from operations was $245 million (up 39%), and net income was $196 million, or $0.33 per diluted share, up 46% and 38%, respectively. The effective tax rate was 18.6% versus 22.0% in the prior-year period.

GPU segment revenue was $1,079 million (up 15%), driven by high-end GeForce gaming products and over 60% growth in Datacenter revenue related to deep learning demand. Tegra Processor revenue was $160 million (up 10%), driven by automotive sales. All Other revenue of $66 million came from the Intel patent license. By market, Gaming was $687 million, Professional Visualization $189 million, Datacenter $143 million, Automotive $113 million, and OEM & IP $173 million.

Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $4.75 billion at May 1, 2016, down from $5.04 billion at January 31, 2016. Operating cash flow was $309 million. The company entered a $500 million accelerated share repurchase agreement (initial delivery of 12 million shares) and paid $62 million in dividends ($0.1150 per share), returning $562 million to shareholders; it intends to return approximately $1.00 billion in fiscal 2017.

The $1.50 billion 1.00% Convertible Senior Notes due December 1, 2018 remained convertible at holders' option, with a $1.42 billion carrying value classified as a current liability. NVIDIA and Samsung resolved all intellectual property disputes through an April 28, 2016 binding memorandum of understanding, with subsequent dismissals also ending claims against Qualcomm; litigation with Advanced Silicon Technologies was resolved with a $16 million license payment. A new Santa Clara headquarters is being financed through an off-balance-sheet build-to-suit operating lease with bank commitments of up to $380 million, targeted for completion in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2018. Restructuring charges of $1 million related to the Icera modem wind-down. Management concluded disclosure controls were effective, with no material changes to internal control over financial reporting.

The coach expressed confidence in Matt, citing his makeup, ability to refocus after unfavorable circumstances, and strong playoff body of work. Regarding Geno, he said the staff encourages players to make plays with calculated risk; Geno is buying into the team concept but must reach another level and balance creativity with simple plays. He does not believe Geno is giving up the puck too quickly, noting opponents defend hard and play a give-and-go game. He attributed the power play's struggles to poor entries and limited zone time, noting fewer penalties are called in the playoffs. He praised the group, including Brian Dumoulin, for stepping into larger roles, blocking shots, and defending hard.

In soccer, individual defending requires a defender to engage an opposing ball carrier quickly, after getting goal side and assuming a proper stance. Depending on teammates' defensive positioning, the defender either uses aggressive defending—cutting off the ball, tackling as the opponent receives it, interposing between dribbler and ball, or preventing the opponent from turning—or attack stalling, which delays the dribbler until teammates recover and set up team defense. Attack-stalling tactics include staying goal side, keeping a clean stance, not over-reacting to fakes, denying passes or shots, slowly giving ground, restricting the dribbler's vision, jockeying, shepherding, and stealing the ball when control is lost. A defender can only backpedal so far—usually about 25 yards from goal—before standing ground or tackling. Oral communication from teammates, the defensive organizer, or the goalkeeper is critical, using delay calls ("Contain," "Delay," "Jockey," "Stand him up") or tackle calls ("Challenge," "Tackle," "Take him"). If beaten, the defender turns and gives immediate chase, possibly performing a defensive switch. Coaches must teach defenders proper stances for different field locations, each technique, and the communication terms, using progressive practice drills, and should find a qualified assistant if unable to demonstrate the techniques themselves.

Michigan State Police closed all lanes of I-696 in both directions Tuesday morning after a man threatened suicide. Officers arranged 13 semi trucks under the bridge to shorten any potential fall. After several hours, the situation ended peacefully, and the man was taken to Beaumont Hospital for evaluation.

This patent application, a continuation of several prior applications, relates to controlling uplink data transmission in wireless communication systems when a device is in an enhanced coverage state. Enhanced coverage functionality extends cell coverage through repeated data transmissions, but this causes high power consumption, which is problematic for devices that cannot be frequently recharged, such as asset trackers.

A device is considered to be in an enhanced coverage state if it is in certain coverage enhancement modes, levels, or coverage classes, if signal strength or quality is below a threshold, or if the number of transmission repetitions exceeds a threshold. When in such a state, the device can reduce power consumption by refraining from sending uplink data based on factors including data type (e.g., emergency versus non-emergency), Quality of Service, device movement, timer or counter status, battery level, and whether the device is plugged into a power supply.

Two solutions are described. In Solution 1, an application queries the modem (e.g., via AT commands) for radio coverage information and decides whether to refrain from transmitting data. In Solution 2, the application instructs the modem to transmit data conditionally based on specified coverage-related conditions. Data that is not sent may be dropped or retained for later transmission.

Additional or alternative conditions include wait time durations, number of attempts, device location/speed (obtained from location sensors or accelerometers), battery level thresholds, and power supply connection. The network can configure transmission restriction parameters through various downlink messages, such as Attach Accept messages, EPS Bearer Context Request messages (via Protocol Configuration Options), RRC messages, USIM application toolkit, or OMA device management. The approach can also apply to mobile terminated messages, where an application server or Services Capability Server receives coverage information from the network to decide whether to forward messages.

This study investigated the association between rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and three comorbid conditions—depression, obesity, and hypertriglyceridemia (HTG)—focusing on whether their coexistence synergistically influences RA prevalence and whether inflammatory status modulates this relationship. Using NHANES data from 2007-2010, 4,136 subjects were included, of whom 305 had RA. RA subjects showed higher CRP levels, and depression, obesity, and HTG were each associated with elevated inflammation. Depression or obesity individually increased RA prevalence, but HTG alone did not. However, the coexistence of depression with obesity or HTG substantially increased RA prevalence, with the strongest effect observed at medium CRP levels (1-3 mg/L). For example, at medium CRP, RA prevalence was 27.2% among subjects with both depression and obesity, compared to 19.5% and 5.5% for each condition alone. Three-way chi-square tests confirmed the synergistic relationship. The authors conclude that inflammatory state plays a role in these interactions and suggest incorporating such comorbidity interactions into RA prediction models. Limitations include the cross-sectional design, self-reported RA diagnosis, and reliance on CRP as a nonspecific inflammatory marker.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated June 26, 2020, reporting under Item 7.01 that it issued a press release announcing a strategic change in its retail operations, including closing Microsoft Store physical locations. The press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration, and Chief Accounting Officer. Microsoft's registered securities include common stock and three series of notes (2.125% due 2021, 3.125% due 2028, and 2.625% due 2033), all trading on NASDAQ under the symbol MSFT.

The speaker argues that age is irrelevant in today's game, which rewards knowledge and positioning over speed or skill, making a mix of veteran players valuable. He notes critics once claimed the team couldn't win playoffs with Brett Hull, yet they won a cup, and says contributions go beyond goals. He reports only minor soreness, no serious injuries. He had expected to re-sign with Dallas, but budgetary delays led him to ask Mike to contact Detroit after speaking with Chelios and Shanny, and he feels fortunate, having had nowhere to play in August.

A hockey player describes a leg injury caused by an opponent falling on him, saying he has not had it checked but hopes to play tomorrow night after seeing how it feels, and that he would do anything to return, especially for the Stanley Cup Finals. SDXC cards with XPC=0 operate at 0.36W maximum; XPC=1 allows 0.54W with Speed Class, requiring re-initialization to change. UHS-I hosts request 1.8V signaling via ACMD41; UHS-II cards always indicate S18A=0.

A survey by True Potential found the average UK person's debt grew by £560 in the first quarter of 2017, with lone parents taking on the most (£930–£940), possibly due to helping children with tuition fees. Around 15% of people borrow "just to get by," rising to 20% of single parents. Average debt is £1,797, highest among 45–54-year-olds and in the North East of England. Information Systems (IS) research has historically shown a positivist bias but has shifted from technical toward human and social factors, as reflected in Ray Paul's 2007 definition of IS as emerging from users' adaptation of IT and processes. The paper examines two parallel developments: complexity science and the User Experience (UX) approach, both of which emphasize time and irreversibility in far-from-equilibrium systems. Complexity science, developed in evolutionary biology and chemistry and accelerated by computing advances, challenges reductionist neo-Darwinian orthodoxy by placing self-organisation, rather than natural selection, as evolution's primary force. Theorists such as Prigogine and Kauffman describe bifurcation points, dissipative structures, and systems existing at the "edge of chaos," where prior conditions cannot predict outcomes. Cilliers distinguishes complex from merely complicated systems: complex systems cannot be understood by analyzing components, exhibit rich, non-linear interactions, operate far from equilibrium, and possess histories. UX prioritizes subjective look, feel, and satisfaction over usability's operational measures, treating information systems as complex rather than complicated. The paper critiques earlier complexity-in-IS work, particularly Benbya & McKelvey's reliance on Simon's near decomposability, endorsing Kallinikos's objections and arguing that self-organisation better describes IS. A Knowledge Transfer Partnership between the University of Salford and UX firm Sigma Ltd will explore how irreversibility affects design, usability, and success.

This paper presents a systematic framework for applying Knowledge Graph Embeddings (KGEs) to Ontology Alignment (OA), integrated into the OntoAligner Python library. Source and target ontologies are parsed into RDF-style metadata, and their triples are unified into a "triple factory." OA is formulated as a link prediction task over the merged ontologies, with KGE models trained via PyKEEN using negative sampling. Alignments are computed through cosine similarity between learned embeddings, followed by post-processing that enforces a one-to-one cardinality constraint and a confidence threshold. The framework supports 17 KGE models—including TransE, TransR, DistMult, ComplEx, RotatE, and ConvE—selected based on their frequency in OA literature and performance in broader knowledge graph tasks. The paper reviews related KGE-based alignment work and describes the modular Parser, Encoder, and Aligner pipeline architecture.

The DAWN-PLASMA study was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 proof-of-concept multicenter trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of convalescent plasma in hospitalized adults with COVID-19, based in part on the WHO master protocol. Participants were randomized 2:1 to standard of care (SOC) plus convalescent plasma versus SOC alone. Plasma (800–1000 mL in 4 doses, with a minimum neutralizing antibody titer of 1/160) was administered early, with the first dose within 12 hours of randomization. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients alive and free of mechanical ventilation at Day 15; secondary endpoints included clinical status, time to sustained clinical improvement, mechanical ventilation or death, safety, and quality of life. Between May 2, 2020 and January 26, 2021, 489 patients were randomized (326 plasma, 163 control). The study was conducted according to the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP guidelines, with informed consent required before enrollment. Analyses used a Full Analysis Set (primary) and a Per Protocol Set (sensitivity); protocol violations leading to PPS exclusion were plasma-arm patients receiving fewer than 4 units (n=26) and SOC patients receiving plasma (n=3). The primary endpoint did not differ between groups (83.7% plasma vs 84.1% control; OR 0.99, p=0.976), with similar results in the PPS. Amendments to the statistical analysis plan addressed consent withdrawals, site pooling, and subgroup analyses.

The match-up zone defense combines person-to-person and zone principles and is unique in that it uses a series of defensive rules. Its advantages are that offensive alignments never split defenders, overloads are easier to defend, and opponents tend to get confused. Success depends on smart, knowledgeable players and communication. While fundamentally a passive defense reacting to offensive movement, it can be supplemented with aggressive traps and can dictate offensive alignment by showing a different zone on the first possession before applying match-up rules.

Basic match-up rules assign X1 through X5 to positions from point guard to post player, with each defender's assignment determined by the offensive alignment—2-3, 1-3-1, 1-2-2, or 1-4. Assignments may be adjusted to a team's personnel.

Against cutters, basket cuts are defended by denying for three steps before switching with a weakside defender, though on certain cuts defenders can interchange roles instead of switching, which simplifies defending and confuses the offense but requires players to play multiple positions. The passage details specific switching and interchanging rules for defending point cuts, wing cuts, baseline cuts, post flashes, and post rolls against each alignment. Against two-guard alignments, playing a straight 2-3 zone initially can force the offense into a one-guard alignment. The 1-4 alignment, which uses agile outside-shooting posts, does not pose a problem for the match-up zone because of its rules-based structure.

Finally, match-up rules can be extended into full and half court trapping, applied when the ball enters a primary trap zone (corner), and used strategically, such as after a timeout, on a free throw, or when trailing late in the game.

The S&P 500 has reached its average annual return of 9.1%, prompting caution ahead of a seasonally weak August–October period. July jobs data missed expectations with only 73K jobs added, while May and June figures were revised down by 258K, signaling economic slowdown. However, Q2 earnings have been strong: 15 of 17 mega-cap companies beat earnings expectations, lifting S&P 500 earnings growth from 7.7% to 11.2% and sales growth from 4.5% to 5.6%. The US dollar rallied to 2024 lows but was rejected after new tariff announcements and weak data. Despite AI-driven earnings strength, high valuations (22x–25x P/E) and a negative equity risk premium suggest potential market weakness in coming months, possibly creating a favorable setup by year-end.

DomeShelter Australia offers the Container Mounted DomeShelter™ (CMDS), a weather-resistant, relocatable shelter engineered to withstand Australian Wind Regions Class A to D. Its steel frame attaches to existing container shelters by welding, bolting, or Twistlock. The CMDS benefits industries including oil and gas, agriculture, events, and tourism by protecting goods and livestock from heat, moisture, and UV exposure. DomeShelter Australia is a family-owned provider of industrial shade and shelter solutions worldwide.

This patent application, a continuation of several related applications, describes systems and methods for providing user interfaces to confirm whether to review or take an action associated with an untrusted email or domain. Noting that existing anti-ransomware technologies remove threats without user involvement and provide no training, the disclosed solution pauses user actions (such as clicking a URL) related to untrusted emails and prompts the user to either confirm proceeding or revert to review, giving users autonomy and real-time training. A driver monitors process creation; a user console determines whether a process is significant and injects a monitor library that detects URL-access requests to untrusted domains and pauses the request. The user console resolves the URL, queries a server about trustworthiness, and displays a notification based on locally stored settings. Company administrators can dynamically customize notification content, wording, colors, and element visibility via a console, with changes deployed automatically without involving the security awareness system administrator; different notifications can be created for different user groups. The server and client compare settings hashes to determine whether updated settings must be transmitted to the client. User responses may be recorded for analysis, training customization, and behavior monitoring. The system also supports browser-based email clients through a URL navigation monitoring module implemented either as injected code or as a browser extension that communicates with the operating system via a Browser Intermediary Application. The invention may be delivered as software as a service and supports training related to both simulated and real phishing attacks.

The passage describes a fluid flow measuring and control device for installation in plumbing. The device comprises a main flow channeling system with an inlet and outlet, a bypass channeling system in parallel containing a flowmeter, a valve (e.g., solenoid) for stopping flow, pressure sensors upstream and downstream of the valve, and a transceiver that sends data to a computer. The flowmeter uses a wheel with rotating blades monitored by a pair of movement sensors, enabling detection of flow direction and backflow to measure net flow accurately. The computer stores pre-recorded fluid usage signatures of specific appliances and compares measured data to these signatures to identify which appliance was used and detect abnormal usage, instructing the valve to close when needed. For leak detection, the valve is temporarily closed and pressures compared: a low-to-medium pressure drop indicates a leak (valve remains closed), while no drop or a high drop indicates normal use (valve reopens). Notifications can be sent to a user's mobile device via a remote server. Applications include detecting overuse, leaks as small as one drip per minute, pipe breaks, appliance deterioration, estimating occupancy in rentals, and scheduling public toilet maintenance.

This passage, from a book on distributed system patterns, argues that identifying common patterns can transform distributed system design from a "black art" into a regularized practice, much as design patterns improved algorithmic development and object-oriented programming. Distributed systems are applications composed of many components running on many machines.

The book first covers single-node patterns built from groups of containers co-located on one machine. Splitting a single-machine application into multiple containers is motivated by resource isolation (e.g., separating a latency-sensitive user-facing service from a best-effort background loader with different resource requirements and termination priorities), team scaling (small, focused teams of roughly six to eight people owning reusable modules), and separation of concerns (easier testing, updating, and deployment with fewer dependencies and more reliable rollouts). In Kubernetes, tightly grouped, coscheduled containers that may share filesystems, network namespaces, and memory are called pods.

Three single-node patterns are described:

- **Sidecar**: a sidecar container augments an application container, often without its knowledge. Examples include an nginx sidecar adding HTTPS termination to a legacy HTTP service, a configuration-management sidecar syncing API-driven configuration to a shared filesystem, a topz container sharing the PID namespace for resource introspection, and a Git-sync sidecar enabling a simple PaaS. Building reusable sidecars requires parameterization (preferably via environment variables), a stable API (where even subtle changes, such as altered units or defaults, can be breaking), and documentation (Dockerfile EXPOSE, ENV, and LABEL directives).
- **Ambassador**: an ambassador container brokers communication between the application container and the outside world. Applications include client-side sharding (e.g., twemproxy proxying to sharded Redis or memcached), service brokering for portability across environments, and request splitting for experimentation (e.g., nginx sending 10% of traffic to an experiment, using IP hashing for consistent user experience).
- **Adapter**: an adapter container transforms a heterogeneous application's interface into a standardized one, such as exposing Prometheus-compatible metrics for Redis, normalizing logs with fluentd, or performing rich health checks (e.g., running representative queries against MySQL) without modifying the original container.

The passage then turns to multi-node patterns, which are loosely coupled and communicate via network calls. Microservices—many components in separate processes communicating over defined APIs—offer reliability, agility, small-team ownership, decoupled release schedules, and independent scaling, but make debugging and architecture harder; shared patterns mitigate these challenges.

The replicated load-balanced service pattern consists of identical stateless servers behind a load balancer; at least two replicas are needed for high availability. Readiness probes inform the load balancer when replicas can serve traffic. Session tracking (IP hashing internally, cookies externally, ideally with consistent hashing) routes a user's requests to the same replica. An HTTP-aware caching layer (e.g., Varnish) is best deployed as a separate tier of a few large caches rather than as sidecars, and can also provide rate limiting and denial-of-service defense; an additional nginx tier handles SSL termination.

Finally, sharded services give each replica (shard) only a subset of requests and suit stateful data too large for one machine. A sharded cache example shows sharding raises usable cache capacity (50% of the dataset versus 5% when replicated). Cache hit rate affects system capacity and latency, so failures and rollouts matter; replicated sharded caches make each shard resilient and allow hot scaling. Sharding functions map requests to shards via hashing and the modulo operator, requiring determinism and uniformity; careful key selection (e.g., country plus request path) is vital, and consistent hashing limits remapping when the number of shards changes.

Analyzing district and school data, the author finds that schools strong in one subject tend to be strong in others. Of districts previously identified as exceptional at teaching reading or math, 140 appeared on both lists, while only 14 excelled in one subject but significantly underperformed in the other (12 of those were strong in math but weak in reading). In Mississippi, 2025 school-level reading and math scores showed a strong correlation of 0.87. Because scores may reflect student composition rather than school quality, the author also examined growth rates using Mississippi's value table model: among the 50 schools with the greatest reading gains, none fell below the statewide average in math growth, and similar correlations appeared in Florida. The author concludes it is rare for a school to excel in one subject while letting students down in the other.

Crystal morphology strongly influences the sensitivity and performance of energetic materials such as PETN and RDX, as well as pharmaceuticals. Existing Wulff-based prediction methods (BFDH, SE, AE) deviate from experimental morphologies: BFDH neglects energetics, while the SE and AE models, though energetics-based, cannot capture growth kinetics or compute kinetic parameters and are sensitive to the chosen set of planes. The authors introduce a kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC)-based technique that predicts crystal morphology using only intermolecular interaction parameters, implemented in an open-source Python package, cgkmc, and applied to PETN growth, showing agreement with the AE model and experiments. In the model, the system is encoded on a colored undirected graph: nodes represent lattice sites with occupation numbers, and edge weights represent distance-dependent interaction energies. Coordination numbers identify surface sites eligible for adsorption or evaporation. Adsorption rates depend on diffusivity and solubility, while evaporation rates follow harmonic transition state theory with a dynamically updated prefactor ensuring equilibrium at a target crystal size. The residence-time algorithm time-evolves the configuration to simulate growth.

Soccer teams must have a corner kick defense plan ready for immediate implementation whenever a corner kick is conceded. Although studies show the chance of scoring from a corner kick can be as low as 2% at professional levels, this success requires tactical decisions and practice; without a plan, corner kicks are dangerous. Common elements of corner kick defense include: coaches developing and introducing the plan, every player having a specific job, the goalkeeper remaining in charge, players reacting quickly to their positions, defenders aggressively winning the ball, clearing it high, far, and wide, and provisions for transitioning into a fast-break attack.

Three defensive approaches are described. Zone defense assigns players to cover specific field areas; it is easy to teach and moves defenders away from the goal, but opponents can flood a zone and defenders may hesitate. Man-to-man marking pairs each defender with one attacker; it is easy to understand and avoids flooded zones, but defenders may run backward toward goal, scramble to cover attackers, or lose focus. A mixed combination of both has been shown in at least one study to be least likely to concede goals; typically, the post players and six-yard-line players hold zones while remaining defenders mark man-to-man.

Coaches should introduce these concepts progressively through drills, scout opponents' corner plays, modify plans game-to-game, and practice until responses become intuitive. The goalkeeper should position centrally, roughly one step ahead of the goal-line at about a 45-degree angle, and the player covering the kicker acts as a "one-man wall."

The Mid Screen Offense, used by every NBA and WNBA team, is a set offense executed in the center of the floor with shooters on the wings, taking away helpside defense. Its basic action involves the point guard driving off an on-ball screen set by a high post player, with options to drive to the basket, pull up for a jumper, drop a pass to the post, or kick out to wing shooters. Because the defense dictates offensive options, players must learn reads and counters for situations such as defenders fighting over, going under, switching, showing and recovering, or trapping on the screen. The offense can flow into continuities including motion, single/double, flex, inside triangle, and side screen. Variations include Post Pop, Horns, 1-4 Low, Post Isolation, and the Two Game. Successful execution requires coordination, defensive recognition, timing, and drills, and teams must also be prepared to defend against this widely used offense.
NVIDIA's combined L1 data cache and shared memory subsystem, introduced in Volta V100, improves performance and simplifies programming. A100's combined capacity is 192 KB/SM versus V100's 128 KB/SM.

Sabres prospect Casey Mittelstadt, whose college season ended, could join Rochester via an AHL or amateur tryout contract, including playoffs. An NHL entry-level deal now would burn a contract year and prevent an Amerks assignment. Buffalo's ideal scenario is a tryout this season with an entry-level contract starting in 2018-19.

A hockey player describes a play against Dallas in which, after the opposing goalie left the bench, he waited for teammates to clear the zone, went wide past Zubov, and got a shot off on a two-on-one, seeking to make up for an earlier turnover; on a later power play he positioned for the pass. He says reaching the finals was a reason he signed with the Devils and that two previous Finnish finals prepared him for the pressure. He feels increasingly comfortable against Dallas, a fast team that cycles well, with taking away their time the hardest part. The team aims to close out the series Thursday rather than let it drag on, has become more disciplined on line changes after too-many-men penalties in the Florida series, matches defensive pairings against top lines, and he is not surprised a veteran teammate has stepped up in the playoffs.

This passage from a Texas Instruments datasheet (TPS7H5001-SP/TPS7H5002-SP/TPS7H5003-SP/TPS7H5004-SP) presents a design example for a synchronous push-pull converter using GaN power semiconductor devices, operating at a 500 kHz switching frequency with a 5 V output. Key component selections include: a 205 kΩ RT resistor for frequency setting; feedback divider resistors of 10 kΩ (RTOP) and 1.4 kΩ (RBOT); a 25 ns dead time set via 20.5 kΩ resistors (RPS/RSP); a 49.9 kΩ leading edge blank time resistor (~50 ns); a 33 nF soft-start capacitor yielding ~7.5 ms soft-start; a transformer with 2.5 turns ratio and 40 μH primary inductance; 170 V rated primary GaN FETs (for 36 V maximum input) and 80 V rated synchronous rectifier FETs, with an optional parallel Schottky diode to reduce reverse conduction losses; a 0.47 μH output inductor with 40% ripple current; and 2.3 mF total output capacitance (seven 330-μF polymer tantalum capacitors), exceeding the calculated 1.3 mF minimum to mitigate radiation-induced single event transients. Additional sections cover an RCD clamp for switch node voltage limiting, a 7.5 Ω current sense resistor enabling cycle-by-cycle limiting at ~35 A with a 1:100 current sense transformer, a 3.3 nF hiccup capacitor, Type 2A frequency compensation (RCOMP 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP 15 nF, CHF 47 pF) targeting a 10 kHz crossover, and a 102 kΩ slope compensation resistor. The document also provides power supply recommendations (4–14 V input range with bypassing requirements), PCB layout guidelines addressing noise reduction, ground separation, trace routing, and CFP package grounding, plus a revision history noting the release of QMLP package options for the devices.

This patent application describes systems and methods for detecting abnormal cardiac activity, such as arrhythmias including atrial fibrillation, using a deep learning architecture. The background notes that current ECG monitoring is cumbersome, invasive, and costly, while PPG-based wearable recordings can be noisy and mask occurrences of atrial fibrillation.

The disclosed method receives periods of cardiac data (e.g., ECG or PPG) and motion data (e.g., accelerometer) from a subject, divides the data into windows, determines signal quality indices for each window, and extracts cardiovascular features. A tensor transform (e.g., wavelet transform) is applied to generate a tensor for each window, and a trained deep learning architecture—comprising a convolutional neural network, a bidirectional recurrent neural network, and an attention network—classifies each window and/or period into classes such as abnormal or normal cardiac activity. Subject contextual information, including medical history and demographics, may also be used.

The attention network weights the windows to determine a classification score, identify windows containing abnormal activity, and determine burden (percentage of time in abnormal cardiac activity). Results are compiled into a report for review, for example by a clinician. The system may include sensor collection devices (such as a wearable smart watch), a cardiac activity processing device, and subject information collection devices, which may be connected via a communication network.

The Society of Automotive Engineers defined five levels of self-driving capability in 2014. Levels 1 and 2, already in production, offer limited automation and require full driver attention. Level 3, expected on BMW's iNext in 2021, lets drivers look away but demands takeover within seconds, so many firms skip it. Level 4 gives drivers minutes to respond and can stop itself; Waymo plans a Phoenix taxi service. Level 5, requiring no driver, likely won't arrive until the end of the next decade.

JPMorgan Chase is deploying artificial intelligence across its global operations to reduce costs, streamline workflows, and improve client services, having rolled out its proprietary generative AI platform to all 200,000 employees. The bank is investing roughly $18 billion in technology this year, with significant portions directed toward AI, machine learning, and cloud infrastructure. AI applications span retail banking, wealth management tools like "Smart Monitor" and "Connect Coach," and institutional functions including credit assessment, fraud detection, and risk management, with over 175 active use cases. Challenges include regulatory compliance, transparency, bias, security, legacy system integration, and adoption costs. Success could establish a global standard for AI adoption in finance, though durability will be tested under market stress and tighter regulation.

This retrospective cohort study used electronic health data from the Carolinas Collaborative to examine the risk of incident hypertension within the first year postpartum among women diagnosed with a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy (HDP) at two academic health systems in the southeastern U.S. (deliveries 2014–2017). Of 9,230 individuals originally identified, 2,514 met inclusion criteria after excluding those with pre-existing hypertension and requiring a blood pressure (BP) measurement 15–90 days postpartum. Cox proportional hazards models estimated associations between postpartum systolic and diastolic BP and time to incident hypertension diagnosis. Thirteen percent (315 participants) were diagnosed with incident hypertension. Higher systolic BP at the postpartum visit (140 vs. 120 mmHg; HR 1.70), severe preeclampsia/eclampsia versus gestational hypertension (HR 1.49), and older maternal age (35 vs. 25 years; HR 1.46) were associated with increased hazard, while a longer interval to the BP check (90 vs. 42 days) was associated with lower hazard (HR 0.52). Approximately 40% of women with HDP had no documented 15–90 day postpartum BP check, and only 32% had BP readings in the normal range. No differences in hazard were found by race, income, or insurance status. Limitations included the retrospective design, potentially missing care delivered outside the two systems, differential characteristics of included versus excluded participants, and reliance on ICD diagnosis codes. The authors conclude that postpartum BP screening guidelines were inconsistently applied and suggest improved identification of eligible patients and preventive strategies.

Research by mobile security company Wandera found iOS 11 drains iPhone batteries more than twice as quickly as iOS 10, lasting 96 minutes versus 240 minutes from full charge. Despite some users reverting to iOS 10.3.3, Wandera advises against this due to security risks. Older devices experience worse drain. Apple's iOS 11.0.1 update improved battery life by 65 percent to 159 minutes. Wandera said bugs in new OS releases are inevitable and will be fixed. Users can save battery by limiting background app refresh and location access, or using low power mode.

Enron Corp.'s shares fell to multi-year lows on October 29, 2001, after Moody's downgraded its senior unsecured debt from Baa1 to Baa2, two notches above junk status, with further downgrades possible. The stock lost more than $14 billion in market value in two weeks following disclosures about partnerships run by former CFO Andrew Fastow and a Securities and Exchange Commission inquiry. Enron said it was negotiating a new $1 billion to $2 billion credit line with banks after drawing down about $3 billion to repay commercial paper; analysts viewed this as a sign of weakness and expected lenders to demand harsher terms, including collateral. European energy firms froze or restricted trading with Enron over credit concerns. At least five shareholder class-action lawsuits were filed against Enron. Moody's also reported that U.S. corporate credit quality overall was expected to worsen.

Connaught Public School in Hintonburg attempted a tunnel ball world record with over 250 students playing simultaneously, exceeding the previous record of 120 set by an Australian school. The event, pending Guinness verification, raised $10,000 for the school's yard renewal project.

This document is a specification update (March 2006) for the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device, Silicon Revision A3, listing errata items 106–116. Item 106: the AuxOutputFull bit is incorrectly cleared to 0 on reads from Port 60h, which can cause incorrect USB PS/2 keyboard/mouse emulation in non-interrupt environments; the resolution is to use interrupts. Item 107: the tACK bits have no effect on setup to IDE_DACK timing, which is fixed at 30 ns; no timing violation occurs and no resolution is required. Item 108: the ATAC can hang when WORD-aligned PRDs are used; all ATAC drivers should use DWORD alignment. Item 109: the LPC controller may abort transactions under random conditions, observed with LPC-to-ISA bridges; a PLD-based workaround is available. Item 111: the SMB controller's NEGACK bit may not set immediately and is sometimes cleared by reads; the workaround is to write twice to SMB_STS. Item 112: the GLPCI retry counter counts all PCI bus retries rather than only its own; the retry limit can be raised or the feature disabled. Item 113: after a suspend, atomic writes to GPIO High Bank Feature Bit Registers clear non-selected bits; Read-Modify-Write transactions must be used instead. Item 114: the SMBus data hold time is too short relative to the specification. Item 115: LOWBAT_FLAG fails to be set after abnormal standby; no resolution. Item 116: Sleep_X is not deasserted when delay counters exceed the PM_SED delay; counters should be programmed to values less than the PM_SED delay. The document concludes with AMD's copyright notice, legal disclaimers, and trademark information.

Several billionaire CEOs reject the concept of work-life balance. Jeff Bezos prefers "work-life harmony," arguing that happiness at home and success at work reinforce each other rather than requiring a tradeoff. Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman calls it "mind-boggling" to think greatness can come from 38-hour weeks, saying building something extraordinary takes "every waking minute." Scale AI cofounder Lucy Guo, a self-made billionaire at 30, works 90-hour weeks and suggests those craving balance may be in the wrong job, though she still makes time for friends and family. Zoom CEO Eric Yuan says "work is life, life is work," but prioritizes family when conflicts arise. LinkedIn cofounder Reid Hoffman claims founders seeking balance are "not committed to winning," and Alibaba's Jack Ma called China's demanding "996" schedule a "huge blessing."

A recent ValueInsured survey found 71 percent of Washington homeowners worry the housing market is a bubble, though the online poll included only 1,079 people nationwide—about 21 per state. King County median home prices rose 18.6 percent year over year, jumping more than $100,000 to $658,000 between July 2016 and July 2017, while inventory fell more than 13 percent. Experts say a 2008-style collapse is unlikely: Windermere Real Estate president OB Jacobi noted King County buyers have high credit scores, above-average down payments, and substantial equity. NWMLS director George Moorhead said a market correction is likely, in the form of prices and inventory leveling out, though he expressed concern about practices easing purchases for buyers with low credit scores or existing debt. The article also ranks the income needed to buy a home in 25 cities, from Detroit ($7,359) to San Francisco ($226,577), with Seattle fifth at $106,709.

American consumer confidence rose in April to 128.7, up from 127.0 in March, near the 18-year high of 130.0 reached in February. Analysts attributed the strength to a strong labor market, tax cuts, reduced stock market volatility, and fewer trade war concerns, though some said confidence may overstate potential spending growth.

NEC Corp has established the NEC Satellite Operation Center, fully operational in April, to operate the ASNARO-2 radar satellite launched in January. Using NEC's GroundNEXTAR system and a high-security data center, the center can operate multiple satellites, and NEC plans to market ASNARO-2 images with JEOSS starting September.

This guide describes Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) operations. For precise halting of the ring buffer, software must place the halt command last in the queue; for precise error halting, only one command should be queued at a time. Interrupt status bits can be cleared via PM_RBCtl[CLEAR_INTS] when the ring buffer has no entries to process or is paused.

In systems enabling SMEE or SME-MK, encryption information is encoded into SPAs; software sets the C-bit to 1 to indicate encrypted memory. SPAs must be well-formed and located in appropriate address ranges.

Key commands include: PM_GET_CAPABILITIES, which queries firmware capabilities and versions; PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, which moves pages in non-SNP systems or Hypervisor-owned pages in SNP systems, can move pages actively used by DMA devices by updating IOMMU host PTEs, requires the CPU be prevented from accessing migrating pages, and does not support direct 2M page migration (2M pages must be smashed into 4K pages); and PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST, which moves SNP guest pages, requires RMP_ENFORCE=1, with source pages in Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid state and destination pages in Pre-Migration state. DMA to migrating pages is not supported for guest migration.

Errors in command format or content result in rejection or partial success, reported via command status and migration list entries. Ring buffer errors are reported in PM_STATUS. Hardware errors are reported via command status and/or the Machine Check Architecture; if TMPM times out, the client should log an MCA and take appropriate action. A command can process up to 128 pages, and hardware errors may render the entire batch unrecoverable.

The TPS7H500x-SP series (TPS7H5001-SP through TPS7H5004-SP) are radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak current mode PWM controllers from Texas Instruments for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge, with switching frequencies up to 2 MHz for GaN-based designs. The devices use a transconductance error amplifier, allowing Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation, where Type 2A adds a capacitor (CHF) for high-frequency noise attenuation. Thermal shutdown stops switching at 175°C (typical) and restarts below 160°C. A design example demonstrates a 500-kHz synchronous push-pull converter with GaN devices producing a 5-V output, covering component selection: feedback divider resistors (10 kΩ/1.4 kΩ), 25-ns dead time, 49.9-kΩ leading edge blanking resistor, 33-nF soft-start capacitor (~7.5 ms), transformer turns ratio of 2.5 with 40-µH primary inductance, 170-V primary and 80-V synchronous rectifier GaN FETs, 0.47-µH output inductor, 2.3 mF output capacitance including single-event transient mitigation, 7.5-Ω current sense resistor, 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor, Type 2A compensation components (RCOMP = 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP = 15 nF, CHF = 47 pF at a 10-kHz crossover), and a 102-kΩ slope compensation resistor. The controllers operate from a 4-V to 14-V supply with required bypassing. Layout guidelines address noise reduction, ground separation, and component placement. The document also includes revision history, mechanical/packaging data, and TI legal disclaimers.

Astronomers have discovered the most distant and most powerful "odd radio circle" (ORC) known, designated RAD J131346.9+500320, located at redshift ~0.94 and featuring two intersecting rings. The discovery, made using the LOFAR telescope and the RAD@home Astronomy Collaboratory citizen science platform, challenges theories that ORCs result from black hole mergers, instead suggesting galactic superwinds may be responsible. Researchers also identified two radio galaxies with similar rings—RAD J122622.6+640622 and RAD J142004.0+621715—both located in galaxy clusters of about 100 trillion solar masses, indicating that interactions between relativistic jets and hot plasma may shape these structures. Future facilities such as the SKA, DESI, and LSST are expected to uncover more ORCs and clarify their origins.

SN NEXT No. 1 McEachern Indians (5-0) visited the Harrison Hoyas (5-0) Friday night in Kennesaw, Georgia, kicking off at 8 p.m. EST. Both teams came off bye weeks. McEachern seeks a statement win for Top 25 consideration, while Harrison, flying under the radar in 2025, aims to raise its Georgia profile with an upset.

Peter Marks, the former top FDA vaccine regulator who was ousted by RFK Jr., has joined Eli Lilly to lead molecule discovery and infectious diseases at Lilly Research Laboratories. His first day was Monday. The move drew criticism over the revolving door between the agency and industry. Marks said he is excited about advancing infectious disease products for public health.

The State of Louisiana sued the Banking Department of the Citizens' Bank to recover a license tax for carrying on a banking business, contending the department was a corporation organized under Act No. 246 of 1853 and a compact of July 26, 1853. The president of the Citizens' Bank, upon whom the petition and citation were served, excepted on the grounds that he had no authority to stand in judgment for the department and that no such corporation existed. The district court maintained the exception and rejected the suit, and the state appealed. The Supreme Court held that corporations must have express authority to sue and be sued, and that neither the 1853 act nor the compact conferred such authority on a separate banking department. Because the suit was brought against the "Banking Department" rather than the Citizens' Bank of Louisiana itself, the question of whether such a corporation exists must be decided contradictorily with the Citizens' Bank, which was not a party. The court limited its ruling to the issue of want of citation, leaving other questions open, reversed the lower court's judgment, and dismissed the suit as in case of nonsuit. Monroe, J., dissented.

A February 25, 2002 email from Kimberly Nelson (ETS) compiles Enron and energy industry news. Enron's pipelines and power plants remain its main source of steady income during bankruptcy and are expected to form the core of a reorganized company under interim CEO Stephen Cooper; UBS Warburg launched a trading operation staffed largely by about 625 former Enron employees in exchange for 33 percent of profits, while Enron sold its wind power subsidiary to GE and its Indian oil and gas assets to BG Group for $350 million. Dynegy previously acquired Enron's 16,500-mile Northern Natural Gas pipeline. FERC admitted 25 contacts between its commissioners and staff and Enron officials between August 2000 and June 2001; Chairman Pat Wood denied any undue Enron influence despite criticism from Senator Boxer. Dutch company Nuon may replace Azurix on a Buenos Aires province waterworks concession, for which Azurix seeks $150–200 million in compensation. BG Group plans to more than double its India investment to $1.3 billion, though its operatorship dispute with state-owned Oil & Natural Gas Corp. remains unresolved. Enron Japan's creditors may receive little repayment, as assets may barely cover liquidation costs. Enron-related overseas power projects received $1.2 billion in loans from OPIC and the Export-Import Bank, with the Dabhol plant in India idle. The Senate prepares to debate energy legislation, with disputes over Arctic refuge drilling, vehicle fuel economy, ethanol mandates, tax breaks, and electricity regulation. California Governor Davis is considering delaying the MTBE ban until 2005, citing potential gasoline shortages and insufficient ethanol infrastructure.

This paper addresses budget pacing in online digital advertising with real-time auctions, where pacing systems adjust spending velocity to align with campaign goals. The authors propose a Bucketized Hysteresis Controller (BHC) combining hysteresis control with proportional feedback as a principled alternative to empirically tuned pacing. Their contributions are: implementing a bucketized hysteresis controller compared with a legacy variable-step pacing system, providing an analytical framework for parameter selection, and validating the approach through real-world auction experiments. Related work spans optimization-based budget allocation and feedback control methods, though prior proportional or integral approaches can suffer from oscillations or require delicate tuning. The system setup describes auctions where final bids equal max bid multiplied by conversion probability, with pacing applied via a discount multiplier λ that rescales bids to influence win rates. The baseline production controller uses multiplicative λ updates with a step size adapted by a fluctuation factor measuring oscillation in recent updates. The proposed BHC discretizes the error between desired and observed rates into K non-overlapping bands with associated gains, applying large predefined steps for large errors and smaller steps for minor errors—inspired by bang-bang control and gain scheduling—to achieve rapid convergence and stability.

In Windows 10, users can change the mouse pointer's size and color through Settings > Ease of Access > Mouse (or by searching "Mouse Pointer"), choosing small, medium, or large sizes and white, black, or inverting colors. Pointer shapes can be changed via Control Panel's Mouse applet under the Pointers tab. In Safari on iOS, closing all open tabs at once is done by pressing and holding the Tabs link at the bottom right, then selecting "Close xx Tabs," or by pressing and holding the Done link if already in the tabs view. Restarting Safari does not close tabs, as the app remembers previously open tabs.

NASA's Dawn spacecraft has released the closest-ever images of the dwarf planet Ceres, showing "dramatic new views" of the 50-mile-wide Occator Crater and its bright sodium carbonate deposits, known as faculae. After moving into a new orbit in early June, Dawn came within 22 miles of Ceres' surface. One photo, taken June 14, shows the Vinalia Faculae; another, taken June 22 from about 21 miles up, shows Cerealia Facula and an adjacent mound. The origin of the faculae remains unclear, though the extended mission may provide answers through gravity measurements and composition analysis. Running low on fuel, Dawn—launched in 2007 and orbiting Ceres since March 2015—is expected to operate until the second half of 2018, after which it will remain in orbit to avoid contaminating Ceres.

The ISDA Press Report for May 16, 2001, compiles news items on derivatives markets:

- Witnesses at an IRS hearing, including Andrea Kramer, Earl Goldhammer, Mark Perwien, Mark Canter, and Linda Carlisle, were expected to argue that proposed hedging regulations fail to fully implement Congress's broader risk management standard, urging coverage for commodities dealers, weather and energy derivatives, life insurers' gap hedges, and services income.

- BIS data showed OTC derivatives growth slowed in the second half of 2000, with notional outstanding contracts rising just 1% to $95.2 trillion, while gross market values rose 24% to $3.2 trillion. A 7% drop in euro-denominated interest rate contracts was a major factor.

- The Federal Home Loan Bank of New York achieved FAS 133 compliance using Principia Partners' Analytic System.

- Former CFTC chairman Philip McBride-Johnson said dual CFTC/SEC regulation, higher margin costs, and a three-year ban on options on single-stock futures may limit their adoption.

- CBOE and CME signed a letter of intent to create a joint venture for single-stock futures, with the CBOT taking a limited stake; products will trade electronically.

- FASB's derivatives implementation group proposed recording option fair value changes in other comprehensive income, offering partial relief from FAS 133's time-value reporting requirement without amending the standard.

- FSA's Oliver Page defended the Basel "w charge" (a 15% capital floor on credit derivatives) despite suggestions from NY Fed president William McDonough that it might be reduced or removed.

- The UK Treasury proposed legislation allowing building societies to use credit derivatives for risk management, but not speculation.

- Heavy credit-linked note issuance (€5–15bn equivalent) drove default swap selling, widening the negative basis between default swaps and bond asset swap values and creating arbitrage opportunities for dealers.

- Lightrade is expanding its neutral bandwidth pooling points network from New York to Los Angeles, with additional US cities planned and European opportunities under investigation.

- ISDA finalized and published the restructuring supplement to its 1999 Credit Derivatives Definitions, limiting deliverable securities to maturities of less than 30 months following a restructuring date, responding to issues raised by the Conseco restructuring.

Canadian Pacific Railway says changes in Vancouver and North Dakota will move imported goods from Vancouver to Detroit up to 48 hours faster than CN Rail, cutting costs for shippers. Hapag-Lloyd welcomed the improved service, which CP says could put competitive pressure on CN.

The Horns Offense uses high post mid screen action; if the on-ball defender gets caught on the screen, an easy layup results. Defenders should influence the ballhandler toward the weakest screener. Two strategies counter it: the Basic NBA Show & Recover and All Out SOS Disruption. NBA teams avoid switching because a Big screening a Little allows the screener to post up against a smaller defender. In Show & Recover, X5 shows on the screen while X1 pushes the ballhandler to the sideline, then recovers to final matchups with pass denial. In SOS Disruption, the defense traps the point guard before any screen or pass, forcing freelance play; rotations follow the near player concept, ending in SOS helpside positions.

The new coarse-fishing season on Britain's rivers has begun, and Roger Poole of Petworth and Bognor Angling Club advises anglers to re-appraise baits and tactics, as rivers differ from March to June. The close season lets fish spawn and recover, so varied baits are worth trying, with natural foods abundant in bankside vegetation. The club seeks young members and supports National Fishing Month (July 27–September 2), led by Jeremy Wade and Nick Hancock, backing over 250 UK events; under-16s get free licences. Children's events at Walberton proved popular, and adult anglers are urged to arrange more to secure angling's future. Early-season tips: tench feed in ponds at dawn; chub dominate rivers, while float trotting catches dace, roach and perch on the Rother, and feeder or ledger methods find bream, chub and possibly barbel on the Arun.

Euro zone stocks climbed to their highest in over a year on Monday, the first trading day of 2017, after data showed manufacturing activity grew at its fastest pace in over five years. The Euro STOXX 50 rose 0.5 percent after the factory PMI came in at 54.9. Italy's FTSE MIB gained 1.3 percent, Germany's DAX 0.9 percent, and France's CAC 0.3 percent. The euro slipped below $1.05 while the dollar index rose 0.4 percent on expectations of U.S. rate hikes and fiscal expansion. Yields on lower-rated euro zone bonds fell. The Istanbul attack that killed 39 people had little market impact, though the Turkish lira slipped. China's manufacturing expanded for a fifth month, the yuan had its biggest annual loss in over 20 years, and bitcoin rose above $1,000.

Guyana's Office of Climate Change opened a three-day Greenhouse Gas Inventory workshop at Herdmanston Lodge, Queenstown, in preparation for the Third National Communication (TNC), which will fulfill the country's UNFCCC reporting requirements. The workshop targets the TNC's Greenhouse Gas Inventory component, with the other three components to be addressed later. OCC head Janelle Christian said the goal is to build a cadre of trained national experts to prepare inventories and improve climate-based reporting. National Project Coordinator Marlon Velloza said the findings could catalyze Guyana's 'green' agenda and urged public involvement. Professor Anit Garg and Dr. Indu Murthy, both residing in India, are conducting sessions via Skype, with certification planned at the end. The TNC is due for submission in 2019.

Napheesa Collier suffered a Grade 2 tear of three ankle ligaments and a shin muscle in a Friday collision, a source told ESPN. The injury requires a minimum six-week recovery, meaning she could not have returned this season had the top-seeded Lynx advanced past the Mercury. The Mercury eliminated the short-handed Lynx in Game 4 on Sunday. Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve was ejected from Game 3 and suspended one game for her reaction to the play.

Nashville police arrested Travis Reinking, 29, suspected of killing four people with an assault rifle at a Waffle House, without firing a shot after a 24-hour manhunt. James Shaw Jr., a Black man, had tackled Reinking and wrestled away the weapon. A citizen spotted Reinking near a wooded area; an officer ordered him to the ground, and he complied. Police found a semi-automatic handgun and ammunition in his backpack. The article argues Reinking benefited from White privilege, contrasting his arrest with police killings of unarmed Black suspects. That day, Chikesia Clemons, an unarmed Black woman, was violently arrested by White officers at an Alabama Waffle House over plastic utensils.

NEC Display will extend warranties on four P-series professional digital signage displays from three to five years, covering the P404, P484, and P554 from first shipment and the P703 for purchases on or after August 1, 2017.

Maxwell Chan of SkyBlue Cross promotes a newly developed "Functional Food Therapeutic Lifestyle Change Intervention Program" for high cholesterol. The passage claims conventional medicine only lowers cholesterol levels without addressing underlying causes, leaving patients on lifelong statins. It states hyperlipidemia is a metabolic status involving liver, kidney, and spleen functions rather than a sickness, with each patient having distinct underlying causes. A book, "Naturally Balanced your Cholesterol Level," reportedly identifies 14 types of high cholesterol and treatment solutions claimed to make the condition curable without lifelong medication. The program involves practitioners observing patients' lifestyles and considering interactions among lifestyle, chronic diseases, environment, and genetics.

The author, who moved to Tarrytown in 1950 and watched the original Tappan Zee Bridge being built, describes the opening of the first span of the new Governor Mario M. Cuomo Bridge. After attending a presentation by Project Director Jamey Barbas, a structural engineer who was one of only three female engineering majors in college, the author highlights the project's scale: a 3.1-mile roadway, a 2,230-foot main span built to last 100 years without major maintenance, and eight chamfered towers supporting cables that carry over 74 million pounds. The "I Lift NY" super crane hoisted 1,900-ton steel assemblies, while floating concrete batch plants kept 20,000 trucks off roads. Modular components were made by American companies, environmental impacts were studied, and the design required over one million hours of thinking and nearly 9 million work hours from 7,000 people.

University of Alabama student Kelsey Hall promised on Twitter to wear a Christmas tree costume to all her classes for the semester if her post received 1,000 retweets. She received 30,000 and kept the promise, but says the attention has been stressful and she may reconsider future social media challenges.

The Internal Bar Strength (IBS) indicator, calculated as (Close-Low)/(High-Low), oscillates between zero and one and measures the closing price's position relative to the day's high and low. Low values are considered bullish and high values bearish in the short term, making it a mean-reversion approach of buying weakness and selling strength. IBS has worked remarkably well on stocks and stock indices for roughly 30 years, though less so on other asset classes. After weak performance in 2017-2018, it rebounded in 2019-2020, with 2020 its best year on record amid Covid-19 volatility. A simple IBS strategy on SPY produced losses in only three years (1994, 2002, 2018), while on QQQ, 742 trades returned 0.56% per trade and compounded at 16.6% versus 9% for buy and hold. A variation produced a 15.3% CAGR while invested only 36% of the time, with a 74% win rate and 1.7 Sharpe ratio. The strategy performs best in bear markets, when the biggest up days occur, possibly due to short covering. Adding a VIX filter or requiring the close to be no more than 5% above the 200-day moving average improves results, though curve-fitting risk is high. Combining IBS with a second indicator further improves results, especially on QQQ. IBS works only on stocks and broad-based indices, failing on commodity, gold, and metal stocks and on Norwegian and Australian markets. A key weakness is execution: entries must occur at the close, and delaying to the next open significantly reduces returns.

Alpha Theory's Analytics Department identifies investor biases through deviations between actual and optimal position sizes. Common biases include: failing to cut exposure after large positive price moves despite diminished probability-weighted returns; slowly building positions in high-conviction names, which reduces returns; lacking discipline, as positions without explicit price targets underperform; and over-diversifying, since concentrated portfolios outperformed diversified ones by 2.2% on an alpha basis (2011-2016 study). In 2016, optimal position sizing would have improved returns by 5.1%. These biases show why unemotional, disciplined sizing outperforms.

In this MIT guest lecture, a professor discusses experimentation and robust design of engineering systems. He traces the history from Russell's advocacy of simple, one-question-at-a-time experiments to Fisher's factorial designs at Rothamsted, which demonstrated a twofold efficiency gain, and Fisher's later fractional factorial designs, which reduce experiment size at the cost of confounding risks. He describes Taguchi's crossed arrays for robust parameter design and their entrenchment in industry practice, including Six Sigma programs. Motivated by an agricultural equipment manufacturer whose robust design program failed—most experiments were left unfinished—the professor's research evaluated adaptive one-factor-at-a-time (OFAT) experiments. An empirical study of 66 systems and supporting theory showed adaptive OFAT outperforms fractional factorial designs when experimental error is large relative to effects or interactions are strong, achieving roughly 80% of the maximum possible improvement with far fewer runs. Crossing adaptive experiments with noise-factor factorial designs improved robustness, validated through sheet metal spinning and paper airplane studies; informed starting points further improved results. An ensemble of four OFATs outperformed larger fractional factorials and became more robust as error increased. He notes practical limits, such as parallel-only experiments and time trends, and concludes that companies should "streamline"—running many inexpensive robust design experiments rather than a few costly ones—given uncertainty about where quality problems lie. The lecture ends with a question-and-answer session on problem sets.

Showstoppers Theatre presents Foiled Again!, comedic melodramas directed by Radu Azdril. The summer program gives children a musical theater overview; no experience required. Performances run 7 p.m. Friday, 10:30 a.m. Saturday, 7 p.m. June 28 and 10:30 a.m. June 29 at La Colina Junior High School, Santa Barbara. Tickets are $7; children 12 or younger free.

NVIDIA Corporation filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended April 26, 2015 (Q1 fiscal 2016). Revenue was $1,151 million, up 4% from $1,103 million a year earlier, comprising GPU segment revenue of $940 million (up 5%), Tegra Processor revenue of $145 million (up 4%), and $66 million in the "All Other" category, primarily patent licensing. Net income was $134 million versus $137 million in the prior-year quarter, with basic and diluted EPS of $0.24 in both periods. Gross margin improved to 56.7% from 54.8%, and operating income rose to $176 million from $151 million. The effective tax rate was 22.0% versus 16.4%. Operating cash flow was $246 million versus $151 million, and cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $4.79 billion at quarter end.

During the quarter, NVIDIA repurchased 2.4 million shares for $53 million and paid $46 million in dividends ($0.085 per share). In May 2015, the Board extended the repurchase program through December 2018 with an additional $1.62 billion authorization, the quarterly dividend was increased 15% to $0.0975 per share, and a $400 million accelerated share repurchase agreement was executed. NVIDIA announced its intent to wind down the Icera modem operations, with estimated restructuring charges of $100 million to $125 million if a sale is not completed. Ongoing legal matters include securities class actions and patent disputes with Qualcomm and Samsung. Management concluded that disclosure controls and procedures were effective.

Zach Parise says the team's focus is to win the current game and try to move the series back to New Jersey. He says the team needs more shots and chances against goalie Jonathan Quick, who is playing confidently, and credits the Kings' defensemen for their gap control and allowing Quick to see shots. He acknowledges a lineup change involving Syggie and Hank. Parise says the team has worked hard but can improve puck movement and challenge Quick more, and relays that comebacks are possible since all three losses were winnable.

Last week's market events—earnings, economic data, Fed policy, and political developments—were clouded by controversy, contradiction, or doubt, ending with a confirmed bearish engulfing pattern at all-time highs and a decisive risk-off shift, with markets down between 2.2% and 4.2%.

Earnings remained strong: 82% of S&P 500 companies beat EPS estimates (above the 5-year average of 78%) and 79% beat revenue estimates, while Bank of America reported earnings revision ratios at a 43-month high globally and 24-month high in the U.S. GDP grew 3% versus 2.5% expected, though tariff-related distortions clouded the data, and personal spending showed softness. Nonfarm payrolls added only 73,000 jobs versus 100,000 expected, with the largest two-month downward revision on record outside the pandemic; unemployment rose 0.1% to 4.2%.

The 2-1-2 zone is a compact variation of the 2-3 zone defense that protects the middle rather than the baseline and corners. It typically places an athletic defender in the middle with taller players on the blocks for strong rebounding. Due to its compact design, it is vulnerable to outside shooting and is mainly used against poor outside shooting teams or to match high post offenses such as the 1-3-1. The passage details defensive shifts for ball positions in the middle, on the wings, and in the corners. Outside defenders (X1, X2) are normally the team's quickest players, baseline defenders (X3, X4) should be skilled rebounders, and the post defender (X5) guards the low post.

Options trading in Amazon (AMZN) is a popular strategy that allows investors to speculate on or hedge against the stock's price movements. Available strategies include buying calls and puts, writing covered and naked calls and puts, and spread trading, each with different risk-reward profiles. Options trading carries significant risks: it is a leveraged investment, most options expire worthless, contracts have expiration dates, liquidity may be limited, and margin calls can occur. Option prices move in relation to the underlying stock—call prices rise and put prices fall when the stock rises, with delta measuring sensitivity to price changes. Advantages include leverage, the ability to limit risk through spreads, and profiting without owning the stock. Requirements include a margin account, sufficient capital (typically a $2,000 minimum deposit), and an understanding of options trading and its risks. Investors can place market, limit, or stop orders, and the strike price determines potential payoff. Tax treatment depends on the trade type and holding period. Higher volatility increases option premiums. Fees, margin requirements, and order execution speed vary by broker. When selecting a platform, investors should consider fees, execution speed, and research and analysis tools.

The paper presents a complete ground-state phase diagram for classical Heisenberg spins with bilinear-biquadratic exchange interactions on a partially anisotropic triangular lattice composed of isosceles triangles, using four interaction parameters (bilinear K, L and biquadratic A, B) instead of the six required for the fully anisotropic case. While previous studies of the isotropic triangular lattice identified ferromagnetic, nematic-like, 120°, and noncoplanar phases, the problem here is reduced to minimizing the energy of a single triangular plaquette, enabling construction of global ground states for many lattices built from identical isosceles triangles, including three-dimensional ones. The angles between the three spins define a tetrahedral parameter space whose vertices, edges, and faces correspond to collinear and coplanar configurations, while interior points yield noncoplanar states. Analytical minimization conditions are derived, and ground-state configurations and energies are tabulated, including ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, collinear-fan, spiral, and noncoplanar phases. Phase diagrams for Heisenberg and XY models are presented for several values of the biquadratic parameter A, showing continuous and discontinuous transition lines.

The guard is an under-appreciated but essential offensive line position, requiring a combination of strength and athleticism. Guards block both defensive tackles and blitzing linebackers in pass protection, and must communicate against stunts, twists, and blitzes. In the run game, they establish double teams, pull to block second and third level defenders, and create running lanes. The origin of the name "guard" is unclear. Guards line up between the tackles and center, and need functional strength, footwork, agility, and blocking technique, with a typical sturdy build of 6'3"–6'5" and 300–320 pounds. Notable guards include Larry Allen and John Hannah.

The passage outlines three phases of early offense in basketball. Phase 1 (Early Push) involves attacking before the defense can organize, creating outnumbered situations and mismatches; getting the ball into the offensive area within 2–4 seconds forces defenders to react. Coaches are warned not to assume players can attack outnumbered situations without instruction, since failing to capitalize cancels the defensive effort that created the opportunity. Specific situations and goals are detailed: breakaways (layup and steal), 2-on-1 (layup), 3-on-1 (create a 2-on-1), 3-on-2 (open jumper and putback), and 3-on-3 (create a 3-on-2). Techniques include passing ahead, minimizing dribbles, staying inbounds on layups, avoiding charges, rebounding, and various screening actions. Phase 2 (Early Flow) directs teams to move directly into set offenses without backing the ball out, preventing the defense from setting up; flow actions can also function as half-court offense. Phase 3 (Continuity) involves flowing into continuous patterns that maintain pressure, prevent rushed shots, and preserve court balance and rebounding position. Described continuity systems include the Flex (pick-the-picker screening), the Passing Game (for smaller, quicker teams with open middle penetration), the Mid Screen (on-ball screen with wing shooters), the Side Screen (post sets on-ball screen for wing with multiple reads), and the Inside Triangle (an inside screening game suited to physically strong players).
