This study examines architectural design education to derive implications for STEM education through analogical inference. The theoretical framework covers STEM education (which fosters 21st-century skills and evolved into STEAM with the addition of art), project-based learning (a constructivist, learner-centered approach based on Dewey, Kilpatrick, and Bruner), design as a cyclical, feedback-driven problem-solving process, architectural design studio education (originating with the 1671 French Academy of Architecture and developed by the Bauhaus, centered on instructor criticism and learning by doing), and technical drawing and visual communication. The literature review presents studies on hands-on learning, robotics-based teacher professional development, engineering and art education models, and studio-based STEM environments.

Using an ethnographic method, the first author observed a first-year Architectural Design course at BUU Faculty of Architecture (30 students) for four weeks in December 2022, taking unstructured observation notes that were verified through interviews with eight volunteer students and content analysis. Four themes emerged: facing open-ended problems, deepening understanding of the problem situation, gaining experience in presentation techniques, and meeting the culture of criticism. Interviews indicated students perceived the course's purpose as developing abstract and conceptual thinking, and reported difficulties such as model making, time constraints, and the invention process.

Through analogical inference, six conclusions for STEM education were drawn: (1) students at all grade levels should solve open-ended problems independently, learning from mistakes; (2) STEM project courses should be graduation requirements at K16/K12 levels, while K4/K8 should focus on problem situations; (3) problems must be authentic, with real-life context, sustainability, and economic value; (4) younger students should experience materials and tools firsthand; (5) technical drawing and graphics courses should be added to high school programs, including non-technical schools; (6) faculty should shift from technical rationality to reflection in action, with jury-based assessment implemented at the undergraduate level.

The lecture examines the soundness of the Fiat-Shamir transformation in the random oracle model (ROM). The instructor first demonstrates a cheating attack: a prover can guess the hash's output bit, commit accordingly, and retry repeatedly, since the oracle can be queried many times—unlike an interactive verifier who allows only one attempt. This attack succeeds even when soundness is made negligible through sequential repetition, because the cheater retains successful partial transcripts and extends them.

A theorem is then presented: Fiat-Shamir is sound in the ROM for public-coin protocols with negligible soundness and a constant number of rounds. The proof shows that a cheating prover P* succeeding with probability epsilon using q oracle queries yields a cheater P** for the interactive protocol with probability at least epsilon/q (minus a negligible term), since the successful alpha must be among the queried ones. For c verifier messages, the probability decays to roughly epsilon/q^c. Protocols with round-by-round soundness, such as GKR, remain sound despite many rounds; Kilian-Micali (four rounds, negligible error) is sound under Fiat-Shamir in the ROM.

However, ROM security does not guarantee security with any concrete hash function—contrived hash functions exist that break the protocol—so the ROM serves only as a sanity check, though in practice protocols verified this way have not broken.

Finally, the instructor explains that parallel repetition of the specific Hamiltonian-cycle zero-knowledge protocol is not zero knowledge (proved in 2019 at MIT), because its Fiat-Shamir soundness implies no simulator can exist: a Fiat-Shamir-based cheating verifier would otherwise be simulatable for both in-language and out-of-language inputs, contradicting soundness.

This white paper examines artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education, addressing how institutions are responding to AI, its effects on pedagogy, research, and administration, and its opportunities for improving learning outcomes, bridging educational gaps, and preparing students for an AI-driven workforce.

AI adoption is accelerating globally, with North America, Europe, and East Asia leading implementation, and China and the United States cited as the most progressive countries. A survey cited in the paper reports that 86% of students worldwide use AI tools for academic purposes, with nearly 25% using them daily. Applications include intelligent tutoring systems (e.g., Carnegie Learning's Cognitive Tutor), predictive analytics for identifying at-risk students (e.g., University of Michigan; Arizona State University reported a 20% retention improvement), and adaptive learning platforms (e.g., DreamBox, Smart Sparrow, and China's Squirrel AI).

Institutions are responding through faculty training, interdisciplinary curricular innovation, and policy initiatives such as the UNESCO Beijing Consensus and Australia's TEQSA frameworks. However, only 20% of surveyed universities meet student expectations for AI integration.

Documented impacts include personalized learning, accelerated research through generative AI, and administrative efficiency via chatbots and predictive analytics; statistical evidence notes a 60% growth in AI applications in higher education from 2020 to 2024 and a 15% retention increase at institutions implementing predictive analytics.

The paper compares three tools: ChatGPT for text creation and writing support, Bard for real-time data access in research-heavy fields, and Gemini for emotionally intelligent learning environments. AI applications span disciplines from performing arts and sciences to business and liberal arts, and support peer-to-peer collaboration, accessibility for students with disabilities, lifelong learning, and career counseling.

Key challenges include academic dishonesty facilitated by AI-generated content, faculty fears of automation, algorithmic bias, data privacy concerns, psychological dependency risks, and a digital divide limiting adoption in under-resourced regions.

The paper recommends robust policy frameworks, faculty training, ethical governance involving diverse stakeholders, targeted investments for equitable access, and a collaborative model in which AI complements rather than replaces educators. Future trends identified include emotional recognition systems, VR/AR applications, and AI-enabled language translation.

The Supreme Court of North Dakota reversed a district court order suppressing evidence against Denise Hahne, who was cited for driving under the influence after failing to stop at a temporary sobriety checkpoint operated by the Highway Patrol in Bismarck on August 18, 2006. A field test showed a reading of .092, and a later blood draw showed a blood-alcohol content of 0.13 percent. The district court suppressed the evidence after finding Hahne had no safe or legal way to avoid the checkpoint, as the only outlet was a potentially dangerous U-turn on a curving road with a 50 m.p.h. speed limit. The Supreme Court held the district court relied on an erroneous view of the law—that law enforcement must provide motorists an opportunity to avoid checkpoints. Following Michigan Dep't of State Police v. Sitz, the court held that checkpoints need not, as a matter of law, provide motorists a way to avoid them; avoidability is one factor that may be considered in evaluating the intrusion on personal liberty. The court declined to address Hahne's argument, raised for the first time on appeal, that the State failed to demonstrate the checkpoint's effectiveness. The case was remanded to determine whether the checkpoint was constitutionally reasonable.

The 13/48 trading strategy is a technical analysis method using the crossover of the 13-period and 48-period exponential moving averages (EMAs). When the 13-period EMA crosses above the 48-period EMA, it signals a bullish opportunity to buy; when it crosses below, it signals a bearish opportunity to sell. The momentum-based strategy works best in trending markets but is risky in sideways or choppy conditions. Backtesting showed it works best on stocks, yielding 5.1% annually versus 7.2% for buy and hold, with a slightly better risk-adjusted return of 7.8%. The strategy is a lagging indicator prone to whipsaws and is not an easy path to riches.

The United States Court of Federal Claims denied Alan A. Brister's tax refund suit. In 1993, the IRS disallowed withholding credits of $10,435.50 (1985) and $5,231.42 (1986) that Brister had claimed based on W-2 forms he prepared for his former employer, Solar Roofing, Inc., and applied his 1989–1992 refunds against the resulting liabilities. The Government conceded the adjustments were untimely under the three-year limitations period of 26 U.S.C. § 6501(a) but invoked § 6501(c)(1), which removes the time limit for false or fraudulent returns filed with intent to evade tax. Brister, Solar Roofing's former accountant, had claimed withholdings that were never paid to the IRS, intending to use the IRS to collect debts owed to him by the company. The court found by clear and convincing evidence that both returns were knowingly false and filed with intent to evade tax, holding that the scheme's effect on refund credits fell within the statute even though Brister would have received a refund from legitimate withholdings alone. Judgment was entered for the defendant.

This qualitative case study examined the impacts of distance education on equality and inequality of opportunity in education through semi-structured interviews with 21 faculty members and 26 students (47 participants), analyzed via content analysis. Faculty members identified learning at personal pace and easy access to information as positive impacts, while citing technology access problems, internet connection issues, disregarded learner competencies, unsuitable learning environments, and increased differences among students as negative impacts. Students viewed freedom from time limitations, free-of-charge education, and access to various sources as contributions to equality, whereas financial capabilities and internet problems were seen as causes of inequality. Suggested solutions included determining learner characteristics, ensuring access to technology, improving digital literacy skills, resolving internet infrastructure problems, official state budgeting for technology access, and teacher consultancy services. The study concludes that distance education both supports and hinders equality of opportunity, with technological access and socio-economic factors playing decisive roles, and its findings align with existing literature on digital gaps and distance education.

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture covers entangled photons and entanglement as a quantum resource. Entanglement is defined as a state that cannot be factorized into a product of two wave functions. The professor clarifies that entanglement as a resource requires two physically distinct, separable subsystems that can be individually addressed and measured—distinguishing entangled states from entangled modes (such as a single photon after a beam splitter) and from inseparable systems (like the electron singlet in helium, where the electrons cannot be separated). Photons are well suited for entanglement because they naturally fly apart, and polarization-entangled photon pairs are presented as examples. The four Bell states are introduced as maximally entangled two-qubit states. Entangled states exhibit non-local correlations and are fragile against decoherence, motivating research into robust implementations.

The lecture then addresses quantifying entanglement and entanglement purification. Starting with many identical copies of a weakly entangled state (a|00⟩+b|11⟩), Alice and Bob each perform a CNOT operation on two photons and measure their target qubits; with probability 2a²b², the remaining photons are projected into a Bell state, while weaker initial entanglement requires more attempts. Supplying many copies does not violate the no-cloning theorem, since states can be repeatedly produced by repeating the preparation procedure. Entanglement is measured as the von Neumann entropy of the reduced density matrix obtained by partial trace; Bell states yield an entropy of 1, and the optimal purification success probability equals this entanglement measure, illustrating entanglement as a resource.

Finally, the lecture discusses entangling atoms, which is harder than entangling photons. A decades-old proposal to entangle atoms via photo-dissociation of mercury molecules remains unrealized due to experimental requirements. An alternative probabilistic "poor man's entangler" uses measurements on photons scattered by two atoms: if the measurement outcome is positive, the atoms are known to be entangled. This scheme relies on Hong-Ou-Mandel interference, in which two identical photons entering a balanced beam splitter always exit together, while fermions always exit separately—a phenomenon recently demonstrated with electrons and featured in Science. Adding quarter-wave plates before the beam splitter ensures that simultaneous detector clicks indicate the atoms are left in a Bell state.

The paper develops quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) methods for efficiently estimating expectations of quantities of interest from nonlinear PDE models of tumor growth, motivated by uncertainty quantification in precision medicine and oncology, where noisy and indirectly informative imaging data introduce uncertainty into calibrated models. The governing model is a semi-linear parabolic reaction-diffusion equation capturing tumor invasion and logistic proliferation, with uncertain diffusion and proliferation coefficients modeled as random fields truncated to finitely many random variables. While existing QMC theory largely addresses linear PDEs, the authors state that, to their knowledge, this is the first analysis of QMC methods for a nonlinear PDE apart from eigenvalue problems. They establish well-posedness for the parametric PDE, prove rigorous error estimates for uniform random fields, and derive parametric regularity bounds requiring a novel proof because the nonlinear term u(1−u) is not monotone. Numerical experiments, including a log-normal random field case on a complex domain used in glioma modeling, support the theory; spatio-temporal discretization error is left to future work.

In May 2007, Victor Reinoso, deputy mayor for education under newly elected DC Mayor Adrian Fenty, had 12 hours to recommend a chancellor to lead the Washington, DC Public Schools (DCPS), which would come under mayoral control in June under legislation passed by the DC Council that April. DCPS—150 schools, 55,000 students, and roughly 4,000 teachers—was among the nation's worst urban systems, with half its schools failing federal standards, high administrative spending relative to instruction, rampant patronage, and six superintendents since 1998.

Reinoso, an MIT Sloan MBA and former turnaround consultant, joined the school board in 2004 after observing poor performance at his neighborhood school. He ran as the "business community candidate," won with Fenty's endorsement, but grew frustrated with the board's consensus-driven culture and Superintendent Clifford Janey's incremental approach, concluding that meaningful reform required mayoral control, as in Chicago, Boston, and New York.

After Fenty's November 2006 election, Reinoso resigned his board seat, built a flat, consulting-style team, hired the Parthenon Group to gather data showing DCPS ranked last in achievement among 11 comparable districts, and privately drafted legislation transferring control to the mayor. The DC Public Education Reform Act of 2007 made DCPS a subordinate mayoral agency led by a chancellor, limited the school board to state-level functions, and created an interagency commission for children's services; it passed on April 17, 2007.

Reinoso's chancellor search sought an entrepreneurial leader willing to fundamentally rethink public education. Candidates included Miami-Dade superintendent Rudy Crew, known for aggressive reforms; Michelle Rhee, founder of The New Teacher Project and critic of union staffing rules; and incumbent Janey, whose caution Reinoso questioned. In early May, Reinoso drew criticism for using unattributed material from Charlotte-Mecklenburg in a council document, temporarily jeopardizing the takeover, before finalizing his recommendation.

Mesh is a short-to-intermediate passing concept, originally associated with the Air Raid Offense, that creates natural picks and confusion for defenses. Against man coverage, it allows playmakers to stay on the move; against zone coverage, receivers settle in open voids. It performs well against man coverage and base zone coverages (cover 2, 3, and 4) but can struggle against zone blitzes or simulated pressure that forces the ball out quickly. The concept uses deep drag, shallow drag, arrow, flare, and corner routes, with specific coaching points for each position against man and zone looks. The quarterback's post-snap progression—flare, shallow drag, deep drag, then FB arrow—stays the same against all defensive looks. Notable variations include the mesh rail, which features the running back as the primary option on a rail route, and a sit route at 8-10 yards as a zone coverage answer. Bruce Eien's single wing offense also runs mesh as a variation of the smash concept.

This document specifies the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for AMD SEV-ES and SEV-SNP, features that protect guest register state from the hypervisor by encrypting it during world switches. The GHCB is a 4KB decrypted page through which guests selectively share register state with hypervisors during Non-Automatic Exits (NAEs). The document standardizes the GHCB memory format, required NAE events, and guest-hypervisor interactions such as NMI handling and SMP booting.

Version 2 adds initial SEV-SNP support and hypervisor feature advertisement via a 52-bit FEATURES bitmap returned through the GHCB MSR protocol. Successive revisions added features including a VLEK certificate GUID, APIC ID list retrieval, multi-VMPL support, Page State Change for SEV-ES guests, SEV-TIO trusted I/O, Secure AVIC backing pages, and 64-bit guest request message sequence numbers.

The GHCB MSR protocol enables protocol negotiation, CPUID requests, SEV information exchange, AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration/unregistration, and termination requests before the GHCB page is established. Defined NAE events include CPUID, MSR, I/O, MMIO, page state changes, SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request, AP creation, #HV doorbell pages, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID list, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Request, Secure AVIC, and termination requests. SMP booting requires AP Jump Tables or the SNP AP Creation feature because register values cannot be modified after measurement; vCPU hotplug is supported only via SNP AP Creation. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported. SNP Restricted Injection defines #HV doorbell pages containing PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields for host-to-guest interrupt and non-maskable event notification, with specified host and guest behaviors.

This disclosure relates to sealing technology for high-pressure flow control devices, such as plug valves and fluid ends used in oil and gas production, which must withstand pressures of 15,000 psi and higher (preferably up to 22,500 psi) while handling corrosive and/or abrasive fluids. In conventional designs, seals are mounted in components such as valve inserts or discharge plugs and seal against the device body, causing erosion of the body bore and leading to leakage. Repairing the body through weld build-up and machining is cumbersome and disruptive. The disclosed technology instead mounts seals in recesses or grooves formed in the body, with the seals extending to engage sealing surfaces on the mating components (e.g., inserts, retaining nuts, discharge and suction plugs, valve seats, and stuffing box sleeves). This transfers erosion wear from the body to the less complex and less expensive mating component, which can be resurfaced or replaced more easily, reducing downtime and cost. Erosion-resistant treatments such as HVOF or tungsten carbide coatings can further extend component life. The invention also covers fluid end assemblies with intersecting conduits, endless grooves for seals, recessed corner sections, and related manufacturing methods, and is applicable to other high-pressure flow devices beyond the illustrative valve and fluid end embodiments.

The passage introduces CTPNet (Channel, Trend and Period-wise representation learning Network), a framework for multivariate long-term time series forecasting. It notes that existing RNN-, CNN-, MLP-, and Transformer-based methods are limited by real-world time series complexity, and that downsampling-based approaches capture intra-subsequence dependencies but neglect inter-subsequence and inter-channel dependencies. CTPNet learns three complementary dependency types: inter-channel dependencies via a Temporal Query-based Multi-Head Attention mechanism; intra-subsequence dependencies via a linear-complexity Transformer applied to downsampled subsequences mapped into a higher-dimensional hidden space; and inter-subsequence dependencies via the same network applied to transposed encoder outputs. The architecture consists of seven components: Channel-wise Representation Learning (CRL), downsampling, an encoder, Trend-wise Representation Learning (TRL), Periodic-wise Representation Learning (PRL), a decoder, and de-downsampling, with residual connections used to enhance training stability. The paper's stated contributions are the explicit modeling of inter-subsequence dependencies, a unified framework for comprehensive representation learning, and state-of-the-art performance. Experiments on benchmark datasets (ETTh1, ETTh2, ETTm1, ETTm2, ECL, SOLAR, TRAFFIC, WEATHER) with a fixed look-back length of 96 show CTPNet achieves the best MSE and MAE results in 54 of the reported comparisons, demonstrating robustness and generality.

Channel 4 chief executive Alex Mahon called the broadcaster's 28.6% gender pay gap "unacceptable" and aims for a 50:50 split in its top 100 jobs by 2023. This exceeds the national average of 17.4%, despite a 59% female workforce. Mahon attributed it to a 66% female lower half and 34 women in the top 100 highest-paid roles. Brought in to score, the player was initially disappointed but stayed positive, believing they were playing well in other areas and that goals would come with time. They emphasized that winning matters more than personal scoring.

Generative AI is transforming higher education assessment, offering opportunities to personalize learning, provide feedback, and create authentic assessments, while raising academic integrity concerns. Traditional assessments such as essays and multiple-choice questions are vulnerable to AI-generated work, and detection tools are unreliable, prone to false positives, and may unfairly flag non-native English speakers. Institutions can avoid AI through in-person exams, design AI-resistant tasks, or embrace AI by integrating it into assessment design. A case study at a UK university redesigned a postgraduate immunology coursework essay to integrate ChatGPT 3.5: students attended training workshops, generated draft outlines with AI, peer-evaluated them, then completed essays independently. Of 20 students surveyed, 57.9% had used generative AI, but only 5% felt very confident; students valued AI for planning, drafting, and summarizing but criticized its accuracy, outdated information, and superficial outputs. Only 26% considered using AI in assessments plagiarism. The redesign met the intended learning outcome regarding AI capabilities and limitations. The paper concludes that AI literacy training for students and educators is essential, AI should complement rather than replace teachers, and assessments should shift toward higher-order cognitive skills, with institutions reviewing policies to integrate AI holistically while safeguarding academic integrity.
A Mission man was arrested after a series of collisions in Maple Ridge that injured a pedestrian and her son; he faces impaired driving, hit and run, and dangerous driving charges.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver said there is "no contemplation" of moving the 2026 All-Star Game from the Clippers' Intuit Dome while the league investigates whether the team circumvented salary cap rules. The probe began after a report on a $28 million endorsement contract between Kawhi Leonard and Aspiration Fund Adviser LLC, a company in which owner Steve Ballmer invested $50 million and which filed for bankruptcy. The game, expected to feature a new U.S. versus international format, will air on NBC on Feb. 15.

The Supreme Court of Louisiana affirmed the first-degree murder conviction and life sentence of Ray Jones, Jr., who was convicted of killing his two-and-one-half-month-old son. On appeal, Jones raised two assignments of error. First, he challenged the admission of three inculpatory statements: one made to his treating psychiatrist after drug treatment left him calm and lucid, a second made to hospital staff shortly before his release, and a third made to police after he had invoked his right to counsel and a detective remarked that "God takes care of little babies." The court held the first two statements were voluntary, unsolicited, and not products of police interrogation, so Miranda warnings were not required. Applying Rhode Island v. Innis, it found the detective's remark was more in the nature of consolation and not reasonably likely to elicit an incriminating response, and that the defendant had simply changed his mind about talking. The court further held that any error in admitting the third statement was harmless beyond a reasonable doubt, given the two earlier witnessed statements and other overwhelming evidence of guilt. Second, the court found no abuse of discretion in the trial judge's sustaining a relevancy objection that restricted cross-examination of the psychiatrist about potentially "bad information" from family members, since the relevant issue was the voluntariness of the statements. The conviction and sentence were affirmed.

From April 1, Scotland's Abusive Behaviour and Sexual Harm Act will make disclosing or threatening to disclose intimate images a criminal offence carrying a maximum five-year prison sentence. Justice Secretary Michael Matheson said the law responds to the ease of sharing private images online and warns offenders, though legislation alone cannot tackle abusive behaviour.

This patent application, a continuation of U.S. application Ser. No. 16/211,507, describes active ground terrain mapping for controlling mobile agricultural machines. A pose detection sensor affixed to the machine generates position and orientation signals at various points along the machine's route. Based on these signals, a point cloud is identified, comprising points estimated to correspond to the ground surface over which the machine travels, and elevation values are generated for each point. The point cloud is virtually attached to the machine and moves with it, with each point's elevation value assigned a confidence (weight) value that varies with distance from the pose detector. Elevation values are aggregated into cells of a georeferenced map structure, where lower-confidence values are merged with higher-confidence values as the machine moves closer. A plane calculated through the point cloud can provide predictive elevation values of the ground ahead of the machine. Control signals generated from the elevation data control subsystems such as sprayer boom height, harvester header height, crop volume estimation, communication systems, and operator interfaces. The approach addresses limitations of prior systems that projected a plane from past GNSS measurements, which deviated from actual ground height by up to 30 cm. The passage also describes machine components, weighting functions, map layers, remote server architectures, mobile devices, and computing environments for implementing the system.

Micro-credentials are certifications assessing knowledge and skills gained through specific learning experiences, defined variously by agencies such as the Malaysian Qualifications Agency, the European Commission, the OECD, and UNESCO. Their uptake is driven by the gap between traditional higher education and the skills needed in the digital world. This qualitative study explored micro-credentials in Mauritius through semi-structured interviews with 10 educational leaders from public and private higher education institutions and four industry leaders from sectors such as ICT and finance. The research addressed three questions: leaders' familiarity with micro-credentials, their integration into higher education credit systems, and their perceived value for recognizing knowledge and skills.

Results showed general familiarity with the concept but varying interpretations. Educational leaders described micro-credentials as short, competence-based units of learning, while industry leaders viewed them as mini-qualifications building competency profiles. Badges were less familiar, with differing views on their relationship to micro-credentials. Formal assessment was considered necessary for credibility and recognition.

Regarding integration, respondents preferred a hybrid, flexible credit transfer model allowing existing credit systems to remain largely unchanged while enabling conversion to micro-credits. Micro-credentials were seen as enabling self-paced learning, customized pathways, and rapid responses to industry demands, with the IT sector suggested as a possible starting point.

Respondents viewed micro-credentials as a disruptive innovation requiring incremental implementation, experimentation, and prototyping. Many education leaders saw them as the future of education, while others expected them to complement rather than replace existing systems. Recognition within the National Qualifications Framework (NQF) was considered necessary, along with an adaptive regulatory framework balancing quality and flexibility.

The study concluded that although micro-credentials were not fully understood by all leaders, there was broad agreement on their importance and the need for integration, particularly following Covid-19. The absence of a national framework was noted, and a unified framework enabling contribution toward recognized university credits and employer acceptance was recommended. The authors suggest Mauritius' approach, emphasizing competency-based assessment, quality standards, and stakeholder collaboration, offers lessons for other developing countries.

Matthew Shashy, 29, of Montgomery, was sentenced to four years of probation for discharging a firearm outside Maxwell Air Force Base. A federal jury found him guilty of impeding, intimidating, and interfering with Air Force personnel. After spray-painting anti-government graffiti during the 2017 New Year's weekend, he fired a shotgun three times toward the base's Day Street entrance on January 3.

Brookfield Infrastructure Partners (BIP), the most successful listed partnership managed by Brookfield Asset Management, has delivered 20% annualized returns since 2008, with Adjusted AFFO growing from $352M to $926M since 2012. It offers a 4% distribution yield versus a 5.84% AFFO yield, retaining 1.84% for growth. Management targets 6-9% annual distribution growth, though the author views this as aggressive given lower inflation; past same-store EBITDA growth averaged 5% on a constant-currency basis. The current lower yield reflects a higher unit price, benefiting existing holders through accretive unit issuances, though this strategy depends on unit prices. The author expects future total returns around 10%, with a safe, growing dividend.

A Phase 2 NIAID-funded trial found that combining a 16-week initial course of omalizumab with oral immunotherapy (OIT) improved treatment for children allergic to multiple foods. Stanford researchers enrolled 48 participants aged 4 to 15, randomly assigned to omalizumab or placebo injections, with OIT starting at week 8. After 36 weeks, 83 percent of the omalizumab group could safely eat at least two grams of two or more allergenic foods, versus 33 percent on placebo, and had fewer adverse events. Larger studies are needed to confirm the findings.

In 1874, store credit was tracked in a blue book noting debt payment history, beginning Equifax's business model. Credit bureaus serve businesses as customers; regular people are the product. They collect financial data without opt-in; lawmakers have struggled to regulate them for fifty years.

An archaeological search at City Hall for a rifle belonging to Easter Rising rebel Willie Halpin found nothing. Family history holds that Halpin, who fought on the building's roof with the Irish Citizen Army, dropped the rifle into a gap rather than surrender it to British soldiers. The Dublin City Council-financed dig, led by archaeologist Franc Myles, uncovered other artefacts including bullet-holed roof fragments, 1930s milk bottles, a teapot lid, and pottery. Myles suggested the rifle was likely removed after the Rising, possibly during a 1921 inspection by the Black and Tans.

Tanzania's government has launched the Tanzania Business Clinic (TBC), an initiative introduced by Industry, Trade and Investment minister Charles Mwijage to speed up improving the country's business climate. Julia Banks, who won the federal seat of Chisholm from Labor in 2016, faced questions about possible dual Greek Australian citizenship, though locals were largely unaware of the controversy. OpenAI's GPT-5 launch faced glitches and criticism for falling short of expectations, but Sam Altman says the model was misunderstood and his attitude toward AGI has changed.

Soccer players use various on-field non-verbal communications, primarily hand signals, during matches. These include arm movements to signal set pieces, indicate openness for passes, or direct teammates' runs; hand gestures for substitution requests, wall positioning, and goalkeeper directions; pointing to indicate runs, coverage assignments, or pass targets; and taps to request throw-in locations. Pre-arranged signals exist for corner kicks, throw-ins, and free kicks. Other non-verbal methods include head nods, ball handling actions to start plays, bouncing the ball to identify corner kicks, and made-up signals such as offside traps. A classic film clip shows Pelé signaling behind his back during a throw-in for the New York Cosmos. Coaches may need to develop complete sets of non-verbal communications when crowd noise prevents players from hearing one another.

This passage is from the SD Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00, covering bus speed modes, card initialization, and command functions for SD memory cards.

For UHS-I, after power cycle the card operates in 3.3V signaling mode; 1.8V signaling can be entered only in SD mode via a voltage switch sequence invoked by CMD11 after ACMD41 negotiation between host and card. UHS-I supports only 4-bit bus mode, except CMD42, which is required to unlock a locked card before switching to 4-bit mode via ACMD6. Driver strength, bus speed mode, and power limit are selected through CMD6 function groups 3, 1, and 4. CMD19 sends tuning blocks for sampling point tuning, which is required for SDR104 and optional for SDR50 hosts.

UHS-II cards support SD Bus Interface modes (DS, HS, SDR104, DDR50) and UHS-II Interface modes (FD156, HD312, FD312, FD624), with performance classes UHS156 and UHS624. UHS-II initialization consists of PHY initialization, device initialization, enumeration, configuration, and SD-TRAN initialization. If STB.L is not detected on the D1 lane within 200 microseconds, the host initializes the card in SD Bus I/F mode.

The specification defines Application Performance Class with minimum random and sequential performance requirements, along with Cache, Self Maintenance, and Command Queue features. UHS-III (FD624) provides a maximum bus speed of 624MB/s.

Card operation modes include card identification mode (after reset until CMD3) and data transfer mode (after RCA publication). CMD8 verifies interface operating conditions and is mandatory before the first ACMD41 for SDHC/SDXC initialization. ACMD41 identifies and rejects cards not matching the host's VDD range; HCS and CCS fields handle capacity support, and card initialization must complete within 1 second.

Data transfer mode supports block read (CMD17/CMD18) and write (CMD24/CMD25) with CRC protection, erase operations (CMD32/CMD33/CMD38) including Discard and FULE, and write protection via mechanical switch, internal protection, and password-based lock/unlock (CMD42). Card Ownership Protection (COP) adds FEP-based protection with COP Unlock requirements. CMD6 switches card functions across groups including access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit, operating in check (Mode 0) or set (Mode 1) modes.

The passage describes NVIDIA's Blackwell GPU architecture and its key features. The AI Management Processor (AMP) is a dedicated RISC-V processor that offloads GPU context scheduling from the system CPU, reducing latency and improving workload management, matching Microsoft's Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling model. Blackwell adds hardware encode/decode support for 4:2:2 chroma video, with the ninth-generation NVENC improving AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% BD-BR PSNR and introducing an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode. The sixth-generation NVDEC provides 2x faster H.264 decoding. DisplayPort 2.1b support delivers up to 80 Gbps bandwidth.

Max-Q power efficiency improvements include advanced power gating, accelerated frequency switching (1000x faster than prior architectures), and low latency sleep states (10x faster to enter than Ada), enabling up to 50% power savings in some workloads.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, producing up to three additional frames per rendered frame using a new AI model that is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM. Transformer-based models replace CNNs for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving image quality and stability.

Blackwell introduces neural shaders through the Cooperative Vectors API, enabling RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression (up to 7:1 compression), Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces.

The architecture comprises GB202 (flagship, 92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA cores), GB203 (high-end), and GB205 (performance segment) GPUs, launching as the GeForce RTX 5090, 5080, 5070 Ti, and 5070.

This Phase 2/3, observer-blind, randomized controlled study evaluated the safety and immunogenicity of SII-NVX-CoV2373 (Covovax) in 920 Indian children and adolescents aged 2–17 years, randomized 3:1 to receive two doses of vaccine or placebo on days 1 and 22. The vaccine was found safe and well tolerated, with no causally related serious adverse events or adverse events of special interest; most adverse events were mild and resolved without sequelae. Immunogenicity results showed more than 98% seroconversion for anti-spike IgG and neutralizing antibodies after the second dose, with fold-rises of 84.9–169.2 from baseline. Both pediatric age groups (2–11 and 12–17 years) met non-inferiority criteria compared with vaccinated adults, with titers in children actually higher than in adults. Immune responses against Delta, Omicron BA.1, and Omicron BA.5 variants were also demonstrated. Antibody titers declined by day 180 but remained well above baseline. The authors conclude that SII-NVX-CoV2373 may be used in pediatric COVID-19 vaccination, including protection against emerging variants of concern.

Mud Bay, a 45-store pet retailer in the Pacific Northwest founded in 1988 by Elsa Wulff and later co-led by her children Lars and Marisa, pursued a "Good Jobs Vision" (GJV) beginning in 2014. Developed by a 20-person strategic planning team, the vision aimed to make Mud Bay one of the best-loved retailers in the region by 2017 through five strategies: investing in staff, offering less at everyday low prices, standardizing processes while empowering staff, cross-training and operating with slack, and partnering with animal welfare organizations.

From 2014 to 2017, Mud Bay raised average hourly wages from $12.12 to $15.06, expanded medical insurance eligibility to 82% of employees, launched an Employee Stock Ownership Plan, introduced new training and leadership programs, reduced SKUs from 3,750 to 3,180, lowered prices, standardized delivery processes, and expanded community outreach. Results included 70% sales growth, same-store sales growth averaging above 9%, turnover declining from 48% to 31%, and employees owning 4.8% of the company. However, net profit margins fell from 2.18% in 2014 to 1.99% in 2017 due to higher wages, benefits, and lower prices. Leadership viewed lower profitability as an acceptable trade-off for long-term success, though insufficient profit delayed finalizing the 2018 budget.

Amid industry pressure from larger chains and online competitors, COO Tracy Yamane proposed closing stores an hour earlier to generate labor savings and improve employee schedules. Marisa supported the idea; Lars opposed it, requesting an impact analysis before deciding.

This study examined the experiences of education students and lecturers regarding the effectiveness of Physical Education teacher training in distance mode at North-West University, South Africa. Using a qualitative design with open-ended questionnaires completed by 17 third-year B.Ed. students and semi-structured interviews with 4 lecturers, data were analysed inductively. Five themes emerged: interaction between students and lecturers; competence, passion and enthusiasm to teach Physical Education; obstacles concerning Physical Education in distance learning; experiences of practical training; and the program's influence on participants' perceptions of Physical Education. Students valued lecturers' availability and passion, and reported increased confidence and competence. Obstacles included students' limited background knowledge, technological illiteracy and limited internet access, and administrative deficiencies in assignment handling. Videos supported practical skill development, though delayed feedback on practical assignments was viewed negatively. The course content positively influenced students' perceptions of Physical Education's value. Recommendations include additional face-to-face contact, technological training for students, improved use of videos and media, increased student-interaction functions in learning management systems, and sufficient management and administration systems.

Rieva Lesonsky explains that document management affects businesses of all sizes, and poor practices cost time, money, and customers through misplaced or inaccessible documents, storage and supply expenses, and security risks such as sensitive papers left on printers. According to a Xerox survey, 40% of business processes remain document driven; improved workflow is the biggest benefit of better document management, with business growth and productivity as key motivations. Tracking printing costs is a first step—97% of surveyed businesses know their print costs, and 81% plan improvements. Xerox ConnectKey-enabled MFPs allow scanning to cloud services like Google Drive and Dropbox, with apps such as CapturePoint and Mobile Link streamlining workflows. Printing restrictions, including PIN requirements, color-printing limits, and low-toner email alerts, can save money and improve document management.

A passport certifies that its holder is a US citizen, and by law only citizens may receive one. The Secretary of State and diplomatic and consular officers issue passports under Presidential rules; issuance to law-abiding citizens who comply with the rules is general practice but not obligatory, and rejection does not itself deny citizenship. Applicants must establish citizenship, US domicile, and intent to return. Expatriated persons—those who quit the country, abandon allegiance, and intend permanent foreign residence—cannot receive passports, though residence abroad for health, education, business, or amusement with intent to return does not constitute expatriation. With no legislative definition, expatriation is determined case by case, and even absent expatriation, persons permanently domiciled abroad cannot receive passports. Adverse factors include severed US ties, foreign family and business; favorable ones include maintained family and property connections, health or financial impediments to return, and representation of American enterprises abroad. In countries with US extraterritorial jurisdiction, passports are afforded so long as pursuits are legitimate, and members of American communities in Turkey may inherit citizenship rights notwithstanding section 1993.

A city court reserved its order on Shashi Tharoor's anticipatory bail plea in the Sunanda Pushkar death case for tomorrow. Delhi Police opposed it, saying he might flee the country, harm the investigation, and influence witnesses. His counsel said the police contradicted its earlier claim that he cooperated during the probe. Summoned to appear July 7 as an accused, Tharoor faces charges under IPC sections 498A and 306 but has not been arrested. Pushkar was found dead in a luxury hotel on January 17, 2014.

The 200-day moving average (200 DMA) is a widely used technical indicator that averages an asset's closing prices over 200 trading days to smooth short-term fluctuations and identify trends. Prices above the average indicate an uptrend; below, a downtrend. Hedge fund manager Paul Tudor Jones uses it as a defensive tool to exit before bear markets, and it performed well during the 2007–09 financial crisis and the 2020 oil price crash. Backtests on the S&P 500 since 1960 show the strategy nearly matched buy-and-hold returns while producing substantially lower drawdowns. However, in the absence of major recessions, frequent whipsaws cause underperformance—from March 2009 it returned 8.5% annually versus 12.8% for buy-and-hold, despite a lower maximum drawdown (19% vs. 34%). Since 1960, the strategy generated 187 crossovers with only a 28% win rate and up to nine consecutive losses. Jeremy Siegel's variant, using a 1% buffer, performed slightly better. The article also notes that differences between simple and exponential moving averages are small, there is no special significance to 200 days beyond being a round number, and adding a 200 DMA filter to a strategy reduces returns but lowers drawdowns and improves win rates.

ITV cycling presenter and former Channel Five news anchor Matt Barbet is launching a podcast called Home Roads on iTunes and Acast on June 8. In the series, Barbet rides bikes with professional cyclists and other figures from the sport, discussing their lives. Four episodes will be available immediately, featuring Alex Dowsett, Sarah Storey, Nicolas Roche, and David Millar, with further recorded episodes to follow.

The NVIDIA A100 GPU introduces multiple architectural improvements over V100. It features a 5-site HBM2 memory subsystem with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth (1.7x faster than V100) and a 40 MB L2 cache (7x larger) with improved cache management controls that minimize writebacks and reduce redundant DRAM traffic for neural network training, inferencing, and general compute workloads. Compute Data Compression saves up to 4x DRAM and L2 bandwidth.

The Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) feature partitions each A100 into up to seven GPU Instances with isolated memory system paths—including crossbar ports, L2 cache banks, memory controllers, and DRAM address busses—providing quality of service and fault isolation. GPU Instances are constructed from GPU slices, each containing a Sys Pipe, one GPC, and L2 cache slices. Compute Instances within GPU Instances enable simultaneous context execution and support Volta-style MPS. MIG supports multi-tenant and single-tenant use cases, and vGPUs can be migrated between GPU Instances.

The third-generation NVLink provides 50 Gbit/sec per signal pair with twelve links delivering 600 GB/sec total bandwidth (versus 300 GB/sec in V100). A100 supports PCIe Gen 4 (31.5 GB/sec per direction for x16) with SR-IOV virtualization. New error detection, isolation, and containment technologies improve GPU uptime, particularly in MIG environments.

Additional features include a 5-core NVJPG hardware JPEG decode engine, an Optical Flow Accelerator supporting optical flow and stereo disparity estimation, improved atomic operations (11x FP16, 2.7x FP32 over V100), and five NVDEC video decode units (versus one in V100).

CUDA 11 provides support for A100 capabilities including Task Graphs for efficient repeated workflow submission, asynchronous copy operations for direct global-to-shared memory transfers bypassing the register file, hardware-accelerated asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls for persistent data accesses, and expanded Cooperative Groups collectives using new warp reduce instructions.

The DGX A100 system delivers 5 PFLOPS of AI performance with eight A100 GPUs interconnected through six NVSwitches with 4.8 TB/s total bidirectional bandwidth, supporting up to 56 discrete accelerators through MIG. Its software stack includes the CUDA Toolkit, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, and NGC Private Registry providing GPU-optimized containers for deep learning, machine learning, and HPC applications.

The passage also describes sparse neural network techniques, where pruning removes nodes and interconnections with minimal accuracy contribution. Fine-grained structured sparsity (2:4) supported by A100 balances workload distribution while maintaining accuracy across image classification, segmentation, and natural language processing networks.

This lecture covers hinged dissections and related topics. No software exists for animating hinged dissections, making this a potential project; Greg Frederickson, a leading expert, authored three books on dissections, including hinged and twist-hinged varieties. The lecture revisits hinged dissections of polyominoes, polyiamonds, and polyabolos, proving universality by induction: each square is cut into two half-squares with hinges visible on every edge, and leaves are plucked from a spanning tree of the dual graph and reattached cyclically. The same approach extends to 3D using tetrahedra cut from their centroid. Hardware examples include Harvard's salt-activated self-folding squares, DNA origami (started by Paul Rothemund), and chain-folding robots built at MIT's Center for Bits and Atoms, which stay connected during motion, unlike typical modular reconfigurable robots. The Montucla dissection (1778) converts one rectangle to another, and the superposition ("perlie") technique yields the square-to-equilateral-triangle dissection; Frederickson applied this to a convertible table in 2008, and the D Haus Company created reconfigurable furniture and house designs. A pseudopolynomial bound for hinged dissections is sketched: for grid-aligned polygons, triangulate using grid points (via Pick's theorem), chainify triangles, use gadgets to move hinges, and apply pseudocuts to superpose dissections while recursing only to constant depth. Finally, 3D dissections require matching volume and Dehn invariant (edge lengths tensored with dihedral angles), per Hilbert's third problem, Dehn's proof, and Sydler's 1965 sufficiency result; this holds in 4D, remains open in 5D and higher, and equality of Dehn invariants was shown decidable in 2008, though efficient algorithms are unknown.

Researchers at the Universities of York and St Andrews found that New Caledonian crows and kea parrots solve tasks more successfully after exploring the objects involved beforehand, suggesting they learn object properties incidentally through play, similar to human infants. Birds explored blocks and ropes of varying colours, weights and patterns before choosing tools to complete tasks. This "latent learning" occurred without reinforcement, and the birds did not change their interactions after learning the objects' usefulness. Separately, World Animal Protection reported a 292 percent increase in wildlife selfies on Instagram since 2014, over 40 percent involving inappropriate interaction, fueling cruel treatment of Amazon species.

This document section standardizes the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol. Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) events—exit events that are not AE events—cause hardware to throw a #VC exception in SEV-ES guests; the guest inspects the error code, copies required register state to the GHCB, and invokes VMGEXIT. The specification defines required NAE events and guest state, along with VALID_BITMAP rules: guests set bits for SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, and SW_EXITINFO2; hypervisors set bits for SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2, with both parties resetting the bitmap before use. Hypervisors must handle VMGEXIT for all listed NAE events even if they do not intercept the triggering instructions, and guests must handle #VC for all listed events.

Specific NAE events covered include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO access (using a decrypted shared buffer at GHCB offset 0x800), Page State Change (private/shared transitions, PSMASH/UNSMASH hints, with per-entry progress tracking and reason codes), SNP Guest Request and SNP Extended Guest Request (firmware communication, sequence numbers, certificate return via GUID tables), AP Creation (VMSA pages via RMPADJUST, enabling vCPU hotplug), #HV doorbell page registration (GET_PREFERRED, SET, QUERY, CLEAR), #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer (emulated APIC timer), APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Request (trusted device binding, measurements, and TDISP attestation), Secure AVIC backing page registration, and Termination Request. Errors are signaled via non-zero SW_EXITINFO1[31:0], with reason codes in SW_EXITINFO2.

Additional topics include guest identification of SEV-ES via CPUID; SMP/AP booting challenges, since hypervisors cannot modify measured registers, addressed through AP Reset Hold and AP jump tables; NMI handling, where the hypervisor must intercept #DB but not IRET, relying on "NMI Complete" messages; debug register virtualization or DR7 intercept caching; and statements that SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

Finally, the #HV doorbell page (shared, host-owned, accessed with C=0) contains PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields for interrupt delivery under Restricted Injection. The host presents interrupts by writing vector numbers and delivers #HV notifications; guests must atomically exchange PendingEvent to acknowledge interrupts and complete EOIs via NoEoiRequired or explicit VMGEXIT-based APIC writes. Guests must execute HLT with interrupts disabled due to the absence of interrupt shadows, and must validate vectors from potentially non-cooperative hosts.

Joan Jordan, a 45-year-old Irish software engineer, was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2010 after becoming paralysed down one side. She had stopped working beforehand and was repeatedly rejected by employers afterward. This patent application, a continuation of U.S. application Ser. No. 16/192,068 by Morgan et al. filed November 15, 2018, describes address obfuscation for memory. Memory devices may wear out from normal use or malicious attacks such as row hammer. Wear-leveling distributes wear by moving data between memory cells, but if a bad actor reverse-engineers the data movement pattern, the actor could induce wear-out, access sensitive data, or apply the knowledge to other devices using the same function.

The disclosed techniques map logical addresses to physical addresses in an unpredictable manner. A selection component selects a mapping function implemented by mapping subcomponents, applying a logic operation—such as inversion, non-inversion (pass-through), XOR, XNOR, or address swap—to each bit of a logical address to determine the physical address. The mapping function may be selected based on random numbers, unique device identifiers, schedules, or trigger events (e.g., boot, reboot, exceeding an access threshold, or detecting an attack), and may vary across devices, dice, and arrays or over time, rendering reverse-engineered patterns useless elsewhere or at later times. Scratch cells beyond the logical address space support wear-leveling transfers. A security key can enable direct memory addressing (all pass-through operations) for manufacturer testing and debugging, with this mode disabled before shipping. Methods include selecting a mapping function, receiving an access command containing a logical address, determining the corresponding physical address, and accessing the stored data.

The passage is the user manual for the SanDisk Sansa Fuze portable media player. It opens with safety instructions: read the manual fully, avoid using headphones while driving, cycling, or operating vehicles, keep volume at moderate levels to prevent noise-induced hearing loss, and keep the player away from moisture. Cleaning tips include using a soft lint-free cloth, not forcing connectors, and not disassembling, crushing, short-circuiting, or incinerating the battery. Hearing safety information cites NIDCD guidance that sounds under 80 decibels are unlikely to cause hearing loss even with long exposure. Disposal instructions warn against discarding the device with unsorted waste.

The player features a 1.9" color screen, FM tuner, built-in microphone, microSDHC expansion slot, support for MP3, WAV, WMA, secure WMA, and audiobook formats, MPEG4 video, and a non-replaceable rechargeable battery lasting up to 24 hours of audio or 5 hours of video playback. The manual covers charging via USB or optional adapters, power on/off/reset, the Hold switch, and thumbwheel navigation. It describes connecting to a computer, firmware updates, and formatting, which deletes all content.

Music transfers via drag-and-drop or Windows Media Player, including playlist creation and syncing. Photos and videos require the Sansa Media Converter software. Instructions cover playing music, audiobooks, videos, and photo slideshows, with options for repeat, shuffle, equalizer, bookmarks, ratings, and Go Lists. FM radio supports up to 30 presets and station recording. Voice recording uses the built-in microphone. Content can be deleted on the player or via computer. Settings include wallpaper color, backlight timer, power saver, language, date/time, brightness, USB mode, and factory reset.

Troubleshooting addresses supported bit rates (32-320Kbps MP3; 32-256Kbps WMA), podcast compatibility, missing ID3 tags, and microSD/microSDHC support. Technical support is available by phone or online. SanDisk offers a one-year limited warranty against material defects, non-transferable, excluding third-party software and damage from misuse. The document ends with an End User License Agreement granting a limited, non-exclusive license for personal use with SanDisk products, prohibiting modification and reverse engineering, disclaiming warranties, limiting liability, and specifying California law as governing.

The Saskatchewan Roughriders are using receiver Duron Carter at cornerback and gave returner Christion Jones his most extensive practice reps as an emergency defensive back before Thursday's game against the Hamilton Tiger-Cats. Jones, who worked with the secondary at Alabama but never played there in a game, says he is prepared and has discussed the position with his roommate Carter. Twelve-thousand-year-old camel engravings at Jebel Misma reveal early human presence in the once-verdant Nefud landscape.

This study assessed socio-demographic factors associated with insecticide-treated net (ITN) use among children under 5 years and pregnant women in Nigeria, using secondary data from the 2021 Nigeria Malaria Indicator Survey (NMIS), which covered 13,727 households and interviewed 14,476 women aged 15–49 years. Data were analyzed in R using chi-square tests and odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals.

Malaria remains a major burden in Nigeria, which accounts for about 27% of global cases, with an estimated 68 million cases and 194,000 deaths in 2021. ITNs are the most cost-effective malaria intervention, and Nigeria's National Malaria Strategic Plan targets 80% coverage by 2025.

Results showed 56% of households owned at least one ITN, with an average of 1.3 nets per household; only 25% owned enough nets to cover all members. Ownership was significantly associated with residence, geopolitical zone, and wealth quintile, with higher ownership in rural areas, the North West and North East zones, and lower wealth quintiles.

Among children under 5, 41.4% slept under an ITN the night before the survey. Usage was significantly associated with age, residence, geopolitical zone, and wealth quintile, but not sex. Younger children, rural children, those in the North West (OR 2.46) and North East (OR 2.28), and those in lower wealth quintiles had higher odds of ITN use.

Among pregnant women, 49.6% slept under an ITN. Usage was significantly associated with geopolitical zone, education, and wealth quintile; women in the North East (OR 2.86) and North West (OR 2.61), those with no or primary education, and those in lower wealth quintiles had higher odds of use.

Household ITN ownership rose from 8% in 2008 to 69% in 2015, then declined to 56% in 2021, possibly due to the COVID-19 pandemic, and remained below ownership rates in several other sub-Saharan African countries. The study concludes that ITN use remains below the 80% NMSP target, and addressing regional disparities, socioeconomic factors, and awareness initiatives is needed to achieve equitable coverage.

The author argues that K-12 education overemphasizes generic "skills"—such as critical thinking, metacognition, and "21st-century skills"—while neglecting the teaching of substantive knowledge. He contends that such skills are meaningless without content: critical thinking requires something specific to think about, and reading comprehension depends on background knowledge, as illustrated by cricket terminology unfamiliar to most American readers and by the impossibility of grasping string theory through internet lookups alone. Knowledge has been devalued, he writes, because it is equated with discredited "memorization" and dismissed as unnecessary in the internet era. He cites grade inflation, declining state graduation testing requirements, and public indifference toward the one state showing NAEP gains—where most teachers use a content-rich curriculum—as evidence of this retreat. The high-quality instructional materials movement, joined by 15 states, offers a counter-push, though AI misuse may undermine knowledge-rich curricula. He concludes that devaluing knowledge especially harms poorer students and that knowledge is essential to a meaningful, examined life.

HMD Global has not shared the Nokia 8's kernel source code 136 days after its Chief Product Officer promised to do so. This violates GPLv2 and has drawn developer criticism. Despite the locked bootloader limiting the source's usefulness, HMD is urged to comply like Xiaomi did with the Mi A1.

Celebrity chef Mario Batali is taking a leave of absence from his businesses following sexual misconduct allegations from a female chef and three women who worked for him. He apologized, saying the described behavior matched his past actions, and was removed from ABC's "The Chew."

A University of Queensland study found that three mamba species—the Black Mamba, Western Green Mamba, and Jamesons Mamba—launch a dual neurological attack, first causing flaccid paralysis through postsynaptic toxicity, then spastic paralysis through presynaptic toxicity once antivenom is administered. Previously, only the Eastern Green Mamba was thought to cause spastic paralysis. This explains why some patients initially improve after treatment before experiencing painful, uncontrolled spasms. Venom effects also vary by geographic location, such as between Black Mamba populations in Kenya and South Africa, complicating treatment. Researchers say the findings could guide development of more effective specialized antivenoms.

Fossils once dismissed as decomposed organic matter may be reclassified as one of Earth's earliest animals. Paleontologist Christopher McKean and colleagues analyzed 39 fossils found off Newfoundland's coast, dating to about 560 million years ago. The spongelike creature, named after punk rocker John Lydon due to its spiky appearance, had fingerlike tubes over pores indicating it was a filter feeder. It grew up to nearly 53 centimeters long and likely lived atop other organisms. The name also references a spiky fruit called jiggamint by the Beothuk peoples. The creature may be an ancestor of some modern sponges.

This systematic review examines the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education, focusing on assessment, grading, and feedback. Guided by the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework, the review pursues three objectives: establishing AI's effectiveness in automating and standardizing assessment processes, examining the accuracy and fairness of AI-driven grading systems compared to traditional methods, and describing the benefits of AI in providing personalized feedback. Twenty peer-reviewed studies published between 2010 and 2023 were selected from five databases and synthesized thematically following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Findings indicate that AI-driven systems enhance efficiency, scalability, and consistency in assessment, particularly for objective tasks in STEM disciplines, and deliver timely, personalized feedback that supports student engagement, motivation, and self-regulated learning. However, challenges persist, including algorithmic bias, limited validity in evaluating subjective constructs such as critical thinking and creativity, data privacy and security concerns, and the need for educator and student adoption. The review concludes that AI holds transformative potential for higher education but requires ethical safeguards, transparent policies, rigorous validation, and collaboration among educators, technologists, and policymakers to ensure equitable and effective implementation.

This article ranks Birmingham City's ten best away days from the past decade. Highlights include the 2017 final-day win at Bristol City that secured Championship survival under Harry Redknapp, a 2-1 derby win at Wolves in 2017, and a 5-2 victory at Fulham in 2015. Alex McLeish's side clinched promotion at Reading in 2009, while other notable results include a 3-0 win at Derby, a dramatic 2-1 Europa League win at Club Brugge featuring Chris Wood's 100th-minute winner, and a 3-2 win at Tottenham with Sebastian Larsson's injury-time goal in McLeish's first game. The list also features a 4-0 win at Crystal Palace, a 4-0 win at Shamrock Rovers in Dublin, and Paul Caddis's added-time equalizer at Bolton in 2014 that secured Blues' survival.

Ray Lewis, Brian Urlacher, and Randy Moss were first-ballot Pro Football Hall of Fame inductees; Terrell Owens was elected on his third try, joining Dawkins, Beathard, Kramer, and Brazile.

On April 20, 2010, the Deepwater Horizon oil rig, leased by BP from Transocean, exploded in the Gulf of Mexico while working on the Macondo well, killing 11 of the 126 workers aboard and injuring 17. The rig sank on April 22, and by the time the well was capped on July 15, 2010, nearly five million barrels of oil had spilled—the largest marine oil spill in U.S. waters.

The passage traces BP's history from its 1909 founding as the Anglo-Persian Oil Company through privatization, cost cutting, mergers with Amoco and ARCO, and its 2001 "Beyond Petroleum" rebranding. Under CEO Tony Hayward (2007), BP cut its workforce from 97,000 to 80,300 while Hayward pledged to focus on safety and reduce the company's risk-averse culture. BP's decentralized "asset federation" model tied employee compensation to site performance, creating little incentive to share risk-management practices across sites. Prior safety failures included the 2005 Texas City refinery explosion (15 dead, 180 injured) and a 2006 Prudhoe Bay pipeline spill; the Baker Report attributed Texas City partly to cost cutting and weak safety communication. Between 2007 and 2010, two BP refineries received 97% of OSHA willful safety violations.

The Macondo project was over budget and behind schedule, and the rig had 390 outstanding repairs identified in a 2009 audit. Three key decisions in closing the well favored cost and time over caution: choosing long string casing with fewer gas barriers, using six centralizers instead of the 21 recommended by Halliburton's OptiCem model, and skipping the cement bond log and full mud circulation despite warnings of severe gas flow risk.

The disaster caused extensive environmental and economic damage, prompted a deep water drilling moratorium, contributed to an estimated 250,000 lost Gulf region jobs, and led BP to establish a $20 billion Gulf Coast Claims Facility overseen by Kenneth Feinberg. Investigations were ongoing as of early 2011, with court testimony indicating the key decisions came down on the side of cost reduction and expediency over caution.

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture (14.13, Lecture 14) covers limited attention. After reviewing earlier topics (time, risk, and social preferences), the lecturer presents motivating evidence that attention is limited: change blindness experiments (person swaps, the gorilla test) and dichotic listening studies show people can direct attention when instructed but miss unattended information. Factors affecting attention include physical environment, distractions, worries, sleep, and poverty; attention is treated as fixed but limited.

High-stakes inattention is illustrated by the EntreMed case (Huberman and Regev, 2001), where the stock jumped on "old" news when The New York Times featured it on the front page, and by trader confusion between two companies with similar Zoom-related tickers.

A simple model defines perceived value as the salient component plus (1−θ) times the opaque component, where θ measures inattention. Chetty et al. made sales taxes salient on price tags in a California grocery store using a triple-difference design; demand fell 8.8%, implying θ ≈ 0.75—consumers react to sales tax changes only a quarter as much as to other price changes. Non-experimental evidence on beer shows strong responses to salient excise taxes but essentially none to sales taxes (θ near 1). Policy implications are discussed: salience matters differently for revenue-raising taxes versus "sin" taxes targeting externalities and internalities, where the government wants behavioral responses.

Finally, the "learning by noticing" paper (Schwartzstein) shows that wrong mental models prevent people from attending to relevant information, causing persistent learning failures. In Indonesian seaweed farming, experienced farmers neglected pod size; experimental trials alone had insignificant effects, but providing summarized data changed behavior substantially—demonstrating that inattention can generate large welfare losses.

In his inaugural address, the incoming President acknowledges the nation's severe economic crisis—shrunken values, rising taxes, frozen credit, industrial decline, farm losses, lost savings, and widespread unemployment—but asserts that "the only thing we have to fear is fear itself." He attributes the distress not to any failure of the nation's substance but to the incompetence and unscrupulousness of those who controlled the exchange of goods, and argues that happiness lies in achievement and work rather than monetary profit. He calls for immediate action to put people to work through direct government employment, redistribution of population, higher agricultural values, prevention of foreclosures, reduced government costs, unified relief efforts, and national planning of transportation, communications, and public utilities. He demands strict supervision of banking, credit, and investments, along with a sound currency, and will urge Congress in special session to adopt detailed measures. Though pledging to restore world trade, he prioritizes the domestic economy and dedicates the nation to a "good neighbor" policy abroad. He calls for national discipline and unity, states he may seek broad executive power if Congress fails to act, and expresses confidence in democracy and the Constitution.

This January 19, 2001 email from Ann Schmidt to numerous Enron employees, titled "Enron Mentions," compiles news articles on the California power crisis and Enron-related developments. California's two largest utilities, PG&E's Pacific Gas & Electric and Edison International's Southern California Edison, have defaulted on debt and payments, accumulating over $11.5 billion in power-related debt because a 1996 deregulation law froze retail rates while wholesale power and natural gas prices soared. Rating agencies downgraded both companies, and state legislators approved $400 million for power purchases after Governor Davis declared a state of emergency. California averted further rolling blackouts as U.S. Energy Secretary Bill Richardson ordered suppliers to continue selling electricity and natural gas to the state. President-elect Bush and Enron CEO Ken Lay, a Bush energy adviser, opposed wholesale price caps, arguing they would spread shortages to other states. Analysts noted the crisis has ended utilities' reputation as safe investments, with PG&E and Edison shares down more than 60 percent since early November. Other items include: EOTT Energy Partners, whose general partner is an Enron subsidiary, declared a quarterly distribution of $0.475 per unit; the Dow Jones bandwidth price table expanded to ten routes, with Aquila Broadband becoming the third bandwidth market maker; Pennsylvania's Public Utility Commission criticized GPU for suggesting California's crisis could occur in Pennsylvania; and Enron Energy Services signed a ten-year, $2.2 billion energy management agreement with Owens-Illinois covering 53 facilities in 20 states.

The State Department disapproved of Mr. Allen's request that the US consul-general at Shanghai seek the surrender of Kim Ok-kiun's murderer to Korean justice, as the consul's jurisdiction extended only over American citizens. Minister Sill reported that a Korean government force marching from Chon-ju was defeated by rebels at Yung-won, who then captured Chon-ju. Admiral Skerrett, whose squadron was largely detailed to Bering Sea, could not yet send a vessel to Chemulpo, though British, French, Chinese, and Japanese vessels had arrived. Sill warned that the rebellion was growing, the government was helpless to compel order, and Seoul could become dangerous for the seventy or eighty Americans residing there. Chargé Denby reported that, at the Korean King's appeal, China shipped 1,500 troops from Tien-tsin, to be increased to 2,225, with three men-of-war ordered to Chemulpo; Viceroy Li Hung-chang assured Japan the troops would withdraw once hostilities ceased.

The MACD and RSI strategy is a trading method combining two momentum indicators: MACD, a moving average-based oscillator used to analyze trends, and RSI, a momentum oscillator used to identify overbought/oversold conditions. MACD is calculated from a 12-period and 26-period EMA, with a 9-period signal line, while RSI oscillates between 0 and 100, with readings above 70 considered overbought and below 30 oversold. The indicators can be combined in various ways, such as using MACD to identify trend direction and RSI to identify price swings, or using one to confirm the other. Whether the combination is beneficial is debated—some analysts view it as redundant since both are momentum indicators, while others find it provides useful confirmation. Accuracy depends on parameters and markets, requiring backtesting. A backtested strategy on SMH from 2001 produced 235 trades with a 73% win rate and 0.88% average gain per trade.

This passage is a collection of @ThingsExpo blog posts dated January 1–2, 2017, covering IoT and related technology topics. Key items include: @ThingsExpo being named a Top 5 Most Influential IoT Brand and later the Number One M2M Brand by Onalytica, based on Twitter analysis; articles on connected devices in homes, WebRTC identity management challenges, and Matrix's open standard for IP messaging and VoIP; 2017 predictions for IoT, big data, DevOps, and the security industry; sessions on data monetization, IoT back-end data platforms, and the role of software in IoT deployments; discussions of blockchain's rising investment and smart contracts; commentary on the U.S. presidential election and data science; Microsoft's changes under CEO Satya Nadella; the 21st anniversary of Scrum; Adobe's keynote on mobile transformation; and announcements for @ThingsExpo New York, taking place June 6–8, 2017, co-located with the 20th International Cloud Expo.

The flexbone offense is a run-heavy system that evolved from the Wishbone offense and is known for option plays and misdirection, sometimes called the Triple Option Offense. It requires a decisive running quarterback, a powerful fullback (B-back), quick and agile slotbacks (A-backs), blocking-focused wide receivers, and athletic offensive linemen skilled at cut and combo blocks. Its biggest strength is its rarity in modern football, forcing defenses to spend extra preparation time, along with strong ball control, long time of possession, assignment confusion, and physically wearing down opponents. Its main weaknesses are a limited passing game, difficulty coming back from deficits, heavy practice time demands, and struggles in bad weather. Common formations include Double Slot, Trips, and Receivers Over; common run plays include the Triple Option, Midline Option, and Rocket Toss; and pass plays include the Play Action Wheel Route, Toss Boot, and Four Verticals. The service academies of Navy, Army, and Air Force have traditionally run the offense, as did Paul Johnson at Georgia Southern, Navy, and Georgia Tech before retiring in 2018. It remains in use at lower college levels—Harding University won the 2023 Division 2 National Championship—and at high schools, especially smaller ones.

As Germany's Protestant church marks the 500th anniversary of the Reformation, clergy are turning to new media to reach dwindling congregations. At Magdeburg's Walloon Reformed Church of St. Augustine, a Twitter service encourages about 40 parishioners to tweet about the liturgy, with a screen displaying posts from within the church and across Germany. Pastor Ralf Peter Reimann views it as an experiment to include people who live online. The approach echoes the Reformation itself, when Luther's supporters used pamphlets—described by professor Ulrike Zitzlsperger as the social media of that era—to spread public debate rapidly. Reactions to the service are mixed: some users post prayers and encouragement, while others, including 86-year-old Ingeborg Brunner, find it distracting and prefer traditional worship with hymns.
