He credited a defenseman's quick play and Penns' screen in front of goalie Marty, saying he simply tried to get the puck on net. The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere architecture, introduces third-generation Tensor Cores with new precision formats and features for deep learning and HPC workloads. TF32 tensor cores deliver up to 8x FP32 throughput on A100 without code changes, while FP16/BF16 mixed precision provides up to 2x TF32 throughput. For HPC, A100 supports IEEE-compliant FP64 acceleration, delivering 19.5 TFLOPS peak—2.5x Tesla V100—via a new Double Precision Matrix Multiply Add instruction. The cuSOLVER TCAIRS solver demonstrated TF32 as the fastest and most robust mixed-precision mode, achieving a 2.0x geomean speedup over FP64.

A100 introduces Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity using a 2:4 pattern (two non-zero values per four-entry vector), doubling compute throughput and halving memory footprint with virtually no accuracy loss across tested networks. Sparse MMA instructions skip zero-value computations for 2x speedup.

Memory improvements include a combined L1 data cache/shared memory of 192 KB/SM (vs 128 KB/SM on V100), 40 GB HBM2 with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth (1.7x V100), SECDED ECC protection, and a 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x V100) delivering 2.3x bandwidth. Compute Data Compression provides up to 4x DRAM bandwidth improvement. Separate FP32 and INT32 cores enable simultaneous execution.

The Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) feature partitions one A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated memory paths, enabling quality-of-service guarantees and fault isolation for multi-tenant environments. Third-generation NVLink doubles per-link data rate to 50 Gbit/s and provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth across twelve links. A100 also supports PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV.

Additional features include a 5-core NVJPG hardware JPEG decode engine, an Optical Flow Accelerator, 11x faster FP16 atomics, and five NVDEC video decode units. CUDA 11 adds task graph acceleration, asynchronous copy instructions bypassing the register file, hardware-accelerated asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls, and expanded Cooperative Groups collectives.

The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs connected via NVSwitch, delivering 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and up to 56 discrete accelerators through MIG, with software provisioned through the NGC Private Registry.

The Larry Swedroe Portfolio is a diversified investment portfolio based on evidence-based investing principles, allocating 30% to stocks and 70% to bonds to maximize returns while minimizing risk. It typically includes small-cap value (15%), international small-cap value (7.5%), emerging markets (7.5%), and intermediate bonds (70%), implemented through low-cost index funds or ETFs. Swedroe favors value investing using a bottom-up approach, targeting companies with strong fundamentals, and favors small-cap value stocks for their historically higher returns and less efficient markets. He recommends rebalancing at least annually or when an asset class deviates 5% from its target. A backtest from 2012 showed a 3.71% annual return, while the portfolio reportedly achieved a 6.28% compound annual return over 30 years with a 5.46% standard deviation. The strategy is designed for long-term gains and is best suited for risk-averse investors.

In 2011, Berkshire Hathaway announced a share repurchase program at up to 110% of book value, under which only $67 million of stock was purchased. The limit was raised to 120% in 2012, enabling approximately $1.3 billion in repurchases (9,475 Class A and 606,499 Class B shares). No repurchases occurred from 2013 to 2016, though the 120% threshold was nearly reached in early 2013, 2014, and 2016. The author argues the 120% limit should be modestly increased, since the gap between Berkshire's intrinsic value and book value has widened, making 120% more conservative than when it was set. Buffett reiterated the 120% figure in his 2016 shareholder letter.

European shares were set for a fifth straight day of losses and their biggest weekly drop since November 2016, pressured by rising bond yields and a stronger euro. Deutsche Bank fell about 5 percent after posting a bigger-than-expected 2017 net loss of 497 million euros, while Spain's Caixabank and Sabadell also declined after results described by Jefferies as underwhelming. Germany's DAX, down more than 5 percent in eight sessions, is now negative year-to-date, hurt by the euro's rise and yields weighing on defensive stocks. Bank of America Merrill-Lynch's "Bull & Bear" indicator triggered a "Sell" signal, and a Miton fund manager warned that leveraged trades may need unwinding as rates rise. Attention turns to U.S. payrolls data, where a strong figure could raise the odds of four rate hikes this year. Tech stocks are also in focus after mixed U.S. earnings from Amazon, Apple, and Alphabet.

The District Court of Appeal of Florida, Second District, reversed a final summary judgment entered in favor of The Personal Service Insurance Company and George Johnson, Jr., and remanded the case. Danny Langston, injured as a passenger in a Florida automobile accident, sued after a vehicle owned by George Johnson, Jr. and operated by Fred Johnson with the owner's permission collided with another vehicle. The trial court had granted summary judgment based on the insurer's assertion that its Ohio-issued surety bond covered only the personal acts of George Johnson, Jr. The court held that under Florida's dangerous instrumentality doctrine, the owner could be personally liable for the operator's negligence, unlike under Ohio law. Because the bond was issued in Ohio, Ohio contract law governed its interpretation. Distinguishing Kerr v. Personal Service Insurance Co., where the accident occurred in Ohio, the court concluded that Langston could qualify as a holder of a final judgment covered under the bond, making Personal Service liable, and therefore reversed and remanded for further proceedings.

This paper examines how an Australian university addressed gaps in primary pre-service teachers' (PSTs) arts education competencies by developing an Arts Specialism within its teacher education programme. Grounded in Ball's education policy sociology and its three contexts of policy-making (influence, policy text production and policy practice), the qualitative study employs critical discourse analysis of the Arts Specialism curriculum text and related documents. The literature review identifies persistent problems of limited curriculum time and inadequate preparation for arts teaching, despite global and national policy initiatives supporting arts education. Neoliberal reforms since the 1970s had reduced arts education within Australian teacher education programmes. Government requirements for primary specialisations, along with advocacy by the National Advocates for Arts Education and the Australian Council of Deans of Education, provided the rationale for the Arts Specialism, comprising four courses covering the five arts subjects: dance, drama, media arts, music and visual arts. Implementation, beginning in 2019, involved stakeholder collaboration, experiential learning, school-based projects and partnerships, with COVID-19 necessitating a shift to online delivery. PST feedback indicated positive, transformative experiences and development of expert content and pedagogical knowledge. The paper concludes that the AITSL-approved Arts Specialism represents a significant advancement in bridging policy and practice, though time constraints and changes in industrial relations laws remain challenges. Future opportunities include expansion to other institutions and mixed-methods research tracing graduates' professional journeys and school-based arts curriculum implementation.

Tales of children raised by wild animals have circulated for centuries; many are hoaxes, but some accounts persist. Sir Kenelm Digby recorded in 1644 the case of Jean de Liège, a Belgian boy who hid in the woods for about sixteen years during warfare, developed sharpened senses, and was captured at about twenty-one, hair-covered and speechless, though he later learned to talk. His hairiness is implausible and may reflect hypertrichosis. In 1672, Nicholas Tulp described an Irish "sheep-boy" raised among wild sheep who bleated and ate grass and hay. An American legend tells of a "Wolf Girl" near Texas's Devil's River, reportedly captured in 1845, escaping when wolves approached the ranch, and last seen in 1852 with two pups. Whether such "humanimals" still exist remains an open question.

A free five-week self-management course for people living with chronic pain will begin in Montrose in May, delivered by Pain Association Scotland on behalf of the Angus Health and Social Care Partnership. Open to anyone aged 18 or over living in Angus, the weekly two-and-a-half-hour sessions cover topics including understanding pain, stress management, pacing, flare-ups, relaxation, and medication. Previous participants reported coping better with pain and improved quality of life. Booking is available by phone or email.

The passage covers SEV-ES/SEV-SNP guest-hypervisor interaction topics. For NMI injection, the hypervisor must not intercept IRET but must intercept #DB, using the guest's "NMI Complete" message (sent via VMGEXIT) as the indicator that another NMI can be injected; guest processing details need not be documented in the GHCB specification. Full virtualization of hardware debug registers is supported when the DebugVirtualization bit is set in the VMSA, in which case hardware saves and restores debug register state and the hypervisor clears debug register intercepts. Otherwise, the hypervisor must intercept DR7 reads and writes; the #VC handler caches written values and returns cached values on reads. SMM is not supported in this specification version, and nested virtualization is not supported under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP.

For SNP-protected guests running with RestrictInjection, the host communicates via a #HV doorbell page containing a 16-bit PendingEvent field (with NoFurtherSignal, #MC, NMI, and interrupt vector bits) and a NoEoiRequired byte; the page must be host-owned and accessed with C=0. The guest can optimize EOIs by atomically clearing NoEoiRequired; otherwise it must perform VMGEXIT to write the X2APIC EOI MSR. Because #HV is delivered without regard to interrupt shadows, guests must execute HLT with interrupts disabled, and the host must re-enter the guest if events are pending. Doorbell page configuration uses VMGEXIT SW_EXITCODE 0x8000_0014 with GET, SET, and QUERY actions. The host must faithfully emulate APIC interrupt lifecycle, presenting the highest-priority ready interrupt and managing NoEoiRequired. Guests must acknowledge interrupts via atomic exchange, validate vectors against a potentially non-cooperative host, and treat #HV received while NoFurtherSignal is set as grounds for a system panic.

U.S. homebuilder sentiment slipped to 68 in April, down three points from March's 71, which was the highest level since June 2005, and fell short of analysts' forecast of 70. Despite the decline, new home sales remain robust, with February sales reaching a 592,000 annual rate, nearly 13 percent higher year-over-year, aided by low mortgage rates and a solid job market.

While Android smartphones such as the Samsung Galaxy S7 and Google Pixel are more innovative and powerful than the iPhone 7, Apple's closed-ended platform offers superior security, making the tradeoff worthwhile for many users. The passage outlines iOS 10.3.1 security features: data encryption through a password, pin code, or thumbprint; two-factor authentication prompts; automatic data erasure after ten failed login attempts; and iCloud backups. Although iOS is not immune to malware, it includes built-in anti-malware layers, regular updates, and an exclusive app store, unlike Android's reliance on third-party antivirus software. Additional features include Find My Phone for remotely locating, locking, or erasing stolen devices, stricter app permission controls, and Apple's exclusive control over hardware and software, which simplifies patching compared to fragmented Android.

Last shot situations in basketball involve more than drawing up a play; options depend on court location and time remaining. Teams should maintain poise through preparation, get the ball to their best player (who should never inbound it), read the defense, and keep plays simple since complexity increases the chance of breakdown. Non-shooters should crash the offensive boards, as most last-second games are won on putbacks. Practicing scenarios with a game clock and physical conditioning are also emphasized.

Holding for the last shot is valuable because combining it with the first possession of the next period can create a 12-point score swing (14 if a shooter is fouled). The basic rule is to hold for the last shot with under 30 seconds remaining when leading or trailing by fewer than eight points. Timing guidelines: players in position at 10 seconds, initiate play at 8 seconds, shoot at 3-5 seconds.

Fundamentals include mastering skip and baseball passes, practicing half-court shots, and tipping the ball. Intentionally missed free throws must be taught and practiced, with the ball required to hit the rim.

Strategies include saving at least two timeouts, taking a timeout with 1-3 seconds left, inbounding to half court with under four seconds, using a counter break, shooting in line with the basket, having the bench count down the clock, reminding the timer of clock rules, practicing from both court sides, and designating an inbounds passer. Guidelines cover various situations across 1-3, 3-6, and 6-12 second ranges, including maximum dribble counts by time remaining.

This passage from the SD Memory Card Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 covers data write operations, erase functions, write protection, card lock/unlock features, and command protocols.

During block write operations, the card performs 1 or 4-bit CRC parity checks on each received data block to prevent writing erroneously transferred data. Cards supporting block write require a block length of 512 bytes set by CMD16. Errors such as BLOCK_LEN_ERROR, ADDRESS_ERROR, and WP_VIOLATION are indicated in the status register. Multiple block write commands are recommended over continuous single writes for faster operation, and ACMD23 (pre-erased setting) can make multiple block writes faster. ACMD22 reports the number of well-written blocks.

Erase operations use ERASE_WR_BLK_START (CMD32), ERASE_WR_BLK_END (CMD33), and ERASE (CMD38) commands in sequence. The DISCARD operation is similar to ERASE but allows partial or complete de-allocation of blocks; it is supported only for SDHC and SDXC cards and not through SPI. FULE (Full User Area Logical Erase) logically erases the entire user area. Busy status is indicated by holding DAT0 low, and the host may deselect the card with CMD7 during operations.

Three write protect methods are supported: a mechanical write protect switch (host responsibility), card internal write protect, and password protection card lock. Password protection uses 128-bit PWD and 8-bit PWD_LEN registers, which are non-volatile. Locked cards respond only to basic command class commands, ACMD41, CMD16, and lock card class commands. The COP (Card Ownership Protection) feature uses FEP (Force Erase Password) registers; when FEP is set, COP Unlock (CMD42[1Fh]) is required after power-on reset. CMD42 handles password setting, clearing, locking, unlocking, Force Erase, and FEP Force Erase. ACMD6 is rejected when the card is locked.

The APP_CMD (CMD55) command causes the card to interpret the following command as an application-specific command (ACMD). The switch function command (CMD6) switches or expands card functions across function groups including Access Mode, Command System, Driver Strength, and Power Limit, with Mode 0 for checking support and Mode 1 for setting functions. High-Speed mode achieves 25 MB/sec interface speed at a 50 MHz clock via CMD6. CMD8 checks whether the card can operate on the host supply voltage and is required for cards compliant with Version 2.00 or later.

SDHC and SDXC cards use block address format (512-byte units) while SDSC uses byte addresses; SDHC/SDXC disable partial and misalign access. The host may lower or stop the bus clock, with restrictions during ACMD41 and a requirement to provide 8 clock cycles after transactions. CRC7 protects commands and responses; CRC16 protects data blocks. Commands have a fixed 48-bit length and are organized into Card Command Classes (CCC), with classes 0, 2, 4, 5, and 8 mandatory. Timeout conditions are defined for read (100 ms), write (250 ms, up to 500 ms for SDXC in certain cases), and erase operations.

As tensions escalate on the Korean Peninsula, Korean War veteran John Bishop doubts Canada could again play a pivotal role like it did at the Battle of Kapyong 66 years ago. Former ambassador Marius Grinius says Canada's "controlled engagement" policy under the previous Conservative government cut diplomatic ties with North Korea, costing it influence. North Korea has defied six Security Council resolutions with nuclear and missile tests, including one that failed last weekend. U.S. Vice-President Mike Pence, visiting the DMZ, declared "the era of strategic patience is over." Veterans and scholars argue Canada must act, citing humanitarian suffering in North Korea and the legacy of 27,000 Canadians who served, 516 of whom died.

October 2025 features a supermoon on October 6, appearing up to 30% brighter and 14% larger than a typical full moon because it coincides with perigee, when the moon is closest to Earth. October 4 marks International Observe the Moon Night. The Draconid meteor shower, produced by debris from comet 21P Giacobini-Zinner, peaks around October 8 with up to 10 meteors per hour, radiating from the constellation Draco. The Orionid meteor shower, caused by Halley's Comet debris, peaks October 21 with about 20 meteors per hour; its full duration runs September 26 to November 22, with best viewing before midnight to 2 am during the new moon.

This MIT lecture by James W. Swan covers eigenvalue decomposition as part of a linear algebra unit, following a prior lecture on Gaussian elimination.

The lecture begins with administrative notes, including a correction to a typo in homework 1. The instructor then revisits reordering systems of equations using permutation matrices, which swap rows when multiplied from the left and columns when multiplied from the right by their transpose. Permutation matrices are unitary (their transpose equals their inverse), and reordering serves as a form of preconditioning—either to minimize numerical error through pivoting or to minimize fill-in so large sparse systems remain solvable in memory.

Using a Plinko game as a diffusion model, the instructor demonstrates a sparse matrix with two diagonals of one-half that spreads probability 50/50 to neighboring cells. Repeated multiplication flattens the distribution toward uniform, and special distributions satisfying AA·P = P are identified as eigenvectors of AA.

The core content defines eigenvectors as vectors that, when multiplied by a matrix, are only stretched (not redirected), with the eigenvalue being the stretch factor. Eigenvectors are not unique—only their direction matters—while eigenvalues are unique. Eigenvalues are found by solving det(A − λI) = 0, the characteristic polynomial of degree N, whose N roots are the eigenvalues. For diagonal and triangular matrices, the diagonal elements are the eigenvalues. Properties include: a real matrix has at most N distinct eigenvalues; complex eigenvalues occur in conjugate pairs; the determinant equals the product of eigenvalues; and the trace equals their sum. A chemical reaction rate matrix example shows eigenvalue 0 corresponding to steady state and −k1 to the A-to-B transformation.

Eigenvectors are found via Gaussian elimination on A − λI, which is rank deficient. The geometric multiplicity (dimension of the null space) is always less than or equal to the algebraic multiplicity of an eigenvalue. When these multiplicities match for all eigenvalues, the matrix has a complete set of eigenvectors and can be diagonalized as A = WΛW⁻¹, enabling easy solution of systems of equations (x = WΛ⁻¹W⁻¹b) and decoupling of linear systems of ODEs into independent exponential solutions. For symmetric matrices with normalized eigenvectors, W⁻¹ = Wᵀ, and eigenvectors are orthogonal. Computers find eigenvalues using the Lanczos algorithm, a Krylov subspace method requiring order N³ operations. When a complete eigenvector set is absent, alternatives include Jordan normal form, Schur decomposition, and singular value decomposition, the last of which will be covered in the next lecture.

Taylor Swift has broken numerous records throughout her career. At 17, she became the youngest artist to write and perform a No. 1 song on the Hot Country Songs chart with "Our Song," and in 2009 she was the youngest person to win entertainer of the year at the CMA Awards. In 2010, she became the youngest artist to win the Grammy for album of the year with "Fearless," and she is now the most-awarded album of the year winner in history, becoming the first artist to win four times with "Midnights" in 2024. She holds the most American Music Awards (40) and the most song of the year Grammy nominations. Her "All Too Well (10 Minute Version)" is the longest song to reach No. 1, and she is the only artist to claim all top 10 entries on the Billboard Hot 100 in a single week. Her Eras Tour grossed $2 billion, making it the highest-grossing music tour ever, and her estimated net worth is $1.6 billion. Her latest album, "The Life of a Showgirl," broke Spotify's record for most-streamed album in a single day, and its single "The Fate of Ophelia" became the most-streamed song in a single day in Spotify history.

The exponential moving average (EMA) is a moving average indicator that places greater weight on recent data points, making it more responsive to price changes than the simple moving average (SMA). Backtests of four EMA strategies on the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) indicate that EMA strategies can be profitable. In the short term, mean-reversion works best: buying when the close crosses below a short-term EMA and selling when it closes above. A 5-day EMA produced a 7.41% CAGR with a 30.54% maximum drawdown. In the long run, trend-following works best: buying when the close crosses above a long-term EMA and selling when it closes below. A 200-day EMA returned 7.84% with a maximum drawdown of 26%, about half that of buy-and-hold. Strategies that exit after N days showed the best result was buying below the 50-day EMA and selling after 200 days, producing 10.17% per trade. The EMA is calculated using the formula EMA = (K x (C – P)) + P, where K is a smoothing constant based on the selected period. As a lagging indicator, the EMA cannot predict future prices and may generate false signals if the period is shortened. The main conclusion is that EMA strategies work best with either a low number of days for mean reversion or a high number of days for trend following.

The authors conducted a systematic literature review of 16 selected Information Systems journals for papers published between 2000 and 2017, searching titles, abstracts, and keywords for the terms "digital business strategy," "digital transformation," and "business digitalization." The search initially returned 292 articles, reduced to 54 through title, abstract, and keyword assessment, and then to 28 after full-text examination. Following Wolifswinkel's guidelines, the articles were analyzed through open, axial, and selective coding, yielding 12 dimensions for digital transformation, 6 for digital business strategy, and 10 for organizational capabilities. Publication activity increased from 2009 and rose considerably in 2016, with research concentrated in the automotive, banking, telecommunications, healthcare, oil and gas, and manufacturing sectors, and geographically focused on the US and Europe. The review identified overlapping dimensions among the three concepts, with "external collaboration of ecosystem of digital platforms" common to all. The study proposes a conceptual framework in which digital business strategy acts as a blueprint for digital transformation, supported by organizational capabilities, and aims to assist C-suite management and IS researchers.

The editors of the Foreign Relations series have complete access to retired Department of State records, and the Department's 1981–1989 central and decentralized files will eventually be transferred to the National Archives for use after declassification. Research also relies on special access to restricted documents at the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library and other agencies. Although all printed material is declassified, some is extracted from still-classified documents being processed by the Reagan Library. Some records were scanned under the Remote Archives Capture project, sometimes leaving editors unable to confirm whether attachments were present, noted as "Not found attached." Documents are presented chronologically by Washington DC time and reproduced as exactly as possible, with bracketed insertions marking corrections, additions, and omitted or still-classified text.

April the giraffe's livestream is YouTube's second-most-watched live channel, behind Riot Games' League of Legends. Since Feb. 10, it has logged over 232 million live views, peaking at 1.2 million simultaneous viewers during the calf's Saturday birth.

This paper addresses multi-period resource allocation under stochastic demands, a multi-period extension of the newsvendor problem with applications in supply chain management, dynamic pricing, healthcare planning, and energy dispatch. The static formulation, where all allocations are fixed at the start, is a convex problem solved efficiently via bisection on the dual variable using only marginal demand distributions; however, it ignores temporal correlations and information revealed as demands are realized. The authors propose a sequential, adaptive shrinking horizon policy, similar to model predictive control, that re-solves the allocation problem at each time step while conditioning the joint distribution of future demands on observed demands. Though a heuristic without global optimality guarantees, this closed-loop approach is designed to improve upon the static solution. For independent demands, the sequential policy provably reduces to the static solution. Simulations on synthetic jointly log-normal demands show the sequential method achieves higher revenue than the static solution, performs close to a non-causal oracle upper bound, and outperforms a roll-forward baseline. The method requires only conditional quantile functions and applies to any demand model. Future work includes incorporating the algorithm in a closed loop where the demand distribution is learned.

This paper examines the cultural elements of digital transformation, noting that while technological aspects are well studied, cultural changes are the most difficult to introduce and enforce. Research surveying over ~150 firms across major verticals, categorized as digital "leaders" or "laggards" based on 100+ technology characteristics, found that tech intensity correlates with business performance, with leaders outperforming laggards on 3-year revenue and enterprise value CAGR.

Based on conversations with both groups, the authors identify four cultural themes of data-driven firms: adopting a growth mindset toward risk and continuous learning; using data to create shared context, collaboration, and transparency; empowering teams to examine data against realistic, measurable goals; and using common targets and objective measurements to align the organization while granting teams autonomy.

Digital leaders encourage sensible risk-taking and experimentation, treat unsuccessful experiments as learning opportunities, invest in long-term training (including critical thinking skills), share data widely with appropriate governance controls, and use data-driven metrics that provide flexibility. Digital laggards prioritize short-term efforts, discourage risk, hoard data as a source of power, favor a "culture of genius" over data-driven decisions, and set aspirational goals ungrounded in data, instead emphasizing process adherence.

Case studies include a pharmaceutical company that fostered localized experimentation within a regulated industry, automating compliance checks in a quarter of the previous time, and a retail company that implemented real-time sales reporting enabling data-driven decisions. Data culture aligns organizations both vertically and horizontally, and digital leaders treat it as central to their business. Firms typically fit one of four patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, or data reliant—and can take targeted actions to build a strong data culture.

Five-year-old Lyla Carreyn, who received a kidney from her 4K teacher Beth Battista, was discharged Saturday night after hospitalization since February 21 and post-surgery complications. She now enjoys footie pajamas and unrestricted water, but faces over 15 daily medications, thrice-weekly labs, and possible re-admission.

This article examines the impacts of anti-Critical Race Theory (CRT) bans on Native content instruction in teacher education at predominantly white institutions (PWIs) in Utah and Idaho, drawing on the authors' experiences as teacher educators and public educators in tribal, urban, and rural Arizona schools. Using Bryan Brayboy's Tribal Critical Race Theory (TribalCrit)—particularly the tenets that colonization is endemic to society and that educational policies toward Native peoples are linked to assimilation—the authors analyze stories, interviews, and observations from IRB-approved research projects. The article profiles anti-CRT legislation in Idaho (HB 377), Utah (S.R. 901/H.R. 901), and Arizona (HB 2898), noting that 42 states had introduced or passed such legislation and that the teacher workforce is overwhelmingly white.

The analysis identifies three impacts of CRT bans: continued silencing of Native perspectives and content, perpetuation of Native invisibilization in public education, and refusal to learn culturally sustaining pedagogies. Examples include a superintendent citing HB 377 to cancel culturally responsive training in a district serving a 70% Native population, unimplemented Arizona laws mandating Native history instruction, white pre-service teachers' resistance to diversity coursework, and state standards referencing Native peoples almost exclusively before 1860. The authors conclude that whitewashed settler narratives and European American power structures dominate U.S. education through colonial unknowing, and argue that critical democratic education must recognize Native nationhood and sovereignty and teach Native history and content at all levels of public education.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on September 4, 2020, it completed the sale of $5.0 billion (before commissions) of its common stock through its at-the-market offering program previously disclosed on September 1, 2020. Final settlement of the shares sold is expected by September 9, 2020. The report was signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn on September 8, 2020.

This study characterizes spatiotemporal variation in self-reported face mask-wearing across U.S. counties from September 2020 to May 2021 using the COVID-19 Trends and Impact Survey (CTIS), distributed via Facebook. Because such surveys suffer from non-representative sampling, non-response, and social desirability biases, the authors applied Bayesian binomial regression models, raking and resampling by age, sex, and education, and bias correction based on discrepancies between self-reported and ground-truth vaccination data. Bias-corrected masking proportions ranged from 0.11 to 0.96, showed high spatial heterogeneity (Moran's I 0.68–0.70), and were positively associated with population density, with urban counties masking more than rural ones. Masking peaked in January 2021 and declined sharply by May 2021, coinciding with rising vaccination, declining cases, lifted mask mandates, and CDC guidance changes. Community-reported masking estimates closely matched bias-corrected self-reported estimates, suggesting community-level questions may reduce survey bias. The findings indicate that one-size-fits-all masking policies are likely ineffective and support geographically targeted public health approaches and locally informed disease models. Limitations include unmeasured biases (e.g., political leanings, Facebook-user differences) and the assumption that masking responses are biased like vaccination responses. The authors present these as the first high-resolution spatiotemporal estimates of U.S. mask-wearing during the pandemic.

In this lecture, Russ Tedrake discusses walking robots, arguing that the fundamental challenge is control rather than actuators or power density. Two key technical hurdles in applying optimal control to walking are limit cycles and impacts (hybrid dynamics). Using the Van der Pol oscillator as an example, he explains limit cycle stability and introduces the Poincaré map technique, which converts continuous-time limit cycle stability into discrete-time fixed point stability. He reviews the history of locomotion research, including Muybridge's gait photography, McMahon's ballistic walker model, and Tad McGeer's passive dynamic walkers—machines with no motors or controllers that walk down ramps. The rimless wheel, described as the only walking system fully understood analytically, demonstrates the essential dynamics of walking: energy gained from descending a slope balances energy lost through inelastic ground collisions, producing a stable limit cycle. Collision losses dominate walking energetics, and push-off just before collision can reportedly improve efficiency fourfold. The lecture concludes with the compass gait and kneed walker models, which extend the rimless wheel concept but have more limited regions of stability, and previews applying optimization methods to hybrid dynamics in the next session.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC dated May 9, 2017, reporting under Item 2.02 that it issued a press release announcing financial results for the quarter ended April 30, 2017 (first quarter fiscal 2018). The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1, and a CFO Commentary by Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Colette M. Kress is attached as Exhibit 99.2 and will be posted to investor.nvidia.com. These materials are furnished rather than filed and are not incorporated by reference into other SEC filings. The report was signed by Colette M. Kress on May 9, 2017.

In his second inaugural address, the President says an extended speech is unnecessary since the war's progress is well known. Four years earlier both parties sought to avert civil war, yet war came. Slavery, localized in the South, caused the conflict, though neither side anticipated its magnitude or duration. Both sides prayed to the same God, and he suggests the war may be divine woe for the offense of slavery, possibly continuing until the wealth of unrequited toil is sunk and blood is paid with blood. He urges finishing the work with malice toward none, charity for all, binding the nation's wounds, and achieving a just and lasting peace.

Sven Henrich agrees with Alan Greenspan's January 2018 claim that both stock and bond bubbles exist, arguing critics citing Greenspan's 1996 "irrational exuberance" call miss that timing doesn't invalidate the premise. Henrich highlights a ratio chart of the 10-year yield versus the S&P 500 showing precise technical correlation. The ratio bottomed near 2008/2009 lows, rose until mid-2016, then broke its trend line after the US election. Falling stocks and rising yields suggest a potential multi-year head and shoulders pattern implying the post-2016 rally was a blow-off top. Henrich isn't calling for immediate collapse but warns bulls need yields to drop soon, though short-term hope exists as the ratio nears critical support.

The article presents a simple trend following system for gold using a 12-month (250-day) moving average, tested from 1971 onward after the dollar left the Bretton Woods system. The strategy goes long when gold is above the moving average and stays in cash when below. In backtesting, 100,000 invested in 1971 grew to 10 million, versus 4 million for buy and hold, across 26 trades, excluding slippage and commissions. Best results occurred around the 12-month average (equivalent to 200–250 days on a daily timeframe). The system works mainly by avoiding large drawdowns, such as after the 1980 and 2012 tops. Practical implementation is via the GLD ETF or gold futures. The authors conclude trend following in gold has worked well, though without guarantees.

This study evaluated the Disk Potentiation Test (DPT) for detecting KPC and MBL carbapenemases among 147 imipenem-resistant gram-negative isolates collected from Evercare Hospital, Dhaka, between January and June 2020. All isolates showed 100% resistance to imipenem, with the highest resistance observed in patients over 60 years and in the ICU. Acinetobacter baumannii was the predominant carrier of both enzymes. Among the isolates, 26.53% carried KPC and 44.89% tested positive for MBL, with the highest prevalence in the ICU. Tracheal aspirates had the highest number of samples with both enzymes. The findings underscore the need for antimicrobial stewardship and infection control measures in healthcare settings.

This passage is from the Texas Instruments datasheet (SLASFA2A, November 2024, revised April 2025) for the MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 microcontrollers. It presents electrical and switching characteristics for the ADC, comparator, DAC, SPI, UART, and timers, including notes on internal/external reference configuration and ADC sampling-time equations. The detailed description section covers the device architecture: an ARM Cortex-M0+ CPU operating from 32kHz to 80MHz; five operating modes (RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, SHUTDOWN) across two power domains; a power management unit; a clock module with multiple oscillators and a PLL; a 12-channel DMA; an event manager; flash memory up to 512kB with ECC plus 16kB data flash; up to 128kB of SRAM in two banks; up to 93 GPIO pins; 12-bit 4Msps ADCs; a temperature sensor; a VREF module; comparators with 8-bit reference DACs; a 12-bit DAC; security features (AES accelerator, keystore, CRC, TRNG, firewalls); a math accelerator; UART, I2C, SPI, and CAN-FD interfaces; a low-frequency subsystem containing an RTC and independent watchdog; general-purpose and advanced timers; a serial wire debug interface; a bootstrap loader protected by a 256-bit password; and factory constants. The document concludes with application layout recommendations (decoupling capacitors, NRST pullup, ROSC resistor, VCORE capacitor), development tool and documentation support, device nomenclature, a revision history detailing the April 2025 specification updates, and mechanical packaging information.

A hockey coach discusses his team's playoff series against Detroit. He notes the powerplay generated chances in recent games and expects Sami to see more time, while stressing the need to manage defensemen's minutes in tight games. He credits Sean, who left as an emerging player and returned as a veteran, for injecting a positive attitude and leadership into the locker room during a four-game losing streak. On overtime ice time, he says the Brind'Amour and Francis lines matched Detroit's Yzerman line, with extra shifts going to Vasicek's line. He describes Roddy as low-maintenance, says Eric Cole stopped being treated like a rookie in December, and worries his line has drifted from getting pucks to the net. The two days off will help reset emotions and address technical options, and the team must return to a grinding style after opening up its game in frustration.

Kenneth Kaylor appeals a marriage dissolution judgment, contending the rehabilitative alimony awarded to Sharon Kaylor exceeded his ability to pay. The trial court gave appellee custody, exclusive use of the home, $4,800 yearly alimony for two years, $7,800 yearly child support, half the house expenses, an automobile, the children's medical expenses, and life insurance. Finding the total award exceeded appellant's approximately $2,000 monthly net income and provided appellee more than her stated needs, the court reversed the financial aspects and remanded, affirming all other aspects.

The passage describes several AMD AGESA™ software procedures. AMD_ENABLE_STACK is a "stackless" native assembler routine using a register-passing interface that initializes the processor and cache system to establish a pre-memory stack region, divided among processor cores, mapped to global address space with MTRRs set accordingly; it must run on all cores and returns AGESA_SUCCESS, a warning for stack re-entry, or a fatal error for unknown processor families. AMD_DISABLE_STACK removes the pre-memory stack, preserves EBX (usable as a return address), disables CAR mode without modifying MTRR settings, flushes all cache lines, and should be invoked once by the BSP when main memory becomes available. AmdCreateStruct creates and pre-initializes storage for parameter structures using PreMemHeap, PostMemDram, or host-pre-allocated methods, and requires a stack. Additional procedures return DIMM data eye bitmaps (31 elements of 32 bits), APIC addresses for specified processor cores (x86-64 only), and the cache size available for execution caching during the pre-memory timeframe. AARCH64 APUs with the Platform Security Processor do not use the stack or early macros, as the PSP initializes DRAM.

This study examines the scope, importance, and role of curriculum literacy in education and the factors hindering its development. Using thematic content analysis, the researchers analyzed 29 peer-reviewed articles in English and Turkish retrieved from the Scopus database with the keyword "curriculum literacy." Findings show that research on curriculum literacy increased steadily, from 5 studies before 2000 to 89 studies between 2020 and 2025, with keyword trends shifting from basic concepts (2010–2015) to activity theory and culture (2015–2020), and then to dyslexia, diagnosis, and empowerment (2020–2025). Social sciences dominated the field (24 studies), while other disciplines were minimally represented. Australia and the United States hosted the most studies (8 each), followed by Türkiye (6). The findings indicate a positive but weak relationship between teachers' digital literacy and curriculum literacy, and highlight curriculum literacy's role in improving pedagogical skills, supporting inclusive and equitable education—particularly for low-income students—and integrating 21st-century skills. The study concludes that curriculum literacy is a critical skill set enabling effective use of digital technologies and pedagogical strategies, and recommends expanding research beyond social sciences, providing teachers with digital resources and training, and adopting interdisciplinary approaches. It suggests teacher training on digital platforms and teaching materials to support digital transformation and improve educational quality.

This paper examines the current state and potential of digitalization in Vietnamese higher education (HE) and proposes recommendations for higher education institutions (HEIs). Government policy has driven digital transformation; before COVID-19, digitalization was slow and uneven, but the pandemic accelerated progress. Vietnam has 237 universities (172 public, 67 private), overseen mainly by MOET, with centrally regulated curricula. Key policies include the 2020 National Digital Transformation Program (toward 2025, vision 2030) and the 2022–2025 Project, which set targets for distance learning platforms, digitalized materials, shared data warehouses, and technology-based management. Before COVID-19, despite favorable telecommunications infrastructure, challenges included low digital skills, underfunding, fragmented governance, and limited investment in e-learning; most HEIs had learning management systems, but few offered distance education. Since the pandemic, MOET has allowed up to 30% online content in Bachelor programs and 50% online assessment, and e-learning and blended learning have become widespread. National database systems and digital repositories of lectures, theses, and question banks have been developed. Recommendations include clearer policy guidance from MOET, increased government funding and infrastructure support, leadership training, and HEI support for lecturers (intellectual property, pedagogy, digital skills, personalized learning, mentorship) and students (digital skills training, paperless administration). Digitalization varies among HEIs but is advancing steadily.

AMD stock surged 23.71% on Monday after OpenAI and AMD announced a deal that could give OpenAI a 10% stake in the chipmaker. OpenAI will deploy up to 6 gigawatts of AMD Instinct GPUs over multiple years, beginning with a 1-gigawatt rollout in the second half of 2026. AMD issued OpenAI a warrant for up to 160 million shares, with vesting tied to deployment volume and share price milestones. AMD said the deal is worth billions but declined to disclose a specific amount. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at record highs, helped by AMD's gains, while Nvidia shares fell 1%. OpenAI President Greg Brockman said the company is unable to launch some revenue-generating features due to a lack of compute power.

The Nasdaq 100 E-mini futures is an electronically traded contract based on the Nasdaq 100 index, composed of the largest 100 non-financial companies on the Nasdaq exchange, primarily technology stocks. It debuted on June 21, 1999, is one-fifth the size of the full Nasdaq futures contract, trades on the CME Globex platform from Sunday 6:00 p.m. to Friday 5:00 p.m. ET, expires quarterly (March, June, September, December), and is cash-settled on the third Friday of the contract month. One contract equals the index value multiplied by $20. A trading strategy involves fundamental and technical analysis, risk management, and position sizing; the article backtests a volatility strategy with three buy variables and one sell variable. Prices are affected by Fed rate decisions, component prices, economic news, and the US Dollar Index, and the contract performs better in Spring and Fall. The all-time high is 16,676.50 (November 2021) and the all-time low is 797.50 (October 3, 2002). The main risk comes from leverage, as losses are calculated on the index value rather than the deposited margin.

The speaker describes winning the Stanley Cup with Washington as a special moment, especially lifting it with Alex, with whom he shares a similar story. He praises the group, including Ovi and Backie, for changing narratives and coming back in every series they trailed. Baseline and demographic characteristics were comparable between the Primary SOC and Additional Educational Program groups. Subjects had a median age of 74 years, were mostly male (59.9%), predominantly had atrial fibrillation (96.4%), with hypertension (87.2%) most frequent.

A player credits Kesler's pass to Hansen for his goal. Tube UK supplied ten audio systems for five carnival floats and five music/compere stages at Manchester's 2017 Manchester Day celebrations, commissioned by Manchester City Council and produced by Walk the Plank. A nine-person team led by Melvyn Coote completed the setup in one day. Four floats used battery-powered systems, mostly Tannoy and D&B equipment, while Graham Massey's float ran on an on-board generator. City centre stage PAs, including the largest at Cathedral Gardens for over 2,000 people, used D&B systems with Yamaha consoles.

A 29-year-old man, Jonathan Rinderknecht, has been charged with starting the fire that destroyed much of Los Angeles' Pacific Palisades neighborhood and became the most destructive blaze in LA history. Authorities allege he lit a fire on New Year's Day that was extinguished but continued smoldering underground before reigniting in high winds. Arrested in Florida, he faces charges including malicious destruction by means of fire. Investigators determined the Jan. 1 fire was intentionally lit, likely with a lighter, and found a barbecue-style lighter in his car. He allegedly fled the scene, returned to film it, made 911 calls, and lied during an interview. The Jan. 7 blaze killed 12 people and destroyed more than 6,000 homes and buildings. The cause of a second blaze remains undetermined, and a September review found weaknesses hampered the county's emergency response.

A bear trap is a bullish trading pattern in which a sudden price drop tricks traders into believing a downtrend is continuing, only for the price to reverse and rise. It occurs in an uptrend when a bearish candle breaks a significant low, taking sellers out of position before the former trend resumes. Market manipulators (market makers or liquidity providers) contribute to bear traps by placing large sell orders to push prices down and then buying back at lower prices, while retail traders' stop-loss orders can amplify the drop through a feedback loop. Bear traps can be spotted using technical indicators such as RSI and MACD divergences, breaks of support levels, and fundamental signals like positive earnings reports. To avoid them, traders should backtest strategies, consider fundamentals alongside price, avoid following the crowd, and resist FOMO-driven decisions. A backtested strategy on QQQ produced 181 trades with a 1.7% average gain, 13% CAGR, 80% win rate, and 20% maximum drawdown.

Pets at Home in Burton is holding an autism hour on Sunday, October 8, an hour before opening, as part of the National Autistic Society's UK-first week-long event to give autistic people a break from information overload. The store will dim lights, turn down music and till bells, and share autism information with employees. Over 340 stores are participating, including one in Uttoxeter.

The passage describes the NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture. Turing improves on Pascal's lossless memory compression, and combined with GDDR6 bandwidth increases, delivers approximately 50% higher effective bandwidth (e.g., RTX 2080 Ti vs. GTX 1080 Ti). A new display engine supports 8K at 60 Hz via DisplayPort 1.4a with VESA DSC 1.2, native HDR processing with ITU-R BT.2100 tone mapping, an enhanced NVENC encoder (HEVC 8K at 30 fps, up to 25% HEVC and 15% H.264 bitrate savings), and an updated NVDEC supporting HEVC 4:4:4 and VP9 10/12-bit HDR. Turing adds hardware support for USB Type-C and VirtualLink, delivering power, display, and data to VR headsets over a single USB-C connector. TU102 and TU104 use second-generation NVLink (25 GB/sec per direction per link) instead of MIO/PCIe for SLI, supporting two-way SLI only.

Turing introduces RT Cores within each SM that accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection, achieving 10+ Giga Rays/sec versus Pascal's ~1.1 in software—roughly 10x faster—enabling real-time ray tracing via a hybrid rendering model combining rasterization and ray tracing, aided by denoising. NGX, a deep learning stack using Tensor Cores, provides DLSS (trained on 64x supersampled images, matching TAA quality with roughly half the shading work and enabling 2x GTX 1080 Ti performance), InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. New graphics features include Mesh Shading (Task and Mesh shaders with cooperative thread models, eliminating CPU draw call bottlenecks), Variable Rate Shading (per-16x16-pixel shading rates enabling Content Adaptive Shading, Motion Adaptive Shading, and Foveated Rendering), Texture Space Shading (decoupled shading in texture space with texel reuse), and Multi-View Rendering (up to four views per pass, expanding Pascal's SMP). Turing also supports DX12 Tier 3 bindless resource views and Tier 2 resource heaps.

The TU104 (six GPCs, 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, 13.6B transistors) powers GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000; the TU106 (36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores, 10.8B transistors) powers GeForce RTX 2070 without NVLink/SLI. RTX-OPS is introduced as a workload-based metric weighting Tensor (20%), FP32 (80%), RT (40%), and INT32 (28%) operations, totaling 78 for RTX 2080 Ti. An appendix explains ray tracing mechanics, BVH acceleration structures, denoising, and ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, with examples from Battlefield V and Shadow of the Tomb Raider. The document concludes with legal disclaimers, trademark notices, and a 2018 NVIDIA copyright.

Samsung's Chromebook Pro, launching in April, runs Android apps from the Google Play Store as Google merges Chrome OS with Android. The UC1825B-SP controller supports standard power conversion topologies such as push-pull, forward, half-bridge, and full bridge. The passage provides PCB layout guidance: use low-EMI ferrite-core inductors; route feedback traces away from noise sources, ideally on the opposite PCB side with a ground plane; place input, output, and compensation capacitors close to the IC, preferably surface-mount; keep power traces short, direct, and thick (minimum 15 mils per ampere); position the inductor, output capacitors, and diode close together; use ground planes on both sides, with one via per 200 mA on multilayer boards; and orient switching current loops in the same direction to reduce EMI. A dedicated power ground is required for high di/dt output currents, with VCC and VREF bypassed using low ESR/ESL ceramic capacitors. The document also covers documentation updates, TI E2E support, ESD precautions, and mechanical/packaging information with associated disclaimers.

This passage is a contents listing for documents on American plans and preparations for the Peace Conference, covering the organization and work of "The Inquiry" from August 1917 through November 1918, with dates, locations, and file references. This passage is from datasheet SLASFJ6A (July 2025, revised September 2025) for the Texas Instruments MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 microcontrollers. "Standard with Wake" I/Os can wake the device from SHUTDOWN mode. The 48-pin LQFP (PT) package has two configurations, PT (A) and PT (B). Section 7 provides electrical specifications, including absolute maximum ratings, recommended operating conditions (32MHz with one flash wait state, 24MHz with zero wait states), thermal metrics, supply current, POR/BOR conditions, flash characteristics (1KB sectors; up to 100,000 program/erase cycles on 32 sectors and 10,000 on the remainder), oscillator timing (SYSOSC, LFOSC, HFXT), digital I/O characteristics, ADC specifications (12-bit, up to 1.6Msps, 10.6-bit ENOB with external reference), temperature sensor, VREF (1.4V/2.5V), comparator, I2C, SPI, and UART specifications.

Section 9 recommends 10µF and 0.1µF decoupling capacitors on VDD/VSS, a 47kΩ pullup with 1000pF pulldown on NRST, and pullup resistors for 5V-tolerant open-drain I/Os. Section 10 covers development tools, device nomenclature, documentation, and support resources. The revision history notes changes from July to September 2025, including removal of the DGS32 package, specification updates, updated CPU features, ADC ENOB edits, an added DEBUGSS section, and updated DEVICEID/USERID tables. The lecture reviews two prior results—a sequence converges to x if and only if |xₙ − x| → 0, and the squeeze theorem—and states the binomial theorem without proof. Using these, three special limits are proved: for positive p, lim 1/nᵖ = 0; for positive p, lim p^(1/n) = 1; and lim n^(1/n) = 1. The instructor notes that positive real numbers raised to real powers can be defined using only the least upper bound property and density of the rationals, without invoking exponentials or logarithms.

The lecture then defines the limsup and liminf of a bounded sequence as the limits of the suprema and infima of its tails. A theorem establishes that these limits always exist, since the sequence of suprema is monotone decreasing and bounded, and the sequence of infima is monotone increasing and bounded; additionally, liminf ≤ limsup. Examples: for (−1)ⁿ, the limsup is 1 and the liminf is −1; for 1/n, both equal 0.

It is then proved that every bounded sequence has subsequences converging to its limsup and liminf, constructed by sandwiching terms between tail suprema and applying the squeeze theorem. This immediately yields the Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem: every bounded sequence has a convergent subsequence. Finally, a bounded sequence converges if and only if its limsup equals its liminf, in which case all three values coincide.

This retrospective single-center study from China compared intravenous thrombolysis with tenecteplase (120 patients, March–November 2023) versus alteplase (144 patients, January 2022–February 2023) in acute ischemic stroke patients treated within 4.5 hours of symptom onset. The tenecteplase group showed significantly shorter onset-to-treatment, door-to-needle, and door-to-puncture times, and higher proportions of patients meeting the 45-minute door-to-needle target (65.83% vs. 40.44%) and 120-minute door-to-puncture target (59.09% vs. 13.79%). Tenecteplase was an independent predictor of achieving both time targets. Clinically, the tenecteplase group had a higher rate of 24-hour NIHSS improvement (64.17% vs. 50%) and shorter hospital stays (6 vs. 8 days), while incidences of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and any intracranial hemorrhage did not differ significantly between groups. The authors attribute these advantages to tenecteplase's higher fibrin specificity, resistance to PAI-1, and rapid single-injection administration. Limitations include the single-center design, lack of randomization or blinding, reporting of only early outcomes, and a predominantly mild-to-moderate stroke population. The study concludes that tenecteplase offers workflow efficiency and early clinical benefits with safety comparable to alteplase, supporting its use in AIS thrombolysis pending larger multicenter trials.

The Western Association of Schools and Colleges Senior College and University Commission has dropped references to diversity, equity and inclusion from its standards. It began considering the change after President Trump's re-election, suspended the DEI standards, and, following public comment, adopted revisions to the 2023 standards. Other accreditors have suspended or are considering dropping DEI standards amid pressure from Trump directives.

The strategic position of the Sandwich Islands, fronting US possessions on the Pacific, gives them peculiar interest to the United States, which would not consent to their transfer to a powerful maritime or commercial nation. Hawaii's government shows a tendency toward decay, and many wealthy islanders desire annexation to the United States. Lacking accurate information on Hawaii's population, trade, resources, and debt, the Government requests full data and instructs its representative not to discourage annexation sentiment and to ascertain Hawaiian officials' views on the terms of such a project. After King Lunalilo died on February 3, 1874, without naming a successor, Kalakaua's election sparked riots; American forces landed at the Hawaiian government's request, while British forces landed without invitation, an incident later covered by an antedated note. In autumn 1874, King Kalakaua visited the United States to promote reciprocity negotiations, opposed by the English and French commissioners.

This qualitative study examines digitalization in education through semi-structured interviews with 20 expert-managers in education working in the private sector, with data collected via email and Zoom during the pandemic and analyzed using content analysis. Most participants (95%) worked in national companies, and 85% had 15 or more years of experience. Findings show challenges in digitalization were company-related (63%), such as technological problems and financial resources, and participant-related (37%), such as fear and resistance. To adapt, participants implemented online and hybrid training (65%), updated training content (40%), and used educational technologies (20%). Perceived positive effects included time- and location-independent access and savings (70%), equal opportunity and increased participant motivation (65%), and improved accessibility of educational content (60%). Negative effects included participant indifference and concentration problems (70%), lack of interactive face-to-face education (60%), and lower effectiveness than face-to-face training (25%). Participants defined digitalization in education mainly through technological opportunities (60%) and easy access (40%). The discussion links digitalization to Industry 4.0, notes the need for digitally literate teachers, and highlights risks including digital inequality, health problems, cyberattacks, and loss of social identity. The study concludes that although digitalization in education is inevitable and increasing, face-to-face education will not completely disappear, and institutions must adapt by using technological tools, virtual reality, and gamification.

The authors present an end-to-end workflow for inverse design of superconductors combining a guided diffusion generative model, high-throughput computational screening, and experimental validation. A DiffCSP-based foundation model was pretrained on ~2 million structures from the Alexandria Database to learn structural plausibility, then fine-tuned via an adapter module on 7,183 labeled superconductors to condition generation on target critical temperature (Tc) using classifier-free guidance. Validation showed guidance shifts generated Tc distributions toward in-domain targets (e.g., 10 K) but fails for out-of-distribution targets (110 K), where the structural prior constrains generation.

Applying the pipeline to 200,000 generated structures and filtering through ML relaxation, deduplication, metallicity, thermodynamic (Ehull < 200 meV/atom) and dynamical stability checks, and Tc prediction (BEE-NET, then DFT), the authors obtained 773 novel candidates with DFT-calculated Tc > 5 K—a 2.3% hit rate, ~135× higher than an element-substitution baseline and ~31× the absolute yield of a prior generative approach. Candidates skewed toward ternary and higher-order compositions.

For synthesis, 18 structurally diverse candidates were selected (ternaries, excluding technetium and substituted A15 variants, restricted to arc-meltable compositions) and arc-melted. Nine showed superconductivity above 4.2 K via dip-stick AC susceptibility, but measured Tc values were lower than predicted, and X-ray diffraction showed the predicted structures generally did not form, yielding instead disordered BCC solid solutions or multiphase mixtures of known binary phases.

The authors attribute these outcomes partly to incomplete convex hulls in underexplored chemistries, where predicted stability may reflect data scarcity rather than true synthesizability. Of 28 stable structures, 15 were completely novel, forming 7 structural families, the largest being substituted A15 (Cr₃Si-type) variants. Future directions include active learning with experimental feedback, cost and toxicity constraints, disorder-aware screening, on-the-fly DFT hull refinement, and alternative generative backbones and guidance schemes.

This patent application, a continuation of U.S. application Ser. No. 15/663,689 (filed Jul. 28, 2017), which claims benefit of U.S. Provisional Application Ser. No. 62/368,415 (filed Jul. 29, 2016), relates to a method and apparatus for channel state information (CSI) reporting for beam operation in wireless communication systems. The disclosed method, from a UE perspective, includes configuring the UE with at least two CSI-RS resources, performing measurements on those resources, generating multiple CSIs where at least one CSI corresponds to measurements on more than one CSI-RS resource, and reporting at least one generated CSI. The background describes the evolution of mobile networks toward IP packet communication, E-UTRAN, and ongoing 3GPP standardization of 5G. The detailed description covers MIMO transmitter/receiver system architecture, communication device structure, and beamforming techniques (digital, analog, and hybrid), noting that higher frequency bands require high-gain narrow beams formed by large antenna arrays to compensate for path loss. It further discusses TRP-based beam operation, mobility types, and CSI components (CQI, PMI, RI, CRI, PTI), and reproduces numerous tables from 3GPP TS 36.213 v13.1.1 governing aperiodic CSI reporting on PUSCH and periodic CSI reporting on PUCCH, including reporting modes, trigger conditions, subband sizes, and reporting periodicities across various transmission modes.

Maikel Kieftenbeld's appeal against the red card received during Birmingham City's 2-1 win over Bristol City was successful. He would have been banned for three matches but can now play against Bolton Wanderers.

A campaign called Zimbabwe Yadzoka/Mayibuye iZimbabwe has been launched to encourage Zimbabweans living in the Diaspora to return home and register to vote in the 2018 general election. This study used bibliometric analysis to determine the place of publications on "special education and mathematics" and "special education and mathematics education" in the literature. Using the Web of Science database and the bibliometrix R-Studio package, 487 English-language articles published between 1980 and 2023 were systematically analysed. Findings showed a notable increase in publications beginning in 2017, with most studies published in special education journals, particularly "Journal of Special Education" and "Remedial and Special Education". Bouck Ec was identified as the most influential author, and the most frequently used keywords were "students", "mathematics" and "children", reflecting that the participants of most studies were students and children. Collaboration networks revealed that the USA and the United Kingdom were the most active countries, while the University of Florida, Purdue University and Vanderbilt University stood out among institutions; however, author collaborations between different groups were very few. The study concluded that stronger collaborations among authors, countries and universities, the inclusion of teachers and families as participants, and further research on technology such as digital tools and artificial intelligence are important for future research. The study was limited to data obtained from the Web of Science database.

The paper proposes SynDoc, a hybrid framework for domain-specific Visually Rich Document Understanding (VRDU) that combines discriminative and generative models. SynDoc uses a synthetic data generation workflow combining OCR/PDF parsing with MLLM-driven multi-task inquiry generation and quality verification to create training data. It integrates a discriminative "warmer" model, built on vision-language pretrained backbones and adaptively tuned on synthetic datasets, with a generative MLLM for zero-shot question answering. The framework employs adaptive instruction tuning incorporating text, visual, layout, and structural features, plus a recursive inferencing mechanism where outputs from both models are iteratively refined through cross-feeding. Experiments on four datasets (FormNLU, CORD, Ephoie, FUNSD) using ANLS show that proprietary MLLMs generally outperform open-source ones, and that incorporating warmer knowledge improves MLLM performance on domain-specific datasets, though it may introduce noise in cross-domain settings. Ablations show meaningfulness verification aids tuning, structural adaptation improves results, Top-3 entity retrieval outperforms Top-1, and recursive inference enhances both warmer and MLLM performance, with OCR-challenging datasets requiring more iterations. The authors conclude that SynDoc effectively advances zero-shot domain-specific VRDU, though further work is needed for cross-domain generalizability.

This lecture covers constructing the spacetime of a compact, static, spherically symmetric body. The most general static spherically symmetric metric can be written diagonally (cross-terms removable by coordinate choice), using Schwarzschild coordinates where the radial coordinate is the areal radius, labeling spheres of surface area 4πr². Isotropic coordinates are noted as an alternative that matches the earlier weak-field solution.

For the exterior vacuum region, the Einstein equations reduce to Ricci = 0. Combining the tt and rr components gives φ = −λ, and the θθ equation integrates to φ = ½ ln(1 + a/r). Matching to the Newtonian weak-field limit of radial freefall fixes a = −2GM, yielding the Schwarzschild metric—the first exact solution to Einstein's field equations, derived by Karl Schwarzschild in 1916 while serving as an ill artillery officer on the Eastern Front; he died weeks after publishing it.

Birkhoff's theorem states that the exterior vacuum of any spherically symmetric body is described by the Schwarzschild metric, even if the source varies in time, provided spherical symmetry is preserved (such variations produce no gravitational waves). This is analogous to Gauss's law in electromagnetism.

For the interior, modeled as a static perfect fluid, the Einstein tensor yields a mass function m(r) defined by integrating 4πρ over radius. The baryonic mass (proper volume integral) generally exceeds the gravitational mass, the difference representing gravitational binding energy. Combining the rr equation with hydrostatic equilibrium produces the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff (TOV) equation. Three coupled differential equations, plus a chosen central density, an equation of state, and surface matching, determine the stellar spacetime. The next lecture will address solving these equations.

A Hamilton daycare is using bottled water and a filter after excessive lead was found. The passage describes the NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture and its key features. Turing GPUs include a new display engine supporting DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K resolution at 60 Hz, HDR processing, and VESA DSC 1.2 compression. An enhanced NVENC encoder adds H.265 8K encoding at 30 fps with bitrate savings, while NVDEC supports HEVC 4:4:4 and VP9 10/12-bit HDR decoding. Turing provides hardware support for USB Type-C and VirtualLink, delivering power, display, and data to VR headsets through a single connector. TU102 and TU104 GPUs use second-generation NVLink instead of MIO/PCIe for SLI transfers, providing 25 GB/sec per direction per link; 3-way and 4-way SLI are not supported.

Turing introduces RT Cores for hardware-accelerated ray tracing, performing BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing to achieve 10+ Giga Rays/Sec versus Pascal's 1.1, enabling real-time ray tracing. Hybrid rendering combines rasterization and ray tracing. NGX provides AI features using Tensor Cores, including DLSS (trained on 64x supersampled images), InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.

New rendering technologies include Mesh Shading (Task and Mesh Shaders that eliminate CPU draw call bottlenecks), Variable Rate Shading (adjustable per 16x16 pixel region, enabling content adaptive shading, motion adaptive shading, and foveated rendering), Texture Space Shading (decoupling shading from screen space), and Multi-View Rendering (up to four views per pass).

The TU104 contains 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores, and is used in GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. TU106 (GeForce RTX 2070) lacks NVLink and SLI support. The RTX-OPS metric weights peak operations by usage frequency. The document also covers ray tracing mechanics, comparisons of ray-traced versus traditional shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, and concludes with legal, trademark, and copyright notices.

He says his style is less unorthodox than the media suggests, crediting goalie coaches who taught him techniques without trying to change him. In this lecture, Yael T. Kalai first covers administration: a correction for pset problem 2B is posted on the website, next week is Thanksgiving, and the following week Jain Jin will guest-lecture on batch arguments (BARGs), leading into the final class on SNARGs.

The lecture then reviews the Fiat-Shamir paradigm, which eliminates interaction by replacing the verifier with a hash function. While the Kilian-Micali protocol is sound under Fiat-Shamir in the random oracle model, soundness with concrete hash functions was a long-standing open problem. Contrived counterexamples exist (including Kilian-Micali with certain collision-resistant hashes), but no real-world scheme proven secure in the random oracle model has been broken.

After recapping the zero-knowledge protocol for Hamiltonicity—committing to a random permutation of the graph, then opening either the cycle or the permutation plus nonedges depending on a challenge bit—which has soundness 1/2 and must be repeated in parallel with fresh permutations, the lecture presents the result of Canetti, Lombardi, and Wichs (2019): this parallel-repeated protocol is sound under Fiat-Shamir in the standard model using a specific hash function built from fully homomorphic encryption (FHE), assuming circular security (instantiable from circular-secure LWE).

The key idea: for each first message alpha there is a unique bad challenge beta that lets a cheating prover succeed, and computing beta_bad requires a trapdoor. The commitment is implemented via public-key encryption with a common reference string (a trusted public key whose secret key is discarded), opened by revealing encryption randomness; this gives a trapdoor that reveals beta_bad. Since publishing the trapdoor would break zero knowledge, the hash key instead contains an FHE encryption of a function g, and the hash evaluates g(alpha) homomorphically via a universal circuit. In the actual scheme, g is an all-zero circuit; in the analysis, semantic security lets g be replaced with g*, which uses the trapdoor to compute beta_bad, decrypts its output with the secret key, and XORs with 1, ensuring g*(alpha) never equals beta_bad(alpha)—otherwise decrypting both sides yields a contradiction. Because g* requires encrypting the secret key under its own public key, circular security is assumed; follow-up work removes this need using lattice techniques. The parameter T is the number of bits needed to represent g*.

Motivations include obtaining NIZKs from lattices (resolving a long-standing open question) and the technique's generality, applying to GKR, sum-check, and batch arguments. The lecture also addresses the apparent tension with zero knowledge: parallel repetition does not preserve zero knowledge, and the NIZK simulator has extra power, namely choosing the common reference string.

Nova Scotia has launched an online survey, open until Oct. 27, seeking input on marijuana legalization, including a proposed legal age of 19 and sales through a Crown corporation. Other provinces are also announcing plans, while Ottawa remains firm on its July 1 legalization date despite pushback.

A randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated SA58 nasal spray, a broad-spectrum anti-COVID-19 monoclonal antibody developed by Sinovac, as post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) in healthy adults within 72 hours of contact with SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals. The study was conducted at 21 construction sites in Beijing from November 26 to December 9, 2022, during an Omicron BF.7 outbreak. Of 1,634 participants randomized 3:1 to SA58 or placebo, 1,222 entered the full analysis set (901 SA58, 321 placebo); 99 baseline RT-PCR positive participants were excluded from efficacy analysis. SA58 reduced laboratory-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 by 80.82% (95% CI 52.41–92.27%), with 7 cases among 824 SA58 recipients versus 14 among 299 placebo recipients, and reduced SARS-CoV-2 infection by 61.83% (95% CI 37.50–76.69%). All 21 sequenced samples were Omicron BF.7. No severe COVID-19, deaths, serious adverse events, or adverse events of special interest occurred; adverse events were mild and similar between groups, most commonly nasal dryness, runny nose, and fever. The study ended early due to China's reopening, before the target sample size was reached. Limitations include a young, healthy population, concurrent isolation practices, and small sample size. Further evaluation in high-risk populations is recommended.

This April 16, 2001 email compiles news articles concerning Enron and energy markets. Carriers and trading companies, including Enron and Williams Communications, have produced multiple master bandwidth trading agreements after earlier failed attempts, though a firm-versus-best-efforts debate persists and most companies avoid public association with the effort. Sierra Pacific Resources' shares fell 8.3% after it suspended its dividend due to high western power costs; Nevada regulators approved a 17% rate increase, and the company still hopes to complete its purchase of Enron's Portland General Electric unit. Houston-based energy traders—Enron, Reliant, Dynegy, and Duke Energy—face antitrust probes and lawsuits alleging market manipulation in California, where utility bills have nearly quadrupled; energy trading received a blanket CFTC exemption in 1993, and Enron's fourth-quarter trading profit tripled to $538 million. Independent power producers including Williams, Calpine, Dynegy, and Mirant expect to meet or exceed first-quarter earnings forecasts despite unpaid California utility bills and FERC refund orders. Seattle City Light spent a record $92 million on power purchases in March, with Enron its largest supplier at $25.5 million, prompting a 28% rate increase and criticism of Enron's profits and political donations.

The analyst maintains a buy rating on Netflix but downgrades from High Conviction Buy, raising the price target to $160.73 from $144.46. The long-term thesis remains intact despite subdued upside. International growth is the key driver, with 52 million international subscribers by mid-year as the critical data point; Q2'17 guidance on this figure will determine whether estimates hold. The revenue estimate was raised to $11.285 billion from $10.9 billion, above consensus of $11.23 billion, and diluted EPS revised to $1.16 from $0.97. Contribution margin should improve as content costs grow slower than sales. With no other growth levers, expectation risk is heightened this quarter. Apple's media push poses potential competition, but the thesis is unchanged.

Cisco will participate in two February conferences: the Goldman Sachs Technology and Internet Conference (February 16, CEO Chuck Robbins) and the Morgan Stanley Technology, Media & Telecom Investor Conference (February 28, David Goeckeler). Aspetuck Land Trust will host three guided walks in April: a hawk walk with Larry Fischer on April 22 at Trout Brook Valley Preserve, a spring ephemerals wildflower walk with Anthony Zemba on April 23, and a stone walls walk with Alan Goldbecker on April 29 at Poindexter Preserve.
