British police declared a major incident after a man and woman in their 40s were found unconscious in Amesbury, near Salisbury, and are in critical condition from suspected exposure to an unknown substance. Initially thought drug-related, testing is ongoing, and reports suggest they may have been poisoned with the same nerve agent used on Sergei Skripal and his daughter in March. Counterterrorism officers are assisting, areas have been cordoned off, and officials see no significant public health risk.

This audit reviewed 74 TB-related mortality files from Kitwe Teaching Hospital (KTH), Zambia, between June 2018 and June 2019; 30 files were excluded due to deaths within 24 hours of admission or lack of clear TB confirmation. Most deaths occurred among males (67.6%), with a mean age of 39.2 years, among residents of high-density areas (83.8%), and among HIV-positive patients (81.1%). Common presenting symptoms included cough (41.9%), fever (40.5%), and diarrhea (29.7%). Pulse rate was elevated on admission (112.1 ± 29.7 per minute). Laboratory findings included anemia in 39.2%, hypoalbuminemia, renal dysfunction, and deranged liver enzymes, indicating multi-organ involvement. Radiological findings were infrequent, with miliary patterns most common (6.8%). The authors conclude that deaths were concentrated among young to middle-aged HIV-positive males in overcrowded areas presenting with unstable hemodynamics, and note that the retrospective file review with missing data was a limitation. They recommend early recognition of clinical instability among at-risk admitted TB patients and a prospective study to identify mortality predictors, including whether malignancy contributes to deaths in this setting.

Autoliv plans to spin off and list its electronics business by Q3 2018, with a cash injection to retain strong investment grade, while its airbag and seatbelt business keeps the Autoliv name. Shares have risen 20 percent since September.

On October 27, 2015, Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC announcing it issued a press release and related data sheet regarding its financial results for the fourth fiscal quarter ended September 26, 2015. The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1 and the data sheet as Exhibit 99.2. The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.
PPP's Taj Haider said Bilawal Bhutto Zardari will launch an aggressive election campaign in Punjab next week, starting from South Punjab, and demanded authorities conduct fair polls.

The Amazon experienced its most destructive fire season in over two decades in 2024, releasing a record 791 million tons of carbon dioxide—roughly equal to Germany's annual emissions and a sevenfold increase over the previous two years' average. A European Commission Joint Research Centre study found that, for the first time in the 2022–2024 analysis, fire-driven degradation overtook deforestation as the primary source of carbon emissions, with 3.3 million hectares of forest affected. Likely drivers include climate change-exacerbated drought, forest fragmentation, and land-use mismanagement. Brazil recorded its highest degradation emissions on record, while fires affected over 9% of Bolivia's remaining intact forest. The study urges reduced fire use, stronger forest protections, Indigenous stewardship support, and climate finance addressing degradation, not just deforestation.

Dell Technologies has signed a strategic agreement to expand its use of Salesforce's cloud-based CRM platform and sales and marketing apps to its global sales team of nearly 40,000. The deal gives Dell's customer contact centers access to Service Cloud Einstein, Salesforce's AI platform for customer service, and the companies will use Dell Boomi to share large volumes of data via the cloud. The partnership also supports Dell's global network of around 200,000 channel partners.
Multiple views of a portable fan design are described; broken lines depict unclaimed portions.

This patent application describes a nanosecond pulsed electric field (nsPEF) generator incorporating a feedback control system, intended for electrotherapy applications such as cancer treatment. The application claims priority to several related prior applications concerning high-voltage analog circuit pulsers.

The disclosed system includes a controller that generates power supply and pulse generator control signals, a power supply that produces power voltages, and a pulse generator that creates pulses based on these inputs. The controller receives feedback signals representing characteristics of the generated pulses and adjusts control signals accordingly, enabling adjustment of parameters such as supply voltage, pulse width, pulse number, frequency, and duty cycle in response to measured current, voltage, or temperature.

The pulse generator uses a Marx-switch stack hybrid circuit with MOSFET switches to produce high-voltage pulses (e.g., approximately 15 kV) with durations ranging from nanoseconds to microseconds. Multiple panels can be combined in parallel to scale current output. The passage describes electrode configurations, including seven-needle and two-pole suction electrodes that draw tumors into a chamber for treatment, as well as endoscope-based and balloon-mounted electrodes for internal tumors.

NsPEF treatment is described as inducing apoptosis in tumor cells and potentially stimulating an immune response against similar tumor cells. The document further outlines methods using feedback loops to control pulse amplitude, pulse width, tissue temperature, and delivered energy or power by comparing measured values against desired parameters and adjusting control values accordingly.

This patent application, a continuation of multiple prior applications, describes systems and methods for using mixed reality (MR) visualization in orthopedic surgical joint repair procedures. The disclosure covers techniques for preoperative planning, medical implant design and manufacture, intraoperative guidance, postoperative analysis, and surgical education, which may be used independently or in combination. The described orthopedic surgical system includes subsystems for virtual planning, planning support, manufacturing and delivery, intraoperative guidance, medical education, patient monitoring, and predictive analytics, connected via a communications network. An MR system comprises a visualization device (such as a head-worn device with see-through holographic lenses, e.g., a Microsoft HOLOLENS headset), processing devices, and memory, enabling users to view and manipulate 3D virtual models of patient anatomy and surgical plans overlaid on the real-world environment. The surgical lifecycle includes preoperative, manufacturing and delivery, intraoperative, and postoperative phases. The application describes user interfaces for shoulder arthroplasty procedures, including workflow pages for planning, grafting, humerus cutting, guide installation, glenoid reaming, and implant placement. Additional features include registration of virtual bone models with real patient anatomy, virtual guidance for surgical steps such as resection, reaming, drilling, and implant placement, tool identification, range-of-motion simulation to validate implant selection and positioning, and educational systems using MR/VR for training and patient communication.

Canada's S&P/TSX composite index hit a record high Wednesday, up 97.66 points to 16,414.19, led by gains in energy, financial, technology and health care sectors. The Senate passed the cannabis bill. U.S. indexes were mixed, while the loonie fell to 75.22 cents US amid rising U.S. interest rates and NAFTA trade fears.
NASA's TESS launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral on April 18, two days late, to find planets around nearby stars for follow-up by telescopes including the James Webb Space Telescope.

After a playoff loss, the team cited defensive lapses in the first period that put them behind early against a deep, fast opponent. They felt the third period was their best of the series, said offense wasn't the problem, and plan to tighten up defensively and apply pressure early next game. With each team having won its home games, they look forward to returning to Chicago, confident they can respond to adversity. One player reported feeling healthy and ready to return.

The Uzbek sum has gained about 9 percent against the dollar on the black market as exchange rate liberalisation appears imminent. Uzbekistan has abolished mandatory exporter currency sales, with remaining steps including full convertibility and aligning official and market rates. Currency controls have been cited as an obstacle to foreign investment.

The speaker, assuming the presidency, expresses humility and dedication to the office. He surveys national progress since the Great War, crediting Calvin Coolidge, but identifies increasing crime and weakening confidence in justice as the gravest danger. He attributes law enforcement failures partly to burdens from the eighteenth amendment but also to complicated judicial procedures that criminals exploit, and calls for reform of the federal justice system. He proposes a national commission to investigate federal jurisprudence and the transfer of enforcement activities from the Treasury Department to the Department of Justice. He stresses that citizens who patronize illegal liquor share responsibility for crime and must either support laws or work openly for their repeal.

On business, he endorses regulation rather than government ownership, with competition for commodity industries and rate regulation for public utilities. He supports government cooperation with private self-help efforts, national concern for education, and public health services organized as fully as public education.

Regarding peace, he denies imperialist ambitions, supports the treaty renouncing war, armament limitation, and the Permanent Court of International Justice with reservations, while rejecting League of Nations membership. He expresses friendship toward the Latin American republics.

Finally, he announces a special session of Congress for agricultural relief and tariff changes, lists election mandates including constitutional integrity and economy in public expenditure, and closes with faith in the nation's future and a request for divine assistance.

The passage reviews eight Vanguard funds for retirement, noting that passive investing gained popularity after the 2008/09 financial crisis because it requires minimal time and effort while providing satisfactory returns. Vanguard, with over $6 trillion in assets, dominates the U.S. mutual fund and ETF landscape and was founded by John Bogle, considered the "father of passive investing." A backtested Vanguard Retirement Portfolio of five funds, using a buy-and-hold strategy with annual rebalancing from 2007 to 2023, grew $10,000 to $23,317, with returns lower than the S&P 500 due to bond allocations. The eight funds comprise four LifeStrategy funds (Income, Conservative Growth, Moderate Growth, and Growth), which use target allocations with differing equity-bond tilts, and four Target Retirement funds (Income, 2040, 2050, and 2060), which gradually shift toward more conservative allocations as retirement dates approach. Investors are advised to read the prospectus to determine suitability.

This passage from the TMS320DM814x DaVinci Digital Media Processors documentation references the System MMU section of the Technical Reference Manual (SPRUGZ8) and notes that L4 Fast and Slow Peripheral Domain memory maps are detailed in Tables 3-5 and 3-6. The DDR DMM TILER provides an additional 4-GB addressing range, enabled by a 33rd address bit, to access frame buffers in rotated and mirrored views; it is accessible only to the HDVPSS and ISS subsystems, while other masters can access a single view through the 512-MB TILER region. Figures 4-1 through 4-8 show bottom-view package pin assignments. Terminal functions tables identify external signal names, pin multiplexing, ball numbers, package designators, pin types, internal pullup/pulldown states, supply voltage sources, and pin functions; the MUXED column identifies multiplexed peripheral functions, the controlling PINCNTLx register, the de-selected input state, and Multi-Muxed options. Boot configuration pins are multiplexed between ARM Cortex-A8 boot mode and GPMC functions, with BTMODE bits sampled at reset to determine configurations.

The Back Cut Offense exploits the Diamond & One defense's weaknesses in the corners and middle, producing open shots, lay-ups, and putbacks while using single/double baseline screens to free the Star player. It features post entry and left side entry sequences, each with three looks: a back cut, a corner cut with dribble penetration, and single/double action with base cross and fake cross options. Success depends on execution and coordination, requiring mastery of double screens, base screens, and post ups, plus defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience. Teaching methods include whole-part-whole instruction and breakdown drills such as low and high post isolation. Game strategies emphasize scouting opponents, anticipating defensive reads, varying alignments, and attacking weak defenders. The Diamond & One defense, derived from the Box & One, uses four zone defenders and one pass-denying defender against the scoring ace, best deployed against odd or one guard front offenses.

The Boring Company sold out 20,000 novelty flamethrowers, but customs agencies won't ship items called "Flamethrower." Elon Musk renamed it "Not a Flamethrower," possibly "Temperature Enhancement Device." The device shoots flames under 10 feet, complying with California law, and includes a free fire extinguisher and serial number.

Features include home screen additions, machine learning recommendations, variable playback speeds, and quick skipping. Plex also refreshed its mobile app with customizable home screens, tabs, and default server locations.

Italy's leading business lobby, Confindustria, has trimmed its 2025 GDP growth forecast from the previously expected 0.6%, citing mounting external headwinds. The downgrade reflects new U.S.–EU trade measures imposing tariffs of up to 15% on European imports, along with a strong euro that has eroded exporters' competitiveness. Export growth is expected to stagnate through 2025 and 2026, leaving investment as the main driver of growth, with household consumption providing only partial support. The Italian government is preparing to revise its official growth assumptions in line with these projections, which are consistent with IMF and OECD forecasts. The lobby warns that without structural reforms to improve productivity and competitiveness, Italy risks stagnation amid global trade disputes, public debt pressures, and EU budgetary constraints.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated November 1, 2017, announcing that it released its financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2017 by posting its Third Quarter 2017 Shareholder Letter on its website. The letter is attached as Exhibit 99.1 and furnished under Item 2.02. The report was signed by Chief Financial Officer Deepak Ahuja.

Senator Leila de Lima slammed defeated senatorial candidate Francis Tolentino's election protest against her over the 2016 elections, calling it baseless. Tolentino, who placed 13th, lost to De Lima, the 12th and last Senate seat winner. De Lima said the recount in his pilot precincts showed no vote recovery and no fraud was found. She accused him of dilatory tactics, unnecessary ballot decryption, and spending millions to please his "new master." She also rejected his suggestion that she resign like Senator Juan Miguel Zubiri did in 2011, noting Pimentel's protest was meritorious unlike Tolentino's.

A fire destroyed the Edisto Island beachfront home of South Carolina Circuit Judge Diane Goodstein, injuring at least three family members. Goodstein, who was walking on the beach when the fire began, had recently blocked the South Carolina Election Commission from providing voter registration information to the federal government, an order later reversed by the state Supreme Court. Occupants escaped by jumping from the elevated first floor and were rescued by kayak. Authorities found no evidence of arson or a prefire explosion.

Care Compliance Expert (CCE) is a company founded to improve the quality of elder care. It emphasizes that better dementia care and greater attention to health and safety in care homes can raise the overall quality of life. CCE has extensive expertise in health and safety in care homes and is consulted by governmental organizations on regulatory changes.

Scientists have documented the first modern case of "river piracy," which they attribute to global warming. Meltwater from Yukon's Kaskawulsh glacier abruptly switched from the Slims River to the Alsek River in about one day last May, leaving the Slims nearly dry; the water now flows to the Pacific Ocean instead of the Arctic's Bering Sea. A 30-metre canyon formed at the glacier's end, rerouting the flow. Such events normally take tens of thousands of years. Researchers calculate only a one-in-200 chance the glacier retreat and piracy are natural without man-made warming.

France, inspired by 19-year-old Kylian Mbappé's two goals and a won penalty, beat Argentina 4-3 to reach the World Cup quarter-finals, where they face Uruguay. Mbappé, who joined PSG for 180 million euros, emerged as a star on the day Ronaldo and Messi exited the tournament. Teammates Griezmann, Giroud and Pogba created space for him, while Benjamin Pavard scored a notable 25-yard goal. However, Uruguay differ from Argentina, being "solid and aggressive" according to Didier Deschamps, boasting Luis Suarez's strong scoring record and the formidable Godin-Gimenez defensive partnership, though Edinson Cavani's probable injury absence is a blow. France remain favourites to reach the semi-finals.

SpaceX plans to launch its first rocket for NASA on Tuesday, using a recycled Falcon 9 booster and a previously flown Dragon capsule carrying nearly 5,000 pounds of supplies to the International Space Station. NASA officials say the risk is comparable to that of a new rocket. SpaceX aims to lower launch costs through reusability. The launch is the first from Launch Complex 40 since a 2016 explosion damaged it; the pad was rebuilt for $50 million.

The Lexington County Sheriff's Department is searching for a woman suspected of making over 60 fake 911 calls between March 25 and April 14, mostly from the Saint Andrews area. Officials released one call recording hoping someone recognizes her voice. Captain Adam Myrick said the calls risk response times and endanger officers and the public. Tips can go to Crimestoppers.

This passage is from the TI datasheet SLASFA2A (November 2024, revised April 2025) covering the MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 microcontrollers. The schematic section recommends 10µF and 0.1µF decoupling capacitors on VDD/VSS, a 47kΩ pullup with 10nF capacitor on NRST, a 100kΩ 0.1%-tolerance resistor for the SYSOSC frequency correction loop, a 0.47µF tank capacitor on VCORE, and pullup resistors for 5V-tolerant open-drain IOs. The device support section explains nomenclature (X for experimental devices, MSP for fully qualified production devices) and lists development tools including Code Composer Studio, IAR Embedded Workbench, Keil MDK, TI Arm-Clang, GNU Arm Embedded Toolchain, SysConfig, and the LaunchPad ecosystem. It also covers documentation support, TI E2E forums, trademarks, ESD handling precautions, a revision history detailing specification updates between the November 2024 and April 2025 revisions, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information with associated disclaimers and legal notices.

Fort Bend ISD maintenance crews and contractors worked overnight to repair air conditioning problems at Quail Valley Elementary School and Marshall High School following a three-day weekend and high temperatures. Students at Marshall reported the school was hot, with some gathering in the cooler cafeteria. The AC was fixed, and students noted only a couple days of school remained.

Since 1993, all gains in the S&P 500 have come from holding the index overnight (from close to open), a tendency also seen in gold markets. Night trading means holding positions from one day's close until the next day's open, which differs from after-hours trading. The average gain from holding the S&P 500 overnight is 0.04%, gold offers about 0.03%, and gold miners (GDX) show an even larger edge. Conversely, buying at the open and selling at the close has produced zero returns since 1993, and GDX shows a -25% CAGR for open-to-close holding. The overnight bias is likely due to inflation, earnings growth, and compensation for the added overnight risk. Despite this bias, profitable strategies must overcome slippage and commissions. The authors' 2014 overnight strategies still perform well, and their combined 24-hour trading strategies produced 950 trades with an average gain of 0.33%. The authors consider overnight stock trading strategies low-hanging fruit for aspiring traders.

Dengue, caused by four dengue virus serotypes (DENV1–4), infects an estimated 100–400 million people yearly, yet no direct-acting antivirals exist and licensed vaccines offer imbalanced serotype protection with low efficacy in young children. AT-752 is an orally available guanosine nucleotide prodrug that, after metabolic activation to the triphosphate AT-9010, inhibits the DENV RNA-dependent RNA polymerase with pan-serotype activity. This first-in-human Phase 1 study evaluated the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of single ascending doses (250–1500 mg) and multiple ascending doses (up to 750 mg three times daily) of AT-752 in 65 healthy subjects, including food-effect and ethnic-sensitivity assessments. AT-752 was well tolerated, with no serious adverse events or discontinuations; treatment-emergent adverse events were mild to moderate and resolved by study end. The parent prodrug AT-281 was rapidly eliminated (half-life ~0.5 h), while metabolite AT-273, a surrogate for intracellular AT-9010, had a long half-life (~15–25 h). Exposure was approximately dose-proportional, with no ethnic sensitivity and no clinically meaningful food effect. In multiple-dose cohorts, AT-273 exposure increased with dosing frequency, and 750 mg three times daily exceeded the in vitro EC90 for DENV inhibition. These favorable safety and pharmacokinetic results support further clinical development of AT-752 for dengue treatment.

This email, sent March 8, 2001 by Miyung Buster to numerous Enron employees and outside recipients, forwards a collection of March 7–8, 2001 news articles on California's energy crisis. Key points include:

- The Davis administration signaled a breakthrough in talks to rescue PG&E, potentially paying at least $7 billion (with PG&E possibly seeking up to $10 billion) for its transmission lines, with an announcement expected within weeks.
- El Paso Energy shut six cogeneration plants in the San Joaquin Valley, citing non-payment by PG&E; at least 10 plants closed within two weeks over unpaid bills.
- The state Department of Water Resources has spent $3.2 billion buying power for PG&E and Southern California Edison customers, but how it will be reimbursed remains disputed among the utilities, the state, and the PUC.
- Governor Davis's long-term power contracts—40 deals worth about $40 billion, averaging $69 per megawatt-hour—remain largely secret under confidentiality agreements, drawing criticism from consumer groups.
- California lawmakers proposed fixes including wholesale price caps and extending daylight-saving time, but no consensus emerged at a House hearing.
- Wall Street analysts said Davis's approach avoids the underlying imbalance between wholesale and retail rates.
- Legislation cutting prices paid to alternative energy generators stalled amid concerns that select generators, some of whom donated to Senator Battin's campaigns, would receive higher payments.
- Smaller utilities such as SMUD are seeking exemption from rolling blackouts ordered by PG&E.
- The PUC was set to decide whether PG&E and Edison could lay off thousands of workers; an administrative law judge recommended blocking most cuts.
- Experts warned that up to 43 percent of summer power needs could come from the volatile spot market, potentially costing billions and risking blackouts.
- Contra Costa County supervisors voted to search for power plant sites, drawing resident opposition, including to a proposed 650-megawatt plant near Concord.
- A column discussed California's $90 billion infrastructure gap beyond the energy crisis.
- The PUC held hearings on PG&E's $91 million Tri-Valley power upgrade project.
- The state Energy Commission approved a 51-megawatt temporary "peaker" plant at San Francisco International Airport.
- A Wall Street Journal article detailed flaws in Davis's plan, including difficulty recovering state power spending without rate increases, legislative limits on bond sales, and risks to California's credit rating.

Two new oral GLP-1 drugs showed weight loss benefits in people with obesity in studies published September 16 and 17. In one trial, a 25-milligram dose of oral semaglutide produced an average weight loss of nearly 14 percent over up to 64 weeks among more than 300 participants. In another, Eli Lilly's orforglipron, a small-molecule GLP-1 drug, led to about 11 percent weight loss at the highest dose among more than 3,000 participants over up to 72 weeks. Unlike injectable GLP-1 drugs, pills require no needles or refrigeration and may be cheaper to manufacture. Side effects included nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and constipation, with no liver toxicity observed. Researchers say longer-term studies are needed, and the pills could be available by 2026 pending FDA approval.

On March 11, 2011, a 9.0-magnitude earthquake, tsunami, and nuclear emergency struck Japan, killing over 25,000 people and causing an estimated ¥16.9 trillion in economic damage. Approximately 80% of Japanese automotive plants suspended production, with monthly output dropping nearly 60% in March and April 2011. Nissan suffered damage to six production facilities and about 50 critical suppliers, but was prepared to withstand the shocks.

Nissan's risk management philosophy emerged from its 1999 near-bankruptcy and subsequent alliance with Renault. The company maintained a dedicated risk management function, an executive-level risk committee, and an earthquake emergency-response plan prioritizing human life, prevention of follow-on disasters, rapid recovery, and community support.

Nissan's response included convening a Global Disaster Control Headquarters 15 minutes after the earthquake and establishing a Recovery Committee. Key practices included sharing information across global regions, allocating constrained supplies to highest-margin products, managing production around anticipated bottlenecks, and empowering rapid field-level decision-making.

Unlike Honda, which faced supply chain constraints, Nissan's localization strategy helped insulate it from disruption. Going forward, Nissan planned to increase localized production in the Americas from 70% to 90% by 2015, reduce Japanese-sourced components in North America by 50% by fiscal 2013, and extend its business continuity planning to second- and third-tier suppliers.

Paleontologist Ashley Leger works for Cogstone Resource Management, a company contracted by Los Angeles transportation officials to monitor fossil discoveries during construction of the Metro Purple Line subway extension. Since work began in 2014, Ice Age fossils have routinely surfaced, including remains of rabbits, camels, bison, mastodons, and horses. The most notable discovery was an intact skull of a juvenile Columbian mammoth, uncovered after 15 hours of excavation about a year into the project's second phase. California environmental laws require scientists at certain construction sites, and paleontologists have staffed L.A. subway digs since the 1990s. The mammoth skull, rare because both tusks were attached, was transported to the La Brea Tar Pits and Museum, where only about 30 mammoths have been found despite thousands of other fossils. The eight- to 12-year-old mammoth was named Hayden, after actress Hayden Panettiere, and is available for public viewing in the museum's Fossil Lab. Similar discoveries have occurred elsewhere, including mammoth and gray whale fossils in San Diego and a centuries-old wooden boat near Boston's seaport.

The provisional government in Cuba will end once elections are held and a new government is peacefully inaugurated. The United States expresses hope that Cubans will preserve justice and order, warning that if elections become a farce or insurrectionary habits become confirmed, Cuba could not remain independent and the United States would have to intervene again. The Secretary of State attended as honorary president and subsequently visited Brazil, Uruguay, Argentina, Chile, Peru, Panama, and Colombia, carrying a message of peace and friendship that was warmly received.
Stocks slid early Tuesday as healthcare and bank stocks fell. Goldman Sachs dropped 3% on weak earnings; Johnson & Johnson lost 2.7%; Cardinal Health plunged 10.6%. The Dow fell 0.4% to 20,563.

This study demonstrates that a simple annealing strategy effectively decouples carrier and phonon transport in Se-alloyed n-type Bi2Te3-based (BTS) thermoelectric materials. Samples were synthesized via a melting-hot pressing (MT-HP) route and annealed at 723 K. Annealing tuned carrier density and mobility through cation vacancy formation induced by Te(Se) volatilization, enhancing the power factor, while atomic-scale defects from volatilization strengthened phonon scattering and reduced lattice thermal conductivity. The optimized Bi2Te2.6Se0.4 sample annealed for 100 h achieved a peak ZT of 1.06 at 373 K, a room-temperature ZT of 0.78, and an average ZT of 0.99 over 300–423 K, with high carrier mobility (295.97 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹) and low lattice thermal conductivity (0.48 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹). This scalable post-synthesis approach offers a practical route for high-performance n-type BTS thermoelectrics for cooling applications.

NTT Docomo installed smartphone wipes in restrooms at Tokyo Narita International Airport until March 15. The wipes also advertise NTT's wifi service and a travel guide app with voice translation. Studies found phones carry germs.

The Supreme Court allowed Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook to remain in her post pending oral arguments in January 2026 on whether President Trump has legal cause to fire her. The order deferred Trump's request to stay a district court injunction blocking Cook's removal, a blow to Trump, who cited mortgage fraud claims—denied by Cook, who has not been charged—as grounds for firing her. The case is seen as a potential landmark on the Fed's independence from political interference. The ruling lets the Fed conduct business as usual through year's end; Cook will vote at the October and December FOMC meetings, and possibly January's. In September, the FOMC cut rates a quarter point, with Cook voting for the cut and Trump appointee Stephen Miran dissenting.

This paper develops methods for evaluating software accessibility, focusing on users with visual impairments. While ISO 25023 defines the "Accessibility" subcharacteristic through the quality attributes "Accessibility for users with disabilities" and "Supported languages adequacy," it lacks methodologies for determining some of their parameters. The authors propose a classification and mathematical model that decomposes accessibility into four subproperties—perceptiveness, operability, understandability, and localization—each measured through quality attributes such as alternative text, color contrast, subtitles and audio descriptions, keyboard and structured navigation, clear instructions, input assistance, correct input support, and localization. Weighting coefficients are established through expert evaluation, and a Fibonacci-based scale classifies results from "very poor" to "excellent." The methodology was validated on the website of Vasyl Stefanyk Precarpathian National University using tools including Image Alt Checker and WCAG Contrast Checker. The overall accessibility score was approximately 0.68, rated "excellent," though attributes such as subtitles/audio descriptions and input assistance scored zero, and alternative text (0.15) and structured navigation (0.47) required improvement. The authors conclude that the proposed methods enable more precise, objective accessibility assessment, support compliance with ISO 25023 and WCAG, and provide practical recommendations for improving web resource inclusivity.

This protocol describes a systematic review examining implementation determinants, implementation strategies, and adjunctive interventions for structural interventions targeting HIV evidence-based interventions (EBIs) in the U.S. The background notes that HIV disproportionately affects minoritized populations due to social and structural determinants of health, and that despite effective tools like PrEP and Treatment as Prevention, disparities in access and uptake persist. The review aims to identify determinants, strategies, and adjunctive interventions relevant to implementation outcomes, gaps in the literature, and how structural interventions differ from implementation strategies and adjunctive interventions.

A search conducted between May and July 2024 across multiple databases identified 8,098 articles before deduplication. Screening uses natural language processing across five domains, followed by manual title/abstract and full-text review in COVIDENCE by trained investigators, with consensus procedures for disagreements. Inclusion criteria require a U.S.-based HIV focus, implementation or hybrid study designs, original data, behavioral/social science, at least one implementation outcome, and structural intervention characteristics. Data extraction will cover study characteristics, CDC priority populations, implementation outcomes (per Proctor et al.), and structural intervention types (per Sipe et al.). Determinants will be coded in MaxQDA using CFIR 2.0; strategies will be coded using the ERIC framework; adjunctive interventions using TDF and COM-B. Analyses will tabulate and stratify findings, supplemented by NLP-based thematic analysis. Results will be disseminated through two primary papers, additional manuscripts, conference presentations, and a public literature review dashboard. Analyses are planned from June 2025 through June 2026, with dissemination through Fall 2026.

The Supreme Court agreed to hear a challenge to a 2023 Hawaii law making it a crime for concealed carry permit holders to carry handguns on private property open to the public without the owner's permission, and banning guns in "sensitive places" such as parks, beaches, and playgrounds. The 9th Circuit upheld the law. Challengers—three Maui residents and the Hawaii Firearms Coalition—ask whether the private-property ban is constitutional and whether the appeals court improperly relied on post-Reconstruction rather than founding-era laws. The Trump administration urged the Court to take the case. The justices also agreed to hear: Exxon Mobil's appeal seeking to sue three Cuban state-owned companies under the Cuban Liberty and Democratic Solidarity Act of 1996 for Cuba's 1960 property confiscation, after lower courts dismissed claims under the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act; Havana Docks' suit against four cruise lines using confiscated Havana docks, which the 11th Circuit rejected because the concession expired in 2004; a Michigan estate's claim that it was owed the difference between unpaid taxes and the property's fair market value after foreclosure, citing the Fifth and Eighth Amendments; and whether a federal motor-carrier law bars a state-law negligence claim against a broker for selecting a carrier or driver.

Schaeffler, sponsor of Audi's Formula E team, built the 4ePerformance, an electric RS3 using four FE01 race car motors producing 1,180 hp. It reaches 124 mph in 7 seconds, with all-wheel drive, torque vectoring, and 64 kWh of batteries. Audi ended R8 e-tron production and now focuses on the e-tron SUV. Formula E is attracting more manufacturers.

This study examined relationships between self- and other-oriented mentalization, attachment insecurity, and personality pathology as defined by the DSM-5 Alternative Model of Personality Disorders (AMPD), covering both Criterion A (level of personality functioning) and Criterion B (maladaptive traits). The sample included 109 participants aged 18–47, recruited from psychiatric inpatient services (N = 60) and the community (N = 49); 54% met criteria for at least one personality disorder. Mentalization was assessed with the Movie for the Assessment of Social Cognition (other-mentalizing) and the Reflective Functioning Questionnaire Uncertainty subscale (self-mentalizing deficits), alongside measures of personality functioning (SIFS), maladaptive traits (PID-5), and attachment (ECR-R).

Results showed that self-mentalizing deficits were strongly associated with both self- and interpersonal functioning and all five maladaptive traits, and were the strongest regression predictor across outcomes, explaining 18–55% of variance. Correct other-mentalizing significantly predicted only interpersonal functioning difficulties. Moderation analyses indicated that mentalizing facets moderated attachment–pathology links: correct other-mentalizing and hypermentalizing moderated the effect of anxious attachment on interpersonal functioning; self-mentalizing moderated the effect of anxious attachment on Negative Affectivity and Detachment; and correct, under-, and non-mentalizing moderated the effect of avoidant attachment on Detachment.

The authors conclude that self-mentalizing plays a broad, nonspecific role in personality pathology, while other-mentalizing is more specific to interpersonal aspects, suggesting self-mentalizing should be prioritized in treatment. Limitations include the cross-sectional design, small heterogeneous sample, and differing assessment methods.

CPI(M) leader Prakash Karat said the February 18 Tripura Assembly polls were important for all of India. He noted the contest is now between the BJP and Left Front, as Congress members joined the BJP, and voiced confidence in an eighth Left government under Manik Sarkar. He alleged the IPFT was an insurgent mask, criticized the BJP, and said the central budget favored corporates.

This paper presents a thermal characterization of Mod-Cam, the single-module precursor and first-light/commissioning instrument for the Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope (FYST), serving as a testbed for the 280 GHz module of the Prime-Cam receiver. The study measured the thermal responsivity (RT) of aluminum and titanium-nitride kinetic inductance detectors (KIDs) and quantified the temperature stability of the 100 mK detector stage, which is cooled by a dilution refrigerator and regulated by a PID-controlled heater. Over an 8-hour measurement period, the RMS temperature fluctuation was 3.2×10⁻⁵ K. Median thermal responsivities were 1.995×10⁻⁴ K⁻¹ for aluminum and −6.081×10⁻⁴ K⁻¹ for TiN detectors, with the opposite signs attributed to TiN's standard superconducting microwave conductivity behavior and aluminum's two-level system defect effects. Using optical responsivity values from prior work, the thermally induced equivalent optical power noise was calculated as 0.20 fW for aluminum and 0.11 fW for TiN detectors at a 5 pW optical load, corresponding to fractional noise contributions of 0.0040% and 0.0023%, respectively. These results demonstrate that cryogenic thermal fluctuations contribute negligibly to the detector noise budget, validating the cryogenic design and supporting the instrument's goal of achieving background-limited sensitivity on FYST.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on May 25, 2022, announcing its financial results for the quarter ended May 1, 2022. Remaining public lands suitable for agriculture should be reserved for actual settlers, as the desert-land, timber and stone, and homestead commutation laws have been perverted to benefit non-settlers. The homestead law has fostered prosperity, but public grazing ranges near exhaustion, and grazing-region settlers need larger allotments than 160 acres, since dry pasture supports few cattle. Unlawful fencing of public lands, once tolerated, will now be stopped, and Congress is urged to act, possibly through an expert commission. Alaska needs better laws: liberal land and homestead provisions, forest and game protection, regulated settler timber cutting, salmon fisheries protection under the Fish Commission, a Congressional Delegate, and possibly a committee visit. Indian policy should aim at eventual but slow absorption into the national body; allotment suits advanced tribes, while tribes on prairie lands should lead pastoral, village-based lives.

The Missouri Supreme Court will hear two cases determining whether the Missouri Human Rights Act prohibits discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, terms absent from the act itself. Lower courts are split on the issue. In the first case, a transgender teenager, R.M.A., sued the Blue Springs school district after being denied use of boys' restrooms and lockers, claiming sex discrimination. A Jackson County judge dismissed the case in 2016, a decision upheld by the appeals court in 2017. In the second case, Harold Lampley, a gay state employee, claimed sex discrimination based on harassment for not exhibiting stereotypical male attributes; the Human Rights Commission denied his claim, but an appeals court disagreed in 2017. The ACLU and other groups support both plaintiffs, while the state argues courts cannot read language into the law that isn't there.

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture by Erik Demaine introduces 6.851 Advanced Data Structures, outlining course topics (temporal data structures, geometry, dynamic optimality, memory hierarchy, hashing, integers, dynamic graphs, strings, and succinct data structures) and logistics (weekly problem sets, lecture scribing, and optional open problem sessions). The lecture focuses on persistence—temporal data structures—modeled on a pointer machine. Four levels are described: partial persistence (only the latest version can be updated; versions are linearly ordered), full persistence (any version can be updated; versions form a tree), confluent persistence (versions can be combined; versions form a DAG), and functional data structures (nodes are never modified). Driscoll, Sarnak, Sleator, and Tarjan (1989) showed that any pointer machine data structure with constant in- and out-degree can be made partially or fully persistent with constant amortized overhead and constant additive space per change, using back pointers, modification lists, node copying/splitting, and potential-function analysis; partial persistence can be deamortized (Brodal, 1997), while deamortizing full persistence remains open. For confluent persistence, Fiat and Kaplan (2003) achieve overhead proportional to effective depth with a matching space lower bound, and a disjoint-case result achieves logarithmic overhead. Functional data structures are known for balanced BSTs, deques, and tries, with a log n separation from ordinary data structures.

According to Finder.com's America's Biggest Money Mistakes survey, 78.3% of respondents admitted making a lifetime money mistake. The most common error, cited by nearly 64%, was overspending on fun activities like shopping, vacations, and dining out. Women admitted this more often than men (66.2% vs. 58%), though overall admission rates were nearly equal between the sexes. Women were also more likely to regret letting a partner control finances, while men more often regretted bad investments and gambling. The second-largest regret for both genders was dropping out of college, which BLS data links to lower wages and higher unemployment. Generational differences were modest: millennials and Gen X-ers admitted mistakes at similar rates, while baby boomers admitted least. Millennials most often cited overspending on fun, while boomers most often regretted bad investments. Other regrets included overpaying for weddings, online scams, and having children.
An experiment found that 6-year-olds worked harder and stayed more focused on repetitive tasks when pretending to be Batman or Dora the Explorer, while those focused on themselves took more breaks.

This paper proposes a queue prioritization algorithm that uses active learning (AL) with a custom acquisition function to prioritize candidates produced by generative AI models in scientific discovery workflows. Generative models often produce nonsensical candidates, wasting computational resources and risking model decay when retrained on poor outputs. The approach trains an XGBoost surrogate model to predict expensive simulation scores, combining predictions and uncertainties into an acquisition function that reorders candidate queues for simulation. The method is demonstrated on discovering metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) for carbon capture, using a fine-tuned DiffLinker diffusion model to generate linkers and LAMMPS molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate internal strain. Experiments show that AL prioritization increases the average number of high-performing candidates from 281 to 604 out of 1000, with less than 1% additional computational overhead. AL also prevents model decay by de-prioritizing unstable structures that would otherwise be used for fine-tuning. Multi-objective acquisition functions incorporating synthesizability and similarity to known linkers, as well as upper confidence bound functions balancing exploration and exploitation, are evaluated; weak exploration (λ=0.1) yields the best results. The authors conclude that AL queue prioritization improves candidate quality in generative screening workflows.

A hockey player injured two weeks ago against Ottawa considers himself doubtful for tonight's game. His condition has improved daily, but he will only know if he can play once he skates and tests the injury on the ice.

Denmark's Systemic Risk Council recommends restricting interest-only and variable-interest loans in Copenhagen and Aarhus for borrowers whose debts exceed 400 percent of pretax income, with about 15 percent of loans exempt. The government has three months to comply or explain refusal.

The passage is an Investing.com page containing financial headlines and a market analysis noting seasonal weakness over the past 35 years, with diminished liquidity, thin volume, tax-loss selling, and institutional rebalancing ahead of the third quarter's end. The author discusses TLT, which sold off after an auction, with Tuesday's rally reaching the July 6-month calendar range high, where the Real Motion Indicator gave a mean reversion sell signal; however, a bullish divergence exists as the dots are above moving averages and price is above the 50-DMA but below the 200-DMA. Yields topped as predicted, and a dollar break below 98 would suggest further declines, which is bullish for commodities. Gold looks strong above 3,350, with new all-time highs possible above 3,450.
