Professor Noelle Selin delivered a guest lecture on mercury regulation and the Minamata Convention, signed in October 2013—the first new global environmental treaty in over a decade and the first covering an entire product life cycle.

Mercury is a global problem because emitted mercury remains airborne for six months to a year, mixing across hemispheres. When deposited, it converts to methyl mercury, accumulates in food chains, and acts as a neurotoxin linked to lowered IQ in children of exposed pregnant women and cardiovascular effects in adults. Major sources include coal combustion (about a quarter of emissions) and artisanal and small-scale gold mining, which was previously underestimated in emissions inventories.

The 2002 UN scientific assessment concluded global action was needed. The US under the Bush administration favored voluntary partnerships over a binding treaty, while the EU pushed for one. The US position shifted in 2009 under President Obama, who had sponsored mercury export ban legislation. China delayed negotiations until 2010 while developing its own regulations. The treaty took five negotiating sessions; the US ratified quickly via executive action because it aligned with existing US law.

The treaty addresses mercury in products (thermometers, batteries, fluorescent lamps, dental amalgam) through a list of banned items with exemptions and phase-out dates negotiated among countries. International environmental treaties lack enforcement, relying instead on transparency, shaming, and capacity building. In artisanal gold mining, mercury amalgamates gold and is burned off, releasing emissions; up to 30% of gold on the market comes from this process. The treaty promotes capacity building rather than eliminating the practice.

The convention connects to other frameworks including the Stockholm, Rotterdam, and Basel Conventions, with funding through the Global Environment Facility. The EU has replaced the US as the global standard leader in chemicals regulation, and developing countries often copy other nations' regulations due to limited analytical capacity. Negotiations proceed slowly until deadlines, disadvantaging small delegations. Analysis suggests the treaty will avoid increases in mercury levels rather than reduce them; it is currently more legally and politically significant than environmentally significant, serving as a signaling mechanism to discourage mercury use.

A research team led by Dr. Shinichi Furuya of the NeuroPiano Institute and Sony Computer Science Laboratories has provided the first scientific evidence that pianists can alter piano timbre through touch, resolving a question debated since the early 20th century. Using a proprietary high-precision sensor system (Hackkey) that measures all 88 keys at 1,000 fps and 0.01 mm resolution, the team recorded 20 internationally renowned pianists performing with the intent to produce diverse timbres, such as bright/dark and light/heavy. In a psychophysical experiment, 40 listeners—including pianists and people with no musical experience—consistently perceived the intended timbres, even when volume and tempo were controlled, with pianist listeners showing greater sensitivity. Analysis using a linear mixed-effects model identified specific movement features, such as acceleration during escapement and hand synchronization deviation, and experimentally confirmed a causal relationship between key movement and timbre. Published in PNAS, the findings quantify previously tacit knowledge, potentially enabling more efficient, evidence-based music education and prevention of mislearning, while also opening avenues in neuroscience, psychology, rehabilitation, skill transfer, and human interface design. The research was conducted under JST's CREST and Moonshot programs.

Jim Cramer has reversed his positive view of Snap, which he had compared to early Facebook after fourth-quarter revenue rose 72%. He blames the unpopular December redesign, which separated media and celebrity stories from personal contacts, and celebrity criticism including Kylie Jenner's tweet that caused a 7% share decline. Cramer now says the stock is too expensive and advises taking a pass for now, though he would buy at a certain price. Snap reports first-quarter results May 1.

The passage covers container-based design patterns for distributed systems. The ambassador pattern separates application logic from service brokering: the application connects to a service on localhost while the ambassador introspects its environment and brokers the appropriate connection, enabling portability across environments. Ambassadors can also perform request splitting for experimentation, redirecting a fraction of traffic (e.g., 10% via nginx using IP hashing and weight settings) to beta versions while ensuring users have a consistent experience.

The adapter pattern modifies an application container's interface to conform to a standardized interface expected by external systems. Applications include monitoring (e.g., a Prometheus exporter adapting Redis), log normalization (e.g., Fluentd adapting Redis slowlog and Storm logs), and rich health checks (e.g., a Go-based adapter running diagnostic queries against MySQL). Adapters provide modularity, reuse, and dedicated resources per container.

Microservices break applications into components communicating via formal APIs, benefiting team autonomy, independent scaling, and agility, but complicating debugging and system design.

Replicated load-balanced services deploy identical stateless replicas behind a load balancer for redundancy and horizontal scaling; at least two replicas are needed for high availability. Readiness probes inform load balancers when replicas can serve traffic. Session tracking (via IP hashing or cookies) routes a user's requests to the same replica. A caching layer (e.g., Varnish) improves performance and can provide rate limiting and denial-of-service defense, while nginx handles SSL termination.

Sharded services distribute data across replicas, each serving a subset of requests, and suit stateful services whose data exceeds single-machine capacity. Sharding functions map requests to shards using hashing and the modulo operator; key selection must balance generality and specificity. Consistent hashing minimizes key remapping when resizing. Replicating each shard improves resilience and enables "hot sharding" to handle uneven load.

The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes request processing across leaf nodes whose partial results the root combines. However, per-node overhead and the straggler problem (overall latency determined by the slowest leaf) limit gains from parallelism; replicating each shard addresses reliability and scale.

Finally, function-as-a-service (FaaS) executes stateless functions in response to events, simplifying deployment and scaling but complicating debugging, fitting poorly with long-running background processing or memory-heavy workloads, and becoming cost-inefficient at sustained high request volumes. The decorator pattern uses FaaS to transform requests or responses, such as adding default values to API inputs.

In this MIT OpenCourseWare lecture, Gary Gensler leads the final use case session of his blockchain course, focusing on digital identity and identity management. Students debate what identity is, distinguishing attributes, claims, credentials, and attestations. One student proposes hashing biometric data as a unique identifier for verification purposes, while others raise concerns about biometric theft and replication. The class discusses how certificate authorities and public key cryptography secure web traffic, and how blockchain might offer a decentralized alternative. Pain points include identity theft, forged credentials, and major data breaches such as Equifax, Facebook, Marriott, and India's 1.1 billion-record hack. State projects covered include Estonia's e-identity system, which does not use blockchain, and India's Aadhaar, which rapidly reached a billion users but experienced hacks, errors, and severe consequences for some users. Self-sovereign identity—where individuals control, transport, and share their own credentials—is discussed, along with challenges such as blockchain immutability conflicting with GDPR's right to be forgotten and the risk of lost private keys. Projects mentioned include ICOs like Civic and Sovrin, Bitnation, the Distributed Identity Foundation, Rebooting Web-of-Trust, and W3C standards efforts. Students also debate whether the US Social Security Number system is an antiquated policy problem. Finally, about a quarter of students say they plan to obtain MIT's blockchain-backed diplomas, though most still want paper copies.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig of the Southern District of Florida was fired by email last week, while he was off work observing Rosh Hashanah, after conservatives published past blog posts attributed to him that criticized President Trump during his first term. Commentator Natalie Winters cited alleged comments calling Trump "mentally unfit" and "an institutional terrorist." Rosenzweig, who joined the U.S. attorney's office in September 2020, worked in the economic crimes section. He is among dozens of federal prosecutors fired by Trump's Justice Department, including three others in Florida who previously worked with former special counsel Jack Smith.

This methodology paper describes a community-based participatory research (CBPR) approach, grounded in an Indigenous Knowledge System (IKS), developed by KaviKrishna for tuberculosis (TB) screening, treatment, monitoring, and research in the rural Sualkuchi-Hajo area of Kamrup district, Assam, India. Noting that over 10 million people had active TB in 2022 and that more than one-third of the global population carries dormant MTB (dMTB), with 10% at lifetime risk of reactivation, the authors argue that existing top-down TB control programs have had unsatisfactory outcomes due to generalized approaches, inadequate monitoring of MDR evolution, dormancy reactivation, host-pathogen interactions, and circulating strains, and lack of community feedback.

KaviKrishna operates three units: KaviKrishna Telemedicine Care (KTC), KaviKrishna Laboratory (KKL), and the KaviKrishna Centre of Indian Knowledge System (K-IKS). The approach uses the Indigenous Kamarupa Information Network (IKIN), a temple-based (Namghar) communication network inspired by the Vedic altruism philosophy Jiva Upakara Tantra and the local silk-weaving community's historical communication system. Since 2010, this network screened 300 pulmonary TB cases among 500 suspects, using trained student volunteers for contact tracing, awareness, and follow-up of 210 patients.

The described methods include: ethical approval and bone marrow collection (6–7 ml) from the posterior superior iliac crest; sputum processing by NALC-NaOH decontamination, Lowenstein-Jensen culture, and Ziehl-Neelsen staining; drug susceptibility testing by the WHO proportion method; PCR (hsp65 and Rv1458c primers) to distinguish MTB from non-tuberculous mycobacteria, plus MASPCR for rpoB mutations; immunomagnetic sorting of BM-MSCs (CD281+) and HSCs with qPCR detection of dMTB; an in-vivo mouse model using a streptomycin-dependent MTB mutant (m18b) demonstrating dormant MTB within MSCs and reactivation after MHV-1 coronavirus co-infection via MSC-to-ASC reprogramming (HIF-2α elevation, p53 suppression); MIRU-VNTR and spoligotyping identifying Beijing and CAS/CAS1-Delhi lineages; a whole-genome sequencing pipeline (Illumina NovaSeq 6000, BWA alignment to H37Rv, GATK variant calling), with preliminary rpoB/rpoC compensatory mutations found in MTB recovered from MSCs of sputum-negative relapsed cases, suggesting the stem cell niche as a site of MDR evolution; Microplate Alamar Blue MIC assays and MPN-based MDK assays for drugs and herbal agents; and a modified MPN assay with resuscitation factor to detect viable but non-culturable (VBNC) MTB in sputum-negative patients.

The discussion concludes that the CBPR-IKS approach reduced TB stigma through temple networks, trained over 50 community students since 2010, and enabled WGS-based surveillance (data deposited at NCBI, accession PRJNA1054003), proposing the model as an effective template for novel TB control programs in India and the Global South.

Stock indexes fell Friday, with the TSX composite down 81.78 points to 15,694.52. Wall Street declined as Costco shares and energy stocks dropped, and a report showed nonfarm payrolls fell 33,000 in September—the first U.S. job decline in seven years—due to Hurricanes Harvey and Irma. However, wages rose 0.5 percent, exceeding expectations and lifting the dollar to a 12-week high. The Dow fell 35.02 points, the S&P 500 dropped 7.54 points, and the Nasdaq lost 15.25 points.

High street banks announced 141 more branch closures in 2017, following over 1,000 closures between January 2015 and January 2017. Meanwhile, mobile-only banks such as Atom Bank, Monzo and Revolut are rising. A Which? survey of 9,076 members found over half of under-40s would open a mobile-only account, though this drops sharply among those aged 40 and over. Atom Bank's competitive savings accounts caused its app to crash, highlighting the drawback of no in-branch service. Commenters expressed mixed views, with some upset at closures and others open to alternatives.

This passage contains three documents concerning preparations for a Peace Conference. The first, a confidential memorandum, states that negotiators cannot possess full knowledge of all complex questions and proposes that experts prepare brief, comprehensive articles on History, Commerce, and International Law, along with topics such as disarmament, arbitration, and international guaranties. Writers would produce pamphlets of 10,000–15,000 words, secretly printed and indexed, with appendices of documents and statistics, all under the direction of one man with assistants. The second document, a memorandum by the Secretary of State, raises questions about U.S. participation in determining European boundaries and redistributing colonial possessions, including the basis of territorial settlement and cases such as Macedonia, Alsace-Lorraine, Schleswig-Holstein, and Dantzig. The third, a letter from Colonel E. M. House to the Secretary of State, praises the memorandum as admirable and proposes discussing the planned organization in Washington.

Keaton Jones, a Tennessee middle schooler, went viral after his mother recorded a video of him describing bullying at his school. Celebrities including LeBron James and Mark Ruffalo shared supportive messages, standing with Keaton against bullying.

Defendants Vasquez and Perez, charged with possession of burglar's tools, attempted petit larceny, and resisting arrest, were convicted only of possession of burglar's tools after testimony showed they abandoned an attempt to steal a bicycle with a bolt cutter following a conversation with a third person. They moved to set aside the verdict, arguing the court erred in refusing to charge renunciation as a defense to possession of burglar's tools, though it was charged for attempted petit larceny. The court denied the motion, holding Penal Law § 40.10 limits renunciation to four specified offenses not including possession of burglar's tools, while noting the Legislature may consider amending the statute.

Insecticides India plans to invest Rs 200 crore over three years to expand its plants at Dahej (Gujarat) and Chopanki (Rajasthan), including two new synthesis facilities and an export-oriented unit. The company expects 10-15 percent revenue growth this fiscal, contingent on a good monsoon, and is launching four new crop protection products. Expansion will be funded through internal accruals, debt, and equity. Annual net profit rose 41 percent to Rs 83.97 crore.

The Supreme Court observed that the CBI-led MDMA investigation into the larger conspiracy behind Rajiv Gandhi's assassination appears to have made little headway and could be "endless". The court arrayed the Centre as a party in convict A G Perarivalan's plea seeking suspension of his sentence until the probe concludes, fixing the hearing for January 24. Perarivalan, convicted for supplying batteries used in the bomb that killed Gandhi on May 21, 1991, has spent 26 years in prison; his death sentence was commuted to life imprisonment in 2014.

The passage is a datasheet excerpt for the Texas Instruments ADS8681W, ADS8685W, and ADS8689W devices, covering functional modes, programming, registers, and applications. The devices feature a multiSPI digital interface supporting multiple data transfer protocols, with host-to-device connection topologies including single-device configurations (all multiSPI options or standard SPI) and daisy-chain operation for multiple devices, where an optimal frame contains 32 × N SCLK capture edges. The device operates in three functional states—RESET, ACQ, and CONV—controlled by the CONVST/CS and RST signals, with two reset types: application reset and power-on reset (POR). Data transfer frames begin at the falling edge of CONVST/CS and are classified as optimal (32 SCLKs), short (fewer than 32), or long (more than 32). The device contains nine configuration registers and supports data writes using four legacy SPI-compatible protocols (SPI-00-S through SPI-11-S), while data reads additionally support dual SDO and source-synchronous (SRC) protocols with configurable clock source and bus width. Output data words can include flags such as device address, input range, alarm, and parity bits. Application information describes an industrial eight-channel analog input module combining the ADS8681W with the MUX36D08 multiplexer, plus an alarm function with programmable thresholds and hysteresis, illustrated with an NTC thermistor example. Power recommendations cover AVDD and DVDD decoupling, and two low-power modes (NAP and power-down) reduce consumption at lower throughput rates. PCB layout guidance addresses analog/digital partitioning and capacitor placement. The revision history notes ADS8685W and ADS8689W status changed from Advance Information to Production Data.

The passage introduces OSCAR, the first one-shot multi-label causal autoregressive discovery method for event sequences. Given a single sequence of observed events, OSCAR infers the causal structure explaining outcomes by extracting each label's Markov Boundary, using two Transformers as density estimators and conditional mutual information for conditional independence testing. It also produces causal indicators quantifying how events affect label likelihood. Unlike traditional methods whose complexity depends on event and label cardinality, OSCAR is agnostic to both and fully parallelised, providing sequence-specific explanations in minutes. The method is supported by a theorem stating that, under assumptions including causal sufficiency, temporal precedence, bounded lagged effects, and oracle-quality density estimators, Markov Boundaries can be identified via conditional mutual information testing. Evaluation on a real-world vehicular dataset (300,000 sequences, 29,100 diagnostic trouble codes, 474 error patterns) showed that baseline local structure learning algorithms (IAMB, CMB, MB-by-MB, PCD-by-PCD, MI-MCF) failed to produce results within a three-day timeout, while OSCAR achieved 55.26% precision, 31.37% recall, and 40.02% F1 in 11.7 minutes. The authors conclude that OSCAR enables scalable, interpretable, deployment-ready causal discovery for high-dimensional multi-label event sequences.

South Carolina Congressman Trey Gowdy, known for his self-deprecating humor about his hair, co-authored a book with Sen. Tim Scott titled "Unified," due out April 3. During the Benghazi hearings, Gowdy aggressively investigated, with critics arguing his goal was to damage Hillary Clinton rather than uncover the truth. Having grown disillusioned with partisan politics, Gowdy announced on Jan. 31, 2018, that he would not seek re-election, intending to return to law. Since then, he has supported Robert Mueller's Russia investigation, disputed claims that the Nunes memo—which he co-wrote—proved a partisan witch hunt, and stated Russia was motivated to harm Clinton's candidacy. While defending Andrew McCabe's firing, Gowdy publicly warned President Trump against firing Mueller, predicting a "very, very long bad 2018."

The speaker is disappointed by a loss in which the team squandered two two-goal leads in the third period but remains positive and optimistic. The team plans to learn from its mistakes, persevere, and stick to one game plan. Returning home to supportive fans will be a boost. Every game is a must-win, and the focus is on responding in the next game.

The lecture covers iterative methods for solving large sparse linear systems Ax = b, where elimination is too expensive but matrix-vector multiplication is fast. Iterations use a preconditioner P, chosen to resemble A but be simpler; options include Jacobi (diagonal), Gauss-Seidel (lower triangular), successive overrelaxation (SOR), and incomplete LU, which discards fill-in beyond a tolerance. The iteration yields an error equation e(k+1) = Me(k) with M = I − P⁻¹A; convergence requires all eigenvalues of M to be below 1 in magnitude, with speed determined by the spectral radius. For the model 1D matrix (2s on the diagonal, −1s off), Jacobi's spectral radius is cos(π/(n+1)) ≈ 1 − O(1/n²), requiring O(n²) iterations, with low-frequency error components converging slowest. Weighted Jacobi (ω = 2/3) damps high frequencies but not low ones. Gauss-Seidel squares Jacobi's eigenvalues, roughly halving iterations, but multigrid is needed to handle low frequencies.

The Trump administration announced an amendment letting US businesses deny employees contraception coverage on religious or moral grounds, unwinding an Obamacare provision. The move drew anger from reproductive rights advocates and praise from conservative Christians.

A hockey coach reflects on his team's four-game sweep in the Stanley Cup Finals, which included three one-goal losses. He is disappointed but proud of the team's progress, comparing their situation to the Red Wings, who rebounded stronger after being swept. He attributes the loss to Detroit's finals experience, solid play in all areas, strong goaltending, and an experienced defense, noting his team's mistakes were costly. He praises Steve Yzerman as a deserving playoff MVP and Olaf Kolzig's outstanding goaltending. He calls Detroit's rally around an injured teammate emotional and professional. Rejecting suggestions the team should be embarrassed, he says his job was to instill a new attitude, views the series as a learning experience, and believes it will make the team better next year.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on January 28, 2020, reporting that it issued a press release announcing its financial results for its first fiscal quarter ended December 28, 2019. The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1. Apple, incorporated in California and headquartered in Cupertino, has common stock (AAPL) and various notes with maturities ranging from 2022 to 2042 registered on the Nasdaq Stock Market LLC. The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

This study examined the views of 45 pre-service teachers at a private university during the 2022-2023 academic year regarding a special education course delivered through distance education, using a phenomenological qualitative design and a researcher-created semi-structured interview form. The majority of participants reported satisfaction with taking the special education course via distance education, but noted difficulties caused by internet connection problems, from which it can be concluded that distance education courses are less effective than face-to-face education. Participants emphasized the importance of attendance for course success, even in distance education. Most participants recommended the distance education system, noting its importance for working individuals, the opportunity to become familiar with technology, and that it does not burden individuals economically. It was also highlighted that students experienced difficulties in their education due to technology/material deficiencies in distance education courses.

The passage addresses growing bearish warnings calling for immediate and drastic action as major equity indices regularly reach new all-time highs. The author plans to present a counterargument to these warnings using Ray Dalio's framework for diagnosing market bubbles, arguing that while bearish theses sound more compelling and action-oriented, historical data shows patient, "boring" strategies yield superior results. The passage also includes promotional material for the author's investing service, an author biography, and standard disclosure statements.

This passage is an April 16, 2001 email from Ann Schmidt compiling news articles, many involving Enron. Sierra Pacific suspended its quarterly dividend due to the Western U.S. energy crisis but still hopes to complete its $2 billion purchase of Enron's Portland General Electric unit. Britain's Crown Estates issued leases for 13 offshore wind farms as part of a renewable energy push. Internet rumor sites are forcing companies to manage layoff announcements differently; Enron denied broadband unit layoffs, and its stock rallied. Large energy companies are investing in solar and renewables as gas prices rise. Tech stocks rallied, with the Nasdaq up 14%, ahead of major earnings reports. Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay criticized the Bush administration's global warming stance, and Enron executive Thomas White Jr. is expected to be named Army Secretary. In India, the Godbole committee recommended renegotiating the tariff and dollar linkage of Enron's Dabhol power project, which has strained the Maharashtra State Electricity Board's finances; trade unions planned an April 25 bandh partly over the Enron issue. The DivX video format poses piracy risks to the movie industry, and talks between Blockbuster and Enron Broadband collapsed. Enron also restarted its 15,000 b/d MTBE plant in Morgan's Point, Texas after scheduled maintenance.

The passage describes the NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture and its key features. Turing's display engine supports native HDR processing with tone mapping per the ITU-R BT.2100 standard. The enhanced NVENC encoder adds H.265 8K encoding at 30 fps with bitrate savings for HEVC and H.264, while the NVDEC decoder supports HEVC 4:4:4 and VP9 10/12-bit HDR. Turing GPUs include hardware support for USB Type-C and VirtualLink, a new open standard delivering power, display, and data to VR headsets through a single USB-C connector. TU102 and TU104 GPUs use second-generation NVLink instead of MIO/PCIe for SLI, providing 25 GB/sec per direction per link, though only two-way SLI is supported.

Turing introduces RT Cores for hardware-accelerated ray tracing, enabling real-time ray tracing on a single GPU—roughly 10 times faster than Pascal's software-based approach. Hybrid rendering combines rasterization and ray tracing. The NGX deep learning stack uses Tensor Cores for AI features including DLSS (delivering TAA-comparable quality with roughly half the shading work), InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. Additional features include Mesh Shading (Task and Mesh Shaders) to eliminate CPU draw call bottlenecks, Variable Rate Shading with per-16x16-pixel-region control, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering supporting up to four views per pass.

The TU104 (used in GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000) contains 13.6 billion transistors, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores. The TU106 (GeForce RTX 2070) contains 10.8 billion transistors, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but lacks NVLink. The document also explains ray tracing mechanics (BVH acceleration, denoising, ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections), the RTX-OPS workload-based performance metric, and concludes with NVIDIA legal disclaimers and trademark notices.

A Reversal Day occurs when a stock or market index changes direction after an extended trend, often accompanied by high volume. A Bullish Reversal Day (Selling Climax) follows a downtrend, making a new low but closing above the previous day's high; a Bearish Reversal Day (Blowoff) follows a rally, making a new high but closing below the previous day's low. Reversals can be caused by changes in market sentiment, economic conditions, company-specific news, and technical factors. Traders can identify them through trend changes, heavy trading volume, and indicators such as moving averages, RSI, and Bollinger Bands. Stock, forex, commodity, and bond markets are all prone to reversals. Backtests in gold (GLD) showed the bullish strategy produced good profit factors but few trades, while the bearish version produced losses due to gold's upward drift. The authors conclude the Reversal Day concept has merit.

Cocoa futures are financial derivatives representing contracts to buy or sell a specified quantity of cocoa at a pre-agreed price on a future date. They trade on ICE (symbol CC, settled by physical delivery) and CME Globex/NYMEX (symbol CJ, financially settled), with a contract unit of 10 metric tons and expirations in March, May, July, September, and December. The minimum price fluctuation is $1.00 per metric ton ($10 per contract), and the block minimum is 100 contracts. As of November 25, 2022, cocoa futures traded at $2,484 per metric ton. The all-time high was $5,379 in July 1977, while the lowest price since 1979 was $707 in December 2000. Prices are driven by supply and demand factors, and the contracts tend to perform better in summer and poorly in spring and fall. Major risks include adverse price movements amplified by leverage and low market liquidity. The iPath Bloomberg Cocoa Subindex Total Return ETN (NIB) offers ETF exposure to cocoa. A backtested strategy achieved a 74% win rate and 2.3 profit factor over 96 trades.

MLPs ended 2016 up 18.3%, beating the S&P 500 for the first time since 2011; the equal-weight AMZE returned 22.5%, over 400 basis points above the traditional Alerian index. December's 4.4% return extended positive streaks and broke two straight negative Decembers. The equal-weight outperformance reflects smaller MLPs' rallies and unusual underperformance by Enterprise Products Partners, which for the first time since 2009 failed to beat the index. Global Partners led the sector for a second straight week; SunCoke Energy Partners was the year's top performer among distribution payers, while Ferrellgas was the biggest loser. General partners underperformed MLPs again. Plains GP Holdings filed to sell up to $500 million of units at-the-market, and Shell Midstream announced Gulf of Mexico pipeline acquisitions at a 7.7x EBITDA multiple.

Health savings accounts (HSAs), a decades-old Republican concept drawing renewed interest as lawmakers seek to replace the Affordable Care Act, permit tax-free investment growth and tax-free withdrawals for certain medical expenses. They are available only to those with high-deductible health plans, and only about 20 million of 176 million insured Americans have them, per a 2015 report. Low participation reflects lack of upfront money and psychological barriers to saving, including stress over financial decisions. Behavioral economist Mitesh Patel notes people hate losing money; his weight-loss study found loss-framed penalties motivated more participants than rewards. Making HSAs opt-out, like 401(k)s, could raise participation but cost the government money. An Employee Benefits Research Institute study found HSA users spent less on prescription drugs but had more emergency room visits, especially lower-income families. Unclear medical pricing complicates saving, and HSAs mainly help those with spare cash.

The S&P 500 Information Technology sector holds the highest weighting in the index, representing over a quarter of its market cap, and has experienced strong growth over the last decade. Major ETFs tracking the sector include VGT and XLK, with top stocks including Apple, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Broadcom, and Adobe. The article presents two backtested mean-reversion trading strategies. The first XLK strategy shows 245 trades, 0.96% average gain per trade, 10% CAGR (versus 8% buy and hold), 12% time in the market, 18% max drawdown, 71% win rate, and a 3.1 profit factor. The second strategy shows 212 trades, 1.05% average gain, 9.5% CAGR, 10% time in the market, 15% max drawdown, 70% win rate, and a 2.85 profit factor. Technology sector strategies may correlate strongly with the broader market, offering limited diversification benefits.

Debate surrounds whether MDC-T leader Morgan Tsvangirai helps or harms Zimbabwe's opposition. Once an asset who united the MDC and forced a 2008 run-off against Mugabe, his 2013 defeat, party splits, and cancer illness have made him a liability. The article argues he should allow leadership renewal, supporting a stronger leader to secure his legacy.

This study investigated the prevalence of burnout, associated factors, and coping strategies among prison officers (POs) at the Nsawam Medium Security Prison, Ghana. A descriptive cross-sectional quantitative study recruited 266 officers through proportionate stratified random sampling; 243 questionnaires were analyzed. Data were collected using a self-administered questionnaire adapted from the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey (MBI-HSS), Work Environment Scale, and Coping Methods Checklist, and analyzed in STATA version 16 using descriptive statistics, chi-square/Fisher's Exact tests, and logistic regression.

Most respondents were male (68.31%), aged 20–30 years (47.29%), single (57.61%), had senior high school education (54.73%), less than five years of service (60.90%), and were junior-ranked (78.19%). Regarding burnout dimensions, 42.0% had high emotional exhaustion, depersonalization was distributed across low (35.4%), moderate (32.1%), and high (32.5%) categories, and 68.7% had low personal accomplishment. Overall burnout prevalence was 9%. Perceived causes of burnout included irregular shifts (71.6%), heavy workload (49.0%), and lack of training and development opportunities (47.7%).

Shift allocation was significantly associated with emotional exhaustion (p=0.010), and officer rank was significantly associated with depersonalization (p=0.010), higher among junior officers. Burnout was significantly associated with sex (p=0.016), with higher rates among female officers; male officers had 69% reduced odds of burnout (AOR: 0.31), and officers with diploma/certificate had 89% reduced odds compared to postgraduates (AOR: 0.11). The main coping strategy was talking to colleagues (62.5%), followed by looking forward to off duty (60.1%) and talking to family (54.3%); alcohol use was least reported (29.2%).

The study concludes that attention should be paid to irregular shifts, heavy workload, and training and development opportunities to reduce burnout. POs experienced high emotional exhaustion and depersonalization with low personal accomplishment; emotional exhaustion was common among night-shift officers and depersonalization among junior officers, while POs adopted positive coping mechanisms.

The SD Card Association releases the Simplified Specification/Addendum, a subset of its complete specification, on a non-confidential, "AS-IS" basis without warranties. Implementation may require a license, and the Association assumes no responsibility for damages or patent infringements resulting from use.

The authors criticize Stanford's Program in Writing and Rhetoric (PWR), arguing it fails to teach academic writing skills. They contend that PWR courses use overly broad topics and lack rigorous instruction, instead telling students to simply write. The authors propose allowing experienced writers to place out of PWR, as Stanford permits in languages, mathematics, and science. They also argue that PWR grade distributions—in which over 80% of students in most courses receive A-range grades—show the program functions as box-checking rather than skill development, with professors grading leniently out of fear of negative course reviews. The authors further claim PWR courses exhibit a liberal political bias and suggest offering alternatives that examine issues through a conservative lens. They oppose a proposed PWR minor, announced at a recent Undergraduate Senate meeting, arguing the department should instead dedicate resources to improving existing classes. As an alternative, they propose that senior humanities professors design a standardized, source-based writing class to be taught by current PWR faculty, concluding that PWR cannot continue in its current form.

The prototype BMW M8 has provisional headlights, standard brakes, and downgraded wheels versus the June model. Though specifications are unreleased, it's expected to use the 7 Series CLAR platform, a 4.4-liter twin-turbo V8 producing over 600 horsepower, and all-wheel drive, potentially rivaling Ferrari or Lamborghini. The original M8 never entered production, but its V12 powered the McLaren F1.

Ottawa police are warning residents about an alleged swarming in which a woman faked car trouble on Innes Road Saturday around 5:30 p.m. to lure a Good Samaritan to her car on O'Toole Road, where she and two male accomplices allegedly robbed him of his wallet and cash. The victim was treated at hospital. Police released suspect and vehicle descriptions and are asking anyone with information to come forward.

At the Code Conference, Aileen Lee, Megan Smith, and Sukhinder Singh Cassidy discussed diversity and inclusion in tech. Lee criticized the "good guy" standard used to qualify men for opportunities, noting women and people of color face different, qualification-focused questions, and called for removing bias from business processes. The panel addressed board diversity and backlash, and Smith noted women of color are most left out.

StockX is adding streetwear brands BAPE and Palace to its marketplace, whose streetwear category launched in October 2017 with an exclusive Supreme collection. Scotty Newman serves as BAPE general manager and Kenny Locklier leads PALACE. At launch, StockX will be the largest authenticated marketplace for BAPE, with over 4,000 products, and PALACE, with more than 3,000. BAPE was founded in 1993 by NIGO and acquired by I.T. Group in 2011; PALACE was launched in 2010 by Lev Tanju. StockX, founded in February 2016 by Josh Luber, Greg Schwartz and Dan Gilbert, has over 200 employees and more than $2 million in daily sales.

Vertigo, an iOS music-sharing app launched last month, now integrates with both Spotify and Apple Music, making it the first iOS app to enable cross-platform music sharing. Users can import playlists, discover music, and share songs so friends can listen using their own subscriptions. The app also offers live sessions featuring streaming video, photos, real-time chat, and audio commentary. Vertigo serves only paid subscribers and pays royalties to rights holders. The app may help fill the social gap in Apple Music, which has downplayed its social features.

Country music legend Glen Campbell is battling the final stages of Alzheimer's disease. In a People magazine interview, his family said music has become a comforting part of his life, as he often smiles and sings along. His final album, "Adios," recorded in 2012 and released June 9, reflects his enduring love of music.

This study presents a streamlined laboratory workflow for analyzing and reporting Optical Genome Mapping (OGM) data using Variant Intelligence Applications (VIA) software in hematologic malignancies. Ten retrospective cases (nine AML, one MDS) were independently reviewed 5-6 times each by technologist-director teams to assess efficiency and reproducibility. All variants identified by standard of care (SOC) testing were detected by OGM via VIA, while OGM additionally revealed variants absent from SOC reports in five of six positive cases, including complex rearrangements and small deletions undetectable by karyotype or FISH. Technologist review times averaged 25.2 minutes for negative cases, 28.5 minutes for simple cases, and 47.3 minutes for complex cases, representing approximately a 50% time reduction compared to Bionano Access alone. The workflow enabled automated pre-classification of Tier 1A variants according to international guidelines, resulting in unanimous identification of key fusions. The authors conclude that OGM analysis using VIA offers a streamlined, efficient, and objective approach to cytogenomic variant interpretation and reporting in hematologic disorders, with potential to standardize analysis and address labor shortages in clinical laboratories.

For Fire Prevention Week, the Montecito Fire Protection District will teach fire safety to 800 elementary school children through Oct. 14. Younger children learn "Stop Drop and Roll" and "Crawl Low in Smoke"; third and fourth graders use a Fire Safety Trailer to practice spotting hazards, calling 9-1-1, and exiting safely. Oct. 3-6 activities are canceled due to weather and will be rescheduled.

The reporter traveled by train through Germany, Austria, Italy, and Switzerland in October 2022 using a weeklong Eurail pass costing $477, plus additional fees of $10–$45 for overnight trains and class upgrades, for a total of $560. Over seven days, she took eight train rides between six cities and preferred the experience to flying, which she estimated would cost about $440. She found trains more comfortable, citing business-class seating, a sleeper cabin, easier boarding, scenic views, and avoiding ear-popping and dehydration. She also noted train travel is more sustainable and plans to travel by train in Europe going forward.

The Rio Blanco 4-H senior team concluded its 2018 Livestock Judging Season at the 73rd annual Colorado 4-H June conference at Colorado State University. Macy Collins finished third high individual overall and Marryn Shults seventh. In divisions, Shults placed fourth in beef and fifth in sheep/goat, while Collins placed fifth in beef, third in swine, and fourth in sheep/goat. Overall, Shults placed seventh with 572 points and Collins eighth with 570. Collins finished third in oral reasons and made the Colorado State 4-H Livestock All State team. She will attend Hutchinson Junior College on a full academic and judging scholarship.

Brazilian stocks rose Thursday, led by miner Vale SA after first-quarter iron ore output jumped 11.2 percent year-over-year to a record, lifting its shares up to 4.9 percent. Steelmaker Usiminas also gained after reversing a quarterly loss. The Brazilian real stayed volatile amid geopolitical tensions and elections in France and the UK, though polls favoring Macron eased some investor concerns.

President Donald Trump warned Iran against restarting its nuclear program as he met French President Emmanuel Macron to seek common ground on the 2015 Iran nuclear deal, which Trump criticized as "terrible" for not addressing ballistic missiles or Iran's role in conflicts like Yemen and Syria. Iran has threatened to ramp up its nuclear program and possibly quit a nuclear non-proliferation treaty if the deal collapses. Macron, hoping to persuade Trump to keep the United States in the agreement, said it offers the best chance to constrain Tehran. A U.S. withdrawal could raise regional tensions and complicate efforts regarding North Korea. The leaders also discussed steel tariff exemptions and U.S. troops in Syria, and Trump thanked France for joining recent airstrikes against Syria.

The holder is the player who holds the ball for the kicker on field goals and extra points. After catching the snap, the holder must quickly and precisely place the ball in the kicker's preferred spot and angle, with the laces facing away from the kicker. Required skills include soft hands, consistency, quick placement, and the ability to rotate the football. Holders may also participate in fake field goals by throwing, flipping, or running with the ball. The position, abbreviated "H," can be filled by anyone, though punters, backup quarterbacks, and receivers are common choices. No holding statistics are tracked, and holders typically have other primary roles. Despite being overlooked, the holder's work can determine whether scoring opportunities are converted or missed.

The Daily Examiner is moving from a metered digital subscription model to a premium model, with some stories accessible only to subscribers. Public safety information and some local stories remain free. Subscriber-only content will be marked with a PLUS symbol. Existing subscribers are unaffected and retain unlimited access, including to News Corp sites. Subscriptions include a newsletter, breaking news alerts, app access, and optional Saturday paper delivery.

Thailand's road deaths fell 11 per cent to 390 during Songkran week after a junta crackdown on drink driving, including harsher penalties, vehicle seizures and mortuary visits; earlier campaigns showed no reduction. Junta chief Prayut Chan-O-Cha said more work remains. Thailand has the world's second most dangerous roads per capita; 28 per cent of Songkran accidents were caused by drunk driving. Myanmar reported 285 road deaths.

The European Union, spearheaded by Germany and France, is preparing a draft policy to push multilateral development banks (MDBs) such as the World Bank to prioritise climate action, despite U.S. opposition. The proposal urges MDBs to align financing with the Paris Agreement, redirect lending from fossil fuels to low-carbon initiatives, improve transparency, provide local currency financing, and de-risk climate investments to attract private sector participation. It will feature at the upcoming World Bank and IMF annual meetings. U.S. officials warn the shift could distract banks from poverty alleviation and economic growth. MDBs channelled a record $137 billion into climate projects in 2024, which EU leaders consider insufficient. If adopted, the proposal could reshape development finance, though consensus may prove elusive.

The Supreme Court of Canada has ruled unanimously that records detailing the abuse of former residential school students can eventually be destroyed, upholding a lower court ruling that sensitive material from the independent assessment process be destroyed after 15 years. The court said the 2006 settlement agreement's negotiators intended the compensation process to be confidential, and claimants and alleged perpetrators relied on those assurances.

Eric Thames hit a two-run homer in the fifth inning, accounting for the only runs as the Milwaukee Brewers beat the Minnesota Twins 2-0 on Tuesday in Milwaukee. It was Thames' third home run in six games. Pinch-hitter Nate Orf walked and stole second before Thames homered off Twins starter Jake Odorizzi (3-6), who allowed two runs and four hits over five innings. Brewers starter Junior Guerra (5-5) pitched five shutout innings, giving up two hits with three walks and eight strikeouts. Josh Hader threw three hitless relief innings, and Corey Knebel earned his ninth save by striking out the side in the ninth. The Twins fell to 1-7 on their nine-game road trip.

This email, forwarded by Enron's Steven Kean on December 8, 2000, contains a McKinsey memorandum dated December 6, 2000, by Carol B White and Pru Sheppard, providing a periodic update on international electric power sector privatization and restructuring for June–November 2000. The memo reports that privatization and restructuring continue globally: governments facing growing power demand are opening generation markets to foreign investors, unbundling state-owned utilities, and introducing wholesale and retail competition, though some international players have scaled back and shifted portfolios toward less risky U.S. and European markets. In Europe, competition has been spurred by the EU Directive, with mergers, alliances, and consolidation a dominant theme; country updates cover Austria, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the UK. In Central and Eastern Europe, privatization continues to attract capital, with the IMF urging reforms and EU membership candidates moving forward. In Asia-Pacific, recovering economies are resuming unbundling and restructuring plans, though IPPs face problems with PPAs and lack of government guarantees. In Latin America, privatizations are restarting at a slower pace after currency devaluations, and droughts have strained hydro-dependent systems. In Africa and the Middle East, governments are increasingly open to foreign investment, mostly via IPPs, with regional transmission link schemes emerging. Exhibits summarizing regional restructuring status and market-opening timelines are attached.

Former CIA case officer Kevin Mallory, 60, is on trial in Alexandria, Virginia, accused of giving a Chinese agent information about human assets and other top-secret material in exchange for $25,000. Prosecutors say his scheme unraveled after customs agents found $16,500 in undeclared cash when he returned from Shanghai in April 2017, and that he then contacted old CIA contacts as a cover. A Samsung phone from the Chinese revealed text conversations, and a home search found discs containing secret and top-secret documents, some sent to the recruiter. Defense lawyers say Mallory was a loyal American who contacted the CIA in February 2017, before the trip, about a suspicious Chinese think-tank offer. Mallory faces up to life in prison.

On Inauguration Day since 1789, Americans have renewed their dedication to the nation: Washington's generation created it, Lincoln's preserved it from internal disruption, and the present task is saving it from external disruption. The speaker asserts that a nation's life depends on its will to live, not the count of years, and rejects claims that democracy is doomed while tyranny advances. Facing crisis eight years earlier, Americans acted quickly, boldly, and decisively, and the crisis was survived within the constitutional framework, with the Bill of Rights inviolate and free elections maintained—proof that democracy is not dying. A nation, like a person, has a body, a mind, and a spirit, the spirit being greatest. The American spirit and faith, formed over centuries by those seeking freedom, appear in the Mayflower Compact, the Declaration of Independence, the Constitution, and the Gettysburg Address. More remains to be done to build security, opportunity, and knowledge for every citizen and to reject undeserved poverty and self-serving wealth. Preserving the nation's spirit justifies every sacrifice for national defense, and Americans will not retreat but go forward in the service of their country.

Industrial enterprises face challenges including geopolitical uncertainty, rising energy prices, supply chain disruptions, skilled labor shortages, and sustainability pressures, while digitalization transforms manufacturing. This IDC white paper, based on a December 2021 survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers at manufacturing enterprises (500+ employees) in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, examines IT-based simulation, modeling, and data analysis, and the role of high-performance computing (HPC).

Simulation and modeling support key business goals, particularly innovation (cited by three-quarters of respondents), faster product development, cost reduction, and improved quality. Deployment is expected to reach 90% across product development, production planning, and quality management within two years. However, data silos hinder potential; IDC recommends a unified data strategy creating a "single source of truth."

Key technology trends include digital twins, virtual prototyping, and engineering workstations as a service. Demand for high-performance calculations is expected to grow sharply, with 81% of decision makers viewing HPC as a game changer for product and process innovation.

Most enterprises prefer external HPC infrastructure: 87% use or plan cloud providers, 74% use or plan colocation datacenters, and only 6% operate on-premises HPC. Key challenges include security concerns (72%), energy consumption and sustainability (58%), and lack of expertise (42%).

Cloud-based HPC and HPC-as-a-Service offer scalability, cost flexibility, and access to modern technologies, with 81% of current HPC users intending to implement HPC-based business models. IDC recommends holistic data strategies, careful evaluation of HPC operating models, attention to scalability, security, and energy efficiency, and leveraging external expertise.

This passage is the AMD Geode™ CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 Specification Update (31534D, March 2006), a list of errata items with descriptions, implications, and resolutions. Key issues include: the PIC failing to recognize new edge-detected interrupts when a source remains high after the Diverse Device's automatic Local bus clock gating turns off, potentially hanging the system (workaround: disable automatic clock gating); ATAC and ACC GeodeLink Adaptor prefetching the first four bytes of the next PRD when PRD tables are not 8-byte aligned, a hazard only if software modifies PRD entries during operation; UDMA write CRC corruption after device termination, caused by corrupted state from a prior UDMA read with host termination; ATAC SSMI during DMA not blocking IDE I/O (debug-only feature); the main GLIU clock domain failing to awaken for statistics-counter ASMIs when clock gating is enabled; byte accesses to ACPI PM1_STS/PM1_EN registers hanging; WORD/BYTE writes to PMC registers corrupting the same or unrelated registers; KEL issues including CmdData always reading 0, Snoop mode altering HCE register state, and AuxOutputfull being cleared by Port 60h reads; most wake event inputs (GPIO[27:24]) not functioning from ACPI S3; RTC CMOS legacy data port reads returning extended-port data; LPC I/O failures during block/demand mode legacy DMA; USB controller clock gating causing register read failures; IRDY#/DEVSEL# tVAL guaranteed at 1.5 ns versus the 2 ns specification; unreliable SSMI generation when an IRQ coincides; UDMA failure when the bus master is enabled before the PIO command packet; ATAPI bus master reset on an unexpected IDE interrupt; ATAC hangs with WORD-aligned PRDs; LPC aborts on delayed SYNC patterns from LPC-to-ISA bridges; SMB NEGACK bit setting and clearing anomalies; the GLPCI retry counter counting other devices' retries; GPIO High Bank atomic writes clearing non-selected bits after suspend; SMBus data hold time below the 300 ns specification; LOWBAT_FLAG not being set after abnormal standby; and Sleep_X/Sleep_Y not deasserting when delay counters exceed the PM_SED delay. The document concludes with AMD copyright and disclaimer text.

Uber's panic button, announced in April following alleged sexual assaults, lets riders dial 911 from the app. In most cities it displays the rider's real-time location; in pilot cities it automatically sends location and vehicle details to emergency dispatchers.

After losing to Detroit, the speaker cited early nerves and a letdown after conceding the first goal. Aside from the first ten minutes, the game was fairly even, but the power play failed to generate chances. The opponent is defensively sound, and the speaker admitted not playing their best, emphasizing the need to improve.

In spring 1953, the free world weighs the chance for a just peace, a hope that has dimmed since 1945, when Western Allied and Russian soldiers met as victorious comrades before the nations divided onto separate paths. The United States and free nations chose cooperation, respect for each nation's right to choose its own government, and peace based on understanding rather than an arms race; the Soviet Union pursued security through force and power superiority. Soviet armament compelled free nations to spend heavily on weapons and unite in purpose, though they remain ready to welcome genuine evidence of peaceful intent. Continued militarization risks atomic war at worst and perpetual fear and tension at best, diverting resources from human needs—the cost of bombers and warships measured in schools, hospitals, housing, and food. Stalin's death ended a 30-year era, and new Soviet leadership faces an aroused free world committed to NATO unity and collective defense. The United States proposes an honorable armistice in Korea with free elections in a united Korea, an end to attacks on Indochina and Malaya, an Austrian treaty, European unity including a free Germany, and disarmament agreements covering force limits, atomic energy control, and UN inspection. Savings from disarmament would fund world aid and reconstruction. The test of Soviet sincerity lies in deeds, not words.

This study examines the effect of digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth on sustainable supply chain performance through brand image and supply chain image, focusing on Indonesian ICT companies. Digitalization is essential for business competitiveness and supply chain performance, though firms face financial and technological constraints in adopting digital supply chains. The study hypothesizes that digital customer experience through e-commerce practices and electronic word of mouth positively affect brand image, which enhances supply chain image and, in turn, sustainable supply chain performance, with brand image and supply chain image serving as mediators. Data were collected from employees involved in distribution at Indonesian ICT companies; 568 questionnaires were distributed and 315 valid responses were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Results confirmed all seven hypotheses: digital customer experience (t=3.086) and electronic word of mouth (t=11.084) positively affect brand image; brand image positively affects supply chain image (t=25.167); supply chain image positively affects sustainable supply chain performance (t=84.298); and all mediation effects were significant. The model explains 82.3% of the variance in sustainable supply chain performance. The study concludes that Indonesian ICT companies should enhance brand image through digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth by implementing e-commerce practices, thereby improving supply chain and overall performance.

This patent application, a divisional of U.S. application Ser. No. 15/200,149 (filed July 1, 2016) and made with NASA support under Contract No. NNC14CA32C, describes a hybrid gas turbine electric propulsion system and a method for operating it during descent. The engine is a two-spool geared turbofan with an electric motor connected to the low-speed spool, allowing the engine to be undersized relative to thrust requirements during takeoff or top of climb. During descent, the core is shut down or operated at a minimum temperature to prevent thermal cycling, while aircraft systems are powered by electricity generated by the motor in earlier modes and stored in an energy storage system. The fan is allowed to windmill, spinning the motor as a generator; alternatively, the motor can drive the low-speed spool to produce thrust sufficient to overcome engine drag. An electric compressor can replace compressor bleed air for systems such as environmental control.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on February 8, 2021, it consummated the issuance and sale of six series of notes: $2,500,000,000 of 0.700% Notes due 2026, $2,500,000,000 of 1.200% Notes due 2028, $2,750,000,000 of 1.650% Notes due 2031, $1,500,000,000 of 2.375% Notes due 2041, $3,000,000,000 of 2.650% Notes due 2051, and $1,750,000,000 of 2.800% Notes due 2061. The notes were sold pursuant to an underwriting agreement dated February 1, 2021 among Apple and Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, and Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, as representatives of the underwriters. The notes were issued under an indenture dated November 5, 2018 between Apple and The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A., as trustee. Interest is payable semi-annually on February 8 and August 8, beginning August 8, 2021. The notes are Apple's senior unsecured obligations, ranking equally with its other unsecured and unsubordinated debt. The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

This IDC white paper discusses High-Performance Computing (HPC) in the manufacturing industry. Cloud providers offer modern technologies and continuous innovation, with 52% of respondents considering fast access to cutting-edge analysis, simulation methods, and state-of-the-art hardware a core aspect of HPCaaS. Executives from Hexagon and Bridgestone cite energy efficiency and a step-by-step cloud adoption approach. The paper concludes that IT-based simulations, modeling, and data analytics are key enablers for industrial enterprises facing disruptive changes, and that HPC technologies are becoming a prerequisite for modern simulations. Public cloud and HPCaaS can expand the agility and scalability of in-house HPC clusters or replace them entirely. A seamless, consistent database across the entire product life cycle is deemed essential for innovation, productivity, and competitiveness. IDC recommends establishing virtual product development, creating a holistic data strategy, evaluating the appropriate HPC operating model, prioritizing scalability, security, and energy efficiency, and leveraging external expertise. Findings are based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 decision makers from industrial enterprises with over 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

NVIDIA Corporation filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended October 30, 2022 (Q3 fiscal 2023). Revenue was $5.93 billion for the quarter, down 17% year-over-year, and $20.92 billion for the first nine months, up 9% year-over-year. Net income was $680 million for the quarter (down 72% from $2.46 billion a year earlier) and $2.95 billion for the nine months. Diluted earnings per share were $0.27 for the quarter. Gross margin declined to 53.6% from 65.2%, primarily due to a $702 million inventory charge largely related to lower Data Center demand in China, partially offset by a $70 million warranty-related benefit.

In February 2022, NVIDIA and SoftBank terminated the Share Purchase Agreement for NVIDIA's acquisition of Arm due to significant regulatory challenges, resulting in a $1.35 billion acquisition termination cost recorded in the first quarter. During the quarter, the U.S. government announced new license requirements restricting exports of A100 and H100 products to China (including Hong Kong) and Russia; NVIDIA responded by offering alternative products such as the A800. NVIDIA also closed its business operations in Russia during the quarter.

By segment, Compute & Networking revenue was $3.82 billion (up 27% year-over-year), while Graphics revenue was $2.12 billion (down 48%). By market platform: Data Center revenue was $3.83 billion (up 31%), Gaming was $1.57 billion (down 51%), Professional Visualization was $200 million (down 65%), Automotive was $251 million (up 86%), and OEM and Other was $73 million (down 69%).

As of October 30, 2022, total assets were $40.49 billion, cash and marketable securities totaled $13.14 billion, and total shareholders' equity was $21.35 billion. Outstanding debt consisted of senior notes maturing between 2023 and 2060, with a net carrying amount of approximately $10.95 billion. During the quarter, NVIDIA repurchased 28 million shares for $3.65 billion and paid $100 million in dividends; $8.28 billion remained under its share repurchase authorization through December 2023. Shares outstanding were 2.46 billion as of November 11, 2022.

The company reported total gross future unconditional purchase commitments of $9.77 billion. Pending legal matters include a securities class action on appeal to the Ninth Circuit and related derivative lawsuits concerning statements about channel inventory and cryptocurrency mining's impact on GPU demand; no accrual for these contingencies was recorded.

Olean's Common Council authorized Mayor Bill Aiello to apply for the state's $10 million Downtown Revitalization Initiative, which awards $100 million to 10 communities. The application was due hours after approval. The proposed area spans Olean General Hospital to the Allegheny River and Franchot Park to Seventh Street. Project ideas include redeveloping the Manufacturers Hanover building, business incubator funding, expanded downtown theater options, better pedestrian access to Lincoln Park, and a park near the hospital. The city may also receive over $2 million through Buffalo Billion. Jamestown Community College's John Sayegh praised the effort and offered to help upgrade the Cutco Theater.

A federal judge ruled that the 1991 Nirvana album cover showing a naked baby underwater is not child pornography. U.S. District Judge Fernando Olguin dismissed Spencer Elden's 2021 lawsuit; Elden was photographed as a 4-month-old. Olguin found that, aside from nudity, no factor supporting a child pornography finding applied, likening the image to a family photo of a nude child bathing.

Donna Adelson, 75, was sentenced to life in prison plus 30 years for conspiracy and solicitation in the 2014 murder-for-hire killing of Florida State University law professor Dan Markel, her former son-in-law. Before sentencing, she maintained her innocence, claiming she was convicted without evidence. Judge Stephen Everett interrupted to warn he could consider her "utter lack of remorse." Prosecutors said she plotted with her son Charlie Adelson, who used his girlfriend, Katherine Magbanua, as a go-between to hire two hit men. The alleged motive was the family's desire to move Markel's ex-wife, Wendi Adelson, to South Florida with their children; she has not been charged.

Rising interest rates have pushed average 30-year fixed mortgage costs near 5 percent. Scott Sheldon outlines techniques to improve mortgage borrowing power: paying off debt, since lenders evaluate minimum monthly payments rather than interest rates and debt-to-income ratios should stay below 50 percent; obtaining a co-signer, who shares 50/50 liability and can only be removed through refinancing or selling the property; changing loan programs, such as switching from conventional to FHA loans; putting more money down, though this is less effective than paying off debt; and changing jobs within the same field, such as moving from hourly to salaried or self-employed to W2 employment.

Singapore is a small, densely populated Southeast Asian nation that achieved developed-world status within four decades of its 1965 independence, becoming a globally competitive hub for finance, commerce, and education, with student performance consistently ranked among the top internationally.

Special education in Singapore developed across two periods, pre- and post-2004. Before 2004, educating students with disabilities fell primarily to the social welfare sector, with special schools run by voluntary welfare organizations (now social service agencies) operating separately from mainstream schools in a dual system. Mainstream schools could refuse admission to students with disabilities, and Singapore had no legislation mandating special education services in mainstream schools; the focus was integration rather than inclusion.

The year 2004 was a watershed, when Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong envisioned Singapore as an inclusive society and called for better integration of students with disabilities into mainstream schools. Subsequent developments included the Enabling Masterplans (2007–2011, 2012–2016, 2017–2021, and 2022–2030) and ratification of the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in 2013. Students with disabilities in mainstream schools grew from 2,500 in 2005 to 35,500 currently; about 80% are served in mainstream schools and 20% in the 22 special schools. The 2019 Compulsory Education Act requires all students with special educational needs to attend mainstream primary schools or government-funded special schools.

Teacher preparation developments since 2005 include Special Needs Officers (later renamed SENOs) trained through a one-year Diploma in Special Education at the National Institute of Education (NIE); the Certificate in Special Needs Support for mainstream teachers; a 2020 professional development roadmap for all mainstream educators; and compulsory pre-service coursework on diverse learners. Special school teacher preparation evolved from the 1984 Certificate in Special Education to the Diploma in Special Education (DISE), the Advanced Diploma, and master's and doctoral options.

These reforms were enabled by tripartism among the Ministry of Education (MOE), NIE, and schools, centralized policy control with decentralized school autonomy, and uninterrupted PAP governance allowing long-term planning.

Salient issues include: special schools and their teachers remaining under social service agencies rather than MOE, with lower salaries than mainstream teachers; limited special education options within mainstream schools for students with higher support needs, despite initiatives like Satellite Partnerships to foster interaction between students; and special education teacher preparation that remains less comprehensive than mainstream preparation, with no undergraduate special education degree at NIE.

Singapore's education system is shifting toward holistic student development through the "Learn for Life" movement, and special education's role in preparing teachers is anticipated to continue expanding.

Myrna LaPlante, a Saskatoon woman whose aunt Emily Osmond went missing in 2006, supports chief commissioner Marion Buller and would withdraw her family's story if the inquiry were reset. She said families weren't consulted before the Assembly of First Nations voted 48-15 to call for Buller's resignation, though she supports a two-year deadline extension beyond November 2018. Other Saskatchewan families, including Lillian Ewenin, back Buller's resignation, citing poor communication at the Saskatoon hearings; Danielle Ewenin said the commission ignored the holistic approach needed to address community trauma.

An email dated July 31, 2001 from Jean Munoz distributes a compilation of energy-related news articles ("IEP News 7/31"). The articles cover: a commentary criticizing Governor Davis' $43 billion long-term power contracts as unnecessarily costly, attributing market improvement instead to cool weather, conservation, recession, and federal price caps; a Securities and Exchange Commission preliminary inquiry, requested by Secretary of State Bill Jones, into whether Davis' energy consultants used inside information to trade power company stocks, following the firing of five consultants for conflicts of interest; disclosure that Davis' press secretary Steve Maviglio purchased Calpine stock, which he denies constitutes a conflict of interest; consultants Chris Lehane and Mark Fabiani agreeing to forgo payment in settlement of a taxpayer lawsuit; Davis' struggling efforts to bail out Southern California Edison, a major campaign contributor, ahead of an August 15 legislative deadline; two San Francisco ballot measures to create public power districts, which PG&E is spending over $200,000 to defeat; a Maryland regulatory hearing on Baltimore Gas and Electric's proposed corporate split; a FERC decision reducing California's potential power refunds to roughly $3.9 billion, well below the $9 billion requested, which Davis plans to appeal; and the launch of Texas' electricity deregulation pilot program.

Sony has released a firmware update for its A7Riii camera, primarily fixing the 'Set File Name' function and improving overall stability. Mac users running macOS 10.13 (High Sierra) may be unable to install it, as that version is unsupported—a Mac OS issue rather than a Sony problem. Workarounds include using an earlier Mac OS version or running Windows.

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture by Professor William Green covers PDEs and introduces probability. Homework 7 requires solving a drug patch diffusion problem using both COMSOL and a self-written finite volume code. The problem's small characteristic length (due to the drug's low diffusivity) and large Peclet number create sharp gradients requiring fine mesh resolution; students must verify convergence rather than trusting code output. The finite volume method treats cells as small CSTRs, computing fluxes exactly at boundaries, which improves numerical stability; ghost volumes can be used to impose boundary conditions. Since the problem is linear and produces sparse matrices, solvers like backslash or conjugate gradient methods (BiCGSTAB) are appropriate, though iterative solvers require initial guesses. For time-dependent PDEs, the CFL number (delta t times velocity divided by delta x) must be kept near or below 1 to avoid unphysical results, and refining the spatial mesh increases computational cost doubly. Adaptive meshing can improve accuracy but is bug-prone. The lecture then introduces probability, noting that real measurements involve noise and intrinsic fluctuations, continuum equations represent ensemble averages, and quantum mechanics yields only probability distributions. Basic concepts covered include joint and conditional probabilities, Bayes' theorem, probability densities (which carry units and must be multiplied by intervals), and cumulative probability distributions.

On Feb. 14, the New York Times reported U.S. agencies intercepted calls between Russian intelligence officials and members of Trump's 2016 campaign team, including Paul Manafort, though officials found no evidence the campaign worked with Russians on election hacking. The FBI interviewed former national security adviser Michael Flynn about his interactions with a top Russian official; Flynn was ousted amid concerns he misled administration officials about contact with the Russian ambassador. Senate Minority Leader Schumer called for an independent investigation of the Flynn matter, insisting Attorney General Sessions recuse himself. At least five Republican senators, including John Thune, withheld support for labor secretary nominee Andrew Puzder pending his confirmation hearing over late-paid taxes for an unauthorized housekeeper. Linda McMahon was confirmed 81-19 to lead the Small Business Administration, and David Shulkin was unanimously confirmed as Veterans Affairs secretary, the first nonveteran to head the department.

A 1968 study by Lew Goldberg, recounted in Michael Lewis' *The Undoing Project*, asked doctors to assess cancer probability in 96 stomach ulcers, showing each ulcer twice without their knowledge. The doctors disagreed with each other and even contradicted their own earlier diagnoses. The researchers then built a simple computer algorithm based on how the doctors said they made their diagnoses, and it outperformed even the best doctor in the group. The author questions how the algorithm was created and how it accessed data, suspecting humans coded the x-rays. While experts may still be needed to write programs, AI and big data increasingly generate rules themselves, raising the question of how long experts will remain necessary.

The United Way of Northwest Illinois will launch Dolly Parton's Imagination Library in Carroll County on March 28, 2018, at the Mt. Carroll Township Public Library, providing books to children ages 0-5.

This lecture continues the discussion of D-branes in string theory. Quantizing open strings on D-branes yields massless gauge fields and scalar fields, with the scalars describing the D-brane's motion, making it dynamical. The D-brane's mass is defined as the vacuum energy of all open strings living on it, equal to its tension times volume, and can be computed via a Euclidean path integral summing over surfaces with boundaries (disk, annulus, etc.), weighted by gs to the power of minus the Euler number, which now includes the number of boundaries. At weak coupling, the D-brane mass scales as 1/gs.

An alternative computation considers the gravitational interaction between two D-branes via closed string (graviton) exchange, represented by a cylinder diagram. Remarkably, the same diagram can be viewed as a one-loop open string stretching between the branes—this channel duality hints at holographic duality, the equivalence between gravity and gauge theory.

At low energies, the effective action for the massless modes on a D-brane is the Dirac-Born-Infeld action, combining a nonlinear generalization of Maxwell theory (originally invented in the 1930s) with the relativistic volume element of the brane. The scalar fields are Goldstone bosons of the translation symmetry spontaneously broken by the brane's presence.

The open string coupling is the square root of the closed string coupling. When N D-branes coincide, open strings carry two indices forming N×N matrices, and string interactions exhibit U(N) symmetry—a global symmetry on the worldsheet that becomes a gauge symmetry in spacetime, yielding Yang-Mills theory at low energies with coupling related to gs. Separating branes gives stretched strings a mass proportional to the separation, breaking the gauge symmetry via a Higgs mechanism, so branes can split into stacks with symmetry broken to products of U(nᵢ).

Which? research suggests lenders have been slow to pass rate rises to savers while quickly raising mortgage costs. After the November base rate rise from 0.25% to 0.5%, 48% of 327 variable instant access savings accounts and ISAs saw no change within five weeks, and only 10% of 95 providers applied the full rise to all such accounts.
