Reference files reside in \Addendum, build control files (.inf) in \UEFI, and environment variables AGESA_ROOT and AGESA_OptsDir must be set. Two build methods exist: Binary Modules (indirect) and Source Integration.

Stack procedures, provided as native-assembly macros, establish or destroy the Cache-As-RAM stack; the host must not modify cache controls (MTRRs) during the CAR period. AARCH64 APUs with the Platform Security Processor do not use these macros, as the PSP initializes DRAM. Service functions include AmdCreateStruct (PreMemHeap, PostMemDram, and ByHost allocation methods), AmdReleaseStruct, and AmdReadEventLog, plus routines for DIMM data eye results, APIC/PCI addresses, execution cache size, core identification, address-to-DIMM mapping, and MMIO range allocation.

Entry procedures in time point order: AmdInitReset (minimal post-reset initialization with execution cache allocation rules), AmdInitEarly (full processor/HyperTransport initialization), AmdInitPost (memory initialization), AmdInitEnv (HOB/artifact transfer to main memory), a graphics display configuration step, AmdInitLate (ACPI/DMI table generation), and AmdInitRtb (Ready-To-Boot suspend preparation). Only published entry functions are assured availability over time. AmdInitResume and subsequent restore routines handle the resume path. Required host call-outs are AgesaAllocateBuffer, AgesaDeallocateBuffer, and a reset call-out (cold or warm).

This Motley Fool Money article reviews credit card offers. The Wells Fargo Active Cash Card offers unlimited 2% cash rewards with no categories or limits, a $200 bonus after spending $500 in the first three months, 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers (then 18.99%–28.99% variable APR), a $0 annual fee, and up to $600 cell phone protection with a $25 deductible. It is recommended for applicants with good/excellent credit (670–850). The Capital One Quicksilver offers unlimited 1.5% cash back, 5% on hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Travel, $300 in welcome bonuses, 15 months of 0% intro APR, and no annual or foreign transaction fees. A Citi card offers 2% cash back (1% at purchase, 1% at payment), a $200 bonus after spending $1,500 in six months, and 0% intro APR on balance transfers for 18 months. The site discloses that it receives partner compensation, which does not influence its product ratings.

This article compares dollar-cost averaging (DCA) with lump-sum investing, examining how luck, randomness, and sequence of returns affect results through backtests. DCA involves investing gradually over time, while lump-sum investing deploys capital at the earliest opportunity; DCA and scale-in are essentially the same. A September 2020 Morningstar study found DCA beat lump-sum investing only 27.8% of the time over 10-month periods and 10% over 10-year periods. However, DCA can remove fear from decisions, as illustrated by Peter Lynch's finding that annual January investments from 1975–2000 returned 11%, versus 10.6% when investing at yearly highs and 11.7% at lows. Backtests starting with 60,000 USD in January 2000 on the S&P 500 showed lump-sum investing grew to 193,157 USD (6.02% CAGR, with a 55% drawdown in 2008), while DCA reached 173,949 USD (5.5% CAGR). When the sequence of returns was reversed, DCA results fell to 87,396 USD (1.9% CAGR), while lump-sum results barely changed. The article concludes that lump-sum investing is generally the better option, as sequence of returns risk can severely harm DCA outcomes.

Weber State University canceled its 27th annual Unity Conference, themed "Redacted: Navigating the Complexities of Censorship," after presenters were directed days before the event to remove mentions of "DEI," "diversity," "equity," and "inclusion" from their slides. Professor Sarah Herrmann and other faculty withdrew rather than comply, and organizers canceled the Oct. 1 event, drawing criticism from FIRE over the irony of censoring a conference about censorship. The conference was funded by the Student Access and Success division, making it subject to Utah's HB 261, which restricts certain discussions in non-academic programming; academically sponsored events are exempt. Faculty noted the Utah legislature has pressured public universities, including budget cuts that led to closing a small queer studies program. The university is considering housing future conferences under Academic Affairs to exempt them from the law.

The article reviews nine Vanguard ETFs for ultimate diversification: Total Stock Market (VTI), Total World Stock (VT), Total International Stock (VXUS), Real Estate (VNQ), Global ex-U.S. Real Estate (VNQI), Total Corporate Bond (VTC), Total Bond Market (BND), Total International Bond (BNDX), and Total World Bond (BNDW). Vanguard, founded by John Bogle—who died in 2019 and is called the "father of passive investing"—is the US market leader in mutual and exchange-traded funds. Each ETF was backtested individually using a buy-and-hold strategy from inception, and a combined portfolio with specified weightings was backtested from 2007 to 2023 with annual rebalancing; $10,000 grew to $19,318. Returns were lower than the S&P 500 Total Return index, partly due to bond allocations. The article describes each fund's target index and investment approach, concludes the funds provide broad exposure to global stock and bond markets, and advises readers to review prospectuses. Passive strategies are popular for being hands-off, cost-effective, and historically competitive; Vanguard ETFs are favored for low expense ratios and simple index-tracking strategies.

This passage is an April 23, 2001 email from Ann M. Schmidt compiling news mentions of Enron. Key items include:

- Dabhol Power Company (65% owned by Enron) faced a payment dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board, which defaulted on 2.26 billion rupees ($48.31 million). DPC's lenders met in London, and its board planned to consider a termination notice; DPC sought lender approval to exit the $3 billion project.
- PG&E CEO Robert Glynn's misreading of California electricity prices and rapid expansion contributed to the largest utility bankruptcy filing in U.S. history; PG&E's ventures competed with Enron and often lost.
- Tri-State Generation & Transmission proposed a $1.3 billion, 1,200-megawatt coal-fired plant in Bent County, Colorado.
- Saudi Oil Minister Ali al-Naimi was to meet U.S. Energy Secretary Spencer Abraham to discuss oil prices following OPEC output cuts.
- Promoters of the Mangalore Power Company in India halved their 1,000 MW project's capacity, partly to avoid "another Dabhol-like situation."
- ONGC disputed Enron's claims about the $15 million Moon Prospect gas well at Tapti, saying no substantial reserves were found.
- A Mangalore group leader questioned KPTC Chairman Baligar about contradictory statements on Karnataka's power situation.
- Spain's government planned to revise electricity market rules to increase competition beyond Endesa and Iberdrola's dominance.
- Brief items covered the Kookmin Bank merger, Japan's polyester-fiber dumping probe, and other Asia-Pacific news.

The President reports continued national prosperity and notes that acts of the last session have been implemented. Measures were adopted to preserve peace with Indian tribes, protect frontier settlements, and secure treaty rights of the Indians. A meeting with Creek deputies at Colerain, Georgia, failed to produce a land sale, but a new treaty confirmed prior engagements and obtained consent for trading houses and military posts. Under the treaty with Great Britain, the United States took possession of posts including Oswego, Niagara, Detroit, Michelimackina, and Fort Miami. Commissioners on the St. Croix River boundary adjourned until August 1797, and commissioners on vessel captures met in London, though British commissioners for the treaty's sixth article had not yet been appointed. Under the Spanish treaty, a commissioner traveled toward Natchez for the boundary line, and Spanish troops were to withdraw from occupied posts. Agents were appointed under the act for protection of American seamen. Arrangements with Algiers appear near completion, with American prisoners liberated, and treaties with Tunis and Tripoli are in operation. The President recommends the gradual creation of a navy to protect commerce and neutral rights, limited public manufacturing establishments for essential military supplies, public support for agriculture, a national university, a military academy, and revision of officer compensation. He reports extensive injuries to American trade from French cruisers in the West Indies while expressing hope for continued harmony with France. Revenues are improving, and further measures for discharging the public debt, along with attention to the militia and harbor defenses, are urged. Concluding his final address, he congratulates the country on the success of the governmental experiment.

Eilish McCready, 25, from Glasgow, founded Fearless theatre school a year ago after graduating from an acting and performance course. The inclusive drama classes welcome all children, including shy children and those with additional needs such as autism, and focus on building confidence and social skills rather than performances, with no end-of-year shows. Classes are kept small and begin with a "Fearless shake" to shake off nerves. Eilish runs the company with drama teachers.

Lizanne Conway, whose three sons have autism, said the classes have helped her older two boys develop confidence, social skills, and communication in a safe, inclusive environment. Lisa Byrne said her shy daughter Rua gained confidence through the classes and now sings in front of people and runs her own YouTube channel. Classes are held at Studio 93 in Glasgow.

Evercore will release its second quarter 2018 financial results on Wednesday, July 25, 2018, followed by a conference call at 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time. President and CEO Ralph L. Schlosstein, Executive Chairman John S. Weinberg, and CFO Robert B. Walsh will review the results, followed by a question and answer session. The call will be accessible by telephone and webcast on Evercore's website, with a replay available for one week and the webcast archived for 30 days.

This compilation of October 2001 news articles covers Enron Corp.'s escalating financial troubles. Enron might need several hundred million dollars over the next 20 months to cover potential shortfalls in investment vehicles (Marlin Water Trust II, Marlin Water Capital Corp. II, Osprey Trust, and Osprey I) that sold about $3.3 billion in notes. Treasurer Ben Glisan said asset sales, including $1.55 billion from the Portland General Electric sale, should raise at least $2.2 billion by the end of 2002, though a worst-case scenario could require issuing up to $1 billion in stock. Enron shares fell 86 cents to $19.79, down more than 40% in a week, after the company reported a $618 million third-quarter loss, $1.01 billion in write-offs, and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity from terminating transactions with LJM2, a partnership formerly run by CFO Andrew Fastow. The SEC opened an informal inquiry into these transactions. CEO Kenneth Lay held a conference call defending Fastow and asserting adequate liquidity, but analysts, including Goldman Sachs' David Fleischer, questioned the company's transparency. Enron also asked Citigroup to arrange a $750 million loan. Other articles note BG Group's purchase of Enron's 30% stake in Indian oil fields, a House stimulus bill granting Enron a $254 million tax refund, a securities class action investigation, and market commentary advising caution on the stock.

Winter offers offshore fishing for sailfish, dolphin, wahoo, and kingfish—sails near 160' off the Dodge Wall, kings around 90'. Live bait from bait boats (VHF 68) is key. Inshore, jacks, tarpon, and spawning sheepshead gather at the inlet; shrimp or clams work.

A new study shows that online media portrays women as younger than men, and that this distortion feeds AI bias. Over 6,000 coders rated women across nearly 1.4 million online images and YouTube videos as younger than men, especially in prestigious occupations like doctors and CEOs. Text analysis using nine language models linked less prestigious jobs with younger females and prestigious jobs with older males. In an experiment with over 450 participants, uploading images of female employees led people to estimate the average age of that occupation as two years younger. ChatGPT, prompted to generate and rank resumes for 54 occupations using male and female names, produced younger, less experienced resumes for women and scored them lower, despite U.S. Census data showing male and female employees are roughly the same age. Researchers say this "gendered ageism" may help explain the glass ceiling, and caution that addressing overlapping biases, not just one at a time, is needed.

The passage examines a weekly rotation strategy between SPY (S&P 500) and XLU (Utilities) based on Michael Gayed's paper on beta rotation. Rotation systems involve switching between assets to exploit sectors that perform better at different times. Utilities are favored due to their risk-aversion, low beta, and interest rate sensitivity, outperforming when rates fall and underperforming when rates rise. Gayed's backtest showed the strategy compounded at 13.1% annually since 1929. However, an independent backtest from 1999 shows the strategy returned 6.7% annually until the paper's 2014 publication, outperforming buy-and-hold's 4.6%, but has since lagged the market by over 5% annually (5.1% vs 10.4%) and never recovered from the 2020 covid crash. The authors note it may be too soon to conclude the strategy has stopped working.

Researchers are working to repurpose grape pomace, the wine industry's waste, as a renewable source of antioxidants, grape oils, and dietary fibers. The global wine industry produces about 14 million tons of pomace annually, which can pollute water, acidify soil, and attract pests. Changmou Xu's team is developing technologies to extract and separate nutrients from pomace while removing pesticides. The compounds have been tested against foodborne pathogens and studied for effects on piglet health. Added to fatty foods like mayonnaise and ranch dressing, the natural antioxidants inhibited lipid oxidation and extended shelf life, offering a "clean label" alternative to artificial antioxidants like EDTA.

Game is selling an Xbox One S (500GB) bundle for £249.99 that includes Forza Horizon 3, Tekken 7, Halo 5, and Gears of War 4. The same items cost £297.10 individually on Amazon UK, making the bundle a £47.11 saving. The Xbox One S received a 4/5 review, praised for its small size, 4K upscaling, and value as a UHD Blu-ray player. The bundled games also scored well: Forza Horizon 3 (5/5), Tekken 7 (4/5), Halo 5 (4/5), and Gears of War 4 (4.5/5).

The Cassini spacecraft has completed the first of five close flybys of Saturn as its 20-year mission nears its end, culminating in a planned one-way plunge into the planet on September 15. The August 14 pass brought it within 1,010–1,060 miles of Saturn's clouds, and a possible "pop-down" maneuver could bring it closer to gather atmospheric, temperature, aurora, and composition data, as well as help determine the length of a Saturnian day. With fuel running low and concerns about crashing into Titan or Enceladus, the mission will conclude with a final Titan flyby on September 11.

This patent application, titled "Method for Smart Energy Device Infrastructure," claims priority to numerous prior U.S. patent applications filed between December 2017 and December 2018, covering topics including surgical network control, clip appliers, smoke evacuation, robotic surgical platforms, and cloud-based medical analytics. The disclosure describes methods for characterizing the state, function, or tissue contact of an end effector of an ultrasonic device by applying a power level to an ultrasonic transducer, measuring its impedance, comparing it to a reference value, classifying the result, and adjusting the power level accordingly. The application includes extensive figures depicting surgical systems, modular hubs, generator modules, control circuits, and impedance-based diagnostic processes for ultrasonic surgical instruments.

This study of the COVID-19 vaccines BNT162b1, BNT162b2, and BNT162b2SA ran at 153 locations in 6 countries from 29 April 2020 to 10 February 2023, including healthy participants aged 12 and older with no prior COVID-19 infection or vaccination. Initial dosing was observer-blinded, later becoming open-label; booster doses were open-label except for one small reassigned group. All 195 Phase 1 participants (ages 19–82) received a study vaccine, and in Phase 2/3 (ages 12–91), 46,297 of 46,406 participants (99%) received one. Participants stayed up to 26 months; the entire study took about 33 months.

BNT162b2 was 95% effective in preventing COVID-19 from 7 days after Dose 2 through the monitoring period ending 03 December 2020, regardless of past infection. Immune responses 1 month after a BNT162b2 booster were as strong as those after Dose 2, and BNT162b2SA produced responses against the Beta variant comparable to BNT162b2's responses against the original strain.

Most injection site reactions (pain most common) and systemic events (tiredness and headache most common) were mild or moderate and resolved quickly. The 100-µg BNT162b1 dose was stopped after injection site or systemic reactions, and 30 µg BNT162b2 was selected for later phases. Fewer than 1% of Phase 2/3 participants withdrew due to medical problems. Few serious medical problems occurred, most not believed related to the vaccine. No Phase 1 participants died; Phase 2/3 deaths (85, 62, and 23 across groups) were not believed caused by BNT162b2, and no participant died in the Phase 3 BNT162b2SA group.

In this introductory lecture on plasma diagnostics, Jack Hare explains that plasmas cannot be measured directly; properties like density, temperature, and velocity must be inferred indirectly from physical effects, requiring mathematical intuition rather than everyday experience. The course assumes prior plasma physics knowledge (22.611, using Chen's textbook). Diagnostics are essential to plasma physics and fusion history: the UK's ZETA device mistakenly attributed neutron bursts to fusion when they actually came from MHD instabilities, but this failure led to the development of Thomson scattering, which was later used to confirm Russian claims of kiloelectron-volt tokamak temperatures, prompting worldwide conversion to tokamaks. Similarly, the National Ignition Facility initially lacked adequate diagnostics, preventing understanding of its failure to ignite, while better diagnostics later contributed to achieving ignition. Diagnostics matter to experimentalists (understanding measurement uncertainties and limitations), computational researchers (code validation and producing comparable outputs), and theorists (skepticism toward experimental claims and designing testable predictions). Ideally, one would measure every particle's position and velocity, but theorists actually want moments such as density, average velocity, and magnetic fields. Diagnostics face limitations: they are sparse in space and time, often line-integrated (especially light-based methods), filtered by instrument response functions, and dependent on poorly understood physics such as atomic data. The course emphasizes principles over practical implementations. In an interactive exercise, students placed their plasmas on a temperature-density-magnetic field chart, spanning sixteen orders of magnitude in density—from tokamaks, DIII-D, and NIF to Hall thrusters and non-equilibrium plasmas. Hare also described magLIF, where neutron spectroscopy can measure magnetic fields through anisotropic secondary DT neutrons.

The Rams are seeking permission to interview Doug Marrone for their head coaching vacancy. Marrone went 1-1 as the Jaguars' interim coach, previously led the Bills, and the Jaguars may consider making him their permanent head coach.

Despite Elon Musk's April Fool's Day 2018 tweet declaring Tesla bankrupt, the company faced serious financial pressures while ramping up Model 3 production. Founded in July 2003, Tesla grew into the world's leading maker of high-performance electric vehicles, launching the Roadster (2008), Model S (2012), Model X (2015), and the mass-market Model 3 (revealed 2016). After a 2008 liquidity crunch, Musk invested $80 million and became CEO. Tesla went public in June 2010, raising $226.1 million, and in April 2017 became the most valuable American automaker at $51 billion. It also built battery gigafactories with Panasonic, sold the Powerwall home battery, and acquired SolarCity in 2016 for about $2.1 billion in stock. However, Tesla never turned a profit and had generally negative operating cash flow, funding itself through repeated equity and debt offerings that nearly doubled its share count and pushed long-term debt above $10 billion. Model 3 production delays accelerated cash burn, leading a Goldman Sachs analyst to estimate Tesla might need over $10 billion in external capital by 2020, though Musk stated no raise would be needed in 2018.

Amazon.com, Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2015 reports net sales of $22.7 billion, up 15% from $19.7 billion in Q1 2014, with a net loss of $57 million ($0.12 loss per share) compared to net income of $108 million ($0.23 per share) in the prior year. Operating income rose to $255 million from $146 million. Beginning in Q1 2015, Amazon changed its reportable segments to North America, International, and AWS. North America net sales were $13.4 billion (operating income $517 million), International $7.7 billion (operating loss $76 million), and AWS $1.6 billion (operating income $265 million, with sales up 49%). Operating cash flow was negative $1.5 billion for the quarter; trailing twelve-month free cash flow was $3.2 billion versus $1.5 billion a year earlier. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $13.8 billion at quarter end. Total assets were $50.1 billion and stockholders' equity $10.9 billion. Amazon acquired companies for an aggregate $341 million, recorded $407 million in stock-based compensation, and had no borrowings outstanding under its $2.0 billion revolving credit facility. Legal proceedings include multiple patent infringement suits and wage-and-hour claims. The IRS seeks approximately $1.5 billion in additional federal tax related to 2005–2006 transfer pricing, French authorities proposed approximately $250 million in additional tax for 2006–2010, and the European Commission opened a state aid investigation regarding Luxembourg tax rulings.

Hurricane Harvey may have damaged or destroyed up to a dozen critical wildlife habitats along the Texas Gulf Coast, threatening endangered species like whooping cranes and prairie chickens. Agencies are beginning damage assessments. Scientists are factoring climate change into wildlife management as storms intensify. Shrimp and crabs survived, but oyster beds and dolphins may have suffered losses.

The passage describes the NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture. Turing is the first GPU architecture to use GDDR6 memory, delivering 14 Gbps signaling rates and 20% better power efficiency than Pascal's GDDR5X, with a 40% reduction in signal crosstalk; combined with improved memory compression and larger L2 cache (6 MB in TU102, double GP102's 3 MB), this yields a 50% effective bandwidth increase over Pascal. Turing includes a new display engine supporting DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K at 60 Hz, VESA DSC 1.2, and native HDR with tone mapping per ITU-R BT.2100. The enhanced NVENC encoder adds H.265 8K encoding at 30 fps with bitrate savings, and NVDEC supports HEVC 4:4:4 and VP9 10/12-bit HDR. Turing GPUs support USB Type-C and VirtualLink, delivering power, display, and data to VR headsets through a single USB-C connector. TU102 and TU104 use second-generation NVLink for SLI (two-way only), providing 25 GB/sec per direction per link.

Dedicated RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection, enabling real-time ray tracing roughly 10 times faster than Pascal (10+ Giga Rays/sec versus 1.1). Hybrid rendering combines rasterization and ray tracing, aided by denoising. NGX provides AI features using Tensor Cores, including DLSS (trained against 64x supersampled images), DLSS 2X, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. New graphics features include Mesh Shading (Task and Mesh Shaders), Variable Rate Shading (adjustable per 16x16-pixel region, enabling content adaptive, motion adaptive, and foveated rendering), Texture Space Shading, Multi-View Rendering (up to four views per pass), and expanded resource binding.

The TU104 contains 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores, and is used in GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. The TU106 (GeForce RTX 2070) has 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, without NVLink or SLI support. An RTX-OPS metric weights Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 throughput by usage, yielding 78 for RTX 2080 Ti. The document concludes with a ray tracing overview, game examples (Battlefield V, Shadow of the Tomb Raider), and NVIDIA legal and trademark notices.

This study proposes a method for identifying the hierarchy of public transit modes based on actual passenger travel patterns, demonstrated with smart card data from the Seoul metropolitan area. Unlike previous studies that assume spatial homogeneity, the method divides each trip into ascending and descending phases at half the total travel distance, constructs transfer rate matrices, and computes a rescaled average hierarchical order for each mode, with separate analyses for intra- and interzonal trips. Applying the method to 10,264,700 trip chains across six modes (walking, community bus, urban bus, intercity bus, light rail, and metro), the results show a consistent hierarchy within Seoul—walking, community bus, urban bus, light rail, metro—with no significant difference between phases. In interzonal trips, the intercity bus ranked highest, and the relative order of the intercity bus, metro, and urban bus differed between Seoul and Gyeonggi/Incheon, indicating regional variation in modal hierarchy.

In Hill v. Morehouse Parish Police Jury, the Louisiana Court of Appeal, Second Circuit, reviewed a wrongful death and survival action arising from a 1987 accident in which 16-year-old Bradd Rudolph drove through a "T" intersection at high speed and into Bayou Bartholomew, drowning two teenage passengers, including 15-year-old Michael Hill. The trial court found the police jury was aware of the intersection's danger but failed to adequately mark it, allocating 20% fault to the police jury and 80% to the driver, and awarding the plaintiff $31,587.53. On appeal, the court affirmed the trial court's factual findings, reasoning that the police jury had notice of the hazard—evidenced by prior installation of double arrow signs that had not been replaced for three months—and that this failure was a substantial cause of the harm. However, the court amended the fault allocation to 65% for the driver and 35% for the police jury. The $150,000 general damage award was affirmed as within the trial court's discretion. Rehearing was denied.

This study used Unpaywall and Shareyourpaper to assess the open access (OA) status and self-archiving potential of 1,897 clinical trial results publications from interventional trials conducted at German university medical centers, completed between 2009 and 2017, and published between 2010 and 2020. Overall, 54% of publications were openly accessible (23% gold, 7% hybrid, 16% bronze, 8% green), while 46% (n = 871) were closed-access. Of the closed-access publications, 85% (n = 736) had permissions to self-archive the accepted or published version in an institutional repository, most commonly after a 12-month embargo. Realized green OA was estimated at 16%. The findings suggest low compliance with WHO guidelines recommending that clinical trial results be openly accessible where possible, and confirm a largely unrealized potential of green OA, likely reflecting limited self-archiving mandates in Germany and unresolved legal disputes over secondary publication rights. Limitations include dependence on the accuracy of Unpaywall and Shareyourpaper data, and the approach may underestimate self-archiving potential. Future applications include library-led repository population, interventions beyond individual institutions, and an ongoing pilot at Charité using trial-specific report cards to promote self-archiving.

U.S. markets fell sharply Tuesday as the 10-year Treasury yield reached three per cent, while Canada's S&P/TSX slipped 75 points, cushioned by gains in gold and materials. Barrick Gold rose on strong earnings. The Canadian dollar edged up to 77.95 cents US, with gold and copper prices higher.

Natural gas settled at $3.27/MMBtu, holding within a descending wedge since March. Europe's LNG demand boosts U.S. exports while North American oversupply weighs on domestic prices; seasonal softness and Canadian supply disruptions keep volatility elevated. The passage also describes Traders Union, a 2010-founded portal offering broker reviews and ratings.

The passage criticizes Ontario Premier Kathleen Wynne for stating that if young people don't vote, "some white person" senior will. The author argues the comment is ageist and racist, accusing Wynne of identity politics and pandering on race. Quotes from Ali Taghva and labour lawyer Sunira Chaudhri support this criticism. While acknowledging that voting participation increases with age and that visible minorities vote at lower rates, the author contends that demonizing one group to increase another's turnout is shameful. The piece concludes that Wynne should instead engage all groups in voting and suggests she would condemn similar remarks from PC Leader Doug Ford.

Global stock markets rose after Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen told a Senate committee the central bank could raise interest rates as soon as next month, citing a strengthening job market and modestly higher inflation. European and most Asian indexes gained, while Wall Street futures were flat. Analysts called the hawkish tone unexpected; markets put the chance of a March rate change at 34 percent. Chinese inflation ticked higher, raising concern about possible tightening. The dollar rose to 114.44 yen, and U.S. crude fell to $52.86 per barrel.

The passage contrasts digital leaders and digital laggards in their data cultures. Laggards restrict data access, hoard it in departmental silos as a source of power, and favor business judgment and a "culture of genius" over data-driven decisions. Leaders, by contrast, embrace transparent data access and measurement; 88% have standardized APIs enabling data flow, compared to 27% of laggards. Leaders use data-driven metrics to set ambitious but realistic goals, and this structure fosters flexibility, experimentation, and risk-taking rather than rigidity. A case study describes a retail company that, after acquisition, implemented real-time sales reporting, enabling data-driven decisions across business units. Laggards set aspirational goals ungrounded in data, leading employees to avoid measurement and rely on process adherence, which stifles innovation. Leaders align organizations vertically and horizontally through transparent, strategy-linked objectives developed via combined top-down and bottom-up processes, though excessive analysis requirements can hinder simple decisions. Leaders treat data culture as central, aligning beliefs, values, and daily behaviors, while laggards show misalignment between espoused values and actions. Changing entrenched mindsets is cited as the hardest part of transformation, but laggards are not doomed; organizations typically fit one of four patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, or data reliant—and can take targeted actions to build a strong data culture. The document closes with a description of Keystone Strategy, a consulting firm.

In this introductory lecture of MIT course 15.S12, Gary Gensler, a Senior Lecturer at MIT Sloan and advisor at the MIT Media Lab, introduces a course on blockchain and money. He polls students on cryptocurrency ownership (about 45%) and blockchain project experience (about a third), then poses the course's central questions: what is blockchain, and why might it be a catalyst for change in finance? Gensler traces the history of the internet, early e-commerce (Pizza Hut's PizzaNet, which lacked online payment), and cryptography, including public-key cryptography and SSL/TLS, which secured online transactions. He discusses digital currency efforts like PayPal, M-Pesa, and Alipay, and identifies Satoshi Nakamoto's 2008 peer-to-peer electronic cash proposal as solving the riddle of moving value without a centralized intermediary. He defines blockchain as time-stamped append-only logs secured by cryptography, hash functions, digital signatures, and consensus protocols, noting Stuart Haber's earlier 1990s work. He recounts the 2010 Bitcoin pizza purchase (10,000 bitcoins worth $41 then, $66 million later). Gensler outlines blockchain's potential in finance—moving money and risk—while noting challenges: scalability (Bitcoin handles roughly 7 transactions per second versus Visa's 20,000–70,000), privacy, interoperability, and governance. He distinguishes permissioned from permissionless blockchains, notes crypto finance's roughly $200 billion size relative to much larger capital markets, and discusses public policy issues including illicit activity, financial stability, and investor protection. The course will cover fundamentals, economics, and financial sector use cases, emphasizing critical reasoning over hype. Requirements include class participation (30%), two individual write-ups, and a group project proposing a blockchain use case in finance.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on January 28, 2016, announcing its fourth quarter 2015 and year ended December 31, 2015 financial results. The filing includes a press release (Exhibit 99.1) and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures (Exhibit 99.2). The report was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Renewed interest in psychedelics has opened drug-facilitated psychotherapy. Phase II trials showed 54% of MDMA-AT patients no longer met PTSD criteria, earning FDA breakthrough designation; Phase 3 results confirmed safety and efficacy for severe PTSD.

Ireland is highly exposed to exchange rate movements, with the weak euro attracting record numbers of American tourists while low sterling deters UK visitors. The euro has risen from $1.05 to $1.18 this year, and sterling has fallen from 76 to about 91 pence against the euro since the Brexit referendum. The author believes the euro's appreciation exceeds what the ECB would prefer, and while sterling may eventually rise, any gain could be years away. Tourism firms have limited hedging options; UK importers enjoy windfall profits and should hedge to lock in gains, while exporters to the UK face difficulties and should incur costs in sterling.

Browns coach Kevin Stefanski was noncommittal Wednesday on whether rookie Shedeur Sanders would be the backup quarterback after Cleveland traded Joe Flacco and a 2026 sixth-round pick to Cincinnati for a 2026 fifth-round pick, leaving Sanders and fellow rookie Dillon Gabriel as the only quarterbacks on the active roster. Stefanski said he would "let the week play out" before deciding on the QB2 role and declined to say if Zappe would be signed to the active roster. Sanders, the 144th pick in this year's draft, has been inactive as the No. 3 and emergency QB through five games but was listed as No. 2 on this week's unofficial depth chart. Flacco started the first four games before Gabriel's first career start, a 21-17 loss in London. Stefanski said the trade "took us by surprise." Deshaun Watson remains on the physically unable to perform list while rehabbing an Achilles injury.

A University of Michigan study found that 21% of women and 10% of men in Generation X and the late Baby Boom generation, now in their 50s and early 60s, meet criteria for addiction to ultra-processed foods—far higher than adults aged 65 to 80 (12% of women, 4% of men). Based on data from more than 2,000 older Americans and the modified Yale Food Addiction Scale 2.0, researchers suggest aggressive 1980s marketing of "diet" processed foods to women may explain the gender pattern. Addiction was linked to self-perceived overweight, fair or poor mental and physical health, and social isolation. Researchers warn that children today, who consume even more ultra-processed calories, may face higher addiction rates, and early intervention may be essential.

A massive rock formation called Qarlinngua—Inuktitut for "like pants"—stands in salt water on the Brodeur Peninsula, Baffin Island, about 80 to 90 kilometres southwest of Arctic Bay, Nunavut. A photo submitted by local hunter Max Kalluk was initially doubted as fake but was verified through local sources and geologists. The formation is a sea arch, created by erosion of Paleozoic sedimentary rock estimated at 250 to 600 million years old. It stands over 50 metres tall, is reachable only by boat during a brief summer window, and few people have seen it in person. Geologists say it may collapse within decades or thousands of years. Arctic Bay Adventures is the only tour company visiting it, and Nunavut's tourism department plans to promote it.

The Bank of England will keep the £5 polymer note in circulation and issue the £10 note as planned despite tallow concerns, having rejected alternatives as costly. It delayed £20 note contracts to consider plant-based substitutes, with a decision due by summer 2017.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC reporting that on September 10, 2019, Bob Iger resigned from Apple's Board of Directors. The filing, signed by Katherine Adams, Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary, on September 13, 2019, also lists Apple's registered securities, including common stock (AAPL) and various notes with maturities ranging from 2022 to 2042, all traded on The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC.

This study examines the career transition adaptation and impact experienced by lecturers and education personnel (civil servants) in Indonesian state higher education institutions, using a qualitative grounded theory approach within an interpretive paradigm. Prior research has emphasized organizational rather than individual needs, and Schlossberg's transition theory (the 4 S factors: situation, self, support, and strategies) has rarely been applied to career transitions in higher education. Education personnel careers were also affected by a bureaucratic reform policy trimming echelons III and IV. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with six key informants selected via snowball sampling from PTN BH, PTN BLU, and PTN Satker institutions, and analyzed using open, axial, and selective coding with NVIVO 12 Pro. Analysis produced eight main categories—situation, self, support, strategies, behavior, role, learning, and perception—resulting in two built theories: transition theory and anchor career theory. Adaptation showed a reciprocal relationship among the 4 S factors, with new dimensions identified. Transition impacts included changes in behavior, roles, learning, and perception, with dual roles causing performance decline in primary positions. Contrary to Schein's Anchor Career Theory, informants used two career anchors: competence and managerial. The study extends Schlossberg's theory to non-student campus groups and offers recommendations for government bureaucratic reform. Limitations include limited generalizability, exclusion of demographic characteristics, and potential researcher bias.

A hockey player returning from injury says he is more concerned about being run from behind into the boards than hits to the head. He felt comfortable in his return game but ran out of steam in the third period, attributing cramping to travel and possible dehydration. A doctor from Duke reviewed his CT scan with team staff, concluding his current injury risk is no different than it would be in September, three and a half months after the injury. The scan happened after he asked a coach whether he would play if a teammate named Dougie could not. He believes returning home for a normal routine will help, is excited to play in front of home fans with a chance to win the Stanley Cup, and says the team must play with more passion and better execution. His family was supportive, and the doctor reassured them on the team plane.
An appeal from a non-jury judgment favoring the plaintiff was affirmed with costs.

This bibliometric study analyzes mathematics anxiety research in mathematics education using Scopus data from 2013 to 2023, processed with VOSviewer and Biblioshiny, yielding 324 journal articles. Mathematics anxiety, defined as feelings of tension, worry, or fear that interfere with mathematics performance, affects all age groups and can hinder mathematics learning. Publication output grew over the decade, peaking in 2022 with 56 documents, and research spans multiple fields, most notably social sciences (35.1%) and psychology (30.7%). Network visualization identified seven clusters linking mathematics anxiety to both psychological and cognitive variables. Of 168 journals publishing on the theme, Frontiers in Psychology was the most productive (39 documents; 55,251 citations; Q2 quartile). Among 978 authors, Garcia-Santillan was the most productive with 10 publications and 143 citations. Research involved 78 countries, led by the United States (62 documents), which also had the strongest international collaborations, while Germany was the most cited. The University of Barcelona was the most relevant affiliate with 23 documents. The study concludes that mathematics anxiety has been a highly researched topic over the past decade, noting limitations of using only Scopus-indexed articles.

North Korea warned the US it is ready to hit back with nuclear attacks, displaying intercontinental and submarine-launched ballistic missiles at a parade marking Kim Il-sung's 105th birth anniversary. Trump said North Korea is "looking for trouble", while China warned conflict could break out at any moment.

NVIDIA Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended July 26, 2020 reports second-quarter fiscal 2021 revenue of $3.87 billion, up 50% year-over-year and 26% sequentially, with net income of $622 million ($0.99 diluted EPS). Six-month revenue was $6.95 billion with net income of $1.54 billion. On April 27, 2020, NVIDIA completed its acquisition of Mellanox Technologies for total consideration of $7.13 billion; Mellanox contributed approximately 14% of quarterly revenue and added $3.43 billion in goodwill. The acquisition drove gross margin down to 58.8%, reflecting a $161 million inventory step-up charge and $84 million of intangible amortization. Operating expenses rose 67% to $1.62 billion, primarily due to Mellanox-related costs.

Beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2021, NVIDIA changed its reportable segments to Graphics and Compute & Networking. Second-quarter Graphics revenue was $2.09 billion (up 16% year-over-year) and Compute & Networking revenue was $1.78 billion (up 130%). By market platform, Gaming revenue was $1.65 billion (up 26%), Data Center $1.75 billion (up 167%), Professional Visualization $203 million (down 30%), Automotive $111 million (down 47%), and OEM and Other $146 million (up 32%).

In March 2020, NVIDIA issued $5 billion of notes maturing between 2030 and 2060, with net proceeds of $4.97 billion, bringing long-term debt to $6.96 billion. Cash and cash equivalents were $3.27 billion at quarter-end, with marketable securities of $7.71 billion. The company paid $99 million in quarterly dividends ($0.16 per share). The filing also discusses COVID-19-related operational impacts, pending securities class action and derivative litigation, and notes that no customer represented 10% or more of revenue during the quarter.

This patent application, a continuation of related applications, describes a detection model training method, apparatus, and terminal device in the field of information processing. The background notes that colorectal polyp detection systems using convolutional neural networks and support vector machines suffer from small amounts of private training data and reduced accuracy when deployed across hospitals with differing devices and image characteristics, while obtaining additional labeled data is expensive and time-consuming. The disclosed method determines an initial training model comprising an initial detection model and an adaptive model, and uses a training sample containing source domain data (images labeled with target object presence and domain identifiers) and target domain data (images labeled only with domain identifiers). The initial detection model determines whether a target object is present in source domain images, while the adaptive model classifies the domain of each image. A loss function value is calculated from the detection result, domain classification result, and identifiers, and parameter values are adjusted accordingly to obtain a final detection model. In embodiments, images are user body organ images and the target object is a lesion target, such as a polyp in colorectal images; the adaptive model may include a gradient inversion module forming an adversarial relationship with the feature extraction module, eliminating domain-related features. This approach allows unlabeled images to serve as training samples, increasing sample size and detection accuracy. The application also covers a training apparatus with corresponding functional units, a terminal device, and a storage medium.

The passage outlines three jump ball situations: defensive (opponent has advantage), even (equal chance), and offensive (team has advantage). In defensive situations, players should rotate early, watch the jumper's eyes and hands for telegraphed tips (right-handers typically tip left, left-handers right), and maintain contact with the jumper. Defensive alignments include box, diamond, and "Y" formations, with rotations executed clockwise or counter-clockwise on predetermined signals. Even jump balls require boxing out, establishing inside position, and coordinated rotations similar to offensive rebounding. Offensive jump ball plays are recommended when holding a 6" or greater height advantage, with tips generally directed to the tallest player while maintaining defensive balance. Proven offensive plays include Possession, Double Tap, Post Split (from box and diamond alignments), Jumper Fly, Forward Fly, Spread, Tandem, and Loop, each specifying player movements, screening actions, and defensive balance responsibilities.

This passage is a collection of news articles from May 24–25, 2001, circulated via email, largely concerning Enron Corporation.

A New York Times report describes FERC Chairman Curtis Hebert's claim that Enron head Kenneth Lay offered continued support if Hebert changed his views on electricity deregulation; Lay recalled the conversation differently. Hebert may soon be replaced, reportedly by Pat Wood. Enron, the largest energy contributor to federal candidates ($2.4 million, 72% to Republicans), supplied candidate lists to the White House and influenced the administration's energy report.

Multiple articles cover the Dabhol dispute in India: the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB), Dabhol's sole customer, rescinded the seven-year-old power purchase agreement, alleging misrepresentation of plant capacity, while Dabhol disputes MSEB's right to cancel. The conflict stems from unpaid bills (reported between $48 million and $64 million); termination could trigger roughly $2 billion in government-guaranteed obligations. Bechtel threatened to withdraw by May 31 over unpaid dues, and the government considered having NTPC acquire Enron's 65% stake. Negotiations were scheduled for May 29, though a former committee member questioned the negotiators' authority, and MSEB was expected to pay its April bill under protest.

Other items include California Attorney General Lockyer's statement about imprisoning Enron's chairman, Governor Davis's declining poll numbers, modest stock market gains (Enron fell to $54.16), PGE's record revenues, an India-Australia energy and mining cooperation pact, renewed business school interest in energy careers, and El Paso's chairman agreeing to testify in a FERC hearing over alleged California gas-price manipulation.

Apple has removed several ICE-tracking and documentation apps—including ICEBlock, Eyes Up, and DEICER—from its App Store after US attorney general Pam Bondi claimed such tools endanger ICE officers. Google has also removed similar apps, stating it considers ICE officers a vulnerable group. The developers are fighting the bans: ICEBlock's Joshua Aaron says he has a legal team and will do everything in his power to reverse the decision, while Eyes Up's developer, who goes by Mark for safety reasons, has appealed twice and vows to continue. Eyes Up and DEICER remain available on Google Play and their websites. Legal experts say the apps publish First Amendment-protected speech, and the Trump administration previously threatened to prosecute Aaron. Digital rights researchers say the situation highlights the risks of centrally controlled platforms, noting Apple's closed ecosystem compared with Android's sideloading option.

Tropical Depression 02W made landfall in the eastern Visayas, Philippines on April 15, 2017, with winds near 25 knots. It weakened to a remnant low crossing into the South China Sea. On April 17, NASA's Terra satellite imaged the elongated remnant clouds; wind shear and drier air are expected to prevent re-intensification.

The Supreme Court heard arguments on whether the double jeopardy clause bars separate convictions and sentences under 18 U.S.C. §§ 924(c) and 924(j) for the same conduct. Section 924(c) covers firearm use in furtherance of a crime of violence or drug trafficking; Section 924(j) applies when such use causes death. The parties agree that lesser-included offenses generally cannot both be punished unless Congress clearly intended cumulative punishment, and that Congress clearly allowed it for Section 924(c) and its underlying offense. Justices debated what language suffices: Kavanaugh and McCloud cited Section 924(c)(1)(D)(ii)'s consecutive-sentence mandate, while Barrett and the government argued it contributes little, pointing instead to Section 924(c)'s "in addition to" language, which they said does not reach Section 924(j). Charging Section 924(j) removes a separate predicate conviction, the consecutive-sentence requirement, and mandatory minimums. Gorsuch questioned the precedent's justification, but those issues were not briefed.

This section from a Texas Instruments document provides mechanical, packaging, and orderable information for designated devices, noting that such data is current as of publication and subject to change without notice. Footnotes define status, material type (preproduction parts are prototypes sold without warranties), RoHS values, lead finish/ball material options, moisture sensitivity levels and peak reflow temperatures, and part marking conventions. TI disclaims all warranties, providing technical and reliability data "as is," limits its liability to the annual purchase price of the parts sold, and states users are solely responsible for product selection, design, validation, and meeting applicable standards. Resources may be used only for developing applications with TI products.

This study developed a clinically applicable biomarker for schizophrenia spectrum disorder (SSD) using resting-state functional connectivity (rs-FC) MRI, addressing challenges of accuracy, generalisability, across-session variability, and disorder specificity. Using a LASSO-based sparse learning algorithm on a harmonized discovery dataset (1,015 participants) from four institutions, the classifiers achieved 79.6% accuracy (AUC 0.876) and 77.3% accuracy (AUC 0.824) on an independent validation dataset (683 participants). A voting method improved sensitivity without significantly changing AUC. Forty-seven important functional connectivities (FCs) were identified, with reproducible group differences maintained across datasets for 44 of 47 FCs. A laterality imbalance between hemispheres was observed among frequently selected regions of interest. The study also explored whether the diagnostic biomarker could function as state and staging markers, assessing relationships between important FCs and symptom severity. Performance varied by disease severity, with voting classifiers showing less imbalance across severity subgroups. The findings may support improved diagnosis and treatment approaches for SSD and other psychiatric disorders.

Rocky View Schools faces a $1 million transportation shortfall. Education Minister David Eggen said the province may allow parents to pay bus fees despite Bill 1, which eliminated fees for students living 2.4 kilometres or more from school. Parents surveyed expressed willingness to pay fees again; other options include changing bell times, longer rural commutes, and moving stops. The board will contact the ministry and may extend its April 12 deadline.

Amazon introduced a mobile accessory kit enabling makers of earbuds and wearables to integrate Alexa, and the Jabra Elite 65t ($170) are among the first earbuds to use it. Alexa in the Elite 65t currently works only on Android, with iOS support planned. The review found significant limitations: Alexa cannot place calls, send texts, or access streaming services other than Amazon Music, and music can be started by voice but not paused or changed without opening the Alexa app. Reminders are unsupported, and timers and alarms produce no notifications. Alexa offers no navigation, though voice shopping is strong, drawing on order history. The earbuds also support Google Assistant and Siri through the Sound+ app. Sound quality is described as excellent, with a comfortable fit and a HearThrough ambient sound feature, but battery life (5 hours plus 10 from the case) falls short of competitors, and there is no tracker for lost earbuds. The review concludes that while sound quality is great, the Alexa experience in these earbuds lags behind that of smart speakers.

Shohei Ohtani is starting for the Dodgers against Cristopher Sanchez and the Phillies in Game 1 of the 2025 NLDS on October 4 at Citizens Bank Park, his first-ever postseason pitching appearance. In 2025, Ohtani pitched 14 games, going 1-1 with a 2.87 ERA, 62 strikeouts, and 15 earned runs over 47 innings, exceeding four innings only three times. Manager Dave Roberts hopes he can pitch through six and into the seventh. The game airs on TBS and truTV and streams on HBO Max, with The Sporting News providing live updates.

After the Oct. 1 Las Vegas shooting at the Route 91 Harvest festival—where a gunman killed 58 and injured more than 500 during Jason Aldean's performance—debate arose over gun laws and concert safety. Country legend Charlie Daniels called the shooting an anomaly, saying the gunman was "a nut," and warned against letting fear win. He supports the NRA's position on regulating bump stocks but opposes broader gun-control laws, arguing politicians misunderstand guns and citing Chicago's strict laws amid ongoing violence. Rosanne Cash urged country musicians to stand up to the NRA. Daniels headlines an Oct. 21 show at Cary's Booth Amphitheatre.

Digital leaders embrace sensible risk-taking and experimentation to compete in fast-changing markets, viewing themselves as learning organizations that rely on data and continuous feedback. Even failed experiments yield knowledge, though risks are carefully assessed. They also invest in long-term employee development, prioritizing critical thinking skills.

The author analyzed minute-by-minute solar radiation data from the Mauna Loa Observatory (MLO) since 1980 to assess atmospheric clarity and test his theory that clouds respond to changes in forcing in ways that oppose them. Contrary to Dr. Keen's claim that the atmosphere is clearer than it has been in decades, MLO data show clarity unchanged since 1980 except following volcanic eruptions. Comparing two-year periods after the El Chichon and Pinatubo eruptions with non-volcanic periods, the author found the two eruptions produced nearly identical results despite differing in size and location, suggesting the stratosphere maxes out in how much light it blocks. Average downwelling solar radiation was about 24.5 W/m2 lower during volcanic periods; clouds partially offset this by admitting roughly 7 W/m2 more sunlight than expected. Despite this ~25 W/m2 reduction—far exceeding the IPCC's 3.7 W/m2 figure for doubled CO2—temperatures at MLO and at four other Hawaiian stations (Hilo, Molokai, Barber's Point, and Lihue) showed no cooling during or after the eruptions. The author attributes this to his view that the climate system responds to changes in ways that restore prior conditions, citing the Constructal Law and Le Chatelier's Principle, while acknowledging he cannot fully explain the result. An update notes wind speed changes were ruled out as a cause. Data came from GISS temperature records and MLO solar and meteorological datasets; methods involved converting data to ten-minute intervals and separating volcanic from non-volcanic periods.

A hockey player praises Winnipeg's new NHL team, recalling passionate fans and good crowds from his time playing there six or seven years ago, including a whiteout and "we want the Jets" chants at the old arena before the move to the MTS Centre. He believes Mr. Chipman's organization will succeed and prefers a smaller, full arena over Atlanta's empty seats. He distinguishes the Sedins by appearance and speech, noting Henrik, the captain, speaks more. When facing goalie Thomas, he emphasizes choosing shooting spots, pursuing rebounds or back-door chances, and crediting Thomas's saves.

The Toronto Stock Exchange financial sector had a choppy March and declining April, with Canada's big five banks dropping from February highs: TD (-7.5%), BNS (-7.2%), CM (~6%), BMO (-5.5%), and RY (-4.6%). The author compared these banks against five small-cap Canadian lenders using five criteria: low beta, high earnings yield, high dividend yield, low payout ratio, and stable dividend history. All big five banks passed the dividend history test, having not cut dividends in over ten years, while First National, Home Capital Group, and Equitable Group had cut dividends. In the final ranking, MCAN Mortgage ranked first, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce second, and Atrium Mortgage third, while First National and Equitable Group ranked worst (9th and 10th). Advantages of small-caps include higher dividend yields and smaller price swings; disadvantages include lower liquidity and less diverse business models. The author holds positions in AMIVF, CM, TD, and BNS.

The Hawk Offense consists of a wing isolation, a high post shuffle cut, and a weakside post up, and resembles the UCLA Offense with a guard cutting off a high post back screen. Two defensive approaches counter it. The Basic NBA Show & Recover avoids switching on the high post screen, since a switch would let the screener post up a smaller defender; instead, weakside defenders "show" against dribble penetration, shuffle cuts, and down screens, then recover to their assignments. The All Out SOS Disruption traps the ballhandler in the sideline wing area, exploiting the Hawk's vulnerability when the off guard cuts into the low post, which hinders ball reversal needed to defeat the double team. This approach uses double teams, contact switches on shuffle and down screens, and near-player rotations when the ball leaves the passer's hands. Both strategies require individual defensive fundamentals and team SOS concepts, with "Base Go Red" and "Post Trap" rotations for baseline drives or post passes.

Energy sector trading involves gaining exposure to multiple energy stocks for diversification and profits, either through a sector-tracking ETF such as XLE or a portfolio of individual stocks. The S&P 500 energy sector comprises oil and natural gas companies involved in exploration, refining, and distribution, plus related equipment and service providers. Major ETFs are VDE and XLE; as of 18 July 2022, the sector returned 52.81% over one year versus about -9.28% for the S&P 500. The five biggest stocks are Exxon Mobil, Chevron, ConocoPhillips, EOG Resources, and Schlumberger, though this list can change. The sector is difficult to trade because oil prices depend on macro factors and are hard to predict. Two XLE strategies are presented: the first has 198 trades, 0.61% average gain, 6.4% CAGR, 65% win ratio, 13% max drawdown, and 2.1 profit factor; the second has 335 trades, 0.21% average gain, 59% win rate, 8% max drawdown, 1.75 profit factor, and 3% annual return. The authors do not reveal the strategies' rules. Diversification is emphasized as more valuable than finding the best strategy.

Madison Snap and William Francis were convicted and fined fifty dollars each for willfully shooting and wounding a mare found trespassing in Snap's oat field. The court held that while an owner may expel trespassing animals with necessary force or take them up damage feasant, the law forbids inflicting unnecessary injury upon the animal, even if it is damaging crops. The judgment was affirmed.

Old paper £10 notes will cease to be legal tender on 1 March and will no longer be accepted by retailers. They can be exchanged for the new polymer note at banks, building societies, post offices or the Bank of England. The new Jane Austen note, launched in September 2017, is more durable, harder to counterfeit, and includes a tactile feature for blind and partially-sighted people.

AMD has launched two new high-end graphics cards, the Radeon RX Vega 64 and Vega 56, ending Nvidia's unchallenged run since the GTX 1070 and 1080 launched over a year ago. The Vega 56 will be compared with the GTX 1070 and the Vega 64 with the GTX 1080; AMD states the Vega 64 is not a GTX 1080 Ti competitor, and Nvidia is likely to keep the single-card performance crown. AMD's advantages include three-way CrossFire support, the 64 PCI-E lane X399/Threadripper platform, a price $50 below the GTX 1070, and the FreeSync ecosystem, bolstered by the new Enhanced Sync driver feature and claimed improved minimum frame rates.

The safety is a defensive back in football, positioned deeper than any other defender and serving as the last line of defense against big plays. There are two main variations: the free safety, who roams the middle of the field with more speed, and the strong safety, who is stockier, plays closer to the line, and focuses more on run defense and tackling. Other names for the position include "Rover," "Star," and the older terms defensive fullback and defensive halfback, which are still used in Canadian football. Safeties must cover receivers, tackle well, and communicate effectively. Notable safeties include Troy Polamalu, Ed Reed, Ken Houston, and Sean Taylor, with 17 safeties in the Pro Football Hall of Fame. A great safety creates turnovers, limits the field for quarterbacks, and gives the defense confidence.

Researchers say Australia's Great Barrier Reef has recovered from near-extinction five times over the past 30,000 years, suggesting greater resilience than previously thought. However, Jody Webster of the University of Sydney expressed concern that the reef may not survive the current pace of warming and acidification. Based on fossil data from 16 ocean floor sites, the team found the reef migrated seaward or landward at 20 centimetres to 1.5 metres per year in response to sea level changes. Five death events occurred: two from sea level drops, two from rises, and one from sediment dumping. A 2016 heatwave killed nearly a third of its coral.

This report, authored by Jaber Mustafa and Younis Bukhari of the Ministry of Education, responds to a 2024 Arab Summit initiative in Bahrain to ensure free education for Arab children. Citing a 2018 UNESCO report that over 10 million Arab children aged 5–15 are out of school, the authors propose the "Hope" initiative, offering remedial and preventive solutions, using the Syrian conflict as a case study.

The literature review shows that conflict disrupts early childhood education through displacement, school destruction (about one-third of Syrian schools damaged or destroyed, with roughly 4,000 attacks since 2011), and inequitable access. UNICEF estimates over two million children in Syria are deprived of education, and nearly 400,000 Syrian refugee children in Turkey are out of school. Conflict also causes trauma, toxic stress, and long-term cognitive and socio-emotional delays.

Using a triangulation design combining interviews and surveys, the study examined affected families, including a case study of Ahmed, a Syrian child in Alkhabor who studies 2–3 hours weekly in poor conditions without electricity or internet. Interviews revealed destroyed schools, scarce resources, trauma, and signs of PTSD among children, while the survey identified resource shortages, psychological challenges, and infrastructure issues.

The report proposes immediate remedial solutions (emotional and academic support) and proactive, sustainable solutions through the Hope Initiative, a structured plan combining immediate action with long-term strategies. It concludes that education in conflict zones is both a casualty of war and a tool for empowerment and peace.
Primatologist Jane Goodall died October 1 at age 91; her legacy includes living chimps and enduring skeletons.

Residents of San Andrés Hueyapan, an indigenous community in Morelos located 18 kilometers from Popocatépetl, have long tolerated the volcano's eruptions but are now stressed by its renewed activity following the September 19 earthquake, which damaged many homes. Authorities advised residents of Tetela del Volcán to keep documents and clothing ready. Some residents are scared and reluctant to leave their homes. Ashfall was reported in Tetela del Volcán and Zacualpan de Amilpas after recent eruptions.

Sean "Diddy" Combs, 55, was sentenced in Manhattan federal court to four years and two months (50 months) in prison plus a $500,000 fine after being convicted on two Mann Act counts of transportation to engage in prostitution, for paying at least eight male escorts to cross state lines for drug-fueled "freak offs" with two former girlfriends, including Cassie Ventura. The jury acquitted him of more serious sex trafficking and racketeering conspiracy charges, finding no coercion. Prosecutors sought 135 months; his defense sought no more than 14 months. At the sentencing hearing, Combs apologized and called his actions "disgusting, shameful, and sick," while Judge Arun Subramanian said his history of good works could not wash away his abuse of women. A witness who testified Combs raped her declined to appear after a letter from his attorneys that the judge called "inappropriate." Combs also faces roughly 50 civil lawsuits alleging sexual assault, which he denies.

The Second Circuit affirmed Samuel Israel III's conviction and twenty-year sentence from the Southern District of New York. The court found no basis to question Judge McMahon's impartiality or require her recusal, rejecting arguments regarding her retention of the case, her comments during an adjournment, and her prior recusal from a related bankruptcy case. The court also found the sentence reasonable, rejecting claims of judicial bias, denial of a downward departure for medical needs, insufficient cooperation credit, and excessive sentence length, given the defendant's criminal history and the money involved.

For the UC1825BEVM-CVAL, an RCD clamp limits switch node voltage overshoot. Starting resistor and capacitor values can be calculated from the allowed overshoot, transformer parasitic inductance, and clamp voltage variation.

Backtests indicate both DAX 40 and Euro Stoxx 50 perform much better during futures expiration week than in any random week. Both contracts expire on the third Friday of March, June, September, and December. DAX 40's expiration week averages a 0.39% gain with a 57% win ratio versus 0.12% for a random week, with December the best month. Euro Stoxx 50 averages a 0.3% gain with a 54% win ratio versus 0.18%, December best and June a big loss. The week after DAX 40 expiration was backtested using a 100% margin strategy rather than futures backtesting, with 100,000 invested in March 2000 and four trades per year. This week performs poorly, averaging a negative 0.1% gain with a 47% win ratio; December and March are positive, while September is worst, profitable only 25% of the time. Markets are more volatile during expiration week due to pin risk, and DAX 40's high trading volume makes it attractive to traders.

This patent application relates to silicone-based elastomeric compositions comprising oxidized (hydrophilic) carbon black particles and methods for their preparation. The disclosure provides methods for producing elastomeric compositions by contacting hydrophilic carbon black particles with a silicone-based dispersant bearing carbon-black-affinic moieties (amino, acrylate, or epoxy groups) that is miscible in a curable hydrophobic silicone pre-polymer, mixing the treated particles within the pre-polymer, and curing (by addition or condensation) to produce an elastomer containing dispersed carbon black particles. The hydrophilic carbon black particles are characterized by properties including low pH, elevated volatile matter content, negative surface zeta potential, defined acid value, and Raman spectroscopy ratios (I_D/I_G and AUC_D/AUC_G) indicating oxidation. Suitable dispersants include amino-silicone oils, silicone-acrylates, and silicone-epoxy dispersants, which are believed to anchor to oxygen-containing groups on the carbon black surface, rendering the particles hydrophobic and compatible with the silicone matrix. The compositions may contain carbon black at concentrations from 0.01% to 30% by weight, with particle sizes (Dv90) ranging from sub-micron to several micrometers. Applications include intermediate transfer members for indirect printing systems, sealants, and articles benefiting from the mechanical, thermal, electrical, or radiation-absorbing properties of dispersed carbon black.

The passage details design requirements for a PGA848 driving an ADS8860 ADC with ±15V supplies and a 5V reference. Three filters are used: an input EMI/RFI filter, a feedback filter (CFB = 75pF, 318kHz cutoff, shifting to 277kHz at high resistor tolerance), and a charge kickback filter at the ADC inputs tuned for settling and THD performance. The PGA848 provides a nominal 318kHz bandwidth with –0.1dB flatness to 41kHz. The PGA REF pin is set to 2.5V using a REF6250 through a precision 10kΩ-to-10kΩ divider, buffered by an OPA192 in a dual-feedback configuration (RF = 2kΩ, CF = 2nF, RISO = 20Ω) achieving 86° phase margin; stability must be re-verified via simulation if bypass capacitance changes. Power supplies are ±15V, and voltages above 40V (±20V) permanently damage the device. Layout guidelines recommend symmetric input paths, local low-ESR bypass capacitors, trace separation, minimizing leakage and parasitic capacitance at the DA_IN pins, and avoiding thermal junctions. The document also lists simulation tools (PSpice for TI, free TINA-TI software), related documentation, support resources, trademarks, an ESD handling caution, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information with legal disclaimers.

U.S. equities rose on Monday, led by the S&P 500 and Nasdaq on strength in technology and semiconductor shares, while energy stocks weakened and the Dow edged higher. Gains came despite investor caution over a potential government shutdown that could delay key economic data, such as Friday's jobs report, complicating Federal Reserve decisions and heightening volatility. Despite hawkish remarks from Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, investors still expect a modest rate cut. Attention now turns to ongoing shutdown talks in Congress.

In *Brooks v. Missouri Pacific Railroad Co.*, the Supreme Court reversed the Eighth Circuit and ruled that a veteran machinist was entitled to a North Little Rock seniority date of November 3, 1955. Hired as an apprentice machinist in Monroe, Louisiana in 1951, the petitioner left for military service, returned, and completed his apprenticeship in North Little Rock in 1958. He claimed that absent military service, he would have finished his apprenticeship in 1955 and been automatically hired as a journeyman mechanic at North Little Rock. The District Court agreed and ordered the seniority date granted; the Eighth Circuit reversed under *Tilton*, finding the promotion lacked predictable certainty. Following *Tilton*, the Court held that speculative possibilities, such as supply and demand, cannot defeat veterans' seniority rights, and remanded.

Russian journalist Arkady Babchenko, reported shot dead at his Kiev apartment building, appeared alive at a news conference less than 24 hours later, saying his murder had been staged to foil an alleged Kremlin hit plot. Ukrainian Security Service head Vasyl Gritsak said a Ukrainian citizen was allegedly paid $40,000 by Russian security services to organise the killing and hired an acquaintance as gunman; the man was detained. The alleged plot was part of a larger scheme involving weapons and explosives for terror attacks in Ukraine. Babchenko, a Kremlin critic who fled Russia in 2017 after death threats, apologised to his wife, who was not briefed, and to colleagues who mourned him.

Americans spent more than $100 billion on summer vacations last year; experts say travel reduces stress and health risks and boosts relaxation, but it can be pricey. Experienced travelers suggest: start with a budget using tools like Excel, budgetyourtrip.com, or @TransAbroad; use online travel sites such as Expedia, Travelocity, and Yelp for bargains; use credit cards without foreign transaction fees and carry a backup card; watch roaming charges abroad; travel in the offseason, book early, and consider trip insurance; sign up for airline newsletters to catch short-lived deals; and find local discounts via information centers, hotel concierges, and newspapers.

PortMiami is the top money-making operation in Miami-Dade County and Florida, according to a new study. Its economic impact rose $12.8 billion to over $41 billion, with cargo growth of nearly 1 million tons in 2016 and a record 5.1 million cruise passengers. The port supports 300,000 jobs and contributed $288 million in taxes. Though the Miami Herald reported the study's numbers may be inflated, Mayor Gimenez defended them. A $247 million Royal Caribbean terminal should generate $500 million annually.

The National Weather Service in San Diego issued a zone forecast for extreme southwestern California on July 4, 2018, covering Orange County coastal and inland areas, San Diego County coastal areas, valleys, mountains, and deserts, the Inland Empire, Santa Ana Mountains, Apple and Lucerne Valleys, San Gorgonio Pass, and Coachella Valley. A high surf advisory is in effect from 6 PM Wednesday to 9 PM Friday for coastal zones, and an excessive heat watch runs from Friday morning through Saturday evening across most areas. Conditions begin with morning low clouds and fog near the coast, becoming mostly sunny, with a warming trend peaking Friday: highs reach the mid-80s to low 90s at beaches, 99–112 inland, 107–115 in valleys and the Inland Empire, and 111–117 in deserts. Slight chances of showers and thunderstorms are forecast Saturday through Tuesday in mountain and desert zones. Winds are generally light, becoming west around 15 mph with gusts to 25 mph in many areas, and up to 40 mph in pass and desert locations.

In response to a congressional resolution, President Madison recommended the third Thursday in August 1812 as a day of public humiliation and prayer, asking Americans to seek God's forgiveness and protection during the war, pray for guidance and success, and for a restoration of peace. Issued July 9, 1812, and countersigned by Secretary of State James Monroe.

As winter turns to spring, the Blue Ridge Poison Control Center at UVA warns of outdoor dangers like poisonous plants, spiders, and snakes, cautions against self-treatment, and recommends protective clothing and awareness.

ESPN, founded by Bill and Scott Rasmussen in 1978 and launched in 1979, grew into Disney's "cash cow" through a dual-revenue model of affiliate fees and advertising built on the cable bundle. After early ownership changes involving Getty Oil, ABC, and Capital Cities, Disney acquired 80% in 1996, with Hearst holding 20%. Growth was driven by NFL rights, direct broadcast satellite competition, and demand for new channels (ESPN2, ESPNEWS, ESPNU, ESPN Deportes). Live sports rights—largely rented from leagues—and news programming like SportsCenter formed its content core, though editorial independence tensions arose with league partners. Brand campaigns such as "This Is SportsCenter" helped differentiate ESPN.

By 2024, cable/satellite subscribers had fallen from about 100 million (circa 2012-13) to roughly 70 million, while sports rights costs rose. Disney acquired BAMTech in 2017 and launched ESPN+ in 2018, reaching about 25 million subscribers at $6.30 average revenue per user. In 2023, Disney confirmed the flagship ESPN network would go direct-to-consumer in 2025, and in February 2024 Disney, Warner Bros. Discovery, and Fox announced the Venu Sports streaming joint venture, each owning one-third, slated for fall 2024. ESPN faced a transition from a B2B to a B2C model, raising questions about profitability, churn, and appeal to younger fans.

The competitive landscape included incumbent media companies (Warner Bros. Discovery, Paramount/Skydance, Comcast/NBCUniversal, Fox), technology companies (Amazon, YouTube, Apple, Netflix, and others) pursuing sports for their own business objectives, sports properties benefiting from rising rights fees ($25.57 billion spent in the U.S. in 2023, projected above $30 billion by 2025), cable/satellite operators shifting toward broadband (e.g., Charter's 2023 Disney deal incorporating streaming services), and fans facing greater choice, fragmentation, cost, and piracy. A Pew survey found only 7% of U.S. adults were "superfans."

In Q2 FY24, ESPN Domestic generated $3.866 billion in revenue (up 4%) and $780 million in operating income (down 9%); ESPN+ subscribers were 24.8 million. ESPN's rights obligations reportedly exceeded $10 billion annually. The case examines ESPN's history, competitive environment, and strategic options as it confronts whether to disrupt itself or be disrupted, with Disney aiming to make ESPN the "preeminent digital sports platform."

The passage argues that IEX, a stock exchange launched with the ambition of disrupting U.S. stock trading, has underperformed, holding under 3% of exchange volume.
