The author describes two versions of IEX: "IEX One," which operates within the SEC's National Market System (NMS) by using its speed bump to benefit buy-side traders instead of the sell-side, and "IEX Two," a would-be market visionary seeking to dominate and unify trading. According to the author, the speed bump functions as an implicit fee and merely extends the NMS's web of costs and subsidies rather than disrupting the market. The passage contends the NMS is flawed, protecting exchanges from competition and serving exchanges rather than traders. It concludes that for IEX to succeed, it must bypass the NMS, deliver liquidity, and balance buy-side and sell-side interests, with backing from brokers and traders.

In January, U.S. employers added 200,000 jobs while unemployment held steady at 4.1 percent, and average hourly wages rose 2.9 percent from a year earlier, suggesting wage gains may be accelerating as the labor market tightens. Unemployment is at its lowest level since 2000, down from a 10 percent peak in 2009. Economist Kate Bahn attributed the January pay boost to minimum wage increases in 18 states affecting 4.5 million workers. Analysts caution against drawing conclusions from single monthly reports, noting a margin of error of about 100,000 jobs. Job growth under President Trump (2.1 million in 2017) has been similar to Obama's (2.2 million in 2016). Black unemployment rose to 7.7 percent in January from 6.8 percent in December, though experts note the overall declining trend predates Trump's presidency.

IT buyers compare Oracle Exadata and HPE Vertica data warehouses via IT Central Station reviews. Users praise Exadata's smart scan and Vertica's columnar storage but cite needed improvements. A 68-page comparison report is available.

The writer praises Coronation Street's sensitive portrayal of Aidan's (Shayne Ward) suicide storyline, which made suicide a talking point. The writer recalls a teenage suicide attempt made while struggling with their sexuality. Friend Cheryl Fialka recounts that 33 years ago her husband John, 31, died by suicide aboard a cruise ship in Alaska, leaving no note, showing no signs, and not suffering from depression. She still experiences grief and anger, having learned to live with the sadness. The writer wonders whether awareness of such devastation would change such decisions.

Competitive Capabilities International (CCi) and R&G Global Consultants have partnered to develop the Stable Operations TRACC, a big data-driven product for scaling predictable, reliable and stable manufacturing operations. CCi states clients can achieve a 15 to 20 percent capacity increase within six months of implementation. Cargill, the first client to deploy the product, facilitated the partnership. The TRACC addresses challenges such as high capacity utilization, supply chain service delivery issues and CAPEX avoidance, with blended learning modules supporting sustained improvement across multiple sites.

This study examines the problems and challenges of women's education in rural areas of Pakistan and Azad Jammu Kashmir (AJK). Female literacy in Pakistan (51.9%) is significantly lower than male literacy (73.3%), and only 40.8% of rural women are literate, with Pakistan having the lowest female literacy rate in Asia. Barriers identified include patriarchal culture, lack of motivation, poverty, illiterate family environments, early child marriages, religious restrictions, long distances to schools, and inadequate infrastructure. Using a quantitative approach, the researchers surveyed both illiterate and literate women through two survey forms and analyzed responses thematically. Both groups reported similar problems: management and resource issues, male dominance, motivational deficits, financial hardship, few educational institutions, and religious factors; literate women additionally cited technical issues, curriculum problems, family pressure, and teacher training deficiencies. The study concludes that despite government efforts, significant challenges remain, and recommends monthly seminars on women's education, use of media campaigns, legislation for compulsory women's education, and open and distance education as ways forward.

The ARM Cortex-A8 Subsystem gives the ARM Cortex-A8 Master control of the device, handling configuration and control of subsystems, peripherals, and external memories. It features the ARMv7 ISA with Thumb2, JazelleX, and Media Extensions, plus an interrupt controller. The Harvard-architecture processor targets multi-tasking applications, including a NEON SIMD engine, VFPv3 coprocessor, separate L1 caches, and debug support. Its trace port connects only to a 32KB Embedded Trace Buffer.

When the author's 20-year marriage ended, she realized she knew little about the family's finances; her husband had managed insurance, investments, and major purchases, and she didn't know where their accounts were or how to locate her own 401(k). During the divorce, her lawyer requested a budget and accounting of assets, which left her frozen. With a friend's help, she sorted through paperwork, and after her ex's financial advisor said she was no longer his client, her father connected her with his own planner, who helped her understand her budget and set a retirement plan. Having been in and out of the workforce for 15 years, she found a job through a connection and has held it for seven years. She now makes major decisions herself, handles home repairs, and expects a retirement on her own terms.

The passage presents the LifeCLEF 2014 Plant Identification Task, a continuation of the ImageCLEF plant identification evaluations held since 2011, aimed at measuring and improving content-based plant identification tools for real-world scenarios such as citizen-based ecological monitoring. The PlantCLEF 2014 dataset contained 60,962 pictures of 19,504 observations covering 500 species from a European region centered around France, collected by 1,608 contributors, with each image assigned to one of seven view types (entire plant, branch, leaf, flower, fruit, stem, leaf scan) and associated with contextual and social metadata. Novelties that year included a multi-image query scenario, user quality ratings in metadata, a new "Branch" view type, and an increased species count. The task was evaluated as species retrieval from multi-image observation queries, scored using an average classification rate weighted per user and plant. Of 74 registered research groups, 10 submitted runs using methods including Fisher vectors, convolutional neural networks, bag-of-visual-words, and global descriptors. IBM AU's Fisher Vector-based runs achieved the best results (top score 0.471), while CNN approaches underperformed, attributed to insufficient training data and disallowed external pre-training. Combining predictions across images of the same observation improved performance, and the LeafScan and Flower categories obtained the highest scores. The paper concludes that scaling plant recognition to thousands of species remains difficult and proposes extending the 2015 task to the full French flora of approximately 5,000 species.

This passage is from a Texas Instruments data manual for the TMS320DM814x DaVinci Digital Media Processors, covering memory mapping, device pins, and device configuration.

**Memory:** Certain regions are decoded internally by the Cortex-A8 Subsystem and are not physically part of the L4 Slow; they are reserved for masters other than the Cortex-A8. The TILER provides an additional 4 GB of addressing range (via a 33rd address bit) for accessing frame buffers in rotated and mirrored views; this range is accessible only to the HDVPSS and ISS subsystems, though other masters can access single views through the 512-MB TILER region in the base 4-GB memory map.

**Terminal Functions:** Tables identify external signal names, pin multiplexing, ball numbers, package designators, pin types (I, O, Z, S, GND, A), internal pullup/pulldown states (IPU, IPD, DIS), supply voltage sources, and pin functions. The MUXED column lists multiplexed peripheral functions, the controlling PINCNTLx register, and the de-selected input state (DSIS). Tables cover boot configuration (GPMC/BTMODE pins), camera interface, DCAN, DDR2/DDR3 memory controllers 0 and 1, EMAC[0] and EMAC[1] (MII/GMII, RGMII, RMII modes), GPIO banks GP0–GP3, GPMC, HDMI, I2C, McASP0–5, PCIe, reset/interrupts/JTAG, SD interfaces, SPI, oscillator/PLL and clock functions, timers, UART0–5, USB0/USB1, digital and analog video input/output, and supply voltages.

**Boot Configuration:** BTMODE[15:0] pins are sampled when reset is de-asserted and latched into the CONTROL_STATUS register. BTMODE[15:11] set GPMC CS0 data bus width, wait enable, and address/data multiplexing; BTMODE[4:0] set the boot mode order, with fallback modes executed if the primary mode fails; BTMODE[7:5] are reserved; BTMODE[9:8] select the Ethernet PHY mode for EMAC boot; BTMODE[10] selects GPMC pin muxing options for XIP (NOR) boot. Documented boot modes include XIP (NOR), NAND flash, NAND I2C, MMC/SD, SPI, EMAC, PCIe, and UART.

**Pin Multiplexing:** Multiplexing is controlled per-pin by MUXMODE bits in PINCNTL1–PINCNTL270 registers; the default (MUXMODE = 0x0) tri-states the pin. Some peripheral functions are multimuxed (MM) across multiple device pins.

**Unused Pins and Pull Resistors:** Unused pins may be left unconnected unless otherwise noted; input pins require internal or external pull resistors to prevent floating. External pullup/pulldown resistors are strongly recommended for boot configuration pins that are routed out and 3-stated. For most systems, a 1-kΩ resistor can oppose the internal pull and a 20-kΩ resistor can complement it, though users should confirm values for their specific application.

In soccer, an offensive switch is an exchange of positions between two attacking teammates used to beat defenders. Switches may be "called" with an oral "Switch" or occur "naturally" during play. In the basic switch, two nearby teammates run diagonally forward in an "X" pattern, temporarily assuming each other's duties, with or without the ball. The objective is to free a runner for a pass by forcing a defender to choose whom to cover or confusing two defenders. Switches usually occur in the opponents' half. A "vertical" switch exchanges positions toward the goal lines; a "lateral" (horizontal) switch exchanges positions toward the touchlines and is useful against the offside trap. Unlike an overlap, switches involve an actual exchange of positions. Players should say "Switch back" when returning to original positions.

The paper introduces MatterMech, a benchmark of 4,800 questions across eight subdomains of nanomaterial synthesis, designed to evaluate large language models' (LLMs) ability to hypothesize physicochemical principles. The benchmark was developed from approximately 17,000 academic papers, with question-answer pairs generated using Claude-3.5-Sonnet and refined through a multi-agent roundtable system (Worker, Reviewer, Critic) to reduce hallucinations, followed by human evaluation on a 5-point Likert scale. The authors also release MatterDB, a dataset of 31,735 papers pairing LLM-extracted synthesis mechanisms with their academic sources. Fourteen LLMs were evaluated using two metrics: text-infilling (TIF) and multiple-choice questions (MCQ). Qwen-Max achieved the highest MCQ accuracy (61.99%), while Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct led TIF performance (35.25%). Reasoning-specialized models performed well on MCQ but poorly on TIF, revealing a gap between logical reasoning and precise knowledge reproduction. Principle-guided prompting outperformed standard Chain-of-Thought, improving accuracy while reducing output tokens. Performance scaled logarithmically with model size. Key findings indicate that LLMs excel at logical reasoning but struggle to integrate conceptual understanding with principle-based reasoning, and that both increased model scale and principle-guided approaches improve performance across subdomains. Limitations include the absence of human expert annotations during construction and the benchmark's static content.

Dr. Edith Mbagwu, a primary care physician at Ochsner Health Center-Denham Springs North, recommends SMART goal setting to help people maintain weight loss resolutions. Goals should be clearly defined, tracked through assessments such as weight or calorie counts, achievable, manageable within available resources and time, and scheduled into daily or weekly routines. The article examines difficulties experienced in university foreign language education due to the transition from face-to-face to distance education during the Covid-19 pandemic. It reviews distance education concepts, models (synchronous, asynchronous, hybrid), learning management systems, and the advantages and disadvantages of distance education, noting that skill-based fields such as foreign language teaching are particularly difficult to deliver remotely.

The study's population comprised undergraduate and graduate students of German and English (teaching-literature-translation) in the 2020-2021 spring term; 294 students completed an online questionnaire containing five personal information questions and a 53-item distance education problems scale with six subscales. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and t-tests.

Students rated internet and computer related problems highest (µ=0.473), with internet disconnection/freezing the most cited item, and problems related with teachers lowest (µ=0.147). Student-related problems (µ=0.396) were led by lack of motivation and low participation; measurement and evaluation problems (µ=0.255) centered on skill-based gains not being measurable. Male students perceived student-related problems more strongly than female students, while no differences emerged between German and English students. Students without training in distance education programs, without an independent study room, or without home internet access reported more problems across sub-dimensions.

Students concluded that distance education is not successful in foreign language teaching, that face-to-face education is more effective, and that materials, measurement and evaluation, teachers' knowledge of distance methods, participation, and students' program knowledge were insufficient. The authors recommend awareness and training programs for students and teachers and a hybrid model combining face-to-face and distance education.

This lecture covers the quantization of the Dirac field. Standard canonical quantization using commutators fails: the Hamiltonian is unbounded from below and the exchanged-particle states are symmetric, i.e., bosonic. The fix is to impose anticommutation relations instead, which is self-consistent because of the sign in the conjugate momentum (π = iψ†). Expanding ψ in a complete set of modes yields operators a and c satisfying {a, a†} = {c, c†} = 2π³δ³(k−k′)δ_rs, with all other anticommutators zero. The vacuum is annihilated by a and c, and the Hamiltonian becomes positive definite up to a divergent zero-point energy E0. Each mode is a fermionic oscillator contributing −½ω_k to E0, and a†² = 0 embodies the Pauli principle: a† and c† create fermions—particles and antiparticles—with two polarizations, momentum k, and spin ½ (verifiable via the angular momentum operator). More generally, the spin-statistics theorem states that half-integer spin fields must be quantized with anticommutators (Fermi-Dirac statistics), while integer spin fields use commutators (Bose-Einstein); in 2+1 dimensions, anyons also exist. A U(1) phase symmetry gives a conserved current and charge Q; after discarding an infinite constant so the vacuum has zero charge, particles carry charge +1 and antiparticles −1, justifying the particle/antiparticle interpretation. Applied to the electron, this predicts the positron, which Anderson discovered in cosmic rays in 1932. Finally, Wightman, retarded, and time-ordered correlation functions are derived; they relate to scalar-field correlators via the operator i∂/+m, and the momentum-space Feynman propagator is i/(k/ − m + iε), the inverse of the Dirac operator. The lecture closes by motivating chiral fermions and Majorana fermions as ways to reduce the Dirac spinor's eight real components.

This study examined interactions between a mitochondrial polygenic score (MGS), lifestyle, and environmental factors on the age at onset (AAO) of Parkinson's disease (PD) in LRRK2-PD and idiopathic PD (iPD). Three datasets were used—AMP-PD, Fox Insight, and a Tunisian Arab-Berber cohort—comprising 9745 patients (486 with LRRK2-PD, 9259 with iPD). The MGS was calculated using 9 of 14 SNPs previously associated with mitochondrial function and PD risk.

The MGS was inversely correlated with AAO in LRRK2-PD, with a higher MGS associated with an earlier AAO (a 1% increase in standardized MGS corresponded to approximately one month earlier onset). This association was more pronounced in patients of European descent than in those of Tunisian Arab-Berber descent. No association between MGS and AAO was observed in iPD.

Regarding lifestyle and environmental factors, smoking was associated with later AAO in iPD but not LRRK2-PD. Black tea consumption was associated with later AAO in LRRK2-PD, and coffee consumption with later AAO in iPD. Caffeinated soda consumption was associated with earlier AAO in both groups. Work-setting pesticide exposure was associated with earlier AAO in iPD but not LRRK2-PD.

Gene-environment interactions were detected. In LRRK2-PD, the MGS interacted with coffee and caffeinated soda consumption; high-MGS consumers had a median AAO approximately six years earlier (coffee) and eleven years earlier (caffeinated soda) than low-MGS consumers. In iPD, the MGS interacted with caffeinated soda consumption and work-setting pesticide exposure, both associated with earlier AAO in high-MGS patients. No interactions were found between MGS and smoking, black tea, green tea, or pesticide exposure duration.

The authors conclude that lifestyle and environmental factors interact with the MGS and affect its impact on AAO in PD, highlighting the importance of including such factors in genetic association studies and the need for more diverse populations in polygenic score research.

This passage is from the Texas Instruments datasheet for the ADS8681W, ADS8685W, and ADS8689W devices.

Data transfer frames begin at the falling edge of CONVST/CS and end at the subsequent rising edge, when conversions start. During a frame, the host provides SCLK clocks; data is shifted into the input shift register via SDI and out on SDO-x pins. Frames are classified by SCLK count: 32 clocks is an optimal frame (valid command word), fewer than 32 is a short frame (writes are invalid and treated as NOP, though output data remains valid), and more than 32 is a long frame (the last 32 bits shifted in form the command).

Input commands are synchronous to SCLK and support one-byte or two-byte (HWORD) operations; for HWORD commands, the LSB of the 9-bit address is ignored. Configuration commands must be 32 bits long and execute at the CONVST/CS rising edge. Output data for frame F+1 depends on the command in frame F and the DATA_VAL[2:0] bits, containing fixed patterns, register data, or the latest 16-bit conversion result, with optional flags (device address, range, alarms, parity) appended per DATAOUT_CTL_REG settings.

The device features a multiSPI interface. Writes use four legacy SPI-compatible protocols (SPI-00-S through SPI-11-S), with SPI-00-S as the power-up default. Reads support single SDO-x, dual SDO-x (two bits launched per SCLK edge), or source-synchronous (SRC) protocols in which RVS provides an output clock synchronous with data, with configurable clock source and bus width.

The device has nine configuration registers, each four bytes: DEVICE_ID_REG (00h), RST_PWRCTL_REG (04h, write-protected by key 69h written to address 05h), SDI_CTL_REG (08h), SDO_CTL_REG (0Ch), DATAOUT_CTL_REG (10h), RANGE_SEL_REG (14h), ALARM_REG (20h), ALARM_H_TH_REG (24h), and ALARM_L_TH_REG (28h).

The ADS868xW is a fully integrated, fully differential 16-bit SAR ADC data acquisition device with an integrated analog front-end and precision reference. An example industrial design pairs the ADS8681W with the MUX36D08 eight-channel differential multiplexer, supporting standard voltage and current ranges and settling to 1% accuracy in under 5µs. The user-programmable input alarm with hysteresis, demonstrated with an NTC thermistor, prevents false triggering from noise.

The device uses AVDD and DVDD supplies, each decoupled with 10µF and 1µF capacitors. Two low-power modes are available: NAP mode (entered via NAP_EN with CONVST/CS held high) and power-down mode (entered via PWRDN; analog blocks power down while the interface and registers remain active). Layout guidance covers analog/digital partitioning and decoupling capacitor placement for the supplies, REFCAP, and REFIO.

The document concludes with related documentation, support resources, trademark and ESD notices, a revision history (Revision A, May 2025, moved ADS8685W/ADS8689W from Advance Information to Production Data), and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information with TI disclaimers.

This patent disclosure describes systems and methods for periodic beam failure measurements in digital communications, particularly for 5G New Radio (NR) systems operating at high frequencies (6 GHz and above, such as mmWave), where beamforming is used to overcome high pathloss but beams are prone to blockage and failure.

Example embodiments provide a computer-implemented method in which a user equipment (UE) determines a measurement period duration based on the periods of one or more periodic beam failure detection (BFD) reference signals (RSs) that have a quasi-co-located (QCL) relationship with demodulation RSs (DMRSs) of PDCCH receptions monitored by the UE. The UE monitors a subset of these BFD RSs during each measurement period and, if measures of all BFD RSs in the subset fail to meet a specified threshold (e.g., signal quality or block error rate), reports a beam failure (BF) instance to a higher layer entity, such as a MAC layer entity. A beam failure is declared when a specified number of consecutive BF instances occurs, after which the UE may identify a candidate beam and send a beam failure recovery request (BFRQ).

The measurement period duration may be determined by the shortest period of the assessed BFD RSs, or the maximum of that shortest period and a specified value, ensuring at least one assessed BFD RS is present in each measurement period. This prevents measurement periods lacking assessed BFD RSs, which would otherwise reset the consecutive BF instance counter and cause occurring beam failures to be missed.

The disclosure also addresses cases where a scheduled BFD RS is not transmitted, such as when a periodic CSI-RS overlaps with control signaling. Embodiments propose either ignoring such measurement periods when updating the counter or treating them as BF instances by incrementing the counter.

The document further describes example BFD RS sequences illustrating these problems and solutions, flow diagrams of UE operations for making and processing BF measurements, an example communication system comprising electronic devices, radio access networks, base stations, and a core network, and example device architectures for an ED and a base station.

The passage presents MOTO, a multi-objective three-layer optimization framework for systematically mapping local transition-state networks around a given minimum on a potential energy surface. It comprises (i) a multi-objective explorer using NSGA-II to generate diverse, feasible initial configurations based on diversity, feasibility, and minimum-mode separability objectives; (ii) a bilayer minimum-mode-following kernel that estimates the lowest-curvature subspace via Hessian-vector-product-based Lanczos/LOBPCG and ascends to index-1 saddles using the minimum-mode force with L-BFGS or CG; and (iii) deterministic two-sided minimum-mode descent to certify connectivity. Benchmarks on atomistic spin systems show the HVP-based kernel scales to 10⁶ spins with under 1 GB incremental memory and 0.5 s wall time, and on a 70×70 system reduces peak memory to about 0.01% of an explicit-Hessian approach with a tenfold speedup. Applications include an artificial Bloch-type spin model, a DFT-parameterized Pd/Fe/Ir(111) system where twelve index-1 saddles and up to 32 transition channels connect skyrmion, antiskyrmion, chiral-droplet, and multi-skyrmion basins via meron/antimeron-mediated mechanisms, and a Ni(111) heptamer benchmark demonstrating transferability to Cartesian coordinates. Noted limitations include sensitivity to mask design and kernel hyperparameters such as Krylov depth and line-search thresholds.

Google fired software engineer James Damore for circulating a memo arguing that women are underrepresented in tech because of innate biological differences—stronger interest in people, greater neuroticism, and lower drive for status than men. The passage argues that neuroscience contradicts the memo's assumption that such differences are fixed. Research shows men and women are more similar than different, with traits existing on a spectrum rather than in two categories, and brains described as mosaics of male and female characteristics. The brain is plastic, changing with experience: spatial cognition training can boost performance, and the gender gap in spatial skills is diminishing or even reversed in some cultures. Stereotype threat—anxiety about group-based expectations—affects performance and brain activity, as do perceived low status and self-critical attitudes. Empowerment techniques can alter brain activity and counter these effects. The author concludes that differences Damore attributed to biology may stem from the environment he endorsed, making diversity training appropriate.
