This discussion paper argues that AI policy and compliance considerations will significantly impact the AI development life cycle, yet such discussions are largely absent from computer science curricula. The authors synthesize AI regulatory developments in the United States and European Union: the US lacks comprehensive federal legislation and exhibits partisan divides, exemplified by President Trump's 2025 rescission of Biden's EO 14110 and its replacement with EO 14179 emphasizing "global AI dominance"; the EU enacted the AI Act in 2024, organizing AI systems by risk level, prohibiting certain practices outright, and imposing transparency requirements on general-purpose models. Three themes emerge: the rapidly changing policy landscape, the challenge of achieving technical compliance with non-technical specifications, and cross-border regulatory influence (the "Brussels Effect"). The paper proposes a framework for integrating AI policy discussions in CS courses, structured around three perspectives (socio-political, translational, technical) and three dimensions (scope, power, agency), operationalized through a grid of guiding questions. Future work includes developing targeted curricular activities and applying requirements engineering to bridge the principles-to-practices gap.

When a penalty kick is awarded during normal play, it is a re-start, meaning the ball is live once kicked. If the kick is saved, blocked, or rebounds off the goal, full play resumes immediately. Under Law 14, all players except the kicker and goalkeeper must be at least 10 yards from the penalty mark, behind the mark, inside the field of play, and outside the Penalty Area. Players must take positions immediately to box out opponents and may only enter the Penalty Area or Arc after the ball is touched and moves forward. All attacking players must follow up on penalty kicks, as the kicker cannot touch the ball again until another player does. If the goalkeeper secures the ball, attackers must switch to a defensive mode. Violations result in a retaken kick or an indirect free kick.

This passage is a datasheet excerpt for the ADS8681W, ADS8685W, and ADS8689W, 16-bit SAR ADC data acquisition devices with an integrated analog front-end (AFE), programmable gain amplifier (PGA), ADC driver, and voltage reference.

Key points:
- The PGA converts single-ended or differential inputs for the SAR ADC, with gain set via RANGE_SEL[3:0] bits (default ±3V × VREF), using trimmed resistor networks for low gain error.
- A second-order antialiasing low-pass filter with a typical 500kHz –3dB cutoff follows the PGA.
- The device uses an internal 4.096V reference (default) or an external reference, selected by the INTREF_DIS bit. The internal reference is factory-trimmed, temperature-compensated from –40°C to +125°C, and can shift due to solder reflow thermal stress.
- The ADC outputs straight-binary data; LSB size equals FSR/2¹⁶.
- Alarm features include a user-programmable input alarm with hysteresis and an AVDD alarm with fixed 4.7V/5.3V thresholds, with active and tripped flags readable via the ALARM_REG register, the ALARM pin, or appended to output data.
- The multiSPI digital interface supports legacy SPI protocols, dual SDO mode, source-synchronous protocols, and daisy-chain topology for multiple devices.
- The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states, uses 32-bit data transfer frames, and provides nine configuration registers with read/write/clear/set commands.
- An application example describes an 8-channel industrial analog input module using the ADS8681W with a MUX36D08 multiplexer for PLCs, supporting standard voltage and current ranges.
- Power supply recommendations cover AVDD/DVDD decoupling; NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption at lower throughput rates. PCB layout guidelines address grounding, decoupling, and reference capacitor placement.
- Revision A (May 2025) changed ADS8685W and ADS8689W status from Advance Information to Production Data.

A multiscale framework linking atomistic solid-melt interface energetics to macroscopic GaN growth kinetics was developed and experimentally validated. Machine-learning interatomic potential-based molecular dynamics simulations showed that liquid Ga forms ordered, layered structures at GaN(s)-Ga(l) interfaces, with stronger, longer-ranged ordering at the Ga-polar interface than the N-polar one, while charge redistribution remains confined to the first interfacial layers. Well-tempered metadynamics quantified free energy landscapes for N adatom adsorption and migration, revealing a "Ga lubrication" mechanism in which interfacial liquid Ga lowers N migration barriers (0.56 eV Ga-polar; 0.34 eV N-polar) compared with a clean surface (~1.1 eV). Step-edge (Ehrlich-Schwoebel) barriers exceeding 0.6 eV were also measured. Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations parameterized by these barriers indicated that under realistic MBE conditions, GaN grows in a diffusion-controlled, layer-by-layer regime. A parameter-free diffusion-controlled model, based on a modified Fick's law incorporating the metadynamics-derived free energy profile, N diffusivity, and N solubility, predicted facet-dependent growth rates of 0.01–0.04 nm/s. These predictions were validated by MBE growth of partially nitridated Ga/GaN particles characterized by STEM/HRTEM, with measured radii and rates reproducing the predicted facet trends. The work establishes that, for systems with low solubility of key elements such as N in liquid Ga, the interfacial free energy profile for adatom adsorption and migration governs crystal growth kinetics, in contrast to III-V systems like InP and GaAs where droplet chemistry dominates. Limitations include unmodeled impurities, machine learning potential transferability, and simplifying assumptions in the transport model.

In soccer, the second defender provides individual support to the first defender who is controlling the opponent with the ball. Also called the "support" or "cover" defender, they position themselves behind and inside relative to the first defender, remaining goalside and far enough back to react if the first defender is beaten. This inside positioning forces the dribbler toward the sideline. The support defender must maintain appropriate distance without overrunning the play, use the same stance as the first defender, and adjust position as play develops. They must announce their arrival verbally, and proper oral communication is critical, including calls for support, jockey/delay/control/contain, and tackle. The second defender makes these calls because they can see the field while the first defender focuses on the ball. If the first defender is beaten, the support defender likely takes over.

This study compared air-conduction (AC) and bone-conduction (BC) auditory brainstem response (ABR) and auditory steady-state response (ASSR) thresholds in infants aged 0–6 months with normal hearing (NH) and conductive hearing loss (CHL), recruited through newborn hearing screening. Fifty infants completed testing; CHL was observed only at 500 Hz. At 500 Hz, AC ABR and AC ASSR thresholds were significantly higher in the CHL group, while BC thresholds did not differ between groups. ABR and ASSR thresholds were poorly correlated. Air-bone gaps (ABGs) were significantly larger in the CHL group for both ABR (36 dB vs. 15 dB) and ASSR (21 dB vs. 12 dB), but ABR showed better separation between NH and CHL groups than ASSR. Minimum "normal" intensities for ASSR (40 and 30 dB HL for 500 Hz AC and BC) were higher than corresponding ABR minimum intensities. Sensitivity and specificity for detecting CHL were highest for AC ABR threshold measurement compared to screening measures and ASSR thresholds. The authors conclude that ASSR threshold and ABG variability was too great to reliably distinguish mild low-frequency CHL from normal hearing, and that the ABR should remain the gold-standard diagnostic tool in early hearing detection and intervention programs, with further ASSR research needed before clinical implementation.

The passage describes the NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture, which introduces dedicated RT Cores for hardware-accelerated real-time ray tracing. RT Cores handle Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, offloading the SM and delivering over 10 Giga Rays/Sec—roughly 10 times faster than Pascal's software-based approach. Turing uses a Hybrid Rendering model combining ray tracing and rasterization, supported by denoising algorithms that reduce rays needed per pixel.

The architecture also features NGX (Neural Graphics Acceleration), a deep learning stack using Tensor Cores that includes DLSS (producing TAA-comparable quality with roughly half the shading work), InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. Additional rendering advancements include Mesh Shading (Task and Mesh shaders that eliminate CPU draw call bottlenecks), Variable Rate Shading (VRS) allowing per-16x16-pixel shading rate control for techniques like Content Adaptive Shading, Motion Adaptive Shading, and Foveated Rendering, Texture Space Shading (TSS) which decouples shading from screen space, and Multi-View Rendering (MVR) supporting up to four views per pass for VR and multi-view applications.

Turing GPUs support VR through USB Type-C/VirtualLink connectivity. The passage details chip specifications for TU104 (used in GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, Quadro RTX 5000) and TU106 (GeForce RTX 2070), and introduces RTX-OPS, a workload-based performance metric accounting for tensor, FP32, RT core, and INT32 operations. Ray tracing fundamentals, including BVH structures and denoising, are explained, along with quality improvements in ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections demonstrated in games like Battlefield V and Shadow of the Tomb Raider. The document concludes with NVIDIA legal disclaimers and trademark information.

This study examines the global, regional, and national legal frameworks guiding inclusive education and assesses educational leaders' awareness of these frameworks in Addis Ababa's inclusive education resource centers. Using a qualitative case study design, researchers purposively selected three resource centers and fifteen respondents—school principals, itinerant teachers, teachers, and Ministry of Education (MoE) Inclusion Department experts—collecting data through semi-structured interviews and document review, analyzed thematically.

Document review identified key global frameworks (UDHR, ICERD, CRC, Salamanca Statement, CRPD, Marrakesh Treaty, SDGs), regional African instruments (ACHPR, ACRWC, African Disability Protocol), and Ethiopian national frameworks (the Constitution, Proclamation No. 1263/2021, the Education and Training Policy 2023, ESDP VI, the Special Needs/Inclusive Education Strategy 2022, and the National Children's Policy 2017).

Findings on awareness revealed varying levels: MoE experts demonstrated solid understanding of international and national frameworks but noted Ethiopia lacks a specific stand-alone inclusive education policy. School principals showed limited awareness, citing busy schedules and insufficient training. Itinerant teachers, benefiting from special needs education backgrounds, showed strong awareness and observed that principals' and district leaders' understanding was low. General teachers were largely unaware of legal frameworks, viewing inclusion as a matter of compassion rather than policy.

The study concludes that while a favorable policy and legal environment exists, successful implementation depends on leaders' awareness, which varies by role and educational background. It recommends regular professional development for school leaders, integration of inclusive education policies into teacher training curricula, and MoE-level monitoring of practitioners' policy awareness.

Yoga and fitness were once separate worlds, but yoga options for athletes and fitness enthusiasts have expanded. Yoga offers benefits including improved breathing, meditation, concentration, flexibility, balance, and injury prevention, with consistent results regardless of motivation. Choosing a class depends on individual goals and needs. Hatha yoga, the umbrella term for styles involving physical postures, is most common in the western world. Popular styles include Ashtanga Vinyasa (a physically demanding set series), Vinyasa Flow (variable pose sequences linked with breath), Iyengar (alignment-focused and therapeutic, using props), Bikram/Hot Yoga (26 poses in a hot, humid room), Yin Yoga (long holds releasing connective tissue tension), Restorative Yoga (slow-paced and prop-supported), and Kripalu (gentle, meditation-focused). Specialty classes also serve runners, cyclists, and other athletes by addressing sport-specific muscle imbalances. Tight muscles can cause joint instability, reduced blood supply, scar tissue, and overuse syndrome, so athletes should choose gentler or complementary yoga styles to balance hard training. The government shutdown prevented the Bureau of Labor Statistics from releasing its September nonfarm payrolls report and weekly jobless claims. The Dow Jones consensus forecast had been 51,000 payroll gains with unemployment steady at 4.3%. Alternative data sources suggest employment growth was anemic but the labor market remained stable rather than deteriorating. Indeed's job postings fell about 8.9% year over year as of September 26, and ADP reported a September decline of 32,000 jobs. Goldman Sachs estimated weekly jobless claims at 224,000. The labor market is uneven, with health care hiring strong while other fields, such as software development, lag. Employers remain reluctant to lay off workers. Spending data from Bank of America and Fiserv showed solid growth, though small business indicators reveal many job openings going unfilled.

The President reports to Congress on an agent's findings regarding Texas's political, military, and civil condition and explains why the Executive has not recognized Texas's independence. Though both houses of Congress passed resolutions favoring recognition once Texas demonstrated a functioning civil government, the President holds that recognizing a state that has forcibly separated from a power still claiming dominion over it is a delicate act that could be regarded as unfriendly or as justifiable cause of war. Following the established policy of avoiding interference in other nations' internal disputes—applied previously to Spain's revolted colonies, Mexico, New Granada, Venezuela, and Ecuador, all recognized only after their independence was secure—he notes that although Mexico's civil authority in Texas has been expelled and its invading army defeated, Mexico appears to possess greater physical force and is menacing a fresh invasion. Extra caution is warranted because Texas was once claimed by the United States, many of its inhabitants are American emigrants, and it has resolved to seek admission to the Union and to treat for the transfer of its territory to the United States upon recognition. Prudence therefore dictates maintaining the current position until Texas's ability to sustain its independence is proven beyond dispute, while deferring to Congress's judgment on the matter.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated April 28, 2016, announcing its first quarter 2016 financial results. The press release is included as Exhibit 99.1, with information on non-GAAP financial measures as Exhibit 99.2. In Q1 2016, Amazon began allocating stock-based compensation and "Other operating expense (income), net" to its segment results, combined as "Stock-based compensation and other." Historical 2015 and 2014 results for the North America, International, and AWS segments are presented in Exhibit 99.3. Consolidated net sales, operating income (loss), and net income (loss) are not affected. The report was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Modeling nanoscale light-matter interactions is essential for quantum technologies, but classical Maxwell solvers cannot capture nonclassical features such as photon correlations and entanglement, while quantum approaches describe idealized systems and become computationally prohibitive for large systems. The authors introduce a stochastic differential equation (SDE) approach, formulated as a stochastic Bloch-vector method, that links quantum emitter dynamics to classical electromagnetic fields and offers potential integration with Maxwell solvers. Unlike existing derivations based on phase-space representations, quantum trajectory methods, or quantum Langevin equations, their approach does not rely on wave-function unraveling, phase-space representations, or operator-valued noise. As a first validation, they model the Mollow spectrum from a coherently driven two-level system, comparing against experiments. They also address a gap in stochastic modeling by deriving a stochastic Bloch vector from a complex, non-symmetric diffusion matrix, capturing asymmetric noise correlations arising from non-commuting quantum operators.

Czech crown hedging costs against the euro hit their highest in over nine months on speculation the central bank would soon remove the currency cap. New car registrations rose 14.2 percent year-on-year in the first quarter to 68,059 vehicles. Prague prosecutors cleared the way for a hearing on extraditing a Russian accused of hacking LinkedIn. RWE is considering selling its majority stake in Hungary's second-biggest power plant. The kuna fell on Agrokor debt uncertainty while other Central European currencies firmed. Press reports: pipeline operator Mero seeks to increase TAL pipeline exports; the cabinet approved an 80 million crown state bid for insolvent miner OKD; Prague Airport plans 27 billion crowns in investment to raise capacity.

Chefs' Warehouse (CHEF) trades at a premium 33.3x forward P/E, which the author argues is justified by growth catalysts. A target price of $79.3 by FY 2027 implies 36% upside from current levels. EPS is forecast to grow at a 16.7% CAGR through 2028, versus a 5.9% staples sector median. CHEF shows 8.4% revenue growth, margin expansion, and strong pricing power in a resilient luxury market segment, with a client base of luxury restaurants and hotels that insulates it from consumer trade-downs in a weaker economy. The remainder of the passage consists of author credentials, disclosures, and unrelated article titles.

Saudi Arabia's government has approved the University of New Haven to open a branch campus in Riyadh, potentially making it the first university in the world to do so. The campus is expected to open next fall and eventually enroll 13,000 students—more than the university's U.S. enrollment of under 10,000. President Jens Frederiksen described a "paradigm shift" in the kingdom toward bringing international institutions in rather than sending students abroad, and said the campus will advance Vision 2030 goals to diversify the oil-reliant economy. Other universities, including Australia's University of Wollongong, also seek Riyadh campuses. New Haven has partnered with the Saudi royal family since the late 1990s and helped develop King Fahd Security College's security studies program, which drew criticism after Jamal Khashoggi's 2018 killing. The English-only campus will include three colleges and remain coed. The university still needs approval from its accreditor, the New England Commission of Higher Education.

The President transmits departmental reports in answer to a Senate resolution. Finding the military commandant of California exercising civil governor functions under an arrangement made by his predecessor, he left it undisturbed, making no appointment, conferring no authority, and allowing no added compensation. He sent Thomas Butler King and other officers to California and New Mexico to aid execution of the treaty and inform Congress. He encouraged the Territories to form state constitutions if prepared, but did not authorize any interference with elections or conventions, insisting domestic policy originate solely with the people. He has no information on laws passed or censuses taken there. He urged early applications for statehood to help Congress avoid agitation over whether involuntary servitude should be prohibited in acquired territories. Western Californians have formed a constitution and will seek admission, which he recommends approving if compliant with the U.S. Constitution. Texas claims much of New Mexico; since no tribunal can decide the boundary question, Congress must devise an adjustment, though he deems establishing a territorial government over the disputed district beforehand inexpedient. Attaching conditions to California's admission affecting her domestic institutions would be resented as an invasion of self-government, as states may later alter their constitutions. He expects no material inconvenience from lacking congressional government east of California and reiterates his policy of awaiting causes that will settle the question, avoiding geographical parties and preserving harmony.

The passage documents the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) specification, which standardizes communication between guests and hypervisors for AMD's SEV-ES (Secure Encrypted Virtualization - Encrypted State) and SEV-SNP (Secure Nested Paging) technologies. These features protect guest register state from the hypervisor by encrypting it during world switches.

The GHCB is a 4KB shared memory page mapped decrypted to enable guest-hypervisor communication. The document standardizes required Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) events, minimum guest state exposure, and specific actions such as NMI handling and SMP booting.

Version 2 introduced hypervisor feature advertisement via a FEATURES bitmap and initial SEV-SNP support. Revisions 2.01 through 2.04 added features including VLEK certificate definitions, APIC ID list retrieval, multiple VMPL level support, SEV-TIO trusted I/O, and Secure AVIC backing page management.

The GHCB MSR protocol enables communication before the GHCB page is established, covering protocol negotiation, CPUID requests, SEV information requests, AP reset hold, and GHCB GPA registration. NAE events include MMIO access, page state changes, SNP Guest Requests, AP creation, #HV doorbell page management, IPI sending, and timer support.

SMP booting under SEV-ES/SNP requires alternative approaches since hypervisors cannot modify measured register states, using AP reset hold mechanisms or the SNP AP Creation NAE event. NMI handling relies on "NMI Complete" messages from the guest. Hardware debug register virtualization is supported where available. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

The SNP Restricted Injection feature limits host communication to #HV doorbell exceptions, using a structured doorbell page with pending event and EOI assist fields to manage interrupt delivery between host and guest.

Researchers at NASA Glenn Research Center in Cleveland use the Glenn Extreme Environments Rig (GEER), the largest and most accurate simulator of other planets' conditions, to replicate Venus's surface atmosphere, heat, and pressure. A record 80-day test radically altered the chemistry of rock samples from Case Western Reserve University. Venus's surface has lead-melting temperatures, pressures 100 times Earth's, acid clouds, and a dense supercritical carbon dioxide atmosphere; Soviet probes in the 1970s survived only minutes to hours. NASA's Phil Neudeck's team developed a computer chip that operated for 21 days in the simulator—the first multi-week electronics test in a Venus environment. Physicist Geoffrey Landis notes Venus underwent a runaway greenhouse effect that boiled away its oceans, but its cooler upper atmosphere could support floating colonies and possibly microbial life, and studying Venus helps predict Earth's climatic future.
The speaker attributed the team's struggles to poor forechecking against the league's best backchecking team, and a save on Bondra that prevented the momentum needed after a bad first period.

Viridor, working with the Somerset Waste Partnership, has begun building a £252M resource recovery centre at Avonmouth to convert Somerset's non-recyclable household rubbish into energy. Viridor states the process is safe, with emissions treated to meet European Industrial Emissions Directive standards and continually monitored by the Environment Agency. A Health Protection Agency report found modern incinerators make only a small contribution to local air pollution.

Andrew Triggs pitched six strong innings and Mark Canha homered as the Oakland A's beat the Texas Rangers 3-2 for their fourth straight win. Triggs (2-0) allowed one run on four hits, and Santiago Casilla earned his first save. Adrian Beltre drove in both Rangers runs but injured his left hamstring. Martin James Cooper, 66, was found guilty of 30 historical child sex offences for abusing four girls and four boys aged 11 to 16 while he and his wife ran the Warminda Hostel in East Victoria Park between 1978 and 1983. Victims described a culture of fear, detailing physical, sexual, and verbal abuse. His bail request, citing dementia and health issues, was denied, and he was remanded in custody until sentencing.

The S&P 500 closed 1.60% lower Friday at 6,212.69, its lowest level since early July, falling 3.33% over two days from a record high of 6,427.02 and losing 2.36% for the week. A study led by Ian Stephen of Macquarie University found that women preferred the body odor of men who ate more fruits and vegetables, while men who ate more carbohydrates smelled less appealing. Researchers measured men's skin carotenoid levels using a spectrophotometer, collected food frequency questionnaires, and had women rate the scent of sweat from exercise T-shirts. Meat consumption did not affect odor attractiveness but made it more intense. A 2006 study similarly found women preferred the odor of men on non-meat diets. According to George Preti, body odor results from skin bacteria metabolizing sweat compounds, not from food smells directly transferring to sweat. The study was small but results were consistent.

A player with a ligament injury (Modano) will make his own call on playing, since no further damage can occur; he must handle shooting, faceoffs, and passing, and the team views the game as critical. This article examines trauma-informed human rights education (TIHRE) in higher education. Although human rights education (HRE) spans lifelong learning and is relevant across disciplines, it remains largely siloed as a law school offering, and existing teaching models pre-date contemporary threats such as climate change, artificial intelligence and efforts to decolonise the curriculum. HRE teaching focuses on legal doctrine while avoiding politically sensitive historical case studies, risking retraumatisation of learners, many of whom have adverse childhood experiences or intergenerational trauma. Based on a structured, interdisciplinary literature review, the article makes three recommendations: educators should clarify their values and cultivate a rights-respecting teaching persona to identify unconscious biases; trauma-informed principles should be embedded in content design through student co-creation, project-based learning, skills development, reflective practice and careful use of trigger warnings, while avoiding retraumatisation and exploitative portrayals of trauma; and dialogic teaching should be adopted, including engagement with survivors and practitioners as guest speakers. Drawing on the UN's 'about, through and for' framework and SAMHSA's six trauma-informed principles, the article concludes that trauma-informed HRE can move learners from apathy towards advocacy, placing wellbeing, agency and dignity at the centre of the shared learning experience.

This study evaluates strategies for developing machine learning potentials (MLPs) for material surfaces using Universal Interatomic Potentials (UIPs). Because UIPs are predominantly trained on bulk datasets and tend to systematically underestimate surface energies (a phenomenon called "softening"), the authors compare four approaches: training from scratch (TS), zero-shot prediction (ZS) with pre-trained models, fine-tuning (FT), and multi-head fine-tuning (MHFT), which trains concurrently on original bulk and new surface data. After benchmarking several pre-trained models on diatomic potential energy curves, MACE was selected as the foundation model.

Three surface systems were tested. For gold (unary, 2,545 configurations), FT models consistently outperformed TS models; fine-tuning with only 40 configurations achieved errors comparable to or better than TS trained on 2,000 configurations, and FT produced physically realistic Au–Au pair potentials where TS showed unphysical short- and long-range behavior. For RuO₂ (binary, 340 structures), FT again showed lower errors, though force errors were larger than for gold; the TS O–O pair potential exhibited unphysical features, while FT was largely reasonable, with a high energy barrier (~500 eV) preventing unphysical configurations. For BiVO₄ (ternary, 928 calculations), FT achieved the lowest force error (0.17 eV/Å) with few outliers, leveraging the foundation model's knowledge of high-force environments, whereas TS produced more large-force outliers despite a lower overall force RMSE than ZS.

In Case 4, FT on gold data degraded predictions for other unary metal surfaces (Ag, Cu, Pt, Ir). MHFT, trained on gold surface data plus 200,000 MPTrj points, achieved the lowest surface-energy RMSE (16 meV/Å², versus 27 for ZS and 88 for FT), though with slight degradation on gold that remained negligible relative to DFT reproducibility limits. The authors conclude that FT improves accuracy with fewer training samples and mitigates bulk-model limitations, while MHFT is advantageous when preserving pre-trained bulk performance; aligning computational conditions and energy references between datasets is also noted as important, particularly for MHFT.

This IDC White Paper examines the use of IT-based simulation, modeling, and data analysis, and high-performance computing (HPC), in manufacturing. It is based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers at discrete and process manufacturing enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

Industrial enterprises face pressures including geopolitical uncertainty, rising energy prices, raw material shortages, supply chain disruptions, skilled labor shortfalls, and sustainability demands, making digitalization and reliable data foundations critical for competitiveness. Three-quarters of respondents consider increasing innovation the most important business objective of simulation, modeling, and analytics, and 57% view them as important for improving product and service quality. Around half of enterprises already use these tools in product development and production and process planning, with deployment expected to reach 90% within two years; 64% plan investments in modern simulation, modeling, and high-performance data analytics. Data silos caused by the absence of a holistic data strategy remain a barrier, and IDC recommends integrating data sources into a unified information base.

New usage scenarios include virtual prototyping, digital twins, digital verification and validation, and high-performance data analytics (already used by 42%). Demand for high-performance calculations is expected to rise sharply: currently 8% report high demand, expected to reach almost half within two years, while half of respondents say calculations take too long.

81% of decision makers view HPC as a game changer for product and process innovation, rising to 96% among enterprises that have implemented it. Over a quarter already use professional HPC infrastructures and another 39% are planning or piloting deployment. Most prefer external infrastructures (87%), colocation datacenters (74%), or research institutions (43%); only 6% operate on-premises HPC. Key challenges include security concerns (72%), high investment and licensing costs, and energy consumption and sustainability (58%).

The paper investigates whether the textual content of earnings press releases predicts stock returns on earnings announcement days. Using over 138,000 press releases from more than 6,000 U.S. firms between 2005 and 2023, the authors apply natural language processing techniques—including Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and BERT-family models such as FinBERT—within a rolling-window framework that avoids look-ahead bias. They find that soft information from press releases is as informative as earnings surprises in explaining announcement-day returns, with FinBERT performing best and a combined R² of about 4%. A long-short trading strategy based on agreement between hard and soft signals generates no profits when entered after market open, supporting market efficiency; however, if press release content is obtained in advance—as in documented hacking incidents—traders can on average correctly predict 56% of the top 10 performing stocks. Topic analysis indicates a self-serving bias, with managers framing internal factors more positively than external ones. Soft information does not explain prior-day returns, suggesting a low likelihood of press release leakage on average.

The Federal Reserve has raised its benchmark short-term rate by a quarter point—its fourth hike in 18 months—to a range of 1 to 1.25 percent, with one more increase expected this year. The effects vary: credit card debt, home equity lines, and some adjustable-rate mortgages will likely rise, while fixed mortgage rates and auto loan rates have barely changed since late 2015. Fixed mortgage rates track the 10-year Treasury rather than the Fed, and the 30-year rate recently averaged 4.04 percent. Higher U.S. rates attract foreign investment, strengthen the dollar, and can pull capital from developing countries. Consumers with poor credit face higher borrowing costs, especially for used cars. Savers see modest gains: average one-year CD rates rose from 0.27 to 0.35 percent, with smaller banks offering better rates than large ones. Retirees holding bonds are advised to maintain balanced portfolios.

U.S. government bonds fell after a jobs report showed wage gains and the first monthly job losses since 2010. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 2.370% and the two-year to 1.511%, both up for four consecutive weeks. The economy lost 33,000 jobs, unemployment fell to a 16-year low of 4.2%, and hourly earnings rose 2.9%. Traders attributed job losses to hurricanes and focused on inflationary wage gains. Fed-funds futures showed an 88% chance of a December rate increase, and anticipated Treasury auctions also pushed yields higher.

A UCLA study found that meat-based food for America's 163 million dogs and cats, along with their waste, generates about 64 million tons of carbon dioxide annually—equivalent to 13.6 million cars. Pets account for 25-30% of the environmental impact of US meat consumption. Study author Gregory Okin isn't recommending vegetarian pet diets but wants owners to consider climate impacts. A UC Davis professor noted pet food mostly uses rendered byproducts that would otherwise be wasted. While some advocates report dogs thriving on vegan diets, veterinarians warn against plant-based pet foods, noting cats need taurine from meat and many vegetarian products fail nutritional standards.

Students returned to North Park Elementary School in San Bernardino a week after Cedric Anderson killed his estranged wife, teacher Karen Smith, and 8-year-old Jonathan Martinez before fatally shooting himself; 9-year-old Nolan Brandy was wounded. Superintendent Dale Marsden called the reopening a first step toward healing, with tightened security and counselors available.

De Ceuvel is an experimental, temporary docklands regeneration project in Amsterdam's Buiksloterham district, described as a 'playground for circular cities'. Built from renovated houseboats on a former shipyard, it serves as a co-working hub for artists, entrepreneurs and researchers, with phytoremedial plants drawing toxins from polluted soil. Designed to last ten years, it minimises waste through a wormery, composting toilets producing fertiliser and compost for gardens and aquaponics, and solar panels with heat exchangers. A smart meter system lets offices earn 'Jouliettes' cryptocurrency for surplus solar power, planned as a future local currency. The project emerged after the financial crisis stalled luxury development, offering an inclusive, restorative alternative that heals the land at a fraction of the cost.

The University of Notre Dame received two gifts totaling $205 million in two weeks. Alumnus Matthew Walsh and his wife Joyce donated $150 million to the School of Architecture, which will be renamed for them. Francis and Kathleen Rooney donated to endow an institute promoting scholarship and dialogue on American democracy, first established in 2008 as the Rooney Center for the Study of American Democracy.

Kilauea's eruption, now in its 27th day, has sent volcanic haze 4,000 miles to Guam, prompting warnings for residents with respiratory issues to stay indoors. On Hawaii's Big Island, fast-moving lava from Fissure 8 is advancing at 600 yards per hour, threatening homes in Leilani Estates and Lanipuna Gardens. Lava fountains reaching 200 feet have produced "Pele's hair"—sharp volcanic glass fibers that can irritate skin and eyes. Officials are evacuating Kapoho residents ahead of advancing lava. Since May 3, about 22 fissures have opened, destroying at least 40 homes and covering 2,000 acres, with roughly 200 people in emergency shelters. The USGS also responded to a public inquiry, advising against roasting marshmallows over volcanic vents.

Peel Regional Police investigating the video-recorded beating of a 29-year-old autistic man at the Square One mall bus station on March 13 now believe the three suspects are originally from British Columbia's lower mainland and recently travelled to the GTA. With the surveillance video viewed more than 300,000 times, police are asking media and residents in the Vancouver area, including Surrey, Abbotsford and Richmond, to view the footage. The victim remains shaken, and anyone with information is asked to contact police or Crime Stoppers.

The RSI indicator appears to work on Bitcoin and cryptocurrencies, but only when used as a momentum indicator. The crypto market differs from traditional equities because it is new, lacks a long history, and does not produce tangible value like equity ownership. Backtests of mean reversion strategies—buying low RSI readings and selling high readings—produced weak results on Bitcoin with few trades; the best variation had only three trades, making it unusable, and Ethereum and Dogecoin showed similar results. In contrast, momentum strategies performed much better. One example, buying when the five-day RSI crosses above 50 and selling when it falls below 50, achieved a 122% CAGR versus 101% for buy and hold, with drawdowns of 39% versus 83%. Similar positive results were found for Ethereum and Dogecoin.

Arkansas inmate Don Davis had his last meal as courts decided his fate. The 8th Circuit Court of Appeals overturned a federal ruling halting all eight executions, finding the midazolam lethal injection method did not cause undue severe pain.

SpinGPT is a large-language-model agent for the Spin & Go poker format, built on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and trained in two stages: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on 320,000 decisions from 8,800 professional Spin & Go hands, followed by offline reinforcement learning with ORPO on 270,000 hands generated by the GTO solver InstaGTO, mixed with 50,000 human hands. The SFT model (SpinGPT-SFT) imitated the professional player with 80% exact accuracy and, after a heuristic patch replacing deep-stack all-ins, achieved a win rate of 13.4 ± 12.9 BB/100 against the Slumbot benchmark over 30,000 hands. The final SpinGPT model achieved 79% exact accuracy on professional data and 72% on solver data (78% tolerant accuracy), with bet-sizing MAE improving from 0.61 to 0.30 BB, and defeated SpinGPT-SFT at 13.2 ± 7.24 BB/100 over 10,000 duplicate hands. Limitations include the absence of a Slumbot evaluation for the final model and typical LLM errors such as numerical mistakes. Future work includes stronger foundation models, retrieval-augmented GTO charts, opponent adaptivity, explainability, and hybrid LLM-solver approaches.

This manuscript illustrates the value and potential of critical approaches to quantitative research in education, offering epistemological and methodological considerations for scholars practicing quantitative criticalism. Its intended audiences include education researchers using quantitative methods and/or critical perspectives—such as students, faculty, institutional research staff, and methods instructors—as well as those evaluating or applying critical theories in quantitative studies.

The authors argue that quantitative research has never been objective and present their positionalities: Jay, a white cisgender queer researcher, studies queer and trans collegians and seeks to dismantle white cisheteropatriarchal dominance; Jimmy, a Vietnamese-Chinese American, critiques the aggregation of Asian American data that masks inequalities and emphasizes minimizing harm in institutional research.

Quantitative criticalism combines quantitative methods with critical epistemologies, holding that numbers are not neutral, analyses must account for systemic oppression, and justice-driven criticality must span the entire research process. The authors stress community and solidarity, community partnership in research design, data sovereignty, and transparency in collaborations.

They identify tensions including the white supremacist and cisheteropatriarchial origins of statistics (e.g., Galton's and Pearson's eugenics work), an undefined threshold of criticality, essentialist demographic variables, limited analytical options for intersectional and small samples, and conflicts between generalizability and community-specific counterstories.

Four example studies are reviewed: Sablan (2019) applied critical race theory through Yosso's community cultural wealth model to develop scales (QuantCrit); Garvey (2017) used queer theory to examine sexual identity classifications and within-group differences; Szymanski and Lewis (2016) applied intersectionality to African American women's coping with gendered racism using interaction effects; and Wilson and Urick (2022) used latent class analysis alongside intersectionality to study opportunity gaps.

Implications encourage methods instructors to integrate epistemology into curricula, frame criticality as a continuum without a universal threshold, and pose reflective questions about intentions, whether methods rooted in white supremacy can serve justice, and one's threshold of criticality. The authors conclude that quantitative methods without epistemological grounding are insufficient and advocate placing criticality at the root of scholarly work.

A global learning crisis, worsened by pandemic school closures, climate change, conflict and economic slowdown, costs an estimated US$129 billion annually. Youth unemployment nears 30 percent in lower-income countries, and 20 percent of youth worldwide are not in employment, education or training—two-thirds of them young women. Employers report skills gaps, with 39 percent of today's job skills expected to transform or become obsolete by 2030. The Global Partnership for Education (GPE) supports countries through policy dialogue, financing and public-private partnerships to build education systems providing foundational learning and 21st century skills. Examples include over $6 million in funding in Lesotho and a $40 million investment in Ghana. In 2024, 20 GPE grants focused on employment-ready skills, with initiatives in Kenya and El Salvador.

The passage lists 17 common mistakes that can sabotage weight-loss efforts. These include drinking from plastic bottles, which leach fat-storing Bisphenol-A; cutting sweets entirely instead of replacing them with fruits; being overly self-critical after setbacks; emotional eating; consuming store-bought protein bars and energy drinks containing artificial sweeteners; eating sweets at times other than before workouts; surrounding oneself with people who derail goals; relying on weighing scales rather than sticking to a routine; using meal-replacement supplements that increase cravings; eliminating carbs or fats entirely; sleeping fewer than seven hours; eating too little while over-exercising; repeating the same exercise routine until hitting a plateau; drinking calories instead of eating meals; restricting the diet too abruptly; and copying someone else's routine rather than tailoring one to one's own body type, metabolism, and health status.

The passage describes the NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture. Turing introduces a new display engine supporting 8K at 60 Hz via DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2 compression, native HDR processing with tone mapping per ITU-R BT.2100, an enhanced NVENC encoder (HEVC 8K at 30 fps, up to 25% bitrate savings for HEVC), and an updated NVDEC decoder supporting HEVC 4:4:4 and VP9 10/12-bit HDR. Turing GPUs include USB Type-C and VirtualLink support, delivering power, display, and data to VR headsets through a single USB-C connector. TU102 and TU104 use second-generation NVLink for SLI instead of MIO/PCIe, with TU102 providing two x8 links (100 GB/sec bidirectional) and TU104 one x8 link (50 GB/sec bidirectional); only two-way SLI is supported.

Turing TU102, TU104, and TU106 GPUs include RT Cores that accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection, enabling real-time ray tracing roughly 10 times faster than Pascal. Hybrid rendering combines rasterization and ray tracing, aided by denoising. NGX provides AI features using Tensor Cores, including DLSS (similar quality to TAA with roughly half the shading work), InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. New graphics features include Mesh Shading (Task and Mesh shaders), Variable Rate Shading (Content Adaptive Shading, Motion Adaptive Shading, Foveated Rendering), Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering supporting up to four views per pass.

The TU104 contains 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores, used in GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. The TU106 contains 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, used in GeForce RTX 2070 without NVLink or SLI. The RTX-OPS metric weights tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations by usage. The document concludes with an overview of ray tracing mechanics, BVH structures, ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, followed by legal notices and trademark information.

The MACD histogram visually represents the difference between the MACD line and the signal line, helping traders identify momentum changes and potential trend reversals. Bars above the zero line indicate bullish momentum, bars below indicate bearish momentum, and bar height shows momentum strength. The crossover strategy triggers a buy signal when the histogram crosses above zero and a sell signal when it crosses below. The mean-reversion strategy enters on the close and exits on the first day the close is higher than the previous day's close, reversed for shorts. It generated 6,669 trades across 77 ETFs, performing better with long positions. A QLD (2x Nasdaq 100) backtest from 2007 produced 85 trades, 2.2% average gain, 10.4% annual returns, and a 19% max drawdown while invested only 5% of the time.

Onesmo Rupil, 23, began using drugs at 17 and was discontinued from the University of Dodoma in 2013 due to poor performance linked to substance abuse. Since his father can no longer afford his tuition, he has been unable to return. Now recovered from addiction, he manages the Philimisana Foundation Sober House in Mwanza, home to about 30 young people in rehabilitation, most of whom use marijuana. He attributes his drug abuse to lacking personal principles and spiritual contact rather than peer pressure, and to limited parental care from attending boarding school from a young age. He spent over Sh100,000 on heroin, stole laptops at Udom to fund his addiction, and was arrested in 2015 for stealing over 200 laptops, serving six months at Isanga Prison before recovering at rehabilitation centres in Dar es Salaam. This study developed and validated an automated system for monitoring adherence to clinical practice guidelines in intensive care, combining FHIR-encoded computer-interpretable recommendations with patient data standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model. Six recommendations, primarily COVID-19-related, were selected from 41 intensive care guidelines based on expert ratings and encoded in FHIR. Data from five university hospitals (82,015 intensive care episodes, January 2020–May 2023) were transformed to the OMOP CDM via individually developed ETL pipelines. An execution engine interpreted the encoded recommendations and evaluated applicability and adherence for each patient. In a validation study across three hospitals, seven intensive care physicians manually reviewed patient data on ten selected days, and two supervising physicians established ground truth. The system achieved 97.0% accuracy versus 86.6% for human reviewers (p < 0.001), with higher specificity, precision, and F1 score, and processed over 2,000 patient days per second compared with approximately 30 seconds per patient, day, and recommendation for human reviewers. Over 80% of discrepancies were due to human error, while system errors mainly arose from unstructured free-text data not transferred to the OMOP CDM. Observed adherence rates were mostly 10–60%, attributed to newly introduced recommendations, incomplete documentation, and imprecise recommendation wording. The authors conclude the system provides a scalable, accurate, and efficient approach to guideline adherence monitoring.

A paper by Nicholas Lewis and Judith Curry published in the Journal of Climate concludes that high estimates of future global warming from most computer climate simulations are inconsistent with observed warming since 1850, implying future warming will be 30–45% lower than the simulations suggest. Using IPCC AR5 forcing estimates extended to 2016, the study derives a median ECS of 1.66°C (5–95%: 1.15–2.7°C) and a median TCR of 1.33°C (5–95%: 1.15–1.9°C) from globally-complete temperature data, compared with CMIP5 model medians of 3.1°C and 1.9°C respectively. These estimates imply future warming of only 55–70% of central CMIP5 projections. The paper addresses previous criticisms of its methodology, finding them unfounded, and concludes that potential biases from forcing efficacy, sea-surface warming patterns, and temperature estimation issues are minor when using globally-complete temperature data.

This passage is from a Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP version 1.0, dated 16 August 2019) for study ZEA-DNK-02170 (protocol ZP4207-17086). It specifies that summary statistics of plasma glucose concentrations and pharmacodynamic metrics will be presented by treatment group, including mean and individual glucose concentration-time curves.

Safety analyses, based on the safety set, include:
- **Extent of exposure**: Listings and summary tables for insulin administration prior to hypoglycemia induction, the induction procedure, trial medication, and post-treatment rescue glucose infusion; time to first IV glucose infusion will be described with descriptive statistics without censoring.
- **Local tolerability**: Assessed at 30, 120, and 300 minutes post-dose, summarized by time point, symptom, and grade.
- **Adverse events**: Summaries restricted to treatment-emergent AEs (TEAEs), coded using MedDRA version 21.0 or higher; causality assessed by investigators, with missing relationships set to related; severity graded mild/moderate/severe without imputation; overview and frequency tables by system organ class and preferred term, covering AESIs, injection site reactions, SAEs, and deaths.
- **Laboratory parameters**: Tabulated with descriptive statistics, reference-range flagging, and change from baseline (screening visit V1 to follow-up visit V3); covers hematology, biochemistry, coagulation, urinalysis, pregnancy tests, and alcohol breath tests.
- **Vital signs**: Descriptive statistics at baseline and postbaseline time points, with categorical pulse rate analysis.
- **ECG**: Tabulated normal/abnormal assessments, descriptive parameter summaries, and categorical QTcF analyses (>450, >480, >500 ms; changes from baseline >30 and >60 ms).
- **Immunogenicity**: Descriptive analysis of ADA occurrence, counting treatment-induced and treatment-boosted (≥5-fold titer increase) patients.

Changes to protocol-specified analyses include rewording of the primary efficacy analysis with added sensitivity and supportive analyses, and terminology changes for secondary efficacy variables.

Appendix A covers data presentation and programming specifications, including formatting rules, rounding conventions, date handling, and derived variable formulas (e.g., BMI, change from baseline). Appendix B details SAS programming QC requirements covering program review, log review, output review, dataset structure, data verification, and documentation. Appendix C provides an ICH E3-compliant list of tables, figures, and listings, including efficacy tables for time to plasma glucose recovery with sensitivity analyses, safety tables, PK/PD outputs, and patient listings.

Former Fed Chair Janet Yellen said higher interest rates are needed to prevent the U.S. economy from overheating, though the pace must allow inflation to reach the Fed's 2 percent goal. She cited February's 313,000 job gains, calling 90,000-120,000 monthly sustainable. Yellen left the Fed after President Trump appointed Jerome Powell, who is expected to continue gradual rate hikes. Arizona has led the nation in school choice, enacting the first Empowerment Scholarship Account (ESA) voucher program in 2011 and becoming the first state to make it universal in 2022, despite voters rejecting a capped expansion in 2018. The state provides over $1 billion annually in private education subsidies. The Grand Canyon Institute (GCI) finds that universal ESA vouchers are a net cost to the state's general fund—at least $330 million in FY2024 and $350 million in FY2025—because most users never attended public schools. Nearly three-quarters of universal enrollees never attended district or charter schools, though about 90% of new FY2025 entrants came from those schools. Vouchers primarily serve children from higher-income zip codes, though income-based differences have declined. In FY2023, no more than 40% of students used allocations for private school tuition; of the $173 million spent on private schools, 51% went to religious schools, with Evangelical Christian and Catholic schools comprising 86% of religious expenditures. Enrollment grew from 144 students in 2012 to 87,602 by Q3 FY2025. Unspent funds accumulated to $175 million across 60,000 accounts by the end of FY2023, with GCI estimating $360 million by the end of FY2024. GCI notes Arizona provides little accountability or transparency for participating private entities.

The passage describes NVIDIA's RTX Blackwell architecture. Mega Geometry is a new RTX technology enabling ray tracing at full fidelity with LOD systems like Nanite, using Cluster-level Acceleration Structures (CLAS) and a Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structure (PTLAS) to reduce BVH build costs and CPU overhead; it also supports real-time ray tracing of subdivision surfaces and is available across DXR, Vulkan, and OptiX 9.0 on all RTX GPUs from Turing onward. Blackwell's fourth-generation RT Cores deliver up to 2x the ray-triangle intersection rate and add hardware support for Linear Swept Spheres (LSS), which render hair and strand-like objects about 2x faster than DOTS with roughly 5x less VRAM. Shader Execution Reordering (SER) 2.0 doubles reordering efficiency and accelerates neural shading. The AI Management Processor (AMP), a RISC-V-based scheduler, offloads GPU context scheduling from the CPU, matching Microsoft's HAGS model. Blackwell adds 4:2:2 hardware encode/decode, a ninth-generation NVENC with improved AV1/HEVC quality and a new AV1 UHQ mode, a sixth-generation NVDEC with 2x faster H.264 decoding, and DisplayPort 2.1b support up to 80 Gbps. Max-Q improvements include advanced power gating, separate voltage rails, 1000x faster frequency switching, and 10x faster entry into the deepest sleep state, with up to 50% power savings shown in an SLM inference example. DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, producing up to three AI-generated frames per rendered frame, and transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA. Neural shaders are enabled via the Cooperative Vectors API, supporting RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. The document also provides specifications for the GB202, GB203, and GB205 GPUs powering the RTX 5090, 5080, 5070 Ti, and 5070, and concludes with NVIDIA's standard disclaimers and trademark notice.

This study examined the opinions of pre-service teachers regarding the Physical Education and Sports Curriculum (5-8), focusing on outcomes, content, learning-teaching processes, and measurement-evaluation. Using a survey model and a researcher-developed questionnaire, data were collected from 100 students at Bayburt University's Faculty of Sports Sciences, with 25 students drawn from each of four departments through cluster sampling. The questionnaire's comprehensibility and necessity were evaluated with 50 pre-service teachers and three field experts, with a consensus rate of 0.85. Results showed generally positive views on program outcomes, though many respondents were undecided about whether scientific errors existed in the outcome statements. Eighty percent agreed the content was arranged in a meaningful order, while most were undecided about other content features. A majority stated that teaching processes were enriched with activities and used concrete materials, but 60 teachers disagreed that different methods and techniques were used. Responses on assessment and evaluation were mixed. The study concludes that pre-service teachers lacked sufficient knowledge about some program aspects and recommends increasing related research, organizing informative seminars or congresses, and including program evaluation courses in teacher training programs.

This patent application, a divisional of prior applications concerning methods for forming multi-layer vertical NOR-type memory string arrays, describes a fabrication method for 3-dimensional vertical NOR-type memory string arrays using damascene local vertical bit lines. The method avoids ribboning—a stress-induced deformation of microscopic rectangular features—by etching local word lines in two steps, which reduces the aspect ratio of patterning and etching word line stacks, improving structural stability and addressing alignment issues. The detailed description covers forming a memory structure on global interconnect lines, creating trenches and word line stacks, selectively removing silicon nitride layers to form cavities, filling cavities with metal, depositing successive layers (tunneling dielectric, charge storage, blocking dielectric, channel, optional liner, and sacrificial dielectric) in vias, forming source and drain semiconductor regions, and connecting word lines via staircase structures. Alternative embodiments use dielectric pillars for structural support of high aspect ratio word line strips and stacked masks to form the word line strips.

This paper proposes Digital Ecosystems—software systems that exploit the properties of biological ecosystems, such as robustness, scalability, and self-organisation—to address the growing complexity of software development and automate service composition. The authors argue that an ecosystem-inspired approach would be more effective at greater scales than traditional methods. They review existing, disparate uses of the term "digital ecosystem" and define Digital Ecosystems as technology engineered to solve dynamic problems in parallel with high efficiency.

Key design considerations are discussed: complex, dynamic fitness landscapes that map to changing user needs; agents that reproduce, vary, interact, move, and die; spatial dynamics implemented through distributed networks of interconnected habitats with migrating agents; and a balance between system self-organisation and user-imposed fitness constraints, since an additional mechanism is needed to maintain diversity among competing solutions. As Complex Adaptive Systems, Digital Ecosystems offer scalable organisation and rapid adaptation, but pose hazards including unpredictability, sudden state transitions, and mass extinctions, requiring trade-offs between stability, diversity, and adaptive efficiency.

The proposed Ecosystem-Oriented Architecture uses two-level optimisation: a decentralised peer-to-peer network forms a tier of distributed agents, which feed local evolutionary algorithms operating at each habitat (peer). Unlike island-model distributed evolutionary computing, where multiple populations evolve for a single request, here multiple evolving populations respond to similar user requests, accelerating adaptation through solution sharing. Network topology dynamically adapts via Hebbian learning based on successful agent migration, producing a topology resembling the user base's small-world structure. Users submit semantic descriptions of desired applications, and populations evolve agent-sequences to fulfil them. Simulations with one hundred users deploying agents and submitting requests were used to test whether the system displayed behaviour typical of biological ecosystems.

President Trump said the government shutdown gives him an "unprecedented opportunity" to cut federal agencies, and he plans to meet with Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought, a Project 2025 author, to determine which "Democrat Agencies" to cut and whether the cuts would be temporary or permanent. This lecture examines effective field theory with fine tuning, using two-nucleon EFT as an example. Fine tuning here means an operator that appears irrelevant under naive dimensional power counting is actually relevant, indicating the naive power counting is wrong and expansion occurs around an interacting rather than trivial fixed point.

The theory is non-relativistic, containing only contact interactions and their derivatives, so all loops are calculable. The lecture derives the effective range expansion—that P cot δ for a partial wave is a Taylor series in P for any short-range potential—directly from EFT without specifying a potential. The kinetic term must include both the ∂t and ∇²/2M pieces (E ~ P²/2M), unlike HQET, to avoid pinch singularities; this gives the nucleon field scaling M⁰ and couplings C₂M scaling like 1/M. All loop diagrams are bubbles that decouple and sum as a geometric series, yielding P cot δ and identifying the scattering length and effective range.

Experimentally, scattering lengths are anomalously large (23 fm in ¹S₀, 5 fm in ³S₁) compared to the natural scale 1/mπ, indicating fine tuning in a alone. To handle this, C₀ must be promoted to a relevant operator and kept to all orders. Offshell momentum subtraction (P = iμ) tracks power divergences that MSbar misses; the resulting running coupling C₀(μ) scales as 1/(Mμ), becoming relevant. The one-loop-exact beta function reveals three fixed points: a = 0 (non-interacting) and a = ±∞ (interacting, scale-invariant, actually conformal, with an emergent SU(4) spin-isospin symmetry). Nature lies near a = ±∞. The pole at a = 1/μ corresponds to a bound state, the deuteron, invisible in perturbation theory.

The PDS (power divergence subtraction) scheme, subtracting poles at D = 3 as well as D = 4, reproduces the same physics within dimensional regularization. The renormalization group propagates the enhancement to all other operators: C₂ scales as 1/(μ²λ), and higher coefficients follow similarly. The resulting amplitude keeps all powers of aP and is μ-independent order by order. The framework has practical applications, such as precision predictions for deuteron formation in the sun.

The D.C. Circuit granted Shieldalloy Metallurgical Corporation's petition and vacated the NRC's transfer of regulatory authority over nuclear materials to New Jersey. Shieldalloy, which manufactured metal alloys at its Newfield, New Jersey facility from 1955 to 1998, had spent roughly a decade seeking NRC approval of a decommissioning plan involving on-site disposal of radioactive waste. After New Jersey applied for regulatory authority under 42 U.S.C. § 2021 and the NRC found its program compatible and adequate, the transfer took effect on September 30, 2009. Shieldalloy challenged the transfer, arguing New Jersey's program was incompatible with the federal scheme. The court held that the NRC's responses regarding criterion 25—which requires arrangements preventing interference with pending license applications—were insufficient, and that the NRC failed to explain why a partial transfer excluding the Newfield site was not viable, despite the Oklahoma precedent permitting exclusions of discrete material subcategories. Because the NRC's action lacked a rational connection between the facts found and the choice made, it was arbitrary and capricious; the court remanded for further proceedings.

This document is AMD's Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) Operations Guide, describing optional extensions to System Encryption, the Secure Encrypted Virtualization API (SEV), and the SEV Secure Nested Paging (SNP) Firmware ABI Specification to facilitate page migration—the process of copying page content and updating virtual-to-physical mappings. TMPM support is determined via the ENGINE_READY bit in the PM_Status register, and TMPM requires IOMMU enablement.

TMPM addresses two key challenges: it can pause DMA traffic to a page while content is copied and IOMMU page table entries updated, enabling safe migration of pages actively used by IO devices, and it acts as a trusted agent capable of migrating pages owned by guests using SEV or SNP, which the hypervisor/OS cannot otherwise access.

Two primary commands are described: PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, which migrates pages that may be concurrent DMA targets (requiring the relevant IOMMU host Page Table Entry location), and PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST, which migrates SNP guest pages (source pages in Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid state; destinations in a new Pre-Migration state characterized by a Platform Specific ASID value, PS_ASID_VAL). Up to 128 pages may be migrated per command via a Page Migration List with no order-dependence between entries. Per-page status is returned; PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS requires checking individual entries, and PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE permits retry.

Performance guidance includes using commands with 16 or more pages (maximum bandwidth at 128 pages), keeping the command ring buffer ahead of the engine, and avoiding interrupts on every command. Certain structures (IOMMU memory data structures, vIOMMU pinned buffers, the ring buffer and argument pages) cannot be migrated, and system physical addresses must be 4K-aligned.

The TMPM firmware can be reloaded only when no operations are in flight and the ring buffer is torn down; reload firmware must be the same or greater version. For EPYC Family 19h, FW_VER_Major is 71. Commands are submitted through a ring buffer managed by a driver, with defined initialization, shutdown, pause/resume procedures and six interrupt sources sharing one x86 interrupt signal. Errors are reported via command status, sub-status, the PM_STATUS register, and/or Machine Check Architecture; hardware errors during a batch may render all pages in that command unrecoverable.
