This paper experimentally explores whether large language models (LLMs) can autoformalize physics problems for cyber-physical systems (CPSs) into differential game logic (dGL), addressing the bottleneck that manually writing formal models for CPSs is difficult, time-consuming, and error-prone. The authors propose 20 benchmarks derived from hard undergraduate kinematics problems and provide an automated checker that verifies semantic correctness via symbolic execution against an expected symbolic solution and ensures models are not in stasis by requiring a minimum number of variable writes. The pipeline uses two LLM query types—Propose Formalization and Revise Formalization—with KeYmaera X parser feedback allowing up to three syntax repair attempts, implemented with Delphyne, KeYmaera X, Z3, and Mathematica. Evaluating GPT 4o, GPT 4.1, and OpenAI o3 under zero-shot and multi-shot prompting, GPT 4o fails every benchmark without few-shot examples, while few-shot prompting improves all models: o3 achieves a 70% top-5 success rate, versus 45% for GPT 4.1 and 20% for GPT 4o. Six unsolved problems fail due to checker limitations, grouped into optimization problems, non-polynomial continuous dynamics, and complicated dynamics. The authors conclude that LLM-based CPS autoformalization is promising, and suggest future work on autoformalization from multimodal sensor data for runtime use by autonomous systems.

Writing from Creeting St Peter, Suffolk, after snowfall, the author criticizes Government ministers for publicly discussing reneging on Theresa May's EU deal, citing Simon Coveney's reminder of the Article 46 commitments on Ireland/NI and noting likely repercussions. The day's content includes a preview of House of Lords business focusing on Liberal Democrat contributions, Paul Walter's articles on a new award scheme for young activists and the Samaritans' work, a "goodbye"-themed musical interlude, and an invitation for reader submissions.

This study addresses gaps in psychiatric diagnosis of depression and anxiety by applying LLMs to speech data. The researchers collected over 15,000 minutes of speech recordings from 1,160 outpatients with 25 different diagnoses at the Shanghai Mental Health Center between August 2023 and January 2024. They designed a corpus of clinical indicators based on Electronic Medical Records and assessment scales, used a pre-trained LLM to identify clinical symptoms and rate assessment scale components, and fine-tuned the LLM with annotations from professional psychiatrists. Linguistic and acoustic features were also extracted. An ensemble machine-learning pipeline fusing these modalities predicted diagnostic groups and symptoms with moderately high accuracy, and analysis of patterns between diagnostic groups enhanced interpretability. The results indicate that LLM-extracted objective cues, combined with behavioral markers, can serve as valuable features for differentiating diagnostic groups and identifying symptom disclosure, potentially improving psychiatric diagnosis and assessment.

Theo Walcott scored the lone goal in the 51st minute to give Everton a 1-0 Premier League win over Newcastle at Goodison Park. It was his third goal since joining Everton in January. Both teams play again Saturday.

Cover 0 is an all-out blitz defense in which every player not responsible for covering an offensive skill player rushes the quarterback. It generates quick pressure and forces split-second QB decisions, but leaves every defender in man coverage on an island, making it a high-risk/high-reward call. Offenses best attack it with immediate, quick-hitting man beaters, since there is no time for double-moves or elaborate play-action. Advantages in perimeter personnel, routes into the vacated middle of the field such as slants and shallow crosses, and pick plays that create natural collisions between defenders are effective answers. The passage presents five example plays: Ole Miss's double slants, Oregon's full-slide fade-out/RB seam gadget, Michigan's trips bunch jerk route, Wake Forest's slant-rub, and Dixie State's Jerry Rice motion slant-flat.

FlowMotion ONE, a smartphone stabilizer with a 3inONE design (wearable, handheld with joystick, or attachable to an extension pole), was funded on Kickstarter in one hour, raising over $600,000 from more than 2,700 backers against a $30,000 goal. Founded in 2015 by Lars Flesland, Julie Bauge, Eirik Dyrseth and Didrik Dimmen, the company—with offices in Palo Alto and Trondheim, Norway—uses sensors and high-precision motors to eliminate camera shake. Its 10-person team has won awards in Norway, Finland, Germany and the United States.

This study assessed awareness of cervical cancer and cervical screening among women aged 15–49 in Benin and Cameroon using Demographic and Health Survey data from 2017–2018. A total of 21,322 women were surveyed (7,706 in Benin; 13,616 in Cameroon), with a subsample of 7,010 asked about screening awareness. Only 9.5% of women in Benin and 46.1% in Cameroon were aware of cervical cancer; among those aware, 51.4% (Benin) and 59.7% (Cameroon) were aware of cervical screening. In adjusted analyses, older age, higher education, and frequent internet use were significantly associated with cervical cancer awareness in both countries, as was higher wealth in Cameroon. Awareness of screening was associated with older age, higher education, and radio and internet use. Awareness was generally higher among urban residents, more educated women, the wealthiest quintile, and professionals. The paper notes that neither country had a national HPV vaccination or cervical screening program as of 2021, and screening uptake in sub-Saharan Africa is low compared with high-income countries. Limitations include the cross-sectional design, a small subsample, possible sampling and recall bias, and unmeasured confounding. The authors conclude that awareness is very low and recommend stakeholder engagement, public enlightenment, media-based communication, targeting younger women, and addressing wealth-related inequalities, particularly in Cameroon.

Former Aberdeen manager Steve Paterson suggested Pittodrie stadium could host the funeral of Neale Cooper, the 54-year-old member of the 1983 European Cup Winners' Cup-winning side, who died in hospital after falling down stairs at flats in Aberdeen. Cooper had recently reunited with teammates to mark the 35th anniversary of the win over Real Madrid. Tributes came from fans and figures including Alex McLeish and Willie Miller.

This passage discusses SARS-CoV-2 wastewater surveillance. SARS-CoV-2, the virus causing COVID-19, is shed in feces at high concentrations, enabling its RNA detection in sewage. Traditional virus concentration methods require large sample volumes (50–250 mL) and centrifuges, limiting applicability in resource-limited laboratories. Nanotrap particles are porous hydrogel particles that capture and concentrate analytes including viruses, protect them from degradation, and can capture multiple pathogens simultaneously; they have been used to detect SARS-CoV-2 and other respiratory viruses in wastewater. Three sampling methods are described: grab, composite, and passive sampling. This study used Moore swab passive sampling and grab sampling from institutional buildings in Atlanta. The study evaluated parameters affecting SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection, including pH, temperature, incubation time, sample volume, RNA extraction method, and concentration method. It compared automated versus manual Nanotrap methods and Nanotrap versus traditional membrane filtration and skim milk methods to ensure sensitivity is not compromised.

This December 12, 2000 email from Ann Schmidt to multiple Enron employees compiles news articles mentioning Enron. Key items include: a Los Angeles Times report on utility stocks' strong year, noting Enron among the Evergreen Utility Fund's biggest holdings; a Reuters article stating four Indian lenders agreed to cut loan rates by 450 basis points to 16.5 percent for Enron's Dabhol Power Company project; a Dallas Morning News piece on three companies (Terra Industries, Mississippi Chemical, Seneca Resources) selling natural gas rather than using it for production amid record-high prices, with Enron spokesman Mark Palmer noting increased demand for energy cost management; a Business Wire release on digital media company Activate, which coordinated with Enron among other content distribution networks; two Times of India articles—one criticizing the political handling of the Dabhol project and another citing retired judge Hosbet Suresh's opinion that the Dabhol power purchase agreement can be nullified on public interest grounds; a Dow Jones report on Green Mountain Energy's application to become a Texas retail electric provider, noting Enron Energy Services and Enron Power Marketing also filed; a PR Newswire announcement that The New Power Company, formed by Enron, was certified as a retail natural gas marketer in Georgia; and Reuters and Bloomberg articles on online energy trading, reporting EnronOnline's average daily volume of $10.5 billion and Dynegydirect's $1.5 billion in first-month transactions.

A veterinarian at Edmond, Oklahoma's Gentle Care Animal Hospital removed 21 pacifiers from a dog named Dovey after her owners noticed pacifiers disappearing and the dog vomiting. An x-ray suggested 7 to 9 pacifiers, but surgery found 21. Dovey is doing well and returning home.

This study examined kratom-associated adverse events in Wisconsin using Wisconsin Poison Center (WPC) data from January 1, 2010 to September 1, 2022. Kratom, an herbal substance derived from Mitragyna speciosa leaves, is illegal to possess in Wisconsin, though use still occurs. WPC received 59 kratom exposure calls during the study period, increasing from 1 call in 2011 to a peak of 15 in 2020. Most exposed persons were male (62.7%) with a mean age of 35.3 years. Exposures were concentrated in southeastern Wisconsin, with Marinette County reporting the most calls. Approximately half of callers reported kratom as the only exposure substance; among polysubstance exposures, alcohol and benzodiazepines were the most common co-substances. The most frequently reported symptoms were agitation, tachycardia, confusion, and central nervous system depression. Among calls with known medical outcomes, 38% were moderate or major, and 7 persons required critical care admission. One death occurred, with postmortem toxicology identifying kratom as contributory. The authors recommend that clinicians and public health practitioners caution against concomitant kratom and other substance use, promote safe storage practices to prevent unintentional pediatric ingestion, and expand kratom-specific data collection.

This randomized, open-label trial studied 1112 apixaban-treated nonvalvular atrial fibrillation subjects for 48 weeks. Subjects were randomized 1:1 to SOC information or Additional Education Program; after the 24-week primary endpoint, the education group was re-randomized to continue or revert to SOC. Adherence was measured via electronic monitoring device; an interim analysis occurred at 24 weeks.

Ben Baby's mailbag column addresses reader questions about college sports. With No. 1 Alabama facing unranked Texas A&M, Baby says a loss to the Crimson Tide wouldn't make the Florida game a must-win for coach Kevin Sumlin, though Sumlin, placed on the hot seat by athletic director Scott Woodward, needs to play well in the final six games to reach 8-4. A&M hasn't announced throwback uniforms but will honor former coach Gene Stallings and the 1967 team that beat Alabama in the Cotton Bowl; Stallings later led Alabama to the 1992 national championship. Baby also jokes about fall weddings, recalls an unplayed DJ song request, suggests inviting former North Texas player Steve Austin to boost attendance for the UTSA game, discusses the "Go Mean Green" nickname, supports Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, and names Chipotle as his favorite burrito place.

The S&P 500 rose 2.2% in July (+7.8% YTD), its third month above the 10-month moving average, though it slipped 1.6% on the first day of August. Volatility and credit spreads show a seasonal upturn, investors are increasingly skewing portfolios toward tech stocks, and US electricity demand hit a new all-time high. While medium- and longer-term trend indicators remain healthy, short-term technicals appear tenuous, with 50-day breadth rolling over from overbought levels amid bearish divergence. July was a risk-on month with stocks up and bonds down; Frontier Markets led monthly returns while US large caps placed third.

Dustin Brown attributed the team's success to its players being together a long time, which builds trust to weather tough situations. He acknowledged the team keeps finding itself in holes but said early leads provide emotional and mental breathing room. Brown added that matchups between big cities like New York and Los Angeles magnify hockey and are great for the sport. Anze Kopitar said now is not the time to reflect, as everyone is focused on the next game; Brown noted players only look back briefly after each round before resetting. Kopitar said the team showed character to battle through slow legs and sloppy play to get the win. Brown described Drew Doughty's development into a leader since the Sochi Olympics, Justin Williams as a laid-back but focused big-game player, and a close, clique-free locker room that helped newcomer Gaborik fit in quickly. He contrasted the current stable core with the extreme roster turnover when he first joined, and said the team's mentality targets a Stanley Cup, not just a division title. Kopitar welcomed compliments but said he does not get caught up in them.

Two-year-old Laylah Washington died after being shot in the head Sunday night while riding in a car with her mother and brothers in Memphis, Tennessee. The shooting followed a parking lot confrontation; no arrests have been made.

Cayman Islands prison authorities will transfer some low-risk inmates from the overcrowded HMP Northward, which holds over 220 men despite a maximum capacity of 212, to the Immigration Detention Centre at Fairbanks. Prison Director Steven Barrett said risk-assessed individuals would be housed in a section cordoned off from migrants, freeing around 22 places. Officials said the transfer would not compromise safety or statutory obligations, and operations at the centre would continue as normal. Meanwhile, nine asylum-seeking detainees at the centre have begun a hunger strike.

An alleged Swiss spy arrested in Germany is suspected of acting for the Swiss Federal Intelligence Service. The OAG watchdog rejected claims of its involvement or of leaking his identity. The case, involving a 54-year-old suspect under investigation since 2015 for dealing in stolen banking data, caused outrage in Germany, which recovered nearly €7 billion in tax revenue from such data. Whether he had a mandate remains unclear; the government stayed silent.

This patent application, a continuation of prior U.S., PCT, and Chinese applications, relates to wireless communication processing methods and apparatuses for managing information in a duplication mode, in which PDCP data on a radio bearer is transmitted on a first RLC entity and duplicately transmitted on a second RLC entity to improve data transmission stability. A first aspect provides a method in which a terminal device determines, triggers, and sends a data volume report for one of a first path and a second path in a duplication mode, avoiding signaling overheads from reporting all paths; the path may be indicated by the radio access network or selected by the terminal device based on priority or data volume. A second aspect provides a method in which the terminal device receives a first indication message indicating whether to activate or deactivate the duplication mode, with multiple message structure implementations described. Further aspects cover communications apparatuses (terminal devices or chips), a computer storage medium, and apparatuses with processors and memory. The detailed description covers the protocol stack architecture, radio bearers with at least two paths, carrier aggregation and dual connectivity scenarios, CU-DU networking, data volume reporting, activation/deactivation procedures, and handling of duplicated data upon deactivation.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2020 (Q1 fiscal 2021) reports total revenue of $37.2 billion, up 12% from $33.1 billion in the prior year quarter. Net income was $13.9 billion (up 30%), with diluted EPS of $1.82 versus $1.38. Operating income increased 25% to $15.9 billion.

Segment revenue: Productivity and Business Processes $12.3 billion (up 11%), Intelligent Cloud $12.9 billion (up 20%), and More Personal Computing $11.8 billion (up 6%). Commercial cloud revenue increased 31% to $15.2 billion. Azure grew 48%, Office 365 Commercial grew 21%, Xbox content and services revenue increased 30%, and Surface revenue increased 37%, while Search advertising revenue declined 10%.

In July 2020, Microsoft increased the estimated useful lives of server equipment from three to four years and network equipment from two to four years, increasing quarterly operating income by $927 million and net income by $763 million ($0.10 per share); the change is estimated to increase fiscal 2021 annual operating income by $2.7 billion.

On September 19, 2020, Microsoft agreed to acquire ZeniMax Media Inc., parent of Bethesda Softworks, for $7.5 billion in cash, expected to close in the second half of fiscal 2021.

The effective tax rate was 14% versus 16% in the prior year. As of September 30, 2020, total assets were $301.0 billion, total debt was $63.6 billion, and stockholders' equity was $123.4 billion. Unearned revenue totaled $36.3 billion, and remaining performance obligations were $111 billion. The company repurchased 25 million shares for $5.3 billion and declared a $0.56 per share dividend.

Microsoft remains under IRS audit for tax years 2004 to 2017, primarily concerning transfer pricing. Legal matters include 70 pending patent infringement cases (none material individually or in aggregate), settled Canadian antitrust class actions, a Chinese antitrust investigation, and cell phone health litigation. Accrued legal liabilities were $311 million, with reasonably possible adverse outcomes up to approximately $500 million beyond recorded amounts.

COVID-19 continued to impact operations, benefiting cloud usage, Surface, and Gaming, while negatively affecting Search advertising and transactional licensing.

Britain's FTSE 100 fell 0.2 percent on Friday, weighed down by disappointing results from BT and AstraZeneca, heading for its worst week since August 2017. BT shares dropped more than 5 percent to a five-year low, while AstraZeneca fell 1.7 percent on a weak profit outlook. Commodity stocks provided support, with miners rising on firmer copper prices and oil majors advancing. Capita rebounded over 5 percent after a Morgan Stanley upgrade.

Environment Canada issued a special weather statement for Edmonton and areas south and east to the Saskatchewan border as conditions favoured funnel clouds Wednesday afternoon. These form from weak rotation under growing clouds or weak thunderstorms and could intensify into weak landspout tornadoes, which can reach winds near 100 km/h. A viewer photographed a funnel cloud near Namao, where students were kept indoors. Environment Canada advises taking shelter if funnel clouds develop nearby.

The United States District Court for the Middle District of North Carolina granted the defendants' motion for summary judgment and denied the plaintiff's motions to strike in a suit by Melissa Jennings, a former member of the UNC Chapel Hill women's soccer team (1996–1998), against the University, head coach Anson Dorrance, assistant coach William Palladino, and university administrators. Jennings alleged that Dorrance made sexual comments about players during pre-practice warm-ups and twice made direct inquiries into her personal life, including asking "Who are you fucking?" during a meeting about her grades. Her remaining claims were a Title IX claim against the University; § 1983 claims against Dorrance for invasion of privacy, against Dorrance and Palladino for sexual harassment, and against administrators for failure to supervise; and a common law invasion of privacy claim against Dorrance. The court denied Jennings' motion to strike the amended answer and for default judgment, finding no bad faith, and denied her motion to strike exhibits C through H of Dorrance's affidavit, finding them properly authenticated and admissible as records of regularly conducted activity. On the merits, the court held the alleged conduct was not severe, pervasive, or objectively offensive enough to constitute hostile environment harassment under Title IX or § 1983; that Dorrance's inquiries did not violate Jennings' constitutional privacy rights; and that the conduct was not sufficiently egregious for North Carolina's intrusion tort. The court also denied the defendants' motion to submit evidence under seal.

This patent application, a continuation of earlier filings, describes a data intake and query system for collecting, indexing, and searching machine-generated data from IT environments. Machine data from sources such as servers, sensors, routers, and mobile devices is parsed into timestamped events and stored in a data store. The system uses a late-binding schema, applying extraction rules (e.g., regular expressions) to events at search time to extract field values, allowing fields to be defined and refined after ingestion. The architecture includes forwarders that receive data from input sources, annotate data blocks with metadata (host, source, source type), and forward them to indexers; indexers parse data into events, determine timestamps, optionally build keyword indexes, and store events in time-based buckets (hot, warm, cold, quarantine, frozen). The system may operate on-premises or as a cloud-based service. Search heads process queries and can access externally stored data collections (virtual indices) through External Result Provider (ERP) processes, which operate in streaming, reporting, or mixed modes, balancing latency and bandwidth. Inverted indexes containing token entries and field-value pair entries with event references support keyword and field-based searching, filtering, and categorization of events based on criteria such as partition, host, source, and sourcetype.

Treasury minister Mel Stride said Britain's fish fingers will be "safe in the hands" of the Government during Brexit talks, responding to Labour's Mel Onn, who sought assurances that continued customs arrangements would protect Grimsby's time-sensitive fish trade, processing sector and 5,000 jobs.

This study examines the integration of information technology (IT) and management strategies in language education in Indonesia, using qualitative descriptive analysis, comparative analysis of previous research, and framework development based on literature review and observation. Of 1,010 published manuscripts identified, 15.1% (151 papers) from the Scopus database were strongly relevant; the bibliometric analysis used the keywords "IT," "management strategies," and "language education," with credibility ensured through multiple researchers.

The findings indicate that Education 4.0 and the pandemic accelerated digitalization, prompting alternatives such as online learning platforms, mobile learning, asynchronous and blended learning, and TV/radio broadcasts, with online platforms and mobile learning standing out for accessibility and effectiveness. Challenges for teachers included insufficient technological proficiency, difficulty maintaining student engagement, limited resources, and remote assessment, particularly for speaking and listening skills. University students faced a digital divide, difficulties with self-regulation and motivation, loss of social interaction, and lack of real-time language practice. Global responses included professional development programs, gamified learning, AI-assisted assessment, peer-led study groups, virtual co-curricular activities, and immersive virtual reality tools. Equity issues, cultural differences, available technology, and community support shaped the success of digital transitions across countries.

Technological innovations reviewed include augmented reality, virtual reality, IoT, AI, learning management systems, gamification, 3D printing, blockchain, cloud computing, robotics, and big data. Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) improves pronunciation and vocabulary through real-time feedback, while task-based and game-based learning foster engagement and retention; combining ASR with games offers a holistic approach.

Effective management strategies include digital platforms supporting synchronous and asynchronous learning, teacher professional development, language support tools, global collaborations and virtual exchanges, cloud infrastructure, mobile learning, data-driven decision-making, and inclusive IT policies. Students generally hold positive attitudes toward IT in language education, similar to STEM, though resistance and unequal access to resources persist. The study concludes that IT can enhance language education if implemented with attention to teaching methods, management strategies, and student needs.

A federal judge in Illinois dismissed a lawsuit alleging the College Board and 40 selective private colleges conspired to inflate tuition by requiring financial information from both parents of students with divorced or separated parents. Judge Sara Ellis found the plaintiffs, a Boston University student and Cornell alum, failed to plausibly allege an agreement among the institutions.

At a human trafficking training session in Oshakati, Prosecutor-General Martha Imalwa said human trafficking is the third largest international crime, generating $32 billion (N$401 billion) annually, with 20-30 million people enslaved worldwide and 600,000 to 800,000 trafficked across borders yearly. Namibia has recorded incidents, including Angolan children found alone in the country. Her office sought UNODC assistance to train locals. Police Inspector-General Sebastian Ndeitunga reported 25 cases from 2010 to 2017, with six pending trial, one conviction, one acquittal, and 14 under investigation.

This Agreement constitutes the entire understanding regarding Software use. Void provisions do not affect the remainder's validity. Governed by California and U.S. federal law, it falls under Santa Clara County, California courts' exclusive jurisdiction. Exports must comply with U.S. regulations; amendments require written signatures.

SA58 Nasal Spray, a broad-spectrum anti-COVID-19 monoclonal antibody developed by Sinovac Life Sciences, was evaluated as post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) in a randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial conducted at 21 construction sites in Beijing, China, from November 26 to December 9, 2022, during an Omicron BF.7 outbreak. Of 1,634 randomized participants, 1,222 entered the full analysis set (901 SA58, 321 placebo). Among participants exposed to SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals within 72 hours, SA58 reduced laboratory-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 by 80.82% (95%CI 52.41%–92.27%) and SARS-CoV-2 infection by 61.83% (95%CI 37.50%–76.69%). No severe COVID-19 or deaths occurred. Adverse events were mild (Grade 1), most commonly nasal mucosal dryness, runny nose, fever, and nasal congestion, with no significant differences between groups and no serious adverse events reported. Limitations included a young, healthy study population, short follow-up duration, and a sample size below the target due to early study termination. The authors conclude that SA58 showed satisfactory efficacy and safety as PEP and recommend further evaluation in high-risk populations such as the elderly, healthcare personnel, and those with underlying illnesses.

The passage is a patent application describing a medical system for assisting rescuers during intubation procedures, particularly rapid sequence intubation (RSI). The system includes airflow sensors (oxygen, flow, and capnography sensors) and physiological sensors (pulse oximeters, ECG, acoustic, impedance, and blood pressure sensors) coupled to a patient monitoring device with a processor and memory. The processor detects airflow in the patient's airway, initiates a timer (typically 5–15 seconds or user-defined), and determines whether an endotracheal (ET) tube is properly placed based on physiological information—such as ETCO2 values, transthoracic impedance, or acoustic data—meeting predetermined criteria. The system establishes physiological baselines (initial averages or dynamic moving averages) after tube placement and detects deviations to verify the tube remains properly placed. The system automatically identifies which step of the RSI procedure is being performed based on changes in gas, physiological, and positioning parameters, and adjusts displayed feedback accordingly, providing context-sensitive guidance without requiring manual display adjustments. The patient monitoring device may be a defibrillator or patient monitor with a touchscreen display, and may communicate with portable computing devices (tablets, smartphones, laptops) and wrist-worn devices. Additional capabilities include automatic initiation of preoxygenation and procedure timers, drug dosage calculation, hypoxemia alarms, event marker storage, and generation of quality assurance reports. The document also describes system components such as electrode assemblies, bag-valve-mask integrated sensor modules, and connections to central facilities for additional patient information.

California Governor Gavin Newsom signed SB 53, a landmark AI safety law requiring major AI companies to publicly disclose how they will mitigate potentially catastrophic risks from advanced AI models. The law establishes mechanisms for reporting safety incidents to California's Office of Emergency Services, extends whistleblower protections to AI company employees, and initiates CalCompute, a government consortium to create a public computing cluster for AI research. Authored by State Sen. Scott Wiener, the bill emphasizes transparency rather than liability, unlike his previously vetoed SB 1047. Industry reactions were divided: Anthropic backed the bill, while OpenAI and Meta offered measured support. Critics, including Andreessen Horowitz's Collin McCune, argue it could burden startups and entrench Big Tech, though supporters note the obligations do not apply to companies with less than $500 million in annual revenue.

Kevin Love, preparing for his fourth straight NBA Finals with Cleveland while recovering from a concussion that could keep him out of Game 1, has revealed he dealt with anxiety and panic attacks for much of his life. Since joining the Cavaliers in a 2014 trade from Minnesota, he has faced persistent criticism and trade rumors despite playing at a high level. After being questioned by teammates at a January meeting for leaving a game and missing practice, he disclosed his panic attacks in a Player's Tribune essay and received thousands of supportive emails. He says basketball is his escape and he does not want special treatment from teammates.

Tropical Storm Nate, which formed off Nicaragua's coast and was blamed for at least 17 deaths in Central America, is expected to cross the Yucatan peninsula and move into the Gulf of Mexico, strengthening into a hurricane by Saturday night. Moving northwest at 14 mph with maximum sustained winds of 45 mph, Nate's forecast path places Pensacola within a warning cone stretching from the Florida Panhandle to central Louisiana. Escambia and Santa Rosa counties can expect heavy rain of 3 to 5 inches, possible flash floods and tornadoes, and tropical storm force winds Sunday morning, with Escambia facing winds of 35-45 mph and gusts up to 65 mph. A tropical storm watch covers much of the Northwest Florida Gulf coast. Local closures and cancellations include the University of West Florida, Gulf Islands National Seashore, and several scheduled events. Gov. Rick Scott declared a state of emergency in 29 Florida counties, activated the state emergency operations center, and has 7,000 National Guard members available for deployment. Santa Rosa County is offering free sand at several locations, and residents are urged to gather supplies and follow local media for updates.

The summer 2017 box office was defined by the dominance of three well-received comic book superhero films—Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2, Wonder Woman, and Spider-Man: Homecoming—all of which achieved top-tier business. Beyond these, nearly every other genre produced only one successful film: Despicable Me 3 (animation), Girls Trip (comedy), Annabelle: Creation (horror), Dunkirk (adult drama), Baby Driver (studio programmer), 47 Meters Down (sleeper), and The Big Sick (indie hit). Meanwhile, many films flopped or disappointed, including King Arthur, Valerian, The Mummy, Transformers: The Last Knight, and War for the Planet of the Apes. The author argues this pattern is troubling for content diversity, as superhero films crowded out other genres, though notes it may be too early to draw lasting conclusions since future slates were scheduled years in advance.

Researchers at the University of California, Irvine and other institutions have introduced a new satellite-based drought severity index using data from NASA's Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) mission. The index incorporates terrestrial water storage (groundwater) into drought assessments, supplementing tools typically based on precipitation. Described in the Journal of Hydrometeorology, the GRACE-DSI covers 2002 to 2014, with data to be extended by the ongoing mission and a follow-on launching in early 2018. Because it relies solely on satellite gravity observations, it provides globally consistent monitoring, and evaluations in the continental United States showed significant agreement with existing indices.
Black Sabbath's Tony Iommi announced the BIMM Birmingham Scholarship, which he sponsors, during a May 25th Q&A at BIMM Music Institute, stating his career has always felt worth it despite knockbacks.

This passage is a May 24, 2001 email compilation of news articles concerning Enron and energy-related developments:

- A Houston Chronicle op-ed criticizes California Attorney General Bill Lockyer for crude remarks about imprisoning Enron chairman Kenneth Lay, arguing California officials are scapegoating Texas energy producers for the state's power crisis.
- A Los Angeles Times article reports that Senator Jeffords' expected party switch, giving Democrats Senate control, could affect industries including pharmaceuticals, HMOs, defense, credit cards, tobacco, energy, and telecommunications.
- Brazil is asking consumers and industry to cut electricity use by 15–25 percent to avoid blackouts caused by a drought-driven shortage, with rationing beginning June 1.
- California PUC President Loretta Lynch says an investigation found evidence that generators manipulated electricity prices by throttling plants up and down to maximize profits.
- GOP gubernatorial hopeful Bill Simon Jr. downplays his Texas energy investments, including a former board role at Hanover Compressor Co., an Enron partner.
- Several articles cover India's Dabhol power dispute: Enron's Dabhol Power Co. and the Maharashtra State Electricity Board are in a payment conflict, and Enron issued a preliminary termination notice. Panel head Madhav Godbole briefly resigned over critical remarks by Sharad Pawar but withdrew it after the chief minister expressed confidence. The federal government appointed A.V. Gokak as its nominee to the negotiating panel and pledged to consider its proposals.
- A Reuters analysis describes a coming shake-up of Central European gas markets, involving a proposed Polish transit pipeline and gas asset sell-offs in Slovakia and the Czech Republic.
- Spain's Endesa will auction its Electra de Viesgo subsidiary, with Enron and AES among invited bidders.
- An Economic Times piece questions whether Sharad Pawar is playing power politics regarding Enron.
- Dynegy told analysts it plans large imminent acquisitions or mergers, targeting 10 percent of the US power market and 15 percent of the US gas market.

Six-year-old Ryan, star of Ryan ToysReview, ranked among Forbes' Top 10 highest-paid YouTube stars, earning $11 million in 2017. Started in 2015, the channel has over 10 million subscribers and eight billion views. The family keeps their identity secret for safety and will continue only while Ryan enjoys it.

The long-short equity strategy is an investment method in which traders take long positions in stocks expected to appreciate and short positions in stocks expected to decline, aiming to minimize risk while profiting from both rising and falling prices. It is popular among hedge funds, which often employ a long bias (such as the 130/30 strategy), and is better suited to institutional investors who can use derivatives and leverage. The strategy requires identifying undervalued and overvalued stocks and works best with a portfolio of multiple pairs rather than one or two. Edward Thorp, known as the father of quantitative investing, pioneered such strategies through his firm Princeton Newport Partners, which compounded at 19.1% annually. A backtest of a long-short pairs strategy using Coca-Cola and Pepsi based on RSI rules produced a 3.8% annual return with an 11% maximum drawdown; because average gains per trade are small, leverage is generally needed to make the strategy worthwhile.

This study presents a machine learning-assisted inverse design workflow for discovering diammonium organic spacers for Dion-Jacobson (DJ) 2D perovskites with targeted energy level alignments (types Ib, IIa, and IIb). The workflow centers on an invertible 12-digit fingerprint representation encoding conjugated organic spacers, linking molecular structure to the target property of energy level alignment.

Using a molecular morphing approach starting from phenylene-dimethylammonium (PDMA), the authors generated 21,306 fingerprints across generations G0–G6, corresponding to approximately 4.9 million hypothetical spacers; all 21 experimentally reported spacers were captured within this space. High-throughput calculations on 3,239 spacers in generations G0–G3 provided training data for machine learning models predicting HOMO/LUMO levels. LASSO regression was selected for interpretability, and SHAP analysis showed that the number of aromatic rings and primary ammonium groups most strongly influence frontier energy levels, while fluorination has a minor effect.

Synthesis feasibility was screened in two steps: availability in PubChem (9,025 spacers found) and a formability score based on five topological descriptors with a 0.88 cutoff, which correctly classified 27 of 29 reported cases; 96.1% of hypothetical spacers were predicted to form DJ phases. DFT validation confirmed 8 type IIa and 44 type IIb candidates within G0–G6, but no type Ib candidates due to synthetic accessibility constraints.

Leveraging the fingerprint's invertibility, an inverse design strategy targeting constrained chemical regions identified 2 type Ib spacers (pentacene-based with five linearly fused rings) in G7–G8, 12 type IIa candidates (acene and oligothiophene families), and 42 type IIb candidates (nitrogen-substituted ring systems). In total, 56 promising candidates were identified from a chemical space of about one million compounds, starting from only 21 known structures. The authors note limitations, including difficulties encoding complex molecular motifs and formalizing expert intuition, and call for experimental validation of the predicted materials.

The passage describes an application circuit in which the PGA848 drives an ADS8860, a 16-bit, 1MSPS, successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter. The circuit accepts single-ended or differential inputs. The PGA848 operates with independent supplies: ±15V for the input stage and a 5.3V supply for the output stage, shared with the ADC, which prevents overloading the ADC inputs during overdrive conditions. A REF6250 5V reference connects to the ADC REFIN pin, and a 10kΩ-to-10kΩ precision divider sets the PGA848 REF pin to 2.5V (ADC midscale), buffered by an OPA192 op amp in a dual-feedback configuration (RF = 2kΩ, CF = 2nF, RISO = 20Ω) providing 86° phase margin.

Three filters are described: an input filter reducing EMI/RFI, a feedback filter (CFB = 75pF with the PGA's 6.67kΩ resistors) yielding a 318kHz cutoff (277kHz at high resistor tolerance), and a charge-kickback filter at the ADC inputs. The circuit maintains –0.1dB flatness to 41kHz, and C0G capacitors are used in the signal path.

Power supply recommendations state that output-stage supplies are clamped to input-stage levels, and supplies above 40V (±20V) permanently damage the device. Layout guidelines address symmetrical input paths, bypass capacitors, trace routing, minimizing leakage and parasitic capacitance, and thermal considerations. The passage also covers TI simulation tools (PSpice for TI, TINA-TI), documentation and support resources, trademarks, ESD handling precautions, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

A New York Times survey of federal judges found widespread concern about the Supreme Court's emergency docket decisions related to President Trump's second term. Of 65 judges responding, only 12 said the Supreme Court made appropriate use of the emergency docket, and only 12 said lower-court judges receive sufficient guidance on applying emergency orders. Of 54 judges asked, only two said the docket improved public perception of the judiciary, while 42 said it caused harm. Some judges anonymously criticized the orders as "mystical" and "overly blunt," though a Trump appointee said they were "flushing out anti-democratic rulings." At least seven of about 20 emergency orders lacked reasoning, and nearly all benefited Trump. The New York Times acknowledged respondents may not represent the judiciary, and the Volokh Conspiracy critiqued the survey as potentially oversampling judges likely to disagree with the rulings.

In 2002, DEA agents destroyed six marijuana plants grown by Diane Monson, a Northern California woman who used medical cannabis legally under state law for chronic back pain. Monson and Angel Raich, who relied on medical cannabis to treat life-threatening conditions, sued, arguing Congress lacked constitutional authority under the interstate commerce clause to regulate their local, noneconomic activity. The government countered that marijuana is a fungible good that would reach the interstate black market, making regulation of local cultivation essential to its broader scheme. Despite earlier precedents limiting the commerce clause to economic activity, the Supreme Court ruled 6-3 for the government, holding that regulating intrastate medical cannabis was necessary to preserve the federal ban on interstate marijuana markets. Justice Scalia concurred, grounding Congress's power in the necessary and proper clause. Chief Justice Rehnquist and Justices O'Connor and Thomas dissented; Thomas argued the original meaning of "commerce" covered only buying, selling, and bartering, and warned the ruling allowed Congress to define the scope of its own power. The decision was seen as a major setback for limiting federal commerce power. Later, plaintiffs' attorney Randy Barnett used similar arguments in the Obamacare challenge, where Solicitor General Paul Clement argued against the government. Raich lost subsequent appeals, and Thomas has remained a consistent advocate for the originalist interpretation of the commerce clause.

This passage is from the Texas Instruments datasheet (SLASFA2A, revised April 2025) for the MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 microcontrollers, covering peripheral descriptions, application guidance, support resources, and revision history.

This patent application, a continuation of earlier filings, relates to computer graphics and 3D reconstruction for artificial reality systems. It addresses incorrect occlusion rendering in "passthrough" visualizations on head-mounted displays (HMDs), which let users see their physical surroundings via front-facing cameras. Because passthrough images are re-rendered from 3D models that may be imprecise—especially at object edges—occlusion boundaries between passthrough and virtual objects can be wrong, causing under-occlusion or over-occlusion. The disclosed embodiments generate instance segmentation masks for objects (e.g., persons, pets) in captured images using machine-learning techniques such as Mask R-CNN, and compute representative depth values for each mask based on corresponding portions of the 3D model. Padded borders around masks are assigned significantly farther depth values to create contrast and enforce hard edges. During rendering, the system uses these representative depth values, rather than measured 3D model depths, to make occlusion decisions, improving passthrough appearance. The application further describes depth estimation via stereo camera triangulation, an optimized technique using a device's video encoder for resource-limited systems, 3D mesh generation and deformation for modeling the environment, and an example method for rendering 3D passthrough, along with example network environments and computer systems.

This document is the Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 for SD Memory Cards. The SD Memory Card is designed to meet the security, capacity, performance, and environmental requirements of audio and video consumer electronic devices, incorporating a content protection mechanism compliant with SDMI security standards that uses mutual authentication and a cipher algorithm. The specification covers system concepts, functional descriptions, card registers, hardware interfaces, and SPI mode operation.

Cards are classified by capacity: Standard Capacity (SDSC, up to 2GB), High Capacity (SDHC, more than 2GB up to 32GB), and Extended Capacity (SDXC, more than 32GB up to 2TB). Bus speed modes range from Default Speed (up to 12.5 MB/sec) and High Speed (up to 25 MB/sec) to UHS-I modes (SDR12 through SDR104, up to 104 MB/sec using 1.8V signaling) and UHS-II modes (up to 624 MB/s). Five Speed Classes (0, 2, 4, 6, 10) define minimum card performance. Two card types exist by read-write property: Read/Write cards and Read Only Memory (ROM) cards. Cards have a User Area and a Protected Area.

Communication uses a 9-pin interface operating at up to 208 MHz, based on command/response transactions, with data transferred in blocks protected by CRC. Cards contain registers including OCR, CID, CSD, RCA, DSR, and SCR. Two operation modes are defined: card identification mode (reset, voltage validation, initialization via CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, and RCA assignment) and data transfer mode. UHS-I requires a voltage switch sequence to 1.8V signaling, with sampling point tuning via CMD19. UHS-II cards use a separate interface involving PHY initialization, device initialization, enumeration, and configuration.

Additional features include Application Performance Classes specifying minimum random and sequential performance, Cache, Self Maintenance, and Command Queue schemes. The specification also defines hardware interface requirements (power-up sequences, bus operating conditions, ESD), SPI mode protocol, and function extensions for power management and performance enhancement.

This study examined the prevalence of artemisinin partial resistance (ArtR) markers in *Plasmodium falciparum* in a low-transmission area of southern Zambia from 2018 to 2023, using amplicon deep-sequencing on samples from four health centers in Choma District. The Pfk13 A578S mutation was also detected in 2023 (0.6%). MDR1 Y184F was present at 41% with no change over time. This study examined factors that attract and retain special education teachers in rural districts, where shortages and high attrition (30–50% annually) have persisted for decades. A survey was administered to special education teachers from three cooperatives in rural remote Midwest US; 93 complete responses were analyzed (60% response rate). Four themes emerged for both retention and attraction: provision of support, financial incentives, job-related factors, and rural initiatives. For retention, 70% cited provision of support (administrative, collegial, and community), 53% cited financial incentives (mainly increased salary), 44% cited job-related factors (reduced paperwork/caseload, professional development, resources, work-life balance), and 2% cited rural initiatives such as Grow Your Own Programs. For attraction, 96% cited financial incentives (including salary, health insurance, loan forgiveness, housing, and sign-on bonuses), 31% cited support, 15% cited job-related factors, and 9% cited rural initiatives including career fairs hosted by rural teachers. Correlational analyses showed support was positively related to intentions to stay, and satisfaction was significantly related to remaining in the profession; teachers planning to leave most often cited job-related factors, lack of support, and limited rural incentives. The authors conclude that a combination of strategies—including administrative support delivered with emotional intelligence, financial incentives, and reduced job burdens—is needed, and recommend future research on job satisfaction, ongoing support, and incentive structures. Limitations include self-reported data, a limited geographic sample, and primarily descriptive analysis.

Thomas H. Fisher appealed a summary judgment granted to Homer P. Hargrave, a partner of Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Beane, in Fisher's suit seeking an accounting for $6,500 paid to Fuller, Rodney & Co. in commodity transactions during December 1940 and January 1941. Fisher argued that Merrill Lynch or its predecessors, which took over some Fuller, Rodney accounts after that firm's dissolution on April 30, 1941, had merged with or succeeded to Fuller, Rodney & Co. and thereby assumed its liabilities. Affidavits from Hargrave and Byron G. Webster, a former Fuller, Rodney partner, together with the April 18, 1941 agreement between the firms, established that no merger or consolidation occurred, no liabilities were assumed, and Fisher's account was not transferred. Fisher's opposing affidavit admitted the material facts were unknown to him except by information and belief, and the court properly disregarded it as incompetent under Supreme Court rule 15. Fisher's claim that the trial court denied him discovery was unsupported by the record, as no such motion was ever presented or ruled upon. The court held that an action for an accounting is equitable and falls within section 57 of the Civil Practice Act, which permits summary judgment. The decree granting summary judgment to Hargrave was affirmed.

In soccer, after gaining goal-side position, a defender must establish a proper one-on-one stance against a ball carrier. The stance features one foot forward (lead foot) and one back (trail foot), usually with the dominant leg behind. Adults typically stand with feet about 18 inches apart at a 30-degree angle, 12 inches wide, toes slightly outward, body balanced on the balls of the feet with bent knees and arms out. This enables quick reactions, slowing or directing the opponent, avoiding being beaten, and preparing to tackle. The lead foot depends on field position: left foot leads on the right side, right foot leads on the left, forcing attackers toward the sideline; in the center, either foot works. Practice involves drills at increasing speeds, and coaches should note that defenders may not block or impede opponents with their arms.

The Iso play is a downhill running scheme in which a Fullback serves as a lead blocker, isolating one-on-one against a linebacker, while the offensive line uses base blocks and double teams at the point of attack. Its strengths are getting the ball downhill quickly and its simplicity, making it easy to teach and execute. Its main weakness is dependence on personnel, requiring large offensive linemen capable of winning one-on-one blocks and a rugged Fullback. The passage details assignments against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts. Variations include Shotgun Iso, used by Art Briles' Baylor teams in the early 2010s, and Weakside Iso.

This passage is from the SD Memory Card Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00. It defines terminology ("shall"/"will" as mandatory, "should" as recommended, "may" as optional) and describes the Mc-EX interface extension. Cards are classified by capacity—SDSC (up to 2GB), SDHC (over 2GB to 32GB), SDXC (over 32GB to 2TB)—and by voltage: High Voltage (2.7-3.6V) and UHS-II (VDD1: 2.7-3.6V, VDD2: 1.70-1.95V). Bus speed modes range from Default Speed (up to 12.5 MB/sec) to UHS624 (up to 6.24 Gbps per lane). Form factors include Standard Size, miniSD, and microSD. Cards are either Read/Write (RW) or Read Only Memory (ROM) types; ROM cards treat write and erase commands as illegal. Five speed classes (0, 2, 4, 6, 10) define minimum card performance. Communication uses command/response transactions, with 48-bit commands protected by CRC; cards contain registers including CID, RCA, DSR, CSD, SCR, OCR, SSR, and CSR. UHS-I provides up to 104MB/sec using 1.8V signaling, entered via a voltage switch sequence (CMD11), and supports only 4-bit bus mode except for CMD42. UHS-II supports modes up to FD624 (624MB/s) through a multi-step initialization process. Card identification uses CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, and CMD3; data transfer uses CMD7 for card selection, with block sizes up to 512 bytes and CRC-protected data. Erase operations include ERASE, DISCARD, and FULE. Write protection is provided through a mechanical switch, internal card protection, and password-based lock/unlock (CMD42) using PWD registers, with Card Ownership Protection (COP) adding FEP registers and a COP Unlock function.

This study reviews eight leadership models in education—administrative/managerial, instructional, transformational, distributed, transactional, ethical, contingent, and participative—analyzing their strengths and weaknesses. Administrative leadership provides clear structure and hierarchy but can be rigid, limiting innovation and creativity. Instructional leadership focuses on teaching and learning but may rely on top-down hierarchy and overlook aspects such as student well-being. Transformational leadership promotes vision, inspiration, and empowerment, though it risks creating authoritarian relationships. Distributed leadership shares leadership across the school community, increasing engagement and trust, but implementation can face communication problems, conflicts, and skill gaps. Transactional leadership relies on rewards and exchanges, improving performance but potentially hindering innovation and long-term development. Ethical leadership emphasizes moral values and builds trust, though conflicts may arise if leaders' ethics differ from the organization's. Contingent leadership requires adapting style to circumstances, and participative leadership involves staff in decision-making, raising satisfaction and creativity but potentially slowing decisions and risking information leaks. The study concludes that no single model can meet the changing needs of schools and advocates a synthetic approach combining the strengths of multiple models to create flexible, adaptive leadership suited to contemporary educational challenges.

Methods and apparatus are described for improving user experience when listeners localize electronically-generated binaural (3D) sound. Two key problems are addressed: (1) listeners have difficulty localizing binaural sound at near-field distances (less than one meter), since head-related transfer functions (HRTFs) vary significantly in the near-field and near-field convolution is computationally complex; and (2) the perceived location of sound may not match a visible image of the sound source. Example embodiments solve these problems by convolving sound to a location behind the sound source—typically using far-field HRTFs even when the source is near-field—so the listener perceives the sound as originating from the source. Techniques include positioning the sound's origination point on a line-of-sight with the source, placing it behind the source, and adjusting volume to match the distance to the source. Additional embodiments enable listeners to switch between binaural sound and mono or stereo sound by detecting actions of a portable electronic device, such as rotation, movement, sensor blockage, face detection or absence, light changes, audio output changes, or battery state changes. Example applications include telephone and video calls, displays without speakers, multiple simultaneous sound sources, and devices such as smartphones, headphones, head-mounted displays, and wearable electronics.

The lecture finishes the discussion of orthonormal expansions, showing that in countably infinite-dimensional (L2) spaces, successive projections onto an orthonormal set converge to the original vector with the residual orthogonal to every basis function; truncated sinusoids and sinc-weighted sinusoids are shown to span L2. The prolate spheroidal expansion is mentioned as an orthonormal set that maximizes energy concentrated jointly in a time interval and frequency band, with 2WT functions capturing nearly all in-band energy. Normalized Fourier series functions (scaled by 1/√T) form an orthonormal basis, though relying only on the vector viewpoint can hide limiting issues. The lecture then turns to data transmission, layering the encoder into a discrete encoder (binary digits to symbols) and modulation (symbols to waveforms); alphabet size grows exponentially with bit rate, foreshadowing the logarithm in Shannon's capacity formula. Layering justifies studying modulation separately from coding, and modulation is further split into signal constellation mapping (symbols to numerical signals) and waveform formation, with the interesting problem being the conversion of signals to waveforms rather than baseband-to-passband shifting. A simple example maps bits to ±1 signals and forms waveforms as sums of sinc pulses; causality, delay, and attenuation are set aside, handled by timing recovery and link budgets (with decibels summarizing power losses, e.g., a factor of 2 equals 3 dB). Pulse-amplitude modulation uses equispaced real signals symmetric about zero, with energy d²(m²−1)/12 for m = 2^b levels, so energy grows as m². For transmit filter p(t) and receive filter q(t), only the composite g = p*q matters in the absence of noise; Nyquist's criterion states that g is "ideal Nyquist" (g(kT) = δ_k) if and only if a filter-then-sample linear receiver avoids intersymbol interference, and no arbitrary linear receiver can do better, while nonlinear receivers fail once noise is present. Via the aliasing theorem, this becomes a frequency-domain condition—sums of shifted spectral copies must equal a rectangle—equivalent to band-edge symmetry, satisfied in practice by raised-cosine filters (about 15% rolloff) whose impulse responses decay as 1/t³. The lecture also includes asides on follow-on course scheduling and on Irwin Jacobs (Qualcomm) as an example of someone who mastered coding, modulation, and channels.

Rutile RuO2 has generated interest as an altermagnetic candidate following reports of a sublattice magnetic moment, an above-ambient Néel temperature, and large band splitting, though recent calculations and bulk measurements report no sublattice moment. Exchange bias (EB) in RuO2/ferromagnet heterostructures has been cited as evidence of antiferromagnetism. This work investigates the origin of EB in incoherent RuO2/Fe/Ru heterostructures using SQUID magnetometry, polarized neutron reflectometry (PNR) and diffraction (PND), atom probe tomography (APT), HRTEM, and EELS. PND found no signatures of antiferromagnetic ordering in sputtered RuO2 films, placing an upper limit of 0.01 µB per Ru atom on any sublattice moment. PNR revealed uncompensated, canted moments at the RuO2/Fe interface whose canting angles vary with the heterostructure's field history. APT, HRTEM/FFT, and EELS showed the interface contains iron oxide, including magnetite (Fe3O4), and an Fe gradient extending into the RuO2. EB was absent in RuO2/Ni heterostructures but present in a TiO2/Fe/Ru bilayer lacking RuO2. The authors conclude that EB in RuO2/Fe-based heterostructures arises from a magnetically active interlayer stabilized by Fe's high oxidation potential relative to Ru, not from intrinsic antiferromagnetic or altermagnetic ordering, and thus EB alone should not be considered evidence of altermagnetism in RuO2.

This paper develops a probabilistic computational model of implicature comprehension based on relevance theory, implemented in the probabilistic logic programming language ProbLog. Motivated by the "probabilistic turn" in pragmatics and Rational Speech Act theory, the authors apply a Bayesian approach to relevance-theoretic pragmatics, focusing on how implicit meaning is communicated through implicatures. Using an example in which Mary declines coffee by stating she avoids energizing drinks, the paper reviews relevance-theoretic notions—explicatures, strong and weak implicatures, manifestness, and the presumption of optimal relevance—and interprets the relevance-theoretic comprehension heuristic as a "fast and frugal" Take-the-Best heuristic.

The model encodes encyclopaedic knowledge as probabilistic graphs, links words to concepts via probabilistic inference rules, and represents the parallel adjustment of explicatures and implicatures as a Bayesian network. Utterance utility is measured as the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the audience's prior and posterior probability distributions over communicated assumptions. Five interpretive hypotheses are compared: those failing relevance expectations are eliminated; when KL measures are equal, the hypothesis with the smaller Herbrand base is preferred; otherwise the hypothesis with the highest KL measure is accepted.

The resulting as-if-optimization model can generate quantitative predictions for testing the heuristic nature of relevance-guided comprehension. The model focuses on the comprehension phase, requires manually constructed interpretive hypotheses, and leaves speaker-side modeling, higher-level explicatures, and metarepresentational uses such as irony to future research.

Cybersecurity researchers at the Georgia Institute of Technology developed a simulated ransomware attack that could take control of a simulated water treatment plant—shutting valves, increasing chlorine, and displaying false readings—to highlight vulnerabilities in industrial control systems. No real ransomware attacks on such control systems have been reported, though ransomware has targeted hospital and business data, generating an estimated $200 million in early 2016. Researchers warn attackers may shift to these systems and recommend stronger passwords, limited connections, and intrusion monitoring.

A hockey coach addresses reporters after his team won a playoff game by a large score, though the team remains down two games to none in the series. He discusses a teammate hospitalized following a late blindside hit, deferring any discipline to the league and expressing concern for the player's welfare. He expresses disappointment that some players engaged in behavior he had warned against that morning. He credits the power play for providing momentum and praises the penalty kill's performance. Scoring on Luongo built confidence, but he expects a tough next game. He notes his goalie stayed in his net more, stresses better puck management and fewer turnovers, describes the opponent's aggressive neutral-zone play, and says the team is even-keel and in good spirits, hoping home advantage helps turn the series around.

Mary Meeker's annual Internet trends survey, presented at the Code conference, shows global internet usage growth slowed to 7% from 12%, with 3.6 billion users worldwide. Smartphone sales have stalled. Google's voice recognition accuracy reached 95%. E-commerce rose 16% in 2017, representing 13% of retail sales. Netflix leads subscriptions with 117 million users. Unemployment is at a historic low of 3.9%.

Researchers from the University of St Andrews trained deep neural networks (ResNet-18, ResNet-50, and VGG16) to classify medical images by modality—CT, MRI, PET, and X-ray—using a hyper-scale dataset of 4.5 million images compiled from 102 medical imaging datasets, primarily sourced from The Cancer Imaging Archive. Data was split at the dataset level into train, validate, and test sets to prevent data leakage, with 3D scans treated as collections of 2D slices resized to 224×224. The best performing model, ResNet-18, achieved 96% classification accuracy and 86% balanced accuracy on unseen data, performing strongly on CT, MR, and PET but less well on X-rays, particularly bone X-ray datasets (MURA and Osteoarthritis Initiative). The authors note that prior modality classification studies used far smaller datasets (hundreds to thousands of images), and that such hyper-scale classifiers could support real-world applications such as medical imaging repositories and national healthcare institutions. Future work will extend the approach to 3D scan modalities.

This passage is a user manual for the SanDisk Sansa c200 media player. It describes the Record button (held two seconds to start mic recording, stopped with the middle silver button), connecting the device to a computer via USB where it appears as a drive named "Sansa c200," and using Sansa Media Converter to transfer photos (supporting JPEG, TIFF, PNG, BMP, and GIF). Files can be dragged into the Media folder in MTP mode if they are WMA or MP3, otherwise into the Data folder, or copied in MSC mode. The FAQ addresses copying files, supported formats (MP3, WAV, WMA, secure WMA), the MTP protocol, playback rights, firmware updates, CD ripping, podcasts (mp3, 32–320 kbps), and missing ID3 tags. Technical support is available by phone or online.

The one-year limited warranty applies to the original end user, is non-transferable, excludes third-party software, and is void if the product is misused; SanDisk may repair, replace, or refund, and disclaims liability for lost data and consequential damages. Mr. Sill reports that the Korean government, discouraged by the southern rebellion and urged by the Chinese representative, requested Chinese aid; 2,000 Chinese troops were sent to Asan, but Korean forces suppressed the rebellion themselves before the Chinese actively assisted. Japan also dispatched troops, citing protection of its subjects and legation. Despite the 1885 Tien-tsin convention requiring mutual notification before landing troops, 3,000 Japanese soldiers landed at Chemulpo and encamped on the foreign settlement without other powers' consent, prompting a joint protest by Sill and his European colleagues. This article develops and defends "educational pacifism," the position that educational harm is morally impermissible as a means to educational goods. Drawing on Feinberg's and Mill's definitions of harm as adversely affecting a person's important interests, it argues that mass formal schooling systems cause pervasive, largely unnoticed harm. Harm is divided into personal harm (e.g., bullying and verbal abuse), which is noticeable, and systemic harm, which is more common and goes unnoticed because it constitutes normality. Systemic harm is categorized as structural (rooted in hierarchical, authoritarian patterns tracing to industrial-era schooling designed to produce obedience and conformity), objective (caused by inequality and the capitalist economic order, for which schools prepare students for subordination), and symbolic (nonphysical harm embedded in curricula, pedagogy, testing, ranking, and neoliberal ideologies).

On morality, the article adapts conditional antiwar pacifism and Kant's formula of humanity: educational practice is just only if it does not harm innocents, and mass schooling fails this condition. Most students are innocent—regardless of personhood—and educational harm prevents no great harm, with peaceful alternatives existing, so schooling cannot be a last resort. The author does not claim schooling is inherently harmful or should be abolished entirely.

The article then argues that Montessori's thought broadly aligns with educational pacifism: she viewed education as the means to positive, lasting peace, critiqued the coercive and dominating schooling of her day, rejected rewards and punishments, and centered freedom and harmonious activity. Finally, it contends that contemporary Montessorians should adopt educational pacifism, supported by three arguments: the moral analysis of educational harm, Montessori's own arguments, and her authority for Montessorians. Both educational pacifism and Montessori education reject paternalism while permitting nonharmful guidance and structure. Noting concerns about weak or inauthentic Montessori implementation, the article concludes that Montessori education is well placed to provide a nonharmful alternative to mass formal schooling.

The DAX (Deutscher Aktienindex) is Germany's main equity index, consisting of the 40 largest blue-chip stocks on Deutsche Börse Xetra, expanded from 30 companies in September 2021. It offers high liquidity and diversification, as it trades during different hours than US markets and moves differently—mean reversion, breakout, gap, and momentum strategies work well on it. The DAX can be traded via futures, CFDs, or ETFs, with futures being the most popular option. DAX futures trade electronically on Eurex from 0750 to 2200 CET and come in three sizes: full (25 EUR per point), mini (5 EUR), and micro (1 EUR). Contracts expire quarterly and settle in cash. Two backtested overnight strategies were presented: a November 2021 strategy (209 trades, 65% win rate, 0.22% per trade, 5.1% max drawdown) and a November 2022 strategy (303 trades, 0.23% per trade). DAX strategies differ from S&P 500 strategies, offering reduced correlation.

In the first lecture of MIT 6.832 (Underactuated Robotics, Spring 2009), Russ Tedrake outlines the course, whose only prerequisites are comfort with differential equations, linear algebra, and MATLAB. Using Honda's ASIMO—which walks conservatively with bent knees and flat feet, uses about 20 times the energy of a human walker, and handles only known terrain—as an example, he contrasts it with Cornell's passive dynamic walker to argue that robots should exploit their natural dynamics rather than cancel them with high-gain feedback. Similar comparisons are drawn between aircraft and birds landing at high angles of attack, the albatross's energy efficiency, bat maneuverability, and a dead trout that moves upstream in a vortex street. He defines underactuation for second-order mechanical systems whose equations of motion are linear in the inputs: a system is fully actuated if the input matrix has rank equal to the dimension of the coordinates, enabling feedback linearization, and underactuated if the rank is lower, meaning inputs cannot accelerate the system in every direction. Deriving the manipulator equations for a two-link arm via Lagrangian mechanics, he demonstrates feedback linearization, then shows that removing the shoulder motor produces the Acrobot. Walking robots, jumping robots, flying machines, and manipulation before force closure are inherently underactuated, and he claims the interesting unsolved problems in robotics are underactuated. The course will proceed through the pendulum, cart-pole, walking robots with impacts and limit cycles, higher-dimensional and uncertain systems, using optimal control, dynamic programming, policy search, motion planning, and reinforcement learning in a computational, spiral structure.

Nick Mathewson, co-author of the Tor paper and one of its main developers, gives a lecture on Tor, an anonymity network of roughly 6,000 volunteer-operated relays serving hundreds of thousands to millions of users. He defines anonymity as preventing an observer from linking participants to actions, distinguishing it from unlinkability and unobservability. Users include citizens seeking privacy, researchers avoiding biased data, companies protecting sensitive information, law enforcement, and criminals. Mathewson walks through Tor's design: single relays are insufficient, so traffic passes through multiple relays, each removing a layer of encryption, with symmetric keys negotiated per circuit—an approach building on 1990s onion routing. Tor relays TCP stream contents rather than IP packets. Node discovery uses multiple directory authorities that vote hourly and sign a consensus. On abuse, IP-based blocking frequently bans Tor users; proposed remedies include anonymous blacklistable credentials. Hidden services provide responder anonymity using public keys and a DHT directory, with key blinding planned to prevent enumeration attacks. Notable attacks include application-level leaks, traffic tagging, denial-of-service ("sniper") attacks, and a Diffie-Hellman flaw that allowed man-in-the-middle attacks. Censorship resistance relies on pluggable transports and bridges, which evade blocking for months at a time, even in China. Future work includes revamping hidden services, replacing older cryptography, improving path selection and congestion control, and scaling beyond current limits.

The Yankees and Blue Jays tied for the best American League record, but Toronto's tiebreaker win made it the No. 1 seed with a bye, while New York beat the Red Sox to reach the ALDS. The best-of-five series begins Saturday, Oct. 4, with Games 1, 2 and 5 in Toronto and Games 3 and 4 in the Bronx. Games 1 and 2 air on Fox and FS1; Toronto won the season series 8-5.

Months after the Trump administration cut staff at the U.S. Department of Education and after DOGE eliminated more than 100 research contracts in February, education researchers report cautious optimism. The department plans to reinstate 20 contracts, a lawsuit gives a reprieve to 10 federally funded regional education labs, and it is seeking public input on modernizing the Institute of Education Sciences (IES). Amber Northern of the Thomas B. Fordham Institute is advising on IES reform through December, and NCES has begun hiring for NAEP-related assessment jobs. Concerns persist: NCES staff was reduced from about 100 employees to three, staff shortages threaten data quality, and an August executive order requires a large retroactive admissions survey. AERA's Tabbye Chavous rated IES at 3 or 4 on a 10-point scale, down from 10 before the cuts.

Saving a penalty kick is considered the most stressful task for a soccer goalkeeper, with success rates generally below 15%, since roughly 80% of penalty kicks are scored and about 5% are missed. Goalkeepers must know Law 14 of the IFAB Laws of the Game, which sets strict procedures for penalty kicks, including goalkeeper positioning requirements and consequences for violations; the law is designed to favor attackers. Coaches must prepare goalkeepers through dedicated training, provide unconditional support, and ensure teammates do not blame keepers for missed saves. Modern emphasis has shifted from "guess and go" to "read and react," as one study showed up to 39% of penalty goals are scored up the middle. Preparation involves psychological makeup (desire, focus, and resilience), mental techniques (visualization, positive self-talk, pre-shot routines, controlled breathing, staying present), and physical training with proper equipment. Goalkeepers should research opponents' tendencies and learn visual cues such as ball placement, run-up, plant foot, hip orientation, and body lean. During the kick, keepers should stay calm, assume a ready position, avoid diving early, beware stutter runs, and react to the ball. Afterward, they must handle rebounds, goal kicks, corners, and fast breaks, while avoiding live-ball errors such as teammates dislodging a held ball. Additional coaching tips include rattling the kicker within the Law, avoiding early goal-line encroachment, and possibly standing slightly off-center to influence the taker's perception of the goal.

The passage is a set of hockey interview excerpts. A speaker describes a win in which a crucial power-play goal off a lucky bounce and a goal by Donovan lifted team confidence. He discusses captaincy, citing young captains such as Shane Doan and Joe Thornton, and says Jarome, already the team's leader on the ice and in the room, earned the "C" like Messier, Gretzky, and Lemieux. Kipper is praised for consistent play and for bouncing back after allowing five or six goals in Colorado; beating Colorado after the all-star break raised the team's standards. Fatigue is addressed, with the opponent also using a short bench. The speaker notes breakout problems against opponents who keep rimmed pucks in, urging more use of the middle of the ice.
