Quiet leaders such as Martin Gelinas built mental toughness, and Darryl, handling two roles, brought in Kiprusoff and three late-season acquisitions.

Metagenomic binning clusters DNA fragments from mixed microbial samples so that each cluster corresponds to a distinct genome, enabling downstream analyses such as functional annotation and phylogenetic profiling. Traditional methods represent sequences via k-mer profiles; while genome foundation models (e.g., DNABERT variants, HYENADNA) generate embeddings directly from raw sequences, k-mer-based embeddings achieve comparable performance with orders-of-magnitude greater computational efficiency. However, deterministic embeddings map each fragment to a single point, which cannot handle sequences appearing in multiple genomes (e.g., through horizontal gene transfer) or distinct sequences with highly similar k-mer profiles.

The authors propose UNCERTAINGEN, presented as the first probabilistic embedding framework for DNA sequences in metagenomic binning. Each fragment is mapped to a distribution rather than a point, explicitly encoding ambiguity. Unlike prior probabilistic embeddings that rely on heuristically selected distributional distances, their contrastive-learning formulation derives non-Euclidean distances naturally from a probability distribution over the embedding space, with closed-form expressions for expected pairwise likelihood enabling scalable optimization. They also provide theoretical analysis identifying sequences that produce large covariance terms.

Contributions include: a novel probabilistic framework modeling uncertainty from inter-species DNA sharing and similar representations; theoretical guarantees showing probabilistic embeddings expand the feasible latent space and improve separation capacity; and empirical improvements over deterministic k-mer and LLM-based embeddings on real metagenomic datasets.

The proposed model builds on lightweight k-mer-based binning methods: sequences are split into segments forming positive and negative pairs, k-mer profiles are passed through a shared neural network trained with a contractive loss, and the resulting embeddings are clustered. The objective is an embedding function where distance reflects cluster membership.

Jeff Davis Parish schools opened last Friday after summer preparations including streamlined processes, campus improvements, bus driver training, and revised teaching plans based on student academic evaluations. The parish ranks fourth in state graduation rates at 92.5%, up three percentage points from last year.

This scoping review examined barriers and facilitators to a sense of belonging in graduate health professions education, with implications for occupational therapy education. Using Arksey and O'Malley's framework and the PRISMA-ScR checklist, the authors searched multiple databases and journals, identifying 202 studies; 70 remained after title/abstract review and duplicate removal, and a final sample of 9 articles (from occupational therapy, physical therapy, and medical education) was included. Qualitative content analysis revealed three themes affecting belonging: (1) environment, including physical space and institutional culture and climate; (2) relationships, including faculty-to-student and peer-to-peer connections; and (3) personal factors, such as students' perceptions of their belonging and academic ability. Students from historically minoritized identities face additional barriers, including discrimination, microaggressions, and belonging uncertainty. The authors recommend that occupational therapy programs create welcoming and accessible spaces, use inclusive teaching practices, foster faculty mentorship and peer relationships, provide bias training and affinity groups, and involve students in research. They call for further research on belonging specifically within occupational therapy education. Limitations include the possibility of omitted articles, author bias, lack of evaluation of study rigor, and the subjective nature of belonging.

This study proposes a world model framework for autonomous endovascular navigation in mechanical thrombectomy (MT), a stroke treatment with limited clinical accessibility. Using the stEVE simulation environment with ten patient-specific vascular anatomies, the authors trained a model-based reinforcement learning agent (TD-MPC2) and compared it to the model-free state-of-the-art SAC across five navigation tasks spanning the femoral artery to the internal carotid artery. TD-MPC2 achieved a significantly higher mean success rate (65% vs 37%, p < 0.001) and improved path ratios, though with longer procedure times. Single-task SAC training achieved high success rates on shorter tasks. The results, representing the largest dataset examined for autonomous MT, demonstrate TD-MPC2's superior multi-task generalization, though performance remains suboptimal for clinical deployment. Future work includes improving generalization, incorporating contact forces and vessel deformation, and transitioning to in vitro testbeds.

The Supreme Court declined to hear several cases, including Alex Jones' appeal of a Connecticut defamation case brought by Sandy Hook families and an appeal by Colorado parents who claimed a school district violated their constitutional rights by excluding them from discussions of their children's gender identity. Lower courts had ruled for the school district. Justice Alito, joined by Justices Thomas and Gorsuch, agreed with the denial but expressed concern that federal courts are avoiding the question of whether schools violate parents' rights by facilitating gender transitions without parental consent. The Court also denied review in a Section 230 case against Grindr brought by a plaintiff who alleged the app offered him membership at age 15 and connected him with adults who raped him; lower courts had dismissed the case based on Section 230 immunity. In a Georgia death penalty case involving juror misconduct, the Court denied review, with Justice Sotomayor, joined by Justices Kagan and Jackson, stating the case should have been sent back for clarification. The Court also declined an appeal from California property owners over jury trials for cannabis-related code fines, with Gorsuch urging the justices to soon reconsider the relevant precedent. The Court called for the solicitor general's views in two cases and will hold its next conference on Oct. 17.

The United States Bankruptcy Court for the Middle District of Tennessee granted summary judgment in favor of Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. and Dynamic Management Company, LLC against SCS General Contractors, Inc. Barnhill's Buffets, Inc. filed a chapter 11 petition on December 3, 2007, operating twenty-nine buffet restaurants in six states, with Wells Fargo holding a $23,256,526.00 secured claim. SCS sought payment of $246,538.59 for pre-petition construction work on three Mississippi restaurant properties (Jackson, Gulfport, and Meridian), claiming equitable liens on both the debtor's leasehold interests and the landlords' fee interests.

The court held that any equitable lien held by SCS terminated when Barnhill's filed bankruptcy, because the debtor-in-possession assumed the position of a bona fide purchaser without notice under 11 U.S.C. § 544(a)(3), relying on In re Omegas. The court further held that under Mississippi law, Miss. Code Ann. § 85-7-137, no lien—equitable or statutory—could attach to the landlords' fee interests absent written consent, which none of the landlords provided. SCS was also found not to be a party to or third-party beneficiary of the leases.

Regarding Dynamic, SCS's alter ego claims failed because SCS offered only unsworn documents and a counsel affidavit, which did not rebut the affidavit of Dynamic member Craig Barber stating that Dynamic never managed, controlled, or had any involvement with Barnhill's.

The court granted Spirit Finance's unopposed motion to dismiss SCS's cross-claims, denied SCS's request for a continuance, ordered the escrowed funds released to Wells Fargo, and left SCS with only an unsecured creditor claim in the bankruptcy case.

The family of cyclist Milton Olin Jr., killed by a texting Los Angeles County sheriff's deputy, reached a nearly $12 million settlement with the county; attorneys are asking prosecutors to reexamine the case.

This passage describes the "Household Sewing Machines-Global Market Status and Trend Report 2013-2023," a market research report offering analysis of the household sewing machines industry for insiders, potential entrants, and investors. It addresses worldwide and regional market size (2013-2017) and development forecasts (2018-2023), main manufacturers, market status by types and applications, cost and profit status, and growth drivers and challenges. The market is segmented by region (North America, Europe, China, Japan, Rest APAC, Latin America), by type (Mechanical and Electronic Sewing Machines), and by application (Home and Light Commercial). Manufacturers covered include Brother, Singer, Janome, Necchi Macchina, Bernina International, Union Special, Merrow, AMF Reece, CR Consew, YAMATA, Elna International, SVP Worldwide, and Henderson Sewing. The table of contents spans seven chapters covering market overview, regional and type forecasts, downstream industry, driving factors, competition status, and manufacturer profiles.

Actress Allison Mack of "Smallville" was released on $5 million bail to await trial on charges of recruiting women as sex slaves for a secret society that prosecutors say Keith Raniere ran within his Nxivm organization. She is under house arrest at her parents' California home. Mack, who pleaded not guilty, is in plea negotiations. Raniere, arrested last month, is jailed without bail and denies abusing anyone.

Human revulsion toward eating insects stems from bugs' constant presence in daily life and their alien movement. The UN estimates two billion people worldwide eat bugs, with at least 1,900 edible species offering sustainable protein, fats, fiber, vitamins, and minerals. Research shows most primates retain genes producing an enzyme that breaks down chitin in insect exoskeletons, and cooking aids digestion. In 2017, the Seattle Mariners sold roasted grasshoppers from Poquitos restaurant, exceeding the restaurant's annual sales in three games.

The U.S. Department of Education has announced a review of the Institute of Education Sciences (IES), which plays a vital role in identifying what works in public education and supporting states and districts. A coalition of education research and development organizations sent the Secretary of Education recommendations in three areas: prioritizing research on pressing state and local needs, maximizing impact through coordination and infrastructure, and helping states and districts apply knowledge through improved communication and support. Proposed steps include establishing learning agendas, faster research tracks, streamlined study approvals, rapid-cycle tools like the School PULSE survey, data modernization such as EDPass, restarting Regional Education Laboratories and Comprehensive Centers, and using technologies like AI to deliver evidence to classrooms. The author argues these changes would make federal education research more efficient, effective, and accountable, improving outcomes for students, educators, and families.

LG has launched its G7 ThinQ flagship smartphone in South Africa, competing against dominant premium brands. The device features Gorilla Glass 5, a bright screen, an AI camera with 19 shooting modes, a dedicated Google Assistant button, a Snapdragon 845 processor, 4GB RAM, 64GB expandable storage, and a 16MP dual-lens rear camera, arriving in early June from about R13,999.

The passage outlines a proposed diplomatic offensive and suggested peace terms. Toward Bulgaria, the Allies should recognize its national claims and Serbia's independence and sea access; toward Italy, support frontier rectification with assurances on evacuation and economic needs. Regarding Austria-Hungary, agitation over subject nationalities should continue with assurances against dismemberment and mention of its debts to Germany, while accepting disarmament discussions. Against Germany, the offensive should stress that failure to democratize means exclusion from postwar intercourse, without dictating its government form. Toward Russia: stating war aims, promoting a league of nations, and demonstrating the offensive. France's morale should be aided by interest in Alsace-Lorraine, and the western Allies by economic unity and liberal American utterances. Suggested peace terms include evacuation and restoration of Belgium and northern France, leaving Luxemburg to negotiation, and undoing the 1871 wrong in Alsace-Lorraine.

Navy veteran Gerard Ah-Fook, who lost his leg in a boating accident, had his specialized handcycle stolen from his porch on Saturday, Aug. 12. After seeing the story, Randy Sooter gave Ah-Fook a handcycle he had bought while rehabbing from ankle surgery. Police are still searching for the thief; the stolen bike is a white recumbent three-wheeler with red "Top End Force RX" lettering.

Members of The Oracles share strategies for beating distraction and sharpening focus. Lewis Howes urges living with urgency and tracking daily performance. Mark Divine recommends working from a distraction-free "secret location" one to two days weekly, using focusing rituals and 45-minute work blocks. Chris Harder advises rejecting opportunities unless they are "heck-yes" right now, optionally using an advisory board to help say no. Kenny Rueter suggests eliminating diversions and tackling one top-priority task at a time. Nafisé Nina Hodjat says focus comes naturally when you're obsessed with your work. Nik Halik outlines a five-step strategy: embrace stress, follow a morning routine, work in 90-minute blocks, create recharging rituals, and optimize sleep. Tom Shieh schedules focus areas on his calendar instead of multitasking. Peter Hernandez advocates building an organizational culture of fierce focus with clear, measurable goals tied to purpose.

This patent application discloses systems and methods for Artificial Intelligence (AI) assisted activity training. A rendering device, such as a smart mirror or a display device (e.g., smart TV, mobile phone, laptop, tablet, or projector), presents a plurality of activity categories to a user as multimedia content. The user provides a voice-based input in a source language, which a Natural Language Processing (NLP) model—configured using a single intermediate language—processes to extract selected activities and associated activity attributes. Multimedia content including guidance steps performed by a virtual assistant is then presented, and cameras capture video of the user's activity performance. An AI model processes the video in real time to extract user performance parameters and generates feedback based on differences between user and target performance parameters, rendered aurally, visually, or as haptic feedback. The disclosure describes embodiments including smart mirrors with one-way mirrors and integrated displays, sensors and wearable devices for biometric data, gymnasium implementations with distributed cameras and a central server, live trainer broadcasts, creation of activity training circuits and playlists, social media sharing, gamification, and language-agnostic operation. The background notes that indoor exercise often lacks expert guidance and motivation, which the disclosed system addresses.

VentureWire's October 31, 2000 issue reports that Trinity Ventures closed a $540 million fund (Trinity VIII), bringing its capital under management to over $1 billion; Sun Microsystems will invest an additional $100 million in wireless companies over the next year; online textbook retailer Bigwords.com ceased operations; and Internet consultancy Concrete laid off 15% of its staff. A correction notes Candescent Technology has raised more than $600 million.

Strength training offers health benefits but requires correct technique, proper warm-up, and cool-down to prevent injury. Common injuries include rotator cuff injuries from repetitive overhead motions, hamstring strains from sudden powerful movements, herniated discs from extreme or poor lifting movements, tendonitis from repetitive stress, and tennis or golfer's elbow from repetitive arm and wrist movements. Prevention measures include good posture, regular stretching, warming up, using proper form, and increasing workout intensity gradually. Treatment varies by severity and may involve rest, painkillers, physiotherapy, or surgery. Fitness coach Ollie Kerr recommends warming up to increase heart rate and blood flow, cooling down afterward, eating well, staying hydrated, and using ice, compression, and elevation for initial treatment of injuries. Persistent pain should be assessed by a doctor, and consulting a qualified fitness instructor before starting a strength-training routine is advised.

More than 3,400 students are expected to receive degrees from the University of North Texas during fall 2017 commencement ceremonies held Dec. 15–16 at the UNT Coliseum and the Murchison Performing Arts Center in Denton. This fall, 2,731 undergraduate, 615 master's, and 72 doctoral students applied for graduation, and some summer degree recipients will also attend. Live streams of the ceremonies will be available online. Additionally, graduates traveling to the New Orleans Bowl are invited to a special commencement ceremony at 6:15 p.m. Dec. 15 at the Hilton New Orleans Riverside, with online RSVP required. A reception for master's and doctoral candidates follows that evening at the Gateway Center.

Amazon.com, Inc.'s Form 10-K for fiscal year 2017 reports that the company, incorporated in Delaware and headquartered in Seattle, operates three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). It serves consumers through retail websites, physical stores, and electronic devices; sellers through marketplace and fulfillment programs; developers and enterprises through AWS; and content creators through services such as Kindle Direct Publishing. Amazon acquired Whole Foods Market on August 28, 2017, and employed approximately 566,000 full- and part-time employees as of December 31, 2017. Net sales were $177.9 billion in 2017, with operating income of $4.1 billion and net income of $3.0 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $31.0 billion at year-end, and operating cash flow was $18.4 billion. During 2017, Amazon issued $16.0 billion of senior unsecured notes, used in part to fund the Whole Foods acquisition. Risk factors include intense competition, expansion strains, international regulatory risks (notably in China and India), fulfillment network and inventory challenges, seasonality, data security, intellectual property, and tax matters—including the 2017 Tax Act, an IRS transfer pricing dispute on appeal, and a European Commission state aid decision ordering recovery of approximately €250 million plus interest. Amazon has never declared or paid cash dividends.

The speaker attributed losing a goal lead in the third period to soft plays and stick checking against Detroit. Despite narrow one-goal losses, he expressed confidence the team would bounce back at home and praised Olie's saves, citing tired defense instead.

The Supreme Court appointed senior counsel Amarendra Sharan as amicus curiae to examine material submitted by petitioner Pankaj Kumud Chandra Phadnis seeking a fresh inquiry into a larger conspiracy behind Mahatma Gandhi's assassination, though the bench said the material prima facie appeared insufficient. Phadnis, challenging the Bombay High Court's 2016 order, alleged involvement of British Secret Service Force 136 and sought a new Commission of Inquiry.

This lecture introduces graph limits, a relatively new subject in graph theory. Motivated by an analogy with how real numbers complete the rationals (illustrated by minimizing x³ − x over [0,1], where the minimizer 1/√3 is not rational), the instructor explains that some graph optimization problems—such as minimizing 4-cycle density among graphs with edge density p, whose minimum p⁴ is approached only by a sequence of quasirandom graphs—are best expressed through a single limit object rather than a cumbersome sequence.

The central object is the graphon: a symmetric measurable function from the unit square to [0,1]. A graph can be converted into a graphon by viewing its adjacency matrix as a pixelated image. Examples include half graphs converging to a diagonal line and quasirandom graphs converging to the constant graphon p, while a checkerboard example (a complete bipartite graph) shows that intuitive "squinting" can be misleading and a precise definition is needed.

Graph homomorphisms and homomorphism density t(H,G) are defined for graphs and, via integrals, for graphons, with the two definitions agreeing. A sequence of graphs is convergent if all homomorphism densities converge. Regarding distances, edit distance is rejected (two random graphs remain far apart), so the cut norm and cut distance—optimized over measure-preserving transformations—are introduced, with associated measure-theoretic subtleties.

Three main theorems are stated: (1) convergence of homomorphism densities is equivalent to being Cauchy in cut distance; (2) every convergent sequence of graphs or graphons has a limit graphon; and (3) the space of graphons is compact. This compactness is philosophically related to Szemeredi's Regularity Lemma, a weaker version of which will be used in its proof, and the theory generalizes quasirandomness, where quasirandom graphs correspond to the constant graphon.

An email from Steven J. Kean to Maureen McVicker dated October 16, 2000, forwards several news articles mentioning Enron. Devro's shares have risen almost a quarter since January. First-half sales rose 11pc to £125m on demand in Russia, south-east Asia and China. The new Chinese plant should reach full capacity by year-end.

Five-year-old Angel, born in a Pakistani slum in Karachi, suffers from CLOVES syndrome, a rare condition with only about 200 documented cases worldwide, which has caused her feet to swell enormously. Bullied and refused entry to school in Pakistan, she was brought to Australia 18 months ago by humanitarian Moira Kelly, arriving severely malnourished and too weak for surgery. Paediatric surgeon Professor Tony Pennington will now perform a double amputation free of charge in Melbourne. Angel, aware she will lose both feet and the lower part of her legs, is reportedly happy about the operation, having dreamed of wearing shoes and dancing.

On May 31, 2016, Tesla Motors, Inc. held its 2016 Annual Meeting of Stockholders, at which stockholders voted on three proposals. Brad W. Buss and Ira Ehrenpreis were elected as Class III directors to serve three-year terms. The CBEC has given central government officers the power to verify transitional credit claims under GST, citing concerns over taxpayers over-claiming credits. Taxpayers have claimed Rs 1.6 lakh crore in transitional credit since GST launch. The CBEC justified the move, stating only the tax authority with prior jurisdiction and records can verify. Experts warn this could cause litigation between the Centre and states. The CBEC also plans to amend the CGST Act to exclude cess credits, though one expert said the government acted within its rights.

This passage documents the AMD AGESA™ software's interface requirements, build process, and procedures for host environments, primarily in UEFI BIOS implementations. Under the binary image build model, all AGESA call-outs are funneled through a single interface portal, requiring the host environment to implement a call-out router function that translates function numbers into execution addresses.

The UEFI environment comprises four execution stages (SEC, PEI, DXE, and RTP) across three execution modes. AGESA core files are organized into libraries and built with Microsoft tools (MASM and CL compilers) for 16-bit, 32-bit, and 64-bit phases. PEI-phase PEIMs perform processor initialization, memory initialization, and reset coordination, publishing PPIs and a memory information HOB. The DXE driver performs late initialization, generates data tables via AmdInitLate, and publishes the AgesaDxeProtocol.

Stack procedures (AMD_ENABLE_STACK, AMD_DISABLE_STACK) establish and remove the Cache-As-RAM pre-memory stack using a register-passing model; they apply to x86-64 APUs, while AARCH64 APUs with the Platform Security Processor do not use them. Service procedures include AmdCreateStruct/AmdReleaseStruct for parameter block storage, plus utilities for data eye results, APIC and PCI addresses, core identification, event logs, and MMIO allocation.

Entry procedures are listed in time-point order: AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost, AmdInitEnv, AmdInitMid, AmdInitLate, AmdInitRtb, and S3 suspend/resume procedures. The host environment must implement the required call-outs AgesaAllocateBuffer, AgesaDeallocateBuffer, and AgesaReset.

West Virginia Attorney General Patrick Morrisey renewed a contract with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, letting state investigators check stores for recalled products and verify recall notices are posted. Since 2015, over 40 compliance checks occurred, with 25 more planned.

The author presents options strategies for gaining exposure to AMD's anticipated upward move without immediately buying shares. AMD has traded in a range of roughly $9.30 to $15.13 since late 2016 and currently sits near $10, a supported level, with Q1 2018 earnings expected around April 25, 2018 as a potential positive catalyst. Three strategies are described: (1) buying a $10 strike call for about $0.60 ($60 per contract), limiting risk versus purchasing 100 shares for $1,000; (2) a call spread—buying the $10 call and selling the $12 call for a net cost of $0.50, capping profits at $12 (a 15% gain); and (3) selling a cash-covered $10 put for $0.56, reducing the cost basis to $9.44 if assigned, or combining it with the spread for a net credit of $0.06, though this adds assignment risk if AMD settles below $10. The author expects a strong earnings report, citing improved products, processor demand, potential market share gains from Intel and Nvidia, and a short position of about 182 million shares that could fuel a squeeze. The author discloses being long AMD, INTC, and NVDA.

The CCAT Collaboration is constructing the Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope (FYST), a six-meter off-axis crossed-Dragone telescope at 5600 m on Cerro Chajnantor in Chile's Atacama Desert, with observations scheduled to begin in 2026. Two instruments are being developed: Mod-Cam, a first-light testbed housing a 280 GHz camera with over 10,000 KID detectors in three arrays, and Prime-Cam, a seven-module science instrument with roughly 100,000 KIDs read out through three readout harnesses. This work characterizes the 46 cm low-thermal-conductivity stripline flexible circuits connecting the 4 K and 300 K readout stages. Measurements of the copper's residual resistance ratio (RRR ≈ 120) and thermal conductivity agree with literature values for OFHC copper, and thermal loading estimates indicate the redesigned Prime-Cam stripline produces lower 4 K loading than Mod-Cam's despite three times more stripline. Warm crosstalk measurements identified the SMP-SMA transition PCBs, rather than the stripline, as the source of elevated inter-channel crosstalk. Simulations of redesigned PCBs using an impedance-matched via predict roughly 20 dB crosstalk improvement, expected to meet project requirements. The results validate stripline as a scalable solution for reading out large KID arrays.

This WIRED article reviews white noise machines for sleep, updated September 2025 with newly tested products from Momcozy, Yogasleep, and Lectrofan. It explains that noise "colors" like white, pink, and brown correspond to different sound frequencies, with pink and brown noise being lower-pitched and less grating. Reviewed machines include the LectroFan Classic (fan and colored noises, up to 85 decibels, 60-minute timer), the Snooz (real-fan white noise, simple design), the Hatch 3 and second-generation Hatch Rest (app-controlled, with subscriptions for full content), the Babelio mini (helpful for anxious dogs), Yogasleep's Dohm, Rohm+, and Hushh 2, Momcozy's portable machine with night-light and Bluetooth, the ErgoPouch, a small Amazon option, and smart speakers from Google or Alexa that can play ambient sounds. For babies, the article advises keeping machines at least 200 centimeters (6.5 feet) from where they sleep. It closes with FAQs on all-night use, fans as alternatives, WIRED's independent selection process, and donation of tested products.

The Inverted Hammer is a bullish reversal candlestick pattern that forms at the bottom of a downtrend, characterized by a small body near the lower end, little or no lower shadow, and a long upper shadow, resembling an upside-down hammer. It signals that buyers are gaining momentum against sellers and a potential upward reversal may occur. Body color is less important than position; if it formed at the top of an uptrend, it would be a shooting star instead.

Because it is a single-candle formation, the pattern should be confirmed with other tools such as trendlines, support levels, moving averages, and momentum oscillators. Common strategies include swing trading in uptrends (entering long after pullbacks to support) and mean reversion using oversold conditions.

Backtests on the S&P 500 (SPY) since 1993 produced 132 trades with win ratios of 53–65% for 1–10 day exits, a 70% win rate, and an average gain of 0.36% per trade. The pattern is the 11th most frequent of 75 candlestick patterns, occurring in overbought conditions 58% of the time. The authors note it behaves bearishly when overbought and bullishly during downturns, but overall regard it as a bearish pattern since better bullish alternatives exist.

Disadvantages include subjectivity, false signals, and unsuitability for all timeframes. Recommended risk management includes stop-losses below the pullback low, risking 1–2% of capital per trade, and 2:1 reward/risk ratios.

President Trump will direct U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer on Monday to determine whether to investigate Chinese trade practices that force U.S. firms operating in China to turn over intellectual property, a move that could eventually lead to steep tariffs on Chinese goods. Administration officials said the potential probe is unrelated to Trump's push for China to do more on North Korea. Violet Brown, a 117-year-old Jamaican woman who spent much of her life cutting sugarcane, is believed to have become the world's oldest living person following the death of Italy's Emma Morano. According to the Gerontology Research Group, she is the oldest person with credible birth documentation, born March 10, 1900. Guinness World Records has not yet confirmed the title. Brown credits hard work and her Christian faith for her longevity and lives with her 97-year-old son.

A University of California, Davis study published in Annals of Epidemiology found gun deaths in California declined over 16 years ending in 2015, largely due to reduced gang violence and fewer black homicides. Of 50,921 firearm deaths from 2000-2015, 24,922 were homicides and 23,682 suicides. The homicide rate fell from 4.19 per 100,000 in 2000 to 3.13 in 2014. After federal funding restrictions limited CDC gun research, California and private foundations have increased funding for such studies.

The passage contrasts digital leaders and laggards in their approach to data-driven goals and culture. Digital laggards set aspirational objectives insufficiently grounded in data, causing employees to avoid measurement and adopt a "best effort" approach; they emphasize process adherence over quantitative metrics, which stifles innovation, and fail to connect goals with strategy, producing misalignment. Digital leaders create structured, transparent goals aligned with company strategy, developed through combined top-down and bottom-up processes that build employee buy-in, though even they risk overburdening decisions with exhaustive data analysis. A data-driven culture aligns organizations both vertically and horizontally, and digital leaders treat data culture as central to coordinating efforts, with employee behaviors reflecting stated values. Laggards show misalignment between espoused values and actual behavior, and changing engrained mindsets is the most challenging part of transformation—though laggards are not doomed, as some leaders have transformed. Organizations fit four patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant—and can take targeted actions to build a strong data culture.

The passage describes the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, the 8th-generation data center GPU built on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture (GA100), fabricated on TSMC's 7nm process with 54.2 billion transistors. Building on the Tesla V100, the A100 delivers significantly faster performance for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads.

Key features include:
- Third-generation Tensor Cores supporting new data types: TF32 (10x faster than V100 FP32, 20x with sparsity), BF16, IEEE-compliant FP64 (2.5x V100), and INT8 (20x faster with sparsity); FP16/FP32 mixed-precision runs 2.5x V100 (5x with sparsity)
- Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity (2:4 pattern) that doubles Tensor Core throughput
- Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitioning into up to seven GPU Instances with fault isolation and QoS, benefiting Cloud Service Providers
- 40 GB HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x larger than V100), and Compute Data Compression
- Third-generation NVLink delivering 600 GB/sec total bandwidth (versus 300 GB/sec for V100), plus PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV
- New capabilities: asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, task graph acceleration, improved error detection and isolation, NVJPG decode, an optical flow accelerator, and five NVDEC units

The A100 contains 108 SMs, 6912 FP32 CUDA cores, and 432 Tensor Cores. CUDA 11 provides programming support for these features. The A100 powers the DGX A100 system, which contains eight A100 GPUs delivering 5 PFLOPS, interconnected via NVSwitch and Mellanox InfiniBand. An appendix explains neural network pruning and distinguishes fine-grained from coarse-grained sparsity.

PSA is the most widely used prostate cancer (PCa) biomarker but yields false positives in up to 47% of cases, and mpMRI combined with PSA still misses up to 30% of clinically significant PCa, while biopsies carry risks such as sepsis (2–4%). This work presents an ISFET-based Lab-on-Chip (LoC) device using RT-pHLAMP, an augmented RT-LAMP assay that monitors pH change from amplification, for point-of-care detection of circulating YAP1 nucleic acid, AR-FL and AR-V7 mRNA from PCa patient blood plasma. After optimising RNA extraction (TRIzol LS was selected over a Norgen kit), benchtop RT-pHLAMP detected YAP1 within 12 min, showing 100% concordance with RT-qPCR for AR-FL and 92.3% for YAP1. Dual-well LoC detection of YAP1 and AR-FL was 100% concordant with benchtop assays, with slightly slower times to positive (e.g., 10.5 min for YAP1 in sample P4). YAP1 nucleic acid presence correlated with higher cancer stage (p = 0.043) and higher initial PSA (p = 0.035). AR-FL mRNA and AR-V7 mRNA were detected only in high-risk or metastatic patients (P4 and P12), within approximately 8 and 12.6 min respectively on the LoC. The authors state this is the first ISFET biosensor detecting endogenous circulating nucleic acids from cancer patient blood and the first handheld biosensor for circulating mRNA PCa prognosis, though TRIzol extraction currently limits point-of-care use and larger patient cohorts are needed.

Mark Schroeder replied to Steven Kean regarding a McKinsey memorandum (December 6, 2000) providing a periodic update on international electric power sector privatization and restructuring from June to November 2000. Schroeder noted errors in the EU summary: the Spanish pool is not mandatory, Denmark has more than two generators, the Netherlands' transitional anti-competitive arrangements were not addressed, and Poland—the most progressive former Communist country—was omitted from the Central and Eastern Europe discussion.

The memorandum, prepared by Carol B White and Pru Sheppard, reports that governments worldwide are opening generation markets to foreign investors, unbundling state utilities, and introducing wholesale and retail competition. In Europe, competition has been spurred by the EU Directive, with country-specific updates for Austria, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the UK. Central and Eastern European countries, many seeking EU membership, continue privatization initiatives, including Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Moldova, Romania, Russia, the Slovak Republic, Turkey, and Ukraine. As Asian economies recover, unbundling and restructuring plans are advancing in Australia, China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, New Zealand, Pakistan, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, and Vietnam. In Latin America, privatizations are restarting at a slower pace following currency devaluations, with updates covering Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Jamaica, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, Trinidad and Tobago, Venezuela, and the Virgin Islands. African and Middle Eastern governments are increasingly opening their power sectors to foreign investment, with regional transmission link schemes noted across Algeria, Ghana, Morocco, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa, Egypt, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Tunisia, and the UAE.

Police arrested 37-year-old Jason A. Clifford after he allegedly forced his way into a southeast Portland apartment while armed with a slungshot. Witnesses reported him threatening to kill people. He was booked into Multnomah County Jail on charges including first-degree burglary. Two others in the apartment were arrested on outstanding warrants.

Compass Minerals International, acquired by Apollo Management from IMC Global in 2001, completed its IPO on December 12, 2003, with Goldman Sachs leading. CEO Michael Ducey considered how to meet investor expectations as a stand-alone salt company. The case reviews the salt industry: salt is produced through rock salt mining, mechanical (vacuum pan) evaporation, and solar evaporation, which differ in cost and purity. In the United States, salt is used mainly for highway deicing (about one-third of consumption), as well as in chemicals, food processing, water treatment, and agriculture. Production has grown substantially since 1900, and the industry has consolidated; by the early 2000s, 29 firms operated 66 dry salt establishments. Production is capital intensive, and high transportation costs relative to salt's price make plant location important. Growing road salt use has caused freshwater salinization, suggesting possible future regulation, though road salt was not currently regulated in the US. Compass Minerals' subsidiary North American Salt was the third largest US salt producer, with just over 50% of salt revenue from general trade salt and about 40% from highway deicing, operating facilities in the US, Canada, and the UK. Ducey weighed regulatory threats against salt's few substitutes and emerging uses such as storage, as he sought to deliver the performance investors expected.

In his sixth and final State of the Union address, the President reflects on continuing national problems—urban unrest, poverty, Vietnam, the Middle East, and nuclear dangers—while citing national strengths, including the economy, democratic system, and the Apollo 8 flight. He reviews five years of achievements: Medicare, voting rights, federal school aid, Head Start, land conservation, job training for five million Americans, and unemployment at 3.3 percent with 8.5 million new jobs. He proposes increased model cities funding, 500,000 homes for needy families, an urban development bank, a 13 percent Social Security increase, medical care for expectant mothers and infants, continued antipoverty efforts, $3.5 billion for job training, enforcement of the Fair Housing Act, extension of the Voting Rights Act, $300 million under the Safe Streets Act, firearms licensing legislation, postal reorganization, and a draft lottery. He reports budget surpluses of $2.4 billion and $3.4 billion, record prosperity, and a balance of payments surplus. On foreign policy, he urges ratification of the nonproliferation treaty, resumed arms talks with the Soviet Union, continued foreign aid, support for European unity, peace efforts in Vietnam and the Middle East. He closes with personal reflections and asks Congress to support President-elect Nixon.

A study by Rand Corporation, Harvard Medical School, and UCLA found one in five Americans report a hostile or threatening workplace. Based on 2015 surveys of 3,066 workers, women reported unwanted sexual attention and young men reported verbal abuse. Four in five found their jobs meaningful, and over half described their boss as supportive.

This paper studies optimal pricing for a monopolist selling a single expiring item, such as an event ticket, to strategic buyers who arrive stochastically over a finite horizon. Because the item becomes worthless at expiration, the seller is time-sensitive, while buyers are temporally neutral and face a trade-off between waiting for lower prices and the risk of stockout from competing buyers. The problem is formulated as a Stackelberg game in which the seller commits to a pricing schedule and buyers, whose private types are two-dimensional (valuation and arrival time), choose purchase times.

The paper makes two main contributions. First, it introduces Value-Based Threshold strategies, which map buyer valuations to target purchase times, and establishes necessary and sufficient conditions to formally prove the existence and uniqueness of buyer equilibrium in a continuous valuation setting, extending prior work limited to discrete valuations. Second, it derives near-optimal pricing schedules for two stylized regimes: in thin markets with infrequent arrivals, a constant price is optimal because it removes buyers' incentive to delay; in thick markets with frequent arrivals, a linear discounting schedule is optimal because preemption risk makes buyers behave myopically. Numerical simulations confirm the near-optimality of these policies and show that the optimal schedule shifts from end-loaded, to flat, to front-loaded discounting as the seller's time sensitivity increases.

European shares rallied Monday after US-North Korea tensions caused their worst weekly losses of the year. The STOXX 600 rose 0.7 percent, with banks leading gains. RWE jumped 3 percent after targeting the top of its 2017 profit forecast, while Danone gained on bid speculation and Ladbrokes Coral fell.

The toss play is a football run play in which the quarterback tosses the ball to a running back attacking the edge of the defense. Its strengths include being simple to teach and install, quickly getting the ball to the perimeter, and consistently gaining yardage with the right personnel—namely a fast tailback and an athletic offensive line. Its main weaknesses are dependence on speed and susceptibility to edge blitzes. The passage outlines blocking assignments against 3-4 and 4-3 fronts, plus two variations: the Flexbone (Rocket) Toss and the Single Back Toss with a pulling guard as lead blocker.

On December 4, 2019, Microsoft Corporation held its 2019 Annual Shareholders Meeting, as reported in this Form 8-K. Of 7,632,138,696 shares entitled to vote, 6,610,123,128 were voted in person or by proxy. Shareholders elected all thirteen director nominees, approved on an advisory basis the compensation of named executive officers (76.69% for), and ratified Deloitte & Touche LLP as the independent registered public accounting firm for fiscal year 2020 (96.48% for). Two shareholder proposals were rejected: one concerning a report on employee representation on the Board of Directors (4.42% for) and one concerning a report on the gender pay gap (29.55% for). The report was signed on December 5, 2019 by Keith R. Dolliver, Assistant Secretary.

The speaker says the opponent is playing the neutral zone differently, acknowledges the powerplay struggled in the last game, and states they will review video and try a different strategy to get back into the series.

Tesla, Inc.'s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2016 describes the company's design, manufacture, and sale of fully electric vehicles—the Model S sedan and Model X SUV, with the lower-priced Model 3 planned for volume production and deliveries in the second half of 2017—along with energy storage products (the 14 kWh Powerwall 2 and 200 kWh Powerpack 2, whose second generation entered production in the fourth quarter of 2016) and solar energy systems following the November 21, 2016 acquisition of SolarCity. Tesla operates as two reportable segments, automotive and energy generation and storage, and manufactures vehicles at facilities in Fremont and Lathrop, California, and Tilburg, Netherlands, with battery cells and energy storage products produced at Gigafactory 1 near Reno, Nevada, and solar products at Gigafactory 2 in Buffalo, New York. The company partners with Panasonic for battery cell and photovoltaic cell production and sells vehicles directly through company-owned stores, supported by 790 Supercharger stations worldwide as of December 31, 2016. Tesla had 17,782 full-time employees and SolarCity had 12,243. The report identifies risks including production and launch delays, dependence on single-source suppliers, reliance on consumer adoption of electric vehicles, execution challenges at Gigafactory 1, lithium-ion battery safety concerns, material cost increases, product liability exposure, and competition from established automakers such as BMW, Daimler, General Motors, and Toyota.

Diane David appeals the judgment dissolving her marriage to Joseph David, contending the trial court erred in awarding Joseph, the noncustodial parent, the marital residence, in failing to divide the property equally as both parties requested, and in failing to consider the tax consequences of liquidating the retirement funds awarded to her. The Missouri Court of Appeals, Western District, found no error on the briefed issues but remanded the case because of a mathematical error: the trial court listed Diane's assets as $62,781.00 when the correct figure was $59,182.00.

The Davids married in 1980, lived in Moberly, Missouri, and had two daughters. They separated in April 1995 after an incident in which Joseph broke a glass gun cabinet. The parties stipulated to joint legal custody, with Diane having primary physical custody and Joseph paying $710.00 monthly child support. The trial court awarded Joseph the farm, equipment, truck, cattle, and household goods in his possession; Diane received Joseph's pension and 401(k), her personal property, and $3,500.00 toward attorney fees, with Joseph paying all marital debt. The court declined to enter an equalizing judgment, citing Diane's $27,130.02 separate teacher retirement account.

On appeal, the court held that § 452.330 does not require awarding the marital residence to the custodial parent and found no abuse of discretion in awarding the farm to Joseph. It found no binding stipulation to an equal division and distinguished Mallams because Diane could draw social security based on Joseph's earnings. The tax-consequence claim, raised for the first time on appeal, was denied. The judgment was vacated and the case remanded for reconsideration of the property distribution.

The Red Cross Society of Ghana has appealed to the government and public for ambulances, saying it has personnel to operate them. Its only ambulance, donated by the Chinese Red Cross, has broken down due to an engine fault. The World Bank funded nine first aid posts on major highways. Ghana's 29 million people share 55 functioning ambulances, and the government has promised to procure 275 ambulances.

A hockey team representative discusses playoff performance, noting improvement in limiting power plays after facing seven or eight per game against New Jersey in the first series. Playoffs are described as a battle of attrition, with the coach credited for keeping the team focused on one game at a time. The speaker emphasizes tightening defense, creating traffic in front of the opposing goalie, and maintaining internal belief in the team. The passage ends with joking remarks about "stealing" the game puck.

A hockey player discusses the Stanley Cup Finals, noting the long wait to reach this point. He stresses the need for discipline, staying out of the penalty box, and improving the power play. He mentions adjusting to travel and time zone changes, praises his linemates Krejci and Lucic, and calls the opponent the NHL's best team. His strategy is to play hard every night, be patient, protect the puck, and avoid giving the talented opponent easy scoring chances.

The passage is from the Texas Instruments data manual for the TMS320DM8127 DaVinci Digital Media Processor. It describes the C674x DSP core, a floating-point DSP code-compatible with C64x and C67x generations, featuring 32KB L1 program/data memory and 256KB L2 RAM with ECC. The device also includes an ARM Cortex-A8 subsystem with NEON SIMD, VFPv3 floating-point coprocessor, and a 32KB Embedded Trace Buffer. All C674x MDMA accesses are routed through a system MMU. The document covers modules including the Media Controller, HDVICP2 video codec accelerator (supporting MPEG, H.264, VC-1, and other standards), Face Detection, Spinlock (128 hardware semaphores), and Mailbox for inter-processor communication. It includes revision history from SPRS712A through SPRS712C, memory maps (L3/L4), and extensive pin maps and terminal functions for peripherals such as GPMC, HDMI, I2C, McASP, PCIe, GPIO, DDR2/DDR3, EMAC, SPI, UART, USB, and video interfaces.

This email chain from Enron (November 29, 2000) forwards a class action complaint filed in San Diego County Superior Court by Pamela R. Gordon, an SDG&E customer, on behalf of herself and similarly situated electricity customers against Reliant Energy, Southern Company, NRG Energy, Dynegy, AES Corporation, Williams Energy, and Duke Energy North America. The complaint alleges that beginning May 22, 2000, the defendants manipulated the California wholesale electricity market by improperly using confidential real-time generator and transmission data obtained through the WSCC, withholding generating capacity from forward markets, parking power with out-of-state affiliates for resale at inflated prices, and scheduling unplanned outages. It cites FERC and CPUC findings that prices were "unjust and unreasonable" and that customers were overcharged more than $4 billion during summer 2000, resulting in roughly tripled SDG&E rates. The suit asserts causes of action under California's Cartwright Act, unfair competition laws, the Consumers Legal Remedies Act, and unconscionability, seeking class certification, treble damages, restitution, disgorgement of profits, and injunctive relief on behalf of approximately 1.2 million SDG&E customers.

The May 22, 2001 VentureWire newsletter sent to Jeff Dasovic at Enron covers venture capital and technology industry news.

Top stories: Kodiak Venture Partners closed its second fund with $290 million, above its $250 million target, focusing on communications, semiconductors, and software in eastern North America. Mercury Interactive acquired Freshwater Software for $147 million in cash. Celetron International closed a $48 million first round led by New Enterprise Associates. Techno Venture Management announced the first close of its TVM V Life Science Ventures fund at EUR 70 million ($61 million), targeting $219 million, and is also raising a $219 million information technology fund.

Features note Lucent Venture Partners is investing from its third fund at a slower pace; iCelerate closed new funding and is seeking acquisitions; and instant messaging firm Odigo is seeking partnerships and predicts profitability next year.

Funding rounds include: CGtime ($7M Series A), MotionPoint ($400K seed), Lawson Software ($40M first round led by TA Associates), NetContinuum ($26M second round), Spinbox ($2.4M seed), Danger ($11M Series A), FlightTime ($25M Series B), Inventel Systemes ($5.3M first round), Cambridge Broadband ($15M second round), Lazy Software ($8.6M first round), Proteus (undisclosed Series A from Lycos Ventures), NuVasive ($29.3M Series D), Celvibe ($2M additional), MiFund ($25M Series B), ViAir ($15M second round), Reinhardt (funding from JBWere), SeeCommerce ($27M Series E), Zinio Systems ($5M Series B led by NEA), Akio Solutions ($3M), Antrim Design Systems ($11M Series D), and NewMarkets ($7.5M in Series F commitments).

Bad news: AgWeb.com cut 20 employees (36% of staff); Ironmax laid off about 30% of staff; Rx.com ceased operations and is no longer filling prescriptions.

New products: AuctioNet.com changed its name to Realm Connect; Nextira Federal launched.

M&A: Blink.com acquired rival BookmarksPlus; everstream acquired AdAcoustics and The MusicBooth in a $10 million all-stock deal; Primus acquired AnswerLogic for roughly $3 million in stock; MindArrow Systems agreed to acquire Control Commerce in an undisclosed all-stock deal.

New directors: John Gibson joined iVita's board; Armando Geday joined Chameleon Systems' board.

Personnel changes: Colorado MicroDisplay renamed itself Zight with management shifts; Icarian appointed Ed Koepfler president and CEO; Viator promoted Jan Knox to president; IKANO appointed Garth Howard president and COO; MRM Fulfillment appointed Antony Francis president and CEO; DigitalMoJo named Thomas Joseph chairman and CEO; Digi-Block hired Bill Rosenthal as CEO.

VC news: The University of Pittsburgh and Redleaf Group formed Oak Leaf Networks to fund regional start-ups; Baroness Sarah Hogg will become 3i's non-executive chairman in January; Dekkers Davidson joined Charles River Ventures as executive in residence; Growth Capital appointed Richard Bidgood executive vice president. Corrections noted that Broadview Capital Partners, not Broadview Associates, backs Red Herring, and that a Porivo Technologies item contained editing errors.

Three members of George Washington University's Alpha Phi sorority chapter are having their memberships terminated after a photo showing two members, one holding a banana peel with a caption reading "I'm 1/16 black," circulated on social media. The chapter apologized on Facebook, citing issues with privilege and lack of diversity. Student Association senator Imani Ross tweeted the photo, and university administrators began investigating. Provost Forrest Maltzman called the image disturbing and hurtful. Alpha Phi International has not yet responded to requests for comment.

A new partnership, Create Sheffield – Adventures in Cultural Education, will bring together education, arts, culture and voluntary sector organisations to ensure every child and young person up to age 25 in Sheffield experiences arts and culture. The partnership aims to improve school attainment and employability, amid concerns that arts subjects are being squeezed out by Sats targets, league tables and the EBacc measure. Its proposals include creating a list of local experiences and a platform for learning resources, plus an initiative developing young makers. Membership begins in September, with fees of £125 to £5,000 per year depending on organisation size.

Oregon's public schools have among the nation's lowest graduation rates, with one in four students not graduating within four years, and also rank near the bottom in instructional days—about 165 per year versus a national average of 180. Oregon Board of Education member Kim Sordyl, the only board member who responded to KGW, believes reduced instructional time contributes to low graduation rates and wants the legislature and governor to add school days. State Representative Diego Hernandez, a member of the newly formed Joint Subcommittee on Student Success, said no legislative studies have been done and argues other factors, such as classroom supports, must be considered. A parent who moved to Washington cited smaller classes and a longer school year; Washington students receive 15 more instructional days annually, equaling an extra school year over 12 years. Tualatin High School, with graduation rates in the mid-90th percentile, emphasizes attendance and instructional time.

Vladimir Putin has won a fourth term as Russia's president, positioning him to entrench power, pursue an expansive foreign policy, and continue tensions with the West. A less-noticed goal is developing a post-Soviet national ideology, as Russia's identity has become tied to Putin's persona amid a stagnating economy and earlier promises of prosperity that rang hollow after oil prices fell in 2014. Over the next six years, the government aims to codify an alternative worldview for domestic and international audiences. The writer argues the West should call out the vision's hollowness and uphold a more positive set of ideals, as it did in winning the Cold War's competition of ideas.

A preliminary USGS study estimates Tropical Storm Nate could erode 70 percent of sandy beaches from the Florida Panhandle to southeast Louisiana and destroy about half of protective dunes. Over 90 percent of Louisiana beaches are likely to erode.

The speaker attributes his team's playoff struggles against New Jersey to poor puck management and turnovers in the neutral zone, while also crediting the Devils as a strong defensive team that limits shots. He notes his team has not executed the style that brought earlier playoff success, failing to sustain offensive cycles or generate quality scoring chances. He praises the Devils' goaltender, emphasizes respect for the opponent, and dismisses suggestions that frustration, fights, or trash talk are factors. Returning home to Anaheim offers advantages such as last change and line matchups. He is focused only on the next game, stressing the need to capitalize on opportunities and eliminate opponents' chances. He also reflects on the team's turnaround over the past year and its benefit to hockey in the area.

The article examines whether copper is a reliable leading indicator for stocks. Because copper is used across nearly all economic sectors, rising prices are often seen as a sign of economic growth, while falling prices may signal a slowdown. The authors developed a copper vs. stocks trading strategy—buying SPY for the following week when copper's last four-week return was positive—and backtested it using SPY data since 2000. The strategy performed decently with smaller drawdowns than Buy & Hold, but was inactive for a long period between 2008 and 2016, when copper fell over 50% while stocks continued rising. Correlation between copper's past returns and SPY's future returns was weak, especially from 2011 to 2016. The authors conclude that copper is likely not a reliable leading indicator for stocks, and the strategy's performance may be due to luck, though copper may be more useful for predicting business cycles.

NVIDIA Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended July 31, 2016 (Q2 fiscal 2017) reports revenue of $1,428 million, up 24% from $1,153 million a year earlier, with net income of $253 million ($0.40 per diluted share) compared to $26 million ($0.05) in the prior-year quarter. Six-month revenue was $2,733 million versus $2,304 million, and net income was $449 million versus $160 million. Gross margin was 57.9% versus 55.0% a year earlier.

NVIDIA reports two segments: GPU and Tegra Processor. GPU revenue was $1,196 million (up 25%), driven by GeForce gaming products, datacenter revenue up 110% on deep learning demand, and Quadro professional visualization up 22%. Tegra Processor revenue was $166 million (up 30%), driven by automotive systems up 68%. Revenue by market: Gaming $781 million, Professional Visualization $214 million, Datacenter $151 million, Automotive $119 million, and OEM & IP $163 million. Taiwan was the largest geographic revenue source at $505 million, followed by China ($256 million) and the United States ($206 million).

Operating expenses were $509 million, down 9% year over year, primarily because the prior-year quarter included $89 million in restructuring charges related to the Icera wind-down. The effective tax rate was 20.3% versus 64.0%, mainly due to the absence of prior-year tax-related restructuring charges and the U.S. federal research tax credit.

As of July 31, 2016, NVIDIA held $4.88 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities. During the first half of fiscal 2017, the company paid $509 million for share repurchases—including an accelerated share repurchase of 12 million shares settled in July 2016—and $124 million in dividends ($0.1150 per share). The $1.50 billion 1.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2018 remained convertible and were classified as a current liability at a $1,428 million carrying value.

Legal matters included a June 2016 settlement with Samsung resolving all intellectual property disputes, termination of claims against Qualcomm, and a resolution with Advanced Silicon Technologies resulting in a $10 million charge to cost of revenue. A $26 million charge had been recorded for the SHIELD tablet recall.

NVIDIA is constructing a new Santa Clara headquarters under an off-balance-sheet build-to-suit operating lease, with banks committed to fund up to $380 million. During the quarter, the company began shipping Pascal-architecture gaming GPUs (GTX 1080, 1070, 1060, TITAN X) and introduced Tesla P100 accelerators and the DGX-1 deep learning system. 535 million common shares were outstanding as of August 19, 2016.

EON Resources Inc. held a special conference call to discuss $45.5 million in funding and a related Farmout Agreement. Participants included CEO Dante Caravaggio, CFO Mitchell Trotter, VP of Operations Jesse Allen, and General Counsel David Smith. Host Michael Porter read a forward-looking statements disclaimer before Caravaggio began remarks, noting he was calling from an airport.

Coach Quenneville said his team had a perfect start but lost the pace and momentum in the second period, standing around while the opponent countered. He praised his goaltender for keeping the team in the game with strong overtime saves. He said Johnny had a solid, well-deserved year offensively and defensively while playing against top lines, and described another player as having elite conditioning, able to sustain big minutes without fatigue. He noted that winning the Cup requires playing through physical tolls such as ice bags and hot packs. After six periods, he felt they had a good assessment of the opponent and became more comfortable with line rotations resembling those of the regular season. He stressed improving from game to game, maintaining momentum and home ice, and credited an even-keeled locker room following emotional wins over Detroit and LA. He expected a low-scoring series given Boston's shutdown of Pittsburgh, and said minutes would be delegated based on how each game goes.

The President transmits to Congress dispatches from the governor of Maine and related correspondence concerning a band of lawless men, chiefly from the adjoining British Provinces but without provincial sanction, who cut and destroyed timber in the disputed Aroostook territory claimed by Maine. Maine's land agent, dispatched to arrest the depredations, was seized by trespassers and taken as a prisoner to Frederickton, New Brunswick, along with two other citizens, and the State authorized an armed posse to disperse the trespassers and protect public property. The lieutenant-governor of New Brunswick demanded the recall of Maine's armed party, and the British minister made a similar demand on the United States, both assuming an agreement existed granting Britain exclusive possession and jurisdiction over the disputed territory pending boundary settlement. The President states that the correspondence disproves any such agreement, showing the two governments differed over title, jurisdiction, and its actual exercise. Both sides had previously exercised forbearance—Maine and Massachusetts suspending land sales and a military road, Britain suspending timber licenses and a railroad survey. The President affirms Maine's right to arrest the depredations but distinguishes this from military occupation of the territory. He will pursue only amicable means of settlement, potentially through arbitration or reference to a third power, and will not employ federal military force to aid Maine, though a military occupation by New Brunswick would be regarded as invasion entitling the State to federal aid. He expects the arrested agents' release, recommends Maine peaceably disband its militia, and invites Congress to consider measures to avoid an extra session.

The passage reports serious medical problems among participants receiving BNT162b2 or BNT162b2SA. In Phase 1, 2 participants (4% each) in the BNT162b2 20-µg and 30-µg groups had serious problems (inflamed appendix, inflamed nerves), not believed vaccine-related; no BNT162b1 or placebo participants had serious problems. In Phase 2/3 after two doses, few serious problems occurred, none affecting at least 1% of any group. Participants aged 12–15 had no vaccine-related serious problems. Among those 16 and older, some serious problems (numbness or tingling, portal vein blockage, mini stroke) were considered possibly vaccine-related. With BNT162b2SA, 4 of 324 participants (1%) had serious problems, not considered vaccine-related. After booster doses in Phase 3, no serious problem occurred in more than 1 participant, and none were believed vaccine-related. For the 30-µg booster in Phase 2/3, 65 of 22,470 participants (under 1%) had serious problems, 2 possibly vaccine-related. One participant had a serious problem after an additional booster, not believed vaccine-related.

Since 1950, the S&P 500 has set 1,526 all-time highs, averaging just under 21 per year, or about 8.3% of trading days, while compounding at 7.67% annually (excluding dividends). The longest streak of consecutive years with at least one all-time high was twelve (1989–2000). All-time highs typically signal strong earnings, momentum, and bullish sentiment, though in high-inflation countries markets may reach nominal highs while declining in inflation-adjusted terms. The article backtests a strategy of buying the S&P 500 when within 5% of its all-time high and selling when it falls more than 5% below. The strategy produced a 3.20% CAGR, was invested 43.2% of the time, and had a 33.75% maximum drawdown; earning a return on idle cash substantially improved results.

The passage presents three free mean reversion trading strategies and explains the concept of mean reversion, where asset prices gravitate above and below a moving average, with abnormal rises and falls tending to revert. Mean reversion is contrasted with trend following: it typically has a high win ratio with many small winners and occasional large losers, while trend following relies on rare big winners. Mean reversion works best in stocks and is less effective in markets like commodities, possibly due to the rise of futures trading since the 1990s and the constant battle between buyers and sellers. Contrary to common belief, the authors state that mean reversion performs best during bear markets because of increased volatility and explosive bear-market rallies; during 2008/09, long positions were more profitable than short ones despite the market falling over 50%. The three strategies are: (1) deviation from a recent high in the consumer staples ETF XLP, published in 2013; (2) an IBS short strategy in the Chinese ETF FXI; and (3) a 5-day low strategy in the S&P 500, published in 2012. Equity curves and performance results are provided, and Amibroker or Tradestation code for the strategies is available for purchase.

This patent disclosure relates to a respiratory mask system for delivering respiratory therapies such as CPAP and NIV to patients. The system comprises a mask interface (a seal and frame assembly) and a headgear assembly connected via various connection systems. The frame includes a gas inlet (optionally angled 10–45 degrees from vertical and substantially elliptical) and an outlet vent, which may contain a diffuser. A seal attaches to the frame via a seal flange, using clips or a lip-and-channel arrangement. The frame features a recessed channel for receiving a yoke of the headgear assembly, with attachment features including apertures, magnets, tabs, latches, retention bumps and notches, anti-rotation grooves, and protrusions/recesses. The yoke may serve as a collector for filaments in an automatically adjustable headgear system incorporating washer mechanisms, and may be covered in a stretchable textile. Nasal seal configurations specify dimensions such as bridge depth, wall thicknesses, overall width, height, and sealing area, and may include a clip assembly defining an inlet and vent. The headgear comprises rear, upper, and front straps connected to the yoke via strap connectors. The disclosure includes a brief description of numerous figures (Figs. 1–150) illustrating mask assemblies, frames, seals, yokes, and connection methods, followed by a detailed description of embodiments.

The Federal Government will release N750 billion this week to Ministries, Departments and Agencies for 2017 Budget capital projects, bringing this year's total capital release to N1.2 trillion. Finance Minister Kemi Adeosun announced this while receiving a delegation of 30 French firms interested in investing in sectors including banking, infrastructure, agriculture and renewable energy, with plans to form partnerships with Nigerian counterparts.

This patent application describes systems and methods for high-speed data communications networks in buildings incorporating optically switchable (electrochromic) windows. The disclosed networks use trunk line segments (coaxial cables or twisted pairs) coupled by passive circuits such as bias T circuits and directional couplers to form daisy chain topologies, supporting data transmission rates exceeding 1 Gbps along with power signals. These networks connect control panels, window controllers, and devices including IoT devices, sensors, antennas, and 5G equipment.

The application describes digital architectural elements (DAEs) installable on building structural elements such as mullions, walls, and doors. DAEs may contain sensors (cameras, microphones, air quality, temperature, proximity), processors, network interfaces, speakers, displays, Wi-Fi access points, and power sources. Digital wall interfaces are similar wall-mounted devices installed after construction. Enhanced functionality window controllers (WC3) add gigabit Ethernet, Wi-Fi, and optional MoCA interfaces to conventional window controllers.

Applications include environmental monitoring and control (adjusting HVAC and lighting based on occupancy and air quality data), security functions (asset tracking, sound detection, gunshot localization via distinctive window tinting), noise cancellation, video streaming, biometric recognition, personal digital assistant integration, and occupant comfort management. Machine learning may be employed to analyze sensor data and control building operation parameters.

Patanjali, Ramdev's company, launched the "Kimbho" messaging app on Wednesday as a challenge to WhatsApp, but the app is no longer available on Google Play Store, though it remains on the iOS App Store and accessible to those who downloaded it. An analyst noted only around 5,000 installations with reviews citing issues. "Kimbho," Sanskrit for "How are you? What's new?", offers messaging, group chats, broadcast lists, and free calling. The launch follows Patanjali's Swadeshi Samriddhi SIM cards with BSNL, which offer a 10 percent discount on Patanjali products.

Minister Schoenfeld reported that Finnish Foreign Minister Witting attributed Finland's 1940 acceptance of the German transit agreement to the failed Finnish-Swedish defense talks and Soviet objection, and said Germany knew of Russian preparations to attack Finland. Witting stated Finnish front activity stemmed from costly Soviet offensives and that Finland, dependent on German goodwill for supplies, could not control German actions affecting supply passage to Russia. Schoenfeld concluded Finns would not voluntarily act against anti-Axis forces but expected military necessity to preclude peace with the USSR, and that Sweden could not successfully exert influence. In a subsequent telegram, Schoenfeld reported his Swedish colleague Westman saw no prospect of a Finnish-Russian understanding, declined to approach Witting for fear of German reprisals against Sweden, and noted Finnish circulation of a book justifying annexation of Soviet territory.

A study published in Nature Astronomy found foul-smelling hydrogen sulfide in Uranus's cloud tops by analyzing light captured by the Gemini North telescope. Authored by Caltech, Oxford, and Leicester scientists, it is the best proof yet of the gas and may shed light on Uranus's formation.

A player expressed excitement for Manny's return after a difficult period, stressed staying balanced after a playoff win and focusing on the next game in Boston, recalled his first NHL shutout against the Bruins, and described being ready for Hank's play in front of the net.

This study examined associations between unintended pregnancy and children's psychosocial problems through adolescence, and the indirect role of maternal mental health and bonding, using the Amsterdam Born Children and their Development birth cohort (n = 7,784). Pregnancy intentions were measured multidimensionally (mistiming, unwantedness, unhappiness), and children's problems were assessed with the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire at ages 5-6, 11-12, and 15-16, using structural equation modeling with controls for co-occurring risks. At preschool age, mistiming predicted both internalizing and externalizing problems, and unwantedness predicted internalizing problems, with small effect sizes; unhappiness was not significant. No dimension of unintended pregnancy was associated with children's problems in early or middle adolescence, a pattern also found in secondary analyses using child-reported outcomes. Mediation analyses at preschool age showed maternal bonding problems mediated associations for all three pregnancy dimensions, while maternal psychosocial distress mediated only the mistiming association; direct effects of mistiming and unwantedness on internalizing problems remained. The authors attribute differences from prior studies to the abortion-liberal Dutch context, multidimensional measurement of pregnancy intentions, and control of co-occurring risks. They conclude that maternal mental health and bonding, rather than pregnancy unintendedness itself, are key targets for reducing children's psychosocial problems.

The Bengals acquired quarterback Joe Flacco from the Browns in a trade announced Tuesday, receiving a sixth-round pick while sending a fifth-round pick to Cleveland. The move comes as Cincinnati seeks quarterback help with Joe Burrow on injured reserve after toe surgery, expected to sideline him at least three months. Replacement Jake Browning has thrown eight interceptions over parts of four games during the Bengals' (2-3) three-game losing streak, in which they were outscored 113-37. Flacco, 40, started Cleveland's first four games this season, completing 58.1% of his passes for 815 yards, two touchdowns and six interceptions. He won the 2023 AP Comeback Player of the Year with the Browns. His departure could elevate Shedeur Sanders to the No. 2 quarterback spot behind Dillon Gabriel in Cleveland.

The passage describes a patent application for a display device having a through portion (through hole) that passes through a substrate. The device includes a pixel array surrounding the through portion, scan lines extending in a first direction, and data lines extending in a second direction. Data lines adjacent the through portion are located at different layers and are at least partially curved along the perimeter of the through portion, enabling them to deliver data signals to pixels on opposite sides of the hole. Because the curved data lines are alternately placed in different layers, the pitch between them is reduced, which shrinks the first non-display area surrounding the through hole. Embodiments may include a thin film encapsulation layer with stacked inorganic and organic layers, a dam that prevents organic material from flowing toward the through hole, and a contact portion where the first and second inorganic layers directly contact each other to reduce moisture penetration. Some embodiments place curved data lines in the same layers as existing electrodes (source/drain electrodes, storage capacitor electrodes, or pixel electrodes) to reduce the number of manufacturing masks, and cover them with inorganic passivation layers or passivation layers containing organic-inorganic composite particles to preserve moisture barrier performance. Applications include mobile phones (camera or button in the hole), smart watches (a driving part with hands), and vehicle dashboards (driving parts indicating RPM and velocity).

The speaker, addressing the University of Michigan graduating class, describes his vision of the "Great Society"—a society resting on abundance and liberty for all, demanding an end to poverty and racial injustice. He identifies three places to begin building it: cities, countryside, and classrooms. Urban populations will double, requiring the rebuilding of cities that suffer from decay, housing and transportation shortages, and eroded community values. In the countryside, pollution threatens water, food, and air, while parks are overcrowded and green spaces disappearing. In education, millions of Americans lack basic schooling, classrooms are overcrowded, teachers are underpaid or unqualified, and over 100,000 capable high school graduates annually cannot afford college. The speaker promises White House conferences on these challenges and advocates "creative federalism"—cooperation between the national government and local communities. He calls on graduates to join the battle to build the Great Society.
