A coach reviews his team's playoff game against Buffalo, saying his side played two strong periods but became conservative in the third while protecting a lead, which allowed Buffalo to get back into a game that went to overtime. He says Buffalo's goaltender, Hasek, had an easy night facing mostly first shots, and his team must create second and third chances and control critical areas such as the front of the net, the slot, and the boards. He calls the matchup one between the league's two best teams at contesting blue lines, expects a long, competitive series, and notes Buffalo hangs in fights longer and has scoring depth beyond its top lines, including players like Stu Barnes and Primeau. He is satisfied with the power play's chances despite not scoring, acknowledges Buffalo won more loose-puck battles off faceoffs, and dismisses a cheating remark about Skrudland as a personal jab from Lindy. He announces lineup changes, with Hrkac and Plante ready to play, and says the team must sustain its intensity for a full game. He adds that the group pulls tighter through adversity and that he is focused on enjoying the moment rather than pressure and expectations.

The Box and One is a combination defense in which four defenders play a box zone while a fifth, the Chaser, denies their assigned opponent the ball and rebounds. Baseline defenders X4 and X5 shift like a 1-2-2 zone, while outside defenders X1 and X2 shift like a 2-3 zone. Against an even front offense, X3 denies the star player as X1 pushes the ball handler to the opposite side, with rotations occurring on passes to the wing, corner, and skip passes. Against an odd front, similar rotations occur, with X1 dropping to the free throw line against the high post. The chaser's strong denial keeps the ball from the opponent's star scorer and disrupts set plays.

The article demonstrates how to backtest a simple trading strategy in Python, noting that Python is the most popular programming language in finance and is intuitive to learn. The authors use pandas for data manipulation, yfinance to download SPY historical data from Yahoo Finance since 1993, and matplotlib for plotting results. The strategy's rules require the close price to be above both a simple moving average and an exponential moving average, calculated with pandas functions. Trading signals are generated through a loop, with the signal applied to the following row since it triggers at the close. Returns are compounded only when the regime column equals 1. The strategy returned 804.82% versus 1505.31% for buy and hold, thus underperforming. The article concludes that backtesting requires no finance or computer science degree.

The passage describes AMD's Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) specification. Customers provide an RSA public key (2048 or 4096-bit) during early boot for SFS package verification, signing packages using RSA-PSS (SHA256 for 2048-bit keys, SHA384 for 4096-bit keys). Update packages can patch registers, replace firmware images, or update firmware portions. SEV updates commit automatically and prevent rollback; SNP-enabled systems require HV-FIXED pages via the RMPUPDATE command. Attestation data is requested via SPDM or DPE interfaces. Packages verify existing firmware and patch levels before applying; if any portion cannot apply, the update does not occur. Updates are non-persistent across reboots and may be applied during OS boot or system operation. Issuing SFS commands requires a 2MB-aligned TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER, with update packages placed at the buffer address plus 4k. The customer deployment agent creates the buffer, appends any co-signing header and signature along with the AMD-provided package, and communicates via the TEE mailbox. The ASP then verifies signatures, loads and runs the executable patch, updates patch level information, and returns status. The GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO command retrieves firmware versions and current patch levels. Packages are named according to AGESA releases (e.g., fam_19h-1006-SFS-1.pkg). Updates run in parallel with x86 and DMA traffic with minimal performance impact; SEV/SEV-ES virtual machines must restart for SEV firmware updates, while SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue operating.

Surfer Dane Gudauskas rode what may be the best wave of his life—a large left at Cloudbreak during the recent XXL swell in Fiji. In an interview afterward, he described lingering soreness and an intense adrenaline high. Despite challenging weather and strong winds, he went because big Fiji swells are rare. About 30 boats gathered, and surfers paced themselves while waiting for conditions. After seeing Shaun Lopez tow in, Gudauskas paddled out while no one else was surfing. He skipped two waves before catching a significant one, was ultimately wiped out, and broke his board. He rode his twin brother Patrick's 8'6" Channel Islands with quad fins, then switched to an 8'10" backup, feeling a board over 9 feet would have been better. Compared to his 2016 Cloudbreak wave, this one had far more energy and speed. He called it the most intense surf experience of his life—wild, raw, and untamed—and credited the water safety crews at Tavarua, Namotu, and the mainland. He now plans to simply enjoy surfing, possibly longboarding at San O.

Amazon.com, Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2022 reports Q3 net sales of $127.1 billion, up 15% year over year, and nine-month net sales of $364.8 billion, up 10%. Q3 net income was $2.9 billion ($0.28 diluted EPS), down from $3.2 billion a year earlier, while the nine-month result was a net loss of $3.0 billion, driven largely by a $10.4 billion valuation loss on the Rivian investment for the nine months (partially offset by a $1.1 billion gain in Q3). Operating income fell to $2.5 billion in Q3 from $4.9 billion. By segment: North America sales rose 20% to $78.8 billion with a $412 million operating loss; International sales fell 5% to $27.7 billion with a $2.5 billion operating loss; AWS sales rose 27% to $20.5 billion with $5.4 billion in operating income. The company effected a 20-for-1 stock split in May 2022 and repurchased $6.0 billion of common stock during the nine months under a $10 billion program authorized in March 2022. Effective January 2022, useful lives of servers were extended from four to five years and networking equipment from five to six years, reducing Q3 depreciation and amortization by $882 million. Amazon acquired MGM in March 2022 for approximately $6.1 billion and entered agreements to acquire One Medical (~$3.9 billion) and iRobot (~$1.7 billion). As of September 30, 2022, it had $62.5 billion of unsecured senior notes outstanding, $11.7 billion of commercial paper borrowings, and $58.7 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities. The filing also discloses legal and tax matters, including antitrust and patent litigation, a €1.13 billion Italian Competition Authority fine under appeal, and European Commission state aid proceedings involving Luxembourg.

Biocon India Group, founded in 1978 by Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw in Bangalore, grew from enzyme manufacturing into generic pharmaceuticals and contract research, guided by an "earn as you learn" philosophy. By early 2003, the firm had 800 employees and US$75 million in annual revenues. Its subsidiaries included Syngene, a contract research organization launched in 1994, and Clinigene, established in 2000 to offer clinical trial services. Mazumdar-Shaw faced a decision about Clinigene's future: while it filled a gap in Biocon's vision of becoming a fully integrated drug discovery and development company, it posed risks including diverting resources, disrupting the firm's collaborative culture, and attracting negative publicity over ethical concerns about conducting clinical trials in a developing country. Possible approaches included limiting Clinigene's scope to lower-value services or acquiring an external clinical services CRO.

Mr. Heard's dispatches to Mr. Gresham report on conditions in Seoul and the Tong Hâk movement. In the first, Heard states that after April 20 nothing disturbed Seoul's quiet; investigators sent to the southern provinces and arriving Catholic priests found no traces of Tong Hâk assemblages, though discontent over officials' exactions may cause recurring rumors. After conferring with Heard, the U.S.S. Alert left Chemulpo on April 29. In the second dispatch, Heard reports that thousands of Tong Hâk gathered at Po-eun in Ch'ung ch'ong Do, drilling and professing intent to march on Seoul under a flag reading "Down with the Japanese and foreigners!" The government sent 800 drilled men with three Gatling guns to bar the road. Though foreigners feared danger, Heard doubted active hostility, considering the Tong Hâk themselves peaceful—seeking their founder's rehabilitation and freedom to practice their tenets—but possibly controlled by an unidentified political party.

The Crude Oil Seasonality Strategy exploits the tendency for oil prices to rise on Fridays by buying on Thursday's close. It performs better when Thursday is a down day, specifically when USO falls at least 0.75 times the 25-day average of the high-low range. Historical data from April 2006 to the present shows a 56.96% profit/loss across 98 trades, with 60 winners and an average profit of 0.58% per trade.

The #HV doorbell page aligns with APIC behavior, defining PendingEvent (bytes 0..1) and NoEoiRequired (byte 2), with bytes 3..63 reserved. The page must be host-owned, and all guest accesses must use C=0.

On Aug. 6, Dylan Kennedy, 19, was ticketed for speeding, possession of less than half an ounce of marijuana, and drug paraphernalia after a traffic stop. On Aug. 5, Caton Preston, 18, was charged with possession of alcohol by a minor and third-degree forgery for producing a fake license. Police collected 75 pounds of unused prescription drugs for incineration. Three children received trespassing warrants, and a smashed mailbox is under investigation. Total calls: 204.

The ADS868xW is a family of single-channel, high-speed integrated data acquisition devices from Texas Instruments, combining a 16-bit SAR ADC with a power-optimized analog front-end (AFE). The devices support true bipolar differential and single-ended inputs up to ±12.288V on a single 5V analog supply and feature an enhanced SPI interface (multiSPI) that maximizes sampling rates even with slower host controllers.

Key features include input impedance of at least 1MΩ (independent of sampling rate), a programmable gain amplifier (PGA) supporting nine software-programmable unipolar and bipolar input ranges, a second-order low-pass antialiasing filter (typically 500kHz cutoff), an integrated ADC driver amplifier, and overvoltage protection up to ±20V. With the 4.096V reference, bipolar ranges include ±12.288V, ±10.24V, ±6.144V, ±5.12V, and ±2.56V; unipolar ranges include 0V to 12.288V, 0V to 10.24V, 0V to 6.144V, and 0V to 5.12V.

The device provides a factory-trimmed, temperature-compensated 4.096V internal reference (–40°C to +125°C) or an external reference option, selected via the INTREF_DIS bit. Alarm features include a user-programmable input alarm with hysteresis and a fixed-threshold AVDD alarm (4.7V/5.3V), with flags accessible via the ALARM pin, internal registers, or appended to output data.

The device operates in three states (RESET, ACQ, CONV) and supports legacy SPI-compatible protocols with single or dual SDO outputs, plus source-synchronous (SRC) protocols. Multiple devices can operate in a daisy-chain topology. Nine configuration registers control operation, with data transferred in 32-bit frames.

An application example shows an 8-channel industrial analog input module for PLCs combining the ADS8681W with the MUX36D08 multiplexer. The device offers NAP and power-down low-power modes, with recommended decoupling capacitors for supplies and reference pins.

Mali's gold exports are declining as its legacy mines wind down, and the future of the Sadiola mine—one of the country's largest—hangs in the balance. The mine requires a $380 million investment to access 3.4 million ounces of gold in hard-rock reserves and remain open for another decade, but negotiations with the government have stalled. Sadiola, a joint venture between IAMGOLD, AngloGold Ashanti, and the Government of Mali, has operated since 1997 and employs about 1,000 people, 93 percent of them Malian. With gold representing 25-30 percent of government revenues and elections approaching in 2018, the outcome of the stalled negotiations is viewed as a test of Mali's investment climate.

In this final annual message, the President reports that the nation is prosperous, with rapid population growth and a strong union. Foreign relations are generally friendly: the 1822 convention with France remains in force, though spoliation claims are unsettled; commerce with Britain continues under the 1815 convention, but West Indies trade and boundary issues remain unresolved, and a signed convention to suppress the slave trade is suspended pending Congress's view; a convention with Russia on the Northwest coast has been submitted to the Senate. Relations with the new Latin American states, including Brazil, are friendly, with a commercial treaty formed with Colombia. Treasury receipts will exceed $18.5 million, and the public debt, estimated at $79 million, may be discharged within ten years. The military and naval establishments are efficient; fortifications, road and canal surveys, and Indian schools are progressing. Piracy in the Gulf persists, attributed to weak local governments. General Lafayette's visit was warmly received, and provision for him is recommended. Greece's struggle and Spanish American independence command sympathy, while the United States maintains that European powers must not interfere in the affairs of its American neighbors. The President recommends Supreme Court reorganization, a plan for Indian civilization on western territory, a military post at the Columbia River, and improvements to the capital, closing with gratitude for public support.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for providing ground support to vertical takeoff aerial vehicles, such as multicopters, quadcopters, rocket-propelled vehicles, and multirotor drones. It presents mobile ground stations comprising a protective casing, at least one charging mechanism, and an extendable landing pad that transitions between a closed configuration contained within the casing and an open configuration suitable for landing. Optional features include an elevator mechanism for raising and lowering a base platform, a centering mechanism, conducting terminals for charging, power supplies such as solar panels, wind turbines, fuel cells, and electrochemical cells, homing aids including beacons and contrasting visual patterns, windbreakers, and a locking mechanism. Modular extensions may add weather station, transportation, carrying, communication, sensor, radar, or night vision functionality. Deploying multiple ground stations, coordinated by a control server, can extend the operating range of aerial vehicles and support continual operation with potentially no downtime.

NVIDIA RTX IO, working with Microsoft's DirectStorage API, enables GPU-based lossless decompression that improves game frame rates, enables near-instantaneous loading, reduces object pop-in and stutter, and shrinks download sizes, while also benefiting professional workloads such as CAD rendering and VR. It delivers 100X throughput and 20X lower CPU utilization by offloading decompression from the CPU to the GPU.

The NVIDIA A40, based on the GA10x Ampere architecture, is described as the most powerful data center GPU for visual computing, delivering up to 2X FP32, 2X ray-tracing, and 5X (10X with Sparsity) AI throughput versus the Quadro RTX 6000, with 48GB memory expandable to 96GB via NVLink, vGPU support, and EGX Platform compatibility.

Ampere GPUs support DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a and are the first discrete GPUs with HDMI 2.1, enabling 8K60 and 4K120 output. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1—the first GPU hardware AV1 decode—offering 50-55% bitrate savings over H.264 with very low CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC matches x264 Medium quality, encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

GA10x doubles programmable shading, ray tracing (second-gen RT Cores with motion blur support), and AI performance (third-gen Tensor Cores with sparsity), and is the first architecture to use GDDR6X, achieving 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec in the RTX 3090. The RTX 3090 (GA102, 24GB, 82 SMs, 10,496 CUDA cores) is 1.5x faster than TITAN RTX; the RTX 3070 (GA104, GDDR6) outperforms the RTX 2080 Ti. New Error Detection and Replay (EDR) technology detects and retries GDDR6X memory errors during overclocking, signaling when memory limits are reached. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU features 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 48GB GDDR6, expandable to 96GB via NVLink.

This study presents laboratory near-infrared (NIR) reflectance spectra of water ice, epsomite, and halite grain mixtures at cryogenic temperatures, conducted in anticipation of NASA's Europa Clipper and ESA's JUICE missions. Using the CRONOS facility—a nitrogen-purged glove box at Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory—the researchers prepared discrete grains in four size bins (<63 µm, 63–250 µm, 250–500 µm, >500 µm) and measured pure samples and 50%/50% volume mixtures at approximately 100–120 K. Spectra were compared against models generated with Hapke radiative transfer theory using both linear and intimate mixing approaches.

Water ice spectra were generally well matched by both linearly- and intimately-mixed models, with differences typically within ~10%, and no discernible difference was found between the two modeling approaches. Mixtures of halite and water ice were nearly indistinguishable from pure water ice, with halite's 1.95 µm adsorbed-water feature barely detectable. Fine-grained materials disproportionately influenced mixed spectra. Epsomite model fits were poor; the published "cryogenic" epsomite optical constants appear to have been taken at ambient conditions, making abundance retrievals using these data potentially unreliable.

The authors conclude that mixtures do not exhibit spectra halfway between their constituents, demonstrating the need for quantitative spectral mixture analysis rather than qualitative interpretation, and note a possible observational bias toward smaller grain sizes. A follow-on study will publish corrected epsomite optical constants.

A Uzbek court convicted Uzbek-born U.S. citizen Zokir Aliyev, 46, of publicly calling for the government's overthrow and participating in an extremist group, but imposed only a $67 fine based on the December 1999 minimum wage. Aliyev, detained June 16 and freed after six days, denies involvement with the Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan. The U.S. embassy declined comment.

The President responds to a Senate resolution seeking information about an alleged forcible resistance to the execution of US laws in Boston. He reports that an affidavit by deputy marshal Patrick Riley describes the incident; private communications support its main facts, but no official confirmation has been received and persons implicated deny some details. He condemns the act as a high-handed violation of law, attributing its success to surprise and some negligence rather than the general sentiment of Boston or Massachusetts. He reviews congressional resolutions of 1789, 1791, and 1821 regarding the detention of federal prisoners, and cites Massachusetts's 1843 act barring state officers and jails from fugitive slave cases, arguing that such state legislation cannot impair the federal constitutional duty to deliver persons held to labor. He notes the marshal was reminded of his authority to hire a jail and will be directed to do so if he has not. He transmits a proclamation, departmental instructions, and related correspondence. On possible legislation, he explains the President's constitutional command over the Army and Navy, the need for congressional authorization to call the militia, and the 1795 act's proclamation requirement, suggesting modifications to that act and the 1807 act so that military force may aid in executing laws without prior proclamation; he also raises the question of whether an organized militia force can be summoned as posse comitatus. He affirms his commitment to faithful execution of the laws. In a separate proclamation dated April 25, 1851, he warns against a military expedition being fitted out in the United States to invade Cuba, a Spanish colony, instigated chiefly by foreigners, cites statutory penalties of fines up to $3,000 and imprisonment up to three years, declares participants forfeit the government's protection, and calls on citizens and officers to prevent such enterprises and arrest offenders.

Options trading in NVDA is presented as an attractive strategy for potentially large profits from small investments, with losses on long options limited to the premium paid. Popular strategies include buying or writing calls and puts, straddles, strangles, spreads, and collars, each with distinct risk-reward profiles. Option prices depend on the underlying stock price, time to expiration, implied volatility, market sentiment, and dividends; dividends generally lower call prices and raise put prices. Implied volatility, often calculated using models like Black-Scholes, strongly influences premiums. NVDA options are generally liquid, and margin and cost requirements are lower for buying than for writing options. Risks include adverse stock movements, time decay, volatility, and liquidity. Risk management tools include stop-loss orders, protective puts, hedging, diversification, and position sizing. Options trading is generally taxed as capital gains, and investors are advised to understand pricing theory and gain practical experience.

The 2018-19 Union Budget, presented by Finance Minister Arun Jaitley, contains no separate allocation for women, unlike the 2016 and 2017 budgets. Critics argue it assumes women's existing social roles rather than addressing barriers preventing them from working. Some economists view the National Health Protection Scheme—offering Rs 5 lakh insurance cover to 10 crore vulnerable families—as beneficial for women's healthcare access, though others question its implementation, noting health spending declined to 2.1 percent of the Budget. Allocations for MSMEs, sanitation, and self-help groups may aid women, but maternity entitlements were cut to Rs 2,400 crore against a required Rs 8,000 crore, and the Ujjwala scheme was expanded despite many women being unable to afford cylinder refills. Overall, the Budget offers continuation of existing programs rather than new approaches to women's economic roles.

A hockey player who has spent seven or eight months in Quebec says playing there feels like home, and family members who have been his biggest fans will attend the game. He attributes the team's success to hard work and preparation begun last summer, believing luck is created through effort. He says the team is comfortable playing at home or on the road, with size and toughness, and will aim to impose its game style while matching the opponent's intensity. He expects a loud, exciting atmosphere, says the first ten minutes will be crucial, and plans to take it one game and one shift at a time.

USB-C and USB-A refer to connector shapes rather than speeds; USB-C, introduced in 2014, is smaller, reversible, and increasingly dominant. USB versions differ mainly in data transfer speeds and power delivery, and any connection chain runs at the speed of its slowest component. USB4, released in 2022, supports 20–40 Gbps and is built exclusively for USB-C, while USB4 Version 2 promises up to 120 Gbps but has not been widely adopted. Because USB 3.x naming is inconsistent, the article recommends checking speed ratings directly; USB-A tops out at 20 Gbps, and USB 2.0 maxes at 480 Mbps. USB Power Delivery enables charging, reaching 240 watts with USB-PD 3.1, while DisplayPort Alt Mode carries audio and video over a single USB-C cable. Thunderbolt, an Intel-owned standard developed with Apple, uses the USB-C connector with stricter certification; Thunderbolt 4 guarantees 40 Gbps and 100-watt charging, while Thunderbolt 5 doubles bandwidth to 80 Gbps and supports 240 watts. Cable ratings also affect performance, so using included cables or checking listed speeds is advised.

The speaker argues that slavery agitation has increased rather than ceased since the policy initiated to end it, and that it will not cease until a crisis is reached and passed. Invoking "a house divided against itself cannot stand," he asserts the government cannot permanently endure half slave and half free; it will become all one thing or the other—either opponents will arrest slavery's spread, or its advocates will make it lawful in all States, North and South.

He recounts a sequence of events: the 1854 Nebraska bill, justified by "squatter sovereignty," repealed the Congressional prohibition of slavery in the national territories—the first point gained. Buchanan's election, secured by an endorsement falling short of a clear popular majority, was the second. The Dred Scott decision, deferred until after the election and then endorsed by the President and the Nebraska bill's author, was the third. That decision holds that no descendant of African slaves can be a citizen, that neither Congress nor a territorial legislature can exclude slavery from a territory, and that U.S. courts will not decide whether a slave held in a free state becomes free.

The speaker contends these elements form a piece of machinery, comparing its architects—Stephen, Franklin, Roger, and James—to workmen whose timbers fit a common plan, suggesting concerted design. He notes the Nebraska bill's inclusion of States and the Court's silence on whether a State may exclude slavery, warning that another decision may soon declare the Constitution does not permit a State to exclude slavery, making slavery lawful everywhere unless the present political dynasty is met and overthrown.

He rejects suggestions that Senator Douglas is a fitting instrument for this work, arguing that Douglas's "care not" policy and framing of slavery as a property right leave him without grounds to oppose slavery or a revived African slave trade, and that Douglas is not now with them. The cause must be conducted by its own undoubted friends. Noting that Republicans mustered over thirteen hundred thousand strong two years ago under adverse circumstances, he declares the enemy now wavering, and that if they stand firm, victory is sure to come.

United States v. Henry J. Adams, III, No. 13-3207 (10th Cir. May 15, 2014): The Tenth Circuit affirmed the 140-month above-guidelines sentence of Henry J. Adams III, who pleaded guilty to armed bank robbery for his role in an October 18, 2012 robbery of an Intrust Bank branch, where he served as lookout and recruited a friend to drive the getaway car. Adams argued on appeal that he was entitled to a two-level offense reduction as a minor participant and that the district court abused its discretion in imposing an above-guidelines sentence. The court held the minor-participant reduction was properly denied because Adams helped plan the robbery, acted as lookout, recruited a driver, and expected compensation, making his culpability similar to that of defendants in comparable precedents. As to sentencing, the court determined the sentence was an upward variance rather than a departure, based on the district court's reliance on the 18 U.S.C. § 3553(a) factors, including Adams's extensive criminal history, pattern of recidivism, and the seriousness of the offense. Because variances are reviewed only for substantive reasonableness, Adams's departure-based arguments failed, and the sentence was found substantively reasonable. The court also rejected Adams's claim of unwarranted sentencing disparity with his codefendant Nixon, a career offender, noting that § 3553(a)(6) requires comparison to defendants nationwide with similar records, not merely to codefendants.

The Sri Lankan rupee fell for a third straight session to 158.60/75 per dollar as importer demand outpaced remittance inflows. Down 3.4 percent this year, it faces pressure from Fed rate rises, the US-China trade war, and rising oil prices. Moody's said the strong dollar raised Sri Lanka's credit risk, though pressure eased after a $584 million Chinese port payment.

Chelsea and Real Madrid are attempting to hijack Tottenham's move for Ajax defender Davinson Sanchez, valued at £40m. Tottenham are expected to initially bid £28m. Sanchez reportedly wants to leave to play in the Premier League and Champions League, while Spurs have yet to sign anyone this window.

The stick concept is a quick-game passing play, common in the West Coast Offense and Air Raid, designed for the quarterback to get the ball out quickly. Five eligible receivers release downfield, with the stick route runner—often the tight end—serving as the primary target who can adjust his route based on coverage. The concept performs well against man, Cover 3, and Cover 4, but is less effective against Cover 2, where the corner becomes the flat defender. Coaching points detail route responsibilities for the TE, TB, slot, X, and Z receivers against man and zone, with the quarterback reading the flat defender post-snap. Variations include the 2x2 condensed formation stick and the "Sticko," which uses double moves to counter defensive adjustments.

In this State of the Union address, the President outlines domestic and foreign policy priorities. He cites past achievements including education reform, creation of the Department of Homeland Security, tax relief, and corporate accountability reforms. He proposes making the 2004 and 2006 income-tax reductions permanent and effective immediately, ending the double taxation of dividends, and limiting discretionary spending growth to 4 percent. On health care, he calls for Medicare reform with an additional $400 billion over a decade, prescription drug coverage for seniors, and medical liability reform. He urges passage of his energy plan, Clear Skies legislation, and Healthy Forests Initiative, and proposes $1.2 billion for hydrogen-powered automobile research. He also requests a Faith-Based Initiative, a Citizen Service Act, a $450 million mentoring program for disadvantaged children and children of prisoners, and a $600 million drug treatment program, along with bans on partial-birth abortion and human cloning.

Abroad, the address addresses Afghanistan's reconstruction, Middle East peace between Israel and a democratic Palestine, and international food aid. He proposes the Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief, committing $15 billion over five years to combat AIDS in Africa and the Caribbean. On terrorism, he reports the arrest of thousands of suspected terrorists, enhanced homeland security measures, and proposes Project BioShield—nearly $6 billion for bioterrorism defenses—and a Terrorist Threat Integration Center. He identifies outlaw regimes seeking weapons of mass destruction as the gravest danger, citing Iran and North Korea. Regarding Iraq, he states that Saddam Hussein has failed to disarm, detailing unaccounted-for biological, chemical, and nuclear materials and alleged terrorist ties, and declares that if Iraq does not fully disarm, the United States will lead a coalition to disarm it, with Secretary of State Powell presenting intelligence to the UN Security Council on February 5. The address concludes with reflections on American character and faith.

Shares of Walgreens, CVS Health and Rite Aid fell after reports that Amazon may enter online drug sales. A Leerink analyst said Amazon will likely enter drug distribution within two years. Amazon declined to comment.

This study examines the value loads (positive, neutral, negative) conveyed through words in the reading texts of 2nd, 3rd, and 4th grade primary school Turkish textbooks published by Turkey's Ministry of National Education (MoNE). The background explains that opinions and values influence decision-making, that values are acquired through experience rather than innate, and that values education is essential for moral character development. The root values in the Turkish curriculum are listed as justice, friendship, honesty, self-control, patience, respect, love, responsibility, patriotism, and helpfulness. Methodologically, texts were converted using OCR software, processed with text editing programs through tokenization and lemmatization, and classified by three PhD experts in applied linguistics as positive, negative, or neutral using introspection and dictionary definitions. The database comprised 3637 unique words from 88 prose reading texts, with 1st grade textbooks and poems excluded. Findings showed 172 words (4.72%) carried positive value transfer, 159 (4.37%) negative, and 3306 (91.43%) neutral, with similar distributions across grade levels. The study concluded there is no observable relationship between grade levels and the values words transfer, suggesting no established standards for value education in textbook word presentation. It recommends classifying words by value load when constructing texts, employing corpus-based methods in textbook preparation, and digitizing print textbooks to support future research.

This is the opening lecture of MIT course 18.217 on graph theory and additive combinatorics. The instructor introduces the course's two parts—extremal graph theory and additive combinatorics—and their connections. He begins with Schur's failed approach to Fermat's Last Theorem via reduction mod p: Schur proved that for every n, Fermat's equation has nontrivial solutions mod p for all sufficiently large primes. This follows from Schur's theorem—every finite coloring of the positive integers contains a monochromatic solution to x + y = z—whose infinitary and finitary forms are shown equivalent by diagonalization. Schur's theorem is then proved using Ramsey's theorem for triangles (proved by induction on the number of colors), by coloring graph edges according to differences of vertex labels, so a monochromatic triangle yields a monochromatic x + y = z.

The lecture surveys a century of additive combinatorics: Van der Waerden's theorem, the Erdős–Turán conjecture, Roth's theorem (3-term arithmetic progressions, via Fourier analysis), Szemerédi's theorem and subsequent proofs via ergodic theory, higher-order Fourier analysis, and hypergraph regularity, plus the Polymath project. Extensions include multidimensional and polynomial Szemerédi theorems and the Green–Tao theorem on progressions in the primes, with structure-versus-randomness as a unifying theme. Finally, Roth's theorem is linked to the graph problem of maximizing edges when every edge lies in exactly one triangle (distinct from Mantel's theorem), with current bounds roughly n/e^(c√log n) and n/log n. Upcoming lectures will cover extremal graph theory.

A weekly trading strategy focuses on weekly price action and can take forms such as position trading, using the weekly chart for broader market context in trend-following systems, weekly rotation systems, or swing trading weekly price bars. Range trading is the most common approach among weekly position traders, who typically hold trades for 6-12 months and look for setups at support and resistance levels. Weekly highs and lows can serve as support/resistance on lower timeframes like H4, where traders can apply breakout or reversal strategies. Whether weekly or daily charts are better depends on trading style and requires backtesting, though position trading suits the weekly chart better. US day traders must meet FINRA's pattern day trading rule ($25,000 minimum), while swing traders are exempt. A backtested weekly sector rotation strategy ranking four ETFs produced 15.1% annual returns with a 43% maximum drawdown over 728 trades.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed the district court's summary judgment for AMCO Insurance on Morello's claims for breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing, intentional infliction of emotional distress, unfair business practices, and Unruh Act violations, as well as the denial of his motion for reconsideration. The court found no genuine issue of material fact that AMCO breached the implied covenant, citing its reasonable investigation, reliance on expert opinions, and a genuine dispute as to liability. The remaining claims, premised on the bad faith claim, also failed.

NVIDIA Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended May 2, 2021 (Q1 fiscal 2022) reports revenue of $5.66 billion, up 84% year-over-year, with net income of $1.91 billion and diluted EPS of $3.03. Gross margin was 64.1%. The Graphics segment generated $3.45 billion in revenue and Compute & Networking $2.21 billion; Gaming revenue was $2.76 billion and Data Center $2.05 billion. The company completed its $7.13 billion acquisition of Mellanox in April 2020 and has a pending $40 billion acquisition of Arm Limited, expected to close in the first quarter of calendar 2022, subject to regulatory approvals. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $12.67 billion, and operating cash flow was $1.87 billion. The company paid $99 million in dividends and, on May 21, 2021, declared a four-for-one stock split conditioned on stockholder approval. A securities class action was dismissed in March 2021, though plaintiffs filed an appeal; related derivative suits remain stayed. Management noted it expects to remain supply-constrained into the second half of the fiscal year, primarily in gaming, and that Gaming benefited from cryptocurrency mining demand, though the extent is hard to determine. The effective tax rate was 6.5%, and no customer represented 10% or more of revenue.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig of the Southern District of Florida was fired by email last week after old blog posts attributed to him criticizing President Trump surfaced. Commentator Natalie Winters said the posts included claims Trump was "mentally unfit" and "an institutional terrorist." Rosenzweig allegedly wrote the posts while at Kobre & Kim and joined the U.S. attorney's office in September 2020. He is among dozens of federal prosecutors fired by Trump's Justice Department, which has also dismissed three other Southern District of Florida prosecutors who worked with former special counsel Jack Smith.

The PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO command processes 1-128 migration entries, moving page contents in both SNP-enabled and non-SNP-enabled systems. In SNP systems it may only target Hypervisor-owned pages; in SEV systems only unencrypted or host/hypervisor encrypted memory may be targeted. It can move pages actively in use by DMA devices by directly updating IOMMU host PTEs. For non-SNP systems with non-secure ATS devices, software must set hPTE.PMS=1, issue ATS invalidations, and complete a wait synchronization before calling the command. The CPU must be prevented from accessing migrating pages, and software must update CPU host page table addresses afterward. If SNP is running, source and destination pages must be in the Hypervisor state. 2M pages must be smashed into 4K pages; direct 2M migration is unsupported.

Firmware performs per-entry checks (valid SPAs, hPTE address matching, page states), marks pages for migration, issues TLB invalidations and syncs, obtains exclusive RMP access when RMP_ENFORCE is true, copies pages while maintaining encryption, and updates hPTEs. Status is returned via STATUS/SUB_STATUS fields.

The PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST command moves pages belonging to SNP guests and may replace the SNP PAGE_MOVE command. It requires physically contiguous, 2M-aligned 2M pages, does not support concurrent DMA (which may be aborted), requires RMP_ENFORCE=1, and requires sources in Guest-Valid/Guest-Invalid state and destinations in Pre-Migration state; afterward destinations take the source state.

A separate command marks the end of migration command strings and may interrupt on completion.

Command/content errors are reported in commands and list entries; ring buffer errors in the PM_STATUS register; hardware errors via command status and/or MCA. On timeout, clients should log an MCA and take appropriate action. Batches cover up to 128 pages; hardware errors may render all pages in a command unrecoverable, and memory state may be unfixable, requiring eventual reboot after software saves state.

School systems nationwide are equipping school buses with new technology, including live cameras, GPS tracking, turn-by-turn navigation, and apps that let parents track students in real time. Kansas City Public Schools signed a $100 million, five-year contract with Zum, citing technology as a key factor in the decision. Transportant, which serves 88 school systems in 19 states, charges about $3,600 per bus upfront plus an annual subscription of about $69 per bus. Districts report benefits including improved safety, more efficient routes, cost savings, and help recruiting drivers amid a national shortage. However, privacy advocates, including the Parent Coalition for Student Privacy, raise concerns about the security of collected data such as GPS locations and video footage. School systems and tech companies say data is encrypted, stored securely, and routinely deleted, with some districts keeping video on their own servers.

Under the GST regime effective July 1, e-way bills are mandatory for transporting goods worth over Rs 50,000 to check tax evasion. The GST Council exempted 153 items from this requirement, including LPG, PDS kerosene, jewellery, currency, live animals, fresh produce, milk, cereals, khadi, puja samagri, hearing aids, human hair, contraceptives and postal baggage. Non-motorised transport and goods moving from international to hinterland ports are also exempt. The provision begins once NIC's software is ready, likely by October.

The Infiniti Q Inspiration concept, revealed at the beginning of this year, will inspire an all-new electrified platform with up to five new models built over the next five years. Production will occur in China, likely as global models. The concept features clear lines, a sculpted athletic body, and distinctive lights and grilles.

The passage describes the SOS pressure defense system, which demands extra time, energy, and commitment to repetitive drills; coach attitude and positive feedback build player acceptance, and in-game success fuels enthusiasm and pride in holding opponents below their scoring average. On-ball defense consists of three actions: SET (a stance and positioning that forces the ballhandler to dribble rather than shoot or pass), ON (guiding the dribbler toward a sideline or baseline checkpoint, using "Sprint and Recover" if beaten), and SMOTHER (maximum pressure on a ballhandler attempting to shoot or pass, which can also salvage poor Set or On execution). Off-ball defense uses three actions: SNUGGLE (pass denial when one pass away, including a Post Front "slip front" technique in the low post), OFF (denying passing lanes to cutters by moving between opponent and ballhandler), and STRIKE (a weakside position preventing cuts into the three-second area, covering backside lob passes, taking charges, blocking lay-ins, and boxing out). When a crosscourt pass is received, defenders execute a closeout—sprinting two-thirds of the distance, then mini-sliding into a Set position.

Fiat Chrysler Automobiles (FCA) has reportedly rejected a merger offer from an unnamed Chinese automaker, citing insufficient financial terms. CEO Sergio Marchionne previously pursued mergers with General Motors and Volkswagen, but in April said he would focus on the company's bottom line. He has expressed reluctance to sell, preferring partnerships, though he said in 2015 that China would acquire rather than partner. Several Chinese carmakers, including joint venture partner Guangzhou, have shown interest. Chinese manufacturers may be motivated by the government's "China Outbound" initiative and a desire to enter the U.S. market, for which FCA's brand recognition and distribution network make it attractive.

In *Givens v. Missouri-Kansas-Texas R. Co. of Texas* (5th Cir. 1952), a brakeman sued the railroad under the Federal Boiler Inspection Act and the Federal Employers' Liability Act after suffering frostbite to his feet and legs while flagging the rear of a passenger train that broke down in zero weather near Hewitt, Texas, on January 31, 1949, when driving wheel tires slipped or came off. The jury awarded $12,000 in damages but the district court entered judgment for the railroad. On appeal, the Fifth Circuit held the trial court erred in failing to instruct the jury on the Boiler Inspection Act, which imposes an absolute and continuing duty on carriers to keep locomotives and their parts safe to operate. Because the locomotive's breakdown while in use established a violation of the Act as a matter of law, and the jury found the breakdown was a proximate cause of the plaintiff's injuries, the court reversed and directed entry of a $12,000 judgment for the plaintiff.

Xiaomi is preparing for its biggest 2018 launch event, expected to feature the Mi 8, Mi 8 SE, Mi Note 5, and Mi Band 3. A Digit report says Xiaomi will not launch the Mi A2 in India; a spokesperson stated no phone exists by that name but more Android One devices are planned. The Mi 6X may launch in India under a different name. Xiaomi is also preparing the Redmi S2/Y2, its most affordable dual camera smartphone.

North American markets ended a volatile week with sharp losses. The Dow fell 666 points (2.5 per cent) to 25,520.96, its biggest decline in two years, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq dropped 2.1 and two per cent respectively, marking their worst weekly losses since early 2016. Losses deepened after jobs data showed the strongest annual wage growth since 2009, raising inflation and rate-hike concerns, alongside rising bond yields and weak earnings from Exxon Mobil, Chevron, Alphabet and Apple. Canada's S&P/TSX lost 1.6 per cent, hit by falling oil prices and continued declines in marijuana stocks, with Canopy Growth down 12.5 per cent.

This study presents the first comprehensive analysis of AI ethics education in Indian computing curricula, examining 3,395 syllabi from the top 100 engineering institutions in India's National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF). Only 2.21% (75 courses) across 22 universities incorporated AI ethics content, mostly superficially—60% devoted a single session, 20% two sessions, 13% one week, and 7% a full course. Most courses (92%) were undergraduate-level, and 76% had no prerequisites. The most common topics were privacy, legal aspects, and data governance (42%), accountability and policies (32%), ethical frameworks and moral reasoning (24%), human-AI interaction (24%), and algorithmic bias and fairness (18%). Over 90% of courses lacked dedicated AI ethics teaching materials, relying instead on standard AI/ML textbooks, and no course documented assessments explicitly dedicated to AI ethics. Fewer than half of the top 100 institutions had publicly accessible curricula. While findings partially align with the ACM/IEEE/AAAI CS2023 curriculum, gaps remain in generative AI ethics (11% coverage) and sustainability, justice, and labor ethics (8%). The authors conclude that AI ethics remains marginal and unevenly integrated, calling for coordinated efforts, dedicated resources, contextualized Indian case studies, and clearer assessment frameworks.
The FBI arrested 23-year-old Jerry Drake Varnell of Sayre, Oklahoma, on Saturday for allegedly plotting to detonate a vehicle bomb in Oklahoma City. He is scheduled to appear in federal court Monday.

Zambia's sugar industry drew migrants to towns like Mazabuka, known as "Sweet Town," where a sex industry contributed to the spread of HIV. At the epidemic's peak in 2003, about 70,000 Zambians died annually, with no treatment available and hospitals overwhelmed. The country is now recovering through a military-style campaign led by the NGO DAPP, called "Total Control of the Epidemic," which has reached more than 1.5 million of Zambia's 16.5 million people. Field officers conduct door-to-door testing with mobile kits, distribute condoms to truckers, and former sex workers and chieftains help spread awareness and reduce stigma. The strategy began in Zimbabwe in 2000 and reached Mazabuka in 2006. UN figures show 250 new infections daily, down 27 percent since 2010, with AIDS-related deaths down 11 percent. Officials say the approach should be extended to other countries.

A federal judge ordered the Trump administration to reverse layoffs of 532 Voice of America journalists and staff, finding officials violated his April order to restore the news organization's operations. Judge Royce C. Lamberth criticized Kari Lake for noncompliance and warned of contempt. Since Trump ordered its closure, Voice of America has broadcast about an hour daily, down from around-the-clock programming.

This passage is a beginner's guide to American Football. Walter Camp, known as the "Father of American Football," developed the game from rugby in the late 1870s and early 1880s, introducing the line of scrimmage, 11-man teams, the quarterback position, and the modern scoring format. The name "football" comes from the American adaptation of soccer and rugby. American Football is not an Olympic sport, though flag football may debut at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Each team fields 11 players (12 in the Canadian Football League), and games last 60 minutes at professional and collegiate levels. Legendary players include Tom Brady, Jerry Rice, Jim Brown, and Lawrence Taylor. The field is 100 yards long with 10-yard end zones. Scoring includes touchdowns (6 points), extra points (1), two-point conversions (2), field goals (3), and safeties (2). The passage also explains common penalties such as offsides, holding, and pass interference, defines what constitutes a catch, describes turnovers (interceptions, fumbles, turnover on downs), and covers key concepts like downs, the line of scrimmage, special teams, audibles, and the red zone.

Heart attacks and strokes in the UK have fallen by 30% over the past two decades but remain a major health hazard. Cholesterol- and blood pressure-lowering medicines, particularly statins—one of the most commonly prescribed medicines in England—have contributed, alongside lifestyle changes such as maintaining a healthy weight. Media scare stories about statin side effects have largely been attributed to the nocebo effect; a study found equal side effects between statin and placebo groups when participants did not know what they were taking, with side effects rising once they knew. Newer lipid-lowering medicines, including Repatha, Praluent and Leqvio, are usually reserved for people at very high risk whose cholesterol is not controlled by tablets. Other recommended measures include quitting smoking, regular aerobic and resistance exercise, omega 3-rich foods, soluble fibre, fortified and soya-based foods, cooking from scratch, and reduced-sodium salt substitutes, which the BHF says could cut early deaths by 12%.

Police have seized a white Holden Commodore possibly linked to the murder of Aaron Marks, who was found with fatal injuries on a Ballina footpath. Forensic officers are examining the vehicle, and investigators are asking passengers to come forward while the driver assists enquiries.

CBS's new legal drama "Doubt" premieres Wednesday at 10 p.m. Katherine Heigl stars as defense attorney Sadie Ellis, who falls for her client, pediatric surgeon Billy Brennan (Steven Pasquale), accused of murdering his girlfriend 24 years earlier. Created by "Grey's Anatomy" alums Tony Phelan and Joan Rater, the series features Dulé Hill and Laverne Cox, the first transgender actor to play a transgender series regular on broadcast TV. Each week brings new cases alongside Billy's ongoing case. The show is described as formulaic but competent, with a likeable cast.

Callum Knott, 21, admitted taking his aunt's car without consent and driving without a licence or insurance. He acted out of boredom and abandoned the vehicle when its battery died. He received a 12 month community order, 80 hours unpaid work, a four-month ban, £85 costs and an £85 surcharge.

Cover 2 is a popular 5-under, 2-deep coverage designed to stop quick passes and deep throws, with cornerbacks serving as flat defenders. Offenses attack it through high-low stretches on the corners (such as smash and fade-out concepts), using 3 receiver surfaces to high-low the middle linebacker with dig/seam combinations, vertical concepts like 4 verticals that put both safeties in a bind, and attacking the open middle of the field with deep routes. The passage illustrates these strategies with five example plays from Ohio State, Oregon, Michigan, Ole Miss, and TCU.

Curaleaf Holdings and the cannabis sector rallied in August on news the Trump administration would consider rescheduling cannabis. The rally faded in September but was reignited by Trump's Truth Social post about CBD benefits for elders. Curaleaf reported in-line Q2 2025 results and is expanding international operations into Turkey. The author maintains a Hold rating on CURLF due to sector uncertainty.

The East Demerara Football Association held its Annual General Meeting with six of seven clubs present; Victoria Scorpions was absent. Alfred King was returned as president of the newly chosen executive.

Andrew Dawes, CEO of Intels Nigeria Limited, says the company is partnering the Federal Government to boost port investment. Responding to monopoly allegations, he stated Intels has invested billions of dollars in infrastructure on behalf of the NPA under concession agreements and pays comparatively more to government than other private jetties. He cited challenges from falling oil and gas prices, with cargo down 70 per cent from several years ago, but said investments are long-term. The Phase 4B project, built in partnership with the Federal Government, is the only facility ready to receive a full FPSO alongside, with 4km of quay length. Investment pace will slow during the recession, and the Federal Government controls port allocation policy. The Badagry deep seaport project with APM Terminals is progressing and is expected to be the largest port in Africa. Intels, established 30 years ago, provides integrated logistics services to Nigeria's oil and gas industry, is a leading logistics support supplier in West Africa, and pioneered the "one-stop-shop" oil service centre concept.

Tesla, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2020. The company designs, manufactures and sells electric vehicles and solar energy generation and energy storage products, operating in two segments: automotive and energy generation and storage.

Key financial results:
- Q2 2020 total revenues were $6,036 million (vs. $6,350 million in Q2 2019); six-month revenues were $12,021 million (vs. $10,891 million).
- Net income attributable to common stockholders was $104 million for Q2 2020 (vs. a $408 million loss in Q2 2019) and $120 million for the six months (vs. a $1,110 million loss).
- Total assets were $38,135 million as of June 30, 2020 (vs. $34,309 million at December 31, 2019); cash and cash equivalents were $8,615 million; total stockholders' equity was $9,855 million.

COVID-19 impact: Tesla temporarily suspended operations at all manufacturing facilities worldwide during the first half of 2020 and implemented labor cost reductions, but resumed operations at all facilities by the end of Q2 2020.

Other notable items:

- Total debt and finance leases totaled $13,151 million in unpaid principal as of June 30, 2020.
- The Credit Agreement was upsized to $2.525 billion in March 2020; a subsidiary entered into an RMB 4.00 billion unsecured revolving facility in China in May 2020.
