This study presents the MOSAIC study, a large multi-omics case-control investigation (N=2,513) conducted across 77 US clinical sites to develop a blood-based test for early lung cancer detection. Motivated by low adherence to LDCT screening and the need for improved early detection, researchers used untargeted proteomics, RNA-seq, metabolomics, and targeted immunoassays on plasma samples to identify over 750,000 molecular features. A machine learning classifier trained on multi-omics data from 1,225 subjects achieved an AUC of 0.96 for all-stage lung cancer and 0.93 for stage I disease, outperforming both a clinical-variables-only baseline (AUC 0.78) and a proteomics-only classifier (AUC 0.91). In a held-out validation set of 398 subjects, the classifier demonstrated 89% sensitivity and 89% specificity across all stages, with stage-specific sensitivities of 80% (stage I), 88% (stage II), and 99% (stages III-IV). The final model comprised 682 features spanning 149 proteins, 346 genes, and 77 metabolic pathways, with no single omics type dominating. Over 60% of model features were significantly associated with cancer stage. The authors conclude that this multi-omics approach addresses an unmet clinical need for early lung cancer detection but requires prospective validation in the intended screening population.

The paper presents a methodology for studying the dynamics of a digital business ecosystem (DBE), a closed or semi-closed system of SMEs interacting through buyer–seller relationships in cyberspace. Because company interactions are asymmetric, Markov random fields are deemed unsuitable; instead, inspired by neural interaction models of the visual cortex, the authors derive a set of non-linear coupled differential equations governing a fitness value for each company. Noting the scarcity of quantitative DBE studies, they construct a simulated DBE of 100 companies trading 20 products that shares the statistical properties of a real DBE. Companies are assigned SELL, WANT, TRUST and MISTRUST lists, with reputation propagation modeled so that good reputation spreads faster than bad. The Weber-Fechner psychophysical law converts qualitative trust categories into numerical weights. The fitness model includes self-excitation with a critical-mass threshold, excitatory signals from companies whose products match demands, inhibitory signals from companies selling similar products, trust weighting, and external and background inputs. The equations are solved iteratively on a fully connected network, with weak companies removed and new ones introduced at average fitness. Preliminary experiments show company survival over iterations and monopoly formation under certain parameter values. Proposed improvements include modeling inhibition based on commonly sought products and random injection of new companies; associating model parameters with real measurable quantities remains future work.

The Camarilla pivot point, introduced in 1989 by bond trader Nick Scott, is an extension of the classical pivot point that provides day traders with key intraday support and resistance levels. It displays four support and four resistance levels, totaling nine levels, calculated using the previous day's closing prices. The strategy is used for day trading, with the approach depending on market conditions, and helps traders identify price levels, entry and exit points, and manage risk. Day traders use pivot points to define support and resistance and identify potential trend changes. Unlike Camarilla pivots, Fibonacci pivot points use Fibonacci retracements and extensions to determine key levels. A backtest of ordinary pivot points showed no super profits, and the authors doubt Camarilla would differ significantly, encouraging readers to backtest their own ideas.

Long-standing criticisms of academic publishing—research fraud, paper mills, a shortage of qualified peer reviewers, and high subscription and open-access costs—are fueling the Trump administration's attacks on the scientific enterprise. HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and NIH Director Jayanta Bhattacharya have criticized the industry, with Kennedy accusing major medical journals of pharmaceutical industry control and proposing to bar government-funded scientists from publishing in them. Bhattacharya has pledged to prioritize reproducible research and rein in the $19 billion for-profit publishing industry, including capping article processing charges, and co-launched the Journal of the Academy of Public Health; the NIH also rescinded a Biden-era public-access deposit policy. Other officials, including then-interim U.S. attorney Edward R. Martin Jr., have questioned journals over political bias. While scientists acknowledge real problems, many doubt these solutions will yield meaningful reform, warning the administration may be exploiting them to advance an ideological agenda; they say incentive reform must be led by scientists and academic institutions.

Lookout researchers found over a thousand Google Play apps containing SonicSpy spyware, capable of recording audio, taking photos, making calls, sending texts, and retrieving call logs, contacts, and Wi-Fi data. The malware responds to over 73 remote commands. Its latest sample, Soniac, posed as a messaging app built on customized Telegram while hiding itself and connecting to a command and control server. The account iraqwebservice posted two earlier SonicSpy samples, since removed. Researchers warn enterprises face risks including regulatory fines.

The Supreme Court cleared the way for the Trump administration to strip hundreds of thousands of Venezuelan nationals of Temporary Protected Status, pausing a federal judge's ruling that had barred DHS Secretary Kristi Noem from terminating the designation. The unsigned order came roughly four-and-a-half months after the court first paused a similar ruling by Judge Edward Chen, who had found Noem acted unlawfully in ending Venezuela's 2023 TPS designation and its 2025 extension. The three Democratic appointees—Justices Sotomayor, Kagan, and Jackson—would have denied the administration's request. Jackson dissented, calling the order "yet another grave misuse of our emergency docket" and criticizing the court for interfering with lower court cases "while lives hang in the balance." Sotomayor and Kagan did not offer an explanation for their positions.

Manjot Kalra scored an unbeaten century as India won their fourth ICC Under-19 World Cup title in 2018, earning Player of the Match. Reserved during the post-match presentation interview with Simon Doull, he was more open at the press conference, saying he took charge after Shubman Gill's dismissal. Kalra, picked by Delhi Daredevils at his base price of Rs 20 lakh, is now in the spotlight, with social media comparing him to Yuvraj Singh, Sourav Ganguly and Gautam Gambhir. However, history urges caution: of the five batsmen with U19 World Cup final centuries, none of the other four—including Unmukt Chand—played for their senior national teams. From Kohli's 2008 winning squad, only three others represented India, and none from Chand's 2012 team. Coach Rahul Dravid hoped the win would be a cherished memory but not one that defines the players.

Blue Cross Blue Shield of Massachusetts is offering voluntary buyouts to about 750 employees aged 55 and older with at least 10 years of tenure, its first since the late 1980s, amid soaring health care costs and steep losses.
Seeking Alpha page instructing users to enable Javascript and cookies and disable ad-blockers to proceed.

This patent application describes a system and method for dynamic graphics rendering based on saccade detection. Because saccadic masking prevents users from perceiving new frames during rapid eye movements, the system detects the onset of a saccade using sensors (such as optical or EMG sensors) and reduces the computing resources used for rendering frames during the saccade—by skipping or repeating frames, reducing rendering detail or resolution, or adjusting the frame rate. This saves power, particularly in VR/AR devices, and freed resources can be reallocated to low-frequency tasks such as complex lighting calculations. The system may predict saccade duration using an eye movement model calibrated for individual users, and can be implemented in head-mounted displays and other processor-based devices.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended December 31, 2017, reports total revenue of $28.9 billion for the three months ended December 31, 2017 (up from $25.8 billion in the prior-year quarter) and a net loss of $6.3 billion, compared with net income of $6.3 billion a year earlier. The loss resulted primarily from a $15.5 billion provision for income taxes, driven by an estimated $13.8 billion net charge related to the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA), enacted December 22, 2017, which imposes a one-time transition tax on deferred foreign income and reduces the U.S. federal statutory rate from 35% to 21%. For the six months, revenue was $53.5 billion and net income was $274 million. Total assets were $256.0 billion and stockholders' equity was $78.4 billion as of December 31, 2017. Microsoft early adopted new revenue recognition and lease standards effective July 1, 2017, restating prior period results. Other disclosures include: the $27.0 billion LinkedIn acquisition completed in December 2016; $12.5 billion of commercial paper and $76.8 billion carrying value of long-term debt; unearned revenue of $23.8 billion and $61 billion of contracted not recognized revenue; $33.4 billion remaining under a $40 billion share repurchase program; a $0.42 per share quarterly dividend; pending legal matters including patent, antitrust, and employment litigation, with accrued legal liabilities of $370 million and reasonably possible losses of approximately $1.3 billion beyond recorded amounts; and continuing IRS audits concerning transfer pricing.

A hockey coach said a line that has provided quality minutes all season is now earning recognition for playing tough minutes away from the spotlight. He called puck possession a major factor in territorial play and credited players' commitment to a system used all year, noting that fortunate bounces helped in a close Stanley Cup Finals win decided by a big shot from Sammy Pahlsson. He said shooting versus holding the puck is situational and that the game is simpler for coaches than players, and he viewed the opponent's line adjustments and his counters as normal strategy. He attributed the regular season's tightly grouped standings to the salary cap creating a level playing field. A player with pins in his hands cannot return until doctors clear him. Playoff routines include optional morning skates, game-day hotel check-ins, and pregame naps. He denied being overly critical of Getzlaf, calling his comments minor and saying he does not criticize players publicly. He praised a big-bodied defenseman acquired at last year's trade deadline who contributed to series wins over Calgary and Colorado. Health has limited the fourth line, as young players Carter and Motzko need their minutes spaced out. After losing to Edmonton in last year's conference final, the team vowed not to accept mediocrity, underscored by acquiring Chris Pronger, and the group's early assembly and familiarity contributed to a strong season.

UOB FX Strategists view a near-term pullback to 1.2900 as unlikely. GBP rebounded from a low of 1.2939, with room for a slow grind higher toward 1.3040/45. The bearish phase remains intact, but patchy downward momentum limits odds of reaching 1.2900, though another push lower is not ruled out.

This passage is a step-by-step guide to building an RSI-based trading strategy in TradingView using its native Pine Script language, applied to the crypto market. The strategy trades DOT on a 5-minute timeframe with a 14-period RSI, using 65/35 as overbought/oversold levels. Long entries occur when RSI exits the oversold zone, shorts when it exits the overbought zone, and positions close at the RSI midline of 50.

The article describes TradingView as a widely used, free technical analysis platform offering charting, indicators, backtesting, and community features. It explains how to add the RSI indicator, adjust its settings, and use the Pine Editor to write a strategy script. The code uses the built-in ta.rsi function, defines long and short conditions, and employs strategy.entry and strategy.close commands, with user inputs added so RSI parameters can be modified via the settings window.

Once added to the chart, the strategy displays results including equity curve, net profit, drawdown, and win rate. Pro account users can run deep backtests using historical data (available since 2019 for DOT), accessing statistics like Sharpe Ratio and exporting trade data as CSV, an option unavailable to free users. The article concludes that RSI alone does not perform consistently and should be complemented with other indicators or criteria.

Max Hayes High School auto collision repair students spent a year and a half rebuilding a Cleveland police cruiser damaged during the 2016 Cavs championship celebrations, after teacher Greg Boykin proposed the project. Using donated materials, they replaced the roof, hood, and side panels, saving the city about $10,000. The cruiser will return to service as a zone car.

Nannette Perkins, 40, was arrested at her Taylorsville home after police received a tip about her identity. She is believed to be the pajama-wearing robber in at least six Salt Lake City-area bank robberies, including five in under two hours, and is being held in jail.

The passage argues that student newsrooms are as vital to universities as local news is to towns, keeping students informed about campus and community issues. It notes that news deserts are spreading across America and that media consolidation has left news controlled by about six powerful corporations, reducing diversity. The author contends that removing student news would deprive students of information needed to make informed decisions and urges that the next generation not be left uninformed.

This study aimed to identify needs for and develop strategies for excellence in vocational education management at institutions under Thailand's Office of the Vocational Education Commission. Using a Research and Development design, Phase 1 surveyed 206 respondents sampled from 424 institutions via Taro Yamane's formula, analyzing data with means, standard deviations, the modified priority needs index (PNImodified), and SWOT analysis, supplemented by interviews at three exemplary institutions. Phase 2 refined the resulting strategic framework through focus group discussions with nine experts.

Results showed current conditions at a high level and desired conditions at the highest level, with an overall PNImodified of 0.179. Curriculum Development had the highest need (0.198), followed by Cooperation Networks (0.196), Personnel (0.193), Teaching Management (0.173), Graduate Quality (0.160), and Management (0.149). The developed framework comprised a vision, mission, objectives, and six strategies: enhancing professional management efficiency; developing competency-based curricula to international standards; elevating teaching and learning quality; developing teacher and staff expertise; building comprehensive workforce development networks; and improving graduate quality. Expert evaluation rated both the suitability and feasibility of the strategies at the highest level. The findings align with the Office's Eight Agenda policies and prior research. The authors recommend prioritizing Strategy 2, adapting strategies to institutional contexts, and conducting future research on curriculum development models and digital content production competencies.

American Mint offers the 24k gold-layered Band of Brothers Men's Ring in sizes 8–14 at $129.90 for a limited time, honoring those who fought for liberty. The Mechanicsburg-based collectibles provider has served over a million customers; its parent company operates in nine countries.

Millions of people across the United States are preparing for a total solar eclipse crossing from Oregon to South Carolina, promising up to two minutes and 40 seconds of totality along a 70-mile-wide track. A small community of eclipse chasers, known as umbraphiles, has planned for this event for decades. The author, a freelance science writer and amateur astronomer, describes totality as an indescribable experience and recounts his history of catching only partial and annular eclipses. He plans to witness his first total solar eclipse at the Pisgah Astronomical Research Institute in North Carolina, while die-hard chasers favor Wyoming or Idaho for better weather prospects. The article warns that approved solar glasses with an ISO 12312-2 rating are required during all partial phases, as some vendors sell bogus glasses. Because the moon is slowly receding from Earth, total eclipses will cease in about 600 million years. Another US eclipse will occur on April 8, 2024.
Cancer cells transfer mitochondria to fibroblasts, reprogramming them for growth.

This study presents the first comprehensive quantitative and qualitative evaluation of mature "AI in Healthcare" publications from 2019–2021, using a semi-automated approach combining deep learning (a BERT-based maturity classifier) with an in-house collection of PubMed publications classified into 34 medical specialties. Of 7,062 publications, only about 5% (385) were deemed mature. Radiology had the most mature models across all three years, followed by Pathology, Ophthalmology, and Gastroenterology. Only 4% (2020) and 1.6% (2021) of COVID-19-related publications were mature. Geographically, mature publications were concentrated in developed nations, with the United States and China leading, while regions such as South America, Eastern Europe, and Africa were underrepresented. Image data dominated mature publications (~88–89% annually), while text and tabular data were underrepresented. Deep learning was the most frequently used model type (62–71%). The authors conclude there is an opportunity to leverage heterogeneous datasets and models across healthcare to increase mature AI publications, and the findings can guide future research and resource utilization.

A QQQ strategy exits when the close exceeds yesterday's high or close. Since January 2000, compounding $100,000 without tax deductions, it showed a high profit factor, lower drawdown than buy and hold, and 12.4% CAGR versus 9%. Mean reversion has worked, but future success is uncertain.

The London breakout strategy, also known as the London daybreak strategy, is a forex day trading strategy that trades breakouts of the trading range formed before the London session opens, typically within the first three hours of that session. Traders take long positions on upward breakouts and short positions on downward breakouts. The London session, which overlaps the Asian and New York sessions, offers the highest liquidity and volatility. The range can be defined using the high-low method or the open-close method. A custom London breakout indicator provides one daily signal at 3:00 am EST, with entry, stop loss, and take profit levels. A backtest on EURUSD showed the strategy loses money on upward breakouts and produces near-zero average gains on downward breakouts, suggesting it needs more parameters or risk management. The authors remain skeptical, noting forex offers little trading edge and that stocks and bonds may provide better opportunities.

Bulk MnBi₂Te₄/(Bi₂Te₃)ₙ crystals grown by the Inverted Vertical Bridgman Method show structural and magnetic properties that vary along the ingot due to Mn segregation and changing melt flow. Four samples exhibited decreasing average Mn concentration (13.5 to 1.9 at.%) and evolving stacking: pure MnBi₂Te₄ (Sample A), MnBi₂Te₄/Bi₂Te₃ (Sample B), septuple layers (SLs) spaced by 7±2 quintuple layers (QLs) (Sample C), and disordered 4–5 QL spacing (Sample D). Samples A and B showed antiferromagnetic transitions at 26 K and 13.5 K, while Samples C and D, with larger SL separation and Mn-depleted SLs, showed ferromagnetic transitions near 11 K and 9 K. Magnetic resonance confirmed increased anisotropy below the transitions, with Sample C showing a higher anisotropy field (~460 mT) than Sample D (~370 mT) and corresponding uniaxial anisotropy constants of 4300 and 1700 J m⁻³. Growth proceeds through four stages: turbulent flow, rapid MnTe precipitation, stationary flow, and flow cessation. An inverse relationship between SL spacing and MnTe supersaturation arises from diffusion-driven competition between MnBi₂Te₄ layer edges. Controlling melt composition and flow dynamics offers a route to tuning layer spacing, magnetic order, and topological behavior.

A Nigerian bank support staff member issued a social media warning about a fraud scheme at ATM galleries. Scammers approach customers, show cash, claim they have exceeded their withdrawal limit, and ask to transfer money into the victim's account for withdrawal. These transfers typically come from stolen phones or hacked accounts. When the original account owner reports the fraud, the recipient's account is frozen, their BVN is flagged, and arrest orders may follow. The banker cited two recent victims—an 18-year-old held at gunpoint (40k) and an adult customer (50k)—both now facing police cases. He urged the public to refuse all such requests at ATMs.

The paper studies the dynamics of antiferromagnetic domain walls under spin-orbit torque. Antiferromagnets offer advantages over ferromagnets, producing no stray fields and remaining robust under moderate external fields. Their dynamics, described by extensions of the nonlinear σ-model for the Néel vector, permit Newtonian and relativistic behaviors and can be probed by spin-polarized currents. The authors find that precessional dynamics arises spontaneously as a steady state; domain walls propagate at constant velocity, though not via a simple Lorentz transformation of the static wall; and oscillatory wall motion occurs when the spin current polarization has both in-plane and perpendicular components. The model goes beyond the idealized σ-model and accounts for the breaking of Lorentz invariance by the damping term. The magnetic moment carried by antiferromagnetic textures is also discussed, as it could enable their observation and functionality. The model considers a spin chain with antiferromagnetic exchange, Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, and perpendicular anisotropy, with equations of motion including damping and spin torque from polarized electrons. A continuum approximation using tetramers yields an extended nonlinear σ-model for the Néel vector. Numerical results come from simulating the discrete spin lattice; for polarization along ê3, spins reach a steady state precessing at constant angular frequency.

Young African entrepreneurs are using new technologies to transform agriculture, improve food security and create jobs amid climate change, as showcased at the MasterCard Foundation's Young Africa Works Summit 2017 in Kigali. In Rwanda, Jean Bosco Nzeyimana's Habona Ltd employs 25 young people to turn waste into fuel briquettes and organic fertiliser, producing 50 tonnes of fuel monthly. In Malawi, Pilirani Khoza's Bunda Female Students Organisation sponsors disadvantaged women science students who train rural women farmers, reaching 360 farmers so far. In Kenya, Brian Bosire's UjuziKilimo uses a handheld soil sensor and mobile phones to advise farmers, aiming to reach 200,000 farmers within two years. U.N. expert Richard Munang noted agriculture employs nearly two-thirds of Africa's population and can reduce poverty two to four times faster than other sectors, urging youth to engage across the full supply chain.

Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia (MEN) is a hereditary cancer syndrome characterized by two or more endocrine gland tumors, encompassing MEN1, MEN2, and MEN4, all autosomal dominant. MEN1 results from inactivating mutations in the MEN1 tumor suppressor gene; MEN2 from activating RET proto-oncogene mutations (subtypes MEN2A, MEN2B, and FMTC); and MEN4 from CDKN1B mutations, presenting similarly to MEN1 but with later onset. This study systematically classified variants in the RET, MEN1, and CDKN1B genes from the IndiGen dataset (1,029 healthy Indian individuals), ClinVar, and Mastermind using ACMG/AMP guidelines to establish the genetic epidemiology of MEN in India. From 1,324 unique variants, the researchers created the MAPVar database containing 3,280 ACMG-classified variants (1,094 pathogenic/likely pathogenic, 1,591 benign/likely benign, and 595 VUS), accessible for clinical and research use. Genetic prevalence analysis indicated approximately 1 in 341 Indian individuals is a likely carrier of pathogenic RET mutations. Comparison across 18 global population datasets showed one variant at significantly higher allele frequency in IndiGen. Validation through the GUaRDIAN endocrine cohort identified pathogenic variants in 7 patient cases. The researchers also developed a multiplex primer panel covering all coding regions of the three genes (38 amplicons, 65 kb across 33 exons), which successfully solved 3 endocrine cancer cases. The study concludes that MEN, particularly RET-linked, is highly prevalent yet understudied in India, and the genetic testing panel and database aim to enable early, accurate diagnosis and help address the MEN-linked cancer burden.

On February 13, 2020, Tesla, Inc. entered into an underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC and Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC to issue and sell 2,650,000 shares of common stock in a public offering under a Form S-3 Registration Statement. The underwriters held a 30-day option to purchase up to 397,500 additional shares, which they exercised in full on February 18, 2020. The offering closed on February 19, 2020, generating net proceeds of approximately $2.31 billion after underwriting discounts, commissions, and estimated expenses. Holders of the required minimum shares waived registration rights under the company's investors' rights agreement in connection with the offering. Tesla issued a press release announcing the offering on February 13, 2020. The report was signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn.

This collection of news articles from November 19–20, 2001, covers Enron Corp.'s deepening financial crisis. Enron restated its third-quarter earnings for a second time, widening its loss to 87 cents per share ($664 million), and warned it may take a $700 million pretax hit from declining asset values in its Whitewing partnership. A credit rating downgrade to BBB- by Standard & Poor's triggered a $690 million debt obligation due by late November; if unpaid or uncollateralized, partners could liquidate assets including a Brazilian gas distribution company. A further downgrade below investment grade would trigger $3.9 billion in additional repayments, primarily from Osprey Trust and Marlin Water Trust. Enron reported roughly $1.75 billion in cash against $9.15 billion in obligations due by the end of 2002, and warned that adverse outcomes could materially impact its ability to continue as a going concern. Wall Street bankers expressed concern that Dynegy, which agreed to acquire Enron, might abandon the deal through its "material adverse change" clause, and shareholders filed suit to block the merger. ChevronTexaco, Dynegy's major backer, cited litigation risk as the deal's biggest hurdle. Representative John Dingell called for a special investigation of auditor Arthur Andersen's audits of Enron and Waste Management, and Andersen had not completed its review of Enron's filings due to an ongoing internal investigation. Enron's water unit, Azurix, also warned it might need to sell assets if unable to refinance debt.

Bar Harbor Bankshares reported 2016 net income of $14.9 million, including $2.7 million in charges for the Lake Sunapee Bank Group acquisition and system conversion. Total assets rose to $1.8 billion, loans grew 14 percent, and non-interest income increased 38 percent.

The Supreme Court heard arguments on whether the U.S. Postal Service and federal government can be sued for intentionally failing to deliver mail. The case stems from Lebene Konan, a Texas landlady who alleged postal workers intentionally withheld mail from her property as part of a campaign of racial harassment, leading her to file more than 50 administrative complaints before suing. The government argues the Federal Tort Claims Act's "postal exception"—covering "loss, miscarriage, or negligent transmission" of mail—preserves sovereign immunity for such claims; the 5th Circuit ruled that intentional nondelivery falls outside those terms. Several justices questioned the government's broad reading of "loss," while Kavanaugh and Alito worried a ruling for Konan could open the door to numerous lawsuits over mail problems. Konan's attorney disputed this, and Sotomayor and Jackson warned against immunizing intentional misconduct, such as destroying mail-in ballots. A decision is expected by early July.

At the Silverbluff Audubon Center in Aiken County, S.C., staff root for the Philadelphia Eagles in the Super Bowl because bald eagles nest there; a nesting pair has been present since 1994. Though the eagles initially failed to appear, one was later seen. Staff note that since the eagle is the national symbol, even Patriots fans can't lose.

Christa Goldblatt of Crossborder Energy transmits the May 5, 2000 rebuttal testimony of R. Thomas Beach, filed on behalf of Indicated Electric Generators in California Public Utilities Commission Investigation I. 99-07-003 regarding California natural gas industry restructuring. The testimony responds to the Southern California Generation Coalition (SCGC) and TURN's support of their Post-Interim Settlement Agreement (PISA), which defers unbundling of SoCalGas intrastate transmission. Beach argues that SCGC/TURN exaggerate differences between the PG&E and SoCalGas systems, that SoCalGas' backbone can be unbundled similarly to PG&E's Gas Accord, and that the Gas Accord's city-gate market has yielded substantial savings for electric generators. He contends SCGC/TURN's cost/benefit analysis ignores unbundling's benefits, overstates demand charge impacts based on unrealistic assumptions, and that the Comprehensive Settlement Agreement—supported by over 20 parties—reduces electric generator rates and risks. He recommends the Commission adopt the Comprehensive Settlement Agreement.

VOT broadcasts on shortwave at 11.510, 9.510, and 15.565 mHz at set times for Tibet, India, and Nepal, targeting Tibet. It also airs via ASIASAT 7 (105.5°E, C-band, 4146 MHz, horizontal polarization) as "MOMO," 24/7, alternating 30-minute Mandarin and Tibetan programs.

California's Department of Fish and Wildlife re-approved Newhall Ranch after certifying an additional environmental analysis resolving greenhouse gas emissions and stickleback protection, two issues the state Supreme Court ordered revisited in 2015. Developer FivePoint revised its Net Zero Newhall plan, which the Air Resources Board found adequately supports a determination of no net additional emissions. Revised bridge and bank stabilization construction will avoid water contact, eliminating two earlier fish-protection measures. The county Board of Supervisors is expected to consider final re-approval of the first two villages on July 19; the fully built project could include 12,000 homes and 11.5 million square feet of commercial space.
All four writers predict Beneil Dariush will defeat Evan Dunham at UFC 216, with three picking a unanimous decision and one predicting a second-round submission.

Radford University has narrowed its search for Vice President for Student Affairs to two finalists, who spoke at forums on September 11–12, 2017. The position opened when Dr. Irvin Clark left at the end of the 2017 Spring Semester; Susan Trageser has served as interim. The first finalist, Dr. Thomas C. Segar, Vice President for Student Affairs at Shepherd University in West Virginia, has over 26 years of experience and emphasized student learning, belonging, social justice, and experiential learning. The second finalist, Dr. Ann Marie Klotz, Dean of Campus Life at the New York Institute of Technology since 2014, is a first-generation college student who stressed adaptability, community, and using social media to tell Radford's story. Both are experienced professionals excited about the opportunity.

Nick Kyrgios defeated Jan-Lennard Struff 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 to level Australia's 2018 Davis Cup tie against Germany in Brisbane, after Alexander Zverev beat teenager Alex de Minaur in five sets. Saturday's doubles pits Ebden and Peers against Gojowczyk and Puetz, with Kyrgios versus Zverev scheduled for Sunday.
Jacob Allen sued Richard and Hannah Knight, executrix of Hope Allen's estate, for withholding sixty-four pounds from his father's will; the jury found for Allen.

Escalating nuclear threats between US President Donald Trump and North Korea's Kim Jong-un triggered a global market sell-off amid fears of potential conflict. Raymond James strategist Jeffrey Saut warned of technical market damage and advised trimming positions, though he believes the market remains in a secular bull market with six to eight years of upside. He considers war unlikely but noted a conflict could push crude oil to $150 a barrel. Gina Sanchez of Chantico Global expects heightened volatility not seen since the crisis.

Only about one percent of U.S. higher education students participate in study abroad despite institutional commitments to global citizenship, with financial barriers being the most persistent obstacle to expanding travel-based programs. Drawing on two decades of experience, the authors present a structured methodology for building sustainable business models for education abroad.

The article identifies three interdependent drivers that must be considered together: curricular, operational, and financial logistics. Curricular design should be guided by learning outcomes rather than logistical convenience or revenue, with considerations including elective versus required status, credit structure, timing of credit earned, assessment and reflection, strategic alignment with host institutions, competitive landscape, location selection, engagement modalities, and program duration. Operational logistics—governed by available resources—encompass risk management, program leadership, travel timing and organization, flights, lodging, partner coordination, local transport, communication, meals, entertainment, emergency preparation, student preparation and wellbeing, and problem support. Financial logistics aim to keep expenditures at or below income, covering faculty, staff, external party, project, and coordination expenses, funded through student tuition, fees, and internal or external funding sources.

Based on a literature review and fourteen interviews, the authors present a typology of twelve business models in three main categories: external party led (private or nonprofit companies charging student fees), faculty led (with four primary options: student payment-driven, revenue-driven, corporate donation-driven, and grant-driven), and student led (typically non-credit club-based programs funded by donations and student activity fees). Models can be adapted and combined.

The article concludes that expanding global education depends on faculty creating and sustaining travel programs. Key principles include leveraging revenue or corporate sponsorship to ease financial burdens, securing dedicated staff support to reduce faculty workload, and delegating certain planning tasks to students to foster professional development. Faculty should critically assess which models best suit their program's unique objectives, constraints, and resources.

On July 8, 2021, Microsoft Corporation announced it will redeem all outstanding 2.125% Notes due December 6, 2021 (ISIN XS1001749107), issued in the principal amount of €1,750,000,000, on September 6, 2021. Under the indenture dated May 18, 2009 between Microsoft and The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A., as trustee, as supplemented by the seventh supplemental indenture dated December 6, 2013, the redemption price will equal the €1,750,000,000 principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest to, but excluding, the redemption date. The Form 8-K itself does not constitute a notice of redemption; holders should refer to the notice delivered by the trustee. The filing includes a press release dated July 8, 2021, and was signed by Keith R. Dolliver, VP and Deputy General Counsel.

A mouse study found black tea alters gut bacteria—increasing microbes linked to leanness and decreasing those linked to obesity—suggesting weight-loss benefits. Since black tea acts in the gut while green tea also acts in the liver, combining both may be most beneficial.

A 19-year-old New Hampshire man, Parker Hogan, is charged with aiding his roommate Michael Buskey's suicide. Police say Hogan brought a gun, instructed Buskey on holding it, helped plan the death, and removed a phone and note afterward. Hogan pleaded not guilty and posted bail.

This study examines the digital transformation that advanced technologies—artificial intelligence, metaverse, brain-computer interfaces, blockchain, brain chips, and virtual reality—are expected to bring to open and distance education, particularly in managerial contexts. Using Perrow's work as its theoretical basis, the researchers conducted a qualitative case study based on semi-structured interviews with four academics from Anadolu University, each with at least 20 years of experience in open and distance education. Data were analyzed through content analysis using Nvivo, producing themes and categories under the main themes of education and management.

Findings indicate that advanced technologies will greatly affect future educational environments and that organizations must adapt and reorganize their processes. Participants noted high initial investment costs with potential long-term savings, the need to train artificial intelligence with accurate and up-to-date information, and public mistrust of unmanned systems. Predictions included artificial intelligence occupying managerial positions at all business levels, blockchain enabling centralized control, a shift from hierarchical to horizontal and network organizational structures, and employees unable to use technology being replaced by knowledge workers. Anticipated educational impacts included AI-supported personalized learning, low-cost synthetic content production, AI meta-assistants taking over instructors' guidance roles, and brain chips enabling recognition of prior learning and knowledge transfer.

Regarding the economy, experts emphasized careful cost-benefit analysis before technology integration, potential unemployment among those lacking technological literacy, increased production and profits, the disappearance of entry-level white-collar jobs, and new employment areas for managing technologies. Socio-cultural effects included increased laziness and screen dependence, virtual addiction and psychological problems, disruptive lifestyle changes, and the emergence of a "meta-culture" in virtual societies, for which legal and ethical regulations must be studied.

The study concludes that rapid adaptation is needed in both educational and managerial processes, recommending the development of AI assistants and managers, blockchain-based certification, adaptive synthetic content, metaverse teaching systems, and further research on brain-computer interfaces and brain chips.

Officials marked completion of the 179-megawatt Switch Station 1 and 2 solar projects, commissioned Dec. 11, 2017, near Las Vegas. The plants will power Switch's data centers in Reno and Las Vegas, though capable of supplying 46,000 homes. Attendees included former Sen. Harry Reid, EDF Renewable Energy, and First Solar. Nevada now has 16 solar plants.

A confidential telegram from the Embassy in the Soviet Union assesses US/Soviet relations under the Andropov regime. It concludes that Andropov's foreign policy departs in no way from Brezhnev's, with no flexibility on Afghanistan or Poland and no relaxation on Southern Africa, though the regime remains dependent on its relationship with the U.S. The telegram argues that security—lessening the danger of nuclear war—is the first principle of the relationship, and that arms control, particularly INF rather than START, deserves heightened priority as the only available catalyst for improving relations. It states the zero-zero INF negotiating position has reached the end of its usefulness. Soviet strategy aims to prevent U.S. deployment without affecting theirs by targeting Western European, especially German, public opinion, without proposing destruction of a single SS-20. The deployment decision was primarily political, intended to reassure Europeans, with 572 chosen to establish U.S. credibility.

KGI's Ming-chi Kuo predicts the Apple Watch Series 3 will offer cellular and non-cellular models in 38mm and 42mm sizes with LTE-only modems, forecasting 17.5-18 million sales next year, including 2.8-3.6 million LTE units launching this fall.

A goalie describes difficulty seeing the puck against the larger Zdeno and the adjustments he made, including ensuring shots came from the side. He calls Tico's goal as exciting as an overtime goal, noting the player's often-unnoticed work. He recalls Timmy's early saves, says both goalies made key stops in a tight game he expected to reach overtime, and credits fundamentals practiced with Rollie for staying sharp after a layoff. The team is happy with the win in the series and will focus on Saturday's game.

This patent application describes systems, devices, and methods for delivering neural modulation, particularly for spinal cord stimulation (SCS). The disclosed system includes electrodes on at least one lead, a neural modulation generator, and a programming system that determines electrode fractionalizations based on a target multipole. The target multipole has at least three target poles that directionally and progressively stack fractionalizations to produce a linear electric field over a volume of neural tissue, allowing a user to control field properties to minimize or maximize the field in a specific direction. User inputs may adjust the angle, focus, and spread of the field, define target regions by drawing on anatomical representations or identifying pain areas, adjust gradient controls for therapy strength, and automatically move the target multipole within an electrode array. Search heuristics may optimize pole distances, amplitudes, number of poles, orientation, focus, and spread. The detailed description covers spinal cord physiology, noting that dorsal horn (DH) fibers have activating functions proportional to the first-order derivative of voltage (electric field), while dorsal column (DC) fibers respond to the second-order derivative. Embodiments aim to selectively modulate DH or dorsal root tissue over DC tissue, enabling sub-perception pain therapy without paresthesia. The base field design uses progressively increasing fractionalizations (e.g., 33%/67% for anodes and cathodes) and, compared to a traditional bipole, produces a larger and wider electric field while reducing the second-order voltage derivative. Implementations may use percutaneous leads, paddle leads, multiple leads, or staggered leads, with flanking electrodes for edge guarding and current steering.

Pro se inmate John Bryant sued the New York State Department of Correctional Services (DOCS), Sing Sing Correctional Facility, and Officer Hanser Hernandez under 42 U.S.C. § 1983, alleging violations of his and other inmates' First, Fourth, Fifth, Eighth, and Fourteenth Amendment rights. He claimed a twenty-day "Code Blue" lockdown (December 24, 1999 to January 13, 2000), issued in response to Officer Hernandez's false report of hidden ammunition, confined inmates to their cells and denied them showers, recreation, library access, mail, telephone privileges, hot meals, clean linen, religious services, and non-emergency medical care. He also alleged state labor law violations regarding inmate compensation of 35 cents per day. DOCS moved to dismiss on Eleventh Amendment grounds. The court, adopting the magistrate judge's report, granted dismissal of DOCS and Sing Sing as arms of the state immune from suit, since New York never consented to federal suit and Section 1983 did not abrogate its immunity. Claims against Officer Hernandez may proceed if proper service is made; plaintiff was ordered to report on service status by June 29, 2001.

A Senate committee report made 50 recommendations to speed up criminal trials, favouring a rethink of the justice system over rigid timelines. Senators criticized the Supreme Court's Jordan ruling, which set trial deadlines, warning tens of thousands of charges could be tossed.

The Grand River Conservation Authority is undertaking a $1.8-million project to map floodplains of the Speed and Conestogo rivers and the entire Grand River over five years using LiDAR laser technology, which creates detailed 3D maps from a plane. The digital maps will integrate with new U.S. Army Corps of Engineers flood forecasting software, enabling near real-time flood forecasts. Most existing maps are hard copies over 40 years old.

The Government is launching a consultation on action against irresponsible directors, aiming to give new powers to staff and suppliers affected by insolvencies like Carillion and BHS. Proposals include reversing asset stripping to claw back money for workers, disqualifying directors who sell struggling companies, and strengthening the Insolvency Service. Greg Clark said the reforms would target abuse, while Frank Field welcomed greater accountability and Rebecca Long-Bailey criticised Government inaction.

Engineers have developed a fast optical technique to screen the structural properties of large numbers of protein sequences, including in living bacteria, reported in the journal Analyst. Natural structural proteins like silk, collagen, and wool form a $40 billion industry, but silk loses strength in water, while squid ring teeth proteins, having evolved in wet environments, do not. The team studies natural and synthetic semicrystalline proteins whose properties depend on crystalline structure, which changes with heat. Using femto- and picosecond lasers in flow cytometry with a process called time-domain thermo-transmission, they screen proteins in milliseconds without heating samples or killing cells. After a successful proof-of-concept, Demirel received a DURIP grant to build a machine for larger-scale screening. The work was supported by the Army Research Office.

This paper proposes a methodology by which a trusting agent can determine, before initiating an interaction, the probability of failure in interacting with a probable trusted agent within a digital business ecosystem. Risk, defined as the likelihood that the trusted agent will not act as expected, is dynamic and varies over time; therefore, the total time space under consideration is divided into non-overlapping time slots. FailureLevel (FL) quantifies the probable level of failure on a failure scale ranging from -1 (unknown) to 5. Analysis occurs in two phases: the pre-interaction start time phase, where the Previous FailureLevel (PFL) is determined either from the trusting agent's past interaction history or by soliciting recommendations from other agents (considering recommendation trustworthiness, timing, and criteria relevance), and the post-interaction start time phase, where the Future FailureLevel (FFL) is predicted using the Gaussian distribution applied to prior FailureLevels, yielding the probability of each failure level (0–5) rather than a single crisp value. The methodology is demonstrated through an example in which a trusting agent choosing between two logistic agents analyzes their FailureLevels across four weekly time slots, taking the level with the highest probability of occurrence as the FFL for each post-interaction slot. Determining the possible consequences of failure is noted as future work.

The speaker calls tomorrow night's game a must win, saying players should focus on what they need to do rather than consequences, which can hurt performance. He says all teammates equally want to win the cup, calling it a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. The coaching staff will review defensive tapes and make adjustments to avoid giving up shots, and the team must improve along the boards. He notes Detroit's lines are all strong, making matchups less important.

Fourteenth-ranked Iowa State suffered its first loss of the season, falling 38-30 to Cincinnati in week 6 after trailing 31-7 at halftime. The defeat ends Iowa State's unbeaten start and, per the article, reopens the Big 12 race. The passage recalls last season's chaotic Big 12, when preseason bottom-feeders BYU and Arizona State tied for the regular season title with Iowa State and Deion Sanders' team, while Kansas State, Oklahoma State, and Utah underperformed. The author suggests 2025 could bring similar chaos.

This study evaluated disabled education in accordance with the quality of inclusive education during the distance education process, based on the opinions of ten special education teachers in Kazakhstan. Set against Kazakhstan's State Programme for the Development of Education (2011–2020, with targets extended to 2020–2025), which aimed to expand inclusive education, the paper outlines UNESCO's three focus areas of inclusive education, the right to education of persons with disabilities under the UN Convention, and the compulsory shift to distance education caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. Using a qualitative case study design with convenience purposeful sampling, data were collected through online semi-structured interviews lasting 30–35 minutes and analysed thematically. Findings showed that teachers used online lessons, video sharing, homework and homework checking, online activities and mobile applications. Seven teachers preferred formal education over distance education, and six found distance education insufficient in meeting students' individual learning needs. Regarding family participation, teachers cited families' high anxiety, lack of technological means, lack of communication and inadequate online family education. Teacher–student and peer interaction was described as weak, insufficient in time, unqualified and disorganised. The study concludes that teachers favoured formal education and recommends diversifying technology-based learning methods, creating content based on individual needs, organising online seminars for families, and arranging regular social activities to strengthen interaction.

A memorial match for Aidan Sutherland, a Kirkcaldy footballer and Raith fan who died in July from diabetes complications shortly after his 20th birthday, will be held at Stark's Park on Sunday. Organised by his friend Ben Graham, the event aims to raise diabetes awareness and funds for the Diabetes Research and Wellness Foundation. Friends and former teammates will play alongside Colin Cameron and Darren Dods, with a pipe band, stalls, face painting and a sweetie bar also featured. Kick-off is 1pm, with events starting at noon.

This study analyzed transcriptomic data from three AD cohorts (Knight ADRC, MSBB, and ROSMAP) to investigate the relationship between epilepsy-causing genes and Alzheimer's disease. Researchers identified a synaptic plasticity dysfunction (SPD) subtype of AD and found that 16 epilepsy-associated genes were commonly dysregulated across all three cohorts, with 15 downregulated and one (CERS1) upregulated. Nine of these genes were synaptic, including GABA receptor and sodium channel genes. Pathway analyses revealed enrichment of epilepsy-related pathways, including glutamatergic, GABAergic, and dopaminergic synapse pathways. Gene dysregulation was more pronounced in later AD stages, suggesting epilepsy-causing genes may be associated with both AD onset and progression. The findings support a bidirectional relationship between epilepsy and AD, with shared genetic pathways suggesting potential therapeutic targets for both conditions.

Uranium prices have corrected from their February high, but analysts remain generally bullish. The World Nuclear Association reports 440 operating reactors, with 160 planned and 300 proposed—an overall increase exceeding 100%. Analysts forecast 6% annual demand growth through 2020, with up to 20% of demand uncovered by current production, and prices potentially reaching $65/lb by 2019. Negative sentiment from the 2011 Fukushima disaster has created a disconnect from supply-demand fundamentals. Seasonally, uranium tends toward a flat/low March with rising prices into a July high. The Global X Uranium ETF (URA) shows short-term technical weakness in the stochastic and RSI, though April is typically stronger than March, suggesting a low may form near the 50% Fibonacci level. Traders should watch the April low as first support, with a support cluster near $14.40 and a worst-case fall to the 200-day moving average.

In his farewell address, delivered three days before leaving office after fifty years of public service, the President wishes his successor well and expresses gratitude for his cooperative relationship with Congress. He notes America's strength despite four major wars in the century and reaffirms goals of peace, progress, and liberty, warning against costly, spectacular solutions in favor of balance among national programs. He cautions that the conjunction of a vast military establishment and a permanent arms industry—the military-industrial complex—risks acquiring unwarranted influence, and that only an alert citizenry can safeguard liberty. He also warns that federally funded research could dominate scholars or allow public policy to become captive of a scientific-technological elite. Urging preservation of tomorrow's resources, he supports disarmament built on mutual trust, expresses disappointment that lasting peace remains out of sight though war has been avoided, and closes with thanks and a prayer for all peoples.

The Tax Court addressed whether noncharitable gifts made by check are complete for Federal gift and estate tax purposes upon delivery of the checks to donees. On or about December 24, 1980, decedent Elizabeth C. Dillingham delivered six $3,000 checks to six donees; the checks were cashed on January 28, 1981, when she also delivered six additional $3,000 checks. Petitioner contended the gifts were complete in 1980 because payment of the checks relates back to the delivery date, which would qualify the gifts for the annual exclusion and bar the estate tax assessment under the three-year limitations period. Respondent argued the gifts were not complete in 1980 because payment does not relate back and the decedent retained the power to stop payment.

The court noted that the relation back doctrine, as applied in Estate of Spiegel and Estate of Belcher, was limited to charitable contributions, and that federal courts have been divided on extending it to noncharitable gifts by check. The court declined to extend the doctrine to these cases because petitioner failed to prove unconditional delivery of the checks, citing the unexplained 35-day delay in cashing, the absence of evidence regarding sufficient funds or donative intent, and petitioner's burden of proof. The court also distinguished Don E. Williams Co. as involving a pension plan rather than a gift by check.

Looking to Oklahoma law, the court concluded that a check does not operate as an assignment of funds, that the donees were not holders in due course, and that the donor could have stopped payment and successfully defended against the donees' claims. Accordingly, the court held that a gift by personal check is not complete upon delivery, and that the decedent parted with dominion and control over the funds only when the bank paid the checks in 1981.

The passage describes NVIDIA's GA10x Ampere architecture GPUs and associated technologies. Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity prunes trained weights using a 2:4 non-zero pattern, halving data footprint and doubling math throughput on third-generation Tensor Cores, with virtually no loss in inferencing accuracy across tested networks. DLSS, enhanced by these Tensor Cores and a 9x Super Resolution factor, enables 8K 60 fps gaming on the GeForce RTX 3090.

GA10x GPUs are the first to use GDDR6X memory, developed with Micron Technology, employing PAM4 signaling and MTA encoding to reach data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec bandwidth—a 52% improvement over the TU102. NVIDIA RTX IO, working with Microsoft's DirectStorage API, enables GPU-based loading and lossless decompression, improving I/O performance up to 100x versus hard drives while offloading work from dozens of CPU cores.

The NVIDIA A40 data center GPU delivers up to 2X FP32, 2X ray-tracing, and 5X (10X with sparsity) AI training throughput versus the Quadro RTX 6000, with 48GB memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU includes 10,752 CUDA cores and 48GB of GDDR6.

GA10x supports DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a, HDMI 2.1, HDCP 2.3, fifth-generation NVDEC (including first hardware AV1 decode), and seventh-generation NVENC. The GeForce RTX 3090 (GA102) offers 24GB GDDR6X and is 1.5x faster than TITAN RTX; the RTX 3070 (GA104) outperforms the RTX 2080 Ti but uses GDDR6 and lacks NVLink. A new Error Detection and Replay (EDR) feature helps users identify memory overclocking limits without crashing.

The speaker discusses how the team learns from difficult conversations and in-game corrections. He describes being tired during a six-on-five and staying in front after Steener drove the net. He expresses excitement about returning home, stresses controlling emotions and discipline, notes all players are used in different situations, and says the team did fine when tested, with Fabbs stepping up amid injuries.

WIRED lists discounted toys available during Amazon Prime Day, suitable as gifts for children or for adults. Deals include several Squishmallows plushes (a 20-inch Bigfoot, a cream cow, an avocado, and a pineapple), Magna-Tiles reduced from $50 to $35, and a retired Lego Icons Dried Flower Centerpiece available only through third-party sellers. Other items include a large Play-Doh set, a skeleton-themed build, a 60-piece building kit, blind boxes, a Melissa & Doug ice cream counter for $36, a Crayola Color Wonder Magic Light Brush Station for $16, and a National Geographic rock tumbler kit for $52.

The passage presents a numerical model for methane (CH4) bubble growth in fine-grained aquatic sediments (muds). Gas bubbles, produced by microbial decomposition of organic matter, nucleate under supersaturated conditions and grow beyond the pore scale by fracturing the sediment—a process accurately described by Linear Elastic Fracture Mechanics (LEFM) theory, which characterizes bubbles as Mode I (tensile) gas-filled cracks. The model integrates solute transport of dissolved CH4, solid mechanics (using a Kelvin-Voigt model and the Force Equilibrium Equation), and fracture mechanics. Bubble growth is simulated from a penny-shaped seed until a mature inverted tear-drop configuration forms, marking the onset of bubble ascent toward the seafloor. Fracturing occurs when the stress intensity factor (SIF) exceeds the sediment's fracture toughness, with propagation direction determined by the Strain Energy Density Criterion. The model is implemented in the COMSOL Multiphysics finite element environment with an adaptive meshing strategy, using input parameters based on summer conditions at the NRL site in Eckernförde Bay. Validation against analytical solutions for mature bubble shape and size shows good agreement across varying fracture toughness values. A stated limitation is that the model applies only to individual bubbles; upscaling to effective properties of gassy sediments for remote sensing, geohazard assessment, and CH4 flux estimation remains future work.

This preprint study investigated genetic polymorphisms as diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers for aggressive behavior in cerebral cavernous malformation (CCM). In a single-site prospective observational cohort of 103 CCM patients, researchers evaluated SNPs in PTPN2, VDR, and FCGR2A genes alongside plasma inflammatory cytokines. The PTPN2rs72872125 CT genotype and VDRrs7975232 CC genotype were independently associated with an asymptomatic phenotype, suggesting a protective role. Patients with the PTPN2rs72872125 CT genotype showed higher plasma IL-10 and lower IL-18 and IFN-γ levels, while VDRrs7975232 C allele carriers had low IL-27 and IL-23 levels. A weighted diagnostic biomarker combining PTPN2rs72872125 CC genotype and GM-CSF plasma levels distinguished symptomatic from asymptomatic patients (AUC 0.663). In a 42-patient follow-up subgroup, the FCGR2Ars1801274 GG genotype predicted future symptomatic events with high accuracy (AUC 0.796–0.875), functioning as a prognostic biomarker. Additionally, VDRrs731236 AA was associated with later symptom onset, while VDRrs11568820 CC was linked to earlier symptom onset. In silico analysis showed FCGR2Ars1801274 causes a histidine-to-arginine substitution at position 131 in a domain conserved among higher primates. The study proposes that inflammatory and autoimmune mechanisms may underlie the aggressive behavior of CCM.

Amazon has received a patent for a "directed fragmentation" system that would allow malfunctioning delivery drones to break apart in a controlled manner rather than crash. The drone would constantly update a "fragmentation sequence" based on flight path, weather conditions, and terrain below, releasing components toward preferred locations such as bodies of water, forests, or open fields. Weather extremes, battery failures, or component malfunctions could trigger fragmentation. Parts would be released via latches, hooks, springs, explosive charges, or compressed gas, with selection based on factors including replacement cost. The patent does not guarantee implementation.

This study developed a teacher education program integrating collaborative inquiry with panoramic cameras to enhance teacher education students' (TESs) abilities to diagnose young students' learning problems and improve instructional design capabilities. Twenty-two TESs participated in a course involving collaborative lesson preparation, teaching practice, classroom observation using panoramic cameras, and post-lesson discussions across four cycles. Observation reports, evaluated with a rubric, showed improving diagnostic capabilities, rising from an average of 0.47 in the first cycle to above 1.88 (out of 2) in the fourth. Questionnaire results analyzed with the Wilcoxon signed-rank test revealed statistically significant improvements in perceived capabilities for lesson preparation, linking student learning with teaching practice during observation, and adjusting lesson plans after post-discussion. The study concluded the approach is feasible and effective, though ascertaining the effectiveness of TESs' proposed teaching strategies remains a limitation.

Social media platforms are strengthening moderation policies and using artificial intelligence to combat inappropriate content like hate speech and extremism. While AI can effectively detect offensive text and recognize images, it has significant limitations. Accuracy issues have occurred, such as Google Photos tagging dark-skinned people as "gorillas" and Twitter's outdated algorithm blocking LGBT-related hashtags. AI is inherently biased because it learns from human-tagged training data, and these biases spread when data sets are shared among developers. AI also cannot determine intent—it has removed posts containing swastikas that condemned hate, flagged a statue as sexually explicit, and deleted historic images like the "napalm girl" photograph. Because of these shortcomings, human moderators remain essential; Facebook is expanding its review team to 20,000. AI does improve efficiency by identifying which posts need human review and prioritizing them, such as Facebook's suicide-detection system that prompted 100 emergency calls in one month. Experts note that technology advances faster than laws and ethics, potentially increasing demand for employees with humanities or ethics backgrounds.

In an address to Congress marking sixty years since the government's establishment, the President reports that the United States is stable, at peace with all nations, and has maintained neutrality toward belligerent powers despite wars abroad. Relations with Great Britain are friendly, with reciprocal port access arranged, and diplomatic ties with France have been restored. Aid to a German war steamer was halted to preserve neutrality, and the minister at Frankfort was recalled because no German Empire government was definitively constituted. A military expedition against Cuba was suppressed, and an abducted foreigner was restored; legislation against such abductions is recommended. The United States avoided interference in the Austro-Hungarian conflict, though sympathy for Hungary was expressed. Claims against Portugal remain unsettled. Relations with Mexico are friendly since the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo; the boundary commission needs additional funds, and counsel is recommended for claims adjustment. A convention with Brazil addresses American claims. Amendments to laws on the African slave trade are urged to prevent evasion through sea letters. Treaties were negotiated with Central American states, and a treaty with Nicaragua would protect a proposed ship canal built by private enterprise without Treasury appropriation. The independence of the Sandwich Islands is supported. Treasury receipts exceeded expenditures, but a deficit of about $16 million is projected; borrowing authority, tariff revision with specific duties, and an agricultural bureau are recommended. California has formed a constitution and may seek statehood, as may New Mexico; sectional topics should be avoided. Further recommendations include a branch mint in California, land-title commissions, reconnaissance for a Pacific railroad, river and harbor improvements, Army and Navy reorganization, a uniform 5-cent postage rate, and enactment of the Seventh Census law. The address closes with warnings against encroachment among the branches of government and an affirmation of devotion to preserving the Union.

Connecticut municipal lobbyists from the Council of Small Towns and the Connecticut Conference of Municipalities met with Gov. Dannel P. Malloy to request help coping with the state's financial crisis, including reduced administrative burdens, changes to the municipal retirement system, easier collective bargaining arbitration, and a higher share of land-transfer fees. Malloy, whose state has operated without a budget for six weeks, called the meeting productive. CCM's Joe DeLong said communities were not asking to be "held harmless" on state aid, a claim Senate President Martin Looney called inaccurate. The groups also seek adjustments to the prevailing wage threshold and municipal employee retirement contributions.

This patent application describes methods and systems for manufacturing orthodontic appliances. The disclosed method measures a patient's tooth positions, receives tooth movement constraints, measures elements of the patient's malocclusion, and generates multiple treatment plans with interim and final tooth positions. Treatment plans branch based on malocclusion elements such as openbite, molar class, canine class, posterior crossbite, overjet, and bi-protrusion, with branches including options for bicuspid extraction, interproximal reduction, and correction of upper anterior spaces. A treatment plan is selected, appliance models are generated for each stage, and fabrication instructions are output. A corresponding system embodiment includes a processor and memory executing these steps. The detailed description covers tooth repositioning appliances (aligners) worn sequentially to incrementally reposition teeth, fabrication via direct methods (e.g., stereolithography, selective laser sintering, fused deposition modeling, continuous and multi-material fabrication) or indirect methods (e.g., thermoforming over molds), appliance materials, auxiliary components, computer-based treatment planning, and data processing systems. Branching enables parallel evaluation of multiple clinically distinct treatment plans, which may improve treatment outcomes.

Tesla, Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2018 presents unaudited consolidated financial statements. Tesla, incorporated in Delaware in 2003 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, designs, manufactures and sells electric vehicles and solar energy generation and energy storage products through two segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. As of October 26, 2018, 171,732,775 shares of common stock were outstanding.

For the three months ended September 30, 2018, total revenues were $6.82 billion, up from $2.98 billion in the prior-year quarter, with automotive revenues of $6.10 billion. Net income attributable to common stockholders was $311.5 million ($1.75 diluted per share), compared to a loss of $619.4 million in Q3 2017. For the nine months ended September 30, 2018, the net loss attributable to common stockholders was $1.12 billion. Total assets were $29.26 billion, total stockholders' equity was $4.51 billion, cash and cash equivalents were $2.97 billion, and total debt was $10.90 billion as of September 30, 2018.

On January 1, 2018, Tesla adopted the new revenue standard (ASC 606) using the modified retrospective method, changing revenue recognition for certain vehicle sales with resale value guarantees from operating leases to sales with a right of return and decreasing beginning accumulated deficit by $623.2 million. The filing also covers deferred revenue, warranty reserves, restricted cash, convertible and other debt obligations, and the 2018 CEO Performance Award of 20,264,042 stock options granted in March 2018.

This study assessed COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) transfusion in patients with hematological malignancies, a population with high COVID-19 mortality (34% estimated risk of death, 39% in hospitalized patients) and reduced vaccine response. Within a French monitored access program (May 2020–April 2021), 112 patients with virologically documented COVID-19 received four ABO-compatible CCP units; 74% had B-lymphoid neoplasms and 72% had prior anti-CD20/CD19 therapy. A propensity score (IPTW) analysis with a 16-day landmark approach compared 81 CCP-treated B-cell neoplasm patients with 120 untreated patients. CCP was well tolerated, with few transfusion-related adverse events. After transfusion, temperature, CRP, ferritin, and fibrinogen decreased, while PCR cycle threshold values increased. Ninety-day overall survival was 64.9% for the whole cohort, 77.5% for B-lymphoid neoplasm, 20% for myeloid neoplasm, and 36.8% for plasma-cell neoplasm. Age over 70, high blood pressure, and COVID-19 severity were associated with lower survival, whereas prior anti-CD20/CD19 therapy was associated with better survival. In the main IPTW analysis, CCP was associated with a 63% decrease in the risk of death among anti-CD20 pre-exposed patients. The authors conclude CCP is a promising approach, particularly for B-cell depleted patients, pending confirmation in randomized trials.

This passage is an errata document for the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3, listing hardware issues with descriptions, implications, and resolutions. Key issues include: the PIT does not cancel an uncompleted counter latch command when a read-back command is issued, and count mode 3 loads new values immediately instead of after current counting completes; the GLIU debug port hangs the system when used, though impact is minimal since all internal traffic exits via PCI; the XPIC does not clear the IRR bit until after the second interrupt acknowledge pulse, causing duplicate interrupts when auto-end-of-interrupt (AEOI) is enabled; DMA rotating priority mode does not rotate priorities as expected, though transfers still complete successfully; thermal alarms cannot be detected during Faulted Standby state because the alarm resides in the Work domain; and the PMC Sleep Clock option must be enabled when using SLEEP_X, SLEEP_Y, or SLP_CLK_EN# options. Issue numbers may not be sequential since resolved issues are omitted.

Steve Yzerman said the Tampa Bay Lightning set no timeline for their rebuild, relying on strong drafting, patient player development, and selective free agency rather than quick fixes. He credited home-grown talent—Stamkos and Hedman, acquired before he took the job, plus later-round picks like Kucherov and Palat—and praised his scouting and development staff, noting ownership supported his patience. This passage is a compilation of news articles from March 27–28, 2001, largely concerning Enron Corp. Viacom abandoned its long-stalled plan to split off Blockbuster, citing the video-rental unit's business turnaround. President Bush named Patrick Wood III and Nora Brownell to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, a move that could shift the agency's hands-off approach to California's power crisis.
