The Bittle tree, planted by Roanoke's first President Dr. David Bittle, stood over 100 years before lightning and wind damage made it a hazard. Its wood became the Bittle Tree of Life Cross for Roanoke's 175th anniversary. Created by Reverend Chris Bowen and George Arthur, the cross is the third symbolic feature in Antrim Chapel, symbolizing Bittle's vision and the College's future.

This patent application, a continuation of several prior applications titled "Identification of Audio Content," relates to media playback systems. It describes a playback device that receives digital data representing audio content and uses it in two ways: to play the audio content and to facilitate retrieval of related information. The playback device sends at least a portion of the digital data to an identification system, receives information associated with the audio content (such as metadata or identifiers), and forwards this information to a control device, while playing the audio via speakers electrically connected by a wired connection. This approach avoids requiring the control device to capture and convert audio itself. The playback device may extract data from different positions in its audio pipeline, detect discontinuities in the data (e.g., silence indicating a content change), send data at periodic intervals, convert sample rates, or segregate data by frequency range before sending it for identification. Control devices may send commands to the playback device to retrieve information, receive the results, and display representations of the received information or of metadata retrieved from a metadata curating device. The document also describes an example media playback system environment, including playback devices with processors, memory, audio processing components, and network interfaces; playback zones that can be grouped, split, or reconfigured; control devices with user interfaces; and audio content sources such as local libraries and streaming services.

Electric Resistance Welding (ERW) steel pipes transport petroleum and gas under high and low pressure. ERW offers high production efficiency, low cost, and material savings, and is used in aviation, energy, electricity, and automobile industries. Made from hot-rolled coils with wall thickness controlled at ±0.2mm and burrs removed to 0.2–0.5mm, ERW pipes follow API or GB/T9711.1 standards and are widely used in urban gas networks.

This disclosure relates to directional illumination apparatus and display devices, particularly imaging directional backlights for use in 2D, 3D, and autostereoscopic displays. Conventional spatially multiplexed autostereoscopic displays suffer from reduced resolution, non-uniform viewing windows, and image flicker. The disclosed display device comprises a backlight with plural light sources, a directional waveguide with opposed guide surfaces that deflects input light to exit through a first guide surface, a transmissive spatial light modulator, input and output polarisers, at least one additional polariser, and at least one retarder, which may include switchable liquid crystal retarders and correcting passive retarders such as C-plates or crossed A-plates. This arrangement provides a privacy display with reduced image visibility to off-axis observers while maintaining luminance to the primary user. The waveguide images the light sources so that output light is directed into respective optical windows distributed according to the input positions of the light sources. A control system can switch between privacy and wide angle modes by controlling the light sources and applied voltages across switchable retarders. Embodiments include stepped waveguides (optical valves) with light extraction features and reflective ends. Applications include observer-tracked autostereoscopic displays, multi-viewer displays, privacy displays, and automotive displays mounted beneath transparent windows, offering power savings, high luminance, and thin structures.

Beth Utton argues health care is a right, not a commodity, responding to Rep. Ken Buck's March 25 statement at a Longmont Indivisible meeting. She contends U.S. health care, except Medicare, operates for profit, equating this with treating human life as a commodity, and advocates Medicare for All as a lower-cost alternative. Bonnie New criticizes a Tribune headline about Denver paying nearly $1 million to the family of a teen killed by police, saying it should have noted the teen was committing a crime by driving a stolen car toward an officer. She sympathizes with the family, views the officer's actions as self-defense, opposes the settlement, and defends police.

The Presidential Election Cycle theory, first quantified by Yale Hirsch in the Stock Trader's Almanac, asserts that stock market performance in the first two years of a U.S. president's term tends to outperform the last two years. Markets perform worst in the first year, improve and peak in the third, then drop in the fourth. Since 1952, the S&P 500 averaged 12.5% gains in election years with an incumbent running, versus 6.7% in all election years and -1.5% in open races. Midterm years are typically the weakest until the fourth quarter, when volatility and performance pick up. The pattern is attributed to presidents emphasizing economic stimulus before re-election, though the theory cannot always predict performance accurately. Historical data since the 1930s shows equities and bonds underperform in the year before presidential elections, while the S&P 500 performs better after midterms; the party in power is generally not a predictive factor. Sector-specific volatility, notably in healthcare and energy, tends to increase before elections. Analysts recommend staying invested and rebalancing portfolios, noting that elevated volatility has become a permanent feature of markets.

Intel's Management Engine (ME) is a microcontroller embedded in Intel CPUs over the last decade, connected to all peripherals, always powered on even when the computer is off, and reportedly included partly at the NSA's request. Researchers Mark Ermolov and Maxim Goryachy presented an exploit at BlackHat Europe enabling arbitrary code execution on the ME, though it requires physical access to the machine. The ME evolved from early-2000s Trusted Platform Modules and Active Management Technology, runs Minix, and has remained closed-source. Mitigation options include System76's firmware update, Dell's Latitude 14 laptop with a disabled ME, Intel's detection tool, and the me_cleaner tool, which tricks the ME into believing it has valid firmware. The ME cannot be fully disabled, as computers shut down after thirty minutes without valid ME firmware. The current exploit is limited to physical access; a network-based exploit does not yet exist.

A Deloitte study shows growing consumer confidence in autonomous vehicles, with those believing self-driving cars are unsafe falling from 73% to 49%. Trust is key: 53% have more confidence due to the brands building the vehicles, and 51% trust traditional car manufacturers over technology companies (21%). Consumers still prefer engine-powered vehicles (73%) over electric (2%), citing range, price, and charging infrastructure as barriers. Customer service remains important, with 71% rating it as a key factor. Despite reduced fear, the UK government is launching an inquiry into autonomous vehicle safety.

This paper presents a philosophical analysis of Mortimer J. Adler's thought on Christian education and global education management. It describes Adler's perennialism, which upholds eternal values, continuity of ideas, and learners' holistic development over instant achievement. The authors discuss posthumanism, noting its ambiguous terminology, the view of humans as dependent on their environment, technology's imitation of human nature (including AI and robots), and Spanos's characterization of posthumanist theory as unfinished and context-dependent. Prior studies reviewed include Christian family-based meal programs, spirituality in managing chronic illness stigma, moral education in Christian schools across Spain and Latin America, and character education balancing subjective and objective dimensions. Using a qualitative literature review based on Adler's works and recent journal articles, the paper examines docility and obedience as enduring values involving postponed judgment and trust in teachers' authority, and presents Adler's view that education and democracy operate symmetrically, with education aimed at children's full development rather than job preparation. The authors critique Adler for not differentiating between men and women in education, arguing that women require prior support, including government intervention. Studies of Christian education management in contexts such as Bangkok, Kenya, New Zealand, and Christian family businesses are also surveyed. The conclusion states that educational failure should not be blamed on children, that docility is not natural slavery, and that education management should extend beyond administration toward timeless perennialist values, including within Indonesia's independent curriculum.

Nicola Sturgeon accused Theresa May of calling a snap general election on 8 June to move the UK to the right, force through a hard Brexit and impose deeper cuts, describing the decision as an "extraordinary U-turn" and a "huge political miscalculation". She said May was capitalising on Labour's disarray and putting party interests ahead of the country, and that the election would be about standing up for Scotland. This passage is from the Texas Instruments datasheet (SLASFJ6A, revised September 2025) for the MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 microcontrollers. The devices feature an Arm Cortex-M0+ CPU running up to 32MHz with pre-fetch/cache, SysTick timer, and NVIC. Five operating modes (RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, SHUTDOWN) and two power domains (PD1, PD0) balance performance and power consumption. The document describes the PMU with brown-out reset, a clock module with internal and external oscillator options, a DMA controller with three channels, and an event manager routing events between peripherals, the CPU, and DMA. Memory includes flash with 1KB sectors (up to 100,000 program/erase cycles on selected sectors) and SRAM retained in all modes except SHUTDOWN. Peripherals include up to 45 GPIOs, a 12-bit 1.6-Msps ADC, temperature sensor, VREF, comparator, RTC, UART, I2C, SPI, watchdog timers, and general-purpose/advanced timers. Debugging uses a two-wire SWD interface with a debug subsystem supporting security features such as SWD lockout. The document also covers factory constants, typical application schematic recommendations, device nomenclature (MSP versus X prefixes), development tools and support resources, revision history (July to September 2025 changes including removal of the DGS32 package), and mechanical packaging information.

Ed Sachse, 56, president of property services at Kennedy Wilson, oversees brokers and 21 million square feet of U.S. properties from the firm's Beverly Hills headquarters. He began a window-washing business at 15 in Detroit, then studied accounting at Michigan State and worked at Arthur Andersen before moving to Los Angeles, where he became CFO of Camden Financial under Douglas Emmett. He later became a broker at Coldwell Banker, selling an empty school to the Simon Wiesenthal Center, and started his own property management and brokerage firm in 1993. Diagnosed with stage 4 non-Hodgkin lymphoma in 2001, he ran his business through six years of treatment. After the Great Recession, he contacted 40 potential clients in 2009; Kennedy Wilson instead offered to buy his company, and he agreed. He lives in Pacific Palisades with his wife Julie and plays in a garage band.

Lawyers for Venezuelan citizens with Temporary Protected Status (TPS) asked the Supreme Court on Monday to leave in place a federal judge's order barring the Trump administration from ending their protected status. Congress created TPS in 1990; then-DHS Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas designated Venezuela in 2021, redesignated it in 2023, and extended the program through October 2026. DHS Secretary Kristi Noem later terminated the designation and extension. Challengers argued the termination violated federal administrative law and the Constitution. District Judge Edward Chen temporarily blocked the termination in March, but the Supreme Court put his order on hold in May. In September, Chen issued a final ruling finding Noem acted unlawfully, and the lower courts declined to stay it. Solicitor General D. John Sauer asked the Supreme Court to intervene, while the challengers argued the prior stay order did not foreclose a final judgment.

The invention relates to optical waveguide display apparatus and methods in which image-bearing light is injected into a waveguide and released for viewing. Prior art waveguides have a field of view (FOV) limited by total internal reflection (TIR) requirements, and the FOV varies with wavelength because a Bragg grating diffracts different wavelengths to different angles, causing light at extreme angles to escape the waveguide.

The invention addresses this by coating the external surfaces of the waveguide, against which guided light reflects internally, with a material (e.g., a meta-material) having a refractive index substantially equal to or less than 1.0 at optical wavelengths. This reduces the critical angle for TIR, allowing light otherwise outside the field of view to be retained and guided, thereby expanding the FOV and/or extending the operating wavelength range to enable wider-field-of-view colour displays.

The apparatus comprises an optical waveguide with a first diffractive part (e.g., a Bragg grating) to diffract received display light for guided propagation by TIR, and a second diffractive part to diffract light for output. The first and second diffractive parts may be mutually conjugated, which reduces geometric distortions and substantially negates chromatic dispersion, particularly beneficial for broadband sources such as LEDs.

The meta-material may comprise a periodic "fish-net" structure of unit cells, each containing a magnetic resonator (e.g., alumina sandwiched between silver plates) between opposing conductive meshes, or alternatively parallel conductive wires. Geometrical parameters may be optimised to achieve refractive index values (real part) between 0.0 and 1.0.

A multi-layered slab waveguide structure may be used for multi-colour displays, with component slab waveguides tuned to different colours, joined and protected by an intermediate meta-material layer that also prevents contaminant ingress. The coating protects exposed Bragg gratings and surfaces from damage and contamination, and optional outer protective layers (e.g., plastic) may be applied. The meta-material coating may be omitted from areas over input/output gratings to avoid optical attenuation losses.

President Rutherford B. Hayes issued a proclamation on July 18, 1877, citing constitutional provisions for federal protection against domestic violence. Responding to West Virginia's governor's report of violence at Martinsburg and along the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad that state authorities could not suppress, Hayes admonished citizens against aiding the unrest and warned participants to disperse by noon on July 19.

Sheffield's Lord Mayor Magid Magid, 28, has branded Donald Trump a 'wasteman' and banned him from the city ahead of his July 13 visit. In a viral photo, Magid wore a sombrero in solidarity with Mexico and a t-shirt reading 'Donald Trump is a wasteman,' and declared July 13 Mexico Solidarity Day. Magid, who moved from Somalia to Yorkshire aged five, cited five reasons for his stance: the Muslim ban, withdrawing from the Paris climate agreement, moving the US embassy to Jerusalem, imprisoning children at borders, and defending white supremacists. He also criticized Theresa May for not banning Trump from the UK. Magid is Sheffield's youngest Lord Mayor, the first from the Green Party, and the first with a marine biology degree.

This lecture reviews three major renewal theorems—the strong law for renewals, the elementary renewal theorem, and Blackwell's theorem—noting that expected values alone do not fully characterize renewal behavior. Blackwell's theorem states that for arithmetic inter-renewal intervals with span λ, the expected number of renewals in an interval approaches λ/x̄. The lecture then analyzes age and duration at a given time for arithmetic renewal processes, showing that the joint probability of age and duration depends only on the inter-renewal interval's pmf, yielding expected duration E[X²]/E[X] and expected age E[X²]/(2E[X]); the factor of 1/2 arises from evaluating age at integer times. The second half introduces countable-state Markov chains, where recurrence must be defined as return to a state with probability 1. Examples include a Markov chain model of a Bernoulli process, whose state distribution spreads like a quantized Gaussian with no steady-state probabilities, and birth-death chains, which are recurrent for p < 1/2, non-recurrent for p > 1/2, and a strange case at p = 1/2. First passage time probabilities f_ij(n) are defined, and if return to a state occurs with probability 1, the sequence of returns forms a renewal process. States in the same class are both recurrent or both transient, with null recurrent states having infinite expected return time.

The author nearly died from sepsis in 2015 after a scratch from a nail led to a coma, but survived after three months and a year of recovery. Sepsis affects over 30 million people annually worldwide, killing an estimated 6 million, and 40% of survivors develop lasting post-sepsis syndrome. It begins with an infection but is caused by the body's uncontrolled immune response, leading to organ failure. Symptoms include mottled skin, severe breathlessness, shivering, muscle pain, and nausea; emergency services should be called immediately. There is no specific cure, though research on metformin and gene therapy shows promise. Awareness remains low globally, and greater recognition of symptoms among the public and medical professionals is the most effective short-term defence.

Stanley Furniture and La-Z-Boy are compared as small-cap consumer discretionary stocks. Analysts favor La-Z-Boy, which has a consensus target price of $30.33 (11.31% upside), while Stanley Furniture has no ratings. La-Z-Boy has higher institutional ownership (86.8% vs. 29.7%), greater revenue ($1.54 billion vs. $43.64 million), and positive earnings, whereas Stanley Furniture has negative earnings. La-Z-Boy is more profitable, with a 5.45% net margin versus Stanley's -6.38%. La-Z-Boy pays a $0.44 annual dividend (1.6% yield); Stanley pays none. Stanley Furniture is less volatile (beta 0.34 vs. 0.89) and trades at a lower price-to-earnings ratio. Overall, La-Z-Boy outperforms Stanley Furniture on 12 of the 14 factors compared.

The paper addresses privacy protection in AI-driven intelligent education systems, focusing on face anonymization in scientific experiment videos, where faces must be blurred while instruments and students' operational techniques remain visible for assessment. Existing anonymization approaches (multi-object tracking, clustering, and GAN-based methods) and segmentation models (SAM, Edge-SAM) are either not tailored to this task or too slow for real-time video.

The authors propose MSFF-YOLOv8, a modified YOLOv8 architecture with enhanced multi-scale feature fusion and an added semantic segmentation branch, combined with a Contour-Adaptive Occlusion Refinement (CAOR) data preprocessing module that dilates occlusion contours toward the face center to prevent mis-blurring of instruments. The system uses face detection, BOTSort tracking, and Gaussian blurring, applying fine anonymization to primary experimenters and coarse bounding-box blurring to non-primary ones.

A dataset was built from 51 experiment videos across physics, biology, and chemistry, containing 7,590 face and 5,240 instrument labels plus tracking data. Evaluation used FPS, SOBA (blur accuracy), and OBR (over-blur rate). MSFF-YOLOv8 with CAOR at 1920-pixel input achieved 96.02% accuracy at 22.67 fps on 1080p video, with OBR reduced to 0.0159, outperforming YOLOv8, SAM, and Edge-SAM. Future work targets precise edge classification during real-time inference.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says intellectual property is trickier for video than images, telling analyst Ben Thompson on the Stratechery podcast that video "feels much more real and lifelike" with stronger emotional resonance, causing rights holders to respond differently. OpenAI's Sora app has produced viral unauthorized videos featuring characters like SpongeBob and Pikachu, prompting Altman to announce more granular controls for rightsholders. He said most rights holders are excited to have content in the app but want more restrictions than for images, and he predicts companies will eventually welcome AI-generated content.

The speaker dismisses outside perceptions, stating the team earned its Stanley Cup Finals spot by defeating three strong teams. He calls teammate Mike Peca the best all-around player in hockey. The team's success stems from physical play by big, mobile forwards like Rasmussen, Varada, Primeau, and Grosek who forecheck hard. The layoff allowed relaxation and emotional preparation. Despite lacking Stanley Cup rings, the team gained experience overcoming adversity and expects no added nervousness playing Dallas.

Scientists are making progress toward fully understanding and manipulating human memories. Combining the discovery of "face cells"—neurons linked to specific people's faces—with research on CREB, a protein active during learning, suggests that activating neuron groups before learning could pinpoint where memories are stored. Because "reconsolidation" occurs during memory recall, memories may be implanted or altered. Dr. Susumu Tonegawa's MIT team created an artificial negative association with a harmless situation and later reversed it, showing memory manipulation is possible.

Trade deficits reduce US demand and can raise unemployment, but this can be offset through budget deficits or bubbles like the stock and housing bubbles. The passage rejects the claim that the dollar's reserve currency status forces trade deficits, noting other currencies are also held as reserves and that countries like China deliberately hold excess dollars for trade advantage. The author criticizes Samuelson's complaints about China's technology transfer requirements, arguing companies like Boeing and Apple voluntarily invested in China and are better positioned than typical workers to protect their interests.

This article presents an RSI(2) mean reversion trading strategy applied to QQQ. The strategy enters a position when the two-day RSI falls below 10 and exits when today's close exceeds yesterday's high. The basic strategy returned 10.01% versus 6.39% for buy and hold, performing well during four bear markets (2000-2002, 2008/09, 2018, and Covid-19 in March 2020). Adding a second indicator improved results further, producing a CAGR of 12.7%, 75% winners, a profit factor of 3, a maximum drawdown of 19.5%, and a Sharpe Ratio of 2.85, with only 14% of time spent in the market. Tightening the buy threshold to below 5 increased average gains but reduced total returns due to fewer trades. The strategy's code is available for purchase or via subscription.

The SD Memory Card is designed to meet the security, capacity, performance, and environment requirements of audio and video consumer electronic devices. It includes SDMI-compliant content protection using mutual authentication and a cipher algorithm, and may support a second security system based on standards such as ISO-7816. The SDIO Card provides I/O functionality, optionally with memory, and is compatible with the SD Memory Card. Communication uses a 9-pin interface operating at up to 208 MHz.

This lecture covers auction theory and applications. Auctions are widely used in government procurement, Treasury bill sales, online advertising, and spectrum licensing. The independent private values model assumes each bidder's value depends only on their own signal and that bidders are risk neutral. In second price sealed bid auctions, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy, and seller revenue equals the expected second-highest value. Oral ascending (button) auctions are strategically equivalent, though experiments show people tend to overbid in second price formats. In first price sealed bid auctions, bidders shade their bids below their values; with uniform values, the optimal bid is (n−1)/n times one's value, which equals the expected second-highest value conditional on winning. The revenue equivalence theorem states that mechanisms awarding the object to the highest-value bidder, with zero surplus for the lowest type, yield identical expected revenue and bidder utilities. The theorem's limitations include risk aversion (where first price auctions raise more revenue), correlated values (where second price auctions do better), and its restriction to always-allocate mechanisms. Reserve prices should be set at the monopoly price, though entry costs and commitment problems can undermine them. In common value auctions, bidders face the winner's curse—winning reveals others' signals were less optimistic—so rational bidders shade accordingly. The Hendricks-Porter study of offshore oil lease auctions examines wildcat versus drainage tracts, where incumbents with adjacent wildcat tracts hold informational and cost advantages. A mixed strategy equilibrium predicts incumbents win over half the time and earn high profits while uninformed bidders earn zero; data from 114 drainage tract auctions (1959–1969) largely confirmed these predictions, illustrating how asymmetric information deters competition.
In HS mode, the ADS7828 stretches the clock LOW after the read-addressing byte is received until conversion completes. To remain in HS mode, issue a repeated START instead of a STOP.

An Alberta Education survey of nearly 10,000 people, half of them teachers, found respondents wanted more emphasis on practical skills and the basics of reading, writing and math in draft K-12 curriculum documents. Social studies drew the strongest views, with some supporting First Nations, Métis and Inuit content while others worried about global history being displaced or students being indoctrinated. Most respondents felt the drafts fostered literacy, numeracy and critical thinking. The overhaul, announced in 2016, aims to complete the K-4 curriculum by December, with higher grades following until 2022.

The BGF China Flexible Equity Fund provides investors access to both onshore (A-shares) and offshore Chinese equities through a single strategy, addressing the under-ownership of onshore stocks by global investors. Managed by Helen Zhu, Head of Chinese Equities at BlackRock, and supported by 10 China-focused research analysts, the long-only, fundamentals-driven, concentrated portfolio invests in 20-50 companies from over 3,300 onshore and 1,000 offshore stocks, exploiting valuation differences and sector-specific opportunities.

This study examines the perceptions and experiences of students enrolled in face-to-face tour guiding departments in Türkiye regarding Emergency Distance Education (EDE), implemented due to the Covid-19 pandemic. EDE, defined by the Turkish Council of Higher Education as the temporary transfer of face-to-face education to a technological environment during a crisis, was adopted by Turkish universities beginning in March 2020. Using a qualitative phenomenological design, data were collected from 81 students at Istanbul universities during the 2022–2023 academic year through semi-structured interviews and an online questionnaire, and analyzed via thematic content analysis.

Findings indicate that students considered EDE insufficient for tour guiding education (TGE), citing insufficient vocational courses, lack of effective communication, and motivation problems. Word association tests revealed both negative perceptions (attention problems, equipment deficiencies, socialization issues) and positive perceptions (cost savings, convenience) of distance TGE. Identified advantages of EDE included effective time management (46.5%), compensation through recorded courses, location independence, savings, and ease of access to materials. Disadvantages included inappropriacy for TGE (29.7%), lack of motivation, lack of communication, technical problems, and low attendance. Nearly two-thirds of students (59.2%) judged distance education inadequate for practical training, and 81.4% perceived differences between the two modes, mainly in efficiency, socialization, concentration, unidirectionality, and self-expression. Most students (88.8%) reported understanding their distance courses.

The study concludes that although students prefer face-to-face education for its practical and interactive benefits, they acknowledge certain advantages of distance education, producing a dilemma. The authors suggest hybrid education and improved communication systems could foster more positive attitudes. Limitations include the focus on EDE in Türkiye, exclusion of regular distance education programs, and the limited generalizability of the exploratory qualitative design.

This passage introduces the ebook edition of *Foreign Relations, 1981–1988, Volume I: Foundations of Foreign Policy*, released by the Office of the Historian at the U.S. Department of State in September 2022. The ebook offers the full content of the printed FRUS volume with features such as full-text search, bookmarking, and offline access, and recommends citing document numbers rather than page numbers. The FRUS series, established in 1861, presents the official documentary record of major U.S. foreign policy decisions and diplomatic activity. Editing standards set by Secretary Kellogg in 1925 guided the series through 1991, when Public Law 102–138 established a statutory charter requiring a thorough, accurate, and reliable record, adherence to objectivity, disclosure of deletions, and publication within 30 years. Most sources in this volume are declassified and available at the National Archives.

Data culture aligns organizations vertically, through data-driven metrics that connect individuals and groups to company goals, and horizontally, through common data models and transparent access that enable collaboration. Digital leaders treat data culture as central, using it to align beliefs, values, and daily actions, while digital laggards often show gaps between espoused values and actual behavior, hindered by entrenched habits, skill gaps, and insufficient top-down focus. Changing mindsets is the most challenging part of transformation, but laggards are not doomed, and even leaders identify areas for cultural growth. Mature firms establish beliefs around learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement. Organizations fit one of four patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, or data reliant—and can take targeted actions from these starting points to build a strong data culture. The passage concludes by describing Keystone Strategy, a consulting firm.

Brad Vis, who narrowly lost Mission-Matsqui-Fraser Canyon to Liberal Jati Sidhu in 2015 by just over 1,000 votes, has been chosen as the Conservative candidate for next year's federal election. A former staffer for MP Ed Fast, Vis criticized Liberal spending and pledged outreach across the sprawling riding.

A hockey player reflects on a loss, saying he felt good and saw the puck well but the opponent simply played better. He credits Friesen's patience on the first goal, admitting he went down too early. He notes the opponent's strong second period and says his team must use its speed, shoot more, and create traffic in front of the net. He calls the experienced Devils a great team that outplayed and outskated them, praises Jeff's performance, dismisses time off as a factor, and stresses the need to bounce back in the next game, which he calls the biggest of the year.

This study examines the relationship between multilingualism proficiency and cultural awareness among university students in Indonesia. Using an embedded mixed-methods design (QUAN with qualitative), data were collected via Google Forms from 388 students sampled from six institutions (population N=537) between January and February 2024. Eight variables were measured: Multilingualism Competency (MC), Multilingual Learning Process (MLP), Psychological Factors (PF), Social Interaction (SI), Cultural Knowledge and Communication (CKC), Cultural Practices and Participation (CPP), Sociocultural Context (SC), and Capacity and Attitude towards Cultural Learning (CAC). Pearson correlation analysis showed all hypothesized relationships were significant (p < .001), with correlations between multilingual learning and cultural awareness variables ranging from 0.245 to 0.553; the strongest was MC-SC (r = 0.553). Indonesian was the dominant mother tongue (61.08%), Javanese, Bugis, and Makassarese were the most studied local languages, and English was the most studied foreign language (63.40%). Qualitative thematic analysis identified strategies including educator training, technological support, cultural integration in curricula, inclusive content, and intercultural collaboration. The study concludes that multilingual learning and cultural awareness are interrelated and mutually reinforcing, offering insights for practitioners and policymakers in Indonesian higher education.

JD Wetherspoon's is opening a new 1,600sq metre pub in Dublin city centre between 2019 and 2022, using two historic buildings on Lower Abbey Street connected by a glazed link. The Circuit Licensing Court granted a full drinks and restaurant license, subject to planning permission. The company operates six other gastropubs in Dublin, Dún Laoghaire and Cork. Though known for cheap deals, its prices have risen in recent years.

Amazon.com, Inc.'s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2015 reports that the company, incorporated in Delaware and headquartered in Seattle, Washington, completed its IPO in May 1997 and trades on NASDAQ under "AMZN." Beginning in the first quarter of 2015, Amazon reorganized into three reportable segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). The company serves consumers through retail websites and electronic devices (Kindle, Fire tablets, Fire TVs, Echo), sellers through marketplace programs, developers and enterprises through AWS, and content creators through Kindle Direct Publishing and Amazon Publishing. It employed approximately 230,800 full- and part-time employees as of December 31, 2015, and recognized 33% of 2015 revenue in the fourth quarter. Risk factors include intense competition, expansion strains, international regulatory restrictions (notably in China and India), fulfillment network optimization, seasonality, data security, inventory management, intellectual property, taxation, and payments-related risks. In 2015, net sales were $107.0 billion, up 20%, comprising $63.7 billion from North America, $35.4 billion from International, and $7.9 billion from AWS. Income from operations was $2.2 billion and net income was $596 million. Operating cash flow was $11.9 billion, and total assets were $65.4 billion. The company has never declared or paid cash dividends.

Suzanne Nimocks of McKinsey forwarded to Steven Kean at Enron a December 6, 2000 memorandum, "Power sector restructuring: international activity, June - November 2000," a periodic update on global electric power privatization and restructuring. The memorandum reports that privatization and restructuring continue worldwide: governments facing growing demand but lacking funds are opening generation markets to foreign investors, state-owned utilities are unbundling, and competition is being introduced at wholesale and retail levels. Some international players have scaled back and shifted portfolios to less risky markets such as the U.S. and Europe. Regional findings include: Europe, where the EU Directive has spurred competition, markets are opening in phases by country, and mergers, alliances, and consolidation dominate; Central and Eastern Europe, where privatization attracts needed capital, the IMF urges reforms, and EU membership candidates are moving forward; Asia-Pacific, where recovering economies are reviving unbundling and restructuring plans despite IPP problems with power purchase agreements and lack of government guarantees; Latin America, where inflation, currency fluctuations, ownership limits, and drought-related hydro power shortages have slowed privatization, though transmission concessions and privatizations are increasingly offered; and Africa and the Middle East, where governments are increasingly open to foreign investment, mostly through IPPs, with regional transmission link schemes emerging. Country-by-country developments are detailed for each region, and exhibits summarize restructuring status and market-opening timelines.

This paper proposes a methodology enabling a trusting agent in a Digital Business Ecosystem to determine, before interacting with a probable trusted agent, the probability of not achieving the full benefit of its invested resources. Risk, defined as the combination of probability of failure and its consequences, is analyzed using the previously defined "FailureLevel" concept, which quantifies failure on a Failure scale. The interaction's time space is divided into non-overlapping time slots across pre- and post-interaction start time phases. In pre-interaction slots, a crisp FailureLevel is determined from past interaction history or recommendations; in post-interaction slots, the magnitude of occurrence of each failure level is predicted instead, accounting for risk's dynamic nature.

The paper then introduces the Amount Invested Curve (AIC), which gives the probability of a net amount of financial resources being invested and at stake throughout each time slot, considering investment patterns. The Factual Amount Invested Curve (FAIC) is derived by convolving the AIC with the trusted agent's FailureLevel using the cumulants method, showing the increased investment probability required given possible failure. Finally, the Loss of Resource Benefit (LORB) index—the ordinate on the FAIC at the end of the AIC—gives the probability of not achieving full resource benefit in each time slot, helping the trusting agent make informed decisions about which trusted agent to interact with.

Jeong-Suk Cha, 77, cares for her 48-year-old son Alex, who has cerebral palsy and spinal cord damage from falls in 2004 and 2015. Alex is on a wait list for a bed at London's Participation House, which has 40 spaces and 60 to 90 people waiting; agencies call such lists the "50-year wait list." A $100-million class-action lawsuit filed by Toronto law firm Koskie Minsky claims Ontario denies services to developmentally disabled adults through wait lists administered in an "ad hoc, inconsistent and unreasonable manner." Ontario Ombudsman Paul Dube previously reported 9,700 people waiting for residential care province-wide. The South West LHIN acknowledges it lacks data on medically complex adults seeking residential care. After MPP Peggy Sattler raised the issue, Health Minister Dr. Eric Hoskins promised to look into it. Alex's sister Jin organizes his care, including 90 hours monthly of personal support worker help (temporarily raised to 140), while their mother provides most daily care. The only alternative offered is long-term care with seniors, which Alex rejects, stating he would rather die than go to a nursing home.

The U.S. Department of State's Office of the Historian released an ebook edition of the Foreign Relations of the United States (FRUS) series, established in 1861. The ebook offers full content, search, bookmarking, note-taking, and offline access while maintaining fidelity with the printed edition; readers are advised to cite document numbers rather than page numbers. The supplementary volume covers the period of U.S. neutrality, with some topics extending beyond April 6, 1917, and includes papers on Latin-American countries, China, Siam, and Liberia. Editorial conventions are described: brackets mark editorial insertions or suggested corrections, parentheses may contain decoders' suggested readings of garbled text, and translations were revised only if found faulty.

The Shuffle offense, predecessor of the Princeton, Flex, Hawk, and Reverse Action offenses, originated with Bruce Drake at Oklahoma. It uses constant player movement and teamwork to create high-percentage shots, eliminating defensive help and drawing taller players away from the basket. All five players rotate through each position, making it ideal for teams lacking height. The offense involves little dribbling and requires strong fundamentals in passing, receiving, spacing, screening, and rebounding, with emphasis on ball possession.

The basic continuity includes reversal passes, a rub cut off a post screen for a layup, a pass to a post popping off a down screen, and a flash cut to the middle. The rub cut is the heart of the offense, with counters based on defensive reads: cutting over or under the screen, switching, bumping back off a double screen, and the post popping out for a shot. Flash players serve as rebounder, shooter, and screener. Against defensive overplay, back cut counters include wing back cuts, dribble clears, point back door cuts, and post lobs.

The passage describes NVIDIA's GA10x Ampere GPU architecture. GA10x GPUs feature a PCIe 4.0 host interface providing up to 64 GB/sec of peak bandwidth. The full GA102 GPU contains seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, 84 SMs, and 112 ROPs, with ROPs now located within the GPC rather than tied to memory controllers. Each GA10x SM contains 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, one second-generation RT Core, and 128 KB of L1/Shared Memory. FP32 processing occurs on both datapaths, doubling FP32 throughput compared to Turing, and Ampere GPUs are up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing GPUs.

The second-generation RT Core doubles the ray/triangle intersection testing rate over Turing and adds an Interpolate Triangle Position unit enabling hardware-accelerated ray-traced motion blur. GA10x SMs can run RT Core, graphics, and compute workloads concurrently. Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32 and BF16 data types and a Sparsity feature that doubles matrix multiplication throughput. DLSS is enhanced with a 9x Super Resolution scaling factor, enabling 8K gaming at 60 fps.

GA10x introduces GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling, delivering up to 936 GB/sec of bandwidth. NVIDIA RTX IO enables GPU-based loading and lossless decompression of game assets in conjunction with Microsoft's DirectStorage API. The A40 data center GPU offers 48GB of memory, scalable to 96GB via third-generation NVLink. GA10x supports HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4a, fifth-generation NVDEC (including AV1 hardware decode), and seventh-generation NVENC. The GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102 with 24GB of GDDR6X, while the RTX 3070 uses GA104. A new Error Detection and Replay feature assists memory overclocking. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU includes a GA102 GPU with 48GB of GDDR6.

This passage describes the AEGEAN study, which evaluated adherence to apixaban therapy in subjects with atrial fibrillation using an electronic medication device (EMD). Subjects were randomized to a Primary Standard of Care (SOC) group or an Additional Education Program group. The primary endpoint was the percentage of days with correct apixaban dosing execution at 24 weeks; secondary endpoints assessed adherence at 12 and 48 weeks.

In total, 1162 subjects were randomized (583 Primary SOC, 579 Additional Education Program). Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups, with a median age of 74 years, 59.9% male, and 96.4% with atrial fibrillation.

At 24 weeks, mean adherence was 91.64% in the Primary SOC group and 91.88% in the Additional Education Program group, with no significant difference (p=0.8117). Adherence was significantly lower from Week 12 to 24 than during the first 12 weeks in both groups, and similarly lower from Week 24 to 48. Persistence at 24 weeks was approximately 91% in both groups and 85–88% at 48 weeks, with no significant differences. Logit models showed that in the Primary SOC group, non-adherence increased with alcohol consumption, technical occupations, and permanent atrial fibrillation, and decreased with higher MMSE scores; no variables significantly predicted non-adherence in the Additional Education Program group at 24 weeks.

Safety outcomes were similar between groups. Before Week 24, 51.2% and 52.0% of subjects reported at least one adverse event, with bleeding events in 6.5% and 9.0%, respectively. Overall, 24 deaths were reported. The study concluded that adherence and persistence were high during the first 24 weeks and sustained up to 48 weeks, and that the proactive educational program did not provide additional adherence or persistence benefits.
The speaker calls the arena a fantastic playoff venue that can favor Philadelphia, and praises a calm, quiet teammate who makes big saves despite opponents' attempts to bump him.

The Brunswick school board approved the first step toward placing a 10-year, $4.67 million emergency levy renewal, expiring next year, on the May ballot, with no tax increase. It also approved issuing notes up to $10 million for a new middle school replacing Visintainer and Edwards and other improvements, and revised Fiscal Year 2018 appropriations as several grants, including IDEA Part B, increased. Superintendent Michael Mayell thanked four donors, and the board recognized departing 12-year member Lisa Durichko. An executive session produced no action; organizational and regular meetings are set for Jan. 8 and Jan. 22.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K reporting that on November 6, 2017, its wholly-owned subsidiary NVIDIA Land Development, LLC exercised its option to terminate a Ground Lease and Real Property Lease with Wachovia Service Corporation and purchase the real property containing NVIDIA's new Santa Clara campus building in Santa Clara, California, for approximately $350 million. The original agreements were entered into on June 19, 2015 with Wachovia, Wells Fargo Bank, N.A., and a syndicate of institutions for construction and lease of the building, which was substantially completed on October 31, 2017. The purchase price covers repayment of the Participants' investment, capitalized interest, accrued unpaid rent, and fees and expenses. Upon completion, the agreements will terminate and NVIDIA Land will hold the property free and clear of secured financing. A majority of Participants waived the 90-day advance notice requirement, and NVIDIA expects to complete the purchase in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2018. Separately, on November 9, 2017, NVIDIA issued a press release and CFO Commentary announcing results for the third quarter and first nine months of fiscal 2018, attached as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2.

The passage describes SD Memory Card specifications. Cards contain a User Area and a Protected Area, with Card Capacity being their sum. Capacity types are SDSC (up to 2GB), SDHC (over 2GB up to 32GB), and SDXC (over 32GB up to 2TB). Five Speed Classes (0, 2, 4, 6, 10) define minimum card performance. SD bus communication uses command and data bit streams: commands are 48-bit tokens protected by 7-bit CRC, responses are 48 or 136 bits, and data transfers occur in blocks protected by CRC (16-bit CCITT polynomial for block data). The card form factor is 24mm x 32mm x 2.1mm or 1.4mm, and cards hold registers including CID, RCA, DSR, CSD, SCR, OCR, SSR, and Card Status. UHS-I cards reach up to 104MB/sec via modes DS, HS, SDR50, DDR50, and SDR104, with 1.8V signaling entered through a voltage switch sequence (CMD11) and sampling point tuning via CMD19. UHS-II cards support up to 624MB/s (FD624 mode) through a separate interface with its own initialization sequence. ROM Cards are read-only and treat write-related commands as illegal. Card operation includes identification mode (reset via CMD0, voltage verification via CMD8, operating conditions via ACMD41, CID via CMD2, RCA via CMD3) and data transfer mode. Data is read/written in blocks up to 512 bytes with CRC checks; erase operations include ERASE, DISCARD, and FULE. Write protection is provided by a mechanical switch, internal card protection, and password-based lock/unlock via CMD42 using PWD registers, with optional Card Ownership Protection (COP) employing FEP and requiring COP Unlock after reset when FEP is set.

A player who stayed in Finland longer than usual before joining the NHL, after winning two championships, scored in a Stanley Cup Finals game, calling it his best performance. He said the team should shoot more, aims to keep the same effort, and is happy he chose the Sharks, who first showed interest in him.

TDSAT passed an interim order staying Trai's tariff order clauses on 'reporting requirement' and 'significant market power', ruling that no penalty can be imposed on operators for non-compliance with tariff reporting until further orders. This followed Trai's 15 March show-cause notice to Airtel for failing to report segmented retention tariffs. Trai can still seek details of retention discounts. While Airtel and Idea challenged the order before TDSAT, Vodafone moved the Madras high court. Incumbent operators argue the new norms favor Reliance Jio.

Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) is the leading cause of maternal mortality worldwide, yet no biomarkers currently predict PPH risk before labor. Because placental angiogenic biomarkers are established predictors of preeclampsia, this study examined whether first- and second-trimester placental biomarkers relate to postpartum bleeding using the NuMoM2b dataset. The analytic sample included 2,192 nulliparous participants with singleton pregnancies; a composite outcome of retained placenta and/or hemorrhage requiring blood transfusion (RP/PPH) served as a proxy for greater blood loss. Sixty-seven participants (3.1%) experienced RP/PPH. Second-trimester levels of sEng, β-hCG, inhibin A, PAPP-A, and sFlt-1 were significantly elevated in the RP/PPH group, as were first-trimester sFlt-1 and the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio; PlGF did not differ at either time point. When stratified by preeclampsia status, second-trimester β-hCG, inhibin A, PAPP-A, and sFlt-1 remained significantly elevated among women without preeclampsia, while no significant absolute biomarker differences were found among preeclamptic women. The magnitude of change between trimesters also differed by preeclampsia status. Limitations include the absence of direct blood loss measurement, a small RP/PPH sample, and over-representation of adverse pregnancy outcomes. The authors conclude that second-trimester placental biomarkers are promising targets for future PPH risk screening.

Five Gor Mahia players—holder Kenneth Muguna, Meddie Kagere, Musa Mohammed, Jacques Tuyisenge and George Odhiambo—head the shortlist for the 2017 Kenyan Premier League MVP award, putting the club in line for a third consecutive player of the year award. Other MVP nominees include Massoud Juma, Patrick Matasi and Lawrence Juma. With KPL postponing its awards, the Sports Journalists Association of Kenya will hold its own awards, sponsored by LG among others, after two seasons of collaboration with KPL. Matasi leads the goalkeeper of the year list, while Musa Mohammed and Karim Nizigiyimana headline the defenders' category. The SJAK Football Gala, featuring eight categories, will be held on December 18, with prize awards yet to be announced.

Patterns in distributed systems offer value beyond learning: they provide a shared vocabulary enabling quick mutual understanding and knowledge sharing. Without common terminology, people waste time in "violent agreement" or explaining known concepts under different names. A shared vocabulary, exemplified by the "sidecar container" concept, lets practitioners skip definitions and immediately discuss applying concepts to solve problems.

Former Boynton Beach firefighter-paramedic Luis Garcia spent nearly $40,000 of his savings to buy 800 doses of Narcan, a nasal spray that blocks opioid effects and reverses overdoses. Since retiring in 2011 after 28 years of service, he has traveled Florida training residents, business owners, and law enforcement officers and distributing the drug for free. On Feb. 3, 2018, he gave away about 50 doses at the Treasure Coast Substance Awareness Coalition Family Fun Day at Shepard Park in Stuart. Garcia, who responded to about 3,000 overdose cases during his career, carries Narcan daily and has revived five of the six people he aided in the past year and a half. His organization, the South Florida Opioid Crisis Mortality Reduction Project, focuses on supplying Narcan to businesses and educating police agencies, most of which on the Treasure Coast now carry the drug.

Researchers from MIT and the University of Cambridge have found that the black hole at the centre of the Phoenix cluster, about 1,000 galaxies located 5.7 billion light years from Earth, is recycling hot gas into cold fuel for star formation. While black hole jets normally quench star formation, the jets and bubbles here appear to produce cold gas that rains back onto the galaxy, fueling starbursts. ALMA observations revealed cold gas filaments extending 20,000 light years, aligned with hot gas bubbles mapped by NASA's Chandra X-Ray Observatory. The findings, published in the Astrophysical Journal, may explain the cluster's exceptional star production.

National home prices rose 0.9% over the last quarter, while annual price growth increased 0.3% to 6.1%, the highest year-over-year rate since February 2015. Regional quarterly trends shifted: Midwest growth slowed to 0.8%, the Northeast rose to 0.7%, and the South and West held steady at 1.0%. San Jose, CA and Hartford, CT metros reported negative quarterly growth of 0.3%, while Portland, OR remained the nation's fastest-growing market at around 2% QoQ. Eight major metros are growing at 1.5% QoQ or higher, compared to three a year ago. Sixteen of the nation's 50 largest metro markets have surpassed housing bubble peak prices, and record-breaking markets account for roughly a third of the national housing stock. National price growth is projected to moderate to 2-3% in 2017, though if growth matches 2016 levels, nearly 40% of homeowners who purchased during the housing bubble could be above water by year's end, according to Clear Capital's Home Data Index Market Report.

The Steelers have won eight straight games, including a 39-38 win over the Ravens, and will host the Patriots in Week 15 with the AFC's top seed at stake. Shannon Sharpe said Tom Brady must be "licking his chops," citing the Steelers' narrow wins and the absence of injured linebacker Ryan Shazier.

This study reviewed the first year (April 2021–March 2022) of the COVID-19 vaccination program in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) through a secondary analysis of data from the DRC Ministry of Health and the WHO-African Region vaccination database. After SARS-CoV-2 was identified in Wuhan in December 2019 and COVID-19 was declared a pandemic in March 2020, the DRC reported its first case on March 10, 2020, and subsequently experienced four waves of infection. A vaccine deployment plan developed in January 2021 targeted 53,984,184 people aged 18 and over, prioritizing healthcare workers, people with comorbidities, and those aged 55 and over.

Results showed that only 16 of 26 provinces began immunization activities in the first year. Kasai Oriental had the highest full-vaccination coverage (6.91%), while Equateur had the lowest (0.02%). By March 2022, 5.7% of the population had received at least one dose and 1.03% were fully vaccinated. Uptake was initially low but spiked in February 2022 with 378,782 doses administered before declining. More men than women were vaccinated in all provinces except Kasai Oriental. Overall, 8,302 healthcare workers and 46,495 elderly individuals completed their primary series. The Janssen vaccine was most used (48%), followed by Moderna (25%) and Pfizer (17%), while AstraZeneca was least used (2%). Compared with nine other Central African countries, the DRC had the lowest performance, receiving 11.48% of the doses needed to vaccinate 70% of its population and administering only 8% of doses received, with 2% of the population receiving at least one dose.

Challenges included a halt in AstraZeneca vaccination due to safety concerns, competing outbreaks such as Ebola in Beni, healthcare worker shortages and strikes, expired or near-expiry vaccine doses, and difficulty reaching high-priority groups. The authors conclude that the first year brought mixed progress and underscores the need for continued investment in health systems.

When stock markets are oversold—meaning they have dropped significantly over a defined period, often measured with indicators like a 3-day RSI below 20—short-term returns tend to be strong, though long-term returns gravitate back toward the average (mean reversion). A backtest on the S&P 500 from 1985 onward, buying at the close when the 3-day RSI was below 20 and selling after a close above the prior day's high, produced 484 trades with a 0.64% average gain, 75% win rate, 7.7% CAGR, 26% max drawdown, and 2.5 profit factor. However, the strategy did not work well before 1990, and markets were not mean revertive before S&P 500 futures began in 1982, so mean reversion may not persist indefinitely.

A sudden burst of listings on the London Stock Exchange has raised hopes the city may regain ground in the global IPO race after a sluggish 2025, during which it hosted only three new listings—2% of Europe's IPOs. The surge includes Beauty Tech Group's £300 million debut, with Shawbrook (potentially valued at £2 billion) and Princes Group also considering London floats. Analysts caution that execution—strong order books and post-listing performance—will determine whether this becomes sustained momentum, while Norway's Visma is reportedly eyeing a 2026 London float.

The concept of social capital first appeared in a West Virginia education report a century ago and gained academic attention in the late 1980s through sociologist James Coleman. Robert Putnam, previously an expert on Italian politics, adopted the idea in his early 1990s book on Italian democracy, using it to explain northern Italy's superior performance over the mafia-dominated South, attributing this to the North's history of independent city-states with civic engagement. A recent retirement conference honored Putnam, who is retiring from Harvard's Kennedy School at age 77. His 1990s book *Bowling Alone* triggered an academic and policymaker fad regarding social capital, making him one of the most cited living social scientists. Two definitional issues arise: Putnam favors civic group membership as the measure, while a competing concept emphasizes generalized trust, which lowers transaction costs; a 1996 Knack and Keefer study found no growth effect from civic membership but positive effects from trust. A further distinction separates "bridging" (cross-group) from "bonding" (in-group) social capital. Putnam's research also found that ethnic diversity does not increase social capital—depressing news for diversity supporters, and a finding embraced by ethnocentrists and nationalists, including Trump supporters.

Tesla, Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2019 reports total revenues of $6.35 billion for Q2 2019, up from $4.00 billion in Q2 2018, with automotive sales accounting for $5.17 billion. Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $408.3 million ($2.31 per share) for the quarter, compared to $717.5 million ($4.22 per share) in the prior-year quarter. Total assets were $31.87 billion as of June 30, 2019, with cash and cash equivalents of $4.95 billion and total stockholders' equity of $5.72 billion. In May 2019, Tesla completed its acquisition of Maxwell Technologies for $207.2 million in stock, recording $78.6 million in goodwill. The company adopted the new lease standard (ASC 842) on January 1, 2019, recognizing $1.29 billion in operating lease right-of-use assets. Tesla operates two segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. For the six months ended June 30, 2019, net cash provided by operating activities was $224.0 million and net loss was $1.06 billion. Customer deposits totaled $631.1 million as of June 30, 2019.

The speaker, visiting Grand Forks Air Force Base after flooding, thanked personnel and described touring the disaster area and meeting with local, state, and federal officials from North Dakota, South Dakota, and Minnesota. Five Cabinet members and the Secretary of the Army accompanied the visit to see the damage, pledge assistance, and express support. Announced actions included authorizing FEMA to cover 100 percent of direct federal assistance for emergency work, adding 18 Minnesota counties and 53 South Dakota counties to disaster coverage, and requesting an additional $200 million from Congress, bringing total requested disaster assistance to $488 million. The speaker warned that the coming days would be emotionally difficult and urged residents to support one another. FEMA Director James Lee Witt was asked to lead an interagency task force on long-term rebuilding. The speaker praised community efforts, including rescue workers, saving library books, continued newspaper production, and offers of free housing, and closed by quoting the mayor's statement that a community's people, spirit, and faith cannot be washed away.

The First Circuit dismissed the government's interlocutory appeal for lack of jurisdiction. The underlying criminal case against Watson and O'Hearn arose from a 1997 incident in which Zachary Dulac stole marijuana from Watson, after which Watson and others assaulted Dulac and took $17,000 from him. The government's key witness, Anthony Spera, was deported to Italy by the INS on June 1, 2004, because a letter requesting notification of changes in his custody status was inadvertently overlooked. After the district court denied the government's motions for a continuance to depose Spera abroad, the government appealed under the Criminal Appeals Act, 18 U.S.C. § 3731. The court held that the second paragraph of § 3731 permits appeals only from orders suppressing or excluding evidence, and that the orders at issue were case-management decisions denying a continuance based on trial delay, not evidentiary rulings. Any effect on the government's ability to gather evidence was incidental and insufficient to support appellate jurisdiction.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC dated April 26, 2021, reporting that it released its financial results for the quarter ended March 31, 2021 by posting its First Quarter 2021 Update on its website, attached as Exhibit 99.1. The information was furnished under Item 2.02. The report was signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn. Tesla's common stock trades under the symbol TSLA on the Nasdaq Global Select Market.

Michael A. Gayed's 2015 paper proposed a lumber/gold ratio as a risk-on/risk-off indicator for trading stocks and bonds. Lumber futures act as a leading economic indicator because housing and construction are major business cycle components, while gold offers diversification and low correlation with other assets. Under the rules, a risk-on signal means holding stocks and risk-off means holding long-term Treasuries. The authors modified the rules using the WOOD and GLD ETFs and backtested them, achieving 11.4% annual returns since 2008 with a 2.2% average gain per trade, but a 35% drawdown. A SPY/GLD rotation performed worse, at 8.7% annual returns.

This VentureWire newsletter, dated November 28, 2000, was sent to Jeff Dasovic at Enron. Top stories include ReplayTV restructuring to focus on licensing its technology rather than manufacturing digital video recorders, with CEO and chairman Kim LeMasters resigning and founder Anthony Wood replacing him; wireless infrastructure firm NetCom Technologies raising $75 million in Series A funding from Willis Stein & Partners; Access Point Telecommunications laying off approximately 35% of its workers as part of a restructuring; and Rational Software acquiring Catapulse for $405 million. The newsletter lists numerous funding rounds, including Currenex ($27.6 million second round), MortgageRamp ($50 million second round), Financial Technologies International ($52.75 million Series D), Medsite.com ($28 million third round), NetSchools ($30 million Series E), and Vector ($30 million second round, plus two acquisitions). Bad news covers European health and beauty retailer VitaGO restructuring, discontinuing its Italian operations, and focusing on Germany. New products include Kasna's Eastern European trade exchange, Cuantra's Latin American ground transportation site, a joint venture between Redpacket and Pocketpass for wireless payment services, and BuzzBack's Web research product. M&A activity includes infoShark acquiring WebXi, Aptimus intending to acquire XMarksTheSpot, AutoMedia.com acquiring a public relations firm, and iSuppli buying Stanford Resources. The newsletter also reports board appointments (e.g., HarmonyCom, Celox Networks, NetQos), executive changes (e.g., Edmunds.com naming founder Peter Steinlauf CEO; Belle Systems promoting Erik Froberg to CEO), venture capital fund news (WaldenVC's final close of a $275 million fund; Spinnaker Ventures launching a $53 million fund for U.S. firms expanding into Latin America), Austin Ventures promoting three general partners and naming three partners, and corrections to prior stories about Walker Digital (which remains in business with about 25 employees despite staff cuts), Promptu (which raised $25.4 million, not $3.3 million), and SoftWatch (which expects a 250%, not 2.5%, revenue increase).

This volume of the Foreign Relations series documents U.S. bilateral relations with the Soviet Union from January 1983 to March 1985 and is part of the Reagan administration subseries. Editorial notes supplement the printed documents with additional material, sources, and references. The Advisory Committee on Historical Diplomatic Documentation monitors the compilation and editorial process. The declassification review, conducted from 2015 to 2019 under Executive Order 13526, resulted in one document withheld in full, paragraph excisions in 13 documents, and minor excisions in 20 documents. The volume examines implementation of the four-part agenda codified in National Security Decision Directive 75 on January 17, 1983: arms control, human rights, regional issues, and bilateral relations. It documents efforts by Secretary of State George Shultz, National Security Affairs assistants William Clark and Robert McFarlane, and NSC staff member Jack Matlock, including meetings with Soviet Ambassador Anatoly Dobrynin and Foreign Minister Andrei Gromyko. No high-level meeting occurred between Reagan and Soviet leaders Andropov or Chernenko.

This patent application, a continuation of prior filings titled "Systems and Methods for Augmented Reality," relates to systems and methods for localizing the position and orientation of objects in augmented reality (AR) systems. The background notes that AR presents virtual image information as an augmentation of the real world, and that accurate, low-latency head pose detection is critical so virtual objects appear stable and users do not experience motion sickness; current localization approaches do not meet satisfactory speed or precision standards.

The summary section describes several embodiments: a display system with a head-mounted AR display device, sensors, and processors that monitor sensor information and trigger access to virtual content presented over the ambient environment; an AR display device with stacked waveguides and cameras that decode a QR code to obtain virtual content from a network location; and methods for sharing content between users via activation gateways, acceptance, and sharing credentials.

The detailed description covers AR componentry, including a head-mounted component with a display, speakers, local processing and data modules (e.g., belt-pack configurations), and remote/cloud processing and storage resources. A "passable world model" stored partly locally and partly in the cloud may be continually updated with imagery, 3-D and 2-D points, and parametric information captured by AR users. Electromagnetic tracking systems—comprising field emitters and coil-based sensors—are described for high-precision, low-latency localization of the user's head, handheld controllers (totems), and other objects. AR-specific adaptations include compact emitters, shorter operating radii, reduced duty cycles, IMU-based pose tracking, time division multiplexing, dynamic coil tuning, and noise cancellation. Various depth sensor types (passive stereo, active stereo, structured light, and time-of-flight/LIDAR) are compared with their respective advantages and limitations. Vision-based pose calculation using SLAM/PTAM techniques with outward-facing cameras is described, including feature extraction, triangulation of 3-D map points, pose estimation, and mapping stages (pre-tracking, tracking, low-latency mapping, latency-tolerant mapping, and cleanup), with sensor fusion combining IMU, camera, and electromagnetic data.

The passage describes SOS Disruptions, a basketball defensive scheme aimed at denying middle penetrations, weakside reversals, and limiting the opponent's operating space. When the ball handler is in the wing area, the on-ball defender pushes the offensive player toward the corner or baseline checkpoints while the other four defenders use off-ball techniques such as first pass denials, fronting the post, and Helpside I positions. Three responses to baseline penetration are outlined: Straight SOS (pushing and smothering the dribbler when the dribble is picked up), the automatic "Base Go I" trap (triggered when the dribbler penetrates inside the baseline checkpoint), and "Base Go Red" (a predetermined early sideline trap used in short intervals to change tempo, create easy baskets, and disrupt the opponent's set offense). Side screen disruptions involve an aggressive contact switch above the free throw line and an aggressive trap below it, where the post defender traps the ball handler before the screen is set. The All Out SOS Disruption traps the point guard before any screen or pass occurs, forcing the offense into a freelance situation. Throughout, all rotations occur as the ball leaves the passer's hands.

The passage describes the NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture and its key features. RT Cores included in each SM accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, offloading the SM for other work; Turing achieves 10+ Giga Rays/Sec versus Pascal's ~1.1, making ray tracing roughly 10 times faster.

NVIDIA NGX (Neural Graphics Acceleration) is a deep learning-based technology stack using Turing Tensor Cores and neural services for AI graphics features; it does not function on pre-Turing architectures and is managed through GeForce Experience or Quadro Experience. NGX features include DLSS (Deep Learning Super-Sampling), which renders at lower sample counts and infers target-resolution output similar to TAA quality with roughly half the shading work; DLSS is trained on 64x supersampled ground-truth images, and a DLSS 2X mode approaches 64xSS quality. Other NGX features are InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.

Mesh Shading introduces Task and Mesh shader stages using a cooperative thread model, eliminating CPU draw call bottlenecks and enabling an order-of-magnitude increase in renderable objects. Variable Rate Shading (VRS) allows per-16x16-pixel-region shading rate control, enabling Content Adaptive Shading, Motion Adaptive Shading, and Foveated Rendering, and can also increase shading rates with MSAA. Texture Space Shading (TSS) decouples shading from screen space by computing and storing shading in texture space, enabling reuse and temporal stability. Multi-View Rendering (MVR) supports up to four views per pass, expanding Pascal's Simultaneous Multi-Projection. Turing also supports bindless Constant Buffer and Unordered Access Views (DX12 Tier 3), Tier 2 resource heaps, and USB Type-C/VirtualLink for VR connectivity.

Chip details: TU104 contains six GPCs, 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and 13.6 billion transistors, used in GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000; the Tesla T4 targets inferencing. TU106 (GeForce RTX 2070) contains 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, without NVLink or SLI support.

The passage explains Hybrid Rendering, combining rasterization, ray tracing, and AI, and introduces RTX-OPS, a workload-based metric weighting Tensor (20%), FP32 (80%), RT Core (40%), and INT32 (28%) usage. Background on ray tracing covers ray casting, BVH acceleration structures, and denoising, and describes ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, illustrated with Battlefield V and Shadow of the Tomb Raider examples. The document concludes with NVIDIA legal disclaimers, trademark, and copyright notices.

The paper introduces a local flow architecture for Boltzmann Generators that enables equilibrium sampling of large crystalline materials, scaling from small training cells to systems exceeding 1000 particles. In contrast to previous global architectures, the approach is based on local environments, using graph neural networks combined with augmented coupling flows, which allows energy-based training without samples from the target distribution. The models are transferable across system sizes—trained on small systems (e.g., 216–256 particles) and applied to much larger ones—reducing training costs and achieving higher sampling efficiencies (effective sample sizes) than global approaches. Conditioning on thermodynamic states and interaction potential parameters further amortizes training costs. The method is demonstrated on Lennard-Jones crystals and multiple Stillinger-Weber parameterizations (monatomic water, silicon, germanium), yielding accurate Helmholtz and Gibbs free energies, free energy differences between crystalline phases, and a silicon phase diagram, with results in close agreement with MD+MBAR reference calculations at substantially lower computational cost.

The passage, from Investing.com, centers on an analysis of gold, mining stocks, and the US Dollar Index. Gold rallied strongly on Friday as the USD Index declined, though gold remains below a rising resistance line and mirrors its 2011–2013 price pattern. Mining stocks, notably the VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF (GDXJ), failed to capitalize on gold's rally, closing below the April high for a third consecutive day—viewed as bearish and suggesting the early stage of a larger decline, since gold stocks typically outperform gold early in rallies. The USD Index displays an inverse head-and-shoulders pattern with potential to rally to at least 101.3, its breakout verified by a return to the neck level. Stocks declined below a rising support line after failing to exceed prior highs, forming two bearish signals despite a current pause. The author likens the setup to 2008, stating the Peak Chaos theory remains intact. The passage also includes market headlines, a critical reader comment, and standard risk disclosures.

Hola Publishing, the Spanish-language imprint of Halo Publishing International, has expanded into the Mexican market, offering publishing and printing services with global distribution. By providing Print on Demand services, rare in Mexico, authors can order 25 to 1,000 books instead of 2,000. Books are produced entirely in Mexico, reducing shipping costs, with a 60-day turnaround in paperback, hardcover, and e-book formats, while authors retain 100% rights. The company plans to collaborate with corporations and educational institutions, citing successes such as Clarita Sierra's best-selling memoir.

In a commencement address at American University, the President praises the institution and its graduates before turning to the topic of world peace. He defines the peace sought as genuine peace for all people and all time—not a Pax Americana or the peace of the grave—arguing that total war makes no sense in the nuclear age. He calls peace the rational goal of rational people and urges Americans to reexamine their attitudes in three areas.

First, toward peace itself: peace should not be dismissed as impossible, since human problems can be solved by human effort. He advocates a practical, attainable peace built through gradual evolution of institutions and concrete agreements, describing peace as a process requiring mutual tolerance rather than affection.

Second, toward the Soviet Union: while calling Soviet propaganda claims baseless, he warns Americans against adopting a similarly distorted view. He finds communism repugnant but honors Russian achievements, notes the two nations' shared abhorrence of war and their mutual vulnerability in any total conflict, and stresses their common interest in halting the arms race.

Third, toward the cold war: he calls for avoiding confrontations that force an adversary to choose between humiliating retreat and nuclear war, strengthening the United Nations, maintaining alliances, and supporting self-determination. He cites steps including a direct communications line between Moscow and Washington, Geneva arms control talks, and the pursuit of general disarmament. He announces upcoming high-level talks in Moscow on a comprehensive test ban treaty and declares that the United States will not conduct atmospheric nuclear tests so long as other states do not.

Finally, he links peace abroad to freedom at home, urging protection of citizens' rights, and concludes that the United States will never start a war and will labor toward a strategy of peace.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting on its Annual Meeting of Shareholders held on May 22, 2019. Ten director nominees were elected, including Jeffrey P. Bezos, Rosalind G. Brewer, Jamie S. Gorelick, Daniel P. Huttenlocher, Judith A. McGrath, Indra K. Nooyi, Jonathan J. Rubinstein, Thomas O. Ryder, Patricia Q. Stonesifer, and Wendell P. Weeks. Shareholders ratified Ernst & Young LLP as independent auditors for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2019, and approved, in an advisory vote, the compensation of named executive officers. Twelve shareholder proposals were not approved, covering topics including food waste reporting, special meeting ownership thresholds, government use of certain technologies, certain products, an independent board chair policy, employment policies, climate change, board ideology disclosure, gender pay reporting, executive compensation metrics, and vote-counting practices. The report was signed by Senior Vice President David A. Zapolsky on May 24, 2019.

Just Patios offers durable carports designed to withstand Australia's harsh weather and protect vehicles from rust and corrosion.
