The passage presents PCB layout guidelines for the UC1825B-SP. Feedback traces should be routed far from the inductor and noise sources, kept direct and thick, and preferably placed on the opposite PCB side with a ground plane separating them. Input filter and feed-forward capacitors, along with compensation components, must be positioned close to the IC; surface-mount parts are recommended to reduce lead length and noise coupling. Power traces should be short, direct, and thick (minimum 15 mils per ampere), with the inductor, output capacitors, and output diode placed close together to reduce EMI, lead inductance, and resistive losses. Grounds should connect directly to a ground plane, ideally on both PCB sides; multilayer boards can separate power and signal planes, using one via per 200 mA of current. Switching current loops should curl in the same direction to prevent magnetic field reversal and reduce radiated EMI. A ground plane is essential, with a dedicated power ground section for high di/dt output-stage currents; VCC and VREF require high-frequency, low-ESR/ESL ceramic bypass capacitors to power and signal ground, respectively. The passage also covers documentation update notifications, TI E2E support forums, trademark notices, ESD handling precautions, mechanical and packaging information, and standard legal disclaimers regarding TI's resources and liability.

Harvard researcher Ian Wallace examined more than 2,000 skeletons from academic collections and found that knee osteoarthritis has doubled in prevalence since the mid-20th century — roughly 8 percent of early skeletons versus 16 percent of recent ones. The doubling persisted even after adjusting for age and weight, suggesting factors beyond these two risk factors. Senior author Daniel Lieberman proposes that arthritis is not caused by wear and tear but possibly by physical inactivity, though this remains a hypothesis. Co-author David Felson notes exercise strengthens joints but may not help severely damaged ones, and activity does not guarantee prevention. The findings point toward further research into which modern lifestyle factors drive the rise.

This non-peer-reviewed preprint investigates how human contact network structure affects disease spread, using COVID-19 as an example. Researchers constructed synthetic contact networks of approximately 3,000 individuals based on US 2019 American Community Survey data, comparing two states—Florida (higher average age, smaller households) and Texas (lower average age, larger households)—with interaction layers for households, classrooms, workplaces, and background community transmission. Disease spread was simulated using modified SEIR dynamics with parameters from the initial COVID-19 wave. Three risk-tolerance scenarios were tested: identical behavior for all individuals, vulnerable individuals avoiding work/school interactions, and all members of households containing a vulnerable individual avoiding such interactions. Key findings were that behavioral changes by vulnerable individuals alone are insufficient to reduce their infection risk, population structure can have varied and counter-acting effects on epidemic outcomes, and co-worker interactions contribute more to disease spread than interactions among children at school. The authors state these results have implications for public health strategies.

This study employed Mendelian randomization (MR) to identify potential drug targets for prostate cancer (PCa), a prevalent male malignancy projected to reach 1.7 million new cases by 2030. As a "cold tumor" with low immune infiltration, PCa shows limited immunotherapy response, making novel drug target identification clinically important.

Using eQTL data from the eQTLGen Consortium (16,987 genes, 31,684 cis-eQTLs) and 4,463 druggable genes, the researchers performed MR analysis with UK Biobank GWAS data (3,269 cases, 459,664 controls) for discovery and FinnGen data (6,311 cases, 74,685 controls) for replication. SNPs were screened at p < 5×10⁻⁸, with weak instruments (F statistic < 10) excluded.

In the discovery phase, 151 genes were causally associated with PCa risk using the inverse variance weighted (IVW) method. After replication, 12 genes were confirmed: HOXA9, MPHOSPH6, SLC45A3, PBX2, HLA-A, PPARGC1A, FLOT2, TKT, CARNS1, GPBAR1, CSF1R, and TRAV21. Five genes (HOXA9, MPHOSPH6, SLC45A3, PBX2, HLA-A) were positively correlated with PCa risk, while seven (PPARGC1A, FLOT2, TKT, CARNS1, GPBAR1, CSF1R, TRAV21) were negatively correlated.

GO and KEGG enrichment analyses revealed involvement in fatty acid, glucose, and carbohydrate metabolic processes, T cell receptor binding, and pathways including beta-alanine metabolism, insulin signaling, and transcriptional misregulation in cancer. A protein-protein interaction network was constructed using STRING and visualized in Cytoscape.

Drug candidate prediction using DSigDB identified five top candidates: Tauroursodeoxycholic acid, Adehl, GDP366, Decanoic acid, and GW612286X. Molecular docking with AutoDock demonstrated binding energies ranging from -4.8 to -11.1 kcal/mol, with the strongest affinity between GPBAR1 and Tauroursodeoxycholic acid (-11.1).

Study strengths include the use of two independent cohorts reducing false-positive risk and molecular docking validation. Limitations include lack of environmental and lifestyle factor consideration and the need for experimental validation and clinical trials. The study concludes that these 12 genes provide important insights for targeted PCa therapy development.

Amgen announced that its cholesterol-lowering shot Repatha prevented a composite of heart disease death, heart attack, and the most common type of stroke in a 12,000-patient trial. Analysts say the results could help the drug, available since 2015, reach a broader market. Repatha generated $2.2 billion in global sales in 2024, up 36% from the prior year. This study investigated first-phase left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF-1), an echocardiographic index measuring left ventricular volume change from aortic valve opening to peak aortic flow velocity, as an indicator of coronary artery stenosis severity in chest pain patients undergoing coronary angiography. Patients were grouped by maximal stenosis degree: mild (<50%, n=73), moderate (50–70%, n=39), and severe (≥70%, n=95). Results showed LVEF-1 decreased with increasing stenosis severity, while LVEF showed no significant difference among groups. LVEF-1 was negatively correlated with the Gensini score and BNP and served as an independent predictor of moderate or severe stenosis, with a higher AUC than GLS, E/e', LVEF, and LVDd; cutoff values of 27.9% and 26.9% predicted stenosis ≥50% and ≥70%, respectively. Among 82 patients who underwent PCI, LVEF-1 and GLS increased and E/e' decreased postoperatively, while LVEF did not change significantly. Gensini score and stent diameter were independent factors influencing the change in LVEF-1 after PCI, indicating greater improvement in patients with more severe stenosis. The authors conclude that LVEF-1 is a valuable indicator for assessing cardiac dysfunction caused by coronary stenosis and for evaluating myocardial recovery after revascularization. Limitations include a small sample size, lack of coronary functional testing, and potential effects of cardiovascular medications.

Peter Drucker's ideas on privatisation, popularised by David Howell in 1969 and later associated with George W Bush's "ownership society", stem from his belief that government is a poor manager. While modern India is not yet an ownership society due to pervasive state control, the Modi government since 2014 has undertaken reforms to reduce the state's role. These include banking reforms such as a new insolvency law, freedom from political interference, and consolidation of public sector banks; abolition of most LPG and kerosene subsidies; and UDAY, which transfers responsibility for electricity boards to state governments. A true ownership society requires eliminating government handouts and mass privatisation.

Researchers measured antibodies against the COVID-19 virus 1 month after BNT162b2 or BNT162b2SA. For participants previously given BNT162b2 without past COVID-19, immune responses to the original strain 1 month after a BNT162b2 booster were as good as those after Dose 2, and responses to the Beta variant after one BNT162b2SA booster were as good as post-Dose 2 responses to the original strain. In participants without prior BNT162b2, responses to the Beta variant after Dose 2 of BNT162b2SA were as good as post-Dose 2 responses to the original strain with BNT162b2. Researchers decided these results were not likely due to chance.

In Phase 1, a few participants had a temporary drop in lymphocytes 1 to 3 days after Dose 1 of BNT162b1 or BNT162b2, returning to normal by 6 to 8 days; none had low lymphocytes 6 to 8 days after Dose 2. Injection site reactions and systemic events within 7 days were well tolerated and mostly mild or moderate; injection site pain, and tiredness and headache, were the most common. All tested doses (10, 20, and 30 µg) of BNT162b1 and BNT162b2 were well tolerated except BNT162b1 at 100 µg, which was stopped after Dose 1; 30 µg BNT162b2 was selected for Phase 2/3. No participants left Phase 1 due to medical problems. In Phase 2/3, few participants left due to medical problems (32 of 21,926 with BNT162b2; 36 of 21,921 with placebo), and most problems were mild or moderate.

Serious medical problems were few; researchers did not believe most were related to the vaccine, though a small number were considered possibly related. No participant died during Phase 1. In Phase 2/3, 85 of 23,141 participants who started with BNT162b2, 62 of 21,371 who started with placebo then received BNT162b2, and 23 of 23,141 who received placebo only died; deaths were from different causes and not believed caused by BNT162b2. No deaths occurred in Phase 3 among participants who received BNT162b2SA without prior BNT162b2.

The TPS7H500x-SP series (TPS7H5001-SP through TPS7H5004-SP) are radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting switching frequencies up to 2 MHz and GaN power devices in topologies such as buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge.

Dead time is fixed at 50 ns (typical) on the TPS7H5003-SP but programmable via PS and SP resistors (10 kΩ–300 kΩ) on the TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5002-SP; floating pins set an 8 ns minimum. Leading edge blank time is fixed (50 ns) on the TPS7H5003-SP and programmable via an LEB resistor (minimum 10 kΩ) on the other devices. A pulse skipping mode prevents minimum on-time issues at high frequency, triggered when COMP is below 0.3 V at the clock rising edge and the previous duty cycle was under 25%.

Maximum duty cycle is configured via the DCL pin: 100% (VLDO), 75% (floating), or 50% (AVSS); the TPS7H5004-SP supports only 50%. The CS_ILIM pin senses primary-side current against COMP/2 (with a 150 mV offset); exceeding the 1.05 V threshold initiates cycle-by-cycle limiting followed by hiccup mode, with timing set by the CHICC capacitor (minimum 3.3 nF recommended). The FAULT pin enables external protection, triggering shutdown at 0.6 V with a 0.4–1.4 µs minimum pulse width and restart after a delay of approximately 15 switching cycles. Slope compensation, set via the RSC pin, prevents subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle; 1× the inductor falling slope is recommended. Thermal shutdown occurs at 175°C with restart below 160°C.

An application example designs a 500-kHz, 5-V synchronous push-pull converter with GaN FETs using the TPS7H5001-SP, detailing component selection for timing, transformer, FETs, RCD clamp, output inductor, output capacitance (2.3 mF including single-event transient mitigation), current sense, hiccup, frequency compensation, and slope compensation. The controllers operate from a 4–14 V supply with at least 0.1 µF of input bypass capacitance. Layout guidelines address noise minimization, ground separation, trace sizing, and component placement. Revision F (August 2024) added QMLP options for the TPS7H5002/3/4-SP.

The passage contrasts data cultures at digitally mature "leader" organizations with those of "laggards." Digital leaders promote transparency, making data widely available across teams and discouraging hoarding, while implementing governance controls that build trust and encourage sharing. They believe data enable good ideas from anywhere in the organization—a mindset requiring active leadership sponsorship. Digital laggards, by contrast, restrict data to a "need-to-know" basis, hoard data as power, store it in departmental silos, and favor business judgment and a "culture of genius" over data-driven decisions. Notably, 88% of digital leaders have standardized APIs enabling data flow between departments, versus 27% of laggards.

Digital leaders embrace measurement, using data-driven metrics and 360-degree reviews to track progress; this structure provides flexibility and encourages innovation and risk-taking. Laggards set aspirational goals insufficiently grounded in data, leading employees to avoid measurement and rely on qualitative, process-focused practices that stifle innovation. A case study describes a retail company that, after acquisition, implemented real-time sales reporting enabling data-driven decisions across business units.

Digital leaders use data-driven objectives, developed through transparent top-down and bottom-up processes, to align the organization vertically and horizontally around a shared vision. Laggards fail to connect goals with strategy, causing misalignment. Even leaders face tensions, such as excessive analytical requirements burdening simple decisions.

At leading firms, data culture serves as a central coordinating mechanism, with employee behaviors reinforcing stated values; laggards show misalignment between espoused values and behavior. However, laggards are not doomed—transformation is possible. Organizations tend to fit one of four patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, or data reliant—and can target actions accordingly to build a strong data culture. The passage concludes with a description of Keystone Strategy, the consulting firm behind the research.

This article compares stock and bond investment strategies. Stocks represent ownership stakes in companies; historically, they have been the best-performing asset class, but they carry capital loss risk, and diversification is recommended. Backtests of diversified stock ETFs were presented against the S&P 500 Total Return benchmark. Bonds involve lending money to issuers (companies or governments) with fixed interest payments and maturity dates; they are less risky than stocks because bondholders are paid before shareholders in bankruptcy, though longer maturities and lower quality increase risk and returns. Bond ETF backtests were also shown.

Historically, bonds (mainly sovereign bonds) have mitigated risk during stock market crashes, with exceptions like 2022; corporate bonds may not be safe in recessions due to credit risk. A backtested 60/40 stock-bond portfolio produced lower returns than a 100% stock allocation but with less volatility and drawdown. The article concludes there is no definitive answer on which is better—the choice depends on factors such as time horizon and proximity to retirement, where shifting allocation toward bonds can reduce risk. The FAQ section briefly covers a seasonal "Sell in May and go away" winter-investing strategy, which did not perform as expected in backtesting.

This patent application describes engineered adeno-associated virus (AAV) capsids and muscle-targeting compositions. It is a continuation of prior applications claiming priority to multiple provisional filings from 2019-2020. The disclosed compositions comprise targeting moieties containing n-mer motifs (RGD or non-RGD) coupled to cargo, designed to target muscle cells. The targeting moieties can be incorporated into viral capsid proteins at specified insertion positions, with the n-mer motif displayed externally on the viral capsid. The cargo can include therapeutic transgenes, antisense oligonucleotides, CRISPR-Cas components, mini- or micro-dystrophin genes, or other gene-modifying agents. Applications include treatment of muscular dystrophies, cardiomyopathies, neuro-muscular diseases, glycogen storage diseases, and expanded repeat diseases. The document also describes vector systems for producing engineered AAV particles, methods of generating capsid variant libraries through insertion of random n-mer sequences, and selection processes using muscle-specific promoters (MHCK7 and CK8) in mouse models. Several tables list candidate capsid variants with their nucleotide sequences, amino acid sequences, and muscle mRNA expression scores from selection rounds in C57BL/6 mice. The background notes that conventional rAAVs primarily infect the liver, require large doses that cause toxicity, and show variable transduction efficiency across species.

This study investigated whether circulating indole 3-acetate (3-IAA), previously associated with chemotherapy response in metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), is linked to treatment outcomes in non-metastatic disease. Researchers measured pre-treatment serum 3-IAA via LC-MS/MS in 124 participants with borderline resectable or locally advanced PDAC from the NORPACT2 cohort (2018–2021). No statistically significant associations were found between 3-IAA and response by CT criteria or CA19-9 decline, surgical resection, or overall survival. In Cox models, 3-IAA had an unadjusted hazard ratio of 0.93 (p=0.52) and an adjusted hazard ratio of 0.87 (p=0.28). Median 3-IAA concentrations were approximately 10-fold higher than in the prior study, possibly due to assay differences. The authors conclude that the earlier findings in metastatic PDAC are unlikely to extend to non-metastatic populations and recommend validation in metastatic PDAC cohorts.

A Michigan family is demanding answers after their five-year-old son claimed two teachers repeatedly taped his mouth shut and threw out his lunch up to 10 times. His parents filed a police report and plan to sue the district. One teacher was removed, police are investigating, and the boy won't return until the other is fired.

Researchers at McGill University and the University of Toronto have proposed a new theoretical model that frames gaslighting as a learning process based on prediction error minimization (PEM), moving beyond older psychodynamic explanations. Lead author Willis Klein, a PhD candidate in McGill's Department of Psychology, co-authored the paper with Suzanne Wood and Jennifer Bartz. According to the model, gaslighters exploit trust by behaving in atypical, surprising ways and then attributing the target's surprise to a flawed grasp of reality, making the target feel "epistemically incompetent." Repeated over time, this leads targets to doubt their own reality. Because people depend on close others to form their sense of self and reality, the model suggests anyone could be gaslit if they trust the wrong person, though future research may identify characteristics—such as attachment styles or trauma history—that affect susceptibility. Klein hopes further research will validate the model and improve support for victims. The study was supported by FRQSC, CRSNG, and SSHRC.

Builder Eric Woodward has begun work on a pop-up public park on a vacant Fort Langley lot at Glover Road and Mary Avenue, after cancelling the Glover Mary Church development over a dispute with the Township. The park will include gathering spaces, play areas, an outdoor lounge, picnic areas and ping pong, with major items expected complete by early July.

The passage comprises archival documents and an editorial note regarding Ronald Reagan's 1976 campaign and 1980 transition. An undated document from the Reagan Library describes Richard Allen's preparations for the Foreign Policy Advisory Board's first meeting on November 21, 1980, and lists board members including Baker, Casey, Haig, Kirkpatrick, Kissinger, Rumsfeld, Shultz, and Weinberger; an October 25 news release had announced the interim committee's formation. A December 22, 1980 document covers the transition team's Department of State Final Report, noting that William Timmons headed the Office of Executive Branch Management, Robert Neumann led the State Transition Team under national security team leader David Abshire, and listing team members. An editorial note recounts Reagan's November 20, 1975 announcement of his candidacy for the 1976 Republican nomination, challenging President Ford, quoting his remarks on military superiority, détente, and unresponsive leadership in Washington.

This paper addresses domain shift (DS) in neuroimaging—the degradation of machine learning performance when models trained on one dataset are applied to another due to differences in scanners, imaging protocols, and subject populations—through transfer learning. The authors use Simple Fully Connected Neural Networks (SFCNs) for age and sex prediction from structural MRI, pre-training on the UK Biobank (UKB) and fine-tuning on smaller datasets (OASIS-3, IXI, ABIDE). Experiments show that pre-trained features are task-specific but reusable across datasets when the pre-training task matches the target task. The proposed pipeline, which fine-tunes the classifier and then the full model, outperforms elastic net regression and training from scratch across datasets, improves state-of-the-art age and sex prediction results, and accelerates training convergence. The performance gain is attributed to actual feature re-use rather than favorable weight scaling. In very small data regimes, fine-tuning only the final layer may be preferable, and negative transfer occurred for ABIDE sex prediction. The authors suggest UKB can serve as an "ImageNet" for neuroimaging, though challenges remain for disease prediction and highly heterogeneous scanner variation.

This passage contains interview quotes from hockey players Teuvo Teravainen and Antoine Vermette following a game against Tampa Bay. Teravainen says he plays better when calm, describes his family's floorball background in Finland, and recounts how his team overcame a slow start to win with two big goals, noting the locker room always believes they can come back when trailing. He calls his goal a lucky one that excited fans in Finland, describes a teammate as a "second dad" since his father is far away, and recalls overcoming doubts about his small size through hard work on skating and skills. Vermette expresses excitement about the playoff opportunity, stresses persevering through adversity with confidence, describes Tampa Bay as a fast, skilled team, and praises a young player's intelligence, puck skills, and active stick.

U.S. stocks fell on Tuesday as the 10-year Treasury yield reached 3 percent for the first time in four years, raising concerns about higher borrowing costs for companies already facing rising expenses, while quarterly results failed to deliver positive outlooks. The S&P 500 and Dow posted their biggest declines in two-and-a-half weeks, and the Dow fell for a fifth straight day. Technology and industrial stocks, including Alphabet, Facebook, 3M, and Caterpillar, each dropped more than 3.5 percent, weighing on the indexes. Apple also declined amid worries about softening smartphone demand. Of S&P 500 companies reporting so far, 77.1 percent beat consensus estimates. U.S. consumer confidence rebounded in April, and oil rose above $75 a barrel before reversing course.

Sea of Thieves generated the highest launch-month sales of any Rare title since NPD tracking began in 1995, ranking second for March and eighth for 2018 year-to-date in dollar sales. Figures exclude Game Pass downloads. The game shows Microsoft has an audience hungry for marquee exclusive titles.

On April 27, 2018, Amazon.com, Inc. entered into an Amended and Restated Credit Agreement with Bank of America, N.A., as administrative agent, and lenders, amending its May 20, 2016 credit agreement. The amendment increased the Company's unsecured revolving credit facility borrowing capacity from $3.0 billion to $7.0 billion and extended the term to April 27, 2021. Borrowings will be used for general corporate purposes, including backstopping Notes under a Commercial Paper Program. The same day, Amazon established a Commercial Paper Program permitting issuance of unsecured commercial paper notes up to $7.0 billion outstanding at any time, with maturities not exceeding 397 days; amounts may be reborrowed, and proceeds are expected to be used for general corporate purposes. The Amended and Restated Credit Agreement is filed as Exhibit 10.1. The report was signed by Kurt H. Zumwalt, Vice President and Treasurer.

This study presents the first large-scale, publicly available Turkish dataset for citation intent classification, comprising 2,650 annotated citation sentences drawn from 723 Computer Science research articles. Citations were labeled using a five-category scheme (Background, Basis, Support, Differ, Discuss) through a hybrid process combining human expert annotation with LLM-assisted labeling. The authors benchmarked LLMs (GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Gemini 2.5 Pro) using In-Context Learning, finding performance highly sensitive to prompt design, with manual prompts yielding accuracies from 52.6% to 85.0%. Automated prompt optimization with the DSPy framework (MIPROv2, Chain of Thought) achieved 86.5% accuracy. Few-shot analysis showed both Gemini-2.5-Flash and GPT-4o reaching 88.4% in zero-shot settings, with additional examples producing mixed effects. To improve robustness, ensemble methods were applied: majority voting reached 90.2%, and a stacked ensemble with an XGBoost meta-model achieved the best accuracy of 91.3%. Key challenges included severe class imbalance (the Background class dominating), difficulty distinguishing semantically close categories such as Support and Differ, and inconsistent LLM outputs across repeated runs. Future directions include hierarchical classifiers, synthetic data generation for rare classes, and incorporating broader contextual features.

Research co-authored by Prof. Ross Levine, published by the National Bureau of Economic Research, shows that easier lending conditions encourage businesses to invest in pollution-reducing projects. As credit supply rises, loans for environmental projects become more available, and lower interest rates improve the payoff of green investments. Companies benefit through reduced pollution fines, healthier and more productive workers, and improved reputations. To isolate credit's effects, Levine and co-authors from two Hong Kong universities studied non-gas-producing counties whose banks received deposit windfalls from the fracking boom elsewhere. Benzene levels fell 26 percent in counties with the largest credit gains, with similar declines in other pollutants. EPA records showed companies whose lenders received shale windfalls cut toxic emissions more, earned higher environmental ratings, and spoke out more on green issues. The study draws no conclusions about fracking's own environmental effects.

Hockey players discuss preparing for a Stanley Cup Finals game where they have the chance to close out the series, noting that closing out is the toughest task in hockey and requires mental and emotional readiness against a team with "no tomorrow." They address an injured teammate who may return but will not play if he is a liability. The team stresses staying even-keeled and businesslike, acknowledges the high stakes for players' careers, and compares the different pressures of winning at home versus on the road.

The 2018 U.S. Olympic men's hockey team, though lacking active NHL players, will likely include at least one player with Olympic experience. Ryan Malone, 37, signed a 25-game tryout deal with the AHL's Iowa Wild to stay eligible, while Brian Gionta, 38, is on USA Hockey's radar but likely must play for a non-NHL club.

David Ellison, who acquired Paramount earlier this year with backing from his father Larry Ellison, is widely expected to bid for Warner Bros. Discovery, though he has refused to confirm any plans. WBD's assets include HBO, the Warner Bros. movie and TV studio, and cable channels including CNN. A merger would combine Paramount's streaming services with HBO Max, merge the studios, add WBD's sports rights, and share back-office functions, potentially creating a challenger to Netflix, Disney, and Amazon. Antitrust concerns could be eased by Larry Ellison's support of Donald Trump. WBD is valued at about $44 billion with roughly $35 billion in debt; Larry Ellison is expected to provide some financing, with Apollo reportedly interested in joining the bid. WBD CEO David Zaslav may try to keep the company independent, though his restructuring plan did little to lift the stock.

This paper proves that the interleaving distance on finitely presented R^d-persistence modules can be realized as an edit distance. Edit distances, originating in the 1960s for strings and extended to trees, Reeb graphs, and persistent homology, measure the minimal total cost of sequences of edits. The interleaving distance, introduced in 2009 as a foundational metric in topological data analysis, already exhibits connections to edit distances: both are the most discriminative stable metrics in their respective settings, and bi-Lipschitz equivalences are known between related distances.

The authors define two categories of finite posets embedded in R^d—join-semilattices (JS_d) and grids ((1D)_d)—and construct edit distances on the corresponding categories of constructible persistence modules, where morphisms are monotone functions with right adjoints (Galois connections) and edit cost is given by distortion. The main result (Theorem 4.1) establishes the equality d_I = d_Ed via the chain of inequalities d_I ≤ d^JSd_Ed ≤ d^(1D)d_Ed ≤ d_I. One inequality adapts a Galois connection-based argument, while the other uses an "easy-edit lemma" (a multi-parameter adaptation of the easy-bijection lemma) together with an interpolation between presentations of interleaved modules.

Consequences include characterizations of interleaving-stable invariants in terms of single-edit stability (Theorems 4.2 and 4.4), which facilitates exploring stable invariants for multi-parameter persistent homology. Unlike earlier work establishing an isometry only for R-persistence modules via Galois insertions and single-step edits, this result holds for any dimension d. Appendices show the equivalence of two notions of constructibility and that finitely presented modules are constructible.

Calgary single mother Shauna Sinfield's stolen 1998 Toyota Corolla contained her 12-year-old son Caden's hockey gear, worth more than the car itself. With multiple sclerosis and a small fixed income, she faces replacing the gear, estimated at $1,500 to $2,000, before his eighth hockey season. Police consider recovery unlikely. A GoFundMe page has raised $685 of its $3,000 goal.

Players discuss their playoff series against Detroit, noting each series has gotten tougher. They emphasize adapting to how the game is being called, sticking to their systems and game plan, and staying strong defensively. One player enjoys playing at home because of the energetic fans. They acknowledge bounces have not always gone their way.

Following a playoff loss, speakers expressed disappointment with second-period lapses that cost them the game, despite strong play in the third period. Both goaltenders performed well. The team remains confident returning home, where they have played well recently, and stressed the need for a consistent sixty-minute effort, harder work to create bounces, and awareness of a strong opposing player.

The passage is from the TPS7H5001-SP/TPS7H5002-SP/TPS7H5003-SP/TPS7H5004-SP datasheet (SLVSF07F, revised August 2024), covering device functions, an application example, layout guidance, and revision history.

The CS_ILIM pin receives a signal representing transformer primary-side current, which is compared against the COMP/2 voltage (with a 150 mV offset) for peak current mode PWM control. A resistor from CS_ILIM to AVSS sets overcurrent protection, with a nominal current limit threshold of 1.05 V that triggers hiccup mode. In hiccup mode, cycle-by-cycle current limiting continues while the CHICC capacitor charges via an 80-µA current; when CHICC reaches 0.6 V, switching stops, and after HICC is pulled to 1 V, a 1-µA restart current discharges it. Switching resumes when HICC falls to 0.3 V, and a minimum CHICC of 3.3 nF is recommended. The FAULT pin enables additional external protections; a fault shutdown occurs if its voltage exceeds 0.6 V (typical) for longer than the minimum pulse width (0.4–1.4 µs), with restart after a delay of approximately 15 switching cycles once the voltage falls below the 0.5 V falling threshold. Slope compensation, set via a resistor on the RSC pin, prevents subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle; the recommended value is 1 × m, the inductor falling current slope. Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation can be used with the transconductance error amplifier. Thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C (typical) and restarts below 160°C.

The devices use fixed-frequency peak current mode control. The TPS7H500x-SP family consists of radiation-hardness-assured PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting switching frequencies up to 2 MHz for GaN-based designs and topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge. A design example demonstrates a 500-kHz, 5-V synchronous push-pull converter using GaN devices, detailing component selection for timing, feedback, dead time, soft start, transformer, FETs, RCD clamp, output inductor, output capacitance (2.3 mF including single-event transient mitigation), current sense, hiccup, frequency compensation, and slope compensation.

Power supply recommendations specify a 4–14 V input with at least 0.1 µF of ceramic bypass capacitance. Layout guidelines address feedback trace routing, switch-node minimization, ground separation, trace widths (minimum 15 mils per ampere), bypass capacitor placement, and routing of noise-sensitive signals. The document also lists related TI documentation, revision history (Revision F, August 2024, adding QMLP options for TPS7H5002/3/4-SP), and standard mechanical, packaging, and legal disclaimer information.

Fourth-grader Lexi Bergeron of Ferry Elementary in Grand Haven, Michigan, sells handmade fidgeters to pay classmates' lunch debts. After her mother's GoFundMe exceeded its $188 goal, they now aim to raise $2,200 by December to clear district-wide lunch debts.

This article advocates a sociocultural, ecological perspective on English foreign language education policy in state school systems, focusing on Malaysia and Thailand. It examines the divergence between policy intentions and educational outcomes, and socio-economic inequality in achievement. In both countries, CEFR-based proficiency targets were mandated despite baseline evidence that most learners could not meet them, with rural and poorer students performing worse than urban peers. The status of national languages—Malay and Thai—and their ties to religious, cultural, and national identity limit opportunities for English use, making communicative targets unrealistic. Teachers' own English proficiency is often low, yet selection for upskilling courses relied solely on standardized proficiency tests, ignoring pedagogic skills. Classroom conditions—large classes, mixed abilities, test preparation pressures, limited resources, and lack of support—conflict with mandated communicative, learner-centred approaches developed through centralized decision-making that excludes teachers. The article concludes that unrealistic proficiency targets are self-defeating where English is not part of learners' sociolinguistic reality, and that policymakers should first analyze social and educational contexts and align curriculum outcomes with system capacity, taking account of sociolinguistic, sociocultural, and socio-educational realities.

Opensource.com's top 5 posts cover DomTerm, a terminal emulator built on a browser engine; Dave Neary on open source's origins in an MIT print jam fix; Daniel J. Walsh on container runtimes; Christine Peterson marking 20 years since coining "open source software"; and an Ontario teacher's Linux program saving 200+ computers. The site marks its eighth anniversary.

P. vivax malaria parasites form dormant liver-stage hypnozoites that reactivate to cause relapsing bloodstream infections. Radical cure requires 8-aminoquinoline drugs, which are toxic in G6PD-deficient patients. The biology of hypnozoite activation remains poorly understood, with proposed external triggers including seasonal changes, mosquito bites, febrile illness, and haemolysis. Two P. vivax sub-species exist: short-latency "tropical" and long-latency "temperate" types.

The authors develop an "exponential clock" mathematical model in which each hypnozoite activates independently at a constant rate with no external triggers. They derive analytical likelihoods and fit the model to data from the SPf66 vaccine trial (1993–1995), a daily-follow-up study of 1344 children aged 2–15 years on the Thailand-Myanmar border over 21 months, recording 2504 symptomatic P. vivax and 1164 symptomatic P. falciparum infections.

Key estimates include a hypnozoite carriage duration of 171 days (half-life 118 days), a mean of 6.9 successful sporozoites per infective bite, and a relapse-to-primary infection ratio of 3.4, implying approximately 75% of symptomatic vivax infections were relapses. The model captures patterns of multiple recurrent infections across age groups. Higher-than-expected vivax rates following falciparum monoinfections treated with artesunate monotherapy are compatible with an external triggering mechanism. Mefloquine was found to provide one month of post-treatment prophylaxis against emerging relapses, a previously unappreciated public health benefit that may have masked triggering effects.

Researchers have identified two bacterial strains from grape plant leaves that can degrade guaiacol, a key volatile phenol responsible for smoke taint in wine. After 96 hours, the bacteria nearly eliminated guaiacol in lab dishes. The strains were selective, not growing on other smoky compounds, and researchers identified the gene responsible for guaiacol degradation. This microbial approach could offer a more targeted alternative to current mitigation methods like activated charcoal filtering, which removes desirable wine components. However, since guaiacol is only one of many volatile phenols causing smoke taint, further research is needed.

The Department of Education will hold its first School Safety Conference at Okkodo High School starting June 26, addressing bullying, harassment, suicide, sexual identity, and rising drug and alcohol use among its 30,000 public school students. Roughly 400 support staff will attend, focusing on law enforcement, legal issues, positive school climate, drug reduction, and crisis response. The DOE has shifted toward treatment rather than discipline for drug offenses, with 352 cases reported in School Year 2015-2016.

NVIDIA Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 27, 2019 reports third-quarter revenue of $3,014 million, down 5% year-over-year, and net income of $899 million, down 27% from $1,230 million. Nine-month revenue was $7,813 million (down 18%) with net income of $1,845 million. The company operates two reportable segments: GPU and Tegra Processor. Third-quarter GPU revenue was $2,565 million (down 8%) and Tegra revenue was $449 million (up 10%). Gross margin was 63.6%. By market platform, Gaming revenue was $1.66 billion, Data Center $726 million, Professional Visualization $324 million, Automotive $162 million, and OEM and Other $143 million. On March 10, 2019, NVIDIA agreed to acquire Mellanox Technologies for $125 per share in cash, an enterprise value of approximately $6.9 billion, with closing expected in early calendar 2020 pending regulatory approvals in Europe and China. NVIDIA adopted a new lease accounting standard on January 28, 2019, recognizing $470 million of operating lease assets and $500 million of operating lease liabilities. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $9.77 billion as of October 27, 2019. The company paid $292 million in dividends during the first nine months and is authorized to repurchase up to $7.24 billion of stock through December 2022. Pending securities class action and derivative lawsuits allege false statements regarding channel inventory and the impact of cryptocurrency mining on GPU demand. One customer represented approximately 10% of third-quarter revenue, and 92% of revenue came from customers outside the United States.

Investors speculate the Czech National Bank may scrap the cap keeping the euro above 27 crowns at today's meeting, after its weak-crown commitment ended; hedging costs for crown volatility hit a nine-month high. Britain's ONS is exploring whether it can identify recessions sooner; its GDP data is fast but heavily estimated, and in 2008 it was three months late spotting recession. Markets whipsawed Wednesday after Fed minutes flagged concern over high stock valuations and plans to shrink its $4.5 trillion balance sheet this year, while Speaker Ryan said tax reform will take longer than healthcare repeal. Wall Street fell 0.3 percent, Treasury yields slipped, and Asian and European stocks were mostly lower.

Jack Wilshere, leaving Arsenal this summer, has held talks with West Ham manager Manuel Pellegrini about a potential move. Fenerbahce has offered a larger deal West Ham cannot match, but Wilshere's family is settled in London, and staying in the Premier League could aid his England recall hopes.

The Education Department concluded its first round of negotiated rule-making talks on the One Big Beautiful Bill Act's changes to the student loan system, with a second round scheduled for November 3–7. The most contentious issue was defining which postbaccalaureate programs qualify as "professional," determining whether students can borrow up to $200,000 versus $100,000 for graduate programs. The department initially proposed limiting professional degrees to the 10 programs listed in the Higher Education Act, but after committee pushback, offered a one-year expansion covering programs designated as professional before July 4, 2025. No consensus was reached, though committee members remained skeptical yet viewed the compromise as progress. The government shutdown limited transparency, as the department's website went unupdated. On repayment, most income-driven plans end July 1, 2026, except a new Repayment Assistance plan, with concerns remaining about the complicated transition process for existing borrowers, particularly those with Parent PLUS loans.

In *People v Yuk Bui Yee* (Supreme Court, New York County, May 9, 1978), the defendant faced a 13-count indictment arising from six alleged extortionate incidents at three Chinese restaurants over a two-month period. He moved to sever the counts related to each incident. The court explained that severance is unavailable for offenses joinable under CPL 200.20 (subd 2, par [b]), but discretionary for those joined under paragraph (c). After reviewing the statutory history and the Molineux rule, the court grouped the offenses by restaurant and found the evidence admissible under the common scheme or plan, identity, and intent exceptions, citing the defendant's consistent Mandarin demands for money for his "brothers" and his claimed membership in the "Eagles" gang. The court concluded all counts were properly joinable under paragraph (b) and denied the motion to sever.

This study examined cardiovascular biomarkers, events, and mortality in 451,355 UK Biobank participants stratified by ethnicity-specific BMI categories (normal, overweight, obese) and diabetes mellitus (DM) status. Biomarkers assessed included carotid intima-media thickness, arterial stiffness, left ventricular ejection fraction, and cardiac contractility index. Among participants without DM, higher BMI was associated with adverse cardiovascular measures, but these relationships were diminished in those with DM. Within each BMI category, DM was associated with an adverse cardiovascular phenotype, particularly in the normal-weight group. Over 5,323,190 person-years of follow-up, myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, and cardiovascular mortality rose across increasing BMI categories in both DM and non-DM groups. However, normal-weight participants with DM had higher cardiovascular mortality (IRR 2.81) than obese participants without DM (IRR 1.84). Adiposity metrics correlated more strongly with cardiovascular biomarkers than diabetes-oriented metrics, though both correlations were weak. The authors conclude that obesity and DM are additively associated with adverse cardiovascular biomarkers and mortality risk, and that other factors likely underpin the high cardiovascular risk of normal-weight diabetes.

This study examined cross-sectional and longitudinal associations between arterial stiffness (measured by baPWV) and renal function (eGFR) in 67,060 Chinese adults, with a longitudinal cohort of 12,324 participants. Cross-sectional analysis showed a significant negative association between eGFR and baPWV. Longitudinally, higher baPWV predicted incident CKD (highest tertile HR 2.17), and lower eGFR was associated with increased arterial stiffness risk (HR 1.21). Cross-lagged panel analysis showed the path coefficient from baseline eGFR to follow-up baPWV was significantly greater than the reverse, indicating kidney function decline preceded arterial stiffness progression. The authors conclude that arterial stiffness and CKD are bidirectionally related, though eGFR decline appears to precede baPWV increase. Limitations include creatinine-based eGFR assessment and a population drawn from central China.

This case study examined one woman (aged 60–65) with a unilateral transtibial amputation who received percutaneous spinal cord stimulation (SCS) leads implanted near the T12–L2 vertebral levels to restore sensation in the missing limb. SCS was delivered during the stance phase of prosthetic-limb walking, with amplitude modulated by insole plantar pressure. Electromyography and motion capture were recorded during overground walking at a self-selected speed, comparing early (Day 30) and late (Day 63) time points, with and without stimulation.

After multiple weeks of in-lab SCS use, the residual tensor fasciae latae (TFL) and vastus lateralis (VL) muscles showed increased activation (77.6% and 81.7% without stimulation; TFL 93.6% higher with SCS compared to the early time point). Co-contraction of the knee antagonist muscles (VL and biceps femoris) in the residual limb decreased significantly from 1.57 to 1.05 without stimulation and 0.95 with stimulation (p < 0.001). Pelvic obliquity range-of-motion and residual-limb pelvic drop increased, with pelvic drop becoming more symmetrical with the intact limb.

The authors suggest SCS-mediated sensory feedback may have a rehabilitative effect on muscle activation and knee and hip stability during walking, though findings are from a single participant with an 84-day implant duration.

The speaker calls for returning to simple hockey—getting pucks deep and limiting opponent speed—while addressing the opponent's shot blocking and collapsing defense. The goalie played well despite inactivity, but frustration affected the team, which hopes to rebound.

Bear Grylls has criticised schools for not fully preparing children for adult life, saying they should "empower" young people rather than focus on league tables. He argued that success comes from determination rather than top exam results, citing his own experience of passing SAS selection despite not being "brilliant at school". He also praised Eton as forward-thinking and said he hopes Donald Trump is "too busy" to join him on an adventure, unlike Barack Obama in 2015.

This study introduces SCIseg, a deep learning-based, open-source method for automatic 3D segmentation of the spinal cord and T2-weighted hyperintense lesions in spinal cord injury (SCI) MRI images. The model was trained in three phases on data from 191 patients (231 scans) across three sites, covering different scanner manufacturers, field strengths, image resolutions, orientations, treatment strategies (pre-/post-operative), and lesion etiologies (traumatic/ischemic), incorporating an active learning strategy. On independent test sets, SCIseg 3D achieved average Dice scores of 0.92 for spinal cord and 0.60 for lesion segmentation, outperforming existing open-source methods and its 2D variant, with better lesion performance on site 2 than site 1, where metal artifacts posed challenges. Active learning improved agreement between automatically derived and manually annotated lesion biomarkers. The model generalized to non-traumatic SCI (degenerative cervical myelopathy), including cases with severe compression. Correlation analyses showed significant associations between discharge pinprick scores and all lesion biomarkers, and between lower extremity motor scores and lesion volume and maximal axial damage ratio, with no significant differences between manual and automatic biomarkers. Limitations include use of a single MRI contrast and treating lesions as single entities. The model is freely available via the Spinal Cord Toolbox.

Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev said on April 17 that the Russian economy is entering a growth stage, citing 1.3 percent industrial output growth and 5 percent agricultural growth last year. He noted agriculture's vast export potential and a 60 percent rise in agricultural machinery production.

Thunderstorms brought hail to North Texas amid a slow severe weather season with four tornadoes. Oklahoma recorded zero tornadoes in 2018, last being this late without one in 1962. Kansas has zero, though tornado activity can rise sharply in May.

The speaker describes a calm, level-headed team that has refocused after games and plans to use the same recipe from clinching games on Sunday. They emphasize sticking to their game plan, wearing opponents down, and relying on mental toughness and big-game experience. They acknowledge needing a better start, praise a teammate's performance limiting rebounds, and note a collective effort against tough lines. They express excitement about playing at home and staying aggressive against dangerous opponents.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC dated July 25, 2019, announcing its second quarter 2019 financial results. The filing includes a press release with the results announcement (Exhibit 99.1) and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures (Exhibit 99.2). The report was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. Amazon is incorporated in Delaware, and its common stock trades under the symbol AMZN on the Nasdaq Global Select Market.

Athletes Unlimited (AU) is a sports startup co-founded by Jon Patricof and Jonathan Soros that launched in 2020 as a new model for women's professional sports. After meeting for brunch in December 2018, the two businessmen decided against investing in existing women's leagues and instead built a new league structure from scratch, despite widespread skepticism. In October 2019, they met with four professional softball players who became consultants and helped shape the league's design.

AU launched softball in 2020, followed by volleyball and lacrosse in 2021 and basketball in 2022, with over 200 athletes across four sports. Its model departed from tradition: no team owners or coaches, five-week seasons at a single venue, weekly team drafts, and an individual leaderboard scoring system modeled loosely on Formula 1. Players made decisions through five-member Player Executive Committees and shared in profits through a twenty-year Profit Participation Plan.

The case situates AU within a history of women's professional leagues marked by underinvestment, unsustainable business models borrowed from men's sports, minimal media coverage, and low salaries, with the NBA-backed WNBA as a notable exception. AU was structured as a public benefit corporation with a "Mission Equity" capital model in which investors accept capped returns, directing at least 50% of surplus to players. The company also emphasized athlete empowerment through childcare support, pregnancy accommodations, the Athlete Causes Program, and the Power in My Voice initiative.

AU secured broadcast partnerships with ESPN, CBS Sports Network, Fox, and others, and invested in in-house production and athlete storytelling to build its fanbase. A 2022 fan survey showed strong approval of AU's innovative approach. The company raised $30 million in 2022 and was named among the world's most innovative sports companies by Fast Company in 2023. Remaining challenges include achieving economic sustainability, scaling, and determining future growth strategies.

This patent application, a continuation of prior filings titled "Trigger-Based Random Access in a Multiple BSSID Network," relates to allocating resource units in wireless networks. It describes methods, systems, and devices for allocating random access resources in a multiple basic service set identifier (BSSID) set, where one access point (AP) is associated with a transmitted BSSID (Tx BSSID) and other APs are associated with non-transmitted BSSIDs (non-Tx BSSIDs).

The disclosed method involves allocating random access resources for stations belonging to the multiple BSSID set using association identifier (AID) values based on a group AID mapping contained in a partial virtual bitmap of a traffic indication map (TIM) element, and transmitting a trigger frame containing those AID values. The AID values may identify a group of stations, a specific BSSID, a group of BSSIDs, or all stations in the set. When the trigger frame is transmitted from the Tx BSSID, its transmitter address is set to the Tx BSSID's MAC address; random resource units (RUs) may be allocated to a selected non-Tx BSSID by setting an AID value to that BSSID's index, to Tx BSSID stations by setting an AID value to zero, or to unassociated stations by setting an AID value to 2045. Management frames may include a Multiple BSSID element and Random Access Parameter Set (RAPS) elements indicating OFDMA contention window values.

The disclosure states that prioritizing random RU allocation among BSSs—based on factors such as station counts, traffic types, priority levels, security parameters, and quality of service—can increase utilization and efficiency of the shared wireless medium and improve fairness among stations contending for random RUs.

President Kennedy, speaking at Amherst College on a day honoring Robert Frost, argues that privilege carries responsibility, urging graduates to serve the public interest amid the nation's staggering problems at home and abroad. He honors Frost as an artist and American whose contribution was to the nation's spirit rather than its size, noting that those who question power contribute as much as those who create it. Frost saw poetry as a means of saving power from itself, reminding man of his limitations when power leads to arrogance. Kennedy asserts that art is a form of truth, not propaganda, and that artists must remain free to follow their visions. He expresses hope for an America that rewards artistic achievement, protects beauty, and earns respect for its civilization as well as its strength.

The CAT offense is a simple, effective attack against traps, double teams, and zone presses. It uses a 2-1-2 spread alignment with sharp, accurate passing, and the middle post position should be filled by a skilled triple threat player. Key rules include baseline back cuts when the ball goes to the middle, post rolls to the basket on corner passes (with an optional post interchange), skip passes to the opposite corner when trapped, and sparing dribble penetration to keep the ball and clock moving while avoiding fouls.
The nonprofit "Look Good … Feel Better" offers free skincare, make-up, and hair loss support to women in cancer treatment on May 8 at Dignity Health Sierra Nevada Memorial Hospital.

Tight ends remain a vital offensive position in modern football, presenting significant matchup problems for defenses due to their blend of size and athleticism. They split duties between running short-to-medium routes—often against linebackers—and blocking defensive linemen and linebackers in both run and pass situations. The name derives from early football, when receivers called "Ends" lined up at the end of the line; those staying tight to the formation became "tight ends." Also called TEs or H-backs, they require diverse skills including strong hands, blocking, and route running, with typical builds of 6'3"–6'8" and 240–270 pounds. Notable tight ends include Tony Gonzalez, Rob Gronkowski, Antonio Gates, and Shannon Sharpe. Their versatility allows coaches to diversify schemes and increase offensive production.

Guangdong Province, China is experiencing its largest recorded chikungunya outbreak, with over 4,000 confirmed cases since late July. Shunde District in Foshan accounts for over 3,600 cases, with additional infections in Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Hong Kong, and Macao. The disease, transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, causes fever and severe joint pain but does not spread directly between people. Authorities are urging residents to eliminate standing water to reduce mosquito breeding. Climate change, urbanization, and international travel are cited as factors enabling the spread of mosquito-borne diseases. The WHO has issued new clinical guidelines and strengthened its Global Arbovirus Initiative. There is currently no specific antiviral treatment or licensed vaccine for chikungunya.

Coalition for Tobacco Control–Pakistan (CTC-Pak) officials urged the government to prioritize health over business on World No Tobacco Day. Tobacco contributes to 16% of non-communicable disease deaths in Pakistan, with 108,800 deaths annually associated with tobacco. Officials called for enforcement of tobacco control laws, implementation of the delayed 85% Pictorial Health Warning on cigarette packs, and increased tobacco taxes, criticizing a tax compromise that doubled consumption. Pakistan ratified the WHO FCTC in 2004 but has yet to fulfill its obligations.

The paper introduces SoDaDE (Solvent Data-Driven Embeddings), a data-driven solvent fingerprint created by pre-training a transformer model on the Spange solvent property dataset, which contains up to 12 properties for 191 solvents. Data augmentation was performed by randomly shuffling property-value pairs (up to 12! combinations per solvent), and masking was used to handle missing values and enable property prediction. The final model used a dimension size of 64, 16 attention heads, and 5 layers, achieving a normalized MSE of 0.107 on the validation set. On solvent property prediction, SoDaDE outperformed Random Forest, Gaussian process, and averaged-value baselines with an average MSE of 0.170. On the Catechol Benchmark, SoDaDE outperformed prior representations including ACS PCA, DRFPs, fragprints, Spange descriptors with GP imputation, RXNFP, and ChemBERTa, achieving MSEs of 0.0026–0.0029 on the full data task and 0.0044 on the single solvent task. Performance was stronger on the full data task, suggesting the fingerprint represents solvent mixtures well. The authors conclude that SoDaDE captures general solvent features, as fine-tuning provided little additional benefit, and that effective fingerprints can be created from small datasets.

Standard variance components linear mixed models are inadequate for gene and isoform expression because cis- and trans-SNPs differ in effects. The authors implemented a minorization-maximization (MM) algorithm for ML and REML estimation of multivariate variance components models in Julia, offering numerical stability and fast convergence. Applied to PsychENCODE, the method showed cis-variants exert sparse but large effects while trans-variants act collectively, with greater shared genetic influence among cis-SNPs. Isoform-level analyses uncovered more genetic signals than gene-level analyses, some linked to psychiatric disorders like autism spectrum disorder.

In this lecture, Oppenheim covers stability and causality for discrete-time linear shift-invariant (LSI) systems, linear constant coefficient difference equations, and frequency response. Stability means a bounded input produces a bounded output; for LSI systems, this requires the unit sample response to be absolutely summable (e.g., 2^n u(n) is unstable, while (1/2)^n u(n) is stable). Causality means the output depends only on present and past inputs; for LSI systems, this requires the unit sample response to be zero for n < 0. While stability is generally desirable, causality is not always imposed, since non-causal systems can be useful.

The lecture introduces Nth-order linear constant coefficient difference equations, where the order refers to the number of delays in the output. A zeroth-order equation reduces to the convolution sum, with the unit sample response equal to the equation's coefficients. For higher orders, boundary conditions must be specified: the same first-order equation can yield a causal solution (a^n u(n), stable if |a| < 1) or a non-causal solution (unstable for |a| < 1). Thus, the difference equation alone does not uniquely specify a system, and boundary conditions must be consistent with zero input producing zero output.

Finally, the frequency response H(e^jω) is introduced: complex exponentials are eigenfunctions of LSI systems, so the output equals the input multiplied by H(e^jω). For sinusoidal inputs, the magnitude gives amplitude change and the angle gives phase shift. The frequency response is a continuous function of ω and periodic with period 2π. The next lecture will address the Fourier transform.

GameStop will ship at least five Nintendo Switch consoles to each of its 4,400+ US stores on August 15, available by August 16 at the $300 price—the first time all stores will have stock simultaneously. Units are in-store only.

This lecture introduces radiation—self-emission from plasmas—as a diagnostic tool. All objects emit electromagnetic radiation, with hotter objects producing higher-energy photons; plasmas emit across the spectrum from radio waves to gamma rays. Radiation has two consequences: it can cool plasmas (a loss mechanism, e.g., Bremsstrahlung) and it provides diagnostic information about plasma conditions.

Radiation transport—how radiation emitted in one place is absorbed and re-emitted elsewhere—is highly non-local and complex, so a diffusive assumption is often made. The spectral radiance I is defined with specific units, and the radiation transport equation dI/ds = j − αI relates intensity changes to emissivity j and opacity α. The equation is solved independently for each frequency, neglecting processes like fluorescence. Introducing optical depth τ (the path integral of opacity) recasts the equation into a form whose solution combines attenuated initial radiation with emission accumulated along the path.

For homogeneous plasmas, two limits emerge: optically thin (τ ≪ 1), where radiation passes through unabsorbed, and optically thick (τ ≫ 1), corresponding to blackbody equilibrium described by Planck's law. Equating the blackbody intensity with j/α yields Kirchhoff's law, which intimately links emissivity and opacity—knowing one gives the other.

The lecture distinguishes optical thickness (gradual absorption with continued oscillation) from plasma cutoff (sudden reflection with evanescent decay). Finally, using Poynting flux arguments, stationary and constant-velocity charges do not radiate, while accelerated charges do. The full radiation formula contains near-field (non-propagating) and far-field (propagating) terms; plasma applications require solving particle equations of motion and integrating over the distribution function.

MMFP-Tableau is a bioinformatics data integration and visualization platform developed by the Mitochondrial Medicine Frontier Program at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia to support precision medicine in primary mitochondrial disease (PMD). The platform centrally extracts, cleans, and integrates siloed data from the CHOP electronic medical record (EPIC/Clarity), REDCap research surveys, and Excel spreadsheets using Alteryx for data processing and Tableau for visualization. It integrates data from over 2,000 individuals and provides approved clinicians and researchers with real-time, role-based access to patient-level and cohort-level data through customizable dashboards, without requiring informatics expertise. Use cases include clinical cohort characterization, clinical trial eligibility determination, genotype-phenotype mapping using HPO codes, medication trend analysis, and risk factor delineation. The platform has improved efficiency by replacing manual chart reviews, enhanced clinical documentation practices, and supports research collaboration and trial design. Limitations include inaccessibility of some EMR data (e.g., scanned PDFs, separately housed imaging), inability to extract external institution data, and server performance issues with live data volume. The authors state the platform's framework is generalizable and transferable to other disease populations and institutions.

The passage describes NVIDIA's RTX Blackwell GPU architecture and its features. The ninth-generation NVENC encoder improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% BD-BR PSNR, adds 4:2:2 H.264/HEVC encoding, and introduces an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode; the RTX 5090 supports three encoders and two decoders, boosting export speeds over 50% gen-over-gen. A sixth-generation NVDEC provides 2x faster H.264 decoding. Blackwell adds DisplayPort 2.1b support with up to 80 Gbps bandwidth, enabling 8K@165Hz and 4K@480Hz.

Max-Q power efficiency improvements include advanced power gating, full memory clock tree gating, separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory, accelerated frequency switching (1000x faster than prior architectures), and low latency sleep states entered 10x faster than Ada, yielding up to 50% power savings in small language model inference.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, producing up to three additional AI-generated frames per rendered frame, with a 40% faster AI model using 30% less VRAM, plus enhanced Flip Metering in the display engine. DLSS 4 transitions from CNN to transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, ingesting 2x more parameters for improved image stability, lighting detail, and motion quality.

Blackwell introduces neural shaders, enabled by the Cooperative Vectors API (developed with Microsoft) allowing shader access to Tensor Cores. Applications include RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression (over 3x memory savings in a demo), Stochastic Texture Filtering, Neural Radiance Cache for real-time global illumination, RTX Skin (first ray-traced subsurface scattering in games), and RTX Neural Faces using real-time generative AI.

The GB202 flagship GPU contains 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, and 24,576 CUDA Cores, powering the RTX 5090. The GB203 (45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs) powers the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti, while the GB205 (31 billion transistors, 50 SMs) powers the RTX 5070. The passage concludes with NVIDIA legal disclaimers and trademark information.

The Trump administration has postponed the 100% pharmaceutical tariffs President Trump threatened to enact on Oct. 1 unless companies built U.S. infrastructure. A White House official said the tariffs have not taken effect; instead, the administration will "begin preparing" tariffs on companies that don't build in the U.S. or make a drug pricing agreement, with no new timeline provided. The tariffs would apply to branded drugs. The delay suggests the White House's threats may be aimed at pressuring companies to invest in the U.S. and strike deals to lower drug prices.

The head and shoulders pattern is a chart formation consisting of three price rallies and two intervening pullbacks, with the middle rally (the head) being the highest. Seen in an uptrend, it signals a bearish reversal, confirmed when price breaks below the neckline connecting the swing lows. Its inverse version, formed by three swing lows and two swing highs, is a bullish reversal pattern confirmed when price breaks above the neckline. The profit target is estimated by projecting the head's height downward from the neckline. The authors could not fully quantify the pattern for backtesting and instead cite Thomas Bulkowski's research from *The Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns*, based on 500 stocks over five years. Bulkowski found a 93% success rate for the head and shoulders pattern, with an average price drop of 23%, and determined that volume and neckline direction were irrelevant; he suggested a stop-loss above the right shoulder when shorting. For the inverse pattern, he reported expected returns of 20–30% within 73 days. A 1995 Federal Reserve study also found the strategy generated statistically significant profits. However, the authors urge caution because Bulkowski's analysis was performed after the fact.

House Of Fraser, owned by Sanpower Group, reported pre-tax profits rising from £1.3 million to £3.4 million on flat revenues of £1.3 billion, with online sales up 16.1%. It warned volatility continues into 2017, will discontinue five under-performing brands, and has opened its first China shop in Nanjing.

Around 125 people attended LDA-organised sessions on September 1–2 to give views on a Newtongrange centre masterplan. The masterplan team will consider the feedback and work with the council and Blueprint Partnership, with further community engagement expected later in the year.

The passage outlines two defensive strategies against the Base Cross offense, which is difficult to stop without proper preparation due to its inside game and quick ball reversal with down screens. The Basic NBA Show & Recover method involves the "Little's" defender stepping out to block the screening post's path, forcing the post high and wide while weakside defenders pack in; it proceeds through three phases: showing, recovering, and final match up. The All Out SOS Disruption strategy traps the ball handler on the wing before an entry pass can be made, using a "Hi-Lo Switch" (defenders switch when the post goes low, but not when the post goes high). If the ball enters the post, trap rotations occur, followed by near player rotations and basic SOS concepts. Both strategies are detailed in three phases: initial action, pass out of trap, and final match ups.

A hockey coach assessed his team's loss, saying the transition game and puck movement were strong in the first period, but a neutral-zone mistake led to a goal, after which the team played on its heels and lost its transition play. He welcomed playing a best-two-of-three series for the Stanley Cup with home-ice advantage, saying the team plays well at home and will feed off fan energy. He credited Boston for playing smart, capitalizing on mistakes, and shutting his team down offensively for two games, and called their goaltender, a Vezina nominee, one of the league's best. He said his team must get more pucks and players to the net and set better screens, and expressed trust in his own goaltender, Louis. The team has raised concerns with the NHL about the opposing goalie roaming from his crease and initiating contact. He said ice conditions are the same for both teams and should improve.

Calvin Alexander, a seventh grader at Caddo Middle Magnet, won the Northwest Louisiana regional spelling bee for the second consecutive year, spelling "nectarivorous" to defeat Rosetta Schultz of Ruston Junior High.
