ExxonMobil sent a dozen traders and marketers, including global crude marketing manager Thomas Martenak, to an oil trade show in Dongying, Shandong province, seeking access to China's independent "teapot" refiners, which won crude import licenses in 2015. The team set up a booth, distributed gift bags, and hosted a dinner attended by around 200 guests—a departure from Exxon's traditional one-on-one sales methods. Martenak said the company was drawn by the teapots' growing regional importance rather than politics, despite a looming US-China trade war, and noted that new International Maritime Organization low-sulphur fuel rules starting in 2020 will likely boost China's demand for US sweet crude. Exxon faces competition from earlier arrivals BP, Shell, Vitol, Trafigura, and Mercuria, which have deeper knowledge of the local market.

This paper introduces the task of automatically detecting hype—promotional or exaggerated language—in biomedical research texts, presented as the first NLP treatment of this problem. Building on a prior lexicon of 140 potentially promotional adjectives, the authors focus on the "novelty" group of 11 adjectives and compile 550 sentences from NIH grant application abstracts (2016–2020). They propose formal annotation guidelines based on criteria including value judgment, hyperbole, gratuitousness, amplification, coordination, and broader context. Three annotators labeled the data, resolving most disagreements and yielding a dataset of 537 sentences (392 hype, 145 not hype). Hype detection is framed as text classification and evaluated using traditional classifiers, finetuned language models (BERT, DistilBERT, BiomedBERT, GPT-2), and LLMs (LLaMA3.1-Instruct, GPT-4o-mini), compared against a human baseline without access to the guidelines. Finetuned BERT achieved the best performance (0.861 accuracy), exceeding the human baseline (0.824), while GPT-4o-mini performed on par with the human baseline and LLaMA3.1 performed worst. Results suggest formal guidelines support reliable annotation and that models can detect hype, though context-dependence, domain knowledge, and temporal awareness remain challenges. Limitations include annotator subjectivity, small dataset size, restriction to the novelty category, the biomedical domain, and English only. Future work includes expanding the guidelines and lexicon and applying the work to downstream tasks such as flagging promotional language in scientific writing.

A career coach describes a friend whose 28-year-old son became angry and defensive when the father offered advice about a problem with his boss. Giving career advice to adult children is difficult because, although they should make their own decisions, navigating the modern workplace is challenging. The author consulted Ruth Nemzoff, author of Don't Bite Your Tongue and an expert on emerging adulthood, who shared three guiding principles: know yourself, since advice is filtered through personal experience; know your grown child, since approaches and timing differ; and know the environment, since context and times change. Nemzoff also recommended four techniques for setting a positive tone: ask whether the child wants to vent or receive advice; open with curious, non-judgmental questions; acknowledge what you don't know; and share your own career mistakes. To avoid overstepping, help the child identify the next best step, suggest consulting an objective third party, and don't expect the child to follow your advice or hold it against him if he doesn't.

In January 2008, Nike launched the Air Jordan XX3, its first high-profile performance shoe designed under its "Considered" sustainability strategy, incorporating recycled materials and minimizing solvent use. After a 1990s labor crisis damaged Nike's reputation, the company began treating corporate responsibility as a core business function. In December 2004, CR VP Hannah Jones, supported by Mark Parker (later CEO), developed a strategy emphasizing value creation ("ROI2") and identified product design as a key intervention point for reducing environmental impact. The Considered Group, formed in late 2005, created the Considered Index (released September 2007), a scoring tool rating footwear on environmentally preferred materials, solvent usage, waste, and innovation, with Bronze, Silver, and Gold ratings. Nike committed to having 100% of its footwear meet a minimum Considered standard by Spring 2011. The Core Performance category successfully implemented the Index, earning Silver ratings across its line and producing its first Gold shoe, the Dual D Hoop. However, implementation faced challenges including EPM costs, performance and aesthetic risks, design complexity, time constraints, margin pressures, supply chain limitations, and uncertain consumer demand. Competitors such as Timberland, Adidas, and Brooks also introduced sustainable products. Jones continued to consider how to expand Considered, including an Apparel Index, and how to communicate its value to consumers.

Sandvik beat first-quarter operating earnings expectations, with operating profit rising to 4.27 billion Swedish crowns from 3.50 billion, exceeding a 4.00 billion forecast. Strong metal-cutting tools results drove the beat, though the mining business was slightly weaker than anticipated. Order intake rose to 25.4 billion crowns, above forecasts, but shares were trading down 1.8 percent.

Future Market Insights forecasts the global bioprocessing analytics equipment market to register a 4.5% CAGR from 2018 to 2028. The market is segmented by product type, application, end user, and region. Osmometers are the leading product type, and the industrial application segment is expected to lead with a 4.4% CAGR. Biopharmaceutical companies are the largest end users, growing at 3.9%. North America is projected to dominate by 2018 end, while Western Europe and APECJ collectively account for 39.2% of market share, with APECJ growing at 5.9% CAGR.

This theoretical study investigates the interaction of the fungicide chlorothalonil (CLT)—a toxic compound classified as a human carcinogen by the USEPA—with single-walled carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and boron nitride nanotubes (BNNTs) of chiralities (8,0), (10,0), and (12,0), using density functional theory (DFT) calculations and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations.

The most stable adsorption configuration places the CLT aromatic ring parallel to the nanotube surface, at distances of 3.38–3.45 Å, indicating moderate physical adsorption. Adsorption energy increases in magnitude with nanotube radius for both materials. CNTs exhibit stronger adsorption energies than BNNTs, attributed to their greater polarizability (lower chemical hardness) and more effective π-π stacking interactions. However, CNTs show negligible changes in band gap and work function upon CLT adsorption, and the (12,0) CNT exhibits a very long recovery time, making CNTs unsuitable for sensing. In contrast, BNNTs show significant band gap reductions (39–49%), high electronic sensitivity, and short recovery times, making them suitable for reversible CLT detection and removal. For work-function-based applications using BNNTs, the radius must be well controlled, as sensitivity diminishes with increasing diameter.

MD simulations confirmed that both systems are thermally and dynamically stable in aqueous solution over 100 ns, with CLT preferentially adsorbed parallel to the surface and no desorption events observed. The study concludes that both nanotubes can remove CLT from contaminated environments, but BNNTs are better candidates for electronic sensing due to their superior electronic response, while the interaction remains physisorption even for larger nanotube radii.

Pneumonia and tuberculosis are major global health challenges, particularly in low-resource settings, and misdiagnosis between the two diseases leads to treatment delays and increased mortality. Deep learning techniques, especially CNNs applied to chest X-rays, have shown promise for automated lung disease detection. However, existing state-of-the-art studies have limitations, including reliance on small, imbalanced, or overlapping datasets, high computational costs, poor generalizability, and failure to handle unknown or non-X-ray images. This study proposes a multi-class classification system using a pretrained CNN that categorizes chest X-rays into four classes: normal, pneumonia, tuberculosis, and non-X-ray. Including the non-X-ray class addresses outliers and improves robustness for real-world clinical use. The study used anonymized, publicly available data requiring no additional ethical approval, and received no funding.

The University of Southern Mississippi's DuBard School for Language Disorders was one of four U.S. schools recognized by IMSLEC. Its DuBard Association Method, accredited since 1998, is used daily to teach reading, speaking, and writing.

Hounds of the Bay is a stock-picking strategy selecting the highest dividend-paying stocks in Canada's S&P/TSX 60 large-cap index. Named after Bay Street, Toronto's financial district, it mirrors Dogs of the Dow, based on the premise that blue-chip companies do not alter dividends with trading conditions; high dividend yields indicate stocks near the bottom of their business cycle, likely to rise faster in price. Due to the index's composition, the strategy skews toward global commodities, especially energy, and underperformed in 2014 after the oil decline. Academic research confirms it has worked well, though the effect has diminished over recent decades.

The smash concept is a pass play used by football teams at all levels, from youth to the NFL. It creates big-play opportunities downfield while giving the quarterback quick release options, and is especially useful for attacking the perimeter outside the hash marks. It works well against man coverage, Cover 2, and Cover 4, but is problematic against Cover 3, where outside linebackers can undercut the hitch route. The concept includes route coaching points for the tight end, running back, slot receiver, and outside receivers, with hitch routes settled at 6 yards and vertical routes to 10 yards. The quarterback reads one side of the field pre-snap based on the cornerback's leverage and cushion, then high-lows the cornerback: throwing the hitch if the corner gains depth, or the corner route if he plays low, with a checkdown to the running back as a fallback. Variations include a 3x1 set answer and a sprint-out version that moves the pocket.

The speaker said the team progressed in the second game after a jittery first but needs to reach another level, particularly in puck battles and possession. Line combinations may be adjusted before the next game at the United Center. The team has taken too many penalties and must compete harder in puck areas to draw power plays. All four goals against were called uncharacteristic, with the third goal, allowed late in a period, singled out as critical. A goaltender was praised for his quiet demeanor and playoff progression, and Nicky was credited with strong positioning and a good finals debut. The speaker cited versatility among forwards, patience when winning, and confidence in Kaner's readiness. Against Pronger, the team aims to be more physical and force him to play defense. Burish's energy and Laddy's return were noted in lineup considerations, and a late goal was traced to pressure and a late shift.

The paper introduces SQuID (Survey and Questionnaire Item Embeddings Differentials), a method that uses semantic embeddings from large language models as complements to human rater judgments in psychometrics. Prior embedding-based approaches to questionnaire analysis were limited by their inability to produce negative correlations between items, a problem stemming from shared linguistic features in high-dimensional embeddings. SQuID addresses this by subtracting the average embedding of all questionnaire items from each individual item embedding, without requiring domain-specific finetuning.

The method is evaluated on the Revised Portrait Value Questionnaire (PVQ-RR), a 57-item survey measuring 19 value dimensions based on Schwartz's theory of basic human values, whose circular structure is traditionally recovered through multidimensional scaling (MDS). Five embedding models were tested. Linq-Embed-Mistral performed best, achieving an average Cronbach's alpha across dimensions slightly above the human benchmark. Dimension-dimension correlations derived from embeddings and human data correlated at 0.74, and after Procrustes transformation, the MDS configurations from embeddings and human data showed congruence coefficients of 0.88 and 0.82 for the two dimensions.

The authors conclude that semantic embeddings can recover latent questionnaire dimensions at performance on par with human rater judgments while being flexible, cheap, and scalable. They position the approach as complementary to traditional workflows and suggest applications such as quantitatively assessing cultural biases in LLMs. Limitations include unresolved measurement validity questions, the possibility that the PVQ-RR was part of model training data, and the philosophical ambiguity of "similarity." Ethical concerns raised include potential displacement of crowdworkers and the risk of treating LLM-derived norms as a gold standard.

The ISM Manufacturing Index, also known as the Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI), was introduced by the ISM in 1948 and measures the health of the US manufacturing sector. It is based on a survey of purchasing managers at over 300 manufacturing firms and covers production, new orders, employment, supplier deliveries, and inventories, with each factor equally weighted and seasonally adjusted. The index is calculated using the formula PMI = (P1×1) + (P2×0.5) + (P3×0), where P1, P2, and P3 represent the percentages reporting improvement, no change, and deterioration. It is published on the first business day of each month; a reading above 50 indicates expansion, below 50 indicates contraction, and 50 indicates no change.

Investors and businesses use the PMI to gauge economic direction: a rising PMI may signal expansion and higher stock prices, while a falling PMI may signal contraction and lower prices. It can be combined with other indicators such as GDP, employment data, and inflation rates. Backtests showed a strategy of holding stocks when readings exceeded 50 returned 7.3% annually versus 8.5% for the S&P 500, while invested 72% of the time, with reduced drawdowns; gold performed better with low readings. The index is considered a lagging indicator whose figures are often already discounted by markets, and it is not a strong contrarian indicator. A sustained decline may hint at recession, as in 2020.

This SanDisk manual excerpt provides technical support contact information (phone and online support for player questions, with partner service questions directed to those partners) and directs users to the Tips, FAQ, and Troubleshooting section first. It outlines the one-year limited warranty, which applies only to the original end user, is non-transferable, excludes third-party software, and is void if the product is misused, improperly installed, modified, or damaged by accident. Warranty service requires returning the product in tamper-resistant packaging, freight prepaid, with tracking confirmation; SanDisk may repair, replace, or refund, and disclaims liability for lost data, consequential damages, and use in life support systems, with liability capped at the purchase price. A user notice explains Microsoft's WM-DRM digital rights management technology and possible license revocation. The End User License Agreement grants a limited, non-exclusive license for personal use on a single computer, prohibits modification and reverse engineering, disclaims warranties, limits liability, permits termination for violations, excludes high-risk use, and is governed by California law. Finally, disposal instructions state the device should not be discarded with unsorted household waste and direct users to local waste authorities.

This paper describes the Shayona team's participation in the SMM4H'23 shared tasks, specifically Task-1 (binary classification of self-reported COVID-19 diagnoses from tweets) and Task-4 (identifying patients reporting social anxiety disorder diagnoses from subreddit r/socialanxiety posts). For Task-1, three approaches were tested: RoBERTa sequence classification (f1 0.83), fine-tuned BERT (f1 0.89), and a hybrid BERT+LightGBM model (f1 0.93 validation, 0.94 test). The hybrid model, which extracts hidden [CLS] tokens from BERT's last three layers and uses Optuna for hyperparameter optimization, performed best and was applied to Task-4, achieving an f1-score of 0.809 on test data. The authors attribute LightGBM's success to its ability to learn complex interactions among concatenated tokens. Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitions a single A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances for improved utilization and quality of service. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth across twelve links. Additional features include PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, hardware JPEG decode, an Optical Flow Accelerator, five NVDEC units, and improved atomics. CUDA 11 supports task graphs, asynchronous copy operations, asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls, and enhanced Cooperative Groups. The passage describes the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture. A100 features Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity, which prunes trained weights using a 2-out-of-4 non-zero pattern followed by fine-tuning, halving data footprint and doubling Tensor Core throughput by skipping zeros; NVIDIA reports virtually no accuracy loss across vision, detection, segmentation, and language networks. New Sparse MMA instructions reduce a 16x8x16 matrix multiply from N cycles to N/2 cycles.

The A100 combines L1 data cache and shared memory at 192 KB/SM (versus 128 KB/SM in V100) and includes separate FP32 and INT32 cores for simultaneous execution. Memory consists of 40 GB HBM2 across five stacks delivering 1555 GB/sec (1.7x V100), protected by SECDED ECC along with the L2 cache, L1 caches, and register files. The 40 MB L2 cache is 6.7x larger than V100's, split into two partitions for a 2.3x bandwidth increase (5120 versus 2048 Bytes/clk read bandwidth). Compute Data Compression provides up to 4x DRAM and L2 read bandwidth improvements and 2x L2 capacity gains.

Third-generation Tensor Cores in 108 SMs share data across 32 threads (versus 8 on Volta), issue 8x fewer instructions, and perform 2.9x fewer register file accesses. A new asynchronous copy instruction loads data directly from global to shared memory, bypassing the register file, while SMEM allocation increases 1.7x to 164 KB.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitions an A100 into up to seven GPU Instances with isolated memory paths for quality of service and fault isolation, supporting multi-tenant, single-user, and virtual machine use cases. GPU Instances are built from GPU slices (a Sys Pipe, one GPC, an L2 slice group, and frame buffer access) and can be subdivided into Compute Instances supporting Volta-style MPS. MIG migration enables moving vGPUs between instances or GPUs.

Third-generation NVLink doubles the per-pair data rate to 50 Gbit/sec, provides twelve links (600 GB/sec total versus 300 GB/sec on V100), and uses non-posted writes. A100 supports PCIe Gen 4 (31.5 GB/sec per direction for x16) with SR-IOV, plus improved error attribution, isolation, and containment. Additional features include a five-core NVJPG hardware JPEG decoder, an Optical Flow Accelerator, 11x FP16 and 2.7x FP32 atomic throughput improvements over V100, and five NVDEC units.

CUDA 11 adds task graph acceleration (launch and execution dependency optimizations), an asynchronous copy API, hardware-accelerated asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls (set-aside in 2.5 MB increments, disabled in MIG mode), and Cooperative Groups extensions including a reduce API.

The DGX A100, the third-generation AI system, delivers 5 PFLOPS via eight A100 GPUs interconnected through six NVSwitches with 4.8 TB/s bidirectional bandwidth, up to 6x DGX-1 training performance, and software provisioned through the NGC Private Registry.

Appendix B explains that pruning removes nodes and connections contributing little to network accuracy, yielding benefits in compute throughput, memory bandwidth, and latency. Fine-grained sparsity causes irregular memory accesses and load balancing issues, while coarse-grained sparsity risks larger accuracy loss; A100's fine-grained structured sparsity balances workloads with virtually no accuracy loss.

The passage concludes with NVIDIA legal disclaimers and 2020 copyright information.

The passage is a datasheet excerpt for the ADS8681W, ADS8685W, and ADS8689W, 16-bit SAR ADC data acquisition devices from Texas Instruments.

**References:** The device includes a factory-trimmed 4.096V internal reference, selected via the INTREF_DIS bit, with REFIO becoming an output requiring a minimum 4.7µF decoupling capacitor. Reference accuracy can shift due to mechanical or thermal stress, particularly solder reflow; multiple reflows cause additional shifts. The reference is temperature-compensated from –40°C to +125°C. An external 4.096V reference mode is also available, using an internal buffer whose REFCAP output requires 10µF and 1µF capacitors; buffer drift is typically 0.5ppm/°C (maximum 2ppm/°C).

**ADC and Alarms:** The ADC supports single-ended and differential inputs with bipolar and unipolar ranges in straight-binary format, with LSB = FSR/2¹⁶. Alarm features include a user-programmable input alarm with hysteresis and an AVDD alarm with fixed thresholds (4.7V low, 5.3V high). Active and tripped alarm flags are read via the ALARM_REG register, the ALARM pin, or appended to data output.

**Interface and Programming:** The multiSPI interface supports single-device and daisy-chain topologies, with RESET, ACQ, and CONV operational states. Data transfer frames begin at the CONVST/CS falling edge; valid write commands require 32 SCLKs. Nine configuration registers are mapped, and read operations support legacy SPI protocols (single or dual SDO) and source-synchronous protocols.

**Applications and Power:** An example design combines the ADS8681W with the MUX36D08 multiplexer for an eight-channel industrial analog input module, including NTC thermistor temperature sensing using alarm hysteresis. Power recommendations cover AVDD/DVDD decoupling, NAP mode, and power-down mode, along with PCB layout guidance. The document concludes with related documentation, trademarks, ESD caution, and revision history noting ADS8685W and ADS8689W advanced to Production Data status in May 2025.

The Rate of Change (ROC), also called momentum, is a technical indicator that compares a security's current price to its price "n" periods ago, plotted as an oscillator around a zero line. Developed by Tom Demark, its formula is (Current Price – Price n periods ago) / Price n periods ago. Positive values indicate rising momentum and buying pressure; negative values indicate falling momentum and selling pressure. Traders use centerline crossovers, overbought/oversold levels, and divergence signals to identify trend changes and potential reversals. The lookback period depends on trading style—shorter periods produce more volatile readings and more signals. Backtests on the S&P 500 showed an oversold mean reversion strategy performed best with 4-6 day settings, while breakout and zero line crossing strategies performed poorly. Overall, ROC strategies underperformed compared to the RSI, stochastic, and Williams %R indicators. Unlike the RSI, which indirectly measures momentum, ROC directly measures the rate of price change. The indicator works best in trending markets, performs poorly in volatile markets, and should be combined with complementary tools, with strategies backtested before deployment.

The lecture covers the dynamics of running using the SLIP (spring-loaded inverted pendulum) model, consisting of a mass on a pendulum with a spring of rest length r0 and spring constant k. The goal is to reduce this 4-D system to a 1-D iterated map and to justify the model biologically.

Comparative biomechanics shows that animals spanning five orders of magnitude in mass (cockroaches, horses, crabs, humans) exhibit dynamic similarity when analyzed with non-dimensional quantities, and their center-of-mass dynamics are well described by the SLIP model. Animals possess physical springs (tendons) that store energy and improve efficiency.

The SLIP model assumes a massless leg and toe, an ideal lossless spring (making ground collisions perfectly elastic), and instant leg repositioning to a desired touchdown angle, making the system fully conservative. The apex of flight serves as the surface of section, reducing the state to just the apex height y. The stance phase requires small-angle linearization to obtain a closed-form return map, which reveals one stable and one unstable fixed point—surprising stability in a conservative system, attributed to piecewise holonomic coordinate switching. A failure mode occurs when the system bounces too low to reposition its leg for touchdown.

A variant with toe mass (Buehler, 1991) is dissipative and requires spring-constant control to add energy, yet shows similar stability properties. The SLIP model also applies to lateral-plane dynamics; cockroach experiments, including a cannon-perturbation study, demonstrate "preflex"—passive musculoskeletal spring responses faster than neural reflexes.

Videos of Raibert's 1980s–90s hoppers (monopeds, bipeds, quadrupeds) show remarkable running, flipping, and robustness. Finally, SLIP walkers—compass gaits with springy legs—can transition between walking and running, mirroring the human walk-run transition that occurs at the efficiency crossover point.

This study estimated monthly SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence among pregnant women attending first antenatal care (ANC) visits in four Zambian districts (Chadiza, Chipata, Chongwe, and Lusaka) from September 2021 to September 2022, using repeated cross-sectional surveys. Of 9,221 women enrolled, 8,304 samples were tested, with 8,304 valid results analyzed. Overall, 63.8% were seropositive, with seroprevalence highest in Lusaka (reaching 100% by August–September 2022) and lowest in Chadiza (peaking at 77.2% in April 2022). Seroprevalence rose sharply during the Omicron wave (December 2021–March 2022). Using a multiplex assay distinguishing infection from vaccination, most antibodies (77.7%) were infection-induced, 20.6% from hybrid immunity, and only 1.6% from vaccination alone. Vaccination coverage among participants rose from 4.4% to 26.6% but remained below national levels. Vaccination was associated with higher odds of seropositivity, and hybrid immunity produced the strongest antibody response. Estimated infections (2,911,393) far exceeded reported cases (90,150), with infection-to-case ratios of 29:1 to 92:1 by district. The study demonstrates that ANC clinics can serve as a feasible platform for SARS-CoV-2 serosurveillance, though limitations include non-systematic sampling, antibody waning, and the cross-sectional design.

The article backtests a rotation strategy that switches between the S&P 500 and gold based on the gold/S&P 500 ratio and its 20-month moving average. This study evaluated the clinical relevance of circulating tumor cell (CTC) genomic variation in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). Using whole-exome sequencing data from CTC pools collected from 29 mCRC patients, researchers characterized the mutational landscape of CTCs and assessed whether genomic diversity metrics could predict patient survival. Results showed that high MATH scores (a measure of genomic diversity) and non-silent mutations in BCL9L were significantly associated with poorer overall survival in multivariate analysis. A custom 55-gene panel (CRC-P55) also effectively predicted survival outcomes, offering a cost-effective alternative to whole-exome sequencing. This is the first study demonstrating a relationship between CTC genomic diversity and overall survival in mCRC, suggesting CTC genomic profiling as a potential prognostic tool. The authors note that the small cohort size may limit generalizability.

U.S. Minister John M. B. Sill reported that Japanese minister Otori demanded a council be appointed to consider his proposals; on Sill's advice, Korea granted a council empowered only to listen and report, and declined the proposals due to the military occupation. The King formed his own reform council, which decided to abolish needless taxes. Foreign representatives discussed Chemulpo's neutrality; the Chinese consented, but Japanese conditions precluded it. Russian representative Waeber returned to his post, the U.S.S. Monocacy arrived at Chemulpo, and Chinese merchants departed on official orders. Ye Cha-yun was appointed vice-president of the foreign office. British Acting Consul-General C. T. Gardner reported being assaulted by Japanese in military uniform, dragged, and struck, with Mrs. Gardner's chair pushed into a ditch. Minister Otori promised an investigation, then forwarded General Oshima's report denying that soldiers struck foreigners, blocked the road, or hustled any lady, stating instead that two foreigners forced past a sentinel into a bivouac.

Kerala, the first state to announce a transgender policy, has directed all state and affiliated universities to reserve two seats for transgender students in undergraduate and postgraduate Arts and Sciences courses, subject to qualification, and to prevent discrimination. The KSLMA's Samanwaya programme offers continuing education and shelter homes, as a survey found high dropout rates due to harassment, bullying, and financial exclusion.

BerkeleyGW delivers exascale quantum many-body materials simulations with performance portability across AMD, Intel, and NVIDIA GPU architectures, achieving double-precision throughput above 1.0 ExaFLOP/s. The work addresses limitations of DFT in describing excited-state properties by employing the GW approximation, which captures explicit electron-electron interactions, and introduces GW perturbation theory (GWPT) for correlated electron-phonon coupling. Key innovations include: portability via directive-based OpenACC and OpenMP models demonstrated on Frontier, Aurora, and Perlmutter; hardware-optimized kernels using HIP, SYCL, and CUDA; a static subspace approximation that accelerates full-frequency GW calculations; and a mixed stochastic-deterministic pseudobands method that reduces the O(N⁴) scaling of standard GW. Optimized GPP kernels for diagonal and off-diagonal self-energy matrix elements achieved 1.069 ExaFLOP/s on the full Frontier machine (9,408 nodes, 59.45% of theoretical peak) and 707.52 PFLOP/s on Aurora (9,600 nodes, 48.79% of attainable peak). Strong scaling reached the full Frontier machine and 90.4% of Aurora. Demonstrated applications include silicon divacancy defects up to 2,742 atoms, LiH defects up to 17,574 atoms, and an 867-atom twisted BN moiré bilayer. These capabilities enable systematic computation of quasiparticle excited-state properties and electron-phonon coupling for complex materials with 10³–10⁴ atoms on exascale platforms.

Wall Street and global stock markets hit record closing highs on Thursday, driven by investor optimism over U.S. tax reform and the global economy. The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq notched their fourth consecutive record closes, as did MSCI's all-country world index. The dollar gained on data showing solid U.S. growth, including a narrower trade deficit and lower unemployment claims. Congressional progress toward a budget resolution boosted confidence that tax legislation could pass, potentially lifting 2019 earnings estimates. Gold dipped on expectations of a December interest rate hike. Oil prices rose as talk of Saudi Arabia and Russia limiting production through next year outweighed record U.S. exports.

The ASP SFS process involves checking DRAM address protection, verifying customer and AMD signatures, loading and running the executable patch, updating patch level information, and returning status to the software agent. The GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO command uses a two-page buffer and returns the API version, current SFS and System Patch Levels, and firmware version information. SFS packages are binary objects aligned to AGESA releases following a specific naming convention, and must match the firmware and patch level combination running on a system. Updates run in parallel with x86 and DMA traffic with minimal performance impact, rarely requiring quiescing. SEV/SEV-ES virtual machines must stop and restart for SEV firmware updates, while SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue operating.

A federal judge, U.S. District Judge Esther Salas in Newark, has temporarily halted deportation proceedings against Indonesian Christians who are in the U.S. illegally but seeking legal status. The Friday order, issued in response to an ACLU lawsuit, applies to Indonesians with removal orders dating before 2009 and affects roughly 50 people in New Jersey who identified themselves to ICE in 2009 as part of a program for work authorization and stays of deportation. The lawsuit followed enforcement actions targeting Indonesian Christians, including the arrest of two men. Among those affected is Harry Pangemanan, in the U.S. since 1993, who sought sanctuary at the Reformed Church of Highland Park and helped rebuild more than 200 homes after Superstorm Sandy. Arthur Jemmy and Yohanes Tasik were already living at the church. Salas ordered both sides to file briefs over the next month, and an ICE spokesman did not immediately comment.

Toronto police say 26-year-old Nnamdi Ogba, an electrical engineer with no criminal record or gang affiliation, was fatally shot by two men while walking to his car in a Toronto Community Housing complex Friday night. Police believe the attackers, who fled in a waiting SUV, sought vengeance against the Scarlettwood Court community and came from another area of the city. Ogba did not know his attackers. Police released security footage showing the suspects and a Nissan Rogue.

A federal judge ordered Alabama to release records about its lethal injection protocol after an aborted execution, ruling the public has a common law right of access, though some security information may stay secret. News organizations sought the records in a lawsuit by death row inmate Doyle Hamm.

A hockey coach speaks to reporters after a game. He says a player who fell into the boards got dazed but is fine and will be in the lineup tomorrow. He notes the power play, a major reason the team reached the Stanley Cup Finals, had poor passing against the Devils' pressure, though the penalty kill was strong and the power play scored the first goal. He credits the team's discipline—avoiding retaliation penalties, sticking to the game plan, not panicking—for its success. He admits the team did not play well enough to win and lost focus despite keeping composure. On Forsberg's absence, he says the team has turned the page and cannot use him as a crutch. Shots were even, and both teams' strong defense limited scoring chances; the Devils scored seconds after penalties ended. He says referees missed two high sticks because they happened in a fraction of a second, and he remains positive heading into games in New Jersey.

The paper introduces ABXLAB (Agent Behavior eXperiments), an open-source man-in-the-middle framework that transforms arbitrary websites into controllable behavioral testbeds by intercepting and modifying real-world web content in real time before agents see it. Motivated by prior evidence that LLM agents are hypersensitive to nudges, the authors study agent decision-making in the OneStopMarket online shopping environment, where agents make binary forced choices between product pairs. The benchmark includes large-scale experiments across 17 state-of-the-art models—over 80,000 trials, ~2.5B tokens, and ~400k requests—using interventions such as authority, social proof, scarcity, negative framing, and incentives.

Results reveal systematic biases: higher ratings increased selection probability by 30–80pp in 14 of 17 models (up to 81.2pp for o4 Mini); 13 of 17 models preferred cheaper options (15.2–34.3pp, rising to 93.2pp for Llama 4 Maverick when ratings were matched); order effects were heterogeneous, with GPT-4.1 Nano showing +90pp and Claude 3.5 Haiku −35.4pp; and nudges shifted selections by 10–60pp on average under matched conditions. The Wirecutter authority nudge had the largest impact, followed by "Buy 1 Get 1 Free" and "best seller." Human baselines showed far smaller effects (4pp order, 5pp ratings, 9.4pp price, 9.9pp nudges), indicating 3–10× or greater agent susceptibility. Explicit user profiles acted as categorical switches that dominated decisions and suppressed competing attributes.

The authors note limitations: the design prioritizes causal identification over ecological breadth, uses binary forced choices, and covers only consumer behavior. They conclude that agent choices are easily bent by superficial cues and release ABXLAB as a foundation for a behavioral science of AI agents. The work was supported by an Amazon Research Award, SK Telecom in partnership with MIT MGAIC, and API credits from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.

By 2011, First Solar, once the world's largest and lowest-cost photovoltaic (PV) manufacturer, faced an eroding competitive advantage. The company, which used proprietary thin-film cadmium telluride (CdTe) technology, had broken cost records in 2009 by producing panels at under $1.00 per watt, but recorded its first net operating loss in seven years ($39 million) in 2011 as revenue growth slowed from 66% in 2009 to 8% in 2011. The slowdown reflected industry-wide pressures: Chinese manufacturers, subsidized by their government, flooded the market with low-cost crystalline silicon (c-Si) panels, while shrinking European subsidies and reduced bank financing weakened demand. Falling silicon prices further benefited First Solar's c-Si competitors.

The case reviews the PV industry's evolution, the two dominant technologies (thin-film and c-Si), and three market segments—residential, commercial, and utility—each with distinct purchase criteria. First Solar, founded in 1984 and publicly traded since 2006, vertically integrated into the systems business beginning in 2007 through acquisitions, growing systems from 5% to 25% of sales by 2011. The company maintained a conservative financial strategy with low debt and high cash reserves, and controlled all production stages in-house across plants in Ohio, Germany, and Malaysia.

In 2011, First Solar held approximately 41% of the U.S. market. Chinese producers, benefiting from an estimated 18–20% cost advantage (partly from subsidies), produced nearly 60% of global PV supply by 2012, prompting an anti-dumping lawsuit and a WTO investigation. Industry-wide price declines forced bankruptcies including Evergreen Solar, SpectraWatt, and Solyndra. Facing a $413 million fourth-quarter 2011 loss, senior vice president of module manufacturing Tymen deJong prepared for a board meeting, weighing whether First Solar's competitive advantage was sustainable, how to respond to Chinese competition, and whether the systems business was a strategic benefit or a distraction.

This message to Congress describes an eventful year marked by a financial crisis amid national prosperity, the near disappearance of political partisanship in agricultural regions, and the seizure of a US vessel on the high seas, now in satisfactory adjustment. Relations with most foreign powers remain friendly. The message reports US participation in the Vienna Exposition, a slight advance in suppressing the Chinese cooly trade, receipt of the Geneva arbitration award (used to redeem public debt), completion of the northwest water boundary with British possessions, and a mixed commission award requiring the United States to pay Britain $1,929,819 in gold. It recommends a commission to audit losses from vessels destroyed by the Alabama, Florida, and Shenandoah, a special court for alien claims, and legislation defining expatriation. The Virginius, seized by a Spanish gunboat with fifty-three of those aboard executed, is to be restored under an agreement with Spain, and the Navy has been placed on a war footing. The message also transmits Santo Domingo's application for a US protectorate, conveys Congress's congratulations to Spain on its new republic, and notes slavery's abolition in Porto Rico while proslavery interests resist abolition in Cuba. Two constitutional amendments are proposed: partial presidential approval of bills and limiting extra-session legislation to subjects submitted by the Executive.

Treasury receipts exceeded expenditures by $43,392,959, though revenues are falling amid the panic; the President urges economy, currency elasticity, and movement toward specie payments, suggesting banking reforms, federal maintenance of waterways connecting State canals in New York and Illinois, an Amazon River exploration, and tariff revision. The War Department requires seacoast armament and staff-corps promotions; the Navy has added eight new sloops of war. Postal revenues of $22,996,741.57 fell short of expenditures of $29,084,945.67; free delivery, postal savings depositories, and postal telegraphs are endorsed. Further recommendations include fixing Utah's jury system, repealing involuntary bankruptcy provisions, restricting claims against the Government, continuing the Indian reservation policy with a territorial government, an 1875 census, support for District of Columbia improvements and a national university, civil-service rules, Colorado's admission with an irrigation canal, general amnesty, and legislation securing civil rights for the enfranchised slave.

The passage provides storage instructions for viral qPCR nasopharyngeal swabs in the DAWn-plasma study: after routine local laboratory analysis, residual swab material should be refrigerated at 4°C for no more than 24 hours, then stored at -80°C (preferred) or -20°C until batch transport to the central laboratory in Leuven for later quantitative PCR analysis at an undefined timepoint. It also lists references to DAWn-plasma publications, including a 2020 Trials correction, a 2022 European Respiratory Journal paper, and two 2022 JAMA Network Open articles on convalescent plasma. Finally, it enumerates figures 2–8 and tables 1–16 covering endpoints, subgroup analyses, and adverse event classifications.

In this lecture, Alan Oppenheim demonstrates the effects of sampling and aliasing, along with properties of discrete-time linear systems, using a programmable digital filter whose parameters (coefficients, word length, sampling rate) can be easily changed. The system consists of a C-to-D converter (sampler), a digital filter, a discrete-time-to-time converter, and a smoothing low-pass filter.

For the first demonstration, the digital filter is set as an identity system to isolate sampling and aliasing effects. When the input frequency exceeds half the sampling frequency, the output takes on an alias and decreases in frequency even as the input increases. Because the real low-pass filter is not ideal, a beating phenomenon appears near half the sampling frequency. These effects are shown on an oscilloscope and audibly.

Next, a low-pass digital filter with a symmetric (linear phase) impulse response and cutoff at pi/5 is inserted. The equivalent continuous-time frequency response has the same shape as the digital filter's response but with a rescaled frequency axis, where 2 pi maps to the sampling frequency. Thus the effective cutoff frequency equals one-tenth of the sampling rate.

Demonstrations show the impulse response, the frequency response via sinusoidal sweeping, and the periodicity of the digital filter response. Changing the sampling rate (40, 20, 10, 5 kHz) correspondingly changes the effective cutoff frequency. The lecture concludes by low-pass filtering live ragtime audio at progressively decreasing sampling rates.

UCLA upset Penn State 42-37 at the Rose Bowl, the first win by a team that was 0-4 or worse over a top-10 opponent since UTEP beat No. 7 BYU in 1985. With Jerry Neuheisel calling plays after coordinator Tino Sunseri departed with fired head coach DeShaun Foster, UCLA built a 27-7 halftime lead and stopped a late Penn State fourth-down attempt. Quarterback Nico Iamaleava rushed 13 times for 150 yards and three touchdowns. The loss badly damaged Penn State's playoff hopes, leaving a projected 1.6% chance of finishing 10-2 and a most likely record of 7-5.

Florida also beat Texas 29-21, with DJ Lagway (21-of-28, 298 yards, two TDs) outplaying Arch Manning, who threw two interceptions. Texas fell to 20th in SP+ with a projected 7-5 record. Alabama beat Vanderbilt after two key Diego Pavia turnovers, and Miami defeated turnover-plagued Florida State, whose quarterback Tommy Castellanos has regressed after a strong start.

In the Big 12, Texas Tech cruised past Houston, Cincinnati beat previously unbeaten Iowa State for its fourth straight win, and Kansas and Baylor won one-score games. The article also covers SP+ rating risers and fallers, a weekly Heisman tracker led by Alabama's Ty Simpson, and dramatic lower-division finishes, including Western Carolina's record 46 straight completions and last-second wins for Georgetown, West Liberty, Wisconsin-Oshkosh, Wisconsin-La Crosse, and Augustana.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated January 29, 2019, announcing that Chief Financial Officer Deepak Ahuja intends to retire after serving in the role since 2008, apart from a 14-month gap. Ahuja will continue as CFO for a brief period and then serve as an advisor to ensure a smooth transition. Tesla intends to appoint Zachary Kirkhorn, currently Vice President of Finance, Financial Planning and Business Operations, as the new CFO. Kirkhorn joined Tesla in March 2010 and contributed to programs including Gigafactory 1 and the launches and ramps of Model X and Model 3. The filing includes statements from Elon Musk, Ahuja, and Kirkhorn, and was signed by General Counsel Dane Butswinkas on January 31, 2019.

Tarren Joseph Titus, 23, of Sarnia, who pleaded guilty to hydromorphone possession and two probation-order violations, was sentenced to three months of house arrest followed by a year's probation. Justice Deborah Austin called his transformation outstanding. Police found him escaping through a window during a 2017 raid. He must continue counseling, avoid drugs, and attend daily sobriety meetings.

Sun Waa, a Chinese takeaway in Littleover, Derby, was rated one out of five for food hygiene by Derby City Council inspectors after fried rice was left at room temperature for six hours, a wok obstructed a wash basin, and food debris built up on surfaces. Inspectors also found the sink being used for both raw meat and ready-to-eat foods, bleach spray in use, insect webbing, and a broken probe thermometer. Despite this, the takeaway averages 3.5 stars on TripAdvisor and 5.5 out of six on Just Eat. The manager says hygiene has since improved; inspectors revisited in January and will re-score in March. The November 2017 report was released after a Freedom of Information request.

Players Jonathan Toews, Brad Richards, and Kris Versteeg spoke ahead of a Stanley Cup Finals game against Tampa Bay. Toews said the team is focused on playing rather than the surrounding excitement, and that for previous winners there is no difference between winning at home or on the road. He described the playoff journey as going by quickly and said the team plays its best in later, more meaningful games. Richards said the experienced core, having won together before, is comfortable in these situations and needs fewer reminders. Toews praised coach Joel for identifying adjustments and bringing out players' best. Versteeg called the playoff run tough and expected close, grinding games against Tampa Bay, noting his new line built chemistry in the previous game. Toews credited health and proper preparation for the team's condition, while Richards stressed patience against an opponent trying to come back and praised a teammate's all-around play and multiple Finals appearances.

Researchers Michelle Munson of New York University and Sarah Narendorf of the University of Houston study how marginalized young adults—those facing challenges such as poverty, reliance on safety-net systems, disabilities, and young parenthood—make sense of their mental health conditions. Their published work argues that young adults' own interpretations of their symptoms, causes, and treatment options strongly influence their engagement with care, and that providers should elicit these "mental health narratives" within a collaborative therapeutic relationship. Using in-depth, face-to-face qualitative interviews, the team is developing training and technology-based interventions to help providers consider these narratives. They note that many marginalized young adults in New York and Houston do not get help partly because they do not feel heard, respected, or understood by providers.

Sixteen-year-old Murad Rahimov, an Uzbek immigrant who has dreamed of becoming an astronaut since age three, received a private tour of NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center. After his family immigrated to Kansas City in 2010, NPR profiled them when they became naturalized U.S. citizens. Listener Aaron Schnittman then connected NPR with his brother Jeremy, an astrophysicist at Goddard, who showed Murad and his mother Limara the clean room, spacecraft testing chambers, and laser lab, and discussed black holes and time travel. Murad, now a high school junior taking AP courses, aims to attend Cal Tech and one day lead a Mars mission. His mother says becoming a citizen has grounded her in her new country. Murad plans to watch the upcoming total solar eclipse from Kansas City, which lies in the path of totality.

The NRA claimed in an April 20 letter to members that YETI had cut ties with the organization. YETI responded that it eliminated outdated discounting programs and offered the NRA Foundation an alternative customization program, calling the NRA's statement inaccurate. Some NRA supporters planned a boycott, and Bryan Atkinson of South Carolina shot his explosive-filled YETI cooler with an AR-15, inspiring the trending #YetiCoolerChallenge. The dispute follows other businesses distancing themselves from the NRA after high-profile shootings. YETI stated it remains committed to the Second Amendment.

This study presents a benchmarking analysis of 15 summary-level data-based Mendelian randomization (MR) methods for causal inference using real-world genetic datasets. The methods were evaluated on three aspects: type I error control, accuracy of causal effect estimates, and replicability and power. Three confounding scenarios were tested using negative control trait pairs: population stratification (1,130 trait pairs), pleiotropy (77 trait pairs), and family-level confounders (82 trait pairs). Results showed that MR-APSS, Egger, Weighted-mode, and CAUSE achieved better type I error control across confounding scenarios, while the remaining 11 methods exhibited inflated p-values. IV selection thresholds significantly affected performance, with looser thresholds increasing type I error inflation for most methods. In accuracy evaluation using six trait pairs with known true causal effects of one, MR-APSS produced the most accurate estimates robust to weak IV bias and selection bias. In replicability analysis using LDL-C and CAD across six GWAS datasets, CAUSE and MR-APSS demonstrated the highest consistency. The study concludes that MR method performance depends heavily on underlying confounding factors and provides practical guidelines: using negative controls, adopting multiple IV selection standards, and gathering data from multiple independent sources.

The passage lists folate-rich foods: asparagus (33% of daily value per boiled cup), broccoli (14%), citrus fruits such as oranges (50 mcg each), legumes including beans, peas and lentils, avocado (110 mcg per cup), lady's finger (103 mcg per half cup), nuts and seeds like sunflower and flax seeds, cauliflower (55 mcg per cup), beetroot (14%), carrots (5%), and corn (34 mcg per cooked cup).

Four Hungarian female winemakers share their experiences. Zita Kovács, winemaking for seven years, initially faced prejudice but now feels respected as a winemaker. Zsófi Laposa, trained in California, Burgundy, and Bordeaux, says the profession has become more open, with women bringing gentleness and uniqueness. Krisztina Csetvei, founding owner of Csetvei Winery in Mór since 2011, balances winemaking with raising her daughter Panna, whose name inspired the Panna Rose wine presented at the VinCE Budapest Wine Show. Andi Gere co-manages her family winery with her father, believing women's elegance enriches Hungarian wine.

Anita Anand, presenter of Radio 4's Any Answers, was dropped from an edition less than 24 hours before broadcast because it was to feature discussion of the BBC gender pay dispute, which she had publicly criticised. Julian Worricker presented instead, and she is expected to return next week. Critics accused the BBC of insulting women journalists. BBC impartiality rules bar presenters who have spoken out on an issue from discussing it; Dame Jenni Murray similarly opted out of a Woman's Hour discussion. A BBC spokesman said editors decide case-by-case on such presenters to ensure impartiality.

This patent application, a continuation of several related applications, describes structurally-colored articles and methods of making and using them. Structural color arises from physical interactions of light—such as scattering, refraction, reflection, interference, and diffraction—with micro- or nano-scale features, rather than from dyes or pigments, which can pose environmental concerns. The disclosed articles incorporate an optical element, comprising one or more optical layers (e.g., a multilayer reflector or multilayer filter), optionally combined with a textured surface and/or a primer layer, to impart structural color without inks or pigments. Applicable articles include footwear (uppers, soles, and components such as bladders, foam, heel counters, and toe caps), apparel, athletic equipment, containers, electronic equipment, and vision wear. Structural color may be single-hued, multihued, iridescent, or angle-independent, and is characterized using color systems such as CIE 1976 (L*a*b*), CIELCH, and PANTONE at specified observation angles. Optical layers have adjacent layers of differing refractive indices (ranging from 1.3 to 2.6) and thicknesses of about 10 to 500 nanometers, and may comprise materials such as silicon dioxide, titanium dioxide, zinc sulfide, magnesium fluoride, tantalum pentoxide, or aluminum oxide. Textured surfaces include nanometer- to micrometer-scale profile features and flat areas whose dimensions, shapes, and spacing influence the resulting color. Optional primer layers may be dark-colored paints, inks, reground polymers, or metal/oxide layers, while protective and polymeric layers may provide durability or adhesion. Polymers used include thermoplastics and thermosets, particularly polyurethanes with hard and soft segments.

A flurry of deals announced Monday suggests mergers and acquisitions among junior mining companies, particularly in gold, may be heating up after slow months. Hecla Mining proposed a US$462 million cash-and-share acquisition of Klondex Mines—Canada's biggest mining deal this year—while Alio Gold offered $128 million for Rye Patch Gold. Only six mergers have occurred in Canada's metals and mining in 2018, versus 19 at this point in 2017. If approved, Hecla would acquire Klondex's three Nevada mines, lifting its annual gold output to about 370,000 ounces; Klondex shares jumped 61 percent. A third deal would see Anaconda Mining pay 14 cents per share for Maritime Resources. Leagold's CEO predicts more consolidation as junior miners seek to lower risk.

The MSPM0C1105/6 are cost-optimized, ultra-low-power 32-bit MCUs based on the Arm Cortex-M0+ core, operating up to 32MHz. They offer up to 64KB flash, 8KB SRAM, an accurate on-chip oscillator, and peripherals including a 12-bit 1.6 Msps ADC, comparator, timers, DMA, CRC-16 accelerator, and UART/SPI/I2C communication with multiple protocol support. TI supports these devices with LaunchPad kits, a free SDK, training, and online forums.
Former Nagaland minister Pusa, 63, who served in the SC Jamir-led Congress government and was a two-term opposition MLA, died. His funeral was held at his residence and he was buried at Viswema.

India's 21 state-run banks posted a record combined loss of 853.7 billion rupees ($12.65 billion) in the fiscal year ended March, driven by surging bad-loan provisions after the Reserve Bank of India withdrew loan restructuring schemes. Gross non-performing loans rose 15 percent to 8.96 trillion rupees. Despite a 2.11 trillion-rupee recapitalization plan, some fear banks will lack funds for growth after meeting Basel III capital requirements.

A Zillow analysis of homes sold or listed for rent between June 1, 2017 and May 31, 2018 in the 35 largest U.S. metro areas found that homes with air conditioning sold for 2.5 percent more than homes without it, a premium of nearly $5,500 for the typical U.S. home. The premium was highest in San Antonio (5.8 percent) and Cincinnati (5.7 percent). Per the 2017 Zillow Group Consumer Housing Trends Report, 62 percent of buyers listed air conditioning as a required feature, compared with 48 percent who considered a private outdoor space essential. The EPA notes unusually hot summer days have become more common, which may explain air conditioning becoming a necessity. Nationally, 66.1 percent of homes sold in the past year had air conditioning, including 99.1 percent in Las Vegas and 97.9 percent in Phoenix. Rentals with central air conditioning rented for 2.8 percent more, about $40 monthly, with the highest rent premiums in New York, Las Vegas and Phoenix; renters may pay more because they are less able to install air conditioning themselves.

This passage is an FAQ-style overview of options trading in IWM. Options trading involves buying and selling call options, which grant the right to buy shares at an agreed-upon price, and put options, which grant the right to sell shares. Benefits include leverage, hedging against market risk, and speculating without owning shares. Available order types include market, limit, stop, and trailing stop orders. Strategies include buying calls or puts, selling covered calls, and buying protective puts. Risks include losing the entire investment and unlimited risk when shorting calls. Requirements include being at least 18 years old, having sufficient funds, and maintaining a margin account, with minimum balances typically around $2,000 depending on the broker. Margin trading is allowed but carries risk. Investors should allocate no more than 10% of their portfolio to options, conduct research, use technical indicators such as moving averages and RSI, set stop-loss orders, and backtest strategies. Taxes apply as short-term or long-term capital gains. The article concludes that beginners should avoid options trading.

Gov. Kay Ivey announced the voluntary Alabama Sentry Program, allowing administrators at schools without a school resource officer to keep a firearm in a safe on campus to respond to an active shooter. Participants must complete training and receive approval from the local superintendent, school board, and county sheriff. Sentries must store firearms in secured storage and provide approved weapons, ammunition, and bullet-proof vests. The program serves as an interim security measure until more School Resource Officers can be added.

A hockey player describes Detroit as the strongest team his side has faced, citing their firepower and arguably the world's best goaltender. He stresses avoiding penalties, noting officials are calling every infraction and that Detroit's power play must not be given too many opportunities. He criticizes embellishment and marginal calls but says players must adapt and abide by the rules. He praises Detroit's checking line centered by Kris Draper as big, fast, and underrated. The team held a meeting to stay focused on the game despite distractions, and he expresses excitement about playing at home, claiming their arena is louder than Detroit's. He says his line struggled last game and must generate more offense, and emphasizes winning faceoffs against Detroit's skilled draw men like Yzerman, Fedorov, and Draper. He also praises Detroit's top defenseman as positionally smart and difficult to hit, and jokes about his growing playoff beard.

This patent application, a continuation-in-part of U.S. application Ser. No. 17/006,431 filed Aug. 28, 2020, describes systems and methods for tracing cryptocurrency money flow and managing blockchain transaction risk using artificial intelligence and machine learning. Noting that cryptocurrency's decentralized nature facilitates money laundering and terrorism financing, and that exchanges struggle to comply with AML/CFT regulations, the disclosure presents a method that receives blockchain transaction data (addresses, transaction identifications, timestamps, and transferred digital assets) and intelligence labels from a blockchain ecosystem intelligence (BEI) database containing known behavioral characteristics of entities. A blockchain transaction flow—comprising source, intermediate, and destination addresses and intermediate transactions—is selected, and input trace parameters (objective directional setting, tracing constraint, transaction filter) are received. Intelligence labels are applied to create labeled addresses, an artificial intelligence graph search algorithm determines an auto-traced path of the digital assets, and a report with tracing destination summary statistics and suspicious addresses is generated. If a suspicious address is found, actions may include alerting a user or suspending transactions. An interactive journey board visualization may also be generated.

A risk management system comprises a digital asset intake engine, an entity knowledge base (including blacklist, device, and computer network intelligence databases), a risk classification engine with a machine learning model (e.g., decision tree or AutoML), a risk scoring regression engine, a rules-based risk policy engine, and a security control system that blocks transactions, freezes assets, or suspends accounts when risk scores are high and approves transactions when normal. Risk scores (0–100) are bucketized as Safe, Legitimate, Unknown, Suspicious, or Risky, with an optional time decaying factor. Behavior classification uses statistics, topology, temporal, linkage, derived, and sequential feature categories to identify exchanges, mixers, bots, and bad actor clusters. The system supports multiple blockchains and fiat tracing via exchange KYC mappings. Auto tracing employs address clustering and graph search algorithms such as greedy breadth-first search and Dijkstra's algorithm, producing interactive visualizations, summary reports, and proactive monitoring alerts.

The passage primarily consists of repeated financial news headlines covering topics such as the Bank of England's AI bubble warning, gold surpassing $4,000, Fifth Third's $10.9 billion acquisition of Comerica, AMD's chip supply deal with OpenAI, and Germany's antitrust probe into Temu. The main article reports that the Bank of England warned the rally in AI-related stocks may be approaching unsustainable levels, with valuations resembling the dot-com bubble. The BoE highlighted the concentration of gains among U.S. tech giants including Nvidia, Microsoft, and Meta, which could amplify systemic vulnerabilities, and cited potential bottlenecks in power supply, semiconductor capacity, and data infrastructure. While the UK financial system remains broadly stable, the BoE warned that Britain's financial openness leaves it exposed to shocks from U.S. equity markets. The IMF has voiced similar concerns. The passage also describes Pan Finance, a global financial intelligence publication with over 200,000 readers across 150 countries.

A survey of 100 financial services professionals by Infosys Finacle found that over 80% of global bankers expect commercial blockchain adoption by 2020, with average investment this year around $1 million. Top use cases include cross-border payments and digital identity management; 69% of banks prefer private blockchains.

Plum School District officials will begin 2018-19 budget discussions Tuesday, earlier than in past years, hoping to avoid a third consecutive tax increase; the district starts the school year more than $4 million in debt. This year's $66 million budget included a 0.866-mill tax hike and no program cuts. The board also plans to recruit tuition-paying Chinese students for 2018-19 after visa delays prevented the program this year. Tuesday's workshop will also address elementary construction, consolidation, redistricting, and the process for closing Regency Park Elementary School.

A pump and dump scheme involves a promoter acquiring a position in a stock, typically a penny stock, and artificially inflating its price by spreading false or misleading information. As the price rises, the promoter sells shares to latecomers, causing the price to drop significantly. These schemes are illegal on regulated exchanges and considered immoral, benefiting only promoters and early investors. They occur mainly in the OTC market and the unregulated crypto market, where low-volume coins are targeted, often organized via Telegram. One promoter, aged 16 in 1999, made nearly a million dollars through such schemes before settling with the SEC. A German study found nearly 6% of sampled investors participated in at least one pump-and-dump scheme, with an average return of -28%. Pump and dump schemes account for 15% of spam emails. The passage advises avoiding such schemes and being cautious with OTC market stocks showing sudden price increases.

This patent application, a continuation of earlier U.S., PCT, and Chinese filings, relates to wireless communications and provides methods, apparatuses, and systems for transmitting paging information. In new-generation wireless systems using high-frequency carriers (e.g., 28, 45, or 70 GHz), beamforming limits each transmit port's coverage to a small angle, so paging information is repeatedly transmitted across multiple beams in a time-division multiplexed manner. Because a UE in an IDLE state cannot foresee how beams or ports are scheduled across timeslots, the LTE discontinuous reception (DRX) mechanism is complex or impossible to implement. To address this, a first communication node (e.g., a base station) calculates the time domain position of a paging occasion (PO) of a second communication node (e.g., a UE) and transmits paging information—paging downlink control information and/or a paging message—within that PO. The PO comprises a group of paging resources on one or more preset beams or ports and may correspond to a synchronous signal (SS) burst set or sweeping resources. The PO is determined using parameters such as the DRX cycle, paging transmission interval, number of paging transmissions, device identifier, and PO offset, with formulas provided for calculating the starting radio frame number. Additional methods use indication or configuration of quasi-co-location relationships between paging-related signals and other sweeping signals or channels. Corresponding apparatuses, a system, storage media, base stations, terminal devices, and computer program products are also disclosed.

In response, Argus Research upgraded the stock from hold to buy with a $120 price target, implying roughly 12.5% growth, citing expected cash flow milestones and increased defense spending. The author disagrees with the buy rating, arguing the stock's valuation—22 times trailing earnings and an enterprise value-to-free-cash-flow ratio exceeding 40—is too expensive given expected annual profit growth of no more than 10%.

Under Director Jill Medvedow, Boston's Institute of Contemporary Art (ICA) transformed from a struggling institution—housed in a converted police station, with a budget under $1 million, no permanent collection, and 25,000 annual visitors—into a major cultural destination. When Medvedow arrived in 1998, her mandate was to stabilize and reinvent the museum. A business planning group determined the ICA needed to grow its audience, expand education, and relocate. Believing a waterfront location was essential, Medvedow pursued Parcel J on Fan Pier, land the Pritzker family had committed to cultural use. Despite the ICA's weakness, her presentation won the parcel in November 1999.

With Gloria Larson's help, Medvedow built political and community support. Paul Bessire was hired to lead a capital campaign that ultimately raised over $75 million, surpassing its $62 million goal, while new board members were recruited from business and finance. After a public selection process, the ICA chose Diller + Scofidio, a firm that had never built in the United States, to design the building. Despite obstacles—including regulatory approvals, the Pritzkers' withdrawal from the surrounding development, and construction delays—the new $51 million building opened in December 2006, drawing over 280,000 visitors in its first year and sustaining strong attendance through 2009.
The Eighth Circuit dismissed Pink C. Jenkins's appeal on April 10, 1937, with appellant's consent.

This study proposes "whole human pedagogy," a novel framework for education abroad grounded in hooks' engaged pedagogy, Thompson's tenderness pedagogy, and decolonial theory. The framework centers four tenets—embodiment, emotions, belonging, and becoming—that treat students as integrated human beings with bodily, emotional, relational, and meaning-making knowledge. The study asked how education abroad practitioners understand this approach across the four themes.

Using purposive and snowball sampling, researchers conducted 60–90-minute semi-structured virtual interviews with seventeen U.S.-based practitioners in Fall 2023, analyzing transcripts inductively in NVivo. Participants responded enthusiastically, with most spontaneously describing two or three tenets. Embodiment was linked to physically immersive, place-based experiences; emotions to culture shock, expectation-setting, and reflection; belonging to communal relationships, reciprocity, and trust rather than hierarchical facilitation; and becoming to transformation and self-knowing.

The authors conclude that whole human pedagogy offers a compelling framework that destabilizes dominant Euro-U.S. epistemologies by centering collaboration, presence, mutuality, creativity, and wellbeing. It holds theoretical significance, practical applications for program development and professional development, and value as a framework for future research.

Sean "Diddy" Combs, 55, was sentenced Friday to four years and two months in prison and fined $500,000 for transporting people across state lines for sexual encounters under the Mann Act. He was acquitted of sex trafficking and racketeering charges that could have led to a life sentence. Having already served a year in jail, he will be released in about three years. Judge Arun Subramanian said Combs' power and resources allowed the abuse to continue. Combs apologized and asked for leniency. His nearly two-month Manhattan trial featured testimony from accusers, including ex-girlfriend Cassie, who described beatings, threats, sexual assault, and drug-fueled "freak-offs." The passage covers container design patterns for distributed systems. The **sidecar pattern** pairs an application container with an auxiliary container that extends its functionality—examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy HTTP-only service via an nginx sidecar, synchronizing configuration from an API to a shared filesystem, and deploying a reusable topz container for resource introspection. Building reusable sidecars requires parameterizing containers (preferably via environment variables), defining stable APIs, and documenting images using Dockerfile directives such as EXPOSE, ENV, and LABEL.

The **ambassador pattern** brokers communication between an application and the outside world: the application connects to localhost while the ambassador handles routing. Uses include client-side sharding (e.g., twemproxy with sharded Redis or memcached), service brokering for portability across environments, and request splitting for experiments (e.g., nginx directing 10% of traffic to a beta service using IP hashing).

The **adapter pattern** standardizes heterogeneous application interfaces. Adapter containers can expose metrics in a common format (e.g., a Prometheus exporter for Redis), normalize logs (e.g., fluentd collecting Redis slow queries and Storm logs), and perform rich health checks (e.g., a Go-based adapter running diagnostic queries against MySQL).

**Microservices** break applications into small, independently scalable services communicating over formal APIs, improving team autonomy and scaling but complicating debugging and design; distributed patterns mitigate these challenges.

**Replicated load-balanced services** replicate stateless servers behind a load balancer for redundancy and scale; at least two replicas are needed for high availability. Readiness probes inform the load balancer when replicas can serve traffic. Session tracking (IP hashing internally, cookies externally) keeps a user on the same replica. Additional tiers can provide caching (Varnish), rate limiting for denial-of-service defense, and SSL termination (nginx).

**Sharded services** split data across machines, with a root routing requests to the appropriate shard—useful when state exceeds a single machine's capacity (e.g., a sharded cache storing 50% versus 5% of data). Cache hit rate affects system capacity and latency; replicated sharded caches add resilience and enable hot-shard scaling. Sharding functions rely on deterministic, uniform hashes with the modulo operator; key selection (e.g., request path, country derived from IP) matters, and consistent hashing limits key remapping when resizing.

Finally, the **scatter/gather pattern** farms requests simultaneously to all replicas, each returning partial results that the root combines, parallelizing computation across machines.

Months after the Trump administration's Department of Government Efficiency cut more than 100 research contracts and sharply reduced staff at the U.S. Department of Education, education researchers express cautious optimism. The department plans to reinstate 20 contracts, a lawsuit offers a reprieve for 10 regional education labs, and it is seeking public input on modernizing the Institute of Education Sciences, with Amber Northern of the Thomas B. Researchers, many speaking anonymously for fear of jeopardizing funding, remain concerned about staff shortages, data quality, reduced NAEP reporting, and an executive order requiring a large admissions data collection. Some view the reinstated labs and IES reform as opportunities to rebuild differently.
