Hubble imaged NGC 5949, a dwarf galaxy 44 million light-years away with a hundredth of the Milky Way's mass. Its loosely-bound spiral arms make it a barred spiral. Discovered by William Herschel in 1801, dwarf galaxies pose puzzles such as the "cuspy halo" and "missing satellites" problems.

The Ultimate Oscillator (UO) is a momentum indicator developed by Larry Williams in 1976 that measures price momentum across three timeframes (7, 14, and 28 periods), combining them in a weighted average (4:2:1) to avoid the early overbought signals and false divergences common in single-timeframe oscillators. It ranges from 0 to 100, with readings below 30 considered oversold and above 70 overbought. Trading signals are generated through divergence between price and the indicator, with specific criteria required for buy and sell signals. Backtests show the indicator performs well across various settings; one optimized strategy on SPY produced a profit factor of 2.5, a 78% win rate, and a 25% maximum drawdown. The UO is a consistent and stable mean reversion indicator suitable for building trading strategies.

Mr. Stevens's 1892 dispatches reported revolutionary plans in Hawaii held in check only by a United States naval vessel, hostility to the "half English" heir, and growing inclination toward annexation. Dissatisfaction persisted over the Queen's subjection to Wilson, a half-caste Tahitian marshal. After a cabinet was voted out and a deadlock followed, a decisive want-of-confidence vote came on October 17. Stevens warned that unless the Queen yielded, the monarchy's overthrow could not be long delayed, and later urged either annexation or a customs union, an ocean cable, cession of Pearl Harbor, and an American protectorate. Navy reports corroborated these accounts until January 28, when news arrived of a peaceful revolution and the Queen's dethronement. United States policy from 1820 to 1893 is described as close friendship and protection, with distrust of foreign intervention and occasional contemplation of annexation, notably under President Pierce. An appendix notes supporting correspondence and three unperfected treaties (1849, 1855, 1867).

The Supreme Court dismissed Pradyuman's father's plea seeking cancellation of interim bail granted to the Pinto family, owners of Ryan International School, in his son's murder case. The CBI held a class 11 student responsible for the killing.

Automation threatens millions of jobs, including 3.5 million American truck drivers who may be displaced within decades, and the World Economic Forum predicts over five million jobs will be eliminated in the next five years. The article proposes human augmentation as a response, a theme explored at Austin's Bodyhacking Conference. Three approaches are discussed: augmenting brains through Elon Musk's proposed "neural lace," an electronic mesh integrating with the brain—building on Harvard nanotechnologists' syringe-injectable electronics tested in mice; augmenting bodies with exosuits, such as SuitX's MAX, which reduces force by up to 60 percent, and Harvard Biodesign Lab's soft exosuits, which cut walking effort by nearly 23 percent and are being developed with DARPA; and augmenting skillsets, per Tom Davenport and Julia Kirby's advice that workers develop non-codifiable skills like creativity or learn to maintain machines—though this guidance mainly applies to knowledge workers, while physical laborers face a harder transition. Davenport is optimistic many workers will adapt but warns that artificial general intelligence would change everything.

Lava from Hawaii's Kilauea volcano crossed Highway 132, knocking out power to Vacationland and Kapoho Beach Lots. Officials confirmed 71 homes destroyed since the eruption began May 3, with the number expected to rise. Over 400 utility poles have been destroyed, and Kapoho area residents were advised to evacuate. At least one trapped person was rescued. A new fissure brought the total to 24. Lava covered two wells at a geothermal plant, but officials said the plugged wells are stable with no dangerous gases released.

Meb Faber's Tactical Asset Allocation strategy is an active trend-following approach that uses market timing to allocate assets across five categories: U.S. stocks, foreign stocks, U.S. bonds, U.S. REITs, and world commodities. Investors enter and exit the market based on the strategy's signals rather than remaining fully invested as in passive strategies. The strategy can be implemented using five well-diversified index ETFs with good historical performance, eliminating the need to pick individual securities. Meb Faber is the co-founder and chief investment officer of Cambria Investment Management, author of five books and numerous white papers, and a University of Virginia graduate. Each asset class receives a 20% allocation; when no signal exists for an asset in a given month, the position is held in cash. Backtests over 16 years showed a maximum drawdown of only -13.24%, much lower than the 40-50% or higher drawdowns of passive portfolios. The timing model is universal and applicable to other asset classes and ETFs.

The Minnesota Court of Appeals remanded a child support modification case for findings consistent with Moylan v. Moylan. Richard Berg appealed a trial court order increasing his child support from $145 to $258 per child per month (a guidelines level of $516 total) after his net income rose 34.5% since the parties' 1981 divorce. The trial court found the increased income made the original decree's terms unreasonable and unfair. While the appellate court found the support amount to be within the trial court's discretion, it held the findings inadequate because Moylan requires specific findings of the reasons for increasing child support under the relevant statutes. The court did not outright reverse the result but remanded for further factual inquiry.

Photographer Richard Mosse's project *Heat Maps* documents the refugee crisis across Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East, where 65.3 million people are displaced according to the UNHCR. Using a military-grade thermal telephoto camera on a robotic arm, the images render human figures as translucent grey forms—a deliberate dehumanizing effect Mosse employs to reflect how refugees are regarded and to make viewers confront their complicity, since camp conditions are created by elected governments. Taken from up to 50 kilometers away, the photos raise privacy concerns, though subjects' identities remain technically intact. The large-scale panoramas are constructed from nearly a thousand smaller frames sewn together. Mosse subverts the camera's surveillance and weapons-targeting origins, as in his earlier *Infra* series on the Democratic Republic of Congo, employing a Brechtian distancing effect. The three-year project faced logistical obstacles, including access to the Calais Jungle and failed attempts to reach Timbuktu. *Heat Maps* is on display at the Jack Shainman Gallery in New York until March 11.

President Trump announced that the U.S. will impose an additional 100% tariff on Chinese imports, on top of existing tariffs, starting Nov. 1, along with export controls on "any and all critical software." The move retaliates against China's new export controls on rare earths minerals, of which China supplies about 70% of the global supply and which are essential for automobiles, defense, and semiconductors. Trump suggested he might cancel a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping at an upcoming summit in South Korea. Chinese imports currently face an effective tariff rate of 40%. China's new rules, effective Dec. 1, require licenses for exporting products containing more than 0.1% Chinese-sourced rare earths or made using Chinese extraction, refining, magnet-making, or recycling technology.

The double bottom chart pattern is a bullish reversal price action formation consisting of two swing lows at approximately the same level with a swing high between them. The swing lows establish a support level, while the swing high creates a resistance level known as the neckline. The pattern appears in a downtrend (or a prolonged pullback in an uptrend) and is considered complete when the price breaks above the neckline, signaling a potential end to the decline. Traders estimate profit targets by measuring the pattern's size and projecting it upward from the neckline, typically placing stop losses in the middle of the pattern for a 2:1 reward/risk ratio, or below the pattern for greater safety. Aggressive traders may enter during the second low's formation, while conservative traders wait for a confirmed close above the neckline with increased volume. Thomas Bulkowski's research found 68% of double bottom formations reach their target, nearly twice the rate of the double top pattern, though the authors prefer fully quantified backtests over manually identified patterns.

India has demanded the UN secretariat disclose information about misconduct cases by UN staff and the immunity invoked against prosecutions. UDMA write CRC corruption after device termination stems from corrupted state residue from a prior UDMA read with host termination. After a device termination, the ATAC passes a correct CRC for the first portion but fails to start a new CRC for the next, causing errors. UDMA writes generally cannot be used; use the UDMA I/O blocking feature (ATAC Error MSR bit 8).

The court fined defendant Pomeroy $1,000 for each of six offenses, totaling $6,000, and the New York Central and Hudson River Railroad Company $18,000 for each of six crimes, totaling $108,000. The speaker criticizes the unsatisfactory state of criminal law, caused largely by judgments being set aside on technicalities unrelated to the merits, and proposes that no judgment be set aside or new trial granted for procedural errors unless a miscarriage of justice affirmatively appears. On injunctions, the speaker doubts that abolishing them in labor cases would be effective or right, since courts need power against mob violence, but their abuse should be curbed. Judges should enjoin violence yet not forbid laboring men's peaceful betterment or aid corporate aggrandizement; improperly granted preliminary injunctions can do irreparable wrong, and habitual abuse threatens the injunction's existence. Judges who disregard wrong public sentiment deserve honor, but criticism of faulty judges should be permitted, as judges are largely answerable only to public opinion.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed the district court's dismissal of an antitrust action brought by Sea Breeze Salt, Inc. and Innofood, S.A. de C.V. against Mitsubishi Corporation, Mitsubishi International Corporation, and Exportadora de Sal, S.A. de C.V. (ESSA), a Mexican salt producer 51-percent owned by the Mexican government. Plaintiffs alleged that ESSA, after terminating its Director General, breached distribution contracts and returned to selling its salt exclusively to Mitsubishi, supporting five claims under the Sherman Act, Clayton Act, and California law. The court held the suit barred by the act of state doctrine, which precludes U.S. courts from adjudicating the sovereign acts of foreign nations. Both required elements were satisfied: ESSA's exclusive distribution arrangement constituted an official act of Mexico performed within its territory, because decisions about exploiting natural resources are sovereign acts and sea salt is a natural resource owned by the Mexican state under its Constitution; and the relief sought would require invalidating Mexico's sovereign decisions about exploiting its salt. The Sabbatino factors—absence of international consensus against such arrangements, significant foreign relations implications given ESSA's output of 90 percent of Mexico's salt exports, and the continued existence of Mexico's government—further supported application of the doctrine. The court declined to decide whether a commercial exception to the doctrine exists, finding any such exception inapplicable because the alleged acts were sovereign in nature. The court also held that Sea Breeze's previously suspended corporate status, since restored, did not require dismissal of its appeal, and emphasized the narrow scope of its holding.

Interferometric second-harmonic generation (SHG) polarimetry is demonstrated as a non-destructive, scalable probe for assessing crystalline quality in two-dimensional hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). Because hBN's threefold rotational symmetry allows two antiparallel orientations to nucleate on sixfold-symmetric metal substrates, grain boundaries form during CVD growth and degrade material properties, yet conventional methods (TEM, STM, LEED, Raman) cannot detect such domains over large areas. Combining polarization-resolved SHG with interferometric detection, the authors optically resolved antiparallel domains and their boundaries in CVD-grown hBN, showing these are pervasive even in films that appear unidirectionally aligned. SHG intensity varied by up to three orders of magnitude across ten CVD growth conditions, far exceeding Raman variations, and a mixed-domain model attributed this suppression to destructive interference among antiparallel domains, with intensity scaling with domain size. Benchmarking against mechanically exfoliated hBN established correlations among SHG intensity, Raman intensity and linewidth, and orientational spread, providing quantitative metrics of crystallinity. The methodology is broadly applicable to other non-centrosymmetric 2D crystals, including transition metal dichalcogenides.

This study used untargeted metabolomics to identify metabolite changes associated with transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) placement and post-TIPS hepatic encephalopathy (HE) development. Twenty-two participants undergoing TIPS provided peripheral vein (PIV) and hepatic vein (HV) blood samples before and after the procedure and before discharge, and were monitored for up to one year for HE.

The largest metabolomic changes occurred between the post-procedure PIV sample and the before-discharge sample, with bile acids as major contributors. Bile acid abundance dropped immediately after shunt placement and returned to pre-procedure levels by discharge. Glycoursodeoxycholic acid was the only annotated metabolite significantly different pre- to post-PIV.

Participants who developed HE showed greater dissimilarity between their pre- and post-TIPS HV metabolomes, suggesting that less pre-existing intrahepatic shunting predicts worse post-TIPS HE. More severe HE was associated with larger decreases from baseline in bile acids and glycerophosphocholines. Three conjugated hydroxylated bile acids in post-PIV samples were inversely correlated with HE grade, and two participants readmitted for HE showed bile acid declines post-TIPS with increases after HE treatment.

Chemical proportionality analysis identified fluctuations in glycerophosphocholine and bilirubin clusters, including altered biliverdin reduction, particularly in participants with severe HE. The authors conclude that bile acids may play a protective role against HE, that pre-TIPS intrahepatic shunting may be protective, and that these metabolites could serve as biomarkers or therapeutic targets.

The passage covers container design patterns and multi-node distributed system architectures. It begins with the adapter pattern, illustrated through examples: using Prometheus to monitor containers by adapting services like Redis to expose a compatible metrics API; normalizing heterogeneous logging formats using Fluentd as an adapter container; and adding rich health checks to a MySQL database via an adapter container running diagnostic queries, avoiding modification of the original image. The adapter pattern enables modularity, reuse, and sharing of solutions across the community.

The passage then introduces multi-node distributed patterns, contrasting them with tightly coupled single-node patterns. Microservices—systems of components communicating over defined APIs—offer benefits including smaller team scope, decoupling via formal contracts, and independent scaling, but make debugging and system design more difficult.

The replicated load-balanced service pattern suits stateless services, with at least two replicas needed for high availability. Readiness probes inform load balancers when applications are prepared to serve requests. Session tracking (via IP hashing or application-level methods like cookies) routes a user's requests to the same replica. A caching layer (e.g., Varnish) improves performance, and can also provide rate limiting for denial-of-service defense; SSL termination is handled by an nginx layer since Varnish cannot perform it.

Sharded services, where each replica serves only a subset of requests, are generally used for stateful services whose data exceeds a single machine's capacity. Sharded caches improve memory utilization compared to replicated caches. Sharding functions map requests to shards using hashing with the modulo operator; choosing an appropriate key (e.g., request path or country derived from IP) is critical. Consistent hashing functions minimize key remapping when the number of shards changes. Replicating each shard adds resilience and enables "hot sharding" to handle uneven load.

The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes request processing across leaf nodes, with a root combining partial results. It faces limitations from per-node overhead and the straggler problem, so replicating each shard improves reliability and enables upgrades under load.

Finally, the passage discusses functions-as-a-service (FaaS) and event-driven computing. Benefits include simplified deployment, automatic scaling, and forced decoupling; challenges include difficult debugging, poor fit for background processing or memory-heavy applications, and unfavorable per-request costs at sustained high volumes. FaaS patterns include the decorator pattern (request/response transformation, such as adding defaults), event handling (e.g., two-factor authentication), and event-based pipelines (e.g., new-user signup flows).

This document is a specification update (March 2006) for the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device, Silicon Revision A3, listing numerous hardware errata with descriptions, implications, and resolutions. Key issues include: UART registers and LPC I/O cycles being inaccessible or unreliable during block/demand mode legacy DMA (single transfer mode is recommended); system hangs from I/O cycles at addresses 10000h or higher; failure to meet USB over-voltage protection specifications, requiring external protection circuits; PIC interrupt failures when automatic clock gating is enabled; CRC corruption in UDMA writes following device termination; byte accesses to ACPI PM1_STS/PM1_EN registers causing hangs; WORD/BYTE writes to PMC registers potentially corrupting other registers; KEL emulation and Snoop mode defects; unreliable SSMI generation when concurrent IRQs occur; UDMA failures when PIO command packets follow bus master enables; most wake event inputs not functioning from ACPI S3 state (PWRBTN# is the workaround); RTC CMOS RAM read errors; USB controller clock gating failures; ATAC hangs with non-DWORD-aligned PRD addresses; LPC aborts on certain SYNC patterns; SMB controller NEGACK bit issues; GPIO High Bank register corruption after suspend; and Sleep_X de-assertion failures when delay counters exceed the PM_SED delay. Several issues have no operational impact or no resolution. The document concludes with AMD's standard copyright, disclaimer, and trademark notices.

In his first inaugural address, the speaker expresses deep anxiety at being summoned from his chosen retreat to lead the country, doubting his own qualifications for civil administration, and hopes his motives will excuse any errors. He offers supplications to the Almighty Being who rules the Universe, asking that divine blessing consecrate the new government, and observes that the nation's founding and recent constitutional revolution display providential agency. Rather than recommending particular measures, he refers to the Constitutional Charter and praises the talents, rectitude, and patriotism of the assembled representatives, expressing confidence that national policy will rest on the pure principles of private morality. He asserts an indissoluble union between virtue and happiness, warns that Heaven's favor cannot be expected from a nation disregarding the rules of order and right, and notes that the preservation of liberty and the republican model are staked on the American experiment. He leaves to Congress's judgment whether to exercise the amendment power under the Fifth Article of the Constitution. Addressing the House of Representatives, he declines any personal emoluments, requesting that estimates for his station be limited to actual expenditures. He closes with a prayer for divine blessing on the government's deliberations.

James T. Hodgkinson, 66, shot Rep. Steve Scalise and several others during a congressional baseball practice in Alexandria, Virginia, before being fatally shot by police guarding Scalise. Authorities said he had apparently lived out of a white van in northern Virginia since March after leaving his southern Illinois home, and was frequently seen at a nearby YMCA, where he kept mostly to himself. He had expressed grievances online about President Trump and Republicans, but a motive remains undetermined. Armed with a handgun and rifle, he died from multiple gunshot wounds. Aide Zack Barth was shot but expected to recover fully, and two Capitol Police officers sustained minor injuries. Hodgkinson had volunteered for Bernie Sanders' 2016 campaign, written newspaper letters about income inequality, and had past arrests, including a 2006 battery charge that was dismissed. Months earlier, a neighbor reported him firing a rifle into a cornfield; no charges were filed.

In this negligence action, plaintiff James D. Rone appealed a jury verdict in favor of defendant Boncar Construction Company and the pretrial striking of a count alleging violation of the Illinois Structural Work Act. Rone, a line foreman employed by Dan Raymond Construction Company (Boncar's joint venturer on an Indiana sewer project), was injured when his hand was caught in a moving cable while descending from a back hoe's gantry, where he had climbed to lift telephone wires. The court held that although the dismissal of the Illinois Structural Work Act count was appealable, plaintiff waived the issue by failing to perfect his earlier appeal. The court further held that questions of negligence, proximate cause, and contributory negligence were properly submitted to the jury because conflicting inferences could be drawn from the undisputed facts; that the Indiana Employers Liability Act did not bar the contributory negligence defense; that the Testa case relied on by plaintiff was distinguishable; and that refusal of plaintiff's tendered instructions was not error. Judgment affirmed.

The President transmits to Congress a letter from the governor of Texas and his response concerning Texas's attempt to extend civil jurisdiction over territory east of the Rio Grande, including Santa Fe, where United States military officers opposed the effort. The AEGEAN study evaluated adherence and persistence to apixaban in subjects with atrial fibrillation, comparing a Primary SOC group with an Additional Educational Program group (plus a Secondary SOC group in Study Part 2). Time to apixaban initiation, drug exposure, treatment interruptions, and dosing (mostly 5 mg BID) were comparable across groups. Mean compliance exceeded 95% at Weeks 4, 12, and 24 and was >94% at Week 48 in all groups. Adherence at 24 weeks was 91.64% (Primary SOC) versus 91.88% (Additional Educational Program), with no significant difference; adherence declined significantly in later treatment periods. Persistence was ~91% at 24 weeks and 85–88% at 48 weeks, without significant group differences. Logit models identified certain non-adherence predictors (e.g., alcohol consumption, technical occupations, permanent atrial fibrillation, MMSE score) in the Primary SOC group. Safety endpoints, including adverse events, bleeding events, and deaths, were similar between groups. The educational program provided no additional adherence or persistence benefit.

Opening range breakout (ORB) strategies, popularized by Tony Crabel's 1990 book, involve entering trades when price breaks above or below the high and low recorded during an initial period after the market opens. Backtests on S&P 500 futures show these strategies perform poorly without additional filters, with minimal average gains per trade and low win rates; short-side breakouts performed even worse, and similar negative results were found for Nasdaq, gold, silver, and oil contracts. However, adding daily filters based on longer trends, volume, or other indicators can produce tradeable strategies—one example achieved a 0.27% average gain, 65% win rate, and a profit factor of 2. The article attributes the decline of ORB strategies to false breakouts, gains occurring during night sessions, powerful computers arbing away strategies, and the tendency for daily highs and lows to occur in the first and last hours of trading. Individual stocks may yield better results than indices, and traders are advised to use strategy optimization while avoiding overfitting.

The Amoeba defense, developed by coach Jerry Tarkanian at the University of Las Vegas, contributed to UNLV's 1990 NCAA Championship. It is an aggressive, trapping, match-up zone defense run from a 1-1-3 alignment, used to disrupt and confuse opponents. The defender guarding the ballhandler applies extreme pressure while the other four defenders zone. Due to its aggressive outside rotations, it requires quick guards but, when executed, results in steals and easy transition baskets. The defense specifies initial positioning and responses to wing pass entries, corner passes, trap options, post/wing exchanges, skip passes, ball reversals, guard/wing interchanges, and cross-court passes. Against a two-guard front, X1 and X2 match up, and a pass into the high post triggers a triple team by X1, X2, and X5, while X3 and X4 close passing lanes for steals.

Momentum investing buys stocks with the best historical performance over 3-12 months and periodically rebalances the portfolio toward the highest-momentum stocks, based on the hypothesis that past medium-term returns correlate with future returns. Eric Crittenden's 2016 research found that between 1989 and 2015, roughly 20% of stocks accounted for all market gains while 80% produced zero returns, suggesting momentum investing can help by buying strong stocks and avoiding weak ones. A backtested monthly momentum strategy for the S&P 500 using a simple moving average crossover turned 100,000 in 1960 into 5.575 million by February 2023, an annual return of 6.6% versus buy-and-hold's 7%. Although slightly worse than buy-and-hold, the strategy was invested only 69% of the time, had smaller drawdowns (26% versus 55%), and a risk-adjusted return of 9.5%. The S&P 500 Momentum Index (SP500MUP) tracks stocks showing relative strength.

This study used an emulated trial design with VHA electronic health record data to evaluate the association between SARS-CoV-2 infection and suicide attempts and self-directed violence among US Veterans. Matched cohorts included 198,938 infected Veterans and 992,036 uninfected comparators. Within one year of the index date, 3,078 Veterans (0.258%) had a documented suicide attempt and 2,887 (0.242%) had self-directed violence, with unadjusted event rates higher in the infected group across all follow-up periods. In intent-to-treat Cox regression analyses, infected Veterans had higher risk of suicide attempts (one-year HR=1.41) and self-directed violence (one-year HR=1.38) than comparators, with the greatest risk during the first 30 days after infection (short-term HRs of 2.54 and 1.94, respectively). Risk was elevated across most age groups and was highest among those without prior suicide attempts or self-directed violence, though analyses of those with prior history were underpowered. Reported suicide deaths (237, unvalidated) did not differ significantly between groups. The authors conclude that SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with increased risk of suicide attempts and self-directed violence, especially early after infection, highlighting the need for prompt suicide prevention efforts. Limitations include possible ascertainment bias, undetected infections, and unobserved confounding.

Overbought refers to a stock market condition where prices have risen significantly over a defined period, potentially signaling weaker short-term returns. It is considered bearish, suggesting a possible price correction or reversal. Overbought can be defined using indicators like the Relative Strength Index (RSI), such as a 2-day RSI above 95. Mean-reversion, or regression to the mean, is the statistical concept that strong deviations from a trend tend to reverse over time. A backtest using RSI showed returns in the first five days after an overbought condition were significantly lower than the long-term average of about 0.05% per day, though returns gravitate back toward long-term averages. The media can amplify these conditions through positive articles creating FOMO or negative articles creating panic during downturns. Overbought conditions predict only short-term results, not long-term weakness, and short-selling based on them is difficult.

The passage covers container-based design patterns for distributed systems. It begins with the adapter pattern applied to logging: Fluentd, a popular open-source logging agent with community plugins, normalizes logs from different applications into a consistent format. Examples include capturing Redis SLOWLOG data via the fluent-plugin-redis-slowlog plugin and converting Apache Storm's RESTful API output into queryable logs, both using shared localhost networking within container groups. The adapter pattern is also applied to health monitoring: rather than modifying an off-the-shelf MySQL container, a separate adapter container runs rich health-check queries (such as a Go HTTP health-check service), preserving modularity, reuse, and knowledge sharing across the community.

The text then transitions from single-node to multi-node distributed patterns and introduces microservices—systems of many components communicating over defined APIs. Microservices offer small-team ownership, decoupling via formal contracts, independent release schedules, and per-service scaling, but make debugging and architecture more difficult; well-known patterns mitigate these challenges.

Replicated load-balanced services are described next. Stateless services are replicated for redundancy and scale; even small services need at least two replicas to meet availability SLAs. Readiness probes inform load balancers when replicas can serve traffic. A hands-on example deploys a NodeJS dictionary server in Kubernetes using a Deployment and Service. Session-tracked services route a user's requests to the same replica via IP hashing (internal) or cookies (external), with consistent hashing minimizing remapping during scaling. A caching layer (Varnish) is best deployed as a separate replicated tier rather than sidecars, and can also provide rate limiting/denial-of-service defense; nginx handles SSL termination, forming a three-tier pattern.

Sharded services are then covered, where each shard serves only a subset of requests, typically for stateful services whose data exceeds one machine's capacity. A sharded cache example shows improved memory utilization versus replication, and cache criticality is discussed in terms of hit rate, capacity, and latency. Replicated sharded caches add resilience and enable rollouts under load. Deployment examples use memcached with either per-pod ambassadors (twemproxy) or a shared shard router, trading complexity against latency. Sharding functions require deterministic, uniform hashes combined with modulo; choosing the right key (e.g., request path or country derived from IP) is vital, and consistent hashing limits remapped keys when resizing. Hot shards can be scaled independently.

The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes request processing: a root fans requests out to leaves that return partial results for merging, illustrated by document search examples. However, per-node overhead and the straggler problem limit parallelism gains; replicating each shard improves reliability.

Finally, the passage discusses functions-as-a-service (FaaS), distinguishing event-driven from serverless computing. FaaS simplifies deployment and scaling but complicates observability, suits neither background processing nor large in-memory state, and becomes costly under sustained load. Patterns include the decorator (e.g., adding request defaults), event handling (e.g., two-factor authentication), and event-based pipelines (e.g., new-user signup), demonstrated with kubeless. The passage concludes by introducing distributed ownership and master election, noting that a singleton under a container orchestrator's guarantees may provide sufficient uptime.

The passage describes the TPS7H500x-SP series of radiation-hardness-assured peak current mode PWM controllers from Texas Instruments for space-grade DC-DC converters. The controllers support three oscillator modes: internal oscillator mode (an RT resistor sets the switching frequency from 100 kHz to 2 MHz, with SYNC outputting a clock at twice the switching frequency), external synchronization mode (RT left floating, with an external clock at twice the desired switching frequency applied to SYNC), and primary-secondary mode (two controllers synchronized via SYNC, with a 90° or 270° phase shift between outputs). Primary switching outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) have roughly 150-mA peak current capability, so external gate drivers are recommended. Dead times and leading edge blank time are programmable via the PS, SP, and LEB pins (fixed at 50 ns typical on the TPS7H5003-SP). Maximum duty cycle is configurable via the DCL pin (100%, 75%, or 50% limits, with OUTB/SRB active only at the 50% limit). The CS_ILIM pin senses primary-side current for PWM generation and overcurrent protection, with a 1.05-V threshold triggering cycle-by-cycle limiting followed by hiccup mode. The FAULT pin allows external fault protection, and slope compensation via the RSC pin mitigates subharmonic oscillation. Thermal shutdown stops switching at 175°C (typical) and restarts below 160°C. An application example details a 500-kHz, 5-V synchronous push-pull converter using GaN FETs, covering component selection for the transformer, switches, output filter, current sensing, hiccup capacitor, and frequency compensation. The controllers operate from a 4-V to 14-V supply, and layout guidelines address noise reduction, grounding, and component placement. The passage concludes with revision history and packaging information.

A Pakistani delegation led by Foreign Secretary Tehmina Janjua attended the first Pakistan-Afghanistan Joint Working Group meeting in Kabul. Pakistan proposed five joint working groups covering counter-terrorism, intelligence sharing, military, economic and trade matters, refugee repatriation, and connectivity, and reiterated that only an Afghan-led peace process can ensure peace. An Afghan delegation also met Prime Minister Abbasi, while Ambassador Aizaz Chaudhry said Pakistan opposes violence in Afghanistan and seeks good US relations.

This patent application, a continuation of several related applications, discloses systems, methods, and devices for wirelessly communicating analyte data using a diabetes management partner interface. The background describes limitations of conventional blood glucose monitoring, including interoperability challenges among monitoring and insulin-regulating devices from different manufacturers. The disclosure describes an analyte sensor system that can receive authorization to grant partner devices (such as automatic or manual insulin delivery devices) access to configuration parameters—including wireless connectivity, access control, and analyte data parameters—and can set or modify those parameters based on a partner device's system requirements, such as battery capacity, accuracy, communication protocol, regulatory requirements, and expected operational time. Configuration may involve whitelist management, advertisement structures, calibration periods, factory calibration codes, bolus calculation parameters, and remote server settings. Additional aspects describe operating modes selected according to device class (partner versus non-partner devices), intermittent or continuous connection models, modification of access levels between display and partner devices, establishing connections with multiple partner devices sequentially, alert configuration through a display device user interface, and monitoring the operability status of a medicament delivery device.

Israel and Myanmar have signed an education cooperation agreement to develop programs teaching the Holocaust, anti-Semitism, and xenophobia in Myanmar's school curriculum. Under the deal, each state may edit passages concerning its own history in the other's textbooks. The agreement also promotes Israeli and Jewish studies in Myanmar and Myanmar studies in Israel, with joint education initiatives from pre-school to postgraduate levels. It comes as Israel faces international condemnation for killing more than 100 Palestinian protesters in Gaza since late March, and as Myanmar denies allegations of ethnic cleansing against Rohingya Muslims. Myanmar welcomed the US embassy opening in Jerusalem, while Israel continued arms sales to Myanmar despite UN accusations. The deal drew skepticism on social media.

The passage describes NVIDIA's RTX Blackwell GPU architecture and its key features. Blackwell's RT Core adds hardware support for Linear Swept Spheres (LSS), making hair rendering about 2x faster than DOTS while using 5x less VRAM. Shader Execution Reordering (SER) 2.0 features twice-as-efficient reorder logic, improving ray tracing and neural shading performance. A new AI Management Processor (AMP), a dedicated RISC-V processor, offloads GPU context scheduling from the CPU, reducing latency and improving multitasking.

Blackwell adds hardware encode/decode support for 4:2:2 chroma video, a ninth-generation NVENC encoder with 5% BD-BR PSNR improvements and a new AV1 Ultra High Quality mode, and a sixth-generation NVDEC with 2x faster H.264 decoding. DisplayPort 2.1b support provides up to 80 Gbps bandwidth.

Max-Q power improvements include advanced power gating, accelerated frequency switching (1000x faster clock adjustments), and low-latency sleep states (10x faster entry than Ada), yielding up to 50% power savings in some workloads.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, producing up to three AI-generated frames per traditionally rendered frame using fifth-generation Tensor Cores, along with new transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA that improve image quality and stability.

Blackwell introduces neural shaders via the Cooperative Vectors API, enabling technologies such as RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. The architecture spans GB202 (RTX 5090), GB203 (RTX 5080/5070 Ti), and GB205 (RTX 5070) GPUs.

The passage concerns Russia's seizure of the bark Cape Horn Pigeon. Russia acknowledged the seizure was unjustifiable and indemnity was due, but repudiated the principal claim for loss of the bark's services during detention. In January 1899, the United States offered $42,000 as a compromise, expressly reserving the claimants' rights if the offer were refused. Russia rejected this in March 1899 and again offered $2,500. The passage argues Russia never asserted a right to control navigation or prohibit fishing and whaling in the Okhotsk Sea beyond ordinary jurisdictional waters, citing the 1824 and 1825 treaties with the United States and Great Britain and the long-unmolested resort of foreign whalers. The Russian commander reportedly declared the sea closed and ordered seizures of whaling vessels—a claim inconsistent with international law and the 1824 treaty guaranteeing free navigation and fishing in the Pacific.

Blue Bird reported record Q3 sales with continued margin strength, driven by strong bus volumes, higher pricing, and resilient demand despite tariff headwinds. This lecture covers coherent (collective) Thomson scattering, which occurs when the scattering wavelength (2π/k, where k = ks − ki) exceeds the Debye length, so the scattering samples the collective motion of the plasma. The relevant modes—ion acoustic waves and electron plasma waves—have frequencies much lower than the laser frequency and phase velocities well below the speed of light. These modes always exist as fluctuations in the plasma, and scattering transfers energy to them, similar to a Landau damping process.

The derivation proceeds in two steps: first, relating the scattered power spectrum to density fluctuations through the spectral density function S(k,ω), which contains all the spectral information; second, calculating those fluctuations using a test particle treatment. Unlike the incoherent case, particle positions are retained via the Klimontovich distribution, so interference between waves scattered from different particles is included. The resulting formula for S(k,ω) involves the electron and ion distribution functions evaluated at ω/k, together with the susceptibilities. Peaks occur where the permittivity ε = 0, corresponding to the plasma's normal modes. The "ion feature" arises from electrons shielding ions, not from scattering off ions themselves.

Because phase velocities are comparable to thermal velocities, a warm plasma treatment with Landau damping is required, though the collisionless Vlasov equation remains valid since the scattering wavelength is much smaller than the mean free path. For Maxwellian distributions, the susceptibilities involve the function W(ξ), related to the plasma dispersion function and the complex error function, which can be tabulated and is available in common programming languages.

This document specifies the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) for AMD's SEV-ES and SEV-SNP technologies, which protect guest register state from the hypervisor by encrypting it during world switches. Non-Automatic Exits (NAEs) allow the guest OS to selectively share register state with the hypervisor through the GHCB, a 4KB decrypted page whose format mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save state area. The document's purpose is to standardize the GHCB memory area, required NAE events, minimum guest state, and actions needing unique support (e.g., NMI handling, SMP booting).

Version 2 adds initial SEV-SNP support and hypervisor feature advertisement via a 52-bit FEATURES bitmap returned through the GHCB MSR protocol. Successive revisions added: 64-bit guest request message sequence numbers, an error code for malformed VMGEXIT input, the VLEK certificate GUID, APIC ID list retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, Page State Change support for SEV-ES guests, the SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob EFI protocol, SEV-TIO trusted IO, Secure AVIC, and Restricted Injection IPI/timer support.

The GHCB MSR protocol (MSR 0xc001_0130) enables communication before the GHCB page is established, including protocol negotiation, SEV information and CPUID requests, AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration, page state changes, Run VMPL, and GHCB unregistration. SEV-SNP guests must register their GHCB GPA before first use; hypervisors may supply a preferred GPA. Guests may also request termination with defined reason codes.

For NAE events, guests copy required state into the GHCB, set corresponding VALID_BITMAP bits, and invoke VMGEXIT; errors are returned via SW_EXITINFO1/SW_EXITINFO2. Detailed event handling is provided for IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, MMIO access, Page State Change (supporting private/shared/PSMASH/UNSMASH operations with resumable processing of up to 253 entries), SNP Guest Request (firmware communication using dedicated request/response pages, with rate limiting recommended), and SNP Extended Guest Request, which additionally returns certificate data identified by GUIDs such as VCEK and VLEK.

In June 2009, Dr. Jeanine Wiener-Kronish, chief of anesthesia at Massachusetts General Hospital (MGH), convened the task force for the Pre-Admission Testing Area (PATA) after receiving a patient complaint letter describing long waits and inefficiencies. PATA, which completed required pre-admission work-ups for surgical outpatients (43% of surgical patients), had struggled with these problems for over two years. Appointments averaged two-and-a-half hours, with some exceeding four hours, and providers routinely worked past 5:00pm. Due to limited capacity, PATA saw only about 65% of outpatients, prioritizing those with co-morbidities; healthier patients received work-ups in the OR on the day of surgery, contributing to delayed surgery starts and an estimated 57,000 minutes of lost OR productivity annually. Earlier improvement efforts, including a proposed second clinic at MG West, failed because PATA was a cost center, and broader perioperative projects faced fiscal, political, and cultural hurdles. In 2008, Wiener-Kronish formed a PATA Task Force led by executive director Susan Moss; in May 2009, an MIT Sloan MBA intern was added to assess current processes. The time study confirmed patients spent more time waiting than with providers and revealed significant variability. At the June meeting, task force members proposed extending hours, adding resources or reducing volume, or improving efficiency with existing resources. The intern offered to evaluate these scenarios using the collected data, and Moss called for detailed analysis to guide the group's decision.

This 4-year naturalistic follow-up of the ePOD-methylphenidate randomised controlled trial examined long-term effects of stimulant treatment on brain development in ADHD. The original 16-week double-blind trial compared methylphenidate with placebo in stimulant treatment-naive boys (10–12 years) and men (23–30 years) with ADHD. Using pharmacological MRI, the follow-up assessed resting relative cerebral blood flow (rCBF) and the rCBF-response to an acute methylphenidate challenge (dopamine-reactivity) in 32 adolescents and 24 adults. Contrary to the neurochemical imprinting hypothesis, no evidence was found for long-term age-dependent effects of stimulant treatment on resting rCBF or rCBF-response over time, and initial RCT treatment allocation showed no long-lasting effects. However, stimulant medication use showed age-dependent associations with regional blood flow: adults with higher cumulative dose or longer exposure duration had lower thalamic resting rCBF, while adolescents with greater use showed a lower mPFC rCBF-response. These associations were already present at baseline, before treatment began, and were unrelated to ADHD symptom severity. Exploratory whole-brain analyses found the CBF-response was associated with noradrenaline transporter distribution, but not with dopamine receptors or transporters. The authors conclude there is no evidence for long-lasting stimulant effects on dopamine system development, though the mPFC association may hold predictive value for stimulant medication use in children and adolescents with ADHD.

Friday's Dow drop of over 600 points—the biggest single-day decline since Brexit—reflected panic over possible higher interest rates after a jobs report showed January wages rising the most since 2009. Analysts see the widespread correction as a return to more-normal, volatile growth, not broader economic trouble.

This cross-sectional study examined associations between personal health literacy, school health literacy environment, and health outcomes among 7,264 teachers from 11 schools in Zhengzhou, Henan Province, China. Personal health literacy was measured using the HLS19-Q12, and school health literacy environment using the OHLS-Q-SF; outcomes included health status, health-compromising behaviours, health service use, and healthcare cost. Results showed 56.9% of teachers had inadequate or problematic health literacy, and only 31.0% perceived a supportive school health literacy environment. Health literacy varied by sociodemographic factors, with lower levels among older teachers, those with longer teaching duration, and those with chronic health conditions. After adjustment, teachers with inadequate health literacy had higher odds of poor health status (OR=5.79), at least one health-compromising behaviour (OR=2.90), at least one health service use (OR=2.73), and higher healthcare cost (OR=2.51) compared to those with excellent health literacy. A non-supportive school health literacy environment was similarly associated with worse outcomes. Limitations included convenience sampling, self-report measures, and the cross-sectional design, which precludes causal inference. The authors conclude that promoting health literacy at both individual and organizational levels may improve teachers' health and reduce disparities.

Linguistics expert Martin O'Leary researched etymology and revealed how seemingly unconnected words share common roots from thousands of years ago. For example, 'architect' and 'dachshund' are fourth cousins, both derived from the Proto-Indo-European (PIE) term 'teks' ('to weave'). PIE, the 'mother tongue' of all Indo-European languages, was last spoken between approximately 4,500 and 2,500 BC and is thought to have originated on the steppes north of the Caspian Sea. It spawned over 440 modern languages, though no texts exist from the time, making reconstruction difficult. Other unexpected pairings include 'blue', 'phlegm' and 'flamingo' (from 'bhel', meaning 'to shine'), and 'sh*t' and 'science' (from 'sek'). Words sharing a common linguistic derivation are known as cognates. O'Leary posted charts on Twitter that received thousands of retweets.

The passage describes the ADS7828, a 12-bit A/D converter. In hold mode, the selected channel's voltage is captured on an internal capacitor array; the analog source must charge the ~25pF sampling capacitor, with charge transfer depending on conversion rate. The device operates with an internal 2.5V reference or an external reference (as low as 50mV); a +5V supply requires an external +5V reference for full dynamic range, while a +2.7V supply can use the internal reference. LSB size equals the reference voltage divided by 4096, so lower reference voltages increase apparent offset, gain, and noise errors; internal noise contributes about 0.32LSB peak-to-peak at 2.5V and can be reduced by averaging.

The ADS7828 supports the I2C bus in standard (100kHz), fast (400kHz), and high-speed (3.4MHz) modes, operating as a slave via open-drain SDA/SCL lines. The passage details the bus protocol (START/STOP conditions, acknowledge, byte-wise transfer), slave receiver and transmitter modes, and addressing: five preset bits (10010), two device-select bits (A1–A0, allowing up to four devices per bus), and a R/W bit. A command byte sets power-down/reference and channel selection; conversions begin when BIT 4 is received, with an ACK returned if the command byte is correct.

Data is read by read-addressing the part; each 12-bit result is returned in two bytes. In high-speed mode, the clock is stretched LOW until conversion completes, and a repeated START (rather than STOP) keeps the device in HS mode. The internal reference defaults to off at power-up, requires PD1=1 in command bytes, and needs settling time for 12-bit accuracy; with an external reference, PD1 must be 0. Layout guidance recommends clean, well-bypassed power (a 0.1µF ceramic capacitor close to the device), a clean analog ground, and caution regarding noise on external reference inputs. The passage concludes with TI legal disclaimers, packaging and tape-dimension notes, RoHS information, and a copyright notice.

Interfacial mobility, a key parameter governing interface migration kinetics, links atomistic simulations to microstructure evolution models, though challenges remain, particularly with solute-drag effects. Mobility is typically extracted from molecular dynamics via the capillary fluctuation method or linear response measurements, both assuming Markovian, memory-free motion. However, hierarchies of relaxation times, especially with solute interactions, produce memory effects that manifest as transient sub-diffusion, as seen in simulations of grain boundaries in dilute Fe-C alloys. Generalized approaches from biochemistry can correct for such memory. The authors adapt these techniques using a simplified kinetic Monte Carlo model of interface migration with interacting solute, demonstrating inconsistency with the capillary fluctuation method, presenting an alternative mobility extraction based on mean boundary motion, and applying a time convolutionless propagator approach. A discrete two-dimensional lattice model enables control over boundary stiffness, solute binding, and diffusion kinetics.

Walter Lippmann's memorandum examines the context of the Inquiry, predicting the war will not end suddenly and that Germany will conduct peace propaganda targeting the Allied Left with minimal concessions, aiming to divide the coalition both between and within nations. German efforts, such as the Reichstag resolution and the Stockholm conference plan, have weakened Allied unity and labor support, though a parallel internal strain exists in Central Europe. Two counter-strategies exist: coercive suppression of opinions responsive to German proposals, which is costly and divisive, and the President's reply to the Pope, which unifies the Allies by emphasizing widely accepted purposes. The European Allies' silence on the Pope's message reflects tense domestic politics rather than full agreement. Declaring peace terms is resisted because territorial debates would reduce the war to nationalism and split the coalition; the primary purpose is defeating the German army or pressuring Germany to reject its current leadership.

FGM is a cultural, not religious, practice considered child abuse, and girls may claim refugee status in Canada to escape it. This study evaluates whether municipality-level (subnational) COVID-19 interventions in the Netherlands could have controlled the first wave (February 27–June 1, 2020) comparably to national measures while reducing societal burden. Using an agent-based SEIR framework with 170,721 agents (each representing ~100 residents) across 380 municipalities and 11 demographic groups, the model incorporates mobility data from mobile phone signals, demographic registries, mixing surveys, and hospitalization records. The wave was divided into four phases of escalating then easing interventions.

Calibrated against national hospital admissions, the model reproduced observed trends, including the doubling time (4.6 vs 4.61 days) and the geographic spread from south to north. Decomposing the lockdown's effects showed mobility reductions contributed most to control—without them, hospital admissions would have roughly doubled—while behavioral changes had a moderate impact and school closures little effect, partly because schools closed relatively late (March 16).

Simulated subnational interventions were triggered when local infection prevalence exceeded thresholds of 3%, 1%, 0.33%, or 0.1%. Higher thresholds traded increased hospital admissions for greater societal benefit: at 3%, admissions rose 157% (~19 thousand); at 0.33%, admissions rose by only 410 while 167 municipalities delayed interventions (36 million additional intervention-free person-days), with roughly 6% of municipalities never intervening; at 0.1%, admissions increased marginally with 18 municipalities remaining intervention-free for over five weeks. Overall, 167 municipalities could have stayed open initially and 12 after five weeks, with only 3.4% more admissions.

The authors conclude that subnational interventions, supported by adequate infection monitoring, could substantially reduce societal burden, with potentially greater benefits in larger countries. Limitations include the absence of household-level detail, constraints of the mobility data, and reliance on national-level mobility patterns.

Scientists studied 105 pet dogs to explore whether toy obsession parallels human behavioral addictions. Through tests measuring reactions to inaccessible toys, preference for toys over food, and calming time, 33 dogs showed signs of addictive-like behavior toward toys. Researcher Stefanie Riemer suspects play—not the toy itself—drives this behavior, as toys are associated with exciting play. The trait was more common in terriers and shepherds, breeds valued for high motivation and focus. An unpublished survey suggests only about 3 percent of dogs show such behavior. Riemer cautions against equating canine and human addictions but emphasizes the value of play for dog-human relationships.

On February 7, 2013, the day before its third annual conference, the leadership of the Sloan Women in Management (SWIM) club at MIT Sloan—three co-presidents and two conference directors—faced a decision to cancel, modify, or proceed amid widely varying forecasts of an impending winter storm (3 to 50 inches of snow).

Founded in the 1980s, SWIM was one of MIT Sloan's largest clubs, with roughly 300 members. Its goals were to build a supportive community for Sloan women, advance their careers, increase opportunities for women in business, and attract top female students. Its annual conference, launched two years earlier, had become the club's largest event; the 2012 conference drew a sold-out crowd of over 400 and was regarded as the best of Sloan's roughly 30 annual conferences.

The 2013 conference, themed "Dare to Fail: Taking Risks When it Matters Most," was led by co-presidents Rachel, Lea, and Tarini and directors Janet and Merrill. Tension emerged over decision-making authority, with the directors feeling micromanaged. Speaker recruitment stalled over the summer; the first keynote, General Janet Wolfenbarger, was confirmed in August, after which Merrill left MIT for a start-up but continued co-directing remotely. Wolfenbarger canceled in January due to government budget cuts, and a replacement keynote was quickly secured. Marketing sold 500 tickets ($25 students, $50 professionals), lagging 2012's pace until selling out the weekend before the event. Operations included a VIP dinner at a new venue, a lost overflow room, and the administration's withdrawal of alumnae breakfast sponsorship two weeks out. Sponsorship reached $38,000 against a $40,000 goal.

As forecasts worsened, attendees emailed about cancellation and refunds, and a sponsor's representatives withdrew. A February 7 morning meeting with Student Life Office staff outlined three scenarios: proceed as planned, cancel that afternoon, or wait for MIT's closure decision. At 1:30pm, the five leaders met with SLO Associate Director Marco Esquandolas. All 15 speakers still planned to attend. Financial pressures included vendor setup beginning at 2pm, tripled rental fees if MIT closed, and a $13,000 catering bill with non-refundable perishables. Rescheduling was infeasible given impending graduation and venue unavailability. The team narrowed its choices to canceling before 2pm, holding a half-day conference with concurrent sessions, or waiting until that night. Esquandolas remained impartial, stating the decision was theirs. The case ends with the decision unresolved.

Baking powder and baking soda are not interchangeable; both help batters rise but differ chemically. Baking powder contains baking soda and a dry acid. Substitutions are possible with specific ratios. Baking powder lasts 3-12 months; baking soda lasts much longer.

Officials cited a weakening labor market and continued upside inflation risks, though they expected inflation to return to the 2% target. Tariffs were discussed but generally not seen as a lasting source of inflation. The government shutdown may limit economic data ahead of the October meeting.

The paper introduces LOT (LLM-proposed Open Taxonomy), an inductive method that identifies reasoning features distinguishing large reasoning models (LRMs) directly from their outputs, rather than relying on predefined researcher-defined taxonomies. LOT works in three stages: an LLM compares reasoning traces from two LRMs on the same question and proposes distinguishing features in natural language; annotates these features in other traces to produce feature vectors; and trains a logistic classifier to predict the source model. When classification fails, the LLM proposes new features, iterating until convergence.

The authors apply LOT to 12 open-source LRMs across five datasets (GPQA-Diamond, MATH-500, AIME 24/25, CRUXEVAL, LiveCodeBench), achieving 80–100% classification accuracy when models differ substantially in scale, base family, or specialization. LOT outperforms few-shot prompting, VML, and a human-defined taxonomy baseline.

Key findings include: smaller Qwen3 models more often exhibit circular reasoning, redundant evaluation, and inconsistent application of scientific theories, while Qwen3-32B more reliably recalls relevant knowledge and verifies approach applicability. Models fine-tuned from the same base family show more similar reasoning patterns. Seed-Coder-8B-Reasoning sometimes applies coding-style reasoning to math problems, suggesting domain fine-tuning creates "inertia" in reasoning habits.

In a case study, a test-time intervention—summarizing, modifying, and re-expanding reasoning traces to align smaller Qwen3 models' reasoning with Qwen3-32B—improved GPQA-Diamond accuracy by 3.3–5.7%, demonstrating a causal link between reasoning differences and performance gaps.

Limitations include the inability to establish causal links between model meta-attributes and reasoning patterns, and potential seed variability in taxonomy generation.

A new study, funded by Boeing and led by Vicki Stover Hertzberg of Emory University, suggests passengers wanting to avoid colds or flu on flights should sit in a window seat and not leave it. Published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, the study involved researchers testing cabin surfaces and air on 10 flights, though no cold or flu viruses were detected. Mathematical modeling concluded that only about one passenger out of 150 would be infected by a hypothetical sick passenger in an aisle seat. The study found 38 percent of passengers never left their seats, with aisle passengers moving most often and window passengers least. The 11 people seated closest to a sick person face the highest risk. Outside researchers noted the small study limits broad conclusions but called it novel.

This final lecture of course 14.13 examines policy with behavioral agents. It begins by reviewing neoclassical reasons for government intervention—externalities, redistribution, market power, public goods, and information problems—before introducing internalities, where individuals fail to account for costs or benefits imposed on their future selves. Paternalism, defined as influencing people's conduct for their own good, is warranted for self-control problems and belief errors, but not for preferences or motivated beliefs. Hard paternalism forces choices through mandates, bans, and taxes, while soft paternalism includes libertarian paternalism (nudges preserving freedom of choice) and asymmetric paternalism (helping mistake-makers without harming optimizers). Arguments against paternalism include government ignorance, heterogeneity, corruption, and freedom of choice; arguments in favor include people's mistakes and dislike of choosing. Popular examples include Social Security, cigarette taxes, and 401(k) restrictions, while helmets, seatbelts, and masks are often unpopular. Evidence shows some nudges work well (automatic enrollment, court-appearance text reminders), but others fail (the HeartStrong trial), and nudge units achieve smaller effects than academic studies, possibly due to publication bias and implementation issues. Not everyone wants to be nudged—some people will pay to avoid energy comparison reports—so opt-outs should be respected. Even a zero default constitutes paternalism, so the debate should concern optimal paternalism. The Save More Tomorrow plan exemplifies successful libertarian paternalism by exploiting present bias, loss aversion, and defaults while remaining voluntary with opt-out. Markets cannot fully solve self-control problems because firms exploit naive consumers who do not seek help. Finally, sludges—nudges used to harm people, such as burdensome rebate forms—should be identified and eliminated.

The passage introduces SOS Pressure Defense, a basketball defensive system by Bob Kloppenburg, developed in response to increasingly skilled offensive players. It argues that pressure defense will increasingly replace or reinforce containment defenses as an equalizer against powerful offenses. The system's six keys are: (1) teaching fundamental defensive skills in a simple-to-complex progression from one-on-one to five-on-five; (2) using key S-O-S words—SET, ON, SMOTHER (on-ball) and SNUGGLE, OFF, STRIKE (off-ball)—to trigger defensive actions; (3) pressuring opponents into "checkpoint" areas at least 18 feet from the hoop to reduce shooting percentages; (4) encouraging two-on-two switching against screens; (5) stopping the fast break by applying pressure in the backcourt immediately after a rebound; and (6) assigning each defender a clear, specific pressure role. The author hopes the system serves as a practical tool for coaching success.

A hockey coach speaks during the playoffs while his Dallas team faces elimination. He praises a player's playoff commitment to hard, gritty play and forechecking despite a tough regular season. He says players generate their own energy at this stage while coaches reflect on what to change, and he believes his team gives itself a great chance to win if it repeats the energy and discipline of the first minutes of the previous game. He says the players' motivation is simply wanting to keep playing hockey together, notes the team has caught breaks during the playoffs, and stresses the need to take advantage of the opportunity. He says the first period will be decisive and cites his team's experience at outwaiting opponents, referencing how Vancouver made the Rangers wait. He praises both goaltenders' performances as a classic matchup, says the team has learned to win, lose, and stay together, and notes Langenbrunner's return and interchangeable fourth-line forwards will add energy, with the series now entirely mental. He calls Brett Hull the team's unsung hero for doing gritty little things.

Amazon updated Alexa to support Outlook.com calendars alongside Google calendars, with setup via the iOS Alexa app. Apple Calendar lacks official support but has a Github skill. Amazon also added hands-free Alexa to Tap speakers via an over-the-air update, which now support echo spatial perception.

New research co-authored by University of Calgary professor Darla Zelenitsky determined how long dinosaurs took to hatch their eggs by studying fossilized embryos of a Protoceratops from Mongolia and a Hypacrosaurus from Alberta. By counting daily growth lines in the embryos' teeth, researchers found incubation lasted nearly three months for Protoceratops and six months for Hypacrosaurus—longer than birds' 11 to 85 days and similar to reptiles. This suggests birds evolved faster incubation after branching off from dinosaurs. Prolonged incubation exposed eggs to risks and, combined with slow maturation, may have disadvantaged non-avian dinosaurs compared to birds, which survived the end-Cretaceous extinction.

The Court of Appeals of Wisconsin affirmed Andrew Anton Sabo's conviction for possessing cocaine with intent to deliver as a subsequent offense and two counts of felon in possession of a firearm. Sabo argued that evidence seized under a search warrant should be suppressed because the supporting affidavit lacked probable cause, that he was entitled to a Franks-Mann hearing based on alleged false statements in the affidavit, and that the informant's identity should be disclosed. The citizen informant had reported seeing Sabo with a firearm and packaging cocaine at his residence, and police independently corroborated his identity, criminal record, and address. The court found the informant credible under the relaxed reliability standard applied to citizen informants. It also held that Sabo failed to make a substantial preliminary showing of deliberate falsehoods to warrant a Franks-Mann hearing, and that the trial court properly exercised its discretion in denying disclosure of the informant's identity.

This patent application describes techniques for enhanced overlay network-based transport of traffic, such as IPsec traffic to and from customer branch offices, using Internet-based overlay routing infrastructure. It specifically addresses selecting an ingress edge region of the overlay network, which has an authoritative DNS. A service hostname received at the authoritative DNS from a DNS resolver associated with a customer router is mapped to an IKEv2 destination of an outer IPsec tunnel associated with a first overlay network edge. An IKEv2 session is established from the first edge to the customer router. Upon tunnel establishment, the first edge performs a secondary DNS lookup to determine whether it is an appropriate ingress region. Based on the response, an IKEv2 redirect is issued from the first edge to a second edge, and a new tunnel is established from the second edge to the customer router. The second edge may perform an additional lookup and, if it is no longer an appropriate ingress region, drop liveness probes received from the customer router, triggering the router to initiate another service hostname lookup.

Trump issued an executive order on Jan. 20 ending birthright citizenship, prompting federal court challenges nationwide. In March, the administration asked the Supreme Court to pause lower-court rulings, seeking to limit universal injunctions rather than address the order's constitutionality. At May 15 oral arguments, justices voiced concerns the government could enforce the order broadly without nationwide relief. The Supreme Court then ruled 6-3 to repudiate universal injunctions, leaving lower courts to determine narrower remedies. Lower courts subsequently ruled for challengers, blocking enforcement and holding the order invalid under the Fourteenth Amendment. On Friday, Solicitor General Sauer asked the Supreme Court to review the 9th Circuit and New Hampshire district court rulings. If review is granted, arguments would likely occur in 2026, with a decision by late June or early July.

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture covers exact solutions of the inviscid Burgers' equation, beginning with the problem of a delta function point source. The expected solution is a fan followed by a shock; the shock position is found using conservation of mass, giving X = √(2t), and this solution is verified against the jump condition and the entropy condition. An exact minimization formula for the solution is then explained, derived from Burgers' equation with viscosity: a nonlinear change of variables (U = −2ν log w) converts it into the heat equation, and as viscosity ν goes to zero, the limiting solution's contribution comes from the point where a quantity b is minimized. The lecture then discusses the Korteweg-de Vries (KDV) equation, which arises in one-way water waves. Numerical experiments showed that solitons—traveling waves—collide and emerge with unchanged shapes, suggesting hidden linearity. An infinite list of conserved quantities was found, and the equation proved completely integrable, spurring a search for other integrable nonlinear PDEs, such as the nonlinear Schrödinger equation. The lecture closes by noting Navier-Stokes is not on this list, recent numerical work disproving a conjectured blow-up example, and upcoming topics: level sets, financial mathematics, and large linear systems.

Mercedes chief Toto Wolff says stress, tension and disruption between drivers may be needed to extend the team's dominance. His comments follow an issue-free season with Lewis Hamilton and Valtteri Bottas, who delivered a fourth consecutive constructors' championship, contrasting with the bitter three-year Hamilton-Nico Rosberg rivalry that still produced title success. Astronomers observed the rogue planet Cha 1170-7626, located about 600 light-years away in the constellation Chamaeleon, undergoing the fastest growth spurt ever recorded in a planet, consuming gas and dust at a rate of 6 billion metric tons per second. Observations from the Very Large Telescope and James Webb Space Telescope showed the planet, estimated at five to 10 times Jupiter's mass, accumulating matter up to eight times faster than months earlier. The event's characteristics resemble growth spurts seen in young stars, suggesting a starlike birth, and 2016 data hint the planet binges regularly.

Reinaldo De Jesus Henao was arrested at Coachella on suspicion of stealing over 100 phones, which festival-goers traced via 'Find My Phone'. Found with a backpack of stolen devices, he was charged with grand theft and receiving stolen property and released on $10,000 bail.

Thruxton circuit marks its 50th anniversary with historic races, demonstration sessions, and the opening of the £2million Thruxton Centre by Nigel Mansell and Murray Walker. Highlights include Karun Chandhok driving an ex-Keke Rosberg Williams FW08C, the return of Niki Lauda's 1972 Formula 2 March 722, 1950s sportscars in the Woodcote and Stirling Moss Trophies, Historic Formula Ford 1600s featuring Tiff Needell, and Adam Morgan sharing Ric Wood's 1980 Ford Capri.

WORD and BYTE writes to PMC registers can corrupt other PMC register writes. The shadow register mechanism updates operational registers at 32-bit granularity without byte lane information, and inactive byte lanes retain previous data, causing local or cross corruption. An SMI I/O trap can control accesses to the ACPI defined registers.

The paper introduces NeuroAdapter, an end-to-end brain decoding framework that conditions a latent diffusion model (Stable Diffusion) directly on fMRI activity, avoiding the intermediate embedding spaces (e.g., CLIP/DINO) used in typical two-stage pipelines. fMRI data are parcellated using the Schaefer parcellation, the highest-SNR parcels (p = 200) are selected, and parcel-wise linear mappings convert vertex responses into token embeddings that are integrated into the U-Net via IP-Adapter-style cross-attention; only the mapper and cross-attention modules are trained, with fMRI token dropout and min-SNR loss weighting applied during training. A brain encoder selects the best decoded candidate images during evaluation. On the Natural Scene Dataset, NeuroAdapter achieves competitive performance with embedding-based methods across eight image quality metrics, particularly on high-level semantic measures; comparisons with Brain Diffuser variants show that its low-level advantage stems from a dedicated VDVAE pathway. The model also generalizes to the NSD-Imagery and Deeprecon datasets. The authors further propose IBBI, a bi-directional interpretability framework analyzing cross-attention dynamics: a brain-directed view quantifies each parcel's contribution to generation, and an image-directed view produces ROI attention maps showing where regions such as Face, Body, Scene, and Word attend in the image. Perturbation experiments show that masking high-level ROIs changes semantic content while masking low-level ROIs does not. The paper notes that current benchmarks may be saturating and positions IBBI as complementary to metric-based evaluation.

Chelsea manager Antonio Conte has urged his players to focus on Tuesday's Premier League match at Huddersfield Town rather than their upcoming Champions League tie against Barcelona.
